text: Four of us went for Sunday late lunch and enjoyed Triumph. We all liked our food food (salmon tacos, triumph burger with good fries, fajita, and turkey club.  The beers were tasty.  I had and recommend the stoudt.  The pale ale also was good.  Nice atmosphere.  We were there in Feb but it looks like it would be a nice place to eat outside in the warmer weather as there is an attractive outdoor deck overlooking the old fashioned train tracks.

Excellent jianbing, and the portions were pretty good. I tried one of each style (with pork floss and bbq pork) and also the curry fish balls. My better half and I split the three items (~$25), and it was filling for the two of us. He used a fork, I ate with my plastic glove-covered hands. :)

The workers were all very friendly. My only complaint is that napkins were nowhere to be found, and the bathroom lights were out!
Absolutely fabulous as always. Got the table side Caesar salad, salmon and Filet mignon. Delicious delicious desserts, Gelato and Tiriamus .Tara was GReaT. We have come here for 20 plus years.
The best food in downtown Tampa. Hands down. If you want breakfast or lunch. Great service. I've had just about everything here minus pork and it's allll delicious! You have to come here!!!

I have been here for happy hour, brunch, and a group birthday dinner now and each time has been a great experience. The food and drinks are tasty and I had great service each time. 

Their happy hour specials include half off select appetizers, and a bunch of drink deals including cocktails, mason jar mixed drinks, and lager. Apps like the brussels (served sweet with apples), calamari, oysters, and paella were delicious.

I had a large group here for my friend and I's birthdays and they were very accommodating. There is a back room where we had privacy and the seating made it easy for us all to see each other (2 long tables). We got several seafood paella, which were very large and everyone enjoyed. The server told us to get one for every 6 people which was about right, because you're going to order other things too. The lobster mac and cheese and tuna tartare were hits too. The waiter brought out oreo beignets  at the end for my friend and me...amazing! They came with ice cream and were a perfect mix of fried crisp, warm oreo, and cold vanilla ice cream.

Lastly, I enjoy coming here for ambiance. It's got that swanky lounge look, but still casual enough to enjoy sitting at the bar or outside on the sidewalk and if you go at the right time it won't be swarmed with people.

Coming in 30 minutes before closing is not only a terrible move on my part as a consumer, but, also a risky move with the quality food I could possibly have. But when I tell you that the chargrilled oysters are hands down the best experience I've had in decades since my first marriage, it is without exaggeration. 
Please do yourself a favor and get them and receive some beautiful hospitality along side it. Thank you mambos!

Ate here with coworkers after a conference at Loews around the corner.  It was absolutely delicious.  We ordered the spiced ribs and bacon wrapped dates.  The presentation and taste were spectacular.  Ordered the chicken dish and it was perfect.  I had the white chocolate cheesecake and it was amazing.  5 stars for sure.

We felt like Indian food and this place was inviting so we strolled in. They seemed a little disorganized, even though the place had only 3 tables with customers. Said we could sit anywhere but all the tables were Dirty! The blonde girl was new -but pleasant and made a good effort to make us comfortable. The dark haired girl (hispanic ? Indian ?) she almost seemed offended that we were there. She was Not customer service oriented At All. The appetizer platter was not good at all. I would never order that again. The naan (flat bread) was burnt BLACK on one side! The Madras was good. Next time we visit Santa Barbara we're gonna skip India House.

Deli staff are professional & generous with the sub portions. Cashier staff also very welcoming & helpful. LOVE the halloween decorations all over the store! They also have specialty snacks & wide variety of flavors from drinks to chips. Big parking lot. Ample indoor & outdoor seating.

What in the unseasoned world? We have all of these herbs and spices that exist and Wheelhouse used not one. I've never had food that was so bland. There were three of us at the table with three different orders and no one had good food.....French toast, buffalo chicken wrap (my order), fries, and hot wings. 

The food lacked all of the flavor. I'm still hungry because I couldn't finish my food. Not a sprinkle of pepper or a dollop of hot sauce could save our meals. The food is so bad that you have to try it to see how bad it is. 

The best part of brunch were the bottomless mimosas. $15 all you can drink. Can't beat that.

My mother and I had been in the area to see a show just up the road at Ruth Eckerd Hall when we had some time to kill.. Not being from around here we just googled food in the area coming across this gem. We both agreed on wanting to grab a bite at a cute place with atmosphere that was not a chain restaurant when we stumbled upon this place, and I'm glad we did.


Howard waited on us and was pleasant from start to finish. We ordered many apps and he steered us towards the perfect bottle of wine to match our taste buds. 
We had the Bruschetta Trio- The Artichoke Heart, Date and Manchego was surprisingly my favorite coming from a huge tomato and mozzarella lover.

We also ordered the Charcuterie Plate where Howard kindly described each cheese and meat on the platter. Fried Goat Cheese was next- I mean its fried.. how could it not be anything but amazing... The outside was crisp and warm as the inside was creamy and cheesy.. YUM

Oh, and if you're a sangria lover.. the Dornfelder Heinz Eifel Shine is a MUST.

Haven't had a better cheesesteak since living in South Jersey- brought me back to my childhood. If you haven't had one there yet, you're missing out.  I love the mushroom steak and ask for hot peppers.  My only hope is that Icehouse will get up to par on their craft beer game. Not a whole lot of choice in the beer dept.

Samuel, Mindy and staff make you feel so welcome. The food is always fresh,delicious and abundant. We do take out at least once a week and love the atmosphere when we do eat there with friends. The food reminds me of the Cantonese cooking my dad (I grew up in a Chinese restaurant) use to make. Everyone we have taken there has become loyal repeat customers. So happy to have them! The best!

When Raijin first opened, there was such a huge hype, you always had to wait in line, there was never enough parking, etc, etc...when I first went here, there really wasn't a line and after eating there, I can kinda tell why. I got the black garlic tonkotsu ramen and gyoza appetizer. The ramen tasted okay, it wasn't the best I've had in Tucson but it wasn't the worst either. The portion size was a teeny bit smaller than other ramen spots here in Tucson and also a little bit more pricey. However, it is kinda nice to have Raijin ramen around considering it's one of the few Japanese restaurants that "specializes" in ramen...most of the other ones have ramen in the menu but are def more sushi-focused (ie Ginza, Sushi Zona, Sachiko, etc). If you are on Speedway, I definitely suggest going to Raijin instead of Izumi--it is not even comparable. Although Raijin is not my fave (yet) I will come back to try everything else they have to offer.

Love the freshness of the food here.  I wish they would either make the portions of the black beans with the jerk Salmon a bit larger to accommodate the large price.  6 ounces for 8 bucks is a bit steep.  

Great food and service.
I knew after having one chip this place was going to be authentic. Must try. Great flavors , nice atmosphere.

Already the luster is wearing off this new store. Loooong lines and out of stock items seem to be the norm now. The only express checkouts are self-scan, and good luck with those. Every other item locks them up, and the attendants are completely INattentive. I almost abandoned my cart and walked out today, but unfortunately didn't have time to start over somewhere else. It'll be a long time before I venture here again.

UPDATE 12/2017: 
I've shopped here quite a few times since my initial review and there continues to be good and bad with this store. Some of the stock issues seem to have evened out, and the store continues to have a nice selection of both groceries and other stuff--housewares, cosmetics, clothing. It's not the cheapest spot in town, but firmly middle of the road, especially if you shop the sales. WORD OF WARNING: Although the store is open all night, don't shop here after dark. They close and lock the north entrance with no warning, leaving anyone who parked at that end to traverse the football field of a parking lot to get back to their car. No fun when it's cold, icy, rainy, etc--and in a sketchy neighborhood, no less. The only signage indicating from outside that the doors are locked is so small that you can't see it until you get out of your car and walk up. I saw over a dozen people angrily leave over this issue on my last visit. Honestly, Meijer: You knew you were a 24 hour store when you designed the building; if you couldn't afford to staff both entrances, you should have designed the building with one central entrance. Jeez.

Bottom line: there are still better options out there and I still avoid this store most of the time, but it's not a complete train wreck if you go during daylight hours.

Seems like this place is always super busy! I hadn't had the time to stop until recently and it did not disappoint. 

I saw lots on the menu for vegetarians. I'm pescatarian but mostly eat vegetarian so it was nice to see so many choices. There was a wait, but it wasn't long. The staff was really nice, just seemed overwhelmed. They offered me coffee refills twice before I was ready then forgot my coffee refill when I asked, but no worries, you can see they were crazy busy. 

I got the lox Benedict because that's pretty much the two best breakfast choices combined! It was great. The hollandaise was a little bland, but of course the smoked salmon and capers made up for it. The potatoes are smothered in paprika and to a heat weakling they might call them spicy - I enjoyed it. 

I came here because I had a hangover and was looking for a giant breakfast. I saw people saying the portions are huge, but when I'm hungover I can eat way too much, and I was surprised at how huge this plate was! The pics don't do it justice, I ate 1 and 3/4 of my Benedict, and only a small corner of the potatoes. 

Also, I've noticed that some places in st Pete just don't salt their breakfast at all and leave it up to the customer. I liked that everything here was seasoned so perfectly I didn't have to touch the salt or pepper. 

Definitely excited to return and try some of their vegetarian dishes
We were very pleased with the food. The oxtails melt in your mouth, so succulent and mouth-watering. We will be stopping back on our next trip down there.

The food was so good, we went 3 times during our 2 week vacation. 

Food: The tamale stuffed with pulled pork was outstanding; got one each time we went. Hands down the best tamale I've ever had. Garbanzo stewed in a very flavorful broth was amazing. Empanadas seemed homemade, it was so tasty and well seasoned. 

Service: Generally the service was standard, other than the really nice woman with the blond hair. She was very friendly, had nice conversations with us, remembered us when we went back and was a good server. 

Ambiance: Small, locally owned. Food served from a buffet by staff.

Great gyros!  I was driving through West central FL this afternoon on the way to Tampa and noticed a few sandwich shops that sold gyros, so many in fact that I decided that would be dinner.  SO when I arrived at my hotel in Tampa and Yelped "gyro" I found a few listings - I decided on Little Greek because it had a review that commented on the vertical spit that is the mark of a true gyro (Kronos brand to boot!). As a former Chicagoan I learned to love good gyros, Little Greek serves up a great version with  tender slices of meat shaved from all parts of the cone, some crispy others tender.  The pita was also great, crusty and soft all at once.  I don't care for the cucumber sauce so mine was dressed only with tomato and feta.  Had a small lemon rice soup, very flavorful.  Also they serve fresh cut fries.  All of it was very reasonably priced.  

You order at the counter and they bring it to you, fast food priced (with plastic ware to eat on and with) high quality food.  The shop as in a strip mall, very neat and clean, greek music playing and Sports Center on TV.  I am sold on this place and will be back!

This a weekend staple for my family. I cannot believe it's been since now to finally review it alas here we are. One of the best breakfast spots in town. Everything is awesome. I'm addicted to their home potatoes. I have put people on to this place and everyone LOVES the home potatoes. They're just ridiculously good. My wife always enjoys the sausage egg cheese biscuit. She doesn't even like cheese on her biscuits. It's just that good. Kids tear up the pancakes and waffles. They have a great patio to vibe out on. Check em out!
Laralynn was an amazing server for a group of 13 of us. Phenomenal service and amazing food. Eggs flamingo was delicious! Great place for brunch!
Excellent poke and service. The ladies working there were very friendly and helpful. I got the large size which could be shared with someone else. Would recommend to eat here if in the area.

Use to be very good, go there a lot for quick pick up. but half year ago food suddenly get very very salty, new and younger employee make mistake a lot(ask for no cheese, commonly forget), recently food taste more normal again, and Texas burger is pretty good. But still, often being disappointed if I order meals(so I get 3 dollar meal, only cheeseburger so they don't messed up, forget to remove cheese still thought. the old triple cheese burger is very salty.

The sushi was fabulous... unfortunately, we got take-out and they forgot to include wasabi and ginger. Such a disappointment :( I'll order again but remember to ask!!

Also- the chicken teriyaki is not even worth mentioning. Super bland and super small portion for the price. Good brown rice though.
Treated like royalty every time we go in! EXCELLENT freshness!!!! Definetly sit at the bar for a one on one experience with the chef :-)

Unique place....the menu changes every week and is always creative/innovative/locally derived.  We've had hits and misses among the menu items we've tried but most of the small plates are so cheap (3-10$) that it was worth the money to try something crazy.  It's not on the menu anymore, but they used to have a weekly poutine that was always incredible.  I think it was usually about $5 and it was a steal.  I wish they would include more vegan options but vegetarians usually have a wealth of options to choose from.  They do have larger plates that range from $9-25 dollars depending on the week.  And they always have a burger for around $10 with toppings that change.  One week it was covered in white chocolate.

Sooo we found ourselves in Sparks today & decided to try this place based on a friends recommendation. I DO NOT concur. Service was lousy, food mediocre, atmosphere bad. 
I explicitly asked for Gluten Free and wrote that on the order. So the chef left off the sauce but included some fried items. 
I asked to speak to the manager who turned out to be our server‍. All she could say was "it's hard" to get it right. REALLY?????

For Scottish themed the food was not what one would expect. 

The sausage meat in the Scotch egg was sweetened...probably to appease the American palette. 

The haggis was quite oily, and probably because there was nothing to wet it with (All Scots know haggis is dry and that's why the potato and turnip are normally with it). 

The korma curry was not a korma. Korma is a coconut based sauce and this was more a madras style sauce without the spice. The curry was served with rice chicken and vegetables on the plate with a small amount of curry sauce on the side. 

Their standard Irish food (Bangers & Mash) was excellent. The sausage was well prepared and the gravy and mash good. 

Overall a bit disappointing and very much lacking the Scottish overtones that we were hoping to enjoy.

Service and ambience was great.  The waitstaff took very good care of us.

Families BEWARE, decided to go out for a snack and some drinks. Our server thought it would be a good idea to add an automatic 20% gratuity after we left a 10.00 cash tip. Called the restaurant and spoke with John Scott supposed Santa Barbara restaurateur, completely denied any wrong doing and blamed it on my financial institution. Now my card is frozen due to the disputed purchase and left with out any resolution to this issue. I get it times are tough, but stealing and disactivating a card while being trusted and mishandled is completely unacceptable, your overpriced limited menu and mismanagement equals complete lack of oversight.

Favorite pizza on the south side . Always fresh, and the homemade sauce is AMAZING!! The owners are friendly and there's always great vibes and music . And on the weekend you can get a slice late night .

I've been going here for many years and whenever I come home to visit family in NJ, I will usually get some take out here.  I have always been a fan of the chicken and broccoli with brown sauce.  My mom says the hot and sour soup is the best she has had.  Love the brown rice.  Nice mom and pop Chinese place and I highly recommend.

Lately the music has been obnoxiously loud and distracting. It makes it really hard to work on anything or talk to the person sitting next to you. The espresso has gone somewhat downhill depending on who makes your drink. The brewed coffee and iced coffee are the only things really worth getting here.

Maynards' sis certainly a nice place, imaginative dishes, nice surroundings and good service, but especially with an overlay of live music in the background (even at the other end of the room), it is hard to hear your dining companions.
We had the schnitzel and spatzle, salmon, burger, gnocchi and a steak. All were good, not great.

Juniper user to be the best restaurant in Boise. Now it's just like the rest of them. Pizza. Salad. Boring. Boring. Boring. I miss the old Juniper. Variety, unique cocktails, exciting. Not exciting anymore. Boring Boise, boring Juniper. Disappointed.

We conduct business meetings here all the time, so I've gotten quite intimate with Pit Boss.  At the end of the day, even bad BBQ is good BBQ, but the stuff here is pretty good.  You name it, and I've ordered it, and it's all good.  My top 3 faves:  The burger (Yes! The burger), which is cooked on the smoker, the sausage and of course the pulled pork.  As for sides, the potato salad and beans are the way to go.  My homeboy always gets the fries and they're excellent as hell, but I just can't personally pull the trigger on ordering that as a side with my QUE.

Service here is always very swift and cordial.

I've only been frequenting The Boss for 3 months, but I will be a continued regular for years to come.

Their seafood is delicioso with lots of flavor  and there is always something for every taste. They have a full bar and happy hour. Servers are always so tentative and friendly.   There's been a few time we go and they are out of fried whole fish or flan but that just goes to show it's a popping place more so on weekends with their Trio on Fridays nights and Mariachi on Saturday night 7-8.

the fennel sausage pizza is one of the best pizzas I've ever tasted here or Italy. 

+1 star

What a great new addition to 104th St! I love having more healthy and delicious options to choose and this place delivers on both.

In the last 2 years, I have been incorporating more vegan/vegetarian dishes in my diet. Trying to educate myself was a little daunting so I took an 8 week program with a wholistic nutritionist. I feel like this place encompasses much of that program with healthy, delicious, satiating food that makes you feel great! No guilt in overindulging here. 

The chilli bowl is so yummy. It is loaded with tons of good stuff like quinoa, beans, tomatoes, avocado, pepper and onion. The sweet chili chipotle cashew cream that tops it, is so flavourful and really compliments the spice. 

I recently had the Quinoa Tabbouleh salad. It was also very tasty loaded with kale, parsley, mixed greens, peppers, cucumber and quinoa. The lentil hummus, olives and tahini-lemon dressing make this salad divine and unique from the others. The combination of saltiness, creaminess and citrus makes you want more! Unfortunately, even after finishing the salad ,you will want more - not only because it is so good, but because the portion really isn't that big. 

The portions being on the smaller side would be my only complaint; however, prices are decent considering everything you are eating is organic and made in house. If you go down the street to Earth's General Store, you will see that it isn't cheap to eat consciously. 

The space is bright, clean, and very modern. I kind of feel like I am going to the spa to have my meal. It is a great break from the busy office.

I look forward to indulging in many more items on the menu and not have an ounce of guilt in doing so.

Made a reservation for dinner over the phone.  Once we Checked in and we noticed that they kept on seating people in the restaurant. They even sat a large group of 8 or 9. I think this may have surpassed the current quota set by the state. 

For dinner we dared the chicken wings and a beef plate. I had the combination pho.   Food wise, they all tasted good. The chicken was crispy and batter flavored well. The pho broth was savory and good for the cold night. 

Service is friendly and quick. But I just could get over the seating limitation being exceeded with the current stars order. Especially with that large party.   Once the pandemic is over and I am back in Reno, I'd come here again for pho.

A pretty good run of the mill Chinese restaurant that is close to my office.  They have a great lunch special for $5.50.  The people were friendly and everything tasted great!  I am glad I found a nice little "go-to" Chinese carry out that's close to me and tasty!

My friends and I stumbled upon Cafe Soule in an effort to temporarily escape Bourbon Street.  Even though the restaurant was pretty empty, we decided to try it anyway and we are so glad we did.  Everything we ordered was absolutely delicious!  The staff was friendly, honest, and helpful.  The owner, John, was just as pleasant.  He was willing to give us a tour of the building, which was the highlight of our New Orleans vacation.  I cannot express enough that this is a place that you must try!

By the way, as we were leaving, we noticed that the restaurant was packed!

,We went here to the Punch Bowl for the first time visiting indy the atmosphere was great and the service we received from Jessica  was probably the best service we received snice we  been here we will be going back here before we head back home thanks Jessica for making our night a good night

Went to Butcher and Singer last night to celebrate my boyfriends birthday. By far one of the best meals I've had in a LONG time. 
Started out with the Crab Louie - the kitchen even split the portion for us to share. 
We each ordered the Delmonico steak topped with truffle butter and it was AMAZING. Cooked to perfection. Also, the bacon and asparagus sides were great. 
And lastly - the service was phenomenal. Our server, Brian, was awesome - extremely helpful in offering his suggestions and taking the time to chat with us after the meal.
We will DEFINITELY be back!

Best we've had in the area. The curry is fantastic and the staff is fun and friendly. Got this one to go but will dine in next time, I was pleasantly surprised with the overall experience inside. Again, the food earns the stars!

I love this place! I've been coming here since the early 70's.  Once in a while a miss but for the most part they are spot on. Solid good eats and nice kids at the window.  Only consist drawback is iced tea,  Bad!

I love this place. The standard bar food is great - their wings, for example, are the best, burgers are good, too. The surprise is what they do with their rotating menu (the typed and xeroxed one). Interesting things, almost always well executed.  The fish here is excellent (they sometimes have terrific whole roasted fish, usually snapper). Who would have thunk, good fish preps at a corner bar!

Goes without saying that the beer selection is wide and deep. The service is always friendly (but not too friendly) and efficient (but never pressured). I've been going to this place for ten years and the whole wait/bar staff is exactly the same, down to the busboy (and I'm pretty sure they aren't related, or at least they don't look like they are). Only thing: it's a good value, but by no means cheap - for a family of four, it will run you $70-80. Otherwise I would be here 2-3 times a week. Feel lucky to have this in the neighborhood.

A last second pizza order that was amazing. Chicago deep dish is the best!! They layer the cheese and ingredients into the dough and it's so good. Family of four could barely put a dent into one of these classics and led to next day leftovers. They know their stuff!!

The food was very good and was ready when promised.  Only reason it isn't a 5 star is because I ordered take out and no utensils were given and the spring rolls weren't very good but the krab Rangoon and lo mein were excellent.

We had dinner and while service is good, the dishes are way overpriced for the quality and taste = 3 stars.  We had the flambee which was too sweet, the poutine which is good bar food, and the grilled bavette beef dish which was blah.

We are not too impress by the food here.  Beer selection is decent.  

Will not dine here again.  We would only come back for happy hour and drinks.  This place is really a bar and if we come back it then we will be sure to lower our expectations and treat it as a bar.
Delicious pimento cheese and pork board for appetizer. Followed by strong service, a tasty burger and an ambient atmosphere. This is a great place for a quaint, casual dinner.

A friend reserved the private room for an event and was told we could show up no later than 30 minutes prior to our start time of 4pm to decorate. Upon arrival while checking in, the host tells us no reservation had been made for the private room and the private room was being used later in the evening for a Wedding party. The Manager calls the Castleton location to see if there had been a mixup while I frantically looked for the confirmation. Finally I find it and show it to the Manager but my friend did not include the person she spoke with.  However the Manager said they would accommodate us with tables in the dining room area. I thought that was good considering the mixup and the fact that it was on the invitations and people could be showing up at any moment. After getting the tables setup the staff greeted us. There were two servers assigned to our table. Initially they were very attentive. They came around took our drink orders and said they would be back. They came back and got our appetizer orders around 4:45pm. We received the appetizers and began to play a few games while waiting on them to come back to get our entrees. After waiting for a while with no one coming back to check on us for drinks or food, we hunted down one of our servers around 6pm. He seemed agitated that I asked when he was coming to take our order. He finally comes over to get our order (alone) and he seems very impatient with questions our guests were asking about food choices. At 7:15 I go hunt down the Manager to find out the delay and to cancel everything since at this point it's been well over an hour. The Manager then says that they weren't prepared for us. Not sure what that meant since they had open seats. I told him it's been well over an hour since we placed our orders and as I'm talking to him the food starts arriving to our table. The food was COLD!  He made no apologies.  It was a group of 13-14 of us. No one was happy with the service. The wedding party that was in the room we "reserved" arrived btw 6-6:30. We later learned from one of the staff that the Bride was an employee. So now it all makes sense that they conveniently couldn't find our reservation. This was the worst experience I've ever had at this location.
Great local farm to fork eatery just walking distance from the Renaissance Hotel! Spicy Bloody Mary's are a must!

Two songwriter nights a week- fantastic stuff! I'm a huge fan. Beer selection is much better than your average bar. Good amount of tv's. Bartenders are great. Prices reasonable. Checks all the boxes for me. Although I could do without the Browns on Sunday :)

When my girlfriend told me there was a new Ethiopian restaurant in Boise, I nearly lost my mind. Ethiopian is my favorite and this place does not disappoint at all! The food is great and the small-business nature of the place is wonderful, the owners are very friendly and the food is authentically prepared, this has become my new favorite place!

Let's start with the dining room. Co- worker and I noticed small ants crawling across our table.  They weren't on the menu. 
    Next: The men's room. Honestly, it smelled like they have a major sewer problem. I had to hold my breath or breathe through my mouth to keep from wrenching. 
  My food was fine. Service was fast. But the above 2 items are the details that set a well-managed place apart from a rag tag restaurant .

Food is excellent! BBQ sauce is on point! My husband doesn't eat everyones dressing if it isn't his mom's. He ate turkey & dressing and went back again for the same plater. Meat tender, place clean & people friendly and HOSPITABLE! Owner is always awesome! I highly recommend their home cooking! Tropical tea os delicious!

Service is very underwhelming. We had a large gropu of 13 and had made reservations well in advance since we were all coming in from different cities. When we arrived 10 minutes early, they told us they didn't know how long the wait would be for our reservation. We had to wait outside in the cold.

By the time the table was ready, it was nearly 45 minutes after our scheduled reservation. Food took a while as well and when the serverse brought them, they were annoyed that they had to ask who ordered what. Isn't that the job?

When we asked the server to set up separate checks by couples, she indicated she could do it but that it would "take awhile". We asked what "awhile" meant and she said "...least 20 minutes so if you want to wait..." We told her we could pull out our phones to do the math ourselves. 

Now to the food....we tried the corn tamales (I think that's what it was), guacamole trio thing, bone marrow tacos, 2 taco plate (choose your own taco), cream sauced chicken thing with pomegranate seeds and a bunch of other things. Nothing was worth writing about except the bone marrow tacos.Super presentation, delicious and just perfect for 2 tacos given it's a beyond rich indulgence. 

Now, to be fair, it was our first (probably my only) visit. The local who took us there loves that place, but told us service is never their forte. So...

Reco: Go if you don't mind hit or miss service. Sit at the bar and order bone marrow tacos and drinks.

Very awkward moment. Younger male server who brought salad to the table with 3 seated children looked at my wife and said "I know that you think I am gay". Since we hadn't had any prior conversation with him, we were in disbelief and ignored him, kinda just assuming that he had some form of mental disadvantage. 5 mins later our daughter's 11 year old friend said "why did he say that you thought he was gay?" When talking to the manager on our way out, she says "I tell him all the time that this is not funny! So sorry, I will talk to him again" WTF is going on at this place? What does his sexual preference have to do with our dinner?

Our service was excellent, as the waitress was quick with our refills. The food comes quickly so any appetizer just gets in the way.  Stick to the chips and salsa.

You get a lot of food but peripherals like sour cream and guacamole are extra.  Pepsi products are what they have on the fountain. Coke is available but served in glass bottles so they aren't free to refill.

Cute little corner Cafe on Russell Street featuring almost exclusively vegetarian/vegan fare. Many different teas, coffees and other unique beverages are available. I was not brave enough to try the sodas featuring shrubs. They do have a few tasty sounding lemonade varieties that I look forward to trying in the future (pink pomegranate lemonade?!). I went with the Aztec mocha latte and subbed Almond milk. It was presented beautifully and it was delicious! 

The food is pretty much small plates and pastries. I tried two types of toast, the avocado and the tomato/goat cheese. Both were very good, although I am not a fan of cherry tomatoes (I tried them, but it was quite an easy fix to remove). I liked them both, but if I had to choose one I'd choose the avocado. I meant to try the pastries but I will have to save that for my next visit. One of my companions today tried to order the vegan BLT but was told that they no longer have this available (despite it still appearing on the menu). I would definitely be up for trying again, although my omnivorous companions were a bit disappointed.

Man, I hate to do it but the 5 star rating I gave this place a few years ago is just embarrassing now.

I was here last night and I got a steak burger with cheese and steak fries. I ordered the burger cooked medium and it was way over-cooked. There wasn't even a hint of pink in it at all. AT BEST it was cooked medium-well and that's being generous. My boyfriend's burger was overcooked as well, though not to the extent that mine was. Service was slow and it took forever to get our check at the end of the meal. I can't totally blame the waitress, because she is working the entire dining room alone, but please hire another waitress to get things moving along a bit. Also, this place is dark- really dimly lit. I feel like I'm eating dinner in an old bar room. 

I don't know, I really liked them the first time I went after the reopen, the second time I was underwhelmed but chalked it up to an off night, but last night was the night that I finally had to put my foot down and say "enough is enough".

Great food and service. We had the brisket, ribs, hot links, loaded brisket fries, and greens. Great flavor and seasoning. We will definitely return. It's rare to find a Bbq place that does great in all three of the main meats mentioned above.

This place is a hidden gem.  Breakfast and lunch I have enjoyed there and hope to continue to enjoy them for years to come.  The white chocolate and strawberry crepes are to die for.  Sandwiches are impeccable.  Try them out.  Fabulous.

Always good and consistent.  Very much an Emeril's restaurant. Had a quick lunch at the bar and glad I stopped. They always have an interesting selection of wines by the glass which went great with a deep rich gumbo and a crab imperial with flat bread.

I've gotten take-out from here a bunch of times but today was the first time I ever actually ate in the restaurant. The food was excellent as always, mac n cheese is a must have and the chicken sandwiches are fantastic. They had great happy hour deals and strong drinks. The atmosphere was pleasant, loved the pacman machine, and our waitress was very friendly and helpful. The only complaint was the fact that the food took forever to come out and we ended up spending a lot more time there than we had anticipated.

Place is so sweet. Ordered about ten items between myself and the lady and everything was solid. 

Loves
Atmosphere - location was so cool. Open laying looking right into the kitchen. Make sure you request a spot in the main dining area. Personally, I feel it's more "in the scene" than the more intimate room off to the side. 
Music - great volume, great transition from rock to more mellow throughout the evening. Manson was on when I walked in and I knew that I was in for a great time. The ambience of the main dining room trumps the little room to the side. Be where the action is. 
Food - you can't go wrong with anything you choose. My top picks : salatim with hummus and laffa (a must), brisket soup, kofte. Didn't get to try the whole roasted pork shoulder with chickpeas and pomegranate but was heavily looking forward to it. It's something you have to request in advance which is something I didn't know. Saw about 6 come out while I was there so I'm assuming it's tasty. 
Chef - all too often you see chefs make get a little bit of stardom and then they're no where to be found. Not chef Michael Solomonov. He was the first face I saw in the kitchen. This guy is as real as they get and saw him take some plates out to the dining room. Such a boss. 
Staff - very knowledgeable and helpful. Sealed the deal at the end of the night with a charming man, Oken*, coming to check on everything. We're from Boston and he told us of the sister restaurants, Oleana and Sofra, in our city to check out. 

Dislikes 
Not much. Tie bar on staff is a great look but having the name of the restaurant etched in is a little much. I know I'm at Zahav but can't knock the place for that. That was my attempt at "trying" to find something wrong with this place. There's nothing. 

Keep it up Chef Solomonov. Absolutely killer.

Stopped in for two coffees and a cinnamon roll to go. 25 minutes later we were still waiting for our order along with several other customers.  The coffee was okay and the food was acceptable, at best.  
We won't be back.
They have Great service.  They are fairly priced.  Scottys has great food, and great beer really cant ask for more.

Major Dive Bar ALERT! As ya walk in from a very rough parking lot and a view of a trailer park behind just go on in. This is another place I would always come to when we would visit! How I've missed the sweet and spicy wings! This was a smoking bar and it still reeks of cigarettes and beer today. Definitely a locals place. Established in 1998. Walls are greasy and beer splattered. The floor is a little rough as well and hasn't been cleaned in forever. Couple pool tables , pinball and TVs, a great place to catch the Eagles games. This place gets loud and grunting is an acceptable form of communication. With that said the food here is amazingly good from soups, burgers to the wings! Cheap drinks and good selection of draft beer and take out beers as well! Daily specials to. I remember wings being 10 cents here those days are long gone. I recommend the sweet and spicy wings hands down the best wings I've ever had!!!! I'll be back I'm coo coo for da wings ya!

Just moved to Maplewood and I have to say that I was thrilled to be living so close to an Imo's.  That's right.  I am a thin crust fan and Imo's is the best chain for thin crust around unless you consider Talayna's to be a chain anymore.  Problem is, that Imo's can be really hit or miss depending on the location, and the location near me is definitely a big miss.  So sad....  Which reminds me that I should probably write a review of that place to warn my fellow yelpers of the dire state of things.  

Being a pizza-holic and lover of all things pizza, I started searching for another place to try.  Desperate for something (really anything) besides the usual, I activated the questionable apple maps app which just so happens to integrate yelp reviews and whoa boy!   I was in luck.  Pizza World had 4.5 stars with 7 reviews (easily enough data points to take a chance) and furthermore, was actually close enough for delivery!  30 to 35 minutes later the pizza arrived at my house.  I ordered the garlic cheese bread, a cookie, and a hand tossed pepperoni pizza since my approach to new pizza places is to first see how they do the basics.  Let me tell you, that this place has a lot of promise.  The crust is some of the best in Saint Louis (just an ever so slight burn with lots of crispiness).   The pepperoni was just your standard stuff as far as I can tell.  Nothing special, but perfectly acceptable.  Overall, I'd say this place is on par with some of the better (not best) places in NYC which for Saint Louis is something pretty special.  

I was a little torn about what number of stars to give this place.  My first thought was 5 stars, but I realized that I was letting the excitement get the better of my senses.  Luckily, before finishing this review, I turned to the cookie I ordered for thoroughness sake and realized that it was just a little bit burned on the bottom.  That allowed me to select a 4 star rating with a clear conscience.  But let me say, given the overall awesomeness of Pizza World, I plan to return with some high  frequency, especially given the reasonable price.  I am looking forward to trying some of the calzones and the "gourmet" pizza options as well.  And who knows.... perhaps in time, I will find come to feel a sense of guilt for that 4 star rating and up it to 5.

I was here and had the Best Wedge I have ever had.
It was even better than the last one here.
The dressing and tomatoes and eggs were so good and fresh.  I would recommend this Wedge to anyone.
It was a meal in itself!!!
Try it Flash said sooooo good!

Cute decor and atmosphere. Service was very friendly and coffee was hot. Good variety in the menu - your standard breakfast options and some southern influences options. Food came quickly, was hot and cooked as requested. Would return.

Murasaki has changed owner - EVERYTHING CHANGE FOR THE BETTER !!!

I have tried this restaurant 2 years ago, and it is not down-to-the-drain bad but definitely not one that I will ever think of patronizing again.

Until most recently, my wife and I went for a quick eat-and-run lunch date. What I can say is the food is amazingly good - i have to say that to give a comment like "amazingly good" on a plain-o-maki, it is a "huge" compliment as POTUS would say it (and I really mean it). The fish has to be very fresh to the point that it can be discerned in the maki-wrap-about. 

It did not stop there, we went for a family date with our daughter on Thai entrees last weekend. Again, superb !!! Pad Thai is not too saucy, and the Thai fried rice is just as Thai as it can be, Sawadee-khrap. We are asian, we knew how a good friend rice can really be. 

Finally, I went alone for the ultimate test - sushi. I am very sensitive to sushi, and I can really tell if it is good one. I have yet to find a decent, not to mentioned great sushi place in PA (I have tried some in Philly and around chester county area). There are all sub-par to my standard, some are eatable if I really want sushi kick. A good sushi restaurant should be judged by their tuna (just my opinion). Man !!! the tuna is superb - they provide the supreme cut. I order a sushi entree, I relish every single pieces of those - it is so good that an order of ala carte (King Salmon). 

In the end, I have a good conversation with the sushi chef who is also the owner. I come to learn that the chef is a man of integrity. His story (I admire and respect virtuous person) about how he sources and prepares the meal is very commendable (he sources his fish in Philly, NYC and Maryland very early in the morning). All his fishes once start serving will never go beyond 3 days - to maintain the freshness - and yeah, he will discard all the unsold fishes after 3 days. I enjoy his story about how he enjoy his work and happy to see people enjoy his preparations. He is very passionate about his job and not only for the money which I would say is a rare gem for humanity in the lustful torrent of materialism. 

This place will be my regular restaurant to visit !!!

Easy COVID lunch spot and easy to-go lunch. Quick service, restaurant is clean, staff are very attentive. The beef broth is some of the best I've had this side of the river. The spring rolls are hands down the best in New Orleans. Highly recommend.
Great place for no nonsense great food. The hot chicken (I got the medium) has plenty of spice but also plenty of flavor. And their pork shoulder sandwich is tasty too. Will definitely be back.

This was my first time trying out this highly rated Cuban spot and my experience was wonderful. Quick service and friendly staff. There were about 4 people ahead of me when I arrived but didn't feel like it was much of a wait at all. I liked the water dispenser and cups available as a self-serve option. My husband and I split a Cuban sandwich and Lechon plate. For us, it seemed plenty as the Cuban sandwich was pretty big and the Lechon plate was hearty of beans, rice and pork. Both very tasty and recommended. They even had Cholula hot sauce available.

We waited for 45 minutes for a table for Sunday brunch, only to wait another 50 minutes for our food to come. The pancakes were hard around the edge, the mushrooms in the garden skillet were from a can. Overall a terrible experience. Will not return.

More like a 4.5, this is a very good spot. I'm not particularly a thick pie kind of person but they do them well with a wonderful crisp. We got the Sausage and the Porchetta. The sausage was delicious and so was the porchetta, but the porchetta was super heavy and I couldn't eat more than one slice. You can tell the ingredients are fresh, overall great spot. Will be back

This place was our savior on a night when we definitely needed booze.  We had been across the street at Moriarity's being ignored by an old bartender (see other review) when we had the idea to come here.  Beer was cheap, cold, and readily available.  They didn't have Guiness; which we thought was odd for a place calling themselves "Irish Pub".  A good time was had in spite of a lack of Guiness.

We go once a week .. But didnt understand why using gift card that was purchase from our family member to us cannot be used all at once? And then the employee said that we have used other gift card already a couple times & he showed emotion that he didnt like it but we told him, only one other time.. He was confused for thinking we are trying to take advantage, but we use them correctly off of the fine print, so even tho my family spent money for two $20 gift card for me and my wife cause we go all the time and always tip, but we could only use One $20 gift card and then pay the difference.... Sucks cause we wont go back now, just because of how he acted towards us using a gift card.. All it takes is one bad experience to lose a customer.
Came in at midnight. Took 30 minutes to get through drive thru line. 30 minutes. C'mon.

Have been going here since I was 5 yrs old and I'm currently 23. Nicest people but not the nicest part of town. Donuts are absolutely delicious. They sell out fast! Don't go there at 9:30-10 expecting to have top pick.

I hate to be that guy and say I never write these things.... But I dont. A colleague of mine decided that we are going to do dinner over at Del Frisco's raved about the service and how amazing the food was even before we arrived. So,  the bar was set pretty high already. Sadly during our order something arose and he had to leave most of the time I would have left myself but the service from Eunice is was kept me there.  She informed me on the great special of the night and even paired it up with a cocktail once I told her I'm a whiskey guy. (Old fashion was a great choice btw)  I ordered the prime rib eye rare  Pittsburgh  style. For those who don't know this is not a easy thing to do right. Along with some scallops. That's in it's self is a challenge but my God chef Siobhan locked it out of the park. Right along side the roasted beets with whipped goat cheese. I CANNOT STOP BRAGGING  about this experience. Erin and crystal came to also check on me even though I was not in there section. I felt like I own the place.  I really hope Laura gets to see this show she can thank her amazing staff for a world class dinner.

This was my first all you can eat sushi experience...I have to say, I left a bit disappointed. I was excited for a Friday night out with my favorite man and my newfound favorite food. The restaurant was dingy and outdated.  The service downright sucked....not a good location for a date night :/

I was very disappointed. I was excited to support a local all vegan restaurant, resting assured that my food would not be contaminated with animal products or bi-products. The food was underwhelming to say the least. Order Pad Thai noodles and hot greens. The greens dish was decent. The noodles though.... just, no. Tasted like a giant squirt of siracha and ketchup comprised the sauce. The mung bean salad and crushed peanut toppings were almost non-existent. I couldn't eat more than a quarter of this dish.  The greens were okay but were lacking key elements as advertised. When I am thinking I will get Bok Choy and Kale and other mixed greens and there is a scrawny portion... from a vegan restaurant... so disappointed. I am not sure there was any Bok Choy at all. 
The brownie was decent thought. That helped the bitterness of the meal. I am not sure if I will try here again, perhaps some of their other dishes are better, but with the steep prices, I don't want to risk another disappointment. If the food were awesome, I'd happily pay the top dollar prices they ask for a truly vegan meal. but ... nah.

Wonderful, authentic Mexican food at an affordable price. The portions are filling without being too large, and the staff is very kind and accommodating. Cash-only payment is a bit of a problem, but it's definitely not enough to keep me from coming back.

A great new idea for Reno! Cake and ice cream doesn't just sound great, it tastes great as well. Krem has brought a great business idea to the area. Dessert was very high quality and the staff was extremely helpful. This has definitely become a great place to add to my rotation.

My girlfriends and I go here every week. The sangria is out of this world and their food is yummy and fun to snack on. The owners are always in there and make their customers feel at home. Opie is awesome too!

I've been to Southwest Diner at least a dozen times now, and they are consistently great each time. Everything I've gotten from there is very good, and I feel like it's the made from scratch sauces, especially the red chili sauce that makes every dish authentically delicious. I usually stick with the regular lunch burrito, not that the breakfast burrito is lacking, but I'm not much of a fan of egg in my burrito. I always make sure it has that rich red chili sauce inside and add that side of rice and beans, it always makes for 2 filling meals (it heats up well for lunch the next day). My husband always gets the cornmeal pancakes, he loves them, they are so hearty and delicious -- with the sweet cream cheese butter and added strawberries, yum! We usually start with an order of sopapillas with an added side of that sweet cream cheese butter and honey -- they are warm pockets of yummy goodness! 

Once in awhile I'll mix it up and try something new; I've tried the Jonathan's fiery scramble; and it is the best way to eat scrambled eggs, cheesy with a bit of heat!  Also, I've had the enchiladas, and they were almost too much for me, a towering stack of corn tortillas with pockets of red chili (or green if that's your thing), melted cheese and chorizo (or any meat you want) on each layer, with rice and beans -- it's huge, but also amazing! I've seen others get the slinger, the grits on fire, and breakfast plates -- and always a completely clean plate afterwards, so it must be good. 

Aside from the food, they have this really fun bus on the side of the restaurant that you can hang out in while you wait to be seated. The bus is heated/air conditioned and has it's own bar to order drinks, or free coffee and water while you wait. About the wait, it's almost always at least 30 minutes (because it's just that good!), so we found that you can put yourself in line before you even leave your house using the Yelp app. This has been great the past couple times we've been there, as we just walk in and are seated almost immediately -- usually at the bar (it's always a bit more of a wait for one of the tables). 

This place is definitely cozy; you will get to see up close and personal what your neighbor is eating, especially if you are at the bar, but also at the smaller 2-person tables. That's ok with us, we don't mind sharing the small space with others, as long as they keep serving us the amazing food! Speaking of which, the service has always been great, it seems like everyone that works there genuinely are happy to be there.

I recommend giving Southwest a try, I think you'll love it.
Some of the best mexican mood in santa barbara. The Al Pastor has the best grilled pineapple in it with the biggest variety of salsas. 10/10

We came here on our first night in Clearwater and it did not disappoint! Their patio overlooks a canal and creates an amazing atmosphere for dinner. The food was great! We're pretty picky when it comes to finding good food, and this place did not disappoint! If we were in town another day, we'd have another dinner here since it was that good!
Its all really good. Sucks they are across the street from dat dog. But liberty is awesome chill place to get away from loudness of dat dog. liberty was awesome.
Would definitely make my way over here for the bottomless mimosas!! A great spot for brunch. Would recommend for a group. Make sure to make a reservation though!

The food, ambience, margs and staff were as good as it gets. If you're looking for cheap, quick Mexican food there are a zillion places in Tucson to go and this isn't one of them. It's an upscale, although not super spendy take on Nuevo Latino Cuisine. It's pretty crowded so I hesitate to call it romantic but the vibe is cool. My only gripe is the lighting is so dark we needed the flashlight on our cellphones to read.

Will somebody from Dickey's please explain to me why the employees DO NOT receive credit card tips and why the owner keeps them.  I have reached out to your corporate office but have not heard any at all.

Really nice hotel with spacious modern rooms- well the king room was great.  It's also very close to beach. You have to take a weird walk to the beach but once you get there it's beautiful.  Complimentary valet.  Complimentary happy hour. Hotel also has roof top bar/lounge.   This is a great property for couples, a single person who wants some alone time R&R or a friends low key getaway. Clubs and  more dining options are a super short drive away.  Fairly new, Kimpton Zamora is a welcomed addition to St. Pete's Beach.  I will be back

I guess I had a craving for more fresh bowls, so I found myself at Ciccio Cali the same evening that I'd eaten at Big Island Poke for lunch! Again, the perfect choice! So, I had no idea Ciccio Corp had opened another restaurant up in New Tampa! I love Water in South Tampa and the Green Lemon which made choosing this easy. 

I posted pics of the menu, mostly because I was so hungry I forgot to take a pic of my food.  I'm happy to say there are several choices here-but I was surprised that so many had a southwestern flavor profile. Not MY fave, but hey! That's just me. My husband ordered one and loved it - I ordered another spicy tuna dish! A creature of habit. If I could eat raw tuna at every meal, I'd be thrilled!! 

The service was impeccable and we sat outside in this adorable outdoor area with lights hanging from the trees and music. They were great about us bringing our new puppy to that area and even came out to pet him and take his pic! So sweet!

I would definitely return and encourage everyone to try it out! Next time I'm going sans puppy so I can stay and relax!

Only suggestion? Please replace the stout that your vendor doesn't carry anymore! Y'all need a dark beer!!

Very fun semi-casual atmosphere.  I say that because there are both people in jeans and others dressed up.  On an excitement scale of 1-10 with 1 being Catholic Church and 10 being the LA riots I'd say this place is a 5.  Be prepared for a good time but leave the brass knuckles at home.

Update 1: Ok. I had to take away a star.  The service sucks. Let me elaborate. Instead of taking your drink order don't look at you while cleaning glasses and basically ignore you.  They are abrupt and rude and kind of condescending.  We are here for a show and if it weren't for that would have left.  I hope to be able to come back and with a better experience give back the two stars I removed.

UPDATE 2: Oh my, lost the last star.  After the most terrible service ever, the bartender chased my girlfriend out to the car after not being happy with her tip.  I had to intervene.  Wow.  Just Wow.
Strange restaurant. Strange food. Seems like they try too hard to be different or unique. An experience, but I'm sure we won't be back. They did have very great service and nice people.

Love this place.  Tried the other Sachiko and hated it.  Ramen is awesome, everything is pretty consistent with what I had in Japan.  They have real curry rice.  The hamachi was perfect.  Prompt service and the waitresses are funny.  Bottom line, my kids love it and they hate everything.  Thumbs up.

Amazing find! Awesome atmosphere, attentive and friendly service, and mouthwatering delicate Italian food. Hot fresh focaccia comes with every entree and the pasta is homemade. Love supporting local business!

Would come over and over again!
Good was delicious however my matcha green tea was over $5 and still had clumps of green tea powder they could of at least es mixed it better.

I have ordered from Bareburger twice now and will never again. The first time it was over an hour late and I got horrible food poisoning. The second time it was 30 minutes late and so cold that it had to be reheated in the microwave. To add to that, the order was wrong. They forgot the one topping on my burger that I was looking forward too- the cheese. This is not the place to go for a quick or accurate meal.

This is by far the best Fast food on the street. Every time I go to this location the drive through is fast, hot and kind. The staff is always smiling and encouraging. I will 100% return to this location and choose this location over ALL other Fast food on Manchester!
Great hidden jem. My husband loooves their beer selection, but the food is amazing and cheap! Best hoagie I've had in a while, not a gourmet hoagie just simple and perfect.

(4) ~ very good overall food; drinks & service.  

FAVORITE DRINKS:
** Pomegranate Ginger Margarita(w. Salt) = (4.25) Very good
** Cuban Coffee = (4) very authentic with a slice of sugar cane & it's strong;)

FAVORITE APPETIZERS:
** Chipotle Honey Queso Skewers(Seasonal) = (4.25) Very good...Hope they keep this year round;)lol
** Guacamole = (4) very good

FAVORITE ENTREE:
** El Cubano(Sandwich) = (4) very good.  Note:  Ask for their "Paladar Caribbean Lime Hot Sauce" to get an extra kick too;)

FAVORITE SIDES:
** "Adobo" French Fries = (4) very good
** Sweet Plantains = (4) very good

FAVORITE DESSERT:
** Sweet Potato Donuts = (4.25) Very good, freshly made & still Hot;)

OTHER DRINKS TRIED:
* Rum Tasting(Super Aged) = (4) very good.  Note:  IF you're not used to drinking straight Rum, add an ice cube from your water to both cool it down and dilute it;)  The Ron Zacapa 23 yr. old was my favorite;)
So happy I tried this place! Terrific gyros and great family operated business. A true gem in the area. I will definitely be back!!

Why have the option to call in an order if they're not going to make it until I get there? This is not the first time this has happened. I'd be more understanding if they were packed but they all look too high to qualify and no one had any clue about my phone order though it popped up to be paid for. The food is always good so that's why I put up with this but they should consider hiring more competent employees.

Nice brunch spot in Zionsville. Lots of fresh bakery choices for sale inside. Fast, friendly service. Omelette and French toast are solid. House made bread kick things up a notch. The small cut home fries are good but overall just small soft potatoes; I prefer bigger cuts that are crisp outside and soft inside. 

Cinnamon bun is OK...the bun itself reminds me of a nice bread more than a cinnamon bun, and there's too much icing in my opinion. 

I've ordered Rosies breakfast on my prior visit which was very good; the pancake and biscuit were delicious.

First time here and was hopeful  looking at the reviews. The fried pickles were  mostly breading because it was over cooked and the pickles were not really present. Ale Panini and buffalo chicken sandwich were edible at best. Our waitress seemed confused by the question of "can I please have some blue cheese dressing for my buffalo chicken  sandwich?" Which was barely sauced and only a bit of lettuce. Pizza was ok. Won't be coming back.

We went to Frenchman street while my wife and I were on vacation in New Orleans.

We noticed Bourbon Street has turned into a EDM street, so we asked where we could see some jazz in New Orleans in New orleans and they said Frenchman Street had all the jazz restaurants. It is about a half mile from Bourbon Street and we decided to get a beer at The Maison.

Great beer selection and the band was fantastic to watch. Fun hour or so. Highly recommended.

I ordered a few dinners for take out this past weekend and everything was exceptional. I find that ordering takeout elsewhere sometimes can leave you with a bland meal or not a full portion size and that is most certainly not the case here. The quality of the food was excellent. The portions were very generous and the flavor in the food was just as good as if you were dining in. We got two short rib platters, a chicken shawarma platter, and the desert rose sandwich. We also got a side of pita and labneh. Everything was so flavorful, but the short rib was hands down the best. The service was also wonderful on the phone and upon picking up. Very friendly and happy to answer any questions we had about the menu. Everyone was wearing masks for those that are curious.
Ordered to go had Mexican tacos tostada both really good had a burrito last time there also very tasty. Very friendly staff and quick service . Highly recommend eating here .

I needed something relatively healthy to eat for breakfast. I ordered the vegetarian breakfast. My daughter returned with food from another establishment and we were asked to leave due to the food from a different place EVEN though I had ordered food from their establishment. Let's be clear. This is an airport, not a brick and mortar restaurant. This is a very poor manner to treat customers. The food was poor to mediocre at best. The eggs were overcooked and cold. I should have stuck with Chick-Filet.

Great food, even better customer service and free Parking. What else can I say. I guess I can say the prices were good too. I came for breakfast and left so full, I don't think I spoke a word for twenty minutes. Just thinking damn I'm full lol, why did I eat so much.

Love this juice spot! They are dedicated to using organic produce and the quality of their smoothies / juices definitely reflect the higher quality ingredients. So tasty and delish. Plus, if you download their app you get a $5 coupon.

On June 26, 2015 we chose Huck Finn's as an alternative to The Ruby Slipper where customers were lined up around the block for a table. We were seated immediately when we arrived and the dinning room was almost empty. The food was good (Omelette, Eggs Benedict, and Beignets) and so were the bloody mary's. The service left much to be desired the wait staff was inattentive and forgetful especially considering the fact that they had very few customers. I would recommend going to Huck Finn's once they've properly trained their wait staff in customer service.
Love the atmosphere there and the service and servers are excellent,  me and my family go there before we go to the bsu games..    go bsu

Stellar service here, beautiful dining room and back outdoor area, and good food here. The live music was a standout too. We went on New Years Day and they had a trio of musicians going around and playing suggestions table side. Some of my friends sang with the band and they had a soprano saxophone soloist that really killed it. One of the servers took us around and gave us a tour after our meal. The house behind a Broussard's is where they filmed AHS Coven. 

For the food, a standout was the crab quiche and the $14 bottomless mimosas.

I was surprised to read all of the negative reviews of this place as that was not my experience at all. I mean, in my view this place has several things going for it:

1) They're open until 4 am and will deliver to just about anywhere. How many times are you wanting to get delivery from a place but since you're not in their 6 block radius you're SOL or it's 30 minutes before closing and they don't even answer their phone? The delivery time could be improved but it's not THAT much longer than your average delivery time.

2) Food is good and more inventive than your typical pizza/sub/wing place. "Build your own onion rings"? Come on- that's awesome (and they're great)

3) Food is well packaged for delivery. It comes hot and they make sure they put it in the right container- fried foods stay crispy and softer foods stay warm and soft (not soggy)

I can't help but guess a lot of folks are drunk/high/cranky when they order and therefore probably dole out a lot of crap to these people. We all have that drunken friend who likes to fight with everyone and anyone and rarely is it justified. If you treat someone poorly, they'll probably do the same in return. I think they deserve a medal for putting up with our bulls%*t!
Best raw oysters I have ever eaten. The horseradish mixed with the cocktail sauce was superb. This is a definite must at happy hour for .75 cent oysters and half price drinks.
Cheese steaks are good as well as the service. Staff always attentive and engaging. I wish they would have outdoor eating

My favorite bar/pub in Indy.  Outstanding overseas beer and whiskey menu and the mug freezing technique is a show in itself. The bartenders pour the best Black & Tan's in town.  Try the fish sandwich or fish and chips. Chips are homemade and perfect.  A fun bunch of people work there and the patrons are the same.  It was THE place to watch the World Cup. Cozy, authentic British pub atmosphere. Best of all, it's a non-smoking environment.  This British pub knows how to do it right.

p.s. local ownership...not a chain.

Great little bistro. Excellent service and food is very good. Had a nice Mersault here also. Overall excellent experience. Had beet and pear salad which was fantastic. Quail with apple chutney was 5 stars. Great spot

Good food. Good music (although I think the singer was faking his Irish accent). Only in Nashville will you hear a Johnny Cash song performed in Irish folk style. The fish and chips was authentic and good. The coleslaw was even handmade with fresh cabbage.

In the words of the guy in Fried Green Tomatoes, "this is the best barbecue I ever tasted". Ordered some platters to go and they did not disappoint. They were ready in 15 min and still hot even after I had biked home with them. This place had 3.5 stars when I got it I'm starting to question all the other "good" bbq I've eaten in my life. I'm from Minneapolis though so I guess that makes sense. Also the amount of food you get for the price is amazing! Really like that the platters come with sides with such a modest price and generous serving!

The pulled pork was smoky and seasoned well but what stuck out to me most was that there were these delicious caramelized blackened pieces that tasted like candy and the rest was moist and juicy. The cornbread was the best I've ever eaten. Once again, they got me with caramelization. You're not going to get a dried out corn muffin, you're going to get a delicious and moist little loaf with a sweet crispy top. The brisket was tender, moist, and had the perfect amount of fat. I've never had brisket check all of those boxes!

Go here!! Get it to go if you want, it'll still be great. If you ever consider opening a second location try Minneapolis please!

Go here!!
The food is good (I think we got the 5 and...something), but it's heavy. My husband likes the coffee also (I haven't had it). Really good for the weekend I don't care what I eat meal:)

This place is exactly what I expected. The perfect little hippy pizza spot. I was excited to see they have a vegan pizza, vegetarian and then all the traditional pizzas as well. 

Even better is you order by the slice at the counter or you can order the whole Shabang! We ordered the Night Tripper and the Earthmother! Both exceeded our expectations with a very thin crust. But the pizza was flavorful and delicious. We also got a beer with the pizza which was awesome to be able to order while we munched down some pizza! 

Only suggestion would be to have sriracha!

Great pickle bar in the back.   Food is really good. Freshly prepared.   Matzah ball soup is yummy!  Rainbow cookies are the freshest around.  

Staff is friendly, except for one rude lady behind the counter.   Don't know if I'll return -- rudeness to a customer is a big turn off.

This place is AMAZING!  You have to get past the ordinary entrance to make your way in, but the food is just fantastic.  

We ordered the bruschetta, which is on thin and slightly crispy bread topped with very fresh tasting tomato, basil, and parmesan cheese.  The portion was generous and large enough to share with our friends.

We then ordered the highly recommended buffalo chicken pizza.  The pizza is perfectly composed with cheese, toppings, and garlic on a crust that was chewy but crunchy and just heavenly!  We followed this with the Nutella crepes, which are even better than I had imagined they would be.

We will definitely be taking family and friends to this little gem.  Great service, wonderful food, and very close to our house!
Love this place. Try the cafe for lunch. It has yummy daily selections

I order the same thing every time. "Route 44 Frozen Peach Lemonade." I have yet to receive one. Sometimes I get the correct size but not frozen or not peach, sometimes I get the wrong size with the correct drink. I really appreciate the convenience on my way to work, but it's getting to be obnoxious, and I never have time to wait for a new one to be made. Two stars because I like the taste of all of my drinks thus far.

I lived in Europe for a year in the past and have traveled back there since - Crave has that European feel to it when you walk in. The couple that works there is very friendly and efficient. I tried their chai latte and had one of their sandwiches - they were excellent. I'm going to go out of my way to eat/drink there because I'm tired of the chains in town and the artificial greetings you get there. Crave is a great place to stop and dine and enjoy a real cup of coffee, chai, etc... - I recommend this place with no hesitations. I prefer to support the local businesses in town and Crave gets my vote!
I heard the food was good here and I was not disappointed! I got their Shoyu bowl and my husband had their Volcano bowl and they were both amazing! We'll definitely be back.

I must say that the steak was good. If you are the kind of person who judges a dining experience on good food and lots of it, this is for you. I found the dining room to be rather crowded, poorly lit, noisy and the decor was the definition of tacky. If bigger makes everything better, they drive that home by guided group tours of the kitchen and wine cellar emphasizing that it is BIG and that somehow that translates to good. The wine cellar is huge yes, but again what does that do for me? All I see is that they buy wine in huge quantities and probably get really great prices. Good for them (profit) but what's in it for me? The tour of the kitchen shows that it is huge and has lots of busy, sweaty people working very hard and very fast. I happened to glance over and see a rather small woman bending over a huge bowl of salad and reaching in almost up to her armpits in an effort to toss the salad. I don't know if I really needed to see that. At the end of the tour I fully expected to be dumped out into a gift shop a la Universal Studios. Instead, you get to go upstairs for dessert. By this time I felt like I was run through a carnival sideshow, not an intimate gourmet dining experience that featured a creative and inventive chef that I would have liked.

People rave over this place and if you are looking for the standard "steakhouse" kind of place and you are of the mind that bigger is always better then this is for you.

While visiting my sister today, we were at that point where we either needed food now, or we were going to have to skip lunch, because we would ruin our dinner.  My wife started looking on Yelp for places near my sister and saw Taco Caballito.  A place they went to and we saw their reviews online too.  Mixed reviews, but we decided to give it a shot.  

The staff were helpful and we both went with the sampler and a double order of fish tacos.  I ate the Carne Asada taco first, because I heard complaints from people about that.  Was decent.  Not amazing, but not bad either.  I decided to eat the fish taco next, to not let the crispiness get soggy.  Loved the flavor of this.  Took a bite of the coconut shrimp next, since I wanted that Banh Mi for the end.  Knew that would be the best...  I was wrong...  That coconut Shrimp taco has the best bite of the day.  It's always a good time when you get that magical wow factor from a bite of food.  I then jumped to the Banh Mi, which was good, but I felt missed some of that Banh Mi flavor I love.  That pickled onion flavor really didn't come out for me.  

I'd be back.  When, no idea, since I don't live in the state, but we enjoyed ourselves.  I feel the price was good for what we got.  I saw something that said two bites, but why would you want to do that?  I could probably fit an entire one in my mouth, but I wouldn't be happy about it.  Savor those flavors.  

My main complaint is that I don't want two of a taco.  I want to be able to order just one.  I'd get the Brussel sprouts, next.  Not sure if I want to get two of those...  I'd also go Al Pastor next.  Love that style and would want to try pork here.  Even if we can't just get one, we'd still split a bunch of them.

I've been here a handful of times mostly for dinner. I've ordered salad, a limited time offer (LTO) German dinner, seafood pot pie, and other dishes. They've all been delicious and you can't go wrong.

The atmosphere is comfortable and modern. The service has also been mostly positive. I recommend Iron Hill as a standard in your rotation if not the default if you're a local.

Of course, don't forget to check out their beer selection and enjoy a flight. Like their LTO dishes, they also have seasonal beers. Yum! Always a reason to come back to check out what's brewing at Iron Hill.

Great for intimate or large group settings, or even flying solo at the bar. They also have outdoor seating..Which admittedly gets a bit loud with all of the traffic on Bridge St.

They are a PA local business.

My boyfriend and I have been to the new crush cakes 4 times since it opened. and I have to say I am sooo excited for this gem to be in Isla Vista. Each time I went I got the breakfast skillet, it was just too good to get anything different. My boyfriend got the lox bagel and also a breakfast sandwich which he was impressed with. I don't really care for much of the iv food places but obviously we like it if we have been back 4 times now. 

   The service is great here as well. the owner is super nice and for our first visit she gave us a free cup cake. My boyfriend came in another time and got a coffee and since they were out of whipped cream (btw the whipped cream is home made and delicious) he got another free cupcake. 

Great food, great service and I definitely happy crush cakes has come to iv!

My first time here and it was typical of all franchise restaurants- salty, salty, salty.  The meal looked better than the taste.  I don't know why so much salt is put on the food before serving, after all there is a salt shaker on the table.  The shrimp was overwhelmed by the salt, wish it were better.  The bread and service was great.
Always a solid place to eat and drink. With no reservation and 2 people there usually seems to be a space to squeeze in. Food is a bit oversold on menu but tasty non the less.

This place is really cool. Immediately once you walk in, the interior decoration and cute vintage nick nacks take you to a whole other world! It's a very nice destination for a "food journey." The food was very beautiful and you can tell that they put a lot of thought into their menu, but tbh, I didn't really like the taste. I'm pretty certain this was completely my fault though because I hate cheese and I forgot to ask for my food with no cheese. 

I know. 

Other than that, I would highly recommend visiting this amazing place! Even if you just go to try it out and end up not really enjoying the food, I think it's worth it.

If I could give Grace Meat + Three 6 stars, then I would be happy to do so.

Service was friendly and professional, food was absolutely incredible, atmosphere is welcoming and decor is top-notch.

You're missing out if you don't check this place out!

Interesting menu - tater tots with short ribs and Sirachi? - and good choices in beer.  Food quality was good. Place was lit up like an office building in the bar area, but otherwise ambiance is OK.  Will be back.

I know I know, everyone has their favorite pizza spots, and everyone also fancies themselves a pizza expert based on some form of "credentials" that often center around where you reside or have past resided. 

I haven't been to the Philly Tacconelli's location and since there's this location in Maple Shade, I frankly don't feel the need to! This pizzeria makes a delicious pie that'll be as good as any, even in our overlooked and disrespected pizza locale that is South Jersey. 

The crust is crispy with a black char on the bottom, but it doesn't taste "burnt." You can taste the chunks of fresh tomato in the red sauce (I'll have to try a white pie next). The toppings are high quality, they don't recommend going with more than 3 because of how thin the crust is. 

I went with a red provolone pie and my mom had a red "formaggio" (a blend of mozz, provolone and Asiago I think). We both had mushrooms, she had black olives and I had sweet sausage and onions. 

Frankly, the provolone can't be beat! While the formaggio was good, the sharpness of the provolone really comes through. I'd consider ordering a plain red provolone, it's good enough to not need toppings!

I won't say they're generous with the toppings but as you can see, it's "enough" to complement the delicious ensemble of crust, sauce and cheese.
