2 pies to go were ready in 20 minutes. The damage for the 2 pies and 2 slices of cannoli cake was $53, and yes, that's cash only. You'll probably be able to eat a slice more than you normally would, this is a true thin crust. 

Not cheap, get dominos medium 2 topping for $5.99 if you want that. If you want quality and a pizza that'll stand up to any pizza snob joints in NYC (yes, I've waited "on line" for a few of them), then come to tacconelli's in maple shade. 

I'll update on the cannoli cake later  I'm too full right now.

Ate at the west end location may times during pandemic and it was very good.  Tonight ate at the gulch and the food was over salted, over peppered, and way overpriced.  The ramen noodles were as if they were from a dried noodle pack.  The pork in the ramen was cold and the broth over peppered and salted with no taste. The edamame was way over salted. The bao buns used to be a slab of pork now they are  like an over salty sloppy joe. The boba tea was warm. For 3 people cost us $140 and I still left a 20% tip for a total of $170 only because it's not the wait staffs fault. I suggest the owner quit responding to all reviews ( bad and good) with the same generic response 'thank you for the review...." and listen to your customer.

I was here yesterday I, ordered Togo, I am on a diet and it was my cheat day and I was craving pizza! I just moved and I'm about 5 mins from Proof, and I saw that they offered a cauliflower crust, so I ordered there family meal to have lunch and dinner for the next day. It include 2 huge salads, and two pizzas. The mushroom pizza was fantastic, not too many mushrooms but a perfect amount and the flavors on this pizza was soo great. The perfect fix for a craving! Even with my healthy homemade ranch, it just added that touch too make it worth the extra 10 min workout! 

Eat Local! 

Oh and the staff was fantastic I called in and she came right out And brought my meal! Everything was hot and fresh!

I love Sarku Japan. This is the only place I get my chicken teriyaki. But the plus side is now they have sushi. Now I don't know to get the meal or the chicken teriyaki roll. When I lived in New Jersey they had sushi but when I got down here the Sarku didn't have it yet. I'm so glad they do. Now I don't have to go far for my sushi and it's delicious. If you are in the mall don't forget to try the sushi. Great price and taste great!!
its the worst restaurant I have never seen before! The boss and the servers are sooooooo rude!!!!!

Ordered on GrubHub. Bacon burger, Cheese steak, fries. 

Delivery was fast, Roughly 30 minutes.. . Burger was great. cheese steak was bleh.. Its wasn't even chipped steak. It was one
 thin slab of meat??? It's what I'd expect from ordering a cheesesteak in San Diego, NOT PHILLY...   Wont be a return customer.

This was by far, one of the best meals I've had in my life. The decor is beautiful and our server, Cati, was just as beautiful of a person! She was so knowledgeable in wine and food pairing and was so sweet. We tried the apple and squash bisque on the fall taster menu, amazing! A bottle of Chateau Gillette Bordeaux paired perfectly with the Pork chop garnished with pickled blueberries and fried onions. The food is definitely worth the price- and thankfully my father treated me tonight. 100% recommend and ask for Cati :)

Egh....Service was great. The food is not as good as what Bobecks use to be. We paid $8 for onion rings and there were only 7 or 8 rings. The French Dip really had no flavor nor did the dip. The chippers were good. The salad was good. We paid $54 for 3 people (2 beers included). Little pricey for what we had. ‍

What a classy place! I am a big fan of their oysters and whiskey drinks. Would definitely go here again. The only reason I took off one star is because the menu is kind of limited and we sat at a high top table, which got uncomfortable after the first hour. Also, try their happy hour specials - oysters are only $1 each and the drinks are pretty affordable for the atmosphere.

Awesome place! Great service from our friendly bartenders and delicious pizza. They use non processed ingredients. And the beer selection is great. It was my first time there and will definitely be going back. Try the Central West End thin crust or any of their deep dish pizzas made with cornmeal crust. Loved it!

What people say about the wait is totally true; we trotted in on a Sunday morning, and were seated immediately upon entering the restaurant. Everything was going quite well, until we were not waited (not even a drink order) on for 25-30 minutes... pretty bad when waiters are just passing by without care.

I am wondering what the waiters are doing this whole time; other people seat you, bring out your food, and clean up your table... what else do these people have to do?  I hardly saw any of them out on the floor the entire time we waited.

Anyway, after two other tables were seated, we asked one of the waiters that was evidentially not ours to snag our waiter.  In the meantime, another table was seated right next to us, and was waited on immediately.

We took our business elsewhere at this point.  If you are going to seat someone, you need to at least acknowledge their existence before a half hour has elapsed.  I was giving this place a little leeway because of the expectations coming in... and I hate to be one of those "one-star" people when everyone else seems to be giving it good reviews.

I would have liked to try the food, the food that everyone was getting around us looked quite good.

Sorry Yelpers, this place is a dud.

The Four Seasons generally delivers and this time it's no exception. 

First, the cons:  it's expensive. $$$$.  Luckily we stayed for the night at the resort so we had a free welcome drink.

The pros:  Everything we ordered were good. The service is on point and efficient (as always). At the tides bar, get a pre-dinner drink and chill out at the aquarium bar counter. Pretty cool!  

Food recommendations:
Lobster truffle pasta (you can get the half-portion or full entree!) - my favorite!
The pork chop (SO MOIST!!!)
The grilled octopus
The steak tartare 
The calamari (at the bar) - my favorite calamari EVER.

I enjoyed my experience at this restaurant. The outdoor seating was very comfortable and my old fashioned drink with the heaters made it very comfy. I was led to this restaurant by a customer I did some plumbing work for and this place did not disappoint. Definitely give the duck a try but everything was perfectly prepared.

Went back to Sama Sama for the first time in two years, and I must say they are just as amazing as back then! 

Signature Wings - Their wings are fried and coated with an addicting tamarind sauce which has a very evident palm sugar caramelization taste the works brilliantly with the sauce and encapsulates the bold essence of Southeast Asian cuisine. The wings were tender yet crisp and very flavorful as expected. If you're in Santa Barbara, these wings better be on your bucket list, they are just that good. (A+)

Krupuk & Sambal Trio - Another excellent dish from Sama Sama is their $5 trio of sambal served with garlic chips! Fried shrimp chips in this style being one of my favorite childhood snacks, I am really thrilled to see this dish elevate the snack into a gourmet side highlighting a core staple of Indonesian food as well. My personal favorite was the sweet and savory peanut sauce, but the tomato-based sambal and the spicy chili sambal worked well for the dish as well. Really excellent dish overall! (A)

Coconut Saffron Mussels - $24 nets you this giant bowl of large mussels! Steamed in a coconut saffron broth with white wine and lots of herbs, this captures the fresh aroma and taste of Southeast Asian food! The mussels were tender and paired very well with the abundance of herbs. Additionally, it's served with some sesame sourdough toast that is incredibly amazing, especially to soak up that flavorful broth! Honestly, this dish is perfect. (A+)

Broccolini Tofu - This is a really interesting vegetarian dish at Sama Sama with every component cooked well -- broccolini is tender and crisp, and tofu is crisp on the outside and soft on the inside. However, I feel like there is something missing from the dish. I could see these ingredients pairing well with a noodle dish, but as a side, its an odd direction, I think because the tofu is a bit out of place. The dish was well seasoned and tasty though, maybe on the salty side. (B)

Kue Gula Merah - This is a palm sugar cake with fresh pineapple ice cream, topped with a rum caramel sauce and sprinkled with shortbread. Honestly, the dessert is so photogenic on all fronts, making it too pretty to eat. As for the taste, the cake is sweet and moist and complemented by the sour ice cream and crunchy shortbread cookies. I think, if anything, the ice cream is on the very sour side, which is unexpected and could use more sugar. Otherwise, the dessert has a really nice taste that captures the blend of SE Asian food with western fine dining! (A)

Overall, really thrilled with my experience at Sama Sama yet again, especially the high quality service, and will definitely be returning :)

My twin sister has been to @bluescitydeli twice and in her opinion they make the best Italian Beef Sandwich she has had. Well, I needed to taste one for myself. I do think it is one of the best ones I have tasted outside of the #chicago area (and Portillo's in various states). The bread is Fresh, the Beef is super tender,  the Broth had a good flavor, and the sweet and hot peppers were delicious. So will say if I want Italian Beef in St. Louis, this is the spot! #bluescitydeli #italianbeef #stlfood #stlfoodscene #chicagofood #stl #stlfoodie #stlmetrofoodie

Eh... I've come here before and tried the nachos and the taco salad, which were good! But to be honest, you only go here if you are craving Chipotle and too lazy to go to Metairie or Elmwood. Alas, I got a veggie burrito bowl today. It was extremely skimpy and more expensive than Chipotle. The worst part of all that made me feel the need to write this review?

EXTREMELY salty. Shockingly salty. I have never been to a restaurant and had this level of salt in the food EVER. It was really, really gross. Be warned... I've been chugging water trying to rehydrate myself.

The food here is always great. After moving to Reno, and searching for a new favorite Mexican restaurant, I think La Fuente is it. The service is always great and food is pretty reasonably priced. The chips and salsa are really good as well!

This Was an exceptional experience. You have to be pretty flexible and adventurous to participate in amigo where there is no menu. However, the rewards are well worth the risk. Every single course was exquisitely prepared. The seafood was fresh, the crawfish etoufe  was the best I have ever had, the crabcakes were made in the true tradition of Maryland crab cakes, the vegetables were farm to table and amazingly fresh and tasty. We met some incredible people around the dinner table.  If you are looking for a unique and memorable dining experience served by people who are passionate about the food they serve, this is the place for you. I highly recommend it!

After waiting for weeks my daughter and I went to Cake bake for her birthday. We had a 1:00 reservation. Upon arriving they asked if the entire party was there and I told them my daughter was on her way. They asked me to wait until she got there to be seated. She arrived in a few minutes and I let them know. Still was told we had to wait. There were at least three two top tables in sight as well as larger tables. There were lots of people waiting and not as many eating. Finally, we were seated outside at 1:28 where there was literally one table filled. The rest were open. We were greeted by our waitress ordered drinks and looked at the menu. We decided to order immediately as my daughter had to get back to work. I ordered coffee with my salad. Wasn't asked if I wanted cream or sugar but no big deal. I asked for cream and sugar when the waitress returned,  which she brought with no spoon. Had to fish a chunk of sugar out the bowl with my fork. (obviously the training is lacking). We both ordered the Green Goddess salad with chicken which was great but $20?? My daughter ordered a cappuccino which never came. When she asked the waitress she replied - Oh they didn't bring it out yet? Again that's her job to keep track, but really not her fault for lack of training. The desserts were very good but only gave 3 stars because of the service. Whatever iPad app they are using to seat people is inefficient and the staff needs to be trained properly. The hostesses seemed disorganized with no clear way of following up with guests for their table. Everyone had to keep checking back with them.  Overall disappointed after all the hype about the place. Total incongruity to have a place so fabulously decorated with good food and really bad service. :(

The freshest, best tasting sushi I have ever had! The rice is a must have take home snack! Service is ok, and the restaurant is not fancy, but you quickly forget all of that once you take your first bite! 

try the banana roll and the kyoto roll! WOW! 

Richard

www.RichGetz.com
Awesome!!!! It was amazing but pricey for brunch. I would recommend to go when you see they have specials!

You might as well go to Wendy's.  I mean, the Company Burger tastes just like Wendy's, but Wendy's is a much better value and can be made to order.  Really, for $8.50, it's ridiculous that you can't get lettuce, tomato or anything other than the dreaded American cheese placed on your burger.  Also, the fountain drinks are ridiculously expensive.  No, never again.

Being a Florida Cracker, I've had tons of bbq and this place is authentic Florida Cracker bbq and the best I've ever had in my life! My husband brought home chicken, brisket, pork, sausage, ribs, baked beans, and cole slaw. 

There is no rival for the taste of each and every one of these items!!! This owner knows what he's doing!!! The meat is perfect and moist and the taste is just absolutely...well, PERFECT! The bbq sauce is just spicy and sweet enough, but not overwhelming, and it tastes great! The baked beans are not your typical baked beans and you will be pleasantly surprised by them as they are delicious!

My husband didn't realize they had smoked cabbage or he would've definitely brought some of that home to me too. I can't wait to try that and the smoked mullet the next time around! 

For all the food he brought home, we have enough for two meals for three people and it was only $40. You just can't beat that for the quality of bbq you are getting here!

We are currently rolling around our house so full it's ridiculous and already can't wait to eat the rest of it later!!

This is my guilty fast food pleasure.  I disagree with the political positions of corporate management but their breakfast burritos rock.  Waffle-cut fries are addictive.  And the staff is, by fast food standards, in a class by themselves.  You actually feel welcomed.  I've never encountered a surly employee.  The owner is frequently on-site which may account for the service level.

Fantastic little coffee shop and market with wonderful people. Checked this place out with some girlfriends when we stayed the weekend and LOVED the iced brewed coffee with coconut milk. Great selection of wine and specialty beers among other fun food items. Would go back in a heartbeat!

My husband and I really enjoyed this place. 

Fabulous Frank from the Inn at East Beach recommended this place and we had a coupon for a free appetizer which sealed the deal. The location is right on the harbor and it all of the servers dressed up for Halloween. 

The vibe was very friendly and the service was good. 

We thought the food was great. We had the calamari for our free appetizer (spicey yogurt dip was yummy). I had the clam chowder in bread bowl: very tasty but a little watery -- we had the best chowder in Boston... it's hard to beat. He had the ahi tuna tacos which were sooo good. 

Overall it's a nice place
Best fried chicken I ever had.  Plus the fixings were incredible.  Mac n cheese, greens, fries, beans.  So good.

The service and staff were fantastic! Greeted me and my wife and were very polite and attentive. I ordered a roast beef sub, my wife got a turkey sub. The amount of meat and vegetables (L,T,O)  and salt, pepper, mayo were fair portions. Why 2 stars? The meat quality was meh for the roast beef, and poor for the turkey- turkey actually looked fake. Both meats were bland- my wife threw her sub out- first time I ever saw her do that. I was really, really hungry so I finished mine. We're used to Boar's Head quality meat and not the cheap cuts used by Largo Subs. The subs were expensive, too- $20.50 for 2 subs!  Should be listed as $$ and not $.  In hindsight I probably should have gone with a gyro or steak and cheese sub, but won't be back now. Too bad, as the people were really nice and I love subs.

Five friends and I came here for a birthday dinner. We enjoyed ourselves and ended up staying well after all other patrons had left the dining room, and the server never once tried to rush us or pressure us to leave. She was extremely professional and patient!

I ordered the bass with potatoes, celeriac and pesto, which was delicious and the perfect portion size. My friends weren't as crazy about their meals, but everyone agreed the food was high quality and the service even better. Highly recommended.

Let me tell you about the red snapper entree at atchafalaya! Straight goodness to the core! Fried to perfection coupled with greens and a unique version of dirty rice! I also had the gumbo which was the best of my 5 day trip. It's very rare that I experience food like I had there. With a group of great people I met in NOLA, we had dinner here for our last night in the city. We all ordered different meals. The shrimp and grits I tasted, and it was equally amazing to my entree. Someone else ordered the fried chicken dish that was light but also full of LA flavor. The vegetarian in the crew ordered the risotto and I have to admit she said it was just okay. I'm not a fan of risotto so I didn't try that dish. Overall, I love this place! I couldn't give 5 stars because my server was not so great. Everyone else from the host to the guy from Jersey showed that wonderful southern hospitality. So happy I left the French Quarter and found this place!
Great relaxed beach environment.
Good authentic chinese food in Saint Pete. Kinda pricey but it's served family style. They also serve a delicious desert soup at the end of your meal.

Best bakery in the area. Best donuts, puts dunkin to shame.  The cakes are awesome.  Everything is freshly made.  I found this place randomly as it is one of the only bakeries opened on Sunday morning.  

I highly recommend

Let me start off by saying this was the worst experience i have ever had. It really deserves no stars. I came here and ordered the spicy Tuna with a few of their specialty rolls. The rolls were mediocre at best, and to top it all off i almost choked on them due to the nasty fish scales left in the sushi. I wanted to yell at the management but it didn't seem anyone with that type of authority was around. As for service it was piss poor. I was treated like garbage and it seemed that i was only annoying my server so i didn't bother asking for much. All in all I hope everyone stays away unless you like fish scales in your sushi. Will not be going back ever.

Just went back yesterday. Some guy is complaining about how long his food is taking while I'm in line and I ask him and he says it's been 35 minutes. 

I get to the front and I ask the girl (Melissa) how long it'll take. She says 20-25 minutes. I say this guy here has been waiting for 35, are you sure? She assures me it will not be longer than 25 minutes. I would've gone to ikes if she said it'd take longer than that, and note, ikes was closing in 25 minutes. So I think whatever I'll wait. 

27 minutes later, I go ask and they're still 14 orders away, and when I remind her of what she said, she says "it hasn't even been 25 minutes" to which I reply it had been 27 minutes. The waiting isn't an issue, it's just that she assured me multiple times I'd be 20-25 minutes, and had she said otherwise, I would've gone to ikes, which was now closed. 

It took a total of 50 minutes to get the food. Lol Hana get your shit together.

I've been having a bunch of day long trainings near City Hall and so my coworkers and I end up at Liberty Place every time.  Every time I think, "I'm going to try something new."  And every time I end up ordered from Great Wraps because they are just so tasty!  The first two days I got there jalapeno fries, which are so delicious!  The last two times I got the buffalo chicken wrap and it is extremely tasty.  I like that you can customize what veggies you put on your wraps.  I am a huge fan of this place and I will probably go again tomorrow when we are back for yet another day long training.  They've made a fan out of me!

Been here a couple times, today I went for lunch with my girlfriend. I got the fried fish with black beans and yellow rice, and an egg on the side. It was delicious, perfectly cooked, egg was perfectly cooked, and a very nice portion size. My girlfriend got the churrasco steak, which looked beautiful and tasted as good as it looked. I'm giving four stars because the service is slightly underwhelming. They seemed understaffed for the lunchtime rush, and that's probably the cause of the lack of timeliness at times.
Waited forever to be greeted, then surly service.  We happily left without getting anything.  Recommend you avoid this venue. Oh....and they smoke inside which is nasty.

As far as neighborhood 'bodegas' go, Citi Market is as good as it gets. Clean, open, and airy, they have an ideal selection of everyday basics, fresh produce, and healthy (and not so healthy) snacks, with a focus on the organic. 

Amazing vegetarian/vegan options, including tofutti for bagels (halle-freakin'-lujah), and pre-packaged Singapore noodles that I crave on a biweekly basis. 

Citi Market has saved the day (or dinner) on many occasions, when I am just too exhausted or busy to cook. It's a bit pricey, but the convenience is worth it.

First time customers for this wonderful sushi place! We were pleasantly surprised with the delicious food and great service. The sushi is wonderful! But if you're not a sushi fan they have other stuff which makes this place great! The dessert was so good as well! Wonderful wonderful place! Will dine in again.
Great food and atmosphere!   Lamb chop dinner, salsa and gyros are fantastic!  Recently expanded and a great patio for warmer weather.

I've lived around this area for awhile now, and finally tried this coffee spot...and I'm so glad I did!  It was adorable inside with lots of space to boot up a computer and work. I ordered a peppermint mocha latte and was very happy with it!  It's also more affordable than Starbucks and just as yummy. The service was super friendly and quick. I'll definitely be back in the near future!

Meh... it's taco bell... They were nice. The food tasted like any other Taco Bell. I finally tried the Cool Ranch Doritos Taco... since I read that it was responsible for huge growth at Taco Bell and something like 15,000 jobs being added in one year. It was not as bad as I expected it to be, but not great.

Love their food and the staff is always friendly and courteous.  My wife loves the Buffalo Chicken gyro and I always lean towards the Greek Burger.  The standard fries as a side are a must.  We eat here about once a month, mostly carry out.  It's a hidden gem that I believe is ran by a family.  Hope more people find this location and it's great food and service!

Quaint place with great cocktails! I've really been loving spicy drinks as of late and they had a fantastic jalapeño margarita.

Walking in I was greeted by the chef in the open kitchen design and the three servers. Friendly, relaxed vibe and with it being a Tuesday and extremely rainy, it wasn't busy at all.

I tried the Mac & Cheese with bbq pulled pork. It had smoked Gouda cheese and a homemade bbq sauce. It was tasty but super rich! I shared a decent size portion with my two cousins and the picture I included is what was left! It will easily feed you 3x.

My cousins loved their rigatoni and burger, too. With it being such a small room, I'd highly recommend reservations on the weekends. I'd definitely come back next time I'm in the city.

Outside of France, this is hands down the best breakfast / pastry spot in the US. Forget all of the other flashy stuff in NOLA -- if you want real food... real breakfast... real croissants... this is the spot.

On our way to Mckendree for a concert, we found Loomy's on Yelp. Based on reviews, we had to try. Note, it's quiet farmland area. 

Burgers & fries were yummy! Service was wonderful. They seemed happy to be there! 

We will return! It made our top 5 burger list !

Stopped in for the first time tonight and was pleasantly surprised at just how good this place is! I am a huge fan of street food, especially from Central America, and El Merkury did not disappoint. Fresh and delicious food, great horchata. My only "complaint" is that portion sizes were a bit smaller than I would have liked. I should have ordered some sides with my taquitos, but now I know for next time!

Friday night dinner,  made a reservation on yelp,  because it's a small place. Live jazz singer set the mood perfectly.  Great wine selection and fantastic food.  The Manzo Brasato was simply exquisite! Highly recommend Cuvee 103, i will definitely be back. Hidden jem!

I have never liked sushi.... EVER. 
I've had multiple bad experiences and figured that I just wasn't a "sushi person".

WAS I WRONG!! 

I went to Peters and felt like giving sushi one more try since everyone else in my life swears that it's delicious and that Peter's is the best around.
I ordered the volcano rolls and shared them with my sister.... but honestly... I wish I didn't have to share them!
It was sooo good! 

I now realize I was getting sushi from places that didn't know what they were doing. It wasn't fresh and Peter's knows what they're doing!

I'm a sushi person now and no one is more surprised than I am.

Nom Wah has the best dim sum in Philly.  It might not be in Chinatown and kinda in the middle of no where but some dishes are good, really good.

The steamed sui mai especially the Pork Sui Mai is really good.  The Shrimp Sui Mai is a close second.  Either dish best with the sweet soy dipping sauce.

The steamed snow pea shrimp filling is delicious but it's kinda wrapped with a glutinous wrapper that is far too thick and detracts from the combined bite.  Of the steamed shrimp dishes this is ok but a better option might be the steamed shrimp dumpling Har Gow.  The exterior wrapper of the Har Gow is thinner in relation.

The Fried Egg Roll is wrapped with an egg and fried but sometimes a bit too oily.  I'd say order this dish if you've got a party to share with.  Just half of the Fried Egg Roll is enough for one.

All the variations of steamed rice crepes are great.  They used to have a dish with a combination of steamed pork on the bone on top of rice crepes.  I used to order this often but they've since taken this off the menu.  This dish also sometimes comes out a bit cold which is odd,...

The Beef Chow Fun was not great here even though the waitress recommended it.  It was far too oily and thankfully there was a pot of tea available to wash it all down.  I do not recommend this dish at all.

They used to also have a sampler dish of either steamed or fried favorites but they've since taken it off the menu which is super irritating.  It was the perfect opportunity for one to order and not be burdened by having to eat 3 or 4 more of the same bite.  I really wish they would reconsider and bring this back but I'm not holding my breath on that.

If Nom Wah was closer to the heart of Chinatown I think it would be harder to get a table and I'd be sad but as it stands I'm happy I don't have to wait long for a seat when I need my Dim Sum.

After 3 attempts to make it here we finally made it on try #4. First try I got sick the night before. The next time we were snowed out as we couldn't make it over Donner Summit to Reno. 3rd time it turns out they were closed over Xmas. Finally made it up a few nights ago. We sample a lot of Reno restaurants every time we come up from over the hill in California. Tonight it was the H Steakhouse. 

Have to agree with everyone else. Very old school. Almost a complete male staff in traditional suit and tie attire serving all of your needs. We started with the shrimp cocktail which was very yummy in a very spicy tequila sauce. Caesar salad made table-side with fresh ingredients was great. We shared a Chateaubriand for 2.  A bit overdone. We requested medium rare, but it looked more like medium well. Comes with an assortment of 5 veggies and not the usual one or 2 and you don't have to pay extra for the veggies like you do at some other steakhouses.

Decent wine list but nothing like the wine list at the Harrah's steakhouse in Vegas which is ridiculous. Best deal for wine this month is the Rodney Strong 2008 cab which they are featuring for half off. Normally at $120 , but going for only $60. We were shopping at the Reno Costco the next day and found the exact same wine for sale for $63.00. Definitely get this wine while they are still featuring it for this price. 

The better half ordered the grand marnier souffle for desert. We almost never see anyone make souffles any more for dessert so she was thrilled to have this. I ordered a Port and we finished off dinner with 2 coffees. 

You can subtract 10% off your bill if you have a Harrah's Total Rewards card . If you don't have one, sign up for one upstairs at the promo desk. It was worth at least $20 for us in savings. On top of that they comped me the port which was another $10. 

Overall a grand experience. Not cheap as the highly rated Sterling Steakhouse at the Silver Legacy is comparable and everything is about 10% less there, but with the Total Rewards card, the price is about a draw. Only drawback was that the service was sometimes a bit short. We tried to strike up a conversation a few times with the waiter, but he was too much in a rush to get to the next table to have time to chat at all. Perhaps if we had come later in the evening the waiter would've been a bit more laid back. Too bad. 

I'd give the  place 4 1/2 stars only for the occasional brusque attitude of the staff, but otherwise a definite 5 star restaurant.
Drive-thru order of the impossible combo with no pickles.  Well i got extra pickles.  Hamburger was still good..but better for me with no pickles
This is hands down the best sandwich I've had outside the city. Porchetta and cutlet sandwiches are next level. Staff is great .

We have driven by but never stopped until today.  Authentic feel and great atmosphere.  The food was not as good as other Thai we have had at Sa Wad-Dee Thai Restaurant.  The garlic shrimp tasted bland.  The Waiter did not refill drinks.  Portions were small.  We left sad and utterly disappointed.

I recommend going somewhere else.  Not good BBQ at all. I was very disappointed in the food and overall experience at this establishment.  I just don't see how they have the high quality reviews they do. Brisket was barely warm, dry, and would have been flavorless if not for being smothered in seasoning before served. The ribs were tough and chewy and some of the worst I've had.

I did what everybody does. Cheese steak off...

As soon as I got into Philly, my first meal had to be a cheese steak. I think I have to say both places are tied.

My pluses of Geno's:

-Tender steak and really juicy
-Spicy condiment accessible: vinegar/chili's

Negs:
-Thin amount of meat. Get more from Pat's
-Bread isn't toasted
-I might be a minority on this, but I ain't feelin' the wiz and onions. Just too overwhelming and plastic tasting. I prefer provolone!

I have been a faithful customer of Dominick's for years. During Covid I have regularly ordered take out. The food is always 4 Stars but the service often has issues. On my most recent take out order I placed the order online. My Fettuccine was ordered with chicken and extra sauce. Once i arrived home there was no chicken and little sauce. There was no marinara sauce for the garlic knots. This happens, i understand this. When I called asking for assistance I received none. I was told by the hostess and the person in charge of the restaurant that they filled the order as they received it. That was all they had to say. There was no customer service. I had driven an hour round trip for fettuccini noodles with a small amount of sauce on them. The error was either in the ordering system or the kitchen. The customer service here needs to improve for me to return. Really disappointed in my once a week takeout treat.

Disclaimer: I am not a member. However, I was seriously considering getting one if I had an awesome experience.

Obviously, great cocktails and tater tots. So fluffy, hot, and melt-in-your-mouth truffle heaven. Definitely get those. 

However, the entree plates were pretty underwhelming for the price point. We got the Amish chicken and pistachio-crusted duck, but both were lackluster. Absolutely no wow-factor at all. Everything was served rather cold and their foie gras with the gelatinous "chicken sausage" left me wondering if it was some kind of culinary joke.

Intimate decor and ambiance, but the windows were quite drafty so I felt cold the entire evening. That was rather unpleasant. 

Given the price point and business model, I feel the staff could use more training. My waitress was friendly and kind, but she wasn't very knowledgeable about the menu. In addition, the staff were dressed too casually. The male staff wore button-up shirts at least, but the female staff were basically in what could pass for pajamas. Management must be going for some laid-back work culture, but it doesn't jive with the atmosphere. I don't know how I feel about dining at a place where the customers are (mostly) dressed to the nines while the servers are dressed like students. If I'm shelling out my hard-earned dough for a luxury dining experience, I expect impeccable service. (This reminds me of where I've had the best service by far in St. Louis: Sydney Street Cafe and Tony's)

Bottom line: If you're looking for great drinks, you can easily go to Taste. I entertained the idea of getting a membership just for the tater-tots, but I'll pass.

Love love love this bakery everything i've tried has been delicious! Their Italian rum cake and chocolate mousse cakes are moist and tasty. The cannolis are super good they will even pipe them fresh if you ask. The almond flavored cookies are all AMAZING seriously the best cookies I've ever had. I will definitely be using them for all my bakery needs in the future the staff is nice they could be better and smile and talk more especially the baker whom kind of ignored my compliments but thats not a big deal to me some people just dont like to chit chat the first day i came to order a cake the young girl with curly brown hair was so kind nice and very helpful. When i went back to pick up the cake the staff wasnt smiling or cheerful nor helpful luckily i knew what i wanted. Regardless i love the products they are responsibly priced for the quality in my opinion the cakes and cookies that ive tried are way better than lochels which ive always been disappointed with the taste of the cakes there.

Garrison Deli is a very nice local deli in the neighborhood where I stayed at during my job assignment. Decided to order take out for lunch for work. I ordered the Pastrami sandwich as well as a Cuban sandwich. The pastrami was absolutely delicious.  Half pound of Pastrami with stone ground mustard and slices of pickles on rye bread. Very well complimented and the mustard gave it a great zing to it. The Cuban sandwich was also good even though the pork slices are kinda missing. If it ain't from a Cuban place the taste and form is very different however good risk taking.

Pretty decent group of people who run the show here. The beer is very good and the addition of Hop's and Hoagie's is a great move.

It can be a little tough in the winter with a large crowd as some seem to gather in front of beer counter, improves with warmer weather as outdo patio is open.

Chargrilled oysters. Don't waste your time trying anything else. As a matter of fact make it your last stop of the night. Not worth the long wait but the oysters are worth a 9pm trip before closing. Get a side of sauteed crab, drench in the butter and top on your oysters then drizzle a little lemon. Thank me later.

My bf and I were lucky enough to tag along with family who had a reservation. Definitely make one unless you want to show up as they open for dinner. 

It was 3 of our first times... so all of us got the tayim. We shared it all- of the vegetable starter dishes, we all loved the cauliflower, carrots, eggplant, and beets. The hummus and laffa were also delicious but a small portion. It seemed like we could have gotten more considering we all ordered the tayim (4 of us) but it was never offered. 

For the other dishes some favorites were the roasted carrots, halloumi, zucchini, hamachi and omg the cauliflower! Plates are definitely small and I could have gone for 3 of just cauliflower but you have to save some room for the meats! 

Of the alhaesh the chicken, lamb, and eggplant were the favorites. The mushrooms were also tasty! 

The lamb was very flavorful and disappeared first, the chicken was a small portion but perfectly cooked. We got a tiny bowl of rice pilaf- again not enough for 4 people/4 dishes.

The desserts were all different but delicious. I was surprised that my favorite was the blueberry konafi! Not a huge blueberry person but the crunchy shredded phyllo complemented it so well... I could eat that every day! The chocolate sorbet was SO rich it tasted like frozen mousse. 

Overall nothing I tasted was anything but delicious however I did actually leave a little hungry. I probably wouldn't do the tayim again and instead order a la carte but for our first visit it was nice to get a taste of the whole menu!
Good food. Dirty bathrooms. Just like all of the other restaurants in the loop. Really nice tacos though! And a cute atmosphere

Came by as this has been rated one of the best quick lunch spots in Philly.  They have two touch screen kiosks to order your meal.  It's not as fast when you have a bunch of undecided folks trying to decide what to order!  Once you do order your meal, it is pretty quick as most items are pre-made and require some assembly. 

One of the few places that I'm aware of that serves Central American food.  Lots of street vendor items like taquitos, tostadas, etc. I got the combo where I selected a taquito and a tostada with beef.  

It's an extra two bucks for the meat and the combo comes with two sides.  Taquito was crispy and not oily.  The tostada was good and I'm glad I elected the meat option. 

They have 4-5 options to choose from. I elected for the cheesy corn rice and plantain chips   Chips were perfectly crispy and nice salsa on the side. The rice was ok.  I probably would've preferred the corn on the cob, but didn't want to get messy during lunch.  

Decent place. I was still a bit hungry from the meal. Portions are a bit on the smaller end.

Revolution is HANDS DOWN my favorite fast casual taco restaurant - my first time here I decided to go for the Korean short rib after getting a suggestion from the girl behind the counter. It smelled so good that I completely forgot to take a photo before I devoured it, luckily I remembered before going for the second. Definitely the messiest of the tacos I've had here, but it's only because they're so juicy from the short rib sauce. If you're looking for something even more wallet-friendly, the Gold Angus Ground Beef and Chicken Tinga tacos are every bit as flavorful and delicious, with just as unique accent toppings. My favorite to-date, though, has got to be the BBQ Brisket. Again, a little pricier than some of the others but the flavor is unbeatable and it's so packed full that by the end of the first taco you're already full. 
Cannot wait to go back and keep trying something new every time. If you're as big a taco fan as myself, do yourself a favor and try out this delicious little gem.

Best surprise I've had in a long time.  Saw the place a couple weeks ago when we were going to sahms next door.  Finally got to try it today.  Took great care of us...beer recommendations were perfect.  Pizza really good...chorizo cheese for breadsticks also really really good.  Top to bottom they were great.  Only complaint is that they aren't closer to my house.

Went here on Memorial Day for the first time. Very good beer selection and the bartender was really helpful. I got the Houla burger which was cooked perfectly. Can't wait to go back and try some other stuff
Excellent BBQ. Pulled pork, brisket, corn bread, rolls, sauce is great, vinegar sauce is great. Clean place. quick service. A little pricey.

Brunch, bakery, massage, tortas, distilleries-- could Fletcher Place get any better? I certainly think not. Welcome to the neighborhood, Spice Box! We've been patiently waiting for you. 

I had the pleasure of chowing with Jon C. at Spice Box last week (opening week). My order consisted of the channa masala (mild chick pea stew), naan and spice rice (has garlic and a little more pizzazz than the other rice option). The food was delicious and very filling for less than $10. They also have beer and wine available at this location. If you're familiar with Rook's decor (former tenant), it is nearly the exact same but it fits Spice's style beautifully. 

One note: I'm hoping they plan to switch over to real plates (even if plastic) for their in-house orders to reduce on waste and create a more relaxed/not rushed eating experience.
Good brisket, amazing sauce, and they got some bomb Mac and cheese! My girl loves the corn bread too. Definitely recommend this place to newcomers and bbq fanatics

don't be fooled by outer appearance and never judge a book by its cover. there is a small kitchen window that you order food from in the back left of its bar where you will find one of the best seafood platters in philadelphia. it's a small family run place where you take food to go or eat at the bar. sometimes, food might take long to be done but it is absolutely worth the wait. the lady was super nice and she will cook you some seafood to perfection. be nice to her.

crab and shrimp platter with potatoes corn and broccoli was what i got for $25 and it was amazing. highly highly highly recommend it.

I ordered breakfast burrito that was supposedly already coming with home fries inside of it and asked bacon to be added to it . For my toddler son I ordered two scrambled eggs with homemade potatoes and fruit cup . 
The burrito was good but instead of couple pieces of bacon that they charged me for it was burned bacon bits in the burrito and there was no sign of home fries in it . 
My son kept spitting out the potatoes so I tried them
To see why - half of them were burned to dark black and the other ones were raw in the middle and bitter . 
 The only reason I gathered to give them 3 stars was because the service was great and the manager lady was very apologetic for potatoes when I reached out to her

After reading lots of reviews containing warnings about the long lines, I decided to go early (got there around 15 minutes before it started at 4 PM) and I had my husband meet me there instead of waiting for him to get off of work to go together. That way, my friend and I had enough time to set up our blanket and chairs and scope out all the trucks before too many people showed up. 

There were so many food trucks and different varieties of food to try! I was wondering how many dishes I could fit in my stomach before I would be compelled to stop eating! It turns out, quite a few, with some help from my husband! Here's what we tried: 

From Zia's food truck, we had the toasted ravioli. They weren't spectacular, but they weren't too bad, either, as long as you eat them while they're hot. I got them so my out of town friend could see what they were all about, since it's a St. Louis thing. 

Cha Cha Chow food truck 
- Grilled fish taco: some kind of white fish on a white corn tortilla with creamy cha cha sauce, and cilantro lime slaw. I asked the lady taking orders what kind of fish it was, but I can't remember what it was called. She said that it was similar to tilapia but with less of a fishy taste. This taco was on the small side, but it was only $3, so I think it was worth it because it was flavored well and I enjoyed it. 
- Lobster taco: butter poached lobster, lemon cream cheese sauce, salt and pepper slaw, topped with cilantro on a flash fried tortilla. This was sooooo delicious! Granted it was pricey, but come on! Lobster. Taco. Need I say more!? Try it out! 

From Guerilla Street Food... 
- Lumpia: this is a Filipino spring roll that's not fried. Rather, the wrapping is sort of like a crepe, but spongier and softer. It was filled with sauteed cabbage, carrots, and green beans and it came with a sweet dipping sauce. I thought it would be the fried kind, but I guess I read the description wrong. Nevertheless, it was delicious and I'm glad I tried it, but I'm not sure I would order it again. 
- Flying Pig bowl: slow roasted pork asado over rice with chilis, calamansi (a type of Filipino fruit), sriracha, and a slow cooked egg (technically a sous vide 1 hour egg, if you want to get all fancy). This was amazing! It was probably the dish I liked the best from everything I tried at FTF. 

From the Holy Crepe! food truck, we had the banana Nutella crepe. There's really no way you can go wrong with Nutella. There was no wait, they didn't skimp on the Nutella (yesss!), and it was a pretty decent crepe! 

Smokin' Monkey food truck 
- Shrimp lollipop: When I read that on the menu, I was perplexed and curious at the same time. I decided to get it and I liked it! It's made up of chopped shrimp that are smoked and grilled on a sugar cane skewer and served on top of a bed of some kind of slaw and yummy sauce. 
- Duck confit tacos: smoked confit duck topped with again some kind of slaw and their house-made chipotle plum jam. These were not as good as I expected. The duck was a little on the dry side and could have been cooked to retain more of the flavor. However, the jam was good and you could tell they made it. 

Drunken Pig cupcake from the Sweet Divine: It had Newcastle beer and cheddar cheese cake, cheddar and cream cheese frosting, and bacon on top. Oh em gee. So good! The cake was moist and the flavor of cheddar was not overpowering, which I was a little afraid it would be. Usually, I find that most cupcake places use too much frosting for my taste, but the Sweet Divine had a great frosting to cake ratio! Plus there were chopped up pieces of bacon on top. Seriously! What more could you ask for?! This cupcake flavor apparently helped them win on the Cupcake Wars tv show. 

Other food trucks that were there included: 
Steak Louie 
Slice Of the Hill 
Seoul Taco 
Deli on a Roll 
Completely Sauced 
Lulu's Local Eatery 
Shell's Coastal Cuisine 
Chop Shop 
Hot Aztec 
(I posted photos of their menus, so check out what they offer before you go!) 

There was also a band playing near the center of the line of food trucks. I can't remember their name, but it was nice to have some live music while wandering around getting and eating food. 

TL;DR - Go early, bring cash and something to sit on, and enjoy the music and wide variety of food truck fare! Be adventurous!

Tasty Pho might as well hire a pharmacist because it is my 'go-to' when I'm coming down with the sniffles. At the - first - sign of a cold I head directly to this place and get a bowl of Pho, load in the hoisin and Sriracha and let the phytonutrients (or was that capsaicin) go to work.

There's a hint of old school in me and I tend to gravitate to things that I know and things that I like. I'm also a Taurus but that may or may not be important at this time. Regardless, I always go for the meatball beef Pho and have never been disappointed. The aroma, the piping hot serving temperature and the consistency of the noodles are superb and satisfying.

As other reviews have mentioned, the large is huge so go easy with it and select the original size.

First a disclaimer - I don't give bad reviews. People work too hard and put too much love and effort into their businesses for some idiot like me to obviate their efforts. I will say we had a decent meal here.  The service was excellent and friendly. Some work needs to be done to get up to its sister restaurant's standards.  I'm sure in time they will get there!

Ordered two pizzas for pick up and was told it would take 40 mins.  Ready when they said it would be, walked in and picked it up quickly!  Food was delicious.  Also ordered calamari.  It was also great.  Calamari can be overdone and chewy, this was not.  Better than I expected.  Will definitely order from here again.
Most of the items I have ordered I have enjoyed. The unique cuisine and friendly service or a welcomed addition to restaurants I frequent.

When I visit a restaurant, I expect knowledgeable and attentive service. While I did receive this from managerial staff, the wait staff was less than attentive. 
When asked if we could have our chicken wings with no breading, the server pointed to the picture on the menu.. I re asked.. what is on the chicken wings  again the server referred to the picture. Third time i asked if there is any breading on the chicken wings, third time the server referred to the picture. At that times, i asked for a nutritional menu, and the server came out with managerial staff, who were able to provide answers. The server also mixed up our orders- i got my wife's steak and Visa versa.
I recommend this restaurant employ more sophisticated help who can do more than point to pictures, and be more attentive to customers needs and even more important understand basic humor. Two servers I encountered when asking for additional butter had ZERO personality.
Great food real reasonable I had the shrimp burger real good my girl had clams,fish,fried shrimp it was real good give them a try people.
I really enjoyed the restaurant in the casino.  It was a great experience for me.  The service was fantastic. I was taking here for our first date and loved it

The wait on Saturday at 1030 for 2 people was only 20 minutes. The food came out quickly and tasted so fresh and flavorful. The cafe mocha was great! Fast service and the owner was walking around to every table helping fill up waters and check in with everyone

Moist brisket. Holy moly. This place holds its own against places that I've visited in Texas... and the best part is that there wasn't even a long wait for it. I went there and ordered several pounds of brisket, hot links, pulled pork, and a number of sides, and my order was out within minutes. No mess, no hassles like you'd find elsewhere.

I know most people will use some sort of sauce with their meat. But this place doesn't need it. Trust me, the bark on the brisket was more than enough. However, I will say that their large assortment of sauces was delicious too. I was also pleased to see white Alabama sauce (comeback sauce) available too... you don't see this in too many places outside of Alabama. Friendly staff, who are attentive of your needs, was also appreciated and made my meal there wonderful.

Yes, I spent nearly $100 there. It seemed expensive when I was paying for it... but for the amount of good quality food I got, I almost felt bad that that's all I paid for it. Almost. ;)

If you're in the area, def check them out.

So I decided to give this place a try. I ordered online and picked from the choices offered online . Type of bbq sauce , I chose onions and pickles and slaw to be added to my pulled pork sandwiches. So I send my daughter to pickup our food . She brings it home promptly, the sandwiches are cold, and none of my choices were on the sandwiches! Why would they offer these choices online if they are not going to fulfill the order?! I had to send my daughter back , they said , oh well it's self serve !!!! What? Why would I order this online ? This is a really poor way to do business. Won't be going here again.

I totally agree with Sean G - "old, cold and tasteless".  All the curries tasted alike and were most definitely recycled from leftovers.  I asked the very surly waiter for another order of Naan.  He nodded and disappeared - that was the last I saw of him.  the dhal was extremely watered down.   I disagree with the others about the price - this place is overpriced for the low grade food that they serve.  I will not be returning.

I live 2 mins away from this place and do frequently enjoy their frozen delights.
The orange-cinnamon gelato is amazing and my favorite.  You can mix flavors and get it in a cup or cone.  
The place is small, but cozy.  Great for a first date, or to meet up with a friend.  
I did not rate the establishment 5 stars because they need to spend money on thicker napkins!! ---and I think it would be 5 stars if they would sell Italian desserts and cupcakes instead of muffins and salads.
More authentic delicacies please!

Service is hit or miss...they can be vacant at times...but mostly friendly...

Went to this location for Father's Day yesterday and our waiter, I wish I knew his name, was amazing. All of our food was great, my husband had fish and chips, I had the seafood feast, my daughter had the kids lobster tail, and my son the chicken tenders and corn. The only problem was my sons corn came cold; they replaced it. Aside from that, we had great service and a great meal; everything was made fresh and came out promptly from biscuits to our deserts and check. It had been 4 years since we had previously been to a red lobster, and based on this experience well more than like go back in the future. Hopefully they can keep up this good service!

We had been going to Luciano's for the 10 plus years we lived just up the hill.  It was our special place.  We made reservations only to find reserved tables but we were not seated at one.  Upon arrival I told the female waitress it was our friends birthday.  She said she would arrange for a candle. Our waiter never introduced himself and when asked if he could repeat the specials he pushed his head back and almost rolled his eyes.  When my salad came it was a small pile of iceberg lettuce and 2 small cherry tomatoes sliced in half.  Unimpressive as the salad was the soup was more broth than minestrone.  The main dish was very good.  We asked if the  dessert was fresh at which he told us it was.  NO WAY.  The tiramisu  had a raspberry sauce all over it.  Just weird, and made us think they were hiding something.  The waiter spilt a glass of water on my lap as well.  Then he forgot my dessert, cheesecake.  He said it was cooling off, whatever that means.  It came with a raspberry sauce as well and was old and cold.  When the check came he almost laid it in the remaining pool of water but I grabbed it.  This guy said he worked there 3yrs.  Seriously?  Taking our friends to an old favorite was embarrassing and expensive.  Sat April 6th 6pm res.
The food was good but what really sets this restaurant apart is the wandering magician going table to table. The marquee outside said he is Dr. Mystic.

Stopped by, after a long day for a quick drink and bite. To my surprise, it was happy hour... yay, for me!!! This place is not very vegetarian friendly, but appetizer's and margarita's were half off.
I tried a mango patron margarita, which definitely did not disappoint. The alcohol level was a bit high but I needed that, today.
 For food, we tried the southwestern eggrolls, soup and salad, and you pick two... with loaded baked potato soup and a house salad and cheese enchilada's and a chicken tostada with rice and beans.
 The food was ok for a chain restaurant, nothing to write home about. I haven't been to a Chili's in years and I kind of see why. Maybe, next time I'll just stick to drinks.

Oh boy, after a below then average experience here last time, I decided to try this diner yet again... The French Fries that came with my burger were cold, the waitress gladly brought me new ones. However she wanted to take the plate I was currently eating the burger off of, I had to ask her if I could keep it and have her bring another plate, a bit odd. There were two waitress that were incredibly loud, talking about there personnel lives, sorry, but I wasn't really interested in the boyfriends they slept with and there friends cheating on there spouses. Sorry Cherry Hill Diner, this time was the last time. 

For others that read this, I can see a Wawa and a Wendy's from my seat. I would go there instead.

I went to this place when it first opened & I was really happy with everything. My friends & I went there on taco night & had margaritas & played games. I figured this place would be very popular & do really well. 
Tonight, I went there again with a friend that has always wanted to try it out. After our waiter took our drink order (which we both just got a sweet tea), he asked to see our IDs. We were very confused because we weren't drinking? When he brought out our sweet teas, there was barely any ice in them. When you're dispensing a warm/room temperature beverage over ice, you should fill the glass with more ice. The waiter also gave us a buzzer that would tell us when our food was done & then we could go grab it from the kitchen. We were confused about that too because if we're expected to leave a tip, why do we need to grab our own food? 
I ordered the Thai boneless wings & my friend ordered the loaded fries. When our food came out (which took awhile, but we weren't in a rush so I didn't find it that big of a deal), my boneless wings really had no sauce on them & they tasted like they had been in the fryer too long. My friends loaded fries were not all the way covered with toppings & they weren't hot. It almost looked as if our food had been sitting out for awhile. 
After we received our food, we didn't see much of our waiter. I ended up having to walk up to the bar to ask for a cup of ice & a water. The bartender didn't seem to care that I was standing there. She was busy putting together another drink order for a table, but I thought what I asked
for couldve been done pretty quickly. 
I have worked in the food industry for a long time. I have trained so many employees & conducted many meetings to encourage employees to work harder & care about the business. I have found ways for businesses to grow & be the place people want to go to. This place was a big hit when it first opened, but it has really gone downhill. Not that I would ever tell someone how to run their business, but I would try to help by giving some suggestions. 
I think that the owner/s need to hold meetings with the staff (even if it has to be done in sections) to address the issues they are facing. I think the main issue is the customer service. Customer service isn't just a smiling face & friendly attitude. Customer service is also the way things are presented, continuously checking on your tables, etc. I also think "recognition" would be a great way for the owners to get their employees to work better & care more. If a customer gives a good review on an employee, the owner should recognize that employee. When someone is recognized for something they do, they will continue to be better & maybe even work harder. I thought everything tonight was done very carelessly. I think the owners should look into the proper training techniques to help out not only their employees, but their business. 
I really do not like to leave bad reviews, but I would just like to see this place turn back around.

First impressions still stand. We live only a mile away. Finally after 5 years we gave it a try today. First red flag , no a/c. Asked the owner how long has the a/c been out?  He said about a week. Could not say when it was going to be fixed. 2nd red flag, no one in there. 
3rd and final red flag ,the pizza sucks. I know the natives and Californians  have difficulty with their pizza tastes but I've had better pizza at carnivals. 
Like CNN  is fake, so is this pizza , fake pizza. Oh!  the price for a large 16inch pizza with just onions and garlic was 24.00.  Last time we ever go into this joint again. Its pre cooked pre packaged garbage. Go to grimaldis, blind onion or true NY pizza.  A big waste of money. AND to order and take it to go was 10 mins. Unacceptable.

Been coming here since it opened and have the sense that it's definitely not what it used to be. I'ts always been part of the experience to overlook the noise--it's a magnet for kids, and to be expected. But it can be a little out of control. And the service has lapsed into the bizarro zone. That said, the food is good and I get a free meal on my birthday.

Never go back again,food was greasy not fresh or over cooked. We walk in for lunch and the cashier nod ok for lunch price. Didn't mention  changing over to  dinner price means don't eat the crab or shrimp! when the host told us that we have to pay dinner price. We said the cashier said it was ok then she grab our plate of crab. saying this is dinner price. Manager came over and exlain that is dinner price for crab and shrinp. We told her employee didn't in form us. She said  crab and shrimp is dinner price and she would ake off $10 offour menu  and will be lunch price. Well there was seven of us. So everthing was fine.  Then the manger came back and said no, no  has to be dinner price because you have coupon.Our friends from out of this country was shocked. Of the rudness of this whole situation.Never going back again as well of large family and friends not to mention friends and family from another country never go there. And they come to Reno a lot. As we where leaving the manager said I don't know what your problem is crab and shrimp dinner price only.

I rolled in here last week as I had a craving for a couple dogs.  The shop sits next to the Goodwill in the shopping center across from Meadowood.
  It's a small lunch spot with room for about 15 people on the inside and the typical strip mall windows.  There are both tables and a cozy side bar to sit at.

  I ordered the Little City Roller and what passes for their version of a Chicago dog and a beer while I waited for my togo order.  The place wasn't too busy, maybe 5 people at lunchtime.

  There was a little confusion with my order but when I finally got it, I was pretty impressed with the Little City Roller and it's unusual combination of toppings.  It was a quite tasty mix of peppers and sauce and the casing had snap.  I was less impressed with the Chicago dog but I think I may be spoiled on the real deal in that regard.

  Overall, a pretty good lunch spot for that area of town and I'll try it again when I am in the area.
My favorite and go to restaurant in the Vail/Rita Ranch area. Nice service, great portions and great location!

I have been reading about this place in the paper for a long time and finally got to try it. I noticed they have some unique and hard to find dishes on the menu. I tried the pork spring rolls and a bowl of pho. The spring rolls were a nice change from the usual shrimp and pork rolls you find other places. It came with a lot of lettuce, herbs, and pork/noodle mix and served with a nuoc cham sauce. The rolls were very fresh and didn't feel like they were made ahead like some places do. The pho was good coming with the usually fixin's. The broth was nice and flavorful. 

Service was good and prices were average. Definitely want to go back and try the specialty dishes.

The food is SO good. Almost everything I've tried has been really tasty. HOWEVER, I'm not kidding when I say this; EVERY SINGLE TIME I've eaten there, I've found hair in my food. EVERY time. It's pretty unappetizing when you're biting into a piece of the best pizza you've ever had...then you feel a hair glide through your teeth. To the cooks, PLEASE START WEARING HAIR NETS! I'm begging you. I really want to come back but don't want to taste your DNA.

Opening back up in November. Grand opening is Nov 15th and 16th. 

https://www.phillyvoice.com/bourse-marketplace-list-of-vendors-officially-opening/

I went here with my SO a couple of weeks ago.  The food was excellent and the bottle of wine was perfect.  

The food was very reasonably priced and the salmon sandwich was fantastic.  The caprese burger was OK, a little dry, but very flavorful.  We plan to return and will probably both get the salmon sandwich.

Save your money and do something else. Maybe this would be ok for just the cruise and to have a few drinks, but I would not recommend this for dinner. We spent over $300 for 2 adults and 2 children. My husband ordered some sort of chicken marsala dish that was covered in a salty gravy that tasted like it came from a powder/packet. The steak is not a premium cut and not worth the price. The crab dip tasted ok, but had a weird texture. Drinks were expensive. The salad seemed like it was intended to be high-end, but failed. The DJ plays to an older crowd most of the time. I will say that we had a bday party and the personalized card on the table was a nice touch. And, the boat looked nicer than some dinner cruises I've been on. I would caution anyone from using the mens' restroom on the 2nd floor--there was a leak resulting in a puddle of urine in the corner of the stall. Also, the woman's restroom stall was smaller than an airplane's.

Classic spanish feel here in a very up scale restaurant/venue. The murals on the wall really create the atmosphere and tone. The open air courtyard offers a great place to eat and enjoy your meal, and if the weather is cold or bad they can roll out a cover over the courtyard to close it all in. 

The food is absolutely amazing, I could not get enough of it. Literally, I was embarrassing myself eating all the appetizers. No shame! it was worth it! 

I also really enjoyed the layout, how the bar was in the back, the seating off to the side, the dance floor int he front, a receptionist to the left, and an open fire to the right. Really helps to control the foot traffic so no one congregated in one area. 

Definitely a good place to have a private event, or wedding!

I love to go to Cuban Breezes on my lunch break at work. Quick service. Great food. Friendly staff. Pricing isn't terrible. Think of it as Americanized Cuban food. Still definitely worth stopping in and trying it out.

Really neat little Bar Rescue project. Went in with a group for a quick cocktail and were told to check out upstairs. There's comfortable patio furniture seating with tvs at each table that wraps around entire upstairs balcony. We decided to go back to watch the game the next day. The food...you'd expect "sports bar food", right? Wrong!! It's amazing. We had meat and cheese spreads, the burgers are AMAZING, fish tacos ...I'm picky...some of the best. We go back here every time we visit Nola. This place is a hidden gem smack dab on Decatur St. So many games on at all times. Coolest, "modern" sports bars in the city!

Food was great. We made reservations in advance. The staff were rude both times we called (1st to schedule , 2nd to alter reservation #).  The service at the restaurant wasn't great either.  Our drinks came out after  our meal and we had begun eating. But food was great

Four star review of a local spot that doesn't serve high end foodie-food, but does a great job at what it's good at. In the age of COVID, there are appropriately spaced tables on an outside deck- admittedly with a view of the road and parking lot, but comfortable and cool.   Our service was great, for 3 adults one kid and a baby. The brussel sprouts with big cloves of roasted garlic were a winner for apps. My mushroom Swiss burger was amongst the best I've had locally, cooked to order with a fresh bun and onion rings courtesy of my friend's western burger (he's not an onion rings fan). You might want to ask for lettuce and tomato, as vegitables are not high on the menu here. The Chop 40 specialty dish with potatoes and " stuff" was enough for 2, easy. The pulled pork was tender and flavorful, if lacking in the spice kick I like.  Sweet potato fries were great, and regular fries good,  both American style salty.  My stoli and tonic was reasonably priced (and just how I ordered it). The beer selection had something for everyone, with a couple of standout Deschutes and local brews, plus a British cider that made a great snakebite.  So: don't expect flashy food, order carefully, and it's totally worth a visit and a return.

A downside of growing up in the same city I reside in as an adult is that I still see areas of town as I saw them years ago. And the Loretto Plaza/San Roque Plaza areas I have never associated with anything classy or fancy.  It's the home of the Farmer Boy diner that crazy Mary Birdie ate at and Federal Drug that used to display all their best incontinence products and aluminum walkers in the window. 
In the spot where Via Maestra 42 now resides, I knew as Swenson's as a child. Then Rich's ice cream. And it took me ages to come to Via Maestra, where I didn't have high expectations. I mean, there's a 7-11 across the street and the whole place is a strip mall. 
But it's now my third time, and for each time I had a quality experience. The place is small, you can't really do anything about that. But bistro style eating and lounging I recall in Europe is much the same. It's probably us that's too fat. Anyway, I really can't fault them for anything. My service has always been really good, genuine. Usually 3-4 people look after me, and just to be clear, I'm an average person. I respect the waitstaff like they respect me.  The service I get here rocks.

On order for the evening: 
 
Bread - char grilled, drizzled with olive oil and sliced into little pieces. 
Bruschetta - thin ciabatta-like pieces covered with nicely flavored tomato and garlic.  I've had enough bad experiences with thick bruschetta that's so crunchy it makes the roof of my mouth sore, and then the tomato comes tumbling all over the plate and lap that I was pretty shy about ordering this. But they are wide, flat triangles of bread evenly covered with the tomato. Easy to eat, and really delicious. It seemed super fresh.
Ravioli Zuccotto - pumpkin ravioli with crispy sage and butter sauce. No salt, no pepper, it's just good to go. It was yummy, nicely presented. Maybe could have been better if the butter was more browned, but I had no qualms with what I ate. The snacking bread was great for dipping into this sauce.
Chocolate hazelnut gelato - got this in a to-go cup so I could walk home with it. 

Dining companion had a glass of Toscolo chianti and the pollo valdostana, which was a chicken breast stuffed with prosciutto alongside truffled mash and veg. Think of it like a chicken kiev but cured ham instead of the butter sauce.  And my dining friend, we've known each other since kindergarten in SB, he lives maybe 2 blocks from here, he worked at Rich's at a teen, and he hasn't been to Via Maestra either. It's not just me that'd mostly written off San Roque.

Nice note: sitting outside, even for being along the side walk of the strip mall, is pleasant! Because they have lined it with planter boxes of flowering hedges. It's not big and beautiful, but it's so much nicer to look at those vines than crazy soccer mom crookedly backing her dinged up dirty minivan into the parking space 4 feet away from your table. (some parts of San Roque will never change)

If we keep heading in the same direction, with Gelson's, Renaud's, Via Maestra 42, even Jeanine's a little further up the mall, San Roque's soon going to be better than the sum of its parts.

The food is good, beautiful place. But the DJ on Saturday is absolutely horrible. He completely does not read the room and is blasting techno and rave music in a relaxing beach restaurant, everyone is annoyed.

I am all the time pescatarian sometimes vegan...LOL! Was informed of this gem a month or so ago and finally took the opportunity to visit! And i must say i was very satisfied! Enjoyed every bite and sip! Excited to return to try other menu items that looked appealing. Drop Squad Kitchen is a must try!
Cute and warm space! Really renews the neighbourhood. Had a chai latte and it was delicious.

I absolutely love this restaurant.  We had the traditional Cuban sandwiches and my wife added a bowl of the Moros.  Everything was amazing as always.  We also ordered the Sweet Pastelitos and Flan with their amazing cafe' con leche.  Overall a 5 star experience once again!!
Best ice cream on the Eastside . Food is typical  for an Ice cream stand tenderloin and chillidongs. Try the onion chips!
Stop. Do not pass go. Collect the brisket sliders. So good I had to get a 2nd order. Mac & cheese was excellent as were the pork belly and turkey sammys. I want to pitch a tent outside this joint.
I went there on opening night and ate  some spicy tacos that were excellent, Plenty of TV's and a nice location(lots of parking) and the staff was very personable.
Outstanding. Sat at the bar during a busy brunch Sunday and ate within 15 minutes. Had the BBQ Le' Bennie. 5 stars and coming back tomorrow before leaving town.

I remember waiting in line on weekends for one hour to get table and back then the food was great! The service was high tempo  and good.
Last week I received guests from Europe and Asia so I decided to show case American breakfast. 
My experience was a désastre it started with how the waitress poured coffee holding  her container high it splashed the coffee  all over the saucer . The silverware was not polished  that's just the beginning!! Food was served cold and tasteless prepared with out any care.
I kept apologizing to my guests and telling them how good it used to be. 
Sad sad sad ....
Well next time I will just stick to regular diner at least I can get better service and decent food for 1/3 of the price...
There was no fried chicken at this place. In my opinion the pics are very misleading and do not match the actual menu!
A pretty good meal.  The white sauce was the best I've found so far in Philadelphia.  The red sauce was rather uninspiring though and had very little kick.
Delicious King Cakes (both the chocolate and the traditional)!

Kool little place, didnt know what to expect at first. Greeted by very friendly and nice waitresses. Drinks immediately brung out, followed shortly by my food.' I could smell the meat soon as i enetered the building. Waitress didnt leave me unattended for one second! 

I had the Zydeco platter: great taste good proportions, beans were Good and spicy, macaroni & cheese was surprisingly good!! Overall I like the place and they have a Bar for Drinkers. I will be back soon. Thanks!!

Amazing evening. Spectacular service in beautiful setting. Great wine list and creative cocktails. I started with the Dirty Rice Arancini flavorful and crispy bites. The Peanut soup had great spice and super textures with crispy rice. The Spiced Chicken was expertly prepared with a moist tender chicken wrapped in crispy seasoned skin.

Awesome food, great servers, very clean. Ayce crab legs are wonderful.
Nice variety on the menu, as well. Seafood, steak and sandwiches.

Hands down. This is the best wine bar in Idaho. 
Wine selection is amazon. The cheese sandwich is to die for. 
The whole atmosphere is great. 
Highly recommend!
Truly a neighborhood hang out place!
Keep up the good work guys! You guys rock!

If I could give zero stars I would. Went through the drive through while driving through the area. Order was not complicated. Frisco burger meal, no tomato, and a 5 piece chicken tender meal. We get our bag and pull away when I realize there is only one meal in the bag. I pull into the parking lot and go in. Let them know we didn't get our other meal. Made the mistake of not checking the meal we had received at first. Get a couple miles down the road and realize the first order is completely wrong, isn't the correct sandwich at all.

We went here for dinner before attending a play at Stifel Theater.  I had the Mixed Grilled Chicken with the Flash Fried Spinach as an appetizer, and they were both delicious, beyond my expectations, especially the vegetables that were served with the chicken.  I could have made a meal out of just those, but the chicken was a great bonus.  The flavor of the food was delicate, the meal was very nicely served, and the staff was very friendly without being overbearing.  This is a restaurant that I will definitely return to.

This Restaurant is beyond great, where do i start, i went there with my family and the host was super friendly and welcoming, i think it was the owner's daughter, but that's not even the good part, the food is crazy good and cooked to perfection, i ordered the chicken shawarma wrap and it was PHENOMENAL, definitely will be a routine going there.

It was really busy when my girlfriend and I stopped in today but we were served quickly by a very friendly employee and got through the line with ease.

The sandwiches were great (I tried the pastrami while she had the grilled chicken) and well worth the price. 

We sat outside because it was a little smoky inside, but no complaint there - we enjoyed sitting on the Circle.

To top off our great experience, the employee who first greeted us brought us free cookies as a thank you for trying Potbelly for the first time. I strongly recommend it if you're looking for a tasty, hot sandwich downtown.

Free lunches do exist! Today for lunch I order the lunch bag special to go and they ran out shortly after my order was placed. They were unable to reach me by phone (missing my work number extension) so when I arrived to pick up my lunch they had prepared a different but similar lunch special and after apologizing profusely for the mix up they gave me lunch  for free!  Their amazing customer service and handling of this situation prompted me to finally write this review.

I have eaten here three times and will be back many more meals.  The food is always delicious and the mixed drinks are fresh and wonderful.  For the love or all things unkosher, if you eat pork do yourself a favor and order something with bacon or pork belly off the menu.  You will not be disappointed.

Cups Coffee has really great coffee (better than I can make at home).  They treat me like a personal friend.  Their multiple downtown locations make it easy to stop in.  I always look forward to going there for the flavored coffee of the day (my personal favorite). By the way, their hot chocolate is awesome!

My margarita was good. That's one star. The waitress was very nice and attentive.  Another star.  Always start with a positive.  Other than that, every single piece of food we ordered was horrible.  Sorry folks.  The food was either completely bland or incredibly salty.  It was kinda like Mexican night at the hospital.

Great local place with tasty food, friendly staff and good service. Plenty of big screen TV's to watch the game and a nice choice for sitting at the bar or grabbing a quiet table.
