We will be back

OMGGGGGGG, this is one of my favorite Happy Hour spots!!!! They have an amazzzzzzzing HH with plenty of delicious options for cocktails and food!!!! I highly recommend. The bar area can get very lively, fills up pretty fast.

I love this place, from the moment you step in the door. It's soo unexpected, I'm immediately transformed into another universe and time. The wine tasting/gift shop/dessert area as you walk in completely all purpose. It's extremely functional for shopping, hanging-out, chatting, sipping, sight seeing, etc. Then you walk towards the back, either make a quick right into the bar area or walk straight back into the dinning room. It's upscale, casual, elegant, romantic, chill and laid back. 

My absolute favorite cocktail is the Bin 61 Sour, their take on a Whiskey Sour. And if you know me, you know I love Whiskey Sours & Bourbon Basil Smashes!!! So this is right up my alley. 

The food is absolutely delicious!!!! I highly recommend the Ahi Tuna Taco's, Pork Belly Tostada's and House Made Meatballs and don't even try to skip out without having dessert. The appetizers are extremely filling and great for sharing. The meatballs were soo tender, light-n-fluffy and that toasted bread was perfect for sopping up all that lovely sauce. The tuna taco's were an absolute surprise. They were hearty and soooo fresh. The pork belly was tender and soo full of flavor. I mean they don't miss a beat here. 

I'm still working my way thru their HH menu, but I would gladly order off the regular menu, if I missed HH from 3pm-6pm. The wait staff is hit-n-miss, as far as service, but not awful. They're all friendly but only 1 server has been OUTSTANDING, Meghan!!!!

They have an awesome wine club, which you should definitely obtain the scoop on. And if you're not into wine, it can go towards your dining rewards.

Just had such a great time here. Always wanted to stop by. A young handsome gentleman by the name of Michael helped us with such sincere generosity throughout the evening. The happy hour was fantastic offering 50% off bottles of wine and great deals on appetizers. I will be back for many more business trips! Very into this atmosphere and the amazing staff at this place!

David C., the bartender at Bacara Bar, is a master at his craft. If you enjoy sweet cocktails and aperitifs, try his delicious version of the classic Kir Royal. I also highly recommend waking up early to enjoy a morning stroll through the grounds to The Bistro. One of the best ways to wake up at Bacara is to soak up the day's first sunrays with a newspaper, The Bisto's Eggs Benedict and their pomegranate mimosas. 

As one of my favorite weekend getaway destinations, I've stayed in the suites and the guests rooms. The guest rooms are beautifully decorated, but you should know that this part of the resort feels like luxury 3 story condominiums. The suites, however, boast the most privacy, the best ocean views, romantic indoor fireplaces  and balconies with bistro sets for private dining. All the rooms are lovely just different experiences, so if you're particular read the amenities list before you book.
I stop in mornings for bread and breakfast. Love their bagettes and salt rolls. They make a nice gorgonzola focaccia. Serve Elly coffee, teas, croissants, crumb buns for breakfast.

I've had a lot of poke living in LA, and was very skeptical about this place, but I have to say I was wrong to doubt it!  Pokeceviche is some of the best I've had. SUPER fresh and flavorful! They're very generous with their portions and very nice about everything! I've been here at least 2x a week since they've opened. Never disappointed me!

Just had the sumo size, custom bowl with Spanish and Matcha white Rice. The best! Salmon was so fresh and the Taki topping is a must!

The space is beautiful and the music was relaxing.  They have a great selection of colors.  My french manicure looked beautiful, but it only lasted 2 days even thought I avoided washing dishes, etc...hence the 3 stars.

We just found this restaurant a few months ago and hands down it is the best sushi in Reno.  The owner is friendly and ready to introduce you to new dishes that you haven't tried before. (even though he is hard to understand sometimes) He said that all of his sushi chefs came from Japan and have trained for many years.  Which is obvious when you have their sushi. The fish is fresh and the rolls are unique.   We ordered many rolls and they all had their own flavors.  I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for quality sushi. My only concern if it even really matters is that I would like to see a better wine offering.

If you're looking for a good tasting breakfast that will fill you up at a decent price. Look no further than Breakfast and Burgers. It is an old Wendy's location so don't expect fine China and Crystal stemware on the tables. We enjoyed our meal that were prepared as expected in a timely fashion. Our waiter made sure our cups were kept filled with hot fresh coffee. Good food and hot coffee, what more can you ask for in a breakfast.
Great food, even better prices. Highly recommend the stuffed hot peppers. The owner has been on site both times I've come in.

I'm visiting Boise for my niece's graduation with my family. We wanted burgers and headed to Fudruckers, but they were closed. So we went to Legends. The menu looked great...lots of variety. There were 8 in our party but the place was nearly empty. We ordered 3 burgers. My dad ordered his medium rare but it came out WELL done so he sent it back. The second one came out better. I was sharing a burger with someone...we ordered it medium but it too was well done. I'm not sure why they bother to ask you how you want your burger if that's the only way they know how to cook them. The bun was sort of dry. I also ordered my fries crispy.  they not only were not crispy but they were luke warm. actually everyone's fries were bad. 

my mom ordered steamed class and they had red pepper flakes in them, which were not listed as an ingredient, which my mom can't eat. 

my nephew ordered a BLT and it only had tomato on one half. We also had two pizzas which were decent. The crust was thin and crispy and the ingredients were good.

They offered us two free desserts, but they were out of both of the desserts we ordered. All in all the food was marginal and I wouldn't go back there.

From the moment I walked in, this place seemed like a typical sports bar. But then it hit me: they were playing clubby dance music, which is kind of rare for a sports bar. One of the waitresses was a RIOT: she was dancing to the beats while ringing up customer checks..

Unfortunately, ours was of the bland variety - not too attentive nor enthusiastic about her job.  I ordered the pacific whitefish from the menu but was served the tilapia.  I opted against having the waitress take it back, for fear that she'd spit in the food.  Besides, the tilapia wasn't all THAT bad.. too bad it was priced the same as the whitefish ($13) which is kind of unreasonable for a cheap bottom-feeder that simply grows big fast by feeding it trash. (My apologies to the few fish farmers who grow their product with better-than-inferior feed).

Anyway, the signature salad has my recommendation.. loved the candied pecans in it! Just go light on the strawberry dressing - it's very thick... hmm.. double shot of high fructose corn syrup anyone? 

While you fall asleep from carb overload during lunch, the waitress might forget about you.. so perk up every once in awhile to find her so you can ask for your check.. else she might accidentally charge you dinner pricing when she eventually comes around hours later.. :P just kiddin - I haven't been here for dinner yet!

My verdict: food 4/5. Service 2/5.
This is another example Mexican food meets American. Happy hour is worth stopping by,  but the food is just ok.

I've said it before and I'll say it again: People can drool all they want over Carmel's Bistro de Paris. It is good. It's just not GREAT for the price point. 

This French restaurant with Caribbean flavors opened in February to much fanfare in Carmel's Main Street. It's in a spot formerly occupied by Pizza King, bringing much-needed fine dining to the growing, bustling area. 

A vegetable canard roller--basically, an egg roll with duck and julienned vegetables--exemplifies the restaurant's fancy, fusion-y style. Yes, the "roller" was crisp. Yes, the trois sauces of blackberry, orange glaze and horseradish Dijon were interesting and intense. But I couldn't taste the duck. So why am I paying around $13 for fried veggies? 

This place is good at layering textures and flavors, however. I was particularly taken with the creamy grilled brie, given form with a nice walnut crust. The crab cakes came with sweet yucca "mash" and plantains, served with an island butter sauce. The crisp, salt-touched plantains against the yucca mash and sweet, smooth butter are a sophisticated pleasure. 

Opinions about this place run strong and diverse. Check it out for yourself.
I ordered a margherita pizza. They didn't use mussarela di bufalo just regular mozzarella. Who does that?!? I lost respect.

A great date night experience. Everything was wonderful! The steak and sides wow, yummy. My bf got an old fashion and it came in a box, the smoke released when opened....how neat. Bascoms is on the pricey side but for a special occasions it was really great.
Longest wait ever in the drive through. Been stuck in this line now 35 min still don't have my food. What gives.

This place is incredible.  I've only been twice and had the Pho Tai (soup) both times, but it was very good and consistent.  Even though I've had slightly better elsewhere, it was still very good, and the service was great.  The guy remembered us from our first time, asked us some related questions from our first visit of a week before, remembered what we had ordered, and even remembered to bring me a specific garnishment that doesn't come standard that I had requested the first time.  I mean, c'mon, how can you beat that?

The ambiance is also superb.  It's very clean and upscale.  Very nice total immersion.  HIGHLY recommended.

Meh.

Super Wok delivers to me, and is my go-to for quick chinese food.
In fact, it is quite quick, usually arriving at my door in a half hour, and for a great price.

This being said, the food is not overly flavorful. The egg rolls, spring rolls, and wontons are standard, with little flavor. The rangoon taste like cream cheese, which can be good, but ehhhh.

The chicken isn't great. The general's chicken is pretty good, but hardly outstanding.
This applies to pretty much everything I've had from here.

It's not great, but certain isn't bad, and is a solid option on which to lean.
Freaking awesome breakfast!! The coffee was amazing!! Grits....OMG delicious!!! Service was friendly and great!! Highly recommend this place for breakfast!!

So we were driving down here towards the beach and I saw this shop and was suddenly in the mood for some Fish N' Chips so we parked and hit it up.

=========
LOCATION
=========

Located on the hustle n' bustle of State St. It's among a bunch of street-side clothing shops, restaurants and bars. Inside it's pretty compact in the area in front of the counter... we didn't venture into the backside.

=========
THE FOOD
=========

~ The Fish - I like Fish & Chips... minus the chips. Ordered one piece a'la cart. It was big, pretty juicy and tasty. The fried / battered part was good, a bit under-cooked not crispy enough but overall it was good. Garnished it with some very sub-par tartar sauce, vinegar, salt and Tapatio. Pretty good, not quite Malibu Seafood Shack levels. (4/5)

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/macs-fish-and-chip-shop-santa-barbara?select=bZ9_pQVmsLGG7o8IsYJe-A#DqMMZ7dqyK94RH2FYl5jgQ

~ Clam Chowder - A friend of mine ordered this. He thought it was "okay." I tried a coupla spoonfuls and I liked it. The clams were kinda small but succulent. (4/5)


=================
THE FINAL ANALYSIS
=================

This was a solid spot. It was like a 3.5 BUT there were a few items on the menu that fascinated me, like the DEEP FRIED CANDY BARS (10 different types including 2 Cadbury types) for $3.50 that I'd be interested to try next time. However it was a bit pricey though for what it was... a fish n chips place.

Disappointing experience dining at this restaurant. We had initially planned on takeout from this place and noticed some strange conditions on take out orders such as a 5% surcharge and no ice-cream included with entree purchases even though this comes with dine in orders. We decided to eat in instead and sat down at a table for 6 (we were 3 people). As soon as we sat down they promptly took away a table even though the restaurant was near empty. The food was just average. The tempura batter was more of beer batter rather than a Panko batter and the California rolls were made with a strange imitation crab salad. As we were leaving we said thank you and good bye and the owner (assumed the older man at the front was the owner) didn't even acknowledge us. Would not recommend this place based on the terrible service.
Yummy.  Had the Barbacoa chicken. Very tasty.  Hubbies had a pizza. Also great.  Nathan was our server great job. Very attentive!!!

Don't have your 14 year olds apply for a job here if the manager is Jody.

Our daughter wants to attend a missionary trip with her church next year.

She went to one of the McDonald's job hiring days and was successful in her first interview. She then received a call for a second interview on a Saturday at the time where she had a medical appointment. Our daughter called and spoke to Jody the manager to ask if her interview could be 30 minutes later and was told to blatantly no as the manager was not prepared to work late to accommodate for the child's interview. This of course left our daughter in tears as she should have very high hopes and was so excited at the fact that she received a call for a second interview.

We have always stopped by this  McDonald's following our daughters soccer matches or Girl Guides. We Now understand why they have such a high turnover of staff.

Very upset. I will avoid this branch of McDonald's going forward
My favorite restaurant in the city! The food never disappoints, such great variety, and the cocktails are amazing.

Actually they deserve a big fat ZERO for their poor customer service and full on pretentiousness!  I can't tell you what the food is like there, because they wouldn't seat us, so we left.  We intended to eat breakfast here.  It was 8:30 am on a Saturday,  and this place was almost dead.  There were maybe 5 or 6 tables that had people eating. Nobody was waiting in line to be seated. We asked for the round table in the corner so we could look out the windows.  We were told NO because they reserve that table for parties of 5 on the weekends.  I looked around the large, nearly empty restaurant, and then behind me, and said "but there's nobody here, and nobody else around."  She said no again, and then an older man came out and said the same thing.   So, we left.  They must have money flowing out of the faucets in this place.  I've never seen anyone turn money down before.  So completely pretentious.  We just wanted to sit in the corner window on a rainy morning and watch the French Quarter go by.

I first ate at Boca in Fall 2010, and I really liked it. I went back a few weeks ago, and it was a total bust. The workers behind the counter weren't very attentive, and the food left something to be desired. I may give it one more shot in the future, but it will be a while before I go back.

This is a cool new place in the down town area.  It's located right off the river and gives a new school vibe.  It brings in a younger crowd.  Expect club style music with a lot of bodies.  If your early enough you can get a table but mostly it is just standing room.  Still this is a really cool place to meet old and new friends
Great atmosphere and fish & chips! Service was fast and friendly too and that was on what seemed to be a busy Friday night too!
Great lunch menu - three courses (soup, appetizer, main entree) and very affordable.  Plenty of food and consistently tasty.  One of my favorite lunch spots in West Philadelphia/UCity.

Sher-E-Punjab is an excellent Indian restaurant. Their lunch buffet is plentiful. I've also enjoyed their dinner fare.

The only drawback is that there can be a wait for dinner. It's a popular place.
This is some of the best pizza around. Quality product from a man who knows his pizza. This two person operation only makes 40 pies so get on line early--5:00.

I have eaten at this place many times since they opened and never been disappointed. The service is good (not great, but more than adequate) and the food is outstanding. They cater more toward long dinners and giving you plenty of time to enjoy yourself. They have a wonderful wine list, try the flavored Saki, and bar. I would highly recommend this place. Just make sure you're not in a rush.

The pizza I ordered was missing toppings that were in the menu description and was burnt. I also ordered an appetizer sampler and added a note for extra of all sauces and got none. Not to mention the mozzarella sticks in the sampler were burnt and completely hollow with no cheese! This was a horrible first experience

Staff was upbeat, prompt and helpful
Heather was a great server, gave candid helped with our menu selections. Shrimp dinners were great. Shrimp pasta was a hit. The bacon cheese burger was a hand made patty on a great bun. Happy hour all day Sunday. 
Nice atmosphere, prompt service
Sick beer list and a lip smacking menu. Terrific choices for food and beer. A great, welcoming space. Andrew behind the bar is the man. Stop in.
Great friendly place to eat.  Great variety on dinners. I go there often. Wonderful place. The staff is friendly and the place is clean. And the manager is very nice.

Who doesn't love pasta and convenience! I was invited to DalMoros and I loved it! The idea of having pasta on the go is my kind of party lol 

Let's start with the fact that they make their pastas in house, and also their sauces! Everything was so delicious and fresh! I tried the pesto sauce, the bolognese, cacio e pepe, and amatriciana! Wow yeah everything was delicious! 

The spot itself is smaller, but it goes with the concept (pasta to go)! However, they do have some space to sit down and enjoy your pasta, and some limited sitting areas on the outside.

The staff was friendly and explained everything to me since it was my first time there. Price is also very reasonable. OH AND LETS NOT FORGET THE TIRAMISU!! *chefs kiss*

I wish I had more photos ... but i ate way too fast lol

Let me begin by saying that these guys have some of the best wings I have ever had.  Managing to keep the wing crispy while smothering it with spot-on flavor is a trick these guys have mastered.  Having this spot so close to home is awesome.  Their pizza is delicious.  You can definitely tell that it's made with fresh ingredients under the delicate care of an authentic recipe and chef.  The first few times I've been, the customer service has left much to be desired.  It seems as though the staff may have never worked in the service industry before.  I will say they are polite, but there was no sense of urgency and way too much carrying on amongst the staff while Myself and others had to wait for their attention. I was taking a course next door.  So I was eating there a few days back to back. I got iced tea again on the second day.  It tasted like it had sat out overnight.    This place does not get the fifth star simply because these are easy fixes.  Tighten up the staff,  make them more attentive, and change your tea daily.  Otherwise, food is great.  I highly recommend the garlic Parmesan wings. Absolutely delicious!

Me and my wife went to this place for the first time for lunch  the wait staff did a wonderful job, me and my wife had a chicken pot pie and i would recommend it to any one that asks it was cooked perfectly the veg it the pie was perfectly cooked the prices are perfect for the quilty of the food i will return and recommend the place to anyone.

1.1k reviews done so far, and with 1 more coming your way where the 4/5 star rating isn't going to change. We are always chasing perfection whether it is in life or anything else.  If perfection was easily obtainable then maybe there wouldn't be anything to strive for. Nashville BBQ is working towards that goal though and as my third big named stopped at BBQ in Nashville over the years; Edley's did not disappoint. Starting the day with a slight hangover, I knew some southern BBQ would be the perfect solution for a little boot and rally! Spontaneous trips to Smashville are my bread butter and with that said; I needed to eat something with bread and butter. Saw the tuck special in photo's and instantly knew that I needed it. Day 1 I had it with brisket and day 2 (yes I went back a second time) I had it with hot chicken and YEEDOGGY it was great! Sides for day 1 were mac n cheese and some really tasty backed beans. After taking the first bite I couldn't stop singing beans, beans, the magical fruit, the more you eat, the more you......  Day 2 sides were delicious green beans (tune on repeat) and grits (great choice to make). Solid BBQ experience from myself and an experienced friend on brisket who came in for the second round and agreed.  He said the brisket was good, but not five star worthy. He also complimented their signature sauce and in his words "That Potato Salad was LEGIT!" I will drop the mic on that note. With the lack of a line and being off the main drag of Smashville.....I'd recommend coming here first before you try the other BBQ spots I have reviewed. Oh an lets not discount how good the catfish taco's were!  Ya'll come back now ya hear?!

Website does not work properly and did not honor my code for the free promo item.  Person who answered the phone when I called to complain was familiar with the issue so it's not just us old guys who don't get the website.  Deep dish was seventeen bucks and was too done to the point of being burnt.  Delivery driver was confronted when my order was incomplete and did not care.  Pathetic.  Usually ok but going down hill fast.  Better pizza elsewhere.

This was my 1st visit to Zoup in Exton ,pa. Very disappointing as both soups I ordered ( chicken noodle & lobster bisque) were so salted they were barely eatable. I make my own versions of these and realize that the best flavor results from excellent stock ,not sodium.the only reason I gave them 2 stars was the fine service & appearance of the store.

Would not come back.  As we entered we were not even greeted just told to seat ourselves by a waitress that was yelled down the hall; after seating ourselves we waited for about 5min before anybody came into the dinning area.  We ordered wings - hot !!! that came out tasting sweet- ; the pizza you may want to bring your own marinara sauce bc our pizza didn't have any!! It was bread with cheese and really tasty sausage probably the only good thing I have to say about this place. The drinks both soda and tea tasted watered down; and you won't eat alone there was two annoying flies eating with us the whole time. They need to do something about those flies; Sorry I really wanted to like this place.  I had heard good things; maybe we just went on a really bad day.

This is my first yelp review. i'm a new thing junkie and my goal is to try every restaurant in CW. Aloha Poke Bowl (APB) opened and i've been twice. i resolved to lower my HDL this year so i'm trying to eat like this more often. APB is like sushi deconstructed. like a sushi salad bar. like ordering whatever you want in a roll and getting it a recyclable bowl.
      first, disclaimers: i grew up in hawaii so i have soft spot for poke. i'm not a food historian. and I can walk here from my house. OK. so poke can be just pieces of something like seafood tossed with stuff like rock salt, seaweed, sesame, chili pepper. 
      i hear fish is delivered every other day and they aren't allowed to cook a nothing. regarding raw:  in my small kid days, i would tuck sashimi (raw fish) under my hot rice to cook it cuz my mom made us eat everything back then and my appreciation for sashimi was not acquired until i adulted. regarding freshness:  i tried the spicy ahi twice and so did my kids and we all liked it. it's good for littler kids too: no bacon, no chips, no fries :-) See rice, pineapple, edamame, shrimp (cooked!), avo, cucumber. chopsticks, sauces. Seaweed salad, jasmine rice, onions, spicy ailoi, crunch...and on... 
    i didn't ask if they cared that i brought in my own beverage as my thermos of hot tea w honey was in my bag and i preferred it to their average beverage offerings and no free water cups (which is no biggie). nearby street parking is easy and free. they had fliers at the register for the Galerie Marie down the road which is cool. and i was told the spicy mayo is in the back. So... to trying new things, being healthy and supporting local, a healthy new year!
So yummy! The outdoor seating is adorable and they are pretty quick at getting you your food. The mozzarella sandwich with turkey added was so gooood!

First time really trying to eat dinner on crutches after the Big Cankle Break of 2017 and packed myself into the car. Brought Mark H for balance support. Have been waiting long enough to try this place here goes! I notice an overly aggressive driver kinda fighting me for a space. He gets out of the car and is a valet driver. He says we can't park there. Okay where can we park? We can't we have to valet or we can't eat here. Okay, BYE Felicia!

This place is fantastic! Stumbled upon it looking for the best margarita and this place popped up. Drinks are so delicious ( Alex was our bartender) just ask her and she will make any drink you wish custom made to your liking. Everything from chips & salsa, salad, wings, skirt steak were all DELICIOUS! The wings are a must! Crunchy and tasty! The steak is so tender. The total experience was so satisfying from the the moment we walked in until we left. Everyone greeted us, the manager came over to our table to check on us, our waiter was amazing and I already mentioned Alex, I would really recommend this place, a MUST TRY at least one! ( This visit was on July 23rd 2021) We will DEFINITELY be returning!

Happen to walk in and was absolutely more than pleasantly surprised.  My 30 minute neck and shoulder massage was excellent.  I am a person who usually gets a massage every two weeks and sometimes weekly.  I will definitely be back.  Very reasonably priced for the great massage and customer service.   Yes, it really was that great!!

I have been in Philly for 2 days and was really looking forward to dining at Amada. To start off my family and I walked in 10 minutes early for our 8pm reservation and the hostess did not even find our reservation, after 2 or 3 mins of a blank look on her face displaying a great lack of interest for seating us she was able to find our reservation.  We were asked to wait at the bar where after 40 mins of waiting still had no table, after the lack of ownership from the now 2 hostess that were just standing there not able to honor their part of the reservation (which was made 3 months in advance) we simply walked out and dined at another restaurant. The name Amada will never even be coming out of my families mouth and we will not be making any plans to go back because if the service starts like this I do not want to see how it will go as the night continues.

Upon a friend's recommendation, I tried out this cutely-named cafe, and rather liked it. The small, single-portioned desserts were beautifully decorated but not interesting enough to me, and while I wouldn't have minded a piece of chocolate, I wanted something that would fill me up after walking around Philadelphia. 

I decided to go with a frozen drinking chocolate which curiously reminded me of Serendipity, though this was a lot smoother and preferable to their Frrrrrozen Hot Chocolate. My friend got the Aztec blend, which she liked, while I went for  a fresh fruit blend, tossing blueberries and mango into the mix. I was happy to taste and feel little bits of the fruit in the drink and to see the actual fruit go into the blender, which I believe made for an even better taste experience. I finished the entire thing, and in conclusion, think that this would be a delightful place for a casual date or for anyone with hypoglycemia looking for an energy booster.

Full-disclosure:  I received a message from the owner  Brad after my first review apologizing that they were having a staffing crisis in the kitchen that night.  I appreciate his response and concern, but had already returned for a second visit before I received his message.

After my first visit, I was a little obsessed with the bacon-wrapped dates, so I went back again the next night with my sister.  Our experience was a big improvement.  Our food came out in a reasonable amount of time and piping hot.  Our server was very attentive and the busboy made sure we were never short of water. 

The bacon around the dates was indeed crispy this time and they were super-delicious again.  I also had the flatbread appetizer which was like spinach-artichoke dip as the sauce with cheese on top -- quite filling as a meal for one.  My sister had the local sausages with pasta salad and cole slaw and was quite pleased as well.

I was glad my second visit went better.  There are enough interesting things going on with/at the Stable to keep me coming back.
Such a great place. Everything was so fresh and tasty. I'll go back often. Summer roll is really good.

On a quick trip through Philly, I made a stop into Buddakan.  I had been hearing about the edamame ravioli for over a year.  It exceeded my expectations.  The ravioli itself is made with fresh dough and cooked perfectly with a little bit of chew.  The edamame filling is ethereal.  I was blown away by the taste and texture.  The truffle-shallot broth it comes up was so incredible I wanted to drink from the bowl.  You must get this when you go.

We also ordered a calamari salad that was delicious and dressed perfectly.  On special was steamed pork buns.  The pork was seasoned with 5-spice and was very tasty.

Our waiter was spectacular.  He was extremely pleasant and johnny-on-the-spot with drink refills and new plates.

This place is a must!  Those edamame dumplings and Kim chi fried rice make my night!  Amazing happy hour which is 7 days a week!  Love the ambiance and very cool out back at the graffiti bar!  The bartenders are great and food comes out very fast and is always done right!  The mini ice cream cones after a sit down dinner are so fun!

I try to avoid this place because of the way the manager treats his employees. The last time I was there I was waiting in line after ordering and the manager started screaming at the top of his lungs at one of girls that works there. She was bringing food out to a customer and he yelled from the kitchen for her to get back and hurry up what she was doing. This wasn't the first time either, the time before he was demeaning to his employees as well. Won't be going back.

I really love this bar this is the best place to go Friday night I went to the docs on Broad Street and Jones Avenue it'sucked big-time all troublemaking people starting fights bungs though on route 130 is so peaceful and quiet the food is good and the workers are nice
Family feeling...food is delicious..just like if mom made it! Friendly people.Chicken fried steak and grits are awesome...as are their sweet rolls.  mmmmmmmmmmmmm

This place sucked so much it was sad. I hate writing bad reviews but the mac and cheese here tasted like it had been sitting all day. it's a pretty big serving for 13ish$ but it was so bad i could barely eat it. it's like a little stand with a couple out door sitting areas that is connected to a bar or something.

Very long wait, always past the time they tell you on the phone and if you order in person ooof best of luck to you. The pizza on the other hand is also not the best quality but I guess this is what you should expect from a place who probably makes most of its income from drunk college students next door (Tulane). Not the best not the worst so I feel like a 3 perfectly fits this pizza parlor.
A great corner bar on the Hill.  You can't really ask for more, except they also have an area out back to play Bocce!   Love stopping in Milo's when I'm on the Hill!

So my friend invited me to this spot. I was a little skeptical because the reviews seemed very 50/50. However my friend said he gives the food a 5 out of 5. 

So we get there and it's sort of self serve-ISH. You order your food, get a buzzer and when it goes off you go and grab your food from the window. There is a bar (doesn't appear to be fully stocked), but has enough options. 

I ordered the Chicken Fajita Taco -- SO GOOD! It's funny because I don't personally eat tomatoes and blue cheese crumbles, but I left it all on there and took a bite and it was SO good! I added a little of the hot sauce on it (They hace sauces on the table). My friend ordered some sort of burrito that didn't LOOK appetizing but it's his favorite. 

We also tried all of the desserts: Cinnamon churros, Oreo churros and another item that I can't pronounce. The Cinnamon churros are SO GOOD! The Oreo Churros are pretty decent but I have to be in the mood for them because I'm not an "Oreo eater" lol. The 'other' dessert I won't be buying again though. It's basically a thin piece of hollow bread with cinnamon/sugar on it and it comes with some icing. I would've better preferred just a bread knot that dips in icing. It was just thin for no reason lol. Try the churros though! 

The atmosphere was great. TVs and music. Friendly vibes. 

The reviews I previously read were many complaints about the service BUT I had a great experience with their service. I was there until they closed and a rather large sized family came in and didn't get their food until closing time and the cook made sure to tell them not to rush and take their time. He was very polite. i just so happen to notice him bringing out their food and telling them to take their time. So I was pleasantly surprised being that the reviews said different. 

One of the young ladies even came and grabbed our trays.

What an absolute joke of a place. The management is toxic they treat there employees like trash, they talk bad about one another  or in a fun joking way, people are always on their phone and talking to each other when there are customers waiting in line. They make you come in when your sick if you can't find someone to cover your shift and there doing this during the pandemic we are in? What a joke of a place. This is the worst place to work at for anyone never let your kid work here.
Great happy hour deal on oysters! Red Beans and Rice and shrimp and grits were pretty good.  Server was helpful.
This is my favorite diner in the area. I never had a bad meal there so far. The service always seems to be solid. The pricing is average with other diners in the area.

I have been avoiding this place for no reason in particular but had a craving and needed to try it finally. It did not disappoint! I was pleasantly surprised and will go back. 

Classic meatball with spicy bolognese sauce - this was my favorite. The sauce was not spicy but very flavorful. 
Classic meatball with creamy garlic sauce - good but probably my least favorite. Not a whole lot of flavor to this. 
Beef meatball with spicy cilantro - this was good and spicy! The sauce was a cross between a chimichurri and a tomatillo sauce. 
Special of the day - pork meatball with a sweet soy sauce. This was a very rich sauce for me. It was my husband's favorite. 
Chef's vegetables- these were awesome and so simple. 
Pie of the day - peach with crumble topping mmmm
Pecan maple cookie with ice cream and syrup - so good and not overly sweet. It was like a big oatmeal cookie with pecans. 

Come early and try this place.

I've had their Rooster Burger, cookie milkshake, smoked matzo ball soup, and sweet potato coconut curry soup. My favorite was definitely the curry soup, and they give a decent amount with the cup size. I also liked how they give pickled vegetables with the burger. In my opinion, the food isn't something to write home about, but it's decent and for a good cause.

I've been going to Grotto's my whole life, and many people have told me that's why I love their pizza. Is it the best pizza I've ever had? No. But it's always had the same unique taste and I still love it. Try the cheese fries and cheese pizza. It sounds plain, or maybe boring to some, but they get both just right. 

My favorite Grotto's is on The Avenue in Rehoboth. You really can't beat the ambiance there! To be honest I think people either love it or hate it. ISo if you've never had it, give it a try!

Such a fun experience! My boyfriend and I decided to check out Gyu after hearing so many great reviews on their BBQ. We did not have a reservation but the host was very accommodating in getting us a table right away.  Our server, Crystal, was extremely knowledgeable about the menu and helped us decide what to get! The Autumn all you can eat deal is an insane amount of food for the price! And you can't beat a $2 draft beer. We will definitely be returning!!

Went here tonight for our anniversary dinner and we were both severely disappointed. All of the sides were just terrible. The bread was easily the worst bread I've had at any restaurant ever- it seriously tasted like old Wonder bread from a bag. The salad consisted of lettuce from a bag and a squirt of bottled dressing- no cheese, egg, or anything yummy. I decided to splurge for a loaded baked potato (because sides are not included, but that's normal for a fancy restaurant, right?) and it came to me wrapped in foil with the sides on the side, for me to assemble. The beans were really sub par and came in a shared bowl. All of that combined made me feel like I was at 6th grade summer camp in a cafeteria line. Admittedly, the meat was good (I got the Cowgirl and hubby got the ribs) but that was all. We were both wishing we'd gone to Texas Roadhouse instead, which sort of embarrasses me because I love trying local gems. I realized that to me, great sides can make up for mediocre steak, but even a great steak can't help rectify terrible sides. Would have ordered dessert if we weren't so put off. $60 is no small purchase for parents of 2 small kids who don't get out much! Such a disappointment.

This was my 1st time coming to BoneFish Grill.... 

Its a little dark but I must admit my favorite memory of this restaurant was there Bang Bang Shrimp.

Entrees are just ok. 

I would come back but not if I'm starving just for a quick bite to eat.

Service was average
Called 3 times to place a to-go order and no answer: didn't even get to try the food. But I will not now.

Food was outstanding!!!  Everything was so FRESH and delicious! Service was friendly and prompt. Restaurant clean and attractive! Don't be overwhelmed by the plethora of shops and restaurants in the strip mall, once you get past this you'll be VERY happily surprised that you ate at Viet Huong.

This review is just for a single visit to the bar:

When they were around the corner at the Bayshore Royal, this was one of my fave little places... they have grown. Good for them.

Service was great - bartender Mike was attentive and took care of our drink orders. A small plate of garlicky shrimp made my companion very happy. We were having a lovely time...

The bar is a nice place to have a drink, dark, low ceilings, a great place to feel secluded... until the reggae band showed up. Ugh. Does no one realize that that band is waaaayyyy to big for that space? How about a nice DJ as background, or small jazz trio... but no... and so we left.
Stopped into this place during a work trip to New Orleans and was pleased. During happy hour, they have $0.75 oysters and definitely order the Brussel sprout dish as well!

What can I say about Hooters, Hooters is about good descent food with fantastic service.  That was exactly what my wife and I got at this Hooters.

We were visiting the area on business, and looked up the local Hooters while in town.  I know we might of been a little early (5PM on a Tuesday night) for the dinner crowd but I was a little surprised, and concerned, that the restaurant was mostly empty.  We were greeted and seated in short order.  The restaurant was clean and had plenty of televisions with a different game on just about each one from any one viewing angle.

My wife and I enjoy the buffalo wings and buffalo shrimp, so that was what we ordered. The meal arrived shortly and was good.

Now for the second part of my first sentence.  Kelsey was our "Hooters girl" server.  She did a fantastic job of keeping our drink orders full, answering our questions, taking our order and making our stay wonderful.

The food is good, had attitude issues from staff on 2 separate occasions. Went on a Tuesday for lunch with wife and friends, the place was almost empty--told them more were coming and we needed a larger table, they copped attitude a told us they couldn't, they even got the manager who refused to move us. We ordered and eventually the other party showed up and we had to move everything to the table I originally asked for. On another occasion it was 20 min before they took our drink order. It's hit or miss

Dat Dog is like that cute girl you broke up with two years  ago. You see her again and think hmmm...So you go out with her, only to remember, well into the date, just why you broke up with her. With me and DD it is in fact about every two years that I, having forgotten, step in for whatever the F they're serving on wiener bread. I like sausage meats of all varieties, on good bread with quality condiments. DD ain't that. Much is prefab frozen. You want sides? Fries or Tots A la carte. A dog with tots and a beer will run you up to $20. Many condiments and toppings are from a bottle/can/Sysco truck. Service is hipster desultory and sub standard. Decor is "Hey we're brightly colored authentic NOLA!" ...and while I spell the acronym, the staff uses it as a word.  I live and own my home within walking distance of the Frenchmen location and DD's construction on a regular performance lot there was the beginning of the douchey tourist era for that decidedly "not-Bourbon St" music Mecca. Thanks, brahs. From now on it's a Lucky Dog and a street beer for me. Or the very fine , determinedly authentic Bratz Y'all! in the Bywater.

I went to Bricktops for the first time with my husband on our anniversary this past Sunday.  Lucky for us, the weather was amazing, so we opted to sit on their patio.  

We began with the grilled artichoke, which was amazing.  The selection on the menu was pretty good, which made it difficult to decide what to order.  Our waiter suggested the Filet, or the Ahi Salad.  I went with the filet and the 3 cheese macaroni - it was my anniversary afterall.  My husband was going to do the filet until an order of the ribs walked by.  He got the ribs, with creamy spinach and ponzu coleslaw.  (All incredible.)  My filet was awesome, but the mac.  Oh man.  Best mac I've ever had.  And his ribs...literally fell off of the bone.  I always thought that was a saying.  It's not.  They. Fell. Off.  Yum. 

The drinks were good - nothing fancy or special.  We tried to order an after dinner cocktail as well, but they didn't offer anything like that.  (Like an espresso-tini, or something.)  

The service was fantastic as well - our waiter was personable, and about our age.  Side note:  warning - there is a homeless man in a wheelchair in front of the restaurant that apparently is always there.  He's perfectly nice, and doesn't harass...just wanted to mention it.   

I hear the brunch on Sunday's is wonderful, so we most certainly will be back.

My husband and I LOVE this place for both breakfast and dinner.  We drive from St. Pete just to eat here whenever we can.  Everything that we have tried so far is delicious and even the drinks are great.  If you go for brunch, their Bloody Mary is the best.
My friends and I went on a taco Tuesday and they didnt disappoint. The tacos and drinks were on point.

It is both a blessing and curse that this bakery is 2,500 miles away from me. I am still dreaming about the ginger molasses cookies and salted caramel doughnut. I would be as big as a barn if this bakery were in my backyard. In fact, there'd be a serious addiction issue in my future. 

Thank you, kind people of Beiler's, for being a highlight to my recent trip. You have discovered heaven and you put it in a pastry case.

I've been here twice now and both times have been exemplary experiences! 
The newly renovated outdoor space is lovely with plenty of heaters to keep diners comfortable, but it is the food and the staff that will keep me coming back. We shared a La Paloma salad that was fresh and delicious with a perfect crunch of pumpkin seeds and the thinnest sliced apples that are the perfect combination. 
The Mission chicken that has been brined for many hours, is the most tender and flavorful chicken I have ever had. I HIGHLY recommend!
A big thank you to Louie and Amanda for making our evening such a fun and fabulous experience!

UGH THIS PLACE. SUCH A FAN. where have you been all my life!!! ...oh in st. louis. why are you in st. louis while I'm spending my time between Chicago and NYC UGH

This place gives me life. I would drown in all their bubble teas especially their corner 17 bubble tea if I could. It's just so good. It's bubble tea. I also tried their super fruit tea and I literally downed that in less than five minutes. 

Also for the food it's just delicious. It's true honest to God authentic and yummy Chinese food. Share your dishes! They are huge and Chinese food is meant to be family style. Share everything you get and you will get to try and enjoy more. 

I was only in St. Louis for three days and I ate here twice. That's how much I liked it. Even the dessert ("fluff") they called it was amazing. I liked everything- the hand pulled noodles so fresh. Try the wontons in chili oil! Really try those they are SO GOOD. I'm just tripping over my words here. Everything is good. Just go.

(Is it weird that I'm happy this was my 100th review? woo!)

Viva was the perfect location for a party of 23 - the upper room was a great place to gather for a going away party for our friends. The food and service were a wonderful surprise - Our waiter Andrew and his team were very attentive and had just the right touch of taking care of our needs. The pork belly quesadilla and the guacamole dip were perfect. I'll come back just to enjoy those again:)  The entries were definitely "modern mexican", not your standard fare, with creative approaches - the Southwest Chicken and Spinach Salmon salads were amazing as were the Shrimp and Crab enchiladas. All in all a wonderful evening provided by the right touch of class, taste and service. We'll be back!

In town for the National Championship and stumbled across this place.  The blackened grouper sandwich and the fish tacos were amazing!   We ate at the bar and our servers we extremely friendly.  I would definitely recommend it.
We're visiting from Texas and wanted a later breakfast  with drinks perfect ... bloody Mary and the Maine lobster eggs

I really love Ike's Love and Sandwiches! They have the best bread ever, great catering for lunch or dinner, really flavorful sandwiches with tons of meat or vegan and vegetarian options. The staff is friendly and the vibe is great! Totally worth trying out!

Stopped here for a late lunch, at about 3 pm and there was still a long line but it moved rather quick.  We got 2 hot chicken sandwiches and they were awesome, well worth the wait!  Sides were Mac and cheese which is the best I have ever had and my husband got the potato salad which also did not disappoint.  Don't miss this place!
Great service.  Awesome fresh margaritas and amazing tacos.

Went here the other night, a new and very stylish restaurant on what had once been an utterly nondescript stretch of Magazine St. Did the Coolinary menu (plus an extra app). The verdict? Excellent food, excellent service, excellent value. The only thing not excellent? My photos which don't do the dishes full justice. Can I give it 4 1/2 stars?!

I got there around 8pm. It was almost full. I was seated at a four-top, which was fine, tho I did offer to sit at the counter by the kitchen as I didn't want to take up extra space. My server Randy was very knowledgeable and guided me to choices that left me happily sated.

Started with the Verlasso Salmon (fermented Napa cabbage, cashews, cilantro, sweet peppers, sesame seeds, black garlic vinaigrette) SO delicious!! (Note: The presentation was MUCH nicer than my photo; I had already had a bite or two before taking the pic. It arrived in a kinda pyramid formation.) It's the type of dish you want to have another of as soon as you finish eating it. Sometimes in a dish like this you get lotsa the extras and only a little of the featured item. Not here; there was LOTS of salmon!

Decided to splurge and also get the Roasted Bone Marrow with pistachio pesto, oven roasted cherry tomatoes and watermelon radish slices, as you don't often see this on menus. Not only was it very very good but (a) unlike some places where you just get the marrow and some bread or, in this case, baguette slices, here the pistachio pesto, oven roasted cherry tomatoes, watermelon radish slices and, a goodly amount of, I believe, dill, fleshed it out wonderfully & imaginatively and (b) for a change, there was a pleasingly plentiful amount of baguette slices so I didn't have to ask for more. Bone marrow may not be to everyone's taste...which just means more for me!!

Crispy Pork Chop (grilled corn, mint, cucumber, avocado, buttermilk, watermelon molasses) Crispy it was; I actually thought it was too crispy, but hadn't realized that was what it was billed as--though I wouldn't've minded it being a little more tender/moister, I guess you can't complain about something for being what it's supposed to be. That said, the watermelon molasses (the brown swirl around the pork chop) was so yummy it should be sold in sex shops for people to spread all over their partner's body after which it can be licked off. Lol Seriously, I asked my server for more of it and covered that part of the chop that wasn't already covered with the buttermilk. I don't think I licked its ramekin...but I sure wanted to! 

Salted Caramel Budino (orange and pistachio)  I wasn't familiar with the budino concept and, while I enjoy caramel, the pleasures of the "Salted" part always escape me; once I got to the pudding beneath the caramel topping, however, I didn't want it to end!

I also had a very nice, and nicely priced, glass of the Syrah/Cinsault/Grenache rose. Light, refreshing, not too dry and with a nice bouquet, it was just what I was in the mood for.

About the only glitch was when I asked the maître d' if he could turn up the light a little bit as it was awfully dark at my table; it didn't seem like it would be a big deal as the lights had momentarily bumped up just before. He came back a few minutes later saying that "the manager was busy" so apparently he couldn't do anything about it. I understand that staffing there is a little crazy due to COVID challenges but this hadn't seemed like a biggie. He did offer to move me to another table but by then I had settled in so declined. Not a biggie but it would've been nice to better see my food.

I understand that due to COVID craziness, most of The Bower's menu (the cheese and charcuterie boards) is currently from its adjacent bistro, Claret. When things return to normal, I was told that The Bower's options would expand offering more entrees along the lines of what I had. Can't wait!

This place is crazy. I don't know why it has so many bad reviews. It's a dive bar in Soulard, they're supposed to be mean- it adds character. But how many dive bars have you been to that have waitresses that only wear body paint? Seriously, that's worth at least 3 stars right there..... it's not for the faint of heart or those with delicate sensibilites.

Bucket list for sure ! Everything was what I expected. I had the chargrilled oysters, boo fries which are smothered in roast beef with cheese and gravy & soft shell crab poboy!! Definitely would come again. Wait Time is crazy be ready to stand outside

So we had a 7:45 reservation and were SUPER excited to eat here. I'm a total seafood freak and had heard great things about this spot. We arrive at 7:45 and our table wasn't ready, we had to wait for close to 20 minutes. there's realy no where to wait, except outside, due to the size of the place so we sat outside in the freezing cold for 20 minutes..not a good way to start my meal. When we wlaked in, there was a table right by the front door and the people at the table were complaining about the table being right by the opening door. When it was our turn to get sat, I assume the server moved the other couple to what was supposed to be our table, and we got stuck with this terribly positioned table. To make it worse, they restaurant placed the coat rack directly behind one of the chairs of this table, so for the 3 miutes we sat there people were leaning over my chair sifting through the pile of coats. We ended up leaving, there's NO WAY i'm goign to spend that kind of money to sit at a freezing cold table with the coat rack situation. WE asked to move, but there were no more tables. All in all, total customer service fail on behalf of little fish. It's too bad because the food looked great, but I'll never know.
I ordered the ginger beef, and sweet and sour pork. There was hardly any meat in it but mostly breading. Would not recommend and will never order from them again.

Totally love Taco Bell, unfortunately it's a hit or miss. Seriously 95% of the time my order is wrong, I debate with myself on if I want to take a chance and come to this store, especially if it's after I get off of work and chance the drive through, because this store runs slow. I suck it up and just accept what I was given, and half the time I've paid extra for items that are not received. Please get it together.

This was my first time eating an Italian beef sandwich and oh my goodness it was delicious!!   I got the Mama's Italian Beef sandwich and that came with mozzarella cheese on it along with the  hot giardiniera.  They asked if i wanted it wet or dry and i decided to get it dry because it's a texture thing for me but I'll try it wet next time.  The owner was extremely nice and came to ask us if the food was good and if everything else was good.  I look forward to eating here again soon.  I also tried the slice of cheesecake and it was really tasty too.

Great foods, and service.  The place is quite classy, so don't be walking in dressing up in t shirt, shorts, flip flops, etc.  this joint is pretty pricy, but the foods are well worth it.  I added the $28 for the wine pairing.  Four red, and three white.  Very good wines, and generous portion too.  We ordered the filet mignon, salmon, and the t-bone turned out to be the most delicious.  Big plate of salads, and bravo for not being stingy like some other restaurant serving it in tiny plate were you can finish it with two bites.  The dessert are good, not excellent.
Minus one star for the hostess for not being too friendly.  I'm a very good tipper, but if you don't wear suits and tie that don't matter to them I guess?

I had an Acai bowl... of that we're the only item ordered here, I probably would rate the restaurant a little lower only because the person who made the bowl put less than an inch of the Acai on the bottom and about two inches of granola, berries, etc on top. An Acai bowl should be a little more balanced than that. We ordered carry out so I couldn't ask them to add more Acai, unfortunately. My husband had the tuna appetizer which was phenomenal. If I were writing this review based on this item only, it would a solid five stars. I absolutely will try this restaurant a second time and will adjust this rating / review accordingly. I do recommend giving this place a try... I think the Acai bowl situation was a simple error in someone possibly not knowing the ratios of building bowl.

I don't know... might have been the sushi, might have been anti-biotics on the salad greens, might have been in the water for all I know, but the day after I ate here, ...
Let's just say it wasn't pleasant to be me.

If it wasn't their fault, I'm sorry. Lunch was a pleasant experience on a very nice early Spring day with a table by the open garage doors. 

The sushi choices overwhelm the menu - three times as many ways to say "rice" in Japan as there are ways to describe a dozen sandwiches. Cobb salad with salmon upgrade for me, was "just OK", as three stars describes it. Too much iceberg lettuce, not enough anything else. Nice bowl. Took a long time to arrive given we both ordered a cold lunch. 

My wife had sushi. She gave me some. She was fine the next day, so I assume the sushi is safe.

My favorite breakfast/brunch spot of all time. Everything I've ordered has been so delicious every time I go and they never disappoint. 
I'm addicted to the green chili french toast but today I tried the the pork belly Beni. Loved it. Killed it.

This is my absolute favorite restaurant. If it's melt in your mouth steaks in sizzling butter you want with equally amazing sides and service this is where you need to be. I laughed at my wife the first time she got the chicken, but wow, even that was amazing. There isn't one bad item on the menu.

My husband and I where visiting from California and stopped here after a Genos  Cheese steak everyone was Super friendly and very great service. Delicious cannoli's !!  Would love to come back to this lovely place!!

I ordered take out from Thai Kitchen so I can't speak for the actual restaurant.  This is the first Thai place that I've ever known to offer this service.  The phone call to place the order ended up being a bit awkward because of the strong accent.  The delivery man arrived quickly smelling as though he had just smoked 15 cigarettes on the .6 mile drive to my house.  I found this entertaining for some reason.

The food was excellent.  I ordered green curry chicken and she ordered chicken fried rice.  I had planned on saving half of it for dinner but found myself unable to resist the urge to eat the whole meal immediately.

If you are in Metairie and are looking for really good Chinese take-out, then this is the place! They have a large menu to choose from with many great combination plate options. I recommend their crab rangoons, wonton soup, sesame chicken, chicken lo mein and egg foo yung. 
I also like that they have a big box of fortune cookies sitting out and you can take however many you want. Not like some places, where they can be stingy and you have to pay extra for 1 more.
***Make sure to look for the coupons on the front of their take-out menu and get some free stuff with your order!
I always call ahead and get my order to go. So, I don't know what it's like eating there.

Went here last week with my family as our first meal out since COVID. We were all super excited. The bread, as always, was unreal. Delicious. Never fails. The outdoor seating is on their roof which is very nice. The service was really good, probably because they only have about 8 tables at a time. The food was only okay. We all ordered salmon medium and it all came over cooked. Only real complaint I have.

This place is amazing!!! It's different than other Korean restaurants as they don't use gas for the grills, just hot coals. The banchan are AMAZING, and the meat portions are huge!!! They even have steamed egg!!! Highly recommended!!!! Korean food can be pretty pricey for the meat dishes, which is the case here, but it's worth it. Since it;s in Olney, I'll only go during daylight hours.

The seafood was really flawless. The ambiance gave off a local and divey vibe, which simply isn't for me. I thought the menu choices were limited. I wouldn't return, although for the right patron there is nothing bad per se about the service or the food.
Love this place. The crab croquets are very meaty and full of flavor. The fish dish is fantastic....Lightly breaded, yellow rice and beans with plantains. Yum.

When my sister told me Mai Lee's is what got her through two years of MBA school in St. Louis, I knew this was a must try. We both love pho, and if she could eat this three times a week, it must be good. While it really is not as good as Golden Deli (in LA), it's comparable, and that's saying a lot. The flavor is decent, but what I really enjoyed here was the chicken curry. Wow. The lemongrass flavor pairs perfectly with the coconut milk, and the chicken is so tender. There are strands of glass noodle which is also a plus. Overall, really good Vietnamese food, and I would definitely return for the chicken curry.

I really want to write a good review of this place after hearing friends tell me how good it is. I was disappointed. Its a pretty simple review. Service was lack luster, employees didn't offer a smile at all. Food order took a long time to come out. Food was cold and my eggs were overcooked. The melon garnish was delish. :-/
One word. Wings! Great wings. Fish tacos rock too. Sat at the bar. Super friendly bartender and huge selection of IPAs! The artwork and paintings are superb too

You may find better Chinese food near the Main Line but the overall experience and price at Yang Ming is worthy of three stars.  The food is good and the atmosphere is quiet.

I usually order the Peking duck that is prepared tableside.

I was pleased to find this sort of upscale fast food during our brief visit to Tucson. The thin crust pizza used fresh ingredients and good quality cheese. The salad was tasty and macaroni and cheese were good but the grilled cheese was far too bland, skip it.

For this place, I requested that yelp be able to give negative infinity stars. Let's start off this WONDERFUL review with some knowledge, I believe the waiters will need this. Celiac disease is an autoimmune disorder that prevents a person from eating gluten. When a person ingests gluten, he or she will get EXTREMELY sick. Even the tiniest amount. If a piece of bread touches another piece of food it is contaminated and cannot be eaten by a celiac. Now to the story.
So shrimp and veggies with rice was ordered off the GLUTEN FREE menu and when it arrived there was a piece of bread! The waiter was questioned if it was gluten free bread and he said sarcastically, "of course not!" (Does he even know what gluten free means?!) He then says gluten doesn't work that way. Let me inform the restaurant of something. I am celiac and EVERY CELIAC AND GLUTEN FREE FOODIE KNOWS CROSS CONTAMINATION EXISTS.
I have gotten sick multiple times from stuff like this occurring. If necessary, the business can message me and we can review the other times and proof. I am outraged that a business can offer a "gluten-free menu", but have a poorly educated staff, never mind a sarcastic one! 
And to top this wonderful review off, there was no apology and the waiter wouldn't get the manager. 
So for the rude waiter who refused to say his name or wear his name tag, try being a celiac and in severe pain for a month and tell me how cross contamination doesn't exist.

Again, stellar service from the bar top on a friday night. Continuing my "let's try something new" I tried the salmon sandwich.  If you like or are craving fish, it definitely satisfies that craving. I wanted sushi but the boyfriend wanted burgers. Let's just say we both got our fix. 
Campfire sauce and bottomless fries always a plus, I've said it before. Again my good experiences outweigh my bad, so I can't say anything bad about the place.
I highly recommend the Mad Love or the Wiskey River burgers if you want deliciousness

Had heard about this Youtuber Ghost Kitchen burger concept on the interwebs so we decided ti try it when we saw it popped up on doordash. We got the mrbeast burger, nashville hot chicken sandwich, mrbeast fries and a plain order of fries. Overall everything was pretty good, took about an hour from order to prep to delivery. Food came hot still.

Our favorite would definitely be the chicken sandwich. Perfect amount of spice, loved thebsauce and the chicken was crunch juicy and perfectly fried! The mrbeast fries were also pretty good, although the onions were missing we still liked the sauce and pickles all over it. The burger reminded me of in n out burgers but twice the price, overall not bad fornafast food burger but def expensive. But it hits the spot so I'd get it again if I was craving a basic burger. The plain fries were ok. Lost any crunch in transit but the seasoning on it was great. Was delicious the next day as leftovers after popping it in the toaster oven!

I visited the restaurent  3 weeks ago the food and service was excellent I went on mothers day the service was good but the food wasn't , I hand mango tuna which had no taste ,my daughter had macaroni with crabmeat which was tasteless and my son had ribs which very overcooked. My pasta was watery.I might think twice before I try the restaurent again

I have no idea how they do it, but this place is amazing! I have tried black sugar boba at other places, but this is by far the best. This place has a very limited drink menu, but they honestly don't need to expand. Lines are out the door and for good reason.

My favorite is the number 2 - it has pearl and jelly. It's so refreshing and love that the balance of milk to tea is just right. If you have never been a fan of black sugar teas, this place will surely change your mind. I go places ordering this, but am always disappointed bc it doesn't taste like Tiger Sugar.

Keep up the great work guys! Can't wait to take all my family members who visit Ctown here.

We went there to celebrate a friend's birthday, group of 7. We tried the $35 tasting menu. We  had brussel sprouts, the octopus salad, pita with different dips, artichoke and entrees.  Other than the brussel sprouts, which was great, everything was ok. The octopus while great had overwhelming amount of feta and onions. I had the salmon entree which was very low on seasoning, as was the papardelle. My friends who had the sole felt the same way. For dessert,  the molten chocolate cake was very good. The rice pudding was exceedingly sweet with a ton of cinnamon. 
Also, they are cash only,   which was an added inconvenience. I don't plan on going back

We order carry out or eat in probably 2-3 times a month. This is hands down the best Thai in Nashville and is vegan, vegetarian friendly. The wait staff is very accommodating and friendly. Great prices and excellent Thai spice, if you like it hot!

My bf and I thoroughly enjoyed our meal here.  He had the crabmeat ravioli.  I had the meatball/sausage spaghetti and we shared the crab and corn bisque.  All were outstanding.  The service was excellent and Vincent even came to talk with us!  The creme brûlée was phenomenal!  Thank you for a wonderful time Vincent!  We will definitely be back.

This is my new take out casual restaurant of choice in South Tampa. I had the chicken roll up meal (now greek chicken wrap), and it was very, very good.  A friend introduced me to this place years back (st pete location) for the Greek salad w. Grilled Chicken. Although I live closer to Louis Pappas, I would make the few minutes extra drive with no hesitation to go to Little Greek. I will only go to  LP for a chopped salad (with no meat) or the pita chips.

I finally ordered from here and let me just say my family and I was very satisfied with our choices of fried chicken wings a 10 piece, a quart of shrimp fried rice, and a small beef and broccoli! The price for whole order was very reasonable and for being a  first time customer the woman who took my order threw in a free egg roll!!! I will definitely be coming back soon to try other things!

Great spot just off Drexel campus. Good brunch options. Friendly staff. Sabrina's is situated in a historic house with a rich history so it would've been great that the staff was knowledgeable about it or the menu had a brief history included.

Cabo's just opened! I'm giving a 3 because they are new and like any new restaurant they have their issues to work out.(ie staff,kitchen,) On another note the atmosphere is posh and they flavored of the food were yummy. I will go back in a month and retry to see if they have changed.

This is my second time here, and again it did not disappoint.  We walked in which is unusual for a NOLA restaurant but we were lucky. Our waiter, Maurice was very knowledgeable and exceptionally attentive which is rare nowadays. We had great cocktails- their house mixed/barreled bourbon was excellent. Until t'amaro and damn thistle were tasty. We shared several dishes, including a dozen of the visiting raw oysters (small and salty the way we love them), the crab bisque, back strap, gator/mirliton dish, and duck hearts.  It was great. Highly recommend for a very unusual menu.

hands down, THE BEST HOT CHICKEN in the world. I am not exaggerating. This place is the best. I had chicken and pancakes. Scorge was the heat level I chose and it was definitely spicy; but a tasteful yummy delicious spicy. The pancakes were the yummiest pancakes ever. the person in the kitchen knows whats up. Chicken and pancakes breakfast came with chicken, pancakes, eggs, and home fries and ya'll....I ate every bit of food and am happily full but not a heavy full...a happy full. remember it is hot chicken and truly is spicy. Just also, very delicious which a lot of hot chicken places are no where nearly as delicious as Slow Burn Hot Chicken.

Savory sweet whatever you like! It all comes served large and in charge within a crepe .. duh! I've tried several crepes here my favorite has to be their chicken and berry crepe :) beautiful garden out back that is also dog friendly ! Perfect for relaxing anytime of the day. Often times when I am out on 4th.. its either Cafe Marcel or the Co-op when it comes to deciding where I want to eat!! yes I am comparing this place to the Co-Op because its just that amazing

I wish I could do the .5 stars and give this place 4.5 however "Yay! I'm a Fan!" does indeed accurately describe my sentiments.

This is my absolute favorite place for martinis. My Hendricks martini slightly dirty has consistently been perfection. They also carry some of my favorite whiskys (Try the Glenmorangie Nectar D'or!). 
To make it better, they have the most sour fresh sourdough bread brought to tables (OH SO YUM!). I am a sourdough fiend and very much appreciate a nice chewy sourdough.
Dinner and their specials have always been very good but I reserve that 5th star for restaurants that blow me away. Call me stingy if you must. I do love the oysters rockefeller and their burger among other great dishes. I often go for their seafood specials and have always been happy. 
Aside from occasionally waiting a few mins to be greeted at the host area for a table, service is consistently good and food is prompt. Servers have always been attentive without popping in too often and are knowledgeable about the menu. You may say "well, duh. They're supposed to be," but you'd be amazed the number of restaurants that have staff that doesn't know where their fish came from or even what some of dishes taste like! But, I digress, KingFisher meets all of my customer service needs. 

Heavenly martinis, great food, excellent service... What else do I need? Happy to say KingFisher shall remain a regular on my dining out for dinner schedule :)
Love their spicy crispy cucumber, mung bean noodle in black bean sauce, and west lake beef soup. 川北涼粉, 西湖牛肉羹,蒜蓉黃瓜. Trust me

I took my wife here for dinner. First time at Gino's and we were not disappointed. A rare gem tucked away, the atmosphere was pleasant. 
 The wait staff were very professional and gave excellent service. We were not disappointed with the menu. Portions we're generous and quite authentic. The salad and bread, hit the spot!
 I will recommend this spot to everyone, reasonably priced and worth a visit.

I haven't been to Yamato in about 15 years.. Growing up this was my father's go to place for sushi.. We were literally there once a week.  

My brother and I decided to head to Yamato for lunch and to check in.. Turns out the owner is still standing behind the sushi bar making the same amazing rolls.  

We ordered egg rolls,  Philadelphia roll,  California roll,  salmon and a shrimp tempura roll.  Everything was delicious and the way it is presented makes you feel good about spending the money. 

I should note we only had sushi on the with th  egg rolls,  but they do have an extensive menu for lunch and dinner.  

This is not your typical sushi bar.. This is somewhere you want to go when you want really good sushi or a true Japanese meal.  I will Definitely make it a point to go back and enjoy their food again soon.
We have always been beyond satisfied with the service and the food and COFFEE!! This has become one of our favorite places to go!
The food is decent here (So is the coffee), but I went here twice and both times, I saw the girl behind the counter handle money and then prepare the food with no gloves on.
Great time tonight with at least 11 people in  our party great food and service.

I only wish I could give this place 0 Stars. This restaurant (so they call it) had the NERVE to serve some watered down tomato sauce and call it 'CREOLE'. I was so offended and pissed. The waitress was not very observant of my disgust or just  wasn't in the mood to deal with the issue. I wasn't rude but still wasn't asked if I wanted something else. I requested to have the 'alfredo' sauce instead and was given mayo with parmesan cheese - much worse than canned alfredo, it was really tragic. Now, I don't own a restaurant but WHEN I do open mine I will never compromise the integrity of flavors like this place did. The food was bland and lifeless. Shouldve gone for something they couldn't mess up like.... fried shrimp? Although, I didn't hear that was so great either. I'm creole and eat creole food regularly, didn't expect this to happen IN the French Quarter.

Would give a 0 if I could. Ordered a Gyro. Typically one would expect that a Pita place could do that. This was the worst Gyro I ever ate. The meat was reheated on a grill and tasted terrible. It was overstuffed with veggies and was unrecognizable as a Gyro. The pita was poor. It was clean. My family had sandwiches which were average at best. Will never go or send anyone I like to this place. The emphasis is clearly on the Pit in the name.

This place was so disappointing, to start it's in the middle of nowhere. I stood on line for about 40mins in the hot sun, only to get Chicken that had wayyyyy to much batter.  You get three pieces of  chicken with your order, and it looks really good until you pull it apart. Then you see, it's mostly batter. The red beans and rice is also overrated, not much seasoning.  The corn bread taste like jiffy corn bread. So I ask myself how the heck did this place get on the travel channel and why does everyone talk about this place WHY?????????
So no I'm sorry I don't recommend. I've had so much better, not worth the wait.

I've been going to Alfredo in Berwyn since it opened. I like the exposed brick decor, and always get my corner table by the window. It's convenient when meeting people for a casual dinner in-between home and the city. 
I didn't know how I was on Mercato's email list until I saw the webpage which branded it as "Mercato by Alfredo of Berwyn." The webpage featured a picture that looked like a tab "now featuring our fall menu', but when you try to click on it nothing happens, so you're not able to preview the menu online. I looked for the restaurant on Open Table as I use it to book at Alfredo but they aren't listed, come to find they use Yelp's system. Arriving at 6:30 Sunday almost every table except three were taken. The bar was full. Our reservation was honored without wait, unlike, cough* Limoncello cough*. The service was good, very attentive but anxious and hurried, yet didn't make us feel rushed. We were watered but bread didn't come immediately. The waiter asked if we'd like drinks which were declined he noticed we didn't have bread, then asked if we'd like it and that he'd grab it for us, came back to ask if we'd prefer olive oil. Once returned asked if we were ready to order when I asked him if there were any additions to the menu, he quickly and apologetically read them from his book. There was someone shadowing him that he, (I hope), was training. After reading the specials we asked for a minute. We ordered the asparagus app and the arincini, I orderd a gnocchi special and my company the papperadelle. The menu is similar to Avalon in that they are listed in courses, unlike Avalon I did not see a pre fixe or pairing menu. Avalon also prices a smaller plate and entree size, there was only one price per plate here. We opted for the apps and pasta and forewent the entree and salads. The bread was good though balsamic was in the oil, I order it tabled to add your own, no big deal, if that's how they do it I'll live. The arincini was prepared well and had good flavor but was not hot, some bites were cold. The marinara was very good. The asparagus was different but enjoyable, it didn't need the runny egg on it but was still good. Not impressed yet. Honestly I only ordered the gnocchi because originally I though he said it was a ravioli special, I misheard him and since I didn't want to make him come back, ordered the gnocchi, which, God forgive me, I really don't like. I actually enjoyed it. It was very good, I didn't finish it all because remember, I don't like gnocchi. My company enjoyed the papperadelle and was very pleased. Redemption! I ordered coffee and dessert the dessert menu was quite limited, only four options. I have a feeling that's because I think the desserts are actually made in house from the taste of them. (incidentally, I saw the owner of Yori's bakery a few tables away, hope he wasn't looking for a customer.) Bread pudding was a dessert special this evening, the waiter mentioned. I quipped, "you get that many old people here?" The waiter boasted, "yes we do!" Only two desserts on the menu did not have alcohol one of which was the pumpkin cheesecake. Honestly I am not impressed with pumpkin anything this time of year, ooh, sugar cinnamon and nutmeg, feh. So I ordered the pumpkin cheesecake (insert LOL), It was actually good. It was topped with pecans ( I think, could've been sugar smacks for all I know) and a caramel drizzle, The top was a little too sugary but if you mixed it together with the center it balanced out well. All and all, I'm going back. Like I said the entrées redeemed the apps, the service really tried hard and they were very busy for being new, I think once they get in the vibe they'll be fine. This is a place in West Chester I want to like. I will stop back within two weeks to give it another shot. To sum it up You're not leaving hungry,  I don't know that I would've been able to fit an entrée, I would have to omit the pasta dish if I were to order an entrée in the future.
