Everyone in the place seemed to be enjoying themselves and the place did smell wonderful. Somewhat difficult layout entering & exiting the bar area for as crowded as it was. Two appetizers, two pasta dishes, one dessert and coffee $70. (w/o tip or booze), A little pricey but better quality than some of the other places in town although I don't know that everyone will recognize and appreciate that difference, I hope they will.
I went there last night 2.26.15 around 7p.  It was really slow, but the first time I tried it.  I got a shrimp roll made right in front of me.  It was excellent and worth the money.

Aldo's Pizzarama on Bustleton Avenue in far Northeast Philadelphia has been at the same location for a couple of generations, and has the reputation for making the best pie in this part of the city. Perhaps, it has changed hands since those opinions were expressed, but it was not our experience when we stopped in for dinner over the weekend. 

The guys behind the counter, although not busy, seemed unwilling to crack a smile or offer any service beyond taking our order and shouting out when the pizza or steak sandwich was ready, for us to pick up and deliver to ourselves. No silverware, no napkins, no courtesy offered. 

My son liked the steak, but said it was not worth the drive to have it. The pizza looked great with crisped sausage slices and well done crust. The problem was the overuse of cheese out of proportion to the sauce. It was such a heavy layer that the undercarriage could not support the topside. Lifted from the outer edge left the center of the slice on the aluminum pan with its contents sliding off. The work involved in folding the slices allowed us to taste how salty the cheese and red sauce were. Just not a good pizza, despite the decent crust. 

Won't be back.
Warning! The 4th Street Cafe is addictive.  Homemade cakes, great coffee, delicious,reasonably priced food. But mostly, interesting people and good conversation.  Bonus--the cleanest place in town.

Delicious food, fast, friendly service, but holy crap, drinking here is expensive. The three of us ordered a plate of steak nachos, crab guacamole, and we each had 2 (delicious) watermelon margaritas (short rocks glass filled with ice) -- total bill without tip: $100 - $72 of it was for the margaritas, and I was barely buzzed. Ordering a pitcher is a better deal, but you're not getting out of there under $100 unless you stick with water or soft drinks.

Stopped in before reading the reviews. Glad I did as my experience was very different than most. Sat at the bar. Bartender was friendly and attentive. Got the chicken lime ciabatta. It was okay, toasted nicely tho a little light on chicken. Yeah it's pricey but you're in an airport so it's going to be. Other reviewers must not travel that much as you always pay a premium in airports. Manager was visible and nice as well. Folks at the bar definitely had a good time.

This place is crazy busy! I went on a Saturday night at 6, and had to wait about 45 mins in the bar just to be able to sit down. Service was good. Food was good. Not killer Cajun/creole, but the gumbo is very good. Nice place, food is fresh and hot Nc reasonably priced.

We joined friends there for dinner last week. The food was amazing and our service was top shelf including a visit from Mollie to explain the specials and take our dinner order. It's our new favorite restaurant in Santa Barbara!

This place is incredible! I'm so glad I stopped in for a quick lunch. They have FREE SAMPLES! When I couldn't decide between two of the entrees that I sampled, they said I can mix and match -so that's exactly what I did! As someone with dairy and gluten allergies, I really loved how clearly they had so many options for me. Fully recommend!

Tried the V-Spot burger while it was a Green Festival in New Orleans. It was so good that I sought out the place. While in the in Washington DC, I stopped in a bookstore with a restaurant in the back. Those that have been there know the place I'm talking about. I ordered the "Impossible Burger ". It was amazing. Now that I'm back in New Orleans, I found the only place to eat a meatless burger with great taste, and a BIG bite. Enjoy!

Needed a quick injection of fried chicken and was directed to this place from our hotel. I know the decor may not be up to date but the food was amazing. The drinks were awesome especially the Bloody Mary. Will definitely be venturing back to this establishment again.
Tasty! I love Lanzhou noodle in China. This is the best Lanzhou noodle I ever have in US.
One of the best sushi spot in WC! Excellent food and service! Well done Kooma! I will definitely come back!

Update 10/7/18

This month, they are celebrating Mac and Cheese. Not mere Mac and Cheese but 5 versions worthy of attention. Choose from Lobster, meatballs, and shrimp  as variations on a theme. 

I chose the Cowboy Mac and Cheese. First, this is a huge serving. It would challenge a hungry Saints defensive tackle huge. The thing was almost 3-inches thick.

They "slice" the Mac and Cheese into two layers, each about 1/2 to 3/4 inches thick. Inside was a generous layer of Serrano bbq pulled pork. Sweet and deep flavor. 

They guild this Lilly with a lot of creamy cheese and Gouda. I brought half of it home for a snack today. Okay, maybe two snacks. Or breakfast. 

Located in the Clearview Mall near the AMC cinemas, access is relatively easy from either I-10  or Veterans Memorial Blvd. Adequate parking is available. 

The decor is more on the contemporary side and is family friendly. When we visited, tables were readily available and we were seated quickly. There are a range of wines and other beverages available. The menu is diverse in that while the focus is pasta, they have a lot of their own interpretations of non-Italian dishes. 

The bread was was outstanding: nice crunchy crust but lite and soft inside. It is served with whipped butter. Yummy. The "side" salad was very large and could be its own meal. 

I chose the double cheese burger penne pasta. Very large and tasty. Juicy pieces of ground beef topped with chopped tomato, lettuce, cheese, and a tasty barbecue sauce. It was served over the penne and everything was topped by skinny cut French fries. The flavors worked well. Very well. 

The chicken Parmesan was served over Angel hair. The chicken was sautéed breast meat and topped with a marinara sauce. Again, large serving with very nice flavor. 

Interestingly, the servers use iPad type tablets to take and transmit your order. The wine selections are distinguished by their button color. Red for the reds and yellow for the whites. The Sauvignon Blanc had a red button so our server was momentarily confused when a white was requested. No, it's a red. No, it's a white; hence the "blanc". No biggy. Quickly cleared up and served.

I liked the food and service and there are a couple other interesting interpretations I want to try.

This is a friendly little coffee shop in the neighborhood that I would highly recommend for you to chase away your hangover blues. You can get food to go, or take a seat and have breakfast served to you.

As for the coffee, they've got it all! One day I had some cold brew, the next day I had a latte. Both were great.

Some of the pastries looked a little iffy but the rest of them were amazing. I opted for the scone both days, just because it was so good!

Nice switch of pace to sit back and relax after a honky tonk overload. My buddies and I are Hookah pheens wanted to get a good bowl during our trip to Nash. This place seemed like the best fit. Its really close to broadway, they serve drinks and is a place we can continue our party. The place was kind of empty for a friday night. But all that mattered was the hookah, it smoked pretty good, and was packed pretty well. Its a nice looking place! Ps the server didnt know what baklava was, even though its on the menu. PPS and know I know why, because it was pretty bad.

I don't really like to gamble, so my experiences here are limited to say the least.  

I've gambled here maybe twice.  I cannot stand to lose money so usually my experiences here are limited to events or to parking in their garage for a local event.  

That said, the parking here is borderline horrid.  Borderline.  Not quite full blown horrid, but borderline.  

The problem is that this garage is easy to get lost in.  I never find my car right away.  I never seem to return from the same door I left from.  I don't know why, but it happens every time!

My biggest issue though is the people that use the garage.  It is NOT a NASCAR track!  The last visit I had here, I was nearly hit by three different cars that felt a need to whip around corners at high rates of speed.  The security team needs to do something to enforce these reckless drivers!

As for the hotel, I think it is a nice place to stay.  I couldn't tell you if the price is worth it because the rooms I've seen have always been comped.  I have family from KC that gambles all the time, and they seem to be in town a few times per year thanks to comp vouchers.  

The restaurants, bars, and other little shops are ok, I don't spend time in any of them, but they always look to be full of people having a good time!

The service was great here , I ordered and the food showed up almost minutes later hot and I was greeted by a friendly delivery guy . Now the food in my opinion was not good . The pizza and the fries literally had no taste at all . Very bland to say the least . Everyone is different and has different tastes but for me It just didn't cut it .

Keep it simple should be the motto of this establishment. The lobster roll is simply a buttered toasted maine style hot dog roll and lobster meat with salt and pepper.. not even any celery or mayo. The price will make your wallet lighter but the trip down the stairs at Lukes may make you think you tunneled to Maine, and came up in Bar Harbor.  Top it off you can get Maine produced soda, in blueberry or ginger flavors.

Awesome sandwiches and breakfast croissants. Friendly staff, efficient service.  We ate lunch there but it is more of a take out place. There are counters with stools if you eat in. I had the Morty- mortadella, fresh mozzarella with olive spread, arugula and tomatoes. It was excellent. I will definitely go back!

I had read all the good reviews about this place and my friend recommended this place so I thought I'd check it out.  The food itself left much to be desired.  The portions were small for all three of us.  I got the spicy lamb (#10 on the menu) which was roughly $14 and was disappointed with it.  It wasn't very tender, although it did have a lot of spice.  Honestly, it didn't taste much better than a can of Stagg chili I could've bought at the store for $1.50.  Being a vegetarian, guest number 2 in our party got the veggie sampler ($12) which included three samples of veggie dishes on the menu.  When I asked him what he thought of his food, he said it was okay but nothing special.  Guest number 3 in our party got a beef dish (#6 on the menu, $12).  When I asked her what she thought of the food, she said it could've used more flavor.  So on all three accounts, the food kinda sucked.

I have read reviews where people said they had to wait 40+ minutes for their food.  We were pleasantly surprised that it only took about 10-15 minutes after ordering for our food to arrive.  Maybe it was the time of day that makes the difference (we went Sunday night at 8pm).  The waitress was polite but those two things are basically the only two good things I can think of my experience.  

None of us will be going back, but this was only our experience.

Dinner last Saturday was awesome at Gratzzi, the filet mignon melted in my mouth and my husband's
Salmon was cooked and seasoned perfectly. The only thing I would change is the waiter, he was not very kind. I still enjoyed my dinner

Chose Thali for a meal on date night. I like the meal presentation and all you can eat option, but not the random food selections. It does feel great knowing your entire platter is plant-based! The lentils were GREAT as well as the pumpkin-based option I was given. I will visit again.

This Wendy's is my go to! I work across the street,so I'm here often. Manager Chris, and associate Justin are usually the one that help place my order. They almost have it memorized. I've NEVER had a problem here. The staff is always helpful! I've been through the drive threw once, and they were also polite. See you soon!

Came here for a late dinner not knowing what to expect, and wow did we leave impressed. 

Me and my boyfriend got here right as their late night happy hour started which offered a selection of draft beers for $4 and certain small plates (tapas) for $3, which we thought was a great deal. We started of with a few different small plates to share:

Roti Canai- it came with 2 rotis (which were really good but tasted exactly like the ready made freezer rotis my mom used to buy from the store so I was a little disappointed that they weren't made fresh at the restaurant) and a super yummy and flavorful curry dipping sauce. Although I was disappointed with the roti, I'm still glad I ordered this and got to try it 

Summer rolls- assorted vegetables wrapped in rice paper and served with a peanut dipping sauce. Simple and really refreshing in my opinion, it was the one dish we ordered that wasn't full of flavor so I enjoyed the simplicity 

Korean meatballs and twice fried wings- my boyfriend will refuse to come back unless we order this again. Enough said.

Mushroom salad (don't remember what it was actually called)- average. Just tasted like lettuce drenched in a salty dressing.

We also ordered the shrimp Tom yom soup to share and that was most definitely my favorite part. The broth was the perfect combination of spicy and tangy, and the shrinks and vegetables really complimented each other. 

Apart from the food, it was really a great atmosphere. The service was great and it was very lively on a Saturday night. I also enjoyed how the food came out as it was ordered instead of sitting under a heating lamp.

Love Love Love this restaurant, the chef is a Master! Each time we have experienced is absolutely amazing! Thank you for Always going above and beyond! The Food exquisite, so very fresh, the service outstanding, every detail is met beautifully!!!
Thank you for All your Constant hard work!!!
Really cool spot, the waffles are really great but their coffee is what really does it for me. Perhaps a little pricey however but a great treat!

Had breakfast twice hear on a recent trip. For a guy from NYC, this place is on par with a decent diner. Had the bananas foster French toast the first time. Not high end decadence like at Brennan's, but good all the same. Had the eggs with fried oysters the second. Considering this is supposed to be one of their signature dishes, thought the oysters were going to be incorporated with the eggs somehow. It turned out to be your standard egg plate, with a few oysters on the side. Still good, but nothing really signature about it.

In e end, if you're looking for a quick breakfast (and by quick I mean the service, not the line) that won't break the bank, this is a good place to go.

Had a tasty meal here - salmon topped with crab meat. Delicious!! Also had an appetizer - bang bang shrimp? A little spicy but very tasty. Service was excellent. We had Harneet and she was really good.

Great local Italian restaurant serving delicious steaks and pasta. La trattoria has become a fan favorite in our household due to their steak/pasta combo. With the ability to have pasta as a side this provides enough food to split an entree. Extremely satisfied with both their dressing (they have to be homemade) and their large portions. Bread served with dinner is always a plus as well and I love that la Trattoria serves theirs with oil/seasonings rather than butter.
My family has come here for years. Great food and excellent service. The best escargot I have ever had and I have traveled the world.
Overall very good (fairly authentic) Mexican spot. A little expensive, but worth it in my opinion. Excellent choices of meats for tacos, burritos and quesadillas.
Amazingly authentic Greek food. My grandfather is first generation Greek so finding a place with authentic food is very important to me... I've just found my extended family!

5/5 stars for excellent service and great food. I was super skeptical about coming here but I'm so glad I did. My waitress was such a doll. She kept checking up on us and kept bringing over kitchen specials which was free and so generous of them to do. I was celebrating my bfs birthday so they customized the menu with his name on it. 

Now to food, everything was super fresh and tasteful. There were loads of flavor and spice. I ordered the salatim( different veggie salads), fried cauliflower, lamb merguez (ORDER THIS) the meat was so soft and delicious. It was slightly chewy but the meat was seasoned well. And my bf ordered the chicken shishlik which was grilled chicken.. also delicious. I ordered a drink and it took me some time to take it down, the waitress noticed...She offered me a different drink or to remake it. I thought that was so nice of her to acknowledge and offer. The service here is phenomenal and the food is great. The hype is worth it and I cant wait to come back again.
I almost don't want everyone to know about this amazing gelato. We hit this place for dessert after a delicious dinner at Venezia. The seasonal flavors are a must!

Pros:
1. FRESHLY made sushi and sashimi. Let's face it, the tuna roll doesn't taste like it just jumped out of the ocean, but for Ruby Buffet...not too shabby at all!
2. Great selection of seafood and generous refills- If it's not for the fact my mom's suffering from gout, i'll be WAITING IN LINE for the lil chinese lady to drop those crabs; prawns; crawdads into the pan!
3. Attentive service. Water filled; bowls cleared. I paid 12 bucks for dinner, and that's all I ask for. 
4. Chinese dim sum. I wasn't crazy about the buns and dumplings since I'm Chinese.....but it's a nice way to be adventurous since it won't the bank. 
5. Ice-Cream Machine. BEWARE of crazy and out of control kids in line. (Usually their parents are just as crazy fighting for crab claws at the other end) 

Cons:
1. DAMN, this place is like a circus when you go at dinner time. Sexually unidentifiable people wobbling in 7 inch heels; kids running on sugar rush; a couple that takes up a booth of 6, and pile their table with 10 bowls of crabs...
2. Americanized Chinese food...your usual lineup, general tsao, string beans. Floating in grease and screaming out to you, "eat me and waddle away in fat and happiness"
3. You might gotta break a leg to get some crabs! People aint so civilized down there, one guy took 2 plates and dished out all the crabs as soon as it got plated. yep...no shame!

I went down there with my bf, after his car got towed. After paying $180 to get it back, we needed an abundance of food; freak show to stuff our faces and be entertained. I was quite satisfied with the results....
This is a great stop for sushi and chicken teriyaki. We order here anytime we visit the beach nearby. The staff is great and makes sure the restaurant is very clean. We love the sushi boats!!

Muffaletta is a great sandwich; the flavors all marry together wonderfully. A whole sandwich is pretty big and can easily feed 2 people saving room for other New Orleans favorites. The evening Jazz band makes for a great al Fresca dining experience.

My husband and I came here for our anniversary dinner. 
We ate so much food - it almost seems silly to list it all because seriously, we ate so much. I will just talk about what was rave-worthy.
The cocktails were absolutely delicious. We had many. 
We had the Seafood Mixto pasta and shared it. The flavors in this dish blended so well and you could taste every bit of ingredient. We also added a lobster tail to the side, garlic mashed potatoes, artichoke fritters and a rich, delicious risotto dish. 
It was the most excellent dinner!
Now, we are not fancy people, but we felt so spoiled. Our server, Dominique, was wonderful! She was a fantastic server and so very professional. She brought us lots of goodies for our anniversary and honestly made our experience so amazing. We were so grateful to have her! Ty was also helping to service our table and I felt like my glass of water was always full to the top.  He was great as well!
Our desserts: my husband ordered the dessert special, which was deep friend cheesecake bites with lots of different, delicious dipping sauces. ‍ Bless him. Haha - they were stupid good.
I had the creme brûlée. It was one of the best creme brûlée I had ever had. Perfect balance and not to sweet! I actually want it right now, for lunch. And every day.

All in all, Barbacoa was good to us and we feel so lucky to have had Dominique and Ty. If you two ever see this, YOU GUYS ROCK! If your boss ever sees this, they deserve a raise.

Course is in really good shape ! Golf Course has made a total turn around from 2017. Lots of improvement work has been accomplished. Greens are smooth, fairways are starting to grow in nicely, pace of play fantastic. Participated is a 2 man (55+) scramble ( every Wednesday) which was fun and competitively fair. The 14th island green is like playing TPC Sawgrass # 17 !
My boyfriend and I shared the vegan blueberry pancakes and vegan burger, absolutely delicious! If we lived nearby we would be back often. Very impressed.

Love Korean BBQ Olive chicken. First had it in K-Town, NYC and so happy to find it here in Chinatown. This location only has the drumsticks and the boneless bites- but, hey - I'll take it! Order ahead as it takes about 20 minutes. Yuuuum.

I'm still learning what's in Tucson and we accidentally noticed this location after visiting the Tuscon Mall.
It's large and you can move around freely between all the good stations.
I always judge by the Won Ton Happiness salad and this one uses enough dressing to make it tasty.
I loved this location for sure. It was not crowded and I liked that.
Yup, we'll be back.

The Donk's staff could not possibly have been more welcoming and accommodating for my birthday celebration. I brought in about 20 gay guys who had never been there before (I hadn't either), none of whom give a damn about a woman's...donk. Everyone was fun and lovely, the service was great, I've gotten compliments for planning something outside of our usual bar comfort zone for months since, and that's because everyone at the establishment was so cool.

Came in on Monday November 11th, 2013 around 11:30 AM for the Veterans Day Champagne Brunch --- and was sat at the last table in the far corner of the room. 

We ordered a Coffee, Diet Coke, Mimosa, and Water from the Waitress --- who took two trips to bring all of the items but forget the cream and sugar for the coffee.  

After our drinks arrived --- we hit the buffet which had mostly lunch items with a few breakfast items (hashbrowns, sausage, bacon) and an made to order egg station.  I ordered two scrambled eggs with cheese and bacon from the buffet line --- and they were not up to par. My girlfriend stated she has had better food at Denny's or IHOP.

Otherwise, I had some of the cheese ravioli, hand carved prime-rib (little fatty); asian and mexican stations along with a few other items. On a positive note --- I found the crepe station --- with the nutella crepe made to order with whipped cream and powdered sugar on top to be on point! Great job on the crepes and the desserts.

For $14.99 per person including drinks -- I found it to be a good value, however, compared to other Caesars Entertainment Properties I was just not impressed with the buffet and would have gladly paid more for better prepared food.

There must be something wrong with their speakers because everything I ordered was being received wrong to them on the other side, weird. I was trying to order a number one combo (cheese burger) & they thought I said a number 9 (chicken sandwich). Fine , I'll eat the chicken sand, then I asked for tots & received fries, tots were even on the screen. I must say that I'm not very impressed with this place, fries were either old or dry or from the bottom of the bag. Chicken sandwich was ok. A little small, lots of lettuce though. I will give them 2 stars for The ocean water soda which was pretty good & the peppermint they had at the bottom of my bag. May not go back.

The paella was some of the best I've had anywhere, they prepared a pitcher of sangria in front of us, the apps the atmosphere, the history all add up to an incredible dining experience. We can't wait to return and try more options from their menu.

The only reason I would go back is for the view of the Ben and the marina.  Besides that, the service was terrible.  Our waitress was second class at best.  The place was not crowded at all.  We were told the kitchen was "broken" and that they only had sandwiches available. Everything on the menu is either made on a grill or a deep fryer so wasn't quite sure how the entire kitchen was broken.   We put in our drink order but didn't receive anything for 15+ minutes so we left.  We told the waitress we were leaving on our way out, but her lithium binge prevented her from caring.  The menu was very limited, and not just because the kitchen was "broken" that day.

No parking
Terrible service
Limited menu
Great views

I chose this restaurant to celebrate my 30th birthday at with friends. I'm very glad I called ahead and made a reservation, as it was packed on Saturday night. The staff was incredibly accommodating with people arriving at slightly different times and splitting checks. 
I loved the theme of the entire restaurant. The cocktails were all innovative and delicious. I had the Al Capone and loved it. Would definitely order it again. Don't be turned off by the basil- it was a tasty addition to the drink and kept me from drinking it too quickly!!
The Repeal Burger is the best burger I've had in Indy. It was cooked perfectly, the bun to meat to topping ratio was perfect and all the different flavors came together as a perfect bite over and over again. 
Hands down, one of my favorite restaurants in Indy and I will be back again.

Not Monell's. This was a very disappointing morning. I was looking forward to breakfast with my son on our way to a car show and just knew that Monell's was the place to try. 

This is a very average place with unimpressive food. They do not offer options for eggs besides scrambled. The gravy for biscuits was bought a t a restaurant supply store for sure. 

If you are looking to eat here, Nashville has a ton of better options, friendlier staff and hamemadier food.
I had the Umbria pizza. It's amazing. eat it. The beer list here is ridiculous too. Legit.

Stopped by this cute little downtown restaurant at the recommendation of a few locals. Large space with  prob a dozen or so 4 top tables, cute small indoor kids play area, and a little nook area with some random things/food items for sale. Order at the counter, small menu seems to change frequently with soups, sandwiches, salads, smoothies etc. Definitely a good place for vegetarians/vegans/health conscious they can accommodate easily. I chose the Italian pressed sandwich with side of fruit. Sandwich was really good, It was around $10 (pricey, but quality made it worth it). Everyone was super friendly.  I would definitely stop in for brunch or lunch

Had dinner here on a visit last weekend (April 26).  The food was excellent.  We had the chef' tasting menu.  So many different dishes, all very flavorful and fantastic.  The hummus was amazing.  The lamb to die for.  For dessert was expecting only one choice, had four different dessert tastings.  Heaven!

Service was excellent.  The staff knew the food.  The service was fast and unobtrusive.

Will definitely be back on our next trip to Philadelphia.

This location does not have delivery. I have avoided ordering from here because they did not have it. But tough times means you drive for the food. This was our first experience with this location for food. We ordered the general tso and fried shrimp with egg rolls, crab Rangoon and wonton soup. 

We were so hungry we forgot to take photos of the food. 

The soup was fantastic. 

The egg rolls were cooked well. Not over cooked or under cooked. The inside of the egg roll was just okay. Not sure we would order them again. 

The crab Rangoon had good flavor but was a bit too crispy for me. But I'll give them another try. 

General tso's was good but had zero spicy to it. It was more on the sweet side. I personally like mine to have a kick. 

Fried shrimp has a red sweet sauce on it. I enjoyed it and appreciated the variety of veggies with it. Little corn for the win! 

Overall the experience was good and we enjoyed the meal and will order from here again.
Good was great and staff is exceptional! From refills, picking up my tray and food from table as soon as we finished. Staff was pleasant! I'll be back :)

Started with some really rich pork belly tater tots that I felt favorably toward, but after that, it was all downhill. For my entree I got the short ribs and a house salad. The house salad was bland and just not tasty at all and I didn't even want to eat it past a few bites. The beef short ribs were dry and blah, served over more blah - everyday mashed potatoes and collard greens. Disappointed.

Not impressed. As much talk as I've heard about this place, I expected a lot more.  Decent place to hang out and drink, and I probably wouldn't complain about the food if I was drunk, but the burgers had an inch of room on each side of the bun around the patty (or meatball), extremely salty, Cajun fries were either burnt or limp and not very cajun, service below avg. 

Come to drink, not to eat.

Great Atmosphere, Great Service and Food, we love the different selection on the menu.
We enjoyed the Mac & Cheese and Cheese Tots, delicious Rib Eye Steak, ever thing was fabulous
Highly recommended for a fun lunch or dinner!

We parked near the Visitor Center to kill time before our reservation. Parking was free if you are out of the garage before 7. The staff will give you a ticket to get out of the garage.  The bathroom was social distanced. The sinks were taped off and they have a these neat air driers which is neat and usefully easy to use.

I heard a lot of good things about this place but I was slightly disappointed. The food is slightly above average Chinese (for St. Louis) with some Korean dishes. You could do much worse than here. It's not bad but it didn't live up to expectations. If you are in the neighborhood, try Shu Feng right around the corner. I think it's a much better place.

I'm just getting around to reviewing Rice though I've been there many times. I waiver between rating them a 3 or a 4. I'm going to give them the 3 simply because I don't go there w the intent to eat dinner normally. I like to go to Rice for happy hour and to have an appetizer. They have a great patio and really that is what I like best. The sushi isn't bad and some of the dishes are good but the menu is a bit overwhelming as noted by most. My favorite is the pad woonsen w tofu and I always specify my own spice level. I do say it is worth a go.

Amazing food, great service. Try the charbroiled oysters and crawfish etoufee, you will not be disappointed. Definitely top it off with the delicious, warm bread pudding. EVERYTHING was fantastic. Could easily become our new NOLA favorite!

We have enjoyed countless meals at Elvira's in Tubac with visiting family and friends.  And they were all terrific.

Our daughter was visiting with a friend and asked to try the Tucson version or Elvira's. She is senior management for an Iron Chef/ James Beard awarding winning chef with dozens of highly acclaimed restaurants.

7PM Saturday night it was partially filled and we were shown directly to our seats back by the kitchen. Not my first choice for seating but...

The house Margarita and Paloma cocktails were delicious. We naturally ordered the $0.50 Hola tequila shots---one for each entree. We started with a table shared Fundido Natural and a Mussels special.  Both were well prepared and wonderful.

Kitchen timing was off---the entrees arrived before we finished the appetizer course and the waiter was in a hurry to clear the table. We were in no rush but...

Entrees were Chiles Poblano Frida Kalho, a chicken Mole negro, a special Snapper and a sizzling hot Flank Steak Molcajete in Salsa Verde. Flavors were very savory. Two of the entrees were barely warm.  We asked about warming and they said they would start over but that would take time and the other table members would be finished when they appeared appeared. The side plates of rice and beans were all cold and one was sent back and quickly replaced with a warmer plate. 

From our vantage point near the kitchen window we noticed many kitchen staff members just milling around.

We were offered a shared complimentary Caribbean Treat (Bananas Fosters).It was then 8pm with few tables taken but it took a while to arrive at our table. The flavors were delicious but the bananas were barely warm as if they failed to flambe the dessert or it sat in the kitchen being neglected.

We asked to take home a portion of the chicken mole negro but it never appeared at our table and the waiter had disappeared. By that point we had given up.

Sooo, overall not a great dining experience. Cold entrees for $200.
We came to this place on a whim and ended up loving it. All of their food is very fresh, flavorful, and reasonably priced. Overall a great spot for lunch!

The food was amazing!!  We had the stuffed French toast, a frittata, the chicken sandwich on the menu and the Mexican breakfast special. The only complaint is the set up. Every time the door opened, the freezing cold air came blowing in. If I had known, I would of waited for a table in the back of the restaurant. Everything else was phenomenal. The service was good, quick, and well organized.

Worst place to get a meal in STL. 
Waited an hour for a pancake, scramble, and breakfast sandwich ONLY to be told that the kitchen is slammed due to a phone-in order. 
When we called the restaurant to see how long it would take for a to-go order we were told 10-15 mins; while we'd been waiting an hour. 
Service sucks and establishment needs to proper management 
Biggest waste of time.

All I gotta say about the Glinch is this. $1.65 windowpane mugs of Yuengling Porter, 75 cent hot dogs, miserable old bitches waiting on you, tabletop Ms Pacman. It's the last great bastion of humanity in the depressing artifice of Center City Philadelphia.

Just ok. We were here for less than 24 hours and wanted to try a "real Philly cheesesteak". Cleavers was the closet to the hotel. We asked a few locals on the street if they recommended Cleavers and nobody had heard of it. It's COVID times so the indoor dining wasn't open (except for the owners kids who were running around). I ordered "The Cleaver" and while it came with a lot of meat, it lacked flavor. We both had to add salt to our sandwiches. Overall not bad but you can probably find better.

So excited that bonchon is in the burbs and it did not disappoint. 
Came here for lunch and they have awesome lunch specials
I liked the wings better than the drumsticks. 
Getting pickled radish with the chicken is a must. 
Fries were awesome as well. 

The space is open but your voice does travel so it made me a little self conscious when I was talking lol.
Been coming here for years. I find myself craving their breakfast sandwich all the time.

We had been away from Tucson for several years and decided to make a birthday dinner reservation with family in a recent visit. To our surprise, most of the moles are NOT gluten free. This was a disappointment as a couple of the diners in our group are allergic and we know first-hand that moles don't traditionally have wheat flour. 

I also ordered gluten free cupcakes from the bakery inside the cafe, and they were perfect. Cup Quequitos offers GF and Vegan options that taste great. Unfortunately there was a lack of communication between the hostess, bakery and our waiter who was not only condescending but also fumbled with his delivery.

Diners beware that the price range here on Yelp ($$) is awfully misleading. Every entree costs $25 and up. The food is good, but not great and does not warrant the high price. The glory days of excellent food at Cafe Poca Cosa are, sadly, gone.

This place was sssooo good! The restaurant is super cute and quaint and reminds me of being in someone's home. The food was super delish and they served huge portions. I had the dish with a blue tortilla and guacamole and eggs and damn those potatoes were amazing. I don't remember what it was called but I finished like half of it and ate the rest the next day. SO GOOD. like home cookin. I def will be back. But I won't order the iced tea. It was flavorless and nondescript. But yeah the meal was amazing.

UPDATE: The manager reached out to me after reading my review, asking for details to enhance the experience.  This is HUGE for me.  When someone cares about their business enough to ask these questions that is always a place I would like to patronize again.  

Original:
I stopped her with my family for a quick lunch before heading out for the afternoon.  

I found that this is a great place to stop for lunch.  I decided on the combo dish, and I selected a mushroom pizza and the french onion soup. Both were very tasty and in my experience getting a French Onion soup to taste right is a very difficult thing to do.

One dish that I think was very cute was the make your own pizza for the children.  They come out with a little flattened dough, then the kids add their sauce, cheese and possibly any additional toppings that they might like.  Overall I thought the food was good, nice place to have lunch.  I did think our server while nice when at our table was more consumed with talking to her coworkers than attending her table.
Best Bahn Mi in the Tampa area. Their's is the real thing.  All of their food fairly priced. Service is quick. They can get very busy during lunch time.

Location is a bit difficult to get to, but if you get there early enough you may be able to park on the street. There is a garage right near there, but it costs $11 and you get a voucher for a can of beer at Mellow Fellow. The atmosphere is really cool with bottles of beer on the walls and over 50 taps of brews. There's always something to look at! 

It is first come, first serve with limited tables so if there is an Ace's game get there early! We were a table of 8 and luckily got a table for ourselves. Our server was Joe and he is quite the character! He knows his beer and is not shy to give recommendations on food or beer. He was very helpful and made sure our food came out with plenty of time for us to eat and get to the game. It was pretty busy and looked like it was mainly only Joe on the floor serving tables. 

I noticed though that Joe was taking everyone's order and then giving it to the kitchen so he was stacking the orders which slowed down the kitchen. 

I noticed almost the entire staff doesn't use trays even when carrying 4 to 5 beers. Even though it is impressive that the server gets them to the table, guests do notice that the entire time they are walking over they are spilling beer all over the floor and if your chair is pulled out enough it could go down the backs of guests. As a guest, I would prefer to see a server use a tray to take care of the mess and they can bring more tables drinks at once, skillfully and neatly.

Grilled chicken salad with a side of honey mustard dressing was delicious! It's usually hard to find restaurants that offer great salads but the Habit's grilled chicken salad was not only fresh but tasted great. My husband ordered a cheeseburger and it too tasted good. He substituted cheese for guacamole and it was perfect, especially for the price.

Probably the cheapest grub your going to find in the area that tastes great! Few notes to keep in mind...
 1. Service is fabulous! 
  2. Make a reservation, waiting area has little seating however bar is right there which is handy.... 
 3. Music is very loud so if you want a nice pleasant conversation this is not the place...lol.   Who needs to talk when your eating anyway....
4. Short rib sandwich, short rib tacos.... OMG. Need I say more...
 5. Local brews... Yowza. That's all! 
 6. If you are looking for more than tacos and chips/salsa you will not be impressed however the choices that are on the menu are all great... Suck it up and get a taco.... Queso is yum too. 
 
 Did I mention service was great and food was very inexpensive.
Worst service I've ever experienced- by the owner himself. Spend your money elsewhere with someone that appreciates your money. This guy is a loser! Other than the awful service the food was good

I had a great dinner here this weekend. We were with a large group which can be a challenge, but the service was excellent! The guacamole and queso were delicious. For dinner, I had the fish taco and a tuna taco - both were fantastic and I would recommend them. Great spicy margaritas. Loved the vibe here as well - very lively on a Friday night. Can't wait to go back to try more of the menu items!

My husband and I have been dining at Arielle's in Argus, PA since the very first day.  We were there opening night, and continue to frequent this warm and receiving establishment.  We have celebrated many holidays, birthdays, anniversarys and have frequently chosen Arielle's to entertain business associates.  I often feel transported in time, and space as I enter the restaurant.  We have had the pleasure of enjoying well over six hundred meals at Arielles.  Jacque, chef extraordinaire, is rivaled by none, when it comes to his utterly delightful soups (bisques) and, his RACK OF LAMB!!!!!  The fare is ALWAYS FRESH and cooked and seasoned to sublime perfection.  I cannot thank proprietors Jacque and Cristine enough, along with senior staff, like Donna.  Bon Appetite, you'll enjoy every single bite!!!
This place was great a little out of the way in a unassuming strip mall but wow fresh everything was great from the service to the food I'll be back

Save your money there are a lot better steaks and up scale restaurants in Nashville. Steak had no flavor. It took about 1 and a half hours for it to even come out. The only thing that was 5 stars would be our waiter he was great. Do your self a favor and steer clear up this restaurant.

I went here for lunch today with my dad. I am a sushi fan and he is a sashimi fan so we got to try both! The service was fast, the food was delicious, and the prices were reasonable for what you get. The atmosphere was fun and has a lot to look at, a lot of sports memorabilia which was interesting and different. It's also close to my job so that is a huge bonus. I will be back next time I am craving a sushi roll.

I was so impressed by everything when I ate here today. I am not sure why I felt like this was too fresh and healthy for me because today's meal blew me away. I ordered the Migos and my friend ordered the "Eggs" Plate and a grapefruit. Both meals were outstanding. The portions were large and I left really satisfied with my visit. The service is also warm and wonderful. I will definitely be coming back and introducing friends to it in the future.

I'm from NYC and have quite a bit of Ramen options. Came down to Florida to visit for a few days, and was craving some Ramen all of a sudden, so Yelp recommended this place. 

The decor was really nice. We came a bit before 5pm so we hung out by the bar before we were allowed to go inside the dining room. The bartenders were super friendly and gave my friend a sample of their Sake. We also ordered two of the pork buns. They were just okay. It doesn't really compare to the ones up north. 

At 5pm, they started letting people into the dining room. I liked that you can write on the menu with a marker to put in your order. This way you can sub, cross out what you don't want, etc. I did notice the prices are definitely on the higher side for Ramen, even compared to NYC. Two people sitting across from us actually got up and left because of it. I got the Shoyu with the shrimp instead of pork belly, my friends got the Tonkotsu and the Mushroom Ramen. All were pretty good. I really enjoyed mine because it was a light broth compared to the others. 

Only thing that would really hold me back from coming again would be the price, but if you're craving some Ramen, this wouldn't be a bad option.

Really impressed with the sandwiches! Mikes way - always!!! Love the original. They slice their meat and make your sand which. There is just something about it that makes them unique to other sandwich places. Not sure what it is but it's good.

OMG!!! Best brunch buffet ever!!! Went for my girlfriend's birthday, and it was out of this world. First off, free parking when you eat there, just make sure you get your card validated before you leave. When I say they have everything there I mean everything. Eggs where good and so was the French toast. Their home fries where amazing. And don't get me started on the juicy steak . First time I ever had a mimosa. They were sooo good. The waiter was great. Always made sure our mimosas where refilled. Really can't wait to go back!!
Came here for the first time and overall good experience. Friendly staff. I had the California burrito, the meat had a good seasoning, but the fries were a little over cooked.
Good place for a brew & a bite.  I would return if i get back in town.

I also posted this on their Facebook page....

We usually have great experiences that the pop shop. However, this morning we had the worst breakfast ever! not only did we have to wait longer than expected for someone to greet us after we were seated, the waitress who finally did come over was nasty and down right rude and uninviting. Her name was Sarah.

My wife ordered tea... Sarah snapped at her when she didn't hear Sarah ask if she wanted cream or lemon. My wife and I just looked at each other in surprise. I wanted to leave right there and then, but we were so hungry we had to stay.

Our food was pretty bad too. The pancakes were probably the worst I've ever had which was a shock because I really enjoy the food at this restaurant. TPS raves about how their pancakes have been voted by be the top pancakes in the area, but they were so dense... I have no idea how that could have been. I also ordered Eggs Benedict, and the Canadian bacon was rubbery and the Hollandaise sauce had pretty much solidified. The only reason why I ate the food was because I had been up since 4 AM with my baby and I was starving. I've never frowned while eating before... I guess there's a first for everything.

Additionally, our server, Sarah, was nowhere to be found after taking our order and then after bringing our food. We saw her talking to her friends(seated at another booth) for most of our meal so we couldn't get refills for coffee or drinks. She only checked up on us wants her friends left and that's when I complained about the pancakes... however it took such a long time for her to check up in us that we were just about done out meal.

It's so sad because this is one of our favorite restaurants so we can take our son without having to worry about having a baby with us during the meal. Don't know if I would go back... such a disappointment.
Mystic Fish is my favorite place to eat in past years.Since the pandemic, i have not gone but definitely is on my list

This place made me fall in love with sushi!

I have never been one to try sushi. It never appealed to me, but one day I had a sudden urge to try it, and I'm glad this was my first bite of it!

The interior of the establishment is pleasant and clean. Service is friendly and this is definitely a family run restaurant.

The sushi menu is extensive but you HAVE to get the Highway 19 roll. It is tempura shrimp, avocado, cream cheese, spicy tuna, and sauces. It is just amazing and the tuna just melts in your mouth. 

I like to share sushi, then order the chicken hibachi plate. Its the usual hibachi chicken, noodles, rice, and veggies. Its the exact same food you get at a hibachi steakhouse, but at a much lower price (and slightly smaller portion). Everything is well prepared and simply delicious. 

I just love this place and will most definitely be back!

Terrible service
-called days before asking if brunch on weekend is on and happy hour applies. Said yes. Asked if prices are still same as before. Said yes. Used to be 7.50$ brunch. Now 12+. Which really is a few $ less than original price
-menu has changed and avocado toast with side salad (top seller) is not the toast with hollandaise and potatoes. 
-had to ask for utensils and waited while our meals sat in front of us
-friend asked for water before I arrived and never came. Had to ask again
-friend asked for coffee and never arrived. Asked again and they showed up with a pot, no cup.
-they didn't ask my friend how she liked her eggs and they came runny. Asked for a plate of cooked eggs.
-asked for hot sauce- got a poor excuse amount. In a cup. Had to ask for more.
-had about 5-6 different people come to our table. Hard to know who actually was our server 
-asked for bills only for them to be incorrect. And waited quite a bit with a fussy child 

Keep in mind. Place was not busy. Was 3 of us. We were never demanding. Asked for basic things, that really should be there to begin with. I am one to hate complaining and returning food etc. But today was the poorest service I've received at Earls and im a longtime customer. 

Sadly won't be returning. And will be finding a new brunch place!

I am surprised by the glowing reviews for this establishment given the multiple options for similar cuisine of higher quality available within a 5 block radius. It's possible that we were there on an off night but I would categorize the fare as 1/3 pretty good, 1/3 OK, and 1/3 barely edible. The well seasoned beef shawarma wrap with tahini and pickles; crispy on the outside/ fluffy on the inside herbaceous falafel; and the smoky/acidic (though a little too chunky) baba ganoush belong in the first category. Poorly seasoned fries, rather bland hummus, and thin chewy pitas go in the second category. Lastly, the grape leaves were just plain "off" and tasted fermented, and the tahini salad was way over-dressed. We may have come on an off night, but it really just wasn't good enough to make us want to give it a second chance.

The service was good. The cuts of pork chop and ribeye were sorry price considered. The "special" ribeye was $8 above menu price ($46 total) for sauce and 2 jumbo shrimp. The pork chop was also $8 above menu price (37 total)for sauce and 2 asparagus sticks. Considering the premium price for everything, you wouldn't expect to get hammered and all the small stuff. My fault for not asking the price of every small item. The extra $3 for blue cheese and bacon. The extra $6 for the 2 up charged  baked potatoes. The extra $4 for a Caesar salad. 

Time to find a new anniversary tradition. Customer lost.

I'm a STL native, currently living in Miami, the land of less-than-great BBQ.  My parents had raved to me for months and months about the awesome brisket and ribs, and after stalking the crazy daily specials and sides on Facebook, I knew a meal at SugarFire was a requirement on a recent trip back.  Thankfully, no one needed convincing to come with me!

We came for a late lunch on a Friday, and the line was minimal.  Between the 5 of us, we ordered a half-rack of ribs, a small brisket platter, a brisket sandwich, a pulled pork sandwich, and a cheeseburger.  We had fries, sweet potato grits, baked beans, and a shrimp and kale salad as our sides.

Wow, talk about a lot of food!  SugarFire definitely gives you your money's worth.  The brisket was nice and smokey, without enough fat to keep it juicy, but not too much to make it inedible.  The pulled pork was tender and delicious, and everyone else seemed to enjoy their meals as well.  The fries were addictive, as were the baked beans - I'd order both again.  

SugarFire makes me wish I lived in STL or at least visited more frequently to enjoy everything they have and their daily creations.  But I'll have to settle for a visit whenever I'm back.  Definitely worth a visit (or several)!!

Not gonna lie: I don't carry cash because I'd wind up with a habit here (& at Cibao on Frankford... & with the ice cream truck). The lines at Dunkin at the terminal are always mad long, and their donuts leave that weird oily residue on the roof of your mouth. These don't do that, and they only cost 75 cents. Also, they have apple fritters. You can't get a breakfast sandwich here, but if you're broke as a joke (or super hungry on your way home from work & have an I-don't-carry-cash policy), they have decent hot dogs -- never old and crusty like gas station hot dogs, never boiled like cafeteria hot dogs. And the sauerkraut is free!

My family's first visit and it will be our last. We were told it would be a 15 minute wait. I'm a very patient person until I'm lied to! We ended up waiting 40 minutes for two platters! They were full of excuses! They only had one cook and the cashier ended up going in the back to assist the cook! Horrible customer service! A reputable place would have offered us something for our wait. The food was below average. Mac and cheese was awful. What was supposed to be elbow noodles looked like broken overcooked noodles and taste like welfare cheese. My asparagus was so overcooked it wilted. I was really shocked by how awful the food and overall experience was given this place has over 16K IG followers. And I really wanted to support a black owned business. But it won't be this one! They got me this time but never again.

This place has some of the most amazing outside seating on the beach, and they have live music more often than not (GOOD live music). Sometimes it's difficult to get served at the bar on a weekend but I suppose that can happen anywhere. They have a garden wrap that is vegan, as well as a black bean burger that you can get vegan by taking the cheese off. Our server this time was Amber and she was PHENOMENAL. Definitely ask for her.

Heard good things about this place and we were in the downtown area so had to check it out. Plus it was a happy hour / half off day. The pictures say a lot. Great presentation great food! Waiter was very friendly and helped with recommendations. We had to get the playboy because they light it on fire. however, that was probably the best part of it as the taste was not good. There were many different warm and contrasting tastes/flavors. We actually ended up sending it back for a different roll (the crab one) which we felt bad about but again the waiter was great and happy to exchange it. You could tell he just wanted us to have a good time and good experience! Great place will definitely be back!

I want to start off by saying that I have never done a Yelp review before, However, this place was so all around awesome that I felt like I had too. I moved to Saint Petes from  Center City Philadelphia (where I lived for 25 years)  in January and I am sad to say I haven't stumbled upon this place sooner. I had the smoked salmon breakfast sandwich which was perfect, from the bread to the meat to the cheese. Everything went together so well. My friend had the "All day breakfast Sammy" which I snagged a bite of because she raved  about how delicious it was. I can attest to that being delicious as well!! I was so impressed with both sandwiches. Everything about Brooklyn South was 5 stars from the food to the service to the environment. The owner who was also the chef was extremely friendly. He was very  passionate and very knowledgeable about everything. After living in Saint Petersburg for 3 months, I would say I have tried a large amount of cafes, food stands/trucks and restaurants. I know this place received #4 best of the bay, but as far as places I've ever tried (Philly included) this place should be all around rated #1!!!

We had a terrific first experience having dinner at Cooper's Hawk.  We even experienced a couple of issues, but the way they were handled still led to an overall very positive experience.

Our server, Terry, was terrific! We will absolutely ask for her when we return. We enjoyed a bottle of their Suavignon Blanc. One of the things we really appreciated was being able to sample a few different wines before committing to the bottle. We also ordered the cheese plate as an appetizer.

We each had a steak, and between us also tried the parmesan fries with aoili, betty's potatoes, and green beans. Everything was delicious!

This was one of the best meals and some of the best service we have experienced in Indianapolis in the last year and a half we have lived here!

Really nice food, crispy Brussels are awesome. I had the special which was great duck dish. French fries are actually potatoe wedges but still good. Burger was a little underwhelming but overall this is restaurant is worth trying once. 

I will add they have some of the best service I have ever seen in Nashville and for that alone many people would love this place.

This place is very cute and cozy, tucked in the Spring Garden corridor. My friend and I ordered nachos, which were not bad, but not note-worthy either. Our server seemed a little absent minded- she failed to mention that some of the margarita flavors were more expensive so I was confused by my very large drink. My friend also asked for a modification on his order, which was not how the food ended up when it came out. It was a generally lukewarm experience.
42 minutes in line and still no food. This is ridiculous. This chick-fil-a needs to get their service in order. I've never seen such horrible service at a chick-fil-a before.

Service is def 5 stars. Everyone was so nice!
We did a take out order.

Chicken shawarma - amazing. It was flavored perfectly. 
Greek salad with grilled chicken - delicious! 
Penne vodka - this was good but not amazing.  It felt like it needed a bit more sauce.
Seafood jambalaya - my friend got this and wasn't thrilled with it.
Lemmon ricotta toast - delicious. What a great combo! 

The chicken shawarma was the best though and we will def be back for it!

nice looking restaurant. great service. ordered the chicken piccate and eggplant parm. both come with steamed veggies and three fried potato discs. the food was ok. felt very neighborhood restaurant like. 

the service was fabolous. the waitress offered us gelato samples in the end. the samples could have passed off as dessert for us..but anyhow we got greedy and ordered the pistachio gelato. was very satisfying.

Wonderul restaurant right in the center of town. I had the Cajun Alfredo with blackened chicken and it was the best Chicken Alfredo I have had in my life! I would come back to Louisiana just to go to the Creole House and get it again! I would definitely recommend coming here to eat at least once while you're in New Orleans.

Eating at Desi Village is always delicious. The sauces are well balanced with a variety of spices and never too heavy. The garlic naan, Somosa chat and chicken vindaloo are consistently enjoyable and never a disappointment. Highly recommend if you want authentic Indian food. It's worth every penny spent!

My bf and I frequently dine at the cheesecake factory in stl a few times a month and it is nothing compare to the one at the fashion mall in Indianapolis!2, we ordered our usual dishes and the taste was not great at all. My salad was welted and the tomatoes were old. Our herb crusted salmon also tasted old. Service was average. Atmosphere was ok. It was humid and smelly during lunch. besides the old tasting food being bad...the hostess was very rude. The girl with the straight across bangs. She was not only rude to me, but also others. She didn't smile or say hi or anything. I found that the other hostesses (the ones seating customers) were by far the friendliest. That other girl with dark hair, straight across bangs need to go!

went again last night (and had the same things because i'm lame!) and i would give this place a sixth star if i could.  definitely do not miss the halibut if it's on the menu, or the scallops, or the key lime pie.  

oh and i was wrong - it's not cash only.  i noticed the stickers and i think they said they recently started accepting credit cards.

Not just wings here, although the wings are GREAT (especially with a coupon) and available with 18 sauces (in varying heat levels).   Dear friends steered us towards the chicken quesadillas, which are so robust that a single order will serve two (with leftovers).  The chicken Caesar wrap also is delicious and enough for 2-3 meals.

Our experience here has largely been take-away, so we have not focused on the restaurant's amenities.

As the first Chinese restaurant I've been to in the Santa Barbara area, I was impressed by how delicious the food was. The atmosphere is a little bit sterile feeling but the servers were pleasant, the food was delicious and prepared in a timely manner, and the dinner was well priced. I will definitely be going back to try more of the items off the menu.
Great pick up food to finish at home plus amazing deli and meat market!!  I bought a few pot pies served them alongside market bought pies !everyone preferred the market bought!

Ummmmm, where has this Salad been all my existence???
Thanks to a friend   I just discovered this gem @goldiefalafel by the genius Michael Salamonov.
For $9 here's what you get :
Salad greens with :
Falafel , cabbage , beets , carrot cucumber sunflower seeds , fresh herbs and tehina. The dressing is insane and there is much more of a special marinated feel to all the homemade ingredients (I don't always like falafel and usually find it and the toppings surprisingly bland)
Make SURE to top it with the flavorful and not too spicy harissa on the table as a condiment . So cute and casual to eat in too!

This is only my second time at a Ford's Garage, and my first time visiting the St Pete location! I am all about happy hours and Ford's has a good one. Its pretty much all day (11am-7pm) and its $4 margaritas, sangria, and house wines and $1 off all their beers. The bartender was on point with the margs  I really like Ford's because (spoiler alert!) I'm not a huuuge burger fan, but they give you the option of getting chicken, a turkey burger, a vegetarian option, portobello mushroom, etc. So I got the jiffy "burger" with a chicken breast, cheese, bacon, and PEANUT BUTTER and it was delicious! They have a lot of sides to choose from as well including fries, sweet potato tots (which I got and came with a yummy cinnamon honey sauce), potatoes, and Mac-n-cheese just to name a few. I will definitely be back!

December 22, 2014, 5:30 PM

"Leanora, I know if I tell you this it might get me into trouble, but this chicken breast may be the best one that I've ever had in my life."  

If you know me, this is very high praise, as my wife is a fantastic cook, and I truly value what she cooks for me, oh, and as a side note, my wife is full blooded Sicilian, and so telling her that a restaurant makes a better chicken breast than her is a bit of a risky thing.  My wife, though, does respect opinion, and, on this evening, she did continue to talk to me.  That's a good thing, but I still didn't sleep soundly.

I've skipped a number of critical parts of the evening, and so, to flesh it out a bit, we were in town overnight to finish up our Christmas shopping, and who am I to go without a meal.  Usually we head to Campo, but after reviewing the input of my fellow yelpers, I thought I'd give the Old Granite Street Eatery a try, and I was not unhappy with the call.  
To jump to the end, we'll be back.

Here are some things to know:

1)  There is no corkage, and we brought our own wine.  I love this.  We brought our own, and we felt very comfortable about it.  In the past, some places have not been nearly as friendly about this.  Too bad for them and three cheers for the Old Granite Street Eatery.  In fact, I had 'messaged' ahead to the establishment via Yelp to ask if they had a corkage and I really didn't expect to hear from them.  Less than 30 minutes later, I got a message from the owner.  This is what I'd call attentive customer service.

2)  As our reservation was at 5:30, we got to enjoy the Happy Hour for 30 minutes from the comfort of our table.  This meant we got 3 starters for $10, and half off on the wine by the glass.

3)  We really liked the starters.  We had the Shishito Peppers, the prosciutto wrapped persimmons, and bacon chips.

4)  If you go this route, you may want to wait a bit on your dinner order, as it was a significant amount of food.

5)  It wasn't enough to dissuade me, but my wife did reach capacity fairly early, forcing me to consume most of the appetizers.  At this point in the meal I still had not had the chicken.

6)  Lea and I both enjoyed our wines by the glass.  She had a Chardonnay, and I had a glass of Carignane.

So, after the above had occurred, Lea opted into a lentil salad and a side of asparagus.  She enjoyed both, but, as you might suspect, I ended up eating the lion's share of the asparagus.  

I inquired about the steak on the menu, and I was told it was a 'chuck' steak.  Now I was in the mood for a steak, but I found myself perseverating on a filet or a Rib Eye.  If the waitress had told me it was one of those I would have forgotten the calorie rich (read high fat) lunch that I had already had that day and ordered it.  But since it was not one of those I asked the waitress what she recommends, and she said the chicken breast.  I listened to her suggestion and that's what I ordered.

It arrived on a quinoa, lentils, and couscous with a ginger yogurt and sliced veggies on top.  Simply put, I thought it was very good, and worthy of a risky comment to my wife.  The breast was cooked very well, tender and moist enough to cut with a fork, and the spice and flavors that arrived with it were incredible.  It's 22 hours later, and I'm starting to salivate again.

Our dinner concluded with a piece of the bread pudding.  I enjoyed it, but, as my wife was full, she didn't have any, too bad for her.

Midtown Reno has a number of great dinner options, and the Old Granite Street Eatery is on the list.

My husband and I were really disappointed.  I made a reservation weeks in advance of our New Orleans vacation.  It was my second trip to New Orleans, and I ate at NOLA my first visit and really enjoyed it, so I couldn't wait to try this restaurant.  

We went on a Sunday night about two weeks ago and we're seated right away.  It wasn't too busy, there were open tables and we probably didn't even need a reservation.  We both had bowls of gumbo as our starter and ordered the fried chicken for two as our entree.  We were really disappointed when our waiter told us they no longer offered the three course meal.  I had read great reviews about it in Yelp, and it was on their website too.  I found out the next day that it was restaurant week in New Orleans, so all the other restaurants we went to had great specials (Commander's Palace, Mr B's Bistro), but Emeril's had no specials for restaurant week.  

We chose the Fried Chicken for two because we saw the platter when we first walked in, and it made my mouth water.  The gumbo was very good, but not the best I've had (it was sausage gumbo).  The fried chicken was disappointing, because it took at least an hour to come out of the kitchen!  An hour AFTER we finished our gumbo.  I thought that was really bad service, especially at such an upscale restaurant.  It tasted pretty good, but I think the wait ruined our dinner.  Especially when we saw everyone else getting served.  Our waiter never apologized or said anything (like you're food will be out soon).  After that, we didn't want to wait for dessert, and we're just ready to go back to the hotel.  I think you're paying for Emeril's name, and not much more.  It was our most expensive meal, about $125 with tip, and a couple glasses of wine.  Our money would have been better spent elsewhere, like Commander's Palace.  Also, we heard the waiters complaining about bad tips (while we were WAITING forever for our food).  Not a classy place.

Been dying to try this place out and finally trekked over there. I'm so glad there are more ramen places opening up! I ordered the spicy ramen and felt the broth and noodles were the perfect quantity and thickness for someone who enjoys a little more substance in their ramen. I almost couldn't finish it! It was spicy but not painfully so and I enjoyed the toppings that came with it. The egg is perfectly cooked. I might make it more spicy next time! I wish the meat didn't have so much fat on it, I had to slice off a lot of chunky bits but that is my only complaint. The gyoza and fried chicken were delicious! The bubble tea wasn't my favorite, I don't know if I didn't get it sweet enough or what but the flavors just didn't come through. I might try a different combo next time. I will say this place is pretty pricey though so plan accordingly. We wanted to try it all out and the check was about $60 for 2 entrees 2 apps and 2 drinks which is a little more than I've paid for ramen in the past.

11/11/21

Happy Veterans Day. Had a hard time getting dinner tonight. Glad we came here. This has been on my to-visit list.

Quality/Quantity -
Free beer samples.
Simple small menu.
Midwest Meat Pizza - Did not think this was made in house, it tasted pre-refrigerated or frozen. Fairly thick pizza, good rise.
Oven Roasted Wings - Good size, meaty.
Good local beer on tap - Sorry, I forgot what I ordered because I drank it too fast.
Nice selection of beers on tap, approximately 62 taps.

Atmosphere - Small parking lot, but empty.
Not sure why there are so few customers here tonight...?
Not sure if we were lucky or not.
Enjoyed the quiet atmosphere while watching the game.
Free wifi.
Good beer information/education decor on walls.
I liked the beer decals/stickers in the restroom.

Service - Good, nice, and took care of us.

Price - $50, I felt a little pricey, but did not care as this was our 3rd attempt to eat dinner!

Owner Suggestion - I hear you are going through management changes. I see new ownership in 2019 on your website. Are you a franchisee? There are 12 locations on your website. I suggest a happy hour. How did Bingo Mondays work for you?

Went to Luke for Happy hour, thinking I would be getting the most delicious 50 cent oysters and excited. When I breezed through the door with my companion, the woman at the desk informed us that unfortunately there were no reservations available. Looking around the restaurant, this was hard to believe, as 85% of the tables were empty. Yes. 85%. So we went to eh bar, and to our dismay there were no seats either. So we returned, oysterless, to the woman the desk and asked again, "are there any seats, just for half an hour, so we may consume our oysters?"

"No" she replied,"All of our tables are absolutely booked. We are just swamped."

"but..... it shows me I can make a reservation on open table,." my intelligent companion interjected, with her iphone in hand, the light glowing on her face and over my heart.

And in my head, the trumpets sounded, while a dark gloom came over her face. Slightly puzzled, and slightly annoyed, she said that she could lead us to a table, bcuz she "trusted" our ability to make the reservation.

WAHT?!?!?!?!?!!?!?! And then she promptly seated us, in the back.

The oysters were fine. They were fine. P & J 50 cent oysters They didn't have minuet sauce. Sad face. Only cocktail and sauerkraut. Disappointed Sad face.

My wife and I came upon Lemmons after taking a trip one day down Gravois.  My wife immediately reacted to memories she had as a child coming to Lemmons from Florissant to enjoy their famous Fried Chicken.  So, today, we decided to try them for lunch.  
What an experience.
We were greeted and seated immediately by our server, Justin.  He gave us a brief history of how Lemmons has changed since my wife's childhood visits and how the newest owners have really transformed this eatery. 
First, we ordered the chicken wings that were served with sauce on the side (as I like HOT and my wife like MILD).  Wow!  What flavor these "naked" wings had on their own and were very crispy.  (I even took the Chili Sauce home with me).
Second, I ordered the Chicken Schnitzel with Carrot Mash and Chef Vegetable, which were Cherry Tomatoes with field greens in a light oil based dressing.  My wife ordered the Pot Roast Sandwich with Provolone Cheese, mushrooms and grilled onions on their Balkan Style Hoagie.  DELICIOUS!!!
Our server, Justin, made this a great experience...thank you!  We can't wait to take our extended family back.
Where do I start? Soup dumplings, minced pork mearballs, shanghai noodles are my top 3. Service is good and prices won't break the bank. One of my go to spots in Chinatown.

Not bad, not great either . I was craving tacos and although satisfied it was very bland, plus all of the salsas were less than hot. Even the "spicy" Verde 

I asked for hot sauce and to my surprise it is the first taco place I've ever been to that does not have bottled hot sauce anywhere to be found. Odd

Also, the Spanish rice is more like the microwave rice with peas and carrots that you get at PandaExpress.

Otherwise, nice cashier and very clean.

A restaurant that is a bit large and with an extensive menu to be called a neighborhood restaurant. However you are treated as if this is a cozy neighborhood establishment. Service is always friendly and attentive.

And also just as important is the food. I was pleasantly surprised at the flavors that are produced in the kitchen. After a few visits to check them out I am now a regular. Their menu will take a number of visits to explore fully. And you will want to return to explore the offerings.The Pecan Crusted Chicken is a must.

Prices are reasonable and the glass of tea or soft drink are bottomless. Free parking in the Warehouse District is another reason to visit and enjoy a very nice restaurant.

Delicious! Visiting from Seattle area and we were so impressed with the food! I got the spicy steak bowl and my husband got the spicy salmon bowl. Both were so good! The staff was super chill and friendly. Highly recommend!

No call back. No apology. VERY disappointed!
Luckily I have over 35,000 local followers I can share this with.

I've gone to Asian Wok for over 9 years.
All of a sudden they were so rude and mean, I was actually in tears.

I tried telling them this... NO RESPONSE!

I don't know what has happened in their lives, but I watched their little boy grow.
VERY disappointing. 
I guess sooner or later it happens to everyone in this damn rude country!

AY Lappa

Crawfish Pasta is the hardest dish to prepare the same consistently. There are so many different recipes, it can really screw your ego over. 

Trust me, Marigny I know the feeling, each time I try to cook it, it comes out a different way. Marigny is no exception to the rule.  I can't say there was a time when it was not tastie.  I just don't want to go to a restaurant and tell a chef how to cook my food. I want him to tell me.. 

I never tried the brunch but i will go back and review it for you fans..

I think the TV is a little obnoxious for a restaurant, but that could be a great thing during Hornets or Saints games...
Food was very good. Ambiance was very nice. Waiter Alex, really had no idea what he was doing.
Love this place!! Great food, good service! We come every time we go to NOLA. Easy to find in the Quarter, right around the corner from Bourbon street.
This is where we went earlier tonight.  It's an old stagecoach inn and you step back in time when you go there.  It's not our NYE dinner but it was a good one!

We've tried dozens of pizza places since moving to the area, and we keep coming back to Emiliano's. It's just simply the best tasting around here.

The sides and dinners are nothing to write home about, but the pizza is always enjoyable.

One of the most affordable sushi spots! I got take out recently. 

We got a crunchy roll, a salmon avocado & the Hana roll along with shrimp dumplings. It came with a big thing of yum yum sauce! The shrimp dumplings were only $4 and change- lil things but really delicious. Rolls were decent and large.

The order didn't take long when I took into account how busy they were inside. Seems like a popular spot for the college students. Inside is a cute vibe- I've heard there's a complimentary noodle salad & warm handcloths, so I'd like to go back & try dining in one day.

Unbelievable we didn't get seated till 10:33 and they stop serving breakfast at 10:30. The waitress said the take the eggs away at 10:30. I didn't see anyone leaving with eggs LOL! 
So we went across to Bay coffee and tea company they had eggs
Cute little bread and bagel spot. I got the chorizo sausage on asiago bread... delicious! Was steady when I came in but staff was still courteous and friendly.
Yummy donuts, yummy muffins, need I say more?!  And having gone to Hillsboro, going to the Donut Den is a nostalgic experience for me.
We had a wonderful afternoon at Perche No. We were well received by the staff and owner, Jules. The food was delicious and served hot! Loved it and will definitely go return soon.

I'll never tire of new sushi spots opening up in the city!  And this place definitely delivers. After eating all-you-can-eat at Aki, it's usually hard to follow up with  regular a la carte sushi, but it was nice leaving here comfortably full and not feeling like I needed to be rolled out the door.

Me and two others went on a Friday night and got there at about 7, white wine and prosecco in hand. We snagged the last seat that was available and it packed up a LOT immediately after. So definitely get here earlier if you can. The other reviews say they don't take reservations, however, the only other available table had a sign that said "reserved" on it, so maybe if you call ahead they will reserve one for you?

Its nice enough inside, with a decent amount of seating, but had a lot of random neon lights and an overall Technicolor vibe. I would say the atmosphere at Umai Umai is way trendier and nicer. They also didn't have chilling buckets for the booze, which I've noticed a lot of BYOB sushi places don't do for whatever reason. Our server was able to bring us a pitcher of ice water in lieu of this, though. Service was good, nothing bad or special.

Between the three of us, we tried 6 rolls. I like that they have different chalkboard specials of the day so the one special we tried was the "Fairmount Roll" which had lobster, a jalapeno soy wrap and fried crab on top. SO good. And super innovative. I've never had a green soy wrap like that. Would definitely order that if it was on special again.

From the regular menu, we also tried the Romantic Roll, Rainbow Roll, Triple Spicy Roll, Fantastic Roll and one other that I forget now. All were fresh and delicious but we all agreed the Fantastic Roll with shrimp tempura was the best.  The shrimp was battered and fried perfectly, yet wasn't overly heavy or mealy.
