I ordered the Rainbow Roll since it's my favorite and the best way to gauge sushi anywhere. It was good, but definitely not as good as the ones from Umai Umai or Aki.

The last set of rolls we ordered took a very long time to come out, but we weren't in any rush and were able to digest, drink our prosecco and wine and get hungry for the next bit.

For 6 rolls with tip, it came to about $88. Not bad prices for the quality, I'd say.

I will definitely be back when I'm in the area.

It is what it is... A cheap fast eat..
So if you are a college student with a fixed budget, this is probably for you. Sure you get a large portion, if you're into being fed in a trough like a pig..

Their credit card machine is flaky so bring cash.  They also took tonkatsu off the menu.

My favorite Italian in Boise!! The best!! Go now, go!! 
We have been to Italy and this is the closest thing we have found in Idaho. We get it for take out and go in and dine. Take out is just as good too, so if you have a little one like we do get take out. If we take our baby though it is still family friendly. 
Good service, amazing food. Never disappointed and we get it every few weeks, we take family there and I have suggested to many friends to go. No one is ever disappointed. 
The best Italian!!!

Older ma & pa's kind of diner/restaurant.  Great location & excellent service.  We had no clue they closed at 2pm as we got there at 1:50p they were more than happy to still serve us.  Many locals there as well.  

Sat at the diner, immediately served.  Great coffee & breakfast sandwiches.  We had the ham, cheese & egg on white toast & the bacon, egg & cheese on a warm flaky croissant, side of hashbrowns.  Excellent way to start the morning & it was all so good.  Love the crispy hashbrowns.  

Next time, I will try an omelette as they seem to be known for them.  The Alaskan or Lox type of omelette featured on their Yelp looks delish!
Nice place in the terminal for food. Small menu but good food. Prices are not terrible either. The waitress was friendly and quick. Place was clean.

Really amazing service. Knocked off two stars because my food is always cold! The staff is so friendly but I cannot stand cold food. I will always give it another try but until they start serving hot food I don't think I will enjoy it as much as I could

Kind of a mixed bag here. Overall, the staff seems disengaged. Not very welcoming. That said, my waitress (Khjadira) was excellent. Her efforts alone bumped this up a full star. 

The food was average at best. I never expect the world from airport food. But, the burger toppings were not the best. The bun was standard, even though it promised to be brioche. Patty was a good size, but the onion ring topper was soggy. 

The fries were pretty good. They had a nice seasoning to them. 

The place does have a full bar. I had Diet Coke, but maybe this is why a lot of people were here - for the drinks. 

I spent $17.22 for a burger, fries and Diet Coke, not including gratuity. I should have gone to Burger King. Would have been about the same quality for a lot less. In this space, they really need to differentiate their food from standard fast food fare.
They have the most awesome tuna steak Phillies I've ever had and the people are over friendly.  They'll even sit in your lap if you ask them.  Great place to go.  Ask for Vicky.

This is my absolute favorite restaurant!!! The food is outstanding and is always of the best quality. Everything they make is fresh and from scratch. The owners and staff are all very sweet and make you feel like family. Some of my favorites are chicken parm, gnocchi Capri, and penne vodka!

Been here several times and finally after todays experience I decided to share. 

Burger came without any lettuce, tomatoes, onions, pickles. When I told my server, the only response I got was "I am sorry."

No thought or attempt to correct the situation.

There were a few other smaller issues which clearly indicated that the staff is unexperienced.

Oh well, another place that I need to avoid in the future.

Great lunch yesterday at Mahoney's. Oh yeah: I have heard the haters and doubters and yes it has changed in the last five years. It's not as divey and informal as in the past. But neither do you wait. bored out of your mind in a long line as some first timer takes 5 minutes to merely grasp the number of po-boys but to then ask: why would it need to be dressed? The po-boys (we had the classic shrimp and oyster ones) are still perfectly prepared. The onion rings and debris fries remain excellent; the beer is cold. The wait staff are efficient and fun. If you want something else--go for it and leave Mahoney's for me.
.

Very nice!  Fun ambiance ,  music, lighting, very upbeat.  I am very picky about my sushi...  And I really enjoyed mine here.  Not your typical sushi bar and I mean that in a good way.  Good service ,  friendly and attentive .

AWESOME spot!!  They serve breakfast, lunch, and dinner but I have only had their breakfast.  They have a great selection, especially for people who are conscious of what they eat or have food allergies.  I eat gluten-free and both times I was here I got the GF pancakes...DELISH!  So, so good.  Everything here is great, from the food to the juice and smoothie selection.  Little bit pricey for breakfast but well worth it.

Although not too far from home, I had never tried this place.  It is quite nice and we will be back.

Salt Rock has a nice atmosphere -- upscale, but fun and comfortable.  There is an extensive selection of beer, wine and craft cocktails at reasonable prices.

The menu is interesting, and all of the selections we saw in our group were creative, high quality, and presented very nicely.  We had a great evening with friends.

If you sit in a booth, there is a TV in each booth, which is nice for Saturday nights when you might want to keep an eye on a college game.  ;)
I like Prince's Hot Chicken. It is nice to see it in South Nashville.  I am glad to be a fan of Prince.
Great taste, great service, enjoyable experience. Sauce bar is pretty cool as well. Big fry portions, burgers cooked to order, full after one burger. Worth my money spent. Cheers

The food is good but the service is like everyone is new and scrambling around, even when there's not many people there.  It's almost stressful watching a few of them struggle.

I sat down and said hi to the bartender / server and she didn't even say hi back she said do you know what you want?  Without even offering a menu.  The two drinks she made me were inconsistent and it was the same daiquiri.

I"m not a regular, been there twice.  Why wouldn't you greet your guests instead of first asking them what they want?  It's basic service.

Salsa's 4.5/5
Shredded chicken burrito 4/5
Enchilada's 4/5
Service 2/5

Good happy hour specials for the $5 burritos and drinks.  Would be nice if the drinks were a little bigger.

Expectations vs reality is a theme lately for plenty of jokes. I, however, just fell prey. Work has prevented my returning to this most delicious sushi location. My favorite roll, giant ramen, and the rolls my better half loved as well. Great prices for wonderful flavors....but I digress, this will be our last visit. The chef remembers the requested favorite roll, but is unable to make.
The reality is the customers are not priority. I shall save myself 40 minutes of travel time for maybe a little less flavor but a whole lot more consideration. Thanks for the memories I Ai, but our time is done.

This pub has a NOLA reputation for its beer culture and selection, and perhaps we should have gone there for that and not tried to have pub grub along with it. As another reviewer here has complained, our burgers were raw and inedible. I carried them downstairs to complain and when I saw the cook furiously wielding her flipper over a tiny stove I decided that if I asked for a replacement it might include some "extra" ingredients. I returned the meal (we weren't charged), we finished our beers, and went over to Voodoo BBQ for our meal.

---Review is 3.5 stars

I enjoyed my time at Brian's. 
They have a set menu concept, and you bring your own bottle. The place is cozy and cute, which makes it ideal for a date. 

I came with my family and we all tried each other's dishes, so I can say my favorites were:
- First course: risotto 
- Second course: Beef a la mode
- Dessert: Banana foster 

The service was a bit impersonal, which was a bit of a shock to be honest. 
They only take cash and Venmo, so come prepared.

Feeling fancy? Head on down to The Dandelion. The place is beautiful. You'll feel like you've made the right choice the second you walk in. We came for tea time which is 3-5. First of all...tea time?! Amazing! Its a different menu. Less food. More tea and booze. We weren't super hungry anyway so we snacked on some marinated spicy olives and Welsh rarebit. Which made us insanely angry we couldn't cone back the next day for an actual meal. Sooo good!!! The bread was so soft and flavorful, we inhaled it. Same for the olives. Our drinks were among the best i've ever had. We got the Queen's Garden and the Basil Punnet. A must stop in Philly, no question!

Ate the Taco Bell for dinner last night. Got violently ill a couple hours later. The tacos were sitting in my stomach all night then at bed time they all came up. Safe to say I'll never eat there again. Plus the service was terrible anyway. Took 15 min for my tacos.

When in New Orleans, you visit Pat O'Briens. (Right?)

The courtyard is always a great place to relax and if you're there when the weather is chilly, there are a ton of heaters to keep you warm - in case the drinks don't do a good enough job.

Drinks aren't cheap, but you are paying for an extraordinary amount of liquor in each one. One Hurricane for me, one mint julep for the spouse and we were both struggling to feel our cheeks. That doesn't happen very often.

We made sure to order drinks in a to go cup so we didn't have to worry about the whole return-for-refund if you didn't want the souvenir glass. It just made things easier since we didn't know when we'd be ready to go nor how long the line might be when we were.

A great place to hang out, if there are tables available, is in the piano bar. Dueling pianos and strong drinks are always a winning combo in my book.

Prepaid for Thanksgiving dinner for four people. The turkey was good. The mashed potatoes and stuffing or in scoops, potatoes only had three scoops, the stuffing had four. We were supposed to get green bean casserole, instead we got green beans that were blanched, put them in the same pan as the potatoes and stuffing. I had to pull them out and further cook them. The stuffing and the potatoes were a disappointment as they were very moist, too moist. The macaroni and cheese, I could have made for my box and paid $10 for. We got one little roll per person, not homemade, just like the ones you get in the store for Thanksgiving....
The food was in nice containers, aluminum so they can be heated up in the oven. 
I should have gone with Bob Evans. Lesson learned.

The restaurant is old 90's Chinese decor but don't let it fool you the food is good fresh vegetables I only ask a Lil more seasoning but great amount of food for the price some of the items on they're menu come close to Hong Kong pearl which is a mile down the street and probably the most popular in the area but everthing I ate here had a delicate taste to it the egg roll was moist and crispy and fluffy and fresh not hard or crunchy there is a difference in crispy and crunchy and the rice was prepared graciously and it takes a good hand to make great rice just rice i ordered the shrimp lo mein combo and the egg drop was great the lo. Mein noodle were delicate and tasteful I recommend coming here cause the food is good and atmosphere is a Lil dapper but I came to eat not gaze at the ceiling and walls

Omgggg this place is amazinnggg.  Get anything off that grill and feel free to go for any of the signature dishes or specials.  Everything is fresh and well prepared.  Even the sides are soooo gooood - cilantro lime rice and black beans oh holy moly.  My favorite is the matrimonio - grilled skirt steak and chicken with chimmichurri.

Went in for a shake to go. I now have to order via the kiosk. It says "Customize". But I can't get a Snickers milkshake with chocolate ice cream or chocolate syrup. No one at the counter to speak to about this. Fortunately, the Sonic up the street let me order what I wanted from a real live person.

I was really hoping to like this restaurant, especially after seeing all the great reviews on yelp. 

Once my party and I arrived, we walked in and had an awkward moment (host see us, see her, see us for about 2 min) yet no one walked over to greet us. 
Once we sat down, the server didn't acknowledge us till maybe 4 minutes after we were seated.... then the table was sticky...our who experience was just super awkward...
Waited approximately 1 hour on appetizers and another 30 minutes on our food. Sat without drink being refilled for a very long time. All of our party did not get their food when it finally came out.

What a great place! In addition to having great fresh sandwiches that explode with flavor in your mouth, they have great shakes, salads and everything else.  The Wreck, is the best sandwich I have ever had.  The people preparing your food are artists, and extremely friendly.  Laid back atmosphere with books, games and occasional local talent playing music make this a great stop for lunch and dinner.  Love it.

stop playing around and order the jumbo gyro!  if you work up an appetite kicking around the loop "Gyro House" is the tastiest bang for the buck.  The atmosphere is nothing exciting....checkered table clothes and posters of greece.....but you won't care after you've taken you're first bite.

I really enjoyed my visit. This my first time there. Great service, decent food, and outstanding live music, The Bishops.

Intended to stay just enough for a couple of beers. Ending up staying 5 hours!

Fantastic Food and service. We had "Brandon" , (Ask for him!). The Mushroom Goat Pizza my wife had was the best pizza she had this year, so much flavor! I thought it was awesome too. My Double Fisted Burger was great. Toasted roll, meat done to perfection, succulent portabella mushroom with a sunny side up egg. What more can I say, so satisfying. 

I'll be back often with my friends and family.  Joining the crowd of good people and positive energy.

This cozy little place was somewhat hidden around the corner, but the small, simple interior gave a feel that you were eating in a friend's kitchen.  The service was very kind and polite, if occasionally slow. 

A free small bowl of chips (with a bit of refried beans and fresh cheese sprinkled on top) with red and green salsas came out first. Our order of seafood soup (large!) and tacos (3 per order and very well-portioned fillings) took a bit long, but we enjoyed waiting and watching some soccer playing on the TV.

Our dishes were delicious and sizable, though we felt that it didn't quite reach the same level as Los Gallos. It seemed like everything was made fresh to order, and the fresh handmade tortillas were superb. 

Also, it seems like they don't offer tamales any more. :-(

This is by far our best experience in New Orleans. We love all the dishes and the service is amazing. You need to wait because they don't take reservations, but there is a bar downstairs and you can wait there.

Service: good

Food: Bland.  I had the steak burrito.  Mexican rice with a layer of beans rolled with barely there steak pieces.  Sour cream and cheese need to be ordered separately, and I think you need to pay extra for them.  The chips were thick and came with 3 different types of salsas.  
The margarita was just meh.  

I'm not the mexican food expert, but I've had mexican food all over the US and Mexico.  And I know one thing... Mexican food is not, and should not, be bland.  
I think they are charging too much for the quality of food they are serving.

We stopped in here for a quick bite while waiting for a friend to join us for dinner somewhere else (I know, a snack before dinner....LEAVE US ALONE!)

Anyway, the snack was delicious. I'm not a fan of soft cheeses, but I was all over this ricotta. So good. I hope to return very soon to try one of those amazing-looking flatbreads I salivated over.

Parran's is a small place on Veterans Blvd. The atmosphere is VERY casual. They serve a varied menu, but, their claim to fame is their roast beef poboy. Well, I will have to say it is good (not even close to the Frostop in Picayune, Ms), and, it is a nice size portion at a reasonable price. No sides come with it. The catch here is that a Dixie beer in a bottle will set you back about $4.00. I guess by New Orleans standards that is ok. But, you serve yourself. You order at the register and they bring it out to you. You get your own drinks out of their cooler and the waitress only cleans the table when you leave. I noticed nobody leaving tips, but, that goes against my dining manners. Food was good, but, I've had much better!! Try it...you might like it?

I would have put five but yelp filters out 1 stars and 5 stars. Anyone who knows me, knows that I am BRUTALLY honest and complain about anything and everything. Having said that and having lived in Miami, their cuban sandwich is incredible! I can not believe Philadelphia magazine has not put this sandwich on their best sandwiches you've never tried in Philadelphia. Stop reading this and order the sandwich

Taco Dirty is one of my all time favorite lunch spots in Tampa and I was so excited to eat it again!
It's been about two years since my last bowl and the flavor is still delicious!
One of the exciting changes I noticed is that their menu is more streamlined and they offer the same proteins, veggies, and bases. 
When I used to go, everything was seasonal.
I am definitely glad brussel sprouts made the cut because it's my fav!
I usually get a snack bowl but since it's been awhile, I got the ALL IN BOWL!
You get to choose two bases, two veggies, two proteins, and toppings!
My bowl had the Citrus Chicken, Lime Chicken, Avocado Rice, Black Beans, Brussel Sprouts, and crispy buffalo broccoli topped with cotija cheese!
This is my first time trying the broccoli buffalo style and I loved the extra crunch!
I of course also had to get a fresh juice that comes with free refills!
My go to juice is the Blue Majik! I just love the blue color from the spirulina and the taste!
Always a pleasure to come here!

This was probably the first place I ate at when I first moved to Tampa a few months ago. Looking at the previous Yelp reviews, I had high expectations and oh boy did they meet them. Blue Sea lives up to its name. The seafood here is made fresh to order and is delicious. I split an order with my mom and we could barely finish half of it. It seriously can feed an army...well, an army of people who enjoy crazy fried seafood. Besides the insane portion sizes, the price tag was pretty cheap. Typically, fried seafood runs upwards of $10-20 per person and this was $10 for two...and we still had left overs. My favorite would be the shrimp, but I'll let you be the judge of that. Overall, the experience was wonderful and the service was great. No complaints here!

tl;dr - Cheap? Yup. Delicious? Yup. Awesome-sauce? Yup.

Perfect timing today as we arrived before the lunch rush. We were seated at a table next to the open windows. The weather was perfect and the Bloody Mary was THE BEST. The blacked catfish poboy  was very tasty as was the chicken gumbo. Loved the atmosphere! Service was great!

I'm actually writing about their Grant Street location in Tucson.  La Salsa is fast-food no matter which location you visit--like the majority of eateries in this city.  Their Grant Street location experience: the person at the cash register stood there stone-faced, no smile, breathing eagerly, expecting the customer to instantly blurt out their order, pay for the meal, take the number and then a table.  The shrimp burrito came out singed, too much cabbage.  The eating establishment itself was a little unkept, you bus your own table.  I'll pass on this next time.

There isn't really much I can say about this place except for WOW. I don't even know where to begin. This place is the end all be all of pizza shops. It's more than just a dinner it's an experience. Your experience starts a few days before when you have to call in your order of how much dough you would like. Usually we order 3 pies(two for there and then one to savor later at home). Once you get there you figure that since you called days in advance you would sit right down to have dinner. NOPE! You usually have to wait to get your table which only adds to the anticipation. Sitting on those benches and watching those people enjoy their pizzas really gets my tummy rumbling. Now, I know this may frustrate some people but I just look at it as them adding some extra love to the pizza. Every pizza is hand spun and then placed in a coal fired oven with authentic Italian limestone that gives the pizza its signature taste.  Once you do get your pizza don't eat it just yet because usually it comes out HOT. One time I tried to eat it and boy was I sorry. I burnt my tongue, ouch! But it's like a souvenir, or a tease of the pure pizza ecstasy you are about to experience.  But when the pizza comes that's my favorite because as soon as it gets placed on your table you can smell all the ingredients coming together. Nothing beats a good sniff! After that it's your time to enjoy.Also, the bottom of the pizza usually comes out black. Don't worry though because you know what they say"the blacker the crust the sweeter sauce"! Dig in, take a bit, and enjoy. Your mouth will be in cheesy saucy heaven. It's pretty sad once your all finished though. But wait! You ordered that third pizza, remember?!?!?! Now you have the deliciousness of your experience coming home with you. All in all I would give this place an A+++

We went to Bristol's for their Sunday brunch today. We've been before and it was wonderful, as always. The oysters on the half shell were small and very fresh. Smalls are my favorite and are sometimes hard to get. They had a hot shrimp Mexican dish that was fabulous -- sorry, I can't remember what it was called. Service was great. My only complaint is that they put sugar in the grits. NO PLEASE! Sugar does NOT go in grits! Would you put sugar on your corn on the cob? Nope....grits are corn; they get salt and butter. Sadly, they were cooked perfectly -- no lumps, well cooked so they weren't grainy, but inedible because of the sugar! Everything else was perfect. The carrot cake is divine with the coconut pecan filling. If you just want a nibble of dessert, they had key lime pie shooters and tiny creme brulee servings. Overall, very good.
1. Fresh Produce always 2. Cafe downstairs 3.Upstairs bistro with tons of seating 4.Fresh,Fresh,Fresh 5. You will love it

REALLY! I expected good food and even better service from your Manager Matt - not the case. When a customer has an issue one should expect your manager to come and speak to you personally - never happened . Obviously his customers are not his top priority. I will take my company business elsewhere..

One of my favorite local restaurants. The food is delicious and the service is impeccable. They do not take reservations and there is always a wait, but it is very well worth it! We try and go earlier or later if we can but don't be surprised if you have to wait even at 9:30pm! It's great in the summer with the outdoor area too.
Really love this place! Food is amazing staff is great! Love that they have live music and stay open late! This is a gem!

Worst service ever. After 20 minutes of being seated, water was finally brought. . but not by our server. Finally after waiting 5 more minutes of no one coming over (mind you the restaurant was not full and very staffed) we got up and walked out.
This place is amazing. The food is light and bright and delicious. We've gotten delivery 2x and it was so good. And I like that they us biodegradable packaging.
Regular bar food- ok. Highlight were the calendar girls.

I usually come to this Moe's  to get burrito. To celebrate the Cinco de Mayo , the burrito was on sale plus the first 50 customers got a free t-shirt. When the customers walked in, the staff greeted them  with warm welcome. Customers choice meat,  rice, beans or vegetable. The employee worked efficiently so the line moved fast. The food was freshly cooked and the burrito tasted good. The soda machine was cool with so many choices of drinks.  They usually have 5 to 6  choices of salsas at the bar. They were perfect for the freshly fried  chips. The Monday burrito special includes a  drink and chips and a burrito. It  is a good value for a delicious meal.

When I knew there was a new Cunningham restaurant on the block I had to check it out. We went on a Monday night so it wasn't too busy. The patio was full but plenty of space inside. We got the Nashville hot chicken sandwich and the grilled cheese. I personally didn't care much for the grilled cheese but my other half loved it. I did like the Nashville hot chicken sandwich but be prepared for a little spice. The inside is way nicer than it was before. I know people are upset about old point tavern closing but I think this is a great addition. Check out their new spot! Also, if you aren't signed up for Cunningham VIP Program you're missing out.

I've gone here a few times over the past couple of months, and actually primarily for the food, not for drinks. I've gotten the cheese plate a couple of times, which is always good. I got their grilled cheese--most definitely the BEST I have ever had because they use I think 3 different kinds of delicious fine cheeses (though I don't remember which ones). French fries fried in duck fat. Delicious. The other customers always always a bit stuffy and kind of unpleasant to be around, but the food & service is solid.

I'm new to TN and someone recommended this place.  Don't judge by the outside. ..This place is a Dimond in the rough.  The Hibachi Shrimp is awesome.  The give you the large shrimp.  Spring Rolls are very light.  I had the white rice and it was the right texture.  You get a lot of food..but not a high price.  It was loaded worth veggies.  It also had red potatoes. . Sounds weird but it  added a great texture.  I was very pleased.  We had 6 people & our bill averaged $10 per  person.  I don't live in Whitehouse,  but will drive back to eat here again:)

We knew we wanted to explore some of the cemeteries in New Orleans.  We wanted to avoid a giant group tour... so we booked arranged a private tour with just our six friends and the guide.  We emailed Phantoms and they were quite accommodating.  The booked our cemetery tour for only $150 as a private group of six.  

Upon arrival, we checked in and got wristbands which permit entry into the St. Louis Cemetery.  The grounds are protected and you must have a certified tour guide to enter.  After check-in, we ducked into the attached dive bar to grab a drink.  It is New Orleans after all!  After a warm-up drink, our tour guide Aubrey found us and introduced herself.  She was friendly and entertaining.  She briefly explained what our tour would consist of, what to expect, etc.

Aubrey discussed the history of New Orleans' cemeteries as we walked towards the cemetery grounds.  At her encouragement, we stopped for quick restroom break, which was a perfect idea.  Finish any alcoholic beverages before entering the cemetery grounds.

Once inside the cemetery Aubrey dived into the history of its residents, structure, layout, etc.  She covered everything from Marie Laveau to why the graves are built the way they are.  Yes, you do stop at what is believed to be the resting tomb of Marie Laveau, but you quickly realize that the cemetery has a lot of other history to offer as well.  You may bring an offering for Marie Laveau if you wish.

Aubrey permitted us to stop and ask questions, take photos, etc.  Her fun and entertaining personality was perfect!

I highly suggest booking a private tour as opposed to the group tours.  They looked massive and difficult to interact with the guide.  We visited in February, but if you are in the commentary in the summer months, bring a bottle of water.  It can get quite hot!

Always leery of brunches because I usually cannot justify eating enough good food to match the price of a brunch buffet. After 1-2 plates of different foods, I am usually stuffed. Today we went to the brunch at Loews ventana canyon resort...one word .....incredible!!!! 
Went with a group of friends and everyone was thoroughly impressed. From the service to the wide variety of different types of food, this brunch is a complete success.

First was a Bloody Mary from the Mary station with a plate of jumbo chilled gulf shrimp and mussels ...the bloody was tasty and bottomless ! Yum
Second, and typically my final plate , was some crispy bacon and plump sausage links accompanied by a wedge salad topped with tomatoes cucumbers and ...more bacon ...when in Rome! 
After 30 minutes or so,I head outside to survey the BBQ station ... Wow wow and wow!!! Carving stations of turkey lamb and prime rib . BBQ ribs ...grilled veggies and fruits among lots of other savory choices.. I scale back and just sample the prime rib with a creamy horseradish topping and two ribs ...succulent to say the least . Prime rib medium rare and ribs that fall off the bone! 
After another 20 min or so, I finish my meal(s) with a trip to the dessert bar ... Once again ...spectacular ...a chocolate fondue station and approximately 20 different types of pies cakes cookies and the like to sample !! 
What a nice treat and top notch brunch to experience with family and friends :)

This has been a neighborhood go-to for several years now. We were very excited to find out that they are now selling bottles of wine. So, we went for dinner. HOWEVER, the corkage fee is $15 which was not mentioned and nowhere on the menu. Our $15 bottle of wine quickly turned into a $30 bottle of wine. We thought we'd get a second bottle to get our money's worth out of the corkage fee, but it turns out the corkage fee is PER BOTTLE. 

And you'll probably leave hungry due to the very small portions (which seem to have shrunk over the past year) and lack of bread basket.

On the bright side, the food (mussels and gnocchi) and wine were tasty and the service is good. 

It's just not worth the price. It seems like Hawthorne's is just trying to get too fancy for what it is.

Michael was an exceptional bartender. My bf and I were traveling back to Oakland airport and we stopped in for a couple of drinks and a quick bite. Drinks were perfect and we had the pretzel and agave chicken bites with blue cheese yummy. Michael knows his stuff and he's very good at what he does. Definitely reasonable prices.

MacNiven's is a really nice local pub with that authentic British feel. They have quite the amazing beer list. I was kinda sad they were out of my first choice of beverage, but I quickly found a delicious substitute. MacNiven's is a great place to talk and grab a beer with friends. What more do you need?

The food was fantastic. I have never received such an amazing portion of charred octopus! (my favorite). Their gin and tonics were right up my alley. I was beyond pleased to bring my friend's here for our girls night out. The only reason I am giving Loquita 4 stars not 5 was because our server disappeared and it took about 20 minutes for us to get our drinks. We had to ask the bussers for silverware and water and no one came to check on the quality of the food or if it was too our liking. The server apologized for not being present and he did comp the birthday girl some amazing churros. The hostesses was very nice and accommodated our request to add another seat at the table.

The pizza at Blackbirds is AMAZING! It was worth the fight through Philadelphia traffic and parking spot hunt. All the slices we had were perfection. The only thing better than their pizza is their wings! My son, after taking his first bite, said, "Oh my God, oh my God, Oh my God...." When we had devoured them he said, "this is the best "chicken" I've ever had... this may be the best day of my life!" The only reason I'm giving them a four instead of a five is due to the disappointing Cubano which was overly toasted (burnt-bitter bread). We'll go back regardless, and I highly recommend this place! If one location is closed, take the time to find the other. It's worth the hunt. The staff is skilled and friendly. The cookies are also great!

I had to write a review, I'm so surprised at the negative comments on this site! The only thing I would somewhat agree with is the service. It took a long time to get a waitress to our table, but once she did... she was great. The food was FANTASTIC. My husband and I shared the blackened sushi roll and the spanish roll - both absolutely to die for. Then after that, we shared the brussel sprouts and the flat bread. Both were just perfection. thanks for the great dinner! i'm in love with the food! half priced drinks (wine included) from 5-7 pm.... um, yeah!

Yummy food in an English pub atmosphere. Good beer too.

Especially fun in the winter when you can sit by the fireplace.

What a wonderful restaurant. Cute, unique atmosphere, great service (Travis and Madee were our staff), an interesting story, and of course...delicious food! Our party of 4 all had the 3-course tasting menu. Most started with the crawfish and goat cheese crepes (mmm!!) and I had the Gorgonzola cheesecake (so flavorful). 

Our entrees were equally amazing: pecan-crusted drum, shrimp and grits, and the largest pork chop I've ever seen! 

For dessert, we tried the unique King Cake specialty dessert filled with cherries and covered in a cream sauce - amazing!

This one is in the Fry's shopping center on Tangerine (cross street Thornydale)  I have been to several Subways in the Tucson area and I will vouch for this one being the cleanest and best run.  The staff is friendly and want to make you a good meal, the food is fresh!    It is my neighborhood subway and even when I'm on the other side of town, I will drive all the way home to get my meal at this one!!  They remember you if you go frequently :D   Bathrooms are clean, floors are clean, they keep food fresh and clean, no overspill into other food bins, they wear their plastic gloves for cleanliness and safety!!

Four of my friends and I went here on a Sunday. There was another table of 4 and another table of 2. I'm not sure what was going on with their staff in the kitchen; however, the service was horrible. I ordered a hummus plate and the deviled eggs and I had no idea that cold food takes that long to be plated and served. After literally 35 minutes of nothing I just cancelled my order. The server was kind enough to offer me a drink for the lack of service which I appreciated, BUT we then get the check and she charges us 18% gratuity because we're a table of 6...so we say "no there's 5 of us" so she reprints it, then we look at the bill and see she kept the hummus on the tab etc etc it was just horrible. I don't know if they were trying to take advantage of us like we wouldn't notice but there are too much pubs and bars to go here.

This location is definitely more my speed than the one on Passyunk. It's not nearly as in-your-face with regards to music and decor. There is plenty of seating, which I imagine is necessary to serve the weekday lunch crowd. 

The menu is filled with healthy choices. I wish there were more places in Philly that catered to a health conscious crowd, and I applaud FUEL for being one of the few. 

So the reason for only three stars is that my take-out salad ended up costing me over $12. Which would have been fine, since I was the one who chose to add grilled shrimp for three bucks, except my salad contained just three shrimp. Three. One dollar per small-sized shrimp. I felt a little had. They were delicious, I just wish there had been more for the cost of the up-sell. 

I'd return if I were in the area and in need of a healthy option, but I wouldn't go out of my way.

Disclaimer it is more like a 3.75! Again I went for brunch so I need to go back for diner to give it a clear rating. Clementines is a new restaurant right on broad street which actually opened during Covid. They have a variety of options on the menu, but nothing super creative. After being stuck between hanger steak or chicken and waffles, someone passed by with the chicken and waffles and it made my decision for me. French toast is served with carmelized apples and whipped cream. Chicken & Waffles has coconut and whipped cream. The burger, which was actually my favorite, was complete with a Russian dressing. I liked the chicken and waffles, it was served with actual chicken pieces and not tenders how some places catfish you with. The waffle was a bit dry. The pancakes are very bland and nothing really memorable about them. I think the menu is pretty simple and they are new so it may get more intricate over time. I'm going to go back and try it again for dinner to give an updated rating. I definitely see the potential and I did enjoy my overall experience there.

Upscale restaurant in Nashville that is honestly only slightly above Olive Garden. Service was okay, not particularly warm and the Rigatoni D, their specialty pasta was extremely underwhelming. It was extremely watery with no creaminess to it at all mixed in with large bites of tough chicken that is difficult to swallow. The only benefit of this restaurant is that they give you a "take home pasta" but this scam only upcharges regular pasta and allows you to go home with a mediocre pasta of your own. Will not come here again, Olive Garden is more convenient.

We were very excited to go here. When you walk in it's certainly very charming with the backyard lights and they do have heat lamps in case it gets cold which were happy about since it got a little chilly last night. There are two things that we were disappointed in with the restaurant. First the service was very slow. Multiple times it took 15 to 20 minutes to get drinks. When we arrived a few of us placed 2 of us ordered to drinks while the others waited to see the wine list. 10 minutes later someone a group ordered wine and some beers. 10 minutes after that the drinks came without the first round of drinks that were ordered by the other people.  We were never brought our drinks. At one point I got up to go get my drink from the bar because it been sitting there. Also the waitresses take turns at your table so you don't have the same waitress which seems to make things difficult for the customer because they don't keep tabs on who is getting what it what time.  Also please note that your dishes do not come out at the same time. Everybody received a dinner plate at a different time. We found this odd.  We even brought over  Eric to our table to tell him that it was taking a long time to get drinks. I believe he's either the owner or the manager. That did not seem to help. Then the second thing we were disappointed in is the portion sizes. We ended up eating later because we were so hungry. I do not recommend the seared tuna because the portion size is incredibly small. We're from Chicago and understand the cost of sushi grade tuna and for $16 it should've been triple the portion. One of our guest actually combined two orders because she thought they made a mistake and gave her an appetizer portion. We later had to re-order another because of that mistake. The potato leek soup was very good and our guest enjoyed the canned seafood choices as well. The avocados salad was very tasty as well. The seating outside is a bit uncomfortable as it involves metal chairs and a bench. It adds to its charm but when six people were saying at a table and there's metal bars below the table it makes it difficult to sit at the ends. I would recommend this as a place to go out to have a good glass of wine and if you're not looking to have a lot to eat. Yes it's romantic like they say but with all the other issues didn't find it worth it.

What a treat! I'm glad in a way more people don't know about how good this place is. It's small and intimate, warm and inviting, and energetic if you want it to be; the food certainly is! This place only gets great marks from my friends and rightly so. 

Recently I had the crab cake entree which, for lack of ANY description, was an "outer body experience!" Ohh my, I cannot say enough about tasty this was. Perfect execution of ingredients, incredibly unique flavours I've never had anywhere else, all in all just a superior dish. 

Service was also great, though they could use some knowledge into latin coffee culture.

This place is so romantic! A cute date spot. I love how it's very small, dimly lit and quaint. A very intimate feel. Food was excellent and the wait staff was exceptional. I had the chirashi and a few of the rolls. Very very good.

I guess my only complaint would be that their mochi icecream had freezer burn. Totally ruined the whole experience of the delectable mochi. Sushi was fresh, but was terribly cut. Inexperience sushi chef? Dull knife? No idea. 

Other than that, I would definitely come back here again.
Excellent Irish food. I had the garlic sauce clams and Guinness stew. Exactly what u expect for well priced Irish fare. Nice clean joint and good service. Recommended.

I must preface this review with the fact that we came in with a group of 16 people. However, the restaurant had time to prepare for a large group as we reserved our table days in advance. 

I'm going to avoid the narrative here and give the overall points of issue:

-While the service was very nice, it wasn't good. Everyone was served in weird increments and my fiance and I were served food like 15 minutes after everyone else without explanation. 

-The portions were small and the quality of food was terrible especially considering the prices. When I buy an $11 flat-bread in St. Louis I'm at least expecting something sharable and when I order a charcuterie board, I'm expecting more than a couple salamis and shaved parm. 

-The cocktails were average at best and very sweet overall. 

-While I know art is not objective, I found much to be desired from the "gallery" aspects of the restaurant. The presentation was amateur -- photos printed on medium weight copier paper and held up with magnets. 

I wanted to like this place but I just can't figure out what the redeeming qualities are. I might stop by for a glass of wine before a show at the Fox or Powell but that's about it.
Whoa! These tacos are so crazy good! Went to a wellness + yoga event and Wakamole was there. They are hands down the best taco vendor. My husband got one of each taco and they even made them quickly.

I moved to reno about 3 months ago, and i found this place through yelp. Due to the positive feedbacks, i had to try this out. It was my first time doing all you can eat and it was wonderful. The price seemed about right and the chefs were very funny and kept me entertained. The service was very quick. Ive heard that this place opened under new management not too long ago. For a place that just opened, the interior design seemed a little bland. But overall, it was a great experience. I'll be back for sure!

The first time I ate here, I became obsessed. 
Everyone knows about the Shanghai steamed pork soup dumplings, which are absolutely amazing! (Definitely use the dumpling sauce on the table also.) 
We have only tried a few other dishes, which have all been very tasty, except for the cold poached chicken with chili sauce. It was definitely weird, and we found a few bones in our dish which we weren't expecting, but it's probably just not our taste. 
As simple as it sounds, they actually have good scallion pancakes here, which in my opinion are pretty difficult to find. The cold cucumber and seaweed salad are also delicious (I know, so simple!) 
We need to keep testing out more dishes here, but the soup dumplings are enough to keep us coming back. 
A great thing about this place is that it's BYO, but a slight turn off of this place is the service being poor. Extremely rushed, as in not even waiting for us to put our coats on to clean the table rushed, but they are nice enough, and again, SOUP DUMPLINGSSSSSS. 
Oh also, don't forget, cash only!
Katie's wasn't great with there service... food was mediocre..the manager was condescending..

I've been visiting this Perkins for 30+ years. I've never had a bad experience. The food is good, the coffee is good, and the staff are the best. I've probably tried most of the breakfast menu and my favorite dishes are the skillet meals. The breakfast potatoes are always cooked nice and crispy. The restaurant is clean but a little rough around the edges as it could use a new decor. But that's typical of any good diner. Perkins stills makes some of the best bakery items. You can stop in just for these goodies. Convenient location with a shopping center across the street.

Savoy is a staple Santa Barbara restaurant that has never let me down. There's a combination of deli style food as well as made to order, but the deli case is always delicious. 

 A few personal favorites are the sides of macaroni and cheese, the quiches, and turkey fritters! Beyond the amazing deli case, they have some absolutely outstanding baked goods. The carrot cake is one of a kind and stands out amongst the deserts available downtown. 

It's a bustling spot, but the line goes quick and the food is always worth it

I really wanted to like Ulele. The flavors were not there. 
While waiting for our table I was drooling over the menu. Everything sounded so good. The inside of ulele is beautiful. A bit industrial but classy. I love it. 
The service was good. Waiter was very efficient, nice, and knowledgeable. 
When our food came out it looked beautiful. The first bit was a totally disappointment. No flavor in any of the tables dishes. 
I got the flank steak with avocado Chimichurri and grilled veggies. My steak came out raw, still cold. I wanted it medium rare. After sending it back, it came back medium well. Anyway, it wasn't great. Pretty boring. Chimichurri did nothing to help it. Asparagus was really thick, too hard, too boring. Everything needed a healthy dose of salt. 
My boyfriend got a bunch of sides. Baked squash was so boring-could have made something way better at home. Jalapeño cornbread was dry and also flavorless. Mac and cheese was fine, but nothing special. 
They have the space, and their wait staff down, but the food is lacking big time. I might try Ulele again once they have more time to improve.
Amazing Thai food, cute ambiance, and such awesome/friendly staff. Go there- you won't be disappointed or hungry because their food is delicious and portions are huge!

I've stayed here a number of times over the past number of years. It's a pretty decent hotel generally: the rooms are all suites, the breakfast is good, the hotel pool is completely sufficient, the business centre is A-OK, and the hotel bar is pretty darn good for a hotel bar (I rather liked the flatbread I ate there for example). That said the elevators are infuriatingly slow (and during my most recent stay there one full bank of elevators was out of order leaving the whole hotel using two elevators. 

This hotel has adequate parking and is near a number of restaurants along with head offices for a number of organizations. There is also a nearby Costco if that's something you're seeking out. 

I find it kind of patronizing to see all the signage about the importance of wristbands for use of the breakfast area, and the pool etc. I mean, how often do non-hotel guests come here for use of these areas? Is there really that much abuse of these amenities in this hotel location? 

Compared to many of the other hotel options in the area, this is a really good hotel location. But though this hotel has been updated/renovated over the years where I've stayed here, I'm really disappointed by the elevators and the fact that the wristband system is even necessary (if it's so necessary why was I not given a wristband? -- if this system is just for the children in the hotel SAY so on your signage, please!).

This sub shop has been around "forever". Their subs are HUGE, I dare say it's unusual for someone to eat an entire large by themself. I think their small is the size of most places medium.
There is actually one in Casselberry FL and one in Las Vegas because some of the family moved away. Plenty of meats, veggies, etc. One of the best is the "Bobbi".

My husband and I are visiting St. Louis from out of town, and we stumbled upon this pub on Yelp.  After checking out the reviews, and then their website, we were really hoping it would be at least pretty good. We stopped by for a beer early n the afternoon and sat at the bar.  Sara (Sarah?) was the bartender, and she was so friendly and helpful with suggestions about what to do in St. Louis, what to order for dinner when we came back that evening.  We did come back, and dinner was amazing!   I had the short ribs and my husband had the corned beef and cabbage, per suggestions from Sara and other wait staff that afternoon.  Both dinners were beyond anything we could have imagined.  The short rib literally melted in my mouth, and the seasonings were incredible.  Even the vegetables - glazed carrots and baby potatoes, with some spinach and mashed potatoes thrown in for fun - were so good you had to close your eyes when you ate!  My husband, who is a huge fan of corned beef and cabbage anyway, was over the moon as well.  This food was way above the usual pub fare most of us are used too, and was into the realm of fine cuisine.  And to top it off, our waiter, Sean, couldn't have been friendlier or more attentive.  We ended dinner, pretending like we still had room, with a huge bread pudding that knocked my socks off.

The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, and the Irish band that was playing (the Irish Brigade) was very entertaining.  If I ever get back when it's not during a record heat wave, I'd love to try sitting out in the beautiful courtyard.  Something to look forward to.  I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone.

Another great color with my favorite stylist Sharon! She always accommodates my when I call home on break from college and in need of a root job.i love the Balayag thing she did in my hair this time and I've already gotten so many compliments! I'll be sending all my friends!

Went for Cinco are Mayo. Was greeted by Becca at the patio bar, super friendly and accommodating through all the chaos. When you come to visit ask her for a spicy Classico margarita. Food was good. I recommend the Nueva sampler to start and the crispy shrimp tacos. YUM!

Friendly and quick service is what you'll get at this cute little BYOB on South St. The miso soup and pork dumplings were delish! However, the sushi was forgettable. We tried a variety of rolls and nothing really stood out as exceptional. The spicy tuna was not very spicy, which was disappointing. 

Overall, the flavors were lacking at Kei sushi.

Awesome drinks.  High quality ingredients.  Friendly service.   SUPPORT LOCAL!!! worth going out of your way to support these people that offer organic food personalized service.  

Blueberry hot tea and coffee were amazing.

Who cares about the yogurt i was extremely impressed with the customer service! "Natalie" was working and had no help another customer was being really rude and she handled herself very professionally and still managed to stay cool and be friendly with us! Im new to the area and we eat a lot of froyo in our house...tonights visit made long term customers out of us! ....oh and the yogurt was geeat! Lots of options and tons of toppings!

Ohhh my Gosh!!!! These tacos are nothing to play with! So much authentic techniques and flavor embodied in such a small Tortilla. We had the steak tacos  and Gordita that bursts with punch and subtle spices that you're not gonna wanna miss. This is one for the record books as the best taco place in Tampa!

No refills policy, on self serve fountain soda. Get outta here!  If you're going to offer fountain soda and a place to sit, I'm going to refill it as many times I well please.  And refill it I did.  Last I checked, this was America. The only times I tend to see no refills policies are in fancy restaurants, and some chains in Canada.  But not in ANY OTHER fast food style / cafeteria in America! And certainly never expected this in A&W, a noteworthy SODA brand!  

PS: your typical customer base may pay nearly quarter of a million dollars EACH to live at this college in University City Philadelphia. Did it not occur to you, A&W-Taco Bell hybrid, that if you could afford them a free soda refill to get them hooked on your bread, you'd be making more money in the long run to pay your overhead, and hence, you might not have to be concerned out of such a trivial thing as bagged soda syrup inventory, you gluts? If I were a PENN student with any standards for service, I don't think I would patron a place that tries to enforce rationing on soda. 

Meanwhile, the soap dispenser in this cafe was not working on a given Saturday, and the A&W fountain was not in service either.  So it would appear that this place is ultimately concerned about lining their pockets, and not relining their soda and their soap.  What's that sound? Cheap cheap! Cheap cheap!  I wonder if A&W/TB Corporate and the Board of Health and Dr. Amy Guttman know about such atrocities.

i am so glad, that when i went there was a group of kids split up between pats and genos, most went to genos so there was actually some place to sit. so we picked pats to try first. 
thankfully no line so we ordered like total rookies and messed it up and the guy just laughed at us and smiled. 3 words.... it was like mind blowing lol. but he did tell us to 'enjoy' after thanking him when we got the food ((unlike genos))
the meat, small but it had flavor, wasnt dry but wasnt overly moist, and i just wanted a touch more cheese seemed like the middle of my cheese steak was perfect while the ends dry. 
and it travels well !!!!!!!!!!!! went to ny and the bread wasnt even soggy, while genos went across the street to the car and the bun was soaking wet and we had to toss it before finishing.

i pick pats!
Nice food and strong drinks. I ordered the Blackend chicken pasta and the bottomless mimosa. The experience overall was ok. The waiter was nice and attentive and the establishment was clean.

I am beyond thrilled to have a chick-fil-a on our side of the tracks!!! No more driving into Brentwood!!!  Only downside... no playground here. But for grab-and-go it's fantastic. This place is pretty -- modern and new. I read horrible reviews about the service but the guy who answered the phone was super polite, the girl who took our order at lunch rush outside was super sweet and prompt, the drive thru people were awesome and got everything right, and everyone we could see in through the window looked hard at work. Love it!!! The parking lot is tight when it's slammed, it's a tight right hand turn but the line went quick and who cares -- I'm so glad it's here. Sincerely, Whispering Hills Subdivision Mom of 5

Gentrified tacos. Imagine something as simple and wholesome as a taco then deconstruct it and suck the soul and flavor out of it and for good measure charge a premium. This food is offensive by any standard barely any seasoning and way overpriced portions for the neighborhood. It's like Booty's Street Food all over again. When will you hipsters learn?

Shocked to see this stop with less than 5 stars, because we had a great experience. While I wouldn't consider these traditional tots, these potatoes were perfectly crispy and every piece was covered with delicious toppings. And oh my goodness, these toppings are flavorful! I don't think I'd change a single thing on this plate- so good!

DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!

We have stayed here many times over the course of 4 years while our child was attending the university. It used to be run by the Marriott. We had great experiences up until this last time. 

We, my wife and I, were bitten by BED BUGS. If you have never experienced this you should be thankful. We were evaluated by a physician and it was confirmed. 

We contacted the hotel to let them know so no one else would have this experience. The manager returned our call swiftly and let us know he would look into the situation. I received a call back shortly after the first encounter with management saying they had already checked the room and no bugs. This was within hours, maybe two. The manager tried to tell me I got bit on the plane. That there was no way it was their hotel. Thing is, our flight was outside the time frame of bites to show up. The only difference in our schedule was our stay there. I doubt they would ever admit to having bed bugs because that would be the death of a hotel property. Manager did nothing to sooth our situation. Just try and blame everyone else. 

Cross posted.

When I can't decide between a star rating I will go to the higher star.  I went with my wife Donna, The Famous Chip K. and his wife Bridgett.  I don't know if I started my slow service myself or if it supposed to be a dining experience.  The server came up and told us about the specials and if we had any questions.  I said could we please have an Amuse Bouche of Gougeres cheese puffs and some fromage which was a "platter" of farmstead cheeses.  I did not sample the cheese puffs but I did sample the cheese platter and for $12.00 I was not pleased with the amount or the selection.  4 very small slices of cheese with raisin bread and grapes.  When I  say small I mean small.  Very overpriced for what was there.  We finished the cheese puffs and cheese in short order and it was 15 to 20 mins before our server came back to take our order.  Hmm did I cause that?  Maybe.  

  The famous Chip K ordered the 3 course dinner, our wives ordered hamburgers, and I ordered the Bib lettuce and the  Bouillabaisse.  The three course consisted of salad, Coq au Vin, and dessert called a floating island. 
The hamburgers were tasty as I had a bite of my wife's.
The Bouillabaisse consisted of mussels, calamari, cod fish in a nice broth.  It was $18.00.  See where I am coming from on the fromage platter?  I have had many types of Bouillabaisse and this one was very middle of the road.  Not the worst and not the best.  The portion seemed a little small but then so was the price. So not a problem. I am sure The famous Chip K will review so you can read about his supper when he posts.  

Observations.
Loud impossible to hear and converse.
Trendy in a good way.
The person I assume was the chef kept coming out from the kitchen and gathering up servers to bring the food out.  It was really weird.  Why did he have to keep doing that?
Age group was all over the spectrum.  Was nice not being the oldest for a change.
The valet parking was slow we never did see the valet so we parked over on the  expressway.  Not a big deal just one of those hmm.
Not really a "French" restaurant but still had some good dishes.

Worse service I have ever had. We sat for an hour half with a 8 month old child. We watched five tables after us receive their entrees. We recieved our app and drinks and waitedand waited some more. Never seeing the server.  I spoke to the server. Her explanation was that she was delivering other tables food. We waited another ten minutes and then the table beside us received their food. They had gotten there forty minutesafter us. That was the tipping point. We left. No one said anything to us. The non-existent hostess was nowhere to be seen. When we first came to the restaurant she gave us attitude and explained that we could not sit at a table we requested. We have a small child we were going to place in a high chair.  We didn't want to have it in the way. Terrible experience,terrible food and management. I have been an executive chef and sous chef for years. I wouldnt allow my staff or restaurant run this way. Never going back. I would give it a negative 4 stars.

This review is based upon my customer service experience only. 

I did NOT dine here nor will I ever. I left a tip here for my fellow yelpers and yelp community to recognize how incredibly unprofessional and rude the owner of this establishment is. I called in with a party of 8, 2 hours before closing to see if they could accommodate us and the woman on the phone seemed hesitant like she did not want our business but told us to come anyway. Once we arrived, she said to us before seating, "We will only serve you if you know what you want to order now." We have never been to this establishment before so how could we possibly know what we want, at least seat us, give us menus, and 5 minutes.... Sure enough we left and did not dine here. Any place that treats their customers with no kindness or respect is not worthy of my business. You definitely can tell we were not welcomed and that they wanted to go home though we arrived at 8:15pm and they had over 1 hour 45 minutes left to closing and they had an empty restaurant. If you close at 10pm then you serve until 10pm, not turn away patrons at 8pm. 

Nonetheless I left a tip and the owner Noi L left a comment saying, "You called at 8:15 and showed up at 8:45, so you were late." - I called at 8:00, I have no reason to lie. Regardless if it was 8:00 or 8:15 or 8:45, YOU CLOSE AT 10:00pm so that means your establishment is opened until 10:00pm.

The second comment she left was, "and you came late also so stop your lying." - you can see how unprofessional the owner is here, I need not to say more. 

The third comment said, "Another jealous Asian woman. Go eat somewhere else. We do fine here." - I was a valuable patron, yes I am Asian is there a problem with that? Do you not serve Asian people? Is there a problem that I am a woman also? Can women not have opinions? I am not jealous because what could I possibly gain from this other than you exposing your professionalism for what it is? I am simply a patron who potentially could've dined and liked your establishment but you turned me away. I DID GO ELSEWHERE, Wild Ginger, a place that appreciated my business and did not treat me poorly. And lastly, you will not continue to do fine if this is the way you continue to treat your customers. 

I can't believe the level of immaturity and Iack of professionalism! Wow!

Awesome food, awesome service, decent prices, great, cheerful staff. This place is a great sushi joint for a date or a friendly gathering of good friends. Nothing beats good food, exceptional service, and good company. Service is always fast, and food always tastes great and looks awesome. I love the way the chef plates the food and incorporates his creativity to each and every plate. I go here with my good friends at least once or twice a month.

I know who would I think to eat Italian while in New Orleans! This place is well hidden on Royal Street but well worth it. Obviously only the tourists who know and the locals go in. The food was fantastic not only filling but tasted great!

At first site you go hmmm..... when you walk in makes you do a double hmmmm... the menu is posted on the wall. They have a " wall of fame " of sticky notes from Customers that have left their comments. So you start reading them and go well, everyone is leaving positive comments. We watched a Customer receive her food who graciously let us peek at it. We were sold and ordered the same thing. 

We smashed!! My daughter discovered this place. It is delicious.  We're heading out tomorrow on our cruise but will return before we leave the Tampa area for sure!!

I had never been to this chain before and within a few months I had been 4 or 5 times. The first few trips were great - both were dine in visits with friends. I was impressed by the quality of the food and the options. I was particularly obsessed with their brunch burger which had and egg and tater tots on it. After a few dine in visits I placed an order online for pick up. When I arrived, there were no pick up spaces open so I parked close. I checked in and said I arrived via the check in online. Minutes passed and a spot opened so I pulled up. Again, I sat. 15 minutes since arrival and I checked in again online. 5 more minutes and I went inside. I went to the pick up area and they said "We are behind and didn't know you were here." I showed them the online check in and they said "the system has problems." A few minutes later I had a burger and a gift card for free fries with my next purchase. I grabbed some of the fries to snack on in the car - cold. I got home (just a few minutes away from the location) and the burger was cold. Warmed it up in the microwave but not a great experience. Maybe it was a fluke so I'll give it another shot. Went inside another day and placed an order to go. Burger and fries to go. Order was ready in a reasonable time. Again, dug into my fries on the way home and cold. I dug into the burger and it was kinda warm. No more chances after that - even for dine in.

Servicio excelente comida riquísima las micheladas mas o menos podrían estar mejor pero la comida y el
Servicio excelente recomiendo este lugar 100%

Came here with a Living Social and not treated any different. That's the 1st Star. They had a party going on at the same time and I don't feel our group of 4 or anyone else suffered. The service was very good. 
Red gravy- excellent & zesty. 
Crab cakes were crabalicious*
Tortellini and white sauce were Devine!!
Shrimp scampi had perfect flavor. 
The flavored butter and roasted peppers were a great delicious touch. 
Didn't get 5 stars because of the music. I should've been listening to Frank Sinatra or Classic Italian, not Lady Gaga. 
We will be back.

Neat clean and bigger than it looks from the outside. Friendly staff, quick service. We've been twice and each time our food was prepared deliciously. Here's my Pad Thai look at the cute carrot bird! A nice touch!

Dear Vegetables ,
"I don't hate you, I'm just not necessarily excited about your existence!"
sincerely,
A veggie hater. 

Seriously, green vegetables and I, are so not close friends. Green. Raw. Leafy vegetable!s!! Yuck. YES, I'm not a big fan! 

I used to be very repulsive to even give it a try, and never accustomed to " that brussels sprout tasted absolutely delicious!.  "Used to" being the key word here, since I'm trying to stick with my New Year's resolution: trying new food and expanding my "food" horizon. I might be jumping on the green juicing bandwagon a bit late, but I'm stepping outside my comfort zone and for that only, its an A plus for me.

Now, that's exactly what I told the young lady behind the counter! Also, I ask her to fix me something surprising, and more of a juice rather than a smoothie.  "The evergreen is famous, she said, but I'll add some pineapple to make it sweeter and less of the kale for a milder base". I have to say, It was refreshing, and not bad at all.
How about a quick shot of wheat grass? Ummm...ok, I will try it as well. 
Holy moly! unsurprisingly it tasted so bad, even with all the benefits of it, that I was told about, I don't think I'll ever take a other shot again. Probably I'll try the lemon/ ginger one.

All of the staff were incredibly knowledgeable and friendly, the cost is on the pricey side, but I think thats how much green juices usually cost. I singed up for the Robeks rewards to try to save some bucks if I ever became a green junkie. 

Four Yelps!

We did a private cocktail/dinner party for 55 on Wednesday night and it was sensational. We worked by phone with Thea and with Eileen to figure out what we really wanted to happen and it happened exactly that way. Food was great, bar was gracious and staff made everyone feel at home and welcome. Frankly, it was like having a party at home. Oh yes, we are from New York City and were having this party in a foreign city, Philadelphia. For anyone wanting to do such a party, let me aim you at P.J. Clarke's. What nice people. Final note, we stayed absolutely in budget.

Having been in Philadelphia for a few years now I have been lucky enough to have great food all around me and a superb choice of cuisine. This venue has embarrassed me. It's been open for nearly a year and I've not been. Huge mistake. It's fantastic. From the reception staff to wait staff, chef to management everyone was professional and friendly. The drinks were delicious. Then the food arrived. My wife had the mac and cheese starter, I had sprouts. Both were gorgeous. Thank I had the fried chicken. I just thought I'd have something quick before I went out. I have to come back for more. This was by far the best fried chicken and pancakes I have ever had. I have had good chicken and waffles in Carolina, great chicken and waffles in New Orleans and pretty damned fine in Tennessee too. All of them paled into insignificance with this meal. What's more even with a few cocktails I didn't think it was expensive. We will without a doubt be back. In fact I think I may have a new go to if everything on the menu is as good as what we had.

One of my favorite spots!  Don't let the size fool you, this place is awesome!  My favorite is the Pork Bahn Mi with egg.  SOOO good!  My husband had the Phi and said it was the best he had eaten in the area.  The prices are great, the restaurant is squeaky clean and the service is fast and friendly.  Love this place for lunch and am quickly becoming a regular.

Wow. 5 star dining at 3 star prices. I had the Industry Burger...short rib/brisket blend with red onion, and cabot cheddar on a potato roll. One of the best burgers I've ever had. The ambience here was perfect...warm and friendly atmosphere. The service was impeccable. To top it off, they have a great beer menu, including my all time favorite the Paulaner Heff Weisse. Will definitely be coming back!
Chicken Biscuit was great along with the service. Nice to have a new breakfast/coffee/dinner place in the CBD. Best part is....FRESH BAGELS!

Every time I come here I stick to my Reuben. I'm not one to not venture around a menu trying new things on the menu when I'm a regular at a restaurant but when a Reuben is done it, it just works! Heads up to new patrons, food ordering is not like your type restaurant, but makes sense when you see it, they do take cards so no sweating that, and the beer selection is awesome! I recommend the Czech. Have fun and enjoy!

Okay--- this might be a lengthy review but I write this with VERY VERY mixed feelings...
I LOVE Hesslers pizza... seriously, some of the best around.. and if you've never had their pizza, you're missing out..it truly is delish! I order bacon and jalapeno, soo freaking good....
 I would give the place 5 stars based on the pizza alone, however, I am seriously HIGHLY disappointed in Hesslers...to the point that we've been coming here for two years, and now we've considered NEVER going back.
.Do you REALLY wanna lose loyal customers Hesslers???? DJ RICH was the GREATEST thing Hesslers had...Seriously...
BRING DJ RICH back!!!! If i could start a petition on Change.org to bring back DJ Rich, I would....and if anyone knows Rich, or where to find him, please let me know, bc we would like to go wherever he is the new DJ at... 
Yes, on the weekends the beer is not cheap, but we used to go for the entertainment that  DJ Rich would provide..... the new DJ seriously sucks balls... yea.. i said it.. I dont care, RIch was awesome...! So my advice to Hesslers--- BRING BACK RICH!! and lower your damn beer prices!

Birthday Celebration Gone Wrong:( 

My friends surprised me this past Saturday for my birthday by bringing me here.  One of my friends had found this place by accident awhile ago and couldn't wait to share his wonderful food experience here for my birthday. He knew how much we love Han Dynasty but we also LOVE finding great new places to eat, particularly, BYOB. 

I guess you're wondering WHY I only gave this place 1-star. I will explain by starting off with food, then service. 

FOOD: 
We started off by ordering Dan Dan Noodles, Dumplings with Chili Oil, and Scallion Pancakes (we always get this at Han Dynasty so we looked forward to comparing the two). We enjoyed every bit of it!!! In comparison to Han Dynasty, the dumplings were not as meaty and the scallion pancakes were slightly greasier but it was close to being as good as Han Dynasty (in my opinion) 4-STARS. 

I decided to order shrimp fried rice but didn't know what to order next. I say that a lot of pork dishes were on the menu so I figured "they must do pork pretty well". I requested to order to Spicy Pork Stew under Hot Pot Style and Yeng Kho-co-owner, said that the dish was like "beef tripe" but pork pieces. I thanked her for letting me know and just ordered the shrimp fried rice. We still wanted to order something else so I pulled out my Yelp app to seek suggestions from the Yelp community. I briefly saw a post about a Scallop dish. Knowing how much my friend loves Scallops, I decided to order the Scallops in Garlic Sauce/Salt and Pepper/Black Pepper. 

While were waiting for the Scallop dish, the Shrimp Fried Rice came to the table. We devoured it!!! It was the BEST Shrimp Fried Rice I've EVER had. 5-STARS. 

We couldn't wait for the Scallop Dish to come out. When it did. The 1st thing I noticed was that the dish had mushrooms. I felt so bad because the menu didn't say that mushrooms were in the dish. I apologized to my friend who replied "it's okay, I'll just eat around it". Knowing how much of a mushroom phobia she had, I was surprised to hear this. I took 1/3 piece of Scallop to check the taste. The closer it got to my nose, the more I smelled something unpleasant. I still took a bite just to see if I would like it.( i was trying to be open) It was REPULSIVE!!! The scallop didn't taste anything like a scallop. I told my friends "I can't eat this! They were shocked because I am "the daring one" in the group. My friends shared a small piece of the same scallop. I could tell they didn't like it either but I think that we all feared "sending the food back". We had 7-minute conversation about "what to say so that we didn't insult anyone" but we agreed that the food had to go back. 0-STARS

SERVICE: 
Before I continue with our food experience, I spent some time yesterday reading Yelp reviews. I am so glad that I did because I read some things that were consistent with my experience. It seems that several Yelpers mentioned that the menu doesn't list the ingredients. I TOTALLY agree!!! Several Yelpers mentioned that the service was poor. The waiter would just ask "what do you want to order?" .....The owners talked too much..... for some reason, that didn't bother us at all!! We also heard that the owners  tried to argue over dishes instead of taking feedback from the customer. That's really interesting because this "traumatic event" led me to thoroughly review the website. Quoted from the site under "Meet the Owners": 

"Gary and Yeng have hired only the best chefs, and invite you to try their food and provide feedback. After all, your satisfaction is their biggest reward.We want you to feel welcome at Pin Wei. Let us know how we can do even better!"~Gary Kuo"

Back To Our Experience.......
We told the waiter that we couldn't eat the meal. We stated that we "were not aware of the fact that the meal had mushrooms". We deeply apologized and told them that "we LOVED everything thus far and we feel bad to return the meal. We ordered more Shrimp Fried, Dumplings in Chili Oil and Scallion Pancakes. The waiter took the scallop meal and placed the order of the requested items. We sipped more wine (feeling horrible), we heard someone yell 30-seconds later, Gary, the owner came to the table, threw the scallop plate back on the table and asked what "was wrong with the dish". We explained and deeply apologized. Gary proceeded to blame us for "eating more than half of the dish" and demanded that "we pay". He continued to taunt and argue with us telling us that we had "to pay". The three of us collectively ate one scallop... clearly he was lying to make us pay. His wife, Yeng, came out with the plate of Shrimp. Gary didn't realize that we ordered more food as he was giving us the check to "get out". He was upset saying "whose gonna pay for the SFR. "Dude, you're kicking us out, we are paying for the scallops dish not the food we last ordered". Needless to say... LOVELY BIRTHDAY celebration for me:( You lost lifetime customers over a 20-dollar-meal.. SMH. 1-STAR
The pub burger is perfect. It's got everything I need. The fries are tasty. Splurge and get the cheese sauce. You've got nothing to lose.

WOWWWW!

This place is sooo good! This is better than any falafel we have ever had in New York. This is the best falafel we have had outside of Israel, so authentic and so fresh and good. 

The tahina shakes are pretty amazing. I don't think I've ever had a better milkshake. I had the Turkish Coffee and I would order it again! 

Michael Solomonov, you gave us Dizengoff in NYC, please bring us Goldie!!!

Outstanding brunch spot.  At first blush, the space itself is underwhelming, but every dish that everyone had was spot on perfect. When four different brunch entrees and a couple starters are perfect, they have my business. The outdoor tables fill up quickly so get there a little early.

This place is the best Indian in town.  The pakoras are not greasy, the lamb vindaloo is respectably spicy, and the chicken korma seemed like it came with an entire Cornish hen.  No skimping on the sauce, or the animal flesh.  Price-wise, it's the same as it competitors, but better.  They don't deliver, but GrubHub will go fetch it for you.

I love wings, and sourkraut and good burgers, but this review is about wings.
Buffalo Wild Wings located in the outlets sparks, next to BJ Brewhouse.
The parking is no problem,and the seating is huge, you should not have to wait unless a popular nfl or college game is on.
There are tv's everywhere and it is a sport bar atmosphere, but it is good for kids. A little girl next to us was celebrating her 9th birthday.
We were seated right away, and our drink orders were taken right away.
We ordered 15 mild wings to split between us. The wings were cooked just right, not overcooked and chewy. These were moist and tasty, and were fairly good size wings.
My only negative is the cost, the wings are not cheap. On Tuesdays, they offer a reduced price on wings. I will definitely be back.

Poor service. Never got any refills. Food is mediocre. Got the wrong food last time and almost this time as well. Server Joel is unaware of his surroundings with people calling and waving. Burgers are only cooked to well done

Oh SB.  How I miss you soooooo much.  And I miss you too Natural Cafe.  With your good sized menu full of healthy food at affordable prices.  And your pretty little purple tortilla chips.  And your water coolers with lemon wedges.  And your nice patio. I miss you.

1. At checkin the gentleman took out phone number and said they would call us once the table is ready in 45 mins.
