2. After 45 mins and no call, we went back to the restaurant and found plenty of empty tables and were seated right away. But the restaurant greeter was still telling people that it will be a 25-30 min wait..maybe they had people coming in for reservations...maybe they didn't..(-2).

3. Servers were great (the captain and a young lady) (+2).

4. Appetizers (Truffled crab and Crepe du jour) were great. And so were the drinks. (+2).

5. Entrees: Burger was eh..Gulf Fish was very good. (+1).

6. Total bill for two (with a couple of rounds of drinks ~90.

Good place and considering the area is mainly tourists, the restaurant didn't seem too touristy. We will go back.

Last night was my boyfriend and I first time here. Great selection of beers, amazing food and friendly service. Buffalo shrimp were AMAZING! Our server was attentive and personable. Can't wait to come back

Only problem I have is now my wife doesn't want to cook anymore.  She just wants to go here every night.   
Really, we've been several times and love it.  The people are great.  The owner and manager go out of there way to meet and greet you.   We find that a rare thing in this area.   The food is outstanding.  Lots of original meals and always very good but just stay out of my way when I'm eating their pulled pork Nachos and don't dare ask to taste one!!!   Best flavored and ingredients I have ever had in Nachos and they are layered with cheese which is critical to great Nachos.    The salads are amazing.  The portion of steak and or salmon you can get is like a meal in itself.  
Really do like the place.and oh, they have the best iced tea I have ever had.

absolutely horrible food 

they have no idea how to cook a kabab nowadays !!!!!! 

terrible experience!!!!!

We Dined at RumFish today during our Travels. It was absolutely delicious !!!!!
Every single thing we had was wonderful. 
The waitstaff was great too. 
There was the most beautiful Aquarium from floor to ceiling as well.
Loved the Gift Shoppe & we bough a bunch of things.

Great place with an awesome home atmosphere. I got the CBB and my wife got the half. It was cheesy and delicious and the heat was on point. Would recommend highly for breakfast and I'm hoping to try it for lunch on a return visit.

We've been here multiple times while visiting Philly, and had the same experience. You walk into a loud, crowded pub scene. The seating is slow, the service is slow, and it is so loud you can't hear yourself think. it is enough to make us want to leave before our food arrives, every. single. time.

Then the bring the food.

Everything my boyfriend and I have had here is simply amazing enough to totally outweigh any other annoyance and keep us coming back. We've had the Irish classics, sandwiches, entrees, and specials. Each was a great experience. 

If you can take that it is a bar seemingly suited for the young 20s' crowd, you'll be rewarded with some delicious nosh.

Service was good and helpful. We had the chicken empanadas and Pico rojo sandwich. The empanadas were ok And so was the sandwich, but I felt the sandwich could've used some work. Buy the food was tasty. They have free WiFi and a Latino music playlist.but no TVs.the decor was simple too.  I've had better empanadas for cheaper price. But overall this place is worth trying again.

Billing is a terrible experience. Do not come here with a party. They use an Apple II E to run their POS system, so bring cash or be prepared to split the tab awkwardly. Trying to figure this strange system out caused our server to throw a fit and take a shot back in the kitchen like the sky was falling. After that she came she got an attitude with the us, and let us know we were lucky to get the service we received. The food was bland to okay (out of 10 different meals). The drinks were overpriced. Definitely not worth the episode we had to go through to get it. This place went out of its way to demand you to treat it like a 5 star restaurant, when really it's more of a pretentious dive. I'll never return. Avoid this place.

The food is typically really good, and the wings are some of the best in the area. However, the service is painfully bad. One time I went late at night when there was barely anyone there, and it took literally 10 minutes for anyone to even notice we were there to seat us. Then, once we're at the table, the server rarely ever comes out. They also "forget" to apply discounts when they're having specials. It really seems like the people who work there hate their jobs. It's also a bit overpriced, but nothing too ridiculous.

The outside is no indication of the bright and inviting decor inside. We arrived for the dinner buffet, shortly before 730pm on a Saturday evening, and the buffet was full and hot. The staff were very cheerful and friendly and the food was tasty and plentiful.  Dinner Buffet was $19.99 and includes 20+ hot dishes, salad bar, soup and dessert. (No ice cream)
Service was great.  Food items were limited because of covid.  Drink specials were good.

I usually love this place , but twice now , a friend and I happened to get there 10 minutes BEFORE their scheduled closing time of 3pm, we were very disappointed by their customer service and general attitude towards the "late" arrivals. They made it obvious that they did not want to serve us and started closing down a section.
My point it that- if you say u are open till 3pm, that means you serve UNTIL 3 pm. You treat ALL your customers the SAME regardless of how close they arrive to closing time as long as it is before that time.

Do not recommend this place at all. I came with my son hoping that the bad reviews were taken care of by the owners. I ended up spending $11 including valet parking and a glass of ice tea and didn't even get to sit down. Let me explain what happened. We checked in at 5 PM and we were told it would be "about 15 minutes". He suggested the bar so I ordered the ice tea. In the waiting area I noticed at least 4 other groups of 2 people each and a group of 4 people. After waiting 20 minutes I was beginning to wonder what's next as none of the smaller  groups were seated.  I moved over to another seat where I can see the dining area. There were clearly many open tables and very few servers. It just doesn't look like a  bustling churuscaria and I have been to many of them (Fogo de Chao, Texas de Brazil, Bacana, etc.). I also noticed uneasiness on some of the other waiting groups. To spare ourselves more pain we walked out and went to eat Italian instead. I cannot remember the last time I ever walked out of a restaurant and I cannot remember ever not being seated immediately at a churuscaria. Go at your own risk people!!

Ordered delivery from them and it was ready in less than 15 minutes. I ordered a mild mie tek tek and it was just spicy enough:) I also asked to have rice noodles and they did it for no charge! The free little fried pork skins are super good too.

We visited on a busy Friday night. Loved that they took our # & texted when our table was ready! Super easy and efficient. The chips and salsa were amazing. The chipotle was very flavorful so the verde was a refreshing counter balance. I was a little disappointed that the shrimp was fried, but overall, the tacos were delish. I liked that they brought the tacos family style and it was a fun and vibrant atmosphere!

Used to be one of my favorites and go tos. The food is outstanding, the beer is amazing, the staff is USUALLY superb. Key word usually. The 1 out of 5 times is enough to kill it. My bf and I used to bring all our friends from out of town to show them a true taste of south Philly, until we had the worst service I've seen in awhile (I've worked as a server for almost 10 yrs and I'm extremely sympathetic to fellos servers), but this was just tragic. I can handle incompetent or slow but this was just downright rude as well. I watched our drinks hang out at the bar for over 10 minute and it wasn't even close to busy. When my bf finally complained he spoke to the manager and she seemed polite and receptive until my bf walked away and then she openly rolled her eyes to her staff- here's a valuable tip...of you're going to do that at least have the professionalism to do it behind the kitchen doors or not in front of customers let alone loyal regulars.

I waited and returned a second time with a small group to give this place (as it was previously my all-time favorite) another chance for Sunday brunch because they were featuring Ommegang brewery (one of my favorites). We were lucky enough to get one of our favorite servers, who is truly outstanding. Unfortunately, it took awhile to be seated although it wasn't very crowded and then we were told we couldn't order food for 30 minutes once sat. I understand being understaffed but for a kitchen to be that far behind on such a largely advertised event on Sunday brunch  where half the tables were empty is just ridiculous. The food was well done as usual; however, they really need to get their staffing or management issues under control. Two strikes, a third and I'll have to stay away for good unfortunately. There is just too strong of competition in south philly to deal with such inconsistency, I sincerely hope they get it together because I really want to be able to brag about this place again.

First time we decided to change our regular restaurant.
Our waitress was friendly but messed up....our order was forgotten as we saw other tables receiving their food before ours, even though they were seated later than us. When our food finally arrived my dish was not what I ordered at which time I proceeded to cancel it, my son's lasagna tasted like Chef's Boyardee canned creations, and my wife's Margarita pizza was just blunt with a heavy taste of basil. 80 some dollars later I was offered one dessert plate to compensate for our ordeal, which I kindly refused as I had already made up my mind for my experience. One star for being so close to our home and confirming the quality of our regular spot.

The place was packed on a Sunday morning, which was to be expected.  Once we sat, service was quick as was the food. We had the green toast and Apple pie French toast and both were great!  We'll definitely be back!

Yum!  I can't say I'm a Vietnamese food expert, but I can say that Chao Vietnamese Street Food is worth a visit!

I would have never even have noticed it in the strip mall if it wasn't specifically recommended to me, and I'm so glad it was!  The place was clean and the staff was friendly and informative about the menu.  I got the Grilled Pork Bún, which originally I was thinking was going to be like a Chinese bun.  Not at all! It was a noodle, veggie, pork bowl of deliciousness!  For the amount of food you get, I think the price is very fair.

I can't wait to go back and try other items from the menu or get it delivered.  I've got my eye on the bubble waffles!

Being right down the corner from my house, it's VERY convenient. But even if I had to go from the other side of town I'd still frequent this place. The doughnuts(and fried pies!!) are that good. Only con is they only take cash =(

This place is my go to when I just don't know what to eat. Great wings, cold beer, always a friendly crowd. Bartenders are always awesome, always great service, even during saints games. Recent improvements are making it even better! Keep up the good work!

Chips were stale, my chicken in the Chile relleno was watery. The pico was only tomatoes and I took one bite and had to spit them out because they were rotten. The salsa was bad. Service wasn't terrible.

I had our drive to wine country mapped out with yelp places pre-determined along the way. This was one I wrote down, and since the 101 fwy had stopped completely we exited for lunch.

Long line made me think WOW this is going to be great. Don't get me wrong, it wasn't horrible, but I think it was way over-hyped (not by you Greg T, I had read other reviews too). 

Hubby ordered the fish & chips, having read "they really know how to do it right here" he was pretty excited. I had a sammich. That plus 2 beers came to $28. Ok, so I imagined it was really, really going to be good!

The husband got the 2 piece fish plate, I think it was about $9. The fish was the size of 2 fish sticks, (no joke). Those 2 pieces were gone in 60 seconds. It's a good thing I am a giving wife, because I had to give him half my sammy (the pouty puss he was making was killing me). 

I had the Loon sammich or something like that. Wheat bread, turkey, ortega chili. It was nice. It was a sammich that was nice. It was not a $8 dollar sammich though. I'm not a cheapo, but I do think what we got and what we paid for it was way misaligned. (Oh, add in the long line and the slightly put off cash register girl).

Unique pizzas. 
Local/regional beer.
Hip waiters/waitresses.
Nice part of downtown (Mass Ave).
Patio.

Great experience here.  I came here with some of my coworkers on a perfect patio-sitting night.  I enjoyed sitting outside on the patio, but it was really cramped.  It consisted of tables packed into the little fenced in area in front of the restaurant.  But after spending a long day in the office, I was thankful for whatever we could find.  

They won't seat you until your whole party is present, which was kind of annoying.  But I guess it can get really crowded there. 

Our waiter was really nice and gave us some recommendations for various pizzas and local beer.  After the meal, he also gave us directions to a great froyo place nearby!  

I have to be in the mood for pizza, and even then, I don't always want to eat all the cheese that is normally piled on. Sometimes I order pizza without cheese and I only ever receive funny looks for this oddity.  Well...problem solved! They actually have a pizza on their menu that is made without cheese.  Oh good god - how fantastic! The crust was perfect - not to thin & not too thick.  There was a lot of sauce, almost too much, but it was yummy and I just scraped some off.  Topped with delicious, fresh roasted veggies, I was sold.  

Being someone who doesn't really like meat or cheese, I normally end up picking off most things on top of pizza when I order with someone else.  For this reason, I really liked that each person could order an individual-sized pizza.  The smallest size was more than enough.  It wasn't one of those lame ass "personal pan" pizzas from Pizza Hut that mostly consists of overgrown crust that can be devoured in two bites.

Love this place. Their coffee is fresh. I had the crisp apple pancakes and they were amazing. Its like a very flat pancake, infused and topped with baked apples. This place lost one star because the owner was a jerk after we were waiting for a long time to get a table. Our waiter was nice though.
I love this pizza place so much, highly recommended to go again. The pizza is top notch, better than franchise pizza. I love local pizza places a lot, but this one is the best.

The perfect coffee shop. I have been here a bunch of times and the coffee and pastries are always perfect. The baristas are very nice. If you want to sit and do work (like me), you can't find a better place in the area!

Went here during a weeknight. They weren't too busy for the time of day. Service was great as my water was always being refilled. We had the chicken pad thai and a seafood soup. Both were very good. We will be going back and eating here again.

Came for lunch on a Friday with my girlfriend. I ordered the turkey club and she had the burger, deviled eggs as an app and hot cider chai as a drink. The cider was not as hot as it should have been. The burger and deviled eggs were awesome. The turkey club could have been better.

Still to date no responses from either the restaurant manager or corporate.  I guess they really don't care about customer satisfaction.  What a shame.  They always get too big to care about the people who make it able to be in business. Oh well , I'm just one person, RIGHT???

Great food, great service! Will be going back for sure!! The lobster grilled cheese was excellent! Good cheese and it didn't over power the lobster flavor! The power bowl was also yummy and tasted great as well!!
Pazookies are worth the extra time on the treadmill. Usually not a long wait and great menu. Will return.

The food was excellent! I got the fig & bacon pizza, and it was so good! The atmosphere is cozy and perfect for a fall day, and there's something on the menu for everyone. My only complaint is we went at a slow time and it was freeeezing & our server didn't come over very often even though we were one of two tables. Everything else was awesome though and I would highly recommend!

Great great food! Mac and cheese was okay, spicy chicken wings was amazing!!! The delivery was fast and everything came in hot! We ordered the fried Oreos and Reese just to try them and it was worth the try but it wasn't good at all, too much dough and very grease.

I loved the fried shrimp and catfish. It was very lightly fried and seemed to melt in my mouth. The portion was very ample. Mandinas had the atmosphere of a neighborhood favorite! it seemed like a very popular spot in the mid-city part of New Orleans. it was very casual and very good, with great service. We were able to catch the trolley about a block away & take a short ride back to French Quarter to our hotel.
Mandinas was recommended by a friend who grew up in New Orleans.

We tried this place for the first time and I have lobster ravioli with pink sauce. The sauce had a nice kick to it in the lobster tasted fresh. My husband had the veal it tasted frozen but the vegetable side it was very tasty.

Get fresh with me!

Lochel's is a family owned bakery that has been around for years, they also have a cafe right across the street.

We happened to stop by on the day they had just reopened after being closed for awhile, after the holidays. To that, I would assume freshly baked goods, which one would expect on a daily basis, but especially on a day after they had been closed for awhile.

They do have a lot to choose from, cupcakes galore, cookies, candies, cakes, pies, Danish and much more. I'll admit that I don't have much of a sweet tooth, but hubs sure does enjoy it and he was pleased. I, on the other hand thought the Danish was chintzy on the fillings and even though buttery pastry, it was just too dry for me. 

The carrot cake was okay, but once again, way too dry and too much ginger? We ordered sticky buns with walnuts and raisins ( for me ) and some without, for Michael. They were loaded with cinnamon and okay, Fritz's are better, but even Fritz's does not compare to the bakery back home that I grew up with.

Next time I am in Hatboro, I may check out some of their cupcakes, but I do believe I will pass on what I have tried thus far. They're just okay.

Although they do not stand out in the realm of Dim Sum, its still very enjoyable =). 

While located in the same plaza as Ho Ho Choy; Chopstix is much cleaner, friendlier, less chaos, nicely decorated, and offers a variety of HK style cuisine. I especially adore coming here due to the cleanliness and the friendly staff. The price is as the same many Chinese restaurants/Dim Sum but they they do have a lot of "Specials". 

X.O Seafood Fried Rice: I don't normally order fried rice when going out just because its one of the easiest dish to make at home but the technique and ingredients put into this is perfect! You'll definitely be licking your lips for more.

A-OK! because as a whole, it really is just an A-OK Chinese restaurant.
The service was great! The food was good. The restaurant was filled with tourists on this Sunday afternoon.

Great beers, and to-go options! 

This is our first stop on a trip to Santa Barbara. We wanted to bring some good beers back to our rental on our first night and found this place with great marks on Yelp. This place looks like fun and has a great outdoor space with plenty of room.  I think the one early knock on this place, in a hip downtown Santa Barbara area, is that it closes at 9 PM, which seems pretty early. 

We went with the homemade Hef and blonde ale and we were not disappointed, solid 4 to 5 beer choices. They came with fun Crowlers, 32 ounce plastic to go containers with their logo sticker it on.  We wanted to get a larger growler but they don't do growlers to go, and that seems like a common Santa Barbara thing.  I would recommend this place and their to-go beers as a fun alternative if you can't sit down and grab a flight!

Fish tacos are outstanding!!!!!  Sangria was perfect!!!!   Can't complain about one thing was great!!   Sat right away, servers were awesome and food was great!   Clam chowder soup was also outstanding!!

One of the best sushi places in town! Always great service and great food! The rolls are always full never skimpy! The staff is friendly and I am always greeted the second I walk in! My kids love it too! And I think it's awesome they have a sign that says they support breastfeeding!

Good stuff!  
Its a lil place with friendly people. Family owned and operated. Fresh ingredients and prepared with care!

We dined here about a year ago and had a fabulous meal!  We enjoyed ourselves so much that we decided to return when in the area last night.  Unfortunately, aside from the appetizer, all three entrees we ordered left a lot to be desired. Our server was not attentive and could have potentially saved our meal had she stopped to ask how it was.  None of us ate even half of the entree we had each ordered.  I think we will go elsewhere next year.
my parents went in to get a drink from the bar and the bartender was so rude to my dad and the waiter ran into my mom. he look at her so rudely like she had done something wrong.

I hate to give this place a bad review but plain and simple...get your customer service together!  We have been here a few times and the sushi is actually pretty good, but after our experience last night I am just really disappointed and I'm not sure if I will return. 

My two star rating is because their sushi is actually not bad at all. They do 50% off nights on Tuesday and Wednesdays making it a pretty good priced meal. That is the only good thing about this restaurant. 

My disappointment is the fact that after we were done with our dinner we paid, left our tip and our waitress thought it wasn't enough, so she asked us to change it!  Really!? Who does that?  Not only was that extremely unprofessional but it was very embarrassing. It was the first time EVER that we have been asked to do this.

Not to mention that during most of our dinner we kept swatting away some sort of fly that kept flying around our food. 

So with all of that sadly I am now in search of a good sushi place as I don't think I'll be returning  here anymore.
Delicious... made our second visit and we just love it. The gyro meat and Tzatziki sauce are to die for. Service was great, kind and friendly.
My old review was for a different location. My apologies. Probably a nice establishment

Overall my experience was good. My issue is that the lady working today wasn't wearing her mask during a pandemic, while I was in the store. The guy who made my sandwich was great. Very friendly. Had his mask on. The lady just walked over with her mask around her chin. Finally just as I was about to leave, she pulled up her mask as she started to make a sandwich. Seems like a bad practice. I know workers don't give a shit, but this kind of thing is unacceptable when 400,000 people have died from the virus.

Someone knew what they were doing when they set out to decorate the trendy Edgehill Cafe. (arm chairs covered in burlap coffee sacks, farm tables, local concert bills) Industry folk meet and pitch their latest ideas. Decent parking options. Coffee is fantastic. Only complaint, they are seriously understaffed so brace to encounter disgruntled baristas.

When we first arrived we weren't sure what to expect because it was 4:45 and there was a line outside waiting for them to open. It was crowded inside when we finally got in, and we though the food was good. I had the lasagna and my coworkers had the shrimp pappardelle. I would go again.

We stopped in here on the morning of our 5th day in Nashville and needed something light. 

I ordered a turkey panini which came with fresh mozzarella cheese, garlic aioli and avocado. It was delicious but not really a panini. The bread it was on was delicious yet kind of like a pita and it didn't hold the sandwich in tact very well, it was almost too thin. 

My girlfriend's stomach was not doing too well so she just had eggs and toast. 

Total meal with drinks was $20, no extra charge for avocado. Great price, friendly waitress and a nice laid back vibe. It looks like it gets pretty busy so there can be a wait. Food also took about 25 minutes to come out, luckily we were in no rush.

I couldn't believe it but this place is an absolute hidden gem. I've been trying to get my pho cravings fixed and Golden Flower seemed to have changed the way their pho taste, then I found this place and it was incredible. The restaurant is clean and tidy. The people working are friendly and served us well. But I'm here to talk about the food. It was, how do I say, simply wonderful. The way the pho smelled made your mouth water. The soup, without all the hoisen sauce or schiracha, was really really good. Beat all the other pho places I've been in in Reno. The meats were tender and the vegetables tasted fresh. I really have no complaints. I think I found a serious relationship with this pho restaurant.

1200 chophouse is the ultimate steakhouse on SPB! I had the ribeye with Gorgonzola cream and it was to DIE for! So delicious! My dad also had the ribeye and mom had the bacon wrapped scallops. Everything was SO GOOD! The dinner rolls and salad are also delicious!! Virgil was our server and he was great.

I wanted to give this place another chance after talking with a couple people who said I must have gotten a bad batch. We went ahead and got a couple Growlers to split amongst us all. I was much happier with the beers I had the 2nd time around. I still feel that they have a lot of room to grow but their business strategy and brewing concepts are spot on. I think that this brewery will turn into something really special over the next couple years. I look forward to watching and tasting their progress!

Food was average. The person answering the phone and waiting on us was lifeless and acted like he didn't want us there. Toilet was flooding all over the floor so we had to step in that to use the bathroom. They remedied that by placing four air wick deodorizes to reduce the smell. There was so much dust on the lighting fixtures over our food. 
We go for Indian food in Media and the servers are friendly and the food is much better.

5/5 starts on all fronts. We went on a Saturday night and had a wonderful time. First, I'll start with the service. Everyone from the hostess, to the food runner, to our server was absolutely amazing. After having horrific service the night prior at a Mexican restaurant in West, we could not stop raving about how truly kind and sweet every person on the wait staff was. I would go back for the service alone. 

In terms of food, everything was delicious, whimsical, and tasty. We got the cheesesteak bao buns (SO good), chicken wontons in chili oil, soup dumplings, and tomatillo pork ribs. Everything was extremely tasty and came out at the perfect times. We each got their signature spin on a negroni and it was a hefty sized, delicious rendition. 

100% will be returning, thanks to waitstaff for making this a truly memorable evening.

Worst service from a BWW! Took more than an hour to get my food to go, not busy at all and on a weekday before noon! They don't care here at all, it's annoying and just purely unprofessional.... I'm standing in line doing this survey actually, ridiculous

Not our greatest experience, service was so-so and no one seemed to be in a rush to help us once we were seated.  We ordered, had a decent meal and when the check came, my wife noticed that her drinks were much more than what was on the menu.  She asked the server about it and his response was, "Sorry, that must have been one of our old menus."  While that may be the case, you offer some sort of compensation for your blunder.  Instead, it felt like we got a big middle finger.  We like this place because it's local and has pretty decent food.  It's amazing what one experience can do to change that.  

Get your menus up to date, know when to right a wrong, and make a little extra effort for those who want to support your establishment.

Disappointed, won't be back for a while.

This food truck came to my neighborhood and we decided to order a couple pizzas to make tonight easier.  Holy cow for food truck pizza it was amazing. It's probably one of the best pizzas I've ever had and my kids absolutely loved it and it was the first time I watched him eat crust.  I will definitely be ordering again when they return to the community.

I called ahead and was told they don't do reservations, it is first come first served.  We checked in at 5:20p and were told it would be a 30min wait.  Instead of 30min, the wait was 1hr 10min.

They were out of steak, so instead of a ribeye or new york strip which would have been my 2nd choice, I got the tri tip.  It was seasoned well but was kind of tough.

The chicken fried steak was good.

The fish and chips were good but we waited 5 minutes after service to have an opportunity to ask for ketchup.

No dishes were cleared from the table until dessert arrived, so the table was cluttered.

There were no drink refills.

I live nearby, so I'm in here often enough to enjoy a quick and tasty soup or snack. But I need to complain about the bathrooms. They really seem like an afterthought for the employees, and each time I'm in there, I tell myself Provence would really live up to the quaint yet refined image they seem to be going for if they spruced up their bathrooms a little. But a recent experience was something else: I was in at lunchtime yesterday, and the hand soap dispenser was empty. But wait: a soap refill pack was left on the sink, where I was apparently supposed to...what? Puncture it to get soap? I don't even want to speculate about what this might mean for the state of handwashing among employees....
Still new to this place, but so far I've liked what I had. The service was exceptional they made sure I liked what I bought before I left.

Looks like a convenience store but their bagels are from NYC and most of their sauces are made fresh. All meals are made fresh to order. Matador burger, Shorty burger and fries are all fresh and delicious! Nicest staff I've encountered in years. Mark was awesome and super helpful.

I went back a couple of weeks ago. I want to withdraw some of my previous statements. The soup dumplings were still the best of the bunch, but still so much less awesome and delicious than those on offer in Queens. 

The cucumber salad, though, has become BLEH! We were served a plate of poorly chopped, overly "soy-ed", and completely lacking in cilantro cukes. I even had a picture on my phone to show the server what used to be - what I raved about in my previous review. No response, no nothing. The care that a restaurant takes in preparation of its simple fare (like the cucumber salad) to me belies the care taken in general. Sakura has become sloppy.
12-12-2020: food was still great, but service still remains an elusive commodity. Our server just seemed all over the place and never makes the time to concentrate on completing 1 task.

If you're looking to take a break from New Orleans traditional food, this restaurant probably offers the best choices. Everything we had here was delicious. I highly recommend the seared scallops. Out of this world.

The Lark is THE HOT Spot in Santa Barbara that everyone is talking about these days.  I had heard so much good about this place I was eager to try it out.  And unfortunately came away feeling let down and not sure what ALL the fuss is about.  The Lark is located in the FUNK ZONE also a very hot spot in town, but I did not have a chance to explore it as I was on my way to LA when we stopped in for dinner (with reservations, of course because otherwise I hear you WILL WAIT).  A funky, cool decor and a large Thursday night crowd.

We were seated at a two person table in a row of two person tables.  The dining room is loud and a lot of our dinner conversation was "what?" and "say again?"  And they had trebly 'funk' music (btw- I really like funk music, but it was out of place and unnecessary here) playing in the background and just added to the noise chaos.   The service was good, cheerful and prompt.  The food, served in plate sharing style, was somewhat of a let down though.

We ordered the crispy brussel sprouts--deep fried with sesame oil and dates.  They were good, but not great (see SIDECAR in San Luis Obispo for the gold standard 'great'). The dish had meejol dates which added sweetness to it.    We followed up with a very underwhelming Spring Veggie Tartine.  Perhaps I don't properly understand what this was supposed to be, it was beautiful to look at, but it was bland and tasteless--the green sauce was what exactly?-- it just added nothing to the plate.  So I quickly ordered the wedge salad which was the best thing we had that day.  Four generous portions of romaine hearts with bleu cheese, bacon and just yum.  I highly recommend that one.  Then we finished up with the heralded MARY'S ROAST CHICKEN THAT so many have Yelped about...  good, but again not great..the grits were plentiful but pasty, the roasted corn was pretty tasty (but not enough of it) and the chicken was definitely NOT the 'moistest and most tender' as other people have related.  

Our bill for that meal with the $25 corkage (we brought a very nice Costa de Oro Pinot with us) and tip was $130.   So there you have it... The Lark gets A For effort, B- for the follow through.  Jane is still my favorite in SB--along with Bouchon, Olio Limone and Ca'Dario.

Haven't been there in a while but used to love it. We went in around 3:30 today and it was awful. The seafood extravaganza was way over cooked to the point I couldn't eat the shrimp or the lobster. The fish and chips was dry. The service was terrible, the server didn't bring our drinks until I reminded him and then never brought refills. The bread which used to be served warm was cold like it just came from the fridge. It took the cashier several minutes to figure out how to check us out and then she was not friendly. We won't go back.
Very good..we tried the double decker pizza.  It won't disappoint.
Recently went to this restaurant for the first time and it was very interesting. A little expensive but the food was great and it's all about the experience.

I only come there when Tim is working. He makes it a five star experience every time. I hope he gets his Christmas bonus every year, because he works his tail off. Never has a frown on his face. High energy. It's hard to find "morning people" round these parts that are chipper and eager to please! The food Is mediocre, but I go in for Tim's pep talk. Some of the servers are really great. I like the redhead, and a younger blonde lady. I can't remember their names, but they  know exactly how I want my eggs, and they always come out right! You guys are a great team! Don't stop giving away free dumdum suckers.

Great service and fresh, delicious food! I was so happy to find a vegan friendly restaurant near our place while visiting New Orleans for the first time. Try the refreshing carrot, ginger drink on a hot day! If you have a sweet tooth, grab one of their delicious magic cookie bars. Also, their vegan crab cakes were bomb!
Excellent chicken. Sides are healthy but some a bit plain. Service has always been very friendly.

Went here to try one of the many unique burgers but then saw they had a Philly cheesesteak and decided to go with that. Best I've had, tender and full of flavor. Definitely will be back to try a burger!

Is this place good? Yes. Is it good enough to be called the best BBQ in town? Absolutely not. I have had way better BBQ on the west coast, in Memphis, in New York City, and a multitude of other places.

Once you temper your expectations, you should be ready to enjoy some good BBQ from Jack's. The people who work there are extremely friendly, which is definitely a plus. I know people will say that the paper plates and self serving add to the charm, but on a crowded night, it's just more of a pain. If you're in Nashville and forget to check out Jack's, oh well.

The service is slow. Very slow. The coffee is not at its best. The donuts are frozen and thawed. The atmosphere is dirty. Inside always smells like urine. The trash can by the pick up window is always full and gross.

AS GOOD AS IT GETS! 

So... I've been wanting to try this place for a long time. I oftentimes drive by it and it has great reviews. For the longest time, I saw the little mechanical lady outside washing clothes and thought this was a laundry mat, but it's clearly not. I also didn't know the size of the place. I made dinner reservations for 4. There are only about 12 seats in the whole place. They do have an outdoor patio area, but it was 2 degrees when i went so it didn't really work for me. 

Is this place an overwhelming 5 start-- not exactly. I would wholeheartedly give it four stars, but the way I felt inside, and the way I left, was so euphoric that I am compelled to give 5 stars because of my experience! 

Walking in-- WHOA! It's soooo small. Only one table and two bar stools and table top areas. I had no idea it was so small, but it worked. Basically this is more of a come get your food cold, take it home, and warm it up type of place. 

The ordering was confusing for me. There are food cases with their food on display that has already been made, or ready to go home with you, and then heated up. Not all food it in there, so you have to look at the chalkboard menu (super cute) as to this weeks specials. The other case has amazing looking desserts. 

This place is owned and operated by a husband and wife team. The wife makes all the desserts and runs the show and the husband cooks the food. They are both amazing people and you feel love when you walk in, when you eat, and when you leave. The love is all in the food. 

The food itself is very good. I am a big guy and like big portions, and was expecting more, but it was very flavorful and filling-- I had room for the desert (which I never do) and I am sooo glad that I did! I had the peanut butter cheesecake.

We were celebrating a birthday and the wife came out with a desert, a candle, and had the whole place sing... usually I'd be embarrassed, but this was too cute. She kept lighting the candle and having my partner blow out the candle over and over and over til there was no longer a match! We all laughed and had a great time. 


The people make this place-- it's more than food. I encourage you to try it. I can't wait to go back again.

1st time, stopped in late (10:30pm) and seated immediately. Server CHRIS was great, offered to share favorites from menu. After ordering he brought us a free small cheesecake from a catering job that came back. Hubby had the HUGE ravioli appetizer and said he could eat just the marinara with a fork because it was so thick and delicious. I had 'Our Cobb'. BEST Cobb salad I've ever eaten! Chris came by to check in and shared thoughts about the owners and story behind the name. It was obvious he loves working for them and was very complimentary about the chefs and kitchen staff. We will definitely be back and are glad to hear there is a Ballwin location.

what a delicious menu. I loved everything I ordered. I had steamed dumplings, Tom Yum seafood, and beef noodle soup. I can't wait to go back to Santa Barbara just to eat here again. service was great and inviting. come eat here!!!

This is a place that has great pizzza and great service.  However, it might not be for everyone.  I have been searching for that crisp thin crust, lots of  cheese and slightly greasy pizza since I left college.  Pizanos checks all the boxes for me and it will likely be a weekly event.  As it is right downtown parking can be a little bit of adventure if events are going on at the near by park.
This place is great.  I go there a decent amount of times.  I usually order one of two dishes, the tenderloin sandwich or the fish sandwich.  They are excellent.

This is splurging for me - I don't eat junk food. 

I had a delicious Egg Muffin - it had been years. 

Our whole big breakfast was only $14.

Good service & the restaurant itself seemed clean. 

I forgot to ask if I could buy an Avengers without purchasing a Happy Meal.

I visited on a Monday evening. The service was fast and overall friendly. I tried 3 rolls from the regular sushi menu - Philadelphia, spicy tuna, and yellow tail - but none of the specialty rolls. All were average quality, though the yellow tail was very bland and I was missing the spicy sauce that usually comes on a spicy tuna roll. 
Prices were excellent!  
I would try this place again knowing now that it's more of a fast food type place than a fancier Japanese restaurant. And I'd definitely try the specialty rolls instead.

My girlfriend recently visited this restaurant and told me I had to try it for myself so we did brunch this morning. Unfortunately we had a terrible waiter that made us feel like us being there was an inconvenience. By the end of the meal which was fantastic by the way I asked to speak to the manager. Mike (manager) came over and we told him about our experience and he was extremely polite and rectified the situation in our eyes. Will definitely visit this restaurant again as we noticed the other wait staff were very professional.

Some of the commenters saying it's quite possible the best burger are only partially right IMO. I had the single cheeseburger, and while yes it was good - I wouldn't say it was the best ever. Could definitely tell it was fresh, not a frozen puck, but mine was smashed a little too thin (making it too large for the bun). The French fries were also good, but I would like to try the seasoned fries next time.

It's definitely a great meal and fairly inexpensive as well! I will definitely be back if I can get there during open hours!

Wow. I just can't say enough about how great the food and service was at this place. My chicken tenders were wonderful, and as picky as I am about cole slaw, I nearly ate the whole bowl on my own. My mom, a native Tennessean, loved the chicken livers, too. I'll have to take her word for it because I am not a liver fan.  Our server, Aimee, was excellent, and we got to swap pet pictures with her.  Even two older ladies, fellow customers, were exceptionally friendly and wished us a safe trip back home when we met again in the cashier line.  I would recommend this place to anyone looking for great food in Nashville.

the first slice merited 4 stars, it was really hot, crust was crusty on the outside and soft on the inside, cheese was hot and melty. I enjoyed it so much and it was a nice night out so my bf and I both ordered a second slice. What a mistake. For some reason the second slices were both mediocre, esp compared to the first. It made me wonder if I was still at the same place. The crust was all soggy and wet so that I tried to pick up the slice and fold it and end just kind of sagged. What a sad sight. 

Also we sat outside where there are no napkins or condiments. I thought the server would bring that out with the pizza but he didn't. No napkins, no shakers. Maybe i'm being too fancy but they did bring the stuff out, and it was on a real plate instead of a paper plate...is it too much to ask that they grab some napkins on the way out as well?

This was my first time at this location. The workers were a little slower than normal hence the long line, but their customer service made up for it. 

I ordered 4 subs to accommodate a meeting and they did every thing possible to make me happy. 

I should've ordered a tray, but didn't realize which Subway I was going to be close to. Saved a lot of money with not ordering a tray. 

The workers gave me ample enough condiments to give to everyone with a sandwich. 

The food was great!!!

I was looking to get my Nawlin' fix in and discovered Cajun Kate's! It's a bit of a drive but definitely worth it! Delicious fried oyster po'boy and jambalaya. Now I know where to go whenever I crave Nola food. Staff is super friendly as well!

Heard about this place forever, finally got a chance to try it out. The eggs were a little bland, but everything else was crazy good. Home fries were very tasty, sausage gravy was amazing, and the prices were really fair, even though it's near offices.  The clan chowder was bland, with little to no substance. This was below Campbell's quality, and had "can" taste all over it. Biscuits were a tad dry, but some people like them like that. Grits were, well- grits. Service was what you can expect in a fast paced diner catering to truckers and execs (weird combo, huh?). It's cash only there, so bring money to avoid an atm fee. Environment was fine, but our daughter was freezing. 
I can't stress enough, those potatoes were the saving grace for an otherwise average breakfast. Firm but soft, Smokey taste, and amazing with the gravy. 3.5 out of five, bumped up due to starchy goodness.

My cousin convinced me that I should try a sushiritto, and I thought that since I was in Philly, why not take the opportunity now? I yelped restaurants and Hai Street showed up. It's a cute little place by Rittenhouse. I had no expectations of what a sushiritto would taste like, so when I ordered Slammin' Salmon, I was very impressed with the taste. It was delicious and refreshing. It's a mix of sushi and kimbap. The "Korean" gochujang and pickled vegetables with the "Japanese" salmon really tied together well. They definitely got "Asian fusion" down. They also didn't skimp out on the salmon either. Aside from ordering a specialty sushiritto, you can also customize it to your liking Chipotle-styled (selecting bowl vs buritto, brown vs white rice, protein, sauce, toppings, and crunch). It was filling and I also took up on the drinks deal and ordered hibiscus and sweet green tea, both of which were yummy and refreshing.

Heard this was a go to location in New Orleans so I made it my mission to try it.   I was greeted by a very kind hostess and seated right away ! Just beat the lunch time thankfully !  Food was really good had the fried chicken and Mac n Cheese ! Would deff go again

We had brunch here yesterday; it was fantastic, how fantastic you ask? Well great enough that we are going back again today!  We shared the mimosa for 2 (actually, I drank the whole thing,) he had a Bloody Mary, so full of veggies it was almost a salad in a glass.  The yogurt with granola and fresh fruit was perfect!  Matched with a crisp croissant (sp?) melt in your mouth.  So good we ordered a dozen and a half to take to a brunch this Saturday.  Can't wait to see there reaction!  He had an interesting sandwich that is  calling his name today....so back we go!!

This place is incredibly consistent. I have eaten there over the past four years about 50 times. Everything is good. Maybe not world- class good, but if you want a meal you can count on this is the place. Portions are generous and there is so much to choose from. Our business also orders from here quite often and it is amazing the amount and quality of food they can deliver by noon when you call them at 11.

I ordered white rice,vegetable lo main and a spring roll at 5:41pm and my order came in at 6:32pm.I find it ridiculous that I had to wait 51 mins for my small order to come in. I would maybe understand if it was a bigger order but this is just crazy! So if you are not a patient person I wouldn't order from there

The food here is without a doubt pretty good although I would definitely not say it's the best in downtown Nashville. It's definitely worth stopping in for some food. But let me tell you if you are visiting Nashville and looking for a place to catch the best musicians in town then you need to be here. Most importantly you need to stop in and either see Carl Stuart or you need to stop in and see the BB King's blues band that I believe is their house band. These guys play a catalog of music that ranges over 50 years and I'm telling you what they play it and sing it every bit as good or better than the originals. Forget going to see the usual Nashville mumbo jumbo that is in every corner and in every bar. You can't miss this

Severely under staffed. Will not survive on Broadway unless they do some major restaffing they brought in bartenders from cheesecake factory and firebirds and think they are gonna survive downtown . Great atmosphere horrible staffing thus far...

I really wanted to have a good experience but alas, it wasn't so hot.

We had lunch here a few weeks ago. It was the middle of the week around 2/2:30 and the place was empty. I was relieved because I always hear how busy it is on the weekends.

The service was fine and so is the atmosphere/decor. I love the photos on the wall. So far so good...

We ordered:
The breakfast salad (aka Salad Lyonnaise)
The flatbread white pizza (tomato, spinach, garlic & ricotta)
Coffee
Passion fruit soda
"peanut butter" cookie

The Salad Lyonnaise was good but not by any means one of the best I've had. Unfortunately the poached egg was way overcooked, leaving me with a solid egg yolk. This bums me out because if you're a lover of the lyonnaise salad, you know that breaking the yolk and mixing it into the salad is an integral part of dressing the salad. So without a yolk, there's wasn't as much flavor. They serve it rustic style, meaning bigger potatoes and bigger slabs of bacon, with huge hunks of fat on them as opposed to the more traditional cubed lardons. I'm not crazy about the huge hunks of fat they leave on the bacon although I appreciate the flavor they lend.  I tend to lean more towards the traditional cubed and crisped lardons but hey, it's still bacon, and hey, I guess that's why they call it the breakfast salad instead of Salad Lyonnaise. Anyway, long story short; it was good but not great and certainly not one of the better ones I've had in the city.

The white flat bread pizza was just...awful. Not only did it lack flavor but it was so dried out and hard as a rock. It tasted like it had sat out for hours, been heated, sat out again and the re-heated, and then served to my mother. My poor mom, I'm always excited to bring her to these places I hear great things about and she always ends up with the worst dish. Anyways, I wouldn't recommend it...at all.

The passion fruit Italian soda I had was good but I probably should have ordered black cherry since I like the flavor better.

Coffee was barely lukewarm. Our server was kind enough to heat it up for my mom. The decaf is not so great but the Sumatra had a good rich flavor.

The Cookie: When I went to pay at the register I noticed some naughty looking cookies nearby. I spotted a big old peanut butter cookie with the mashed fork impressions in it and I immediately bought one and brought it back to the table. Christ, what a dick tease. That cookie tasted nothing like a peanut butter cookie. It tasted more like a cross between a snickerdoodle and a sugar cookie. blah. I dunno...maybe it wasn't peanut buttter flavored...? If it wasn't then it should be illegal to put those crossed fork impressions in them!

I'm going to give this place a few more tries. It had to have been a fluke. But until then this cat gets 2 stars.

Yang's roast beef is different from any other I've tried in NOLA. The gravy is suspiciously similar to gravy you'd find on New Orleans "Mandarin Chicken". Its a light colored, thick gravy, thats heavily seasoned. 

The beef was moist and plentiful but personally, didn't care for the gravy.  The fries were expensive given the size and the small amount of gravy. They also use a thick (cheap) nacho cheese on the fries which I think is gross. 

The atmosphere is a bit odd. If you didnt know they serve traditional New Orleans poboys, you'd think you were in a Chinese restaurant,  from the sketchy looking counter where you order, to the random Asian decorations scattered around...


Not on my top list of places for roast beef poboys.

It's not a perfect place: the service is often painfully slow, the coffee is just okay, and sometimes the place can get sketchy after dark. That's not why I go there.

It is the only place I know of in the STL area that's open 24 hours, has free wifi, and will let you come in, get a coffee, and leave you alone. It is a *fantastic* place to get work done for that, and I've seen them named in more than one acknowledgement section of doctoral dissertations. Goodness knows I'll owe them a shout-out when my time comes.

The food's a little pricey and a little greasy, but portions are generous and the large menu has vegetarian and vegan options. (I'm addicted to the 3-cheese grilled cheese sandwich, myself, though it's a heart attack on a plate.) Decent selection of desserts and ice cream, biggest selection of gooey butter cakes I've seen (I didn't know there were variations, but they've got some good ones) and wide selections of coffee drinks and teas. The staff is friendly when they want to be. Mostly, they'll just tolerate you, but rarely have I seen anyone be flat-out rude. To be fair, they get all types in there at all hours, from rich CWE types to high schoolers to bums and everything in between, so I suspect they deal with a lot.

Well if you like bartenders who make fun of you and talk sh$t about you to other patrons. Go here. 

This was my first time here and I had been excited to check it out. I didn't know what the bar theme was just that it was this cool new place. So I joined my friends. I had heard from my friend their specialty drinks were pretty sugary, which isn't my thing. No big deal, I was digging the vibe and and since they have a FULL BAR and I saw they had Bullet bourbon - on the FRONT SHELF, and that it was nearly empty, I obviously wasn't the only person who had visited there that had ordered bourbon. I asked for an old fashion, as fall is in the air and it seemed like just the right drink to warm me up. The bartender offered their "rum" version, I kindly said I'm not really a rum drinker and say just the regular would be great. He then begins to complain that he'd have to go to back to get the ingredients, ok that's odd, so then I say "I'll just take it in the rocks then if it's easier" he then states no, no I'll do it. Ok I figured, well I offered. As I wait for my drink and watch him make it, first I noticed he never went to the back, AT ALL...but the real kicker here is.... he starts talking to the patrons NEXT TO ME about "what idiot comes into a rum bar and orders bourbon" I looked at my friend and was like "are you kidding me???" I say loudly "I can hear you" and he doesn't notice....so he continues to BASH ME thinking I can't hear him saying "why don't you just go somewhere else" and even states "it's like going into Hattie B's and asking for something other than chicken..." - news flash it's NOT at all like going to Hattie B's because they literally don't have anything else!!! You have a FULLY STOCKED BAR YOU F-ING idiot, but I'm not allowed to order what you literally have??? 

At this point I am fuming, and highly offended. Apparently he kept saying sh$t and I had walked off to find some type of management. Literally all I did was order an old fashion, THAT IS IT! ...not.one.other.word.

I found someone and calmly explained that one of their bartenders was out of control. Explained along with my friend that it needs to be addressed. Don't be a bartender if you only want to make certain drinks. So the woman was super nice of course and seemed genuinely sad this had happened. I showed her who it was, she got us shots and we stayed to finish our drinks. 

Still being pretty upset over how ridiculous this guy was, my friend realizes this isn't just any bartender, this guy who was RUDE, DISMISSIVE, MADE FUN OF ME, was none other than....wait for it...THE OWNER OF 308!!!! THE OWNER!!!! ...and a partial owner of Pearl Diver...whhhhaaattt??? Now I'm officially pissed, because I love 308 and always have a good time there. I couldn't believe it was the owner himself who was so horrible to me for just ordering a drink. Some example to set for your employees. I took a pic of him so I could show you the bartender to never order from...even more sad this guy owns businesses and he thinks this is an appropriate way to treat people. 

Look if I was rude, wasted or caused a scene, sure I could see it. But this was my first drink there, and like I said, I offered to just get it in the rocks. I'm still so offended as I had to sit there and listen to him make fun of me. Unreal. 

I just have no words.

I was recommended Booty's by my NOLA-resident friends, and it did not disappoint.  They're mixed drinks are truly inspired, such as the 'El Como Tiemblo' which had cilantro and lime - a real treat!  The tapas is inspired by culinary traditions all over the world, from Korea to Africa to South America, and they all seem delicious.  I very much enjoyed the tuna Poke and the dumplings, but my only regret is I didn't come with more friends so I could taste their small plates.

I look forward to a possible visit to New Orleans so that I can visit Booty's once more.
I love this place. The scorpion is a great drink to try. The food here is also wonderful, and the atmosphere is uplifting.
The extra-salt-laden foods was a fluke. I went back two days later to get the same thing my dad did and it was much better and I didn't worry about requiring a triple bypass after eating it. ^_^

I just got a bag of food that was wrong 
I get to my job and nothing I ordered was in the bag 
I'm Allergic to onions  
I paid $10.54
And the only thing that was correct was the ice and the ice cream....

This Change is not good:

We've been coming to Sea Critters Cafe in Pass-a-Grille for over 20 years. We probably visit a few times every week between November and May (before escaping for cooler summers in the northeast). We have always loved the staff, the 'very best margaritas' in Tampa Bay (especially at happy hour), terrific Grouper sandwiches and, of course, the lobster rolls. SeaCritters has been a great place to have good food and drink right on the water, meet up with other locals, or enjoy chatting around the bar with strangers who may be just visiting the area or just hopping off a boat to enjoy the local fare at SeaCritters. Unfortunately, things have changed. It appears that the restaurant management firm, BE-1 Concepts, purchased  Sea Critters late last spring (2019). BE-1 is the company that has many successful restaurant concepts in larger metropolitan markets like Tampa (Armature Works) and still another planned for downtown Saint Petersburg. We were hopeful they would retain some of key elements that make Sea Critters the "go to" waterside restaurant in quaint Pass-a-Grille. We flew back down to St. Pete on Sunday and headed to Sea Critters for our favorite lunch and margaritas on Monday. We were greeted by a pleasant receptionist, Dawn, who seated us on the dock as requested. On the way to the dock, got "welcome back" greetings from servers Tyler and Ken, and greeted by our very friendly server, Patrick. Our margaritas were served promptly. But, one taste and we knew something changed, and it wasn't good. Instead of the great margaritas with fresh squeezed lime juice, the new owners must have felt "their" formula was better. If a sweet bottled mix is your choice for margaritas, you'll be happy with the new "formula". We were not, and hope the new owners come to their senses and get back to offering the margaritas that made Sea Critters' margaritas the best in Tampa Bay...But, there's more. We opened the menus and we were stunned to see that the new owners have really "jacked-up" the pricing across the entire menu. The cost for margaritas alone went up about 20% and, worse yet, 50% over the prior happy hour price...really, for a sweet, bottled mix? Item by item (though some items were dropped from the pre-acquisition menu) most food item prices increased from 9 to 15%. In a low 2% CPI environment, this might, in theory be good for short-term profits, but not good for long term loyal customers looking for a reasonably priced, water front, casual dining restaurant with a great staff.
Hopefully, the numbers (customer volume, revenue/profits, etc) will inspire BE-1 Concepts to rethink "their" concept for Sea Critters, and bring back some of the elements, like the "real" Sea Critters' Margarita, that made this a great local waterfront gathering spot.

PS- Please, BE-1, I'm sure you know It costs a lot less to retain loyal
customers then it does to acquire new ones. So, bring back some of those things that kept us loyal customers coming back. You'll be more profitable in the long run if you do.

Sent from my iPad

I'm very iffy on this place. The food was very good but it bothers me how trendy they are trying to be. It's your standard too cool for school overpriced American food.

I understand you use all local ingredients but it is very pricey. First walked in at 7:30 with a reservation at 8, checked in with the hostess and said if they can seat us before 8, that would be awesome, if not, we understand. We were replied to with a snooty attitude of "well it's really busy and you're just going to have to wait" paired with a stank face. Understand you're busy and we couldn't sit early, but I was with my 8 month pregnant sister and you could have said it nicer. 

The food was very good though, everything tastes amazing. Scallops was expensive and a small portion but good! Bone marrow was only a split bone with very little actual marrow, not worth the $12. A guest in my party had the burger and loved it, so that might be the way to go here. 

This place is probably exactly what you think it would be.
It's only breakfast but they have a dynamic atmosphere and routinely surpass the competition in Clayton . Fresh and clean. I don't eat eggs or pancakes but if you do , they are great.

This place has THE best roast pork sandwiches in Philadelphia.  I have been to all of the well known places in the city that have roast pork but Chickies is by far the most flavorful. You can actually see the herbs they add to the pork and the fragrance is to die for. On a Sarcones' sesame seed roll (the best bread baked in Philly), sharp provolone, and broccoli rabe, the roast pork sandwich is pure heaven.

If you like soup, don't forget to order the soup of the day because they make it on the premises and they are ALL fabulous. So far I've tried the Italian Wedding, Chicken Orzo, Minestrone, Seafood Chowder (tons of shrimp, oysters, crab meat and scallops in that one), and the best of the best-their Split Pea Soup.

We placed an order almost 40 minutes ago online (8pm) , and after it told us it would be ready at 11:40om. We have been calling on multiple phones for the last 30 minutes to cancel the order and we can't get ahold of one person.

Disappointing and less than average. All of the food was bland and obviously recooked. Barely any chicken in the General Tso's and the  mixed vegetables were soggy and without any flavor. I'd avoid this place if you want good Chinese

So I went here for a quick bite to eat my server was horrible I had to keep searching for her just to get help them when I finally get her she takes my order disappear for another 20mins then some one ask for salt and pepper she takes it off my table when I told her I was using that she said oh I will get you another one I said no for all of that you could of gotten that table another one not take it off of mines  ummmm anyway on to the food... So I ordered the spicy bbq wing omg I was disappointed they were very big and had no flavor, I didn't like it at all but on a good note the garlic knots were delicious, and on a bad note I will never go here again....

To me Honeygrow is a good option for a quick healthy (hopefully) meal when in Philly  This locally based chain also utilizes as many local ingredients as possible which is good for the carbon footprint of what I am eating. The Honeygrow in the heart of Center City Philly is the one I use the most.  Their Walnut Street Noodle Salad is my favorite.  This consists of whole wheat noodles with arugula, roasted broccoli, roasted walnuts, and parmesan crisps topped by a walnut lemon dressing.  They have condiments you can add including Sriracha and a Hoisin sauce.  Service was friendly and though it is very popular, it's possible to get a table if you just wait a few minutes.  It would be even easier to obtain a table if they had more space and a separate area for people who are only waiting for their takeout orders and often sit down at an empty table. 
Note - you do have the option on the ordering tablet of building your own salad or stir fry by choosing all the ingredients ... but sometimes I don't feel like making any more decisions in life!

I love that a place like this is in JP! After all we are losing Lager's (hopefully only temporarily) and there's not many places where you can go that are smoke free to just hang out with friends over some drinks and food. It definitely pulls an older crowd on a Saturday night. Happy hour is a good mix. 

Pros: 
- location: great if you're in Metairie, Kenner, River Ridge area! 
- happy hour even on the weekends!
- wine on tap so your reds are perfectly chilled at the optimal temperature 
- ambiance - the owner put some work into making it look great and full of character. I also love the outdoor seating. 
- smoke free! Yay! 
- lots of free parking close by 

Cons: 
-location: coming from I10 you still gotta truck it down Williams or airport service road to get to Rivertown.
- service: they need some work here, but still new so give them time. Right now they do not seem very knowledgeable about the menu, both food and drinks. 
- food: some things are better than others and some things come out the freezer. We are a foodie town so the menu could be better.

Overall, wonderful addition to the area! Kudos to the owners for putting a place like this in Rivertown. I've really enjoyed watching this area develop.

Hotel restaurants are not what one might call memorable.  Frankly they are designed for one thing and one thing only, refreshing weary and indifferent travelers.  Eat bucks that trend.  Tucked away in the lobby of the Loews Vanderbilt Hotel, Eat makes a subtle albeit important statement.  With it's head Chef Garrett bringing creativity and ingenuity to his craft, Eat sets out to make remarkable the otherwise unremarkable.  On a recent visit I was pleasantly surprised by a few menu items that I have not seen other places.  

Before I launch into my review of these items, let me say that service was impeccable.  Hotel restaurants have a reputation for lackluster service, but that is not the case here.  My glass was never empty, and I wanted for nothing throughout the meal.  Attention to and anticipation of needs was the name of this game.

For appetizers we had Deviled Eggs and Lobster Fritters.  Deviled eggs are a brave menu item, having a tendency to get rubbery and stale.  These were delightful.  Garnished with small pieces of house cured bacon and a small vial of house made hot sauce, these were simply terrific.  The lobster fritters had amazing flavor though they were slightly overcooked.
For Dinner I had the pickle cured fried chicken.  Before you dismiss me as crazy hear me out.  This chicken was sublime.  The pickle flavor was mild but cut nicely through the fry.  This chicken I can honestly say is some of the best fried chicken I have had.
Dessert was great too.  The house made corn ice cream with toffee was incredible as was the salted caramel ice cream sandwich.

Concluding here is easy.  Give it a try, they might even pay for your parking!  (no seriously, they will pay for your parking if you eat at the restaurant)

Good was OK, service was beyond terrible

Food came out on the cool side but our sides didn't even come out utill we asked.  

Best part the milk shakes we ordered came out just before we were ready to leave in to go cups

It's cheap and the service was terrible.   Take a ride to sping hill thier service is better

Really want to give this place 5 stars because the food is fresh and perfectly seasoned.  I just can't justify spending $16.50 for lamb kabobs and $11.75 for chicken kabobs. It's not that the food wasn't tasty, it's just the idea of paying 30% more for what you can get at other establishments. To be fair, they do have a monopoly on kabobs as the next closest entity is 19 miles away.

Pass on the falafels - cold and soggy. 
Chicken tikki masala was good, but a healthier take on an otherwise decadent dish.

When I was 2 years lesser of the man I am today, I came to this establishment, drawn in by high reviews and the appeal of fresh seafood I could not find anywhere else. Of course, expectations were high given the price. But that experience blasted my ideas of good oysters out of the water - I had to come back and review this place.

Here I am, ready to take on the challenge of writing about Oyster House, the next place receiving my utmost praise. When going inside, it was busy as always. But a pro tip if you're with a small group of people: SIT AT THE OYSTER BAR. It's a nice view of how they prepare the oysters, and the vibes are immaculate.

With excellent service, especially for how busy the restaurant was, we ordered numerous smaller items alongside around 20 oysters and clams of various types.  Furthermore, we also had Fried Oysters, Grilled Octopus, New England Clam Chowder, and a true Fisherman's Stew.

I'm going to save you some time. While I write long reviews for a majority of restaurants, all you need to know is that this is a MUST TRY. Everything I had was amazingly tasteful, and was demolished within seconds. The freshness of this seafood is unparalleled from what I've seen in Philly - would love to hear if anyone has better option.

I really enjoyed my visit to Vito Provolone's.  The service (Amy) was pleasant and efficient, the food cooked perfectly, and the atmosphere was  comfortable and well suited for Italian dining.

After parking in their lot out front, I was one of the first customers and was greeted and then seated on the right side of the restaurant.  They have a partial brick wall that blocks off the view of the rest of the restaurant unless you are standing.  It also helps reduce the effect of the opening of the door when it is cold out.

After hearing about the day's wine special ($3.50 a glass), I opted for a nice Chardonnay.  I placed my order for stuffed mushrooms (lots of cheese and spinach), and Orange Roughy Florentine which comes with choice of a side salad or a cup of soup.  I chose the salad.  My server then asked if I would like the salad brought out before the mushrooms since they would take a while to prepare.  (Great move!)  I said yes and enjoyed my salad (dressing came on the side...another plus) while waiting.  And before I finished the salad, an entire loaf (8") of sliced garlic bread arrived hot from the oven.  Very tasty and hard to resist eating it all at one time.

The mushrooms (6) were covered with cheese that was melted and stretchy, but not impossible to cut or bite through.  Just about perfect!  Some were bite sized and others I simply cut in half and had no problem finishing them.  Highly recommended.

Note that my server was clearing plates whenever she passed by and kept my water glass filled as well throughout the evening.  A pro!

My entree came out and looked fantastic.  There was a bed of spinach (with roughy bits underneath) and two fillets of fish that appeared to be covered with paprika and two slices of lemon on the side.  It looked great and was cooked perfectly!  Most and flaky.  

The only problem was that there just wasn't much flavor.  Not sure what the chef was going for.  The white fish doesn't have a lot of flavor on its own and though I added the lemon and even a little bit of salt, I couldn't get much flavor out of it.  The paprika was not adding much to the flavor, so I was a bit disappointed because it looked so yummy.  There was nothing wrong with it, it was simply less flavorful than I had hoped.

I passed on dessert and was quickly processed after letting my server know I was finished.  A very nice experience for me, but I would probably go back to one of the dishes that comes with a rich sauce.

Love the oysters here! this place and drago's are my favorites

They have good croissants and that's about it. Service was the worst I have ever experienced anywhere! Chef was cursing and yelling at staff member who was late on the phone so loud that the entire restaurant heard. Then they proceeded to argue when the staff member arrived. It took thirty minutes to get my fruit bowl. My mom ordered oatmeal that on the menu claimed to be made with milk and she was served raw oats. The server said they do not cook the oatmeal. Would never go back here or recommend to anyone.

Food is exceptional. However, service is extremely slow from the moment you walk in the door. There are more people waiting for tables than sitting at tables and wait times consistently exceed 30 minutes. Even once seated, the service does not pick up and you will easily be waiting for your food for 30-40 minutes. We have given this location a few chances and this has consistently been our experience.

My co-worker and I ordered two burritos, mine was the "Express burrito" it was amazing! Stuffed to the point of almost bursting with meat (chicken in my case...this time)! It comes with the enchalada sauce on top with some cheese melted on top as well. It was amazing! Full of flavor and huge! My friend got the carne asada burrito. It looked delicious, he said it was well worth the price. Which seemed like a lot for a burritos, but the quality, amountvyou get, and the taste make it well worth it in my opinion! I will definitely be eating here again. Next time I will bring my wife and kids down and see what they think! Oh, the bar looks to be fun too!

Great burger spot! Our party of five was seated after about 20 minutes of waiting on a Sunday evening around 7. Cool atmosphere inside. We sat in the enclosed patio which was nice. 

I had a blonde ale that was on draft -- can't remember the name but it was reasonably priced and tasty. 

For my meal I had the black and blue burger but white cheddar instead of blue cheese -- it was awesome!! The burger was cooked to perfection and the toppings were good. I also liked that the burger was filling but not gigantic -- I didn't hate myself after eating the whole thing. The fries were also really good -- nice portion size and perfectly fried. I don't really like ketchup or honey mustard so I didn't try the house made sauces but everyone else raved about them. My sister had the patty melt and she loved it. 

I would recommend!

Delicious, enjoyable, 100% recommended and I give most of that rating to Anthony. He was the best most comforting and informative server I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. The food and drinks he recommended after feeling us out were so spot on and satisfying. This was our first time in New Hope and this experience made us want to legit live here! Thanks Anthony! You deserve the highest praise and pay!

I have eaten lunch here twice. The outdoor patio is pleasant and a great place to sit and watch the foot traffic on State Street. The food is just OK and the lunch menu is standard sandwiches, burgers and salads.

The floor was dirty, I had to clean the table myself, and the trash can was full...looks like management must not be around.  I have had better experiences here look tonight just was bad. The pizza was greasy the fries seemed like they were made with old oil and nobody seems to be picking up the trash on the floor or clearing off the tables.

Overall I have noticed in a lot of places that I visit that the people working there don't really bust a××.  This is no exception. Good before training, could before management, we could be that management is gone so everybody is not giving a darn.

I ordered the lamb gyro and chicken over rice.  The lamb itself is very good, however, the pita could not handle the mass amount of lamb, Tzatziki  sauce, hot sauce, lettuce, cucumber and tomato.  it collapsed almost immediately.  Great flavor but by far the messiest sandwich I ever ate.  It was a shame because the pita was very good.  I would order it again but with the pita on the side so i can assemble it myself.

Chicken over rice was very tasty, great flavor!  Rice was good too.  I think the lamb over the rice would be even better but chicken was excellent.  Good food and large portions. Gyro was $4.00  and the chicken with soda was 5 bucks.

Pros:  Had two salads and shared a pizza,  They fixed it for dairy sensitive folks.

Cons:  They won't combine tables of 2 when you have a group of 3.  We were compelled to sit at the bar.

Unfortunately I have to update my review from last year because Anthony's has new management and most likely a new chef as it is not the same place anymore.  We usually get take out from them 1-2 times a month but last time we ordered it was terrible.  My daughter and I had the chicken parm and the sauce was awful!  It had a very sour/acidic taste that was not pleasant at all.  The chicken was also over cooked and dry.  Real shame as their chicken parm was always very good and is usually a safe bet at most Italian restaurants.  My wife had the shrimp scampi and it too was not good as it lacked any flavor at all.

The real bummer was the garlic knots.  Anthony's garlic knots were always our favorite as they were always baked nicely, tender and loaded with butter, fresh garlic and herbs.  Not any more.  The knots we got were dry and lacked any garlic flavor.  Sad!

It is really disappointing what has happened to what was our favorite neighborhood Italian restaurant.  This customer since day one won't be back unless something changes.

Pleasantly surprised. As a service industry professional, I will admit - I wasn't expecting much from a little chain restaurant on my way home from work. I was starving, sat down at the bar and was engaged by the bartender, Mindy. I was not in the mood for conversation...she didn't lay on the usual corporate banter or sales pitch in specials. She was very personable and I was further surprised as I watched her take care of the other patrons ( can't help it. Once a bartender always a bartender). She was quick, attentive, and never missed a beat. I'll be back ONLY because of my experience tonight . Thank you !

Very disappointed with my most recent visit. Waited over an hour for food, constantly asked the waitress for an ETA on our food. There was a table of 8 white males across from us who said they got there 15-20 minutes before us (we talked to them multiple times as we waited) who also were waiting and the manager on duty came out apologized to them and gave them free shots. I was sitting with another person (party of 2) and we didn't even receive the same courtesy of management apologizing. Then my order was wrong and my onion rings were cold as if they had been sitting there waiting.
