Very disappointed with the service and lack of care to address our wait because if we the party ahead of us got there 15-20 minutes before us we just about waited the same amount of time to get our food because after they got theirs we definitely waited another 15 for ours. Very terrible experience

Solid food and solid prices!  This is a fantastic bakery with really nice crusty breads and amazing croissants.  I love carbs so for me, I can't get enough of this place.  Their cranberry walnut breads are my favorite.  

The place gets pretty busy because there isn't too much seating so make sure you come early because there might be a wait but it's worth it!  The prices are super reasonable which is one of th reasons I keep coming back!

I was blown away by their pizza considering I hold pretty high standards(for pizza) coming from NYC. 

Mozzarella sticks were amazing. 
Pretty noisy inside. 
Hostess was a 9/10

I love this place. I live a couple blocks away and I visit when I can. Get the nachos to share (no, seriously, they're a full meal for 2 people unless you have a black hole instead of a stomach) and a couple margaritas to unwind. They do not have a vegetarian meat option despite our constant pleas for soy chorizo, so we just have them plain. However, they do have some other veggie items on the menu that more than make up for this nacho oversight.

We even came here for New Year's Eve since we didn't feel like doing the typical kind of party. The waiter put up with our silliness and everyone made sure we had a good time.
Best dinner in fl...the food is to die for.sevice with a smile.bussy but worth the wait!!!
Sitting here smoking some fine melon blue shisha and reflecting on the savory chicken shish tawook digesting in my belly. Yum!

We had dinner, for my son's graduation at USF, as usual were not disappointed, The Hostess Seated us right at our reservation time. Maria, Our Server, was very knowledgeable
And helpful in choosing our dinners, the food was great as usual as well as the desserts, I suggest you see Tim the brewmaster, he can give you quite an education, the manager is very nice, we look forward to our next trip back I never been disappointed, I would recommend to anyone

GNO on the coldest night of the year.  Beware: there is absolutely NO protection from the elements when sitting st the bar.   We were literally shivering the whole time we were there. Mental note: either don't go in the winter or get seated in the far back of the dining room.  (Management needs to look into adding some sort of curtain or vestibule at the entry)
 

First off,  I was disappointed that a "whiskey house" was out of my favorite whiskey, Basil Hayden. I tried Rebel Yell - it's ok, but not one I have to have again. 

Secondly, the food was great (we had some shareables: Brussels sprouts, potato wedges and bread plate) but the service was a bit slow. That was surprising since you could count the number of people at the bar on one hand.   Side note: A guy next to us had THE most delicious looking steak which I must try on my next visit. He could almost cut it with his fork. 

We'll definitely go back, but probably not til spring.

This Wawa is an older location, but it still has all of the goodness of the newer places (even if it's a little cramped inside). It's also got one of the most awkward parking lots I've ever seen at a Wawa (except for the one on Belmont Ave). It's narrow and one of the three entrances is down a very steep/twisted hill.

And it sure gets poppin' at lunch time. There were people dashing everywhere. It was a little overwhelming. Otherwise, this Wawa has everything other Wawa's boast and will certainly be a place I frequent.

I ordered a custom poke bowl and added pretty much everything under the sun. Ha! The ingredients were all very fresh and the bowl was pretty. I enjoyed it, but I have to be honest and say that it wasn't my favorite poke place. I couldn't tell you why, but the sauces just lacked a certain punch of flavor that other poke places in downtown STL offer. However, if you live or work close by, I'd definitely recommend it! I wanted to try the much-hyped sweet potato fries, but I was too full after my poke bowl.
I guess REMOVE CILANTRO from Pad Thai really means "Leave Cilantro, but Remove Sauce."  I hate cilantro!  I like Noodles Pad Thai, but no longer from the Des Peres location...
The Oreo McFlurry is AMAZING and just loveeeeee how it's open late because it's so convenient after a night out.

The yelp reviews are very misleading. I got the carne asada burrito and my boyfriend got the shrimp burrito. My boyfriend had to ask for beans in the burrito because it only came with shrimp, vegetables, and rice. They were both incredibly bland and made both of our stomachs upset shortly after. Go somewhere else for Mexican food in SB.

Hot dogs typically do not fit into my diet plan, but I got convinced to come here for an office lunch one day.  I was impressed with the selection of different dogs, buns, and toppings.  
The sides were good too, and my dog came with the biggest pile of tater tots I have ever seen. 

Service was friendly and fast, and some co-workers got beers with their lunch. I think it would be a good place to stop with your kids to have a quick, cheap, unhealthy meal.
Fantastic food, straight from the heart. Dabeli, Dani puri were among my favorites. Professional staff and quick service, a must try!

Delicious pizza! We ordered the upside down jawn with pepperoni which cost $28. The pizza weighed about 4 pounds and was HUGE! 
We went around 5PM on a Saturday and there were a decent amount of people there. It is cash only. After ordering, I waited about 30-40 mins for my pizza. Well worth the weight.

A coworker and I were training in Tampa and decided to try this place. I'm so glad we did. We went for a late happy hour and dinner and we were so pleased. The place wasn't packed so we sat at the bar to relax. The regulars were so friendly and Dominique the bartender was lovely. We had tapas since they were on special do we got to try a little bit of everything. It was all amazing!

I don't know what's going on with this restaurant,  it used to be good.
Last time I ate here I said I would never go back.
They don't seem to care about  the quality of the food they are serving anymore.
When I order food to go, I don't  want my meal heated up in a microwave in a styrofoam container. 
The chips are hard as rocks.
Oh and god forbid you ask for any salsa.
They always say it's in the bag and we get home and nothing.
Come on!
 It doesn't cost much to make salsa...so tight!
I've been in there before and asked for salsa after buying 3 large meals and they tell me I have to buy it. Normally restaurants will give you salsa with your meals.
In the future if anyone experiences this, I say....take cost out of tip!
I always give them 25%+ in tips.
Rude

This is definitely my last trip.
Great service and great food. A must visit while your in the French quarter. Best biscuits hands down!

Hellas is not just a meal, it is an experience.  The food is divine every time. The atmosphere is upscale without being snobbish. 
Inside, the restaurant is lit in beautiful blue lights and a stunning decor.
After a delightful meal,  A trip next door to the bakery for coffee and homemade baked goods is a must! I always find we end up with baked goods to bring home as well.
 Over all, how was consistently cares for and about its patrons. In addition, I have been told by the wait staff that they take good care of their employees in that is important to me as a customer.
Huge plus the place is open late. The food was ok. The service was really good. Try the raw oysters! Best thing in my opinion on the menu

Last night I came here and ate dinner and it was pretty good. First you walk in and grab a menu see what you want and go up to the counter and order. Prices are pretty decent, I think they could've been a little bit cheaper for how much food you get. 

I ordered the chicken Alfredo pasta but my boyfriend ordered the catfish thinned platter and it was delicious. My food was actually pretty good! I wasn't in the mood for seafood so I just decided to be simple and try the pasta but I actually really liked it. 

The place and the restrooms weren't too clean, but on the bright side they give you FREE ice cream with your food. You go up to where you fill up your drinks and you grab a cone and make your own ice cream which is awesome! I mean honestly what's better than free ice cream? Lol

Went there on a Monday night, walked to the bar with two minority friends. Was completely ignored for first 10 minutes. Finally got drinks than bartender proceeded tohave conversations with people at the bar for another 20 minutes. Finally got the bartender attention and got my check and left immediately . Not really a mixed crowd

This place is full of the most miserable human beings. Delivery driver will give you an attitude, especially if you order off a third party App. I recently called to check on my late night order and was told "If you don't get here in 10 minutes no one will be here." Spare yourself the ungrateful workers and head to Vince's or Cafe Antonio!

We were super excited to end our week in NOLA at this iconic restaurant! We had 6:00pm reservations and arrived right on time and were greeted warmly and seated right away after a short walk through the kitchen and lovely courtyard. 

The servers and all members of the staff could not have been lovelier! Service truly was top notice throughout the meal - from coordinating the placement of our dishes, to sweeping crumbs, to refilling drinks promptly - we truly wanted for nothing. 5 stars for service!!

Now on to the food :) There we're highs and lows on EVERY plate. A little bit of a Bummer. 
We began with the gumbo which had a dark rich roux and was seafood tonight. The seafood was all cooked perfectly, but the texture of the gumbo was a bit too rich and it was hard to finish the whole bowl without something to cut the fat/richness with. We also got the bacon appetizer which was awesome and literally melted in our mouths. It was served with a lovely fresh mix of veggies that balanced the fat of the bacon. It also had some polenta or grit cake with it that was dry and inedible. We left it on the plate. Then we had the squab which was lovely yet tiny (only a half bird seemed served) with a HUGE portion of rice stuffing/dressing. The dressing was sadly pushed around on all plates, but the squab was well cooked and completely deboned. We polished it off completely but everyone left the stuffing. For dessert we opted for the signature bread pudding soufflé. Perhaps we will be shot for saying this, but it was only okay. The bottom of the soufflé had a sticky cake and then was topped with a sugary merengue. It was served with a very "boozy" sauce which we opted to keep on the side from reading other reviews and we were glad we did - it was overpowering and would have made it inedible for us. 

Overall, the service and ambiance was just lovely. There were some highs (bacon, squab) and some misses (polenta, stuffing, soufflé), but we so appreciated having had the experience. Our total bill was $150 for two people with tip.

Last Friday my wife and I went to IHOP @ midnight.  We waited 10 minutes to be greeted, and another 5 minutes to be seated.  Then we waited 15 minutes for a server who never came to our table.  We walked out.  The following Friday we saw, around 11pm, multiple police cars addressing a disturbance in the IHOP parking lot.  This place should be avoided (especially on Fridays)!

Came here sort of as a last resort option while down on Wash Ave during the late hours of the day. 

Everyone was very nice and pleasant when I went in; I sat at the bar to order to go. The bartender was sweet & helped me decide on what to get, gave some suggestions and whatnot. I went with a "popular choice" the el polo loco burrito. It came out about 5 minutes after I ordered it so I was instantly nervous. Sure enough, when I get to the car to eat, my burrito was BARELY lukewarm. Not fresh or even pretend fresh, at all. It tasted like slop. Like it had been sitting there forever before I came and ordered it. There was no flavor or texture, just soggy tortilla, soggy beans, unseasoned chicken. If I would have known that my sour cream, guac and pico would have been piled on top automatically, I would have asked for it on the side. Maybe then I could have possibly seen if the burrito had potential. 

I might come back once I can have a drink and to maybe experience some other food options.

I have never been inside this place but actually discovered it during covid through uber eats. Once I'm ready to go back to going out to eat, they will be one of the first on my list. When food is still good after delivery, you know they're doing things right. Even fried food is excellent here whereas usually when you get something fried delivered it's soggy and greasy.  Highly recommend their popcorn shrimp, crab cakes, key lime pie and the list goes on. Somehow they even make broccoli that makes my mouth water!  I've now ordered from them about a half dozen times and they have yet to disappoint. Great job you guys!  I know how difficult it is to operate in the world of COVID, I work retail, and you guys are really killing it!  Thank you!!!

Why my family loves this place: 

My grandma is hard of hearing and there's an amazing back room where our whole, large family can meet for a peaceful, Christmas meal together. It's large, so people can move around/switch seats to talk and the babies can run around without disturbing anyone. The lighting is dim and peaceful, and the service is always attentive.

You can choose menu options for everyone ahead of time (which is what my grandma always does) and then we pick between those. My favorites include the filet, salmon, mashed potatoes, chopped salad, and apple crisp.

I made my own wrap,  spinach, corn/bean, cucumber, spinach.  And mixed in balsamic on a wheat tortilla and fountain drink,  came out to like $12.29.  The place was clean and the people there were very friendly.  There soup selections were clearly labeled which I liked because I am vegan

I've heard negative reviews before from different yelpers about the long wait but my bowl came within 5-10 mins!! Honestly amazed by how cute the shop is and how good the bowls were ((: I had been craving acai bowls for the longest time and I gotta say the the Beach Bowl has been the best one i've had around the area. It was around 7ish bucks for a medium bowl with greek yogurt and strawberries/blueberries/almonds/bananas/granole/etc.!! The bowl was so so good and I would definitely go back to Carpinteria JUST for the acai bowls!! Definitely would recommend this amazing little shop on Linden Ave ((:

Oh, and the service was GREAT!

I LOVE this place! They have never gotten my order wrong, always been overly kind, and they always take the time to wave hello to my dog when I bring him through the drive through. 

Honestly I was worriedfor this place being right met to a taco bell? But it's the taco bell who needs to watch out! El pollo loco guacamole sauce is wonderful, their salsa is always fresh and it's SUCH a good deal. Their churro always makes a bad day all better.

Very sad they are closing :(. I finally just got to try it. 
Since moving to Northern Liberties I've been on a brunch spree spanning The Hinger and Green Eggs, to Cafe La Maude and Cafe Lift. I have to say Estelle's stuffed French Toast won. They had a special for Raspberry Cream Cheese Stuffed French Toast and I just cannot remember the rest of my day since I was hit so hard by the shock of first bite. I ate so much of it I am pretty sure I just passed out from food coma the rest of the day. So worth it.

GO BEFORE IT CLOSES!!!!!!!
Great donuts for affordable prices! Great spot to also just chill or catch up on work.

I swing by Le Bus anytime I need fresh rolls or a baguette.  Their bread is fresh, delicious, and well priced, especially for the area.  

I've never had to wait in any type of line so even if I'm in a rush I can swing by and have fresh bread on the dinner table.

I had a very disappointing dinner at this location this past weeekend.  The service was good but the food was sad.  I love Carrabba's and I find that it is usually synonymous with good Italian food so my dinner was that much more disappointing.  Our starter of calimari was good and came out fast.  Next came the salads (one Italian and one House) which had obviously sat around for hours if not a day or two in the kitchen fridge; the vegetables had dry edges and the entire salad was slightly wilted.  DInner came out shortly thereafter and it was nothing special.  The marsala dish I always look forward too and order was slightly oily and just didn't seem fresh at all.  Trying to salvage the meal I did what I never do, I ordered dessert.  I ordered one of the mini desserts and was sorry to find that it too had sat around in a fridge or freezer for at least a few days based on the mousse being dry and almost flavorless from freezer burn.  I will admit it was busy when we went to the restaurant but we had an early dinner before 6pm and since the restaurant opens at 4pm you would think nothing would be older than 2 or 3pm.  I worried the entire rest of the evening that I was going to get sick or at least have a stomachache from earting so much old food.  If you're not going to serve fresh food then don't serve any at all.

Great location & view of the intercoastal way on the mini boardwalk. Ordered it to-go & was delicious. We tried the pizza with pepperoni, sausage & spinach along with the house salad. The salad was made with good greens, olives, onions, thin sliced carrots, tomatoes & vinaigrette dressing. 
Since the order was to-go, they provided parmesan cheese & pepper flakes, paper plates, napkins, silverware & additional house bread with dipping oil which both were also really good. 
Since staying at the Marriot ever other place on or near the beach can be so overrated & overpriced. 
Will be back & will recommend...So glad I found & chose this little hidden gem!

Normally I would not eat on Bourbon St, but this place was new, so we decided to try it.  We had the Mambo and Rockefeller oysters and they were really tasty.  Came out hot.  The drinks were awesome.  I had the deep blue horizon and she had a mango tango.  Both really good!!  The crab cakes were great as well as the poutine.  Our waitress, Felicia, was terrific and took great care of us. O ya, try the bread pudding, seriously good.
The best selection of pizza and sandwiches you can find in the area. The service is great and food is even better.  The prices are reasonable considering what you are getting.

The Haus Coffee Shop was such a nice find. We came in search of tea this visit as it's been cold and we were all quite sick. The place was large and inviting, with comfy chairs and wifi- all you'd expect from a great coffee shop. I'm holding back on the 5th star only because I didn't get the chance to try their coffee and feel like I should try the coffee before determining if I like a coffee shop enough for 5 stars. Definitely has the potential to be the perfect spot. I don't live in the area, but if I did, I imagine I would go here frequently.
I had a croissant egg and cheese (made perfectly with provolone cheese), and a key lime cookie which was delicious. My choice of tea was the lemon sencha, which I was delighted to find was brewed with loose leaf tea and strained before serving (so it took a few minutes). My cousin got the chai latte and was also satisfied with his choice. I would definitely return- the staff was super friendly, and it seemed like a cool local business to support.

FINALLY was able to come here! I'm usually on wash ave at night so they aren't open late but we came this afternoon and I literally can't believe we didn't come sooner.

When we walked in, I was actually surprised with how small it was. The menu wasn't too long either- which is good because the best restaurants have shorter menus anyway. 

I ordered the original Palestine shawarma. I love shawarmas but they are not meant to be put on French bread so I highly recommend the original Palestine (which is made with pita) with mixed meat (chicken and beef) It tasted authentic and was so good. The sauce was great in it and it filled me up. I almost ordered a second one because it was soooo good!!

I heard the baklava is super good so when I saw it wrapped up in plastic wrap sitting in a bowl, I thought it would be nasty but I gave it a shot anyway. Turned out SOOOO GOOD I actually bought another when I was done. It was the perfect amount of sweetness. Probably the best baklava I've had in St. Louis!

Last but not least, the customer service was great too! The people were friendly and even asked how we liked the meal. Great place!

Very friendly staff in a very clean environment. The gentleman at the counter offered a sample of gumbo that was top notch. The food is hot and very fresh. I opted for the crawfish tail Po boy, and dos not regret it. I will definitely be coming back here when I am in town.

Service was great but that was about all that was above average. Food was fine, but nothing special and portions (including our wine glass pours) were pretty small. Most memorable of all? The acoustics were terrible - must be something about the way they remodeled after it changed from the old Booty's decor - it was very echo-y and to top it off the music selections were bizarre. Might need a bit more time to work out the kinks. I do hope to see the place improve + succeed.
Joe's cafe has the best donuts on the Westbank !! Joe's isn't particularly great for dinner but is for desert ! The donuts make your mouth water , especially when hot !!!

Best deep dish pizza ever!

I could not believe that this pizza is so good and cheesy. Way too much cheese than your heart is supposed to handle, yet, I still love eating here. don't come here if you're on a diet. The Heart Attack Special is my favorite deep dish pizza. It has ridiculous amounts of meat such as sausage, prosciutto, pepperoni, roast beef, etc. I love this place because I always indulge when I'm here. If you leave still hungry, you must be from another planet because I always take home left-overs.

2 dollar cans of Old Style beer which is a Chicago classic. Decent beer at a decent price.

Oh, and the freakin' wings are 25 cents on Wednesdays! Get there early and be prepared to wait about an hour or so if you have a party of four or more. Totally worth the wait though. 

BEST WINGS IN TUCSON! I'm not even kidding.

Jason's Mexican Food doesn't look like much, being located in the shell of a former Sonic (and Kenny D's). Their only seating is outdoors and it looks like standard Mexican street food. That's what I get for judging a book by its cover.

The menu is pretty straight-forward and while everything looked really good, I settled on a Sonoran hot dog and a carne asada taco. The food came up quickly, and it looked pretty awesome.

I'll admit that sitting outside is never my first choice, but the weather is nice this time of year and it worked out pretty well. I think if it were summer, I would take the food to-go.

I ate the Sonoran hot dog first, and it was one of the best I've had. The bun wasn't as chewy as some others, and the mustard and mayonnaise were in such abundance that they dripped from the bun. But the hot dog was cooked perfectly, and the bacon was just right. And the wax pepper on the side was also wrapped in bacon, like a special savory/spicy treat.

The carne asada taco was good, too. I should probably have grabbed some salsa for it from the salsa bar, but I didn't think of it. The rice and beans on the side were ok, if not anything special.

All in all, I thought Jason's was a pleasant surprise and it's nice to have good Mexican street food in this part of town. I would definitely go back for another Sonoran hot dog, and perhaps to try more of their menu.

This is a gem of a place to go in downtown Indianapolis if you are looking. For a romantic evening with your significant other! I spent the lovely night with my man who set up a reservation for just at sunset! As the sun was lowering we enjoyed a chocolate cocktail (that was to die for) and a garden salad! For dinner we had the chicken and duck! The half chicken was so good and the duck was also really good but I wish it had been more well done. The best part was the restaurant rotated in a circle so you could enjoy dinner with a full view of the city of Indianapolis. Had a lovely time and would definitely go back!

Christina H was an awesome Server and sooo very nice! Great food! Enjoyed our experience and would come back again!:)
Had the Blackened fish salad and it was wonderful! And the Big Easy Po Boy! Awesome!

I got the teriyaki wings with a side of fries.  The service was fast and courteous, as always. The wings had a nice crunch to them, and the flavor was good, but everything was so salty I ended up getting a headache. I will stick to the BBQ wings, in the future.
I love this greasy spoon.  Order what they do well - sandwiches off the grill and keep your ticket!.  Cheesesteaks.
We love Leo's!  Great food at a good price.  We've been going there for years and have gotten to know Leo and his wife really well.  Great folks who care about their guests.

This place just opened in the Voorhees Town Center. My fiancée and I were very excited to go. Here's how things went.

We were greeted immediately by the host. She let us choose where we wanted to sit. She did recommend the chef's table, so we decided to sit there. 

The inside of the restaurant is very cozy! The ceilings are really high and the fans are interesting to look at. lol. OK, enough about the decor. On to the food!

Here is what we ordered:

Crab Stuff Gougere
Seared Ahi Tuna Sashimi
NY State Duck Breast
Bananas Foster

The crab was just ok. It wasn't bad but wasn't great either. I wouldn't order it again. The seared tuna was ok also. I felt it was over priced. My duck was cooked right except I believe the skin on the duck should be crispy and it was a bit rubbery. All the flavors were developed well in that dish. The bananas foster desert was good. It is prepared table side to dazzle diners. I think the desert still needs another ingredient to add a wow factor because it seems to ( yes I'm going to say it again) simple. 

The service also seemed to drag and just to let you know I'm a very patient diner. Our waiter apologized numerous times about the wait.

Like I said this place did just open so I guess they are still working out some issues. The restaurant visually looks amazing. The food needs some work or the prices need to be adjusted. I do plan to go back because some other menu items did catch my eye. However, the decor alone will not make me a regular at this place.

Great place if you are ready to explore a new cocktail! Very small area with light snacks made from the new grocery store next door. I had the meat and cheese board and was very impressed! Not sure why they put pop-rock dust on their drinks, but who cares after a few right? I'll be coming back here. The staff was great!

Great spot for Chinese food! They offer online ordering through Eat24 and free delivery. 

First of all, my food was at my doorstep in 15 minutes, and the delivery guy showed up on a bicycle in the pouring rain.  Great service. 

They offer a bunch of entree combos for less than $10. 

Chicken with Cashew:
For $9.25 it came with pork fried rice and an egg roll. Everything showed up nice and hot with lots of sauces and utensils. Portions were huge. The chicken and cashew was really flavorful with lots of crunchy veggies (although I think they went a little overboard on the celery). 

Noodles with Bean Sauce:
I've never had this before, and I needed to hit $12 for delivery. It was basically lomein noodles with what I assumed to be a bean sauce. There were chunks of meat (prob pork?), but I didn't see any beans. And it didn't taste like beans. But, beans or no beans, it was pretty good.

This place was really good! The cuts of meat were very generous. The mashed potatoes had a baked cheese that was delicious. We also had gnocchi with an extremely tasty sauce. Overall, we really enjoyed ourselves.

My buddy and me walked in the other night everything was cool and smooth. I've gambled away most of my money and we had left to go get my debit card which I had left my car so I could pull out more cash from the ATM. We had walked in together as we had a conversation and I got through and my buddy got stopped and they asked him for his ID. Note I'm caucasian and my buddy is African American and also that they saw us walk in and out from the place. They did not want to let him in because simply they were racist old duche bags. Even tho his license was expired by a few days. One of the old duche bags didn't even look us in the eye and the other one shook and got scared once I called him out and called him a racist. They definitely could've let him in but just were racist.

Tasty "Americanized" Chinese food.  We each got a different dinner special which was plenty of food (choice of soup, entree, choice of rice, egg roll) and little scoop of ice cream at the end.  Was pleasantly surprised the hunan pork came with so many different veggies and not just only broccoli ( broccoli, zucchini, carrots, mushrooms, pea pods, water chestnuts, bell pepper)

Maybe I caught you on a bad night, Marra's, but nothing thrilled me about my experience.  That's not to say anything was particularly bad, but nothing was remarkable either.

Service was spotty and the server seemed easily confused.  The pizza here is the star with the large stunning us with it's alarming size.  For the price however, I would have been shocked if it was any smaller.  The topping combinations seemed interesting enough, however this turned out to be the type of place that relied on lots and lots of cheese (don't get me wrong, I love cheese) and not enough on well seasoned flavors.  The eggplant, parmesan, and ricotta pie was too bland for my tastes.

The dishes that my dining partners enjoyed also seemed heavily drowned in cheese.  Yes, the portions are huge, and yes, you will be taking home leftovers.  But I would rather pay the same price for a slightly smaller, though well seasoned and cared for dish.

I'm so glad I got to come back here!

The beignets here are unparalleled to any I've tried elsewhere. 

My first time here was in August 2018. 3 years later, I had a chance to come back to New Orleans and once again reunite with the beignets at Cafe du Monde. They were just as amazing as I remember!! Maybe I am just a huge fan of sugar and bread, but let's be honest. There is something they do differently here at Cafe Du Mode that makes them especially phenomenal. 

In addition, you can't go wrong with the coffee. 

The line can get crazy long on weekends, obviously. But if you have the chance to go on a weekday, you absolutely should! There are also performers on the sidewalk that you can watch while you eat, and they are amazingly talented. 

Definitely a must-visit here!

I actually give it 4.5. This place is amazing.  At least the food is.  The food is just what I want. Mild(perfectly mild), Medium(perfectly spicy inbetween mild and spicy) and spicy)(perfectly spicy, not too hot and not too mild) I have a high tolerance for spice though, just a warning.  The food is always flavorful and barring what you order, it is usually healthy to boot.  I usually get the chiken balti which comes in a flavorful red tomato sauce with green bell peppers, onions and chicken with a side of rice.  the naan is also exceptoinal.  The only reason I knocked it a .5 star is ebcaue sometimes the staff seems unhappy to work there and thats going a bit far, they're never mean but if I am going to give a restaurant a perfet rating, everything about it better be perfect.  Either way, I would recommend this place if you want something healthy and different.

This place is fantastic. I've been looking for that spicy no rules breakfast spot. This far exceeds anything I imagined. I had a late lunch and immediately returned for the breakfast! Get the Breakfast Burrito.

This place is very good if you're looking for finer "Diner" food, and I assume that's the style the owners are shooting for, so I don't think it's offensive to say so.  I've tried about half a dozen items on the menu and none are terrible, some are better than others.  Their chilli is pretty basic but darned good on a cold night.  My husband claims his wings have varied greatly depending on the night he ordered.   The prices are fine and the atmosphere is great. Friendly service and music at night.  I just realy like how laid back this place it, but it's not so laid back that you feel ripped off!

Unfortunately you have to give at least one star to leave a review. Went through the drive through, started to drive home and I got a phone call that I needed to pick up more food. Headed back to KFC and on the way I noticed that I never received the cookie that I had paid for, instead I was given the driest biscuit I've ever seen. I mentioned it at the window when I went back and they said "oh we are out of cookies so that's why we gave you the biscuit" so instead of a dessert you include the driest biscuit you can find? How is that even comparable? They offer to give me a free side for the inconvenience, I was never told about it until I had returned and asked. They gladly took my money without telling me I wasn't getting the product I was paying for. Will never go back to this place. Sad because it's close to my house and I have tried a couple times randomly over the years but never gets any better. Actually staff gets worse.

Whenever anyone asks me what my favorite restaurant in Philadelphia is I always say Talulas garden. Every time I come here I have an amazing meal. The decor, service, and especially the food is always exemplary. The way the layers of flavors are created by the chef blow my mind each time I visit. On one of my visits we were also given a free desert which is always a plus.

Great food.  Exceptional Service.  Great view of the park at Christmas.  But it's no bargain!!   I'll just try to rationalize it by convincing myself that the overhead is a killer. If you enjoy wine, see if you can get an advance copy of the wine list... you will need at least  3 days to get through it... or you could do what I did and just ask the sommelier to pair it up for you.  You will agree that they've got some terrific sleepers in there.

I hate that the best Conch Stew I've ever had is in Brandon Florida.  I hate even more that the only Conch Stew I have ever loved is in Brandon Florida.  I just don't know how many excuses I can make to visit Brandon Florida.

And here's a note to the previous reviewer who complained about the greeter . . . live a little tootsie roll . . . it's a wild world out there.  Sometimes people are in the kitchen.

For a brick oven pizza joint, it sure don't fit the bill!! Crust was non-descript/ needed more good oven time and salt!!!! Nothing was special or really good! Oven roasted veggies were either over-done, or so mushy they were not identifiable!!
And, don't even ask about the free appetizer rolls - ask about the hockey pucks!!
Went to get a fattoush salad only to be told that they don't actually have fattoush even though it's on the menu and in the name of the restaurant

A mini cannoli. $2 a piece.
A delicious mini cannoli! Definitely worth a trek if you are in the Italian Market area. 

(Note I have tasted only the minis and not the regular-sized ones, eg the Anthony's.)

The filling is creamy sweet-y smothery freshly prepared and filled. Rich and luscious.
The shell is crunchy and nutty-toasty with roomy arms to hold the cream.
The filled cannoli headed straight to my stomach before I walked the short block between Passyunk and the S 9th. Delizioso.


When I walked to the storefront at around 11:30am, the day after Christmas, the curtains and the door were closed. Almost walked away, the door suddenly opened. He quickly filled a cannoli.

Let me add that I should have gotten the tomato pie here... I spread the word here on Yelp so fellow visitors get a chance to try!

What a disappointment!  Jimmy Buffet would be appalled!  We were in Nashville for the weekend, and decided to visit Margaritaville.  We walked right in and our party of 4 was seated. That was the only positive thing about this experience.  When our server approached us, I asked for a bucket of loaded Coronas, something we always order when we visit Margaritaville.  Not once did she ask the other members of our party what they would like to drink.  She returned about 10 minutes later to ask for their drink orders.  Another 10 minutes before she returned with the bucket of Coronas.  We took a drink, and they were horrible.  When we were finally able to flag the waitress down, she insisted they were correct, and argued with me.  They were not filled with Lime tequila, and the tequila added was a very short pour.  When she finally decided to make them right, she returned with only 3 beers in the bucket, not 5.  Service was horrible, even though the restaurant was not busy.  When our check arrived, it was $85!!  For a bucket of beer and an appetizer!  I asked to speak to the manager, explained my issue, and he took the bill and walked away.  The waitress returned about 5 minutes later with a new bill that was $45, no explanation from anyone.  If this is how business is always done at this location, it would explain why it wasn't crowded.

We found this place by accident driving around the neighborhoods. We did not stop to go in though, and since then all we talked about was how cool Piccadilly looks and how we definitely need to try it. 

We finally managed to come here for dinner on raining cats and dogs kind of night. I did not anticipate a wait or the hustle and bustle coming here but place was packed and had a waiting list and reservations.  The hostess did allow us to sit outside though in the covered patio. With the rain pouring down and the twinkling lights above, the patio was amazing. I love outdoor seating. They had plenty of room and lots of tables which I was surprised. The patio is probably super busy during the cool nights when you can actually enjoy STL weather... 

The food here was delicious. The menu was short and sweet and not overwhelming at all. They have home style meals like Meatloaf, Pot Pie, Fried Chicken served with Mashed Potatoes and Green Beans. I had the Fried Chicken and it was freaken amazing. I am not a huge Fried Chicken gal but this stuff was finger liking good.
My bf had the Meatloaf and even that was mouth watering. For dessert we had the Peach Cobbler with Ice Cream.....No words can express how my taste buds felt after the first bite. 

The prices are reasonable and fair for the portions you get. I think the only thing about this place that knocks down a star is the parking. its a little cramped on the street and on busier nights you will have to park further down. No biggie really, just not as convenient. Despite that, Piccadilly is really good overall in the food department, the service, the atmosphere and  uniqueness.

Sunday Jun-2-2019

This is not the first time I ate their food ,I was disappointed because the last time I try their Pho was very good but now Their food is bland ,I am not satisfied with

a local radio station reviewed 30 cheese steak places in 30 days and this was rated #1.  My uncles always told me to go to this place because they all know I love a good cheesesteak.  I was skeptical because it looked like a old shack on the railroad tracks but after reading the #1 review I tried and boy was I blown away,  I do not eat cheesesteaks weekly like I did in the past but when I am craving a really good cheese steak, I go to Johns!! only Johns. side note there roast pork is to die for.   there is no better cheesesteak!!!
Great food, Guinness on tap great atmosphere to watch football! Would definitely come here again. Plus they support the Nebraska Cornhuskers. Great place to get a "quick 6" at the oyster bar!
such a good environment for a brunch (or a hangover brunch if you're into that). food is good, but could use some more variety. somewhat pricey but you get a good amount of food!

We just moved to Boise and have been looking for a good mexican food place. Cafe Ole is NOT this place. The decor wasn't just tacky it was gross. The tables and booths are very old and worn. Warning bell one. The waitress brought chips and salsa and refried beans. The salsa was basically tomato juice with bits of onion and cilantro in it. The chips were stale. The beans were straight out of a can. We should have left right then. We ordered our food and drinks. Margarita mix was straight out of the bottle. The food was very bland and obviously mostly prepackaged. The tortillas were so old they were hard and crunchy. My fajitas were so tastless I decided to try and spice them up with some salsa from their "salsa bar" There were 4 offered. No signs to indicate what they were or the level of heat. Two female employees were standing near so I asked them about the different salsas. Neither one of them could tell me anything. They did not have a clue about what they were. Do not, under any circumstances, dine at this restaurant.

I've only had breakfast here.  They have a standard menu and a buffet.  I have only gotten things off the buffet in the interest of time.

Not stellar, but not the worst I've had.  Decent service.  Clean, minimalist décor.

Went here for lunch, I usually judge Mexican food by how good the salsa is with the chips, let's just say it leaves a lot to be desired, and we didn't want a refill. I ordered tacos and we had fajita's at our table as well. In my honest opinion the food completely lacked spices and seasoning, I felt it was very bland and Americanized. The fajita presentation was cool, but seriously none of the meat had any seasoning.  I will not go back, the prices were high for what I thought was very average food, I would rather go to Chipolte or On the Border and I'm not a fan of chain restaurants.

Just your typical Fro-yo joint. They do have a great assortment of fresh fruit to choose from, but their selection of actual frozen yogurt was a little too eclectic for me. I had a swirl of strawberry and lychee (both tart, which I found odd that they would suggest such a combination, but still delicious nonetheless). Other flavors included coffee, toffee, chocolate and vanilla. Definitely a great place to end the night, but not worth driving around town for.

I was really torn between a 2 and 3 rating for Kitchen 519. If I could give Kitchen 519 a 2.5 I would for the atmosphere which had interesting decor and a cozy dining room feel.  Service was slow but we weren't in a rush and our waiter was friendly. 

I was excited about the food. The menu was very interesting. It had a spin on your typical choices (i.e. mussels with chorizo, calamari with hoisin sauce). We went with the spicy fish tacos for an appetizer (which took a really long time to come out). For $13, the two tacos were tasty but there was hardly any fish on them. It was disappointing because it was the most expensive appetizer they offered and actually more expensive then our actual entrees. 

I ordered the vegetable sandwich that came with spinach, roasted peppers, tomatoes, basil, mozzarella, and garlic aioli. I also ordered the garlic fries for an additional $2 (based on the rave yelp reviews about them). I'm not sure if they were having an off night but the garlic fries were a total miss. They had no flavor!  They were hard and cold by the time they got to our table. The sandwich was OK but too much aioli which made it very soggy and messy. Maybe a crunchier roll to vary the texture?

My husband ordered the smoked gouda mac and cheese with grilled chicken. It was very flavorful and rich and they served with a lot of chicken. He really enjoyed it and had it for lunch today!

One thing that really bothered me was the kids menu. They had only three choices and no prices on the menu. I should have asked but I didn't notice at first. My daughter ordered the grilled cheese which came with fries and a scoop of ice cream. When we got the bill we saw that it was $8! Her fries were horrible and I felt bad because she really wanted them. Way too expensive for grilled cheese. It cost more than my veggie sandwich! 

I'd to give Kitchen 519 a second chance but I'll be more careful of what I order and definitely skip the fries.

My childhood. Growing up and being raised in New Orleans ,when my family didn't feel like boiling up some crawfish,Michoud is the only, I repeat,the only place we would buy cooked crawfish from. Michoud will always be #1 Til the day I die.
Visited on my first trip to Reno.  Great coffee and great service.  Near the park.  Will come again soon.

DID NOT EAT HERE!!! HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE!!!

Went on Thursday 07/31/14 around lunchtime. There were 2 customers in the whole restaurant. The hostess threw an attitude about setting up for a party of 9. We sat down and the two waitresses stood behind the counter talking and didn't acknowledge us at all. After 15 minutes of just sitting there while they chit chat we walked out. As we were walking out they finally spoke to us ans asked if we were leaving. My husband said yes and we walked out of the door. NEVER EVER eating here. I wish I could give them 0 stars!!!

Came here for breakfast with my parents on a Sunday. It was pretty busy but moving quickly. We didn't have to wait long for a table. All of our food came out super fast after we ordered. The French toast was delicious. Had to add some sugar to my latte but that's just a personal preference. The prices are amazing too. This is a nice casual breakfast spot and look forward to going back.

There was hair in my food. Yuck. I guess they know how much fun it is to pay for that experience full price. The eggplant appetizer was interesting. But seriously though, this review ended when unclean food arrived at the table and they charged for it. Wow. Maybe the flea that is flying around the table likes the food here.

A hidden gem off Main Street! 
The owner is so sweet and chill. This place has got some great homemade gelato that's bold in flavor. I also tried the affogato, and MAN their espresso is strong! If you love coffee, I would definitely check this place out. 

Great outdoor seatings, and the inside is a beautiful cozy sweets shop. Wish I could've tried more items, will be back for sure!

Your typical loud eating experience.  I'm so frustrated by these eating places, I can't hear the waiter or anyone you are with.  They must all talk to each other about how to build a place that has loud seating.  Pretty good food, a little pricey.  I'll never go back but visit yourself and decide.  Not my kind of place.

this place is full of children acting out. there is a 17 y/o " manager" that has no idea what he's doing.  most of the rmployres are in their teens which is ok except the adult managers leave before the nightshift starts and there's the 17 y/o in charge.  the night crew is very rowdy and, disrespectful and unprofessional. sitting in my car at the drive thru,  I heard yelling, cursing and the "n" word.  the "minor manager" was standing there listening to all of it. there should always be an adult on duty to manage this store. I'll won't go back to this mcdonalds.

I would love to review the food, but the rude staff refused to serve me. They literally looked past me while I was at the register, asking "Can I help the next GROUP?" They had no interest in taking my order because I was only one person. I eventually gave up and left. It is probably for the best; my girlfriend showed up with a group a few minutes before me (so she was served) and she said her ice cream was not good and overpriced. She ended up throwing it away, which I have never seen her do. Definitely will not be returning.

Went here on a Friday evening and was thrilled by the decor and the vibe of the restaurant. The menu has a good set of tapas choices for everyone although it can be pricey if you want to try several things. 

My experience was less than average because of the terrible service we received. The server was not knowledgeable when we asked for recommendations, and kept forgetting about our food and drink orders. After waiting for 1.5 hours we managed to receive our first round of tapas. The service is generally sloppy, most of the servers can be seen spilling food and drink on the floor as they don't use a serving tray. Pretty unsightly for a chic looking restaurant like Sanctuaria. 

The food is alright but there are definitely better tapas options in St. Louis.

Ordered food from the website.  Website was very easy to use and friendly.  Website said order would be ready at 1pm.  I ordered at 12:45.  Got to restaurant at 12:53, went to counter, she asked my name, I gave it to her.  I paid and then she gave me my order.  Quick easy fast.  The only reason getting 4 stars.  The girl didn't smile, and when I said, that was fast she shot me a look, and the fortune cookies were stale.

I like this place, but every time I'm there it's packed. This is business as usual for any bar set up in a Philly row, but it's EXTRA crowded in here. Still, I like the place. I just wish the crowd weren't so dense.

If you want beer selection, come here. Their taps offer a pretty good variety on their own, but Eulogy's beer list is where this place shines. They have EVERYTHING (Belgian, and lots of German and Bohemian too). And some of the beers come in really novel sizes, so you could probably play a really expensive game of Edward Forty-Hands if you wanted to.

Anyways, I may be beating a dead horse by mentioning this, but it's worth trying their fries. Thick cut with various sauces. I think there was a mango chutney somewhere in there, and it was tasty.

Pro-tip: Keep your party small.
The freshest noodles in the area! It's an unassuming, delicious and reasonably priced BYO with a lovely owner. I'll be ordering my take-out from this place from now on. Great!!

Firstly, the burger was arguably the best burger I've had in a restaurant in a long time. The bun was soft, beef was very tasty and high quality and there was some sort of tomato jam the took it over the top. Our server Evan was on it too. He has a nice 70's mustache. We also had the veggie sopes which was a lighter entree since we had an appetizer. Super good. Oh it's a full bar but we had some beers and the Hitching Post Pinot Noir...their bar list is very well done! Fun atmosphere too especially the patio. Have fun.
Love their food , food is always hot and customer service is great , main Chinese place I go to in the area don't go to many others .

Thoroughly impressed with this restaurant. We went there for dinner last night and breakfast again this morning. Last night our waiter, Michael, recommended an excellent New Zealand wine to accompany my husband's dinner. My husband has to eat gluten free, so we were thrilled that they offered the lobster mac and cheese with gluten free pasta. They also brought out gf bread - nothing fancy, but if you eat gf regularly, you are excited by even this. I had the chili lime mahi mahi; it was delicious. I'm not a huge fish eater, so this was a perfect choice, as it had a light flake and very light fish flavor. Service was excellent, especially when you consider that we had our six-month-old daughter with us. 
This morning my husband had the homemade corned beef and eggs, and I had the Cuban breakfast sandwich. Unfortunately, I cannot eat dairy and they put cheese on it though I'd asked our waitress to ensure it didn't have any. Our waitress and the manager felt so bad that I had to wait while they remade it that they covered our entire bill - they didn't want a dime - AND they kept asking if we wanted anything else, such as a cappuccino to go. Above and beyond service, all with a fantastic view of the beach.
This gem of a restaurant is a Tampa staple.  The food is scrumptious and priced perfectly.  Stop in for lunch although you might not find a table because it's always so busy!

I would choose Rai Rai over Terakawa any day. I have only tried their house ramen, and I am a total fan! The broth is filled with garlicy-goodness, and it comes with a side of fried oyster that is cooked perfectly and pops in your mouth. Their egg is also cooked perfectly. The house ramen also comes with bamboo shoots and chinese vegetables.

The service has been nothing but friendly, prompt, and quick in the 3-4 times that I've been here. I've also received their 10% off coupon a few times now, so it's hard not to keep going back ;) $15 minimum for credit card though!

Granted, this is not even comparable to places like Daikokuya in LA's Little Tokyo, but Rai Rai is a solid Philly ramen restaurant.

I absolutely loved this place! I had been looking for a pupusaria in Philadelphia for a little over a year and I finally found El Cuscatleco. The food was very good as was the service. It wasn't very busy, so we did not have to wait long. Plus, the pupusas are so affordable! Love it here! Can not wait to go again.

Delicious food, attentive servers, spacious dining area, ample parking, & open on Mondays.  I liked my experience.  It was a tad expensive, but how could I complain - I had so much food!!!

There's a lot of competition not far away (Velvet Cactus, etc.), but this place is legit.

Music was insanely loud, barstools were super uncomfortable and the bar tops were all sticky and gross. Maybe if you like grungey bars you'd like this place but we walked out... ‍ The website made it seem like it was more of a sit down restaurant but it was like a dirty indoor/outdoor club.

When you're craving BBQ, Lucky well definitely caters it all. On a Sunday night, the place was empty so we were seated immediately. 
The drinks are pretty good. 
The wings were good, but not as great as I remember them being before. 
The Mac and cheese side was delicious, but the side of brussels was not and I would not recommend ordering those. 

Overall food was okay. I got my BBQ fix but it was definitely not as savory and finger-livdelicious as I hoped.

I have been coming to this restaurant for 20 years never got a bad meal tonight I had tuna chili Thai sauce my mom had an early dining scallops with apricot curry sauce happy hour till seven I had two margaritas for seven dollars my mom had a glass of wine for six food excellent if he never been there try it excellent.

Very cute, gourmet cheese shop. Great for gifts. They're also generous w/ the samples, though I almost puked when trying one of the cheeses.

Good thing you can sample before buying!

I've been coming to this great spot for a few years and decided to finally put a review thanks to a Great experience I had recently:

Patrick helped me out on the phone and in-person. He went above and beyond and reassured me everything was okay and helped me with some complications that came up with my order by using the mobile app.

Had I known Islands restaurant had a mobile app, I would've used it to build up my points for a while already, since any time I pass through Santa Barbara, I make sure to stop by here every time for a great meal made the way You want it.

My go-to is the Kilauea burger (with the veggie patty) and a cool Breeze smoothie...and maybe some wings!

There is always something that this location is lacking. This time there were ants in the hot tea. Then when I brought it to their attention, the manager was more interested in looking inside the tea jars. I had to ask for a new cup. 
They are constantly out of something or things are over baked, such at the gooey butter danish. 
Also, the place smells of a dirty rags cleaned with dirty water. Very disappointed. You never see any management out and walking around or helping.

Grew up dining at some of the great Brooklyn and Manhattan delis.  This place is right up there with them.  The service is cafeteria style and even the long lines go quickly.  The food is not for the faint of heat, with generous portions on everything.  Reubens, Pastrami on rye, sides, etc., were all excellent.  Perhaps not the healthiest eating but certainly delicious.  Walking distance from the Colts stadium.  Nice to go to with a small, intimate group willing to order different items and share.

I first stumbled on El Jarocho after a particularly hard night of partying.  I wandered hungover through the streets trying to find some food and something to quench my thirst. I ordered a Oaxaquenos Style Egg burrito, This place is totally a gem, probably my favorite mexican place in Philadelphia.

I used to be a Frothy fanatic, but sadly since the pandemic they have continued to disappoint. 

First of all, I mostly visit the downtown Franklin location and at least they let you go inside and order just a drink. They don't, however, let you sit down at a table after you order a drink. 

Today, I visited the 12S location and I had to wait in a long line just to order a drink with all the other "to go" orders. 
I'm sorry, but the food and drinks are just not worth the hassle. It wouldn't be an issue if it wasn't always so crowded, but it is with locals and tourist. 
If you plan on visiting here (at least on the weekend), expect it to be at least a two-hour visit.
As a Quarterite I've been going here for 20 years.  Atmosphere is wonderful even when it's crowded.  Not a chain, in fact they supply many other coffee shops with pastries daily.

My boyfriend and I couldn't get enough of this place! We went here every morning for breakfast/brunch during each day of our trip to NOLA. I ordered the pain perdu, which is a NOLA style french toast. It's light, fluffy, and absolutely delicious. I ordered it multiple times, couldn't get enough! We also ordered a bagel and lox which was so fresh and tasty. If you're going to New Orleans, Surrey's is a must!

Ate at Talula's Saturday night, we got there just as it opened for dinner so garden seating (which is first come, first serve) was not a problem. Server was efficient and friendly, it was our first time there and she explained everything wonderfully. We started with the domestic cheese plate which was delicious, I even ate the goat cheese and I normally hate goat cheese. One of the cheeses (my fave) was made by the Von Trapps, of Sound of Music fame, in Vermont. They also brought excellent brioche rolls with basil butter to the table (so warm and flaky). 

Since it is a bit pricey I got an appetizer portion of the ribbon pasta with truffles and ricotta, it was amazing. Very flavorful and not overly filling, plus the zucchini and summer squash tasted like they were just plucked from the garden. We also got some crispy Yukon Gold potatoes with ricotta and lemon zest for the table, so good as well. 

My friend got the bluefish with sweet and sour eggplant and kale. I am not exaggerating when I say the eggplant and kale was the best I have EVER eaten in my life. I didn't even think I liked eggplant much until eating Talula's. His bluefish was also perfectly cooked and really fresh tasting. Finally we finished with the ricotta donuts which are served with plum jam and covered with cinnamon. DELICIOUS, it is so worth getting dessert here. 

Highly recommend this  place, the best food I've eaten in Philly in awhile, fast service and beautiful atmosphere. Talula's is definitely a MUST. Can't wait to try their brunch!

Thank you YELP restaurant finder for leading me to this little gem when I was in desperate need of a 10PM donair a few weeks back on my way home from a concert!

The owner was friendly and the food was fresh.

Since moving to Canada, I have fallen in love with Donairs and I take my Donair meat seriously.  I'd give Donair Station a 8/10.  The meat was fresh the toppings a plenty.  So what didn't sell me on Donair Station completely?  The pita?  What you say?  Well yes, I've become quite spoiled by my local Donair Shop that picks up fresh Pitas daily and makes them all fluffy and warm in their steamer.  

I've visited this location twice now and both times I found the pita itself a little on the dry/chewy side.

They make up lots of other treats here you wouldn't typically find at a Donair Shop like fresh house made hummus, schwarma platters, kebobs, etc.

Definitely has something for everyone!

This review is in regards to the food.  Food was okay.  We came here tonight 90 min before the game.  We were told they were out of chicken, beef, and had a hard time finding mustard, ketchup, and silverware.  We ordered a pulled pork roll,  hot dog, and panini.  When the food was delivered they were all prepared  on Wonder Bread.
Pretty good food, nice menu options, beautiful interior (40 TV's lol) and most importantly, friendly staff!

I typically can't be bothered to write a review whether it be a positive one or a negative one, however this place has gone so far down hill... I don't know how they stay in business. This was once a really great place to get sushi or a Chinese entree, but that was under different management apparently. Now the sushi is mediocre at best and to say the staff is inattentive is an understatement. Very sad. This used to be one of my favorite restaurants in the area.  :c(

Paella del Mar. If you enjoy seafood this would be the right dish for you. It's loaded with lots of seafood: clans, mussels, shrimps, calamari, crabs and chicken. All on saffron rice. 

It was delicious but it was too watery had lots of juice still I think it's supposed to be served dry. 

A+ for the service and the food was delicious.

Wish I could give this place no stars. The worst bar I've ever been to. Firstly, there is a cover to get in. It's a bar not a club. Smh. Then you go in apparently if you want to get to the roof you have to buy an overpriced watered down drink. You get to the roof and it's not even worth going up there. There is no music on the roof, just loud noise from the city life. The first floor bar only has 6 stools and no other seating besides what I thought were 6 dining tables you could eat at but apparently not, it's for VIP only and cost $200 to even sit down. The security was so rude, I tried to step right outside the door to take a phone call and they said I couldn't get back in unless I pay another cover, even though I already regrettably paid the first time and he saw me just walk out the door. The shots taste like juice I don't even think there was any alcohol in the bottle it was so watered down for $20 smh. I will never come here again. It's like they are desperate for money I was scared to go to the bathroom it might of been a fee for that too. And it was 1130pm and only 40 people max. Music was blah. The place wasnt even popping enough to demand so much.
Best place to come and get a awesome steak and shake beats a lot of other places around here highly recommended

Went here for Valentine's Day (wanted wine but no one offered even tho I knew I could have ordered it but still) BUT honestly the Food is probably the best Indian food I have ever had since I moved to tampa! Absolutely delicious! The staff is the extra touch very patient and cool. Who ever is the manner seems to have it all working together nicely. Very Clean establishment! The chicken samosas are the best I have ever tasted. 5/5

Ugh this place smells so bad. As soon as I walked in the door it hit me. It smells like they have been reusing the same dirty wet rags over and over to wipe down the menus and table tops. Literally the whole place smells awful. The only reason I stayed was because it was a work lunch. I went there at 12pm today. It's now going on 7pm and I can still smell it in my hair. I literally threw all my clothes in the wash as soon as I got home and will be washing my hair right after this review. The servers are very sweet but omg someone needs to do something about the stench. I will NEVER return. PLEASE CLEAN YOUR RAGS!!!!!

Mandolas was apparently founded by one partner connected with Carrabas.  The other side of partnership is World of Beer I believe?
So first time eating their food and I have to say Carrabas in my opinion is much better.  The lasagna tasted and appeared like something you would buy in a frozen food container and heat up.  It did not seem homemade at all.  The garlic bread which is an extra had little or no garlic.  I would rate that 1/2 star.  The Lasagna I would rate 2 star.  The salad was ok, but nothing great.  I ordered the chocolate cake for dessert and I'd say it was just average.  I would be hard pressed to say Pepperidge farm frozen chocolate cake isnt equal to or better.  Nothing seemed fresh and homemade. 
For those that love it, I wonder if you have ever been to a real homestyle non chain Italian restaurant to see what real homemade delicious one of a kind Italian food is really like.  There are better choices in this town and in  fact there are much better Italian restaurants than most all of the Italian restaurants in Tampa bay in general.  Once you've had it you'll know it.  
In northern states and cities you can get real Italian food and there is no comparison.  Sorry, 2 stars is the best I can give this attractive new restaurant.

If you have to go, stick with the drinks.  Dinner drinks and service were  ok... the food wasn't.  The upstairs is too tight and too loud.  Couldn't hear my date talk!  After dinner, we thought we'd try the bar for a drink.  The female bartender couldn't be in a worse mood!  Literally threw our bill at us.  We weren't alone... the place attracts a weird crowd too.  We left after 1 drink and won't be back.

Very creative, all vegan selection. Their Philly Cheesesteaks are awful though- definitely go to Wiz Kid! But their pizzas are really good! My only suggestion is to order a whole pie, since their "by the slice" case is not under a heat lamp and they just reheat 'at room temperature' slices in a toaster oven to serve. Made my tummy hurt a lil after- not sure if it is up to health code, but my dumb ass was hungry and went for it! Just get some friends and split a whole pie, they are very good!

Why 5 stars? Well did I tell you I was a vodka buff? We have been to this place several times since May of 2011 and not once have I had a BAD drink. I love vodka and the first time my boyfriend and I went, they allowed us to sample a lot of things. Needless to say, I had to drive us home that day, LOL. 

What I like about Sub Zero is that they have many selections and drink creations. I can always have my vodka in more ways than one, AND I can taste different ones. The atmosphere is diverse and relaxed (like I like it). I'm sorry that I can't tell you how the food is because we've always gone for an after-dinner drink or two, but when we do finally eat here, I'll let you know. I have not had bad service, the bartenders were always pleasant, and I always felt relaxed here. Humm..maybe it was the alcohol, LOL.

If you like vodka, this is the place to be. Although the drinks can be a little pricey, stick to the Vodka of the week and you will be okay.

I feel like this is the only place in town where you can get normal bananas. And by that I just mean just normal everyday bananas. 

Other than that, it is basically a cheaper cooler version of Whole Foods, with pretty much the same stuff, and better parking.

Most importantly, the parking lot slopes downward from the store, so you can ride your shopping cart out like a chariot.

Chinese food has never truly cracked my list of favorite foods, I much rather do Japanese instead. I find Chinese food to be a little on the heavy side, every time I have good chinese, I just wanna take a long nap. Anyhow, having finally tried YH after all the fuss, I must agree with the majority of my fellow Yelpers. This place more than met expectations.

Had to order quickly because lunch was about to close, so went ahead and ordered right away. It was a group of six so we all got a chance to try the popular at YH. 

I'll start with The Fried Calamari, this dish had hot pepper flakes all over so make sure you like some heat, we all enjoyed it. Fried to perfection, and very tasty.

The fried rice and the lo mein were very good. Though I was more impressed with the fried rice. I was expecting the usual fried rice from other restaurants , this one stood out IMO. Very well cooked with the right amount of egg mix.

We also ordered The Mongolian beef and the sweet and sour chicken. Never been crazy about sweet/sour chicken, the kids seemed to like it though. Now the beef didn't look very appealing but trust me, this dish along with the calamari were the stars of the show. 

Overall, I was satisfied with the food and the service, keep in mind that the food here is served family style and come in great portions, we ended up getting three to go boxes. 

Though I'm not likely to go back any time soon, YH will be the place that comes to mind the moment on those rare occasions when I crave for nothing else but Chinese.

One of my colleagues loves this place, so I have suffered through many a lunch.  The service is always horrible, the food is gross, and it's always more expensive then it should be.  And it's HOT inside.

I'm not a huge fan of dining out for Italian food - although pasta is one of my favourite foods, I like the simple hearty stuff I cook at home and find that a lot of upscale restaurants overcomplicate things - it still tastes good, but doesn't have that homey feel that I have grown to associate Italian food with.  Tasty Tomato brings that homey feel with a twist - delicious!!

I started with the Tri Colore salad on special.  It was a bed of mixed greens, with grape tomatoes and Bocconcini cheese on top, with vinaigrette dressing.  Everything tasted great and fresh, but I wish there was more cheese (there was only 2-3 little pieces) included.

For my entree, I had the Lobster Medallions with Rose sauce (on special).  The pasta was well-cooked and lobster wasn't overdone, but the Rose sauce was the standout!  It was tangy, creamy, with the perfect amount of spice to give it a little kick.  It was decently sized for a full meal, or can be shared (with an appetizer) for a light meal.

The service was fast and friendly, and our water glasses never sat empty.  There was complimentary bread and oil/vinegar too.  We arrived at 5:30 on a Saturday night without a reservation and sat down right away, but the restaurant was full by 5:45 and there was a line of 5-10 parties waiting as we left.  I'll definitely be back but will be sure to make a reservation!!

Super excited to Come here on a Saturday evening to celebrate my birthday with family. Place was pretty packed and busy. Should of made reservations but was easily accommodated outside seating for our party in their cute alley seating that resembles the outdoor seating in Europe. Very cute! We were there for two hours waiting on drinks then finally menus, slowly but surely appetizer, salad, and entrees. Waitress was very apologetic about the long wait for everything, stating they were very busy tonight. Food was pretty darn good. I had the spaghetti and meatballs. the rest of my group had the meatless rigatoni dish and the pistachios chicken, everyone was pleased. All entrees came with a complimentary sample plate along with a salad . From the reviews also an expresso as well . We weren't offered that but I'm sure it was due to the busy night. Overall nice experience at oggi will def plan to return and try other menu items
Was out of SEVERAL vegetables, toppings and condiments. Poor food prep planning. Only two employees working during the lunch rush. Men's restroom was filthy. Last time eating here!!!

This was our second time eating there. The first time was "okay".
I am not expecting a fine dining meal but we were a little disappointed. We both ordered a side dinner salad. While my Caesar was okay (alot of the ribs) our other salad had what seemed to be old diced tomatoes. The salad looked great but the tomatoes were a turn off.

We had a crab cake app and "hot" wings and fish spread as our dinner. The crab cake came out more like a pancake. It was rather "wet" on the inside with a very strange texture. The fish spread was just plain bland and that's the best way I can explain it. The wings weren't very good either. They tasted like they had been tossed in butter. No flavor whatsoever. We asked our server for a side of the hot sauce (what they use to toss the wings in) and it was completely different than what our wings tasted like.

Our server, Erica, was very good, engaging and turned what could have been a rather poor meal into a more enjoyable time. 

Hopefully our next visit will be a better meal.

I went on a week night for happy hour and it  was extremely quiet.

Nice glass of wine and ordered the veggie flat bread. Unfortunately it was too sparse on the veggies so it was more bread with a sprinkling of veggies, not what I desired. 

I also had the grilled fish tacos yet the tortillas were over sized compared to the taco filling. Fish was good  just overwhelmed by the tortillas.

Not sure I'd choose to go back .

What a shock how much this food was absolutely inedible(the appetizers were stuffed in the bag, the salads were kind of warm in there too. The sushi was fine which is to be expected.) The only salvage was the bartender who was suffering without any air conditioning! on a 95 degree day! The atmosphere here is always a little dark and gloomy but that makes the place sexy in a way but this wasn't the experience I'm used to. They were trying to tell us the reason they have no air conditioning in the dining area is because of the ceilings, but in the winter it'swarm just fine. I have never see a heater in the winter months. 

Either way I stayed for a drink, thank you to the very overheated bartender for being so kind during our orders. 

The 3 kingdoms was was practically inedible i could only find the shrimp in the order and nothing else. It was supposed to contain scallops, chicken and crab. I even called to tell someone I may have the wrong order, got put on hold and disconnected 2 times. Seeing I don't live close to this location it would have been quite the ride back to correct the order. 

If this is the level of a quality they are going to be serving We won't be back. I will kindly update a review once(well if) I go back to see if this issue is ever fixed.

The pizza here is not bad. It's actually pretty good. They just need to get their orders right. They delivered the wrong pizza to us. We looked on the receipt and it was our order the person just wrote our order down wrong. We ate it anyway and it turned out to be pretty good. This time it worked out but next time it may not. They should pay more attention.

It's a tourist trap with lots of fried food. My dish wasn't seasoned well (way too much black pepper) and the manager wouldn't refund my money because I "didn't like the taste. It would be different if your food was cold".  I've never heard crap like that before. You over season my food and I'm the one who has to pay.  Let me add that my family is West Indian so I like seasoned food, just not a pile of pepper on my food. I wouldn't go back or recommend  Deanie's.

Started ordering take out from Sushiman about 6 months ago. Now we order at least 1x/ a week. Great quality, great price. The young man who runs the take out/front of the house does a great job! Especially on the weekends when they have a lot of orders! Looking forward to dining in once they open back up.

These 5 stars are primarily given because of service. Our waitress Gentry was well versed, extremely knowledgeable, and very willing to help with any and all questions regarding the menu. She was delightful and I would return simply to have her wait on me again. The food was great as well. Ask for Gentry :) staff is very friendly as a whole! 
I manage a local restaurant and would hire her ANY DAY!

Chicken is delicious. Crispy & juicy. I typically don't eat slaw but worked well with Nashville hot chicken. My son enjoyed the mac & chz. Unfortunately not really any other kids options (he thought the tenders looked too spicy). Only real negatives are parking & lack of beer.

Wonderful little cafe / bakery in the heart of downtown Boise. 
Most of their regular business is Breakfast - Brunch - Lunch and they are open for dinner Thurs - Fri - Sat. 
They have many specialty dinner services most commonly on Thursday evenings. 
These include: Farm & Wine nights, where they prepare a dinner with local produce and meats pared with wines from a local vineyard - French regional cuisine dinners - French holiday inspired dinners - Seafood & Shellfish inspired dinners - Tapas nights, which highlight foods from areas throughout Europe and the US - Paella night, etc. If you don't want to miss out on these, fill out a card to be added to their mailing list next time you are there!
When you walk in the front door, you are greeted with the most amazing pastry case filled with all sorts of delectable and beautiful, handmade treats along with their beautiful crusty breads and baguettes, and croissants. Their breads and croissants are sold at by other retailers in the area also, including the Boise Co-Op. 
Their food is always expertly crafted. Portions are elegantly presented, and very flavorful.
Noteworthy Brunch items include: Crab cake benedict with poached duck eggs, quiches, and of course 'pain perdu' (french toast). Besides their lovely coffee selection, they also offer fresh squeezed orange juice and mimosas!
Also a nice place to pick up a bottle of wine and a baguette to go with your own dinner.

I show up to pick up àn order that I had placed on the phone with the manager, Gaby, a week ago. She took the order on the phone even though I had told her I could do it on line. She never turned the order in and now my family Christmas dinner is screwed! Oh and I called àn hour in advance of pick up to confirm. And they said ok it would be ready. So I drove all.the way down there. This is the downtown Indianapolis location. They didnt even apolgize.

I have to be honest, I would never get pizza here (it just does not look appetizing enough for me to try it), but that spicy curried cheesesteak is my life...like i actually live for it. I might be blaspheming right now considering I am in Philly, but I  just don't enjoy cheesesteaks typically. So if you're like me and are willing to try them again but with a twist, check out this place. 


I first heard abt little Sicily from a co-worker, otherwise would have never given this place the time of day, especially based on other reviews but I'm glad I did. The service is quick and the product is consistent: good enough for me.. I'd give more stars if the rest of the menu was similar

Perfect pizza. I have only had the Square but I've been to dozens of the best pizza places (apizza Scholls, amodern, all the New Haven spots, and many more) and this is my favorite (tied with Apizza scholls in Portland and Delancey in Seattle- both different styles). They are nailing it here.  My only issue is that I don't live right next door. I'd volunteer here just to be around this pizza if I could.

We came in to this Ihop for a quick visit and we were pleasantly surprised. We found this Ihop to be much better and more enjoyable than our hometown Ihop in Santa Clara.
