There are endless options, including hibachi, and no matter how particular someone is, there is something for everyone on the menu. The lighting is very dim, however, which makes seeing the food somewhat difficult. Despite this, it's an enjoyable place to eat. If you're searching for premium sushi, though, you may want to go elsewhere. As this is an all you can eat restaurant, you shouldn't expect the finest of the finest of sushi. However, the sushi has always tasted good and I've never felt as though the fish was questionable. I'm simply stating that you do get what you pay for. I come here a couple of times each semester and each time I leave feeling full and happy. As a matter of fact, I'm due for another visit soon.
Really good food fast service great atmosphere! Loved it! Shrimp tacos were great! Salsa was fire!

Why can't we have a place like this in Norcal? Ensenada beer battered fish tacos were really great, but the standout was the tuna ceviche with pomegranate seeds and watermelon, the cauliflower taco was incredible and the Octopus and shrimp taco was so gooood. Every taco had so much depth of flavor that we came here two nights in a row and ordered the exact same thing. Just wow.

This place just gets better each time I visit. The enchilada sauce is amazing! The nachos were just right amount of crispy, and the steak taco  shell was grilled slightly and such a nice surprise. The pollo Cancun was perfect! Donaldo our server was full personality and very attentive. To top it off, they were playing the Stanley cup game 7 and dis not mind we stayed until the end.
Sushi was great!  I love that this place is low key.  I was here for a conference and didn't feel awkward eating dinner alone.  I'm also giving them thumbs up on their decor.
Nothing special here.  The fries were cold, and the wait is long. The milkshakes are TOTALLY worth it though!

PF always runs a 20% off takeout discount on debate nights, and considering that this was the final presidential debate, we decided to order some dishes for our late dinner.  The food was pretty standard for the chain, and I did like that I was able to place my order online, pay for it in advance, and park right outside the takeout register and have my food practically delivered to me in minutes, complete with utensils, napkins, and fortune cookies.  Yes, I do realize that my laziness is almost sloth-like but c'est la vie.  I noticed that they have a few new menu items, like the crabmeat fried rice, pad thai, and a duck duo, so I ventured to try the duck, which had a slow cooked leg and a cripsy pan-fried breast served with a watercress salad.  The duck was just okay and the portion was a bit on the small side, but that may be a good thing considering that duck isn't exactly the most cholesterol-friendly poultry meat.  I liked the slow cooked leg more than the breast since the flavor was icily imbued throughout, whereas the breast was a bit bland in the innermost section.  It wasn't bad for a chain but I would definitely get my duck fix at Margaret Kuo, Sangkee, or New East.  The Shanghai shrimp dish was very solid, with tender shrimp, plenty of veggies, and a light yet flavorful garlic sauce.  Definitely better than what you would get from your typical greasy takeout place.  The crab fried rice was pretty good, and it had pieces of bacon, which definitely gave it a bit of a twist.  The actual amount of crabmeat was skimpy but that was to be expected.  The flavor was good, and I was glad to see egg and shitake slices in it; overall, I did like it a lot better than what Dad would usually get from China (insert noun here).  It came to about $37 for all 3, which wasn't bad at all.  Next time, I will probably go back to my usual Singapore street noodles, moo goo gai pan, and cumin lamb, but it was a nice change tonight and a good break from cooking.  The 20% off didn't hurt and we were able to thoroughly enjoy the debate while chowing.

So apparently these are a chain. I've been to the one in Philly before and was not impressed. This one is a lot nicer and the food seemed a lot better too . . . right up until I got out to my car and I had to jump back out to puke my meal all over a bush in the parking lot. Hopefully it at least serves as a deterrent to others looking to eat here but with the rain today my warning is probably long gone by now.

Awesome veggie food in new restaurant w cool vibe.  Easy background music - none of the big bass techno music.  Recommend shredded tofu rolls - crunchy vegetables w tofu in rice wrapper.   Green papaya salad is the best I've had - and pretentious moment here, I've been to Vietnam.  Haha.  I had the satay noodles w a broth that would satisfy a carnivore, it's so hearty.  Dinner mate had spicy noodles that were also delicious.  End your meal w burdock tea for your digestion and a healthy liver (according to traditional Asian lore).  

Definitely a place to return to again and again.
Excellent food, wonderful price and incredible efficient service ! Love it and highly recommend this place

Ordered pizza to get here at a particular time and showed up 3 hours later. On top of that driver was over 2 hours with my pizza in the car. I'd avoid ever ordering from this dominos if you can avoid it and get a closer delivery from another location. Terrible customer service and no explanation given....
Reading all these yelp reviews now and they are TRUE! 
Nothing good comes of this location and I would avoid at all costs
Their spicy coconut soup is incredible! Only if the best I've had in the whole Nashville- Murfreesboro area! Staff was helpful and friendly!
Yummmm!  We came for a fun dining experience. We got it, but we also got delicious food. Amazing Qhattro Framaggio, California salad, filet mignon Coq au Vin, and chocolate fondue. We will be back.

I would give Tres Carnales 6 stars if I could. 
I walked in here to try a few tacos on the advice of a fellow yelper friend. I was waiting in line when someone approached me to ask about my order and if I wanted to sit or take out. It turns out it is one of the owners (Chris) and I really appreciated being greeted with a personal touch. Chris offered to let me hang out with a friend of his who was in for a bite on his birthday. He also took my order and I trusted his taste and told him to order me something I would like.
The birthday boy and myself hit it off immediately and what I had originally thought would be a 20 minute culinary diversion ended up lasting a few hours and a smorgasbord of amazing food. The head chef and part owner made some amazing dishes that isn`t on any of the menus and I was in awe by the quality of it. Home made 16 hour Creme Fraishe!!!
The food was amazing, the company was cool, the service impeccable but the best part of it all was the ambiance. Carnales has an energy of it`s own, like a heartbeat. I could say it was partly due to the decor or the open kitchen or the never ending line up but I actually believe the underlining current is great food. People are happy when they`re filled with tasty, authentic and affordable fare... This is a success model every restaurant should follow!
this place is good. the oysters are everyone's favorite. the new tuna dish is a must try as long as they don't run out.

Seriously, this place is as good as it gets for salads.  The options are too numerous to list.  I'd bet there are 5000 salad combinations.  You order, pick your ingredients, watch them make it, tell them how much dressing to add, then they shake it all up and serve it in a hipster recycled-looking cardboard container.  The end result is a perfectly-coated 72 pound (joking) salad.

I haven't had a sandwich yet, but they look fantastic.  I can't wait to get back there.

This place is a gem on State Street.  

Surrounded by overpriced, touristy restaurants on lower State Kadiz has an impressive ambiance and delicious food.

The margarita flatbread was great.  Just the right amount of flavor and not loaded down with all the normal grease and heavy toppings.

I had the Kobe Hanger steak with yukon potatoes.

Great bar in the Marigny section, really nice local ambiance, there is a pool table on the first level and live music and tapas on the second floor. The owner is a lovely lady, and Daphne the manager is the best.
An absolute must, if you are tired of the tourist scene, and want a taste of the real NOLA

A great spot we found. Perfect for a really nice evening meal. Wine was delicious. Nice place in SB. Food was really interesting, not all of it to my taste but I appreciated it nonetheless. Staff were nice too.
I'm a vegetarian fyi. The veggie burger was the most disappointing one I have ever eaten. The service  was great the bartender nice which is why they recieved two stars instead of one.

Beautiful view! We stopped here Friday before I hopped on the plane to Canada for Xmas and watched the sunset! It was beautiful! We ordered the queso dip ad gator bites to snack on, our server was very pleasant and helpful in recommendations. The queso dip was ok but Mcalisters by far has the best if you ask me and this wasn't even close. The gator bites were tasty we ordered buffalo sauce on the side and it was so spicy I couldn't believe it even Brandon thought it was spicy! The bites had a little flavoring of their own so they were ok without the sauce! We've had better gator bites else where in the Bay Area these were a little chewy but still tasty. Brandon has also ordered a beer while we waited and some how with two appetizers and a beer our bill was about $50.... I'd say the view is beautiful but the food is definitely not worth the price.

Oh also they are sort of genius with the fishing line over the patio so the seagulls don't bother you while you eat! #mindblown
All the sandwiches I have had are excellent.  Especially the rueben.  Salads are really good. The Caesar salad is very good.

This is a cute little restaurant and bar that serves food late. The bar area is cozy, and the alcohol selection is decent. We got a milk stout and the brugge beer, and both were amazing. 

The spinach and asparagus dip was pretty good, I liked the flavor the asparagus brought to the dip. The soup of the day was a creamy asparagus, which was my favorite part of our meal. It was certainly very creamy and there was lots of yummy spinach chunks. We shared the pork chop entree and I was disappointed. First of all, there were two thin pieces of pork that was pale, limp, and just sad looking. I would rather have one thick piece that actually had a lovely sear. The chops were also over-cooked, the worst offense to meat. The flavor was pretty good (fairly sweet), but a bit under-salted for my preference. The peppers and brussel sprouts were a bit soggy and just a bit of a strange match to pork chops. The dish reminded me of a Chinese pork stir-fry, to be honest. Overall, the experience was good, great service, good beer...I would definitely come back for the milk stout, but not that pork chop.

The food is good for what it is - it's an inexpensive lunch for ones wanting Americanized Chinese with the convenience of ordering from your car. Today I got the steak and shrimp rice bowl with brown rice and a chicken egg roll - all for under $10. The rice bowls are usually around $6 but they charge you more for steak and shrimp. Fine, I get it. The portion size was ideal and filled me up - lots of steak but just 1 piece of shrimp. However, 25 minutes in the drive thru? Ridiculous! Of course the day I wanted something fast I got stuck in the drive thru line for almost half and hour. Not sure what the hold up was, but "express" it is not. By the time I realized the line was not moving after 10 minutes, a few other cars came up behind me and I was stuck. I just hope this was just a fluke cause I like coming here for lunch.

With three four-seaters open, I was told I had to wait for a two-seater to open. The bar was full, so I couldn't sit down. 

The decor was nice. As I noticed all tables that could be separated, I grew to appreciate the skull hanging above the bar. Very authentic. I even grew to feel empathetic for it: slowly dying of hunger and thirst, left to be gawked at by intoxicated patrons wondering why I'm there. Just there. Waiting. Watching. 

A strand of Christmas lights was out. Even more authentic. I felt like I was in solidarity with those lights: dejected, noticed but not acknowledged. 

Finally, I asked the hostess if she could split one of the tables for me--you know, capitalizing on the paying customer that actually is there instead of the one that may or may not come in--she said they couldn't.

This is the second time I can, and I'm so disappointed. The first time it was ok. I had the penne Rosa which I liked better, but they messed up the first time and I had to sent back. The staff was real friendly, both times. 
Today I came for the truffle Mac and cheese. I love truffle everything. It didn't really taste like truffles at all. Truffles have a strong taste and there wasn't a truffle taste at all to me. The Mac was dry. It tasted like box Mac and cheese. I also got the Parmesan encrusted chicken in it and the chicken had no flavor either. All the breading was falling off the chicken. Also the bread crumbs were all over the Mac and cheese. Bread crumbs are only suppose to be a topping, not all in the Mac and cheese. If I would of know that I would of ask without bread crumbs. I'm not fond of bread crumbs in Mac and cheese anyway, but it's ok for a topping. I also ordered the 3 piece garlic cheese bread, because I haven't eaten all day and it's after 7:30pm before I ordered, and I'm starving. It tasted gross and very salty. Like they just put garlic salt and cheese on the bread, gross. I just wasted almost $18 for dinner. I will post a pic. I didn't even eat half on it and can't, it's gross. I will get something at Schnucks to have later to eat. I think the only thing that's decent here is the penne Rosa,if they don't mess it up. I'm so disappointed. I know it's fast food, but it would of been nice to have somewhere to get a decent truffle Mac and cheese that I didn't have to cook on days that I can't cook.

Actually this time the service wasn't so friendly. They didn't check on me like they did last time, and they didn't pick up my dishes, but they picked up everyone else's. I don't like I'm ever coming back after this treatment!!!!!

Would enjoy this place more if you weren't being suffocated by the smell of cigarette smoke. And because the smoke smell, the food tasted very bland. Will never come back because of that. I'm not sure why St. Charles still allows smoking in their buildings. The only thing I liked was our server and the fruit.

Oh my YUMMM!    I had the lunch prix fixe menu and my husband did regular menu so we could get a variety and not break the bank on our first visit.    Service is fine dining type exceptional, atmosphere is beautiful, and it was a joy to have this kind of wonderful experience including cocktails for under $100 for two.  We had a lovely amuse bouche (for lunch!) in an eggshell topped with a little caviar and I had a wonderful champagne cocktail while my husband had a Sazarec manhattan.   The pâté starter with a variety of mustards and conserve from the prix fixe menu is some of the best pâté I've had anywhere and the portion was ample with a good amount of brioche toasts so you weren't stuck with having to ask for more toast.   My hubby had the alligator confit that was almost enough for a main dish.   It was tasty, with the alligator having a sausage quality so you didn't get chewy chunks, just savory alligator goodness.      I had the Drum fish main dish that was more than ample, fresh, delicious, and prepared well, with vibrantly fresh veggies in the succotash.   My husband had the parmesan brioche topped speckled trout with a whipped hollandaise and it was also exceptional.   The panna cotta dessert that came with my lunch was heavenly.    The quality and service came up to the standards of some of the best of the best.... And to do this for a lunch...with the prix fixe lunch for $20,  is a very special gift for folks that really love food.

Went for the first time today. We live close but hardly ever eat breakfast out. Good sign that it was busy.  I had the Eggs Benedict and home fries! Very good! Would have liked a little more Hollandaise but very tasty! Hubby had The Station. A little bit of everything. He loved the sausage links and the pancakes! Owner introduced himself, so friendly. We had a great experience and will go back!

It does look much from the outside but their food is simplistic and outstandingly good. A vegan Reuben sandwich was my first entree and I've been visiting as often when I'm in town. This is a local's gem. Don't miss it!

This food is amazing. Absolutely, hands down, best place I've been to in a very long time. Went in on a recommendation because my friend has worked with one of the chefs! Best decision ever. They were amazing and we didn't try one thing that wasn't delicious. 

We suggest the bacon wrapped dates, whipped feta, confit sweet potatoes, brussel sprouts, and the fatty cakes (? gingerbread and marscapone cookies). Everything is next level good.

Ps they pickle lots of interesting things in house...if you like pickled things, give that selection a try.

This place makes its own beer. I got a flight of six beers to try. It's strange that you can't pick your choice for the flight. So I had to get the flight of six in order to sample one that I wanted to try. Beer was okay. I prefer sweet or sour beers which they did not carry. Service was good. We got the alligator appetizer which was a small portion for the price you pay. Nice atmosphere otherwise.

Had the BBQ Shrimp Poboy because everybody is raving about it. Well, the bread is fresh and tasty and the BBQ sauce tastes pretty good, but they don't clean their shrimp. If you enjoy eating a crap ton of shrimp crap then by all means, you're at the right place. There were like a hundred of shrimps in that poboy, which is good bang for the buck, but I lost my appetite after like five of them.

Every time I visit Tucson, I stop by. If you like walking around with your drinks, this is the spot hahaa

I'm saying that honestly, there is so much space to explore. I've only ever been there when they had a DJ, but people have told me they've had a lot of shows here.

Every time I stop by, I meet people w/ a trippy story that's fun to hear.
I've seen a couple there that showed up in their wedding outfits, just to sit in the booth they had their first conversation at. One dude got sad-drunk, & started explaining to women how beautiful they are. I've even seen a shot-for-shot battle between off duty bartenders that ended hilariously.

Booze is solid, prices are relative, crowd is cool, the staff is cooler.
Stop by some time.

Not bad! 

Crab Cake 2/5
Ok the crab cake wasn't that good. The cheesy consistency of the crab cake threw me off. It was filled with mascarpone. 

Carbonara 4/5
This was delicious. The spaghetti was definitely made in house. It had a wonderful al dente texture that I really enjoyed. However, I did not like the bacon gelato. It made the pasta a bit cold. Also, i ordered it with no pepper. 

Tiramisu 5/5
Yes please! This tiramisu was so delicious. I was eating it very slowly to savor each bite. However, I almost started choking because it has cacao powder that I inhaled. Not fun but delicious nonetheless

The dog is yet another Nashville great. The types of dogs are awesome. The fries are to die for and the names of each dog is hilarious. I don't care if hot dogs are all the left overs of beef.... they are an American past time. The only down side is that the restaurant is one of the convert houses. So space is limited, make sure and get their early during lunch.
Love it here! Perfect outing for spring/summer day with the family.

For the eclectic semi-fast food market, this place is probably the best in the area. That being said I hope this place gets more customers! I think the location isn't in the best parts of town, they would do much better downtown but I'm assuming the rent isn't cheap down there.

Service is lovely, food is surprisingly delicious and incredibly flavorful. Their collard greens are probably the best in the area, cooked to perfection. And their waffle fries are crispy, starchy potato gold. Cover them in cheese, chili (beanless!), and onions and you won't be disappointed!

Went in for lunch last week and they have real nice lunch specials at reasonable prices.  The sushi was ok, the fish quality was good however the rice was not so good, very heavy and mushy.  I would go back and give it another try maybe an anomaly?

came here and had the tortilla soup and it was great in fact Iam surprised as to how low the other yelpers have rated this place.Even though it was the weekend and place was crowded I received great customer service.We returned for their $2.00 taco special and they were also very good

Came here with a friend during our visit to Tulane during mardi gras and were pleasantly surprised. I would give this place a solid 3.5 stars.

While their servers seemed a bit spacey, once we were seated and ordered, everything came pretty quickly. 

We started off with the spinach and artichoke dip which was super delicious and a great size for two people. I then ordered the meatball Stromboli and enjoyed that as well. The sandwich was pretty huge as I came into the meal starving and could barely finish it. 

Overall, was pretty quick service and food was better than expected. The pizzas looked good too so maybe try that there also.

Wonderful experience at the Juice Bar today! Feeling under the weather so the JB employee told me which juices would be best to combat my cold. I went with the Ginger Green. Then she offered me a shot, but I said I didn't need one today. When she came out with my finished juice, she included the shot anyway! So kind of her. It was definitely strong, but I'm glad she let me try it on the house! Great service.

Service was great, food was okay. 

Maurine (I think) was our server and she was great. Happy helpful and very polite. Thanks Maurine!

Food:
We went with the 3course meal (42$): appetizer, soup/salad, entree. 

Husband got cheesesteak egg rolls, Caesar salad, and New York strip. 

Egg rolls were an interesting concept, comes with some sauce on it and mustard which I'm fine with. Husband doesn't like mustard that much. It's also kinda heavy. Also, should be labeled egg roll; it's one egg roll cut into two pieces 
Caesar salad is normal. Nothing amazing. 
New York strip was cut into 5-6 medallion pieces, appeared to be cooked to medium rare and generally tasted good. Husband's comments are that it was good but not amazing, not bursting with flavor or anything. Medallions were over mashed potatoes

I got calamari, fresh greens salad, filet mignon. 

Calamari has a sweet and sour sauce. I don't like my Calamari that way, but that's just me. Generally the flavors were good, balanced, crunchy enough and not too much, and the bean sprouts in it were refreshing. 
I really liked the fresh green salad with a lot of fresh ground pepper. Flavors were light and refreshing, felt great to eat it after the heavy egg roll! Greens tasted great and there was corn on it too. I liked it so much I took half home. 
Filet mignon was great, lightly seasoned so it still had a lot of its own flavors, and the sauce it came with and the mashed potatoes it came on just added to it. Mashed potatoes had a good butter flavor to them and slight horseradish. Great balance. I'm so full!!

Lastly, because it was our anniversary, they treated us to a dessert. Thanks!!
We got the banana pudding which, although quite sweet, was really good! The middle was soft and juicy and the outer edges were harder and chewy. 

Overall, it was generally a good meal and they helped make our anniversary a special one!

This is the best Mexican food in Reno/Sparks. 

In fact, it's 100 times better than all the Mexican food in Seattle... which is where I live now.
The salsa here is so good that I actually order some to-go and bring it back to Washington & freeze it for later. 
Contrary to what one other reviewer said.. the food did not change when this restaurant changed locations. It's the same owners and the same food. Thank goodness!!

I grew up near the gulf coast in a small town in southern Texas. If you read my reviews, you're probably thinking, "Wow, this guy mentions that he's from Texas a lot." 1) I apologize. 2) Bear with me.

The reason I mention my upbringing near the coast is my strong affinity and familiarity with southern style seafood cooking. Candidly, I've had some of the best boiled, fried, and steamed seafood imaginable, and that is what makes this restaurant so spectacularly impressive. Peacemaker's phenomenal food will transport you to a geography very different than where it sits in Benton Park.

For starters, we shared a variety of seasonal oysters that tasted as fresh as can be. We also split a lobster boil, steamed mussels, a crawfish po-boy, and a bowl of gumbo. Everything that we laid our hands on was absolutely fantastic. To finish it off, we tackled a slice of their homemade blueberry pie, which just dissolved in our mouths. I don't even like blueberries.

Peacemaker is as good as it gets, and it will make you forget that you're in a land-locked state where good seafood is few and far between.

Pros:
-The long line moved very quickly 
-My husband liked his sweet potato pancakes 
-My bacon, although expensive, was tasty

Cons:
-The service wasn't very friendly, and she did everything she could to move us in and out (we hadn't even received a menu before she asked what we wanted). I know there's a line, but still, it wasn't welcoming. 
-The buttermilk pancakes were just ok. After two I just lost my interest in eating them, and it wasn't because I was full. They were underwhelming. I know buttermilk pancakes aren't exactly exiting to begin with, but still, good ones can usually captivate my attention long enough to to be eaten entirely

Moved from New York a few months ago and have been having a hard time finding good wings. My sister and a few friends stumbled upon this place and I am BEYOND pleased! I ordered wings and OMG so good!! Our server, Sydney, was amazing! We live not even 2 miles away and will DEFINITELY be back!
Service is always good and food is good a lot of flavor and presentation . Love the fried chicken

No problems here.  Picked up and had delivered a few times.  I like the on-line ordering system.  You can see the progress of your order.  No problems with the delivery person delivering at a reasonable time.  It's a Domino's... not much else to report except there are no problems, deliveries on time, food is fine.
Small but packs a punch on food and customer service! Yolanda is awesome and welcoming!

This is my first Wahoo's experience and I am glad to report that it was a good one! I had the fish taco combo plate with both kinds of rice and beans. It's really cool that they let you do that... most places would charge extra for this type of thing. I chose the blackened, spicy fish for the tacos and it was delicious! None of that battered fried mess here! The salsa was just right and I love that little bit that they put on top of the beans and rice. The cajun white beans were so flavorful. The black beans with the white rice went well together too. The brown rice was a little dry for my taste. Prices weren't bad either! I think my combo plate was $5.99.

I finally had a chance to have dinner at Poco and Mom's after hearing so much about it from several friends. I have to say, I was not disappointed. I am a big fan of spicy food and grew up eating it, so I was excited to try their hatch green chile sauce having had dishes with them at some other places around town. I decided to go with the combo plate since it was my first time and I was warned that it was a lot of food for just one meal. Knowing that, I still decided to go for it since I wasn't going to be sad about leftovers. 

The combo plate comes with a chicken enchilada in green sauce, a chile relleno in sour cream sauce, a shredded beef taco, and a generous helping of both rice and beans. The chile relleno was divine and the chicken enchilada was quite good too. I typically order enchiladas at Mexican places, so I'm glad I was able to try more than just that. I was not surprised by the fact that the hatch green chile sauce was actually fairly spicy. I loved it and am happy to see that they didn't make it milder by adding cream to satisfy more people's spice tolerance. The balance of the green and white sauces on the plate was also helpful since there was definitely a good amount of heat from the green sauce. I ended up taking my taco and much of my sides home as leftovers and they were still tasty the next day. I should mention that the price for the plate was only about $13, much less than a regular sized dish at other restaurants. I am looking forward to coming back to try their breakfast some time. 

I should also mention that I went early to put our names down for a table of 5 and I appreciate that they let you do so without your whole party present. I understand why many restaurants don't allow this, but given it's popularity, it would be sad to miss out on such great food due to reservation rules. We only had to wait 20 minutes for our table to be ready and the timing worked out great.
Lasagna is super good and the calamari is highly recomended. Our server was great. Kept the bread coming and the refills. Well be back soon.

I lived in the Central Coast for about 5 years and didn't step foot in a Cajun Kitchen until recently on a visit!  I know now what I've been missing!  I ordered the chilaquiles with their spicy sausage and it was so delicious! I just wish it had more avocado.  Otherwise, the chips with the sausage and scrambled eggs were a satisfying combination.  I missed out on the cornbread with the apple butter.. so I need to make a trip out to SB again!

I have been into Vietnamese food since 1982, when I had my very first dishes, "Bun Bo Xao" and "Cha Gio". Most places I have been since then have been a disappointment compared to that original, awesome experience. Kim Son is the first place I have been in a very long time that can compare to that very first meal. Hint: Always look for fresh mint on top of your Bun Bo Xao. If it isn't there .... then the restaurant doesn't really get it.

The breakfast burritos are amazing! You will potentially wait for hours if you go during a busy time because they take so many delivery orders and have very limited seating; however, it may well be worth the wait depending on your circumstances.

I hate the standard menu presentation. Treat me like a three year old who has never been to a steak house and I will leave a bad Yelp review. Overpriced and oversized. Take your extreme sized filet and eat it yourself. Be brave - cut the size in half and the price by a third. My dog does not need $70/pound left over filet.
Check out the asparagus - you think one half inch thick asparagus is a luxury - come on! Thin asparagus cooked correctly is much better.
The salad I had was nice. Maybe I had relaxed from the 10 minute presentation by then.

Me and my boyfriend decided to come here on a nice Friday evening. We knew that it it would be a long wait. We waited about 45 mins for a table. While waiting we decided to order 2 margaritas. The margaritas were good but the bartender irritated me. My boyfriend is from Philly so therefore he has a Pennsylvania ID. He tells my BF he never seen a PA ID and then proceeds to ask
him if he has another form of identification. Then he says nvm and serves us our margaritas. But I'm thinking in my head like are you kidding. It's a state ID what other form of ID would he have. But anyway so we finally sit down. Our waiter brings takes our order. The menu wasnt all that great i order garlic shrimp and some rice and beans my bf order some type of stewed beef with rice beans and we order empanadas. The empanadas came out about 20 mins after ordering. They were DISGUSTING!!! We then wait another 50 to an hour for our main dishes.  The food from 1-10 was a 4 i had way better Mexican food then this. I do not recommend this place to anyone. The food wasn't that great and the service there is horrible. This place is seriously overrated!!!

Whoever voted this place the best margaritas in Nashville came real close. They really do make a good one. My issue with this restaurant lied with the food. This is About the third time I've eaten there and I like to hold off judgement based on a bad experience or 2. This is no mistake though. The food just doesn't measure up to their great patio ambiance and margaritas. I've had an assortment of the usual Mexican fare there including chicken and beef enchiladas, tacos, flautas,  and all the usual fixings. Each was bland or dry or something just wasn't there. $10 Mexican food should be on par with the rest of this restaurants very impressive other exploits, but is not.

Hope your dish is better than mine, I'll be sitting at the bar next time.

Friendly staff, delicious coffee and yummy food (breakfast or lunch)! Staff comes outside to get your order in drive thru and keep line moving. Also the reward reloadable gift cards are great too because you get money back on it when you reach certain amount points.
Breakfast was excellent and service was very good. Also very easy to find. The portions was good you won't walk away hungry.

Newsflash!  Guido's serves more than Italian cuisine.  I just ate one of my favorite Spanish dishes, paella. It sounds like Pie A Uh.  Saffron rice with chicken, shrimp, scallops, and mussels.  Veggies include peasandgreen beans.  It takes 30 minutes to prepare so get a couple glasses of white wine to tide you over.  The new owners are from Madrid and they do this exactly the way it should be done.

When you get the menu be sure to look at both sides they are not Italian onl
Baja bowl with blackened chicken. Between this bowl and the cheesy beans and rice I cannot give it enough stars. Amazing food and portions for the price. So much flavor and greatness in both.

The best restaurant on the beach! We spent the day on the beach and walked up for lunch and it hit the spot! The Cuban nachos were amazing and the fish tacos did not disappoint! Atmosphere was great with live music to really give you all the vacation vibes. Service was also very good. Definitely a repeat customer.

REALLY GOOD crafted tacos! I had the pulled pork and a fried avacado, and they were both very good! The sauces and salsa have really nice flavor. I had elote, the corn on the cob, and it was okay. Unfortunately, I had to take my order to-go, so it didn't have a great texture to it. The big drawback to this place is obviously its wait; there's typically a line out the door, even on a weekday. So, you're probably best to go during a less busy time. It's Nashville famous, and definitely worth a try!

Best Indian food in town, brought my entire crew for lunch (most of them were first timer of Indian food exploration). And they all love it as much as I did! I'm a patron to this restaurant, been there  countless time, and I am never tired of their superb delicious food. I highly recommend this place! So what are you waiting for? Go for it!

Friendly staff, good space, tough to spot, so look for their "Victory" welcome mat.

Excellent rye whiskey recommendation from the bartender. Cajun pizza was good if you enjoy chicken on pizza.

Will visit again!

Best cookies to send ANYONE. They are definitely large homemade cookies that come fresh and soft. My roomies mom sent us some last year (08)....2 dozen mixed variety cookies. Since then this online store has been my first choice when sending baked goods anywhere in the country. Anytime I want a care package for any who is sick, boyfriend, back to school. I will get the cookies from here. Even if you can't finish them all at once just microwaving them for a few seconds make the cookies better then any other cookies you have ever eaten. I have shipped them to michigan, california, and many places in between.

First time I've had Nashville Hot Chicken in Tennessee.  That is definitely some bomb chicken, crispy, spicy and cooked to perfection.  I went with Cry Baby and that was enough spice for this guy.  I don't think you could pay me to try their Death Row.  Both the coleslaw and the potato salad were quite good as well.  My beer was cheap and the servers were helpful and kind.

This place is clean, and the employees are very kind and helpful.  If you are unfamiliar with banh mi or unsure what to order, the employees will help you make a decision.  One employee let me look at a booklet that had pictures of everything that goes into each sandwich.  What a great resource!  She told me which choices were the most popular, and I was happy with my meal.  (I had a chicken banh mi and a canned Sprite for $4.50.)
Note:  To use your debit/credit card, your bill must be at least $4.00.
This is my new sandwich place. Delicious quality sandwiches and a cool atmosphere. I recommend the smokehouse beef & cheddar brisket but add veggies!

You know how people act toward someone after they've said or done something blatantly offensive and it has gotten around the group what that person did? That's how I felt when I stepped up to the counter. Like, this is the first time you've laid eyes on me, what did I do? Damn. Everyone behind the counter seemed like everyone ordering had just cussed out their grandma. The burrito was good, but I don't really want to go back. It was really unpleasant.

This place is dope. Think of a Chatham Tap where the food tastes better, the prices are more affordable, you aren't judged on your beer choices and you don't have to grow a beard.

Da Beef is da bomb. I recommend adding mozzarella for a dollar more. You don't need a side. The sandwich is huge.

The staff is terrific. Very friendly and helpful. I don't know if Paula is the best server that I've ever had, but I can't remember having a better one.

Love this joint.
Best friggin' burger nearly ever. Got the XXX and sweet potato fries. I inhaled them. Fast and friendly service to boot.

We had dinner tonight and Ryan was our server. Wow is what I can say. He was so great, attentive to our needs, professional and extremely efficient. He was fun to be around and I will definitely request him on next visit. The food was great and it was a great dining experience

Excellent beer list.  That being said, the food is AWFUL.  Not one thing at our table didn't taste like it was frozen, processed, and/or super salty.  Not even good for pub food. How this place has 4 stars is beyond me.

I visited this place for lunch with my office colleague who recommended the place to me for its authentic wood-fired pizzas. The place had a warm, friendly ambience and was not too packed with people.

We skipped the appetizers and jumped straight onto the main course. I ordered the Chopped veggie pizza and my colleague ordered the Pepperoni, Sausage & Portobello pizza. The veggie pizza tasted delicious and the crust was amazing and fresh. The toppings complimented each other really well. 

The food was bang for buck. My only criticism about the place would be that I wish that the place had more veggie pizza options. (Only 1 option currently) Otherwise, a great dining experience. The staff was really friendly and courteuos.
They have it amazing shrimp n grits and their hot sauce is awesome. The server talked me into trying duck bacon which was delicious I have been coming here once a week ever since

We came here for restaurant week lunch. I love their pork belly and Barcalao croquetas. The most popular squid ink rice wasn't that good, too salty and no cheese flavor at all. Even my friend said it was as good as last time. Both desserts are good, churros was warm and soft, best ever! Overall, the meal was a good value

My wife and I ate here for the first time today. The curb appeal is awesome. Inside the restaurant was clean and inviting. The staff was very friendly. The service was awesome. We both ordered sandwiches. I had the bacon club and my wife had the chipotle sandwich. We also had soup and cookies. The food was fresh and delicious. We are now looking forward to going back and trying their breakfast offerings. Definitely five stars.
I've been 3 times now and honestly think the food is way overrated. Fun atmosphere and always crowded but the food is average, maybe a half-step above average, at best.
The view the view THE VIEW! Panoramic view of the city was beautiful at night. I enjoyed the atmosphere and decor. Service was great, enjoyed my drink "sweater weather."

We had a great dinner at Provision. They had several delicious cocktails on their menu. My favorite was "Off to the Races" which was a bourbon drink. I had a filet mignon for dinner which was cooked perfectly. I thoroughly enjoyed the bacon potato terrine which was very spicy. Great atmosphere but prices are high. Great for a date or business dinner. They have outdoor seating.

We got a winner by accident! The night we went here, I made the reservation thinking it was another restaurant my hubby told me to book a table at. When we got there he was a little disappointed that I'd gotten the booking wrong but at that point we'd driven all the way out from Philly and had no other prospects. Thank Goodness! This place was crazy family busy and friendly. There was a large party of at least 12 people plus 3 kids when we entered so we felt comfortable bringing our two dolls in without worrying about prejudiced staff. The server, whose name I remembered until now, was an awesome young woman of 20 years that had put her years of food service to good use. Attentive and polite and intelligent she was always a pleasure to see coming to the table (she kept bringing food!) and my daughter loved her. Now to the food... pastas aren't made in-house but ARE handmade by another pro off premises. The sauces are clean and exactly what you expect when you order chicken piccata, angel hair with red sauce, or the amazing starter with white beans, broccoli rabe, and Italian sausage that my girl ate nearly every bite of (I ate 1/3 as soon as I saw her going in hard). The dishes were all hot, the server kept an eye on our progress like a hawk and made sure we needed nothing. Man, I wish it was closer so we could go more often. I'd honestly eat here two to three times a month if they were more accessible to Philly. Meanwhile, they're not. So pick I nice day to drive, make your reservation, and take bottles to pop. Yes. That's right. They're BYOB. Major plus in my book.

First time here, and we are already planning on when we can come back with friends and family! Ambience is amazing, great for groups or intimate seating for two. Our waiter Norbert was very personable and attentive, and the music done by Kayla and Alex (now here every Monday night) set such a great mood for our date night!

I had the Beef Poutine and my wife had the Blue Nachos -- both were excellent, but I'd choose the nachos as well next time! The bleu cheese adds so much flavor!

I'm always happy when I leave El Gato Negro. The table side guacamole is delicious and they have quirky margarita flavors like cilantro pineapple, along with a wall containing every tequila ever invented. So have fun and eat up, you'll definitely leave with a full belly. Olé!

The food is bad - the gumbo is watery, salty and tastes like a supermarket mix, and the "fra diavlo" sauce tastes like nothing more than catsup and pepper. The place is a dump and the bathroom disgustng. To add insult to injury, the prices are high like fine restaurants with good food. If I could have, I would have rated it a "0".

I am glad to see they closed; this place was the worst ripoff in New Orleans!
Pre check in before u arrive!! Good food and nice environment!! Chicken and waffles were good!! I purchased the ham and mushroom crepe and it was good .

Awesome place. With great potential. Came in for the opening and as they settle in they will get their service in and process so be patient. The food overall was awesome. We walked in and greeted with the cheddar hot link taste so I would consider it in the future. In terms of the food, I had the ribs, brisket, and pulled pork. ORDER THE PORK STEAK. Thats what they are known for and it will not dissapoint. The brussels were outstanding, the mac was great, and honestly didnt even get to the beans. Come get it.

Got a strong craving for a good steak?  Don't go here!  Horrible service, and the food is lousy.  My steak was too rare, and when the waitress took it back to heat it a bit, she must have taken a nap as well.  She was nowhere to be found, and when we finally did stumble upon her, she was annoyed that we asked about the steak.  Brought it back, and it was cooked to jerky!  And it was cold, which meant it was sitting around waiting for the waitress to swing by.  This is the third time we've given this place the chance to do it right, but now we're just wasting our money.  Too many other great restaurants in the area to suffer through this place.  Moving on....
Love this place ! Try the ziggy burger and or the crispy hip city ranch. :) staff is super friendly and always answers questions in a courteous manner. Keep up the good work :)

I had a coupon for a 2 for 1 deal for lunch.  Usually we don't eat lunch out but I had a bit of shopping to do at Safeway so it seemed like a good opportunity to get the deal.  I must say the system they have is really good.  The manager is the one who took our order.  I have seen him many times before and he has always been very pleasant.  It came within 5 min. and was tasty.  I had the lox, cream cheese with fresh capers, red onion on a toasted bagel.  Hubby had the turkey, bacon, mayo. Both were good.  For me the  prices are high for a lunch.  It would have been over 15 bucks for lunch but with the coupon we both enjoyed our lunch for 7 bucks.  Can't beat this deal.  Was so full, we had no dinner that night.

Stop reading and just order the damn meatloaf sandwich already. De nada. 

Shy away from the fish tacos. They are dry and the fish was charred - not blackened, charred. Tastes like burning.

This is the second time I have returned to Termini Brothers Bakery inside the Reading Terminal Market. Their best seller which is the cannoli is worth the 1 & 1/2 hr. drive from where I live. This time, aside from the customary order of cannoli, we tried some of their other offerings i.e. - their mini cakes 1) Limoncello cake & 2) Red Velvet cake. They were heavenly! The cakes were moist, decadent & not overly sweet. Needless to say, you cannot just stop at one bite (they were history before we even got out of the Reading Terminal Market). This review however is for the "pecan bar". Had to make sure I had to get some this visit. It did not disappoint. This pecan bar was heavenly, just the right amount of sweetness, texture & moistness. I am so glad I got more than one. I will most surely try other pastries they offer next visit. Definitely in my must visit list when traveling back to Philly. This place is highly recommended.

We had Sunday brunch at Ricky P's today. It was our first time.  The waitress recommended the Ricky P's Eggs Benedict.  If you try it you won't be disappointed.  The crab cakes were great.  The beignets were good but not outstanding. We certainly will be back.

Was hesitant to go due to some of the reviews but wanted to return to a place that had many family memories growing up in the area. 
Arrived early to have a drink at the bar and enjoy watching customers come and go in the lounge. The mixed drink was $11 but it was a good drink. Most of the patrons were older and seemed to have also enjoyed manny friends and family meals at the Pub over the years.
Entered the massive dining room and seated, and everything flowed great. Salad Bar was gigantic, and everything was fresh. (Caesar salad was popular and fantastic). We ordered the Managers Cut Prime Rib and Bourbon Steak and both came out perfect, as ordered. I had made up my mind to send it back, based on previous reviews, if it didn't come out right, but no need.
Service was great and handled by Patty and an attentive Bus server, all the Pubs fixins made the meal more enjoyable. Hope some younger family's give it a try to start their own traditions....as my memories have always been great times going there.
Final thoughts:
Ambiance- Cool wide open space that is clean and well decorated for the Holiday
Prices- they are above average compared to some chains, but the food is good, portions are large. 
Service- had no issues and waitress was attentive but not over bearing. 
Food- thought the taste and quality matched the price and atmosphere. 
Give it a try and if you haven't been, start your own family traditions! (Your kids will have the size and decorations in the massive dining room engrained forever in their minds).

Went there with a large group (17 people). They handled our group beautifully and split the checks with no difficulty. 

Be sure to try both oyster appetizers - bbq and on the half shell - I can't decide which one I like better!

My friends and I went to Coop's at the recommendation of our hotel concierge and left with mixed feelings. We ordered the pasta jambalaya (9.95) and the seafood gumbo with extra seafood (11.95). The seafood gumbo was lukewarm, not very flavorful, and had very little seafood even though we ordered extra seafood. The portion was also extremely small considering its price. However, the pasta jambalaya was really good, so definitely try that out if you planning on visiting this restaurant.
Average as fuck. Nothing stand out about the food. Good enough to eat but not go out of your way for by any means

Great beer! Phoenixville is becoming heavily saturated with breweries (which is great for me) and this one is up at the top. The service is a little spotty and slow but they're brand new and going through growing pains. The beer quality was great though and the variety was pretty good too. I think they had 8 on tap already and are only like a month old. 
If you like breweries you should check this one out!

I rarely give anything less than 3 stars, so I feel like I should explain why!  I did some research before eating here, and everything I read gave it rave reviews.  Also, it was pretty hard to get in to (we made reservations 5 days ahead of time and still had to settle for 5:30 pm).  Needless to say, I was pretty pumped to eat here and had really high expectations.  I had a couple glasses of the Pinot Noir, which were good, but everything else was just mehh.  We ordered a bunch of small plates, and I felt like everything was just too rich, creamy, and salty for me.  After the small plates, I had the kale salad, and that is when I started to feel really WOOF.  I don't know if it was the rich food, too much kale (which can do a number on your stomach because of all the fiber, I suppose), or what...but I felt absolutely awful after eating here.  I don't know if it was food poisoning or something else (my husband reported that his stomach hurt awhile later too), but now I can't even picture the food I ate without wanting to spew.  Maybe I should give it one star, but I save that for places where I had a terrible experience - the service here was fine and our waitress was attentive.  All I can say is that I will not be eating anything involving garlic aioli or lots of butter for a long, long time!
Very very good service was great owner was very caring clean I would high recommend this place support local is always good

this place is incredible! everything is so so so good! and vegan to boot! get the dim sum, you wont regret it. you can stuff your face til you are absolutely sure you are going to burst, but you will feel so good you'll swear you could run a marathon. my top picks are the wonton soup, the pork buns, the pineapple chicken, the fried bananas & the cheesecake (any flavor, all the flavors!). ming is the best & he deserves your business!

I was all excited to try this place because of all the great reviews and vegan options but it was a huge disappointment. The service was downright awful and the food just like two deserts for a meal so sugary! The kitchen was beautifully laid out and bathrooms fun. Some interesting plants in front! 

Smell: All I smelled was fried grease throughout the place and I am probably certain I smelled like it when I left. They desperately need to air it out. Breathing it was difficult for the first 20 min till I got used to it. 

Service: My dish did not come out till after every single person who had arrived after me got theirs! No apologies, no explanations, just a mention that my food was coming.  I got my salad, then my partner ate by himself and then when he was done my meal finally arrived and I ate by myself. That is unacceptable. How does everyone who was seated after me have their food, my partner is done with his and I still don't have mine!? The waitress had little personality and never made me feel welcome. It wasn't unwelcome but more apathy than anything. It gets worse...

Food: Well I love the creativeness of the food! Aloe, goji berries in my salad but it was spicy and no mention of that on the menu. Had to have it remade.  My waitress said without the fish sauce it would not be spicy. Remade it was still not really palatable. It was super sweet like candy even the aloe was marinated in sugar sauce and the carrots were just large curls and took forever to chew! Raw carrots need to be grated or chopped smaller to break down instead of 6 X 1 inch curls. It was big and I was too tired to chew through it all. Cucumbers were just ok.  I couldn't wait to eat something soft and savory.

Then I got the Buddha stir fry. It's not on the menu. Again, all I taste is sugar. I know that's a popular way to make food and others love it, but it should say these things on the menu spicy, sweet, savory etc. I'm sorry I didn't think to ask but I thought if a food doesn't taste like the food description they ought to let us know so we don't have a surprise on our hands and have to send it back. That much sugar is not an enhancement it's the main focus.  Another issue I did not like was the veggies were hardly cooked at all in the stir fry. They were essentially raw.  The food needs a bigger plate or a rim so it's not falling off and then you don't get to mix your rice and veggies to your own proportions it's just a huge premixed lump on your plate and takes forever to chew through the sugary raw veggies. Is it supposed to be that way? Gross...

I just have a feeling that my order was forgotten and made too quickly. 

My partner had the General Lee's chicken just said it was ok. He didn't clean the bones off or anything, in fact they gave him a to go container for what was left and he didnt even use it. 'I can't comment on it, but I'm surprised to hear such great reviews about it. 

Then waitress asked if we want desert. Smh, no thanks I just had two. Between the smell, the taste and the awful service I doubt I'll ever go back. Oh and they don't have non-alcoholic drinks on the menu. I love my beer but during the day I want something healthier. You have to ask for non-alcoholic items and all they have are iced tea and coke or they can "make" you a lemonade. The way she said it feels like you're asking them a favor. I'm not one for sweets as you can tell. Would have liked hot tea with my Chinese food or a Perrier, filtered water, coffee...we settled on tap water with our meal.

We spent just over $40 and would have rather gone to one of the authentic neighborhood  to go places where they have great customer service, make your food to order, it's cheaper and faster and tastes like what you expect.  I'll definitely spend more for healthier foods but not when it's sugar laden.

Have loved this restaurant for years but this is the first time we tried their sushi. 

It was amazing. The Baked Salmon roll was by far the best. Great service, awesome food, and an all around perfect experience. 

Chris was our sushi chef and he was attentive and had great humor. And obviously- an amazing chef. 

We were surprised though that he was the only chef at the bar. It seemed like a lot of work for only one chef. 

We have read reviews about the bar being slow and having rude staff. That was not our experience. Obviously cooked rolls take longer but other than that everything came out in a timely manner. Madison was our server and she was very attentive and sweet. 

Also, local discount with an ID!
I'd the best shrimp sandwich ever, and would definitely recommend it, if you haven't tried it already. With a strong peber flavour, but not too spicy.

The food and service are decent. We came for lunch on a Sunday afternoon after walking our dogs along Hendrys Beach. The patio out front was filled with anxious, barking dogs waiting for their owners, so we decided to leave the dogs in the car (hey it's early January!) and we waited about 10-20 minutes for a table. The place was packed but we got a table next to the window, which was great because the restaurant is with the visit mainly for its view. We got the Seafood Pasta ($18.50) and a Lobster Roll (~$16-18). The pasta was delicious but came with a side of bread that was half burnt, and pretty oily, which I was not a fan of. The lobster roll was average size, topped with sliced avocado. The lobster was mixed with several different ingredients so it wasn't purely lobster, which was alright but not preferable. Overall the atmosphere and the service are good enough, and the food is above average. A good place for brunch or a laid back meal after walking along the beach, or somewhere to take your parents.

I want to give The Gold Standard 3.5 stars, but I can't go up to 4. They have a great location in west Philly with some nice outdoor and indoor seating.  When approaching, I noticed a sign saying to walk in to see the host for outdoor seating.  We went inside to the counter but everyone kind of ignored us for a minute before telling us to just find a table outside.   

The servers were nice, though they seemed a bit unorganized since different people came up to ask us if we've been helped yet.  As for the food, I ordered an iced coffee and the potato chorizo hash.  The iced coffee was good, though I never got a chance to get another because the servers didn't stop by until the end.  The hash was very good.  It was a bit saucy and had man soft textures for my taste, but definitely had some nice flavors overall.

SAMMICHES!!!! They're great...got a killer cheesesteak....the combo comes with  seasoned fries and a drink ....pretty affordable and never disappoints...they've got other food as well like fried chicken (not bad) and the cuban pork (awesome).  Lunch crowd is busy, but they're still pretty quick...their meat prices aren't too bad as well and they have a huge variety of spices and sauces for sale as well.
If you want bad food, and even worse service this is the place for you. Everything we ordered was just so, so even the salsa.

We went here last night. Party of 4. Only waited about 20 minutes@ 6:30 on a Saturday night. Not bad. The place was very crowded and slightly disorganized. However our waitress was very good and we started out with the Vodka squareee pizza for an appetizer . It was excellent. 2 of our party got the chicken parmigiana over rigatoni. I have to say that it was the worst chicken parmigiana that I've ever had. It was either freezer burned or just way overcooed. The other two meals were just average. I would just stick to the pizza there. But I will come back because it's a nice atmosphere, nothing fancy btw. But overall a descent place.

Great spot for Sunday brunch. We were sat immediately, which is always a positive. The servers were extremely polite and kind. Our drinks were delicious and the food was great. 
I personally ordered the Petite Filet with the truffle scrambled eggs, was the perfect portion. My fiancé ordered their famous BBQ shrimp, very tasty but were a tad over cooked, was very difficult to remove the shells. When we mentioned it to our server she was very nice and even offered a complimentary dessert. Also ordered at the table were the Eggs Benedict and the Fried Oyster Sliders, they were also enjoyed very much. A tad expensive for breakfast but it was all very good. 
To finish our meal we ordered the Bread Pudding....amazing, also the White Chocolate Brownie was very good!! Overall a great experience. 

Keep in mind they also have live music for Sunday brunch!

Food was meh, pretty good. Burger was crumbly but otherwise good flavor. Lovely atmosphere. Everything took forever, staff seemed very disorganized. Our pie, right out of the fridge, took 30 minutes? Best of luck guys, but please get your act together. These high prices do NOT match quality. 
P.S please work on presentation! Food does not look very appetizing.
Burgers are simple but good. Very tasty. The fries are crisp on the outside but soft inside.

The customer service was impeccable!!! The manager greeted us upon entry and made us feel very welcomed. The burritos are huge, enough to split with two people if you wanted to. The shredded beef had a hickory twist to it, and the shredded pork tasted mild with a hint of lime. Overall great food and very filling.
Had their country fried steak and eggs with a biscuit. The food was delicious and their doughnuts were AMAZING!! Will definitely be back!
Bachelor Party, they went above and beyond to make us feel like royalty, we loved it!

Three star buffet that I definitely would recommend to others who are in town and looking to feast like a beast. But don't be a fool and pay the full dinner price, get yourself a free players card with the Grand Sierra Resort to get the discounted dinner price of $11.99. 

What you'll find here are salads, soups, Mexican, Chinese, Italian, Seafood (cooked fish, crab legs, shrimp, no sushi though), Meats (prime rib, beef ribs, turkey), and desserts.

The best stuff I liked had to be the shrimp and prime rib. Wow that prime rib was impressively good. Tender, good taste, and when I asked for medium rare, I actually got medium rare. 

I'd recommend staying away from the desserts though. Our party of 6 all agree that the desserts were pretty gross.

We had a party of 22 and the service was great. They handled our party and multiple other parties at the same time with no issues. The food was delicious. We had the Ahi tuna, bang bang shrimp, and crab cakes. All of it was amazing.  Will Def keep going back!

I was visiting a mourning friend in Philly & this is where we ended up for dinner. I loved the dining room! It was warm, cozy & classy with a rustic charm & nice big windows. The waitstaff was attentive & friendly and the food was quite good.

BUT

Go for the cheese plate! The cheeses were lovely but the reason to travel to this restaurant is the truffle honey. This stuff is like crack! It's wonderful mild honey speckled with tons of REAL truffle shavings. It was so decadent , so rich, so wonderful...words cannot describe the awesomeness of this sensual delight. Just go get that damn cheese plate!

They have amazingly good drinks and the bartenders were cute and friendly. She made sure my drinks were sweet enough for my taste and strong enough for my likens. 
The food however was disappointing. I get it how they want it to be upscale so it's very pricey, however the potions are ridiculous small and to be honest there were no taste(I had to add salt to every dish). To start off we had the oysters, tartar, and a salad. Oysters were literally just thrown on the ice, because it was still sandy and poorly presented. Tartar was good since it's deer meat which is something I've never had before but the portion was so small I ate it within 6 mouth bites. And the salad was so tasteless it's so sad. 
The entree we decided to go with the specials of the night, seafood and Wagyu because there was nothing special on the menu. And that was a terrible mistake! The meat came out hard and chewy I literally thought I was eating a beef jerky. 
I understand it's a nice elegant place but for the portion and the way they present the food, I rather dine at urban farmer for a much better quality food and won't be disappointed with the bill later in the evening.

This was a great little sub shop to eat at.  I was on the ground with a friend while at the county building during a ground stop away from MacDill AFB, and we saw this place.  I ordered the meatball sub, and it was the best I've had so far.  Definitely eat at this place; I highly recommend this restaurant.
Love the rootbeer!  More sweet than spicy, but very tasty.  Onion rings were huge, and our puppy appreciated being able to join us for lunch.

The food here is good, but the buck stops there. I think most people know that Popeye's is probably one of the slowest fast food places out there. However, this location tops the cake. I will only go here if there's a maximum of 2 cars in the drive through. 

Recently, I placed an order in the app for curbside pickup (due to COVID 19). The app informed me to park in a spot and that my food would be brought out. I waited about 10 minutes and an employee came out to say that I had to go through the drive through. I told him the app said I could park and asked if they could bring my food out. He said no. There were at least 15 cars in the drive through and I refused to go sit in that line. I would have never placed the order if I knew I had to do that. I then asked if I could get a refund and he went back in to ask the manager. He came out and told me I had to request it through the app. Well...there's no way to request a refund through the app. I just left and sent an email and tried disputing with my bank. Thankfully I was refunded in about a week. The entire experience was ridiculous. The app shouldn't give an option if the local store isn't going to acknowledge it.

1) Hella uncomfortable seats. Equivalent of plastic stools.
2) No outlets
3) Wi-fi slow AF
4) Cuties

Service here was horrible it took us at least 10 minutes to get our drink order taken and then another 20 for them to ask what we wanted to eat. There were only 3 groups of people in here including us and that is ridiculous! It is also very annoying that they dont give you their 2,4,6,8 menu and that you have to ask for it. Makes it seem like they dont want you to order from it.

I love going to this buffet because there is always so many different choices to choose from. I like to go through all the bars and take a little bit of everything. I usually start with the rice and noodles with vegetables and meat, before making my way to the seafood. Crab legs and shrimp are my favorite seafoods here. I also love the chocolate fountain. I usually dip the strawberry and bananas in it when i finish with my food. They also have a HUGE selection of ice creams! Mint chip is always the way to go for me though! 

One of the main reasons I choose this chinese buffet is because of the large selection available. I usually come with my family, and my sister is a vegetarian while the rest of us arent. So while we go for all the meats and seafoods, she can still enjoy the chinese vegetables and fruits.

I ate lunch with a group of ladies recently on a Saturday afternoon, and we had a great experience.  We checked the Yelp app and saw that they had no wait list, and we were pleased to be seated right away upon arriving. Our waiter was courteous and provided great service.  The food was excellent, and we all enjoyed dessert.  This is an iconic art eco St. Louis restaurant that is a must for out of town visitors and St. Louis natives alike.

After moving from New York last year, I have been searching for my new local slice shop. While Alice pizza is far from your typical NYC-style slice, it has won a place in my heart for top pizza and philly restaurants. 

As other reviewers mentioned, the pizza is what I think of as Italian style - super crispy crust and baked in square pans with fun toppings. The best thing is that they sell it by the ounce, so you can try multiple types of pizza. My (vegetarian) favorites? The potato pizza and the (spicy) bruschetta pizza.

The service is great. The first time I came, I ate it take-away, thinking there wouldn't be enough space to sit. Not only do they have a table service portion of the restaurant, but they have ~10-15 bar style seats as well for those who want to enjoy the pizza in a more casual environment. When I was sharing 4 slices with my SO, they cut each piece in half and came and brought it over to our table (after talking us through the merits of each slice as we struggled what to decide to eat).

For those who love pizza or are just trying to find a cozy / casual neighborhood joint, make Alice (uh-lee-chey) pizza one of your next stops.
Everyone is so friendly. Food is delicious. My 9yr old loves it here. Eat outside !! It's beautiful.

Gave it a try with the family during a weekend stay at Fantasyland Hotel at West Edmonton Mall.  I have to say that it was a very pleasant experience, both with great food and excellent service.  You won't go wrong bringing the family here, and the great thing was that it wasn't as long a wait for a table as it was at most of the other places on Bourbon Street in WEM.  Would definitely recommend!

I was a regular here for the first few months of school - that is, before I found better places nearby.

I hate to give this place a poor review.  The service is almost always incredibly friendly.  They're all such nice people.  I just don't think the food is amazing.  It's certainly better than the places on campus where I can spend dining dollars, but there are places with much better food for less money.

(I must say before I continue that their tuna hoagies, grilled cheese sandwiches, and fries are A+, and that I enjoyed the cheese ravioli dinner.)

My friends and I used to go here for breakfast all the time, and it was a pretty good idea, since the portions are so ridiculously large that I could eat two eggs and a third of the stack of pancakes and have plenty of leftover pancakes for the next morning.  However, the only reasons to come to this place for breakfast rather than another place (which shall remain nameless) on the other side of campus are 1. they serve breakfast all day, and 2. they're less far to walk.  It's a lot of money for not a lot of quality.

I'm not sure I'd say the pizza is "terrible", and I certainly wouldn't say it tastes like frozen pizza.  It's certainly not the best I've had, but it's kind of like most of the other food here - acceptable.

We recently got jamba juice delivered and the açaí bowl my friend got looked just like it should but myself and another friend got the vanilla blue sky bowl and it was literally soup with hardly any toppings. 2 blueberries, 3 strawberries, and a tiny sprinkle of granola and coconut on mine. Very disappointed, especially for $9.

Self serve coffee, hazelnut. Yea!  I got the Cuban "sandwich". There was this wonderful jalapeño sauce on the side, thank goodness.  Otherwise the sandwich is without a lot of flavor.  On another note - I'm really glad that Gregg M and I share - his sandwich was absolutely mouthwateringly delicious!  Did I mention the self-serve coffee?

Okay, this place is my mother's favorite. And I can definitely taste why. Their curry and coconut infused flavors in their food are REAL authentic Thai ingredients, not that nonsense from a jar. Literally the real deal and no shortcuts. Real Thai food has strong tasting aroma, that's easy to differentiate from easy Thai commercial cuisine. While I did enjoy my Coco ave noodle soup, I kind of felt like there was more to be desired. I wished they gave more soup than a ton of noodles (I just felt like I ate more noodle carbs than anything) because the soup base was fragrant and addicting. For the price of $14-$15 for that big bowl, you think it's worth it. It kind of is... but maybe next time I need to ask for more soup and cut back on the carbs. Then, it would be worth it. I guess I also wish they could have a little more variety and other choices with the food selection. One day, hopefully the menu can expand. Another thing was their price, seemed a slight bit steep on some of the items in the menu. The flavors and authenticity of the ingredients partially make up for that though. Next time I want to try other things for sure.

First time at Pancake Pantry yesterday (Tuesday)! Got to the restaurant a little after 9am and was seated right away. I was so surprised as I have read the lines can go around the block. After I left around 10:30 was when that happened. 

A friend and I shared the banana bread pancakes and the Georgia peach pancakes. Both were very good! The banana bread pancakes are not as sweet if your looking for something more mild to start your day. They have cinnamon inside as well as walnuts. The Georgia peach came will slices of peaches and a peach sauce on top. All in all good service and very good variety of pancake choices
The best pizza in Ybor! Be sure to stop by this little gem! The pizza is fabulous and the customer service can't be beat.

always loved this place but this week came and order a flank steak had good flavor but all the food we ordered was COLD so disappointed cause we really enjoy the place and one more thing IF HORCHATA SELLS ALOT WHY YOU DONT MAKE ENOUGH  LIKE SERIOUSLY!!!hope i have a better experience, Next time hagan mas Horchata no mamen!!!

This is the best meat and three I've found. The tortilla soup is amazing. Baked tilapia is perfectly cooked every time and seasoned to perfection. Both the green beans and the turnip greens are packed full of flavor. Friday's hobo surf-n-turf is a must for you catfish lovers. You get a half order of catfish and half order of another meat. I could go on and on but this is a place you just have to try. I eat here about once a week and it never gets old.

I understand we ordered a pizza before they closed, however, I called and ordered through the gentleman because I thought they were closed but he placed my order etc. I asked for half pepperoni half cheese since my boyfriend doesn't eat pork, and the "manager" Sydney was a complete bitch.

Owner is a lousy person, greedy and a liar!
While I was ordering my two breakfast burritos and about to pay, the owner came up and whispered in the cashiers ear that one of the burritos was 1$ more, the cashier questioned his boss because he thought breakfast burritos were cheaper, but he ushered him to continue, I said nothing and continued the transaction until I could have a chance to question the owner when he gave me the order. When questioned about it he denied trying to hide it from me and refused a refund even despite the menu's bad representation of prices and what is included in those. I will never go back and neither will my friends, we will take our business to La Michoacana for half price breakfast burritos that are larger and taste better.

FINALLY a well-prepared and enticing meal was to be had in Santa Barbara! We opted for this fine dining coastal cuisine restaurant for our first dinner of 2010 and I am so glad we did.  First off, the service was really nice. We decided to sit out on the heated patio and even though it was a little chilly outside, it was quite warm on the patio.  We were surrounded with white lights and candle light which added to the romantic tones of the restaurant.

We had a very friendly and attentive waitress as well as a friendly and attentive hostess who sometimes helped out the waitress in providing us with exceptional service. They started us off with a basket of freshly baked sourdough bread and homemade butter. This basically melted off my tongue. DELICIOUS.  Then this was followed with a citrus flavored palate cleanser which came compliments of the chef.  Nice touch!

Our first course was the pacific oysters which as soon as they came out, we were immediately taken with the amazing scent of freshness that came from this dish. They were accompanied with a nice garlicy dipping sauce that accented the taste of the oysters perfectly. After this course, we knew we were in for an amazing main course.

I opted for the kobe beef ribeye which came with potato gnocchi, chanterelle mushrooms, spinach and bordelaise sauce. I had it medium-rare.  When my main course finally arrived I was just taken by the presentation and oh my goodness, the flavors! This dish was prepared with love and you can tell.  I loved how all the flavors blended so well in my mouth and the meat was absolutely incredible!  I could not have been happier with this meal!

I highly recommend Seagrass if you are ever in Santa Barbara and want to try some local coastal cuisine. You will not be disappointed and I could not have asked for a better meal to kick off the start of what I hope to be a great year!
The beer selection here was great.  They have great rotation and some options that are difficult to find on tap.  Food was great too, overall a good time.

This is one of my favorite restaurants when I visit New Orleans. Although there are several places to eat in New Orleans , I've been here twice just for the New Orleans BBQ Scallop Fettuccine. Oh my! This meal is delicious and the scallops are fresh and prepared just right. The customer service is nice, too.

Our first time at any Flowing Tide Pub, and it was okay. I'm mostly judging on the food and drinks for the price. The fish in my fish and chips was a little hard, but the ranch and tartar sauce dips were good, and the fries were passable. My margarita was a bit weak and very sweet. 

Our waitress was friendly and working hard all night. We sat in the non-smoking family section but could still smell smoke. Pubs aren't necessarily my kind of place but I could see it being a hangout spot for locals.

The food was good. We had the antipasti appetizer, the spaghetti bolognese, and a burger. All the food was good. Including the House sangria. It wasn't heavy. It was light and refreshing. This place isn't to expensive, either. In addition, the ambiance is nice and the background music (Frank Sinatra, Harry Conick, Jr.) made the meal even more enjoyable. Two thumbs up for this place!!! I will be retiring, with friends!!!

I must say this. My first 2 visits was completely very satisfying. My third visit was my last visit. The employee was chewing on a straw. Taking orders,dealing with cash an cards. An going back an forth in the kitchen. Look like he had been chewing on it for hours. Great food but I have to pass.
The wait time is insane but the food was delicious. The grits alone made the wait worthwhile

I went here recently on a Wednesday night, not sure what to expect.  The thai places in this city can be hit or miss, and beyond Circles, I'm not the biggest fan of many of them.  However, Sawatdee made me very happy.  The interior is a beautiful green color, and very warm and inviting.  We arrived at around 6:30 / 6:45 for dinner - with our own beer (BYOB).  We were seated right away, however about 15 - 20 minutes after we arrived, almost all the tables were completely filled.  They stored my friends stroller in the back for them, and provided us with a high chair for the wee one.
