Had heard about this place from family and friends, its their favorite place to go. Went the 1st time on a Monday for lunch. The staff was so nice and helpful, offering to explain everything and help with changing things up as needed! They also never let our drinks get below half with out bringing a new one. We were seated and given chips and salsa, the chips were wonderful and fresh made my husband loved the salsa, I prefer pico de gallo and it was more saucy but very good. We started with the tejas chicken and with a suggestion from the waiter got hot tortilla's with it. The tortilla's were wonderful on their own but wrapped around a tender buffalo strip was devine. My husband chose the chicken burro with jambalaya on the side, both were delicious. So delicious in fact he has said at every meal since he wish he had it on the side! I had the tacos combo 1 beef, 1 chicken. They were both great! I had french fries on the side and they were wonderful, shoestring, crisp and tasty like a cross between a fresh homemad potato chip and french fry. And they were piled so high I couldnt finish them and I could eat french fries for breakfast. We shared a side of corn bread which was warm and sweet. Can't wait to try more. The best tex-mex we have had in a very long time. Will be going back, soon I hope!!!

Come here if you want your food with a huge dash of COVID-19. It is so sad because their food is good, but literally no one wears masks properly. They just sport the masks chin-diaper style with the mask pulled waaaaay below their faces exposing their nose and mouth. Go to Craft Fry instead much more precautions are taken and everything is better. Why go to a restaurant that doesn't value your health/safety? You are literally giving people money to make you sick....think about it.

Since my last review we have been living near this little restaurant for several years. I wrote the first review after my first or second visit and my opinion has greatly improved. we love the staff they always know our name and are always very pleasant it's definitely a family ran business and community-oriented. My fiance loves fried zucchini and garlic fries to start with. I love their Alfredo which initially I didn't care for it was because it was slightly different but they add what I believe to be as a touch of nutmeg which is really fantastic. I don't really care for their chicken so I just order a alfredo with no meat. They also have a special which is often on the menu or at least as an option of a green chili carbonara and it is really great and my fiance loves that option as well. the lasagna is always a favorite of people that goes in I'm not a huge fan of red sauce but it is a very large portion and quite good, this is coming from someone that doesn't really care for red sauce. it is a little bit pricey but you have to consider they are the only ones in the area. I believe that Alfredo is $17 and the lasagna is similarly priced. They do have several dessert options and I believe all of the desserts come from Phoenix. They recently did a remodel and the restaurant looks great and I'm glad that they are doing so well.

I just moved to Reno and was hoping a Chinese food place delivered and came across this place and placed my order. Good thing I didn't see the reviews for this place before hand or I would have been dissuaded.
As far as the delivery the gentleman was kind, friendly and didn't take long to arrive at my door.
The food was great to be perfectly honest. The steamed dumplings were amazing! Hot and steamy and full of flavor, so delicious. The beef & broccoli actually had beef! Not just loaded with broccoli, don't get me wrong, I love broccoli but when I order beef & broccoli I want beef too and some places don't give you a lot of beef. The beef was soft and tender, flavorful and the broccoli was blanched perfectly. The combination fried rices was fantastic I'm a plain white rice guy I'm not big on fried rice but this was beyond delicious! It was so much better the next day to be honest. The wonton soup was simple but full of flavor, it was the best I've had so far, the wontons' were made perfect, and held together so nicely. I LOVED the chow mein as well, the combination was delicious! And was the first thing to go in my house! It was the perfect texture! I plan on ordering from then soon! ... like as soon as I'm done with this review soon!

First, I'll say this is an interesting space... multi-purpose dining... house?

I don't know... judging from some of the other photos here I may have missed out. My challah french toast definitely didn't look that exciting in comparison. It was cool for what it was, but honestly not too memorable. The sausage and eggs I had were pretty standard too. I suppose, most of all I liked the dining experience as I'm rarely in Powelton Village for anything. It was an early weekday morning so the waiting that other people mention wasn't an issue for me. We were seated no problem.

And to all the Drexel med school girls, I noticed you noticing me and I just wanted to put you on notice that... I noticed you too.

And to Sabrina, it's not you it's me.

Looked online for top BBQ reviews and saw this one. Decided to head on down to try it out. 

Place was very quiet for a Friday at happy hour time. Expected to have to wait but walked right in to the order counter. Food came out very fast which is nice since no one was here. 

Had the ribs and two sides. The mac and cheese was very good. The beans fair at best. Maybe adding some pork or meat would make them seem more traditional for a BBQ place. The ribs smeared in seasoning were just ok. Not a lot of meat on them. Seasoning leaves your hands all red from it. Can't say would hurry back to eat. When a side dish is the best thing going for a place it's kind of sad.

So after raving about your food to our family we all ordered over $100 in JUST burgers and fries for dinner one weekday evening    --your burgers were dry shiveled versions of the buttery soft ones we previously enjoyed, the truffle fries were limp water logged barely covered in what you call aioli (not at all worth $11)..and that left 4 people still hungry and pissed at me for ever having vouched for you:(
Ordered a burger, which was supposed to be "to die for". Let's just say, I didn't die. I was disappointed.

At 26 years old, I should be able to have a beer with my seafood, no problem, right?  WRONG.  I was in town from NY visiting my cousin who lives in St. Pete.  We went to lunch here and I ordered a beer.  After giving the waitress my id, she asked for backup ID.  No problem, here's my credit card with my name.  Nope, that still wasn't good enough.  OK, here's my library card.  Nope. Still not ok.  They asked me for another photo ID.  Who carries 2 photo id's on them while on vacation????  After speaking with multiple servers, and the manager, they still wouldn't serve me a beer because no one there was familiar with the NY State licenses/ids (It's not laminated like other states).  We ended up leaving because they were so rude and difficult.  I will never go back and we've told lots of family and friends in the area how awful they are.  

From the other reviews, it seems like they are generally rude and the service is terrible.  Why would anyone go here when there are so many other great dining options in the area, offering good service with a smile?

Haven't had salmon that bad in a very long time. When I asked if the salmon could be cooked medium, the response was the cooks always cook them well done but she'll ask. And to think I almost splurged on a streak! The lady across from me had a salad served in a stainless steel mixing bowl. It looked terrible!

Wow! Fun to try something different!  Great service (from Georgene) & accent to boot!  She was well versed to explain differences to novice German food eaters...and with a smile.  Decided on the Jaegar Schnitzel and from other review,  knew to order bit extra mushroom sauce (which added great depth & flavor to the spaetzel). Also,  the pork schnitzel was best and you really should try a bit of lemon squezed on..provides a nice  brght punch!  Another in our party had the Brat Wusrt (DELISH) and the Curry catsup...really tasty and different!  ONLY reason didn't get 5 stars is for the older members in our group (86 & 89!) struggled with the picnic bench style seats (we were quick to grab table when one came up!) It was very chilly today& with such small place, every time door opened was bit brisk, we put our coats back on!  Also. ..make sure to try the Cheese Spaetzel...bacon, cheese etc. ..could have eaten just this! Overall, great experience, little pricey for 5 of us ($90) but greatly enjoyed!

Delicious!! My opinion very pricey and we got a 25 parking ticket for parking in a normal sized parking space that apparently said for 40 foot parking only???? You wouldnt be able to fit in that space with a 40 foot vehicle!!! Shame on the city of Clearwater!!! Its a scam, trick and deceit!!! Apparently they dont want people doing business there!! Food was delicious, great location, very busy but the prices ridiculous!!! 4 people eating there with 4 sandwiches and one appetizer and NO alcohol, with tip, 93 bucks!!! Insane!!! Wont go there again, to many places to eat without parking problems! Im pissed!! Not restaurants fault, but I say again overpriced!
Just wanted to say that Tiana and the management is amazing! Thank you so much for everything today. We thoroughly enjoyed our experience.

Unfortunately, I was not blown away. I thought Chef Aaron Sanchez would be running a kitchen that would be up to par with his standards. The place is beautiful but the service is awkward and uninviting. The food looks really good but the flavors aren't there. Pollo con arroz tasted like public school food- bland. The burrito massive but mostly tortilla and pickled mess.

OK, I'm a sucker for Mexican. It doesn't really matter if it it Authentic Mexican, Cheap Mexican, or America's Idea of Mexican, I like it. TF definitely falls in the later category. 

I'll usually get the Ultimate Blackened Chicken Nachos or the Dos Enchildas with a whole wheat tortilla. It isn't mind-blowing, but it is always good. 

The staff is always nice. I don't know if I am just getting old, but they always seem really young. Like I'm surprised they are allowed to work, let alone serve beer and margaritas.

It is a pretty fun place to be in. The decor is stimulating and less canned than, say, Fridays/Chili's/Applebees. There are kinds of autographed pictures of famous people  that I don't recognize and the themed wall painting are vibrant and trippy. 

This place gets PACKED with kids. I know, it *is* Westchase, you what do I expect, but if you go for what you think is happy hour, you might find that it is really stroller hour.  But I love tots of all sizes, so I think it is great.

Yep. It's amazing. Simple menu. Vegan option also. 

I had the veggie ramen, spicy! Amazing flavors! Great service!

My wife and I are Cafe Central for lunch yesterday and it was so good.  There were so many options that it took us a while to order.  I decided on chicken quesadilla, which was delicious and HUGE.  Kim got turkey, stuffing, and mashed potatoes and it was very good. She couldn't finish it because there was so much on the plate.  Our waitress was amazing, very friendly and personable and prompt. Thanks Cafe Central!!

I still dream about this place. The pizza and drinks were amazing, and I would recommend it to anyone who likes to leave their house and eat - which means, this restaurant is for everyone! The decor is fab, the service is great, I wish I lived closer, because I would be happily heavier from eating here all the time.

I really appreciate that they have tons of vegetarian and vegan food options on the menu. They even have a plant  sign next to those dishes so it's easy to find. 

The kimchee fries are so good! Various veggie rolls (the Lombard was our fave), tempura, side dishes and more.
The original. The best. Will literally melt your brain. I usually start a newbie out here, on a medium, testing their tolerance and work out from there.

Bar was great, excellent bartender. Food just "so so". Good steaks but my med rare was the same as my husband's medium. The beans were dry and flavorless. Mac and cheese was gritty, not creamy.  The dinner salad was large but skimpy little cup of dressing. Worst of all was the service, waitress training another took our order then disappeared. After 20 minutes we asked a busboy to track down our salads. Finally a different waitress arrived with our food, but we didn't see her again until she brought the check. We probably won't return.

A real scam of a restaurant! When you get your bill, they then tell you that if you pay with a credit card you will be charged 3.5% and you must tip waiter in cash!  Service sucked and food was 2 stars out of 5. Don't waste your time coming to this dump!

Greenhills across from McDonald's. Wonderful smells and good looking offerings. Sadly only had the wine with the ladies. Trying to get in some girl time before the month became crazy. Had a plan to eat there and enjoy a glass of wine. Time and kids stopped that, but was a lovely place to put one toe in before we go for a full blown lunch and dessert. I did ask a neighboring table and they were all engaged in a bourbon caramel shake and Chocolate Decadence cookie skillet and finally the Nutella Goozy Cake. The loved the shake and the cake with the highest marks. We will def be back for next Girls time out meeting. Parking is shared in a small parking lot.

Soooo much grease. Rubbery mozzarella sticks. I've had them forget to cut the pizza.... I've had them not bring change for cash deliveries so I have to either over tip or not fully pay for my order. Of course I end up over tipping. There's a million pizza shops in Philly, you have to try to be one of the lesser ones. I understand going here if you're a local. But don't go out of your way for this place, and don't get delivery if you're paying in cash.

Their Reuben eggrolls are probably the best things I've ever eaten. The Mac and cheese was pretty rich, but I didn't love the panko topping. It could be that I had the eggrolls first, and so nothing was good enough for me afterwards.

The Mai tais are good for those who love boozy drinks. The Moscow mules are great as well. 

The only thing I didn't like about this place was the lack of space. It's definitely not the most spacious place if you have a large party.

I've had my order messed up here numerous times and cashiers are very rarely friendly. The music is loud and they have extremely quiet people saying names for orders. I didn't get a puck to know when my food was done and when I grabbed my food, another lady waiting for hers said it had been waiting up there for at least five minutes. I didn't have any headphones in and was listening, but someone saying a name in regular volume is not going to get their attention, especially over the music. Additionally, I get the same soup/side of bread combo every single time and their portion sizes always vary. I wouldn't recommend this location.

Delicious variety of unique dishes available. The wait staff was friendly and engaged throughout our brunch. I had a hard time picturing what my meal would look like based on their descriptions but was pleasantly surprised when it was sitting in front of me. My only caution would be focused on the pricing. It did seem to be a bit expensive for a brunch. Just keep that in mind as you enjoy your creative meal.
Great atmosphere, great food, great service! I haven't had anything from this place that isnt delicious. I definitely recommend sitting outside and taking in the natural beauty Florida has to offer.

I'm from Los Angeles and we found this spot on Yelp. As we was in line a guy who worked here walked up with open food container pile up high and had it leaning against his dirty shirt. Then as we approached the counter to order are food a baby roach was on the counter top by the cashier. When we told him he tried to kill it with the EBT machine, but it turned me off so we left without getting food.

Just Ravioli just made a new favorite customer! I stumbled upon this company looking for lunch for myself and 9 other coworkers. I'm vegan so I try to find options for everyone on the team. Not only did they have multiple combinations of vegan choices, they had enough options to get everyone excited. The gentleman happened to be out of 2 of the fillings we ordered online but I was promptly notified by phone and given several options to exchange them with. Will return soon, highly recommend!

MEH. 

This is definitely a tourist spot. The food is mediocre and hugely over priced. There are sooooo many better options a few steps away. If you are huge fan of the movie, definitely go - if not, head somewhere else.
Every time my wife and I visit Epice we expect and they deliver an excellent meal with excellent service. Hands down one of our favorites!

It's been a bit since my experience here, but I remember it perfectly.  Came in to watch the Cardinals 2014 season opener.  I sat at the side bar, had a couple of drinks and a Chicken Caesar Salad.  The salad was good and the waitress was very nice.  I walked away pretty satisfied until I found out they charged my credit card wrong.  I thought I had been charged twice, but as it turns out they had charged another person's ticket to my card, which was over $50+ what my ticket was.

The next day (when I found out about the charge) I posted initially on their Facebook page to initiate the complaint since the place wasn't going to open until 4p.  The social media monitor said they would get a manager to contact me.  After several hours, I ended up driving back because no one contacted me.  I talked to the manager.  Long story short, he gave me the run around saying it would be 3-5 business days to research the charge and someone from accounting would have to get back to me.  This seemed very unreasonable as it should have been a matter of going through the previous days receipts and reversing the charge.

After about 72 hours of going back and forth, I was finally refunded the money and satisfied by the manager over food and beverages for the entire casino.  I was sent a certificate to come back, which I haven't done yet.  If I do go back, I will be sure to bring cash.  From what I have heard, mistakes with charges are commonplace at Amerisports, which should be a big red flag to anyone considering going.  Just make sure if you do, bring cash.

This bakery is by far the best bakery I've ever been to.  I would gladly eat here even if I didn't have Celiac.  The donuts were phenomenal and the cupcake was so moist and tasted delicious.  They were reasonably priced, also.  Definitely coming back for more soon.

Perfect anniversary dinner! Everything was phenomenal with awesome service. We had steaks that were amazing - they even gave us a quick tour of their aging room. I have to say my favorite thing was the crab Rangoon though.

We made a reservation on Open table and our table was ready before our whole party arrived. The service at the bar and our table was excellent, especially for a Saturday night. The food was very good! We are looking forward to going back soon.
If you plan on using the app I'm getting your food quick you're better off going to the store and ordering it there.
This was delicious. They have many choices of broths and ingredients. They also have a large buffet and sushi. I like that they have gloves everywhere so people don't spread germs touching tongs.

Super impressed with this place. First, drinks are fun and tasty. Second, it's a whole lot of food for a perfect price. You don't get too much of that in The Gulch so I would recommend coming here. They offer complimentary parking'

Went to eat for my boyfriend's birthday since it was in the Pizza Passport. Very nice atmosphere, good outdoor seating. Covid precautions were on par. Masks, sanitizer, distancing. The pizza was stl style and deeeelicious. You can do other cheeses if you aren't a provel fan. Sweetish sauce and great topping options. Pricing is very reasonable, I'd definitely go back to try the tapas. Yummy sangria. Our server was having a bit of a rough day, but she was real up front about it and apologetic so we didn't mind, everything still came out in a timely manner and her coworkers really had her back and helped out. Would recommend!

Not bad. The service was really good but the selection of meats didn't have a ton of flavor. Maybe I'm bias but I think Na'Brasa on Easton road is a much better Brazilian Steakhouse. Again, not bad, by for the money, you can do better.

Why did I take away 1 star? First of all, they advertise online delivery and/or carry out. Not only did the website say they are not "currently" accepting online orders after entering my desired food, but I tried to call more times than a car warranty salesman and kept getting punted to a full mailbox. Needless to say, my "pick-up" order became a "order-and-wait-at-the-bar-bored"...order.

With that said, the pizza was slightly doughy but very flavorful. A bit pricey for a small pie, but I enjoyed it nonetheless. The wings had good sauce, but they looked like they were plucked a bit early, because they were extremely small and dry. The beer cheese? Who doesn't like beer and cheese?

Overall, I enjoyed the food enough to overshadow most of the negatives. 4/5 would order again (Hopefully online next time.)

While brunch was an hour wait, Tommy DiNic's had a few seats available when we arrived on Sunday at 10 AM. We quickly jumped on those seats and ordered a roast pork Italian sandwich with broccoli rabe. Noting that the Reading Terminal Market is full of goodies, we wanted to be certain we will have capacity to try a few things. So we made a quick (and smart) decision to split a sandwich because one sandwich measures to approximately 10 inches long. 

The slow-cooked Italian roast pork is made in-house and served on Sarcone's Italian rolls with a splash of gravy. The roast pork is evenly and thinly sliced while holding most of its moisture. It is not heavily seasoned - you taste its true essence. The Sarcone roll is crispy on the outside while the inside soaked up the meat's juice and light gravy. The broccoli rabe with a dash of bitterness and garlic, was the perfect counterpart to the pork. The next time I return, I should add the provolone and see if that will bring it to a whole new level of greatness.

I'd give 10 stars if I could for this oasis in the middle of East Nashville. We stopped at Nobles after spending the afternoon shopping on this side of town. Although there were only two ciders on tap, a superhero (aka, our bartender) recommended Lola, Diskin's version of the hard seltzer. I loved it! My faith in Nashville is restored.

It's an average bar. The beer selection is good, with the ever awesome Victory DirtWolf Double IPA in bottle. Staff was friendly but nothing amazing. Prices are fair. There are a few TVs, but this certainly isn't a place to go to focus on sports - that would be secondary. I did not have any food, but it looked fine. The bar itself is clean, but the bathrooms are cramped and a bit questionable.

So confused about the varying reviews - I was expecting a 5 star experience from the pics online and reviews but overall I'd say it was good, not great.

I had a Hyatt free night from a credit card so figured I'd use it for a staycation. The hotel is beautiful from the outside, the gym inside is amazing, and the restaurant (XIX) on the top floor is pretty deluxe albeit overpriced in my mind (kind of like the hotel in general).

Overall, I'd give more stars if it was a more cost effective stay for those paying cash, but I think for someone spending $400+ a night for a weekend stay there are far betters options in Philadelphia (although perhaps not as central of a location).
Currently sitting at Texas Roadhouse. No forks, empty waters, and my friend has a salad and can't eat it. Disappointed ;(

Went here on st pattys day. With my family and my mom is a regular here. So we ordered drinks and they were never refilled and that was only the sodas. We had to walk up to bar to get our beers because the waitress was not around at all. She was so rude and acted like she hates her job and like we were doing somthing wrong when we were just trying to have a nice dinner out with our family. She was very slow and inattentive to our needs. She complained that we got our beers from the bar and caused a whole scene with my boyfriend. The manager had to ask her twice to get us more drinks. Then we had to ask her if she could clear a plate that was finished for over 30 minutes. Then ordered dessert and had to stop her on the way past our table to get dessert. My boyfriend made a joke to the waitress and the snapped back assuming he worked in a kitchen and said "I'd never come to where you work to eat there." After we paid and everyone else left I was standing at the table waiting for my boyfriend to come back from the restroom. The waitress came over and LAUGHED OUT LOUD at the tip!! I'm a server so I always tip very well, for good service and she was lucky I left anything. If it was based on service nothing was deserved. We eat out everyweekend so this place is obviously loosing alot of business because of this lady. Dont know why they cant just hire happy good servers. Such a shame.

Had the hot hogtown sandwich and it was awesome. Great spot for some BBQ. Sauces are excellent, brisket is well-cooked, and the mac and cheese is a great call for your side. Would recommend this every day of the week and twice on Sunday.

Worst service ever & the food was below par. The cook had 1 speed.....s l o w. It took more than 10 minutes to get acknowledged & the food took at least 25 minutes to be handed to us. We took the food to go, NO napkins were in the bag. Won't be stopping at this location ever again.

This est is a 30 min drive for us but so worth it! This was my first visit and we will certainly be back. 
 The ambiance is so welcoming, it sets a rustic farmhouse atmosphere; very welcoming and casual. 
 I ordered the duck confit hash..  OMG the duck was moist, not really seasoned but it didn't need it, the goat cheese mousse I expected to be sweet just because of the color but it was not wile really complimenting the meal with the creaminess of it. There were also surprise raisins, dried cranberries, or something that was a nice touch and the potatoes! They didn't have much seasoning but again they didn't really need it, best of all they were had a crunchy exterior and perfect inside. I didn't finish all my potatoes, even though we had just finished hiking 7 falls.
 Hubby had the chefs dip of the day which was your standard prime rib (could def have used a better portion of) but it had a delicious pesto, muenster cheese which was actually a bit too much (the amount used), and sautéed peppers, the four stars are for the fries and au jus. The au jus had no flavor whatsoever and I would suggest a larger bowl for it as it was very awkward to try and dip to begin with. The fries were nice and crunchy but again not really seasoned. 

 The service was also spot on. They were prompt and courteous, I believe our server was Mark/Max. 

I cannot WAIT to go back and work through their menu

It's a fun little bar. There's a couple of pianos inside which they play some upbeat, fun music. The two women playing the night we went were fun and were playing good songs.

The best part was the outside patio. They have a nice atmosphere and a really kick-ass flaming fountain.

I had the Hurricane.  It took me three but after I had a nice buzz going.  They're a little expensive but if you turn your glass in you get $3 back.  Or you can just keep them as a souvenir. They give you a little box and bag to take it in.

Everyone was happy and friendly, (customers and wait staff) which made for a good overall mood too.

This is by far the best pizza spot in Tucson. Authentic wood fired pizza, with such amazing service always given. Every single time I eat here, I am never disappointed. Scott is the best pizza cook ever and is really nice and always willing to put the guests first. People like Scott are the hard working employees who bring back returning guests :) This is my favorite Pizza place in Tucson and I just want to recognize Scott for the attentive amazing service and for always being so respectful to their guests!

I was told that Columbia Restaurant is the oldest restaurant in America! Is that true or was he BSing me????

After hearing that of course I had to take advantage of stopping by here before taking off on my flight back to California.  

I ordered the crab croquettes and the Cuban and will say that most were not very memorable.  Both items felt dry and lacking flavor.  

I really wanted to love this place and will be happy giving it another shot on my next visit back into Tampa.

Never had Chicken & Waffles before so I thought I would give it a try. Tried the southern style chicken with plain waffle and all I can say is Wow!! The chicken was fantastic. Going to take the family back tomorrow so that I try something else on the menu. 
Good stuff!!

Came for dinner after wine walk. Great food. We had spring rolls, yellow curry and spicy basil. Excellent.   Quick service. Friendly staff. Would recommend for people staying in the casinos. Just 1-2 blocks away.  Portions were large despite others review

Wow, amazing food. Delicious and authentic is right. I had jerked chicken - tender and juicy. Terrific rice and to die for plantains. Really nice people, too. Can you open one of these in Portland, Oregon?

If we could click ZERO stars, we surely would. This place was HORRIBLE. Poor service with attitude from the waitresses. Lousy food with brown lettuce served. And a TWO HOUR WAIT FOR EGGS. We asked to speak to the manager and was told "she's too busy". The restaurant was 1/4 filled. Don't waste your time. This place is pure trash.

I've been here three times since they opened, and I can't say enough good things about Izzy's. 

Jo and her team have practically done the impossible, opening a new restaurant in 2020. The food is thoughtfully prepared, and menu has options for all kinds of palates.

The food here is subpar if anything. I have given them two different tries and, both times tried different things. The food is over seasoned and just not enjoyable. The service is horrible. While,  the staff is nice it just takes forever to be waited on here.

I had to credit the place for its service. The girl there was sooo nice... She served hot towels to us before the food was served and came over several time during the eating in a not disturbing way. In terms of the food, the barbecue ribs were really juicy and tasteful, the steamed buns were below the average but still okay.

It was fine. They made a big stink b/c we sat in the wrong color chair (apparently you can only order off the full menu if you sit in the brown chairs, not the green ones). Additionally, while our initial margaritas were strong, the next 2 rounds had so little alcohol that myself and my dinner companion both noted it. Perhaps the reasoning is that tourists won't notice. At 13$ a drink, it's pretty unacceptable. The sweet potato fries were undercooked and the shrimp were overdone and given the price, most of the fish was stale bread. Other than the beach view, I would not recommend.

Went on a Wednesday night around 6:30 pm, and had less than 15 minutes to wait, the locals say that's a GREAT night!!! We tried the Farmhand Fries and the BBQ nachos ( they were both EXCELLENT), and polished them off quickly. For out of towners the Jack's Creek sauce is a vinegar based sauce, and I like a thicker and sweeter sauce, just FYI. We chose not to add more sauce to our nachos and fries. 
The sides we tried were Mac and Cheese and Potato Salad, and they were both pretty good with just the right amount of sauces. Everyone had the pork sandwiches, and we were house divided... out of 5 that got it, 3 loved them and 2 liked them. The 2 who liked felt like the meat wasn't smoky enough, and needed more bark. I was picking through looking for burnt ends. I did not see a burnt ends sandwich in the menu at all; and that disappointed me for a BBQ place. I may have missed it though! We had no problem finding a table, but getting drink refills was hard despite being told just to ask a server. Just all the FYI's for the out of towners!

Came here on Sunday during Brunch and I've been the other location in The Germantown section of the city and had to try this location in Cheltenham. I knew what to exact before entering but had to check it out and show support since it's a relative new opening around the area.

There was a little wait but that's expected at any good establishment and since this a BLACK OWNED BUSINESS. I don't mind the wait at all. 

The food was delicious. I ordered breakfast and it came out fast and hot. Definitely a great go to place if you coming alone or with a group of people. The ambience is very chill, music is playing the background but not overpowering. The thing I enjoyed most besides the food and staff was the fact they have literature in the front to read as you wait. Very nice touch. 

If you are in the area I'd def recommend.

Oh wow, this place is horrible.  Started with the chips and salsa, they provide one red and one green salsa.  The green is just nasty bad, the red is ok.  My husband had the rib-eye steak and he said it was so so, for a $37.00 steak it better be more than so so, right?  Anyway, I wont be recommending this overpriced restaurant.  But to each his own, we will be going to Pinnacle Peaks next time for a steak.

Celebrated a special anniversary with Matyson this week, so we went with the tasting menu ($45/pp)... with a corn theme. The tasting blew us away. Overall, we experienced excellent presentation, special/creative cooking, and great service. Add that to BYOB (we chose well) and it was a perfect evening. 

Course 1: smoked corn vichyssoise, served cold. Delicious flavor, with great texture coming from the fried leeks and pickled corn kernels. Started the meal with a yummmm.

Course 2: corn-encrusted soft shell crab, served over a Mexican-style corn salad and huitlacoche paste. Strong flavors, can't go wrong with soft-shell crab done right. Only complaint: only half a crab per person.

Course 3: corn and lobster risotto, with mascarpone and peaches. The risotto (which was a bit loose for a true risotto, but I digress) was laden with chopped tarragon, which gave an entrancing, anise-like bounce to this otherwise sweet-tart dish. Excellent combination of tastes.

Course 4: roasted veal chop, served over sweet corn puree, with smashed blackberries. This is the best veal we have ever had: perfectly prepared, tender, delicate, laced with briny flavor. Great contrast with the sweetness of the corn and the tartness of the blackberries.

Course 5: corn & black pepper ice cream, with caramel corn. This was the only underwhelming course. Not nearly peppery enough, and not enough caramel corn.

Would definitely swing back through here the next time we are in town.

Don't go here.

The employees are completely rude. The hostess and servers all saw us walk in. They looked directly at us because they were standing right next to the counter, and then they made us wait for them to finish their conversation. It was uncomfortable just standing there. Then finally the hostess turned around and said, "oh, I'm sorry for the wait" as if she hadn't locked eyes with us the moment we came in and as if we weren't standing 2 feet to the right of her the entire time. 

Then they proceeded to tell us that since it was 5pm, they were switching staff and just needed a moment. It was just turning 4:30pm. When we mentioned that, she said, "oh never mind, you're right it's not 5 yet, we can seat you." And then a server came up to her and said no, we're booked for the rest of the night because of a reservation at this time and a reservation at that time. There were clearly 5 tables open from my view and from what I gathered, the reservations weren't until later on, so I have no idea why they ended up saying they couldn't seat us.. are 2 people really going to take up so much? 

I've worked in the service industry for years and normally try to cut employees some slack because I know how it feels, but that was by far the worst customer service I've ever experienced just to try to get seated.

Just want to let you know your food if subpar I purchased a steak potato & boneless chicken appetizer my wife got the chicken with apple chutney on it. She said hers was ok but my steak and chicken taste god awful. I was a meat Mgr for Kash n Karry for 25 years that was not choice or even good graded. The meat taste like it was from Mexico and I know the difference for the price of those steaks was a rip off maybe you should go see what they are serving because I know meat. The apple bees on county line Road has no business selling poor quality meats at prime priced . This was not the first time it's happened we gave it a chance months later but still the same. This time my burger was red in the middle when asked for burnt. If you want more feed back my name is rick my number is 7273899724 email tolmo@ tampabay . Rr . Com I won't hold my breath

This is such a great idea. On this side of town there isn't anything close to as good as this. The workers are so nice and very helpful. There is plenty of options and the food is very good quality. I'll definitely be going back there.

Never returning to this restaurant again. I'm not sure what their deal was but we waited about 45 mins for take-out. About 20 of the 45 mins was spent waiting for someone to even acknowledge us, and take our order. One waitress told us she would be right with us, but then proceeded to do everything else but take our order. I had to flag another waiter down for our order to be taken. Although I know that Sunday's are usually busy at these types of places, there seems to be no order of business & that leaves some confusion as to who is doing what. Already this experience is annoying. After about another 25 mins of waiting for our food, I asked a waiter what was going on with our order, and no one could seem to give me an answer. I noticed there were a couple of to-go boxes on the bar counter, & finally our waiter come back & of course the to-go boxes are ours. Now, I am livid. This what my first time at this place, and all of the waiters seem to be more focused on their regulars than anything else. Didn't leave a good impression on us at all. Only reason I rated them with two stars is because the food looks decent.
City house never disappoints!! Just finished the PB&J pie. Sorry it was half eaten before I thought of a pic. Between the two of us we opted for a couple small plates. Awesome.

I decided to redo my review from a year ago because our experience here this afternoon was exceptional. We ordered everything online through their interface and it worked well. I got to the restaurant 10 minutes early but the proprietor was engaging and whipping up all our food fresh, from scratch in an open spotless kitchen. It was incredibly clean.

We had a nice chat and she showed me their Best of the Bay awards and I told her I was impressed. Also, I was impressed by the style and decor of the restaurant. It's really quite stunning for a medium size restaurant in a strip mall. Check it out!

Our food, when we got it home, has all been delicious. My wonderful wife ordered toum which is a native Lebanese garlic sauce. Toum literally means garlic in Arabic. She loved it and we received a great portion. We've even made this at home in the past. 

Life is good with a fine restaurant and toum!

There is not much to say about this restaurant.  Good service and mediocre food for non-mediocre prices.

Ordered:
Bouillabaisse - Just OK... I can actually make much better
Prawn pizza - good
Vegetable Napoleon - Nothing special.  It looked really pretty, but tasted like mashed potatoes and mushrooms.

The good was delicious and extremely reasonably priced.  I'm picky about Cuban or Latin food, and this food is definitely above the usual small place cut.  My only complaint is the service, or they would have gotten all five stars! Although the waitress was extremely pleasant at the table, getting her there was a chore, even when they forgot part of an order (lettuce and tomato), it took her 10 minutes to bring that out. They also had to call the owner to figure out how to use my Yelp coupon I bought-maybe if the owner sets up a deal like this, he/she should educate their employees how to redeem them...

Try their Spicy curry sauce Pizza. You will not regret.. awesome place. Veggie Pizza.
Very close to our hotel. Definitely a to go spot for pizza.
This was a phenomenal culinary experience.  The different courses created from locally sourced ingredients were excellent.  The staff was incredibly attentive.  Would definitely recommend.

I had the worst experience at this restaurant. They get zero stars because their manager was rude and made it feel like my children were not welcome there. After 3 employees watched me bring my small stroller down the stairs and chose not to inform me that strollers weren't allowed inside, a  blond employee 
actually told me I was in the way while I was trying to get settled into the restaurant. Rather than saying they couldn't accommodate us or offering assistance they made several remarks that made me feel uncomfortable and unwelcome. Apparently the person who told me that I was in the way and needed to hurry up and make a decision was the manager. If children aren't allowed then they should make it clear to the public. I gladly walked across the street and spent my money elsewhere.

Went on a date here recently. Get the steak, it was cooked perfectly. The drink prices were typical of a tucson bar so no surprises. They rock the surf and turf menu so come hungry wanting steak or seafood. They have cocktails, beer, and wine selections with some notable surprises. Go check it out. I was not disappointed. The local reputation lives up to the name. Dante's Fire is indeed

I have only two words for this installment: Bon. Appetit. I peregrinate to the grill & tavern approximately once a month, as the establishment is within walking distance from my resting quarters. I often commandeer myself the Tadano steak sandwich, hmm, just thinking about it makes my mouth salivate. The service is customarily hospitable and always treats their guests with the proper care that any Yelper and fellow aficionado are entitled to.

I first heard about this place via excited freshman boy ranting about how he could stuff himself with "mama style pancakes" here for close to nothing. My boy friend reaaaally likes breakfast foods, I on the other hand am very indifferent but since the boy made it clear that it was a Tucson must have I decided I'd try it out. I ordered the blueberry pancakes and when it came out I was impressed. People usually say "Wow! Look! Its almost big as your head!" but this pancake was "Wow look! This pancake is 3 times the size of your body and can stop world hunger alone status!". Pretty freaking huge. On the downside, sometimes, they're so big that they come out burnt without the inside not cooked all the way through, but pish posh that rarely happens.

Overall it's a great place to dine but I'd be aware of the huge waiting line you'll probably encounter in the mornings but its worth it. Service is fast and friendly, so you'll never have to see the bottom of your coffee cup. In addition, it's probably one of the cheapest sit down joints around.

Fresh squeezed OJ available here --- 11 oranges makes one cup!

If you are in the mood for a typical diner breakfast, this is a good spot.  Huge portions!

One of the staff is in costume as black bear, handing out balloons to kids.  Nice touch and unexpected for breakfast.

A drunk person's safe haven. This place is the holy grail for the inebriated person. Not only can you fill your carnal desire to go up two pant sizes but you can do it till 3AM. Angelo and his staff are exceptionally friendly and hilarious. The food is of course, what you would expect at 3AM at a pizza joint - nothing to brag about, but satisfying nonetheless when you're drunk (Kind of like that girl/guy you're taking home after you eat your pizza  of whom you just met at that decrepit bar a few blocks away).

Definitely recommend this place (but not that person you are taking home).

Came here for a date night based on other yelp reviews.  It was a bit brighter and noisier than expected,  with mostly large tables of groups.  We did come a little early in the evening though around 7, they might turn the lights down later.  We tried the filet steak and it was pretty good.  I wouldn't say it was the most incredible steak in the world,  but it was tender and thick,  and I definitely liked it. It felt more like a $22 steak than a $32 steak though. Nice spot for a date or a business dinner.  Good ambiance.

Are you kidding me with this elote? I'm pretty sure I've died and gone to heaven where chorizo and lime meets roasted corn. The stuff is amazeballs! Sopapillas are delish with salted caramel whiskey sauce. The chili relleno dog is soooo tasty too. I'm all over the place, but this place was dynamite! 
I'll be back soon to try the quesadilla because word on the street is its fabulous.

I ordered a take out from this place. They heated the food in microwave while in plastic container. It was melted when I opened it at home.eat was super dry. I am really disappointed. Adding to that the salad side is the smallest I ever seen in my life

I would said this is 3.5 stars restaurant. It is not a four stars restaurant to my opinion. Since we don't have 1/2 star, four stars was given. 

We select the Christmas for our visit at the hour of their opening of the door. This will take out the crowed conditions for serving and the busy kitchen situation. This will give them a fare review. 

We have order the two appetizer- the Roti and the Pla Muek Yang. The roti is two round roti cut in eight pieces. It has the Malaysian roti taste. Although this may be from packaged factory made but was pan fried perfectly. I like the curry dipping. 

Pla Muek Yang aka grilled squid. It marinated in curry or Cumming. It is flame grilled and you can see the grilled mark. The only complaint it the dish come out cold. Seem like sit a bit before it was brought out. It serves with sweet sauce. It is about three squid cut in ring. 

Our entrees order is disaster. It take three rejections before we got our order. There are three items they don't carry yet. But I did not count against them on this review. I have order the Phat Chinese Broccoli and pork belly and they have given me Asian BBQ pork and Pork Belly  noodle. I did not ask them to change since it look interesting. We also added the spicy chicken seafood noodle. 

The Asian noodle soup base is very interesting and different. I believe the ingredients was not the same as described in the menu. The spicy chicken noodle are very close to Thai street noddle but in the sweet side. This two dishes is just ok. 

Food is about 3.5 rating; service is about 4.0 and the kitchen crew is about 3 ratings. I believe the kitchen should not have any excuse because there only three customers when we were there. They should not busy and should handle the food better.

Love this place. The service is good, they always pay attention, my water glass is never empty. 
The red curry is great, my friend loves the ginger salmon. They have a really nice brown rice, real brown rice. The prices are good. 
Great small restaurant.

I stayed here a few years ago. My room was clean and cozy aside from the roach issue (read my other review). This stay was different. It feels as if the property has gone down since then. My room had an odor like mildew or mold that we couldn't seem to get rid of with air freshener. Also, when you turn the water temperature knob to a certain point, there would be this loud, continuous noise and the knob would start to shake rapidly until you turned the knob slightly to the right or left. Problem was, that exact agitated point on the knob was the perfect temperature setting for me so I always had to have my water either slightly too hot or too cold. Very annoying. But the main issue we experienced can't really be explained by the hotel staff. We were two families, in two different rooms and both families experienced allergy problems while in the shower. The water from the shower seems to burn the eyes and almost immediately after the eyes begin to burn, severe sneezing begins. I initially thought it was the hotel hair conditioner but at breakfast, my cousin asked if I was feeling weird while in the shower. He explained the exact same symptoms but he had not used the conditioner. Then a woman who was eating nearby overheard our conversation and she said the exact thing was happening to her. That night, I was rinsing my daughters hair after swimming and she began to cry and said the water was burning her eyes and then she began sneezing as well. This morning I heard my husband sneezing while he was in the shower. I went to the desk and asked about the water in the hotel and they looked at me as if I were crazy and said they have never heard anyone complain of this. Weird, we all experienced this and we weren't on the same floor. The woman was staying on the 18th floor and we were on the 4th. Can't say the water made my skin feel any different but my hair certainly did. It felt hard and wiry after shampooing and so did my daughters'. I blame the water for sure! I can't understand why the hotel staff are saying they've never heard this before when it seems like a common occurrence. Morning breakfast was ok...much better than a lot of other free breakfasts. They have an omelette station and a small hot buffet with scrambled eggs, potatoes, bacon, and sausage. The area gets crowded at times but they have a sign near the elevator that lets you know the high traffic times for breakfast. Most of the staff was  pretty nice in the hotel except for an overzealous young guy at the front desk. It's not that he was rude...he just has a "know-it-all" way about him that came across as a little annoying and especially since he decided to jump into the conversation I was having with another desk person and give me an answer that ended up being very wrong. I don't think I will ever stay in this hotel again. There is a Marriott across the street that I normally stay in but Hilton Honors sent me an email with an offer I couldn't refuse except whenever we went to the desk to inquire about the offer we had, no one seemed to know anything about it. Overall, the stay was a little bad and I don't think I'll stay again.

Ran out of steam while shopping and so glad I remembered this was here!!! Had a BLT with sweet potato fries - the BLT was phenomenal. Bread was toasted perfectly, avocado was fresh, and the bacon was plentiful. Sweet potato fries were some of the best I've had in town. So impressed with this place and love the decor - feels like a New York diner. Will be back! Try it instead of the crowded and overly priced Cheesecake Factory next time!
Lots of food for the $. Burgers tasted great, seasoned very well. Fries were a good complement too."Onion Thangs" were tasty, You'll want to ask for a fork. Will be back.

New Deck has good service and ambiance, and the prices aren't shabby for the amount of food you're ordering. I ordered the New Deck Burger, and the meat was juicy and delicious, cooked to the medium well I asked for. The fries were nice and crispy (but soft and potato-y inside) - and the quesadillas seemed quite large given their price.
The food was good, not amazing or something I'd die to come back for.
A couple of standouts, but overall a pretty average place to get tacos. Cool environment, though.
Above average Pho, just never enough meat in my opinion. Always have had good service there and it's a clean, professional place. Lunch special is a great go-to if you're uptown.

Had a big problem with substituting one kind of soup for another... They wouldn't do it and I ended up paying for both?
Very rude service and manager.

We love Italian food, so we really wondered what we would find at this restaurant.  We made a reservation 24 hours in advance on a weekend and the only options were 4:45 or 8:45, neither is an hour at which we usually dine.  When we arrived we were graciously welcomed and the interior is nice, up to date and inviting, and, as it should be in an Italian restaurant, the aroma was mesmerizing!  We quickly ordered wine, they had a lovely selection and settled in for a nice meal.  I eat gluten free and this is a gf eater's paradise...pizza and pasta are offered as gf options.  When I told my sever about my gf diet, she suggested that I leave the capers off the pesto chicken pasta as they have some gluten...well I never would have guessed that. Hooray for a restaurant that trains their staff well.   We split a caesar salad (without croutons), it was excellent.  We each had pasta and wine and we announced to one another that we would return.  The service was good, the food and wine were good, it was a fabulous experience!

Finally had an opportunity to visit this market place after getting correct directions from Neal P. They definitely have a large selection of cheeses & cured meats. An awesome olive bar. Fresh bread. Take the time to find them and just go wild !

Late night on a Sunday... Came for Poutine because I've heard so much about it from a former manager... Appetizers of scallops with risotto started off OK until one of the three scallops was raw... Nicely braised brown on the outside but just this side of edible... My date was really put off by it... Well lets reserve rating until the Poutine and Caesar salad arrive.   
Yelp! The Caesar salad that we ordered without anchovies .... Two ugly critters on top... My fries are cold
Two stars...?the risotto was tasty
Pizza was tasty and waited approx 20 mins for a half pepperoni and half cheese. Big slices of pepperonis. Would go again

Never been to a Capital Grill that disappoints. Great staff and great food. 
Drinks were generous. Plenty of parking. Place was spotless. We usually go to the Wall Street location, sadly, because of the creep stinking up City Hall , there's no indoor dining in what used to be a great destination for restaurants and a nice night out.

We've made several visits to Butcher & Bee, namely for the whipped feta with fermented honey. But everything is stellar here. This restaurant would be at home in any city. Great food and happening atmosphere. Smith & Lentz Beer from across the street.

I came to the Vine with a couple of friends on a beautiful Friday Saturday evening.  We sat outside in front of the restaurant and enjoyed the warm weather.  (this was before the huge heat waves that hit STL)  Now let's break down my dinner:

Environment:  The inside of the restaurant is relatively small so I wouldn't recommend coming here with a huge group.  But if the weather is nice they open up their patio which is really nice and The Vine actually had a jazz group playing in the background so that was an extra plus! 
4/5

Service:  The service was friendly and quick with our orders and food.  I also liked how since I went with a big group he didn't rush us for our orders and actually let us settle in and chat with each other before asking what we wanted for dinner  
5/5

Food: The food was AMAZING.  Not only was it good but it was cheap.  You can get a chicken shawarma which is basically a chicken wrap for about $4 and their other menu prices are unbeatable in price and taste.  I did not get the chicken shawarma but I got something similar to it and I gotta say the chicken was very juicy and so tender that it almost melts in your mouth.  Also, many people in my group got their famous fries and they indeed are good but nothing too special.  A Turkish student also joined us for dinner and he said that it was perhaps the best middle eastern/ medditeranian food he has had in Saint Louis and that if his parents would visit him from Turkey he would bring them here!  That sure says alot coming from someone who eats this kind of food everyday back in Turkey!  Perhaps the best part of the night was the mint hookah and mint tea we ordered as a group later on in the night.  The hookah was average but the mint tobacco flavoring was addicting!  The tea was also very fresh and not too hot to be undrinkable but it was also not too cold to be disgusting to drink.  It was perfect.
4/5

Overall: 4/5 You guys should definitely check this out if you want authentic and cheap Middle Eastern/Mediterranean food.
They have cleaned the place up a bit and also serve real guacamole again.  Much better than it had gotten but not as good as it used to be waaaay back when I first started going
Best pizza. Sweet Lil Razorback is my favoriteservice was also excellent. No complaints!

Great sandwiches, superb home-made tamales, long hours, clean, well lit, untouchable service; it's a good thing I live just around the block from here, because otherwise it'd be a long-ass, but worthwhile, walk.

Corner stores are to Philly what water is to fish, and this is the well-spring of life.
I really had a good meal here.  I had the scallops and the Filet mignon very good and very cheep.  the staff made the night very special.

I'm sitting at the bar right now because I just placed my order. I ordered at the bar because I called to place a 'to go' order and was put on hold for 6 minutes and no body answered. Now I'm here. It's dead. There are bartenders and servers shootings' the s**t behind the bar and I'm wondering why no one had time to pick up the phone and take my order. I figured I had to drive here to get it anyway so I may as well force someone to take my order in person.

I went there for the first time yesterday.  I totally enjoyed the Gluten Free Carrot Cake and saw many other goodies that I want to try in the future. 

I also had a Tuna sandwich on homemade Gluten Free bread. It was tasty and the bread was moist (not all crumbly like many GF breads). The reason why I will likely not order that sandwich (or probably any sandwich) again is all about the size for the price. You pay $1 more for the GF bread, which is understandable and pretty customary. The problem is that the sandwich is really small.... evidently about the size of a half sandwich, because the lady who was going to give me my To Go order thought that they mistakenly put a half sandwich of some sort in my bag. So, I paid $1 more for about half the size of the usual sandwiches.... about $9.25 just for the small sandwich. (After looking at other Yelpers' pictures, I didn't get the carrot and celery sticks either. That might have helped. Also the picture of the GF veggie sandwich looks fuller with all of those wonderful veggies topped high. Maybe I should have had that one. You can kind of tell the size of my sandwich yesterday, but mine was much flatter.)

My plan for the next visit is probably to just go with a GF soup, salad, or quiche. I will get the same amount of food as non GF eaters and pay the same price. 

I'm definitely a fan of my new Gluten Free find. I just believe that I need to order differently, unfortunately.

Just had dinner there. Terrific service and food! Made a Rez for 4 people on a Saturday and had no problems at all. The wait staff was super attentive and super friendly and happy to chat with our questions. 
We ordered the fried chicken, goatfish, shoshito peppers m, grilled peaches with goat cheese and honey, chicken liver mousse with pickled peaches. Peach financier cake with honey ice cream was so yummmmm. 
Only thing not good was the clam pasta dish. The clams were pretty chewy and hard. My Rhode Island crustacean connoisseur also agreed. 
For all the ones upset there isn't enough chicken...
I asked about why the limited amount of chicken and was told because it is outsourced from a specific small farm-It is not sustainably feasible to order mass quantity, so it's 5 chickens weekdays, 11 chickens weekends. Makes sense. Don't need to over farm, and they don't want to purchase from a larger farm and become wasteful with their animals. They are head to tail so if they offer meat such as beef, they purchase a whole cow. And so the menu revolves around all the parts of the cow. Hence the reason why they don't have multitudes of animals to offer on the menu.

Pretty good, lovely spot. Vegetarian paneer tikka masala and vegan aloo Gobi, simple yet deliciously spiced. Butter naan was good. Friendly server but he wasn't "really" listening. 

(Had to remind him of a dish we ordered when we only ordered two dishes, got a roti we never ordered but paid for anyways, etc)  

No complaints, nice lunch!
Not amazing, not bad.

NOTE to owner; if this were my restaurant, I would get a more noticeable main sign. Somewhat bland sign on a busy / fancy street.
We did the tasting menu here. It wasn't bad, but I don't think it was worth the money either. There were some standout dishes, but unfortunately the majority of the courses were just okay.

This place has been around since I can remember-- when there were few Asian places in South Philly. I know Cafe Diem is well known for their Bun Bo, which is super spicy and super good. However, I don't see what's the hype. I guess since I am Vietnamese and my family can cook most of the dishes served in Vietnamese restaurants, I have less of a craving for them when I am out. Also my sister is an amazing cook and so I do hold Vietnamese food I eat out at a very high standard. 

I recently came back here with a friend and saw that it has been renovated and is looking much newer in the inside. My friend ordered Bun Bo and I didn't know what to order since I wasn't giving a menu. But then I realized people just order what they know. I don't think they have menus? I ended up ordering Banh Cuon that was not good.

Anyway, not a bad place to eat but of course there are better choices on Washington. If you do decide to stop by, just order what they are known for.

We stopped here on our way through Indianapolis. The service staff was polite and service was excellent. We were never short on anything. The food was plentiful and my wife and I really enjoyed it. I had the Quesadilla Grande which was stuffed to the brim with meat unlike many quesadillas you get that are all cheese with just a little meat. My wife enjoyed her meal as well (sorry meal escapes me). She couldn't even finish it, there was so much. Thanks for the great meal.

I love this place for lunch. It's quick, easy, fresh and conveniently located on Washington Square. The employees are nice and helpful and they get you in and out.  There is always plenty of seating too if you don't want to sit in the park and enjoy your lunch. 
I highly recommend their baked goods too!

I'm learning that New Orleans restaurants or all overrated, any place you go to in this area will be. I ordered shrimp and grits but it had a sour taste. The waiter said it was the beer in it. Service  was nice but the food not so much!

Fantastic Mediterranean food - amazingly fresh.  Falafel was hot, smooth, light(not greasy).  Hummus was out of this world, tabouleh was zesty, fresh and filled with good parsley.  The food is 5 stars hands down!

The only negatives:
They were all out of babaganoush.  
Service understated.  Could have been more helpful. But for the food's sake, definitely overlook it!

i have been here a dozen times, often just for happy hour and special appetizers. as a mug club member, i get a discount on the beer and a large goes for the price of a small.  try a two-pull, 2 different kinds of beers at once.  very good. i don't think i have had anything bad there off the menu, but it is unfortunately one of those places that tries too hard to add oddball stuff to make a good meal fancy.  no need.  it is all pretty decent, but check  the prices on meatloaf or the mac n cheese as a main course.  way over-priced.  some prices are quite decent tho.   i'll go back again, for beer and appetizers, as i have a hard time finding something i like on the menu.  skip the ribs--it is hard to detect the flavors advertized, nor much of any flavor.

service is always good.

I have heard great things about Vessel. Not sure if today was an off day but I was very disappointed in the slow service and bland, mediocre food. Brunch took a full 60 minutes to receive. All food was underwhelming- crawfish croquettes, shrimp and grits, fried Brussels no flavor, bland and meh. 
The Mediterranean burger was the best of everything but not worth $23. Just as my husband finished his burger he found a blonde hair inside. Disgusting! Was gonna be a 2 star review, taking off a star for it. The manager did not charge us for the burger. 

Response to Eddie: 

Thanks for confirming the food was slow... 37 minutes for appetizers! It was actually 27 minutes, I added some time stamp photos for you! You are so defensive but instead you should be apologetic about MY experience! Like I said, maybe it's an off day. I gave you a pass. Don't try to discredit my review while you sit at home watching video instead of personally quality checking your establishment! Your staff told me you don't live in New Orleans! Ha!

I went in to Yakuza at 8:10 pm on 12/5/13 with my brother to have dinner and use the Groupon I had.  We ordered our food and ate, and when I went to use the Groupon, "the manager" claimed that we couldn't use it because we didn't present the Groupon ahead of time.

I wasn't aware that the Groupon stated that, but I politely told her I wasn't aware this time and would present it next time.  She proceeded to lie by saying that "Groupon wouldn't accept my barcode unless presented before the order was placed."  Knowing a little about technology and seeing that they used an old register to ring up orders, I knew she wasn't telling the truth.

I pointed this out to her and her story changed to "How do I know that you were here after 8 pm."  I again pointed out that several other people there were using Groupons that were there before me.  She said there was nothing she could do and advised me to call Groupon, and they would be able to re-reimburse me.  Knowing that it was past hours to call, a phone call would useless.     

This continued for 45 minutes, and in the end I was forced to pay full price for a meal of $31.22.  

This night was a horrible experience for me and my brother who was visiting from out of state.  We both felt pretty humiliated, and I couldn't understand why she was fighting so hard for it unless they had given us something that they normally don't give to Grouponers.

On an additional note, the rolls were the thinnest I had ever seen, and we were still hungry when we left.  Also for some reason, the sushi chef coughs without covering his mouth to signal to the server that the food is ready.

Don't go here for the food. Don't go here for the beer. Don't go here for the ambiance.  The only positive was that our server was prompt and pleasant.  

The Chicken Nachos were microwaved and barely had any chicken on them.

I ordered the chipotle chicken sandwich. It was so drowned in cheese that I couldn't taste anything else.

My friend ordered the Reuben sandwich, also smothered in cheese with hardly any sauerkraut.

There were only 4 beers on tap. 

We were seated upstairs where it was about 85 degrees and they had the fireplace going.

Excelente servicio y la comida extraordinaria!!!!!
Recomiendo el lugar para cualquier persona que quiera probar comida puertorriqueña . Cuando vuelva regreso!!!!!!

We went here late one night after class. You walk past a Reginelli's, i believe, and it's right next door. I ordered the grilled shrimp plate. I believe it was around $15.00. The service was great, but the shrimp was so salty/over-seasoned, that I had to wipe each piece of shrimp off with a napkin before eating them. Seriously. 

My friend had the catfish and hers was good. I love my food seasoned, but, when it's overdone to the point that you have to wipe it, it's not a good look. I also didn't think for the price that it was worth it. But, it's open later, so if you need a late-night meal, this place is an option.

Always delicious. Always friendly. And they have grits, which is a huge plus to me. And they'll do half potatoes and half grits as a side on eggs. Only downside is putting the car at a meter. But the prices are low enough that the extra is no big deal. Cash only.

EX.PEN.SIVE.

The rolls are pretty tasteless, save for the spicy rolls, which are too spicy (I think).

The udon is good, but of course, expensive.

Also, slow as beans.
A good place to grab a breakfast or lunch omelet. I recommend their Baja frittata and seasoned potatoes.

I only find myself in Siberia on occasion when I'm catching a show. (And for the delicious food... but that's for a different review.). I appreciate that they offer a specific type of musical act that you can't find much elsewhere in NOLA. And the covers are reasonable. However I do find the drink prices to be a bit higher than comparable establishments in the area so I usually just opt for the $3 high life or bud light. 

Expect a crowd fully invested in the show and the venue being a tight squeeze for the bigger shows. A seat at the bar makes for a good view of the stage if you're lucky enough to snag one. Pro tip: sometimes the back bar is open for cash only.

I guess I went in here with high hopes because I kept hearing how awesome it was.  I liked the free peanuts to snack on while waiting for your order.  

I had to have someone in my party explain to me the difference between burgers.  Apparently a regular burger is a whole pound of meat and a little burger is a half pound of meat?  But that didn't seem right..when I received the burger the patty was that of a McDonald's value menu burger.  

I liked their choices of toppings.  The grilled onions aren't anything special since I don't think they season them with anything.  They also pad the burger with iceburg lettuce if you opt to have lettuce on your burger - so avoid that option if you can't stand a crispy lettuce burger.  I also didn't really like the fact that you can't ask for a rare burger since I usually don't like ground beef well done.  

Their fries come in a drinking cup which makes it kind of hard to pick through all of the baby fries they seem to put in there.  It seemed like the whole cup was baby fries so I kept getting fry sauce all over my fingers.  Their fries were alright, but I prefer Dick's Drive In or In-n-Out fries much better.  It was neat that they tell you where the fries are from that day (Shelley, ID on 1/1/2010).  

It was a little overwhelming to have all of their newspaper clippings surrounding you saying how great they are.  I didn't really concur with the newspaper clippings.  Most of them were from Washington D.C. anyway.  Apparently their deliciousness didn't carry over to Idaho.

I didn't feel too well after eating their meal and neither did the others in my party.  

I'd say if I ever went back I'd probably only eat the free peanuts and order a Coke.

Was so excited to finally get to Upland this past weekend. First of all, this place is HUGE! I was really excited about how much seating they could put in it, and the outside layout is great.

I went to school in Bloomington so Upland is really close to my heart and this one did not disappoint either. The beers were good. My food took a while to come out though and my burger was for sure well done, instead of the medium I asked for.

All in all, the food was good, atmosphere was great, and had a beer selection I loved. Just speed up the service a bit, and cook my burger correctly and I'll be in lol
Great food Jeremy is one hell of a server host or order taker would recommend this food to anyone in the area

Enjoyed our food very much. Great taste and great value. My husband got the fried catfish lunch plate, was awesome! Loved the homemade tartar sauce. My chicken pasta dish with artichokes, tomatoes and capers was very tasty too. Excellent service as well.

Sometimes I think hype can ruin your opinion before it has a chance to form properly... 
I'd been hearing so much about Tijuana Flats for so long that I was practically desperate to go here by the time I finally arrived!

...And it was okay!
The service was friendly, the food came out pretty fast, the place looked pretty clean... but I guess we were there early on a Friday evening and it was pretty quiet, and we didn't bring any booze.... so... 

Maybe I need to go more exotic in my next order. We got handmade chips & queso and it wasn't anything special, and my Dos Tacos plate was good. (I really appreciated that I was allowed to mix it up and have one soft taco and one hard taco!) but I feel like it didn't feel all that authentic -- unless you went crazy with their very fun-looking hot sauce bar. 

I'd ABSOLUTELY eat here again, in particular if someone suggests going back to On the Border... The prices alone and the lack of waiting make it that much better.
I think we just need to bring something to drink and perhaps arrive when it's a little more lively.

Cute little Vietnamese cafe on Magazine Street with very modern decor. We came here for pho after a night of drinking on Bourbon. Ordered the grilled pork springrolls (goi cuon thit nuong), chinese sausage and eggs spring rolls (goi cuon lap xuong voi trung), banh mi, pho oxtail, pho dat biet, and several glasses of cafe sua da.

The service was amazing, the waitress even told us other places to go in New Orleans.

Now look, I have literally been to almost every Lebanese, middle-eastern restaurant in New Orleans, and I can tell you that The Halal Guys is leagues below the quality, and taste. It's 10 dollars for a platter of minute rice, (gyro meat, falafel, or chicken), and some iceberg lettuce and diced tomatoes! At least make a salad with lemon olive oil and some olives. The food just tastes poor and just really bad. Now, the only reason I'm giving this business a 3 star rating, is because the customer service, cleanliness, friendliness, and location is exceptional. If you want good Lebanese style food, then go to Lebanon's Cafe, or Byblo's. If you want a cool place to go with a group of friends, then this could be an okay option.

This place was such an awesome place when I first starting working Downtown, about 10 years ago.  Since then, It has slowly dwindle down to what it is now:

   A fast food Mexican sit-down restaurant AKA Expensive Los Betos.

And the cashier that works here has no business working with people.  She had the worst attitude and was rolling her eyes when I was asking her about the menu.

I got the Chicken Flautas.  They tasted and felt as if they were fried earlier in the day and microwaved.  Microwaved with the lettuce, tomatoes, and rice.  I know when lettuce has been microwaved.  I would have sent the plate back, but then I would have had to deal with the cashier again.

Maybe it was a bad day, but after today, I will probably not return until 2016.

Note: The soups most people were eating/drinking looked pretty damn tasty.

Our favorite. My husband didn't even like sushi until he set foot in here, and we make the hike from Elkton just to indulge here, and we are never disappointed. Byob, excellent service, ambiance... The Vietnamese roll is my favorite.

This place is my favorite Indian restaurant in Reno. The naan is great and I highly recommend their chai. They have many vegetarian options which are great, and the meat dishes are also amazing. The service was also great and they were always checking up on us to make sure that we had enough refills or to ask if we needed anything else. The location is interesting, it's right next to the old Starlight Lanes bowling Alley which is currently defunct, but it doesn't bother me. The atmosphere of Taste of India is fairly casual. It's my go-to and I'll be returning there many times.

Came here for the first time on Monday. 
I had a carnitas burrito wet with red sauce. The burrito was good with a lot of flavor. Carnitas were delicious. 
My girlfriend had a RBC burrito and a crispy chicken taco she loved everything.
The salsa was delicious one of the best. It's not to watery and the seasoning was on point. 
Will definitely come back to Rudy's great little spot.

From the hostess, to the bartender, and every other server (they use team effort); to a person the service was outstanding. Oh,the food, just the same.  Wonderful atmosphere and fair pricing.  This place is worth the drive; keep up the great work!

Something Sweet is right! 
This place delivers on sweetness and does it well!

Sweet drinks, Sweet pies/cakes.  
Could use a sweet update on decor though... 
they are a bit blahh in that department. Oh well!

Terrible, terrible, terrible!!! As a patron that actually lives in Nashville, I will NEVER ever step foot back in this establishment, nor will anyone in my party and then some. We were there for 2 hours, had the worst service I have ever experienced in a restaurant (saw our server for a total of approx 4 min in the 2 hours).....I even had to get up from the table and go to the bar to purchase a drink. The food is mediocre at best. If you are going to charge high end prices for a burger then I suggest you don't precook them in the kitchen and then warm them up so they are over well done and crunchy!!! Disgusting!!! Tourists....I really really recommend going elsewhere!! I am one to give a raving review when deserved, but it was the worst $130 (for 3 people) that was spent!

We had my mothers birthday party catered by this Olive Garden.  We ordered the pasta stations.  The food arrived hot, was exactly what we expected (this is two different kinds of pasta, three sauces, meatballs, sausage, and grilled chicken, salad, breadsticks, grated Parmesan, even the signature dressing in a bottle and the dessert mints!).  Our set up was done by Holly, who did a great job.  Our hostess that took the order was Kathy, and everything went very smoothly.  Very nice!  Will use them again for future needs!

This place is great, on Gulfport beach (across the street). Small quaint town, nice quiet beach, beautiful scenery, couldn't ask for better on a Sunday!
Food was great, HUGE sandwiches, menu items were original (lobster salad sandwich) w/ fries, which were excellent. Reasonably priced, considering the view and peace and quiet. It gets crowded busy, but well managed. You can sit inside or our on the patio. Take a stroll after lunch thru town or sit on the beach and watch the boats go by!
Definitely will be back with friends.

We were a large group, and we had a reservation at Red Fish Grill; however, apparently something happened, and we were delayed in getting to our table by almost an hour.  Of course, we spent that time drinking at the bar, which had an above-average beer selection, so we weren't entirely miserable -- but it was quite crowded, and they seemed a bit dismayed that our large party was crowding up the entryway, so it was a bit hard to feel welcome.

Once we were seated, the servers were attentive and helpful.
