After dinner we walked out onto the lawn to the river walk to view the lights and take in little stroll before returning to the valet.  They have complimentary valet so parking is not a problem.
Overall I did enjoy the restaurant and will return again to try more items.
It looks a little suspect from the outside, but inside it is clean and comfortable.  The food is well-priced, cooked appropriately, and really tasty.  I will definitely go again.

All of the servers are very friendly and helpful to one another.  Their uniform is jeans and non matching polos, very informal.  The decor is clean, pleasant with a touch of country charm.

We couldn't decide what to get, so the server very nicely brought us a taste sample.  Yep, the Montana Chili was worth ordering.  Yummy and not too spicy at all.  It came with fresh crunchy tortilla chips with just the right amount of salt.  

One main reason I continue to come here is for the hash browns.  They are awesome.  Cooked all the way through in butter, crunchy and great compared to the half cooked hash browns that seem to be the norm these days.

The bacon was just the right amount of crispy without being over done and chewy. The moist fluffy scrambled eggs looked great, but they were a bit bland.  Not sure how to fix that besides adding more pepper or butter.

There was a 15 minute wait for the food but with ordering the chili and meatball dish, it probably took them a while to get it together.  The meatballs were very full flavored, a touch spicy and chewy.  The hoagie roll was very fresh and soft.

Soda tasted good.  No music blaring in the background.  This was my daughter's favorite restaurant.

Tried the deep dish. It wasn't bad pizza but I guess my expectations were high after the rave reviews.  The pizza sauce was a bit too acidic and sour for my taste. My choice of mushrooms and spinach wasn't great since have the whole pizza a very mushy taste.  Gotta say though, the crust was awesome.  

I'll keep my 3 star rating for now but will definitely give them another chance in the future.

Parking in Nashville is RIDICULOUS. The closest public parking appears to cost $10. The restaurant has a big sign out front to let you know that they have their own parking, but it fails to mention that you have to drive around the block to get there, and God help your undercarriage as you pull in! If we hadn't enjoyed the Urban Cookhouse in Montgomery, AL so much, I would have driven on.

The line was out the door; I hadn't realized that it was Thirtysomething Meet Market Day. But the food was our sole objective here. Different menu than the one in Montgomery; not surprised given their local food raison d'etre. I ordered a Cubano, Darling Bride wanted an Urban Cowboy (it's a sandwich), and the Boy ordered a Buffalo Chicken wrap. We all ordered the cheddar pasta as our side, and we got an order of their orange yeast rolls as our appetizer.

"Cheddar pasta" is their fancy way of saying "mac and cheese." It's pretty darn good. So was my Cubano; no surprise, as I think serving subferior barbecued pork is against the law in Nashville. Judging by the way the others' food disappeared like your friends when there's a couch to move, it was good, too. If they fix the entrance to the parking lot, I'll give them 5 stars.

Its a complete disappointment. the food itself was inedible and i will not stand to be paying for something to be sub par. My boyfriend and i decided to order in on our anniversary and was shocked to get this kind of laziness. the freaking ribs that my boyfriend ordered were inedible and burnt to crisp, it didnt even look like we could get some meat since it was dry and hard. on top of that the fries were missing. How can you send an order without checking its quality and making sure that orders are complete. To say the least this wasnt the first time we've been here and are thinking of making it our last. Its disappointing to see this in an establishment who is well known, but bringing out a shitty order. Applebees used to be great, i dont know what is going on.

Went there for the first time last night and it was amazing!!  Our party actually had 3 kids and I was so surprised (and excited) to see a kids menu, high chairs, and even a changing table in the bathroom.  The food was delicious and the beer was amazing. I loved the Hefeweizen.

Love this place!  The acorn squash salad is the best.  Great location to drop in for lunch or for large group gatherings. The illy coffee is served to perfection although I wish they had an option for coconut milk. Sandwiches are rather large, so best to plan on sharing or taking a doggie bag.

I've never had Vietnamese food before and I would definitely recommend going here. The staff were great help when we were deciding what to eat from their huge menu. It had flavors I've never tasted before and much better quality than Chinese food. I would totally come back!

You can't go wrong here.  Chicago Deep Dish pizza is to die for.  Love the sauce.  Their Sicilian pizza is awesome.  The crust is very light and crisp, not weighed down and doughy like other Sicilian pizzas.  Their wings are decent but are a little chewy.  We like our wings not so jerky like.  Their mild wing sauce was delish.  We will be back!  (The owner is extremely nice, makes you feel like you're part of the family!)

I came in here for a late lunch and not many people were here. When I walked in, I thought to myself, this is a pleasant restaurant. The service and the good was good. I had the Tom Kha soup (coconut soup with lime), which was probably my first time having it and I enjoyed it. I practically finished it to the last drop. I also ordered a sushi combo bento box which came with pad thai. I love pad thai and have high standards for pad thai. I would give it 4/5 on it, but overall, the sushi was pretty good.

A little pricey, but worth every penny.  Whether your looking for a place for a special celebration or just a date night you won't go wrong with the chophouse.  Their prime rib is outstanding and seafood is cooked to perfection.  The wait staff is super knowledgeable and courteous which makes the evening a real treat.

I need to update now that there is a new owner. The menu is smaller which I think is good because they can do a few things really well. We got some wings for their wing wednesday deal. It's 50 cents per wing. Today they had a special peppercorn Parmesan creamy sauce. My bf got 15 buffalo wings and I got 6 parm sauce wings. The sauce was so delicious. It was a little salty but I expect wing sauce to be salty. It goes with the wings. He made them carefully because of my bf's allergy (which the old owner could care less about). The new owner really took the time to make our meal great. For 50 cents per wing it was a great deal and much better than any other bbq place in the area. The blue cheese dressing also tasted homemade because it had a strong blue cheese flavor with big chunks in it. It's not the common Ken's dressing that is questionable about whether it is actually blue cheese. We will be back to try more things. I also thought the waitress was nice and personable. Stop in and try the new food if you've had a bad experience in the past with the old owner.

Best way to describe twisted ranch is ... solid. The food was great for the price that is paid. The food has tremendous value. The restaurant itself is in a historic building in soulard that comes equipped with stainless steel tables and very cleanly amenities, including the bathroom! The fries and tater tots were fried to perfection. As well as the mass amounts of different ranch we're above average! I personally do not care for ranch but this place will hit anyone's taste! I got the BBQ ranch at the recommendation of our server (I wish I could remember her name) as well as the buffalo ranch. Both sauces were amazing. The other flavors covered most ranch taste, but gave off a different texture and flavor than traditional BBQ/ buffalo sauces and this is the reason I will come back... the server herself was a fantastic server keeping drinks refreshed and taking orders in a timely manner. The only reason I am docking a star is because the wait for our food was quite a bit longer than expected. Other tables that walked in after as well as ordered after us received there food first and our wait was a good 45min - Hour. Other than that the food was terrific and warrants a second trip!
Reasonable drink prices and specials. Good chips and queso. Not at all into either entree we tried. Not as clean as we would expect, for example, there was dried food all over the menu!

So I am an avid Dat Dog fan! Y'all were on my "must eat" list for my out of town wedding guests! I particularly enjoy their cheddar bacon ranch fries! Which I had for the first time Halloween night in 2015 where I met the owner (you probably don't remember me I was wearing a mad hatter costume at the Frenchman location) anyways I have always been impressed by the service and of course the food is spectacular! But I went to Voodoo Fest (VIP section) and I was absolutely BLOWN AWAY!!! So as I mentioned before the cheddar bacon ranch fries are my absolute favorite!! Well y'all didn't have it on the menu so when I went to order I asked if it was possible for them to be made and Jackie was working the register and she said absolutely! Then found out they didn't have ranch and so suggested BBQ sauce and let I found my new favorite thing!!! It is AMAZING!! Please try it and consider adding it to your menu cause it was absolutely phenomenal! If you do add it to your menu I suggest the name "the voodoo Jackie" cause she is the one that made it all happen and as much as it is truly on my bucket list to have a menu item named after me (the voodoo elena) lol it was her and the above and beyond service that made it happen! I also have to brag on Jason! It was Saturday night and I forget exactly what happened but the tank needed to be changed I had ordered already and they told me to come back in a few mins. I think I may have taken longer than I should've so they were packing up but Jason not only hunted down my dog he made it for me and because of the mix up offered a free dog and fries for Sunday! He remembered me Sunday took care of me personally made me "the voodoo Jackie (or elena)" jazzed up my dog for me and was absolutely awesome! I cannot brag on Jackie and Jason enough! The whole team really that worked voodoo went absolutely above and beyond great customer service they were absolutely SUPERB!!! Brie was the only other persons name I caught but I had to write this and brag on them cause Jackie and Jason remembering me and being so incredibly accommodating it truly blew me away! I very rarely leave reviews but I absolutely had to for multiple reasons one the new menu suggestion and two to tell you how spectacular your staff is!!! Thank you Jackie and Jason y'all truly made my voodoo experience!!!

how is there only one review of this place?

this is probably my favorite breakfast place in the world, or a close second to cosmo's in montreal. this is not brunch. repeat: THIS IS NOT BRUNCH. brunch is recycled leftovers from the night before. this is all super fresh, done competently, and usually delicious. the fritattas can be out of this world, and the waffle topping are great. even the coffee is good!

the place is small, so get there early or be prepared to wait. but it's totally worth it.

I think this is the best vegan restaurant I have ever been to.  The menu was innovative, presentations were interesting, the service was friendly, and the food was fabulous!  We loved every dish that we ordered and can't wait to visit Philly again to try more!  Also, we didn't have any, but the cocktails looked great as well.

I feel bad leaving a "less than stellar" review, but I'm just not feeling it today. It was a night out for me and a close friend. Have only been once, quite some time ago. Coworker was excited I was going. 

Service was a tad slow, but it was starting to pick up as we ordered. Wednesday was wing night. They're really nothing to write home about. $0.39 each and there's not a lot of meat to them. Flavour alright (honey garlic & teriyaki). The teriyaki ones were barely warm and the honey garlic were still a few degrees from hot. In the darkness of the pub my friend and I questioned the "doneness" of the wings. Is chicken pink? How pink can chicken be? After we each ate a few, we figured we might as well finish them, if we're going to be sick, we're going to be sick. 

Drink specials were ok tonight, $4 Caesar & Long Island. 

Thought about ordering more food, but turned to Yelp and wandered off to a place down the road for further food.

Wouldn't put this place high on my list to return to.

Sorry! If you're going to do a wing night, do a WING NIGHT right.

This place is adorable! Really nice and open ambiance. For sure get the frose (frozen rose). I had the biscuit with country fried pork and sausage gravy and it was the best of all comfort foods. My friends got the avocado toast and hangover bowl and they were also amazing. Service was the best we had in New Orleans. Gets busy so if you're in a rush you may want to skip because they'll likely be on a wait for a weekend brunch.

I was excited to visit this Next Door American Eatery.  I am not sure what I was expecting, but the space itself was nice and modern, the food was ok and seemed fresh, but I would love to have seen a more artfully executed menu.  It's a bit pricy, but proceeds, I understand, go to support local education, which is well worth it.
Broken Goblet is doing a good job of keeping their patrons socially distanced during these trying times. I was pleasantly surprised by the number of beers they're currently offering.

Great location but looks like that made them nonchalant about the food. We ordered fish sandwiches and looks like all they did was just reheat it from the frozen packets they came from. The Mac n cheese for kids was literally the Kraft kind from grocery store. There was no effort put into the food. No flavor no effort no nothing.

HOLY CRAP AMAZING FOOD! The Bernie sandwich is super big and filling! My husband got the turkey burger and it was flavorful and juicy. I have the say the portions are worth the prices. They also have a happy hour menu with choices. I would definitely come back again! I highly recommend it.

This place definitely left something to be desired. Menu was WAY overpriced for the quality of food. I got the Crawfish ravioli, only had 4 small crawfish in it and was supposed to have a crab topper, still looking for it. My wife had the shrimp and grits, 3 small shrimp and some grits that were over cooked. Stuffed mushroom app was okay, service was okay. Bill was $68 no beverages, maybe had we racked up a $40 Bar tab first the food wouldn't had been so disappointing.

I was on a short roadtrip to Santa Barbara and after a bike ride along the beach I was hungry for seafood. I greeted by Jonny and was seated at the counter overlooking the open kitchen. I was looking at the oyster selection and Jonny gave me run down on the oysters they served. I ordered a half dozen oysters mixed variety.  They were very fresh and tasty along with a nice mignonette sauce and seafood sauce with a dollop of horseradish an addition of both a lime and lemon wedge. Looking over the menu and with the recommendation from Jonny I ordered their house Cioppino which was loaded with shellfish (king crab, mussels, clams,scallops, shrimp) in a very flavorful broth set inside a bread bowl. I barely finished the shellfish and could only finish some of the bread that soaked in the great broth.
Jonny was very helpful, courteous and very alert to the needs of his guests. 
When I'm back in the area again I will definitely stop in for great food and service!

This place is seriously great. I was impressed with the variety of options they have. They also provide a large portion, so it is easy to split the food between two people, or two meals. Their desserts are also pretty good. I will definitely be coming back.

I've loved this place since it was called Spice Avenue! The $10 lunch buffet is so satisfying. The staff is always friendly; my best friend and I eat here often and one of the ladies always encourages to go for the rice pudding after we've over done it on the buffet haha! Definitely my go-to Indian food!
Poor service.  Food oversalted and oily.  The owner did not speak to us, only greeting one table out of six.  No longer sells fresh oysters.  Disappointed.

The place is a little small so it will be really crowd on weekend. But it is clean and nice. I came here on the lunch time and the table was almost full.

I went here several times, but today is my visit after more than a year. Nothing quite change. And i ordered the same menu, tan tan Noodle which was ok. My mom ordered spicy ramen that tasted good. And takoyaki for appetizer.

The price of the ramen is average about 10 dolars or so. U'll get a medium size of bowl. And u have to pay for hot tea, 1 dolar and no refill. Better ask for water if u want to save some money. Lol.

Ordered a pizza and stuffed bread sticks. Also - a couple of sauces. Took quite a while for delivery and when I got my delivery sauces weren't there. I called and all they said was they'd bring my sauce when the driver got back. Still waiting for my sauces right now! Can't wait to dip my cold pizza and bread into this sauce if it ever shows up!!!! Not holding my breath. 
So then he never came back and was supposed to come get pizza and bread and issue a refund after waiting for so long. Still no show!!!
Ok so driver made it back at 1:15am to pickup my pizza and issue a full refund. That was amazing of him!! Big shout out to the delivery driver! Big thumbs down to the manager for hanging up on me!!!

Ha so I ended up finding my sauce the next day in a random bag... sorry dominos driver. You rock- still don't like the manager though because he was mean and hung up on me!!!

If I knew then what I know now, I would have ordered my food to go. 

Conveniently located in the beautiful Marriott hotel, this was an easy pick for dinner. Luckily my good company helped distract the fact that so much time had passed before someone actually waited on us. And by the time he finally did come by, we were ready to order our entire meal with our drinks. Aside from him taking the order, he was nearly a ghost the rest of the dining experience. 

I will say, the food was delicious. They were kind enough to give a complimentary salad and dessert. The salads could've gone with far less onions but that's my personal preference. Besides that, the steak was cooked as ordered, lobster ravioli was delicious and the asparagus and creamed spinach were great vegetable sides. 

Overall, definitely lacking in the service department, especially for such a nice hotel. Would dine here again if I had a plethora of time and patience, otherwise I'd go somewhere else.

Excellent!!!! Got the ham fried rice and 1/2 an order of general tso's chicken. I tried the chicken based on the reviews and I'm so glad I did. Been looking for a good rice place in the city. The reviews about the location aren't as bad as they seem. Yes there were people in a few booths selling things but they didn't hassle anyone. I went on a Friday evening and they were busy. But I figure busy is good!

I'm one of the few who has had BOTH the yogurt and the sushi here - not at the same time, I promise.  

Sushi: I've snacked on the California roll and the baby octopus.  I'm a big fan of both here.

Yogurt: I've tried a lot of the flavors, though I usually choose the original, which reminds me vaguely of Pinkberry (yum).  I find some of their flavors to taste a little artificial, but my friends never have this complaint.  Their topping selection is solid, with lots of fruits and candy/chocolate, plus cereals, nuts, and syrups.  The punch card is good incentive to keep coming back, and their daily deals are cool - 2 punches instead of 1, bring a dude and get 50% off, etc.  

I've heard it sometimes turns into a strange dance club atmosphere after work... somehow that seems like the last thing I'd want to walk into after a long day at work, but apparently it's entertaining to observe.
Solid 7.1 on the David Portnoy pizza scale.  GREAT CRUST, thin and crispy.  Not greasy.  Wonderful sauce and perfect amount of cheese. Slices could be larger but overall a great pizza place!

This is a brand new BYOB restaurant conveniently located right next to a liquor store.  I ate dinner there with some friends and the food was great.  I got an appetizer called golder bags or something close to that and it was amazing.  For the entree I got the surf and turf hot rock.  They bring a piece of rock that has been heated to about 800F to your table with shrimp, beef, scallop, etc.  It's sizzling and cooks right in front of you.  The aromas were amazing.  The service could improve slightly but as I mentioned before, they are brand new and there are always a few kinks that need to be worked out at first.  I'm sure however that they will be running smoothly soon and that the quality of the service will improve to meet the quality of the food.
This place is fantastic!  There is a load of meat in their cheese steak!  Go here when you're on South Street because they've been here since 1986.
We have been here a few times.  Best BBQ we have found locally. Friendly service. Looking forward to going back again.  Take some sauce home. It is reasonably priced and delicious.

Great Place and looking forward to going back very soon.  My Granddaughter had a great time playing and great to see her jumping up and Down anytime she made the ball in.  Kids meal was also good to go along with the regular menu for adults.

Last night my wife and I decided we'd like to use our gift certificates here, but were not impressed when we discovered that this location is no longer accepting them. 

They were a Christmas gift from my parents and they had bought us the same ones last year, apparently from Costco, and we had used them at this location without any difficulty last year. We also dined here on a few other occasions. We liked it here, but I'm not sure I'll ever be back.

We walked in the restaurant and right away had noticed a sign saying they didn't accept the Costco gift certificates. Oh, great. I talked to the manager and he gave me a line of BS about corporate restaurants and franchise restaurants. 

When that didn't faze me, he explained that they didn't like them because Costco charges $80 for $100 worth of gift certificates, so they lose $20. I hadn't even been aware that they were purchased at Costco and I don't care.

My wife, who loves to sign up for newsletters, pointed out that Ric's Grill is offering a deal through bookatable.ca, which the manager informed us is owned by Ric's Grill, where you can buy a $75 gift certificate for $40. They're losing nearly half there, so they're worried about a measly $10 on a $50 gift certificate? And it's not like we only have gone there with gift certificates or spend only what our gift certificate will cover.

It's also short-sighted because we've always said nice things about Ric's Grill. We like the downtown location, the food has always been good and the service, not bad. Are we likely to say anything nice now or go back? Yeah, right. We're going to tell everyone our story.

Great business plan there guys. If your restaurant is going to participate in a gift certificate deal with a store like Costco, don't play games and have stores opt out because they're afraid of losing a bit in the deal. When businesses start arguing over these kinds of things it makes me wonder how long they're going to be around.

I'm really not impressed.

I had the Sonoran hotdog and what was essentially a carne asada quesadilla.  The hotdog sounded great, looked great, but was really nothing special.  The quesadilla was good but nothing spectacular.  My take?  This guero expected more and didn't find it here.

Absolutely terrible.  I hesitated to write this review because our waitress was so kind.  This review is no reflection on her whatsoever.  This is strictly based on the horrific dining experience we had here about a month ago.

We arrived at the restaurant at 1:30, a half hour before brunch ends.  We offered to leave, but we were told it was ok to stay.  We should have gone with our first thought.  The food was absolutely awful.

I had bananas foster. It tasted rubbery and hard like it was old and microwaved repeatedly.  The bananas were too hard to bite. My fiance' had the chicken and waffles.  His waffles were gummy and his chicken was flavorless. Their potatoes were the worst either of us have ever tasted. We were extremely disappointed with our meals.

I should point out that the whole reason we stopped here in the first place was because we visited the Philadelphia location countless times in the past and the food was always fantastic. This was not even close to what we were accustomed to. Granted, we DID get there 30 minutes before brunch ended, so we probably got all the scraps, but I'd prefer they just say,"We're closing" and send us on our way.

Appearance-wise, the place is small, but charming. However, simply put.... the food was disgusting.  After we left, we ended up going to ANOTHER restaurant because we were still hungry. No one should ever have to do that.
I had the delicious Ahi Tuna salad. My server was very knowledgeable about the menu and answered my questions about the food.

People seem either too ashamed or too shy to tell how hot they ordered their chicken. I am a pretty shameless person, and no one has ever described me as shy. I feel that this is pertinent information, so I'll tell you.

I got the "hot." As did my husband. We like hot stuff. Hot was perfect.

Our poor friend, on the other hand, went for "damn hot." The difference is insane. He couldn't even finish it. Of course, out of morbid curiosity, we just had to try a bite.........

And the next day, we were moving. (And so were our bowels...?) Even after just a bite, each of us had some sort of bathroom emergency that we had to take a break for.

Yet I want to go back soon!!! And never attempt anything spicier than "hot" again.

As far as the sides go, pimiento Mac and cheese was awesome. Black eyed peas were a little disappointing (kind of like the band). Get extra pickles! Oh my god, you'll need them.

My go to spot for breakfast. There's nothing to compare it to because it is in a class of its own. I could eat snicker doodle pancakes for the rest of my life and die a happy man. Then add great service, and amazing Benedicts. I love Baja.

Delicious authentic Chinese food! Did not expect to find authentic Chinese food near Treasure Island/St.Pete but the food was just as tasty as flushing! We had the garlic pea shoots and the half of ginger scallion chicken both well cooked. Only weird part was owner was surprised wife wanted to use chopsticks, kept offering her knife and forks. Recommend them for authentic Chinese food!
Best Long Island Ice Teas in the country!  Great food...wings, fish, pastrami sandwiches, apps, etc.  All great!!  The bartenders are great as well.
If you have a chance to come here and you don't, you're a real shmuck. Large portions and delicious. No booze, but nice big cups of ice for your soda choice. Stop thinking and drive over already
Consistently good food, good atmosphere inside and out.  Much better choice for eats than Hannegan's next door.

Really bad food today, the fries weren't fresh I felt like I went through a drive through. The Ahi appetizer we got was bad, no flavor to it and the avocado wasn't ripe it was like chewing plastic. The fish had freezer burn and the French dip sandwich had old fatty over cooked roast beef. What's happened to this place? The service was good though, hence the one star. I complained about the bad appetizer and they refunded it but I didn't want to complain about the whole meal, if everything was that bad they should know already.

I just moved to Tucson and came across this lovely coffee shop, I'm a big vibe person and all good vibes here, friendly people, great coffee and the owners are so sweet and friendly! They also serve beers at night that I haven't experienced yet but will be in the near future.

I have only ordered from here a couple of times, as I prefer the Chicken Panang that I make at home. However, the other day when I wanted to make my favorite dish, I realized that I had run out of Kaffir Lime Leaves. The other Thai restaurant that I normally frequent was closed, due to it being a Monday. Lemongrass, however, was open and fully welcoming to my presence even when I seemingly interrupted their family lunch time (it was in between the lunch and dinner rush). Upon hearing my inquiry, the kind lady offered me several leaves in a nice ziplock bag at no charge. I felt bad about not having any cash on me, as I usually pay $5 dollars to express my gratitude, but she insisted and I thanked her and went on my way. Thanks to Lemongrass, I was able to complete the dinner that I had planned for my friend and I! I will definitely return as a dining patron in the future!

Thanks to all the good reviews we checked into this tiny little hole in the wall. Well, first we passed it even with google maps directing us because it's in an older residential neighborhood...there's no way a restaurant could be in this place, but we flipped a U and found it. 
The place is small, and if it weren't for good reviews I would've skipped right over it. It's clear this place isn't there for looks- but man oh man does it make up for it with hospitality and especially the food. 
Al was behind the counter- cheerful, joking, and ready to cook us up something awesome. I didn't know what I wanted so he suggested the pork shanks- which he threw in the fryer. I'd never had pork shanks before, and let me tell you- lip smacking, finger licking good swimming in his bbque-esque sauce. The beans were spicy and tasty and the smashed tatoes were good as well- all rounded out with a delightful fluffy biscuit. 
My husband ordered a cheese burger and holy burger- that thing was huge! It's probably the first burger my husband wasn't able to finish. It was juicy with hand pressed meat that had been mixed with something special. And that bacon was smokey and delicious. 
We're heading back for breakfast tomorrow... And I can't wait!

So many people had said this was just an ok trip and over rated so I wasn't going to waste the money.  As my husband and I were strolling down the river walk, a very nice lady came up and said, two members of their tour didn't show up and did we want free tickets.  Sure why not.  We sat with the tour group and had a great time.  The trip comes with lunch buffet which was just ok.  The main dish was fried catfish which I happen to like, my husband doesn't but it was pretty good.  They of course had okra which was nasty, red beans and rice and some BBQ dish.  

You travel up the river and there is a guide who points things out of interest which is fine if you happen to be on the correct side of the boat.  There is also a jazz band that plays.  They aren't wonderful but it was nice to listen to.  

It was just sort of boring in my book.  Had we paid for it I would have been disappointed.  Since it was free was glad that we got to do it.

First time to eat here. Took my wife daughter and niece for a birthday dinner and was pretty excited. We were greeted professionally inside immediately once we entered. Jed our server was right on the spot and asked us if we were interested in drinks. We ordered our drinks and return in a few minutes and asked us if we were ready to order. He was great at explaining the menu and how it matched out tastes. Each of us ordered a different kind of steak. I decides on the Spinalis and was excellent. Well prepared and very tasty. The side dishes were really good as well. Large portions so a little goes a long way. They provided a desert for my daughters birthday and she said it was super. Overall a great experience. The decor was trendy with an open feeling and the food we had was superb. Definitely a high end place to eat in the central Indiana area.

I really enjoyed this bar. On a hot Nashville day, my wife found this jewel in Printers Alley.  It almost has a dive bar appeal to it, dark, cool with quite conversations going on.  They have separate more intimate area you can sit and be alone and secluded with that special someone.  I came back in the evening a few days later and they have song writers playing their own music on stage in a very personal setting.  Truly recommend an escape from the summer heat!

Hot and new! Not AYCE. Clean, simple intimate atmosphere. Great for small appetites, solo or entry level sushi diners. Food was super fresh, with nice portion sizes. Music included a lot of my favorite artists. Had an elegantly sufficient meal and personable conversation with the owner Mark. Please support this unique small business.

Well I have been sitting here since 10:50. It's 11:27 and they forgot a sandwich when they finally called my name. I don't think it takes this long for any other. I haven't even tasted it yet. Might not even be hungry and this long wait. All for two hot sausage and a hamburger.

Although there are great beer and food selections, improved bar tending service and daily specials has offset some of the overpriced beer and menu items. I tend to avoid times when the bar gets overcrowded.

On my first visit I didn't have a clue what to expect. After going over the menu, I was able to comprehend the concept. What a great idea! A combination of Southern American Classics and Italian Classics I had grown up with and cooked my entire life. Fried chicken, grits, pasta and pizza. I was primarily an Italian chef and always can appreciate a new level of creative thinking. Noble has taken classics a step and a half higher. We started with a Mushroom Pizza as an appetizer. Perfert crust! Yes, I would call it noble! Flavorful like no pizza I've ever eaten.Then the Rigatoni with Short Rib reminded me of Sunday dinner as a kid, but mom never did a Ragu this tasty. (Sorry mom). With ricotta and chunks of fresh mozzarella... Oh my! My date had the steak which was delicious as well. The only catch is they do not prepare it rare. All steaks are medium rare and above. Not something I would order in this amazing place. We went back a second time for a quick bite one nite and ordered a Bianco Pizza and a Noble Pig Calzone. Holy cow! Who would ever think a "white" pizza could be packed with so many flavors! Rosemary, pistachio, truffle! Every bite was an adventure! The Calzone was stuffed with a variety of Italian meats and treats. Of course the crust again was perfect, perfect, perfect! In all my years I've never had a regular restaurant I visited except my own . This place will definitely be a regular stop for me. My goal is to eat my way through the entire menu. 5 stars + an off the hook!

Cozy family owned restaurant serving authentic middle eastern food. I'm quite confused about the restaurant name : Gyro zone, but inside, it says Worlds best Shawarma!  Anyway we tried an appetizer Baba Ganoush! It's a dip with pita ! It's delicious! The owner said its home made. He is the cook and the server at that time. We tried the Chicken Shawarma! It's very good!
Will recommend to friends and family!

Absolutely a wonderful place to grab lunch or a snack. Handcrafted soups are what their known for, but their salads don't disappoint either. Love the African peanut soup, and the chopped salad is always great. Order online and skip the line, use the pickup window near the back!

Super delicious! Had the waffles and chicken with family and friends. Outdoor dining was super nice during the summer in NOLA. My grandmama and mama had omelettles with spinach and gruyere.  
Green SaladFried Chicken

The best place for a fancy celebratory drink in town! This place makes everything possible in house - infused liquors, bitters, etc. Each drink is unique and fun. The bartenders and servers are SO knowledgeable, so just tell them what you like and they'll help you find the perfect drink!
On the weekend, be prepared to wait. This is not a "standing room" type of place. You must be seated by the hostess in order to get a drink. Because of this, the atmosphere is top notch. I've sat at tables and at the bar several times. Each have their pros and cons (easy for a group of 2 at the bar, more than that is better at a table). I love the Patterson house and will always recommend it!

Had dinner here for our first time and definitely not the last, the Ahi Tuna salad was awesome, burgers were terrific as well. Had the sampler app and wings and loved it all. Friendly staff as well, loved it and recommend you try!!!

I was without my partner in BBQ this evening for dinner so I wasn't able to try enough menu items for a definitive review but am giving them 4 stars for effort and intent until I can come back and try some more.  I like the menu.  You can create whatever combination makes you happy.  I wanted to try the ribs and pulled pork but was afraid it would be too much food.  You never know how meaty the ribs are from joint to joint.  These are not meaty at all.  You could eat a whole rack and I could have ordered another meat to try as well.  These don't need sauce. They have a huge amount of glaze built up into a candied sticky sweet rib.  They're chewy but still a little moist.  This isn't my style of rib at all really but I did enjoy eating them.  I like mine meatier, juicier and a lot more savory than these.  They're lean baby backs and I think they went too far with the sugar but that's my preference.  I would like to try the pulled pork and some of the other meats to see how well they actually barbecue something.  I didn't get much smoke on these but they might just have been covered up with the sauce.  

I tried the KC, the Lou and the Peachy sauces and didn't like the KC or the Lou.  Way too much chili powder for me.  They're really very similar in basic flavor.  I liked the Peachy a bit more but didn't love it.  I would try these again on some of their other meats to see how they marry up but am not a big fan of any of them.  They also have a XXX sauce and a Thai sauce for those who would care.  Neither are real BBQ sauces.

I tried the tequila lime green beans and the burnt ends beans for sides.  I really liked the green beans.  They were haricot verts.  Nice job.  I didn't like the baked beans.  I want to taste the beans.  These are heavily seasoned, again with too much chili powder for me.  They're trying too hard from the food I tried.  Everything needs to be a little subtler.  Simpler.  This food emanates from Southern food which is simple food done well.  I want to taste the pork, the beans, all the main ingredients.  I want them prepared perfectly and seasoned to compliment their essence.  

Two different guys came out to check to make sure I liked my food.  That's really awesome.  I appreciated the effort.  It's a nice place.  I really like the vibe and the service.  Last bit of constructive criticism.  I hated the plastic, paper and styrofoam.  Especially the plastic tableware.  The knife snapped trying to cut the ribs and the plastic wrapping clung to my fingers after I tried to get the utensils unwrapped.  Could you wash something?  How about trays with butcher paper like you get at a lot of BBQ places?  Styrofoam really bums me out.  All the sides and drinks use styrofoam.  How about using that biodegradable plastic tableware?.  Too much waste and this place really isn't a dive.  Consider how you can deliver this product without some or all of this.  Please consider your responsibility to your community and planet.  Thanks.  I am really at 3 stars but am giving them a pass until I can try some more of their barbecue.

I'm updating my review - the last review that I wrote was in mid-2014. I had gone to Rigo's many times after that, and noticed some aspects that the restaurant needs to change. 

Believe me, I dislike leaving bad reviews, and will not leave bad ones unless I feel like the business is deserving of such review.

Let me start off with the positives. The food is consistent. I didn't notice any differences in the taste of the food, and it has been good for the times I have gone to Rigo's. They have pretty good deals for buffets. 

Here's the downfall: the service. I went with my parents a few weekends ago, because other places were packed. We all asked for water before ordering our food, and the waitress very rudely placed (more accurately, slammed) the water on our table before walking away. We asked for straws, and she returned with those much later, and carelessly threw them on the table, giving us a look before leaving. Instead of getting the buffet, my dad decided to order off of the menu, and asked for extra jalapenos on the side after the order came. We never saw the jalapenos... well, we never saw her. I would have been more reasonable with my review if there were many people in the restaurant, but the restaurant was quite slow, and the waitress couldn't have had many people to attend. 

I have never seen service that bad before, especially when I was with my parents, who are elderly. I, a long time supporter of Rigo's, will not go back until news has it that they have upped their service.

Another great meal at what has become my favorite Italian restaurant.  It has been months since we've been able to eat out, and it was soooooo worth it.  We were celebrating our anniversary and it was a given that we would eat at Maialina.  We invited our best friends to dinner to help us celebrate.  As soon as we walked in, we were sincerely greeted with a "happy anniversary" and it just felt soooo good to be back at Maialina.

The menu is currently smaller than usual, but not to fear . . . they still have many of your favorites!  We started with the parmesan garlic toast, which was bursting with parmesan flavor and came with marinara sauce, meatballs (oh, the meatballs!), and the calimari (the best in town - not sure how they bread it so lightly and it turns out so crisp yet tender.)

Our entrees were chicken parmesan with spaghetti pomodoro, lasagna, and the Gamberi.    Amazing lemon gelato and a lemon cake with mixed berries for dessert. Everything was absolutely perfect!  We had such a great time!

I know some reviews say that the portions here are small and yes perhaps they are smaller than the chain restaurants, but you won't find better Italian food of this fine quality that also includes impeccable service, great atmosphere, and maintains a safe, sanitized restaurant that ensures proper social distancing. We are EATERS, the four of us.  Trust me, you will NOT leave here hungry.  It's just not possible.  And you WILL be dreaming of your next visit.  If you want twice as much food that's cheaper and average tasting at best, go to that other place and save $5.  We're going to Maialina.
Pretty good.  Oysters fried a little too hard tonight.  Bout to try this bread pudding though.  So stay tuned

We hit this place up on our way back from vacation. The ambiance was great for us...high energy, a little loud (great when you bring younger kids!) it definitely has an upscale sports bar feel. Our beers were great - oatmeal stout had a good sweetness and the red ale was flavorful.

Kids good was good, though simple. Chicken was flavorful. Adult meals were just so-so. We ordered the pulled pork nachos and specialty grilled cheese with avocado and bacon jam. Nachos first...they were ok...not disappointing but not as good as I hoped (or they looked) amount of pork was limited and it was more long strings than true pulled. The grilled cheese was a little disappointing. Based on the description it should have been the bomb...but it just lacked flavor. The bread wasn't super grilled and the flavors didn't pop they way I thought they would.

Would I go again? Maybe if I wanted good beer and a fun vibe. But I would order different food.

My coworkers and I order take out at this restaurant at least twice a month. The food is only mediocre, but it's the closest place to us. I usually get the Pad Thai, and the color and taste are very different compared to other Thai restaurant. The food is super salty, and the service is terrible.
Good sushi. Place is clean. Service is nice. Hibachi chefs are awesome. I like this place.
This place is awesome! Had the chicken and waffles...so good! Drinks were on point! The menu have a little of everything. Just try it! Very nice ppl.

We were a party of 7 people.
Had been to several Red, Hot & Blue Restaurants in the past (a number of years ago), so we figured the food would not be bad and
we also chose this particular one because of it's close proximity to where everyone in our party was coming from. Here are the results of our "choice":

We shared one of each of the three rib choices, one pulled chicken,  one beef brisket, with sides of coleslaw, fries, fried okra, and 2 onion loaves......the "appetizer".........not.
 
Ribs: Probably the worst I've ever had, mushy, not a lot of flavor, some strange cartilage things lurking in the meat...........yeach.

Pulled chicken: "steamed or boiled white meat with BBQ sauce applied over it, not cooked in BBQ sauce, mind you". Beef Brisket: "similar".......Cole Slaw: "bitter, but mostly flavor less"......(how exactly does one screw up coleslaw?) Fried Okra: "yes fried but also flavor free".......Finally, the Onion Ring Loaf:  "greasy, oily, and flavorless?" (actually, that's not totally true, it tasted like the oil is was submersed in). In reality the only acceptable food on the table were the fries...........not as horrible as the rest of the food.
Our recommendation.........Choose better........I've had Healthy Choice Frozen Meals that were better than this food!!!!

La Famiglia Ristorante Italiano is a very affordable restaurant serving Italian cuisine. The food was excellent with a slight exception, the bread can be a better quality bread, service was slow as it seems that they could not handle a full restaurant. My wife Maria and I were going to the Reno Philharmonic concert on January 18, 2020, at the Pioneer Center for the Arts. The restaurant is directly across the street. When I say full, I really mean that. Folks who popped in without a reservation were turned away. Our waitress as the rest of the staff could not adequately handle the volume of customers. I am certain this is the case every night there is an activity at the Pioneer Center. We waited for about 10-20 minutes before our wine bottle was opened and then another 10-12 min before our waitress took our order. A wonderful young waitress with a good sense of humor. I ordered a Ceasar salad, the baked Penne with Italian sausage, marinara sauce with cream and mozzarella. We had to wait at least another 25 minutes because my dinner has to be baked and baked it was. My Penne dish was an extremely appetizing sight with caramelized cheese clinging from one side to the other. My food stayed extremely hot for the next 15 minutes or so. It had huge crumbles of Italian sausage. Overall, from kitchen to table, a lot of TLC went into making my dinner, and I too appreciated the visual image it presented and my taste buds thank the chef for a delicious, tantalizing dinner.I don't know if there is a new owner at Mi Famiglia, but I could not find a menu on their website. However, we were fortunate it was opened, I had made a reservation for two, and the end result is we want more and look forward to our next culinary experience at La Famiglia Ristorante Italiano. On nights when they are having an event at the Pioneer Center, I am hoping management will be able to adequately staff the establishment to alleviate the long wait by customers. As we were preparing to leave the place was more than half empty, a visual testimony that many concert-goers were there to enjoy a great meal prior to enjoying the concert.

Probably the worst meal I've had this year. 
Lobster bisque should have at least some lobster in it or its tomato bisque. Twin lobster tails were decent sized but undercooked. Service was good. 
Mitchell's quality has gone downhill and they'll not get any more chances at my business.
Food was good, nice date spot. Too bad we had a loud table next to us, but we will 100% go back

I love the 4 for 4. Who doesn't ? This place is moderately clean but the bathroom could use some attention. It was out of toilet paper and I had to wait for someone to come in and help me out. 
The food was fresh but they seemed short staffed. 
The manager was super friendly though and I got my food fast. 
I'm not a fan of the nuggets over McDonald's but nothing beats the junior bacon cheeseburger. Yum !

The food tonight was warm and fresh. I particularly enjoyed the general tso chicken. There was a nice kick of spice to compliment the sweet flavor. The mushroom pork on lo mien was another fav of mine. The sushi was ok and the rice was clumped together. The bottom of the dish I'm sure.

The service here is seriously lacking. This is one of those places that if you don't ask, you don't get. As in, if you don't ask for napkins, condiments, or a fork, you won't get it.  And napkins used to be kind of an automatic thing. Guess I'll have to remember to ask for everything the next time I come here a very long time from now.

Made a reservation for a Friday night for six after having our reservation cancelled at Five Palms (see other review).  We sat in the room where they had live classical guitarists and flamenco dancers.  There was an additional $5 charge per person to sit near the music but it was well worth the cover charge.  

The service was prompt and attentive.  We started with a couple pitchers of red sangria and ordered a couple dozen tapas to share over the course of the evening.  All of the tapas were delicious.  The portions are small and somewhat pricey but the food quality is well worth the cost.  With three couples, we each started out by ordering two tapas were couple and kept going.  Keep a menu at the table and order a few tapas at a time until you're full!        

The only downside was that the music and dancing (odd to say dancing was loud but it was!  Stomping feet on the stage!) was pretty loud so it was difficult to carry on a conversation.

my past experiences with this dim sum place have been relatively positive and i am disappointed to say that my most recent experience was very poor. the service was mediocre at best. we felt neglected and had to wait around 20 min for our orders to arrive. food quality was not as great as other dim sum places and many of the popular dishes were unavailable. waiters were also rude and loud and failed to show they cared about their customers. definitely will not be returning in a long long time, if ever.

So we made it down to the Legendary Fogo yesterday and we were very pleased that they lived up to the hype. Our expectations were surpassed in every way. The place is huge and the atmosphere was immaculate. The dining room was very modern and the dishware and silverware were sparkling. The salad bar was well kept and organized. The bathrooms were spotless and modern. The only problem I had was paying Thirty dollars for parking which was no fault of theirs. They do have Valet parking but I guess not on Sundays. 

The food was absolutely Amazing. There was nothing I had that I didn't enjoy. We had so many meats that it was hard to keep track. Top sirloin,  Baked chicken,  Lamb chops, Garlic chicken,  Spare ribs, Sausage and many more. I can't tell you how many people served us because we lost count. they were all very attentive and came by the table regularly. Our waiter Christopher was very professional and helpful. The Salad bar was absolutely phenomenal my favorite item being the Chicken salad. I could have eaten just that the whole time but I knew there were a ton of different meats coming. I was just blown away by the whole experience, although the price is a little hefty you absolutely get what you pay for here. I dont mind paying for great copious amounts of delicious food. I will definitely be back for a return visit and would surely recommend this place to anyone.

Excellent food, Macaroons are historic!

Food apart, it's not great but it is fixable so hopefully they will turn it around.

It's all about Sunday Brunch on the patio. Eating brunch while looking at the ocean with a mimosa and friends is what Santa Barbara is all about.  The sevice is decent and the buffet is good.  I'm not a big fan of the indoor seating because it's a bit cave like.  If the patio was bigger I'd give this another star.

Large amounts of food. Quality is so-so.  We were starved.  Salad had some dead leaves.  Chicken gumbo is very good.  Crab cakes slightly burned, suppose to be broiled but was pan fried.  Ask for tartar sauce she brought cocktail sauce.  Server was very nice.  She moved it from 2 to 3 stars.

Stopped in for a bite and I am so disappointed. Sat at the bar and everything seemed fine. Ordered our food and noticed the bartender was completely messed up out of his mind. He literally asked us 5 times if we were ready to order after he put our order in. He was so incredibly high. My order came out and it was all wrong. When I asked for the bill he had the nerve to ask what I ordered. Told him and he still got the check wrong. Never coming back due to the face I'm scared the bartender might have an overdose in front of me. A manager was there but I don't think he cared or he was just as high.
Another Stephen Starr miracle! Best brunch by far....and you must order the Dark and Stormy

So this As seen on food network promo from Guy F guy... well, they weren't kidding in the fish tacos. It's the only thing that's really well advertised as best fish tacos in the Bay Area. The grouper is fried deliciously and fresh. The sauce and slaw they used it very juicy and tasty. However, the prices and cost of tacos per add-on is the dealbreaker. They prob charge more add-on than any other local taco food trucks. Do t get me wrong, the tacos are good but not so good the overprice is worth paying for. I would say Xtreme taco fish isn't that bad or even Los Comparres. But I would put Cali tacos over both of them. Not a landslide but over the top. They don't really use cilantro & onions than your authentic Mexican tacos. It's more of the sauce and sour cream. Another word... very Tex-Mex aka White tacos but not Taco Bell white lol. I do give them credit as they're the only one that offers Chorizo & shrimp as a combo taco. That's genius in their end and very tasty. But once again, they do charge an arm and a leg for it. Also, the wait time when ordering your food is kinda ridiculous. Of all the taco trucks I've been to, they seem to take a lot longer than the others. Very odd. Especially when they use less ingredients. They do offer a lot of choices on their menu like Xtreme. You can say it's like a franchise!! Oh wait... it is. That's another reason I don't considered as a true Mexican taco food truck or even in my Top 5. It'll be in 6 or 7. The fish is the savior but the franchise chain and over price tacos ruin it for me. Best fish tacos and shrimp/Chorizo taco. Just not enough to overwhelm me. Did I mentioned they don't give you any sauces to add onto your tacos?!?! So not cool. Bc they charge you for it!

Final verdict:
3/5: It's Aiight!! I won't say don't go there or not recommendable. It's just theres a lot more authentic cheap, you get more bang buck for your money tacos than Cali tacos. But if you want the best fish tacos in Tampa... def recommend this place and the value you get for a Chorizo/shrimp combine taco.

Avoid this place at all costs.  The food is mediocre at best.  If you want delicious hummus, go to Dizzengoff or Goldie's nearby, or even Naf Naf Grill.  The food and service are both horrible at Cava.  In my most recent interaction, I had $65 worth of food delivered through Cava and they failed to include the basmati rice in the delivery of the "Family Meal" package.  It's like eating a pizza without cheese or dough - it frankly ruined dinner for me and my guests. Cava customer service offered me a $5 rewards coupon for the inconvenience and claimed it was the maximum resolution they could offer.  No refund.  $5 doesn't even cover the cost of tax/tip/delivery.  I will never order from here again and encourage you to do the same.
Bad service, hour and  a half wait for large party to have our table given to the latest walk in. Forgotten drinks, dinnerware and rude waitstaff.

Not as good as Einstein Bagels from my hometown, but they are pretty darn tasty. Try the Parmesan or the Cinnamon sugar bagel (Best toasted). I don't personally eat cream cheese, but some of their combinations sound really good. Cool people, cool atmosphere, and super fast service.

Had a great experience at Barrio Charro today.  The staff was very friendly and helpful with recommendations.  The restaurant was very clean.  I loved that they offered an assortment of locally sourced goods for sale as well as on the menu.  They also have Vegan options on the menu.  We didn't go that route however.  We dug straight into a giant pulled port sandwich which was awesome.  The bbq sauce was really good.  The slaw was crispy.  The homemade bbq chips that came with it I even liked and I'm not a fan of kettle chips.  The coffee was really good as well.  We will definitely be back.

This place has a lot of different influences and they are all good. My favorite are the singapore noodles and the larb chicken. There's plenty off the menu to choose from. This place has never let me down. Great portions as well :-)

Came in looking for pandan buns like I had in Bangkok, but couldn't find them here or anywhere else in Chinatown. Still, they had pandan cake, and one of the ladies behind the counter recommended another pandan product (like a jelly cookie) that turned out to be quite good. Very friendly and helpful staff! Will be back next time we're in town for a durian roll!

Went here with out of town friends who were in town for a foodie trip. Service was great, and the food was amazing. Made friends with the couple at the next table which made it a fun experience for my friends visiting. Truly a friendly, warm, inviting place and I will continue to go again and again.

Wait: we were told a 20 minute wait time when we arrived and then the staff kind of dismissed us. We asked if we could get a drink at the bar or wait somewhere. We were told to wait in the waiting area and we ordered two purple margaritas and a circus margarita. We waited about 20 minutes at a table that looked like all of the other tables. We were confused why we could wait there but not eat there. There were no signs that said the table was closed for social distancing. Our friend did not like the purple margarita because it was too sweet, but I loved it as usual. Mike liked his circus margarita. 

When we were seated, the staff was fine but not super friendly or attentive. The music wasn't playing for the duration of our meal but they tired on some elevator music as we were leaving. We love the patio with all of the plants. It's a really grey set up but the vibe is slightly off due to the music and the staff's demeanor. 

We ordered cardinal queso and several kinds of street tacos. We love the cardinal queso usually but this time they were out of ground beef so we got match meat. It was okay but not as good as it was the last time we had it with ground beef. 

We waited a long time for our checks. I'm not sure if they were understaffed today but in general we didn't understand why everything took so long. 

We will be back because we live so close and like the patio, but if we continue to have a mediocre experience then we will have to find a replacement.

Use to have the best prime rib sandwich ever. Until last night. I ordered it rare and what I got looked to be the shavings of leftover cuts of
Prime rib in a meat slicer. It was very fatty and sloppy. The service was great, as well as the coleslaw and horseradish.

12/31. I walked in before 5 and used the restroom. A employee said hi. So I sat for about 5 minutes to see what to order. Then some kid walks up and says we're closing. I spoke to the cashier and told asked her do you always close early when your  website says til 9.  I then asked for a 800 number and was told we don't have one. Look it up online for yourself. Fully understand that they want to go home but when your business doors are open might be a clue you need to manage these kids more closely.  The cashier that gave me attitude has directed me to the numerous sandwich shops in the area.  I really don't care but thought maybe someone other than kids running the shop should know. 

Thank you for your time

Drove by on my way to an art opening and came back after for a bite and a drink. 

Love it. Beautiful bar, easy to get a good seat (and on street parking). Bartender acknowledged me right away and gave me cocktail and food menus. Music is good, not too loud, able to have a conversation. One not too big tv screed playing b&w john ford films. Ordered wine and tuna tartar. Loved it! I'm am picky af and hope it can stay like this. Thanks for the good service, Rarest! I'll be back.
This is such an amazing place. Some of the best Burrito/Mexican food I've ever had. Our waitress was a short blond woman. Amy maybe? I don't remember the name. She was amazing! We will be back.

10 pretzels for $5.00 yes please!  You can't beat a good soft pretzel and this place nailed it!  They are just about perfect.  This was one of my last stops in the City of Brotherly Love, and it sent me back home to Virginia with a smile.  We got there about fifteen minutes before they closed, the staff was happy, singing, and still slinging pretzels around!  The price seriously does leave me speechless!  I brought some back with me, and even now, I am sitting at my desk at work, dreaming about that doughy goodness waiting for me when I get home!

So good. I'd always been a bit intimidated by Firefily (Green Hills and super cute must mean really expensive and posh, right?), but I should have read the Yelp reviews first! It's so casual and not nearly as expensive as I imagined it would be. 

I ordered the grilled chicken over baby spinach, and I loved the slight kick from the harissa yogurt topping. But I'm really writing this review to praise the sweet potato fries as highly as I can - they were simply the best sweet potato fries I've ever had in a restaurant, period. They practically melted in my mouth, but were perfectly crisp on the outside. Also, WHAT is the mayonnaise they serve for dipping spiced with? Fantastic.

Our server was also great - she obliged us by arranging candles on a storebought birthday cake and lighting them before she brought it back to the table. 

Overall, excellent. I didn't want to leave.

We came in here around 10 pm on a Saturday night to grab a drink after a movie. There were only a hand full of people inside the place and after being served by the bartender I understood why.   

I ordered an Irish mule and my sister ordered a Moscow mule. Both drinks were super weak and overly sweet. I could of looked past this faux pas in light of the fact that the drinks were only $6 a pop, however the bartender gave us such bad service we didn't stay long enough to see her attempt at making another drink.   We couldn't understand why she never returned to see if we would like another round, we couldn't even see her to wave her down. Finally we called it quits and sadly went home after one drink.

It's too bad the bartender was so crappy because this place had a great ambiance and they even had live music which was actually pretty kick ass.  Drinks were cheap too.  I don't care how cheap drinks are though, I will never go back to a place where I have to beg to get service.

Amazing, delicious, fresh Indian cuisine! Our favorite spot in St. Pete. Peshwari naan, Navratan korma, Paoli rice, fish curry... All are really tasty! Monte (the manager) runs a great show here. We'll be back SOON!

Longest line ever. I dont like to blame workers, since it's usually due to being understaffed. Though they do give you a lot of attitude, I can imagine being stuck working there for minimum wage, so I won't hold it against them. Horribly put together food and it's never even for me. So I have to wait almost 25 minutes or more in line at every burger king and I dont even eat. It's supposed to be fast food.

This place has very good food that is hot all time. Fresh food very clean food area and the rest rooms are also clean! I wish they can open a Fred Markets where I live Kingsland Georgia. There is no buffet there!

Big Shakes is the real deal. Friendly people, great chicken as hot as you want it and crispy, salty fries. The fish is also really good. This is t classic Nashville hot chicken- more like breaded tenders- but it has every bit the ability to light you on fire as you move up the heat scale. If they bring it out wearing mask and gloves, prepare for some entertainment...

Hello little shrimp!! Yum.
I go here because the seafood is fresh off the boat! (usually) I wont talk about the bad incidences I've had there because it's been maybe two or three times in all the years I've been going here. 
PROS:
everything on the menu is delish! The portions are big and the ambiance is pleasant, especially the outdoor seating at the one on Grande.
CONS:
Its a little pricey for Tucson, the waitresses can be idiot bitches at the one on grant near 1st
MUST READ:
I may not love this place AS much if they didn't make a killer michelada HOWEVER because they're made from scratch it depends who you get, which SUCKS.

This place is awesome. I love the chill atmosphere they try to provide, it's very relaxing, accommodative, and their lounge chairs are inviting and help to get everyone in a serene and conversational mindset. My girlfriend and I are here at least once a week and we look forward to coming each time. We've grown close with a lot of the servers. In three years, we have yet to experience bad service, I can definitely attest to their commitment to consistently providing terrific service. 

Foods that I would recommend: The Chicken Tender Basket tends to be go-to for a lot of people, it's a sizable portion for a low price, I prefer to have with the crispy fries, the thick fries tend to not have as much seasoning. I would also recommend their Gyro, which is enormous, comes with a variety of ingredients and I usually can't finish it in one sitting. Recently I tried their Philly Cheesesteak - the best I've had so far. Perfectly seasoned and the bread is quality. 

Hooka recommendation: We've tried just about every flavor, now we just ask for suggested house flavors from our server whenever we go. But if you like fruity or semi-fruity flavors, these may appease you: Eshta, Pharaoh, Starburst, Watermelon Freeze and we recently tried the guava, peach, and berry blend, we thought it wonderful.

Absolutely abysmal parking situation...got chased out of a spot by someone working in the jewelry store, had to circle (several times) and finally found a spot in the next lot over.

The rolls for the banh mi we're dry and inauthentic (bought in bulk from Sam's Club).

The BBQ pork in my bun was very stringy and fatty. 

I don't think I'll return.

Great for meat eaters, but literally no vegetarian options. They cooked us up some steamed veggies and corn tortillas, which were good, but definitely not worth going out to eat for. Even the sauces and beans all had meat in them with no non-meat alternatives.  :(

We were craving gumbos and glad we found this place! The restaurant is a little drive from the city center but I would recommend checking out this hole in the wall place if you get the chance. The restaurant is small but very quaint. 

I love how the menu is simple and short. When ordering the gumbo, order the biggest size because it will totally be worth it. Plus, the price for the biggest size wasn't that much more. We had the mumbo gumbo and original which were both SO GOOD. They don't have much rice in them so if you're like me and love rice, I recommend ordering a side dish that contains rice. We ordered red bean and rice which was more than enough between two gumbos. 

Highly highly recommend checking out this place!

These are the best wings!  And while I wait mango bubble tea!

Order ahead for take out or its a 30 minute wait, but worth it!

I love Morimoto. I have been here several times for both lunch and dinner and have never been disappointed. I'd say that this is a surefire way to have a positive and delicious dining experience.

Things I highly recommend:

The rock shrimp tempura might be the single tastiest thing I've ever had in my life. I've had it every time I've gone and it's been a blissful gastronomic experience every time. The sauce on it is tangy and delicious and it is perfectly balanced by the refreshing and crisp lettuce-like vegetable that it comes out with.

For lunch, go with one of the special lunch boxes - it is incredibly reasonably priced. I got the spicy beef box and thought it was absolutely fantastic. The assorted Asian mushrooms that came with it were so fresh and a great balance to the flavor of the beef. The person I went with got the chicken katsu box and said that she would highly recommend it as well.

Their rolls are great. The fish melts in your mouth. I got a spicy salmon roll (my favorite) and I thought they did it very well.

Their menu changes from time to time so it's been a pleasant surprise to go back whenever I visit Philadelphia and go there! Overall, I can't recommend this place more highly.
This place is so delicious!  The staff is so friendly and the food is amazing! Finally an awesome Vietnamese restaurant!! The summer rolls are a must and the beef bah mi!

This was my first time coming to Eckert's for apple picking and honestly couldn't believe such a fun institution could be in the middle of Illinois. It's been on my St. Louis bucket list for awhile (the drive is less than a 40 minutes from the city) and honestly wasn't expecting to have this much fun, should have came sooner. 

Here are my favorite parts about the trip:
- The apples are so extremely cheap. Usually at other U-Pick places, the U-Pick fruits are either comparable or more expensive than the supermarket versions but not at Eckert's. Not matter what type of apple you got, it will just be a flat fee of $2/pound, even more expensive apples like Honeycrisp. 
- I really appreciate how much variety there is at the farm. There must be 10+ different kinds of apples and trying all of them out to really understand the different flavors was one of my favorite things to do here.
- I also enjoyed how many different activities there were on the farm from restaurants to petting zoos. You could really spend an entire day here without get bored.
- The tractor rides were quite fun as they take a loop around the farm before getting back so you can see all the different types of crops they have in season.

Hot Tips for your trip:
- 2 hours is not enough here. Budget more like 5 as if you are bored of apple picking, you can go to the petting zoo or eat at the restaurants.
- Bring sunscreen, it gets HOT especially in the middle of the day.
- The food here is actually very cheap and would actually recommend buying a ton of their different apple products - especially the apple cider donut - home for breakfast.

Overall a wonderful experience at Eckert's! Can't wait to come back again and next time for a way longer time.

Good food, always feels fresh and fun! Some of the dishes are a little "out there" but if you are adventurous... Try them! I have not been disappointed yet! Their menu is always changing, which is great, but if you are craving something you got last time you were there, chances are, it's not on the menu anymore! The cheese plate is always fabulous! And they make an amazing pizza!
A couple of the dishes were good, the salsa is delicious, was not a fan of the combos with rellenos, burritos, enchiladas. Service was fast and friendly.

Did you know that Cracker Barrel won an award, given by Nation's Restaurant News (a trade journal for restaurant professionals), as consumer pick for best restaurant in the Family Dinining Category? I know a few people have had a bad experience but ours is almost always great, no matter the location.

Came to this one for supper on Mother's Day. They had obviously been slammed. But the waitress was still cheerful and the food fantastic. Only reason I'm not giving 5 stars is that they were out of baked potatoes and I had to send my steak back for a little more time on the grill (server stood right by me after initial delivery and insisted I check it before she left and sure enough, it needed more time). A big Kudos to the cook who figured out how to make hashbrown casserole hot and crispy!

An incredible space, with kind and gracious owners..but most importantly clean food.  It's so nice to eat out and not worry about all the glyphosate or allergens such as gluten, dairy, soy and corn in your food.  To top all that, the food was DELICIOUS! I can't wait to go back there again.

1st time going to this establishment and LAST from the disrespectful Dirty nasty employees to Scott the managers lack of customer service HORRIBLE people couldn't even enjoy the food because of the Staff! Trash environment!!

Table of 8..Pizza was SOGGY and took a long time to be served, half the table ate their food before the other half got served. Had to chase down the waitress for beverages refills multiple times. Mom had to eat dessert with all the dirty dishes on the table, very disappointing. Poor service and mediocre food.

LOVE! Good Prices. Great Food. Fun Experience. Will be back.

Tried 4 different crepes and all were very good!

My favorite crepe was the Spicy Jamaican Chicken Crepe unique flavor, and the level one spice was warm and wonderful in the mouth!

We also enjoyed the Ma Province crepe it tasted like garlic chicken pizza at papa murphys.

The De Poulet crepe would be great for bacon lovers and would be better for breakfast in my opinion!

FOR DESSERT we had the bananas foster, with creme brulee on top and added strawberries!

They were super accommodating, and the guy who looked like Antonia Banderas was super hepful, and willing to answer all my picky questiona!

We also tried the tomato basil soup it was good well worth $2 for a cup.

It was my husbands and I's first time here upon entering we noticed it was VERY dusty, they seriously need to dust aside from that I like the decor.
   Both of us ordered the special The Espresso Burrito I was not happy that they charge $1 extra to melt cheese? That is crappy when our food arrived we started eating and I didn't. taste the chicken, it hardly had any and it lacked in flavor there was none. It looks nice but it tastes like fast food, it lacks in flavor needs SERIOUS dusting I think when we come this way again we won't come back to this place. The air vent and fake plants have so much dust its blowing into the food yuck.

My cousins and I came to celebrate a birthday. We shared several plates, like the shahshuka hummus, acorn squash, sweet potatoes, eggplant, scallops, and brussel sprouts. It came with the best pita bread ever. I loved the sweet potatoes and acorn squash the most. The eggplant was still rather firm and undercooked, which is a shame because I love eggplant. The scallops were a little underwhelming, but I can't put my finger on why. The waitresses were really nice and helpful. Their menu changes frequently, so it might be nice to see what new things they have.

If you are looking for the perfect burger in Tucson and are willing to pay for it, Diablo Burger is your best choice. Everything from the venue, the service, the presentation to the fries is excellent. I always get one of their burger creations with melty cheddar and green chile aioli. I wasn't sold on the idea of having an english muffin as a bun, but it works. I appreciate that all the ingredients from the meat, veggies, bread, and potatoes are all sourced locally. They really use the best ingredients to make the best burger. The fries are to die for, crispy yet not double fried and just the right amount of salt. I love all their in house sauces, and I always order a couple to dip my fries in. I'll admit I don't love the price for the portion, but this is a quality over quantity joint and some days you need to treat yourself to a $13 burger.

Tuff one.  We had midnight resos and weren't able to get the room until 12:45.  Which left us about an hour until we were kicked out at 1:45.  Because of the wait we were comped 2 $5 bottles of champagne and the room charge.  By the time we figured out how to use the machine we were being asked to leave.  It  is also a bit, how should I put this...the crowd is less educated and has less income?  Would we go back?  Probably yes, because we will know how to use the machine and we will rent the room for longer.  Make sure you get your reso in early, because you don't want the midnight slot.

We have been wanting to try this place for a while, and were pleasantly surprised there was no wait.  My husband is immediately put off because there is zero social distancing.  The tables are not spaced.  No covid protocol...even if it is ok by Jefferson county standards, they could do better. Our waitress comes over and takes our drink order.   There is a table that seems to be taking most of her attention.  One of the diners at said table has a sybergs shirt on. Maybe they are VIP because the manager visits the table more than once to visit. But our waitress seemed more concerned with pleasing that table then serving any of her other tables. Needless to say, the service was lacking.   The food was good, but not good enough to put up with poor service. Not sure we will return......I'm pretty sure my husband won't.

This is a new 24 hours diner in downtown Nashville...
The design of this place is a contemporary industrial...
 It is a place that they will not seat you...You will be the one to seat yourself ..When you walk in here they only had t nowo booth table and all the seating is a counter seating...I had a chicken waffles and it is awesome as it is not too greasy or too sweet unlike the chicken and waffles I had tasted in other place...The serving of food is just enaugh not too large and not too small... However, their chicken quesadilla is too dry so I only gave them four star..  and they should had salsa on the side or  even sour cream it guacamole so that their chicken quesadilla is not that too dry...The service is good and the server is friendly...I recommend this place whenever you're in for a late night food...
I didn't even know I liked Peruvian food until I came to this place.  Everything was phenomenal especially the chips and green sauce!

I normally don't write reviews. I work very close to here and I hear ppl talking about it . Referring to the food as 'ok ...  Let's start by the containers didn't have no dividers so I ask the gentlemen if he could put my greens in a separate container he going to reply and say that is a side and I would have to charge for you . I'm like whatever who want green juice in there macaroni .
