Also the curry chk was very bland no flavor at all also the jerk chicken was very bland it was baked jerk chicken also I had to put hot sauce on the jerk . I would never ever come back here . The guy was a lil rude as well so if you in the area I suggest you go somewhere else and spend your money .

If you go to this restaurant understanding that is a Chinese buffet you will not be let down. The staff is friendly and the food is always tasty. This is not five star dining, but it satisfy your Chinese craving any night. The price is extremely reasonable as well. I do like this Chinese buffet more than the one in Arnold near the Wal-Mart. 

A previous post gave bad reviews because they thought this restaurant was going to be Sho-Guns... Seriously? You thought they were building a Sho-Guns in Imperial, Missouri... Get real people.
A favorite for years. Great Italian food, great atmosphere. Go in and take a frozen Pizza home for dinner.

Great atmosphere, really nice staff, Ramen was ok. Ramen is not really my thing so I wasn't impressed with the food. Edamame was good. This 4 stars is purely on atmosphere and service. They have a million drinks to choose from. Soft drinks come in a mini can and they give you a small glass of ice with it.

The food is great. The service. Not so much. Even when it's not extremely busy the servers hardly ever come to check on you or refill drinks. It even take about 10 minutes to just cash out. Seriously. The service is terrible.

I have been to a few Montanas in Edmonton. Most times the service and the food have been mediocre at best. I haven't bothered writing a review cause it wasn't so bad that I felt I needed to, until my most recent visit at this location!

So I was here last week for lunch 12:30, It wasn't overly busy. I ordered a pulled pork sandwich with a side of Caesar salad. The Caesar salad was good. Now my pulled pork sandwich....it was dry, tough and chewy. Weird right??? How is that possible with pulled pork? Easy... what they put on my sandwich was not pulled pork!!! Check out my pictures. They used strips of pork and strips of pure fat from where I don't know, but to me it tasted like tough rib meat. And where's the sauce? If your going to try and fake a pulled pork at least try and hide it in some sauce!

The Lava, a great coffee shop by day just decided to become a BYOB by night, so I went to check it out. Food and service were great. I had the Rib Eye steak with home made chimichurri which was done exactly right and was delicious. For starters, I recommand the MAZOT, which is basicaly a selection of home made salads and pickles served with Pita bread.

All in all, a great experiance, looking forward to going back and check out the other items on the menu.

Heard that this was a fantastic restaurant in New Orleans. When we arrived, I soon realized this wasn't the restaurant I had seen pictures of or read about.  The newly renovated decor is terrible...a bad 80's rendition of pastels and grays. The menu is completely new so we couldn't order what we had been hoping to.  The food was just ok...nothing to write home about but we couldn't get over the ambiance of the restaurant. It felt like we were in a diner. Unfortunately, we won't be back.

People living in New Orleans should not complain about the availability of good  restaurant food....but we do.  I had been missing decent American Chinese food like I used to get in NYC.  Today I found it!  My usual first time order when trying a new Chinese place is Gen Tso chicken and wonton soup.  Yes, it is unauthentic, and yes, I like it.  If a restaurant can't pull off these 2 dishes, in my mind, there is no need to return.   I ordered the lunch special portion to go. 
 The chicken pieces were plump, white meat chunks with no fat globs.  The fried rice was a delight.  Really fried, not just drowned in soy sauce.  There were hunks of roasted pork and vegetables too.  The token egg roll was small, yet I could taste ginger.  And none of it was greasy.  The portions are very generous too.  The wonton broth was ok, but not too salty.  The wontons were thin skinned and nicely made.  There was bok choi and pork in the broth. Due to the dearth of good wonton soup around here, I learned to make my own.  Mine is better (IMO) but this is really, really tasty.  It's certainly worth the drive to Kenner.  Next visit I will be more daring in my menu selections.

The food is pretty good. I really like the french friends, they have great french fries. I like coming here for a change of pace when I'm in the area. I also like the hoagies and pizza. 

The service is alright, none of my servers were ever very friendly though. I've also never seen the place busy--I think the most tables I've seen at a time was 5 on a weekend evening. The lack of business makes me wonder.

Just sat in the drive-through for an amazingly long time. Got my food and my garlic double cheeseburger the bread is crunchy like a crouton. My milkshake had more milk in it than ice cream it was like banana milk the whip cream on top of it was shaking when she handed it to me. No one seems to be able to answer the phone there. Don't go terrible terrible !!!!
It's aright. Over pieced food but flavor is there. Place is cute with mugs and such from around the world. Close home family feeling.

This is a wonderful place to watch football games or various sporting events . The facility is always clean, mgmt very friendly. Most servers are wonderful but some of the young gals are too interested in talking to each other or their friends. This is the only negative and is VERY minor. I love this brand and will frequent this establishment

One of our great popular hot spots on Oak Street. The food is good, great choice of our variety of seafood. There are so many different ways our delicate specialties  are prepared. You can always find something new to please your pallet. Prepared in a concoction only know to our great cities many cultures. Do not miss out on one of our great dinning experience.
Grilled satsuma old fashioned!!! Best cocktail ever. Try one. You won't be sorry. That is all.

Went for dinner tonight and it is probably better served as an after work watering hole or spot for a work group to gather vs dinner with the family.  Decor is nice and there are tv's in every direction.  Standard sports bar menu.  The service was ok, nothing great.

My bro had the chicken ciabatta sandwich and it looked good.  We got calamari which were nothing special and chicken nachos for the table.  The nachos were not that great.  They don't melt cheese on it, they use a queso. The chicken was like purdue cuts you by in the bag at the store and it had lettuce and tomato, but no jalapenos.  

The waitress convinced us to order dessert, we waited 10 minutes and she brought us out the wrong dessert so she took off to get us the chocolate cake and another 10 minutes went by.  When she brought the cake I jokingly asked if she had to bake it and she said it took forever for us to find any . . . so I said is it old and she said no, it is from a brand new box - oh great, can't wait to dig right in.  It was nothing special, just like the rest of the food.

I won't be rushing back.

Had dinner there last night - the service was atrocious.  The waiter disappeared several times - it took over 30 minutes to order the first drinks - and he forgot one person and didn't come back.  We had to ask for bread as we had a child that was starving and that took another 10 minutes (so 40 minutes and we still didn't have appetizers).  The crab bisque had a skin on the top as it had clearly been sitting under heat lights for some time.  The waiter came to tell me that they were out of snapper and then after giving me the menu to select something else - never came back to ask me what I wanted.  The mac and cheese looked like it was made last week and the crab cakes were alright but nothing spectacular.  Used to be much better - seems to have gone down hill significantly.

If you're looking for a traditional cheesesteak, come here! Don't allow the location to deter you! As soon as we walked in, they were aware they were tourist because we were taking pics and calling them Philly's instead of simple cheesesteaks. The cooks were friendly and joked around with us, especially with our southern accents. 

Here are a few things I believe you should know when ordering a cheesesteak from Max's:
1. Don't call it a Philly (you'll sound like a tourist)
2. Don't take a billion pics (you'll look like a tourist)
3. Know what kind of meat you want. Chicken or steak
4. Know what size you want, half or whole. Our uber driver told us that we would only be able to eat half of a half. She was right. A half is about a foot long and a whole is about twice its size. 
5. Know what toppings and condiments you want to add: mayo, ketchup, cheezewiz, onions, peppers, or jalapeños. 
6. Always add cheesewiz! 
7. Always have cash. They only accept cash, but they have an ATM in the restaurant 
8. Keep it moving or go to the Clock Bar or Eagle Bar for Music and drinks. All three are owned by the same person. 

Overall, I enjoyed my experience. The cheesesteak was cooked perfectly and the toppings added to the deliciousness.

I hate to do this because my mom taught me to never say anything bad about anybody but my experience at this restaurant was the worst experience I've ever had in any restaurant I've worked in over 38 and I've never been treated so poorly I was with a friend of mine who was handicapped and he looked at him like he was a leper the food was terrible the chili relleno was it canned green chile about two bites wrapped and burned scrambled eggs they should be ashamed of themselves for the way they treated me and my handicapped friend shame on you Elko Giro

I see my good friend Bill added this business as did I.But I added it with the proper address and name :)  This place is new and huge.  I would classify it as an ABC buffet as it is almost Anything But Chinese buffet.  It has many tables of food from crayfish to beef tenderloin.  For $12.50 I don't see the beef tenderloin lasting long.  It was however nice and tasty.  I did have my favorite beef with broccoli and it was not the best not the worst.  The beef tenderloin while cooked to well done was tasty and not dry as it was sitting in beef juice.  They also had on the meat section self carve ham to go with the self carve tenderloin.  There was some chicken on this section but honestly I could not identify what cuts they were.  The other thing of note on the ABC buffet was it chicken wings very plumb and tasty.  

This place also has a sushi section and soon to come a grill.  I did not sample any of the sushi.  I really think it was an ok deal as for as price to value

Edit
This is located in the old Hometown Buffet building and the bar that was next door the old Ice and Fuel West.  They have completely did everything over.  The bathrooms are new and clean.  To tell how how much change they did the old men's rooms is now the women's and you guessed it women's is now the men's.
It's exactly as advertised. Really good burgers and fries and the new building makes it a much better experience. I'll keep coming back.

Truland Burgers stands out in the burger arena.  Perfectly cooked and flavorful.  You know that you're getting good food when the ingredients are premium and fresh.  The salads are hard to pass up and not to mention the sweet potato tots.  My go to salad is the Bacon and Brussels.  Packed with flavor.  
The prices may seem a little more pricey but some may be willing to pay for healthier options as you would see here.

Went here for the first time a few weeks ago, have been back twice since for the soup - cream of chicken, cream of sweet potato, cream of broccoli. At at this point I feel I can recommend cream of anything. The rest of the food has been good too, but not cheap. The more ambitious dishes seem to be the best, not always the case at diners.

i like this place because they sell some really good tea. i also like how they let you occupy their seat/table for hours. they have wi fi and they sell odwalla juices. they also have like 3 outside tables and various newspapers. the people in there are pretty friendly and its definitely a cool place to chill.
granted there are other local places that have much better coffee.
This is average NY Pizza. No taste, so-so crust. Go 15 minutes down the road to Pomodorros. Well worth the drive. They're the real deal. This is poser NYPizza.

I have been going here since I was 6 and I don't think the menu has changed a bit (which is a good thing!). This is the best place on the Main Line to get a cheesesteak without having to go to Philly. I like the pizza too, if you like thick crust and lots of cheese.

Fast and friendly service!

ANYONE WITH DIETARY RESTRICTIONS watch out for the Rock Hill location. I'm a vegetarian of 15+ years and I was given chicken instead of tofu TWICE then still not taken care of. I'm a long time customer of Crazy Bowls due to the healthy vegetarian options available and I order at least once weekly. My last experience at the Rock Hill location was completely unacceptable. I ordered a wrap with tofu on the app for pick up. I drove home and ate part of it only to realize I was given chicken instead of tofu. I called the restaurant and spoke to the shift lead (her name started with a K) on 1/20/20 around 7:30pm. I requested to pick up a new wrap made correctly and for a refund due to the inconvenience of having to drive back. I also informed her that I had eaten meat though being a strict vegetarian due to the error. She told me I had to choose either a refund or a new wrap but could not have both, which really isn't taking care of the customer. Despite the poor customer service, I drove back to get my new wrap. I drove back home only to find it was made with chicken AGAIN! I called back and spoke to the shift lead again. All she could offer me was a refund. She said "I should have asked for her when I came in because she would have made it correctly." WHAT?! I requested a phone call from the store manager, which I was told I would receive on 1/21/20. I never got that phone call. I've filled out 2 feedback forms on the website with no response either. The reason I used to go to Crazy Bowls was because I always felt taken care of with my dietary restriction. I will not be back. This is completely unacceptable. I'll spread the word to my vegetarian community. I'm extremely disappointed and would hope that Crazy Bowls would make this right..

I walked by Qu Japan Bistro & Bar several times, but I finally took the plunge. Qu's happy hour rivals some of the best in the city.  Currently 3-6pm Mon - Fri, their $5 menu is hefty and allows you to sample some of their best menu items.  

I hope they go all out with fun promotions during the traditional cherry blossom festival season and take over the courtyard in the spring/summer months.

As long as the staff continues to focus on service, they could become a mainstay.

Note: They should add hooks under the bar as well as USB and/or AC outlets throughout the bar area would go a long way for those who want to escape the office and work through lunch.

I have been a customer at Mangia since I was 16. I've seen lots of owners come and go. Idk who is running it now, but the last couple of years the service is just awful. I am not one to give a bad review because of one bad experience. It makes me sad to see what it's turned into. You wait and wait and wait just to be recognized at the bar and they act like they are doing you a favor by serving you. This is the last time. I waited for over 15 minutes and the bartender never came to get my drink order. There were literally 5 customers including myself. There is no excuse for that kind of service.
attractive waitress, wet spring scramble, small portions, tasty self serve coffee, delicious greens. I think Ima pass next time but thank you!!!

Fast, Fast cooked noodle dishes!  Did I say Fast??  Walk in order and pay but don't sit down because your food will be ready in mere seconds!  Noodles slightly greasy but good taste.  Cheap prices too.

The food is amazing. I really loved my beef Wellington & have been pretty much craving it non-stop since. I do wish the portions were larger for the price and the staff was particularly friendly. I'll probably still go back for our next special occasion.

I would totally give five stars if they would institute an alternative to YELLING out everyone's name and food type when their order is up. 

I visited during a busy lunch hour and granted, it was loud enough already. I sat near the counter, so I was able to hear when the order for every. Single. Person after me came up. I've visited before and sat elsewhere, when it wasn't so busy. 

It's a reeeeeally annoying practice. 

Especially because we live in an age of buzzers and tented plastic table numbers and whatnot.

Also, they've been open almost a year now and the pies are still a bit inconsistent, as far as doneness. I'm guessing that with the way that they are cooked, depending on toppings, and where in the oven they are  placed, as well as the dough used, along with the cooking time...many factors go into  how the finished pie is presented.

Being a pizza blogger, these are the little details that matter to me! 

Barring those things, I love it. The roasted garlic is amazing. No matter how many toppings you put on it, it's still the same price.

It appears they do a lot of business from the college right across the street, Lindenwood University. It took about 15 minutes from the door to the counter, plus about another five minutes to get my food. Overall, very satisfying and I will definitely be back.

Maybe if it's not a rainy day, I'll just sit outside...

Good food with absolutely great service and atmosphere.  I went to Create Cafe last night with some family who was visiting from out of town.  We had a few little kids with us and my wife told me how Create Cafe had a cool kids play area so we decided this place would be a good idea.  The kids had a great time as they have cool toys and areas for them to play.  My curry chicken salad was good but I wasn't a big fan of the dressing.  My wife's grilled cheese on the other hand was wonderful.  The staff was extremely helpful and nice and gave me a cash refund when they accidentally put 2 kids meals on my bill instead of the one I intended to order.  I will definitely go back here again.

As a South Asian, sometimes I just crave quick Indian food that will hit the spot. This place does not do that and my first couple tries at this place were disappointing. They have many culturally "mixed" foods on the menu that are both intriguing and confusing at the same time. For example, wraps with paneer and arugula or wraps with veggie chicken, salad, and a chutney on top?! 

I tried one of their wraps and their chilli paneer and both were like a tease for my palate. When I was craving that spicy Indian food full of flavor, what I got was food that looked great but was safely bland and mild. Definitely got the feeling they were catering to non-South Asians with their dishes. The only exception to this rule is their weekly "Chef's Special" which I am convinced is the one weekly dish they offer to the authentic Indian food cravers - last time I went they had this Paneer Bhurji wrap which was DELICIOUS. 

Overall, I do appreciate that this place has a variety of vegetarian options that are fun, different, and use meat substitutes in creative ways. Their food is good, fresh, and not greasy, so I would definitely come back here again, just not when I'm craving my Indian fix.

The food here is great, make sure you get something with their chocolate!  We got milkshakes with our lunch, but we'll definitely be making a special trip just for dessert.  I took a star off because i wasn't a huge fan of the atmosphere... loud, cramped,  and not enough booths. The tasty meal certainly made up for that though.

I'm not too much of a sports fan, but this place has a really cool atmosphere.

The TV's, the bathroom (one way mirror!), the dining area, basicly the overall decor of this place is impressive.  During big game days it gets pretty crazy, but then again I assume most sports bars/restaurants get this way during games. 

Now on to the food. Some people I dined with didn't care too much for their order, but I personally love the food i've tried here. Most of their appetizers are amazing. Try the boneless wings, or the pretzel sticks. I haven't ate here for a long time so who knows whats on the menu now, but their cheesy cheeseburger and the breakfast burger were very tasty. 

Their desserts are impressive too, I love the cheesecake here. Beats cheesecake factory in my opinion. 

Overall, if you're a sports fan, or someone in the downtown area just looking for good food and a cool atmosphere, give the Colts Grille a shot.

They just opened up a spot in our mall in Sierra Vista and is is delicious.   We tried everything and could not be happier with the amazing taste and great customer service.  We have very few good places to eat in town and are happy to be able to finally have a place we look forward to going to.  Be sure to check them out!!!

Excellent pork fried rice served here. I'm getting away from my go-to shrimp dishes and tried pork instead. I've had theirs on three occasions now and it's so delicious! Ive had the salt and pepper pork as well. It's hit or miss on whether this is good on the day. My orders were all to go so I can't say much about table service. I don't like the look of the place inside, too dark and dank, but the food is really good.

Love this place. My favorite dishes are the club sandwich. Make sure to ask for ranch dressing for your fries and sandwich. It's amazing. I also love their pecan pie warmed with ice cream on top. Soooo good.

Ummm. Wonderful!! Bartenders, patrons, drinks, food...everything was fantastic. Karaoke, trivia, just a good time. People were there for birthdays, or just for a weekend night of fun. Everyone was so nice. It isn't smokey, just the right amount of crowded. Drinks were served quickly, and the food was wonderful and brought with enthusiasm. Staff is personable and kind. Going again, tonight!

Copperfield Inn is the name of the new restaurant that was formerly called, for many years, The Lakeside Inn (on Ridge Pike).

We had lunch there on Saturday and I can't think of one thing that could have been better, except for my creme brulee, which didn't have a crispy crust . Our server, Maria, was the best and the food was just as good.

The blue cheese and caramelized onion foccacia appetizer was very good and the lunch selections were reasonably priced and included a choice of chips, fries or fruit.  We both chose the fruit, which was very fresh.
The breads included a sourdough and a very authentic rye.
We both had sandwiches; mine was meatloaf and my wife had a portobello and vegetable.

We were each served a complimentary glass of wine (Merlot and Pinot were our choices).  I preferred the Merlot. They are awaiting their liquor license, so (in true PA fashion) I'm sure it will be a BYOB for awhile.

We are hoping to get back soon, so we can try dinner!
(BTW, they do banquets, even brunch, for your business or family events.)
I enjoyed their pizza but the price was too pricey for a large pizza and it was about $21 including tax.

Tried Jerry's Bar for dinner this time. I ordered the Fried Chicken Sandwich with fries. The chicken is dipped in hot-n-honey sauce then topped with charred scallion aioli, lettuce, and tomato all on a brioche bun. I found the chicken too thin with mostly breading and the sauce had a nice tang, but a little too heavy. Maybe the classic slaw and pickles would be better topping than the lettuce & tomato as they did not add much.
Empty restaurant takes 30 minutes to greet you, completely unacceptable!! The managers were just as rude as the servers! Don't worry Copia, you achieved your goal, we won't be back!

My wife and I would always have lunch at this place every time we're in Santa Barbara. Sadly, today is the last. Our favorite dish, scampi, was taken off the menu. Their half sized orders is now more like a quarter without a reduction in price of course. I thought the main dish I ordered was an appetizer. Service has declined considerably as we had to beg a couple of times for some more bread. To rub it in, they included a service charge for our party of three.

Such an awesome spot and location. I've been going for years. Mostly because of the decent prices and amazing location. But their food is sort of average. I wish they'd improve it because it can be a 5 star spot in one of the most beautiful places of SB. Gorgeous both indoors and outdoor seating. I feel bad writing this because I have great love and memories of the place, but it's done in the hope that they read it and take it to the next level. I think it can become an icon of Santa Barbara if they do.

Alberta avenue needs more like this. Nice, not fancy sit down Columbian restaurant. Service was good. Three beef tacos $13. Made in house soft corn taco shell, roast beef (not ground), cilantro, onion, tomato. Red and green salsa on the side that were not spicy but very flavourful. Delicious. 
Arepa von todo (loaded) $9(!). Larger taco shell, roast beef, chorizo, cilantro, lettuce, tomato. Mayo and ketchup sauce (meh). Ask for some hot sauce. 
Also delicious. 
Coffee was not special but not bad.  
We'll be back to try other menu items.

Excellent doner kebabs! Quality meat and veggies used in a sandwich that will set you back less than $8 and leave your belly happier than it has ever been. Everything is fresh and house made. Bright and clean space with lovey staff. There is also a little pile of books to read by the window while you wait for your food and sip on your iced mint tea. Open Friday- Monday 

These are not your kebabs that you would expect to find at a Greek or Mediterranean place. This is a doner kebab. It's a bit more Eastern European and a little Turkish thrown in. Doner kebabs are the king of all sandwiches and were cornerstone of my diet while I lived in Germany; it is drunk food at its finest. I have not been able to find a proper one in the U.S. since moving back about 10years ago. Thanks to the spit-roasted meat gods; my prayers were finally answered. Kebab has the most beautifully roasted and seasoned chicken and pork to stuff their sandwiches. The meat is juicy and perfectly crisp on the edges from twirling around that spit for hours on end. The sauces for the sandwiches are amazing and go oh so well with the cabbage, pickled cucumber and red onions that the kebabs are dressed with. Oh and the french fries... My husband agrees with me that Kebab has the best fries  in city. The small order is splittable between two normal hungry people and the large is splittable between three famished 20 year olds (stepson and friends...)

But what is a doner kebab with out the bread? That IS the most important part, no? This is where other places have failed miserably and this is where Kebab excels. It is not quite the same type of round, pillowy bread used for my beloved German doner kebabs, however, Kebab's bread is much, much better. Their bread is the perfect home for all of the meat, veggies and sauce. It is a little airy, a little chewy, super flavorful, and definitely substantial enough to hold everything together without falling apart. They make their bread fresh all day long and I always buy a few extra rolls to take home with me which will set you back all of $0.99 each. 

TIPS: add feta to everything and throw on some of the homemade hot sauce that is over by the silverware. Order an extra side of garlic aioli, it is MOST delicious. Pass on the side of falafels and just get a bread basket with aioli. They do accept credit cards with a $0.50 extra charge. BYOB!

This was the worst experience I've had at a local restaurant.  Sandwiches are sub par, we couldn't even finish the meal. Had a Philly sub. It was so soft and flavorless I couldn't even eat a half sandwich.  Save your money.  Walk away......walk far away..

Came here for dimsum on Sunday morning. We were seated very quickly. The food carts come around and we start eating almost instantly. We ordered all the usual dishes (shrimp rolls, Sui mai, ha gow, chicken feet ect) everything was mediocre, nothing amazing. We then started ordering other dishes by appearance. It just got worst and worst. Customer service here is very bad. The hostess and one male server was probably the better ones. Everyone else was very hesitant to get hot sauce, water for whatever reason. We had to ask multiple times just to get something! The worst part was when I wanted to get some dishes to go for my aunt and uncle, it was pretty much impossible. I asked one female server and she just told me to wait until the cart comes and then ask for a take out box... We waited for about 25 minutes and the cart didn't come by yet. We asked the hostess and she got the take out quickly. Will not be coming back!

My friends and I went there for dinner and karaoke. We were told that there is a minimum charge of $300 for the room so it is either we order food until meet the minimum charge or we just pay that amount. So we ordered food and we asked the waiter if what we ordered was enough. Waiter keep saying not enough. At the end the total was almost $600... This restaurant is a Rip off and not honest. Thank you for not letting us know
How much we had order so far. All my friends will not go there ever.

I've been here twice and both times I loved my entire experience. You don't exactly have options, but I do recommended the Spicy Chicken over reg chicken and the beef over then lamb. The only disappointing dish here was the lamb. 

And it's a BYOB!
Food was just ok. $30 for a double burger and a grilled chicken. My first time there.

This was probably the best meal we had over the long weekend.

Decor/service: the service was attentive and friendly. The decor was nice as well. 

Food: this is deff not only a seafood place. the food we tried was all excellent. The zucchini straws and homemade hummus were both good. The steak was surprisingly cooked to perfection and had great flavor. The seafood options I tried were all cooked excellent with plenty of flavor. The puff pastry potato side was decent but would of been better if the inside was a little more creamy/cheesy. Overall it was a very good meal.
Best new Bywater spot in my opinion. Great friendly service. Reasonably priced delicious cocktails and great food! Burgers are juicy and cooked to perfection!

We come every year but it seems like it has gone a bit downhill. I saw a gentleman walking around with shorts and a lady in exercise pants. They clearly have a dress code, it's stated online but yet it's not really enforced it seems. I ordered a lobster bisque which they didn't have so that was disappointing because that was something I was looking forward to. Paul was attentive it was my husband's birthday and friendly enough. He still charged me for the lobster bisque when the check came so I had to bring it to his attention and he had to take it off the check. Paul gave us a mini tour of the restaurant as he escorted us to the stairs to the dessert room which was nice of him. He explained a bit of the history of the restaurant and of each dining room. You get a decent amount of food for the price and our steaks were cooked to perfection. You pay for the experience and ambiance. They did automatically charge a 12% service fee, I left more but for a place like this I feel like there is room for improvement. I feel like the servers have been there so long they get complacent and don't really seem like they enjoy it and try anymore. The feel is very pretentious. We were sat next to a table of six loud obnoxious men was annoying. They were cursing which was very inconsiderate of them since they were obviously not the only patrons in the room. I feel like the staff could have told them nicely to watch their language or try to keep the noise level down a bit. It got so quiet after they left and it was only then that we could really enjoy our dinner peacefully for the last half hour of it. The Harry Waugh dessert room is a must. Eric was friendly and attentive. We always sit in the piano room so we can watch Kenny playing live and he is always open to song requests. Just FYI valet is $5, NOT complimentary.

So, yeah, the food was delicious. General's chicken was amazing. The Chinese Food Tater Tots were two great tastes that taste great together. But get this: I went with a friend, and one of the wait staff ended up being her childhood friend from 6th grade that she hadn't seen in years and years. Go to Red's! You'll never know who you'll run into!

I cannot believe what I just ate. The interior doesn't suggest Italian restaurant but this is easily the best Italian food I've ever eaten. I had the Lobster Ravioli and my girlfriend had the Pear Gnocchi. Out of this world. We got lucky and sat at the bar but it can be a bit of a wait in this small place. Absolutely worth it. I can't recommend it enough. Lovely staff and the chef is an artist.
Come here, come often, come soon.

If I could rate this place and "NOT" give any stars...I definitely would!
I think this is one of the TOP worst fast food experiences I've ever encountered... 
The workers there were rude and obnoxious.
They acted as if they were doing me a favor or something. 
There was no spicy chicken ready.. and the knucklehead young kid in the back that was supposed to be making the chicken thought everything was funny and instead of doing his job he just sat there instigating. 
I sat there for an extended period waiting for whoever the girl was that came up in the front to help the new guy.  She had disappeared in the back supposedly to get some red beans and rice for me and I inquired after standing there for quite some time as to whether or not they were actually "GROWING" the rice and beans... because it was taking so long.... 
But I still kept my positive demeanor up until the point when some other chick comes from the back with a bad attitude. 
Assuming she was a manager because of her different shirt she never introduced herself nor apologize for
my prolonged wait. Or even say "Here here... have a complementary drink or anything for my inconvenience. So I asked her if she was going to offer anything for my trouble? and she proceeds to say "Well what's your trouble? in a very snotty way...and I told her that I had been standing there for quite a while waiting for red beans and rice.
She didn't care she proceeded to keep on doing what she was doing and get smart and that little knucklehead in the back kept on giggling and laughing and I finally asked them what was so funny? and he proceeded to say "What you just asked"... I said "Why is that funny? Is poor customer service funny to you? He couldn't say anything I guess he wasn't expecting that retort.
I just walked to my car and the chick said something snotty as I walked out the door and I kept going I got to my car and I looked behind and she's standing at the door looking my way and I asked her if there was a problem? So she proceeded to say " I just wanted to know if you're STILL thirsty? in a snotty/ condescending / slang-type of way because we all know what it means in slang and it isn't anything good.
 so I replied I'm good are you thirsty? She said something else smart but I had started my car it was getting ready to pull off.
 I laughed and kept doing what I was doing and drove away... all the while I'm thinking of this logo on the wall by the drive-through window while you're standing there inside waiting for your food....That was very obvious That the customer is right and how you should be empathetic and apologize so on and so forth... not one of these people tried to be apologetic or even speak like they had good common sense. Other than the new guy who I felt bad for. 
If this is the example that this so-called manager is for her workers... I feel really bad for them.
 This definitely IS NOT a good look for this establishment!
And to add insult to injury, I returned home only to find  that there were no biscuits in my bag. WTF????
I can't wait to hear from corporate about this one!
It's sad when unhappy people project their NEGATIVITY onto other people. 
If they are dissatisfied with their jobs, then they should find other employment. "NOT take it out on the customers!
But...I'm a firm believer of karma! And what goes around comes back around folks!
Phenomenal food and service. Best Brussels sprouts in Philly. Excellent old-fashiioneds. Highly recommend this place. Well worth it.
This place never ceases to disappoint. The flavors of the eastern mediterranean are so well represented. It's a must try in Philly.

While they're known for their croissants I can honestly say everything I've had from sandwiches to quiche is amazing! This is a don't miss! The almond croissant is my absolute favorite. The staff is kind and helpful. Wonderful spot!

I was happy about the fast delivery through GrubHub.  It was downhill from there.  The Lemon rice was not traditionally made.  Tumeric and slices of lemon, no peanuts, is not traditional lemon rice.  My Saag paneer was tasteless, no spice, although I selected medium spice.  The heavenly chicken was acceptable.  It's not Indian, but was ok.  I spent a lot of money to be disappointed with an inedible "Indian" meal.  I guess I should have ordered Chicken Tikka Masala, but I can make that at home.  Won't be ordering from here again.
Get the vegan tasting menu by Chef Lenka and prepare to be dazzled. Amazing flavors & presentation, from start to finish.
Love this bar, friendly staff, great beer/cider selections that change regularly. Food is mediocre but standard pub grub (please avoid the pulled pork).

Came for lunch and was delicious. 

I told the order taker, who was very friendly, that it was my first time. She promptly handed me a cup for a free drink and was exceptionally helpful describing the free condiments that are available to all.

The place was much bigger than it originally looked, which was cool. We found a booth and I much enjoyed my pesto chicken sandwich. The chicken was flavorful and the pesto/goat cheese blend wad awesome.

Only nitpick I have is that the downstairs ice machine was out of ice, so had to get my refund upstairs. But really, this place was great!

This was a very touching moment for me on Mother's Day-
After a wonderful dinner  as our family was leaving Anna pulled me aside - it was also their 5 year anniversary. My husband and I were customers from the time she opened, and we would stop in for a respite from his Cancer treatment. He did not survive his treatment. She wanted to thank me. She thanked me for continuing to come all these years and for bringing so many new customers to her restaurant. We both cried and hugged. Then my son & I hugged and cried. Needless to say Anna's Mexican Grill is the best restaurant anywhere in the world. Not because of the complimentary bottle of Herradurra Silver, but the amazing love Anna delivers with the best Mexican food to her customers!

Super clean and cute. You can sub out meat to make things vegetarian. My breakfast wrap was smaller than expected, though. 
Theres a pretty cute baby in the pictures, so im likely to come back.

Certainly not your typical coffee shop, but the quality of their coffee is very, very good.  Additionally, it is a quiet place to work, read, and spend time.  Friendly feel but respectful of your peace....you need to be careful about the atypical hours, but worth the visit.

My husband and I decided to try Ohana Sushi. Excellent service and tasty decision! We were both greeted by the owner, Tony. Very friendly and social environment. Staff are attentive as well and appear to be happy. That says a lot about the owner. All you eat $23.95, well worth it! Only sushi restaurant in Reno I've found that serves legitimate soft shell crab sushi. We'll definitely be back!

We came to this little hidden gem during U of A homecoming weekend last week. From the Google reviews, we decided to check it out. Located in a little strip mall, it didn't look fancy. Small place but once we walked in, I loved the homey and inviting energy. It was definitely a mom pop establishment, but the aroma of the food was heavenly. Our waitress was very friendly and accommodating. I could tell the majority of the customers are locals and I loved the ambience. As for the food.....DELICIOUS! I had French toast, eggs over easy, hash browns and bacon. Everything tasted amazing. Just when I thought I was done, I overheard our waitress ask one of the customers if they wanted a slice of coconut cream pie of pecan pie. I knew I couldn't leave without having a slice; especially since coconut cream pie is my all-time favorite. The slice was big and I could have easily shared it with my husband, but I was being selfish. He ended up getting a slice because he knew I was not going to let him have a bite. Talk about delicious! It was probably the best coconut cream pie I've ever had. All in all, this place is amazing! Much better than the chain restaurants and very reasonable for the amount of food you get. We will definitely be coming back next time we're in the area!

Let me start by saying find another location. I have visited Qdobas all over the country. When I walked into this one a sense of food safety fear raced through my mind.
1. Dirty floor and tables
2. Employees looked, acted like they were intoxicated
3. Customer service was nonexistent 
4. Unclean food construction line.
My date looked at me I looked her and we decided to leave. I am just unsure of how the owners and corporate would let this happen. Do your self a favor and avoid this place.

Everyone who works here is great. Very attentive and genuinely interested in getting to know their customers, not to mention being a positive addition to the neighborhood. 

Fantastic food and friendly service right at the girard el stop. Open for weekday breakfast sandwiches (look delicious but I've never had time to stop) and then lunch and dinner everyday. I think they'd develop more of a following if they opened late night on weekends to serve the nightlife crowd. That might be a good way to get more people interested. 

Overall, it's a really well executed concept in a location that seems perfect for freshly made sandwiches. Hoping that the neighborhood will increasingly come out to support them.

Food was very good. To zero in a little closer and when I ordered was a cheeseburger and fries. Cheeseburger prices decent but the cheeseburger was very mini... Mini as in small. The fries were quite expensive at $3.95 but you didn't get a lot. I feel like I got a lot more fries than I did my burger and I would like to see that adjusted but I'm sure they're not going to adjust that just for me. And maybe that's just me and everyone else is happy with that quantity, price etc..... Going back to the mini burger I would actually say that it's the right size for what a person should eat and I didn't need it much bigger but comparing it to other places you should know it is small and if you're very hungry you might need more. Taste on all.... high thumbs up. Excuse my typos as I'm voice typing.
All i can say is OMG!!!! Be prepared to share.  Only open a few hours daily,  call ahead to be sure

Not very good.   Limited menu and they were out of half of it when we were there.  Pita is store bought and wrap was a tortilla.  Humnmus was good so got 2 stars.   Not really interested in trying again.
This a staple in our house. We love chop house food it's just good eats and the atmosphere of the place is inviting as well.

My sister-in-law and I decided to try this place yesterday afternoon for lunch.  We got there about 11:30am and the doors were locked.  I read the sign which said they were opened so we walked around to the other set of doors which were also locked.  Finally some guy opened the door and literally asked us what we wanted and of course we said we came to eat.  He seemed annoyed and bothered from the moment we got there almost like he had better things to do and telling him we had a LivingSocial deal seemed to make matters worse.  He seemed irritated with us the entire time which came with a great deal of heavy sighing, eye rolling, complete attitude and lack of service, which was astonishing given that we were literally the ONLY people in the entire restaurant!  Then we were told that they hadn't even turned their oven on so we were going to have to wait before they could even cook our food.  Every time he came to the table which wasn't very often he was completely rude.  I asked him if he was the owner and he answered "yes."  I was floored that an owner of a business would treat his customers in the manner that he did.  After we finished eating we sat there waiting for our check while he stood behind the bar talking with someone who walked in and completely ignored us.  After waiting for what seemed like an eternity my sister-in-law finally got up and approached him letting him know we were ready to check out.  He told us we could just leave since we had the LivingSocial deal.  She asked him if he wanted the number off of the coupon and with a good eye roll and heavy sigh he said "I guess" and walked around to the register.  As she was checking out I came out of the restroom and she told me how rude he was yet again.  I was so irritated with our whole experience that I approached him and asked him if we had done something to offend him or if he was annoyed that we had a LS deal.  He said "no its the last day for that deal so I figured I would get a lot of people using that coupon" I said well then I don't understand why you have been so rude to us.  I told him had he not been the owner I would have made sure I got a hold of the owner to notify him how horrible our experience was there.  I told him it was my first and last time ever stepping foot in his restaurant.  You would think that as a business owner this would be a good time to say something to make the situation right and earn someones business back but instead he just looked at me and said "Ok."

Besides the horrible service, the food was terrible and the portions were comical.  We actually stopped by Taco Bell after wards which was more filling and satisfying than that place.  Maybe now the owner will understand why he had two customers in his entire restaurant during what most well established, quality restaurants consider to be a busy lunch hour.

A good 4 stars. Nice staff, and a pretty..... interesting place, to say the least. :) I feel like I can go there, and nobody would ever think to come looking for me at a place like Shameless! LOL I had an espresso, and it was good. A nice, cozy, out-of-the-way spot.

Cute and small neighborhood coffee and ice cream shop, with a very limited breakfast and pastry menu as well. Have lots of options to combine coffee and ice cream of your choice.

Have some seating, but it is very limited. 

Woman working there was extremely friendly.

Delightful place with authentic food and friendly staff. I always get the Three Meat Breakfast Burrito which is absolutely HUGE and tasty to boot. Definitely worth a try if you're sharing or have a hell of an appetite.

Step back in time at this saloon-style bar and gastro pub. Vintage wallpaper and furniture give the bar a charming, old-world vibe fit for sipping - you bet - bourbon. The food menu is limited, but well crafted, with a showcase of artisanal updates on classic favorites like turkey burgers, sloppy joe, and pizza. This casual, neighborhood bar makes you want to be a regular ... or maybe a prohibitionist. Either way, it's a great place for craft cocktails and bar bites without the fuss or pretentiousness that sometimes accompany dimly lit, speakeasy-style lounges ... which of course I love too; but the laidback spin on this classic favorite gives the vibe a fresh, easy update.
The view alone is worth the trip. Have a drink, snack on some lite bites and enjoy the phenomenal view of St. Pete Pier!

Manager regularly takes the phone off the hook to stop incoming orders. 25-30 minute wait MINIMUM for a sandwich... A SANDWICH! severely under staffed and seem to be overwhelmed everytime you go there

I had a ridiculous craving for Arni's, since my roommate from Purdue and I now live in the Indy area.  We didn't have time to sit-in and eat because we had our puppy with us.  Nevertheless, we had to have something to-go.  So we both decided to have the Arni's Sr. Salad w/ Ranch (of course!). We decided against pizza because it would have gotten cold by the time we got home.  

Anyways, this location is very different from the Lafayette ones.  Much more "swanky" and upscale.  Maybe that's why the price was so exorbitant.  It was a little over $20 for our salads.  I guess it was worth it, since it's probably my favorite "meal" salad because everything goes together perfectly.  It's nice that that they have a carry-out window that has a separate entrance near the bar.  I hope to return in the near future to have a pizza with friends again.

We had lunch today and the food was excellent, try the eggplant parmesan.
Wait staff, Cammy and Julio were friendly and helpful.
Our complimentary desert was a delicious lemon caramel offered since we were first time guests.
Please try this restaurant as an alternative to Olive Garden. The food is fresh, tasty and plentiful.

I had heard great things, but was still skeptical. It's impossible to look at their menu, compare it to other restaurants and then decide to come here. You just need to go. From start to finish, this was one of the best meals I have had in Philadelphia. Ever. Each dish was perfectly portioned and more delicious than the last. Just make a reservation, grab a good bottle of wine or beer and try something different. Don't be afraid to try a new dish. This is the place to do it. They absolutely nailed everything.

Came back after being gone for a year to what use to be my favorite pizza place. I was told to find my table in the back room which to my disappointment was in front of the men's and women's restrooms. I sat down without complaining because the restaurant was full. 

Just after my pizza arrived, the staff came into the backroom where I was seated and started deep cleaning and shutting down the room. While I appreciated the fact that they were cleaning the room, turning over chairs and putting them on tables while there were numerous parties still eating made a lackluster atmosphere even worse. Couldn't they just wait until the room was at least half empty? Or better yet shut down part of the room and clean it? 

The worst part was when one staff decided to clean the women's restroom. It was 4 feet from my table where I was eating and she propped open the door with a dirty water bucket and proceeded to clean it with chemicals. The worst part was she went off and left the door propped open for the remainder of our meal. 

Good pizza but I will not be back.

I just love these place.  Now I am a pizza snob so I will tell you that the pizza is decent... Not the best I've ever had but decent.  Now their sandwiches...  Hmm Hmmm Hmmm.. Every sandwich I've ordered top notch.. The chicken parm.. OMG... The meatball parm.... OMG  The cheese steak... OMG.............. ok ok..... you get my point.. The bread is like some Sicilian has an oven in the back baking it on a daily basis.... the sauce those parms I could just take the bread and dip it and eat it with nothing else.  Fortunately for me these guys are 2 minutes from my job.... hoo yah!!!!

Jason

One of the best pizza I ever had!! Can not ask for fresher pizza then blaze. My first time having blaze pizza was from left overs and it was already amazing when simply toasting it back up. But the last time I had it I went to the store and had it fresh right after it was made! I love the idea that all pizzas are the same size no matter what due to the machine they use to help them measure the size of the pizza. Along with that I really love how all ingredients are fresh and we get to put whatever we want on the pizza as long as they offer. They have many options and choices to offer from different sauces, cheese, veggies, meats, and seasoning. Besides that the smores pie they have is very delicious. The smores was quite expensive in my perspective but it's definitely worth a try. But the pizza they offer and amount of topping we can add on it is definitely worth the price !

Have only visited this location once.  Chipotle is always one of our favorite places when in the mood. Can always count on fresh ingredients and savory flavors. I typically go for the Sofritas bowl which is basically marinated tofu crumbles in a savory sauce. Pair that with some fresh grilled veggies and mild salsa and sour cream and OMG. If you've never been to a Chipotle it's very similar to a Subway where instead of building your own sub, you build your own burrito or burrito bowl or salad or taco. They even have kids meals and even though not on the menu will do a quesadilla. Love their chips and guacamole -- best Guac in town!!

Everything at Heartbeet is gluten-free, organic, dairy free, egg free, and meat free. That night scare away some customers, but it shouldn't. Everything we ordered was great. I had the Pad Thai which is peanut-free and a creative veggie based version of the classic dish. My friends tried the BLT, which has coconut bacon and was delicious. 

They also have smoothies, kombucha, and almond milk to go.

WOW!!!  If I could give 10 stars, I would!  

The idea of trying to find a gluten free wedding cake was always a concept that seemed daunting.  And it was, until I found Paula.  After a terrible experience at a local well known GF bakery, I stumbled upon Paula's website.  She answered my laundry list of questions via email without any hesitation or grief & even set us up for a tasting.  She was flexible, accommodating to all of my desires for my wedding cake, and very quick to respond.  The cake we received far exceeded ALL expectations!  On top of being beyond beautiful, every single guest was astonished that the cake was both dairy free and gluten free.  I had a few even try to argue with me!  

I cannot thank Paula enough for giving me the opportunity to have a real wedding cake!  We will use her for ALL of our future GF/DF baked needs.
De-lish!  5 or 6 miles off Hwy 80 but well worth the time it took.  Fresh, tasty, clean, friendly & while a little pricey the quality is worth it!  Hoping to stop by again on the trip back home!

After being a loyal customer for almost two years now to the Plumb location, this is pretty much our favorite sushi restaurant in town. We love the staff, we love the sushi, and the to-go specials they have been offering during COVID can't be beat. We still order here at least once a week, and they recognize me by name on the phone at this point lol. It is our absolute favorite to sit at the bar for all you can eat sushi, but since we haven't been comfortable sitting indoors yet the take out here has been helping us survive quarantine. They did set up some outdoor tables with umbrellas which look super cute, so we will likely venture there soon :)

The beginning of our visit to Red Gravy was a little awkward.  We didn't have a reservation and there were three of us.  Upon talking to the hostess we were going to have to wait 10 minutes, which was fine.  They, however, do not let you wait at the bar.  When we asked if we could eat at the bar she said usually yes but tonight no.  (Later we saw a gentleman eating at the bar, huh?!?)  We were asked to wait outside until our table was ready.

After we were sat things got better.  The menu is full of options and the special that night was pancetta and ricotta ravioli.  Bread is brought out with garlic olive oil.  We also ordered the meatball appetizer and the cheese and meat board.  Both were great.  Our server, a nice lady from New Zealand, gave recommendations for our selection.  For dinner we ordered the chef's special, the shrimp and sausage pasta, and the egg plant rotini....all were very tasty.  We ventured in to dessert after dinner with tiramisu, Belgian Chocolate gelato with cookies, and cannoli.  The cannoli was inundated with cinnamon, it was overpowering, yet the filling was good.  The other two desserts were great!  I would highly recommend this place. We will be stopping back for breakfast prior to leaving.

Looking for a place to satisfy your taste for Thai in a comfortable setting? Look no further than this new addition downtown Indy that seamlessly pairs Thai food with jazz. The relaxing ambience includes candlelight dining in a part modern, part traditional setting that incorporates decor from Thailand. 

The menu is rather extensive, offering noodle, rice, specialty and curry entrees.
I enjoyed the spring rolls and dumplings for an appetizer and the Chicken Eggplant Thailand for dinner, and Sticky Rice with Custard for dessert. The ingredients were fresh, portions generous, and prices reasonable. A return visit is going to be a must!

Worse place ever and I never write reviews. We come here always and will never ever come back. I walked in 15 minutes prior to close and ordered less than the $10 credit card minimum which by the way is illegal from a vendor standpoint to enforce as a restaurant as visa and MC will revoke the ability to use this form of payment. The polite son looked at the dad and he barked at the son which was translated to me "it is a $10 minimum".  I asked him to make an exception because we get takeout here every time we get Chinese. The "Dad" looked at me and said, IN ENGLISH "I ONLY SPEAK CHINESE". OK!!!!  Never again.

Everything about this place is old and gross.  The tables, the seats, the carpet, the walls...everything.  We went here for breakfast and there was nobody at the hostess station, so after several minutes we seated ourselves.  Our server was very nice, but she forgot a few things. One of us had to stop eating until she finally came back with the drink refill she had promised over 10 minutes prior.

The food, to be fair, was okay. The only real disappointment was that the over-medium fried eggs were way underdone.  The pancakes, potatoes, and sausage were all fine.

We won't be going back, though. There are too many clean and updated places in town for me to slum it and come back here.

You'll never see High Voltage being touted by a Food Network guru, and thus by definition, it is truly a hidden Edmonton gem.  Owner Telso has been slingin sammies here for decades, first as a Mr. Sub franchisée, then as an owner/operator under his own moniker, High Voltage.

Why it's touted as a "coffee bar" versus just a sandwich joint, I don't know. The coffee part of the equation has never really been operational. Stick to the main sandwich menu, no deviations, no side orders, you'll be good.  

Telso is Edmonton's "sandwich nazi" à la Seinfield's "soup nazi". Come prepared, don't ask for substitutions, order-pay-done. Get yelled at if you hold up the lunch rush. Telso ain't got no time for that; his food is high quality with no compromise. When the bread quality and price was not up to demand, no more bread. I hold out hope for the return of toasted sandwiches, but in the meantime, the wraps are top-notch. I'm not a big fan of donair meat, but here it's great quality, not too fatty, grilled after slicing, just perfect. Has been for years! 

The fact that High Voltage has weathered years of economic turmoil speaks volumes. 2+ decades and COVID pandemic in, High Voltage has mellowed a bit. One long-time employee is now competently and congenially running the show. The food is still excellent quality, as it has always been. 

YOU GOTTA EAT (a sandwich)  HERE.
I've been here about 5 times and prior to that I've never had creole. This tiny place is an absolute gem. Great service, amazing food, and they are quick to get your order ready.

Don't show up here without a reservation, especially on a weekend unless you don't mind waiting around for a half hour! 

The place is small and cute. You can sit by the pizza counter and watch them make the pizzas or you can get a regular table. Since there were only three of us we had to share a big table with other people. To start off the mean we go the rotolo and a salad. The rotolo was quite nice weird tasting. The mortadella, ricotta, pistacchio pesto combo didn't taste right. We got two pizzas to share between three people and they were more than enough. We got the Quattro formaggi pizza and the Melanzana. The four cheese pizza was my favorite and I highly recommend it. The melanzana was borderline average. It was quite thin (which I like) but somehow it was a little soggy and they were being super conservative on the cheese. Overall pizza quality was quite average! 

The service was really good and we got our food pretty quickly!

Another winner from the Brick & Brew crew! Food is as amazing as Havertown but the atmosphere in this place just blows you away. Spacious and bright with industrial accents and a rustic feel. So excited that they'll be doing takeout at the Malvern location! I've been missing their skillet desserts and hot chicken sandwich.
Truly a taste of NOLA! Loved everything from the oysters to the gumbo! Can't wait to go back on my next trip to the big easy! :)

If you are looking for real southern cooking, this is your spot! You are seated at Formica tables complete with several kinds of hot sauce. Warm yeast rolls appear quickly, paired with butter, not margarine. Your menu is written on a large chalkboard and is full of classics, pork chops,
Fried chicken etc. The Mac and cheese was not the style I prefer, but the warm almond poppy seed cake was amazing!

A great spot for lunch! It has such a cool and relaxing vibe. We had the chicken salad which was delicious and healthy! The kimchi coleslaw was so good we ordered more to go. My kids loved their sandwiches and the popcorn. The owners a super sweet couple. Don't miss having lunch here!!
Tapas style dishes, great for sharing, and experiencing a culinary delight. Friendly staff and generous bartenders.

Best steak I've had in Nashville.  I didn't know how anything could top the delicious pork belly with maple cotton candy appetizer or the heirloom tomato salad with fresh Burrata...but that delicious steak almost made me forget the previous courses.  Boyfriend and I both ordered the small filet med-rare with a truffle Bearnaise.  I'm not even kidding when I say that I felt my eyes begin to water with my first bite.  It was that good.  We barely touched the risotto tots we ordered, but they were also delicious.  I can only eat 3 or 4 oz of steak at a time so I actually had a decent amount to take home.  Also worth mentioning are the killer popovers that arrive with your main course.  It is probably good that they wait until the main for those as I could have easily made a meal of them.  

Service was excellent.  We had two servers and both were very friendly and knew the menu well.  They were also very attentive despite have a very large party of separate checks behind us.  They also brought me a complimentary birthday dessert complete with candle, which was unexpected but appreciated.  

As is the case with all of the M Street restaurants, the decor was gorgeous.  

My only negative comment is that I'm not a huge fan of the wine list being on an iPad as once you order, it goes away.  I like to hang on to the wine list, especially if I'm drinking by the glass.

Santa Barbara Roasting Company is a cool little coffee shop that is actually better than I expected going in. 

My girlfriend ordered an iced mocha with some cinnamon added on request, while I ordered a blended cookies and cream, due to my intense love of sugary drinks that anger most coffee snobs.

My drink was surprisingly good, satisfying my sweet tooth and not as overpowering or heavy as I had feared it might be. My girlfriend, whose coffee standards are far more refined than mine, was quite pleased with hers as well. 

After splitting a lovely little banana bread muffin, you really can't find much to complain about - aside from those silly eco-friendly straws that inevitably turn into soggy paper as time passes.

I'm all for supporting little local coffee shops that serve up good drinks and offer a low-key place to hang out - without trying to go for that whole pretentious "scenester" vibe that far too many of them are guilty of embracing.

Ultimately, I'd say it's definitely worth a visit!

Terrible
Our waitress took an age to take our order and the place was only half full. When she arrived she looked like she was writing an essay on her order sheet. 
Ordered the escargot and the mussels. My wife had the steak sandwich.
My escargot were like rubber and the mussels were cold, I mean stone cold. Wife said her steak sandwich was only ok. 
Will definitely not be going near this place again.

I am very upset that my beloved irony and hipness-free cafeteria-type Pho bastion changed their menu's design, and finally bumped up their prices (well warranted, I might add).  Too many dicks in trucker's caps coming in to resist, I suppose.  Whatever; if it keeps them in business and they keep up the quality that's been consistent from the first time I went there all those years ago, I'll still pay it for the best Pho in this city.  Not to overshadow the bahn mi, mind you.  Wonderful mystery pate, sweet fish sauce and crunchy veggies.  Not the best bread in the world, but it works so well for this application.

Don't let the chumps who shy away from it's sterile aesthetic influence you--Viet Huong has the BEST BROTH in the city.  Hands down.  I would eat a bowl every day if I lived closer.

We had a great brunch here this past week. This was the first place that we went to in NOLA and it didn't disappoint. Everything was amazing. My friend and I both had delicious egg white omelets with the hash and mac and cheese bites. I wish we had room for the famous pecan pie though!

Perfect place to have mexican food. The place was crowded. But didn't have to wait long. The waiter was very friendly and served hot n fresh chips with salsa. We ordered margarita, blackened chicken fingers,  egg plant and blackened chicken entree. The blackened chicken was very well cooked and tasty. Will visit again

If you can get past the incredibly rude host staff, you might be okay. However, we have been to this location 6 times and each time we were greeted with quite possibly the worst attitudes I've ever encountered at a restaurant. Had I not had out of town guests who wanted to try Paula Deen's, I would have left. By the time I got to my table, I was done. I couldn't even enjoy the meal because we were treated so poorly.
If this restaurant wants a shot at staying open, they need to clean out the host staff and start over. They are nothing like the staff in Pigeon Forge. 
After my last visit, I will never visit the Nashville location again. Southern Hospitality?! Yeah right! FAR from it!

2 meat combo. Pulled pork, dry. Brisket, very dry. Baked beans were delicious and highlight of the meal. Coleslaw very bland and didn't really taste like anything. Typical Jiffy like cornbread, I'm not complaining. Overall I've had a lot better, I've had worse.
Best pizza in town! Great customer service reasonably priced. Bit of a hidden gem for us local foodies. Meatball pizza is our jam here.

How does BK run out of burgers?! That's complete incompetence on the part of management. Unless a freezer went down, there is absolutely no excuse. Walk across the Chilis, spend a dollar more and eat a decent burger.

I love this little place. I'm not a huge meat eater so I only get the pulled chicken, but it never disappoints. They have three choices of BBQ sauce to choose from (my favorite is "tangy"). This isn't necessarily a sit-down restaurant considering you just order at the counter, but there are several tables if prefer not to carry-out. The staff is also incredibly friendly and helpful.

P.S. their fries might possibly be my favorite of all time! They're perfection.
Really good Pizza! We had the Avocado Fiesta,  delicious! Nice atmosphere too! Service was good and friendly.

Great burgers, salads and atmosphere! My friends and I like to meet here every now and then for just that. I'm the one that usually gets a cheeseburger and fries, it's always really good! The servers have always been great! The parking isn't that great, but it's at an outside shopping mall. Definitely a place you can take the whole family too!

Nice casual place for Mexican & Central American food.  The food was made fresh to order.  I enjoyed the fried chicken served with plantains and pico de gallo.  It was very filling.  It came with dark meat (leg & thigh) which I'm not a big fan of.  I much rather have a wing and breast, and it didn't list white or dark meat on the menu.  Not that big of a deal.  There was only one person waiting all the tables, and somehow she managed to stay on top of it while keeping a friendly smile on her face.  I will be back again.

That's right folks you heard it here first. The words affordable and downtown used synonymously in the same sentence. Breakfast wise I had one of the most delicious omelettes with all the fancy garnishments. I paid eight dollars and a the portion was more than enough. 

The reasons for being downtown vary for a lot of people. Maybe it's a trip for business or a fun weekend abound. Or like me you frequent the area daily for work. 

The sum of all these parts is simple you won't find a better "bang" for your buck downtown. For a meal in the single digits (what you might pay for a latte) there isn't much of a risk.
Still lots of kinks to work out....both service AND food.  But as a neighborhood local I am rooting for it as we need good spots in our hood. Fingers crossed  .
Should be one star. Bad service cold burgers half empty should have known better. Go to Texas Roadhouse for a better burger and good service. Yuck%!!!

AMAZING!!!! From the environment and decor to the food this is a great place to go if you're craving some good BBQ. Also the service is really fast, we ordered and sat down and our food was out 10 minutes later! The customer service was also great, very friendly. 

I got the pulled pork, mom got turkey, and bro got smoked wings - no lie, they were all the best I've had. Dessert was good but nothing special.
Great Thursday night special , kill the keg . Awesome food . Chill atmosphere.

Mother's is a New Orlean's institution so my friends and I had to give this place a try.  The restaurant is pretty easy to find - look for the long lines at all hours of the day.  The line moves fairly quickly, as the restaurant is huge.

Once you step inside, you'll need to step into another line to place your order.  You'll be able to see the food being prepped and review the specials of the day.  Know what you want, because that line also moves fairly quickly and there is no time for anyone to hem and haw.  There are a lot of people they need to serve!

We were there a few minutes before 11 am and were told we could not order off the regular menu as breakfast was still being served.  We decided to step back to let a few parties move in front of us but even that did not allow us enough time.  An employee noticed our dilemma and ushered us to the front of the line and told the cashiers to let us order from the lunch menu.  Others were having the same issue as us and it was creating problems.   Many thanks to that kind gentleman.

I ordered the shrimp and oyster po'boy with a side of dirty rice.  Be warned, their sandwiches are HUGE and can easily be shared.  The seafood was lightly battered and seasoned.  It was not the slightest bit greasy.  The sandwich came with mayo and some shredded cabbage on a soft, thick sandwich roll (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/mothers-restaurant-new-orleans?select=CqOy-1uLjwIG5L1McsSR2Q#CqOy-1uLjwIG5L1McsSR2Q).  A few dashes of hot sauce and squirts of lemon juice completed the sandwich for me.  Overall I the sandwich was okay.  Nothing out of this world, but it was just as I had expected and it was good.  The only bad side, if this can be a bad thing, was that there was just so much food!  I ended up eating only one half of the sandwich and then picking out the seafood from the other half.

As for the dirty rice, I quite enjoyed it.  I shared this cup of rice with my friends and we all thought it was good.  The rice was cooked well, and the bits of meat-to-rice ratio was good.  Seasoning was spot on.  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/mothers-restaurant-new-orleans?select=9qtVZCaYNV0ucwis2HwaFw#WFc4lbeegnG_0zktkmKYeg

One friend ordered the Famous Ferdi Special, which comes with ham, roast beef, debris and gravy and loved it.  I tried some of it and thought it was delicious.  It could have easily fed three of four people!  

Another friend ordered the omelette and noticed that the eggs were prepared ahead of time and filled to order.  From my sample taste I found it to be okay, but nothing I would go out of my way to order at Mother's.  Stick with what they are famous for, I say.

As for the service, I found the staff to be direct and efficient, but my friends found them to be bordering on rude.  Quite frankly the service was similar to what I've seen in many other super busy/packed restaurants.  The staff have a lot of tables to take care of and lots of requests to meet.  They do the best they can and don't have time for customers that don't know what they want.  Rude?  Not to me.  Actually I found the attitude a bit comical.
I love the patio! It's beautiful peaceful and truly makes an evening special! We had a last minute large party and they were extremely accommodating to us! Great place with superb service!

Great coffee. Just that black rimmed glasses with out lenses, laptop taking up the whole table,loud projecting cell phone voices,yuppity yuppie type clientele. I'm from California and I'm saying this so...... The building is old, where you gotta go up and down stairs to find a spot to sit. You'll end up outside for sure. Coffee is way overpriced. People who work there are nice. Just a shame they have to deal with the people who hang out there. I have to go to Starbucks to get away from the Yuppies?????huh???really??Geez!!

What a fantastic hidden gem!! Found this place on Yelp and decided to visit for lunch. The two of us sat inside the restaurant and enjoyed the lunch specials plus 2 drinks for around $15.00. Our orange chicken meals came with fried rice and a choice of egg roll or crab rangoon. This is probably the freshest Chinese food I've ever had. Everything was so good! The interior is nicely updated and very clean. As we sat and ate tons of people filtered in and out for take out orders. The staff were so friendly, we will definitely be back!! One tip: bring cash--they don't accept card.

The hotel room itself is fine, nothing fancy but perfect if you're traveling with a small family. Make sure you get the newer renovated rooms as opposed to the older rooms because it makes a huge difference. I think if you want a larger room you'll get put in the tower with the older rooms. The older tower decor and vibe reminded me of the Tower of Terror ride that used to be at California Adventure park lol. Anyways, the elevators were packed anytime we used them because of how tiny they are. They have 8 or 10 elevators in use but you can only fit 8 people max and less if those people have luggage with them, which most of the time they do. I know there's not much that can be done about that but I've never had to wait in a long line to use and elevator. I would've used the stairs but hiking up 12 flights with a 3 year old was not on my to-do list.

Stopped in with the girlfriend on a Saturday afternoon. The place looks and feels like a down home BBQ joint and it really is. 

The staff was extremely nice, and helpful. Service was great and the food was amazing and not too expensive. If you are in the area you have to try it at least once. The smokes wings were great and the ribs were fall of the bone tender.

I'm not a big cafeteria-style restaurant fan, but this place is A-OK in my book. Again, I hate the cafeteria set-up but the food isn't too bad. Most of it I won't go anywhere near being that they put 80 lbs of butter and oil on everything but some of it is good. I gravitate towards the roasted quarter chicken with broccoli on the side. I also love their marinated vegetable salad and a few other cold salad options are good.  The crowd here seems to always be people over the age of 60.  The workers here are nice for the most part. I find the cashiers to be the nicest of all of the staff members. I don't eat here but MAYBE 4 times a year, it's just not my type of food. But the chicken is always juicy and the cold salad items are always fresh...... that's all I can speak on!

This place is so unique.  Being on vacation that is something you look for.

We were casually walking down beach drive and saw that it was the one year anniversary of Flute and Dram.  They had specials live music and really friendly faces at the door.

We went inside and the atmosphere was trendy and cozy all at the same time.

We ordered true champagne which I honestly do not think I've ever had it before.  It was soooo amazing and on special.  Our waitress even brought us a free glass of sparkling wine to celebrate their one year being open.

We had a great time and wonderful service!

I should have known when I walked in and the place was almost empty!  The rice was mushy, the fish was room temp and the sushi chef was rushing us through.  My daughter ended up sick on the ride home and left her sushi on the side of the road.  Never again!

We've been going to this restaurant for a year or so and have always like them. It's always a decision between going to them or pho noodles. I've always like Nan Zhou, but honestly, sometimes it's really a hit or a miss. 

Their price is very reasonable (cheap). I have noticed they seem to have cut down the amount of noodles they give you lately and sometimes the clams are not fresh. I'd still go back for their beef noodle soup though.

This is one of my favorite restaurants. It's very authentic and reminds me of food my mom cooked. The service is always great and the food comes out quick. I have been a patron for over 19 years and will be for another 19.

Pretty much all the positive reviews of this place seem to be older, before they lost their cook and shortened the menu. Expensive sandwiches that weren't very good and took over 30 minutes to get to us. The bartender was not very bright and spent most of the time we were in there on her phone. Overall just a bad experience here.

This place has some good stuff. Ordered the cleaver, tri tip sandwich, sausage sandwich, and mac and cheese (not pictured). The cleaver is my favorite out of the four and I've gone back a few times specifically for that sandwich. I like how there are a variety of sauces to choose from. The mac and cheese was average in my opinion, nothing about it stood out to me. Staff is super friendly and the bathroom decor is interesting. Will definitely be coming back to try out the other food on their menu.

Wonderful service from Adam and Andrew at the bar. Adam went way out of his way to get my husband's IPA as the tap was acting up.
