The salmon, as usual, was delicious as was the new to the menu Club Sandwich. Our last visit the staff was only playing country and western music so we were happy it was back to a mix of good tunes.

First time here. Due to the Coronavirus I had to order take out. We got the shrimp basket. It was delicious. I also got a small order of red beans and rice, delicious as well. We will be back when we can eat in for some boiled crawfish!

We went here for brunch but I have also been in for BBQ crawl and a glass of wine so three separate occasions. The decor feels like they are trying too hard for what it actually is. The staff were equally snooty. When we went for brunch the host (maybe owner) visibly rolled her eyes when we asked to sit at a high top (why?). The food was bland and extremely expensive. I guess that's why they were the only restaurant without a wait for brunch on Saturday at noon.

Went here for a reception after a conference- I'll start by saying that we had the advantage of having the rooftop to ourselves, but it was magnificent.  We had a great fall evening to enjoy the stunning views of the new downtown Tucson.  You can't get a much better vantage point of Congress and the nightlife than this patio!

The food, brought over from Hub I learned later, was great- we did more appetizer based, but the Prime fries were my favorite- the prime rib on top very flavorful, and the caramelized onions/cheese making the fries have layers of flavor.  Definitely not a diet snack, but worth it.  Mac n' cheese was also divine- especially the chicken one.  Go for the extra protein!

Drinks were also good- pretty standard, but strong enough to get the night going.  Bartenders were nice, efficient, and willing to chat as much as you wanted them to.  Definitely a good place to go for a special event.

I just can't get over how old the crowd is on Saturday nights. I guess it's a niche that needs filling, but it's not for me. The bar itself is fine, a good space, dancy and loud at night like many others in the area so the place itself isn't so bad, but it's just weird look around beyond my friends and not see anyone within 10 years of my age.
Grear hang out spot with an excellent staff, Jafra is the place to relax with a few friends
Always good!  Best Jewish deli around.  Service is great, prices are fare!  The challah French toast is a must!
Pretty good chicken sandwich. Chicken was moist and the condiments were fresh. The place was clean and staffed by young, hip dudes.

The setting gets 5 stars. The food, service, and prices, 2 stars. Yes, it's a beautiful location (and I'm a sucker for great restaurant ambiance). However, the food left a lot to be desired. We had reservations for brunch. The place was almost empty, with just 1 large group and a few stray visitors like ourselves. We were seated outside with a great view, but no shade. The sun was glaring in our eyes. We didn't think to bring sunblock to brunch, so we had to request to be seated inside, which was vacant, anyway. Our waitress argued with us, saying, "But the view is what you're paying for!" She was 100% right, but the check would have been harder to swallow with sun poisoning. She sighed in an annoyed fashion and finally agreed to sit us inside. We even got the treat of an eye roll from her. The brunch buffet is adequate for a smaller, cheaper venue. There isn't much variety and nothing stood out taste-wise. Our soundtrack to brunch was the staff loudly joking about how crazy their Saturday nights were and who had the worst hangover. Whoever owns this place should make some major changes. It's such a shame that the place has such potential, location-wise, but is so poorly managed.
Service has been so/so when we've gone, and the place empty, but the food has been absolutely delicious. We try a little bit of everything we can whenever we go.

I have been to Abyssinia, just right next door several times. I have liked Abyssinia's food, but I find their service very slow, and their servers also do "random billing"!

So I wanted to try this smaller place just adjacent to it.

At first I found the food to be very very delicious and liked it instantly, but towards the end of my meal, I started having weird unbearable cramps in my stomach, and then for the next 12 hours my stomach was EXTREMELY bloated.

I wonder if they used a lot of baking soda in their Injiras or Lentils, because I feel bloated like this whenever I consume food with heavy use of baking soda (or some variant of that)!

I wanted to like this place, but now with this experience during my VERY FIRST VISIT here, I don't think I will eat here again.

So eat here at your own risk!

Really like  the food and this particular location.  But looks like the new help here are a JOKE! I had to correct my order twice, pretty hard to do when the person is right in front of you. Not to mention I caught one of them eating behind the counter... Didn't quite see where he got the food from and sure as Hell glad he didn't do it while I was getting my food. I really hope this experience doesn't happen again. I really like this place.

The food and service were phenomenal. I went with a party of 9 and every single plate ordered was delicious and rich in flavor. The majority's favorites were the Courtbouillon and the Trout Eugene. I have to say, however, that my favorite dish, appetizer, was the chicken gumbo. It was heaven. The banana bread pudding and banana parfait and crème brûlée were delectable. The prices were fair to the quality of the food. My only preference would have been for the New Orleans entree to also include rice or vegetables versus a slice of bread.

I went to Wings Gone Wild for the first time in years a few weeks ago and had a wonderful experience.  It was a Saturday afternoon and college football was in full swing. I tried Mango Habanero wings as well as Honey Sriracha wings and both were fantastic.  it was nice to have something different.  I also spotted Southern Fried Chicken and Beer on their menu and just had to order that as well.  Crispy fried chicken served with a PBR, it was INCREDIBLE!  I can't wait to go back and explore more of their new menu. Service was fantastic and the crowd was great.  Definitely a fun neighborhood spot.

My date and I both had the pork with sweet potatoes, and greens.  We were both pleased but just wished the portion sizes were a little bigger.  I had the beef chili and she had a soup that we both liked.  We each had a mini dessert which was good too.  Ran about $65 so a little steep.

I've read comments about food lacking flavor, I had no issues during my visit. It was busy and we didn't mind waiting, I was occupied eating chips n salsa, while having a conversation. Place isn't perfect, but it's good enough for me because I enjoyed my meal, waiter periodically checking up on us, it was busy so we understood. Gladly return to have another meal at some point in the future. Thank you/ Gracias la comida estaba buena.

After a long day of work this restaurants open floor plan and relaxing vibe with live band help put your work day stresses at ease. The restaurant is very spacious and has an huge open kitchen concept so you don't feel boxed in.

I was also terribly impressed with the food. 

My husband and I came here for drinks and appetizers. Good beers and cocktail choices. 

The buffalo chicken wings were hands down the best I've ever eaten. Even if u r not into buffalo wings go ahead and order them!!!

The pretzel bread with fondue was a nice addition. 

Hummus was very good. 

Chicken tortilla soup was meh. Probably wouldn't order than one again. 

Look forward to coming here again when I'm visiting Tucson.

Came here after a Soul game Saturday night and the service was terrible. Must have different owners now or something- the whole interior looked totally different then when I remember it. The staff didn't greet us and I wasn't even sure the waitress actually waits on you. I sat with my friend for about five mins- no menu nothing just waiting for someone to come help us. 

Finally when the waitress came over after I walked up to find out if they actually do take the order at the tables- she didn't bring any menus. No place setting or utensils. Besides the worse service the wait time was horrible when it came time to wait for our food. We ordered a plain pizza and fries with cans of soda. No cups or anything for our soda. 

When the food finally came- it tasted just okay nothing too special- the pizza didn't taste like it was made with fresh ingredients like the previous owners had once had it. Deff won't be coming back here because I felt like the customer service was lacking and it took way to long to actually get our food.
I love this Zoe's Kitchen.  It's the cleanest I've ever been to, and the staff is very friendly.  I've always gotten my food quickly.  This is my go to restaurant, love it!!

I came here while staying at the airport Marriott which makes sense because this is the restaurant attached to the motel.  First, it was very busy.  There were no bar seats available and when eating by myself I would much rather sit at the bar so that was my first disappointment.  My second was I had to wait an extended period of time for a table for 1.  The hostess was just slow.   Once I sat down, the service was fast, and I have no complaints there.

I ordered a NY Strip and there is nothing to say besides it was ordinary.  It seemed to be totally unspiced and simply bland.  I ordered it rare which it was.  However, I like the outside to be much warmer than this steak was.  I know it is a hotel restaurant, and that is what you get.  

I also had a garden salad which was good.  I have no complaints with regard to the salad. They had blu cheese which was not on the menu but they had it.  I prefer really chunky blu cheese but they had creamy.  I guess that is just a preference though.

The bottom line is this is an ok place to eat.  The issue is that it should be much better at this price point.  I will probably eat here again if I ever stay at the Philly airport Marriott again, but the best I can say is it is a serviceable restaurant.
Had the chicken tikka masala and naan combo.  The chicken had great flavor and spice and the naan was great also. Was impressed.  Would definitely go back!

Don't let the uninspired name turn you away.  This is our favorite Chinese restaurant,and by looking at other Yelpers' reviews, we are not alone!  The service is always great and the menu offers, not only American-style Chinese food, but Chinese-style Chinese food.  I really dig the Pork in Szechuan sauce Chon King flavor.  I did a story for The Wok on KKOH: https://soundcloud.com/monty_wolf/christmas-dinner-alternative

Awesome food.
well treated jeff game a sample as i waited.
Very proffesional. verry delicious. 
I was full but had to finished.

This was the first restaurant I tried at fountain square. I was intrigued by how many good reviews they had. 

I ordered a portobello spinach melt sandwich with a side of their soup special (black bean and ham soup). It was good, the portobello was a bit too done so it was very black. 

The food was good nothing too exciting where I'll be telling all my friends to come too.
They layout was nice, the server was friendly, overall this is very hipster looking for sure!

I might try it out again soon, there's a lot of variety so maybe I'll find something that really stands out

Had brunch here, sat outside. The waitstaff is extremely helpful and attentive. Food was pretty good however they were out of the pulled pork that I wanted (must mean its great). Food took a bit long to come out but once it did they kept checking in on us. 

Brunch was inexpensive, would definitely go again.

Disappointing.  We were walking Main Street on a rainy Thursday evening and stopped in for dinner.  The area was pretty empty on account of the rain and it not being one of the Christmas celebration days so we were not surprised to find the place empty.  Our waiter was nice, but got at least one thing wrong at every step.  I'm pretty flexible so I only asked him back if it was a critical error, but even that got annoying over time.  Much of this could have been solved if the waiter paid attention to basic details.  For example, my friend ordered a salad, actually said "I'll have the XX salad" and the dish was served as a wrap.  Items generally expected for a dish were not included or offered such as ketchup for fries or malt vinegar for fish and chips.  

At the end, we asked for boxes, only got one.  Then we asked for separate checks (2) and got one.  One of us paid with cash (needing change to leave a tip) and the other paid with a card.  When the waiter collected payment, he picked it up and started walking away.  I stopped him and requested the be split by person (again) and he nodded and kept walking.  I had to follow him into the back room to clarify what was supposed to be charged on the card and what was to be covered in cash.  When he returned to our table, the charge was correct, but our waiter decided to round down the cash change to his advantage of a larger tip.  

Both myself and my friend are generous tippers, and having been a server myself, I know the ropes and usually tip 30-40% or more on slow nights.  We both tipped only 15% (minus the extra change already taken) but the server could have gotten much more had he paid attention. 

The food was ok, typical bar fare, not great enough to inspire a return visit.

Excellent food and service all around. They have their recipes dialed in for sure. It was pretty packed but that's going to happen when the food and drinks are good. It had a sort of dinner charm which I kinda like. It wasn't your typical Mexican or Tex Mex joint painted up to look like all the others.

Worth a visit.

Great food and service  We love to sit in the bar, first come first seating but full menu selection   Love the managers choice selection.    Bang bang shrimp is a must have.   They also have my favorite wine conundrum

This is my absolute favorite spot for breakfast!! For the first time in my review history I decided to rewrite a review. What's even more shocking is that they already had a 5 star review from me but it just didn't seem good enough anymore. I would give them even higher than 5 stars if I could. I wake up craving Shrimpy's every weekend. What makes this place so special is that I don't ever order or crave the same thing. I have had the vast majority of their menu and I have loved all of it. I don't worry that I will regret not sticking with my usual because every time I try something new I am thrilled with that dish as well. There is no other place I can think of that I trust that I am going to love everything on their menu and that not only makes it special but spectacular! 

Another great things about Shrimpy's is the customer service. I have never been disappointed in the service and Sian, the bartender, is one of the best! She will fix you right up with a craft beer or stiff drink for their all day happy hour on Sundays. 

The restaurant is also extremely clean and decorated fun and funky with a cross between a musical, beachy, and cajun vibe. If you haven't tried this place you really need to do yourself the favor!

Don't believe the attire Listed and this is a lot less classy than u would think. People treat it like a sports bar wearing baggy Jeans jersey and sneakers. Seating was uncomfortable although they had plenty of empty tables. When I walked in I asked about my reservation and the two girls as hostesses turned to each other and continued to talk about the boys that were hitting on them for 2-3 minutes letting me just stand there and watch. I sat down and we were only brought the restaurant week menu not the full menu, which was insulting? The place is just way more casual than they led you to believe. Food was good for the most part but I don't think I would come back here again. Server also didng come back to refill water at all nor did she come back to give me a to go box. I had to find someone else

Unique (maybe misspelled) was the best thing about this place. She was pleasant and knowledgeable. Drinks, or premade concoctions, as the manger explained them to be were HORRIBLE! I ordered the perfect margarita and there was nothing perfect about it! Then the manger had the gall to tell me that if I wanted it specially made, I had to pay for it upfront. Off-putting and rude! Had the appetizer sampler and it was just ok. Needless to say that I won't be back!

Great food, drinks, service & atmosphere. You can't go wrong at Del Pez! Shrimp tacos are AMAZING! And if your having folks over your place for dinner, try their take out taco kits, packaged well & yummy.

Service was horrible!!! Our waitress was forgetful and non welcoming. We sat there without silverware with our food sitting in front of us for a long time. Had to ask multiple times for drink refills. Other waiters carried out food. And extra item was added to bill! Sat there again for 10-15 minutes while bill was straightened out. Food was meh. Won't be coming here again!
Friendly staff, cute atmosphere and pizza was hot, fresh and ready by the slice .... definitely and easy quick spot for food.

Crawfish is a bit pricey and very salty. If you pay cash it's $3.40 per pound. If you pay by credit card, it's $3.60 per pound. I was disappointed that they were so salty. They are usually better than this.
Higher price point but the ingredients are A+.  Always a good experience, service is on top of it.  Always recommend eating as a group

Love this local Carp joint for breakfast! My friend Debbie and I go often and the owner Rick and his son are oh so nice and the food is awesome! Love that they have kombucha! The service is actually really good and quick they won't have you waiting. The interior could use a little spruce up besides that A+ keep up good work guys!!!

I've had the chicken, lamb, & falafel here. Each of those was pretty good, albeit kinda dry. I'd recommend the falafel of the three. In a vacuum, the food is probably 3 stars. But there are 2 things that bump it up: the fact that you get a gargantuan amount of food & the lavash, which is easily the best I've ever had.

Seriously, it's basically 3 meals for the price of 1 (2 if you're super hungry). And the bread is just incredible. It's slightly charred on the outside, but pillowy on the inside and it's probably the best thing since sliced bread (because it is sliced bread). 

In summary, the food is pretty ok, but the bread alone is worth it, I could eat it all day.

$37 for this. I called in and order a Maqluba with lamb. Upon check out I asked does this one dish I order cost that much? They then told me I'd ordered BBQ lamb AND maqluba lamb.  

Okay great so I paid $40 for 2 dishes and was extremely disappointed upon trying them. The lamb was bone dry and way over cooked and the maqluba had no flavor at all. All I could taste was cinnamon. 

If it were a big restaurant chain I'd a refund immediately but since it's a small family business, I'll choose to walk away. Not good food at all I'm very sorry to say. The Baba ghanoush was good but that's it.

It was nice the cook came over and introduced her self I ordered a mushroom swiss cheese burger with fries and was really delicious over all it was a nice little bar with decent food.  I went because my friend he loves bars and drove in from St. Charles, Mo and he had to go to the famous Jack Patrick Bar and Grill. So we did, I'm a more of Cinder house,  Preston, The Chase Club, Dominic's, Herbie's and Tenderloin Room type of girl myself I'll even Do and Love BB'S jazz and Blues and soups and Hamerstones but Jack Patrick was ok.

Showed up at 830a on a Friday. Major wait for a table for two. Should have called ahead for a table. We will know better next time. We have eaten at the other Maggie Mae's place on the bluffs but this is the original location. 

This is an unpretentious, friendly cafe. There is outside seating looking over the bay. A bit too cool & windy today to sit outside.

Upon arrival you add your name to the list. There are booths and a couple of tables along with 6 chairs at the counter. Many locals and regulars are seen. Three firemen were seated before us. 

Service is prompt and efficient. I got Mom's Favorite two eggs sunny side up, nuclear bacon, whole wheat toast and a hash brown casserole. Truly delicious. My wife got the breakfast burrito. Everything was exactly as ordered. Bottomless coffee. Our server Maggie was very solicitous. There is no "Maggie Mae" we were informed that the place was named after the  Maggie Mae of the R. Stewart song. 

$24 breakfast for two. 

A very good breakfast stop. We will return regularly. 

Mark & Nancy

Worst Carryout Service.  Can't wait for the Management to be REPLACED.  
We Love Portillo's.  Enjoy it in Chicago and each year had we ship sandwiches by the case as Christmas Gifts.  

We CAN NOT PLACE A CARRYOUT ORDER due to the horrible customer service and poor phone skills at the Fishers location.  

You call, get placed on hold for at least 5 minutes.  Hang up, call back, get placed on hold again.  Give Up and just keep driving down 69 never even placing an order.  

We let the Management know this was our 3rd and final attempt to place an order and his suggestion was to order online.  There is Something Really Wrong with this Portillo's.  Chicago doesn't stink like these guys.
Best homemade food for cheap in the quarter. Everything is fresh and homemade. The staff is very friendly. Eat there a few times a week

I really liked eating there. The food was really good. I like that do you have a meal planned poke bowls. The girl that was serving me was super nice. They give you water for free. Also on your first day you can get soda for free by putting in your phone number. I liked poke bowl with the salad base instead of the rice. I like having choices. Everything looks fresh.

The sauces are great, especially the one they call "the heat".  The meat is good and tender, too.  The sides are all disappointing: dry potatoes and vegetables, bland beans, overcooked hushpuppies and hard bread. The service also leaves a lot to be desired.

Great place at international mall. This place is always packed, so we went during the non busy hrs, at 3 pm.  The vegetarian burger was amazing, the patty was made of quinoa and other herbs, it was topped off with white cheese and kale. The burger came with home made fries. We also had a quinoa tofu bowl, which was too good as fresh vegetables and tofu were sauteed just right, not to greezy nor too raw, and the flavoring was perfect, right amount of quinoa was provided. These were both filling items and healthy. Service and atmosphere was both very good.
Hands down the best coffee in the Treasure Valley. They roast all their beans locally.

My wife and I have been to Terrain several times. We eat out a lot, but typically at good restaurants. Terrain is very pretty, quaint, very unique. It is byo, which is great. 
As far as the food goes, very inconsistent. The breakfast is great and we always enjoy, but dinner is another story. The last two times we were there, our steaks were overdone and my fish was dry. At $35 a plate, the food should be perfectly cooked. I mentioned both issues to the wait staff and we were still charged full price for our meals even though we left half our food on the plate. We may go back for breakfast, but I think we are through with dinner there. Unfortunate, and we couldnt help but notice that while we were there Friday night, the place was half empty.

Not a bad spot for a meal. I liked what we ordered- tuna appetizer and a burger.  However.. if you want to have a conversation with your companion- go elsewhere. I tried this place on a Friday evening around 7. The bar crowd was very drunk and very loud. Perhaps at non-peak hours this could be a great place.

One of my faves that my fiance and I frequent rather often. Love the ambiance and dim lighting. The food is amazing. Every time they get it right. I actually find myself craving Sea Bass mid-week. Just the right amount of crisp to the skin, paired with a simple vegetable and couscous, yummmm. I had my birthday dinner here last year and yet again it was a hit! A little hard getting a lsat minute reservation but that is to be expexted as everyone shares the same good feelings about the food. Keep up the great work Melograno and thanks!!

Local cafe. Nice place to meet friends for a quite chat or to have a nice casual lunch. Like they say not Cha mama but your always at home. 
Happy birthday to Tasha a server there. 
Hope u have an awesome day
Great location for a staycation in Nashville.  Walking distance to many great restaurants.  Hotel is high end but not over the top.
Had pancakes, bacon and eggs.  The pancakes were way above average and the server was excellent.  When in Goleta, I will be back.

Cheap, tasty, 95+ health rating, open late take-out, and offers Eat24: Booyah!

Ok, Best Wok lacks... ambiance but who needs fancy fish tanks or large statues for the added up charge anyway???? 

Best Wok has a small space located in the Swett's strip mall. It is best suited for to-go orders however; there is limited seating for dine-in. 

I was feeling under the weather so my co-worker recommended their Hot and Sour soup (large) with a side order of Spring Rolls = $6.50. I placed a order Take Out on Yelp 24. My order was ready before the estimated time and service was quick and friendly. When I arrived home, my food was still warm and well contained, no spills. I am pleased that it was really good! I was only able to eat have of it and saved the rest for lunch the next day. Two days of vegetarian comfort food. Yes!

I actually felt bad that I had such low expectations for this place. In case you were wondering it did cure my sore throat and dry cough. Guess there is some truth as to Chinese food medicine ;-).
I went here with a friend of mine once. The taste of the food was great. However the next day I have some serious stomach problems due to the food. Other than that I would give it 5 stars.

Second visit, this time for lunch and their lunch buffet.  My only disappointment here was the size of the buffet.  When my lady and I first came for dinner, the server told us that they pretty much have the whole menu available at the buffet, but that didn't appear to be true since the buffet only had 7 or 8 items.  Regardless, this is excellent Indian food.

They had a good selection of chicken and vegetarian dishes, including staples like Chicken Tikka Masala, which I had for dinner last time and was a good as I remember, and Tandori Chicken, which is good, but strange that it is so popular.  Just tastes like cooked chicken to me - its good, but the other dishes are so much better.

I tried a couple of new items, including something called Dal Tadka, which is a soupy kind of dish made with lentils, and also a veggie kolapuri and a chicken do pyaza.  There were multiple dishes there, and I couldn't tell you how they were made or what was in them, but I can tell you that I wrote down a few of them and I cannot wait to try them at home.

The best praise I can give this place is that we never had Indian food prior to our first visit, but since then, it has become a staple in our house.  While our recipes may not be authentic, we probably cook an Indian dish once to twice per week, and I can't wait to incorporate a couple of new ones from this visit.

Anyway, back to the buffet - they also provide you with naan bread, but it is not part of the buffet - presumably because you (I) would eat most (all) of it.  

Besides the slightly limited selection, the only other complaint I have is that it was freezing.  I know its early September in Florida, but you do not need your dining room to be 60 degrees.  Nothing stayed hot once removed from the buffet line.  Still, that's not enough of a reason to remove a star.

I only had 2 plates (yes, only - shut up, it was a buffet), but that is not a mark against Gateway to India.  I could have gone back for a third and probably a fourth, but I was being good.  I hate it when I'm being good.

Ok. I don't really eat red meat much. However...
O to the M to the G!

I force my sister, who works in the area, to bring me a burger when she can. I live in Jenkintown, so you can imagine that the burger's not piping hot when it gets here. But guess what? It's still delish! 

Wonder if it would be better reheated? Perhaps one day I'll stop scarfing it down fast enough to find out... Somehow I think it's like counting the licks to the center of  a Totsie Roll Pop. The world may never know.

I enjoyed having lunch here, I got the coconut shrimp lunch dish with the chicken fajita soup. Both were good and I was happy they had the calories listed on the menu. 

It was a fun lunch and I want to go back for drinks very soon. 

I think my favorite part of the restaurant was the atmosphere.

Had to stop by and have some BBQ
The girl was really nice taking our orders and letting us know the different options 
I got the brisket, TriTip, and sausage 
With Mac and cheese and Mac salad 
Will be back
Best taco(s) I've ever had...and I've had a lot of tacos!!!  I always get something different and everything is amazing!!  The Federale is my favorite though - shrimp + bacon = amazing!

A nice chill spot nestled in Chestnut Hill.  Great outdoor seating and friendly service.  Food is terrific.  Haven't been let down yet.  And it's only a few blocks from where I live.  Will have to check out Tuesday night's poker game sometime.
Average at best.  Coffee mate?  Frozen OJ? Weak coffee? This gets 4 stars? Tampa standards must be pretty low.

Been going there for last 5 years or so, tried other places but they just don't do it for me. So I keep coming back, I usually sit with Juan because he makes my rolls just how I like them, atomic spicy, if you don't believe me, ask your rolls to be made with "sugar". Have to ask Juan sr. Anyway best sushi in town imho. Always get treated real good.
Always fresh and delicious, staff is friendly and accommodating.. outdoor seating was safe and comfortable.

US Hotel suffers from being on the wrong side of Main St (well, from my place anyways).  As such, I don't get there as often as other spots and have had limited experiences to rate.  Nothing about my few visits blew me away, and I've been waiting for something (good or bad) on a trip to US Hotel to truly "review".  Well, I just got tired of waiting and decided - its an average bar on a street full of bar.

And done...

A few months ago I would of given a 5 star review. The quality of the food is excellent. Authentic Italian meats and cheeses. Love the hoagies. In fact I would go as far as saying it one of the best hoagie I ever had. The biggest selling point to me was the size of the sandwiches. I could easily make 2 meals out of one their hoagies. One day in October I went in to get my usual. Brought it home and realized the quantity of the meats and cheese was cut back to more than 50%. At first I thought it was someone new making the sandwich or someone wasn't paying attention to it being made and it got skimped. A few weeks went by and again I order my favorite hoagie. With the memory of the last hoagie and the lack of meat and cheeses I was hoping it was going to be the normal size that I grew accustomed to. Very disappointed to find out it was actually smaller than the last one. The biggest selling point was the size of it. I understand if the cost of the meats and cheese go up. I would rather spend a extra dollar or two and still receive a sandwich packed with meat and cheese. Instead the price is the same and now it's half the size. To me you are now no better than any other pizzeria. I hope the owner or management reads my review and take what I am saying seriously. I am sure I am not the only one that has noticed this decrease. Like I said the quality is still there. The size of your sandwiches set you apart from your competition. I plan on letting some time go by before I return with the hopes my review will be read and considered.
The last two times we've gotten tamales the masa was not cooked and the tamales were gross.  I hope they fix the problem because there tamales used to be amazing.
I loved the hummus plate appetizer I ordered but the burger was too greasy and messy ( not in a good way).  The drink specials are ok but there are better options literally blocks away.

This is my go to spot being at CHOP. The food, atmosphere, and drinks are outstanding. The manager was a super nice guy, too.
The soft pretzels are my favorite, Guac was also on point. Ahi tuna burger was delicious, and the mac and cheese is a family favorite. Definitely recommend to all in the area!

Oh my goodness!  I made a reservation at this place, then when I received an email telling me there would be an extra $50 due at the hotel to pay for internet (they called it a "resort fee"), I cancelled the reservation and they refused to refund my credit card... I think they kept $60 or $70.  Afterwards, I looked up the other reviews and realized this is a regular thing this hotel does.

Oh well.  Live and learn, right?   -  Terri

3.5 stars

ORDER THE BANANA MILK SHAKE!!! (If this review would be just for the milkshake it'd get 5 stars)

This is a little shack about a block or two from the beach in Carpinteria. We stop by here every time we are visiting Santa Barbara. The ONLY thing worth ordering here is the BANANA MILK SHAKE...I mean they do have a full menu of hamburgers, and mexican food. The food is okay nothing amazing or life changing but every sip of the milkshake is an experience. Now your thinking really, that amazing for a banana milkshake? She can'st stop talking about it...well let me tell you...this Banana Milkshake is creamy with chunks of real bananas. It doesn't have that artificial banana flavoring! It also thick and oh so wonderful...its always a great delight!!! There are other flavors that you can order but I personally adore the BANANA MILKSHAKE!!! YUMMMM

For Sunday morning we were looking for the breakfast place and decided to have breakfast at First Watch. One of the best thing about first watch is that from website online you can add yourself to the queue. So this gives you an opportunity to go at the restaurant when it is your turn for the seating. So when we reached at the restaurant our table for 2 was ready. We were greeted by our server with water and menu. By browsing through the menu we decided to order coffee and hot tea for the drinks and Chickichanga along with Avocado Toast with the side of bread and jam. The coffee served was freshly brewed and tea was also good. Then came our breakfast which was delicious and tasty. We really loved Chickichanga and it was delicious as well as fulfilling. The avocado toast was also freshly made and it was well spread. Loved the delicious breakfast to start our Sunday.
So yummy! They were very busy during essence weekend and because of the wait brought us a fried shrimp starter which was delicious! Everything was so good we'll be back next time we're in Nola

On the day I visited this new eatery/food store on Bourbon Street, two poboys were featured, roast beef and turkey. I chose the turkey with swiss. It arrived very quickly on an excellent sourdough loaf, fully dressed. The meat was moist, the bread fresh,and the construction solid. The only issues were the gobs of mayonnaise which threatened to launch the sandwich's insides all over the table whenever I took a bite, and the non-New Orleanian feel; lacking sauces and the traditional bread, it seemed to be more like a hoagie from back east.

The 20oz soda cost $2.00, which is a bit high, even in the Quarter. The cheese was also extra. This struck me as a little stingy.

The Candy Bar is located in what used to be Mary's Hardware, just down the block from the Clover Grill. The owners have done a nice job of erasing any hint of the space's former use. Shelves are stocked with gourmet snacks and candies; refrigerated display cases at the front hold a variety of pastries and exotic chocolates.

Service, while not cheery, was fast and efficient.

Overall, worth a visit if you want a decent sandwich in a quiet place.

Not super awesome or terrible. A no frills coffee shop with good internet and good tables for doing work. An excellent selection of brewed teas. I can't speak to the food, but they had a nice range of breakfast and lunch options if you get hungry while working or want to stop by for a breakfast or lunch date with a friend.

Went here for lunch for the first time.  Our waitress was fantastic and guided us to the best food I've ever had in Nashville.  Wine suggestion was right on the mark too.  Great food and delightfully prepared.  Very thoughtful chef and menu.  Loved it!

My story with Homemade Goodies is one of many emotions, with both good news and bad news (only for me!)! My mom asked me to find a flourless chocolate cake for my brother's engagement party, since my family is full of gluten-free folk. I called a lot of my regular bakeries, Isgro's, etc. to see if they made them. No-one did, which I thought was strange. Anyway, I ran a search on Yelp and Roz popped up. I called her and she was so excited and happy to make me this cake - one of their specialties (I later learned) that is usually only made for Passover. So, I left work early on a Friday to pick up the cake before they closed. It smelled bangin' and I was excited to bring it home for my family. I even bought some fresh raspberries at Greensgrow to top it with while I was on my way! The sun was shining, birds were chirping, the stereo was blaring... all the makings for a great day. Until I got to the party, and realized I left the cake back in my fridge in Philly. I cried a little, and bought some Gluten Free cupcakes from Whole Foods for the party. However, my boyfriend and I have been eating the hell out of that cake all week - in tiny, decadent, rich and delicious slices. Topped with fresh berries. Topped with powdered sugar. Plain. Warm. Cold. In a house. With a mouse. This cake, is the freakin' bees knees guys. I'm giving Roz and co. 5 stars because (1) they specially made me a cake (2) they genuinely want to know your opinion about their goodies and make you feel like a valued customer (3) they are warm, friendly, and inviting (4) the shop is adorable, colorful and filled with kitschy knick knacks and furniture and (5) the treats are delicious. I will be back, and I will recommend it to others, for sure.

So many bubble tea flavor options to choose from! Delicious bubble tea with good service. Would definitely recommend to a friend. Great study spot for students or a place to hang out that has board games and video games.

Love the Copper Kettle brunch - BUT this time they did not have hollandaise sauce on the usually delicious Eggs Benedict.  They put a big glob of butter on the Benedict.  Please fix this.   There are far too many brunch places in Nashville to mess this up.

We had a lovely weekend brunch here.  The service was fantastic, the coffee was great and my Egg Frittata was delicious.  
Even though this restaurant is on a very busy street with lots of pedestrian & motorist traffic once you are seated in the patio and sipping a chilled Chardonnay and admiring the gorgeous ladies prancing about the last thing you will think about is the traffic.

You know the food was ok, but what really earned this 1 star was customer service. I specifically asked our waiter (Angela) to split the tab amongst 2 cards, well she ran the full tab + half on my card. I called to speak with the mgr who claimed to be working on it, never got back to me. Called again, same thing. Like damn get it together. I won't be returning & make sure you watch your checks!
One of the worst steak sandwiches I ever had, don't know what the hype is all about!!!!
Great atmosphere, service , and food. Locally owned with an amazing back story .  My kIds can be picky eaters and they all enjoyed what they had . The spicy turkey sausage was a big hit .

Della Piazza serves up a hell of a pie so anti-St.-Louis-style you'll get home from eating it and pack up to move to Chicago.  Their crust options (I paraphrase) are deep dish, very deep dish, ultra deep dish, and don't-drop-your-keys-in-there-because-you'll-never-see-them-again-deep dish.
Fun! Great place for a get together or early morning games and drinks. Just a bit pricey but love it here
Great for taking out or dining in.  Very friendly, quick service, and super food.  Reasonable prices, too.  I have tried several dishes here and have yet to be disappointed.

went here for dinner around 7pm on saturday night & the service was fast + food was delicious! wasn't too busy but we had a reservation; it's not too big inside so i would recommend making a reservation regardless!

If you read my other review, you know I ate at Pat's and then came straight here for another cheesesteak (yeah, I know, I know). The proportion of cheesy meat goodness to bread ratio here far surpassed Pat's. The taste?  Pretty much awesome. The downside is that ordering is cramped, and seating very limited. My family ate our cheesesteaks right on the sidewalk, picnic style, but we're not complaining. How could anyone really complain when they have an authentic Philly cheesesteak in their hands, and on their hands, and on their shirt. Actually, I think that kinda added to the experience. Don't worry about my calorie count for the day, I washed it all down with a Diet Coke!  Hmm.

Over all not too bad but needs more heat! I ordered a level 3 and had to add a lot more spice and chile seasoning. My wife ordered a level 4 and the same thing. Normally a 3 and 4 and perfect for us, keep in mind we use habaneros in our Mexican food.

So my visit to this establishment was less than stellar. First time and last time. 

First off, their genuine "gyro meat" is 80% beef (upon asking). Genuine Greek gyro meat is 100% lamb. This was a major disappointment. 

I ordered the original gyro in a combo with Greek fries which are okay as I'm eating them.

While waiting for my order I witnessed employees shun and berate one of the workers (newbie I'm assuming), as they said out loud, "he doesn't have a f***ing brain."

I understand workplace banter, but it's an open kitchen, and myself and another gentleman were uncomfortable standing there.

On to the gyro... as I bit into it I almost broke my tooth on a piece of bone that got lodged in one of my molars. Barely got it out.

Overall, I don't know how this place has a high rating. I actually started this review with 3 stars, but I think for my troubles, a 1 star review is justified.

Stopped by here for lunch one day on my way to check out Lafayette Cemetery... I was only looking for a quick lunch, so I didn't care whether or not it was a chain restaurant. I was pretty impressed that this restaurant has free, valet parking... kind of odd, but "thank you sir, here are my keys..." 

This place is definitely the southern version of "The Cheesecake Factories" I'm used to seeing on the west coast, but at least Copeland's menu isn't the size of a dictionary! Great customer service and the food was good.. had the typical lunch fare of sandwiches and salads, but didn't have room to try the cheesecake. This place served it's purpose, and I would go back again if I was in the same lunch time predicament.

We ordered espresso martinis but when they arrived they weren't what we wanted.  Luckily, bartender Matt fixed it and saved the day because they were perfecttt!  If you're looking for a late night wake up- find Matt!
Good breakfast of poached eggs, bacon,avacado with a small salad. Enjoyable service by funny, smart, pretty,modest, and humble Nicole. We had a good time.

We were somewhat familiar with this franchise due to two pleasant experiences with similar stores in the Louisville, KY area. When we learned this was being built in our back yard, we visited as soon as the store opened. They really were not up to speed yet, coming out of pandemic 2020, understaffed, and trying to train a youthful, inexperienced staff to operate the restaurant. Our third visit today provided evidence that this is a good store on its way to great--fresh food generously prepared and served quickly by friendly staff. Managers are friendly, responsive and on-the-ball. We hope cafe hours can be extended through the evening meal time soon. Both inside and outside dining areas are new, clean, and comfortable. The indoor/outdoor fireplace is really cool.

I'm absolutely uncertain as to why this business gets such bad reviews and ratings. Seriously. We just left there after having a fantastic lunch! 

The soup was excellent. The Asian Salad was chilled, delicious and crispy. The Tuna Sashimi was so fresh. Our Sushi lunches were impeccable and the service was outstanding! Not to forget how clean this establishment was! 

Bottom line - we'd eat here again in a heartbeat! Great food - great atmosphere - great service!

I loved my breakfast here.  Stopped in on Saturday morning because, well, the Bloody Mays.  Ordered biscuits and gravely with poach eggs.  Delicious and somehow prepared quickly. Also, ordered a Poor Betty--a kind of upgraded Bloody Mary.  Delicious again.  Service was friendly and fast.  I highly recommend this place for breakfast!
Loved the choice of sides.  Very attentive staff. The sweet potato fries had sweet coating that was too much for me. But my son loved them
I love coming here during the day and eating outside. It's quite enough that if you need to do some work you won't get bothered. It's even nice when you just want to relax on the patio.

I got the Atlantic salmon with lemon butter, green beans, and jasmine rice to go. 
Pretty fast service 
Salmon was awesome 
Rice was a little on the hard side 
Green beans WERE NIT FRESH and okay tasting
The bread was AWESOME 
Lemon butter was more butter than lemon but good!
Nice staff!

It really is real food - and it's really good!  I went with the Strawberry Goat Cheese Salad.  It has baby spinach, strawberries, goat cheese, figs, candied walnuts with a vinaigrette.  The fig was a great touch and the candied walnuts were outstanding.  For "fast food", it tasted like salad at a sit down restaurant.  My husband had the El Guapo burger.  It has bacon, homemade jalapeno ranch, lettuce, tomato, onion.  The jalapeño ranch was hot, hot hot.  He loved the burger and the serving size was perfect.  Finished off with a Kale Crush smoothie that my 3 1/2 year old even loved.  The staff was friendly and accommodating and even brought my meal to my table since I had an infant with me.  Can't wait to go back!

Yet another option in SoMaNoLa. Only got to try the Tommy D, and it was very good, although a little messy. I'm a fan of Chef Lopez, it didn't disappoint. The only thing I dislike is the industrial feel inside and layout of the bar. It feels like it's not quite sure if it's a downtown lunch spot or a hip bar hangout. Maybe it's both.

I'll update on my next visit when I get to try more.

Right off the bat I was impressed with packaging and the labels on the sushi (not many places do this). Everything was fresh and delicious. The Spicy Girl Roll was not as spicy I expected so I found myself adding extra wasabi to make spicier. Overall great place to order from!

Food quality is good, flavor was there but needed a slight tweeking.   It was very windy out the night we ate there but it's right on the river walk and would be most pleasant other nights. Service was a little slow but again they were busy.
All homemade food, so fresh an delicious, worth coming back to for sure.  We sat outside on their small outdoor table an very pleasant place an staff very friendly as well !!

Portion much smaller than expected based on pictures. I recommend trying the matcha layer crepe cake; it is very spongey/moist with good texture. The matcha latte coffee art was basically scribbles; it tasted good though. Any of the deserts that come with matcha ice-cream tastes like grocery store matcha ice-cream so it is nothing special.  Service was awesome, workers kept checking up on us. Cafe is cute and hip. Expect to spend about $30-35 with tip for two people getting deserts and a drink each.

Wow, this is a very good restaurant.  Starting with Al the bartender mixing up very good Cosmos, to Alberto, our waiter, David, the chef and his lovely wife, the pastry gal--it was a delicious experience that I highly recommend.  Especially good for meetings and social gatherings.  The upstairs banquet rooms are classy and cozy!
Nice variety of dogs but way too expensive! Same for the fries. New York dog fell apart do to being too wet from the onions. Liked the bacon wrapped Texas dog.

I stopped by with a coworker after a long day at work. We shared the fresh  Burrata  and pickled tomatoes, basil, aged balsamic to start. So fresh! I had the Squid-ink  Cavatelli  pasta with fresh Blue crab. It was very light and delicate.  My friend had Tagliata di Manzo grilled hanger steak, arugula, balsamic, grana. We both had wine suggested by our very knowledgeable waiter.
The entire experience was very good from start to finish.
Great food.
Great service.
Great atmosphere .
Very authentic Italian.
We will be back!

Everything is vegan and the staff are friendly. I ordered the ramen for a starter and the pan seared tofu for a main course. 

The ramen was over cooked, almost soggy, and the broth was too strong; the bok choi was the right texture. I wouldn't order it again. 

The pan seared tofu missed the mark. The dish was too bland without anything to pull it together. It seemed like the bits of cauliflower were an attempt to creatively add texture which is commendable, but unfortunately it just felt strange in the mouth. The tofu itself was under flavored, which is a big no-no for tofu in my book, and it was a mistake that a dedicated vegan restaurant shouldn't be making. The outside of the tofu was over-seasoned with salt despite the general lack of flavor. On the positive side, the tofu was well cooked, and the Oregon white wine brought out the black pepper which crusted the tofu. 

I really wanted desert but all the options sounded too rich and heavy. The fruit crumble I had seen and wanted on the online menu wasn't on the list. 

The only reason I would go back is the seitan dish my friend ordered. It was moist and soft; by far it was the best cooked seitan I have ever had. The sauce was delicious with a smoke flavor that turned the dish from good to great. I would consider going back for another try but felt like it was too expensive for a boring meal.

Hubby and I went to Cottonwood Grille tonight to celebrate our anniversary.  Overall, it was a great dining experience.  There were a few "rough around the edges" details that surprised me.  First, we made our reservations online and I specifically mentioned that it was our anniversary and that we'd like a table near the fireplace if possible.  When we arrived, there was no mention made of our request and we were seated in the middle of the room.  Our reservation was for an odd time - 4:45 p.m., so it was far from hopping at that point.  Also, it seemed really dim in the restaurant, and the gas lamp on our table wasn't lit - we had to light it ourselves (thankfully hubby had a lighter on him.  We had an extensive wait before a waiter came by to take our orders (first asking, has anyone helped you guys yet?...umm, no..)

After this point, the evening improved dramatically.  We ordered the croquettas for an appetizer.  They were okay, but I've had better at Bar Gernika.  Still, they were tasty and for $5, not a bad deal.  Both hubby and I ordered the prime rib for dinner and had salad to go with it.  The salad was good - not great, but good.  The prime rib, however, was amazing.  Perfectly cooked, generously cut.  Highly recommend it.  Hubby loved his sides of baby red potatoes and green beans.  My sides were decent - rice pilaf and veggies.

We took dessert to go, the banana bread pudding and a slice of french silk pie.  The pie was fabulous, the bread pudding, so-so.

We would happily return to Cottonwood and recommend it to others.  My entree's have always been solid performers, even if the side dishes were just, "meh"...

Nice vibe and good food! We were bummed they ran out of biscuits but "settled" for their chorizo burrito. Wow, It was great and hit the spot for my wife & I. To top it off they had 5 Daughter's cronuts so the we were in heaven.

Valanni offers a perfect vibe for a night out and a great spot for happy hour! I went here with my SO during dinner time and we ordered the appetizers sampler and the lobster mac and cheese. The lobster mac and cheese was very filling! The flavor was creamy, cheesy as what you would expect from a mac and cheese dish with some lobster meats. The appetizer sampler was also good. Each had a nice and unique flavor of its own.

All I had was a salad with grilled trout, but based off of my dish and the fact that everyone else eating in my group was smacking, licking their fingers and raving about the food...I'll give it 4 stars.

Atmosphere- I sat on the patio and never made it inside.  It was set up for a graduation lunch I was going to. Nice covered area with corn hole if you want to play a game.

Service- our servers were super friendly and helpful. It felt like a great place for locals where you get to know everyone by name.

Price/ Value- expect to pay around $15 for most dishes. Servings are just right. Not huge portions where you have to take some food home, but you'll probably be full.

Food- my food was delicious. Everyone said their food was good but people especially raved about the corned beef, the sausage plate, the nachos, mac and cheese and I personally want to try those waffle sweet potato fries.

I'm looking forward to my next visit here and will be back soon!!!

Despite the friendly nature of the staff, the food was very subpar. The bacon was undercooked and the sausages were bland. I got two eggs plates; the Benedict and scrambled. Inside of the scrambled eggs found a strand of hair and the Benedict contained a bone of some sort. These two occurrences ruined my appetite completely.

Been here about four times so far, for family birthdays. Each and every single time we've come, we have been blown away at how extremely entertaining and unbelievably friendly our servers/cooks-chefs have been. Would recommend to any and all wanting some pretty amazing entertainment and delicious food!
Delicious, fresh and creative sushi, centrally located on State Street.  Highly recommend this spot!

Dear Yelp.....let's get straight to the point:
This spot offers one of the best Happy Hour in St Pete...the prices are really decent....the atmosphere is really chill n laid back.....service is on point( my bartender was Jack cool guy) and the food is good !!
If you looking for a place were the locals like to hang out....look no further this place is it !!

Whatever you've read or seen about this place, nothing can prepare you for the explosion of gold, white, pale pink, and glitter that greets you when you first walk in the door. Every detail is clearly developed, down to the dusty gold distressing on the mirrors. If you've got a sweet tooth, you're in the right place, maybe the best place - if you're willing to drop 12+ a slice (if it's a treat yo self kind of visit it's certainly well worth it). Word to the wise, they do NOT serve sandwiches and salads after 4pm, which my friend and I discovered when trying to get dinner here well after 7. We were able to get quiche and their soup of the day (butternut squash, good portion size, and delicious! also $12+). I got the millionaire cake, which was so decadent and rich with bite size pieces of shortbread adding the perfect crunch. This is definitely a place you have to try at least once!

Real beef
Real good 
Real fast
Real good price
And real close to my job
I wish i could meet fat mo
Sugar pie !! Yes please ! Never have I heard of a sugar pie, but let me tell you , it was the most delightful thing I've ever had !!!

I can't express how happy I was when I took my girlfriend here. The ambience the restaurant, staff everything was strikingly authentic and extremely fresh. We ordered the chirashi. That was literally to die for. I can't wait to turn more people on this place

This little place is amazing! It's clean, the people are friendly and the food is outstanding! The chimichanga plate is to die for. So good! And the prices are reasonable. We will definitely come back!
I checked out vault a year or two ago, but the beer was good, and the ambiance was nice. Can't remember if I got food, but it's great to have more local breweries!

Excellent bar. Bar attendants were friendly and helpful in offering beer suggestions. Did not know prior to walking in that this is the original World of Beer. Fun vibe with good music. Felt very welcomed and had a great time trying local beer.

I have known about Mazzaro's since I was a little girl because we lived right down the street, so I've been there quite a bit over my lifetime. Everything here is incredible. I really don't think you can go wrong with anything. I have had most of their sandwiches and have finally settled on getting either the tuna or the sausage and peppers every time I go along with various other things to have around the house.

We had reservations for four at their fancy prix fixe Valentine's Day Dinner last month. The service was superb and the waiter put up with my husband's sarcastic jokes very well. He also did a great job clarifying some of the fancy vocabulary on the menu. The food was wonderful, especially the ahi tuna dish. I was shocked how delicious the uber-healthy sounding fruit and nut dessert bar was, I even traded it for my Warm chocolate chip cookie pie. Avoid the beet puree soup though, it tasted like barbecue sauce.

Chick at the counter needs training on how to make ppl feel welcome and asking what they'd like and be acknowledged upon entering when no one else is around. Straight up rude. Dude making stuff behind the counter has long hair w no hair net and full beard so you know there's hairs in food. And don't bother w the lobster roll. That thing is a soggy bland mess.
I've gone here for my birthday the past two years. The food never disappoints, and the service is beyond amazing. Try the budino.

The most COVID-friendly restaurant experience yet (and the best food). All silverware and plates wrapped up, temperature taken when you walk in, hand sanitizer with the check just to name a few. Our time at Anejo was one to remember. Not only was the food exquisite and reasonably priced but worthy of a trip back, more like many trips. The staff is cool and friendly and adds to the enjoyment of your time at the restaurant. Manager Tika was as kind a person as you can meet and is doing everything right, same with our waiter Justin. Get the carne asada, yuca fries, and Brussel sprouts! Will be returning very shortly.

I had the best meal of my life here today. Hands down. No exaggeration. I even went into the kitchen afterwards and told the chef I wanted to marry her. A friend and I stopped in and both ordered the linguine with lobster. It's was just $11.99 a plate. You pay at the register and take a table in the back. A pleasant waitress brought us water, silverware and complimentary popcorn that was dusted with Parmesan and pepper. The pasta arrived and the smell alone was the stuff of dreams. Two slices of the best garlic toast I've ever had we're in the plate. There're are no words adequate to describe to pasta. Stop reading this review and just go. GO NOW.

I seriously go here a few times a week now. Lovvvve the sausage breakfast burrito and the green salsa is perfectly spicy. Sorry I haven't ordered anything else to review because my burrito makes me so happy, why bother with anything else?

My favorite restaurant in New Orleans.  The food is out of this world and they have a very difficult menu - difficult in that it is hard to decide what to order.  They have a friendly and corteous staff who always have to help me make my selection and they have never missed.  

I've eaten here 4 times and have never been disappointed.  You leave with your taste buds tingling and the staff alwasy makes me feel special.   Its a must when in New Orleans for me.  I've even stopped by late on my way back to the hotel just for desert and coffee in the beautiful and tranquil back courtyard.
This place was super cute! I had the fresh rolls and some of the steamed greens, everything was awesome. I ordered take out and the service was very quick. I definitely will be back.

been coming here for years.  just thought I would write an update, as I think the sushi they are making here these days is excellent. I always thought it was good, but lately just always seems GREAT.  I would encourage anyone who tried a while back and didn't like to give another shot.  game has been upped here.  peace and love
Great salads, great portions and good prices. Quality and fresh ingredients at a reasonable price.
I love this restaurant. Yelp got mad at me for not writing more than my first sentence. Sorta think that the first sentence says it all. The food was incredible, cool decor, good music

Their menu talks a big game but it just wasn't a good experience. The Hoppy Trails beer was flat and tasted like something I made in my Mr. Beer kit ten years ago. The bean burger was mushy. No one else at the table was impressed with the food or beverages. The servers need better training too. The hosts were awkward and the server struggled with simple questions about the drinks. Our order had mistakes and it took too long to run our card. The atmosphere is nothing to get excited about either. I had been excited about another brewery in town, but I won't go back. There are better options.

Best food i had in Clearwater so far.  Not fancy but really good.  The poke tuna avocado appetizer was great, and so was the fish dip.  I'd come back just for those alone.  Cajun grouper sandwich was really good, and my wife's grouper Santorini was maybe the best thing we had.  Great views of the beach and the service from Jamey was top notch.  Would come back again!

All you need to know is to go here and order hot crisp fish and cumin lamb. They have SO many delicious dishes, but those are my husband and I's go-to for a two-person dinner with PLENTY of leftovers. We have introduced many of our friends and family to Cate Zone and it has become a regular for many! Go here! Eat food! You will love it.

This place is worth the wait.  We went during lunch and it takes about an hour to get through the line but the tacos are amazing. We also went for dinner and the line much shorter (about 5 minutes).

I had the fried Tilapia, the pulled pork and the chicken tacos. Each of them were amazing.

Really good Americana tacos. A little pricey, especially since the tacos are smaller than regular corn tortilla tacos. Nice beer selection (always good with tacos). One time we were there, our tacos were cold. The manager brought us more tacos on the house. He didn't have to do that, that was very nice.

I visited Jack's London Grill last night for the first time and was very impressed by the service, atmosphere and food! The fish and chips were excellent! Jack himself came out and asked how things were going - he is a very friendly guy! My group and I wanted to consolidate cars and drive downtown, and Jack was perfectly okay with us leaving one of our cars there for a while. This is a relaxing, cozy place to go for some delicious British food and sports.

Love this place.  The old train depot transformed into a brew house...yes pls!  Good beers, good bourbon, fun atmosphere, outdoor seating (even with the interesting walkers on 4th street).  

P.S.  some people take themselves way to serious as yelp reviewers...see below.  If you want good comfort food done well and a great selection of beer and spirits...check them out.

If you like crazy ice cream flavors and over the top cupcakes with extreme decorations - then this place is for you!

I tend to like simple ice cream flavors - their mint chip is one of my favorites. They used have the ice cream in a separate location from the cupcakes and cafe, but now it seems like they are combined. The space is a bit tight on a busy day, but still a little space to move around. 

The cupcakes here aren't my favorite, but it's always cool to see which new flavor combos they have come up with. Their cupcakes definitely look the prettiest with their elaborate decorations!

I wish there were more garbage cans easily accessible in the cafe area. If there is a long line for ice cream and a long line for cupcakes, then it's hard to get to the garbage.

Sat at the bar near the man shucking oysters... and I'm not sure if it was his attitude or his "forgetfulness".. but it wasn't the experience I had before. The food was okay... the alligator bites were cold and so was our entrees. I wasn't pleased with the service or the food. Mediocre... and that's what I would rate it as of now. Nothing spectacular.

This review is only for delivery orders. 

Italian Express is quickly becoming my go to as one of the only places I can order a reasonably priced and fresh and delicious salad. They also have the best delivery wings I've been able to find. Bonus: great prices!

Delivery orders usually arrive earlier than expected, which is great on a weeknight when I'm starving!
Excellent Italian specialities and service too. But the best thing is they play The Beatles music!!!...lol

OMG  THIS SOFT SHELL CRAB WRAP IS BEYOND AMAZING!! I ordered on DoorDash and had my food in under 40 min and it's absolutely amazing! Wrap shack wth you been all my life?!?  sorry no pics available I demolished this food!

Our dinner was amazing! We did the three course dinner. Shrimp and grits were
Delicious.  Traveling to the area and definitely the
Best meal we had here.  The BYOB concept was new to us but saved us a ton of money on our
Dinner bill.

Had the fish and chips but chose mac and cheese instead of fries. The fish was fried perfectly. The coleslaw was definitely homemade and good and the beer is cold.. A little pricey but that's why you get quality food. Nice ambience.

The Garlic Wilderness Pizza was a huge hit. Garlic sauce, with tomatoes, mushrooms, pepperoni, sausage, and more. Absolutely loved it and I thought it had a thicker, crunchy crust that complemented the toppings very well. Whenever I come back through the area, I'll be sure to get this again!

I came here with my bf for the day and we just hung out by the pool getting cocktails and ordered a sandwich from inside.
No complaints. They are no longer a "clothing optional facility" so maybe it would have been a little more intense if it were, but whatever. My man and I did our own thing and didn't interfere with everyone else, so no problems. Just a nice chill day at the pool.

What can you say but WOW!  Salad to start is the best you can hope for.  The homemade table side dressing was fantastic.  The menu keeps you reading for quite sometime!  During the week I was in Tampa, I was there. I visited two of the locations 3 times total!  It never got boring.

So my friends and I (being the geniuses we are) tried get food and drinks right before the we went to the Garth Brooks concert. Well would you believe that thousands of other people had the same idea...

After trying several other bars and restaurants downtown we found ourselves at JOEY and running short on time. Well as packed as they were they got us a table for 6 in less than 10 minutes. We sat down, our waitress gave us some small talk and we told her what we were a little rushed because of the concert. I think she completely understood where we came from because I have never had quicker service all while our waitress was polite and friendly. 

The restaurant was clean (considering again how busy it was), it's the kind of place were you can show up in jeans and a t-shirt or dress it up a bit, Would make a very nice date night and the food was excellent, I ordered more of an appy meal but other got fuller entrees and it looked and tasted wonderful. I like it here because you have a lot of options.

We will definitely be back

First visit to Booker's today and it'll probably be my last. While the service was excellent that's where the compliments end. 

We began our meal with a pitcher of mimosa and for the price of $32 I hoped to walk away from the table feeling as though I had more than one drink. 


My partner ordered a go to favorite  chicken and waffles and I the crab Benny. The chicken had no flavor  and was as dry as the waffle, the waffles had a far too much of their " strawberry butter" and alone had no flavor at all. The syrup had a strange layer on the top but once removed was the only tasty thing on the 

The Crab Benny lacked texture and after a bite or two felt like I was eating a dish designed for those with no working  teeth. The cakes were thin and at first I believed they were missing until I moved the egg slightly. They were the saving grace of this meal and whole experience as they were the only thing we had today that delighted our tasted buds.

I've been ordering delivery from the other Italian/pizza places on Main St for years and hadn't yet given this place a chance, but had heard from a few folks that the food was great. Not sure what took me so long, but wish I had tried it sooner, because just had it for the first time tonight and the food was fantastic - believe the hype. I almost never write Yelp reviews so the food/service has to be exceptional for me to post anything - in fact this might be my first review. The food came in half the time they said it would, they got a complicated order perfect, the portions were huge, they threw in free garlic knots and dessert donuts, it was much cheaper than either of the other two pizza delivery places in the center of town and they were more pleasant on the phone.  Not to mention the quality of the food. My wife got a chicken Cobb salad, and I got a buffalo chicken cheesesteak and waffle fries and all were done perfectly.  Also ordered a single slice of plain and the slice was so big it was basically two. Would highly recommend if you're looking for great tasting, quality Italian. Now I just need to try more of the menu.

One of the first ramen restaurants to open in Indianapolis. The food is very enjoyable and very consistent. The menu is not large but all the dishes are good. There are a variety items that can be added to your ramen. Additionally, the post stickers are enjoyable as well. There is a limited selection of beer. The space is not large so the restaurant can fill up easily. The restaurant is definitely worth a trip.

After reading all these mixed reviews for Sal's I was excited to try it out for myself and put all the madness to rest.  The restaurant is located in this little plaza that has other gems like Yummy Sushi and my fav dive Firkin, so I was excited to be 3 for 3 if Sal's was good. 

As we walked in, the lighting was nice and dim, like a romantic restaurant, which was very unexpected by looking at the outside area. It's BYOB, so we popped open a bottle and started looking over the menu, as the older Italians started looking us over too. They gave us complimentary seasoned bread to begin, just skip it, save your calories for the pasta, Pumpkin.

Pesce Rustico - Was my meal, a light garlic sauce, did not feel heavy or oily, perfect for the angle hair pasta it was lathered on. The pasta was adorned with giant fresh scallops, jumbo shrimp and more importantly crab lumbs all over. There was soooo much pasta it could have fed 3 people. I think it was a steal for $17.

Rustica di Mare - As soon as the waitress walked over with our plates, I knew I had made a big mistake...and no longer wanted to mine. This was a volcano of seafood, a giant bread bowl surrounded by lovely clams and mussels. I literally put my plate to the side and try to get my beau to swap plates, thankfully he shared. The cream sauce was what made this dish, but the seafood medley was incredible! It was $24 and a bowl of creamy seafood heaven for 2, that we are still talking about.

Throughout our meal our servers were very attentive and nice, I will definitely be returning since they had a ton of other menu items I would love to try. I am so happy to have found a local Italian gem...especially with all the history behind this family.
This place is the absolute worst. Oder was wrong. I was overcharged and they refused to refund me. Manager was rude and aggressive. I will never spend my money here ever again.

Our annual Reno Fun Train trip always includes a group dinner, followed by a visit to a comedy club, Karaoke bar or cabaret show at one of the casinos.

This year we wanted to so something different for our Saturday night dinner and decided to try Louis' Basque Corner.  

We arrived before 5:30 and were pleasantly surprised to be treated to Happy Hour cocktails - Yay!  - a very nice way to warm us up from the snow storm this past weekend!

After enjoying our drinks for a few minutes, we were whisked cheerfully into one of the dining rooms, engineered to maximize occupancy withe several long tables all meant for large groups and/or European dining arrangements.  The place is very quaint following a mid-American "saloon" decor, complete with grape lights and Basque artwork of differing sizes and styles.  All-in-all, very comfortable.

When the first item placed on your table is a carafe of wine, you've got to know you're in for a good meal.  The fair-to-good, Chianti-style red wine was followed immediately by fresh, warm bread and hot vegetable soup, with mounds of carrot, potato and cabbage.

Our entree orders were taken by a quite friendly server who was efficient, but patient with this group of Basque cuisine newbies.  Meals are served family-style with entrees being the only selection to be made.  The night we were there, Sirloin steak, Lamb chops and Sweet breads (in two styles) were the entree choices.

After the soup, a Greek, green salad with vinegar/oil dressing & sweet cherry tomatoes, red onions and Feta-style cheese was served.  Two, large delicious bowls of Chicken & Rice were then delivered along with two bowls of Basque style beans; Yum!

Entrees followed quite soon.  We enjoyed a sampling of the evening's fare.  The Sirloin was well-prepared and quite large enough for two (along with the side dishes).  The Lamb chops were double-cut and two to a serving, excellently prepared and served with a nice mint jelly.  Sweet breads were available sauteed (Choriak-style?) with garlic and green pepper - OR - in a mushroom (Champignon-style) wine sauce which was truly delicious.  Though the sauteed version offered more of a taste-texture sensation, both versions are highly recommended if you're into Sweet breads.

Two large platters of fried potatoes were served just in case there was ANY room left in our bulging stomachs.  These are the kind of french-fried potatoes you love to find: golden crisp on the outside and fluffy, creamy on the inside.  I sopped up my Sweet bread sauce with these potatoes and found the combination to be fully satisfying and delicious!

Dessert was either a serving if vanilla ice cream with chocolate syrup - OR - a delicious, aged goat cheese which we LOVED!!!

Say what you will about the decor and/or the seating arrangements.  Some may have issues with either.  Regardless, the food and gracious, friendly service we experienced make this place a MUST visit for everyone in our group!  We can't wait to go back.

Food and service are 5 star, but........
Noise level is NOT average!!
We were enjoying fine food until the place got about half full.  Then the noise level became very unpleasant.  The bare wooden ceilings need major work to make me want to come back.  I like to be able to speak to my dining companion without shouting!
The breakfast is always dynamite.  The best bacon in St. Louis. Great pancakes.  Great service. Old school diner. Prices are fair.  Portions large.

Stopped in for a quick lunch and had Mongolian Beef lunch special.  The food was very good and lived the hot and sour soup.  Enjoyed it enough to come back tomorrow and will order Pho soup.  Place is small so tables are tight and limited but worth it.
Standard McDonald's experience! Service was quick, plenty of parking, restaurant was clean, and they also got a TV to watch NBA!
Girl that made my poke bowl was rude and although I paid for extra sushi was not given a portion even 50% greater than what was ordered. Wouldn't go back

One of the best tacos of my life!  Yes, the line was kinda long and it moved slowly..maybe because there was only one person manning the register.  Trust me, it was worth it. Heck, I didn't even want to eat here because I just finished a big sushi dinner. How we, this couple next to me at the sushi place was raving about Corazon Cucina.  They made it sound so delicious!  So, of course I strolled over there to assess the situation. I saw the long lines and big portions they served. I figured, "why not?" 

MY MIND WAS TELLING ME NO, BUT MY BODY WAS TELLING ME YESSS!

Ordered their carne asada taco and was tempted to order another taco just to see what they tasted like, but I didn't since I was full.

Omg, it was so yummy. They give a plenty amount of protein, and the tortilla was perfectly crisp and yet did not break apart! So good! I regretted not getting a second taco even though I was full af!

Will return with a bigger appetite so I can binge more.

I live in the neighborhood and was very excited for this diner to open. I've been there 3 times now each time giving this restaurant a chance but I don't think I'll be back again. This place had a lot of potential but the service is slow and the food is not good. I got a buffalo chicken cheesesteak. It came out cold and missing ingredients. I've gotten the Caesar wrap I don't know how you mess that up but it just wasn't good. The pancakes are fine but they serve you syrup in packets. Get some real syrup. I've been there for breakfast and dinner and it just doesn't work whatever time of day you go.

The atmosphere had an old time feel to it with the wooden and glass interior but was very comfortable with the dimmed lights. The starting bread was tasty, but nothing special. The pasta was average as well with a bit of variation in types of spaghetti on the menu, but the portions were generous. I ordered one of their unique ice creams for dessert and it was a satisfying end to my meal but not memorable.

This place is awesome. As a local, this is my new favorite place. Been here for years and never really gave it a second look. Now it's the place I like to go for lunch. Food is great and the employees create a great atmosphere of fun.

"Where the menu at?" the man behind me asked. I shrugged and pointed at a tiny letterboard about the size of a piece of paper. Besides the muffaletta sandwich, there were only a handful of deli items, like roasted red peppers, to go.

But, my friends, that is all the menu Central Grocery needs, and the only reason to brave the crowds at the counter. The sandwich is an ethereal combination of light, chewy sesame bread, thinly-sliced salami, ham, provolone and mozzarella, and an olive salad that's been the subject of countless impromptu soliloquies.
