Roughly-chopped olives mingle with capers, carrots, celery, peppers and other vegetables, having been marinated so they're the same tender texture but provide bursts of different flavors. The dressing is pleasantly oily, not too heavy, and doesn't weigh down the pillowy bread, even though the sandwiches are prepared in advance and lie in wait on the counter.

We also enjoyed crawfish-seasoned potato chips, thick and crispy; cold Abita Amber beer completed the meal. It was ecstasy, the perfect first stop on our whirlwind 24-hour tour of the city. 

Despite having visited this charming city a number of times, we had never made it inside Central Grocery before: its conservative hours (9-5 T-S) and the long lines at lunchtime had deterred us. It was well worth the wait!  For locals or tourists with extra suitcase space, Central Grocery also offers a store full of Italian grocery items like amaretti, polenta and frozen filled pasta.

In fact, my only regret is ordering the whole sandwich; even sharing between two, there was too much to finish, and the thought of those half-eaten quarters lying pitifully in the butcher paper brings a lump to my throat today, hundreds of miles from the sacred grounds of Muffalettaland.

We walked in on a Sunday evening and waited 25mins to get seated, which is fair. It was pretty busy which is probably why I am giving this review 3 stars because they have forgotten about us for a while. We were seated to the back corner against the wine rack wall. This wasn't my first time at a seasons restaurant so I was kind of familiar with the menu. The chicken flat bread was basically the best part of our dinner. I had the grilled tuna salad which was cooked perfectly, but for a $30 meal, there was a very miniscule amount of tuna in there. The ginger dressing over the greens was very harsh, that my mouth felt numb after a while. LOL. 1/3 through the entire spring mix, i realized I didn't have enough tuna to neutralize the acid from the dressing so I gave up. My fiance had a steak which was well overcooked for a medium rare. (it was gray in the center). The two glasses of Malbec we had, we enjoyed so overall it was an okay experience. I also asked for slices of avocado to be added to my salad when i realized that the dressing was intense, but they have forgotten about us for 15-20mins until I asked for it again, then they told me they do not currently have avocados. We also were not given glasses of water and flatwares and waited for these items a few mins after they have served our meals.

We visited Smashburger and got to watch the staff screaming at each-other. The most alarming thing was as we finished our burgers the staff told everyone who came in from 7:30 on they were closed on a Saturday night when they are clearly open until 10:00 pm. We watched them turn away at least 14 people while we were there. More were coming as we were leaving. They also told 2 girls who came in to order around 7:00 that they needed to get caught up and it would be 10-15 minutes until they could take their order. There was no line. The girls were actually there to pick up a to go order but they didn't even take the time to ask them.  They complained about being overworked and not having a second cook. Great burgers but very dysfunctional.
Despite uneven service and serious noise issues inside, this is still an excellent place.  The food and carefully crafted cocktails easily outweigh our service experience.

Came here for a late lunch. We ordered the boiled crawfish. So glad we did. The boil they cooked the crawfish in was so full of flavor and seasoning. We ate the entire platter between the two of us. The service was alright, the cooler half of the restaurant was closed off, but I think it was because the staff was trying to keep the window side of the restaurant looking filled with customers. Plus, it was towards the end of lunch service and they were probably going to be vamping up for dinner service soon. Other than that, the restaurant is nothing too spectacular. The restrooms are upstairs and when I went into the stall, the shutters were wide open (I guess they were keeping it ventilated that way with the window open) and there was some missing floor tile too. All in all, I'm glad we ate the crawfish (AMAZING!!). The staff was friendly and they made sure to keep our beverages filled. Based on the other reviews, I can definitely understand how this place could be a hit or miss. I think we just happened to be in the right place at the right time.

It's a great little place to have BBQ . It took us a minute to find it - but we were traveling in the dark  it's always the little places with authentic food that puts a smile on anyone's face and belly

Stopped in for lunch during the week as this place is walking distance from the circle. They do a ton of takeout but I decided to dine in and the place was pretty busy for lunch during the week. They have a great weekly lunch special so I decided on the chicken with broccoli bento box. It came with soo much food and the food came out within 5-10 minutes of ordering. Everything was really hot too so I knew it was fresh. All of this food for only $10, you really can't go wrong! 

This is definitely going to be one of my top stops for lunches during the week. The staff was friendly and food was great.
Great old fashioned, cucumber gimlet, and Asian wings. These were my top three and decor is really nice as well.

This Pan-Asian noodle joint is located in Parx Casino East (adjacent to the area of the casino that hosts all the Asian casino games).

The menu offers a selection of  Chinese, Korean, Thai and Vietnamese noodles and rice dishes. Typical of most Pan-Asian restaurants, the items they serve are passable, but none are great. 

If you are already at the casino, it's a fine choice, but don't make a special trip to eat here.

Worst of all, no beer or liquor! No BYOB!

I went on a Sunday for the live jazz music which was excellent!  I loved it when the musician asked the crowd for a random word and someone yelled gumbo and he on the spot made up a song called gumbo!!
Too bad they don't have live music on the regular. You have to like their Facebook page so you can be alerted to when they have music.

The shrimp and grits was creamy cheesy with fresh shrimp - I had 2 bowls! The red beans and rice with andouille sausage had a spicy kick to it. And the etouffee was equally good as well.

I especially like the intimate feel of the place and the Afro-American themed artworks.  

It was full of people (including many older ladies) who looked like they just left church, so you know it must be good if people's mothers are eating there, LOL!

Great date place if you want something off the beaten path. Oh, and they have an outside garden which is nicely shaded.

Unfortunately, I do have to leave one bad comment - the wine selection has a lot of room for improvement. You know those little pre-filled bottles of wine you can buy, Copa? Lets just say I should have ordered beer; at least they carry decent name brands of beer.

All in all, I'm definitely going back and will choose this place if I want to impress a fellow foodie.

I was here for dinner with a group (someone else chose the place) and it's edible.

I wasn't sure what would be good there and the waiter recommended the Grilled Filet, so I went with it.  Steak was tough.  Not good.  Sauce was all right.  I'm a little confused why she'd recommend something so clearly not good, but maybe that's the best they can do?

I wouldn't choose to go back if I had to pay full price.  Or if I had a choice.

Sabrina's is the perfect combination of excellent fare for an affordable price on the Main Line, where most places are mediocre, at best.  Consistency is also key as we've been there many times.  BYOB, open later, and best brunch on the Main Line.  Jennifer is tops in terms of wait staff - we follow her to any location she works - thrilled she hooked up with Sabby's!
We had 4 dishes. The best was the Mee Siam; it was superb. The iced coffee was good. Plenty of free tea. Restrooms were clean. Staff friendly.

I really enjoyed this place! I got the chocolate chip pancakes and iced mocha and they were both amazing - although maybe too much chocolate for one order! It's relatively new considering other restaurants on Baltimore and packed for brunch. I want to come back and try some of the Mediterranean options.

I love this place especially their lunch buffet!

Oddly enough, I don't come to their lunch buffet for the sushi but for their noodles and fried rice. They are so good. They have got to use sushi rice for their fried rice because it's delicious. 

Sushi roll wise, don't expect anything grand. One good thing tho is they have sashimi! That's a deal for a buffet. My fiancé loves this place just for that. 

Their lunch buffet also had hibachi. So you can have your meat and fried rice cooked fresh.

It's a family owned restaurant so you always have the same servers and they're all really nice.

I also come here to get nabeyaki udon. Soooo good! Best in Nashville. 

You definitely need to check this place out. They validate your parking across the street for $1 so it's not bad!

I ordered a Tuscan Chicken sandwich with modifications from the kiosks, however, once I got the sandwich I noticed that it was made without any of the modifications. I am unable to eat roasted tomatoes and really wanted the avocado that I ordered, so I went back and made sure to get the modifications, even telling them I couldn't have the roasted tomatoes on it. They didn't remake the sandwich and gave me a bag of ingredients instead for me to make it myself. Because they didn't remake the sandwich, I'm out $8 because I cannot it due to the roasted tomatoes contaminating the rest of the sandwich.
So Yummy and Authentic!!! I got elote in a cup and mangos. so good. i'm Salvi and my boyfriend is Hondureño so it's really all about the authentic taste :) Will be coming back for my weekly cravings
Amazing food! Great staff and always fresh ingredients. Tables are distanced and staff is always wearing masking and sanitizing surfaces.

Saaaddd excuse for Italian food. It's like the Olive Garden and a sub par Steven Starr restaurant had a baby. The staff is completely clueless. At least teach your 12 year old waiters to pronounce the names of Italian dishes properly. And teach your cooks how to use garlic in the recipes. There is such a thing as too much. Do yourself a favor; just go next door to Two Stones Pub and have some really good food and awesome service. Or save a lot of money and just go to the Olive Garden.

I eat here once a week. I love their teriyaki chicken-on-a-stick. I order it every time i go. The food is great, always hot and you get a lot for your money. And I think the girl behind the counter is cute, lol. Never had a problem with hair in MY food. Best chinese food in Donelson.

We have wanted to stop in here several times and decided to do just that after picking Strawberries up the road. Everything was hot and fresh plus out waitress did a great job. They have plenty of TV's and neat things to look at on the walls. When up this way again we want to go in the outdoor area and have some drinks!

Nice hangout!

Okay the place first of all is a nice hangout for the Summer with its open and roomy floor plan and opportunity to eat outside as well.

So me and my wife when we entered were greeted right away by a friendly hostess which is a plus. The waitress was not so friendly and her personality was very flat. 

We ordered chicken wings and they were like a honey chipotle type and they were not bad, They were not the worst, but not the very best either. They could have been cooked longer to give them a little extra crispiness. Their fries were good. 

We were not overly impressed with the place as far as the food, but definitely a nice place to hang out.

Maybe Missouri doesn't have Waffle House, but this is Waffle House.  Quick and greasy, meets the needs for late nights or but you're getting what you pay for here.   I had bits of potato in my eggs, and didn't order potatoes, but this isn't the type of place you can complain about having potato in your eggs. It's more the kind of place you have to go, "hmm, thanks for extra potato, I think".

The gumbo is good, but their attitudes are nasty! This was my first and last time going to this restaurant. I'm from Louisiana and one of my coworkers told me about this spot and raved about the food. So I decided to give them a try especially because I love supporting black owned businesses and I heard they were from Louisiana. I drove an hour to get there. So I called to place a to go order for me and some other coworkers and everything was going great! I ordered the gumbo, fish dinner, and the oxtails. Another one my coworkers asked me to call in her an order as well, so I call it in and they tell me their out of gumbo. Im like I just ordered gumbo five minutes ago and no one said anything about the restaurant being out of gumbo. The young lady went to check and came back to the phone asking do we still want to place and order. I'm like I'm waiting for the update on the gumbo like where did you go when you went to check the gumbo. By this time, I've made it to the restaurant and I'm asking about the gumbo because I didn't get an answer. They proceed to tell me they have one gumbo left. I asked to see the gumbo because I didn't want all juice and no meat since it was the last of the gumbo. The lady with the short wig in the front proceeds to get an attitude because I wanted to check the quality of the food before purchase. She tells me its not the bottom of the pot and I'm like you just said its the last of the gumbo. By no means was I trying to offend her but as I told her I have every right to check my food before I purchased. She had the worst attitude about it trying to act like it was an issue with me checking my food after I asked several times. I finally was able to check it and it looked fine. I wanted to leave but I proceeded to pay for the food because I promised other ppl their food as well. My coworkers who were with me declined to order because of her attitude. I was totally disgusted beinggirl that I'll be here for months, would have been only a few minutes away, and I was hoping for this place to be a regular spot but a first impression is everything. I really felt that because she was the only black owned restaurant in the area (from what the locals have told me) she felt that she could of treated us anyways but I would never spend another dime in that place as long as I'm here.
They were okay, the service was great everyone was super nice but the food wasn't too good my honey sand which didn't taste to great and the sauces aren't the best but I love the cornholes

My friends and I were in search of a tapas bar that wouldn't cost as much as Jose Garces offerings. This seemed to fit the bill, and I like trying new places. 

We ended up getting about 8 dishes plus two desserts for three people. Seemed like plenty of food for us.

The food was excellent.  Innovative, fresh, beautifully plated.  We got raw seafood, veggies, pasta, and meat, all of which were tasty.  One dish (pork belly with lentils) was a bit over-seasoned, but still very flavorful. The desserts were kind of lame, so go somewhere else.

Got a bottle of red wine, which was good and not horribly marked up.

My only real complaints were the service. It's a new place, but some of the servers seemed really amateur. One guy who poured the wine tried really hard to be suave about it.  He didn't remove the foil correctly, so his tasting pour was messy and foil-tinged. All of his subsequent pours were splashy and we got drops of wine on a couple dishes. This wouldn't have happened at Amada!  Also, one of the waitresses had her shirt hiked up exposing her "bullseye" back tattoo. Maybe that could fly at a bar or club. But I won't complain because our other server had cute glasses, which slays me every time.

Brad's rating (out of 5):
Food: 4
Price: 4
Decor: 3
Service: 3
Wild card: Easy to get a table because it's so new.
Staff is excellent helpful and friendly. Service is always quick and their rolls are awesome! Will ever going back!

Absolutely delicious!!!  The hot peppers were the perfect amount of heat and the portion size was excellent. I got the Jewish style grinder with everything and finished the entire thing in one sitting, I couldn't stop eating.

Great local restaurant.  We thoroughly enjoyed it.  Brady the manager greeted us at the door, and we were seated immediately.  Tracey our server was at our table in a minute to set out water and get a drink order.  She explained the specials to us and went to get the drinks.  When she returned we had a couple of questions about the menu items and she was very knowledgeable about the menu and made some suggestions, such as sharing a salad (they are huge).  We had the crab coquettes which comes with two sauces. They were hot and fresh, and we couldn't decide which sauce we liked better.  The salad was big, as described, and really tasty.  We ordered the diver scallops and fried chicken.  The scallops were really good, very tasty and tender, not rubbery like they sometimes can be.  The fried chicken was really tasty, it's a different taste than traditional friend chicken, it's got a little bit of sweet more so than a savory.  Hot and crispy and a huge portion, 2 breast, a wing and a leg.  The potato salad was chunks of tender potatoes, skin on, with a tangy taste.  Baked beans have black beans also, which is a nice twist.   There are many unusual sounding items on the the menu, but they all sound SOOOO good.  We have already marked this as on of our go-to local restaurants, so we will be back. I cna't wait until they open for lunch!

On Mass. Ave in the basement under a restaurant you will find this little treasure. With exposed brick, polished concrete floor, steel beams, and eclectic decor you truly feel that you have entered somewhat if a hidden space somewhat homey space.  There are a few booths at the foot of the stair, a couple spaces with tables and chairs, and seats along a very long bar.

They focus on classic cocktails, craft distillers, and boutique wines.  My focus was on the amazing craft cocktail list, as well it should be.  The bartender was kind and fun to talk to.  Happy to chat about the various drinks.

If you are planning on making a visit be prepared to experience the space and enjoy a craft cocktail.  If you are looking for a cheap well drink this probably isn't your spot but you can enjoy a nice can of PBR for a good price!

Been here a few times, tried both dim sum and dinner.  I'm from New York so it's hard to compare this place to the high standard of dim sum places in Flushing for example.  I will say that the live steamed fish was as good as any I've had.  Other items are solid old school Cantonese but not as good as back home.  I've only been to Ocean Harbor across the street once towards the end of dim sum service which was not good at all.  I will say that this place is a solid Cantonese restaurant which though not as good as the places back home is good for the area.

We primarily get sashimi here and it has been consistently very good. It's not the quality of Harusame but it's the only downtown Media Japanese joint so not a whole lot of competition. 

My biggest complaint is the lack of a high chair. It really sends a message of "go away families with young children."

We called on Saturday morning for a 6pm reservation for 5. We could not get a reservation inside until 8:15, so we decided to take the 6pm reservation for outside dining. This was a great decision. Outside was very comfortable and cozy. We ordered a bottle of wine and used the 10% coupon found on yelp. We ordered the antipasto for 2 which was very good. We ordered the lasagna, chicken parm, and chicken piccata which were all delicious. We took home half of the lasagna. Bread does not come with your meal. A little disappointing in an Italian restaurant. We did get a loaf of homemade ciabatta bread for $5.00. Again hard to believe no bread to clean up all the different Italian sauces. Service was very good

Oh. My. God. I may have just died and gone to heaven. I got take out tonight from Mirko and it is seriously... EASILY... the best Italian food I've had in Nashville. (I'm Italian... and hard to impress - I mean... have you TASTED my Nana's coking??) 

I'll go through things one by one... 

Salad... didn't even taste it. Too excited to get to the stuff I could SMELL! 

The Bruschetta... the bruschetta itself is PERFECT - the right about of tomatoes to garlic... the bread... meh. 

The Crispy Brussel Sprouts... this is where it starts getting good! These lightly fried brussel sprouts are so delicious - I could eat them as a snack any time!! 

The Fettuccini Alfredo with Crab... LORD have mercy!!! This will set your taste buds on fire! Cooked perfectly, just the right amount of sauce... and REAL crabmeat!! Not that fake orange stuff... realllll crabmeat! This made me forget every other pasta dish I've ever eaten at a restaurant - almost as good as Nana's! 

Mangia!!

This is a must go when we visit St. Louis. We ate here 4 times for lunch in our week trip. We have not found a place like it. They have such good food! It's fresh and so good. Also the people that work there are so nice! Great place to eat!

Breakfast tacos were so delicious, must try. The potato chip/fries were also really good. Happy with the service and decor also. Went on a early Friday morning, so I avoided the large crowds and long waiting time.

The atmosphere here is very open and friendly, very much like a family style vibe. Vibrant colors and an "up to date" dinning area is very inviting for a single diner or a group. The bar area is nice and roomy with plenty of seats and a big screen tv above to watch football, baseball, etc. 

Now to the food: 
I have eaten here 3x and every time I have had a wonderful experience. Each time, the food seems to bring a different flavor that can be enjoyed with a single bite or with everything on the plate incorporated. From their starters like the fried egg rolls or the pork belly tacos, to their main dishes like their beef satay vermicelli, lemongrass chicken vermicelli, or any of their pho. 

Needless to say, I will definitely be going back and will also recommend to anyone and everyone I know.
I recall this place being cozy and cheap, with a very decent menu. I haven't been since 2011 or so, but it's about time I returned. I've never experienced or heard anything bad about this place.

Grew up going to South City Diner. Brought my youngest daughter for lunch at 1230 on a Saturday for her first visit. At least 10 open tables and told there will be a wait due to staffing. As I am waiting I notice the counter is open. Ask if we can sit at the counter and rudely told "I said you have to wait your turn!"  Never will go back.

Sit at the bar!

When you sit at the bar you get to watch their open kitchen while people toss pizzas up in the air and slide them into their giant brick oven. It is pretty cool, and ensures they can't do something untoward to the dish you ordered :-)

I really like their small plates menu - it is reasonably priced and has some yummy options - flatbreads, salads, some soups on occasion. I highly recommend their Sangria - both their red and white - both are delicious and come with a lot of tasty fruit to snack on as well.

Though they are known for their BBQ pizza, I really dig their mushroom pizza and their spaghetti bolognese is a winner too. Good place to grab a nice drink and hot bite after some shopping around the Galleria with friends. Good place!

Baby when I tell you amazing! I have always loved to come here. Went there on my lunch break and was too full to continue my work. Prices are just a little high but great food. The burgers should be a little bigger. And they should get a location on the Westbank. The atmosphere is always pretty good. I never got a drink from there but I need to try one. Will return!
Good harbor views but food was so so. Steak sandwich overcooked and the forgot the horseradish aioli so really dry. The shrimp poor boy was tasteless.
Much delicious food. The servings are generous and they are made to order. Friendly staff. So far there's nothing to not like.

OMG I WILL BE DREAMING/CRAVING THESE BAGEL SANDWICHES FOR THE REST OF MY LIFE!!!

Stopped in after a crazy night with friends while visiting Indy.  I love bagel sandwiches and they have SO MANY options!  We had such a hard time deciding what to order.  I customized my own bagel sandwich (two meats, cheese, garlic & herb cream cheese on a cheese bagel of some kind, I think) and everyone else ordered something different.  Nobody left hungry or unsatisfied!

Their bagels are great; nothing like supermarket blah bagels.  I hope I visit Indy again so I can stop by- meanwhile I'll be trying to recreate something similar at home!

I have been going to this restaurant for decades.  I do not understand the reviews of the cheesecake.  Don't people understand what homemade Italian cheesecake is.  It is not supposed to be creamy like American cheesecake.  I love the cheesecake and always get it.  It is consistently great and authentic Italian with great flavor.  Button bread is awesome.  Immaculate décor.
Pick the longest amount of time you'd ever want to wait for your drinks/food and multiply that by 4. That plus a never up-to-date beer list and indifferent servers is Fox and Hound.

Gina's has really good hearty Italian entrees & pizza at very reasonable prices.
When I am not in town visiting elderly relatives & I have food delivered from here to them.  They love the food which is always delivered very promptly and the people I have spoken to on the phone have all been very nice & accommodating.

What a wonderful place!! We were traveling from Salt Lake City to Sacramento and a place with a nice quiet atmosphere was in the wish list. I'm glad my husband found this place on Facebook (and I am surprised why it didn't pop up here on Yelp...). We had mocha, cappuccino, breakfast panini and a scone. A lovely lady also brought awesome coffee cookies for free!! Great customer service, food and coffee were amazing. Highly recommend!

This was my second time dining at Cafe Roze but my first time for dinner.  We had reservations for four people on a Tuesday night--it was quite slow but I would definitely recommend making reservations because the restaurant is small.

Our table split two appetizers--the avocado hummus and the roasted sweet potatoes.  Both were very good but the avocado hummus was my favorite.   The hummus was so creamy and the sourdough toast served on the side was so delicious that we had to order extra bread.

The drinks were good.  The Pistola, the margaratia and the Inglewood Spritz were the cocktails for the table before we switched to wine.  

We all ended up ordering the Steak Frites.  It was a pretty small portion of steak and I was told by my friend who is a regular there that that the portion sizes have gone down.  The shoestring fries were good but wish they were hotter when they arrived at the table.  The salad on the side was really good--perfectly dressed and seasoned.

We did not have room for dessert, so I can't comment on that.  Overall, this was a GREAT dinner and I can't wait to bring my husband with me!

We visited on a Saturday morning and it was very busy, had to wait about 30 minutes for a table. Our drink order was taken as we were being seated and our food order was taken when the drinks came. For as busy as the place was the service is outstanding, our food came out quickly and was delicious. The only thing that was less than desirable for me was the "bottomless mimosas crowd" the place was packed with 20 somethings who think doing brunch is cool and need to take 20 selfies while holding a drink. Of course, this is likely their target audience during this time of day, but it was annoying nonetheless. I would totally recommend and will be back if ever in the area again, maybe just not during brunch.

This is my new favorite sushi spot after just one visit.  The restaurant is tastefully decorated, the service is excellent and most important of all, the sushi is top notch.  Everything was very fresh with delicious flavors.  We also had a larger party and they handled it well.  

Will be back many times!!

PS.  Why are other reviewers saying this place is expensive?  $13 for a speciality roll with tons of ingredients is about as good as it gets.  I thought it was very reasonable for a city location.  Also, The sashimi pieces were massive and extremely fresh.

We went last night to King of Tandoor and were treated like kings.  They were so kind to us and the food was absolutely amazing.   I usually don't take the time to write reviews (I should) but they were so great I had to.  The service and the food was really wonderful.
The food and service were exceptional. Our waiter was hovering and around when needed but not intrusive. The atmosphere was lively, the music enjoyable, provides an intimate experience.

My husband saw this place while watching a show on the Discovery channel.  He said the food looked awesome and told me that we should try it while in NOLA on vacation. We did and was pleasantly surprised. You enter into the bar area and they walk you past the kitchen area to the back. The area is small but quaint. The wait staff is friendly and take time to suggest items you might like. We started with chicken livers and shrimp etouffee. Super flavorful and arrived hot. We both had the fried chicken with mashed sweet potatoes. He had corn and I had smothered cabbage.  Everything was hot and full of flavor. The chicken was moist and crispy. We finished with the bread pudding. Not to sweet but warm and satisfying. We will definitely visit again!

I really love this place. I like all the options you get. It really has something for everyone. The only thing I wish it had was one area to order food from. Like a kiosk for all the restaurants to do your order. Might help with the crowded areas in front the establishments. Otherwise, totally dig it. Can't wait to go back.
This place was great. Food was amazing and their menu has almost anything you could want. It is BYOB so keep that in mind if you want wine

Pretty good sushi. Tried new stuff there other sushi places don't have. Didn't like that there was only one guy serving everyone. The one guys asks what I want for my next order when I was chewing my food just about every time. But the food was great.

Everything about this place was mediocre. The service was eh, the place was ok, and the ramen was ok. I got the spicy crispy pork ramen and the pork came on the side and the ramen just had cabbage shreds on top. It was good the first couple of bites but then I realized it was pretty salty and not that good. Maybe I'll come back to try the other options on the menu.

Great little place, did not expect such great food from place like this. Initial thought of pulling up into a gas station parking lot, is no way there is a restaurant in here. But inside hides a great restaurant with an awesome owner and great food. The wait can be a tad bit long for food but the wait is well worth. I highly recommend the beef hearts and fried rice. So so so good. Can not say enough good things about this small family owned restaurant.
Pretty disappointing. Chicken was over cooked and dry. Rice was far too hard and dry to eat. I will not be going back.
I have always heard good things. Took a long time to get the food, Fried Chicken was horrible and the hush puppies tasted like seafood. First time and last time.

This location sucks. Every time I go they mess up my order. I ordered a cookie dough coffee that doesn't even look or taste the way it's supposed to. I asked for my sandwich without cheese and got cheese. I even asked to make sure they heard me say no cheese
I have never been disappointed with a trip to Maggianos and Nashville was no different! Excellent food and service! Well worth every dollar!

Juicy (soup) buns for the win. We were lucky enough to snag seats on a Saturday for dinner. I strongly advise against sitting on the cushion seat along the wall if you have back problems. It's also pretty snug in the restaurant, but in a cozy way. 

Had the grilled lemongrass chicken egg noodle soup. The chicken was fantastic, even cold a few days later. The noodles are Neverending loops, and the broth neither had high density flavor or the delicate aromatic taste I kind of expected. After the veggies had time to chill in the refrigerated broth, the leftovers were tastier.

 The owner is really attentive and nice. The chopsticks are annoying for some reason. You automatically get green tea, which is awesome. All in all, I dig.
A typical PF Chang's. Food was fine, service was good, nothing out of the ordinary though.

I literally work around the corner from this truck, I've been here for a few months and still not stopped by.  However, last night my girlfriend brought home some Sugar Truck macarons and they were hands down the most delicious I've ever had. After spending the last couple of years working NYC and constantly seeing bakeries charge insane amounts for these little french cookies I caved and tried some.  I understand the hype, macrons are delicious, so I eventually sampled a few from some highly rated bakeries in NYC and they were all great. After paying top dollar for cookies in New York, I never really considered that affordable macarons from a food truck in Philly could be that great. That all changed last night.

I don't know much about how a macron should be constructed, but these were neatly put together, the baked pieces were light and flakey, the fillings were delicious and creamy, and somehow each macron managed to be massive.  Aside from the size, what stood out was the flavor These macarons are so delicious, they're much more flavorful and memorable than the ones I had in New York. I don't know what Sugar Philly Truck is doing to pump these out, but they win hands down for taste.
This place is a lot of fun. Huge beers, fire pits, ping pong!!!! And board games galore!!!

I love this place.  Great thai food and a wonderful staff.  Always very welcoming.  I've never had a wait but it is good to see this place is filling up on weekends.  BYOB is added plus.  I love their thai curry - it isn't as spicy as all that!  Their tofu options are also excellent.  Prices are just right for thai food.  Far better food than the others in the neighborhood.

Stopped here for lunch while on a day trip to Nashville with some coworkers!

Blackened tilapia + cheese grits for lunch! The normal order comes with eggs and home fries and toast which would've just been way too much food for me, so the server was able to adjust a few of the menu items to get me just the tilapia and cheese grits with a side of cole slaw - yum!

I'm not an expert on grits (have only had them a handful of times), but these were creamy and delicious!

Tilapia was also super flavorful and seasoned perfectly. Cinnamon in the cole slaw was a nice surprise!

Service was also super attentive, and everyone cleaned up their plates. Coworkers had the BBQ shrimp and grits which looked GOOD.

Open 24 hours on the weekends! And yay for sweet tea (they also have beer available in the cooler).

I heard about Aki from a few people in the area because of their ALL YOU CAN EAT SUSHI FOR $25. There's a catch, if you want any signature rolls, you add $2 to the charge. However, I didn't get the all you can eat sushi so I could save room for dessert! 

I'm a sushi lover, so it'll take a really awesome spot to get all of my stars. This place was really, nice though. It had great ambiance, dim lighting, and friendly staff. 

I had the VOLCANO ROLL which was pretty good. I like a lot of flavor, so it was missing the kick I really wanted. I also had the POMEGRANATE MARTINI, which was also pretty good. It was heavy on the liquor, but lacking in the flavor department. Good depending on what you like to get out of your typical cocktail. 

For dessert I had the BANANA TEMPURA which was top notch!! This was the only reason Aki earned my 4th star... This was so tasty. I've had desserts like this before, but this just might be the best! The batter was crispy and light, and the ice cream was just perfect! Perfect for sharing, but of course it was so good I didn't even share a bite!

Best Mexican in Hendersonville. The tostados and rolled tacos are my favorite.
Also love the enchiladas.
There was a few times I've gone and they were out of tostada shells. Which is extremely bizarre since they still had corn tortillas. Don't you deep fry a tortilla to make the shell? Uh yes

I really like this place.Every thing is cooked fresh. It's fast and service with a smile. I love the  burrito bowls without the rice for a lower carb alternative. Somebody needs to add Tofu and they would increase their business.

What a discovery! Absolutely LOVE this place; from its delicious (and authentic!) Thai dishes, to its classy-yet-cozy ambiance, to its fantastic waiting staff - Ploy Thai is an absolute gem.

We were looking for a good Thai restaurant and while some were pretty yummy, nowhere really knocked our socks off...until we found this place. Hidden in a busy shopping plaza, it's almost easy to miss altogether, but the moment you walk in, you know you've entered somewhere special. The entire atmosphere is so well-done, so genuinely Thai (the owners brought back one-of-a-kind pieces from Thailand and designed the interior of the restaurant with tons of unique touches), that you can't help but be transported. Even the smallest touches make the biggest difference (the salt and pepper shakers on each table, even the restrooms are impeccably done!)

As for the food, one word: spectacular. We've traveled a lot, and authentic Thai that really shines is hard to find in Tampa. But here, the dishes were amazing; pad thai, green curry beef, spicy noodles and the tom kha gai soup, all magnificent (with the right combination of spices and herbs). This place packs just the right amount of heat into any spicy dish (their Thai Spicy Beef Salad is to die for!) and upon our fifth visit, we still have yet to find another place that can compete; talk about consistency! 

They even have sushi, and it is some of the freshest I've had anywhere in Tampa. Try the Volcano roll, the Dancing Eel roll and the Spicy Conch roll for some serious yumminess. Their wakami (seaweed) salad is also so fresh, I couldn't remember the last time I had any that good. Meal after meal, each time we've come, we have never been disappointed :)

Very casual and comfortable atmosphere. Service and food presentation was excellent however, our food was served to us cold and we were the only people in the restaurant.  Highly recommend food timing be reviewed ,heat lamps  ,and a food expediter!  That being said , this establishment is filled with potential !  I must say the biscuits and gravy were delicious and hot but that probably because we ordered them at the end of our meal and it did not sit on the counter for 10 minutes . Recommend ordering 1 plate at a time until food timing is resolved .
Finally, after 2 years in the States, I found a restaurant that serves authentic Sichuan food. Wonton in Spicy Sauce is especially good!! Alas, I thirst for spicy Sichuan cuisine is quenched!

Does anyone tip to-go food? The first time I went there I left a two-dollar tip for to-go food and they did my order right, and I was satisfied. The second time I didn't tip for to-go food, cuz sometimes I don't tip to-go food and I usually tip guys less. I had the short cool-looking black guy w/ the rad haircut. That time, they replaced the crepe for pancakes, and hashbrowns for a fruit cup. I'm not sure if you need to tip a to-go order but next time I'll tip a to-go order.

Came here for brunch this morning with the BF. We pass by this place all the time and finally decided to try it.  It's a small cafe with a few tables and a limited menu, but the food is good.  I had the apple cheddar and bacon sandwich while he had the roasted eggplant omelette.  The sandwich was a solid choice with plenty of crisp apples, warm cheddar, smoky bacon, and honey on a sliced french baguette with salad.  His omelette was also delicious: fluffy scrambled eggs wrapped around roasted eggplant and goat cheese that could be on par with any of Philadelphia's top bruncheries.

The one thing I didn't like was the service.  The food and coffee both took a long time to come out of the kitchen and during our meal, three different people waited on us.  I'll give them a pass for now, considering their strength lies more in take out and coffee, but if they want to expand or market their dine-in service, they need to do a better job making the customers feel comfortable and taken care of.

But regardless, I would totally come back for take out or coffee to go.

The space has a lot to offer...

Want to dine out? Got restaurants.
Want to drink? Got bars.
Want to shop? Got gift shop.
Want to watch the game? Got BIG screen and lots of little ones.
Want history? Got the Cardinals Hall of Fame Museum.
Want to people watch? Got all kinds.
Want to party like it's 1999? Got fun spots.
Want entertainment? Yep, got that in spades with the piano bar and PBR bull riding and main stage and live emceed events.
Want family fun? Check their schedule. They have that too with family movie nights and even outdoor yoga.

I love the multipurpose space! It's great for company events too - the staff are always helpful.

It can be noisy. And during a Cardinals home game - WHOO EEE! That's the next best spot to Busch Stadium, if you don't mind crowds.

Parking can be a bit of a hassle, but what isn't in downtown STL? I'm not a fan of their parking kiosks - half the time they act up. 

It's worth checking out if you haven't been. Bring your sports fans friends from out of town - they'll love that BIG screen and BIG sound! With any sporting event it's almost like being there! 

And just like a sporting event, prices can be a little high. So prepare yourself and your wallet, because at BPV you're sure to find something to do, people to see, and food and beverages galore!

My friend and I went to lunch after the Y.  The service and everyone that works there are very nice.  The food however was not good.  We had a philadelphia steak pizza and wings.  Not only would I never go back, I cannot figure out how they are in business.

I want to love this place but they still have so many things to work out. Seems like there are enough people working there but the staff still seems rattled - like there is a kink in the chain somewhere. The food has just been OK in my 3 experiences with Shep's. The bagels aren't great - more like a roll, not chewy and my "cheesy eggs" were just high priced scrambled eggs. 

The initial menu that I saw also included organic meat and lettuce, etc but they seemed to have fully abandoned this idea. So disappointed. 

The pigs in a blanket were really good and my husband loved the matzo ball soup. I have hope it'll get better because we really need somewhere like Shep's to succeed in East Nashville!

Amazing food - croissants are incredible - been consistent for over 10+ years despite changing hands many times.  The Bechemal (sp?) croissants heated are incredible - the almond or apple croissants are amazing.  Quiche is pretty good too!  One comment on recent visit - service was ridiculously slow at counter - the system isn't working - one young Asian girl on her phone checking texts in between helping people and she isn't very swift or efficient.  She lost track of orders multiple times in the 10 mins or so I stood waiting to be served.  If the counter service had been better it would have been a 5 star.

They have so many vegan choices it might make your head spin but they will do a great job of helping you to choose!!! The food is great. I ordered the XL vegan machaca breakfast burrito enchilada style!! It could probably feed 3 people!! My wife ordered the soy chorizo. Both where awesome!!

Nice, fancy dinner white tablecloth kind of place, without the pretentious feel. Seems like a great place for large parties, and food comes out relatively quickly. Parking at the lot right in front of the restaurant is pretty difficult, so we parked in a lot designated for Drago's a few blocks away and walked.

Chargrilled Oysters -- Acme still takes the prize in my book, but Drago's is a close second! My expectations were pretty high based on reviews and word of mouth. Buttery and flavorful, a little on the salty side and a tad too cheesy. Though, service is great and they offer to give you more bread if you need it to soak up all the oily goodness!

Fried Catfish Platter -- pretty disappointing. It came on a huge plate so it didn't look like a complete portion, and the fries were cold and mediocre. The only thing I appreciated was that it was a little less pricey than the other dishes, yet filling. Would've been better if it was thin catfish slices so it could be a little crispier too!

Lobster Empire -- this was my favorite dish! It's a Maine lobster over  angel hair pasta with sautéed oysters and mushrooms. The lobster was amazing and they were very generous with the oysters. The pasta sauce was light yet creamy, and perfectly flavored as to not overwhelm the lobster. It felt more guilt-free than most pasta dishes, which was nice because I felt pretty unhealthy starting my meal off with chargrilled oysters. If I came back to Drago's again, it would definitely be for this!

Kick A**. Gumbo was incredible!  Wings were good. Jumbalaya was a strong B and the crayfish were also a strong B. Meal was pretty cheap. Ambiance sucks.  It's a re-purposed KFC but the waitress was probably one of the nicest and happiest waitresses I've seen in years. Good job!

Have been here before and we're fans of the Yard House. Came for dinner and drinks with friends this week and had a great time. Love the general atmosphere of the dining area, although after a few of the large delicious Oktoberfest beers, the dark bathrooms make for an interesting time! Food was great, we had the spicy jambalaya, a pizza, and the korean tacos. Overall, great service, very clean, and good food!! Only complaint would be the prices...be prepared to spend quite a bit more than their competition!

I have been here about four times a week so far . Their Mexican Spiced Mocha is to die for. I haven't been to another coffee shop since I've found out they're back!!!



This location is BACK!!! Just went there 10/09/2015 It is no longer a Cafe Capri.  

What it turned into when the three owners split their Moxie Java stores. I'm nosy I asked what happened.  They divided the stores. One owner turned their stores into The Lucky Perk, the other Cafe Capri, and one kept the original Moxie Java. 

They have all new hires!  (Yay because I boycotted Cafe Capri for the horrid and entitled baristas). Me so happy because I love Moxie!!!

As a handicapped woman I am completely disturbed by the service I got from this company. After waiting almost 2 hours for my food I was told by the delivery driver who told me it wasn't her job to deliver the food to my door because she wasn't a delivery driver and it was too dark for her I was told I needed to get into my wheelchair to come outside to meet her because she wasn't allowed to come to my door. So after going outside to meet her and getting very angry at this point with this woman she dropped the bag of food and the soda and left not even offering to help bring my things inside. Then the manager called and I asked for a full refund because I had waited two hours for my food and received the worst customer service of my life he said it would not be possible because I received my food even though I did not get the food delivered to my door and was told that I had to get in my wheelchair to come outside to meet her. I would never recommend this place to anyone how they treat people is mind blowing I'm not even sure how they are in business. Just

I live so close to this place I can see it from my window.  That being said, I've dined here and gotten take out several times in the two years I've lived here. This is the only place at this end of town where you can eat a beer after 10:00pm because Indiana has the weirdest liquor laws ever. 

The food is overpriced and will be cold whether you eat in or take out. If you take out, your order WILL be wrong, just assume that from the beginning. If you dine in, bring the heaviest coat you own and consider wearing a hat because for some unknown reason this location BLASTS the AC 24/7/365. It's so cold in the bar you can almost see your breath. I'm not a freezy baby either. It's so cold you can't wait to leave. 

The service at take out is awful. Those poor folks hate their jobs more than any of us can imagine. 
Instead of leaving a tip I want to sit 
down and offer to write their resumes so they can get better jobs. 

The only reason I continue to eat here is because it's free. Yes, free. Many of our friends get us gift cards assuming we eat here a lot (not if we could help it).

If you're local you already stay away. If your staying locally in a hotel and want good food and a tv, go a mile in the opposite direction to Moontown or the Friendly tavern. Or pop into Meijer and get some boneless wings at the deli and a six pack and enjoy your hotel room. It will be better than this BW3 location!
Great food. Even better margs. Not your typical atmosphere but def a place to check out!

Smiley's gave me a fresh new perspective on Manayunk. I used to feel like I have been to every restaurant on main street too many times, my friends and I would spend too long trying to think of where to go. But today my friend and I discovered an amazing mom and pop giro place after initially walking by, but smelling something delicious soon after. Smiley is a gregarious talented chef who makes everything from scratch, with love. You can taste it! My friend is the son of a well known chef and its so hard to find a place he likes. He is a relentless food snob but couldn't help in joining me in raving about smiley's. I have lived in three countries, two of which are littered with delicious giro shops (I was a regular), smiley's was the best and right here in 'merica! More than that, it is a charming venue, full of potential. He just moved in but he has big plans to offer hookah, belly dancers, and stay open until 3 am on weekend nights. Hope to see some of you there after the bars close! Places like these bring character to neighborhoods.

We had a fabulous time at the Bridge Street house. Carol Ann was so accommodating and thorough, we felt right at home.   When we travel back to Lambertville, we will be staying here. We reserved the room downstairs with the kitchen and the king size bed and we were able to walk right outside to the most beautiful Terrace. We enjoyed cocktails and coffee on this terrace. We were able to walk throughout the town and come back when we needed a rest because it was close enough and very centrally located. It was truly a wonderful experience and we will be back!
The room was clean and neat and had everything we needed. The kitchen was a bonus, we were able to store things in the refrigerator and make coffee in the morning. We highly recommend the bridge street house.   Carol Ann showed us the other rooms at the house which were all equally beautiful and clean.

I'm a big fan of Stephen Starr restaurants generally, and there were things that I really liked about this place and then some not so much.  The all American comfort food menu and reasonable prices were big turn on's. But I sat there looking around to try to figure out what the aesthetic and vibe were supposed to be, things that normally have immediate impact at other Starr restaurants.  I'm definitely not feeling anything related to a ski lodge, as some other reviewer's have commented on. And I don't really say the Brady Bunch hip wreck room thing from the 1970s either. To me it just looks like a me-too post-modern design aesthetic. That said, a fun spot to go to in this neighborhood.

Had the shrimp and grits and it was very good! All the different dishes we had, including appetizers, were very tasty. Great customer service and good flow to their service. Like that we were seated upstairs with a good atmosphere. The beer was cold and the food was hot. My buds enjoyed the large oysters and their dishes as well.

I went for brunch on Easter and while the food was ok, I couldn't get past the buffet style. I think that they should have servers due to the popularity of their brunch hour. It had all the makings of a buffet with picked over food and long lines. Also, the omelette station was poorly placed by the bathroom. While the food was ok, I think the serving style for the brunch should change. I would go again, but not for brunch!

I may be biased because I love New Orleans, but this is one of the best restaurants downtown. The food is really good, and they have some interesting items on the menu (think alligator cheesecake).  The environment is really cool. Think if New Orleans and the City Museum had a love child who dropped out of culinary school after a year. They also have events and music nights, which really adds to the appeal. And please don't leave without trying the bread pudding. You're welcome. 

Cons: The waits can be long, I've had some iffy experiences with customer service, and I would skip the mixed drinks (they can be a little watered down IMO). I'd also avoid if you don't like/can't handle spice or seafood, but it's a Cajun restaurant, so that's probably obvious.

I got a delivery from Hershel's that included corned beef, fresh roasted turkey and beef brisket.  All of the meats were great.  I used the corned beef to make the best corned beef hash I've ever had in addition to a couple of sandwiches.  The photos here are from my making the corned beef hash.  

The delivery was brought from Reading Terminal Market by Mercato and it showed up a couple of items short.  When I noted this in an online review, Steve, the Hershel's owner called me personally very quickly and made the whole thing right.  

So great quality meats and great service.  Thanks, Steve!

One check in.  I have been here dozens of times but not since I started to Yelp.  El Nopal is the typical St. Louis Mexican. This is not to be confused with Milagro or any other upscale Mexican.  This is copious amounts of food for a great price.  I ordered the "Grande" Special.  Two plates of taco, Chile relleno, tamale, burrito, refried beans and rice.  The food is served fast, hot and good.  I really enjoy the Mexican cheese which is their version of cheddar but much more tasty.  

The crowd when we arrived the crowd was very young and vibrant.  A table of 16 something year old girls having a birthday party.  They were just darling.  Another table of young college students having a night out.  Then there was me moving the average age too far north.  Very nice time tonight I really enjoyed my meal and company.

I am here with my husband. I ordered spinach on my burger they gave me cooked. The fries were dead. After they brought out fresh fries and fresh spinach. My husband 's burger was cold. Both sweet and unsweetened tea tasted extremely weak. The server was amazing. My husband kept complaining about a dumpster smell during dinner as we were seated outside. Also I had to wait for the restroom. The burgers flavor wise were great. But the rest of this place sucked big time. There are better burger places than this place.

Latest refurb looks good. Pretty trendy. Pool is also nice and great to have in the summer in this city. Bar was funky and a welcome sight (despite surly bartender) because ... Horrific check in experience due to the lobby being full of 5 different events at 11pm on Friday night and the desk staff being overwhelmed... Then being told we had to return to our car to move it to the correct level (3 upwards) and put a bit of paper in the window. Room not made/cleaned until 5pm on Saturday night which was just the time we were using it to get ready to go out!

Mission "try hot chicken" was made more challenging considering that it was New Year's Eve. Acme across the street was charging a $50 cover even if you wanted to just eat hot chicken! Luckily we crossed the street and noticed Music City Chicken. Very affordable priced, great vibe and delicious, juicy fried hot chicken. The mild was a good kick to my tastebuds, and bordering on the verge of "too spicy". Turns out I'm a chicken when it comes to hot chicken. We ordered 2 greens for sides (collard greens and fried okra) which were nothing too special, quite bland. Go for the hot chicken!

I love Ghini's. A warm, friendly Caffe with delicious food. Dee is awesome offering wonderful customer service. Having traveled the world, I put Ghini's up there with some of the best cafes I have visited. I visit Ghini's every time I am in Tucson and when I move here it will be my go to favorite!

Dead fly. I ordered a only small strawberry banana milkshake and a regular vanilla milkshake. We  had to wait 10 minutes for just these two items. After we had driven away I saw a dead fly on the top and side of my milkshake. Disgusting. I doubt a fly would land on my shake and suddenly die, so I'm placing this blame on one of their employees and assuming someone had put an already dead fly on top of my shake. If I hadn't been with father I would have gone back and done something about this disgusting event. Would not recommend this location whatsoever if they send out bug-ridden service to people. Save your money and go elsewhere.

We ordered takeout. My husband came home with someone else's order. I called immediately. They told him to come back and to bring back the the other food. Yuck. My husband wasted over an hour going back and forth. And barely an apology for his troubles. Bad customer service. The food however is good.

Best place to watch sports, meet friends, grab some great beer! We typically meet large groups of friends here & have a blast every time. Must-order items - Buffalo wrap (MoFo sauce comes on it, which is pretty hot. If you can't stand the heat, ask for Mild, a bit tamer. Get it with WAFFLE fries, loaded if you don't care about calories-or just nacho cheese. They used to have mixed steamed veggies as a side option, but now it is just steamed broccoli (bummer). Dill pickle chips are a classic appetizer, the best I've ever had. Prices are decent & the food quality is awesome. More flavor, generous portions, better quality than any other sports pub/restaurant in the area! Every location is a winner & the food quality is consistent at whichever location you eat. Delish!
Ordered the roast beef sub. Not very good. Very weak ice tea. Just not a good experience.

Had a desire for some burgers, and a $10 gift card that was burning a hole in my wallet for a long time, so my family and I decided to use it.  We got 4 regular burgers (regular has 2 patties, Junior has 1) and the toppings are all advertised as "free."  

Each of our burgers got done exactly how we wanted, and they put a corresponding # sticker on the wrapper to match with the receipt.  The fries were plentiful and tasty.

Service was nice, and the place was clean.

About $40 for the 4 of us.
Food was delicious. Definitely recommend the salad bar. Probably the best salad bar I've seen. Service is fast. Upscale buffet. On the pricey side but well worth it.

Walked in on Saturday afternoon at 3:30 pm thinking we would try a quick pint and late lunch. I can't comment on the beer or the menu since we sat in the bar for 12 minutes without being acknowledged, much less offered a menu or a drink. We live in the area and go out at least one a week, so we were very excited for a renaissance at this location, but this is not a place we feel we need to patronize when Chestnut Hill offers more options for decent food and good service.

I expected better out of Fairchild's, after reading reviews on Yelp. The dependability of Yelp comes through 9 times out of 10. Unfortunately in this case, I don't agree with the average 4 star rating.

Fairchild's Oyster Bar is strategically put together in the casino, such that people walking by can see and smell the food. A money making ploy, most definitely. 

When you're seated, you're not protected from the noise of the casino, including the pulsing drum of a Chinese New Year marching band sent through the corridors. Yes, they're fun to watch when they're near you, but when they're out of sight and you can still hear the pulsing, it gets kind of annoying.

Let's move on to the food. The introductory free bread is delicious. I found myself wishing it were served with olive oil, or at least non-foil packaged butter (considering the pricing of things on the menu) but alas, your only choice is the butter neatly packed in rectangle candy wrappers.

I had the southern-fried catfish. Quite frankly it was pretty bland. I feel like frying a fish kind of takes away from the worry of overcooking it. However, a good fried food should have more flavor than just breading, and I think Fairchild's failed in this respect.

I was disappointed, and would not recommend Fairchild's to others.

The best tacos I've had in the area by far! Been there three times and every time the food has been delicious. Buy their Groupon if you can, four tacos, chips, and 2 drinks for two people for like $8.50, it's worth over $14. Definitely a great deal. Their regular prices are very fair without the Groupon though.
Outstanding meal and great atmosphere. A New Orleans tradition. Best breakfast in town

Being new to the area, we had to do some research when our 9 year old decided she wanted German food for her birthday.  My wife found German Bistro 2 online and after reading the reviews, we decided to make reservations and head over on a Thursday evening.  It's a small place very reminiscent of European restaurants.  We were greeted by Irina and shown to our table.  Not a huge selection of items on the menu, but plenty to choose from.  The bread and slaw brought out before dinner were both very fresh and tasty.  Our dinners were all very large portions and absolutely Wunderbar!  The schnitzel was so tender and cooked to perfection. The spaetzle was obviously homemade and was equally delicious.  Our waitress was attentive but not intrusive.  Irina and her husband both came by the table to chat and make sure everything was to our liking.  
This is an absolute gem of a find and we will definitely be coming back.

I LOVE this place the food is great,service is wonderful and to top it all off their prices are low enough so you can afford to go there.that is what I cal trifecta. Make sure to check out their happy hour menu which has in addition to the usual drink and appetizers several dinner options makes it a great option on a work night.In short give it a try you will not be disappointed

Ordered take-out and the service was excellent. Staff is professional and very helpful. I got an order of the sliced brisket and 5 St. Louis ribs. Smoke on brisket was good and meat was moist. Wish I had chosen my BBQ sauces better, as the Texas Twang wasn't what I was really looking for, but that's on me. The ribs had a beautiful smoky flavor and I didn't even need a wet sauce as they were so moist. Everything was excellent. So why only 4 stars? I wasn't a fane of their cornbread, a bit dry and lacked flavor. Still, that's a throw-in item and if I'm in the area again, I will get takeout again.

We had a birthday and they were very accommodating. My boyfriend's great grandfather's 90th birthday. Wednesday night at 6:30 p.m. wait was about 15 minutes. Server was not the best - we went long periods in between seeing him but overall was nice. Food was delicious.

Came here to get take out for some 2AM eating. First let me say...the bouncer at the door is the FUNNIEST part. Hello? Why is there a bouncer here? I guess for dine and dashers.... Second, my waiter was rude. I don't know if it was due to him being tired from having being at work all day or if this is his natural nasty attitude: either way it was very unbecoming, i didn't feel very welcome, hmp. On a better note, the food was amazing. I ordered a cheesesteak w/ American & wiz and it was prettty amazing! They give you lots of fries with it :)

Ate here tonight and feel awful for the servers. Only had two servers and help from the rest of the staff with busing tables and other things. Please pack your patience if you're going out to eat, these are the people who showed up to work and are doing the best they can.

Was visiting my in-laws in Reno we are from La and I stumbled across this coffee shop. I loved it so much that I came 5 mornings in a row. The Keto coffee was my favorite. Their Americanos are great, the espresso is top notch. That mixed with the people working their and the vibes. Cannot beat this coffee shop in Reno!!!
Nice people but the area is pretty bad. Food wasn't that good either. Had high hopes for this place too!

Loved the Grilled Oysters tonight! Delicious garlic and parmesan dipping sauce for the bread! Absolute best sunset views and fun ambience on the deck. Helpful servers! You have to try Jimmy Iguanas!!! It never disappoints!

After eating here, I left this restaurant very unenthused. Several of my friends warned me not to waste my time but being the stubborn food snob that I am, I wanted to try it for myself. We started off with the salmon dip which was very tasty. I would definitely order it again. I ordered the kale salad with pulled chicken and my husband ordered the infamous chicken and waffle which came highly recommended. Salad like previous reviews stated was drenched in dressing and very unimpressive. Fried chicken tenders were delicious, but the waffle was not up to par nor was it worth the money. Although it was stuffed with delicious bacon pieces, it lacked something (I still haven't quite figured out what) and crumbled apart like a cookie. Overall prices are way too high for the quality and portion sizes. Will not be back anytime soon.

Today was my second time visiting this restaurant.  The first time was much better then today.  Today, for lunch around 1:00 the place was full and there were no seats.  The hostess was not her station and did not greet my party.  When we walked in there were no seats.  We were asked to wait 5 minutes while a small group prepared to leave.  The small group never left and remained talking.  We went to the bar.  While at the bar I noticed a small private booth that was open. I asked the Hostess if we would be seated in the small booth.  She said she would check but that they were not seating anyone in that booth. The small party continued to sit and talk.  After over 15 minutes waiting we decided to eat at the bar.  After we ordered, the hostess sat a small group in the booth and never asked us if we wanted the booth. Then the small group that was finished eating left but by that time we had already ordered and didn't want to still the bartender that took our order. I hate to bring race in to this but we are black and everyone else was white except the hostess. She went out of her way to make sure the white guest were well taken care of.  Make this experience even worst, as we were leaving she even held the door for a white couple and as we approached she let the door go on us and never told us goodbye. I am disappointed but somethings never change. We will not be visiting this restaurant again. It's sad because the seafood salad was good.
The food is always fresh! So yummy! Jenna is always very nice and always friendly! Thanks for the delicious food and the great service!

Love love love Uptown Café! We are so glad they opened near our home as we have been going to the one in Noblesville for years. They do an awesome job! They have the best omelettes in the world!  Whenever we're traveling and have breakfast, my husband invariably says  "this doesn't hold a candle to Uptown."  And they have the nicest servers and staff!

Food is good, atmosphere good...SERVICE IS THE WORST...You feel rushed and uncomfortable as all the servers stand in front of the restaurant and stare at you making comments to each other.  And usually just playing with those damn phones?  Don't  they have anything else to do, perhaps clean.  There seems to be NO MANAGEMENT ANYWHERE.  This goes for the restaurant on Park Blvd .  Same story.  ( except there the Manager just sits behind the cash register.  People have to get up and look for their server for ANYTHING.  I WATCH THEM AND JUST SHAKE MY HEAD...
If owned this restaurant, I'd kick these servers out on their lazy asses

My husband and I decided to get a quick dinner on Christmas Eve.  It was not that crowded.  
We have been going to Peters since it opened.  We feel that it is going downhill.  My glass and plates were crusted with food.  They were not washed properly and when I brought it to the attention of the owner he told me it was just the way the plate was made!  I was actually pulling off old food with my nail.  Then the owner acted very perturbed and got me a new plate.  I've noticed a lot of the old waitresses are gone.  Service is a little slow.  Also they now charge you for a container to take your leftovers home.

Considering this is a mini mart their food is great! We had the All that Jazz and it was intense and delicious. The best shrimps I had. We also had the spinach-artichoke side and it was really good. The area this place is in is beautiful which you have to consider since you'll probably eat in the street as there's no place to seat inside. All the food they have looked great and we got to see many locals eating there which is always a good sign.
The drinks here are some of my favorites in Boise, especially the lava flows. The thai/peanut chicken tacos were amazing. The other food we tried wasn't as good as the tacos, but not terrible either.

Worst Papa Johns I've ever ordered from. They delivered my food to the wrong address and when I called back after waiting an hour they told me if I want them to deliver pizza to me, I need to give them the right address. Told them my building number which they argued and said didn't exist. Then hung up on me. Don't ever order from here.

I had their fajita bowl which was very good.   Their cocktails, however come up short.  I had their cucumber martini which was only filled half way up the martini glass which is less than a third martini (think of how the martini glass is shaped).  Same with second drink.  Too expensive at $10 for a cocktail with only 1/3 contents.  Other than that, the bowl was great.

I had never heard of this place, but I went with it based on the stellar Yelp reviews and also the 1,000 OpenTable points.  It turned out to be awesome!

Our server was really talking up the Picpoul de Pinet white wine, so I tried it, liked it & ordered it.  Afterwards I realized they had carafes of house wine for $11 or $12 & each glass of picpoul was $9, so I would totally order the carafe next time.  But no biggie, I guess it was my fault for being trigger happy with ordering.

I have never had escargot and I really wanted to try it here, but we chickened out and ordered the mussels & egg app.  It was amazingly delicious, almost like a runny egg on toast covered in alfredo sauce and perfectly cooked mussels (and I don't even really like mussels).  We were sopping up the sauce with our bread, yum!  I saw someone else who ordered the escargot and they were prepared in little egg cups (you weren't wrestling them out of a shell a la Pretty Woman) and I wished we had tried them.

For entrees my husband had the duck, which was *amazing*, and I had the steak, which was good but extremely peppercorn-y.  The waiter warned me of this in advance and I said that it was ok because I like spicy, but it was almost ridiculously too much peppercorn.  I just scraped them off.  The steak was cooked perfectly though, like dictionary-definition of how I ordered (medium well).  We had the macaroni and cheese side dish and it was amazing.

For dessert we had the apple tarte tatin and it was good, but pretty small and a very small amount of ice cream.  Husband had a cappucino and enjoyed it.  With the check they brought two dark chocolate truffles which were yum.

There was outdoor seating out front, but the hostess told us about the garden in back and it was adorable.  We really liked sitting there and weren't too close to other people that way.  Service was great, our server was a very quiet talker but attentive and helpful.  Just a great place to try!

We had breakfast here and it was good!  Eva was our server and she was all over getting us what we needed.  We had a pretty big group, but she still did a great job of getting everyone fed and making them happy.

We had a variety of breakfast foods - pancakes, eggs and the royale which is a burger with an egg on it.  All of it was hot when we got it and everyone ate all their food.

I wasn't sure what to expect here since my parents are frequent visitors and they have pretty low standards, but I was pleasantly surprised.

Hubs and I stopped in tonight for a quick dinner. I was craving some good bar food and thought Dachshund's might hit the spot. The restaurant is huge and super clean....one of the cleanest bars we have seen. Our server was great...super friendly and served us quickly. We started with chicken fingers and each had a dog. I had the shih-tzu and hubs had the Chicago dog. The chicken fingers were great...although it's not terribly hard to cook chicken fingers, these were great! The shih-tzu was ok but the flavor combo was a bit weird. The Chicago dog was tasty. I wish they still had those waffle fries people posted pictures of! But the sweet potato fries were tasty. I would definitely go back to try the different dogs or some other items on the menu.

We came here while visiting tuscon and didn't know what to expect. We got the all you can eat. The nigiri salmon was great, large portions. But I'm only giving 3 stars because they left the doors open and we had to deal with flies. As well, we ordered the calamari and the tempura. Way too oily and basically flavorless. The portions were quite large on ordered food, and that wouldn't have been a problem if there weren't an extra charge for wasted food. There was no way I would finish a plate of vegetable tempura with broccoli, red bell pepper, carrot, onion, zuchinni, and 3 shrimp had I known it came with all of those. Great if you're into tempura so oily it soaks through the doily on the plate. And so much bland flavorless calamari... The saving grace and the reason I'm giving 3 stars is that our waiter, even after warning us about the charge didn't enforce it. For that, I was very grateful to him.

Local brewery, second location. 

We went in a football Sunday. That's ok they were busy. The menu have the usual salads, sandwiches, burgers - the regular bar food. You go for their selection of beers. The food was ok my friend enjoyed his Mac attack pizza. The lettuce wraps looked good. My Cobb sandwich was a little dry- it needed the garlic aioli on it or more. Not a fan of the French fries. Next time just try the salad. 

The waitress was swamped but did find time to bring some ranch and to let her know the sandwich was eh, dry. She took care of it. She also didn't have an issue with our group of separate checks

Food and atmosphere are ok. I'm not in a rush to return

My First time here with family. 
Sis and bro in law have been here. The blackened chicken sandwich and the Philly cheese steak were very good. 
I had the bone in wings, all flats and with the WILD sauce. Great flavor, crispness and meatiness. The sauce was flavorful and very hot. I'm a hot connoisseur, these gave me a great endorphin rush as well as a the other effects of the heat. 
Definitely stop by if you can
Heaven on Earth, it's like a prayer. And you can't get in without your gold card, you've got to be a player.
Al thought the RAM used to be a great place to eat, the menu is very predictable and disappointing.  The beer is OK, and the meals are OK.  It has lost it's luster......
Worst delivery service. We're over an hour late, cash only and did not say that, pizza was cold, they forgot half our order, the guy on the phone was VERY rude!

(Note: this review is for night time/early morning, sober/daytime is one star. )
After living in Louisiana for 28 years and moving away, when I come back  to visit I have very little time to try new things or research trends in cuisine that have changed since I last lived here. Now, I'm like all of the other denizens of Bourbon Street: I'm drunk, I'm hungry, I don't want to think, I don't want to exert any effort, and I want what I ate when I was 22 years old when I was on the exact same st. Who wants to waste time researching munchies at 2 am? Nobody. Just go to Krystal. No one remembers what it tastes like anyway. And don't forget to exaggerate the amount: ie- tell people you had 8 sliders when you really had 6...etc.

Wow, we loved Coop's place. It was our last night in NOLA and we took a stealth suggestion from a woman at Urban Outfitters..."if it's got a line it's worth the wait" is what she said. Sometimes I think that's a viral "lemmings falling over the cliff" deal, but not with Coop's. We waited for maybe 30min or so in line, and then were seated. We sat next to a lovely couple from NY and checked out the menu. 

We had creole soup, some gumbo, a few appetizers, and a beer. Everything was great and I thought the service and food were excellent. Yes, the ambiance is "come as you are" and it definitely feels like a bar that serves food, but wow, what food! My wife and I are not fried food people but I was ready to convert after being at Coop's! I look forward to coming back to NOLA and to Coop's!

If you check in here - you get free desserts. I did..unfortunately they ran out ..so no free desserts for us. Appetizers were great, food was alllright. I had the BUN combination...and as I TRY not to be a wasteful person ... For the love of god, could not finish it. Such a shame.

We came here on a whim. We thought maybe it was a sit down where the server took your order. Found out you order at the counter. Nothing wrong with that. The onion rings are very plentiful for a starter. One order can easily serve 2 or 3 adults. All the entrees we ordered were large portions. Even though most of what we ordered was fried, nothing came across as greasy. Kudos for that. A special shout out to our server Summer. Extremely friendly and personable. Out of the blue she swept in and grabbed our dink glasses (non-alcoholic) and refilled them for us. Thanks again for a great meal.
Second time in and as good as I remembered. I like this place. Ryan does a great job at the bar with attentive service, communication and representing the menus. Top notch in my book.

NEVER JUDGE A BOOK BY ITS COVER! 

Where to start?!? This place is located right off of Johnson Hwy and Pine St. At first glance, it appears to be a rundown store in an old building. Once you walk though the door, it really looks old fashioned. Older appliances, but very bright and clean looking. You'll see several different coolers with prepared and fresh seafood. Full service seafood depot!
