After walking back and forth, concerned that the food won't be too good, I opted for the snow crab legs. I was going to cook them at home, but they offered to cook them in house. Okay, I will give it a shot! They offer it by the pound ($11.99/lb). 2 snow crab clusters are about 1.10lbs. The guy brought them over. OMG, it was a sweet and spicy butter sauce! I'm in heaven if they taste as good as they smelled. I get home, put on my big boy bib and start crack'n! They were the best freaking crabs this side of the Delaware! I was won over by the first trip! 

I made a second trip tonight for what.... MORE SNOW CRAB LEGS! I honestly told half the staff at my work about this place! Upon entering tonight, I was greeted by the friendly staff. I ordered my 2nd dose of the snow crab legs and ordered a seafood platter. 2A to be exact. Comes with crispy battered fries, 2 fried scallops, 2 fried shrimps, flounder and crab cake. Everything was super fresh and perfectly cooked. This place is my new friend. I will become a regular very quickly! 

Go give them a shot, you won't be disappointed!

The Lobster Chowder & Sangria were fantastic. Order the largest servings of each and enjoy. Nice place to sit and relax ... casual atmosphere with folk art on the walls. Service tends to be slow... but the food is very good. (Cool side note, for each bowl of soup sold they donate some soup to the homeless.)

My little sister offered to cut my hair. So I offered to take her and her roommate to breakfast. She is Vegan so I normally let her choose the place. That way I know she won't be disappointed when there are no options on the menu for her. 

First off it's Sunday brunch and we were seated immediately. The outside area is great. I'm sure it's mostly due to COVID but I really hope the whole eating outside sticks. I know I've said this to everyone I know.... it reminds me of Europe. Everything was outside. 
They were playing country music which I consider brave being a city spot. Most people I know living in the city describe their musical taste as "every thing but country."
So first off I love the metal cups they use. I really want to purchase one. Secondly the coffee was really good. I totally forgot to ask what it was. 
Then came our meals. My sister got the seitan chicken and waffles. Her roommate got the BACT to the future(Bacon, Avocado, ? And toast) she added an egg. I got the regular chicken and waffles. My meal was excellent. I tried my sisters Seitan and that was super good. However I am glad I got regular chicken in this instance. The chicken was fried but still remained super juicy on the inside. I wish I could cook good chicken like that. I've traveled down south and they know how to fry chicken. 
I really want to go back for dinner sometime. 

If you're around here I highly suggest you check it out. I plan on going there again for dinner like I just said. Pete, repeat, Pete. The pictures of ribs on the website look delicious.
The service is horrible, delivery time can go over two hours, but the pizza is unique and pretty good.

Pizza was generic, totally tasteless wings not even a little salt or pepper. Stuffed mushrooms sucked, cheese sticks soggy grease sticks and took 45 min to deliver 5 blocks away. I have been traveling the country for 30 years and this place is Sad..... should get a quarter of a star

I am lucky enough to have Miles Table as one of my neighboring restaurants. This place is wonderful and I am a huge fan! I have eaten here plenty of times and have never been disappointed. The interior is very clean and modern with a slight touch of color.  BYOB, half priced burger nights, fast service and great food. My favorite things to order are the miles burger and the grilled cheese on the multigrain bread with lettuce, tomato and avocado. Make sure to visit this cute, delicious and affordable little spot. You'll leave with a happy stomach and a smile on your face.

What can I say other than EXTREMELY UNPROFESSIONAL !!! This place was called on Monday to make reservations for Friday evening for a party of 20. Everyone arrives on Friday only to find that there is a closed sign on the door.  Their phone line states that they are thankful for their loyal customers but will be closed for a couple of days and may reopen under new management. I would think that they would have at least called the reserved parties to let them know that they had to temporary close ... but no ... not a call , not a word. They won't get any of my business when they reopen.

Looking for a place for late breakfast, I found Jimmy J's was nearby. Walked over to find a que waiting,but not too bad. Very short wait to get into this tiny dining room with musician motif. Quickly had an idea that I was in trouble. Everything on menu was so interesting. Not your average tourist run of the mill selection on menu, and the daily specials were even more exciting! I ended up having two entrees, with sides too! My wife had eggs Benedict and raved about them. I had eggs couchon, as well as biscuits and gravy. Awesome! We also had fried green tomatoes. Yummy,.With garlic aioli and balsamic vinegar. BEST fresh squeezed OJ. Very good French roast coffee.

Later went back for PO boys, and again wasn't disappointed. 

We WILL be going here for more before we go home!

I love the selection and that they have St. Paul  sandwiches. Don't like the cheese on them so I always get it without. I'm a classic girl like just mayo lettuce and pickles! The lo mein is good a little greasy but the meat is always full of flavor. The wontons are flavorful but a little dry. Still good though. Love the fried rice!!! Their workers are always nice and the food is always super hot when its delivered!!!! Also if you order so much they throw in cookies or egg roll! I really like this place!!!

The best & only peanut burger have ever had.
The magic is upstairs...very nice setting. A must do in the French Quarter!
Food did not live up to the hype and we waited over an hour to be seated i definitely won't be coming back.

Best Sashimi I have had in Tampa, and really glad to find this place. Fish is fresh, firm and very delicious. Served in beautiful plate settings, and with plenty of wasabi and pickled ginger. The Tri-Color Sashimi plate (Maguro, Hamachi, and Sake) was a nice portion, almost too much!  Had a serving of Toro also, since my girlfriend had never had it... and I wanted to see what the quality and portion was like. It was delicious, but I thought the portion was a bit small for the price.

Service was wonderful also.. very attentive and friendly staff!

Highly recommended!

There was an MSG tanker truck parked outside.  They were using a huge hose to pump it into the restaurant.  There was a warning sign on the side of the truck. It had an overflowing plate of Chinese food and the words "More than six plates risks OD!"   What a great way to start our visit to the best Chinese buffet in the western burbs!

This is truly a great buffet-

First it's clean.  I mean really clean.  Everything is spotless.

Next it's busy.  This means constant replenishment of the dishes so everything is always fresh.  

Third, their service is great.  Drinks are filled and dirty plates are whisked away faster than you can say Moo Goo Gai Pan.
  
Fourth the buffet is huge.  Sushi, fried food, salads, veges, there truly is something for everybody.

Finally it's cheap.   A weekend lunch is $7.99.

Definitely a "meh" rating. But people LOVE this place!

I cringe from locals who adore this joint, because the food barely exceeds the boring mark. I just don't understand it. I've eaten here maybe 6-8 times, and every visit confirmed my suspicion that this place makes a killing off of its Montecito patronage, but at the expense of maintaining any kind of culinary viability. I never hated my meal, but I never remembered it either. Do yourself a favor: drive the extra 2.8 minutes and go to Milpas.

Reminds me of growing up down by the lakefront of New Orleans, when decor was an after thought, noise was just fine, but service was friendly and familiar and great seafood.  If you've ever heard someone say, "how's ya mama and 'dem?", then you know what I mean.  

A group of 5 ate there last night after picking up a friend from the airport. It's always a busy place and so we had never gone in before. It's not big and half of the place is their seafood market, which is usually a good sign around here that the seafood in the restaurant is fresh.  

Also, parking is right off of Williams and  a cross street into the mall and there's more in back of the restaurant.

We walked in and the hostess was there immediately. We were seated right by the front door. The place was packed so we were lucky not to have to wait.

Our server came over immediately and was very nice and efficient. I had a couple of questions and she was happy to answer, and she knew the menu very well.  It's a pretty good menu with a nice standard variety and then there was the specials sheet, which also had a nice assortment. I ordered from the specials sheet.

We had for appetizers the onion rings and fried pickles. Nothing special here and the usual ranch dip or whatever. Personally I could take or leave both of them - from any place, not just here - but the others liked them.

For entrees, we had stuffed mirliton (chayote), boiled shrimp with potatoes and corn, a fried catfish basket, an eggplant pirogue (which is a boat; in this case a hollowed out eggplant stuffed with good things), and something else I don't remember one of the group ordering.

Food was really good. I had the mirliton, which was a combination of crab meat, mirliton and veggies in a bell pepper with a cream sauce with catfish. Very tasty. It came with "Harbor Potatoes" - red potatoes boiled with the seafood, diced and sauteed. Excellent. 

The slaw was unremarkable to me but not bad. The potato salad was first rate. We tend to eat a sort of smooth and creamy style potato salad down here and it's usually made with russet potatoes, unlike most of the country, which uses a waxy potato and sort of a sauce. 

The catfish was strips, not thin like Middendorf's (and if you're reading this and are from around here you know what I mean :-).  It was tasty too.  

Boiled shrimp were really good; well seasoned and not too hot. However, the corn on the cob was a bit too spicy even for this bunch of Cajuns and Texans. 

Too stuffed for dessert or we would have had the Chocolate Beyond Reason or the bread pudding. C'est la vie, it wasn't to be.

Overall, the food was very good and a good value too. The service was beyond very good. Our server was very attentive, friendly, and casual in a down home sort of way without being "chummy". Not a bunch of "honey" and "baby" and "dawlin" here. 

Good service in a place that's comfy, like being among friends or a favorite sweater. Glad we went and we'll be back.

The best Pho Ga place in the city.  It's in a dodgy part of town, but the food is worth it.  The chicken is so fresh and well done that it makes the meal.  The chicken broth in the Pho you can tell is not done with powders.  It has the flavors that my mother use to make at home done with a spice bag that she created herself.  The wait staff has a bit of the hurry you out the door attitude, but the place is so popular that there were at least 8 guest waiting to be seated in the 45 mins that my group were eating lunch.

So, dodgy part of town and cold staff ... but did I mention the best Pho Ga in town.  If you are Vietnamese and want Pho Ga like your mother made or a foodie looking for something authentic, go and order a standard or large bowl of Pho and 1/2 a chicken you'll enjoy it.
This is a hidden gem. Literally everything is delicious. A banh mi and some Bobba Tea at this place is on point

We stopped in to try this place because a good number of the reviews are favorable. Sadly, we were led astray by the Yelpers of Wiregrass. 

We ordered a NY style pizza and some wood fired buffalo wings. The wings were relatively tasty and super hot but there was a turn for the worst when the pizza arrived. As Gordon Ramsay would bloodcurdlingly bellow, it was RAW. Raw dough all throughout the pizza. The outside edges were the only parts that were not raw. In addition, the pizza was sopping wet and soggy, with the toppings glooping off into piles of sadness if you tried to take a bite or move a slice. 

This depressed me. When we informed our server of this distress, he was defensive and made an excuse for the pizza, saying it was just how they do it and it was "Italian style". Yes, their raw New York style pizza is apparently "Italian". 

The next part was our mistake. We spoke to our server about what to do about the pizza mishap and agreed to have the same pizza again, only for it to be "well done". After this decision, I perused the other Yelp reviews and found some that resembled what we were experiencing, including one that contained a story of being yelled at by the manager because they were not happy with their pizza. 

The replacement pizza that arrived at our table was mostly cooked and edible. The toppings still sloughed off when you tried to eat it, and it was still sloppy and wet but we ate it because we don't like to waste food and our previous pizza had just gone into the garbage. I also didn't want to be yelled at. In hindsight, this was also a mistake on our part.
Burgers are really good & fries are good too! The ketchup they have isn't the best I usually just bring my own but other than man it's awesome!!!
The food is awesome there but the service is not that awesome. Cash only and waitresses especially are not that friendly.

Sams Beach Bar is a wonderful hangout on the water. Delicious food, great drinks and a absolutely breathtaking view. The staff is always friendly and very accommodating. Make sure to watch the sunset from the outside deck. Thanks Sams Beach Bar for a wonderful experience!

Currently due to COVID you must order online. The employee was extremely kind and asked us what we were ordering so he could get started on it. 
1st sandwich: Turkey Club 
They don't skimp on the turkey slices, great flavor, and soft hoagie bread. 
2nd sandwich: Phoagie
I tried this one because I love the concept! It is literally a bowl of pho in a sandwich. This one is vegan and has mushrooms instead of meat. 
Overall, I would be back to try other sandwiches. I would order sauce on the side next time or light sauce.

My wife and I were in town to visit my son. Jonathan's Grille was right next to the hotel we stayed in. The four of us went to dinner there and we were all very happy with our meals. We split the pretzel appetizer, and  we had: Taco's, Wings and a Salad, Linguini Alfredo, and a Pulled Pork stuffed potato. We were all very happy with our meals, and we would go there again.
Pretty consistently good food at affordable prices. Some of their specials get a little weird but the regular menu is pretty classic comfort food.

New location on Ina Rd. is excellent, just as good as Speedway.
Great Reuben, and fish and chips

It's taken over five years for a new restaurant to occupy the big gaping hole left at the corner of Napoleon and St. Charles when Copeland's never reopened after Katrina, but it seems like the new occupant, Superior Seafood and Oyster Bar, is a keeper.  I've been there three times now, and the food has been consistently good each visit.

I'm a big fan of raw oysters, and Superior serves up some good ones - plump and ice cold.  The bar has a nice selection of draft beer and some specialty cocktails, although I'm not much on mojitos, which seem to be one of their specialties.  I had some sort of bourbon-orange juice-mint concoctions on one visit that seemed a little too sweet for my tastes.  

The charbroiled oysters are better than Drago's.  There, I said it.

The entrees range in prices from more moderately priced sandwiches (I particularly enjoyed the crab cake sandwich) to gulf fish and steaks running $25-$30.  The fish is done quite well, and they have a very nice dish of steamed mussels in a rather flavorful tomato sauce.  Someone obviously put some serious thought into this dish instead of just phoning it in on steamed mussels.  In a town full of seafood options, they do have some originality on the menu to stand out.  

I think the only knock I have on this place - and it is minor - is the number of large, loud, big screen televisions.  I'm sure this will help draw people in during football season, but the decor of the place seems to be a throwback to old New Orleans - white tile floors, tin tiles in the ceiling, dark wood fixtures, waitstaff in black and white - but the televisions are a bit overbearing.  It's not to the point that I would be deterred from going, but it seems like a bit of a contradiction to me.
There's no true king of pizza in newtown square/ broomall area. Each have their own little perks. I like this place because of their fries. Nice thick steak cut fries.

It's all you can eat sushi.   You can get better, but it's good for an evening out with friends.

Some interesting selections, although sushi snobs will be unimpressed.

Quality is good, a group from my gym frequents this one and we've never had a bad experience.  Sometimes there's a bit of a wait on the weekends to get seated.

A bit disappointing for the money.

My Wife and I went here for dinner to try something different. Their prices are comparable to a Mortons, Palm, Old Homestead, or a Ruths Chris and they are obviously aiming for the same demographics, but I think they are missing the mark a little bit.  All of the meals I have had at these other Steakhouses were much more memorable.

It was a good meal and the service was great, but for the price point that they come in at, the food should have been better. Their price point should be more in line with Outback based on the meal we had.

We started with a Ceasar salad that was pretty good but the croutons had no crunch to them, they were in the in between stage of crunch heading to soggy/stale. The dressing of the salad was tasty with a nice little mustard hint.

Sides were the Mac N Cheese which turned out to be the highlight of the meal and the Half and Half which is fries and rings. The rings were very good but the fries were so varied in size that some were crispy and others were not quite done all the way.

I had the new york strip bone in and it was good, but for $45 I was expecting great. My wife had the petite filet and was very disappointed.
She likes a medium temperature and they did check right in on us when we cut into our meats, but it so dark in there she didn't realize how well it actually was. It was pretty well done and dry.

Chocolate Lava cake for dessert was average.

Unfortunately, we will not return to a Fleming's based on our experience.

Husband took me here for my birthday, and the food was awesome. The atmosphere is fun, but a bit loud. Our appetizer came lit hot, and very fresh. My blackened tuna was so good. We didn't try dessert,  but the people  next to us were vwry happy with theirs. Would definitely go again.
I feel like I'm on a magic carpet ride every time I'm here. Maggie, Hamza, and Aimee always make my experience incredible.

My sister and I just randomly stopped in on our way back home to NJ,and we were sure glad we did. Cheese steak joints, we've tried THEM ALL, and Jimmy G's is top notch. Great customer service, and friendly to first timers. The best bang for your buck in Philadelphia.

The phrase that comes to mind when I think about this bar is to call it a classy joint.  It's a great experience that is a must when you come to New Orleans. Everything is working here from The decor, service, menu, availability of seating, and the service. Can't fault this spot for anything. 

I like that it isn't in the French quarter, otherwise the vibe would be ruined by badly behaved tourists.

This was my 1st experience in Philly's Chinatown.  Food was authentic Chinese and full with Asian guests....fresh everything in tanks as you walk-in.  I had wonton soup big noodles filled with meat very good and Lobster ginger scallion which was pieces of lobster caked with ginger and scallions  wrapped in the original shell...delicious.  It was a little hard to get some on the lobster out but pretty similar to other fried lobsters meals.  My wife had chicken and vegetables..it was ok....nothing special about it.  I would recommend if you go here eat seafood!

Asian people stay away. This is not a authentic restaurant. The pics may look good, but trust me, it's NOT WORTH IT. My experience was NOT like any of the other reviews here. 

We ordered 2 shrimp dishes, the veins were not removed, and where over cooked (rubbery). Nothing was spicy. The dumplings shell/pastry was thick and hard and NOT like real Chinese style. Our noodle dish was way too oily. 

The service was also poor. My family and I were attended to last compared to the family that walked in after us. They got their water, serviced, and food first. 

None of the servers were friendly or did they check up on us. They disappeared after the food was brought. We never finished all the food anyways, but when time to leave and get our checks, the wait staff were all gone and hiding in the kitchen. We could have walked out and no on would have stopped us. We had to sit and wait till one came over.

Now, if you're white, you might get better treatment, but from a Chinese man reviewing a Chinese restaurant, the over all experience is poor. NEVER AGAIN.

My 115th review of Harrah's Reno!

OK, so after almost a year of boycotting the place due to a sudden huge price spike, it's tentatively back in the Reno weekday rotation. Don't get me wrong, I still think the $10 resort fee is bullshit, but the prices have otherwise cooled off since down to $41-45 on uneventful weeknights after tax and fee. Our little Reno is growing up and getting all Tech Gentrified, and the hotel prices have elevated across the board a little bit such that that price is now on the competitive side again. Espc. if you get upgraded to the West Tower at a "value room" price, which seems to happen most of the time if they have a bunch available and you either have some status in the player's club or you flash a Total Rewards Visa at check-in. For the East Tower with its sound-leaky walls and $1.50 Keurig coffee its a bit more questionable value, but I'd take it over Circus Circus at least. Plus you can pop straight downstairs and across the street to Pho 777, which actually is a selling point for me.

To be fair the $10 increase wasn't a 100% complete cash grab. It does get you fitness center access and WiFi (where you had to pay for those separately before), and at some point in the past year they upgraded the TV selection to about 60 channels too. 

Slightly better value for Total Rewards Visa wielders as even at the lowest rate you get $2 back in comps per night thanks to the 5x rewards for spending on anything at Caesars properties. Plus the points for the base price count toward your tier points for the year.
This was such a delight to eat here!  Homemade pasta, wide variety of choices and great service.

My friend's and I went to have drinks and snacks tonight and one of my friend's had her bag stolen. Be very careful when you eat here. Don't leave your bad on the chair. There are customers who are stealing purses. Other than this the place has been very nice to us. We've been here many times.
Absolutely terrible food and service.  If I could give it zero stars I would.  No redeeming qualities.

So let me start by saying that Courtney was our waitress (WTF AWESOME CHICKA) she was amazing on point attentive and great customer service. Kept us smiling and enjoying a good time while making sure my group was comfortable. She needs a raise I would request her for services every time I entered this place perfect service thanks court!!! 
Oh wait food was deliciousness to the fullest  BBQ pulled pork nachos is a must!!! Shrimp Po'Boy is for the next time !!!! Huge 
And might I add the scenery simply gorgeous sunset and atmosphere 
Once again thank you Courtney for making our first time and enjoyable rememberable on its an adventure full of laughs I would do it everyday if she kept serving me (forgot to mention) Tropical Tea!!! Ummm only drink one the second was a doosey!
Didn't live up to the rating. Rolls were flavorless, miso soup was inedible and even the pocky box was expired...

This place has one of the most extensive and expensive wine lists ever. The ambiance is classy and romantic. The interior is a mix between classic and modern. The menu is not too long but includes many delicious items. My date and I enjoyed the scallop appetizer and had the infamous cheesesteak and sea bass as our main courses. We had sorbet/ice cream for desert. The scallops and sea bass were both excellent. Scallops were huge and well-cooked & the sea bass was the best I've had outside of a Japanese establishment. The cheesesteak was alright. Way too greasy, could not really taste the wagyu. I guess it's cool to try once but I would not order it again. Definitely would rather pay for a wagyu filet so I can actually enjoy it.

I haven't had a full meal here yet (yet being the key word) but me and my friends appetizer/dessert meal was fantastic.

We sat at one of the bar high-top tables, She got the pork sliders and somehow coursed me into trying one, before I knew it I had scarfed down the entire thing. Then I turned me attention to my chocolate cake dessert. It was very similar to a molten-chocolate cake. it had a gooey warm center and was a nice darker chocolate and wasn't sickeningly sweet. 

The decor is adorable and I would love to go back and sit on their roofdeck as it looks adorable. Our server was super sweet too and attentive enough, but not annoyingly so. 

love it!

I tried the gyro and Greek salad special.  This was a surprisingly good meal.  The gyro was delicious.  The Greek salad was very good, lacking only anchovies.  The price was reasonable.

Like the Terminator, I'll be back.

This is a brand new location near my home so I've been excited to try it eve since I saw them begin building. I was NOT disappointed! I ordered through Uber Eats and it was delivered to my house very quickly. Food was fresh and delicious. I got the hummus wrap and it was FULL of flavor and exceeded my expectations. The smoothie I got was a medium and it was big enough to share! I can't wait to get food from here again.

Been to Mere Bulls twice while visiting family in Brentwood. It is one of our "must dos" while in Brentwood.

I will start by admitting that I've never met a French Toast I didn't like. But the Crème Brule French toast  at Mere Bulles deserves 100 stars! It is truly magnificent. 

Other highlights are the made-to-order omelets, salad bar, crepe station, crispy bacon, chocolate fountain, rich crab bisque and many amazing desserts! 

Love this place!!

I came here for brunch the morning of Mother's Day. We were expecting a large group, but it ended up only being 7 of us who could make it.  Chef Caprice greeted us at our table and asked us how everything was. I tried both sweet and savory crepes. Both of which were delicious!

The staff is extremely nice. Came here for my Veterans Day meal . It's like an Asian Chipotle. I would take a picture of my bowl but it's almost gone. Glad I came to this place...oh and they have a variety of sauces. I got the yum yum of course. I will be going here again.

It's often loud and crowded. The service is not always the best. The food was usually good. But the beer made this place great. If you are on the west side of University City, closer to Spruce Hill, this is a great place to drop in an have a beer in the evening or catch a quick bite of something other than fast food.

The Brewte Salad (romaine lettuce, tomatoes, sunflower seeds, parmesan cheese) was wonderful - large portion of perfectly dressed greens with delicious house made pita chips. The black bean burrito was good when I got a bite with guacamole and black olives but bland for the other 90% of bites. Adding some of their salsa helped but the beans need some seasoning.

The staff is always super nice and emulate warm positive vibes however the restaurant always seems short staffed so the service can be very slow and erratic.

Amazing! So worth the trip!! Best Jamaican food I've had in a while. The dark meat chicken was far better then the white meat. Unfortunately when we went they were out of ribs, but I can see why... the chicken was so mouth watering I can only imagine how incredible the ribs are. We will definitely be back for those!!!

Really cool staff. Ziti was just ok not a whole lot of flavor you expect  from a Italian  dish. definitely  had better  pizza by far. Being from nyc I'm a little  critical  on pizza but at 3.05 for plain there is NOTHING  about the taste that  warrants that  price. Not saying I will never eat here again.... just don't see me ever saying I really want some Giorgios

I came here for their "Community Day," because I was promised a free dinner.  I was not able to enter this store because there was a line of people around the block and the door was blocked by people with video cameras apparently documenting the store's "success."  Yes, Yelp, i am documenting my experience "as a customer" of this store, who was very disappointed with the lack of service i was provided.  You can't tell people to show up during a two-hour window during which they'll be given free food, and then make them wait outside, in January, after dark.

Wow, this may be the worst restaurant I've ever been to.
The sushi was decent for the price, but the service was terrible. The waiter was so freaking dumb and put everything into the system wrong, and didn't seem to understand anything I was saying (wonder if he graduated high school).
It took like a year to get the food and it was gross.
They were also out of seaweed salad, which was kind of why I went because I was craving it.
Do not go here!

Best breakfast I have ever had in NOLA! Had the early bird..eggs, grits, sausage, buiscit and gravy. Throw on a tub of crawfish, which are hard to eat, but awesome! Great flavor!  Jodi was our server. Great personality! Taught us how to eat the crawfish. Great meal!
Ridiculous I waited 40 min to get a caldo de queso to go. They need to be more prepared at lunch hour. Barely even gonna have time to eat it before i go back to work.

Amazing. Great dinner, even better service. Food and drinks arrived promptly despite the Friday night crowd. Our waiter, Mike was super attentive, knowledgeable and friendly. The food was outstanding. Started with cheese curds and the heirloom tomato salad to split. Both delicious. For dinner we both had Marilyn's Fried Chicken. I was going to try something else and have some of my husband's, but as I saw servers walk by delivering this dish to other tables, I knew I wanted one of my own. It did not disappoint! The standout for us was the dessert. Banana Cream Pie. It is definitely not your average. It was probably the best dessert I've ever had. Even after a very filling dinner and a declaration to only have a few bites, I ended up eating more than my husband. We both agree it was one of our favorite meals and can't wait to return. Also, The GM who sat us and visited our table couldn't have been more accommodating or friendly. We will be back!

Absolutely a fun place.  You get 3 or 6 dumplings per order along with a specialized paired dip.  Food comes out fresh and quickly.  A great first experience.  Service was great, except for a bit of a mix-up at the start.  

They have a good drink selection and a decent bar.

If you plan to enjoy this place with friends and you want to share food (I always do this!), be sure to go in multiples of 3.  ;)  A 4-person party will have an odd man out for the 3 dumpling plates...  though I guess you'll just have to get the x6 plates!  

Definitely on my list to give another try.

We were in town for the Fleetwood Mac concert visiting from Miami and boy, were we pleased! I had the create your own omelet made it egg white with veggies. The coffee is amazing and the service was superb! The manager made his way to our table at least twice to make sure everything was in order. Our waiter was also very hands on. Even offered us coffee to go! Sold!! We even took a pen home as a souvenir! Would love to see one open in Miami so I can try the pancakes! I was totally eyeing them to a table that ordered them across from us.

My husband and I like to sit at the bar. The bar was pretty full. The couple a cross the bar from us had their infant in a carrier on the barstool then next to us was s family with 3 children all under the age of 8. Isn't it against the law to have children at the bar. Don't get me wrong i Love kids. And yes They each had their own barstool
Nicolette was great and the food was good
This is by far the best Indian around.  The food is fresh and flavors are delicious.  Very authentic.  The service is also excellent.  A great addition to the mainline!

Nice for lunch on a sunny day. I had the crab spaghetti which was listed under their "larger portions" option. It was the exact opposite. I finished it 3 bites and left me to wonder what a small option would look like if they offered it. Although it was tasty, it was definitely overpriced for the portion that they served at $20. I'd go back and have the burger next time. I had a bite of it and that was delicious.

Eat Here Now and thank me later. The Chicken and Dumpling soup will make you question your Grandmothers recipe. Super fresh sandwiches, any way you want them. Fresh Boars Head meats and cheeses. Very affordable pricing. Great local place with a wonderful staff and ownership that fully appreciates everyone that walks in.

3.5 stars. I have had delivery from here a couple times now--it's consistently good but not amazing. I've tried both the saag paneer and the saag with shrimp, and my boyfriend gets the chicken vindaloo which was too mild when he asked for medium spicy and too spicy when he just went with the normal level of spice. The portions are good sized, and it usually lasts me 2 meals. 

A big plus for this place is their speedy delivery. Both times I have ordered they have quoted me 45 or so minutes for delivery, and they are usually at my door before 30 minutes has passed. I definitely want to dine in sometime soon because it's BYO!

I want everyone to read this review carefully. When this restaurant opened a few years ago they served average pho. The broth was too brown and somewhat cloudy. It worked in a pinch.
Things have changed! New owners! This broth is very light in color and clear. It needs no additions. Taste this broth!!!! It is the best pho broth I have had. I have had alot of pho. I lived on the stuff in med school. This is phenominal broth. Big bowl too. Tons of perfect noodles and meat. 
Please give this place a try and experience what real pho is supposed to be!

Ubered over to this little gem after playing and drinking at the casino. This was a brand new place for me, but I'm so glad we stopped!! The food is kind of pricey, I understand it's the Quarter but it could be a tad cheaper. Portions were nice, everything was flavored and spiced amazingly! The corn appetizer, the chips, the carnitas tacos are items I'll be back for. Do yourself a flavor and splurge on this amazing place!
Good food. Good service (I'm sure it's better when it's not crazy brunch time). Good drinks.

The pizza here is insanely satisfying! Had just the plain cheese pizza twice during my visit. It's a convenient location near the Marriott, and just a 30 minute wait for fresh perfect pizza. Hole in the wall place with very little seating, but most people probably got theirs to go because we were out during Mardi Gras and we were able to find a spot (AND charge our phones!). Very good, standard pizza! My friend and I polished off a medium without a second thought, except where did all the pizza go?? Be sure to bring cash!

En route from Columbus to Chicago, I decided to meet with my friend, Paul from Guam who I haven't seen in a decade.  Luckily, he moved to the midwest for an orthodontics residency.  Anyway, as I was yelping Indianapolis, MacNiven's caught my eye because they serve haggis and veggie haggis as well, and decided that this be the place for me, Paul, and Amish to dine out on our first night.  

I was excited because Chicago does not have restaurants that serve haggis on a regular basis.  The only time I had haggis in Chicago was at the Robert Burns supper at Martyrs.  But...the haggis was not too good here.  It was a bit too mushy and wet.  While the veggie haggis tasted just like chilli.  So the only thing going for MacNiven's that night was that they served Belhaven and Tennet's.

Excited to see a more casual establishment enter the Ironworks neighborhood. A lot of places in this area include expensive Italian and steakhouses. It nice to be able to come here with some friends and have a few local beers and eat bar food. They were very busy and I think everyone who visited was excited for their opening. We got several orders of the pretzel, Kung Pao wings, and poutine. Everyone seemed to enjoy the food. The pretzels are hot and soft and I love the little bits of lemon in top, very different. The poutine is a delicious heap of indulgence. I liked the wings but I didn't think they tasted like Kung Pao in any way, maybe just because there were peanuts on top. The sauce was topical, as the wings tasted plain on the inside, decent size though.
Maybe the worst tacos I have ever had . Two bite tacos with a bottle of water.12$ wtf  asada meat was fat and chewy . Stay away

Came here as part of a big group and the food was awesome. The fried green tomatoes had one of the best sauces I've ever tasted and it was paired with some shrimp that was excellent. For the main course the filets were cooked to perfection. The spicy margarita was also excellent as a pre-dinner drink. Would definitely return.

Not authentic at all!! I've eaten at a lot of Indian restaurants and I cook Indian food so I know what Indian food tastes like. The tomato based dishes taste like they use spaghetti sauce. Malai kofta was bright yellow when it should be dark yellowish brown. The naan was a regular pita bread. This place is new and they are already skimping on the rich, authentic ingredients that Indian food needs! Very disappointing. The host and staff were very nice but you can tell they don't know what they are doing. They advertise they deliver but your order has to be a $50 minimum! That's outrageous!! I really hope they spend more money on ingredients. I won't be ordering from there again.

Amazing food! I always order the same entrées brisket, waffle batter chicken tenders, bisque, lobster mac&cheese, and French fries you can go wrong. I always order dessert too I love the Chocolate cake, the pecan pie, and cheesecake are also very good.
Line was 30 minutes long and they still didn't mess up any of my orders and I got quite a few.

Food was good but the service was horrible and my burger was cooked way under medium and I was given the excuse that temperatures here at goats beard are different from the normal medium temperature that society goes by.

This place came highly reviewed by a few of my acquaintances. The sandwiches looked good the entire place smells good however the quality and taste of the sandwiches we're not up to par. I got the notorious pig. The pork was very dry and mostly flavorless. The onion and the cheese were the most flavorful parts and if it was just a plain grilled cheese I would have loved it. I am willing to give them another try in the future but maybe just something simpler.

As a note. If you check in you can get a free dip sized tomato soup. Trust me, it's enough for a sandwich.

This place is my second favorite pizza place in Philly (after Lorenzo's 3rd and South) and it benefits the homeless so that's an added bonus.  Food is good and cheap and the people are nice.  Their salads are pretty good too.

One of the worst dining experiences ever. We made reservations for a party of 13. We were initially greeted promptly and were told we would have 2 servers (one for each side of the table). One server took appetizer and food orders promptly while the 2nd server only took appetizer orders. We had to beg another server to get our severs attention. Once we got him to our table, we explained that the other side of our party had already ordered their entrees...his response..."oh dang". Needless to say half of our party was eating while the other half was made to wait over 30 minutes. There was no communication between the two servers and never an apology...only from the manager when we requested to speak with her. We did get 2 desserts and a couple of appetizers comped. We won't be back!

The food was OK, but with really really poor service especially to Asian people. Both of the ladies were putting on a face like you owed them millions of dollars. The cashier lady was extremely rude and disrespectful, no verbal communication at all and asking me for tips like giving an order (pointing to the table with her finger, emotionless look). I was really hesitant but at last gave them a dollar, which I regretted so much. I came to this place because of the grocery I wanted to go and the other Vietnamese restaurant  was too crowed. Apparently, I made a mistake and it ruins my day. I don't know if it ever happened to anyone else, but at least for me, NEGATIVE PLUS EXPERIENCE and WOULD NEVER RETURN AGAIN!

I just wanted to thank you for making two elderly women very happy today. My husband and I are Aruba Marriott Timeshare owners and long time platinum members. We have been to your hotel multiple times. However, my 83 year old mother never was. When she mentioned her and her 84 year old girl friend were going to drive to Nashville from
Cincinnati for a visit, I strongly recommended they stay here. They love to drink wine and see things and this would enable them to park the car, have everything they needed, and "walk" home after a few drinks. It wasn't in their budget as they both live on limited fixed incomes, but after much convincing, they agreed since it would probably be their first and last visit since they are getting older. When they arrived today, your gracious front desk staff upgraded them to a
balcony room since the holiday travelers have all gone home. I can't thank you enough for making a great trip better for them. As soon as they got to their room, I received a text with the news. We are forever Marriott fans!!

So I finally tried this place out for dinner and I have to say that this is probably my favorite continental (bistro?) place in St. Louis.  For lack of a better way to describe continental cuisine, a companion called it "white people food."

Their menu is seasonal and you know that whatever they'll serve you will be fresh.  They even take the time to mention where some ingredients come from (Hudson Valley Foie Gras represent!).  For the most part, I felt that the food that I had emphasized the flavor of the main ingredient with minimal seasoning beyond salt.  The scallops tasted like scallops, the foie tasted like foie (think seared fatty part of a ribeye), and the lamb was pretty lamby.  In other words, the food was your typical excellent "white people food."

I do have the say, though, that the service isn't that great.  They try to do the whole informal thing (at first I thought it was just like that for lunch) and many times we had empty glasses of water.  

For the price, I wouldn't come here without a gift certificate, because I feel that the service should be much more attentive than it has.  Nevertheless, their amazingly simple but great-tasting food keeps bringing me back with said certificate in hand.

If I could give it zero stars I would. I went here because it had no line in the drive through and I was in a hurry. I've sat through a McDonald's line with 20 cars that was quicker. I ordered the 4 for 4 with the jr cheeseburger deluxe in it and all that came on it was meat cheese and onions. They forgot lettuce tomato and the condiments. Was in ha e drive thru for 30 min. DO NOT go to this location

I was in St. Louis Hills and it was around lunch time and I was like why not try the new Raising Cane's? Chicken fingers are always a good idea, right? I have been to 2 other locations numerous times.  The employees are always super friendly and their product is pretty consistent. On this day I felt the French friends were undercooked and the chicken tenders were a bit greasy.  I have a closeted love for Chick fil A and I will change direction and branch out once in a while but for the very few times I allow myself a fast food meal I think this would not be a regular choice for me. I know you can do better here.
Excellent! Don't let that it's in a KOA deter you. It's very good and the people are friendly.

The best subs for the money period. The bread and meats are great and the chips are good too. And the biggest thing I like is they will deliver even if it's one sandwich for only a dollar. Now who can argue with that.

Was recommended by our hotels front desk and wasn't disappointed. Food was hot, delicious and decent portions. We were uneasy because there was no rating on the door, but we were assured it was great, so we tried it. Family owned, decent atmosphere and decent prices. Service is quite brusque but very efficient. We will be back if in this area again
Great service, yummy food, nice atmosphere; We return here when visiting and always enjoy!

Evangenline's is a wonderful gem in the CWE neighborhood. I visited this place right after a school function, and the live music/drinks was definitely the right way to end a long night out. The server was kind enough to bring us happy hour menus even though it was a bit past. The performers were doing a soul/blues medley, which suited the ambiance perfectly

All in all, it's a very intimate eatery with live music and good eats, which is an absolutely perfect spot to bring a date :)
Truly enjoy this sushi bar.  The quality of the sushi is incredible.  I eat here often and recommend it highly.  It is one of my two go to Sushi Bars.

It is seldom that I am underwhelmed by a tiki bar. But I have to say, overall, I was not that impressed with this one. My bf and I stopped in one night and ordered a drink to share, as we were already getting a little soused. The bartender looked disinterested and bored, and did not crack a smile or engage us in any way. He had the personality of a piece of cardboard, which is not typical of a tiki bar at all. I have yet to go to one and find such a surly welcoming committee. 

The bar itself is actually very lovely, and HUGE. I think it has a bit too much space, given how empty it was when we walked in. But who knows? Maybe it gets busier over the weekend. I am not really sure. It is, however, well-decorated, and about as tiki-fied as you can get. Bonus points for the decor and seating. They also have an interesting spin-the-wheel game, for those who can't decide what to drink. 

The next night, I visited once again, and the bartender that night was much more engaging and friendly, cracking jokes and bantering with the patrons sitting at the bar. The only downside? They were out of the liquor gummies I wanted to try, and they were also out of their house-aged rum they use to make their strong Mai Tais. Oh, well. The drinks he made for us were good, though. Made up for the experience the night before, anyway!

My friends & like to try new all u can eat sushi places around the area. I really enjoyed their sushi for lunch today. I loved that they had a lunch special for students (with ID) of $14.50. I had the Godzilla roll, the New York, and Sakura. All very good rolls. I also had a "red wine cooler" which consisted of cab house wine with a little 7UP. Was a good mix actually! Would recommend this place to my fellow sushi lovers!

Bru Burger will always be a favorite! I got suckered into going here after attending a spin class at CycleBar (plug!) and per usual it was delicious. I do have to say the service was a bit slow - which was somewhat surprising because I could see the kitchen from where we sat.

I had the tuna burger this time around and it was delicious. I ordered well done to try and ensure the burger wouldn't be as messy - this did not help whatsoever. I ended up using a knife and fork to eat the burger and I mean, I am not a knife and fork for a burger type of gal. 

I prefer the mass ave location - but this one is a hidden gem in the Carmel area.

I live in the general area but I have not been to this Einstein Bros bagel restaurant in a few months, but what a difference. When I walked in I noticed it did not seem the same, as always they were waiting for the cinnamon raisin bagels to finish cooking (this is a general theme here), but other than that the store was dirty, dusty, crumbs on the floor, under the soda machine, tables were dirty and had crumbs on them.  it did not look nor smell clean.  I ordered Ice tea but when I went to serve myself it was cloudy and dark, the young man that I told asked me if it was coffee that I had taken instead of tea, that's  how bad it looked.  Also the ice machine was not working as another reviewer noted in August of 2014, guess that was not fixed yet.  It was dim and the employees were not engaging and look so bored and tired.  It was a very bad experience.  I hope that someone important reads this and contacts the "owner" whom needs to make some changes, please start with wiping and cleaning.  The place was disgusting!!
Had Baked chicken wings with dry rub. It was okay, slightly undercooked, not spicy enough. Should probably pick a pizza at a pizza place.

It almost feels like a rite of passage to leave a review for Bern's. Bern's has been on my bucket list for years and after living in Tampa for over 20 years, I can finally cross it off! 

This restaurant is truly an experience from start to finish. You have to make a reservation about 3 months in advance, but is worth the wait! Our waiter was phenomenal and gave great recommendations. The food from appetizers to dessert was some of the best food I've ever had in my life! Speaking of dessert, make sure you save room for dessert, because the Dessert Room is my favorite part of Bern's! 

I was sad that they are still not doing the wine cellar tours, but hopefully they will be running again soon. Sounds like a good excuse to make another Bern's reservation...

Left the sonic on Broadway because I was there for 35 minutes without any contact from he staff. 

The sonic at grant and I-10 was much more responsive, but indicated a 7 minute wait time for my chicken wings to be ready. Seven minutes is not fast food criteria.  Marginally better, but still needs work. WORK ON IT SONIC.

For being a cheap Chinese buffet I was overall pleased with the selection and freshness of the food.  For my family of 6 it was a cheap trip. Most of the kids liked it.  They had a few American options line chicken nuggets, fries,  and mac n cheese,  etc.  There were several chicken options like honey chicken,  general tso, chicken and broccoli among a few others.  There was only one beef option. There were a couple rices but I didn't see any noodle options. It's not high quality food but i wasn't expecting high end food for $9 adult price. I also wasn't disappointed. It looks sketchy from the outside but worth a try.

Another Sunday Morning with Fiddle Cakes, as always we were greeted with a wonderful Good Morning and a great cup of coffee.  

Sweet Treats and Quiche, even Gluten Free !

We Love this place and want to tell everyone about it.

Newest Fan of National Mechanics..this place has a cool vibe; great service and even better food!  I started out with the frisky sour drink special as we waited for our food!  This was a good call on my part..drink was well balanced with flavor and nice amount of alcohol!

The wings are so delicious and my friend love her burger! We were so full because we wanted to order the 'Pretzel', but that is for the next visit!

The server was attentive and made good recommendations!

This place!! We were there midday (2ish) on a Friday. Service was pleasurable and attentive! My drink stayed full, even without a prompt. The charbroiled oysters were nothing short of amazing. A dish I order anytime a menu offers, however, Royal has it figured out!! The crawfish ravioli was truly amazing. The dish was true to the NOLA creole taste with lots of flavor and sass. My mouth is watering now thinking about it. We can't wait to go back.

I know it is gonna be really hard for all of you city slickers to believe, but the county is boasting the best sushi restaurant in the St. Louis area. I made sure to shake the hand of the chef before we left, as this night goes down in history.

Our customer service was everything to be expected. Our server, seemingly new and slightly unfamiliar with the menu made up by being perfectly attentive and helpful. 

The menu is slightly overwhelming with multiple pages to peruse of a la carte items. Be sure to come with friends if you are in for dinner. I did notice that their lunch special comes with several options in one bento box, but I'd come with a group in the evening for a family style dining experience. Most of the items we ordered came in groups of two or four, which made it perfect for sharing. 

There were about six beers on the menu and if you ordered one, the second was only a dollar additionally. That was a steal we couldn't resist. We also ordered a small bottle of sake which was a perfect addition for sipping (or in my case, slamming!).

I believe the four of us ordered about twenty items... we were kinda celebrating, and went way overboard. The things I remember being the best.... The house salad with an awesome ginger dressing could be a meal in itself, but we shared with the table. The pork dumplings were great... the calamari was awesome... octopus had a strange texture but really delivered a fantastic flavor! We had some super fresh red snapper nigiri. My two favorite items for the evening were the Hawaiian Tuna Poke, which doesn't warn you on the menu, but is seasoned with fresh jalapeno! and the fried cheesecake... which is unspeakably divine. 

Every time we ordered more food, we were impressed even more. I just can't believe this gem is all the way out in Valley Park.

I find it hard to believe I haven't reviewed this place yet. 
I'm not privy to all the ins and outs of Indian food. 
I love this place. 

The bathroom signs have Braille on them but it's just a printed piece of paper that has been laminated. 

I know a guy that stayed there for five weeks. He said it was great and tasted just like real Indian food.

I had dinner there tonight with a friend from out of town. I went with 4 items off the small plates and my friend had the Chicken and Green beans. All were tasty. I really liked the veggie dumplings (pan fried) the crispy garlic wings, and the scallion pancakes. The short ribs were ok but as good as the other small plates. The wait staff were attentive and helpful.

Pretty delicious food and loud and entertaining atmosphere. You'll find all kinds of people here and thats what i like about it. The staff also has great service! Definitely Recommend this place to others.

Let me start out by saying that I love Lolita. I moved to Philly 6 months ago from Los Angles (home of the street taco) and I've frequented Lolita many many times since moving here. The two star rating is more related to the service/experience I received rather than the quality of the food. My server's name was Maggie. When asked if I had any questions about the menu, I asked her if it would be an option to get the fish tacos on pieces of lettuce instead of tortillas (which I could've sworn I've done before here). The ONLY reason being that I am a Type 1 Diabetic on a low carb diet and straying from my normal diet could lead to serious complications. She responded very condescendingly and said, "Um yeah we don't do things like that here". Umm okay! I would never ask for a substitution to be difficult, especially when I know that the food is way better as is! It was a simple request and I don't think my question warranted that type of response. I immediately shut down and got the salad. I have never had this happen anywhere. Normally, the waiter will gladly ask the kitchen to make sure or will ask about dietary restrictions. I'm super bummed about this. Needless to say, I will think twice before coming to Lolita next time.
The food is amazing and the staff is very attentive and friendly. My favorite breakfast spot. My only wish is that they were open on Sundays.

I have had such a craving for some authentic Mexican street tacos and thankfully I found this place. I picked out 5 tacos, one with tongue, one de pastor, one with chorizo, and two with steak. All of them equally packed with delicious flavor. I'm stuck between the tongue and chorizo as my top picks. The tongue was so tender and not on the fatty side which can happen a lot with tongue tacos. The chorizo was just so juicy and and flavorful with all this spices! I must say all the tacos I had where really good those two are were just my top picks! I would never think this little truck on the side of the road would be so good. So good that I ate all 5 tacos with not a bite left behind. I will be back to test out the tortas and most definitely for more tacos.

We've eaten at this Carrabba's a handful of times, but after the last two, we will not return.  A few months ago, my husband was sick hours after eating a pepperoni and sausage pizza at this location.  We boycotted the place for a few months, but decided to give it another try this weekend.  The food is usually good, and we had a gift card.  Well that was a mistake....  My husband ordered the seafood canneloni, and I had Pollo Rosa Maria (my favorite!).  Our order took 45 minutes, and when it came to the table the canneloni was burnt (and I mean it was Black!) and my chicken was dry and crunchy.  :(  Disappointed, we sent it back.  The manager was apolegtic and discounted our bill.  The reorders came back and were cooked fine this time around.  My husband wasn't impressed but my dinner was good....so I thought.  We left the restaurant around 9:30 and by 1:30, I was as sick as a dog!  Food poisoning 2 times in a row?!?!  We will never return!
Great food, staff and atmosphere. Great weekend spot too for an outdoor breakfast/lunch with mimosas!

Four Words: Black and White Milkshake. This is the good stuff. These guys really know what they are doing. The shakes are awesome, the grilled cheeses are delicious, and the pancakes are some of the best I have ever had. Word to the wise, the portions are HUGE. Two pancakes can easily feed two people. If you don't like kids or crowds then stay away especially on weekend mornings. But I am a huge fan and make it a point to stop in whenever I am visiting the area. If I had the dough i would become an investor. This place is sure to spread to other locations. Go now. Eat. Drink. Be Happy.

Theres nothing special about the food. The portions are good and the food is slightly pricey. If you really want a meal near the beach, this place is fine, but your paying a premium for location, not food. Skip the artichoke app.
nice shop. went in the weekend before Christmas. wasn't a huge selection. a bit over prices. the pie I got was delicious though

Good Burger, little skimpy on the side order of fries. Brewed ice tea was a little weak. No complaints, but it still felt like something was missing. I think it was the personal interactions that brought it down to a 3 star. Not bad, but not left with an impression that someone was actually running the place.

Not only the best froyo in old city, but the best froyo in the entire city.  I've tried them all, and am happy to have the latest addition to the philly market so close to home (though bad news for my waistline).

This place was just ok. It was overpriced but I was ok with it if quality matched. Ordered a sweet crepe with strawberries and nutella - for an extra $4.50 for those toppings I expected at least fresh strawberries but they were these thin soggy slices that got mushy really quickly. On top of that, we just wanted some water to wash the sweetness down with ... 2 cups of iced water that I assumed was tap water .... Got charged $2 for "infused water" ... I didn't taste any infusion of anything and I certainly didn't buy a fancy bottle of water so that was total BS. The only positive was the nice staff. Will not be returning or recommending anybody here. Too bad the other crepe places aren't closer.

I have a love/hate relationship with this place.

LOVE: The passionfruit mojitos and peach long islands are strong and GOOD. A little spendy, but it seems like you are paying a little for the atmosphere. The rooftop patio is an awesome place to start out for the night, and they always have some sort of band (sometimes good, sometimes bad) playing on the weekends.

BAD: Every server we have had has been HORRIBLE. Last weekend my friend asked for a lime for her drink. In turn, the waitress scoffed at her, stomped over to the bar, picked up a lime with her bare hands and basically threw it at my friend. WOW. She also messed up our drink orders about 1/2 the time. Also, try to get there before 9 (like 8:55) so you don't have to pay the ridiculous cover charge, but you won't be able to find a table on the patio, even if there are several open, until 9. Apparently they take reservations and 1/2 of them don't even show up, but at 9 they open up. Also, be ready for a lot of upper class crustys with fake boobs and Tommy Bahama shirts. This is where they tend to congregate when they aren't at their Maui vacation home.

All in all, this place is good every once in a while for a fun drink, but don't expect anything from the service. You won't get any.

Really disappointing experience.  It took 15 minutes to get seated, and the place was only one fourth full. It took another 10 minutes before my server even showed up to ask me for a drink. My cocktail was not well prepared and did not taste good at all. My steak was overcooked and not particularly special.  For the price tag should have been much better. I asked for one minor side accompaniment, and the waiter forgot to bring it. It just felt very snobby and not very much like Nashville which is pretty chill and laid back and friendly. Definitely can't recommend this, especially for the price. They need to lighten up a bit and work on their service and food if they're going to make it. The location is perfect with great outdoor seating so they really need to try harder and make this place work. It could be a cool place.

Our very first stop and first meal. I'll be honest... this was not on my food list but glad someone recommended it. Looks like regulars and locals eat here. Their menu is extensive... lots of seafood items.

We tried the hush puppies... my favorite thing on the menu. They're huge, super crispy on the outside but light, fluffy, and flavorful!! Definitely recommend this dish! 

Their gumbo was also good! Hubby got a cup with his shrimp po boy. And I had grilled catfish stuffed with crab, served with pasta, shrimp and cream sauce! Huge servings! 

Definitely try this place out! I would come back for the hush puppies!!

The guys and gals of this Jimmy Johns location have literally saved my life.  Well, maybe that is a bit extreme, but they have saved me from missing lunch many times when I have gotten too busy at work to go out or forgot to bring my lunch.

When I realize that it is after noon and I don't have time to leave the office, I go online to jimmyjohns.com and order my trusty #12 Beach Club (cut in half... it's less messy).  Within 5 - 10 minutes, without fail, they are knocking on my office door with sandwich in hand.  They are truly "freaky fast".  

The food is standard Jimmy Johns; it is consistently the same.  Their location and the speed of the service is what makes this Jimmy Johns stand out from other sandwich places in the area.

If you've had the pleasure of going to Chef Tia's west side restaurant, you know how lucky she picked South Broad Ripple for Chicken Scratch. We drove over to the west side twice for lunch just for the fried chicken Alfredo fries. 

We made the mistake of driving over since it was so close (this will be very dangerous!) to order but it was packed on a Friday night. Order online and pickup so it's as fresh as possible! 

We got our standby and it was delicious! Now that it's not a far drive, I can't wait to try the wings and hot chicken!

I placed an order for a pizza to be delivered to me at 9:19PM they close at 10PM. 10 mins until 10PM the manager calls me and says that they had to cancel my f*king order because they're closing and don't have "resources" to make more pizzas. Some straight BS! I was waiting this whole time and they hit me with this sh*t.

Love this place for an early brunch or for dessert  after a dinner or breakfast when I'm in the mood for a nice French pastry. I love having brunch here with my friends to catch up. Nice French decor, great atmosphere, delicious food, and the servers are super friendly. Love this cute little spot. If you're into eggs Benedict, the ribs Benedict is awesome and very filling along with a nice coffee.

The barista was very nice and friendly. The Latte was adequate.

This place is hard to find. And seems to be connected to some car place and an audio store. There's hardly any parking and the atmosphere is super weird. 

The other customers (maybe locals) seemed annoyed that we were there. 

The music inside was very loud.

We just got our coffee and left.

I enjoy Vietnam Palace (AKA the Electric Ao Dai) because it's not the ususal crap Pho-in-the-wall place. The decor is nice, the servers are attentive and they have a liquor license(!). Yes, it's more than $6 a bowl for soup. This seems to offend many people who are dead set on cheap pho, but try to remember that you're paying to sit in a place that doesn't look like someone set up a soup kitchen in the remains of a Bosnian McDonalds. Don't worry, there are still plenty of cheap pho places with dirty bowls and filthy seats around (Cafe Pho Ga Thanh Thanh in Kensington comes to mind). We've eaten here dozens of times and I can say that everything I've eaten has been good and remarkably consistent. 

Food-wise I'd say its a 4/5- good, craveable, but not mind-blowing. The setting pushes it up to five stars, because its the type of place where you can take a group/family/a date and get a drink, bullshit, eat and generally turn the meal into a 3 hour affair. There are better Viet places out there in terms of food, but very few in Philly have an atmosphere that is conducive to staying for more than 20 minutes. If you're in Chinatown this is the spot for Viet.

Wow wow wow!!! 

Needed to upgrade my review because the squads been taking care of business! 

Started off a couple weeks back, Amanda came through for yuh boy and princess Grace hard, a good reminder of the important things in life. Smile from ear to ear the entire time  . #rockstar

Then Katrina I think it was, late night run to the Roadhouse on a Sunday, sweet and professional. Can't get enough of this smokehouse burger. Was in n out in like 30 minutes. 

Tuesday night came along and it was burger time again, I'm out of control, back to meal prepping tomorrow!!! Anyways, Azhleigh and I'm sorry if I spelled it wrong , helped me and my other Roadhouse fan friend and was so nice! 

Love the Roadhouse

Ok - I am being generous with the 4 star because we went on the first Friday of a full open, knowing there would be room for improvement and there were some kinks to be worked out. The staff was a little nervous - especially our waitress and cocktail waitress on the patio. When encouraged, these young woman provided great service. The appetizers - charbroiled oysters and alligator hush puppies were above average. My husband thought they were outstanding. The preparation of the duck was spot on. The grouper was slightly overdone and hidden beneath an overwhelming amount of stewed tomatoes. The rice had zero flavoring and did not add to the overall meal (duck). The mashed potatoes with cheddar popcorn was loaded with delish. The overall ambiance and space was incredible. With a few tweaks, this restaurant could be one of the absolute best in Tampa.

Very good service and drinks but most of the entrees were very average and lacking flavor. The cioppino was likely the best dish we had and the shellfish and sauce were very tasty. Calamari appetizer was good as well and not overly breaded.The Colorada lamb however;  the sauce wasnt very good and the chops were cut too thin. A double cut would have been a nicer presentation. The pumpkin gnocchi were tende but had very little pumpkin taste to it and the sauce was bland. I had the pappardelle with meat sauce which was ok but again the sauce was bland with very little seasoning to the dish. Not sure you can even call it an entree with the small portion you get. I've had better meat sauce pastas in mom and pop restaurants for a lot less. The veal Milanese was the worst of all the dishes being incredibly dry, not tender, and once again, no flavor. I really wanted to like this restaurant since I'm staying with my family and friends at the Bacara Resort and Spa for 3 nights and this is really the only option for family dining; but the quality and value is just not there considering the high cost of having a meal here. This restaurant did not meet my level of expectation.
This place is awesome. The BBQ Bacon Cheeseburger w/ Smokey Cheddar is off the charts!

I had a very disappointing experience tonight, eating on a Saturday with my family, the wait line was 45 minutes and we went for the restaurant part without the amazing food show, just straight jibachi food, it literally took 30 min to get the food, and it was cold, very disappointing , the manager was negotiating and giving excuses why the kitchen couldn't handle the order on a busy night.

The food is good here, but we only go here as a last resort. 

No one is ever eating food when we done here. 

Their are always bar flies sitting at the bar. 

This place has an older crowd feeling.
This is my favorite cheesesteak place in Philly, hands down. A cheesesteak wit whiz is the way to go!!

We were looking for a quick bite to eat while passing Santa Barbara. I got car sick while browsing the Yelp app, but we ended up stumbling upon Cuernavaca anyway, which is one of the places I bookmarked. 

I was a little confused at first, because I thought it was a restaurant. When I saw the front door and the "express" sign, I went to the second door, and it said the same. So I meandered to the third door, and that was a completely different establishment. 

I wasn't sure what to get, so I ordered El Fortachon. It had so many things in it that I figured it couldn't be anything but delicious. The boyfriend got 3 tacos and ended up wishing he had ordered 5, since they were small. I gave him some of my food, though, so it all worked out.

My meal was, as expected, very savory and satisfying. Even though I didn't eat the whole thing, I was stuffed by the end. Btw, tacos come out fast, but everything else seems to have a wait.

I've been waiting to try this place for a while now... and now, I kinda wish I hadn't. I was feeling indecisive so I ordered 2 items, figured I could save the other half of each for lunch tomorrow, or later today if they were that amazing.  They weren't. First, chicken Cesar Salad. Absolutely ZERO flavor, and only about 1 Oz of dressing (but that ended up being ok because it too has no flavor and I didn't eat the salad anyways). Soggy croutons, chicken and artichoke that felt like they had previously been soaked in water. Plus I found a surprise in my salad, a twist tie, hummmm I don't remember ordering that? Anyways, I had a few bites, pushed it aside... Next item, the Gobbler panini. Nothing special to report here, not awful, but not good either, not sure if they forgot the sundried tomatoe mayo or if it just had no flavor, but all I tasted was feta .  I was really excited about the pickle, and was greatly disappointed to find more of a slug like texture than a yummy crispy spicy pickle I was hoping for. To be honest, the best part about this meal was the potato salad and the fact that they have cherry coke.... well at least I've been now and I know I'm not missing out on much, I'd rather pay $20 for 2 lunch items somewhere else!

A stupid ex-bf introduced me to David's many moons ago, and even though I have many horrible memories of going there with his Chinese family, I somehow manage to stow away those memories deep into the depths of my brain, and head to David's for my usual dishes of salt & pepper squid, beef chow fun, and dumplings with the ridiculous ginger scallion sauce.

That ginger scallion sauce is magic: it heals all wounds AND makes the stomach very, very happy.

Went to this restaurant with friends. Old style with mature waiters, white table cloths, very nice. Great steak NY strip cooked rare tender, juicy. Cold broccoli. Good baker all the way. If I still lived here this would be a regular place
Amazing, amazing and EXCELLENT. must try!! Best and most creative breakfasts in Tucson.

The signature bagel is a hidden gem in Fairmount. 

Thinly sliced avocado, perfect spread of cream cheese. Chocked full of crunchy almonds drizzled with honey and dashed with a signature spice.  If you don't know, now you know.

All beef hotdogs adourned with the freshest ingredients to ensure a positive response with each bite. With over 20 different dogs and almost as many fry combinations, there is something for everyone at this gem. 

Owner is super friendly and inviting. Enjoyed his humor and he was SUPER knowledgeable about the menu. Soda selection includes fountain drinks only made with real sugar - reallt good. Clean dining area. Didn't have to wait long for our made to order dogs.

My guy and I got the Philly dog w/ pizza fries and Reuben dog w/ mac 'n' cheese fries. Hands down best hot dog I've ever had and the fries made the experience. Perfect temperature. Perfect concoction for a great dinner. Can't wait to try it again soon. Seriously, right now they have a limited time Lo Mein dog that I'm dying to try.

Treat yourself at this place. You won't be disappointed.
And remember: If you don't hotdog, you don't America!

*Note for my next visit: Upgrade to pretzel bun!!!*
A wonderful experience - great food and service.  Owners are very friendly and attentive. Menu was able to easily accommodate a vegan diet.
Corner bar meets great food and fun atmosphere. We had the nachos and the fish and chips....delicious! Great beer selection and friendly service. Can't wait to return!
The food was delicious. I'm here for a conference and when it was lunch time the line was long. However the line moved steadily along. Prices are good. Limited space for groups.

Dinner inside the Gaylord Opry Hotel. The service is awesome. There was no wait and our waitress so far has be wonderful. Drinks and appetizers were brought out shortly after ordering. 
The restaurant is well decorated, clean, and the food is amazing!!! It's fun, up beat vibe and relaxed for tired travelers. 
I ordered Maui Fish Tacos and they are so good. There were some pepper so it had a kick to them. The drinks are definitely worth the price. They have more alcohol than I've ever had in a restaurant.
The restaurant manager is quite a humorous guy!!! He walked around and greeted all his customers. He joked around with us, teasing my friend about her location in FL. Our nicknames are now WIFI!!  :). It was a pleasure to have dined here.

I will do 4 star for the bloody and Tot bowl
They were excellent
The service lacking, I always enjoy when your food comes to the table and the kid is looking at you - Do you need anything else? I say how about silverware and napkins? He shrugs and come back with a mug that has theee forks and three napkins for a table of 5 people.
So we go inside to ask for more silverware and napkins and after a google eye second they produce another mug with 3 of each and a quizzical look.
Again Tots cheesy sauce, fried egg , crispy house made tots yummy. Bacon garnished Bloody and excellent side partner - service needs some help!
Out of town and stopped by after the day at the state fair.  Found this to be a great place.  Above average service,  tasty appetizers and nice cold beer. . RECOMMEND...

The building and location are very nice and open. Very much loved the fact that the outside seating was smoke-free! Always happy when we can enjoy the nice weather in the cooler months without smelling smoke with our food. 

The various food choices are good, but on the high side. We wanted to get the oysters, but another critic on Yelp complained of shells in them and other diners around us confirmed about the same, so we decided against ordering them. The octopus was very good, but not enough to justify the price. The calamari was chewy and not crunchy. The drinks were very good and most in our party liked the choice of beers. The other diners in our party enjoyed the deconstructed seafood pot pie and the lobster risotto. 

Can't say we'll add this restaurant to our rotation each week, but it was a nice change. Parking is a little bit of an issue, especially if you arrive a little later. They do have valet parking to help.

I  am giving this a five for good comfort food not healthy food. The Mac and cheese is excellent. The burgers are tasty. A great place to meet with friends to have a beer and watch a game. If you are looking for healthy low cal, I would go someplace else.
A quaint restaurant located on busy Hillsboro. We loved the unique dishes served at Santo. Their small menu allows for each dish to be executed perfect with delicious flavors.

This seems to be a favorite for many co-workers when on layover here in Philly, so naturally we had to check it out. Have to say I wasn't impressed with the food... 
Service was pleasant, the ambiance was cool in a very kitschy way. Swinging chairs (which were fun but kind of hard for me to eat in) I blame it on my short legs, lol! I would like to check out the rooftop bar though.

The hubby has been talking about this place for a few weeks, so we decided to stop in for lunch.  The salad was so-so, I mean, how much can you do with lettuce and veggies anyway?  Bill had the meatballs which were very good.  Juicy and tasty!  

There come the main course.  Makes me wish I had skipped the appetizer.  The strmboli was HUGE and oh so delicious.  I had to sneak a few bites when Bill stopped to breathe, which was not often.  I ate the entire bowl of stuffed shells although I was stuffed as well.  

All in all, it's worth the trip!  All I needed was a cot to take a nap in a soundproof booth to silence my snoring.  Be prepared to take some home as the portions are pretty big.

Great: ambiance, decor, food, drinks (Bloody Mary is a little spicy which I love, but not overwhelmingly so which the bf likes) biscuit gravy( gravy unique flavored-I prefer Bob Evans or cracker barrel's but commend them for making a unique gravy-has cheese, cream like quality.
