I can't eat pork sausage/pepperoni and the only options would be a meat ball pizza or hot chicken (covered with coating).  The pizza is about $20 for a 6x10 oblong, thick on the crust on the sides with just a little sauce.  I was sharing with a friend and we asked for the sausage on half - came to the table with the sausage spread down the long way, cut not down the middle but about 2/3 which meant I had three pieces of pizza about 2 x 3 inches mostly crust.  The taste was fair but certainly not worth $20.  So, we ate the pizza, paid the bill and left......I no sooner got to the car when I got sick from the grease.  
So, between that and an atmosphere so loud you could not carry on a conversation, there are much better places to have a decent pizza.

What a brilliant business plan. This cafe truly makes the North Mass Boulder a community that you don't have to leave. You can climb, do yoga, workout, cowork/have a meeting, take one of their other classes then hit up the Top Out Cafe and replenish.

The cafe offers juices, brews, booches, coffees, teas, sandwiches, salads, breakfast bites, and so many more things. It's always nice to have this as an option in case you're in need of a beverage/bite to eat in between activities at the campus. 

I've had their turmeric juice, which was tasty. It seems that they add some water or another filler as the juices aren't as strong/potent as they can be. I've also tried their ginger/turmeric tea, which was delightful. And, then I also tried their fall-themed iced latte with oat milk. Not my favorite, but it was still tasty. 

One word of caution: unless you're just getting a pre-made kombucha or beer, it takes some time. The environment is casual (which I love), which results in items (drinks and food) taking a bit of time. 

Other notes:
- they do ask take out or dine in
- they're no-tip which I love
- there are seats and tables/chairs surrounding the cafe

The Little Radish at the front of the market is the absolute best! They have crazy delicious soups, salads, and desserts beautifully prepared made from locally sourced ingredients. Lots of gluten-free options. Everything looks so pretty and tastes amazing. The Call Me Bleu salad is ridiculous!! And the gluten-free carrot whoopie pies... OMG.
A love this place...good food...good service...good location. Great location for a gem show lunch Having chicken salad on a croissant today.  Yummm...may have dessert if we're not too full

If you are visiting Tucson and looking for authentic traditional Mexican food, this isn't the place.  It's definitely gourmet Latin American fusion. If you go with the mindset that it isn't Mexican food, per se, you will be very pleased. The servings are huge and the food is amazing. The plating presentations are works of art. The food and experience are very unique and stand out from the rest. The restaurant is  beautifully decorated, aesthetically pleasing,  and very romantic. It is the prettiest restaurant I have ever been to, and I have been to many. The service is fantastic and the owner checked on us as well. My favorite dishes are the heavenly tamales as well as the seafood. I'm not a fan of the beef but I think it's the seasoning that's used. The chocolate moose paired with a red wine is to die for. Cafe Poca Cosa is an experience that satisfies all the senses as well as the heart and soul.

It's my second visit, this time for dinner with an old friend.  I had the Baja fish tacos and an IPA and he had a tall cheese-filled polenta dish.  The food was out of sight good.   The service was very competent and very friendly. I have some concerns for Zest that perhaps the menu is too thick and that a the Thursday evening dinner crowd was too thin. As for the menu, I'd be more comfortable with a shorter daily selection, perhaps with a rotation, for the sake of quality.  As for the sparse attendance at dinner, we can only hope that the lunch crowd is floating the boat and that more people will quickly  "get it".   

Viva Zest!  I'll be back soon!

I came in thinking this was Cochon Butcher. It's not! But I don't regret the choice since my partner and I had a nice, air conditioned, sit down lunch at Cochon. The food is very good. Oysters are amazing. 
I forgot to take a pic of the short ribs and the gumbo that we ordered. They were so good. The gumbo was the best I've had in NOLA. The servers were also friendly and accomodating. However, there's a bit of a wait 30mins for 2 people during lunch time. I suggest that you make a reservation prior to going.

I love hot dogs.  I really love this place!!!  

Food is always great, the place is clean and the owners take pride in delivering an outstanding product.

The food was decent but there wasn't much meat! Usually a philly has meat falling out the bread...NOT HERE! The seasoned fries and very salty. The service was great at first. She asked us how we liked our food. When we said "There wasn't much meat." She walked away as if we insulted her parents. #neveragain

We have tried this place twice now. I was hesitant to review critically the first time due to extremely poor service, as it was cinco de mayo and they were slammed. We went this weekend and the service was yet again miserable. It is really too bad because the food and drinks are really very good. I love the bar staff, really good bunch of folks. The hostess and wait staff should really work on service and stop with the blanket apologies.

I went for Sunday Brunch on a beautiful fall morning. I got there right at 10 when they're supposed to open but the place was already packed with people eating so I guess they opened early due to demand. Luckily I had made a reservation so was seated pretty quickly; otherwise, it looked like there was a 20 minute wait. 

My server Walter was really nice and funny and had the best reply to my question of "is it too early to order dessert?" "It's never too early!" So I did. I actually ordered the Highway (chicken and waffles) with the strawberry rhubarb shortcake. Both were delicious and I finished my plate. I'm a pretty good eater and it was just enough food. Some may not feel the half waffle and 2 fried chicken breast cutlets are enough but I think they would've been fine even if I didn't order the dessert. 

The inside and outside both have a great ambiance and I was lucky enough to sit outside on the patio overlooking Lower Broad. I'll definitely be going back since they are open all day everyday which makes it an easy Downtown lunch option. And I hear you get two hours free parking at the Pinnacle garage next door :)
They're actually open on Sunday's! Yelp says that they're closed. This is my favorite Banh mi place. We get at least 4 of these babies every Sunday! Favorites are Dac Biet and Xiu Mai.
OK, slightly more upscale than Carrabba's, but I actually prefer Carrabba's. There's nothing exceptional about Bonefish Grill, though it's a fine place for dinner.

This is my new place to go for soul food. So far I've had the lemon pepper wings, Whiting, cabbage,  yams, and chicken broccoli mac. I used to have a strong aversion to mac n cheese with anything added. Craftys changed my mind. Their food is soooo good. The service is excellent.
This place is okay. Forgettable for sure but not terrible. But the server Sarah is lovely so this place gets 3 stars for her stellar service.

Great place with an AMAZING atmosphere. If you go here, dine outside! Service was excellent and the food was delicious as well. Their fries and falafel are great to get as an appetizer. The pita bread and dip is also a must have with your meal. Expensive but well worth it!

This is a really delicious chain restaurant.  A bit noisy but the food has been excellent every time I've been here.  I ordered the salmon salad, dressing on the side and my cousin had the salmon sandwich.  Mine was DELISH! And too big to finish!  She enjoyed hers as well and we both had enough to take home.  They also have AMAZING lobster bisque.  The patio is relaxing on a nice crisp afternoon too.  
Note:  parking at this location is a bit of a hassle, but if you are patient (and lucky) you will find one not too far away.
A classic "go-to" spot for some simple and familiar comfort food. A definite top contender on my DoorDash list

$52.00 Dinner and this is the salad I'm brought. Never again will I go to the Carrabba's on Fowler Ave. And the Manager Morgan is the one that brought us our food and I spoke to about we're they out of Romaine lettuce because that was all the hard yellow and white pieces and it nasty taste that I couldn't even eat! His response was Eeewww sorry and walked away. He was more worried about the event that the girl he talked to on the phone was planning than pleasing his customer that paid $24.00 a plate. Thanks for the nasty beginning of what was supposed to be a good dinner Morgan hats off to you for ruining our night out! #neveragain

Point of service is critical to any business, and if you can't take an order every 30 seconds with a line out the door... well you suck.  

I waited in line what seemed over 30 minutes with about 20 to 25 people infront of me.  If someone isn't teady, just say "next" like Frau Farbissina from Austin Powers screaming "Scott". They should open another register.  

I also git cut by a bunch of groupie chick's who inserted themselves with their boy toys. I didn't want to say anything and cause a fight, but there should be some sort of security with a line like this.  Fights start this way.  

The food here is decent,  but not worth the wait.  I'm sure there's another place that can fill your arteries with grease at 2am.

I want to like this place, I really do. I enjoyed sharing the chicken liver nuggets with friends, but the heirloom bean salad felt like something I could have whipped up at home.  I tried my boyfriend's hoe cakes, but that left me feeling disappointed.  Should I have ordered something different?  I know this spot can whip up a phenomenal cocktail, but why not a kick-ass meal?
good food and excellent service! Love the book area.
The best place on the southside to get craft beer. The menus has a lot of great gems; get the wings!

Have been here many times and recommended it to many friends.  Has reservations for lunch today with my family to celebrate a graduation.  Got there early but the doors were open so we went in.  Rudely greeted at the front door but that was not the problem.  THEY WERE PAINTING THE WINDOW FRAMES.  THE SMELL WAS HORRIBLE - ACTUALLY CHOCKING.  Made a comment and the hostess said Oh we are painting all the windows -  My reservations were made thru Open Table days ago.  This was not a great situation and an impossible situation.  WE went across the street to the bar on the corner.  It even smelled a little in there.  Did i mention that our party contained two young boys who were looking forward to "pancakes"  

Called the Health department - hoped they shut them down

Stopped by today for the first time and tried the blackened shrimp po' boy. Service was fast, comfy seating and, most importantly, the food was really good. Just the right amount for lunch. Will definitely be back.

So much fun to be dining outside, on Victoria Street, and under the Arlington Theater tower. 

Delicious breakfast, hot coffee, and thank you server Andrew for taking good care of us. 

Cinnamon Roll, Avocado Toast, Steak and eggs, and all this sunshine . . . perfect.

Their new location on Victoria Street, right next to Olio E Limone, and across the street from the Public Market.
The product doesn't match the hype. Super crowded and wait staff is overwhelmed

The food and drink is pretty decent here probably the best in cherry hill but the only reason why I gave it 2 stars was because of the service. There was no customers when I walked in and they did not seem busy, however the female cashier gave me an attitude because I was taking a couple minutes deciding what to order. She literally stared at me the entire time and did not sound happy to take or make my order, which made me very uncomfortable.

The breakfast here is phenomenal! I ordered pancakes w/ strawberries, bacon sausage and eggs. Was seated immediately on a Saturday afternoon. My toddler loved the pancakes and bacon. The portions are HUGE! The booths are update and the waitress was very attentive!
Always good.  One of my wife's favorites.  We just want them to bring back the great empanadas that they used to have.  They were an awesome desert  Francisco was a great  waiter.

I was not impressive with this place overall.  I think they have some good things like the raw bar and the service was pretty good but, the cooked food was not.  The rock fish was over cooked and the butternut risotto was way to sweet, it was like eating spiced cream of rice.  The steak was cooked perfect but under seasoned as were the mushrooms.  The fried shrimp and calamari were nicely breaded and tasty.  Another bland element were the sauces, the one served with the calamari was unremarkable and the one with the rock fish, well I don't know what the point was, it tasted like nothing.  The deserts were good.  Probably would not go back considering the cost, it's not worth the mediocre meal.

Service was unfortunately very poor. We sat on the second floor on a Tuesday night at 8pm and our waitress didn't even acknowledge us.  Even after poking my head up a number of times (and she seemed to be looking in our direction) it took her at least 15-20 minutes to even get our order. Initially she blamed it on the fact she wasn't informed there was a reservation; having two patrons sitting there patiently waiting I would think would be enough...

The food overall was also unfortunately not very good. I ordered ahi tuna and my piece was very tough (not exactly how its supposed to be served). I could barely eat it because the cut was so tough and gave up after a few bites. My girlfriend ordered shrimp and grits that was OK, but a little too rich. However I would say in fairness the appetizers we ordered (we split a salad and got avocado soups) were good.

In finishing the meal our waitress again took exceptionally long to stop by, even with my girlfriend and I clearly pushing our plates away and waiting. She walked by our table a number of times and didn't even acknowledge us. Even the bill took long to receive. In poor taste, rather than removing our meals and disposing of them in the kitchen, she also started dumping out my half eaten meal onto the other dirty patrons plates on the overall serving dish after picking it up in front of us. Overall it was VERY bad.

The manager of the restaurant never acknowledged our table. Despite paying attention to a larger party a few tables down, there was no customary stopping by to see how everything was, despite him also walking by our table as well.

Overall - whatever misses they had on the food could have been quickly overcome by the service.  However, the service for this meal was worse than most places I've been, and with a pricey menu and upscale vibe - one would think they'd get much more for what they are paying.  We were wholly dissatisfied and I unfortunately could not recommend this restaurant.

I've been going to tequilas for years seeking as I used to work at one of the clubs next door . And their food is amazing . I went in tonight an hour before close and placed a to go order. After waiting in the front for about 25 min, I was then informed that everything was shut down so they couldn't make my order . I find it very unprofessional seeing as it was an hour before close when the order was placed, and it wasted 25 min of my time waiting.

I have been a costumer for this restaurant for a long time and I always told other Chinese that this is a good restaurant and they have good food and dessert. But I was very disappointed at how the owner do the business. They are desserts are always 2 dollars each and this time they charge me for 4 dollars. I was very surprised and asked if they were wrong. The owner insisted that they were always charged in this way and said I must had not been here for a long time (which is not true because I just hung out with my friends here). And then they tried to explain to me that because I didn't buy anything so I should pay double for my dessert which really upset me. Clearly they have a lot of customers and they really don't care about if you are satisfied for their service or not and charge based on their mood. I don't think I deserve this kind of treatment so one star. Good luck to this restaurant!

This place has been, and likely always will be, the benchmark against which I compare other pizza places.  The pizza here is PERFECT.  Every detail of the slice here is amazing, slightly crispy bottom, tender crust, savory mozzarella, and a remarkable tomato sauce that has just a hint of sweetness.  I have since moved away from Old City, but have yet to find anywhere that compares to Gianfranco.  You'd never notice the place just walking by, but make a point to stop by whenever you're in Old city.

This used to be my favorite pizza place. Now they pre cook way to much and let it sit out to get gross, it used to be almost fresh out the oven when you came to get a slice. And they changed the prices recently to make it even more expensive for a slice of pizza that looks like it's been sitting out since the day before.

This was my first time hitting the downtown location. As with the other Scotty's locations, they have a good beer selection and good food. There are good veggie burgers for the vegetarians. 

The thing that sets this location apart from the rest (besides being surrounded by downtown views) is their massive outdoor seating area. If it's warm out, eat outside. it's worth it.
At the recent food truck awards they were my winners. The poutine and Italian Ham sandwich were excellent. Can't wait to see them at future events around town.

Good deserts, ordering is complicated.  We came in the first time and ordered cake.  It is TOTALLY unclear how to order and where to go.  We ordered cake at ice cream and ended up feeling like we screwed up.  We ended up getting helped but got passed around a bit.  We'll be back, but better signage would help us newbies.

Came twice and both for brunch! Their pork belly sandwich is hands down a must at the Polite Society. There were no regrets especially with the bottomless mimosas. Their other entrees are good and would recommend for a nice brunch spot in the St. Louis area.

I agree with several other recent reviews-- the Brewerytown Taproom is significantly different compared to last year and its start as "Flying Fish Crafthouse." 

The decor and industrial feel is still there, but the beer and food menu has been upgraded and tweaked (for the better). Now, rather than just Flying Fish and a few can options, the beer selection is huge with both local breweries and larger more generic beers. This new beer menu far outweighs the previous menu both in price and selection. 

The food was never an issue (at least for me). Yes, they could have a few more healthy options, but for both brunch and dinner I have yet to have a bad meal. My wife and I went for brunch on Sunday (and although we were the only customers in there around noon), we had great service, friendly wait staff and enjoyable conversation. It did become more crowded as the meal continued! Brewerytown Taproom is and will be a great destination once new developments around the neighborhood are completed. They are trying hard to beat their initial reviews and hopefully continue to get better! I will certainly be back.

We really enjoyed our first visit here! DH got the Sunshine Breakfast with pulled pork. The poached egg on deer potato was unexpected, and delicious! Great juices and coffee. Everything made with great care here. Atmosphere is chill and arty.
This place is a great improvement over the original establishment. Our burritos were so flavorful, the service was fast and the interior felt clean.

The service here is phenomenal, we got the polenta, lobster arogosta, and the shrimp risotto. The food was fantastic, and the service was better. The server kept checking our table every 5 minutes and the manager would the sweep the restaurant every 10 minutes to make sure everything was good. Now the food, the polenta serving was quite nice, it was enough that if you were not that hungry you could eat that and have enough. However, the polenta flavors would want you to keep eating more and more. The lobster arogosta(on dinner menu) was a lobster pasta and it was fantastic. The sauce was a really good compliment to the lobster. Lastly, the Rissoto with Shrimp. This dish was fantastic, the risotto was very fresh and tasty, and the shrimp flavor developed the risotto flavor. As I had said, as good as the food was, the service was better, out waitress constantly made to sure to keep out water filled and checked in multiple times to see if we were okay with Parmesan, black pepper, etc. Overall, the place is pricy but definitely worth the trip.

Tried this place back in April for a friend's birthday. When we walked in, it was clearly shift change and the front area waitstaff was agitated and ready to head home for the evening. We witnessed a disagreement amongst co-workers. Once we were seated, the waiter was very friendly and suggested the seabream. We weren't to sure about the fish since we'd never heard of it before but the entree was pretty good. I was not impressed with the cheesecake though.

Excellent food and super friendly wait staff! I went last Friday with a group of friends for Karaoke. I had a great time watching people sing and listening to music. Maybe next time, I'll do a number. As a new restaurant, I was excited to try the food. I had the creme brulee and shared the peanut butter torte with a friend. So delightful! Desserts were very good and came out fast. One of my friends ordered the House Cut Fries which seemed pricey for fries but once they came out and you seen the sauce, many toppings and experienced the taste it seemed completely worth it. I learned there was a smaller version of just fries which are very affordable but I dunno if I can get go back to just fries now that I ordered the House Cut Fries. Too delicious to pass up! Another friend, had honey hot wings. Great mixture of hot food and sweet, very meaty and delicious, also. If you haven't noticed  by now, we were all sharing and sampling everything in the group. I doubt there is any item on the menu that is not incredibly delicious. I have already been back, this past Tuesday for Trivia and to order the wings for just me this time. The entertainment is wonderful. They have a female DJ! How Cool! The Decor is sleek and nice and brings a great atmosphere to every visit. Check it out if you haven't yet!

I had an TERRIBLE experience here, probably my WORST EVER. I walked in to no hostess, whom I waited patiently for. After 5-10 minutes one of the customers had to stop a waitress to tell her we were waiting. There were only two tables occupied in the whole place. The hostess asked us, "can I help you?" like she didn't know what we were there for... it was dinner time, why else would we have been there? She turned out to be our waitress and was rude throughout the meal.

My friend and I both chose a meal with a side of mushroom ravioli (which we both love). When the meal arrived, the side turned out to be mashed potatos instead of ravioli. We questioned our waitress who explained, "Our meals are made to order, so sometimes he replaces parts of the meal." She clearly doesn't know what "made to order" means... because I ordered my meal with a side of mushroom ravioli, and it was not made they way I ordered it! 

The food was rather tastey, which is the only reason I'm giving them two whole stars. But it wasn't even the food I wanted!

I'd like to give them another try, because I've heard wonderful things... but I don't want to feel even more frustrated than I do already.
I don't give 5 stars too often but this place is pretty damn cool, great vibe, great people, great service. People from all walks of life. Not rowdy or loud just a very cool dive bar setting!
AmaZing! I have never had a poached egg like it. We shared a corned beef hash that was absolutely mind blowing. I would whole heartedly recommend it! The best breakfast in town.
Great food and cafe con leche!  I really enjoy the Latin cuisine and the friendly service.

These donuts are off the hook delicious! We waited in line for 10 minutes and the line moved quickly(and it was fun to watch them make the donuts) and so worth the wait. They were delicious light and not too sweet. We highly recommend it!!

We stumbled upon this place as we were walking down the streets of Philadelphia. Terminal Market is a true hidden gem! We were so impressed by the options and quality of food here! So much to see and pick from. We ended up trying a bit of everything from different vendors. I do have to say that the cookies were everything!! So glad to have found this place! Will be coming back next time I'm in town!

The service was VERY good.  The meats were just okay for the most part.  Considering how we felt about the quality of the meat (though there was a LOT of it), we felt the food wasn't worthy of the price.

Came here because we sat down at another place down main strip to get some green fairies. They didnt even look at us or notice us. That place was twice as much for two drinks. This place was half price. I quickly yelped it and foudn them a block away. Just off main street. Either way. The bar tender was friendly and talked to us. But the whole show on for the absinthe. Food was cheap. There were other also who were ordering food. 

Place was actualy cleaner than a couple of the other bars we walked into as well.

If I didn't try to get this sandwich a thousand times I didn't try at all. Man it took me forever to get my hands on this masterpiece, even after me talking shit about the sandwich I proceeded to Popeyes for the sandwich. The wait was decent not too long but when I got to the window she told me the sandwich didn't come with blackened ranch sauce but I got 2 to go along with it. When I tell you this sandwich was so damn good I couldn't believe it. Y'all have to try this for yourself, it was so crunchy and had the right amount of spice. Would definitely pass these out at my wedding.

Finally tried the place after waiting for the kinks to be worked out.  We never go to a place when it first opens since it is usually inconsistent.
The drinks were good. Don't think they were over priced as others have mentioned and they are cheaper than places in Philly. The Whiskey list was larger than I have seen anywhere else in the burbs
The Poutine appetizer was ok. Wish it didn't have as much fat and the portion could have been slightly bigger. The Beet Salad was outstanding
The BBQ was top notch. The ribs were hot and the sauce was good. The Brisket was not fatty except for a spot on the top. When do you not find brisket with some fat on it. 
It could have had more sauce on it but the server got it for us. I also wanted to try the beef ribs my friend ordered but, there was none left to try. We will definitely be going back again and can't wait

One of those bars that accommodates a variety of crowds, well. Sports screens all over, but totally family-friendly, often see kids here. Fantastic beer list typically. Significant beer destination, actually. Great food. I have no idea what the haters are talking about. It is always busy, every day of the week.

So I'm not the type to complain about restaurants, but when I do it's when the service is just shit. The restaurant today, dinner time is very empty. Probably 10 people MAX are here. You'd sit and think, oh cool not busy so the service should be consistent? Nope, probably have seen our service at most like 2 times. Once for drinks and order, next was bringing plates. Because of the restaurant being so desolate I also was mistaken to have the thought of dishes being out quick too? Nope, probably 30 to 40 minutes later (for chicken tenders with mashed potatoes, and a burger with fries) we were given lukewarm food. The mashed potatoes weren't warm, completely stiff, the tenders very crunchy and once again not warm, and the burger not very warm but also not even cooked properly. If a place screws up the most basic meal, or even completely forgets your existence and not even a drink refill during the whole 40 minutes being here, then don't even bother. Also receiving the check and trying to leave and pay? Also a 15 minute obstacle. As there was no one at the front desk and because of the absence there was a line of 4 or 5 different people.
Great food and never unhappy. The hoagies and cheese steaks have plenty of quality meats and I know people who go out of their way to get the potato salad

Hands down the absolute worst Thai restaurant I've ever eaten at. I recently moved into the area and as my friends boasted about the authenticity of this restaurant , I thought I'd give it a try- that was not a good idea. I ordered the Pad Thai which I can undoubtedly say was the worst dish I've had at any restaurant. It was not properly cooked and radiated a disgusting stench. The service was non existent and when I asked the waiter about the preparation he did acknowledge my question. Later that night I became extremely ill. Save yourself the trouble and don't go!!!!

Many many, entirely too many shameful nights out with my gay besties are followed by brunch at Knock. My first apartment in Philadelphia was shared with five gay men and my life has never quite been the same since. Most straight girls would find themselves saying that they need a night with their "guys", for them that means throwing back a few beers and singing obnoxiously to Journey. In my world, a hangover is not even a question when you're downing Stoli O and club sodas listening to Britney's newest remix at Tavern. 

Many morning's after require a hair of the dog that bit you and what I need fast is something that will not only subside my body's alcohol withdrawal, but also replenish my vitamins...this place is home to the best bloody mary's I've found in the city. Not only do they make it with absolut peppar upon request, but they don't skimp on the celery and olives, my faves. 

Food is pretty tasty, more often than not I order a lunch item over a breakfast, usually because the thought of eggs disgusts me, however their french toast specials always sound fantastic. I love that they have outdoor seating so I can mask my puffy eyes with sunglasses and still people watch, aaaand if no one passes by at least you're guaranteed to have a hot waiter ;-)

I am in Morocco. I can hear the Call to Prayer and feel the dust on my face. The henna on my shoulder and taste the tajine. Saffron Cafe is the real deal.

Only two months after getting back from Morocco, my friend and I visited Saffron Cafe. The authenticity of this quaint restaurant nearly brought tears to my eyes. Even the bathroom reflects the culture with traditional Moroccan babouche shoes covering the walls.

Let's talk food. Being the soup and legume-obsessed goonie that I am - I had a hayday with the Harrira soup filled with chickpeas, cilantro, tomatoes and saffron rice. I also had some sort of side that included avocados and oranges - couldn't seem to find the name of this item on the online menu but it reminded me of the sliced oranges with cinnamon that we had at our riad in Marrakech. Again, real deal. Tajine! This is as close to Morocco as it gets. The Almond Chicken Tajine was amazing. That's what is so great about tajines, they have this mysterious way of achieving sweet and savory harmony in the best of ways...not to mention the adorable pot that they are cooked in. 

Last but not least. Dessert. I can't recall the specific name for it but don't let my lack of memory be a reflection of how glorious this sweet mascarpone cheesecake is.   

Good news fellow Indianapolitans! The next best thing to enjoying a meal in a riad in Morocco is located on Ft.Wayne Avenue in Downtown Indianapolis.

Nice find in a quiet area.. 

I've been here twice now when staying over locally.  Small place with an outside area.  The bar is rather long so there is plenty of room.  The two times I've been here it's been quiet but that's not a bad thing. 

Drinks: cold 
Food: very good
Service: good 

I will say that the wings here are excellent!  Non breaded buffalo is the way to go.
The worst, worst, worst service ever. A bunch of teenagers in charge if running the place, and they don't really care too. Never again!
The place was very clean. The staff was very friendly and took our large order 25 minutes before they were set to close. The food was amazing. I'll definitely be going back to try more menu items.

Very happy with our first two visits. We got the gyro platter on the first and the broasted chicken on the second. Both were priced well for the serving size and tasted good. We're yet to sit down and eat but the service during our take out orders were good. If they included coffee with their breakfast special I may have to find a reason to take the train from the Lansdowne train station.
Great iced coffees, huge cappuccinos, tons of flavored syrups to choose from. It's not a hipster coffee shop and it isn't a straight businessman coffee shop; it has a warm and welcoming vibe.

Came here late night with a group after a marathon drinking session. As the food was passed out to the table I immediately noticed how small an i ever cooked the burger patties looked. The table pretty much ordered burgers, chicken souvlacki, fries and onion rings. I've already described the burgers. Some of the fries were cold. The chicken souvlacki was meh. Pretty bland and stingy on the chicken. I don't even know how this

I had the vegetarian omlette and it was the best I ever had! The potatoes are like a cross between home fries and hashbrowns -- DELICIOUS! The staff was really friendly and the service was great. I will be back!

On a recent December day I traveled to the Range and partook in the Ozarks-themed burger. It was a bit smaller than I expected, but it was cooked perfectly and it tasted delicious. I passed on a milk shake but did indulge in a Charelville Whiskey-Scented Santa seasonal brew, which was phenomenal! My favorite part of the meal though was the ketchup. I know - I'm a weirdo - but it's homemade ketchup and I get really excited about that stuff. The house ketchup has an "apple butter" quality to it, which reminded me of my grandparents and the foods they made on the farm! The house-made beer mustard was pretty spectacular as well. I did share some ice cream with my fellow diners for dessert and found most of the flavors lacking the richness I prefer in ice creams. (I suppose they don't use heavy cream or eggs in their recipe?) My only real gripe with the Range is the noise level. It is really, really loud in there, and my fellow diners and I had to strain to hear each other. Worth it for the ketchup though.
This place has some awesome tacos! I got the surf n turf tacos. Blew my mind! My wife got the crab tacos. Those were crazy as well. We will be back had a great first experience. Def worth a stop in!

The food is amazing and the staff is helpful.  We have been going here since they opened in willow grove. The pho is great but the other dishes are equally as delicious. If you like this type of food.. definitely add this place to your list.

Absolutely lovely! Wasn't excited about my butternut squash & was presented with the best bass dish I've ever eaten! Restaurant was suddenly packed & was a long wait for dessert, but otherwise outstanding experience!
Yum,alpine cheese, beer, and dirty mussels! We were going to go to the city but glad we stayed local

Well, it is quite unfortunate that I have to do this. I loved this place, I really did. I have been about three times since my last review, and there always seemed to be some thing wrong from the order not being correct, the coffee being cold or tasting burnt, but the worst would be the fact that they served my wife regular toast when it was supposed to be gluten free! Any ways, enough with the vent here is the story of my most recent visit that signaled the end of my four star review.

We arrived on a busy weekend as usual, never minding the wait of course and figuring to give them one more shot before we wrote them off. The only place to sit was at the bar, we had not sat there before and it seemed like it would be fun to watch all the hustle and bustle. I could not have been more wrong. All of that delicious food that seems so healthy and fresh, its all a front. The potatoes and bacon sit on huge trays on top of the waffle irons, just sitting there until needed and then get tossed in to the microwave. The waffles are frozen, they take them and put them in to the waffle iron and the microwave to heat them. Do you get ice in your water? Well they scoop it out with an ice shovel and then throw it back in to the ice machine. Let me explain, the handle that they just had their hands all over is now all over YOUR ice. 

After watching this for a good half hour it is easy to say we had much less of an appetite, not to mention the sloppy un-showered appearance of the workers in front of us. If you have a relaxed appearance on work that is lucky for you! But please at least take a shower and try to comb out your hair. At least the woman that was barking out orders last time was much more subdued, although I find the constant appearance of her touching food while looking like she just ran a marathon in 100 degree weather extremely off putting. On a side note as well, yes they wear gloves, but I saw a few employees handle money or dirty dishes with said gloves and then go back to grabbing pastries or food!

Now when we finally did get our food, it was obvious to us that the bread was not gluten free. Gluten free any thing has a distinct look, and this looked the same as the toast on my plate. We advised one of the gals in front of us that it was not the gluten free and were promptly told without her even looking that we were wrong. Whether or not we were right or wrong (which we were right) does not matter, THE CUSTOMER IS ALWAYS RIGHT. My wife can not have gluten, it makes her extremely ill, but for others it can cause hospitalization. Its like giving nuts to some one that is allergic to them. Any ways, seeing as through those three visits things slowly became worse and then this, we will not be returning.
Better than any Asian restaurant we had while living in Tucson.  The pad tai was delicious & the food wasn't greasy. I really liked the BBQ fried rice too.  Will definitely go again.

If you want to take someone home for dinner but are unable to do so then this is the place to go. A place gleaming because it's so clean. A friendly warmth from all the people inside the owners, staff and other patrons. Trust them and let them guide you to an unforgettable meal. Comfort food that my father who just got out of the hospital craves. A delicious experience.  Look inside  then decide!

We came here for an early dinner. Could've gotten seated immediately, but had to wait until all of our party arrived. The place is busy! I'd walked past it a couple of times the previous days and the line went out to almost half a block! Inside, it is definitely cute. Their bar has an ancient pharmacy feel to it. Bright interiors.

Drinks were decent enough. My friends ordered margaritas, I ordered their German Riesling (wasn't too sweet, which I like). We chose the seafood okra gumbo because the server recommended that as 100%authentic. Because I love crab cakes and they had them on their specials list, we ordered them as an appetizer. My friends also ordered to chicken gumbo and a pasta. Everything was simply delicious! 

If you like okra, the seafood gumbo is definitely worth a try. I don't understand why they put a whole small crab in there though. I am not very good at eating crabs, so ended up leaving most of it in the plate. My fellow diners did the same.

The crab cakes were delicious. The sauce they came with was good, but maybe put a little less salt on the sauce so that the whole thing does not become too salty. 

The pasts was heaven!! We ended up finishing all of our portions, so I think thats a win. 

Recommend this place- get here around 5 pm before the crowd gets in :)

I came here for restaurant week and I was so excited because I've been wanting to try it for such a long time. I heard mixed reviews about the food and I wanted give it a chance and see for myself. So glad I did. We got there and decided to not even order off the restaurant week menu because so many of the lunch options looked good. We shared the filet mignon cheesesteak as an appetizer because I couldn't go here and no try it. I'll just say, they made philly proud with that one! For entrees we shared the baked crabmeat stuff flounder and horseradish crusted halibut. For the halibut I did switch out the chili sauce for lemon butter and the broccoli rabe for asparagus due to my own personal preferences. I think it is probably a success either way. The only downside is the fish was under seasoned on both dishes. Don't get me wrong, they were cooked to perfection and I even enjoyed the lemon butter sauce, but a little salt would have bought out the flavor especially with the halibut being a breaded dish. In their defense it is possible when you order it with the sweet Thai sauce it all comes together, but then the flounder was under seasoned as well. However, such good food and drinks. It's a bit formal but very well impressive and sleek decor. If youre looking for something more causal they do have a separate outdoor area, but they may have different menus. All in all its worth a visit.

Well, this is our 5th time dining here! NO need to go anywhere else for Italian fare! I had the mushroom risotto. And a side salad, both which were great! Tasty risotto, clean and smoothie with rich overtones with the mushrooms. . My husband had the risotto as well, but added shrimp which was outstanding! Next time I will be getting that! He also had oysters R, and he lived it! Now last but not least here...I've got to announce that they serve THE BEST family made spumoni. I'm quite certain sonny said it was a family recipe. Correct me if I'm mistaken. Anyway...omg. This ice cream had very prominent flavors and real fruit and pistachios. And cinnamon!!! SO delicious! It took me right to fall and Christmas as soon As I tasted it. I had another scoop, it was THAT GOOD! SO, once again, YOU knock it out of the park! We will see you again soon! Blessings! Thankyou.
My wife and I stop at Riverwinds whenever we are in the area. Great place, great food and great service, especially Shauna. She has to be the best bartender in South Jersey.

3.5 stars. The food is comforting and savory. Crab & corn chowder is particularly flavorful, the kind of thing you want to just keep eating. 

Service is friendly and low-key. Environment is definitely casual--a few TVs, but it's a good place to take kids. 

The bad: We ordered an apple tart for dessert. It was baked in a cast iron skillet that hadn't been seasoned properly, so there was black, metallic-tasting residue on half of it. The weird thing: Our server said he'd get it taken off the bill, and it was, but apparently the manager wouldn't let him take it off, and he'd bought it for us. Not sure why the manager thought serving metal-coated apples was something we--or anyone--ought to pay for. (We tipped big.) It was an odd way to end what otherwise was a perfectly satisfying meal. 

Despite that, I would come back. It's reasonably priced, tasty, and easy to get to.

My husband and I went here for lunch. We enjoyed our time here. The food was cool. Different form my normal choice. The staff was very polite. Its a very casual vibe. 

While we were her there was a live band playing blues. It was so awesome. They even pulled me on stage to participate and sing happy birthday to me. I loved that. I would go here again!
Love this place--been several times!! Great beer, food, and entertainment--love their IPAs especially the chocolate ipa and their cheese curds are to die for!

I order with the Grubhub app. They never sent me a text when the food was supposedly delivered. I called the restaurant they delivered to the wrong address  and wouldn't refund my money. Will never get food from this place.

Small place, big flavors!! We started with the chili tots. My husband loved them, saying they were the best thing he's eaten all vacation. I ordered the Blackhawk burger I never thought of buffalo chicken ontop of a burger patty but it was tasty!! The side of sweet potato fries were on point as well. The pencil fries are nothing to write home about but my husband loved his don Carlo burger with hot sausage. Our only negative comment was the things that were labeled "spicy or hot" were not very spicy...but we like our stuff hot. Would most definitely return when in the area.

Definitely not the Acme I grew up with as a kid growing up in NOLA. The manager, Leslie was so cold and rude we left and went across the street and went to Felix's. Much better experience start to finish. I will NEVER refer Acme to anyone again.

Well that was not good. I used to come here to get my fix of Southern Food back when I was in college here in Philly. It was awesome. But those days are gone. 
I ordered the Special, Scotch Eggs. They were over cooked. Hard as rocks. And cold. Really? The manager stopped by to ask how my eggs were with a smile on his face and I told him not so great. He said he noticed but shrugged. Asked if he could do anything else for me. I asked for more coffee and the water I never got. All with a smile on my face because I just find it better to interact that way. I got that but nothing else. He seemed indifferent to the fact my breakfast was awful. 
To top it off, my waitress was nearly nonexistent but I did catch her smash down the trash with her bare hands right in front of me, rub her nose, flick her hair, and then go make toast and place biscuits on plates. I've been here at the counter 30 minutes and she still hasn't cleaned her hands that were in the GARBAGE! 
Never coming back. 
And not that I was looking for a free breakfast but I didn't. Oh well.
Great choice of  craft  beer  on tap!  And lots of TV screens  all over. Appetizer  are  greasy.
Always friendly service and their pastries are great. The buttercake is probably my favorite, followed by the woopie pies they always have.

This was our first time at South Philly Italian Kitchen - and we will definitely be back! The food was delicious and it felt like a friend was cooking you a good meal. 

We had the pleasure of meeting the owner, Joe, who was attentive and enthusiastic. He encouraged us to try his homemade mozzarella (which we got with roasted red peppers) and it was SO good. 

My partner ordered the chicken parmesan and loved it. Well seasoned, crispy crust, and served with gnocchis. I got the gnocchi and thought it was great!

We can't wait to return for another great meal or order takeout. Thanks to Joe and his staff!

I was so excited to come here..like really excited...and it did not live up to my expectations at all. From the outside, it looks like a big, fun honky tonk. On the inside, it was just meh. The music wasn't that great, the drinks were overpriced and not made very well.

   There is a mechanical bull that's five dollars to ride up on the top floor, which is probably the best thing about this place. Honestly, the only reason I'd ever come back is if I just want to listen to the live music, or maybe try the food.

   There wasn't a cover when I went , but I was told by a local that there normally is. With most of the other bars being free to get into, I wouldn't step near this place if I knew I had to pay for a mediocre experience.

We had a private room booked for about 20 people as we have done successfully for several years. All 20 of us arrived; they had our reservation but no rooms to offer "due to a mistake"; tried to crowd us into a room with 2 other large noisey private parties in progress where everyone would have been exceptionally crowded.  The front desk guy asked me if "we were all over 21"---our group is all in their 70's.
Huge disappointment, as we have enjoyed George's in prior years. We left and scrambled to find another place.

We had dinner here tonight and was very disappointed in the food and service. We were a party of 6..reasonable we thought. We needed to ask the waitress for every single we needed...plates, napkins, silverware for our apps...salt a pepper, napkins, sugar..everything. They brought a small carafe of water to the table...after asking 3 times...clearly not enough for 6 people. We needed to keep bringing the carafe inside for refills. The food took a long time to be prepared and was not worth the wait. Every plate had the wrong sides on it. The fried chicken was very good. The salmon arrived cold and overdone. To add insult ...an 18% gratuity was added...not unexpected with our size party but aggravating with such poor service. Did not enjoy our meal and will not go back!

We are from Jersey and this by far is the closest we have found to delicious pizza in Florida. They definitely have a great selection of Italian food. The staff is very nice amd helpful. We go every Friday night for pizza and garlic knots they are to die for.

Being from Jersey I was both skeptical and critical of this location.  We tried and it and I have to say if you're looking for what NY/NJ style pizza tastes like, this is the place to go.  The sauce and cheese were outstanding, the crust was good, but that's something you can't get in the midwest.  The place also had all of the Jersey fav's taylor ham and zeppoles.  The restaurant itself was also great, the owner actually grew in the same town I'm from strangely enough.  She was really nice and prices were right on target.  It misses the 5th star for 2 reasons, one the taylor ham was way over cooked, but still good.  Second the crust still wasn't from jersey and just didn't meet the standard.
Very good food and service.  We went for Sunday brunch at 1 o'clock and the place was full yet we received excellent service. We will be back.
Fabulous pizza! Very friendly servers. The food comes out fast. Will definitely be back

For almost $10 you can get a full plate of food!  I do wish they would give more chicken than they already do. But what are you going to do.

Great place to get food if you are hungry and want a quick bite to eat.

I had a good experience with the service here and they gave hearty portion sizes. I was not a fan of what I had ordered but I would be open to trying something different next time. The flavor of the yellow curry was pretty good I just could not eat a lot of this food since it is not what I am used to. The mild still had a strong kick when it hits the back of your throat so beware if you do not like spicy.

Great service with fast seating. Reservation recommended, however. Great ambiance with Jazz music and blue light. Place has an amazing 360 degree view of the city skyline and the outside floor spins around while you're sitting to get an entire view at all times. If you have motion sickness I would recommend sitting in the middle of the restaurant. Food was delicious according to my friends. Not vegetarian friendly, however so I just got the bruschetta, a side of asparagus, and a side of rice. The bruschetta was really good but the rice and asparagus lacked a  bit of taste. My friends ordered the escargot which they stated was 'amazing.' They also ordered the cheese platter which they enjoyed. They also ordered seared Ahi Tuna and crab ravioli. All comments were very positive.
ALWAYS GREAT SERVICE & FOOD.  Oysters are small but always taste good.  Trout from Idaho is especially sweet as are the biscuits.

It was the first time I had eaten here.  The food was really good, the meats tender and flavorful.  They also had a meeting space in the back that can accommodate around 20-25 people. The meeting room is separate and away from the main restaurant.  Our Lion's Club had an event there and everyone loved how quiet it was to meet.  Definitely coming back and looking at perhaps moving our Club meeting place to here.

Excited to have Small Mart in the neighborhood I frequent. Its a great place for vegans and vegetarians but I being neither its a great way to get extra veggies in my diet. The stars here are the bagels which are legit NYC bagels, oh how I wish they offered breakfast sandwiches with those. They also offer a great daily curry for $6. Small Mart is good but for what it is its a bit on the expensive side. Even the $6 curry is more of a side dish than a meal but if you are a light eater and and vegan/vegetarian this is your spot.

I love Charley's Chicken Philly sandwiches and have consumed them in mall food courts from Rochester to Honolulu.

My wife and I tried this Charley's in the Westfield Countryside Mall two weeks ago.  She had a small Chicken Buffalo, soda and fries combo for $6.99, and I just ordered a "regular" Chicken Philly for $7.99.  I then ate most of her fries (at her request, of course) and had a couple of sips from her soda.

I found my sandwich to be up-to-par with the Chicken Phillies I have enjoyed at other locations.  The fries were good too.

One thing I have noticed in the last couple of years is that Charley's have started including a thin slice of dill pickle in the Chicken Philly. (They haven't always done this.) I don't like the pickle slice but it was easy to pull it out of the sandwich with my fingers.  I need to start remembering to say "hold the pickle" when I order.
Food was ehhh. The atmosphere was AMAZING. Worth the trip to just hang out and have a few drinks.

This is such a great restaurant with beautiful ambience. It's perfect for when you're craving homestyle food but you want a beautifully plated meal as well. Also I definitely recommend getting a cocktail if you enjoy drinking. It's a really nice venue for a date night or dinner with friends.

Im just writing this as a way to contact the owner. I come here at least once a week for the past 2 years. I've come to know and recognize the staff who've been here awhile and they've always been amazing to me. I love the drinks, If anyone comes here for coffee its great 10/10

However, after coming here for years this is the first time I've seen toxicity among staff and it made me uncomfortable enough to post here about it. I've been sitting on the couch doing usual coffee shop work and  for the past hour plus I just hear the staff speak so rudely to each other and about guests. For example, one just started talking about a woman in the drive through saying "she comes here a lot, i don't like her though" and then went on a rant about why she doesn't like her. This woman wasn't the only customer that the staff had rude things to say about, this was just the most recent one that pushed me to write this. They also clearly don't speak to each other respectfully as I heard one of them yell at the others for not rinsing the blender right away saying to them "its literally not that hard like just do it." I used to manage a coffee shop and I know I would have never wanted to hear my staff talk to each other this way and I especially wouldn't want to hear staff talk about customers this way.

First off, service was perfect (Valerie) and the menu is vast - featuring all the classics you would expect at a pizza, pasta, sandwich family restaurant.... but then - there are "bistro-esque" small plate offerings like fig crostini and white bean brushetta to add interest.

I have antipasto chopped salad that was tasty and my son had chicken parm panini which was more like a hoagie.  He liked the sandwich although he prefers more sauce.  His crinkle cut french fries -- I don't think I have ever seen them served in a restaurant north of the Mason Dixon line -- were phenomenal!!  Go figure! 

Pizza was good, but not my favorite pizza ever, but I can see how so many people like it.
Just had the best early bird Mahi Mahi lunch with great drinks! We will be back again soon!

Unfortunately it was exactly what I had assumed being a Moxie's restaurant. Menu with way too many items for any of them to be extremely well executed. 

If you enjoy the other Moxie's or places with a huge menu like the mega restaurants of Chilis or Cheesecake Factory you'll probably like it. Disappointing because the interior is quite nice and it is an addition to an area of town with not a whole lot of good restaurants. I will not be back as everything we had I can make at home better. Easily. 

Too bad they didn't decide to compete with actual good local restaurants than crappy national chain restaurants. Maybe that's the clientele they want.

This store is just as winded and useless as it's Broad Street counterpart, except filled with more annoying yuppies in suede jackets and three hundred dollar haircuts...must be the neighborhood.

Unless you are into the latest fake-wanna-be-Buddhist self help book or the latest on Barack Obama they are utterly useless. It's a shame because I use to love riding my bike over to Rittenhouse,  grabbing a coffee and browsing what's new. Now whenever you ask for help finding something the staff either:

                 1. Gives you "the look" - like, ew why do you want that?
                 2. Gives you "the sigh" - like you're actually going to make me 
                      work, huh? I hate the stairs, even though they're electric. 
                 3. Give you the wrong section to look under, then you have to 
                      start all over again.

Sorry dude, it's your fucking job to help me so just stop flirting with that waif in the Prada jeans and direct me where I actually need to go. 

B&N is one of those bookstores that you can wander in for days trying to impress yourself with your Renaissance man type knowledge  in a hundred genres but when it comes to looking for something specific you're screwed. No one has ever offered to order a book for me, even though  it is quite obvious that they do so for other people since the "book search" shows, "Oh, that's a special order for someone." Well maybe I'd like to order a copy for myself now wouldn't I? No, actually I wouldn't - I'll just ride back down to Head House where the staff is actually helpful.

The basil fried rice and Thai basil meals are both exceptional. Portion sizes could be a little bigger but I'm a giant so take that with a grain of salt. This is my new go to restaurant when I want Asian flavors. Love having them in the area. 

I have to say that I found the pad Thai to be disappointing, but Thai basil rice and basil fried rice were both great. Especially basil fried rice. Spectacular. Get it.

Top Golf is good for group events, casual gatherings & some interactive fun with friends and family. Valet available. 

By all means if you are a serious golfer this may not the practice type range for you. It's designed more for fun and interactive occasions. I see it more as a way to make golf approachable & fun with food, alcohol & DJ && a dance floor. 

The service was pretty good given we went for an event & they were extremely busy. We ordered some appetizers and dessert while spending time with friends & practicing my swing! 

The food however was just average at best. Ordered a couple of their appetizers and dessert it was recommended to us and had to send the sushi roll looking appetizer back: it was not good. The rest was just ok. The cocktails were not made with fresh ingredients and were made with super sugary syrup type mixes.

My girlfriend and I were disappointed. We'd been wanting to go for some time and we finally went today. The food, admittedly, was at least somewhat tasty. But it was not worth the price. Especially not at the portions given. But what really got to us was the poor service. Almost everyone in the shop looked pissed to just be there and they weren't nice at all while taking our order. Maybe it was just a bad day, but we aren't keen on going back. Sorry to say that. We really wanted to like it.

Never had Yunnan rice noodle soup before,  so this experience was all new for me.

I've had the original soup and I've also had the fish with sour cabbage soup, and I must say the latter was far superior. It was a taste I'd never quite experienced before, and a bowl I will come back for. Don't be afraid of the title; contrary to its name it is neither stinky nor pungent. The fish is tender and mild and the sour cabbage adds a nice little zing and crunch. The broth is the true winner, though. They use some kind of chili oil and the overall flavor is very deep and comforting. I hear the pickled pepper one uses the same broth.

I would skip the original; it's very similar to your typical hot pot broth.

As others have said, they don't accept cards, but they do take cash, venmo, and wechat.
This place is the bomb!!  Great folks, food, big screens everywhere.  Prices are probably the only problem, but whatever, its worth it!

My wife and I stopped by here for lunch today. We have been to the Meridian location but not this one Boise downtown and decided to try it. It's on the 2nd floor of the 8th and Main building, and has a classy, upscale yet casual look inside. We were greeted warmly and shown to one of the tables located next to the best feature: floor to ceilings windows overlooking 8th Street. I believe they open them in nice weather as well. They have a bar that has a couple tv's (extra points for having hockey on!) that looked like a nice place for a casual drink.

We each got the Pick Two lunch combo, intending to share so we could taste 4 dishes. My wife got the lemonade which she said was delicious, and I ordered iced tea which more water than tea. 

The first combo was the Tomato Bisque Soup and Chicken Portobello Sandwich. I am not a tomato soup fan really, but my wife loves it. In the interest of my fellow Yelpers I took one for the team to taste it. It is creamy but not too heavy, and tastes of tomatoes and herbs. It's not bad and the texture is fine- just not my favorite. She did finish it all however! The sandwich was not my top fave, mainly because it was a good 85% thick bread. Awkward to eat, very little filling (I would not have been able to identify a single ingredient if I hadn't read the menu description) and to me very dry. Again, my wife seemed to find it better than I do, but she also generally enjoys bread products more than I do. 

The second combo was the Tuscan Chicken Pizza (it comes as a "pizzette" or individual little one in the combo) and the Chicken Arugula Salad. The pizza was delicious. The crust has the signature wood fired taste, the toppings were in good relation to the pizza. It was a touch dry and had I had a sauce to dip it into I just might have. The salad was fresh and well balanced and the dressing was delicious. My only annoyance is one I have with many restaurants- cut your ingredients to at least somewhat fit on a fork! When you are trying to eat salad and every piece is so big you can't fit it in your mouth and it's a mess, it drives me crazy. It doesn't have to be a chopped salad but just some simple cuts to make it more manageable, especially at a place where business lunches are common (end lettuce rant).

The service was good. Our server knew the menu, was very polite and helpful when asked to place an ingredient on the side, and seemed friendly and sincere. Lunch didn't take a long time to get to us, but we lost our server after the food came and he focused elsewhere. It was quite a while before he got back to us and we had to request the check and a box (I couldn't finish my combo). All told, lunch took 55 minutes, which isn't horrible but is cutting it close as I was on a work lunch break. Bill was $28 for the two combos and two beverages, so a bit pricey for an everyday lunch spot but a good "once in a while" or "special" option. 

Overall it's a nice little lunch spot and the service was good, the place was clean and inviting, and the food was solid. I would love to see a few more options on the pick two menu geared towards a stronger protein base- like some of the meatball or prawn appetizers maybe, or just a grilled chicken breast with the toppings maybe. I suppose I could try ordering a sandwich without the bread but it isn't the same thing usually as an option that is actually meant to stand alone. I'd happily pay a bit of a "up charge" for a solid, lunch protein option in the Pick Two line up.

I've always liked this restaurant but was disappointed recently. The servers lack of English hampers their ability to describe the foods on special. I ordered a Japanese Burito from the specials board. It was good but was maybe a scoop full of fish on huge rice crackers. When I asked the manager about the size he said it was "appetizer" portion. The bill for this was $13.25!   My partner's dinner of salt and pepper shrimp was $15 there were 6 medium sized prawns.  Not a satisfying experience.

Stopped in last Friday night for a quick bite.Our server Sasha was so nice and provided great service.We ordered the cauliflower,burger and surf and turf.Food was very good.Not the same old bar food.I also had a moonshine mule that was VERY good. Atmosphere was fun.Friday nights is karaoke nice crowd. Definitely will return

What a great find! Big menu and great, seriously great! Prices! Staying at a resort where bagels and coffee are like $15 - this place has good, home-cooking breakfasts. Also went there for dinner and got my veggie burger just the way I wanted at a great price! Good ambiance, great happy hour! Must go again!!!!
Charming, pleasant, and absolutely delicious! Make a reservation for the patio. Just lovely!!

First time here and it had some ups and some downs. I'm a self-proclaimed Mexican-food connoisseur and love street tacos so I was told to check this place out. 
The chips and guacamole were some of the best I've ever had and that includes places in Mexico. Great avocado base with pico and shredded cheese on top. 9/10

2 salsas - one kind of smoky and mild-had better flavor than the "spicy" salsa which wasn't very hot at all. Nothing special about either but decent and the chips have such a great yield and saltiness that we went  through both salsas. 6/10

I tried two of the street tacos which are small but filled high with various meets, toppings, and sauces. I had the chicken which was delicious with a BBQ base and mango topping and the carne asada which had impressive cuts of flank steak. Only problem was that they only offered corn tortillas which ruined the taste for me. I'm not sure why they don't offer flour as an option but these tacos are probably very good if u enjoy corn tortillas.  6/10....would b an 8/10 if flour. 

Atmosphere is lively and enjoyably open-air with a couple bar TVs to catch the Cards game. 8/10.

Service 9/10.  Hostess and waitress were friendly and helpful and even got a couple hellos from support staff. 

Overall 7/10 or 3.5 stars which isn't an option here.

The food is organic, gluten free, and delicious! The atmosphere is quaint and charming, and we found the owner and crew to be warm, friendly, and very helpful. My husband and I are so happy to have discovered this little vegan  gem!

Looking at the menu, the prices may seem a little high, which is due to the quality of the ingredients used in the dishes. Anyone who tries to cook like this at home, can definitely relate!

On this visit, we had the tofu scramble with pancakes, along with a green smoothie, both were really good - and the pancakes didn't have that odd texture that often comes with gluten free foods.

This is my new Saturday morning tradition!

We went there for her first time a few weeks ago, and got the pistachio gelato. This was not pistachio you would expect, it is salty like an actual pistachio! It is absolutely delicious! I don't know about anything else that they have here because this is all we've tried, but I highly recommend it!! And ask for Angelo, a real sweetheart!
Ordered delivery from here with door dash. Do NOT eat here. I found a maggot in my food.

I guess that I'm alone in my ambivalence about Yats. Granted, it's been awhile since I've been here, so I may need to give it a second try. But when I did visit, I recall feeling underwhelmed. Having been to New Orleans pre-Katrina (and having fallen madly in love with it), I have high standards for my Cajun food, and I found Yats to be kind of...mushy, honestly. It just lacked a certain snap and bite. 

I do appreciate the punkish staff, though, and any place that posts as many flyers for local events as Yats does earns bonus points from me. So I think another visit is in order.

This place was so welcoming and friendly. The food was delicious (and cheap: home fries, biscuit, eggs) and the coffee was tasty. Omelette was good too. Convenient place on the way to a conference and fast service. This place is not fancy but it's great in other ways. I definitely recommend it.
Great sandwiches and pastries here, but I always get soup. My favorite is the baked potato. Friendly staff, always busy. Wonderful lunch spot.
If you don't mind a wait this is the place for breakfast food.  Delicious omelets and milkshakes!  Small and elbow to elbow, but the cooks make you feel right at home.  Definitely worth the wait!

The hubby loved the concept and I loved the pricing. It's subway for pizza. You choose your pizza then the toppings and it's all ready for you freshly baked in a wood oven in 5 minutes for under $10. 

I ordered the pesto pizza with tomatoes and artichokes (next time I will probably add some sort of meat). My hubby ordered the margherita with sausage. 

The pizzas were ready in about 5 minutes time and there were plenty of places to sit down. We loved that this place was family friendly but also great for couples, friends, etc. 

They serve beer, wine, and a pretty nifty soda machine that has a gazillion options. 

Great option for college students or young families, everyone gets exactly what they want. If you are expecting gourmet pizza this is not, but for the price, it's well worth a visit.

I thought L and C was supposed to be a "nicer" dining experience? Food was slow on this Monday Memorial Day afternoon. Waiter seemed aggravated and more intent on half sweeping around us at 330 pm. Food was bland and boring. This place looks dingy and unkempt. Disappointed. :(

This is a plesant little cafe in an unassuming strip mall. It has been upgraded, apparently, with help of Restaurant Impossible. The food we had--full belly clams, Mediteranean fish (cod), and a sandwich and fires, were all good. Huge portion of clams and very tasty. Prices were fair I would say. This is not a dive but also not a real upscale place. It's the type of place that can probably do a few things well, but may suffer a bit because of location. However, if eating good food is a priority and not necessarily sitting seaside (and paying extra for that), then this could be a good call.

Small point: a side salad with the entrees would be nice. There was plenty of room on the plate with my fish and potatoes.

Their food is pretty good thought their tastes are on a sweeter spectrum. This is common on most Asian-fusion restaurants. This place offers a good mix of regional Asian cuisine. Ambiance is relaxing and the decor is rather pretty. Wait staff is friendly and responsive. Considering it's a Friday evening, the food items were served relatively fast. Now, only if they offer boba teas. Will definitely revisit again.

Awesome burgers and shakes.  I was stunned that this little place tucked into the Paoli shopping center was that good!  The burgers are super moist, I've been ordering mine with delicious, sweet, fried onions and tomoatoes, They're so juicy and tasty.  In addition the buns are from Le Bus and they are fantastic.  The shakes are big, smooth and real -- real, hardcore, creamy ice cream.  Don't know what brand ice cream they're using but it's excellent

Okay---
So---heres the scoop:
Better half and I decided to eat here for lunch the other day because he had a gift certificate he had gotten from work--
We got there around 11:45ish and we were seated promptly-
We both ordered beers, and water--- took a few minutes to get our beers-- which i dont understand bc there was no one in there....
We were offered an order of complimentary flash fried spinach---
I really cant even put into words how odd this dish is--
It was weird----and I wouldnt order it if i had to pay for it--and we hardly ate any of it to begin with.....i dont even know really...... 
Ick....just weird...like something from outter space or something.
Seriously.
My honey had the chicken salad and he loved it--- he said it was some of the best he's had--however...it DID have TONS of celery-- and I HATE celery..GROSS.
but if you happen to like celery then you might possibly like that---
I ordered the strawberry and goat cheese salad that had grilled chicken on it--
it was good.... nothing that stood out to me, but it was good..... 
We still have money left so we'll be back---other than that, Im not sure---
There are tons of other stellar restraurants around closer to work, but maybe if we are in the area.......
The ambiance seemed---uppity--maybe it was just me---
Who knows---just whatever you do, dont order the stuff from outerspace.

I must give it 4 stars, as I keep coming back.  Blueberry Hill is one of my favorite burgers in the city (O'Connel's; 5 -Star; Flemings happy hour, and I used to like a Mike Duffy's burger).  

We are in a stretch of weather that is delicious, therefore lunch outdoors was a must today.  Order the larger of the burgers, medium rare and choose your cheese.   I selected the "lump" of soft cheddar and spread it out along with a basket of fries.  The fries were great and sitting outside on Delmar in the Loop is a STL thing to do!  

And great service on the patio even though it was very busy.  Thank you.  

Go!

And Joe Edwards (owner and OWNER of the Loop) is always around and eating his own cooking for lunch.  Impressive.

Service was just ok. The waitress seemed very uninterested in her job. Food was pretty good. The beignets were sort of blah to me. We tried the ravioli, ribeyes, and brisket. The brisket was pretty tender for TN brisket. The ribeye was prob the best ribeye I've ever had which it better be for $40. The ravioli was good but just ravioli so didn't knock my socks off. We also had the cornbread which was pretty amazing. They could def improve on the ambiance. Def not rustic chic if that's what they are going for. The lighting in the place is terrible actually. They need some updates.  Prob won't go again.

I am frequently in the area around this restaurant, wanting to stop by for a cup of tea or coffee, or just find a place to hang out for a while and chat with friends.  We often eat at Jules Thin Crust, and this place is right next door.  I wish I could find more here that I like, but it just doesn't speak to me.

The inside of this place is cute, and there's a pleasant patio outside (although it does look out on a vast expanse of parking lot).  But it seems to appeal to an older audience, and one with a bit more money to drop than me, and with slightly different tastes.

This place has a little market area with a number of retail items for sale.  The prices are very high and there's nothing that really strikes me as unique or something that I really want to get and can't get elsewhere.  I could see buying high-quality loose-leaf tea in a place like this, but the tea selection doesn't impress me; it's all stuff I can get elsewhere for cheaper.  And in spite of the name suggesting cheese, I don't see any cheeses that really grab my attention either.  Across the way is Trader Joe's, which has an outstanding and cheap cheese selection, so if this place wants to draw me in with cheese it needs to either offer low priced cheese, or truly unique artisan cheeses.

The people who work here are pretty nice, but the place is usually really busy.  They seem to be doing really well without me so maybe it's just not my place.

Oh, as one final note, the company's website doesn't have any useful information (like hours, menu, etc.).  It's just a flash-only photo gallery...that seems a big no-no, if you are going to own your own domain name, at least put up your business name, address, and hours, at a bare minimum!

What type of breakfast restaurant has a line out the door on a Thursday at 1030a?  A great one.  We almost left because we didn't want to bear the cold, but the line moved rather quickly and it was worth it.

I ordered the dish called the Lindstrom, which is shaved Brussel sprouts with parmesan and a lemon vinaigrette.  It was so tasty.  Of course, I had to have a biscuit as well, which was basically a cake without icing on it , it was so good.  Everyone else in the party had dishes with biscuits and all of us were happy.

The place is really cute too.

Don't be dissuaded by the line.  The food is worth it.

The lady at the counter is a blast of sunshine!!! Much needed on a slow morning :)

I got an iced Irish coffee: I know that's not special for NOLA, but in the rest of the country getting a nice drink at an organic bakery is unheard of. I also ordered an almond filled cinnamon roll. Like an almond croissant but in a cinnamon roll?!?! Amazing! I also bought a croissant- yes I do carb overload sometimes- and it was nearly perfection. A little small, but crisp, flaky and buttery the way croissants are supposed to be! I had one yday that tasted like unsalted white bread lol! I think it's the labor and use of ingredients but it's hard to find a 'real' croissant! Breads on Oak has the real!

Great spot! I'd definitely come back again... and again... and... again

Right in downtown Nashville so get ready to pay for parking if you want to eat here. The place was nice and our server was good. As for the food for the price it could of been better. It wasn't anything mind blowing or anything. We had the fried oysters steam bun and there was 2 for $11 with one oysters in each bun. Not really worth it to me even though it was good. Waitress said the chicken and waffles was the best she's had but I had way better. Its a cool spot to hang out and watch a good game or something and drink with a big group. They also had bogo mimosas as well. Wish they had parking bc I hate paying for parking especially after spending money on food and drinks.

Have been to this location a number of times.  While there is a mask mandate for the city, this location neither requires their employees to wear masks properly nor can they ask a customer to wear a mask.  I have been told twice that this directive comes for corporate.  In a city where the vaccination rate is below 45%, there policy needs changing.  Just today, a customer was blowing her nose at the ordering counter with no mask and no tissue - just her hand to wipe her nose with.  No employee was wearing a mask properly - all were below their noses.  I have written to their guest relations department at corporate and get the same canned response that they care about their customers, et al, but no changes have occurred.

Went for buffet with my husband after our grocery shopping in Bensalem! Buffet had plenty of choices! Service was good place seemed little cramped! And they do charge for naan extra which is surprise to me but overall we had good meal!
