I give them a 1 star only because 0 is not an option! 
So here is my experience with them; 
I can't get there in person so I call to make a delivery order. After 4 calls someone finally answers and says "thank you for calling 3 countries, how can I help you?" 
I tell him I want to make an order for delivery. He then tells me "we are closed". So I get a little upset because according to their menu says they are open. He puts someone different on the phone who tells me the same thing. However, he also says they are busy and that is why they can't take an order.

Just a little advise. If you are going to print "to-go" menu's that say you deliver and hand them out at businesses for customers to order your product and then tell a customer that you are closed when the menu and your website both say you are open, you need to really learn how to operate a business.

My sincere hope is that you never get another customer until you know how to properly operate a business.

Robert T.

I was in there yesterday, and was really stunned at their lackluster customer service.  I made a very simple request, the employee told me they'd get around to it eventually.  I stood there and waited for 5 minutes like an idiot while my pizza got cold, and then asked another employee if he could help me.

He told me they had forgotten to prep, and he'd get around to it eventually.  I then just left as there was no sign I was ever going to be helped.

TLDR: if you know you strictly just want pho, go to Pho 75. 

Cash only. Previous reviewers were right in describing the ambiance to something like a cafeteria. Very noisy and hot during the summer time. The pho is cheap, a small is like $7.10 and a large is like $7.65; it also comes out within a minute of ordering and was scalding hot. However, the quality is meh. Bean sprouts and basil were not crispy or fresh either. The broth is clear of grease, but it had a darker color too it. Also wondered whether it had msg because it was very savory. This place has a good assortment of rice dishes, and offers spring and summer rolls too. Overall, I think Pho 75 just does it better.

We stumbled on Mamma Mia when we were actually trying to find another restaurant in the area with the same name.  Oddly enough we looked up Carlucci's Grill and were going to go to another restaurant due to the reviews and we found that the place mats and wrapper around the napkin all were labeled as Carluccis Grill.  I am not sure if Carluccis bought this location, but if they did it would be better to stick to one brand name so people aren't confused.

About the experience
We went in and were seated immediately.  A waitress came out to take our drink order quickly and bring some bread to the table.  During the whole time we were there the service was excellent.  All three of the people in the party ordered Chicken Parmesan and shared some mozzarella sticks.  The mozzarella sticks came out in about 6 minutes and were tasty. The bread basket included a couple different types of bread: bread shaped like fat bread sticks, which was average at best and bread with  tomato sauce,which was really delicious. 

The meals came out in about 15-20 minutes from ordering and were hot.  My chicken parm didn't have any real sauce on top.  I think it was under the cheese.  The chicken tasted good, but was very thin for my preference.  Overall the food was good, but didn't blow me away, but was solid in a pinch.  For me, the best part about this place was the service.  I may go back if I am in the Oxford Valley Mall area.
They have pretty good food & REALLY good drinks. :) Live music is a little on the loud side.

I've been going to Vietnam for years - and I consistently get the same 3 things (having been around the menu a few times):

- Chargrilled pork rolls 

- Shrimp wonton and noodle soup

- The House Special----awesome

They let you share their soups if you have a party of two. Good times are had by all.

The food, service, and atmosphere were great.  The waitress and staff took good care of my family.  Chargrilled oysters were some of he best I have had in New Orleans.  We had fried shrimp which were plump and plentiful.  Bread pudding was do to die for.  I would highly recommend a visit you would be pleased.

Happy hour oysters and beer! It looks like the wait can get long, especially during happy hour.  But they also have an open seating area right near the bar and it was just our luck that a table for 2 opened up right as we got to the hostess stand. That definitely saved us from the 30-45 minute wait. The happy hour menu is pretty decent and you could fill up on that alone. I also wanted to try the cioppino so that I could dip more of their delicious bread into.

Good sushi spot we found through yelp!.. definitely a hidden gem.

Oh....the FREE mini KitKat was a bonus!!
Really cold beer,  Really bad bar food,  and pretty good scenery!  Don't sit in the booth by the bathroom.  Try to sit at the bar.

I used to LOVE this place but as of recently the service has gotten worse the chefs less interactive and the way they seat you is annoying ... why would you seat a 2 11 yr old boys next to an old woman and man enjoying a night on the town. This poor elderly couple looked so excited to be there until the bratty boys annoyed them the whole time by being spoiled brats and the mother wouldn't control them. The food is still the best the atmosphere has just gone down hill.

Seamus McDaniel's in Dogtown is a St. Louis staple.  There is a small parking lot in the back and street parking all around.  

Walk into Seamus McDaniel's and immediately feel at ease.  From single diners to large groups, Seamus has a seat for you.  There is bar seating, table seating, booth seating, and even patio/enclosed patio seating depending the time of year.

I recommend the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich or Burgers.  Ranch is King at Seamus; you must try their homemade Ranch Dressing.  Fries dipped in Ranch Dressing are a total win.  Caramelized Onions make the burgers that much better.  I will be back soon.

Was excited to go here after reading the reviews and looking at their website. Ordered a Ruby Negroni before dinner - nice cocktail. Ordered a charbroiled chipotle chicken sandwich (should've ordered the salmon) - pretty average. After dinner ordered a Boulevardier and got some cocktail in a martini glass (not sure what it was - no Campari in it). The waitstaff, Chris, was friendly, attentive, & accommodating but I'm in no hurry to return.
Basically hot dogs wrapped in bread, occasionally with some cheese or jalapeños thrown in for good measure. It's just not that good.

Went to enjoy one last meal before they closed for good. Advertised opened at 11am. Doors locked and looked unkept thru the windows. 
Really wish that we could have had one more meal here.

Customer service could be better but the food was great. They were able to accommodate a group of 7 without reservations on Sunday. They seating is limited and the downstairs area is small. The food was delicious. 3 of us ordered the catfish which was just fine but the sides were great I had the Mac and cheese, potato salad, and greens. A good thing I wasn't to highlight is that one of us wanted oxtails and they were all out. However, our waitress said it was a small amount left and let us have that. I thought it was very nice gesture. I was very pleased with the food just wish the waitress was friendlier.

Feeling nostalgic after going to the WWII museum or like me just staying in the neighborhood and need a quick bite or treat. This place with certainly take care of the nostalgia even if the food doesn't live up to the standard they had in the 1950's.

Service: while there were three counter people, all very young, they all seemed to be a contest to see who could be slower or more sullen. It was dead when I went in there but it got more busy after a while and they moved just as slow. Also they don't bring the food to the table just call out the names and they weren't the clearest of speakers. 

Food: I was too late for the make your own biscuit breakfast so I got another southern favourite, pimento cheese and ham grill sandwich (7) which was tasty but nothing special. I also got a lemonade that tasted like it was from a mix and a single scoop of ice cream. The ice cream was way too sweet.

One of the best seafood restaurant in town.

I love this place because of its simplicity ... not only with the restaurant, but also with the owners on how they run the place. Very simple... they only open on lunch and closed on Sunday. So, you know how popular this restaurant with this limited opening time. The people working there seem to be very happy and treated as family by the owners. Anyhow, I love this place from their ambience...

Their dishes never disappoint. I normally started with fresh oyster, they have a number of choices of oyster type, so you felt like in oyster bar in New Orleans. The only thing is that they charged $1 per shuckle, but if you order more than half a dozen, they gave you some discount... I love how they serve the raw oyster with fresh cut lemon.

My favorite dish is fish taco. My goodness, one of the best in town... the freshness and tastiness of the fish taco is to die for. It's a little spicy with burst feeling once it goes into your mouth. They serve it with chips and salsa.

My son loved their clam chowder and fisherman soup. He could eat more than one bowl with multiple bread. The owner knew my son, as we came here so often, and sometimes he gave extra soup on the house. We just loved this place.

My wife loved their Ahi Tuna salad and Fish & Chip. They are just prepared to perfection.

Yes... you felt like you are having homemade food as you come and visit this place. Thank you guys, for the job well done !

We came in and sat in the lounge as our friendly server came ( she is dressed very unprofessional, if your short and significantly over weight, then short tight dresses is not recomended) asked for our drinks we asked for ice tea and she recommended an alcoholic drink of the day after repeatedly informed her we are driving.  Ordered the seafood fett. It was gross. Oily. And heavy. Not as spicy as I expected . Very disappointing .  And. Over priced servicy was mediocre and the good was a joke . Serves dressed unproffessional made us pose our appetite.

Decent tacos, but they are not very filling and I need to eat several before I am full.  However they provide grilled onions upon request and have good qualty salsa, limes and cilantro for their tacos  I eat at Lilly's tacos on occasion and would recommend them to someone who wants relatively inexpensive tacos but be prepared to buy at least 4-6 of them and spend around $7-10 dollars.

I was excited for this place to be finally open and even more so when I was able to snag a Saturday night reservation to celebrate bf's birthday. 
When we got in, the hostess checked our temperatures first. We still had to wait a bit even with reservations. Initially they were going to put us by the bar on the high tops which we asked for a different seat as I have back issues and can't sit too long in a chair with no back. I was also a bit taken aback because in all of my concerns past dining experiences the bar area is typically for those without reservations or first come fist serve. So that was weird for me. Anyways, they were able to seat in a regular table.

Finally seated, we were deciding on appetizers and asked our server (Jessica) about her opinion between the crispy artichokes vs. veal meat ball. She gave the description and told us that it's canned artichokes in batter and deep fried  we weren't expecting canned and deep fried. We were thinking fresh and crispy from a broil...not so much so we decided to go with the veal meatballs. It was 3 pieces served over a piece of toasted bread, the sauce on the meatballs was different but really tasty! 

On to the main course, I ordered the cowboy steak (one of the priciest on their menu) because I love me some steak and bf ordered the lamb chops. We also ordered a side of the wild mushrooms and pancetta. My steak (medium rare) was charred quite well, so well that  all I could taste was the bitter char and a weird taste of idk, it's smoke but kinda also tasted like gas. Like when you don't have the accelerant burn off when starting your charcoal grill before putting food on it. It also needed some salt. The crispy oysters was were the salt was apparently. So I was sad for my order because I really wanted some darn good steak and I barely ate it, I just couldn't get past the taste. Bf's lamb chop was delicious (in the couple bites I got lol) the sauce on it was also very tasty. He said that the sides (potato gratin with goat cheese and veggies) were pretty bland and the veggies (carrots were really hard and not quite cooked) 

We ordered dessert (so I can get rid of the lingering taste in my mouth lol) the lava torte was ok. The gelato was tasty. 

The manager did finally came by our table when I told our server Jessica about the steak. The manager was chatting with some friends for most of our meal so it was really too late for a new main course but he did eventually came and checked on what's wrong with the steak and took that off the bill (thankfully)

Over all, the venue is nice, a bit louder than most fine dining places, but still nice. Service was good. Food is ok. The restaurant is still definitely working their kinks out. I would wait a bit longer if we ever go back.

This was the best pizza ordering experience I've ever had...

Super fast delivery
Picture perfect food
Awesome cheat night

I have been hearing so many great things about this place so when I had the chance to swing in for lunch I did! It was the middle of the day on a Tuesday so it wasn't busy, and we sat at the bar.
The bar is beautifully stocked with local spirits and top shelf favorites and the drink names are fun and playful. 
I ordered the Lil-Let it be which had killer blanc, gin, orange and basil. It was fantastic and perfectly balanced with a lovely fresh flavor. 
For an appetizer I ordered the falafel fries- they were AMAZING! These lovely slender rectangles of delicately spiced falafel fried to a perfect brown crisp on the outside and a warm fluffy inside : my vegetarian taste buds did a little happy dance! They are served with a herbaceous tzatziki aioli that was so creamy and really made for a unique flavor combo! I highly recommend giving these a try even if you are not a vegetarian! 
For my entree I ordered off the seasonal special menu which included a Vegan mushroom and barley soup, and I couldn't resist that. I am a sucker for barley. This soup was so very good! I didn't know what to expect, and it had carrots and celery and savory spices like thyme, sage, rosemary, bay maybe some marjoram? It tasted like bread stuffing in a barley soup. I thought it was delicious! 
I wish I was more hungry because the pitas and hummus looked amazing and the desserts would be worth the trip back alone!
I can't believe it took me this long to visit this place! I can totally see what the hype is all about, and the cleverly named dishes are musically inspired and punny! Well done to the whole staff for creating such a lovely restaurant nestled in the Grove.

Food is the best in Tucson, lucky to live close by! Egg Rolls are uneatable though - weird taste you can't get past, so for that and that the inside needs new booths badly, I didn't give 5-star. But beside that, food is AMAZING!!!!!

First time here for brunch per recommendation by a local friend. Freaking delicious! Ordered the chilequiles (or however you spell it), and it is literally the best I've ever had. Super light and full of flavor. 

Be ready to wait, but we'll worth it!

There's 1 espresso shot in a 12 oz latte. Isn't the standard 2? It tasted cheap and I wasn't happy to spend $5 on steamed milk. I've worked at coffee shops and been to so many, it feels like a slap to the face to not get quality espresso or even the right amount of it.

Went to grab a pizza late on a Friday night. The hours state that they are open until midnight but when we arrived around 9:30p- the place was cleared out and the staff seemed annoyed that we wanted to order. 

We chose a spot at the bar and the bartender was friendly. Pitcher of Shock Top and a Haley's Comet (double pepperoni & double mozz) pizza later.... Nothing special. Maybe the Double Decker is where it is at but the original thin crust doesn't have much to offer. It reminded me of a frozen pizza and to say that this includes double ingredients is a definite stretch. $17 for a 12" seems a little steep too- probably won't go back. Sorry JJ's....
Probably the worst I have ever had. Please.... Save your money. Pay the extra few dollars for quality food.

This is, without exaggeration, the most authentic and best tasting Korean food I have had in the United States.  I lived in Korea for 3 years and ever since then it has been hard to find a place that is authentic and good.  I have sampled the food of many Korean restaurants from many different parts of the US and this one sits firmly on top with no contest.  It was delicious, and paired with the Korean TV and Korean style decorations/arrangements I honestly felt like I was back in Korea the whole time I was there.

I've been a close follower of Mr. Bianco for a couple of decades. Standing in line for 2+ hours on Adams Street "forcing" patrons to a chauterie of apps & throwing back fine champagne. Pizza for 2, easily $100. Anything to get out of the heat. Travels to & from San Luis Obispo were timed to openings & closings. I missed the stories  that Chris' team had when they traveled to NYC... Back to pizza...outstanding pie with added prosciutto yum! The lingering aftertaste of quality stays in your mouth much like a quality Zin would. Not having  to navigate to Adam's Street is a blessing for Tucson. 
Maybe a spedini app wouldn't be too over the top!

Had a wonderful experience here.  My boyfriend & I were looking for a new place to check out & we stumbled across this gem on Yelp.  The food, atmosphere & drinks were fantastic.  We both agreed that we will be back often.

The moment We entered the establishment we were greeted with great customer service. We had our daughters with us so I asked if it was good for kids. I was told yes with a huge . 

We ordered wings, the adult grilled cheese, a  and loaded tater tots. Delish!! Our waitress was attentive and very personable.

Crazy overpriced. Crazy. Lunch was $30 for bagels. 

Lines are insane which is great for the business but probably wouldn't be so long if the cashiers knew anything about what they were doing- I mean anything!! Been 3 times and have been so frustrated (tried different times hoping for better experiences) that I will not be back. Flavorless food. My friend had to cover her tuna and chicken salad with salt and pepper and still didn't eat it. She eats everything!

Display is beautiful and gets you excited but that's the best part- the display. Downhill from there. 

No permanent menus- in fact, there aren't even types of bagels listed on the menu so when you FINALLY get to order you are in a mad dash trying to figure out what you want after someone hands you a menu and you stare into a case of bagels. Needs a lot of work. The next bagel place will get it right. I am not going to be wasting my time anymore.

Too bad I ordered sauce on the wings since they clearly made this order for a canine. The wings were ridiculously over cooked and the fries were cold. I can forgive cold fries but wings are supposed to be your thing. This was such a waste of money. Unfortunately the carrots were the best part of the meal. With so many restaurants closing, you would think those still able to receive business would try a bit harder to survive. Skip this place.
That is one of the best restaurants in Santa Barbara. From the time you enter the door you are treated well and the food is simply outstanding. Worth every dollar.

I know it's a bit cliche to start off a review by saying, "I really wanted to like this place but..." the insert list of gripes. But seriously this place has great service, location, prices, and concept, but where it counted most, with the pizza, it just didn't live up to the hype. I dined solo that day so ordering a large pizza was not going to happens, so I ordered the personal Chicago style pizza. It just wasn't that good.  Lacked the density, flavors,  and "sauciness" of a tradition Chicago style pizza. It was just blah. 

I will definitely give this place another try because seriously the service was GREAT. Plus I love the laid back feel of the place. Maybe I will try a larger version. I don't know, but despite the stellar price of the personal pizza combo it just didn't hit home with me. Maybe the second time will be the charm.
Really fun vibe and great food! Neat location and fun sitting outside.

Today was my fourth time I've eaten at Tacqueria del Sol, and each time it gets better. It started out very good when my friend suggested this place on a whim. but now I am really taken with this place! 
The tacos are all in soft shells, and they have a variety of choices, from fish tacos, Southern BBQ pork, fried chicken, and a bunch of other offerings. All have been served very fresh, very quickly, and the service has been stellar. If you're so inclined: check out their frozen or regular margaritas. Very good, and all at a modest price. I can't imagine someone having anything negative to say about this place it has been a pleasant experience each time so far. I suggest you check them out!
Really good food, we had an excellent server.  Food came out fast and hot, and they have a very good breakfast buffet!  Everything was fresh.  It was pretty busy too, but they were efficient.
My better half had the Rainbow Trout Almondine, blackened. I had the fish sandwich and grilled vegetables. Both dishes were good. Oreo ice cream pie also very good. Excellent customer service.

Do they still serve the true pepper lion?  They had this ahi app that was pathetic.   The service sucks. I am an Alton native and will give Paul one more chance.  Pick it up Paul and start looking over your staff like a hawk or say goodby to an Alton landmark.

Asked for wet wings, totally dry. Asked for extra ranch and blue cheese, they charge for even 1 side of that on Tuesdays. When we asked, she said it's clearly written on the menu. There's signs everywhere for .75 wings, doesn't say anything about extra charges. Your job, as a waitress, is to explain. Not tell the customer it's on them. And, watch your tab, I had 2 Stella's on mine, don't even drink that. Waitress was not customer friendly about any of it. Not going back. 
Oh, and then last time before, these in the pic are the $7 shots we got. Supposed to be Jolly Rancher. Kool aid without sugar or alcohol and half the size of normal. We were there for a birthday and happened to see owner on the way out. So, birthday boy actually got a real shot. Yet this week was no better. Owner needs to get on top of his staff.
This is the best po-boy anywhere. Not just New Orleans but ANYWHERE. And if you feel otherwise...fight me!
Great food and service! I highly recommend coming here. It is the best place to get a tenderloin in the city! I will be back very soon!

If I could give this place less than a star I would. Ordered food from here a few months back. The wings were disgusting. They tasted like they "going bad" but the cooks decided to fry them anyway. I called to say they tastes really off. I wasn't looking for a refund at all. The manager was extremely rude for no reason at all. I will absolutely never eat from this place again.

This unfortunately wasn't a good experience. We ordered food after midnight because that's when our flight arrived. We decided to try this place because it was open. It was supposed to take 45-50 minutes yet it took over 1 1/2 hours to get the food when they're 9mins away... It came super cold and missing stuff. I honestly should have just gone to bed hungry.  Only reason I'm even giving them a 2 star rating is that they were open but I don't recommend them unless you're super drunk or don't care about frozen, over-cooked yet cold food.

What a nightmare, I would give less than 1 star if I could. We booked a block of rooms for our wedding recently at this location and they made it our whole experience stressful from day one. The sales manager we worked with seemed completely incompetent and had extremely poor communication skills from day one. They had only one working elevator which I should say was semi-working since one of our wedding party got stuck at one point. In our room our sink was clogged, the room was gross and the vents looked like they were not cleaned in some time. Another guest did not have a working toilet. The upper floors had a strong mildew smell. We also wanted to pay for breakfast for our guest the next morning after the wedding. The front desk was supposed to hand out vouchers to our guest but tried to make us do it. When it came time to pay for the breakfast they lost the vouchers our guest handed in (server left with them) so they elected to make up a number to charge us which was much higher than our guest count. So it took them ~2 hours the day of checkout to get this sorted out. Long story short, I am surprised this place is in business. Save yourself some time and look elsewhere. If it wasn't for this place, our wedding would have been perfect.
I love West Avenue Grille for breakfast and lunch. They have fresh and hot food. Their menu is spectacular. I don't live far and can walk there.

The Buffalo Slices are a must. Actually, pretty much any specialty slice here is good. I believe it's $3.75 for students if you purchase two slices and a drink. No seating, so don't go there with hopes of sitting in. Otherwise, pretty good.

Ate lunch here as a party of 5. Place is really clean with a ton of newspaper articles hung and framed to read about the history of the business. I can't even begin to explain the enormity of the servings here, I'll leave that to the other reviewers that remembered to take pics! Prices seem expensive at first until what you ordered arrives. One serving of any dish can easily feed 3-4 people. We started with an order of onion rings that of course fed all 5 of us. I ordered a roast beef sandwich of which I could only eat less than half after giving up on the bread! My better half had the corned beef hash and it was the size of a giant homemade meatloaf, served on a large oval plate. He ate his leftovers for 4 days! The other couple were smarter and ordered a ruben to share and it was to die for. 

The only negatives are the cramped seating and lack of parking, which in the city is completely expected on both points! Definitively a must stop while you're in the area or do like we did and go there purposefully from the burbs, you won't be disappointed!

When South Philly food indecision had led me to here I thought that I found IMMEDIATE BBQ salvation. While it didn't exactly hit that mark on the first attempt, Dickey's was definitely a decent quick fix BBQ joint that I'd visit again for the daily specials and then some.

Being that it was a Saturday evening, the promise of a BBQ brisket sandwich special that came with 2 sides and a large drink had me entering the door. But in an odd twist the only thing that I didn't enjoy about my meal was the brisket. While it was far from the worst that I've had (good riddance Q - http://www.yelp.com/biz/q-bbq-and-tequila-philadelphia), it was just a let down compromised by both bites of dry meat and chewy fat. And unlisted topping of raw onion didn't help matters either. Grant it things may have improved had I remembered to grab a side of BBQ sauce to counterbalance the dryness of the meat. but other spots have me so used to the meat coming sauced that I didn't even think of it.

But other than the dreadful brisket, the meal that I had was quite promising. The fried okra was the perfect mix of slimy okra and fried crunchy bits that had me wanting more. And for a BBQ franchise chain, its mac & cheese was smooth and creamy. Their house brand of sweet iced tea also hit the spot. So overall while the meat failed to deliver on my first attempt, Dickey's definitely has enough to bring me back for at least a couple more attempts. Especially when its specials lead to a good deal every day of the week.

Okay so I didn't try anything with the mushrooms because I'm not a mushroom guy. So if you're not a mushroom guy do what I did- get the baked potato and hamburger with everything they offer besides mushrooms. It was life changing. I know, I know, I was skeptical too. "Oh, another burger joint people love, don't believe the hype." But it has been two weeks and I can't stop talking about it or remembering how good it tasted during that first bite. I think the flavor profile that they master here is cold sour with hot savory. The baked potato is so soft and with their sour cream it really nails it. The hamburger is hot and salty and with a pile of shredded cold cheese on top it, once again, NAILS it.

If you're like us you may be full when you show up because you've been eating rich food all day or all week because everything that's cooked in that town is super rich and super salty but I don't care. You have to try the baked potato and/or burger here.

If you're reading this now you're probably considering going. You may already be on your way. And if so... I'm so jealous.

The atmosphere and ambience were delightful--sitting outside and people watching as the lights cascaded gently on the patio felt relaxing. The charcuterie board was impressive, but that's about it. 

I ordered the gnocchi, and if I didn't know any better, I'd say that Chef Boyardee personally opened his own can of pasta and emptied into my bowl--and microwaved it. Wasn't impressed. Our server was hung over from the night before, that was great to know as well. worst $90 spent on dinner.

The best thing about this place was the service. Our waiter was great. The food was okay...definitely not the authentic Mexican I was looking for and a bit pricier than I would like. I will possibly try this place again...but probably not if I can find somewhere cheaper and more authentic.

Anytime I come to the Nashville area i stop at this place immediately after my flight lands.  I could eat it like every single day.   I loooooooooooooove the extra hot fish with wings and their fruit tea is amazing as well.  The service is a bit slow but the food is well worth the wait.  I wish there was a way to have their food shipped to the DC area

Absolutely love this place. The food is delicious and the portions are significant. To make things better they have a good selection of little known beers that you cant get anywhere else in town and that fit the food perfectly.
I think there is a bar on the side of the restaurant where you can order just the beers, ive never been to it though, when I come here im going to be sitting down to eat.
The only one thing is that it isn't the cheapest, but good food rarely is so im not complaining and its only open 4 days a week, which is dissapointing.

The difference from my first visit to my latest is unreal; if I didn't know better,  I wouldn't believe this was the same establishment. The food I received tonight was TERRIBLE.  Both the garlic knots and the pizza were burned to a charcoal color. The pizza itself wasn't even sliced: the server made some mention of the juices running out. What? This is pizza, not a steak!! Get the thing home and it's like sawing into wet plaster. A total mess. The toppings overwhelmed the crust and had zero flavor. The only tasty item was the marinara sauce! 28 grams is a 47 minute drive from my home~ over an hour and a half drive for a meal my family tossed in favor of a salad and garlic bread. I used a prepaid CL Deals coupon for this dinner, otherwise I'd be attempting to get a refund.

Edited to respond:
Your self-righteousness is worse than your food.
Seeing as how your response is triple the word count of my review, yet doesn't includes the magic word "sorry," I'll just let these pictures speak for themselves. My review stands.
Great food, a little more than the chains $, but better quality. Mostly a take out place, not really set up to dine in comfortably.

I have only drank there and never eaten there, so I can only speak from a drinking perspective.  Everytime I go it's uber crowded, standing room only.  The bar itself can be crowded and hard to get to.  I ordered 1 beer and gave the bartender a $20 expecting change so I could tip etc... instead she took the $20 and did not offer me change and then went on to help others.  It was so loud and crowded that I couldn't waive her down to get my change, so basically I left a $15 tip for what I got...
But I will say they have Not Your Father's... on tap, which I had never seen before on tap until I went here.  And I really love that.  Just FYI though, it's like $8 a glass.  Not sure how much I will frequent this place, maybe on a none weekend night?

Great variety of pastries both savory and sweet. Staff was super friendly and made great recommendations. Glad to have them on Central! Coffee cake is a must get!!! Ooey and gooey and amazing! Highly recommend!

Friday lunch was amazing!!! Love the food and staff. So friendly. We ordered 5-napkin burger,lump crab cake, fish tacos, veggie sandwich, buttermilk chicken sandwich, cheese burger and barbecue bacon burger. We were hungry and couldn't take pics. As it was Friday lunch from work couldn't get that beer burger combo. Definitely will visit again for napkin burger.

This place is Amazing!!!! First off when you walk inside there are tons of Fresh Pastries on the left wall that you can choose from. The vibe and atmosphere is nice and enjoyable. Lots of good stuff on the shelves. And the fruit smoothies are super good.  I got a pineapple smoothie for lunch. It was so good that I went back the same day and I ordered the Torta Streak and Cheese in the evening. WOW just WOW it was ridiculously good. Better food than anything else is here in North Valley.  They were super fast both times i went there today.  Each time they walked my food over to me where i was waiting and personally handed me my order. Tomorrow I'm going back to try their breakfast burrito i heard was super tasty and I'll get some fresh Mango for lunch. I recommend this place 100% with a 5 star.  I don't even do Yelp reviews but this place is so good I felt like I had to tell everybody about it.

Love, love, love this place.  Staff is always friendly, food is always delish and you get BIG portions.  I've been there for breakfast and dinner and both times were a pleasant experience.  Defiantly going back!
Omg- I have died & gone to heaven in the South. The fried chicken, greens, mile high biscuits & slap ya mama bread pudding are AMAZING!

Today, after a pointless day at the DMV (I didn't have my birth certificate with me), I decided to try Trolley Stop.  

It's not too far from my house and I haven't really had breakfast food out in the 2 months I've been living in New Orleans.  When I walked in it looked extremely busy.  There were no empty seats at the bar or waiting area so I assumed the wait would be long for a table.  In about 3 minutes I was greeted with a man asking me "How many baby?"  "Just one." He quickly sat me at a four top in the middle of the dining room.  As a single diner I loathe sitting at a big table in the middle of the dining room, but didn't feel intimidated at all.  

Although, it was very loud, I was able to read my book while I waited for my eggs benedict.  Yes, that's right a heart attack on a plate, but it sounded different and good.  It wasn't your typical benny.  Thick cut canadian bacon, a slice of tomato, a square of american cheese, on top of a toasted english muffin all doused with country gravy.  It was also served with amazing potatoes and just enough grits.  Obviously, this isn't fancy food, but it was so comforting, a few hours later I'm still thinking about it.  

As previous reviews stated, service was slow, but friendly.  I wasn't asked whether I wanted toast of biscuits, that was supposed to come with the meal; I wouldn't have been able to eat it anyway.  

I can't really see myself going there for dinner, since the menu is typical diner fare, unless it was after a night of hard partying.  So many good choices in this city I hope to try some more.Overall, I recommend the breakfast menu at Trolley Stop, since it's very comforting and filling.

Atmosphere and food are great.  Service is lacking, as to be expected in a newer restaurant.  Server charged us for three things we never ordered, but management fixed it right away.  It also took 20 minutes to get our order, when we were ready immediately

If you're from out of town and staying at the hotel, look to yelp to provide better options. We only come here to watch a Lightning game if we don't have tickets that night. The food isn't great and the staff lacks in service. They're not rude they just lack in service.
Great iHop, even tho their all the same, this one is nicer and doesn't smell like rotten eggs and Bibles like the rest of them. Overall, okay for an iHop. 3 stars.
I'm giving 1 star for the karaoke DJ. Not the Bar or the bar tender who I rarely saw on a Saturday night....seriously???!!!??!?!!??

Bab is the perfect little spot to run by and grab lunch or dinner. Their appetizers are amazing, their Korean bbq bowls are delicious and they make it so easy to get the ingredients you want. 
My only desire is to have two sizes for their bowls because I can never finish it and don't always want it again that same day or the next day. 
Great concept, and love the convenience of Uber eats too- happy to have these guys as an addition to Downtown :)
Love their donuts. Light and fluffy. Just melts in your mouth. Blueberry fritter is yummy!! They also have "cake" donuts which are a little denser but still tasty.

Went to this place with very high expectations and very excited to try a new French restaurant. I have lived in France and was hoping this place would take me back.  I went there for lunch and had their lunch specials a Quiche Lorraine and a salad, the quiche left a lot to be desired and so did the salad, the fries and crepes were good. I thought it was a little pricey for what you got. I would probably go back and try it again since I love anything French and try the other items on the menu.
We enjoyed a fine dinner.  The food was good but not particularly special.  Big busy place.  Felt chain like.

I've eaten at Beefy's three times now. For me, the burgers are okay. The 50 cent chicken wings on Wednesday is what I like best. 
I ate at Beefy's shortly after it opened. I don't remember what I had, but I thought it was just okay. A month or sho ago I was watching a show with Anthony Bourdain eating a Korean-influenced burger in New York. I got the hankering for any burger and decided to try Beefy's again. By coincidence they had one on the menu so I ordered it. I had an excellent Korean-flavored burger at Bachi Burger in Las Vegas. The Beefy's version didn't do much for me. They have a Korean paste and kim chi but nothing stood out as especially flavorful. 
I did get their wings and they were tasty. Large and distinctive.
I was in the neighborhood yesterday and decided to try something else on the menu. This time I got the chili burger. Ordering something with chili here can be risky, since Beefy's is located in what used to be Landrum's, where I ate many of the hallowed chili-cheese omelets. I didn't like the flavor of the chili. It tasted overcooked, almost burned, and old. Not much zing to it.
Service is always friendly here.

This is a favorite. Very accomodating servers.  Wife loves the fish and the chicken quesadilla.  I love the Thunderbird chicken sandwich. I've probably had it 20 times.  Branched out recently and had a burger and was very happy.  They've got a side dish with black beans, corn, cilantro.  Its so good (but hot) I'll substitute more of it for the fries.  Dozens of visits and I bring friends and tourists.  Can't say I've ever had a bad experience.  That's why I keep returning.

Poor service!! The manager continued to sit at their bar eating and chatting it up the entire time we were dinning. We ordered nachos snd that took 45 mins to receive and yet it was something I could have made at home and yet faster than what it took to get them to the table. The place was slow but the one bartender seemed to struggle. We decided to skip ordering any other food and go eat food somewhere else. Just very poorly ran period!!

Visited Metro diner for the first time today. This will definitely be our go to spot for breakfast and looking forward to trying lunch and dinner as well. 

Portion sizes were great and food was delicious. The manager, Tim came and spoke with us and our sever was one of the best we've encountered. 

I highly recommend this local treasure!
This place is an amazing example of craft food and coffee. Everything is given time and dedication. I absolutely love it.

Food options are strange. I'm open but there's not enough variety to choose from. We had the pork chop good but the overall dish was over flavored with different profiles that do not fit together. In other words food that's trying way too hard. Seems it's like the weirder the better, not so. The drinks I feel the same way about. I have been there a few times and tried quite a bit. Don't think it's worth the money. Weak menu, over flavored food, strange choices, overdone craft cocktails, expensive.

You would think all Chez Cora cafes would be the same standard of service and meals - but not so! This is probably the best location in south or west Edmonton. Always busy but usually able to sit you down in 10 -15 minutes. The staff are happy and eager to serve. The breakfasts are served in reasonable time and as ordered. Unlike other Chez Cora in the city, this west end location must have a higher standard for food service.

Happy hour Mon-Fri 3-6pm! We came here before 6pm on a Tuesday and made the happy hour. There's outdoor and indoor seating. It wasn't that busy when we were there. We got to sample some beers before committing to pints. We loved the Nitro Mango-Chiffon and Nitro Chocolate Maltshake. The menu seemed smaller compared to other places. They have a vareity of beers like IPAs, Saison, Sour, Ales, blonde. Street parking.

If only it wasn't St Louis !! What a glorious place!!  Everyone raves about the ice cream, so I won't bother! I will comment on food and an amazing server!! 
Went to Fitz's for lunch, was promptly seated, our server came over and introduced himself. He recognized my sister and her husband though they had only been there twice before and he was their waiter only once!! Kyle was his name!! If you go to Fitz's on Delmar, ask for him to be your server!! You will not regret it!! He took took our drink orders,  I had a Black Cherry. It was very good. The other 3 had Diet Root Beer which they all claimed was excellent. Kyle could see we were in a quandary as to what to order. Even though he was really busy ( he was covering a lot of tables) he really took his time and explained the menu to us and made recommendations. We were ready for a drink refill before we ordered. They had a soft drink called Cardinal Red. I asked for a taste to decide if i liked it. He brought all four of us a taste. Honestly, it was not very good. Of course a Cubs fan could hardly like anything Cardinal related !! I ordered the 1/4 pound chili dog. Quite tasty and filling, lots of chili on it. Served open faced, I had a side of baked beans instead of onion rings. Slightly above average, but I wish I had stayed with onion rings. My Sister and Brother-in-law ordered the dog too with onion rings. The rings were huge and delicious!!  My chauffeur had the patty melt With sweet potato fries. It was huge, and she said it was delicious also!! I Ordered a mug of root beer, and when Kyle delivered it he found out my wife and I were from Rogers Park, and it turns out he used to live in Rogers Park, just off Touhy!! Small world. The Root Beer is absolutely the most wonderful Root Beer ever!!  I even ordered a case to go,for Drinking at home. Okay, wait one ......., sorry, had to go get one, simply the best!! Not overly carbonated, you just have to taste it to understand!! 
I am down to my last 2 bottles, catastrophe waits just around the corner!! Back to Kyle like I said he was very busy but took his time with us. He was always happy to answer questions. He had a real smile on his face when interacting with us not one of those fake " so glad you're here " ones that turn to frowns and grumbles when they are out of customers sight!!  He even insisted on carrying the case of Root Beer to the car for us. They have a bottling plant on premise for their product. If they could bottle Kyles personality and dedication ,fortunes would be made!!! Mmmmm, another gulp of root beer! Go to St. Louis, wear a Cubs shirt, stop at Fitz's, ask for Kyle and have a care free afternoon!! See Pics!!!!
Definitely the best pho in the area. The food is amazing and the servers are very friendly. Truly a great addition to the area.

I don't have many opportunities for Trinidadian food in this area. So when I discovered this gem I was excited and it did not disappoint! The food was freah prepared and appropriately spicy. The portions were generous too. I have only tried the shrimp roti so far but will update with other menu items

Not a fan at all. Usually hit up uncle nicks for slices but was ashamed of going twice in a week so wanted to give this spot a try. 2 plain cheese slices were 8$, that's insane. I should have asked the price before i ordered but I digress. Cheese was overpowering and hardly any sauce whatsoever on the slices. Lower crust was crazy flimsy, so thin and floppy it was almost transparent. Upper crust was nice, had a good crunch and had some bubbles which I love. Can't justify paying 8$ for 2 plain slices when you can get better a few feet away and cheaper.

Ok so I'm here at 3 Crow now and it's SO smokey inside that you could choke to death. Im actually outside on the patio area where I'm about to eat my food in cold weather with the other non-smokers. Does this sound right?? Why don't they make the smokers go outside instead? Isn't that how it works everywhere else? Thing is there's literally only 4 selfish a-holes smoking, which is enough to make it so they'll never need a fog machine. This is so unfair to the majority of people who aren't cancer lovers.  

Come on. Seriously?
Nice new adult decor, good frozen margaritas. The enchiladas supremes were excellent. Will make this a regular stop for us.

Central Grocery is home to the Muffaletta sandwich... a salty, cold cut sandwich with an olive mixture served between two massive pieces of bread. The old grocery store also has cold drinks, dusty old shelves full of product, and a vibe that is cool enough for a quick visit to order a sandwich.

Do they serve these at other places? Yes.

Is Central Grocery two parts shameless tourist trap? Yes! Yes!

Is it worth waiting in a super long line to get one here? No.

Does the place have enough tourist charm to warrant a visit? Yes.

Will you start eating muffulettas every day after you have one? No, but still worth trying.
This was a really good evening. Our party had the sampler for starters and fish, steak, and pork for the main dishes and they were all delicious.
Pho.  Excellent pho with no frills.  Friendly and very kind host.  This is the best Pho in Boise.

Nice coffee shop with excellent coffee. I wish they had more offerings. Almost no cookies or anything else. I was a bit disappointed I wanted something besides my ice coffee. The cold brew was as good as it gets but it was almost $4 for a pretty small cup. The service was very good and the space is very pretty.

Well, I have to say, this is the best barbecue spot in Dunedin! 

After hearing and reading great reviews, I decided to try out Q Southern BBQ.   

 I ordered the brisket dinner.  The dinner comes with two sides (greens and Mac-n-cheese for me) and an array of BBQ sauces to try.  The meat was amazingly moist and absolutely delicious.  You can tell they know how to BBQ to perfection.  I left there very full and very happy.  

It's a great casual spot for lunch or dinner.  I suggest you walk next door to Soggy Bottom Brewery and order one of their beers.    They go great with the BBQ.   

So glad Q Southern BBQ has come to Dunedin.   I can't wait to go back and try more menu items.

I haven't been in this building since the late 90's. Back then it was called "Hot Rods". The owner then was trying to emulate the vibe of A&W, with burgers and dogs. While hosting weekly and sometimes daily car shows during the warm season. Sadly the fun only lasted a couple years. 

Flash forward a decade or two this building was transformed into a super breakfast location. I've seen the crowd grow bigger since they opened. Even seeing folks waiting outside to get a seat. 

Today was my first time in here since "Hot Rods". The decore is contemporary with a home feeling. Somewhere you could feel comfortable. I sat at the bar. Where there was a nice spread of different tequilas, a fridge with a variety of Mexican beers and an expresso machine. The staff was super nice and friendly. 

I didn't have to wait even a minute for service. I ordered a Denver omelette. Within ten minutes it was placed in front of me, piping hot. My meal was super delicious. Although I was in a bit of a hurry, I ate slow to savor the flavor of every bite. 

I will be back.

We live within a couple of miles of this restaurant and had no idea that it was a Vietnamese Restaurant until a couple of weeks ago! 

My husband & I had dinner there last night and were very pleasantly surprised. Our meals were excellently presented, delicious and reasonably priced!  

We started by sharing the Vegetable Spring Rolls....fantastic! For our main meal my husband chose Kung Pao Shrimp (Stir fried with onion, dry chili pepper, celery, water chestnuts and peanuts) and I had the Curry Chicken (Chicken breast cooked with fish sauce, lemongrass, potatoes and sweet potatoes).

If you enjoy Vietnamese food we can thoroughly recommend this wonderful restaurant. If you have never had Vietnamese food before, then you should definitely try it at Sandra's. You won't be disappointed!

Check out their website http://sandrariceandnoodles.com/

I usually come here for happy hour where steak and chicken quesadilla and chips and dip are cheaper w the purchase of a drink. I like the quality here better than some of the other places around the area. Service and atmosphere is fine.
Definitely recommend the fish tacos.
Their website menus and on app do not match up. No turtle soup. Food was mediocre at best.

New restaurant in Lafayette Square. Pretty good food experience. We shared 3 dishes, starting with the gumbo. Served nice and hot, smoky, a creaminess. Not an authentic gumbo, but good. Wished we had some authentic French bread! Next, jambalaya! Lots of rice, andouille sausage, minimal shrimp and chicken. It needed more protein and seasoning. The best dish, was the chicken and waffle. The chicken was moist, well seasoned and was drizzled with a cayenne pepper sauce. The chicken rested on a delicious waffle! Crispy. It was the winner of the 3 dishes we tried! One problem with the restaurant was the noise! We arrived early, very few tables, but very loud. The server had to bend down to discuss the menu! The noise is a big problem! And, no French bread! What's that about? If you are calling yourself Cajun/Creole, the Bread is a necessity!

I almost judged this book by the cover until I read a few reviews that convinced me to walk in. 

When you walk in the chef and server had big warming smiles when they greeted you. Then you noticed, the place is spotless!!!!! It's so bright and clean. They do only have four tables in the dining area. 

My wife used their facilities and said it was even cleaner than the dining area, which identifies great behaviors for a sushi bar. 

The sushi was exceptional especially considering the price and quantity. If I lived closer, I would definitely be a regular. 

Great people, great environment, great sushi, great price. Hidden gem for sure!!!!
Garbage food, staff is rude. I would rather eat canned dog food. Go to the vending machine across the isle. Trust me your better off.

This is a D-I-V-E...odd, love it or hate it kind of place. The inside smells of sour beer and a faint whiff of stale smoke and vomit. The porch is very cool and seems like a great spot to see music. 

I had the hot chicken bites - they were moist, crispy, and hot out of the fryer. Needed a little salt, but very tasty. The medium heat definitely had a kick! Fries were soggy and not really edible. My waitress was sweet and attentive, but many of the other employees were loud and seemed a bit off. $7.50 for a 32oz draught beer, great price.

I went to this restaurant for the first time today after eating next door almost 3 years. What a gem, the food is very good, reasonably priced and very clean. The staff were nice, polite and engaging without being overbearing. Celebrating my friends birthday, she ordered the Friday AYCE fried fish special and was thrilled with the flavors and skills shown in the preparation. I tried the 4 meat calzone which was dynamite, it hung over each end of the plate and was loaded with tasty ingredients. We spoke about onion rings and they brought us some to try, freshly cut, battered and fried. YUMMY!! We will return for the Prime Rib, NY Style deli sandwiches and their handmade hamburgers, too. Easy to get in and out at lunch or call ahead and pick it up, this is a great spot. Don't miss it!!

I've been coming here for years, even stayed loyal through the change of ownership years ago where the sweet older ladies who worked the counter were replaced by a younger, less friendly staff but it's a corner S. Philly bakery I'm not expecting over the top customer service. The white creme filling in their donuts is always good so I look past this subpar customer service & dirtiness of the bakers when they emerge from the back, it's kind of a turn off though to be honest, I mean their aprons are disgusting. 
Recently my past few experiences haven't been great, I can deal with a lot until I just can't anymore.

Pros:
- the white creme in their donuts is my favorite 
- now that they got more attn b/c of the cronut they usually have donuts later in the day where in the past that wasn't the case

Cons:
- Now that they are filling donuts to order there is no consistancy at all, 1 day you will get a donut that has so much filling you have to squeeze half of it out, others you get through 3 bites before there is any creme.

- Earlier this week as I was walking in there was a woman outside smoking a cigarette & seeing me pull up she rushed inside with me, walked around the counter & started waiting on people!  No washing of the hands, so you smoked, touched the door handle and now you are touching other things behind the counter (jelly dispensor, creme dispensor, etc) and MY Food without washing your hands or putting on a glove, oh hell no!  She was an heavy set woman with a grey Frangelli's hoodie on & reddish dyed hair. Then the woman baker who has been there for years (always eating, always a dirty apron, heavy set, very sloppy look to her) comes over, grabs at the cookies on the counter (no glove, no tissue paper) touching several in the process and takes a couple & eats them right there behind the counter talking with them in her mouth to the counter girl. Nope, that was it, I left.  That's the last straw!

- entire variety of donuts aren't available very early in the morning so can't grab them on the way to the office

- When you ask for a certain donut that is not in the counter the 2 usual responses, "I think they are making more" (but they never bother to go check) or "I guess we're out" (again never an attempt made to check in the back with the bakers)

- No real greeting from the counter staff, they are almost always very involved in a conversation with each other and make no attempt to stop it while they wait on you, which was also noted in outher reviews.


From now I will drive the extra few blocks and go to Baker Bros @ 3rd & Wolf, the customer service is always so warm and pleasant and their donuts are always on point, never had a disappointing experience there in my life, just a little further from my house.

This was our first date night since COVID started and it was not what we expected. The wait time was 1 hour! We arrived at 6p and we actually got our food at 8:30p. We waited 1 hour, but we were initially told 40 minutes. Then the long wait for food. We ordered quesadillas and Tex Mex eggrolls as a appetizer. Then we had Chicken and pasta with a flatbread pizza for entrees. The variety on the menu was NOT AVAILABLE. They didn't have lettuce, spice for the chicken and a number of other short comings. Most of the popular appetizers where gone. So I asked for a discount due the limited selection process and long wait. It was denied. So, the drinks, food and service were okay. But not worth what we paid, which totalled $96 with tip... plus I never got any cheesecake. Everything just took to long.
Erawan is my favorite average priced Thai restaurant in the area. Great for eating in or taking out, the food is ALWAYS awesome.

They advertise pickup and delivery. I call and ask if I can place an order for pickup. The girl on the other end of the phone tells me to hold. I wait for almost 10 minutes. Finally, the girl picks up and says "We're extremely busy, there is no one here who can take your order". I felt like asking her if she didn't know how to read and write. Needless to say, I'll never give this place my business again.

My brother suggested trying out this Vietnamese plaza. I was happy they had their own parking lot. Tips: The menu is strictly Pho soup/Cash only business!! The waiter gave me a hand in my face, after I gave him my debit card. Like a guard Halt gesture lol. Major cultural barrier, I let it go. So guys, credit cards aren't accepted! The Pho was definitely good and authentic. Nothing different from other places I've tried. Anthony Bourdain made a visit here about 4 years ago on his the episode of "The Layover"-Philadelphia. Overall, it seemed VERY quiet and lacking ambiance. For that reason, I would still return to my go-to spot at Pho Saigon (Christopher Columbus blvd).

Chow mein isn't supposed to taste like soup, or have this consistency. Slimy texture and not sure where the noodles are exactly. I ordered chow mein, not soup. Chow mein is supposed to be crispier, or at least not served with a egg drop soup consistency. I even googled it to makes sure I knew what I was craving. Highly disappointed in this.

Tried Blaze for the first time today during the lunch hour. 
The pizza was okay, and the concept is good. But this location missed the mark on execution. 

Of the four employees I saw, one seems to work while the rest just kind of wandered around and were barely even visible. From order to having my "fast" fired pizza - it was a 28-minute process and I had to get a to-go box. 

Wanted to like this place and add it into the work week rotation. But it won't be a regular stop. Maybe this was just an off day for them?

My first try at this "seafood in a bag" concept was at the Crab Hut in San Diego and I instantly fell in love with it.  So I was uber excited to see it here in my hometown.  The food and flavors are amazing!  If you're not into spice, even the mild may be a bit much.  But throwing your seafood in with all the spices and some red potatoes, comes out tasting like heaven.  My only "complaint" is that in comparison to similar places in other states, this place is pricey (hence the 4/5 stars).  You could probably have a reasonable meal if you limit your choices, but I like to get exactly what I want and in comparison to my SD experience, this place was double the price.  This hasn't stopped me from going though, and I will be back just not nearly as often as I'd like.

When will this location offer carry out? I'd love to run in and grab my food after ordering online or by phone. Also uber eats or any type of delivery would be FANTASTIC. Taco Dirty, Ciccio and Cali all have options for Uber Eats why not FK??

We've been to fords a few times and have always been impressed. Great service. Great atmosphere and great food.  We will be back many times.  Looking forward to giving their curbside option a try soon.

I have taken many people from out of town here for the Strawberry Boss Lady drink as well as the white cheese shredded chicken nachos. The customer service is arguable, I for one do not enjoy being asked (on average) every seven minutes if everything is okay. When I am out to eat I want to relax & enjoy the food/drinks as well as the company.
Just visiting New Orleans and found this place. What an absolute gem! Amazing desserts and confectionery with a really cool vibe! Staff is really nice!

This new small Thai spot is defintly worth the try! Love the interior and service! Their Lunch Specials are amazing! You get an option of soup, appetizer AND entree for $12.95. They are kid-friendly and extremely nice. The star of the menu so far are their soups such as, Tom Yum and Veggie Soup. It had so much flavor!!! I can't wait to go back and try their Tom Ka.
Have not been to wiener schnitzel in a few years. This location was very clean staff was awesome and service was prompt. Glad I stopped in

Met friends for lunch here. Arrived at 12 pm, expecting a huge lunch crowd and was pleasantly surprised. Got seated right away and was able to order relatively soon after being seated. We were waiting on an additional person, so we had to let the waiter know we would order without that person since we were on a tight schedule. Everyone was able to order, eat and pay by 12:45. (That's better than at some fast-casual restaurants!)

Definitely go for the sliders if it is your first visit. You'll be able to try multiple types of meatballs and sauces. I'm not a beef or pork eater, so it's always great when a restaurant has turkey options. Their turkey meatballs were great. I had a turkey with marinara sauce and a buffalo turkey with the honey siracha. Full of flavor and not dry, which can happen with ground turkey. I'd also recommend the brussel sprouts. They are fried and crispy, not just sautéed and called fried.

Great food and service. When I went for my first time, the owner personally approached me and my friends to greet and seat us which I thought was very kind and welcoming. Definitely enjoyed the Shepards Pie a lot and nothing could ever beat the Chesapeake Fries they offer! Servers are really nice and really good at what they do. Definitely would come back and recommend anyone to visit for a nice pleasent meal.
Amazing fajitas and the service is very friendly.  The food is well priced.  Good parking.

Had lunch here today and was not disappointed. I really like the salsa. I had one chicken and one beef burrito. The chicken was great the beef burrito was a little dry, but still tasty. I will try something else next time. It wasn't as good as Miguel's, but it was still good.

Great food again.  Just too much food...amazingly, as we left my wife said "one less fish and something with artichokes..."  

That was what we said the last time we went!

Based upon my lunch time visit, I was expecting a fabulous dining experience with my wife and our friend.  Sadly, all our entrees were improperly flavor balanced.  Maybe it was the chef's night off.

We arrived on Thursday evening and were seated promptly.  The room was very dark, relying mainly upon the natural light at the front of the restaurant and some dimly lit hanging lights that were more ornamental than functional.

Our service was friendly and efficient throughout the evening which started off well.  We put in an order for the Bacon Wrapped Apricots - tequila soaked apricots, hickory smoked bacon, jalapeno kumquat honey glaze.  These were tremendous!  There was a bit of sauce on the side that added an extra layer to the flavor!  Definitely get these!

We also shared the Foie Gras - sauternes, charcoal honey, espelette jelly, pistachios, country bread.  I really liked this, especially the bites where I got a whole pistachio.  The ladies thought it was good, but thought it a bit light on flavor.

I then ordered the "Toad in a Hole" - toasted brioche, egg, asparagus, prosciutto, roasted peppers, poached pears, shaved brussel sprouts, brie, truffle mushroom puree.  The way it was served, I ended up cutting up the entire serving first so that I could get multiple flavors in every bite.  Otherwise, there would be some bites that were mostly bread.  If you look through the ingredients, you can easily see that lots of flavor combinations made this a delicious meal.  My only complaint was that the tableware knife was too dull to cut through the prosciutto.  

Our friend ordered the Harvest Salad - endive, roasted beets, goat cheese mousse, portobello, blackberries, buttermilk vinaigrette, pistachio granola.  She raved about how good it was.  My wife agreed.  They both thought it the high point of dining.

And then the entrees came out.  

There was no balance to my Pork Belly - red chile glaze, bacon braised swiss chard, smoked onion rings, white bean puree, sweet corn relish, peach coulis, arugula salad.  Again, I needed to cut the meal completely because the plate was stacked high.  The pork was very salty.  The chard and arugula were clumped and had a more intense flavor than expected, overwhelming the rest of the ingredients.  The bites without the greens were overwhelmed by the saltiness.  It just didn't work.  I could see promise in that the pork was cooked tender and the plate looked rather nice, but the balance was wrong.

My wife had the Beef Brisket - sweet corn pudding, roasted creamer potatoes, heirloom tomato puree, baby carrots, hickory gastrique, pickled mustard seeds.  She found the brisket on the dry side.  

Our friend ordered the Fettuccini - crushed tomato sauce, roasted garlic ricotta, pancetta.  The restaurant does offer meatballs for another $3.75, but since our friend is usually a light eater, she passed and just went with the basic plate.  Sadly, the flavors were basic.  She thought spaghetti at home had more appeal than what she was served.  I get it:  If you want spicy, get the meatball.  But if they are going to offer a meatless version, then the flavors should stand on their own.

We finished sharing a creme brulee with pear sorbet and candied rice krispies.  The brulee was good, but the sorbet was teeth chilling cold (I wonder if they used liquid nitrogen?)  Uncomfortable to eat, and then it tasted like juice.  Not much flavor complexity.

I don't like writing negative reviews or down grading from excellent ones.  But I could see the disappointment in my guest's faces.  Since we traveled nearly an hour to dine, it is unlikely we will be back any time soon.  Maybe we were just a few years late catching this place when it was one of the best in town.
Rev #17

When we had the salsa, we should have stopped there and cut our losses.  It tasted like stewed tomatoes from a can!  This is not authentic Mexican food by no means.  So bland, it was disgusting.  Every dish we ordered was hard to swallow.

If a friend asked me for great Italian food I wouldn't say here. But, if they said that they wanted a fun place this would definitely be the place I recommend. The food is good but it's just a fun place to have a  casual dinner, and play some bocce ball. You come here with friends, drink, eat, laugh, and make memories. Not many places create that atmosphere.

I'm really only rating the oyster happy hour. Don't know about any other aspect but happy hour is definitely worth it. $1 oysters.. Can't beat that price! A little less fresh than what you'll find elsewhere on the coast but then again, we are in a landlocked state so thats kind of what I expected. Seems like a lot of other people felt that way too since it was pretty crowded on a Friday afternoon. Also, you can get one free hour of parking in the garage across the street. We managed that easily - those oysters go fast!
I had THE WORST lasagna from this place. The taste was awful. It was served cold and the service was terrible. Don't waste your time.

YESYESYES - my new favorite neighborhood place.

My boyfriend and I went to Audrey Claire last night for a late Valentine's Day dinner. We had been meaning to come here for months and are glad that we did. The food was PERFECTION from beginning to end.

READMEH: Let me preface this by saying that I'm disappointed that so many people have knocked their star rating because of such meaningless $h!#
The ONLY complaint that I have that seems to be pretty consistent on here is that though we had reservations, we were seated at a table literally right in front of the door and it was a biting 25 degrees out BUT, what the hell do you expect? It's a small space, it's bound to happen, and the place was so toasty warm it barely bothered me and I CERTAINLY won't knock them a star because of something so silly.


I ordered the pear gorgonzola flat bread for my appetizer, lamb for entree, and we shared creme brulee for dessert. My boyfriend had asparagus & feta for appetizer, the pork chop w/ apple butter as an entree.

The flatbread was HUGE - too much for just me, but it was delicious. My boyfriend isn't a big cheese fan and he loveddd it. And we had leftovers to take home :)

My lamb was literally cooked to perfection. The accompanying mashed potatoes were creamy and yummy, the asparagus was cooked just right. It was literal meal perfection.

My boyfriend VERY much enjoyed his pork, but indicated it was a bit overdone for his liking. He still loved it nonetheless and said he would absolutely order it again. The apple butter was to DIE for.

The creme brulee was creamy and a wonderful way to end our meal.

PS - It's a BYOB, what's there not to like?

I love this restaurant the managers and owners are brothers and their father is the chef in the kitchen. The food is always good and fresh. They even deliver locally. The dishes are full portions with fresh vegetables and decorated beautifully. One of my favorites is the salt and pepper soft shell crab perfectly cooked there is a family basket and the basket is made out of shredded potatoes then deep fried and not greasy at all and filled with seafood I also like there beef in the oyster sauce and their lettuce wraps. But Who am I kidding I've been going there for over a year and have not found one thing
 that I did not like.  They do not rush you thru a meal and make us feel right at home.

I'm sorry, but the only reason I gave it two stars is because the crepe lady made me a wonderful strawberries and chocolate one. The crab was wildly over cooked, the roast beef was drier than the surrounding desert, and the bbq pork and noodle soup was miserable, the little oriental who cooked it had to be reminded twice that there was a customer waiting. $30+, never again.

This was my first time at Frankie's.  I ordered the Mexican omelette with chorizo.  It tasted great, was perfectly salted, and had a hint taste of sour cream in the mix, which was surprisingly great.  I also really liked that you could get asparagus on the side instead of potatoes.  My only so so feelings were towards the coffee which was average (mug was dirty on the outside).  Overall I would definitely come back for the food.  Very nice staff.  My waitress was quick and friendly.

I absolutely love The Hollow and feel so lucky to have it as my neighborhood restaurant! The waitstaff is so kind and thoughtful and have given me and my family excellent service even during busy evenings. Their beer and food is delicious and there is no better place to sit by the fire in the winter, or sit on a patio after a summer dog walk.

Can't beat it! Some of the best pastries in the area. All of the pastry pockets are delish,  my favorite is the sweet cream cheese one. The cinnamon bun topped with fresh whipped frosting is to die for. Extremely well priced! A box of 8 different pastries cost me 18 bucks, I love it!
Sad to say but they are closed.  We just had a family lunch last Sat.  Great service & food was really good.

I stumbled upon this place by accident the first day I moved to town and I'm so glad that I did! This place is absolutely adorable. The brunch was mouth watering and the service was so entertaining. You can tell the people who work here really love their jobs. You know I had to grab a slice of cake for the road and it did not disappoint! I'll be back for sure.

One of the best restaurants in town. Great food. I have ordered a  different entrée every time I've eaten there and they've all been awesome. The prices are fantastic, you don't get more bang for your buck anywhere. I would gladly pay more for every plate that landed on my table. Try this place if you haven't. You won't be disappointed.

I had a horrible experience at this place.  We were looking to try something new as I don't eat meat and they have lots of choices. Neither my husband or myself like what we got.  The waiter after taking our order was not attentive and I told him I did not like my food.  The waiter helped my husband with his food but did not come to even check if I was OK.  I would never return.

I don't often have any issues with this location, I come often on my lunch break. The staff are friendly, every now and then there's someone who is not, but my food has never been wrong so I could care less. I was compelled to leave a review today because I overheard one of the staff members instructing another staff member on how to properly flip and store food. I've worked in food for a long time and that is one of the worst things a restaurant can do incorrectly. It made me breathe easier to hear this girl give proper food storage instruction! Love it!

What an amazing hidden gem!
The service was impeccable.  The food was beyond my expectations.
Our entire table was so very impressed.
If you have not stopped in to experience this establishment,  it is time to be impressed.

I would be eating oysters; but, the Corner Oyster House is out of Oysters on the half shell.  You would think if Oyster House was in your name, you wouldn't run out of oysters.  It's sort of like McDonald's running out of burgers.
Seriously, no freaking oysters, REALLY? Who manages this place?  No Oysters- I would have shit canned him just for the principle.
Ugh!
Oh yeah, their restrooms are a mess too!  You can't un-smell urine; I can still taste it!

This was the last place I ate in NJ before heading out west, so I've got a bit of a soft spot for it. That said, it really is a perfectly fine place for what it is: a restaurant in the mall. Have reasonable expectations for price/quality/portion and you won't be disappointed.

I loved the b&b-like setting - it felt like eating brunch in a charming old house.  There's limited porch seating, which would have been nice had the weather been nicer.

The menu had all sorts of yummy options - mostly vegetarian-friendly, but there were a few sandwiches that a meat eater would enjoy (BLT, etc).  I had a very tough time deciding between some of the grilled sandwiches (all of which came with your choice of side) or the yummy sounding breakfasts.  I ended up with a delicious egg dish scrambled with tomatoes, cheese, etc.  Overall, everyone was pleased with their food & ready to head back for more!  

BOTTOM LINE:  The service was friendly and attentive, the old-house setting was charming, and I loved all the delicious vegetarian-friendly options on the menu.   Bonus for having a few meat options so your carnivore friends will be willing to come along too!

Tijuana Flats is one of the better food chains with a different flavor I'm a big fan. I personally have probably been to 20 different Tijuana Flats this location the staff is very friendly and fast pace it is one of the better locations to try

Had the pleasure of checking out this brand new bakery today with some friends.  The interior is beautiful, classy, and clean.  Right away, the bakery case filled with the most beautiful cakes caught my eye, and I had such a hard time deciding what to order!  I finally settled on a slice of Carrot Cake and a Toffee Nut cookie, both of which were delicious in that "you'd never know it was gluten free" kind of way.  Decadent, moist, and so flavorful!  The icing on the cake was so light and fluffy.  I also got to try the Berry, Birthday, and Chocolate Almond Praline cakes, and oh man- I can't wait to go back and try more!  They also have great looking coffee/espresso drinks.  I hear they will have lunch service in the future-yes!  Each staff member was welcoming and friendly; service was prompt.  I'm hooked.

If you don't want to read all of this just know:
Food: Bad,Old,Microwaved
Costumer Service: Horrible. No matter what your wrong.




My family went to this restaurant to eat because it was recommended by a friend. So we were expecting pretty good food and we love Peruvian food. When my mother order Peruvian fried rice (arroz chaufa), This dish was NOT cooked fresh and was obviously pre warmed/microwaved. My sister order a Pesto spaghetti (tallarin Verde) and the pesto sauce was sour. My sister couldn't not even eat the dish. When my mother smelled the pesto is smelled spoiled. When we called the server she was very nice and removed 2 dishes and when she went to the back to talk to the owner and chef we could hear screaming and yelling in spanish. They were saying that's how it was supposed to taste and that we were wrong. The server told us the same thing even though we already heard it from all the yelling. When my mother confronted the owner she also said the same thing and even got mad at us! We have had this dish many times and this was one of the worse. Please save your money and go somewhere else.

Was in Santa Barbara for over a week and went to San bar on our first weekend there  and had so much fun. The cocktails were amazing. There was a big group of us and maybe a bit loud but food was great and our boy Nicholas kept the chips and salsa coming. And he was quite entertaining. He told us places to see and hiking locations. Had so much fun. Can't wait to visit again!!!

It was incredibly flavorful! Wide range of fresh produce. Great selection of seafood and meats. The white fish was very tender and flaky. The small sausages were my favorite on the meat side. The conveyor belt was consistently well stocked. I got the spiciest soup base, and it was very enjoyable.

Service was friendly and on point. Drinks and soups were refilled without delay. If you have any questions the staff are happy to help. It was a great experience, and will definitely be back.

The food was decent but the service cheapened the experience.

There are not that many seats in the place, but the two servers somehow seemed to be missing all night.  Water is never refilled... no actually they did refill the water twice all night, but we were there for almost two hours.  Which emphasizes the main problem.  The service was extremely slow by (what appears to be) no fault of the chef.
