We got our appetizers almost 30 minutes after we ordered them, and when we got them they were cold... as if they were sitting somewhere in the kitchen for 10 minutes before someone could "find the time" to drop them off.

The entrees, while also decent, would have been much better if they were hot... and on warm plates... and served with a refill of water.  It was odd how quickly the server walked away after dropping them off.  There was no "can I get you anything else?" or even "enjoy!"  Come on guys, you could be much better than this! Sub par experience.

This could be a great food town if it wasn't for misses like this.

What gem of a find. Outstanding food. Was packed but they still fit us in at the bar. The French fried eggplant is a must. Also tried charbroiled clams. Outstanding. Fish was fantastic, not over done. Highly recommend.

I LOVE it here. The servings are a good size and the combinations are so good. I wish it was in a better location because I don't like having to drive through downtown to get it but because it's so good I'll definitely be coming back

Well I finally made it to Mama Irma!  We went on a Saturday evening and were trying to make it to the Pacers game so we only had an hour for dinner.  We showed up around 6pm and there were still several tables available.  By the time we left around 7, a few more had filled up.  

We had planned on ordering the fried rice with chicken and the seafood soup (I can't remember their true names).   The waitress came back and said that because the only fish they had left was mahi mahi and due to that they were going to have to increase the price of the soup that evening to $22...it's already the most expensive item on the menu at $17 (I believe) and $22 seemed a little steep for soup so we switched that out for the cilantro beef dish instead.  

Both dishes were quite excellent!  The beef was super tender and had a nice sauce.  I think we both agreed that we liked the fried rice better which really was delicious.  

The service overall was okay (but I wouldn't say spectacular).  We asked for our check and the waitress brought it relatively quickly but then took her dear sweet time coming back to actually take our card.   They kept mixing up the orders between our table and the one next to ours and there are only about 10 tables in the whole restaurant so it seemed a little silly that they couldn't keep them straight.  

I would go back to this and try a few more items but I think we'll order the fried rice every time!
This place sucks. The manager was condescending and they took 45 just for my fries. I paid way to much for the free burger i got.

just had Wings for the first time after moving here recently and probably wont be ordering there a ton, just average for Chinese, prices are really good, but some of the meal items were not the greatest.  We ordered about 4 different meals, 2 different soups, and an appetizer sampler platter.  The one thing we all commented on was their wontons, there was absolutely nothing inside any of them it was basically just a chip, kind of strange.

Fantastic happy hour! Half off every drink, bottle, pitcher on the menu until 7pm. Service is friendly and efficient and the tapas are fantastic. A few of my favorites include: patatas brava, short rib sandwich, tartar de atun and the meatballs.

Okay, this place has been featured on more shows that we can swing a dead cat at.  Ellen, the Today Show, countless cooks/chefs from Food Network rave about this place...for good reason.  The food is good (yeah, its all about the biscuits) but the ambience is really fun, friendly, and is full of character.
If you come expecting fine dining or exquisite southern cooking you'll be disappointed.  But if you want good food for a good price in a place that's fun and makes you want to come back again...then you'll be very pleased.
Came to Geno's before going to Pat's, and overall I think Pat's sandwich was slightly better. The flavor of the meat better, but Geno's cheese sauce takes the win.

Decent Po Boy if they have all of the ingredients there. Went during tropical storm Barry. Decent area and had to deal with no AC but what can you do during a storm. I got the roast beef po boy. It was serviceable but nothing special to make me want to keep going back there.

Il Posto is tiny, and it's located on a "nowhere" corner in the dead of uptown, but it's an excellent place to stop in for an espresso, a gourmet grilled cheese sandwich or a salad. I've had their "bruschetta grilled cheese," with fresh tomatoes, garlic and basil grilled between two crusty slices of Italian artisan bread. It was really good. I've also had their Italian tuna sandwich...no mayonnaise on this, just a high-quality oil-packed tuna with a lemony dressing. So good. Their coffee and espresso is not mind-blowing, but certainly as good as CC's or Hey Cafe or any of the other places you could visit in the area. There are 7-8 small tables and chairs where you can sit and eat your food, drink your coffee and even use the wi-fi, although I wouldn't really suggest Il Posto as the kind of coffee shop where you should park yourself for hours. The seating is somewhat limited, so it seems a bit rude to overstay your welcome. The staff has always been friendly, even if they are sometimes flustered during peak hours. I've never had their baked goods, but I've heard very good things. I've been to Il Posto many times, and doubtless I will return.

One of the best meals I've had in STL, hands down!  This was the full experience!  Historical Missouri ingredients, local Ozark cuisine, presented in 2019.  So cool!  Everything on the plate had a defining purpose and taste!  So cool!  Just GO!!!

Are we being pranked? We wanted to love this restaurant! Did chef's tasting for full table.
Please keep in mind, we are not the Karens and Kens of dining out. We are gracious, respectful patrons, as well as very generous tippers regardless of the experience/ food we receive. 

This experience was so underwhelming on so many levels, MAINLY for the price point. I've never walked away from a place feeling like I got robbed  until now. The portions were minuscule, even for a chef's tasting. There were fancy, seasonal ingredients prepared in tiny portions with odd sauces, with nothing particularly delicious or craveavble about them, and with no flow or connection from one dish to the next. 
I'll also say, the ambience was just awkward- the whole minimalist upmarket-cafeteria Phish (?!) vibe was a bit much. 

Our server was ok, although did not offer us a single word of apology or correction after we all pointed out being dissatisfied. There was an odd (slightly snobby?) vibe I got from other servers. 

It feels like a place created by hipsters for hipsters who don't care about food so much as about being seen and congratulating each other on mediocrity. Do yourself a favor and save your money for a place a bit less obnoxious, and A LOT nicer on all levels. This place is just not it. 

PS: the wine was great!

Our server was Marina. She took really good care of us. The prices were astounding for fish in California. The drinks were also cheap for the quality. $8-$12. I got the Mussels. The sauce was to die for. It was thick with garlic and vegetables and light tomato. Again Marina was very professional and fast on her feet. My second drink took 3-4 minutes to get to the table. The atmosphere was upscale/ casual and very clean.  We will be going back again for sure!

Excellent service. Ordered beef carpaccio, parpadelle, chicken with panzanella salad, brocollini, and olive oil ice-cream and olive oil cake. Everything was delicious. The skin on the chicken was a bit salty but the meat was tender and juicy. I usually don't enjoy many Italian restaurants because I feel like I can make the food a lot better at home. But this was definitely worth trying. Highly recommended.
Good place for brunch with fast service. Food tastes good. I would recommend it if you're on the go or if you would like to sit down and enjoy!
Awesome dive bar with great staff, had probably one of the best guiness's I've had in the states and an actual pour

This Place is the best! 
The drinks are over sized strong and just the way i like em! 
although it is a smaller venue it has personality just like the people in it and the bartenders serving you. The shuffle board is so much fun! A few hot dogs after a few drinks and you will come to realize why it is called "The Buffet" 
when you are on a dive bar crawl stop by this one its a must that is for sure!

Quality products. Great customer service.  However, when ordering on their mobile app it takes a good 30 to 45 minutes for my food to be delivered. That wouldn't be a problem if I weren't less than a block away from the location. Same street and all (City Ave.) Kind of frustrating when they pride themselves on "fast delivery." I even asked the delivery person do they take priority with phone orders over online/mobile app orders. Of course he said no which made me annoyed.

Meh. The wine is good - but when you're a wine bar you have to really try to fuck this up. The food is bland AF. I got the harvest salad which features chicken, cranberries, goat cheese, bacon, apples, and candied pecans. On top of a heap of greens (not iceberg lettuce which was nice!) was maybe an ounce or two of unseasoned chicken, two cranberries, a couple shards of pecan, two tiny pieces of bacon, and I'm guessing they put the dressing next to the salad based on how extremely dry and flavorless it was. The gnocchi that my husband got wasn't much better. 

Recommendation: this place is trying to be bourgier than it actually is when it's about as basic as a French manicure. Have a drink or two here and then head to ANY other place on mass Ave for dinner.

This was our first time here. We ordered 2 items, the meatloaf and grouper sandwich.  The meatloaf was dry and ketchup was put on the dish after the fact (not cooked with the food). Grouper was super small; totally not worth the $18.  Overall, not impressed with the food or the value of the food.

My husband and I came here for our first sit down meal on our trip here to New Orleans. We had Sierra as our server and she was fantastic!! She was so personable, asked our names and where we were from. It felt like we were regulars who she knew personally. It really made the experience great because it felt like home. The food was delicious! We went at like 3pm so it was not super crowded but it was still a nice environment. Definitely recommend.

Based on the restaurant's diverse food offerings, my family decided to visit Amerigo to celebrate my birthday. The food was good (I enjoyed the seasonal grilled peach salad), but the service was lousy. Since we wanted to dine on lighter fare, my family and I had ordered simply. Our meal should have come out quickly. However, we waited more than fifteen minutes for salads, and our waitress forgot to bring my daughter's beverage with her meal. She paid much more attention to a table with two women near us. Overall, this was not a good birthday experience.

Fantastic food, comfortable and inviting atmosphere, extensive menu with a variety of options.

A beautiful layout that offers quality meals using fresh ingredients. I've been here multiple times since they opened at the end of May. As with any new restaurant they needed some time to iron out the kinks but each visit has improved dramatically. 

Their breakfast is some of the best the city has to offer, from Mascarpone French toast to insanely delicious cream chip beef.

Their chicken salad is dynamite, fresh roasted and handpicked.  Most incredible crab cake I have ever sunk my teeth into, challenge it vs any on the planet.

Pizza is also top notch, smaller pie but tons of flavor. Service continues to improve, I'll keep visiting on a weekly basis for breakfast and lunch!

Butchertown has a limited menu with a dozen or so items between starters and main courses and probably twice as many beers plus three times as many wines. For some, this could be a thing. For me, this means that what they have is going to be good. And it was.

I chose the guacamole to start. Fresh made and a little chunky, this scooped up nicely and would have been easy to share if I had been in a sharing mood.

Main course, I chose the tacos. Handmade tortillas (corn or flour) with a choice of proteins. I chose the brisket and the fish. Both were very tasty and very well filled with meat and toppings. Two was enough, three would be fine if you can pick which one you like the least and share it.

Lots of good choices for dessert but I was stuffed after the guac and the tacos and two beers.

Service was top notch. Friendly and warm and sincere from (it says on the receipt Raihanna?). Very nice.

While on vacation in the Redington Shores area, my wife and I viewed many positive reviews for this restaurant so we had to see first hand what the hype was all about.
18oz Lime Margaritas for only $3.00 and $5.00 rum runners started us off with a great taste in our mouths, both figuratively and literally speaking!! 
We started our appetite with a fried coconut shrimp appetizer that was AMAZING! My wife ordered the fried grouper fish with a side of French fries that were soooo good. I order the grilled Mahi (something can't remember) with a side of cooked vegetables. This meal was soooooo good. Our waitress was very quick to bring drinks, napkins, anything we needed. All the interactions with the restaurants employees was very positive and friendly. We will be back again and will tell many friends about this place!!! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND, you WONT be disappointed!

I have reviewed Sushi 7 in the past. It used to be our favorite sushi place, by far. We moved away for two years and were eager to go back to Sushi 7 after moving back. We were very disappointed in the experience. 

We arrived around 3:30pm on a Saturday- there were some people there but it was in no way busy. We made our first order and then proceeded to wait for a very long time. Some of our order came. The waitress told us the rest was on its way. It never showed up and she had to put the order in again. This happened a few more times during our visit- food just didn't show up. I understand a roll being forgotten if a bunch of stuff was ordered at once, but these were stand-alone orders.

We were never offered refills on our drinks. The waitress would apologize for forgetting something, and then say "it's been a very long day." Umm, sorry? Not exactly something you should say to customers.

We found out that Sushi 7 had come under new ownership. Not sure if that attributed to the service issues. We will not be going back.
Only been here once for a special occasion, but loved the food, wine, service and atmosphere.  We will definitely go back again!
Very good, reasonably priced lunches. Excellent variety and nicely prepared food, but service is spotty. Now open in Ardmore, Pa.

The Misses had never been to Cracker Barrel before, and, for some reason, wanted to rectify that situation. So, we loaded up the baby and headed over for a Sunday brunch meal. We probably should have just stayed at home.

Upon arriving, it was packed. We were told the wait time was 20 minutes, but to their credit, they got us sat way faster than that. That was the last time anything moved quickly. As I said, it was VERY busy, and Cracker Barrel was apparently not staffed for it. Literally 15 minutes passed before our SUBSTITUTE waiter arrived; he wasn't our server, Kara was, but he was there to get our drink orders while we waited for Kara to show up. By this point, and without any food or anything to distract her, the baby had started her countdown to meltdown. We place our drink orders with our backup server, (a regular coffee for me, and a raspberry tea for her), and an order of toast for the babe. Side note, the flavored tea is ASTONISHINGLY sweet.

Drinks and toast come out fine, but we still haven't seen any of this elusive Kara we had heard so much about. (Also, we had to ask server #2 for the breakfast menu, as they had given us just the lunch menus). We quickly look over the menus, and after a few minutes, Kara finally makes her arrival. She was very nice, but the wait was a bit ridiculous. Also annoying, Kara is the soft spoken type. Like I said, the place was packed, so there was lots of ambient noise. Cracker Barrel also had the background Muzak going, so the Misses couldn't hear anything Kara was saying. The Misses told her FOUR TIMES, "I can't hear you...." but Kara didn't raise the decibel level ONCE. Finally, I just relayed what was being said between the two.

Communication volume issues conquered, we got the orders in and waited for our food. By this point, I was halfway through my cup of coffee. A server walked by with a carafe, and said "sir, did you have regular or decaf?" I said "regular" and that was the end of that.....he just strolled off, with his carafe of decaf, never to return with regular coffee. Oh well.

The food finally makes it to the table, and by now, we are in Toddler Meltdown level 2; she's out of the high chair, and tossing food off the side of the table, so we ask for to-go boxes immediately. Kara whispers if we need anything else, and I ask for more coffee, plus my biscuits that didn't come out with the rest of the food.

We spend the next 2 minutes WOLFING down rubbery eggs, flavorless grits and gravy, and old looking sausage and bacon. The pancakes were ok at least. We ask for the check and get out of dodge; the Misses completely underwhelmed with her inaugural Cracker Barrel experience.

Cracker Barrel avoids one star because the people were nice, the food isn't expensive, and they have good choices, but you will be utterly nonplussed. It's a kitschy, main street Americana themed diner. But, you probably already knew that. This location is probably a little busier than others because it's RIGHT off of the NJ Turnpike. Eh, we won't be back for a very long time, if ever.

Sketch: It was love at first bite!

I'd been dying to try this place so imagine my surprise when I went to a friend's house one night and he lived right next door! Totally Jelly! He would rub it in my face how whenever he was hungry, he'd just call them up, roll out in his PJs, run next door, grab a burger and get his munch on. 

I finally went for the first time on New Year's Eve. Sauntering in in my fancy NYE attire, I sat down at a small table and ordered a Cyclops burger. The waitress asked how I wanted my egg and I said "Cooked?" She told me "No no - you don't want a scrambled egg on top of your burger. Get it over easy. Trust me." So I did. There was no turning back. When my burger appeared, there was a delicious fried egg on top with delectable looking bacon peering seductively out at me from underneath. On first bite, the yolk broke, blending - NAY - melding in the warm, delicious, perfectly medium burger sandwiched between two lightly toasted brioche buns. I was in heaven. If the clock had struck midnight and the world ended that evening, at least I would have died knowing I had just sampled the best burger I'd ever tasted. 

Fries are huge and hand cut, made in house. If you're with a friend, get one to share. There's plenty to go around! Try the aioli for the dipping sauce - you won't be disappointed. PS: They have stuff other than burgers and they also cater to all your hipster vegan friends as well - plus desserts! 

Oh, and can we talk about the decor? Bring your art school skills (or your Draw Something skills) to a real piece of paper: construction paper & crayons & markers are provided at each table so you can be a Burger Picasso. And I mean, come on, who doesn't effing love coloring!? 

Subsequent visits (Once to go, once to eat in just last week) have tried to get me to steer clear from the Cyclops and try something new, but I just can't do it. Me + Cyclops Burger = BBFFL (Best Burger Friends For Life).

I do n I don't want to post this review...I want to post cuz this place n the familia who runs it are absolutely amazing but, I don't want to post cuz my selfish ass doesn't want to share this awesome food lol. But due to covid19 n Reno/Sparks beginning phase 1 of opening up I feel they truly deserve the love and support. Tonight, we ordered Chemas my dad happened to introduce me to this wonderful hole in the wall taqueria when he lived in Sparks. We have become frequent customers n I tend to ALWAYS want to have my bday dinner here. The owners are always there either one or both of them,when dining in before the Coronas, they have always been fast fresh n friendly on drinks n chips n salsa. I haven't been here since my bday in February n since my medical office decided to fire me during Covid19 I needed a pick me up, n this was it. I absolutely adore the Chile Verde Wet Burrito there I also occasionally order the cabeza (beef head) burrito, n again, most spectacular!! Tonight's order from Uber eats didn't go well at first, as I never received it...I was super sad. My BF said go ahead n reorder with pick up from car n instructions to contact us...the second time was perfect everything was hot (actually made it to the correct address) n still hot. My driver was cool n witjrdceith me when he couldn't find my apartment (which I assume happened to the first driver,but he could've called instead of leaving it wherever or taking it). All I have to say about chemas is the staff, the good and depending on who us delivering from Uber eats is amazing...eat here you WILL NOT BE DISAPPOINTED!!!

My girlfriend and I eat a lot of sushi ...no really ...a lot and Zento is the real deal. Creative menu items, quality food and service, reasonable prices. One of the best sushi places that we have been to on the east coast.

The suggestions from the help are endless. they really truly know their teas! I had the peach infused oatmeal and a large iced green tea and it was transcending. just so good,life changing.
I ended up leaving with tea to go and a honey bear.
Beautiful view and wonderful people.
I was so relaxed i thought i was going to slip into a coma.
overall a lovely experience fer sure.

Madre de Dios!

In addition to vegan cuisine they're now serving dishes with meat. Excellente.

Great food! Great service! Very welcoming (hence the name). This place is the closest to real Cajun food from Louisiana as it gets here in the desert. The food made me smile, which is the true essence of southern food. Great job, guys!

P.S. I thought their prices were very reasonable...

I had Tom Kah soup at a Thai restaurant near Huntington Beach this past weekend and enjoyed it SO  much so I sought it out here.   had eaten decent+ curry at TAP before so I ordered a take out of the soup.  I was quite disappointed... it was salty and the soup base didn't convey an aroma of coconut or other fragrance... only mushroom.  I like mushrooms but this was more like a mushroom soup with 3 large shrimp in it.  It was darker colored not coconut (whiter) ..actually rather bland and I ended up adding Siracha to it... didn't help much.  I'll continue to search for a good Tom Kah soup.

Shoutout to el diablo of trolley square for hooking my drunk ass up at 9:55 when they were trying to close up shop. Didn't even give me an attitude. 

You're the true heroes of the night. I'll be back.

Visited: 12/3/18 & 12/5/18
Ordered: Breakfast tacos and orbit bowl

Finally finally finally. A quality driven company with fair prices, fair portions, quality ingredients, a thoughtful menu, and consistency. Why is this so hard to accomplish in today's world? 

We are constantly on the hunt for this type of place and virtually every restaurant who claims to focus on these things fall terribly short. The food was flavorful in the right ways, excellent ingredients and not an over indulgence in oils and fake fillers/ingredients. 

I'll also add a gentleman who I believe was the owner, went around to each table and asked how everyone's food was. Customer service, quality food, fair prices, and counter service. This should be the standard. 

Thank you and well done!

It was a touch overpriced but worth it for the experience. Atmosphere is 10/10 and the staff is amazingly sweet and helpful. Our apps were great - awesome pork buns and crab spring rolls. My sushi was good too. I just really enjoyed it for date night.

My Wife and I decided to try the fried chicken at the Firehouse Bar & Grill. We were very pleasantly surprised. Our server, Jennifer, was very prompt and attentive at getting our drinks and taking our order. We asked about the fried chicken and we decided on the four piece meal. It came out fairly quickly and included green beans, mashed potatoes with chicken gravy,a piece of French bread with garlic butter and four pieces of perfectly cooked and seasoned fried chicken. It has been a long time since we have had chicken that was seasoned well enough to make us want to come back for more! All pieces were cooked perfectly, crisp savory coating outside and piping hot juicy inside. the portions were ample and we were able to take home a couple of pieces to have for lunch the next day. We will definitely be returning soon to try some other menu items but wouldn't hesitate recommending the chicken to family and friends.

Awesome locally-owned cafe with large portions! Pancakes are bigger than your plate! Debby has owned this popular place for 17 years. I love going here for their breakfasts. If you don't show up at the crack of dawn, expect to have to put your name in and wait a while outside. Well worth the wait. I like to go by myself or one other and sit at the counter to watch the cooks in action. If you don't mind the counter, you can get in and out faster than those waiting for a table.

Our office is right around corner, so we thought, hey try it.  
OMG:  FOOD:  yumola!!  Service, superfriendly!  
Heading to Brewery Light tour?  Give Cafe Piazza a try!

Teetering on the edge of 3 or 4 stars on this one.  As a few others have noted, there are some stellar things going on with parts of the menu; but, there are other parts that for one reason or another lag behind.  And, unfortunately, something (attentiveness? attitude?) about the service seems just a bit awkward and rough around the edges.  The overall experience seems to clash with what management appears to be striving for.  Hopefully they can figure it out, soon, because the medi/tapas concept is a welcome addition to the burgeoning dining seen in Conshohocken.

From our first visit, I remember enjoying the tartufo pizza and the lamb chop tapas with fig & sherry reduction (though they took the words "petite" to heart with the lamb).  More recently, I tried the Kobe burger, which was definitely juicy, but, the entree was a little bit too simple and casual above, below, and around the Kobe itself.

In a nutshell, this place exudes high potential, but, the general consensus on Yelp (and I agree) is that Isabella is under-performing slightly in it's first 6 months.

Because we live so close, I am sure we will be back, at least for light dinners or happy hour.

Oooof this place is so good! Cant go wrong with any of the food or drinks on the menu. I'm a sucker for a good dip spread as an appetizer and BaBa does it so well. The pita that comes with the dips is unreal. I could eat the pita without the dip.

Best breakfast cart in University City. If you're a Penn student, you know Bui's as THE magical hangover cure on campus. If you aren't hungover, it's still a filling, cheap, delicious way to start your day. I usually get the veggie special with Bui sauce (some heavenly combo of mayo and sriracha) and I highly recommend you try it too!

I come here once every few months when I'm in the area.  I think in the last few years, the quality of the food and service has declined.  The latest example was our dining experience last night.  Our server greeted my husband and I when we arrived.  We were waiting on another couple, so we ordered just waters to start figuring we might share a bottle of wine as a table.  When our friends arrived, they stated they needed a few minutes to look at the drink menu as the waitress pounced on them when they came in.  After a good 10 minutes, our waitress came back to ask if we were ready to order.  I went ahead and ordered my food as did everyone else.  I knew I wasn't going to order a cocktail, but the waitress neglected to ask anyone else if they wanted anything else to drink.  She walked away and I asked my husband if he had decided against a glass of wine.  Our friends mentioned they, too, had forgotten to order drinks since she just took the food order.  The waitress never came back to ask if we needed anything else until the appetizer came out (sweet potato fries - they were pretty decent).  Before she ran off, my husband and friends managed to get their drinks orders in.  Then the food came out...
The person who brought our food out gave the steak fajitas to my friend who had ordered them, then asked who had the tuna (none of us), and the hummus platter (none of us).  He then figured he had the wrong table so he took the fajitas back from my friends and went to figure out where he was going.  A few minutes later, the waitress found him and brought the dishes back to us.  The "tuna" was my husbands filet, the "hummus platter" was my lentil salad, and we were short one entree which came a few minutes later.  The problems:
1.)  I had ordered filet tips with my lentil salad - there were no filet tips to be found, and honestly, there were no lentils to be found, either.  The vinegarette was also extremely bland.  
When I brought up the filet tips to the waitress when she came by to check on us, she said they were coming right out....a solid 15 minutes later.  I was almost finished eating by then and requested they be taken off our bill (they were, but I was looking forward to them!).  
2.)  My husband had explained to the waitress he liked a "hot, pink center" and she mentioned that would be "medium".  The filet was severely overcooked.  I encouraged my husband to send it back, but he didn't.  Later, he mentioned he wished he had but was hungry.

Overall, a disappointing experience.  We won't be returning which is sad - I used to like this place a lot!!

Homey Charm, but I Would Prefer a Menu

Some friends were visiting from out of town so 6 of us met at this restaurant.  The place looks very homey and you would expect it to be an inexpensive place with an emphasis on pasta.  Instead, it is more pricey than usual and they focus on high-end proteins like grouper, rib-eye steaks, veal chops, etc.

The squirrely thing is that there is no menu.  Since they only show the high-end mains, you really don't know all the options.  And you have to be a bit aggressive to ask prices for everything.  The veal chop, for example was something like $38.  And when we asked about wines, our server suggested one.  When I asked, I discovered it was $90.  That would have been a rude surprise when we got the check.

The food was very good, but nothing transcendent.  The best thing was probably the grouper piccata.

Service was friendly.

I would go again and I would ask lots more questions about what they have to offer.  I guess they feel that there is a certain amount of charm in not having a menu.  But I would have appreciated one.

I seriously cannot say enough good things about the Tavern. The owners are some of the kindest and most genuine people you will ever meet. They have started hosting open mic nights, trivia events, special occasions for the colleges clubs/fraternities, and more. They care for the students and their community more than some of the staff do lol. On top of that, the food is amazing. You can't go wrong with the grouper sandwich, the buffalo shrimp mac n cheese, the nachos, or any of their beers on tap. I will be leaving my college soon and will be coming back here as often as I can, it's worth it!
Great service, nice ambiance!  The bread is so delicious!  The flounder was excellent.  Jambalaya was meh.  Gumbo was good.

You know what? I really enjoyed this place. I can't get enough of their sesame tofu, but after tonight- I'm done. The last time I ordered from them, they spilled a container of soup all over my food. The delivery guy threw out the rice and left me with half a container of soup. I contacted the restaurant and they were very rude and gave me the old "Sorry! Nothing else we can do!" 

Tonight I ordered several things from them and after an hour and a half I get a call from them saying they decided to close early and wouldn't be delivering my meal. Great. Thanks for waiting an hour to let me know. If only this place was run by people with even the slightest bit of common sense. 

Now it's time to find a new vegetarian Chinese place....

the other night i went to saudia shuler's and had a great meal.someone had told me it was the best soul food in philly and coming from georgia, i believe it. mac and cheese excellent, sweet tea that will melt your teeth just as it is intended to do. good fried chicken. i was also really impressed by the place because i left my wallet there and when i called, saudia herself told me she had found it and would hold onto it for me until i came to get it. i never thought i'd ever see that thing again and was very grateful. this place also has a cool atmosphere with the barberseats in the back and the r&b. i'll be back!

So a kind of weird review. I went in on a Sunday night about 6. The atmosphere was amazing and the hostess was the best employee on the whole restaurant. I was alone and wanted a table and as it got later all the two tops around me filled up. One table left because a server never came over. The other table next to me was told about the specials ( I wasn't). I ordered a beer  ( the didn't have it a Miller light). I then asked for a pinot Grigio. They don't have that. I ordered a PBR. I ordered the spinach dip. Was good very different but good. I ordered a green apple martini. They didn't have the ingredients to make it. So I ordered another beer. I was by myself and didn't notice when they brought it and they placed it at the end of the table in the exact spot my empty one was and never said anything ( mind u.  I'm alone and missed this. I get my chicken fingers. I cut them because they are fresh from the flyer. First one raw in the middle. 2nd one. Raw in the middle.   The rest where perfect and delicious. Server offered to make more, but I already finished. So she said I'll take one of your beers off. I said yes only had one beer. She was like no here's one. I was thinking  I just ate all the fingers. Drank all the water because I didn't know u delivered a beer to my table. So recap. Server was good just over busy. Took 3 tries to get a drink.  Didn't know the specials. The hostess was busting her ass seating.  Bussing tables.  Getting water. Food that was cooked was delicious. Not sure if I would ever go on again.  Maybe I'll try breakfast

Our neighborhood ordered food last night from the food truck. Delivery was super late due to truck issues (an hour), but they didn't contact us to tell us even though we were waiting outside during the window they told us. The food was poor quality and cold.
Great food and great service! Beer flights were great.  Our waitress was very helpful. Had good parking options.

The food is amazing they really have to have good customer service. I request food by Uber eat snf the driver don't bring to Items I request, the driver say he never received the items, when I call the restaurant they show me the driver received and because it's not my fault they get me the two beers and call me personally and they apologized for something that was not their responsibility.

So far into NJ that it is rare to be owned by Koreans. The flavours were not off. That means it doesn't taste a little like Chinese or Japanese or American even. But it is blanded down for the American taste.

Very low cost for Korean too! Korean cuisine feel so special that they are pricey in NYC. Here, it is reasonable. That is why I gave it four stars.

Three stars for acceptably made Korean food and clean restaurant with a clean bathroom. Nice enough staff. The extra star is for the price! That's right. Korean food shouldn't cost an arm and leg.

Another great meal at Emmas  (3 courses  $24) started with the crab risotto cakes; two large cakes served with marinara, then onto the salmon filet over pasta in a blush sauce; excellent. I had to try the tiramasu, great choice. The $24 special is the summer menu with a lot of choices. Emma's is a BYOB. Will be back next week to try the scallops
Love it. Had the pesto grilled cheese and carrot ginger soup. Great taste at a great price. Plenty of seating on a random Saturday for studying. Across the street from the farmer's market.
Pegs was rated high for a reason.. Best breakfast spot in Reno for 10 years.. Packed and people kept coming in.. Great service and awesome food.. Cannot go wrong with a meal from pegs!

We have eaten here almost every week since this restaurant opened. Food is delicious, fresh, and tasty. Customer service is always great. Waitresses are welcoming, warm, and informative about the menu. 
I'm only giving 3 starts because my food was not the same this time. I asked for medium spicy shrimp eggplant lover. Food was plain, salty, and no spices at all. Also vegetables were saggy. I ended with a mix of shrimp and chicken on my plate. I guess I really missed Chef Kob culinary experience. His food is always amazing. His treat dessert are delicious

Dine here in confidence! You and your party will be sure to get food poisoning that lasts for 3 days!  If you LIKE getting food poisoning this is THE place for you!! The manager is guaranteed to patronize you and insult your intelligence! The owners, ever eager to be their best will deny that anyone can ever get bad Sushi at their 3 star mediocre worse than a sushi buffet place!

Absolutely wonderful experience. Went here on as part of my pledgesister's bachelorette party. Planning the food options for the weekend was an experience because we had to find places with options for: lactose intolerance, vegetarian, general picky-ness. The waitress definitely was showing some "southern hospitality" to our table. Inspite of fact that it was relatively busy, she made it a point of checking in on our table & getting extra salad for the soon-to-be-bride when she noticed that the portion was a bit small (the bride is a combination of lactose intolerant & vegetarian so she had to omit quite a few things from the salad causing it to reduce in size). Pinewood social had a solid selection of upscale cuisine with a modern twist and a very intimate atmosphere. I think the menu might change based on the season but don't take my word as final. The portions aren't always huge but the flavor profile is absolutely indulgent. Excellent selection of drinks Unique to this place is the fact that they have a bowling alley. I absolutely recommend it if you're in town for the weekend, or if you want a chic date night!

Don't expect a gourmet pizza here. This is pretty much a takeout only place. The $5 ready-to-go 1 topping pizza is a quick, cheap and tastes really good for the price. They are much more friendly and personable than the other $5 "pizza, pizza" joint across Fairview. I went here one time and they did not have a pizza ready to go and were very apologetic. They already had one in the oven anyway and it was ready within 5 minutes They more than made up for the small wait. You can also call ahead and get any single topping pizza for $5, which is nice because the other "pizza, pizza" joint now charges an additional $2 for any topping other than cheese or pepperoni.

This is a great, budget friendly option for those busy nights when you just don't feel like cooking.

I am so extremely happy I found a delicious and reasonably priced spot right around the corner from my apartment that has great hummus, and Mediterranean food.! AND ITS DOG FRIENDLY!! The food is great and cocktails are amazing. Plus, they have a great whiskey selection! You can stop by here for a great burger, or try something new.
You will leave loving whatever you get, guaranteed! Personally my favorite thing on the menu is the fattoush salad!! Thank you foxtail for being my new weekly spot!
Amazing place ..love the food ..very clean healthy and peaceful cafe ..me and husband love to go there !!

When I first arrived in Indianapolis I wondered where all of the cafes were (beyond Starbucks).  I wasn't looking for coffee; I was really looking for a tribe of people huddled over laptops to join.

I found them at Henry's on East Street.  It is a bright, mellow cafe with good music and a neighborhood vibe.  Straight-forward food offerings that could be a meal or a snack.  Plentiful seating that includes a sidewalk patio.  Free wifi.

The burger was good and plenty of onion rings and French fries per order.  The staff were very nice.  I would have preferred ice in a cup with my soda.  Not a fan of drinking from a can.  Simple, but on food
Great location for lunch. Our server Andria was awesome. Food tastes great. Very pleased with service, food and atmosphere.
It was good, but I hoped the 'Philly steak' would have been juicier. It seemed as dry as the bread. The toppings were good. I got my hopes up a bit here.
Amazing food vibes and service ! We drove an hour to come here and it's totally worth it and authentic !!!

Disappointing. I went out of my way to come here. I probably should have gone for brunch instead of the normal lunch menu. I'm sure if you're looking for clean, healthy salads and smoothies you're in the right place, but don't go looking for vegan versions of southern food. I just wasn't blown away. The tofu nuggets were not great--pretty bland. The nuggets at Hip City Veg (Philly/DC) are SO much better. If I'm going to eat fried food I'd like it to be worth it! The nachos were good, but each sauce (cheez, salsa, sour cream, and guacamole) should be eaten separately because the flavors are so delicate. Maybe I ordered the wrong thing but it was just too "vegan"--the kind omnivores don't enjoy. I went to Killer Po Boy that evening and had the roasted cauliflower (on po boy bread) and it was ten times better.
I'm sorry to report the were out of beans. yes folks, a Mexican food restaurant without beans. running out of a staple usually means poor management. seriously?? out of beans???

I've been a long time West Chester resident and the meal I had last was sub-par to say the least. Some how two crab cakes and some wet noodles turned out to be over a $100 tab. Our 'entrees' did not come with any type of side or vegetable. My cup of soup appitizer, was just that a cup of warm, what seemed to be your standard generic  lobster bisque. The bright spot of the meal was the Korean BBQ short ribs, but again the theme of the meal was beyond over priced for what you recieved. The Seafood Bouillabaisse.... oh my... you're better off with a bowl of buttered noodles at home. The 'seafood' was non-exsistant, calms the size of dimes. It was such an abomination to anyone calling themselves an oyster bar.

Don't confuse this place with anything else other than a college bar with Thursday night Fish Bowl specials... and to the person saying Red Lobster is gourmet, they are 100% correct.

Amazing food and service great job. Prices are super worth the quality. I always get the pot roast it's so tasty and the dip is fantastic.
Team are super friendly and always making sure I get the food on time.
Awesome fish, chicken, and briscuit tacos. Also the Po'boy was amazing.

Very good burgers!  Kids meals are all good sized and come with dessert. NFL ticket so you can watch all the games. We were not disappointed with anything.  Don't lift the leaf on the painting of David in the ladies room!

X Frenchy's saltwater Cafe is very phenomenal. Jordan was a very excellent server. Jordan  told us    about the fresh seafood that we can get.   Which were coming back to get the next day. Everything was just really good.
Best burger I have ever had! Had the Fat City burger, a must have. Our server Sam was awesome, a great guy. Make sure you ask for him.

I've been here a few times now and have concluded that I'm confused about how this place ended up in east Nashville. I'm not the targeted clientele for BB, but I do eat food, and in a time when general dining seems to be apologizing for not being fine dining, sometimes you want to go somewhere that you can just eat and just leave and not have to know where your produce came from because honestly you're not eating any in this scenario anyway, and this not be at a chili's. Amirite? This is the backdrop of my choices.

Here's my roundup: The service here has always been awkward, the food is grossly overpriced, not inedible by any means, but it's also not anything I'd ever miss eating. Lastly, I'm quite certain that on my last visit my glass of Malbec was diluted with water. Gasp. To those who may claim this enhances the flavour of wine, I commend your resourcefulness and ability to really make a bottle of yellowtail count- perhaps you do not like wine though, which is also possibly commendable. I, however, am not resourceful or commendable and do like wine. A lot. Please don't put water in my Malbec. I will know. 

These problems seem like management problems or business model problems and definitely first world problems. Anyway, I now know what I need to do: Next time I want good old american restaurant "food" that was frozen just for me, I need to buck up and haul myself to a chili's. Hell, who am I kidding- it'll be a TGIFridays.

Its really good food. I loved it. Its authentic South Indian So I kinda liked it because I ve been eating more at americanized Indian restaurants. This one is really good. The ambience is not extravagant but decent enough for a wonderful meal EnJOY guys

C_R_A_P
Wok King in Boise does not care about any customers.
We made an order, picked it up and it wasn't what we ordered 
We called and they argued with us.  
We ordered vegetable chop suey, and we got mixed vegetables - not a single bamboo shoot in the meal.  Their offer was that if we brought it back to SEE IT!!! they would exchange it on our next order.
As a final note, they hung up on us.  
Our conclusion is that WOK KING in BOISE = does not care about customers.

+ The food, that they did get correct - was pretty good.

This rating is based solely upon service. I frequent this particular Starbucks often as it is close to work/school/home. I typically pick up beverages in the morning while placing an order using the Starbucks app which is super easy and convenient. I'm not sure of the gentlemen's name who works the drive thru but he is an absolute pleasure as he offers excellent service with a side of humor. I adore the service but if someone can make me smile BEFORE my coffee and while I tackle traffic on North Lindbergh then they're alright with me! Oh! The Unicorn Frap was delicious!
Solid and very good local restaurant for Thai-Mexican.  All entrees are very large and very flavorful.  We've been a few times and walk away pleased and full each time!

Love shopping at Mazzaro's! All your Italian needs can be found here and then some. High quality ingredients, an olive bar, pastry counter, cheese room, they have it all! They make some great sausages, meatballs, and pastas!

Good food , excellent service and can't beat the price .
Food always taste good and fresh, Feta fries are my favorite , friendly stuff always smiling, and very clean place.

I really wish we discovered this place on our first morning in NOLA because we would have gone here two days in a row. We tried the poached eggs over jambalaya, the eggs cochon, and the peaches and cream french toast. The two savory dishes were out of this world and I recommend both of them highly! The french toast could have used more peaches but was still very delicious.

The highlight were the mimosas... we watched the bartender split an entire bottle of champagne just for our two drinks and then splashed in some OJ and pomegranate juice. So strong and yummy, we got two to-go when we were done with our meals! Basically, go here. I will come to this place every time I am in NOLA!

Great service.   We had the fried Brussel sprouts as an appetizer.  They were great for Brussel sprouts.  One kid had the Po Boy sandwich and the other the calimari.  I had the double eagle chicken sandwich.   I did not want chips so I substituted a side salad with key lime vinaigrette... delicious!   The chips came out as well regardless.  The free hush puppies were excellent!   We will be back.
Most of the items were good. Crab legs small but tasty. Sushi good for price. Bathrooms not so clean. Restaurant clean. Lots of choices.
Everything is so yummy! Never disappointed. With the new expansion service is much faster. My only previous issue.

Ahhhhh.... Hemingway's..... we love this spot inside of Armature Works. One of our favorite places. The food is always so good. Sometimes they're sold out of stuff but that's only because the food is so delish that everyone wants it!! The crew is always friendly and greets you with a smile. We've met the manager a few times and he always has great convo with us. Definitely a staple for us !
Nice atmosphere, very good food. Had the Mahi sandwich and fries. Great fresh fish, only drawback was finding 3 large bones in my filet. Otherwise, a very nice find in Port Richey.

This has to be the worst location. Every time that I come here, I'm always given an attitude. My food is never right. Even after ordering online, I still have to wait 30 minutes when I arrive, this is ridiculous.

5101 Pointe of Tampa Way
Tampa, FL  33647
United States 

The crew at 1:15 had no idea how to operate. When we went through the drive thru we placed our order and included two large iced caramel macchiatos. When we paid for our food we were instructed to pull forward and wait for our order. Moments later a girl walks out and try's to give us someone else's order. Then she came back out with our drink but in a size smaller than we order and they weren't made right. I walked into the store and asked for them to be remade. The manager helped the girl and while they remade the drinks I overheard them complaining about me and the drink. Then when I was given my remade coffees the manager had made me the smallest size of coffee with I did l not order. I am completely unsatisfied with how the manager handled the situation and in the end I didn't get what I ordered. Thanks for a great afternoon stop. Not.

St. Louis Gyros is great to grab a quick gyro to go. They have a ton of options other than gyros but I've only ever had the gyros. They cut the meat off a spindle and throw it on the grill. Then you tell them what toppings you want on it as they make it in front of you (kind of like Subway-style). They have all the classic gyro toppings options but also some that you wouldn't expect like jalapenos and mushrooms. For a gyro and fries it's about $10, which I think is a fair deal. My favorite is the lamb beef gyro, but I've also tried the chicken gyro and it's pretty good too. Also make sure to get some samosas, they are really good too.

Great little hidden gem on the north side of Indianapolis!

When you walk in, you're immediately transformed to a classic Italian restaurant: dim lights, dark stained wood and old pictures of Italy across the walls. I sat in the bar where the chairs were like lounge chairs, there was a fireplace and a full bar with many seats. 

I had the caprese salad and the spaghetti of the day with veal meatballs and a cream tomato sauce. Everything was delicious. 

My only cons: the service was a bit slow. It seemed that they were understaffed at the time but this could be a pro if you're there to catch up with friends. Another con, the bar felt a little crammed. The chairs are oversized (which i love) but your chair will more than likely be up against someone else's chair and it was difficult for the waiters to walk in between tables. 

This place is a little bit more on the expensive side but it was worth it. Plan for $30-40 per person. 

Overall, i was very satisfied with this find and plan to go back!
Pretty good food. No better place to get authentic Mexican. Also good to swing by, have a drink, and watch a game of soccer. Would reccomend.

This place is AAHHHMAZING.

Where else in Nashville can you find a restaurant with an italian deli attached to it. I've been coming to this place for several years and I am never disappointed. The last time I came here, I got their caprese sandwich and it was so freaking good for less than $10. You honestly cant beat that in Nashville.

The deli is really cool because they have homemade gelato which they make every day! So exciting. They used to be the only one for awhile who sold gelato in Nashville. 

Sometimes during dinner, they typically have a long wait for big groups so just make sure you get there early. They also have a little activity area where you can play outside while waiting. It's really neat.

Check this place out!
Avoid this place . Food isn't done right and we had to wait 50 mins for a pick up order . I was bloated and my bf had stomach ache !

A great hidden gem. Very affordable too! The neighborhood is a little sketchy, a man came in that had just been robbed. Anyways we loved the food so much and will definitely come back next time we're in town!

Saw it online while looking for some Korean food. It's not exactly Korean, but it's definitely strongly influence by that cuisine. We enjoyed the rice bowls with pork belly, chicken, and chimichurri. We will stop by again soon. It's in the old Ayers dinner building near Hillsborough High School. We used to stop there when I went to HHS and wanted something better then the cafeteria. It brought back memories of cutting classes and being an idiot as a teenager in the 70s.

We had dinner here last night and all 6 of us loved our meals. The portions were so large everyone had a doggie bag !  Keri, out waitress was very attentive even with having lots of tables in her section. We would definitely come back !

I've been here twice so I'll update if I come again, however the first time I ordered here it was 
 early about 830, I had ordered an everything bagel and an 8oz cream cheese, cinnamon raisin bagel with bacon and egg, and two blueberry bagels regular. Basically they the made the best breakfast sandwich ever! It was quick and they toasted and cream cheesed the everything bagel anyway! The second time I ordered the next day around 945am and it was busy, waited outside to order and waited outside for my order,it was hot outside, and no shaded place to stand, people who called in received their order faster, and after about 10mins I got my order after a couple who ordered the same thing... so I suggest to call ahead if your going there later then 9:15am so everything is ready when you arrive.

Nice atmosphere, food is hot , good and served timely. Staff is always friendly. Our Server, Kim was extremely busy, yet remained focused and polite. She went above and beyond to insure a pleasant dining experience!

I ordered from them tonight. They usually have good pizza. Tonight I had delivery and it took over an hour to be delivered. They got my pizza order wrong. I also ordered a cheese steak and fries. The steak barely had any meat on it and the fries tasted as though they were left over from the night before and reheated and delivered to me. Bottom line I give this place two thumbs down and probably won't be ordering from them again. And to top it off when they were called back about how long the order  and how the food was, the person who answered had he nerve to get an attitude instead of hearing out the customer. Two thumbs down

Overall, a good place to satisfy a crowd of varying palates. I went for  sushi, while my companions who are unfamiliar with Asian food, went for the "safer" kung pao chicken and fried rice. Everyone was satisfied with their choices. The sushi is slightly above average, and the prices are just ok ($6 for spicy tuna, $5 california roll). Not a high end sushi spot, but good for take out. I believe they deliver as well.

I find it very sad that more people don't go here! This buffet is so delicious, their chana masala and paneer are my favourites :) Small buffet but almost every dish is a hit so the extras are unnecessary in my mind. The price is more than reasonable and if you love sweet Indian desserts there are lots to pick from.

i ordered via the drive-thru .. my drink was just blended ice.. the person assisting at the window stopped helping me to tell the other workers about an officer pulling over a car instead of making sure she correctly scanned my app to reload. this isn't my usual SB location but i def don't want to go back and i'm in the middle of moving so i'll be very disappointed if the service is typically this poor.

We have eaten here several times and love it! Last year, we enjoyed our business Christmas party at Provision. The private room was lovely along with the well staffed room and fabulous food. We thought it was such a great, fun new restaurant that we bought several gift cards for Christmas presents. Everyone seemed to love the restaurant! Great place, location, atmosphere but most importantly the food. Highly recommend Provision!

Great place and service. I had the lobster combo the lobster was great, potatoes were cooked perfectly. The crab cake appetizer was also very tasty. The whole family enjoyed their meal. Would have never found it had it not been for yelp the sign is not very big.

For the love of god can I get hot fries. This location I think likes to save the $.03 by saving yesterday's fries then toss them under the heat lamp to heat up the chewy, dehydrated wafers. I just want hot fries! Make sure you always order your fries without salt so they make new ones, I'm mad that I haven't thought about that until now.

Texas Toast Burger on COLD bread.  Burger was not cooked to order as requested and the Sweet Potato Tots were lukewarm at best.  Coleslaw was tasteless.  Staff was very unprofessional.  Won't be back, ever.

Pros:
-nice staff
-cafe is great
-hotel dog

Cons:
-outdated rooms-- cupboards are tacky and kept falling down, carpet is gross 
-service was slow-- had to call 3 times for towels to be delivered to our room
-they said they would clean our room on day 2 of our stay (less frequent due to Covid, understandable)-- they never cleaned our room during the entire 3 day stay.
-rooftop bar was closed every time we tried to go up there.
Both the pizza and wings are good here. General Tso pizza was off the charts good. Hard to find good pizza in South Jersey but we finally found some!

Bang bang shrimp is amazing like always. Went with a party of 5 and my food was the only one correct. Simple bang bang shrimp with sides. They give large portion sizes and try the corn crab chowder it is the best! The presentation is beyond gorgeous!

Great spot in downtown Indy! Tried this place out for my birthday & was pleased with the experience. The cauliflower "risotto" was my favorite - could eat it all day. Drink list is extensive, filled with options for the pickiest of friends. Service was pleasant but dragged a bit. The aura is nice & the prices match the product.

Okay this is not an all u can eat sushi joint, nor is it your average sushi place if you are expecting to eat plate after plate of rice laden rolls.  However, if you are a true sushi lover and you want to take your experience to the next level and try some things that you may not have experienced before or even some that you think you don't like, this is an incredible experience.  It was our anniversary and we wanted something unique and different.  This tasting menu was amazing and fulfilled our desire to have a new experience unlike the typical.  We did the lower priced version of the tasting /$90pp and bought sake separately, but didn't do the pairing.  The courses of fish were bite sized delicacies too many to count.  Each was dusted or brushed or dotted with the perfect lemon dust, or yuzu juice or  onion relish that complemented the delicate flavors of the fish without overpowering them.  I thought my husband would panic because there was no soy sauce offered.  We quickly realized this experience required no soy sauce.  The flavors would have been lost in the mundaneness of salty Kikkoman normality.  Instead we were wowed by each course and kept looking at each other amazed by the simplicity and yet the complexity of each bite.  The fish changes defending on what is fresh and available, but some of our favorites tonight were the scallops, o toro, a special type of king salmon, a never like you've tasted spicy tuna hand roll and so many more.  I've never liked mackerel before but the Japanese mackerel was an entirely different experience.  Make no mistake, unless you've been to Japan, or somewhere not of this area, you've not experienced anything this good.  Worth every penny!  We are planning when we will go back for the grand tasting already.  The guys were great and made us feel so welcome.  Please try this and support this amazing addition to our downtown St Pete restaurant scene.  You will definitely find this to be a refreshingly new experience.

This is one of those situations where I could/should have had so many more pictures of our food, but by the time we got it, we were too ravenous and salivating to even remember to grab my camera.
We had such a hard time deciding what to order because everything on the menu just looked THAT good. Similarly, when asking our waitress what she liked, she had trouble choosing. Our solution was several dishes shared family-style. 
One of our friends does not practice veganism, so she had the pork version of the Rico (I had a taste. It was amaze.), and we ordered the Quinoa Sweet Potato Fritters to start. I don't love fried food, so these were a little heavy to start with between that and the dip, but fortunately, it was a small dish. 
We then had the Esmaralda Salad (glad to have shared because it has poblano chilies and was excellently spicy- maybe too much so had I eaten the whole thing alone), Kottu Roti (love that they made noodles of this!), and Peruano (my least favorite of the others because it contained an overload of white bean, but the cheese was convincing). 
Excellent service, excellent food, a top vegan recommendation!

The chicken was fresh but so greasy, taste was good but not sure if very healthy.  Dipping sauces are good.  We skipped potato sides so not so many calories.  Fried jalapeños with cheese were also tasty and good.  Good value for the price.

I have been looking for an authentic soul food spot & THIS IS IT YALL !! I originally went in for the fried chicken but they unfortunately didn't have any when I went so decided to try the baked chicken. Personally don't ever really care for baked chicken BUT THIS BAKED CHICKEN HERE WAS AMAZING !! Probably some of the best collard greens I've had in a long time & the Mac & Cheese just delicious. The sweet tea was SWEET & tasted different in a good way then any other sweet tea I've had. The actual spot is very spacious & had great music ! The staff was very sweet & patient & you can tell they work hard to make sure all their customers leave happy. The portions are great for the price and will leave you stuffed or with leftovers. Will be coming here with my friends often

If you are hungry, this is not the place for you. If you want a decent dinner, this is not the place for you. Portions are small and overpriced. Menu options are limited. The decor is nice and drinks are good. But that's it. If you want authentic food and food, this is not the right place.

Never tried their food, but the beer is top notch.  Wife and I like to take the little one on stroll to pick up a growler. Not a game day or date night place, but the beer is tasty and the pizza makes me resent my wife's lactose intolerance.
1 Nov 13. Great food great service. Service dog friendly. Best clam chowder south of Boston!  Good prices and great happy hour deals. Highly recommend for families and for dates.

Pretty good. Western take of quite good dim sum. Would be great for larger parties so you can try more dim sum. Was surprised with how authentic it is. Of course, you could get cheaper food in chinatown but the ambiance and interior is much more refined and quiet than your typical hectic c-town restaurant. good job jane g's.

I can review as an ex employee and a customer 

As a employee for almost 4 years , it was terrible! But it also pays rent and the bills . The GM yelled at employees in front of customers making them completely uncomfortable and humiliated and at customers when they caused confusion within the transaction. If you had to call out he would guilt you into working ( even if you were sick ) . 

As a customer now , I still see him yell at employees and have altercations with customers . The food most of the time is good , if the order isn't messed up . The bathrooms are always a disaster with toilet paper thrown about . I notice that the team members aren't very friendly but most like because of the gm yelling and talking down to them . 

Ideally I would go to a different location where the employees aren't taken for granted.

This is just ridiculous. My delivery estimate was like 45 minutes-ish so when that time had elapsed I called them and was met with a condescending dude on the other end who acted like I was stupid and told me that the actual delivery time would be over two hours for my fucking small pizza!! Not doing this shit again.

I love nothing better than finding a new hole-in-the-wall eatery serving up housemade comfort food. Candelaria's Mexican Food made me feel comfortable and then some.

An order of chips and salsa whet our appetite ($2), with a chunky salsa I'd call medium-hot served with a good-sized basket of fresh, warm tortilla chips. Being my wife and I both love to add a good salsa to a plate of food, we were happy to accept the offer of a free refill.

Our server warned it would take a little extra time for a ceviche tostada (citrus-cured fish, $3.99), as each one is made-to-order. It really didn't take too long, and I certainly prefer fish to be as fresh as possible. A huge pile of diced cucumber, tomato, onion, and fish was stacked on a fried corn tortilla that stayed crispy throughout. The fish tasted fresh and the citrus marinade was excellent, but I could have done with a little less cucumber. The result--though tasty--was akin to a cucumber salad, seasoned with fish.

Next, our hungry group ordered three combination plates: chile relleno (stuffed pepper, $7.99), bistec encebollado (steak with onions, $9.99), and camarones a la diabla (deviled shrimp, $11.99). Combos come with rice, refried beans, and salad (really more of a lettuce, onion, and tomato garnish). For the money, there was quite a lot of rice and beans on the plates. The beans had the the flavor and texture that tells you they didn't come from a can, but the rice was kind of just there. Adding some of that good chunky salsa gave it more reason to be on the plate.

Although not indicated on the menu, the chille relleno plate featured not one, but two sizeable peppers stuffed with melted cheese, drenched in ranchero sauce, and sprinkled with cotija cheese. Or at least I think the sauce was supposed to be ranchero. The tomato puree was pretty bland with not much seasoning to speak of, but the addition of a little hot sauce perked things right up.

The beef steak with onions was very tasty, featuring a 10x4 inch well-seasoned and grilled skirt steak served with what appeared to be an entire grilled onion. Seriously, there was so much onion I couldn't see the meat until I cleared it aside. Not that this is a bad thing; I love steak with onions and boy, they really hit it out of the park. The flavor of an adobo spice blend combined with fresh garlic--and other things I can't name--was perfect. Just don't plan on kissing anyone after eating this dish, unless of course you both ordered the same thing.

Deviled shrimp doesn't begin to describe our last dish. The sauce was both piquant and complex, with strong notes of garlic, onion, and chipotle pepper mixed with a savory blend of spices and what might have been a hint of lime. The shrimp themselves were cooked just right, a little bigger than your average "peel-and-eat" variety, with plenty on the plate. Though by far the spiciest dish ordered, it was a very approachable level of heat for those not into the burn. Great balance of flavors and a good value; definitely something I'd order again.

It isn't fair to visit a taqueria and not try the tacos, so an assortment of carne asada (steak), carnitas (pork), and pollo (chicken) tacos were shared by the table ($1.49 each).  The meats were lean, tender, and decently seasoned. The slow-cooked pork was particularly moist and flavorful, and all were dressed with tons of onion and cilantro. Nothing fancy, but a good example of "street tacos".

Hungry for Mexican food and don't want to leave your couch? Want a great value for the money? These folks offer delivery to most of Sparks-- including bottled beer and soft drinks--which I sincerely hope becomes a trend.

Good Bbq. Chopped brisket sandwich was flavorful and more than filling. The garlic mac and cheese was delicious. The selection of sauces fits everyone's favorites.  Would recommend to first time NOLA visitors.
Fun place to eat. Interesting surroundings.

Slooooooooowwwwww

Pros: food is decent, good price nice portion 

Cons: unreal slow service, messed up the order, gave us a dirty coffee cup which took 15 minutes to replace. Asked us three times if this was on the same check. Took 10 minutes to get the check.

The food here is okay. Run of the mill burgers, pulled pork and salads. But what on Earth are they doing in the kitchen?!  There were 8 people in our party today; 4 of us had a salad. We ordered at 1:05 and received the first plate 45 minutes after placing the order. Sad thing was we were there for lunch on Monday too and it took just as long to receive our meals. Next time our group suggests going there I will be going somewhere quicker.
Authentic shaved ice!!!  Definitely best in town. Can't wait to try their coffee. Clean and friendly staffs.

I've been here a few times. I am a fan of the under 400 calorie meals. Last time I got a $7 Caesar salad, that was more like a $4 salad. Had the XXL turkey burger wrap today. They were out of the low carb wrap. It was basically mushy turkey on a wrap, I wouldn't recommend it. The chili everyone talks about was not good. The side $2.99 Caesar salad was ok, you kinda can't mess That up. I think I'm gonna stick to the Champion Pasta, Penne Vodka sauce, and teriyaki meals. They could do better. Also delivery was 50 minutes. They need a make your own bowl option. So you can build if to your specs.

This is my first Yelp review after a few years of having the app. I was heartbroken to see that Monsu has closed 
What a wonderful little restaurant it was: amazing food, excellent service, warm ambiance (big candelabra's with heaps of molten candlesticks line the windows).
I moved to the city a few months ago, and went there around once a month, bringing friends and family who were visiting.
My favorite thing was their crab pistachio gnocchi. It's probably the best Italian food I've ever eaten in the US. One time I went, it wasn't on the menu for that day, and the chef suggested to modify one of the plates to make it more like my favorite gnocchi.
Their desserts are excellent too, and they always offered a little treat.
I really hope that Monsu will reopen soon, so I can keep introducing groups of friends and family to this lovely restaurant.
Please start going here-- it is such great food-- but I fear the location is not drawing people-- it is better than any Thai place around

Against the preference of my wife, I have always been a fan of Olive Garden.

The recent menu changes have been thought out and executed well.

I particularly like their Buy One, Take One promotion.

This particular location is updated and clean.

The Garlic Rosemary chicken was drastically overcooked to the point of being stringy and almost crunchy. Seeing that I generally have decent meals at Olive Garden, I am willing to overlook this one meal.

Moved into the area not that long ago and we have been trying new places. We're foodies and so we love to find the places to eat in town. We heard about this place from a FB friend that raved about it. This place was HOPPING so that was a good sign. Super popular and so we waited for about 30 minutes. Each of us had something different so we could share and try each other's dishes. We had the lobster grilled cheese (was good and full of lobster but not very "grilled cheesy"), grouper sandwich (good but nothing extraordinary), kimchi fish tacos (these were really good but super spicy), the Rachel duck burger (hubby and kids said it was good, I didn't try it), and the crab Mac n cheese (OK but it did have quite a few pieces of shell in it). I really wasn't impressed with the food and the prices were a bit high for the quality in my opinion. Anything with crab usually has shells in it but it's usually 1 piece in the whole meal. I was finding a piece in each bite. That made it difficult to eat so I just left most of it. We ended up spending $100 without drinks. It's seems like a good place to hang out with friends and drink. However, it is not a place that we would go back to to have dinner.

First let me start off by saying - If you want a wonderful evening out in a classy, up and coming restaurant that will leave you with a great taste in your mouth....this is it. My wife and I, along with my brothers family had dinner there the other night and honestly really enjoyed ourselves. Everything from the service, to the wine, to our meal - and it's very clean. 

We had the Fried Brussel Sprouts as an appetizer...very, very YUMMY !! 
Just for reference Yummy is a very technical term we restaurant snobs use that means "if I was stuck on a desert island and could only eat one thing this would be it"...LOL. THIS WOULD BE IT! 

I had the Vegetarian Pasta with Shrimp - Very tastey with the right amount of balanced flavor and freshness. The pasta was done the way pasta should be - not mushy, but firm and ready to be dressed with a wonderful white sauce with mushrooms, very flavorful. 

So bottom line - If you want a night out to impress your friends or other half this is the place you NEED to visit. If you want a mediocre place that has a big name and average food, go someplace else......

Always a good deli meal.

Be sure to try the shrimp louie. 

consistent, clean, friendly, good food

I love the style and the roof deck is such a great spot. There guac and chips is delicious. Sadly, I only go when I am feeling very patient and not on any kind of a schedule because the service is horrible. Several times our food has been forgotten or our waitress never came to our table. The last time when I went in the evening the young guy taking IDs at the door was rude and in no way welcoming. Its too bad really because if the service was good this could be a great place.

La Ha is one of my favorite restaurants in Avon. Authentic Mexican food for a good price. 

The staff is usually very attentive and our food comes out fast. 

My last experience wasn't the greatest but usually it is much better. 
Cons:
Long wait time for drinks
Long wait time for server to address us
Not receiving things we requested 

Pros:
Great food
Good for groups 
Friendly people 
Clean facility

For me, it didn't hit the mark. The pierogies were very good. My herb crusted prime rib was fairly bland. The seasoning is actually very good. But 95% of the seasoning made it to the part that was entirely fat which was about 50% of the size of the prime rib. My wife's cauliflower steak was fine, no major complaints, but nothing special either. Looked like a large chunk of cauliflower grilled with some pesto on it. 

Our server was tremendous though. Right on top of everything and just so nice. Brianna was fantastic.

I'd love to give the place another chance but the prices are pretty high, and I just can't see paying those prices for average (at best) food. On top of that, they levy a 4% "pandemic charge" for dine in only. It's a tough climate for all businesses, but for those diners like myself who like to go sit and enjoy time out to pay an extra fee for that right is tough to swallow. We, unlike most people doing take out, are already paying the additional charges of beverages, alcohol (if inclined) and tip to the wait staff. All of those are things I'm more than happy to pay and support, but an extra 4% going to the house...no thanks. It should be more readily noticeable on the website as well.

My business is better served elsewhere.

EXTREMELY UNHAPPY that new owners decided to increase the prices & took away combination specials/plates. It's all a la carte. Before I knew this I ordered my usual veggie burger & 2 sides. With a drink it is now $18+ dollars. Yes, you read that right. OVER EIGHTEEN DOLLARS. That's insane. It's a veggie burger, beans & potatoes. Not an enormous amount of food. This sadly certainly has tainted my view of coming here. I will now have to choose it less often & likely won't as readily suggest it to others if this continues to be the case. (Most of my friends are on a budget too.) Plus they're bringing beer on the premises. So I get the message the agenda isn't to provide affordable clean vegan food--It's to make money. Sure, we all need & want to make money. But, this is food - not the doctor's office. We have to consume food everyday all day. My trust value drops too when things like this happen because owners who do this typically eventually slowly skimp on quality. Maybe that's not the case here. Let's hope not. In my opinion, it's a terrible move & not a way to grow your business - but given how Berry Hill continues to be more & more upscale,  I suppose the elite will love it & the rest of us will move along. Sad. And if I seem upset well, yes, I'm upset. One of my favorite places just bumped itself out of my already on the bubble budget. In a positive note, the owner was kind and took my complaint thanking me for being here. He said they had to raise prices to keep up with rising food costs.

Ok - simply wonderful hot as hell tasty chicken!  Cute place with limited seating but well worth the wait!  They cook your food to order so you wait for about 20 minutes by again it's worth it - order the okra you will not regret it!

First time here and I really enjoyed it. Came for breakfast with a friend. I ordered the sausage egg and cheese biscuit and was very happy with this choice. The wait wasn't long and loved the option of sitting outdoors. Will definitely be back.

Wtf. Amazing. Some of the freshest of pastries and chocolates I've ever had. Not only is Rene an incredibly friendly host, he also has a set of bongos and congas he plays "when the mood strikes". When we arrived, he was giving a private ricotta cheese making class to the local restaurant owners and shared its deliciousness with everyone in the cafe.

I've been here a few times and have had good luck.  They're always so nice when taking my order on the phone.  During my last visit, I was very disappointed when picking up my pizza.
