When I had walked in, there was one gentleman in the back doing dishes and one gentleman by the front window playing with his phone.  I walked in to pickup a vegetable pizza that I had called ahead and no one came to help me at the counter.  I waited a bit and was getting annoyed.  There was one family dining in and they also kept turning around to look at the gentleman playing on his phone by the window because I wasn't being helped.  I yelled excuse me a few times and no one came to help me.  I then went to the front of the store by the window to the gentleman playing on his phone and yelled excuse me again.  I took a few seconds because turning over and seeing what I needed.  I guess his playing on the phone was more important than the waiting customer.  I picked up my pizza and drove home.  It smelled so good on the ride home but that quickly changed when I opened up the box and picked up my pizza.  It was SOOOO WET AND SOGGY that I couldn't even pick up my pizza and had to use knives and fork to eat the whole pizza.  The pizza was so wet that the box was soaked.  At first I thought it was the pizza because too greasy but it was just too wet.  That said, I haven't been back since and also look elsewhere just because my last experience was so frustrating and disappointing.   Two stars because I've had better past experiences....

Plus: 
Great food, excellent live music and not crazy loud so you can still have a conversation, pleasant wait staff, Carabean atmosphere, nice outdoor
, happy hour, cool tee shirts, !

Cons:
If it was on the beach instead of a parking lot , I would just live there !

I had never been to Sawasdee before, but the guy I'm dating swears by their food, so we checked it out last week. It's an intimate and casual place. Quiet and tucked away inside a strip mall. The menu seems rather large. 

I ordered the Pad Thai, Crab Rangoon, and hot and sour soup. All three were delicious! The Crab Rangoon is a large portion, plenty for 3-4 people to share, and more crabby than most I have had with a really good side sauce. The Pad Thai could have been shared between two people as well, but I had yummy leftovers instead. I ordered mine with shrimp, which adds to the cost, but didn't really seem worth it. There were maybe five shrimp in what was otherwise a massive plate of food. The most interesting thing was the the hot and sour soup. It is very good but very different from anywhere else I have had it. Super tangy and flavorful. 

Our waiter was attentive in making sure we always had a full glass of water, but he wasn't over so much that it felt intrusive. He was polite and helpful with suggestions when I was trying to decide what to order. 

I'll definitely return, and this time with a bigger appetite!

Went here on a whim with my Mom, Sister and Boyfriend. We like Thai food, so we've had our fair share but this place... OMG probably the BEST wonton soup and drunken noodles we've EVER HAD! The Pad-See-You was also very good. Flavorful but not too much sauce or over powering.  The pretty was chicken/garlic rice soup with a spring roll that preceded the lunch special OMG I've never had Garlic rice and it was AMAZING! Not to mention the yummy broth the chicken rice came in. Very pleased, would order that on its own. As for the amazing drunken noodles.. would definitely order again.. actually, we did, right then and there, two more to go for my brother, and my sisters fiancé! Go here, you won't regret it!

My husband and I dined here with another couple last Saturday night.  We were all pretty excited to try someplace new that had gotten such great reviews.  They raved about the duck tacos and I thoroughly enjoyed the heirloom tomato and melon salad that I started with.  For an entree, our friends shared the "for 2" Ribeye which really was a great value since it came with two sides and two dinner salads.  It was plenty of food and they said that all of it was really good.  My hubby got the Hangar steak which I tried a bite of and I really loved the flavor of the chimichurri sauce.  I had the scallops which were very plump and juicy and cooked to perfection. However, the arugula didn't really complement them well and it didn't mesh with the texture and taste of the risotto.  Also, the dish was just a little too salty so I probably would not order it again.  For dessert we ordered the panna cotta as well as the bacon infused chocolate chip cookies.  Both were very delicious!  I was a little disappointed that they didn't offer cappuccino since that is usually my favorite way to end a meal.

As other reviewers have mentioned, the wine list has a lot of unusual options on it but I was disappointed that they didn't offer any Arizona wines.  But we tried "Brian's Pick" and it was very good.  The restaurant itself was a little less formal than I was expecting and had a sort of modern bistro vibe to it.  The decor was very minimal and contemporary.  And the place was pretty small and felt somewhat cramped.  Also, it was a little too loud at times.  The service was friendly and prompt.  He answered our questions and complied with our requests but didn't really offer up anything extra.  I just didn't feel like I was being pampered as you would at most places at this price point.

I did really enjoy the overall vibe of the place as well as the food but it wasn't quite what I was expecting for $50+ a person.  I agree with one of the other reviewers who said that they can't seem to decide if they are an New American bistro catering to the hipster crowd or a fine dining establishment courting the foodies.  Either way, there aren't many good options for a splurge dinner in Tucson so we will likely be back.

I have been back to Pete's a few times since my first review. Pete is usually there himself now and I think that makes a huge difference.  The Pizza is great and Pete is great to talk to.  I would recommend to anyone looking doe a great Slice.

So the obvious joke would be to suggest this place change its name to Yesjaks. Because any time I am thinking about  where I want to eat I will undoubtedly think to go here. Yes, please. 

The truth is that whatever the name, and there is nothing wrong with Nojaks, the food is no joke. I have been searching far too long, and in far too many wrong directions, to find a tasty veggie burger. This, Is. It.

Everything about it just worked. The presentation is not messy or sloppy but neat and really well constructed. The aroma, texture and taste are, in my humble opinion, transcending. I don't often eat meat but do remember how good a really good burger can be. And this rekindled that memory.

Located on a downtown side street with little to distinguish it except that it is just around the corner fro the infamous Hub bar and the historic Tampa Theatre, it might be easily overlooked but make the effort to find it and try it.

Place your order, pay for what you requested, pick it up and take it away. Nice and easy. There is a burger made with tofu and another featuring grass-fed beef so pick your preference and enjoy. All are served on a house made potato roll that is the perfect accompaniment for these sandwiches. 

Sides are available and the beverage selection includes sodas, natural wine, beer, cold brew/cold brew latte * oat and H2O and fizzy H2O.

Love having a place like this that provides quick service, is convenient to where I live - and anywhere in downtown Tampa - and makes it easy to get really enjoyable, and really healthful, food.

Maybe the name should be changed to Gojaks! As in, what are you waiting fo? Just go!
The Cafe is always clean and inviting. Pleasant music and artwork hanging on the walls adds to the great atmosphere. Service is always wonderful and the food is excellent!

Legit Mexican. Fast good tacos. Good prices and fast service. I ordered the chicken, carnitas, and lengua. All were good and thr green salsa was tangy and spicy without too much heat. The only complaint would be that the tortillas are really small so the taco is small. Order at least 3 for a meal.

What can I say about this place?  It was a wonderful experience!  

I was just walking around the South Street area, not really dressed for dining out and stumbled upon S&H Kebab House.  Sal the owner proceeded to introduce himself and tell me about the menu.  You can tell he was someone who loved what he do (owning a restaurant) and meeting new people who loved his food.  I was heading to a greek restaurant on south street, but his infectious and charming manner was enough for me to go to my car 4 blocks away and walk back to have a meal in his restaurant.  As I was looking at the menu, I noticed platters on other diners table and wanted what they had just by looking at the food.  I settled for the combination (cold) appetizer which is big enough to feed 2-3 people and got it anyway so that I can take it home and nibble on it for lunch and dinner.  I also ordered the pan fried veal livers (hot appetizer).  There are no words to describe this dish!  Tender, flavorful are some of the words that I would use to describe this dish.  The staff was wonderful, the guys would come up and talk of their favorite dishes on the menu.  Sal in between welcoming other guests would stop by my table to talk about the menu and NYC.  Only complaint that was my server forgot me sometimes, but the other servers picked up the slack.  I enjoyed myself and would visit it again when my friends come to visit in April!  Thanks again Sal to you and your staff for the wonderful dining experience!

This is maybe a 4.5/5 in terms of veggie availability but I'll round up :) The waiter/chef was really accommodating and told us what dishes were vegetarian and what could be made vegetarian. I got the fava bean risotto (one of the only dishes that was vegetarian) and my friend asked for the Bolognese pasta dish to be made vegetarian. He ended up getting a really good hand made (I think?) pasta with a spicy red sauce and suggested adding it to the menu! We followed it up with a chocolate cake and got some free fancy desserts too. 

* Vegetarian / Veggie / Vegan review * I'm a vegetarian foodie that has a lot of meat eating friends who want to go to fun places that may or may not be veggie-friendly, so I'm here to tell you what to order if you find yourself in the same situation :) Just search "vegetarian" or "veggie"!

We went out today on Labor Day in search of tacos.  Since the usual place we get them was closed for the day (and the second place we wanted to try was closed permanently (!!!)), we went here.  Not a bad place for second choice.  We've been here before for dinner and so hopefully lunch was going to be just as good.  We got there just before lunch was over but got the lunch menu anyway.  I'm not going to complain at all because the 2 course prix fixe lunch is a great deal!  No complimentary chips here but if you go with a group, no need to order more than 2.  And that's if you like a lot of chips (delicious!) and guac and salsa roja.  

$14.95 for a drink (non-alcoholic, duh), choice of an app (or salad or soup), and main dish.  Not bad!

I got the carnitas tacos, the wife got brisket tacos.  Both were delicious but I liked mine better.  :)  The only thing I was slightly disappointed in was the lack of anything on the lunch menu with mole sauce besides the vegetarian taco option.  But everything else was GREAT!

Splendid! Absolutely splendid! It was like hiking up the hills in Thailand! Atmosphere was great and food came out amazing. Pud Thai was my favorite even tho I ordered the noodle platter, I picked off my girlfriends plate and wish I ordered the Pud Thai instead. They had golden basket as one of their appetizers and it was magnificent; full of flavor and just falls apart in your mouth.

Hoagies are always good, employees are also always rude. They'll look right at you more than once, not say a word and continue to let you stand there. I encountered whom is described as the owner on here and he seems very nasty and bitter when I'm nothing but polite. Just a heads up, don't expect good service even though you get good food.

Came here for lunch as I was en route to a ski vacation/bachelor party trip. I was so happy that Yelp produced this great result. 

Sometimes you roll the dice, but this place had some truly great vegan food. Plant-based food, made with love.

Mmmmm.  Two words: Classic and Delicious.

Of all the places my brother wanted to take me during my visit to St. Louis, Blueberry Hill was the top choice.  Walking in, you can tell this place has HISTORY.  The decor is inviting and whimsical, with warm wooden booths and various decorations along the walls.  The restaurant is very large too.  My one gripe is that the bathrooms are less than stellar (ex:. there is a nice Dyson hand dryer, except its busted) and matched the "Bar" in the Blueberry Hill title more than the "Restaurant."

But on to the more important details: Food and Service.  We ordered their signature burgers, fried ravioli, and buffalo chips with hickory sauce.  KNOCKOUT MEAL.  Service was quality.

Burgers were excellently crafted, we wolfed down the fried ravioli and buffalo chips.  Man, those buffalo chips were DELICIOUS, full of flavor, crispy on the outside and warm potato goodness on the inside.  Dip in it in the cool hickory sauce and that right there is a quality side.

My one recommendation for the burgers is to pay the extra 50 or so cents and get the fried onions.  The raw onion slices were too big for the burgers and made them harder to wolf down.  Other than that, if you ordered what we ordered, you'll come out satisfied.

Oh and since you'll be stuffed after that meal, I recommend taking a walk in the Botanical Garden or Forest Park, but that's for another review.

Ever since I can remember I've LOVED coming to JB's for shows and their amazing burger/chicken sandwich.  I was there this weekend for my burger fix and was soo sad to see the drop-off in the food.  I'm not sure if it's the new chef - but the burger was waay drier and smaller than before.  A friend of mine got the meatball sandwich and felt the same way.  I was there with five other people who were really disappointed that the (normally amazing) chicken sandwich was taken off the menu.  Still love JB's but probably not as a dinner spot so much anymore.
We like the food at Topgolf. Wings are always a must. And we love the lil donut balls. Fun place & good food!!
Food is very good, very good taste. Love this little restaurant out in Marana. The staff is very friendly, felt at home as soon as I entered.

5 stars for the wide open modern space with lots of natural light, great acoustics, great musicians and Greg the bartender/waiter whose great mood and energy are contagious. 3 stars for the average food but that's not what you are here for.  Definitely worth stopping in.

Asian people would say if you're at an Asian restaurant or one that sells Asian food and you do not see a lot of Asian, than you probably shouldn't eat there. I find it to be somewhat true, because Asian people would know where the best Asian foods are. And it wouldn't be P.F. Chang's. LOL Anyhow, the food here is great and so is the service. (Even though we received the wrong check).  I came here with my boyfriend during their opening week. It was super crowded and we had to share a table with others, which wasn't an issue. I really admire the spirit of the place and the decor. The tables, chairs, and especially plates that look like the one I have at home. 

Even though the food is great, I have to say that they are overpriced because of what was served and food portion. You can find better authentic alternatives in Chinatown for less. One of my favorite snacks is Chinese egg waffles, which I get in Chinatown NYC for a buck. Here it is call "bubble waffle." Cute, but  when the lady in front of us referred to it as funnel cake. It was like  "OMG." And she's Asian. Gzz... I love funnel cake too. But these are not the same. But I see her confusion, because at Bing Bing's they sprinkle powdered sugar on the egg waffles. Ahh... 

Overall, not a bad place, hipster like, American take on Asian food similar to how "Cheu Noodle" was done. If you're like a clean place with wait people who speak English and a clear to order menu then come here but I like all the quirkiness that comes from eating in Chinatown. It makes me laugh when I think of some of English translated names on the menu.

Unorganized, scummy, ridiculous place. If these adjectives inspire you to head here.. have  at it. Worst venue I've ever been to and have seen hundreds and hundreds of shows. Bands should book elsewhere.

This place is such a gem! It's a low key, chill environment with the best hummus. The food is unbelievably good. We got the taste of Lebanon platter to share. Perfect for two people. It had a little bit of everything and we were blown away by the taste and how much food we got. Delicious! We will be back
Salmon cheese steak is the best thing I've ever had. Service is great. Owners are cool peeps. Can't wait to get another one of them jawns.

Not worth going out of your way for. 

All the rave reviews on the sushi made us come but we were not impressed. Sushi quality is ok but we could get this quality sushi almost anywhere. 
Chicken tempura soggy not crispy. Hot sake is hard to drink- not smooth at all.
Beef and asparagus entree had too many asparagus pieces wrapped around a thin piece of beef.  
Parking is extremely difficult and the atmosphere of the place is ok, nothing great.

Not a bad place if you are close by and there is room in the parking lot, not a destination place though.

We held our rehearsal dinner and wedding at the JAI and it couldn't have gone better. The staff was extremely helpful and catered to all of our needs. Even though it rained on our wedding day, the venue was very accommodating and everyone had a great time. The food was great, the rooms were comfortable and the setting was perfect. Just an all-around fantastic place to have a wedding.

Well the atmosphere is different but it's not the reason for the lower review the food also isn't the reason I actually quite enjoyed the meal. The problem was a really poor waitress and either by her fault or the kitchens we waited over an hour for our food while others nearby who came in after us got their food. Breakfast is nit a meal that takes that much time. It's a shame I might consider going back but not without a much better server. As I said it could also be the kitchen but 2 others at either side of us got their food before us/ much quicker and she was also their server

I do not write a lot of reviews but after eating lunch at Lobster Haven yesterday. I had the 1.5 lb lobster crab cakes and I have to say it was the best lunch I had since I moved to Florida. I will be back.

Love this place. Let me start by saying the food is made fresh as soon as you order. Often places will already have food cooked before you get there that has been sitting there for awhile. I got the lunch special for $6 which includes a gyro and pita chips. Soooo much food for such an inexpensive price. One of my new favorite lunch spots.

I guess the food would taste better after a long night of drinking. But as far a ordering at a normal breakfast hour and the Resturant not being crowded we were very disappointed. The hash browns were luke warm at best and the grits soupy. The only thing that was hot was the order of pancakes! 8-10 yrs ago this was the spot for breakfast. 
I would suggest closing for a twenty four period and cleaning the place from top to bottom, and purchasing some new plates and silverware. Over time everything needs to be replace and new stuff purchased. It would go a long way with your new and old clientele alike. It just shows you care about the people coming thru your doors!
Sad to see this place go it was a favorite of mine. I never knew a few busted windows would build up to them closing for good. I real shame.

The fried chicken and cat-fish is a must. The dining area might look run down but just imagine you are eating during the late 1950s or something. Their service is kind of slow but as long as the food is good, then it's all worth it.

I heard so many good reviews from people that we know about your restaurant. The prices seemed a bit high, but that's to be expected at a steakhouse and sushi restaurant. So, let's get to the nuts and bolts, our chef was lude and told rude jokes, our portions were measly, I'd say maybe a 6oz steak and 6 scallops we were also supposed to get shrimp, but didn't. I know I could get a king's feast for the $80 we spent elsewhere. The only good note I can say is that the sushi and roll we ordered was great.

Went there on a recommendation from a friend. Seated at 7:35. Didn't see our server until 8. Food was just ok. My chicken dish was mostly potatoes with a few pieces of over cooked chicken. Server didn't refill water glasses until requested. At best an average experience.
How delightful to find a taste of aloha right here in Florida! The food reminded us of home and the music made us feel like we were where we belong!

We have been unsuccessful in finding a really good Chinese restaurant in West County.  I had high hopes for China in Bombay with so many positive reviews, unfortunately it did not live up to the hype.  We ordered the chicken potstickers, crab rangoon, general tso chicken and vegetable manchurian.  

The chicken potstickers were pretty good but VERY greasy.

The crab rangoon was gross.  The wrappers were not cooked long enough so they were super doughy and chewy.  The filling was just a SUPER sweet cream cheese.  No crab, imitation crab, green onion-nothing.  It should be called sweet cream cheese wonton if you aren't putting the ingredient in the title in it. At $6 for 5, this was very pricy for something lacking the main ingredients.

The general tso chicken was also excessively sweet.  The chicken was mostly tough dark meat, the breading was weird and soggy-we couldn't quite figure out what was off, and the sauce lacked any real flavor other than super super sweet.

The vegetable manchurian...  Now to be fair, this was something new to us so maybe we just picked the wrong thing but it was not good.  I don't know if the dumplings were under cooked or what but it tasted like raw doughy mush. It was the color of bread dough with tiny specs of orange I assume were carrots but no other vegetables that could be identified. It was sticky and mushy and just unappealing. The sauce had good heat to it but the consistency was like gloppy gel which was again, unappealing.  After a couple bites it went in the trash-we just couldn't stomach it.  

The rice was cooked well-light and fluffy.  

Maybe we tried the wrong things but the meal was so off putting I don't think we will give it another shot.

This place  is amazing. The owners are kind and personable. We had an event there tonight and everything was  perfect. If we even thought we needed something, they were offering it to us. I will definitely be back to support outside of our event. Also, the food was  great so  make sure you go support. Thanks Will and Rah!

Fantastic place!  Were there last night and feasted on a never-ending stream of plates, each as good as the next.  It really created a fun atmosphere.  There was no coursing, plates are delivered as they come off the line.  Once everyone had a bite, no one cared who ordered what, we just all sampled everything.  Created a neat interactive experience.  We never got to dessert, too many good tapas were ordered initially.  Definitely would return.

I order from here almost weekly.  Was kind of surprised when I saw a lot of poor reviews.  I have tried many items on the menu ad have never been disappointed.  Even had them do the catering for my engagement party and everyone complimented the food.  Buffalo Chicken Cheese Steak is one of my regulars and i think its one of the best around.  Most of the time we get delivery and they are here in a reasonable time.

We went here for lunch and were both pleasantly surprised.  The service was fast and courteous and the food was delicious.  We both enjoyed the Wilford Brimley burger very much.  The pretzel bun was fresh and the toppings / ingredients were all delicious (bacon cheese sauce, bacon jam, fried onion, and bacon).  The burger was perfectly cooked and a little pink in the middle.  Be sure to let them know if you want your burger well done.  We like ours just the way they came!  And let's talk about those fries!!!  Perfectly seasoned and crispy golden brown.  Excellent for dipping in the sauces that were provided (apricot ketchup and dill dip).  We were expecting an okay lunch ... what we got was a total surprise ... one of the best burgers in town!  We will be back soon!!!

I usually visit Watkins Drinkery for the excellent happy hour. With the jukebox, ample seating, and tv's tuned to something interesting (think top gear, not sports), it's the best place around to have a couple good beers at a great price ($2.50).  

However, I've found the ambience to be hit-or-miss, depending on the bartender working. And the food is lacking.  Most of my meals here have been disappointing and none have been good.  While I appreciate the adventurous menu, the dishes tend to come out bland.

Had to try it. The food was very bland. My Mac and cheese had hard pieces of macaroni, like it had been sitting out all day. The rest of the food was also not very good, it just all tasted like it had been reheated. Not impressed

It's difficult to find gluten-free food in New Orleans so I was taking a chance to order from a pizza place. Boy I am so glad I did. The gluten-free crust was done perfectly and the pizza was fantastic and flavor I definitely recommend this. I ordered in to my hotel and not only did the pizza arrive nice and crispy but they even included a side of ranch which is something that I love but forgot to ask for.  I will definitely order from here again

BEIGNET ALL DAY! Such a cool place in a very hip side of town. The beignets were amazing. We got the beignet flights and were pleasantly surprised how big they are. The fillings were delicious and it goes well with the iced cafe au lait we ordered. Overall, it's a great place to meet up with friends and just hangout with great food options. My only complaint is that it's almost 2000 miles from where I live. =( Will definitely go again when I visit NOLA

Let me tell you, I'm in the Boro and this is the very best seafood I've had in all my time living here. The sweet potatoes fries were too hard to eat, I tossed them out, but everything else was so good. I will be seeing you guys again real soon.

Wow! This place was outstanding! We had just arrived in Tampa, after a very long car ride. We decided to give this a try, based on the reviews, proximity to the hotel and it being touted as something quick. I had absolutely no reason to suspect that it wouldn't be good, but it far exceeded my expectations. 

I wish that I would have gotten the name of the employee acting as cashier. I'm not sure if he was an owner/manager/or just exceptionally good at his job. He was so friendly and personable. He took the time to offer us a sample of the delicious beans, rice, and chop chop, while explaining that they are made fresh. He checked in with us to see how we were enjoying our food. He made sure to thank us & wish us a good evening on the way out. Seriously, exemplary customer service!

The food- DELICIOUS! Everything tasted fresh & flavorful. The toughest critic in our group, my ridiculously picky 9 year old, said that she was going to "call the Mayor of our Hometown & tell him that he needs to put a Zeko's in" haha. She asked if we could come back for every meal during our trip! 

Everything was wonderful, but I will say that the Beef Kebabs truly stand out. They were incredible! This is not at all what I was expecting from a "fast food/quick service" style restaurant. I frequently order similar at table service restaurants, which aren't nearly as good. These were cooked perfectly at the requested temperature. They were so tender and juicy! I HIGHLY recommended them!

The only think I purchased was a drip coffee. I was not impressed. I did not taste any of their food offerings, but I was also not inspired to purchase anything. The next day, I went to the French Press instead. Their coffee was **so good** and the food looked delicious, so I was inspired to buy some, and then was quite taken with the tastiness. So, I suggest going there instead.

The atmosphere was also not my scene. The music was a bit loud for sitting and chilling.

Honestly, without a doubt some of the best Mexican food I have ever had. I thought I was in the wrong place walking in but I am so happy we stopped here. I just wished I lived in the area to make this a weekly occurrence. Absolutely delicious!

A group of us came in last night to celebrate my wife's birthday. Our waitress Christina was wounderful. She gave us a great experience. There was a delay in the kitchen, but she was on top of everything. I would recommend her section, she has a welcoming personality. The food was delicious and we enjoyed the happy hour at the bar.

Ive been to this exact green eggs before and it was a totally different experience this time I went. I believe because I went closer to the closing time everything seemed more relaxed and way better. I order the Mac and cheese with buffalo chicken. The presentation was amazing which also makes the food experience more enjoyable. I do believe the cheese was liquid which is not what I am use to I think creating a 4 cheese sauce broiling it and then having a little cheese on top with parsley as a garnish would make this a stable here. I also tried the French toast which were great a little on the sweeter side. John front end manager was pleasant and was visiting every table which is always great to see. I would recommend this particular location because there is an outside seating area, parking in front and across the street and it doesn't feel overcrowded as other green eggs location.

P.S- there need to be a greeen eggs option on the menu as this is the name of the restaurant!
J

Wow! What a surprise! We haven't had really good seafood in awhile and decided to try take out from here - glad we did!

Ordered through their web site and it was ready on time. They delivered curbside and the staff was really nice! 

We ordered the 1/2 order boil of crab, lobster & shrimp in Old Bay Lemon & mild! Also, an order of fried shrimp with house fries and garlic bread! 

The boil was awesome! Reminds me of seafood boils from LA. It was a hearty portion. Crab and shrimp were the best. Lobster was okay. Sauce was really good. Also has some red potatoes, corn on the cob and sausage. Wish there was a little more sausage, but you're really going for the seafood anyway. Some of the potatoes were not cooked all the way.

Fired shrimp was great. Coating they used was good and good shrimp cocktail sauce. Fries were normal skinny fries. Wish they had a kids portion, since it was for our L.O. 

The garlic bread is not your traditional garlic bread. It's in rounds and has some red butter stuff on it. But then again you're using it to dip in the sauce...so all good.

Food was great, good quantity and prices were reasonable! Also food was packaged appropriately, so no spills or mess.

This place IS 100%!!! We spotted this place though a side street and had to go in! We selected a discounted bottle of wine from Brazil and headed to our table. The spinach artichoke dip is the best we both have ever had!!! The tacos were amazing and the service was wonderful. I believe it was the highest tip we ever left. The lighting, the outdoor seating just was the perfect date night for us and we will be back!

3.5 stars.  

The good: well cooked, well seasoned, crispy fried chicken breast.  House made hot sauce.

The okay: save for the serving temperature, Nashville hot chicken lacks heat.  Nashville hot, it is not.  Which is too bad, as this was my big draw.  The potato salad was alright--a bit bland out of the box, but easily doctored up.

The not so good: holy moly do they overload their sandwiches.  Impossible to eat with one hand alone.  Some might say this is a good thing.  Not me.  The menu also not what I was expecting for a chicken joint.  Fried chicken breast and tenders dominate the menu.  There is a quarter bird option available, but you have to look for it.  They definitely cater to the deboned chicken crowd.

The bad: cookies and cream pie.  Attaching a photo.  Hard to make heads of tails of the photo, so let me spell it out: you are looking at a whip cream pie, like you might make for that silly pie to the face game, with oreo cookie crumbles.  Yeah, there is an actual cookies and cream pie filling in there, but it constitutes maybe 0.5 cm in height of the total pie slice, vs a 5 cm in height whipped cream topping. Sure it tasted fine.  But whipped cream even by itself is good, so no surprise there!  Just not what I expected (or thought I was paying for, and it wasn't inexpensive).

Bottom line:  was alright.  Was not Nashville hot chicken though.  Sad face.

This was the worst experience with a food truck at vail fest I have ever encountered. Was the 4th person in line and after 25 minutes and having other people that ordered after I did get served I ask for my money back. Flies everywhere and a strong smell of a propane leak were enough besides the poor service.

This is like a Denny's, in that they offer a huge variety of foods, but in no other way - it is one hundred times better than a Denny's. When you walk in you see a wall of cheesecake and you pretty much know it is going to be a fun experience. We were fortunately seated near the HDTV at the back of the restaurant as we watched the Jets fail their faces off against the Steelers - that part sucked, but even that sucking moment was still fun since we were hanging out at the diner. We were in a big group and we also were sitting right next to another big group, the Duke University fencing team. This place draws big groups in because it has a legit reputation among everyone, locals and those from far away who had a great meal here once a long long time ago.

The big guy (4u) waiter right off the bat was friendly, gracious, and funny - top notch staff here for sure. The water was not exactly refilled at a regular pace but I guess it was pretty busy. It was really hard to choose a dinner since everything sounded so good. I finally settled on the open faced Monte Cristo, longing for 'ye olden days when that deliciousness of the Monte Cristo used to be available at Bennigan's before their shenanigans shuttered their doors across the country. Penrose does not make 'yo daddy's Monte Cristo and that is not an entirely bad thing.

This is french toast as the base, two pieces and very moist and eggy. Not fried like Bennigan's. Just french toast that is AWESOME. Then meat piled on top of the french toast. Then some cheese on top of that. And a big helping of fries. The fries were solid, the good diner kind, not the shoe string or crinkle cut or that other junk places try to pass off.

I will be back for more Penrose.
Enjoyed a spinach salad with a variety of toppings along with a wrap. Fresh ingredients and pleasant staff. Will return.

o taqueria del sol how i wanted to love you.  perhaps you have been opened too short a time?  the food was meh, the service oscillated between helpful and completely rude.  your location is perfect, the concept works for you in atlanta....but, today you felt like "a chain restaurant".  maybe you are?  not my thing. i did not know that was what you are....

had i known you were a chain, i would have been satisfied with the food. 'hot plate' mexican with zero spice - ready in 30 seconds (wow, amazing how fast that could be created & then appear in front of me).

i was told afterwards (from food loving friends), that i need to venture out to murfreesboro road for fresh and authentic mexican food...with flavor.  think i will take that advice.....

Avoid 

It may be  and likely is the managers first but it is not the first time I've been to a restaurant. 

We came here for my grandfather's 94th birthday. We arrived at 7:30pm and our food didn't come for 2 hours. Completely ruining our plans to bowl and dink stroke for his bday.. Overall the food was good but the service was terrible...

This place is AWESOME, after hearing that it was best of Philly, I was afraid that my expectations were too high.  Well my expectations were met and exceeded.  Food is great, service is great, price isn't too bad for what you get.  Next time I go, I'll probably just get the hummus and salatim.  Don't get me wrong - everything else was great, but the starter was the star of the show!

J. Alexander in King of Prussia is our favorite go-to restaurant now. Everything that we have ordered has been absolutely phenomenal and we have NEVER been disappointed. The staff is professional and knowledgeable. Special kudos to Mary who has been our bartender nearly every time we go in. She is attentive, very personable and her work ethic is extraordinary. She makes each and every patron feel welcome and special. That's a true gift.
Great service and great food! The beer was fantastic and the knowledge of the staff was fantastic!

I've been to Agno several times now and have been pleased every time.

I have Celiac Disease and need to eat gluten-free.  Agno is entirely gluten-free so I don't have to worry about cross contamination issues.  I've actually had a hard time finding gluten-free take-out/casual locations in Philadelphia so Agno is a wonderful treat.

The staff is knowledgeable about gluten-free preparation and the food is fresh and flavorful.  Additionally, the atmosphere is open, clean and inviting.  If you are gluten-free and need a healthy, easy, trustworthy place to eat at I would recommend Agno.  It's really wonderful.

Came to this White Castle since I was in need of food. I'm glad to say this place didn't disappoint. I will say this place has the strangest parking lot design that I've seen in recent memory. The chicken rings were definitely phenomenal! They tasted like when McDonald's & Burger King used to make really really good nuggets 25 years ago. They got strawberry banana smoothy as well which was great. The staff was very friendly, prices were very good, great quality!

Good grits accompanied my meatball omelet with marinara-esque sauce.  The meatball was good and I could see coming back for traditional spaghetti and meatball dinner ... But I won't.  My low rating is for the idiot managment that wouldn't allow our server to substitute a $2 biscuit for $4 worth of potatoes or grits. This type of stupidity is hard to overlook.  I offer them a better bottom line and a happy customer, and they respond with wasted food (I didn't eat the grits, but for a bite) , a frustrated customer, and waitstaff who got marginally less tip. The lost opportunity offends my sensibilities, and I'll not return. 2 stars for meatballs... Fair is fair.

UPDATE * Upon leaving, the hostess / manager wanted to know if there was a problem- so I told her 'yes' and expressed myself much as I have above.  She pointed out that 'no substitutions' was printed on the menu- and said rather defensively, "We didn't lie."; and took pains as to why it was sensible economics that one biscuit is magically more costly than a side of potatoes or grits.  True, they didn't lie.  True, on the side opposite the breakfast items the menu said "no substitutions".  True, she argued with me.  True, she would rather be right than have her restaurant liked.

True, they have a line out the door.  True, WTF do I know?  I'm just a customer.

I agree with many of the other customers. I live almost next door to this place and routinely come here. Bagels are great but the staff is so miserable and rude. They seem like college kids who hate their parents, hate their friends and hate serving bagels. 

We get it; it's not a highly skilled job but at least smile when I'm ordering my 8$ bagel. 

Tip: when getting iced coffee ask for half the usual amount of ice. They tend to deceptively add more ice than coffee to their drinks. Weekdays are the perfect time to come as it's not crowded. Don't get bagels after 2pm as they've started to harden in the shop.

Kabutos is delicious every time we go. Tonight I went with my two sisters and my son ( who is 2) even though I didn't purchase him a meal the chef made sure he got some food and was a part of the experience... Love going and will definitely b back

Went for a quick appetizer 20 minutes before close, open sign "ON" and people in the restaurant.   We were told that they were closed and would only make a "to go" order.  I get the concept that you are tired and don't want us there after closing, but the fact is YOU ARE OPEN.  Our intention was to be gone before closing.

I will not go back.  Disappointing because most of the reviews say they have good food, yet terrible customer service.  Turn the sign to OFF and just stay home.  You won't have to worry about waiting on anyone, ever.

Excellent.  The beef patties tasted like homemade and the goat was tender and amazing.  I got the jerk wings to take home for the next day, but ate them when I got home.  I like more spicy food but even though it was very mild, the flavor was excellent!  Great addition to Paasyunk Ave.  I'm going for lunch next time.

Great option for beignets if you're in the French Quarter. My friends and I also had beignets from cafe du monde the night prior but these tasted way more fresh!! Area near the register only has enough space to stand in line to order, so 4 of us made our way to the outside seating area. They offer way more than beignets so we also had a carrot cake to share. Overall very cute space and great dessert/coffee offerings!
Love the chicken kebabs!  Consistently great food with every visit. Very friendly staff. A go to place for me when I'm looking for quick, healthy food.

I was there on a Saturday night on a date with my boyfriend. Joe was our server and he was awesome. Made great suggestions and I had the mahi mahi. Very good over the rice and green mole sauce. The cocktails were great we had the regular margarita and upgraded to the Noble margarita. It was worth it :-). I expect it to be very busy on a Saturday here and it was 45 min wait but we went to the casual bar attached first. They text us when they were ready. Only issue is it's very loud with no sound absorption in the decor. Some fabric added might help but again, it was a Saturday.

We had a great overall experience while in town for a few days. We were quickly seated and able to take advantage of happy hour before 6pm as they had great food and drinks specials. Our server recommended the unique Corn on the Cob special and we ended up ordering a second because it was that good. We also sampled the tacos and chicken enchiladas and loved both. The flavor was awesome, with classic presentation and great service. Highly recommend for quick bites or hanging out with friends. Very unique compared to traditional Mex restaurants.
Great service...friendly. Ordered steak and eggs and it was ok. Nothing special. Steak was undercooked and so was the eggs.  Wife's Jonathan eggs were good and flavorful.

I agreed with MN about the front door being locked and ringing the bell. It was kind of odd.  But being situated down the street from shitty 107 Ave where the vagrants are, I can see why they do that.  

This seemed like the most organized out of the Fork Fest menus.  Being a veteran of Summerlicious, we decided to check this place out.  It was a 3 course menu.  The food wasn't too bad.  It was all about presentation though.  The veal schnitzel was my favourite part of my prix fixe dinner.  

The website is a little left to be desired and their twitter page isn't very active. So right now it's just average.  I would give it a try again to see if I'd change my mind.

I spent $80 for two people and left hungry. I got a seafood bowl with one little chunk of lobster in the whole meal. No flavor at all. Waited forever for food and drinks and wasn't even given bread until we had to ask while everyone else was served. Will never go back with all the other great restaurants in the area.

Flavors are great
Options are pretty plentiful
Once I was given too much fat with the brisket and was disappointed 
On 3 different times they have run out of potatoes for their Bakers but inside scoop is you ask them to make  your Baker with the twice baked potato side instead. 
They are typically really busy at dinner time.

Hellas has come a LONG way over the years.  I ate here many,many years ago and swore I'd never go back.  But my husband wanted to try it, so I agreed to return after a long hiatus - and I'm glad I did!

We generally go at lunch, since it's right around the corner from where I work - which is good, because their lunch prices are a bit more reasonable than their dinner prices.  I always get the pork souvlaki, and have never been disappointed.  Their tzatziki is high on the garlic scale, which I love!  I'm not a big fan of the greek style green beans, so I try to substitute for something else when I can.  The greek style potatoes are consistently good.

A reasonable choice.  We read about it in the local paper while traveling through and decided to give it a shot. 
The order process is a bit different in that you order outside and then are served inside the former shop. Nothing fancy about the location, the decor, or the process.
The food is good with generous portions and an attempt for fresh and local produce.

This place is amazing!! The service is always excellent. The hot & sour soup is the best. There are also awesome lunch specials! We drive 30 minutes past many other Asian restaurants to come here because it's our favorite ! Keep up the good work Pinang!

I placed an order with Postmates and the restaurant completely disregarded my special instructions. I simply wanted to change my type of pasta and sauce that is normally no different charge in house. Im only giving two stars because my meal was hot and tasty - but not what I was looking forward to. My pasta was supposed to have chicken, and there's about four bites worth. I've never had a problem with Carrabba's in house, so I was really disappointed to see they completely ignored my customizations. I will probably not order to-go with them again.

its been a while since i stopped here.  service and food were suffering last time, hasnt changed.  Pizza sauce is strong flavored, not enough cheese at the edge, sauce very pasty.  Generally not enough cheese at all.  Seating is way too close, hard to get o the counter when 3 tables are lined up across the front and none of the women will sit close to the table.  place is very noisy, not conducive to enjoying your meal.  Prices are gigh, and i think i was overcharged by a few bucks.
All in all, i think papa murphy's is a better deal and the pizza is better from there.

I had dinner with a friend today at Thirsty Marlins and the atmosphere and food was amazing! Our server, Tyler, was impeccable and very attentive. He recommended his favorite items on the menu as well as drinks. The food came out in a timely manner and our drinks were never empty! I can definitely say i recommend this restaraunt to anyone who's in the area and request Tyler if you can, he was one of the best servers I had ever experienced. He made us feel very welcome and as if we knew him for years. 5/5 stars We will definitely be coming back!

5-13-2018
We have our favorite restaurants in the area, but decided to give D town a try.   We started out with the nachos.  Chips were stale and the cheese was not real cheese. And the salsa had no flavor.   I had the chicken piccata and my husband had the surf and turf.  Would not recommend either.  The chicken was very bland.  Hardly any crust on it.   The pasta was cooked perfect.  But the sauce was so greasy with no favor. I couldn't eat it.  The steak was cooked perfect but was chewy. We do not complain for fear of what happens in the kitchen if you do.  I hope the Breakfast is better.

I want to write about their winery. After the guided tour and some walking around and picture taking, my friend and I stopped at the winery/gift shop. We sat down along a tall counter and received a tasting of all their different wines- all very yummy. One in particular stands out for me- the Blackberry wine. I found the taste to be very unique and I ended up buying 2 bottles as gifts and one for myself. All three ended up being gifted and my family still asks about the blackberry wine from Tennessee.....

Disappointing lunch to say the least!  I started out by ordering a sweet tea only to make a weird face to which the server came over immediately to see what was the matter.  I had her swap out the tea immediately after explaining the strange after taste.  I should've known then that this was the downward spiral to my meal.

Because Yelpers were raving about the hush puppies I decided to give them a whirl and ordered a side to accompany my meal.  They were the highlight and shining star of my lunch!  Crispy on the outside and soft and sweetly flavored on the inside.  These can be eaten perfectly alone or joined in perfect unity with the secret sauce - the choice is yours!

Their name is Shrimp and Company yet their shrimp was probably the worst part of my meal.  I ordered the shrimp Po'Boy which comes with a weirdly flavored coleslaw and fries.  The Po'Boy barely had any shrimp on it - mostly lettuce and secret sauce which was very good and tasted similar to a remoulade sauce.  The shrimp were coated in a crispy batter which was very tasty however they were so over cooked they were tough - the only saving grace was the bread they were served in between and secret sauce they were slathered in.  

  Also like other Yelpers I found that they were a little pricey however I will say they offered a 10% discount for anyone dining for lunch.  Although my lunch was served hot, service was good and hush puppies were uber yummy the shrimp did not knock my socks off which is sad considering they were the main attraction of my meal and reason I decided to eat here in the first place.

Service was not really great and the food was pretty mediocre compared to all of the other BWW I have been to. I would not expect fast or great service, but the food is edible at times. Some of my wings were over cooked and others were perfect. I don't really recommend this location unless you really want wings.

Great place for kids on a Tuesday ‍‍‍

Ask for Mr. Niceguy.

The happy hour is great from 4-6

Delicious food! I had the legend poboy and it was very good. The pork in the bottom wasn't quite as sauced as the rest but it still tasted great. The dessert cake was ok but I wasn't all that hungry after how big the poboy was.

A lot of interesting stuff here - good for groups.

For the pizza places in the area I wouldn't recommend Lazos. Very mediocre pizza. Very greasy. Average fries, cheesesteaks, and mozzarella sticks. I used to live only a block away but would rather walk the couple extra blocks to Angelino's or Italian Express.

Pizza Baron has been my spot for 30 years. I'm not kidding when I was four years old five years old all the way to seven years old my father one Sunday a month would take me to get my hair cut next door and when we were finished we go to the pizza Baron for a slice and a soda and he would have a slice and a beer and that was the most amazing Sunday of every month I loved it. Now that I'm older I frequent this wonderful little establishment this local business. I know the owners the son of the owners the son of the son of the owners and I always feel like family when I'm here. The food is amazing the staff is great and frankly a pizza parlor that's been open for 45 years deserves recognition. I will highly recommend Pizza Baron - everybody has they have a wide variety of menu options not just pizza. They're little bar is fun they have karaoke on certain nights and Tuesdays is buy one get one heck of a deal I mean two pizzas for the price of one who could beat it. I've seen families have their birthday parties here and I've had great amazing times during karaoke I mean it's the whole deal.

I've got one word for this joint - overrated. Their calzones are pretty good, but no where near the type of calzone that you get in NY. The crust/bread does not have the taste or texture that the crust of a NY calzone has. In addition, I thought their sauces taste like  jarred sauce... not even something homemade.

The salads were pretty much disappointing. Greens cut too small, not enough 'stuff' in the salad, and salad dressings that were just ok.... and speaking of calzone and salad - if you don't like either of these dishes, then you're out of luck here, as that's all they have.

In the scheme of calzone and salad places, SOTS is just ok.

After coming back two(!) more times during my second ever trip to Reno I've bumped this place up a start - to five. It deserves it.

I tried the Along Came Pollen pizza and it was flavorful and delicious. Came back again, two times in one week while visiting for work, and tried the Rigatoni with lamb and it was great! And - coming from a dessert guy - the dessert is what really did it! I tried the Carmel Budino and it. was. incredible. I'm not usually a custard / pastry-like dessert (I'm more of a cookie/brownie person) but this dessert stood out above a lot of desserts I've tried. Refreshing Carmel-y with a tiny bit of Oreo like cookie crumbs at the bottom.

While the food really impressed me here, I was also super impressed with the atmosphere and the service. Both huge in my book. This place hits it all out of the park. It may be one of my favorite dinner finds in all of the cities I've visited (it at least makes the top five for sure!).
Love! Patrick is the Best Bartender in Nashville, and the grilled cheese is amazzzzing!!! And the owner Don is great,

Delicious sushi, huge cigar selection, strong drinks and overall unpretentious vibe! The King Kani roll is incredible (lobster tempura inside and king crab on top). Stixx is a great spot, even if you're not a cigar smoker.

Went in for luch, I always time the greet time due to having a previous time as a server. At the 8 minute mark without being greeted the hostess came and asked if we wanted something to drink,  she promptly brought us waters, 3 minutes later we still weren't greeted by a server so we left. Very disappointing that couldn't be greeted with literally 9 total table in the restaurant with people at them, 4 including us didn't even have waters at the table. Either management or servers, maybe both should do their jobs or find another. I worked as a server at one point and can understand if it was busy, but it wasn't at all. Wish there were negative stars.

All the essentials that I need from an Asian supermarket (except cup of noodles, wtf). 

This supermarket has all the "exotic" foods that you need: Chinese, Vietnamese, Japanese, Indian, etc. Pretty large market with lots of variety...

However, the items are VERY overpriced. :( That's what I get for moving to the middle of nowhere.

How else can you play drunken skee-ball?  An arcade/bar/grill restaurant has something for everyone.  Format here is just like Dave & Busters or Gillians (sp?).  Drinks are reasonably-priced and well made and the games are reasonably priced.  Haven't had the food here though.
I had the Shrimpzilla when I went and it was very good.  The wait staff was very friendly and helpful.
This place is great. Large portions and the best hot sour soup we've had up here. Staff is friendly and the restaurant is really clean.

Located near Clearwater Beach just 0.3 mi away, this little gem is my "go to" after a day at the beach. Their food is delicious and price is comparable to any near the beach food shack. It is all outdoor seating with very cute decor with tables from old surfboards, and lights strung underneath beautiful palm trees. It is a cozy spot where you can casually grab a bite to eat. They have a variety of foods to choose from on their menu. My son loves the BBQ burger and fries, OH the FRIES, So so SO GOOD! And the portions are way more than enough for one person, but somehow my 12yr manages to eat his entire burger and most of his fries. I always like to try something different so last night I tried the Bahn mi wrap: Fried shrimp, fresh cilantro, jalapeño, pickled carrots & jicama, garlic mayo, sweet chili sauce. It was very very good! A little too spicy for my taste buds, but I am a wimp when it comes to spicy food. However, the flavor was amazing. Honestly,everything I've had from this place has been delish. The staff is super friendly, food comes out in a timely manner and it's just such a cute place. I'm not kidding when I say this is our go to spot after a day at Clearwater beach. 

The ONLY downside to this place is the parking! On a busy weekend, it is hardly possible to find a nearby parking spot, but don't let that deter you from checking this place out, you will not regret it! 

**Sorry for not having food pics, it is unlike me to forget to post a review AND to not have food pics** And the pics I posted with this review is actually from the first time we went there, which was 5/2020. I am sure I had pics of the food, but already deleted it from my phone. I will update this post with food pics next time! Promise! Ciao for now!
The food was really good esp the brisket.   Friendly people. We sat outside and it had a great atmosphere.
Burger deals on Wednesdays. Save money. Have been here twice. Burgers were similar to five guy and fries the first visit. The second visit was disappointing. Not as friendly staff.

This is NOT susharitto-so don't expect it. My mistake was to think that it would be like the original. Hai street is ok but it is very expensive and does not even try to be "sushi" influenced except that they use raw fish in some rolls. Otherwise there was lots of pickled vegetables, lettuce and bland items. Will not be back. 2 rolls 1 drink = 30$ and seriously it was not yummy or memorable.

I was so disappointed.  The risotto I got tasted like glue and the scallops were cold and rubbery.  My husband enjoyed his steak,  however.  The service was OK.  But we spent a fortune on an AWFUL meal and felt rushed.  They sent us a 10.00 coupon....they can keep it.

Just check in today! 
And seems that everything change
to the better, 
We were so surprise 
We had such a great service from Miranda   
And delicious food !

Great service!  Waitress broke down 9 checks separately drinks and food if we needed to write it off.  Smoked wings are awesome59 calories!  Great oysters.   Not too crowded for a Friday night!  Lots of parking.
The service was fast, friendly and attentive. The food was very delicious. We loved ambience of the place: modern, clean and fairly spacious. A very nice place and wonderful staff.

small and quaint little italian restaurant in the town & country area. me and the misses randomly decided to pop in as we wanted to enjoy a very low key dinner. best part, the prices here for each dish were pretty decent (ranging from about $8-$12 for each dish) & surprisingly didn't break the wallet at all! 

Aside from another person who was dining by himself, we were the only ones in the restaurant which was perfect because we felt as if we had the entire restaurant to ourselves! Our waiter David was super attentive to our needs & was such a gracious host to us - Thanks David!. He recommended us a few dishes until we finally decided on our plan of action.

We ordered the Chicken fettuccine alfredo and our waiter was more than pleased to split the portions up for us evenly as we were sharing that night. 

The tiramisu tasted like it was in the fridge a little too long as it was a little on the icy side when we bit into it so i may skip that one during our next visit.

for a nice quite and intimate dinner, go on and give this place a shot!

Went for Mother's Day brunch, my parents were less than 15m late for our reservation. While walking us to the table the manager was insistent on letting us know we would be kicked out when their next table arrived, to the point where I asked him if he'd rather us just leave right then. Never had an experience like this in a restaurant. To top it off when we were finished there were several open tables. 

Coffee, cinnamon bun and omelets were very good, hummingbird pancakes were so gummy they were almost inedible. Overall good experience, but embarrassing show by management.

Recommended by a local foodie friend for its vibe, relaxed seating and general ambience, not to to mention great drinks. Staff has been great! Mix if people tonight. Two ladies in fur coats/wraps. Low key vibe at the bar. A place I can see visiting many times now that I live here.

This is the old Stratton's space, with a sleek new modernist finish. I had the ham and brie sandwich; my husband had the bananas foster French toast. Both were large portions (neither of us could finish) and we both ended up eating off each other's plates. Delicious! We will be back.

The Melting Pot is a great place for a sit down dinner with a large group of people. The food was excellent, but the price was way too high and the service is moderate. I was displeased when my friends and I were taken to the worst possible table, even though there were better tables available. I will return simply because the food was AMAZING!

PROS: Delicious arctic char, creative flavors
CONS: Too salty, small portions

We came here for Restaurant Week. Talk about salt overload... Almost everything we got was a tad(!) oversalted --- the potted shrimps were interesting in flavor but too salty. The fried zucchini/squash were interesting in taste and texture, but again... too salty! The arctic char came wonderfully cooked: sensuous, savory, and fresh, paired with a smooth hazelnut cream, which I enjoyed. Last... and maybe least, I got the trifle for dessert, which, though not bad, was ultimately underwhelming --- a whad of thick cream with a mix of crunchy granola and... grapes?  Another member of our party got the Lebanon County Peach for dessert, which he described as... a big block of corn bread with some peaches stuck on top. 

I had high expectations based on yelp reviews, and High Street fell short.

Sunday Brunch here was amazing!  I got the vegan ranchero and my husband had the scallops and grits with luscious fried oysters.  The coffee options were impressive as well.  Great food and great coffee made for a memorable birthday celebration.  Everything was perfect and really delicious!  We definitely plan to return soon!  Even though it was really busy, the service was personal and attentive!

Food: 2 Stars
Service: 2 Stars

HuHot has been around for ages and despite our last visit (years ago) being a total abomination, my brother wanted to go back and give it another go. I reluctantly agreed...

Interior was cleaner than I had remembered- it looked like they had replaced their old dingy carpet. The buffet line was kept much cleaner than before and each bin was filled with fresher ingredients. (Fresher, not necessarily fresh.)

The large cooking station was an eye sore. I couldn't help but notice the large pool of goop collecting on the floor where the cooks repeatedly sloshed around in. There were pieces of food and grease along the side walls and who knew how long it had been since that entire space had been cleaned out. 

The food itself was mediocre, but what can you expect when your ingredient choices aren't fresh and the area it's cooking looks as if it has never been cleaned in 10+ years? Still trying to figure out how this place has survived this long...

This is a casual Florida restaurant. Our waiter Jessie, was amazing very attentive and professional. We had three orders of the ribs , the Burger and grouper sandwich. All of us thought our food was really great. The ribs were really tender and the grouper sandwich which I had grilled with light blackened sessoning was to die for. It was a very enjoyable evening in a relaxed Florida environment. I love the way they  took care of my 88 year old father . Very sweet to him and attentive . We will be back. My family are locals and this is one of their favorite places.

Not very happy with the quality of the food. Two of our group had the buffet, two ordered seafood. The food was like warm, not what we expected from this place. We heard how good the food was, this wasn't a good day. The chicken came out hot and if you don't rush up there you won't get it. They cook such a small amount when people are waiting outside to get in. We happen to be here with the Red Hats, and common sense should have told them to cook enough chicken. The seafood came out Luke warm and no special taste. Dookey Chase has lost it great standards. We don't recommend wasting your money here.

Love everything about this place! Food selection, atmosphere, service, quality. Have never had an unpleasant experience. They have an urban garden they harvest some of their greens from that are yummy. Ask your server about this so you select something from their UF offerings. The freshness is wonderful! Nice wine and cocktail assortment. I've heard they have a nice happy hour offering that is a hit with the locals. Have not done this yet!

Is it a better casual Mexican place than Chipotle? Maybe. 

For sure there are a few things that sets Qdoba apart of Chipotle and I am glad to have this place available for lunch in Wilmington. 

For starters, they were the first to offer queso on their menu. Drizzle that yellow goodness over your rice bowl or burrito and you're in heaven. No charge guac? Sign me up please! Bacon? Throw that on anything and it tastes good. They also have preset tacos where you can get 3 for $9.50. As for the other items, they have similar offerings in terms of protein and vessel types (rice bowls, burritos, tacos), but they do have a taco bowl!

It's a nice place to stop into for lunch and there really isn't a line as Wilmington rarely gets busy enough to have one. I do wish that they had the double doors as it does get chilly sitting at the tables, especially if they are near the entrance. Other than that, no other complaints! Swing by for some free guac.

First things first, I think they food is generally very good. I like it better than most of the other Chinese places in and around Lansdale. But their service and delivery is absolutely awful. Most times the delivery time takes around an hour to an hour and a half, and we live approximately 7 minutes away. This past time we ordered, and after waiting the usual hour and ten minutes, I open the bag to find that my sweet and sour chicken came with no sweet and sour sauce. So I call to find out why, and the girl gives me an attitude that yes it came with it and that it is in a container. Now, I wear contacts, but I could definitely see there was no container of sweet and sour sauce. She then asked me how far I live from them, and then told me they would bring it right to me. That was 30 minutes ago. I'm still waiting for it, so I have currently waited almost two hours to eat my dinner. This will be the last time I order from them.

This location is very close to me!! Been to Marlton one& Cherry Hill !!  Love it.. great coffee and such variety of food to choose.
Love the call ahead seating.
Score!!

We love the shrimp fired rice and Hot & Sour soup.  We have not had a dish we did not like.  The only drawback is that they are so anguish to serve that sometimes the main dish arrives before you finish the appetizers.  Easy solution wait to order the main dishes.

Love this place!  Great Southwestern food that tastes fresh.  Nice atmosphere especially when the weather is nice and you can dine on the patio.  Love their margaritas and sopapillas!  The staff has always been friendly and attentive. Highly recommend this restaurant if you are looking for good Southwestern food.

5 stars for what is, a restaurant in a hospital with sit down dining! The loaded nachos with chicken is my go-to meal. The buffalo chicken Cobb salad has always been fresh and delicious. Always satisfied with the quick and friendly service. A menu with lots of options. Have heard patrons that  after going there for over a year, wish they could have a new/refreshed menu.

It's gets three stars for the duh attitude.   We called, placed an  order and MENTIONED the YELP AD - didn't get the discount. That was irritating. 

So Food ok - hot, tasty - would order again.  - Wouldn't be my NUMBER 1

Eggs were great 
Bacon great potatoes great 

But the French toast wasn't as good as egg spected 
An for mediocre breakfast it wasn't really worth the price of almost 100$ 

But first for everything

Hate to play the role of Buzzkill Bob here, but I can't see how Boswell's deserves it current 4.5-star Yelp rating.

Solid burgers, good buns, weak fries, pretty good onion rings, decent milkshake, smiley waitress, fast service.

That's the Cliffs Notes version of my experience.

For Harley-Davidson fans and nostalgia buffs, I can see why this would be a 5-star experience. The atmosphere is certainly one of a kind.

If you're just talking about the food, it's A-OK (3 Yelp stars).

Quiet because people don't come here to get attention or be hip. They come here to partake of a cozy, friendly place run by down-to-earth people. Coffee, Food, WiFi and Charm - that's what you'll find.

Probably my favorite place for chow on the east side! Huge menu with many diner food options and they do them well. Don't come here for eating healthy but if you need warm, Midwest home cooking it's the spot. Nice service too

Short and simple review. Had family dinner here a couple nights ago and it was great! Lasagna as our entree and fried mozzarella as our appetizer. Food was great and the service was even better. We were there on a crowded Friday evening, but our waitress came around often to ensure we were doing okay. The food also came out rather quickly which is always a big plus. Will definitely be back.

My husband and I decided to try this place for dinner on Weds night since it got such great reviews on Yelp; plus we both come from Neapolitan roots, so the menu intrigued us as dishes that our mamas and nonnas made us as kids. We arrived at 6:30ish and the place was relatively empty with only one large table of 6 filled and a table of 2.  We were not greeted or welcomed - it was actually kind of surprising in a small place. Eventually, a woman (she seemed overworked) came to our table to take our order - no explanation, no questions about whether we had been there before, etc.  Just all business with very little comments. We could have placed our order on an iPad for all the communication she offered! When she did speak, she seemed to speak perfect, albeit accented, English. When my husband ordered the Spaghetti Capri, she explained they were out of mussels but he was fine with just clams.  It took 30 mins for our salad and soup to arrive. They were very good, the pasta e fagioli loaded with fresh carrot and celery shreds. Thirty minutes later (by now the place was filling up and the lone server was really harried) our main entrees arrived. My husband's Spaghetti alla vongole in a red sauce was surprisingly loaded with mussels and clams but not the Capri that he ordered - he didn't say a thing and just accepted it.  His pasta was also swimming in sauce, ala a typical American-ized Italian restaurant, which was very disappointing. My 3 flavors of gnocchi were delicious, the cheese sauce my favorite. Overall, the food was good but not great. The pizza, which appears to get all the rave reviews, looks fabulous and we should have ordered that.  It's a small neighborhood place, however, don't come here and expect a warm welcome!

Service was so bad I had to review. Like another reviewer who came on cinco de mayo, my experience was embarrassing. The music was very loud and conversations were very hard to have even between us and the server. The service was the worst I have ever had at a restaurant and the servers were inattentive but could be found on the dance floor rather than helping those at tables. The restaurant staff was clearly not caring about the service of their customers. It took way to long for us to order and be served and for our check to arrive. There was a man in a cantina polo who seemed to be managing the floor but was also then drinking on the job. I will not be back.

RACIST!!!!!!! Do not support this establishment. We went on a Friday and ordered one hookah for 15 and service was ok. It was a party of 4 no issues. Come on a Saturday and they are racially profiling customers. Seating who they want to seat. They tell us as a party of 5 we need to order at least 3 hookahs to sit. Then we meet some ppl there and they said they were ordering hookahs we could sit together, then he says no now you need to order minimum of 6 hookahs to sit and do you have the money. Because your tab will be 300-400 dollars. We are African American and they clearly don't want our business or could do without it. do not support this establishment !!!!

Ate here when I was back home in TN for Thanksgiving. Had a great meal at Josephine. The highlights for me were:

- Very nicely executed old fashion, and I tried my gf's tequila based cocktail. It was delicious as well.

- The Brussels sprouts are some of the best I have had anywhere. They were the best food highlight for me.

- I had a bolognese dish that was very good and nicely done. My gf out ordered me and got a beef cheek dish with risotto that was melt in your mouth. 

Overall, I would absolutely eat here again when I'm back in town.

My usual: sausage, egg and cheese on an everything bagel (pepper & ketchup)

The bagels are toasted to perfection; not too soft, and not so toasted that it squishes out the contents of the sandwich when you take a bite.
The everything bagels are truly "everything" bagels.

Prices are great for the level of quality that you get.

Set in the trendy 12South district, this coffee shop is Bond-themed in a tasteful way - drink and food names, decorations. The custom lattes are delicious, albeit a little pricey. The breakfast menu, served all day, is extremely reasonable and varied, and very reasonable (ie. $5 avocado toast). This shop is a great place to work inside or out, with WiFi and ample seating. Parking is free for the first hour, but then you have to pay quite a bit.

We got takeout from here while on vacation. Food was pretty good. I got the country fried sirloin and it was delicious.  Only small gripe is about the rolls, only gave us 3 when we ordered 3 entrees. May just have to ask for some extra ones
This place is pretty good, i recommend the omega3 and sakura rolls :) (i think that's what they're called if i remember right)

I have been interested in going here for quite some time, and finally had the opportunity to go on Friday night.  I took my sister who was in from out of town and was willing to be a guinea pig.  Their menu is well laid out with full entree and small plate options so you can try different things!  She ordered the lamb shank entree and I ordered hummus, the swordfish skewers, and the stuffed grape leaves (small plate options).  Before our meals came out, or server brought us some pita wedges and this tomato-type spread to go on it.  Our server was thoughtful - he made sure that we had fresh pita wedges when the hummus came out rather than have us use the pita wedges they brought out when we first arrived.  We thought the ambiance of the restaurant was really charming, our service was great, and the food was tasty.  I will be back!

This is the place if you are a hip people watcher. If you want good tasting Mexican food, go to many other options in this area.
I have never had green sauce on my enchiladas before and hope never to again. Horrible taste. I only ate a little over half of the two of them and only because I was hungry.   The chips and salsa complimentary were the best part
of a $20 meal for one.  I don't recommend.
This has always been my go to Chinese. It's quick and good. However over the past year, their prices have gone up so much. At this point, I may as well go to Panda Express across the street.
Food is EXCELLENT! just hope they dont get cocky...the best in new castle....cant get any better chinese
Ambiance, atmosphere, unusual seasonings on all the food, jazz on Wednesday nights and Flamenco on Saturday nights make this a treat time for the small town of St. Petersburg.

Looking for a quick bite to eat? Chili's in Jenkintown is your place, but not if you expect quality food.  I ordered quesadilla explosion salad...basically bag o salad topped with Pico De gallo, corn and beans, served with frozen salad chicken (you know the processed white meat strips in a bag).  I know it if because we held our up to my husband's chicken and you can see it is processed.  and hubby's fajitas came with a skillet of chicken and veggies.  no rice, no beans...nada.  Didn't even bother with a drink because I didn't want to overpay for a syrupy mess with a touch of liquor.  Service was good.  This is definitely not the Chilis that we used to know.
I have been in 3-4 times since they opened a few months back. I have not found a single item that wasn't great. Friendly and consistent!

I just was at this location.  I have been a customer since it opened, often coming 2 times per month.  It is not busy and I was sat with my husband, the hostess was less than happy to be there.  We sat at our table on the patio and watched 3 other tables be sat and served and we had not received even water.  We decided to leave and asked to speak to the owner,  so they knew our issues, the original hostess still was rude.  The owner didn't response to our concerns, I don't know if he was there, but the young women who helped us tried correct the situation, too late. For a establishment of this caliber it has gone down hill. Never going back.

We come here often to sit in the back room and get work done. There usually are not many people and it's really spread out, so comfortable. The problem is the service. While very nice, isn't very good. Even getting a mug with some milk to put coffee in can be a small ordeal, and the various coffees they have out are rarely hot. Having said that, prices are reasonable.

Why is it that there is always someone either doing business loud enough for everyone to hear or talking on the phone loud enough for everyone to hear? And it happens in the main section and the back room.
This was my first Waffle House experience ever and I didnt know it was so stinkin cheap!!  That chocolate chip waffle sure was super delicious.  Cant wait to go back and try has browns next

I will give this place a 2-star for the intimate decor inside which feels very authentic. 
I went on a Sunday evening. We requested to sit on this table where the lantern is right on top. The waiter/host says that place is for party of 12. This place was empty and there were so many areas where group seating could be used.  So we were denied to sit in a table of our choice. This is not the way you make customer feel welcome and bring business.
