Second, we ordered the fez half chicken which is basically a baked chicken with gravy. (Almost curry style).  There was no rice or bread served with the chicken??  How do you serve a chicken with no rice or any sides?  The taste was not even good.  

I really don't know who is rating the food here as 5-star. I'm sure it's people that never even ate good Moroccan food.  I'm from NYC and this is by far the worst Moroccan cuisine I've ate.  
The service is dull, the waiter has no guest service etiquette and he tried to rip us off by charging us for double.  No, it' was NOT a mistake. 

We did not try the Hookah, but the food is terrible.  This spot may just good for hookah which are over priced as hell lol. $25-35 plus they charge u tips and max ppl per hookah policy.
Bar none the best restaurant experience I've had the pleasure of enjoying.

This was a pleasant surprise! I stopped in for what was originally just a snack and ended up eating dinner before a long drive home. this is definitely a place I see myself coming back to on a regular basis. Love the crush on this pizza definitely a must try

We had the most amazing experience at this restaurant. The staff is incredibly friendly and the food was impeccable. The portions were great to share so there is more food to try. Gonna be visiting St. Pete every weekend just to get a bite to eat here!

Had the Italian and it was delicious! Big sandwich so it lasted for two meals. The free coffee with purchase was a nice touch as well. Pretty good coffee at that! I'm going to make this my traveling-north-on-19 stop from here on out.
The oasis diner is a lovely little oldies style diner like something out of a detective movie.  Awesome food! Can't wait to come here on a rainy day and pretend I'm a rugged cop.

I got to go order from this restaurant oh my g that was delicious brisket so good cook and tender, sausage was the best I had in Reno and sides Mac and cheese was good traditional coleslaw was so good and not too much saucey for defenetly recommend this restaurant specialt in corona period because everybody stay in home.

Don't bother...
Overpriced undercooked poached eggs Stanley not worth the $14. We went for the softshell crab Eggs Benedict, which aren't on the menu anymore. Had Eggs Stanley instead, which was Eggs Benedict with fried oysters on the side. Oysters were way overcooked- I grow my own oysters on Chesapeake Bay and know how a fried oyster should be. And there was effectively no sauce on the dish, just a runny drizzle of something that had no flavor. I guess butter and fresh lemon are too expensive?

I visited this place for the first time at 2:00 in the morning, so I wasn't expecting a stellar meal. However, despite that, the experience was still lacking.  Our waitress was friendly, but also insistent on saying "good morning" or "have a good morning."  I get it.  At 2:00 a.m., it is technically "a.m.," but I would guess that most people frequenting this place aren't exactly starting their days at 2 a.m. 

Anywho, back to the food. I ordered the soup, and while it was delicious, it was room temperature at best. We asked the waitress to reheat it, and when she brought it back, it was warmer, but still not hot.  

Also, they didn't want anyone sitting in the back corner where they couldn't be seen. But, instead of blocking the section off, they yelled at everyone who went back there to sit. "Please seat yourself." "No don't sit there."  Maybe just tell people where to sit, or block the section off instead of getting mad at everyone who tried to seat themselves like they were told.

If other pieces of the experience were different, I would probably go back and try some of the other menu items. But, cmon, it's soup. It should be hot!

Can't say a bad word about this place. The only thing I could've complained of they changed (back and front house menus being exclusive to one another.) Since they've remedied that I have nothing to comment on. The service is always kind and fast, they have stellar food options whether brunch or dinner. Their cocktails are on par with the high end cocktails places that have been cropping up in Nashville. Great spot in Germantown!

Let me be the first to say that this place is a great spot. Really good pub grub and good service.  The service is friendly and they are fast with a joke or to light up your smoke.  It would be great if they had a better dessert menu, but for a young drinking hole,we will let it slide and keep checking.  Someone said this place is just "Ok" we buried him outback.  Again don't expect white linen but a solid burger cold beer, biker and hippie friendly.  Thanks and I'm looking forward to more Memories!
The owners and staff are super friendly here, the food is definitely the best Chinese food in the Rivergate area! If you like crab Rangoon's you have to try theirs!

I really want to like this place but unfortunately, it just wasn't special. My wife and I placed an order for a 10 inch birthday cake. We asked for a chocolate flavored cake with mocha filling. The cake texture was stale and the mocha filling was thinly layered, comparable to Betty crocker. The fondant was more than 1 inch thick and was unbelievably heavy. To paint a picture, when you cut the cake, you actually have to use a spoon to dig out the cake because the Fondant stands still while the stale cake breaks apart completely. 

If you want a cake for presentation purposes, classic cake truly does a great job. If you want a cake to eat, you might as well go down the street and buy some cake mix and make it yourself.

We came here for Valentine's Day and could not be more impressed. Our server was so nice and very attentive. Drinks were outstanding; my husband said it was the best Old Fashioned he'd ever had, and my martini was delicious. The food was even better. The crab orzo, which was a special for Valentine's Day, was incredible and loaded with crab (we literally joked about coming back with a bucket and having them fill it with orzo). I ordered the red snapper, which was seasoned perfectly, and my husband's filet cut like butter. We can't wait to come back.

Great little barbecue place, good selection of beers and locally bottled sodas, seating is very limited so get there earlier on the weekends. Portions were good for the prices especially for a restaurant featured on Food Network.

Great place to hang out and have a few beers with the boys. Good selection of beer too so you can't go wrong with that.  Food is good all around. We didn't have any complaints with any of the food. Staff was attentive and nice so we're all good there

Went for a work lunch with a few people and they got every sandwich wrong despite it being relatively quiet in there when we ordered. 

Staff is young and inexperienced, which is fine by me (you have to start somewhere!) but the attitudes are really poor.  It also was not clean in there and they weren't using really hygienic processes to make the sandwiches. 

This isn't the type of place I'd eat lunch normally but I went in with a completely open mind. My mind was quickly shut. 

I wouldn't go back.
Great and fast food and friendly staff per usual. Never disappointed after visiting this place.

Visited last month with a large group of friends and family...can't say enough good things! The food was so delicious, the wine choice (and I'm very picky) was great, my fiancé had beer and also sampled wine and was very impressed! Wish we lived closer because this would be a regular spot for us. Can't wait to visit again in the near future!

Simply, the BEST. We accidentally stumbled upon this place after leaving a nearby restaurant (in disappointment). That was over 5 years ago and now we make it a point to eat here whenever we are in town.

The positives: 

#1 - The food is FRESH. You can distinctly taste every ingredient, which means it hasn't lost its integrity by sitting in the freezer for days.

#2 - Everything is made from scratch right there in the kitchen. Even the tortilla chips and salsa, which tells me the owner is attentive to detail and truly cares about what they are serving. Warning: the salsa has some kick to it, not recommended for first timers or those who cry easily.

#3 - Flavorful and perfectly seasoned (which is why you won't find a salt shaker sitting on any table, it's not needed). The chicken and braised beef can stand on their own, but are also wonderfully complimented in many of the dishes.

#4 - Consistency. Same great food ..... Every. Single. Time.

The negatives: 

#1 - I have yet to find any, other than I wish I lived closer so that I could eat here more often!

Possibly the best breakfast in the French Quarter. Big portions at a small price. Seems more like a locals spot. 

Try the hash brown meltdown. A layer of hash browns topped with cheese, bacon, poached eggs then country gravy poured all over it. I am craving it again already. They also had a crayfish quiche that looked pretty damn good.

Disappointing....for all the hype about pats and genos ... The food was wack.. I have had better cheesesteaks from a bodega for half the price and twice the quality...,do yourself a favor and never eat here...save your money it ain't worth it

A really cute family owned middle eastern restaurant serving you good portion sized warm meal. I love their sandwiches and they are perfect for a lunch meet up. I also am a big fan of their olives. The variety of olives in the big barrels are amazing !

I am late posting this, right before christmas, I stopped here by accident! I was very impressed with the food and service. Small but nice and perfect. I went to Chickie and Petes but they had this wait due to Covid so decided to just try this place. I am so glad I did, I am a fan! Will definitely be returning. I had a  the handcut cheesesteak sandwich and OMG the chips were homemade, you will Love them! Try this place!  You will not be disappointed!

If you eat nothing else here, you need to eat the tres leches cake. Chuy's has the best tres leches that I've ever had, and I've had a lot of tres leches from some hardcore Mexican establishments. This is the tres leches to end tres leches. It will satisfy your soul.

So now that you've had the most important part of any meal (dessert), the next thing you must eat is the queso. Now, I'm not a big queso person, because queso in Indiana is usually white and watery. But Chuy's queso is perfectly orange and housemade -- the cheese is balanced perfectly by the chiles that are added, which give it a nice kick.

You'll need something to wash down all that sugar and cheese, so you should naturally order a margarita. The lime juice is squeezed fresh here (no
mixes), so I suggest the house margarita on the rocks. It's not too sweet, and you can really taste the lime. If you're not into lime, they have a mean watermelon margarita. (Yes, I tried both, because por que no los dos!) 

I could make a meal on those three things alone, but if you want "food" food, I suggest ordering something with sauce, like an enchilada. In fact, order the tomatillo enchiladas, because that sauce is bomb. I had the pleasure of talking to the owner during my visit, and he let me know that they make all of their sauces from scratch. From scratch! They also make their tortillas from scratch, which I tasted when I ordered a chicken quesadilla. You can really tell the difference when you eat a quesadilla made with a housemade tortilla. 

This restaurant is super family friendly, and there are lots of tchotchkes and art on the walls to look at. They have this game going where they've hidden a bunch of tiny dogs everywhere, and kids are encouraged to find them. Speaking of dogs: If you bring in a framed photo of your dog, they will hang it on their wall! That's so great.

As a avid sushi lover, I would give this place three stars at most.
It's not terrible, but not amazing. I enjoy eating udon quite a bit and I was glad to see they had that on their menu. The broth is quite tasty but I guess since its only an appetizer, the amount of udon noodles they give you is quite pathetic. I don't really recommend any of their "fancy rolls" since I don't think they are worth the price but the regular ones such as crunchy spicy tuna is not bad. The roll size and thickness(?) is appropriate.

One of my favorite date night treats. The dining room is excellent but we prefer the lounge with the live music and chef tastings. Drinks are fantastic, food always good, service is top notch. Only down side is how far away it is from us. Always a good meal here.

I Have been to Ceviche countless times and have never had a bad experience. My favorite Ceviche location hands down is in downtown St Pete and the main reason for this review. The food is great as well as the service. You cannot go wrong with the Solomillo Segovia (Wellington), Patatas Bravas (potatoes with aoili), Morrillo De Cochinillo (pork shank), Atun Estilo Tartaro (ahi tuna) and for dessert the Almenrado (almond pastry with vanilla ice cream and berries). I only give this restaurant four stars because the thought of the immaculate service and quality improving...really excites me.

In last weeks Caliente section of our newspaper there was a coupon for a buy one get one free dinner.  We haven't been to a Macayo's for years.  Too many other smaller places have opened that we really prefer.  However, being a real Gringo at the time many years ago.  We thought that Macayo's was great.  For starters lets go to the chips and salsa.  Chips were OK very thin and crispy.  The sauce was tart and too salty.  I ordered what I ordered so many years ago the Chicken Poblano.  It was just fair as well as the beans and rice.  Very ordinary.  My other half ordered the carnita taco, with BBQ sauce and pineapple.  Sounded kind of trendy and different.  He liked it.  I tasted it and it was fair.  To be fair about that is that I am not a lover of BBQ sauce especially on carnitas.  The tortillas were pretty bad.  Like soft cardboard to try to describe them.  The place is so dark you can barely read the menu.   The wait staff is great.  Believe it or not, I remember the waiter we had from over at least 15 years since our last visit.  I am afraid I will have to wait to go back again.  It was just very ordinary.  They were very crowded mostly with retirees who probably think the food was perfect.  It well may be.  But we'll keep exploring.

Wonderful authentic Irish place.
What a fantastic jewel. 
A must stop in Nashville.
Food was great, drink just the same(Harp & Guinness) but the hospitality  was awesome. Colm waited on us Saturday and we found out he is following his Dad who is a great Irish entertainer. On second visit we saw Colm provide great entertainment in the form of Irish and country music and song. We also found out that Colm has produced his first cd .We listened to it today and it was fantastic. Best of luck Colm. Just remember us when you get to perform at the GOA.

Paula McNamara greeted us with a most warm welcome. Paula and her husband Sean are fully engaged in overseeing the business and it is very clear how proud they are of their product. The brown bread and tea was on the table in no time.we enjoyed great salmon as well as bangers and mash. For dessert we listened to Colm and his team captivate the audience.
In short this was a wonderful smoke free extremely clean facility with great food and drink. It was capped by the fantastic service and hospitality shown by the entire staff.
As Irish born customers (3 of 4) we visit many Irish restaurants accross the country. We find many Irish in name only. McNamaras is the real deal. It is 15 minutes from airport and the same from the GOA.

The Volcano Shrimp was one of the best shrimp appetizers I've had, also the San Burned Steak Burrito and Zim Zari Wrap (got to try both : ) we're very tasty! My wife and I ate outside on the patio, very nice, the service was excellent, the waitress very friendly, gave us suggestions, and the food came out very fast! We'll be back, with friends/family next time ! Tge manager came by our table twice to make sure everything was ok and also gave us a gift card for a free appetizer for our next visit. Highly recommended for something different that you can't get elsewhere :)

Love their salads! I make my own but the best part is the fresh mozzarella! I also get their peppers, cranberries, almonds, roasted chicken, with the raspberry dressing. Can't tell you how much money I've spent on these during college at SJU living in manayunk!
The stomach issue was definitely from the buffet despite your accusation to the contrary. I understand it is difficult to keep a buffet 100% safe it is what it is.

We ordered takeout from "just wings" inside of this chili's.... it was horrible we ordered a bundle of 44 boneless wings and curly fries...
We ordered 11 Buffalo 11garlic Parmesan and 22lemon pepper....... they all tasted exactly the same they had basically no flavoring on them at all. Honestly just glorified chicken nuggets... there was so much breading and close to no chicken in them... then the curly fries are sooo salty! It was a complete waist of money I am so disappointed!!

Haven't been to Simon's Cafe & Lounge for several years but glad to see that nothing has changed since the last time I was there. I love the decor because it takes you back to a time when cozy family dining was what most restaurants looked like. The menu is varied and full of selections that I'd say will fit most patrons taste. Portions are (in my opinion) the right size and when I finished my dinner I was more than satisfied. Ingredients are fresh and cooked just right. Service is good too. Simon's bar scene is more lively than the dining room where the "regulars" gather. Gaming is available to those who wish at the bar and there is an ATM available in case one needs it although there is a BofA ATM just outside the door too. The patio is large with plenty of tables and distance measures are followed as well as masks and heightened cleaning is visible. A neighborhood gem for sure!

To do research for Sunday's Dining on a Dime podcast (wildfireradio.com sundays 5-6)  we went to Jack's Tavern in Media and I am glad we did!  The cheesesteak was big, tasty and $8.75!  The roll was chewy and the fried onions were plentiful and gave it big flavor! Carole got a pound of amazing steamed garlic shrimp for $9.95.  Jack's Tavern is cash only and smoking is allowed.

You must go here!!! Robin needs to be your server!!! It was a great experience. The grounds are adorable with a lot of parking and a lot of opportunities to shop. 
I purchased peach preserves, a hat, and pumpkin pecan butter. 
The food - amazing! My sister and I ate two servings of the piping hot biscuits served with housemade preserves that would make you sing! 
My sister liked the blackberry preserves the best. I loved the ham and eggs (the ham and fried chicken are signature dishes. Oh and the hasbrown casserole is soooooo good! I also had a strawberry dipper made with Strawberry Whiskey that was phenomenal. This was a truly great experience I would recommend coming even though you'll wait a bit for a table, grab the kids, grab a drink and play some bean bags (cornhole) or sit on one of the many benches around the property and relax. It's worth it and the drive to get there even better!

I hadn't been to an Einstein's in years. Most locations have closed. I've always been a fan of their bagels, so I was happy to stop in today. 

I got a poppy seed bagel with cream cheese and bacon and it hit the spot. Not many places have poopy seed bagels and I just love them! 

The service here has much to be desired, but the food is good.

So me and my boyfriend constantly get food from this truck , their tacos are good the corn has became our favorite but today we purchased food from these guys and my boyfriend got a drink it's a special drink they have , he didn't taste it until he got home and it was horrible it was straight water ! So he went back and explained to them that this drink was no good could he get a new one they tried to give him a small one when he bought a large one , he had just left this place like 10mins ago from this situation , they told him they can't give him a new drink because he tasted the one he had like wtf ! They literally just lost customers because of that , they gave him the hardest time ever just for a drink so my boyfriend left very disappointed these people are BAD BUSINESS ! It was a guy ! Usually it's always ladies but this guy was a straight ASS

Had brunch here recently - pretty hipster joint; I was excited to go having heard great things, but this place didn't really knock my socks off as I had expected.  I did the make-your-own frittata with veggies and smoked mozzarella.  It was decent; they bring out a bottle of some type of sauce which I thought was ketchup - I was wrong. It's very sweet and I wasn't a fan.  I like that they have sriracha on all the tables, though. Being a huge brunch fan, I'd say I'd be less inclined to go here again.  I think there are definitely better spots nearby.

I came for my birthday & my waiter Fred had shouted me out for it... it was so great I cried!!! I went back the second day and the egg Benedict was soo good. I recommend the St. Charles Benedict !!!! Yumm!!
Vegan southern cooking that tastes better than it would with meat and/or dairy! Phenomenal

Great experience at this restaurant on The Pier. Started with our server Colin and continue with some great food and recommendations from Colin. Every dish was delicious! Started off with the special Shrimp dish and the mussels. Sooo good. Then on to the Grouper and for dessert Banana Pudding. Everything we had was great and even had live music. Located on the water with amazing views. Couldn't be any better. Thank You Colin for the terrific service and friendly personality.

Pizza was fresh, great service we loved the pizza. If we are in Nashville ever in Nashville again we would definitely go back here. It's a most try if you are Nashville and in the mood for pizza. Great find!

I had enjoyed Lovebird takeout twice since it opened and loved it but decided to ask them to cater a small socially distanced party and it was perfect. The food was ready on time and packaged individually, no sharing or touching anything. Each meal was in a separate shopping bag too. 
The food is wonderful; crispy and tender chicken, flavorful Brussels Sprouts, crunchy fried pickles. And really, the prices are very fair.  I heard one of the young guests say to her father, "it's just like KFC if KFC was good!"  
Thank you Lovebird for making my very small, socially distanced celebration of a very special occasion so easy and fun.

Had dinner here Saturday (11/11) with a large group celebrating my sisters birthday and engagement and had a fantastic time. The establishment was beautiful and very accommodating. All the food and drinks were delicious.They even helped coordinate a surprise birthday cake. Our server, I believe his name was Adrian (AAAAADRIANNN!) did an incredible job. Overall the entire group had a great time and it will definitely be on my list when I return to Philly!

Puckett's is a mix of so many wonderful things from live music to unique concept to the steady stream of customers enjoying themselves late into the evening. Chicago doesn't have musicians playing on every restaurant corner so it was nice to relax after work with a little country music while we ate and drank. The food was okay but I have a feeling it's the music and concept that keep people coming back in droves. The place was packed! 

Our 7pm reservation on a Wednesday turned out to be something we actually needed. People were standing 2 deep near the front wall as open tables were hard to come by. And this was after we were seated. The music was inviting without being too loud. Some songs reached a level making communication rather difficult but in general the noise level wasn't too bad. 

The beer list was primarily full of mass produced domestics of which I wasn't a fan - then again I'm a big city beer snob looking for great craft brew from small breweries around the country. Our spinach artichoke dip and fried pickle & jalapeno appetizers were a nice start. Both were better than some of the other restaurants we've visited in Nashville. But my ribeye steak was a little disappointing. It was tough, stringy, and I ended up leaving 50% of my steak uneaten due to the large amounts of fat. I understand ribeyes have fat - this is why I order them. But this was more like I ordered a fat steak with a little ribeye meat on the side. It was served with bacon wrapped green beans, mashed potatoes and a corn cake. The sides played their supporting role as nothing special was eaten in the group. 

The apple pie with ice cream for dessert was good as well. I'm an apple pie maker at home so they were up against stiff competition from my taste buds but it was a nice close to our dinner. The best thing about Puckett's was the atmosphere. It's a fun place to be and be seen. You can get better food in Nashville but you may not get a better place.

This the second time I have gone here, both times the food was amazing. I always suggest the Chef's special, It's the best deal, you get a suprise of four different meals from the special menu on one plate. Between the 2 of us we had 8 options to taste! That's the way to go. This time I tried the fish, it was amazing and a very large portion.  I finished my fish later on in the evening at home! 

This place is always packed, so I suggest making a reservation if you don't mind waiting for a bit. 

Can't wait to go back!
I have eaten here for the last 4 weeks and every meal was so delicious and fresh. Jill is taking great care of me and I love her sweet personality. Keep it up Bernini!

Open 2 days....me and fellow Yelpie, Katie A. are hot on it.  Wow.....Chef Tyler, Merritt and comrades put on quite a show.  

Located on the edge of Algiers point, this unassuming darling eatery sits nestled in the middle of a neighborhood.  Easy for Westbankers and The New Orleans crowd to find.  Literally the first exit and 5 minutes from off the expressway(or the last exit depending on your direction).....Plenty of street parking to be had.  
While the dining room is currently undergoing her transformation (take notice of J. Pierre's masterpiece in progress) you can either call ahead or order at their clever walk up window.  
I had looked at their website (plumealgiers.com) before Katie arrived to check out what this new gem had to offer.
And.......yep just order one of everything off the lunch menu.
What a treat! I preface my opinion but saying these are standard ingredients in epic combinations.  The choices are daring and perfect for any adventurous tastebuds.  I found my self ohhhhing and ahhhhhing with every bite as did Katie. 
I can't say I have a favorite because I enjoyed it all.  Something was really spicy for me that caused me to perspire, but not to Katie.  I really loved the Aloo Chaat, it reminded me of comfort food with a surprising chickpea crunch.  The Chow Mein was substantially delicious and the Kaathi Roll is so perfect for a grab and go.  Keep in mind the salads may not be what you would expect, no lettuce, just combinations of great ingredients. I found both to be delicious.  The Recheado full of delicious crab and shrimp & the Mango salad with its ripe mango, plethora of summertime tomatoes and dressed in a dynamic yogurt. 

Welcome to the neighborhood Plume, you're going to be quite the adornment that Algiers was looking for. Can't wait to see how the menu changes based on the fresh ingredients you acquire, it's all so exciting!

Love this place!! 
A great spot that focuses on fueling their customers with nutritious and healthy foods so our bodies can flourish. Drop the fast food and start feeding your body what it needs!!

The Brassery  At Saint James has a nice relaxing place Hannah great place to catch a local microbrew.  The service I received there a during this my 1st visit was extremely good and the food was more than I expected I thought their prices were fair.    I enjoyed the atmosphere  and the friendly staff.  I know will definitely  come back.
Great brunch place! Looks like a speakeasy Bar. I got the spicy chicken and bacon eggs benny. Very good!
YOU GUYS. They have something here called "Crunchy French Toast." It had oatmeal and almonds on the outside. I think it was deep-fried. I will dream of it for the rest of my life.

Best real Mexican taqueria we've found ( although a few on Cherokee street are very close). Chips, salsa, cheese dip, guacamole, tacos, a chile relleno if we're feeling starved and a few cheap (but good) margaritas - a great way to spend less than $20 on a fun date.
The food was alright, but the cashier was so rude! He seemed annoyed with even taking our order. He will drive business away
Definitely became one of our favorites in Reno! Cute atmosphere and delicious food. I had the pulled pork, the corn bread was to die for as well.

This is my favorite pizza place in Reno! Naples style... light and fresh. They get special flour from Naples and they wood-fire then in a custom made 900 degree oven... my daughter lives to sit at the bar and watch them make them. 

Their flavor combinations on their gourmet pizzas is fabulous... some combinations you might not think of pairing. We like the hot honey try drizzle on the Paulie G pizza, our favorite. You can get some in the side to dip your amazing crust in. 

Another great menu item are the green beans mixed in olive oil,garlic, herbs and bread crumbs and cooked in the hot flames of the fire.  Order it with pizza points and use them to scoop up the goodness in the bottom of the dish. 

They make their sausages and meatballs there, all ingredients except the canned tomatoes are fresh and made daily. 

They also let you bring in wine purchased at Whispering Vines near by and drink it there, although they have beer and wine as well. 

Family run and always great service!
Great pizza.  Awesome wait staff.  Wednesday night from 6 to 7:30 they have awesome music.    Highly recommend

I absolutely like the way you are welcomed and greeted there. They wash your hands with rose water. 
I like the 7 course meal and ambience was good as well. The other thing I liked about their was since we all were given the same food it felt more like a family ceremony where you all eat together from one served item at a time. 
They had options for vegetarians too so that was a plus for us.

What's more to love than a reasonable priced Thai food and byob? 
The usual are always roti canai and curry chicken on rice. Can't go wrong with these here!
If I'm feeling a bit fancy, it'll be changed to pad Thai or basil chicken, also can't go wrong.
Big birthdays that need unlimited alc provided by you? Here's the perfect place!

Probably the best place to get authentic tacos in the Bensalem Area. 
The restaurant is in the back of a Mexican Market and has available seating. Very informal but I think that's what makes this place unique. 
The decor is very nice and tries to make the restaurant look nice without looking tacky. 

You can order food for here to to go, and the staff is very nice and always are very polite. Haven't had any communications issues yet (I only speak English) and usually at authentic taquerias I can barely communicate my order. 

Food is absolutely delicious and not overpriced. 
I usually pay the same for 3 carnitas tacos in South Philly compared to here.

Pro: The owner is a simply as nice and accommodating as she could possibly be. It is unlikely you will come across lovelier people in a food setting anywhere in Central Indiana.

The food is excellent. You get what you ask for every single time. I must have eaten at this restaurant no less than 100 times and I can not think of a single complaint, ever. 

Con: There is only one Thai Lanna. 

Some might say that the service is slow and that the food comes out a dish at a time; however, I would say this is a Pro because the food is always high quality and it is like she is making it herself in her own kitchen and is not interested in letting things sit under a hot lamp. 

Overall: If you don't eat here, it is your mistake.

We had a very pleasant stay here, as the room was quite and staff was very friendly. The only issue we had was having to request a new iron and shampoo as they forgot to relish our shampoo on the second night. One thing I would suggest they have to make it 5 stars is having room service and a bigger convince store options. We also arrived at the restaurant at 11am which was right after breakfast ended. It took us a few mins to get acknowledged and get menus although there was apparent management staff all over tallying receipts but they didn't acknowledge us.
Absolutely lives up to the hype. The aesthetic is everything and the food is delicious. The fresh juice and craft coffee is wonderful.

Great oysters, cold beer and awesome hushpuppies. The gumbo is good, but definitely has a different flavor than other gumbos I've had in NOLA. Went at lunch time and the place was COVERED UP. Be prepared to wait... Or get there right when they open. We sat at the bar- squeezed between other foodies, but it was a great experience.

On our road trip to Philly, I recommended to my boyfriend that we stop at DiNic's for our first meal. We walked from our hotel to Reading Terminal Market. Immediately upon entering the market, we both were in awe over all the different and numerous things we could eat. Nonetheless, we headed straight for DiNic's, which had a line that wrapped over to the soul food seating area. 

The line moved pretty quickly though and we both ordered roast pork sandwiches with sharp provolone and broccoli rabé. Luckily, we managed to snatch two seats at the counter and devoured the sandwiches right there and then. It was so good. The pork was juicy, the bread held up well and soaked the juices nicely, and the greens paired very well with the pork, cheese, and bread. It was perfection in a sandwich.

I couldn't finish my sandwich so I wrapped the other half and took it back to the hotel for a midnight snack. Even hours later, the sandwich tasted delicious. Highly recommend DiNic's to anyone who visits Philly.
I am a pho addicted and I was looking for a good pho restaurant, great ambience and presentation, but the pho didn't meet my expectations. All ALL.

I'm not going to lie. I was a bit let down. I had very high expectations as a friend of mine had been saying this place had the best sushi he had ever had and would always crave the sushi from here. So I went in with that on my mind, so that could account for the less than stellar review. 

They have all you can eat at a decent price, but you have to sit at the bar. You don't have a choice. Your chef is right in front of you, so you can talk to them all you want. Our chef was a real nice guy, but I had a hard time hearing what he was saying for the most part. 

The quality of the fish is overall, pretty good. The fried roll was probably the worst fried roll I might have ever had. It was huge and almost all of it was fried. Most fried rolls have more fish. Also felt like it was just warmed up versus being freshly fried. 

My gf liked this place a lot more than I, but I dunno. It didn't wow me. It was very similar and there are no pictures of any of the rolls. The special rolls should have pictures as you don't know what you're getting with rolls that are designed for a particular location. 

Not a bad place, by any means, but nothing special either.

We stopped by for a late lunch after going to the wwii museum. Ordered the muffaletta, salami sampler and Hungarian white wine (awesome wine; had two!). You order at the counter and they bring your food to you and then you can order from your table it seems without having to get up to go to the counter again. I agree with the comment on the muffuletta not quite Central Grocery good but still good. Salumi was good and the staff were great. Lots positive vibes at this place. Would definitely go back!

Located in a strip mall, this restaurant has a great variety of pancakes and such. There is not much of a selection for eggs. I had to order a la cart to get a simple two eggs and bacon. While the service was friendly, it was very slow. Ran out of coffee twice. There were just myself and two police officers in the place. 

It was clean but pretty empty for 7:30am. The food I had was nothing to brag about. If I go back i will try something else.
Delicious! Everything made fresh. Chicken coming off the bone, great seasoning. Plantains made fresh. I'll be back soon.

In case you haven't noticed by the title of the list that I have this review in, I generally have a dislike of corporate coffeehouses. So with that said I've been hesitant to check out the ING Direct Cafe for quite sometime now. it definitely combines two things that normally don't go together very well.
Is it a bank? Is it a coffeehouse? It's a place where you can get information on starting a savings account while drinking a latte???
But I finally gave in and have been taken a back over how good and useful it can be. You get free Internet access with the purchase of a coffee and it's a pretty damn good connection speed. And as said below they serve Peets coffee and it really is some of the best. The Wall of televisions also do a pretty good job of keeping you informed on things that you should be checking out further while you browse the web.
So overall it's the best place to go when you need to keep informed about whats going on. So I'm giving in just this once.

So I did online ordering, however when it was delivered, it was the wrong order. I called the store, and the woman who answered was rude, and acted like it was my problem. No apology ever. Won't be ordering from them again.

Lovingly referred to by my other co-workers as "subway sushi" because of its unfortunate location in the suburban station concourse near the broad and market street lines.  

The place ain't much too look at, the dining area has seen better days, and the whole place probably needs scrubbing, but the food is cheap, portions generous, and it all tastes good if not better than the sushi offered at the Comcast center marketplace that costs twice as much.  

Lunchtime bibimbop with salad or soup with a soda will set  you back only $8.  They never skimp on the delicious contents.  Not bad, right?

The 4 pm deal also can't be beat, already prepared items to go are all half-off.

Don't stay to dine, just get it to go.

Oh and on an entirely unrelated note, did you know that there is Jolly Ranchers soda? Yes, it comes in Sour Apple, Blueberry, Watermelon and Grape flavor. Gross - and they sell it here too - in case you're into weird, overly sugar-y soda pop things!
Slow service .. Waited 15 minutes for someone to acknowledge is after stopping two servers. This was a 3:45 on a Sunday.

Atmosphere is cute and the service was good. Unfortunately I payed $10 for what I though was going to be a bowl of soup and it ended up being a small cup. Not only that but the soup was not good at all. I told the waiter and he did offer me anything else just gave me the check and sent me packing. I was also a little disappointed in the wait time. I was told it'd be about 5 minutes but it ended up being 20. 
I don't think I'll be back.
Service was amazing and food was just as good. A little tough to find the location but well worth it.
40 min and not even coffee. Finally got the wrong order when we asked for our money back. Food was pnot good when we got it.

Great place for drinks and tapas! A hidden gem on the mesa, I've passed this restaurant plenty of times and never even glanced at it, so happy I did tonight. We hit the tail end of happy hour, the mojito and sangria were really good. The food was amazing! Definitely recommend the manchego and guava, eggs on toast, and the beef sliders. The pigs on a date were delish too, but I didn't like the honey getting all over my fingers. Will definitely visit again, the atmosphere is very intimate and the service was outstanding.

Went there for the first time and I got a sample of taco half lamb half pork. Very good. Spicy but not to hot. I bought half kilo. It comes with tortillas, salsa, cactus, and other condiments. The tamales is very good too, it has pineapple, so it is sweet. Opens Friday at 9. Saturday and Sunday at 5. Cash only. Definitely will come back and highly recommended.

One of my husband's and my top choices!! We are vegetarians and have never been let down here. Food and service are always amazing. Their red curry with veggies and tofu is amazing!  And their vegetable tofu is drool worthy! Tastes so fresh. Great price for the quality of food. And good portions.

Heard great things about this place so I wanted to try it out while I was in the city. I ordered the Kimchi fried rice, vegetarian fried rice, edamame dumplings and duck scrapple bao. The kimchi fried rice was the most disappointing. It had no taste, did not taste remotely like kimchi and had no kimchi in it - not that I could see. Everything else was okay  and nothing special. Pretty mediocre food.
The best bar in New Hope!  Awesome food, drinks and hospitality!  Charming authentic atmosphere!  This is the place

Every wait staff in this place had a look on their face that screamed "i hate my job."

The food was good, but the service was sub-par. From a far you can hear the waiters complain about tips and how they were not making good money on tips; perhaps their attitude are the reason for this? 

either way, i don't see myself going back.

We stopped in for Mother's Day lunch (around 1ish) and we're seated immediately. The waitress was friendly enough. We ordered two appetizers and they came out quickly (fried pickles and spicy chicken pieces) they appetizers were good as well as their house made ranch. The kids orders chicken (grilled and fried) we order NY strip and filet mignon.  Our salads were served quickly and they were good. The food came out after a about a 30 minute wait (we did order them medium well). Our sides were quite cold as well as the NY strip, my filet looked flat like a sirloin and was barely warm.  We question whether we should  just eat it or send it back .... it took our waitress 10 minutes to check on us (she was taking orders on the other side of the room for some reason).  We were able To grab the attention of another employee who took our plates back.  We waited over 29 minutes with no food and the kids the were getting restless and loud so we decided to ask for the check and go.  The manager Jennifer came over and was extremely nice and tried to get us to say a few minutes longer as the food was almost done ... or box it up for us and add a dessert; we thanked her but declined because we were not going home anytime soon to put the food away. She felt bad because it was Mother's Day and insisted on giving us a generous gift card.  Was asked to pay for our appetizers and the kids food, but she wouldn't  allow us to pay. We tipped our waitress and left feeling fine - no hard feelings and we will definitely give them another shot.

I was surprised for my birthday with a dinner at Volver.  I will admit that my expectations were not high as it was Restaurant Week - a period that we generally avoid like the plague.  However, I was pleasantly surprised and frankly blown away by the food that was served.  

We both had the Rose Gold cocktail which was delicious and $2 of each drink went to the Garces Foundation. The $35 Restaurant Week menu was severely limited, in effect a pared version of the $35 pre-theater menu; but we each found dishes that looked interesting/appealing. 

For the first course we had the Hamachi Tartare and the Milk & Cereal.  The tartare was phenomenal, sublime, fresh and delicious, the togarashi flatbread was genius.  The milk & cereal a fun play on a composed asparagus soup with rice flakes, chicken thigh and thyme marshmallows - delicious.  

The second courses were the Veal Hangar Steak and the Pastrami Trout and again, both were surprising in good ways and delicious in all ways.  I had a great by the glass Riesling with my entrée and my partner had a fantastic by the glass Merlot ($28) that was worth every drop.  

We finished with the third and last course with Panna Cotta of black sesame, yuzu meringue, mandarin sorbet, Thai basil and cherry with a black and white sesame crisp that brought it all to a fantastic close. 
 Josh was our server and he was great as was Phoebe who checked in on us all night long and brought us a yummy sparkling wine sent by my sister-in-law to accompany our dessert.  

Based on our experience, I can absolutely say that it was THE BEST Restaurant Week experience we have ever had and we are definitely planning to check out the regular menu & tasting menu plus wine pairing as soon as Restaurant Week is over.

Burnt ends and coleslaw!!!!!! We had chicken too which was smoky and juicy. Beans pretty good, pass on potato salad as it had only potatoes
 and mayo. Fast delivery thru Uber eats made this weary traveller happy! Best burnt ends i had in years!! Sweet tangy homemade slaw:)

St. Louis has a ton of dining choices..therefore if would be very wise for restaurants to ALWAYS put their best foot forward...Today,  Blondie's forgot that rule.  While the food was tasty, service was HORRIBLE!!  The restaurant was not particularly swamped, so being overwhelmed was not our server's issue.  It took her far too many minutes between her table visits and in fact, appeared to be very pained each and every time we had to ask for something.  Took our order and even recommended some of the spreads for the popovers.  Our food order arrived BEFORE the popovers and the side of sausage arrived AFTER my daughter had finished her pancakes.  Light bulb moment, the popovers should have come FIRST and the sausage WITH her pancakes.  When asked, her snotty replywas, I forgot to put the order in!  How could she forget, she suggested the spreads!  Never refilled water, never got ordered additional drinks and just generally acted very put upon and disinterested. For that matter, the food server also had much attitude.  Word of advice Blondie's, if you have workers that do not willingly want to wait on ALL  of the customers in a professional, friendly manner, FIRE them.  There are plenty of people who want to work.  Now you've received negative comments and aliented customers.  BTW/the manager did adjust the bill and provided treats, but that should not have to happen.  Wait staff should not have to be cleaned up after.  So if you go,  you have been warned, expect crappy service!
New place that has great drinks that are associated with Hotel Tango spirits     Some pizza and small plates available via the fountain square location

This is a great place to grab some sushi. Both guys in there are extremely nice. A review mentioned the lengthy wait and I believe it shows the care that was put into making these rolls. They seem to genuinely care about what they're doing and it shows. I didn't have a long wait but the plating was beautiful in addition to tasting amazing. 
Mike's roll is a new, fresh spin on sushi with diced mango and was delicious. Love this place!
Absolutely delicious pizza. They have a decent beer selection and their meat Sammie's are finger lickin good!

I'd love to have given Cafe Mosaics more than a 3 star review.  It's a decent place that's a little dated in their idea of being modern.  It's okay if they were old school, but they're not.  The menu is filled with vegan friendly and vegetarian options along with a variety of interesting sounding dishes.  The prices are quite good too.  The quality of the food is okay.  Nothing that really blows me out of my socks or makes me think - wow, what a gem of a place!

I remember having the portobello mushroom salad here recently and found the dressing too be too strong in flavor - too much of balsamic vinegar.  The mushroom pieces were tasty but the greens were just too hard to eat.  They also have a simple house coffee that's reasonably strong and works for a morning jolt.  

The ambience is slightly hippie in feel and reflects the older culture of Whyte that seems to be getting lost nowadays.  Lots of posters of music, comedy and theatre adverts on the wall.  The staff is friendly and approachable and the service is pretty fast.  I think it's a lovely little place but they need to work on their menu and make the tastes a wee bit more subtle.

Location: Just north of Irvington and East of I-19. 
The Skinny: Its not bad if you want that type of steakhouse fix and are around that area. It seems as if this place is always packed so those in the area must thing it is the best but I found it to be just okay. 
The Restaurant: The restaurant is clean (albeit the peanut shells on the floor in the front) but over all seems to be nice. The wait staff seemed stress when I was there but we were seated right away. Although, they did forget to bring plates and napkins right at the beginning and we had to actually find someone to get those for us (happen to be the bartender)
What I liked: The food came out in a timely manner and the restaurant was clean. The happy hour special was just $5 house margaritas and $1 off the Draft beers. The bartender was very nice since he helped the servers out and actually helped to split our check for us.  
What I did not like: I did not think they actually do that well on the thing they are supposed to be known for...and that was steak. I asked for Medium in which the delivered but the Sirloin was pretty dry when it came out.  I also asked multiple times for artificial sweetner but they kept forgetting which was an annoyance but not serious enough for a manager-call. 
Should you go: Why not if you are in the area but they are so many other places to eat why not just go to those other places. If you really really really want a steak and have no other choice then go. We went only on having a coupon but I don't really think I'll be going back unless there is a group of us that go. 
My Kids Review: "It was good! They had good Mac'N'Cheese! (it was just Kraft Mac N Cheese)"

This is the quintessential Chinese-American food restaurant. I have to hyphenate because no other country has this type of cuisine, not even China. As far as I know. After living in Japan for three years it was sourly missed. I will leave out atmosphere and décor evaluations because, let's face it, it's fast food. Although, the lady behind the cash register was hilarious. She cared about one thing, getting your order as quickly as possible. She was not rude just overly expedient than normal. It was if she had 10 seconds to complete every individual order. Anyway, on to the food.

We had our food there at the restaurant. The tables were clean-ish. It took about 10-15 minutes for our order to be prepared before we had to go back up to the speed queens throne to retrieve our food. I guess she didn't have time to bring it to our table but like I said, it's fast food. At first glance I noticed that the takeout containers, without the top lid, were stuffed with food. That's a big plus so since I usually start with five stars on my evaluations and mark down from there, I have to mark up from five to six stars (don't worry it'll make since in a minute). 

I ordered the General Tso's chicken combo (fried rice and 1x egg roll/1x crab rangoon (CR). They have it listed on the menu as something spelled slightly different but I knew it would be the same. I've had this many times before and sometimes they use very low quality chicken but not here. The sauce was the perfect blend of sweet and spicy for this dish. I have to deduct a star (5 star) because the chicken was not as crispy as I like but it was good. The pork fried rice was average but a little dry. My wife ordered the seafood combo with large chunks of "crab meat" but the artificial taste made them inedible. I have to deduct another star (4 star) for the "crab meat."   

The best part of the dish was the CR. Although I always opt to get CR instead of an egg roll whenever possible I also ordered an entire order of CR (4 piece) as a side. I was pleasantly surprised with how large these CR were. The wontons were crispy, a little chewy and not overly greasy. Probably the best CR I've had in a long time. This calls for another star to be added (5 star). Oh, if you go, make sure to get "red sauce" with your CR. It's 85 cents extra but it's worth it. 

I will definitely return.

I recently ate at Cochon Butcher (which is the cheaper version of Cochon, a fancy restaurant right around the corner - don't get confused and sit down there, like we did at first). They specialize in sandwiches. I tried the muffaleta sandwich, which had 'house meats' and olive salad. I loved it - you could definitely taste the olives. I also had the seasonal Abita beer, which had just a hint of strawberry - great for a hot afternoon.
This is my go-to take out spot. I highly HIGHLY recommend the Sweet and Sour Fish soup!

Why 5 stars? Because this is one of the better lobster rolls in TB.

   ---   ---   ---

On night one of the Heights Public Market being open to the public, my wife and I frantically marched around in an attempt to decide which vendors we would choose to visit for this momentous occasion. We agreed that Surf and Turf would have to be one of them because lobster rolls are one of our favorite things in the world.

As much as I love lobster any form, we both agree that a lobster roll is best served warm with butter, rather than chilled. Thankfully, Surf and Turf offers you either choice, so we scored the hot, buttery version.

After one bite, the buttery toast really stood out to me. While the lobster is always the star of the show, the quality of the roll is ultra crucial. This roll passed the test with flying colors. And the lobster itself was definitely quite meaty and delicious. 

I've since tried quite a few vendors from Heights Public Market and Surf and Turf is definitely one of my favorites! I'm bummed that they are only a temporary vendor (4 months) but will definitely keep an eye out for their food truck in the future!
Hands down the best BBQ I have ever had.  The smoked corned beef on St Patrick's Day was ridonkulous.
Papa John's is the best pizza place EVER. I am NEVER disappointed when I eat here!

Great place for brunch! Came here on a Sunday morning at around 730am which is the only time there isn't a line. 

You've to order and pay at the counter first and then will be served. Got the princess with 2 over easy eggs on top along with the amazing Bonuts. Must try the Bonuts even you might be dieting or hate sweets, it is just pure deliciousness. The hot fried chicken was great and spicy too and loved every bit of it. Their ice tea is also really good. 

Food service was very quick, all of the staff appear busy for good reasons I guess. Didn't know about the state law of no alcohol before 10 on Sunday. Also not sure why there was a line outside when there were quite a few empty tables inside. Overall, 4.5 stars, id get here early to beat the line and take that post brunch nap later:)

We went to Fuszen on a Friday night shortly after their grand opening. The restaurant was fairly full, but every table was not seated. There was not enough waiters/waitresses to staff all of the tables that were full. It took 15 minutes after we ordered to get drinks. Everyone at our table received their food, except me, and I sat for an additional 10 minutes without food. Also, if you order certain dinners your only choices for a sides are chips and fries. You cannot substitute rice, at an Asian restaurant, even for a fee. The food was mediocre and of course pricey because of the location. Probably will not go back.

So I actually discovered The Tomato Bistro from a Groupon a few months ago.  Holy cow what an awesome deal!  4 course meal for 2 people for $25!

Pros: The Bistro is located upstairs, cute atmosphere, good service.  Perfect portion sizes, we were actually full before the pizza came out (salad and 3 small plates prior to the pizza).  And the waitress was pretty attentive.  Oh, and I did sample duck bruschetta at a Yelp event 2 weeks ago - tasty!

Cons: I guess my only complaint is that when they did have live music the one night, it was a little loud, but fortunately it started towards the end of our meal.

Overall, I would definitely check it out again :)
This is my favorite sushi spot. The quality of service is impeccable. The best sushi in town. Everyone should try sushi sushi at least once. I promise, you will not be disappointed.

...Yawn.

I know this place is or was supposed to be one of "the" places to visit in the Philadelphia dining/nightlife scene, but I can tell you, save your money until the pretense - and the prices - go down. 

The interior was "luxuriously and fashionably" appointed, sure, but I just can't fully enjoy myself in an environment surrounded by loud, pretentious jerks. I suppose I can't fault anyone for wanting to feel "important" when they've paid those prices for the same level of fare attained at a P.F.Chang's, but I'd rather go somewhere less "fabulous" looking and, ah, be able to hear my dining companions.  (The food at P.F.Chang's is actually a bit better, truth be told. Sad state of affairs.) That said, the giant Buddha is great, but not worth the price of admission.

The dessert bento box was the highlight of the meal, so don't miss that if you go. Other than that, if you're trying to take someone there to impress them, I think choosing a place with a truly unique menu and original atmosphere will impress them more. Unless you're one of those aforementioned pretentious jerks. 

I DO know a couple cool people who like it here, so I'm not calling you a jerk if you do - I'm just saying the vast majority of the clientele make me... er, want to go somewhere else. Very. Fast.

Website's cool, though. ;)

I was in Reno for a few days and my boyfriend and I heard about having to come here because they had the best breakfast in Reno. I have to say, I really did enjoy this place. The food and service were both amazing.

First let's start with the service. Our waitress was super kind to us and we told her it was our first time there and she was very helpful with giving us suggestions from the menu. Props to her for being so attentive and nice!

If you know me, then you know whenever I go to a new restaurant, I always look through the entire menu. Like maybe two or three times and thoroughly read what will be in my dish. And moreover, if the waitress/ waiter is kind and I feel like they aren't rushing me, I will usually ask what they recommend or what is popular. Our wonderful waitress recommend I try the salmon eggs benedict and I did! It was absolutely delicious. My boyfriend ordered the huevos ranchero? I think and he said it was also good. Man, the plates were huge! Our table barely fit everything! I did also order a bowl of clam chowder and that was huge too! I definitely wasn't expecting that. Also, I don't order eggs benedict very often but since it was a recommendation, I had to try it. Whenever I go back to Reno, I will definitely come back to this place because the food and the service were just wonderful!
Decent selection of breakfast food that gets 3 stars. Giving an extra star for the fun factor of eating while watching small planes take-off & land. Staff was friendly. Will be back.

Have been there 3 times since they've opened. The first time I went, the chips were stale. The second time, the chips were better. I always get the chicken bowl which is always good. The food is consistent and the service not bad. I got thru the line fairly quickly each time. So happy there's Chipotle in NE Philly!

Prepare for a wait - although not too long if you have a small party! The service was prompt and the food came out fairly quick. A lot of people come here before going out  for drinks since it's right next to all the bars.

Garlic Bread - get the cheese with it if you are going to order it. We had it without and it was nothing special.
Colossus - Good supreme pizza. Came out fresh and packed with meat and veggies. The cheese was still string-y melting and it was delicious.
Greek - Too much feta cheese. I found myself picking off chunks and chunks of feta cheese. Once you removed about half of it, the pizza was good. 

The portions are good, prices reasonable, good service, and good food. It is a great place for dinner and meet-up before going out on Mass Ave.

This review it for Tuesday Oct 12, 2021 in the late evening.

So we placed an order for the following:

1 Chicago Combo Bowl
2 Italian beef sandwiches with sweet peppers
1 Big Italian Beef
1 Cheese Fri with 2 cheese cups

I will say when we got there, they were not as busy as they usually are. So we placed an order with one the gents in drive thru, and the wait was not that long to be honest, compared to other locations. I will add that I believe we may like this place a bit more, mainly because they read our order to us before giving it to us, and the order was 100% correct, unlike other locations 

The only bummer was that when we got home, one the cheese cups opened up and half the cheese leaked out into the bag, but no biggy as these things do happen. I will not judge them on that minor issue for now, unless it is a constant thing.

This is one the main reasons for the 4 of 5 stars. 
Overall everyone who got their meal here at the home liked it, but my father and I noticed our sweet peppers were both salty, but my lady's was not salty. The peppers were not sweet, mainly sadly which was a down side, when you need to slightly watch your sodium intake. 
Other than that the meat had flavor, and everything else was good. 

We will order form this location again in near future. Also, maybe I will try and get pictures next time, as we were in a hurry I was unable to shoot photos of anything.

i ordered 80$ worth of food the burgers were missing everything i asked for .if i had to guess it was microwaved the cheesesteak was dried up the wings say they are breaded and that's not the truth! i've always gotten food from here but the past few times it's gone down hill big time .. I will not be going here anymore i thought maybe they just had a bad day but this was the 3rd chance i gave and the  food was nasty! save your money

Why are these wings so delicious!!!!! A friend told us that word on the street is that they marinate the wings with leftover cooled seafood boil. If that is the truth, other ppl need to try that trick bc it makes for some awesome chicken!

How have I lived in Indy for 15 years and have not eaten at Iaria's?! Better yet, how have I lived 2 blocks away for 6 months and not been here yet?!  My mom was in town from Southern Indiana and my boyfriend and I suggested we try something more off the beaten path.  Mom was excited and we walked the short distance to dinner. We fell in love with the atmosphere of the building and decor inside. What a cool and old history in this neighborhood! We sat at a table in the bar and were quickly greeted by our server, Julie.  She was amazing! She was very knowledgeable on the wine list and made excellent suggestions for dinner. We ordered fried ravioli, but next time will get the mozzarella appetizer. I had the chicken marsala, my boyfriend has the tortellini, and my mom had the spaghetti and meatballs (all recommendations from our server). Wow! Everything was amazing. The creamy tomatoe sauce on the tortellini was delicious and I look forward to trying the spicy vodka sauce next time. The marsala was on point and exactly what we expected.  We had plenty of leftovers and took a canoli for the road. We look forward to many more trips to Iaria's and can't say enough good things about this historical hot spot.
Steak green curry, pad see ew, and panag curry were all on point! You can't go wrong with any of those dishes.
This is my favorite ramen restaurant, period. They put legit effort into the broth, which is key. I don't live in Philly, but visit often. I always make room for Nom Nom Ramen in my schedule.

The bacos... little taco like appetizers with Chinese bun-like texture were outstanding.  The pork belly and lobster and creamy spicy shrimp were standouts.  Really good fresh spring rolls, but not as good as Lilly's.  The pho was also really great, good flavor.  Best I've had so far on the Eastbank, though not quite up there with westbank standouts Pho Hoa, etc... The servers were nice and attentive.  Fun place, clean.  Exact opposite of  Charcoal's (Yeah, yeah apples and oranges)  I'm definitely going back.  No liquor license (I guess), but I did see diners bringing their own wine bottles, so that's an option.  Don't know if there's a corkage fee.

For me, there isn't a whole lot to say about Tony's "Italian" Deli.  It's filthy, the staff wasn't terribly helpful or friendly, and the food wasn't very good.  Actually, my turkey sandwich tasted like someone sprayed some Windex on it or something.  Maybe that's a sign that they actually clean the place, but I'd prefer if the cleaning products weren't on my food.  I couldn't finish my sandwich because it just really tasted off and I didn't want to get sick.  Everyone else seems to love this place though, so maybe we went on an off-day, but that day was so off that we'll never go back.  There are good Italian delis in Tucson (Roma Imports, Fortunato's), so don't waste your time on this grubby place.

Why 3 stars? Because the people were nice, but we didn't love the sushi.

   ---   ---   ---

We moved to Carrollwood about a year and a half ago, and quickly discovered that Carrollwood is a haven for mom and pop sushi joints. The problem is that my favorite restaurant in all of Tampa Bay is Samurai Blue, so when I'm craving sushi, I usually roll* with the best.

*Pun Intended

But on this particular evening, we rolled* the dice and tried out one of the many sushi spots within a couple miles of our house. Toki Sushi was bookmarked on my Yelp for some reason, so that's what we chose.

*Double pun Sunday!!

The Crab Rangoon sushi roll and the Spider roll were solid, but the Green Angel and Mexican Deluxe left a lot to be desired. I did enjoy the sashimi though, which is what I was especially craving when we decided to come here.

After tip, our meal ended up at $80, and I just felt like we dropped a pretty penny for a kind of disappointing experience. Our server was very sweet, but I don't think that's going to be enough to bring us back to Toki next time we're craving sushi.

I don't think that I could ever say enough about Taste. My mom and I found this delicious hotspot two years ago and have been obsessed ever since. Where to even begin? As a fries fanatic you cannot get better than Taste's pomme frittes. Made hot and fresh to order these perfectly seasoned suckers with coarse salt and served with a basil aioli sauce will have your mouth watering the moment they are placed in front of you.

What I love most about the food is how light everything is. I have tried numerous dishes but my favorite is still the prosciutto and caprese sandwich. Everything is fresh. Fresh mozzarella, fresh greens, fresh tomatoes and best of all a freshly made vinaigrette that adds a nice kick to the sandwich. This is the perfect light, but filling, meal that will leave you satisfied and happy that you just filled your tummy with so many good ingredients. 

On top of that, my mom and I love to treat ourselves to one of their many freshly baked desserts. I have tried everything from their tangy lemon squares to their mouth watering peach cobbler. No matter the dish it tastes as if my grandma was in the kitchen whipping everything up. You cannot get more homemade tasting than that!

On top of everything the atmosphere is chic and trendy. You order at the counter making it a great meeting spot. The sleek wood tables that seat multiple parties make this restaurant very casual and open. There are also cozy booths if you want to hide away, and a great outdoor space in the front. Although Taste is always crowded I have miraculously never not found a table.

I've been to locale numerous times at this point. I love their cocktails, the ambience, and their food. Their pizza is huge for a slice and has crispy edges. Their patio is dog friendly. Their calamari is cooked well and the spicy marinara with it has the perfect kick. There is often a wait but every time I've had to wait they serve drinks and the time goes by fast.

This is my oldest favorite place to eat in Philadelphia and my go-to for a special dinner when guests come into town to visit me! We are never disappointed - the food and wine are outstanding (over 120 rotating wines on tap...need I say more?) and the ambiance in the bar room or downstairs is just too cool - old school Italian. 

My personal favorites are the fried calamari, which they nearly always have on special, the antipasto misto, funghi, and insalata di Caesar for starters. Plus the addicting little bread nuggets on your table as a starter! 

For my main course, I almost always opt for the gnocchi con provola affumicata - they are just so perfectly executed that I can't seem to get past them to try many more things, but I'm always tasting what everyone else gets too. The Trenette di Spinaci is spinach pasta with sausage and grated parm, also a good choice. I've tried the pesto over gnocchi as well and it's to die for. Their specials are also great and we've ordered lobster ravioli and many other dishes from there, I have not once been disappointed with any aspect of my meal.

Now...onto the wines, the part of the meal that hits it out of the park! They have over 100 wines on tap, which are circulating seasonally so there is always a crazy huge selection! Personally, I like to go big or go home, so I choose from one of their wine flights (5 glasses, with a dozen options!). The wait staff is so incredibly knowledgable they will make sure you find one you love, and you can try it for free!

This place is perfection in my mind, and in over a dozen visits I have not had anything but a stellar, incredibly classy dinner here. Mmmmm

I would give 0 star if i could. SERVICE WAS HORRIBLE. I worked in the restaurant before and i think this is by far the worst experience i have ever had. The manager was rude. The food didn't come out till 45mins later and it was during the afternoon. The food was just ok but with the wait and the bad services? I would not recommend this place to anyone.

Today we got donuts for my birthday!  
Guru donuts is a really cute shop. Upon walking in, the staff was friendly and attentive. We weren't sure what we wanted so we just asked them to put together a box for us. What they brought us was some absolutely fantastic donuts!
It's a pretty "hip" spot and definitely clean. They are taking good COVID measures! 
The donuts are delicious but the coffee has a little bit of a soy sauce taste. It is just over roasted - which is probably due to the quality and time of the actual roast from where they source their coffee and not so much the brewing process. 
All in all, pretty good! The coffee could definitely use a boost.

We always try to hit up this place whenever we're house sitting for my boss. It's a nice, homey place, with great service and yummy food.

We usually start off with the fire feta, which is great. I love feta and, with a little heat in there, it goes very well with pita bread.

I usually get the soutzoukaki, which is one of the best I've had. The lunch portion is a good size too.

I really wanted to like this new restaurant, because we loved the quaint bar! But left with an experience we probably won't come back. Food was ok. Fries extra crispy, burgers ok. Big issue is the sound quality of the place. Too loud. Then throw in live music- I'm sure the performer was good, but all you heard was nails on a chalkboard. We will be back for drinks/apps before the live performer. 
Hopefully they can figure this out.

Inside the J.A. Nugget, a 24hr place to eat.  Kinda reminds me of a Marie Callendars.  Had a late dinner after drinking and partying, we both ordered the prime rib- it was good, veges were -eh, salad- decent, service - friendly and little slow, prices- decent.  Still 4 stars from me! (it was late, I don't expect much)    :)

Five stars you say?!?  Almost all the other reviews are 1, 2 and 0 if they had the option stars...  What happened different for me you wonder...  

I walked in at 830pm on a Saturday night.  The man at the counter greeted me with a big smile and hello, offered a deal. I took him up on the deal, chose my crust and toppings then paid.  I was told it would be ready in ten minutes and so I went for a walk.  I came back eight minutes later and my pizza was handed to me when I walked in.  Done.

It fresh, hot and as tasty as one could expect for dominos.  Figure it out people, if you want this and you're really as close as you say you are in your reviews, just freaking get up and walk there.

Nice use of this space in Nora. Found the acoustics a little loud so was difficult to converse over dinner. The menu was nice but similar fare to many other new brewpubs around town. Kings Jive and Quintana were excellent! Cheese curds were ok. Shrimp Goddess was delicious!

Been a few years coming here intermittently. Simply, they achieve my umami here. I appreciate this along with the local loyalty they promise with their sourcing. Oh, and the beers on tap. They hit all my checks... consistently. Service is thoughtful and inclusive. Come with an appetite and leave with a smile. Lovely place in Cherry Hill. Happy energy.

Edit: oh baby, those cherries... mmm mmm mmm

Closer to 3.5 stars.

Just had this for lunch.

The place was nice looking and clean.

The staff was really friendly.

I paid 15.99 for a fire quacker duck burger and some sweet fries.

The burger itself was a little smaller than I had anticipated.  It wasn't as flavorful as I thought it was going to be either.  It wasn't even remotely spicy.  The duck was cooked very well though and tasted good.  I've had better sweet fries.  

I think I will try this place again though, I really want to try the duck bacon or brisket on a burger.

I went to Yakitori Boy this past Saturday night to sing karaoke for a friend's birthday. We had about 15 people gathered in the main area of the bar, which was apparently way too many to be comfortable. The bar itself is unbelievably crowded starting at about 11 PM, and the cocktail service is borderline impossible. Not only did the server confuse us by saying we could not pay for drinks in cash from the table (she took all of our cards instead), but we ALSO could not walk up to the bar and order any drinks to have added to the tabs we assumed they had in their computer. This was both inconvenient, confusing, and frustrating. Furthermore, ONE girl was responsible for drink and food service too all groups at tables that night, including selling karaoke tickets. It was difficult to flag her down and even more difficult to keep track of who would be getting what delivered to the table and when. If you want to have fun at this bar I suggest going early in the evening so you can hear the person next to you and so that you don't feel like you're spending $10 on each drink only to find that you can't enjoy it in the loud crowd of people standing like sardines.

Excellent dinner at kona grill.  We were there during happy hour.    Would go back and have just appetizers and dessert.  Great value.  I had macadamia nut chicken which was very good but way too much food. Husband had Caribbean chicken which was also good... Spicy... Just like server said.  We split piece of banana cream pie.  It was delicious.  Nice atmosphere.  Good service.  No parking close to entrance.  Use valet if walking is an issue.  Would recommend.

Everything I've had at The Shaved Duck has been good.  I can't give it 5 stars because I've not had anything that was really great, but this place has a solid menu and a decent beer selection and a laid back atmosphere.  I'm a fan.

First course: salt. 
Second course: salt.
Third course: SALT!!!

After 4 trips to the Memphis Taproom, I must wonder whether the normal diners are the hip kids the Taproom seems to be catering to or, in fact, thoroughbred horses whose salt licks just ran out. 

And it's a shame too, because there is a lot to like about The Memphis Taproom. Stepping inside is a breath of fresh air in a neighborhood essentially devoid of comfortable dining. It really does feel like a restaurant trapped inside a bar, with the back room made up of tables, low lighting, and highbrow art done in a tasteful manner. Sometimes, you can even forget that you stepped inside a bar. 

That being said, don't think you cant get a great pint at the Taproom. I was wonderfully delighted to find a hand-pump done well, which so many other bars screw up and simply serve sub-standard pours to diners with a curt explanation of "this is how hand-pump beer is done."  The Victory hand-pump was simply delicious. 

And then there's the food. 

My first two visits were for brunch. What a fantastic menu. There are light items, heavy items; there are savory items, there are sweet items; there are breakfast items, and there are lunch items. 

I chose the Cream Chipped Beef. One of my favorite dishes, it is making a comeback on brunch menus in the last few years. It's a comfort food for me, harking back to the days that my mother would stir it all together on the stove on cold December Pine Barren mornings.

Sadly, this dish resembled nothing of that. A tiny portion with a salt shaker dumped into it. There is no other description. 

We went back, give it another try. Different dishes, same salty result, this time This time, it was the now-discontinued Port Richmond breakfast. 
 
Recently, some friends suggested it as a pre-Johnny Brendas meetup spot. Heck, the environment's great, the brews are tasty, and the menu is imaginative. Why not?

The suicide rings were true to their name. Death by salt. 

The burger was less salty, but still a bit much. This dish, however, lacked any sort of imagination. 

In the end, I do think I will keep giving the Memphis Taproom chances. Why, I do not know. By any sort of measure, it should be off my menu. But I have to think at some point The Taproom's friends and family will corner it in a room, sit it down with a therapist who specializes in these things, and shoot it straight from the hip:

Memphis Taproom, you have a salt problem.
SUSHI SUSHI SUSHI! Definitely love their crazy roll and mom's da bomb! Sushi is not too big and rice is not too thick. It is just perfect! Also try their bibimbap!

Simply the BEST Tacos!

This location is a taco stand with a picnic table loaded patio off Bearss and Skipper and next to the Army/Navy store.  Despite sitting just off the road, you do feel like you are removed - probably spirited away by the awesome food!!

Go to the window and place your order and definitely get a drink (its hot!)  Then find a  picnic table and sip your Mexican cola while waiting.  It does take a bit because they put your order together fresh, but it is worth the wait.  You pick up your order from the window and then dive in.  Fresh ingredients bursting with flavor will greet your mouth.  Yum!

On the pricey side, the tacos are overstuffed and large so you will fill up on less.  You may want to order a couple and then see if you can move to order more.  ;-)
