Went here on a day the Colts weren't playing but my Redskins were!  My boyfriend and I were allowed the pick of any seat we wanted to accommodate our game watching preferences.  We sat down and checked out the menu and were overwhelmed with the awesome options.  We started with the Buffalo Shrimp Wontons were turned out to be an excellent choice.  We then ordered and split the Bangkok burger (a great one if you love Asian flare) and the Deep-Fried burger (a total and complete experience type of meal).  We upgraded our sides to sweet potato fries which turned out to have a cinnamon/nutmeg kick to them and the ultimate mac and cheese which was to die for.  The meal was superb.  By that time we finished my team had just broken into the fourth quarter so we let our stomachs settle a bit and then ordered dessert with five minutes to go in the game.  We got the chocolate peanut butter mousse concoction and not only was it HUGE it tasted awesome.  I highly recommend this place especially if your team is playing.  We wer given great service but keep in mind it wasn't a packed house because the Colts game wasn't on.  I'm not sure how they are going to do with a full seated section but who knows.  They seem game for it!  =D

Hmmm. We tried Smashburger last night. Disappointing.

The setup is really awkward. It's open, but closed off at the same time. I was surprised by how small it felt inside. The other oddity was that the staff's cleaning supplies/garbage area is completely exposed to diners and it's directly below where the food comes out. Not the best layout.

I had a hard time picking out my order ... all the choices were a little "off" for me. I ended up going with the avocado club, regular size. My husband got the bacon burger, large size.

When the food came out, my burger was presented open faced - presumably to show off the avocado - but the avocado left a little to be desired. My husband's order looked to be the same size, if not smaller than mine, although his was supposed to be the large. Both our burgers and fries were fine, but not special. 

Will not be back.

Was very pleasantly surprised at this place! Tried the pulled pork nachos and grilled tenderloin and both were very good. The only downside is I did think the beers were a little expensive.  Service was very friendly - we will be back for sure!

Nice that they're expanding outside of their original location and into B&M, but it's not quite the same as 53rd and 6th. The prices are also significantly higher than the original. That said, though, the taste and quality is good, and it's nice that they let you have as much sauce as you want!

I live downtown so I go here quite a bit. I'm now writing a review because everytime I go here in the evening the employees really lack customer service skills. I'm all about customer service and because I've come here 4 times in the past week and a half & got terrible service ever single time I give y'all "" Last week when I went I got a pizza and the employee making my pizza had "0" customer service skills. It was like talking to a brick wall. Not sure what was going on with her but she didn't seem to be all there. (Girl with purple hair) She was so out of it she actually made the couple ordering behind us literally walked out upset because she was "making things complicated" Our pizza got done faster than usual. Now I know why... because she didn't cook it long enough. The pizza crust is thin but the dough on my pizza was still raw. I took my pizza up to the counter and asked an employee if she could put the pizza back in the oven because it wasn't full cooked . She literally just stared at me never gave me a response so I sat down and then she came up to me and said we will remake it and took the raw pizza. Once the new pizza was done the girl came to the table and just sat the pizza down, zero eye contact, no words out of her mouth she set the pizza down with an attitude and walked away. Could have at least said sorry about the raw pizza. It wasn't onetime I received bad service it's been multiple times. Don't get me wrong the pizza is great when it's cooked by someone who knows how to make it but I'm over the crappy customer service I get every time I come here. The location is cool, the ingredients are fresh but service is AWFUL. And then having to sit there and listen to their personal gossip conversation that are in no way work related is quite annoying. I went today and ordered a salad and the girl was putting stuff on the spicy southwest salad that doesn't even go on it I had to tell her to add stuff it comes with because she didn't know how to make it and then to have an attitude?? Your employees should know the menu if they are gonna be making food. I didn't know it could be so complicated to make a salad that has the ingredients listed right in front of them. I used to go to the fired pie on Speedway but I go to this one now since it closer. If you can I definitely recommend the speedway location because the service they gave me there every single time was EXCELLENT. Won't be returning to this location anymore.

Based on many people's ratings, I have a feeling I am a minority here.  I think it is partially because I love breakfast food and partially because I had such high expectation before walking in here that it had to be better than perfect to be wowed. Some of the "downside" of being able to conduct so much research work on restaurants...

I arrived a bit before 7am (I don't know of any breakfast places in my home neighborhood that doesn't open until 7am, so this was probably the first ??? moment) and the door remained locked until one another patron, who also arrived 1 minute before 7, knocked on door at 1 min past 7.

Service was very good.  They kept coming back for coffee and water refill and food arrived very fast.  I had challas french toast.  It was nice tender french toast (using challas bread, nothing less is expected) but unfortunately I had a real wow factor french toast several times.  So compared to those, nothing was wrong with this french toast but it just didn't wow me.

Maybe I should try this place again with a different mind set.

If you're hungry for a solid breakfast, then come here.  I've been here a few times now, and my meal every time has been great.  Hot cakes are good, omelettes are well made, and the coffee is just ok.  My biggest complaint about this place is the wait both to get a table and receive your food.  Wait time for a table was about a hour.  Now we're starving.  We waited an extraordinary amount of time to receive our food.  Not sure if the kitchen is out of sync or they are just slow.  Kind of a bummer.

Was it worth the wait?  Yes and no.  Food is amazing, but the wait kills it a little for me.
New name same tired restaurant and the critic who gave this restaurant four stars is clearly in cahoots with the owner. Too many other places to go then this one unless you adored the Marlin Darlin.

After waiting two hours for a delivery, we gave up. We tried to call and no one answered after a half hour. We went by the store and there was a line going out of the parking lot. Obviously a lot of people were having issues. Avoid 75th and Shadeland Donatos. Three hours later they finally knocked on our door. Over two hours late for the scheduled delivery. Hope they enjoy the pizza we declined to accept.
While the margaritas are good the food not so much. Everything tastes the same,  very bland.

These burgers are bang'g...  I love them.  These little burgers blow away White Castle and Crystal Burgers of the South...  this is like a Mom and Pop's of the Burger biz- so you know these burgers ROCK... My wife totally loves the sweet potato fries and the potato hamburger rolls...  Plus they actually deliever up until 2 or 3 am....
Great place for an afternoon snack and fabulous view for people watching on State St. , Santa Barbara on a Wednesday afternoon.

Yummy! Great daily specials and great service. I love this place because it's warm and cozy and there is never a wait. This is my go-to Mexican spot and I'm sad they closed the one closer to me on Keystone. Mushroom fajitas are one of my regular orders, but I also love the plain beef tacos and chicken chimichangas. Great queso, big drinks, and reasonable prices.

Bonuts = amazing. I got the East Nasty - something to write home about. Similar to Tupelo Honey Cafe. 
http://www.bonappetit.com/restaurants-travel/best-new-restaurants/article/best-sandwich

Best spot for gyros n shawarma on the wb. The Philly cheese is good too. 
Look at that gyro burger. Food coma afterwards but worth it after a long days work on the wank.

Dope. Dope.  Dope.  Dope.  Dope. 

In an old Ms. Winner's joint and converted to kinda tiki lounge. 

Prices are good and atmosphere is great.

Not large selection of offering so be prepared to like beer, bourbon or mezcal.
Beautiful ambiance and food presentation. Friendly staff, quick service, delicious and flexible menu--especially if you're a vegetarian. I'm looking forward to coming back.
Love them!!! We go there any time we are in Nashville as we live in Atlanta! Great food!

If you find yourself in St Louis (like we did this past week) I highly recommend Remy's. We like to share, so got a bunch if little plates.  The falafel was the best I've ever had!  Polenta fries amazing.  The cheese plate was good. The homemade hummus was ok - better with other stuff. But OMG the Gorgonzola potatoes.  A must try.

Always love this place. Have only eaten inside the cute awesome place once or twice but it is one of our go to delivery places. I have never had a bad meal here and love the steamed sea bass, curries, crab rangoon, hot & sour soup, fresh thai rolls, eggplant, you name it. Everything always arrives on time and at the right temperature. They also have fun lunch specials to check out and outdoor seating if you go in person. I think it is the oldest thai restaurant in the city. One note of caution there is only one of them so other folks with the name are not the same! I found this out the hard way when I ordered from a wrong one and well I was not happy about it.

Came here on a afternoon with the family. Great place!  

The restaurant is below street level, and there is additional seating upstairs and outside. Walking down into the restaurant you get a  classic town pub feel from the place. They even have quiz nights!  There's a dart board and a small place set up for acoustic guitar. Would be a great place for music. 

Their Black and Tan was excellent. They offered everything I would expect for pub grub; shepherds pie, burgers, sliders, beef tips, fish and chips, and they even have Ahi tuna and Cod selections. 

I had the shepherds pie and stuffed mushrooms. They cheese layer on top of the pie was different, but I think it locked the heat in the pie and it was very good. 

If you're in the area this place is worth a visit. If you do the Lotz house tour, you can get 10% off if you bring a flyer.

Best fish and chips in town! Great place for seafood- everything tastes really fresh. Good wine and cocktail menu and prices are very reasonable. Dinner ranges from $15 - $25. Fun, lively environment- can be loud, but their big booths are really comfortable. Outside patio is the best! Only complaint is that every time we have been here, the service is really SLOW- from ordering drinks, to ordering food, bringing the food and taking forever to bring the bill- hoping they can improve this, but if you're in a hurry to get in and out, this is not the place!

I hate leaving a bad rating for any place.  I know how hard it is to make a living these days in a small business.  Having said that, I can't help but give this place one star.  We have been here twice this year and both times the young bozo behind the counter messed up our order big time.  Both times we had the misfortune to have this same boy make our food.  Knowing he messed it up last week, we should have checked it before we left this time.  Our mistake.  Well, never again.  There's a much better DQ in Dublin.  There employees are literate.
Living in Santa Barbara there are many restaurants to choose from. I came through Groupon and what an amazing spot to have found. I will return, the food is delicious!

This place makes a good bagel but they have "lost" our order multiple times and the wait this morning was a full hour long. No apologies, no remorse, no awareness of customers waiting. Clearly not a good system. Also, they need to make more everything bagels because they're constantly sold out. We won't be returning because it is just not a reliable establishment when you have somewhere to be.

Compared to the Grand Sierra I recommend to skip this hotel. Standard rooms are close to $100 whereas you can get the same type of room for around $20 at the GS. WiFi in the business center is a ridiculous $247 per day - a major reason to skip this place.

Warning: don't come here if you don't have self-control. I was in pain because I could not stop eating.

The food here is incredible. Come hungry but pace yourself. You'll start off with pita, hummus, and salatim, followed by the grilled protein dishes. Everything was flavored to perfection. The pita was a soft, pillowy bite of heaven, and it went well with everything. The pita and salatim are bottomless, but we did not need refills and had plenty left for two more meals. They give you these perfectly sized takeaway boxes that's enough for everything you didn't eat. Quite thoughtful and yay for reducing food waste!

Also, I love that there's a 20% gratuity added to the check to ensure $15/hour for the employees. There are other places that do this in Philly but are quite sketchy about it, so props to Laser Wolf!

Adele's food transports you to another time and place. The fried trout, sweet onion chips and dip, jw potatoes, and chicken have been our staple orders. However, there is so much to try. Never disappointed, always full.

Finally something has claimed the old Johnny Rockets spot in the food court.    Also, finally some authentic Mexican food so  I am no longer forced to go to Taco Bell on the other side (blegh).

They must be pretty new as the only thing they had available to order were the tracks (and they didn't even have all of those available).  There aren't even prices listed on their menu yet (3 tacos were about $9).

I didn't know this at the time, but you can mix and match the tacos (not that it would have mastered because the selection is so limited right now).

I hope they get it together soon so I can come back to try some different items.    The tacos I did have (steak) were very good.
We walked here from Frenchman Street to find it closed at 1230 on a Wednesday.  Call ahead to make sure Kayla' s is open before making the trip.  Sorry we missed it.

I don't remember if it was my first bagel, but I do recall the one that hooked me for life as a young kid. San Francisco, mid-70s. Dark-as-midnight pumpernickel bagel with cream cheese from a kosher bakery, eaten at the beach while listening to barking marine mammals on the rocks near Cliff House. Devotees argue endlessly on what makes a "true" bagel, but most agree an unsugared bread doughnut from your average supermarket ain't it.

The discussion on what should or shouldn't go into a bagel is similarly contentious, but as long as the dough has been properly proofed then briefly boiled before baking, I'm happy. You can detect this detail by looking at the cross-section; the boil creates a visible "skin" that is tougher and chewier than the dense, bready interior. The presence of this telltale sign indicates The Daily Bagel is doing something right, and the good news doesn't end there.

As with many bagel shops there are various flavors of cream cheese mixed in-house, and a variety of both savory and sweet bagels. I'm afraid I can't report on cheese blends and fruity items because my trio of diners had a mind toward sharing a few sandwiches. Though the place has been open for a decade, it was recently purchased by a young lady who said--while taking my order--she preferred cooking shows to cartoons as a child. My kinda gal.

On the owner's recommendation I ordered the Number 1 breakfast sandwich on a tomato basil cheddar bagel with fried egg, ham, and American cheese ($4.95), as well as a Number 4 breakfast sandwich on a bacon cheddar bagel with fried egg, tomato, avocado, and Swiss cheese ($5.25). The first thing I noticed was a decent ratio of filling-to-bread. Great balance of flavors, plenty of food and a good deal for the price. The bacon bagel had big chunks of meat baked right in, yet the overall effect was subtle. Can bacon be subtle?

As evidenced by the name on the door there is a newspaper theme at work here. From the hot lunch menu I ordered a Headline melt on an onion parmesan bagel with roast beef, turkey, tomato and Swiss cheese ($6.95). This may have been the favorite amongst us, probably due to the contrast of black pepper seasoning with the sweet onion. The Black and White melt on a sesame bagel with turkey, Swiss cheese, tomato and sliced avocado was also enhanced with black pepper, a touch I really liked ($6.95). Completing our sandwich order was the Dear Abby on an onion parmesan bagel with lettuce, tomato, onion, sprouts, cucumber, avocado, and cream cheese ($6.50). Sadly, this was our least favorite item. We all like our veggies, but this sandwich was pretty bland and underwhelming. It probably would have been better if I'd ordered it with hummus instead of cream cheese.

The menu includes breakfast burritos, scrambles, and plenty of other stuff I didn't have room for on a single visit. However, I had to try a cup of the day's soup, made with spicy pork sausage, potato, tomato, onion, garlic, spinach, chicken broth, a little cream and seasonings ($3.95). For my taste it's rare to find a good sausage-based soup, but this one met the challenge. I had a taste with the sandwiches and then enjoyed the rest reheated with dinner. Though the sliced-rather-than-diced spuds seemed a tad odd for soup, I'm not complaining. Hearty housemade soup wins me over every time.

The room is cute in both decor and size (seating for perhaps 16), and there's a large menu of smoothies and coffee drinks available. Even with a largish order I didn't have to wait more than 15-20 minutes. If you're like me and limiting carbs due to diet, this is an excellent option for your "cheat day".

Will not be returning really bad experience. Me and my wife both got sick. The waiter was very not service oriented. My wife had to ask for water with lemon at least three times. We had to ask for a straw at least four times, I ended up borrowing my wife's straw. The Swordfish was really "fishy" and not appetizing. It was a slow night and the service was very poor. Extremely disappointed. Me and my wife both agreed that Oceanaire Seafood room downtown was 150% better which is where we will be returning when we want seafood again.

Here we are again.  Wifey wanted to go here Sunday night because she really likes the peanut sauce that comes with the spring rolls.  I admit that the peanut sauce is really good so I was happy to oblige.  

Ever since we got back from a trip a couple months ago to Marfa, way out in far West Texas we've been ordering club sodas for our drinks.  There, we were introduced to a club soda called Topo Chico.  Turns out it's a Mexican brand that comes in glass bottles and is served from a metal bucket filled with ice and water to chill it very very cold.  When opened you stuff a lime wedge in the bottle neck.  Let me tell you it's very good.  AND, it turns out it is available right here in little old Tucson at the local Wal-Mart for only $7.42 for a case of 12 bottles.  It's a bargain!  I want to see all the local bars and eateries start carrying it.  So when Miss Saigon doesn't even offer any club soda, as in "ew" club soda, I knew this was going "down the hill."

I ordered the fried egg rolls for the appetizer because I don't really care for the cold spring rolls that Wifey got.  I was pleasantly surprised by the somewhat unique flavor of my dipping sauce that seemed to have a mild citrus flavor.  I also liked the crisp iceberg lettuce, sliced cucumber and cilantro as well.  This made for a great wrap and more then made up for the tiny and otherwise average tasting egg rolls served in the giant boat shaped dish.

For the main course I ordered a large bowl of pho with spicy broth and Wifey asked for a regular bowl.  And here's where things went from bad to worse.  Normally, I give Asian places a pass on this, but this Miss Saigon wants to pretend to be an upscale Tucson restaurant with lots of young cute Vietnamese servers running around in a nicely appointed well-kept place in a trendy Broadway and Craycroft neighborhood.  I believe that in this place I expect that they understand that appetizers come out and the meal is paced to serve the main course AFTER the appetizers are finished or the customer is clearly ready for the main course.  So, when you are halfway through the appetizer and the server waltzes out with two steaming bowls of pho I don't like it.  Normally, like I said, Asian places don't understand that and food just comes out of the kitchen when it comes out.  When you order a mix of appetizers and main course food it's not a surprise that food just comes out in no particular order. But I expect this place to know what they're doing.

My spicy broth was only just mildly spicy.  Worse, although it was somewhat spicy, it was watery and otherwise tasteless.  I'm looking for a flavorful and rich broth that just makes you swoon it's so good.  But not here.

Another red flag was that the server didn't bring us any vegetable plate.  In fact, after we put in the order we never saw the server again until it was time to bring the bill.  We always had to flag down someone else to help with refills, etc.  When you get pho, (in Tucson) you get a plate of jalapeño peppers, bean sprouts, cilantro, a lime wedge and basil.  So we got the pho but no veges.  And there we sat....  We flagged down another server and asked for some veges.  Some several minutes later he came back with this tiny little plate that might be considered almost enough for one bowl of pho.  A real pho place will give you more than twice what we got since we got two bowls.  But I looked around and this seemed like their normal serving so it's a bit disappointing.  

It's sad that Tucsonans flock to this place in the belief that they think it's good.  It's not.  There are better places in town to really enjoy pho without having to drive to the coast or Texas or practically anywhere else.  I won't spoil this review with where to go but if you message me through Yelp I'll tell you where you can get some really good pho right here in Tucson.  Meanwhile, I can't see any reason to go back, unless Wifey wants some more peanut sauce.
Tacos were tasty. Mexican bread is awesome. Drinks were pricey, but good.

We waited at least 10 minutes for the waiter to acknowledge us (after I bussed the table myself and the place was relatively empty) then 40 min after ordering when we asked the waiter about our order. She asked if we wanted to pay with cash when we hadn't even received our food.  20 min later we get watery soup and bland crepes. Disappointing to say the least.

I love Tria and it doesn't hurt that this location is right up the street from my house. It a great go to when the weather is nice and you want to sit outside and have some refreshing wine and/or beers with apps. Its a nice happy hour choice in the warmer months as well when its still light out at night and you just want snacks rather than a whole meal. Their cheeses are great as are their salads and brushettas from my experience. I will be back!

We have been here several times and have never been disappointed! The restaurant is often crowded and very loud - so if you need more quiet, wear something warmer and sit outside under their heat lamps! I LOVE the clam fettuccini and their clam chowder is delicious! The head cook is quite a chef and watching him prepare the food is very entertaining. He does bang the pots LOUDLY - so be aware of your ears are sensitive. The restaurant has a nice ambiance to it and is cheaper than many in town. The wharf is fun and we love going for lunch as well - they will allow your dog at the outside table and even brought ours a fresh bowl of water - and I didn't even ask them! We will be back!

No complaints. Food isn't fancy, but it's good and prepped in front of you. The service is good with several people taking orders and picking up empty plates. The drinks are self serve but this isn't a full service restaurant.

After church, i came by here to try their sushi out. Their sushi wasn't the best, i admit. I've tasted better. But compared to other buffets, they have pretty decent sushi. I did enjoy the hibachi (WARNING: the lines get long in the weekends)

Fresh ingredients is what makes this place sit above the rest.  From there the owner really cares about his clients.  Too bad it's in a strip mall.

Place changed owners in the last year. The Prices since have gone up 15-20%.  More importantly, the vegetables and the sushi  are not as fresh.

So, we've been here 3 times in total...
1st time *
Service- excellent ... the bartender which was also our server was really nice & attentive 
Food- delicious! We had a large pepperoni pizza (h/h special) & a pitcher of beer, we loved the pizza so much we couldn't wait to come back next time we were in Reno 

2nd time *
Service- Ok. Server not so friendly, but whatever .
Food- pepperoni pizza (h/h special) & order of wings... the wings were COLD ... the restaurant wasn't even busy ... I guess they had just been sitting there, until our server decided to bring them over 

3rd time *
Service- was okay 
Food - ordered the happy hour special like we always do, large pepperoni , but asked to add tomatoes to half of it ..
When we got the bill, saw we were charged around 22 for the pizza , I asked her why if the one topping large was $15 for h/h .. she said yeah but you got 2 toppings ...
Ok... I assumed you would just charge me for the extra topping ... "oh, no it doesn't work like that"
So we basically paid an extra $6 for tomatoes on HALF of the pizza ...

Overall, I had really liked this place on our first couple of visits, but will probably go somewhere else next time I'm in Reno.

excellent noodle !!! the BEST Ramen in Edmonton !!!
it would be better to change the friendliness of the staffs !!! but I would like to hear more Japanese songs playing ..  so feel more authentic ! lol

First Champagne Sunday Brunch at this establishment with my 12yr old daughter. We both thought the bacon was the best we've ever had. The biscuits were amazing as well. Loved all the food on the buffet, which was actually set up outside the restaurant, in the hallway. Kind of strange, but it worked. Our waitress took our order for 3 entrées not on the buffet, but included in the price. After several trips to sample food, our entrees never arrived. My coffee was never refreshed. Had to ask for her to check on our food and to bring coffee. When the entrees did arrive, they, or she forgot one Benedict. The ones she did bring seemed awfully small; the crepe was smaller than my hand and the Benedict was only one small egg/muffin. We were also charged for two adults, which I asked about, and was corrected. Delighted by the food, disappointed by the service.

Finally got the opportunity to come to this restaurant. Made sure to make a reservation (hard to get) for lunch with my girlfriend for her birthday. Just pulling into this place you're in awe, checking everything out. Once inside, even more oohing and ahhing, every room as pretty as the next. 
We chose to sit out on the patio. So glad we did. As luck would have it, we were the only ones there, and got (I think) the best table out there. We were situated right by the beautiful pond, with several ducks and koi as company. 
Our waiter (which is why it's only a four, would definitely have given it 5 stars), although friendly, seemed a little not sure of himself and robotic at times, telling us the daily specials, etc. We chose the lunch special which was a steak sandwich covered with gruyere cheese on a brioche bun, with an onion soup dipping juice (supposedly) and special fries (which we ended up feeding to the ducks and koi. Not that they were bad, but the wildlife were making us feel really guilty lol). 
Our lunch started with fresh warm bread and scallion butter. Delicious and very hard to resist so I gave away the rest of the bread to avoid more temptation. Our waiter highly recommended a specialty drink which I ended up ordering. Although it was refreshing like he said, it's not something I would order again for myself. Our lunch arrived shortly later and was delicious. 
As we were sitting there, the patio really started filling up. I overheard our waiter giving the same scenario to various other patrons, not once coming back to our table to see if we needed anything else. 
For dessert we ordered an amazing gluten free chocolate cake which came with grilled(?) peaches and lavender buttercream dots, along with a cup of tea for myself. Our waiter came over with a messed up tea box (luckily I knew which one I wanted), but never inquired about what (if anything) I would like with my tea. He even brought our check in the middle of our dessert.
I would absolutely love to come back here, between the beautiful scenery, or the food, I personally love this place, and I just found out that they have a Happy Hour! Awesome! 
Would love to come here for a special occasion! Worth the road trip!
P.S. - Be sure to check out Grounds For Sculpture which is located on the grounds!! That's my next review.

I personally did not like the food at all. We ordered General Tso's and sweet and sour chicken and both were probably some of the worst Chinese we've had in awhile. The General Tso's was very chewy (perhaps overcooked?) and the crab rangoon was also not the best. The sweet and sour sauce was very bland as well. 

I want to like it due to the location and great reviews, so I might be willing to try something else one more time but for now I recommend taking your money elsewhere.

Hands down the best wing place in STL. The flavors  here are unlike any other place. Ridiculous ranch, coconut curry, and sesame ginger teriyaki are my personal favorites but I don't think you could go wrong with any of their flavors. They did skimp me on sauce one time so I always order extra sauce now (no extra charge) but I like em saucy so it's mostly preference. Forget b-dubs or wing stop, Wing Co is where it's at!

Brunch this morning. Good food huevos rancheros and build your biscuit. The decor is awsome and concert venue looks great. It has a warm fire place right in the middle of the room. Will return for dinner and drinks.

From the time my wife and I walked into this AMAZING casual establishment we were SOLD!!!

Everything was clean and just welcoming from the hostess' demeanor all the way to management being visible on the floor ready to jump in to assist when needed. 

Today we were served by the AWESOME Liz!!!

Liz's attitude was very good......her aura was just natural and unrehearsed whenever she checked on us, even when she checked on her other tables!!!

It's rare to have someone compliment things like the scent of a fragrance and have the ability to make both my wife and myself laugh!

This experience has definitely made us regulars and we'll bring family and friends to this particular location!!!

Liz we look forward to seeing you again and thanks for suggesting the Bacon Infused Blood Mary and The Big Easy Mimosa.

Do not waist your time or money  at  this dump. I went there on Saturday, it was my 6-7 time there. The major reason for my visit besides gambling  was to get a choice of a free Kurig  or another kind of coffee maker. When i arrived i aksed the person that gave me a daily pass for $10.00, that i need to earn 10 points that day to get a free coffee maker. I asked  the person how difficult  it is to get 10 points and she was vague  in her answer. She should  have told me unless I had $4000 or $5000 to play with not to bother.  I played for 3-4 hours and only got 2 points. What a discrace! When I asked how many point i have, i could not bealive it. Please do yourself a favor, and go spend your money at Harrah  or Parx, at least you do not have to spend a small fortune to get a free gift. Harrah gives you free stays  at Atlantic city and great gifts, and yku do not have to spend  all of your  money.  DO NOT  SPEND YOUR  MONEY WHERE YOU GET NOTHING IN RETURN.

This was the worst restaurant experience I've ever had. We got to the restaurant it was not even full and we had to wait 20 25 minutes. Who placed on joint orders at tip 10 minutes for them to come back
The food in the service was extremely slow we had to end up getting it to go. Kids ordered two cheese pizzas and take 30 minutes to come to the table and they came 15 minutes apart. The manager needs to be fired she didn't offer any Richard any reimbursement recompense for the service or food and she goes is there anything else I can help you with I almost want to slap her in the face!
Il miglior risotto allo zafferano mai mangiato. Zafferano dell'Aquila e gelato allo zafferano top.

First, the atmosphere: 
This place feels new. The space is big and it just needs something to fill it in and make it a little more homey. Also, why is it so cold in there? It made me feel like I was eating in a museum.

Now on to everything else:
I should warn you thay we've only gone to Sukho Thai once because the food is just too expensive for the quality and size when compared to La Thai. The waitress we had was great- super friendly, came by the right number of times/at the right times, and knowledgeable. But, I just don't feel that the food is worth it. 

Our friends swear this place is the best Thai in Nola, but maybe it's just one of those personal preference things? Try it out yourself, it's not awful, and write your own review :)
Great place with great people. The phill cheesesteaks are fire. They have cheese wiz! The people are even better and always feel welcome there. If you like cheesesteak, skip the fake places
Excellent food and service. we try a different meal each time we go. never been disappointed. Strongly recommend it if you want something better than TACO BELL

Cute restaurant located in a popular shopping center. The first thing I noticed when I walked in was the pretty decor, you can tell this restaurant is a little fancy, good for a romantic date or dressing up with girlfriends for a night out.

Prices are a little high compared to other Thai food places I've been too, but the portions were fair and the quality of the food was good.

I ordered the Masaman curry, a yellow curry with potatoes, peanuts, and cocunut milk. It was pretty good, though I can't say its the best I've had. I was surprised that the menu offered teriyaki dishes, which made my bf happy because he loves a good teriyaki sauce. He also ordered a roll of tempura sushi. He liked it, I can't say how good it was myself because I don't eat sushi.

Overall everything was tasty, and I want to try some of the other dishes on the menu. Honestly, I don't know if the food is worth the prices though, so when we do come back it will probably be for a special occassion.

Had lunch here today... Ordered their daily special called the Tyson Trio--different each day.  Awesome!!  It's the 2nd time I've had the Trio... equally good both times.

Also had them cater an event a couple years ago at Ovation (couple blocks away) for a 100+ people -- Fantastic!!
New owners have taken over, and we were amazed at the improvement in the food!  We will definitely go back!

Had a great time at Treehouse while visiting Nashville with a group of 12. Tasty cocktails, enjoyed the Floral Fashioned, and tried one of all the small plates plus a half bird, shrimp and a 12 oz. steak. We generally enjoyed everything, the highlights being the curry gnocchi and the roasted chicken. They also brought us out some bonus burgers and dessert as we were celebrating a bachelor party, which was a nice touch! Definitely a good stop.

Where to start. In a nut shell this place desperately needs Gordon Ramsey. I ordered a Boise Cheesesteak...BTW, Cheesesteak is one word, not two, as the menu states. It's supposed to be Filet Mignon...which it may have been before it was super old & over cooked.
As for the restaurant in general, its in dire need of an extreme makeover & is very disorganized.
The service was one of a kind. The food was beyond our expectations! The 25 cent martinis are so strong but so delicious! It's a must go to in New Orleans!

My bad.  This review is WAY overdue and has probably been sitting in draft form for a couple of years now.  The struggle is deciding what to order - every. time.  I have some "usuals" but am never disappointed in other items either.  

First Timers - here are some tips:
1) Depending on the weather it can be really crowded, especially during the winter months - so be patient.  But if it's nice out - decide whether you want to sit inside or outside.
2) If you have a wait, help yourself to the coffee bar.  

Love. love. the Omelettes.  The best one I've ever had was an OmeletteOTD:  bacon, tomato, basil pesto, and parmesan.  Add that on with cinnamon toast [so good!], lightly dressed greens and blueberry coffee...I'm in heaven.  That there folks is my unicorn.  It does not exist.
So, I usually go with a Custom Omelette (with a side of fruit instead of greens) and have to choose three from a variety of exquisite toppings such as:  bacon, kale, white mushrooms, sausage.  Don't forget the Sriracha! 

If I'm in a lunch mood, I'll go with the House Roasted Turkey Sandwich.  Now I know what you're thinking...no it's not like deli meat from your local grocer.  It's the real deal.
Love Pudges. No shortage of juicy meat and cheese. Pat's and Geno's are tourist traps if you ask me. They have nostalgia and that's about it. Their cheesesteaks are boring compared to Pudges.

The food was legit disgusting.  We couldn't even stomach it.  The steamed pork dumplings tasted like old meat (you know how they say fish shouldn't smell fishy? like that).  The general tso sauce was like sweet and sour, not spicy at all, not thickened.  The chicken was poor quality and had tendons in it.

Good for smokers. Bad for everyone else. I typically take my food and drinks to go.

One of the best burgers in the city! Their burgers are on par with Ya Mama's and Port of call.

It's kind of divey. If you're not into roughing it or you're too fancy, this isn't the place for you.

I always get the blue cheese burger. Very generous servings. 

Every time I go it's the 40+ crowd, but like I said before, I typically just go for the burger and grab a drink to go. Nothing special about the drinks. Go for the burgers and fries.

4 stars only because while I love the burgers/fries, the bar is not my speed.

All I can say is wow. My husband is a big coffee guy and we are in town visiting from Boston. Peter the barista was so helpful and patient explaining the coffee to me. My husband got the cold brew and it was absolutely delicious I was worried I wouldn't like mine, the flat white latte. I was wrong I LOVED mine. Peter noticed I liked my husbands sweet and as he was making mine even made it sweeter for me. The place itself is very cute and clean. If you love coffee do yourself a favor and stop by you won't be disappointed.

I am not really sure what to say about this restaurant​.​  Initially, it went well and then went downhill​. I was greeted​ at the door which is always a positive note.  Beverage and bread were served.
Whatever, I ordered seemed to take so long. I ordered the gyro platter.  
The salad as one of the side took 10 minutes to arrive.  Nice sized salad lettuce, red onion, and red pepper, black olives.  With it came a nice size piece of feta cheese.   A creamy salad dressing came with the salad.  
I waited for​ another 15 minutes before the main course came.  Unfortunately​, the bread and salad seemed to fill me up and I asked for a to-go​o box.  The waiter did say they had a problem with a piece of equipment and that is why it took so long.  The individuals were more interested in the equipment that preparing the food.
I enjoyed my salad and the warm bread came with whipped feta with garlic.
I would try again another day to see if the ​service improved.

My family had such a wonderful experience here! Harold was so kind and considerate to allow us to open our Christmas presents amongst our family and take our time ordering.

The food was exceptional, I highly recommend this place.

The drink were on point and the seasoning was so wonderful!
Food wasn't bad but definitely not worth the prices they charge...I can't say I would never return but I would rather go somewhere else considering all Tampa has to offer

Our air b and b host recommended horn to us. This is a cute little joint a little outside the French quarter. The ambiance and food are both fantastic. I suggest anything on the menu that includes cornbread and pulled pork.

Went for a fun date night with my husband. Lately come Friday I am craving yummy wings. I tried their crispy smoked fried wings with spicy BBQ and also a side of buffalo. The service was great and our server answered our questions and helped us make some good choices. I will definitely come again and try their ribs.

This place is absolutely amazing! It's definitely a must try in Tucson.  We have the tamales and Cuban tacos both were absolutely delicious. The salad served on the side was probably one of the Tastiest salad I've ever had.

We have been here at lest 10 times since they opened. Stellar service, amazing food, and immaculate restrooms.  We have not had one experience that was even below average. They have a great scratch kitchen and even if you don't play golf it's fun to play here. Kids love it as well. One of the best business models I've seen for this industry.

Having eaten at so many Thai restaurants in the NJ/NY area, I was really disappointed with my overall experience. Yes, the waitresses were really nice and friendly but there is no way this is authentic Thai food. Tasted more like Chinese to me. 

I was in the St. Pete Beach area for vacation and decided to come here for dinner one day. I had their salad: lettuce, tomato, cucumber, bean sprouts, and tofu with peanut dressing. Although the peanut dressing was good, they put way too much and it overpowered the small salad.

As my entrée, I ordered the Spicy Basil Noodles with Chicken. Usually Spicy Basil Noodles at the places I've been to consist of flat rice noodles, with bell peppers, onions, black pepper, and basil. That's it! Instead, this place had lo mein noodles (really?!), tons of tomatoes, string beans, and broccoli, and hardly any bell peppers, onions, and basil! The basil is what gives it the unique flavor! At first I thought it might have been me, but as I continued to eat through the dish, there was absolutely no taste at all of any spiciness or basil. 

Unfortunately, I wouldn't recommend this place, unless you really don't care if you're having authentic Thai food or not.

I'm sorry but I'm just not a fan of cheap furniture made of chemically treated particle board. Don't get me wrong. I understand the appeal, especially when you throw in a few swedish meatballs. But, it's just not for me.

Recently went to Cooper's Hawk for a celebratory lunch. Our party of two went to inquire about a table and there was a long wait for a Saturday at 1 pm. The hostess offered up the bar as an option so away we went.
The bar area is nice with booths, a couple of high tops, and a full length bar. We decided to sit up at the bar and have some lunch and a celebratory drink.
The wine list a Coopers Hawk is nicely extensive and food and wine paring suggestions are printed in the menu for every item. Both my friend and I started off with a class of the Almond Sparkling Wine which arrived cold and quickly. Sitting at the bar is great here if you want to ensure you get your refills quickly.
The food menu can be overwhelming at times but I love how diverse the menu is. Smaller plates, salads, sandwiches and entrees are all delightful. I have a hard time making it past the appetizer menu because there are so many good options. We shared the chips and dip. This is not your boring party chips and dip. Smooth, creamy, and tangy onion and bacon dip (and who doesn't like bacon?!) served with an overflowing basket of fresh cut potato chips. My only complaint was there was not enough dip for all of the chips. For my lunch, I had the thai chicken lettuce wraps and my friend had the short ribs. The lettuce wraps come with julienne fresh vegetables, sweet chili chicken, fresh cucumbers, wonton strips, and butter lettuce. I really enjoyed two of the three sauces: the soy caramel and the peanut sauce. The dish is messy but very delicious. My friend thoroughly enjoyed her short ribs and mashed potatoes. I was so into my dish I forgot to ask to taste hers before it was gone. For dessert we shared the banana bread ice cream sundae. Two huge pieces of banana bread with two huge scoops of some of the best vanilla ice cream I've had in awhile topped with a caramel sauce. It looked so good that even our bartender asked if he could have a bite. Very rich but a great way to end a celebratory meal.
I also love that on the way out, if you find a bottle you love, you can take one home with you. My friend picked up a bottle of the Almond wine to take home for later.

Ridiculously awesome.  The food and drinks are off the charts.  Esthers Medicine is phenomenal.  Best cocktail ever.  The service is great.  But what really makes this restaurant stand out is the excellent service provided by its GM, Stevem Khuu.  This guy gives you the Napa Valley 5 Star Michelin star service in little Bryn Mawr.

Excellent job guys.  Congrats!!

My family of four was in for brunch on Sunday (father's day).

We waited 45 minutes to be served though the restaurant was NOT busy and the food ordered was not complex (scrambled eggs, pancakes, eggs Benedict and chicken and fries). 

We waited an additional 5 minutes for utensils after being served. 

My food, scrambled eggs with vegetables, was simultaneously raw, over cooked and frozen. The veg was a store bought frozen medley which was obviously added to the pan with the eggs at the same time. The result was gross. The frozen veg was still cold in the middle and the eggs that were cooked near them never had time to fully cook while the rest of the eggs we so cooked they were hard. 

My wife's crab cakes Benedict was also gross, smelling of spoiled crab and the eggs were, again, raw. Not poached. Not over easy. Raw. Period. 

My daughters pancakes were fried in oil giving them the smell, flavor and texture of funnel cake. They charge an extra $3.00 for a small handful of chocolate chips. 

My sons chicken fingers and French fries were served as we were leaving. The fries were tiny for some reason. Like every individual fry was no larger than an inch and the chicken was terrible. 

We did order Beignets, their signature dish. They were doughy and raw in the middle. 

Beware!!!  You must pay for your food first.  A huge gamble considering the inconsistent reviews on Yelp. This experience set me back $55.00. 

The coffee was good, though no one ever asked if we'd like more. One cup, 3 bucks. 

Good luck.
Great take-out service and THE BEST cold corned beef sandwich I can find in the Wilmington, Delaware vicinity.

I really wanted to give a good review. It was my second time at this restaurant - this time I brought friends, but we won't be back. Our server was great, actually, but the food not so much. We had the appetizer of PEI Mussels in white sauce, but reminded me of dirty dish water with a hamburger bun toasted in the grill (really!?) as the bread to dip!  Our party then ordered entrees. Our NY strip steak came out charred, since it was the last one they had - we had to settle for a spinach salad. We also had a salmon dinner that was barely cooked. Dessert was no better. A homemade snickers bar came out as two pieces of chocolate, really not a dessert. So disappointing. What a great location that could be so good but really falls short of the mark.

The disproportionate size of the Dong Phuong bun to the meat was a surprise, but somehow this burger still managed to work. It was like something dad threw on a really hot grill, and had lots of char and smoke--one of the crustiest burgers I've ever had in a restaurant. The smoked onions were a terrific compliment, and the quality of the bun is worth overlooking the size. The amount of char is a tradeoff of tenderness, but serious burger lovers should check this one out.
If you are looking for fresh tortillas and chips, there is no place better to go.  House made, and prepared the same day, there is no better product or price.
The frites are great!  Love the variety of food.  Dogs were great too :)
I've never been there was a good and what did you have. I have never been there so how can I give you a review I have a friend that's gone there she and her husband were quite happy

Not worth it. Rude staff, food was close to average. The cheese sticks were good but the past was bland and very generic. Expensive for a plate of bland spaghetti sauce reminiscent of ragu pasta sauce.  Cars frequently get stolen and broke into.

I've been here a good four times. I was first introduced to Toup's by friends who frequent here a lot. The duck was delicious the first time but greasy and too fatty the next time after that. The  Host is a little too sassy for my taste. He's not that friendly to new people but caters to the regulars. I had a reservation here for my birthday and it was almost ruined by his attitude. He gave us shit at the door because i asked if we could sit indoors instead of outside because i didn't want to get eaten by mosquitoes.  But when our friends came (who come here often), he literally said, "oh why didnt you tell me you were with them?" Because clearly i wasn't important enough. Birthday or not. Newsflash: your newcomers will never be regulars with that attitude.
The salmon was superb.  My husband felt like he needed to go to dinner again after the mushroom stroganoff.  The salad was just a B, nothing special.
I have been going to this restaurant for the past 40 years. I find it to be a moderately priced family friendly restaurant. Everyone's taste will vary, but I find the food to be excellent.

Food is pretty good, but nothing mind-blowing. The eggrolls are good. WAY overpriced; $17 for a CHICKEN vermicelli bowl? And now I am giving them no more than three because they just forgot to add chicken to TWO orders of chicken vermicelli.  They refunded, but still....how do you just forget to add meat to BOTH orders?

Are you sure this is in Clermont? The building that this place is in has been home to a few different little dive bars where the people sit around and play those pull tab things so when I saw that an actual restaurant was going in, I was pretty stoked. Lola's offers flatbread pizzas and a few entree options that change daily. The menu is pretty limited but everything on it sounds legit and I get nervous when restaurants have huge menus. I actually prefer a small menu.  My wife opted for the Asian steak flatbread pizza and I decided to go with shrimp and grits. My food was delicious and something that I would compare to the quality of a hotel restaurant. The portion size was adequate and I would consider the prices to be a good value for what arrives on the plate. My shrimp and grits arrived hot and in a clean bowl. The shrimp were plentiful and served atop a bowl of creamy grits accompanied with chorizo and cilantro. It was seasoned well and tasted excellent with a little hot sauce. The pizza was equally tasty and came with good pieces of meat, red cabbage and a sauce that tasted like sweet chili sauce. The drink selection was a little bare bones yet offered something for everyone with red and white wine, a couple macro brews and a micro on tap. I feel that a little more emphasis could be placed on cocktails and signature drinks. 
The inside was well decorated and reminded me of eating at a friend's home. It's hard to believe that this used to be a cruddy little bar and I'm impressed to see what a little style and design can do to a place. There was maybe one too many televisions on the wall and I felt that this distracted me from the food a little bit. 

A note about parking.... If the bank across the street is closed, you can park over there. There is also some parking behind the building.

I love Amici Milano -- it's one of my favorite restaurants.  I have been going there for years and have never had a bad meal.  My husband and I frequent the restaurant with large family gatherings and dinners with friends.  The atmosphere is wonderful and so is the food.  The service is excellent and the prices are great.  I feel it is one of the best places to go for dinner.  I can't praise them enough.

Charlene M.

Everything about this place was on point. For starters the waitress was attentive, friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. The space was a little small but just right, we got there at a good time. A bit chilly but the atmosphere was awesome, people chatting amongst themselves and nice house music to fit the mood. We sat at the bar, Blair was cool she was busy but attentive,  checked on is, made small talk and kept the drinks coming. We had every Happy Hour drink except the "old fashion" will try next time. 

The oysters were to die for, it could have been just a meal because they were fulfilling. I ordered the crawfish pasta and my friend ordered the seafood platter. Seasoning was perfecto, a bit too much batter on the oysters but they didnt make or break the experience. 

Atmosphere was awesome, bathrooms clean and kitchen away from the seating area. We even got serananed by one, yes "1" host that lit up the place for someone's birthday. 

I am not disappointed and will definitely be back with the ladies to enjoy more of the Morrow experience, to add to the story.

I went to eat at Triumph last week, because the restaurant that I wanted to eat at was closed on Mondays. The ambience was nice, I sat outside right next to the railroad tracks, and was lucky enough to see the train come into the station and then depart again. However, that was the highlight of my experience.

The waitstaff was friendly and attentive, and the menu was extensive. But then I made a mistake. It is a mistake that I have made more than once in my life. I have a deep love for the fish and chips that I get in England a few times a year, and I have ordered them in various American restaurants, always with great expectations, and I have always been disappointed. When will I learn? The menu description was promising, and they even had malt vinegar, which is an indispensable condiment for true fish and chips, but the fish was soggy and greasy, the fries were cold, and I left feeling as though I had just consumed the ultimate gut bomb.

It is possible that other menu items would be more palatable, but I was really disappointed. I may go back, but I will not be ordering the fish and chips. My mistake.

The quintessential old-school good-old-boy dimly-light insider's club steakhouse.

Nice steaks, great salad bar, and everything else is a la carte so you can have just the experience you wish.

Sperry's is not cheap, but the experience isn't cheap, either.  Everything they do is first class.

If you are a wine lover, you're in the right place.  If you're not, you can still enjoy a great meal and you'll be even happier when the check comes.

They are offering Sunday brunch these days, and the prices at brunch at very reasonable so absolutely check that out - they make a great Eggs Benedict.

Sperry's is locally owned and they are some of the nicest people you'll find anywhere who genuinely give back to their community.

If it's a special occasion, go try them out.  You'll thank me later.

As a music venue City Winery in Nashville downtown near the Music City Center is now in the top ten here. Yesterday I loved the sound of roots music great Rodney Crowell singing the songs he has written, in the big room of this performance venue. The day before the Deslondes performed from the new stage, which features a great sound system and acoustics. I think the City Winery Nashville will be as well known for its music as for its tart Napa Valley wine and wines produced here, in Music City USA.

We visited for Saturday brunch with a party of 4, and were able to squeeze into the last open table during a busy period. I enjoy reading Yelp reviews that mention specific menu items, so here were our orders:

-Veggie maki roll appetizer; everyone's favorite dish.  I really loved the interplay of the miso dressing and ginger-tinged carrot pate.
-Tuna melt with broccoli side salad; I typically despise mayo-laden, fishy tuna salad, but SoBro's version was advertised as lighter and with the mention of "harissa", I had to order.  The sandwich was okay, served on a huge piece of Texas toast with an ample amount of melted cheddar; I could not taste any harissa sauce. I'd probably order something else next time, more so out of curiosity, not disappointment. The broccoli was still crispy in the side salad and not overladen with mayo-sauce.
-Vegan biscuits & gravy: okay, although the gravy tasted a bit sweet and nutty. I wonder if they use cashew cream as a cow milk sub?
-Wildfire omelette- my dining partner gave it an "okay, but not enthusiastic" thumbs-up, liked the Canadian bacon.
-Cajun tilapia wrap- rave reviews for this sandwich from the fish-fanatic of our dining group. The bite I had did not taste very Cajun, but was fresh and complemented well by the sandwich's veggies.
-Chai; this was one of the best chais I've ever tasted, and I'd definitely re-order it during future visits.

Service was sporadic and a little absentee, although the multiple servers who tended our table seemed friendly.  I was wavering between 3 and 4 stars due to the service and "just okay" entrees., but I think the delicious chai bumped it to 4.

The aesthetic alone is worth a visit. But then when you see the prices for such s beautiful, new and hip space you are astonished. Wine and cocktails under $10. Whoa! We went on a beautiful Sunday and truly enjoyed ourselves. Nothing Like sitting in a courtyard that was once a rectory, drinking champagne and apperol spritz. I can't speak on the food but the menu looked fabulous and seasonal. Great and appealing sharable bar bites. I most definitely will be back for dinner next trip.
So delicious I would eat there again I love the way it tasted in my mouth it felt like so warm and delicous like Sunday breakfast

This place was so cramped and the decoration was sub par. I could hardly enjoy the food because we were placed in the back where the door was slightly ajar, letting in a cold breeze. I would not come back.

Delicious for most of the courses. Foie gras , salmon mouse one of the more intriguing amazing combination of flavor and texture , rigatoni with pork shoulder is amazing , surf and turf was pork belly and squid was basic, I was disappointed after so many wonderful dishes then this being brought out , pork belly seemed to charred on the outside, not much flavor, for the third course maybe a larger portion , and the Bavarian was mediocre TOO MUCH SALT for me, my other half got the macaron which was fantastic. Mainly the third course needs to be amped up in many ways. Overall great experience would return in 1-3 years.

Their happy hour has $5 old fashioneds which were fantastic. Also some great beers on tap as well.

The food is small-plates style and they recommend 2-3 per person, which is about right. They range from $10-$20 or so, and those were hit-and-miss for us.

I heard a lot of good things about HPC, including it was one of the best nightclubs in Tampa for top 40s music. Maybe that's true on Saturdays, but I came for Thanksgiving Eve. They are normally closed Wednesdays, and it's normally not 40 degrees in Tampa.  The second issue-the weather-shouldn't affect the music, but maybe the DJ felt he could mix things up since it was slow. As for the first issue-the off night-maybe it wasn't a top 40s night. The promotional company advertised it as top 40 and hip hop, and there was lots of hip hop, but also lots of Miami bass and almost no top 40. 

It's a nice enough place. 2 rooms with different music. The room they were doing Latin in was nicer, and much more space and a bigger bar. Maybe that's because Latin dancing involves a lot more movement then just raising your hands in the air every time Lil John tells you to, but I don't know. 

They also have an awesome patio between the rooms. Lots of space to move around and relax and take a break from dancing. On this night, they had space heaters around, but they were no use against the cold front. 

$5 cover for me (free for my girlfriend) is reasonable. Drinks were strong, bartenders friendly and attentive. And I liked the venue, though I would have preferred the "top 40" room be bigger. The biggest issue was music. Just didn't think it was that good and certainly lacking in the advertised top 40. In fairness, most of the patrons were enjoying it and having a blast. We had fun too, but the music left a lot to be desired for us. 

I think I need to check it out again on a regular Saturday and see if the music is better. Will update my review when I do.

Great place to eat! I love the chicken philly sandwich. Fries are fresh, crispy, and have a nice seasoning on them. The sandwiches depend on who is doing the cooking that day, I'm not complaining though because at their worst I still would give them 4 stars. They are also close to the USF campus and open late which makes them a great choice when you get hungry during those late night study sessions.

First off, any time you go to a restaurant and personally meet the Chef and the Owner, that shows the passion they have for what they do.  I met both of them during a busy night and that says a lot about the place.  

As far as food goes, I did a bit of a Nashville tour over the last few visits of restaurants, and this place hands down made all other experiences worth it.  The food was awesome here.  Big portion, amazing flavors, and true TLC in every plate you get.  The Prime Rib is so perfectly done that you can cut it with a spoon.  I almost shed a tear at how delicious it was.  


The cocktail program here is incredible too.  A lot of time and effort went into it along with the beer selection.  Top that with entertainment, and you don't even need to go anywhere else.  Get there early because people know how good it is and it gets packed.  I tip my hat to everyone here.

Believe the hype. All of it. Just. Go. Now. The line is extremely long but moves pretty quickly. The seasoning on the food is awesome. My friend and I shared 1lb of crawfish, 1lb of shrimp, 4 corns, crab legs and a shrimp fried rice. Everything, and I do mean everything was bomb.com. I would go back again and again and again! And I like this location because we were able to get our gloves, sit and eat! Highly recommended!

I love Qdoba because it's not around where I live, so I tend to stop when I see one. I stopped at this one and within 10 seconds I could see that it wouldn't be a pleasant experience. Made eye contact with the man at the register as I walked in, he had no customer in front of him and didn't even say Hi welcome to Qdoba, just stared at me. The first guy taking orders was very short with people and almost seemed annoyed that he had to listen to what you wanted to eat. The woman putting on toppings also seemed annoyed and was simply plopping the toppings on there. My girlfriend hadn't been to a Qdoba before so asked a question and the woman acted like that was out of place. I did enjoy my food, so 2 stars for that, but my god, you're in the service industry, smile and be friendly.

Very good option if downtown, especially if going to an event at TPAC, as it is within easy walking distance. The food is excellent. I had the chicken fried chicken (a bit salty but delicious), while my wife had shrimp and grits (which she raved about). The food arrived quickly, but tasted freshly cooked, not heated in a microwave. 

The primary reasons for a 4 star and not a 5 are 1) it was a bit too noisy in there, especially when the musicians performed and 2) the tables are a bit too close together. Still, we are very likely to return.

Not your typical breakfast from @torshi_egyptian_food in @st.rochmarket. The perfect falafel with a hard boiled egg inside, served on creamy hummus. This breakfast was incredibly filling, but didn't leave me feeling that 'I need to take a nap' type feeling after brunch. The fresh Greek salad  on the side with fig vinaigrette was also refreshing and delicious.

This place is pretty much over-rated. I give it 2.5 stars. I'm a huge fan of pulled pork sandwiches and have tried my fair share but this is not one of the places to get a really good one. Sure they give you a lot of meat but the quality, tastiness, and moistness is just average. I'm pretty sure one of the the reasons why the meat is dry is because they chop up the pork too finely, instead of it being pulled or slightly chopped. And this place is real stingy with their BBQ sauce. You have to ask for it on your sandwich (or meal) and then they pour just a little bit on your sandwich. Then there are no dispensers or bottles to put more BBQ sauce on if you want to. But besides that, the sauce isn't that good at all anyways. The sauce has this sour & odd taste to it that just doesn't taste right...or that good. And the hotter BBQ sauce wasn't hot at all and also lacked taste.

As for the sides, the macaroni salad looked and tasted exactly as if you were to buy the store brand kind at Publix / Sweet Bay / Wal-Mart / etc. Cole slaw was plain & average. Not sweet whatsoever and even salt didn't help kick up the flavor.

Price wasn't cheap either. And there is no lunch specials there at all which is surprising.

The new layout and remodel is nice but doesn't make up for the average food and high prices.

We tried Krystal's place after reading reviews online and now it is our favorite. Food is fresh and home made.  Portions are generous and the prices are more than reasonable. 
Grandfather chicken is delicious and the egg rolls remind me of what they tasted like when I was a kid. 
The owner, Krystal is friendly and hospitable. 
Food might take a little longer than most but that's the trade off for fresh made.

The ambiance is endearing with private booths and organic decor, and good vibes. The staff is friendly and sincere. The food is excellent with a nice variety of offerings but not an overwhelming menu selection as most fusion Thai spots do. Think best of 
I went last friday night with a friend and split the following; Thai Sarong to start, tom yum soup, tom ga soup, Pad sew ee Noodle with shrimp, Thai Green Curry with Chicken. 

The shrimp is elongated then wrapped in noodles, fried crispy, and served with red chili pepper sauce. I needed more dipping sauce. But I dip a lot. I ended up dipping them in my Tom Gha soup for fun. Wish I could make this at home, but yea probably one day. I highly recommend it.

Both soups have a well balanced broth. Tom Gha is my favorite, with coconut milk and lemongrass bringing comfort and refreshment all at once. How do they do that? Yes, it was 90 degrees outside. Yes, I ordered soup, so did my friend. It was great, I don't regret it. I'll be back in the fall for a very large order of it. Tom Yum was great too, this is sweet and sour and they did the right amount of both making it a legit start. 

MMMM, so the Pa Sew EE Noodle is an extra wide flat noodle in a brown sauce. They really have the flavors down here. Great balance again, not oily or drowning in sauce. Just right with fresh vegetables and shrimp done right. 

Thai Green Curry Noodle was delicious in a creamy coconut curry sauce. The spice was perfect, the waiter did say the green was spicy but it was like a medium/5 on spice level. I can handle spicy, but don't want it to be overpowering the dish. This was on point. The light sweetness from the coconut balanced it well. The noodles were thick round, nicely cooked soft medium chew. The veggies added that healthy feel with a crunch, woo! 

It's hard to say which dish I liked more. That's why I always bring a friend and share folks. 

All I can say is, I wish I had room for dessert.

Danger on the spice level. This is over the top Thai spice scale. I ordered a 3 out of 5, and the spice level was comparable to the Indian hot level of spicy at my favorite Indian restaurant. Like coughing and sweating while eating and not being able to finish my meal while toning it down with acid. Flavors are good. So I'll be back to try their dishes with mild heat scales lol. I imagined the puss Thai wings to be a bit better than they look, but they are good if you like fish sauce. Love they have fusion and creative items on their menu.

Was told it was an hour wait.... 2.5 hours later they had set multiple parties in front of us... Hostess Eliana (or whatever) was horrible! Rudest person I have EVER met! She should not be a hostess or work with the public at all for that matter. Then once seated, we were sat at a table meant for 4 and there was 9 of us.... sat on a dang porch that was slanted, with no room to even be able to pick up a fork! All you can eat crab legs or not DEFINITELY NOT WORTH IT!!!! Will never eat there again... and DONT recommend it!

My absolute go to for happy hour. They have a wonderful rotating menu for small plates ($7) and everything is also amazing. Also always a cocktail, house wine and house beer for $5-6 too. The staff is always friendly and is the inside is amazing! Go down to the basement to the speakeasy part of the restaurant.
Great restaurant, interesting menu, superb service, wines by the glass as well as a nice wine list.   Focus is on taste and presentation.

Oops, we had trouble with an important delivery promise being broken. In the morning I ordered two large pizzas for delivery that evening.  We were hosting a get-together for hungry people.  I asked for a promise that they would arrive on time and they assured me it would happen.
Time came,...no pizzas.  Called the restaurant.  They couldn't find my records.  After talking to several
people and repeating my order, we sent a guest to retrieve our order rather than waiting for them to deliver.  Kind of a downer.  The pizzas were ok, and they said an oven had broken, but they could have called with a warning and a better solution.

Went here for a tasting collective event and wow this was wonderful. All the food was A-amazing. I mean really I could write a 20 page paper about how I could eat this food everyday but I will put it sweet to the point. We had many different dishes from citrus poached shrimp to brussels sprouts ravioli. My top and most favorite dishes were the castle valley grits with the lamb bolognese. I mean come on the richness and texture in this was so yum.  If the chef came out and told me they just had this I would eat a pot of it myself. Also another dish I really enjoyed was the roasted pork loin with galumpki. If you are not aware of what galumpki is trust me you should try theirs. It is an amazing polish/ eastern European food of stuffed cabbage and it is a must try. We ended on a giant Gateau Basque which was oozing with a chicory coffee anglaise and just topped the night off. This place is a hands down must and I will be going out of my way to come back to try even more.

As most people know the first Sunday is on donation. We started by running up the stairs - doing the Rocky thing. We saw the Armor and medieval weapons. It was nice, they had a lot of small kids and they were more excited. We then went to the European exhibit. It was good, like the rooms that had been recreated as it gave a unique perspective. Lastly we went to the Asia wing. Was impressed by the Indian and Chinese rooms. It took us about 2.5 hrs. I would recommend to see it in this order as it got us interested to start and then kept on getting better.

Cool joint. Stopped in after my sister picked me up from the airport. This place is not far from her house so she has been wanting to try it because of the cauliflower pizza. 
When we walked in it was very quiet and had only a few customers at 1:30 PM. Also, as we learned, it looked like there was only one server who was also the bartender. That and the fact that they messed up on our pizza and had to redo it is why I am not getting it five stars. The house boom bazz salad was excellent, and the cauliflower pizza was fantastic as well. Check this place out.

Love the pizza. Fresh ingredients, interesting combinations.  But stick with the pizza. Salads are no-hum at best. Had the chop salad, and for $10 you get a whole bunch of lettuce, six little toasted tomatoes, a few red onions and some cheese. The lettuce overwhelms, despite the yummy house dressing. This salad needs some help, and I expected more from a place that has great gourmet pizza, but honestly, the chain pizza joints have much superior salads. Will not go back unless I plan to chow down on only the pizza. Frankly, I can get both at  Napolese.

Used to eat here when it was Zayna's, now it's under new management...still same great food. Husband gets the gyro and fries, I get the chicken shwarma and fries - both excellent! Staff and owner are very friendly.
Will be trying their breakfast next - lots of great options.
overall a good place but I ordered some pizza's on a stick and hotdogs on a stick but I finished my bubble tea while waiting for them & wanted to order another one service could be a little quicker .

Don't let the location and the sketchy-looking exterior stop you from coming here.The inside is always clean and the owner is super friendly and quick to greet you. We always order the baleada and the pollo con tajada (the chicken comes on a bed of fried plantains and cabbage slaw).  Both come in huge portions and are delicious.  I also highly recommend the pupusas and the horchata drink. We love to support local small businesses and this is easily our favorite place for Central American food in the New Orleans area.

Great place to hit before a Vandy game.  Convenient location is about 10 minutes walking distance to the stadium  Chill vibe, 60's style artwork on the walls.  The restaurant has a long narrow side to it but it is equipped with several TVs on that side to keep you occupied.

Decent beer selection but it was missing the one Yazoo beer I am currently drinking, Dos Perros.  The Hawaiian Pizza was good with nice quality ham and lots of cheese.

Went to Kipos for the first time last night because I knew it was newer and wanted to give it a try. I am SO happy I did. I'm in love with Mediterranean cuisine so trust me when I say this place nails it. Their tzatziki is bomb. I had the gyro on pita and I will definitely come back to try other things. Really awesome spot! Great addition!!

Varga Bar has gradually become my favorite bar in the city in the year of its existence.  Clearly, I'm not the only person who feels this way, which means I've resorted to being choosy about when to drop in.  Nevertheless, I'm glad so many people are as taken with the drinks, eats, décor and staff as I am, and I don't mind saving my visits for the every-now-and-then rather than every Friday night.

The sliders and pickles remain my go-to meal, and I have yet to try much else from the menu, apart from my very first visit just over a year ago.  It's a shame, but I can not bring myself to deviate from those shiny little brioche buns enclosing perfect little mounds of bacon and boursin-topped kobe beef.  Throw in a few of the world's best onion rings and some housemade pickles and it's all over.  Somebody hand me a bib.  I hate that the Varga salad now comes with blue cheese instead of whatever cheese it used to come with (more boursin, perhaps?).  I love blue cheese but the salad was perfect as it was already.  The concept of change has never been easy for me.  Hopefully everything else I know and love about Varga remains the same for years to come.
HORRIBLE PERIOD. Burgers were dry. Managers not around. Waitresses were awsome. Just not a fan of there food.
Personally I just think this is an overpriced burger joint. I mean the food was ok, but nothing I would go out of my way to eat. Maybe it's just me but I think this place is way overrated.

As the saying goes, my eyes were bigger than my stomach. It was an incredible price of $22 for all of the sushi I got that included 2 rolls, 4 different types of sashimi w/2 pieces each and a hand roll including tip for curbside delivery. Yes, I got a lot and it was all for myself!

FL ROLL 3.5/5: Some pieces had more cream cheese while others had less, my opinion is that less cream cheese is always better. 

GATOR ROLL 4/5: Spicy tuna & yellowtail that's mixed with arromatic sesame oil, liked the aioli sauce on the top & I think more restaurants should make rolls this way! 

SUSHI HR (EEL) 5/5 (hand roll): So impressed, got 2 long pieces of smoked eel w/rice and strips of cucumber. It's the same amount of eel you'd get as a roll, a must reorder. Anytime I eat sushi, I always need my eel.

SHASHIMI (conch, octupus, salmon, tuna) 4/5: Two slices of each & the low prices allowed me to retry octopus and conch; I rarely order them. The way they were sliced it didn't have too much finesse & texturewise I didn't like & couldn't commit to, so I gave it to my dog after I tried a couple small bites & made her due a few tricks. She happily ate it. lol

Needless to say, I couldn't finish it all because I also ate some of my hubs wings from WWB. At the beg. Of the week, they were offering Happy Hour even for To Go orders, so I ended up on getting a sample platter...made my stomach smile being able to have a bit of everything; I will know exactly what to get next round. 

It'd normally be 4/5, but I have to say, they are doing a lot to make the Curbside Pickup as seamless as possible with amazing Happy Hour deals during Covid-19, so a 5/5 for this happy sushi enthusiast!
Had a great Luncheon at the Chattanooga location. The food was excellent and service was just as good. Would cater another function there again

Best (French) macarons in the city. Fresh, full of flavor, and delicious, they are worth the nearly $2 per pop price tag as an occasional treat. The flavors are out of this world (cinnamon almond and pumpkin pie were my favorites, with chocolate ganache as a close third). The lady who works in the truck is friendly and helpful.

An absolute must if you love macarons. 

PS- These are French macarons- maringue-based  cookies with rich decadent filling, not to be confused with coconut macaroons.

A dark wooden abyss.
