And that's a good thing. get there early cuz it gets packed. went about 730 on a friday and got one of the last remaining tables without a wait. the wings are amazing. i'm thinking of them now. plus we got a bonus order for free because we were brought someone else's order first by mistake. one's gain is another's tragedy. good selection of beer on tap. a jukebox. bar stools are limited. this place is small. lots of menu choices. i'm going back soon. Prices aren't really that bad. A bargain nearly.

I have been very pissed off at this place for a long time. The second star is for the sake of the bartenders. I'm a 21 year old bartender, and i look young, but I don't appreciate being treated like an ignorant child, by a hipster waitress who hates her job. 
I took my younger sister and her friend, and my boyfriend. There is a sign that says seat yourself, so I went to seat myself and the server stood in my way and told me that if I was sitting at the bar, I had to close out my tab, and when I told her we just got here and needed a table she continued to stand there and stare at me. I could tell she wanted me in someone else's section.
We sit down, and she tells us the specials on beer, in the most monotone voice I have ever heard. She then says, "I don't know if you guys are 21 or whatever." What? okay. we all get cokes and my boyfriend gets a beer. 10 minutes after we get our drinks she comes back to take our order. I really wanted the potato wedges and cheese (which are awesome), so i ask for those as an appetizer. The food runner drops our food, and we eat them all. And wait. And wait. It was absurd. She finally decides to grace us with her presence and says, "Uhh, soo do you guys WANT to order entrees? or do you just wanna sit here." I was literally staring at her with my mouth hanging open.
So onto the entrees. Shepards pie was terrible. I can't even pinpoint why. The gravy tasted like packaged salisbury steak and the potatoes tasted like nothing. The girls' chicken cheesesteak had no complaints, and my boyfriends chicken sandwich was most likely frozen and microwaved.  Good place for drinking, and appetizers. But I never want to see that server again in my life.

Succulent, delicious, juicy meats!  What's there not to like about this taqueria?

Seriously, this is one of the only places I can find ojo, lengua, and labio in the same place.  The tacos are smaller which means that you get more variety!  I love being able to order three or four different tacos, all containing different meats.

Also, this is definitely one of the best salsa bars in town.

My only complaint is that tripa is only avaiable on the weekend.

We went there after visiting the discovery museum down the street. We sat in the restaurant section. 
Food was great, the portions were large and flavorful. 
The wait staff was very helpful and split an order of pasta on 2 plates for the boys without us even asking.
It was quiet so we did not feel rushed.
Overall we would come back next time we are in the area.

Side note, there is Vietnamese restaurant in the same plaza that's good as well.

I loved the ambiance of the place. I shared the Kobe beef burger and alligator burger sliders and while both were excellent I would return for the alligator! 
While not a big venue, they appear to be understaffed and my service was delayed. They took long to bus the table, take our order, deliver the food and give is the check!

The only saving grace for this place is the music and the food. If service is a deal breaker, then either lower your expectations or choose another area.
Ramen portion sizes are really small, and the broth is subpar. Ambiance is nice with cute anime decorations though

After working up an appetite while hiking around Crystal Peak Park we stopped in at Chop 40 -- a rustic, western themed dive we had heard good things about. Hubby ordered the Western Burger - a big, juicy burger topped with an onion ring, melted cheese and bbq sauce. I got the Cuban sandwich - a jalapeño focaccia bread stuffed high with pulled pork, melted cheese and pickles. Both meals came piping hot, along with crispy, seasoned fries - all served on a black-handled skillet. Large portions and excellent quality provided a great value. We will be back!

I stopped after work for a light dinner at the bar. The wine by glass menu was very small and my first choice which was the headliner special was not available wouldn't you know it. So I paid $11 for a 6 oz pour which I thought looked small but I'm sure everyone is used to the pour we make our selves at home. Anyway on to the calamity. I ordered the calamari which tasted delicious and was lightly fried with peppers and jalapeños. Two hours later I was cursing the my choice and I continued to pay for it ALL night long. Needless to say I won't be back to any Chart house restaurants after this intestinal event. When thinking back on it, I was the only person eating ....hmmmmm

This place is an awesome hidden gem tucked away from the bustle of the busy Broad Ripple area. Pastries look stunning. The food is extraordinary. I almost don't want to review this place so it will not get busier than it already is. You will not want to leave.

Run of the Mill AYCE Sushi.

The Sushi chefs were great.  Friendly and seemed to be enjoying their work.  I really like spicy food so the chef made me a couple on the fly creations that were all pretty tasty.  They use habanero peppers instead of jalapeno and it was a nice change.  Their menu is pretty standard assortment of cooked and raw rolls and nigiri.  I thought their nigiri was sloppy and not that impressive.  

The reason I'm rating it so low is the entire restaurant REEKS of fish.  Bad sign when it comes to any Sushi joint in my opinion.

Some of the best BBQ I've had in Florida...and the nachos were great!  My only complaint was that the portions seemed small...but that was overcome by the quality.  The pulled pork, ribs and jalapeno sausage were great.  Sides of BBQ beans and greens were also very good.  Our server, Myles, was great and provided some of the best service in recent memory.  All of the staff seemed to share responsibility for ensuring the customers received good service...kudos to them and the manager!!  Will definitely be back.

We came here and did the chef's choice which ended up being 7 dishes for $45 a person 

We sat down and ordered two drinks and opted in for the chef's choice but it would've been nice for the server to explain what's included or preferred flavor profiles. She merely asked us if we had allergies then walked away. 

We were given 7 dishes:
- Whipped feta: best of the meal 5/5
- Turnip noodles 
- Avocado crispy rice
- Cauliflower "steak" and potatoes
- Fried chicken
- PB&J malabi 
- Can't remember the last but I think we had 2 cauliflower dishes?

Each dish was fresh and full of flavor but the standout was definitely the whipped feta. I would've appreciated at least one other protein selection instead of all the vegetable dishes but it was still a lovely experience overall. Very cosy inside and well crafted cocktails.

LOVE LOVE LOVE the Pho. However the loud, rude, crude crowd of 20 something's need to find another place to go, maybe like a frat house.  I'll think twice before going again, maybe for takeout only to avoid the people that think Hook's is their private party house.  The manager needs to step up and say something.

I love the vibe of this bar.  Drinks are reasonably priced and the food menu looks great. I've had some apps but never anything more. Everything I've ever tried here has been good. they also do a brunch with some vegan gluten free pancakes that are supposedly the bomb. They buy their bread from Jamison b breadhouse so you know it's going to be a good meal. Lots of parking and a great place to visit when in the area. Service is wonderful. They also host a Evening market called the Vagabond Gita Monday's and moonlight market. With henna artist, tarot card readings,fortune telling , Dj's and lots of bohemian vibe.

As soon as we walked into this restaurant it was a hostile environment. We were not properly greeted upon entry. As protocol the hostess (whom refused to provide her name) requested to see our QR Codes for proof of vaccination, although she glanced at them and did not scan them. My elderly mother was asked to show hers and only had the pharmacy proof of vaccination clearly showing she was fully vaccinated. They refused to allow her in without a QR code which we proceeded to setup for her. When questioned why it was necessary as they did not follow their own protocol of scanning. They made an excuse claiming that paper copies do not need scanning. Another member of the group did not have a paper copy rather a digital and they did not scan. Also I've been to other establishments where my paper copy was in fact scanned. When asked why this was the case the manager Ishaan Sharma proceeded to raise his voice, and showed a loss of patience with my elderly mother. This behaviour is unacceptable, this man was very aggressive and argumentative. We decided not to stay and went to a different restaurant across the street. 
 
Be prepared to face aggressive staff on topics related to COVID.

The pour over was excellent, I think it was the best we had in the city. Also had the bourbon latte drink which was amazing. It's a really cool, open space that's relaxed. Barista was friendly. We'll be back for sure.

Pizza Delicious is just that, delicious pizza.  I feel like such an idiot when friends ask how I feel about Pizza Delicious and just exclaim, "it's delicious!"  The crust is thin, but has a nice chew and there is never an issue of finishing the ends of the crust.   I love the ever changing menu, but even when the amazing specials don't speak to my cravings the margarita is always a solid choice. The garlic knots are good, but the pizza rolls are even better.  How genius, pizza dough covered in cheese, pepperonis, broccoli or cauliflower rolled up and sliced like a cinnamon roll.  The cauliflower roll is by far the best and I always order one with my pizza.  The pizzas are huge too and can easily feed several people.  I'm literally craving Pizza Delicious as I write this, because, yes, it's that good!

Salt is definitely worth a visit. Great atmosphere, great drinks, great food, and a James Beard award finalist none the less! I'm sure I will find myself here again in the near future.

The Place: As you walk up to the door you feel like you're walking up to an old colonial mansion... because you are. This makes for a really great, unique space to enjoy a meal. Really enjoyed the vibe and had a good waitress.

The Food: Myself and a friend went for dinner. We ordered drinks first. The complexity was impressive. We both ordered a couple small plates and shared. All were great! I would recommend a cocktail (or two) & the gnocchi for sure. Was very close to giving this place 5 stars.

The Bathroom: The bathroom at Salt is GREAT. As you walk up the stairs the decor changes. The bathroom feels like a hunter's lounge. Pay it a visit!

Great breakfast spot! Best we've found in the area. We love home grown places with GOOD food and this is just that. Both my husband and I ordered skillets, which depending on which one you choose contain a type/types of meat, hash browns, veggies, cheese, and your choice of eggs on top. We got the american with scrambled egg whites and the Texas three way with scrambled. Each comes with your choice of toast, a short stack of pancakes, English muffin, or biscuit. We, of course, got the pancakes and holy yum. So fluffy!!! We got there at a good time (10:45 am) but about 20 minutes later there was a 40 minute wait. 

This will definitely be our go to local breakfast spot!

What a great food truck.  I haven't tried their brick-and-mortar locations because this is just a couple of miles from my house.

The carne asada and pork are my favorites.  They're perfectly grilled and served.  The salsa bar has no equal.   Overall, this is about the best taco and burrito place in town.

Honestly, their Sonoran dogs are good, but not my favorite.  Since I'm not a big Sonoran dog fan in general, it's no big deal.

Just opened and we've been twice. Steamed lobsters are good my only complaint is they offer them at dinner not all the time. Lobsters are priced equivalent to New England but appetisers and drinks are expensive however the ingredients are all natural (no icky corn syrup) so to me the extra $$ is worth it.
Still great! Friendly and good service. Great menu filled with all the classic diner-breakfast options along with healthier options.

I have to say I was slightly disappointed after hearing and reading all the great things about this place. Honestly, its was just OK , prices are high,and our server was "blah".  I wasnt in the mood for meat or seafood so asked if they had a vegetarian option....my own fault I suppose....I was beyond disappointed with what I got. However, my husband ordered the filet and lobster tail and he enjoyed it. Even though he was halfway done before the server came back to check on us and realized he needed the melted butter for the lobster tail...by then, why bother. I guess we will try again another time but not on my list of priorities. Overall, not what I had hoped for.

I really like this place! I love the "ambiance" of dining in - the giant fireplace gives it a cozy feel. They have a great selection of salads with all kinds of deliciousness (e.g., candied pecans, mandarin oranges, apples and bleu cheese - mmmmmmm), which I appreciate. They also have some pretty great happy hour specials on both food and drinks!

My husband and I ate here on Wednesday night for our anniversary dinner after being recommended by a Friend. We're so happy we did! The food was delicious, fresh and wonderful service! Our waitress Sherry was sweet, attentive and personable. We started with the cream cheese crab rolls and the steamed pork dumplings. Mm! They were delicious! Both fresh, hot and obviously homemade to order! Then we split the mango chicken with fried rice and the pad Thai, all washed down with a thai iced tea. The mango chicken was fresh and delicious and the sauce was full of flavor. The pad Thai was a perfect level of spice and came with both chicken and shrimp. The Thai tea is made by the owner, Ben, and was so good! Portion sizes were plenty- brought home leftovers, too! We are already planning our return trip. Excited to have a new neighborhood gem!

I can't say enough great things. The Avocado Toast is amazing with the crumbled goat cheese and pico de Gallo. The Churro Waffle which was so yummy and not at all overly sweet. It was perfect! Our waiter Jordan was awesome! Great food and great service!

Good service, molcajetes was good as well, everything ok not great not terrible. The dessert Tres Leches is more like a child's menu dessert really not good unless you want sweet condensed milk poured on yellow cake.  boo for $8 
Table side guacamole is much better at Besitos go there for great Guacamole not here.

Amazing stuff. I've never seen most of the menu options anywhere else which intrigued me at first, but it's the quality of the food that keeps me coming back. I've never had anything I didn't like here but the Toad in the Hole stands out as my favorite. Specials are always creative and delicious, the breakfast deal blows my mind, and the service is reliably great. The seating is a bit uncomfortable but it's kind of a smaller space with high turnover so it's really understandable. 

The only thing that confuses me is that pretty much every time I've eaten here, Weezer's Blue Album was playing. I'm not complaining, just curious. Once I stayed for a bit longer than I usually do in a restaurant waiting for a friend and it played twice. Seriously, what's up with that?

Took my wife here for brunch. I don't know if the food, drinks, or service was the high-light of the experience. Edward took amazing care of us and is a real hustler. He made sure we were well taken care of and if there are any issues he takes it personally and will hook you up. The food is fresh, savory, and unique. We will be back soon.
This is my favorite fast food! I do not feel guilty after eating it! Fresh ingredients and amazing taste! Always fast and friendly. Spicy ahi Tuna with crab meat! This is a must try!

We did not have reservations (our bad) and had to wait for 45 mins to get a table.. But boy.. Was it worth it!! The food was absolutely delicious!! Two of the most amazing dishes were the shrimp and grits and the chicken gumbo... Definitely a must try. Their cocktails are delicious as well. I loved the cucumber cocktail.. Oh so refreshing!! Don't miss out on this place and don't forget to get a reservation.

Gentle Giant is amazing.  Being a student in college, it can sometimes be hard to find vegan options that actually taste good.  I love coming to Gentle Giant for some comfort food, while feeling good that it's sustainable and not harming my health/the animals/the environment.  The staff is so lovely and always kind.  If you're looking to decompress and take some time for yourself, consider dining in.  It's a wonderful setup and you'll probably leave with a couple new friends.  Definitely give it a try!!

My husband and I eat here regularly, the food is good, price are good and the staff is good. 

My problem is all the many deaths that have happened while driving in or out of the parking lot. It is VERY dangerous. People speed down So. Virginia all the time, some people may leave after a few drinks or maybe a lot of the drivers are careless. But something must be done, soon.
A family member died last year and now in the last few days/weeks another friends sister in-law died. Please do something to slow traffic in the area.

I know nothing about Indian cuisine, but really enjoyed the quality and flavors of the Butter Chicken and Tandoori Chicken.  The yogurt and naan were fabulous also.  I appreciate that they offer delivery to our Eagle address, without having to use a delivery service.  Online ordering is very convenient.

Came here and ordered the Tex Mex Haystack burger and a side of fries with a drink. My total was around $13 which was a bit outrageous considering you order your food at a counter and get your own drinks, napkins etc. The food was ok, my burger was really salty, I think it was from the onion strips, so I took them off. The fries were very  unimpressive. Overall the food was alright, but way too overpriced for a burger and fries.

Very disappointed. I ordered the sauerbraten. It was a tiny piece of over cooked meat on a pile of red cabbage. There was so much cabbage on the plate it was in everything. My wife had the rouladen which was ok but it came with over cooked spaetzel. Very unappetizing. We ordered the sampler desert for $10. When I got the bill it was $13. I was charged $3 for a scoop of ice cream that I hadn't ordered. With a glass of wine and tip it was$73 for a very disappointing lunch.

What a terrible over priced meal.  The grilled chicken sandwich had no flavor and was fatty not much of a presentation that it had nothing on it like the picture on the menu.  I will never waste my money there again.
Does not uphold hours of operation. This establishment states they are open until 1am, but they left the business at 12:30
Great atmosphere and friend staff. I have had the filet steak many times and the blackened grouper or mahi-mahi was to die for. Also try the shrimp and scallops another excellent dinner.

Went with my friend who is a long time friend of Georges Perrier. Perrier personally cooked for us and we ended up having about 8 courses. It was my first time having pig's trotters and I enjoyed it a lot. I am very passionate about Foie Gras, and it was done perfectly. 

If you're not accustomed to spending that kind of money on food then you're going to be disappointed once the meal is over and the bill is paid. And remember, it's nearly impossible for a restaurant to live up to it's hype.

This is a really great place to go for special occasions. Or just to try it out before it's too busy to get in. The atmosphere is wonderful. With the layout and design of this place you can tell that everything was very well thought out and planned to create an inviting place for dinner or just an evening of cocktails. The food was heavenly and just a melted in your mouth with every bite.

This place is THE BEST!! I'm new to Delaware and my first stop was a late night 2am dinner here at marsh road (24hrs is great especially for night shifters). We had a very pleasant server the first time and the second time equally an amazing server. I didn't catch the First Ladies names but they were both phenomenal. (Linda was our server the second time, AMAZING!!!!) Great service and very friendly! 

Now to start on the food. For one it's quite inexpensive which is great but always iffy. Their menu is very lengthy and diverse so be prepared to take a while to even know what the heck you want. I feel like with any choice you make you won't go wrong! I had the Reuben melt, the buffalo salad, and I've tried the chicken roast with gravy. You get a bang for your buck and it's all fresh and delicious! The side salads are great, the side items are all delicious and the entrées have yet to fail me!! Delectable home cooked food. I'm extremely pleased. 
If you're ever in northern wilmington do me and everybody the favor and check out marsh road diner!! You won't go wrong. Thank you marsh road diner staff and management

You failed me Chago's!!  I was super excited for my first visit.  I knew they had pupusas on the menu and I was finally ready to see what they were made of. Well, pupusa you are not!  It was more of a tostada.  I was sad. :(  Things go inside of the pupusa, not on top of it!!  I left confused, what type of establishment are you Chago's??

Even with the pupusa debacle, I'm still willing to give Chago's another chance.  I'm sure there is something on that menu they do well and I'm willing to do the legwork to find out.  Until next time Chagos!

I enjoy Maxines, especially on a weekend morning. It's always a fun experience to bring people here... no one expects to come to brunch in a gas station. The staff can be a little mixed, some folks are great but others can be slow and the coffee is really terrible. But that being said, the waffles are excellent, I dig the egg sandwich, and you can't beat chicken wings!

This is my first time here and I am very impressed.  The prices are great and the food is exceptional and filling. This is one of the best in town. I had a carne asada chimichanga, and it was nothing short of spectacular. My brother had a chicken enchilada combo and he could not stop talking about it. The people are friendly and the service was good, so we  will be back a lot.

Loved it! I was wondering why I had never ordered from them yet as I stuffed my face full of the Drunken Noodle dish and Green Curry! So Yummy! And very happy that they had Thai Iced Tea with bobba as well!

OK so my in-laws swear this is the best breakfast in the city.  I was pleased.  Portions are huge, staff is awesome, parking is terrible.  The food itself was prepared excellently.  Couldn't have been happier.  Not sure if it was the best because it just didn't jump out and wow me.  If you get a chance you really need to go and try it for yourself but at the same time don't feel like your life isn't complete if you don't make it.

This place is AMAZING! 

If you have the appetite of a truck driver and don't mind having someone tell you what you are going to eat (There is no menu, it is one set meal for breakfast and lunch) then this is the place for you!!

I kind of like going in and not having to make a decision. (But you can choose if you want meat with breakfast and they have a few options. I HIGHLY recommend the bacon!!)

Usually for breakfast they feature their sourdough pancakes (YUMM!!) and perfectly cooked eggs (the chef, I believe his name is Nick, makes the BEST eggs. I always get over easy and he does it just right) ... On Saturdays they shake things up a bit. I had French Toast and excellent hash browns  last week and today was biscuit and gravy day.  There was A LOT of food! 2 biscuits and gravy, a pile of hash browns, 2 eggs over easy, and bottomless coffee for $7. My mom added bacon (enough to share with me!) and her meal was $11. Tax included.  

WOW!! It was DELICIOUS (as always! But my mom doesn't like sourdough so she isn't crazy about their pancakes. I love them. It reminds me of when I first had them in Alaska.)

Also, try the chef's killer homemade hot sauce. A little goes a long way and for those that like the heat, it is so good.  It is a perfect condiment for the hash browns and eggs.


I REALLY (really) LOVE this place.  I would give 5 stars but when they are busy, the wait staff doesn't know how to handle it.  Today for example they were working hard, but not working smart. They were like a chicken without a head. A family walked out because they didn't even have drinks after 10 minutes. I asked for the hot sauce and instead of just grabbing it for me (or looking to see which table it was sitting on) she started completely doing something else. (It is a very small place.) I know she was busy, but it would have taken seconds. After a few minutes I had to go ask the chef for it. (He is proud of his hot sauce and won't give me the recipe even though I keep asking for it.)

The chef (Nick?) Is a very friendly guy. He loves talking with his customers (but not today - they were REALLY busy!) It makes me like the place even more!! It is like an old time diner ... Just a great place. BUT IT IS NOT THE PLACE YOU GO IF YOU ARE IN A HURRY.  I can't stress that enough. It is a laid back kind of place with ONLY ONE cook!

BUT YOU HAVE TO GO! The food is AMAZING!

Listen, if you told me a couple of weeks ago I'd have an amazing meal at a restaurant that would completely blow me away -- somewhere off Telegraph road -- in a strip mall -- I would've looked at you like you were crazy. If you told me next that I'd have one of the best old-fashioneds of my life, I would have TOLD you that you were crazy.

But it happened. Hell-oooooo Cellar House!

We were in the area because we were looking at cars at Dave Sinclair Ford, and I was immediately intrigued when my Yelp app recommended this spot nearby. I am so glad we gave it a shot.

This place is dimly-lit with a bright, gorgeous bar, and seating is definitely limited. We lucked out with a high-top but it was the last one, so beware. I soon realized why they were so busy.

The staff was so friendly, and as I mentioned, wow -- the bartender knew his stuff. I was so impressed! The menu isn't huge, but is a nice size and has something for everyone. We decided to share the free-range sliders since they were $3 a slider for happy hour. Happy hour went until 7pm which was such a nice surprise! The sliders are topped with pickled onions and cucumbers, Vermont white cheddar, and house tomato-bacon jam. Yeah... they were as good as they sound. We also shared the "your goat's in my garden" flatbread, which was piled with herbed cream cheese, goat cheese, seasonal vegetables, caramelized onions, yellow peppers, crimini mushrooms, mozzarella, sweet slaw, and balsamic reduction drizzle. It was really wonderful.

I don't know how often we'll be back since it's quite a ways from home, but it was SUCH a fun, local discovery. It's 100% worth the drive.

I don't know how they can call themselves Famous.  There is a gas station in Dunedin that makes a FAR superior Cuban than this. 

Here's the deal;
I was craving a Cuban on a busy day at work and UberEats suggested Really Famous Tampa Style Cubans.  I ordered and food was delivered quickly.  I was so stoked at having a Cuban Sandwich/black bean and rice combo, I didn't mind paying $13.47 (plus tip) to have it delivered to me.  Maybe I had built up my craving too much, because I was very disappointed once I opened the bag and sat down to eat.  

The sandwich:  I went to pick up my sandwich and I notice that it was not cut all the way through.  No big deal, I went and got a knife and finished the job.  I try to pick up my sandwich again, and this time the whole sandwich and wrapper rise off the table.  The wax paper they send it in had completely infused with the bread forming a symbiotic relationship to prevent that portion of bread from being consumable (see pictures).  It was not cheese sticking to the wax paper, they must have put a hot sandwich on wax paper.  How could they not see this is a terrible idea and have chosen a better vessel?  Butcher paper doesn't melt, maybe aluminum foil... I love Cubans and have consumed many. The meat in my sandwich tasted like discount grocery store cold cuts, and there must have been a pickle shortage, because my sandwich had one sad looking pickle on each half. The bread was the best part.  Really delicious, too bad I had to peal so much off and throw it away. 

The black beans and rice: Bland

I repeat, I have had better Cubans from gas stations.  

Update: Next time I will check Yelp first and not trust Uber Eats.  I realize now that I am echoing a whole lot of bad reviews.  The owners should take note and make some changes.
So many beers available! And it was like a bottomless pit of mussels. I had such a great time here the other night. Wonderful atmosphere.
Good bar food, usually good drink specials and good options if you are trying to eat healthy!  Great beer selection as well if that's your thing.  I've been a few times and will go back!

Fresh, delicious and beautifully presented sushi in old city. This unassuming storefront is home to our favorite Philly sushi joint. 
Alex is the owner and head sushi maker and possibly the friendliest person I've ever encountered in a restaurant.  Nearly every patron walked straight to the open kitchen to embrace and greet Alex like old friends. 
After saying our hellos, we sent Alex a few samples of home brew along with some rare beer samples and were met with a warm smile and a sincere thank you. 
We were excited to see our much awaited special "the half n half" now a menu staple. A tuna roll topped with Ava ado and get this... perfectly thin slices limes. The line adds a bright pop of citrus and compliments the tuna perfectly.
Did I mention Kisso is a BYO?!
Romantic enough for a date, open concept great for meeting friends and counter seating overlooking the chefs meticulously slicing and crafting dishes creates a welcoming space for any day of the week.
Do yourself a favor and try Kisso, you won't regret it.

Hodak's, to sum up in a couple words that not only describes their food but their overall respect for Saint Louis patrons... Terrible with a greatest in awful. 

If I could compare Hodak's to a musical it would be the Phantom of the Opera because it is both alluring and frightening. We love the idea of an angel of music but in reality it is just a deformed, jealous manifestation of days past. 

Sure, your chicken was probably good about 25 years ago, when the dining options were limited, I mean it was the 90's, and Saint Louis had just filmed a movie about the end times in the film "Escape from LA." That's right, downtown mirrored what "dystopia" would appear to be, a lot like your food. 

It seems your "chicken" has won (awards), it's easy to grant yourself accolades, and maybe, just maybe, if you put all that hard work into your kitchen as you do in your parking lots, for invisible customers, maybe, you would be recognized on a national scale. 

Your pettiness, and obligatory nature make me vomit in my mouth as I drive pass that carnage you call food. I've had better food out of an MRE bag with a 100 year self life. 

Your staff is just as rude, your food is inedible and the very presence of this restaurant is a reminder that you are not apart of southern or mid-western hospitality, but part of a small minded, closed off, "where did you go to high school" mentality. The audacity to own all the parking lots, is a calling card for insecurity and self loathing. 

Instead of embracing other cultures and restaurants in the area and a place for people to park to enjoy the benefits of Benton park you choose to hire intimidating assholes to stand in a parking lot shooing people away from your competition. Your food should entice people, and your generosity should entertain all walks of life. But since your food can't hold a candle to even fast food restaurants you try to intimidate customers of other restaurants... well I have news for you, your self awarding asses can bugger off, because I'd rather park in the street and Uber to nearby restaurants then try my hand at your goons or your goop. 

I feel sad for the chickens that end up being destroyed in your mobile one deep fryers. You should have called your restaurant "repeats" because I guarantee you will taste it twice! All in all I wish I could rate you zero stars, because there is no glimmer of hope, you have destroyed all chances of it. I only pray that the chickens find peace in the next life, because being apart of Hodak's is truly hell.
My favorite restaurant in town!  Great food and friendly staff.  Irish bacon burger is delicious.   Perfect for families or if you want to grab a drink at the bar.  A gem in New Hope on North Main.

The Clay Oven is a FANTASTIC restaurant! This was my 3rd visit here and I will definitely be coming back again. I had the Alloo Baigan and wasn't disappointed! The vegetables were prepared just perfect, the spice was as I requested & the roti was fresh. 
The service was very friendly and attentive- we were immediately seated and had our needs attended to.This seems to be the only restaurant around that has Vegan options listed- many in fact! I highly recommend The Clay Oven for any & all!

45 mins for a delicious grilled cheese, and a bowl of soup.  Not sure, but you shouldn't make caramelized onions to order.  There's no other reason why it would take you nearly an hour to get a grill cheese, and soup to my table.

Staff was very friendly, made you feel like family. I had the brisket (very good!!!) and it was wing night so I tried some of them too. I had smoked wings before at other places and the skin would be chewy but at this place it was easy to bite through and had a good Smokey flavor but not overpowering. The pepper sauce that came with the wings was well suited for the wings too. I would recommend this place to all.

Good quality food, a bit pricey. If you like calamari as an app this is your place. They use large calamari steaks and haven't skimped me on serving size. My wife and I enjoy afternoon patio lunches here in the summer and watch the happenings of Main Street Speedway.

My experience went from 0-10 Thanks to tommy the owner.

Walked in, chose to sit outside. After asking if we had to order from the bar, we got a server. She seemed to be in too much of a rush. Was very attentive when we ordered our drinks. When it came to food I told her I wanted a sushi roll and she grabbed the menu and walked away. I wasn't done ordering and there were two other people with me. Didn't care to ask if they wanted anything. She just walked away. Like I also said I wasn't even done ordering myself. She wasn't organized as she didn't write our stuff down and forgot my friend's order completely. She sat next to her every time when my friend ordered her drink and food. She had other tables and I get it can get busy. I've worked at a sports bar before and I understand, but I also understand what good customer service is. My friend and I are both servers so we understand being busy. So when we go out we are not picky or needy. We get to the point to let the server be with tables who might not be understanding. 

Like  I said, it got better thanks to Tommy. He offered to pay for our tab which was not needed. My friends drink would've been enough for us! He wanted to make sure we would come back and we deff will.

I also got another round with a bartender named Kendal outside and she was extremely sweet and went out of her way to make me a mojito. She didn't have all the things at her bar, but instead of sending me to a different bar she told me it would be a second but that she would do it and bring it to my table.

So at the end of it all we were content (:

Went to Brio for a co workers promotion celebration.  I arrived a bit late but was able to enjoy the calamari app and a couple pieces from the bruschetta.  Both were very good, particularly the bruschetta.  Fresh taste, crispy toasts, simple but good flavor!

The people around me very happy with the entrees they had.  Pasta fra diablo with shrimp was good; angel hair w pesto was good; pepperoni and sausage flat brad was really good.  I had a pasta special over rigatoni with spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms in a light oil, pesto sauce with citrus.  I really liked it!

No desserts this time but will have to keep my eyes open on the road for other Brio locations.  Yes it's a chain but it's a cut above your traditional chains.
Always a treat to come in and enjoy the seafood. According to Stephen M., though, don't go there at or near closing time...hahaha

Great food!  Excellent service!  I had the crawfish etouffee and it was fantastic.  My wife had a shrimp poboy and loved it.  We're looking forward to coming back.  The only drawback is the florescent lighting.

Don't stay here if you expect to get any sleep. The walls are so thin you're able to hear everything from the rooms around you. I am currently staying on the second floor and I am able to hear every move made by the people staying upstairs. The floors creaking is driving us nuts. The rooms and reception are nice, and the decor is great but I will not be staying here again.

We opted for the Sunday brunch for our second visit.  We both agreed we prefer their regular breakfast menu.  The omelet bar was good, but the buffet options were lacking.  The biscuits seemed like they were from a can and overcooked, the gravy was lacking flavor.  The pastries were all hardened like they were old.  There was a very pretty shrimp dish served in a martini glass, but the flavor wasn't as attractive as the presentation.  We both agreed their regular menu was more impressive.  Service also seemed a bit chaotic.
The space is nice. We got beer and wine which were both fine. The chicken fingers seemed like other frozen chicken fingers I've had. The mustard dip made up for it.

Mercato is the kind of place 5 yelp star reviews should be reserved for. This Italian BYOB has some of the best food I've ever tasted and I can't believe it took me so long to try it. 

I went here for restaurant week and was blown away with all three courses. The famous artichoke lived up to the hype, I would gladly bathe in that sauce, but the calamari stole the appetizer show. The meat was so tender yet smokey on the outside which just went perfect with all the other components (especially the different kinds of olives). It was served like a salad and a bite with a little bit of everything was to die for. 

I tried both the short rib ragu and the pyramid pasta, both very rich and delicious. The gnocchi was shaped differently than I'm used to but those little ricotta balls were some of the best I've ever had. Amazing sauce that I was sure to soak up 100% with the table side served bread. You can't go wrong with the combination of brown butter and lobster/shrimp, I could eat those pyramids every meal. 

Dessert was the perfect ending to such a great meal. Both the cheesecake and chocolate cake won't win originality points, but the taste speaks for itself. The chocolate cake was warm and moist and served over ice cream, completing the knockout punch for my food coma. 

Our reservation was for 7:30 and we were seated promptly. We were on the somewhat rushed side but I was quick to forgive them as the combination of restaurant week chaos and torrential downpour shook things up as the outdoor tables were out of commission. Nonetheless, the service improvised and did a great job considering how small this place is. 

Can't wait to go back and try everything else.

The only reason I even left "ONE" star, is because you can't leave a review without one. I have waited a long time to write an honest review of this (hole), I guess I always thought to myself to overlook all the health code violations, and drunken staff being in charge of my "well-being". 
After tonight I know now it's ok for me to post the pictures I have saved in case this ever happened.
All establishments have health codes and violations. Such as "You cannot wear open toed shoes while working!!!"
It's disgusting seeing this establishment get away with no excise even present. I can speak from experience that there shouldn't be open- toed shoes, or drinking alcohol behind the bar, or bottles of booze covered as "mystery "shot?!!?
We realized very quickly after finding out we were out of place. 
Being a neighborhood bar....I worry about the neighborhood, and over serving.
Be careful coming here!

Best bang for your buck when it comes to the amount of food you get. I don't think anyone needs to order the extra large unless they're feeding a family of 4. I'll get the normal size and that's my lunch and dinner.

By far my new go-to lunch spot, since I just work up the street. Can't get enough of those pickled jalapeños. Thank you Hana Kitchen for bringing State Street some good, simple, bang for your buck, quality lunch food.

Ordered online for delivery.    Received email a7 6:43 saying order was out for delivery.  I live maybe 15 minutes away.  I called and the girl that answer the phone got frustrated with my questions and I guess put the manager on who quickly told me the order was on it way and hung up.     I received my order at 7:32pm.   Food was not even warm.  

THe thing is my house is under construction and the door bell doesn't work so I was hanging up front waiting for order.

 There are too many great restaurants in NO to deal with these people.   I won't be back in any capacity.
Ordered through Uber eats and they totally messed up my order. Even though it wasn't what I wanted food was really good! I'm very happy that it's open 24/7!

Lots of ingredients.  Sauce has good flavor.  But they under cook it.  The cheese is not only still white, but it's barely melted.  The ingredients are actually still cold!!!  Cook until the cheese at least starts to turn a little brown.  I certainly understand the average 2 star rating.

Overrated. Great decor, lovely staff..but the food was mediocre at best. I had the London broil, which was not great, and the twice-baked potato left a lot to be desired.
Should have tried the Mac and cheese..
Margaritas, however, were delicious!

Came here for a business lunch recently. I am usually a huge fan of tapas style restaurants, but the selection here did not wow me.

The place was next to empty at lunchtime midweek, which surprised me. Perhaps this is more of a dinner spot, I wouldn't know since it was my first time trying.

Neither of us were ravenous so we ordered three tapas dishes and a flatbread pizza all to share. 

The sautéed mushrooms in truffle oil were fantastic. Everything else I could have done without. The ceviche was extremely "wet".  It didn't seem fresh at all and we barely touched it. We also had the tapa-sized orange glazed salmon that was very dry and unimpressive overall.

The chicken flatbread pizza was very dry as well. Overall, I was just unimpressed by the whole thing. Lunch was not ridiculously expensive but certainly wasn't cheap for a meal I walked away from feeling disappointed. 

The space itself is beautiful with dark wood and high ceilings.  I'd imagine it gets some good happy hour and dinner action, so if I were to ever return, it would only be to check that out. Lunch is probably not in the cards for me here again.

Breakfast wrap grilled on pannini press, uh yes, please! We came back today because we had one last week and it was so delicious. I subbed out tomatoes for spinach, added mushrooms, and had gorgonzola for my cheese...oh my! Do it you won't regret it (assuming you like those ingredients). 

We split a side of fresh fruit. It costs $3, but it beats a load of greasy home fries (nice change up) and it was SUPER FRESH!

Lady next to us got the bananas fosters French toast which looked really good. 

The place is so small, so seating is at a premium, but the food is prices well and very good. If you can grab a seat or have a short wait it will be worth all your breakfast desires.

Our doctor prescribed a handful of vitamins for my son and recommended looking at one of the natural, whole foods type grocery stores for what he needs. Since Earth Fare was close, we chose to stop there. 

Typically I am all about doing my research to find the best price. However, my son had just received a diagnosis, and I had to much on my plate to sit and research prices. I just wanted to get the correct vitamins, at the right dosage, while all the doctor's instructions were fresh in my mind. Now that I know exactly what I'm looking for, I know I overpaid. 

My son's multivitamin alone was $27. Walmart has it listed for $17. On Amazon, if you put Smarty Pants vitamins on monthly auto ship and have at least 5 auto ship items, you can get it even cheaper than Walmart. 

I did appreciate that they have clerks stationed back in the vitamin and supplement area. One of the women came and asked if she could help us, shortly after we arrived. She was extremely helpful in finding exactly what we needed. 

The store is quite nice, yet a little dark in spots. The bathroom, however, was gross and in desperate need of cleaning. I've been to this location a couple dozen times since it opened, and their employees are always friendly. 

The cashier, this time, offered me a discount card and let me know that there were rewards for buying supplements. I had just spent nearly $60 in supplements, so I was definitely intrigued. Once I was home and settled, I downloaded the Earth Fare app and got my information connected with the card. This morning, I went back in and my receipt from yesterday had finally uploaded. They offer $5 off your next order when you spend $25 on supplements. But it's unclear if there is a limit. I can also see that I've earned the award, but it doesn't list what amount. So I'm unsure if you earn $5 for each $25 you spend or just the first $25. If it's not $5 for each $25 you spend, then their vitamins are definitely way overpriced.

The tacos were excellent! I had the Al Pastor, Baja Shrimp, and fish taco and they were all very good and flavorful. I ordered takeout which can sometimes be risky with tacos but these were delicious. I'll definitely be back when I am in Tucson again!

GREAT place to enjoy a casual and delicious meal.  I was visiting Boise and a friend suggested it and said it reminded her of Elephant's in Portland where I'm from.  It was kind of like that - but better!  Very cool vibe and I like the fact that the food is important but it's not the first thing you see when you walk in.  We ordered and shared a 
Croque Monsieur - BIG mistake!  We should have each had one it was so good!   Which means I had to have a whiskey pecan bar - another BIG mistake - so good I ate the whole thing!  Great coffee - great service at our table.

I accidentally left my wireless headset and when I called back 2 hours later, a good Samaritan had turned it in.  I got lucky - Stephanie the manager answered and went out of her way to make sure it got back to me before I returned to Portland the next morning!

I'll be back!  And you should go.  And don't leave your expensive wireless headset.  But if you do, (or leave anything else), Stephanie and the crew will do their best to get it back to you.

Thanks everyone - back to Boise in June - looking forward to seeing you all!

Checkers is the high point of culinary experimentation in North Philadelphia. These renegade chefs are whipping up a plethora of boldly flavored dishes and appetizers. It is difficult to imagine how someone could possibly pack so much perfectly viscous (and delicious) grease into toasted mess piles of bacon, toast and "burger." You may be tempted to go to the McDonalds across the street, and you also may be the dumbest person alive. These burgers are the bomb dot com. You like milkshakes? These milkshakes are the bomb dot com. You like weird semi-outdoor ordering areas? This semi-outdoor ordering area is the bomb dot com. Additionally, you will almost definitely be offered Oxycontin on market pricing. I don't know any foodie that doesn't like to "get his downer on" before feasting on the finest marbleized Kobe beef in this area. This beef is the bomb dot com. 

My only real problem with this location is the patio-style terrace seating outside of the weird, semi-outdoor ordering area. I can deal with the slightly-slower-than-average service, but this tiny seating area is really unacceptable. I had to listen to so many cars during my meal. Sure, the restaurant is located on the busiest street in Philadelphia, but I expect better soundproofing from a restaurateur like Mr. Checkers. Maybe they could put up a large bush or something? I'm not a sound-proofing expert, so I will not step outside of my bounds here. 

In short, come for the best cuts of beef in the northeast and stay for the drugs.

Beautifully remodeled place. I love the contemporary look and feel. Lady who took my order was very nice too. The only thing that I would suggest is to clean it up a little bit. The bathroom was dirty and window next to me was in stains too. Even though I got here in the morning the place looked like it was not cleaned after late evening huge crowds passed by. But people who work here are very nice and this is the most important to me.

Manager's Tirade Made Me Cry!

I hosted a large event at Sidney Street Cafe and noticed that I was overcharged by about $350.  When I brought it to the attention of the manager, Chris, he began to yell and berate me.  Even after I presented the original agreement he said that he "had been doing this for 10 years" and "does this three times a week".  I believe it doesn't matter how long you've been overcharging people, it's not right.  

He acknnowledged the agreement but said that my guests "ate a lot of appetizers" and he was "going to lose money" on the event.  (You can imagine, it was a couple thousand dollar tab.)

I'm a visitor to St. Louis, and don't know the area very well. The restaurant is on an out of the way, dark corner.  As I sat there, and this guy stood over me yelling, I was scared.  I didn't know if he was going to attack me or something.  Later he sent me an email saying that he overreacted.????

I would not recommend this restaurant.  The food was excellent, but the service has a reputation for being rude, arrogant, and in my case, mean.  I have never had someone add extra charges to a bill, or attack me publicly for addressing it.

If you want great service go to Tony's or Triumph Grill.  Both will give you a memorable experience, and appreciate your business.  I wish I would have listened to other review re: the poor customer service.

Good meat here, bread is alright. Exceptional service.

I had the Chipotle Cheesesteak. Maybe this was not the best thing to order, would probably go with a cold cut going forward as they seem to taste much better.

Ok so this place has become the order out spot on Fridays for myself and my co-workers. We had their fried potato greens with chicken, turkey, and today shrimp. We've also had their fried spinach (w/meat also) which was equally tastey. We've had their fish as well. I don't know what type of fish it is but it was seasoned to perfction and tasted sooooooo good! This place definitely gets 5 stars from myself and my co-workers. If you are concerned about spice don't be. It is a very tolerable spice. A little water and you will be fine. I'm not a person that can tolerate very spicy food, but I was more than able to tolerate all the dishes so don't worry. Everything always taste fresh and the portions are very generous.

The place inside is very small. So it's really only a carry out place.

They accept cash only from what I know and there is no delivery.

I really love this place and will continue to try new things from them.

Not as good as they used to be.....food is average.  I went on Thursday 9/21, and ordered the black and bleu burger. Burger was okay, not horrible but nothing about it really stood out either. They were out of potato salad.  No pickle on the side.  I used to really look forward to going here, but probably won't venture back for a while.

FLIES. FLIES. FLIES. I'm so upset that I reacted before taking a photo of the fly. Too busy barfing. When speaking to the owner she implied there were no flies in her kitchen. But a wingless fly was stir fried into my shrimp and pork fried rice. I received a portion of my money back, but for a gas station stop this one ain't it. I will never eat here again.

After eating here twice, once for brunch and the second time for dinner, I left wishing there was more. 

Brunch: We ordered a $16 dollar mushroom omelet, the mushrooms were the only vegetable component for this price, the only side included was standard toast. 3/5 stars.

Dinner: We celebrated a special occasion and told the restaurant in advance, but the waiter failed to acknowledge our event. We ordered the $70 dollar restaurant week special. Turns out that all four dishes including the main course were put on one plate and were supposed to be shared. Basically, there was nothing special about this deal  there was one appetizer, one salad, one main course, and one piece of cake. The service was good, not personable, but efficient. At around 855 the house lights turned on as a signal for everyone to leave, yet they were supposed to stay open until 930, felt like a nightclub during last call. 

Can't say we will be back.

I see this place has very high reviews and is well recommended and that's part of the reason I decided to go there for dinner last Sunday. I unfortunately did not have a pleasant experience like the ones I have read below. 
Honestly it's pretty simple , our service was below average. When I first arrived , my girlfriend was sitting at the bar having her first drink (waiting on me ) . After I got my drink I immediately cashed out because we wanted to sit outside . On our way out , we stopped with the host naturally , and let him know our plans to sit outside. We asked him to send a server over once he got a chance . 
We sat outside with our drinks for at least 25 -30 mins without any server coming over.  
The server in charge of the area outside we were in , had a table right next to us and constantly checked on them without glancing our way . Eventually, my gf decided to remind the host that we were outside and indeed needed a server. At this point it's annoying but still not a big deal.
The same server who served the table in front of us came over finally and her first words were "hey sorry I thought you guys were only drinking from the bar"

I found it strange of her to assume we only wanted drinks and not food but okay .( food was the whole reason we where there)  

Obviously there was miscommunication between the server and the host that had absolutely nothing to do with us , and I just found it quite odd , that after we have been deprived service for close to 45 mins now that's what her first words would be . Like mam , in no way , shape or form is this our fault . We still didn't have menus at this point so I kindly asked her to grab some. When she came back she explained to me that vaping wasn't allowed on the patio. The whole reason we sat outside was to hit our vapes . So at this point I have been deprived service and now I can't vape ( even though the whole time we were being ignored we vaped )
I personally don't mind the vape part I respect all establishment rules , but after like 45 mins of no service and then that .. we were pretty fed up . So we left 

I honestly would love to go back , again the place itself is so pretty and aesthetically pleasing but service really is everything . I do hope in the future the host , servers take their jobs more seriously, and don't take their own errors out on customers .

This place is the best sushi restaurant in SB. Their customer service is unparalleled. They make you feel valued as a customer, and the environment is delightfully unique. I got the dinner special which was delicious, affordable, and filling; it was incredibly worth the money. Their strawberry mochi is also delicious! I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a comforting, fresh meal.

We got the groupon before looking at the reviews, which were worrisome. However, we had a very good dinner. The pizza margherita and the sausage pizza were both very tasty. The waiter had good recommendations. Although it took a bit for the pizza to come out, pizza normally takes longer. One pizza is enough for two people. We're going back.

(3.5) ~ good overall food & service.  There are plenty of Tables & TV's at this location.

MENU:
** Provel Cheese Bites = (4) very good
* Toasted Ravioli(w. marinara sauce) = (3.5) good
* Egg-ceptional Pizza = (3.5) good
* Minute Maid Cherry Limeade = (3.5) good
* Cheese Pizza = (3.25) pretty good
* Deluxe Pizza = (3) ok

I have been wanting to have sushi in the city for a while, and this was one of the places with the most good reviews. I think they have SO MANY reviews because of their location, not because it is amazing sushi. I got the Volcano Roll and a Yellowtail Roll. It was very fresh sushi and flavorful, just not the best sushi I've ever had. The volcano roll was spicy, but did not burn my mouth. Oh yeah and I had miso soup, it was very good. Prices were what I am used to paying - glad it was not overpriced for their location. Service was pretty slow, that was the biggest negative for me.

We were visiting Santa Barbara from out of town and staying at a friends beach house.  We randomly came across Sharkeez and it looked like a good time so we stepped in.  The staff was very kind to us and showed us a great time.  Sharkeez was a fantastic start to a great night

I stopped here over the weekend, the place was packed!  the food is pretty good, excellent hamburgs.  The only problem was that most of the people were ordering to stay while I was ordering to go.  It seemed like those that ordered to stay were served first even though they ordered after us.

The setting was great and atmosphere was fun. However, we had very high expectations due to all of the wonderful reviews. The menu changes we understand but the menu we were given was not appealing. The dinner choices didn't have many options unless you were vegan. Disappointed we went when we did.

My friend and I were so excited when we saw this coming to our neighborhood because we love the truck. After weeks of trying to figure out if it was open or not because some days it looked open others it did not (website is no help) we finally went. We walked in and thee four employees behind the bar did not say anything. We finally just assumed it was "seat yourself." After sitting for 5 minutes with no one coming over (there was only one other table and one guest sitting at the bar) we were still wondering if we did the right thing. Eventually someone came over to bring us menus and take our drink order. 

We started with the apple sauce cheese waffle fries (not certain that was the exact name). We were very disappointed when we were served fries with basically nacho cheese with maybe a hint of something in it. Our flat 'wiches were decent but not anything awesome like I have experienced with the food truck sandwiches. 

Once again service fell flat when we waited for about 10 minutes after it was obvious we were done for our checks.

There are only two fast food place I go too. One is In and Out and the second is Chick-fil-A. The service, food quality, and price simply can't be matched by any others. Can't wait for the one in Sparks to open up next year! Love to see Reno getting better quality fast food options. 

Spicy Deluxe Sandwich, Chick-fil-A Nuggets, Waffle Potato Fries, with a Fresh-Squeezed Lemonade with Ranch and Zesty Buffalo sauces my go to order!
Great service, food, and atmosphere! If you're looking for a good hot dog, this is the place to go.

Ok, look...this is standard Mexican fare.  This isn't The Tamale Place where they can do just a few things and do them really, really well.  They're new in the building, so they're still trying to figure out the processes and logistics of getting patrons in, food and drinks to them, and then getting those patrons out the door.  So maybe you're there longer than you'd like.

But go if you need a bite and a beer.  Just know what you're getting.  I enjoyed my beer and enchiladas.

We stumbled across this grocery while walking around the French Market area. This an old fashioned Italian grocery dating from when the neighborhood was largely populated by Italian immigrants. We ordered the half mufaletta. Large enough for the two of us to split. Basically an Italian hoagie. Italian meats and cheeses with a savory olive spread. The roll was round and topped with sesame seeds. Fresh and delicious. They have seating and bottled beer as well. This sandwich was a welcome break after all the Cajun and Creole food typical of the city.

Woke up way too early this morning, so by 11 am I was looking for a big burger for lunch. Decided to try Brown Boxer on the south end of the Clearwater Beach strip instead the usual Frenchy's or Palm Pavillion on the north side. Super quiet at 11 am on a Tuesday so happy! 

Very sweet and efficient bartender. Juicy burger (1/2 pound!)with mushrooms and Swiss. Took awhile but I ordered it medium well - so I'm glad bc it was perfectly cooked. Only downside was the brioche bun a little stale, prob due to being first one of day, using up yesterdays. Mad I didn't get a pic for you yelpers, I usually try to. Solid sports tavern on the "quieter" part of crowded south beach.

Waited in line for an hour. While people who came in behind us were served ahead and only to be told there wasn't space for us yet. Considering the turn around and the fact that tables here can be rearranged, the front of the house staff only hustling when we asked questions is a sorry sight.  As someone from the service industry, keeping a party waiting for such a length of time with just an "a large table isn't ready yet" is pathetic. I can understand it's a Friday and it's a busy night. No freaking excuse for the surly attitude, horribly inattentive and blaze attitude of the hosts. 

I love the wings here and I'm sorry to say that we had gone at My behest. We would have been better off eating dominos wings at the food court in the mall...Will never be back. Wings were delicious and ultimately the sweet woman who was our server were not worth the front of the house crap service. If I could, I would leave no stars.
Cute diner , great food -awesome full menu.  I had the Bradley's breakfast sandwich -wow ! huge serving of french toast , eggs ,  bacon al in a sandwich of deliciousness !!!

Wow!  We just had the best brunch, delicious, non-rushed and well worth the money

Julian was our server.  He was very attentive and professional.

Since this was a brunch and you order off of a menu, we were concerned about how "all you can eat" would work.

Answer is it worked great. Julian came by to check if things were ok and offer more off of the menu.

They serve street tacos, certainly not Taco Bell, and delicious.  Everything we had was unique yet yummy.  "Gourmet Mexican",  what's not to like about that?

We definitely will be back!

You have driven by Fausto's a zillion times.  It's on the lower end of Vets just a few blocks from the 17th Street Canal.  It's a small little traditional Italian restaurant.  The food and service have always been acceptable but never outstanding.  I have been here at least a half dozen times over the years.  I have always thought the portions were a little on the smaller size, I don't think I have ever taken any leftovers home from Fausto's.  Don't get me wrong, it's solid but not over the top.  A very small, quiet atmosphere and very much the opposite of someplace like Bravo.
Food was cold. They dot follow covid-19 guidelines. Chicken was tough. Should be curbside only.
Omg yes. Delicious hot and tasty Thai noodle bowls with the perfect seasoning and spice in a fun food court setting.

Awesome little joint! Great for drinks and food after or before a hockey game! The food is great! awesome stuffed hadick for all you seafood fans! even better drinks! This time we had perfect service! quick and right! Spend our St. Patties there this year! No complaints here! Can't wait to go back again!
While visiting Nashville, I stopped her after countless reviews - this place was amazing!
Chargrilled oysters are amazing. Came at off time and got right in. If your in NOLA this is a must! Staff is super friendly & helpful.

Only the second time I've had Noodles and I don't know why I don't frequent there more often! They have variety of pasta options from asian to Italian to good ole mac and cheese. 

I tried the pesto with the pork this time around and it was right on point. Love the walk up and order with table service. A little pricier for a quick lunch but very filling!

Absolutely a big surprise! A welcome addition to Dresher.  The sushi was the best we have had anywhere.  Everything is fresh and the plates looked beautiful.  We tried the Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wrap (better than PF Chang!), Vegetable Tempura Roll, and a Smoked Salmon Roll.  Service was excellent.  We will definitely be back to try the many other temping items on their menu.

We've been here a total of 5 times and each time gets progressively worse. The first time was just my husband and myself, the food was great, the service was fast and we were pleased. The next four times were with groups of 4-8 and that seems to be the downfall of this place. Each time the service was slower than before and very spotty and the food took at least 45 minutes each time, even though there's hardly anyone ever in the restaurant. Don't even get me started on the terrible parking. The parking lot always looks packed, then you walk in and the place is practically empty. 

The one thing that has been consistently terrible here are their bar drinks. I hate to send things back, especially drinks, but I've sent back three drinks here because they taste like dishwater so now I just stick with draft/bottled beer. 

Now for a few good things - the restaurant is clean, and so are the bathrooms. The view on the lake is really pretty and they have a nice outdoor seating area that's pretty large. 

Overall, there are so many other options around here if you want to eat at a place on the water. Don't waste your time on their terrible service, mediocre food, and view you could get at 100 other places.

Solid 4 star breakfast. I would like to express one minor quibble- "CoffeeMate" is NOT "just as good" as 1/2&1/2 in coffee, and the coffee in a breakfast joint is so important. I asked for half and half and got some, ymmv. 

If it's about food, plenty of choices for gringoes as well as those of us that love the Mexican palate even if we struggle with remembering how to pronounce gracias. 

Nice people, give it a try.

Guacamole was great but we never got our food.  Very disappointed.  Waited over 45 minutes for the food we ordered.  We then went to pay for the guac and drinks we actually had. The cashier gave us some lame story about how our dinner had been dropped on the floor and that was the reason for the delay.  Ironically,  no one ever informed us of this while we waited for 45 min.  VERY POOR SERVICE.  We will not be going back.

We had heard a lot about this awesome sushi joint in Fairmount so my girlfriend and I decided to give it a try. We were greeted by extremely nice and knowledgeable wait staff. This place was byob which helps cut down spending on alcohol. We started out with the crispy rice, crispy Brussels sprouts and shrimp tempura which all impressed us. The shrimp tempura was better than Nobu rock shrimp! We got three of their specialty rolls which were all unique, cleverly infused with fruit and nuts, all of which were outstanding. We had just hoped for some other star menu items that were maybe more classic to compliment the other, more inventive items. We definitely would come back again and consider this a premier sushi spot in Philly.

We were in the area for a day (from NY) and decided to lunch at this place! The environment is very nice and inviting and the food is pretty good too! We got Sahara fries, hummus with lamb, mixed grill and a shawarma sandwich. I used to live in the Middle East and have had my fair share of shawarmas. This one is pretty good out of the ones I have had in the US. The portion sizes are pretty good too. We had leftovers! While it says its a Lebanese restaurant, I dont understand why there is an additional fee to make the shawarma "lebanese" style...Other than that, its pretty solid food. IF we are in the area again, we will definitely revisit!

Awesome vision, local supply and inspiration from the area, there is a reason for each item on the menu and it's fun to hear the stories behind the dishes! I've always had a really wonderful experience here. Twice we've sat outside, comfortable heat lamps and atmosphere, attentive service, delicious food and wine. 

Can't get enough of the RANCHERO SCOTCH EGGS! My boyfriend and I have always been impressed with the taste and presentation of the food. Really can't go wrong, vegetarian or meat lover, you can find plenty to enjoy. Cant wait to go back:)

When I last went to Roy's, my friends took me as a surprise for my birthday dinner. What a treat! My birthday also happened to land during restaurant week, another plus. This restaurant considers its food to be Hawaiian Fusion, whatever that is. There was an array of meats and fish on the menu. All the food was spectacular (I tried some from everyone's plate, my right as the birthday girl!)

The thing that made me love Roy's is the fact that they introduced me to the pure goodness of coconut ice cream. After I tasted their ice cream, I searched far and wide for another place that served the same deliciousness. I still have had no luck, not that I am complaining about having to go back to Roy's. 

UPDATE

I went to Roy's on Saturday for my anniversary dinner. Another amazing trip. I had the American Snapper. The most delicious non-salmon fish that I have ever tasted. I also tried the Mango Pineapple Sangria. Also amazing.
They have everything you need for a road trip stop. Food cooked fresh at their restaurant, and a good selection of snacks. They also accept EBT.

Hated the food... as an indian... the food lacked flavours and the authentic indian spices. Everything tasted the same. The salmon tandoori was pathetic with zero flavour. Ordered the papdy chaat and it is by far the worst that i have had in bay area and mid west.
Would not recommend, waste of money

Got to New Orleans before 11am and saw people waiting outside till they opened for lunch. Parked and walked over to acme. Got in quickly since it was only 2 of us and it was right at 11am. 

Server came by quickly, took drink orders, ordered half of dozen raw oysters, and half a dozen chargrilled oysters. I've always loved raw oysters, I've tried chargrilled oysters a couple times, wasn't a big fan. Decided to give the one at acme a try since their chargrilled oysters were known. 

Chargrilled oysters were good, but I wasn't amazed. I'll always be a big fan of raw oysters. For lunch I ordered the soft shell crab, which was delicious! My boyfriend got a crawfish po boys, he said it was good, never been a fan of po boys. 

Overall def a place worth trying when visiting New Orleans. If you like chargrilled oysters than you'll probably love acme's. Soft shell crab is huge and good!

Absolutely delicious! You can tell it's homemade. Loved how cute the interior was too. I tried about 5 flavors and they were so nice about it. I also loved how they were able to describe the tastes of them too which helped a lot! My favorite was the Pistachio Honey! I definitely recommend it or at least trying it!

We went here for a late night bite on a weekday. The bar itself is pretty great. I ordered a veggie grinder with garlic parmesan fries and my wife got a grilled cheese. Both were amazing and so as the service. The only thing I don't like is their bouncers. We sort of fell out of place and intimidated because the way our IDs were examined. He took it to the back of the office and he said he has to verify with his boss. I am not sure we will visit here again, although the food is good.

WOW!  Talk about a STRONG drink!! The bartender definitely has a heavy hand...which could be a good thing or a bad thing. So, yes, obviously, I like the bar here...hahah, but the food is really good too and very reasonably priced.  Guacamole is pretty awesome....and so are the tamales.  The set-up is kind of like a Chipotle or Qdoba chain

Hate finding myself in the minority when it comes to reviews.  Makes me think, what did I miss?  Did I order wrong?  Was it just a bad day?  What is wrong with my taste buds?

So, I had a bad experience.  Not terrible, but not good.  Came here for a quick lunch - just grabbing stuff to go for me and my girlfriend.  We called in our order and spoke to the cafe clerk.  I ordered a veggie wrap for my girlfriend (no problem when we ordered, but that came later) and tried to order a pork wrap for myself.  The clerk had no idea what I was asking for.  She asked if I wanted the pork sliders turned into a wrap.  Here's the problem - go to their website, and they have a pork wrap.  So I told her I want the wrap that is shown on their menu on the website.  She said they can turn the sliders into a wrap - so the pork, the cole slaw...anything else?  I said whatever the menu says it comes with.  

We show up and I grab the wraps.  Lets start with the veggie wrap.  The menu on the website mentions avocado, also arugula (I think), maybe roasted red peppers.  I don't recall it exactly, but it doesn't matter.  She got spinach and carrots.  That's it.  My pork wrap, which should have had roasted red peppers, a chipotle mayo, and maybe one or two other ingredients had pork and cole slaw that was drowning in mayo.  Not at all what we wanted or ordered.

When I mentioned to the guy who rang us up, he said that the menu was an old menu and they should probably update it.  Ya think?  This isn't a hard concept - we research restaurants and yes, we look at the reviews, but the reviews are meaningless if you don't serve something we want to eat.  So the primary reason we choose your restaurant is because we saw something on your menu we wanted.  You're essentially pulling a bait-and-switch; bringing people in with one menu and then serving something else.  It is complete B.S.

It isn't difficult - update the menu on your website.  How long does it take?  30 minutes maybe if you do it yourself?  5 seconds if you just need to email your administrator with the new menu?  This happens so often that it defies logic.

Anyway, one more bookmark for a St. Pete restaurant has been deleted.  Moving on.

I went to Shells after a morning at the beach with my father and two children. We walked in and were seated immediately. Our server was super nice and we were able to order our appetizer and kids meal quickly. After that was served my father and I ordered our main meals. While my children were eating the manager came out to visit and even gave them some toy sharks to play with. Our food was delicious and our drinks were filled when needed. They have a good happy hour and awesome food. Too bad we are leaving Florida today.
First time having a shrimp po-boy.  Along with the live music...I finally felt the vibe of New Orleans.  The service was on point and super friendly.

We tried Sage for the first time last night and it was fantastic.  I had the meatloaf based on other Yelpers reviews and it did not disappoint.  The appetizers were also delicious.  Our waitress was attentive and even went out of her way to find out exactly what was in the Thai sauce we had with our shrimp so we could try to make it at home. The wine was great and the atmosphere was hi-end but comfortable.  Not to mention, we got the best seats in the house.  I will definitely be going back.

Atmosphere is excellent! One of my faves in the city. Staff is always very friendly! Service is always great. The food is a solid 4 stars--wish they'd bring back the full menu! But I know Covid causes restrictions. Best margaritas in the city, hands-down.

This was our first time here and we don't know why we have never been before. The service was excellent and the tacos were great! The cholita margarita was so fresh and made with real juices not some premade mix. Their outside deck looks amazing and has heaters. I love that they have the option of corn or flour tortillas unlike some other places. The queso was so very good and instead of chips came with soft flour tortillas. All the tacos were so flavorful and delicious! Will definitely be returning! It was also taco Tuesday so tacos were $3 and pitchers of margaritas were $25. Based on the menu it looks like also have a bottomless brunch

My husband and I just ate here tonight and we really enjoyed our experience.  The service was great and the use of iPads to order food was fun and convenient.  The only reason I am giving this 4 out of 5 stars is because we found the food just a tad salty.  Overall, everything was great but it could do with just a bit less salt.

I highly recommend the chick pea fries, they are unique and delicious and the dipping sauces are excellent!  We will definitely come back again to try some other items on the menu, although I am pretty sure those chick pea fries will be ordered again.

Seasonal sangria, vodka cranberry, Makers and sprite --the bartender is good! Oysters were good, scallops were amazing! Wedge salad was the best salad I have had in a while. Filet was so tender, you could cut with a fork! Strip had excellent flavor  and cooked perfectly! Potatoes au gratin, creamed spinach and truffle fries were wonderful. They handled a large party of about 20 with perfection!

Been coming to his business since it was "horizons". The grilled Seitan  is out of this world. I have never had a bad experience at Vedge. He staff is always courteous and attentive, without being overbearing. Everything from the dirt list to the desserts are delicious!

While not up to the quality of the Memphis location, the chicken was well cooked and the staff friendly enough. I found the beans and slaw lacking the love that is needed to make the meal memorable; they bordered on the fresh-out-of-the-can taste that you get at lesser chicken joints. Overall, a cut above the pedestrian fried chicken chain stores, but not as good as I had hoped.
Summer rolls were tasty. Lo mein was great. Recommended by my sis and brother in law who live in Nashville. I wouldn't recommend the tofu again.
Sorry Arby's, your fish sandwich is terrible!! Soft, no crunch, flavorless! McDonalds is so, so!! Much better.....
SoFresh has really upped their game! They have more selections on the menu that are even better than before. I really recommend their Cesar salad. Excellent restaurant!!!
