Thankfully a second bartender started her shift and I was finally able to put in my food order. Ordered the pizzadilla and it was not as advertised. It came out room temperature almost like it was microwaved. The toppings on the pizzadilla were falling off like a pizza not ran through an oven would do. Food and service were subpar. I probably will never go here again.
Brisket was great,  the collard greens amazing and all the sides we tried were plentiful

Huge ripoff and difficult to deal with.  We couldn't get a reservation for two hours and they wanted us to put a credit card down and if we left early before the room was available it would be a 40$ fee.  Rooms are open yet they won't give them to us.  I will not be back here.
So many delicious items that you must go on Monday for the buffet. Be sure to have the cornbread. It's authentic and scrumptious.

Went for breakfast on a Friday morning and surprisingly it was packed, but only had a 15 minute wait. I got the Alabama pork biscuit which was okay. They gave me too much far on my pork, which someone may love. The ingredients on it were a good mix. The Alabama white sauce was tasty! The home fries were delicious too! It was early but I had the milk and honey sangria which was a great start to my morning and kicked off my weekend in Nashville.

My first time here and before I got my food I got a very bad taste in my mouth. 
The female manager started screaming at an employee over what  to charge for my order. No manager should scream at an employee as no customer should hear any type of unnecessary or negative exchange between employees. All the employee did was ask a simple question in order to do the right thing and he got screamed at for doing so. 
The employees are being verbally attacked by this woman who seems to enjoying her power trip. 
Today is May 4th and we arrived approximately 3:30 and left a few minutes after 4:00 so if this company cares about their employees they should dismiss this horrid excuse of a manager immediately !

Oh Sitar. You used to be my staple Indian restaurant in Nashville, and you've fallen short my past visits. 

I've been going to Sitar for years and always loved the food. However, I've been disappointed lately due to inconsistencies and sub par dishes. There are 2 dishes that I love and order all the time. The past 5 or so times I've had a craving for my favorites and made my way to Sitar, the food doesn't even taste like the same dish! I am fine with some variances (I like freshness!), but when I can't even recognize the dish (and it's not very good on top of it) I rapidly loose my motivation to go there.

I am sad that Sitar has slipped from greatness; I guess all that I'm left with are the memories.
you can't go wrong!!! reasonable prices! real good food!

Really a hidden gem. I usually come for weekend dinners and wonder why it isn't packed but I'm guessing everyone comes for the lunch Buffet. Really authentic delicious Indian food. Love their masalas and makhanis. Always fast service and friendly. My go to Indian place!

My wife and I are in town for a few days and stopped by for dinner.  The burgers were huge and filling. I was really surprised.  They had an incredible selection of craft beer and liquor.  Our waitress Alison was awesome. She had suggestions, was very helpful, and attentive.  We came back 2 days later for some drinks.  Great experience.

I absolutely love their 49¢ ice cream, but I'm disappointed that they took their chocolate ice cream. They're usually clean, but sometimes they're completely disgusting. I still hold them for high esteem for cheap food and snacks! I just wish they would keep on top of their cleaning, not becoming laxidasical.

I've been to the Tin Roof in Charlotte, NC many times, so it was kinda fun to go to the actual Tin Roof - as I imagine this was the original.  It looked identical to the one in NC.  It was fun, good music, dancing, busy yet still places to sit down and converse.  I'd come back for sure.

Love love love this place! You can't beat the rustic decor and romantic atmosphere. Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or simply grabbing brunch or dinner with a girlfriend, dining at this place is simply a must! Not only is the decor and ambiance amazing, the food was delicious to boot! I had the steak which melted in my mouth. I also highly suggest getting the truffle fries, yum! I wish there was something like this back in Colorado! If I'm ever back in PA, I will be sure to visit again.

Wow! What a great restaurant. I do have to start off by saying this is not your Saturday evening, go all the time Steakhouse unless you have money to burn. But for a celebration or once in a while it is a great place. With that said they do have burgers and salads and soups etc ..so it depends what you want, but if you are looking for steak, expect to spend a bit here. 

Now the ambiance is very nice. From the moment you walk in, it is elegant buy not so fine dining that you feel uncomfortable having just dropped in on an afternoon for a early dinner. The staff were friendly and prompt. Our waitress came right to our table and brought us water and offered cocktails when she saw me looking at the bar menu. The attentiveness of our server to our responses and how we were reacting to our food and when we slowed down and whether we seemed to like or not like things was amazing Tee ( or Tamia, I don't know if that's how you spell it but she goes by Tee and again I don't know if that's how you spell it but I told her my cats name is Tee lol so it's how I know to spell it) anyway she was a great waitress.

Onto the food. We got the fried Lobster bites as an appetizer and it was truly fantastic but part of what made sixnfried lobster chunks so amazing were these housemate shoestring potatoes that everyone at my table loved.

My daughter got the bigger sized Lobster and she said it was very good but after trying my steak, that is what she would get when we went back. I ordered a NY strip and let me say I have never ever eaten steak without A-1. Even steaks with sauces and butters etc. Our waitress told us I would not need it but brought me some happily....and boy she was right....this steak was fantastic. Cooked to perfection and so juicy and tender. The flavor was amazing. my mother got the Hog Chop and OMG this was so good. It had a great Kraut on it and a nice maple reduction and that sauce was truly a star. I can't even begin to tell you how great that chop was. 

We also got a couple of Twisted Shrimp and my mom and daughter each had one. These were offered as an add on to my mother's chop. They said that they were a little spicy but very good and if a dinner if just those shrimp was offered, they would get it.

Finally, dessert. A Smore tart of chocolate ganache on top of graham cracker flanked by toasted marshmallow fluff. And this was delicious. My mother got the triple treat with fudge and that was one of each of their ice cream flavors, pistachio, butter pecan, And vanilla with fudge. I ate the pistachio which was great. The butter pecan was the least favorite. But the chocolate sauce made for a great sundae my mother said. My daughter got something called a double chocolate gooey. We were told it was like chocolate gooey butter cake and this was not the cake. It was more like a half cooked brownie. If that's your thing, wonderful. Some people love the richness of brownie batter. I do in shakes and in little portions like brownie batter ice cream. But this was a large dessert that tasted nothing like described. My daughter ate what she wanted and left the rest. I explained my opinion to the waitress and she said others had also said the same, that this dessert does not taste like chocolate gooey butter cake, however they ....the cooks, owners....did not listen to the waitstaff about this and they needed to describe it like this. While I understand and appreciate the consistency and wanting food to be described the same way by everyone all the time, the description of this needs to be tweaked.

The food is big and thick and though pricey you do get a huge amount of food for what you are spending. You will leave full for sure 

I really enjoyed my meal here and am so glad that I continued to get the suggestions for Twisted Tree Steakhouse in my results. You will not be disappointed here

Not quite as outstanding as I once remember. Perhaps the success has gone to their head and, subsequently, the need to impress us waned. Nonetheless, in T Town I'll sometimes take what I can get and this is one of the best sandwiches

This is the greatest taco joint in Indianapolis....The Birria Tacos with Cheese are probably the great thing I have had in forever...I appreciate the service here it was amazing...The Chips, Salsa,  Queso and Chorizo were amazing....I love to listen to Mexican Music as well when I eat. It sets a nice calming mode when I enjoy fantastic food. I'll be back many more times...I would recommend it for anyone in Indianapolis..I drove 30 minutes to give it a try...You'll love it just as much as I did...The Wall Art is amazing too...
Best tasting menu! Service is more than excellent. Just enough food to make you full but not super full. Their hummus is divine!

This place has a fair amount of menu options so it is a good something for everyone.  My husband and son really enjoy the pho (me too) and I like that there is a variety for me.  The are very nice and are pretty quick in here too.    Thanks SK noodle!

I enjoyed this place a lot, it's much more than just a lounge. More of a club feel. They've got a great M-F 7-9 happy for half price all food, hookah and drinks. I can't say much for downstairs since we went straight upstairs. The service was a tad slow but my waitress was so nice I really didn't mind. There's tables and couches, a small bar, and dance area. It's really red in there as in lightning. I really enjoyed this place and would definitely come back.

I haven't been here for years but my daughter's dance recital was near by so we decided to go here after. We had around 10 people and we had a nice table set up. We ordered apps and dinner and was so pleased. The size portions were plenty but everything was amazing!!  We had family from out of town and they even loved it (hard to please everyone). We had left overs for days. It was great that it was byob. 
Can not wait to go back!!

I discovered this place a while back when I was in my phase of wanting to try all the local coffee shops I could find in Tucson. I don't think I ever completely succeeded that..., but I was very glad to have found Crave. 

Although it's a rather small coffee place that can fill up quickly during busy times, I have never felt claustrophobic or cramped. The seating is nicely arranged, so every customer gets their personal space The atmosphere is great. Very clean, mod, and cheerful. The coffee is top-notch quality and if you are ever in a hurry, they do have a drive through. They also serve a small selection of cute and delicious homemade pastries, desserts, and paninis. Moreover, the baristas are extremely friendly. 

I mostly came here to study especially on those days when I couldn't stand staying at the UofA library anymore or I just had to find a hide-out from all those distractions at my apartment. Outlet's galore! So, never had a problem with my laptop running out of juice. BUT I have to warn you, this place can get pretty cold! The owners don't seem to mind cranking down the a/c... Personally, I freeze easily, but to be safe, you should bring a light jacket. 

Overall, give Crave a go!

Restaurant was almost completely empty when I walked in at 5:45. I asked for 1. Was told I could not be accommodated until 8pm. I asked if I could sit at the bar and was told no even though there were plenty of seats. I asked the guy if he was serious and he said he was. Called him on his bullshit and said if they didn't want my money I would go somewhere else. He got all angry and defensive. The place was EMPTY! Will not come here again.

After I finishing eating somewhere else I walked back by. The restaurant still had many empty tables.

There may be fancier BBQ places. There may be more local legend places. But, for a consistently good BBQ, you can't beat Sonny's. 
I've been eating Sonny's for over 40 years. Yikes!
Started out with the Gainesville location back in the 70's when I went to college. 
The food has been consistent over the years and I have never had a bad meal there. 
Be it the ribs or the sliced pork, it's all good. The sauces have some good variety to them for a mass produced product. The Cole slaw is always a winner.

Some of my favorite pizza in town. Also always has great dishes ready to eat, I love the crabmeat smothered catfish. This place is literally a shabby dirty hole in the wall. But Nino & his son are almost always there & are so friendly & generous you forget all about the rickety tables & dingy walls. Never had a bad meal here

Salsa is peculiar, pureed something-or-other.  Chips are out of a bag.  Chile relleno was great!  Actually made on-site.  Frijoles also homemade.  Carnitas were delicious.  Rice is totally unremarkable.  Service was prompt and friendly.

So I was really excited to try this place as I'm always looking for yummy vegan options in town and I love supporting those places that provide those options. The menu here, which is all vegan, has some fun options. We ordered the croquettes and the schnitzel Sando, both of which were delicious! The bummer for us was that sometimes we choose not to drink alcohol but still want to go out and the only non-alcoholic options were cold brew coffee and kombucha. We would have been happy with the kombucha but they were out. No other options unless you want to get caffeinated at night. This is the kind of place people will come for the vegan food and not necessarily want to drink. They really should provide more options, maybe even a good non-alc beer. We were disappointed that it seems if you don't want to drink, there's not a fun option for you. It makes non-drinkers feel unwelcome. If they fix that, I would give them 5 stars cause the food and ambiance are great!
A French fry lovers paradise where your sandwich has fries packed inside and then served with another side of fires. Think a Lebanese Primanti Brothers.

I had been looking for tiramisu, noticed this place when I drove by and finally remembered to go in. I was not disappointed. It was available by the slice, entire cake, and a medium size package in a plastic tub, perfect for taking somewhere. I also got some fresh pasta, which was made that noting I was informed and should be eaten that night. The business has been here for 25 years according to the little Italian lady who does the cooking. They have an excellent selection of fresh pastas, ravioli, sauces & miscellaneous in addition to what you expect from a good Italian bakery. I'll be back.
Awesome!!  fun atmosphere really nice drinks ... pool, darts and diverse group of people. Loved it.... can't wait to go back!!

I only came to try the snoots....they were not to bad at all.  I believe next time I will ask them to put less sauce on them. 

The price was moderate for what was a large order by their standards.   Even though I felt I should have received more for $12.00.  The snoots were cooked very well, they stayed crunchy in the sauce and we're very fresh flavored snoots.

However,  the potato salad was just to seeet...they had way to much sugar in there as I could not taste anything else.  This made them the worst part of the plate.  I will not be ordering those ever again.

Parking was ample taste and texture of snoots great...but that's it.  A nice little place it is a bar b q shack...and I appreciate that.

I used to work right by Bo'diddly's, so I came here with a bunch of co-workers for a fun night of "Name that Tune." This game is fairly simple. The DJ plays the beginning of a song, then you have to try to guess the name of the song. Anyone could play the game--it didn't matter if it was only two of you or a group of twenty. Our group was considerably large and rowdy. What a few drinks do to middle-aged women--we had people dancing on the chairs and the table.

At one point, I was asked to "Name that Tune!" I knew it was a Bon Jovi song, so I said "Livin' On a Prayer." Then the host said, "You Give Love a Bad Name," that's right!!!" Huh? I'm not sure if he heard me wrong or was just being nice. There were also points awarded to the most "outgoing" teams, so there were a lot of dance-offs. It was completely insane. I am a very shy, reserved person, but even I was coerced to get up and dance, and I embarrassingly did the robot dance. I'll never live it down. There was one group of young, cool, and attractive people who were amazing dancers and guessed all the songs correctly. It was obvious they should have won, but for some reason our team won. We figured out that they must have been hired to create a funner atmosphere.

I also ordered some food here, but it wasn't that great. The pizza was bland and doughy. It was a fun night, but there are better bars out there.

Delicious Cuban but not traditional. Bigger, thicker and more like a poboy!

Got there at 11:25 and waited awhile during busy lunch hour. No searing - take out only.

Just your standard and expected chain location, but Mom loves IHOP so we come here every so often to feed her need.

The food and actual table service here deserve 4 stars.  The only "bad" experiences I have had here were because of fellow diners!

While not totally IHOP's fault, shouldn't the staff really make some form of effort to reduce the chaos??

My last visit, around 7pm, there was a very drunk lady in her 50's, blasting Van Halen tunes on her smart phone.  The staff ignored her, while all nearby diners looked around in confusion and quickly finished their meals.  This lasted well over 30 minutes.  No fun!

My previous visit?  7pm again, four adults let their 4 kids run wild ALL around the restaurant, throwing food, screaming, and causing an overall miserable dining experience for everyone else.

Again, the staff here just hid in the corners, ignored it, and did nothing.  The manager should have taken some form of control.

To conclude, we almost consider this place "Dining with a free show" here now.  Joker's wild.  Calm or chaos?  Roll the dice and take a chance?  Eh, no thanks...

I think I will take Mom to the new nearby IHOP location and hope we have a better experience and hope there is some adult at the helm!

I love Radish Kitchen! I have been a few times now and it's delicious. I feel like I am making healthy choices when I eat there. Thank you Amanda Frederickson!

I really want to build my own but I've ordered the Rad Thai every time. It comes with grilled steak, napa cabbage, mango, toasted almonds, mint, and a jalapeno ginger dressing. I honestly just want an extra serving of the dressing. It's the perfect pairing! It adds the flavor the bowl needs to soak into the napa cabbage. Would I like a little more mango? Of course. Who wouldn't? The steak is cooked nicely and it's not dry and right consistency of chewiness. The grains were great and napa cabbage was fresh with a light crunch.

I've had their lemonade and my friend ordered their tea and Rad Cobb. We were pleased with the drinks. They taste pretty standard. Shout out to the ice. I LOVE cubed ice aka Sonic ice. If you know, you know. 

I honestly want to try the Falafel Fattoush + baked crispy chicken. Who is with me? I also want to build my own but feel that I would try to add everything. I'd like to go back and try the wrap as I've always gotten a grain bowl.

They are social distancing and have tables blocked off so no one is close to each other. My friend and I ate outside and had the entire patio to ourselves. It was awesome! I look forward to coming back and working my way through the menu.
Solid Vietnamese restaurant, and really affordable too. I was definitely surprised to find this place right by the hospital.

The first and absolute worst experience ever! Couldn't find anyone to help us find the check in area. Then we couldn't find our room! We were told to wait for the one and only bell hop. I am Handicapped and had to call security to use the wheelchair elevator. Waited 15 minutes for just one time! Finally found our room. No microwave, no room service, windows don't open. Had to figure our way out to find food as the food court was closed except for pizza! Will NEVER stay or go there again!
The service is always amazing. The bang for the buck is amazing. The food is amazing. I make a special trip here every time I'm in town. Keep up the great work guys.

I love the atmosphere of Willa Jean on a sunny Sunday morning or afternoon! The sun shines through the big windows and it's so beautiful. I loved the veggie grain bowl. Would definitely go back for this! Perfect light breakfast. The hangover bowl was kind of salty, although the grits were really good! It also lacked a bit of texture as the grits and the brisket were soft. You can also grab a coffee or pastry from their cafe while you wait for a table.

Sunday Brunch Review: 

The short- My brunch was meh... I wouldn't come back. Jazz music is nice, wait staff are all very nice, but food leaves little to be desired. 

The longer- we came for an 11:15 am Sunday brunch. I made the reservation on open table. This spot is in a very touristy area near the French market. We were seated in the mezzanine area & the air conditioning was BLOWING. I had to wear my coat. We shared a caesar salad to start. It was good, but nothing special. We also considered the $15 unlimited mimosas (my kinda dealllll), but decided to go for the unsweetened iced teas. 

I ordered the crab cakes and poached eggs with hollandaise on the side. My eggs were cold and over cooked. The crab cake was mushy. My boyfriend ordered the crawfish & andouille omelette & it was loaded with shredded cheese.

Pretty disappointing meal, overall... and our waiter was good but the service was SO slow. I have had way better meals in NOLA and wouldn't come back here.

It was Friday night, and yes, they were busy. They might need some more staff, but it should have been manageable and things should not have taken so incredibly long. Our server was great but seemed to be stretched too thin. Burgers were fine, Italian sausage was not what was expected, but it was tasty. The environment is very nice, the drinks are WAY overpriced, and the food is just okay. Don't think we will return anytime soon.

I came here since it was a restaurant on The Hill.  It was starting to rain so I had to make a decision quick before I got soaked.  We went here, and it was OK.  I had the fried ravioli, which was great.  The food was OK, not great but I got what I paid for.
Authentic diner.  Food was excellent and coffee was just what I was expecting.  Try the scrapple if you eat here.

This is a really good Mexican restaurant in the neighborhood! I would take my friends and family.

I placed an UberEats order for 3 Pastor Tacos and a Tamal. I did put a note to not add onion to my tacos but when I received them they had onion (main reason for the ding). The tamal was also warm when it arrived, but it was cold by the time I finished my tacos. I felt like the tamal was too dry (but again, it was cold when I started eating it).

I was very impressed with the flavor of the marinated pork, and 3 tacos for less than  10, you can't beat it.

Place was like stepping back in time.  Beautiful interior, some may consider dated, but I found it amazing.  Prices seemed high, but servings were huge!  Worth every penny.  Waitress was very friendly and felt like I was being served in someone's home.

I've been a customer for a while. The soup is usually good, but tonight I ordered two large crab bisque and a small spring salad to go. Soup is normally $4.75 (it's supposed to be anyway), while the small spring salad is $4.75. Gourmet soup is supposed to be $5.00. I guess you could classify crab bisque as gourmet. The total should have been $14.75 plus tax, which would have made it $15.64. I was charged $17.81. 

I wouldn't normally make an issue of such a thing, but I've noticed this seems to be a pattern here. Prices here seem to vary from one day to the next, even when ordering the same thing. There's a bald guy behind the counter who usually man's the cash register and I've called him out on this before. He made some lame excuse that he thought I ordered something or other that is more expensive than what I actually ordered. Just dealing with this guy makes my skin crawl. 

Tonight he did it again. I don't normally order crab bisque, but tonight I did. I figured they must charge a premium for the bisque. Well, they shouldn't, because I probably could have gotten better crab bisque at the Wawa next door. I called down then to ask what kind of soup they have and ask how much the crab bisque is, and I was told it's $5.00. I'm hesitant of ever going back there again because I hate the fact that they would take advantage of a loyal customer. 

Buyer beware. If you happen to go, I'd definitely watch out for the bald guy, because he's shady as F***!

Took 1 hour 15 min to get 2 pizzas and wings, I live 8 min away by car, they texted me that it was out for delivery but did not get until 50 min later.......why did it take so long? You call and get rude service, they keep u on hold. The wings were missing half the breading and was smashed, the pizza was good but not worth all the hassle, will not order from them again.
This place is my favorite in the city, awesome steaks and their cheese fries are perfect. I always take friends from the burbs or out of town here. They all love this place.

Pub n sub is great. It's locally owned and they use some of the best ingredients. It may seem expensive at first, but it you go on a special day it's an amazing deal. You get so much food for so cheap. It's also really good for vegetarians, because there are quite a few options on the menu. Some of the ingredients seem like they shouldn't go on a pizza, but don't diss it till you try it. Try one of the pizzas that are house specials, you won't regret it.

I am a Barbeque snob. I was born in Kansas City, and have chef's throughout my family. Enough about me. This is not KC Barbeque, but in the City of Indianapolis, Andre's is easily in the top three if not the best all around barbeque in the City (Squealers and Hanks Brisket are my other top picks).  If I was to recommend anything it would be their pulled pork (best in Indy and flavored like no other) There sides are pretty amazing, and The ribs are really good (I prefer the tips, but I like to take my time.)  If you want to try something unique and delicious be sure to get the Burnt End French Fries. The large is a meal in itself, and will have you "fired' up for the next few hours.....no need to sit around a campfire.

I was really excited to try this after the reviews.
I had the banana leaf chicken. I was really disappointed. The rice smelled and tastes really bad and the flavours didn't work together at all for my palate. I'm also ordered the beets and they were amazing. I would try another dish next time.

I really didn't know what to expect when I walked into what can only be described as a pizzeria-turned-bbq joint. The smell of delicious meats was evident in the parking lot - good sign! I ordered a half rack with beans and fries. I was really REALLY afraid that the ribs would be chewy, under/overcooked or otherwise lackluster but boy was I completely wrong! These ribs were moist, tender, spicy, and lean. 4 great qualities of perfectly smoked, perfectly seasoned ribs. As an added bonus, the place apparently makes their own variety of bbq sauces. The bbq beans were excellent and were definitely more thought-out than a typical side dish. Honestly, this place (for me, anyways) is right up there with the best BBQ joints in NYC and some of my favorites down south in Atlanta. Some of my coworkers had the brisket which also looked awesome, and they seemed very happy with their meals. I smoke ribs on a 40" smoker and I am not easily impressed but BBQ BBQ has won me over as a customer.
Awesome food great service nice area pretty facility.  one of the best brunch places i have been to in Tennessee.  very healthy food choices also

Really cool, unique restaurant! 

My sister and I got the "damn good nachos" which were damn good and big enough to feed 4 people. Eating it was like attacking Mt. Everest, if the Himalayas were delicious and loaded with pulled pork, jalapenos, cheese, etc. We also got the "taco trifecta" with scallop, calypso beef and flaky fish plus a side of coconut rice. All 3 tacos were good, I did think the scallop could've been cooked a little more and the beef could've been a little more tender, but still good and nothing at all like the Mexican tacos I'm used to back home; these definitely have a Caribbean slant to them. I especially liked the tzaziki-like sauce that was on the flaky fish taco. The coconut rice was excellent and incidentally the waitresses are all pretty.

Next time I'd probably get a cocktail as they looked amazing. Like other yelpers have pointed out, avoid this place when there's a Saints or LSU game going on. Parking is tricky as well.

I forgot how good this place is!  It's been years since I've been here, and a friend invited me last night.  I didn't want to leave.  The grounds are so inviting and calming, the sky was beautiful.  I love looking at the fish in the coy pond and the peacocks.  The outdoor is so big and nice, and the indoor seating is nice as well.  We went on Thursday, which is vegan night.  The buffet was fantastic!  The salad ingredients are so fresh, and I love the dressings especially the walnut one!  Everyone had plates piled high, and there's no guilt because it's mostly veggies!  I love the flavorful rice, and the vegan tacos, all of it was fantastic!  I really need to make it a point to come here on a more regular basis!

I had soup with pinapple and pork, I'm not going to even try to remeber the name of it much less spell it. Just know this...If I could fall face first into a bowl of that soup and drown, I'd die a happy happy girl. The food was execellent, portions large, and service very very friendly. I will be back here soon.

The food was great and service with a smile but the wall in our booth was covered in dried food and 2 dead gnats.   They need to sit in a booth and see what the customer sees.  Wash the walls and the moulding and this place is a 5.

This Starbucks is a little difficult to get into due to the small and busy parking lot. It also does not have a drive-thru. However, they are always very fast and efficient on the inside. We have never had service issues at this location. I typically order an Iced Vanilla Chai and it comes out perfectly mixed (it can be grainy if done incorrectly) and delicious every time.
the wervice was terrible expresso machine was very visible they did not know it was there paid $13 for two cups of espreeso the cup was ssooo big and a drop of coffee in it. very dissapointed.

Great location right on the bay, the guy that play live on the patio is so good I thought it was a recording untill I saw him on my way out LOL service is good, drinks are ok, do not eat here unless you are starving.. there are so many option in the area with much better food
Stayed in the hotel across the street. First time to the restaurant. I had a steak kebab. It was made to order and had great seasoning.

I have only had good experiences at this place! I've gotten the same waiter twice (Rigo) and he is so attentive and friendly! I got excellent service at the bar (the margaritas are so good!!!) My husband and I got the Texanas fajitas and they were delicious! This will definitely become a frequent spot!

This is for those folks who don't want to drive to the city for a real steakhouse. This imitation of the Palm falls short in many ways. The Steaks are below average and this place has no idea of aged meat as stated on its menu. On our recent visit,  the meat was over cooked as to what we ordered, leaving the meat dry and not pleasant. The staff does a good job to please, but overcoming the pit falls of the kitchen is a challenge. Try  one of the great steakhouses in Philly, it's worth the trip. Capitol grille, Del F or Union Trust are much better.
Disappointing food compared to how awesome the joint bar is. Come for the drinks, not the food.

Kelly is awesome at knowing what new wines I will like every time I stop in. The flatbreads and the pear bruschetta are amazing! I live 4 hours away and it's always a treat for me to go on a road trip to visit this restaurant for wine and a great meal.

THEIR BLOODY MARY'S ARE AMAZING. This Ruby Slipper is the perfect location because it's just a little away from the main busy streets, making it a prime location for a nice quiet brunch. The food was amazing, definitely recommend the Bloody Mary's though.

It's the BEST Vietnamese restaurant on the north and northeast side!!!

Sounds like a resounding endorsement, except it's the only Vietnamese restaurant (that I know of) on the north and northeast side. Yes, that's what we're down to. There are 5,000 chain restaurants on the north and northeast side and one Vietnamese restaurant - chain or not.

I often wonder how they stay open. Without exaggeration, there are typically twice as many people on the waitlist at the very meh chain Outback Steakhouse two doors down than there are inside Viet Bistro. It's a shame.

The food is pretty good but nothing special for Vietnamese food. Why four stars? Because you have to go to the west side or south side to get better Vietnamese food, and that's 30+ minutes away. And pretty good Vietnamese food close to my house is still better than the crap at the ubiquitous chains smothering Indianapolis.

The pizza was very tasty and the service was great. We ordered pizza for pickup and when we picked it up we were able to quickly get our pizza and it was kept in a warmer so it was nice and warm when we received it. Also good value for what we received.
Everything was beautiful and delicious. delicious. Service was amazing. Loved everything about it.  Delicious deserts too.

Second visit was not as good as the first! I had the ribs this time. Very good but way too much rub. I had to scrape it off as it was overpowering the meat. My daughter had the smoked duck. She enjoyed it but when she tasted the brisket she liked the brisket better. The Mac and cheese was way to dry and did not have much taste. FYI, I can share my Mac and cheese recipe, it's the best!! Had the sweet potato salad, which I also make, I enjoyed that. The creamed spinach was a fail. Needs some onion and spinach needs to be chopped and creamier. Taste was not there. Also noticed customers leaving it on their tray, not a good sign. Also I think the slices of pie are priced to high at $5 a slice. The cole slaw is the best!! I will be back to try some more. It's gonna be hard to beat my smoked pork butt as I use the APL recipe and its the bomb!!!

Great vibe at this place! Loved the crowd, not overly "hipster", very cool decor. The food was great, definitely a lot of new flavors. Shells and paneer was amazing! Great vegetarian options. I had the salmon entree and it was great. Pretty good beer selection, the night we went they had some Zombie Dust which was great. Waitress could've been a little more friendly and attentive to our questions considering I hadn't ever had or heard about 80% of the menu, otherwise it was great. Definitely will be back.
Very very good ... def a wait on the weekend ... but so worth the wait !!! Glad we found this place !! Everything was so good

This place is all hype. Coffee is mediocre and the staff seem to like to gossip and chat other than do their jobs. The dishes sometimes are dirty and the food, despite being expensive, is bland and presented in a very amateur way. Honestly you're better off just going to Panera. Same style etc. Not recommended.

I've been here numerous times for the food and the service. Rarely do you find a local pizza place that cares so much about the community it serves. The owner is a cool dude, the staff is great and friendly, and the prices aren't too steep.

I have two thumbs and another appendage up - because it makes me that excited.

Not my favorite pho. I found it bland. Also, when I called in the order, I was told 30 minutes. I arrived at 20 minutes, and my food had already been sitting on the table for awhile I feel. I had to warm it all up again when I got home.

I usually try to write more in a review.. but I want to make sure I keep this short and to the point so people don't glance over it. 

BEST.. BURGER.. IN RENO!! Always cooked right and doesn't break the bank. 

Pro Tip: Park by the sporting book section on the back side of the Atlantis casino. It is the fastest route to the Deli.

Unfortunately, I am giving this restaurant a negative one star.  I used to go there quite often until I find out they always short on inventory and lack of customer service.  
Last time, I took my lunch break, ordered a vietnamese cold cut sandwich to go. The cashier said that they were out of the cold cut sandwich meat.  So, I've ordered a  chicken sandwich,  then the cashier said the lady who make sandwiches won't be back until an hour later, can you come back? I replied my office lunch break is one hour, let's order something else.  The cashier said Pho noodles will be available in 15 minutes, then I ordered one to go.  15 minutes pass by, the order has not come out from the kitchen yet while they only have two tables of customer were eating at the restaurant. The cashier kept saying my order is coming out soon.  I was waited and waited, after a 45 minutes of waiting, still nothing has coming out from the kitchen. I have to go back to work with an empty stomach.  I am done with Pho Bensalem!

Words are inadequate to convey how much I love Downtown Kitchen's happy hour! The HH food is soooooo goood and cheap, with a beer for $2.5. I have tried pretty much everything on the happy hour food menu, all delicious. The absolute stand-outs for me are: oaxacan fries, fish and beef tongue tacos, and crispy calamari. The J Dawg and Downtown burgers are huge, only for $3.5 and $7 respectively--totally a meal in and of itself. While frog legs and bone marrow are not your daily happy hour type of food, it certainly pleases a more daring crowd. Food heaven is what my friends and I use to call this place after a happy food coma.

For happy hour, you can sit at the bar or outside patio. But with the weather being so nice out right now in Tucson, I don't mind a single bit.

Worst service I have ever had. The server was not friendly at all. When he brought the calamari, he never came back to see if we needed anything. Had he come back, we would have asked for salt and lemon.
The creole pasta was good and the red beans and rice was okay.
After we received our meals, our server never asked if we needed anything, like more water or drinks.
After waiting 20min for our check, we had to ask one of the managers for it. Our waiter finally arrived to collect our credit cards and split our check down the middle, he returned trying to charge us each $58 for a $77 total bill. Had to wait another 5 min for him to return with the correct bill. Because of the poor service we will never come here again.
Fast service, dog friendly, food was delicious and well priced. Convenient location to explore Dunedin. Would come back again.

Let me start out this review by saying that I love Bonefish. This bonefish though, I do not love. We started out the night by not getting waited on for 10 minutes. We then ordered a bottle of wine, some waters, and some ahi tuna. (The Ahi Tuna was good) We were served the Ahi Tuna before we were even served waters or our wine. Next, we order the steak and crab cake entree each. We both order medium rare. How do our steaks come out? Well done. Bonefish apologizes and sends them back. How do they come out? Both raw. We send one back just to see how it comes back and low and behold it comes back well done. The incompetence at this store is outstanding. I strongly recommend not to go to this bonefish.

Our group of five waited over 1 hour 45 minutes for our food, while several groups of people who came in after us got food, paid for it and left. We had reservations but our waitress kept saying she would be right back, and explained at one point in time that another group knew what they wanted right away. That was 30 minutes after we arrived for our 4:30 pm reservations. She basically forgot what we asked for with drinks and appetizers. When our food finally arrived it was lukewarm. And when we complained, the chef said every meal is cooked to order and started to argue with us. There is no excuse for us to have been ignored by the staff. If the food was cooked to order, why were all of our dishes lukewarm?  The only reason I am giving this one star is that they comped our dinners for us.

Ok so I spotted the sign coming down Virginia and went into search mode as I can never say no to tacos . First the man and his wife are super friendly . Decor is cool and the pink doors are a nice touch . I ordered 3 tacos al pastor and they were loaded with meat very good savory and sweet mix and the onions weren't huge the Chile wasn't to spicy but I would of liked a little more burn . My wife got 3 taquitos and the were stuffed with very soft and seasoned chicken . My only complaint is one tortilla with that much meat makes it almost guaranteed to fall apart but I'm still gonna eat it . I will be going back to try a torta and try the carnitas . Support this place they try hard and the food is good .

One on my most favorite restaurants in all of Tucson. I'm both a fan of the main restaurant and the small sushi side.  However, service on both sides is inconsistent (especially on the sushi side).  I think they should add more servers during peak busy times, as the servers seem to regularly be frazzled/over loaded.  To be honest, it's the food that keeps me coming back.

The main restaurant recently added servers (previously you ordered at the counter), which is fine, although they still seem to be working out the kinks.   I would recommend the veggie udon, Yoshimi's Favorite salad, ginger tofu or any of the bento boxes.  The Japanese pizza is also pretty good.  They have great lunch specials for under $10.  The food can take a while to come out.  On more than one occasion, I've waited, at most, for 20-25 min., so beware if you're starving or in a rush.  

The sashimi from the sushi restaurant is super fresh and melts in your mouth.  Their sushi is reasonably priced as well.  Yummy squid salad and a nice selection of traditional and inventive rolls.  

The decor is unique and inviting.  They always have fresh flowers on the table, which is a nice touch.  

Overall, this place is definitely worth a visit.

I bought shrimp lo mein there for lunch. The portion was very small for the price. Most Chinese takeouts are big portion. 

Also, the lo mein was not even that good. So not going to come back again...

Clean store, and lots of helpful and outgoing employees.  They must have a great training program for their staff.  Teenage kids seem to be everywhere, and they are delightful--really interested in doing a good job, which is nice to see.  Excellent wine selection, good prepared foods.  Would really like it if the produce were more reasonably-priced.

Biking downtown SB at 3P on a Saturday on State and saw a big placard sign for happy hour 2-6. Locked up the bikes and took a seat. Asked the first server for the happy hour menu. He grabbed it and on his way back was intercepted by a female server. Couldn't hear the convo but can guess it was something to the extent of we don't offer HH on Sat. I ask her for the hh menu, and she tells us  they don't have it on Sat. I point to the giant sign that says happy hour 2 - 6p. She says she told someone to take it down but that it says Sun - Thurs. I told her it didn't say that, walked over and checked again. Sure enough, all the sign says is Happy hour 2 - 6p with some adorable swirls and stars. I reiterated that the sign brought us in, and did not say anything about days...asked again for hh pricing. She says no, then goes and grabs the sign (quite easy as it's portable....). Awesome false advertising. Awesome never admitting fault, blaming me for not reading the Sun - Thurs that wasn't there. I guess I have a problem reading invisible writing, I should get that checked. Walked out. Thanks for wasting my time and making this an easy peasy 1 Star yelp review.

Best grilled oysters in the city, hands down. The Sunday brunch is delightful, especially the lemon zest pancakes. 

Great for outdoor seating. A little pricy for a neighborhood spot, but really tasty. 

Sometimes the service is terrible, especially when they're busy.

Loved the atmosphere, food, service. We had The lobster roll, hush puppies, fried green tomatoes and ice cream with magic shell for dessert. Even the valet was speedy. Wonderful night celebrating a friends birthday!

This is absolutely the worst Dairy Queen I have EVER visited. First of all I was charged twice as much as the ice cream actually cost and then given the wrong topping. When I returned the next day to report the issue, the owner/manager asked if I had the ice cream to return and when I laughed at that, he asked for the receipt. Of course I had neither so he would not assist me. I then was ready to pay for another order, but he would not service me and told me to leave the shop. Since the man actually owns the store, he cannot be censured or made to pay the consequences. What makes it worse is that I have to pass this location every day, and as much as I would love to have an ice cream, I'll be damned if I will ever go there again. To those of you who read this, what you do is your own business, but I believe this man should be made to pay for his lousy service and insolence.
We had Covid carry out and it was delicious. The pickup process was very easy. They communicated clearly via text. Will definitely be back again.

The worst customer service I have ever experienced. We called for order and waiting 45 minutes after ordering over the phone 20 minutes before our arrival.  To only take cold food and they customer service was horrible they ignored us and kept saying  our food would ready in few minutes but took 45mins. They also seemed to rush us out after giving us the check they kept asking didn't we need anything else. When we was just checking out food. Once we told the staff member our food was could she asked "did you guys want a a manager or something" we just walked out.  Please don't go here !

LOVED it! A local on the street said "You want the Gumbo Shop" and it was incredible. So of course we all chose one form of Gumbo or another but started with mouthwatering BBQ shrimp. All had white sangria and shared FANTASTIC drool-worthy bread pudding. The best part? Our adorable server Brenda, who felt like Mom, making us feel right at home, even though the place was hopping. She closed her eyes as she sung out the pages of specials and made the whole walk to get there worth it. Should you? YES. You should.
Delicious steaks, martinis and that stuffed hash brown is my version of heaven.

Yesterday evening my gf and I ventured out into the land of chain restaurants that is Cool Springs.  I'm guessing we arrived before the dinner rush, around 6 pm, because we were seated immediately and experienced super fast service during the entire meal.  I wasn't sure what to expect having read other reviewers issues with bad/slow service.  
Anyway, I wasn't too hungry so I didn't try any of the delicious sounding appetizers.  They have both hot and cold tapas which all had very interesting combinations of ingredients.  I opted to go with their sushi for dinner and ordered the Baja Breeze- cream cheese, asparagus, ebi, crunchy, tempura fried, topped with baked spicy crabmeat, eel sauce & chives and an eel nigiri.  My gf had the Tropicana- spicy cream cheese, mango, tempura salmon, topped with macadamia nut and chives, miso sake sauce, eel sauce and the California Sol- ebi, avocado, crabmeat, tempura fried, topped with crunchy, spicy mayo, miso sake sauce & wildberry sauce.  Our dishes arrived within 15 minutes of ordering.  For a Saturday night, I was surprised at how fast the food came out.  The sushi was fresh and the rolls, while rich, were delicious.  They had a decent draft selection of beers, although at $6.50 a pint, I found it to be a little on the pricey side.  The cocktail menu was equally pricey but had some interesting drinks that I look forward to trying in the future.  I found the ambiance to be relaxing.  The jazz band playing out on the patio added a nice touch.  If budgeting is an issue, I would not recommend Wild Ginger.    I plan on coming back for another early dinner in the future.  I can see how it would be a mad house when the place gets packed.

We had no intention of going to Santa Barbara however, took a little detour to try this place out due to the great reviews.

We get there around 4 pm, a couple tables were full but it definitely was not busy with plenty of empty tables. We were told to wait for about 10 minutes before they could seat us. We were confused since there were plenty of tables available, about 5 minutes later a couple walks in and they were told to wait 10 minutes as well, they had the same confused look on their face. Not sure if this is an inside locals joke because seems like shortly after a couple locals walked in and they were told to wait 10 minutes and they laughed it off and proceeded to seat themselves.

Hmmm on to the food. We got the jackfruit tacos & picadillo empanadas, pictured below. The empanadas were delicious & very flavorful. Didn't feel the same about the jackfruit tacos, felt like there was something lacking. We also got juice, was expecting freshly squeezed juice but it comes in a bottle which you can return for $2 off your bill. I would've have opted for a smoothie had I known it wasn't freshly squeezed. 

Our waitress was extremely sweet, kudos to her. The ambiance was nice & the restaurant is very clean. Owning a vegan restaurant is no easy feat, I appreciate the creativity & effort.

This place is so good! I had the chicken tinga warm bowl. Way larger servings than I was expecting! Couldn't even finish the whole bowl. Really fast service also, less than 5 minutes in line. I wish they had more locations around Nashville so it would be closer to my house. They should open one at Capitol View in the Gulch! It is worth the drive though. Anything you order here you can't go wrong.

Absolute trash location with an even worse proprietor that doesn't understand how to manage. I live her in Feather Sound and after numerous interactions complaining about waiting in line for 30 mins, trash routinely not taken out and soap and paper towels not being in the bathroom. The straw that broke the camels back was my trip for breakfast this morning. No soap amidst a virus outbreak is unacceptable. The "supervisor" on duty took five minutes to even acknowledge me after I asked to speak with her. She simply stated "yeah, sometimes it doesn't work". This one statement sums up how this place is ran. Please go to any other location and i'm sure it will still be somewhat better. Trash location and trash employees that are better suited for lower tier fast food joints.

First time at this place and I walk in at 11:45 PM on a Tuesday and order a couple slices. The lady at the counter told me they had no slices available and that it would be 15 to 20 minutes before any would be available. The funny part is their specials were for slices and they had none at 1145pm???

Expensive for Italian but absolutely predictable, consistent , decent homestyle Italian food and very friendly service. The food is genuine Italian and the owner is too. If you are rude and unfriendly he might kick you out. The signs on the front door remind you not to wear your hat and basically send the message that no bums are welcome. Clean bathrooms too!!

I love sweet and they have a nice sweet sauce that really gets me excited when someone wants to go to Johnnys and invites this guy!!!

I like the crust, I like the sauce, I like the fresh toppings, I like the atmosphere, I like the service, they are very friendly, down to earth, helpful, quick, all this would pretty much have to put Johnnys on top of my list for pizza in Fairview Heights area.

the bread sticks with pizza sauce and nacho cheese sauce mix, oh how did i almost forget about you! I get them every time and I love them every bite! 

If your looking for good pizza hit up Johnnys, you wont be disappointed... if you are, bring me those leftovers!!!

Famoso has many different locations throughout the city; I've only been the Whyte Avenue one. The sit-down restaurant does allow you to feel like you've stepped away from the busyness of Whyte Avenue. The environment is nice and clean and bright, and the service is decent. The food is good, but what is possibly most exciting is all the Nutella inventions they have (hot chocolate, ice cream, etc.)
Little disappointed. My husband and I were just in there getting a to go beignet and when we both finished one we went into the bag to split the other one and it wasn't in there  so sad!

The Hungry Cat is a real treasure of SB. Great food and delicious drinks. A bit pricey but you can cut down on cost by attending Happy Hour. Service is usually OK, the food makes up for it. Can be a little crowded so get there early.

Overpriced for a cheesesteak with hardly any steak 
Possibly the worst steak I've had in a long time 
Will be even longer before I will be back

Well...the menu is extensive and exciting, the atmosphere lovely, service friendly, and I will return!  We ordered 2 items off menu...chilaquiles specials that were recommended by our server ( a chile verde and a mole). Both came with 2 fried eggs perfectly oozing and both not on the menu. My daughter's and one breakfast pizza that was on the menu, was excellent as well. They claim to fry the chips in house and make sauces on site. My tastebuds agree. Fresh and wonderful. Coffee was excellent to, and for a tad more, I was able to order soy milk. The oudoor seating was superb on a fall Sept. morning.  Expect a weekend crowd. The lost star is due to the fact that we waited a long time for out food to arrive...that wasn't the problem. The problem was...when ot finally arrived, 2 plates came out a good 5 minutes before the breakfast pizza and we saw others who arrived after us get served before our 3rd order.

Sadly I notice this place has really gone downhill in just the past couple of months. I have been a regular customer here for several years, and their food used to be great. But, recently, it appears the young grandson of the owner has taken over their daily operations, and the food quality has deteriorated. Also, there is a young woman at the register, (possibly girlfriend) who also helps out in the kitchen, and she is totally incompetent, untrained, and is inappropriately dressed and groomed, for this type of a restaurant. She wears very low cut tops, has long nails, and long hair. I have seen her play with her hair then touching the food. If you're working in a restaurant kitchen, you need to be covered, perhaps wear an apron, and a hair net, or at least tie your hair back, and keep your hands clean! Basic restaurant hygiene!
I'm going to avoid going to this pizza joint in the future. 
Also, the parking is really terrible, in front of the store. Very challenging to back up safely into busy rt 3 traffic.
The sweetspot of the Fox chain: good service, quality control but still cheap. The $20 summer special with pizza and salad and two wines is a very good value.   We like the salads, the pizzas so-so.
First time here..absolutely excellent service..$7 unlimited microbrew Thursdays was the best..would definitely come back and would definitely recommend this place

I haven't shopped at your store since you stopped carrying food that my family enjoys. I did stop in just a few days ago to see if you had Chestnuts for the holidays. You did have a nice selection of chestnuts at over $12/Lb. I went to Whole Foods and got a great selection for $7.99/lb and they are grown in the USA. How do you justify charging 50% more than WHOLE FOODS for the same quality product? Unbelievable!!

Head to District Donuts for a big win on deliciously decadent donuts! Carb and sugar lovers can rejoice here! (Disclaimer: If you're counting calories, avoid this place at all costs!)

This isn't your ordinary donut shop- it's a donut shop on steroids and all that pizzazz, with tasty sliders and addictive coffee brews. Breakfast, lunch and dinner can all be consumed here upon one visit or multiple visits. Pick your poison of beer or coffee to complement your snack or meal! But don't forget to bring your voracious appetite, and either a hammock or wheelbarrow for the food coma aftermath.

Cruising down on Harrison, you can see this location has an adjacent parking lot which was quite convenient. You walk in, get mesmerized by the psychedelic blue and teal floor designs, check out the menu and order at the counter. I admired the beautiful decor of this location- custom wooden booths with a splash of teal color on the back cushions. All of the staff members were friendly and helpful with menu recommendations.

Donut selections change daily and on my most recent visit, I fell in love with the cinnamon roll and chocolate peanut banana donut. The cinnamon roll had a cream cheese glaze, topped with bruleed raw sugar. After ordering, you can contain your excitement by watching a staff member flame the raw sugar on the cinnamon roll. The cinnamon roll was as good as any cinnamon roll should be! The bruleed sugar gave it a nice little crunch with every bite. The chocolate glazed donut was topped with peanuts and stuffed with the yummiest banana pastry cream. The flavors worked oh so well together and I regret not getting another one to bring home for a midnight snack. To seal the deal, the Vietnamese iced coffee was a great afternoon caffeine pick-me-up!

District Donuts is a must if you happen to be in the area and are in need of a snack/coffee/donut fix. Yes it is a little pricy for a $4 donut but remember that these are extraordinary donuts! I look forward to my next visit so I can try out some more of their sliders, kolaches, biscuits, and other donuts.

DONUT worry, be happy and DONUT let anyone ever tell you that you're less than incredibly amazing, yes I'm talking to you dear Yelpers :) !!!

Huge fan of the basement! The location being off downtown Reno is nice. We have two dogs and we love to stroll by the river, stopping in the basement is great because the dogs are allowed!

The building is quirky and cute. Everyone posts about how it's an old post office but you really don't get the full picture until you go. There are vaults and it's really cool!

I LOVE that you can support a bunch of businesses at once. That might be my favorite part. The communal area allows you to get lunch at one place, while also getting a coffee at another spot, while also getting a drink somewhere else. It's really great. There are also some shops and of course west elm. The basement is a staple in our weekly routine!

There aren't a lot of places to eat in Carpinteria...  and everyone in this place seems to know the owners - so that must be the reason for the good reviews.  Because the food was just not great - or even OK.  

Walking in, it smelled like not fresh oil.  The menu has a lot of items - but not much in the way of choice - if that makes sense...  it's basically either eggs, sandwiches or - weirdly, Asian food on the back of the menu.  If you don't want one of those three things - or want something a little more inspired, you're at the wrong place.  

I finally settled on a grilled cheese - that's how limited this menu is - and it was like something I'd make.  Which isn't praise.   The side of fries desperately needed ketchup, but the bottle on the table looked all watery and not clean.  I couldn't use it.  I just gave up on the entire "school cafeteria" looking plate.  

My SO ordered from the Asian side of the menu - Udon.  Which was a bowl of messy looking veggies that I'm not sure belong in any bowl of Udon.  I'm no expert on Udon, to be clear, but this didn't look at all like what I've seen before.  And she said it wasn't very good.  

Service is solicitous.  You must ask for a straw (a policy I'm still getting used to).  I wouldn't consider a return visit.  The place needs some freshening up all around and some more interesting menu items.  Again, there aren't a lot of choices in Carp, but there are certainly better ones than Hugos.

I just ate crawfish at this Inn and it was quite an experience.  My guest and I ordered each 3lbs of crawfish with potatoes and corn.  The crawfish flavor was good but they seem to have mixed up batches.  About 1/2 were overboiled, some were fishy and cold, many heads with no tails and the good ones were very good!  There were many fish scales in the serving with more than usual dead ones.  My experience was that they had to have mixed batches to get a serving with so many differences.  The potatoes were just boiled in water to a point of over boiled and the corn well, frozen and mushy.  The manager came out and asked me about my concern and he immediately got defensive to a point that he insulted me.  All he did was defend his kitchen and what he was boiling then.  We paid $38.64 for a very unpleasant meal.  I was not looking for anything for free but after being treated the way the manager treated me, I would have liked a full refund!  The bathrooms are dirty and the waitress was not very attentive.  There is one waitress there that is very, very good!  They are lucky to have her!  This was my second time going there for lunch.  I will never go back!

Good food, an decent sized menu, great atmosphere for meeting with friends or family Besito checks those marks. 

It unfortunately also checks the expensive, niche, and inconvenient marks which keeps it at 3 stars. 

The parking is atrocious, and it has very few options for a group that has someone who doesn't like more authentic Mexican food. Fortunately I do like that cuisine so I enjoyed the food but in general when a restaurant doesn't have options for a more picky eater it makes it tough to choose for group outings. 

There is also the issue of the price tag which is on the higher end. While inside has a great atmosphere and is easy to carry on conversation in, it is still set in  the outside of a shopping center with no good parking options so it is far from high end. 

Would I return? Yes. Would I understand why someone might not? Also yes.

I come here alone almost every night once a year when I attend the Tucson Gem Show in February for a week.  This year February 2020,  the 22nd St Golden Corral is closed due to fire and remodeling.  

I  eating weekday dinner for $12.93 senior price including tax, and water.  

Place is clean and servers are attentive.  The fried foods such as chicken wings, fried Alaskan Pollock, fried shrimp, fried zucchini are all pretty good.  

I like the steak cos it is charbroiled, but you must eat it rare otherwise it your jaw will be exhausted in 4 chews.  This is low grade steak, full of veins, gristle, and oingy boingys.  Had good charbroiled taste, tho.  

The Chinese donuts are good too, like I said anything fried.

I was so angry with this meal - and the beaucoup bucks I spent - that it took me a few hours before I could describe anything without using the words "fucking fuck". Overpriced and under delivered. Three stars for the hummus. Everything else gets ZERO stars.

Appetizer (served with all entrees)...

Hummus with assorted condiments and pita.

The hummus is GREAT. Smooth and creamy with the obligatory puddle of fine olive oil and tasty spices. Pita is freshly baked, fluffy and warm. Slather it with hummus and it's a great meal. 

Condiments are okay. You can sense the tremendous effort that went into creating the colors and textures but nothing said, "come back and eat me again."

You want a great "stuff your face on bread and dippy things" experience, go to Suraya.

Entrees...

Lamb and beef koobideh
Beets with dukkeh

Koobideh is an Iranian ground meat kebab, grilled on a skewer and served over saffron colored Persian rice.

What we actually got were 5 tiny, over cooked sausages, laying on a bed of dill. Plain white rice on the side had hot (peppers?) things in it. $40

The beets came on the same plate as the sausages and I thought it was a side dish. Literally less than a handful. Undercooked and flavorless would be an apt description for this uninspired dish. $36

Drinks...

Mish mosh: take on an aperol spritz. Pretty but tasted like soda water. $12

Sting in the tail: no real distinctive flavors. Felt like the ingredients canceled each other out. $13

Dessert...

Soft serve brown ice cream, Sicilian pistachio rice crunch and sour cherry sauce. 

I tried a spoonful and left the rest to melt into pool of brown goo.

If you're ever in San Francisco, head to Souvla and order their vanilla frozen yogurt with sour cherry sauce. There can be only one and this is the one.

Our first visit (lunch) to Augustines and the food was excellent! Decor and ambiance very lovely. Giving four stars account of service which was not quite excellent. We sat in the dining room at a far end booth. We were taken to our table by a friendly young lady. Wait staff was quick to bring water to our table. There were at least two waiters in our area, however, I'm fairly certain it was a bartender that waited on us. Waiter/bartender came to our table in a timely manner for drink order and I asked what soup of the day was. Upon return we said we needed just a few more minutes to order. In the meantime we overheard other waiter telling about special bread, better description of soup and there was a lunch special offered not on the menu. I feel like our waiter should have told us about the specials and soup of the day on his first stop at table instead of me asking. That is why I generally don't like to be waited on by bartenders, not as prepared (they have their own expertise at the bar). A different waiter brought us more ice tea (mid meal) without asking. That is service I expect at a restaurant like Augustines. Different waiter cleared our plates. By the time our waiter/bartender came over, we were out of tea and all he said 'are you ready for check?'. We needed to ask for more tea and dessert menu. Maybe the guy was new and needed a little more training. Service just a little bit lacking but we will definitely go back for the great food and overall fun area. Highly recommend.

My son and I went here on our way to a baseball game.  1st time. My super picky son said 10/10 would eat the breaded shrimp taco plate again. The food had such good flavor. Salsa and chip bar was great as well.

Great atmosphere as noted before. Today I'll have a salmon lox bagel and get a side of loaded hash browns. I surprised them by asking for garlic in my potatoes...took them a bit longer yesterday. Let's see how it goes today :)

As New Yorkers who come to this restaurant rarely, we've enjoyed the occasional hearty meals here. However, after last night we will no longer be giving money to this franchise thanks to the behavior of one waitress. What started off as hospitable behavior slowly progressed to not so nice manners. I used to work in food services so I always treat restaurant staff with the upmost respect as it's not an easy task so not sure what brought about the sudden attitude but there are things you just don't do. For example, judging the amount of food a patron eats and without being asked bringing two "takeaway" containers to them and upon arrival to the table saying "oh I guess you guys won't be needing these" once she saw our meals were completely eaten and enjoyed. I said "oh thanks but we were hungry" and she replied "I see that". I'm by no means overweight nor is my significant other which sadly is the treatment those who are receive often, but on a Friday night after a long work week and exercising all week, we have the right to indulge and it's none of anyone's business. As a restaurant you should be happy your visitors eat all their food as it speaks volumes to what you're bringing to the table (no pun intended). On top that, she rudely placed the second beer ordered on the table. The waitress' name is on the receipt but rather than reciprocate the same classlessness and risk the possibility of her losing her job, I will refrain from mentioning it. Never coming back though and if you continue to treat others this way, you'll see a pattern. Just because you're miserable or having a bad day doesn't give you the right to treat others a certain way.

To management, 

My girlfriend and I had a wonderful breakfast this morning....Up until I inquired with the curly black haired server who'd worked Sundays for 25 years ( never got her name).  I first asked the busser.  The one who actually did everything for us aside from write the order, if there was a possibility of getting an apea cake but have it cut in half and have it rewrapped so I could give half away to my sister.  The busser said she would check with our server, to see if you could do that.  No problem there.  The problem arises when our so called server returns and we ask the server the same question.  Her reply was, I have orders to take, I can't help right now, she ( the busser) will have to do it.  Now, I write today as a server for 20 years.  Never, do you tell a customer you are too busy to help!!!, or with her attitude...Even care. A give me a few minutes or even a no we can't do that would have been better than the grouchy attitude we received.  Yeah, 25 years serving and its made her bitter I suppose, or maybe the clientele enjoy surly waitresses.  We do not!! So she still got her 20% tip, like I said I know the biz, but the busser was the one who should get that money, and needless to say, we didn't get our apea cake based on your servers, I'm to busy for you attitude.  We will never be back.


Unhappily,


DB

Surprising authentic in a sea full of chicken tenders, fast food, and chains. Kids were craving something asian and we found this little gem in a strip mall and were pleasantly surprised how good and authentic it was. Didn't have time to take picts but the ground pork ramen was very good, as well as the milk buns.

Wow, excellent food, nice open air dining. Had the quesadilla which is very unique, soft hand made outer tortilla with wonderful cochinita pibil, wow. Wife had the tacos, chicken tinga, cochinita pibil, and the Poc, all very flavorful. Definitely coming back.

Out of the way great find. Don't judge this restaurant by the neighborhood. It is a cute diner atmosphere (blue walls, rotating bar stools, stenciled 1950s murals) with really good Thai food. We got the Panang curry with fried tofu which came out flavorful with the right amount of spice. Additional spice containers (chile, peppers, chili powder) were provided as needed. The pad see eew with chicken was also flavorful. Staff was friendly, we will return again.

This is my favorite, non-chain restaurant in Tampa/Florida!  I loved being in the South (MS, LA, AL) and absolutely love New Orleans, LA...This is the closest thing to feeling like I'm back there and I'm only missing Cafe du Monde beignets! The waiters are so nice, cater to you and your needs--They will make things right! I loved everything I tried so far, but the char-grilled oysters are my fave..Thank you for bringing a taste of Orleans here in Tampa!

Spent the football Saturday here at Double Dogs. It was good!  
You have to review a place for what it is  and how good they are at doing what they do. This is a sports bar, TVs all around, loud, deep fried food and burgers, oh yeah, and BEER!
The wings are good, plump and tender.  12 for  $9.99 nice value.  Good salads and a nacho dish served in an oversized dog bowl, hard to get past but it works for them. 
Plenty of people watching plenty of games drinking plenty of beer!
Recommend for a good time.

I'm no connoisseur but I don't know why everyone is obsessed with these wings. We got mild and they were a little watery. There is also an extra charge if you want bleu cheese/ranch dressing or celery.

I ordered my burger and asked for it to be "a little red inside," and it came back completely brown, which was disappointing. They also ran out of the chips which came with the meal. They didn't even apologize or mention that they didn't give us anything until we asked where the chips were. Then instead of saying they could substitute something like fries for us, they asked if we wanted to add the fries (for the extra charge). If it is the restaurant's fault they ran out of the side that comes with the meal, I think they shouldn't charge us extra for the substituted side - or they should at least mention that they ran out, but hey, that's just me.

Otherwise, the place had a cool vibe which was nice for hanging out and the food was still pretty good, but overall I was not very impressed.

The venue is stunning and very impressive.  The service attempts to be engaging and white glove but comes across a little desperate and aloof at the same time.  The food was good but not great.  We ordered at least half the appetizers and quite a few of the entrees.  The foies gras and corn dumpling apps were the best.  None of the entrees were amazing but the desserts were very pretty and tasted great.  The wine list is nice but very overpriced (assume 4X what you would normally pay for retail).  I would go back if someone wanted to check out the venue but not go back solely for the food.
Pizza sex and tacos are great even if bad. EXCEPT TACO BUS. Worst taco ever. Do not eat here. Dry flavor less waste if money. Be warned.

Food was great, service okay.  Concern with mor than half employees not wearing mask over nose including servers, kitchen, cashiers.  Unsanitized menu's thrown in sanitized menus without being cleaned.  Love this place but very disappointed not taken COVID serious.

I wish I could give no stars. We had a reservation but they had us sit in the bar before we were seated in an almost empty dining. Why did we have to sit in the bar? I had 20+ years in restaurant industry and felt this was ploy to have us spend money at the bar. Service had always been good but this our third and last visit due to rude and arrogant owner/ chef. My husband wanted the pasta with seafood. He asked if the chef would put in an assortment of seafood for an upcharge. The apologetic waiter came back and said it would be $40.00. are you kidding me? This is a little restaurant in front of a half deserted strip mall in Land oLakes. Really??? Well he ordered something else but was so angry that we decided that this was it. In a bad economy to insult patrons you deserve to go out of business. Don't waste your money here. Over priced mediocre food and rude arrogant owner.

Very good pizza, price, and quick service.  The rare combination of good/fast/cheap earns 5 stars in my book + beer and salads and gelato.

Seriously, we eat a lot of pizza (we like all styles and judge according to the style of pizza), and the margherita pizza was top notch, produced in 5 minutes, for less than $10.  And a good beer selection.

Love the concept of this place (don't expect ambiance, but it's clean and a totally acceptable seating arrangement):  it's like a salad bar for pizzas -- order your customized pizza, they make it in front of you then throw it in a gas/wood super hot oven for a few minutes.  And it comes out delicious.  

Looks like they want to franchise, and given the high pricing for Neapolitan pizzas in our area, I'd love to see this concept come to town.

Not worth the price. I was not particularly impressed with the service, ambiance or the pasta. For a minimum of $20 a plate you can sit uncomfortably at a picnic table and get mediocre service. I was excited to splurge for a night to try this place, but was sadly disappointed. I feel like I could have got a bigger, better portion at Mama Casale's or Lanza's for the same cost. This modern style Italian fare needs work.

Tonight was our first time dining at The Rez. The food was delicious and our waiter, Shea, was amazing! He was very attentive, made excellent recommendations and made us feel very welcome. I had the king crab legs which were grilled to perfection. My husband enjoyed the Garganeli Pasta with short ribs. We highly recommend this restaurant if you are dining at the Hard Rock in Tampa.

My husband and I were looking for something fun and different to do for date night and came across the reviews for The Boom Boom Room on Yelp. I thought it would be fun - I love a good Burlesque show and the reviews were really good so we decided to try it. I'm not sure if we went on an off night, but I can't believe that I was at the same place that all of the 4 and 5 star reviews were for. 
I can't speak for the food - we went to the 10:00p show and had already eaten dinner. The table next to us ordered the duck wings for an appetizer, but were told when they tried to order their meal that they stop serving food once the show starts. They were not told that before or they would have ordered as soon as they got there.
The 10:00 show started around 10:40. Everyone was standing at the bar and there was only one bartender so the service, while friendly, was very slow.
As for the show - it was not good. It looked very amateur and at points I felt bad for the dancers because they looked uncomfortable. Burlesque is supposed to be sexy and attractive. This show is neither. The male dancer did more of a strip club show and had so much make-up on it was distracting.
The MC LuLu was entertaining, but at one point in the show she took almost 20 minutes to call out everyone who was celebrating a birthday or anniversary. While that was nice, it became very drawn out and I lost complete interest in what was going to finish the show.

Definitely not what it used to be pre-Katrina, but still a great spot none the less.

Having worked in the French Quarter, I have fond memories of their wonderful pastas and pizzas and turkey sandwich at 2am after getting off work.

It seems like the menu has changed a bit, but all in all I consider this spot a good stand by in the Quarter that I will continue to frequent.

The calamari and the sauce it has was some of the best I've ever had..... With that said the steak sucks , I had the $15 sirloin and the $10 outback / longhorn special blows it away . I even got
It with the "Oscar" which is crab meat and vegetables and that was not great.  The view is nice and the restaurant has a nice decor and atmosphere however the steak was really sub par

I came back twice to this place because I wanted to try the food and came too late the first night. The first time I tried the poutine, and as a Canadian, it wasn't exactly what I was used to. It was still good, just not what I was looking for. The next day we came back again and the food was all great. It was quite busy, and it was a "seat yourself" situation. Seats were hard to come buy and it was a little chaotic in that sense.
