I visited before work one evening, ordering off the new honey pepper menu. I got honey pepper chicken over Mac n cheese, for $11.99.  The portion was small. Chicken strips were 3 inches long and about an inch wide. There were only 3 of these petite strips on the entree. There was an equally petite bread stick on the plate. Very over-priced and not a good value. Won't be back.

Blackstone is actually the last of the Nashville Brewpubs that I visited.  I am not sure why I held out so long.  Maybe because of its location. It always seemed to be a little to ON the beaten path if that makes sense.  That stretch of West End is usually a nightmare around rush hour and that is often when I want a beer the most.  

Regardless, I waited far to long to check out a very good local brewpub.  Since I gave it a chance it has actually passed Bosco's on my go to beer list.  

Once you get inside Blackstone it is fairly comfortable.  They have a good sized bar area the library area which is done up like your grandfathers study, if your grandfather is a stately British Gentleman.  The restaurant seating is pretty straightforward if slightly bland, but it is easy to fit a large group in if need be.  They will even reserve one of their semi separate rooms if your group is large enough.  There is an outdoor patio, but the proximity to West End makes it a little too hectic to really enjoy.  

The food is pretty typical brewpub fair that treads the line of having something for everyone and overkill pretty well.  The pretzels with a selection of mustard and the buffalo burger are my favorites, although I have family members who swear by their fish and chips and steak and biscuits.  Overall, the food will probably not wow you, but it is good comfort food and very appropriate for the setting.  One of those places you could take a large group from out of town and everyone would find something on the menu they liked.   

The service is fair at best.  Not bad, just kind of detached.  I have never had anything go wrong, but I have never felt that much of a friendly vibe from the service staff.  Not a lot of smiles or chit chat.  Great if you want to just eat and drink, but not the kind of service that makes you want to move in and live off of beer and fried food (and believe me it wouldn't take much).  

Now the important part.  None of this would matter if the beer wasn't good.  I think the beer is actually a little better than good.  I don't now if I would say great, but it is pretty close.  They seem to do the darker English style ales very well, but that might just be personal preference.   They also usually have a hand pumped cask tapped which is a nice authentic touch.  Growler refills are also available, but more expensive than some other places in town (cough, Yazoo, cough).  

If you just go to Blackstone to enjoy the beer you will not be disappointed, you might even find yourself coming back more often than you thought for the food and the atmosphere.  It might just sneak up on you and become one of your favorite spots.

Love this place! After 10 pm is the time to go since it's happy hour and $2 tacos and tequila. Favorite tacos are the shrimp and fried shrimp. All the tacos are really good. The burritos are huuuge and worth the money. Street corn is delicious. You get nonstop refills on chips and one refill for each salsa. Salsa and chips here are so fresh. Staff is also very nice
Recently was in NOLA and returned to Katie's.  Once again, the best shrimp poboy sandwich.  If I lived here,  I would come here once a week if not more often.

Great authentic Asian restaurant! Service was great and fast. Wonton soup-awesome, kimchi fried rice had the best flavor and the kimchi was not over powering. Ground pork and bean curd was very tasty. I wasn't quite sure how good the food was going to be when I walked in, but was very pleasantly surprised!

Visit the hard rock periodically to have some fun with my friends, they have a decent amount of food choices and the dealers seem friendly. I'm happy they stoped charging for parking, this was almost their a nail in the coffin for the hard rock as I noticed how many people stopped going.  the fact that they already don't serve free drinks like most any other casinos once you add the parking charge on to the most profitable hard rock in the country it just hit me as super cheap. Wish there was another casino to choose from but I guess it's back to the hard rock for now.

Most affordable wine tasting!

Here's what you need to know:

For $8 you can try eight different wines.

There are three different menu options: variety (more red wines), sweet, and lux (lux is $11-$13 and you get a dessert at the end). Every month the wine variety changes. If you love a certain wine, you can buy the bottle after your tasting (all bottles are super reasonable).

You'll be served bar crackers and make sure to wear comfortable shoes! You'll be standing for the wine tasting. Cooper Hawk does wine tasting Monday-Sunday from open until close. Friday and Saturday evenings tend to get crowded so just be aware.

Let's talk their reward program - it's a great one (especially if you live near CH). So for $37 a month, you'll get two tastings, and two bottles of wine. It's a steal! The bottles of wine can be up to $22 worth.

One of the worst McDonald's ever. Police have been contacted regarding sexual harassment involving my wife and an employee. You SEE she's wearing a ring and yet you comment on her outfit and her eyes and hair? I don't care. Sexual harassment is not taken lightly. If I wasn't in a hurry, I'd have smacked the shit out of that employee and made him live on the streets.

This place is unremarkable, slow service, expensive for what you get and the bagels we had were dry and tasted old. We waited over 15 minutes for 4 basic bagel orders and they were not busy. The temperature was freezing inside. All the patrons were complaining how cold it was and we finally had to ask them to turn down the air. They forgot the lox on my sons bagels of just lox and cream cheese. We will not be back as there are much better restaurants around to waste time on this place.

Amazing service all day long. The staff always seems to find you even when busy. Took my son for his first visit. He couldn't believe how many people from all over the world that visited here. We are New Orleans.

Honestly one of the most overrated Mexican places in Indy. They are always way too crowded for the quality of tacos. The margs are also just okay. They don't take reservations so try to go during an off hour.

I don't agree with 1 star. Neg is needed. This pizza was the most disgusting tasting. I asked for a salad I received a chocolate cake. Driver was over weight,  he wouldnt get out of his car so I had to leave my downtown apartment to go to his car in front. Chicken sandwich had faty meat couldn't chew through all that fat. Where was the chicken. Fries where greasy and soggy. Dont eat here. Go to true st. Louis pizza Imos on Hampton ave.

My advice... Go to Jersey Mike's by Publix on Collier or get a sub from Publix!

Larry's Deli is a classic example of a local Mom & Pop shop that's going to lose business to the new and big franchise (Jersey Mike's)....and for good reason.

Haven't been to Larry's Deli in months  because the last time I was there, they messed up my order.

Got got home with my sub and not only was it  cold  (with unmelted cheese) but two ingredients were missing.  I called the manager who offered many excuses but no offer to make it right.

At least at Jersey Mikes I get a drink and a bag of chips for the same price... And I'm sure if I call them after they made a mistake they would send me a coupon to come back and have my sandwich made correctly.

I just love the mentality of a restaurant manager who thinks I'm actually going to run back and have them redo the sandwich... As a busy mom with 2 jobs... I was lucky enough to sit down and eat lunch the first time.

Unfortunately, this was the worst food my boyfriend and I have ever ordered from grubhub and I feel bad writing this because the manager called us shortly after we ordered to offer a promotion, but the food was just not good for us to be willing to try this place again. We were looking to try a new place and Gianfranco's was rated so well on Yelp we decided to give it a try. We ordered fried ravioli, a cheeseburger, greek salad, and cheesecake. My greek salad was not a greek salad. 

My salad was supposed to have olives, tomato, feta cheese...when I got it the cheese was literal blocks of cheese, it had 3 slices of cucumber, 4 little slicecs of onion thrown on top, 4 olives...just not good. My cheesecake did not taste anything like cheesecake.

My boyfriend said that the only good thing about his burger was the bun and the fried ravioli was watery/rubbery.

They may have great pizza, but I don't think we'll be trying this place again to find out.
First time trying the Thai food. I got the original pad Thai and Thai iced tea.. it was tgood for the lunch special

Went here today after doing errands and I liked Beaks right away. We sat 'inside' meaning the tiki-bar-like section which had fans going full on and only two other people seated nearby.
Our waiter was friendly though unknowledgeable about the white wines.
He brought out a bowl of popcorn, M&M's, wasabi nuts and tiny crackers in what could only be best described as 'some guy who had the munchies late one night's invention'. It actually was a tasty tidbit which went along with my Anchor Steam on tap.
I got the Angus Burger on a bed of potato chips. Pretty good burger in all. My friend got the Pimento cheese sandwich served on the best cracked wheat bread I've tasted, served with a cole slaw. It was pretty good too.
Not a lot of people there but the waiter said biz had been slow of late. I asked if they have a happy hour and he said on the weekdays between 4-7 it's half off every other drink. Hmmm..that's a strange twist. Wonder if they give you punch out cards to keep track of the 'every other' drink.
All in all, not a bad place and funky, cool artwork. Check out the bathrooms!!
Whenever we're in the neighborhood we stop in. Great breakfast and lunch spot. You can't go wrong there. I recommend the hue is rancheros

Great ambience. The bands that play at night are good as well.

Food and drinks are awesome. We had the hand-cut fries and sticky chicken wings for appetizers. I recommend the garlic aioli sauce for the fries. I had the delicious Gunthorp Farms' Chicken for the mains. 

My friends had the Squash Gnocchi and it sounds like its a great option for vegetarians.

This is more of an average for the two times I've been. The first time we were seated outside and waited 20 minutes for someone to come out a get our drink orders and the only reason it was this soon was because we asked a guy who came outside if he was going to get our drink orders. He grumbled and looked like he was inconvenienced by us being there. The second time we came we sat inside and had much better service. Pizza was very good and a large served all four of us with some pizza to spare.  We spent 16$ on the pizza so around 4 bucks a person! Couldn't beat that.

We were visiting, it's was late, we were hungry looking for something to eat.. 

We were greeted and promptly sat.. Our server Andrew introduced himself and took real good care of us.. We ordered the Lucy juicy burgers and were not disappointed at all.  One of the best burgers! Caesar salad was delicious and so was the Mac n cheese... 

This place exceeded our expectations!

I'd give this place another few months. We went about three weeks after it opened. Very slow food service, and we only ordered sandwiches. Oddly, one side of most of the sandwiches was burnt while the other side was almost completely untoasted. It is also sooooo loud when full - needs sound treatment badly. They make it decently clear that kids are discouraged...only two kid food options, with tart apples as a side? (Kids don't really like Granny Smith apples, right? Mine didn't.) Anyway, I live in the neighborhood and want this place to succeed, but I wouldn't recommend it at this point. I'll chalk this mess up to them still trying to get it together and try back in a few months. Our waitress and another member of the staff were very kind and apologetic...just not aided by their kitchen.

I can fit it into my macros, it's cheap, they always get my order right, and who doesn't love Taco Bell?!?! For the record I have lost 160lbs with Taco Bell as my go to fast food. This location is quick, friendly, and a great location so I'm never late getting back to the office. Great job guys! I'm not saying this is health food, but when you forget lunch on the counter and live 30 minutes from work, the fresco menu is where it's at!

The food is good and the prices are in line. Our meal would have been enjoyable except there is this guitar and vocal guy who is just plain awful and exceptionally annoying. He was trying to sing Cat Stevens and Johnny Cash standards and within ten seconds it got on our nerves. 

Next time we'll drive by and if there is some guy caterwauling on the porch, we'll keep going.

Terrible experience, host was D'ja and was treated without any respect. Seated in an area where I clearly advised was not accommodating due to my leg injury. When asked to be seated elsewhere she mentioned there was a wait, meanwhile the restaurant was fairly emptied. Left unfortunately and hope to come back with a better service experience in the future.

We went shortly after first opening and had a horrible experience, but chalked it up to new-place-stumble.  We waited this long to try it again, and it was worse.  Horribly slow service, the servers are wearing masks but they happen to be under their chins.  Occasionally, our server would fumble with his mask and pull it up, then down, then run his hands through his hair repeatedly.  Drinks finally arrive and margaritas spill all over the table but he never cleans it up, so I go the bar to get napkins myself.  He kept apologizing for the bad service citing, "because these are "weird times" man" and we keep firing the hostesses.  Food finally arrives, no silver or napkins, so I get them myself and everything is super-smoky and salty.  

1 pitcher of margaritas, 1 nacho and 2 entrees-75.00 for some of the worst Mexican food and drink ever.  And we had to sit and watch our server ogle the young lady at the bar (she seemed like she worked there but was off, but she got a lot of "service") whose shorts were so short that her multiple trips to the restroom became the floor show (we actually saw it all).  

Can only recommend, if you don't care about value, untrained, unprofessional staff, Covid, salty, smoky food, impossible parking for anything but a Smart Car and slooooow bro service.

Consistently delicious. Great vegetarian options. It's nearly always crowded, but the cashiers are very efficient and they let you sample the bread in line to tide you over. My favorite is Maya's Market, but Fran's Fromage is also quite good. I've had salads here as well, but in my opinion they are not quite on par with the sandwiches. Also, don't pay extra for the pasta salad. It's not good.

I ended up there for lunch today since Zupa's next door had a long line. When I walked in, there were several people who where congregated at the front door and I couldn't tell if they were in line or not.  I stood there waiting until someone told me they were just "talking". I checked out the menu and was quickly disappointed in the options. I understand the simplicity needed on the menu to keep things simple and fast but the combinations were lack luster. I ended up getting two Tin Roof tacos to go. Like the other reviewers I was disappointed in the "size" of the taco. I fully appreciate the desire to provide fresh ingredients that affect the cost of things, but I was still disappointed. There was too much onion paired with canned pineapple and it was dry and not very flavorful. I did add some sauces that were given to me which still didn't improve the experience. 
I also observed  the staff was dealing with some missed orders and having to make things right for customers.  It is a new business and I understand that it's a process to iron thing out to get the business rhythm going. I will say I am not a big fan of dining in at a fast food places and this venue is no exception. I didn't find it inviting. If what another reviewer said is true that they will be bringing a TV into the place then I definitely won't be dining in. Too many places have TV's in their business and if I want to watch tv while I eat I will eat at home. 

I will give it another try in few months and hopefully things will improve.

I admit I was skeptical...  But I am now sold.  Nice clean shop, with friendly service.  The sandwiches looked  delicious, and tasted even better.  I had the Ultimelt, and it was amazing!  I also decided then and there, that if your sandwich doesn't come with the parmesan crusted bread...  It's worth the upgrade!  I also snuck a bite of my friend's Pepper Popper (with a bacon upgrade), and that was good too.  There's a very small beer cooler, but it's stocked with great local beers.  I look forward to when they're able to do indoor seating again.  -Right now there's two two-person tables outside, otherwise you're looking at to-go.

Me and my coworker ordered sushi from this place one night. I ordered a Jessica Roll and a California roll, both cooked crab rolls. My coworker ordered a Maki Sake roll and a spicy tuna cucumber roll, both raw rolls. We ate around 7:30 and by 8:45 I was running to the bathroom vomiting. I was so sick, broke out into cold sweat and could not even stomach cold water. The next day my coworker had said she was up all night vomiting and making bathroom trips, she even had to call out of work sick. Just thinking about eating there now grosses me out. And yes we believe it was from the sushi because both of us getting sick like that is no coincidence.

Decided to try someplace new and laid back for my birthday tonight and I am SO happy we chose the Black Barn! The atmosphere is comfortable, and the guys are super welcoming and friendly. As we were waiting for our sandwiches we were saying how we hope the food is as good as the energy and we were not at all disappointed! Between the four of us we had the Philly cheesesteak, chicken pesto, Monte Cristo and pastrami, along with the mac'n'cheese side. Even my picky kids were impressed with everything! Looking forward to coming back for sure!!

I loved this place, for all of the reasons listed by others and because of the salt! A little of the coffee salt (!) on the chili was amazing. The smoked alderwood salt on the sweet potato fries was really good too, as was ghost pepper. I had more fun with the salt than the sauce. And a little goes a long way bc the flavor is so intense so it's not like a sodium overload. Very decent vegan chili too. The woman working (owner?) was very nice and gave us great service as well as to he other people who walked in. I was totally full from hLf the bowl of chili snd a small order of waffle sweet potato fries (plus one wedge that I stole from my little girl's medium order. There were a lot of fries in that medium and they are thick. Maybe the sauce is a little pricey. I would rather get to try two smaller portions of different sauces for a buck than one container of one. I'm not a heavy saucer though ( but the chipotle mayo was addictive, I brought it home.) and yeah, ok, our fries were not hot just out of the oven. They were fresh, but not hot. I think more people coming in would mean more turn around and hotter fries. I was surprised they were not busy at noon. I think it's the location. It's not obvious that you can park in the back and it's not easy to stop at that busy part of Broad. But we plan to stop many times to come!

This is without a doubt Oro Valley's best Mexican restaurant. The food is fresh and tasty but it is not cheap! The takeout service can be fraught with mistakes (they are busy and there is sometimes a language barrier) , so check your order carefully before leaving the restaurant ! In the end it is all worth the price for fresh delicious Mexican food.

Yet another great location in Downtown. The table enjoyed rueben sandwiches,  irish dip, and appetizers all which were AMAZING. Nothing wrong with this downtown gem except a lack of a full liquor bar. Service was great, prices were on point and it's an awesome location to get pumped up for a Rays game!
Pretty cool college vibe...pricey house coffee

I stopped in here for breakfast on a weekday and was greeted by a nice lady on walking in. I was seated and served quickly being it was empty. I got the cupcake pancakes and a poached egg and I haven't been to IHOP for years but it is what it is and a standard chain restaurant for breakfast in my mind. The pancakes was good but definitely over powering with the frosting on it. The poached egg was overcooked but I still ate it. My server was nice and attentive so that was definitely a plus. So if your looking for something quick and to the point then this is a place for you. It's cheap and there pretty much everywhere. Overall I might stop back but I think there's a lot of other options for you as well in the nearby area if this spots not your cup of tea.

This steakhouse was amazing.  The aged steak was full of flavor.  We eat at places like Ruth Chris, Frankies, Fogo, STK and many other high end steakhouse.  Berns has the BEST porterhouse steak we've eaten.  Not only is the food amazing but the service was fantastic.  The atmosphere was awesome.  Their French onion soup was great.  Also, they have a great wine selection.  You can tour the wine cellar and kitchen.  We heard the dessert room is great, we will have to try it next time.  The servers are well educated in the menu and process.  This is a great place for a nice dinner.

Me and my husband went here about 2 weeks ago with some friends cause we were told they had a good belly dancer. The food was EXCELLENT, and I know my Arabic food. I had the chicken sandwich and it had the garlic just like I like and it came with the pickles and turnips and all the good stuff. My husband had the kafta and he LOVED their rice. The hummus was really good also and fattoush was good. I loved the food. The main reason I came here though was for the argeelah ( hookah ). Now I make my own hookah at home and dont usually go to restaurants to smoke cause they dont make it as good. But at Ya Hala they had THE best hookah I've ever had outside my own house. It was so thick and lasted a really long time. We stayed until the belly dancer came and watched her for like half an hour. And she was really the only downside of the place, she was cute and danced good and everything but she wasn't doing real belly dancing. You need to have the right kind of fast paced song and have someone middle eastern doing it who knows all the tricks and customs and everything. There was a huge crowd while we were there with all different kinds of people. But I dont mind the group so it wasn't a problem for me. We were there from like 9 pm til 1 in the am. I loved it and will definitely come back again!!!!

2 stars for the view which I didn't get a chance to see during my dinner.

I made reservations and was seated in front of a window which was covered by a large pillar. Wonderful, right? No.

As far as the food - not even mediocre. I got a salmon and it was $32 and very small and bland. Not worth it. Overall bad experience. Nothing to rave about. I left the restaurant down $200 and rather disappointed. 

I will not be back.

I stayed at the hotel a week ago..  I was put into an updated room with no windows, it was great, I never stayed in a room like that before.   If you go you must eat at valley tavern in the lobby!  The food and service were excellent!  I would suggest the sweet potato fries and the prime rib sandwich!    I will definitely go back!

Danielle the manager and the Chef Anthony were the best! By far the best restaurant experience in all of Tampa Bay Area. Family own restaurant and they make you feel as if your part of the family. Must go and experience this for yourself.
Best Vietnamese in New Orleans. Clean, friendly, consistent. Literally everything is great from the spring rolls to the vermicelli bowls to the cocktails. Lychee mojito is perfect afternoon treat!!

This is the best place in the barb to start the evening. Happy hour is loaded with specials and cheap food, as is the clientele. Every night they have a cheap drink special and CHEAP burger taco etc. The $2 fish tacos were great and they have free chips. This is the only place on State that advertised half gallon boozey drinks. I almost switched to sweet drinks just to try the $28 rum thing served in a fish bowl. Yep fish bowl. 2 for 1 boilermakers and $5 fat burgers was good enough for me. School was out and it was a weekday, so the crowd was chill and a little older (24+), but it struck me funny when Good Charlotte was on the system singing "girls don't like boys, girls like cars and money". If school's in, I hope you brought your BMW and your A game, broseph. I'd probably find another place to drink around 9, if I could walk.
Great service. Came here for the first time over the weekend and will be coming back again this week. Manager was amazing and super quick to give us service. The food was terrific.

Well they have finished the remodel and it looks terrific.  Just like the new one in Pigeon Forge actually and the Pf one is an entirely new building so that is impressive in itself.  It is open, modern and elegant.

After a day of shopping we decided to finish with a splurge so hubby went with his old staple the Ribeye and I, fancying a wee bit of surf with the turf this time, went with the filet and lobster.  

The Ribeye was perfect as usual and my lobster was unbelievable.  It melted in my mouth and was perfectly prepared with no chewy rubbery-ness that sadly happens more often than not in a Steakhouse.  However my filet was severely overdone, instead of being Med-rare, it was Med-well.  When our super friendly waitress came by to check, she saw it and said she would put another on the grill right away.  Being in the Christmas spirit, I told her not to worry, I would muddle through. She  sent the manager to our table who also saw it and was determined to fix it immediately.  

I cannot tell you how impressed we were with the service and the way this issue was handled.  The best steakhouses can overdo a steak, it is a common thing but what is uncommon is the friendly professional way the steak was not only taken care of but the entire situation was handled.  Five stars and 2 thumbs up!   

Thank you Wesley Chapel Outback- you are truly a cut above!

Moon Dog Tavern is a great place to grab a drink after work or even on a weeknd night if you're not looking for a Broad-Ripple type scene.  Theyve got a respectable beer selection and always have daily special on beer and alcohol.  The food is so-so at best, your typical american fare like burgers, sandwiches, appetizers, etc.  Nothing to write home about but the type of food that goes well with excessive beer drinking.  

There is a great outdoor patio that is perfect for wasting a night away with friends on a summer day.  If youd like there is also a live music aspect on weekends in a separate part of the bar.  There are TV monitors where you can play trivia games, poker, and a bunch of other games while you hang out which is pretty fun.

As many have said - really a tourist trap. Food is lazy & cold. Wait staff - friendly and try very hard but couldn't get much right. 
So many other choices in a town known for food. Popeyes is a better choice but then I like Popeyes.
Always excellent. Great food and atmosphere. Nice staff and local flavor. Thoughtful menu and great Happy Hour specials. Try it for Brunch too.

Tucked away on the edge of the CWE on Boyle, this spot feels like a part of the neighborhood. It's rumored to have a great happy hour and brunch, but we tried it for dinner. Hungarian Goulash and Mussels both delivered as exceptional eats. Atmosphere is great as well- the space is broken into a dining room and a more casual bar room. There's also an outdoor patio for warmer months. We'll be back to try out one of their numerous Happy Hour specials.

This is one of my absolute favorite restaurants and wine bars in St. Pete. Their wine selection is extensive and their food is to die for! To be able to sit at a table under an umbrella on Beach Drive, drinking Pinot Grigio and nibbling on a charcuterie plate was the highlight of my day. You can't wrong with anything on the menu and I love that you can pick and choose the number of meats and cheeses on the charcuterie plate to customize what you want. Fantastic restaurant that everyone in St. Pete should try!

My third visit here. It's a neighborhood restaurant with modest decor. It's clean and tidy. Staff is friendly and the food delicious! I had the Guru Curry. Flavorful, spicy (tofu/veggies). I always opt for brown rice. Portions are adequate. It is a favorite

Although it's not the best Mexican food ever, my husband and I enjoyed Matador...until our last 2 visits. The first bad sign we ignored was when my husband was served a bottle of beer that had expired 2 years ago. During our most recent visit, 4 mice scattering about was our entertainment at dinner time. After we told our server I was expecting the manger to come over and comp at least half our Mel but instead we received our tab with not one cent discounted. So never again.

Frequent this location. Exc customer svc. Received wrong order. Offered new burger, which I refused. Everything  tasted good! While finishing up lunch, a staffer quietly placed a "free lunch" voucher next to me and thanked me for my understanding. Classy customer service. Nicely done, Voorhees!

Ordered the a cheesesteak for $14.50.  A little confusing when you walk in as the cook is doing double duty.  Cooking and at the same time taking orders and finishing up with those that previously ordered.  

You first pick the steak of your pleasure which comes with a standard slap of mayo and a layer of white American cheese.

Once your steak is ready, you can add what ever toppings you desire, from sweet peppers to cheese whiz.

We completed our steak with half cheese whiz and half provolone. 

We ate at John's Roast Pork a couple days prior, and I have to say Max's steaks were more pleasurable.  Not for the faint of heart, but if you are looking for a great steak and not worried about the possibility of getting car jacked, Max's is the place for you.

Next time in Philly I would probably try another joint, but will always remember the steak at Max's

Where do I start? We were in town for the Outback Bowl. (GO VOLS!) We had just came from a restaurant down the street where we were treated poorly. We walked in and were greeted immediately and were taken to our table. Great Live music, great atmosphere and the food and service was nothing short of amazing!! 10/10 in our opinion. We will be back as soon as we come back down there. It was hard for us to name a place that did everything perfect until we came here.  Rumba Island Bar and Grill is second to NONE!
Just ate this entire 14" pie - 1 slice myself so yes 5 stars... lol. Ordered garlic knots as well and great.. great pizza place... must stop if in the mood for pizza you won't regret it

I love the Howlin Wolf.  They put on fantastic shows from Burlesque to brass bands and everything in between.  It's a great atmosphere and always a good time.  The staff is always nice and friendly and I always end up having a good time here.

The Howlin Wolf den is also located right next to the main Howlin Wolf.  In this dimly lit bar, you can get a drink before you check out your favorite show, you can order food, or you can even see one of the shows that play regularly in the back of the den.

The last time I was at the Den, I had a cuban sandwich with fried pickles.  It was so good!  Way better than your average bar food.

My recommendation would be to check this place out for the "must see" events that they have here, get some food at the den and have a good time.

I'm not a complainer and generally like everything (especially food) but PBR was so bad, I feel I have to add my first "meh" review. Three fish tacos consisted of nasty fish, a lil shredded white lettuce and a couple cubes of tomato. That's it! No flavor whatsoever -- had to ask for hot sauce, of course. Cup of coleslaw on the side was only half-full, and that's all I got for $9. Such a disappointment. Didn't expect it to be great, was going to Wells Fargo and needed to eat something, but thought it would at least be decent. Would have been better off eating fries for dinner. Only bumped up to 2 stars because I liked the waitress.
This is the best Indian restaurant around. The food is positively delicious. And the service and staff are just lovely.
The food here is great. The fish is always fresh and the staff is very kind. The variety of sushi available is wonderful.

I was so excited that I remembered Chimichanga's for Cinco de Mayo!

We were headed to Cherokee St and changed our minds when we realized that the party wasn't until Saturday.

Service was good, there was a little bit of a language barrier/rush barrier... Our server seemed to have tables on the other side of the restaurant.  

Food, excellent as always, I cannot believe I have stayed away for so long!  I discovered this place about 2 years ago, and somehow completely forgot about it!  I got a plate called Alambre, which had several kinds of grilled meat, including catfish, and chicken.  I was intrigued by the catfish. Two of my lunchmates got the seafood fajitas, I totally had lunch envy!!!  Next time I go back, I am so getting them!

Went here on Valentines Day with my husband. Really love the ambient intimate decor and so glad one can carry on a conversation without shouting. However, the food was just mediocre for the price. My husband had the stuffed trout which was served whole with a veggie stuffing. He found it very bland and unseasoned. I was eagerly anticipating the short rib, but also found it lacked tenderness and was on the dry side. The waitress was very nice and attentive. The drinks are outrageously expensive. My husband had a glass of cabernet which he said was very good but $15, really? I would come back again maybe for lunch because I love the atmosphere.

Bad really BAD customer service !!!! Staff very RUDE , management unhappy and unprofessional team . Very slow day ..... 20 minutes waiting for 2 bagels and one oatmeal !!! Definitely we're not coming back to this location :/
I finally ate here.  What a great find.  Cool decor, great food, served late on a Sunday and the sangria was great too.  There is a little walk outside that seemed worth checking out in the daytime.
EXCELLENT food and even better service!  We had a wonderful family celebration dinner and being at Zorba's made it even more special.  We couldn't have picked a better place

I live here Not tourist that you can't depend on. I get Ice cream all along the beach. I always order a small cup not the tiny one with 2 flavors. Go down to the corner of Gulf and 5th to choose from over 100 flavors and see how it's done. That guy has Ice cream stores in other countries. This one takes in about 1500 people a day. Ice cream is sold by weight but these people refused me service. They don't understand business or what a valuable customer is.
I had their Vegan Buffalo Chicken Wrap with a side of Quinoa. It was one of the best wraps I've ever had. I'd definitely recommend this place to family and friends.

Still loving my order of #9. 

Side note - why does the lady making the sandwiches look so miserable?!

I have been coming here for almost 20 years and if your looking for only the BEST Mexican food you need to come here! They bring out a plate full and I can never finish my food.this is the best and my favorite restaurant. If I could I would eat here all week! If you go, you have to try the cheese dip.mmmmmmm...
I always find the food to be pretty tasty. Portions are a little small for the price you pay, but I find the quality to be above most mexican food places I've tried.

I loooooove sandwiches and this place did not disappoint! I wish I would've known about Wright's a long time ago. We took the kids with us as well, they have a small children's menu but not very many allergen free options. The lady in charge was very helpful in getting some sort of foods for my son to eat due to his allergies, but it would be reeeeeally cool if they had some gluten free, dairy free, soy free type options for those people who can't go out and enjoy a sandwich like everyone else. It was definitely a great place to experience and the sandwich was amazing. I'd love to bring more friends here when we are looking for a good place to have lunch. :) DEFINITELY stop in and grab a sandwich if you're in the area!

LITERALLY some of the nicest most accommodating people I've ever encountered. I travel anywhere from 2 to 8 times a month so I am hotels very regularly. I hardly ever leave reviews because "things happen". But I must leave a review about the two lovely ladies that checked me into the hotel. Tracy was one of them and Leah was the other. I believe Leah was her trainer. They were very kind and accommodating and I could've sat there and talked to them for hours because they were just downright nice people. Thank you so much for working so hard to find me a non-smoking room because I absolutely positively could not deal with the smoking one. And thank you for just being nice people. The world needs more of those.... Oh and then I got on the elevator and there was a very bubbly 86-year-old woman and I talking about how much she loved children. I wanted to adopt her as my grandmother immediately. Before I got off the elevator I looked at her shirt and noticed that it said Ameristar. So apparently you guys are strategically hiring angels and I love every bit of it. Good job

So I started working at a nearby office a few months ago and heard the pizza there was good...went in for two plain slices and waited off to the side. I watched the young male chef go from his phone to making food-without gloves and without washing his hands. He seemed lost at what order was next, and the counter girl sensed that, went back to where he was and moved slips around and directed him.  After a few minutes of heating up my slices, the girl at the counter had a to-go box on the workstation next to the trash can to put my slices in.  He took the slices from the oven, and, I guess they were hot (duh) and he threw them in the direction of the box-over shooting and both slices landed in the trash.  The girl was clearly annoyed and calmly walked away.  He put two more slices in the oven and took them out 10 seconds later (pizza was still cold) and put them in the box and handed it to me.  Phone touching and dirty hands was all I could think of.  So I threw it away.  By then my lunch break was over and I didn't have time to go anywhere else...

Have been here for many years and we'll keep coming back the food is great and at a great price that's what it's all about. Try to go down the street to that new place farm truck and it was a waste of money. Portside is definitely the place to go in the area great food for a great price what more can you ask for

Food was fast and good, but....pretty terrible customer service.  Was there with a small group of well behaved high school kids on a band trip (only 5 of us) and received nothing but attitude since we arrived.  One of our kids had ordered a creme brulee, and when it came out it was full of strawberries which one of our kids was highly allergic to and we politely asked if we could get another.  The waitress suggested she just scrape it off and eat it...yikes, not great medical advice for someone who would have gone into anaphalactic shock! We told waitress up front that the check was going to be split. Bill came. Sorry one check, your problem. Tip was included in bill. Terrible service. Tourist trap. Avoid.
the food is good but i dont like the fact that they wrote a tip on my receipt and said i did it so ...,.

Went last night with a group of 12 sat upstairs it's a nice room a bit loud. We orders two apps (artichoke dip and tomatoes with mozzarella- smaller portion then most places the crowd at the table said) and a half dozen  oysters (charbroiled on the half shell). 

4- people got the shrimps and grits and licked their plates pretty clean so I would recommend that for a New Orleans style dish. I got the crawfish étouffée- pretty good- good size portion for most entrees. Others tried the ribeye that was tasty and cooked well. 

All-in-all for first time experience was a success. We also received 15% for being New Orleanians

I found this place when I was on the bus going to the mall and me and my bf decided to give it a try. We didn't try the BBQ because we want to try their other dish out first. We didn't regret not getting the BBQ either! Their utensils were very old and looks dirty so we have to ask for the plastic forks and spoons:( And the foods(squid and teriyaki chicken) that we ordered were ok. What I try to say about this place is that it is over-priced and not worth your hard-earned money!
P.S. Be careful, the people here can't really speaks English so you have to be very patient with them!

Stopped in for something sweet after a tour of Vanderbilt, it's very close. We were greeted by friendly, cheerful staff and felt right at home with the cozy interior. 
We ordered bonuts and hummingbird cake to share. The bonuts are fried dough balls with a lemon cream topping that rests on a warm blueberry compote. The flavors and textures were incredible. They say they are made with love and we definitely got the warm and fuzzies! The hummingbird cake is a hundred percent southern comfort. The frosting is so delicious I could eat it by itself. The next time we are in Nashville we will have lunch for sure.

Best food I had while visiting NOLA, the burgers were perfectly tender, juicy, abd tastey! We got the swiss mushroom and Atomic burger, both great. The restaurant was clean and gave fast service. Fries were also good, and they provided a complementary sauce. Would definitely recommend and would def go back!

Don't come to this restaurant 30 minutes before it closes as you will be very disappointed because they're already put all the sweets away and everyone is spending their time cleaning rather than paying attention to the customers.  I even had a discount for a pastry.  The order takes have been rude the last couple of times. Even though I like the food, the staff ruin it.
Believe all the 5 star reviews! I was worried looking at the tiny building from the outside, but the food was amazing. Will def be going back.

The pizza is actually really tasty! Probably the best pizza I've tasted in the area since I've been here. I would give 3.5 stars though based on the wait and the restaurant itself. The last time I ordered for pick up, I was told it would take about 30 minutes but in reality I waited an extra 20 minutes in the restaurant for my order to be finished. And there was only one other customer in the building. Also the inside is in terrible condition. Doesn't look clean or up to date, and made my wait in the store kind of uncomfortable. But the pizza makes up for it.

If hubby and I have a date anywhere in the vicinity of lunch, we go here. The food is awesome and you can have as much as you want of it. 

I will give it four stars because I agree with other reviewers that the staff could be nicer. However at this point I just expect it. There was a Mexican restaurant we loved where we would always be given the stink eye, assuming because we weren't Mexican. It always made the place a little more endearing because we were hated so. Is it the way a business should run? Of course not! But it does make me feel like I am in a different culture and life does not revolve around me as the customer.
First time with this food truck. Chose the Boom Boom Shrimp.... delicious!! The spicy shrimp will leave your lips with a slight burn that you can savor all afternoon :)

Great prices and huge portions take this from a three to a four star. The food is really nice, but it is still very much a hole in the wall. This is not a five star fine dining establishment, but, for good food at decent prices this is a safe place with a huge menu of options.

Delicious seafood!!
Our table had the Asian glazed salmon, zucchini fritters, fisherman's platter, and wasabi seared tuna. Everyone enjoyed it!! 
The serving portions are plenty, you could probably even share! Prices are reasonable for a seafood place and definitely worth it with the presentation and size!  Food also came very quickly after ordering. 

Their house salad is very simple but delicious! 

It was pretty crowded when we went on a Saturday night around 7, but there is an outside wine bar that you can grab a glass of wine or beer while you wait. We still got our table in about 25 minutes. 

Only beer and wine at the establishment no liquor. Not the most terrible thing but definitely good to know going in!  

Plenty of outside seating but a bit limited on the inside.

So apparently Pascal's Manale is famous for their "Original Pascal's BBQ Shrimp." I was so close to ordering it until I found out I had to peel the shrimp and our waiter shared the off the menu dinner specials of the evening. One of them was a Crab Cake Fettuccine, which I couldn't resist! The portion was very generous and I could only eat half of my dish. The crab cake unfortunately was too mushy, and I am pretty sure crab cakes should not be. The fettuccine however was divine and well-cooked! The noodles were light and airy and the sauce was rich without being too heavy if that makes sense. I wouldn't order this dish again however given the weird consistency of the crab cakes.

I also ordered a cup of their Gumbo soup ($7), which I do recommend ordering. This was probably the best Gumbo soup I've had in New Orleans! It had lots of flavor and depth to it.

Fantastic service and dining environment. I would like to come back and try their "Original Pascal's BBQ Shrimp" one day and see if it is worth the hype!
LOVE the greek Salad with Chicken.  Chicken is warm and well cooked...

Food was average! Nothing special, burger over cooked , fish taco special  not that special ..bland. Maybe an off day for the kitchen! Worst part was the staff , hostess hardly looked up and was busy on a device , we were clearly a burden ...  our server     Was very knowledgeable  with zero personality. All the staff & manager looked and acted miserable.  It was not very busy when we were there at around 3:30 . Such a great location with nice outside seating.
The masala dosas are the best you can get from anywhere around. If I could, they would be the only thing I'd eat.
Their selection of toppings is the best I've seen in a quick pizza place in St Louis. Awesome, personable service, and a cool wall collage of STL.
Food not bad, but if you want to be gossiped about by the male owner; this is the place to go!  Very strange that an owner in this line of business would act like that, no Thanks!

OMG! They aren't kidding, this is "Smack yer mama!" good chicken (lucky for my mom she was back in Illinois). Don't look around, don't peek into the kitchen, just eat your food son...just eat your food.

Passing through Tennessee we found this place on Yelp. It was a couple miles off of our route but we are sure glad we went. It was a little awkward at first, I think most of the people were regulars and knew what was going on. We ordered two mild quarter chickens w/fries to share. THEY PUT PICKLES ON YOUR CHICKEN! and that was OK by me. The chicken is hot, the pickles are hot, and it all tastes great.

This place is a dive, a dirty, dirty dive but if you know that the dirty dives have the best food, this won't bother you. Don't pass up this gem. Stop by and get yourself some "smack yer mama" good chicken!

It's a vegan café coffee shop. Really nice and light and airy inside with plants running all across the ceiling kind of folk art style on the walls. Little patio facing north and one facing west. Nice Place to chill. They are licensed so you can get organic beers and wines as well. And they do have a food menu. All in all a great spot considering it's edge of downtown low income location.

This place is GREAT! 
We went there for the Sunday Brunch...for $13.50 you get so so much to choose from, most of which is Vegan!  They have this stuffed french toast that was excellent, all the standard breakfast foods - potatoes, sausage, oatmeal, many diffrent breads (banana was the fav, although a Ginger Pear bread too second place), and coffee cakes along with fresh fruit.
The food was great, the variety just as good & there is many a places to sit, if you want to go upstairs, downstairs or even outside.
Highly recommend stopping in if you were to pass through St. Louy on a Sunday AM (although I believe the brunch goes until 2pm...)

Worst ever place # they are not clean here at all they will give you the same sandwich that you ordered by using the the microwave. They use no gloves or care to. Management is really lousy and with no response at all with 5 messages sent. Don't eat here you will get sick. Don't go at all the burgers are not real only 2 %real beef in this 98% chemical burger patty #the they are pre made  then put in a steamer for hours they turn brown from bacteria the burger that's fresh.should be Grey with a char mark on them if it's brown you know it's bad food. They do this daily.  Bk is owned by rbi Co. Which owns Popeyes chicken  be aware this is salmonella. 
They don't listen to you when you call the company or respond  at all..poor grade fast food rating is  -10 ..thumbs down here Longwood Ave cherrhill nj.

Yet another hotdog-only restaurant in Nashville, except this one has the most character of any hotdog place in Nashville (it is located in the Five Points area, how could it not have a lot of character!).  It is basically a VW bus with a wooden deck built onto the side of it.  No inside dining here!

This is one of those places that looks so funky, you just have to stop and check it out.  Plus, the name "I Dream of Weenie" is outrageous.  For vegetarians they offer a tofu dog, but I think I will pass on that one, thanks.  I had the Rebel Yelp, which comes with Chow Chow mustard and jalapeños.  Really good, but super hot!  The guys in the stand are super friendly.  Parents should take their kids to this place, as it is sure to be a memorable experience for the little ones... I mean, what could be cooler as a kid than getting a dog at a place as funny as this, right?

It's a little hole in the wall, but we came for the sandwiches. Specifically, we got a couple grilled cheese and wow, they were delicious!

Although the bar seemingly only had one lady doing everything (cleaning, taking orders, cashiering, cooking, etc), we didn't wait long on a Friday for lunch.

I got one with cheese, chicken, bacon, ranch, and ciabatta bread, all grill-pressed to perfection with a side of bbq chips. My wife got one with mozzarella, provolone, red peppers, basil oil, a fried egg, and ciabatta bread, also grill-pressed. They turned out so cheesy, simply perfect for those craving some good grilled-cheese. We'll definitely go again!

We decided last minute to give Eagle Tavern a try. It was a busy Valentine weekend so the hostess sat us at the bar, but we were not given a wait time, she said this is all that is available. I went on open table and made a reservation for 45 mins later. We had fried cauliflower at the bar, which was very tasty.  We were seated at our reservation time and had a great waitress who was very attentive even though it was busy.  Saturday night is prime rib night. I ordered a queen cut which is reasonably priced and huge!  (See pic)My partner ordered the Tavern Steak and cleaned his plate.  We will be returning and recommend Eagle Tavern.

I am SO GLAD my mother and I decided to try brunch here yesterday! Hands down the best breakfast I have ever had. 

Monday mornings certainly aren't prime hours for any restaurant, so we were one of only two parties in the large, extremely tastefully decorated restaurant. Even practically empty, the space has an amazingly inviting feel, with warm leather booths and comfy gray upholstered chairs. The attention to detail that contributes to the on-point atmosphere is striking.

As for service, out host and waiter were both very personable and knowledgeable about the menu. Every request was fulfilled perfectly. 

The food was incredible. We ordered the crab cake benedict and the lemon ricotta pancakes to share. The crab cake benedict ($16) consisted of two toasted english muffin halves, each topped with a crab cake, avocado slices, a perfectly poached egg, and delicious cilantro hollandaise sauce, accompanied by cooked-to-perfection, flavorful  home fries. It would have been enough to share had we both not been ravenous! The lemon ricotta pancakes ($13), while a simpler dish, were equally tasty. The dish consists of four medium-sized fluffy, lemony pancakes, topped with blueberry compote, powdered sugar, and a mint leaf, and a side of real maple syrup. 

All in all, the food I had at Finch and Fork was the best breakfast food I've had. The way the chef combines ingredients really lets each one stand out, yet they blend together to create an amazing combination of flavors. I can't wait to come back here to try their lunch and dinner menus as well! Thank you for a restaurant well done.

Starting off, the ambiance in this place is amazing for a date. I love the fireplace in the middle of the restaurant. The service was good and friendly. The Bread they start you out with is to die for!! I couldn't stop eating the bread! I ordered Shrimp Fettuccine Alfredo. It was yummy, but not enough shrimp in the dish.

Greg's Review for Korean tastes

Hibachi dishes : Great... I like that much sweet taste. General taste of hibachi in other japanese restaurant tend to be too sweet but this restaurant is perfect for korean taste.
Sushi : good
Side dishes : good and fresh
There are many tables over 15.
Waitress is so kind.

Five stars just on service today. Haven't been here in some time but decided to come to celebrate my step father's birthday. We were greeted upon entering and seated promptly. Our waitress came right over and was so friendly. She took our drink orders and appetizer. We opted for the chips and salsa which was quite yummy. They make the chips fresh in house. It's a must try and they are refillable during your visit. I really like their chili so I ordered that in a bread bowl. I prefer the bread bowl so that I have something to dip into my chili. If you don't order the bread bowl their soups and  chili don't come with anything such as crackers or bread. Wish that for the price that ya so get something like garlic bread or crackers. But their chili is very delicious. My daughter got the kids tenders and a  Cesar salad which she liked very much. My hubs got the steak and chicken meal which he said was good as well. The waitress even brought over the Palooza dessert for my step father to top off his birthday dinner. Great service and great food today.

Were should I start, if you want the freshest meal possible this is your place. Only way to eat healthier is to catch or hunt your own protein. The salad is grown in house, the veggies are picked up from local farmer markets daily, and the drinks are superb. Prices are reasonable considering the quality of food. Honestly, what else could you ask for in a restaurant?
Expensive, but so worth it. Checking in online is pointless, your time doesn't count until you check in with the hostess, but again, worth it.
Great place! I used to go to the boulder location all the time. I was amazed to see a location in Tucson and it is amazing! Highly recommend

Incredibly overpriced.  I tend to judge Thai restaurants by their pad thai first, then move onto specialty dishes.  Their pad thai was something ridiculous like $12 and it was not phenomenal.  I've definitely had better at even half the price elsewhere in the country.  My dining friend had the Bird's nest with scallops and shrimp and said it was good, but kind of bland.  I would tell my friends to skip this place and try somewhere else.
Happy people. You enjoy being there and make friends easily when you go. The food is amazingly delicious.

Just my new favorite go to on my days off...my favorite is the farmhouse scramble with asparagus goat cheese pesto and you can add bacon, service is good...I love the infused butter for the toast...good cocktails ;)  just a kick back cool place...only thing I haven't liked is the hash not much flavor or the veggie patties for the same 
Try it it will become your favorite too

Went to lunch here after the swamp tour and had a great time. Had my first (of many since) French 75 cocktail. View of the swamp from our table. Food was great. We had oysters, stuffed mushrooms, turtle soup appetizers and all were great.

Pretty cool little spot for after work drinks. Great service and good food. They run daily specials that don't break the bank and beers always cold. Some days they have card tournaments, other days live music, but over all a great atmosphere. Also Michelle's awesome.

I took a few things for take out and they were really good! The beef chow fun is delicious. Their menu is rather extensive so I can't vouch for everything, but the food we got was tasty, not overwhelmingly salty or full of sauce like some Chinese places, and overall very good.

My husband and I have been to The Crossing a number of times, but I have never written a review, until now. The new menu is fantastic! I have had the blackened tilapia 3 times now, and it is consistently fantastic!! I know this restaurant is going through a few growing pains, but the atmosphere is fantastic! I highly recommend is sitting on the patio! There are trees for cover during the day, and heat lamps for use in the evenings, if needed. The wine list and beer selection are fantastic. By blackened tilapia had a crisp outside, & a flaky inside, paired with rice and fresh veggies, it is fantastic! I also had the apple crisp tonight, and it was unbelievable! Homemade, a la mode, what else could you ask for?

My husband gets the burger, pretty much every time we go. He loves it! The fries are crispy, they have a coating on them which makes them extra crunchy. I tend to prefer fresh cut french fries (think 5 Guys Burgers) but he really likes these! Overall a 5 star experience! Love this little gem that keeps getting better with time!!

We visited My Pie and ordered 3 pizzas to-go. We hadn't tried them before, but we have had Mod Pizza before and figured it would be very similar since it's the same concept. We were pretty disappointed. I wasn't a fan of the sauce, the pizzas didn't have nearly enough cheese, and overall I felt like their ingredients weren't the best quality. I love the concept of this restaurant, as we all usually want something slightly different on our pizzas, but I think we will stick with Mod in the future.

Fantastic food and amazing customer service! And this is coming from a girl who was born in Vietnam and knows authentic Vietnamese food! The gentleman who always takes my orders is always smiling and cheerful! Portions are generous. The decor is just right for the family friendly and comfortable restaurant it is! Even though I live in Chicago, I always make sure I stop by there for food every time I'm in St. Louis! Our favorite dish is the Bo Luc Lac, just writing this review is making me drool! Love,love, love this place!

First the Positive: Ambiance!  Cool layout, nice bar areas, wall-hung fireplace, sports on TVs over bars.

Negatives: Service - Don't get me wrong, they are nice people, but they just don't know what they are doing.  It feels like you are over at another couple's house for dinner and they have their teenage kids dressed up like waiters and they are walking around not knowing what to do.  You have to wave furiously to get their attention away from the Xbox for a minute to get another drink or to place your order.  Their parents think it's cute, but you wish you had stayed home.

The sushi was ok, but not professional.  What I mean is the rolls are "loose" and what I like to call "trash can" rolls where the chef throws everything in them and on them to create flavor, but the chunks of ingredients are too big and don't meld together so it just doesn't look or taste  professional.  It's kind of like being at that same couple's house for dinner and the husband read a book on "how to make sushi," so he wants to try out some new recipes on you as he learns how to roll them properly.

The place was easy to get a seat.  They had many empty tables, but they all had tacky "Reserved" signs on each one.  Reserved for who??

My suggestion: Go there for drinks, ambiance, and maybe an appetizer with your date, but save the big sushi dinner for another place in town.
The pizza is uniquely fresh and California-like here in the Midwest. Great ambience too!

Waiting for their liquor license, only reason for the 4 star. Great decor, service, and food. Loved their burgers and grilled Brie with bacon and tomato. My daughter was busy playing with the tool box that is packed with toys.

Good God A-mighty! Had the pork tenderloin and was enough food to eat on for 3 days. Everything was so flavorful. Soul food at its best. With that being said, my friend ordered biscuits and gravy and I can't recommend the gravy-- it is not what you would normally expect, very spicy and brown, just not my style but everything else we had there was delicious. Really cool family owned and operated atmosphere where you can talk with the chef as he's making the food.

More spacious than the other Tria near Rittenhouse, this one offers a more intimate experience without as much noise and bustle.  If you really want peace, head up to the second floor and crawl into a wine bottle...never to emerge.  Food is comparable to the other Tria, with the truffled egg toast and fontina being a major score.  Get it, but don't check your cholesterol for awhile.

Aj and I always order Chinese food from here. He's been going since he was young. The food here is always very deliciously flavored and the quality is always fresh. I've ate at a lot of Chinese food places in my life, but this is one of the best. It's family own and run, so you can count on the taste. 
I forgot to write reviews all this time, but here's a Szechuan Shrimp customized to have only string beans and broccoli. The Crab Rangoon appetizer is a crunchy, cheesy, yummy must order. I also bought the pork egg roll and a wonton soup. Sodas here are $1 a can.

Ordered pizza 2 hours ago, called 3 times and spoke with the same woman. Each time she had a different story for me, ranging from having the wrong name of the order to not having my phone number and also not having the drivers phone number. I received a call 2 hours later, saying that they had to remake the pizza and resend it because the first order was sent back. They didn't even try to call me!!!!!! If I could give this place 0 stars, I would. On top of that, after cancelling my order and asking refund it, the guy said he couldn't do it through my debit card. Unbelievable.
Good BBQ! one of the only BBQ joints on state st. $2 for 2 sliders on tuesday are my favorite. oh and the mac and cheese balls! So glad to see this place is doing well!

Disclaimer: I know it's Easter Sunday and "The Houl" was open, we were starving after church and needed some drinks/snacks. By the end of the meal Houlihan's showed us that next year (if they are still in business) they should consider being closed. Why? They were suffering from staffing and quality issues in the kitchen, the bar tender was too oblivious to look up a simple drink recipe, the food runner did not know the difference between lettuce wraps and tuna wontons,  and I had to get my own roll ups from the manager so that my wheelchair bound mother could eat.
I usually don't care enough to write more than a few lines about any dining experience but this was an unusually poor showing and has really left a poor taste in my mouth. Below is a rundown of how the meal spiraled down the tubes. 
Tuna wontons: We didn't order the wontons. However, when the runner dropped off the plate she said, "Lettuce wraps?"  I said that they were not lettuce wraps and she was already out of ear shot. Our server did let us eat them and later even had them voided from the check.
Meatloaf:  I had a few bites and it was really good.
Spaghettini: Overall not a bad dish, however, for $ 15.95 I would expect some spices and some asiago and/or parmesan cheese to warrant this high price.
Sm.  Shrooms: I am a big fan.
Chicken Fajita: A mediocre presentation at best. Too much oil on the non-sizzling skillet, the chicken was dry, flavorless, and the portion was undersized for what "they" charge. The guacamole was good, the salsa was not, and the peppers were not cooked enough.
Steak wedge salad: Because the core was never removed from the lettuce wedge the dish was immediately not pleasing to the eye because it looked like it had just come unwashed from the field. The steak had been ordered to be cooked medium but when it was cut open at the table turned out to be cooked just a few minutes beyond well done. 
Lettuce wraps: A fairly good appetizer but not worth $ 8.75 when comparing it to P.F. Chang's lettuce wraps that are delicious and only cost $ 7.50.
3's company: Do not include the Chocolate cappuccino cake with this order. The offering really did not taste good and suffered from texture issues as well.
Brandy Alexander: The first meager portion came out served in a rocks glass and tasted like ice milk that had been watered down w/ a splash of crème de cacao (Never taken off the check). After complaining about the portion size and the severe low quality of the drink our server brought a second one that was served in the proper cocktail glass and tasted quite good. The third drink had a bit more brandy than the second but that is a good thing.
Overall: Sunday nights is half off drinks, wine, and beer in the "bar only."  Well, we would have gladly sat in the bar but one of our people is wheel chair bound and is in no way able to belly up. Therefore, we requested the closest wheelchair accessible table to the bar area and were happy we could watch celebrity apprentice when it started at 8 pm. Of course after our server takes our drink order at 7:55 pm I asked him if the first round would be full price because it was not 8 yet and he said "the special is only for the bar area." I told him that we would relocate to "the bar area" but my mother who is the person in the wheel chair said in a very snippy tone that we would be leaving. The server returned and said that we could have our discount. How generous, thank you so much Houlihan's,

Been coming here since I was a kid and they continue to provide excellent quality NY bagels. The closest to real NY bagels with out actually being in NY and certainly the best I've had in Florida. They bake them fresh every morning. My only complaint would be they don't keep well after you take them home.

I was very disappointed in the pastrami sandwich on an everything bagel which I ordered. I had seen pictures of this on an advertisement and it looked delicious so I was very much looking forward to having this for lunch.
 The everything bagel looked nothing like the picture in the advertisement. It was pale and had hardly any everything. The sandwich consisted of one thin slice of pastrami one slice of cheese a cut-up pickle and a little mustard. I asked for extra mayo on the side and was given a minuscule amount in a cup. In my consideration this was not a suitable sandwich it had hardly any content and was all pale bagel.
 Seems like the advertising which showed a healthy looking picture of this sandwich was false because it was nothing like the picture

to be honest, I like my coffee shops a little grungy, a little rude, and with lots of table space. satellite was just a little TOO grungy for my taste. 
service was lovely when I was there, despite some of the other reviews...

Long overdue review. One of my favorite places in town. I randomly stumbled upon it a few weeks after I moved to Reno and has been a favorite of mine ever since. It reminds me so much of Grand Central Station in NY, Grand Central Market in LA, or Mercado de San Jacinto in Mexico City. As someone who works from work, I need a change of scenery once in a while and this is a nice place to set up shop. I can work from there, have coffee, a healthy meal and do some shopping. When I first discovered there were just a few shops but that is changing. I like how the businesses complement each other: Escape, Chomp and Rawbry seem to work together to promote an active, healthy lifestyle. The shops also make a smart use of the space and collaborate to cross promote. A few months ago, The Basement hosted a yoga class in hand with Juice Box Yoga and the Rawbry offered discounts to the attendees. Or the hand soap in the bathrooms is provided by The Pantry, a fellow vendor. Sugar Love holds Sugar Love University at the community space. In a nutshell this is a beautiful and smart space and see myself spending more time there in the months to come. A one stop shop for all the things I like: exercise, coffee, fresh food and chocolate.

I so enjoyed coming here! The atmosphere was lovely, and the waiter was very knowledgable and attentive.  The food was great, especially the potato croquettes. What really impressed me about the service was after I accidentally knocked over and spilled a drink and started to clean it up, the waiter graciously came over and quickly finished cleaning it up for me. Then, he brought me a replacement drink without me asking for one which I thought was really nice!

So this is an inexpensive little restaurant on Olive Street. It has a large menu of various items including burgers, steaks, and chicken wings. This isn't high end dining but tasty American food. I preserved the spicy chicken sandwich and it was great. Breaded chicken that actually had a kick to it. The Fries were fine but generic although they had some seasoning which was nice. The staff were friendly and the food was made to order. We'll be back!

Snapshot: 5/5 Authentic, 5/5 Atmosphere 5/5 Price & Quality

When the locals and Yelp say go...you venture out. Though it was an hour wait, the Maple Leaf Bar is next store door which offers stiff drinks and local beers at a college prices.

If you are looking for fresh seafood with amazing sides and local cuisine, there's nothing better.

The service is prompt and attentive. Price point is very reasonable. Less than $30 for the entry which includes two sides plus a salad.

The ride or drove down St. Charles is entraining. 

Tip: Get there early as they don't take reso's!

I'm confused by the reviews here. Bella roma has been our go to place for 4 years now since we moved to springfield. We've always had excellent service and the pizza is always excellent. I tell everyone who we meet how great it is and how thankful I am to have found a good pizza place. We've ordered maybe a dozen pizzas over the years and it's always been fantastic. My opinion at least is that Bella Roma is a fantastic pizza place.

This place is very good. I do the pad pak rUam spicy. The lunch specials are  great. Soup and salad are solid. I may actually prefer this over sawasdee for certain dishes, but they are very similar in quality/taste. My #1 Thai restaurant still remains Thai Taste in metro Indy. I've ALMOST  tried everyone.

The almond croissant is amazing. The almond filling I believe is homemade. The pastry is very crispy. Next time I will try chocolate almond. They have other croissants such as pistachio, hazelnut, berries. Their baguette is really good too especially when it just comes out from the oven. Cash only.

Service a 2!!! We were rushed.... Not just rushed----pushy!!!

Food a 4.5!!!  Phenomenal!

We told the waitress we wanted to enjoy our cocktails and appetizers before we ordered our entrees.  We were denied!   Same thing happened with dessert and coffee!
She would not allow us to order appetizers without an entree order at the same time. Our food came out almost simultaneously!  However, the food was phenomenal!  
Because the food was so perfect, we will be returning for another visit. I do hope the service will be improved upon on our next visit or I will not be returning for a third.
I enjoyed a BANGIN' oyster salad and deliciously spicy Bloody Mary!
It's a slow bar. I like the food because it was pretty good fusion. Don't expect authentic experience here but it's good to get drunk on and have fusion and feel fancy in.
Nice large location for big groups. Food is Average not great not bad. We had a good time and enjoyed checking out the race car and garage through the window.

I just wanted a quick bite for lunch so I stopped in to grab a Gianni with prosciutto, sharp provolone, and roasted red peppers.  As with any other Primo's, you have to order the Primo size in order to get the seeded Sarcone's roll.  The sandwich was good with a nice balance of flavors and the prosciutto was good for a chain.  It's pricier than Durham Deli but the seeded rolls are great and it's aeons better than Subway.  Plus, I get to eat the leftovers for dinner since a primo size will easily last two meals.  Service was fast.

Best.

I have nothing bad to say about these guys, they're doing Mexican Jesus' work and showering Fishtown with tacos as God intended.

I've tried most of their dishes and enjoyed the living fuck out of each one.

Drunken midnight nachos and Margaritas is a guilty pleasure.

Viva la flatulence!!
When everything you ordered is wrong that's one thing, but then on top of it you get next to no meat. This taco literally has 2 pieces. The burrito bowl you could fit the meat on a single chip.

Amazing place, great bar, prompt service good hookahs. The food is fantastic, one of the best hummus in Nola. Definitely what the city needed. The service is great, Sierra has been my server every time and she's amazing.

Insanely good. Mind blowingly good. 

I don't want to over hype this place so you go and are disappointed... but I really don't know how that could happen. 

My dad is an Italian chef by profession so I feel like I have a prettttty good idea of this cuisine and this place is OUT OF THIS WORLD. 

Like no surprise given who runs it, but seriously go here. My family went and we all did the chefs tasting. You can choose what you want for this but we let the chefs surprise us and every course was delicious. 

*also it's very decently priced for the superb food you are getting. 

I will be back here and again and you need to go.

Ate here twice while visiting Franklin for the Main Street Festival and the food and service were great!  I got the chicken salad sandwich both times and loved it!!  The skillet pecan cobbler is to die for and the onion rings are really good too!!  Will be back!

This is my favorite place in Wesley Chapel to go when I am wanting tacos, nachos, or chimichangas. The food is always prepared fresh and fast and at an affordable price. My go to is the steak nachos. They load up the nachos and is a lot more than a single person could eat. It is a meal for two easily. The tacos are also great and they have many options to satisfy and craving or taste.  It is easy to pass them by and not notice, but I would recommend anyone to stop in and get hooked on this gem in Wesley Chapel.

We went there only for a drink after having lunch... And we saw the ahi tuna and it looked delicious!!.. Then we decided to try it, and it was Awesome!!.. I didn't try the rest of the menu, but the appetizers looked good, and the drinks were incredible!!... We had a great time there!!

Fabulous place to go. STRICT ON FACE MASKS. It gets busy you may have to wait a bit for a table. Great food and service. Great for couples and families. Would most definitely return when we're in the area. Come with an appetite and a sense of humor.

3 need to knows

$30 bottles of wine - ALL OF THEM
No menu Monday
Constantly changing menu

Culinary artistry at it's best.  I mean you really ante up and  say "we're great in the kitchen" when you're willing to forego a menu one day a week and just "wing it," with no menu.  Home Wine Kitchen definitely delivers.  I'm not even going to talk about the dish I had because chances are it will never make it back to the menu because of the diversity this place has.  Just know the sentence "I ordered X and it was delicious."  

If you like to order the same thing at restaurant every time, then this may not be your restaurant.  Then again if you like to order the same thing at a restaurant every time, let's not hang out.  However if you like delicious fresh veggies, hand cut meats, everything local, and well priced wines then this is your joint.

Service was awesome, waiter was very knowledge (which is a necessity in a place like this), food was prepared exactly as requested and was delivered in a timely manner.  The ambiance really was like hanging out in your own house with some friends, very cozy and intimate with a lower volume level.

PHOTOS UPLOADED 

If you love soup and salad, then this is the place for you. We finally tried this place. After driving by it thousands of times, we decided to stop by for an early dinner. 

PROS: 

~ Excellent service. The staff is friendly and cheerful. 

~ Clean and relaxed ambiance. 

~ Dishes are flavorful. The cheddar broccoli soup is tasty. 

~ Locally owned. 

~ Ingredients are fresh. 

~ My toddler enjoyed their food too. 

CONS: 

~ Parking can be a challenge. 

~ The restaurant is a bit small. 

~ Menu is limited. 

~ Does not accept American Express. 

It is such a gem. I wish this place will become successful and will be able to move to a larger place and provide better parking.

A great lunch!  We enjoyed fresh ingredients in carefully prepared sandwiches.  Healthy alternatives abound.  Fast service!  Cucumber water self-service. Limited table space.  I believe many customers carry out.  It is hard to think of other sandwiches I enjoyed more than at this place.  While $13 sandwiches are a bit pricy, they are worth it.  We look forward to a return visit.

This was ok, but I'm not really going out of my way to return.  The garlic bread was very good as was the salad so I had high hopes for the entrees.  Totally dissatisfied with the bolognese.  The pasta was over cooked and the sauce basically tasteless.  I really wanted to love this place because the atmospheres very cozy and welcoming but food was just not what I expected.
Not very impressed. Gave it a try after many years. Disappointed.  Cost a lot though. What are u gonna do? Sorry but this is true. Food taste like leftovers.

Came here because my friend wanted me to try the Sparkling White Sangria... Unfortunately, I didn't have my driver's license with me so I couldn't get one myself.
