This Eritrean restaurant was a wonderful experience! The food was authentic and delicious and the staff was kind and professional. I would recommend this restaurant, especially to  those who enjoy an international experience.

GREAT BURGERS!!!! Hands down the best in ALLL of Nashville , that includes all its sub cities.... Also had a chocolate malt milkshake , pretty good I must say! Atmosphere is good , a chill and diverse crowd , chill music , good waiters , about 1000 different kinds of beers lol

Got the pleasure of trying their old spot in gretna and immediately fell in love with this family and their love for food. Was anticipating their opening on magazine and they met ever expectation. Went with my parents when they were in town and we shared a lot of different things. What stands out was their fun cocktails and the oyster appetizer. We got a goat dish and a bunch of the Roti Sathi. Again everything was fantastic. I would highly suggest this restaurant for those who like to support local families, you can meet the family who truly loves what they do, and can taste such wonderful eclectic foods.

I don't get what the big hoop-la is about this place!  Yes, it is sushi, that's it.
Let's keep this short and sweet.  First, what the heck is up with the menu? Manilla folders and office paper....WOW.   Secondly, the sushi was eh.. a level above mediocre. Third, service was awkward; not very personable.  

I just don't get it? Is it the clientele, the location?  I mean come on, let's be honest.

Saw this place on the entertainment book as a buy one get one dinner and figured why not? Never had Moroccan dinner before and boy was this amazing! SEVEN COURSES! Tiny little spot on a side street off South, you ring a doorbell to be allowed in and the place is two floors and packed! My girl got a glass of wine(they fill the whole thing up ) and it's only four Bucks a glass! Food was superb! Best dinner of the weekend

We love this place. After a day of fishing or the beach this is the perfect place to go to sit by the dock and watch the boats go by. Weekend ceviche and a couple of Jai Alai IPA drafts and I'm in Florida heaven. It's fun to watch the boats come in and dock. We rate the docking skills as each one comes in. You can tell the boat owners from the renters. I'm sure I would fall in the latter category. Grouper sandwiches are awesome also. Disregard the reviews that complain that they run out of things. They get it fresh, and sometimes they run out. It's not like they can just pull it out of the freezer... That's what authentic is all about. I've never seen them run out of grouper though. Small, authentic, rustic, and local. That's the experience I want, and I get it here.

I ordered egg drop soup and their Chinese lunch special which came with fried rice and sesame chicken. Normally comes with 2 enrolls but I got extra rice. 

The soup was good, not the best I've had by good

The fried rice had nothing in it. It was just plain ol rice tossed in sauce. The sesame chicken was ok.

Tequila has gone downhill. 

We stopped in for lunch the other day and we remembered why we hadn't been there in a while.

1) Slow and rude server
2) Tasteless foods smoothered in cheese
3) Margarita that tasted like dish water
4) Decent chips and OK salsa

Too bad since it's only 5 min from our home.

This place is a 3.5. What I like is the food and drink. Everything was awesome. The appies, the meal and the drinks. Also the place is a good looking Irish pub. While the server was super nice it took 5 minutes for drinks. Also when I ordered a Ceaser I got a salad not the drink I wanted. I mean I would totally go back, even the prices are pretty good.

Good Dog is one of my favorite bars in Philly.  They have an excellent beer selection which changes pretty frequently.  

Their food is awesome -- I usually go with the Good Dog burger which is off the charts.  This place has a great vibe - ususally pretty crowded and dark inside, there are 3 floors as well.  If you get there at the right time you may be able to score a booth downstairs which is great.  

Overall - great food, great beers, great spot!

The people that work here are very warm and welcoming and the food is excellent! One of the best places in Nashville for dinner. The rooftop is amazing and the VIP manager Fabiano is very accommodating. Highly recommend this place for a beer or nice date night.

This location is bullshit Bc all the time the I go to.. don't have anything and even when is a daylight the employee doesn't do there job. And never have the food on time.. is so pretty bad store I don't recommend go to

My wife ordered the fish and chips, while I opted for the fish burrito. We were both pleased with our meal. The fish was crunchy on the outside, moist and flavorful on the inside. My fish burrito was also good and huge; I had to use a fork to eat it. The fries were crisp. The outside patio area was the perfect place to enjoy lunch over an ocean view.

We'll be back.

The best happy hour deal in Reno. It's half off and the menu is amazing. My family LOVES the oysters and Ahi (used to be tacos now it's nachos). The flatbreads are also great and the "sexy fries" are a dream for any truffle fans out there. Award winning cocktails -- we love the jalemango and the chocolatini-- and great wine list! Happy hour is over at 6pm but the will give you a last call and usually are lenient on exact timing.

If Ursula ran a seafood place this would be what it's like, food is bland and makes red lobster look like gourmet, plus the food prices are ridiculous, only fish smell is from the upstairs bar after 9pm when the 21 year old WCU girls start drinking fishbowls

"GET THE BRISKET!!!!!!" It's  so good you don't need your teeth to chew it. Only need your tongue and the roof of your mouth to mash it into baby food Bar B Que paste. By far the best I've had in a long time. My wife and I will definitely be going back on our next visit to New Orleans.
Hmmmm. ya got to like some biscuits.  Wanted some eggs and got 2 eggs over easy in what could be described tomato soup.  Wasn't half bad.

This place is hit or miss.  I have been here for breakfast and dinner a few times and each time was a different experience.  The food is not consistent (sometimes good, sometimes bad). And worst of all they don't accept credit cards! I know go figure in this day and age.  The food I would give 2 stars but I added a star because the staff has always been friendly and the bakery actually has really good pies.

Um YUM!! So so good. I recently moved down the street and decided to give this place a try and I can say right now it will be a regular stop for me. We got pizza and queso dip and it was heaven in my mouth. The pizza is amazing and filling and the queso dip is unlike any I've ever had but I can't put my finger on what spices they use. The prices were beyond reasonable. I will say we waited a while for out food, I think the pizza took a while but it was worth the wait. The service was great, friendly and efficient. So yummy!

let me start off with telling you that I drive about 30 minutes out of my way to get this delicious food.  There are 2 king wong's but the one on rt 70 is still ran by the owners.  The other one was sold and you know how it is, because people get cheap and sacrifice quality for quantity.  But anyways, I grew up on king wong and I recently moved but I am still loyal to this place.  They always have fresh food, and everything on the menu is absolutely delicious.  I've been to other restaurants in my area and nothing compares to king wong.  If you want fresh chinese, this is the place to go no questions asked. It is a takeout place so don't expect to come there with a family. you have to go here!!
I love Marko's. Nothing better than a fish sandwich on their fresh bread with peppers, onions, and pickles!  Branko and His team take great care of us.

I'm not a Pho expert but I've been trying Pho at a few local places and this is still one of my favorites. When not ordering Pho, I've enjoyed their other dishes as well. Staff is friendly and if you have any questions about any of their dishes, they are happy to explain. Place is kept clean and neat and the food is fresh.

This review is for their only their sushi . I went here for their happy hour and i was not impressed. 

First off, 
I wasnt impressed because there were flies flying around everywhere and i saw a fly inside the sashimi case... Talk about gross. I also saw a fly fly onto the waiting to be delivered sushi and the sushi chef saw that i saw that so he took it off the counter and made a new one to be delivered. The sea weed in the rolls were stale . The rolls also had alot of rice and not alot of content in it js untasty rice . The price is good for their happy hour if only the sushi was decent but i would NOT come back here, maybe to try their teppanyaki and for sake bombs .
It just doesn't get any better than here, best fish I've ever had including in Japan hard to say that service even better congratulations to Morimoto for being here!
Loved the ambience. Amazing taste! My only issue was they have only a couple of options in chicken. Otherwise great place to try.
Way too expensive, $14 for a very small glass of wine, food ok but $150 for 2 entree's of pasta, will never return.

Good food but not always. There were times when I was served stuff that has gone bad. Eg: chutney, tandoori chicken.etc.

You don't have to gamble with food.

I really wanted to like this place but was dissapointed. Why the "geekery" theme is a cool idea it didnt make up for the lack of service. They just dont seem to have their act together with the kitchen and bar. My husband who is never a complainer had to tell upwards of three people he had yet to receive his beer and yet still took over 20 mins for him to get it. The place was busy but not THAT busy. I felt like the servers were trying but some how there was no communication between the servers, bar and kitchen. My entire party waited about 15-20 mins per drink order, some just completely forgotten. The service just felt akward an disorganized and food was mediocre at best. I hope this place can get its act together because I would like see it succeed but they have some work to do.
They argued with me because I asked for steamed rice instead of white rice. Instead of fixing my order, I was in a heated 30 minute argument

First, Reno is not well known for food (well, probably not well known for anything, but I'll try not to anger the Reno Yelpers)... so I was surprised that there was a sushi restaurant in Reno (that people actually encouraged me to try). The food here is actually pretty good. Not sure how fresh the fish was but no one got sick so that's a good sign. The rolls were a bit on the "excessively" flavored side (a.ka. salty and/or too sweet) but overall not bad. The line at the door was a bit discouraging but we only waited for about 20-25 minutes on a Saturday night at 6:30pm so the line isn't as bad as it appears. We opted for the "all-you-can-eat" option which was great except for the time it took for the food to come out. What they do is they have you check off on the sushi list which ones you want and they bring them to you one by one... this somewhat took away from the all "all-you-can-eat" experience since you get full just waiting around and drinking tea. I can't give this place more than 3 stars since I think its just average, but if you're ever in the Reno area and feel like sushi, this place is the place to try.

Who cares where the owner is from. He has the best spanish food in Pinellas Park and is the last Spanish restruant standing. All the others never made it. He is a family man and the food is very good. That is all that matters.
Impeccable friendly service and the taste of the food is as wonderful as it is displayed on the plate. I have been going for years and it never disappoints! Absolutely Amazing! The best cafe around!

Omg this pizza is awesome!! I first found out about pizza at work. They ordered like four to six  28" plain and pepperoni pizzas. It was    so good. What catches my eye is how it's the slices are so big and long!! Getting the pizza into the house was so funny, the pizza and pizza box is so big that it doesn't even fit through the door but we tilted it and it finally got it into the house. It was really good my family and I usually can get through a large pizza in minutes we didn't even make dent into this one lol. I read all the reviews and I love this place and the service was also really awesome! Coming back again!!

I would have given Dugout bar a better review, but my experience was less than perfect. The only highlight of my experience was the food. The grilled pork tenderloin was wonderful and one of the best pork tenderloin I've had in a while. Chase, our server,  was good to our table and gave us good service,  but one of the women who waited on us on the patio was very rude and was going to cut us off from having drinks because she thought we were affiliated with a group of people who just got off the pickle pedaler and were totally smashed.  We were not affiliated with the group and we had just arrived and ordered a drink when she waited on us, so she had no right to cut us off from ordering alcohol.   The woman was dressed in black and had a ponytail, brown hair.   Thank God Chase saved the day and smoothed things over with us, so we were able to order a beer with him.  Needless to say, because of this incident,  I doubt I will be coming back to Dugout bar for a beer or food anytime soon.  If you do decide to come to Dugout Bar, just be careful with who your server is at your table and don't come off of the pickle pedaler, because you will not be served alcohol from Dugout bar if you do.  Be smart and just come to Dugout bar to have one beer and chill out with friends.

After several months in Indianapolis, this has to be my favorite place!!

Great atmosphere, great service, great wine, and great food. We were a party of about 12 people. Everything we ordered was amazing (and we tried most things). When we walked in we were enamored with the herb wall. The staff working on plating the meals noticed us staring and plucked a few fresh items for us to try as he explained the hydroponic setup they had.  

Bonus: They frequently change the menu so there are always new dishes popping up!

Well done. Hope to see their continued success.

The service was extremely friendly, but the food was mediocre-to-moderate. The meat was not cooked with any sauce on it, so it just tastes pretty much boiled with sauce added after the fact. Plus, probably a quarter of the meat on the pulled pork sandwich was fat that had to be pulled off first. Decent meal, but we will explore other options in the area before considering coming back.

Our experience at Taco Mamacita was great! I've been wanting to try this place for a while, and what better time than after a long 12 hour shift on a Sunday. We were greeted by and very friendly hostess who quickly seated us outside on their cozy patio (don't remember her name but she said she was a new employee- she's doing a great job!). We decided on two things right away- queso and margaritas, of course. The pomegranate margaritas were really sweet and could've been a little stronger, but were still yummy. Next came our queso. It was so delicious and was exactly what we needed after a long day at work. Basically, we devoured it. 

For our entree, we ordered tacos. This was such a great deal- two tacos and a side for $8 and change. They were a good size and the selection is great. I had a really hard time deciding because they all sounded so delicious! Ultimately, I chose the General Homeboy and the Oy Vey with plantains for my side. I was really happy with the way everything turned out! I was only able to eat half of both my tacos, however, because I accidentally filled up on queso. Oops! Leftovers are never a bad thing. 

I would definitely recommend this place, and will return soon. Ps. On Sunday nights sangria is half off and you can get an entire carafe for $7!

I'm not a fan of Chinese food. However, this place changed my opinion! Best Chinese food I've had around the Newark/Main Street area. I go here with my friends all the time! Wonderful service and great prices as well!

Absolutely outstanding!  Tampa needs MANY MANY more places like this.

The place is beautiful to look at; right down to the colanders-turned-lights above the tables.  :)   A little industrial meets clean and elegant in a great old building; the layout is simple and open, which I can see being noisy if you arrive at prime time.

The bartender comes from years at Gaspar's and is one of the top in Tampa - quick, friendly, and knows his game very well.   Kudos for scooping him up, Domani.

We were with a large group for a birthday, and the service was impeccable.  Dueling servers, sharing responsibilities (none of the "this person takes these people, the other those", etc) and absolutely on top of everything from start to finish.

The food was beyond our expectations for a newish place; the creative menu is loaded with everything from burgers to ahi yellowfin, bacon-wrapped pork tenderloin, mussels, brie/pistachio-wrapped grapes, stuffed grape leaves... the list goes on.  

We had a sampling of almost everything between the group and there wasn't one thing anyone didn't like - and that's something with this group.

Many great combinations of flavors and outstanding presentations for all; right down to the s'mores martini for our birthday guest at the end.

All-in-all we can't wait to go back - with the existing menu, the execution of the kitchen and the perfect service, withouut a doubt they'll be around a long time!

 -B
Had the One Meat One Side selection,  tried the pulled pork and baked beans with garlic pita bread ...Simply put it was delicious, outstanding, excellent. Will definitely be back for some more.

I was in Kirkwood shopping at Global foods and stopped at First Watch for breakfast. I was seated in the back corner. I looked over the menu and was only interested in the standard breakfast. Several servers came to other tables near me but seemed to ignore me. I figured there was a specific server for my table. After 14 minutes and 3 groups who were seated after me recieved coffee and water, I got up and handed my menus to the closet server and left. At Spencer's now, review to follow.
Wonderful food and great staff!!! Everyone has good attitudes and help eachother when needed to make sure all the guests are happy.

This is a beautiful temple/restaurant. The buffet isn't large but it is very good and inexpensive. The staff is super nice and their festivals are phenomenal. I highly recommend going to their Krishna birth festival.

When you're done eating, you should take a walk around the grounds and go visit the altars, aviary, koi fish pond, and goldfish pond. They have peacocks and love birds. ^-^
Pizza was great! Lots of pizza options to choose from and delicious crust. Had it delivered via grubhub and still enjoyed it! Definitely worth a try!

Update. Ate here yesterday for a late lunch. It was ridiculously hot. I asked if their AC was broken, and they said that they had opened their windows earlier and then when it got warm, they didn't want to close them and turn on the AC because they didn't want to bother the patrons. And that they hadn't anticipated the heat. Huh? First, it was all over the news that the temps were going up to 86. Second, just don't sit people there by the windows when they come in and when eventually the front clears out, close the windows and turn on the AC. Our server was very nice, but it took 50 minutes to get our food. It was not that full BTW.  Asked for salt and pepper and finally had to get up and get them ourselves, as well as a second beer for our group.
My favorite hamburger was not as I remembered. It used to be the best in town. Someone in the kitchen was off his/her game yesterday.
I go here a lot and I've noticed that it is very hit and miss. Sometimes it is really great, other times not so much.
I have been here twice and both times it was ok. Pretty good food, but definitely overrated for all the hype. The atmosphere is crowded and loud. I much prefer the food and atmosphere at Nada.

Can't believe I waited so long to try this place. We typically get barbeque from another local restaurant that we like, but this was even better!  It was easy to order a family meal on their website and it was ready and waiting for pickup at the time we requested. You know ribs are good when they are so flavorful that you don't even need the sauce! Pulled pork, chicken, and sausages were all moist and flavorful. My toddler loved the fried pickles and ranch. Baked beans were great with nice hunks of meat in the sauce. Cornbread was also moist and delicious with just enough sweetness that it was actually the perfect dessert. Only thing I didn't care for was the coleslaw because it was on the sweet side and "chopped" instead of shredded, but that's just personal preference and there are plenty of other side options to choose from. We'll definitely be back again and again. I can't wait to try the fried fish and fried chicken lunch special.

The outside of this place looks dull and unappealing but once you get inside it's just a nice diner vibe. It's basically a cheaper version of red lobster with way better food. I have had tons of items here and the portions are always huge and the food is always cooked amazing. It's a great place if you want to come in and relax and enjoy Florida seafood. They also have some good draft beer prices. I highly suggest stopping in here if you want some good seafood with nice service.
Decided to give this place another try. 45 minutes for a salty burger, and only 3-4 other groups in the restaurant on a Sunday at noon.

Can you say authentic? Tucked away, in the heart of this grocery store is a little restaurant with the tastiest tacos. The tacos are a great price, for around $2.15. If you're feeling bold try the cow tongue, if not that's okay they also have chicken, steak, and I believe pork. It's usually a pretty quick wait time unless you arrive around lunch time because the secret is finally out about the great food you can get here! The food is made is front of you, and the taste and quality reflect such. While you're in the store, browse their produce section. They always have onions and limes for much less than Marsh or Meijer and also look fresher.

This small place is near the University of South Florida.  I ended up there after doing a yelp search of seafood restaurants.  I love seafood.  I had shrimp tacos with blackened-shrimp.  They were delicious.  The shrimp had a crispy quality I associate with very fresh shrimp.  Have you ever had mushy, twice frozen shrimp?  Not here.

It's an order-at-the-counter place with hard tables and chairs (not that many).  Service was fast and attentive.  Food was excellent.  Five stars.

I'm giving them 5 stars for quality,
unique flavors and friendliness.   

Have been here twice in the last week.  It would have been 3 x but one afternoon they were completely sold out of donuts!  

In addition to standards they have Mango w/ Coconut cream topping, Butterfinger, Red Velvet cake, Boston Creme Pie, S'mores and many more.  

Brewed coffee is from Brazil and very good.  

If this place was open in the evening-I'd come here for dessert after dinner.
What a fantastic meal! Excellent service, great kids meals and the food was to die for (bbq bacon wrapped shrimp). Prices were also reasonable.
Great beer selection, excellent service, and fantastic Irish style pub food! I truly loved this place and the servers really made me feel welcome. The Crowley's Pie is a must!

I live just a few blocks from Big Dan's.  I have to tell you, there aren't many restaurants within walking distance where I am not afraid to eat.  But, what a SURPRISE I was in for when I walked into Big Dan's.

My favorites are the 11th St. Italian Hoagie and Dan's cheese steak.

There are no cheap ingredients used in the 11th St.  Top of the line Italian meats are used along with sharp provolone.  This is one of the best hoagies I have ever had.  The roll is perfect, the meats are beyond good and the price isn't too bad.

Everyone likes their cheese steak done their way.  I like mine with fried onions, marinara sauce and sharp provolone.  When I bit into this steak, I thought I was in heaven.  You can't compare Dan's fresh sliced rib-eye with some frozen minute steak.  The fresh roll is packed so full I have to use a fork to eat what falls out.  Absolute heaven!

What a gem of a place I found on the corner of 11th and Jackson.  I am now a regular and everyone knows my name.  Can't wait until they get their "Best of Philly" award.

My morning was off to a rough start but Celeste turned it around with her fantastic service! The food was prompt,  she was polite and attentive as everything was delicious. This is by far my favorite breakfast food chain.

I've gone here three times now and it does not disappoint. 
It's a sure great location by bike or car. The trail directly connect to it. 
The outside dog area is an awesome idea and perfectly executed. Especially for people like me who don't like leaving their mutt at home! 
My two favorite dishes are the meatballs and the broccoli César salad.
Soup crackers stale, soup and egg rolls were cold, pasty noodles and old clumpy rice. Not good.
Horrible service. Waiter ignored all of our needs and reached across my face constantly to grab food

Awesome spot in an up-and-coming hood.  I've been here about once a week for the past 4 and each time I've come there has been a new selection of beers to choose from and a special of some sort to take advantage of.  I'd hate to blow this for myself, but on Tuesday nights, it's 3.50 domestic drafts.  "Pork Me Sundays" discounts the pork dishes on the menu and might be the best name for a promotion ever.

I've tried some really great pours here, all perfect for the winter - McNeil's Dark Angel, Laughing Dog DogZilla Black IPA and Bell's Best Brown Ale.

Really good pub grub in general--tasty salads, solid sandwiches (you can get them with a salad, fries or a little of both) and nachos that are simply off the hook.  Service is always tight and the bartenders know their brews.  

This place delivers everything you could possibly want and more.  It'll leave you wishing there was one on your very own street corner.

Food is good but 25 mins to get it? Sorry. I can't afford to lose my job over this.

So I usually judge how long it takes to get food by the time I check-in to a place (on Yelp or other social media) and the time I actually get my food.  Normally, I check-in when I'm ready to order, or ready to at least enter the queue to order.

For whatever reason, despite being the 2nd people in line on an otherwise unremarkably slow day, 25 minutes elapsed between when we showed up and when our food did.  For an establishment that isn't fast food and certainly isn't gourmet, 25 minutes is an awful long time to wait to get some grub, especially for people who have a precious 60 minutes to get to lunch, eat it, and get back to work.

Given that it takes at least 10 minutes to get anywhere in Goleta because of the dreaded traffic lights and elderly drivers, you have an average of 20 minutes shaved off of your 60 minute window of time.  So, starting out with 40 minutes to enjoy a lunch, Nikka's staff consumed more than half of that time making us wait.  We had about 15 minutes to scarf down an otherwise delicious meal.

So, given all of that, what good is very tasty food if you don't have time to do anything but shovel it in your mouth?

This place is disgusting. It was so filthy, and staff didn't seem to care. Staff was nice enough and food was average, but the filth of it all put a sour taste in my mouth. We will not be going there again.

I am highly confused at all of the people that give this place five stars. Are these the only crab cakes you have ever had!?? Frozen ones from the grocery store are better than this. You're much better off going to Albie's in the Booth's Corner Farmers Market, esp for the crab bisque. There were two girls working on a Friday night when we went, and I don't think one of them cracked a smile at all during our entire meal there.

My husband and I googled bars near us to watch the Final Four. Pleasantly surprised with this bar. The staff was one of the hardest working staff I have ever seen, you could tell everyone enjoyed working together and helped each other. The food was amazing. We had the pulled pork nachos, ribs, boneless wings and traditional wings. The love music was fun as well. Katie the bar tender was awesome! I don't remember the bar tender that took care of us after Katie left but she was so kind and fun as well! Even though it is a big bar you could tell it was like home to many. If we ever come back down to Nashville we will be back!
Delicious fresh food. Can't wait to go back and eat again. Great service and easy access

If we could give this a zero star rating we would. 
The food looked promising the marketing made it seem fresh and on par with Chipotle and Moe's so we were excited to see who would come up on top. Sadly this jawn is at the bottom of the barrel and their taco neighbors across the way (The one with the Bell) puts this food order to shame.  At a whopping $41 give or take a few pennies-4 street tacos; one burrito; one kids cheese quesadilla; one side of chips and nacho cheese fresh out of the can and one side of chips and what appeared to be guacamole and more or less tasted of bland baby food and the side of rice and black beans which was conveniently left out of our pick up order bag...you can rest assured we will not be returning anytime soon.  If the overall taste of fish is something you're after or the lack of seasoning and spices in of all things 'fresh Mex' is your bag-by all means rape your wallet here.  So disappointing.  Really hoped for a better outcome.  Sad. Just sad. Looks like we're ordering a pizza now for dinner. Ugh.

It's definitely in my top two of pho places to eat in Nashville. The "special pho" in a medium bowl is less than $10 and fills me up every time. I love their egg rolls as well! Be sure to bring cash. I can't tell you how many times I've forgotten. They're good people though and have allowed me to come back and pay them on "honor code"

I really liked this place. The staff were pleasant, the menu options were pleasing and the food was good. First time trying Alligator bites.... and I liked it. The dish was seasoned very well. The grits were delicious! You won't be disappoointed after eating here.

When I have any reason to be near Santa Barbara, I make sure to save time for a meal at Stella Mare's.  Lunch or dinner, it's become a favorite.  I like everything about the experience.  Starting with the way it's decorated.  Everywhere your eye travels, there's something else interesting.  The staff offers exactly the right amount of attention - not hovering, but then you'll never want for anything either.  Did I mention the food?  While this part of California offers many great places to eat, the food at Stella Mare's is so good, and the decor and service both exceptional, so I keep postponing trying other nearby places. Sounds like I'm on the payroll.  I'm not, but I do believe in praise where praise is due.  If you want a memorable meal, lunch or dinner, alone or with a group, you'll find it at Stella Mare's.  If I didn't live hours away, I'd be there for lunch today.
Amazing. One of my favorite places in Tampa. The mac n cheese bites are to die for and the shrimp n grits were absolutely delicious. A bit on the pricey side, but well worth it. Highly recommend.

Wanted to check this place out: it's so well-situated and crappy restaurants don't last long in East Nashville. Couldn't be that bad, right?

We were ignored when we walked in, which should have been our first indication of what lay in store. We walked to the counter after a few minutes and asked if we should seat ourselves and we were sort of waved in the direction of the dining room. We chose a table and sat. 

Granted, it was a Friday night and they were busy. Our waitress came over, took drink orders, brought drinks back, took salad and dinner orders, and brought back the salad relatively quickly. So far so good. 

When the pizza appeared, the kebobs (for me; I can't eat wheat) did not appear. It also wasn't said whether they were coming at all when the pizza was dropped off. After about 10 minutes of watching my husband force down a few slices if pizza (he likened it to freezer pizza) I proceeded to try to flag down the waitress to ask her where the kebobs were. 

She IGNORED me. Every trip past the table she looked away, looked down, did not even glance at the table. Finally I stuck my hand out in her way when she had nothing in her hands, I smiled, and said "hey, are the kebobs coming--" "They're on their way," she said, interrupting me. 

Rude.

Then, when I finally did get the kebobs, they were very tasty. Good marinade, crispy from the grill, tatziki was solid. I was enjoying them and starting to forgive our waitress when I cut into a larger piece of pork and found it verrry pinkish red. When squeezed, the juice was not clear. It was red. Bloody. 

Not okay. I don't know about you, but getting trichinosis from a substandard pizza joint is NOT my idea of a good time.

By this time, we were done, ready to go,  cut our losses and get out. Waitress was on IGNORE mode and couldn't be bothered to give us our check, let alone hear about the undercooked pork. After 20 minutes, we stood up, walked to the counter and asked for our check. 

Fortunately, I didn't get food poisoning from my dinner.  But I warn all against this place. Avoid. Avoid avoid avoid.

My experience at this location was terrible. I came on a Saturday at 8:30pm. There were 7 of us at the table. The waitress took about 15 minutes to come to the table and take our drink orders, which she did not bring out until the food came. Food? What food? They completely forgot to put my order in and when I was asked if I still wanted it the waitress replied "OK AWESOME!!" when I said "don't worry about it." Very annoying. Those who got food reported the food was OK. The watermelon margaritas apparently tasted peppery.

Came here after a morning in the park, nice and close! 

I ordered the car broiled chicken sandwich, with a side of onion rings. Sandwich was very tender, and onion rings were amazing (it's nice to see a place not using bottom grade onion rings). 

My boyfriend ordered the fire hotdog, with a side of chili cheese fries. Was very impressed with both. 

Atmosphere is very old school, which gives it a great charm and the start was extremely friendly

090614/Bright, sultry, New Orleans day at the long awaited Willie Mae's for that No.#1 Fried Chicken feast. And that rave was on after a very short wait ! A bronzed crispy crust with a moist, lightly seasoned meat and a side of fried okra. Any where else is less than the best!

I'm in drink heaven.... not a straight cider fan? Yeah they have you covered! Get the Slap & Tickle mixology vodka and cider yumminess! They have a drink menu on top on of full wall of taps. Like food? Deviled eggs, crab cakes, bruschetta, and a coconut chocolate cream cookie pie! (Plus a bit more....) Staff is AMAZING! They are currently working their tails off for a group of 75 plus their Thursday Comedian night event! Not usually this busy but still super quick on service and food delivery. They love this place and it shows! Come check it out, try the SIX ONE FIVE or the Babe Magnet! Cider has never been better or easier to drink! I've been in the restaurant industry for a long time and I can see what works and what doesn't. This place has it dialed in.

The wait took awhile. We had a group of 6 and waited about 45-60 minutes. A few things were really good but others just okay. Definitely get the chargrilled oysters, they were delicious. The fried catfish was also good. However the shrimp po boy, gumbo, and sweet potato fries were nothing special.

We absolutely love this restaurant and visit every time we are in town.  It NEVER disappoints! The service and atmosphere is top notch and the food is out of this world! The tuna appetizer--melt in your mouth, Brussels sprouts are a must try, the Caesar salad is divine, crab legs are unbelievable, oysters are always fresh and wonderful, crabcake was amazing! I seriously have never had anything I didn't love!

I need to go again.  I had a pleasant experience the only time I've been.  They hook it up with the portions.  I spent about $15 on a reuben meal and the sandwich was amazing on many levels.  My girlfriend got chicken salad.  I had a bite and it was really good, but we're both picky over chicken salad, and it definitely wasn't the best we've ever had.

They give you pickled veggies as an hors d'oeuvres which was cool.  

The waiter was very polite and engaging.  We had a talk about getting thick slices of pastrami on my sandwich in the future and he said they could easily accomodate.

wanted to go out the next day to get cheesesteaks Geno's and Pat's.  They said those were just tourist traps now and Chubby's had the best cheesesteaks.  We wound up going at 11:00 a.m. on Sunday morning, with at least one relative who probably should have stayed home in bed after the late night.  I'm not an expert in authentic Philly cheesesteaks, but what I had -- a cheesesteak with whiz and onions -- was really great.  I actually ordered the whiz on the side and provolone on the sandwich, but used all of the whiz on it.  That flame orange, goopy stuff is the difference between a cheesesteak and an ordinary steak and cheese.  The pepper bar was great -- especially the "Oil Peppers" which added a lot of flavor.

The quality of this place has declined since their move from down the street.  They still have the best fries--crispy, well-seasoned, hot and yummy.  Burgers are still pretty good.  The service, however, has dropped from decent to disinterested.  Beer glasses not nearly cold enough, and the crappiest sides that go with the burgers.  NO NOT expect delicious pickled carrots when you select that option--just pre-packaged baby carrots in a crummy little plastic bag.  Get the fries.

I ordered takeout here last night. 

I called by phone and was able to place an order quickly. One thing to note, the menu on Yelp is different than the one at the restaurant. 

I ordered the Brooklyn which included a ton of cheese, sausage, pepperoni and anchovies. The food was made quick and was ready for pickup in about 15 min. 

Overall the food was hot and tasty and the service was quick and easy.

I called on Saturday Aug 1 at about 4:50 P.M. to place a to-go order. The website states that they open at 3:00 P.M. but I get that its COVID and things are weird so whatever. The person who answered immediately asked if I could hold. Sure, no problem. About 2 minutes later, the person who picked up asked if she could help me. "I want to place a to-go order." She said (so quickly and rudely that I had to ask her to say it again because I couldn't hear her the first time) that they don't open until 5:00 P.M. (which is now in about 7 minutes). I asked if she could just take my order now and I could pick up when its ready? She said no because their computers are not on yet. I would have to call back at 5:00 P.M. I waited until EXACTLY 5 and call back. Again, The person who answered immediately asked if I could hold. Sure, no problem. This time, I literally was on hold for 6 minutes (phones track your call times). The same rude woman finally picked up and asked if she could help me. "I want to place a to-go order." This time she told me that to go orders were running behind and would take AN HOUR AND A HALF TO PREPARE. How is that possible since you just opened and you just turned your computers on? I did not order from Gianinos that night nor will I ever order from Gianinos again.

Not very good customer service. Waited over 15 min for a happy hr drink. There restaurant wasn't crowded. Happy hour prices are ok. Espíritu has $5 margaritas and $2 happy hour tacos. JS. The ambulance is very nice tho.

Service is friendly, but they are overwhelmed.
Pho is pretty good, not the best I've had, but good enough to come back.
Wish their prices were $1 lower per dish, then they would be a really good deal and a weekly visit.
Their Vermicelli Bowl was hands down the best one I've ever had. The flavor, the portions, everything about it was phenomenal, well except the price, a bit pricey, but it was so YUM!
My husband really enjoyed it, and he can't wait to come back again. 
I'm just happy I found a above average Pho place in the area.
To the reviewers who said the bathroom was horrible, the bathroom I walked into was actually pretty clean and neat. You have obviously never been to bathrooms in Chinatown. That's an adventure..

Today December 25th must of the restaurants and fast food were closed we found this place, we enjoyed was a great food, good service and even though was very busy we did not wait a lot and the food was served on time, delicious.

Ordered on line from work at 1201 am . Been standing here 15 min before i was even spoken to then they were looking at me crazy cause they dont know my order. And i payed for it online.  So now im going on a half hour when im on break as a nurse. Unacceptable.  Boo on your customer service. It isnt even that busy in here.

We came for breakfast and this was a great way to start the day. Beautiful breakfast buffet until 11am with made to order eggs, biscuits including gluten free biscuits, cheddar grits, sliced prosciutto, and bacon, sausage, country potatoes. Also French toast, oatmeal and pastries. Great value and quality food. Service was attentive and Nashville friendly. Would love to return for dinner.

Absolutely ecstatic that a boba place is open in this part of St. Pete. Not only that, but that they are actually delicious. Their boba is perfectly soft. Their milk is is wonderfully and fully flavored. Some places have yet to master the milk to tea ratio for milk tea but this place has it mastered. 

Not only do they have boba and tea, they also have poké that is super flavorful. The portions are generous. I got one bowl and had enough food for two meals. 

The location is brilliant and makes it easy to get a cup of boba as you are taking a stroll down Cental Ave. The only downside is that parking can be a headache on Central. 

I will definitely be coming back to this place.

This was one of the best meals I've had in New Orleans, which, considering most things in this town are covered in butter and deliciousness, says a lot. In particular, I usually dislike BBQ Shrimp but that dish is really fantastic here. The sauce is unreal and there is definitely a reason it's their signature dish.

Indianapolis is a city of neighborhoods. For many of us there is the search for that perfect neighborhood haunt. If you live in NW (and even if you don't) Lulu's is that place. An ample menu, interesting daily specials, friendly staff. If I often default to the Lulu's BLT, well, it is so good!!

To give my sister the ultimate Philly experience I decided to take her to get none other then a Geno's Cheese Steak. Honestly this place is overrated. It's a little annoying that you have to purchase your cheesesteak at one window and your drink and fries at another. I mean I get it there is always a line so they want to keep people moving but you're just forming a new line! We ordered a wiz with everything.  Due to all of the hype we were preparing ourselves for the best cheesesteak ever. But unfortunately it did not live up to its hype. Don't get me wrong it was good, it just isn't something that deserves as much hype as it has.
Love the grouper sandwich!!! It's so good!!! Also love eating out on the covered patio overlooking the lake!

Stopped by this afternoon and am so happy we did! I saw on their Instagram account they would be serving a Quesabirria on the weekend and I HAD to try it! They also had a great 3 taco special with drink for $10. The quesadilla was HUGE and loaded with cheese and pork. It was so delicious and very, very filling! The tacos were great too! The al pastor was our favorite and even though we're not huge guac fans, it was not over powering and complimented the tacos! I will for sure be back to try more. You order and pay at the window and there's a cute patio area to dine at. There is also on site, free parking.
Great service and clean restaurant. Tried the Philly cheesesteak and Al- Sham burger..both were good

Just popped in at the recommendation of a friend and loved right away. Small and quaint; not flashy. Options included a couple hot breakfast sandwiches, a variety of croissants, bagel balls, puff pastries, muffins, waffles, cookies; espressos and coffees. All looked like amazing quality. I ordered a hot bacon, egg and cheddar cheese and it was the best (real cheddar). There are a few tables to eat in or one can take out. Friendly service/pleasant environment. 
Another great place and a reason to #lovesouthtampa #notachain
Great Dominos service in the echelon area! We ordered our meal online and it was delivered within 20 minutes!

My wife and I dropped in here for a quick drink while we were visiting New Orleans.  It has a great classy feel to it without being pretentious and overbearing.  The cocktails we tried were mixed very well and hit the spot quite nicely!

This is the real deal! If you're looking for authentic & comforting Korean food, please visit Sa Ri One, because you ain't gonna find seoul food like this in town. Get it!? Soul.... Haha, lame joke. I know :(

The service and overall exterior/interior isn't something to praise about, but the food is spot on. The menu has a little bit of everything from things not so scary to items you have to be adventurous to try. 

I re-visited Sa Ri One recently and fell in love with their food all over again. Fresh and HOT food. I wish they have more banchans because I'm so used to having 10+ little side dishes but they certainly all taste amazing. 

The dol sot bulgogi bibimbap is so bomb! The stone pot certainly changes the dish from a regular bibimbap to DOL SOT! Crispy rice for life. 

I was certainly surprised how busy a Sunday dinner was. It was exciting because it feels good others know how good this place is. I would love to go back if only it wasn't so far! I want Korean food now!!!

The seafood gumbo is fantastic !! Except the food, the service is excellent too, especially they also help me keep the lost phone when I returned to find it. Thanks to my server Tyler and the front desk people :))

Overall its a nice restaurant with a nice soulful ambience...BUT the food was flavorless and bland!! It was sort of busy when I went so i expected a little wait but 30 minutes to bring the appetizer which was the Carribean Chicken Flatbread and cornbread which I must say was very good..after that i waited an extra 40 minutes before I recieved my entree. I ordered the Red Snapper with Crabmeat ?? Sauce and not only was it flavorless and dry but they put COLD lump crab meat on top of the fish along with bland cabbage and overcooked rice!!! For the most part it was an ok experience but I don't think I'll ever come back or recommend it!!!
I love the food here but the employees are rude and unhelpful. I understand working a minimum wage job sucks but people come here for the experience too.

Never had these at a Texmex place - and I'm a Mexican. They are like fried boneless chicken wings (deconstructed). OMG. Really good. Called - Chicharrones (yes, yes, but never seen them on a menu). The Cadillac Marg has fresh ingredients with a Grand Marnier floater - - - Super hand made love and delicious. Cool vibe but they have these beer and margarita towers. (never seen those before anywhere). You need to see them to understand...Bartenders were great, very friendly and attentive.

The corner of Chartres and Toulouse is one filled with fond memories for me. When Quaffer's was across the way and One Eyed Jacks was still the Shim Sham Club, I spent many a night at this crossroads. So for some reason, no matter how mediocre the experience, I keep coming back to Chartres House Cafe whenever I have an excuse, such as visitors in town or just wanting a cocktail and some people watching in the middle of a Saturday afternoon. Sometimes the muffuletta is decent. Sometimes the eggplant napoleon is delish. Sometimes the servers don't seem like cast-offs from daquiri dens down the street. Other times....meh. Not so much. However, if you can get a seat by the open doors downstairs (or by the fireplace AND the doors on a cooler night) or a place on the narrow balcony upstairs (parties of 2 only) , the Chartres House can be really enjoyable. They have a nice wine selection, chilled vodkas, decent appetizers, and of course the location is marvelous. Just close enough to Jackson Square and Bourbon Street without being totally obnoxious. The place is owned by some conglomerate that runs several daquiri bars and other little places scattered thoughout the Quarter (Cafe Fleur de Lis among them- good breakfast!), but I don't hold that against them too much. Another note, my vegetarian friend really liked the veggie muffuletta and the spinach and artichoke dip.

Wonderful dinner to celebrate our 1st anniversary. The tomato pie was surprisingly the star of the meal and the beet salad was refreshing. We ordered the halibut which was cooked to perfection. The desserts- the homemade ice cream and skillet cookie were delicious. To top it off, the service was fantastic!

Four stars is a really good review in my book. The food was very good, it's counter service so there isn't really much interaction to rate. However, the service was friendly, very efficient and they have a good system in place for managing the orders. 

They give you a pager so you don't have to stand around waiting for your food. We took a minute to find a table, get beverages and then our food was ready.

I had the chicken rice bowl. It was very good. Everything was the correct temperature, it all had good flavor and the veggies were fresh. The chicken is mild (which I like but not everyone does so I wanted to mention it) and it had the nice thigh flavor. Well cooked, not overdone at all. 

The standout of the meal was was chicken dumplings, aka potstickers or gyoza. Wow! Great flavor on the fillings, just enough of a very nice soy sauce based drizzle on top. There are 5 in an order, I would go back just for those!

If you're in the mood for quick Asian food and you live in Fishers this is a great option.

We went several times both for lunch and dinner HOPING it would get better, but it never did. Having a Downtown Sushi restaurant is a must I believe and I REALLY wanted to like this place. I went with the kids the first time, and they were almost rude to us, but the food was okay. I was amazed and surprised that they wanted to charge and extra 50cents for Ponzu sauce. I didn't care about the 50 cents, it was the point. Then they added insult to injury by telling us it was because they made it fresh. Well, we ordered it and trust me...This was NOT Ponzu Sauce. I've had REAL freshly made Ponzu sauce at REAL Japanese restaurants, and it's citrusy and light. This was not, it was heavy and salty. The next time I went with a girlfriend for lunch, and both of us felt the rice was stiff, and the taste of the sushi, just not very good. Then I went back for dinner with a friend, and experienced the wait staff to be over worked, and again, the food eh. Great idea...bad execution.

Nope. No no no nope. $80 (before tip) for: scones for 3 served with exactly enough clotted cream & lemon curd for 1/2 of a scone ($5.50 PER SCONE because it included "toppings" even though it didn't actually come with enough); no cream served with the tea, surprise from server when we requested cream, and then served one literally doll-sized pitcher of possibly 2% milk (which was supposed to be enough for 3 teas, one of which we got a la carte for $6!); more surprise/confusion when we asked for water; zero vegetarian main course options--unless you count egg salad, which we did, until it arrived full of chopped BACON (which was also in the deviled egg); none of the traditional tea sandwiches--some of which weren't actually sandwiches, and the ham & cheese was made with American cheese; a somewhat scattered and 100% hard-of-hearing server...and the piece d'resistence? A HAIR baked into one of the cookies. They did replace the egg salad (settling for a cheese sandwich, which was the only non-meat option, and also used American cheese) and all of the pastries that were on the same plate as the hair-cookie, but aside from that and an apology, no discount or anything. Also, their menu online boasts crepes and many other options not found on today's in-store menu.

To be fair, the place is very cute & totally Victorian-ed out, there's ample parking in the back (we were there at 2pm on a weekday), there are a few outdoor tables, and the key lime mousse and chocolate cupcake were delicious. But there are WAY better options in the Phila. area.

This is usually the best pizza on the planet, but the crew working tonight did not seem to know what they were doing. I had to beg to have cheese put on top of the pizza. I waited an hour for a pick up order. They were more interested in getting the store clean so they could close on time. I give them a pass this time, but seriously Bellacino's you're better than this!
Edit:  Got home and pizza is not done, veggies were not even hot. Wow, just wow.

Very good food.  Surprisingly, it was exactly what I expected.  I was expecting a diner food / comfort food take on classic Italian and Mexican dishes and that's exactly what I got.  If you're looking for authentic, this might not be the place to go, but authenticity is only sacrificed for comfort and flavor.

I tried the fish tacos and my wife had the chicken fajitas.  We also shared an order of queso loco dip with chips.  Though the queso claims to be made with queso blanco, the cheese was yellow.  It tasted more like a mild cheddar cheese gravy with rotel and that's not a bad thing.  The fish tacos had great seasoning and although the shells were greasy, it was very good.  The chicken fajitas surprised us because of yellow peppers instead of the red we're used to.  We normally don't like yellow peppers because they are more bitter, but it was just the right flavor to go with the chicken.

Overall, it was a good experience.  And having Jarritos (especially tamarind) is a great touch.  The dining area is still a bit noisy with its bare walls, despite much effort with the sound dampening panels, but not nearly as bad as other places in Edwardsville (We're looking at you, Cleveland-Heath).  The walls are lined with electric outlets just above eye level, but they all have covers on the ports.  I think they're missing a great opportunity for the business lunch crowd.  A few cents of electricity right at the table is a great draw for those with laptops.

I'll be coming back and trying the italian side of things - especially their Italian Beef.

Best Burgers and Fries EVER! But last night wanted wraps. The bartender suggested Mango Habanero sauce on it. I'm so glad I went with it cuz it was AMAZING! And the fries..... Mmmmmm Mmmmmm they're so good, soooooooooo good!!! Not only is the food bomb, but the customer service is good too!
Nice dive bar, friendly staff, great wings, not my first choice but a definite back up when I need one!!!

I tried this place for the first time. The food was ok.  I asked for the toppings for my loaded nachos on the side and instead they didn't give me any of the toppings. When I called they said they would refund me for the missing sides but they never did.

This place being ranked so high can only be from a few reasons. 
It's a spot young folks like for the variety. 
Folks just missed going out. 
Or they are based on space *easily accommodates large groups* and the number of TVs.
Because there is NOTHING about this place where I would ever go back. The only reason its not a 1 is because the fried pickles were good and our server was very helpful. 
The prices are super high. 
And I know I took a chance getting a sushi roll but my goodness, the grocery store stuff is better. The rice was like paste and not seasoned.
The mini burgers packed seasoning and flavor.
If you order a drink they don't let you modify your liquor choice without it being a big deal. 
On top of there were so many servers and staff around but not working. You were seating yourself and still waiting to get greeted. 
And again these prices were ridiculous for what was offered.

Service-5
Ambiance- 4
Food-5
 Located in a strip mall next to its sister establishment-Nippon tei.
The menu is limited- hence taking away a star. 

We tried the chicken wings and gyoza. Loved the gyoza; chicken was crispy and sweet- I like it spicy though. 
The tonkatsu ramen was the star of the evening with the poached egg. Totally satisfying and yummy. The Khao suey is more a thai curry with noodles instead of rice. If you have serious ramen cravings this won't do.. go for the miso ramen or shoyu ramen.

The drink menu is extensive with a variety of sake and cocktails. I tried the Japanese strawberry soda which was good too.
Called ahead and grabbed a pizza to go. It was ready when I got there and it was good.

Aside from being really hard to find, this is exactly what is needed in the SB area. Good food at odd times. Everything in SB is either closed or Mexican American food passed 12 am.  I got buffalo wings, and Mac attack and was surprised with the huge portions. I saw images on their yelp but they were out of context and appeared small. Both items were delicious. The wings came with fries and had an awesome flavor.
good staff in here  parking lot sucks though, as iM sure others have mentioned, but there isn't much they can do about it

The pizza deserves 5 stars. It's the best pizza I've had in Philly.
It took us a while to figure out where Enjay's was, though. Enjay's is less a location than a name for the food inside the bar Smokey Joe's, which is extremely confusing. Everything was pointing us to Smokey Joe's. We finally asked the bartender and he told us we were in the right place, as in, inside Smokey Joe's, and if we ordered food we'd be eating at Enjay's. This is needlessly confusing. And I wonder how often this problem arises. If they want to have the dual name thing, maybe better signage outside would help.

Atmopshere: Excellent. Nice, open kitchen, and warm decor. Slight recommendation to add an outdoor vestibule in the winter time...every time patrons open the door a strong cold breeze comes in. Also the door hinge spring must be broken, because the door tends to stay open.

Menu/Price: Ok. Their online menu doesn't match up at all to the menu we received once there. The online menu displays traditional ordering in the sense of entrees (described as "platters"), whereas in person and to our surprise, everything was tapas/small plates style once we arrived. Would have been fine if we knew upfront, but nowhere on their website was this stated/made clear.

Food: Decent, but definitely not the best Greek food we've had. The sauteed mussels were described by neither the menu nor the waitress as breaded, and were kind of bland to be honest. The grilled lamb was decent, but have had better. Wouldve been better on top of rice versus peppers/onions.

What's a plus is that it's BYOB. 

Also was very surprised there weren't many/any traditional Greek desserts, especially balklava.

Overall, if you want better Greek food in the city, go to Zorba's in Fairmount, which also happens to be BYOB. Much better, hands down.

I took my kids here for lunch during spring break.  I've been wanting to try this place for a long time.  They are open for breakfast and lunch, closing at two. We were there during the week about an hour before closing and there were still about 4 tables full.  I imagine on the weekends it would get pretty busy.  We each ordered a little something different but all portions were a good size nonetheless.  I went for the spinach omelette which came with grits and toast.  The omelette and the grits were very filling. The toast was a little stale and I was given white instead of wheat.  I wasn't too worried about it though since I was full off the other two items.  My son ordered the $100 burger (no it's not $100) and it was HUGE and cooked perfectly!  He opted for the onion rings which I have to say were the best onion rings I probably ever had.  Not only were they crispy, but the onion did not pull out of the fried outside.  Instead, it melted in your mouth.  My daughter got the grilled chicken sandwich which she did say had good flavor despite the chicken portion inside the bread being too small for the bun.  Her side salad was large, fresh and crisp.  The person at the table next to us ordered a pancake and it was overlapping the size of the plate!  Definitely something to try next ime. 
 Overall, it was a good experience at this place and nice to see a small place that is tucked away in a residential subdivision doing so well.  I'm sure it's pretty neat to see the planes taking off on days the airport is busy.

Espresso is expensive but delicious. The pain perdu is worth trying. Delicious. But a heavy sort of affair inherently. But it has the nice feel of a local Nola cafe, unpretentious and nice. Rest of the menu looks fantastic. I recommend the place overall.

We absolutely love Pho36. The servers are always helpful in helping patrons choose new items to try. I've personally had the pho, the clay pot pork, fried rice, the egg rolls and a dish with crispy noodles, veggies, pork, chicken, shrimp, and calamari. Everything I've tried has been delicious and fresh tasting.  The egg rolls are the best I've ever tasted anywhere.  (I typically don't care for egg rolls). They are always accommodating to my kids in helping them find new foods to try.  My kids both really like the fried rice and the pho.

I try not to eat bagels because I'm fluffy enough as it is, but wow, there are so many choices it's hard to pass up. I loved the upbeat music playing and it was cool to see the Office playing in the background. I love me some Jim Halpert. 

On the plus, staff is friendly, the bagels are not too expensive ($5-7) and there are tons of flavors to choose from. I had the Kuma on jalapeño, and wow. The first bite I took had me hooked. I think it has something to do with the lemon pepper. It took me a few minutes to figure it out. Definitely order something with lemon pepper. Bagel cafe has not seen the last of me.

The Cheesecake Factory is a mix. The food can be amazing. There have been a couple time where I have had something that is just OK but never bad. The Cheesecake is so awesome that is has ruined me for other cheesecake. The downside, is that is always packed and also so LOUD. The other downside is that is always an expensive dinner out as well.

I read a review of Panda House in the local paper.  It was about where university students like to eat (foods that are similar to their home towns).  Panda House was listed so I met a friend there for lunch.  
The parking situation is not good as the restaurant is close to the university and parking permits are needed even for most street parking.
But the food was worth the hassle of trying to find a parking place.  
I love the way eggplant is prepared, Chinese style, and I wasn't disappointed by it at Panda House.  I ate all I could and took the rest home and had it for breakfast the next day.  Companion had a shrimp dish and loved it.  
I will be back to Panda House.  The atmosphere is college funky; plain and clean.  The food was delicious!

Not too impressed with the spa treatment. We extended our stay here by a day just for the spa. I took a cleopatra milk and honey body wrap spa treatment. It was definitely not worth the money. I thought I would be soaked into a tub of milk and honey, but all they did was apply some coconut cream on my hands and back. Does that sound great? No!!!

I'm fairly new to SB but my husband and I are so happy to have found Finney's! It's our go to when we're not feeling like cooking and NEVER disappoints. We've noticed that every time we come we get Margo as our sever. She is so amazing always balancing the line of making sure we're taken care of but not hovering! She genuinely cares about her customers and remembers us every time we're there. Definitely a great feeling coming from a small town. Margo makes us feel like we're actually longtime friends.

One of my favorite restaurants. I knew I would like it from the start when I noticed they had placed a fine spiked wire all along the ledge outside and on their sign to keep birds away, and also a much needed and commonly overlooked air curtain, which is a device establishments place between their doors to keep insects and birds out - a powerful, toupee dislocating, downward blowing fan. After walking through the air curtain and realizing El Diablo is possibly the most anti-bird restaurant I've ever visited, I didn't even care that my carefully styled hair was blown all over the place.

Once I gave the staff my anti-bird hand signal (cross your hands over one another, link your thumbs and flutter your fingers like wings, then transition into the "blow it up" move that has become a popular finale for a fist-bump), and it was returned, I decided this was the place for me.

Anyhoo, the braised short-rib is unbelievable, as is the citrus braised pork. If you're looking to dine on an avian, try the chicken with the chipotle barbeque sauce - it's a doozy. All of El Diablo's ingredients are fresh and absolutely fantastic, and the sauces and dressings make me want to punch Taco Bell in the face.

El Diablo might mean "The Devil" in translation, but no burrito more heavenly has ever crossed mine lips. They say Jesus resides inside each of us - well I hope he likes burritos, because that's what he's going to get.

In closing, a quote often associated with the legendary cartoon heroine Jem - El Diablo, you are outrageous. Truly, truly outrageous.

Thank you, THANK YOU Caffe Aldo! You provided an awesome birthday dinner for my wife and I during this challenging time.  All of the things we love about Aldo Lamberti's were there. You politely and professionally took our order over the phone. Uniformed and masked waiters put the food in our hatchback. And we enjoyed your delicious food and felt the way we would in your dining room. You even remembered the olives! You will continue to have our business long after this virus is gone. And we thank you again.

A Very Good Sushi place that is NOT CROWDED.  To be fair we came at 6pm just after the Saturday Happy Hour ended (at 5pm) and we were seated quickly in a mostly empty place.  It filled by 7pm with lots of people asking about the Happy Hour.  From Monday to Thursday the Happy hour goes from 11am until 7pm and the specials on food and drinks look awesome so that we will come back again to try out.  

On arrival we had very friendly staff greet and seat us quickly.  As we were seated Miso soup arrived and we were offered Edamame while our drink orders were taken. We had a Sake bomb, Plum Wine which arrived quickly.  We were not that hungry so we had a Vegas Tempura and the Chef's Choice 7pc Nigiri Sushi (we asked for no shrimp and it was accommodated).  The Vegas Tempura was rolled thick with wide pieces, yum.  The Nigiri was a decent size.  Edamame was not salted, which is fine.  

The place has a sushi bar and tables.  Lots of room.  There were two small (19 or 21") TV's to watch sports, which was not very convenient, but decent to check scores.  On entering my eye caught the large selection of Ramune and Pocky Sticks and other Japanese candy and drinks at the front, my daughter loves that stuff.

The rug seemed a little dated and the restrooms were clean.  No issues and we were checked on frequently.  We will definately come back for the Happy Hour and we totally appreciated the quieter and casual atmosphere.

Having grown up in NJ, bagels are high on my list, in general. It's been hard to find places in Philly that compare to what I've known because I understand they will never actually be quite the same. Having that said, I think Knead Bagels successfully satisfies my foodie side.

Their types of non-traditional bagels are unique and unlike ones I've seen in philly and the quality of the bagels are good and fresh. Beyond non-traditional bagels, Knead Bagels also offers a variety of flavored cream cheeses that are fun to try. I love the menu of suggestions combining their bagel flavors and cream cheeses.  

Further, and the reason for this four star review, is the "special" bagel combination I had the other day. I can confidently say, that with one bite, it went straight to being my third favorite food item in all of Philadelphia (I'm continuously making my way though Philly Mag's Best Restaurant list and so have had my fair share of trying a variety of food) right behind Giwa's pork taco and Barbuzzo's budino. 

The special of the day was a lemon pepper bagel and truffle cream cheese. Truffle cream cheese - enough said. And no, it wasn't cream cheese with a little bit of truffle oil to give it a hint of truffle... it had tiny pieces of actual truffle in it. And not in a heavy, bulky type way. But it was smooth, rich and creamy- the texture of how slightly melted cream cheese should be on a toasted bagel. It was perfection. I even went back later that day to get a second to save for the next day, because with it being a special, I didn't like the thought of not knowing when I would have the opportunity to have it again. Oh and the best part- each bagel sandwich equated to about $4. 

I urge you, if you see this rare special, get it. You will not regret it. You may even buy two, too.

My very 1st night in Nashville, for Yelp Spring Break 2014, I got the scoop on the town's signature dish. You see, in TN, I was told, Memphis is the town known for its BBQ & in Nashville it's all about the Hot Chicken. & when it comes to Hot Chicken, Prince's Hot Chicken Shack is the original.

Good enough for me. The next afternoon I drove on out to the tiny strip mall building Prince's is located in. Arriving between lunch & dinner time, it wasn't busy & there wasn't a line to order. Service was friendly but also, um, shall we say unique. The characters in this joint had plenty of character. This was the sort of place that easily could've been on an episode of Seinfeld.

With the word "shack" in its name, Prince's Hot Chicken Shack is simply & sparsely decorated with a few picnic-style table booths. Ordering is done all the way in the back through a hole in the wall to the kitchen. The menu is similarly simple: various parts of chicken & a few sides. Since it wasn't busy, my order didn't take long. My foray into Nashville's Hot Chicken was in hand & about to begin.

*** HOT CHICKEN SHOWDOWN!!! ***

Yup, that's right. Lots of folks in Nashville have an opinion on who makes the best Hot Chicken. While there's no real disputing that Prince's is the original, judging from the number of Yelp reviews & numerous mentions during conversations, I'd say that Hattie B's is Nashville's most popular Hot Chicken. Before leaving town, I got to try both. Following is a head-to-head comparison of Prince's vs. Hattie B's.

*** COMPARISON ***

Both places feature identical menu items, though Hattie B's has a few more items that Prince's does not. I ordered the same exact thing at both places: half chicken, coleslaw & baked beans. For the chicken, both places have 4 levels of spiciness. Only the 2 hottest got my interest. I eat some seriously spicy stuff (can you say over 1 million Scoville?), but this time I took a more measured approach & chose the 2nd hottest level of spiciness.

The grand total was a couple $ more for Prince's than Hattie B's. Both orders were taken to go & eaten shortly later back in my room. Both places put their sides into small plastic-lidded styrofoam cups. The serving sizes of the sides, between Prince's & Hattie B's, were close to the same, but Prince's sides looked a little smaller.

Hot Chicken - Let me get this out of the way from the get-go. At the same listed level of spiciness on their respective menus, Prince's Hot Chicken was MUCH hotter than Hattie B's Hot Chicken. No contest. Prince's chicken was also moister & more tender inside. The fried shell of Prince's chicken was thin, delicate & crispy. The fried shell of Hattie B's chicken was thicker & crunchier than Prince's.

Sides - Both Prince's & Hattie B's baked beans were very similar. Both were good. I'd rate the 2 as being about the same. The cabbage in Prince's coleslaw was snappy & the dressing wasn't heavy while still very flavorful. The cabbage in Hattie B's coleslaw was a little soggier & the dressing was thicker with noticeably a lot of mayonnaise.

*** VERDICT ***

Overall, for my personal tastes, I'm taking Prince's over Hattie B's. I do love me some truly spicy food & Prince's Hot Chicken brought the heat, big time. I also liked Prince's coleslaw better. I'm not a fan of coleslaws with too much mayonnaise. I'd consider service a wash. Service at Prince's was somewhat disorganized but very friendly & entertainingly quirky. Service at Hattie B's was uptempo, attentive & on the ball. Convenience, however, has to go to Hattie B's. Located not far from downtown, I walked there from my room. Prince's was a drive way out to B.F.E.

O.M.G. Wow you guys, this place is an absolute must when in the big easy!

Details: As soon as I landed in NOLA, I asked my Uber driver where were some good places to try. This was my fourth trip to the city, and as expected he ran off the common/popular places in and around the French quarter. Then I rephrased the question: if you wanted some good, no-fuss, soul cookin aka, where would you take your friends, where would you go? That question led us to Neyow's. 

Located in mid-city, this place is far from all of the hustle 'n flow from the French quarter, but is still only about a 5-10 minute drive from the city centre. Once we were seated, I remember what our Uber driver told us were the must-orders: The Bow Wow drink and an order of their famous charbroiled oysters. This leads me to the...

Food/Drinks: People. You cannot visit the big easy and not sample some good ol' gulf oysters. This place serves up the absolute best oysters I've ever had. Just left of the bar, there is an employee with his own station dedicated just for making these special mollusks. Grilled over an open flame, the oysters cook in their own salt water, are drenched in butter, then topped off with plenty, and I do mean plenty of parmesan cheese. Lemon wedges, which I highly encourage you use to cut through the fat, and some bread are served alongside. My gf doesn't even like oysters, and I had to convince her to try these, but by the time we got to the last one, I had to fight her off for the last bite (jk, I let her have it, but I digress). 

If there is one tip I will leave you with, it's that you must make sure that you come to this place absolutely famished, because Neyow's doesn't even understand the concept of what a small or normal size portion is. For my entrée, I opted for the fried catfish with some red beans and rice. My gf ordered their shrimp creole. When the dishes came out, we just looked at each other and rolled up our sleeves. We easily could have split just one of these dishes and still left full, but this was vacation so there was no backing down. Plus, it was extremely delicious, so that helped to scarf it down.

Now you may be wondering, with all of this food, what did you possibly wash it down with. Well I'll tell you what. Per the above recommendation from our Uber driver, my gf and I split a Bow Wow drink. This innocent looking libation packs one of the strongest punches I've ever tasted, but because it's so sweet, it still goes down easy. All I can say is CAUTION. We only had half of it each, but could feel the effects only a couple of sips in, and were definitely on the tipsy side when we left. The restaurant will only serve you two of these, but please even if you're only having one, please don't drive as these things will put any hurricane/hand grenade/shark attack to shame. Best drink I had in all of NOLA.  

In conclusion: I left Neyow's feeling pretty good. I was stuffed from all of the food, definitely buzzed from just half of a bow wow, and the best part, unlike the French quarter, I didn't have to break the bank. When in town, I will definitely be back.

My wife and I love Jae's seafood!! We visit Jae's atleast once a week for their all year crabs and seafood. The staff is great and very friendly. They are knowledgeable about your seafood needs. They suggested their mussels and shrimp platter with butter, garlic, corn and broccoli... it was amazing.. Jae's never disappoints!! A must try!!

First time here and loved it. Great ambiance! Buffalo cauliflower is amazing! Meatloaf sliders missed the mark, but a little more bacon, tomato jam would've helped. The bourbon banana bread pudding was "plate licking" good. What really separates CSK from the gastropub pack is the staff. From the friendly hostess who greeted and sat us to our lovely and attentive server, Kate, these folks know how to do it! We even received a table side check in from the GM, Josh! The cocktails were awesome as well.

Good food. Vegeterian friendly. Definitely recommend this place to vegetarian friends out there. There any many options for meat lovers too. Place is really small, few tables inside but I prefer sitting outside. There is extra parking space available back side. More than worth for what you pay. I loved the vegetable taco and Sope.

Bad boy burger on fairview is really good. I have had their burgers in the past and they are great. This morning I saw they were open on my way to work and stopped in and grabbed their $3.75 bacon breakfast. I am amazed how good it is and how little it cost. I couldn't of made this at home for how cheap it is. It comes with two eggs, 4 pieces of bacon, hash-browns and toast. You should really give it a try. The best part is I took it two work and my coworkers sent someone back out to order more for everyone else.

What you do when you love hot chicken and you are looking for something vegan? You could put hot sauce on a carrot OR you can race down to Joella's Hot Chicken and get yourself some Vegan Hot Chicken. I was sold after I learned it started with J-O-E and I had to have it. Also, the one lady on 90-Day fiancé works at one which is why I googled it and why I found this place to begin with! That show has never steered me wrong!

I will say the Vegan Hot Chicken didn't look all that appealing as it lacked a sauce. It could have been breaded so it had the crunchy layer that held the sauce and heat. I ordered the tweeny which was between medium and hot and it definitely could have been hotter. The spice levels are vastly different at these places and some medium means Hot AF and some medium means it has black pepper on it. There needs to be an industry standard!!!! I feel I could have ordered the hottest one here as I was only 2 levels removed.
