I went to Friday Saturday Sunday with my partner and ordered six dishes: 1) Artic char, 2) Sweetbread Katsu, 3) Bucatini, 4) Collard Greens and 5) pig blood sausage pasta and 6) Black and Tan dessert. 

The food was good but not exceptional. Compared to Michelin 1-starred restaurants I have dined before in DC and NYC that serve small-medium dishes, Friday Saturday Sunday is not quite there yet. But, their food certainly stands out in Philadelphia. I dined at Serpico about two weeks ago and I would say taste-wise, F.S.Sunday is better though Serpico serves more stylish dishes. So, F.S.Sunday is pretty darn good especially their pasta. 

But, one thing that makes F.S.Sunday stand out even from other Michelin Restaurants is their service. My server, Tim, was exceptional. I think Tim was the best server I had in my 2 years in the U.S. 

I just wish they change their menu often enough for me to revisit.

Came upon this place on way to French Quarter Fest. Didn't have time to stop at that time. Was back in the Bywater with wife and friends,  this past Saturday and decided to have brunch. Glad we did. Had a bit of a wait, because only inside tables were available because of rain. Our waiter was very attentive. Thoroughly enjoyed. Will be back!

I didn't get to experience much here, but from what I did get to experience, I think I may be coming back.

I like the atmosphere here. It's not too loud so you can hear conversations relatively well and seating and space are ample. Right now, the outside is going through some construction so you look like you're going into a really shady place. But don't worry, once you're up the stairs, you're on your way to a good time. Just make sure you don't come here on a later leg of a bar tour.

The bartenders were pretty friendly and Saison was pretty good as per Aaron's recommendation. I definitely digged this place, but couldn't dig it enough in such a short time to up a star.

Only been here for happy hour and it's really a hit or miss. Located in St Pete, they occupy the 2nd floor of the Locale Market plaza. Valet Parking is available for $5 or you may opt for the garage across the street for $1 per hour. 

Love the layout of the restaurant, there are indoor and outdoor seating. There's a huge wine wall inside the restaurant carrying bottles ranging up to $1000. The bathroom has a salt scrub for your hands you can try, makes your hand feeling silky smooth. 

So I've tried few happy hour faves lie duck fat edamame, calamari, wagyu burger, fish tacos and lamb koftas? I really didn't like the calamari, very salty and lamb was dry. The drinks aren't good either (watered down),  instead of cocktails, they serve alcohol and you can add mixers with it. 

Overall, i gave them two tries and both times were meh.

We ordered the Lovebird and the Ricotta Ravioli. The Ricotta Ravioli was amazing - the sauce was extremely flavorful and left me desiring more. The ravioli itself was also delicious, and my only qualm about the dish is that I wish there was more ravioli. However, the Lovebird was not as good. We thought that the chicken was a bit dry; the breading was nice and you could tell it was real chicken, but we thought it was nothing special. As always with STARR restaurants, the service was great.

This location is great and the staff is very friendly. This was my first time at Dutch Bros and I took a while to figure out what I wanted. Luckily, the location wasn't busy at all and the employee actually helped me decide on a drink. The drink itself was okay, maybe it's just because I'm used to my Einstein Coffee and Starbucks. I would definitely recommend trying Dutch Bros at least once. It might be your cup of tea (coffee) and they have a really large variety of drinks to choose from.

Loved it. Awesome (in size and quality) french toast - order half! Long wait after 10a. Bustling diner atmosphere, friendly and hip. My only complaint: too much food! Next time we'll order one thing and split it.
I got the texan and it was dry and tasteless. My whole table had a bad experience. Big price tag with a little taste. The fries were amazing but that was it. Service was mediocre.
A nice little beach coffee shop. We got there just as a little morning rush arrived. We were served quickly and the coffee was good  as well as the muffins and breakfast sandwich we had.

Stopped here for lunch. Very cute and modern shop with a large menu. Quiches, pies, other baked yummies. Sandwiches and salads on their lunch menu. Everything was good but it seemed like the staff was flustered though the place wasn't very busy.

Food: 3/5 - If you get the quinoa salad it is very citrusy.
Baked goods: 4/5 - The warm apple pie and the PB&chocolate cookie we had were very delicious!
Coffee: - didn't try this time around
Service: 3/5
Location: 4/5 - Clean and a great variety of seating.
Best noodle house in East oak lane!!! I miss live next to this place. They Speak bad English that's why gave four Stars. But my family love this noodle house

$6.70 for a Mediterranean Sandwich is too much. Between 2 pcs. of bread is a piece of lettuce, 1 slice of tomato, 2 rings of onions, 2 slices of cucumber and some crumbly cheese. And mind you, the slices of bread is smaller than the regular slices we are used to. I will not order this again.

This is a tough review for me because I want to give it 5 stars for the food ... but 2 for the service. Since the food is more important to me, I settled on 4 stars.


We arrived around noon on Sunday so the place was packed. In an effort to avoid the 40+ minute expected wait, we chose to sit over on the Twist side. It was dark, quiet, and relaxing. The 4 of us sat in the section with the nice comfy couches and little barn-wood looking tables. We loved the decor and were happy to be seated right away. The waitress came up to us and spoke a mile-a-minute, was extremely frazzled and seemed to not have slept for a few days. Since it was our first time at the restaurant, we asked about the brunch drinks and what was in them...specifically the bro-mosa. She didn't know what beer was used in the drink and said she'd have to ask the bar tender. No big deal..right? Well about 10 minutes later, she returns to say that Sun King is used in the drink. So we get it.... and some bloody mary's and a hibiscus mimosa. About 10 minutes later, she returns to tell us that the bar tender is running behind or something... and 10 minutes after that we finally get the drink and she mentions that its actually High Life in the bro-mosa...then makes some comment about how the bar tenders don't even know whats in the drinks. While I agree with her in that they should know their stuff... she shouldn't comment on it to customers. 

FINALLY we begin to order our food. My boyfriend and I both order half biscuits and gravy/half french toast. His father orders the same, and his mother gets the corned beef hash. His mother asked the waitress if she got an egg with the meal, since she ordered a half size ... the response from the waitress ... "I dunno...what does the menu say?" 


WOW ... so then she goes on to explain the response ... apparently she tends to work nights and was asked to return only 3 hours later to work the morning shift. She says that since she only works nights, she doesn't know anything about the food and drink menu. GREAT. 

Having worked in the service industry before, I understand how crappy that can be and I did feel bad for her but still ... you've got to be able to come in and do the job ---and not share the details with your customers. She was grumbling/frazzled/talked way too fast/ and didn't seem to care very much. 

Anyway - the biscuits and gravy was the best we've EVER had and same goes for the french toast. The corned beef has was very nice and we certainly look forward to returning. The drinks were also great. So that's why I give Zest a 4/5 .. I want to give it a 5 but the service really took it down a notch. 

The experience that we had was very pleasant and we enjoyed the atmosphere of the restaurant. I'm sure that had we gotten a different waitress (also it looked like she was taking care of EVERYONE on the Twist side) it would have been a very different interaction.

Decent place but it's Carmel, more specifically city center. Corporate feeling but good beer selection and decent flatbread.  Bar area is to the right after entering. Great classic wooden bar and comfy stool. Few other high tables. Bar back includes lighted shelving, hdtvs, and a beer list. Beer towers / taps on the bar. Not bad for a quick drink and bite to eat if in area. Be careful if driving, Carmel cops are a$$es.

This place is a hidden gem! I went to their happy hour over a year ago and loved it! So when our New Year's Eve reservations got cancelled elsewhere due to pandemic restrictions - I jumped at the chance to book a reservation here! Reservations are available on their website and on Open Table.
They had a special NYE menu which is where I ordered the short ribs. They tend to rotate their menu a little bit as is anyway - but the featured dishes were great! My significant other ordered a tomahawk steak with potatoes and broccolini which was equally delicious! We both added on the side salad and the lemon vinaigrette and it was so refreshing! We also ordered a bottle of their Barbera and it complimented the meats perfectly! 
The four of us had 4 meals, 3 salads, 3 cocktails, 2 desserts,  and 1 bottle of wine and the bill came out to a little over $300. 
Social distancing was strongly enforced - we were nowhere near another table! Everyone was wearing their masks.
Our server Katie was attentive and friendly. Overall a great experience and we will be back!
The chef needs to learn how to make risotto.  Absolutely a flop.  Salty, soupy and over done not creamy or anything I would call risotto.

Excellent place for good, quick and cheaper Chinese take out. You get a lot of food and it's worth the price. It's always quick and the employes are nice. I live in Lakeview and this is my 'go-to' Chinese take out place.

R Bar is a friendly bar that attracts locals more than tourists, so they must be doing something right. Daily all you can eat specials are priced right and food is delicious. I recently had the Calamari appetizer. A lot of places give you more breadcrumbs than fish and over fry the Calamari making it rubbery. At R Bar the Calamari is lightly breaded and fried just right. Heather the bartender mixes drinks with flair and a style all her own. Ask for a spicy Bloody Mary and Heather will quiz you on how spicy you want it, then make the drink to your taste JUST RIGHT. Plus, Heather will remember how you like it the next time you order one. Stop by once and become a regular forever.

Went here last week for dinner and was a pretty solid experience. We were seated right away and service was very fast. We ordered the boneless wings which were okay. Nothing really special about them , they had a garlic sauce on them and were pretty average .  I also ordered the chicken caesar salad. The chicken seemed a little dry but everything else seemed okay. Overall not a bad experience was just an okay one. This place reminds me a lot like a TGIF or an applebees.

We are visiting Indianapolis for the Indiana state fair and decided to try this place out, we were not disappointed! The guacamole was perfect! We could see our waiter making it fresh. My husband got the mr. nachos and said they were delicious. I got the fajita burrito and it was very good and enough for 2 meals. Overall we were very happy to have this as our first experience in Indianapolis, I would definitely recommend it to any locals!

I have eaten here before and it's always decent but I ordered two medium two topping pizzas that were a special and both have barely any sauce on them. The cheese was very salty too. I couldn't even finish the pizza I got for myself. Not only did they talk crap about me and my request when I came back for a refund but Lisa tried to tell me we ate 1/2 of each pizza when we had each eaten a slice and tried to eat a second and just couldn't stomach it. They were all incredibly rude except for James Bagsby. I will NEVER eat here again!

Recently stayed at this hotel in Reno. Very nice atmosphere. But what I really enjoyed was the buffet. Great selection with lots of fresh foods. My whole party was definitely satisfied and I will return to this place next time I'm in town!

This review makes me so sad. I've been going to Buddy's since it opened, bringing all my friends to happy hour. 
The good news, the wait staff, all of it is outstanding! Friendly, attentive, observant.
The food, not so much. I really don't care that the prices have increased, times are hard. But the quality of the food- especially the chicken fingers, salads and rest of the starters have bottomed out. What used to be flavorful is bland, the coating are tasteless and the salad dressing have separated so that all you taste is oil. I would rather pay a bit more and have quality food again. Rita Ranch deserves more.

I am ashamed to not have reviewed the one Pho place that I visit with great regularity and have been a loyal customer since 1997 !

Consistently good Pho.   Is it the greatest Pho out there ... no.  Is it the most reliable bowl of steamy soup-for-the-soul ... a resounding YES.

My 5 stars comes with great love and a history with this place.

I came here with my first significant other and we were weekly regulars for years.

I continued to come even after we broke up.

I come when I don't feel good and when I leave,  I feel better.
I come when I have been deeply sad and my mood is altered after I have been nourished.

This is more than just soup at this place ... this is medicine for anything that ails.   There is great nostalgia here for me and Pho 75 has never let me down.

Best Pho Ga I will say that.  Many places don't do the broth or the meat well like this place does.

And ... you can get vinegared onions (if you are a fan of this sort of taste like me) and it's not on the menu,  so you just ask for it.   That tidbit was from watching Vietnamese folks ordering it,  then lathering them in Sriracha -- it's an incredible addition to the Pho !

I was so happy to find this place when I moved here a year ago! The food is exceptional and fresh the people and service is outstanding.  They keep improving on what they have, they've expanded the facility, added brunch and music wonderful!  The bakery is fabulous including the gluten free amazing options.  

I've brought several people here who now love it as I do! 

Thank you Cottage Cafe/Crumb de la Crumb for being so good at what you do serving healthy options with great people and offering decadent deserts!!

Excellent food and customer service from this family-run business.  I had first read about them on Yelp and was extremely intrigued by two things: the cuisine (Mediterranean AND Classic Italian; and the excellent reviews)!      Don't be discouraged by the strip mall setting, the food is incredible and staff are wonderful.  

I ended up getting the hummus to start -- simply out of this world! Smooth, creamy, and a taste of lemon.  Then decided for a traditional pasta dish honestly not knowing what to expect; it was so delicious, and the tomato sauce was homemade with only the best  tomatoes.  My friend got a seafood jambalaya of sorts and said it was excellent-- both of our portions were very generous as well. 

We closed out the night with two cappuccinos and a fantastic chocolate cake.    Our server was a sweetheart (I think her name was Amanda?) ... kind, personable, and funny.  I think she may be the owner's daughter ... but she added to the greatness of our night.  We thanked the owner and said we would be back.  If you're looking for a good meal, in a nice place, with lovely people, take the time and go to Alarz!

The best food I have had The gumbo is amazing fried chicken is awesome and the shrimp is to die for and Mia and Marty were our servers and they were absolutely amazing seriously give this place a five star service was great!!

I've been hearing all the rave for el Diablo and so today I finally gave it a try because it's cinco de Mayo. Sadly, it didn't meet the expectations I had based on what other people said...

For my first ever order, I got a citrus braised pork burrito with black beans, half pepper jack, half cheddar, guacamole, pickled peppers, pico de gallo, pineapple habanero salsa, and salsa verde. The part I enjoyed the most was the pineapple habanero salsa. The pork was tasty enough.

The serving size was huge but I saw that they had to rewrap mine because it was practically overflowing. I think seeing it dumped again on another tortilla made it look less appetizing too. I actually asked if I could do the recommended combination but either they didn't hear me or didn't mind it.. Last comment is rgat it was a bit too soggy. :(

It was very filling but the flavor wasn't the best. Maybe I'll try it again in the future, and maybe then I'll have a better experience.
Very good food and atmosphere.  Food is healthy and unique choices.  Portion control.  The desserts are a delight.  Small, but just enough to end a satisfying delicious meal.

Ordered a carnitas burrito, pork was cold and soggy, rice was not fully cooked.  Probably just a bad batch, will try a Qdoba in the area for comparison.

*5/2 update - Stopped in again for a chicken burrito, better this time around, bumping them to 3 stars.  Qdoba is still better to me.

Very disappointed! My husband and are in Santa Barbara for the first time and we were excited to go to Santa Barbara Brewing. We got there and the girl seated us and nobody had come to say hi or take our order while we waited for 15 min, so we left. They weren't even busy. We ended up going to Enterprise Fish Co. where even though they were packed we were greeted and gave our drink order in less than 2 min.
Good music, cod was good, my son said the bbq sandwich, he loved it.  Two craft drafts and only $32 but I tipped very well

Went there with my wife for lunch. We are from Europe, so walking in, I already feel the atmosphere! A neighborhood gem! Food was good, service was good, we will return
and try dinner.
I loved the house specials the gray skies was amazing. I loved the unique flavor it had when you first sipped it. The decor was very cozy and a great place to just have a chat and drink some coffee.

This place is horrible. I came here once before for a drink and I was really unimpressed. I was still willing to give 3 stars because it was clean, the employees were decent, and it was possible that what I ordered was just bad choice on my end. I went back again with an open mind. I ordered a different drink (milk tea) and it's safe to say I hate this place even more. First of all, my drink was the most disgusting milk tea I have ever tasted. I don't know what was worse the tea or the boba. I could not finish it. But let me rewind to before I even tasted it. The girl handed me my overpriced drink, I went to sip it and a least a quarter of my drink spilled all down my shirt, pants, boots, into my shopping bag, and in my hair!!!!!! SHE DIDN'T SEAL THE DRINK PROPERLY!!!! I was soooooo upset! Still in my head I was like it's okay accidents happen, don't get mad. I walked up to the counter to show them what had happened. She clearly saw the mess all over me and the floor. I asked for napkins and not one person budged. I asked again and the girl was like " oh there are napkins on the tables". No employee cared to help or said sorry. That is some seriously messed up customer service. While I was cleaning the mess someone came out to mop the floor and someone else came up behind me to place a newly covered drink on the table and walked away without saying anything. I'm so confused it wasn't even busy. A little acknowledgment would have been greatly appreciated. I left drenched, sticky, and so upset with how rude they were. I never give one stars but I guess there is a first time for everything.
One of the best Mexican restaurants in South Tucson. The meats are done to perfection. Give them a try and you will find yourself returning for more.
Awesome sound system with a fun 80s-90s playlist, and probably the best wings in Boise.

Eccentric brewery, because they serve food only on weekdays. This is very disappointing for weekend visitors since I had an excellent sausage parm sandwich that came with a side GREEN ---no white leaves--- salad with a mustard vinaigrette, but lucky me since I came on a Thursday. I have not tried all of their beers, but I've been pleased so far. Fruit beers like Pynk or the Grapefruit Ale? Include me out on those, but I'm willing to gleefully plow through the rest. Food trucks and tours on weekends, but try not to miss their own kitchen on weekdays.

Friendly staff, great beers, mostly free parking.

Neighbors recommended Susie's and we were not disappointed.  The bread was great but save room for the large portions of great food!  We tried the chicken marsala, chicken cacciatore, and crabmeat stuffed fish all were delicious.  Service was friendly and prompt.  No room for desert.

Ordered the chicken red curry, the chicken was very tough. I always order and love red curry at Thai restaurants but I was not a fan of this particular recipe. If a friend wants to meet here again, I will try something new.

I enjoyed the jasmine tea and the crispy fried spring roll, but I didn't like their spring roll sauce.

I appreciated the Splenda for my tea (instead of the pink or blue stuff.)

Had a Christmas get together with my nursing friends and the staff from Cooper's Hawk located on 96th street was phenomenal! Thank you for accommodating our large group.  The servers were very professional, the people at the front that checked us in were super frienfly, the wine was amazing and the food was delicious.  Will definitely come back. I did not catch their names but i highly recommend this place. 
Ruth Boberg
Best pizza in Florida! The wild knots were amazing and the staff, particularly Jacob, was fantastic. We can't wait to go there again!
Pleasant atmosphere. Clean. Cold beer. Great band. Friendly patrons. No fighting or riff-raff!! Like this place a lot!!

I am a regular at Casa Ramos Tampa​... at least two or three visits a month. Service is usually fair to good ( I still miss Gino, he was odd, but Awesome Service!) 

Tonight... we were seated by Sonia and were told that Josh would be our waiter. Cally brought chips and salsa immediately, as she is always on top of it! We waited and waited some more. I noticed some customers that came in several minutes after we did, already getting their drink orders (bar, not just water)... and we had not even seen our waiter yet. And at that time, there were very few tables that were full... if you had been really busy, I would have understood! 

I finally got tired of waiting and flagged down Sonia... who took our orders, and Cally brought us some water. I had been planning on at least a margarita... but decided against it since I mildly upset already. Sonia brought me a margarita on the house, which was appreciated.. Thank you for that. 

I had the Carne Asada (a favorite usually) and it seem to be lacking the wonderful marinaded flavor that I usually get. But it was edible. Beans were good, like always. Usually we love the rice... but tonight it was dry, and seemed off, not as fresh as usual.

My girlfriend had the Camarones Monterey... one of her favorites. She said the shrimp were tough, when normally they are tender. 

All in all a less than perfect night at one of our favorite spots. We will be back, and hopefully things will be back to normal? I hope so... we really do like Casa Ramos! From 5 stars to 3 for now!

Bonuts are deliciously baked biscuit-donut balls topped with lovely marscapone and berry compote. It was a perfect complement to the spicy hot chicken on a biscuit (the Princess). 

There was not lineup on Sunday at 7:45am (no surprise!) but when we left there was a queue outside!
Marisa & Dan's rehearsal dinner was here. It was perfect for a rehearsal dinner. The service and staff were great. There was a prefix menu and it was good.

With such high acclaim, it was impossible to pass up the dining experience at Commander's when visiting Nola. Made reservations easily online. We even got there 20 minutes early and they still sat us right away.

Atmosphere; This restaurant is HUGE. We walked through a few rooms and up a few stairs before we were led to the beautiful garden room. Very dim, very intimate, very pretty.

Food: My parents opted for the Prixe Fix Menu. For starters my mother go the gumbo, which I tried and figured it was way too salty for my taste. My father ordered the turtle soup, and surprisingly I enjoyed the flavor, but not so much the texture of the turtle. I ordered the Fois Gras, and although it was decadent, the fatty taste was overwhelming.

For the main course, I ordered the Filet Mignon, medium rare. OH MY GOD IF THAT WASN'T THE MOST DELICIOUS STEAK bdfjksdbfjks (my mouth is watering thinking about it). The meat was tender and the portion was generous). My dad ordered the quail, which I think was the best quail I've ever had. It wasn't gamey, the meat was juicy, and the flavor was out of this world. My mom ordered the seared gulf fish, and that was probably my least favorite of the three. It was too salty.

Dessert: Bread pudding and creme brulee. The presentation of both was amazing, and both desserts were awesome. 

Service: Great, but there were too many servers bringing us different things, it was hard to tell who to inquire with.

Overall, great experience. Worth the hefty amount of money it cost.

We were staying only a few blocks from this place so i decided to grab a slice of cheese pizza  and wash it down with a cold Red Stripe. Pizza was good, service was good, and the beer was good. I will definitely revisit this place when I come back to Philly

Where do I start.  I like Toto's pizza, it's made from quality ingredients you can tell.  It's not greasy and the crust is really good and you can get a wheat crust as well.  My son's favorite is the buffalo chicken....that's not really my taste.  I like the fact that they have an array of pizzas to choose from to just get a slice.  My favorite is the white pizza with ricotta and basil.  

I live in the neighborhood and this is Mt Airy at its finest.  The owner and staff are super friendly no request is a problem.  The neighborhood kids stop in after school and get pizza and are welcomed and taught a lesson or two should they get out of hand (imagine that).  

Great neighborhood pizza joint!

It is said that this place was an old Bob Dylan hangout, but that's not the reason to come here. Come here for the food and drink!

www.coopsplace.net adding the website helps too.

I've never considered myself much of a rabbit person, but the Jambalaya made with rabbit and smoked sausage here is F'n unbelievable. I've visited New Orleans 3 times. After I found this gem I try to eat here twice on every trip.

Splurge a little and order the Jambalaya Supreme. They add in shrimp and tasso (cajun ham). The smoked duck quesadilla was pretty good too. I"m getting soooo hungry just writing about this place.

PS...They also pour a mean drink here.
Bacon infused Bloody Mary is delicious! Might sound gross but it's a must try! St. Peter's was delicious. I had it with catfish instead of the drum but it was still delicious!

I really would give this place a 4.5/5, if it allowed it. 

The food is awesome, if you're into Indian cuisine and good kabobs, this is the place for you. I went to the NE location in Philly, but I know they have a West Philly location that all my friends love. It's a small place but it accommodates a lot of people. I usually visit with my family but most recently I went with 10 friends and the space was perfect. 

The quality of food is good, especially the meats. I love their side of chickpeas and spinach, but all other sides are equally delicious. My favorite is the chicken kabob platter and my friends all liked the lamb chops. They have amazing mango lassi, it's not as thick as they usually are.

Service is good, everyone was nice and accommodating. It took around 30 minutes for all of our food to come out, and it's really good for freshly made meat. When you're there...DO NOT MISS OUT ON THE NAN.

I have been eating at hipcity for years. I crave the hipcity ranch occasionally and treat myself to it. More recently, the sandwich has been tasting not amazing and at the price point quite honestly not worth it. It used to have a crunchy outside and juicy inside and was covered in the delicious ranch sauce. However, the recent times I've gotten this sandwich it has been very dry and flavorless. The brioche bun(which before got soggy very quickly so wasn't great in the first place) was replaced by a rubbery bread. We also made the mistake of trying the new oh maitake burger which was dry and tasted like cardboard, and was such a small burger at a ridiculous price. Overall, I'm pretty disappointed with the decrease in quality in what was previously a fantastic alternative for vegans/vegetarians.

Great place that is quick and has the best queso in the world. They definitely don't skimp you on the burrito portions...holy crap those things are the size of a footballs. Margarita's are also off the chain and the outdoor seating is pretty awesome as well.

This is my favorite place in town for breakfast or brunch. They have a great menu from veggie burgers to amazing pancakes and fresh juices. I have tried several things on their menu and I loved all of them! Their waiters are super friendly and the food always comes right away. Jessica is always super nice!! 

I love this place!

We haven't gone in a while so I figured why not give it another chance. The food was horrible and the host was not very friendly and the waitress was subpar. Definitely worth the 5 minute drive to the Woodstown diner. Which stinks because this diner used to be one of our favorites.

One word: FINALLY! Finally, there is a decent Chinese place around here! After trying the worst around here and Speedway I was about to give up! But.. what's life without Chinese takeout? I ordered the General Tso's.. YUM though I ordered Mild (you never what there version of mild is) and it wasn't the most flavorful/spicy.  Next time I know to get spicy or whatever the next step up is. We also ordered the Sweet and Sour chicken which was great as well.  All I can say is thank you Fei Da for existing and catering to my very pregnant wife's cravings, I might get to sleep in the bed tonight :)

Panera's is a (national or just northeast, not sure) chain, but it is one of my favorites.  You can eat meat chili and greasy chicken sandwiches, or you can eat very healthy with a salad and soup selection that is extensive.  So in short, they seem to have something on the menu for everyone.

It's a tad pricier than I would like, but an excellent alternative to burgers or sub sandwiches and I trust the food more.

First stop while visiting Nashville was biscuit love. I'd highly recommend for a unique meal. I ordered the nasty princess which isn't on the menu but it's a very popular alternative from what I had previously read on yelp reviews.  The bonuts are phenomenal.  Everyone visiting should do themselves the favor and try. My wife had the blacklock hash and she would rank it as a b- to a c on rating. It's mainly potatoes, which isn't a bad thing but she was hoping for more sausage. The coffee and sweet tea was exceptional. All in all I'll be back and I think everyone should give it a try!

Great romantic and quaint setting. This restaurant is one of the handful of restaurants that make 104 St THE best street in Edmonton. 

The owners are part of the staff which makes the service stupendous! 

They have a lovely wine selection and freshly made espressos for after. Their cheese board with meats is very unique and delicious and carries all naturally produced and locally made selections. Our server was well versed on where each thing on out board came from and what to expect in your first bite. 

The restaurant is small, which would normally be unfortunate because I've had to go elsewhere, however it's the cozy quaintness that is one of my favourite things. You feel like you're just one of a couple handfuls of people who got lucky that night to be guest.

This is exactly what downtown Tucson needed. 

A grocery store that offers local and non local foods, pastries, meat, fish, and a bar. They have everything from Poptarts to salmon. The produce looks fresh, the only thing they don't have yet is the meat market. The salad/breakfast bar looks versatile and fresh. The deli section has all the classic sandwiches and I can't wait to try one. There is a patio outback for people to drink their beers, for which you can either get on tap or buy from their alcohol section, so they are pretty diverse. 

They don't take amex yet.

AMAZING CHICKEN SHAWERMA. Juicy, seasoned, just right! They are flexible and will let you get combo bowls, and to get multiple servings of toppings.

Be sure to go to the second floor! Very cute place to sit.

They also gave us basbousa and falafel on the house along with everyone else who was sitting there! So nice!

I don't know what the fuss is all about...its a beautiful place yes....but they open the walls and the flies are in your face and your swatting trying to eat and I left with mosquito bites on my legs and arms....a very expensive picnic. Our server was wonderful !!! But the Hostess was a SNOB...this is a beautiful restaurant that charges way too much for the food and a beautiful atmosphere doesn't make the food taste better and the high prices lower.  Trying to make back the "millions" (ok) on the making of this restaurant.   Our table had serveral items off the menu and I am sorry its just not my cup of tea.  Just because they bring you a glass water bottle to the table and charge high prices for uneatable food doesn't rate high marks. My food went in a to go box because the others with me didn't want me wasting food...it went in the trash when I got home....

I was a looking forward to trying Ray's Burgers and Fries as soon as I saw the menu, and I couldn't help but compare it to Five Guys.  Ray's features the same build your own burger setup, and is almost as good as Five Guys.  I loaded up on toppings, and all were very fresh, except for the canned jalepenos (fresh would have been better).  The fresh cut fries were also good, and come in a large styrofoam cup, just like Five Guys, but Ray's isn't quite as generous as Five Guys.  In addition, Ray's has hot dogs, shrimp, crabcakes, fish sandwhichs, chicken finger, and chicken wings.  Overall, Ray's has great burgers and fries, and I'll definately return.  Only one start demerit, because I couldn't shake the compairson to the slightly better Five Guys.

This used to be my go to place to take friends from out of town. Ate lunch there on 03 Feb 18, and it was average at best.
I'll give it to them  that the beer was cold as always.....Draw Two....but the roast beef poboy was dry & not near what I remember it.
Fried pickles, 3 Po boys, two cups of soup and 6 beers and the bill was $105. So not only did the food quality decline, the prices increased.
I'm guessing it's new ownership.
The place was a great find!!!   The service was friendlyand the food outstanding! The breakfast sandwich with eggs, arugūa, and cheese - delicious and gifantic.

The coolest little spot in Midtown. Our group loved the drinks and the food there is awesome. The female bartenders there also have great customer service. Definitely making my way back soon! (Pro Tip: order the garlic fries you won't regret it)

Super excited that there is a new coffee spot in Clay Terrace that isn't Starbucks! This coffee house is MASSIVE! It has a really fun vibe inside though and the staff was super friendly and helpful because it can be a bit overwhelming at first. They have a specific drink menu if you do not know what to get but I just went ahead and got an iced vanilla latte with soy. It was pretty good! I didn't really feel like I was drinking coffee because the coffee flavor wasn't really there and it was a little pricy but it was still good! They have plenty of seating (indoor and outdoor) and if you ever need to rent a conference room, they have you covered! I will for sure be back to try some of their cold brews and hang out for awhile rather than getting it to go.

There is a first time for everything.   

At first glance I was going to skip it because of the way the outside looked but when I got inside you could not believe the decor.   It was stunning. 

One of the things I judge a restaurant on is the clientele.   Now I am not saying a seafood restaurant should be filled worth sailors.   But a good Polish restaurant should have some Polish people looking for a taste of home dining.   Likewise,  a great Mexican restaurant would have people who are from that culture enjoying a meal. 

There Journey is primarily a Asian buffet.   They do offer ribs,  grilled steak,  chicken and pizza (hopefully for the kids).   But it is an Asian restaurant. 

I would have to say that approaching 50% of the customers were speaking one of a variety of Asian languages.  Each one of them seem to be excited about and satisfied with the offerings. 

Yes,  there are some of the old buffet regulars like General Tso chicken.   But for the most part,  it was hand crafted,  what I would call,  comfort food. 

There are other reviews that are not as glowing as this one.   If they are regulars,  maybe I got lucky.   All I know is that if I find myself in the area,  I will make an attempt to return.   At $10.99 on a Saturday for lunch,  it is a great value.

Appetizers were great. Service was great. The chicken parm was the most over cooked thing I have ever tasted. Key word. Tasted. I didn't finish my meal and neither did anyone else at my table. I don't recommend unless they improve their food.
BEST SUSHI EVER!!! I love the tuna fantastic appetizer! Great food, great sushi!! The staff is very nice and accommodating. They are very good with my one year old daughter.

My girlfriends and I came to share some sushi. We had the dynamite roll and the black widow. The dynamite roll was okay and the black widow was amazing! One of my favorite rolls to date.

We started with the edamame and that was also good but way too salty. There was what looked like a cup of salt just dumped over the top.

Had the most wonderful young girl by the name of Brya. Apologize if the spelling  is incorrect. She was polite, helpful, knowledgeable , patient and so sweet! I needed to order pizza for my students but didn't need it till next day. We came up with a solution and she helped me order pizzas! The visually impaired students will be thrilled tomorrow! Thanks Brya! 
Yes

Absolutely love their pizza !!! Totally worth the money and quite filling to be honest. They are a family owned restaurant on the mainstreet of Newtown and the owner's are very down to earth and kind. Their pies are packed with a plethora of fresh mozzarella cheese and their sauce is to die for !!

We visited Hawkers last week and were excited to share this restaurant with family from out of town. I told them about the delicious food we had there last time and was looking forward to enjoying their street skewers and spring rolls again. 

I called ahead for seating so we only had to wait a few minutes when we arrived. Our server was very nice, but the first thing he did was tell us that they were out of some of their menu items, which is never a good start. They were out of all of their Street Skewers (Bulgogi Beef, Bulgogi Chicken AND Satay Chicken), Spring Rolls, Siu Yoke, and Coconut Shrimp! Since they were completely out of everything I had planned to order, this was very disappointing - but we already drove 30 minutes to get there and were hungry so we stayed. The server came back and mentioned that they ran out of something else, but I forgot which item it was. 

After reviewing what was still available on the menu we found a few things to order to share with our table: Roti Canai, Pork Belly Steamed Baos, Golden Wontons, Wok Seared Chicken Dumplings, Korean Twice Fried Wings and Jo-He Bag O' Donuts for dessert. 

Everyone at our table enjoyed the Roti Canai. We only wish it came with more of the flatbread. 

The Pork Belly Steamed Baos were good, but I didn't realize they came with a slice of hard boiled egg and some type of relish (not on menu). That threw the taste off for me. Most of us ended up picking off the egg and relish, and enjoyed the pork belly and bun by themselves. 

My kids liked the Golden Wontons, but I didn't try them so I can't give details. 

The Wok Seared Chicken Dumplings looked good when they were brought to the table, like they did on our last visit. After biting in, I noticed the chicken inside looked like it was still pink, but I thought it might have been the lighting. They also tasted a little undercooked so we ended up taking one basket of the chicken dumplings home. When we got home I cut one open to double check in good lighting and they were in fact still raw in the middle. Not sure I would order them again after that. 

The Korean Twice Fried Wings we're definitely the hit of the night at our table. The wings looked HUGE (see photo) - not like the tiny wings you see at some places. Everyone enjoyed the wings and we went through at least 2 baskets. 

We got one Bag O' Donuts to share, which were served in a small brown paper bag with a few wooden skewers to use to pick the donuts up out of the bag. No one at our table liked the donuts. I was expecting a light and fluffy interior with a crisp exterior. Unfortunately, the inside was raw dough and inedible. This was disappointing because they looked good from outside. 

We were told that the reason they were out of so many items was because it was a Monday and they are so busy on the weekends that they are often out of things on Mondays. If this is not a one time event and they know they are that busy on weekends, why don't they prepare and order extra food so they don't run out for Mondays? Otherwise, maybe post online that they are out of particular items (or that they usually tun out on Mondays). When we called ahead for seating they really should have mentioned it then - I wouldn't have driven 30 minutes there if I knew they were out of everything I wanted (or even if there was a good chance they could be). 

The raw food was concerning and a safety issue. It was a Monday evening and they had plenty of empty tables, so it didn't seem like the kitchen would have been swamped and in a rush to get food out. I could see if they were swamped on a Friday or Saturday evening and some things slipped by their QC as a result. 

I hate to post this bad review because we loved Hawkers on our first visit and wanted to love them this time. Being out of so many menu items and getting 2 items (chicken dumplings and donuts) that were still raw inside was a huge disappointment. The kind and attentive staff would have gotten 5 stars if we could review them individually. Hopefully our recent visit was a fluke and they will return to their high quality on future visits. If we do go back, it definitely won't be on a Monday!

Very average Mexican food. I can think of at least ten other places off the top of my head with better fare than Abuelo's. The chips and salsa were nothing to write home about, and my chicken fajitas were good, but very basic. Note that the portions are quite large.

There's a trend with chain restaurants like Abuelo's and Olive Garden using "Ziosks" to pay for the bill - which is convenient, don't get me wrong - but serve as a distraction throughout the meal. Maybe my opinion would be different if I had to entertain small children, as you can play games on the device, for a price.

*This location is difficult to get to with the new US31 interchange.

Unfortunately not a good experience. Both people in the party ended up with nausea, cramping, diarrhea. Called manager to make her aware...said she'd look into it and get back with me...and that never happened.  Hope they figure it out!

I ordered the shrimp fajitas tonight using UberEats, and I have to say, this was one of the most pleasant experiences I've had with customer service. My order was placed at 8:15, and by 9:25 I still had not received it. I called the store, left a message, and a manager named Will immediately called me back. He stayed on the phone with me for almost 20 minutes trying to figure out what was wrong (turns out a driver had been assigned to my order but never showed up). Since the store had closed in the meantime, he granted me a full refund and even offered a voucher for another free meal on the house for my next visit. So nice! Right at the end of our conversation, another driver actually came to pick up the order. Will still refunded me, sent the order with the new driver, and even gave me an order of guacamole on the house! Great job, Will, you've gained another lifelong customer!! I'll be telling everyone how wonderful you are. (Also, the shrimp fajitas I ordered were FANTASTIC). I love Taqueria del Sol!

I can't believe I've never heard of this place before.  I saw all the good reviews it was getting on Yelp while my wife and I were Christmas shopping and decided to check this place out.  I didn't even realize it was in a mall.  But they're absolutely delicious burgers.  And it is a full bar.  It would be worth the trip just to come down here from South Jersey.
This place has odd hours but the food is so yummy here. They have good portion sizes, my favorite is the catfish platter
We had a great takeout meal! The place was a little difficult to find, but the food was delicious. We enjoyed pad thai, and a spicy noodle dish, and would definitely get takeout from here again.

Best chicken sandwich in MO! Hand breaded chicken, that is crispy on the outside but tender chicken on the inside. The sauce selection is top notch and special salt for the fries is something different. I got the spicy chicken sandy. Not too spicy but a steady kick....

This place was right across from my hotel and I'm glad I stopped in. The waitress was very attentive and friendly. My drink (can't remember the exact name, strawberry something) was so good and my salmon was excellent! The crab cake dip appetizer was probably my favorite thing we had. I'll definitely come back next time I'm in town.

The food was good, and the queso dip was excellent. However, I will not be visiting this establishment again due to the roach we noticed crawling on the wall by our table. Unfortunately for us we'd already eaten & were waiting on the check. I personally can not eat anywhere I know has roaches. If this is something that doesn't bother you, by all means give it a shot. As stated previously the food was good. I, on the other hand, don't care how good the food is if roaches dine there as well.

The owners are fellow alum, so I wanted to check out their cafe and grab some whole bean coffee while I was in the area on a quick weekend getaway. The space is bright and clean with plenty of seating and a cute curation of non-coffee goods for purchase, including totes, postcards, shirts, etc. in the corner.

I was tempted to order the bouquet latte, because it sounded delicious, but I ended up opting for their cold brew. It was super good, and I love being able to see their open brew process on top of their cabinets behind the service counter. For those needing a bite to eat, they did have a few things in the case, including granola and vegan bites.

If you have Instagram and live in the area, you've likely already seen their building whether you knew it or not. They have the iconic black and white Saint Petersburg mural (very postcard-esque) on the outside of their shop. People stop and snap photos in front of it all the time.

I'm hoping work sends me back to this area soon, because I'd love to set up a remote office for an hour or two and be able to really stay and enjoy the space. Love that I finally got to check it out!

LOVE this place. Amazing flavors, great portions, fresh ingredients. It's become at least a once a week thing for me, if that tells you anything.

**If you are weird about textures, avoid the noodles. That's my only thing, not a complaint. Just a personal preference and trying to save you the disappointment if weird textures are a thing for you**

The coconut pudding with mango is soooo good. And you don't have to feel guilty about eating it either. A nice, healthy treat. Win win
This was a fun place to eat. You are able to try multiple types of meat, that they carve at your table. Highly recommend.

It doesn't look like much but if we come to New Orleans it is a must! It's a tight fit but trust me it's soo worth it. Love the people and the whole atmosphere. Look forward to the visit every year and I'm not a hamburger person either! Food is so amazing buns are toasted and so fresh. Love it! Happy Mardi Gra everyone.

It is my Birthday, I have been sitting at this table for 20 minutes, before this my Son ( he is 18)& I we're seated at the. As We sat there for 25 extra minutes. We came all the way from Wrightstown, to watch the 4 servers walk past Us. Until someone final spoke to let's Us know Due to my 18 year old to sit at the table. 1/2 later she tells Is to scan to place order. What happened to customer service and the tables to sit at& signs ti know how/ what to do?
Recently my friends and I had a late lunch at Abel's. Food was fantastic and the service was wonderful. I plan on going again!

Big Firehouse Subs fan here. I have had Firehouse Subs in Carson in the past, but some how must have slipped my memory. We ordered online and I loved that you could select your time. I got the Meatball sub and it was so fantastic. The bread was perfect and not too soggy, the sauce had great flavor without being spicy, and the meatballs are some of the best I have ever had!! The sprinkle of Italian seasoning on the top of the cheese is a great touch. 

Our order was ready when we arrived with no issues! This was a great quick dinner on these crazy nights.

Thank You Lord for Flambo Burgers & Bar.  
Mason's GMBCC (God, Government, Building, Company, Clubs, & Club)
Terrance D. Walsh, Jr.

HORRIBLE service.  We sat in the bar area and the place was packed.  I am normally understanding when it is busy, but I am not so understanding today.  The table next to us had faster service and they turned over that table 3 times while we were there.  You figured if two women spending close to $100.00 for lunch we would receive a little more attention.  We ordered appetizers and it took forever to come out.  When the entrees finally came, the waitress attempted to give me a dirty spoon but I looked up and saw her trying to wipe the crud off the spoon.  So I sat there for 10 minutes waiting for a spoon.  NO one came back with a spoon.  So I had to use the teaspoon because I hate eating cold food,  About 10 minutes after starting on my gumbo, I see a wait staff come walking by.  The person didn't come back until 10 minutes later.  When dessert came out, they only brought out 1 spoon for 2 slices of cheesecake.  It took another 5 minutes for someone to bring one.  I miss the customer service I usually get it this chain.  

The gumbo that I ordered was ok.  The shrimp was hard and chewy.  I ordered brown rice and white rice came out instead.  I didn't want to send it back because they are so damn slow here.  The food isn't as good as I remember it.

Went here with my family for lunch on yesterday, and was quite impressed. The barbecue was very good. It had a great smoked flavor and their sauce added a good taste to the meat. 
If you get a platter you get three sides but the sides are pretty small. Also you get a piece of corn bread which is very moist. It is also the sweet kind of corn bread.

The service is friendly and very helpful.

The atmosphere is much more like a McDonald's or Burger King but a slightly nicer feel. It is a nice place to go and get a bite but don't expect anything more than that.

Now that the daughter is committed to another three years in the Lou, it is time to commence the Burgers of Dogtown competition, and the first contestant is gonna be tough to beat!

Seamus McDaniel' has: lots of room, friendly staff, simple but great buffalo wings, and juicy, succulent 10 oz Seamus Burgers on heavenly sesame buns! Now, the place seems like every dive bar you went to in college but trust me, it has way better food! They even have diet Dr Pepper, and they had great pops! Or sodas, or cokes, whatever you call them.

Cheddar & bacon, blue and bacon, or southwest, medium or well done, this is a tough burger to beat.

Wish we could get in here to try it. My husband and I have made several attempts to eat here but every time we go iit's crowded and there is a long wait. Can't tell if it's the slow service or popularity. We waited once for 15 minutes and we were never even greeted so we walked out. We tried ordering and taking sushi to go. By the time I got home it was good and I am sure it would have been better if I had gotten to eat it when it was freshly made. (It was a fried California roll.

For the 3rd (and final time for me!) Online ordering is a disaster. Food isn't ready on time. Long waits inside....at least 20 people waiting. Half a dozen employees on the scene. If you plan to grab & go in the time of COVID, be prepared for hiccups.

The chicken was great. The pizzas crust was great but the sauce was a bit too sweet and not flavorable last night. This morning it was better! Delivery guy John Jr was kool and accommodating because the wrong address was in the system.   Thanks - I will purchase again.

Never, ever, ever bother with this place on a Friday or Saturday night - which is, of course, when you're most likely to crave ice cream. I always attempt to get a cookie dough blast, when ends up being a cup of vanilla ice cream with practically NOTHING in it. To solve the problem, I asked for extra - of course, am charged extra, and I swear they put in even less. It's freaking ridiculous. If I wanted vanilla ice cream, I'd stay home.

Also, on warm summer nights (or any Friday or Saturday after sunset), the parking lot is over-run by spoiled teens harassing customers with a megaphone, or shouting at them, or being generally unpleasant to anyone but themselves. If management is even present, they sure don't intervene.

Super frustrating. How hard can it be, really, to use a full cup of the topping?  9 times out of 10 this happens. Never EVER again.

My husband and I live in the Marigny/Bywater, and make our way over to Who Dat once every couple weeks.  The service is great, staff is always friendly.  Their standard breakfast (eggs, grits, toast) is pretty good, but the corn cakes are aaaamazing.  Huevos rancheros is one of their specials... corn cakes topped with eggs, black beans, salsa, cheese, and a dollop of sour cream.  It's one of my favorite breakfasts in New Orleans, and it's huge- big enough for my husband and I to split.  We'll continue to frequent Who Dat!

The tuna app was fantastic but oddly served with tortilla chips.  The sushi was good as well as the wine and decor.  We had excellent service by our waitress, but wasn't sure to laugh or be totally disgusted when there was a mouse running around the restaurant during our dining.  Just a simple apology- nothing more, nothing comped.  Just sorry bout that, and i will send the boys out to trap him.  UGH!! I live, work and play in downtown Philly and have never experienced anything like this.

I came here for Sunday brunch a couple weekends ago.. it was pretty good. I recommend the chicken and waffles along with the biscuits and jam (at least that's all I tried). They serve a pecan butter and a blackberry jam with the biscuits - both were delicious and it comes with a large piece of cornbread!

I loved the feel of the restaurant, it's inside of a garage but all dolled up inside and has a nice wood finish. They had a tasty looking cocktail list and a nice bar area where you can sit as well.

The service was great and our waiter was really nice and welcoming.

I don't know what is happening here. This use to be my favorite OG. My boyfriend I went for dinner. We were greeted and sat right away... The place was dead. It took about 5 min for anyone to come by and take our drink order. Our server was nice enough but I couldn't for the life of me understand anything he was saying, so when my order was wrong... I assumed it was because when he read it back I had no idea what he said.

My chicken was way overcooked -- I couldn't eat it. My boyfriend got the tour of Italy and barely touched it. The salad was dry... DRY salad! 

Overall we just wanted to get out. We were right by the kitchen and there were about 6 servers in there at any given time messing around... We just wanted a simple dinner from somewhere we thought we knew what we would expect. We probably won't be back.

this is literally best restaurant I have eaten at in a long time in New Orleans. Most of our great food is cajun, creole, and southern based foods, so when a new kind of restaurant comes out, we will flock to it. The food here is inventive, creative, delicious and does not disappoint. Our table ordered the lamb, two kinds of hummus, the ikra, and about four other dishes. Our bill came to $40 each including a generous tip for our waitress who was patient, attentive and all around awesome. Anyone who eats out knows that is pretty cheap for the quality of ingredients being used in each dish. You can feel the care and love as each dish hits the table and literally every dish was incredible. I didn't have one complaint. The atmosphere is gorgeous, inviting and clean. My favorite dish was the Lamb. As a Persian, I appreciate all the traditional middle eastern ingredients being revived in a new, inventive fashion. Also, if you love coffee, this was literally the best cup of coffee I have had in my life. Better than any espresso in Italy. I will be going back here for lunch, dinner, dessert, drinks and coffee.

I live a block away and have always wanted a good bar to move into this space. Unfortunately, for one reason or another, they never work out and I won't be surprised if Bar One follows suit. 

The drink menu does not have prices. That should have been the biggest indicator. We ordered Kenzingers and Philly Pale Ales and the prices were absolutely ridiculous. Almost $7 for a single Kenzinger is unheard of, even in the most pretentious Center City bars, and this is South Philly. A shot of Jim Beam- $8. 

I'd rather walk a few blocks and go to literally any other bar then give this place my business again. 

Two stars go towards the half-way decent music and I can't deny that the food smelled pretty good. Can't imagine how overpriced that must be, though...

Came here on cold Wednesday in April. It was a tough day at work so I figured I'd try this place out for happy hour. 

They had a few decent crafts on draft and they were half off. 3 bucks for a decent brew? Hell yea! I read the reviews about their pasta so I decided to try Murph's pasta. Jesus H was it delicious. It was nice and hot (including spice) and a decent portion for 12 bucks. I don't know what kind of pasta was in it, but I think that along with the sauce was homemade. Also the bartender's service was freaking great. Even though she was talking to the regulars, she would always look over whenever I sat down my glass to make sure it wasn't empty. 

It did smell a little funky though so I deducted a star for that. Either way, whenever I'm craving pasta and beer at a good price, I'm coming here.

Went to the new storefront location. I knew it was expensive before going but figured all the good reviews would balance it out. It's not horrible but insanely overpriced. $26 for two coffees and  two tiny pre-made sandwiches. Maybe that would be ok if the sandwiches were bigger and made fresh. I was still hungry after eating my sandwich that was literally the size of the palm of my hand. It was a huge disappointment and will not be back.

Called to check if they delivered to my address was told yes. Called back 5 min later to place order and was told they didnt have a driver right now and they were too busy. They shouldn't advertise delivery of it is only on a case by case basis.
First time in and around Nashville for food and we decided to try Thai is wasn't too bad! I had the Volcano Roll and some Miso soup the roll wasn't terrible, but the Miso soup was on point!

Good to see improvement.  This summer Gentle Ben's did a major remodel and long overdue deep cleaning, In addition, the staff now provides excellent service.  GB hired their new manager about six months ago and he is doing a great job.  

Good restaurants are in short supply in the University's Main Gate area.  Gentle Ben's is a longtime favorite for after- work functions when plentiful beer and bar food are the only standards.  Their lunch offerings, atmosphere and service were all pretty dismal during the past few years, and GB had fallen to last place for me.  In fact, during my visit prior to today's lunch, I waited (and waited) at my table for 20 minutes before finally I gave up and left.

The restaurant is now clean and comfortable and the menus no longer offers "free samples" of pub cuisine on their laminated surface.  More importantly, the host seated me promptly, the waiter arrived within minutes and the service was cheerfully efficient.  The food could still use some work, but hey - they are trying!

So - thank you to the owners, terrific manager and great waitstaff.  It's heartening to see a restaurant take the effort to turn things around.

This USED to be my fav pizza in Indy!  WHATS HAPPENED??  I was a huge supporter, have eaten here at 3 different locations many many times.  Service has always been hit and miss, now even the fare is suffering.  Favorite menu items are being removed: my daughter loves the meatball sandwich, it's gone.  They take no reservations, no problem, but then they leave a table there with a party that hasn't arrived, on a Tuesday, no problem, but on a Saturday night it meant my party stared at an empty table for 40 minutes while we waited.  I used to suggest Pizzology to my many friends, now, go the the standby Bazbeaux, you won't be disappointed.  Too bad Pizzology, we had a great run together.

This is one of my favorite places to dine at in New Orleans. We've been here multiple times over the years as visitors, and now as locals. We always enjoy great food and atmosphere. We especially love the "Chef's Selection" cheeseboard and their courtyard area. The only issue I've ever taken with Grapevine is their service. It's not consistent. Sometimes we have  fantastic wait service, sometimes it's just so-so. However, I highly recommend this place!

Good environment, great spot in downtown Tampa. Huuuuge pancakes, and other portions - god bless America. Friendly waitress that smiled when we were wasting her time, can't get any better than that. Gave us coffee to go. Now that's good service.

surprisingly good food. you can tell the food is made with care, and designed or selected by someone with a good palate. would be fitting to serve in an upscale restaurant--dont let the look of the place fool you. food comes out on the slow side, but not unusual for dishes of this caliber. dont expect low prices despite the decor; the food is priced appropriately for the quality you get. service is good too.

So freaking good' I've been turned on to this place because of people I work with, we have had it two times in 4 days and I need to get control of myself.
The wings are tasty, I had the sweet chili and the lemon pepper, the flavor/ spicy was awesome. All around tasty on its own and with hot sauce and ranch, perfection as well.
The fries "slap" as well, not soggy, perfect amount of salt, and having them with the dipping sauces is perfection.
Loved both of my sets of wings, I love traditional wings, and was impressed. The price point is also great and the quality doesn't disappoint! 
I'll be a repeat customer since both times we've gotten wings they have been awesome. I'm glad I've gotten turned on to this place!

We came into town on a birthday trip and stumbled upon this quaint establishment. 

Our poor server seemed to be the only person at the front of house, and the restaurant was almost at capacity. I can only assume that this was an atypically-busy Monday lunch service. However, she handled everything as efficiently and commendably as anyone could expect. 

The prices are far more than reasonable, and the food surpassed our expectations. We've already decided to come back to Petit Valentien on our next visit to Santa Barbara. 

Well done!

I see you, Portillo's.

I waited as long as I could, but finally had to give in after 2 weeks of Portillo's officially opening here in Fishers. I knew the lines would be long. I understood that it'd be congested due to traffic, so for anyone looking for complaints where that's concerned, look elsewhere because it was exactly what I expected. The biggest line I saw was for the drive-thru, so just be prepared if that's your plan. The parking lot is huge with more than enough spaces. My husband and I ventured in and at first we were confused as to where to start because there are several lines. The line to the left was for pick-up orders (fyi download their app, order ahead, and pick it up just inside the entrance...I heard there's a special $5 off $15 code upon ordering). The line for the main dining is to the right and the crowd you see in the middle is everyone who is waiting for their food.

The menu is large but what makes this place famous is their Chicago hot dogs and Italian beef sandwiches. The cake shakes aren't half bad either! I set out to order the Italian beef with extra gravy. My husband did the same, but had his dipped (i.e. they dip the whole darn sandwich in gravy so it's extra moist) and he also ordered their Chicago dog. Everything was delicious as expected!

We will travel to Portillo's several times and start ordering different menu items just so we make sure we try everything. Worth the wait, worth the lines, but if you want a more relaxing visit, maybe think about visiting Portillo's a year from now :)

Go Cubs Go!
The roast pork with roasted peppers and sharp prov is one of the greatest sandwiches in Philly. Never go to Reading Terminal without getting a roast pork from DeNics.

Delicious food and great service!  Had the strawberry and blue agave margaritas.  Our waitress gave us great advice, and we got the jumbos! Salsa must be made with roasted tomatoes. So good!  Menu is really different!  Loved it!

Great selection of fresh fish and veggies. That also offer baked goods and ready made meals. Dessert and Ice cream selection is excellent, they even have PANDAN ice cream, which is hard to find even in Asian stores. Keep you jacket or sweater on though, coz it's really cold in there. I live up in NYC and wish i had an hmart in my neighborhood.

So the food is pretty good here but it's not the best ever and there are plenty of other places in the New Orleans area that serve better food, however those places aren't open 24 hours! The staff could definitely use a little training on customer service and how to speak to customers but the food is consistent and at 3 am, it's probably the best you can get!

Cute place for some creative brunch food! A group of us (6 people total) went at ~8 am on a Saturday, and there was no wait.

Nutella Pop Tart: 5/5
A tasty treat! With a flaky crust and smooth Nutella filling, this was significantly better than a store-bought Pop-Tart.

Hot Mess (with home fries): 3/5
This was a decent breakfast sandwich. It was a little hard to eat, and the portion looked to be small at first, but it ended up being the perfect size, as I left the restaurant full but not overstuffed. I loved the combination of ingredients, with the egg cooked to be perfectly runny, the bacon adding some crispy savoriness, the hot pepper jam providing a spicy kick, and the avocado contributing a creamy freshness. However, the biscuit was served cold, and the home fries, while flavorful, were a little overcooked for my taste.

Service: 5/5
Our server was attentive, knowledge about the menu, and patient with us, as some members of our party took some time to arrive. Our food came out relatively quickly, and there was no problem dividing up the check among the 6 of us.

This place was absolutely GREAT!! It all started with the friendliness at the front counter, and the great customer service continued throughout our entire time spent having dinner. The same lady from the counter cane by to ask us how everything was and offered to get us refills on our drinks, which was followed by the cook himself coming up and asking us how everything was tasting. 
Now as far as the BBQ...it was as good, if not better than the customer service. We had chicken, ribs and prime briskets and I gotta say that they were ALL absolutely delicious, not only was the BBQ sauce great, but meat was tender, juicy and absolutely great as it would fall right off the bones. Also, the sides were delicious as well as we went with some Mac & cheese, beans and potato salad. Overall, this place was amazing with there service and attention to their client, but more impressive was their attention to their food which by far one the best best BBQ's I've ever had.
Wow! My family and I just finished our first dinner and we all so happy with our full belly's. The ribs and chicken are five stars along with great sides!

I enjoy the Turkey burger and sweet potato fries but the mgmt needs work. If you get there after 8 they are removing condiments from the table, turning chairs over and sweeping the carpet. I guess they're trying to chase me out. Message received. Even though  they are just around the corner, I won't be back for a while
Can't speak for the food here but the biscuit are good as H*ll!!

I went there today with my family, we love meat, and we usually visit Chima or Fogo the Chao, those are expensive place, good but not better than this place, the meat has a great flavor, the Colombian host was super friendly, everything was great, it doesn't look great from outside, but inside is clean and once you taste the food, believe me you got to come back, and the price is excellent.

Well this one here is a doozy, so buckle up. Being from there northeast originally and having moved out south I haven't experienced a lot of my native food or culture. Recently though I was recommend Frankies Cheese Steaks by a co worker and I had to go and see if this place could hold up to its name. Sadly it could not, the morning worker Michelle or Micheal I can't recall, was a bitter lady who did not represent Frankies in a good light at all. I can get past this, it's early it's a Tuesday morning whatever. But the food, now back in my youth I experimented with food and had some good results and some bad results but god almighty I never created anything so atrocious. The meat was cold and the cheese tasted like it was fresh, fresh from sitting outside for several days in the heat. Now I don't like to use this language but if anywhere in town is worse than Grant and Alvernon it is that (Pardon my langue) shit hole. I would recommend a complete shutdown until they get their staff and their menu in order.

My biggest disappointment with this place is that I hadn't been here before! Seriously. I have eaten at every place around the TVC a dozens times, but I now know I could have done as well or better if I had just gone here.

It all starts with the meats. I made sure to try the pork and brisket, both of which were tender and well flavored. The pork had a great smoke like you would find from a really top level BBQ joint. The variety of sauces used throughout the menu were spicy and well thought out. 

I encourage you to get the loaded nachos with the pork. Keep in mind, this could be enough for most people to split three ways as an entree.

The wait staff was great and kept on top of things while not giving you that feel like you are being watched all the time. If the weather is nice, be sure to eat outside. The porch is well shaded with the festively decorated trees.

I will be back soon and get more specific. I would have been more so but I was so focused on the food that I didn't even think to document my dinner.

I was really craving boulevard pizza on Friday to take home I thought I would call it in and run some errands while I was at it as I called it in I noticed the girl on the phone seemed flustered and annoyed I tried to place an order she immediately shut me down with it's going to be an 1 hr and 1/2 wait I said even for pick up? She said yes I was disappointed ended up going to pizza plus on Oddie who was way busier but managed to get my order in and ready in 30 minutes... maybe they just need more employees or better phone etiquette. Either way this place has lost a very good consumer!!

This place was great!!  I started with the duck fat tater tots. Which were fantastic. Followed that with the Nashville chicken and waffle which set my mouth ablaze but I couldn't stop eating it. Highly recommend this place

We have had several bad experiences here and we now refuse to order food anymore. Our first experience was dining in near the bar area. The service was appalling and the food was only ok. We moved to the area shortly after that and began ordering take out. While the pizza is ok and cheesesteaks are delicious the service is so bad that we can no longer go there. Also, I think they overcharge you for your order. Our last bill was easily $10 more than what we ordered. Overall if you're going to eat here check your receipt and be prepared for rude employees.

I went out to lunch with myself and 5 other girls this past weekend. Our bill was at least 150.00. I order a mimosa and the drink was placed down next to me. I had no idea the drink was there... (THIS WAS NOT THE SERVERS FAULT) and I knocked the drink over. The server told me I had to pay for the drink. Excuse me?! So I guess the manager couldn't take my drink off!! I spent years in the restaurant business ... Every girl at the table has worked in the business. My one girl friend was a restaurant owner in South Philly. We were all appalled. At least come over yourself and tell me instead of making your server. I know Adelphias makes money...you are no small business. I know what liquor cost are and how much you up charge for drinks. Have some class. I would have called you over to take the drink off but I would have ended up cursing you out and we had 2 young girls with us and I didn't feel that was appropriate. 

To whoever that manager was.... Your a douche bag 

To the two girls who took care of us .. Thank you girls you were great. Tell your douche bag manager you don't need to split a 6 top. That's lame no one makes money that way.
I absolutely loved the beers, the service, the crispy calamari appetizer. Excellent experience!

A lovely family ran restaurant. We wanted a low key dinner before going to the theater.  The service was efficient and friendly.   Both my fiancée and I enjoyed our meals.  There aren't a lot of tables but even on a Saturday night, we didn't have a problem grabbing one.

I have to say, the decor and atmosphere are great. The cashiers were friendly and prompt.  After that, however, it all went downhill.  The drink machine was out of ice--for a long time.  The orders seemed to take a long time to come out. The server was a a little abrasive.  You could tell it was just part of her personality; she wasn't being mean or anything.  The food was underwhelming. There was a group of six of us and nothing was really all that great. 

I may try them again, just to be fair, but it's not a place I'd suggest to the group next time.

Had a great late breakfast here after the Blink 182 concert. Creative drinks, and food. Good service. We had the hush puppies, french toast, and crab cake. All were delicious. Easy to reccommend this place! Get a bloody mary!

I love the ambience and the food. Had the American cup burger it was beyond juicy and tender. Love the service love the look and will definitely be coming back to try more things. But it is on the expensive side.

Imagine you've made the mistake of visiting Santa Barbara with two children who are growing up in a Mexican food-deprived city, and who are therefore unwilling to eat Mexican food of any kind -- no, not even a quesadilla! I know, kids suck.

So you decide the kids are old enough to stay alone for the hour it will take for you to go to the legendary taqueria made famous by Julia Child's patronage. You give the kids a couple of bowls of noodles and unlimited access to Minecraft, and race the mile to aforementioned taqueria....only to discover that it's closed on Wednesdays. Why, God, why????

Now you've got a dilemma: the clock is ticking and you have to choose another Mexican restaurant fast. Yelpers also Los Agaves, which you passed on the way over. So you stick your head in, only to be dismayed by the relatively modest array of choices on the giant chalk board over the counter where you're supposed to order.

But wait...what is the nice man by the door handing you? It's a menu with EVERY Mexican dish you have ever heard of, and many you haven't. You order the Los Agaves (seafood) enchiladas, and then because you can't resist mole and aren't sure whether you'll be happy with a molcajete, you order the mole enchiladas too. You take your seat, and then remember the salsa bar...and load up on glorious salsas just as a perfect bowl of tortilla chips arrives at your table.

They're followed in short order by an exquisite plate of seafood enchiladas, which come with a salad that has a dressing that tastes EXACTLY like a Creamsicle. I know that sounds like a criticism but it is actually so delicious that when I get home I am going to try melting and bottling a Creamsicle to use as salad dressing.

Shortly afterwards, the mole enchiladas make their appearance...and they are just as tasty! In fact I have to stop searching my memory for the right adjectives because it's making my mouth water to think about it.

As for Julia Child's taqueria...well, maybe we'll still get there. Or maybe we'll skip it, and head right back to Los Agaves for another delicious meal.  We can let the kids eat the tortilla chips...if they're worthy.

Little off the beaten path Valentine's dinner. 

Bread starter was average with a garlic curry hummus that was very tasty. The filet mignon was very good as well as the mashed potatoes and grilled veggies. Pork chops were tough and a bit over cooked. 

Prices were a bit much at about $30 a plate. Good sized portions, but still too much for basic food. Food took about 45 minutes to arrive. 

This place is trying hard to be fancy. It's a tiny room with decor from A.C. Moore and IKEA. Just because you add tablecloths and linen napkins though, doesn't make it work. 

Service was five stars.

I may try it again if the lunch prices are more reasonable and if I can order take out. This place can't be done in under an hour.

Garlic Rolls YAY!!!!

Ok, I hate to say this, but I'm strictly rating this place based on their garlic rolls, but only because it's a rarity that I ever eat pizza!
