best chicken piccata ever, scrumptious desserts.....try the Jane Sunday...
and a warm and welcoming wait staff.  
I said near perfection.....cold dry sour  dough bread.  Skip it and save  the calories.

I have been going to this place and I must say the food is really good. The service in the drive up window on the others hand is not very good. This is the 2nd time they have messed my order up the first time they got it wrong I order a Santa Barbra char and they gave me a regular burger  witch I called on since I live 20 mile out of town and just today I ordered the Santa Barbra Cobb salad an sure enough they forgot the dressing. I know ordering one item is a tuff thing to take care of . But i just wanted to let you know if you go through the drive thru make sure you get the order that you ordered.

Always good. We even went on New Years Eve. The service was very good. And then you have the food which was yummy as always. 
After many visits over the years, Lorenzo's always is on my list of good Italian. 
Great house salad!

OUT OF TOWN VISITORS EXPECTED JUST A BIT MORE FROM A HIGH REVIEWED RESTAURANT!

This rating is based on there service. After we were seated, we were only given a sheet of paper for ordering rolls and never received a menu until we asked for it. 

As a party of 5, four of us ordered multiple rolls and I order the Sashimi dinner. My Sashimi dinner never came. Everyone finished there rolls and waited around and still no Sashimi dinner. When the waiter came to check on us I told him to cancel my Sashimi dinner as my party had already completed there dinner and we were ready to leave and to bring us the check.

The waiter comes back with the Sashimi dinner and states that the Sashimi dinner was quickly made for me and applied a discount on the check. That discount was about 4 bucks off the $14 dollar dinner WOW. 4 bucks really? I didnt want to make a scene and I did not decline the Sashimi dinner as I should of had and  I did leave tip as I should'nt have. I took the dinner to go as I just wanted to get out of there.  

SERVICE IS HORRIBLE WHICH RUINED THE EXPERIENCE. When running a business its all about the customer service and the food. You cant have one or the other, they come in hand in hand.  

If your wondering how the Sashimi dinner was,  all I have to say is,"You cant complain.... its Reno"

AWESOME. Chicken patty was enveloped in a flaky, yummy, golden crust with perfectly seasoned and tender chicken inside. The jerk pork was tender, flavorful (I wanted mind a bit more fat), the sweet plantains and cabbage were very tasty sidekicks. Don't be a jerk, go here and get some jerk!!!!!

COVID19 Update: I love love love Five Points and am so grateful to their entire team for their tireless work during this pandemic. Prior to these crazy times, 5 Points has always been a favorite and I can't think of a better reason to update my review that was originally written in 2015. Take out during Covid has been tricky for me since I personally prefer the dine-in experience. Food isn't always the same when it's ordered for takeout or delivery (it can get soggy, cold, etc) but that is not the case here! The 5 Points pancake is my all time favorite pancake. I always add walnuts and banana. It's simple and cooked to perfection. It didn't lose any of it's texture or flavor even in a takeout box. They have kept their regular menu available for takeout, which is amazing! And they have a tons of grocery items and fresh produce that they either grow on their  farm or source from local purveyors. I love their attention to detail from the food they make to the products they source. So, the main points of this update are to highlight what they are up to as this pandemic continues:
1. Order online! It's super easy and the most efficient way to get your order in. You can order brunch and groceries at the same time! 
2. Curbside Pickup and delivery available as well. Curbside pick up is seamless. You order online, call when you arrive and they come to you! Totally contactless.
3. Grocery/Pantry/Wine and self care items available via their online marketplace as well!

They are sticking to takeout and delivery only for the time being And post updates on Instagram regularly!

19 Degrees has changed a lot in the past few months.
To begin with, they are now open later:
11pm Mon-Thurs
Midnight Fri & Sat
10pm Sun
And, most importantly, they now sell BEER! This is a blessing in the South of South neighborhood, which used to be a verified "beer desert." They offer six packs, 12 packs, and single 24-oz bottles to go.
Over the winter, they've fully remodeled the place. Their Facebook page states that they now offer delivery, have outdoor seating, and are dog-friendly, but I can't personally verify any of those claims.
They sell sandwiches, wraps, sushi, fresh baked goods, La Colombe coffee, and fresh smoothies.
Just about the only thing that hasn't changed about 19 Degrees Cafe is the genuine "Mom & Pop" feel of the place. It's run by a family of generous, caring, friendly, and hard-working people who aim to please every customer and give back to their community.
This is the type of refreshing neighborhood spot where they get to know you by name, and if you're short a few cents on your purchase, they'll trust you to pay them back next time. Don't take advantage! This small-town style of generosity is hard to find in the city, and it doesn't always last!
19 Degrees Cafe is a diamond in the rough. Let's return their spirit of kindness with appreciation and frequent business.

From the moment you walk into this place they make you feel as if you are an intruder.  No "How are you this evening?" or "Nice to have you with us.". Arrogant, curt and obnoxious.  Both the host and waiter acted as if they were doing us a favor by serving us.  A great combination to really piss you off.  The food is very good here however.  But it is no better than many other great Italian restaurants in South Philly.  

Don't waste your time unless you don't mind serious attitude!

Diner experience.  DO NOT WATSE YOUR TIME! 

I'm unsure how this restaurant is still in business.  My wife and I chose this restaurant due to its location and we love Italian cuisine and ambiance.  The decor and service were nothing like we expected.  I'm in utter shock that this restaurant shares the same location as some of the prime eating destinations in Philadelphia.  This was a cheap diner experience except that it cost well over $100 due to over- charging for low-income grade drinks and food.  

Shockingly, the staff didn't remove the regular specials and just inserted the restaurant week menu over.  The regular special was a $25 prix fixe 3 course meal that was almost identical to the restaurant week menu except for offering caeser salad, lobster ravioli, and a dessert but $10 cheaper.  I could have had my same meal minus dessert for ten dollars less if it wasn't restaurant week.  Disgrace to the city.

If you want box pasta (100% not made in house as suggested by owner) for premium prices, this is the spot. How about bad bar drinks in water glasses for the same price as a martini at capital grille? I will never return here and I recommend for you to save your money or go to another restaurant to actually get your money's worth.  There are so many amazing selections in the same vicinity that you will get premium service, drinks, and atmosphere for around the same price.

If I were to rate this restaurant on a national scale,  I may give it 4.5 stars; however, for a hotel restaurant it met and exceeded every single expectation I had. I have had the pleasure of eating here 3 years in a row and would not hesitate to eat here again. The food is superb, the service outstanding, and it's a memorable dining experience. A solid choice for sure.....
We enjoyed our meal. Well prepared Korean dishes. Family-run, friendly atmosphere. (Can accommodate about 40 dinners. Seems popular. We called ahead to reserve.)

Warm service and really good food (quality and flavor) clean restaurant with interesting decor, invites to a good lunch in couples or with friends. Again, service was on spot, very attentive and caring. If I ever come back to New Orleans, I would definitely come back to this restaurant. Give it a try! :)

This place was fantastic!

Three of us showed up around 10:30 on a Saturday. We were seated in about 30 minutes and got a look at the deep, creative, amazing menu.

Then we met Alex (our server). In a place like this I had a feeling trusting the server would go well. It did. 

I said vodka and refreshing, he said apricot and pineapple? I said yes. I don't know what it was but I loved it and my companion said it was the best drink she'd ever had and ordered one. The third member of our party was also pleased with her choice. Second round was similar: two repeats and another challenge for Alex: creamy, dessert-like. "Have you ever had a Brandy Alexander?" I hadn't. It was spot on. 

We also ordered sliders and a cheese tray, but it was the drinks and service that were really outstanding!

review about korean food from a korean person

sigh. i had high hope for this place. i crave korean food on the daily so i've been looking for a go to place in philly... unfortunately still looking.
i came here for a quick to go meal; ordered my custom bibimbap and watched at my table waiting for the magic to happen.
as i was watching my meal being made, movement was slow. there was 1-2 people working to get everyone's orders done and then about 2-3 people standing around just staring at me and other customers in the store. i made eye contact with one of the workers to nudge her to say, "why not help?" but no movement.

i finally got bibimbap after about 10 minutes, which is weird because all the ingredients are already made and ready to go, all they have to do is place it in the bowl. 

the bibimbap was sooo mediocre i wish i went behind the counter and made it myself. and for $14... i wish it was better. spicy chicken came out in huge chunks, egg was so stale and old, mushrooms & bok choy were OK but overall, it was not satisfying.

I wish I could give this place a great review, I was really looking forward to going, I've been following on social media for a while and have gone to the location in NY, so when I had family visiting from out of town I thought it'd be the perfect time. We went on a Saturday night group of 3 women, the ambiance and decoration is very pretty, great for pictures, we waited about 20 minutes and had drinks while waiting. Once we were taken to our table we waited about 20 more minutes to order drinks, was about 20 minutes for a pitcher of mojitos, once we got our drinks we asked for water, utensils and placed an order for appetizers, while waiting we received other tables orders, 3 times, about 30 minutes later we got our appetizers, however did not get the water or utensils. The appetizer brought out to me was not what I'd ordered and when I brought it up to the waitress she became argumentative then explained that what I'd ordered the kitchen was out of (still no water or utensils) I noticed the other tables near us having similar issues with the service and food as well, and quite honestly was tired of waiting for water, I went to the front and explained to a gentleman that said he was the manager what was going on, he immediately brought us out the water we'd requested and utensils, shortly after our food came out. I ordered the puerquito (slow roasted pork sweet plantains and rice and peas) which I thought was just ok, it wasn't as flavorful as I'd expected, my sister and cousin had the cazuela de marisco which they said was good but the sauce was sweeter than they liked. When the bill came out the appetizer that was sent to me incorrectly was still on there as well as %18 gratuity (even thought the menu says parties of 5 or more will include %18 gratuity) so we had to request that fixed. I've heard great things about the club part, I myself haven't been, after the experience that night left pretty disappointed with the restaurant but more so with the service. I hope Mamajuana's work on providing better service because this location is absolutely beautiful.
Service was terrible, my son almost slipped and fell on there greasy floors, and it's well overpriced. Would have been happier going ti applebees. Will not go back
Don't know what all the bad reviews are about. Very good food, very good service.  Little bit heavy on olive oil with the calamari and chicken with rabe and roasted peppers.  PS-parking was ample.

Always good, if you like pizza try the XL Brooklyn.
Fast delivery. Also, try the app for coupons.

I think I was really supposed to like this restaurant. I didn't. 

I actually had a relatively bad experience overall. The space is super cool and made me feel like I was in episode of Gossip Girl. The cocktail list is pretty cool. You could convince me to come back for drinks I think. 

It could have just been a really off night. 

Our server was not happy to be there at all. The service time was painfully slow. The cocktail took longer to come out then our first sushi roll. The fish in the sushi dinner tasted like it possibly got really dried out. They were all rubbery. Maybe they sat an expo counter too long. Maybe it wasn't great cuts of fish. Who knows. We waited for our bill for 27 minutes. Literally sitting there with empty plates and drinks in front of the whole time. It was odd. And it was uncomfy.  Beyond that we were so close to a table next to us that I could smell the gentleman's BO. 


The Kamikaze Roll is what intrigued me the most to go here, and it was actually the most redeeming part of the meal. It was super spicy, and super exciting tasting. The prices are impressively low. The sushi dinner comes with a house salad and miso soup and comes out to under $25.
Jasmine makes the best horchata I have ever had! Grew up in Chicago and work in downtown Joliet, and hers is the best!
Enjoyable wait staff, food not as good. Chicken kabob only thing I could taste  'grilled burnt'. Mussels, hhhhmmm, not-so-fresh. Sorry, left hungry; NOW WHERE DO I GOT AFTER $57 bill???

Let's just get this out there. We came here for the table side banana foster that they have. But our meal was great as well. That, combined with the fact that there was no wait when we were here on a Sunday night was why I am glad we made the decision to eat here. We were seated immediately at a nice table in the middle of the restaurant. We had a good view of everything from there. The kids got crayons and kid's menus.

I started with the gumbo and had another appetizer, the crab claws, for my meal. The gumbo was good, a bit salty and clammy for my taste, but good nonetheless. The crab claws were perfect! I loved that the work was already done for you and that all you had to do was bite at the meat. They were a bit smaller than I expected individually, but you got a decent amount of them. And lastly, the banana foster was definitely a show. All the tables around us were watching and yes, it was delicious!

We decided to come here over Hash A Go Go in Reno. Wait for a group of 8 was about 15/20 mins on a Sunday, not bad!

I tried their belgian waffle because it looked really pretty on Yelp! I would have enjoyed it a little more if they didn't already drown it in syrup. I'm not an extreme sugar fanatic, so I couldn't finish my waffle. It was WAYYYY too sweet for me. Then I asked my friend for some toast to wash out the sweetness, and they upcharged her for the unlimited toast that was suppose to come with her meal. They said it was because she shared her toast, but she was already sharing a plate! Maybe I shouldn't have added the bananas on top and got a plain waffle instead. I couldn't even finish my $14 waffle. Sadface. Oh well, at least you know that the servers are pretty attentive because they noticed even that! Other than that minor turn off, I would say the service here was pretty swell though. 

Overall, good place for breakfast, but not the "best" in my books.

4.5 Stars. Could not tell from the outside but this place is huge. We had a group of 14 and were taken through what felt like a maze until we got to our private room. Very classy place, The main dining room looked very nice, intimate, dimly lit. Our room was nicely decorated away from the main room as this was a boisterous bachelor party. The service was impeccable, we had an excellent team serving us and they were very accommodating. We asked if they could pipe in some musics and right away we heard Sinatra crooning in the background. The drinks were spot on hand crafted fair. Extensive wine list as well.
Our waiter recommended we get a few appetizer samplers as we had such a large group and that was a great idea as we all had a little taste of several items before the main course. 
The food was excellent. I had the duck which is one of their specialities and it was damn good and surprising the portion size was more than I expected. The lamb, fish, steak and all the rest were tasty.
As I said this was 14 guys for a bachelor party and we were loud and rowdy and we never had one complaint to keep it down, our servers seemed to think we were very amusing as well.
This is a great spot, I highly recommend it.

Good pizza just a shade behind the original in Trenton (which is the standard that all pizza should be compared). Crust is missing a little something. But still really good food and the service is incredibly friendly. Great atmosphere too.
Delicious, high-quality, great concept! So nice to have an alternative take away lunch option besides Robert's (which is awful).

Menu has changed for the worse. It looks like a move by corporate to make all locations consistent but a once kid friendly go to restaurant pulled everything that made you want to go there away. Variety has been sacrificed for pricing, not sure If it's because of the new tap house across the street, but won't be the "go to" anymore.

I came here once maybe three months ago and it was such a bummer. There were so many good reviews so it stung that much more. They had no air conditioning and it was a sauna inside. We came in, paid, then sat and waited. That was when the red flags started popping up. The restaurant has people bus their own tables but there's no actual cleaning of the tables meaning no disinfectant, no wiping down, nothing to keep things hygienic even as a pretext. Next I saw the stand mixer which is terrifying for anyplace that makes biscuits because a biscuit cannot be made with a mixer. A mixer will overmix the dough and create a tough biscuit. I ordered the biscuit with fried chicken and mushroom gravy and the mushroom gravy was good but everything else was a disappointment. The biscuit was rubbery and had a texture like it was microwaved. The fried chicken had the breading coming off and way mediocre. It was an overpriced disappointment.

This place is so overrated. We ordered crabs, they didn't have any so we tried Dungeness crab, it tasted like they was frozen in salt water for a long time. The meat was dry, briny, and so salty that I had to ask for some lemon juice to eat with. On top of that we pay 22$ just for 2 legs.
Next thing was boiled shrimps. They looked so old, dry and tasted plain like they just got boiled again. We should've went to Hooter, their boiled shrimps are much better than that
Overall, I've never tasted any re cooked seafood that worst than that. The only thing this place worth one star is because the waitress was friendly. But I wouldn't come back ever again

Absolutely beautiful place.. decor is amazing, employees were sweet... However, housekeeping was TERRIBLE.. We booked three days... The second day was a complete nightmare.. We left for the day, when we turned tired and sweaty our room had not been cleaned.. Beds unmade , no clean towels.. We complained for hours and NO ONE CAME .. THEY Finally showed up at 8 o'clock at night to give us clean towels and clean our room...

The raw oysters were great. The jumbalaya was not very good. Too much rice and not enough meat. The sausage in it wasn't very good either. The atmosphere is fun. if you want to come in and have some drinks and oysters its great. get your jimbalaya elsewhere.

This has been bookmarked on my Yelp for a long time and finally I got the chance to check Mama out! It was very crowded durimg lunch time, which I guess is a good sign of great restaurant. Surprisingly, the staff is very efficient and they prepared the order super fast so I dis not feel I was waiting for long. I asked about its signature dish and was suggested to try Samatha's Platter because it has pretty much everything -cucumber, tomatoes,eggplant, pattie, pita bread and falafals. They really give you a big portion. I walked out of the place super full. The reason I gave 4 stars is because they only accept cash! Although there is an ATM inside the restaurant, I wish they accept cards which bring more convenience to the customers.

We have tried Ruth Chris in a lot of different cities. This particular location went above and beyond to make my husband's birthday extra special. I thank the waitstaff and management, kindly. The filet and lobster mac did not disappoint. Give this location a go, if you're a local or visiting. Either way, you will be welcomed.

Food is good but not amazing. The interior needs cleaned up some more, good for a corner bar tho.  The worst part is the lack of management or courteous patrons on weekend late nights. I live on Ann st and can here these fools screaming and yelling outside the bar at 2 am like they are in Old City.  This is a neighborhood, not a club scene. Not sure why management (owners) have a DJ at such a small place and highly doubt that have the permit to do so.  Hopefully they clean their shit up soon.

Came her to celebrate a friend's 50th birthday! I cannot say enough words on how wonderful the experience was! From the bottomless Rose to the deviled eggs to the Josephine Benedict's to the sumptuous desserts! Everything was delicious. The service was excellent and to top it off, the musicians that came to the table to serenade our birthday girl! Definitely a meal to remember! I will Definitely return for future trips to Nola!

The food was amazing! Enjoyed having a Döner sandwich just like in Germany. Staff was friendly and helpful. Also the german beer selection is big. I recommend eating here!
P.S. prices are affordable as well ;)
Not a big sandwich eater, but love the fact that I can make my own. House made chips are outstanding!
Tucked away on a side street, this was a DELICIOUS surprise!  Excellent food and service in a fun and quirky place!

Stopped by yesterday.  Big -Al sub was great, had two lunches out of it.  Can't wait to try sausage.  Cannoli are great, as we're the anisette toast cookies and the Sicilian sesame cookies.  Can't wait to try fresh mozzarella and the artichoke salad.  It was pouring out and the man was so nice by bringing my bags to my car because I had a walker and it takes time to fold it up and get into the car.  And he smiled all the time.  As Arnold says "ill be back".

I've lived in spring hill my whole life and always heard great things about Donnelly's. Finally tried "the beast" and my god instant heaven. I've said goodbye to those corporate sandwich places and head straight to Donnelly's. The owner is a really nice guy as well always up for conversation. I would suggest this deli to anyone!

Food was bland. Very bland. My boyfriend ordered a mojito and the training waitress asked for both of our IDs. I thought it was strange but no bid deal. Five minutes later, we received two mojito drinks. We only wanted one.. So that was annoying. Also, I got the fried catfish and that was just okay. Although, the fish seemed to be very very white like cod white and the "catfish" did not have the texture of one. I asked the waiter and he said it was catfish. I still don't believe him. I have never seen a catfish filet as white as cod before. 

Food and service was just okay. I don't see myself coming back.

This place was recommended by 3 different people and even a few locals via blogs so I came right here from the airport to get breakfast. 

Pro's:
My food came out fast. 
The bathrooms were clean. 
Prices are reasonable. 

Con's:
Nothing was seasoned. NOTHING!
The server mentioned a breakfast buffet to the couple next to me after I ordered and I was a little upset she didn't mention it to me. Then I heard them complain about how few options there were and how awful the food was and I was glad it wasn't just me and that I didn't get the buffet. 

This place is downtown so parking is gonna cost more than your meal. Plan to do other things since you're paying a second mortgage to park (it's cheaper to park in NYC than Nashville...let that sink in). 

I really don't see the hype. Could I have ordered the wrong thing?  Could the chef have had an off day? Maybe the other reviewers just like really bland food?  Let's pretend all of that was true. Who doesn't put at least salt and pepper in their eggs?  

Do yourself a favour and skip this place. With so many other options, it's silly to make this mistake.
Quick and easy slices at the ready. Helps a drunk stomach for sure.

Horrible experience!  Sushi rice was mushy.  Japanese restaurant that can't make rice doesn't deserve to stay in business.  Ordered miso soup which was a bowl of salty water with no flavor.  We told the server that the soup was salty and terrible so they remade the soup for us.  New soup was much better than the original but still salty and inedible.  All you can eat menu also includes an all you can eat salad bar...which consisted of a whole four items- edamame, pickles cucumber, coleslaw like salad and an ambrosia like salad with zucchini...really?  Too many of the sushi rolls came with cream cheese-which we didn't order.  Ordered the tempura appetizer for my kids which consisted of a few pieces of sweet potato and potato and carrot. - and about a tablespoon of tempura sauce.
The quality of the fish in the sushi was good and the sushi was displayed nicely but it couldn't overcome the mushy rice.
The restaurant was crowded so perhaps the other patrons liked the food- our party of five all thought it was terrible.  Fuki Sushi in Vacaville and Davis are much better.  We were hoping for a good alternative and were highly disappointed.  I had heard from a friend that their other restaurant with sushi and Korean Food was good so we thought we would give Ijji a try but after this terrible experience we won't dare give their other restaurant a try.
My favorite taco spot great food  quick in & out service conveniently located in the heart of center city . Be sure to try "The Phat Pig " my favorite

So I have tried many ramen places, and with this being listed as the top 21 ramen places in the nation, according to an article I read, I was disappointed. I ordered the Summer Miso Ramen with BBQ pork and the soft egg. The egg was not my typical ramen egg, but more like something I can boil at home. The BBQ pork was delicious but let's get to the main part, the actual ramen and broth. The ramen noodles I have to say were really good. It's texture and taste was perfect! On the other hand, the broth was the worse thing I ever tasted. The miso broth did not have the slightest taste of miso. It tasted like Tom yum soup or even a basic sweet and sour soup. I was so disappointed because I always get the miso ramen at every ramen place I go to, so I have a lot to compare to. 

The house bowl's broth tasted pretty good, but anything tasted better than the miso broth. 

We order the fries too and they were pretty good. The pies will be judged later as we were too stuff to eat them but read good reviews on them. 

In all, I couldn't believe how disappointed I was to order miso ramen but not taste miso whatsoever.
I love this place, it's very small so plan ahead if you want to sit down during busy hours, but everyone is always lovely and the food is great. Highly recommend supporting this local small business!

I can't decide which is best - the super friendly owner of the restaurant or being delighted that Chuy cooked exactly what I wanted even though it wasn't on the menu or the incredible deliciousness of my dish. I brought a visitor from Dallas to Chuy's and we were both delighted! 
I can't wait to go back to my favorite mid-town Mexican food place! Thank you Chuy!

An excellent start followed by a mediocre ending gives us this 3 star rating.

It's been years since we have been here and I did like modernized sleek feel the place had now. We felt a little underdressed so maybe I would suggest slacks if you go. The drink menu looked nice for cocktails though we did not sample this time.

We started off with the beef tartare toast and the shrimp cocktail. The shrimp was fresh and good sized, though the sauce was not what we would have expected. The beef tartare on toast allowed the beef heats to excel, not over dosing you with horseradish. Excellent portion excellent dish.

The gnocchi was phenomenal, star of the dinner. Small portion size, but almost like au gratin potatoes in gnocchi form. Fantastic. You could not make a dinner out of the size if you were one person.

Finally we had the ny strip and the halibut for dinner. Everything was nicely cooked and seasoned, but it was just a good steak and a good piece of fish, not worth the price for sure.

Very expensive, one of the more expensive meals I have ever had in the city and not worth that price. May be next time, drinks and some gnocchi

First and foremost, I have to compliment BJs for having purse hooks under the bar...love this! Every bar should have purse hooks. Thank you BJs, thank you for being thoughtful enough to have purse hooks. A truly considerate gesture. Hooray for the purse hook!

We always sit at the bar, not only for the purse hooks, but also for their great bartenders. Dara and Chad are definitely the best: great customer service, attentive, knowledgeable and funny...they could probably teach a class on what it means to be a good bartender.

As for the food, it is yummy. My favorites are the artichoke dip, angus burger sliders, California club flatbread (love the garlic aioli), bacon cheeseburger pizza (so good with the pickles and special sauce) , cuban burger, fish tacos (crunchy, breaded fish and the oh so good avocado cream), and the delicious chicken-fried steak. 

I'm also really enjoying the new items; they are a nice addition to their tasty menu. Love the fried artichokes! Also like the stuffed mushrooms and gourmet mac-n-cheese. Mac-n-cheese with bacon, chipotle,and garlic, baked with a crispy breadcrumb top...oh, yeah!

Highly recommend.

We had a wonderful meal last night at Domenica. The restaurant was packed when we arrived without a reservation, so we ate at the bar.  We ordered a small plate of the garganelli pasta and the cotechino pizza with anchovies added.  The pasta was delicious and the small order was a perfect portion to split alongside the pizza.  
The waitress asked if we wanted white or brown anchovies on our pizza.  Not knowing the difference, we ordered white.  The anchovies we special ordered ended up taking over the entire pizza in flavor.  Our waitress sensed we were not completely loving the pizza and kept asking if we wanted another pizza. We replied we didn't need another pizza.  She went ahead and cooked a fresh one for us anyway with less anchovies, and, this time, the brown, milder in flavor anchovies. 
The pizza was delicious and we really appreciated the attention and service the waitress provided.  We will definitely eat here again when in New Orleans.
We were looking for a place other then cracker barrel. ...and we found this place. Breakfast was great and I will definitely will be back. Service was friendly too.

'Twas the 14th of November, and all through downtown
The Oxford Exchange was preparing, for a grand event to go down.

The decorations were hung by the windows with care
In hopes that the Tampa Bay Bloggers soon would be there.

The books were nestled all snug on their shelves
And goodie bags were packed by stylish little elves.

The food was all prepped and the drinks nice and steamy
The whole atmosphere was so festive and dreamy.

At the stroke of 6:30, there arose such a chatter
The doors opened up and welcomed the pitter patter,

Of little blogger feet all sparkly and bright
All ready for an evening of holiday delight!

They mingled, and greeted each other with glee
They ate, and drank, and were definitely merry.

For two glorious hours they took in the sights
They shopped, and they toured; it was a fabulous night!

They feasted on butternut soup and cheesy figs
Nibbled on fancy chocolate, and took coffee and tea swigs.

Two lovely ladies spoke all about their creations
Their family's hand made candles are cause for celebration!

The night ventured on; the bloggers perused around the shoppe
While others learned all about the commerce club spaces atop.

What makes the Oxford so special is it's uniqueness and style,
It's beauty and charm will make you want to stay a while.

With floors of reclaimed wood and a retractable ceiling
And lots of comfy furniture to give guests a warm and cozy feeling.

The shoppe is jam packed with trinkets oh so sweet
It's the perfect place to holiday shop...and maybe by yourself a treat!

The lights, how they twinkled!
The cookbooks stood neatly!
The candles' aroma swirled around
And made the room smell so sweetly!

As the evening wound down, and the bloggers grew tired,
They reminisced about all the fun that had transpired.

They wrapped up the night, and expressed grateful words,
And were shocked at the news they had just overheard!

Not only did they leave with a bag full of loot,
But a gift for our readers! An offer none of us could refute!

Visit the Oxford Exchange ASAP. You will fall in love. I promise!

The shows at helium have always been very entertaining, however I think the building itself could use some work. 
When compared to Punchline, I think helium comes up a little short. I went to a show last night and the seating situation was totally awkward. My date was sitting behind me off to an angle so it did not make for the best date night. I was uncomfortably close with a stranger and it was a bit weird. 
There is a two drink minimum here, but I saw poeple fulfilling this obligation with bottles of water, so it shouldn't be an issue for anyone. 
The food is typical bar appetizer types. We ordered cheesesteak eggrolls and they were fine. 
It pays to sign up for their promotions. A few times on holiday weekends we have gotten free tickets to shows, as they were trying to fill up the venue. 
Helium is a fun night out but could stand to be a little less cramped and dingy!

These guys are masters of marketing. The storefront is incredibly appealing. The menu is very well composed and easy to come to terms with. (Yes, I know it's barbecue, but you wouldn't believe how long some of their competitors get...)

The television is huge and well placed. You'll love it if you're out for drinks and want to catch your favourite team.

I'm not sure if the service was meant to be pooled - my gut says no - but my experience was that if one waiter had something else going on, someone else stepped in. This was an unexpected bonus in this setting. A table not far from mine was occupied by one of the pickiest eaters I've seen. The waiters should have earnt a commendation for not tossing something accidentally. So service gets very high marks for juggling this table with all of the others and not letting any of us suffer.

The prices are a little on the high side for barbecue, but I would not mark it down for value to cost. I went for dinner and paid about as much as some of my pricier lunches.

I ordered the pulled pork, which is my go to for barbecue until I trust a place. That said, the local favourite seems to be tri tip, which you might want to go for. The sauce was interesting. It had sweet notes to it and just the right amount of smoke. I felt that the meat itself was a little under on smoke, but that sauce helped clear that problem right up. The bun lost structural integrity with alarming speed. I can never decide if I like that or no. I suspect a potato based or sourdough bread with a little more spine would have been a better compliment than a straight up white.

This brings me to my carrot cake and one of my current culinary peeves. 

The fries are evil. Ate all of those little bastards.

Frost to the edges if it's a cupcake and down the bloody sides if it's a proper slice. If you want to get on the trendy frosting bandwagon, the entire cake better be gone within a day or before it gets dry. That said, the cake itself was quite nice in terms of complexity. This really was closer to spice cake than carrot, so I found it worth its price. The cream cheese frosting was spineless, more suited to Martha Stewart than a barbecue joint.

In all, this was a very pleasant meal, and I'd say you probably can't go wrong here. It was only $18.29 for my dinner.
Definitely try this place if your near magazine street in New Orleans. The crawfish quesadilla was great.

Drove past this little restaurant and figured we would stop in since they were new. We were impressed as soon as we walked in the door. It was a small little restaurant with cute decorations and a very warm and welcoming atmosphere. We were seated immediately and the waitress came over to greet us. I read over the menu. It stated that they are cash only. The chef does not want to make changes to anything on the menu. (Totally fine with us!) There are six tables. Reservations are not accepted and it is first come first serve. There was plenty to choose from on the menu from appetizers to salads to entrées. We decided to get a flat bread and chicken parm. The flatbread was the best flatbread I had ever tasted. The crust was so crispy and the arugula, tomato, and shaved the parmigiano were fresh and delicious. I will go back just for this 10 times over! I want to try each one on the menu. Next came our  chicken Parmesan. There was enough food for two. The sauce was to die for! The sauce was 100% homemade by the chef. It was so good I wanted to lick the plate! The owner Luigi came over and greeted us and introduced himself he was very nice.  I love that the owner made a connection with us!!He runs the establishment with two of his family members. We were made to feel welcomed from start to finish. I can't wait to go back! I feel sure word of mouth will get around about this restaurant so in the future I expect there will be some wait  but it will be worth it
Not bad. Good food. Try it. Yelp hates short reviews so i have to add this sentence. I need to add another sentence.
Absolutely epic! Amazing fried chicken and sides. Probably the best that I've had anywhere. Exceeds the hype by miles.

We sat and the bar, and Fred immediately greeted us. He asked if it was our first time dining here, and in fact it was. He asked a couple of quick questions about what kind of food and drinks we usually like. He completely tailored our drinks, appetizers, and entrees to our personal tastes. The drink was unlike anything I had tried before. Tasty, without holding back on the liquor. Our food consisted of items we would never usually order myself. It was all delicious. Fred's service was timely, while still remaining funny and personable. The food was great, but Fred really sold me on the entire experience. Will absolutely be back to ask for him!

Hot Chicken is a Nashville staple and until this trip I had never tried the delicacy. So what is it? If you've ever been to Popeye's and they ask you if you want spicy or regular, take that and make a few different incredible flavors. You can get the mildest (basically just fried chicken) or you can get it "clucking" hot. My mom and I both got Hot! to feel the heat but not the "Shut the Cluck Up!" flavor because that seemed too extreme for our first time. We also had the pimento mac & cheese that was creamy and incredibly cheesy. Pro Tip: Order online before you go, you can pick it up at the counter and eat it on the porch instead of waiting in line! We wish we had known this.

Magical, beautiful, well located and historical hotel. Check in was exactly on time (on the minute), which is always nice. Our room was a bit dated- a torn curtain here, a ripped bed skirt there but it was spacious and the bathroom was large and very clean. I could see where if you were picky (which we aren't), you could find a lot "wrong" with the rooms. Comfortable beds, friendly staff, and seriously the pb&j happy hour was so super fun. Pretty good location too. I'm not sure that I would stay here again but that's only because I love checking out different hotels every time I'm in Nola.
Literally the worst experiences of my life. Went there twice, got turned away for my REAL ID. Worst establishment in Philly.

The church-to-brewery conversion is really unique and cool. Their beers take on names with a tie in to the Catholic Church -- We had the Confessional IPA and Pew Buster. So punny! The beers were good. We ordered food as well, the poutine and mahi mahi tacos, but we were not impressed. The tacos lacked flavor and the tortillas easily fell apart from the moisture. If I come back, I'll be coming for the beer and scenery but not the food.

My favorite pizza place in Maryland has brought a franchise to Tampa which I visit often.

Ledo Pizza is a rectangular thin crust pizza with a great sauce.Their sauce is sweeter than most places.

Pizza is served on their traditional rectangular cafeteria type trays

Can't wait to get back to Tampa area and enjoy lidos again

When the store manager is not there, this place falls apart. I order a meal, the cashier reads it back. My food comes out, and it's wrong. Every time I go here they cannot seem to get an order correct. And, to make it even worse, they over charged me because she entered the order wrong. 
Past visits are typical of this experience. At least once in a while it would be nice to get an apology. Once I had the girl argue with me telling me I ordered it wrong. Kinda hard to order wrong when you tell them a combo number.
And, again only when the manager is not there, we watch the workers hand out free food and drinks to their friends.
This place should be shut down!

My aunt and uncle had many dates here years ago. In 2013, after my uncle died, we had the post funeral dinner for him here. It was easy to see why they loved it so much when they were young, and I want to come here every time I come back to St. Louis.

Very disappointed in the customer service skills here. Long story short, one entree for our party of eleven came so late the rest of us were done eating; the server said "don't worry about it" - we thought meaning it would be comped but it was on the bill. Music so loud you couldn't hear the server's announcements or have a conversation with someone across the table and the server's response was that the manager wouldn't do anything about that. Food was average. Too many better options for me to think about returning here.

I don't normally write reviews but this place needs to shape up. They used to be great. Consistently awesome hot delicious food. Usually go thru the drive thru. Rarely eat inside so I can't speak to the inside service. The few times we did eat inside the service was slow but the food was good. Lately, the quality of the food is poor. They messed up my wife and my order on several recent trips there. On top of that, the food thru the drive thru was barely even warm, suggesting that it was not made to order but sat there waiting for someone to order it. If I want food that sits already cooked in a draw till someone orders it, I'll just go to McDonald's.

The side order of onion rings was burnt (that was the only part of the meal that was actually hot) and there was only 4 puny little onion rings in the entire order! 

I don't know if their issues are because of some recent management change or something but they really need to shake things up (no pun intended) and get back on track.
One of my fav Jamaican restaurants in philly! The oxtail is amazing and they serve the best rum punch.  This is my go to spot for authentic jamaican food in a lively environment.  S/o to the owners!

I've had enough of this place.  It's turned into the Coffee XChange with better furniture.  What happened to Ike's circa 2005?  Wasn't the coffee a lot better then?  The staff less obnoxious?  The venue less strip mall-y?

One of the worst Indian food experiences I've had in a while. We used to love coming to Aman's but their quality has gone down. We were seated at 6:05 and did not get any water or anything until 6:19. The restaurant was also half empty so it wasn't like they were super busy or anything. We then got to order our food at 6:24 and by 7:15, still hadn't gotten the food. I ordered the salted laasi which ended up smelling putrid as if it had been made with spoiled milk or yogurt.
Very good chicken kebab with 2 falafel, special order...very good and reasonable. Fresh pita &  good humus. Wish they'd upgrade their chopped salad but I have a thing against iceberg lettuce

I went here last Saturday and it was nice. I didn't have to wait long for a table or anything. The worst part was the waitress that served us dinner. It took her some time before returning to the table and providing our drinks. When she did, we asked for two waters where she only provided one. Dinner went well and at the end of the night to pay, we had to wait 40 mins to pay! We sat at the table for thirty mins then went to the front and waited and additional 10-30 mins. Turns out the place charged the credit card twice then a manager had to come redo it and all he could offer was his apology. We wanted to pay with a gift card but was told that it wasn't possible. After the card. Wing charged twice and waiting a very long time for a manager, he offered an apology and fixed it. Absolutely ridiculous! I never had such poor service here before and I don't think I'll be returning. I'll go spend my money in Clearwater before returning with this horrible service and literally 10 people just standing at the front while one person made an attempt to assist us.

Loved my holiday order this year. My meat lovers pizza came pipping hot with an amazing ratio of toppings, a perfect crust, perfectly flavored. Came super quickly too. The chicken sandwich and burger were some of the better ones I've had in a while from a pizza joint, and the fries were good. I look forward to eating here again soon. It kept me full for a few days of leftovers two, almost better then next morning!

The food is always fresh and the staff is consistently polite. Even if it's 5 minutes before close, they always seem so positive. A great place to have lunch or dinner if you are feeling indecisive or want something homey/healthy. Recommend the chicken or turkey with mashed potatoes and steamed veggies.

These guys are the best, always friendly (they remember the frequent visitors) and the food is soo great without the fussiness of the restaurant.  Excellent for a good quality meal to go.

The market is insane and has just about everything in international foods you can ask for.  Their hummus is the best in the city I always get extra and pita to go. A must try is their garlic paste.  intense garlicy awesomeness!

no highchairs for small kids (wish they would get them!)
love popeyes but I found this in my lemonade when I went to pour it out and recycle the bottle. :-)

(18 Dec 2015)

My wife raved about a place called Lenny's when we first met. When we travelled to USA it was our first stop, and man was it goooood! 

Typical diner setup, boothed seats and bottomless coffee. The family owned restaurant is known for their breakfast, and that's what we came to get. I ordered dacon (duck bacon) with scrambled egg, hash brown and home fries. The wife got deep fried chicken hollandaise on a waffle with a biscuit. Both meals were filling, delish and left us satisfied. 

I just love the decor, baseball bats on the walls and picture frames of the family that owns the diner. 

It's a popular spot and I can see why.

I'm not the world's biggest barbecue fan, but when it's done right, I'll love it. In short, I loved Edley's. I ordered the chicken sandwich with macaroni and cheese and bean salad. Even sauceless, that was one of the best chicken sandwiches I've ever tasted! Hot BBQ damn.

Recently, a friend and I planned a brunch for another friend who was about to get married. Our requirements were pretty straightforward: an at-least-halfway-cute space for a group of about 20, a menu that could accommodate vegetarians as well as Atkins followers, and booze, preferably available in a variety of tasty cocktails. 

We called approximately 1.7 billion restaurants serving brunch in Center City, and got a lot of "Sure, but we'll have to...seat you in 4 different rooms/charge everyone a minimum/do it on this other random date/etc." I understand why restaurants place such restrictions, but we got none of that from Devil's Alley - they were super accommodating, friendly and easy to deal with. 

We hosted the brunch in the back of their upstairs area, which is nice and open and has a fire pit, and we had our own server who made sure everything ran relatively smoothly. The Bloody Marys and French toast flowed, and everyone was happy.
I eat here at LEAST once a week. Sometimes twice a week. No joke, I'm pretty much living off of the gumbo as my only source of nutrients these days. I don't know what I'm going to do without Bro's.
Great food, great atmosphere, and this place looks a lot more put together than you would expect from your average Thai place. Delicious.

The food was very tasty and filling.  My gripe is more with the app/process for online ordering.  After placing an order, information is displayed indicating you will be informed when the order is ready.  We were waiting outside, with the app indicating estimate of when order would be ready.  I decided to go inside to check and my order was just sitting on the counter.  No information was ever received indicating the order was ready to be picked up.

I rarely visit Reading Terminal these days, but had to stop in today because I was in the area and I had a sweet tooth. Where else can I get a great Cannoli this side of South street? Termini Bros was just the answer. I got a cannoli, tiramisu, and chocolate cake. The desserts are pretty, let's start there. The cakes are moist, light, and no one flavor is overpowering. Let's not forget the cannoli, I went with the chocolate since I'm a chocoholic and what a treat.

Hands down best burgers in St. Louis, other than Carl's,  but between the two it's a matter of style. Burger with goat cheese is my favorite, but havent had the same burger ever since the options are always off the charts. Build your own old fashioned or Manhattan is a cool touch. Anytime you want a burger, stacked is the place to go. I used to like Baileys Range but wont even step foot in the place after trying stacked.

Big fan of Argentinian style restaurants.  Was not impressed at all. Menu was very sparse. The empanadas tasted as though they were from frozen Costco. The fried calamari had fried onion rings in it which really wasn't that bad. I'm a huge fan of Vacio and I can honestly say that it was good. The cocktails were tiny and mostly ice. The server was friendly.  In my opinion the only real reason to go here would be for the vacio. Everything else I would pass on! I don't see myself going back.

I only reserve writing Yelp reviews for exceptionally good or terribly bad experiences. Tonight, my friends and I had an exceptionally good experience. The food was flavorful, complex and simple at the same time. The staff acted as if we grew up childhood friends, and the environment was very welcoming. Can't say enough about this spot and can't wait to visit again.

Their burger is huge, and the patty, very thick. Dark, musty atmosphere filled with antiques and old paintings.

Perfect for when I feel dark, dreary, and in need of a drink.

We originally were headed to Datz but after having been quoted a damn near 2 hour wait time we knew that wasn't going down. We stopped here because it was down the street from Datz and the Yelp reviews looked pretty good. 

You order at the counter (cafeteria style) and then grab a seat. First off let me warn you that the food here looks really good. The meat looks good and juicy and if you're hungry you'll want everything. Don't do it. Ok, maybe just a little bit.

I got tri-tip and it was delicious! We also got some okra and sweet potato casserole and both were good. The sweet potato casserole was good without being too sweet. Sometimes that's a hard balance because some places will have it tasting like diabetes with sweet potatoes on the side. The only thing I wasn't too impressed with was the pecan pie. I think it was a chocolate pecan pie and I wasn't really too into it. Everything else though...YEA!

I also loved that the ownership seemed to be really involved in the community. That would be enough to get me to go back when I'm in town.

This place is so great that my dad and I went here twice in one week! 

I highly recommend the sunchoke soup. I don't even know what a sunchoke is, but somehow they manage to make this soup sweet (but not too sweet), creamy, and light.

Other favorites are the mushroom and barley toast and the chocolate cake. So decadent even though its vegan. The atmosphere is also cool =)

Great food okay prices! Best clam chowder! Good serving on the clam strips! Our waiter (a darker skined male) was very funny and gave us a good time at the restaurant! It started raining and gave a bag for my sisters cast who didn't want to get it wet! Great food for the price

Sushi after a long time, was great! Me and my friends we're out exploring Philly and spotted this Sushi place for lunch. They had a nice outside dining at up, limited seating, but we called ahead and we had about 10 minutes walk. When we reached there, they had a table set for us under the nice tree shade outside. Me and one of my friends ordered three rolls from lunch menu with a side of salad and one of my friends ordered veggie fried rice. Everything was great! I had Philadelphia, shrimp tempura and California rolls, my friend got the Clinton rolls, Pennsylvania rolls and the Ohio rolls! The fried rice was pretty good too! 

The owner and the servers of the restaurant were very welcoming and friendly. They also served us some readbeans ice cream, which I had for the very first time. And the ice cream was complimentary. 

Just had an amazing dining experience after a long time. Very happy!

Yum!!!! I tried this place for the first time just yesterday and I was hooked. The beauty bowl is filling, delicious and absolutely fresh. I can't wait to try to salads, wraps, and toast options. Plus they have all the calories listed. I couldn't ask for a better breakfast spot!!

Went for lunch. Fairly busy. Didn't have to wait to be seated. Server was prompt with our drinks and taking our order. Ordered the tuna melt and sweet potato fries. Sandwich was served on grilled sourdough. The tuna was nicely seasoned with pepper and had chunks of celery and the right amount of cheese. The bread was buttery and perfectly toasted. I always order sweet potato fries where ever I go. Hands down these were the best fries I have had. Perfectly cooked. They were crunchy and not greasy. Not over cooked and just enough salt. It was my first time and will not be my last.

Already ranked as one of the top restaurants in philly and I totally agree. The food is delicious- don't think you can go wrong with whatever you order. They are constantly changing the menu too so you can keep going back and trying new options.  They are well known for their toast and I highly recommend you try a few, they are all great...I especially liked the pumpkin one. I also highly recommend the chicken from the entree section. The ambience is very nice and the staff is very friendly...we spent several minutes talking with the manager and the head chef too. The drinks are great as well. Highly recommend this place, I'll definitely be back. Make sure you call in or get there early as this place will get busy!

Yes so good!  So glad i found this place on yelp as we were driving towards chicago.  I was a little wary because the place felt a little rough on the outside.  But after a couple minutes of deliberating in the car, we decided we were too hungry to drive to another place..."why not!?"  After all that, I'm so glad we went inside.  Immediately took a liking to it's scribbled walls and there was something in the air to signalled to me..."oh this is going to be good!"  Po boy is what they're known for so we went for it.  

I got the wrap with pork and he got the soft bread with fried catfish....  and they were BOTH SO GOOD!  Did I mention the sides are free?! and unlimited?!?  For the sides we both got cornbread and (cheese talsdfkjslk...can't remember the name)  but cornbread was so good I finished it before the meal.  At the end even though we couldn't stuff any more food into our mouths we....went for the breaded pudding...and yes somehow we finished it all.  At the end of the day...we had to take a little lap around the parking lot before heading back to the car because of how stuffed we both were.  Papa Roux is a little out of the way but worth it!  

Word of advice....come HUNGRY!

My partner took me here recently for my birthday. It was only my second time, but both times (a year apart) were excellent. The food prices are pretty reasonable, but be ready to shell out a lot if you go for a bottle of wine, which we did both times. Each time our server recommended a lovely local red that went well with our meal from beginning to end, and we enjoyed the whole experience. 

This time around we started with the braised pork belly appetizer with potato crisps on arugula. We totally mistook the potatoes for pork belly, and were surprised by the size of the entire dish. It was way bigger and heartier than we were expecting! And so delicious! We also had the scallop trio starter. Tasty, and light. I followed that with the maple glazed duck breast and confit of thigh. The duck breast was tender and juicy and oh, so amazing. I'm salivating thinking of it now. The boy had the venison medallions. They were a bit too rare for me, but according to him, "They were AWESOME." These were accompanied by a 2009 Ojai Pinot that was super good and really complimented our entire meal. 

The meal itself was fantastic, but I have to say that something that really stood out for me, was how amazing the service of the staff was when a fellow patron collapsed on his way out the door in the middle of his meal. They helped the man up and helped him into a seat, got him water and air, and called an ambulance straight away. They were super attentive while being quiet and subtle. I'm sure the poor guy was confused and embarrassed but the restaurant employees handled it very gracefully.
Enjoyed the outdoor seating and chicken gumbo! My vegetarian girlfriend enjoyed the vegetarian gumbo and has already asked we come back again during our short stay!

I never write lunch reviews but for this place I will.  Outstanding service and food.  One of my favorite pasta dishes I've ever eaten.  I love the in interior renovations as well.   This place is excellent.

Cornflower is connected to an art supply shop. The space is open and quiet, so it's probably a good place to get some studying done. Parking is limited to street parking, so it can be tricky at times. 

I ordered a seasonal latte ($5). It came topped with whipped cream, crushed andes mints, and chocolate drizzle. The drink description made it seem like it was going to be a very minty flavor, but I didn't taste any mint at all. That was disappointing. Either they forgot to put in the syrup, or the flavor is just super faint and my taste buds just suck. 

They accept apple pay (major score for me since I never carry my wallet), and the employees are nice. They care about the quality of their espresso, and take their time to connect with customers.

A few weeks ago, I had a serious Thai craving. Per a co-workers recommendation, I tried Senae for lunch and now this native Californian (the land of abundant Asian cuisine) has a new favorite restaurant!

As a strict vegan, lunch options in Downtown Tucson are few and far between. I usually order the pad see ew (vegan style since they cook with fish sauce) with tofu ad veggies or the vegan pad thai. Very authentic Thai with fresh ingredients. Service is always super friendly and fast even during the busy lunch hour. I'm always satisfied. Can't wait to try more items.

Highly recommended!
A small place with friendly and helpful service, and top quality sushi. Definitely coming back.
The drive thru line is efficient.  I like the Mcgriddles.  They have the typical McDonald's  food and a lot lay area for children.

Look at me, venturing out to the 'burbs again. I went to Fuji a couple of days ago with my current crush and her BFF. The restaurant is tucked away in a strip mall but you forget about the locale as soon as you're seated and your wine bottle(s) uncorked. It's a BYOB and I'm not sure if I should be proud or embarrassed to state that the three of us went through three bottles of wine and one of sake that night. We started off with edamame (I made an exception to my "no green food" rule and was pleasantly surprised) and pillowy, tender shumai. As we were finishing the last bite of appetizers, a giant sushi boat docked on our table. I'm not even sure what all we ordered, but I think I mostly ate the maguro, hamachi and unagi nigiri. Everything was fresh and expertly prepared, and for once I was able to nibble my sushi without it falling apart. (I refuse to stick the whole darn thing in my mouth at once. I'm delicate like that.) And to top it off, the staff waited patiently as we (the last patrons in the place) got all sorts of tipsy, not rushing us out even though it was after closing time.

First time eating Tupelo Honey, and in all honesty, it exceeded my expectations. I was expecting a water down version of something that may appeal to a crowd with a less adventurous pallet, but instead, i found myself with a face full of one of the best breakfast dishes I have eaten in many years thanks to the staff at tupelo honey. Taylor, one of the managers there, was great too. She not only helped me choose which breakfast dish was going to be the best fit for me, but also carried on genuine conversation with myself and two other Guest (who were also very pleased first timers), making the experience sitting at a bar on a Sunday morning in a small southern town that much more comforting.

ummm yeah not impressed at all. Sonoman cousine or not, it just didnt have anything special that would even remotely excite a food connoiseur. bland, lacking originality, just regular mexican food from just some regular mexican restaurant that happens to be in a hip location. i hear the drinks and the specials are really good thats all the reviews say too. but i came here for the food and left hungry and unsatisfied. only thing worth mentioning from the menu is thier buffalo white queso dip. it was surprisingly good but try it with the regular chips they offer, the ones the dip came with were thick and burnt-oil tasting.

Sushi Nara is a great sushi option on this side of town. I'm usually skeptical of sushi in landlocked states but I was very pleasantly surprised. I've been here twice and really enjoyed my food each time.

Pour house was awesome. A great place to listen to live music. You can stay inside or enjoy the weather outside on the patio. Happy hour was awesome 2 for 1 beers. I didn't get a chance to eat but the good going by us looked delicious! They were handing out free samples of moonshine! Valet is free and easy!

This was definitely one of the best dining experiences my husband and I have ever had. The food was amazing. We started with the rabbit and dumplings, oyster shooter and smoked deviled eggs. All were excellent. Really and truly excellent. You can't go wrong with any of these. We then moved on to the specialty cocktails. The two that were my favorite were the Rorschach Sour
Cana Brava rum, raspberry, lime, egg white, squid ink. Verdict: a hint of sweetness and not dry at all. Just very good and different. 
California Blues
St. George Vodka, blue, cucumber, lemon, raspberry, bitters. Verdict: Amazing!  Not too sweet, not too dry. Just perfect and very refreshing. 
Dinner consisted of the Chanterelle mushrooms with roasted grape tomatoes, sweet corn, leeks, mashed purple potatoes and basil. Extremely tasty. My husband ordered the beef heart stir fry, red beans and rice that were seasoned with ham hock and the corn muffins. We ended up splitting most of the food and could not have been happier with our choice for dining last night. The bar staff were professionals in the sense that it was an art and not thrown together and they were very knowledgeable and were great with beverage recommendations. We will definitely go back. The menu can change daily which can aggravate some, but I consider it exciting. 
Price: we ordered 3 appetizers, 2 entrees, 2 sides, and 3 cocktails. Total bill was $127.
Absolutely incredible food! Loved the atmosphere and the vibe. Service was fantastic. It was such a memorable experience with the way they do things. I would definitely go back. In a heartbeat.

This place is ok, mediocre. We had a view of where the food is made, seen one of the cooks drop a bagel and then went to wash it off in the sink where employees wash their hands.  There isn't anything inviting when you walk in, it gives a cold atmosphere. Not sure we would ever return.

There aren't enough good things I can say about Tired Hands. I fell in love with the Fermentaria and love enjoying the intimate feel and humble beginnings at this Brew Café. It's no wonder they are able to open their own General Store a storefront down the street from here! 

At the Brew Café where Tired Hands all started, you can find a constantly rotating list of beers of all types. They always have their HopHands (classic Pale Ale) and SaisonHands (saison, as expected) on tap at both Brew Café and Fermentaria but they both typically won't have the same rotating beers so I will typically go to both locations over one weekend. The beers change all the time and their tap list with extensive details including ingredients and key taste notes are always given to you and found on their website. No flights here; you can get them in 4, 8, or 16oz servings and can take them home with you in 32/64 oz growlers (but only using their growlers). 

Also food!! You aren't going to get a meal here like you do at Fermentaria; they just don't have the kitchen for it. But what they do have is solid, delicious local cured meats, cheeses, and pickles as well as a panini press for some light meals. They not only make their own beers and sodas but they also bake their own dense, delicious bread that they serve with nearly everything that they have here. Their foods also rotate to keep up what is fresh and local so I'm always looking forward to what they bring to the table. 

You can tell they really care here about quality of their food and drinks. I mean, they make homemade soda, have some ballin cold brew, and Darjeeling iced tea? Man, if only I didn't come here for only their beer and food...  Anyway, I love this place and you certainly will too if you enjoy quality beer and food by the Main Line, this is the spot to be.

Came here for Father's Day and was pleasantly surprised regarding the quality of the food. As far as the service, we were quickly seated and greeted by smiles by the waitress. The space itself is quite small so for occasions like this or even large parties...beware. However, the food makes up for the tight space where you literally can reach over to your neighbors plate and grab a piece of food off their plate.

For appetizers I tried the coconut shrimp which were ok...nothing to write home about. The sauce that it came with was overly sweet so I wasn't a big fan.

For entree I ordered the crab cakes with French fries and broccoli. The crab cakes were plentiful and filling (with crab that is). Many places use other misc meat filling along with their crab to makes a meaty crab cake which takes away from the authenticity of a crab cake but here there were no crab lacking. The broccoli was just ok..could've used a little bit more of the garlic seasoning. The French fries were very tasty and seasoned. 

I came away full and satisfied from my experience. Prices were very reasonably. Being that I love right around the corner, I will definitely venture here again and I would recommend anyone else to give it a go here as well.

I disliked most aspects of this restaurant. I don't like that it is 100% self service but they still have a huge tip jar and expectantly look at it while giving you your change...before you even get food. 
I don't like having to go up and stand in line to order breakfast.
I don't like that you even have to get your own coffee.
Then, when your order is ready, you have to go up and carry your own platters to your table. 
I don't like waiting for 25 minutes for my food when we are the only people in the place.
I don't like that, instead of clearing the 4 dirty tables when it WAS so empty, the little blonde girl behind the counter played with her phone.
I'm guessing the two teenie-bopper girls were hired more for their looks than waiting ability since they were both pretty but didn't do anything other than take the order and yell numbers.
I don't like the tons of political signs all over the place. I'm here for food, not politics.
Now, having said that, the plate servings were well sized. The bacon was good. The hashbrowns were actually hashbrowns (unlike NOSH and Betsy's) and the hot sausage was good. 
Like so many places, the cooks need a "Cooking Eggs for Dummies" book, because over medium does not mean runny whites and sunny side up does not mean liquid whites.

I don't know about lunch, but in all honesty, I'd probably never eat another meal inside the place again. Maybe call in an order and take it with me...which is the only activity I saw there besides me and the girly.

If the eggs had been right, I might have given this a 3...or if Yelp implemented half stars, 2.5.

Forget the fact that this isn't authentic Chinese food. They didn't claim to be. They claim to be "mission style, san fran chinese". This food is bland. BLAND. Do not let the photos fool you. I think they rely on the fact that their portions are ginormous to up the "like" factor. News flash: I don't want loads of bland food on my plate.

We always order from Dynasty, Sara is the best delivery girl. The chicken wings with that sauce they use are really good, I always order the special fried rice, how can you go wrong... Oh my wife loves the stir fried vegetables, with the light brown sauce.
The food is really good. I had the wagyu steak and it's delicious. It is a very pricey place...the cocktail was hit or miss. The view at the restaurant is stunning.

This place is a pass.... However, no shirt, no shoes, no problem! at this restaurant. Come right in.

Sitting in the booth for dinner I witnessed, a guy come in with no shoes, another guy no shirt, a situation go down in the men's room (glad that thing had a door) and some odd behaviors with some peculiar gentlemen selling what seemed to be stolen goods... I don't know the details, it was clear they were not showing up for fries or burgers. 

I truly was trying to mind my own business, but no one was being discrete whatsoever. I was amazed, and unsettled I brought my kids here! 

Well, I am still hungry so I am going to take off my shoes and head back. Nope.! Haha

I would expect this after 10:00 pm on a Friday night, but this was the dinner crowd on Sunday.

Private glass-walled room was great for corporate dinner.  Nice ambience, good service.  BUT my Delmonico steak was so tough and full of gristle it was nearly inedible.  Very difficult to cut even with a steak knife.  Like what you'd get at a cheap all you can eat buffet.

I tried Keke's Breakfast Cafe in Brandon on my day off recently. I'm okay with dinning alone when I want to try a place that my husband or kids are not particularly fond of experimenting with. I'm the guinea pig that goes in first! I was pleasantly surprised with Keke's and will definitely be back with my husband since he is the resident breakfast lover! 

In fact, I think Kekes is one of the better breakfast places locally. I recently learned that they're a chain but they originally started in the Orlando area. And I like supporting locally owned establishments! 

The restaurant was clean, they provided disposable/ throw away menus and individually packaged condiments.... I just didn't like that they sat people in the boothes next to you. During the Covid19 pandemic, restaurants should be more cognizant of seating their customers at least six feet away from the next table, Kekes was not doing this. This is the only reason they are a 4 instead of a 5 in my opinion.

Their food, on the other hand, was spectacular!! The pecan waffle was crispy and golden brown like I asked my server to do for me (well done) and loaded with whipped cream! The bacon was a generous portion with the combo ... four pieces! The bacon was thick and flavorful, the home fries were soft and well-seasoned. I also had a cup of hot coffee, which I was offered refills for multiple times. 

All of the staff seemed happy and to be enjoying their jobs and routines. The customers seemed content. It was a positive vibe and a great way to start the day!

This place did not disappoint! I was looking for some good wings while passing through New Orleans and saw the reviews on yelp! I had the Chipotle BBQ wings, and they were absolutely amazing!! I also had the grilled chicken sandwich which was equally as good too! What's even better is the customer service! The guy taking our order took the time to explain the different sauces and made us feel so welcome! Will definitely stop by next time I'm in town!

I heart this place- so please stop going there if you are super loud and annoying, you heard me!

Prohibition on a Monday-Wednesday night is so nice, you don't have to worry about finding a seat because there are plenty. The bartenders are incredibly nice and remember your face. Fridays and Saturdays it seems littered with young fools who forgot what inside voice is- yea I'm old, get off my lawn!

Sundays is bring your own vinyl which is cool, I'm searching for the worst thrift store album I can find just to put them to the test, haha. In due time....

The food is always on, with a late night kitchen open to 1am, and awesome specials I always find myself nomnomnoming on something delicious.

The neighborhood is kind of sketch so bike or drive there-walking seems like a good idea if you want someone to drag you into a dumpster.

Overall, I'm happy to have this as one of my local haunts. And the best thing about it, it doesn't reek of old mildewy floors or piss littered bathrooms- they keep it clean and that's quite the task in filthadelphia.

For the price you pay for a small pizza (15 bucks) I expected a bit more. I ordered small half bacon half onion. The carmelized onion topping was so minced and covered by the onions and chunks of tomato in the sauce, you barely knew it was there. The bacon was almost as bad as bacon bits. WAY TOO SALTY and tiny chopped up pieces that probably sit in a fridge precooked all day. Yuck. I ordered at 505 online and was told the pizza wouldnt be ready until 6. Ok..I figured they must be busy. I got there about 545 and my pizza was already ready. That means luke warm pizza. Not good! Dough was soggy and cold. Note to self..not good for carryout!
The Frita burger is awesome! However, my only negative comment about this place is the time it takes to get the food. It takes a while.

Popped in to get a latte (dreamy and frothy) and a Rolex. Wonderful! The Rolex had this spicy roasted tomato garlic sauce and was excellent! I am excited to see this coffee shop cafe on upper Milpas - it's been a neighborhood need for a long time! I can't wait to try the YOLO (You Only Live Once) - a buttermilk biscuit drenched in gravy - when the chef rolls it out. Great owners, nice place - welcome!

Average fast food Korean results in 3 stars.

I like that you order by computer terminal - makes it easy to see the menu, understand the options and see pictures of the food. Similar process ' concept as Honeygrow. 

I'm no expert on Korean food but had it enough times in both higher and lower end restaurants to know the dishes and how they should taste. None of the traditional appetizers/sides to start were very good. I tried the Bibimbop and the Duk Bok Gi ( rice cakes and veggies in spicy sauce) over 2 visits. I thought the flavor was simply bland and not spicy at all. I've had much better for lower prices. The meat portions were incredibly small. The Bibimbop came to $15 at least if I recall correctly. You pay extra to add meat, an egg etc... just not worth it in my opinion. 

I sum up my review with one word - Average

BK

Love this place! I think this is going to be my go to place for sandwiches. I got the Chipotle Turkey Club. Its so good. The turkey they use is so delicous. Yumm. Service is pretty quick too. They also have these dill pickle flavored popcorn which is good. Different but good.

Finally got to stop into Bandana's BBQ today for carry out, just to sample their fare. I'd been hearing their catchy jingle all the time on the radio, and people have told me that it's a main destination for BBQ in St Louis. Though I didn't sit down to dine, I was received ever so courteously by the wait staff, and they assisted me in what to get. The waitress even offered me a glass of water while I waited for my carry out, and I thought that was an incredibly kind gesture of her; really who does that nowadays. I haven't had much luck with Barbeque before, especially pulled pork. This time around I got the pulled pork dinner plate with baked beans and slaw, and after taking it home and eating it, I was pleasantly delighted. The pulled pork is more hearty and thick, instead of being usually very watery, and because it was done in this way, I was able to get a good aftertaste of the pork. They have 6 different kinds of sauce for you to put on there, and my Memphis style complimented the meat quite fine. I really enjoyed my meal, and I thought I'd given up pulled pork. The inside of the place looks stellar! I will take my family here when they are in town again. I'm happy I stopped by, it's a bit tricky getting into this stripmall, but it's worth a stop!

It goes without saying that when people think of the best iconic (and maybe historic) places in St. Louis, CCK comes to mind. I'm not sure where to start; I guess the food: food is great especially their heart-stopping BLT. I also really dig their shakes, especially the seasonal ones (eggnog, peach, etc). I haven't tried most of their sundaes, but I always gotta order one to top off my meal when I'm here! Their homemade candy (which is made by them in the back) is just plain awesome.
