Actually, no words can explain the many kinds they got. The only negatives about this place is no french fries and even though the neighborhood has improved over the years, its still kind of sketchy. Otherwise, its a great place that takes you back in time!

I also forgot to mention that service as well as the food was quick! I'm usually there during the dead hours but during peak hours I strongly suggest planning ahead...I've seen long lines there!
Great food!! I just moved to Nashville and this was one of the first Bar B Que joints I had the privilege to go too, overall great!!

Came here to catch up with an old friend while we're both back in our hometown. I was craving something hearty yet healthy and this place definitely hit the nail on the head.

Located right on busy Tyrone Boulevard right near the intersection, I was surprised how quiet and subdued it was inside. The ambiance was perfect for some good conversation and I could definitely see myself do a business meeting in there too.

My friend ordered the omelette with home fries and a glass of orange juice while I got the chicken pesto quinoa bowl. My friend loved hers and commented on how it was definitely a lot greasy than a comparable entree from Denny's or IHOP. I loved my quinoa bowl. Quinoa was super well done and the pesto tasted fresh. The sundried tomatoes and nearly crunchy chicken breasts provided nice contrast in texture.

Prices were a bit steeper than the big chain breakfast fare but I feel as though it's worth it, except for the orange juice...my friend's large orange juice costed almost $4! It's Florida, that's almost highway robbery for our state beverage.

But all joking aside, this is a super solid place for breakfast and I look forward to coming back here the next time I'm back home.

1. It's a good cheesesteak, not going to lie.

2. The line is not worth it. I feel bad for tourists. 

3. My first time I stood in line and when I left I had to wash my clothing because the cheesesteak smell was IN my clothing.

4. Indoor dining, upstairs a plus. Who wants to sit outside when it's chilly and the weathers changing like today...

5. I felt unbelievably pressured to order quickly my first time around... I don't like that feeling.

6. only 3 stars because I've had better for cheaper.

Terrible customer service. When we entered the restaurant. We were not greeted nor acknowledged. The guy with the weird hair cut was just focusing in making dumplings in the back. Other waiters ignored us. 

The dumplings were plain dough with no meat. Tasted nothing like dumpling soups. 

People go here because they have good salt pepper wings and open very late. Other than this the service sucks.

Delicious southern comfort food. Don't miss out on their homemade pickles. I had them the first time I ate at the restaurant and dreamed about them for months. Next time I visited, I made sure to take home a quart of pickles.

second time ever going to chili's, i had the two for $25 with a friend and was pleasantly surprised. we had the chips and guacamole for our appetizer. the chips were a little too oily but good, nevertheless. we both had the bacon burger. that was amazing! the burger itself didn't look very big but it was heavy and filling for sure. we finished off with the pizookie type dessert and that was also delicious. prices were great, food was great, service was great as well. will definitely be back soon.

Was out here for work for a week. Eat at this place everyday for lunch because my boss was obsessed with bbq. I have never seen such poor service in my life. The food is pretty good and the prices are decent. The service was the worst I have ever seen. I asked for a coffee 4 times. Finally when I'm almost done with my lunch it shows up cold. No sugar or creamer brought with it. I ask for creamer. wait 15 minutes. Nothing..... I finally gave up.
Then asked for water waited for another 15 minutes. Never to be seen. So I finally get up go to the bar and get my own water. Then the waitress comes back with my water after I'm completely done with lunch and gives me the attitude because I went and got it myself. 
If u MUST have bbq then the food is ok but be prepared for crap service

Healthy, fresh, reliable.  In a nice, unpretentious atmosphere. 

In all the years I've lived in or visited Philly, this place has been slightly empty, with eager, charming waitstaff, plentiful mint tea and fresh food at bargain prices. I used to get the meat platters, but the sandwiches, falafel and baba are delicious too. Every time I visit, I'm afraid the restaurant will have disappeared. But no.
Walking distance from our condo and nice view from the patio. Food was great and service was friendly. Added bonus was the friendly bird that visited the patio.

WOW!!  I hesitate to write this, cuz I don't want everyone invading this little gem, but WOW!

Great margaritas, HUGE portions!  I mean HUUUUGE PORTIONS!!  This is arguably my new favorite Mexican restaurant in Franklin. 

Prices are ridiculous based on the amount of food. A Margarona, swirl margarita, sweet tea, chimichangas, fajitas Pueblo, and a Colorado burrito, with an opening appetizer of three amigos dips. Total damage? $75, and we took THREE boxes of food home. 

So, looking for a FANTASTIC Mexican restaurant, come here!  Just make sure you leave a place for me!!

Also...  Fantastic wait staff. Miguel, our waiter, was just great. Good sense of humor, nice guy.  Nice to have a good wait staff, with everything going on. 

Now, If you'll excuse me, I have to pass out on the couch. Food coma...

Every time I go to Philadelphia I go to Pat's and Geno's Steaks. All other times I've been there it's been great but not so much this time.

The location is 5 blocks east of Ellsworth-Federal Station on the SEPTA Broad Street Line. It isn't a scary walk from the restaurants (9th & Passyunk) to the station.

After a long line, like usual, I got my steaks. I got a steak w/ onions & no cheese. The Pat's sandwich was good, the meat was juicy and the onions were warm. The Geno's Steak had no onions, so the meat was dry and left out the warmth of the onion. 

If I had to choose between the two, I would give Pat's 3.5 to 4 stars & Geno's 2 to 2.5 stars which leaves me with a 3-star rating.
Came here with a group of friend. The staff was really great and knowledgeable. However, the food is not worth it, Overpriced and overrated. Won't be coming back.

I rarely risk dining in the suburbs as it always seems we pay a premium for a mediocre experience.  Surah was neither mediocre or priced at a premium.  The service was extremely attentive without being overwhelming, the menu had a good amount of choices without feeling like you were at an establishment that specialized in nothing and the food, oh, the food!  Everything we ordered was spot on.  Support this local gem so it doesn't go away!

UPDATE...

Have been here a half dozen times since the initial review and still have nothing but good to say about Surah.  They've added grills (for Korean BBQ) into some of their tables which adds some options to your dining experience and actually makes dining there with a family both fun and a bit more affordable (as you can share).

I live in Devon and our family was really looking forward to avero opening, especially as the build out appeared very stylish, so we finally went on a Thursday night... and I was disappointed.  I like the space quite a bit (was not too loud for me; although I have four young kids so my frame of reference might be different than others).  Our server was quite nice and pretty efficient.  I liked the menu as well but unfortunately the food is just not that good and is over-priced to boot.  The pizzas were very small with pretty sparse toppings (literally 1-2 bite pieces of pizza) for $14-$17 each; the bolognese was average at best and the smashballs which sounded very cool were average at best as well (I think the sauce needs to be re-worked as much too sweet and very little depth).  We ordered a salad for 3 and she served two very small salads and barely enough for a third and then charged us $25 (which they did reduce to a one salad price after discussing with them).  The salad was actually good so too bad so small.  The final bill was still much too much for this food.  All in all in this age, there is no excuse for such mediocre food at a place like this and the prices are just too high for the portion sizes.  This place should do incredibly well in this location but I am concerned now that it won't make it.  Owners - please step in and re-tool the food quickly.  My wife is already saying we are not going back.  Sincerely a concerned Devon resident.
Visited a year ago with a friend and it was incredibly amazing! Loved the items on the menu. The drinks and food was increidbly worth it!

We ate there yesterday morning during rush breakfast time at 10 a.m.
We were seated in less than 10 minutes.  The four of us ate pancakes, waffles, eggs over easy and a breakfast sandwich.  Everything was very good.  The coffee was also was delicious.  Finally, the staff was very friendly and the atmosphere was neutral.  I would go again and refer friends.

Had the worst experience the owner or said to be was super rude and not professional at all I asked about being over charged for getting half rice half noodles which I was going to pay for. And she yells out we don't do that and screaming out her lungs while all the rest of the people in line watched I had already handed her my card to pay while she still kept screaming at the end I just took my card and left the food this has had to be the worst and unprofessional experience ever . As a paying customer I should receive some respect.

After reading many other reviews, I was a little bit hesitant to eat here, but it was my date's choice.   The service was great, except they totally rushed us to pay the bill and kept returning to the table to see if we were finished.  It was early afternoon on a Saturday and the place wasn't crowded so they didn't need the seats.    

The food - I ordered a veggie sandwich and they brought me a veggie burger.  I didn't complain because the burger was fine.   It was a bit tasteless and the fries were lukewarm.   Not sure I need to return here for any reason.

Besides getting political, (come on guys, this is a site to review restaurants and their food, not if you like their political stance) Jason's is just alright. When they first opened it was a lot more of a friendly place. The food is alright but the last time we were there, my croissant was stale, an the fruit it came with were all hard, close-to-the-rind pieces. For the price I paid I was pretty disappointed. That and the lack of worker moral, (seriously, you can't even crack a smile?) will probably keep me from going there. Because nothing says 'We don't want your business!' like an employee with an attitude!
Should chicken tenders and fries take 40 minutes to make? When asking the employees I was left with a rude response and attitude. The chicken tenders were dry and all breading, minimal meat.

I really love this place. 

I've never really had much experience with Thai so I can't say I'm an expert in any sense of the word. The atmosphere is relaxing and the restaurant is spotless. The starter salad is refreshing and an actual salad with more than just a chunk of tomato and a bed of lettuce. I probably annoyed my waitress by asking her to explain how they make the house dressing for it. 

I ended up having the Voodoo Noodle with the tofu/veggie combo as my "meat" choice. Since I don't really have a vegetarian bone in my body I figured I would end walking away from the meal being even more hungry than when I sat down but surprisingly I couldn't even finish the plate. Portion size was really generous and the flat noodles and veggies were absolutely delicious. The tofu tasted like...well, tofu. But not in a dear God I can't even keep this down kind of way. I think the redeeming quality was in whatever soy sauce mixture they used to cook it.

Definitely check this place out if you want a quick, affordable, and healthy lunch!

I dined here on Thursday evening.  I had a Caesar salad to start.  It was very good.  For my entree, I selected the Spaghettini and meatballs.  Nicely prepared and served piping hot.  I have a quick question that was prompted by the menu description of this dish...  what are sustainable meatballs? At any rate, I enjoyed the food and the service was very good.
Stopped by to pick up some coffee beans. Tried the Mexican roast for espresso. Delicious! We didn't stay because there was limited outside seating, but I'm glad we got the beans to go.

I had to update my review to 3 stars after trying their pho. I had previously been disappointed with their Rice Vermicelli, but since my boyfriend said he had liked their pho, I decided it was only fair that I give it a shot. I got the P2 Pho with White Meat Chicken and although I wasn't a fan of the meat, the broth was decent. The vegetables were fresh and the broth was piping hot which I appreciate. 

Prices are reasonable and their $1.50 delivery charge via GrubHub is less than most restaurants so I can see myself ordering from here again.
Wings are awesome. Waitress's  are hit or miss but thats everywhere. . Buffalo chicken salad is amazing

So maybe I'm a tad biased on this one. I used to live two blocks away from Chapterhouse, and it was my go-to coffee place for a year and a half. Whenever I go there with someone new, I usually point out (wistfully!) the stool at the counter by the window where I wrote a novel once. Memreez!

OK, but beyond that, Chapterhouse is pretty kickass. First of all, the atmosphere is laid-back, the baristas are chill (there's a couple in particular who I'm always glad to see when I make it back to Philly for a visit), there's always good music playing (although I think I've now heard enough Ratatat to last two lifetimes), and the art gallery aspect is a nice touch. Furthermore, the owners are frequently present, friendly, and helping out in the space, so you know that any issues will be addressed.

I get that there are some people who don't dig a place that allows dogs, has couches and board games, and is just as often full of chit-chat as it is full of people with their eyes glued to their Macbooks. But this gives it the feel of being someone's home (there's a fireplace, for Pete's sake), which makes it a lot more welcoming than a clinical get-your-coffee-and-go kind of location. If you want one of those, you can walk half a block up to 9th and South and no one will think less of you. (Well, I won't, at least. Well, maybe a tiny bit.)

As for the menu: omg BERRY MOCHA. It's delicious cold and better hot, and you should be drinking one right now. The other specialty lattes are delicious and decently priced, the iced tea sodas are unique, and all the other standard drinks can usually be manipulated one way or another if you want. I don't generally go for the food (a tad pricey), but what I've sampled is good; the pastries can be a little bit hit or miss. (Best to get them around 11 am, after they've arrived and had time to thaw a little bit, especially the squares.) And: a nice varied tea selection.

There are a couple qualms: a high credit card minimum, a basement space that isn't very inviting (there used to be vintage clothing sales down there before they converted it; aw), and occasionally (weekends) it is downright impossible to get a seat. But as coffeeshops go, you'd be hard-pressed to find a more versatile, interesting, and welcoming one. 

This is exactly the kind of place I want to open someday. But don't worry, guys: I'll make sure it's safely outside your exclusive economic zone. :)

I'm from North Jersey originally and have been missing pizza and bagels for months. This place came recommended to me and it did not disappoint. I got the penne vodka pizza, wow. Other people got pasta dishes that came with salads, highly recommended.
Great food!! Sometimes I find certain dishes to be better than other, some servers better than others, but its a good place. Just remember, it gets pricey.

They have really good broth! According to the menu you can tell that they really only pay attention to their ramen --- only 3 ramen options when I was there during March 2018: Pork Broth, Pork Broth with Black Garlic Oil, Too Spicy, and you can add different types of toppings to your ramen. I would strongly recommend the one with Garlic Oil; Ramen is always better with black garlic oil. 
     Their Too Spicy Ramen is truly too spicy for me and my friends. We, three people, took turns to eat the Too Spicy Ramen, trying to finish it without putting all the pain on one person, but still couldn't finish the broth. It's REALLY SPICY. Guess you'll like it if you enjoy spicy food.
Hip atmosphere, great servers and very good food.  Really enjoyed. 4 star means to me very good.

Okay, first things first.  We've been looking forward to this restaurant since we heard it was opening.  We heard the one in the warehouse district had delicious food.  We live 3 blocks from this restaurant and we usually like to eat around our neighborhood since we have really great restaurants.  We went to La Casita on the second day it opened.  It was me, my husband and our 2 girls.  Like the Margaritas, but it took 20 minutes to get. Food was okay, but it took a long time for it to come out.  We spoke with the waiter and manager and told them that the whole neighborhood had been waiting on its opening and they were probably going to get slammed and they need more wait staff/bartender.  We went a second time with some friends. Drinks took 30 minutes to come out and food even longer. Then we went last week on April 14th for my husbands birthday.  Drinks took 45 minutes to come out, Food 1.5 hours.  We got there at 6:00 and left at 8:30. we had friends and kids with us.  Waiter brought wrong orders and said that the guacamole wasn't going to happen.  We spoke with the new manager since the original is no longer there (don't what happened to him.) They have only been open a month and a half maybe and already a new manager.  It's such a shame.  I really wish they make it, but they have to have better trained wait staff.  I worked as a waitress in the past and I know that it shouldn't take 45 minutes to get a drink.  Good Luck La Casita.  Maybe we'll visit in the future, but y'all gotta get your act together.  Jazz Fest is right around the corner and y'all are going to get slammed.

Not sure this place could get it more right.  The service is the best.  It's a fun comfortable place with awesome steaks.   The cowboy ribeye is fit for a king and the kitchen always gets the steak perfect.   Some of the old traditions of tomato juice and bean soup for starters is quirky but adds to the fun.  If your in town stop by.  You run into celebrities a lot here.

I give it a 3 because of the service and my drink, but the actual food was not that good at all. My boyfriend and I went here last night because he wanted some italian and they have several options which was great. I had the chicken piccata and my boyfriend had fettucine alfredo with salmon which wasn't originally on the menu. He had to put so much salt on his food for it to taste good it was shocking. My chicken was tender and not dry, but the actual sauce was very salty and unflattering. The best thing was the crab meat that was on top of my chicken. I may try this place again for a more simpler dish, but I doubt it. Our waitress Tara was awesome very nice and professional.

This is a solid staple in my rotating restaurant list. It's close to home, has lots of outdoor seating, good happy hour, delicious margaritas, and my favorite, the Rum House salad!

I have tried most of the tacos. Honestly, none of them have ever really blown me away. I feel like I order them based on the description and then once I taste them it's totally not what I expected? They're not bad, just not why I come here. (Although, Taco Tuesday is legit.)

My favorite thing to do here is drink margaritas, eat the Rum house Salad, and people watch on Magazine street. I don't know why the salad is so good...everything I love..spinach, beets, goat cheese, and some other mystical ingredients that are just super dank all together. Never had a bad service experience here. Good place to watch sports too, although it definitely gets crowded.

After you catch a nice marg buzz, head across the street to one of many fun boutiques and shops :)

Great food.  I usually stick to the breast quarter.  Medium has good flavor and spice, get the hot if you enjoy spicy foods.  Lemon pepper is really good on the wings too. For sides Ill usually get the fries and baked beans are really good.  
The only reason I'm not giving 5 stars is for the wait. I always call ahead with my order and they will typically tell me about 30 minutes till its ready.  It is consistently much longer than that.  I dont mind waiting for food to be made fresh, but if its going to be an hour, tell me it will be an hour so I can plan accordingly.  I definitely recommend trying hot stuff but call ahead and then double the wait time they give you.
Food is original, fresh, tasty, perfectly prepared. All this at a great, low price. Very impressive.

We had an outstanding Valentine's Day weekend dinner here. Have had this spot bookmarked for a while, but this was our first visit. Arrived early for our reservation so had a drink at the bar. Turns out they have happy hour even on Saturday so that was a pleasant surprise. Had some drinks and then sat at our table. Started off with a Cesar salad that had a delicious soft boiled egg and fresh dressing. Also tried the crab cake which had an amazing Asian fusion twist, on top of kimchi with sesame sauce and carrots. It was so good! For our entrees I had the catfish and my husband had the pork chop. He said the chop was moist and  juicy. My catfish didn't look like anything special on the plate (no color) but the taste was a sophisticated mix for my palate. The mix of sour pickled cabbage with tangy mustard and spicy beans and rice was literally a taste explosion. This is one of the better restaurants in Nashville. Can't wait to come back and try something else. Thanks for a great date!

We saw this restaurant featured on the show,"Burgers, Brew and Que" and it looked very good so we decided to try it on our trip to NOLA. 

Unfortunately, the hype from watching it on TV led to being very disappointed by our experience. First of all, our server was borderline rude and just not a very pleasant. We started our meal by trying the Fried Gator appetizer which tasted like they were pulled out of a box in the freezer and popped in a microwave. For the main course, we ordered the Crawfish and Grits since that what was featured by the TV show. This meal was very good and tasted fresh. 

Overall, the ambiance, service and appetizer were very disappointing. The main course was very good so that's why I will be generous with 3 stars.

The Mac and cheese that I order here is great! 
The one with bacon bits is pretty darn salty though. Overall the service is great.
came here for lunch the other day.  the food and atmopshere were both great.  Definitely will return.

I previously gave The Italian Affair 4 stars. This time out it is 2 (on sentimental value alone) and should really be a 1. The food was what you would expect from a diner. Big portions, very average. This is not good Italian food anymore.

I love this place. Every opportunity I get I make it a point to eat here, even to go. I order the same exact thing at every single Thai restaurant and it's the cashew nut chicken Thai hot with brown rice. Ploy Thai by far exceeds everyone else's cashew nut chicken and they're brown rice is the bomb Diggity
The burger was all right but paying $15 (once tax is added and that's not including tip)  I give it 3 Stars. It's probably worth $6 less than what you pay for.

If I could do a negative star I would. This location is by far the slowest I have ever experienced. The over night manager always has some excuse why she can't take orders and acts like you're a huge inconvenience... also, she said the store was closed except for door dash or grub hub. I do not recommend!
New owner , new cook. SAD we were regulars. My sandwich could have been mad by a six year old. Our server, Denny was awesome as usual.

Went here to see the sidny raymond band and have nibbles.  The bar / restaurant was sent up well for a band. We had some drinks, nibbles and watched an amazing band. We had the roast beef wow yummy...fresh rolls and lots of roast beef.  He had the meatball grinder which was also very good. Plenty of parking and lots of tables.

Is there a sauce shortage today? I received your spaghetti bake with barely no sauce and your antipasto salad came with just one packet of dressing. really? You couldn't have spared another packet for your 8.99 salad? 
 This is my first Westshore Pizza order I guess I should have got pizza

Live music nice view of the lake especially if you get to see the sun setting 
The food Yummy haven't been disappointed

Spur of the moment lunch destination, and I couldn't have been more surprised and pleased! From their unique sandwich collections, to their art and live music (at certain times), this place was quite rememberable. 
Ordered a turkey sandwich which had tons of flavor and ingredients that I've never have had on a sandwich. For example the cranberry jalapeño jelly, really tasty! 
My lady had the simple grilled cheese but even then, it was still full of flavor. 
Staff was friendly, food was delicious and experience was unique.

We didnt make it to the table. After waiting outside for an hour we walked in to only be disgusted. The place was filthy and they put us at the counter near the kitchen. We got up before they could attempt to take our order. Definitely would pass regardless of what people think of their food.

Wonderful family-run place. I love places that show some pride of ownership and Pop's definitely does! The owners are super outgoing, and very excited about their menu and all of the homemade options they have. Reasonably priced and worth making part of your regular lunch/dinner out routine.

The All-You-Can-Eat sushi here was not up to par. All the sushi came out room temperature. The fish was not fresh. 

We also had alcohol beverages here which tasted like pink lemonade minute maid with lychee liquor...

Our server has no knowledge of the menu when asked about their sushi rolls.

RUDE! long time customer (see previous reviews) picks up a high dollar to-go order- bartender asks if he can help, and I tell him my to-go order is right behind him- he says nothing and walks away to help another customer- when I finally get helped, I ask the wandering bartender why he ignored me, a second bartender says , "we're really busy" and the restaurant is 1/3 full. This rudeness and unprofessionalism is new to Bardanay- this is why Boise will never be a first tier restaurant city- the service tonight was more like a Stinker gas station than a restaurant- Management needs to pay attention to hiring and training - otherwise Bardanay will end up being yet  another Boise restaurant  disappointment.

Very upscale breakfast establishment.  Been to other locations and they are always fantastic BUT the one in Lutz off 56, I had a few hairs in my omelette.  Rather than apologize and get some manager involvement I was just ignored by the server.   Then I was presented the bill for full price on an omelette that I hardly touched.  Very poor customer engagement in my opinion to make something right.  Won't be going back to this location ever again.
Tremendous service and even better meal!  Fantastic wine list and overall great vibe.  The food leads the way for this amazing unique place.  From appetizers to desserts you will not be disappointed.

I was really looking forward to some TN BBQ as I am traveling from KC. I placed my order through Yelp and a hour later nothing came. I called the number that was sent in my "confirmation" email and the gentleman I talked to from DoorStep Delivery said the order had been cancelled due to it being ordered through Yelp.  I had never been notified. I called Corky's and spoke with OJ a manager who told me that there was really nothing he could do. He offered me nothing for my wasted time and told me that I would have to order through DD again. 
I love Yelp, I use it all the time when traveling. 
I guess Corky's managers should be aware of who they contract to do their deliveries. As OJ stated to me, "This is all new to me too." 
Severely disgusted with Corky's lack of trying to fix a problem with their process.
Had an 8:00 reservation last saturday and after being seated our party of 4 sat there for 45 minutes and were not even acknowledged by staff.

Heard lots about this restaurant and held high expectations, but I was let down. My party arrived late afternoon-early evening and was promptly seated. It took an excessive length of time (~30 minutes) for food to arrive for three people without special requests. When the food arrived, the manager served the meals to the wrong person; one steak was overcooked; and the side dishes were cold. When speaking with the waitress, we were offered "comp" drinks while we waited for the chef to cook a new steak, but we were billed for the "comp" drinks. We were so upset we just wanted to leave, but the mgr. then served a new steak which we then had it packed "to go". I would normally never return to a restaurant with this experience, but given the reputation of this restaurant and being our first visit, I'll most likely go back and hope for a better result. Disappointed!!

Amazing place! We booked a table, but showed up more than 1 hour in advance; still, we just waited about 10 minutes, even though there was a waiting line - very nice service. We shared a vegetarian feast and a main dish with 3 kinds of meat -  it was amazing! Everything was tasty and definitely enough for two people. We also had one dessert (Baklava), which was great.

Besides the food, the atmosphere is very nice; we enjoyed it a lot.

I wanted to go here after reading all the reviews and I was glad I got a chance too. I totally didn't know that you could reserve ahead of time online and I wish I did. Do not forget to reserve on Yelp!!! It was an hour and a half wait at 9:40 am so we got seated  at 11:20. Luckily our hotel was nearby so we left and just chilled while they texted us. 
We got the banana foster french toast and the two eggs benefit of the Chicken St Charles and the Shrimp Cortez. And a side of eggs. The Food was amazing. I loved it so much. Who would've thought fried chicken would be good with a poached egg. I absolutely loved it! The shrimp one was amazing too. The sauce on that one was better. However, all of this was INCREDIBLY salty. By the end of it I couldn't take it anymore and actually left some behind which isn't a good sign. 
The eggs were scrambled perfectly. I devoured them. I wasn't a huge fan of the Banana foster french toast because it was drenched in some honey syrup sauce or something and it made it sooo soggy. I like my french toast crisp. But it was interesting. 
The mimosas were pretty good. Nothing out of this world but you have to get the ruby slipper. It's what they're named after! Super strong so that was a plus. 
All in all, they need to cut down the salt. That's why I'm taking off one star. Also horrible lines so reserve  a spot early.
These are not tacos. Tortillas are tough, meat has no flavor. Also fried chicken and brisket do not belong in tacos. You're better off going to Taco Bell.

Have not dined here yet but did stop inside. Very cool space with inviting seating options and hip hop themed original art perfectly placed.  Music was audible but not too loud. 
The menu is reasonably priced with something for everyone.  
More once I dine in!

Can only base this on my uber eats order, with that being said anyone who loves jamaican food knows callaloo is where it's AT but also know it's hard to find GOOD callaloo. This place has got it down to a science, perfectly seasoned (not too much salt which is common) not overcooked and basically took me back to when I was eating callaloo in St. Ann Parish in Jamaica. Definitely will order again. Note: snapper and veg patties where also amazing

Ordered a Cortado and a chocolate croissant, we got service with a smile. They were very excited to answer any questions we had about their blends. 
The pour over was fantastic! 
Cortado and cappuccino were aromatic and rich. All with a great flavor- definitely PACKED no place to sit at all but a great atmosphere.
Asked the doorman at hotel montelione.  Where do you go for lunch.  Said Johnny's.  It's on my list every trip to Nola.   Absolutely great food
For being just off Bourbon Street, Oceana is a pleasant surprise! Go here for fried food. The service was very friendly and the back patio is nice for dinner on a nice evening!

Had a wonderful breakfast here this morning and then free happy hour appetizers convinced us to try dinner.  Made the right choice.  Nice atmosphere, N'Orlins blues, attentive wait staff and that was before the food arrived.  Blew us away.  Sunchoke soup with truffle oil, shrimp and croutons was perfect.  Crap!  Forgot about the cornbread and sweet potato rolls with butter and Liam bean puree.  Then French baby chicken with crawfish and okra was the Best chicken I've ever had.  Nice find. And it was a quiet respite from the craziness of French Quarter....

Waitstaff are terrific! Masked, attentive, polite. Drinks are great. Food not so much. Steam bucket was ok. Crab chowder arrived barely warm but waitstaff took care of that issue graciously.  Grouper melt was disappointing.   A very thin piece of fish.  No social distancing here.

Just enjoyed a HUGE dinner via caviar delivery. It was perfect after a very long week. We ordered the volcano maki, fire cracker maki, chicken katsu and shrimp tempura udon. Although they forgot one of the rolls in the first delivery, they were so apologetic and sent another delivery out to make up for it. Everything was absolutely delicious!! The chicken katsu was a generous portion size (enough for 2 to split) and came with yummy miso soup and side salad. I was pleasantly surprised that everything was separated so that the tempura and katsu were crispy, even in take out boxes. The sushi was fresh and beautifully presented, too! I truly appreciate their kindness with the missing roll, and will definitely be ordering again, hopefully sitting at the restaurant next time!!

I was so excited to try this palce for brunch, but ended up disappointed. The decor and ambiance is extremely well done (the bathroom is magical!) But atmosphere is only part of being a restaurant. We did the brunch buffet, with reservations, and were seated right away. We all go the bottomless mimosas/bloody Mary offer - the mimosas were lovely (good variety too!) But the bloody Mary was horrible. I generally love bloodyMary's, especial with savory brunch food) but this one didn't taste right at all, and I sent it off after q few sips. I actually went to the bathroom and rinsed my mouth it tasted so bad! The buffet sounds promising on paper, but once you wander the options you realize it's not that great. The food is low in quality, and doesn't seem fresh. Nothing is warm enough, and everything tends to be dry. It is nice in that the options are spread out, so you aren't standing in a giant line, and you can order food as part of the buffet. The cooked to order food is a bit better than the buffet table options, but still is pretty poorly done. The mimosas and the atmosphere are the only saving grace. People rave about the evening events, so hopefully that is better? For the price, I am expecting higher quality - how hard is it to make a decent waffle?
Food was ok. Nothing special. Service was terrible. Had to get up from my table multiple times to ask the server for things I needed. Will not go back. Do not recommend.

Staff retraining necessary.  This newer Chipotle was extremely disappointing.  Every table was dirty; no unsweetened or sweetened iced tea containers, pinto beans looked old and dried up; the lone trash bin area had all overflowing containers (need another bin area near the doorway to the side parking lot for the store); did not have appropriate baskets for eat-in tacos.  Customers are last here.

Wouldn't normally leave a review for an order at the counter place, but the people here are always so warm and welcoming and friendly. The food is good and a nice refreshing lunch spot during the work day.

Spotted the trailer while I was hungry, decided to give them a try, got a brisket sandwich.  Eh...meat and bun were both dry and you'd think for $9.50 they could include something besides meat on the sandwich (pickles, onions, etc.) and/or a side.  Middling 'que at best, there's better around.

I stopped in with a group of out of town business buddies on Monday night.  Really good crowd and energy for a Monday.  Young crowd.  DJ.  Small dance floor with some dancing.  Nice outdoor patio and fire pits.  Slow but very friendly wait staff.  Good prices on drinks.  Extensive Tequilla choices.  Definitely a place I would go back to.

Unique place to try some interesting cocktails. Bartender was extremely knowledgable and friendly and even recommended some books for us to
Check out in our home mixology. Tiny bar was a bit crowded, but several open tables at about 9pm. It would be better if they expanded the bar space. Good selection of whisky. Didn't try the food but would come back again to do so.

Everything on the menu is fantastic! The Philly Tri-Tip sub is so worth it. Love the old fashioned style burgers. Grilled  cheese and hit dog sliders for the kids!  And the music played inside the diner is awesome. I recommend highly. Family friendly.

The food was SO great here. And the beer with a really awesome happy hour price! I highly recommend the friend zucchini appetizers (they're pretty unique) and the fish and chips. So good. The service was meh but I was overall happy with my experience here.
Worst BBQ ever. Ribs were extremely fatty and luke warm. Fries were underdone and smelled like old oil. Corn was just bad. And who can screw up corn on the cob??  Avoid this place.

Awesome.  So much better and more flavorful than the Dunkins of the world.

Really friendly, reasonably-priced, can't really ask for more.

The food and service disappointed me.  

I'm a vegitarian so I had their salad bar.  Bad idea.  There were many dishes on the bar with meat in them.  The lettuce for salad was the iceburg mix that you get from your grocery store.  (im not a fan)  I will give them this, the ranch was delicous!

I also agree with the fella above me, it was too expensive for what you get.  But I also didn't get much!  Bad Salad, mashed potatoes, and a roll.  All for 8 bucks?  I don't recommend this place.
We have found our new favorite breakfast spot!  Great coffee, hashbrowns, pancakes.  Huge portions, very good prices.  Excellent service.  The CLEANEST.

I came in for a drink, which was fabulous.  Met a great bartender and a great diner next to me.  I just ordered an appetizer of mussels and it was terrific.  Cooked perfect and the broth was divine!  I was going to get the sweetbread dinner, but they were out!

Overall I loved this place.  Cool chill spot.

Quick and dirty fast food, except not so quick...  for some reason everything took a million years to get to us (how does a strawberry milkshake made from vanilla ice cream + strawberry flavoring/coloring take anywhere over 5 minutes??).  Bread was meh and the strawberry milkshake was nothing impressive.  My lukewarm double cheeseburger was also nothing impressive and apparently the steak sandwich was good, but I only had a bite.  Acceptable food for what it is, but I've had better for cheaper.  And Lee's would get the 2 stars of "meh"ness from me, except:

- Super friendly service dude
- Moderately clean space
- Also decently clean bathroom!
- Aaaand the whole place smelled heavily like french fry oil.  So delectable.
Burger must of been sitting in the grill all day. Fish tacos were good but no better than anywhere else. Fries were the best part of meal.

I don't ever remember if I tried Thai food.  However, I don't like curry as my Taiwanese friend, who really like Thai food, say it consists of.

This restaurant had a booth at this year's Indianapolis Chinese Festival.  I decided to try their appetizers of a vegetable spring roll, a wing, and a drummette with sweet chili sauce for $2.  I was puzzled that I thought there was meat in my roll; then I tasted just that piece of food and realized it was mushroom.  Oh, I love mushrooms!  It was great.  I thought it must be unique to this restaurant.  In my next restaurant review, I will indicate otherwise.  See Thai Kitchen review.

The chicken was good.

Great location but drinks were very inconsistent and more often than not honorable.   Ordered long island ice tea and rum runner.  The rum runner was a deep red purple color and great.  The long island was the worst I have ever had.  Sent the long island back and ordered the rum runner.  This one comes out this time is light pink in color and tastes completely different.  Waitress questions bar tender on it and the bartender tells her its made rught and she can get behind bar and make it hereself.  Won't be back

We found this place when I wanted to support local business. My kids are gluten free so finding food they eat is sometimes hard. But they were able to eat catfish nuggets because they are seasoned with corn meal. My husband had the meatloaf with rice and gravy. He said it was good, a little dry. His two sides were the potato salad and hush puppies. The potato salad was fire and same for the hush puppies. I had the ox tails with rice and gravy, black eye peas, and collard greens. We got banana pudding to go. I also had chicken gizzards which were really good!

Came here with my gf to give this location a chance to redeem itself from the subpar service and crap fries we got on national chicken wing day some weeks ago. (The fries were burned or refried and tasted bad. Service was VERY slow as well.) 

We arrived there around 1:50. We were greeted and seated quickly, and ordered and got our drinks promptly. We did need a few extra minutes to order because they had a new menu with lots of new items. 
After about 10 mins i had to flag our server down to place our oder. (About 2pm).Chicken tacos and a chicken wrap nothing that should have taken as long as it took. 

After 15 min she came out to say our food will be out in a few min. "Ok no problem." So we continued to wait..... and wait..... and wait. 

So about 10min later she came back out to apologize about the wait and said it will be out in a few min. It was now 2:30 and no food. I set a timer on my phone for 2min..... then we left a few minutes after it went off. 
It was now at least 2:35. 
So they never got a chance to even redeem themselves. So i can't even comment if the fries were cooked well or burned again. 

We we're at mellowmushroom now.

I was excited to visit the Pour House. Shortly before I thought I was going to go there, I read a recent article listng several health code violations discovered in a recent inspection by the local health code inforcement agents. That was enough to change my mind.

I find this the best selection a craft beers in WC. Not the quantity, but their careful curation, and rotating the wide tap list.

Also, my favorite burger in town - the Inferno, with jalapeño and cheese stuffing. Take the first bite right over your plate, as the cheese and juices come out volcanically.

Interesting sides and appetizers like sweet potato pirogues. Nice seafood options, loved the scallops in bacon cream sauce (how could you not?)

Noisy when school is in session. Sit upstairs by the window where it is quieter, and watch the people on the street.

This is my favorite burger in town. They always manage to make the burger so juicy and tasty and the fries make a perfect side. I love coming here for the food alone, but beware it can get really busy during peak hours so expect long waits and it can be really loud inside. Otherwise I recommend it to everyone in Indy.

Nice little place hidden in the corner. Have been several times and was pleased with the food each time. The Thai dishes are fresh and flavorful with enough heat to make it all work. Sushi was average but still tasty. Service can be a bit slow but it is still a local favorite.

Union jacks is one of my go to spots in Broadripple. There is some strange sort of charm about the place that gives it a cool vibe. They have an excellent beer list full of local and regional craft beers. The staff is always super friendly and very quick with their service. But obviously we all read reviews for the food.

If you come here and your looking to spend a good amount of time here, then order the deep dish pizza. So far it is the best in the city. After a bit of a wait you'll receive a hot, thick, pie covered in a ton of gooey cheese. It is so delicious it will make you forget that the polar bears are dying in the artic.

While you wait for the incredible pizza. You might as well have a snack. You're going to order the spinach and artichoke queso. It is incredible and just the perfect size to eat while you wait. 

If for some reason you dont want one of their incredible pizzas, they have a great selection of burgers and sandwiches, and of course what kind of British establishment would they be if there was no Fish and chips.
Been a couple times to watch a ball game nice place service has been good. And it's close.

So I don't know why the spot is so famous for their food. 
I came here Saturday night I want to say an hour before they closed and the food was OK. We had to wait on a table the lady said about 25 minutes but we got seated pretty fast which is a good thing. I ordered the Cajun pasta with chicken and my boyfriend got the red beans and rice with fried chicken and we got the oysters as an appetizer. This place is definitely a tourist trap. My pasta was dry and it was warm not even hot, the chicken for the pasta was very salty I had to take it back to the waiter I didn't get the picture of the first one but this is the picture of the second plate after they brought it out again and as you can see it is very oily they put a lot of sauce on it the presentation was terrible the bread was cold and stale. I work in food service so I know when it is closing time you are trying to hurry up and get customers out but at the same time you could at least make sure the guess has quality food. The red beans and rice was cold but my boyfriend ate it because he was hungry. The oysters was very salty and warm. I don't understand how they came off the grill warm.  We also got an order of french fries and the first time they were undercooked so we had to get a whole new order.The decor in there is very old the chair that we got seated on the cushion was peeling off which was very uncomfortable and the seat was so low from the table. If I ever come back to New Orleans this place will be the last place I will eat from.

Disappointed at the quality of the food and show that my boyfriend's family and I received for the NYE Murder Mystery "3 course meal" Magic Show. The main act by the Mostly Magnificent Steve was poorly designed-- it had no plot, the jokes and "magic tricks" were hardly funny or entertaining. The food was underwhelming as the vegan 3-course meal (a salad, tofu entree, and 3 slices of fruit for dessert) probably was only 150 calories and not filling to say the least. The last acts by two other magicians were okay, but they didn't make up for the extreme cost of ~$100 a person for this show. The balloon drop concluded of only about half of the balloons actually falling and they fell maybe 3 feet. We expected much more from this show for what was paid for, I don't recommend you buy tickets for your family or anyone you know.

I love this place!!!!!

I love the flat breads and wine selection. Everyone there is really knowledgeable and I can't wait to do a wine a dinner party here. 

Request MJ as your server she's super friendly and on top of it. 

Super happy Brandon has a great restaurant like boca , I always find something to eat there

I thought I finally  found the one place I was looking for in Nashville to come every Sunday to eat seafood. But after the 3rd time (the salmon was good every time btw) I don't think I'd go back. All 3 times I asked for limes or lemons and got the same response "we forgot to get it this morning" which wasn't a big deal. but the last time I had a late lunch  there (about 3 weeks ago) THEY DID NOT HAVE SALT, AT ALL, ANYWHERE IN THE RESTAURANT! I mean... what kind of restaurant runs out of salt and thinks it's okay to go the day without it? Smh. I algo have to agree with the other reviews, the attitudes from the girls working the register is not the best, they will not acknowledge you while waiting in line more less smile.
Nice place. Very crowded on Tuesdays! Avoid the crowd and get food delivered by UberEats. Download the UberEats app and enter code UE-uaduw for $10 off first order!

They have inside and outside seating and outside is first come first serve so it can be awfully busy.   We had gator for an app and it was really good.  Things kinda went down hill from there.  The main entrees came out very slow and neither dish was really that great.  Nice atmosphere outside and not so great inside. I recommend that next time you go you sit at the bar and get a few apps and drink your dinner because it will be cheaper, more fun and you won't leave disappointed

Poor excuse for a business. We sat there for 30 min and never was acknowledged. Two different wait staff passed by us but never stopped to take our order. It was busy the night we were there but to never get acknowledged is poor business. 

We did go back at 11 am a few days later. They weren't busy as they had just opened. We had a very nice gentleman that waited on us and the pizza was good. I advise to go early if you want good service to go along with the good pizza.

I stayed at the chloe for a few nights and it was wonderful! Very eclectic and unique vibe, comfy room, EXCEPTIONAL service, and delicious food! It's in a beautiful part of the city, and there is a streetcar stop right outside the hotel that can take you downtown to the french quarter and uptown towards tulane. Plus, it's only half a mile north of magazine street.

Quick recap:

-          Food: Poor
-          Portion size: Average
-          Service: Order at the counter; Nice Staff
-          Environment: Fast taqueria
-          $: Low
-          Perks: N/A

More details:

Went there for lunch. Most tacos are below $3. It is pretty obvious that the ratings are driven by the prices.
Quality is not there.
The staff is nice though.

Overall?

Except if you really are looking for the "cheapest options around"... These tacos are not worth it, and definitely not worth another 30min wait.

Dropped in while traveling through Edmonton.  The food arrived quickly, but my wife's burger was very cold, and my chicken burger was overly deep fried (making it fairly dry and very crunchy).  You have to ask for ketchup because they keep it behind the counter and don't automatically give it to you-- then they ask how much you want and give an odd look if they feel like you're asking for too much.  The washrooms were a bit dirty, but not too bad.  Surprisingly, the washrooms didn't have change tables for babies-- odd for a place that has an area for children to play.  Definitely not the best Burger King I've visited.

All around this place is just great and a wonderful, needed addition to Main Street.  
The store itself is clean and fresh looking, all white with stainless steel appliances and counters it feels airy and open.  Not to mention that they keep it spotless.  The menu is easy to read, and even with a line you don't feel cramped.  The employees are sweet, and patient (there are lots of choices so you may need some time or some help!) and full of advice or recommendations if you need it.  
One of my favorite things is that they have a little grab and go area with pre-made cold pressed juice, some salads yogurt and other things.  I loved that I could come in for a smoothie but grab a green juice for breakfast the next day.  
Speaking of the green juice, the Kale with a Kick is probably the best one I have ever had.  Sweet from the green apple but not too sweet, and a little spicy from the jalapeno.  It met a perfect balance and when eaten along with a banana made the perfect quick breakfast in the morning.  The other items in the grab and go section looked great and I'll definitely be stopping back to pick up some more. 
I was a little disappointed they did not have the stuff to make the whips with, but at the same time I guess it shows they use only fresh things.  Oh well, next time.  My Simply Green Smoothie was perfect - large, cold and fresh.  It was delicious and filling.  I added flax seed at the suggestion of the girl serving me and it was great.  Though they are a little steep at $7+ for a smoothie they are filling enough to be a meal.  All of the smoothies looked great and I cannot wait to try some different ones! 
All in all you should definitely stop in here and grab something healthy and fresh to nosh on!

Pretty neat mom and pop shop. Food was pretty good (cheese pizza and cannolis).  

Restaurant was pretty dirty.
You can't go wrong. I would have to rate it as one of the top ten most impressive restaurants I have ever eaten at. It is somewhat pricey, but you are guaranteed an amazing meal and fun experience.

As a taco lover, I have tried many places in Philly for the best of the best, and I have to say, this place had THE best steak tacos I have ever had. The place was wonderful, small but great environment. Staff members are very polite and with the amazing food, this has become my favorite taco place in Philly!

This place is off the chain good! Steak had a good caramelization. Inside very juicy and tender. This is the New York. Actually put a little butter on steak sorry! Great selection of wine was offered as well.

Will never get a dime of my $. Walked to the front entrance at 8:05 pm on Monday 3/23/2021. The woman that was at the guest stand was speaking to another customer that was asking how long the wait on a to go order and she responded they were full. I literally saw not one customer inside, coming in or leaving! I saw her and the bar tender who btw wasn't making drinks for all those invisible patrons. I believe they forgot the upstairs is completely viewable from the street level & it was also empty. My best guess is the upstairs was full of paying ghosts & You had to be a certain skin tone to be seated! Imagine that in New Orleans.

Wow where to begin!!!! Destiny was a FANTASTIC server. Started off with a Bloody Mary and I was NOT disappointed, maybe one of the best bloody Mary's I have ever had. Then got the scotch eggs...... I was weary at first but so happy I got them! They were by far my favorite thing I ate that day. You gotta try this place it was AWESOME!

Cook: how's the Jam (Jambalaya)?
Me: it's really fucking good
Cook: yea I put a lotta love into that one

This kitchen makes some of the best food I've ever had, I'd eat here at least once a week if i lived in New Orleans. The jambalaya is the best I've ever had... piping hot, spicy and made with heart. 

The most rare experience you can have as a foodie is having something that tastes home cooked, as if your aunt is cooking specifically for you, putting her love and affection into the meal;  that's how I feel whenever I eat the food from Marie's, like I'm home away from home. Whoever was smart enough to start a kitchen there and hire the cooks they did has succeeded far beyond what they hoped for, I assume. To pay $8 for a  bowl of 
Jam that good is a treat.

Been ordering here for 6 years and it's the only Chinese place I will order from in Philly. Consistently delicious, always quick, kind, and clean. This is the only one, folks. 

Recs: hot and sour soup, wontons, chicken and veg, veg only, and obviously the fried dumplings with extra sauce and hot chili oil.

This food was so good and the wait from ordering to being ready was fast. They give you a lot of meat and the staff was super friendly. It's a little food truck but there's a decent amount of parking so you shouldn't have a hard time finding it. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because I also ordered the lemonade and I'm not sure how they made it but I couldn't even get half way through it. But the food gets 5 stars if you're in the area it's definitely worth checking out for real authentic tacos.

Been a few years since had been there. Took my wife for her birthday and we both thought both the service and food was excellent. My steak was done just as ordered and nice piece of meat and the salmon my wife had seemed very fresh and served with just the right amount of side items.
We will be planning on going back again....

I stopped by here after the free evening yoga class for a healthy dinner. It was walking distance and the perfect place to eat out and still feel great. 

I ordered the Rise & Shine. It was a nice, fresh salad that didn't bore me. I especially liked the quinoa, sweet potatos, and bacon along with a side of mashed avocado. For protein, the bowl comes with 2 poached eggs. I added chicken for $2 and they seasoned it well and it came out tender. My friend got plantains from across the street at the Jamaican restaurant and I added some to the salad to give it a nice natural sweetness.

I like the concept of quick and fresh healthy meals here. However, the downside is the cost.

Great restaurant. Great atmosphere surrounded by a neighborhood with a rich culture and history.   This only adds to the most important component - THE FOOD, and it doesn't disappoint.  It delivers in a flavorful and creative fashion.  The dusted wings are some of the best wings I have ever had anywhere in the country.  I travel extensively for my job so I LITERALLY  mean anywhere in the country.  The Gumbo is authentic - the most discerning Louisiana taste buds would approve.  

I would absolutely say try this restaurant, you won't be disappointed.
Wow! This place had amazing service and even better food! I would eat here every week if I lived in St. Louis!
Chicken cordon blue Sammie, Mac & chz with andouille sausage special order.  All very tasty

Read the Yelp reviews, and were impressed so we decided to try it out. Hidden gem across from St Pete's beach. We ate big for 2 as we are land locked in Georgia and were dying for some seafood, and sought out a new place. We are relo'ing here next year, and Amanda, who grew up here, took the time to talk with us about different areas around St. Pete's - what a great ambassador for the area, and we hadn't even ordered yet.  Were we amazed! Had the wasabi blackened tuna appetizer with the fisherman's platter and blackened grouper with andouille etouffe. Incredible - all of it. Almost didn't get the fisherman's platter because my eyes glazed over the name of it - typically "fisherman's platter" means a plate of fried pre-prepared frozen stuff which is terrible, but this was all fresh caught. Sat outside, was a great vibe with incredible service, we will be coming back at least a few more times this week - thanks to Amanda and the great food at Snapper's Sea Grill!

Nice and beautiful place, top notch service and the food was Amazing! The drinks are about 5 dollars more expensive but we are in fishers. The bartender Chris was our server, he was friendly and help us decide of the best pork chop I have ever eaten...such a wonderful experience..We will return.
I really like the quesadillas here but after finding a dirty band-aid in our food tonight, we will never be back.

This place was great! Our server, Steve, was very attentive and helped us with the menu. He has great enthusiasm and loves what he does. A+ service. Now to the food, food was amazing, everything came out hot and fresh. I got the smoked salmon Benedict, forgot the actual name. But it was very good. I also ordered the chicken and waffles to share with the table. Be sure to get the Nashville sauce on the side, cause it's pretty spicy. It has some maple syrup added into the hot sauce, so you get this nice sweet and spicy sauce you can dip with.  Which I prefer over having my whole chicken dipped in it. They also have pitchers of mimosas for about $23.99. Pretty good too. Overall, great place for breakfast/ brunch. I will be coming back.

I can understand why this place does well, and I really appreciate its existence. It's super cute and so I was lured in for my second visit last weekend. The inside is bustling and smoky on the weekends, but the subway tiles and chalkboard menus are very charming. I tried to snag an empty seat while my boyfriend ordered, but was rudely told by a man working there that it was taken, when no one (nor coat, purse, etc) was in sight. I was put off a bit, but we found seating in the back.

The fritatta bagel is pretty good. It has jam on it, with the egg and turkey bacon, which I thought would be better. I know this is Montreal-style, and I'm open to new flavors, but it was more "okay" than "wow". Also, I know the bagels are wood fired, but ours were about half black, and looked like ones that possibly should not have been served. The eggs were cooked amazing though, and I kept finding bits of yellow yolk reminders on my fingers throughout the day.

The sidewalk area is cute, though it was too cold to sit for long. There were a couple people playing live music outside and children dancing, which was endearing. Inside, a woman had her small dog at the table and it kept barking loudly. Mind you, I absolutely love dogs, but I would never bring mine inside a bagel restaurant to sit at my table, especially if it was loud. I feel like someone should have said something, but oh well.

If everyone could try Vedge, there would be more vegetarians.  
I'm convinced.  People just limit their ideas of vegetarian options.  The creativity in flavors, the beautiful plating, served in a tapas style menu makes Vedge one of a kind.  It's incredibly difficult to reserve a table, so go with V Street (same group) if no tables.  If you can get in though, it's worth the slightly higher price point.  It's still not on the bouchy vegetarian side so don't be deterred.  I really recommend the rutabaga soft pretzel and smoked potato.  Oh, and the desserts.  Save room.  Trust me.

Price: Expensive, but better than the kbbq in chinatown. 
Food Taste: Galbi is Satisfying and delicious.
Parking: Plenty in the lot.
People: Asian, hipster. 
Staff: In a hurry, really busy all the time. 
Place: New and modern and relatively big. 

Bottom-line: I would come back, but rarely. If the price was cheaper, I would come back frequently.

Horrible! I came here the first time and loved it. The second time, the saucy was watered down and chips were over salted. The meat came out burned. The tortillas were crunchy. Very disappointed and will never return. I suggest you try a different place.

I ordered take out for lunch and was not that impressed with it. My office has great reviews for this place so I was looking forward to it but I don't think I'll order again from there.  However, I'm willing to try it at the restaurant next because many of the reviews are pretty good and some of the photos look really good. 


I got the lunch combo meal that comes with an entree, side , chips and salsa and a soda.  For the entree I ordered pork tacos on corn tortillas and the side I opted for was a salad. 

The pork in the tacos were shredded and marinated in a sauce but the pork was pretty dry still.  They were topped with melted cheese. The chips and salsa where forgotten as part of my order. I didn't notice until I was at the office so I just had to deal with it and eat what I had. No a big deal really but the salsa would have helped me the pork not as dry as it was. 

The side salad was more of a colesalw because it was shredded lettuce and drowning in dressing. I tasted some cilantro and that was the best part of it. I ordered salad thinking it was a healthier choice but no, I would have been better off with the rice and beans because it was soaked in mayo-based dressing. I think I'll try their rice and beans because my co-workers were all happy with theirs.
I love this style of restaurant. The quality of the food is great but the service i got both times i was there was exceptional. Tucson needed a place like this. Hope it's here to stay.

The food was good. I think the best part about this restaurant is that you can select your own stir fry and have it prepared in front of you. They give you a variety of items to choose from including fish and shrimp. The Chinese buffet is also quiet good. I would return. BTW they offer coupons on groupon.

Went on a Saturday for lunch and had an awful experience here. Sure it was busy in terms of half the tables were full but I don't think I'll be coming back.
The first time I came I had their triple AAA set where they put your meat on a hot stone and it comes with miso soup, rice, and I think pickles. It was pretty great! But when I tried to order the same thing on my second visit, the waitress clarified that for the same price you would only get the meat without any sides. This is a really strange change which is not updated on their website's menu.
The tables were sticky and stained, the water was only refilled ONCE as we were paying our bill and leaving, and the food took about twenty minutes to arrived. My whole table ordered altogether but the last person's food came fifteen minutes after the first. 
We had to get our own cutlery and plates since the waitress barely came to our table. When the sushi was served, we had to walk over to the entrance where we spotted chopsticks and plates. I've never been to a restaurant where I needed to get my own cutlery...is this how Dorinku operates?
Food was a 3/5 overall. Only thing I really liked was the salmon pressed sushi.

Really cool place ,but a bit spendy. The hot rock fillet is awesome and so is just about everything else i have tried there before. The remodel has got the place quite loud .Not the place to go if you want a quite dinner with the wife .But other then that i would no complaints.

Doesn't serve lunch all day like other chick fil a . Shorted us on sauce and dressing for the salad. Come on great service until lately. We went back to the window to ask for what they left out order was $50+ they gave us 2 sauces and a mayo. After arguing said they were out of sauce. Wtf

Just a great place, simple menu, very delicious. The Bloody Marys are very good! The staff is very friendly, and there is always a place to sit, no wait at all. Please don't come here and make it all hype and packed.

Oh Casamentos you are so dang delicious! Brought my family, visiting from the Midwest, for some amazing oysters and they didn't leave disappointed! 

Started with 2 dozen raw and 1 dozen chargrilled. The little sister who is new to the oyster eating experience was raving about the chargrilled goodness. The rest of us couldn't stop eating the divine raw oysters. So fresh and plump and juicy! 

I would've been happy with anther two dozen oysters but the fam wanted to sample some loafs... We ordered shrimp and catfish and a shrimp dinner and lots of beers. Much happiness was had by all.  

Docking one star because I wish the oysters had been cleaned a bit better and our waitress was slooooooow to bring the bill despite asking for it.
My favorite hibachi restaurant of all time. Food quality is great, nice atmoshpere, and great service!

The food was decent, our wait was long but that's because I was there for a conference. I really loved the salad, just the plain house salad kinda blew my mind. I also got a sausage pizza of some sort but really didn't enjoy it because of how it's constructed with massive pounds of sauce on top.... I prefer massive pounds of cheese.... Sooo that really wasn't my fav and ended up giving it to my friend and ordering another earth shattering salad, which was probably better for my waistline anyways. I would go here again if I were back in town and I would just try and order something less saucy

Had our first boiled crawfish and fried shrimp, fish and crab cake, coleslaw and fries. The crawfish was tasty, but a lot of work.The fried fish and chips was very tasty. The crab cake was so so. Overall, food was very good.

This shop is very welcoming! It is set up as a tasting room and I love the concept of try-before-you-buy. 
The staff member that helped me was attentive and very informative. They even had recipes to go along with the oils and vinegars I purchased. I love the combination of Meyer Lemon Olive Oil and Huckleberry Balsamic Vinegar. My favorite is the Honey Ginger Balsamic which I put on everything...omelettes, chicken, vegetables, etc.

I can't speak on the menu in its entirety but what I can tell you is how I had two frozen mango margaritas yesterday and I was litty kitty by the time I left. I don't know if it was because I only had chips and queso as my only  meal for the whole day but it was the best bang for my buck.

Their mango puree is fresh and the only reason I knew is because I would be able to taste the actual pulp in my drink. The queso can be topped with chorizo and there's even a back patio.

Solid bang for your buck and if you're coming for drinks and a small nibble you can't go wrong here.

V Street has a tantalizing menu, and nearly all the dishes I have tasted continue to vividly remain on my mind.  I like V Street more than Vedge because she is the more adventurous, approachable dining spot, but both kitchens spin out the same joyful dishes and superb service.  I am so grateful to have this vegan restaurant in Philadelphia because it truly is one-of-a-kind and unique--I continue to frequent V Street (several times per month) and order the same dishes over and over again.  Said dishes include the grilled tofu skewers, jerk trumpet mushrooms, and dan dan noodles.  This is truly delicious food that satisfies both the body and spirit.

Had the Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup and Vegetarian Pad Ke Mo at level 5. I love spicy food and this was the perfect spice level for me. The tom yum soup was delicious and I am craving more as I write this. Very light and veggie full. The drunken noodles portion was huge and I took most of it home to finish. Looking forward to going back and trying more dishes.

edit: went back and had the tom yum soup at level 5 again. My tablemate got his curry at a level 6 which he had gotten before too. And my esophagus felt like it was burning in a hellish fire. I didn't want to complain but god damn. I love love the food, but somehow their spice level wasn't consistent to the other couple times I've been there.

I won't lie: the only reason I set foot in Chipotle was because I received a "buy one, get one free" coupon and figured that was enough of an incentive to give the place a try. Don't get me wrong, I don't have anything against the place, but despite living within spitting distance of the place (yum?), I'd never frequented it simply because I don't really do fast food.

I guess the obvious comparison to make is between this and Qdoba (where I admit that I have eaten MANY times in the past). I think that for the money, Chipotle is the better pick simply because the ingredients seem fresher, which is probably reflected in the relatively slimmer menu at Chipotle. Rather than overwhelming you with myriad options, you pretty much decide whether you want a burrito, a burrito bowl, tacos (soft or hard), salad, or tacos. The filling choices are the same for all of them (chicken, steak, barbacoa, carnitas, or veggies) and everything costs about $6.25. It seems like Chipotle has decided to focus on providing the best product possible, so while eating here every day would probably get boring, what you do get tastes pretty good. Also, the portions are HUGE. A single burrito will probably get you through the day because the amount they manage to cram into a flour tortilla (how do they do it?!?) is enough to feed a small family... or the average American, I suppose.

The first time I came, I got the carnitas burrito, which was sufficiently good that my husband and I decided to come back. I think the barbacoa burrito is probably my favorite - the meat is juicy and nicely spiced. We both splurged and got guac on our burritos, and while $1.25 for this add in (the only one you have to pay for) may seem pricey, it was well worth it because this guacamole is muy delicioso. That said, if not for the coupon we had, two burritos and one drink would have cost us nearly $19... which seems kind of insanely expensive for fast food in my mind. Sure this is a healthier choice than a lot of other places, but for $20 there are a lot of other (non-fast food) places I'd hit up first before coming back here. It's a decent choice if you need to eat and run or really want a burrito, but in my mind, it's not a huge game changer.

Terrible place arrived at 4pm for happy hour group of 6. They tell me they ran out of happy hour chardonnay had to buy a glass of chardonnay for 10 dollars awesome.  Then order the chicken tacos.  Arrived 3 tiny soft shell w half or less teaspoon of chicken no flavor then we are seated by the kitchen the cook is texting w his gloves on for cooking food totally nasty. I asked the server for cheeks took her 30 minutes to get them. Very noisy place. The sliders that others order looked like something out of a fast food joint.  Probably one of the worst places to visit.  The only bright side was the guy serving outside was fabulous.  Thanks us.

I had no idea this hole in the wall existed... but now that I do I can't go a day without going! I've been there literally every day this week, and have loved every day more than the day prior! The staff is delightful and accommodating, they were so patient with me when I started coming through and had no clue how to navigate the menu (Which can seem intimidation because of how many fantastic options and combinations there are, but just start off by checking the specials board! Once you're more comfortable with the styles of drinks, the fun of customizing your own drink is a significantly more simple process) Do yourself a favor and skip the Shmarbucks line by stopping here instead!

Stopped here after a golf game and it was amazing!!!! Found it on Yelp and SO glad we did.  The fried Macaroni and Cheese was beyond spectacular! We live in Ellenton and I will be back here.  Awesome selection of  craft beer and some good local ones.  Highly recommend this place.   Glad I didn't pay heed to any of the negative comments or I would have missed out on a great meal!  Ps: Service was great - no issues.

I absolutely love the chicken here and apparently so does everyone else! My daughter and I pulled up about 8:30 pm on Friday night figuring the dinner crowd would be long gone. I planned on just going through the drive thru. Well was I wrong! There were 12 cars in the drive thru and the parking lot was full! We decided to go inside and order and had  to park in an adjacent parking lot.  But if you have a hankering for fried chicken  you'll go the extra mile and wait it out. The chicken strips here are always cooked perfectly, especially for a fast food joint.  Tonight as always the chicken was tender and moist and the breading was absolutely perfect! We both got the box dinner which includes bread, coleslaw and fries. And who can eat here and not love the garlic Texas Toast? It's outstanding and the cole slaw is just the way I like, sweet, crisp and not to tart. The fries are what I would consider your typical everyday fast food fries, nothing to rave about. Customer service here has also always been great, and they give military discount.  I would have given a "five" rating today, but the tables were very dirty between customers and the turn around to clean them and stock the condiments was definitely behind. I'm sure this was due to how busy they were but cleanliness is really important, especially during this record flu season. I will definitely be back!

Legacy Kitchen is my kind of place.  It couldn't be anymore "me". Allow me to explain. It's super laid back, the decor is so cool it's almost indescribable and the food is out of this world.

We ordered room service from here and we were so blown away by the Duck Debris Fries we went the next day for lunch just to taste those again. My guy loves loaded cheese fries. I mean, LOVES them. When they're on the menu, he's getting them and it is saying a lot to have him declare that these are the best he's ever had. They are hand cut, salty, chili, cheesey, duck and crawfish loaded goodness and you should get these in your mouth sooner rather than later. I'm serious.

The space is so perfect. There are ample televisions to watch football and huge windows to people watch on Girod and Tchoupitoulas if that's more your style.

The burger here is legit, but I'd skip the nachos. Enjoy!

We came back here after a long break. I have been so busy trying out so many new places and I wanted some comfort food so I came back to Mi Quang again. I didn't think it was possible but it taste even better than before. If you're tired of the same old Vietnamese food like pho or rice then come try this.

Mi quang is central Vietnamese noodle dish with many complex flavor. The dish is composed of shrimps and pork ribs that's been marinated and cooked separately before coming together in the bowl. It also comes with quail eggs and Vietnamese ham. The noodles are flat and very soft yet retains elasticity and does not fall apart. 

Another highlight here is their bun cha Ha Noi, which is a northern dish. It is lemon grass pork and pork patty grilled and is marinated in sweet sweet sauce with scallion oil and daikon radish before coming out to be served with a side of vermicelli noodles and vegetables. The grilled pork has an amazing charred flavor to it. The patty has the texture of a tender meatball and is packed with lemongrass flavor in every bite. If you are here, make sure you get these 2 items first before anything else, make it a priority, they are the best in the east coast!!

Nope. Please save your money and go to another stop at the airport. The service was good (speedy, friendly), but the burrito I purchased fell apart in my hands after two bites. It was actually okay because the burrito was soggy, and the tortilla and all the contents in the burrito were very bland. The chips were stale too. $12 gone, and disappointed.
This place has the best oxtails I have ever eaten! Desserts are out of this world. Especially the guava cheesecake! And smoked Gouda Mac and cheese to die for!

Came here about 8 years ago to try this new place we found, still quality ingredients still just as good as ever
They've grown they now have three locals way super cool
I concur with other yelpers best pizza hands down

First time I have eaten there, and these tacos were unpretentious, simple but very delicious! The chipotlado taco was smoky, cheesy with just the right amount of heat, and the carnitas taco was distinctively a different flavor than the al pastor, which was rare in my experience.
