If you're going to charge me premium prices you better not serve me the same potatoes I can get at a hotel buffet, and my English Muffin is supposed to be toasted.

Nice waiter, not so nice food. We love to eat Vietnamese food and do so often in Philadelphia.  We were very excited to read about Pho Tan.  It sounded great. 

However, the food did not live up to our expectations.  Frankly, it was not very flavorful or fresh-- both qualities that we associate with Vietnamese food.  We ordered the Pho and Bahn Mi as well as a starter of Summer Rolls.  The Summer Rolls were cold, almost frozen.  The Bahn Mi was the best thing but could use some more meat and veggies.  The Pho had very little meat, four thin pieces in a large bowl of bland broth.  At the end of a disappointing meal we order what might have been the worst bubble tea we've ever had. 

Maybe it was an off night...

I went today Saturday night around 11:30. The place was packed,however I just wanted a six pack to go. The bartenders needed some more training. I paid $11.75 which was not bad at all for Budweiser. However the bartender forgot I have her $20 in cash. It was a process I definitely won't be going there to hangout.

Wow! This place is the first place in Tucson we've tried for Indian, and it did not disappoint. Came here on a Groupon and will be back! We had the appetizer sampler and the Chicken Tikka Masala and Lamb Vindaloo. Both were perfect in terms of flavor and spice. The Chai was legit, felt like I was back in south India - tasted like the chai from the local street vendors. The ambience is calming and peaceful. Check this place out!

I wanted to try the Philly cheesesteak, but I'm not a fan of cooked green peppers,, and they said the meat, onions and peppers were all pre prepped combined. So I chose the steak Stromboli sandwich and side of potato wedges. Portion size was ample. It was served piping hot and still was by the time I got home. The bread, tons of cheese, mushrooms and sauce were wonderful. The steak burger reminded me of a frozen patty you get from Costco. It was tasty but the weakest part of the sandwich. Still, overall it was good and I would be interesting in trying wings or pizza. #ReviewsByRL
Korean food is delicious in general. I can't say because I haven't had a lot of Korean food but this place was great. Also the workers/ owners are so nice that it makes the food taste better.

Consistently good food. The pitaco is a great plus to the menu especially for veggie lovers. It's a pita  layered with hummus, cucumbers, alphafa sprouts and feta. It's definitely worth trying. The pizza is good with lots of options. I like the spicy chicken. Not too spicy just enough for flavor. 

Five stars for consistency with food and service! More stars for delivery!!

Taqueria Veracruzanna used to be my absolute favorite. Lately my meals here have been lackluster at best. 

The quality of the ingredients must have gone down or they are too busy and the food especially the beans and rice have gone way down hill.

The waitstaff is really slow and you may die of thirst waiting for your beverage, especially if you just order water.

Go to El Jarocho, or any other awesome place in the area.

I really like this place! I've been a few times and had good experiences each time. The service is good and they have always gotten our food done really quick.

Last time, I had the grilled cheese with caramelized onions and it was FIRE. I'll def go back and get that again.

Portions aren't huge, so go with the bigger size if they suggest a half order.

About 7-8 years ago, Ginza was our favorite sushi in Indy ... but until our takeout order on Christmas Eve, we hadn't visited in several years.  Could be that our tastes have changed or their sushi has slipped in quality, I don't know, but Ginza sushi is just average at this point.

Everything was a half step up from good grocery store sushi - I don't *necessarily* mean that in a negative way as it's definitely workable in a pinch.  Caterpillar, Inside Out Philly, and Rainbow rolls were all between 3 and 3.5 stars.  The smoked salmon nigiri was not top quality fish and a bit chewy, 2.5 stars.  The shrimp shumai (off appetizer menu) were a little dried out but were a slightly above average version, 3.5 stars.

Simply put, there are better options.  On the west side, I'd much rather hit Ocean World on W 86th, Hirosaki in Avon, or Tegry Bistro in Brownsburg.  Sorry Ginza, I think it's time for us to disappear for another few years ...

Great addition to grand!!!  Best wine list on grand and yes the vegetarian food is great and I am not a veggie... Yum. Start with the fried beets and move thru the menu the chorizo tamale is soooooooo good just go ahead and try it. In the mood for a steak... No steak here but oooooooohhhh the tree house Wellington will fill u up and u will love the mash potatoes!!! Go now

Amber has the best Indian food in the U.S.! My husband and I have been to other Indian restaurants in Chicago, Seattle, Portland and so far none came close to the creamy goodness that's in our favorite dishes in Amber. Our favorites are: Malai Kofta, Vegetable Korma, Chicken Tikka Masala.  The Malai Kofta stands out because of the creaminess and surprise sweetness from the grapes. It's definitely good to the last drop.  I am definitely going to miss this restaurant!

I went there last Sunday (1/10) for breakfast before working the boat show at Music City Center. I was there a little after 10am, and it was the small crowd I'd expect at almost any place on a cold Sunday morning downtown. The place had an instant "hipster vibe" to it. The kind of place a bunch of friends opened on a whim and had it actually be a success.
The ordering system is a bit odd, in my opinion. I looked for a wall-mounted menu, but found you had to grab a laminated copy from the counter. I went for a menu, and was asked if I was ready to order. I mentioned I'd never been there before, and the response was just, "Oh, ok!". Cheerful, though.
I decided on the whole wheat pancakes with farm eggs and turkey sausage, with a black coffee. I only partially enjoy the idea to pay up front, but here you're still served your food, unlike a place where you pick it up yourself. Having paid up front I'd added a small tip, not realizing there was still someone bringing the food out. Was I supposed to tip twice? How can I know if it was worth the tip? The one who took my order was not so welcoming. You'd have thought it was 5am. I tried to get him to smile, and was barely able to.. The one who brought me my food was much nicer.
As for the food: it was good. I'm not sure if it's a "thing" to put food on plates almost too small for it, but I did my best to not make a mess. I ate the sausage and eggs first to make room to scoot the pancakes over. The "house-made syrup" was way, way too runny. I use just pure maple syrup at home, and wished that were the case, here.
Overall it was a nice breakfast. Really just the process was a bit foreign to me, but I'm sure it just takes getting used to.

Great, unique atmosphere! Not another boring chain restaurant. Good prices and very good food. Never too crowded. Great place for a lunch meeting or to watch a game. 
The Smothered Chicken is amazing and if you love a great tenderloin, you can't go wrong with the Hoosier Daddy! Generous portions and friendly staff. Also, if you're there on a Wednesday, you get a free, straight out of the oven cookie for desert. Kind of a nice touch. Great place!

I like to think I'm a breakfast connoisseur.  This place has blown my mind. Best grits ever, hands down. Best breakfast burrito ever, hands down... Etc etc. It's really a special place to indulge in culinary mastery.

No bueno!!! This is very much a tourist spot....and because of location, I probably should have known better. But...we tried it anyway. 
Im sure tourists love the bland/watered down creole menu but I was quite disappointed. Hate to give bad reviews but I wont be back.

This is definitely my favorite pita place in the area! It's family run and everything I've had has been aboslutely incredible. I really suggest trying their arepa's. I am a big fan of pitas BUT i'll take their arepa's any day!!! Their falafel is really good but they have delicious options of meat/beans/rice/plantains as well to try. I love their grape leaves and empanadas as well (they have like 8 different empanadas and ALL have been delicious- but note, they're fairly small empanadas). They make a green hot sauce as well that i really suggest grabbing (for those spicy lovers!)- goes great with the empanada's but much like Betty White, i'll put that shiiz on everything! They have a couple different sauces aside from that one and all are good, but my favorite is their lemon/oil sauce that's not always out- so just ask! They offer several desserts too...some of the best Baklava i've had!! The service is great too such a nice and friendly family...i've gone  here about 100 times and every time the service and food has been consistently suberb! :)

Can't comment on the food quality as my husband and I have been waiting for 40 minutes and still not received our order (with only 4 people ahead of us when we ordered). We have had faster service at full on sit down restaurants and are now going to be late for an appointment thinking this was a somewhat fast food joint. I'm not sure if this is typical or not but it would take a lot for me to eat here again if this is their normal speed.

I know, I know..."who eats Thai food when they go to New Orleans!?"  We were in town for nearly two weeks and having lived in New Orleans for several years and having visited many times (both before and after being a resident) one tends to "branch out".

Sukho Thai did not disapoint!  Food was fresh and VERY tasty and the service was great.

But be forewarned..."Medium Hot" is pretty damn hot, so order accordingly!  I can't even imagine what "Hot" and "Thai Hot" categories are like?  Yikes!
I had a great time at Joey B's the staff was friendly and food was good. Definitely would recommend this place.

Just stopped here for lunch and we had the Chirashi bowl and it was fantastic. The rice was perfectly cooked and seasoned all for a reasonable price.  The green tea was also very authentic green tea not the fake stuff you typically see.   This is definitely Japanese owned and their sushi is the real deal here.

Not the quality of the San Francisco location. 

I was very excited to see that Patxi's had come to Santa Barbara and had loved the prior pizzas from one of their other locations. 

The service left a lot to be desired. We waited about 25 minutes for 2 beers and had to talk to three different servers and 2 of the managers (who asked us again what our drinks are) to finally get our beers. Our pizza took about 40 minutes and just wasn't at the quality it should have been. 

We shared a large 14" deep dish "Favorite" pizza. A few minutes after we ordered, our server came by asking if we were sure we didn't want the smaller 12" pizza. The crust was stale, mushy, and crunchy, and the dough tasted old. 

The lights were trendy, but flickering every few seconds and completely distracting.

I was completely surprised our beers weren't comped because of the horrible delay. I will be coming back to try again in a month or two once things improve, as I know they can make good pizza, this time however, was not.

This was a local favorite and has a sister bar in Clearwater Beach.   Currently going through a big remodel.   I am sad to see that what was once outdoor covered seating has now been all closed in.   For me CSDH has lost some of its charm.   Has the feel now of any other restaurant.   Menu looks to be trimmed down in size but all the good items have been kept.    Still great food but for me not the same personality.

Husband and I had Domino's again last night after talking with the manager earlier last week... Pizza was deliciously perfect this time around! Order was hot when I showed up for carry out, the manager was up to date on the situation that occurred, had follow up for me regarding issues we had beside the pizza, and was very informative on the direction he wants to go with training his employees. I look forward to ordering this pizza again and hope it stays consistently this good...

Unacceptable. Paying 16 plus tax on some sub-par, unseasoned, UNCOOKED food. Sriacha buttermilk and Tabasco honey?!?! They must have forgot that too, no heat whatsoever. Had high hopes with all the comments saying they belong downtown. Saturday's are usually the A-team. They couldn't hack it downtown or SP.

Not bad. I ordered the fresh Mex bowl with steak. The steak was very tasty but the lettuce mix they used wasn't my favorite. It did not seem very fresh. All the other ingredients were very good. I particularly liked the chipotle sauce that the salad was served with.

We stopped by for lunch on Saturday and had a great experience.  We had the antipasto salad and pizza.  The food was wonderful and the service great.  Michelle, our waitress, definitely complemented our dining experience.

DO NOT GET TAKEOUT FROM THIS PLACE! 
I got the Gnocchi Bolognese and there's NO gnocchi! And their "meat sauce" taste worse than the stuff you buy in the jar at Publix! My Husband got Chicken Alfredo and for a 4$ up charge for chicken in it they literally gave him 4 pieces!! The only reason why I gave two stars was because the Alfredo sauce itself was decent!

I really wanted to like this place. My husband and I came here on a Friday night, it was popping and there was a long line out the door so we knew it was worth the wait. By the time we get to the counter to order with the chef who makes the food right in front of you, we had several different menu options flooding our mind. " would you recommend the tacos or the burritos" my husband asks " I don't know man, i've been working all day and now we're closed" The chef responded. WHAT! I was so disappointed by his response.. I checked the time and it was 9:45pm and Google showed Parrilla Grill closes at midnight.. so we guess what the best option is and sat down. Unfortunately my husband forgot to mention we don't eat meat and his taco salad had beef on it. He had to go back up to the mean chef and correct his order. "You don't eat meat" he asks in a rude tone. "No" my husband responds. 5 minutes later he sets the most basic salad down without saying a single word and walks away.. Wow. We are very disappointed with the service! We wont be back!

I walked in the door and it was like a scene out of Aminal House. All heads turned and stared. Nope. I don't live in the neighborhood and everyone knew it but this little bar on Morganford won me over with its better than average bar food and great people watching. By watching I mean staring at 98% of the bar wearing sports jerseys. Welcome to South City.

The meatball appetizer was awesome and the french fries were decent. My friend ordered a hamburger but sent it back to be cooked a little more after which she determined it was excellent. Good beer selection and casual friendly atmosphere once you settle in for a bit. Our waitress Olivia was great. Can't complain about the service at all. Very accommodating. I would go back again.

My husband and I walked here from TradeWinds - which is a beautiful sunset beach walk. The atmosphere at Jimmy B's is incredibly chill and inviting. We sat ourselves and were greeted almost immediately by staff. The beer is cold. The food is hot and SO DELICIOUS. We got hot shrimp as an appetizer and a bacon cheeseburger that I will dream about back home. Seriously! So good. So fun. We had a phenomenal time.  10/10 would recommend

I got one of your pita pit cards, after I asked about what it was.    it was explained and I said YES....    only to find out that it wasn't activated at this location.    
I will be back and this time I would like to have it activated.    please?
seems odd to go through the explanation and then not activate when I purchased.    I'll take it the person at the counter missed the memo.

If you are looking for a quick and tasty dessert at a dog-friendly location, you should check this place out.   They stand out with their selection of mini cupcakes that you can pair with a variety of drinks (coffee, tea, prosecco, etc) in a shot glass.   I tried their lemon (awesome), coconut (awesome), peanut butter chocolate (awesome) and blackout chocolate (can't get enough).  It's a great little place if you want something small and sweet.   In addition, you can order a "pup cake" for your dog - it involves peanut butter and bacon, so the dog I was walking gave it two paws up!

I think people claim to like this place cause it's in St. Louis. The food isn't very good and I think overpriced. Last time I was in there they wouldn't take a credit card. They had some scheme where if you didn't have cash it cost an extra couple of bucks. I was embarrassed. I'm not willing to give them another chance but maybe it's gotten better. It has been a while since I was in there.

Very affordable for the quality of food. byo makes it even better. the paparadelle with pork cheek wad so good. the gnocchi was good but I can't imagine only getting that because it's pretty rich. the waiter was kind to do half and half so I could try both. my friend had the chicken and the portion was large. the olives were a good choice as well

I know so many people here and have so many memories. I used to do shows at IBT's, even.

The drinks are always reliably strong - there is a regular crowd where "everybody knows your name," if you go often enough (oh yes, I did!).

Also, I recommend karaoke on weekends in the afternoon/evening. I still go when I visit. :)

I don't know what the night life is like there now, because I haven't stayed there very late the last few times I've been, but I do remember that out back was getting pretty straight girl and pop music/hip-hop, while inside was less busy until near the end of the night (where the dance/electronic stuff was played). Also my fav dj - Q - is gone now, but that's cool - things change.

Check it out!
The only place in town to find AUTHENTIC Lao cuisine!
Great service great food great beer. Overall awesome experience. Dog friendly and helpful waitstaff make this place over the top with your sit-down, mid-price range, Taphouse. A MUST SEE in tarpon

I had heard good things about this place but, truly, it is a tiny little hallway.  We went in there and it was jam packed, mega loud and total chaos.  I can't imagine how anyone would ever sit in there to eat unless maybe it was a weekday and totally dead and there were no customers.  If anyone came in to order and you were sitting at one of the table, they would be literally on top of you.  I have no idea about the food or drinks bc we left after a few minutes.

I was disappointed.   The service was GREAT and everyone was very friendly and helpful. The food was a letdown, though.  The fried chicken was average, the mac n cheese was good.  The cornbread was very SALTY!   No desire to return.

Thanks Hogie House for another great experience. 

I had called eegees for a party pack that I needed ASAP last weekend and they told me that I had to call it in 24 hours ahead. When I called Hogie House to see if they could  have 2 36in charmichaels ready to go within an hour and they told me ABSOLUTELY! They saved my life that day. Not to mention everyone at the party loved the sandwiches! SO good!!!! 

Thanks AGAIN! :-)

Just drinks but the atmosphere and service are top shelf. Old pharmacy building, , live stage (so disappointed I won't be here for the music).  Kayla R.  is an awesome bartender ( really enjoyed watching her mix drinks- the Anthym Spirit looks awesome) What more can a weary traveler ask for when looking for a spot to wet his whistle?
I think 312 refers to the number of minutes you'll wait before getting your food.

Be going here about 3 years every now and then. Drive thru line never too long. They are alway very nice happy and full of smiles. Food is warm and almost the order is always right. Inside bathrooms could use some better cleaning but all in all good store.

I work in Upper Darby and was in the office well past dinner. I wanted pizza but had ordered from various places in the area before (usually whoever left a flyer in my door last) and was unimpressed. The pizzas were either not good, too expensive, took too long to arrive or all the above. So this time I figured I'd go with Pizza Hut, the devil I knew. Well, they knocked my socks off. Pizza came within 30 minutes, piping hot, with a courteous, friendly driver. And for what PH pizza is, it was quite tasty. At 10 dollars for a medium with 2 toppings (13 bucks and change total, excluding tip) I felt I had paid a fair price for a solid pizza, delivered timely. Good job.
Amazing food, fast and cheap. Numerous "best if of philly". This place won't let you down.

OD is such an awesome part of South Philly!!!  I have some of the best memories of going here while on vacation as a child.  And I went frequently when I moved to Philly as an adult.

I love the veal parm, which is my favorite dish.  I love the dessert case.  I love the waitresses who range from old, crabby goodness to kind-hearted plush lovies (one of which I witnessed save a woman's life with a FIERCE Heimlich one moment and then turn right around to finish another table's order the next!).  

The service is fast.  The price ain't too shabby.  It's relatively easy to get to by car or public transpo.  And where else can you see a 4'6" Asian woman chase a 6'4" black man around the car her car, which he had just rear-ended??!!  No where, that's where!!!

CLASSIC!  I heart The Oregon Diner!!!!
Dragon ball z and fine dining japanese cuisine, yes!! Chill atmosphere and fast service. Food was delicate and fresh. Fatty tuna is a must. So glad to be in the neighborhood of this gem

Horrible slow service couldn't get a drink refill 
Waitress took two tables orders before ours that sat after us even though we ask to have our order taken also when I received my meal i got fries with it and it was literally 12 fries I received pitiful my wife and my son never got a refill in the hour and half we were there tried to charge us for items we didn't even receive never again will I come here plus I will tell anyone and everyone I know not to dine here 
You blew it  collinsville Dennys
Grate place with excellent service. The food is outstanding. Real European (Italian) style.

Jan 11 2015 we usually like the breakfast at the ricky's restaurants we had gone to before. The service was excellent friendly and fast.  me and my wife order the Belgium waffle with side of bacon. We got our coffee which was good. Then we waited for our waffles to come and they didn't take long. When we saw and expected to see a big fluffy Belgium waffles we were very surprised to see four small ego  like waffles. They tasted awful and were very greasy. We didn't get what was printed on the menu at all. They must have gotten frozen waffles and through them on a greasy flat top. We have gone to other ricky's before and had a good breakfast this one we will not return to.

Disgusting run of the mill pizza, I ordered two pies, my group ate their first slice, then we decided to toss the rest (no lie, we felt we were eating school cafeteria pizza).  Lucky I did try their subs which are actually very good.  But if you want pizza you might as well buy frozen before Pat's.  I give two stars in light of their good sub, which my experience with is limited...

I'm not sure why anyone would waste there time here if not for not for the raw and char-grilled oysters. The oysters were fresh, though they were rather muddy. At least when grilled some of the mud burns off so to speak. Their cocktail mixture was really good, but the worst part of this experience was the sour attitude of the bartender. Its not easy working in the service industry but I have zero appreciation for service with an attitude. We also ordered the blackened gator, which was not appetizing. If you do go, just stick to oysters.

Talk about terrible interior design. Tell me how you have such a nice location and a nice building and the walls are dirty and undecorated. The tables are uneven and don't even have table covers. The chairs are old and under appealing. 

The cashier just stood and starred at us when we entered, as if we were aliens. No greeting whatsoever. 

We sat at a table and waited for the server, 10 minutes later we get up to ask about the waiter and then they tell us "you order and then eat your food at the table". Well couldn't you tell us that when we first entered instead of just looking at our faces?

The prices are high..  I understand if you are serving us but you're not serving us so why are the prices so high?

Secondly the portions were so small. 

I don't get it. If you have a restaurant why don't you make it nice so people enjoy the experience. 

The worst part is despite all that... The food didn't even taste good lol. The meat from the kabobs were chewy and flavor less. 

This was literally the worst restaurant experience we had in several years.

A take out place that has prepackaged meals that are Broken down into categories for your fitness and health needs. A must stop place for a tasty and healthy quick bite. My low carb chicken meal satisfied my taste buds after a hard workout at the gym.

I don't understand the hype surrounding this place. We've been there twice and each time the service and the food were just ok. It's pretty bad when you ask your breakfast mate how their French toast is and they just shrug shoulders like meh it's ok. We've been to the original bisbee breakfast club in Bisbee and we're expecting this place to be good like that one.... Boy what a disappointment.

I have stayed at this Hilton a dozen times and would only eat at their restaurant if I was desperate for a quick bite.  Well tonight was one of those desperate late nights, but to my surprise the newly renovated hotel has a new restaurant called alloro.  It is seriously the best meal I have had in Tucson.  Started with a grilled artichoke with a great aoili and Parmesan dipping sauce (sounds odd but it rocks).   Then I had the salmon which I assumed would be microwaved or over cooked.  But it was top quality crispy skin cooked perfectly at medium.  Not dry at all and perfectly seasoned.    I am seriously floored that I got this kind of meal at the Hilton, but at this point I will eat here even when I am not staying at the Hilton.

This was an amazing meal.  When we travel we love to experience amazing local restaurants.  This did not disappoint.  The food was beautiful and very flavorful.  My husband picked two small plates and i had an entree.  Both meals were great
Clean & stylish rooms at a can't beat price. Best food & cocktails we have found in Boise.....by a LONG shot. And walking distance from downtown & a block from A tavola (another must when in Boise).
Decent burgers,  pretty good pizza (sauce is very acidic), prices are awesome. Servers are fantastic.  It's a a little loud on game day.  But it's great to sit back, have a good burger and chill.

So good for the price!

It's classic boiled seafood in a bag in a no frills spot. I would've ordered more pounds of crawfish if I had more time here!

"House Of India" has bunch of items to try on their lunch menu . They include 
1. Vegetable rice ( tasteless )
2. Chicken tikka ( it isn't spicy at all !! )
3.spinach paneer ( not great )
4. Chicken chili ( Not great )
5. Dosa ( dry and not fresh )
6. Jalebi (
7. Tandoori chicken (smells )
8.Aloo curry ( bland )
9. Kheer ( very good )
10. Naan ( dry and not fresh )
11.white rice 
12. Matar curry

I believe it's one of the very few Indian restaurants in saint Louis that serve these many items on a Buffet menu .

Although the menu looks Huge , the taste is below average . I wouldn't recommend this to folks who have tasted Indian food before . Because if you walk in with high expectations you will be disappointed .

Healthy, delicous, and all customizable.
So Bol offers a variety of beverages, smoothie bowls, waffles, soup, and little snacks you can buy.
They have many toppings available for you to choose from. You will pay for your toppings based off how many scoops you want.
The food is always ripe, taste really good, and very refreshing

Dont bother, go to Olive Garden, food no better and 1/3 the price of Romanza.  The only thing that was good was the bread and the service, otherwise really sub standard Italian food under the guise of "fine dining"  6 of us and the only one who enjoyed their dinner was the person who got the lamb shank.

This restaurant was pretty good all in all. The food was excellent I got the wood grilled burger and it was delicious we also got the sweet bacon chips as an appetizer and those were also good. The only thing they could have worked on was there service not that it was bad or horrible it was just very impersonal.  Overall though I would definitely suggest this restaurant.

My husband and I had breakfast here October 2019 and everything tasted amazing!  I had the Shrimp and grits - it was soooooo creamy and had a great tang to it. Service was great and was near Magazine Street. We live in NY and I think about Surrey's all the time, that's why I'm writing this review a year later! I regret not going back a second time while we were there.

What a time to try to start up a new business! This is a very clean-appearing place, and they have hand sanitizer as you walk in the door. As it is new, I think you can either get take out or eat in (I was the only customer, so social distancing wasn't a problem).

Dona Kitchen serves basic Mexican street/cafe food. Tacos (mostly around $2), quesadillas, sopes, and made to order guacamole. The owners are very friendly.

I tried three tacos: asada, campechano, and carnitas. I was a little perturbed when the cashier asked if I wanted flour or corn tortillas, as I don't think flour tortillas should ever be an option for Mexican tacos. But whatever. I had mine on corn tortillas, Mexicano style (with onions and cilantro). They were served with lime wedges and my choice of spicy or mild salsa. When they were served, the server asked if I needed instruction for how to eat Mexican tacos. (!!!) She stopped herself when she watched me with the lime wedges. 

I thought the tacos were good. Not the best I've had, but solid. They needed the lime juice and salsa as they were bland otherwise. And they were served on two tortillas per taco, which is an indication of store-bought tortillas. My preference would be Taqueria Emanuel (on MacDill closer to Columbus) as they do a better job with the meat and have clearly home made tortillas. Or Loli's, if you want a fish taco. But this was not a bad option if you happen to be in this part of Tampa and crave tacos. And the homemade guacamole certainly sounds promising, so maybe I will have to return to try it.

Wanted Indian Tuesday night. This place was the only place open until 10pm.

Parking: Lot

Atmosphere: Bright and spacious

Service: I called in for takeout. 

Food: Lamb biryani. I don't think this was lamb. I've ordered this from other Indian restaurants and this tasted very different. The "lamb" was ok. Not very flavorful.  I also ordered the meat simosa and it was different.   Maybe it was me. 

Overall: I'm a little Leary and not sure I will go back; well not for the lamb. 

Enjoy

I like the concept of Barcade, being a huge fan of retro arcade games, but this place falls short for me. 

I went with a friend after a Flyers game, so our Jerseys clashed at bit with the attire of what has to be the most hipsters I've ever seen in one place. Regardless, the other patrons were all nice with no issues at all.

The beer selection is great, with a lot of selections I knew well and many I'd never experienced. When I asked the bartender for advice on the selections, she said a lot of strangely incorrect things about the beers I'm familiar with, so I stopped paying attention to her advice. That's fine, as the beers were great.

Where I had issues was with the cramped layout, the super dark lighting, and the fact that 4 of the games were flat-out broken. We pointed these problems out the first time and were refunded the tokens we spent on the broken games without issue. The second time, a racing game broke and ate a couple dollars in tokens. The manager was incredibly rude and dismissive, to the point where we decided to leave as a result.

I won't be back.
Came in late at night and the bartender Carly was very accommodating. We ate and drank and mentioned we were from out of town and let us know all the specials and went above and beyond.
I had the chargrilled oysters that never fail to be delicious. As always all of our food and our service was wonderful. Highly recommend this place. If in Nrw Orleans you must check this place out
Food and service are good but we were so cold we had to leave dinner early. Don't sit at first two-top on Jena street facing side of restaurant. You'll freeze.
LOVE THIS PLACE!! Great healthy dishes and amazing protein shakes!!
So awful for such outrageous prices - for good food I am happy to pay premium prices - none of this was good
This was our first visit, they had great customer service & oh my, the burgers are awesome! Had a lovely experience for Saturday date night.

After enjoying delivery from them a few times during this pandemic, after getting my Covid vaccine, decided to finally make a in person trip.  

Didn't make a reservation for a party of two and was seated in the Hibachi side within 15 minutes.  Could have sat in the non-Hibachi side and sat right away.  Not bad for a Saturday.  I must say I was a bit weary about Covid-19 precautions and it was very obvious most Customers arrived without a mask, or used the hand sanitizer provided at the front.  I observed staff wearing masks and could see them cleaning tables as customers left.

When offered seating at the Hibachi table we were sat with a large group of 9 people with chairs side by side no dividers provided or even a separation between the different parties.  Being I am higher risk I asked to at least sit with one chair empty between our party and the other party.  The seater had to get permission from management and it was granted.  We've been to Kobe Japanese Steakhouse in Clearwater with plastic dividers separating the different parties and felt more at ease.  Both of us are high risk, but have had the vaccine. Personal preference for me is still caution, so we will wait to return.  

Now for the Hibachi presentation.  It was not the best and half hazard, but for the party at our table it was their first time ever seeing one, it was still fun.  The chef was not able to do the Onion stack volcano trick correctly and instead set it completely on fire.  He dropped his utensils, and only once engaged one of the adults with the squirt a drink into her mouth.  

We ordered the Hibachi for two people which includes the steak, shrimp, and chicken.  It comes with the clear soup, salad, and fried rice with egg.  We added a side of Udon noodles.  Now I must say the Udon noodles were the biggest I've seen and tasted wow!  We added an appetizer of Pork Gyoza fried and they are definitely not home made, but still tasted good.  The meal was overall good, not spectacular or any different than any other Hibachi place.  Cheap veggies, but fresh.  The steak was done to our request medium well and was chewy but tasty.  Shrimp were over cooked.  Chicken which always is finished cooking last was perfect.  Overall our favorite was the fried rice, as it was moist and tasted delicious.  

I had a Mai Tai and it was okay.  Overall we liked our food, but it was not perfect and pricey for two people.  I expect a better entertainment experience with the extra price and the food not overcooked.

Cornerstone is our go to pizza place ! Their food is always consistant no matter what time of day we order . The employees are always polite, from the person who takes the order, to the delievery driver.

The waiting area was crowded with people waiting on to go orders so I knew I could be in a good spot. I chose to dine in. The only complaint I have is the table I sat at was tiny and in a high traffic area. I ordered sweet and sour shrimp with the sauce on the side. You get a choice of egg rolls or Cho Cho on the side and the Cho Chos are very fantastic. Also comes with fried rice. The food came out fast and hot. The customer service was great. Great food great atmosphere. I will be back.

My boyfriend and I just came home from Zachary's BBQ and we are stuffed! The food was absolutely amazing especially the Mac and cheese! The staff was phenomenal and friendly! I highly recommend stopping by for a quick bite at a reasonable price

One of my top favorite places to eat in Santa Barbara! Food, service, ambiance are all outstanding. Their dishes are so unique, fresh and very tasty. I recommend the chiefs plate to start. Oak Tagliatelle, & the Raviolo are my favorite. But everything is good here. You can't go wrong.

They recently added brunch on the weekends. Which is amazing!!! Huevos is my favorite. And there iced coffee is a must try.

A lot bigger than it looks, some pretty good local brews on tap. Oh, and very very college-y. But not in a horrible way, I guess.

But I've done this all before - in Ithaca. Kinda past that scene, personally. But, for reasons I won't go into right now, I found myself in this place with a group of my younger friends, getting shitfaced on a Thursday night.

Anyway, being the only one with a job, I buy us a round of shots. They were stupid cheap at like, 4 or 5 bucks each. I don't remember. All I know is by the end of the night, I'd only spent about 50 bucks. That probably made me a high roller in the joint.

Despite that, the bar staff is incredibly patient, surprisingly knowledgeable when it comes to "old people" drinks, and really quick. I suppose they'd have to be to survive the daily onslaught. The beer special that night was "crappy light beers for a dollar," but the main bartender offered to just upgrade me to a bigger cup of Yuengling or Kenzinger at no extra cost. I think he recognized that I was a little older than the average college student. Thanks, guy!

Also, this place is cheap as hell. Which I suppose is why there are so many students every night.

So, congrats to you, Blarney. You were a lot better than I expected. I might even go back when there aren't so many students around. Summer's upon us!

EXCELLENT! Our new favorite Chinese restaurant! The portions are big enough for my 6'5 240lb fiancé, which is hard to find. Both of our meals were delicious! I got chicken, shrimp and noodles just to be safe, sense this is our first time and he got duck with fun noodles. Can't wait to bring friends and family here :)

This place is worth the green! We ordered delivery and everyone was satisfied with their orders. I got the Red Curry (mild spice and tofu) and a Thai Iced Tea. The red curry was amazing- very flavorful and just a good amount of spice. The Thai iced tea was on the sweeter side but was a good combo to the curry. There was a good amount of veggies in the curry and the rice was nice and soft. Overall, amazing quality, great service, could not be happier!

The meat lovers pizza was amazing. The combination of meats had so many flavors that each bite tasted a little different than the one before. We also ordered a margarita pizza. It was good, but didn't compare to the flavor of the meat lovers.

Too bad there's a one star minimum. Packed day at the mall. We ordered $60 worth of food and had no place to sit. We noticed 2 young ladies with food court food chilling in a booth. We notified management who eventually said something to them and apologized profusely as if these two that brought outside food into the restaurant were the ones being inconvenienced. The manager did not acknowledging us after wiping down the table. Another inconvenience obviously. Very disappointed in this Panera.

I went here for a party with some friends on Saturday night.  They gave us a private room, and we had a blast!  We had a server dedicated to running drinks our way.  She did a great job of keeping tabs on everyones tabs... you like how i did that there?  Some people ordered food, and again, they did a great job of tracking down the right people and getting them the right stuff.  By the end of the night, it was like herding kittens, but they kept their cool.  All the beers were delicious, and the little food i ate was also fab (should have eaten more!!!).  Everyone I talked to was very nice, and the place was super-clean.  For a chain, this place was great!

We came here on a Saturday afternoon around 3 for lunch.  I had a meatball sandwich and my boyfriend had chicken raviolis; both were about $13 which is rather pricey for luch, but since it's a small business I was ok with that.  My sandwich was very filling but the portion size of the chicken raviolis was pretty small, especially for a guy, so my boyfriend was still kind of hungry afterwards.  The service was quick and friendly and we will probably be back to try dinner.

Found this place here on Yelp. 
The husband wanted dinner last minute and he wanted something new.
This place has :
Dim sum
Hot pot
Pho
What else do you want ? This place is amazing !

Lula is a Restaurant and a Distillery much like many places over the last 10 years have made brew pubs. Much like the highly refined process of distilling, their food is also elevated above pub quality. This formula has worked with the brew pub, and I'm excited about the possibilities of a Restaurant Distillery. 

We started lunch with a flight of their spirits to size the place up, we weren't disappointed. Vodka, Gin & Rum. The vodka was smooth with a heavier mouth feel. It has a softer sweetness with a little bit of a bite. All of the spirits are based of sweet Louisiana molasses or cane sugar. The vodka is distilled three times. 

The Gin is their vodka pulled out after the 1st distill and then infused with the juniper and other botanicals and distilled again. It's got a less pronounced bite so it's a much smoother drinker. 

Lastly is their rum. Only distilled once this molasses based beauty is a clean nice rum. It's not spiced and not aged. So for a newer Distillery it's a nice entry. Drinks well but shines in a mixed drink. 

Naturally a Distillery and Restaurant wouldn't be complete without a bar. And they make up lots of options with their three spirits so you can experience them in new and different ways. They batch create draft cocktails, bottle up individual bottles cocktails like a gin & tonic and hand craft others. All great choices, here's hoping they can start selling their bottled cocktails soon, so good with their house made tonic!

Oh, did I mention they have food. Because it's good and should not be missed. There were so many good choices it was hard to decide. But, we opted for a crab meat mixed guacamole to start. Mixed through the guacamole was shredded crab and it was such a nice mix of texture. 

We followed that up with their fried Cornish hen and their seafood boil of crab claws with a lemongrass sauce over fries. Both were beautiful and delicious. I'm hoping this concept catches on because I'd love to see this in every city!

Got in line at 4pm on a Saturday and burnt ends were already out, and the brisket ran out by the time we got to the front of the line 45 minutes later. Nevertheless, my girlfriend and I still had some great food while feeling like a local:
- full rack of ribs (in retrospect, a half rack would have sufficed)
- 1/4 lb pulled pork (+4 when added to the ribs)
- baked beans (YUM)
- sweet potato fries (sprinkled with sugar YUM!!!)
- fried corn (yum but unnecessarily salted)

They do a great crowd control, but honestly, there are plenty of seats available and once you get seated, it felt like the restaurant was at 2/3 capacity - meanwhile we had just stood in line for 45 minutes and we all know the food is already ready to go. But I guess it's nice to not sit elbow to elbow with others. Service was friendly, food was good and well priced - glad I came here for my one weekend in St Louis.
Cheap beer.  Great atmosphere. Live music in Nashville is awesome  and Tin Roof keeps the vibe going.

After running the Rock and Roll Half Marathon we stopped in for some quality cheesesteaks. There was so many other 13.1 runners with the same idea. 2 American With, 1 Pizza and a Turkey Hoagie.... The lines was long but they having taking and filling orders down to a science. My #1 spot for Philly Cheesesteaks !
Always tasty! Service is generally kind of meh in my opinion. I guess I expect more when I take in the ambiance. However, I have been here for two private parties and they were executed very well.

The location is within a strip mall near Kroger. It's a good place if you're looking for an inexpensive meal. The place appeared to be clean 

The food wasn't bad. I highly recommend the Mediterranean Skillet (onions, bell peppers, hash browns, eggs, gyro meat etc). Yum! 

My service wasn't terrible, but it wasn't the best.
I wasn't greeted. As soon as I was seated my waitress asked did I know what I wanted to order. I hadn't even opened the menu yet or received a beverage. My waitress was sitting at a table eating her breakfast and checked on me occasionally when she was able to pause from consuming her own meal. She didn't give off a friendly server vibe. It seems as if the waitresses eat their meals while servicing customers as well.

Ok. I'm going to flip my flop. 
We finally tried it again after years and it was pretty good. Not five stars but a good 3 1/2. I got the steak salad, and it was just fine.My husband's tacos were really good.

This is one of my favorite neighborhood places. I come here all the time, and each time is a great experience. Their menu is awesome, I've never ordered something I didn't like. Their cocktail menu is fantastic and they are always adding new drinks. The servers are always prompt and friendly, and I love the ambiance. I've also attended their Monday night quizzo which is always a blast. My most recent visit to Moonshine was with my mom. We sat outside, ordered several appetizers just to pick on, and I got a Jack's cider from their extensive beer list. Everything was delicious. The popcorn shrimp was crispy, the humans was incredible as always, the broccoli bites (one of the daily specials) were perfectly cooked, and the barbecue pork tacos were out of this world with flavor. Halfway through our dinner, we were serenaded my Quaker City string band passing by. Overall, a great neighborhood place and I highly recommend it.

I shed a tear because I lived in Santa Barbara for a year and only discovered this terrific sandwich and salad place a few months before I left.  All of the salads I've tried have been delicious, especially the gorgonzola salad.      

You can buy some of their absolutely fabulous salad dressings for around $5 a bottle.  Sadly for me, I bought two bottles when I happened to be down in Santa Barbara and then left them in a friend's fridge.  Too bad, so sad.  I hope she enjoyed them.

A friend and I stopped in on a Wednesday night and it was packed. One whiff of the food and a glimpse of the beer list and I understood why. 

You know when you walk into a place and have a good (or sometimes bad) feeling as soon as you put your foot down? That's how I felt here, in the good way. People were just chillin' and I got the sense that everyone was so satisfied. We walked past the content crowd and grabbed a two-top in the back, by the kitchen. MISTAKE. I couldn't stop staring at the food in the window. Bummer that I just finished a sizeable dinner. 

Anyway, I forced my focus to the suds selection: about 12 taps and a firkin with another 30ish bottles available. Winner, winner, wish I didn't already eat dinner! Okay, enough. I ordered two great beers, enjoyed great company and mentally plotted my next visit.

Everything was perfect from the pre dinner wine to the okra fries, the Caesar salad, our entrees were the vegetarian dish of the day (tofu and eggplant) and the water works meatloaf. The dessert was the maple duck bacon candied ice cream which just melts in your mouth. Of course The service was exceptional like I expected. The only real complaint I could have had was that we still waited about 35-40 minutes even with a reservation. However, those without were waiting an hour+

This was a great spot for lunch! I met a few friends here this past week and really enjoyed it. 

The waitress was very polite and attentive. I ordered the vegetarian plate, and everyone else in my party ordered the gyro plate, which looked very good (and was a lot of food). My vegetarian plate was good enough, I probably would order something else next time, however. After reading reviews here, though, I did order the pistachio baklava (at $1.99, why not get dessert after lunch??) and was not disappointed. 

I will make a note that they do not have a changing table in their woman's bathroom which had my girlfriend explaining how she changed her 1-year-old's diaper while sitting on the toilet with him on her lap. Yeah. A definite con for me, even without children, as I do not want something so seemingly insignificant to deter us from frequenting a place like this, but it will. 

The place is very small, and you WILL drive right by unless you know it's here but I thoroughly enjoyed eating here and look forward to coming back so I can try more of their menu!
Love the meatballs and fried chikcken!  They were fast in preparing the food.  Would love to try more of their other dishes in the future.
Food here is amazing, all of it. The chef, Brad, has love for cooking. Angela is the best bartender in Reno when you're looking for mixed drinks.

Great place!  Great Beer!  Great food!  It is hard to find a brewery which has both great Beer And great Food.  This place has both - And the location in historic YBOR makes it better.  They had the best Pumpkin beer I have ever had as one of their specials.  Pizza was excellent too.

Food is decent   reasonable prices  shrimp is good ....however the day was ruined by a drunk server who came in to shift "drunk " as she openly admitted when she walked in she said to a co worker she had "been drinking :" (our party with children over heard ) and she laughed, red headed ,older server with  tatoos ,,  she then proceeded to dance like a stripper in front of and on the band members that were playing,  it was quite odd,    I felt embarrassed for the owner ,the afternoon was great until she came along ,  she really made the place go down in class with her behaviour     also this is a family place     it was not good

Everything was OUTSTANDING. I was upset we were full and couldn't finish everything on our plate. We shared hummus, 3 appetizers and lamb kebabs. It was more than enough for 2 people for dinner unless you prefer a large meat serving. Then go for less apps.

I will go back the next time I'm in NOLA no question.

If I could give this place 0 stars I would. Not only were they "out of tortillas" so you couldn't order anything made with tortillas (good luck with that) they were so lazy they wouldn't make the cheesy fiesta potatoes I ordered and PAID for. They said they were "out of those too" after I already paid for them! You see it was close to closing time, so they were "out of a lot of stuff". They could refund our money, but that was about it. Do not go there whatever you do. They are a bunch of lazy employees that do not care about their customers. I even spoke to the manager on duty who said there wasn't anything they "could do" to make it right for us. Spend your money elsewhere.

I was lucky enough to hit the soft open and tried almost everything on menu, so here we go!!!!

Uštipci: Good appetizer to share. My favorite sauce is the Ajvar with the kajmak coming in with a close second 

Smoked wings: Perfectly seasoned 

Panko crabcakes: BOMB but those are always good

Chip twister: My favorite appetizer on the menu! It's perfection. Literally. 

Cevapi: Technically this is my favorite thing to eat. Ugh I don't know. Can we just make a sandwich with Cevapi and put the chip twisters in there?

Fried chicken: It's no Hodaks nor Southern but the chef can knock out some bitchin' fried chicken

Trout: Good flavor, if you're into eating well 

Chicken tenderloin skewers: SOOOO TENDERERR

50/50 burger: I haven't had you yet, but I'm coming for ya!

All the salads: ?!?!? For real? Waste plate space for green stuff? No.

Honey grow has great salads, that you can customize to your liking. Their noodles are also amazing. However, I had to deduct a start because when you order any protein for your noodles they are not warmed throughly. I thought it was a one time incident, but I was mistake.

Absolutely delicious pizza!   I had a slice of Sicilian(a middle , of course!) and one of white broccoli (yay - not too garlicky!)

The chicken noodle soup wasn't as good as it looks in my (awesome!) picture - the chicken was a bit tough.  Overall, pretty good though. 

I'm definitely going back to sample other delicious looking pies!

(Good prices & sweet staff!)

Me and the Columns are in a long term relationship. Even though I don't see her that much anymore she stills knows we're cool. Our flirtation began back when I was a youngin' in my college days. I thought this place was so awesome because me and my friends could feel fancy and have real talks without any fist pumping music in the background. Fast forward 5 years and I see the Columns is still infiltrated with college kids reminding me of my ever fading youth. On weekends its really more of a mixed crowd so everyone feels welcome. My most recent trip was great and it made me realize I never wrote a review for such a nostalgic. On a rather busy night, my group of 6 scored a table outside. We had a lovely cocktail waitress who brought us drinks all night. My French 75s were on point. 

Even thought he interior is pretty, I love sitting outside on the big porch watching the streetcars go by. I still would recommend you to explore the rooms inside if you have never been because coming from a historic standpoint its really beautiful.

Before I talk about how delicious the food was, I just want to comment that the experience was unbeatable due to our server - David. Good service is something that is hard to find these days. David smiled, chatted with us, and made us feel like we were dinner guests in his own home, rather than in a public restaurant. He was so attentive and strove to ensure our every expectation was exceeded. Thank you David!! 

This establishment is beautiful inside as if every detail was considered, down to the wonderfully smelling tropical handsoap in the bathroom (yes i notice these things). The menu is full of hard-to-choose-from dishes and everything was delicious. I will definitely come back.

Had a light dinner here after a long travel day.  Unfortunately, our server did not realize he had another table so we sat patiently for around 15 minutes.  I probably would have let it slide but he wasn't even apologetic so there goes the 5th star.

The food was great. Very unique beat salad that was beautifully presented.  The duck wings were definitely the star of the table.  My wife wrinkled up her nose at the thought of duck, then promptly ate half the order.  We also had a caramelized onion tart that was excellent.  

We decided dessert/all we needed for the rest of dinner was a great cheese plate and the deliver a gem.  All in all, great meal, would go back and request a different server.

Montana's has OK food. This place is geared towards families with children. All the tables have paper on them and servers provide crayons so that kids can draw and color while they wait for their food to come out. I would assume that parents love this place. It keeps the kids busy instead of impatient. 

I go here every now and then because they have great nachos. They are so good and covered with the perfect amount of cheese. I also enjoy the Oven baked antojito's, they are pretty filling.

OK and I enjoy coloring while waiting for my food.

Yum! Tai's is a great place to stop by for Viet food on Temple campus. The staff is super friendly, and their food is always yummy. I love their vermicelli with grilled pork and fried spring rolls. Their drinks are great also. Reasonably priced great tasting Vietnamese food.

Wow----thought this was great pizza !!
We ordered two LARGE Specialty Pizzas............deep dish............one the "Super Special" and the "All Meaty"..............both were REALLY delicious. Tasted so fresh and thought the crust was wonderful. These pizzas are a BIG step up from the other chains. We are really happy to find them. 
We picked up our pizzas.
The LARGE size is HUGE ! Am sure it will be delicious leftover too.
First time here and I'm impressed I didn't know a Fucking soup place can be so good wow.

I hate to rate it a two because the food was sooo good. However, our waitress on the other hand..... we sat at a table in the bar, there were four of us. We ordered drinks and apps. She barely made eye contact with us. Immediately we felt awkward. She then brought us our drinks, then apps. We asked if they had Ranch and she said no as she was walking away, still not looking at us. Once our dinner came it took almost an hour to see her again to order another drink and desserts. For almost a $250 bill I would expect impeccable service. We were so disappointed because this restaurant came. highly recommended. I would understand if she was that busy but she was standing in the bar area chatting most of the time.

My husband and I come here often. We love the food. Everything we have eaten here has been amazing. And we love bringing out of town guests here because we know they'll love it. They also request to come back to razz's! Yum!!

Great food and great value! Huge portions at a very reasonable cost. We always get it as take-out and they do a great job, putting salad dressings on the side for me and gravy on the side of my husbands' Chicken Fried Steak for him. Good quality food, too!

I always enjoy going to the Bistro because of their atmosphere, there multitude of beers on draft, and their food. You can sit outside or in depending on your preference. If you're up to it, you can even visit the upstairs outdoor area. All in all, a great place to unwind and relax.

Everytime we are down this way, we stop in for happy hour because I absolutely love the key lime martini! It's incredibly tasty and has a Graham cracker crust around the rim, which makes it more like a key lime pie martini. It's the only place I've ever seen a drink like this and I wish more places had something like it because it's my all time favorite cocktail. It isn't too sour and doesn't upset my stomach as some cocktails do. I remember the bartender with the ponytail from all the times we've been here before and he's awesome! He pumps the drinks out very fast and with incredible accuracy. Never had a poorly made drink or had to wait long with him at the bar.
Happy hour is from 4-closing Monday-Thursday and 4-8 Friday and you can seat yourself in the specified area.
To be honest, I've never had dinner here, but I've had their happy hour food items and they were always delicious.
Today, we had the spicy popcorn shrimp. It was perfectly cooked and the sauce it came with was amazing. It was just a little bit sweet and I still don't know what was in it, but if we had gotten another appetizer, I would have requested another helping of the sauce just to have more of it.
I have been to this place 5-6 times, which is a lot considering that I live 6 hours away.will definitely be back the next time we are in town!

Found this place in CWE on an impromptu date night and my SO and I fell in LOVE! They had plexiglass in between each table for safety. Even so, it still had a nice romantic ambiance. We were really hungry so we got a 3 course meal! For apps In order of tastiness: The smoked salmon dip, jerk wings, Mac & Cheese. OMG the smoked salmon dip was the best smoked salmon ANYTHING I've ever had! It came with crostini crackers and when those ran out I just scooped the rest with a spoon. Creamy yet teeming with flavor. 10/10 would recommend. The jerk wings and Mac were still pretty good but the dip really blew everything else out. For my meal I got the Salmon over risotto. It was delicious! The fillet was cooked to perfection and the risotto and pistou (not pesto) were the perfect complement to the dish. I couldn't get enough and I was sad when my meal was over. To drink I got the 3 toed flamingo, it was sweet and strong, just how I like my men . For dessert, we got chocolate chip cookie ice cream with peanut butter mousse in between the cookies and vanilla ice cream on top! THAT PEANUT BUTTER MOUSSE COULD WIN AWARDS BY ITSELF. It was like a whipped and creamy and light and airy and just BEAUTIFUL. You get the gist, you won't be disappointed if you come here.

Yeah, the cocktails are the best in Idaho. Had a Pisco sour and a Caparinia (sp?). Man those bar tenders know how to do it. Must be all the red bull and vanilla infused 320 vodka they slam.

I haven't eaten here in a while either. Got to go sometime soon to review that.

My husband & I used to go here every other Tuesday for the half price wings. We would always sit at the bar & the bartenders were very attentive.  The problem was the wings were so tiny!  It seems like they hold the small ones for Tuesday nights.  I realize they are half price, but you get half a wing.  We stopped going there a few months ago.  We go to the Jug Handle Inn for their half price wings on Tuesday night. They are much, much bigger & taste better.  See ya, PJ's

Delivered on time, food still hot. Burger isn't cooked the temperature I requested (it's overdone) but it's still a good basic burger. Cheese fries were crinkle fries with cheddar melted over the top layer - more cheese would've been nice. The baked macaroni is not baked. It's egg noodle pieces in a cheese sauce with pepper. It's very disappointing.

What a great little unique place attached to an equally unique hotel.  The restaurant has some great indoor and outdoor seating options.   We elected to sit inside as it was a bit cool outside but both are great options. 

The staff were friendly accommodating and customer focused.  My wife was still a bit chilly inside and they provided a blanket straight away.  She elected to just use her sweater but they were right on top of things.  

The server was attentive and helpful.  I would put this on my shortlist anytime I am in Santa Barbara.

My wife and I have dined at Fattoush a number of times since they opened and have always been very pleased.  The decor is pleasant, the food excellent and the service attentive.  Highly recommend the Mediterranean Sampler appetizer and Lamb Gyro.  They're also a BYOB.

I wasn't expecting to be wowed by PATB, and didn't come out feeling cheated there -- i.e., I wasn't wowed. There was nothing particularly distasteful about the restaurant. The ambiance is classy. The owner/hostess seemed nice enough. The food was good-- but just that - good.

Guess I should clarify that I am comparing it with some of the best Indian places around the country. I should also clarify that I am an Indian foodie who lives (and earns) just so I can travel around the country and try some of the best restaurants in town - so I am a lil bit of a food snob :)

Did I mention the service was amateurish for a restaurant at this price point? Try Bombay Club in DC to see what attentive service should be like!

The one thing that did wow me -- Kulfi -- it's a traditional Indian ice cream -- although much firmer than ice cream. That was some of the best kulfi I've had - EVER!

I am really easy to accomodate when it comes to a coffee shop.  I only have two drinks - Iced coffee and hot coffee.

Daily Grind always has excellently brewed iced coffee - perfect flavor and boldness - never watered down.  

Their hot coffee selection is the best in town - all their brews are delicious - I have never been unhappy with a hot coffee choice, even their bold brews are smooth without a hint of acidity.

Their staff is always friendly, patient, and fast.  

Seeing as they have a huge menu and people are always ordering more than just coffee - my guess is that the rest of their stuff is just as good.

This is a routine stop for me!

I am giving this Outback Steakhouse 4 stars. When we first walked in the place was pretty empty and the hostess just told us to seat ourselves anywhere in the bar area. They weren't too friendly. That was the worst part of our experience. The rest of the experience was great. Josh was out waiter. He was excellent. Attentive to detail and charming. Food came out quickly. Orders were taken correctly. We even got a free drink. The app we ordered was the coconut shrimp. It might've been a little over cooked... The salads and steaks we ordered were prepared perfectly. The steaks came out as an amazing medium rare steak. Loved them. My mom ordered some croutons to go because she loves than and josh brought us a boatload. She was very greatful. Great experience and great food!!

This was my first ever jazz club experience, and for only an extra $10 per person to eat good southern food while listening to some amazing live jazz music, South is the place to be.

We made reservations for 6:15pm in the jazz club area (it's first-come-first-serve for seating in the jazz club area and the live jazz music starts at 7pm) and sat in a clean and classy dining area. The whole restaurant, including the jazz club area as well as the regular restaurant area, is beautiful and welcoming.

We ordered the $22 Buttermilk Fried Chicken (with sides of mashed potatoes and broccoli) and a $5 side of Stewed Turkey Green Beans. It was some of the best fried chicken (the honey drizzle took it to the next level) and green beans (the stewed turkey flavor was evident and tasty) I've ever had. We also got three complementary biscuits, which paired well with the fried chicken. I like jazz music, but wish I had more exposure to it or knowledge about it, and my wish came true listening to the combination of talented musicians on the drums, bass, saxophone, and piano playing beautiful and harmonious music together.

Thank you South for a delightful experience with delicious, reasonably-priced food/live music, great service, and a beautiful new memory!

Last night I went with a group of friends to P.F. Chang's at Westshore and had a great time. The food was flavorful. To me for the price, I expected a little better playing as it came out kind of slopped on the plates. I think it was a little expensive but I guess you're paying for a more upscale experience. We ordered a double order of Mongolian Beef, and a single order of Pork Lo Mein, and Sweet and Sour Chicken to share with the table. This was the best way to try a little bit of everything and made it more sociable with our friends. I am a huge fan of social eating and sharing food and felt it brings us closer together.

Previously I've gone to P.F. Chang's during their happy hour during the week and the prices were very reasonable. I even had my favorite lettuce wraps on the menu. I would highly suggest going for happy hour for drinks and food. You'll spend the same amount that you would've for just the entrees at a fraction of the price. All in all I've had good service with attentive servers every time I've been.

Amazing. Excellent service, and my favorite meal I ate while in NOLA. Definitely make a reservation, many people got turned away when we were there- and it was a Monday night! Great music, interesting and engaging atmosphere. Definitely will go back next time i'm in New Orleans.

It's a hotel bar.  When I was visited, there was scaffolding all up front, and it was tough to find.  I wasn't too impressed with their food choices.  (I probably didn't have the best experience in STL, unfortunately). It was tough to find anything green there, TBH.  I did manage to get a salad that was okay there.  My experience in the whole area was just "okay." Meaning, I've had better.  Meh.

Pro:  This is simply a great cheesesteak!  While other Philadelphia businesses may get the greater touristy acclaim (you know...places that may rhyme with "Brats" or "Green-O's"), Jimmy G is putting out a product that boasts all the flavor without the hype. 

Con:  The sliding glass at the cashier booth (that appears to be bulletproof) doesn't lend itself to promoting any ambiance. But hey, you're eating a cheesesteak, right?!? 

Bottom Line:  No frills, no thrills, just a man and his cheesesteak. Life is good...
The only problem I have with Port of Call is the parking.  Once you find a place to park, then the rest is easy.  Burger or Steak with loaded baked potato.  YUMMY!!!

Nice healthy vegetarian fare in a trendy but friendly ambience. The sandwiches are mostly just fancy grilled cheese, but the bread and the cheese are high quality. The kale and quinoa salad was delicious. I thought the "blue bottle" coffee was overpriced and overrated compared to Cartel or Aqui, but I'm a coffee snob.

I don't really eat Vietnamese food since I prefer American food, but this restaurant serves some of the best Vietnamese cuisine I have ever had. The pho and vietnamese sandwiches are delicious and made with fresh ingredients. I came back another day and ate a rice plate with grilled pork - I don't like eating pork, BUT I loved eating the pork from this restaurant. And for drinks, the avocado shake is one of the most refreshing and sweet drinks you could have during the hot summer. The staff is very friendly and the wait for your food is non-existent on the weekdays. It does get busy on the weekends though! I will be leaving Philadelphia and will miss this restaurant. I highly recommend this place if you want a taste of well-made Vietnamese cuisine.

I was impressed with this incredible Korean grill! We had incredible tablee service and it felt like the waiters always had their eye on us-- making sure we had plenty of water and appetizers. It's a little pricy for the unlimited buffet, but is worth every penny. The sauces alone were so delicious-- unlike anything I'd had before then. Excited to come back and being friends again soon.

My only knock was that when I ordered an oyster po-boy to go, with a side of fried green tomatoes, they put the order in for a fried green tomato po-boy. My bad for not paying attention to the final cost of the order. Not complaining too much b/c both were really tasty. 

HOWEVER - all of the food I saw coming out while waiting was looking so good I was wishing we got up earlier to have breakfast here. Plus, the service was fast, friendly and no one was loafing around. They all seemed to be working like a well-oiled machine. 

Definitely on my short list next time I visit NOLA.

The deck, parking lot and skee ball take this spot from a 3 to a 4.  I agree with the others that aren't nuts about the food.  I see the problem as inconsistency.  I've actually had decent food here - I've also had awful food here.  My fix for this - get the fries and one of their good craft beers on tap, play some skee ball and stop complaining.  You're in East Falls people - not Manhattan.

So glad we stopped by this place! On holiday from England and wanted a quick beer as we were driving by. Had the best service ever from a young gent (i think his name was Keeran?). Highly recomendable for great beer at reasonable prices. Keeran needs a promotion!

What can I say?  It's a McDonald's, but this location has got to be the nicest associates working there, ANYWHERE!  The people were so pleasant that I wished all the McDonald's around our home was as nice!  The service was fast and was as good as any other we have been to.

This review is primarily for the bar area, staff and beer selection. The draft beer selection is limited but varied. They also have a nice selection of bottles. The food is decent-nachos are good, deviled eggs are tasty and have a slight Asian flavor to them. The burger is decent, the crab cake sandwich is just ok, the steak sandwich is not bad. The bartenders are great and so is the manager James. I hear their building has been sold so they will be closing. Unfortunate as this is a fun place to grab a beer and a bite to eat.
Not that great of a chicken sandwich and the girl with the glasses cashiering seem  a bit challenging cause she  just looked at me for seconds and never said hello until I did

Really great patio, food, beer selection but our waitress was kind of rude and the service was not good, took a long time to get drinks and food out. When we sat down we got waters then got two flights, when one of us was deciding on the last beer for the flight the waitress was tapping her pen and seeming very annoyed about having to wait a few seconds, didn't like that.  Although the service was not the greatest the food was really good, highly recommend the roasted cauliflower and spinach artichoke dip!  This place is a fun environment to be in and has a good patio so will probably be going back.

Yum.  Yum.  Yum.  Yum.

My husband and I came in on a Sunday for Brunch for his birthday - we had a reservation (which i HIGHLY recommend) and were seated quickly.
I started with a bloody mary - VERY tasty and good garnish (I am an aficionado of Bloodys and detest just a celery stalk - this place had good little garnishes!)
We decided to have a cinnamon roll as an appetizer (don't judge!) and holy wow.  It was warm and gooey and huge and perfect - exactly how a cinnamon roll should be!  We couldn't even come close to finishing it.
My husband went with the Chilaquiles with carnitas and I had the Nashville hot chicken sandwich. Neither one of us could barely make a dent in the large portions - but man, we tried!  The food was DELICIOUS!  The chicken was perfectly spicy and fried and the homemade biscuit - just get out of here!!  My husband loved the salsa verde on the chilaquiles and we were stuffed and deliriously happy.
The wait staff is VERY on point - they know how to serve tables and are pleasant and cheerful and very knowledgeable.  
I would HIGHLY recommend Bud and Marilyns for brunch - a great spot in the city and the food was DELICIOUS!

LOVE this restaurant. The decor is so quirky & fanciful. The drinks are lovely. Service is outstanding. The food was phenomenal (especially the crawfish egg rolls). My husband & I split the chicken Parmesan which may have been a tad undercooked because we both felt some moderate stomach upset after dinner, so just double check that, otherwise the dish itself was fantastic. I'm not at all sure why, but the pasta that accompanied the chicken Parmesan was the best I've ever had. Also since it was our anniversary they brought us champagne in a bong style glass, which was hilarious & so fun to drink. We also ordered the mile high pie. Unfortunately is just a very tall slice of various ice cream flavors. No actual pie involved. Maybe I read the menu wrong, who knows. It was still good, if ice cream is what you are wanting. Regardless, we had a wonderful time & will definitely return.

My husband & I  breakfast here every Sunday, Meaty Peter omelet for me  &  Triple Berry Pancantkes for him.    VERY GOOD!   PUT  that   together  with a friendly staff you have a winner. Our  server is Maria a very pleasant person who always has a smile for everyone we look forward to seeing her.

I stopped here for the lunch buffet on the way up the coast. On the plus side, it's a nice space, and the servers are very hospitable. Unfortunately, the buffet was a disappointment. Yesterday's offerings included salad offerings (including what I guess would be called a chickpea chaat of sorts), pakoras, tandoori chicken, a potato dish, chicken biryani, both chicken tikka masala and a veggie tikka masala, and, if memory serves, chicken jalfrezi. There was also fruit and rice pudding for dessert. The chickpeas were probably the best thing out there, and helped pump up the pakoras when eaten together. But the other dishes, sadly, ranged from OK but bland (the chicken tikka masala) to deeply lacking in flavor (the tandoori). I appreciated the substantial naan--which was OK--that was brought to each table, though it probably didn't help that I'd just eaten at Vij's in Vancouver a few days before; it's hard for any naan to hold a candle to theirs, and this didn't. I get that buffets tend to cater to the lowest common denominator when it comes to spiciness (read: mild), but that doesn't mean that dishes can't be well-spiced and flavorful. Also, considering that there are relatively few choices compared to most buffets, do you really need to have chicken tikka masala (probably the most boring dish on an Indian menu) and a veggie version that's more or less the same dish on the same day? Again, very nice people, which is why they get three stars instead of two, but there is definitely room for improvement here. Alas, I think I'd go elsewhere next time I'm in SB.
Everything from the crispy brussel sprouts to the creme brûlée was SO DELICIOUS. Definitely recommend for anyone with a craving for Italian food.

Convenient location and good service.  We sat outside by the marina.  Our group had grouper, clam chowder, burger, and chicken strips and onion rings. Everyone was pleased with their food.  Decent prices. Fresh grouper.

Extremely disappointed in tonight's order. The onion rings were floppy and weren't cooked long enough. The sandwiches were pathetic. Not enough meat at all! One bread was toasted and one wasn't on all three sandwiches. The turkey tasted funny and was dry. No mayo on the club at all. It was like they half assed it. Not sure if I'd give them another try. I'll have to think about it. The first time was good. Not sure if tonight was a different cook.

Ate at the bar and both of us had the burger and fries. One of the best burgers I've ever had and maybe the best fries I've EVER had! Got our food fast during Friday night happy hour! Our bartenders were very entertaining as well!

Llama Tooth is fun spot. Great beer selection but regarding the food... I would imagine this place gets most of its patrons due to the fact that it is so close to Union Transfer. 

We went prior to a concert and it was just what we need to get us ready for the show.  I had their barbeque mac n cheese and it was tasty and very filling! The interior is fun as they have llama heads glued on top of whomever was one on their portraits.. i thought it was hilarious.

They also have a great little outside section facing spring garden which is cute.. although the last time we were there, they were serving beers out of a cooler which we thought was sketch at the time lol.. now it's just part of the charm. ha! the servers are really nice too. Overall, we typically have a good time at this spot but don't usually venture there unless in need of a pre-show buzz/bite :)

Enjoy!
We had an awesome experience and the food and ppl were outstanding!!! Special shout out to Ms. Sherry...excellent customer service

Wonderful little outdoor cafe with yummy choices: the flatbread pizza with roasted red peppers and caramelized onions and the Greek salad were a delightful surprise. This cafe is located  for tourists but must also be a local favorite, the food is that good.
