My husband wanted to get the duck fat fries but they only came with the steak. He asked if he could just get the fries and they said of course! We also got the funghi flatbread and a pasta. The food came out really fast and everything was delicious! And don't underestimate the bread and olive oil. The oil is so good and bread is fresh. If we weren't going out after we would have bought some oil to take home. 

I hope to come back (with a reservation) to try some more dishes.

I have been putting off this review because I am really on the fence about this place. Yes, I did end up giving it four stars but it easily could be a three.  I am mostly on the fence because of the service.  Not that our server was rude or annoying or made a big mistake, it was that she just didn't seem to know what she was doing. Oh, and we had to wait for beverages and she was guessing who's order was who's. Anyway, I decided not to knock Mathew's due to the service we received.  She may have been giving wonderful service to the rest of the place! 
So on with the review.  We met up with two other couples for a celebratory dinner of sorts.  It was reasonably busy and we were sat at a table upstairs in the very back of the restaurant.  The restaurant itself is decorated very nicely. It had a romantic darkly lit vibe which was nice but also a bit awkward for our table of six.  So, the food and drinks were all tasty and everyone seemed to really enjoy their meals. I had the shrimp and grits and would definitely have them again and again.  The grits were flavored well and the shrimp were, well they were shrimp - can't really go wrong with shrimp!  We ordered as much as we could to taste and be able to review and find out favorites.  The pretzels were really really good and the pig wings were also tasty, but maybe a bit overpowered by the buffalo sauce.  The not pizzas were hailed as another re-order item on the next visit.  
All in all the place is worth checking out.  Hopefully you have better luck with the service!
A little overpriced, but still quality.  Loved by tourists and locals alike.  Great vibes, difficult to find seating.

From the service to the food everything was fabulous. It's like a better version of Panera Bread. They have about 100 soups and they offer 12 of them daily which they alternate out. The staff is very kind and knowledgeable on the products. They offer you samples of anything you'd like to try. I opted for the Try 2 which offers half a sandwich and a small cup of soup for about 9 bucks. I tried the spicy chicken enchilada soup and the chicken toscana sandwich. It was plenty of food. I even had leftovers. Panera Bread was my favorite fast food chain until I met Zoup!
Our server Felicia was fantastic! The food was amazing,  blackened redfish with cream sauce to die for! And of course Pecan Pie!

Quetzally is a bit off the beaten path, just a few blocks away from South Street, in a fairly residential area. Doesn't look like much from the outside, but I think is a gem in Philly. Delicious and inexpensive Mexican food with fast service and really delicious food. There's also really lovely Latino music playing too.

My friend and I had the chips and guacamole to share, which was $6.50 I believe. It was an enormous portion though with lots of fresh beautifully green guac. The table does come with some chips and salsa though, so if you would just like some chips to satisfy your craving, you don't need to order an appetizer if you don't want. The tortilla chips were thicker than usual, but very fresh tasting and great scoopers for the guac. Loved it.

I had the Mexican veggies fried rice. Lots of veggies mixed into the fried rice, including some extra hot jalapeño peppers, with a sunny side up egg on top. Again, a HUGE portion and the dish was $6. So delicious and flavorful. 

Overall, would highly recommend if you're in this part of Philly. Lots of choices for Mexican food and happy wallets for inexpensive prices.

Sorry, but the fish taco was very mediocre and the ceviche tostada was sub par.
No free tortilla chips either. 

This place sucks and have crying kids.

Pass, next.

i used to eat at this place all the time when i was like 4. haven't been there for atleast 10 years. it's always packed and i think i celebrated my birthday there. mom and dad stopped bring me there for a reason i guess.
Staff was very nice but living in San Diego I guess my expectations were kinda of high. Booty sushi. Sorry guys! I would not recommend the zen or island roll

I visited their Bottleworks location at The Garage. Instantly, I really liked the care and attention the staff gave towards wearing their masks, even when they weren't engaging with customers. 

I previewed the Yelp reviews before visiting, so I knew I wanted to try their pasta. I was not disappointed. I'm sure the pizza is great, but their pasta combos I consider to be their "secret sauce." Bold flavors, fresh ingredients, delicious pasta. The picture I posted does not do it justice. It was good!!

The owner was just a delightful. She provided an Inca Kola for us to have the complete experience. 
All in all, please support this wonderful business - it checks all the boxes.

First off the delivery driver was late...before I opened the container the food smelled really bad & I know it was not the garlic because 
I am a garlic lover. Then when I opened the container there were 4 little shrimp in my "shrimp" scampi & when I finally tasted the food it was disgusting, there was absolutely to much lemon juice; I couldn't enjoy any part of the food because it was drowned int lemon juice. And after a few bite I threw the food in the trash . I am very disappointed & I wasted $12. The salad and bread was the only thing worth eating.
The wings are okay. The breadsticks taste stale. The pizza is barely edible. I don't plan on ordering pizza from them again, but might try their other options at a later point if I'm hungry enough.

Food: Bottomless soup and salad during lunch time as well as free tea is a yes to me! Their bentos which hold an assortment of goods neatly placed into a tray are to die for. Recommended rolls are the "Sweet Passion" and "Volcano Roll"

Service: Attractive and thoughtful servers who were quick on their feet to attend to our questions and bring our foods. I think I've made quite a friendship with them :) 

Atmosphere: Casual restaurant which maintains a sophisticated and proper air, especially during Dinner when servers are dressed up. Faint Japanese and Jazz music play lightly in the background. 

Overall: Kobe is a must go, baby!
Best Mexican place in the northeast. Service is always good and the enchiladas are good.

For my money this is one of the better tex-mex places east of the Mississippi.  It's not anywhere near the quality of good tex-mex in Texas or Arizona but it's not bad either.  They work had to please you with what they have - fish included.  

I've often asked for their pork instead of the beef or chicken that some dishes use by default.  It's usually a winner.  They are happy to add fresh jalapeno or poblano slices to your fajitas to jazz it up for you as well.  Just be certain to let them know you want the bell-peppers too or the cook might substitute instead.  

Their drinks are not whoo-hoo fantastic but they are pretty darn cheap during happy hour.  Some of the cheapest in town.  I give them a 5 star for effort.

(This is a review for the new location) BEST MEXICAN RESTAURANT IN THE CITY!!!!!!! Everything I've tried from them has been amazing and the atmosphere/ambiance of the restaurant is great, music not to loud or to low and the artwork throughout the restaurant is breathtaking.
Great pizza.  A bit of a rough start early on but they seem to have worked out the kinks. We order from there every week now. Love it

My husband and I were headed to IHOP, but as soon as we got out of the car, we were captivated by the amazing smell coming from California Tacos. Both my husband and I are from California and have found it difficult to find Mexican food similar here in Florida, so immediately we were sold on trying out this place for lunch. California Tacos did not disappoint. Their carne asada fries, or "Cali fries" are to die for and big enough for two, but my husband loved them so much he finished them all. Their burritos are large and stuffed! No skimping here. Their prices are more than affordable for the amount and quality of food you get. The staff is extremely kind and accommodating. Lastly, the owner is a California native! So you know it's authentic!

Friendly workers and good food. Slices from Ed's are definitely work the price, good size, great taste! The coated fries are the way to go! If you're feeling like something sweet, they always have treats at the front counter. The chocolate cake is delicious, and the baklavas is even better!! Don't hesitate calling Ed's!

Not a fan. Service was poor. The food was mediocre. I was actually worried upon leaving that I was likely going to get food poisoning from the shrimp. I came out okay but this place isn't good. It is a shame because the location is awesome. I wanted it to be great but bummer it sucked. Avoid. I got the gator bites (icky) and the shrimp pot which came with the nastiest sausage ever. Do not get either if you do go.
This was a cute place.  It wasn't overly crowded and tables weren't to close to each other.  Our first time here food and drinks were good! The waitress was also very friendly! We will def be back.

I'm pretty sure I've written a review for F&N's before.  I think this is a duplicate entry, but it's worth singing the praises of this place once again.

For me, F&N's is my neighbourhood diner, and quite a good one.  Count on it for a solid weekend breakfast/brunch when you can pull on some sweats and curl up in a booth with strong coffee.  Otherwise it serves all the diner comfort foods, sandwiches and "blue plates".   Curiously enough there is a strong selection of Asian items, often on the specials board.  It's often "beef cube in sauce", which hints at needing a better marketing approach, but many have told me it's quite good.

I tend to stick to the two eggs any style with bacon, hash and toast (sometimes with a breakfast sausage side).

Great place for breakfast. It is always busy so get there earlier or you will wait outside the door. It is one of the best places to enjoy the European home style cooking and oh boy, their Eggs Benedict are by far the best in town.

Has the best server!  Wendy, always ready with drink refills, attentive, and very knowledgeable of the menu.  Food came out extremely quick, and quite delicious.  Late afternoon on Saturday is full of young families so choose time depending on noise level.

I had the roast pork sandwich with rabe and provolone. I have to say that while it was overall a tasty sandwich, it did not live up to the hype. The greens were well cooked, the provolone was sharp, and the pork was moist. However something was missing. The pork just wasn't as flavorful as I was expecting. I personally thought it could of used more seasoning, imho. But then again they do provide gratis hot peppers for those who want it, so props to that. The guy who rung me up had a super thick accent and I could barely understand him. He was a nice dude though, he was impressed I finished the whole thing hehehe.

I don't get it.  The food isn't that great.  Why pay so much for such poor quality?  People say it's healthy, but why can't it be healthy and good?  I've eaten there 3 times thinking that it must have been me.  I'm done.  It's just not that great.  Overcooked burgers.  Strange blended drinks. uhhhhhhhhhh!

After touching down at MSY, we came here for dinner as I was in the mood for Asian fusion. Modern establishment located at Park Avenue Place with plenty of parking. Nice ambience going on.

MOPHO is known for their chicken wings ($12) and I'll give them that. The wings were nice, crunchy and flavorful with fish sauce. Haven't really had anything like that before. Bf enjoyed his glazed pork belly bowl ($15). I wanted something soupy so I built my own pho bowl. Coming from the bay where pho standards are high, it was average. The broth wasn't as flavorful as I preferred and there were interesting toppings.

I was excited about the alcoholic boba, but I'd say skip it. There were a few popping bobas in there, but the drink was icy, tasted artificial, and boba was hard. Service was pretty good; although the waitress kept checking in on us a few more times than we liked, we appreciated the gesture.

I love Miller's Ale House. I'm very familiar with the sports bar chain that I found in Florida over 20 years ago. They have 80 HDTVs. I'll say that again, EIGHTY HDTVs. I don't think a single one is smaller than 60". They have NFL Sunday ticket, NHL season pass, NBA league pass and a true HDTV signal. If you want a certain game, they've got it.

Why I love Miller's is simple. Great sports bar, terrific bar food and dinners, along with great beer and drink specials. $8 Miller Lite pitchers everyday, all day. A total of 48 beers on tap. Ranging from the obvious American beers, local micros, national micros, and international favorites. A full bar, with $2.95 Captain Morgan, Smirnoff with any mixer. Doubles are $5. Kettle One at $5.95 with any mixer, $9.95 doubles. I can't cover all the pricing, but this should give you a very good idea of how cheap it is to drink here. 

I'm in no way affiliated with Miller's, though my review may seem that way. I'm just excited this chain moved into my neighborhood, and I hope they succeed. Very worth the trip, you won't be disappointed!

Yuuummm! This pizza is so great and super fresh. The #5 is stellar, and these brunch pizzas (only available during brunch) were epic! The one with Lox was a super interesting take on brunch pizza. Pair it with a beer from NOLA brewing and you have the perfect meal!

Next up I'm going to try their slice lunch special which includes a slice, salad, and beer or non-alcoholic tea if you can't have a boozy lunch.

A very cool place with a good selection of craft beer and solid pub style food.  It was also suggested to visit the men's room to see the decor and it was very amusing.  I'll try to make it back on my next trip to FL.

Very disappointed with my chicken portabella sandwich I got yesterday, I have gotten it a few other times and it was completely different. I spoke to the manager and was told she spoke to the chef and she followed the recipe. I order from here at least once a week it was one of my favorite places but after yesterday not so much unfortunately. This is what my chicken portabella sandwich looked like absolutely nothing like the pic on the menu.

We ate here tonight seeing the new place as we headed down town. My husband got the hot chicken and I got the ?reverse Cobb Salad with hot chicken. Both were fabulous! The chicken was crunchy and spicy! The salad was a large portion loaded with veggies blue cheese lots of bacon and spicy chicken. Service was quick and with great smiles and warmth. We will be back.
While the food is generally pretty decent, the service is absolutely horrible at the bar. Awful. How insulting coming from a service background, and being treated the way we were today.

We frequent the place often.. this and the Kirkwood location. My grandson's favorite place! 
Lately, the steak has been a little dry, so we switched to the pork chop! Very good.
The problem last night --- my daughter was eating a salad and a huge dead moth was wrapped into the lettuce. She was disgusted of course.  The manager assured us they are professional and clean and that moth must have flown in from outside while a door was open.  He would give her the meal free.  
As we continued to eat... while debating if we should be eating, there was a curly black hair in the baked potato! 
Enough is enough. We were done. We didn't report the hair to the manager, feeling he wouldn't believe us and think the whole thing was made up... but EWWW!
This place was amazing! Nothing like any other wine bar we have been to. Can't wait to come back

Well, went for the first time tonight. We live close and people are always saying how good it was. We made a reservation a week ahead. Got there, seated right away and then.....waited...waited... no server. We waited about 15 minutes then we noticed the table across from us just got seated and the server took their drink order. A server walked by and I flagged her.. she was like "hasn't she been over yet? " she took our drink order. At this point we were thinking we would leave and pick up Taco Bell' well finally our server comes. She's like are you ready to order? No sorry or anything! Yup lets order. Then she goes over to another table and spouts off all of the specials and happy hour!! Took their order right away!! Like a minute after they were seated!! Wtf? Later she made a snarky comment that we had to wait. The food was awesome! I had the shrimp al Greco, And hubby had the crab cake. Very good.  Ceaser salad blah.  No flavor. We have had better service at Bonefish! We made a comment to the manager on the way out. She seemed like oh well. I guess this is a good place for snowbirds but never again for us!
The Banana pancakes were amazing! My husband had Shelly's pancakes they were perfect as well! We will return!
Got delivery with DoorDash but they forgot my sandwich. They said they would refund me so I'll add a star if that happens.
PF Changs never disappoints and remains our favorite destination for Hanukkah and Christmas Eve meals. On today's list is Orange Peel Beef, Crispy Honey Chicken, and Salt and Pepper Prawns.
So good! Everything is vegan and excellent quality. There were a variety of interesting options to choose from. 10/10 would recommend!
Love this place  Love the Schnitzel with the white paprika sauce. Great portion too. I always have left overs.

My boyfriend and I went on Saturday night, 11/10/12. Actually, we were headed to Bobby's Burger Palace as we were both salivating for a really good burger and thought..hmm, Bobby Flay...it has to be good right? First, we walked in to Bobby's and the first thing I noticed was the ugly decor and the Burger King-type atmosphere. Then, there was the long line at the counter where, we presumed we were to order our food. NOPE! Not for us! So, we strolled passed Bahama Breeze to the Grand Lux Cafe..we figured since it was a pretty big place, it wouldn't be so crowded...WRONG! Long line of miserable-looking people waiting for tables. We were going to just leave the over-crowded mall parking lot and just go home and order a pizza when, as we were strolling past Bahama Breeze, we decided to go in and have a look.  The decor was very nice and we felt transported to the islands. Much to our surprise, we were seated right away and in a booth no less!  We were delighted to see burgers on the menu so, much to the delight of our waiter, we ordered exactly the same thing. We received our burgers in 15 mins. or so and they were awesome! One of the best burgers I've had in a long time. We got the Applewood Bacon and Cheddar burger. They were cooked to perfection and served on a brioche bun. The fries were a bit disappointing though. I found them to be rather limp. I would suggest they offer steak fries and cook them well done. But that's just my preference. We will go back again and try something else on the menu like their fresh fish. I recommend Bahama Breeze!

Fusion makes me wary.  The descriptions sound so good that you're expecting a culinary Kristin Kreuk on your plate.  However, the beautiful meal of your mind's eye never comes to be as you sadly hunch over and pick at the Frankenstein creation of misplaced flavors on your plate.  Nectar, however, thoughtfully chooses a minimal mix of cultural DNA to provide an excellent hybrid dining experience.

So hip, so zen dining room fits in with the best center city has to offer.  Service is attentive and helpful, with no difference in the quality of the food or service between our prime time and off peak visits.  

Good wine list with a nice Sake selection.  Sake tasting was fun with some intriguing choices, while the carafes keep single serving choices nice and cold.  

Edamame dumplings are incredible.  Filled with a smooth edamame puree atop delicious chanterelles in a savory herb sauce, they single-handedly prove that fusion can work.  

The seasonal tuna and salmon roll is as fresh, delicate, and perfect with the eel sauce.  The no rice roll with tuna, salmon, and striped bass is delicious, though difficult to handle with chop sticks. 

Grilled calamari salad with chorizo, parmesan, and lemon vinaigrette was excellent.  Just the right amount of everything.

I was hesitant about the crispy panko calamari and edamame, but the amazing spicy papaya and tamarind hoisin dipping sauces allayed any doubt about how good it would be.  

Steamed pork buns with hoisin and lettuce were good, but not at the same level as the others.

Entrees get the trend of success going again.  Striped bass with mushrooms, asparagus, and a black truffle sauce that tastes very similar to the one that came with the dumplings.  Not a bad thing as it's wonderful.  Bass was moist with a nice sear.

Tenderloin with Thai basil, Chinese broccoli tips, scallion, and chili peppers was substantial and excellent.  As you may have surmised, this is far more on the Asian side of the flavor spectrum.  Chunks of tenderloin were cooked correctly with a nice sear, and the sauce had a solid kick to it.

The ribeye with heirloom tomato salad was juicy, flavorful, and cooked correctly.  It's been a while since I've had a steak done right, and it was good.  I think I am about ready to write off steakhouses, they seem to be the only places that can't cook steak.  Wife pilfered many of my tomatoes on account of their deliciousness.

Chocolate torte is pretty delicious.  Blood orange sauce does the perfect job of complementing the different layers and textures of chocolate.  Mini doughnuts are simple and delicious.  Coffee cake with maple anglaise, orange sauce, cinnamon ice cream, and orange confit is pretty ridiculous, probably my favorite of all the desserts.  The creme brulee trio has some nice flavors, and while the carrot cake is a bit subtle, the German chocolate gets it just right.  

One of the best restaurants in the Philadelphia region.

Delicious food!  I've had some of the burgers, sandwiches, 4 Horsemen--everything has been excellent!  This place is on the ground floor of a high-rise apartment building down the street from me.  I would probably be here all the time except the food is not the healthiest (depending on what you order--but if I come here, I'm gonna order something fatty and meaty!).  The location is somewhat interesting and street parking can be hit or miss depending on when you come here (I walk since I live so close).  The staff is great and I wholeheartedly support the owner's restaurant venture!

Online order pick up is horrendous. In the past month, we had to wait for more than 25 minutes from the scheduled pick up time for our orders. The staff is apologetic and both times, we were told just waiting for one more item. Go wait in your car and we will bring it out to you. 30 minutes later, here comes our food. We understand restaurants are short handed during this difficult time but when you placed an order hour in advance, you would think it will be ready for pickup at the scheduled time. Unfortunately, tonight is the last time we will get food from here.

Here's the important stuff:

Price - It's reasonable but be CAREFUL cuz it can add up quickly.  It's type of place where you pair you dish with wine, and add an appetizer or dessert and then you can really see your check double in the end.

Service - Excellent in knowledge of the menu and hospitality, however there is a hint of pretentiousness.

Food - More hearty and heavy, but delicious.  Not as refined and elegant as you would assume of a French restaurant.

Here's the less important stuff:
Yes, it is French but the menu is more like "home-style" food.  So don't think Paris, but rather the country-side of France.  Which also explains why the prices are reasonable.  French dishes have some of the most difficult technical preparation out there; which how they justify those crazy prices.  Those are the super expensive meals that offer about 5 ounces food... but this isn't that kind of French restaurant.  Personally, I prefer it that way.

However, the staff comes off as if they are a high-end French restaurant.  Maybe that's their marketing ploy, so I'm not gonna knock it if it works for them.  But what I'm really saying is that don't expect the same type of service if you come in dressed kinda shabby.  Regardless, the servers are very intelligent and know a lot about ingredients and how things are prepared.  That is pretty rare, so I wanna highlight that.

Yes, I would quickly agree that restaurants like these are about taking your money.  BUT if they recommend a wine with your meal, you should at the least hear them out.  I had the cheese plate before my meal, and it made my main course taste rotten.  The server (Derrick) was smart enough to give me some complimentary white wine, which saved the dish and the experience.  

Honestly, the food isn't enough for me to come back.  But I see myself there again because the service is refreshing.

The tacos are mind blowing and the margaritas are so fresh! But I just have to rave about our server, Keira! She was delightful, patient and really helped guide us through the dining experience. She also had great recommendations for things to do around town which were on point and really rounded out the rest of our vacation.
Good food can be pretty easy to find but it's servers like Keira who make the experience memorable!

I'm pretty sure if you're in the New Orleans area then you already know about this gem! It's so popular and always super busy!! Thank goodness they have a covered patio outside because sometimes you have to wait a bit for a table. I don't come down often but I've noticed they've remodeled the outside in recent months. They carry a full menu of authentic and amazing Vietnamese cuisine. Everything I've ever tried here is always delicious. The fried rice, Com Suong, Pho, Bun Bo Hue, everything. Wonderful! And the bakery!!! OMG. The tastiest freshly baked bread you can find! They make the ever so famous banh mi sandwiches too. They're great for a quick lunch if you're on a break from work. King cake isn't my favorite but they are known for the best around. With lines sometimes down the street to get them during Mardi Gras!! Oh I almost forgot. The salted coffee smoothie is one of a kind!! I've never been able to find it anywhere else. It's a must try. You won't regret stopping here on your next trip to New Orleans East!

Sweet Jesus.  This place is fantastic.  Hubby got fried catfish with collard greens, cheddar mash.  I had crawfish etoufee with greens and hush puppies (not on menu, but saw it as a side for another entree and couldn't resist).  Daughter ordered chicken tenders and mac and cheese.  We all cleaned our plates, and the only complaint is that they ran out of the bread pudding.  I'm so glad my husband and I each got our own collard greens, because I love him, but I'm not sure I would have shared mine.  These were hands down the best I've had anywhere in the country - a touch of sweetness but not syrupy, right amount of meat, good acidity and just a little bit of body left in the greens.  

I hesitated on the etoufee because I wasn't in the mood for something overly creamy, and the waitress offered a sample.  You had me at crawfish.  It was loaded and while rich in flavor, the base wasn't overly heavy.  Oh yes, the waitstaff.  We ate at a high-end downtown steakhouse the day before, and can't stop talking about how much more attentive the ladies at Chef Dan's were.

The Chef himself came out and he was so likable... was really sweet with our daughter who wasn't feeling well.  We will definitely be back.

*Note - their website said they weren't open Saturday for lunch.  We drove by anyway and were pleasantly surprised.

This place used to be pretty good, but tonight I got a banh mi sandwich and it was awful. No flavor and the bread was rock hard. I know it's hard to keep bread fresh, but once it's stale, just tell folks sandwiches aren't available.
Service was a bit confused though they tried. The food was excellent. Cooked to order and good sized servings. The band that night was very good.

Nestled adjacent to the city's historic African American neighborhood, Top Hog can be difficult to find for those unaccustomed to Gallatin but it is worth the effort. The pork sandwich is big, juicy, full of flavor, amazing. But this place also has one of the best catfish sandwiches around. If you are hungry, get both! Prices are very reasonable and service is friendly. Take out is available, which is what we used yesterday. Some limited outside seating. 

The business is cash only, has always been that way. We invented ATMs so places like Top Hog can stay traditional. Plenty of parking but at lunch it can be busy.

Hands down the best Chinese food in Tucson. I come here at least once a week with friends, sometimes more. I love the spicy dishes the most as well as the hot and sour soup. The staff is always really friendly and attentive too. Very authentic Chinese food definitely reccomend it. Great flavor and great prices.

I have no idea why some locals despise this place. Maybe they feel it's too touristy or they're too snobby since they live on the beach. I really do like this place (am a local). Have been for years. Best prices on oysters and stone crabs, bigger and tastier too. The wings are actually pretty good. Service has always been great. And the sunset view, priceless. There's live music and the drinks...are ok. Don't forget the she crab soup. All of the Frenchys locations are good. Nice place to bring family from out of town if you're a local. Can get busy at times

Beautiful decor, wonder staff and customer service but the food was only okay. I ordered a shrimp and kale salad that wasn't all that great. I also ordered the pulled flatbread which was delicious but there was something grossely sweet in it that kept throwing me off when I took a bite.

All morning and afternoon I was watching TV and got bombarded by Popeye's commercial for beer can chicken. I decided to make their investment in this heavy and expensive marketing pay off by going out and paying for an order of it. 

I went through the drive thru put in an order for the beer chicken combo and ordered two extra sides and a drink ! I gave my money got the soda and then was asked to wait in the parking lot for a couple of minutes for my order. 

After 5 minutes I went inside dropped my receipt on the counter and asked for my money back because, "I did not come through the drive thru to wait 5 minutes in the parking lot for my order."

Counter dude said, "Let me go get the manager." 

The manager walked out from the back opened the drive thru register with her keys and dropped my money on the counter in front of me without saying a word and walked away. 

Thanks for the free soda.

I am vegan and LOVE bahn mi, so I was so excited about this place. I ordered the tofu rolls and the tofu bahn mi with no mayo and my total was only 7.50 for a large amount of food. It was sooooo good! Perfectly cooked tofu and a super soft roll. AMAZING!! 10/10 reccomend... can't wait to try the pho!!

Mediocre at best. I understand they don't take reservations especially being new-so that said-there was a wait for 45mins on a Sunday night. Finally got seated-took another 10mins to be noticed-
There are No chips and salsa as a free starter...which semi sucked...
Service was lousy-and when we finally started to get served they forgot 2 out of the 4 tortilla soups we ordered (which wasn't great-sorry-just wasn't) AND they forgot my salad that came w/the carne asada. Which again-not great. 
The worst part-another table got seated a good 30mins after us and got served apps the same time as us and had their dinner before us. 
Sorry-we won't be back. Too many other amazing Mexican restaurants in the area to go to instead.

Well I am amazed, my son and I went to market grill for the first time and I was disgusted by the entire experience. The place smelled gross the moment we came in. We ordered crab cakes which were the best thing we had, sadly that does not say much at all. No real amount of crab, a total rip off. Then I ordered after a strong recomendation from the waiter the meat loaf, this is where their fate was sealed. The meatloaf was dry as the sahara desert, the mashed potatoes tasted instant. And the gravy was for sure nasty cheap powdered stuff. The biscuits were good as well as the mixed vegetable of the day. The waiter came up and asked us how the food was. When I nicely mentioned that the meatloaf was dry his exact comment to me was " ummmm I am sorry", he did not ask if he could get anything else or take it off the bill he had a total lack of concern or respect for me and my money. I will never ever go back there again and I will be telling ALL my friends the same! Poor job market grill, you ruined it forever for us!

Greek salad with gyro meat - large portion, deliciously thin meat. Gyro is solid and the fries are excellent.

Ambiance inside is casual/sports barish. But no need to go inside as they have a drive through window!!!

Wow,what a wonderful dining experience,the service,the food all wonderful,best dinner since moving to sparks. There were 5 of us i had the mixed grill scampi lamb and filet and honestly it couldn't havw been better,cooked perfectly came with soup or salad had the soup jerk seafood chowder it was great flavorful,really good job. Dinner also came with choice of potato and veggie of the day today was brocini,very good.great bread assortment and watermelon sorbet as a palete cleanser,what a great meal.make sure to make reservations always booked.

my wife and i went there for dinner and after being  seated it took forever to place our order and the place wasnt even busy. after a long wait  the waiter brought only my food and not my wifes, mumbling something about a problem thawing out the food. i waited almost 10 minutes then started eating because my food was already cold,her food still had not arrived. if i wanted to eat alone i would of stayed home. her food finally arrived, was mediocre at best. the whole experience sucked, was a big waste of money.
I LOVE dry dock! Great place to sit, relax and enjoy some awesome food. I honestly don't know how it's not always overrun with people.

Mathias made our Friday lunch SO fun. He surprised us with a sample of the Harper's Punch when we arrived and made us cocktails based on our personalities. We had the best time and loved the cheeseboard we split. 100% will be back to visit and hopefully see Mathias again!!

Really disappointing. 

First, let me say that the cookies are outstanding, but pricey--especially the ones they do for the holidays.

That said, I'm writing this review because of their cakes. I recently tried one of their cupcakes and was extremely disappointed. The frosting had no flavor whatsoever and the cake seemed stale. The biggest issue I have with this bakery, however, is that their cake was recently served at a party I attended. When we tried the cake, all of us looked at one another like something was wrong. It was like a scene out of a movie. The cake had no flavor. None. Frosting maybe tasted like butter, but certainly wasn't sweet? How is that possible? Needless to say, none of us ate the cake, which was extremely awkward for the host / buyer of the cake. The party then focused on discussing how bad it was, which was a first. How can a bakery get cookies right and cakes so wrong? Doesn't make sense, especially given all of the positive reviews.

To the owners of the bakery, please fix your cakes. Your cookies are awesome, especially the shortbread...but how were the cake products I've had so bad? Am I missing something? I've had some amazing cakes in my life and expected that to be the case here. Definitely not the case.

Always fresh & boiled stuff cooked perfectly....
Never too salty or too "over-seasoned".
My favorite place for boiled crawfish & lobster!

Very fast! We never sat down we just ordered to go so I can't review any servers but very fast and the food was good! I got the hawaiian chicken sandwich and it was BOMB! My boyfriend go the jerk chicken sandwich and he said it wasn't too spicy at all and it was good! Definitely recommend!

My favorite Thai restaurant in Tampa. Food is very fresh and tasty. Small, quaint, very clean. Family owned and staff is very friendly. Just came home from having Panang Curry Shrimp with brown rice and a glass of sweet plum wine. My husband had the Baby Born Chicken - lots of tender baby vegetables in a brown sauce. Chicken was very tender and tasty. Portions are very generous. I always end up bringing half home for another meal. Next time you are in the mood for Thai food, give Benjarong Thai a try!

Got to the airport nice and early, decided on a cup of coffee. Despite the line I decided to grab a cup from River City. Mistake! I only bought a bottle of water and a small drip coffee, the cashier said she didnt hear mthat i ordered a coffee so had to wait for my cup. She wasnt happy about me! Then the dark drip was empty and the gal behind the counter was very unpleasant when i asked if there was any more! I didnt feel that a small drip coffee and a bottle of water was an extremely difficult order but the looks on the workers faces sure made it seem that i had asked the world. Won't bother next time!

Walked in, party of 2. Stood unacknowledged for several minutes. Finally hostess came over. Asked to sit outside. All empty tables were covered in plates n glasses. She bussed one quick so we could sit there. Sat 15 minutes at the table and was not acknowledged by anyone, so we got up and left. What a joke.

This is really one of my favorite eating haunts, constantly visited throughout my four years @ UCSB. Their food is consistently good (read: the dishes are consistently executed and consistently enjoyed upon consequent visits). The on-tap beer, while relatively limited in options, is usually served promptly and by a friendly waiter. I would highly recommend the $21 filet mignon + 2 sides dinner, or the "auld favorite burger" for around $9. I have really never had any issues dining here; the only criticism I can offer is that occasionally the service is a bit slow, especially on busy / music nights.

Amazing! Food was great and so was the service! I had the Cajun Carbonada and it looked so good that I didn't notice I hadn't taken a picture until after I was half way through my meal. Again, AHHHHHMAAAAAZING! Perfect kick, an abundance of shrimp and sausage. The flavors just natural blend together. Really enjoyed!
Soccer & London fan's Indy paradise!! Great food and drinks, but it's usually pretty busy so not always the best customer service!

I have been here twice now, once in the sushi side and once in the hibachi side and both times the service and food were both amazing. The restaurant is plot in two so if you want a communal dinner there isn't a problem but if you want a more intimate one on one that can be done as well. The hibachi chef was well trained and knew all of the table show displays that are sometimes ignored. This has quickly become one of our favorite restaurants.

This is the second time I have visited this location and problems both times. See attached picture for their version of large fries. Hmm, maybe that's more like a medium. No extras in the bag either as I had hoped. My singular weekly cheat day thwarted by a lazy or uninformed employee.
Loved it here! Highly recommend the beet salad, bone marrow, uovo pizza, and the gnocchi. Everything was so delicious, and the wait staff was very attentive and helpful! Can't wait to go here again!

This place has great food, great music, and great beer. And, you know, a hip young Asian client named Vichet. Who could ask for more?

You? Well cut that shit out.

I came in with 3 friends from Cornell, one being my roommate and the other two happening to be in town to visit. I ordered the chicken-fried chicken. Two words: tasty, tasty. 

The gravy was rich, creamy, and meaty without being too salty or overpowering. The home fries - crab-apple sized chunks of potato crispy-fried and spiced - were fantastic. Even my scrambled eggs, which, I mean, are really just eggs, were fluffy and ready to beat the record for ending up in my stomach. All this, for 11 bucks. Seriously. I need to go brunch more often.

Nothing breaks my brain like a comfort food filled Saturday brunch. They even had Ithaca beers available, so I indulged like I was still far above Cayuga's waters.

And James Brown, Marvin Gaye, and Al Green were crooning on the radio the whole time. Wonderful.

Will definitely come back.

Pro-tip:
I hear this place gets insanely busy on Sundays. So... nurse your Saturday morning hangover instead!
This is a fabulous place. The food is fantastic and the staff is very kind and attentive. The food tastes fresh and great portion sizes. A must try if in the Delmar Loop area!

Alligator Po Boy and Beignets as big as your mouth! I'm no creole expert, but I loved everything I ordered and tried a little bit of what other diners with me got. 
Every.
Single.
Thing was delicious.

Their creations are definitely worth the 5 stars but I wish I could give them 7 or 8 for service and friendliness of staff. On our first visit we met the husband and wife owners and found out all about them.

You really felt like you were guests in the dining room of their home and they just happen to be world-class creole chefs. It's the kind of place you want to take anyone visiting from out of town to show them what kind of "local" place Indy can pull off.

The comparison to Yats is pretty natural but I never think those are fair either way because you really need to have them both in front of you. No matter which is better Indy wins because both Yat's and Borel's rock and their owners are hardwired into the community they serve.

Excellent ramen! I had the karai (spicy) ramen and it was amazing. 
Walk up to the counter to order, and they bring your food out to your table. Bring cash, because they don't accept credit/debit cards, which is a minor inconvenience and the only thing that keeps me from giving 5 stars.

Can't beat the prices. Great crawfish pie and it's only 13.00, wow. Oysters on the half shell was outstanding. Managers very friendly as well as waitstaff.  They take good care of you and the kids. Great job.

Great food, great service! I love this place the ladies (sisters) who work here are always nice and very welcoming. The food is fun, flavored well and reminds me of home (Africa) especially when I can't have anymore burgers and pizzas lol. Keep up the good work and I will keep supporting.

I'm a local and I've been going to Brophys my entire life, but recently I was there and overheard the manager Nora talking negatively to another employee about a patron! I found it to be completely unprofessional and tacky. That particular day my peel and eat shrimp was really mushy and the ceviche tasted old. Maybe she should concentrate on her job rather then talking about customers that are paying for good food and service!
The pizza is awesome, but their pasta is nothing impressive and their chicken is definitely frozen and poor quality.
Great place to eat! Burgers are delicious!!! Fries with anything on top is so good! New owners are wonderful!! Makes the place a homer feel.

Was hungry about noon this past Wednesday and ended up stopping here for a little lunch.  After studying the menu decided on the green salsa pork burrito.  When it was ready I had the best burrito filled with well spiced shredded pork mixed with grilled potatoes, beans and green chili sauce.  It was all wrapped up in a perfectly warmed up tortilla and served with yet another spicy red salsa.  It was so good.  I want to go back and try something again.

Our experience was extremely frustrating. We were not waited on for 15 minutes into us being seated. The first thing we ordered when we were seated was for a glass and a half of moscato. Our 3 person party ordered drinks and an appetizer. When the server returned 15 minutes later with our drinks, I was surprised to see that there was not a glass of wine on her tray. I figured she forgot and reminded her. She said would get it and came back with no wine when she brought the breadsticks. I asked yet AGAIN and she asked me what I ordered. Our food then didn't even come out for another hour and it was cold. When we expressed our frustration she responded that if we came on any other night than Sunday it wouldn't have been so bad. I didn't realize there were days customers weren't supposed to come eat. Never going back.

Absolutely love this place! I love to walk over in the morning & grab my latte. The service is exceptional and the attention to detail is what keeps me coming back. I always try their featured drinks & they are always delicious.

They sent a letter "dismissing" my daughter from the practice over this review! I dismissed myself after you made her sit on the floor with a cast on her leg! Shame on you and your office for how it treats people! I should take this up with county!

A girlfriend of mine recommended this place for lunch today for us and our two kids. When I first walked in I thought very traditional. It was nice and clean though. My son had the 2 sushi roll lunch special with soup or salad he just ate the Mexican rolls he is only 7 but the tempura shrimp in the roll was fresh and crispy. I ordered the bulgogi bento lunch box. It was a sampler of that, California rolls, gyoza, and some tempura veggies and shrimp. I've tasted better Korean food but it was still not bad. Prices were reasonable just as I would expect it to be and everything was satisfying. I have nothing bad to say about the service or food I'm always open to try new restaurants out. I would join my friend again for lunch there if she wanted because it's not really close to home for me.
It's soft serve not real ice cream, but good. Kids liked it. Service a little slow. Only outside seating this time of year a little chilly. Ate in car not a fan.

The almost prototypical local Italian joint. Local Italian joint service, local Italian joint decor. Pretty good soup (chicken velvet). The Tortellini is also good. The house salads need a little help, but the in-house creamy Italian dressing is quite tasty. Overall good enough to go back to but not a standout.

Great atmosphere. I love the decor. The chefs are super nice and the service is knowledgeable and timely! They have the best hummus and falafel in the area. Plus it's right off the tow path so just a perfect spot.

We had an amazing dinner tonight! There were 7 of us and shared a couple appetizers (Brussel sprouts, and Rangoons) that were all tasty and cooked well. Each of us tried different main courses and everyone was happy with our choices. The Caesar salad with cauliflower and broccoli was delicious! We all shared the cobbler for dessert and could have had more...
Reasonable prices and great food- couldn't ask for more! Can't wait to come back for their happy hour very soon!
Great cheese steaks which can hold up to any city steak!    Good fast service and affordable prices!  A true DELCO landmark.

Love coming here. During the most recent visit, Hector provided exceptional customer service. He was polite, professional, and kind to my children. Although I am a Tucson native, we recently relocated from out of state and had some questions about the menu. Hector was quick to offer samples and was patient. I appreciate that level of customer care! Our food was delivered to our table fast and exactly how we ordered. This location happens to be the closest to my home but it's also my favorite:) Highly recommend!

Mother's is the destination for Po Boy's in New Orleans.  Delicious!  The hard part is getting in - but luckily they are open early so Po Boy for breakfast!  Get the Debris - so good.  The bread makes the sandwich.....they have limited beer on tap, and make a great bloody mary!

Love the options at Cafe Patachou! I always enjoy their Vegan Cuban Bowl, but their salads and sandwiches are also delicious. The servers are also fantastic and treat you very well. The only reason I wouldn't give the restaurant 5 stars is because it's very expensive to make accommodations. I have a few intolerances and I figured I could just ask for substitutes for the meat or sauces, but everything is an additional up charge. I just wish it was easier to modify their dishes and they were more transparent with how expensive it would be to make substitutions.

Food is overrated and overprice at best it's a 1.5, The shrimp and fish burrito AKA the agave burrito its really a rice burrito hardly shrimp or fish. Save your money stay away!!! You're better off going to Costco and getting a hotdog or slice of pizza.

Today I went here with my mom and they said since I wanted a water with my meal (no caffeine or sugar) that I could not get the 99 cent treat that comes with the meal. I used to go here everyday and i will never go back again. They were very rude.

Great Korean food, great service! As an avid Korean food eater, most Korean restaurants will have a no-nonsense ambience, which is fine for me since I hate stuffy, low-lit restaurants. I think the reason Ktown BBQ stands out is its service. Most Korean restaurants are run by staff with limited English. Ktown's staff and owner are all fluent in English and will gladly help the non-Korean diner by fielding questions, offer suggestions, and talk Philly sports.
The only knocks I would say is that if you want to do-it-yourself BBQ, they don't have it. Which is fine for me, since I don't want to leave smelling like I've been manning a grill. They BBQ their meats well back in the kitchen. Knock 2 would be occasionally I would get a watery soon tofu. 7 out of 10 times it'll be perfect, but the other times they'd be happy to re-do it for you.
Final knock would be their fabulous Koagies that have been gaining local fame in the area. The spicy chicken and spicy pork are all fabulous on the seeded hoagie roll. Personally, I think theres a bit too much bread for the meat and flavor. My suggestion would be to scoop out some of the bread and find the perfect balance of bread and meat.
The blue Owl Restaurant Bakery has change.  The serving sizes and the bakery have made servings 30 percent smaller.  Wow what a way to drive away customers after years of great food and baked goods.
Wow. Italian cuisine how I have missed you. I absolutely adored the Branzino and lobster with Roasted vegetables.
Terrible food, Hugh disappointment... communication with the manager was terrible. This restaurant could use some training skills, and a new cook

Sneakily placed in the middle of a menu full of deli sandwiches and American breakfast staples, are 3 options of Greek specialties: mousaka, gyro, and chicken souvlaki. For the random amount of 8 dollars and 30 cents, you get a plate of mousaka with a side salad and a roll. It is a pretty amazing deal.

Mousaka is a host of some of my favorite things. I enjoyed the varying flavors and textures of my layers of cheese, meat, sauce, and eggplant. There wasn't a strong showing of bechamel, but nobody is perfect.

Sandy's mousaka is definitely one of those hidden gem lunches that get me all warm and fuzzy inside.

http://midtownlunch.com/philadelphia/2010/09/20/by-the-beard-of-zeus-home-cooked-mousaka-at-sandys/

This was my first time to this place. It was only two of us and we didn't order that much. A Waffle and a breakfast sandwich to be exact. We waited for over 40 minutes for our food. The waitress didn't tell us what the hold up was until we asked. And it was some bullshit story about the computer not registering our food. This is after tables of 4 and 6 that were sat after us had already received their food. After we finally received our food, I asked if I could talk to manager, and our waitress said he or she wasn't there! Mind you, this was a busy Saturday morning for brunch. While I don't think it racially motivated, I must say that I'm black and the groups that came after us and received their food before us were Caucasian. It did make me feel some type of way.  If I wasn't really hungry I would of left. And I don't believe it dining and dashing even though in this case it was warranted. Not the best experience.

This location is new to the area, they moved from their old location in Glen Eagle Shopping Center.
I've been here many times since it's opening and have never had an issue. The staff is super friendly and the entire restaurant is clean. 
I love their ribeye steak it's my favorite!!
Love this place. My son is addicted to the meatball sandwiches, I prefer and Italian hoagie. Everyone that works there is super friendly. It's the closet thing to the candy stores that used to exist.

Went here this past weekend for my sister's birthday.... sad interior, dirty bathrooms (and you have to walk past the kitchen to get to the bathrooms, and the kitchen looked dirty too), and weak food I could have made better myself. 

Waitress was very friendly, and the beer selection was extensive (but still between $4-7 for a pint!). However, the food was cold, not spicy, bland, dull and ridiculously overpriced. 

My vegetarian fajitas were bland... the veggies looked like they had come from the supermarkets frozen veggie bags, and the only spice I tasted on them was pepper. Wayyyy too much pepper. I didn't think it was possible to screw up Mexican food, but the MFF needs to seriously re-think their menu and the quality of their food. Get back to basics guys! Use local veggies, meat and ingredients! Use chiles and better spices!

I would not recommend this place... could be a great Mexican place... but it just isn't :(

Called to arrange for a party of 8 and told they don't reserve table. Went someplace else. Next time in I saw tables with "reserved" notes on them. I guess you have to know somebody. They always have an attitude if you have more than 4 in your party and are NEVER helpful. I have been there when they are busy and there are empty tables sitting there full of crap and no one cleaning them to accommodate waiting customers. I go to other Beefs because I like the food but this one, even though it's blocks from my home, I now avoid entirely. Done with them !!!

The Cheesecake Factory never disappoints, food is always delicious.  We eat here about 6 times a year and it's one of my favorite places to bring the kids.  Try the fried Mac N Cheese....it's delicious, and not just for the kids!  Obviously dessert here is a must so make sure you pace yourself when you order dinner, or skip the appetizer so you have room to rock one of the 200 different cheescakes.  

We stopped by tonight for dessert only and had the Godiva brownie Sunday.  It's was good but not at the caliber of the cheesecake so next time I won't stray from the usual.  Had a nice time and sat in the bar.  Service was good and the manager came over to check on us.

Make sure to get there early because it's always a wait at the peak dinner times.  Be prepared for a 30 min wait any day of the year.

The biggest issue in my opinion is the menu.....does CCF need a 100 page menu?  It's a bit rediculous and it takes everyone 45 minutes to decide what to eat because the choices are a bit over the top..  Throw in the advertisements on the menu and it might take all day just to order.
Top notch for an elegantly evening and gourmet dinner! Taking your significant other here will definitely get you not the right track!

Went here after staying away for many years. The new renovation is definitely a plus. Chanal was an excellent server and so funny. The boiled seafood was delicious and so filling. Will definitely be back.

If you're in the mood for amazing, mouthwatering, delicious Italian food and you're willing to splurge a little (it's doable if you're not drinking vino but what's Italian without vino) CENA IS YOUR PLACE!

It's location is perfect for anyone wanting to continue their night to the walkable bars located right outside. 

Their service is great. Very attentive and friendly. Willing to help satisfy your pasta cravings. 

We ordered the Baby Kale to start - fresh, tasty and a healthy start to what's about to come next... Rustic Bolognese, which was recommended by our server, and for that we are forever grateful. I wish they did it Olive Garden style so it never ended. Get this, no questions asked. 

Basically I can't wait to return to Cena and try everything else on the menu and become a fat happy 1/3 Italian.

My date and I were happy to see that Goat Hollow has reopened and in fine form. We had the scallops which were delicious, but the otherwise tasty risotto was too salty for me. My date had the savory jambalaya; she observed that it was the only meal she'd had in a long time that was salty enough for her. I had the steak frites, excellent and the remoulade was perfect but the fries were-- well, too salty. Overall, the setting was fun, the service was very good, the food was excellent but someone should tell the chef-- please dial back the salt.

I'm writing this review an hour into my seating and they are so understaffed we didn't even get water for an hour. We had a reservation and had to wait 30 minutes to even sit, followed by an hour with no food still. Hilariously, I waited for an hour for a beer too and was told the bar was backed up. But when it came, my "draft" beer was in a bottle and warm. Apparently it takes an hour to pull a beer out of a case on the floor and walk it 30 feet. I don't fault the staff per se, they appear to be working hard. But they are so understaffed and overbooked they are doing themselves no favors. 

And oh, to top it off, someone at our table asked if they could add cheese to a panini and they refused citing a backed up kitchen. Seriously? Slapping a slice of cheese on? So the server had to get the manager to finally agree to add the cheese. That extra 5 minutes could have been used to, ya know, serve us?

The foods amazing. Maybe the best pizza in the area. Haven't fully explored the menu quite yet. The only reason it's not 5 stars is the prices. It's a little steep... large cheese pizza is $14. There are some other good pizza places in Pottstown and they aren't as expensive. Giovanni's is more of that special occasion type of takeout pizza...if that's even a thing.

The food was alright. Not good or bad. My issue was with the service. Our waiter was extremely slow. He would disappear for a long time then come back and see a drink was empty and say he would get another one. After awhile a woman waiting other tables would ask if we needed a drink and would say he is getting it. Then she would come back with one before him. This happened twice. I'm sure he was busy but come on. Plus the food took a long time to come out. not sure if that was the kitchen or him getting lost. We were very disappointed. I'll stick to the one in Brandon from now on.

Lots of hard surfaces and minimal decor...so go expecting a lot of noise.  Table next to us was filled with family (the owner's family) and they were exceptionally loud and close to drunk.  Food was decent -- not exceptional but decent. Beans and rice and salsa were all good, and that's one way to judge good Mexican food. Portions were large.  Tea was old but once I mentioned it she took it away and said we wouldn't be charged. 
Not a very pleasant meal. Food was good but the noise level ruined everything.  Service can only be described as fair.

Excellent Chinese food.  The eggplant was great, my friends said the wonton soup, fried rice and chow fun were all outstanding.  Very very good prices, but the staff were sort of on the not so friendly side.

All I can say is wow! We were there for the NFL Draft party. It was our first time, but certainly not last! It was all you can eat and drink which was great, but the service is what blew us away... Nothing short of amazing. The selection of food was what dreams are made of, the taste was exquisite, and the ambiance and setting of everything was the perfect atmosphere. I mean who thinks of popcorn lobster bisque and cotton candy pork belly? Fantastic combinations!

Their beef and cheese tamales are to die for! I was staying at a hotel in the area for a wedding and was craving Mexican food. I found this place in the local listings and decided to give it a try. I ordered the three tamale plate and chips with guacamole. It was later in the evening, around 7pm, and they were out of guacamole so they offered to make me a fresh batch! Great food and great customer service!

The pizza was so good here that my husband finished his then snatched my piece from my hands and ate it. We had the BBQ chicken pizza and tomato pie, both were excellent. Service was fast and courteous. Prices were reasonable. Can't wait for nicer weather to eat outside!

Had the Pete's Chicken Sandwich.  One of the best chicken sandwiches I have ever had.  Chiken was grilled with char marks served on a delicious Chibatta bun.  Onion rings and ranch dressing great, too.

Stopped in for lunch at 1:30 on a tuesday & the place was extremely busy (USF students and business crowd) but the friendly staff moved everyone through very quickly. This is my first time at this location, but not at Jason's. I love their gluten-free options and fresh salad bar! I had the 1/2 Mediterranean wrap with fruit and a side salad, and my hubby had the penne pasta with meatballs. They have delicious sweet tea too! Everything was good, the place was clean and service was excellent.
Our daughter recently moved nearby and we needed pizza for her friends who helped. It was delicious! I got the meat lovers pizza. It was heaped with meat. It's my favorite pizza now.
Try the new clam chowder! Such hot peppery goodness, ahhhhh!!! LOVE!

Gave away our reservation while we were sitting in the waiting area for 10-15 minutes awaiting a hostess to actually pay attention to us. Drove there for no reason. Really disappointed. Offered to kick out the people they had just sat down which would have been really rude. Wouldn't recommend this place for any special occasion or event where you need your reservation honored.

If you are in the area and wanting some delicious wood fired pizza this is my go to place.  Their mushroom truffle pizza is mouth watering. I've also had their charcuterie board and it was amazing. The mustard was the best I've had.
Awesome bourbon selection.  Amazing meat and cheese tray.  Service was absolutely impeccable.  I would highly recommend this if you are in Philly.

Outstanding salad, hand made pizza and a lot of high quality food for the price.

Fresh bread was soft and tasty. 

Waiter was nice.

Great place for family site down dinner. Very nice elegant interior.

This is THE spot for a cheap, greasy spoon breakfast on the weekend.

And, for the most part, the young and hip have yet to discover it.

Enjoy it while it lasts! Maybe I shouldn't even post this review...

Noticed this place while stumbling out of Scotty's one evening.  The first go round I just had the breadsticks and, well it was a Tuesday night so who am I to say no to their $1 pint draft special! Made it in again last night.  Wow, what a coincidence another Tues night! Actually tried their Portabella pizza this time which was pretty tasty and loaded with fresh ingredients.  Great pizza, breadsticks and oh did I mention the special on Tuesday?!?!

Looks like Don Ramon finally got their credit card reader and made it onto Yelp. The new owners opened the restaurant soon after Tamaleria Lupita closed but have been cash only for quite some time. The new owners have been trying some new touches such as soup and chips and salsa with each order, but the important thing is that the Mexican street food that they offer is excellent.

The tamales are very similar to the ones that Tamaleris Lupita offered with respect to size,  ingredients and taste. In my opinion, the steak taco is even better now with charred pieces of seasoned beef covered in onion and cilantro. The tortas are very large and offered with many ingredient options. They are almost big enough to feed 2 for lunch. If what you want isn't on the menu, just ask. I'm sure Don Ramon will fill your request if possible. 

For those that did not read the reviews for Lupitas. The restaurant is in a strip mall. It is still a relatively small "order at the counter" place with about 10 - 12 tables and little décor. Food is brought out to the table when ready but there is no wait person available. Just good food and nice owners.
This place is the epitome of unprofessionalism, rudeness, would never ever ever patronized this establishment again.   The owner is the most arrogant, angered person ever met

Their breaKfast is one of the best I've had in Philly. The stuffed French toast is the best dish! But their eggs and hashes are also good. The location is pretty quaint, it's built within two homes on a regular street and it gives it a more home-y feeling. The bathroom was a tight fit but the food is so good that it does not really matter. The servers were also super accommodating and pleasant. It seems to be a family business and run like a good one. Will be back if I'm ever back in the city!

Not impressed!  Country style, and not that great! Don't waste your time. Simple menu, fried chicken tasted as if it was from KFC, just cost 5 times that!  There are many better places for brunch in Nashville

First off I would just like to thank Symphani our waitress for the exceptional service. She accommodated 7 of us as a walk-in table and was so kind in splitting our bill 7 ways, remembering who split which meals too. She also was so fun to talk to, and at the same time was really patient with how much time we took to decide on our meals. Top tier service! I hope I get her again when I come back.

As far as the food goes...it just really hit the spot. We started off with the $6 waffle fries for the table which I didn't get a picture of because they were gone in about 2 seconds. Whatever it was it had like hatch chili's and bacon on it (which I don't normally like to put on other foods but I would make an exception for these fries). And we got a double order which was perfect for our group. Several people in the group got the pear-fect cocktail and all loved it, and they had a solid selection of wines (according to my friend Lizzy - the honorary wine connoisseur of the evening & so helpful to me in writing this review since I myself do not drink alcohol) and I had a root beer which was incredibly refreshing and never empty! (Again, thank you dear Symphani!!)

The salads were divine, and apparently the Caesar typically comes with whole anchovies on top but Lizzy opted out this time, but she said she always gets the Caesar when she comes because of how good it is. We also got the vodka pizza and I added pepperoni to my half since I was splitting it and it was arguably the best pepperoni I've ever had. It reminded me exactly of the pizza in NYC from Prince St pizza. Also I never eat crust on pizza but the crust was so good I ate every last bite. It was big enough to share but small enough that if you wanted your own you could definitely eat your own. I will be going back, it was DELICIOUS!

Interesting looking place, a bit hard to find. Parking was a bit difficult.

Food was ok but not spectacular. It is presented well but lacks flavor. My smothered burrito was a bit bland, and was like a Chipotle burrito with zucchini. Since I was just passing through I will probably not be back.

I love kolaches! My favorite is the pizza one, because I LOVE PIZZA! It is best to stop by early since that is where you'll get the best selection possible.  The cost does add up if you're buying some for work, but everyone is happy when they're eating it. 

Another reviewer said to try the sticky buns - YES! This is a must! It reminds me of the rolls my dad used to buy from the local bakery back home (but they weren't sticky buns). 

The service is not that bad for the times I have been there. If you go there close to closing, maybe you might feel a little horrible.
LOVE this place!  The food is good and you don't have to feel guilty about eating it.  Each member of the wait staff I've had has been polite and kind.  It's expensive but worth it!
Totally awesome!!!  Yummy and such a good price!!!  I can take my whole family here and have great food for under $30!!!  Best pho around!!!!!!!!!!!

Blown away!  Stopped by on the fly this afternoon because their A-frame board out front said Bangers N Mash.  

Here's what I had...
Started with a pot of English tea and a $2 app -Bacon Chips.  The chips had such a good flavor and were served with homemade tartar sauce.  My husband choose the fish n chips.  His face melted when he tasted the fries.  Cut fresh and triple fried in fish oil. Dynamite! The fish was crispy on the outside.  Flaky and light on the inside.  Perfect! For myself, I had the bangers n mash.  No pun intended, it was bangin'! 
Don't skip dessert! Their Puddings Menu sounds amazing, although we had a peanut butter tart from their display stand!

In addition to the food, our server was very friendly.  The manager came over to make small talk with us as well and the owner/cook came out at the end of our meal to ask how his food was.  

Really great people and business to support!  Give them the opportunity to serve you next.  You won't be disappointed.

Okay so I admit I used to always go here until the one off Myrtle opened since I live downtown. However we returned to this one today since we were going see a movie at Edwards on overland. 

It was busy during lunch time so we had expectations that our food might take longer and that's chill. Anyway we finally got our food and my girlfriends pasta she ordered wasn't warm and we asked the server if we could get it heated up and her response was "we have a microwave you can go use" and got all huffy when we were like we'll can you just do it? She ended up just making us a new one but she acted all put out which really rubbed us the wrong way. 

Honestly it left a bad impression and we won't be returning to this location. However at least we won't have to see her tacky poorly done tattoo sleeve? Lol

Super friendly service, great prices and they have an outdoor patio (enclosed with A.C. in the summer).  I have eaten here more than 10 times; magnificent every time.  I just had two fish taco' s, a red chili taco and a Dr. Pepper.  The bill was less than $6 and everything was great once again!

This was the perfect spot for me and my girls to have our last meal before heading back home from our mini-getaway.  SOOO glad we picked this place!

Santa Barbara is known for their super fresh seafood, so we were delighted to find that there was the perfect spot, at the end of the pier.  We came at around 11:30am, which was perfect, because we beat the big lunch rush.  We were seated within 15 minutes, so we just enjoyed our view of the ocean while we waited.  You're also able to order up at the window and eat at one of the picnic tables they have set up on the pier if you don't feel like waiting. 

We were seated outside, so we were literally eating a few yards from the edge of the pier.  It was beautiful.  

The four of us shared a pitcher of Hefenweizen, which paired deliciously with all of the food to come.  Light, refreshing, and the view was a big plus.  And the whole pitcher was only $18!

We started off with an appetizer and shared a dozen of the Morrow Bay Oysters and Kusshi Oysters.  The Morrow Bays were bigger than the Kusshi, so I expected a saltier, less sweet taste.  It was actually just as sweet and the smaller, Kusshi Oysters.  I was pleasantly surprised, and these were both very fresh!  

For my main course, I ordered the half MAINE LOBSTER, which also came with Onion Rings and a soup-- I went with the LOBSTER BISQUE.  The half Maine Lobster was super fresh and tender.  The tail was a little chewy, but better than a lot of lobsters I've had lately.  My favorite part was the super meaty claw!  It came out of the shell beautifully with ease, and melted like butter in my mouth.  I didn't even need the side of melted butter!  This dish was simple and sweet.  The Lobster Bisque was good, but nothing I'd be craving.  I hoped that there would be at least a few pieces of lobster in it, but I think they just used lobster for the flavor.  Oh!  The Onion Rings here are amazing.  Light, crisp, and flakey!

My friends ordered the Lobster Roll and the Rock Crab Claws (the rounder shaped claws with the black tips).  The Lobster Roll looked amazing, and it wasn't super drenched in mayo either.  I noticed that my friend didn't eat the roll-- it looked pretty basic/grocery store bought.  It would be nice if they used a buttery, toasted, baguette, as I've seen in other restaurants.  The Rock Crab Claws were fresh and meaty, I must order this one next time.  

Overall, we loved the food and ambiance here-- a perfect ending to our trip! :)

my cousin took me to this place and it was soo good I love the fact that they do provide different craft alcohol beverages. 
I ordered the French onion soup rings for the appetizer and I was thinking that the portion size was going to be small OMG it was soo big 3 people could have eaten. 
My cousin ordered the sticky chicken wings they was absolutely delicious and I thought I was not going to like them. 
I ordered the gumbo it was absolutely amazing I was not able to eat it all and it was just as good the next day

I will not be eating again  at Burger Me in Reno. 

*The Kids Hamburger was SO SMALL, like 2 adult bites. The Kids hot dog was a HALF of a hot dog. 

*The prices on the website do NOT match the prices in the actual restaurant, and in fact because of this when placing a phone order it was quite confusing due to the kids meal pricing, what it included, what it didn't include, none of it matched the website. 

*I ordered a hamburger with cheese, bacon and avocado. They charged me for the avocado but forgot to put it on the burger. The burger was dry and flavorless. 

*Hubby had the trainwreck burger and he loved it. 

*The food was made quickly and ready for pickup when he got there. 

Lesson learned. We will stick with Archies.

Great meal, even better experience in the wine bar downstairs. My wife and I enjoyed a great meal here and after dinner being our first time in Lambertville asked the waiter for a recommendation for after dinner drinks. The waiter recommended a few local spots and lastly mentioned the wine bar on site. We chose the wine bar on site and thoroughly enjoyed ourself. We had so much fun that the following weekend we took family and friends for drinks. Needless to say being that we live in new hope we will be regulars here!

Stayed in a hotel on the other side of the restaurant, usually a restaurant near an airport, dicey at best, but not this chain.  Sad to say we don't have a Ruby Tuesday's in Houston, yet.  Service was kind, slow, not ADD like Texas restaurants.  Menu was exceptional, not 5 star but tasty, clean environment, adequate servings, yummy soup on a cold night.  Found my way back here on my return flight, same scenario, consistently pleased.

Priced right, easy access.  Sad to say had to click my heels, no ToTo we are not in  Ruby Tuesday's anymore.

Love BBQ and trying new places so we eagerly came for lunch. Sat outside on their pleasant patio. The highlight was their homemade sauces. The D"OG" was my favorite and nothing like I've had here in the Lou. Sweet but had an oniony consistency. The  half chicken and pork steak are only available at dinner so I opted for their brisket sandwich . Was a bit tough but the cherrywood smokey  favor made it still enjoyable. The hogie style bun was fresh but I prefer it grilled or toasted to better sop up the sauce. Mac and cheese was cheesy and had a nice crispy top. Homemade creamy  slaw and potato salad were pleasant. My friend loved the smoked turkey breast and was more tasty than other places in town. Staff welcoming and we had a nice chat with the friendly owner. So many BBQ options here in town yet I'll be back to try the dinner options.
Delicious veggie burger & hummus w/pita plate.  They had good beers on tap and the bartender was very knowledgeable.  Highly recommend!!

While the food is delicious in this restaurant, the service is simply outstanding. And big reason of such a great level of quality and awesomeness is with no doubt her manager, Jennifer. She's by far one of the best and absolutely cares about pure satisfaction of her customers, proudly representing this great brand. Big kudos for her!

I love this place. Everything on the menu is a very big portion, and just delicious. It's well-made, and the staff is always so nice. I especially love the pizza, but the hot open faced sandwiches hit the spot. Also the breaded tenderloin is great, and the breakfast omelettes are huge. I'm going to go call and order something right now!
Looking for a homey down to earth meal? Come to Merridees! The food is great and super friendly. Good vibe.

First experience in New Orleans we walk in on Sunday night , September 22,2019 I won't even call him a gentleman because he was not.  He was extremely rude and nasty when we came in sober and asked for a menu!!  He acted like that was beneath him !! He said that was a waitress job to give us a menu!! Anyone that works in a restaurant can give you a menu to look at if you are BEHIND THE COUNTER!!! To make a long story short we did not get a menu and we kindly walked out!!! No stars for this place!!!!!!!WOULD NOT Recommend!!!!!!! I accidentally gave it 1 star , I actually give it zero stars!!! Fire the racist behind the bar!!
Had lunch here and of coarse had some Gumbo. Some the best gumbo and jambalaya I have ever had. Service was good and drinks were on point. Great place right in bottom floor of Jax brewery.

Given all the glowing reviews, I was a little disappointed.  

I love spicy food, but the Cha Cha chicken was weirdly spicy given the otherwise fruity sauce.

Other dishes ranged from very good to uninspired.  One of our 4 dinners was incorrect.

Cocktails were decent.

We usually love Roma and specifically the Roma Italian sub. But after spending $17 for 2 subs today, I cant say how disappointed I am! There was hardly anything in the sandwich, one piece of meat slices in half to appear like more and they put the oil on it that usually comes on the side, which made the whole thing soggy inedible. Complete disappointment and the subs went straight in the trash after one disgusting bite. We'll be taking a break from Roma for a long while.

I work super close to this place so I decided to try it for my lunch break! So far I've tried the fried udon (AMAZING) and their veggie ramen. The veggie ramen was super comforting and flavorful. I got the fried udon with chicken and it came with lots of veggies also and your choice of two sides, I got Mac salad and rice. Can't wait to try their shaved ice sometime.
