I gave this 4 stars for their lunch menu - they are fast, have lots of choices at reasonable prices and great flavor. The dinners are a little bland, especially when compared to some of the great Italian restaurants here in NJ.

Terrence and David are what kept us here all afternoon. Seriously - the best entertainment on Bourbon!! The banter between these two kept me laughing all day. I'll come back to see these two for sure!

For our annual Christmas Eve family dinner, we selected this restaurant because of its ratings. Unfortunately, we didn't have an experience similar to that of other Yelpers. Given that it was a busy evening, there were several missteps that we had no problem overlooking (e.g., five people seated 4-top, multiple requests for wine glasses, etc.). However, after waiting approximately 45 minutes for our food, we started to lose patience. The owner/manager came by the table to inform us that it was a busy night, but the kitchen was cooking our food. Entrees ordered by two people were eventually served, followed by an additional dish served 20 minutes later. When we asked when the dishes for the remaining members of our party would be out, we were told that there are different cooks in the back - one of whom is much slower than the other. When another 15-20 minutes passed without the other two people (including my mother) being served AND two other tables (one 3-top and one 5-top) that were seated 30 minutes after us receiving their entrees, I went to the owner/manager to complain about the service we were experiencing. However, rather than take responsibility for our experience, he "restaurant-splained" that chicken egg foo young is a dish that takes a very long time given that you must "cook the raw onions and bean sprouts in the oil". At this point, we became acutely aware that he did not care about our experience or business. So, we requested that all of our food be packaged to go so that we could salvage our family dinner in the comforts of our own home.

Given that the holidays are a time for benevolence and tolerance, I must look on the bright side and say that I am grateful for the opportunity to have spent quality time with family. However, if I move beyond Christmas present and think about the future, I sadly and sincerely doubt that we (individually or collectively) will revisit Yu Hsiang Garden.
amazing.  I live in china town in nyc and i came to new orleans thinking that i had the best viet in town -- but was shocked that this was the best vietnamese i've ever had!  fresh and flavorful.

WARNING, double check your order! This location consistently messes up my salad order. I went to this honeygrow location four out of five days last week for lunch and they screwed up 3 out of those four days. They usually forget the Parmesan crisps that I order extra which costs an additional $1.25. Today, they randomly put chicken in my salad which I never order. I'm returning my salad later today.

This is one of my favorite places in Tampa to go to, that I don't go to often enough. This was my second time here and it was just as wonderful as the first time.

I love the small cozy atmosphere of the place. The service is always great! Very attentive, never have to wait to be seated, to get my drinks or to place my order. 

Both times I have ordered the same thing, not sure what it's actually called but, it basically a platter of the chefs choice. Now, I'm not knowledgeable of Ethiopian food in the least bit. But, as a person who is very picky about what they eat, literally everything on that platter is amazing. 

So, if you're looking for "something different" to eat in Tampa, this is the place you want to go. Great atmosphere, great service, and best of all great food!

Southern Delco and chain restaurants go together like flies on sh&t. And Applebeez fits the bill. Sad thing is, people around here LOVE them. This place is dirty inside. Service is unprofessional at best. Diners are packed in like sardines. The food is all pre-packaged, deep fried food-distibutor drek. You wanna be "eatin good in the neighborhood?", then stay home.
Friendly staff but my family was served a SOUR and SPOILED pancake. It was disgusting and the place was filthy as well.
Great place for 360 views of St. Pete and great food! Our waitress Evelyn was fantastic and made the visit awesome.
Just go.  Thank me later.  Pizza is off the charts.  I have been to 2 of their locations.  Great food, good beer and wine menu and reasonable pricing for the quality of food they serve.  Just go!
We love Marchwood tavern! Wings are still original recipe and so amazing. On the newer menu the tacos are delicious as well.

I cannot recommend this location. I have put off writing a review for a while but it is obvious they are doing nothing to improve their service. If you don't want chicken for dinner, then you are in luck, because they often run out.  What KFC runs out of chicken before 5pm?? The last time I gave them a try they had run out of chicken fingers by 4:45 pm. Next time there is a family picnic or gathering and the family wants KFC, I will go to another location.

You better be hungry when you enter this place because if you don't leave with the meat sweats and a food baby, you did it wrong. First, they provide an assortment of food in their Salad bar that you can get full from just focusing on that portion of the buffet. After you have tackled the salad bar, you can get an assortment of meats and cuts from pork, filet mignon, bacon wrapped chicken, sirloin etc that are served to your table in abundance. After your meal, you do have to pay extra for dessert which is worth it if you still have room in your stomach. Reader beware, meat sweats is a guaranteed result of eating at Texas De Brazil properly but worth every minute of anguish.

Food is very good beer is not cold enough.
Chicken parm sandwich was very good the first few times been marginal the last three times. Very dry and overcooked. Don't really care for the lack of waiters and waitresses.

We were invited by friends to drive up to Nashville and take a ride on the General Jackson Showboat, see the show, and have lunch. I've seen the boat on the river and figured it might be worth the trip. 
Seeing friends was great. The boat and show was just ok. 

I have to caveat this with the comment that I'm not big on this type of canned entertainment myself and this lived up to those expectations and seems very typical of tourist-type venues. 

Lunch was a buffet with BBQ and fried chicken as the main dish. About as good as you might get at Golden Corral if you chose to eat there. We don't because we like good food. 

The show was fun. Honestly I thought the main show was a little hokey but afterwards two of the gentlemen performers did a more casual show that I would have enjoyed as the main performance much more.  

Overall it was ok but we probably would not have done this as our own outing and will consider it a "one and done" deal.
Best pizza in Santa Barbara! The owner is friendly and accommodating! $7.99 for two slices, small salad and a drink, available all day! I will be back soon!
Some of the best Tom Yum Kai and Panang Curry ever. I miss this place.

I made my way downtown to this new restaurant that bought one of the buildings along the first block east of Meridian on the north side of Washington Street.  It shares the space with two other places:  Citybytes Cafe which is upstairs and T-Swirl Crepes which is right at the front of the building on the main floor.  Finding Wei Ramen is a little confusing, but you simply walk passed the order counter for T-Swirl and you will be greeted by a host/hostess from Wei Ramen who will help you find some seating.

Wei Ramen has full wait service (the other places you order at their respective counters).  I was greeted by my waitress and brought my beverage before ordering.  I started with a pork bun which was really tasty.  The soft steamed bun was folded over sliced pork and some veggies and had a somewhat sweet taste to me.  I simply ate it like a sandwich.  There isn't a lot of meat in the bun, but considering they have to fold it, they are somewhat limited on how much they can fit inside.

I also ordered a Rice Don entree which came with a side salad that was also quite good.  My waitress asked if I needed silverware in addition to the chopsticks which I decided would make eating the salad much easier for my lack of skills.

The Rice Don I selected was a Tempura Shrimp and Veggie option (others are more like stew).  It had close to 2 cups of white rice as a base with some tempura shrimp and a veggie that reminded me of a fried potato wedge.  There was also some cooked white onion and the meal was topped with a fried egg and a drizzled sauce (Eel sauce).  The menu mentioned Kimchi and a half soft boiled egg, but I didn't notice any spicy kimchi and the egg was definitely hard fried on my dish.

Service was quick and attentive.  I was able to talk with the owner and he filled me in that in the near future, you will be able to order food from his shop even if you are sitting in the coffee shop upstairs.  Note that you will have separate checks for each business you order from, not a consolidated one since each business is separately owned.

Good food and service in a tough location for restaurants historically.  

Parking is always a challenge and requires some fee.  I chose to park in the Circle Centre Mall ($3 for a few hours) and walk over to the location.  Hopefully, folks already downtown will choose to try this (these) shop(s) and enjoy some tasty Japanese food.

Review #3648

Best breakfast sandwich and pastries in Indy- Hands Down. 

I have been coming here a few times a week since they opened and am impressed every single time. Highly recommend Raspberry walnut danish.

We have been coming to Shiroi Hana for over 15 years and this was our first time back since before Covid. Taking into consideration the challenges restaurants have faced, the meal was still disappointing. The waitstaff no longer greet you with a warm towel at your table. This may be due to Covid measures. Cloth napkins are gone. The menu was new. Gone were old favorites like the bento boxes. The my meal started off fine with miso soup, seaweed salad and tempura. The sushi was inedible, however. We had mostly tuna, eel and salmon and the  quality of the fish is poor. Even the water tasted like it came from the bathroom sink. The issues are too numerous and we will not be back.

I was fortunate enough to be the first customer to enter the doors--literally, and quite by chance.  Aside from the waitstaff, my friend and I were the only ones in the restaurant eating and trying the food (and all for free!).  It was definitely a nice experience--not sure how and why I was permitted entry, but it was definitely fun to smirk at those denied entry after me.  now onto the food....

Money has obviously gone into this place, as expected of an establishment bearing the name of the rather conceited Bobby Flay.  I decided upon the Napa Valley burger, simply because "goat cheese" immediately caught my attention.  I ordered my burger to a medium doneness, and it was cooked perfectly so.  My Napa Valley came with a substantial amount of goat cheese that melted and oozed pleasantly with the patty.  I also ordered a side of the sweet potato fries that came with a delicious honey mustard horseradish sauce (tables come with an assortment of condiments as well--jalapeno sauce, which was my friend's favorite, a chipotle ketchup, a burger sauce, and a honey mustard, off the top of my head).

i enjoyed what i had.  especially cuz it was free.  that having been said, i dunno if i would come back to pay $8 for one of those burgers.  if you want fries?  another $3.  and a milkshake?  tack on another $5, and suddenly you're looking at a $15 bill.  now, if they had some sort of meal plan, or HAPPY HOUR (!!!!).... bump this review up to four stars immediately.  until then.... three.

Wowowowow. I had heard great things, but never gotten to experience it for myself. We were here for a rehearsal dinner. And the menu was absolutely spectacular. They had a delicious charcuterie board for when we arrived. For our meal we had a butter green salad, mashed potatoes, green beans, Brussel sprouts, and a duck pot pie. There was not one bad thing on the table. I only wish I was able to eat more of the food. Tha I fully they gave us boxes to take home the left over food. 

 For dessert the had a variety of macarons, tarts, and some sort of pillow dessert that put me into a state of bliss. The staff was very friendly and polite. Especially when dealing with a room full of people celebrating. It was also fun for us to watch them prep the food.

The best Eggs Benedict with their own version of southwestern Not So Benedict and waffles with pecans.

Love it! Love it!

Orders come out quick and the service is good.

Omars has the best truck stop food! 
This is true authentic truck drivin' eatin here. Real waitresses, real home cooking. Comfortable booths to sit in (some even still have telephones there, harking to a long ago era in truck driving). There is a big carafe of icy cold water with cups waiting at each table. The menu offers up every kind of item imaginable for a truck stop, from 24-hour breakfasts to hearty burgers and fries. This is kind of place to get the "Lumberjack-size" breakfast plate with so much food it is ridiculous.

The ice tea keeps getting refilled, the food is massive, and there is fresh baked pies available. If they have a special, consider it. I got a burger and sweet potato fries with a drink and pie for $10 last time. 

TTT isn't my favorite truck stop, by far, as it lacks a good gift shop. There is plenty here to offer a weary driver and includes a hotel to sleep in, barber, laundry and video games as well as lots of trucker supplies and parts for a rig. There are books and snacks in the gift shop. But come for the eating even if you're a local Tucsonan. They do offer a plate or two for "dieting" eaters, but forget the diet and feast here!

This is a fun place! It's very colorful on the outside with strange cat paintings. It's dark and dreary on the inside. It was completely empty when we visited, but the bartender was super attentive. The outdoor seating is pretty cool. It is casual and intimate with a little tucked away garden area. They say they have plans for a few TV's to be placed outside for football season.
The bartender must have been bored because he kept bringing us mini drink creations. We were so hungover from the day before so it was hard to assess if they were even good drinks. At one point I asked him what drink was on the Yelp photos and showed him the pic, to which he replied "I don't know but I'll call the bartender." Um, aren't you the bartender? It was a little weird but comical as well.
The food took forever, like 45 minutes. And we were the only people there! I think he had to call in the cook too. It was a one man show in the kitchen I saw later. But still, it seemed like a ridiculously long time. I would have understood and been more forgiving had the place been packed.
I had the island burger which is a veggie burger with quinoa. It was a little too mushy for my liking but the flavor was good. My sister had the "real" burger and said it was really good. I had a salad on the side that was really fresh and good. My friend had a Caesar salad that looked really good but he was too hungover to eat.
I know this review is contradictory, but I actually really liked it here. My only complaint was how long everything took, they could be a little more prompt. It is like the friendly little new neighborhood hot spot. It has a limited menu but the food is pretty good. I'll be back, especially to sit on the patio in the cooler months.

An absolute favorite in Nashville!  Even non-vegetarians I've brought here have had nothing but great stuff to say about it!  I've had nearly everything on the menu & always love each dish!  Haven't found anything I don't like.  Favorites are probably the buffalo beans & greens, chipotle seitan tacos, veggie quinoa bowl, portabella Caesar salad, French quarter dip sandwich, chickpea salad, garlicky kale, & raspberry tea.  Really, you can't go wrong w/ anything though!  I highly recommend trying this place out!  You might just fall in love.

I had high expectations from their IG page. The food looked delicious. But it was nothing more than fried frozen French fries and shrimp, loaded with ranch dressing, and Tony's sprinkled on top. Disappointing. Over priced.

If your in the French Quarter and looking for something to eat that is not Cajun or Creole come here. We decided we were hungry for a good old greasy burger. Looked on Yelp- this is where we ended up. We order 1 bacon cheeseburger dressed with fries & 1 cheeseburger dressed with onion rings, 2 cokes= $36. Very pricey for what it was but we are in the Quarter and on vacation. It hit the spot. You sit around the counter so it could be very intimate depending on how busy they are.

This place is the jam! From the structure of the building outside to the food, drinks, service, and atmosphere inside, National Mechanics is a good time. The best part is the dance party that takes place at 10:00 on Fridays. Awesome music (though the DJ is not down with requests-- perhaps the only drawback of this whole place). The staff is so friendly and attentive, which really adds to the whole experience. If you're ballin on a budget, I would recommend forgoing the food and sticking with drinks. This will definitely be my new Philly go-to when trying to turn up.

Pro tip: Be the first one on the dance floor, and your courage will likely be rewarded with free drinks by the bouncers/wait staff.

Thanks for your awesome service! I'm kind of picky when it comes to my pizza so I usually make my own. My family saw the commercial so I caved in on one request.. I get my own dough. At first the girl in the phone was hesitant, but her manager stepped in and took total control of offering us a more than satisfactory order. 
We received our order on time and complete by a driver who was new but very friendly. She was compliant by calling me upon arrival and more than happy to assist in carrying the order to my backyard. She was very nice! I'm so used to a pizza delivery guy who smells like booze or looks like a person of concern. Her manager Scott did a great service in hiring a person who makes customers comfortable in the receiving end of the transaction. I forget her name but will never forget the experience. The entire team at this dominoes deserves a huge recognition from their superiors. 
By the way, I didn't even have to make my own pie, the feta cheese pizza was superb! 

Great job!!!!!!

Tonight I had a plate of chicken cartilage covered in a soggy breading and broccoli that tasted like it was made of aluminum. A side of 'rangoons' that were fried crispy bread with no filling. The Shrimp actually managed to taste fishy despite the hugely bland breading.

I usually tend to treat myself to the fortune cookie before I eat... This is what it said;  

:) "Your luck has been completely changed tobay" :)

...this should have warned me of what was to come... (this is what I honestly got during the dinner typo and all)

when it comes to philly cheesesteaks, everyone has a place that they swear is the best and if you ask me, this Jim's location is it.  I've had Jim's on south street and I've had Jim's on Baltimore pike but this is the real deal.  Make sure to try both of their homemade pepper sauces in the containers on the stand up counter.  I've been coming here for years after my father showed me this place.  Don't waste your time with Pat's or Geno's (I wouldn't even feed that to a dog) and don't bother with Phil's or Steve's neither. You want an amazing philly steak, go to Jim's on 62nd

Chicken is delicious. I got the nashville tender basket flavor was on point. The Texas toast is amazing. Fries were a little soggy but still good. Wish their was an option for thicker fries but overall a delicious meal

PM is a fantastic restaurant located on Belmont. Their glass noodle pad thai is my favorite dish but I was surprised to find that their sushi is really good too. Try to sit on the porch when you go and definitely order the peanut fondue if you're with a group. Kudos to the chef for designing such a tasty menu.
Tastes like dog food. Not much flavor. My rice was hard. I was very unsatisfied and since I ordered it on WAITR I could not ask for something else. Really sad because I love Mediterranean food.

This is your run of the mill yogurt shop.  The required tart flavors are in stock (my preference) and the more traditional Cookies n' Cream and Cake Batter type flavors are there as well.  It's self-serve, so like 99.9% of other self-serve yogurt shops they went with the two (large) sized bowls - so definitely do not let that trick you into filling it full - you pay by the ounce not the bowl.  

One concern, the tart flavors must not appeal to their typical crowd as I've had more than one flavor not be tart like it was other trips, but actually be sour like milk gone bad.  My hunch is they do not make the yogurt fresh daily - which is kind of a shock as all it is is concentrate in a bag dumped into the machines that swirl it to keep it smooth.  

Not too concerned about the pricing as it seems in line with other frozen yogurt shops around the city - but their quality doesn't seem to measure up.
One of my favorite Italian places to order from.  The food is always delicious!  They do pasta and sauces right!  I have yet to eat in person but hear it's wonderful as well.

I wish I could've given zero stars. I've been a regular since Kayne opened and have enjoyed dining there whenever I've been in town. Unfortunately, I will NEVER return. Despite being mostly empty on a Sunday evening, and given no forewarning when we placed our reservation weeks ago, we were actually refused service because I was wearing khaki shorts. Kayne has apparently now become the fashion police. It's so disappointing to find a restaurant that suddenly becomes so pretentious and full of itself especially in a city with so many wonderful dining choices. The manager and the hostesses, who themselves were dressed unremarkably, were unapologetic even while admitting they may not have notified us of their new policy when our reservation was made. To add insult to injury, a young man was leaving in his ripped jeans and tattered shoes while my wife, daughter and I were booted. Save the pretension and find great food and ambiance elsewhere.

If you like breakfast, this is your spot. Old school diner. Nothing fancy about it. Good food and generous portions. My omelette was about the size of Tom Brady's football (heh, heh....Deflategate humor). 

I think their prices have gone up a bit recently, but the prices are still fair...especially for the portion sizes.

The Rotni was very good the pad thai was decent a bit mushy but I have had better. I didn't enjoy the Tom Yum which is odd I always enjoy it maybe because it wasn't as spicy as I like it. The shrimp fried rice had two pieces of shrimp uhh yeah that is a no no lol if I order shrimp fried rice I expect SHRIMP!!! Overall it was ok wasn't thrilled but it was a Monday and Ubon was closed. Ubon near the waterfront is the BEST in De hands down no competition.

Wanted to try the Nashville Hot Chicken.  The chicken was cooked very well, moist meat with a shattering crisp skin.  The only drawback was that the coating, though well seasoned with a nice heat, it was just too sweet for my taste.  It was like eating spicy powdered sugar.  This was my first Nashville style chicken, so I do not know if sweet is part of the overall seasoning. 

The house cocktail was on point.  I do not remember the name, however I do remember it was made with a homemade carrot shrub.  My request to my attentive waitperson, was a cocktail that was not too sweet.  He made a very good suggestion, that tells me he knows the profiles of the drinks served.  The drink had a lovely balance of tart, smoothness and bright flavor.

This place is up for another try, for the menu is worth exploring.

This place has decent food and solid beers on tap with a good atmosphere. Main qualm with the experience was the service we received in trying to get seated. A group of 7 of us (young professionals all in our mid 20s) were meeting for drinks and food and were told to wait roughly 15-20 minutes for a table to open up. It was a busy time for a Friday evening so we understood and it was totally not a big deal - we just hung out until the table opened up. What was annoying tho was that not only were several other parties of equal sizes seated before us who had walked in after us (extending the wait to 30-40 min) but when we did finally get a table, the hostess put us on a time limit of an hour and 30 minutes. The conversation was essentially  "hey guys we're able to seat you but we do have an 8:30 party coming in to sit here. So that gives you an hour and 30, that should be enough right?". We weren't trying to give the hostess a hard time and realistically it was an okay amount of time - but we all thought it was pretty unprofessional. It's a bad way to to business - telling your 7:00 party of 6 that there's essentially a more important party of 6 coming at 8:30 p.m. and that we should essentially hurry the fuck up. I understand a need to turn tables and be efficient, but your patrons will realize that without being told they're on the clock WHILE BEING SEATED. It was a weird thing to say to paying customers who already waited, and chose your place for their night of dinner and drinks. Just set the dinner off on a weird vibe. Lastly, the lobster roll was pretty overpriced for what it was. $28 for a hot dog roll and fries. It was fine, but was relatively bland and the bread became soggy toward the end. And yes, I've had many lobster rolls before. This one wasn't great. Get something else if you come here. All in all, it was a solid meal and we had fun - just felt like we were treated like second hand citizens cuz of our age or something. Will probably not make a big effort to come back here. The time limit thing was such bad business.
Good food full of flavor, but service is a bit slow and often there wasn't any wait staff in the dining area.

3.75 stars 
If you are in the downtown area and are craving some Korean dish and don't feel like driving a little outside the city to get authentic Korean food, this place will do the trick. 
The restaurant itself has gone through 3 different owners (started as an American restaurant, then Mexican, then now Korean). I really hope they do well and stay. However the food has been really inconsistent, one day it would be amazing, some days meh, it's like they have different chefs each day. Going to this restaurant is like eating a box of assorted chocolate, you never know what flavor you will get. 
However, the portion for noodles was generous. The tofu stew is delicious on  certain days. Most of the servers are very nice and welcoming. They do have a full bar as well. 
The ambiance was casual elegant, it would make a good spot for a date night as well.

Recently had dinner at Iron Hill on the Riverfront and had the worst experience. We ordered appetizers and dinner. After our appetizers came out we never saw our waitress again. We also never got our drinks refilled and our bill was wrong. We eventually had to go to the host stand to get our check fixed. Horrible service, we will not be returning!

I thought from the unpretentious vibe of Elizabeth's that this would be one of my less expensive meals while visiting New Orleans. I was definitely wrong. The average breakfast entree was around $14! This just seemed incredibly overpriced to me. The food was good, but nothing amazing. They did have a basic breakfast options with 2 eggs, toast and potatoes for less, but it really did seem like they've taken advantage of this seemingly neighborhood place becoming more of an attraction for tourists. Because there are so many other great and cheaper breakfast options in the Bywater/Marigny area, I would skip this one.

THE GOOD:
-Food is very tasty and lots of it is actually authentic Irish cuisine (I'm a snob about places tacking "Irish pub" on the end of their name and doing absolutely nothing else to go along with the theme)
-They have Irish bacon (almost like ham), which is delicious and goes well on a burger
-Relatively cheap; good for smallish groups
-Can be fun late-night
-They can pour a pint of Guinness the CORRECT way (and some of the bartenders can even draw a shamrock in the foam--AWESOME.)

THE BAD:
-The food used to be better when the old owners were running it
-If you're local, you'll see at least 5 people you know here. If they're people you don't particularly want to small-talk with, then that will put a damper on the meal.

Overall, it's still the place I go when I want to go out casually with friends or take my Irish friends to when they visit.

There's a bit of a wait but it's well worth it! The food is absolutely delicious and you're given large enough portions to leave you feeling satisfied and ready to start the day. I'd recommend this place to anyone.

umumum, sashimi are fresh, better than many japanese restaurant here in Philly.  udon are tasty, but need more seafood in it
service good

I came in for late night wine and snacks with my family. We had a fantastic time here. Their wine list is extensive if you're ordering by the bottle. But they have only a few options if you're ordering by the glass. My favorites of the evening were the apple tartine with oka cheese, chicken liver tartine and citrus posset dessert. All the other dishes we ordered were also delicious but those were my top picks of the evening. The service was excellent and food came out quickly and at a great pace for us to finish one dish before moving on to the next. Overall, excellent experience here and I will definitely return!!!
Great spot to hang with the fellas, have a few beers & grab some grub. Always a good time.

Tried Danté for Brunch today and had a sub-par experience with this relatively new addition to East Passyunk Ave. 

The space is clean and well maintained. I didn't care for the large murals of (what I can only assume is) Italy on many of the walls, but that is a mater of taste. The front area is set up with a bar for quick eats and coffee. The back room is laid out with tables - very similar in format I many other local eating establishments of this size.

Out beverage service was pretty quick though the latte came out lukewarm. They offered to bring a second one and it was also lukewarm, though a little bit warmer than the first.  The plain coffee was la Colombe and tasted good and was a reasonable temperature. 

We had been seated for nearly 40 minutes by the time we actually got our order taken. The food took another 35 minutes to arrive. 

The good wasn't that bad. I had eggs Benedict and aside from a perceived lack of hollandaise sauce, it was tasty. The potatoes seemed a tad under cooked inside but were a crispy golden town on the outside.  My friend had 2 eggs with veggies substituted for meat. No complaints. 
We were notified that it was cash only when we went to pay, even though the bill folio said AmEx on the front. Not a huge deal since they had an ATM but could have been better advertised as most sit down places take some form of electronic payment these days. 

SUMMARY
Food was average.  This is a new entry Ina neighborhood with a high reputation for good food, so average isn't really a compliment. 

Service was lacking - Food and beverage delivery was spotty, issues with the bill, etc. This is my reason for not giving three stars. If the food had been really good it would have made up for the service.  

This place has a fair amour of potential, but would benefit from more experienced management for the front of the house.

I went to Rosalitas tonight for carry out in light of the Covid-19 crisis going on right now and i was SO impressed with their ability to still provide quality and great customer service! They offered to put my chips separate from my nacho toppings so my chips wouldn't get soggy without me even asking. They also gave me tons of chips and salsa just like you would get if you were actually eating in. Thanks for the phenomenal food! PS i read they have margarita kits too so i cant wait to try them!!

Such amazing drinks and food. All of their appetizers are amazing. Fresh fruit in all the drinks. Arepas are so delicious and come with different sauces that are also insanely good. A favorite for sure.
A staple dessert of New Orleans! And no flavor of fried Hubig's pies should go untasted!!

Since this restaurant is part of the Gonzmart group, I had high expectations and they did not disappoint. The restaurant interior is beautiful and you can tell how much thought was put into it. Our server was excellent and made some great recommendations. We started with cocktails, the meatball appetizer/side and the scicatta (?). They also brought each of us our own huge piece of bread to dip in olive oil and spices, it was amazing! For my entree I went with the spaghetti aglio, olio y peperoncino. It was simple but so good, will definitely order that again. Everyone's portions were huge, definitely 2 meals worth. Of course we had to get gelato for dessert, I'd recommend the dark chocolate! Overall it was an amazing dinner in a relaxed atmosphere. I can't wait to come back again to try sitting near the kitchen, they have a few special tables that look like a fun experience.
Great place to get a meal with the family. Our favorites include salt and pepper porkchops, sautéed baby snow pea leaves, scallop tofu, sizzling beef short ribs, and pan fried noodles.
Great atmosphere and great food. Perfect place for food or just a drink.  Smee's is nicer than your normal Bar and Grill.  I would recommend this restaurant to any age group.
Went back to Gratzzi's for a friends birthday and was once again wowed by the food.  I had the Chef's special Diver Scallops.  Perfectly prepared and a ton of flavor.  Expect me more often folks!

OK first off let me say I go here every week since I moved to Reno from San Jose and San Jose has the best Vietnamese food outside Vietnam. I have had only the nicest and fastest service coming here with my wife and kid if your getting bad service ask yourself wtf is wrong with you and people who compare golden whatever to this have never had a decent Vietnamese dish this place has awesome broth and meat is always tender and fresh . The pho GA will cure a cold it's medicinal man. Eat here screw the other places and there is a little panaderia across the way pick up some pàn and help out the small business.

Great place for some good food and drinks. We just came here and it was really great experience because of the food and the service. I appreciate a restaurant where you feel valued for being there. Thank you and we will be back.

We've eaten here a few times and the food is good, nothing outstanding or particularly out of this world. No matter how good the food is, though, the service is abysmal. Stood waiting at the empty host stand for a full ten minutes while severs looked directly at us and retreated to the kitchen. When my best friend caught a server and said we wanted to eat, he shuffled over, complained about the host not being there and threw menus on a booth where we supposed we were to sit. Another ten minutes went by with no recognition, water, greeting or anything we decided to go into the bar.  Normally at this point I would have just bailed but I had a meeting in 45 minutes and didn't want to search for another place. 

When asked if we could actually get served, the bartender informed us defensively that she's the bartender, not the host and she didn't know where the host was. 

Meal went by slowly and unsatisfactorily. We'll never darken that doorstep again. 

And we never saw a host.

Went in recently for a beer dinner I had won by naming their mascot. Chef Ean prepared a five course tasting menu for myself and a few friends. The first course was duck prosciutto with fontina and a peach ginger beer marmalade. It was such a great representation of a cheese plate without being a cheese plate. I wish I had thwart marmalade for my everyday breakfast. I have dreams of this marmalade. The prosciutto was impeccable, buttery and delicious.
This was followed by house made lobster spring rolls. The wrappers were made at the restaurant and were the perfect texture. Lumps of lobster just danced along your palate with just the right amount of shiitake for texture.
A salad with wild boar prosciutto, deviled quail eggs, and whiskey infused cherry tomatoes followed. Yes, I said deviled quail eggs. Be jealous. It was that effing good.
A palate cleanser of lemon thyme sorbet followed. It had just the right amount of sweet and tang to really perk you up for what was to follow.
I wanted to die when I saw what was next. Grilled sirloin with local grilled peaches, tomatoes and corn. There was a portabella carpaccio that went so harmoniously with everything. And lobster roe butter. Yes. Lobster roe butter. The steaks were a perfect mid rare and even though I was mildly hallucinating at that point I could not stop myself from finishing everything. It was incredible. Btw. Lobster roe butter.
At this point in time I had named my food baby Vincent. 
Grilled peaches with marscapone caramel and toasted almonds streusel completed the evening. It was just set enough to make you crave more without being overbearing.
The decor was wonderful, service a delight, and drinks were fantastic. Their beer selection is impressive and cocktail menu inventive. I will definitely be back and implore you to do the same.

I wasn't overly impressed but it wasn't horrible.  Our meal just alright and I have definitely had better.  

-Our pot sticker appetizer seemed like it came from a bag like what I cook at home.
-The swordfish was good, had a nice flavor and was cooked nicely.
-The rice pilaf is not really rice pilaf, it tasted more like Mexican rice so that was a disappointment.
-I got the steamed veggies, which was just broccoli.  Wish our server would have told me it was just broccoli as I would have ordered something else.
-My friend got the asiago mashed potatoes, they were blah considering they were supposed to be cheesy.
-Our creme brulee was soupy and cold.

The drinks were not very good, I would not order the sangria or the margarita again.

The service was just okay.

Wouldn't be my first choice to go back to.

Great place to go hangout, watch sports, and all the bar necessities. 

We got the nachos and quesadilla. Both were humongous and really good. Give both a 8.5/10

Definitely will be back

This place is absolutely fantastic. I've been there for both lunch and dinner and have been blown away. Their chicken salad sandwiches and sausage pizza are on my list of favorites. They also have very good pastas. For dinner i've ordered the BBQ chicken pizza and braised beef. Portion sizes are large. For dessert I had the apple tart which was also perfectly flakey and warm with a scoop of ice cream. 
I love the ambience here, makes you feel like your at a restaurant in NY. This is one of my favorite restaurants in Tampa by far.

Wow, Reno now has a second restaurant with mostly authentic Chinese food. I don't know if this is proof the Mayans were right, that the end times are near.  
101 Taiwanese Cuisine opened in a strip mall on Fifth Street just east of Ralston Street. It's the same strip mall that has a Starbucks, a Subway and a sushi place. My food here was excellent and I look forward to exploring many of the items on the menu.
I ordered the braised beef noodle soup, the shrimp roll and a melon smoothie.
The restaurant won me over with the first bite out of the shrimp roll. Fresh shrimp taste. In so many places the shrimp has no flavor and serves as a vehicle to deliver other flavors, like deep fried fattiness. This shrimp roll had some nice delicate flavors. The sweet-and-sour sauce has a different take, too. First off, it's Day-Glo orange. The sour part has a different tang to it. It was interesting and I liked it.
The soup was also pretty good, too. The chunks of beef looked black, like dark chocolate. They tasted nice and there were plenty of them. There were peppers but it wasn't that spicy. Nothing like the great spicy soup at Jia's Wok. I wonder if there are options to give it more zing. Maybe I got the gringo version. The noodles are egg noodles and were tasty as well. I think egg noodles do better with this dish than rice noodles.
There are lots of other things on the menu that look interesting. I don't think I've seen dan dan noodles on a Reno restaurant menu before. They have stinky tofu on the menu. I've tried that once before. I think all foodies should try it. At the end of their meals. But once was enough for me.
This restaurant is operated by the guy who was (maybe still is) chef at the Dynasty restaurant near Keystone and Booth streets. I'm glad he decided to open something with authentic food instead of another sweet-and-sour chicken joint. Hopefully, Reno's dining community will embrace the difference and support the place.

I usually love Tijuana Flats. My favorite thing to order is the Banging Chicken Tostadas. Today I saw they had the option to make the Banging Chicken Tostadas into a burrito. I thought why not give it a try. I'm honestly very disappointed. All that's in the burrito is chicken, cheese, and peppers. They did not put any refried beans, lettuce or give you a side of salsa like they do with the traditional meal. When I asked about the missing ingredients they said it doesn't come with it as a burrito option. That would have been nice to know before I ordered it and honestly, how could they even still consider it a banging chicken tostada burrito with half the ingredients missing??? Feeling ripped off

Service at Hoa An is quick, even if it isn't the over-the-top, effusively friendly service so many in North America tend to expect.  I ordered something rather basic: pho tai, with extra steak.  If that's extra steak, then I'm a monkey's uncle!  And it was more expensive than other places in the 'hood.

All in all, I'm glad to have checked out Hoa An, but I'm unlikely to make a return trip.  I'd pass on this place in favour of Pho Tau Bay if I were you.

Gelato and espresso are really good here! The chocolate scurro and bacio gelato are especially amazing (so nice to get free samples!). Tiramisu is okay but nothing impressive. A bit rather expensive for my taste so thats one star off, and i dont come here a lot.

I came in with a group of friends on a weekend and was greeted by a friendly hostess who sat us right away. A server was quickly around and get our orders in and our food was out right away. The food was really good. (The "Lucky Balls" are a favorite of mine.) The staff was attentive and kind and I would definitely recommend it. They have options to eat inside and outside.  Great environment.

Kind of a let down after all the hype I've heard about this place.
Came here for brunch on a Saturday and the line was very long but moved fast enough. We were able to get our order in and sit down within 20 minutes.
I tried the bacon & egg croissant sandwich, beignets, and cafe au lait. 

The croissant sandwich was so disappointing. The croissant wasn't flaky and was just so flat. The croissant was also a lot thinner than I'm used to and it ended up getting really soggy from the oil from the eggs & bacon. Wouldn't recommend & wouldn't order again.

The beignets, while good, were also nothing to write home about. It was a lot more doughy & dense than I would like. I still prefer Cafe Du Monde beignets over Cafe Beignets. Not to mention, they charge $4 for 3 pcs whereas CDM charges $2.50.

The cafe au lait was average. However, my friends ordered their orange juice and they told me it was freshly squeezed and good.

Overall, a very average and uninspiring experience. One of the cons CB has over CDM is they have a bigger menu and you can actually get food other than beignets but if you're just looking to try their beignets, I would suggest just standing in line at CDM.

P.S. At night, CB has live jazz in their backyard seating area.
Stopped here because we were craving Mexican food. It was very delicious! We have had lots of Mexican food before and this is at the top! Nice surprise.

Well, I wanted to love this place but I can't. The fried oysters are pedestrian and the crab cakes were very average, our crab cakes were delivered only slightly warm, I suspect they were microwaved and just left sitting a bit long before served. The server was very good and attentive. I was just, shall we say, underwhelmed. They will probably survive on the tourist trade and I wish them well, just not for me.

In their defense, the Sazerac was great, nicely prepared.
The best authentic indian food I have had in a long time, my favorite is the lamb curry with naan. The food is always hot and fresh, and the   customer service is excellent.

Very good food. Very good drinks. Very attentive and friendly service. Clean and welcoming environment. Live music. Loved it! 

Split the Mac n cheese app and the calamari. Really good calamari! Had the blueberry yum yum to drink. ($15$) Super delicious and not overly sweet! Would recommend.

I've always liked Currito even though I've only eaten at airport locations. I ordered a made-to-order bowl with chicken as my protein. Going down the line, I added cilantro rice, mild and medium salsa, corn salsa (my favorite), cucumber, carrots, and green scallions. I was surprised that filled the bowl to the brim! The price is also more than reasonable for the quality of the ingredients and portion size. 

My trick to mixing the flavors is to shake the bowl prior to eating so everything is mixed in the bowl. When the bowl is too full I'll eat a portion of it then put the lid back on to shake the contents. It's low-tech and works great! 

Currito needs to expand to California ASAP!

This review is only for the pizza. I ordered the white pizza for takeout to try an alternative to Olce which we have been ordering for years and really like. Big mistake. The pizza was completely overdone. I can only compare it to those cheese crisps you get in a bag that are loaded with Parmesan.  As hungry as we were, it was not edible.

I decided to give this place a try in hopes of finding my STL bubble tea joint and unfortunately, I think I've got some more looking to do. 

I had their mocha blast with boba and it was, as Yelp would put it, "a-ok." It would've been a nice drink to have in the Midwest heat... had my drink not kept on leaking through the lid. On the flip side, I think it's just the coffee-type drinks that have the lids.. all other drinks options (and they've got a lot of them) come with the plastic covering. 

For about $4 a drink, I don't think I'll be frequenting this place very often.

Quite possibly the best restaurant in Chinatown.  The spicy stir fry bowl is highly recommended.  For a Chinese place, the sushi is surprisingly good, fresh, and interesting.  Lunch specials are top notch and a excellent value. Service is fast and attentive.  They did a great job for our group of 15.

What a burger! Ok. Let me back up. When you walk in your attention is drawn to a well appointed bar. The atmosphere is quite relaxing. We started off with white cheddar pimento tomato jam goat cheese with dusted pita chips. I know, that's what I thought too but my lunch date wanted it so we tried it. Fantastic. It was smooth, creamy, sweet, and spicy all at the same time. What a great creation. I ordered the black and blue burger with Mac and cheese (just ok, duck fat fries for me the next time). My daughter also had a burger, the Bernie. Another odd combination of ingredients that worked really well together. She added the duck fat fries. To say we were happy with our burgers is a bit of an understatement. There are several more on the menu that I will try when I go back. Very attentive waitress. In spite of average Mac and cheese, this place gets five stars. They also have a QR code you can scan if you don't want to touch the menu due to the Rona.

Nice variety of menu choices, mostly average tasting entrees, upscale setting, great service. 
Starters:  Octopus was easily the best tasting dish on the table, you will get one arm that is grilled and the other arm fried.  Yellowfin Tuna is basically eating rolled up poke, there are various veggies cut up on top and sprinkle of sauces which doesn't really add anything extra or better to the dish. 
Entrees:  Wagyu culotte was average as far a beef goes, I expected more marbling and fat.  The trout was also average, portion size was decent, the skin was a bit on the salty side.  Rabbit Pappardelle pasta was a unique and tasty dish, I don't think I've ever had rabbit before, it's more tender than chicken, and I liked the variety of flavors (earthy mushrooms with the rich buttery taste of the foie gras).  
Dessert:  Warm Chocolate Cake was very good, come with a large scoop of gelato, makes for tasty and sweet dish to end your meal. 

Not much parking available, about maybe 15 spots in the parking lot if you're lucky enough to find an open spot, otherwise you have to valet acording to the waitress.  
We came on a Thursday night about 8pm, not crowded at all, we had a reservation but it would have been easy to get a table just walking in.  Interior there is a lot of echo, so I understood what other reviewers mean by it being loud inside, we sat outside on the patio during perfect weather and it was nice and quiet.

We went to Bonefish on Mother's Day. When we called to make a reservation the person answering the phone said, sure! Until we told her we had a party of 7. She then proceeded to tell us large parties take too long and we're welcome to come in and wait for a table. FYI, we wanted a 4pm reservation which was quite early and a slower volume of patrons. She refused to set a time. Regardless, I called the following day and was able to book a table after holding for management to give a table of 7 a nod. Which, implies this level of customer service is coming from the top. The food was ok, some arrived lukewarm but, they rectified issues. The wait staff was pleasant and efficient and certainly did not reflect management issues. The restaurant bathrooms could use updating as the bathroom door is still broken and was broken on our visit 6 months earlier. But, oddly there were many tables open and the restaurant was about half empty and no one waiting as we left.
I went to Chase & it was awesome. Lola was my server. She gave us really great service. I had the al Capone to drink and the salmon with sautéed veggies. Highly recommended.

First of all this I like this establishment solely for their roast beef sandwich and gravy fries. The ambience is typical dim lit bar, but let's just say the crowd is full of regulars. The regulars don't fair to nice with people who don't go inside often (example is me) for whatever reason. I would highly recommend getting a roast beef sandwich, but be sure to have napkins on stand by. I would say everyone around the area should try Nick's at least once

As alot of you had said i have also had an issue with the delivery driver.  First he ran me and my fiance off the road.  So i ordered some food and asked him to slow down.  He said F*** you.  you are the police.  i asked him to leave.  I figured i just wouldnt order from there again. The second time he ran me off the road i honked my horn and was very upset.  It was really close to my house, which being a delivery driver, he knew so when i went to turn into my road he completely locks up his brakes trying to cause an accident, turns around and gives me the finger, and starts to pull away.  That was the last straw. I had planned originally to go talk to the owners.  When attempting to tell them what happened He came in screaming "I F*** You" over and over.  The owner asked me to leave so i did.  He followed me out screaming "I F*** You" which i was ok with until he said "I F*** YOUR WIFE"!  This is a rather large man who knows where i live.  I on the other hand am not, luckily I am undefeated in my professional mma career at 145 lbs.  I made quick work of the very large man before chocking him unconcious and soccer kicking him while 3 people pulled me off him.  You do not threaten peoples loved ones.  We have since gone to mediation where we agreed to ignore each other if we are seen.  These are terrible people.  After speaking to all of the business around the shopping area they too have had issues and do not like the man.  I am glad to see it wasnt just me.  we do not order from them any more.

Food was really really good sushi chefs were quick and friendly. The waitresses were decent but suddenly became high pitched squealing 13 year olds at a Justin Bieber concert when we were leaving. Felt like they were REALLY happy to see us go!!

For any breakfast aficionado, there are pancakes, but then there are pancakes! And Le Peep has the latter stack of glorious goodness that I must tell you about fellow Yelpers.

They are gloriously nutritious feeling with whole grains, blueberries baked in and blueberries on top make for a delicious rendezvous for your appetite. Throw in a side of bacon and bottomless coffee and you will be thoroughly pleased.

We went before our Regatta competition, completely decked out in Hunger Games attire, and the server actually rooted us on for the competition, when we were worried that we looked silly. I appreciate the fact that she encouraged us, so it made breakfast all the better.

Such a cool view. Too bad it's seasonal and only open in the warmer months. But it's entirely outside so understand. Try to come before sunset so you can grab chairs by the railing and watch the sunset/admire the city. Had the grapefruit seltzer which was quite good and a philly brew. They have cans of beer, wine and the like and a small selection of food like hummus and veggies. Would recommend.
Fantastic selection of local and national special brews.  This was a great stop on our walk though Virginia City.  The hot dog.....not so great but okay.

Since I'm pescatarian and my boyfriend is not, it was nice to go to a restaurant that had the best of both worlds. The wait time for food is a little long, but it's worth the wait. The fish section of the menu is FANTASTIC. The server was very nice. I would recommend 100%
There were 6 of us and everyone's breakfast was really good... They have a huge menu with tons of options. Service was great!

I usually order food from here through one of the major food delivery apps and really enjoy it. Recently I was in the area and had the opportunity to try in person. 

First off they have a nice large outdoor space. Unfortunately it was raining and was forced to eat inside. The inside isn't as nice or large. It's kinda cramped and a little too warm for my taste. 

Now for the food. My typical online order is the bratwurst platter. It's expensive, but it's my favorite thing on the menu and gives you a sampling of German food with sausage, mash and gravy, and sauerkraut slaw. As good as the sausages are the potatoes and gravy are even better. Also, the platter is large enough to get two meals out of it, which kind of makes the price not so bad. 

For my in person meal I went with the giant German. That name does not lie. That is one honking huge brat. It was very filling, messy, and a good crunch on the bun. Definitely only order if you're really hungry. 

Overall good experience, but next time the in person meal will be had with nicer weather to enjoy the outdoor space.
Excellent place to relax with friends and family to enjoy good food and great drinks. Try the boxtys!

My partner and I often enjoy trying new places. We're locals, big foodies, and love to drink. I'm not a type to leave feedback but today was the day. 

I had friends who recommended this place and told me about their splendid experience here although my partner and I left extremely disappointed this Sunday evening. We read the glorified reviews and were excited to try out such a highly rated restaurant but felt that nothing except the concept and interior design actually lived up to the hype. 

Approx. 6 total customers at the time of entering. We were not initially greeted. A typical bartender, with a sarcastic response says we may sit wherever we want because "the place is just so busy.." She was charming but it just felt awkward for your first time walking in.

Michael, our server who never told us his name, was a sad quiet man. I actually felt that his depression rubbed off on me. 

The seafood dip was delicious, however, we needed to order more naan bread for additional $4. Unfortunately, by the time it came out, the dip became too cold to enjoy with our hot bread. So don't do that. 

We had two glasses of wine. My partner's glass had a bug swimming. (Understandably sitting on the outside deck, but the bug was noticed upon it being picked up) My red wine was inappropriately chilled with lipstick still left on the glass. As my server had promptly already left, I immediately went in to simply request from the bartender another pour into clean glasses.

Upon her return she apologized with the reasoning of the bar being too dark inside to see the glasses and asked if it was ok now.
At this point, we accepted our glasses and proceeded to believe this was something they could not fix since she took a cloth napkin to wipe the glasses beforehand and we were now forced to drink noticeably swimming napkin lint in our wines. 

Michael asked the other people outside dining next to us how their wines were because he must of misunderstood what actually happened here. 

The caesar salad with salmon was decent. Salmon slightly overcooked but the well seasoning covered up the dryness. 

The tomato basil pasta was average. The grilled chicken made it fairly better. The sauce is more chunky than saucey. Kinda basic but much more flavorful with the chicken, though. 

The drink menu is a bible compared to the front and back menu. If your server is persisting on getting our drinks, maybe they can make a recommendation? 

We sat outside but don't do so unless you want to woo with the pedal taverns, hear tiny men on their motorcycles rev their engines obnoxiously along with the across street construction, and like to yell over the restaurant's music speaker... 

Overall, $87 and 20% tip later, we paid full price for looks rather than service and quality. Maybe it's our own fault for previewing an expectation through the reviews. 

I hope this place reaches it potential someday soon for our willingness to give it another chance of what could be a lovely date spot.

Top 3 sandwhich spots in Philly. What makes Stockyard standout from the rest is its inclusive menu. Whether you're in the mood for some meaty, artery clogging goodness or satisfying vegan delights, Stockyard has it all. 

Their menu is definitely on the pricier side, but they source their ingredients locally and aim to reduce waste by utilizing off cuts of animals and seasonal produce ... and every creation is delicious! 

So yeah, I can get behind that.

Second time here I really only come to shop at Ralph Lauren but I must say this time I shopped at other stores.

Tory Burch has a sale 50% off sandals I felt like that was a steal and brought 2 pairs.

Went to aunt Annies pretzels and they had a long line.

Will be back to shop

Call for turbo shot, they didn't put it in first couple times. Next time call turbo for to go they asked for .30cents plus more. Asked him why they said because amount of turbo to put in the coffee and to go are different. Make no Fuken sense. People be careful for what your order at this place.

This is an extremely clean rest stop inside and outside with lots great of information to help you to know what do and see on your road trips!!!

There's a lot of great things to buy, fun games for kids to enjoy and great massage chairs for all to enjoy too. Tons of great food places and great convenience store. You could easily spend hours in this test stop just enjoying the beautiful atmosphere, eating and browsing all the shops.

Drove 2hrs just to come here and have their Baja Fish Tacos. Been coming here since a kid to go camping at Carpenteria and this place is still the same. Still the same home feel atmosphere and awesome food. They are only open half days so come before they close.

We recently had dinner at Monaciello, an Italian restaurant in Reno.  I give it a 5 star rating because both the food and the service were excellent.  I had a Caesar salad and the lasagne and both were top notch.  Our waitress was attentive and very friendly.  I would highly recommend Monaciello as a restaurant near downtown Reno that is reasonably priced, with good food and service.

Unless it a classic staple like Little Pete's or a redefined gastropub like Silk City, I don't really see the need to nitpick my meal at a diner.  It's pretty much standard everywhere you go.

Given that I've been to this diner a couple times to either soak up alcohol late at night or power through my hangovers late in the afternoon, I figured I might as well throw a helpful review its way.

When in doubt, while staring at the seemingly endless pages of menu, remember that you can't go wrong with breakfast- no matter what time of day.  The bacon's always crispy and the scrapple is always wonderful.  I've never been blown away...it's breakfast...but I've never had an undercooked egg or floppy piece of toast.  Generally, it's pretty good.

For dinner, I try to steer clear of entrees other than a sandwich or a burger.  The cheesesteak wrap is pretty good.  The buffalo chicken one was soggy.  The bacon cheeseburger was delicious, as were the gravy cheese fries, but the bun was like the kind you get in packs of 8 for barbecues....very frail by the time I was done with it.

The milkshakes are tasty, though I wouldn't recommend mixing them on a stomach full of alcohol.  I have yet to converse over a slice of pie and a cup of coffee, but I'll have to try sometime.

The staff every time I've been here has been extremely accommodating and friendly.  Be patient with them during the peak midnight to 4 am shift...they're dealing with a lot of drunken idiots.

I've had the great fortune of finding myself in a Waffle House booth somewhere between closing time and sunrise more times than I can remember.  I am happy to report that this location of America's favorite hotcake habitat is consistent if nothing else.  The ability of a national company to locate the exact same cast of characters for each of their more than 2,100 locations across 25 states is nothing short of a miracle.  In addition to the the crew that was most notably highlighted by a barely adequate waiter ironically named "Quick", the most important reason we go to this establishment also lived up to all expectations... the hash browns.  Smothered, covered, capped, and chunked then topped with gravy.  If that doesn't help a hangover then fat babies don't fart.  If you find that you've been over-served in Nashville make this your last stop before calling it a night, but whatever you do, don't leave your friend at the hotel...

Went on many high praises. Ordered a $9 glass of wine , came in a large glass with 1 1/2 inch of wine! When I questioned the size of the pour, she offered to add a bit more while other people had much larger portions in their glass, almost full. 
Ordered a split pizza , upon delivery the whole thing was wrong, pizza could have been delicious if it was right, we gave the leftover to parking attendant. 
Waitress was not a "good listener"!!
She did in her defense give us each a free drink.

The stars are for the beer only, we did not eat here. We sat at the bar and they were friendly, helpful, and attentive. It was stout week so we did a sampler tray of 6 stouts. The vanilla stout, the coffee one, and the outlaw on nitro were great. We also tasted the bitchin berry which was tasty. We preferred the tectonic ipa (reminds me a bit of lagunitas lil sumpin sumpin) over the icky. Quick stop on our road trip, but worth it for the beer.
Delicious from start to finish! Chicken was perfectly seasoned and cool yogurt, cucumber sauce was perfection!  We will definitely go back.

Okay, so it's been a while since I've actually been to an IHOP since I've recently been obsessed with Waffle House, but I came because I was really craving some strawberry pancakes. I arrived before noon on a Sunday, which I'm aware is the peak time for the after-church crowd. I told the hostess we had a party of two, and she let me know that the wait was going to be 20 minutes. Sure, no big deal. That's expected for peak Sunday brunch time. Well that 20 minute wait turned into more than an hour. People were coming to the counter to pay their bills, but no new tables were being seated. I was thoroughly confused as to what was going on, so I looked to the hostess who was worriedly looking towards the back of the house. She began turning away new people who were walking in.
I could have asked what the heck was going on, but I thought someone would have come up to us and let us know of the situation since there were about 20 people getting antsy for their tables. Didn't hear a word. I was eventually seated with an apology for the long wait. Overall, service was not very attentive since we had to ask for little things such as two new sets of silverware, since I didn't have a set and the other one was missing a fork. My eggs were kind of over scrambled and rubbery, but everything else food-wise was fine. When we went up to the front to pay our bill, the workers were standing around talking and didn't realize we were trying to pay. 

The food is pretty standard here, but the slow service is what plummets this location's rating.
WOW!!!! Best Thai food ever! The service was phenomenal and flipping through page after page of local and imported beer made my day! I will definitely be returning!

It upsets me immeasurably that even though I love coming to this establishment that some of the service members have heavily declined. This use to be a place I wouldn't mind bringing my partners to. Now, I thought I could mention this to a manager that the employee Trey or Tray was openly making jabs at my girlfriend and making her uncomfortable even after being told to leave her alone, but as well this manager named Nina took my complaint and seemed to barely be paying attention. Looking around the room, not making any eye contact, barely responding with mhmm, yes, yep. Disrespectful at minimum and as said before, very disappointing.

I've been here a few times and I'm a fan.  The food is very good with the rock shrimp being the MVP IMO.  We usually end up ordering another helping of the shrimp at the end of our meal.  The fish is fresh and the roll combinations are interesting enough.  Its also a very sharp looking place.    
Now for the downside.  It's overpriced (but most good sushi places are) and the service is aloof.  Plan to spend 2 hours having dinner.  There were times when half an hour would go by and I wouldn't see our waiter.  And that's happened on multiple visits so it wasn't a one time thing.  So that means empty water and wine glasses, large spaces between courses, then after a long wait, the food all comes at once causing intra-table course mixing which I don't like.  
Overall though, good food, convenient location, ample parking (as Grandpop used to say).

The food was awesome! We found them off of Yelp and figured we would try it. I got the avocado toast and was worried about it being filling and boy was I wrong! It was amazing and so filling! Probably the best avocado toast I've had! Definitely a must try and the waitstaff was great!
I had the shrimp poboy. The shrimp was really good, but I was less than impressed with the bread, toppings and sauce. The sauce was excessive and the slaw was tangy. Not my preference.

Awesome! Great food, huge portions at decent price. One of my favorites. Been coming here for a while. Had the burgers, the salads, the "dinners" and a lot more. All great.

My family does miss our favorite waitress, "Grandma Judy". We miss ya :(

She was the best.

Breakfast = Yes!! This place is a solid 3.5 stars for me. I want breakfast all the time, yet it's hit or miss at many places.

So here's the rundown of this cafe. The clam chowder was spot on delicious. Creamy, not too salty, and very meaty. The blackened chicken melt surprised me on how good it was! Order it. You won't be disappointed! Also, the fries were golden perfection! The pancake was just meh. The outside was tough, but the inside was light and fluffy. The biscuit and gravy were spot on! The omelet was pretty underwhelming, there were no punches of flavors, or frills.

Service was quick, the staff was friendly, and the tables were clean. All good stuff!

I had heard of the popularity if the west side location and anticipated the opening of this Castleton location. Rumor has it this is a lot like In N Out. So, I was exited to try it.

The inside is not open, so it is drive thru only. Ordered a mushroom Swiss burger with curly fries and a chocolate shake. There were up charges for the curly fries and the shake. Also, for a California knockout burger with fries. 

Customer service throughout our transaction was great. 

My regular fries were not crispy when I got home, so it was necessary to freshen them up in the air fryer. The curly fries are your typical seasoned curly. The knockout burger was a bit much. It has a lot of stuff on it. Had the menu offered a description I might not have gotten it, but the drive thru only has pictures. The bacon on the burger was a bit undercooked and stringy. The rest of it was good.

The mushroom Swiss burger was much better. Not as mess and had a good flavor.

I wouldn't say this is the same as In n Out, but it's a solid fast food burger joint.  Check them out!
PHAT hoagies and steaks. Can't go wrong with their turkey sub. Service is always friendly and fast!

My favorite place in SB - the food is great, the beer is great, the service has improved drastically since I started frequenting this place in 2003. Don't judge a book by its cover. Order the enchiladas - either the filet or the veggie - equally delicious!

Looks like i'm the big bad wolf! yow! 


I tried this place because of the reviews on Yelp. I did the buffet sushi via conveyor belt. I'm a huge sushi person and always have been but it wasn't as good as people have made it out to be. The ingredients used for the sushi don't seem very fresh. There wasn't a wide variety on the conveyor belt. It also seemed like many of the items had a raw fish on them. There were only a couple others we could try that didn't have raw fish. Except those weren't ever tasty or fulfilling to my taste buds. 

It's going to take me awhile to give this place another chance.

The Old Spaghetti Factory was a great experience!

The food was delicious, and the atmosphere of this restaurant was dark and cozy with and interesting style. The decor in this restuarant is truly unique and it was great to experience their "famous 3 course meal"

The only reason I am giving it 4 and not 5 stars is because my finace and I waited almost 10 minutes for the hostess to make it to the hostess stand.
Food and beverages were ok. Beignets come in orders for three. I would have been ok with just one. Decent spot but can get way overcrowded for breakfast on weekends.

54th street and grill still has one of the best hot wings and gringo dip! Tonight we had both along with rattlesnake pasta! I was very pleased with the rattlesnake pasta tonight considering I haven't ordered it in almost a year. It looked and tasted a lot better! I would love to try more things on their extensive menu but am scared after many bad experiences. I will stick with what I like and know for now. As for service...our server was very friendly and accommodating even though he messed up our order. 

One thing we learned about ordering food here is that you should offer appetizers first. Wait for it to come out then order your entree. Otherwise all food will pretty much come out at the same time.

I love Tuna and this is the best place to get it.  Plus this place has hands down the best spicy mayo ever and I have been to easily 200 sushi places all over.

Best meal that I get every time and I leave full
-Miso Soup
-Tuna Cake 
-Tuna Box

The cake is made with spicy tuna and the Box is made with red belly tuna.  Both come with the spicy mayo but the box has a dark tint to it.  Whatever it is it makes THE BEST spicy mayo ever.  I practically eat the plate.

I came here for lunch on whim while I was in the Irvington area. The lady who helped me at the counter, Megan, was one of the most pleasant restaurant employees I've ever encountered. She was patient, kind and informative. The restaurant is very clean, my veggie burger was good, and the patio is lovely. I will be back!

Wow, what a pure disaster of a let down.  I just heard on the radio that this particular casino has a great new promotion!  If you lose up to $500 on slots, they will reimburse you that $500. What an awesome deal...NOT.  Turns out that it's only for NEW Total Rewards Club member sign-ups.  And if you're already a loyal TRC member for years, you get punished...I mean, "rewarded" for your loyalty, by being barred from the promotion.  I'm so glad I became a member early enough to get screwed over and NOT get $500 back.  I guess membership DOES have its privileges.  Lousy ones!

Anyway, when they started calling this a "Philadelphia casino", it really got under my skin.  It's OVER 30 minutes from Philly.  And it's located in the WORST and most run down city in the country...Chester, PA.  The casino is dark, unfriendly and comes across like a place that wants ALL of your money.  Bad payouts, bad service, bad cleanliness, bad vibe...and now of course, bad promotional lies to lure you into the building.  It's become a VERY depressing place.

Also, the promos I used to receive in the mail have also stopped coming. I guess the casino making $30 million dollars a year isn't enough to print up paper mailers.

I hate saying it, but I really can't wait until this "Philadelphia casino" finally goes under.  Goodbye and good riddance to a very shifty and very uncaring business.

i had a very nice dinner here. the food was good and the waitress and owner were very nice. the dining room is very relaxing with low lights and a live paino player. very intimate. however, you wouldnt want to sit right next to the paino because it would be hard to talk to your dinner mate. also there is a theater across the street so it can get busy. the night that i was there the resturant was full and the kitchen could not respond properly because it took over an hr to get my food. we were not rushing so we didnt mind, but i would keep that in mind in the future.

I'm trying to expand my reviews as I get in a restaurant rut and it's hard to get out of. This place is close to my kids school so I stop by here on occasion, pretty nice, pretty, pretty nice. 

Fresh veggies in the front, pizza shop, deli, sushi bar and cheese area that is excellent. Booze follows up before the meat selection with anything your drunken self could desire, huge selection of all libations. 

Place is open 24/7 use your Kroger card to save .03/gallon on gas, super job they did here, much better than the Kroghetto in the city.

Usually when my husband and I go to Reno, we avoid the buffets. But this time, before we left I checked out Yelp and we decided to try 1 buffet a day while we were there. 

All 3 were decent so I'm going to rate 5 stars for the best of  the 3....4 for the second best of 3 and 3 stars for the last, which was still not bad. Of the 3  Toucan was our number 2. Pretty good buffet...El Dorados buffet  was better but it was better than the Circus Circus.  It was my first time to Atlantis Casino. The hotel/casino is very nice though.
Great food. Love the porterhouse steak. Going again this Saturday.
Best Chinese food in Perkasie! Lunch menu is awesome. Very nice, friendly people too!

I had mixed feelings about this bar. Went there to shoot some pool both tables were full, the one had customers playing while the other had employees. When I had asked to play next game they had said they paid for an hour and the two ball bags decided to play from 11 to close. (Probably playing to see who would be catcher and who would be picture if you know what I mean). Needless to say I never got to play pool, but aside from all that the bartenders were great and the drinks were good.

Couldn't wait for the Sugar Factory to come to Tampa, because driving to Orlando and Miami for one is just a bit much.

This location is inside and upstairs of the Seminole Hard Rock Casino, across from The Rez and the adult ice cream, Aubi and Ramsa. 

Parking to avoid walking through mass amount of tobacco smoke would be the Lucky Street or Orient Road Parking Garage. 

Sugar Factory is so cute and has an instagram wall , plays great up to date music and would be perfect to celebrate child's birthday.

I was simply let down because the fish bowl drinks are 36$ which is well over priced to not taste the alcohol or even catch a buzz. I ordered "The Drake" which is a peach drink with whiskey, and a strawberry lemonade cotton candy stacked. The drink is great, just don't expect to turn up from it.

I've had their food in Miami and it is not the best for the cost of their menu items.

I do believe the bright lights, rainbow of colors, and many celebrities with their face stamp of approval makes this place a trap and gives people high hopes. 

 The wait wasn't bad, maybe a ten minute wait on NYE around 6pm. I do suggest reservations, because that was the first question asked when we arrived and there was a line. 

 Jacqueline or Jackie was our server. Service was decent, not extraordinarily nice but she did her job... maybe a little overwhelmed and ready to start her New Year celebration. 

When it's your birthday, they play a really popular song and they dance to it in the aisle-- so cute! They had a whole routine for "Level Up" by Ciara, had me wishing it was my birthday! About the coolest part of my experience.

After being exposed to 5 Guys for almost 4 years now I still don't see the fascination with this place. The burgers are just OK and are way over priced, Their fries are good especially Cajun style, But you and I can both make a better burger at home for a third of the cost. This place is nothing special and nothing to rave about.

But they must be doing something, because of their success they have actually lit a fire under In-n-Out burgers ( a southern California chain ) ass to start moving east before 5 guys takes over the mid west.

in my opinion you can get a better burger for cheaper at any of the themed chain restaurants (chili's, apple bee's, smokey Bones, etc.)

Really solid falafel joint. The five falafel sandwich wasn't enough to fill me up on its own but had a great balance of ingredients, and the side bar of unlimited condiments (pickles, fruit, etc.) was a pleasant surprise. The fries were fine bite slightly disappointing: oily, not very crispy, and only ketchup for dipping.
