It's slightly frustrating that the $12 combo of a sandwich, fries, and a drink doesn't actually save you any money, it's just the sum of how much each would normally cost. But that said, they do give away free bananas which is pretty cool.

This was a perfect place to stop in with my parents after a cardiology appointment. They have so many wonderful healthy plant based options. The brioche lemon curd puff was amazing with coffee. We tried a few of the breakfast sandwiches and the one that was bursting with flavor and definitely worth a return just to get it again was the pumpkin cheddar biscuit. Wonderful bakery baked full of yumminess.

Amazing service! Great food! Perfect atmosphere! Thanks Maggie for being such a great waitress. Being vegan can be a struggle when eating out, but they had a little small vegan section on the menu and I was thrilled! Got the chilaquiles and everything was so fresh. This is a must when visiting Reno!
Chill spot. Dug the art, music, service and big windows looking onto 4th ave. Nice mixed crowd with plenty of chatter.
Best pizza around, 6 packs of tons of different kinds of beers, ciders n malt beverages. The guys there remember you! Very friendly n not too expensive
Grandkids love it.  I wish they would clean the playground area.  It is very dirty underneath the play equipment.

There is so much to say about this place. We bring here everyone that comes to visit us from outside of Tampa. The lawn outside, the food hall inside, the restaurants, they are all amazing. Sushi place, Burger place, Pizza place, Ramen, fried chickennnnn! So much to try, it is definitely one of my favorite places to be at.

MUST try for me and my favorites are:
1. Fried chicken and fries from Empamamas.
2. All empanadas at Empamamas.
3. Ramen from Ichicoro
4. Poke and sushi burritos from Zukku Sushi.
5. Cuban Sandwich from Kuba.
6. Drinks at M.Bird during the sunset.

There is so much to try here!

This place is great. Their gluten free crust is delicious and comes in 2 sizes! The people who work there are always nice and are very helpful. The NFL ticket is just amazing. I've already been there more times Han I'd like to admit! Their wings are the best I've had in town. The place seems to be running very smoothly since the opening day, and being in the F&B industry for ten plus years, I know that isn't easy. Great job guys!!

Wonderful place in downtown Tarpon Springs!  Delicious food and quaint atmosphere. Their paninis are so good and made even better with all if their olive oil and balsamic selections. Cheesecake is SO yummy too!  We will definitely be back!  :)
CC on Esplanade is an original. Sidewalk drinking coffee people.  Everyone is friendly at this spot.

Cuban pork sandwich?  Amazing.  Short of swimming over, it's probably the best you're gonna find.   Satisfies on every level, the tangy pickle bringing the flavors together in a symphony of wow.   The sandwich will fill you up -- one of the best 8 buck meals I've had!  Don't know when I will be back, but I WILL be back.

I came here yesterday with my friend, ordered the Nico's sampler and I got the sifrina arepa pictured. It was very delicious as I am a cheese lover this was really good. The waitress was very attentive as well.

Great place! We walked over from the Flower Show and were not disappointed.

*Plenty of Vegetarian options. I had the Vegetable Monsoon. It was very flavorful and absolutely the right amount of food.

*Thousand Layer Coconut cake for dessert - great blend of salty and sweet, and I'm not usually a fan of coconut.

The only thing we didn't like was the "Mango Salad". We're not sure where the mango flavor was -- we had to confirm that they brought us the right thing -- and it was waaay too salty.

Otherwise, nice joint. Plenty of room.

We came to the Greek Lady for a snack after a day of socially distant walking around U Penn. We wanted ice cream from Ben and Jerry's but they were closed, and bae wanted something more "food" like than ice cream anyway. We popped in here and ordered curly fries, a scoop of vanilla ice cream, and a scoop of strawberry ice cream. All for takeout because it's May 2020 and we're all quarantining and such. A "scoop" of ice cream was approximately the size of a pint of ice cream, so that was incredibly filling. The curly fries were perfectly crisp. I dipped the fries in my ice cream. Perfection.

While we waited, we could see that the place was BUMPING for a Saturday around 3pm. We saw some meats roasting, and we witnessed some delicious looking sandwiches being made. We definitely were enticed to come back even though University City is not usually our area for going out to eat.

Thanks for providing us with a quick afternoon snack!

Maoz, how I love you.

My first encounter with Maoz was in Barcelona, where the store itself possibly saved my life (long story). So I have quite an affinity to the chain.

Back in Philly I had it couple times before sucumbing to the Celiac Disease gods. When I heard Maoz now had gluten-free falafel I knew I had to get there asap! The guys who worked there were totally helpful, funny, and nice. I got an order of Belgian fries and dipped it in the garlic sauce and ketchup-mayo-mix sauce they had. Potato-ey inside and crispy outside, just how I like :-)

After the server confirmed with his manager that the falafel there was gluten free, I got some gratis to try and munched up those babies as soon as I got home. I was also informed that the eggplant is NOT gf. Make sure you ask them to leave this off if you get the salad box. As for cross-contamination, I live on the edge (as do most of my gluten-free friends). But it could be an issue for some.

For those who can get a pita sandwich, it really is a cheap, quick, filling meal! Unlimited fixings from the 'salad bar,' which has several different salsas, cucumber salad, beets, and so on. Great haven for vegetarians and others wandering around South Street who don't want a goddamn cheesestake or burger.

After coming here 4 times in January to partake in their various customer appreciation specials, I figure it's about time to write a review for this place.  I hadn't been here in several months, and they recently switched to table service

The good:
- The front of house staff/manager.  On Taste the Gratitude night (50% off everything, y'all), the place was obviously swamped, but the main guy taking tables remained calm and collected, and remembered who we were (even though I was sitting in a different area to wait) while keeping us updated as to how long the wait was.
- The deals.  They had a $8 menu all of January where you could get various food, drink and dessert for $8 a pop.  A full-sized Margherita pizza (normally $13) and Elicoidali Bolognaise pasta (normally $14.50) were $8 each!
- The pasta was actually surprisingly good - I hadn't tried pasta here before (it's new to the menu) but was cooked al dente and very hearty (didn't skimp on the meat in the sauce!).
- Soooo many choices of pizza - my faves include Funghi, Proscuitto Arugula, Sweet BBQ Chicken and Spicy Thai.
- Gelato floats - pick any flavour of gelato and any flavour of pop (yes, the San Pellegrino ones!) - I am partial to Limonata/Blood orange gelato (or one of their berry-based seasonal flavours if they have them)
- They take reservations!  There is also a teeny bit of parking behind the restaurant (which is very welcomed for busy Whyte ave)!

The not-as-good (but not dealbreakers):
- service is inconsistent and depends on your server.  There were a couple times where we had a server that took foreeeeever to come take our orders and get us drinks (even on a day that wasn't super busy - and tables that arrived later than us got served first with a different waiter), but there were also a couple of times that everything was pretty prompt.  Luck of the draw, I guess.
- For the reason above (and for the type of diner I generally am for this type of food), I actually preferred seating and ordering yourself at the counter (and they'd bring out the food to you)... but it could be confusing to new diners and understand why they switched to table service.  It is definitely classy enough a joint that warrants table service- just hope prices don't go up to reflect that.
- Desserts.  The gelato is fine, but there are way better places in town for it.  It was kind of on the melty side.  Also, the Dolce and Banana dessert was yummy and rich if you limit yourself to one bite, but make sure you have at least 4 people sharing this dish if you want to go home without diabetes.
We enjoyed a four cheese pizza and Caesar's salad here.  The food was good and the service was great.  If we lived in Tampa, we would definitely be back!
Had the best experience at grillsmith. Our server was James and he was so nice and accommodating. Will go back to see him
Incredible service. Everyone is so very friendly and welcoming. Great prices, great food. If I lived close by I would come here every single day.

What a great place to get some fantastic steaks! Where to start? From making a reservation, to greeting to being walked out, A+ app the way. Service was fantastic, they made us feel like royalty, yet entertained us like friends, with a closeness of family. We had a group of 16, we were given a private room downstairs and what felt like at least one private server, not sure if he had other tables too, but felt like he was just for us. We had the "must try" shrimp cocktail. We were warned that it was very spicy/hot, it was great, not over powering and not too spicy by any means. Definitely felt the horse radish, and it cleared the sinuses. I order a filet mignon, medium rare, mushrooms, and green beans. Everything was cooked to perfection and the taste was fantastic. Every single person at the table had a fantastic Neal and was thoroughly satisfied. I also spilt a Duck something Cab with a friend, and that went very well with the meal. A few had room for dessert, they all looked good, and I snuck a night of a creme brûlée which was amazing!  We were walked out, and door held and pleasantries exchanged. Fantastic night!  We used the cat walks to get back to our hotel as it was raining, what a great addition for the city for traveling during bad weather (I know we saw rain, not "bad" weather, but was still nice for us!).

We try to come here at least 1 time a week... its a bargain on food, a good mom and pop place, where can you get a glass of sangria for 1.99? and a complete dinner for 2 with beverages and dessert for under $25.00 you just can not... I took my brother here a few weeks back and he enjoyed himself... the Liver and Onions if you like this is like the way My mom made it for me too when I was a kid.. Everything fresh and delish... you can not beat the prices...

First, the good;
Excellent bruschetta - very fresh and clean. Added celery to it for some reason but was good. Very limited wine menu but the chianti was good. And the pasta was tasty. Even the location had its charm if you enjoy OLD SCHOOL (note the caps, thinks 50s-70s) building and dining style. 

So why am I giving this a single star?

This was the worst service I've ever experienced in 30 years of living (and trust me that's included alot of restaurants). After it took me a little extra to decide on my dining selection my wife and I were ignored (as in the waiter repeatedly!) as he walked past out table and refused to stop even when asked on numerous occasions. 

The manager Abraham swung by on occasion but gave us sarcastic half assed service. Upon asking why it took 30 minutes to make bruschetta he said it was made fresh and that he had checked so no worries. After that he barely came to us except at the end of the meal thinking maybe he deserved a tip. 

The waiter only spoke to us at the end of the meal thanking me for coming. Beyond that he didn't refill out water or check on us one time in the entire meal. We had tabled of older regulars or just older clientele go through multiple courses with numerous checks on them before we even got bruschetta - and I don't care how fresh it is it should never take 30 minutes. 

I don't ever plan on patronizing this restaurant again. Nor do I recommend anyone else do it.

I am so excited that the near Southeast side finally got their very own farmer's market! Thanks to the help of the neighborhood association and other local businesses, the residents of Garfield Park and surrounding areas have a farmer's market located near the tennis courts in Garfield Park.

My hubs Andrew D. and I decided to visit this past Saturday to check out the new market in town. I was super impressed. There was everything from fresh produce to meats, kettle corn to apple sauces and ciders with mustards and a vendor selling savory waffles and sandwiches.

We tried a bit of everything. The kettle corn was super delicious-try the cheddar...omg. That tasty (so was the maple)...but you know, you can't eat it all...or can you? It's a challenge! Batch No. 2 was there with their saucy mustards and condiments (get it?? buahaha) Pleasant Street produce was there selling starters for your snazzy urban garden and a variety of other places with local produce and meats.

I purchased a 4 lb. container of lard and this adorable pet food supplement from a butcher (blanking on the name!! If I see it, I'll edit my review). The lard was reasonably priced and the supplement was all the extra bits and pieces ground up for your dog or cat's pleasure.

I'll definitely be back to support my local farmer's market. It's a great spot with parking and guess what?! You're in one of the best parks in the city. You've got the Conservatory and Sunken Gardens to meander through before or after and the entire park with the pool, trails, and amazing playground. My only suggestion is a bike rack nearby. But hey, that's ok. I can manage!!

Right off Main St in Manayunk, the Tomato Bistro is a cozy restaurant right upstairs from the Couch Tomato Cafe. We made last minute reservations to go last Saturday night, and I was very glad we did. We were taken up to the third level and greeted by a very friendly and knowledgable waiter who told us about their awesome special: A pizza, salad, small plate, dessert, and round of drinks for two for only $45 total! We obviously went with this option, and really enjoyed most of the food, including the Margherita pizza, burrata salad, seared scallops, and Belgian waffle. All of the food was pretty good, especially for the prices, although the dressing on the burrata salad was just too sweet for me. The scallops were GREAT though! Otherwise, there wasn't anything mind-blowing about the experience. Rather, it was a good, solid meal that didn't break the bank. I'll be back!

This is a place we stop into every time we visit NOLA. Its become a great staple in all of our trips. The food is filled with love and flavor. You can tell the staff love what they do and really put their heart and soul into the food. They have the best gumbo I've ever tasted!

Vang/Skybar Lounge is the AT&T of rooftop bars. My friend and I were excited to go, when we were promptly told we had to wait "10 minutes" for the top to clear. Fine, we sit, order hummus (barely enough food and not even good for $5), and come back after about 30 minutes. Nope, wait another 10 minutes. Really? I should describe at this point there is a strange mix of people grinding on each other and of people staring at their cellphones waiting to go to the rooftop part.

And...it's a complete disappointment. Lots of strobing lights in changing colors, weird bed like scenarios where nearly every chair is reserved. This all might have been tolerable, if you could ACTUALLY see Philadelphia! Instead, you're treated to a wonderful view of a 6-7 foot high wall. Presumably to prevent the many wasted customers from falling off. Ugh.

My daughter and I stopped here at the upstairs Itialian restaurant, Villa Vito, after shopping in New Hope.  The pasta was very good, the veal tender, the garlic toast pungent, the portions ample, the service attentive and the price point was fantastic.  The ambience is homey and tight inside, I have not dined on the patio.

Villa Vito will never be confused with restaurants like Marsha Brown's around the corner, nor should it.  We had a complete meal for two, including drinks, for the price of an appetizer at those other New Hope eateries.  I like fine dining as much as the next guy, but when a place like Villa Vito offers such a fine value for the meal, I am disappointed when other reviews are so harsh.

Bear with me here. 

It has been a long running joke that the author C.S. Lewis's greatest fiction was tricking American children into thinking Turkish delights were delicious. As an American kid, I remember reading, "The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe," and thinking, "These Turkish delight things must be the most decadent dessert in all the land for Edmund Pevensie to betray his entire family to an evil witch!" only to be completely bamboozled when discovering they were weird, chewy, nutty, powdered sugar covered squares.

Fast forward to 2019. A local coffee shop opens up specializing in teas, coffees, English toffee, and...Turkish delights! I saw several Instagram worthy latte posts and found out that every drink gets a square of Turkish delight and knew I had to check it out. 

Located in Midtown Pangolin Cafe is a small building with aesthetically pleasing, modern decor. Upon entering the owners were super friendly and gave us a little run down of what they had. Coffees, teas, and turkish delights and toffee (sold in 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, and 1lb portions). I ordered one of their signature drinks: the Cubano Breve, and opted for the sour grapefruit Turkish delight. My friend ordered a vanilla latte with the pistachio Turkish delight and we got 1/8lb of Dark Chocolate Sea Salt toffee to share. 

The drinks were delicious! It had been a long time since I had a drink with regular milk instead of soy or oat. They were creamy and not too sweet. Would highly recommend the Cubano Breve! The toffee was also not too sweet and was firm but not too hard the way some toffee can be. 
Now for the moment you've been waiting for...the Turkish Delights.

To put it simply, I WOULD BETRAY MY FAMILY FOR THESE TURKISH DELIGHTS!!!!

They were so different than the store bought stuff you get at the holidays. Soft, good flavor, and totally not what I remember about Turkish Delights. Of course, after having my mind blow, I knew I had to bring some back for the family to try because they would never believe me. We ended up getting 1/8lb of every flavor (about 5-6 squares) ranging from fruits, to nuts, to traditional rose (all are naturally vegan and gluten free!). The verdict was in. Everyone was in agreement that these things are delicious, different, and worth trying.

I can't wait to go back and try the teas and more of the toffees! I would highly recommend Pangolin Cafe! (Just currently not on Saturdays!)
Not good. Sad-quality ingredients. Couldn't stomach the fries (I thought eggs came with toast?). Sat like a greasy lump in my stomach. Friendly service, open til 3 a.m. Friday and Saturday.

I went here today after shopping wanting to try something new. We walked in wasn't too busy and waited a bit too long in my opinion. The staff seems very unorganized and thought somehow we were getting to go orders. After a while we were seated and ordered the queso dip and family fajitas. It wasn't very seasoned the chicken or steak. It came with rice and beans. The beans were the only thing that tasted good. The waitress gave us one drink and checked on us one time. When it was time we wanted the bill had to ask someone else for help,she apparently went on break. I'm conclusion my take on this place it's highly overrated! I've heard so many good things about it and will definitely not be coming back. I feel it just better options to spend my money with friendlier staff and better food.

While I'm questioning myself why I'm giving it 3 stars when the service is horrible and the delivery is even worst because someone forgot items of food and then the older guy (manager) rude, rude and more rude! Talks with an attitude and all you're understanding is okay and just like that he's hung up without you knowing what's going on. So i ordered pineapple fried rice and they don't make theres with cashews or the raisinsso i ask to be charged for adding cashews and i got pineapple chicken fried rice with shrimp. Of course i asked what came in pineapple rice carrots, onions, egg, tomato green onions etc. this has got to be THE BEST PINEAPPLE FRIED RICE WITH SHRIMP EVER! Now if they hurry up and bring the missing food i might give them 5 stars because my daughter is happy with her order and my grands are just patiently waiting for their fries and chicken

What can I say! It's worth the wait. Stay in the long line! It moves pretty quickly. The employees are friendly and helpful. The gelato is amazing. Many flavors to choose from. I recommend the praline and tira mi su. The raspberry fruit ice is refreshing. They have regular or mini cannoli. Delicious!! The biscotti is amazing. Dip it in your coffee! 
I love that you can get many of their items which are prepackaged if you want to take them home to share. I adore their fig cookies. A must visit place if you are a tourist or regular.

We had a marvelous time. The wild salmon was my favorite entree. Martin our server was awesome. The wine and food were amazing. The desserts are full of flavor. Also this place is very queer friendly!

What a complete horrible store!!! Absolutely horrendous service, ownership, etc.  it's painfully obvious this franchisee is absolutely clueless, as his management staff is the bottom of the barrel!!! I have ordered food more than once, hoping the previous visit was a fluke, but it's just the FACT that the owner doesn't know how to hire seasoned pros to run a simple restaurant!!!!! Terrible food and service

My friend took me here, and I'm sure she will be checking to see my review. First of all, thank goodness for amazing service. Finally, some place where the people are actually nice to you in Philly! (Please don't kill me Philadelphians...) My friend and I both had two short rib tacos. Meat was a little chewy, but the flavor was all there. Slightly spicy, tangy, and overall amazing. A bit pricey for tacos, but two each was enough to fill up our beliies.
This place is too good to be true. I've lived in the neighborhood for two years and this is the best addition yet. Everything is home made, the chips, horchata, amazing.

We had a good time, we chose to eat inside and were seated quickly. They had a coupon for calamari in Yelp and they honored that without any issue. We had good drinks and food and the atmosphere was child friendly. I liked that they had some beanbag games for my daughter outside.
Not my favorite place at ALL. The ice coffee is disgusting as if I was given to me by a 5yrs old kid who has no sense in the world what coffee should taste like
This is one of favorite stops to go to for some cheap yummy chinese food. The owners are nice. The kitchen is pretty clean from what I've seen.

Easily one of my favorite restaurants in the city. Definitely  recommend making reservations. Food is delicious and service has always been good the multiple times I've been there. I'd highly recommend the Sheeps Milk Ricotta and Roasted Bone Marrow, Uovo pizza, Braised Shortrib, and of course, the Budino for dessert!

First time to Rosalita's Cantina in Des Peres . . . and my last.  Took 14 minutes to get iur drink order taken.  When fajitas came to table, had to send fajita wraps back because they were left over from yesterday.  The Sargento very thin cheese was dry on top and uneatable.  Would have stood up and left restaurant, but was meeting a friend for lunch.  Ruined my day and will not be returning.

TERRIBLE service. Party of 9 and all food came out at different times. Ate all of my wings then finally got my side of fries. Drinks were terrible. I see why this Hooters location has terrible ratings. Talked to the manager and she was absolutely no help at all. Her name was Lisa. Get it together Lisa.

If you are looking for good Indian food and proper service, please avoid this restaurant at all cost. We were in Santa Barbara for the weekend and stopped for lunch. The decor is nice but the food was bad. The worst part was poor service and upon giving feedback to the manager, his response was "I don't care". 

There are very many good restaurants on State Street and you money would be well spent somewhere else.
The broken egg is always good but even better when you have a great server. Athena was absolutely wonderful. All 4 of us really enjoy our visit there. Thanks Athena.
Everyone has finished their apps and two drinks, and we are still waiting on an order of french fries. Hostesses were very accommodating, but server left without telling anyone.

This was my first time here. I was a little skeptical because there didn't seem to be too many people here. I was pleasantly surprised when the food came because it was some of the best. 

My wife had the chicken pad thai and I had the red curry beef. I forget what the actual name was for it. The spices were amazing and the texture was as well. The food was very spicy but not to the point where it would burn your mouth. I will definitely be coming here again.

The prices were reasonable. We got a $10 gift card and afterwards the dinner was about $30.

100% recommended for anybody who likes Asian food.

The 2nd best ramen in the city.*

*See Cheu Noodle

Excellent food! Being from Seattle, where there are hundreds of amazing restaurants, we have struggled to find great food when visiting Santa Barbara. Toma is wonderful! Steamed clams with chorizo appetizer was delicious, and the black spaghetti entree was too. 
The personal attention from our wonderful waitress made the experience a five star evening! We'll be back for sure.
Wine list is amazing! I also had to go with the duck ravioli... And it was the right call. The montepulciano by the glass is also highly recomended.

Do yourself a favour and get the white ganache mocha!

I gotta say, this is a great place to lounge with friends, study, or just come to warm up after walking whyte ave in the cold

I happened upon Fat Jack's for lunch one day. The ribs and slaw were decent, so I picked up some ribs, chicken, corn, slaw and cornbread for dinner for my huband and me a couple of weeks later. The chicken and ribs had been cooked quite some time earlier and were heated in the microwave, then put on a hot grill to char. The corn had been frozen and then slapped on the grill. The chicken was so dry it was inedible. My husband ate the ribs only because he was hungry. The corn was water-logged with no flavor and a weird texture, so it also was not eaten. The cornbread was nothing special, but edible. The slaw was decent. In the end, we threw out $40 worth of food because we just couldn't eat it.  Maybe the lunch was better because the food hadn't sat around for as many hours. I'm never going back.
Always a great experience! Elizabeth is my favorite server there! She great and so is the food!
Great large meals for the price and incredible beer. I'm getting hungry remembering this place.

I've been a customer of Chipotle for years. This location is terrible. My first online order from location was disappointing. The portion size was unbelievable. When I got home, this is what I was given. I was too exhausted to drive back. I responded to the survey and didn't get a response. I reached out again and received a response. I gave this location a second try and was still disappointed.
This is a cool little place. If you love vodka they have a huge selection.  I liked the infused ones. I did not try the food, but it looked very good.

I went March (shortly after the grand opening I presume) with my group of friends as it's been a place I've been frequenting since 2007. 

So when I pulled up and noticed the signage had changed, you could imagine I was a little confused. 

Upon getting seated, something just felt off. We got seated a table with a dirty grill. When we got the menus, we noticed the price had gone up exponentially for the BBQ ayce. We eventually ordered and sat there for about 5 minutes or so before they brought us rice, soup and water. The rice was cold and hard. The soup was nothing compared to the original.

We sat there another 10-15 minutes waiting for the meats to come out. They didn't. The staff just sat around talking. 

Eventually, I called who I assumed was the manager over and asked if the place was under new management. He confirmed and asked if something was wrong. I told him we wouldn't be staying as the quality had clearly gone down and the wait was unacceptable. 

I'm so bummed. I don't ever write yelp reviews, but I felt the need to a place that was a staple of mine. If anyone knows if the original owners opened up shop anywhere, lemme know! 

If you go expecting the same service from last year or the years prior, don't go. 

Otherwise, best of luck.

Had the pleasure of coming in here for lunch today and I'm very glad I did. First the guy who made my food was extremely nice, and not in a way were it seemed fake. Now on to the food. I got the build your own pita bread with chicken. I asked the guy for some recommendations with the sauce and got their garlic sauce. Whatever you get, PUT THAT SAUCE ON IT!!! It honestly made the meal. While I could've gotten something cheaper for lunch on campus, for the price I paid(10$) i am very content. Will definitely be coming back!!!

Nothing stood out about this place, basic food that is overpriced but it's Florida.

Might be a nice place to have drinks in the evening but definitely not a place to eat at.

Brown chicken gravy on a bIscuit for breakfast, who does that????

My family visited Bahama Breeze for Easter lunch and had a wonderful time. We were greated warmly, seated immediately, and waited upon attentively. Our server, Aaron, was among the best with whom I've had the pleasure of interacting in quite some time.

Our food was cooked to perfection, flavorful and filling without being heavy. I had a rice bowl with Mahi Mahi and a sweet 'n savory lemon sauce that I will definitely be ordering again in the future. The kitchen was able to handle my allergen-related special request with aplomb, and substituted out an ingredient I couldn't eat in such a way that you'd never guess the dish was intended to be prepared differently.

Bahama Breeze is likely to be our go-to spot for special occasions from now on.

Fantastic Thai food in the heart of Philadelphia. It's a small restaurant, so definitely make reservations if you're coming on a peak night. You can customize the protein and spice level in almost all of the menu items, so their food is definitely vegetarian friendly. I would recommend their soups, which are all packed with flavor (my favorite is tom yum), and their basil fried rice. Try "Thai-spicy" level is you really want a kick!
I'm here right now and just finished the Tom kah and a side of fried rice. I'm stuffed. Definitely the best Thai food I've ever had outside of Thailand. Two thumbs up.
If & only if they tried less on presentation an more on quality it would be a food place. The chef should come to Miami and have some cooking classes from the Cubans. The service was good.

The wait was really long for our party.  We made a reservation, and still had to wait an additional 30 minutes.  By the time we were seated, they were out of brisket for the night.  Overall, the BBQ was mediocre, and the service was about the same.

This place is totally awesome!!! Love the modern vibe with a wooden menu and open concept kitchen. Our meal started with these delicious shrimp chips and ended with fresh baked cookies! Very clean and a welcoming staff! I highly recommend this place for anyone who comes to the North Wales area!

Went here for brunch over the weekend on a recommendation from a friend, they are part of the Century Hospitality group. Our server was friendly and efficient, although it was brunch time on a Saturday there were only 2-3 other tables while we were there so overall it was definitely quieter than I thought it would be. Coffee comes in french presses with about 4 cups per press so we shared two of them, the coffee was quite strong and I enjoyed it. The brunch menu looked really delicious but left a little to be desired, the benny I ordered was a bit overcooked and the muffin was difficult to cut through, the tots were great I mean who doesn't love tater tots but they were the same kind you can buy in the frozen food sections so hard to warrant the $18 price tag, a very small side of fruit, more garnish than side. So great points for atmosphere and service but for someone who takes brunch seriously there are other options that are a bit more satisfying.

My 2 year old has a gluten allergy, and I had heard about Blaze's gluten free pizzas and thought we would give them a try. The service was fantastic and they were very friendly. The pizza... wasn't as good. It was alright while it was piping hot, which, we all know, cannot be given to a toddler. I had to wait for the pieces to cool off, but once the pizza was "warm" instead of "hot" the consistency changed from 'this is kinda chewy' to 'I can probably use this to fix my roof'. It was tough and very gummy, definitely not something a special needs 2 year old could chew. I was disappointed, and I really wanted to like this place. But their gluten free pizza crust leaves much to be desired.

Won't be back. It's a shame as the place is cute and reasonable with some great dishes. 

Unfortunately though after sending back a plate of runny and crunchy grits I was charged a $2 tasting fee (apparently they "can't let the customers just taste all the dishes"). Although I ordered a replacement meal and paid the full price for it. 

But to charge me $2 for taking two bites of improperly cooked grits wasn't enough, I was also told that "they cooked the grits right" - so I'm wrong. When I responded "this is how you lose customers" I was told "that's OK".  

Apparently they don't care.
This place is amazing. The hot and sour soup was the best I've ever had, fried dumplings were tasty and my pork and cabbage in chile was fresh, well seasoned and the sauce was fantastic.

We were happy about the beer selection! The strip steak dinner was delicious. 
It had a lot of flavor, and the sides were tasty,  as well. The carnitas taco plate was flavorless, and disappointing.  Our server was the worst part of our experience.  It's sad when a new place that has good food will lose business because of bad service. It took her 15 minutes to get our order and deliver our beer.  The most attention we got from her was when she was hovering over us to get the money for the check so she could leave for the night. Not pleasant, and didn't ask if we enjoyed our food, or if we needed anything.

I like this place to go out to party and dance at night. I also like to sit and chat on their sofas and lounge chairs with my friends. They have parking, but are also in a great location in Broad Ripple. There are two bar areas. Actually, if you walk in the front door the one on the right is kind of calmer and more laid back. On the left side it is about the music and people and some energy here. It is a bit about the posing scene but that is kind of fun when in the mood for it to kind of see the cute clothes on the girls, and all that stuff. The DJ here on Saturday plays good music nice variety also. I haven't eaten here so I can't discuss that part . It has some kind of good atmosphere that is interesting but I can't quite peg the reason for this. Maybe the lighting, and the fact that they don't blast you out with the music, not sure, but reminds me of a few of the fun places in Santa Monica and Venice I used to go to . Check this one out for a fun place to chat and dance. I went back recently and had a very nice time once again, so I think they are really very good.

Drove up to the drive thru intercom and the intercom loud as F#$%K. Honestly, I did here the ignorant female said drive around to place your order, but NOT like this professional statement. So, my mom said Hello and she come back on the intercom "I said drive thru to the window", OK. I was NOT ordering anything, but moms wanted chicken. When mom drove up the blackass N@#$% going to look at us and turn and walk away from the window. I told my mom really. We waited 3 minutes before I told my mom to go. This is why you don't deserved $15 dollars an hour. Ignorant and very unprofessional. This review don't deserved a star.

Other than the freshness of the fish, the best way to determine if Sushi is high quality is the kind of rice used and how the rice is cooked. Osaka has scored an A+ in my  book. The only other Sushi restaurant in NOLA area that I found with this impressive quality rice is Horinoya which closed a number of months ago. I like the ambience of the space - casual yet chic. Every employee was very friendly and welcoming. I highly recommend the Double Bang Salad. It is a big plate of healthy deliciousness and very fresh as well. I also ordered a Dynamite Roll, a "go to" sushi roll of mine. It was good. Lastly, I tried the tempura chicken and veggies. I think another Yelper rated this dish as the best in town. I would have to concur. The chicken and veggies were fried to absolute perfect. Go check this place out and please let us know what you think.
Ordered the ocean salad and other things to go. Ocean salad had no seaweed in it like I it was supposed too. Of course. Didn't know till I i got home

Sitting down at the restaurant is relatively painless. The serving staff is attentive and engaging with the kids. Drinks are brought right out and the food doesn't take too long. We've have mainly positive experiences at this location. This is why we come back

Walked in this place randomly at midnight looking for food, and glad I did! Food was yummy and reasonably price, and Thomas the bar tender was AMAZING!

Red beans and rice with sausage is a MASSIVE plate of perfection.

Chorizo bean chili cheese fries hit the spot and are beyond delicious.

I don't just hand out 1 stars, but this place Sucks Balls. Sweet Tomatoes is like a trick, fat ppl come here to make themselves feel better about eating like shit. Yeaaaa you ate salad, but you put about 3 gallons of dressing on it, so you were probably better off eating that burger you were avoiding. Nothing in here taste good. It's all bland and average. The food at Buffets are usually mediocre by nature, but this place takes it up a notch. If you want alot of salad ill hook you up with a cheaper alternative. Go to BK and order yourself about 3 side salads, at .99 cents a piece you'll achieve the same effect as going to sweet tomatoes and you'll save yourself the bill and the temptation of eating mediocre pasta, cookies, and all that other crap.

Have been here for supper and breakfast. No matter the meal, the bread is outstanding -especially the rolls at supper and the biscuits and pancakes at breakfast. So glad they have peach cobbler at both! Fried pork chops with gravy are sublime. For Southern food, especially a buffet, this place is tops!

Ever since I heard about the opening, I've been meaning to stop by. Finally got around to it the other week.

The place itself is nice. Especially like the paper umbrella lights hanging from the ceiling. The place is definitely still in the newbie stage, with its menu written on a whiteboard. We decided to sample different types of ramen. I ended up getting the Karai ramen with an egg. The broth itself was pretty flavorful, although a bit too spicy, which might be my fault (I asked for extra spicy, I have a high tolerance. Just go with normal spiciness). The noodles had a great chewy consistency to it and everything else in the bowl definitely added to the cohesiveness. And I have to comment on the egg, which was cooked perfectly. I love cooking ramen at home, boiling an egg just right and having the yolk spill out all over the noodles when I'm about to chow down. Also, love that they put lemon in their water pitchers and the Asian pop music playing in the background (shoutout to BigBang). Small, but appreciated touches.

Only four stars because I feel the flavors were a little bit off, but definitely a place to try if you're looking for a new lunch spot. And get an egg with your ramen!

My friends and I came here at about 10 pm on a Saturday night before braving Broadway. Though a teeny bit out of the way, this place was a perfect place for drinks and games before going out.

Service & atmosphere: the open space was trendy but relaxed with high ceilings, modern light fixtures, and comfy booths and couches. There's bocce outside on the patio, bowling in the back, and board games at the tables in front. Service was amazing, shoutout to Andy for the free pazookie, you really made our night! 

Drinks & food: I got a whiskey smash which was refreshing and with a huge ice cube which was great since usually whiskey smashes come with crushed ice that waters down the drink too much. The pazookie was more melty chocolate than cookie, which was delicious. 

On top of a game of Jenga that took away three years of my life, this was an awesome place for drinks.

Stopped by Tijuana Flats on the way home. I love the vibe inside...it's a new TF than the one I normally go to in Land O Lakes.  Service was fast and staff was friendly and checking up on you for refills and to make sure everything was ok! I ordered Corn Taco Bowl with chicken. It was good! I love the combination of corn, avocado, chicken (Would've preferred shredded though), black beans, lettuce and tiny chips. My hubby got the shredded burrito.  They forgot to put the Chipotle sauce in his burrito :(. But he ate it anyways....that would've been a bonus. I was a little disappointed in the chips.  Even though I didn't have room for them and they came with my meal, they were a little stale tasting, which was really surprising. Maybe we just got the bottom.  Nevertheless, we enjoyed our meal and our beer!! Place is super clean, plenty of outside seating (not for me with this heat) and just a nice place to have lunch!

Not to shabby great food great service very slow but it was the lunch rush. Hint call your order in ahead lol 
Other than that not too shabby

This place is delicious, fresh and amazing. Made my own bowl- Lettuce, spaghetti squash, both kinds of chicken, mushrooms and cauliflower with kale dressing. Everything tasted unique and just so good. Only complaint is that there is no soda. Will come back again and again
We came for happy hour, but the food looked great. The bartender, server and hostess were nice.  Very good atmosphere will definitely come back when in town.

Italian gem hidden in strip mall on rt.70. Very good food! Under new management and the pizza is always fresh! The best grandma's pizza I have ever had. also, their penne vodka  and the Tiramisu desert are delicious!
I went here for brunch, and just have to say it was just OK. The highlight of my experience here was the  salted caramel grits. the end.
The waiter had such a calm excellence about him! Loved getting relax and get the meal for two with my fiancée! There is so much food left over it will be enjoyed back home too!
Great food and friendly service! If you love Mexican food you need to try this place.

We found this place by accident. It had some construction in the front but noticed a sign and specials so decided to check it out... AMAZING
We had amazing drinks, delicious food and wonderful people. We ended up coming back for the late night portion and the entertainment was awesome. The waitress was so wonderful and helpful and we came back a couple more times before we ended the trip. This was definitely a hidden gem. The grouper tacos are bomb.com, the quesadillas soo good! The prices are the lowest in the area and quality on point . Seriously we ate at a few higher point places and got kissed the eff off and came back here .

We were a little wary to begin since every other bar we had passed was busy and this place only had one patron sitting at the bar on her laptop; however it was clean and nicely decorated so we decided to give it a shot. 
The woman on her laptop turned out to be our bartender. She was curt and distant but friendly enough. We ordered a margarita and a cocktail from the menu. My margarita was one of the worst I've ever had. It was somehow simultaneously watered down and too strong. All I could taste was poor quality tequila and water. My friend's cocktail was also poorly made and didn't match the description from the menu. Instead of leaving, we ordered food and had an equally disappointing experience...the loaded nachos was mostly just chips slathered in a cilantro sauce and a couple of chunks of meat. 
Despite being the only customers, and sitting at the bar, it took a long time to get the disinterested bartender's attention when we were ready to pay the bill. We weren't in a rush, so we didn't make a big deal of it, but there was little in our visit that inspires a desire to give this place a second chance.

Pleasantly surprised by the Ale House! I mean if Aunt Ellen liked it then it must be good... Right? Lol! 

It is a standard pub with a large bar, dining on both sides of the bar, tons of TV's, pool tables, and video games. It's good for the whole family. It just had that happy laid back feel. 

Good drink specials, solid food, reasonably priced, and great service.

The parking lot was busy, so be careful out there. Cheers!
This place is money ..good food, good service and lots of tvs they are very accommodating for changing the Channel  to your game

Came here since I was craving taiwanese popcorn chicken and Uniboil was sold out. I heard this store is the same owner as Uniboil in Goleta, so it assured me the recipe was the same (gotta have it with Thai basil fried along side it!) I called and did a phone order and the eta was about 20 mins. Since I was already nearby, I showed up to pay ahead of time and they were able to speed up that process. Pretty pricey though for a snack order of chicken, it was nearly $9 which is crazy considering in LA it's $4-5.. but the taste was exactly what I'm looking for in popcorn chicken. It was flavorful, crispy, and came out piping hot. 

4 stars due to price and also it does look like the store can be a bit more up kept. I saw stained floors and the hand sanitizer dispenser was also a bit dirty  anyways- they have some unique offerings but I think I'll stick to swinging by for just this item whenever I crave it.

In town visiting and wanted a great brunch place that was reasonably priced with mimosas. Jimmy J's was the bomb-diggity!!! Our group ordered the rum raisin French toast and the crab cakes Benedict. Holy food heaven!!! For not being a French toast person, it was the best meal I had while in town. My friend who ordered the crab cakes Benedict said the eggs were cooked perfectly and the crab cake was amazing!!! The mimosas were great of course but the staff was even better! Super friendly and attentive! A must-do brunch place!!!

I went here when I first moved to the neighborhood and it was pretty good. The fries are a little disappointing. They tasted like a freezer bag of Walmart fries that I could pop in the oven myself but the food was generally good overall. I have no other complaints.

Well I'm sure what was worse, the bar manager scolding and belittling his employees in front of the patrons, or the fact that they quit serving the menu after 8.  I could also talk about 9pm happy hour not really being a  thing cause I paid full price for my drinks.  Add this place to my skip it list.

I've been to Bella's several times over the last 8 years and each time I'm reminded of why I don't go there. Everything is either average or below average. Their sauce is lackluster, salads over dressed and soggy, cocktails watered down, and entrees are missing any depth or creativity.  Service is also mediocre, but it didn't ruin the meal. I can't recommend this restaurant and will not be back.

The food was ok. The flavors were dull and lacked the vibrancy. We are of Korean descent and know this impacted our expectations. The bulgogi was ok but the mandoo definitely lacked a fresh touch, though the yakimandoo was better and cooked well. The jaepchae was full of coarsely cut vegetables rather than thinly sliced and it also lacked flavor. The traditional condiments were sorely lacking flavor - the bean sprouts had no additional flavoring, the kimchee was fresh but lacked the spice and seemed watered down, the potatoes were not flavored well, even the daikon was lacking the saltiness. Thankfully the soy sauce dipping sauce seemed to be more traditional and they did have a squeeze bottle of the gochugang sauce. Those two items got us through. Had high hopes but not satisfied. The wait staff was good and the parking is very good.

Pub food is always a gamble. We had a 50/50 experience with ours. One dish was great, the other...meh. 
We ordered the nachos and the southwest rolls.  The nachos were ok, but the pork we added detracted from them.  (Maybe better with chicken?) The southwest rolls were awesome though! Crispy on the outside, tasty chicken and corn mixture on the inside.
So happy with the service from Kari!!! She was so awesome! Food was amazing!! Just to go for her!!!!

Amazeballs!!! Everything was delicious. Beef tartar with rustic bread--omg. Smoked oysters with a dill sauce and caviar--perfection. Chicken and dumplings--the best, I wanted to drink that sauce. And the sticky toffee pudding was phenomenal as well. This is definitely one of my new fave spots.
Good friendly vibe, chill place for drinks and casual food. Usually a very fun environment!

Found this great little place off I-295 while on a road trip (Thanks to Google Maps).  Lots of great little Asian places off of exit 34 in the Cherry Hill area, and Pho Eden is just a great example of the variety available here.  Besides pho, it offers a full menu of Vietnamese dishes (rice, noodles, soups, etc.).  But we stuck with our favorite, the pho.  This is the best pho I've had in a long time, better than almost all the places we've recently tried in Northern Virginia.  The broth was flavorful, with no hint of MSG.  They don't skimp on the meats like some other places.  We also had the summer roll which was very well prepared with large pieces of shrimp in the wrapper.  I'd love to have this place in my neighborhood.  If I'm ever up that way, I'll be sure to stop again.

Yes. The best restaurant in King of Prussia. Consistently delivers an excellent meal and service. This place is great for a special occasion, bites at the bar or just a really good lunch or dinner. My favorites and some of my family's faves are the avocado bomb, ribs, shrimp, any steak entree, burger, the carrot cake and key lime pie. The croissants before the meal are also excellent. The service here is also the best in KOP. Bobby Joe is probably the best of the crew. Super personable and accommodating.

We came to Indy from Lafayette and wanted to try something new. Decided on Giordanos and I'm so glad we did! Customer service was great. We ordered the traditional pizza. The only problem was that the restaurant ran out of pepperoni! But the waiter apologized and tried to suggest other options. We weren't too worried about it though. The atmosphere was nice. The food was amazing and the price isn't too bad! Kinda wish the had personal pizzas past lunch time. But overall it was a great experience.

This place was recommended to us and we went with high expectations. The food was good but we did not find it to be 'knock your socks off' good. The garlic knots were delicious but not the best I have ever had and the pizza was also good--but not something that will stand out in my memory. Is it better than a chain pizza--yes it is.

This place is horrible. I'm not sure I saw a single employee without a scowl on their face. 14 dollars for fish and chips, 14 for fried shrimp. The shrimp were inedible. We saw our waiter 3 times the entire time. Just as a side note - take it as a subtle clue when a restaurant says the will not serve their hamburgers any way other than well done. I hardly ever give one star. This place is weak. Eat anywhere on Hampton Ave before you get stuck in this tourist trap.

The bar was empty when I came in here. It is part of the hotel and I didn't want to go further afield as it was raining. I had a good IPA and they had a good beer selection. The food menu looked appealing so I figured I'd try a couple of things from the menu. 

I had the beet salad which was terrible. It was a good size but the goat cheese was all wet and sloppy at the bottom of the salad, drowned in dressing. Very off putting. 

For an entree I had pork with mash potato and asparagus. This was just ok. Nothing spectacular. It was supposed to be chili rubbed but there was zero spice in it and overall very disappointing. 

The plus side was the decent beers to wash it down with.

Third times a charm?  Pack your patience.  Been down to the Madeira beach area every year for the past couple.  Fell in love with Salt Rock (my previous review) the first time I visited.  This last time, not so much.  Started innocently, made a reservation for 6:30pm on Saturday of Memorial Day weekend.  Arrived a bit early as I recall how bustling this restaurant is.  Was guided to sit in their "back room."  A lovely space, just off the front doors.  I knew immediately from the atmosphere that this wasn't going to work for my wife, so we declined to sit in this room and awaiting a table for 5.  Half hour later we were seated in the main dining area, a great seat.  At this point eager to eat and drink.  Thought our troubles were a bit behind, but the overall cadence of the meal was off.  Our server was very polite (Cory), but I could tell overworked and stretched.  All in all we wound up finishing up dessert around 9:10.  Just a very, very long time between courses.  I'll chalk it up to the holiday, but doesn't seem the kitchen could keep up with the dining room.  Overall the meal was excellent.  Not a value, but quality of fish and meat is excellent and the staff always aims to please.  I might not be so eager to go back next trip as being here one or twice a year, but will be back at some point in the future.

We've been here now several times and have always enjoyed the food. They even have my favorite dish, "Evil Jungle Princess" which I haven't been able to find at all Thai places. 

The seating is comfortable and and not too cramped as I've experienced at a few Thai places. Obviously it depends on the location size, but I thought I'd mention it. 

It's never been too crowded when we go, but it does usually seem to be a husband wife duo taking care of the tables and they are constantly on the move. I've also noticed they make a concerted effort to speak in English, most likely not their mother tongue, to each other. This is certainly not important to me, but it shows their effort to please all. I personally think it shouldn't matter, but alas, it matters to some. The woman is often seen going above and beyond. My husband asked about a certain spice and the next thing you know, she's  plucking fresh leaves of the spice (plant) and giving them to us to take home. Another table asked about the manga ice cream and she ran in the back to grab them one of her special mangos. 

This is the kind of establishment you want to support. Go do it :) Oh, and you HAVE to try the taro ice cream. It's amazing.

Wow, incredible value. Huge steaks with all the trimmings for $25-$30. Steaks were awesome and cooked perfectly. I had the ribeye, my GF had the porterhouse both were exceptional. It's not fine dining but the food and service are amazing. We'll be back!

hahahahahhahahahahah.......alpine, really 3 stars? really? I would suggest Ali babba around the corner OR......my favoflave Yo' Mama's without the torture of having to sit through a snack here. 

I swear, I am not a mean spirited bloke, but when I see 4 star and 3 star ratings for the Alpine......I consider it my civic duty to speak up. 

In a word....BEWARE

At least its clean and touristy and not the country flame which should be closed.

5 star burger with one of the most amazing buns. 

I had a bacon cheeseburger with grilled onions on a potato roll. The roll was soft like a White Castle but had an amazing grilled crunch layer. 

Would definitely return!

I usually order pho ga and it's pretty good. I also ordered the avocado smoothie from there and it taste reallllllly good! Not too sweet but not too bland. They don't have a long wait at all and does to go orders pretty fast if you didn't want to dine in. They also have also of options to get off the menu if you don't want pho. They have things like vermecilli & spring rolls. They accept credit card if you don't have cash.

I try to taste BBQ in every city my travels take me.  This time I wanted to try BBQ in Delaware and my stop in Limestone BBQ was good.  I had the mixed chopped sandwich which was brisket, pork and chicken in their BBQ sauce.  It was good but I should have just gone for the brisket.  My wife had the pork sandwich which was actually better as you were able to add your own sauce. 
 The white cheddar mac and cheese is a must try side.  Very good!  Good beer and bourbon selection and if in the area, this will satisfy your BBQ taste buds.

I'm a brand new Tower Grove East resident - Grove East Provisions is a revelation. Why? 

Setting: Grove East is the perfect spot for a meal to go, a relaxing sit down breakfast or lunch, or a place to meet a friend for coffee. Walk up to the counter and order your food and beverage, and they will bring it out to you. (Bonus tip: there are outlets available in the seating area if you need want to bring a computer and get some work done. This pairs nicely with their bottomless coffee.)

Food and Beverages: They use high quality / fresh ingredients, and that makes the sandwiches, salads, and breakfast items fantastic. I had the club sandwich during my last visit and I couldn't help myself from eating the whole thing in all its beauty. Grove East serves a variety of beverages including coffee, soda, wine, beer (draft or bottle), and bloodies/mimosas during brunch. 

Service: I've had nothing but positive experiences and I've always gotten the sense that they care about what they do. 

Go here!

I can't believe I haven't written a review for this amazing place, especially after all the times I've eaten here!

It's appropriate that this will be my 1st review since being honored as a new member of the Yelp Elite Squad.

If I could, I'd give it 10 stars...nah...20!

I'm originally from New York City and before they opened, I thought the only place to get pizza like I grew up with was back in NYC.

Fuggettaboutit...they prove me wrong...time and time again!

This is classic East Coast, New York/New Jersey pizza at it's finest.

Let's mention a couple of points relevant to the times we're living in, which makes it challenging for any eatery to operate in.
1) It's a small dining room and sit down dining is not available at this time. Fortunately, they have a beautiful patio with lots of seating.
Their curbside/takeout service is exemplary.
2) The staff are all wearing masks and follow the safety protocols.
3) They're open substantially less hours than when they first opened the restaurant...now Tu-Sat, 5pm-until they run out of dough. You have to start calling to reserve your order when their phones open at 3pm. They have only 1 phone line and it might take you a while to get through, but, trust me, it's worth the effort!

I strongly suggest that you make plans to eat on the patio...even though it'll hold up perfectly for however long it takes you to get to where you're going to eat it, there's nothing better than experiencing it placed in front of you fresh out of the oven!

Don't even think about asking for extra Parmesan Cheese.
Walter uses copious amounts of the finest imported Parmegiano Reggiano and Pecorino Romano cheeses on his pizza...you don't need to add any more. When he had sit down dining, he wouldn't even put cheese shakers on his tables, that's how much cheese he uses.

ALL of his ingredients are the best available, hand sourced personally by him...no 3rd party delivery...he does his own shopping every morning. His hand made dough makes one of the best pizzas I've EVER had.

His pizza has made so many "Best Of" lists, both nationally and locally, that it would take practically the entire review to list all of them!
Here's a small sample:
#1 pizzeria in the nation on Yelp
Best Pizzeria in Nevada by Money/Time Magazines & MSN
"The best NY pizza in the world"-Norma Knepp (Caputo Cup Champion)
"The greatest little pizzeria in America"-Paulie Gee (Owner, Paulie Gee's, Brooklyn, NYC...the official pizza of Madison Square Garden)
#11 best pizza in the USA on The Daily Meal

I've tried all his different styles of pizza: NY Ricotta (Red or White), Sicilian and Ricotta Sicilian. While they're all delicious, my favorite is the old school style that I grew up with:

CLASSIC NY 16" ($23)
[hand stretched dough, crushed tomatoes, herbs, whole milk mozzarella, imported Italian Parmigiano Reggiano, Pecorino Romano cheese]
Toppings ($2) Anchovies ($3) Fresh Garlic (.50 cents)
List of toppings:
[House made Sausage, Mushrooms, Pepperoni, Peppers, Black Olives,
Onions, Fresh Garlic, Fresh Basil, Anchovies]

A word of advice, if I may: DON'T OVERDO THE TOPPINGS!
Keep it simple...don't hide the pie under a mass of toppings!
I keep it to 4 of my favorites:
Home made Sausage, Pepperoni, Fresh Garlic and Anchovies.
YES...Anchovies!
For all you Anchovy haters...I get it...BUT, you're probably a hater of the raw application...when they're cooked, they lose the "fishy" taste and acquire an almost "nutty brown" flavor that compliments a pizza PERFECTLY.
I love a nice shake of red chile flakes on my pizza for that little extra "zing".

I'd also like to suggest that you go to their website (www.smilingwithhopepizza.com), click on the history link, as well as the media link at the top of the page to find out about their amazing mission statement and all the well deserved recognition they've received.

There's good pizza around the area, especially some really good California style, but, no one does East Coast style like this...it's the REAL DEAL...

I can't get enough of this pizza...you should check it out.

Had our anniversary dinner here.  The view of Indianapolis was incredible!

We started out with a bottle of champagne and an hour later we were seated for dinner.  The lobster bisque was one of the best things I've ever had, and I don't even like seafood!  The service was impressive, their cocktails were nice and strong, and the food was delicious.

The only concern I had was how long everything took.  In all, dinner alone ran over 2 hours, so we were at the restaurant for quite some time.  No worries, it was all worth it!

Venice Cafe has become one of those places where I always send out of town people.  It is so quintessentially St. Louis: random, weird, friendly, intimate, affordable, surprising, and appearing to be smashed together.  

The staff here are your typical neighborhood bar kind of folks, but they know how to turn the bar when it is busy.  Seeing bands here is really fun, but be prepared to be physically friendly with the band - it is TINY.  

Their outdoor area is the BEST and is a constantly-shifting work of art with random found things here and there and welded and cemented into odd places.  

I love this place. It isn't the absolute greatest place, but some of their food is great (esp the jerk chicken), the bands they get are very fun, and you're always going to meet some crazy new character there, whether it's a frat guy raving about how he loves to be spanked, a South City regular who is discussing brick theft, or some artist discussing foucault.

Food and ambiance are really great! I love coming here to grab a coffee and study, although sometimes it is hard to find a place to sit. The sandwiches are very tasty but a bit expensive. 

The staff is really friendly, and if you come in a lot they seem to get to know you! Food price is really the only downside. And it can be a bit cold studying during the winter.

We made reservations and took a large group this weekend to Barcelona . The service was amazing the food piping hot with lots of flavor. I loved the fried artichokes and the spanish meatballs.  Our server Bethany was outstanding. It says a lot for a restaurant to keep a big group of hungry thirsty people satisfied and that is exactly what we did. When we left we were all happy and praising the staff at Barcelona. Thank you Barcelona!
First time here: Food was great! Great appetizers, salad, & sliders. Nice inside the tavern. Our server was very good as well. I believe his name was Robby. I'll be back!

The food is solid. To the owner/manager, if you are listening, I have two suggestions:
1) Take the salesmanship way down. Don't make Chubbies feel like a car dealership or mattress store where you can't flinch without a salesperson explaining every single option to you. Let your food speak for itself - it's good! 
2) Put out a pitcher of ice water and plastic cups for people.

I can't receive deliveries next to this school. Apparently it's not profitable for the company to send drivers 2.3 miles away. As I was forced to I just placed an order for a pepperoni covered piece of dough.

I am from the Los Angeles area, and I've eaten at dozens of Indian restaurants in my life. Taj of India is in the top 5% as far as Indian food goes. I've been eating there since they opened about 15 years ago, and they know me by name. I'm a Saag Paneer junkie and they do it perfectly. All the rest is top notch. Same owners all these years and consistently fabulous. I highly recommend. The daily buffet is a great value, and the food, of course, is superb.

EDIT: After they closed

Goodbye, my dear friends, goodbye. You will be sorely missed!

Great customer service and food is excellent! I recommend coming here. 

Thanks Abigail

My partner liked this place better than me therefore 3 instead of 2 Stars.  (He may give4) The pork belly buns were very good and I had high expectations after that.  goyza ... not so much look better than they taste browned only on one side, ok with that, but really over the top on ginger ( which I like). We had the seafood ramen and short rib.  The seafood is much better than  the short rib ( again, which I love).  The grease in the broth was not good at all, If you it order I highly recommend getting the chili oil    Only 2 choices of beer on tap ... I've come to expect better Inst Pete but the beer was good, even though it is 1/4 foam, For $7

My husband and I are from the West Coast where plenty of authentic Chinese cuisine options are available. We were looking for a good noodle place and this is it! The braised beef noodles and the hand pulled noodle dishes are absolutely delicious. The soup dumplings were juicy and very filling! If you're looking for authentic, delicious noodle options, this hidden gem is your spot!

Not a fancy pizza place at all - it's not Angelo's or pitruco BUT it's delicious. 

The crust is very thin with lots of flavor, the sauce is tasty, and ultimately, the pizza is super satisfying and yummy. For me the best part is the ultra thin crust. 

If you're looking for an affordable, classic old school pizza spot, this is it.

After hanging around in the neighborhood for a while I just like to say Le Sel is keeping up its standard and I'm still finding great new things on the menu.
No matter who I take to dine, business or pleasure, this place is yet to let me down!

I remember this awesome Szechuan restaurant in Old City. Small space, cool little bar, good beers and fresh, spicy food. The vibe was fun, the Dan Dan noodles were tossed table side and the flavors were balanced and delicious....

Last night I went to this ostentatious, touristy crap hole in old city where the mushy noodles were already tossed when they arrived. Very little spice and no balance. Average service. Bathrooms that reeked of piss. The only thing that made my mouth burn was the salt and MSG in the food. 

Here's the thing. If you have one great restaurant and open many more, it's hard to maintain quality.  There is no quality or value here anymore. The second star is given for the spicy cucumbers which were still delicious even with the pool of raw white sugar sitting at the bottom of the bowl. 

Oh, and I definitely won't be purchasing one of the $15 t-shirts hanging in the front window.  In fact, I'll never have the opportunity to purchase one because I probably won't be going back to Han Dynasty. What a shame.

CPK is a chain that is a must go. The fusion food here is very well put together.

Food: we love the food here and the food can be customized to vegetarian friendly diets. For appraisers, you cannot go wrong with the Thai Crunch Salad (avocado substitute for chicken). Entree: tostada pizza & Thai chicken pizza (no chicken)

Service: service is always attentive at this and KOP location.

Ambience: the seating and lighting in comfortable

We were so excited to get back in here, to have a drink on the patio and eat some delicious (not homemade!) food. The visit started off really well... which is why they have any stars at all. He walked in with a group of 4 adults and a couple kids. Waited 15ish min for them to set up the patio table.. so far so good. The table is perfect... exactly what we wanted. 
Then we sat for 10-15 minutes without seeing another employee. So when the server finally came for the drink order we just ordered everything.. drinks, food... the works. 
Drinks come out and are delicious but it's another 20 min before we see a server. No water refills, no drink refills. Fail.
Food comes out and it's 2 entree salads and 2 burgers. Both the salads are so over dressed everything was just sitting in a puddle of dressing. 
Both of the burgers were tasty but pretty severely undercooked. Fail.
The food was delivered by runners, so again we have no water refills or drink refills. No service for 10 min easy. My son had requested a spoon for his Mac and I eventually just went and got it myself. No one came to ask how the food was. No refills for anyone. Fail.
The server eventually finds her way back to the table, we order a couple drinks. The server appears didn't hear 1 of the 2 drinks ordered so we canceled it because the drink that finally did come out took 15 min to arrive. Fail.
Never once did any empty glass or plate get removed from our table. We were a party of 6 and glassware is falling over whenever anyone moved. The fact that no glasses were broke is a damn miracle. 
Look, I know it's tough right now... finding people to work.. but this was absolutely atrocious in just about every respect. The wait times alone should have earned a visit from the manager. If the service was crap due to the servers being slammed you'd think that we would see management running food, drinks, touching tables, something... but nothing. 
It's been a very VERY long time since I've EVER seen such a complete shit show. I wouldn't enter this restaurant again if I was paid to do so. 

The only reason there are any stars is for the host staff! They really did a great job at getting us such a wonderful table on the patio. Also, my son (8) said his Mac and Cheese was "the best ever".

My husband Dan and I visited the Inn of the Hawke on a recent chilly evening.  When we arrived, we were greeted by the bar in front of us but there wasn't a hostess at the hostess stand.  We weren't sure if we should seat ourselves or should wait.  After a few minutes, the hostess arrived and we were quickly seated.

The dining room is split into several areas.  The room we were in had a fireplace (gas, I think) tucked in a corner.  Once seated, our server, Sue promptly arrived with water and took our food and drink orders.  

We each started the meal with the tomato parmesan soup.  The soup was a bit thick, more like a puree.  It was nice for a chilly evening but nothing great.  For his entree, Dan had the portabello mushroom sandwich and I had the penne with vodka rosa. Dan enjoyed his sandwich and but would request no cheese on it the next time. 

I'm not a big fan of chicken in my pasta so asked for the penne without chicken.  Sue obliged and offered me extra proscuitto in place of the chicken.  I've had penne with vodka at many restaurants and that's what I expected.  However, what I received was a generous portion of slightly overdone pasta with a scant amount of sauce.  The kitchen was so overzealous in the extra proscuitto that I probably had 2 or 3 pieces of meat for every piece of pasta on my plate.  The chopped pieces of proscuitto were too thick for my liking and I left most on my plate.  I did eat around and had a lot of the pasta before calling it quits.  Knowing I wouldn't eat the pasta at home, I declined to take home the uneaten portion.

Wanting to end on a positive meal choice, I opted for a strawberry peach fruit cobbler ala mode for dessert.  The cobbler was ok.

With tip, we spent around $125 for the evening.  This includes a bottle of wine and a couple of pre-dinner drinks.

This is by far my favorite Chinese restaurant in Indy! We have been going here ever since we were kids and the owner still recognized me and says hello! The food is Amazing! I love the Beef Sticks & Crab Rangoon!

The Broadway Oyster Bar is a St. Louis institution. Delicious Cajun food and amazing live music. I recently attended Crab Fest with some friends. We ordered the crab stack and chargrilled oysters of the regular menu to start. I recommend them both...so good! For my entree I enjoyed the Crab Fest special seafood boil complete with snow crab, crawdads, mussels, shrimp, potatoes, and corn. Everything was wonderful as usual. The amazing Chubby Carrier and the Bayou Swamp Band played and created a Cajun party atmosphere. It was a blast as always.

Of all the places I' ve gone, this is one of the few that I have a great experience with on a consistent basis.

Their Bloody Mary is the best in downtown Indianapolis.

Monday night movie night is great, and luckily the owner has good taste in movies.

The food is good too, had I only rated based on food I'd say 3.5 stars but as a bar and chill location, it attains its rating.

Alleycat is my favorite place to go for appetizers and drinks on the East Side. The food is a little pricier than some of the other places in the area, but the quality is noticeably higher as well.  The nachos are absolutely to die for.  They list them on both the appetizer and entree menu so you can't miss them.  I also enjoy recommend the black and white bean dip.  It looks cool, tastes amazing, and costs under $5.

The outdoor seating is plentiful and pleasantly landscaped.  That is usually where you'll find me unless I'm just in for a late night drink at the bar.  The bartenders are great for conversation if you're in the mood and they take great care of their regulars.
I love that this restaurant has vegetarian options. The prices are good with large portions. I enjoy the atmosphere here too, it's fun! The staff are always friendly!

First time here! And soon as I walked in with my family we were greeted and we sat anywhere we wanted! The waiter was so sweet and nice and always checked on us! The food was great! I recommend coming here for a bite to eat

While on a walking tour through Philly with the family, we decided to stop in for pizza.  We were pleasantly surprised with prompt seating for our large party.  The menu had many classic Italian dishes and an excellent set of beers in tap.  Half my family opted for pizza, the other half had a mix of salads and ravioli dishes.  A quick poll after dinner yielded high ratings from each person in my family.  Our server was excellent.

Found this to be overpriced. Ordered the Chicken Piccata early bird special for $15. Upgraded from pasta to vegetable for $2. If there was 3 oz of chicken that would be a stretch. I have never seen a chicken cutlet so thin- not even a 1/4 inch. For my $2 vegetable upgrade I got 6 small pieces of broccoli. Broccoli was supposed to be sautéed, but appeared to be steamed. Overall, chicken and broccoli were pretty tasteless. Two stars because the salad that came with the meal was great.
Most amazing ravioli. Overpriced for sure..... but if you're willing to drop a ridiculous amount of money for 6 raviolis and side (not included in price) this is fantastic and really delicious!

Now that Rose Bowl is closed, this is now our go-to option for thick crust pizza delivery. It's the same Royal Pizza you've always loved, and they deliver from downtown. They set the expectation of a delivery time of  an hour and 15 minutes, but can usually get the pizza to you in 45. the crust is springy and fresh.
Elevator breaks constantly. Had to climb and descend 11 flights of stairs often. Front desk said they stop working when there is too much demand.... Super. Can't imagine people on the 20+ floor.

Second visit! Had the Petite Filet and it was perfect! Cooked as ordered with mashed potatoes and asparagus. Delicious! Great location and the night view of Philadelphia is amazing. My first visit the staff was great, this time we sat in the lower bar and the staff was a bit surly. We did come in a bit after 9 and they close at 11 but no excuse. Will definitely go again because the food was great.
Everyone in the group was extremely satisfied with their meal. Great service and amazing food! All I have to say is get the German potato salad ...you won't be disappointed! Can't wait to go back!

If you're searching for a great burger, search no more. Square 1 is the place to be. 

Value:
Average here. Not over priced at all though.

Food:
Burgers are incredible! Bun is perfect, toppings are fresh, and they are always cooked perfectly. My personal favorite is the "Rise n Shine" burger. It is topped with applewood smoked bacon, a fried egg, and grilled onions. 

Service/Concept:
Square 1 is a full service burger and tap house. They have a very good selection of beer on draft. I have sat both in their indoor dining area as well as on their outdoor patio. I've been twice and both times I encountered phenomenal service.

Another of the "gem show" stop offs for refueling.  South of I10 on 6th Avenue, E side of street, big yellow independent building.  What the facility lacks in ambience the customers make up for, colorful weathered characters wearing their rancho attire, lovely lunching Latino women of all ages and the large happy Mexican families make me feel like I am back in old Mexico.  Well South Tucson is old Mexico.  
Seat yourself and a small bowl of refried (bacon grease) beans are delivered with fresh corn chips and salsa in a plastic squirt bottle.  So many memories of my childhood with that plastic salsa bottle.  Salsa is classic thin with nice oregano and heat from the tepin.  The food is Sonoran style mexican.  I like the two eggs with chile verde breakfast, served with beans and potatoes, hold the cheese.  Way too much food, but fun to try and eat it all without bursting.  If I order taco's I go for the old style which is deep fried, really crispy and you can order just one for $2.50.  The meatball soup is good and hearty.
