The adults came in at about $25/ea and that was with appies, beer, and everything else. No sticker shock on the prices, so I say good value.

I notice Montana's had a bar area with some big screens for hockey, so I will go back and try that out sometime soon.

Last minute decision to eat here on the last day and hours of our trip to Nola. we went on a swamp tour and stopped in on the way back to our hotel. It's a dark lit place on the side of the road. A true neighborhood hot spot. I ordered the shrimp po-boy, onion rings and my wife ordered the muffaletta , oh my the onion rings are homemade and delicious , the wife proclaimed they were the best she has ever had. My po-boy was wonderful. Now I can eat but could not finish the sandwich and the same was true with the muffaletta, HUGE portions, delicious food and the service was from the nicest people we have meet in a long time. Truely a gem and ST. Rose should be proud of this place.

This place is beyond amazing anybody that gives it a one or two star are basically a Karen and are looking for a handout. From the soup the salad the baked potato to fillet is and was beyond amazing. The dessert upstairs again perfect.  Brother and I came with 2 other friends, they are from Miami and brother is from Virginia!!!!! From me working in a open kitchen for 8 years, I see how they pump out food!

Waited in line 20 minutes to order a salad, then was told "too bad" since they weren't in the cooler. There were visibly 5 employees in the back, 3 of which weren't doing anything. So if you want a salad and it's not in the cooler don't try to order one even though it's on the menu.
Hands down one of the best burgers I've had in a long time. It's pretty much the only burger in Chinatown. Highly recommend

Another great place to try in the Boro of West Chester. Breakfast, lunch or dinner. Beautiful décor, tall ceilings, great background music. Staff is awesome, so friendly and professional. Love their coffee. Nice Sunday brunch, to include crepes, French toast, yogurt parfait. Not to mention reasonable prices. Highly recommend.

Best arepas I've found, period. A love the whole menu but I have to be honest - the arepas are so good I keep ordering them. Really have to try a few more options, like the Venezuelan bowl my wife keeps ordering. Will take pictures next time. It's just too good, we never remember until after we start wolfing everything down. Oh, and try one of their delish hand-made drinks. I love the fresh passion fruit!

I stopped in here for dinner around 7pm on a Monday night a few weeks ago.  Its a cute little restaurant and I sat in a booth on the bar side of the restaurant.  When I arrived there were only two other occupied tables on my side but as I dined more and more tables started filling up. I ordered the moussaka.  I've been to several Greek restaurants and I can't say this version is anything special.  It was suitable but looked like it had been reheated and the meat was on the drier side. Service was fine but again nothing special.

All in all: Fine, but I'd probably check out other Greek establishments in the area before going back here.

Absolutely love this place! Sure, it's your standard takeout Chinese place inside, but the food is consistently awesome, and it doesn't break the bank. I order out from here on a regular basis, and never regret it. The employees are friendly enough too. I completely recommend this place for all your Chinese take out needs!

Overall, my experience at P.F. Chang's was really good! The food tasted fresh and was well seasoned. Due to it being a more expensive place to eat at, I expected the amount of food to match. 

For my entree (not pictured), I ordered the dinner portion of the Mongolian Beef, but the portion that came out looked like the lunch portion. I would just be mindful that the price doesn't reflect the amount of food being served. 

Other than that, we had an amazing waitress and great service! She was super nice and personable!

Well things were starting to look pretty poor for barbecue up my way in somerset county, NJ. Bobby's in Somerville closed a couple of years ago and that really hurt. Then we got a famous dave's which worked out ok but was a little crowded sometimes. They just closed down. That left nothing. Then started working down in Cherry Hill near that famous dave's - it's ok also. used to get the 1/2 all american feast.

So was really dying for some 'cue last weekend and a coworker said why not hop over the tacony/palmyra bridge to northeast philly for Sweet Lucy's? It's right of I-95 on state road. It's 11 miles on rt 73.

Phoned ahead for a feast for four, the deluxe pigout which is 1 full rack of ribs, 1/2 whole chix, 1 pound of pulled pork, sauce, 4 servings of cornbread, 1/2 pint chili, 1/2 pint mashed. 1/2 pint mac and 1/2 pint beans.  good sized portions of everything. wished i got more chili though.

Got home back to jersey with the fragrance nearly killing me on the drive - OMG - i demolished almost everything myself except for the ribs, garlic mashed and the mac - my kids ate that. A couple of reviews said the ribs could be a little dry but they looked great and my kids were ecstatic.

hands down the best i've had in 3 states including 'where pigs fly' in dover delaware. didn't eat in so i can't say much but the dining room looks fine and the menu is very extensive. Suffice it to say there was nothing left.

Can't wait to go back!

I went to Crazy D's about a month ago and it's amazing! I went to their second location by the Atlantis and it's a cute little place. It was empty but many people were coming in for to go orders. The girl working was doing a great job getting everything done and out the door as well as serving me and my friend. I got the medium heat combo #1 and it had some kick! I like spice to it and this was perfect. The chicken fell apart easily and the fries were bomb! I also got a peach tea and it was perfect. Definitely go check it out.
Food is good, Original Margarita is good and the service is great.  Manager makes sure everyone is taken care of.

Nothing like waiting on yourself. Holy crap. I had to go and get our own beers for the table.  Don't these places realize that there is an extra 200k people in town. That means you staff extra people to run your establishment smoothly. 2 servers and a bartender . There was the 500 parade today. Don't you think people are going to go out and eat and drink afterwards. I mean, a little thought into this would mean a better running business.  Is there a manager even running this place. No one in sight that looks like the part. BAD PLANNING!!!!

Wow!
Everything was so delightful. Loved the farmhouse tacos, potatoes and iced coffee! Tried my love's lemon ricotta pancakes and biscuits and gravy. Just so impressed by everything we've had here. I think this is our new go to breakfast spot! If you can then try to add yourself onto the waitlist if it's a weekend. The place was packed but so worth it!

Just so delicious. My family and I, and my friends, have been going here for 15 years or so, and it's always been really good food and accommodating staff. My wife is gluten and dairy free and they are easily able to work with her.

I would definitely encourage anyone in the area to check this place out for a great meal. And the new building is great, too.
Great food & excellent drinks, wonderful staff, and excellent patio. Staff works hard to provide a fun and safe atmosphere for guests. Good spot to enjoy queso and margs and catch the Saints game.

We came here the Sunday after Thanksgiving around 7pm and were very surprised that the restaurant was largely empty (usually a bad sign). And then we remembered it was the Sunday after Thanksgiving, a notoriously dead night for the service industry. Since we had our 22 month old with us, we decided that the empty restaurant was to our advantage and decided to give it a try. We were so glad we did! We have eaten chargrilled oysters at at least 10 different restaurants in our 7 days in New Orleans and the oysters at Basin were BY FAR the best. Bubbly and crusty and so fresh. We also had the special of the day which was mussels in the most delicious creamy sauce served with crusty bread and French fries. It should go without saying that our server was extremely attentive since we were his only guests, but I'll say it anyway: he was extremely accommodating and attentive. Definitely give basin a try - we really want to try and get back to enjoy their happy hour.

Wow, just wow, best pizza hands down, glad they sell by the slice, the grandma squares are great and the brocolli rabe squares rock.  We thought Massimo's pizza  from booth's farmers market was good, this is much, much better, the linguini Zuppa di Pesce is to die for, fresh ingredients, service is great, owner is very personable, glad it is close to home in north wilmington, as owner's other restaurant Marias is in Hockessin, this one is a staple in our home.  It also beats L&B in Brooklyn, NY.

I have visited several of the Ijji restraunts, and this one is my favorite. I have been to Ijji 2 multiple times and never had a bad experience. The staff is friendly and accommodating and quick to seat customers. Whenever my housemates and I want sushi in Reno, this is our top choice.

First I want to say that I really enjoy visiting Lambertville and New Hope.  I think it's pretty special the way they've kept the charm in tact even though it can get pretty crowded sometimes.  I went to this restaurant with my wife to celebrate Valentines Day and had a pretty good time.  Initially I wasn't so happy because we had to wait quite a bit just to get a table.  There was no host that greeted us and surprisingly we were the only ones at the door with plenty of open tables.  Other than that we had a fine dinning experience.  

Even with few open tables, it was still very crowded and buzzing with noise from all the chatter.  It's true.. if you're looking for a quiet intimate dinner, this might not be the place (especially during the weekends I suppose).  Other than that the menu was small and the food was excellent.  We both had salads before our entrée.  I have to say my salad was excellent.  I can't remember exactly what it was called but it had a drizzle of olive oil (I think), walnut, and some blue cheese.  It was divine.  Then we both had the braised beef for our main course and that was also fantastic.  The meat was so tender that the bones just came right off.  I almost wanted some rice to go along with it because it was so rich.   To be honest it almost tasted like Kalbi Jim - Korean dish that's one of my favorite.  It was obvious to me that No 9 took it's time and effort to make this delectable dish.  I'd like to visit this place again and try some of their other dishes.

Good Job No 9!

Don't try this place unless you like to wait. They know how to honor a reservation like the rental car company in the Seinfeld episode. When we arrived they said "We will have your table in 15-20 minutes. Have a drink in the bar." There was no room at the bar. We left and do not plan to return.

It's not often that I write a review after only 1 visit, but in this case, I think Three Brothers deserves high praise and recognition.

Mrs. W and I tried several items last night and if you're a thin crispy crust pizza lover, YOU MUST try their pizza!  It's great!  We were super-impressed with the crust, and also the quality of the cheese.  PERFECTION!  The tomato sauce is slightly acidic, so if you're looking for sweet sauce, perhaps the AMAZING CRUST will override the sauce.  

Tampa seems to have more pizza places and steak houses per capita than any other city in the USA, and Three Brothers stands high above 95% of all other pizza places in town.

Here's what else we had:

- Caesar salad - it's alright, nothing to rave about.  (Note to management:  We had 3 romaine stems in a medium size serving.  Not good.)

- Balsamic eggplant sandwich - great

- Cheese steak sandwich - great, even though it was somewhat dry and overcooked.  Really good and fresh hoagie roll for the sandwiches, although we have one recommendation to the chef:  Carmelize the buns - they'll be even better.

Nick, our server (and I suspect he's one of the owners) was very informative and accommodating!  Very pleasant!

All in all - worth the drive for that amazing thin and crispy crust pizza!  Mangiare!!

Oh yeah - they have slices!
Great place to go, whether your grabbing take out or dining in. Staff is always pleasant and I'm always happy with my meal. Love the pineapple fried rice!
This Mac and cheese is EVERYTHING. And the chicken. SUPER crunchy. The girl behind the counter was really nice and this is now a spot I have to make it to before I leave Philly!!!!
Delicious, fresh food, excellent craft cocktails, top notch service and exceptionally clean! Highly recommend
The wings that i've been waiting for in SB . High quality food, awesome bold flavors, & great service.
We really enjoy coming to this flowing tide specifically. The service is always spectacular and the drinks are always very consistent. We never go un-noticed here.

Can't say this location lived up to the hype that everyone talks about when talking about Edleys. I ordered a Bushwhacker and plate of BBQ Nachos. The nachos are actually house chips, no forewarning there. They were luke warm when served and lacking flavor..although they look the part. I've fancied many Bushwhackers and this also didn't come in as noteworthy to me once again looking the part with chocolate sauce

Out first and probably our last visit.  Nothing awful but nothing knocking it out of the park. And at 25 dollars a rack im expecting fireworks.  Ambience waa cool laid back. Sides left a lot to be desired.  Staff was fine but not overly friendly.
This is a fantastic family place. Perfect for enjoying a beer and watching the sunset while kids play. The food is good. The setting -- right at the beac -- is wonderful. What's not to like!
We're from California and found this place on the map. Food and service was great, we'll definitely be back.

Ordered online 1 hour before pick up, showed up and sat in the parking lot 45 minutes to get our food and had to leave to let our pets outside.  Came back and still waited 10 minutes to get our food.  Total wait time: 2 hours and 25 minutes for a couple of burgers to go.

We will never go to this store again as it is obvious they do not care about their customers and their management allows this.  Very sad.  This great location deserves a better restaurant...not this one.
Screw Carmalita's - this family owned restaurant excells at 2/3 the price, with excellent service. The food is better also. It's my go-to place in the neighborhood for a cuisine eat weekly (or more)!
Excellent, tasty food and great service. Well worth the visit to Midtown's only Korean food!

Had to show *another* friend this place.. so I tried the tomato & basil sauce and taglioni noodles. Good, but my favourite is definitely the pesto sauce.

Also got to try a bite of their prosciutto, mozz, pesto, and arugula sandwich-- really delicious. When summertime comes and hot noodles are no longer appealing, the $7 sandwiches will be a great option.

I couldn't believe the amount of ingredients I had on one plate.  Each was more delicious than the last.  All of the service was very quick and genuinely friendly. The price point was a little high, but easy to understand once you see the portion sizes and variety in the menu. Well done cafe la maude.
Food great!! Definitely recommend the Ozark burger and the beer cheese with the fries amazing!  Matt the bartender was the icing on the cake!

I called this place the TGI Fridays of New Orleans. Stopped in on my first night in town when we decided not to wait in line for Acme Oyster house. 

The food was better than expected. My catfish poboy was very good. My wife had Cajun Alfredo with alligator sausage which she raved about. 

All things told not a bad start to a trip

Sorry.  For the money, I just don't get this place, and I LOVE ramen, and their's is...pretty good.  When they say small dishes, they mean it.  I was most excited to try their mushroom appetizer, and I swear they brought out 3 tiny mushroom caps on a skewer doused in teriyaki sauce.  The waitress swore they didn't even have teriyaki sauce, but that's what my rubbery mushrooms tasted like. 

Then I got the fried corn.  MMMMMMmmm, right?  Unless they use very short ears of corn, you get 1/6 of an ear of corn.  This restaurant could be the bees knees as it's pretty beautiful and in a great spot, but for me the food just fell flat on it's face.

Came in Thursday night with my service dog & asked to sit on the patio outside. Was immediately greeted with unnecessary attitude & told dogs aren't allowed on the patio. I said: 'It seems like you're assuming it's not true without even checking'. The same young lady then said: 'Well we need to see documentation'. I was already reaching for it in my wallet & showed her the service dog card. This would have been the moment to de-escalate & correct this. Instead I got: 'well I just see stuff like that all the time'. It was said as if I just annoyed the hell out of her & like she was trying her hardest to hold back the worlds biggest eye roll. 
This is the teaching moment for this young staff member. I've been in the restaurant industry for a long time. I know what people do & what people try. You have to treat everyone as an individual & not like they're anyone else. It's not my problem if a hundred people tried to get their dog on the patio without a license that same day. I didn't do it. I have it. Even after all that, if she had just said: 'Hey I'm sorry, long day & people have been trying to pull one over on me'. I'd have no problem & this would have been a 4 or 5 star review. I'm not a negative review guy. This really set the dinner off on a very uncomfortable note. 
Luckily, our server Betsy (who witnessed this & wisely didn't get involved) was professional & on top of everything. I was about to just leave & she gave me a chance to let it go & enjoy my meal. 
The meal was very decent. We had the wings, a steak meal & some sort of mixed shrimp/chicken/sausage sauté. All decently flavored & recommended by our server, who seemed to know the menu well. 
I would gladly consider changing my rating, but before I do, I would appreciate someone reaching out for the apology that the young staff member never offered.

Excellent pho spot. Went here around lunch time after a heavy night of drinking and it hit the spot. Ordered brisket and steak large. Let me tell you, heaalthy serving size for sure. Added some hoisen sauce and pepper and i was on my way to recovery. 

The meat was definitely tender which was great and the broth delicious. Paired with the spices and added bean sprouts definitely a solid remedy for a hangover. Can i say also dirt cheap?? 5 bucks for a small (which woulda been enough) and 7.50 for the large. Great spot and lively in there as well. CASHONLY

A+ grocery store. Wide selection including vegan/vegetarian foods. They sell high quality salon shampoos/conditioners. Food bar(expensive) has a great variety and everything looks delicious. Also, this store is very clean and organized.

If you ever go to West End Cafe, make sure to bring your own coffee and be ready to take an active role in your own service.  We arrived at West End Cafe on a Friday morning which was not particularly busy.  

It was only when we sat down that things started falling apart.  Our server was not particularly friendly, giving us the usual diner greeting "y'all set to order."  We did not really care at that point, as we just wanted omelets and coffee, which we ordered.

If you're a breakfast place, the one thing you need to get right is coffee, and West End Cafe just could not manage the complexity of serving a hot cup of coffee.  We ordered coffee and waited 5, 10, 15 minutes.  No coffee.  I went up to the counter and requested coffee.  5 minutes later someone other than our waitress brought us coffee.  It was cold.  Waited to actually find someone.  

10 minutes later, they brought us coffee and said "we can bring you some more once we have a new pot."  It was clear that they heated up our cups of coffee in the microwave.  Once again, I went to the counter.....you get the idea.

The disappointing thing was that the coffee was pretty bland when we finally got it.  If West End was trying build suspense over a great cup of coffee, they failed.  

Now, the dining room is wide open, but our waitress had a special ability to remain completely out of sight during the entire dining experience.  I actually had to go up to the counter to call for some type of help 4 times.  Now, I was a waiter back in high school, but I do not have aspirations to serve myself again, unless I can get the tips.

Interestingly, the food was decent, thus the 2nd star.  Had the Atlantica omelet with salmon - really good.  If only.....if only.....I had something to wash it down......

Food is always good and so is service. However, there often is no one upfront to check in or to pay bill when sever is delayed. Can be frustrating. short of staff to check in and to pay bill. Today, they are holding us up, even though we are almost at the front of the line and there are available cleaned tables. Waiting until all the tables are cleaned, not just the 1 or 2 that are ready to seat a few of us right away. To their credit, they posted, on the table, a note that they are looking hard for more staff.

What a cute little restaurant! When I pulled up I'm not going to lie I was a little sketched out but as soon as I walked in I was in awe about how cute it was. I ended up sitting outside and the weather was perfect and the atmosphere was amazing ! It was set up to look like a little outdoor Italian cafe. There were cute flowers everywhere, live music and even lights going across the top. It was picture perfect, except my phone had died after I checked in! So mad. 

There is street parking and so parking along the back. There were a few larger groups when I was there, but they both had reservations. It's not huge so that's the way to go with large groups. Especially if the patio is closed. 

I had the cheese ravioli and it was awesome! My salad that went with it was also really good! They had a great wine list, I'm pretty sure I'll be back to just to try some of them. 

It's on the pricier side but I would 100% recommend trying it out just because the atmosphere is so cute . I loved everything about it.

I ordered the traditional rice with chicken and it was delicious!! Also got one Korean taco and did not like it. However I will come back. The online menu seemed to not have the same things they had on their wall inside the restaurant... but no biggie.
Great service. Really good chicken and corn cheese. The bento boxes were affordable, and had assorted appetizers and salad with it. They're closed on Tuesdays though.

I've never been a fan of cafeteria style, and I'm still not, but a friend came into town desperately wanting to try this place from the tv show on OWN. I obliged.

Real foodies know that this place is grease- and salt-stricken to the core, and nothing looks even remotely appealing as you walk to choose what you want.

Upper Crust seemed like it may have had a more upscale feel to its predecessors (the Mangrove and North County) but it just felt like we were at a large, clean diner. A little unpolished I might add. And that's not referring to the food.

But anyways, he ordered the pork steaks with gravy and cabbage and macaroni & cheese. I ordered the catfish fillets with green beans and macaroni & cheese. The macaroni was way too overcooked, much like everything else. It was too soft and mushy, cheese was clumpy. Made it very undesirable after a bite or two. The green beans were also overcooked and oily - if there are more seeds than shell, you my friend have cooked your beans too long. Now my catfish was fried way too hard. Wasn't very flavorful - more salty than anything. And to top it off, there was a large, thick piece of hair fried right into the batter of one of my fillets. *gag* And because you pay before you eat, the only restitution was a half-ass apology. Smh.

My friend on the other hand seemed to enjoy his meal. He wasn't too happy about the hair, but overall I assume he had a ball - but he also enjoys dirty, hole-in-the-wall Chinese food "restaurants" with grade B ratings. *shrugs*

Nonetheless, the Sweetie Pies hype is severely overrated and it needs to be stopped immediately.

I love the cho cho and triple delight! Omg so fresh and so good! They give combination fried rice with all meals and its delicious as well. Definitely a great neighborhood spot yo grab something to go. I haven't dined in but I will say they use quality ingredients.

Nice meal in beautiful patio setting. I got the fish tacos. They were good but not great. I prefer corn tortillas (they serve toasted flour) and more spices. Service was great and enjoyed the quiet serenity of sitting under the tree.

Go. There. Now. Los Agaves is proof that not everything good revolves around "state street". It's off the beaten path and well worth every turn you make. Best Mexican food I have EVER had. Start to finish was great. Line moved fast. Service was great. Salsa bar...let's talk about that for a minute. HUGE selection of various homemade salsas, my favorites being the tomatillo and habanero. No (2 oz.) mini containers either. They provide actual bowls, yes bowls, for their salsa. They mean business, and so do I. I filled up 4 different kinds and enjoyed every single bite. FYI. Most of them border on spicy, which I love. But if you are sensitive to spice, beware. Moving along, the guacamole. I have never, yep never, ordered guacamole that I didn't need to doctor up with lime, salt, etc. Their guacamole is fantastic. As far as entrees, hubby and I ordered steak burritos. Delish!!!! Not one bite of gristle, great flavor, cooked perfect, AND a generous amount of steak! Their side rice was a pleasant surprise. Fantastic. I highly recommend this place. It just may make me want to take a trip from Santa Monica to Santa Barbara much sooner than later! Trust me, when you live in a beach town, it's hard to justify going to another one, just for food. But I see it happening! And soon. Can't wait!

Thank you, thank you, thank you, Kimu for sharing your delicious food with a group of Yelpers. I went to Kimu with a group of Yelpers and had the pleasure of diving into Burmese cuisine. Some of the dishes seemed familiar where as other were new. Kimu was kind enough to provide appetizers for our group so that we could sample different dishes. One of the servers/family members talked us through the menu and provided recommendations which was really helpful. I tried a noodle dish and it was excellent. I think sometimes the best ethnic food is in a family owned restaurant with no frills, just good food. Kimu is one of these places.
So good! Great prices, big rolls, AMAZING udon soups. I've never had anything bad here and I've been here a lot!

Came here on a Sunday afternoon and was seated right away in one of their big booths. Our server janessa was great and very attentive the whole time, always filling waters and asking if we needed anything. The menu has so many options it's hard to choose, but we stuck with appetizers. The fried mac n cheese is delicious and tomato bisque that comes to dip it in is so good. Calamari was so good and the tarter sauce with it made it even better. Caesar salad and French onion soup combo is a great deal. The Brussel sprouts were my favorite thing ever and the sauce underneath them was amazing, I could dip anything in that. Lobster and crab dip with the pita was also great. Nachos were okay, could have been more flavorful. Drink menu is also large and good. Will definitely be back!

Great food and service. We made a reservation for brunch and were seated immediately even though we arrived 20 minutes early. The avocado crispy rice was incredible, definitely recommend!! Very cool and chic vibes inside

I'll start off by saying yes I did hear about this place and the facebook post about it. I was made aware of this place by Yelp. They sent me a notification cause this a hot new place. That's when I saw the Facebook post. It's a awesome story no doubt, I like those feel good stories. 

I'll start by saying yes this place needs to advertise a lot better. They have a small sign and that's it, when I went today the wind was blowing so you couldnt see the sign about the 99 cent slices. So I go in, nice lady at the front no doubt. Although it looks shot in there, looks a mess one of the worst looking places and kitchens I've ever seen. 

Get 2 slices, and man it looks nothing like the picture I saw online. The slices I got had to be from yesterday, I've worked in a pizza shop before. Even pizza that is over 8 hours old look like they have cheese. This didnt look like it had cheese but nonetheless it actually did. I mean the pizza is just not good. It was nice and fluffy and the crust did have a crunch. I just think that people are trying to say it's great just to help the place. I want to like this I really do it's just that it's one of the worst slices I've ever had. 

I should've tried a fresh pie but still when you go in beginning of the day you would expect a fresh pie this wasnt fresh.
Delicious coal fired pizzas. Sweet and fresh sauce, fresh mozzarella and spicy sausage. Can't beat it. Nice atmosphere on the porch.
Really good - burger/fries/soda all for $5! Highly recommend. Fast friendly service. Really glad I found this place - much prefer this to one of the drive thru's.
Great food and drinks and Shelly is an awesome waitress. We even ate here twice in our few days in New Orleans.

Susan and I went on a busy Saturday morning and they had us seated within 10 minutes - pretty good!  Susan had the eggs Benedict and enjoyed them - the sauce is made on site and they will not share any part of the recipe.  I had the huevos rancheros, which was delicious.  The waitress did ask if I wanted the tortillas served with my breakfast (these are supposed to be included with the meal).  It was odd to me that she asked, but she explained that most customers don't eat them when they serve them with the meal and it is part of a cost saving initiative when they ask if the customer wants the tortillas, or not - kind of like trying to get a glass of water served with a meal in California.  Overall, good experience and we'll be back.

The first time I tried Gus's was when we were in Memphis while my mother was visiting.  I have not had fried chicken for maybe a year when I decided to try some from Gus's but I was glad I did because it was superb!  When I heard about Gus's opening a location in Missouri, I was beyond ecstatic but was also afraid that I will want to eat there every single meal.  Of course, the one thing that is going against this whole theory is the fact that I don't like crowded places and since Gus's soft opening, the restaurant has had constant lines outside that made me think, "well, maybe next time" as I drive by.  That next time I kept thinking about finally came and luckily, the place wasn't as packed.  It was on a late Sunday afternoon but it seemed as though everybody had the same idea of ordering to-go instead of dining in.

I ordered the 3-piece white because I love breasts.  Wow, they were huge!  I am pretty sure I ordered the same meal while in Memphis and don't think I got as big a breast as the ones they gave me in the Maplewood location.  What I love about their chicken is the fact that they are crunchy on the outside while tender and flavorful on the inside.  I love the spicy flavor of their chicken!  Honestly, the pieces were so large that I ended up taking some leftovers that I ended up eating twice.  

Another menu item I love from Gus's is their fried green tomatoes.  I love fried green tomatoes in general but theirs are perfectly  breaded and so delicious!  With my most recent visit, I also discovered my new love for chocolate chess pie.  Pardon my expression but it was to die for!  I am not a fan of pies but if you serve me Gus's chocolate chess pie, I will definitely not refuse.  I am highly considering going over and picking up a whole pie while I write this review.

The service was nice and friendly and of course, this is a new restaurant so everything is still looking great!
A great little restaurants with a local beach feel. The daily special are good, but original grouper sandwich is the best on the beach.

UPDATE -- Well, here we go again a week later on 8/9/18. I order an omelet with crab meat. Several mins later the server comes back and informs me they're out of crab meat. You're a seafood restaurant. Really? One of your signature dishes is crab cakes. How can you be out of crab meat? The person next to me ordered a mimosa and was told they're out of sparking champagne. This place is a disaster and such a disappointment.

Run! Run to Bruegger's! 

I visit Bruegger's on a regular basis. Not good for my thighs but good for my belly. Bruegger's offers a variety of food options including coffee, salads, soups, sandwiches & bagel sandwiches. 

Soups: 
I've had the Butternut Squash soup and the Tomato Bisque. The soups were creamy, thick, filling & is served with delicious bagel bites. I've also had the Leonardo Da Veggie bagel sandwich. It's a combination of lettuce, cream cheese, onions & red peppers on an Asiago Parmesan bagel. The sandwich is a delicious combination of veggies & bagel. The food here is excellent. I look forward to my next visit.

Tonight my son and I went to bonefish for dinner
We had an amazing experience. The food was outstanding but most of all our waiter Harry
Made our dining experience unforgettable. He was super friendly and extremely efficient
He made suggestions that made our meals even
More outstanding. My family and friends will definitely be returning quite often and will be sure to reserve times when Harry is available
Donna D

I love this place and try to order from here regularly even though it's not that close to my home because the food is awesome. I always get the Pho Tai, portion is huge and enough to be a full meal. I also love the charcoal grilled grape leaves that has some type of pork sausage inside. I haven't had anything yet that I dont like. For the money, this is my spot.

This is a really great place. Didn't give it five stars because their pizza could have been better. The calamari was one of the best I ever had. Most of all, the staff was insanely awesome, the ambiance was out of this world, and the open kitchen offers a symphony of good food made by cooking staff straight out of Top Chef. It's definitely not your average restaurant. We were pleasantly surprised.
Great food, great service, reasonable priced menu too. They even give you complimentary mini appetizers as well

Both ordered eggs, bacon, and hash browns with my hash browns well done. Wait for food was longer than it should have been. Constant customer line but also constant empty tables and booths. Server did not return after taking the order. Coffee refill came when food was delivered by someone other than server and we asked them for more. The bacon was room temperature, limp, half cooked. Not only were my hash browns not well done, the hash browns on both orders were barely cooked in middle. Server returned to drop off check. This is located about 20 minutes from our house. Not worth the trip even if around the corner.

Why only 2 stars? Let's say I was let down. 
*
Came on a Saturday night at 6pm and didn't have a reservation. Waited about 35minutes and we were sat (told an hour but was quicker!!).
*
Atmosphere: super cool place and in the beautiful Hyde park. Live music started too which I didn't know about later in the evening in the corner by the bar!
*
Service: let's just say this was my deal breaker that made my night not so enjoyable. I had my parents in town and wanted to check out this place since it was rated well. Our server (honestly don't think he ever said his name) was no help. It was all our first time and when asking "what do you recommend?" He couldn't give us any ideas but rather made us feel silly for asking the question. We even overheard him talking to another server about us asking this... like HELLO, that's the point of going to a new place; to hear what you best serve. As someone whose in the service industry, If it's someone's first time I'm going to be breaking down the menu, say what we're known for and make a great impression. 
*
Food: the pizza was very good! I ordered the diode. Loved the taste of the crust and how airy it was. Not heavy or greasy and packed with flavor. Only good thing about the night. 
*
Didn't really explore the drink menu since we got a bottle of Pinot noir which paired nicely with the food.
*
Sadly the service was a deal breaker and can't see myself going back.

First time eating here, wanted to try a new place and it was very busy so figured it had to be good. Started out not good with our waitress, Madeline who looked completely miserable to be there. When the staff is unhappy it really translates to the whole experience. They bring you bread and butter before your meal, and we have to say it was the worst bread ever, how can you ruin bread??? It was those dry yeast rolls can buy in bulk at store that are dry and tasteless and they just microwaved them. Horrible, couldn't even eat them. We got a burger with fries and chop steak with asparagus and side salad. Burger was not impressive, poor quality charbroiled burger. Fries were a neat concept twisted and beer battered however had to load with salt and pepper to make them edible. He hated his steak it was seriously just their burger on a plate covered in flavorless sauce. The asparagus was served cold and the salad was bag quality at best. I left 3/4 of my burger and most of the fries and when the waitress came to see if we were done she didn't even ask if I wanted a box just took the uneaten food. That says something right there that she didn't even ask if there was something wrong or if I wanted a box, just took it to throw it away where it belonged. We aren't sure where the good reviews came from for here but it was such poor quality of food and service we won't be back.

I haven't been to Santa Barbara in years and I was eager to go for 2 reasons. It's a beautiful, vibrant city, and it boasts 3 restaurants I've been wanting to try. This is exactly what you want in a local eatery. Great food, great staff, and a totally relaxed atmosphere. I enjoyed the Savoy Benedict. Perfectly poached eggs served with black forest ham and a delightful Charon sauce, placed on a grilled Ciabatta roll. Extraordinary! My wife had their Quiche of the Moment. This day it was the Quiche Lorraine with bacon Swiss cheese and onion. Very nice! Our friend had the house made granola with Greek yogurt. We also had the carrot cake featured on the show. Almost a meal in itself A special shout out to our server Chloe. She made our visit even better than expected. Everything was exceptional and we look forward to a return trip.

I was so  disappointed tonight, all of our steaks were ordered rare or medium rare, and they all came out medium or medium well! We had to send one back,  and when it came out a second time it was better, but it wasn't medium rare, it was still pinkish Grey. The server knew we were disappointed and offered us some free drinks, which was really nice of him. However to have four people's steaks come out different than they ordered is unacceptable.
Also when the bill came out they charged us for one extra salad bar then we had. The library used to be a great place to eat but it's going a little downhill I'm sorry to say

I stopped here the other day for lunch with my girl friend and we both left full and very happy.  There were so many delicious looking things on the menu I had a hard time deciding on what to get, but ultimately tried their pulled pork sandwich.  They put orange marmalade on theirs, just a smidge (it could have done with a little more).  The flavor was great!  I won't say it's my favorite/best pulled pork ever but it was really good.  Not spicy (yay!), very generous on the meat and fresh and delicious.  My friend liked her fish tacos (good deals on taco Tuesdays) and our server was attentive and friendly.  I'd definitely come back!

Pretty good cheese steaks and fries. They have good options for cheese including the classic whiz or the ever popular provolone. One of the best things about this place is that the staff is patient, friendly, and helpful.

My favorite place for Thai food in the area! Service is fast and always fresh. Pad Thai and drunken noodles are delicious. Hefty portion size as well. Food is usually ready in 10-15 minutes. They keep the establishment clean and traditionally decorated.

Love Glory Days and wanted to check the new one out. 
Nice layout. Wide open and great TV viewing. The big screens are pretty cool. 

Great food! Dry Rub wings are my favorite. Best wings anywhere. 
Service was great. There is still newness but very nice abs efficient.

We went to seasons 52 for our Friday date night and it was Absolutly a disaster. As we were walking to our table there were people walking around without masks by peoples tables and indoors. When we got to our table table was flimsy fine ok no big deal. When the server comes we order drinks and apps right away apps come before drinks no waters no plates nothing. We get our main course it's ok my fiancé got a filet I got a salad. Couldn't really find our server to
Get a refill at all finally get our check and had to wait like 15 minutes to get our receipt to sign. And now
Well I woke up to throwing up everything we ate last night and feeling like I got food poisoning.

One of my favorite sushi places in the area!! It's in such a convenient spot, I can even walk to it from my apartment. The wait staff is so nice and from you the menu, you can tell it's a wonderful family run environment. The spice roll is to die for as well as their chicken fried rice!

Food: 3.5
Decor: 2.5
Ambiance: 3
Service: 3
Value: 3

Their chicken cheesesteak is fantastic. Every other aspect of this place is very average.
Unique menu. Try Hanger Steak, that was juicy and delicious. Salads are also good. They have a nice back seating.

The food is good and they have good sandwiches and wraps. 
They also have few options for mac and cheese which is always good considering its a great comfort food.

Meh. Maybe it was just a bad Thursday evening before Easter.

It wasn't late when we arrived but wasn't primetime either.
8:30ish.

I love a Chicago dog. I ordered 2. I was so disappointed.
My poppy seed buns had the texture of typical squishy white bread soaking wet apparently from the wet relish and a sopping wet dog.
 
She got the breaded chicken sammie - she was fine with it.

Fries could have cooked another minute or two as they were served wimpy, wimpy, wimpy.

Chatting afterwards w/ my friends from the Region agreed with my experience - they haven't been wowwed yet either.

In search of a brunch place we haven't been to yet, I checked out Yelp this morning and decided to try Estelle. You'd never really think to go there passing by since it's on the ground floor of the 444 Lofts on 4th Street, but I'm glad we did.

Since we got there on the earlier side for Sunday brunch (10:30am), we were seated right away with no wait. It was great - fresh, homemade, and one-of-a-kind brunch options in a laid back, café-like atmosphere.

The breakfast pizza was amazing, the shirred eggs were good (but definitely on the smaller side), and the sticky buns..yum! Estelle uses all organic & locally grown ingredients, too..if you're into that. The staff is super friendly, too.

Final thoughts...
Good, quality brunch in a laid-back location where you can easily find parking. Would definitely come back!

Bad Bad Bad!!!  this Sunday February 23 2020 took a drive to Carpinteria from Ventura just to Eat there got there,  at 1:30 pm, sat down order  the food,  was ok, that's not the point, got my food with the bill and then I was told i need to pay at that moment because they were closing was never informed feeling rushed right after I got my food  did not eat it paid did not tip and left BaD BaD BaD Service.

Wow! The best best best best pineapple fried rice I've ever had! If you're in the mood for thai in downtown SB, this is the place to try... trust me, get the pineapple fried rice with shrimp and chicken and enjoy. The chicken and shrimp are fresh and the pineapples are juicy, sweet, and a little tart and cooked to perfection which makes this dish an all around winner... try it!

One of the best websites for ordering Chinese food... Great interface and really easy to order.   Their delivery people are awesome too,  really friendly and FAST! 


It is so convenient and is why I keep ordering from them. 

The food on the other hand is pretty inconsistent.  Sometimes a tasty treat with the right amount of sauce...  Other times just not that good with way too much sauce.  

Their house fried rice is always really good.  I also like the sesame chicken.
VERY satisfied with the overall experience. The food was fantastic, the drinks were perfectly mixed and the service was attentive and friendly. I'd definitely come back again!

I was hoping the food here would be decent based on the reviews, and while it was ok, you can do better at almost any establishment off Bourbon.  The Pappadeaux chain in TX serves better Cajun/Creole food than here. Service was acceptable but not particularly friendly.  Go elsewhere for lunch/dinner unless you are in a crunch or don't care.  They do have a rooftop bar, so probably a good place for drinks.

I got a Montecito burger and a small chocolate shake. The burger was really good and it came with fries. The shake was not thick at all, which was disappointing. It was like drinking chocolate milk. My biggest qualm was the price. My friend and I got two burgers and two shakes and the total bill including tax and tip was $40. It just seemed a bit pricey for burgers. Overall, the food was good, service was prompt and the ingredients were fresh/local. I will definitely come here again.

We are a group of friends who get together once a month for dinner club. Every month a different person selects a restaurant and we hit it up. Today was our two year anniversary and we decided to start reviewing.

Below - all attendees were given 1-2 sentences to review. So this is a conglomerate

- Great Beer diversity. The Lucky Rooster w/egg was a very tasty & filling
- I particularly enjoyed the offering from Miller Brewing Company which perfectly complimented the Lucky rooster soup (which was rich, but the broth was a little too crowded)
- Great beer, great service, great food and drinks. Only Complaint was a hair in my dumpling
- excellent beer selection, great staff, great food...excellent food. 5 stars.
-I enjoyed my veggie fried rice. Also really liked the service/staff. 4 stars
- The dumplings were a real delight. The KFC was quite good.
- Good wine selection. Noodles & broth was great & good service.
- Sticky beef boa was excellent. Fun atmosphere for a group
- such tasty. Much food.
- Satisfying food and agreeable atmosphere, missing a little extra to merit a 5.

Thanks!

My husband and I have been dining at the prime restaurants all over the Haddonfield/Collingswood area for the past few years and have basically tried every one at this point. We were so excited to try a new place and this place did not disappoint. From our appetizer to our dessert, everything by was spot on. Not one drop was left on our plates. Plenty of seating available on a Wednesday and the staff was very hospitable but not overbearing. 

After taking one bite of our meal, we knew we found our new to-go dinner spot. This place has the potential to be a top restaurant in South Jersey. They've only been open for two months at this time, yet everything was spot on. Everyone should give this place a try because they sure do deserve it!

Spent the weekend in NOLA and i loved this place! Our waiter Maddie was great and gave us many suggestions on places to visit while in the city. The food was phenomenal and came out just on time although they were extremely busy. Definitely 5 star and worth the long line wait.

I love sushi, it's right up there with pizza. I only eat veggie sushi and their avocado roll was great. Also I had a pot of green tea, also great as was my miso soup. 

Our server, Mayumi, was friendly and attentive. 

And now for the cons.....
website said my avocado roll (at dinner) was $4
The menu said the avocado roll was ........$6
The bill? .........$7 each.
The spicy edamame was 1.50 extra for spicy?
My husband's spicy chicken was not a favorite. 

One small thing. We were seated 10 ft from the door and were hit by a cold breeze with every person entering. 

Not sure if we will return.
My husband says three stars is generous.

Mayumi gets five stars though.
Everything was delicious!!  Calamari, Chicken Parmigiana, Sangria!!

SO DISAPPOINTED!

Today was our first stop for this restaurant & we were SO excited! We placed an order of 3 Cubanos to go at 11:52 am exactly (on my receipt)  & there was only 1 table seated & finishing their lunch. That's it. Nothing else was happening at lunch crunch in this place. 
Our order was never made. We watched food for the freshly sat table start to come out and asked at 12:15 pm if our simple sandwiches were ready. We were told it would be ANOTHER 20 minutes because a table had come in 10 minutes AFTER us & was being taken care of first. Um, What? We watched 2 fresh sandwiches come out to that table - but not our little to go order?

We asked for a refund, these are $12 sandwiches each after all, and we were told by the annoyed server/cashier to CALL AHEAD NEXT TIME. (The refund took another 10 minutes)
Again, What?

First time in, last time in! 

Horrible way to treat any customer. As soon as they learned we could actually speak Spanish, they were all of a sudden willing to hustle. No gracias! Serve ALL your customers equal from the start.

More than disappointed - feel very disrespected.

The burger is fantastic, it just melts in your mouth. The fries are also top notch. I ate about half of the burger before remembering to take a photo. I didn't realize they closed at 8 during the week days so almost missed the opportunity to order dinner due to not seeing our waiter for quite some time. With short staffing this is understandable and I would recommend!

Worst comedy club ever. .rude, terrible employees, who ruin the show..it's a straight money grab. .take your money then threaten to kick you out for talking at a whisper. .don't ever go here. .trust me

Although the the first hostess left a sour taste in our mouth, there wasn't much open around the area. We tried a second time and the second was really sweet. The food was great. I ordered the burger and it was juicy and had a great taste. I really enjoyed the atmosphere and would like to try the brunch on our next trip. The cornbread hit the spot as a great starter. Thank you to the bartender for squeezing us in so we were able to enjoy the great food.

Their food at Donnie Mac's is good if they could just get their orders right. Every other time I come here my order is wrong. This shouldn't be a problem since they make simple deli food, hoagies, breakfast sandwiches...etc. but without fail something is always wrong with my order. I loved Donnie Mac's for awhile it's also conveniently in walking distance from my house but it is getting old quick that they just can't get orders right.
Definitely the best California rolls we have found anywhere. Shrimp Tempura rolls are another favorite. The pad Thai is also quite delicious. You can't go wrong here!
Came for happy hour to try out their specials. Well we got happy. The food specials were great but there are no drink specials and our tab was large.

Very friendly and accommodating waitress. Lots of drink choices. Good was very good. Prices reasonable. Would have given 5 but my order came out wrong after very specific direction. The waitress did take the meal off the bill and offer for it to be remade. Very sweet waitress.

Cadiz is an absolutely lovely, romantic and exotic gem in SB. I come here any chance i get a night off or have a rare opportunity to be out. My boyfriend and  I have claimed Cadiz, to be "our spot", I love their fairy lights, tilework , decor, the greenery inside, music selection, and the ambiance is so sultry yet classy. There is not a bad seat at all whether its inside or out, they have overhead heaters for the patio as well as some heater vents in the wall ti warm up tables. And the inside tables are spacious comfortable and spaces apart well so as to maintain privacy.  Messina, is absolutely fabulous, on top of things, and is genuinely involved with the restaurant. Its so very refreshing to see someone involved in the service like that and it's always a pleasure that she personally checks in on guests when she is in. 

Every single time I have come in for dinner or stopped by to have a drink the service has been consistently impeccable. 

Hands down, Justin is my favorite server! He has a contagious smile, genuine cool vibe and is extremely knowledgeable about the wine and food. I work in the industry as well and I appreciate his efficiency, honesty, and attention to detail. 

Favorite things to order are:
Arancini (fried risotto balls served w/ lemon basil aoli)
Steak Skewers!! omg if you love beef you cannot pass these up! i literally foodgasm everytime i have one, the cauliflower puree is insanely delicious
Calamari always a winner, freshly breaded and the spicy aoli that goes with it is delicious

Entrees: I am obsessed with their Salmon, the skin is always perfectly crisped and the fish is never over or undercooked, The wild rice and sweet corn and shaved radish go so beautifully together. 

My boyfriend loves their Mary's Chicken with marbled potatoes as well as their Steak, which is always so tender juicy and flavorful, but i still prefer their salmon.

All in All We love Cadiz!
My husband and I love New York sandwiches. We were glad we found Stein's because it's the closest we can get to a East Coast sandwich. A bit over prices yet still very worth it.
We had the Sunday Brunch her and it was fabulous! The hollandaise was made from scratch and was perfectly lemony. Great service, good prices, beautiful patio and dog friendly! Wonderful!

Not friendly at all. Not only was there bad service, but there was no service at all...

20 minutes to wait for ice cream sundae. It came as a soup, already melted on the plate and oozing.on the table. . .Really?

Coffee came as weak dishwater tasting. I'm not kidding, even Starbucks is better than this. And the server set down all of the mugs on one side of the table for us to "pass down". That was just great!!!

Sent the coffee back, and waited 10 minutes for a replacement.

I would have complained about the sundae, but what's the use seeing how they could spit in the next one.

On top of that, the whole place was empty, yet there were like 10 front of house teenage employees running all over the place. Overstaffed much?

Even the Diner up the street is better with their service and desserts, and that's saying something.

The vibe here was nice. I enjoyed the music and the outdoor setting . It was pretty to look at. Our waitress didn't tell us about the specials however . We happened to see some items on other tables that  were not on the menu. Once we asked is when she decided to say they were specials for the day. We ended up ordering the special, The fajitas. They lacked flavor. I had to doctor mine up because I wasn't wasting money. If it wasn't for the salt and pepper, the different salsas and the hot sauce, I wouldn't have liked them at all. It was a little disappointing. I had high hopes and a great meal that day. 
There is a time limited on seating as well.
Great looking place, mediocre food!! Chicken and waffles (all three plates) were cold, fish batter was soggy with a sour beer taste. No thanks!

Thank God for the smoking ban.   This place used to be the smoky bar you see in the movies where politicians and lobbyists make backroom deals (it's the closest bar to the Statehouse).   Now you can actually breathe (and see) in there.  

They have a nice selection of local and regional beers which is a plus in my book.   The bartenders are very fast and will chat you up if you desire.    The food is pretty standard bar fare, but it's decent and comes out really quick (they're used to turning around the huge lunch crowd fast).

The crab legs were very tasty full of flavor... The fries were good... The clam chowder soup was amazing. Great atmosphere... Would give it five stars but I took the elevator up to the third-floor and when I got there somebody was working on it in the elevator locked up for about five minutes on me...

Came here for lunch around 11:45. There was maybe 4 other groups dining until 12ish, then it started to fill up a bit more. We were seated right away & asked what we'd like to drink.

They also have a separate take-out area for anyone that needs to get in and out.

We didn't get an appetizer but for my main course, I had the MANICOTTI $12.50 Homemade shells stuffed with ricotta and romano cheeses. When it came out, it looked like it was basically a bowl of melted cheese! Yum! The inside filling was really good. I think the shell was a little harder than I'd like but other than that, it was good. It was also a pretty big bowl so I was only able to eat one of the two.
If you order from the "baked" menu, it also comes with bread & a salad.

If you ask for dessert, they will bring you a whole tray with what they are offereing. I actually like this approach because I "eat with my eyes". We ordered the cannoli & tiramisu to go.
The cream for the cannoli was so good! I got it for my brother because he likes cannolis & normally don't but I tried this one & wished I bought one for myself. I was also able to try the tiramisu which was okay. I am not a huge fan of tiramisu but I thought the top part of it was pretty good but the bottom kind of watery.

Must get: Cannoli
Try: Manicotti
Pass: Tiramisu

this is the other 'sal's' - original to washington twp but now in mantua...and just like twp, the pizza is the best but, the rest of it sucks...because, just like the twp 'sal's', the counter is run by highschool girls who don't know shit about customer service - they only know that you should respect them and think that they're hot and awesome because they're....like.....girls...working behind a counter or something....and just like twp, the guys doing all the pizza-making  don't give a shit how these little bitches act - meaning that they don't care how you were treated while you were giving them your money.....and don't buy anything else from them besides pizza, because it all sucks - the wings are awful and the sandwiches are terrible - just order a pizza, go pick it up, and get the hell out of there - and don't tip the little girls behind the counter because they expect it and won't even thank you for tipping them,  for doing nothing....you know what? - don't even go there, try another one of 100 pizza shops in the area....

*update: you won't get better pizza anywhere though, so if you like quality pizza - don't bother with the other 100 shops in the area....i'm so conflicted.....

Totally NOT the same owners and NOT the same food. The service was good, they've made improvements to the interior and expanded the menu but I honestly was disappointed in my food. The fries weren't the same, but the seasoning was! I got the chicken philly like normal but it was just really not good...tough, dry tasteless meat with too many hunks of onion and like two little green pepper pieces. I was bummed because this location always had faster service than the one on Jefferson but I'll take my familiar Pop's over this place any day.
This place is all u can dream about market! Everything is fresh! Great cheeses and meats selection! Love there salami!

We've been here twice recently.  Previously we were frequent customers of this establishment, but have since opted for other places when eating Mexican food.  The service was good in both of our recent visits...we were seated promptly, brought chips and salsa right away, got our food and drinks quickly, etc.  The food is solid here and I really like the flavor of their chicken.  I am not a big fan of their salsa(too much cilantro for my personal taste) as I prefer a thicker salsa.  

You won't be disappointed if you go here, but I don't think you will be blown away either.  A good solid choice for Mexican food.

Really excited to try this place, but was kind of let down. I'm not sure what all the mystique is about, however I heard it was much better years and years ago. 

Started with the Italian salad, very plain Iceberg lettuce with tomatoes and Italian dressing. Not horrible, but positively unremarkable. However, it was large enough to split comfortably between two people.

The rolls were kind of tough, a little stale, and served room temp. Eh, not worth the calories.

We ordered Oysters Mosca, Shrimp Mosca and pasta. The pasta comes plain, and is necessary as the main dishes come with nothing -- not even some crusty bread :/

Oysters Mosca was delicious, great big garlicy, breadcrumb, Parmesan Italian flavors! Nothing to complain about here.

Shrimp Mosca had the same great flavor but was incredibly over cooked. Shrimp came with shells on, and while I have no problem digging in and getting my fingers a little dirty -- they were impossible to peel because the were so over done. I CANNOT stand shell-on-shrimp that are OVER COOKED!  It's takes only a few short minutes to cook shrimp, don't serve them overcooked and then have me attempt to peel them! The shrimp were so over done that the meat stuck to every part of the shell!! Argh, what a waste of 30$ and some beautiful shrimp! I was better off just pouring the seasoned shrimp butter over my pasta, now that's a dish I wouldn't mind paying $$ for! 

Overall I found this place overrated, overpriced and probably just outdated.  I think they've gotten comfortable with serving mediocre cooking and making a $

Ordered food tonight that never showed up. Received a confirmation email following the order  Attempted to call to check on the order after the expected time of delivery passed and the phone rang busy. I'm not sure if suddenly they are out of business or they are just incredibly unreliable.
Absolutely hands down the best Bank I know. All employees are included in being the best too. FYI this review was by my own free will. I highly recommend banking with Suncoast

Although the prices are a bit steep, it is quite tasty.  I tried the squash soup today and it was delicious.  Most of the sandwiches I've had here are quite good.  One of the beat things for me is that they don't add chopped up raw onion to their mixes.  I'm allergic to raw onion so I'm always happy when I find a place that doesn't add them to the mix.  That way people who can eat raw onion can always have it added, whereas people who are allergic cannot pick out all the pieces safely.    I also really like the pastries here as well.

My only gripe is that the sandwich makers sometimes  put the fixings in the center of the bread leaving the sides completely dry and barren.  They don't all do that... some sandwich makers pay attention to the sides as well and I'm always delighted when they do!

Went here during lunch and it was decently slow -- lots of open tables and not loud. We were seated at a high, round table that was not big enough for all you can eat. We asked to move and the host was very rude about us moving. When we got to a different table, it took about 10 minutes for the server to come and get our drink order. By the time we got our food, it had been about 45 minutes of us waiting. The server never came up to check on us and we kept getting the wrong rolls. The lady told us, "Will you guys just keep it, or else it will go to waste." With that being said, we kept it and had to pay $8 for a box to take it in. Working in a restaurant myself, I was very disappointed with the service. For a $75 outcome for two people, it's not worth your time and money. Go elsewhere.
Nice menu selection!  Even great for people who can't eat seafood. Food was excellent and so was the staff.  If visiting on a weekend evening do call-ahead-seating!  It's always packed.

I cannot say enough about the staff at the House of Blues.  We held our wedding here on April 2nd and my friends and family have not stopped raving.  I can honestly say everything went PERFECTLY.

The Venue
We had the ceremony in the Voodoo Garden, followed by a Second Line around that side of the Quarter, and then a reception in the Parish.  The tent in the Voodoo Garden stays up year-round, which honestly was a relief; knowing that we had a built-in rain plan.  In the Spring and Summer it's a clear tent, so we still very much felt outside.  They drape the tent to cover the poles, if those bother you.  The atmosphere in there was so perfect.  It's a quintessential New Orleans courtyard and was exactly what I was looking for.  The Parish is the smaller of their two indoor venues and holds up to 250 people.  We had around 90 in there with tables and chairs and it was great. We still had plenty of room to dance.  If you are looking for something "bridal" this probably isn't the place.  It's funky and wooden and vintage.  It was exactly the look we were going for and as a bonus, you don't have to buy or rent a bunch of furniture or decorations to fill it!

The Food
Holy cow!  The food was excellent.  When you have guests traveling from all over, some of whom have never been to New Orleans, you want to treat them to a meal indicative of the city, and I feel like we had the perfect New Orleans meal. Raw Oysters, Crab Cakes, Shrimp and Andouille on Grit Cakes, Crawfish Monica, and Baked Fish were all standouts. Their catering menu is extensive and they are completely patient and willing to work with you to make it work within your budget.

The Staff
Kari, Britt, and Kelly were all amazing throughout the entire process. From our first tour I felt confident and knew they would be able to help me, an out-of-town bride who couldn't just drop in any time, to plan and execute the whole thing.  Honestly, I have no idea how I would have been able to do it if we picked one of the other four places we looked at.  They really do take care of EVERYTHING here.  They even helped with things that we outside my contract with them like choosing a brass band and dj. Britt and Kelly were a calming force for me day-of.  I never felt stressed or hurried.

The Value
When we were first touring venues, HOB was at the absolute top of our price point. When we took a look at what's included compared to other venues it was no contest.  The higher price point was more than worth the peace of mind of knowing that they take care of everything from tables and linens to the food and bar and coordinating deliveries from vendors.  It was seriously the difference between having to hire a coordinator and not.


Again, I can't rave enough about our experience.  It was seriously the best day ever and I'm forever grateful to the team at HOB for making it happen!

The owner is the sweetest. She's so cute and honestly reminded me of a actual Korean family. The restaurant gives such a homie feel. There isn't a open grill like other kbbq but it's okay with me. If you don't want to drive all the way to Philly, it's worth it. The food was good and the seafood pancake is really amazing. It is a lot thicker than other ones I had in the past so prepare your stomach to be full by the time your meal comes out. I will come back for sure to try other meals.

Great drinks and sangria. Excellent bartenders aswell. I think this is a great little addition to S. Grand. The food is decent, but not worth what you pay. I feel like when a resturant says it serves 'tapas' it gives them free reign to serve skimpy small plates at elevated prices. The edamame hummus is top notch...

Missed the mark at dinner.  I ordered Chicken and Shrimp in a brandy reduction sauce.  It was served as  Marsala sauce.  the potato was totally undercooked.  2 tiny pieces of asparagus as the vegetable.  Burrata appetizer also lacked the pear infusion.
Just picked up a veggie white pizza and now I know where I'll be getting my white pizzas. It was tasty and so pretty see my photo. First time here and will be back!

Go here if you desire top knot have Korean food! Gluten free choices easily adapted as it is home cooking. Kimchee was good. Not spicy so speak up if you wish to taste authentic hotness. Great waitstaff and cute lunch spot. Loved it!

A sad day when I walk in, then immediately out of this place. The waiter who won't be professional and speak to me and 2 of his relatives. The 3 worst waiters here!
So glad they DO have some great waiters. Wish one would have been there.

What a great sushi spot! Located in the Northern end of Fountain Square, Mori sushi delivers delicious sushi entrees made with high quality ingredients. Go on a lunch break and try their specials, your stomach and wallet will both be happy. 

If you're feeling adventurous, try their rain drop cake. Made with mineral water and agar, the gorgeous little cake is paired with a rich dark honey and crushed nuts. The desert is light and refreshing, perfect for the end of a sushi feast.

Wife and I wanted to be outside and take a little ride so headed to High Tides. First time here and as others have stated very nice new place. Atmosphere is lively (we were there at 3pm on a Saturday). Post lunch crowd about to leave and we stayed long enough to c dinner crowd come in. We sat at both outside bar and inside bar both were enjoyable. Our servers were the bartenders and at both bars the bartenders were very good. Food was bar food so I knew what to expect. Clam chowder has bacon in it so a no-no for me. Wife had burger and I had black bean burger and both were decent. As someone else wrote burger to bun ratio needs to b improved. On both burgers bun broke up a little. 
Overall a nice time and would return.
Food was great! Great location! Service could have been better. Garlic Crab Fries were excellent!!

Khyber Pass is defiantly a bar I have enjoyed. The food is good and it's a BBQ place that accommodates vegetarians and vegans! How cool is that? The service we have received there has been good as well and they have an extensive beer list. My only complaint is very specific to the types of beers they have. I don't love hoppy beers (I know, that's not a beer drinker thing to say) and I also really enjoy wheat beers when it starts to feel a little warmer out. The only beer on the extensive tap list that really spoke to me was the allagash white which I have had several times before. I would have liked to try something different but they all looked to be IPAs or some other hoppy or dark beer. Again -- very minor complaint.
Great food , loved the lobster escargot !  Sat outside for lunch, server was great and so was our food

Was back in Fishers for the first time this weekend in a couple of years. I had heard about Four Day Ray and being a craft beer aficionado, we gave it a try. 

We were seated outside early Saturday afternoon, which is a nice area and very well done. Unfortunately, they allow people to bring dogs onto the outside area. I love my dog, but they don't belong in an outside eatery. Especially when the dog is a high strung puppy and the parents are trying to control young children at the same time. It was knocked over glasses, food on the floor and general chaos the whole time.

Our server was a young man that was nice enough, but his attention to detail and responsiveness was very lacking. We had to ask for condiments and water a couple of times and finally got our own condiments from another table. He never checked back to see how our food was or if we wanted another drink. After waiting for a long time, he finally came back and we were able to get our bill. I was long past ordering another drink at this time. It was odd, because it seemed he had no other tables outside that he was waiting.

The munchies we had were good and the blood orange blonde my wife had was excellent. Just not the experience we were looking for that would make us visit again when in town.
This coffee is pricey but awsome! Not too sweet. Perfect amount of foam. I ordered the Vanilla Bourbon and it was definitely worth being five minutes late for work.  I will be back!

My husband and I went to seasons 52 for lunch and I can't say enough great things about this restaurant! Christina our server was knowledgeable and had great suggestions for lunch.  We enjoyed season 52 so much that we went back for dinner.  We had  a great meal, drinks and dessert, thank you, Josh (server) and Adam (manager) for going above and beyond!
Always good chicken.  I'd prefer ordering ahead and picking it up because of the crowd and insane line at lunch.

Really enjoyed this place. I thought the portion sizes were generous and the staff was very friendly.  I enjoyed the high-quality craft style soft drinks that were on tap. I don't really expect much regarding poke when in the desert fairly far away from the ocean. But the fish tasted fresh and all the ingredients equally. My only complaint was they seemed very light on the sauces. So I know to ask for a bit extra next time around. I will add this place to my shortlist!

It was an ok dining experience. The house is nice and the menu has options. 
Both of our dishes were barely warm, but the sauce was tasty. The price was too high for the quality, especially if served off-temperature....

The food comes out in generous portions and is very tasty. Very dog friendly which is nice. Friendly staff, Michael our waiter was great, and the grilled muffins, which is a unique dessert that you don't find most places, were awesome. The outside seating is very enjoyable and shaded. The jerk chicken salad was very tasty, and although it is a little bit spicy, we found it to be spicy in a good way. And the blue cheese cheeseburger was awesome! Overall, a very enjoyable experience. We will definitely come back again.

This place was really great. Excellent service. We went at around 3:30 on a weekday and it was not crowded. 

I had Mac and cheese and my husband had a burger. Both were delicious. I still prefer Fido's Mac and cheese and my husband has had a better burger, but I was impressed with the food and restaurant over all. Besides the only thing my husband didn't like was the soft bun, but next time we can order it "toasty". 

The place looks really nice and there's a good view of downtown from a lot of the tables. I can't wait to go back.

Yummy sandwiches, sides, and desserts. Staff is always friendly and I still haven't tried everything on the menu I want to try but everything I have has been good. Serve yourself coffee and stay awhile. Cute atmosphere.

Philly is a food city; it's also a drinking city (like our water supply blows over the legal limit...).  While good food and drink abounds, rarely here do you find the one ingredient that renders Caribou Café delightfully unique:  class. The staff is like family.  Young at heart, casually elegant, and all hipster-funny as hell.  The drinks - reasonably priced.  Admittedly I have yet to sample the menu as much as I have the spirits (**hiccup**), especially the champagnes.  But I will say this: the French onion soup and their fries? Rather orgasmic.  The split-level indoor seating, the outdoor patio, the easy breezy music (both indoor, awesome playlists and the incredible jazz ensembles) -all of it...dovetail to make a consistent 5 star experience.  Solaris, Suzanne, Brian, Ashley, Andy, Colleen, the entire staff.  They are like family to me.  In fact, when good news finds its way to me, I go out of my way to celebrate there.  Thanks, Caribou; this Yelp's for you all.
1 word: Yuck!  Stopped by to grab a bite to eat while on my way to my Sissies. The smell of the Lo-Mein was so bad, so repulsive, so disgusting that we had to throw it away. Never again.
Loved the SOHO Acai Bowl! It was $12 and change but was well worth I could of split it with someone. The girls were very informative and gave me all the info I needed about their juice cleanses
Four stars for friendly counter service, great sauces, and cute storefront.  Had two corn tacos with carne asada and a side of guac. Reasonably priced ($10.00), overall, underwhelming....

I visited the location yesterday evening and had an exceptional visit! First off the margaritas are on special on Wednesday's ( we didn't know this prior so it was exciting news lol) and they were able to make a peach one on the rocks! We sat at the bar top and received wonderful service from both ladies. I captured a picture of my margarita but did not get one of my steak, probably because I ate it so fast since it was delicious. I ordered a filet mid rare and it was cooked perfectly and had the best flavor. My baked potato was piping hot as well. We will definitely be back soon!!
Great breakfast here with a bachelorette party. They were very accommodating and the service was great. They had a breakfast buffet, and great drinks! Perfect for large groups.

Visited based on recommendation from a colleague
Very quintessential family italian restaurant vibe
Had the Chicken Cabonera with corn crab bisque soup( small portion on the soup end)
Meal was served in a timely fashion
Very rich and flavorful, entree was a great portion for the price
Service staff was very attentive
Will return in the future
Great food and awesome staff! My bowl was so fresh and very clean! We were visiting from FL and they went above and beyond to make sure we had a great experience!

The ONLY reason that I'm giving this establishment a one star is simply due to the customer service that I received and the fact that I can't rate it at a zero for the outright prejudice that the staff displayed during my brief, first & last visit. When you're a business owner, the only color you should be concerned about is green. Though I was disappointed, I was not surprised in the least. This lesson cost me $38.24 and I'm just grateful that I didn't give more to an establishment who didn't care to greet THIS customer nor check to see if I enjoyed my meal or not. Very embarrassing experience on their behalf, shame on you guys.

Finally, this Byblos location has started offering Gyro dishes. My wife and I stopped in here for dinner a few years ago and I was stunned to find out that they simply did not have gyro meat. There other, less fancy locations (like in the mall) had the dish, but this location didn't. Anyway, I stopped in for the first time in a while the other day and was very excited to see my favorite Greek item finally added to the menu... and, it was pretty good! 

BOTTOM LINE: I'll be a regular again here at Byblos now that they finally have Gyro meat!

On our first trip we weren't sure what to expect from a new place billed as 'Halifax Street Food', but we've since come back a number of times because of the great food and hospitality.
