Each server has been so friendly and outgoing, and so far we've had most of the menu from the Hali Cheesesteak to the Forager Pizza and everthing tastes SO GOOD. Excellent beer selection and a little older crowd which is nice for this thirtysomething couple.

we went here like 10 years ago. this is the first time i stepped in here in that 10 years. not much has changed and it maybe another 10 years before i go again. i got the tilapia, it was overcooked. my mummys chicken was overdone also. they were generous portions but a little over cooked. the baked potato is very good. salad was ok. 

my chief complaints about this place are that you can't sub soup for salad. i am not much of a side salad eater. even at olive garden i get soup instead of salad. also, they have special post is certain places in the restaurant but not on the menu or a special card of anything. what am i supposed to do, walk around the restaurant trying to decide what i want to eat? just not my kind of place.

the food is just OK. i would go back sooner if i don't have to pay for it.
Great place to grab a drink or quick bite. Never too crowded, but rarely empty. Loved by locals and traveling beer lovers.

#1.) I didn't realize yuppies were still allowed out in public, but apparently they all come here. Not everyone here belongs in that category. However, if this is your category, this is where you belong. 
#2.) There was a completely awful band, playing their awful music, awfully loud. Then, as I'm writing this review; those shitty, know-nothing sons 'a bitches start defecating all over Folsom Prison Blues. Then, I realize it! People are enjoying this music. Yuppies think Johnny Cash is Donald Trumps nickname. 
#3.) service was slow. 
#4.) food was right on par with O'Charlies. 
It's the perfect place for people who I don't like.

So, we are always up for a good brunch buffet and based on other reviews we decided to check out Lil Dizzy's. We do not shy away from "hole in the wall" restaurants because they usually have the best food. Lil Dizzy's was not just a hole in the wall, but it was packed FULL of people, which made it very hard to get to the buffet. The food was decent, but our server, Tracy, was terrible. She didn't remember our drink orders, didn't check on us, took forever to bring out our made-to-order items and never brought the second cup of coffee I asked for. A large party came in after we did and got their food before we did. The buffet plates are very small, so you pretty much have to go back for seconds to try everything you want, but it was so hard to maneuver in there, it wasn't worth it. I've seen people say that Lil Dizzy's has the best fried chicken in NOLA, but those people obviously haven't tried Willie Mae's! Also, the ladies room door doesn't lock and there are two toilets in one room...weird! Long story short...we will not be going back!

Better than most diners. Looks like it was recently renovated so it looks bright and cute, but I thought it was pretty chilly in there! I had a Belgian waffle with eggs and bacon, my boyfriend had pancakes. My waffle felt a little overdone since it was crispy and dark brown. Waffles should be on the softer side with a golden brown color and no crispiness to it, but that's how I like my waffles. Service was friendly.

Being from NJ I'm always biased towards Italian food out of my state- but this place is great! Their pizza is on point and their salads, ziti & eggplant parm are delicious! Don't let the walk-in pizza front fool you, there is a full restaurant with seating in the back that is quiet and a great place for a sit down meal. I've eating their catered food multiple times and their quality is great.

Wow! What can I say, I was in town last week for a convention and I spent some good time at Foleys. The happy hour specials were very good, especially the Irish egg rolls. The servers were on top of the drinks and they all had a good sense of homor. They made sure we were all taken care of and happy. Mr. Foley welcomed the CDF Firefighters Honor Guard Pipes and Drums band to play at the pub on two different nights. The band got the place rockin' with their bagpipe tunes. His hospitality was above and beyond and the local news crew even came out to film the band. I haven't enjoyed an Irish Pub this much ever! Thank you Mr. Foley!

Had a very positive first impression of this conveniently located restaurant on Mass Ave. I went here for lunch with a couple coworkers and tried out the chicken sandwich, which I loved! It had a bit of a spice to it - so, so good! It came with fries, and I HIGHLY recommend getting the garlic fries. They are so much better than the plain ones - great flavor. The atmosphere is perfect.. I loved the modern but slightly rustic look inside, like something I haven't really seen in the Indy downtown area. Service was pretty good, wasn't anything amazing (possible area for improvement in my opinion) but still good. I feel confident that I will take friends here when given the opportunity.

The food was good but to be honest it was nothing special. The steak and the short rib had very similar flavors. It was like a pot roast. If that's what you're into then definitely check it out. However I do have to admit that their crab soup was very very good same with the cheesecake dessert. Over all I give it 3 stars because it was expensive and I don't see why it is priced that Hugh for average food. Food also took forever to come out too.
Having lived in Nashville for 3 years I have eaten hot chicken at ~5 places and Big Shakes is by far the best. The "Rambo" heat level is awesome!!

The owner was there the night my group was in.  He was very friendly and added to the atmosphere.  The food was amazing and the service was great.  We had 18 guys in the place and the pizza and beer kept flowing quickly.  I highly recommend this place and I can't wait to go back.  Oh yeah, don't forget to dip the crust in the honey - AWESOME!
Smells awesome.  And the waffles live up to it - they are really delicious.  And so is the coffee.  Get yours to go though; the cafe itself (on 10th and Walnut) isn't very comfortable.
They make the best pizza in Marlton!! I will not order from any other pizza place in Marlton. This place hands down makes a delicious pizza!! Fresh toppings! And yummy cheese!!

This wasn't our first choice as we ventured out on Saturday night.   We got there around 730 and it was an hour wait.  We were hungry and tired of trying to figure out where to go. So we opted to wait.  The wait was only surprisingly 30 minutes. I noticed that the floors were super slick-as I had heels on I could have just slid over the floor. So watch your step!  We had reviewed the menu on line while we were waiting and nothing really jumped out as a had to have or try.  There were a few things that seemed ok.  We settled with our beer-my husband said it was ok.  And he likes nothing more than trying new beers. I settled with a glass of wine and we decided on getting the pretzels with cheese/beer sauce as an ap.  The pretzel sticks were pillowy and soft. The cheese sauce was runny and sort of bland.  This should have been an indication of the way the rest was going to go.  I settled on the Adult Mac and Cheese-which has pepperjack, alfredo, and cheese sauce that's simmered in one of their crafted beers with red pepper flakes, bacon, grilled chicken & breadcrumbs.   My husband got the BeddaChedda Burger.  My food was warm at best and between the pepperjack and red pepper flakes I was exepcting some sort of zip to it...it was very bland. The chicken chunks (there were 5 all together) had no flavor.  The burger review was I've had better it's ok.  Not much flavor.  Our waitress came back to check on us and I actually sent my mac & cheese back.  I've never done this but I just couldn't eat it. She did ask if i'd like to try something else and I opted out.  I wanted flavor and we were 3 for 3 on that I doubt a 4th item would be above this.  The manager came over to talk to me and ask me what the problem with my food was and he was very nice.  He offered again if I wanted to try anything else.  I  did not.  They did take my meal off of our tab.  All in all I'm in no rush to go back. There are plenty of other options in this city that are way better.

Food = Scrumtrulescent // Price = Poor Person Friendly // Service = Felt like I could've been Afghani in a past life

It's like being the first to discover a killer band. You want everyone to join in your enthusiasm but you don't want everyone jumping on the bandwagon. A secret you just can't help but share.

If I was on death row, this would be my last meal.

Sambosa appetizer with some spicy, mint chutney for dipping. Chai tea - the real deal. Vegetable Teekah Masala. 

I would die a happy, full convict.

Now, go enjoy the best meal of your life and tell no one! :)

Was there last night and the food could have been great but arrived cold.  For the prices charged one should not have to send their plate back to be heated up.  The atmosphere was pretty cool but the iced food ruined the entire dinner.  No one wants to send their plate back to the kitchen for any reason (I'm sure you know what I mean).  Would we return? Probably not because we would not want to chance the same thing happening twice. Additionally the portions were small and this is coming from a 120 lb. female.

If you decide and insist on going to go GiGi's use a 1/2 price coupon or voucher.  At least then you won't be as pissed off.

Chicken. Waffles. Peach Butter. Syrup.

If you want to chow down where the locals go, hit up Maxine's for some good 'ol fashioned soul food. I hear their fish and collard greens are delicious, but I have a hard time not ordering the traditional chicken and waffles (because of course).

The service is excellent and it's nice that there are still restaurants out there where the managers walk around and chat with customers. Everybody's a member of the family at Maxine's.

Been here a few times over the past few years. For me, it's just ok. Food is good, but nothing overly special.
I am not a craft beer person, so their wide selection of beers, does nothing for me. But I do appreciate that they will let me "try" a beer if I want to (think a shot glass size), before I commit to a whole glass.
Not to much on their menu appeals to me personally, so I stick with what I know. the Mouse Trap grilled cheese & the occasional Fish and Chips plate.

the grilled cheese is very tasty and made using their "Icky" bread. four cheses, and a grilled tomato. the fish and chips are good, and so is the tarter sauce.

service averages to be slow enough to make you wonder what is taking so long, but fast enough so as not to make you want to say something. staff is usually friendly.

parking is a challenge sometimes considering their location and they are so close to another eatery, as well as a book store. so if you plan to show up on a weekend, allow for time to circle the lot a couple times.

This place is one of the best "sleeper" / time capsule establishments in the city . 
       You don't hear much about this restaurant but it is a true gem .  It's location is a bit out in left field but you will be very glad you went.  The steaks are prime and are always cooked properly.  There are a lot of sides to choose from which are all fresh , so you won't find s lot of Sysco from a can food here.  Their wine selection is very good as well.  The atmosphere is that of an old family establishment like something from The Godfather , but without the mob hits.  Give it a try , you'll be happy you did.

Their hours say 9-9. Apparently the girl working decided that she wanted to close down early. Came at 8:20 and the open sign was off but she was still in there. Change your hours if you close earlier. You just lost a frequent customer.

We were recommended here from a friend, and after a while we gave it a shot for date night! It was way better then expected, very intimate dining and quick service. Our waitress (Katie I think) was amazing and went above and beyond for us. We shared a pizza, salad, and the scallops. I have never had scallops so good, they melted in our mouths. Location easy to get to, and the green house is so cool. WE WILL  be back!
1st Time in Clearwater Beach was given many recommendations on food but this by far was the Best! Everything we tried was delicious! The Grouper Sandwich amazing!!

It was raining and needed to eat a bite before we left town and we found Mr.B's on Yelp. We were lucky that we went there way past the lunch rush and so it was easy to get a table. And the food, oh my! As a vegetarian, I was resigned to eating a salad. I started out with eggplant sticks, which were not bad. To be fair, the waitress offered a veggie linguini and I was not sure if I wanted to order that because I try to avoid pasta/wheat even though I don't have celiac. But my son ordered fettucine with veal and one look at the fettucine, I wanted the pasta! He absolutely loved the veal. My pasta was oh so fabulous. It was tossed in lemon butter sauce and the vegetables were plenty. 

My partner ordered the BBQ shrimp and he thinks it is his best meal on this entire trip over the past two weeks. Order the shrimp. What else is there to say? The sauce it was served on was delicious, buttery and nicely spiced. It is not at all what you think when you think of barbecue. 

The only disappointment was the bread pudding. Perhaps we were too full to appreciate it. Perhaps another favorite bread pudding from  a different restaurant spoiled us. It was just okay.  Overall, a fantastic meal and a fantastic place.
First time here since the remodel. The food is still just as good, but it needs to be 24/7 again. Late nights there use to be my go to spot after the bar!

The eclectic ambiance was fun, nice place, good vibes. Food was amazing! I do want to share that the Lobster tamala is not a tamale like I was expecting and it's pricey. So if you're wanting that tamale substance, it's not this dish. It was good tho! :)

A long time favorite! Every time my wife's family cones to town they ask to grab a pizza here. They have a great selection of pizza and a very inviting atmosphere. They have great locations all over town. I highly recommend
Limited menu, servers not familiar with the ingredients of the food, AND THEY ROUND UP YOUR TAX! Isn't that stealing? Yikes, not going there ever again.

Not a fan.

I ordered a burger with grilled onions, mushrooms, and pepper jack cheese on Texas toast.  The toast was partially burned and SO greasy, and the mushrooms tasted like they came straight from the can.  The fries were mediocre at best, and the service was kind of slow with hardly anyone in the restaurant.  It has a cute diner feel, but the entire floor was so sticky I made sure I walked on the mats.  If the floor is that dirty where the customers can see it, I can't imagine what it looks like away from the public eye.  I will definitely not be back.  The only reason I gave it two stars is because the staff was nice and it wasn't the worst burger I ever tasted.

One of my favorite places.  Varied menu, both food selections and prices.  I have always had excellent service.  

I'm not a beer drinking so i can't comment on that.  But the food is delicious!

Normally I would be scoring 5 stars for Lincoln Square, but this location left a bad taste in my mouth and it wasn't because of the quality of the food. I ordered the same thing I get at every location and it was not at all like it used to be. The portions were smaller than I have ever seen especially the queso, but if you like onions then you're good. 
I asked for more queso (since there wasn't any) and was told I had to pay for it. Apparently the cooks call the shots and even though they don't give you what you order in the first place you will have to pay for it twice. Luckily my waitress saw that I was dissatisfied and comped it anyway.

What can you possibly dislike about Thistle? Friendly staff that aren't just lazy impersonal college employees, great vision and message, and clean warm interior done with obvious intentionality. And of course...very good coffee. And music that is actually BACKGROUND music. If I go to one more coffee shop in Nashville with ear grating indie emo music at concert volume I'm gonna pull my hair out. Actually I'll just give them a poor review. But there's a reason those places get three stars and operations like this get 4.5.
This place is my new fave spot. Everything here is insanely fresh and delicious. I CANT wait to go back

Kayaks is such an amazing gem. The food is out of this world, and the drink selection is so unique, especially the seasonal flavors. The atmosphere is great to study in or meet a friend for coffee. I can't wait to come back to Kayaks at least once a week!
Awesome food!! Had grilled Artichokes to start, followed by a SoCal burger, and Israeli Couscous... Definitely will return
Great pizza, it's very similar to other "fast food pizza" places such as blaze pizza. Very busy though!

Okay so this was an awesome, simple, delicious and gratifying experience! Our server Kelly was gracious fun and engaging. Love the food. Bolognese complimented the classic meatball perfectly. Polenta was on point with a sting note of garlic and cream; bravi!
Great cheap prices and nice bistro feel. 

Will certainly return

Ahh the love for The Lark!

The Lark doesn't need another review raving about how good it is - but it is deserving of one.

This is my second time returning to this restaurant - the first being shortly after it opened in 2013. The service has been consistently on point; the menu is perfectly satisfying (we wouldn't expect less being that the team originated in San Francisco); and the ambiance is always enjoyable (the urban interior just adds to the appeal).

If you've experienced The Lark and are as in love as I am, check out their other locations around the corner: Lucky Penny for cafe and pizza, Caveau Wine Bar for some tastings, and their upcoming Spanish resto set to open soon.

Til next time Santa Barbara...

Setting: 6 pm on Wednesday, party of 20, upstairs seating (2 round tables)

Vibe: was here for an interview and was expecting to be taken to just any old restaurant and I was INCREDIBLY wrong. Commander's is next level, it's extremely elegant, when they serve your food all the waiters reveal it from their metal hiding place JUST LIKE A PALACE. Genuinely spectacular.

Food: ELEGANT selection, everyone I was with loved what they got. I got:
- turtle soup (5/5): first turtle soup of my life and never looking back, it was amazing, rich flavors that reminded me of chili, almost licked the bowl it was so good
- pecan crusted fish (4/5): extremely tasty, unique dish with tons of flavor
- bread pudding soufflé (5/5): oh my gosh this is just spectacular, it's just as good as it sounds and more, make sure you order it at the beginning of the meal

Drinks: I had the vodka Collins, it was refreshing and tasty, they have a HUGE cocktail menu 

Bottom line: very elegant, very delicious place for a celebratory event with friends, dinner with parents (@ college students) or date night

One word : BRUNCH
You just gotta try the brunch. Never have I eaten so much high quality food for such a low price... I died and went to brunch heaven. 
And waiter Julian is surely the angel of this brunch heaven. The service was stellar. Our rowdy hungry party of 10 didn't faze him at all. He took all our request and even separate check in stride. Kudos Julian. Psst management, give the man a raise...

So you can choose any and all items on the brunch menu's right side and at any quantity you like. We tried about everything, except the beef or fish  tacos... and oversight on our part. All the tacos are quite small, but you can have as many as you want, so it's all good. 

Chips and fire-roasted salsa: The chips are awesome, seem to be made in house. Not a huge fan of the salsa as I like mine a bit chunkier, but it is tasty.

Breakfast Tlayuda: When they say giant crispy tostada, they mean giant. That thing had to be 15 or more inches across. It reminded me of a breakfast pizza with a nice thin crispy bottom. Lots of toppings and the flavors play well together. A must have.

Sweet corn tamales: I'm not a big tamale fan, but the rest of my crew found these to be delicious. 

Queso Fundido: Damned that stuff is delicious... yeah, I said damned... a big bowl of melted cheese that is a little crispy on the edges, a few flour tortillas and some salsa... you can add stuff like chorizo or mushrooms, but it really doesn't need anything else... I enjoyed the cheese on my chips, but it would taste great on anything. 

Adobo chicken tacos:nicely seasoned chicken and all the fixins... yummy

Cauliflower carnitas tacos: Good, but not our favorites

Al Pastor tacos: yummy, one of my personal favorites

Cholita Benedict: Deemed very good taste wise, only drawback was the Hollandaise was a bit too thin, it could have been a bit creamier

Mexican chocolate waffle: a favorite of the entire table, served nice and hot and so chocolaty

Cholita chilaquiles: i wish ii would have discovered those earlier into the meal. By the time I got around to these I was already quite full or I would have had a ton more of these. The crispy chips with all those toppings and the perfectly flavored pork carnitas was like a party in my mouth.

Mexican street corn: yes,  you must have some of this. Simply delicious. 

Bacon wrapped hot dog: I was a little surprised that this is a taco. I didn't care for the beans in there, but the rest was yummy. I mean how could you go wrong with bacon wrapped anything? 

Mexican style crispy chicken Milanese sliders: this one will surprise you as it is quite spicy. Tasty, but spicy. 

Cinnamon spiced churros: Piping hot, crunchy on the outside, soft on the inside...num num... I would like to have a bit more sauce with it to dip it in. Yes there is some decorating the plate, but I like to dip them. 

And don't forget the libations to go with your brunch. We indulged in margaritas, of course, which you can get by the pitcher, if you are serious drinkers like we are. 

I highly recommend trying the different flavors of mimosas (passion fruit for the sweet folks and pomegranate for those less sweet) and then there are the Bloody Marias... 

And as if we needed more food, we ordered a round of guacamole and chips , which ... you guessed it... was also delicious. Freshly made, nice flavor and with little chunks in it. 

Needless to say, our entire party will be back. I am  pretty sure they will raise their prices on the brunch soon, as they cannot possibly be making money this way... I am just happy that I got to experience such a fabulous meal.
Best Hot chicken in Nashville, the parking situation.....sucks, but it is what it is.

An open letter to John Besh

Ummm. Hi. Will you marry me? Please. I mean I know you're already married and all and while I am certain that she is a lovely lady I would like to steal you away. Okaythanksbye.

Xoxoxo,
Angie

I don't think he will say yes and I have to say I'm relived for that. Can you imagine being married to Mr. Besh? He would be in the kitchen all the time whipping up delicious things, wanting you to taste test them. I would weigh a TON. 

American Sector is great. I love all of the old photos on the walls. We were seated at a regular table graciously by request and not the long bench with the tables practically on top of one another. The atmosphere was perfect.

We started with the Fried Louisiana Shrimp with Tabasco mayo. Sounds boring...was anything but. They were perfectly presented and delicious and wrapped in little strings of phyllo. (We had to ask what the little strings were because we couldn't figure it out) So good! For my main entree I had the Blue Crab and Shrimp Saffron Étouffée. I've never had an étouffée with pasta in it instead of rice. This dish makes me wonder why all étouffée isn't made this way. Oh yeah, maybe because we'd all weigh a ton. Anyway, it was spectacular. Rich and just so damn delicious.

Definitely go try out American Sector. The old photos on the wall are worth a visit alone. The food, though, will knock your socks off.
Love the ambience and the waitress was outstanding. Had the Bar burger and it was excellent. Their beer selection is on point, definitely will be back

Mistake coming here - the other negative reviews are accurate.  We ordered drinks and food. When the jambalaya came, it had no sausage in it (even though it said so in the menu), and we were overheard another server telling one table that the seafood gumbo had no had no crab despite it saying crab and shrimp on the menu (and after we had already received our order of it). Our drinks were very poorly made as well, one of which obviously had no alcohol in it... DONT go here. Waste of money.

**After our bill came, my husband went to the bar to get it taken off the bill (server never came back to our table) and the bar tender said it was a virgin mint julep, despite us ordering a mojito, and being billed $10 for a mojito...
They moved! Now across the street and around the corner from the original location. Now located at Renaissance Square, Rt 70 and Locust. Still awesome-even better with pizza and an expanded menu.

I don't eat Wendy's much but I love this one. They are always very fast and very friendly whenever I go. They also have the best strawberry lemonade which is one of my favorite drinks. Also I really enjoy their salads which come in half and full size which is great for those who like to watch their portion sizes. I recommend trying the spicy chicken ceasar salad, it's wonderful!
Awesome deli came in on business trip to St. Louis. Me and a co worker both got the hog father very tasty and filling.

This is the second and last time I come here. I came late morning. We ordered and it took over 30 minuets to get our breakfast. When I finally got my order the eggs and potatoes were cold. I don't know what happened but I'll not be returning here.

Ate here when our flight was delayed. Ordered the wings and the 48 hour steak.  The salad that comes with the steak was warm from sitting out too long. The steak was mediocre which was a surprise given the Mike Shannons name. The rice that came with the steak was over seasoned.  

The wings were the worst part. It tasted like someone rolled them in paprika and chilli powder (and not in the good heat producing way). I love spicy wings when the spices work well together and create a nice flavor. This was over seasoned to the point of just being spices for their own sake. They were also over sauced. 
Marcella was our waitress and she was great. Best part of the experience. 

Would not recommend.

Completely forgettable...  Asked what the difference was the fish and chips and the fried cod and chips.  Server said they are both cod one is square!  Really?!  I have never seen a square fish.  Plus I was the youngest person in there by 30-40 years!  Lol.

Chicken parm hoagie sucked, it was made with chicken tenders instead of a whole slice of chicken not much sauce or mozzarella cheese. The pizza sauce was better almost smell like there was bleach on it. Will never order from here again. If you want something good just go to Zesto!
I went here for first time with friends. The Northern Spain soup & fish were delicious. I can hardly wait to go with my husband. Excellent.
Fun place love the atmosphere. Food was interesting and good? Did the Chef's sampler which I recommend! The was only one dish I did not care for. Loved their creative cocktails too!

Great food, great drinks, open late! We tried this place after having a sub-par experience somewhere else, and we were pleasantly surprised! Close proximity to our hotel was a definite plus!  We will most definitely be back the next time we're in St. Louis!

Stumbled upon this place and based on other Yelp reviews, decided to try it. I ordered the Cobb salad with a steak burger and the herb garlic fries. The salad was huge. Fresh greens, nice sliced tomatoes, avocado, crispy bacon. The balsamic dressing was very good as well. 

The fries left something to be desired. First they were topped with a pile of mozzarella cheese. Nowhere on the menu did it mention that. Once I picked the cheese off, I found less than crispy fries lacking herb and garlic. I love a good garlic fry and these were disappointing. 

The restaurant was clean, the service was quick, and the option to build your own burger is great EXCEPT the constant up charges as you add toppings. I understand it with more expensive topping options, but not for lettuce, tomato and pickles. 

So price wise and soggy cheese covered fries, allotted it only 3 stars. If the fries had been better, it would have increased their star power!
This small Thai restaurant has authentic Thai cuisine. Mango Sticky Rice is my favorite! Service is polite and efficient .

Deliciouso! Came here on a weekday night  when they weren't too busy and they were very accommodating for our large party including one in a wheelchair. Wine was fantastic, pizza was authentic Italian and portions were more than generous. Friendly waitress, and the staff clearly knew a lot about the Italian culture especially the food! No complaints from anyone and we eventually decided to visit again later in the week and we left with the same satisfaction! I would recommend if you are in the area craving Italian!

I'm almost embarrassed to say this, but I heard about Norton's while watching "Diner's, Dives, and Drive Thrus."  As soon as Guy Fieri and the owner talked about the PLT--Pastrami, Lettuce, and Tomato--I knew that we had to visit Santa Barbara just to eat here...and that's exactly what we did.

This Norton's location is located just off of the main strip in downtown Santa Barbara.  It's a small place with about 4 or 5 tables and a counter inside.  They managed to fit a bathroom in there, which is pretty impressive but very necessary after you've eaten and smell like pastrami and grease.

The owner took my order (and I admirably resisted the urge to tell him I saw him on TV): Mom's PLT, Pastrami Dog, and a small order of onion rings.  We managed to snag a small table and within about 10 minutes our order arrived.  The first bite of that PLT was heavenly.  PASTRAMI IS THE HEAVEN OF MEATS.  Seriously though: they grill the pastrami so that it's crispy on the outside, and they put it on bread with fresh tomatoes, lettuce, and mayo, and you wonder why you would ever desecrate your mouth with a BLT.  They cut the pastrami super thin; and when you order the PLT you have an option to have a small or large--small is about one layer of meat, and large is two layers.  The pastrami dog is a kosher beef hot dog with pastrami, sauerkraut, and swiss cheese on top.  Salt over load in my opinion, but my husband loved it.  The onion rings are beer battered and delicious.

If I don't return to SB for any other reason, it will be to eat here again.

Another Year has gone by and Casino Del Sol has more rooms added because of the new detached Estrella Hotel on the CDS property. This review is mostly about our stay there.  The bottom line for us:  We'd do a Complimentary stay at Estrella again, but not ever pay for a room (as beautiful as they are) at Estrella. There are some very nice additions, but as 60+ adult smokers, we would prefer not to stay there more than one night. Here's why:

We like convenience for what we consider the basics for a hotel as in a clean/comfortable room, housekeeping, food and beverage.  Our room was exceptional in most aspects (neighbors' room sounds were audible) as in the main resort, as were Registration and Housekeeping. 

CONVENIENCE for food and beverage, even ice, didn't exist. 

Restaurants away from the hotel complex are at least 10 minutes away, so the closest Food and Beverage Dining/Fast Food (except for the Pool Bar) are in the Main Resort Building. Those were at least a 5-minute walk from OUR ROOM at a regular pace. I don't believe the Pool Bar was open due to the weather (Rainy, windy 40-50's). 

The Vending Machines and Ice are on Floors 2,4 and 6.  Unfortunately, our room was on the 5th Floor at the opposite end from Vending on the other floors. However, our room, and presumably all rooms, had a Keurig for coffee. No complimentary coffee (or anything) in this hotel lobby was detected as of this writing. 

Room Service was not available at Estrella as of this writing. 

It would have been nice to have an indoor smoking space as in the CDS building because the weather was cold and rainy the 3 nights we were there, but it wasn't a deal breaker. 

The cold, windy, rainy weather was a factor during our hikes back and forth to eat, drink, smoke, gamble, etc. Hot weather would be a factor May-September for a stay at Estrella as well.  The open walkway/breezeway between the buildings were very little protection from the weather. 

On the plus side, the Video Arcade, Hotel Gym (Spa is in the Main Building) and the Pool with Water Slide looked very nice. Our room had a nice Pool View. 

Estrella has no Parking Garage (Main Building does) but there seemed to be plenty of self-parking. The best, closest parking is BEHIND the hotel. The existing Parking Garage at the Main Building was about a 10-minute walk from our room. 

Staying here made me wish for a Best Western with a Complimentary Breakfast, at least.

Jerry bobs at this location is ok dining but if in a hurry or have to catch a flight beware service can be slow. Portions are generous & prices decent. I had the Machaca which was very dry & chewy. Not impressed. Husband had biscuits & gravy. It was ok but have had better. Others in party felt similarly about their food. Overall disappointing experience.

Came here yesterday for my anniversary. Service was very prompt and food was so good! My boyfriend and I started off with the fried calamari which was pretty tasty....I had the shrimp fra diavolo which was superb...the dish had a lot of shrimp so I was happy. My boyfriend had the gnocchi with pork which he was raving about the entire day. Finally we finished off with the tiramisu. I'm not a tiramisu fan usually, but this was so creamy and delicious

Well my boyfriend got food poisoning from this place. He ordered chicken quesadillas and the kitchen staff was more concerned about closing early (as we could hear them talking the whole time we were at the bar) than cooking his chicken.  Service was not great either. Our server maybe said five words total the whole time. We won't be back.

This place was very clean and had a nice variety of foods and beverages. Light with great flavor. 4 stars because I felt the menu misinformed me. Upon looking at the images on the wall, a saw that the bun salad was a lovely choice. The picture showed that it came with a spring roll. I paid and sat myself at the table. 5 mins later, an Asian lady placed the salad at my spot. I had no spring roll. I asked why the bun salad picture on the wall had a roll. She replied in her VERY broken English, "you no order bun with chicken or shrimp. You orda beef and beef no come with roll." Dissapointed, I said "well there is no were that says that." And her response was, " It no come with beef only." As a first time customer, I would have appreciated a spring roll to rectify the confusion and misleading picture. I would have learned and anticipated not getting a roll with on my next visit. Hence 4 stars since I thought that was lame service and an extremely misleading  photo that DID NOT specify what kind of bun salad i had to get. Fortunately for them, the meal was quite light and tasty and I would totally go back for more.

Great sandwich (roast beef and brie) and wonderful chili in a mini bread bowl.  Perfect lunch.

Beer list looked FANTASTIC and inexpensive for some of the craft beers they featured.

I don't understand why they tout the "no separate checks--do your own math!" thing as if it's something to be proud of.  Is it really that difficult to provide that service to your guests?

I pre-order my cheesecake over the phone 2 days prior. The selection was never ending online. When I walked in to my surprise, they have individual slices!! I almost went in on everything they had. Tiramisu is my favorite and it taste like I was in Italy! Not to sweet, creamery and a little tart. I enjoyed every bite, sadly I had to share!
Un restaurante de hamburguesas igual a los demás pero con un sabor increíble sus hamburguesas y sus batidos tienen un sabor más casero absolutamente delicioso

This was a fun night out. Good food, good music, good times. $7 cover charge to get in and the music makes it hard to talk but that's not why you'd go here. If you like blues music, looking for some good food and nice drink menu, this is a great place to go.

Finally a decent pizza place in Saint Babs!  Great deal and taste for the price.  The place is a little narrow and they need to offer pitchers of beer on tap (not bottles) but for the price in SB, who's complaining.  I relocated from Seattle.  We have AMAZING pizza (and all other cuisine) on literally every corner from high-end joints to places similar to newcomer, Persona Neapolitan Pizzeria!  

I am so glad there is something way better than the people's #1 choice, Olio Pizzeria. And at 1/3 the price overall!  And, Ummmm, Rusty's (voted #2 in Santa Barbara)! Let's just say you need to travel to the great NW and try Apizza Scholls located on Hawthorne Blvd., Portland, OR, or Seattle's Pagliacci, Tutta Bella, Via Tibunali, Serious Pie, Flying Squirrel Pizza Co., Streetzeria, Delancey, Northlake Tavern (if you like thick slices), Toscana, Zeeks, and the list goes on and on and on.

No longer does my pizza fix have to be solely from TJ's frozen pizza section (but what a great Arugula pizza they do have)!

And if you are thinking maybe I should just move back to the Great (BRRRRR) NW?!?!?!  Believe me,  I have considered it since trying nearly every pizza place in Santa Barbara and been utterly disgusted at what they call pizza here!

I wish I had $$$ because I dream of recruiting a team of experts- from making the best pizza dough to managing business related tasks-rivaling what is known to be the best pizza/ best pizza delivery here in SB.

But for now, let's welcome Persona! Finally a pizza with a persona of its own!
The lattes and cappuccinos are both beautiful and delicious. The staff was fantastic and I love the urban feel. Must check out.
A bunch of people suggested this place for cheese steak. We were underwhelmed with our cheesesteak. The fries were fine, but we wish we tried somewhere else.
My first time there and I bought the sauce, fresh cheese ravioli and pesto, all were excellent!  And at a good price...would highly recommend.

Dios mío!!!" Ohhh Dios mío!!!", these are some the best tacos we have ever had the pleasure of consuming.  Now do not be fooled by the exterior.  My husband said, are you sure this is where you want to eat?  I said Yep, I am a cheap date.  And as usual I was right   
The menu is written on the chalkboard and is simple with enough choices to satisfy everyone.  The prices are incredible ($3 for a taco).  We go up to the counter, order and pay and they call you when it is ready.  Bring cash, no credit here.  
The food is fresh and light with flavors abound.  We had the fried avocado, pulled pork and sweet potato with Quinoa.  Each taco came with roughly the same toppings of slaw, cilantro and sauce but each filling worked great with the toppings.  The pulled pork was perfectly cooked with fantastic flavor. The sweet potato gave a what else, sweet flavor to pair along with the texture of the Quinoa.  Last but not least the fried avocado, whoever thought to fry and avocado was a genius.  If an good avocado is not creamy enough, batter it, fry it and eat away.
This is a must try for so many reasons.  And me being a connoissuer of cheap, $10 bucks for 3 tacos and a water.  Heck Yeah!!!

The woman working the counter was blatantly rude to me and the people I went with. Not sure whether they were having a bad day or not, but their negative attitude really ruined the experience for us. If you can be downright rude to customers, maybe the service industry isn't for you. As for the caramel apple pie I purchased, she didn't put caramel on it and walked right away without saying anything. When I was given my change back, she placed it on the counter out of my reach. It was a strange experience and I won't be going back. If the woman with long(it was in a bun), brown hair is working, just leave.

Get to the Chase:
After recommendation from Avi http://www.yelp.com/biz/koreana-philadelphia#hrid:s30NDCDp53fJagyXxzkzcg


Pros:
1) My go-to Korean restaurant back in my college days! It's cheap, delicious and quick on delivery
2) Has a nice area to sit in both outside and inside and no tip required because you order up front
3) Bubble Tea is not half bad either, moreover they sell asian snacks (Pocky, shrimp crackers, Aloe drinks, custard buns...etc.) 
4) Proximity to class, affordability, quick service, good variety of food selection, decent quality, clean area = 4 stars!!

Cons:
1) sometimes the food can just be too greasy, like the bulgogi one time was a little more greasy than usual and i had more fatty pieces than meat (you know those squiggly chewy gunks that trick you into thinking their meat?)

Pita Pit is known for being a healthy fast food style chain.  However, every time I go in there, I end up adding cheese, mayo, and bacon to my pita!  Kind of defeats the purpose, but at least it is good.  I have been to a couple Pita Pit's in my day, and this one is definitely not as good as some of the others, service wise.

The pitas are really good.  If you go for the club it has ham, turkey, and bacon.  Of course you are able to add whatever other fillings you want like chopped tomato, lettuce, etc.  You really can't go wrong with anything at Pita Pit, and I must say it makes for a really hearty lunch.  I would probably say it is one of the better places to eat lunch in the downtown area.

I have been going to Pastaria for five or so years and I stand by that the food is excellent! The pasta is some of the best, and coming from someone who frequents the restaurants on The Hill this speaks for itself. I have to address the service as of recent though. I understand with the COVID-19 pandemic that servers are hard to come by but tonight our server, who I have had multiple times over the years, seemed disinterested in his tables. This was obvious especially after the majority of his tables finished their meals and left. Our table would have ordered dessert but after 15 minutes of waiting for our server we gave up and decided to get the check. I have to say that if a restaurant is charging upwards of $20 for a pasta dish, I personally expect the service to be above average. I want to recommend Pastaria to friends and family but at this point I would likely suggest something else. Hopefully the service quality increases but I'm not sure I'll be back for awhile.

For the price, this place could be a lot better.  My husband ordered the NY strip and it was super fatty.  He hardly had any actual meat to eat and left hungry.  Not cool for a $34 a la carte steak meal.  The best thing I had was the salad.  Skip this place and save your money.

My wife and I love Stonewell, it has become our go-to place. We usually get the dolsot bibimbap with beef, and it's really great. We have tried the other Korean dishes on their menu as well and they are also very  good. We particularly like the sincere and family friendly service.

Went here and was worth the wait. 

We started with pre-dinner appetizers and drinks at the bar downstairs. We ordered a sampler of steamed mussels, clams, shrimps, and oyster Rockefeller. It was absolutely so fresh and delicious! 

For drinks, we ordered house red, bloody mary, and margarita...and our bartender really loaded my margarita with tequila and asked if I had any preference of tequila to use. 

After about an hour of wait, we got called upstairs and had our dinner outside with views of the harbor. Luckily, it didn't smell too bad - like Fisherman's wharf in SF does with all the sea lions so close...so you have the wonderful sea breeze and it is so picture perfect postcard-y. 

We started with some oysters on a half-shell which were traditionally served with cocktail sauce and lemon. Was delicious, but as long as you get fresh sweet oysters - you can't go wrong with the taste of fresh from the sea. 

We got a cup of clam chowder which was served in a Brophy's coffee mug served with oyster cracker. Now, I consider myself somewhat of an amateur chowder connoisseur from my days working at Pier 39, my trip to Boston (trying chowder from different restaurants every day I was there), and my trips to the Chowder festival...and their chowder here was definitely ranked up there with good chowder.

The consistency was not too thick or watery.  The pototoes didn't overwhelm the chowder.  It wasn't starchy or floury...had the right amount of clam stock and was not salty at all.  It had big chunks of fresh and tender clams (not chewy at all).  The sprinkling of parsley gave it a freshness.

By the time my meal came (seafood pasta) - I had to take it to go.  We were stuffed!  The pasta was creamy and light with scallops and shrimp.  The drizzle of fresh lemon cut through the heaviness of the cream with that touch of acidity.

This is a place to go for a nice seafood experience.

Would like to go back when it is spiny lobster season  and try their lobster.

It definitely did not live up to the hype.

Wins:
- Location
- Decor & Build out
- Cocktails - solid, but not memorable
- Housemade Spaghetti with Guanciale and Fried-Poached Farm Egg was delicious!

Opportunities:
- The menu online is outdated by 5 months (confirmed by our server when we inquired about the lamb neck)
- Muscovy Duck Leg Confit was so overcooked (it was like jerky) that we sent it back to the kitchen
- Rabbit Fricassee with Garganelli, Bacon, Pumpkin and Madeira was uninspired

Overall, with so many delicious restaurants in NOLA, I wouldn't recommend going here, which is disappointing given the wonderful dining experiences at Butcher and Cochon. We were hungry when we left and went to Mimi's in the Marigny and had mushroom and Manchago toasts which were a standout at $7.

I wanted to visit my childhood home near Broadway Village when I returned to Tucson for my 50th high school reunion and searched Yelp for nearby Mexican restaurants where we could lunch while in the neighborhood.   The tamales at Tucson Tamale Company lived up to all of the five star reviews.

Well we had a great experience. The waitress was friendly, made great suggestions, and was very attentive. The food quality was what we expected. Great flavor, good pricing, good bang for the buck. We will definitely return and plan on bringing our neighbors. Until next time... happy eating!!

I was visiting my friend from out of town and we decided to go to Supper for Sunday night dinner.

At 6:30pm, the restaurant was surprisingly empty.  Just my friend and me and two other groups of diners.  The restaurant is really beautiful inside and there is an open kitchen you can stare into.  

Our server was polite enough, although I did not like the fact that she waited on the other two tables more and was very inattentive to our table.  In fact, after getting us our water, it took her 20 minutes to return and take our order because she was socializing with the other tables and telling them the specials when we had actually entered and been seated in the restaurant well before them.

At Supper, they recommend that you get 2-3 plates of food per person because the portions are tiny - they are not lying.  My friend and I each got an appetizer, an larger portion, and split a dessert.  Afterwards, we were barely full.

I recognize that Supper should be considered a "special occasion" restaurant, but the prices at this restaurant do not match what you are getting.  The plates are way overpriced.  If the food was amazing, then I could easily overlook the hefty price tags for such little portions, but I thought the cheese gourges were too salty, the deviled eggs were interesting but not amazing, and the red wine braised beef brisket was strange in texture, though the grits accompanying were awesome.

If I had to pick a dish that might be worth it's price tag, I would say the striped bass.

I, personally, would not go back to this restaurant.  But with such high reviews from everyone else, maybe it was just an off-night, or maybe I just didn't order the right things here...
literally waited for my food for over an hour after it said it was ready to find out they closed early and i never got my food or money back lol

A few Fridays ago I found myself with time to kill before an event and since the Springfield Mall was directly in between my work and the event location I decided I would see if I could get any of my holiday shopping done. ( I didn't but that is for another review) Frustrated with the store choices I decided to grab a quick bite since I was unsure what the food choices would be like where I was going. Not wanting pasta, I found myself in Ruby Tuesday's, somewhere I thought I would never be. Places like this tend to not work for me as a vegetarian and I really dislike kids running around where I am eating.

I found a seat at the bar, grabbed a cheap drink and started to look at the menu. I was very surprised to see things like spaghetti squash and other "healthy" vegetables available. I decided on the Mini Zucchini Burgers, which came with fries and endless salad bar for $8.99, a steal in my opinion. 

They were great! Clearly fresh made, with roasted red pepper and feta also in the patty, served on cute little buns with lettuce, tomato and pickle slices. The patties were seasoned well, flavors were great, and they didn't fall apart (a reoccurring problem in the land of veggie burgers). I was shocked to find myself thinking I would want to come back and have this meal again.

The fries were the worst part, but I was expecting this. Clearly frozen at some point in their lives with zero seasoning. But the salad bar proved to also be enticing, with a large variety of toppings and even 3 or 4 lettuce choices. It was a lot of food, so I would maybe suggest they offer an option where you don't get either the salad or the fries for a buck less. 

As far as service, it was fine. I was left alone with my book which is what I wanted. It was very clear though that the various bartenders were having a lot of tension with each other and also that someone was training that night which was causing them issues(probably not the best day for this since it was packed at bar and in dining area).

 I also noticed that they make their sangria to order, so that the flavors and fruits don't get to meld which to me defeats the point of sangria.  So if you like real sangria I would avoid it. 

Overall I will definitely think of this as an option if I find myself in the same situation with work events or I am traveling somewhere and just need a quick bite.

I love St Louis Bread Co. and the customer service they normally give. This location is the exception to the norm. I consistently have problems with my "rapid pick up orders" not being completed properly and sometimes not at all.  The staff mostly offers poor customer service when I ask for the coffee to be refilled, which is a very common our rance at this location. I have now decided that I will drive a little further out to the Forest Park Parkway location where the service is exceptional.

This is my favorite place!  The staff is always super friendly and the food is excellent! Their catfish is fried to perfection and their ribs are falling off the bone delicious.  The biscuits are so good & soft with the cinnamon butter that I'm getting hungry just reviewing this place.  The waitresses are always friendly/attentive and it's genuine as if they were born to waitress or something.  About the only thing I can think of to improve this place is when they dance and clap, they need to loosen up a bit and really get down into those dance moves with some spunk! lol

Loving the new management!!! We rarely went to sushi 7 even though it was just blocks away from our house. The sushi wasn't terrible, but not our favorite. The new management has definitely changed this!!! We have gone 3 times in the last month. It is by far the best sushi in Reno now. LOVE IT!!!!

Pros: portions were HUGE and the price was great. 

Cons: cleanliness wasn't great. There wasn't a menu, just a bunch of options with prices hand written pasted on the walls. The person taking our order over charged us for the salad. She didn't know how to give us a refund so she gave us the cash out of the tip jar.

Went here today after church with a couple of new friends. I got the Eggs Benedict, finally after 45 minutes our food arrived. Yes, it was busy, but we were chatting, so that was fine. My poached eggs were harder than boiled eggs, no where near poached. I turned one of them over & it was brown, not sure how this happened with poached eggs. I don't like to send food back, but everyone at the table said that was inexcusable. I was just not going to eat it. I also didn't get the fresh fruit the 1st or 2nd time after asking. Eggs were slightly better the 2nd tlme, but my hone fried potatoes were from my 1st plate. Waitress never asked how the 2nd plate was. Very disappointing when you pay $11.99 for a plate of food!

We have had great experiences at Bonefish Grill previously, however we had a horrible experience this time. I sent this to them first, but I received no response, so here it is for all to see. 

I visited Bonefish Grill for brunch Sunday morning. We (a party of 4) had reservations for 10am and arrived on time. The restaurant was virtually empty other than the staff. We were seated promptly. 
The server brought water, took our drink order and offered bread which we said yes we would like some. We also asked for lemons for the water at this time. We ordered 3 mixed drinks and one coffee. They brought some drinks in a reasonable amount of time. One drink was wrong (we ordered a Tom Collins and received a mimosa), one drink was made improperly (Amaretto Sour which they forgot to add the amaretto), and we had to ask for the coffee. The server seemed to have a hard time keeping straight what was ordered from what table (she had 2). On more than one occasion during the "experience" she brought items to the wrong tables and then seemed "put off" when we told her we did not order the item. We still had not received the lemons or the bread. We were being told the bread was being baked, no mention of the lemons, except by us. The server seemed pretty much disinterested. We passed on appetizers, probably one of our better choices of the morning.
The server took our meal order without incident other than my wife and I ordered the Surf and Turf Eggs Benedict. My wife asked if she could request how her steak was cooked and the server told her no, it was all cooked well because of the kind of steak it was. I found this answer somewhat strange, but let it go at the time. We asked about the bread...still baking. Lemons? "Oh Yeah", was the response, but still no lemons.
When our meals arrived, one was wrong (we ordered the California Omelet and received a Cajun Omelet. The manager came to our table, assumingly because we were still one of only two tables in the place and there was a discussion in progress with the server who disappeared when the manager arrived. He offered to change out the omelet for the correct order and the server finally returned with the bread, dumping oil all over the floor and the table as she carried the plate through the room and nearly pouring it on me. 
The person that had ordered the omelet told the rest of us to go ahead and eat for fear of our food getting cold, but it was too late. They had arrived cold. Both mine and my wife's meals were less than room temperature. When the manager arrived with the correct omelet, we sent back our meals to be remade. The lemons finally showed up with no apology, but a hint of indignation. When the manager arrived (the server was pretty much out of the picture by this time) with the second breakfast for both of us, the plate was significantly warmer, the food was not. As I examined my meal, it was obvious why the steak had to be well done. The meal had obviously been cooked long before and assembled in the kitchen when we ordered it (now the well done steak makes sense). The eggs may have been prepared at the time, but based on the temperature, I seriously doubt it. I could have bought the identical meal out of the freezer section at Meijer (which is located a couple blocks away) and wondered if it had been. 
We ate most of the meal because I was very hungry and a diabetic and had taken my medications so I had to eat something. Sending the meal back for a second time didn't seem to make sense since it arrived with the very same problem it had to begin with. Performing the same actions and expecting different results just didn't seem to make sense.
The cap on the "experience" was we were presented our bill by the bar tender (3rd person) because we were told our server had slipped and fallen in the kitchen while unloading the dishwasher. We had asked that our bill be split between the two couples. They incorrectly placed the Cajun Omelet on our bill and removed it, but they apparently compensated my coffee (nice guys) because it wasn't on the bill. 
This was a $40.00 mistake on my part and that does not cover the frustration we experienced. This was by far the worst meal I have ever experienced. I know food service is a hard business and does not provide the compensation that is deserved. I generally do not blame the wait staff for the kitchens mistakes or the reverse. However in this case, there was enough fault to go around for everyone. The server was disinterested and treated us like she was doing us a favor. The kitchen put out food that was not even close to the quality of food I have previously had at Bonefish Grill ever, and the manager while highly apologetic failed to recognize and correct the deficiencies, which told me he genuinely didn't care, or our meals would have been correct the second time. 
It will be a long time before I return to a Bonefish grill, I am deeply disappointed that I had to pay to be treated so poorly.

Unice Robinson , had a wonderful dining experience at Besito. I have traveled all over the world and this was the best Mexican food I have ever eaten! Our Server Derrick was very helpful in explaining the menu to us. The presentation of the food was like looking in a food magazine,  it looked to good to eat! I was so eager to eat I didn't take a picture of the food!  As we were getting ready to leave, it started raining very heavily and the restaurant gave us umbrellas so we wouldn't get soaked!  From our Server Derrick to Management they made our dining at Besito, a wonderful experience! If you want the best Mexican food on the planet,  make a trip to Besito's! They will be opening up a Besito's in Charlotte, NC in April and I will be there!

Stopped in today for the Thai chicken lettuce wraps & a beer.  The chicken wraps are really good, I live an hour away so that's my go to when I'm in the area.   Our beers were good & cold.  The bartender was great.  The chicken wraps were delicious. My only complaint was that the 4 pieces of lettuce were a little brown. I wasn't in the mood to complain so I just ate it.  If the lettuce wasn't brown I would have given 5 stars.  Next time I'm there I'll still order it again. 
    Had lunch here the other day and ate outside on the deck.  We shared my favorite peanut chicken lettuce wraps & they were delicious as always.  All 3 of us ordered a chicken panini, had pesto, fresh mozzarella, tomato, bacon.  It's was very good.

I had a cheeseburger, which I haven't had since my husband converted to a vegetarian.  It was heavenly. They even had a veggie wrap for him, which he said was delightful.  We are returning for a breakfast
This place was my fave! Huge great tasting where "the other place" was smaller and a little over done.

Other than the individual answering the phones being a bit rude and abrupt, the food was okay. I ordered the Chicken Dumpukht, it was cooked well. A tad bit heavy on the grease and the pastry cover lacked the flakiness I would have expected. They definitely need to update the pictures for these dishes or relate it to something like an Indian version of chicken pot pie for those who are not familiar with this unique form of cooking. The flavors were good. The garlic naan I ordered as a side was under-seasoned. I think the place has potential and probably a good chef, but seems it requires some update in finishing of a plate and garnishing that is key to bold flavors in Indian food.

I had a spectacular experience here with my friends on Friday evening.  Wonderful sangria and incredible tapas.  Try the tequila-flamed manchego cheese, patatas bravas, and goat cheese balls!!  Laid-back, casual atmosphere was also a plus.

Love the atmosphere and the pizza. The service was quick and the staff was friendly. Someone even took the time to show my kids how to play shuffleboard.

We're kind of a plain cheese bunch but it was perfect. The crust was thin and fresh and the sauce was delicious. Really as perfect as a pizza can be. I'm sure I'll try some of the other creations at some point in the future. I hear they have a good happy hour.

Digging this neighborhood pizza joint & bar.

I LOVE their food, but we order to go each time, they tell us 20 minutes but then we get there and have to wait sometimes 20+ more minutes for it to be ready. I just wish they gave us realistic times.
Falafel gyro was the biggest and tastiest I've had. The guy at the front is very polite and super efficient.

Decent first visit to McMenamin's.  We walked in and there was no one there to greet us.  We kind of stood there for a second, but no one from the bar seemed to notice us so we decided to just take a seat at one of the high top tables by the door.  After a little while I decided to go seek out a staff member to make sure we were where we belonged.  Turns out the guy I went up to was just on his way over.  Then we ordered two glasses of water, but for some reason still had to be carded.  Kind of strange.  Okay so a rocky start.

They had an interesting menu that seemed to feature the burgers I've heard so much about and the chicken sandwiches.  They also had a menu for the day's specials.  I found myself going back and forth between customizing a burger or chicken sandwich or going with the schnitzel from the specials menu.  I went with the schnitzel and was recommended to get the mashed potatoes with that.  Also got a bowl of spicy soup with andouille sausage.  That was very tasty with the right amount of spice.  The schnitzel was awesome.  I'd never had it before and had been dying to go to a German spot to try some.  It was nice and thin and was topped with capers, which I'm not sure if that is traditional or not, but it tasted great.  The mashed potatoes were also as good as the server said.  

Overall I was kind of annoyed for the first five minutes with the way things were going, but in the end I really enjoyed the food and would love to try more.  It's definitely a cool hangout for locals, but we were not regulars so it felt like that lessened our experience.  I would like to go back, maybe get a drink and try one of those sandwiches I was debating over.
I'm from Philly, took my picky boyfriend here for a cheesesteak and we really enjoyed it. Staff was very friendly too. Would def go back

Good pizza, just a solidly consistent place to eat. I eat there once a week and I am never disappointed. The staff is very attentive and friendly, they work very hard to know and cater to their customers.

I am not a breakfast person at all but this was my favorite place to eat while I vacationed in Clearwater.  The staff was very nice and made sure we liked everything we ordered. I had the breakfast pretzel roll and it was the best breakfast sandwich I've ever had. It's a little out of the way from the tourist are in Clearwater but well worth the drive. They gave us free cookies too when we paid our check and those were also delicious!

Shocked that Chili's doesn't have a higher overall rating. This restaurant is spectacular, and a welcomed surprise to my palate. Phenomenal food with exceptional service. You really can't go wrong here. 

The setting is quite charming - they really hit the nail on the head with the whole southwest-mexican feel. 

The menu is dynamic and diverse - we had a hard time narrowing down our favorites (spoiler alert: we couldn't narrow down dessert and ordered two! ha! ), but ultimately, we enjoyed the following:

Appetizers: 
We got the skillet queso. The beef in the queso was cooked to perfection and the tostada chips reminded me of summers in Mexico in my Abuela's kitchen. You can order a bottomless portion of the chips for $3. 

Entree:
I ordered the chicken fajitas and was thrilled when our server brought out a sizzling skillet with freshly sliced peppers, carmelized onions, warm tortillas and typical fajita topping fare ( sour cream, cheese, salsa etc). The fajitas are of the "make-your-own" craze that has taken the world by storm. I felt quite trendy as I constructed the perfect meat and veggie filled fajita. 
It paired well with the Arnold Palmer, and I definitely recommend this beverage. 

My dining partner ordered the Old Timer burger - pretty standard, but grilled to perfection. 

For dessert we ordered the Molten Chocolate cake ( I swear it's the best lava cake on earth), and the Skillet Chocolate Chip Cookie - can you tell I'm a chocoholic?!?!? They both were wonderful but the molten cake was so moist and indulgent, and the whole dish is the perfect ratio of cake to ice cream to melted chocolate. 

I can't wait to go back again - looking forward to celebrating my next birthday here!
Chips and queso and margaritas! Yum!! Such a gorgeous restaurant. The food is amazing. It has become a common spot for my coworker and I. The service has been good.

My husband insisted on going here. I'm not sure that sushi is a good idea far from the ocean and it's not. I know everyone raves about this place, but....
Maybe people like it because it's different ?
We had the brussels sprouts which were more than charred and more like burnt. It was soy sauce sprouts burnt to a crisp. The sashimi was marginal at best. I did like the roll- 
We sat next to a table that was cooking meat on a hot stone. That looked fun but get some ventilation if you're going to do that. 
Not impresse

Had a company event event which was a large group and the service was absolutely awful.  Spending over $3500 for our food and drink and JIMMY was absolutely unprofessional and rude the entire dinner.  He could care less about the customers, and he would yell at the two bus boys who were working their tail off.  This place doesn't even deserve a 1 star, the food should be compared to a fazoli's for Italian and the steak would compare to a ponderosa or old country Buffet.  DO NOT EAT AT THIS ESTABLISHMENT, service and food are way below standards and no one in the whole restaurant cares!

Great food, great atmosphere, great location! Unique selection which never disappoint. Sunday brunch included an entirely different menu which was unexpected and fantastic! Recommend for date night, girls night or family outings!
This McDonald's is the slowest in Boise. Don't think skipping the drive through would be faster because inside is just as slow. They also aren't very friendly. This McDonald's has gone down hill.

I frequently travel to New Orleans for business & am always looking for local flavor when dining out.  I ordered the gumbo & even though it was chicken & sausage rather than seafood, it was possibly the best gumbo I've ever had!  I also had the Gallier fried oyster sandwich with pickled turnip.  It was phenomenal!  Kelly was a doll & made me feel right at home!

Came by here on my way home from traveling up north for the day. Went inside and it's very clean, but very slow traffic wise.  Not alot of customers.  They have an open cold case where you can grab and go or order behind the counter. If it's your first time definitely go to the counter
You can try a small sample of anything you would like before buying it.  I highly recommend doing that. 
It was very hard deciding on what buy and navigate through the menu. If you want several different chicken salads because alot of them are really good,  don't go with the individual package chicken because that will run you over $30 plus dollars and those containers are not that big. I was looking at doing 3 different chicken salads. 
So I navigated through the menu and I finally spoke up to try and keep this order to go less than ordering a meal at a fine dining restaurant.  
My favorite was the original chicken salad with added onion,  chicken salad with egg, and the lemon chicken salad. There was more I had not tried and will be back to try those. To the left of the menu is your chicken salads and to the right is chicken salads with fruit.  Never got that far with the samples.  
I did try the potato soup and it was so good not salty at all.  It had bacon, and  cheese. 
I also got the Italian side pasta salad very good not bitter. Definitely everything was fresh. 
The way to go is to get the 3 scoop meal and added the soup for an extra charge. 
Definitely go with the 3 scoop meal comes with a pickle, cookie, and small upcharge you can add the soup. I got it to go so I had bread at home.  
I will definitely be back to try the chicken with fruit.  It had apples and a nut in it.

Bonefish is good..what can I say.  Its safe and it is consistent and you can never go wrong finishing your dinner with an esspresso martini!  That said as one could imagine there is better seafood to be had in the bay area.  The mussels are great and you can make a meal out of them with the bread they serve becuase the broth at the bottom of the bowl is fantastic!

Stopped in with 14 students (4th&5th graders) during lunchtime and we were welcomed with a big smile & amazing service! They were quick & food was great. Thank you Deb's Coney Cafe for making our end of year student council trip that much more special!

Super delicious sandwiches although I'm not gonna lie, a bit steep in price. It's a once in a while treat for me only because I can't afford a $15 sandwich lunch daily. Sometimes drive by, salivate and rush home to make myself a copy cat version that's never as good! Highly recommend otherwise. Ps- skip the garlic bread option it's too oily/greasy makes sammy soggy!

It was alright. Layout was kinda cool, they have some sweet older video games.  The place needs a facelift for sure.  I don't know what the compititions like on the eastside but the pizza was probably 3.5 outta 5.  Got a sad order of breadsticks before the pizza since we were dying and suspected it might be awhile before we see our pizza.  I was correct, took a long time and not the greatest place to have to wait. 

Next time I'll hold off till i get to my side of town.
Best Indian Restaurant in Williamson & Davidson county!!!! The food is ALWAYS amazing and the Owner and staff makes you feel like family!! Always a wonderful evening!!!!!

The French Quarter Cafe is sort of out of the way, on your way to East Nashville.  Parking is tough unless you get there early, but there are a few spaces in the lot behind the building and in the bank parking lot down the street (park at your own risk).  The best thing about this place is the great sound, and the Nashville Jazz Orchestra, which performs there every Tuesday night. The food isn't bad, (although I'm not sure what part of New Orleans they get their recipes from) and there is a limited bar.  Seating is limited too, a few booths, a few tables and a few bar seats. You may also want to be prepared for the show to start late, because the sound check always seem to be happening at the time the show is supposed to start, but for $7 you can see a swingin' big band in Nashville on a Tuesday night.
Attentive staff, fantastic spin on classic Southern dishes with a modern twist, and fun atmosphere. Great for big groups!

The food didn't taste the way that it was hyped up to. The price was great but the taste and seasoning wasn't what I expected. I hope to try it again and it taste a little bit better because I heard a lot of great things, that just wasn't my experience.

Great artistic atmosphere with hand crafted cabinets and nice tables. Beautiful baked goods to buy at the counter. 
Fun vegan options. They should massage the kale or parboil before they put the curly kale in a salad. It was curly and unruly with large spines to put aside. The salad would have been great if they would have spent the extra time thinking about how to prep the kale to put the nicely flavored quinoa salad. I would definitely go back.

This is a great little breakfast spot my friend and I recently discovered.  They actually use REAL eggs, not the fake/liquid ones. I did not specify and they just came out that way - I was pleasantly surprised. I hope The Scrambled Egg sticks around a good long time so we can remain  regulars.

Fantastic restaurant with view wrapped all around the rooftop.  We ordered quite a bit off the menu and everything was surprisingly good.  Cocktails were yum too.  Negative: hotel elevator system sucks.

Food tasted as it was re-fried.  We had the chicken and lamb dibi with plantains.  Chicken was okay, lamb wasn't good.  The chicken wrap was okay. 

It might be the way they cook in their country, but wished I would had like it more.  Might be better to for takeout.

Let's set aside the usual squealing ebullience of Yelp reviews and cut to the essence:

Obon's ramen is respectable stuff--and you will pay for that respectability. Depending on your appetite, it may also leave you hungry. If you don't like pork, you won't like most of their ramen, though it's nice to see that chicken now appears on their menu for those sensitive or pious diners who shun the pig. Away from soups, their bibimbop is excellent, but their pork belly bun is unexciting despite being vainly self-aware.

Service has always been friendly, but I've had appetizers fail to arrive until after the meal and different diners' entrees arrive separated by nearly ten minutes... so if you're with someone who eats fast, they could finish before you start.

Even if you focus on the quality of Obon's ramen and sideline the fact that the restaurant is suffocated by bro-rich (or rich bro?) student housing, the overall experience is neither better nor worse than okay. I'd be happy to go again but I wouldn't go out of my way to do so.

Another "Independently owned and operated" Subway that doesn't honor Subway coupons.  Must be the same owner as the one on Vista Blvd.  Sorry Subway, got to go to Port-a-Subs for now on.  #BoycottSubway. Avoid Sparks Subways!!!!

Pro tip- if you want a chance at eating warm food, show up and order. Door dash here is 50/50 that you even get food within 90mins. And that's from ordering through the chipotle app. I do not understand why this location gets so backed up....most of our drivers leave because they are wasting their time. We don't even get our food sometimes. For chipotle, just seems strange. Guess it's just the location.
Excellent food. great service.  The filet was just right!!  I loved the small room setting.  Overall great.

By far the most beautiful decorations out of any Mexican restaurant in the area.  Their tacos al carbon are super.  Ask them to bring you some salsa picosa with it.  Everybody is super friendly there as well.

Food: The quality was mostly exceptional. We ordered the duck breast, crab cakes, beet salad, a cocktail apiece, and had the crème brûlée for dessert. The cocktails, variations on standard repertoire classics, were amazing. Reno has some stellar mixologists. A standout from dinner was the surprising use of fried polenta that accompanied the duck. The slaw served with the rather tiny crab cakes was pedestrian, albeit well seasoned. The crème brûlée tasted like crème brûlée, but the texture should have been smoother and more consistent throughout. 

Service: Our waitress was present just enough so as not to be intrusive, our water was never half empty, and the plates were cleared famously. Someone is ready for fine dining.

Ambiance: If you're charging these prices you should consider the environment in which your guests are dining. This is café ambiance for bistro prices; I'm no fan of hearing every conversation at the bar when I'm on a date.

Overall, 4 stars. I would come back for some of the food and to try other items (and to recruit my server), but the ambiance should be the first thing updated here; it took a lot away from what would otherwise have been a 5 Star experience.

the thing is, Wasabi House is just quaint. plain and simple. the staff are always reeeeeeeally nice. the sushi quality is constant. and the dining room is cute, clean, cozy, and inviting. there are some bonuses, too. for one, they have udon soup - something i find hard to come by at sushi joints in the city. and also, they started having specials - like bibimbop. that's definitely "special" for a sushi joint. and i plan to give it a try one of these days. 

oh, and thank you, Wasabi House, for being there for me at 8:30pm when i don't want to eat pizza.

Mama Palma is wonderful. I stopped in tonight to order a pizza to go, and the staff was incredibly courteous. They offered me a seat and something to drink while I waited. I ditzily forgot to pay at first, but as I went out the door, they politely brought me back, accepted my apologies, and even threw in a free bottle of water. And as usual, the pizza was delicious!

My clutch place for chinese food these days---I'm going to be describing the lunch special which I think is a SPECTACULAR deal for the money you pay (around 4.95)

The lunch special includes a warm soup (hot and sour/egg drop),  an crunchy egg roll  w/ traditional sweet/sour sauce and main dish---once again ALL for under 5 bucks.  It hits the spot let me tell you.  The service around lunch time has been good for me (granted I go a little later than peak lunch hours--like 2ish); they are always quick about getting hot sauce etc


Apparently it was rated best in tucson for chinese food for the last two years for Chinese so you don't have to take my word for it.  (RR shoutout)

My review is only based upon their fried chicken, green beans with ham and their mac-n-cheese.This place has the best fried chicken around!!!  It's different because they use corn meal.  It has the best tasting crust and the chicken has always been juicy inside, never dried out.  I like Mr. Ed's too, but this has my number 1 vote.  I love their green beans with apple smoked bacon.  They are very tasty and I often have 2 sides of them instead of one of their other sides.  The pimento mac-n-cheese is to die for!  You can't come here and not have it.  I haven't tried any of their other menu items, but my friends have and they have been extremely happy with their meals.  Yikes, I almost forgot to mention the servers.  They are fantastic.
