All of them have been quick to take our orders.  They are very friendly and do their best to make sure you have a wonderful dining experience.

My only other comment is that I wish they had fried chicken every day!!!!  Please High Hat, please...

I'm gonna be very real here for a second. I love Merritt's. I've been a Patron since the tender age of 9. Great value, great portion size, great coffee, great scones. But I gotta say. Ever since the management changed and they got new honey, the honeys been weird. Which in turn makes the honey butter weird. Butter's weird.

Our company reserved the entire place  on a Sunday night. About 400 of us filled the two floors. Live band was playing and buffet style food at both floors. Bars are plenty abound, friendly staffs!! Few of Their staffs were on the dance floor encouraging everybody to dance and even  dance lesson on line dancing.

Delicious food and a very friendly staff.  We read about the long waits, but we went around 1pm on a Tuesday.  No wait and we were one of on a few tables in the cafe.  They had the BEST coffee and the breakfast food was amazing!  We told the servers we were from out of town and they gave us really great ideas on what to do/see/eat while we were there.  Will definitely visit again.

Came here for a late dinner after I arrived in Philadelphia. We picked a few small plates, bruschetta, and cheese! Figs with Gorgonzola and prosciutto, warm white bean dip, broccoli rabe bruschetta were all great! The truffle egg toast was ok, hard to taste the truffle. We picked a Brie cheese and creamy blue cheese that were both delicious on their own but the fun part was that they paired a truffle pate with the Brie and honey with the blue cheese. The waitress was very knowledgable about the menu and wine list. Would come back for one of their paninis!

The pizza looked really good, but unfortunately, I never got to try it. My hand was burned really badly from a hot pizza pan that was left on the counter where customers rest their hands. I leaned on the hot pan, and burned my hand so badly that I have a blister three days later that is pussing and bleeding.

When I tried to inform the worker, who didn't seem to speak English, I asked to speak to a manager, and the "bouncers" started telling me to get out, after I burned my hand so bad! My friends and I left but the employee chased my friends and I six blocks down 3rd street, and to be honest, it was really scared. I even cried.

I really hope the owner reads this, so he knows what type of people he has working for him. I'd be livid if an employee represented my company like that. I hope he gets fired.

Hubby and I do not consider Havanna's to be a dining destination, but rather more of a kick-back-and-relax-listen-to-the-music kinda place.  Sure, they have a modest size menu, but the choices and offerings are nothing that you wouldn't find anywhere, and while the name of the restaurant would suggest perhaps a Cuban flare to their cooking, this isn't the case.  Food is just so-so, not terrible but not inspiring.

We do, however, love to come on the first Sunday of every month, where the orchestra Midnight Sun performs.  They're terrific, doing the old standards and they're usually accompanied by a caberet-style singer who is normally quite good.  We love to sit back and savor the wonderful free entertainment and sip a cocktail or two 

Naturally, parking in New Hope is next to impossible, so leave yourself plenty of time and wear comfy shoes, because it's likely you're gonna have somewhat of a walk from the time you park until you reach Havannas.

What a fabulous option to fast food chains!  The wraps are healthy and taste great, priced fairly and many, many options; can even build your own.  I have been here many times and have my family hooked.  The main standby on every order for us is #30 Basil Cashew Chicken, but I like mix it up and get Thai Tuna or something with roast beef.  The hot wraps are good also, but a bit messier to eat.  The owner is a great guy and will do anything to please his customers.  Very strong recommendation for Roly Poly !

After a pleasant experience here last year, we stopped in last Saturday with two out of town guests hoping to grab a drink before dinner reservations down the block. Waited at the (empty) hostess stand for five full minutes. Four different members of the staff (three servers and the bartender) looked directly at us, made eye contact, and proceeded to ignore us. We weren't even greeted. No one seemed to be taking care of the two parties in the front room either--both were sitting there with menus but no drinks, and the waitstaff didn't interact with them while we were there. Eventually we gave up and walked out. I realize restaurants get busy on the weekends and presumably the servers were in the weeds, but we felt like we were invisible, and there's no excuse for that. Definitely won't be setting foot in there again.

I really love la cabra! The building looks really nice and the food is great for the price. I recommend the burgers, crispy pork belly, truffle fries. The beer flights are cheap, around $2 for a 4 oz glass. I did buy their growler for $20 but was disappointed to find that it didn't keep my beer fresh. It was less carbonated by the next day. The growler looked nice but just didn't do the job. Overall, I'll probably be back and bring some of my friends. Will definitely try the happy hour specials.

Worst Taco Bell around. Not once in 6 years have they ever got my order correct. Im back sitting in the drive through right now because my $40 order was botched when I got home. 
This place is a complete joke!!!!!

Really good food.  This restaurant has excellent hard working owners, one in the kitchen and one working the front of the house as maitre d / bartender.  
The menu is short but imaginative.  Each of the dishes we tried was really good.   Tuna, chicken breast, duck, and filet were all really good.
Staff was nice and their veggie burger is surprisingly good, but they don't have all the salad dressings represented on the menu. Bathrooms were clean.
Only been there for lunch, but these are some good freaking sandwiches. Great relaxed atmosphere too. Clearly Anne or whoever runs this place cares about the experience.

Nada in general is good, but a bit heavy-handed with the salt.

Pork belly & hot chicken tacos are excellent and highly recommended, though! The Al Pastor taco is just decent. It's not bad by any means. Just not all that great. Shredded pork has a tough time fighting against a lower ceiling as a meat, I feel. 

Crispy potatoes. Just fantastic, very very impressed. Sweet, complex, crispy, savory, so good!

Their mac & cheese was shockingly salty. Couldn't taste cheese, just salt. Server just got complete silence from the entire table after asking if everything was ok, which was a tad awkward. After remaking it, it was still pretty salty, but a little more bearable...

Guacamole is decent and I appreciate the other veggies to dip in it. Helped abate the guilt from eating so much meat and cheese-based dishes.

Mexi-Korean fried chicken is... a bold experiment that is not entirely successful. It was really salty (sense the theme?) and mostly consisted of an absurdly thick layer of light, crispy, layered & flaky batter. Like 1 cm thick on all sides. Madness. I'm all for experimentation and Mexican-Korean fusion, but for every successful idea is one that falls to the wayside...
Amazing service. The staff is friendly and helpful. The food is top notch. The food came out hot and the perfect amount

Disappointed. Great ambiance however we sat outside on new beautiful patio and the service was very slow. Took forever to get drinks and even longer to get food and pay bill. We were there more than 2 hours. Prices seemed steeper. Was looking forward to this new fiesta patio. Bar looked great but will re-think having dinner here again.

I had not been there in a long time. Today I can in to eat a good hard salami on rye sandwich. The guy at the counter seemed to not pay much attention to what people where ordering kept asking them to repeat their order. My turn came and the same thing happened. Should have left then but figured I was already here. Found a table that was dirty, asked another guy behind the counter if he could give me something to clean the table, after what seemed like a minute or two someone came out from the kitchen to clean the table. When my sandwich came I saw the salami but the bread looked like two small ends. Bread sucked, salami was great potato salad so-so. Won't return and don't recommend.

America's best fried chicken? I can't say, but it's definitely the best fried chicken I've ever had. The place is in the middle of a (supposedly dangerous) neighborhood away from downtown. If you don't have a car, you can always get there by cab, and the waiters there can help you call a cab once you're done eating.

We arrived for lunch around 1pm, and were seated almost immediately. The restaurant was full of patrons, so I guess we got lucky. However, it took about 1 hour from the time we sat down, to the time our food arrived. We waited about 15 minutes to make our order (including drinks). Then we waited over 45 minutes for the chicken. It took about 20 minutes for our drinks to arrive.

Although we waited so long, the waiter was very attentive and apologized twice to us during the wait. He communicated that they made some error in the kitchen and had to re-make the chicken. This was actually good to hear, they seem to really hold up to their standards.

I must say that the chicken is worth the hour wait. I had it with a side of potato salad, and the boyfriend had it with a side of red beans and rice. The breading on the chicken is very different from your usual fried chicken. It's thin, fluffy and crispy - difficult to describe, but SO AMAZINGLY GOOD. The chicken was hot and juicy.

The corn bread was too dry, Jacques-Imo's corn bread is much much better, but the potato salad was bomb! The peas that came with the potato salad were the best I've ever had, the texture is so smooth and it tasted great with the potato salad. The red beans and rice was good as well.

The plate came with 3 pieces of fried chicken. BF got two wings and one breast, but I got one wing, one drumstick and one thigh... I guess they do it randomly. Every bite was heavenly. It was fresh, hot, crispy, juicy..... more than I could ever expect.

The price is very reasonable for the quantity of food. 3 piece chicken with one side is $10. The decor is very simple, and had a vintage feel to it. Overall, highly recommend this place for fried chicken!

The space is pretty cool!  Nice bar, lots of TVs and draft beer selection. The food is very good, but I don't think their hot chicken (which is their main dish) is that great. I have tried it several times, just to be sure it wasn't just an off night, but the flavor is extremely salty. It's good if you mix it with something, like the poutine!

This place is awesome! We got here at 11am and huddled underneath the awnings to avoid being pelted by the rain.  I highly reccomend the spiced coffee, and the mushroom taco that is on the special menu.  The mushroom taco will convert those who have never appreciate good fungus. 

Make sure you bring cash and an appetite.  This is a must visit!

Great pizza spot with delicious food and drinks. Great place to chill during their happy hour 4-6ish or something. Logan is a pretty cool bartender. Will definitely be hitting this place up again and again.

We had dinner with friend and had a fabulous time.  The wine is well priced.   We had the stuffed catfish and pan seared fish.   Both were fabulous!   The atmosphere is great but it is a little noisy.

I know this is a Mexican restaurant but the only reason to go here is for wings.  some of the better wings in Manayunk (25 cent wings on Wednesdays) and chips and salsa are top notch.  My girlfriend and I routinely go in on Wednesdays, each eat a dozen wings, have some chips and salsa, get drinks, and leave without spending 10 dollars.

Dill Cream cheese I got this morning was moldy and dated for 7/6/17 when i got it out later to schmear. Guesswork would lead me to believe that was the production date since sell by was crossed out. Bummer to see fresh dairy served not so fresh since I work in the dairy field. Tried calling and got no answer. Otherwise, an ok bfast sandwich n coffee I had there.
This has to be the hottest restaurant in New Orleans right now. The food is memorable!

This used to be a favourite place of mine, but I ordered take out last week, chicken spring rolls and vermicelli, I got mostly lettuce, 2 spring rolls and six sad, tiny strips of chicken. Still tastes good, but the portion was mostly lettuce.

This place is very delicious and has a great vibe. It is the only bar & restaurant in walking distance to my apartment so I hope to make regular visits. Good beer selection here including Sour Monkey!

One of the fancier places I've had in Nashville and well worth it. Service was very accommodating and environment is definitely high class. A nice place for a formal, adult dinner. Upscale modern American cuisine. Entrees are about $30-40 a plate. 

Had an old fashioned cocktail that was very solid. Heard a lot about the cauliflower appetizer dish, rightfully so. The cauliflower itself is pretty decent, but the sauces it comes with (the green pea one especially) are really good. For my entree I had the scallop dish which was also great. The scallops were cooked extremely well, and the black sauce with it was very good, although I could have used more. Can't remember the desert dish, but we all tried and shared different ones so you can't go wrong.

The nacho platter made with homemade potato chips was excellent! Well worth sharing as an appetizer or to have as a meal. The chicken and waffles benedict dish, however, was very disappointing. Chicken was dry and lacked the satisfying fried chicken flavor I was looking forward to. Hollandaise sauce had a strange spice in it that was distracting and bitter, which is disappointing since I love hollandaise. The potatoes were very ordinary and lacked the "bacon infused" flavor that was being promoted. I will be back but I will order differently.

I would prefer to leave zero stars.  I ordered the spaghetti with Meat Sauce, completely inedible!!  I would have complained, but the server took forever to come back to our table.  Several people around us were angry about the service.

Atmosphere:
 I was glad to find this gem in NOLA because it reminded me of the restaurant boom going on at home (Nashville). It didn't surround itself with that tourist ambiance you get with the French Quarter and that was nice change. We made a reservation ahead of time and arrived early but were seated instantly.

Service:
I think the wait staff was a bit confused on who was manning our table as we had two servers but we didn't mind - they worked very well together.

Food:
We started with cocktails before changing to wine. Our wine choice was a bit boring but the cocktails were great.

My girlfriend had the fried chicken and watermelon & tomato salad which was good but my oyster and bacon sandwich blew it out of the water. We shared a twice-baked potato which was delicious.

We had a slice of the chocolate peanut butter pie which is also a must try.

Overall:
If you haven't been I would highly suggest it whether you're on a business trip or having a date night. I'd recommend a reservation ahead of time just in case - but same day reservations weren't hard to make either.
First time there and breakfast was very good, as well as the service. Prices are fair as well
I went there for lunch.. great food, hospitality and very reasonable pricing.. mixed meze plate, mixed grill and adana kebap is great options.. definetely going back

Had the Porchetta Louie. Its claimed as being one of the better things on the menu. Personally.... I didn't find it very appealing. Bread wasn't very good and the flavors of the sandwich were pretty bland. Seemed like something unadventurous people would love.

Nothing struck me as being very good and the table we were sitting at was very warm on a hot summer day.

Great food, complimentary coffee and cookies while you wait and friendly service. You can call ahead to put your name on the list. Loved our server, Jeremy, he was friendly and attentive. Actually all of the staff was great - so nice and accommodating. The owner was kind and humble. Great food and experience! Thank you!

I enjoyed my poke that I got from here. I know this is a California chain, but I think the owners did a great job incorporating New Orleans things like big easy bucha on draft. They also have a lot of different options here like noodles and forbidden rice for a base, raw and some cooked fish for protein and a huge variety of toppings and sauces so you can come often but always get a different taste. For a picky eater like me a lot of toppings are good because that means they actually have a lot that I like! The interior is decorated really nicely, and it feels really clean. Will definitely come back here for my future poke cravings.

Don't eat at this one go to 116th street.  Food is old and sits out.
Ordered a burrito and the beans had that weird dried layer on it. So no one is taking time to oversee the freshness. 
Never have I seen that at Q'doba.

I went to R & R BBQ for the first time on 4/26/21 in Meridian ID. I had the three meat plate with sliced brisket, spicy andouille sausage and the Highly Rated "Championship" ribs. Sides were hush puppies and potato salad. The hush puppies were delicious. Fried to a golden brown, not to dense, great flavor with a hint of jalapeño. Potato salad was very good. The brisket was very moist and tender with a good smoke on it. Flavor was outstanding! The Andouille sausage was smoked just right. It was spicy, but not to spicy. And then there was the "Championship" ribs. A tougher Rib I don't believe I've ever had! It was a fight to get a bite off the bone. Another fight ensued trying to chew it! Flavor was lost in the struggle. Very Very disappointed. I was excited to hopefully have another good BBQ Restaurant to frequent, but I think I'll pass on R & R BBQ. In my opinion, as the ribs go, so goes the BBQ Restaurant.

What a terrible place to eat pizza.  The silverware and plates taste and smell like dirty, sour, dish water.  The host got visibly upset when I asked for a table instead of a booth.  He said "it gets hectic in here that is why I put you in the booth".  Seriously...there were less people in the restaurant when I finished the meal than when I first stepped into the building.  We had four strapping guys in a tiny booth.  The pizza was under cooked and the crust was soggy.  Here's an idea, calibrate the brix, of your soda pop machine.  Avoid Gondoliers Pizza unless you like to be treated like vermin by the host!

Amazing, amazing, amazing. Went there for lunch and had a great dining experience. They have a special menu to choose from with different wine pairing recommendations. Food (lunch) is a set price of $13 or $21 and comes with free dessert.  I never got that far because I ate everything on my plate and was too full. Going back for dinner with the boyfriend.
Great spot, friendly staff, home cooking feel, very clean and affordable. Be back soon!

It's in a little rundown plaza but is so cute when you go in and the food is exquisite. Hands down the best sushi in Tampa Bay and some of the best sushi I have had. Everything is flavorful and fresh. I have been twice now, I also tried the Kimchi, Takoyaki, Chicken Skewers, and the Tonkotsu Ramen. All amazing! A must go if you're in the area!

I've been to this place 4 times because it's close.  But all four times have been difficult.  The first 3 times it was only the owner, I presume.  But he is so slow.  Seems he can't manage to talk and move at the same time.  The 4th time he had two other young ladies there to help him but still managed to pour the last cup of the house blend only to turn around and pour curdled half and half in it.
I won't be returning.

Fantastic service and food,  IMHO- the best Mexican Grill and Tequileria!  I had the Lunch Special Chimichanga for $7.50.  Their lunches are as low as $5.50.  The homemade Salsa was great with the chipS.   
The inside of the place I is all new and I love the giant marble bar. I hope more locales visit soon.   It beats all the other Mexican Resturants in the Rivergate area hand

Went on a random Tuesday afternoon and the place was packed- for very good reason. Everything here was great- we had my 2-year-old in tow and scored the little short bench-table in the front corner, which was perfect for him. The muffelata was great, but I really wanted to steal my father's BLT- which was really one of the best I'd tasted. The toddler had the little mini-pizzetta small plate, which he thought was a little personal-sized toddler pizza (I took a taste and it was great, too)... 
Perhaps the ultimate highlight of the meal was the Pancetta Mac & Cheese- omg- this was so good it should have a warning. 
After eating, I got a sandwich to go for my SO at home, and then had to stock up on some of the homemade cookies, some bacon chocolate covered almonds (I liked them, but thought they were a little too cocoa-tasting and not sweet enough, my SO loved them) and some bacon pralines (I loved them, my SO thought they were too sweet for his taste)
I need to go back sometime to get some of the meat here so I can cook up something incredible on the grill at home...

Nice pizza if you can get it. 

Seriously, after a couple of years not ordering from them anymore due to their awful customer service, I tried giving them another chance and it went ok for a couple of times but, unlike other businesses on Postmates, they won't take orders over the phone and so the Postmates workers have to go there, stand in a long line, and order--which is pretty awful given the fees that Postmates workers earn. Like a few years ago, I was on a tight timeline and ordered. An hour after the order, the restaurant tells Postmates they can't do the order. When I call, the restaurant says Postmates cancelled the order but I called Postmates and they said it was the restaurant. The restaurant insists they don't work with Postmates but Postmates says that it they would remove any restaurant that doesn't want to be in there so clearly this restaurant is perfectly ok ruining their brand via their refusal to insist that Postmates not deliver their pizza. Mind you, it's pretty foolish given that the restaurant's own delivery service is so bizarre, their delivery range is super strict and unbendable. I did have a few choice words for them, and I'd probably apologize for it except I had to go onto a long livestream meeting without any dinner for the second time due to the ineptitude of this business. Their pizza is pretty good, but they have beluga caviar at $20 an ounce and it wouldn't be worth the hassle.

Great experience today!  Food and service was amazing. Love us some shrimp fest AND the service was outstanding. I highly recommend asking for Marcy to be your server. She was great!  Will definitely be back!

Welcome to the neighborhood!!  We are locals, living in a near by condominium and are very excited to have a interesting and enjoyable restaurant within walking distance. We went last night for the first time with friends who had been there the week before.  We were sat immediately, waiter was attentive and pleasant. We shared a bottle of the Muscadet, which lived up to its reputation.  My husband and I enjoyed the escargots, some of the best I have had in Philadelphia.  Our table had a rainbow trout, steak and assorted appetizers.  We are already planning on what to order at our next visit. Mary Ann L.

Not bad sushi. Not the best I've had but certainly not the worst. I would say it was just a tad more expensive than I would've expected, but not outrageously priced by any means. The service was a little slow but the waitress was super friendly.

This is seriously the worst Mexican food place I have ever been to.... I would rather eat taco bell every day of my life.... even then it would be waaaay better. I asked them for a veggie burrito with cheese and guacamole as well as all the veggies they had.They seemed happy and said okay.  I assumed since they had a veggie burrito on the menu that might mean something. I got home and it was awful... There was ONLY rice and lettuce. It was very dry. not cheap either... and we tipped...

For $8 a pop I'd expected more than 90% noodles. I could barely even tell if there's sauce in this because i dont see any red coconut sauce....now that i think about it, they probably forgot it and the coconut taste was from the chicken...How many thai basil did i get in here? I saw probably 2 leaves. Sure i wasn't expecting a truly authentic stir fry but they were pure stingy with the ingredients.

I could walk into any asian place and get something more for my buck than this place, except okay, this place is 'healthier' in the sense that there's less oil. All in all, im paying way more for way less. Not a fan.
Beer = food. Got the chicken club sandwich. Chicken is a whole check breast. The Chicken was not fried out and was juicy. Good stuff.

This Church's use to be the worst, but they have greatly improved! More professional, I think it's because they got rid of that Supervisor named Dave, if not maybe he has seen the light. Anyway the young ladies are courteous and friendly now

Where do I start! My boyfriend and I love this place!! They have amazing prices and amazing customer service. The beach ball was amazing very flavorful! The ahi tuna tacos(my personal favorite) are to die for along with the beach ball and those wonton chips *heaven* go here and you won't be disappointed but beware theres always a line but its SO WORTH IT!

What can I say that hasn't already been said one of the best burgers I have had. All the ingredients you want for toppings and fresh. But most of all I'm a fry guy so I love the fact you get all the fries you can handle. Gotta love it.

This place is so horrible. We were staying at the circus circus hotel and since the buffet place next to it was closed and we were starving we settled for this place. Big mistake! The food was disgusting! Even my children weren't impressed and they usually enjoy buffets. We had the breakfast buffet that day. I ordered coffee and it was like water. Later that day all four of us were vomiting. It ruined our whole trip since we were confined to our hotel room for most of our vacation. My father in law told me before that be gotten sick from that place and we still went. Never again! I even decided to call the health department.

I was cook for about 9 years before changing my profession, mostly fine dinning along with tje occasional "bad ass burger joint", at the first the service was spotty, i was asked to pay my tab before i even got my food or let alone finish my first beer which a bit off setting , but the apps were fantastic, got the fried deviled eggs which came with a sriracha hollandaise, the eggs were fried perfectly, but the hollandaise was bland and lacked that pop which could have been corrected with a tad bit more lemon juice, regardless it was bomb. We also got the the fried mac and cheese bites which came with a Monterey jack cheese which was good, no complaints. For dinner i got the chicken and waffles, before i get into let me first state that i travel across the country for work and honestly, i track down chicken and waffles every chance i get, something about the simplicity blows my mind and i love. I got the chicken and waffles with a side of bourbon maple reduction which was point , solid AF, and also a side of gravy which was also spot on. The waffle was beautiful, pretty damn close to perfect, and the chicken was fried just a yard short of being on the money but it was still excellent. Not the best ive had, but i could take the love and effort the boys in the back put into it. Some seriously heavy shit guys , i loved it
Great drinks, great food, awesome service, and a fantastic concept. I WILL be here again!

That firecracker cauliflower sandwich--dynamite! A definite must try for vegetarian foodies. They should sell that tasty breaded cauli as an app. I'd totally buy it. I loved the spicy mayo, the lightly toasted roll, the acidity of the coleslaw... the flavors work together rather excellently. It was giant, too, and I ended up taking half to go, making both lunch and dinner.  

Faubourg is difficult to find if you're not specifically looking for it. It's tucked away at the back of a bar, corner of St. Peter and Burgundy. There isn't a whole lot of seating, but they do both takeout and delivery. New music videos play on a flat screen while you wait for your meal.

Delicious homemade pasta, especially the gnocchi!  It melts in your mouth!  Have  been there several times with friends and family and each time all entrees ordered were thoroughly enjoyed.  Do try the artichokes appetizer - Wonderful!  Of course you have to end the meal with the Tiramisu dessert!  Yumm!  The owner takes great pride and pleasure in the food prepared and served.  He enjoys meeting the guests and talking with them as if hosting a meal at his home!  Good food, service and atmosphere!  We highly recommend!

Some amazing Italian food! This is probably the best Italian food I have found in St. Louis. Very small space inside but very romantic setting. Staff is on top of everything and service is top notch. I recommend the Tagliatelle with Prosciutto, Mushrooms and a light Garlic Cream Sauce. Can't go wrong.

Went with a coworker here the other day. I am a big fan of indian food but not such a big fan of buffets so I was a liitle reluctant. Then after walking in I was even more worried: styrofoam plates and plasticware. Walking up to the food the buffet counter looked awful. I grabbed some tandoori chicken and chicken ticka masala and a whole mess of naan. The tandoori chicken was sub par, kinda tasteless in flavor. The chicken tikka masala (my favorite indian dish) was excellent. The naan was decent, nothing really to complain about but I've had better. Overall for the price I had  a very enjoyable meal. Looks can be deceiving, I was expecting to have a terrible meal and be sick for days afterward. I definitely plan on going back since it's just a block or so away from where I work. When I go back I will pretty much just get a couple plates of the chicken tikka masala and naan and call it a day.

i figured it i ate something as big as my arm, i wouldn't need to eat dinner.

boy, was i wrong.  
sure, it's light and vegetarian.  kinda flavorful...but somehow i felt like i was missing a nice little kicky spice to round out the flavors.

but seriously, i know i eat a lot... but 3 hours later, i was hungry again.  is that possible?  
good snack.  not a meal for me.

I've been here to eat three times with my lovely wife.  She loves this place.  I think it's just okay.

The food is good, just not real special.  I don't mean to sound like a chauvinist, but this is definitely a "chic restaurant."  If you're looking for where ALL the moms eat lunch, you'll find them all here!

The funny thing is that, while this place is configured almost like a bakery first, with a restaurant added on the side, their baked goods are not that amazing.  They are no better than what Fresh Market has next door, for example.

My daughter and I found this restaurant on a list of places you really want to try when visiting Tucson. We drove past it before stopping as it's really hard to find the restaurant due to its size and lack of signage. Perhaps that is a good thing, as we waited 40 minutes to get a table. But everyone ahead of us were regulars and told us it was worth the wait.

We enjoyed a marinara and margherita pizza, and an olive oil cake, But apparently we missed out as they were sold out of the seasonal vegetable of the day. Actually the person just ahead of us got the last order - shoot. 

They have a beautiful pizza oven, and when going to the restrooms I couldn't help but have a fun conversation with Chef about his style and the food at Anello.

Vegetarian Review: Mike's is NOT to be missed by us non-carnivores! While Mike's is obviously known for the heaping mounds of bbq meats, served appropriately on those silver platters, their sides are soooo bangin'!!

The Gouda Mac & cheese is to die for. It has a slight smokey taste and is ultra creamy!! You will not regret getting a large tub of this to-go, because I guarantee you'll be craving this again later on! I actually plan on stopping in and grabbing some cartons for a side dish for Thanksgiving! I think my guests are going to flip!!

The cornbread is definitely one of the most delicious ever! It's a huge square for $3 and it can surely be split. It's super buttery and crisp around the edges with a hot soft middle. YUM!!! Although we took out, it still held it's own and didn't get soggy at all! 

Their homemade sauce selection is unreal! It's honestly really hard to choose a favorite, although their traditional comes close. Perfectly tangy, thick and smoked! Wow! They encourage lots of sampling and I say go for it, because it's so much fun! They even have little sauce containers for takeout! 

Hanks root beer In a bottle completed our veg-tastic takeout meal, although they are BYO and we plan on bringing back the whole fam for what we can imagine will be a fun, casual great night out! 

The place is small but homey and when I called ahead to see the wait, the guys couldn't have been nicer on the phone and then so sweet remembering me again when I arrived! It's such a South Philly style spot! And what else would you expect from Mike, who also owns Taproom on 19th on Ritner. 

I would give a 5 star for these few items but I'm not sure that's fair since I didn't taste the meat. I dunno. But definitely don't skip the sauce bar and sides! For me, worthy of a stop alone. 

*easy unmetered street parking and no wait 2pm on a Sat!

We came for take-out.  Here's the short version: It was delicious.

The bruschetta has its own section in the menu -- 12 different toppings.  You pick four.  We went for the first four on the list.  It was very good, and the dish survived the trip home in a reasonable manner.  

We got a roast beef and a vegetarian panini.  It's not obvious from the menu, but you can choose one of three breads -- ciabatta (thin and crispy), focaccia (thicker and softer) or gluten free.  We went for the focaccia.  Note: it's a lot of bread, albeit tasty.  I would not do the roast beef again, but the vegetarian was seriously tasty.  

COVID-19: the restaurant was quite crowded.  While waiting for my food, I sat at a table by the door, and the staff graciously served me with ice water, while I got to watch the comings and goings of hopeful diners.  A lot of people wanted to eat in the dining room.  The restaurant is very popular, and to my eye, overly crowded given the pandemic.  For my next visit, I think I'll opt for curbside delivery.

Tonight we had dinner at Athena in Glennside after a hiatus of about 8 years. My wife and myself ordered the combination plate and the grilled octopus as appetizers and the grilled Flounder as the Entrée. The grilled Octopus came partially grilled  and we returned it back to the kitchen for extra time on the grill. The pita bread was cold. The combination plate consisted of Humus, Dolmades, Baba Ganoush , Tzatziki salad and a Turkish Salad or possibly  Red Peeper Salad. The can opener is probably a very useful tool in the kitchen., since  the Dolmades and the Red Pepper salad were served directly, unadulterated  out of the can. We were not sure about the Humous but it was nothing to write home about,
The main course of the Flounder was served raw and we returned to the kitchen as well for additional grill time.  It was unadulterated cardboard with no flavor or real texture. We left most of the portion untouched even after the "redo" .The grilled veggies were good.
I must complement the service that was truly outstanding. Total bill $47.00  with a tip of $10.00 =$57.00
As we were leaving we learned that the place changed ownership about a year ago. regardless, the place is not ready for prime time yet.
I would recommend that they contact the TV hit  show  "Restaurant Impossible" with Robert irvine  for a major face lift of the place. Give it some  ambience and more importantly revamp the menu and find a new chef.

Spicy Chipotle Beef!! 

As I sit here writing this review, I'm contemplating doing the responsible thing and taking the soup I've already prepared for lunch tomorrow, or giving into tamale temptation. 

This is my favorite place in City Market. It's within walking distance of my job and unbelievably budget friendly! I typically order two, one for lunch and one for a snack/breakfast the next day. They reheat well and are very filling. To my great fortune I've just realized that there's also a standalone location on Rockville Rd, so now my tamale cravings can be tended to during even longer hours!

Also known to be good: queso, tacos, nachos.
Hot chicken is a Nashville treat!!  We waited in line for about 30 minutes.  Chicken was delicious and the sides were great too.  I would recommend the greens and the pimento macaroni and cheese.
We had a great dinner at Casa Don Alfonso. The ambiance, Menu, Food quality, Service was all over the top. Highly recommend
The staff was excellent! The food is typical and unique. Coming from out of town we treated with southern love. The BBQ meatloaf was delicious!

Occasionally, the girls (and I do mean girls, ages 21-29) I work with get together and they graciously include little "old" me to accompany them to go out for dinner.  Last evening, we visited the Primavera Pizza Kitchen for dinner.  Granted, it was a Monday night, but 10 of us presented ourselves without reservations and were immediately seated in the upstairs dining room.  Atmosphere great and very clean.  We were not rushed through our meal and we took advantage of a leisurely dinner.

I enjoyed a angel hair pasta dish named Pasta Capri.  It was comprised of the above mentioned angel hair pasta tossed with olive oil and garlic with fresh diced tomatoes, spinach and five extra large shrimp.  Delicious!    My dining companions enjoyed gnocchi in a blush sauce (they cleaned their plates), eggplant parmigiana, a seafood pasta with scallops, shrimp and calamari.

God bless our waitress!  When dining on the second floor, waitstaff has to carry all food and drinks up the stairs, a feat she neatly accomplished.  

For dessert, I had the creme caramel, beautifully presented and so rich with a hint of raspberry coulis.  My dining partners enjoyed an apple dumpling and double chocolate cake.  I would definitely recommend a visit to the Primavera Pizza Kitchen.

Warm beer, cold food. 
Server asked if we needed a box... was told "No thank you, it was terrible." Server says "could you use the thing to split your bills up and pay" 

ZERO comment as to the quality of the food.

Fun place to go !! Great drinks great people ! Great food would recommend this place . Enjoyed a Friday night here after kind work week got to let loose and enjoy some drinks and great food . This is the place to go in westshore . Try some good food here

I was visiting from a different state and trying to find some of the nicer areas and good places to eat and I stumbled upon Bartaco. The whole area is really nice. Lovely little shops and restaurants. a free parking garage close which made things delightfully easy. 

This place had such a good vibe to it. Very lively, super diverse crowd of young and old. It just felt like a place you'd want to sit and enjoy for a while, which I did. I was traveling by myself so I just hopped up at the bar on the end and kind of took in the atmosphere while I ate. 

My initial order was 2 pork belly tacos, 1 carne asada and 1 duck taco with chips and salsa. That quickly turned into 2 additional pork belly tacos because wow. Let me tell you. That pork belly is insanely delicious. The duck and carne tacos were also incredible it's just that wow. That pork belly was something special. The house made salsa was also really good. Very fresh and delicious and the hot sauces they had did a great job at adding some spice. 

All in all it was a great experience with incredible food and service. If you live in the area let me live vicariously through you all and make this one of your regular spots.

Lindy not only creates the perfect burger, but incorporates his creativity and innovation in each original menu item. 
 
A true Tucson staple.

My wife and I stayed at the El Dorado this past weekend. We were there for a friend's birthday. Our thoughts:

(1) We sprang for the Playa's Club Spa Suite, while our friends got the Large Playa's Club Spa Suite. From what we could tell: the only difference is that the large suite has an extra couch, instead of a dresser for clothes. They were very close to the same size. I'm very, very grateful that we saved the extra $40 per night, as we found the extra storage space much more useful than the additional couch. Unless you're planning on having 6 people spend a lot of time in your room, you don't need the large suite.

(2) While the room itself was very large, the bathroom was tiny. Not the washroom area - which was ample, with dual vanity sinks. But the toilet and shower are literally located in a small broom closet. If you have a belly, like me, or a sizable bust (like my wife), you're going to have to step into the shower in order to close the bathroom door to get to the toilet. It's THAT small. And, also: there's no bathroom fan. Which is archaic.

(3) Another hotel that uses "Angel Soft" toilet paper?? Ugh. Trying to pass off those movie-theatre napkins as "angel soft" is like calling McDonalds "body fuel." It's just completely dishonest marketing. If you're a Charmin user at home, you will leave the El Dorado with supreme road rash on your culo after 2 or 3 nights here. I can take the tiny bathroom... but the Angel Soft? That's just rude and unbecoming of a place that's suppose to specialize in hospitality. [Minus a star]

(4) That mid-room soaking tub in the Playa's Suite is MONEY. I have never felt more Scarface in my entire life than watching March Madness from a soothingly hot jaccuzzi tub with jets bubbling up both sides of me as I sipped my beverage and enjoyed the lights of the city from my 15th-floor room. Didn't break the bank and certainly made the trip infinitely more enjoyable. [Plus one star back]

(5) The room service crew is on the ball. We stayed 3 nights and ordered food 4-times (3 breakfasts, 1 dinner). The cook staff was always quicker than the estimated wait time (ie, a 45-minute estimate typically arrived in 25-30 minutes). The delivery guy was always friendly, helpful, and personable. And the trays would be whisked away within the hour, when we'd set them outside of our door. And for hotel food, this was top notch eats. We had good results with the chicken strips, burger, and El Dorado breakfast.

(6) As good as the room service was overall, we had one meal that was just a trainwreck. I ordered the Blackjack special (aka, pancakes, instead of toast & hashbrowns). It comes with eggs, which I asked for scrambled, and what showed up was 2 pancakes and an over easy egg on top. Which put me in a weird scenario, because I didn't want to break the yoke over my pancakes and I didn't want to get syrup on my eggs... but since the egg literally sat on top of the pancakes (which took up the whole plate), I had nowhere to put them. I ended up eating the egg like a taco, which was not fun, but it successfully evaded getting yoke on my cakes. My wife's toast was also wrong (wheat, instead of sourdough) and the staff didn't bring up any jam, salt, or pepper with her meal. On top of that... we noticed that these guys are tacking 18% gratuity onto the meal - which seems excessive, since they're just dropping off a tray (not refilling drinks or waiting on us). I'm all for tipping the room service guy a few bucks when they drop it off, but 18%? Aka, $11 on a $60 meal?? That's gratuitous. [Minus another star]

(7) The vallet guys are quick and helpful. We needed to retrieve a backpack during our stay and they went and grabbed it in under 5 minutes. No scratches, didn't move my seats or mirrors. Good job, overall.

(8) The front desk ladies were quick and helpful. Got us in and out in less than 10 minutes both times.

(9) The elevator system is obnoxious. They make you flash your room key every time you approach the elevators or they won't let you on. I'm guessing they're trying to avoid a Mandalay Bay scenario, but it's just annoying from the customer perspective. Get a better solution for security and don't inconvenience me to cover your own ass. Do better.

(10) When we first arrived, our sheets and pillow cases had pimple stains on them. The bedware seemed washed, but it's still pretty off-putting to roll back the covers and see someone else's splotches where you're going to sleep. To Dorado's credit, the cleaning ladies immediately came up and changed the sheets.

Bottom line: If we go for El Dorado again in the future, we'll definitely head down to the restaurants and bring food back up to our room, as 18% for walking a tray of food to someone's room is absolutely absurd. We enjoyed our stay and will definitely book a Spa Suite again on our next trip to El Dorado, but the small bathroom and deceptive charges may lead us elsewhere on our next trip to Reno.

My husband and I came here today to try this place. The food was excellent and the service was great. This is a great Greek restaurant and we will definitely be back. The food is so fresh and the place is very clean.

As a Penn student, Biba is now my top spot around campus if I want to have a romantic dinner or take a friend out for a classy meal that wont break the bank.

I recently went to Biba for the second time when a good friend of mine (who is a total foodie) came to visit.  Every first bite he took of each plate was with closed eyes and a look of utter ecstasy on his face.  The only dish we thought was only "good" as opposed to delicious was the meat plate.  We really enjoyed the mixed olives, the truffled egg with spinach (served in a cute sizzling skillet), the cheese (I forgot the name) that's served shaved into a pretty flower shape with honey that you drizzle on top, and the truffled mushroom pate.  It doesn't sound like much food for two but with all the bread, you feel full surprisingly quickly.  They are always willing to bring you more bread as well if you need it.  I don't know a lot about wine but the really friendly staff are always willing to help me choose something that always tastes great.  At under $10 a glass, it's a steal.  

My only complaint about Biba is when it's really crowded, it can get really noisy.  The first time I went there with my boyfriend I could barely hear him from across the table.  Otherwise, definitely one of my favorite restaurants for an upscale dinner without the hefty price tag.

Wings aren't bad just not great. Requested the wings be well done, instead they came out luke warm and not well done (crispy). Lemon Zinger sauce was pretty good but they should probably go easy on it because it was drowning. Everyone has a certain way they like their wings. People were friendly though and they have a ton of different a flavors. I may give it another shot. It's worth a try if your looking for wings.
UPDATE: I used to enjoy this place, but when I asked for water with my sandwich they said they no longer give free water, I have to buy it. I'm gonna miss coming here.

Visiting Indy on business and came in on a recommendation from locals . Was very impressed ! I loved the atmosphere . I will agree that it is a bit loud in here but that did not ruin my experience as I was still able to have great conversation with the person I was with. The jalapeño margarita is to die for and I'm currently craving another one even though I've been home for hours.  I am the queen of guacamole and their homemade recipe was impressive . The manager came up and talked to us and when he found out we were visiting he gave us our guacamole and chips on the house . Very kind staff ! Tacos were on point as well. I'll be back on my next trip!

I really enjoyed our visit to Highway 61 Roadhouse.  I took my family along with my dad and step mom here for dinner on my daughter's birthday.  The food was good (although not quite as good as Gulf Shores) but the entertainment was an added treat.  My dad, who never wants to go anywhere but Cracker Barrel, wants to go back to Highway 61 Roadhouse, even wants to go listen to the music again.  Definitely will be going back.

Great experience! 
The server was super friendly and sweet. We bonded over our vegetarian ways.He knew what all of the dishes consisted of and what he didn't, he didn't hesitate to ask the kitchen for me immediately. They were very accommodating to my dairy free needs. 

The food came out super fast!

Very reasonably priced too. 

The samosas were some of the best I've had. Perfectly crispy, not mushy but hot and filled in the inside. So good I ate them all! Sorry kids, Mommy didn't save you any of the appetizer for an after school snack. Part of me feels awful. Just a SMALL part haha Too delish!!!

I had the Aloo Gobi, cauliflower and potatoes stir fried with mild spices and rice with tiny carrots pieces came with it. So flavorful and just a tad spicy the way I like it. I got mild. 

It's hard to find good food in the NE (sorry folks but it is) This was an unexpected treat. I will be back for sure. My parents live around the corner so when they order Station for the 123,550th time, I'll be sure to head right next door and grab some of this goodness. 

Highly recommend.

This was my first time eating here. I ordered off grubhub and had it delivered. Delivery was quick, received my order within 30min. The delivery girl was friendly. I ordered their soul food - half baked chicken, collard greens, yams and cornbread. The chicken was tasty and juicy. The collard greens and yams were both delicious. The cornbread is huge and sweet but a little on the hard side. I would recommend and order again. Affordable prices as well! My meal was $10.25

Great service with our crowd of 30.  The waitress was awesome.  She was a little shocked to see us all come in but she handled us so efficiently.  Like a pro.  Thank you Theresa for your service with a smile.   Individual checks is always a pain but you didn't mind and you were so organized and got everyone's food order and check correctly.  Food was great.  No complaints.

What can I say? This is a college classic! If it's a beautiful day (I mean what day isn't beautiful in Tucson? 80 degrees early February), this is a place to come sit on the patio with some friends. Enjoy some draft beers and delicious food. A pitcher is always good to share here of the many variety from all around. This place is like the baskin robins of beers and they even do pitchers of mixed like a dark and tan! Now that takes gusto! Today my roommate was curing his bday hangover and got the green skins to start. No we didn't have any frogs. These tiny delicious boats of flavor magic are amazing! Filled with artichoke hearts, fresh diced tomato, and mozzarella cheese. Then topped off with a fresh pesto! With the perfection completion of flavors together, this is like a food love story happening in front of you! I got the jester and added jalapeño with it. The awesome combination of that sweet/tangy and kick of spice in my mouth was amazing. Each bit was a little slip of the south and southwest together. True bliss. The roommate shared a pitcher of kona big wave! With the sun coming down and a sweet breeze for a second you thought you were in Hawaii! Minus the expensive plane ticket. It was the best beer ever. We've never seen this beer anywhere! Our server Britney was great as well, very laid back, was around enough if we needed her, but to where she wasn't constantly on us. She was also training someone and I can see why, she is awesome, even a stealthy ninja to rid the killer pigeons ready to start a fight with us for our food! It was almost like a scene from west side story. But Britney was not going to have any of it! Thanks for saving us and the awesome time.

Came here on 10/30/21. Heard the food was good but to our disappointment it wasn't.  Ordered the nachos,sandwich and pizza. Pepperoni pizza was ok didnt finish it. The nachos weren't bad, I just didn't like the lime taste it had. The sandwich was so-so...very soggy that we had to get rid of the bread and eat the chicken by itself. Our stomach started hurting when we got home we felt very bloated...the atmosphere and service  was great, everyone was friendly

Two stars is extremely generous. The wine was terrific and they gave us the happy hour price even though we ordered it after happy hour. Also, we were seated right away and waters came out quickly. That's the good part. Everything went down hill after that. I ordered the Mac and cheese (10.99), my SO ordered the meatball pizza (16.99).  We were sitting facing the kitchen and could see my Mac and cheese was done WAY before the pizza and so they kept it warm by the pizza oven. Note two pieces of Italian bread were on the edge of the plate and they also got lightly toasted. When it arrived at the table, the size of the dish was surprising. I would expect for that price, it would have been about double of what I got. There was pancetta but the pieces were so tiny that they didn't even add any taste to the dish. Such a disappointment. My SO's pizza was as good, meatballs didn't taste homemade, but the cheese was amazing.  He liked it but would not order it again. No worries there. I don't think we'll go back. Ever.

Food is always good in my opinion, as well as service, atmosphere, and cleanliness... but I have never felt like their menu has anything extra special about it and it has become "pricey $" for the portions recieved. Last few experiences have left me feeling like I'm paying too much and not leaving the restaurant  thinking I had a "great" meal... just okay!

I can't get enough! So thankful for this south Tampa location, it is by far the best açaí bowl I have ever had and the staff makes me feel welcomed always!! They have lots of variety and some yummy avocado toast. Please give them a try, you will thank me!!! This is how you do healthy

I went to the wheelhouse Clayton for lunch in Feb 2016. The restaurant was empty and were waited on promptly. I ordered a wedge salad and it was not good. Part of the lettuce wedge was wilted and the lettuce was far too saturated with blue cheese. The bacon was cold. My companion ordered a Caesar salad and it was fair.

I ordered the buffalo chicken wrap with fries for entree. I sent it back, the lettuce was wilted and the grilled chicken was poorly sauced. My companion ordered the lobster Mac and cheese. I tried a fair amount and it had good flavor. Nothing to go back for, but was good effort for a bar. As a replacement for my wrap I got the petite burger with aioli spread. The wheat bun was burned so bad it was bitter. The meat had average flavor with the aioli giving an original flavor. No dressings were offered. The fries were good and fresh. They appeared hand cut medium with sea salt.

I expected much better quality food for this bar in the middle of Clayton. I had better food at Applebee's recently. I'll go back because of the location and ambiance were good.

What can I say that has not already been said?? Goooood stuuuuffff :-)

Enjoy!

The one star is generous. We showed up and told that it would be a wait of 35 minutes, because a party of 17 arrived before us. Not a big deal, at least they told us. They took our name and said they would call when they were ready to seat us. 50 minutes later the call never came so I called them, and they were, "oh, yes, we're ready to seat you". We return and they tell us that it will be 15 more minutes; I wish. We reminded them that we just called and they were ready to seat us. Oops, they seat a large party before us, but they put us at another hibachi table, and we waited an entire hour before the chef showed up. No apology, no updates. At a certain point they stopped check on our drinks. I thought maybe we were just unlucky, but noticed they say another party after us and they waited a very long time, as well. When we first arrived, they said they had two chefs, but it seems like there was only one doing everything. Maybe the other one quit while we were there. Whatever the case, let us know so that we can make an informed decision on whether or not to eat there. So. This is a long winded way to say that we revived very poor and slow service.

The food was mediocre (2 stars). My kids had the steak which was really good, but everything else was over-doctored.... Tons of sauces, garlic, salt, pepper, etc. It's like they didn't trust the meat to stand on its own. 

I will not return, I would recommend any other place over Koizi's.
Small staff, but so nice! I love coming in for their dumplings when I'm just looking for a quick bite. They also have great lo mein, beef & broccoli, wonton soup, and ooh the orange chicken!

Kitchen staff was yelling at each other at the top of their lungs so it really ruined any ambience. Shrimp were tiny. They were almost popcorn shrimp. Shrimp remoulade fried green tomatoes was just ok. Overpriced because taste was not there on the dishes that I ordered. M ordered salad with calamari. She thought it would be grilled but it came fried, they didn't bother to ask. This was 2 pm on Saturday. We won't return.

Ikea will teach you life lessons.  You'll learn that

-Nice things don't have to be expensive
-You get what you pay for... so when it breaks in a year you know why
-Wooden planks are annoying and necessary
-Most people were never meant for carpentry
-Those guys on craigslist who will build it for you = geniuses
-Like Jenga, one missing piece can bring down the whole stack

We went here for dinner on a whim one Wednesday night. There was a little bit of a wait when we arrived around 9pm but it was definitely worth waiting for. The service and food were both awesome. I had the beef brisket with horseradish potato salad for entree and fried pickles for appetizer. Will definitely go back again to try other entrees.
Love this restaurant. Top notch food, service and atmosphere.  Nachos are terrific. Burgers are fantastic. Good selection of craft beers.

This place is awesome we came here after 3 years of living here in New Orleans and it's so convenient because it's around the corner from out home, the people that work here are very friendly and very customer service oriented. This is my second time here and brought more people to try it as well.

What an Experience!!!!!! If there was an option for 6 stars, they would easily exceed that. The food was AMAZING but more importantly, the service was UNREAL! It was my birthday and my boyfriend made a reservation here because steak is my favorite. We drove up from Baltimore and as soon as we arrived, they sat us immediately in a quaint booth and I was handed a handwritten birthday card from the staff. VERY NICE TOUCH!!! Our server was Everton who was an expert in hospitality!!! He knew the menu like the back of his hand. He explained the cocktails, food, different cuts and best temperatures to have your steak prepared. I ordered the heirloom tomatoes as an appetizer and although it's a simple dish, they were absolutely delicious!!! My boyfriend had the shrimp and calamari and they were GOOD!!!! For his main course he ordered the rack of lamb and they were cooked to perfection!!!! I ordered the butcher's cut Wagu. Man oh Man!!!!! They couldn't have done a better job at the seasoning and temperature. We were stuffed but couldn't resist the Crispy banana split!!!!! What an excellent rendition of a banana split. 
Just when we thought we had the best dinner the next day, we received a phone call at noon from a Representative from Steak 48 asking how our experience was. That is what you call EXEMPLARY CUSTOMER SERVICE!!!! If you are on the fence about a 6 star restaurant for a special occasion, MAKE THE RESERVATION!!!!!
The food is really fresh. The owner is very nice they have party  rooms which is cool. A good place for seafood

First it was terrible shitty service it took them a whole hour to give us our food the workers this family came in after us and go there food way before us the food over seasoned the waitress came at the last minute acting slow making an excuse saying she forgot our ticket but we ordered separately. It is so disorganized and waitress was just staring at us like we got our food all ready. It was my birthday and it was really disappointing to have it like it. This restaurant is a tourist trap which is very disappointing to you tourist.
The Pizza is great as everyone has said. The house salad is also really good. Some of the other things i have tried have been hit or miss but all in all a great place.
The best sushi in Tampa. Dare people to find something better. This is real sushi, not just California rolls.

We ordered the BBQ Chicken pizza and it was amazing!!! I love the BBQ sauce it was sweet and delicious. We also ordered the sampler with the Philly egg rolls, jalapeño peppers and garlic knots which came with a delicious sauce. I'm from Pennsylvania and this spot reminds me of home, delicious pizza and Philadelphia! 

Thanks staff!

The food was excellent! We ordered it to go due to COVID-19. The first time I called I was transferred to the bar and then they hung up on me. The second time the hostess answered and recognized me and asked if the call was dropped. I told her that They hung up so she made sure that they answered the second  time. The bartender had a very poor attitude on the phone, but I got the order placed. When we arrived to pickup the order it was obvious that the bartender did not want to be bothered with us. When we returned to the hotel we had our food but no utensils to eat it with. Our order was almost $200 and should have included some sort of cutlery. The food was excellent.

The stuffed pies are served at lunch. For faster service, order to go.
With all due respect to the Bosnian restaurants in south city, Berix will top them all in south county.  The food is always made to order.  The preperation looks good, smells great, and the taste is wonderful. I'm a big fan of the cevapti(sp)and the desserts.  
This place misses a five star rating because of the service.  Good things due come to those who wait and wait and wait. It takes the kitchen quite a while to turn out these great meals.  If you arrive at the end of lunch, don't wear your watch.
The building looks like a ski lodge and the parking lot is ample. Great place with reasonable prices.
Everything was great! The braised oxtail and chicken and waffle were sensational! Can't forget the bottomless mimosas that kept on coming.

Mixed feelings here.

First off! Was excited to see Beholder participating in Devour and thought it would be a good chance to try it. The atmosphere was fun, celebratory and high-end but still approachable. We were seated right away for our reservation, and the server walked us through the menu including the Devour options.

We started off with cocktails and then elected to do the Devour menu with wine pairings (nice touch!)

The food was excellent, I loved my beet salad and my husband enjoyed the spicy miso shrimp soup. The main entrees (chicken thighs and lamb) were also delicious, and I appreciated that many of the items on the Devour menu were from their regular menu.

Now the not so great. The timing and the service were just not what I would expect from a restaurant like this. Our cocktails and first course came out quickly. Our second wine pairing arrived and we waited... and waited... and waited. About 20-25 minutes after the entree wine pairing arrived, the entrees arrived. We didn't have the correct silverware (which happened with the appetizer course too), so we waited longer for the sever to check back in and bring silverware. At that point I asked if we could refresh our wine pairing since we had been waiting with our drinks without the food pairing for so long. The server said she would check with the manager, then came back and said no, but we could purchase more wine. That left a bad taste in my mouth and honestly soured the experience a bit. The timing snafus weren't huge, but the experience could have been greatly improved with another splash of wine or an apology. Wouldn't rush to go back above other experiences in town.

Wow. We were happily impressed. Booked via OpenTable for three for a weeknight. Matthew and his assistant took care of us and there was none of the long wait times or cold food that I have read about here. In fact, the timing was impeccable and the chicken scampi, Cioppino and chicken parmesan for our table were all fabulous. We has started with the Fried Artichoke Hears and the Captain's Mushrooms and that was more than enough for the three of us to share. No rushing us to order or to clean up or pay. Just a really pleasant evening. Drinks were well constructed, too. You won't be disappointed. 
Thanks again, Matthew.

First off the food is great! But the design and service is horrible! 

You enter through the back of the restaurant and nobody greets you. So after navigating through the restaurant to the bar the bartender tells us to sit anywhere. He also told us there is no wait staff so our party of 6 had to walk up to bar to order drinks and food. Even when the food was ready we had to go inside to the bar and pick it up. Nobody else was even in there, I was surprised the bartender didn't bring it outside, he wasn't doing anything! Then when we finished we had to sit there with dirty plates all over the table because again they don't bus your table either. Each time we spoke to the bartender he was rude and acted like he couldn't be bothered. Maybe his poor attitude is why nobody was in there even though most fields were full with players and spectators. 

The fact that he couldn't be bothered to take our orders or bring us drinks/food really turned me off. If it is a concession stand the prices should not be restaurant prices. Also, the hours are sporadic. We visited the other day and we were told they sometimes open around 6:00pm. We waited until 6:30pm and they never opened. This review is of our second visit.

I was initially looking for crawfish, which they didn't have. I ended up having the beans and rice which was really actually very good, it had sausage, grilled, in the red beans and rice. With the check in from Yelp, I also got our gumbo sample. My son had fried shrimp and fries, no better or worse than any fried shrimp and fries as far as I can tell. The service was good, and the place was packed, not that there were a lot of tables. Chef Ron was a really great guy really nice, I would definitely recommend it to anybody. It's in Metairie off the causeway and I 10.
  It's a mom-and-pop shop, which in this case means of the food is really good and reasonably priced.

We were in town from Chicago for Bears vs Rams game and stood close to this restaurant. We looked it up on Yelp and had to try it. 10 Bears fans walked in to a great meal. The food was great!! Pancakes and bacon were really good. Too bad our Bears werent. LOL Definately a good restaurant. Inexpensive and great service.

We searched breakfast places in Lansdale on Yelp and Cafe V-Dal came up so we tried it. Everyone was so friendly. The food was fast, good and inexpensive. If you are looking for a quick place to eat while you are waiting for the train this is the perfect place.

Hidden gem off of Brandon Blvd, ended up going here on a whim and enjoyed the food.  The only dig is the house salad dressing was a bit funky for me.  Portions are huge and well put together...lots of options.  I enjoyed the gyro platter

had a wonderful experience at epi's this past weekend. it was our first time going and everyone told us OMG YOU HAVE TO GO! which i thought was really cool, that so many people love and appreciate this place. 

chris- the owner- was so sweet. she confirmed my reservation by text and she called me. she really does love all of her customers. she greeted us by name when we arrived and came and chatted with us throughout the meal. you feel like you are in her home when you're in there.

the ambiance is low-lit, lots of family style tables filled with people, bottles of wine flowing, the smell of home made food wafting through the air. my husband couldn't help but want to hold my hand across the table- the place just makes you feel like a warm hug.

the food was delicious but the menu is not large so everything we ate has already been covered on other reviews. my review is more about the service and the restaurant itself. we left full, happy, and loved. they gave me a candle on my dessert, and chris hugged us when we left. overall, i look forward to coming back again. a very memorable birthday dinner with my husband!

So the guy at the register isn't nice enough for you?  Or you didn't check your order to make sure they charged you correctly?  Their carryout beer selection sucks?  Really?  Go to a beer distributor or somewhere that may specialize in it.  Reviewers are funny.  

Hands down my favorite NY style, thin crust pizza on Earth.  Yes, its pretty much a hole in the wall type of place...and that's where you usually find the best food anyway, perfect.  I've been here with girlfriends, families, and friends.  The booths can fit you.  There's some grease to the pizza, not a lot of sauce, but just right.  If you want a lot of sauce, this isn't for you.  The crust is crispier when you eat in rather than take out, but thats like that everywhere.

Enjoy....and really, look at some of those other reviews.  Lighten up.

I ordered uber eats from here a few days ago and was disappointed. My garden salad did not include any dressing, which I found odd (but was not upset as maybe I had to specifically request dressing at like special notes or something). But then my sliced turkey dinner did not include the cranberry sauce it was supposed to include and it barely had any gravy on it.

To be honest there food is amazing that's why they got a 4 Stars but I think your lucky enough to be able to get ahold of somebody on there phone. I called 10 times on 8/22 and got no response . Oh don't worry there hours are wrong to on google. They pretty much open and close whenever they please. The reason I know is because I work and live 5 min away from Charlie's and they don't even open till 2 . Too bad People 
at my work have money and are looking for new spots to eat lunch and this would be it if they knew how to answer a phone.

Everything I ate was fuggin delicious and the ambiance was stunning. Went during happy hour for a birthday dinner. It was happy hour so we shared a handful of apps and entrees. One of the best meals I have had for sometime. The miso ramen & the chicken ho fun were both exceptional and had tons of interesting tastes and textures. For apps, the pastrami bing, fried chicken bao buns, garlic curry chicken dumplings, and crispy potatoes were all outstanding in their own way. Highly reccomend and will visit again!

I'm a tiny bit saddened with the intensely negative reviews about this place.  I love Mexican food.  I eat it often.  And while I won't say that this place has the best Mexican food in the city (no where is really all that good here), it's definitely a fun place to go.  The margaritas are awesome.  Not sure what that other guy was saying about the drinks being weak.  I'm kinda a lightweight, but I can typically handle one drink.  The drinks here are HUGE and I am tipsy after one of them.  Just saying.  
The salsa is great, the chips are fresh and homemade, and the food is yummy.  They also have a live guitar player mexican-singer-guy on Friday nights.  Weird, but adorable at the same time.  
Oh...  and it's in EAST FALLS (worthy of an extra star right there)!  Yay for somewhere to go within walking distance of my home!

I tried Smokin Thighs again a year later and had a great time. Cheap beer 2 for 1s and friendly service.    The moonshine flavors were killer too. Also, I'm super impressed with the cash back deal. Will be back to try more moonshine!

Welcoming service, amazing burritos, cute and bright interior for a hole-in-the-wall. 

PROS: There is no breakfast burrito on menu, but they do have breakfast and burritos, so at 1pm the lovely woman taking my order talked to the chef who agreed to make me one with basically anything I wanted. It's unclear whether they do breakfast all day, or decided "why not?!" since the place was entirely empty. We settled on egg, chorizo, beans, tomato, onion, cheese, and sour cream ($10). Far from the ones reminiscent of LA that I'm seeking, but I love the flexibility and willingness! This thing was big, full of eggs and chorizo, super fresh, and had amazing flavor! The al pastor burrito (con todos, $10) and the salsa verde are both knockouts as well!

CONS: Eventually, I ate it all :(

There's a reason this place has 5 stars; come experience it!

This place has always been a pretty solid restaurant. The chargrilled and raw oysters are always good and the beer is always cold. This place also has very good chicken and andouille gumbo. The poboys are pretty good but if you don't need the French bread I would get the boom boom shrimp. It is cheaper than the Poboy and you get a bunch of fried shrimp ( more than the poboy )in a spicy sauce ( not too spicy). Also , the oyster Rockefeller soup is pretty awesome!! If it is a salad you want, the grilled marinated shrimp salad is huge and very good. I would recommend this place to anyone who would like to try a variety of New Orleans dishes that isn't overly expensive. If you don't eat seafood , the burgers are good as well as the roast beef poboy.

One cool spot! I really enjoyed the cinnamon ice cream. They only have 9 flavors to choose from, but they were great pairing options for cookie/doughnut sandwhiches. 

The space is really fun, but has a small amount of seating inside. I would love to see the outside patio transformed for summer.

TERRIBLE. 

The floors need to be vacuumed. 
Every menu is sticky. 
The plates are all dirty. 
There's a complete lack of communication.

Ok Reno this is one of the best restaurants! Open your self to the experience of contemporary Thai food.  Having been in Thailand, this equals the BRILLIANT flavors of well prepared Thai food.  Cone on Reno splurge ! Worth every cent!

What I would like to do is take a nice thick drinking straw and stick it down deep in that sauce and just sit there for like 45 minutes, almost breathing the Korma sauce deep into my gut.  Purely, deadly, delicious.  I'd like to ladle that stuff into my pockets and walk around warm and flavorful all day.  Friendly, quick service.

This place is the quintessential New Orleans neighborhood restaurant. Ive been coming here for 40 years and I'll admit the food was better before the storm but it's still very good. They lost all of the old cured pots and pans in the storm but they have hit their stride again.
Appetizers: I used to get the crab fingers every time and sadly this just isnt the same as it used to be but there's still the unbelievable Shrimp Remoulade. Enough for two but you wont want to share. It is amazing. 
Entrees: You cant pick just one. It's all great but the spaghetti and meatballs are just unreal. 2 huge meatballs that are simply delicious an a authentic Italian marinara sauce. When im not in the mood for spaghetti, one of my favorites is the half and half poboy. Oh my god, the Fried Oysters and Shrimp are to die for. The french bread is so fresh and soft, seafood cooked perfectly. 
After you eat here, save room for Angel Brocato's for italian ice cream and cookies about 2 mins away on Carrollton.

Amazing classic NY style pizza! The crust is the perfect texture, not too heavy or light. The portion of pizza is worth the money. They are always working hard and making the orders as quick as they can! It is our weekly treat!
Lovely staff, friendly. Great food, beautiful atmosphere. Soothing comfort food, no uppity crap, just goooood!
Great service, very friendly. Mike is cool dude. Food was amazing. The Buffalo Parm wings were on point!!! A must to stop by everytime I'm in Philly. Wish they were in Cleveland, Ohio.

I want to say this place is like a whole foods but with a more ethnic selection.

they have a eating area on the side. we ordered a few things. 
-ramen: it was a solid ramen, especially being in stl. the broth was flavorful, pork was tender. they even added some seaweed which was a pleasant addition for me. the noodles were the perfect consistency. 
-seaweed salad: always good no matter where you go.
-edamame: also good always.
-eel nigiri: eel was flavorful and had a nice crispy skin and tender within.
-we ordered a spicy tuna roll but they gave us a regular tuna roll. it was disappointing.
-they also accidentally charged us for a white tuna roll which we didn't order. they weren't busy at all and we literally checked off what we wanted so these errors that were made really had no explanation. 

the store itself had a nice, clean, fresh look. they had a wide variety of international food. I was pretty impressed with their short ribs and ox tails. they were really big and meaty with minimal fat which is hard to find even at whole foods. overall it was a pleasant surprise. will be back again.

Service is always slow but the food is on point and the long islands keep this place on the top of my list.

Sit on the patio if you have the chance!

Love this place, great neighborhood sports bar and restaurant. Bartenders are attentive and make sure you are taken care of. I've been here twice in the last week to catch the NBA finals game. Both times they had great deals. I went on Sunday and they had 8$ mix well pitchers. Food was good too. Their wings are cooked well done which I love. I like my wings with crunchy skin they have a variety of sauces that you can have them tossed in but I got mine dry. Jalapeño poppers were what I expected but the fries were a pleasant surprise. Seasoned well, no salt and pepper needed.
Good food n good service too..I eat from like every once or twice a week ..one of the best Indian food in Tampa.....whenever I think of Indian food here ..this is the first place I go to ..

Ridiculous. Walked into an empty restaurant, placed one order for dining in and two to go. Meal was delivered - cold. Asked repeatedly where the to go orders were. My order number remained on my table. Two separate food runners asked three times about the number. I told them yes - it's TO GO. Is it ready?

Finally I flagged down a server again. Without stopping at my table or even looking at me - she said "Ask him up front." Ummm what? 

Grab my number and head to cashier. She looked at me already apologetic. She says - your whole order will be comped. Soooooo - that means the order I placed 45 minutes ago is now behind all of these other to go orders? Yep. Having run out of time, I told her to forget it.
