The entire dining room was complaining that their orders were wrong, so I guess I should have known. Corporate needs to pay a visit ASAP! This is a mess.
Breakfast sandwich was yummy but everything was different than the picture! Chopped bacon, why??

We stopped in on a Tuesday evening (gotta have tacos on Tuesday!). We were worried about a line since this was a DDD joint and we'd seen it on other websites about the best places to eat in Nashville. We ordered the chicken tortilla soup, a tamale, a chicken taco and a carne molida taco. The soup and tamale came out first. The soup was different than the chicken tortilla soup I'm used to. It was more watery (or not creamy, I guess). It had a lot more lime favor than anything I've had. But it was good in its unique way! The avocado, tortilla strips, and tomatoes added extra depth to the dish. My husband really liked the tamale. I'm not a huge tamale fan, but the flavor was good. Poblano and something else, I can't remember. The chicken and carne molida tacos were both really good. I think our bill was $14. After we ate, we noticed the bar on the other side of the building. My husband went a got a margarita, lime, on the rocks. It was $6 and not store bought mix. It was really good! Overall, a great experience!

The food is mediocre at best,  the place is very run down but clean and the service is not very good.  The menu is small and the food is overpriced but is a decent alternative to spending $50 for a salad at the Marriott.

Amazing queso Biria tacos ! 
Really good chips and guacamole .
Also tried the street corn.
Service was excellent. 
I would definitely return!

Excellent vibes. I want to hang out here. Just had biscuits and gravy with a fried egg and a black & white cocktail. Put me right. I've also had the burger for lunch and the pot roast at dinner. All good! Can't wait to come back and see what else they come up with. Oh yeah the almond croissant was excellent too. I'm really happy it's in my hood.

Adding to this review. The lattes are delicious and the ham and cheese croissant is super good. Once I had the chicken with accoutrements and it fed me for 2 days! I am saying this again. I really dig this place. The Hungry Pigeon is like going to a friend's house who happens to be an excellent chef and baker and loves to have people over.

Just as delicious as I remember. This was my second time dining here and it was great. I treated my husband here for his birthday dinner and he loved it as well. I had the shrimp and grits and he had the crab cake appetizer (amazing!). He wasn't a fan of the chicken entrée but the crab cakes made up for it. Muriel's is definitely a spot we must visit again the next time we're in NOLA.

Mozzarella sticks were a thick layer of breading with the tiniest bit of mozzarella inside. It was like all the mozzarella exploded out, except it didn't. There was just nothing inside? The cheesesteak barely had any meat on it and some very strange type of melted cheese I couldn't quite decipher. I thought this would be a safe bet at the airport, and well, I didn't get food poisoning but the food was truly unremarkable. Especially for all the hype this place gets.

This is the bakery to go to in boise. Especially for birthday cakes they can add artwork/photos to your cake and the frosting/cake is fantastic. The best part is I recently ordered a cake with black frosting which at many other bakeries would turn your tongue/teeth black it wasn't really a problem with these guys. Service is good to

I have finally found my new go to fast food Chinese restaurant.  Score one for me!

Ever since moving to Seminole Heights, I have been on the hunt for good take out Chinese.  I have found some other places in the neighborhood that are okay, but the insides always sketched me out a bit.  I can tell you, China Dragon is CLEAN and the food is pretty good.  Nothing gourmet by any means, but a close, cheap, and yummy take out Chinese restaurant which I will surely order from in the future.  Free spring roll with every meal !

This place is not Tex Mex.  With the bright lights and furniture it has all the ambiance of a Dennys.  The food was not hot or fresh when served.  The chips seem like they came out of a bag and the salsa out of a jar.  The service is not very attentive as the dishes and glasses just pile up.
I love smash burger kinda pricey but ultimate food to fill you up and tase great highly recommend it to friends family and any really. Going back asap

Don't always judge a restaurant by the street view. Attended a  couple's baby shower held at the second floor level of Petra.  Was surprised when I first pulled up. Walked through a spacious, well furnished outdoor area. First indoor floor is small but clean and attractive. Second level is great for private parties (take a look at the photos).

Room was payed out well for our group. Food was fantastic! The owner set up our buffet; very nice woman.
Not sure about prices since I was a guest at the shower.

We will definitely go back for lunch or dinner!
Love when a tourist attraction is worth the hype. Enjoyed a classic Pimms Cup & came for dinner. Good prices for the area. The outdoor courtyard is lovely.

My boyfriend and I recently discovered this new restaurant while Yelp-hunting for cheap, filling eats near out apartment. Both of us wanted something warm and satisfying, while I was craving something vegetarian with a brewing Hanger (my boyfriend's greatest fear). Yeeroh was the perfect solution, with the addition perk of finally putting to rest my confusion on how the word "gyro" is pronounced!!

The venue is very hip and clean (exposed brick, twinkle lights, trendy music); there are several tables, but they are obviously catering toward quick meals and takeout. Staff was awesome, very friendly and efficient. Yeeroh's menu offers Classic Sandwiches (set ingredients) as well as build-your-own sandwiches, a variety of starters, and some desserts. Each sandwich comes with a choice of zucchini fries or regular fries - you can choose to have them put into your gyro, or you can opt to have them on the side.

We decided to start with Feta Fries, which are similar in concept to Mozzarella sticks with a less Instagrammable cheese pull. But the feta flavor with the wonderfully seasoned and crispy coating really hit the spot, and successfully stemmed the Hanger while we waited for our gyros. I ordered a lovely vegetarian gyro on a wheat pita. The warm grilled veggies are well seasoned and paired perfectly with fresh spinach, tomato, and cucumber  that I opted for. The zucchini fries were amazing - thinly sliced, crispy, and indulgent but still "healthy" (I.e. guilt-free!). My boyfriend ordered The Diavolo - this monster of a sandwich is perfect for those who are hungry and those who love spice. It's stuffed with chicken, spicy feta sauce, GHOST PEPPER HOT SAUCE, pepperonis, and fries (yes the fries are IN the gyro). My boyfriend loved it, and I definitely had a few bites and many stolen fries. It may be that my boyfriend and I are used to spicy foods and have had our taste buds burned off, but The Diavolo wasn't overwhelmingly spicy. It definitely had a good kick, but anyone who can handle Hot Cheetos would be able to handle The Diavolo.

We ended our meal with Baklava (because when there is baklava, you can't not order it). It was a tad pricey at $5.50 a piece, but it's a decently large piece. I'm a bit of a baklava snob so I wouldn't say it was anything special, but I definitely enjoyed it.

To conclude, I must emphasize how generous the portions are, given the price. For less than $10 a person, you will get both quality and quantity. Definitely planning on returning here if I need a quick take-out meal, regardless of whether I'm feeling more of a #cleaneats or a #treatyoself mood!

Husband and I came here at 10:30pm on a Saturday for some late night snacking but not expecting too much because we are snobs who always prefer the real thing in Asia. But we were pleasantly surprised that the soup dumpling was on par with the some of the ones you get in Asia. Not only was the dumpling skin super thin and delicate, which is how it's supposed to be done, each dumpling was filled with delicious pork broth. The flavor of the pork was just right and not overly seasoned. We also got the crystal shrimp dumplings which were amazing and filled with fat pieces of shrimp. The BBQ pork bun was ok. The pork didn't have enough flavor and was not as tender as I had hoped for. I prefer ones that melt in your mouth.
Unfortunately, we had already eaten dinner before going there so we were too stuffed to order more food. Next time when we come back to Philly we will definitely try the spicy soup dumplings and some other dishes that look very promising.
Some other pluses were that the service was excellent (servers were attentive and friendly), and it seems like many people were there for the drinks but no one was annoyingly drunk.

Highly recommend it. We will be back!

My friends and I chose this place at random, because we were searching for seafood and gumbo. This place definitely delivered! I got the catfish and shrimp dinner, and it was delicious. We didn't have too wait long for the food, and thank God, because we were starving. The staff was also really friendly. The owner greeted us at the door and checked on us throughout our stay. Our waitress was very attentive and took great care of us. The place has a down home, cozy atmosphere, and their music selection was superb. I would definitely come here again when I'm in town. 

FYI - They don't separate checks here by what you ordered. The only way they can split the check is evenly between the table.

Had a hankering for some Chinese food and this is where we ended up.

The server was attentive and we got what was ordered. The soup was ok...broth with what looked like veggies from a bag and a few plops of rice. The eggroll, and the wontons were cold. The main courses were plentiful but also weren't real hot.

I have visions of many chafing dishes in their kitchen with food ready to go that they assemble for your meal. Not the freshest at this place.

To top it off...the fortune in my cookie wasn't a fortune at all.

Awesome experience at umami 
Great food and service especially Jonathan
Delicious food I really recommend the all you can eat.

The lady behind the counter today was cold and far from friendly.I wanted to buy more items but  she made it out to be like I was bothering her.The place was adorable. What we did try  was excellent .Would love to have tried more.

Visited from the Bay Area and dropped in to try this place.   Service was great, soju guava flavor was soooo good (we got the medium size which was perfect for 2), easy wait time and food selections were plenty; only downside is that the meats were not as advertised.  I ordered beef brisket and beef bulgogi; both lacked flavor and bulgogi didn't look like bulgogi (see posted pic).  He ordered Cajun shrimp and fish (both pretty delicious). Dessert options were Mochi's or ice cream...part of their AYCE.   $32.95 per person for dinner was a little pricy for the quality we received but given the COVID pandemic setbacks, I'd proudly support a business.   Service and drinks .   Meats quality....mehh could use some improvement.
One of the best we've been to. Great food, amazing entertainment and overall great experience. What hibachi should be. Will be back soon.

Since my last review (holy crud!) 4 years ago, we've moved to Lenny's and eaten here no less than 50 times (all for breakfast), I swear.  It's ridiculous.  

Because of that, I decided that I'm officially an expert on all things Lenny's and that it is my duty to inform you of the awesomeness which is Lenny's.

So without further ado - 10 tips to make your breakfast experience the best!

1. Get the biscuits and gravy.  This is literally the only gravy outside of my own that I will eat in town.  I've had a lot of sausage gravy, and this one only needs a touch of pepper.

2. If you're wanting a full meal and would like to taste the gravy - get a meal and ask for a biscuit instead of your bread, and a side of sausage gravy.  I believe it's $.75 extra, if I recall correctly.

3. Get the thick cut bacon. It's amazing.  We fight over it.

4. Try the chili omelet.  The chili is slightly sweet, it's not spicy - but that's okay, it's still super tasty.  Get it with American cheese and top the whole thing in Cholula hot sauce (and some Tobasco if you want it hot).

5. Not a meat eater?  Try the Portabella Benedict. 

6. Like toast?  Get their sourdough. It's a super thick chewy slice of awesome.

7. You'll be asked if you want onions on your potatoes, if you do - expect them to be somewhere between browned and caramelized.  None of us are fans.  Some people are.  You could ask for it on the side, it just comes on top.

8. Ask for non-dairy creamer if you need it, they have vanilla flavored!

9. Look at the ceiling while you wait.

10. Enjoy.

I wandered in Boccadito after a stranger on the street recommended that we try it and I had an amazing lunch here with my young son.  We ordered the vegetable quiche and the fish tacos.  The fish tacos were terrific, they were probably the best fish tacos I have ever had....no exaggeration.  The fish was super fresh and cooked in a little olive oil and served with fresh (in-house-made) pico de gallo, a white sauce with greens and some vinegar and olive oil.  It was all so well balanced and fresh.  I would go back over and over again just for the fish tacos.  The quiche was also excellent.  The vegetable was fresh zucchini, sliced very thin and seasoned perfectly.  It was so tasty that I was inspired to make a zucchini quiche in my own kitchen (which sadly wasn't as tasty as the one at Boccadito).  The owner is super nice too; she was very patient and kind to my wild 4 year old.  I really wish we lived closer to Boccadito, it would be on our regular rotation it we did.

2.5

Decent food...I wasn't too impressed tho.  They have specialty house made chips that our entire group had but no one liked them.

I tried their chicken sandwich which was good and a decent portion.

Bar vibes here...not sure I'd return.

Definitely a hidden secret of New Orleans! We were down for vacation and were looking for a nice place for lunch. Came across this online after searching for the perfect spot. We did not realize how small it was, which made the service so much better. 

I enjoyed the roast beef poboy and let me just say, it was to die for! That was my first roast beef poboy and every time I ordered it thereafter, did not compare to Diamond's!

Really great friendly atmosphere, and not your typical bar food.  Delicious fondue cheese dip with homemade pretzel bites.  They have poker on Tuesday nights for free and fun trivia MOnday and Wed.  Great place for sports too, with 3d tvs.  Chicago Bears fans are welcome which is a nice treat!

So the 1st room they gave me wasn't remodeled like the photos online and spelled pretty stale. When they moved me to a remodeled room it's far away from the main building, like a half mile away, and the rooms were still bummy. The mirror was broken and held together with tape and the furniture had stains on it. For the price I would've stayed at a motel. Probably won't be staying here again.

Yummy Yummy yummy! A hidden gem! Don't be fooled by the ambience or outer looks - the food is delicious and the service really good. We have eaten there as well as got catering for an event. The daal fry is simple and hits just the right spot! Paneer bhurji and paneer masala are divine! The Rasmalai is the perfect finale to a scrumptious meal! The four stars rating is due to the ambience - I would have given 5 stars but for the ambience.

Me and a group of friends went to 86 last friday. While we were waiting for our table we went to the bar. My girlfriend and I ordered mind eraser shots from the bartender kat. She was incredibly rude and asked us if we were on a mission to get drunk. We ignored it at first but then we ordered another round of shots and she rolled her eyes at us and told us she hadn't made that kind of shot in 20 years. We weren't the only people put off by her attitude, as we found out other bar patrons had the same experience. We approached the manager and he gave us a free round in an attempt to make things right but it didn't change the fact that we were just blatantly disrespected by the bartender as paying customers. It didn't seem like there were any repercussions for her actions. It's safe to say we will never return. Horrible experience all around.

Pretty empty last Tuesday night. We were already in the Channelside center and looked up and decided to go to Oishi for dinner. They have a "People Love Us on Yelp!" sticker on the door, I am assuming it is for the Thai Thani restaurant right next door (co-located).

Average service, food was not bad. I ordered the Sushi A entree, which consisted of 7 pieces of assorted sushi and a spicy tuna roll. The entree came with a salad and miso soup, both of which did not look very appetizing. I gave the miso soup to my coworker (not because it looked unappetizing, my entree just sounded pretty big at that point and I wasn't super hungry). I wasn't expecting to be amazed here, but the sushi and spicy tuna roll were actually good.
Update my last review, they did not go smoke free.

I went to this place because I had a coupon for $10.00 off a tab of $20.00 from www.restaurant.com. Based off of the reviews I was expecting a phenomenal burger and ribs. This is not what I got! 

Based on appearances alone the place definitely stands out and looks inviting both on the outside and inside this is where the praise of this place starts and ends. 

Maybe 1/3 - 1/4 of the restaurant was filled with other diners, we let this go bc of the time of night (nearly 7:00 on a school night) we sat down and looked over the menu. Both my husband and I decided on the BBQ. After we ordered the waiter tells us of we just ended  a promotion that was every Monday night that when you order a burger you only pay half. Ok great, why are you telling me this now when the promotion is no longer valid? It made no sense! Actually it really irritated me and I wanted to leave right then but my stomach held me back and was like "noooo I need you to fill me" haha 
we waited about 15-20 minutes for our food to come out, which if you ask me is way to long when over half of the place is empty and half of the people who are there are at the bar drinking NOT eating food! 
The burger itself was totally unseasoned, like the cook just grabbed some piece formed it into a patty and threw it on the grill. The bacon was chewy and tasted like it had been in put in and out of a fridge for some time and reheated and finally the bun was stale. Our waiter came and checked on us halfway through eating but he wasn't super attentive and as soon as he took our plates he just threw the bill on the table. No "would you like dessert" Almost as if he was trying to hurry us out. My husband is a brownie sundae fanatic and saw it on the menu so he asked if we could get dessert. we ordered the brownie sundae and apple pie. Both tasted like they were low quality store bought and the ice cream was crystallizing in the center indicating it had been removed from the freezer several times, thawed, and then refrozen. After we finished eating the waiter again threw the bill on the table my husband again had to get his attention to let him know we had a coupon. Our bill was about $23.00 after the coupon and I feel we paid $23.00 too much.

Summary:

Bad food
Bad Wait staff
BAD experience 

Don't waste your money or time at this place

I was visiting Nashville with my boyfriend and we needed to have a small bite before we continued our day. We came across this super cute spot and decided to have lunch. 

The restaurant is casual but has a great design and decor. They also have a bar with some TVs if there's a game playing, which my boyfriend loved. 

I wasn't starving so I just ordered the pepperoni and mozzarella stuffed empanadas. I am a huge pizza lover so I obviously fell in love with these empanadas. They were delicious! 

My boyfriend ordered the chicken and biscuits and he said they were great. They had a little spice to them but he likes spicy. 

I wish I would have tried more because the menu looked great! 

Overall I would definitely recommend this place to anyone!
The food here is fresh and tasty.  Love the salads!  They give out free popcorn while you wait which tastes like dill pickles.  Excellent!

I love it here! I enjoy everything about it. The entire staff is a lot of fun and the GM is a great guy! I have brought many people here and they rave about the burgers, the chicken fingers and the fries. They really do make great burgers. I love the twisted mac and cheese also. Since they remodeled it, this place is even better. I really enjoy their live music and the ambiance. Definitely worth a visit!

I've been here twice to this established Metairie institution. 

The first time was for a luncheon and we had a set menu to choose from. I chose their redfish in a lemon sauce with a side of roasted potatoes. Fish was perfectly cooked and very flavorful. Same with the potatoes and the haricot verts that accompanied everything. Bread pudding was served. Slightly dry but still pretty good. 

So I was excited to hear about their anniversary on the local morning show. To celebrate their 30 year anniversary, in January, they had a limited menu of stuff they served when they first opened. It 
was also going to be their prices during that time too! 

Needless to say, I was very excited to check this place again. Since my mom's birthday is in January, I decided to take her to lunch there for her birthday dinner. Once we got there, I realized it was a good decision. 

Most of the patrons were my mom's age (read 60+). Not sure if that was because of the anniversary or if it was because they were their normal clients. Either way, I was hoping the stuff wouldn't be overcooked or bland. 

It ended up being much worse. We got the shrimp linguine and the mushroom ravioli. Both of us decided to get a couple of salads. My mom's Caesar was drenched in dressing on the 4 romaine leaves that consisted of. My Caprese was very old mozzarella and a very garlicky vinaigrette which was more garlic and oil than anything else. Major disappointment.

The entrees were actually not much better. The linguine had a horrible alfredo sauce while my ravioli was 5 raviolis. Sauce was much better than my mom. But I was still very hungry after the server took away my plate. 

Overall, could not believe the portions, prices and quality of what was served. For an Italian restaurant, I was hoping they would be have great alfredo sauce. Unfortunately, Andrea's proves that's not the case.

We were excited that we found a restaurant in our neighborhood that we have not been to yet, but we were quite disappointed by the food.

We made reservations for four of us on New Year's Eve. The place was crowded and every table was full. The restaurant has a cute ambience and has a very comfortable feel, I did not feel like we were crowded by our neighbors. 

Our table was ready right away, but the service was a bit slow. We ordered some cocktails from their specialty cocktail menu and all of them were fantastic! The cocktails were definitely the highlight of our meal.

We started off with a few appetizers - The meatball with ricotta and the special warm octopus salad. The meatballs were on the dry side and nothing special. However, the warm octopus salad was the best food item we ate here! The octopus was cooked perfectly tender and it came on a bed of deliciously blistered and well spiced tomatoes. 

For entrées, we got the chicken Parm, the veal piccata, the eggplant Parmesan, and the veal Milanese. We were all a bit disappointed with our entrées (although the portions were nicely sized). The spaghetti that came under the veal piccata was cold - the only part of the spaghetti that was hot was the portion that was sitting right underneath the veal. You could tell it was sitting out cold and they had just threw it on the plate. The spaghetti was also overcooked. The pasta and red sauce that came with the eggplant Parmesan and the chicken Parmesan tasted like raw garlic. I love me some garlic, but this was pretty much eating raw garlic. It didn't taste like it has been cooked at all. 

Although we did not really enjoy the food, we did have a nice night- Our server was very nice and friendly and the bartenders also made us Espresso martinis which were not on the menu.

Father's Day meal: Ribeye Costata cooked with sage! Ravioli al burro e salvia- one of the best raviolis of all-time- brown butter sage sausage with spinach & ricotta filling!! The branzino was just as amazing! To be honest, I can't tell you which one was best! Pancho was the man- outstanding service my friend.

We stopped by on a local's advice.  No lie, the food is good and the vibe is chill.  No pool table or other entertainments in case that's what you're looking for.  If you sit at a table like we did, someone comes fairly quickly to bring you a menu and ask for your drink order.  We got a couple of beers and the street taco trio.  

Miguel was pretty friendly but we got some mixed signals which lost one star.  Street tacos come with one shrimp, pork and steak each.  We wanted one shrimp and two steak so we asked.  He told us the trio comes with one each of shrimp, pork and steak which we already deduced by reading the menu so we just gave in and said whatever.  Once we did, he told us we could ask for one shrimp and two steak but we just asked that!  We ended up with the original order and the steak was definitely the BEST, pork was good and shrimp wasn't worth it.  

He came back one more time to pick up the dish and asked S if he wanted another beer.  S said no, so we got the check without asking for it.  I could have used one more but after that we figured we were done and left.  We may or may not come back.

I went here because if the reviews. Food was ok, but nothing extraordinary. Had the duck taco, fish taco, and seafood chimichanga (spelling??). Everything was average, nothing stood out. Ultimately I'll forget about it. Servers were attentive and it was a nice environment.

My husband and I went here to see if they sold just cupcakes to snack on. We had a bet going because I was sure a wedding cake shop was only for ordering special occasion cakes. But alas! I was wrong.

A woman showed us their cupcakes and went over all the flavors. They were super inexpensive and so delicious. And the woman was so helpful and friendly. If you need a couple cupcakes, or a whole 5 tiered cake, this is a great option.

My party of four loved it!  (It's next to Dollar Tree - your phone will find the shopping center.)  We have been to Thailand and have a good idea of what constitutes good, and this place was GREAT!  Delicious green curry with seafood, pad Thai, couple of different duck dishes.  BTW, my friend asked for duck instead of chicken with the curry, NO PROBLEM and they gave her a giant portion of duck.  Medium Hot was great, giving me a nice healthy sweat.  Menu doesn't say but you can go mild too.  We sat and talked for about 4 hours and the staff didn't mind a bit.  The servers were all super friendly and committed to our enjoyment.  Substitutions were no problem at all.  This place truly represents Thai spirit, a culture where strangers do kind things without being asked.  Our visit was today and I am already checking the hours for tomorrow.  Great gourmet menu on the bottom if don't want one of the traditional Thai favorites.

Well clearly I have been spoiled living in California and having access to fresh fish.  

While in town for business I was meeting a friend from my hometown.  She suggested a couple places but I had read great reviews on Sushi on Oracle,  and I had a someone from work tell me it's his new favorite place for sushi, so I had to try it.  

First the sign for the restaurant is not noticeable and I actually put my name down for the neighboring resturant.  After 20 min of waiting we realized my mistake and had to wait another 15 min to be seated at the right restaurant. 

Once sat at the sushi bar I was a little disappointed they didn't have any rice beer.  We ordered an extra large sashimi (more than enough for 3 people), spicy tuna roll, spicy yellowtail (I think they gave us salmon), Philadelphia roll, and fried California roll.  I also oredered the salmon salad.  

Well...I was expecting a nice spring mix salad like I get in California.  Instead I was given an ice burg/cabbage mix.  The dried salon on top was disgusting and tasted like it came from a lake and grilled on a camp fire (I'm not into that).  The sashimi was alright,  and I know this sounds weird,  it smelled a little too fishy for me.  It tasted ok.  I was also pretty disappointed in the rolls I ordered (spicy tuna and yellowtail).  Neither were spicy and the fish was a mashed up glob instead of a nice piece of fresh fish that I'm used to.  

The service was ok.  The waitress rarely stopped by, but the sushi maker was very attentive.   I was explaining to my friends that one of my favorite sushi restaurants serves a wasabi relish that is so good.  The sushi maker didn't even hesitate to offer me some.   He was also very attentive toward our order and letting me know what was gluten free and which was not (he over heard me tell the waitress earlier).

This resturant is small and cozy and I enjoyed sitting at the sushi bar.  I just wish their fish was fresher, but I am in Tucson which isn't near an ocean.   I'm also very spoiled from enjoying fresh sushi in Californian and Florida.

Nope, just nope.  Came here for breakfast with some out of town guests.  The restaurant smelled like a dirty public bathroom from the moment we walked through the door.  The mix of industrial cleaner and yuck aroma permeated and ruined any chance of enjoying our meal.

I asked for a side of fresh fruit with my meal...they don't serve fruit?  Hmmm.  The eggs were the mix and water kind, not real.  Home fries were good.  The meals weren't served at the same time which was awkward for a table of 7.  Server was nice enough. 

Pretty dive-y overall...maybe more of a guys hangout or gaming place than a clean place for a family friendly meal.  I'm not "that mom" but I felt the need to keep my kid from touching pretty much everything in this place because of the smell and grime.  Just wasn't what I was expecting which is a bummer since it's close to home!
Fabulous from start to finish! The waitstaff was accommodating , attentive, timely and really made us feel they were there for us.  We were not disappointed. Oysters fresh and tasty.

Went to breakfast on Wednesday this week and had a truly wonderful breakfast. Food was good, hot, exactly what we ordered. However, our waitress was dishonest and ran our credit card for $1 over what we wrote in!  That is inexcusable! We won't be back. Her behavior was petty and unnecessary as we had already left a generous 20% tip. Good food - but not worth being taken advantage of. I know it's only $1 - but it's the principle. They have lost 2 customers. :(

Absolutely amazing. We did the chefs table experience and it was worth every penny. Phenomenal service. Bayé was so amazing and helped us every step along the way. We had a vegan in our group and there kitchen curated a menu specifically for her as well. Impeccable.

What a wonderful surprise! We visited Alma Llanera after we placed a phone order with them for custom-made hallacas with chicken only (no pork or beef.) They were very accommodating, with a quick 2 day turnaround on our specialized order. The restaurant seems small and somewhat nondescript from the outside, but is warm, colorfully decorated, and inviting on the inside. I lived in Venezuela, and the Venezuelan-themed decor is amazing! The food was equally impressive. We ordered a fried fish plate (with rice, black beans and fried yuca,) pabellon (w/shredded chicken), a cachapa, and a cheese empanada. All were authentic, plentiful and delicious. The waitress was very nice, friendly and helpful. Prices were reasonable; they seem slightly higher than some other places, but the food is actually well-prepared and great tasting, so "vale la pena" (it's worth it.)  Empanada was around $5, but bigger than normal, quesillo (flan) was $3.50 but it was the real thing and also a bigger serving than normal. Visiting Alma Llanera was a very impressive experience. Venezuelans will love it (a little taste of home) and so will everyone else (great place to eat.)

Decent  food, but extremely frustrating place to try and get takeout from.  I live down the street, prior to moving in I was excited to be so close to them.  

Three times now we spent the time to put together an order, called in to make an order and then have been told that they are not taking any take-out orders at the time.

Once was a Friday night (okay, understandable), the others were week nights (typically around 830).

To me, this is just a bad customer experience.  Perhaps if the person on the other end of the phone had more tact it would not be as big of a deal.  Busy? Fine tell me it will be ready in 90 minutes, or tell me to call back in an hour.  Every time though I get a condescending tone telling me that they simply cannot take the order, as if I should have known better then to call in and try and place an order over the phone. 

If you allow take-out then ALLOW TAKEOUT, otherwise simply state that your policy is no takeout.

I've had some ramen in my life. Never the authentic kind where the cooks labor over thier stock to perfect it while taking great pride in thier craft more than any other. 
That being said, I've also tasted ramen that was nothing more than a glorified instant ramen. So going here, I wasn't sure what I was going to get. Or even what to expect. The place is nice and has multiple TVs displaying various Japenese music videos, shows etc. It's a nice immersion into another lifestyle/culture you rarely see in Reno. The service is nice and the owner works the room sharing stories of his past and how he got here. He will also leave you to your meal if you seem to be slurping away not wanting to talk (nice actually because I've seen owners try to talk to you while you're chowing down). 

Now to the food, I tried a few things so I will go over them heThe takoyaki is really sumptuous but not for people that can't take the fishiness of squid/squid flakes. 
the broths are well made but not quite as deep a flavor as some ramen places. 
The tonkatsu ramen is good but the pork belly tastes old and leaves a funky aftertaste. It probably shouldn't be there if it's going to taste that way. 
The korean spicy ramen is super spicy and delicious. 
The seafood udon is my personal favorite and isn't overly "seafoody". The noodles taste like they were made relatively soon before they were put in the broth. 
The takoyaki is really sumptuous but not for people that can't take the fishiness of squid/squid flakes. 
The prices are reasonable and the food is good but not the best you could ever eat. So overall I give this place 4 stars because the service is so exemplary.

Went here while visiting Nashville for the weekend. Honestly, I don't think I've met a friendlier staff in my life. Besides the fact that the food is AMAZING, Kristin was the sweetest person ever. I wish I could come back here every day to try everything and hang out with the great people. Thank you for an amazing meal and service!

For a location that has been there since 1954 the food was underwhelming at best and overpriced.  I ordered a cheeseburger with sweet potato fries and a drink for almost $10.  The patty was small and dry, the fries were good but certainly limited in quantity.  For the price I would have expected better.  The cheeseburger with its sauce basically tasted like a substandard big mac.  Save your money and go elsewhere

Grand Daughters Birthday 4 of us went to lunch.  The Lettuce had brown pieces in it, the Lobster Bisque soup was like pudding.  The sandwich I ordered took forever and the girl that brought it to the table was rude and didn't care.  She took the sandwich off a plate  and dropped it right on the plate I already had with potato chips on it.  Bam right on top of the chips instead of just giving me the plate.  She walked away saying sorry but it was the sorry that you know was just lip service. All 4 of us had problems with the entire experience.  We will never return.  Oh! we all had gas pains all day after lunch.

We came on valentine day. I would have given more stars but they sat us in front of the doors on an extremely windy cold night and there were plenty of seats not in the line of the doors blast.  Also if that wasn't bad enough window seats are drafty also. 

Our waiter was friendly. Drinks were reasonably priced. Our appetizer came out quickly but then the wait for entrees was on. Buttermilk fried chicken was delicious and the servings was huge. Prime rib platter was also another large serving and very flavorful. My Cajun catfish was very overdone. The blackened was charred to the point you couldn't take the seasoning. We opted not to have coffee and desserts here because we were just too cold! We will come back but now we know not to sit anywhere on left of building!

2 Cupcakes. 
24 Karat Carrot Cake & Twisted Pink (approx names)
The carrot cake was EXCELLENT.  No complaints. Buy this cupcake, and you will thoroughly enjoy.
The Twisted Pink was an absolute fail. Red velvet cake was SUPER DRY; no flavor at all. Caramel filling tasted off. The icing was good, but, not good enough to make this cupcake edible. Between the 3 of us, we threw away half the cupcake. 

With the prices and reputation, this place needs to improve. Perhaps they need to drop the "cafe" portion of the business, since nobody was in there during the lunch time actually eating proper food.

Just because they made it onto a reality competition, doesn't mean they get a free pass or that they know what they're doing.  :/

Commanders Palace was an amazing eating experience. 
The food was out of this world! The menu had a variety of things to choose from -- it took forever to make a decision, everything sounded incredible. 

The restaurant is HUGE with a lot of different rooms including outside sitting. I was nervous to use the restroom since I might not be able to find my seat again. 

Unfortunately, the service did not match the food. The wait staff appeared awkward and were NOT educated on the menu items. We had so many different people come to the table that I was not sure who even was our server. 

I was disappointed in the service and it did not met my standards.

Osteria is everything I want from an Italian restaurant and a lot of things that most people wouldn't expect. The place itself is absolutely gorgeous with that rustic osteria feel, farmhouse door wood tables, clay dishes and paper place mats. We were situated at a table right next to the antipasti prep station which had me directly next to a deli slicer which was being used to output some outrageously fragrant, cured meats. Coupled with the constant opening of bottles of wine next to my nose, I was in heaven.

Seeing that Vetri himself was in the kitchen keeping an eye on the pizzas, we started with the 'Lombarda' a pie consisting of baked egg, bitto cheese, mozzarella, and cotechino sausage. I have never experienced a more perfect crust, wafer thin and crunchy and cooked as well as it could possibly get without being too brown. The combination of the bitto, mozzarella, a slightly salty sauce and the zest of the sausage made for an incredible experience of sweet and sour. The antipasti we ordered (a special that night) was mediocre, three tiny slices of baguette with grilled escarole and a slice of marinated mozzarella in the center, it was delicious but not exactly what I was expecting.

We proceeded to order the rib eye with borlotti bean schiacciata and capon chicken with parsnips and chestnut stuffing as our entrees. The steak was so unbelievably flavorful and literally melted like butter on the tongue. It was cooked to perfection (ordered medium) with a crisp outside and juicy pink center. The chicken was also expertly cooked seemingly poached as it also melted in the mouth. The accompanying stuffing was baked as a casserole and was outrageously sweet while still staying savory from the chicken stock used.

For dessert we ordered the 'chocolate flan' with pistachio gelato which isn't really a flan, but more of a lava cake. Also ordered was the polenta budino, supposedly a staple of the restaurant and it lived up to the hype. A delicate italian style rice pudding served in a mug topped with gianduia which is a stunning mixture of hazlenuts and chocolate and a caramelized sugar crust. Our server also sent over a sampler plate of all of the housemade gelatos and sorbets as she notcied the birthday cards I had left opened on the table. Outrageous flavors like kiwi, pomegranate, amaretto and hazlenut were situated in heaping creamy scoops on a plate adorned with pizzelles.

The service as noted before is very accommodating and helpful with a great knowledge of the food and wine list. We enjoyed an Italian cabernet with our meal whose name and vineyard escapes me right now. All in all, Osteria is a substantial step forward for Marc Vetri and I will be returning soon to experience the pastas he offers.

EDIT: Just wanted to add that I realized my visit to Osteria was on their 1-year anniversary. A lot of the kinks that previous reviewers experienced seem to have been worked out and the restaurant was running like a well oiled machine.

I love going to The Palms and getting cheap, decent drinks and the salad bar.  As was previously mentioned, the croutons are very tasty!  It is a good deal for a steak as well since you cook your own.  The bartenders and waitstaff are all locals and great!  I do not recommend going late on the weekends as people get a bit out of hand, see note below. 

*Beware, on busy weekends like Avocado Festival and New Years; people get very drunk and it gets crazy in there. I turned around on a very busy evening to find a very drunk patron rifling through my purse! The owner seemed concerned until he realized it was one of his regulars. He felt the guy was harmless.  I handled the situation myself by going to the guy and telling him the cops were on the way. He left in a hurry.

3-Stars and here is why.  Our neighbors invited us to join them for dinner tonight at the Green Lemon.  It was our first time dining at the restaurant.  One of the greatest things about dining out with friends is the conversations over what you hope will be great food.  Hold that thought.

So we arrived around 6:30 pm and we were told that it would be an hour wait.  They were correct, we were seated around 7:45 pm, a little over an hour.  Is it worth waiting that long for a meal?  I suppose really that it depends on a number of factors.  Lets get back to the conversation part of things.

The place is loud.  No, not just loud, painfully loud.  It was hard to understand the server without her bending down to speak with us, and once I left the restaurant my ears were ringing and I am not exaggerating. 

Lets talk about the food for a moment.  We were seated at a relatively small table for four people and spent a bit of time juggling plates and glasses, until they were picked up by a bus person or the server.  Thankfully, the empties did not stay on the table too long.  We ordered the trio of salsa, guac and queso to start.  Nothing really special flavor wise, but the ingredients are fresh.  The tortilla chips are fresh as well and crispy.  For dinner, I ordered the Trio of tacos with a side of rice and beans.  I had the carnitas, carne enchilada and ancho chicken on soft corn tortillas.  The presentation is very nice and each of the tacos...though a bit on the cold side, were very very tasty.  I loved the portions.  The protein's were cooked perfectly and the ingredients very fresh.  The spicier of the dishes hit all of the right notes with a nice kick.  The rice and beans- eh...they're rice and beans, a side, a lonely addition to the tacos and maybe enough for 4 bites?

Lets get back to the noise.  First, it was a Friday I will give them that.  The restaurant is clearly popular with the millennial crowd, and the place was PACKED WALL TO WALL.  All of that said, LOUD.  I am only 47 and I still have a lot of fun in me and like to have a good time like anyone.  But the music, and the noise of the patrons does not an evening out with friends wanting to enjoy conversation make.  Its not that we won't return, but most likely not for dinner. I will try the lunch service at some point because I enjoyed the food, but never on a weekend.

My ears are still ringing a bit and I have been home for about an hour as I write this.  Not sure what they could do to change this, but ya know, the owners probably give two flips what I think because the loud and obnoxious folks that fill the place, pay the bills.  

Again, the food is great, but the atmosphere- if you don't like eating your food and not being able to hear your dining mates unless of course you scream at one another..be thoughtful in your choice of Green Lemon on a weekend night.

I have no idea what is going on here. The food is tasteless. Is this the Nashville standard? If so, there is no need for me to revisit. Do not be fooled with this thinking you will be pleased if you are not a local, I was awful. Service was good, very pushy on up selling more of there tasteless food, but the staff was nice. The one star is to counter the four stars they currently have because I literally found the food awful which is the truth for me. I ordered a fried chicken quarter with mash and the apple cobbler looking side, did not eat it. Waste of money and I paid for two.

We had a party of 13 and food took about two hours to come.  The food came out one dish at a time.  The sashimi took more than 1.5 hours to come. Restaurant was not busy at all.   This was our first time at location and will be last.  We are giving it one star only because the server was friendly.  

We wish we read some of the other reviews on this restaurant before coming.

The food is always delicious. My boyfriend and I eat here all the time since it's right down the road from our house. The line is usually long but they get everyone through pretty quickly. The only thing I recommend is to check your bag before you leave. I can't even count the amount of times I have paid for cream cheese Rangoons and gotten home to see that they were not placed in my bag with my order. Other than their oversight of my sides, this is my favorite panda location. Highly recommend! Just check your bag!

One of my favorite food spots in Philly. Amazing food. Service isn't always the best, but granted they're always super busy. 

I tried most of their menu items. 10/10 would recommend to a friend.

Good food, but filthy, disgusting bathroom that smelled like a landfill. The service always takes too long, too, so it's not a great choice if you have a limited time for lunch. But the curry is good.

Came here because I heard about their fish and chips. Another Yelp review tells me that this is the place to come for my favorite dish.  We also ordered a burger with bleu cheese. Our server Caitlin (Hawaiian girl) was pretty chill and gf liked her jewelry. We sat outside on the patio and caught some great tanning!! Little bummed to hear they charge you extra if you want to eat healthy. I didn't want fries and they were wanting to charge $2.50 for some lettuce (salad). What's up with that!? Pretty sure it costs more to make fries when you factor in the energy cost :-) food came out within minutes. 
Food: fish and chips were actually very good.  Cooked almost to perfection and extremely tender. The biggest thing is that it was not grease at all, thumbs up. 
The not so good: our burger looked amazing but lacked flavor. Could not taste the meat, normally organic meat has a strong taste. 
Overall good place to come once in a while and grab beer. Will come back when we're not on the clock to try out their beers.

The food and waitstaff are great but getting seated was a nightmare.  We arrived at 630 and we were told 40 minutes.  The manager Joe was busy seating his friends and made the families with kids wait.  We waited for an hour and a half with not so much as a sorry for the wait.  We looked at the seating list and found that we were passed over many times.  Completely unprofessional.

We won't go back.
We had high expectations based on friends' recs, but found it to be very typical and not very fresh.

Don't expect speedy service.  Also expect the food to be OK, not great.  It's a greasy spoon.  They make their money off people who enjoy sitting chatting for a long time.  If you want a quick in and out breakfast, go somewhere else.

4 1/2 stars (1/2 star deduction for noise).

We have been there a few times. 

Always great food and service!

The only downside is the acoustics.  The noise levels really get up there when it gets crowded - which can be a drag when you are trying to enjoy dinner conversation.

That should definitely NOT stop you from giving them a try though. 

It is one of the best restaurants we've been to in the city.

Cheers!
New place from owners of Holden's in the old pastovino space. Decent happy hours. 3 food choices. Nachos, sliders, wings. - good prices

This was our first time here as it is new. Food was well proportioned, great range of flavors, accurate with how much spice you want. Really delicious! Will absolutely be back and tell others! Great addition to the neighborhood!
A family favorite. Wish they delivered tho and not through some 3rd party app. Their Sicilian pizza reminds me of home

We planned a 50th birthday dinner at Rose Tattoo cafe.  Made a reservation for 6  well in advance.  I even called a few days prior to confirm.  When we arrived, they couldn't find our reservation and asked if we wanted to sit at the bar.   We did not.  They scrambled to put us at a table so we went to the bar while we waited.  We asked the bartender for one drink and she proceeded to clean about 40 glasses that were sitting on the bar.  We asked if she was getting the drink and she said 'after she cleaned the glasses'.  After waiting about 20 minutes and never getting a drink, we were seated. We sat and waited and waited.  No one came to take drink orders.   After an extensive about of time, a girl comes over and says 'can I take your order?'   She didn't welcome us.  Didn't tell us her name.  Just 'can I take your order'.  I said 'we haven't even ordered drinks yet'.   She took our drink orders and again - we waited for probably 25 minutes before getting up to leave.   As we were leaving the hostess said 'if your food is ready will you stay??'   If our food is ready????  WE NEVER EVEN GOT TO PLACE AN ORDER FOR FOOD - we never even got our drinks!!!   
I had always enjoyed the food at Rose Tattoo but I will NEVER go there again.   They wasted half our night on what was supposed to be a big birthday celebration.    Luckily, we pulled some strings and got into another restaurant and had a delicious dinner.

This review is for the cooking class. I attended the Thanksgiving class. This was a group gift and something friends wanted to try since we are new to vegan dishes. The instructor was personable and passionate about her choices for living a vegan lifestyle. The materials provided resources to documentaries, etc. which was nice if you are new to vegan lifestyle. But I'm here to see if I will eat any dishes and feel less intimidated. Happy to say they delivered! My favorite take always were how to make your own almond milk and repurpose pulp, recipe for cashew mayo(yum!), and how to make vegan pie crust with dates. Most useful take away was the food tasted excellent and I have dishes to share at pitch-ins that please many diets, look amazing, & taste great.

Worst coffee I've ever had. 10/10 would rather go to Starbucks. Went once and got a drip coffee. It didn't taste like anything so I bought an espresso shot to try and make it stronger. That made it worse. Literally threw it in the trash as I walked out. Went to get other coffee down the street at The Well just to get the bad taste out of my mouth.

Where to start?  We went to Fellini about 3x before the shutdown, and it was uniformly excellent.  Particularly amazing were the lobster ravioli (that sauce!) and the chicken Marsala.  Also the beautiful salads.

I didn't have any of the issues noted with service then or ordering in (see below) -- t owner is super nice.

During the shutdown we ordered their dinner for 4 I think 4x now.  It's routinely dinner for 4 and lunch for 4 more :)  let's just say the chicken Marsala got ordered repeatedly. The Chicken Fellini is also great.

I think at this point we have had all the pasta varieties on their menu, I think. You really won't go wrong, but the mushroom pasta is the one we keep coming back to.

Also once I forgot several of the dishes and the owner found the number I ordered using and called to make sure I got the rest of my order.  Awesome service and greatly appreciated.

If I ever start an Indian restaurant, which I won't, I vow to have a "combo meal" for one or two people, vegetarians and non. (I can't think of a good way to make that into a joke about naan).
This place doesn't have one. It's good, though. "Good" as in if you like Indian food, you'll like it here, unless you're really aiming to be critical about Indian food which is a thing.
The lunch buffet is damn meager.

Wonderful location.  Service was ok, but slow.  I always enjoy having the wait staff present a table full of 6 guests with dinner plates simultaneously a la Emeril's restaurants.  However, the quality of the food does not match the prices.  Apps were good but nothing extraordinary-- jalapenos stuffed with seafood and an artichoke dip.  Shrimp po boy was weak.  Fish and chips weak.  Clam chowder good.  Angel hair pasta with seafood looked good and was good according to one member of our party.  This is between a 2 and 3 star experience.  Should have gone to Hard Rock next door--at least we would have known to expect mediocrity.

"Would love to give this place ZERO stars. Ordered a burger and the bun was moldy. Not a little moldy but alot moldy. Took it back and they didn't even apologize. They barely spoke to me. The manager asked "so you want another one?" I ended up getting a full refund, and will NEVER eat here again."
For taste,  no one beats walden's. But if you go on a weekend morning they are usually very crowded

We just ordered take out.  Mofongo with chicken in salsa criolla, alcapurrias and pernil with amarillos.  

We plan to try it again.  It is fantastic to find Puerto Rican food in Idaho.
I love the Tom Yam Kung, it is very good. however, I think the curry is not very good because I think it is not spicy enough. The layout and the service are very good. and it is not expensive

The donuts here are decent but it a tad on the sweet side. I tried two of the seasonal donuts and they were really instagram worthy but was definitely too sweet to finish in one sitting! I would recommend coming here with a friend or two so you could share and try different ones. I didn't try any of the savory items but all the yelp pictures look great! I will say this place isn't really worth going out of the way for... but it's decent if you're in the area already.
My husband and his friends love this place. Its an older pub, the bathrooms are kind of gross. The food is ok. I wouldn't choose to go here unless my friends were already there.
Off the beaten path but well worth finding! Delicious mahi-mahi Cobb salad! Jalepeno ranch dressing! Yummy!

TERRIBLE!  The service was horrible. It's like this place is run by a bunch of kids. No manager or anyone making sure customers are satisfied. The drinks were overpriced and tasted bad. My friend waited 20 minutes for a drink while eating dinner and it wasn't that crowded.  The food was ok. The bill was 266 bucks and we gave waitress 366 expecting change from large bills to then leave a tip. She brought a receipt and said thanks and walked away. Um, did you think you were getting 100 tip for your terrible service? She didn't say I'll be back with your change. When we addressed it with the host cause there isn't a manager he said oh she was looking for change at the bar. Really? 10 minutes later. I then she totally avoided us. We had to go to the bar to get another drink. Hostess was totally lying and covering for there shady untrustworthy service. I will NEVER go there again and will tell everyone his horrible the service was.

Is there always a Flyers game on in here?

This place has an impressive beer list and features my 3 favorite beers: Kwak, Leffe Brune, and St Bernardus 12.  Nuff said!

SERIOUSLY?? What a joke! Don't go here. There is better service and a walk-up bar at the Anchor and Brine two doors down...
So I have a question... We came to sit and grab drinks as we normally do on a Saturday and was told that we couldn't walk up to the bar and grab our drinks and that we needed to wait for a table - despite many open tables the host was very rude. We watch two couples walk over to the empty tables who walked up from the oppostie side AND GOT SERVED?! WHAT?! After the hundreds and hundreds of dollars that we've spent over the past year... and even after promoting your location during construction ...with no bathroom THIS is the new sail??? Are you now only a restaurant?? As your locals... not a good move. What happened to the place you could stop and grab a water or a drink on a walk on the Riverwalk?? You can't even walk up to the bar for a to-go drink said the host! I e-mailed and sent messages on facebook and Instagram explaining this situation... I got a response saying the management would get back to us. No response. What a crappy way to treat the ones who gave you business for years and through your transition phase. Thank goodness the Anchor and Brine at the Marriot two doors down on the Riverwalk doesn't mind bar patrons just stopping in for a drink... Ugh. My suggestion...just keep walking past The Sail. Ugh.

Wow, where do I begin? There are so many amazing things to say about Spartan Manor and the staff, especially the coordinator, Daphne. She is so incredibly sweet and funny! My husband and I had to change our wedding date several times for numerous reasons. Throughout each change, Daphne was understanding and beyond accommodating. We even got to the point of forgoing the idea of having the ceremony and settled on having a small dinner with a few friends and family. Daphne was once again more than accommodating and understood our reason to keep the dinner small due to COVID and financial limitations. When we arrived for the dinner (which we turned in a Halloween Murder Mystery Dinner Party), we were astounded by how beautiful the table setup and décor were. The staff went above and beyond to make our small party feel so elegant. The food was incredible. Everyone was raving about how delicious the grilled chicken meal was. It tasted like something from a 5-star restaurant. The cake was extremely good as well. The baker accommodated our request to make it a Halloween-themed cake, and it was beautifully decorated and delicious. Our server, Nilsa, was so attentive and kind. We felt like royalty! We couldn't have asked for better treatment. We will definitely be recommending Spartan Manner to anyone searching for a wedding venue or place to host a dinner party.

If I could give -10 stars I would. I put in an online order at 7:00pm. Food was supposed to be ready by 7:35pm. When I got there I was told to wait another 5 mins, no biggie.... finally 20 mins went by and still no food.  I finally asked someone, the woman rudely said "not ready yet". I was standing waiting until 8:30pm & I had enough. I had no choice but to ask for a refund. No explanation given or apology. I was warned about the service but decided to see for myself, I should've listened. First and LAST time here. Thank god there's a Chick-Fil-A close by.

My wife and I tried out this location as we were looking for a new dining experience. Our choices were interesting but the servers could help its new customers by being a little more informed. We will be returning to try some of the other menu options we saw.

Love this place! Awesome atmospher and cool lounge area. Beer selection is great and always has a little bit of everything. All the servers I've had have always been super knowledgable and great with their recommendations. Food items that I don't usually like I end up liking if it's on their menu. I got clam chowder once that was extremely salty, but that's the only complaint I've ever had from this place. I very much enjoy going here.
Great service. The drum was incredible but the desserts were just OK. I would still recommend it to anyone passing by New Orleans.
The Po-Boys are the best (fried shrimp with the cocktail sauce). This is my absolute favorite place to eat in New Orleans.
This is the best pizza in SB, hands down. But lets be honest, they aren't competing with much. Its the closest to east coast pizza you'll get out here so when I'm craving it I head to Ginos

We have been to Casa Tina a few times and every time has been great. The food is always fresh and it's healthier than most traditional, fattier dishes. On the weekends they do an aerial acrobatic show that is really cool to watch. The prices are a little more than traditional Mexican places, but they give you huge serving sizes. My husband and I typically split a dish when we go and have not been disappointed yet. Their sangria and their mojitos are very good, as well as (of course) their margaritas.

What great venue for eating, drinking, and listening to your favorite music groups.  Last night we saw New Riders of the Purple Saga and they blew us away.  A trip down memory lane when I hung around San Fran in the early 70s.  Jam band elite, although the founding members are dead all but one they still got it.  They were working their way toward Chicago for the Greatful Dead 50th and last show over the 4th of July weekend.  We started with a Scottish Devil egg, Cobb salad split, peach n Beacon flatbread with a very young Vinhe Vino wine.  All in all. A great evening!  We will back!

I was anxious about edison after reading the mixed reviews, but I was happily not disappointed.

We had an early dinner, which meant that the restaurant wasn't too crowded, and we got plenty of attention from the waitress.  The place wasn't full until we finished our meal, so it wasn't too loud.  Everything about the place indicates that it'd be loud if it was at capacity, though.

Their wine list is very reasonable.  There aren't any very expensive bottles, which is nice, although I wonder if a bunch of their selections might be hangover precursors.  We went with the most expensive bottle on their list, and we both felt fine the next morning.

To start, we shared the conch fritters and the caesar salad.  The chef very kindly split the salad so that only I got the anchovies, since my husband hates seeing the little fish on his plate.  Both were good but not great.

For his entree, my husband got the Kobe culotte steak, which he thought was good but not great.  I thought the outside was a little too charred -- I tasted burnt fat, not carmelized meat.  I tried the monkfish (a daily special).  It was heavenly.  The fish was so mild and flaky.  The miso caramel was a perfect complement.  The garlicky mushrooms and salty sea beans were so addictive -- I would have happily eaten them for the whole meal).  The celeriac puree was unnecessary in my opinion but wasn't bad.

We didn't have room for dessert.  I wish we had, but we did order a lot of food.

Will never return.  My daughter had just gotten engaged there and we looked forward to having her birthday party there with some of her future bridesmaids. Manager, Jessica, was unprofessional and treated my party of 9 horribly.  I couldn't reserve a table for 10, so we split out party into 3 tables.  I emailed ahead to say that while we were 3 tables, I would pay for all 3.  2 of our tables were sort of close, so they pulled their 2 chairs over and we used the 2nd table for our food and gifts. My husband went to all 3 servers and said they could order what they wanted but he would take care of the bill.  The 3rd table was never acknowledged until I went to find a manager.  The server came once to them after.  Our waitress, Jenn was great! When Jen handed my husband the bill, she explained that we were being charged for a 20% gratuity for all 3 tables.  Had our service at each table been equal to our service, it would've been Okayama if we hadn't been told multiple times that we were not a cohesive party, we would've been fine.  In fact, that's what we wanted! The real issue came when the manager came over after we were handed the bill (no one had taken our card yet) and she told us she needed the table that had our food on it.  She said she needed to make room for the next shift. We had roughly 20 minutes left on our reservation for 2 of the tables.  But we were in the process of leaving but waiting to pay.  Jessica started yelling at me when I asked about paying the gratuity on a table that never received service.  She stormed off and slammed a door in the middle of yelling at me.  As we were leaving, she was in the parking lot area yelling at a bridal party "thanks you for being an AWESOME LARGE GROUP", obviously meant to embarrass me and my guests as we left.  We've been there many times and thought it would be great to have an engagement party there in the fall.  I'll be looking for another winery to frequent.

We had a wonderful experience after Hurricane Irma. They were short staffed but the food was awesome. Some people left irritated because they were impatient. We were glad they were one of the few places open so we could get out of the house. We will definitely come back again!
Had a great phone interview and a scheduled face to face interview then I get a call that says we changed our minds. So rude glad I'm not working for these people

they do craft donuts here, and they do it well! the salted caramel is my favorite but i always order the chocolate covered yeast when i go there. the stumptown coldbrew coffee is the real deal and the best thing about them is the customer service! they earned my very 1st review on yelp because of it!

Wanted to updated after chatting with the manager:

Our experience was at Nom Nom was an anomaly as they do actually accept credit cards and are a full service restaurant
Woody's accommodated our work dinner and did an excellent job. The food was awesome and hospitality even better!

Ordered three burgers and only two came out. After several groups and to-go orders left they asked for the order again. Watched several groups come and go with no response. They took my order two more times and never received my food. Left hungry and frustrated.

I eat at Cori's DogHouse A LOT! My husbands current mission is to get his picture on their Weiner Wall which consists of eating all of the hotdogs on the menu.  Cori's has amazing dogs on a brioche bun.  You can get your standard toppings or some more unique options.  My favorite is the Chicago Dog with a side of fried mushrooms.  If you like hotdogs you won't be disappointed at Cori's.

Great food- can't go wrong with any of their pastas and a dessert.

They just have an older vibe in there which I think deters potential clientele.  It would be a beautiful date spot or even engagement/birthday etc.... party location

We were looking for a place for Fresh, delicious seafood for a party we were having at home. We stopped in ahead of our event to see the selection and ask questions and the man in the store was so helpful. He showed me everything and made suggestions. He went over prices and talked about how to best prepare everything for us to serve at home. We went back 2 days later to buy what we needed. The woman employee was equally as helpful and made great suggestions. She told me about the garlic sauce for the clams which was out of this world. She told me to best serve and prepare everything. We bought 4 dozen little necks, 2 lbs Upeel shrimp, 16 crabs and garlic sauce. Everything was amazing. The price was $155. A great value for fresh seafood. We will definitely be back

Love coming here all the time. It's a tarpon classic and favorite little gem at the end of the sponge docks. The Fat Bobs are so delicious worth $16, drink these with caution, not for the lightweight drinker. Crab  bisque soup is amazing and key lime pie made in house. You just have to come out and try it for yourself. It's pricey but worth it especially for special occasions, or if you  just want splurge, a little bit. SUSHI IS SO GOOD!!!!

Horrendously slow service on a Sunday with only 3 other tables in addition to ours. From the start is was painfully slow to get our drink order, just as slow to get our food which came out barely warm- must have sat back in the kitchen for a bit. Then we had to get up and ask the host to help us get our check as we were waiting for quite some time, clearly done with our meals. It took another 10 min for that to happen. I had ordered another drink before our meals arrived but never received it - of course it was still on the bill. 

Mediocre food and painfully slow service has ensured we will not be returning.

I attended a rehearsal dinner here in their second floor private room so please note that this review is for usage of the restaurant as a rehearsal dinner venue only. 

The food was decent and the beer not that great, for a brewery. The second floor private room did not have a separate sound system which kind of was a disaster because the groom attempted to give a thank-you speech to the group and there was bar-type music playing not so subtly in the background. All in all probably a good hangout/meetup spot for friends, but maybe not the best for a rehearsal dinner, if you're looking for a quiet space that you have full control over.

Not impressed! I had heard good things..but was really disappointed. There was not very much cheese under the sauce. Chicago deep dish has cheese an inch thick! I couldn't even tell if there was cheese. The sauce was bland to me. The crust was the best of it all. I'm gonna leave the deep dish to the pros up north!!

Nice choice of beers on tap, you need to park across the street or behind the building so plan accordingly.  Staff is real friendly and will help with offering suggestions.  the only reason for four instead of five stars is the size of the place.

Many reviews say to get the grilled oysters. They are very good, but, not their fault, I expected to be able to order more than a half dozen oysters. I expected to be able to order a dozen, two dozen, whatever I wanted. It only comes as a half dozen appetizer. Yes, I could order 2 or 3 appetizers, but that's not the point.

Same with the gumbo, which was the best I had. It only comes as an appetizer. Double or triple the portion, let me get a dozen oysters, and I would have been in heaven. 

The entrees I had were good, but all I thought about was the gumbo and oysters.

I came here after a long day of sightseeing, and was dressed in a t-shirt. Severely underdressed, but I didn't care, and they didn't look down on me. Great service.

A comfortable spot with delicious noodle soups rivaled only by a select other spots in Philadelphia's Chinatown. This place does get VERY busy, as you'd probably expect being right next to the famed tourist destination Dim Sum Garden, but it is famous for different reasons.

Curiosity led me to this place, and I was blown away by the quality of the food I ate. Of course, I had the get the house special noodle and was pleasantly surprised by the flavor and appearance of the soup.

We stopped in for a beer/drinks and snack on the way to dinner.  I love craft beers and was not disappointed.  Good beer and a nice selection with the sampler.  The oysters were not up to par, not a great taste nor large.  My advice, skip em.... we did get the Pimms Cup - that was very nice.  Never had one before and enjoyed the flavor very much.   Even stopped back for another Pimm's on the way to the airport.

Although the place was a tad tricky to find, I'm so glad I drove around the property and found it! Everyone there was very nice, positive attitudes, helpful.  I ordered the 3 piggy bread and it was very tasty. I also ordered a chocolate chip pumpkin bread to go. I'm so glad that someone supports us GF people!!

Bains deli is a place I routinely visit when searching for a breakfast meal (typically around 11am on a weekend). I almost always take out (because I live close by) but Bains does have several flat screen TV's for viewing pleasure if you choose to eat in. Here is the breakdown...plain and simple. 

-exceptional service, friendly people
-good sandwiches but pricey. 
-above average coffee, $1.50 for a 16 oz.
-insane Mac and Cheese, ask for hot sauce mixed in
-satisfactory bacon egg and cheese

Wings are good, but service at the bar has to be the worst I've experienced. From someone who travels for a living, sitting at the bar is an easy go to, but when the bartenders have no personality it's hard to enjoy the town your in. Not impressed with the service but the salad bar is well kept. 

From an outsider not from this town I would advise the managers to train your bartenders to be social, lively and vibrant! Reach out to them that a sense of urgency goes a long way with customers not from here. At least smile! 


As far as cleanliness, have your bartenders wash there hands.. I saw on numerous occasions her wash dishes, serve drinks and touch her mouth without some hand sanitizer. Yikes!


-HR Director
Best place for tapas. The only con is limited seating. They also do not accept reservations.

I spent a weekend in St. Louis recently, and after eating here on the first day we changed our food plans so we could eat here again on the second day! It really is that good, and the owner is super friendly; not to mention the prices are fantastic!!

This is by far the worst restaurant experience that I have had recently.  We went one Saturday after going to the flea market.  The restaurant that we wanted to eat at did not open for another hour and fifteen minutes. The inside was busy and really loud so we went and sat outside.  After about ten minutes a server came out and waited on a table that was just seated and then asked us if anyone had helped us.  We said no and he said that he would find out waitress.  Another ten minutes later he brought the other party their drinks and took their order.  Then came to us and said that he could not find our waitress so he would take our drink order (the place is not that big I am unsure how you would lost a waitress but ok).  

After about another ten minutes he brings the other party their food and goes back and comes back with two of six drinks.  About ten more minutes later my husband goes inside and brings out the other drinks after the bartender said that he was waiting on our "phantom" waitress.  Finally about fifteen minutes later the guy comes back out to clean off the other party's table and take our order.  I seriously wanted to just leave because by now it really wouldn't be that big of deal to wait for the restaurant we wanted to go to but I did not want to embarrass the one person in our party that suggested this place.

So we placed the order (even though I was skeptical anything here was going to be edible).  We really should have left.  Three of the six meals were left sitting on the table virtually untouched and we left still hungry.  I will starve on the way to another place before going anywhere near here again!

Have ordered twice from here and both times the pizza was amazing.  The first time got bacon as a topping, the bacon was super crispy was so good.  The second time we got a pepperoni pizza w banana peppers on the side.  Also extra sauce.
 The pizza was perfect the peppers were so good can't wait to order again obsessed

I worked for this business for three days before I was fired.  NOT customer oriented, in fact I found myself repeatedly apologizing to tables for the owner's demands.  I was not allowed to warm up a croissant for someone, this customer subsequently got yelled at by an owner, cancelled their order and left... I was not allowed to re-fill an iced tea, once the customer had requested a to go cup.  I was told to charge for another $3.25 iced tea.  

These owners treat their workers like dogs and are verbally abusive to their staff on a daily basis.  Please if you dine here, tip your waiter well, they deserve it.

Yo what up, I'm going to give you some key info really quick here. Arnold's is dope. The staff is friendly and fast, even with a line out the door the service is excellent. The Brussels sprouts go, the chicken fried steak goes, the mashed potatoes go. The staff will help you get whatever you need and let's be honest the free parking is a no brainer.
Love, love, love Royals! Excellent service and tasty food every time! I'm a regular and love ordering from them.

Yelpers, you really disappointed me on this one. If I didn't know better, I would think you'd all been paid for these reviews. We tried it tonight, and it was a disaster from the get go. For starters, the guy taking my order on the phone knew nothing about the menu. I had to repeat each item 4 or 5 times while he searched the computer to find it. Even then he got it wrong. While I ordered 3 rice balls, I got 3 orders, or 9 rice balls.

If ordering was the only problem, I probably wouldn't be writing this review. Truth is, the sushi was only mediocre. The selections were pretty much the same as what they offer at grocery stores. Admittedly, the fish was fresher, but that alone is not enough to get me back here. I'll stick with real sushi places.

We have eaten at Pappys, Bogarts, and other chain BBQ joints, and Wilson's put's them all to shame. That is some awesome BBQ. I could not believe in, the pulled beef with slaw was better than I have ever tasted. They have to be the best in St Louis. Wow hats off to the owner. I would eat there before I ate at a five star place, it is that good.

Wonderful breakfast! Was recommended on the idea I should try their shrimp and grits. That was OK. Had a bbq sauce base I think. The wife got the dish named Trifecta.It was absolutely Epic! I recommend exploring their menu. If we are back in the area we certainly will!

Small shop offering authentic Columbian pastries. I go to them for my cravings and end up getting more than I planned because everything looks great in the case and no's prepared with skill. The prices have increased but it can be worth the trip for authentic cultural food.

Chick-Fil-A Lima is very well run and has worked with my kid's elementary school many years now to organise fundraisers and family events.  There is a play area for the little ones, and even though I can not STAND the political views of the company's CEO, I was not able to boycott them, because they are the only fast food I will allow my child to consume.
