The chicken sandwich (whole wheat bun available) is pretty good for a fast food option - and you can get fresh fruit instead of fries.

El kiddo also loves the mini cones (not so mini!) of "Ice Dream".

This was a great family experience with extended family. The service was great and the food was delicious.    We will return again very soon.   Everyone liked what we chose and we are more full than we need to be.  Great place for celebrations.

Best take out Chinese in Clearwater.  Food is always very fresh and VERY hot!  Egg rolls crispy on the outside and delicious on the inside. Boneless spare ribs are outstanding. Spicy dishes are just right. Portions are phenomenal, plenty for lunch the next day.

Love this place, the staff is always super friendly and helpful. Every single dish I have had there is outstanding!! I say if you have not tried this place yet, I would ask you why the heck not??? I HIGHLY recommend the wings and Brussels spouts! Delish

Not impressed. Where I come from, you wouldn't be able to stay in business if you charged people for salsa. Also, where is the cheese in my enchiladas? Aaaaand expensive. Maybe it's because there isn't a lot of competition for Mexican food in the middle of Philadelphia but y'all should call the West and get some tips.

Updated to add: the waiter was nice. The chips were great. The vibe of this place is hipstery early 1980's.

To maximize the hot pot experience: come with a group of friends, take your time and prepare your favorite sauce.
Our group of 7 people occupied the big round table so we got enough table space for all the materials . I tried Coty S sauce recipe. It turned out quite delicious , I loved it. We ordered, cooked or grilled, ate, enjoyed the conversation. After 2 hours, my tummy was happy. We were each served a complementary small Yogurt drink. The services were good. They added venting vacuum on top of each small table, so the grilling was less smoky . Overall the materials were fresh . The selections were wide.  I enjoyed the hot pot meal.

Where else can one have a pork belly sandwich with mint and cucumber or a duck pastrami slider for lunch at the price of a big-mac meal?  Add homemade pickles and onions, homemade potato chips, and a local NOLA beer -- you are in cochon (hog)-heaven.  If one is visiting the WWII museum, this restaurant is only about two blocks south.  By all means go out of your way to try it.  A great find by an out-of-towner.

Yummmm! The newer bigger location is spacious and has a fun atmosphere. The waffles are served warm (SO good!) and I always go for the strawberry and chocolate combination. Don't forget the toppings area with chocolate and caramel sauce. Such a good spot and the prices are really good, too.

Man, I only had one night in NOLA, really just a few hours. Having never been, I rode around the French Quarter looking for a bar/pub/restaurant that looked interesting but just wasn't really feeling any of the spots. I fuckin hate tourist traps so I decided to call it a night and head to my hotel which was about 6 miles east on 10. As I made my way out I happened past Gene's. It definitely wasn't a tourist trap so I made a U-turn parked in Walgreens across the street and headed in. Now, so you know, I'm a fairly large, scary looking to some black dude from the inner city. Despite that, Gene's had me with my head on a swivel. I went there at about 11pm and it was grimy. The regulars weren't hiding the fact that they were sizing me up. Anyway, got the philly steak (roast beef) PoBoy which was my first. That fucking thing was perfect, albeit a little messy but god damn it was good!!! Fuck the tourist traps...this is where it's at. Go, be a little afraid, be leary, worry, look over your shoulder in eager anticipation of your number being called, escape with you food and head back to wherever you're staying and enjoy all that hood goodness.

Been on a bit of a Thai fix recently, and when I heard that the son of the lady who cooks for Sa-ing in Vail is the guy who runs this place, I had to try...

I really like that this place does both chinese and Thai, but I did not try the Chinese. You can get that anywhere. Thai, especially GOOD Thai, is a bit harder to find. Overall, I would say this place is fair. I tried both of the dishes I judge most Thai restaurants by (Pad Thai and Gang Garee), and was extremely impressed by one, extremely depressed by the other.

The Gang Garee is what I ordered while I sat down and ate. It was fantastic. Very very similar to his mothers lol. Thats a good thing though, as hers was the best Ive ever had. The chicken was also cooked fantastically. The spice--awesome. Because of this dish, I decided to order the Pad to go.

Two big things were wrong with this: the flavor and the portion. The flavor was rather bland despite clearly having enough sauce and having all the elements cooked correctly. It just simply didnt do it for me. I mean, I've had A LOT worse elsewhere, but id give this a 5/10 tops. Really disappointing. Then on top of that, it came in a small chinese to go box which really made me question the value of it. Just for reference, the same dish at the same price at Sa-Ing comes in one of those big square Styrofoam  3-section containers, and it overflows all 3 compartments. 

So I think overall so far, Im going to rank this place 3rd next to Karunas and Sa-Ing for Thai food in Tucson. I'll definitely be back. Pretty cool that this place delivers too, but unfortunately I dont live within the delivery area :(

This place was packed on a Thursday night and we could tell why! The servers are energetic and fun and the place has great music! The crowd seemed relatively young and the ambience was warm and cozy! We ordered a cheese plate with monchego, blue cheese and tetilla. The tetilla was v creamy and we all loved it but the monchego had a great form taste and I would definitely get that one every time. The cocktails were fantastic! The fourth star is for the ambience and music!

Terrible biscuits. They were completely the wrong texture with no flavor aside from salty. It was just like an oily bread and not flakey at all. Perhaps this works fried and covered with sugar but I didn't try it. The fried chicken and gravy meal was decent but only because the gravy was very good. However, for a place called "Biscuit Love" I could not have been more disappointed. 

Staff was friendly and food was well plated. I assume that's why this place is so popular as people love instagraming food more than eating it nowadays. But if you like eating food, I recommend 5 daughters instead.

Yo Dogs! loses a star...
Hamburgers are actually about half the menu at Yo Dogs! and now I've had their burgers twice.  The first time I got my burger to go and I was disappointed to find that the bun was completely dry, that is, no mayo, ketchup, or mustard. The second time I made sure to specify that I wanted mayo and ketchup. What I got was one packet of ketchup wrapped up with the burger, no mayo, and still no sauce at all on the bun.  In addition, both times the burger was pretty rare.  While rare steak is perfectly safe, rare burgers are less so (former Food Science major here); no one should be served a rare burger unless they specify that's what they want. Don't get me wrong, it was juicy and delicious (and actually that helped make up for the lack of sauce).  When I'm asked how I want my burger cooked, I always specify medium; if I'm not asked, I assume it's the restaurants policy to cook the burger all the way through (I don't think any of the major fast food chains will ever intentionally serve you a burger that isn't cooked all the way through, even if you ask for it). I think I'll stick with the hot dogs if I go back.

I have been getting pizza and cheesesteaks at Padrino's for years.  The service is a little slow but always done with a smile.  The pizza is great.  I get take out as the place is usually too crowded for me.
This place is amazing! The food was incredible the staff were hospitable and the ambiance was perfect. I did the 9 course chef tasting option and loved everything, especially the bacon yakisoba!!

I have never, in my 67 years,  been thrown out of a restaurant! Well... that changed last Friday night when 7 of us went to Bacio to celebrate my daughter 's birthday. The food was mediocre at best... (and yes Jay I too am Italian) the pasta was from a box ... not homemade as stated, and under cooked...and the serving sizes were very inconsistent... but mostly small.
Having said all that, we were still making the best of the night as we were enjoying each other's company. Until that is the owner started screaming at the large table right next to us! Ultimately the customer he was yelling at was thrown out by the owner! We all agreed that was bizarre... until a short time later we heard the owner screaming at a woman at ANOTHER table!  By now we were beyond appalled....as he threw out this woman also!
The owner saw my daughter looking at him in shock so he proceeded to push the woman's plate of half eaten pasta in my daughters face yelling at her telling her to taste it!!
By now we had all had it... my daughter told him she had no intention of tasting it.... one thing led to another... he was now screaming at all of our table telling us to get out of his restaurant!! He threw a pad at my son and told him to write his name down (also gave him nothing to write with!) so he would never take his reservation again! As if we would go back!
What put me over the top is he made my grandson cry!! So I told him he was a poor excuse for a man let alone a restaurant owner... so he pushed me!! He put his hands on me and pushed me!
Fortunately I raised my son to be a good man and exercise restraint when needed as he wanted to deck him!! The owner then calls the police telling them we were refusing to leave! All we were doing at that point was making sure we gave our waiter Ken, who was awesome, a great cash tip !
The police came and after a brief statement asked me if I would like to press charges against the owner for assault... I declined as I never want to see his face again in or out of his restaurant!
Please heed my advice(and The several other reviews that are similar.... NEVER GO THERE! If you need further proof... read not only other negative reviews... but the owner's crazy replies!

Second time eating here and it was just as  as last time! Chicken Marsala dumplings and crispy wings on point, followed by a tasty serving braised pork cheeks and oxtail ramen. Banana bread pudding w/ walnut praline ice cream for dessert. This place is amazing!

Don't stay here! The hot tub didn't work and we reported it to the front desk immediately. We were told that it has' not worked for awhile! The room was like a motel six room. So disappointed for what we paid for this room. We did not even stay the night, we left after two hours in the room. We left at 6:30.

We picked this place via yelp simply because the photos of the food looked so good! Not only did the food live up to the photos but the taste was outstanding. The fish and chips were to die for. The staff was friendly as well. 12/10

I have been to the TacoBus (the original location only) a dozen times. I've had everything on the menu. I love it. I take everyone who will come with me so they can love it too. The staff is always happy and helpful. We have never had a bad experience. Open insane hours to calm your craving when you're in the area. 
Yeah, it seems sketchy... But its wonderful! Go to the Yellow bus to order and the White bus makes the goodies. You can even score a table inside and get a server to take your order if you feeling fancy. 
My favorite.... Heck y'all.... I love it all. Carne Asada, Cochinita Pibil, and tonight I got the Spicy Chicken! But my go to was the Chipotle Chicken. I've had the grouper and the shrimp... I think I have had everything but the tofu and tempeh. The house red or green salsa is banging (especIally the green if you like spicy.) I love the vegetarian rice and beans and the cheese is so fresh and melty! The Horchata is the best I have had EVER! I love this place... I tell everyone I love this place.... Then they eat here and they love this place too! I can't even deal with thread to have to drive 150 miles from Jacksonville to love this place.

Denise was our waitress at Metro Diner and we were very happy.  Not only did she give too noch service but her up beat personally was awesome.   She was so attentive to our orders never had to wait for a refill.  The turkey plate was delicious.  We enjoyed our time here so much we went back the next day... Too bad we live in NY otherwise we would eat here every day..
Best bagel place ever.  Warning: their bagels are so good that it is hard to stop at one.  This place is the closest thing to a New York bagel in the tri-county area(bucks, montco and philly)

Yummm. We came here out of desperation of Mexican goodness and this place delivered. The food was delicious and the service was great! Our chips and salsa never ran out as they continually were refilling. All of our meals were very good. I got the build your own burrito and it was sooo much food. Which I'm honestly okay with because now I have lunch for tomorrow. The atmosphere was also really great which is a huge make or break for me. We'll definitely be back.

Went for lunch yesterday because it's fried chicken day and my spouse loves the bird on the bone.  At 12:45 line was short, though seats were scarce.  The chicken wasn't crispy but did taste good, the sides were good except I prefer my mashed potatoes a little chunky not so smooth, but that's just me. Meat and two for two was $15.xx before tip, so in today's market not bad. I would go back but probably wouldn't make a special trip.

Ordered a quesadilla and small queso this afternoon. All appeared to go well except I did not receive my receipt. I did not think too much of it and took my food and left. Get home. The quesadilla was ok but the queso cup was filled with cheese on top and SOUR CREAM HALF WAY DOWN. I am totally ticked off. Why would someone do that? I did not find it amusing and will frequent the Moes here in Nashville from now on. Any server who would do that would do other things to your food. A young Caucasian and a Latina young lady were the servers. I guess it was some joke on a black woman. Anyway, I did NOT recommend this place~!

This place is too cool. Love the atmosphere. The decor is really funky - trombones, figurines and even a stuffed armadillo holding a beer bottle. The food was tasty. We had drunk chicken, red beans n sausage, jambalaya, and the white chicken chili. All served w rice. I'll be back again.

I was craving for soon dubu so I ended up here late on a Thursday. (Not the best time of the day to go eat soft tofu soup since the broth is likely to be more salty). The host, who probably had a long day didn't utter a word or smile at us walked toward a table by the window and placed down two menus. (Asian services I suppose). Anyway, food was good and spicy. My mushroom tofu soup could use more mushrooms and of different variety. I was surprised when the waitress asked if I wanted rice with my soup. My soon dubu always come with rice. I also ordered dukbokki, which had an add on of ramen, but ended up with none. Lastly, the portion of the side dishes were so little, like real little. Did they ran out? For awhile now, I wanted to try the restaurant, but my friends gave me mixed reviews. In term of taste, variety of food, service and price. This is not going to be a regular spot to eat Korean food for me. Overall, Korean food in the city is dissapointing.

Food was decent, but service was not so great. Our waitress took a long time to take our order and didn't check back to fill up our drinks. It was a busy night but I've been in many places which are just as busy with better service. 

I did like the variety of menu options and the salad bar. My buffalo chicken tacos I'd say were a 4/5. Good and tasty. I'd come back for brunch if it's a buffet so we wouldn't have to wait.

Found this place via yelp by the reviews and it being outside the city. The staff is super friendly even when they are soo busy! The food was amazing! I definitely recommend the raw oysters if you are an oyster fan! Their crawfish is VERY authentic and delicious. My husband had blackened halibut and it was also to die for! Will be coming back!!

Most of the food is very tasty. But too much junk on the plate so one can not see what they are eating. Take off all the food decorations so one can see the beauty of the food and it will be top rated.
Not bad. Saw a review raving about the Cuban sandwich, it was ok. Burger was mediocre but the broasted chicken was really good. Service was pretty slow. Priced modestly.

WOW WOW WOW! My new favorite restaurant in Philly!! Took some family here when they were in town for the holiday and we were all blown away. It's super small and cute inside. Service was great, and all of the food was phenomenal! Love that it's byob too. This will be a staple from now on for sure!!

Went here based on other Yelpers reviews. This place is close to my new job and I've been looking for new places to try. Let's just say they didn't disappoint!! They are a food truck operating in the parking lot of the Comfort Inn hotel on Waters near Anderson Road. You walk up and place your order. They have seating available but it was a hot day in FL so we decided to get our food to go. Reasonable prices--about $8 for my pad Thai. Food prep takes about 10-15 minutes depending on your order. I had the tofu pad Thai which was so good. I like that it had a lot of sauce so that the noodles didn't get dried out. The flavor was spot on -- I ordered it medium spice and no bean sprouts. My friends ordered the shrimp fried rice and panang shrimp which they said were fabulous. The friend that ordered fried rice isn't a fan of Asian cuisine and she raves about how good this rice was. So that says something. We will definitely be back here. And next time I'm getting the fried rice!

Yelpers Take Note Seafood by Crush Velvet has moved from their previous Belleville IL location and are now open in their new STL Location at 1317 Washington Ave St Louis Mo!
 (The Former Side Bar Location) 
While Crushed Velvet are still ironing out some of the details of moving to a new location and all the logistics and challenges involved 
*Seafood by Crushed Velvet has some major potential to be the "go to" seafood spot in St Louis. I suspect will have a major increase in business once discovered by those roaming eateries along Washington Ave. (Look out when the weather warms up!)
The restaurant:
Think casual, and at this time food is served in to go containers....which is ok by me. (Note many other local eateries serve all sorts of foods, BBQ,Chicken etc on a cookie sheet like pan, so for this type of restaurant,it works) 
I can tell they are doing their best to get up and running and make it all "happen"
Flavors are good with a definite cajun feel.
First owner Jasmine gave us a sample of the crab balls....Nice Touch! 
 Panko type battered crab balls with a nice crunch, drizzled with a spicy mayo type sauce with a rich cheesy center. (yes I would order these)
Entrees We had the following
Her: The Crab Leg Platter which includes 2 clusters of Snow Crab Legs and Shrimp served over new potatoes,sausage a hardboiled egg and Corn on the cob
Mine: Given I'm alergic to Shrimp (not severely) owner Jasmine graciously suggested a Crab Leg and Lobster Tail Combo (One Cluster of Snow Crab Legs and a decent sized Lobster tail) again over new potatoes,sausage,hard boiled egg and corn. ($29 pp)
I noticed some comments re price in other reviews.... 
I'm not sure what they are talking about because newsflash!  You would easily spend this much if you went to a local grocery store and cooked it yourself not including any of the side items! Seafood is Not Cheap!

I hope to see Jasmine and Co really make the most out of the many possibilities this location/building has.
 Great Bar Area with hightop seating, again a casual atmosphere and a stage which she states they plan to have music and possibly comedy!

Is it perfect? No, and no place is, especially after a major move and getting everything ironed out, that being said I predict Seafood by Crushed Velvet will see Major Success in the future and I'm Confident Jasmine and Co can make it happen!

I ordered the Enchiladas Criollo. They were very good and tasted authentic. The portion size was great and managed to fill me up, the salsa was also very good and the rice complemented the enchiladas very well.

We were looking for somewhere interesting to eat in Nashville. Mme D and I had an excellent dinner there while on the outside deck on the second floor. It was a warm evening and it felt great to be outside. They have a wide selection of wines and other drinks. For an appetizer I selected the Carolina crab cake. It was a small and delicious. My entree was the yellowfin tuna - very good. 

We asked our waiter for recommendations for what else to do that evening - we went next door to The Station Inn to hear some live bluegrass and beer, and the next morning we went to the Pancake Pantry for some pancakes.
Adding a star. Frostop isn't perfect, but it is very good. Great simple burger joint. Don't know why I ever gave it three stars. Possible brain fart.

Food was very good and they have yum yum sauce! Super bonus. Most of the smaller Japanese on the go restaurants don't, and it's always disappointing. Good portions, fresh, light taste. Would definitely order from again and recommend if you're craving Japanese food and are looking for a quick carry out.
Honestly the best sunday brunch ever! Sea bass, crab, oysters, eggs benny, applewood bacon, bottomless mimosas, peach bellinis and much more! A must if your here.
Not bad at all for mall pizza. I haven't tried any of the other food there but people say it is pretty good. Rating this solely based on a comparison to other food in the mall.

Just moved to St. Louis & a friend of mine brought me here last night.  Very cute place with lots of character & great people watching!  We just had some drinks & a charcuterie plate which was good!  Definitely will be back, love the ambience!

First time trying this place after watching it being built.....first impressions,very nice and welcoming.No wait even for a Saturday evening which is surprising , but thought to our advantage .....food was lovely although not experienced with polish food , the chocolate mousse dessert was amazing and made for a great finish to the evening..the downside was the service was very slow even though it wasnt busy and rather pricy ....but will definitely go again ...even if its just for dessert !!

This is my first time here, having ordered one of the bowls recommended to me, I pratically swallowed it whole!! This place is great, and a nice change from traditional local flair. Give it a try, and let them order for you

To continue with the maturity and poor customer service someone from the deli reached out to me and maturely wrote, "YOU ARE AN A**HOLE!". I'm totally vindicated in banning this place. Good luck to you.

Food was great, service was poor.  We ordered our food 15 minutes before their kitchen opened at 4pm.  We ended up getting our food 30-40 mins later than everyone else who came after us.  After speaking to the manager/owner there was no apology other than letting us know our food should be ready soon.  Very disappointing!  Unfortunately this is the only Japanese store/restaurant around Indy.  Had this been in the west coast it would be the last time we come back to this place.

Great atmosphere.  Had a problem with the tomato soup that did not looked like the photo and did not taste like a tomato soup. But the Manager Stephanie saved the night. She brought me the perfect tomato soup. Kudos to the Manager!!!!

Wow... where do I begin?! Ordered though Uber eats on a Friday night. We Loved EVERYTHING we got. Indian Burger was super juicy and flavorful ( salivating just thinking about it lol ) . Got two poutines, one with saag paneer and the other with chicken Tikka. Hubby and I devoured everything!

Such a delightful experience. Kind and helpful owner greeted us. Delicious, fresh, and nutritious food served in a lovely outdoor patio. Enjoyed a Cobb salad and fresh bread with house made strawberry butter!

As a veteran Nashville Hot Chicken connoisseur,
 I have to say I was quite disappointed in Hattie B's chicken tenders today.
 they lacked flavor and really lacked the famous crunch that were all after when we have Nashville hot chicken. I truly hate to say it but they really didn't even taste like chicken.
 I won't comment on the spice level.
 Hattie B always has great sides,
 no complaint there,   but you guys need to up your game on your chicken fingers they were definitely not double-dipped crunch.
Food was not that Great. Waited 40 minutes to get seated.  Restaurant is very loud! Then waited 35 minutes to be served mediocre burgers. Complete waste of time.
My fiancee and I came here for lunch and loved everything. I got shrimp with garlic oil, rice & black beans and tostones. He got fried chicken, rice & red beans and tostones. Service was great!

Had brunch here on a Sunday afternoon for our girl's bach party :) 

Cool interior, music and atmosphere, food were decent, drinks were good and service was excellent. There was no wait for the table, and a short wait for food and drinks.

- Bloody Mary: loved
- Country Fried Bites: greasy
- Eggs Florentine: good and enjoyed the spinach cream glaze and potato pancake!
- Parmesan & truffle fries: good

One of the guys who worked there came by, chatted with us and gave us a background of the establishment...cool and interesting...

Waitress was quick and efficient. She even bought our bachelorette a shot of drink, so sweet!
You have to try the Asado Negro - never had anything like it. The service was excellent as well.

Food is good. But the amount is insanely less for the price. And the annoying bit is the rating is done on the basis of cost, and not the corresponding portion. Felt a bit fooled. Don't come here. Similar or better food daily available elsewhere

I like it there but if you yell out "hot bread"  then do not give me cold bread. This happened twice recently.
Maybe they should yell out: hot bread when we get around to slicing it.
Friendly & attentive staff. Lasagna noodles were soggy. Meat sauce was bland. I would expect this from Fazoli's. Not here.

Love eating a burger here.  I have ordered many of the different varieties of burgers and the daily special burger and am never disappointed. The shocker is exactly what it says, extremely hot (and I am a girl that loves some heat).  

This place is perfect to grab a quick burger and feet with friends, a causal low key night out or by yourself.  Nothing fancy, just a really cool laid back atmosphere.
Crowded and noisy... higher priced than comparable. The Griddle/ Terries and even the Bear always much better!!

I eat takeout here almost once a week. I always order their vegetable green curry with tofu. It's a huge container that you could have two dinners with or share it with someone, and it comes with rice.  Nice service.  I need to come here for dinner and have their whole fried fish.

I only ever get one thing here on my lunch break from work but I love it.  General Tso's Tofu, light sauce, extra spicy and the broccoli raw, if they can handle my special  needs I'm sure they can handle yours :D
The banana waffle is so good! This was our first time here and we will definitely be back. Very friendly staff and yummy food!

A small diner on the "English" side of Canal within easy walking distance of the French Quarter.  This is a place where "locals" mix with tourists. The food was good, wholesome and quick. Breakfast ends at 11:00 and lunch starts promptly at the same time. Service is friendly and the crew works to make you one of their family. Note they are only open until 2:30 so if you're close to closing, call ahead for take out.
Great food.... We've been going here for years. I usually get the chicken quesadilla and it is quite large. Their salsas are really good.

A beautiful little spot tucked away behind a McDonalds!  It's a great spot to come for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.  They make their own tortillas and you can tell when you taste them, so fresh!  They have a little bar there too, well stocked and have daily specials.  The portions are a bit on the small side but the food is good.  The restaurant is situated so that you can look out onto Tucson, very cool to see at night.

So good I had dinner and I went back for lunch the next day!

I was attending a conference at the conference center about 5 blocks away. I was sick and tired of eating the typical conference type food. I wanted a place that had a little passion and tasty food. Thank the Lord I found Cochon Butcher. 

I was beginning to think that New Orleans had lost it's soul over the years but after a nice hot sweaty walk to Cochon Butcher I was parched and hungry as hell. If you are squeamish about animal parts this might not be the best place for you. It is very much like a butcher. However there are meatless options on the menu if my memory serves me right. 

But this place is fantastic! It was oozing with charm and character. The food was creative and tasty. I am from Boston and live in SF. I was curious to know how locals are feeling 1 year after the oil spill. So I asked my server. Her response was "Folks are still F@#! PISSED!"

I respected the candor and ordered another beer!

What a quaint and tranquil atmosphere hidden in an industrial area! We enjoyed our breakfast burrito, breakfast tacos, avocado toast and blueberry muffin! We also had great iced coffees and lattes. (Family of 8) 
The trees outside in the sitting area are gorgeous and give enough shade. The inside is clean, and I love the true expresso machines. Our vegetarian brother who happens to be very picky with his food, LOVED the avocado toast and rated it a 10/10!
Hot Chicken was amazing.  Top 3 fried chicken I've had Great service and very hospitable.

Hospitality = 10 stars

The lady that took our order treated us like family. I swear it was like being in family's house. 

The pizza was yummy!! Crispy crust, loaded with pizza. I was a little shocked at our good luck. We are pretty picky with our pizza and being away from home, we were very happy with the food and service.

Epic Cafe-- ::sigh:: this place hits the sweet spot. I don't know if it's because I'm a caffeine junkie or just a big Epic groupie. This place spells love in my heart. Their vegan cookies and cakes are super yummy. I've had better in other cities-- but for a honky tonk town (yikes! this is where half of Tucson gets bitter)... the food aint bad. A little on the dry side, but when it's the only place out of like 2 that offer vegan delights, you realize quickly its the best.

People watching... more like swooning. Such a variety, such an awesome time. I once saw a man with a beret on his head made out of foil. Jealousy ensued and I came home wondering why I didn't ask him to marry me.

Don't try to flirt with the cute staff. They'll just want to quiz you on your hipsterness and proceed to tell you that you're not "hip" enough for your super hip Chrome messenger bag straight from hipster SF. (I wont get into what Tucson even knows about hipsterness). But that's probably what attracts me to this place even more... it has TONS of sub-culture character. 

Back to the coffee rather than Tucson bashing, I love their choices of loose tea. The cherry one was my favorite for probably half a year, until I couldn't refrain from their delicious coffee. Never burnt.. never watered down. 

Sometimes finding seats outside is hard... but finding a lighter to borrow is never an issue (the important things in life... I'll sit on the sidewalk as long as my ciggarette is lit). I can't really do homework in here. The music is too loud and the people are too weird or too damn cute.... I just stare and stare, getting absolutely nothing done.

Prices are written on a chalk board, which only screams at my inner repressed childhood youth. Something about smoking outside, people watching, streaming youtube off their free wi-fi.... and a DAMN good cup of coffee.... you can't beat Epic at ALL.

Tattoo Moms is a really cool place to visit if ever on South Street in Philadelphia. It is easily accessible right on South. The atmosphere is insane. It is very odd in a good way. They have several rooms upstairs and downstairs. The walls are decorated with just about anything you can imagine. It's a really cool vibe you get while walking around. The staff was friendly and helpful and it is kept very clean. 
The lunch we had was absolutely phenomenal. We had an array of different things and we were satisfied with just about everything. My Wife also had a few cocktails and she enjoyed all of them. We just popped in while walking around South street and I'm glad we did because we discovered a real hidden Gem. The waitress was very friendly and professional. The order was promptly delivered hot and tasty. We didnt wait long at all. She was very attentive to our needs and kept checking in on us. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to get off of the beaten path and wanted to try something new.

Probably my favorite restaurant in Broad Ripple. Great Staff and great food and wine selection. Always seem to have excellent features. Our server Samantha couldn't have been more accommodating and great. Keep it up!

Not sure how Yelp doesn't have this gem at 5 stars across the board.  Every dinner they serve is phenomenal, no exceptions.  Size portions are enough for 2 dinners and at a price that cannot be beat. Best Italian food in Bucks County second to Mom.

This place was recommended by my Uber driver, came here with my friend we got eggplant, the Dan Dan noodles and spicy tofu fish. Everything was great, especially the tofu fish dish, will come back for more noodles! stuff was friendly!

I thought this was average at best.  It was good chicken, but not fantastic.  I also thought it was a bit pricey.  I had the three-piece dark, which comes with two sides (about 1/2c each) and it was $9.95.  You could get a half-chicken at a locally owned place with larger sides (and better tasting) for $1-2 less.  I will say though, their French fries and coconut pie were fantastic.  

As a side-note, I'm not an environmental activist or anything, but I was a bit shocked they used disposable plates and utensils to serve food on.  I realize they are going for the southern roadside chicken-shack motif, but I was surprised in this day and age a business wouldn't have reusable dishes and utensils.

I figured I'd put up a review after another positive experience at this Chick-fil-A location. The staff is always pleasant, the service is fast and obviously the food is delicious. Can't get enough of the chicken strips and real ice cream milkshakes!
One of the best meals I've had. Service was great too. Delish, creative & topped off with superb desserts. If u have a sweet tooth & an appetite, order the S'more! It's insane.

JES,Kelly and Nicoles reviews from 2015 are spot on! 
It's a  pizzeria, Sandwich shop that steps out of the box with gluten free and vegan options. You don't come here for the decor you come here for the food. 
Great Delco staple I have been dining in for the last 10 years.It's homey. It's comforting and the food is quite simply really really really good food. 
Best meatballs in the burbs!!
Stop by you won't be disappointed

We ordered carryout tonight and it was fresh and hot upon arrival. It was plentiful for a reasonable price. It was delicious! The bread is eh but made me happy. The capellini com salsa marinara is good, but a lil spicy, although I liked it & my daughter didn't complain. I was slightly annoyed to see there was cheese on it as the menu said nothing about cheese & we're eliminating dairy from our daughters diet to test a sensitivity. I was able to eat around it, but I should've known it was on there. Much like the surprising heap of meat on the insalata cunetto. My husband took it all off, but it's cut small & was annoying. Again, my daughter & I are strict vegetarians and the salad description should include meat. Please be more descriptive on your online menu for the growing number of customers who rely on it. Other than that, yum! It's been awhile since I'd been, it's still good. And perfect amount of sauce!

Went here for dinner tonight - started with  6 oysters and an order of the white mussels. Both were very good, although a few of the mussels were a little gritty. I ordered the broiled seafood combo for my entree, it was served with mashed sweet potatoes and string beans. The seafood was very fresh, and the mashed sweet potatoes were also very delicious; I would order this entree again on our next visit. We arrived around 7:30, and it was very busy, I think all but one table was occupied and the seating area is a little tight. Our server was nice, and the hostess who seated us also checked in on us multiple times too - she was very nice as well. Reasonable prices, delicious food in a convenient location. Definitely will return again soon.

4 stars because the Pho is authentic and delicious. To me an authentic restaurant like Pho An Hoa must first and foremost deliver an excellent product. The customer service in this case is truly secondary in my opinion, unless it's just awful- which it wasn't by any means.

The food is wonderful and delicious. Only one other Pho restaurant in the Tampa area has gotten our approval. We ordered the Pho Ga with Shrimp, 2 orders of fresh rolls and Pho Bo. 

Each bowl of Pho was full of noodles and the protein's. The expected plate of sprouts, basil, lime and jalapeños was plentiful!  The broth was tasty without being overly salty at all.

The fresh rolls were tasty and indeed fresh. Chock full of pork, shrimp, noodles and veggies. Of course the accompanying hosin sauce was great too.

I found the server- though only one- to be very attentive and sweet. We will most assuredly return to this restaurant.
Alway looking for good pho restaurant no matter where im at :) best pho noodle in town5

Delicious & a nice variety of options for every diet. Only open on Sundays, though, but they do have a seasonal menu that changes each month. I ordered the waffles with lemon curd, fresh blueberries, and Missouri pecans - absolutely amazing! They definitely do not skimp on the lemon curd or drizzle of maple syrup. Would highly recommend getting there on the early side, as table space is limited inside and filled up quickly. They do have patio seating outside once it warms up, too!

If you are looking for some good smoked "BBQ" you MUST try Smokin' Out. For quite some time I've driven by with my husband and we said, "We need to try that." On August 18th, 2012, we made a point to head there for dinner. We are so glad that we did!

The appearance of the place is very casual. The selections of sizes is nice but standard BBQ joint fair (side salad, potato salad, coleslaw, corn on the cob etc.). I was undecided on what meat I wanted to try so I chose the Combo Meal and picked pulled Pork and 1/4 chicken (white meat). OMG, it was so delicious. My husband selected the chopped chicken, mac - n - cheese and the garlic bread. He loved the chicken so much that he ordered a whole chicken to go!

The pulled pork was so amazing that I didn't add any sauce to it! (Just like their slogan!) The smoke flavor added so much taste to the meat it was great! 

I highly recommend Smokin' Out to anyone. This is our new BBQ place over our local Sonny's BBQ. Smokin' Out blows them away!

I've been here two times. The first was probably 3 years back, and the other time was yesterday! When I came a few years ago, I cannot remember what exactly I ordered (but I remembered loving it).

I think the reason it's taken me so long to venture back to this spot is that it's location is clear across town for me. Luckily, yesterday I was running some errands for work and just so happened to be in the neighborhood. It was about 2 pm and my hanger was starting to set it, so I did what any hangry person would do...I set out in search of a sammie.

As soon as I realized my craving, the heavens split open and behold...Great Harvest Bread Co. I stopped in, ordered a cold sammie (the Baja Chipotle Turkey), checked-in on Yelp (and got a free cookie for it, hola!), and left with my on-the-go lunch in a matter of 8 minutes. Now it's not Jimmy John's fast, but for the quality of food, that is not an issue for me!

I ordered a half sandwich and this was more than enough food (especially with that giant cookie I got for checking in). The sammie was yummy, veggies piled on and crisp, turkey was piled on generously, bread was fresh, and the condiments that came with it were tasty. I'd love to go back and try out a hot sammie when I have time to sit down and enjoy it on their little patio. 

Overall, great experience! Friendly service, great quality food, and a lot of bang for your buck! I'll come back, and when I do....I'm coming for that Turkey Pesto sandwich I spotted on the menu!

I stopped by before leave NoLa. You have to order your food and then if you want to stay there then you can but you have to fine a seat yourself when one opens up. The ham is the thing that people talk about the most. It is pretty good. The bread pudding was good but very sweet.

I thought it was excellent.  The place was packed when we got there, which is always a good sign.  They were very accommodating, and we didn't have to wait too long for a table even without a reservation.  The waiter was very friendly, yet very professional and knowledgeable.  The ossobucco  was excellent.  The tiramisu was divine.  I would highly recommend this restaurant.

Think Chipotle for Poke.

Not bad, but certainly not as good as the Hawaiians .

Choose you own ingredients by shouting across a counter.  Lettuce and cucumbers were old and dried out.

That said - I could see myself returning if I worked nearby for a healthy lunch option. Wouldn't go out of my way otherwise to eat here again.

Mediocre at best.

We were hunting down a new place to try....Ulele came up on the list.  We were very pleased.  Comfortable surroundings, friendly staff & really good food.  A very busy place.... we hung around for a bit to get seats at the bar.  Worth the wait. Hubby ordered their hamburger and I ordered the grilled oysters with parmesan.  Both were very good.  Hamburger was large and properly cooked as ordered.  We'd go back in a heart beat next time in Tampa area.

Craving some cheesy triangle-shaped deliciousness, we opted to check in here on our way up the 101.  We were ready for the best pizza ride of our lives with all the yelpers' claims that this is SB's pizza mecca.  Well, I regret to announce that SB does not know pizza!  (maybe this is common knowledge to others, but we were sad to learn it only recently.)  The Margarita could maybe pass as the best college cafeteria pizza, but that's about it.  Maybe good for a slice on the run when you need a quick fix, but not for a whole pie.

Much better than expected due to its location! The sushi was very good for a decent price. We also got the pork dumplings for an appetizer and they were so good! Paid around $16 for the appetizer and two rolls (16 pieces total). Plus you get a 5% discount for paying with cash.

I held my husband's surprise birthday party for about 35 people in the basement bar at Black Sheep. I couldn't have asked for a better experience. From the first call I placed to inquire about hosting the party and spoke with James, the owner, to the night of the party where Adam, our bartender, made sure all went smoothly, everyone I dealt with was fantastic. Overall, a great experience.
I got the impossible Philly sandwich on a pretzel bun and it was sooo freaking good. I wish I took a pic before devouring it lol. I will most definitely be back again.
My girl Carla sent me here, and I throat-punched Charlene. She was an a terrible employee anyway. It was all run-down and the bathrooms were crappy.

Always a favorite! Long overdue review. Might be the best ramen in philly, always flavorful, hearty, great quality and fairly priced! Overall clean restaurant with clean and spacious bathrooms that smell really good. Wait time for seating and meals are short. Great spot for a quick lunch during work hours. Will definitely recommend and be back.

Terrible. Wanted a quick in and out lunch while babysitting a three and four year old. Mostly I like Wendy's because they have a great menu with healthier options. This Wendy's, quite frankly, b.l.o.w.s. Their lines were backed up both inside and out. The bathrooms were so dirty, as were the tables. Our food took thirty-five minutes!! If we hadn't had kiddos with us who were hungry, I would have left but that was not an option. We did receive a refund after asking, at least. But were given no explanation and/or apologies for the long wait and delay. I will not be going back to this particulatar Wendy's again. Ever.
Love there brick oven pizza. Plus if you sit outside on a Saturday you have perfect seats for music on main.

First off, I didn't have the pizza or dine in.  A friend and I went to try their desserts, which we got to go.  That being said, there isn't a sign (and for some reason addresses on buildings are elusive in Tucson) so we actually passed it a few times before finally locating Anello.  They also don't have a phone so you can't call for directions.  The interior of the restaurant is very small but crisp and clean feeling with intimate lighting.  I think there are six or seven four person tables.  The place smelled amazing though.  I definitely will go back to try the pizza, which you can see being made and baked in a really cool looking oven. 

The rye brownie is pretty darn tasty, but is covered in nuts.  I'm not a fan of nuts anywhere near a baked good so had I known I would've asked for the brownie sans nuts.  Did that stop me from eating it?  Nope - absolutely not.  There is some sort of sea salt either in the brownie or on top of it that adds great flavor.  My friend got the flourless almond cake (also covered in nuts, but she loves nuts on baked goods) and said it was really good, with some sort of orange honey glaze on top.

Basically, be prepared to make a bunch of u-turns as you try to find this place, and if you don't like nuts be sure to let them know.

Very good ramen spot. The restaurant manager was super attentive and thoughtful. Also a great people watching spot if you sit outside. My husband had the chicken Ramen, it was just the right balance and not spicy. I had the braised short rib which was fantastic - perfectly cooked. Highly recommend if you want something with a little more kick. All in all a great spot.

I had dinner here on a whim recently and found it good, but not necessarily worth the hype. The restaurant is nice enough and has a varied menu, but it is fairly casual American fare. I will say that the service was attentive. Overall, everything was decently priced and well presented, so it's a good choice for a casual dinner, but nothing to write home about.

Sometimes despite the best of intentions you end up dining at a tourist trap. And perhaps that's the price you have to pay for a meal over the French Quarter on a sunny balcony.

Sunny indeed, as my 4 travel companions and I were unfortunately seated on an awkwardly shaped long table with direct sun exposure. It's unclear to me why ownership decided to leave a few tables without umbrellas - we were told they could not accommodate a shift to a more comfortable space.

I ordered the vegetarian latkes, which were OK. My love for Gujarati food prepared me well for the sweetness that seems inherent in some Creole cooking. But I took issue with the carrots on the side, which were an unsettling mix of tender and hard.

We unanimously agreed the best part of the meal was the incredibly rich butter that came with the baguette. If anyone knows what brand they use, do send me a message.

Impressive! This place is very clean and welcoming. Staff is friendly and bartenders are knowledgeable and skilled at there craft! The food was delicious! Perfectly cooked burgers and the fries were seasoned and I didn't even need salt! They also use a seasoned catchup that was really good!

Pretty close to a 5 star experience! When I'm back in town I'll certainly keep this as a lunch or dinner option!

Kids enjoyed the games but that's about where the enjoyment stopped. The pizza is some of worst in St. Louis, the bud light draft tasted like lines hadn't been cleaned in a year, and the sweet tea was by far the worst tea I've ever drank and it's something I order everywhere. Staff was very accommodating however and kudos to them for caring in that environment. Was in general a very dirty place as well which is a huge turn off when trying to enjoy a dining experience. Won't be back for sure.

Great place to catch a game and have some drinks. This has definitely been one of my spots over the years! Great beer selection and friendly service. Big fan of the flatbread pizzas, specifically the spicy Thai pizza.

Pascale's Manale is the perfect embodimentm of the Creole-Italian mixture. I hate to beat a dead horse, but the BBQ shrimp are great and oughn't be missed (unless you have the opportunity to eat some home cooked ones instead). I had the fine pleasure of showing up on an evening when the special was fried drum toped witht he BBQ shrimp. it was amazing. The tender fish was swimming in the butter sauce. The waitress made sure we ALWAYS had pleanty of french bread at the table to soak up the wonderful sauce.

If you are staying in the quarter (even though you really should be staying up river of canal), its a 20 minute street car ride ($1.25) away; its a block away from the stop at Napoleon (the halfway stop).

Cool little spot. Jessa our bartender was super funny and made bomb bloody Mary's and Moscow mules. Recommend this spot if your walking around magazine street and your in need for some good laughs and affordable cocktails. 
5 stars!!!!

Awesome sauce, literally. 
They have Greek food, BBQ, pizza, tacos, ice cream, and a butcher shop. It's a good mix of food and portions for the most part are big, only thing I would say is needed is a few more options like Asian foods and sandwiches. 
Give it a shot
The owner made us feel at home. The chili dog and the Italian beef sandwich were both fantastic. I'm glad we stumbled upon this place. Definitely hit the spot.

Hat Date #1

The only strike against this place is that it is on South Grand, so it basically feels like you are walking into an American Apparel advertisement photo shoot.  On the other hand, it is located on South Grand, which is the hub of Asian food restaurants in the area as far as I am concerned.  So you really almost can't go wrong in choosing a restaurant in this area.  And Lemon Grass is no exception to that rule. They have reliably decent service, and really good food.

The Restaurant: is a casual sit down place.  They have a good number of tables, and I have never been there with a wait of more than a few minutes.  With the number of tables they have, it always seems quiet in here.  Basically unless you try not to, you are going to hear the conversation at the next table because there is just no white noise.

Service: So its reliable.  But its not great.  The servers are prompt, polite and as far as the amount of service you expect from a place like this right on par.  They seem disinterested, but on the flip side and preferred by me, they are not hovering around asking you how every thing is all the time.  But they didn't let my water glass go empty either.  

Food: I have had a few things here, and as with many Vietnamese food restaurants, the menu is a bit long.  I suggest you pick a section first, then look at the food listings, or it can be overwhelming.  Also good, you can order by number.  I have always wondered which makes me seem more like a dumb American, ordering by number or mispronouncing the names?  Either way, they will figure it out.  And the food is good.  You have a selection from soups to stir fries.  I enjoy the pho here, but most recently tried the Hot and Sour soup.  Not really sure what to expect, having had Chinese hot and sour soup, and knowing the flavors of pho, but this soup delivered a series of flavors that were a bit sweet, and to bring it up to a spicier level, I added hot sauce.  We also ordered Crab Rangoon, which honestly is a food I don't know how to compare, because though I enjoy it, I don't really get it as a food... 

Anyway, overall I will be going back to this restaurant a few times.  You get a good amount and quality of food here, but that is because you really are not paying for an atmosphere or service, just bare bones in those departments.  But the next time I am craving the hipster paradise I have always dreamed of being a part of, you can find me here.

They finally accept credit cards but the original Parasols is good but not as good as it's still standing neighbors down the street. At the current Parasols the bread is bigger and toasted with garlic herb seasoning which puts it ahead of Tracey's. Tracey's was good but not as good as around the corner as far as the roast beef is concerned. If I come here again I will try one of the other sandwiches that look great. It is though a great place to hang out and watch a game so on that and decent food it get 4 stars. An update will be made at my next time passing through.
Exceptional Italian food with a small bill at the end. :) Pizza is good but their entrees are exceptional.
I'm a "JerseyBoy" and bagels make my day. MFM is my starting point for each day... their bagels, service and friendliness are a welcomed beginning for my adventures, in Reno !
Wraps are very hearty and good flavored. Smoothies are fresh and satisfying. A little off the main road but once you find it its worth the trip. Excellent for a light lunch or dinner

A hidden gem?  This Tucson brewery is relaxing and the beer is good.  I ordered the Copperhead Pale Ale and the wife had the Hola Hefeweizen after a very informative waitress provided answers to all of our questions.

The food was beautifully presented for a brewery...and the flavors popped in my mouth!  I had the Phoenix sandwich, which had s a succulent chicken breast, bacon, and Italian red peppers.  My  wife had a salad, the Lizzie.  With chicken, bacon, and fresh greens, the salad also was a pleasure to consume.  Good food, service, and reasonable prices...overall...a great experience!

We ordered delivery online. It came quickly. We upgraded to the full order of ribs. They arrived and it was smaller than a half a rack of ribs. I called the location explained this to the manager and he could not have cared less. He said our full order of ribs have six bones and they are very expensive

I purchased a cake from here for my 40th birthday which cost $220.00.  The day I arrived to pick up the cake, the young lady that assisted me only opened the top of the box to show the cake and from what I saw from that view, I was satisfied. I arrived home and decided to fully take a look and found, running down the bottom layer of the cake, smack in the middle was a clear, very visible, hardened drip mark!  In addition, the loops in the bow that was on front of the cake were uneven!  I chose to not even complain about that, but after paying what I did, the cake should have been perfect!  The pic of the cake is pictured as my profile pic, as I couldn't figure out how to add the pic any other way.

Whoever prepared and boxed this cake HAD to see this very visible drip mark down the center, but they chose not to do anything about it!  I immediately called, explained and was told to bring the cake back in to have them fix it.

I arrive and after waiting 5 or so minutes, the cake decorator presents the cake to me and it was unacceptable.  Yes, she removed the clear drip mark, but the indentation of the mark was still there and the icing covering it was discolored and did not match the rest of the cake!  I told her I was not happy with this, as I paid over $200 for the cake and she needed to go back and do a better job of "fixing" it.

She then took it back and I waited around for another 40-50 min.  Not sure exactly what they did, but the cake was presented again in an okay condition that I just had to accept because I had somewhere else to be.  The indentation of the drip mark was gone and the icing was all the same color.  But, I could tell they had to remove the top layer to achieve this and in the back of my top layer there was discoloration/damage to the icing!  Again, not what I expected after paying $200+!

After all of this, I was not given an apology, offered a discount on my cake, gift card, pastry, NOTHING!!!  I was highly disappointed in the extremely poor customer service I received.  I will not be ordering anything from them again.

It's so comforting when I'm on vacation and stumble upon something that I would eat at home. The space is large and open with plenty of seating for a quick meal. The staff accommodate dietary restrictions and allergies without issue- it's one of those places you feel safe eating when you're allergic to more foods than not. 

The smoothies are refreshing- had the berry bucha with coconut milk. The açaí bowl was a balance of tart and sweet- a little too soupy, but still tasty and filling. The rainbow salad topped with eggs was a satisfying breakfast. The wellness topped with eggs is a hearty and warm breakfast. Both would make good lunches or dinners. 

I will definitely be back for some matcha or chia pudding tonight.

DolsotBibimbap ,Galbi Ribs, Beef Bulgogi, Ddeokboki( Spicy Rice Cakes)Jap Chae, a handful of hot and Spicy Soups to choose from and Soju to wash it all down with! I love going from 11-2 and getting the lunch boxes which include 2 fried pork Dumplings . Great selection of kimchi included with all entrees.. Enough said.. This is my favorite Korean Restaurant in Tampa!

The best Sicilian pizza with extra sauce was delivered to me this eve. It came hot and fresh with a great amount of cheese. Delivery man used excellent touch-less delivery method! You can tell the team is conscious of maintaining great sanitation standards!

That pizza was the best thing that happened this week! Thanks team at Giovani's for putting a smile on this world worn face. The world would be infinitely worse without good Sicilian pizza and Giovani's nailed it!

Thursday are half off seafood! Food was good for the price! Service was good. The only thing is that I felt the soft shell crab was a bit over cooked for my taste. Will definitely come back for Thursday's half off seafood deals! Overall a good place for a nice dinner with friends!

Went there during coolinary month. It was delicious! We went with 2 other couples. We had the thin, crispy onions rings, wedge salad, steak (choice of center cut or filet) & plenty of sides. Our sides included crab meat a gratin (full of crab... they didn't hold back), potatoe wedges which were tasty, creamed spinach & potatoes augratin. I have never had spumoni but it was really good! I wound definitely go back & it's definitely worth it! Excellent wine & beer selection along with fabulous service.

Should be called BLAND mkt eats.  How do you have an unseasoned fried chicken tender in a wrap?   Tasted like I was eating at Karen's cooking, the same lady that adds raisins to her potato salad.  Whomp whomp.  Won't be back.............the woman ahead of us was offered a free drink and the guy behind her was offered free chips, but we weren't asked at all, and it was also our first time.  Also our last. :)

We had a party of 12 we all needed separate checks cause we all had a pay with cards and they said they don't do that and the waitress and manager gave us attitude and said we do not know how hard this business says. They just us because we were young and dressed in gym clothes we where only there for 5 mins and to just give the waitress a heads up to try and make it easy for her now and not at the end then she turned in to a bitch and gave us a attitude so we want to talk to the manager then he gave us a cocky attitude and talked down to us so we said fine will take are money somewhere els and we won't come back

My YELP friends and associates I have an announcement. This fabulous gem of a restaurant that I have been enjoying for decades closes its' doors tomorrow night. The place we know is going dark. It is my understanding that the business will open in the new year under new ownership.

Grew up wining and dining at Feeling's my adult life. And I married the love of my life at Feeling's in April of 2013. 

Life moves on but the memories will never die.

So far I've been to Hiro's twice - once the first week they were open, and then again last night.  The service has been good both times -- the staff is fast and friendly.  Hiro's also has nice ambiance - its fresh and funky but quiet enough that you can actually carry a conversation.

The food is pretty good as well.  Both times we had primarily sushi -- I can vouch for the Tuna Tacos, Tuna TarTar, Spicy Tuna (geeze, can you tell we love Tuna?), Golden Child and Crispy Lotus Chips.  The quality of the fish is good (not amazing, but  what one would expect at this price point.)  The execution of the sushi improved between the first time we went and our last visit.  

My only complaint is that the menu seems to be very shellfish heavy.  My fiancee doesn't do shellfish, so that does put some limitations on what we can order.  But, I will be back...and even more frequently if they expand their selection of maki!  :D

Our Nashville stay was only a few days long, and Oak was chosen because it had been a long day & the restaurant was attached to the hotel. That turned out to be a stroke of fortuitous proximity, and I wish it was closer to home so we could easily visit again.  The 16 ounce ribeye was cooked perfectly medium-rare, and our server, Courtney, was absolutely fantastic in every way, and worth a star on this rating by herself. Seriously. No Courtney? Then this is a 4/5 rating. She recommended the bacon plate as a starter, and if your server does the same, take them at their word. My spritely burst of a partner had the vegetable entree and loved every bite. Overall, very good food & even better service.

Arrived early evening pre-show dinner. Attractive restaurant clean.  Young upbeat staff very attentive. Great for brunch   Fantastic wings omg it was like a religious experience, salad, tacos and burger all very good.
Yes my dinner was destroyed in the kitchen by burning. But! Still love the music .love the dinner rolls and the bang bang shrimp.
Closed an hour before closing time. No signs posted. Person still working but literally went MIA. Window was left open and the person's car was still in the parking lot. Very unprofessional.

Had the meatloaf sandwich and the turkey pesto wrap! Loved it and locally sourced food! The chips are crunchy. I brought my brother here from out of town and he loves the local food everything is locally sourced way cool check it out

Katie's Pizzeria is a beacon in the dark abyss of mediocre St. Louis pizza. Katie's makes their dough daily, it is light and airy, with a great flavor....simplicity. The Potato pizza is my favorite, the combination of slightly crispy potatoes and prosciutto is mouth watering.  I love the hummus and Italian Chopped salad.   We bring our three boys in regularly, it is their favorite place also!

A perfect day to drive out of our comfort area,  and try a new lunch place

It's a good 15-20 min. drive, so since I'm always the driver I chose here. 

I called in two orders of teriyaki chicken with Mac salad, and one spam musubi.

We arrived within ten minutes from the time I called.

It's hard to review for take out only.

Wanted to eat it while it was warm, so we just had lunch in the car.

We both liked it a lot, the food and the flavors were spot on. The only disappointment was the chicken not being like it just came off the grill temperature wise..

Also I like my musubi, with a  minimal a rice and plenty of sauce.. unfortunately it had neither.. too much rice and no sauce..

Glad we were able to try it with everything going on.
This hotel is well-kept and functional.  The room was clean and the service was very good.  If you're visiting the U of A, you can't beat the location.

My husband and I traveled an hour to have dinner here tonight for the first time, and it was absolutely worth it! The salad bar was decent, I loved the lobster bisque. Once we flipped our cards from red to green, the meat fest began! I especially loved the top sirloin, filet mignon and sausage. The cheese bread was wonderful too. For dessert I got the cheesecake, which was the best I've ever had! We came tonight because my husband is a veteran and they were gracious enough to offer 50% off for veterans and a guest, which was extremely king and generous. We will definitely be visiting again!

Big AL's BBQ is open but at a new location on hwy 109. They give large sides an top notch BBQ pork,brisket and ribs. Very nice staff . Brisket was moist an ribs also coleslaw was mayo style great potato salad was homemade along with all the other sides go check it out
Good oysters at a reasonable price.  Fried shrimp and oyster po'boy was really good too.  Definitely a place worth checking out.
The location not as busy than the one in Clearwater.  The coffee and cream are not all ready at 8'ish am the peak time.  The staffs are friendly though.  Coffee doesn't taste as good as used to be.

While I mostly enjoyed what I had at Roscoe's Tacos, I think the word 'bland' comes to mind first. I'm new to Roscoe's and wanted to try a few different things to see what was good. I ordered a #3. Mike Fink shredded chicken burrito, a side of black beans and rice and drink, I also added a Lil beef taco. I started with the Lil Beef Taco. Normally I don't prefer hard shell tacos, but this was quite good. For its size and price I was pleased with the amount of shredded beef it had. The side of black beans and rice were nice and cheesy but lacked much flavor. I added quite a bit of the Texas Brushfire sauce to them as I ate. Finally, I moved on to the burrito. It was a good size burrito, filled with a lot of chicken and a good amount of extras (lettuce, tomato, cheese, etc.). The shredded chicken was disappointing. There was no flavor at all and fairly mushy. I added a lot of sauce to this burrito as I ate. I understand why restaurants have to make things palatable for a broad range of customers, but mushy, bland chicken isn't appealing to anyone. 

That said, the shredded beef was enough to make me want to come back and order something different. Next time I'll just avoid the chicken.

My wife and I came here for breakfast multiple times during our stay at Peddler's Village. We had vouchers for free breakfast as part of a deal with the Golden Plough Inn, so I can't speak to prices. The restaurant is directly connected to the Inn, which makes it very convenient for those staying in the village. The breakfast menu was limited, but everything we tried was very good. My wife loved the home fries, as did I. The eggs were cooked perfectly, and the pancakes (which I had on a different day) were quite good. We would definitely consider coming back here for breakfast, should we be staying in town at a future date.

If I could have given less than 1 star I would have.   Worst service ever!   Order arrived wrong, they would not answer phone so we drove up there.  After being inside this place there's no way I would eat anything from here!!   After arguing with multiple "managers" on the phone I finally received a refund.   Save your money.  Mcdonalds would be a better option than this dump!!!

I've been going for a very long time and almost all the time I've been there they always end up giving me something different, i'd ask for a spicy and they would give me mild and vise versa and it gets annoying. Today i went and ask for 3 chicken tenders they gave me chicken breast instead, and the girl that works at the drive thru is very rude.
Unbelievable great Food!!It's been a while since we tried Wolf Street everything was good !!It was a pleasure talking to Joanne your great service

*** NICE ATMOSPHERE ***... If you are looking for a really hip place to hang out this spot is it.  

Great atmosphere and decent food but still lacking in a few key areas... Service and Sound... 

After over a year in business you would think things would have gotten better in the SERVICE department but it doesn't appear so...  I wouldn't go as far as to say the SERVICE is horrible, but the staff even though very polite is noticeably under trained.  With a decor as nice as the Rustic Goat offers you would think the staff would be equal to the appearance.  Not so.  Service is slow to none existent....

If you enjoy live music the Rustic Goat is the spot... Serious talent... Only issue is the SOUND... Don't plan on conversing too much while the artists are performing your words won't be audible....

As you see the complaints don't stray too far from each review... St. Louis needs a spot like the Rustic Goat... It's my hope that the owner(s) view this page and fix what is easily fixable...
Food is really good. Margs are amazing. The outside tables seem to be spaced out for COVID. Service was great. The GM Tony was super nice. Def will be coming back.

Seated very promptly, lovely dining experience. First time dining at this location. Lettuce wraps, terrific as always. Honeydew walnut shrimp, seabass, asparagus , all amazing! Will make the 4 hour drive here again because the food is incredible and wonderful service.

I've been here twice now, and I'm still trying to wrap my head around it. In short, the food and vibe are great, the service is not, and the prices are high. They're at a 3 right now, with room to grow to a 4 if they can work out some kinks, or a 5 if they work out those kinks and lower their prices.

MENUS (3.5 stars):

The food that I've eaten has been a 4.5, but getting there is a little tricky, as the menus are confusing to navigate. They have a bar snacks menu, which overlaps with the appetizers section of the main menu. Most of the main menu is what many would call fusion cuisine. Many of the small plates and mains are familiar western dishes with Indian flavors and ingredients. They also have a traditional "Desi Fare" section of the menu where you choose your protein and curry, but these dishes are overpriced.

Rounding out the menu, they have a daily meat & three. Admittedly, I haven't tried this yet, as it's hard to justify the price tag, but I can't imagine this sticking around as a successful staple of the restaurant. It seems like one gimmick too many. Let's delete this and simplify the options.

FOOD (4.5 stars):

The food has been great. So far, I've stuck with the small plates and bar snacks.

The best thing I've tried has been the garam masala pork belly, served with simple greens and fresh apple and radish. The chunks of belly were crispy and caramelized on the outside and wonderfully melt-in-your-mouth on the inside.

They have their take on both fish and chips and Nashville-style hot chicken (of course). The fish and chips were okay, but the fish was sadly pretty limp. I expect more of a crunch from fish and chips. The hot chicken is quite good, though hardly authentic - the ghost pepper dipping sauce was the best part.

Other good snacks include the tandoori chicken poutine (amazing!), the kale parkora chaat (lightly battered, well-seasoned kale chips), and the black eyed peas tikki (black eyed pea cakes with cucumber raita for dipping).

DRINK (3.5 stars):

For an "ale" house, I was surprised that their beer selection wasn't more extensive. You can enjoy a relatively small array of craft beers and traditional Indian beers (e.g. Kingfisher), but the thing to try is their custom beers brewed in cooperation with Cool Springs Brewery (e.g. Garam Masala Ale, Chai Milk Stout, and Saffron Cardamom IPA). They also have some nice inventive cocktails at the going rate of $10-12 per quaff.

AMBIANCE & DECOR (4.5 stars):

It's nice in here. The vibe is very contemporary and modern, notably the projections on the exposed brick walls, but it's complemented by traditional Indian patterns and artifacts. Nicely done.

PRICES (2 stars):

Overall, this place is just a little too expensive, especially for Nashville. If they can sustain at these prices, more power to them. In order for me to become a regular, I know I'll need the prices to come down. Given their north Gulch location and proximity to downtown Nashville, I especially think they should rethink their lunch prices and make a real push for their happy hour.

SERVICE (2 stars):

Front of house is a mess so far. Both times, I encountered awkward and poor customer service at the host stand.

The first time, we walked in at 5 p.m. on Sunday. We were asked "What's your last name?" as if we must have had a reservation. We didn't. How about "Welcome to Chauhan. How many are in your party? Do you have a reservation?" Our subsequent service was also terrible. It was a trainer/trainee situation, so they get a bit of a pass there. But it was early on a Sunday night, not crowded at all, and we had to wait so freakin' long for anything to happen. The dining experience took nearly two hours for a total of 4 drinks and 4 small plates. Unacceptable.

The second time, I walked in with a group of young professionals at 5 p.m. on a Tuesday. We had a reservation, but if you had seen us, you would have known to ask, "Are you here for dinner or for happy hour?" After waiting for 1-2 minutes (which was unexplainable because no one was there), we were sat at our six-top in the completely empty dining room, only to find out that happy hour is only available in the bar area. So we had to move, which seemed absurd, because we were literally the only people in the restaurant who weren't being paid to be there. The only breath of fresh air service-wise was our bartender Asher. He was great.

As a former server, I really hope to see the front of house improve.

Went here for lunch today and we thoroughly enjoyed it.  My husband had a patty melt and I had the chicken croquettes and they were good. I had a chef's special and the portions were nice for lunch. There were 2 nice sized croquettes. We were seated as soon as we went in and the waitress came over shortly thereafter.  Food didn't take that long either. Our waitress was very nice.  Prices were good too.

After reading tons of reviews, I decided to try this place out because I love a great sandwich.  I ordered the turkey and brie sandwich and the beau ordered a muffalatta.  I was not a fan of my sandwich at all - perhaps, I'm just not a brie fan because the cheese completely overwhelmed the sandwich.  I really wish that I had stuck with something else.....really anything else.  Also, the bread to meat ratio was off too - so it was pretty pricey for what you actually got on your sandwich.  The boyfriend had a 'meh' reaction to his sandwich (but, it's hard to mess that one up).  The real star of the meal was the potato salad with bacon - YUM!!!  I was definitely a fan.  

I want to try Mitchell's one more time before I strike it off my list, so I'll try one of the safer options that other Yelpers have recommended!

If I can give this dump a negative 5 I would! The wife was very rude! Food was cold. Was very rude to my elderly family who were just asking questions. Very bad experience. Waited 2+ hours for the food asked why the long wait and wife said "you don't like it, u can leave"

What a delicious lunch! We enjoyed the Munto, Rice pilau and the Sultan's Pilau. We also had the falafel appetizer with fresh naan. Good choices. We would definitely eat here again. So ail distancing was observed, too.

The end result of this visit was food poisoning. Which, after the series of events at the restaurant, qualifies under the "go figure" category.
We arrived mid-morning during a week day and, while the restaurant was busy-ish, there was no one in line in front of us. We were seated, given menus, and upon mentioning to the waitress that we were waiting for the rest of our group to arrive, were berated for being seated without the entire party present. (I would like to add here that we did tell the person at the host stand that our whole group wasn't present yet.)
Then our waitress came by every five minutes asking if our third person was close, if not we may have to give up our seat, even though there was literally no one waiting for a seat.
The rest of our group arrived, she then ignored us for about 30 minutes. Once she finally did bother to take our order, it was another 45 before the food came out.
Other tables came and went in the time it took to get our order placed and food brought out. If I wasn't in such a state of hanger I would have said something, but in my desperation for their supposedly amazing breakfast, I decided not to rock the boat.
The food didn't have much flavor, and after two bites, I thought the eggs tasted off, so I didn't eat them (I ate around them). What followed can be summed up as three days of porcelain misery.
There are so many other places in STL that are sure to give you a better meal without the attitude and racist undertones (yes, that really happened, but the details do not feel appropriate to discuss on here), that it's better for the local economy to spend your money and satisfy your hunger elsewhere.

I've just visited The Wild Cow for the first time.  Let me highly recommend it to you.  Being a vegan, traveling often means I become king of the side dishes.  This little tucked away hole in the wall in East Nashville, is a major find for anyone that appreciates healthy, veg food.  I lived in Nashville for awhile but had never been to this part of the city.  Great service and a super-friendly staff. Not fine dining but the food is delicious. (I had a difficult time deciding on a particular dish since everything seemed like it would be delicious.  I settled on the Buffalo Tofu Bowl which includes pinto beans and kale).  See ya next time!
This place is great! The food is delicious, cocktails are super refreshing and the atmosphere is nice and cozy.
I lived beside The Goat's Beard for a year and they have the best weekly specials in Manayunk.  Thursday $5 select specialty cocktails and $5 Goat Nuggets accompanied by some live music is a steal.

The building's inside and outside were cute with a nice ambiance. Good date place. The choice of music didn't really lend itself to the ambiance, IMO. The service was friendly and attentive. The waiter was sloppy in appearance, which seemed an odd contrast to the rather crisp appearance of other staff and the overall interior of the restaurant itself.  The food was average to good, with the exception of the blue cheese flan which was outstanding and itself would have earned 5 stars.  If you come here you must order this. It's more of a cheesecake than flan texture without being as heavy as cheesecake.
