The flavor is sweet with a slight blue cheese aftertaste with some bites--nice creamy texture and a great sweet-with-a-hint-of-savory bite! The alligator appetizer was tasty. Not sure what alligator is supposed to taste like, but it was good. Like a fancy, well seasoned chicken strip. The shrimp and grits were ok. It took a very long time to get this dish. I ordered before the table next to me (they ordered the same thing), yet they received their food well before I did. I don't mind waiting a bit between courses, but this was an excessive wait. Maybe I wouldn't have minded if the dish was outstanding rather than mediocre. The dish was flavored ok, but the sausage was overcooked and there wasn't enough of the grits at the base. I wouldn't order this again if I came back. If I lived here I'd likely visit again, but I'd definitely try a different entree. The server was slow to drop off the check also despite the fact that he had already cleared my dessert plate and asked if I needed anything else. It wasn't especially busy to warrant such slow service.
The food was very good, price was also good. I had the blacken grouper and my wife had the lamb. Wait staff was excellent. Crab cakes were in my top ten. Cappy visits everyt table. Overall very good.
Great bar tenders and amazing service. Potato skins are fresh and delicious. The outside is an amazing area to hang out. Would highly recommend.

We have had take out from here three times.  Their food is consistently good.  Not the best Italian I've ever had but good. Stuffed shells were oddly dry after reheating. Have buy one get one free at end of nights at times for garlic bread etc at end of night.  Tortellini pasta salad with vegetables and ham and cheese baked bread pockets are awesome. Cannolis are yummy! Can be pricey if getting a lot.  Usually have some sort of family special each day. Close early so call ahead before going. Great staff.

Service was good. Food is marginal. Soggy pizza crust. Cold Baja fish tacos. Over priced. Just a cheesy sports bar with bad food. Not a place for a good dinner with friends and family. Expected a lot better quality food from the Yelp 4 star rating. Disappointing.

Dirty restaurant, trust me you don't want to eat there, the food is okay, but there's water dripping AC outlet, gambling machine room inside the restaurant, and some homeless just come in to get free beverage while we eating like it's his own kitchen.

Unbelievable establishment!  My husband and I joined another couple for a Saturday night out. We had a reservation for 7:30 pm. The place was packed, they had us wait a little but offered to open up 1 of our 4 bottles of wine and had a delicious appetizer sent over to us to enjoy while waiting, on the house of course. When we were sat there was a huge antipasto salad in the center of our table, again on the house. The bread was delicious and they gave a oil, spices & hummas to dip it in which was amazing. All staff including the owner apologized to us for making us wait. The service was impeccable and their menu is amazing!  Since we had apps we didn't need to order anything to start so we ordered our entrees. They had 5 specials for that specific night and one sounded better then the next. I had a chicken dish, my husband had New York strip, our friends had seafood (the fish was filleted table side which was enjoyable to see). We all loved our meals and raved all evening. Unfortunately we were too full for dessert but the menu looked wonderful. They ended the evening with house shots of lemoncello.  I would absolutely recommend this wonderful establishment to anyone who wants a perfect date night out.

Look we only came here for the char-grilled oysters, not the ambience etc.... We heard from locals that their char-grilled oysters were comparable to Acme and there was less of a wait.

It was true that there was less of a wait, but we ended up getting seated in the worse area of the restaurant- the other room where they were actually grilling the oysters so the entire room smelled like smoke. It was pretty terrible and no one even opened the door to let some fresh air- for that I docked off a star.

But their oysters were pretty damn good- not as hot as the oysters from Acme, but it had a lovely grilled taste- smoky (well obviously) and less cheese than Acme. They're different but delicious (both places had pretty damn good oysters).

I would come back if I could sit in the other well ventilated room!

Food was excellent for the other members of our party.  Service very slow. Gluten was a Huge problem.  Was told by waiter that the chicken dish I ordered was gluten free and corn free.  Had a violent reaction upon leaving the restaurant. Beware if you have any food allergies!!!!

This place is SO GOOD! I love ordering via the paper checklist, gives you time to review all the options and customize your order. I had the poke bowl, which was actually a very large box I made into two meals. The ingredients were fresh and delicious. You really can't go wrong here. The atmosphere is nice with a calming effect. It's a good spot to eat take your computer and do some work. I highly suggest checking out this new gem on Mass Ave.

I came here with my Mom, Grandma, Sister and my little cousin..it was for my BIRTHDAY and it was our first time there..no hostess or waitress in sight so we sat at an empty table waiting to be redirected or have our orders taken...My mother had caught the attention of a young female waitress with long black hair and highlighter on her nose, and she asked the waitress if we could sit there..to which she replied "This isn't a free for all" & that we need to go through the hostess which was not around, and refused to explain any further..I also had asked her if she could check if it was ok for us to sit at the table we were already at and she told me the same exact thing and continued to be very rude and unhelpful, when I tried to ask her if we could get a hostess she walked away in the middle of my sentence with an ugly look on her face. Our new waitress was very nice, but she had forgotten to give us a number of things when we only ordered drinks and 2 appetizers throughout our time there. Probably never going back unless your fix your staff
Haven't been here for a while. Took my wife and her friends this weekend. They loved it; I did too. Worth the price and a lot of fun. Great way to hang out with friends.

If you want poor slow service this is the place to go. Took forever to take our beverage order. Free refills limit of 4 where do they do that? Don't drink your beverage too fast the waitress will let you know.  The taste of the food was just ok.  I had my favorite rueben with the tuffest corn beef I ever had in my life. One thing I can they were slow with EVERYONE.  We saw one group of about six just leave because they took entirely too long to bring their food. We will not be going back. My friend said it not the first time they got poor service. Well that is our first and  last time!

Philly Dine-not!!

eggs were running so much, i expected to see a gold medal pop out.

waffle was so tasteless, i had to keep looking down at the fork to make sure something was actually on it!

and i swear, one sniff of that water made me wonder if the facuet was made of cow dung.

and i went another time by request of a friend and of course the diner was closed and i could only buy dessert.

Service is top notch! Food is even better. They'll accommodate where they can. Really friendly staff. In my opinion this may be one of the better restaurants in the Hyde park area. Definitely plan ahead and have reservations. This spot can get quite busy during dinner times. Only downside imo is that I wish they had more main plates. But sometimes having less main plates makes for quicker ordering from people on your group lol.

From the outside, it looks like an unassuming old home.  On the inside, it's a family-oriented and family run steakhouse.  Apparently, prime rib is the specialty, but I had the petite fillet.  Even as "petite" as it was, I still couldn't finish it.  Overly salty, but good.  Fellow diners did have the prime rib and the small order of that was HUGE.  All dinners are served with a salad and side- the baked potato was perfect!  OK wine list, but the selection of micro-brews was amazing.  They easily accommodated our table of 10 with fantastic and efficient service- great for groups.  Place is a bit loud- so for an intimate dining experience, this may not be it.

OUTSTANDING

i must come visit,   and will someetimes have dreams about how awesome the bison burger is!  oh my goodness. . .    the burgouise fries are to die for!!  try everything on the menu ( im speaking from experience) the best absolutely best hamburger.  gods order lunch here to-go 

the Rootbeer they brew here is made from Holywater blessed in the heart of the Tibetan mountains. 

mad respect for how awesome this business is

completely blows the hinges off of all expectations

My oh my!!!

We remembered Coop's fondly from a trip to N'awlins before Katrina. We couldn't remember the name, but knew it was there on Decatur, east of Central Grocery. We ate there last Thursday for lunch.

My wife had redfish meuniere. While not a classic meuniere, it was absolutely delightful. The redfish filet was lightly breaded and fried, served on a bed of white rice and smothered with perfectly cooked shrimp and a deep dark sauce that had notes of roux, stock, cayenne and something sweet - an absolute gem of a sauce. I want to fly back RIGHT NOW!!

I had shrimp creole, which was also very good, if not as memorable as the dish above. It is a much simpler dish, but was executed perfectly - shrimp not overcoooked, creole sauce well seasoned.

And of course we are in love with Coop's blue cheese dressing on the house salad. They add red wine (reduction?) and it really deepens an excellent blue cheese dressing base nicely.
Authentic Mexican food....I had the poblano fajitas which is my favorite from there.  They have a live band on Saturdays.

I've been here many times. Portion sizes seem to be declining. This must be a franchised store. Too much focus on reducing costs for the restaurant. What was once was a moderately sized chicken sandwich has morphed into a chicken cutlet sandwich. Very disappointing and it doesn't meet the Chick-fil-A standard. I will definitely be going to a different location from here on out. Fries were adequate but not a large portion like I ordered, just a medium in a large box. Maybe it was just an off visit but this isn't the first time this has happened to me here.

Great food for the price. Try the fresh oysters but especially the charbroiled oysters. So delicious! Crab claws are really great too. Be sure to go through the kitchen to the bathroom to take in all the incredible smells!
One of my favorite places in the city. Really unique food. A little expensive, but the portions are bug enough to make up for it.

Everything about my experience here was 5/5 and I hope everyone else who comes here gets the same feels. Do not be put off by the somewhat unassuming entry way (a hallway with stairs leading up to the resturaunt)! The resturaunt is cozy and had a live singer who was really just amazing (I think he comes every weekend). Our waiters were all superbly friendly (like beyond the usual, our main waiter made lots of small talk everytime he checked in on us) and on top of all our small requests (hot water, bread refill, etc). The food came out quickly and well-paced with complimentary bread first (crispy outside and soft warm inside!), then soup/salad that comes with any entrée (the minestrone soup is very unique and good with the bread, not overly salty either!), entrées (piping fresh and hot), and dessert (oh so delicious house tiramisu). We had one of the daily species which was grilled sea bass and risotto with side of vegetables ($28) and it was very well made. If you're used to American pan fried or baked fish, you need to try the seabass. It's much more moist and tender and the risotto was on point. Not to mention, their vegetables are very well done (not too soft and not too hard, not too salty but not bland). We also ordered the tube pasta with Italian sausage (can't remember the actual name) and linguini shrimp (again apologizes can't remember the exact name) and both were very good. The linguini has ample amounts of vegetables and shrimp and the pasta was very good (texture and taste) without a super heavy cream sauce. We finished our meal with a delicious tiramisu that is definitely unique and different from anywhere else I've had tiramisu from so I would highly recommend this.

All in all, I can't stop raving about this place and will be recommending it to anyone especially if you're on your way to Reno..this is definitely better than the food you'll find there.
Had another great meal here with friends last night. Great drink (Figueroa) and food-- deviled egg, shisedo peppers, cauliflower, duck, risotto, and scallops. Excellent service.

I cannot speak highly enough about my first experience at Fratellis! This place was amazing (food, service, experience). My girlfriend and I sat outside, which was nice. We were greeted by a very down to earth waitress that immediately developed great rapport with us. We chose our meals from the $25.00 prix fixe menu.... Which was a pleasant surprise that they offered something like that on a Friday night. For our appetizers we got fried calamari and stuffed mushrooms.... Amazing. Highly recommend the stuffed mushrooms. Second course was a pretty standard dinner salad, but we both got the balsamic vinaigrette which was delicious. We found out in conversation that they actually make it in house. For dinner my friend got the penne alla vodka which was absolutely to die for. I actually preferred hers over mine but mine was great too. I got a beef tortellini in a Marsala cream sauce, interesting spin on the Marsala sauce, loved it. For drinks, hahaha they kept them flowing, we got a couple bottles of wine, and each got the espresso martini which was spectacular (not too sweet, which I like) and a couple espresso shots (with lemon zest slither as any good Italian restaurant should). But what I especially loved about this experience was the special attention one of the owners Johnny gave us. He was so nice and accommodating, checked on us  a couple times and was chatting us up a little (but NOT in an annoying "leave us alone kind of way"). Something interesting is that the two owners are brothers... You can feel the family run business vibe in the place too, which was fun. This is a very laid back, yet nice restaurant, great food, amazing service and it even seems like they treat their employees well too. Overall, highly recommend this Fratellis.
Great food.... Breakfast was the bomb. I had the BearCat breakfast everything was perfect. My friend had the shrimp and grits that I tried and they too were perfect. I will be visiting again soon.

Food is good, atmosphere is friendly for all ages, staff is absolutely wonderful and I could eat those cheese fries with gravy everyday. HUGE improvement over the last owners. Great neighborhood spot. Please keep up the good work. We eat here at least 2 or 3 times a month. Kim & Ed.

The food was pretty good but they are missing out on making a dope ass chicken and waffles. If they made a cw I would go broke there. If the eagle is listening, make sure you put sausage gravy on it. Thank me later.

Wanted to like it...We visited during Restaurant Week after hearing positive things about the new owner. Had not even pleased in past. Service was inconsistent at best. Waited 20 minutes for glass of wine and beer. Was told bartender was "making our drinks". Food was good but atmosphere and wobbly table ( wait staff did help to stabilize it) contributed to unpleasant experience. Sorry we tried!
Thank you cashier Amy Chamblis for your superb service and a wonderful smile. This kind of person is what makes me want to go to the same place over and over again.

I love chick-fil-a.... I mean really who doesn't? But the drive-through time is ridiculous at this location. And honestly, the inside wait isn't too much better. The prices are good and the Service is awesome which kind of makes you not worry about waiting so long. My daughter loves the play place on the inside which is OK for her to go play in while I'm waiting in the long line. I don't do the drive through at this location at all anymore. Even though it's double lanes you would think that it would move a little faster, but it doesn't. The quality of the food is 100% on point. And I'll definitely be back. The long wait isn't enough to scare me away!! Lol.

We ordered delivery to the hotel and it was super fast. I had egg foo young I know but I was craving it lol and Mongolian beef dinner special. 

It was one of those nights where you just didn't want to think about what to eat and where. Something fast, close and possibly good enough to eat. 

Surprisingly this was actually that spot, plenty of food to feed 4 people of the egg foo young, and another two for the dinner special which they forgot the egg roll lol whatever 

Anyway it's a good spot

Hands down the best place to get a slice in the city, if not the whole state... Not much else to say other than they have GREAT PIZZA at very reasonable prices. This is not necessarily the first place I would go to order a whole pizza, (I might prefer Tony's, Cassanova's, or Flying Pie for that) but if you just want to grab a quick bite to eat, look no further!!!
Cool vibe, open air dining in the heart of Clearwater Beach. We all had grouper. It was great and the fries were perfect.  Third floor is the place to be for sunset. Super views

When I woke up today a total hungover zombie, I was like,"BRUNCH!" I haven't been here in so long for no particular reason! So I called up my friend, we went, of course there was a wait (it's Saturday and who cares), and I'm so happy we did. Please, if you haven't been, get the Eggs in Purgatory! I aaaalways order this. So good. Eggs (any style you prefer) simmered in GMM's extremely flavorful tomato sauce with some basil on top/comes with toast. Guzzled some mimosas and coffee down too, naturally. Their interior is a dream as well. 1950s bright decor, teals, yellows, oranges, a juke box, and great furniture. I just love it. The servers aren't creepy-fake nice too, it actually seems like genuine kindness and I appreciate that wholeheartedly.

Stopped in for a quick lunch. They had their buffet up and running, but decided against it.  Was just looking for something light.  Really nothing light on the menu, at least light in Senior citizen terms.  Ended up having the finger steak and my wife had a salad.  Both were okay, but not what we were looking for.  Can't  fault them, rating comes from our needs not their service.  Did have their Bloody Mary bar - neat idea!

Absolutely the BEST Mexican I've had. Very authentic. The Posole was amazing, as well as the sopes. Honestly, we didn't get anything sub-par there. We went there twice in 4 days! The staff is friendly and welcoming. Although you have to wait a few minutes for your food, you can tell it's because it was prepared fresh. If we return to the area, it will be first on our list to go to.

Georgia's catered my wedding rehearsal dinner and it was awesome!!! Alissa was super helpful in working with us on our menu, and even though our event was on the 4th of July (on the beach) and traffic and parking were all crazy, they made it work. The food was great-  my guests especially loved the sauteed kale!
Absolute best steaks in STL and super affordable! I make sure to go here at least once a month!

We use to frequent this location a lot, recently the speed of service has significantly dropped. I placed a take out order at 9:10pm, we were told to come and grab the order 20 minutes at the conclusion of the call. We showed up 30 minutes later to ensure they had enough time to complete our order. We waited from 9:40pm-10:15pm. 
Although the staff were very kind, the wait time for a pickup order was atrocious.

So now the card scanner asks if I want to leave a tip. For what??  I have to go to the counter and pick up my own food and then bring my plate and trash to the trash receptacle. This tip thing is getting out of hand!!  . Food is average and expensive.

We ordered via bite squad so unfortunately we couldn't really have the kitchen fix what was wrong. But ... What I really like is the soft taco shells..: they are legit like you get off the streets when you travel to Mexico. Bravo on that part. The spicy beef was awesome too. Chicken was ok in my book but hands down... the beef tacos are great. 
We ordered w cilantro and there was not one trace of it at all on the 4 of ours so poo poo to the guy who made our order to go. 
What made me sad was the size of the side of guacamole. It seriously is no larger then a tablespoon size and lacking any flavor... side of chips were enough for maybe one person. 
Also we ordered salsa and that was missing from our to go order too. So if anything ... great beef tacos and soft shells ... as far as quality control and who ever handles the to go orders... you have room to grow.

Went here for lunch today and was very impressed.  For $7 we got a full buffet with some of the most popular dishes...tandori chicken, butter chicken, a spicy veggie curry, dal.  The meal included papdums and FRESH naan.  I read that the dinner buffet was only $12...might have to take the hubby back next week.  The service was good and my 1 year old enjoyed it as well.  Great place.

While the food is very good, the way the take out line is run undermines the customers waiting in line for food. While waiting over an hour in line, we saw multiple groups of people order online and then cut us to go pick up their food from the take out line and then go sit down at a table. More effort needs to be put into serving the customers that are in the actual restaurant rather than the take out orders. After waiting over an hour, we decided we were going to leave because it still would have been another probably 45 minutes to get our food once we finally could order. If you want to come get take out, you're in the right place. If you want to come in and sit down to eat, it's going to be VERY slow.

Been enjoying breakfast and lunch here for forty years.  Changed ownership recently and now offers dinners at the end of the week.  There are several    upscale options.  Enjoyed a dinner combination of three small Lobster tails, a small crab cake, and a small Filet.  It came with a salad (or soup)  and two sides.  At $27.50 it was a bargain.  The food was very good - probably the best Crab Cake that I have  tasted in a while.

A bonus -  still the comfortable atmosphere with efficient, pleasant staff.

Ordered through Seamless, which runs on GrubHub or through GH i guess... Either way, they messed up the order and they did not call when they arrived. I specifically both put my number and to call please when they got there...I thought i would never see the day when someone could mess up a Caesar salad so royally (no dressing on it) ... 0 stars 2 thumbs down...get it together y'all

1st time going to sushi Inc 
5  I Will be making this my every week sushi place , service was amazing and everything I got was on point.... full bar with unique drinks !

3.5 stars. We've had Brazilian steakhouse in Colorado and in Cancun and this was our least favorite.  Not bad, but not just great or memorable. We made reservations just a few house before and were able to get seated right before our reserved time. The restaurant itself is big and open; however, it felt tight, the tables and chairs were a tad bit too close. There's valet parking at $10 with validation which is cheaper than parking so that was great. 

Service - our waitress was horrible - we asked for straws and brought only two for the three of us stating she must've dropped one on the way and if everyone needed a straw. Uh, what? She also didn't want to explain the desserts and when she brought our creme brûlée, only brought again, 2 spoons! The meat guys were incredibly nice and accommodating. Although there was a good 10-15 minute dry point where they didn't bring any meat to our table until we asked what looked like the manager. 

The food - there's a number of different meats - ribs, different flavor steaks - sirloin, ribeye, flank, pork sausage, chicken,lamb, even fish. Some were good, some not so much. Our favorites were the sweet and spicy chicken, most of the steaks, and the pineapple. They also bring you an assortment of breads - fried banana, cheese biscuits, fried potatoes. All were pretty good. The salad/sides buffet had a good assortment including - quinoa salad, mash potatoes, asparagus, cheeses, and fresh veggies/dressing. Another soup option would've been nice. Best part of the meal was the orange liquor creme brulee, which was delicious! Not overly sweet, creamy, with the perfect crunchy of sugar.

We love the concept, and overall it wasn't a bad experience, we'e just had better. And for the price, its not a place where we will frequent often. But good to have if we have a hankering.

This place used to be great.  I am guessing an owner or two ago. Their prices were great and their food was fantastic.  Now, they are just another sandwich place in South Philly.

My wife, daughter, and I have ordered there for years.  We would always get one of their little pizzas and a couple of sandwiches.  Unfortunately, they don't offer the pizzas anymore.  My 2 year old daughter loved their pizza, but since they don't offer it anymore we just order City Pizza all the time if she wants pizza...oh and they don't have pizza rolls anymore either!

The sandwiches also seem to have gone down in quality.  I always try something new, but each sandwich tasted like it was the same dry meat on bread combo.

Sorry Amato's, but until you go back to lower prices and higher quality, this guy is just going to support the other local joints!

Trying new restaurants while girls on a two week vacation. Two of the ladies had been here before but I had not. Great surprise....food was above our expectations. Peel & eat shrimp were amazing, blackened grouper some of the best we've found. Salads were fresh and nice size. Atmosphere casual and family friendly. Prices were some of the best we've seen especially for a tourist area! Going back for sure!!!

Meh, I can take or leave this place. I like coming here when I visit Eastern State Penitentiary, because it's directly across the street. 

The time before last time I went, we met up with a whole bunch of our friends and family after visiting ESP. It was crowded, of course, being a Friday night. At first we attempted to just stand around a table talking to some of the people in our group that were there. Quickly, we were told that that was not allowed and we'd have to wait for a table ourselves if we wanted one. Great. I totally get it, it's busy, servers need to move around, fine. But this hostess was frazzled and not kind. So we continued to stand at the table and talk to our group UNTIL a table was read. The hostess came over again and super rudely and half-shouty told us to stand by the door until the table was ready. 

The food is just okay. Their tots are overly salty.

The last time I went was again after ESP, but in the early afternoon. I was with my wife and our two friends and we had brunch. It was fine, nothing spectacular. There was a table behind next to us that was super obnoxious--super loud and wayyyyyy drunk. Straight up laughing hysterically and hitting the table. Would have appreciated someone telling them to turn it down a bit. Our server was nice enough, but brought me a beer when I didn't ask for one (and didn't want to pay for one), but I didn't want to say anything so I took it as if I had ordered it. 

Okay place if you're just looking for a quick bite or drink. OR if you're coming from ESP across the street. :)
Great sports bar in Philadelphia. Menu is pretty typical, but the food itself is good & that's what's important.

Food: less than average
Experience: poor
Service: poor
Food was not worth the wait for what it was and also not worth the price. Would not recommend or go here again.

From the moment we walked into this restaurant it was already a bad start to our experience. I will preface this review by saying that we only went here for two reasons: because the restaurant we wanted to go to was closed (Labor Day), and it looked like a good place to go because their outside seating was packed!

Upon walking in, there was no one at the hostess stand. When someone finally saw us, she had no sense of urgency and looked as if she could care less if we got a table or not. Within the first five minutes of getting a table, I overheard a waitress apologize into a table near us for messing up their order, that is never a good sign.

Fortunately, our waiter was the only server at this restaurant that seem to have any sense of urgency whatsoever. The place was packed and probably understaffed since it was a holiday. after getting our drinks, our server told us he would be back to take our order in "2 seconds." Which we obviously knew was just an expression, but he continued to walk back-and-forth past our table doing other things for five minutes. Just don't say you're going to be back soon if you won't.

We ordered and expected the wait for food to be longer than normal because of how busy they were. But it was definitely too long, same with the other tables around us. Unfortunately when we finally got our food one of the orders was messed up. We didn't even bother saying anything because we knew it would end up taking too long to fix it.

The food was nothing special. Everything was average, but not worth the price. Also, sandwiches are served with potato chips, which I thought maybe they made their own in house, but they don't, it's just regular potato chips from a bag. Slightly disappointing. nothing we ordered was anything you couldn't make at home yourself, and it would be just as good if not better. Also, everything on their menu is pretty basic, and you could get it anywhere else. So just go somewhere else.

Don't let the outside appearance/location fool you. This is really a HOLE in the wall venue, but the sandwiches are SO GOOD. I love the honey cuban. I'm not even a big fan of cuban sandwiches, but this cuban is delicious. The honey bread pairs so well with the rest of the sandwich. I've been to this Shop 2-3 times now, so I've also been able to try the Palomilla and La Tripleta sandwiches. Both great as well! I love the crunchy potato sticks in both of these. Coffee here is authentic: grab some espresso. On top of the great flavors here, the prices are so low. You can order a cuban in small, medium, or large sizes. I think the small is $4, medium $5, large $6. Can't beat these prices, and the portion sizes are huge.

I can assume that parking here may be difficult at lunchtime, but I've always been able to grab a spot on the side or in back of the restaurant. It may be tempting to park in front of one of the neighboring homes, but don't do it! I've seen a gentleman come out and yell at someone. ;)

Obama has eaten at the West Tampa Sandwich Shop. So should you!

Let me state up front, that diners are not my favorite places to dine.  My husband, on the other hand, loves them.  We found ourselves in Mt. Airy/Chestnut Hill, were hungry, saw the Trolley Car Diner, and decided to stop for lunch.  The place is quite large...two rooms plus a third room in which there are 450 (!) different kinds of beer displayed.  In that room also is an ice cream parlor where donuts, baked fresh each day, are served.  The aroma was wonderful!  

We were greeted warmly by the hostess, again greeted warmly by our waitress, and also by the friendly man sitting in the booth in front of us.  

The menu is enormous!  Even someone like me who prefers cafes & bistros would have a hard time not finding something to whet the appetite.  My husband settled on a (huge) plate of black bean chili, which he loved, that was accompanied by house-made corn bread, while I had a tuna melt on whole grain toast.  Excellent, but there was no way I could finish it.  The remainder of the black bean chili went home with us.  

There's a real trolley car outside of the diner and in summer it's open for ice cream (milk shakes, floats, etc.), hot dogs, burgers, etc. that can be eaten at picnic tables.  All food served inside also is available to go.

Would we go back?  I'll never give up my preference for more bistro-like spots, but I'd certainly return to The Trolley Car Diner, perhaps next time for breakfast.

Amazing place. Food was great and it match the company of Chef and Owner Ian Gladue. We had the Nehiyaw Taco and Elk Stew. The complimentary tea was amazing. 

On our way to Anchorage, Alaska, this was a must stop for us. We are big supporters of #Aboriginal #FirstNations businesses, this was a treat as it was on our way. Thank you!!

The food is good , the fries are nice. Fresh Sammie's .
I use to come here when I was in highschool since it was in walking distance but the customer service is poor
The women they have working behind the counter hardly speaks English 
poor service , she mistook my order more than once and charged me for fries before I gave her my card I told her, before I paid since she didn't run my order by me and she did not give me what I ordered def. Could be better with better staff, not interested in this place any longer.

Well, after being shooed out of Raijin Ramen for whatever reason, who knows, 20 minutes before they were supposed to close, I came here since I had a hankering for tonkotsu ramen. I was not disappointed and very pleased! Nice to find a wonderful restaurant after being turned away from another.

Surprised at how slow business was for them, especially since they have good reviews. 

The tonkotsu ramen was delicious. It had a nice smooth broth, sweet corn, bean sprouts, fish cake (kamaboko), marinated boiled egg, seaweed and ki-kurage (a type of mushroom) in it. I upgraded and opted for char siu. The char siu was grilled and the three pieces were about 2-1/2 inches in diameter. It was delicious, some of the best char siu I've had. And it wasn't overly fatty like some char siu can be. Plenty of noodles. Good comfort food. I enjoyed it. 

The restaurant is large and seats many. The decor is modern and the restaurant is clean. The service was very pleasant and attentive. 

This is a family owned and run business. And they are from Hong Kong! LOL Well...they do Japanese very well, at least the ramen. They have a very extensive menu, you are sure to find something that you like. I will have to return and try some of their other dishes to see how they have mastered other Japanese recipes.

5* = A top favorite. Mind-blowing good. I will definitely return and I will go out of my way to go here. Worth every dime of my money.
4* = Outstanding. Tucson-top-tier. Some elements not quite as good as it gets, but it still is worthy of my regular business.
3* = Good experience. I might do repeat business if it is convenient, the only option, the only one in its category, or on a whim, but would not be among the first thing to come to mind. Would definitely recommend you trying it to get your own take on it.
2* = Not so good. Would not recommend at all. Waste of money.
1* = How are they still in business? Stay away at all costs!
You can keep your Genos and Pats. This is where it's at. Went on a gloomy Saturday. The line wasn't too bad. But definitely had to wait a while. There's just something about that cheese whiz !

This food is so great! I tried a seafood option enchiladas and they were so good. Enough  food to where I couldn't finish it all. I also tried the chorizo queso dip, also yummy!! And there drink were unique and they were not stingy with the alcohol. That is a whole other story but I don't like to get drinks out normally b/c you get charged the price of a small bottle but get a cap full of alcohol in a cup full of ice....NOT the case here, drinks were great. We will be going back too. Prices are not too bad either about  $40 for a couple. It took us a little longer to put or order in but food was done quick.

We went to Cibo Bistro for an anniversary dinner and thought it was awesome. We love Italian food and thought each plate we ordered was fantastic. They were well put together with great flavor combinations and absolutely amazing tomato sauce and any meat we had was cooked to complete perfection. This restaurant and it's head chef are serious competition for Corso 32 as our experience was on par with our meal at Corso. Our waitress was fantastic and very personable. She made excellent recommendations and helped us to understand some of the dishes on the menu. This isn't a typical Italian restaurant so don't come here expecting Chianti's or Picolino's, it's high end Italian with food made like you were in Rome. They use fresh local food that is available and in season if possible and work hard to create complex flavor combinations. 
We can all be grateful that Edmonton is getting such outstanding restaurants like Cibo Bistro and Corso 32 as they are setting the bar way higher for any future restaurants. Go to Cibo, you will not be disappointed!

Place is bang average for the dollars spent. The pita is usually dry. The hummus seems like canned hummus with plenty of olive oil poured in. Food is presented very well though. Falafels are dry and undercooked from inside as well. Not very 'Mediterranean' or 'Greek'.

Unfortunately I had a give From the Boot a poor rating because of our experience  there. My girlfriends and I recently went about 1 month ago-there was 6 of us total. This was our first time there- we decided to come here based on reviews. They seated us in the back corner-3 walls surrounding 6 girls. Of course it is going to echo! And of course the restaurant is BYOB so alcohol was involved. Anyway, the manager had to tell us to be quiet. Having said that- our dinner was ruined. Why put a table to girls in an enclosed corner?? The food was great-unfortunately we had a bitter taste in our mouth due to our "noise complaint".

I do really enjoy this Thai food.. but I ordered from them on Yelp one time. They confirmed my ordered. On yelp it said it be ready in 20-25 mins. I drive down there. Walk to the entrance and they are definitely closed. I'm not sure if that was closed for good. Or what the situation was.
This place has good food and good cocktails. The blues bar is fun! And it's in a great location, just a short walk to Main Street!

Absolutely horrible.  Even if you were lucky enough to order the couple of things on the menu that do not taste like horse meat, the restaurant - the bar, to the dining room, to the kitchen to the bathrooms - DISGUSTING.  I have witnessed dirtier things in there than on the actual streets of St. Louis.  I have no clue how they pass inspection.  I work and live downtown and when I hear people not in the "downtown dining know" send people from out of town here basically because of proximity to a few local hotels, I just cringe.  I feel for visitors that go here and think this may be the best St. Louis has to offer.

I made a private party reservation for a surprise birthday party for 10 people. Not only would they not let us sit until every single person was there which ruined the surprise, the hostesses were also extremely RUDE to our entire party. They gossiped audibly about other tables and how they didn't like them and another waitress joined them and started bashing another table of customers. This was so unprofessional and was made even worse that everyone at the bar could hear them talking. Seriously get some class.

Currently sitting in the drive thru, it's been a total of 40 minutes, 4 cars have left the lane and I've already paid so I can't drive off. I wonder how this place is still open.

The food is delicious and I love coming here, but it's not worth the wait anymore.

Outstanding!  Busy, but worth the wait to be seated.  Got a recommendation to go here from several friends and I'm so glad we finally went!  Breaded mushrooms were crisp with substantial breading and mushrooms - not your usual puny fried mushrooms!  Servings are large, so come prepared to either eat a lot or bring leftovers home!  Loved the southwest chicken salad, the boys inhaled their chicken fried chicken and my husband enjoyed his 1/2 golden fried chicken w/ fries & coleslaw.  Desserts are good too - today's special was lemon shortcake - yum!  We'll be returning!
sunday evening, burger was given cold, bun hard and stale. chesse wasnt even melted much. literally a cold burger. nice guys.
The rize pizza crust is amazing! The upside pizza on the rize crust is hands down my favorite pizza in west chester! I highly recommend.

The most beautiful and ornate hotel I have seen. The rooms are large and very well decorated. There is beautiful art and architecture everywhere. The staff is friendly and amazing. Shop and eat here, quick walk to any spot near City Hall.

When i was in Philly i stayed at the Radisson hotel which  is right next to Miel, this is what brought me into the Patisserie :o)  I stopped by here in the morning for coffee/tea and some pastries. I had the chai latte and the almond croissant. The chai was a lil spicy, the way I like it and the croissant was nice and soft. The staff was really friendly and attentive to me and friends. 

All of the items are bit pricey, but overal very good!

Really good quality sandwiches and lots of other off the shelf items.  The staff is well trained, runs very efficiently and he products they produce are consistent. The sandwiches are reasonably priced for the quality but most of the other stuff in the store not so and doesn't have a price until you get to the register. For instance a kombucha is $4.50 there and up the street it's $3.25 which is more towards the norm. I could do without the religious music.

Came back to Stanley's and had the oysters benedict which was even better than I remembered. Perfectly cooked, flavorful oysters. Not greasy at all. Excellent dish. Good iced tea as well. A little on the pricey side but worth it.

I must say this place offered a relief after coming from an establishment that gave horrible service (no acknowledgement or even a hello).  Pollo Tropical offers some of the best fresh food around with exceptional service and periodical check-ins to make sure that you are doing well (when dining in).  Thank you for bringing a smile to my face and a Happy tummy to me!  I will be back again...That's for sure!

I have been back a few more times to have sushi. Johnny makes beautiful rolls that are delicious. And there is another sushi chief, I think his name is David and he makes rolls that are almost two bites they are so huge. 

Also, their pineapple fried rice is absolutely delicious! They serve it in a hollowed-out half pineapple. And it's about $14 but there are so many delicious things inside it, like chicken and shrimp, it's a whole meal.

I have to admit, I haven't tried other things on their menu but their sushi has been making me come back. It is expensive though compared to the other places around with their Angry Bird roll being like $18. But it never disappoints.
Super friendly and fast service. Delicious southern chicken biscuit and hashpuppies to begin our day of exploring
Kep coming back to this wonderful down to earth place.

I've visited this Tijuana Flats location about 3 times over the past 4 years.  It's conveniently located on the southwest corner of Belcher and E. Bay in Clearwater.  The store is a typical fast food layout, always clean and neat, with plenty of seating in  front of and to the side of the order counter.    The staff is always friendly, and ordering taking and food delivery is always prompt.

Tijuana Flats serves up a fair sized menu squarely in the Tex-Mex tradition.  Although the delivery is fast food, it's a significant step up from any Taco Bell-type store in the area.  I'm not a fan of most Tex-Mex style restaurants, and vastly prefer the places where you can get more authentic Mexican flavors.  But that's not a criticism of places like Tijuana Flats....they are what they are, they shouldn't try to be something else, and for what they do they do it well.

I usually order the basic taco or enchilada dinner, and it's always been good.  Baskets of tortilla chips have always been warm and tasty.   Which brings me to the one thing that I truly don't like about Tijuana Flats, their basic salsa.   Yes, they have a huge selection hot sauces......I imagine the biggest in the area.   But I find their basic salsa simply harsh tasting, almost like they've taken some tomatoes along with with some variety of pepper in there and pureed it far too long into a monochromatic liquid.  I suppose if you look at it as a hot sauce in a long line of other offerings to cover many flavor ingredients in Tex-Mex, it's ok.  But I vastly prefer salsa's where it's a bit more clear, liquidy, richer and more complex in taste, and you can see what has gone into the ingredients.....the kind of salsa you can find at virtually every taqueria around town.  Yes, it's nitpicking, but for my taste buds, the salsa should be the crowning flavor on top of a soft corn tortilla, meat filling, cilantro, maybe some onions.  And for me, the salsa here just doesn't pull that off very well.

Other than that, though, I've simply enjoyed Tijuana Flats for what it is, a chance to get a shot of Mexican quickly, with a minimum of effort and time.   Actually achieving what I suppose Taco Bell tries to do, but falls far short of most of the time.   With so many good authentic taquerias in the area, I'm not likely to drop in here unless it's for convenience.  My scores on a "Pinellas taqueria scale":

Atmosphere:  4
Service:   5
Food:  4
Value:   4

I looked at most of the reviews on this page, and I'll admit I was a little intimidated to even call this place.  But... I did, and I placed an order to go (the Chicken Salad Club Sandwich featured on Triple D) and I must say, this is the BEST sandwich I've had in this area!   Plus, everyone was friendly there, and I had no problems what-so-ever with the service (and it only took about 15 min. to make the sandwich).  Mind you... it was a week night that I went in there, but never the less.  I highly recommend this place... Guy Fieri on Triple D mentioned to the owner, "Props man -- you're the real thing."  And he was right.  I will be back!

Very nice addition to the local foodie scene.  Has a bit of that warehouse look, industrial floor and ceilings, with just a hint of the natural farm to table thing with the raw wood table tops.  It all comes together very well.  A down side of the hard edge, all metal and wood decor is the noise level is quite loud.  Not the spot for a quiet, meal and easy conversation.  The wait staff was very friendly, well prepared and very professional.  We started with a warm, marinated olive app that was quite good.  The addition of apricots and smoked almonds was a nice touch to the appetizer.  The entrees were the kale and mushroom lasagna, and chicken sausage and grits.  Both very flavorful and nicely presented.  A small issue with the lasagna, a bit to much cheese on the top.  For wine we opted for a Pinot Noir from the barrel fresh selections.  The wine is poured from a tap and delivered to your table in a glass bottle, with juice glasses.  If you want stemware rather than the juice glasses you need to make a special request.  Not a big deal if you know what's going on.  We did not until I asked later in the evening so we felt a bit like second class citizens until I knew what was going on.

I love street tacos with corn tortillas, fresh ingredients and cilantro. This place had them.  So good. Don't miss out on this place. It doesn't look like much from outside, but when you go in. Oh so good.  Places that are simple looking usually have the best food.  So glad I found this place

My boyfriend and I flew to Tennessee for a weekend and we knew we had to go to Hattie B's to try their hot chicken. He had seen it featured in David Chang's "Ugly Delicious" on Netflix and it had rave reviews, so we decided to check it out. 

We stood in line outside for about 30 minutes before we got to the counter. We ordered a large white meat plate with mild heat and a large dark meat plate with medium heat with sides of greens, beans, fries, mac and cheese, and coleslaw. The food came out fairly quickly and we dug right in. We chose the mild/medium spice level because we didn't want to suffer from burning tongues, but the medium was not that spicy... at all.... I guess I was expecting even the medium to be very spicy. I think we'll dare to try the "hot" or "damn hot" levels because that's what this place is known for, right? Besides the spice level, the chicken was fried well and the chicken was well rubbed which resulted in a nice crispy skin.. It was good and very filling!

The place is much smaller than expected and we noticed a lot of people ordered their food to go, which was a good thing for us since we were able to find seating in the patio area.
Great dim sim- not greasy and the soup dumplings hit the spot. So delish. I will be back!

Did this place buy their reviews???!!! I mean seriously... Holy cow, a roast pork place selling "famous steak"?? Both steak and pork tasted aweful!! A steak without cheesewiz!! Cant believe it... and the pork supposely their signature sandwich, all you taste is the seaseme from the bun and black pepper from the pork. It is wayyyyyyy too overpowering!!!!! Leaves bad tastes in your mouth for hours. If u really want to try, make sure u bring a bottle of water tk wash down the smell you try!!

I just feel like I need to update this review.  

I'm a regular here.  I average about three times a month for lunch.  I just have to say that one of the best things about this place is that they maintain the quality of their food.  I know exactly what I'm going to get every time.  This is very important to me because not every Indian restaurant in this area is good at that.  

While some Indian places have some dishes that might be tastier than what this place has, I can honestly say that I've never had a bad item here.  Maybe some places are more flavorful in some of their dishes.  But the important thing about Himalayan is that they are always well crowded during lunch.  This helps them do a better job in keeping the buffet fresh.  

Also, everyone I've ever taken here who is new to Indian food has come away more of a fan.  I think this place is perfect for "first-timers" on the buffet.  And there's enough spice to satisfy more experienced fans of Indian flavor.  Personal favorites of mine include the Gobi Manchiurian (best I've ever had of this dish), the Chicken Kabob Masala (I've never seen any other restaurant make this particular dish, and it's fantastic), and the Chili Chicken (goes perfectly if eaten on a hot piece of naan). 

Plus, the owner of this establishment is quite honestly the nicest guy you will ever meet.  It's at the point now where he knows my favorite dishes, and if they don't have them on the buffet, he will actually have the cook make some for me.  Let's just say I've never left here without having my Gobi Manchurian.  Great touch that keeps me coming back.  

Finally, 8 bucks for a lunch buffet, how can you beat that?

Very cool place. Kinda crazy inside and parking can be a nightmare. BUT! These are all minor things and fit with the atmosphere of the place and adds to the experience. Very fast service. Coke served in a bottle is a great choice but dont miss their aqua fresca. The thing that Ill be craving is their Elote. Get that, trust me. Great music. Oh and cash only, theres an ATM inside.
Great customer service, yummy cocktails and the food is fresh and hot. They have great specials of the day plus it's family friendly.

I am in town for work and a few of my local counterparts brought me to this restaurant. I wasn't sure what to expect but can I honestly say it was far better than so expected. The crab and bacon rangoon was excellent and the pork couldn't have been better. The service was also excellent. I will definitely be visiting this place again.

This place is awesome! Free queso appetizer with Yelp check-in, awesome food, and excellent friendly service (Thank you to our amazing server Daniel!). I would definitely recommend this restaurant if you are a tex-mex fan. The Baja tacos were awesome, and they even gave us a couple of free sopapillas for dessert. The wait wasn't bad at all, but we went kind of early (5 pm on a Saturday). Will definitely visit again!

Dine in at Sal's on Wednesday evening, February 29.  We were a group of 5 friends, all arriving at different times.  The staff was very warm and welcoming, providing a table for us away from the main dining room.

We ordered some wine, and chatted for a while before ordering.  This was our choice, and our server Sarah, was attentive yet not pushy.

First, the wine menu left a lot to be desired.  While we were not looking for fine wines, I was disappointed that there was so little to choose from (by the glass).  

Sarah brought bread, thick sliced, but very airy - like something you would get in the Wonder Bread section of the grocery isle.  I was not a big fan of the dipping oil either. It was orangy in color, and really lacked flavor.  Being an Italian restaurant, I would have expected some herbs or garlic in the oil, something a bit more bold.

We each ordered an entree or salad. I had spinach ravioli with house salad.  The salad was average, but fresh.  The ravioli were massive, 3 on my plate.  It was very tasty, although the red sauce was not as flavorful as I prefer.

Overall, we had an excellent experience. We obviously go out to eat for the food, but the service is equally important to me.  Sarah was great!  She is the reason I would go back, but try the pizza next time.  

I had confusion about the bill.  Our food items were on the bill without sales tax included, but the drinks included tax.  This makes it a bit confusing when trying to figure out the pre-tax total for tipping purposes.  It's not that I am trying to be "cheap", it's just that is how I always base the tip.
Went the for a Christmas party and the food was exceptional and the service and staff was great will definitely go back.
took 20 minutes to order and get our pizza but that wasnt a big deal. got home and the pizza was burnt and cold beyond belief. definitely dont go here for "hot and ready" pizza

Well this place doesn't look like much from the outside, but who cares when their sandwiches taste this good?! We had the Seminole and the Rolando with broccoli salad and potato salad. The Rolando was incredible! The pastrami melts in your mouth. Then we had to try the bread pudding with ice cream. Wow, it was perfectly sweet and moist. Delicious! I also had the cucumber and mint infused water which was super refreshing. Wish we lived closer so we could make our way through the menu!

A great neighborhood bar that I've never had a bad experience at.
Servers are attentive, but not overbearing - great beer offerings for their size and the food seems to get better every time I go there (And it started out really good too!)

Karaoke night's a blast, they've got nice big screen tv's to watch the game on - and the high hat tables give you a nice bar feel if you can't squeeze a stool at the bar proper.

If I had to describe this restaurant in one word it would be Delicious! The atmosphere really has you longing for the beach. I loved the use of mixed light woods and metals. The service was fantastic! Our waiter made great recommendations and guided us in our fantastic selections. The oysters were on point as well as the bloody marys. We had the lobster BLT and hot shrimp and avocado toast (brunch). There were so many other options that I would have loved to try. We will definitely be back to try their dinner menu!

Horrible, horrible, HORRIBLE!!!!!!!!!! Ordered my pizza online and the tracker said it'd be ready in about 10 mins. I got there 20 mins after my order had been placed and the pizza still wasn't made. Not only that, but the cashier, Tyquan was extremely f*****g rude!!! He was cutting me off while I was trying to explain my frustration over my pizza not being made and then proceeded to get loud and belligerent with me and literally almost came over the counter and assaulted me. After speaking with the manager AND the owner, they assured me his employment was terminated and tried to compensate for his actions. But it still doesn't change the situation. Plus, the pizza tasted horrible! NEVER AGAIN will I eat at ANY PIZZA HUT!!!!!!!!!

I had been meaning to try this place for a while.The counter service was good, and my sandwich came out fast, but I just wasn't really impressed with the food. 

I got the pulled chicken sandwich, and the sauce had a bit too much vinegar, without so much as a piece of lettuce to balance the flavor. The bun was plenty big, but sort of dry. And the black bean and corn salad was not really memorable. I had gone in hungry, but I didn't really finish anything.

Next time, I'll try something else, but I don't think I'll be rushing back to do so.
Love this place. They serve the true authentic andhra tiffins like no one else does in Saint Louis,have been here couple of times and they never disappointed me. My personal fav is rava dosa.

First , I love the Metro in Christiana . This was just the worse. Sunday morning, 9:15 crazy busy. Wait about 20 minutes for a spot at the counter with a friend. Ordered coffee and tea. They are out of decaffeinated tea. Ok. Asked for it with lemon. The lemon never comes. Ask again . Nope. I got up and got it my self. Finally the server takes our order. Wait 30 minutes. The manager comes over. There are no hash browns. They will be an hour if we want to wait. Really? To be honest they are the best hash browns ever. It's why I went there for breakfast. That was it. It's now 10:15 . No breakfast . We left and went to Hollywood Diner  down the street. What a mind numbing bad experience. If I was a first time guest I would never return. Basically ruined my morning.

Love love love this place! Had the Cabo shrimp & grits and I can now say it's one of my favorite foods! Our server was so sweet and everyone was so kind to stop and say hi to our pups! Loved the Shark attack drink! Perfect spot walking distance from where we are at! When restaurants say "dog friendly" this is the standard that it should be! Truly genuinely DOG FRIENDLY!!!
What's with the manager??? Horrible.  The staff are so much more  respectful than the person they are supposed to look up to.  Tip to the owner...deal with it

This place is so great. I usually only get coffee, but my husband and I ate breakfast there the other day. We got 2 sandwiches, a smoothie, and the Honey Bee coffee. So good! It was $23 for all of that, which really isn't bad for Nashville. 
I love the atmosphere...not hipster and judgemental, but not commercial and Green Hills-y. It's very easy to figure out and there's plenty of seating. 
Tip: park in the back to save yourself a headache.

Was here a couple of weeks ago with my two roomies. Wow! When u walk in, it's just such a kool place, very hip and futuristic. 
When we walked In we were promptly greeted, then escorted to our table which was surrounded by stylish chairs. We had no reservation btw and we were accommodated. This place was busy and still had great service from the waiter, which btw was very informative, knowledgeable and cute :)
I forget what I got but we got it on time and was delicious!!
Will definitely go back if I stayed here in Philly but I'm not. 
Of course, I still like my little hole in the wall sushi place in Downey,CA... I can't find any better place than that!

The water bottle was pretty the service was good but the food was bland. Expensive, $30 for two sandwiches. Could have made better at home. Looked like they went to Fry's for the bread. Will not go again.

Battista's Calzone is a place I try to take all of my friends for a quick bite when I happen to be in the area.  I love places that only do one thing, and do it right. The owner is always here and always smiling when he greets you. He's often trying out new recipes and is happy to share samples with his customers.

There are only a few different calzone choices on the menu here and they are all pretty great. The meatball and pesto are my favorites. 

These calzones are very light, so don't expect your typical cheese packed greasy calzone like you'd get from other pizza places. There's nothing wrong with those calzones, but sometimes you just prefer something lighter. And Battista nailed it.

Truly a hidden gem in the city for bottomless brunch! I went for the first time with some friends and it was very easy to get a reservation. The food choices are all very good and the portion size is great. Our waiter was awesome with constantly keeping our glasses full and even gave us one last to go mimosa! Nice ambience and great for groups as well as just two people.

When you want fried food near Franklin...the Boathouse has you covered. Coconut shrimp basket is certainly no slouch. There may be better to be had...but definetly not in the area. Great ambiance and service keep it in tbe 4 star arena.

was there for new years eve and could have been better - husbands salmon was dry and horrible - my steak was rare and baked potato not hot - also my sons girlfriend was not crazy about her entrée either - appetizers were good and service and atmosphere were great (fireplace was on) but left the restaurant feeling like we should have had a good meal !!! used to be regular but will not go back.

Delicious food!! Got the Tres Amigos- a combo plate with a cheese enchilada, a chili relleno and an quesadilla with beans and rice for only $12! So much food and so delicious!! The leftovers were even more delicious if it's possible!

Regular cheese pizza was definitely "meh"overall, but I loved the actual cheese on the pizza- definitely a blend of cheeses beyond standard mozzarella.  Additionally, the service was quick and friendly and offered a cash discount.

You must Gojo here! Their food is so good and unreasonably affordable. I have taken several of my friends here and gone on many date nights with the girlfriend, and every single time we have left impressed, satisfied, and happy. The restaurant itself is small, pretty low key, and family run. They have a lot of great offerings, but I would recommend getting either the meat and veggie sampler or the veggie sampler if meat is not your thing. You get to pick four different items for either one and it costs about $12. Generally, two orders seems to be enough to fill up four hungry but not starving people - especially if you also get an order or two of their delicious sambussas to start with. Also, super awesome, they are a BYO as well. So you can bring your favorite wine/beer to go along with all of that great food. If you are looking for a change of pace from the normal Nashville food scene, definitely give this place a try.

The biscuit I had here was definitely the greatest biscuit I've ever had. My husband and I were in town for the weekend and heard this was the place to try. We went on a Sunday just before 9 and only had to wait about 10 minutes in the line, but by the time we left 30 minutes later the line was really long. 

I had the east nasty and my husband had an item a worker mentioned on their special menu, called the nasty princess (combining the east nasty and the princess). The chicken was really good on my sandwich, and the biscuit was awesome, but I wasn't a fan of the gravy. I couldn't really taste it on my sandwich, and it felt like it was just there. I definitely wouldn't wait in a super long line to eat here, but it was decent and I'd come back if I was in Nashville again.

I love Hymie's and have been going here for 8 years, seeing that this diner/deli is less than a mile from where I went to both high school and college. They have a pickle bar here, they sell their bread and famous matzo ball soup to go and they have an abundance of baked goods and deserts that you can get get to go. You can also get their infamous turkey, meats and cheeses by the pound so you can make your own mouthwatering sandwiches at home. Major plus! 

I am a huge fan of the classic turkey club sandwich- the bacon and rye bread make it irresistible. I find that there is always too much turkey on my sandwich, and I always end up taking half of it off and taking it home to make lunch with the following day- not a bad problem, but the way it comes, it can hardly fit in your mouth. My sister loves the French dip- it is excellent and the meat is cooked to perfection. My mom comes for the endless pickle bar- any pickle you can imagine and she loves that. The menu options are endless here.

The only drawback is that there is usually always a wait, especially on weekends. They could also use some more seating in here, given its popularity. It's always crowded and the layout makes it hard to move around sometimes. I would advise getting your order to go or buying your cold cuts and cheese to take home- you can't beat the freshness and quality of Hymie's products! You don't want to miss this deli!

Chips and salsa come to the table as you are seated.  

I ordered the veggie mercados (veggie tacos).  Came with three for $7.25
The tortilla was authentic and delicious and the veggies were superb.

The restaurant itself is very nice and the food was good. The hush puppies were great, very dense. I also had the steak with fries and béarnaise sauce which was delicious. Wouldn't recommend the ginger sazerac to drink unless you really like the taste of alcohol, it tasted like I was drinking a glass of fireball.

We continue to return to Nardonne's and once again, we had an excellent meal and very enjoyable interaction with the staff. Laughingly, they seemingly know our preferences even without us asking. Nardonne's is exactly what we prefer when we dine out. Clean, well-appointed, reasonably priced, great food served by interested, smiling people who thank you for your patronage and make the evening a pleasure!

Agree with the other reviews out there. The falafel was good once I got through the bad lettuce, tomato, and too much dressing!

The seasoned fries were the highlight and I'm pretty sure that's not Greek.

Fun family-oriented restaurant. I had the western burger with fries. Very tasty! Rhonda, my server, was very nice and stopped to visit with me. The menu is extensive. I will be back to try one of their dinner items and desserts.

I went for lunch and had a nice meal. The Food seemed carefully prepared and the I had a grilled calamari which was very tasty. The place was a bit pricey for lunch, ( it is near Rittenhouse though) but the food was of a good quality for the price. I would recommend it to others and will be back.
Great food and friendly staff! The service is very good. The shrimp creole was amazing!

Oh. And this is my message I got in return for my review. 

"Don't forget to give 5 star review, bi***"  

Then a "compliment" calling a bi*** again. 

Ok then.  Yelp is not for honest reviews, according to this restaurant. Fun times.

Dickmans is a carnivores delight. Go there for quality choice meat. Into exotic meats? They've got you covered too. Prefer to grab a sandwich! They've got that too! Really- they have so much to choose from and will make sure you leave happy.
My favorite store is Babylon market ,I always found what I want in this store, the halal meat is very good quality

I'm only putting one star because it requires me to put 1 star. I was having a fun night out and then I decided to come here with my sister who is DD but is 20 and the lady kicked us out when it was EMPTY because she wasn't 21 and all she got was a water and now I see why they dont have clientele here. RULES SHOULD BE CHANGED.

This is one of those places to where nearly everyone that works here is a millennial and they have a stuck up attitude. The food was okay and the service was okay. Nothing extraordinary at all. I may or may not go back because there are so many other better places to go.

This dinner was much better than the last time I ate here back in February of 2013.  Our server was absolutely delightful and very energetic with a great sense of humor.  It's surprising what a difference the fine dining and kitchen is compared to the casual sports bar dining here at the Junction. 

We brought a bottle of wine from home and since I'm an employee at Whispering Vine I also brought with me a special card for a free corkage fee, which helped save us money on our bill in the end  (I'm your gal if you want to acquire on of these in the future, maybe).  We brought our bottle to the restaurant an hour or so in advance then we walked around the casino for a while until our reservation time, about 8:15 on a Friday night.  When we arrived a little early they had our bottle of wine already sitting on our table, which was an incredible booth facing the restaurant by the elegant front entrance.

We started our meal with two appetizers: the tuna tar tare with cucumber and the AMAZING crab cake, my favorite was the crab cake for sure.  Their rolls of the evening came in a lovely basket wrapped in white cloth and consisted of a wheat roll and a cheesy roll, both were warm and delicious, but we constantly needed more butter.  

For dinner I ordered the amazing Chilean sea bass with lobster chunks and mashed potatoes.  I'd never actually had sea bass before and to me it tasted a bit like crab meat, the texture was superb.  I saved half for lunch the next day.  My date ordered the rib-eye with scalloped potatoes, he enjoyed every bite.  We passed on dessert and finished our wine and were then given a damp, warm cloth to clean up.

This was a lovely Friday night at the Tamarack!
Our new favorite place to eat! The food is amazing and the employees are very friendly.

Commanders needs another review like I need another hole in the head, but if I had only one meal to eat in Nola this would be it. And it would include Turtle Soup and a bread pudding souffle. These are the things dreams are made of. I laughed with the guy who took my bowl away (which I all but licked) that I didn't even want to think about what went in the soup and preferred to think "veal" he winked at me. Proof it's veal like the rumor goes? I hope so.

We always move around on entrees and they're always exceptional (Bob leans towards beef and me to seafood) Service sets the standard. Just go here. That is all the advice I have.

Just one more piece of advice...if it's your birthday decline the balloons and hat. We did. Who wants to be living the dream in a dorky hat that Dick's last resort would stick on your head? Not I. Not Bob.

This place has a fun atmosphere, sitting inside or out.  It's true and authentic.  They make a pretty good pizza too.  I haven't ventured much past a plain pepperoni, but I have never been disappointed with the food.  

The one thing I will say is that I've been disappointed with the service, each and every time.  Slow as molasses!  It doesn't matter if it's busy or not, you aren't getting in and out of there in under an hour.

In addition to a coloring paper and crayons, they've hit the mastery on entertaining kiddos while they eat - - - a small handful of pizza dough.  Best idea ever!  I guess that is supposed to make up for the really long wait times and trying to entertain the kids!

This place appears to be a poorly done version of Another Broken Egg. The chicken and waffles may just be the worst chicken and waffles you can purchase in all of Tampa Bay. The chicken was rubbery and appeared to be frozen tenders. The waffle was tough and chewy. I would have brought it to the attention of the waitress but we saw her so infrequently that by the time she came around I just wanted my check so I could get out of there. There's a lot better options in the area for brunch.
filthy needs a makeover bad new carpet for sure and better restaurants that fit the community

Oh good heavens.

This restaurant is seriously the best I've had all year. I'm from out of town and this place has definitely left an imprint on me! We ordered Tabbouli, tzsaziki, baba ganoush, and a flatbread. Everything was incredible. Absolutely no complaints here! Wish I had a chance to try everything else on the menu. Great atmosphere, amazing food. 10/10
I know a lot of people love this place, but I was disappointed. I really didn't think the food was any better than say Filibertos. Just not my cup of tea.

Just ordered a few rolls to go and seriously just ate the best sushi I've ever had! Ordered the panko salmon roll and corona roll and they were both so ridiculously good. My only complaint is how full I am from trying to eat it all. I can't wait to go back! Such a great addition to East Nash!
So good. Had lunch and very good. Had cheesesteak sandwich with fries. Fries weren't as warm as should have been. Still good though. Someone also cauliflower tacos--excellent!!
McEEK! ME THINKS NOT! McHeart failure, Mcliver failure, obesity #2 cause of MCdeath! McNever happening!

First off, let me say upfront, we didn't try the food. First impressions are everything. If you found a cockroach in your salad you would probably immediately walk out. We called to make a to-go order and our call was answered by a human cockroach.

It really isn't that hard, even if you hate your job and hate your life, to at least pretend to be polite and attempt to be helpful. Don't be condescending to new customers who have simple questions about your menu. If a customer twice proclaims that they have never eaten there DON'T SCOLD THEM FOR NOT KNOWING THE MENU! Suck it up put a fake smile in your voice and be a useful human being.

Also, When you have two other BBQ places that may be just as good all within a block of each other, it might be a good idea to put your best foot forward and not be a creep. The customer will put THEIR best foot forward and go, literally, across the street to your competitor.

I'm feeling lazy now so i'll just wrap up by paraphrasing Edward W's review... 

just attempted to have my first meal from Champion BBQ and it was infuriating my mind is still dancing with sadness from the lack of standards and human decency. As my imaginary daughter would say "any where but there."  Its doesn't stand a chance of making my speed dial and I will raise a finger to salute you as I drive by.

Debating between 3 and 4 stars but giving them the 4 because of the wonderful service and the fact that it's BYOB. 

It was 10:15 on a Friday night and the restaurant door was already locked. I called earlier to ask what time they close and she said the kitchen closes at 11pm. Okay, so I peeped through the window and saw no one inside but I decided to call anyway to see what the deal was. She said they are starting to close the kitchen but will kindly let us in. I felt bad to keep the restaurant open just for me and my boyfriend but honestly I've been banking to try this Turkish restaurant out for awhile so I really didn't feel too bad (*smirk*).

Mix Meze - love, love, love. The acili ezme (spicy red dip) and humus were hands down my favorite. Also comes with unlimited pita bread. 

Lamb Chops - Good, not great. Could've been more flavorful plus in my opinion $28 is a little too pricey for 4 pieces of lamb with some couscous and salad. 

Manti (turkish ravioli) - would not recommend. Way too much oil and I could barely taste the meat. If you really want to try it, I would suggest asking going easy on the oil and make it more spicy/flavorful

Quick easy place for a breakfast sandwich. I had a standard pork roll, egg, and cheese on a kaiser roll. I sacrificed most of my mouth, because it was piping hot until almost my last bite. All of the ingredients were fresh and the best part of the sandwich was by far the egg. They have a limited amount of counter space and a few tables to eat in, but most people take-out.

I came here for brunch with a party of 6. We did have to wait some time to be seated but were rewarded with a table outside. The service staff is very, very good. The hostess, the waitress, manager and bus staff all stopped at our table at some point to drop off food, clear the table, or refill drinks. And they did all that without making it feel overbearing.

This place is well worth the wait to see what all the fuss is about.

"In America, the professional kitchen is the last refuge of the misfit. It's a place for people with bad pasts to find a new family."-- Anthony Bourdain

I found myself in the heart of NOLA, in the French Quarter, and the only place that I knew in the area is Villalobos Rescue Center, which is home to Animal Planets, "Pit Bulls and Parolees". They have a restaurant near the French Market, along the Mississippi River, where each time you drink you feed a dog! Tahyo means big hungry dog in Cajun and pronounced TAY-YOUR. 

68th person to review Tahyo and my 468th Yelp review

In 1987 a terrible attack involving a Pit became highly publicized making Pit Bills the new American misfit as many know-- a stigma that still surrounds the breed. Villalobos cares for hundreds of Pits, providing medical care and getting forever homes. In addition to that, the owner, Tia, hires parolees to help foster their development and acclimate back into society in the hopes of lessening recidivism. The Pit's seem to be therapeutic for people, and the "parolees" find a purpose and specials connection with the animals-- as it is, they're both the underdog, living in the shadows of past mistakes. 

I digress-- this review is on the restaurant, but I wanted you to have the backstory as to what the mission is and who Tahyo exists.  

I approached the corner lot on a cold day. I felt a little lost and overwhelmed by all options available, enticed by the many bars, clubs, music, and people but I pushed through and made my first meal in NOLA here at Tahyo and you know what, I'm really glad I did. And I will again, and again, and again. 

The inside is smallish. They have a bar-- friendly, genuine people. I sparked a conversation-- FREE DRINK WHEN YOU CHECK IN ON YELP! I had a Lucky, which was super good. There weren't any other customers in there when I was there, but the echo of "Who DAT" was a reminder that the majority of the town was at the Saints Game at the Super Dome less than a mile away. As I sipped on Lucky and watched the Saints game on the television inside the bar area, I could hear the chants of the fans coming from the stadium just down the road-- that was super cool for the record and somewhat surreal. 

I wanted to try something different-- after all, I am (was) in the Big Easy! 
I ordered their southern take on curry-- and I am so glad I did. I didn't eat too much of it but I took it back to my hotel and ate it over several days. They gave me a doggy paw bag to place my leftovers in-- cute pun (see photo). 

They have drinks named after real dogs at the center-- Each time you drink, a dog gets fed. I don't know about you, but there is nothing better than good libations, food, and giving back, especially to the underdogs-- the ones that can't speak for themselves--
