I encourage you to check out both the television show and this restaurant. Be sure to visit the rescue center, too, if you're in the area. You can help walk some dogs, or clean up if you'd like. 

Anyone local that hasn't been? I am in NOLA from Idaho every other week and I'd be happy to meet you for an UYE! 

http://www.vrcpitbull.com/
https://www.animalplanet.com/tv-shows/pitbulls-and-parolees/

Special thanks to Dani S. My irl friend I met on Yelp... You know why :)

What will save me from the wasteland of Santa Barbara's Asian food selection? Red Pepper to the rescue!

Although I am Cantonese and prefer my Cantonese dishes I will eat here at this Mandarin centered restaurant. I usually go during lunch time because they have the best lunch specials! You get a ton of food for under 10 dolla. I usually order the kung pao combination and think it is pretty delicious. I also suggest the fried onion pancake which is quite crispy and tasty with the sauce. My friends like the shaolin bao, but I think it is just okay. And I think the fortune cookies taste a little weird.

The best part and most important part of the Red Pepper experience (echoing other reviewers) is the lady of the restaurant - the one who greets you with a smile when you enter and hugs you when you leave. She is kind and welcoming and makes you want to come back.

This place is exactly what it says... Po Boys.  But they are excellent!  From their 'imported' bread, to their beignets for dessert... if you want to feel a little Louisiana, it' a great place to go.  It's become a regular place for us to go for a quick meal that we can thoroughly enjoy!

Doesn't look like much walking by but wow was it worth the stop in. 
Tacos were amazing. Guacamole was better than most in California. Margarita was to die twice for.

the house of Bayona has proven the test of time.  if you are looking for really good food and excellent service for a special night out in the french quarter, this place should be on your list of considerations.  

we had perfect service and all the food was done to perfection.  none of it is cheap, but the prices of bayona reflect the location and susan spicer's culinary history.  

the garlic soup, we knew the recipe is published, but we wanted to try the original before attempting it ourselves at home.  both were good (home version and bayona tasted the same).  we also had the scallops (appetizer), and the duck.

I've tried a few different tacos from Capital's menu. I've never been disappointed. The tiger shrimp tacos are my favorite, but they have a huge variety The tacos are above and beyond any others I've had at the many taco joints in the Bay area, which is saying a lot.
Disappointed that the St. Pete locations have closed. They are actually closer to home.

I love this restaurant so much I have to make myself stay away. I think Bonefish has just gotten better and better over the years.  I love the seasonal items on the menu because it gives the restaurant some variety that it might otherwise lack being a chain.  My favorite item while not a seasonal one is the bang bang shrimp.  Another side of Bonefish that you might know about is there willingness to donate to non-profit organizations. I am a part of a non-profit and usually contact  Bonefish once a year for a donation. Not once have they turned me down.  I thank them for this, and it makes me want to spread the word about how awesome this restaurant is.  The institution of Bonefish is amazing and their food is equally amazing so they have a customer for life! Thanks Bonefish!

I wanted to like this place more. It sounded a bit like Treo: a nice bar with a nice dining option. Maybe we just had a bad night, and maybe we would have liked it more if it hadn't been SO DARN COLD in there. I know this is typical of restaurants and they'll never learn: the staff is working and is hot, so they crank the AC. But this small dining room, with the window unit pointing right across the space, was simply too cold to be comfortable. We saw one table get up and finish their drinks outside. In August. When nobody wants to be outside. We actually ended up doing that also.
So....the menu was nice, with an interesting selection of items. I had a good beer, my date had great wine, and we ordered food. After freezing for a very long time, and being assured once that "the food was coming", our waitress did finally realize she forgot to put our order in. She handled it well and professionally, and I really don't want to make too big of a deal about a human mistake that was owned up to. But it was SO COLD. It was August. We were dressed for August. This isn't San Francisco, where you're used to carrying a sweater or jacket. 

So, the food finally got there. And it was okay. Not bad at all. And as soon as we finished, we asked for the check so we could finish our drinks outside. The drink we had to finish was a comp glass of wine, as an apology for the mix up, so that was nice.

Way too many restaurants are oblivious to how cold they keep their dining rooms, and to how to design/decorate to help with noise. This room was also noisy when we first arrived and it was a little crowded. But not just 'crowded room' noisy, but hard ceiling, hard floors, hard corners, lots of noise reflecting, noisy. Maybe plants, maybe soft things hanging in the corners, Or, maybe we were just too cold to relax. 

Too bad...I wanted to enjoy this place more. Very nice people.

This place is amazing!!! Mimosas are delish with the fresh oj. We went twice while there for the weekend and never had anything bad. It's a little small but service is great. It's a counter order place. Food is made fresh.

I cannot rave about this place enough. Went here with a party of six and for 2 (HUGE) pitchers of margaritas (literally I think there were 12 glasses in each), 6 entrees, salsa, guacamole, queso and shots of patron it was only $130 (not bad in my book). Not only that, but the food was delicious, the staff was beyond friendly, and they have a trio who walk around singing and playing music (they do a killer Santana cover!).  We drank, we ate, we laughed, and they even brought out a big sombrero and dessert for my mom's birthday (much to her embarrassment). 

The food was delicious, but pretty standard. The only thing I can complain about is the fact that some of the entrees come with rice OR beans (not both) and I asked to have both and they said they couldn't do that (Hmmm...?). We had the following and there were no complaints from us!

Tilapia tacos with rice, steak fajitas, bean burritos, chicken enchiladas, chicken chimichanga, and steak enchiladas. Also the salsa and chips are complimentary and they keep bringing more! The queso and guac were gone within seconds of hitting the table!

I would love to go back and do it again soon!

Came here for brunch with my boyfriend's family. Although there aren't many vegetarian options, the ones that they have are quite good.

The vegetable hash was excellent, all of the veggie cooked to perfection! Served with a sliced of grilled bread and butter? Yum! 

I met one of the men, Bob, and he was incredibly kind and welcoming. A great face for a restaurant.

The only downside was our waitress who was rude. It was a Sunday morning so I suppose it can be excused! Nobody wants to work on a Sunday!

2 Tha Joint is one of my favorite sushi restaurants in town. They offer a huge variety of bothe raw and cooked rolls this is nice for my husband and I because he isn't able to eat raw sushi. I like there Calamari they cook it perfectly. I also enjoy the seaweed salad. I LOVE tha sassy tuna, tha BLC, tha escape, tha spider. I feel like they give a good balance of the rice and fish some places give you so much rice that if fills me up after after one or two rolls.  Also the diameter of the rolls is great they are  skinny enough to get a piece in my mouth in one bite. Staff is great on top of service and polite checking in often. It also seems that they work well together as a team and communicate regularly with each other.

Growing up a Gentilly denizen in Edgewood Park, McKenzie's Chicken In a Box was a semi-regular meal offering at our house.  Although not my favorite chicken as a child, my parents liked it; therefore, my sister and I had no other choice for dinner when it was served.  Don't get me wrong, as there was absolutely nothing wrong with this chicken.  However, as kids, my sister and I were always wanting the television advertised chicken from Popeyes and/or Church's chicken. But I digress.

Frying chicken can get messy, especially if you don't have a deep fryer and you are using your trusty cast iron frying pan.  McKenzie's chicken "looks" more like home made chicken than all the other local offerings.  The pieces seem to be a little smaller, but perhaps they use smaller birds.  Who knows.  I find the flavor to be good but the skin is sometimes inconsistently cooked.  At times it can be nice and crispy, but sometimes it can be a little chewy.

The sides dishes are decent at best, with the dirty rice being my favorite of the limited options.  Now that I live in Lakeview, this is not my go to place for fried chicken.
Amazing service! Thank you Chasleigh!!!  I hate going out if the  service isn't great, but she was on point and very attentive. Also best wings ever!

Eat somewhere else in the neighborhood.  Sit at the bar here. The food is average...and that's generous. If you chose to sit at the smallest 4 top tables ever assembled be prepared be constantly moving plates and glasses around to accommodate your drink or plate. And you had better hope you like your tablemates..because you will be in each other's way all night.

The music is good..,but this is not the millennial version of the Latin casino or copa they hoped it would be

My wife and I had a lovely meal at Herbsaint.  The cocktails were inventive and deftly executed.  I greatly enjoyed the fried oysters.  The cornmeal breading had great texture and was fried to perfection.  The oysters remained moist and flavorful.  The beef short rib was moist and flavorful.  It was wonderful to see goat on the menu and in this case the crisping provided a wonderful textural contrast.  The fleur de sel caramel accented the banana wonderfully in our tart.  Our service was excellent--attentive without being overbearing.  We would highly recommend Herbsaint.

Generally speaking, I have never been a fan of this chain. So, I was expecting the worse, a crowded, messy room filled to capacity with children and overwhelmed staff. However this location was far from that. I was here with my little ones for a  birthday party. There was a designated party table and host. The play areas as well as the bathroom was clean. All the staff were very friendly and accommodating. We were there Saturday afternoon and it was surprisingly not crowded. I will say there were a fair amount of activities for toddlers and older kids. Both my kids 4 and 10 had a great time. 

The concession stand could use some help. I ordered wings for me and the hubby and it took forever. On the plus side they delivered it to the table eventually. They were good and came with a celery and dressing. Overall a good day out with kids.

I live quite close to this place and tried it for the first time a few days ago when the roomie brought home some chicken fajitas for me. The veggies tasted fresh and tender-crisp and the chicken was well-seasoned. They were served with corn tortillas which I'm usually not a huge fan of but these were soft, warm, and delicious. The rice that was served with the fajitas was a little bland and the beans were so-so. It's a place i'd definitely return to again for some yummy mostly-authentic Mexican food.

Horrible experience. Food was bland, waitress was ditzy and overall overpriced. I've had better food from Trader Joe's frozen meals. Party of 6 and we all left feeling sick as well. I highly recommend saving yourself the trouble and just avoid this place like the plague. Extremely disappointed.

So good - one of my goto places when I go to DTSP.  I love their cider options.  My fave menu item is the shrimp scampi pizza.  Excellent!  Atmosphere is fun and relaxed and great place to bring visitors to.

Phenomenal service, this place has.

We were here the other day for a brunch and had 12 people total all with specific and very different orders. The waitress that served us knocked it out of the park and was very efficient with the timeliness of the order.

Honestly, the service staff here is probably one of the most attentive staffs I have ever seen at a restaurant. It's honestly impressive with how busy it always is and they really do it from memory a lot of times.

Usually when I come here, I get the deluxe nachos with beef. I always underestimate the portion size of this meal, because it always comes out on a huge plate spread out perfectly with the perfect ratio of the different ingredients.

Biscuits also has recently opened up a new spot with in the restaurant to make more space. It used to feel a little cramped but with the new back area extending to the bar, there is a lot more room to go through the restaurant and less wait time.

I got a small Bloody Mary and it was everything, but small. So be weary before you think about ordering that medium sized mimosa or Bloody Mary. The portion is bigger than you will think.

I love that this is not only a breakfast place, but a Mexican restaurant. You would honestly have no clue with the name of the restaurant and the location, but it certainly does not disappoint. 

I like that it is a diner/cafe feel to it, so it is nice looking back and being to see what the kitchen staff is making and gives you the right anticipation of when your food is coming.

The food here is also very reasonably priced and you will leave satisfied. The only negative part of this experience is that you can easily overeat and might feel heavy afterward, so be attentive of how hungry you actually are. 

This is definitely one of the go-to places when I'm in the Broad Ripple area.

I wanted this place to amaze me, I really did.  Alas, I left with more bad memories than good.  

The Good:

1)  The staff was friendly, knowledgeable and eager to help without being pesky about it.  But their recommendations always seemed to be towards the most expensive thing on the menu.  

2)  The setting.  This place is beautiful.  The decor and how they have the place laid out is great.

The Average:

1) The food.  High in price (which was expected), but average in preparation and taste.  There was nothing bad about what I had, and it all tasted fine, but I wasn't "wow'd".  A great steakhouse stands out for their food.

The Bad:

1) The acoustics of the place.  My date and I couldn't even hear each other talk since the room they had us in echoed the conversations of the other tables around us so loudly.  It was so bad, we asked to be seated elsewhere and the only place they said was open was the bar area.  Since we went on a Tuesday night, I think they just didn't want to open rooms that weren't being used.

2) The lack of a proper beer menu.  The wine list seems good, but I wouldn't know since I don't like wine.  I like beer.  Why a steak house wouldn't have a beer menu with more depth is beyond me.
Great Lasagna (beef) delicious Italian cold cuts. Nice fresh selection of Italian bites... Friendly staff.

We had my step-son and his fiancée's family-style. rehearsal dinner here and it could not have been better.  The service was beyond wonderful.  Josie, Nick and the rest of the crew helped make this a memorable event. There were a lot of first-timers eating at Caruso's and they were wowed by the food.  The Sunday gravy with ziti, the chicken Parmesan and the ravioli alla vodka we all excellent. We all look forward to having future dinners here.

It is not a fluke..I repeat it is not a fluke.

This is the second time I have tried Joe's Steaks and they are tremendous. Seriously you do not have to travel all around the city searching for the best cheesesteak as once you reach this level of excellenence its really just spinning your wheels. If you are ever in the area of Fishtown this is the place for a A+ Cheesesteak. The seating can be very hard to come by and you MUST tell them when you order if you are dining in or not....or they will throw you out or politely ask you to leave if you sit down. And if you are a beer drinker I highly recommend you take your cheesesteak across the street to the Garagae bar where you can shoot some pool, play the jukebox, or order one of there beers (They have over 200 to choose from)

Cheers! And SYOY!!!

I had lunch here for the first time, and what a nice experience! They have many different types of gyros, but I went with the classic. I did opt for feta and spicy tzatziki sauce vs regular tzatziki. It was delicious and very large. I was glad I didn't get any fries with it. I will definitely return.

My husband found this place on Yelp last week. He has been dragging me around Tampa trying to find good Mexican food and we had all but given up in finding any. When he asked to go here I was really weary, thinking that we were about to waste even more money on sub-par Mexican. 

Luckily I was wrong! This still doesn't quite compare to the Mexican food I grew up with in California but it is the best we have found in Tampa by far. The menu is very limited (tacos, sopes, and tortas. Tamales on Fridays and Saturdays). The first time we went  we each got a shrimp taco and a chicken torta. The taco was perfect, the only thing missing from the torta (in my opinion) were beans. The guy up front told us that they do have beans and he would give us some next time.

We went two days later to try the tamales. They were amazing! I don't really like green sauce so I asked for the chicken tamale with red sauce. They are already premade with green sauce in them, but it wasn't too much at all. It added just the right amount of flavor. My husband also ordered a sope which was very good.

The food is very very good and the service and staff are really amazing. They truly go above and beyond. They are a new business and they want your honest opinion so that they can improve things (there really isn't anything to improve!) We will definitely be back here many times. I think we are going to try to make it a Friday lunch tradition to get more of those tamales, they really were good, and at $2.50 each they really can't be beat! One more thing, the prices here are very good. You could easily get a meal for around $5.

The lady working the counter was awesome. She's one of the friendliest customer service people I've come across in a very long time. 

The place itself is pretty cozy, and seemed to service a lot of elderly people. It was sort of like an old school diner feel (which I like). 

I ordered one of their skillets which was very good. I kind of appreciate that they don't add a lot of salt to their food. I was told that their egg salad was good too. However, when I tried the pancakes, it hard a super weird taste to it. I don't know if something was bad in the batter, or if they add a super weird ingredient to it... Either way, I felt pretty bad to ask because the experience was good otherwise so I let it go.

Overall the experience was good, and I can see us coming back. Id recommend the skillet to anyone because they aren't too many places that have them in the area, and it's a very good portion for a fantastic price!

I just love the Trail's End Cafe! It's a wonderful place to stop off for iced tea after walking down the trail with a friend, and great place meet to sit and chat. Checking out the featured art is something I look forward to. What a neighborhood treasure!

I've never had a bad experience at J Bucks, but I've never really had a remarkable one here, either. It's one of those places that I avoid, unless someone really wants to meet here. 

Don't get me wrong, the bartenders and servers are all very nice. The beer selection is fine and they even offer a decent happy hour. It's just the fact that J Buck's is always crowded and I don't really understand why. There are so many other great happy hour spots in Clayton, why would you stick around at a mediocre establishment?

Maybe it's the clientele that irks me. Usually it's full of people who want to be "somebody" but didn't get the memo that the A-listers don't hang out at J Buck's. It's kind of sad. But not sad enough to get more than three stars from me :)

i have been here 100 times. all different times of the day, including 4 in the morning. that is my favorite time to go. people watching at that time is magic. Like everyone else said. it's a diner. with diner food. but their french onion soup is the best in town. i went this morning after a long night of drinking. it always makes me feel better. it was mobbed and i was seated in 2 minutes. the pastries are great as well.i usually grab some on the way out as an impulse thing. the service is fun.i like that theyre a little angry. it cant be an easy job. but i have never had bad service.

This is the 3rd time I've come in for lunch and walked out without even being seen or spoken to by staff, the drive thru line is small, I get into the shop and only one person is in line. It still takes 15 minutes to get that one person's order, then the cashier has to call the manager to complete his order. Pathetic. Overpiced elementary school lunchroom food paired with bad service. I only ever came in for an order of cheese curds and a small soda  and you can't even deliver that in 10 minutes for almost $10? A&W here I come.

It's OK. It's not terrible. I have had better, but I think the thing that saves this place is the portions and family style seating. Both go hand in hand. It's basically like a less done-up Buca di Beppo in Brandon. Huge portions because they expect you to share. Try the dishes with the sun-dried tomatoes. Delicious.

But, basically, if your family is in town and they don't mind Italian or sharing, then give this place a try.

I was incredibly impressed with this Waffle House. I hate having to go to these when we travel but they are my husbands favorite. This was THE CLEANEST Waffle House I had ever been in and I've been in probably 10. Fast, efficient, CLEAN, not greasy!!!!! And so so so sweet. Even the bathroom was clean and updated. This location is a game changer. Kudos
Charming, friendly people, great food, on the way to the beach.

This is such a neat throw back place!! It reminds me of a 50s burger place combined with that hole in the wall feeling of a small family business!  The burgers are fantastic and there are lots of choices for sides.  Don't expect this to be a diet option though.  This place is pure guilty pleasure!! I had their mushroom burger sooo yummy!!!

The food is good, but the host/owner was so rude during my last time there that I will definitely not be going back again.  While having coffee at the end of our meal, I gave my two small sons a cookie from the bakery two stores down for behaving so well at dinner.  The owner said they were not allowed to have it because, if they wanted dessert,they could order it from them. My sons are 2 and 5 and would not eat tiramisu. I would completely understand if my mother or I had brought in desserts for ourselves, but this was just a small cookie apiece for a little boy. I was so appalled that I spoke with him, but he was disgustly rude and refused to see how ridiculous he was being. Talk about penny wise and pound foolish - we had a decent meal but will not go back due to the owner. I wonder if sippy cups will be outlawed next so that parents will have to buy milk there for their children...

Visiting my retired parents in Florida, we stopped by here after checking out the mermaid show, with the family, at Weeki Wachee.  For an informal, "Panera" type feel, this Greek spot was on point!  We enjoyed everything on the menu (we stayed on the vegetarian side) - so that included the pita chips (very large portions) as well as the falafel.  The only negative was the hummus.  It was not creamy nor fresh (it tasted like it had freezer burn), but hopefully next time I'm visiting my parents, that won't be the case.
What a gem! Lovely staff, delicious food. Chicken and waffles and the sausage gravy were our favorites.

Good food, great drinks and reasonable prices. It's a comfortable atmosphere and my friends and I had a great time there last week for our girl's night out. The only bummer was that they had a decent tequila selection that I wanted to try but it was a tad pricey. No doubt I'll go back but I'll have to start a tequila fund.

Stopped in after dining down the strèet and was extremely shocked and displeased that they did not have one single sugar free option. Diabetes is a worldwide epidemic and there was nothing I could have that wouldn't spike my blood sugar. I only ate half of what I chose and threw the rest away. Other frozen yogurt places have sugar free options, including a sugar free chocolate syrup. This place had limited toppings and nothing sugar free at all. I will not be back.

This place opened recently and I've fallen in love with their decor and friendly staff. It's actually my favorite cafe in the neighborhood. They have bubble tea, shaved ice, lattes, coffee, sweets, and more. It's a pretty small cafe so it might be easy to miss but once you walk in, you'll be happy you did.

Split the sampler platter and was more than impressed. The muffins they serve beforehand are a really great touch as well. Our waitress was wonderful, very sweet, and she checked on us regularly.  Such a great experience!

We ate here a couple nights during our stay and were pretty pleased. I can't say much about a wait or anything because both times it was well after the dinner hour. Our servers were always prompt and very pleasant. They also were able to help me determine what was gluten free on their menu. 

The atmosphere is beautiful with lots if soft blue and water themed decorations. Huge bay windows right on the water and nice low lighting to give it a casual feeling.

The menu had a decent amount of options for gluten free. I don't remember there being a ton of options, but enough to find something I'd like.

I don't recall everything I tried but I do remember having the shrimp cocktail, sharing an entree and having their creme brûlée. Everything was good and the cream brûlée especially memorable. 

Price wise, things are pricey as you'd expect in a hotel restaurant, but not exuberant. Portion size was alright, perhaps a little smaller than normal. 

Overall I think it's a great hotel restaurant with tasty options, some of which are gluten free. Id be happy to eat here again.

Really disappointing experience! Had walked in and didn't see a "please wait to be seated sign". Went ahead sat a table as there were many tables available to pick from. Bartenders saw us walked in and didn't acknowledge us. Was hoping to be greeted by a server and she just had walked past us multiple times. Didn't even get any menus. Waited about 15 minutes to only find out kitchen closes @ 9pm. Only way I found out is I overheard the bartender telling another customer. My party got up and left. We won't be returning
My wife and I had lunch a La V and it was great. She had the fusion fried rice and I had the beef Pho. The service was good and our food came out quickly. We will be back.
This pizza is terrible. No red sauce at all it seemed. Pizza was so dry and salty. Tasted as if I was eating a salt block. Blah!
Excellent food for a very good price.

Party Fowl is a busy, high-energy and fun atmosphere restaurant with a dog-friendly patio.  The decor is fun and well suited for Nashville.  The patio is a great addition for dog-lovers, as well as people who want to eat outside and enjoy the beautiful local climate year-round.  
We made a reservation, were seated right away and ordered a Hot Chicken Cheddar Sandwich with chips (which was excellent), and a Kale Salad with Chicken.  The Kale Salad was a messy miss.  The kale had long stringy stalks that weren't trimmed which made eating it with a fork and knife impossible.  The dish would be better served with a fork and a spaghetti spoon.  I ended up just eating the chicken (which was overcooked and dry) and diced vegetables.  The server never asked about the almost full plate he took back to the kitchen, and handed us our check right away when clearing plates.  
I truly hope that the Management can correct the issues with this dish, because the homemade dressing was terrific!

We went here for SIPs because it seemed to have one of the best varieties of SIPs offerings- drinks and food-wise- out there. We got the pulled pork sliders, truffle fries, and grilled flat bread which were all pretty good and even better at half price. The flat bread dough was a little odd for an Italian place- more like a tortilla/ pita mix then pizza.

We ate dinner there because we got the SIPs discount. The bread came with a sundried tomato dipping sauce that seemed promising, but was bland and oily. I got the half-portion of the bucatini with mushrooms because bucatini is one of my favorite pastas. The mushroom sauce was really tasty, but unfortunately, the pasta was underdone. My boyfriend got the gnocchi with truffle cream sauce which was flavorful and light. I was expecting more of an alfredo sauce, but we were both pleasantly surprised that the gnocchi were pillowy and the sauce just rich enough. And the picture of the gnocchi dish on this site looks a lot heavier than it actually is, so don't think you'll be rolling out of the place if you order it.

The server was friendly, and the atmosphere is more comfortable and private than at La Viola (read: more space between the tables). I also like how they offer a lot of their pastas in half portions.

This sandwich place is a triumph of what I can only assume are some very interesting zoning laws in New Orleans, as it is on a residential side street across from a cemetery with no other businesses in sight. But it has a nice atmosphere, and an eclectic menu with some enticing vegetable options. It is a breakfast and lunch place (no dinner), and I stopped in for lunch.

The source of my dissatisfaction was that it took them some 25 minutes and change to produce a sandwich (one of the things about Yelp checkins is you can check how long ago they were), during which time it went from clear outside to heavy rain, while the time I had to actually eat lunch evaporated. They acknowledged and apologized for the wait, but I do think it's fair to expect faster service from this sort of place, and the food was certainly not as good as it could have been if I'd been able to eat it fresh.

That being said, the food was tasty enough that I will most likely give them a chance to do better on service: an intriguing toasted sandwich with a variety of vegetables, rosemary potato chips on the side, and some fried bell pepper rings. Why haven't I tried this before? Is it healthy if you fry a green vegetable? Why don't more places offer fried peppers? These are the kind of questions I want to be asking if I spend good money to eat out for lunch. I won't come in a hurry again, but I will come back for what they call an "oreo beignet".

This is the most decent place and peaceful place with a beautiful view of the bay. The price is reasonable compared to the prices that surrounds this restaurant $$. If you want something decent and old fashioned cooking , come by may not seem much compared to the surrounding restaurants but I guarantee you it will put a smile  on your face. P.S.Great Hostess!

Such terrible, horrible customer service. The sign in the front of the building read "happy hour" when we arrived and the bottom of the sign was torn off. We assumed it was happy hour.  We ordered off the "happy hour" menu.  After our orders were placed, I overheard the next table ask our same waitress to place their orders once happy hour started. She NEVER told us that it was not happy hour. When I asked if we could wait for our orders to be placed, she said that it was already in. She sent the owner who was the on-duty manager over to the table who informed us that nothing could be done since happy hour was still 30 minutes away.  Just 30 minutes away!  We were charged full price for all of our food and drinks.  We're classy so we still left a tip. I won't be back. A simple reminder that happy hour was 30 minutes away would have been nice. The sign outside shouldn't have been turned to happy hour if it hadn't started yet.

Went there Wednesday night - in a word, Excellent!  My friend and I shared the smoked beets salad, the
Cauliflower small plate - both very unique flavor combinations. Beets with ricotta purée and pickled onions, roasted cauliflower on curried cauliflower purée with pickled white raisins and a crunchy topping that I can't spell.  Then we shared the ratatouille pasta. Also very good.  (No meat for me). After I saw the smoked fish salad I will try that next time!
My friend had a gin and tonic and apparently they make their own tonic water, interesting. (Gin is not
My gig so I did not try) 
Definitely do again.  Dishes are good and clearly labor intensive therefore a little pricey but worth it.  We had an early reservation 5:45 and by halfway thru it was packed.

My family enjoys getting together regularly and we love to support the smaller, local establishments so it's not unusual for 6-12 of us to end up somewhere for dinner. I can honestly say we've never had an experience come even close to as bad as this past Saturday evening was at Kuma's and to think we changed plans at the last minute to eat here so some under 21 family could join. Our issue revolved around wanting our group of 8 to be seated on the patio so we could enjoy visiting without the loud music. There were at least 7 open tables on the patio and one group of 8 already seated there. We were initially told we couldn't sit outside because fire code didn't permit a group of our size and since there was a fire station directly across the street, they had to be extra cautious. One of our family members decided to head across the street to pay the firefighters a visit, offer condolences on the tough week for first responders in our city and ask about the fire code. Their response was to laugh and inform him if exits weren't blocked, there was no fire code violation. We then offered to split our group into 2 sets of 4 and sit at side-by-side tables outside. This was initially acceptable for about 5 mins then we were told there was a group of 6 that had been waiting longer than us.... Really? And you were going to push two 4 person tables together for a group of 6 but not a group of 8? Given the small size of the restaurant, we never saw a group of 6 waiting and interestingly, they never materialized for their patio seating. At this point we began to feel like "facts" were being fabricated to suit the staff. We ended up being seated inside while one family member spoke with the manager who obviously had no concept of a customer being right. I realize that sometimes that's not true but, again, this was a family outing that included a 13 yo gal....the purpose of our evening was to celebrate a baby announcement and an upcoming wedding of another couple in our family. The manager then proceeded to head back to the kitchen and slam something loud enough to be heard above the music in the dining room which then resulted in a visit by the "executive chef/owner" who came out ready for an argument and obviously already believing our group to be in the wrong before even hearing the full story. The owner decided to have his conversation in the middle of the restaurant and all of his patrons in spite of my brother suggesting they might want to go someplace a little more out of the way to talk. To this point our only "crime" was pushing for a table outside with a complete lack of understanding why all were so ticked.One could argue we were "loud" but we were there to visit and had to get loud to have a conversation over the music, again part of the reason we hoped to sit on the patio, but our "loud" had noting to do with anyone being drunkenly obnoxious. We'd spent quite a bit of money already and tipped well, 20%+....it was blatantly obvious they wanted us to leave but we chose to stay and finish dinner as it would not have been easy to get seated quickly at any other place by this time. All of this for a decent burger, but I've had better, and being out of 2 different beers in spite of a light crowd on a Saturday evening. (Maybe there's a reason this place wasn't packed out in popular Fountain Square on a beautiful Saturday eve?) At one point, I was brought the wrong beer because the waitress hadn't been able to hear me and was again made to feel like I was at fault for this.  After waiting approx. 10 mins and asking twice about my beer, I was informed they were now out of that choice. Our group has been to places like Livery, District Tap, Red Lion Grog House and Scotty's Brewhouse just to name a few. We've always been welcomed and had a great experience.  The management staff at Kuma's was rude and hot-tempered and there were so many half truths told to us with facts that changed each time that this was one of the absolute worst dining experiences I believe I've ever had and do not plan to return.
Awesome atmosphere, great happy hour! Our server Erica is awesome, ask for her!! Cheese sticks and Tang drank are the best!

This pizza is the best pizza in Nashville, hand down.  We have tried to many other places and Castrillo's is the first place to maintain consistency.  Its always ready when they say, fresh, hot and delicious and all for a great price.

The food at this place is amazing.  The rib Mac n cheese sandwich is out of control.  So are the rosemary fries.  They also have a great selection of beer.

The reason for the three stars was the service.  Our server was very nice but seemed more into the tvs than being a bartender.  The sandwiches are enormous and we had to ask for napkins.  Pretty much had to get her attention for most of what we asked for. The chairs at the bar are also too low so you feel like you're sitting at "the little kids' table".

I'll def be back cause the food is so good, and maybe during a busier time, the service will be more up to par.
Vanilla cinnamon French toast is bomb. Great service. Too pricy for breakfast for families.

Nice atmosphere. Overly nice and excited staff: everyone was happy and attentive! And get the plantains- those were yummy!

I must say, though, the food was fair. It tasted good but nothing excited. And the tacos were small. 
If you get their salad make sure to choose a different dressing because it taste like they just squirt limes on there as the dressing, which wasn't my thing.

Also it was pretty pricey for the drinks. The food prices were also a little high for my small taco.

And can someone ask what's with the chopsticks at the table? I thought it was Mexican?

Arario could become a new go to for me in Reno.  The Korean dishes were excellent, and - actually Korean!! We had the tartare and the short ribs, and the flavor and textures were right on. Our server pointed us to her favorites (always my plan in a new spot) and did a great job.  We also tried the special Arario bowl, which was bimimbap-like but with a fusion twist.  It was hands down my friend's favorite. The kimchi side could have been spicier, but still, this is Reno, and the other small bowls of tasty things that should always accompany korean food were varied and flavorful.
CoVID: the outside deck appeared closed, which was too bad. A couple heaters on a cold night and it would still be very doable, and more covid (un)friendly than inside. We sat at the bar, well spaced from other customers but not the best ventilated space I've been in. Staff wore masks, and provided great service. 
Overall our tab with soju, beer, appetizer and two main dishes was under $100 - good value for fresh, well prepared and welll served meal. You can get by for a lot less.

Our family has been going here since they opened. ALWAYS SATISFIED, til tonight... we placed our order for pick-up. It was awful! We ordered 3 pizzas and a calzone. Well, the calzone was missing and 2 out of the 3 pizzas were totally wrong. We specifically told the girl on the phone, NO onions (due to an allergy). And guess what, the pizza had onions. And extra too!  
I think we're gonna take a break from LaScala and go elsewhere.

Food was amazing! My husband and I ordered the chicken cooked two ways (fried and roasted), skillet green and caramelized sweet potatoes. All were cooked to perfection. The service was impeccable!  I didn't have to ask for a refill on any drink, This place is a must if you are in New Orleans.

Bbq shrimp ribeye awesome- came as ordered at med-well, sauce gave it nice pop of flavor, shrimp were plump n fresh. Bf's strip steak was juicy with a nice char outside. Service was pleasant. Prices werent even crazy. Appreciated this experience at a landmark spot.

The drink was meh but the food was good. I definitely want to come back and try other things on the menu. The menu is pretty small; great for indecisive people who get overwhelmed with having too many choices.

Drinks//
I got the boba green milk tea. The drink came in a pretty big cup, taller than the length of my wallet (see picture). The flavor was okay; it tasted pretty much like milk/cream with no actual tea flavor at all. The tapioca wasn't bad; it could have been less mushy but I guess I've had worse.

Food//
I got the Super Spicy Wonton Noodles and I found it really to be 'super spicy'. For me, it was right before the point where I couldn't eat it. However, I'm not on the extreme end of the spicy-eating spectrum. The wontons were good and the noodles were cooked to the right done-ness level.

Entrées come with soup unless it already has or is a soup. I think it's supposed to be an egg drop type soup but seems like they just threw a bunch of ingredients together. The taste was decent.

Service//
Service wasn't bad. There is one lady who speaks Mandarin, so if you want to order in Mandarin, you'll have to talk to her. Really nothing else to comment about.

Ordered delivery from GrubHub. Super disappointed. Everything was bland.

Ramen Noodle Soup: Noodles tasted like the kind you get wrapped in plastic from the super market. Broth was completely flavorless, I had to add soy sauce to make it taste like anything.

Shrimp Shumai: Rubbery, also flavorless, came with a side of plain soy sauce instead of the typical soy-ginger-sesame. 

Green Salad: A handful of iceberg lettuce with 2 slices of cucumber, a piece of broccoli, and watery "ginger" dressing. 

Spring Rolls: Decent. Crispy, good sauce.

The only positive I would give about this restaurant are the large portion sizes, which is unfortunate because I didn't even want to eat any of it. The delivery was quick, but I also live only a few blocks away. Would rather make $0.50 microwave ramen than order from here again.

I come here about once a year not for great or even good service because that never happens. I really really come here because the food is good and  it's close to my gym.  Because the food  was good I never wrote up a review for I would've had to be honest about the service.  Service stinks here. Even when I had service that didn't  stink that much, it's come with an attitude.

No sign for wait to be seated so I seated myself. I was Seated 10 mins  and no one came by. This is a small  place where you can see the entire restaurant from the grill and the cash register. 2 or 3  people were rung out while I was waiting and  could see the head of the person grilling so I wonder why no one was aware I was there?

I saw 2 people  seated with their menus propped up so I asked one of them if I may have one of their menus. I decided on what I wanted to order within a minute so I pushed the menu to the end of the table in the hopes of someone would see that I was ready to order. When that didn't work I pushed it nearly off the table, just hanging on the edgeand still no one came by. See my pic !
10 minutes and no acknowledgement. I'm off to find another place to eat that wants my business.

We've been coming here for years. Not necessarily this location but within the indianapolis area. We love it!! Most recently had the turkey burger and won't be going back to anything else. To be honest, two cosmos have me feeling fine and you can't even taste the alcohol. During COVID they have been able to keep the patio open and provide to go drinks to enjoy while sitting street side waiting for a table. Only complaint was the extended wait time and the wobbly tables, but I say go go GO!!! Also, take a sample of the peach dessert. TO DIE FOR!!

Authentic tacos!  No frills but the food and service were excellent.  The salsa bar had so many choices from pico de gallo to extremely hot habernero salsa.  Fresh cilantro is always a plus.  I like how you can make it the way you like it!  Absolutely worth the trip!
Somehow this place manages to get worse year after year. Even if you're the only customer, they still get your order wrong.

Went here with my friends for lunch and "mid-day margaritas". It wasn't that busy so we were able to get a table pretty quickly. Didn't care much for the decor...it just seemed like a typical Mexican restaurant. 

I ordered a chicken quesadilla, an order of cheese dip for the chips, and a small watermelon margarita. The food was good, but nothing special. The margarita was pretty strong for a small amount...I had to keep sipping my water to get the strong taste out of my mouth.

I'll probably come back mainly just because my husband wants to try the food here.

Why 5 stars?  Because I friggin' love it!

   ---   ---   ---

Sunday's...why did it take me so long??  I used to work in Ybor and before that, I lived there on two different occasions for a year and a half.  I never once stumbled into Sunday's.  For shame.

When I worked in Ybor, my office was very close to Sunday's, and anytime we walked down 7th Ave to lunch - we would just skip right on past it.  I'm really not sure why this happened, I guess I just got an unappealing vibe from my view across the street.  For some reason I got the impression that it was catered to older people and was a place that was not going to last in an area that is already pretty crowded with restaurants.

When I actually got the nerve up to hit this place up...my eyes were opened!  As I walked in, I quickly learned that my impression that this place was for blue-hairs, was overwhelmingly false!  The interior and decor are as cool and hip as they come!  

I went with the Knuckle Sandwich and was very pleased!  The crisps that come with it are an excellent side.  This experience was probably 4-stars for me, because it was very good.

I returned a few days later for breakfast...and this is where my rating was bumped up to 5-stars.  I went with the Eggs Benedict and she had the French Toast.  You can call these two pairings Simon & Garfunkel, Michael & Scottie, Tom & Jerry, Sonny & Cher...whatever successful duo-pun that fits your demographic is an accurate one.

Overall, I have thoroughly enjoyed Sunday's and I hope you do as well!

There is always a wait to get in to Safari's. We went on a 5/5 when everyone else in town was having Mexican and got right in without a wait. Service was amazing. Very tentative to our needs. Food was delicious. My wife raved over the chicken Alfredo pasta. The pasta sauce was very fresh tasting. I ordered chicken fajita. The chicken had a pineapple glaze that added an interesting twist to this dish. Overall, I was pleased and will return. This was a great place for a family of four with small children.

Delicious food!! Accommodated dietary challenges with ease. Triple tacos with carne asada, pork & chorizo-- so tasty. The beans were cooked perfectly and I dipped my tacos in them. Yes, totally dipped. Hubby had fajitas, a huge portion, with fresh sides. Lots of great salsas to select, ask for the arbol sauce, it compliments the already super flavorful meat and beans. Service was excellent, clean restaurant... Pinellas county needs good authentic Mexican places and this place meets that need and then some. I'll probably never be able to come to natures food patch again without coming to this restaurant! Yummy!

Nice thin crust crunchy pizza.  Walking the French Quarter needing something to eat and drink and stumbled upon Louisiana Kitchen which was away from the hustle and bustle of the quarter.  We had an Abita amber and IPA  along with a cheese pizza.  The service was prompt and professional from a very friendly server.  The pizza was made in a wood burning oven and arrived quickly, hot and crispy.  After a nice relaxing break we left with our batteries recharged and ready to head back to hustle and bustle.

Love this place!  Located in the Siena Hotel in down town Reno, it's a great secret.  They offer an "all-you-can-eat" lunch & dinner menu, along with other choices.  One of the best things is that, IF you're with a group and someone is dead set against sushi, no big deal.  You can order off one of the other restaurant's menus and still dine in Sushi Saga.  Great option to have.  The chefs were helpful, and gave assistance when asked for.  Also, you could understand them, because they spoke English.  Sorry, if that offends some, but we are in the USA and when I go out, I should be able to understand whom ever is assisting me.

The Rolls - the rolls are large, full of flavor, and delicious!  The Priscilla is the BEST ROLL I'VE EVER HAD!  In a 10 hr. period of time, my hubby and I dined here twice!

The only down fall....again, as w/ my previous review...This place does not stay open long enough.  We were told that we were dining on the first night they stayed open until 9pm....9PM??!!!  People, when gambling, will eat!  you need, on the weekends, to stay open until 10 or 11 (I'm thinking 11) and although the place was completely empty the entire time we were there (both times) by 9:08pm, even though we were still eating ours, they had turned away 2 couples.  Kinda of wrong, in my opinion, because the entire place - hotel included  - is struggling....and I have no idea why.

My last three or four times here were very pleasant experiences ( personnel wise ). 
The products are excellent. Let's see if the attitudes remain so.

Wow, this place was fantastic when I was in college and beyond inhorrible. My friend went there a few weeks ago and raved how horrible it is now and I didn't believe him because its always been awesome. Went there today and it was TERRIBLE. We had the Generals Chicken and the mandarin chicken. Worst Generals I've ever had....and it used to be fantastic. Mandarin was better than the Generals but it still wasn't very good.  Both were so bad we each ate half and left it for them to throw away.  Hot and sour soup was not very good either. Wife said the egg drop was decent.. Rice was bad too. Eggrolls were not good either. Kid had lo mein and thought it was ok. He brought his home. Damn shame. An uptown legacy is now horrible.

Ambiance- 4 stars
Wait staff personality- 1 star
Food - 3 stars
Tap beer selection- 0 stars

Sorry to be so rude but did not feel welcome here.

Excellent service. Friendly staff. Warm feel. The menu may seem limited but every choice is a great one. The cannoli cream is homemade and is one of the best I've had, and I've had plenty. You should go here. AND it's byo

The general consensus about this specific location is the portion sizing as well as staff attitudes and it couldn't be more accurate. I have been to countless Chipotle locations throughout the United States and THIS location is the worst I have ever experienced.

Why so surly?  I really don't know why, but no matter what I order here, whoever's at the bar seems unhappy about it.  This location is open late and has a big lovely window, so despite the mediocre drinks and whiff of pretension, I wanted to like it.  But I just don't enjoy being here.  There are nicer, warmer options all over the neighborhood and even right down the street.

I went to the Cup thinking the main draw was the fact that this building is where Dillinger was caught. And I was not disappointed by the classic architecture and articles lining the wall. But actually I think the food might be the reason to keep coming back here.

They had a wide range of eclectic sandwiches. I stayed basic by going with a club and was very happy with it (definitely a large serving). My girlfriend had the meatloaf sandwich, and that was tasty too. I hope to get back here and work through the rest of the menu.
Fun place for the college kids, but my spouse and I sit out of the way and people watch.

First of all, the coffee is good. Now that that's out of the way; the place is nice, if not plain, which is perfectly fine. I asked about sizes of drinks, and ordered a latte and a mocha. I was not notified that there were to be any size differences between my drinks - having just ordered a specific size, etc. So, even though I requested one thing, I got another. Which in itself is fine, but that would have helped in my ordering had I known beforehand.

How did I not write a review? My booze-soaked brain told me I already had...

You've had your fair share of (insert brand or flavor here) martinis, downed enough pomegranate Manhattans to fuel Oppenheimer's project and slugged down the requisite number of Mojitos needed to buy into a sugar cane farm. 

Enter the cobbler and shrub. Google them because I can't spoon feed you everything.

This spartan yet inviting den of craft and culture fills a void - enjoying a great drink in Lee Circle. You can watch any parade from the windows in climate-controlled comfort. Listen to live piano music. Watch and chat up the boys behind the bar and learn about the delicious drinks you're ordering.

Go before every other SOB swarms the place.

The crab legs were buy a pound get a 1/2 pound free on Mondays!  And my oh my were they delicious!  Their sweet and spicy sauce in addition was phenomenal! I will go back and I can't wait to have crab legs again and try other items on the menu!

While visiting St. Louis we made a special trip to this restaurant because we read rave reviews about their BBQ. As anticipated the place was packed. We waited over an hour for a table. While the food was good I didn't think it was the best BBQ we had during our trip. In addition the other restaurant was better at getting people seated, hence the four star rating for Salt and Smoke.

Nice little place to grab lunch after a pedi nearby. The lunch menu is tasty and depends on the day for service. It a bit dark inside so for lunch our group usually asks to sit on the patio. Bonus is the little beer selection/store connected.

I wanted to love this place, I really did...Valentines Day lunch, I ordered Mac and Cheese burger medium rare.  Looking around I see maybe 8 other diners.  Hubby orders Blue Baller , medium and side order of onion rings.  My burger was first to be shared.  Mac and cheese was barely heated through before being placed on my well done burger.  Blek. Cheese was also grainy and no flavor.  Onion rings were from frozen but tasty.  Hubby's Blue Baller was much better, done perfectly, great flavor, crispy bacon.  Will I come back?  Hmmmmm maybe
Amazing food and smoothies! Service was quick and efficient. Would recommend the spiritual spinach salad with grilled chicken! Definitely coming back!

I give this place 5 stars the hotdog was delicious and plentiful with the fries. I had the Chicago style hotdog and even tried the chicken tenders and those were awesome also. All smiles over here and will definitely be a repeat customer.

This is totally a sports bar. If you want to be able to watch sports on four big flat screens, this is your place. We came there for dinner. I ordered a cup of Clam Chowder and the Fried steak bites appetizer for my entree.

It was such a let down that my Clam Chowder wasn't hot in temperature. I didn't send it back because I never send food back just because I'm paranoid to what they will do to my food. The fried steak bites were pretty tasty. They were fried and it's not a kind of food that I can eat all in one seating. It's definitely not an appetizer portion.

Service was so so. I think our server didn't really want to be there that day. Overall, I will come back when I'm in Boise because my fiancee's family love this place. I will not order the soup tho.

Quoted a 20 minute wait. Then they changed the quote to 40 min. Now, were at 50 min and counting. Terrible terrible terrible service. Chelsea is running the stop watch.  The gal who quoted 20 minutes isn't standing up to correct the apparent mistake. Too bad, the food is usually not too bad.

We went for dinner on Saturday night. We wanted to sit outside so I made a reservation reservation for the patio. When we got there we were seated at a table that if you put a glass on it would've rolled off. We asked to move to a different table that was even and we're seated right away. The waiter took our drink order quickly however after 30 minutes we still didn't have our drinks. We ordered a charcuterie plate and for tapas.The patatas were very good as was the octopus. For dessert we had churros, however they were a little disappointing because they were cold. This place has the potential to be much better than it was. If you're gonna have patio seating I recommend getting rid of high top tables. The table was not comfortable and the chairs were not even.
The Food is sooo good! The staff is nice. It's also a awesome place to hang out with friends, there are table games just to use will you are there! Love it!

I love this place!  The ambiance is lovely and is a great place for dinner and a date.  I came here on a recommendation from a coworker and boy am I glad that I listened.  I had the ricotta gnocchi and it was absolutely delicious the only downside is that I wish it was a larger serving.  It's enough food if you are eating lite but if your on a carb binge like I was, it definitely left me wanting more.  This is why I also ordered a side of potatoes hehehe.  More extra yummy delicious carb loving.  I usually do not order dessert after dinner anymore but I had some room that was available in my stomach so I got the coconut cream pie.  Another hit!!! It was so fluffy and fresh.  My only regret is letting my date try it because he ate it all up.  In short I would highly recommend Noble Crust.  Whoever is in the kitchen putting together the dishes is a genius and my hat goes off to you for making this a great experience. Salud!

I've been to Lotus Inn multiple times and have had a pretty good experience every time.  I always start with the sweet potato sushi roll...since I don't eat any fish.  It's not on the menu, but they always know what I'm talking about when I ask for it. The sauce they put on top is amazing!

For entrees..I've only ever had the sesame chicken and the pad thai.  The sesame chicken is good, very standard.  The pad thai was different than other pad thais I've had...it was pretty spicy! but overall still good. 

The inside of the place is a really cool vibe, with a large bar and nice interior. Would definitely recommend for a night out.

I love the mussels.  They have a great selection of seafood.  The place is very modern and cool inside.  They have a lot of very nice fish paintings inside.  The owners own 3 other restaurants downtown.  The hanger and parkshore grill.

They have a really nice brunch they serve on Sundays.  I normally like to attend it for Mothers day its that fancy.  Its about 25 bucks but it is better than the vinoys in my opinion and they charge 60 for that.  They have a ton of beers on tap as well.  I would try this place for sure and if the weather is nice sit outside.

All of the items I have tried from here are delicious. I don't live super close to The Buttery but I appreciate that they have added in the option to order ahead online and do a pick up since Covid started. 

I have gone in since then and they have a nice set up that allows you to see the items available for the day but keeps their staff safe so they can stay open and we can get their delicious goods.

This place was packed around 7 pm on Thursday! We thought we would have to wait a long time to be seated but the wait was literally 10 minutes. I was overwhelmed by the many options they had. I opted for a frozen margarita (Mango and strawberry) which was very good! Then I chose the pick 3 and got a beef taquito, beef enchilada and a chicken quesadilla. Everything was SO delicious and the portion sizes are HUGE! You won't be disappointed at all.

I have no idea why this places ratings aren't that great... then again I've never been in the restaurant.. but I get delivery from here and it straight KILLS it. Their menu isn't huge but omg the pizza is so damn good. Can't order from anywhere else

Thanks to yelp I found a new soul food place that's near me. I had the Lulu bang wings,veggie rice and yams. The sauce on the wings is really good. A little sweet,a little spicy. The rice had a really nice flavor and was full of veggies. The yams were sweet and flavor filled and the addition of the pineapple chunks was a plus. I can't wait to try some other menu items.

Husband picked me up some food, shrimp egg foo young to be exact. I order from this place quite frequently and never had a problem. The only reason I am writing this is because of the most rude and nastiest treatment I received from them today. When I took the food out of the bag it had a weird color to the gravy and before even opening it there was an off smell. I just figured it was a different gravy or it cooked down and would still be ok, because again, I've never had an issue with their food. So I put the rice in my bowl and proceeded to scoop out a patty of shrimp too young and gravy and still the smell was off putting to me. I go to eat it and immediately the taste does not taste right, I sniff the food and something smelled spoiled or sour. I let my son smell it and he said the same thing, it almost smelled like a curry seasoning or something that isn't usually in it was cooked in it. So I call to let them know I could not eat it, I apologized and asked nicely if I can get something else. The girl that answered the phone was speaking to someone in the background who was yelling and she finally told me to bring it back and they would fulfill my order. I get to the store and immediately the man in blue sweater aggressively starts telling me "put in trash!!, put in trash! I can't take that back!" "So I said did you want to see it or smell it?" He starts yelling at me saying next time you make sure what you want to order, this is a waste of food! I'm loosing money. So I told him no I was sure of what I wanted, it just didn't taste right do you want to see what I'm talking about. This entire time he is yelling and his arms are flailing all over and I asked him why he was yelling at me? He continued! Then proceeded yo tell me he cooks everyday and nothing was wrong with the food and showed me another order and said people order it all day long. So at this point I want nothing but my money back! I'm not eating anything from someone who is angry with me! NOPE! So a woman starts yelling at me and throwing stuff around and I at this point start yelling back! I want my money, give me my money and I will leave! She started taking her neck scarf off as if she was coming around the window to fight me. The man is yelling at me to shut up and all kinds of stuff. This is by far the craziest thing ever. I was ready to just call the cops. They are insane to eve treat a customer this way, especially not knowing exactly who they are dealing with. God bless them!  And after this experience I wish I didn't have to give them the one star. Not sorry!

If you want an artery to explode full of fatty meals go here! 
The owner doesn't even greet his clients.

So I am here right now with a couple of friends and we haven't gotten our food yet. But as we wait here and chat we can't help but think about the wait on our food. We have been sitting here for 45 minutes and still haven't gotten our food. And to top it all off, they don't even have guac!!! Like wtf what Mexican resultant runs out of guacamole..... please explain.

I like the food here. We got there around 12 pm (noon) on Tuesday and there are a line outside but the wait was not bad (30 minutes) 
It is very cool inside so prepare a light jacket for inside. Super hot outside 
There is a construction outside of restaurant so the walk way was tiny....

Somehow this location just can't seem to get its act together service wise, hence the 3 stars. Beer selection and food quality are fine if not mildly forgettable. Not a bad place to meet up for a beer or two with a friend but service is just consistently slow and forgetful, in my experience.

Was here for the long weekend, and was really pleased with this place! Although it was a holiday Sunday (valentine's day), and we were told a table would be 20-25 minutes, we were seated within 10 minutes. Ordered the cioppino which was delicious and tomato-y. Super fresh. The sea bass was soft, flaky, fresh, and flavorful. Strawberry salad also light. Good portions, reasonable prices.

Farm to table is our preference in food. Urban cookhouse did not disappoint . We had the lime rice and marinated steak with a salad and the turkey crunch sandwich with broccoli salad.  The seasoning was excellent.  Not a single crumb left on our plate.  Love the casual atmosphere.  Great lunch!

Lobster Omelet is delicious, with lots of lobster bits!Biscuits & gravy with over-medium eggs were delicious as well. The biscuits were a bit hard but flavors were good. Will definitely come back to try other items on menu next time we're in town
I do not do this review stuff but this place is fantastic.. fantastic fried chicken and great new concept.. i will be a regular

Always get great service.  Menu changes up-adds nice variety. CRG does a good job providing a pleasant, quality dining experience.  Check special occasion menus (Mother's Day, Easter, etc) for wonderful carry-out catering-style options. Great deals and superb food.

Many pizza joints in Jersey call themselves a "Pizzeria & Grille," but Forno's is the first one I've seen to actually pull it off. Instead of focusing just on pizza, they have a great deal of italian entrees.

Upon entering the restaurant  to pick up my order, I was greeted by some of the friendliest staff around. Not only were they happy to explain the menu and passionately give recommendations, but they offered a number of samples of their appetizers.

Unfortunately, I was less impressed with the pizza. While far better than Dominos, Pizza Hut, etc.; I have definitely had better in the area. If you live in the area, it's worth giving Forno's a try - it might be just what you are looking for.

If I could give zero stars I would!! What the heck is happening to this place??!! The service here is disgusting! The waitress took my order, standing over me with a mean mug and her arms folded Before taking my order- she rolled her eyes. Yes! Rolled her eyes! I didn't take it personal. Figured she was just having a bad day. I quickly ordered my food to dine in (media noche, devil crab and croquettes) and an order of picadillo to-go. My devil crab and croquettes was delivered to me on wet plates. I didn't say anything to my skank faced waitress. Obviously, she delivered the food and didn't care so there was no point for me to say anything. I wipe offed the water and proceeded to eat. The croquettes were flavorless and my deviled crab was completely iced cold in the center. So gross... At this time, I was so disgusted with everything I didn't even bother eating my sandwich. When the to-go arrived, I opened it to check and again COLD ASS food. Never again!! I rather get punched in the throat then eat here again. Also, I smelled like dirty oil all day. You can attribute this to a dirty restaurant and a unkept hood system.

Spinnaker's is a good choice for a casual night out with decent food, nice view, and reasonable prices. 

A few different places have tried to make a go of this prime location in Gulfport over the last few years, but none have hit their stride. The Mrs and I decided to give the new iteration a try on a recent lazy Weds evening,  and are glad we did.

Spinnaker's has a very nice open-air upstairs patio with several tables and large bar which offers a great view of Boca Ciega Bay and Gulfport. It's almost one of those idyllic Florida dining views complete with sailboats and sunsets that you might post on Facebook if you are trying to make your Northern friends a little jealous. 

We were pleasantly surprised by the service. The server was quick and efficient, and throughout our meal we didn't wait long for anything we asked for. Timing was good, and we weren't rushed at all. Good service certainly adds to the experience, and this was just right.

We lucked out and happened to arrive on half-priced wine night. We ordered a bottle and the classed it up with a basket of pickle chips. They were ok, but one minor complaint is that fish and non fish items should be fried in different oil... The pickles definitely had a bit of a fishy undertone. 

The rest of our food was passably good and nicely presented. I got the fish and chips while the Mrs went with the grilled Mahi. Neither was to die for, but the food was hot and tasty, and really as good as you can expect for entrees in the 12 to 15 dollar range. 

Because of the wine deal, our total bill for an app, bottle of wine, and two entrees was only in the $50 range, very fair considering the atmosphere and reasonable quality of food. This isn't fine dining, but it is a good mid-level experience with a lovely outdoor environment, good service, and decent food. I'd definitely recommend it for a casual Florida beachside experience.

We had a great late lunch here.  My sons still rave about the chimichangas, and I had terrific tacos al pastor.  Very nice small place, extremely reasonable prices, and an extensive menu. I had a mango licuado and my sons had Jarritos sodas, but they also have Aguas frescas and horchata.  Definitely have to come back and try other items.  They serve authentic Mexican breakfast items, like chilaquiles.

Went here for lunch.  Lots of people in the restaurant. I ordered an iced tea and salad and chili.  Iced tea was ok, salad was absolutely a mess. The lettuce was so heavy with water that the whole salad was drowning. I had the dressing on side but due to the amount of saturation on the lettuce, you couldn't taste it at all.  The chili was just ok. Served with no crackers or  bread. No refills on iced tea because server was also checking people in and collecting bills.  She was impossible to catch.  Dining partner said her chicken was tough. I think it needs better management and to iron out some of these things.  Invest in a salad spinner for one.  People like crackers or bread with chili.  Offer refills for iced tea. Come back to the table and check in.
Very enjoyable ! Good Food and nice staff. And I like the variety of beer. They also have dart boards. Lightning good be better. That is the only downside for me.

We ordered too much, the food was alright, but the service and drinks were good.  

Ps. 
We were here- Jan. 2012

Went here for a casual lunch with my partner. Absolutely beautiful view of the golf course and ocean. It is so lovely you'll want to stay to bask in the sunlight. 
The food is classic and fairly tasty. Nothing too special with the food. We got the Ellwood sandwich and a side salad which tasted like a classic turkey melt with leafy greens and the Tuna Wrap with mango coleslaw which was a blandish tuna wrap with pepperoncini slices and a basic coleslaw with slices of unripe mango. 

3 stars for the food. 5 for the view. 4 overall, Sandpiper. If I'm looking for a solid view, I'll come back to see you!

My husband and I love going to the Fresh Harvest,  a bit of advice come with an empty stomach.  Our server was great and the food was so fresh and delicious.  BUT the smell from the cigarettes was  so strong coming into the restaurant my eyes were watering I get it,  this is about money but I bet you since your the only casino in the area if you stop the smoking people would still come. Ps or get a better ventilation system.

My husband and I came for the 5 course tasting menu and we were completely blown away. Both of us have dietary restrictions so we were amazed that each dish given to us was innovative and totally different from the previous one. Additionally, the service is incredible and the food is amazing, fresh, and definitely in-season. Each dish was creative and delicious, and you can tell the chef takes a lot of pride in the work that he does. 

We were given 2 amuse-bouches to begin and there was an additional course of lime sorbet as a palate cleanser. Some of the things featured in our meal were carrots, cucumbers, tomatoes with an almond cremma, and crispy chanterelle mushrooms. We did not try the wine pairing as there was a Merasault I really wanted to drink, but next time we are in NOLA, I am going to leave the wine in Coquette's very capable hands.

My husband and I were visiting the city recently and made reservations to eat at GW Fins. Upon arriving the snotty hostess informed my husband that he had to wear a collared shirt and handed him a disgusting, dingy, orange polo. My husband declined and said we would sit in the bar, she gave him a nasty look and told us that we would have to just sit and wait until something became available. We said that was fine. Let me point out that little miss snotface had on a sleeveless shirt with a plunging neckline so she was able to show off her tattoos that adorned her chest area and arm. Cute. As we stood and waited some kid who looked like an absolute dirtball wearing shorts, untied boots, a t-shirt, a camo coat (outdoor type of coat, not something that would be considered ok by their dress code), and a backwards ball cap came sauntering in and walked right into the dining room and was seated. We asked the hostess why that was alright when he was wearing a ratty old t-shirt and she said "I didn't see anything". The girl is an insipid little brat who works there because her daddy owns the restaurant. I would absolutely never step foot back in that place, there are so many other restaurants down there that have amazing food. Pierre Masperos being one of them.

This restaurant is beyond delicious!!! The staff was remarkable as well. They were so polite, explained every dish and always smiling! The chef is brilliant and sometimes brought food right out to us. I would definitely come back again. Bravo to the staff at Beholder!!!

China Gourmet is a perfect example of what a Chinese restaurant should be. I took my daughters here and we all loved it. This is not your typical fast food Americanized Chinese food. This is the real deal. Everything we had was delicious and plentiful. The atmosphere is what you would expect at a real Chinese restaurant. The staff is friendly and helpful if you don't understand what something is. They have an immaculate dining area with all types of live seafood tanks. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone. It is definitely worth a stop.
I love this place been going there since it's grand opening. Staff are very friendly and check up on you often. Food is great for the price and comes in big portions. I have absolutely no complaints.

My dad and his friend, who are both from Sicily, went on a short trip for desserts. Usually we go to Termini or Varallo but his friend insisted on Nonno's. My dad ended up raving about Nonno's and said "it felt like I was in Sicily at a cafe". The desserts he brought back were incredible. I've been to Sicily and have not been able to find cartocci near me. But Nonno's finally answered my sweet tooth prayers. Everything was fresh and good quality. Thank you for bringing a little bit of home here for my dad! I think we found our new favorite bakery.

What a wonderful place to have lunch. All types of assortments of chicken salad. My very favorite is Lynda's lemon basil.  The service is exceptional, and I had a healthy and exciting experience at chicken salad chicks

This place is only a few months old and we have been meaning to check it out. We ordered carry out and it was GREAT! Our dishes were well spiced and super tasty! There was only one table there and I really don't understand why. I can only guess that no one knows much about them yet. Go check them out! This place needs to survive!
Great meeting spot with a lot of outdoor seating. Sweet potato fries are really good w cinnamon cheese/butter dip. They also have a cool gaming room that includes darts. Huge draft menu.

Super long line but worth it. We shared crab cakes, Caesar salad, the Louisiana platter, and ended off the night with bourbon pecan pie with ice cream. 

Crab cakes were delicious! Smothered in a Cajun cream sauce with mushrooms crawfish. The Caesar salad was just a Caesar salad, nothing exciting. The Louisiana platter had red beans and rice, gumbo and etoufee. Red beans and rice was really good. Gumbo was good but I can confidently say, mine is better ;) etoufee was a little off in my opinion, can't put it a finger on what it was but it was meh. The pecan pie was delicious! Flaky crust, not overly sweet, just perfect! 

They were under staffed but did really well managing the crowd and expectations! Well done!

This place is so unique! I love how many Comoros you can pick from. My favorite is the classic meatball with bourbon bbq sauce, which is good. Also love the mashed potatoes. We called about 10 minutes before we got here and they set us up with a table for 10 immediately. Daevice was incredible kind. When the mashed potatoes were going to take an extra 30 minutes, they not only comped the potatoes but also brought us free dessert! Speaking of which, highly recommend the banana pudding. It was delish.

Now we're talking! This place has some really great flavor and if you like it spicy they'll make it that way for you. I was there for a pick-up order but the owner had me sample some items from the buffet. Really good stuff and a great variety. The staff is very friendly and the restaurant is clean and welcoming. 
I will most certainly be back!

I'm quite a fan of Bryn & Daynes and their healthy fast food concept. The food is clean and I know I'm eating healthy on the go for it. 

I have enjoyed their self service point of sale option to take my time in looking at the menu and not feeling rushed into a poor decision. 

I also now have a spot to go to for an alternative to ice cream (especially during whole30...) thanks to the banana whip and many more new whip options!

This location in particular is amazing to go to during spring and summer. The open air window treatments, plants galore making you feel as if your are in a greenhouse and with little to no noise thanks to it's location within a small development right outside the plymouth meeting mall makes it an ideal spot to meet up with friends and relax before a busy Sunday morning grocery shopping!

Silo was a last minute decision for my partner and I, and it did not disappoint.
