As far as food, it went as well as it could have I feel like. We ordered the deviled eggs, which were fun and yummy, but we also got the ricotta-- Whoa. That's all I can say really, other than it was delicious.

I ordered the NY strip, medium rare. Meat was well seasoned and was complimented greatly with the green beans, tomatoes & the sauce.

My girlfriend ordered the pork chop. I don't even know what was on it, but she shared a bite and it was amazing. Also even the shallots on her dish tasted great, wtf. 

We decided to stay for dessert, got the Pot De Creme, I was a little hesitant because I thought it was going to be overbearingly sweet, especially with caramel, but it was perfectly balanced.

All in all, the food was great.

Atmosphere: Cute, small & intimate, good for a date night, but also the bar area and outside patio is good for a casual meal. It can be loud due to that, but it just depends on the day. ( we had a bachelorette party pull in, but it was a lot quieter when they left haha. )

Service : everyone was super nice, our waiter was a little forgetful but I don't even care. He was super attentive and took great care of us. 

thx Silo. lol.

All I can say is the food was nothing short of amazing!!! The staff was very attentive and made sure our drinks were constantly refilled. Just my fiance and I, we had 2 dinners, 2 drinks and 3 sushi rolls all for $45!! This is my new favorite place in Tampa!

I thought the exotic food was a nice change of pace, but I definitely would not eat here again, but not because of the food.  Our waiter had insufficient knowledge of the menu items, I had asked him what the difference between boneless short ribs and LA style short ribs, he replied "one has bones the other doesn't". I ordered the boneless ribs and my wife ordered marinaded pork belly. At least he got mine correct, he gave my wife "LA style ribs." (Which I swear looked and tasted like pork) (and was over a $10 difference) Our waiter was not terribly busy but acted like he was running a marathon the way he was sweating over the grill. He was also extremely awkward and handled conversing with us a very hard and awkward experience. Upon conversing with us he discovered my occupation, which I am a butcher. He then came up behind me and complained to me about an American couple not understanding how the restaurant worked. I told him that this was my first time here as well, being American, but he just further complained about his own customers!! He was American himself! (Btw there was a majority American people running a Korean restaurant, odd huh?)  he told me that at least when he talks to me that he doesn't have to explain what flap meat was, not hearing the term before I made a guess that it was the lifter meat above the ribeye? And he whole heartedly agreed with me that I was correct.  A quick google search shows I was wrong, it is meat off the BOTTOM SIRLOIN.  This waiter was incompetent. He hardly checked our drinks and seemed focused on making himself look busy. After inquiring on the incorrect entree items we went through the "manager" or more like the head waitress. And after a slightly short exchange of them acknowledging a miscommunication on our order they took $15 off our bill. My wife ordered pork belly and that's what we got, (the meat was white, not red, I even tasted it it was pork fat on the bones) but they were positive they had given us short ribs when it was clearly not. They tried to scam the wrong person, I sir, am a butcher of 10 years.  Try it on someone else. When our waiter came back out with a revised bill he made a snide remark "at least you saved some money at the end of this!"  Wow. Rude and incompetent. Enough said.

This was the best Mexican food I've had outside of being in Mexico.  Great friendly staff greeted us and explained the menu. There was a little mix up with our order and it took longer than expected,  however the staff went above and beyond to make it right. I wouldn't mind waiting for this amazing meal! Everything from the fried grouper taco, to the chicken taquitos and I can't forget the guacamole, queso and home made chips!!! Definitely will be back!!!
The best seafood spot in New Orleans next to Deanie's. Shrimp and catfish are on point and it's great for parties or big groups. The wine selection is a very nice touch after or before your meal.

This place makes my soul glad and my stomach sing! First of all, the staff is so kind. The man that greeted us and took our order has the love of Jesus deep within his heart, and it shows by the way he greets people. The food is AMAZING! I got the curry fried rice with salmon, and my husband got teriyaki shrimp. Both were amazing. Their homemade sauces were amazing. And, as icing on the cake, there's a section with FREE BOOKS! We'll definitely be back--It was worth driving over 20 miles to get there!!!!!!

It was very busy so after waiting and watching everyone around us get their orders we asked and were told our ticket was lost but ours would be next.  Ten more orders walked through the door still not ours. The guy behind the register told someone three times to get our order still nothing. Just as we were about to just ask for our money back we get handed a bag ..... if we had not had beignets before we might have thought these were good.  They were awful!!!!!! We should have just gone to Cafe du Monde and waited there at least after the wait it's worth it!

Good Food! Have been here twice and was seated very quickly even though there were people waiting inside.  We had a party of 3 first time & Party of 2 on second visit.   Second visit went here with a date and we opted to sit at the bar which was a great choice.  Bartender was very personable and attentive.   Both times really impressed with how low the bill was even with drinks.

On our honeymoon!!

The good: Historic hotel with nice restaurant/buffet, friendly staff, convenient to bourbon street (about 15 min walk) and nice views of downtown (particularly the super dome).

The bad: was cold the first 2 nights. I tried to turn on the heater but noticed freezing cold air kept coming out. Called the front desk and they sent maintenance up who said they are doing some construction, so the entire building has no heat... SWEEEEET. No vending machines that I could see or complimentary items (toothpaste, etc). Older hotel, which can be a plus or minus depending on your preference. Was promised complimentary champagne (for our honeymoon) and that never came.

Had a good price and location but the "I'll give you a few extra blankets so you won't freeze" deal (among other smaller ones) didn't exactly win my love.
Best pizza place in philly! My family and iO have been coming for years. We love the calamari frita also and all of their appetizers and pizzas are yummy!

What a gem in Santa Barbara. Each dish was a mixture of wonderful, fresh flavors. Our server did an amazing job with recommendations. The Crispy Brussels were amazing and set a high standard for the rest of the meal. Our other two courses did NOT disappoint. We also asked for a mocktail since we don't drink alcohol. It was delightful!

After reading reviews and hearing many recommendations from friends, I finally decided to try Sputino in d-town yesterday on my way home from work.  I was not disappointed whatsoever.  I reiterate my previous statement about not over-utilizing the 5-star review, but this place definitely deserves each and every one of those 5 stars.  I do wish I'd waited until after I showed up in-person to order, as the special pizza of the day sounded absolutely amazing, but alas, I'd already ordered on the phone after checking out the website.  I got two pies - the Formaggio (I love cheese) and the Capricciossa.  I do understand what some of the other folks are talking about with the occasional soggy crust toward the center, but this was due to a TON of delicious toppings - a small price to pay.  Quite frankly, had I eaten the pie there right out of the oven, I'm betting this wouldn't even be the case.  Nevertheless, a truly amazing pizza at a reasonable price with obviously fresh toppings and a true sense of pride and care in the product they produce.  The staff was overwhelmingly friendly and courteous, so I REALLY don't understand the reviews to the contrary.   I mean, these guys addressed me by name, and were so happy I was there.  I'll be back to this little gem again and again.  Thanks to Sputino Wood Fired of Doylestown and its amazing staff!!
A sweet throwback gem to old nola. Simple old school diner - not an imitation - complete with waiters in white with black bow ties. Delicious diner food but check out the milkshakes.

Hostess was nice. Gentleman behind the bar shucking oysters was nice. The place itself looks nice. The woman behind the bar is a total disaster. Very vague in her "welcome" - acted like she was doing us a favor by our patronizing the place. Glared at us like we were just some unwelcome folk from the North. When we got up to leave, her response: "ok good". There's no excuse to treat paying tourists that way - tourists who help you pay your bills.

Wow! I never wrote a review here? And I'm a weekly regular. Well, let's start off service. The girls at the front cashier are always nice. Food comes out fairly fast. I remember when this place first open, it took a little bit longer to get your food. This place could get a little crazy during prime lunch hours. So, I usually come at 1PM. The burgers are very consistent in taste. Just the right amount of salt, always juicy, and buns are done right. Tator tots are good, nothing special, but all of the sides are fairly cheap. Onion rings are great. Fries are good. All the burgers are tasty but I always stick with the original with an added fried egg. Service, speed, and taste; You guys get 5 stars any day from me. 

Oh! And if you bring your own gluten-free buns, they will prepare the burger for you.
Great service, great food!! Menu has lots of options, something for everyone. Salads and tater tots were fabulous. No wait for a table either!! Would come back in a heartbeat.
The place isn't bad except for the slow ass bar tenders. It's impossible to get a beer. They slowly lumber around making one drink at a time as slowly as humanly possible.
One of my favorites...everything is so delicious especially fried chili fish..very friendly atmosphere, I highly recommend...

You will love the salmon salad, just perfect every time. The old stand by combination crispy taco, amazing enchiladas, rice and beans are delicious and delightful. Amazing level of quality always here. Consistency all the way around. 

Enjoy!

My husband and I went here last night to celebrate my birthday. Both of us are vegetarian and decided to opt for one of the specials on the board, the veggie white ramen. My husband and I both agreed that it was the best bowl of ramen we'd ever had! The tofu had a delicious meaty taste and texture, the noodles were great, and the broth was creamy and had a ton of flavor. I really hope the veggie white ramen becomes a permanent addition to the menu! My husband and I will definitely be coming back for more.

I feel bad for not reviewing Martin's sooner. We lived in Nolensville before, so went to that location for quite a while. As for the Belmont location, I like it even better. The layout of the restaurant works better for me visually and since we mostly eat at the bar, it works better for us as well. The food is always on point and the servers are always very attentive and helpful. As long as things don't change, Pat's Belmont location will remain on my rotation anytime I want great barbecue!

Well after sitting for 10 and waiting for 50 mins for the food. It comes out unimpressive. I order a hickory burger that was to be seasoned with hickory seasoning I received a plain tasting burger with a 1/2 oz of hickory sauce. Burger was dry onion rings that I ordered with it(it doesn't come with a side) where dumped from a bag and the toasted ravs where pretty much the same. Guys I think it's time you revamp the menu and update.
says they due bottomless mimosas but they did not. fix your website and menu. could have gone somewhere else that offered actual bottomless

We had dinner there tonight for the first time. The inside has been remodeled with new tables, chairs, paint and decor. The tables and chairs look to have been carved and hand painted giving a feeling of being in Mexico. We did not see it before but it looks very nice and colorful. The service was fast and friendly. The menu was nice and not overwhelming with choices. The food was priced reasonably. There was four of us and all the meals were very good and looked nice enough to photograph and share. We will make this one of our regular stops for a good meal. It was hot out tonight but there was a nice seating area out front that would be good on a cooler night.
They get an extra star for being a vegetarian/vegan restaurant in meat happy Missouri. The food was good, but expensive for what you get. I'd check it out again to support vegetarianism

This review is overdue. I can't believe I haven't reviewed this place yet since my hubby and i have been coming here every time we are in Santa Barbara. We ate here again tonight and it doesn't disappoint. We had our favorite clam chowder. Tried the Santa Barbara shrimp cocktail and it was very good and fresh.  We also had the Oyster Rockefeller and it was the bomb ! 
There is usually a waiting but they have a clipboard outside for you to list your name and they will call you once your seat is ready.  Service is always on point. Will come back again and again..

I rarely write reviews but after what I have experienced in the last hour I had to.

I am visiting New Orleans for my birthday and anniversary with my girlfriend. This place happened to be a block right down from where our Airbnb was. We walked by and noticed an amazing smell.
The next day we decided to give it a try. My girlfriend got the Bearcat (standard eggs, bacon, potatoes)  The potatoes were incredible. I am a huge fan of five guys cajun fries and these were so similar. I absolutely loved them. Bacon was not too crispy but not too soft. Eggs looked like a spiral. It was all perfection. 

I ordered the Brisket Hash. This was the best breakfast I've had in a very long time. I usually am the type to just get eggs, bacon, and toast. I love smoked brisket and usually prefer it that way, but Bearcats roasted brisket was an absolute treat for my tastebuds. On top of the brisket was egg in a hole which is one of my favorite things to make at home. I don't know what kind of sauce they used with the brisket but it just worked incredibly together. 

They serve their own freshly squeezed orange juice... it was a little pricey (in my opinion) but at the same time it was worth it. 

Cortado was strong and delicious.

Mugs and plates were unique and makes Bearcat a special place. 

Atmosphere and Service was great! 

If I ever find myself in New Orleans again I will surely make my way back to Bearcat

Oh man, I am so happy they opened a location here in Reno. I've hit them up several times in Portland, and I never regret it. The biscuits are just the right texture, the gravy is delicious, the eggs are perfectly cooked, the fried chicken is juicy and crisp. 

(Why is there fried chicken on biscuits and gravy? Because shut up, it's delicious.)

The house coffee wasn't *great*, but certainly consumable in quantity. Plus they have simple syrup instead of sugar, which is the superior option but for some reason just hasn't caught on in the coffee shops 'round these parts. And they have a variety of soda options if you're not the coffee type.

Worst attitudes ever.  Hostess walked us to our table and air conditioner and fan blowing cold air right at us.  Before we sat, we asked for another table.  Her response was "It's this one or this one." The other Table was right next to that one - same issue.  There were several empty tables in the area but none of the others were even an option.  We told her and the hostess we were leaving and all we got was a shoulder shrug.  
Never again!

Your rating will largely depend on what you see. If it's a performer you like, you'll likely overlook the uncomfortable seats, but if you see a variety show that is more schmaltz than substance, you'll likely be disappointed.

I'm a big fan of free chips and dips and whatnot, however, I am not a fan of stale chips and flavorless dip and this happens to be what I got at Cactus. 

I enjoyed the decor but the food wasn't really anything special or out of the ordinary, especially with the prices they charge. They have taco Tuesdays where tacos are 2 bucks each...Let's just say I'd refer you to taco bell before telling you to come here for tacos.

In any case, also on Tuesdays, they have their "Cactus Margarita" for 5 bucks. I'm not gonna say it's a great deal because it tastes like something straight outta the mix bottle, therefore, something I could've made for myself and a bunch of friends for much less than $5 per head.

I've eaten at the Cactus twice- the first time wasn't a great time and I swung back for a 2nd round just in case I could prove myself wrong but alas, I've come to the conclusion that I won't be making a 3rd trip here.

I like the food but the price is high for Q. They have fried green tomatoes along w sweet potato fries but charging extra should be a crime. The ribs are very good as is the brisket, the chicken and pork are a little dry. Staff is very helpful and pleasant.  It is the best in Carrollwood! Enjoy the Q here monthly!

What a disaster!
My friend commented that Chef Ramsey would have a field day trying to fix this place.

We showed up on Friday at 7:15 pm.  Seated promptly.  Ordered relatively promptly- the server could not really answer our question of what meat was inside the dumplings- she said beef- they were pork.

Everyone was being served a house lemonade with alcohol gratis since they don't have a liquour license yet.   Did we get any? Nope.
I think there was a soup people were getting, but we did not get any.  I wonder if it was because we were not Korean?  I think it was just disorganization.

My main dish (the wrong one) came out before our appetizer or the side dishes.  I asked for our side dishes and if our appetizer was going to come out.  My companion's meal was no where to be seen.

The couple next to us had all their food and they had been seated well after us.

I asked the server to describe the side dishes to my friend who had never eaten Korean before.  She said she did not know what they were because they change every day.   HUH??!?!

While all this was happening, a huge queue had formed.  Tables were not being bussed- the manager was bussing the tables, but he was dealing with the disasters left and right (loud crashing noise at one point).  So, no one else could get seated.  The hostess looked frazzled and was running all over the place and not greeting at the front of house half the time.  I saw the kitchen grandma bringing out dishes- that's how short staffed it was.  Hire some bus boys!

People were queued up for the restrooms and looking desperate. 

Korean food is spicy and my friend ran out of water.  We had to grab someone so he could get a refill - took about 15 minutes.

Like the table next to us, it took forever to get our check and to get the tab closed on the credit card.

We saw a couple come in, get seated, and then leave because they got no service.

The food was okay.  GIWA is still my go-to for Korean.
Cheap- $34 for two before tip.
I always loved Pasion back in the day.  Sigh.  What a beautiful space.
My family had a wonderful brunch.  Perfect cocktails. Friendly service and fantastic food.  Can't wait to come  back.

My wife & I discovered DJs Clam Shack while vacationing in Key West.

DJ has a simple concept, take fresh fish and serve it to the public. Well the one thing DJs does very well, they make a great Conch taco. You know those big seashells they sell in tourist shops across Florida? Inside is conch.

We're driving south to St Pete beach and my wife sees the cool DJ's rat rod out front. We pull into the parking lot and are ready to tear into a Lobsta roll. 

DJs makes a great Lobster Roll (I'm typing this review and I'm headed to Boston) one of the best in business. My wife ordered her conch taco. It comes to her and she forgot to ask for no special sauce on her tacos. Me? I ordered a fat lobster tossed in warm butter and put into a toasted sandwich  roll. Heaven..

The lobster meat isn't over cooked. This is a well executed lobster roll. Even the bread has a cake like consistency, it still invades my dreams.

DJs clam shack Key West was on Diners, Drive ins and Dives. I see a sign for the Key West location yet Long Island has *two* DJ Clam Shacks? Some Long Island swag needs to be in the restaurant! 

If you're looking for a great meal and a cold beer? I highly recommend DJ's clam shack.

Not as good as the ones up around Phoenix, but at least I can still get my "fix" every once in a while.
The super nachos are awesome!

This place was a great value and the service was terrific. We descended with 7 kids and 7 adults after a long day at a robotics tournament. One mom said as we entered: "when I used to waitress, we would be the nightmare table." The waiter kept his genuine smile throughout, and kept us all satisfied. 

The food wasn't extraordinary, but we all had the $9 specials, which were very acceptable, and we got out of there for only $11 each, including 27% tip. There was a very decent selection for $9 (soup or salad, entree, and desert) plus a much bigger selection at a variey of prices.

I wasn't given enough word space on the photo I added to adequately express my feelings about this restaurant. Let me recap. This is the most turnt breakfast I've ever been to. Meatballs in the morning? You got it. Waffles with those meatballs? In a heartbeat. Mimosa with no Oj? Done. Mimosa with no champagne? *laughs**dabs* done. Come eat here. Even if there's a wait. *dabs* *comes up for air* *dabs again*

I ordered the chicharrón burrito and it was the worst burrito I ever had, the size was ridiculous, a beef and bean burrito from 7/11 taste better and it's bigger and it's only $1 at 7/11, they added too much salt on it, not to mention the grumpy cashier that couldn't smile even if her life depended on it.

I wasn't able to have much here other than coffee but it was very tasty! Lots of seating! Good for studying, they have oat milk, BLTs, coffee pretty good!! Oat milk cinnamon latte was delicious but the sizing is pretty small for the price. OAT milk +0.85 which is more than usual. $5-6 for coffee and $6-8 for food

I've only been here once. It had a pretty good vibe. I'm REALLY not a bar person so I am usually pretty uncomfortable in places like this. But I felt pretty good here. I had some good chicken wings and a couple beers. We played pool with some friends. I may not be a reliable reviewer for a bar given my inexperience with them but I enjoyed this one.

I read this in another review and it is so true. It's a great place, but your GPS will lead you astray. It thinks you are there when you are still on the highway. I got there prime Sunday brunch time (about 10am), and the seats were packed. However the bar/counter was almost empty, so I was able to sit there immediately. Others waited in line for several minutes, because they apparently don't understand the concept of eating at a counter. A mother with a couple of small kids seemed to be under the impression that it was a part of the waiting area. But that's purely a customer flaw. Prompt service despite the crowd, good food, and great prices particularly for the Carmel area.

Conveniently located near the Vinoy, the cafe is one of the few places open late night if you're craving something sweet.  They have an extensive selection of gelato flavors, but I always stick to hazelnut.  You can choose up to 3 flavors with a small, if you're undecided between flavors.

I came craving so much a good  Cubano sandwich and a cefecito( el Cafecito is the name of this place) 

They did not have pickles for the Cubano:( I they did not know what I was talking about when I asked for a cefecito :((((( the name of the place is EL CAFECITO! (Cafecito is basically an espresso with sugar made from highly roasted coffee beans) 

So, they did not have any of the things I wanted but I still wanted to give it a try. I order the Boriqua sandwich which is a Cubano sandwich minus the pickle and with the addition of lettuce. The pork was delicious, spices were well balanced except for the salt, it was a little on the salty side but still tasted very good. 

I will go again to try their famous Cubano sandwich, im sure it will be good and I will update my review.

Great service. I ordered the Waffle Benny with cheesy grits and it was delicious but it was novelty version and I prefer the traditional English muffin version. Only negative was they did not offer menus to us as we arrived, but that could be due to COVID as there is a QR code on the table so that you read online menu. My wife ordered the California omelette but she didn't like that ingredients were all mixed together like a scramble. She preferred my food (Waffle Benny) and how it was presentated, so she ate my food and I ate her scraps.

Hands down, must try!!! Great spot, very flavorful food! I tried the hand  pulled noodles and fell in love! Broth was rich and embodied every part of what I was expecting. There weren't  many people, but it was perfect vibes. I can see this spot becoming a local favorite quickly. Definitely come and try!!

I found this place to be excellent. Its is a bybo and they have a wine& sprits store accross the street . The staff was really accomodating ,friendly ,and gave great service. 

Now the food 
was seasoned to perfection I ordered a 
fettuce pasta dish in a light cream sauce with mushrooms seasoned perfect, not too much sauce , which a lot of americanized italian places do and kills the many other flavors of the dish. with grilled chicken on the side seasoned perfect as I wanted to experience the dish as the chef intended ,but needed some meat , my mouth was so happy for my choice. The chef put his heart into his food and the details where evident from the care he took in the correct balnce  .

I had a long walk at Valley Green Park , and arrived at the in between time( 2pm-5pm). This is my luck to get hungry during these times and limits where I can go. But here in this cozy little niche of germantown ave, I found this little place with a good customer base as it quickly filled up with people who had resevation as i was finishing my meal. They gave me and my companion a complentary glass of wine as it was my first time there and I didnot know it was a byob. They were so nice. 

I will update on the other dishes I had there soon.

Ciao for now!
ps . if you arent there on in between time I would make a reservation as it fills up fast in this cozy romantic spot in the eves.

I was in between the busy period for the bar Sat. night on the Hot August Nights this last weekend 8/10. Literally there were four people in the bar but the restaurant was packed.  I ordered a martini and decided to have dinner at the bar. My selection was whiskey piggy aka pork chop on mac & cheese. Looked good on arrival. I sliced into it and was shocked to see it was absolutely cold, not cold like sitting around and still warm, cold like refrigerated and warmed up on the outside.

I took another bite just to make sure and it did not get warmer! I informed the bartender and had him touch the center of the chop for confirmation and he immediately took it back.  The GM came out and apologized offered a free desert which I declined so he picked up the two martinis.  The chop was great and the mac cheese was okay, but the service and response by the bartender and the GM was great. Both checked in on me several times to see if everything was fine.  Probably a cook getting lazy but I'm sure he will hear from the management because they repeatedly said that a "review" will be done later.

What can I say that others haven't already?  We have become frequent fliers at Cleveland Heath.  I have yet to order anything here that I wouldn't gladly order again.  The Pozole is as awesome as the burger or the pulled pork or the BLT.  You get the idea.  I could go on and on.  Instead, I'll encourage you to make the trip and try it yourself.  You won't regret it.

I've debated leaving a review, but maybe I just need to come back. My food was just okay, but I think it was the time I went. Friday at lunch time gets busy, the place isn't huge, and I don't think a lot of people were working. My food wasn't bad, but it wasn't all that hot. A coworker with me made a comment that his food was kind of cold. Also, wasn't a big fan of how the food is served (cardboard box, paper forks). Maybe coming at a different time of day would be better.
Over an hour for a delivery- Alyssa the manager needs to learn people skills as she is unapologetic and borderline rude. Will consider reordering from this dominos when she is replaced.

Very fast and friendly service, with meh food that used quality ingredients.

Ordered calamari as a starter, but probably should have gotten something a little more adventurous. The sauces were great, the squid itself was tender and delicious, but the batter was pretty tasteless and bogged down with oil. Even for a fried dish, this felt really heavy after the two of us got through half the plate.

I also defied my own instincts when I ordered the Spiced Tuna with golden beets, green beans, and brie. This was NOT a harmonious dish. The spice clashed too harshly with the tuna, and the veggies were uninteresting, including some undercooked green beans. I could fit the brie easily on the tip of my pinky. The only saving grace on my plate was the balsamic sauce that was dabbed 4 small times along the periphery of my plate, which I rationed to get through the heavy spice on the tuna. While I wouldn't call the dish "disgusting", it was certainly not enjoyable, and the vegetables - as uninteresting as they were - rescued me from any particularly bad bites.

My date definitely won this round with her choice of truffled scallops. They were big, fresh, and grilled evenly to near perfection. The dish was overall a little heavy and somewhat salty (maybe some of it was the residual calamari appetizer), but delivered on Oceano's promise of fresh seafood.

Curiosity might take me back here one day to try their prawns and a more predictable main dish with obviously fantastic ingredients, but Oceano's was 2/5 in the taste department tonight.

The food is amazing. Best Indian food I've had in a long time. All homemade and very authentic. It is really, really good. Service is a bit slow because it's just the owner and her husband working, but worth the wait.
This place is great! They are incredibly attuned and adaptive to my dietary restrictions, their service is great, and it's in an awesome location!
This place is exactly what you would expect.  Is the food good? Not really...  Is there a lot of it?  Yep...

We loved lunch at etch! The server was helpful with recommendations, and we got to try a lot of things for a very reasonable price. We loved the roasted cauliflower app, and the cobia with mango salsa and donut bread was such an interesting combination, and wonderful! You have to get the chai panna cotta. It was amazing, and I don't usually like panna cotta. Can't wait to go back for dinner!!

Very nice restaurant and bar. Sat on the rooftop patio which was crowded. It offered limited views downtown Nashville. They had two individuals performing inside and the music was great. I would definitely come back.

The food was good once we got it. We checked into the hostess stand and told it would be a 30 minute wait. We sat in the waiting area about 5 minutes until we saw 2 chairs open at the bar. We went to the bar and looked at the menu and we got hungrier thinking of what great thing we were going to order. There were 4 bartenders when we sat down then 3 dissapeared. The other bar goers were all either drinking or eating. The waitress walked by us 5 or 6 times never looking at us. She went to the group next to me and visited with her fruends for several minutes. We sat unhelped for the 30 minutes. Luckily my husband didnt give up our spot. We were seated outside in the heat. After we were seated I noticed several empty tables so im not sure why the long wait. After 10 min we finally were waited on and 10 min after that got drinks. The food was good but I was starving by then. We ordered a sampler of beer and it came as we were finishing our food. I dont know if they were short staffed or what but being Memorial day they should have had more help.

Last night was our first experience at Cobalt Smoke & Sea and it will not be our last. We loved the atmosphere and vibe of the whole restaurant. We sat underneath a Ginko tree!  Our server, Lisa, was attentive and informative about the menu. We ordered the charcuterie board and truffle fries as an appetizer=delicious, do not miss out on either of these items. There were six of us and everyone enjoyed their meals. Risotto with chicken, risotto with scallops, burnt ends and salmon. Everything was hot, well prepared and tasty. A few ordered Bread pudding for dessert and enjoyed that as well. 
If you are looking for a nice night out, make sure you check out Cobalt.

Had the pleasure of being guided by Bobby Thomas.  He was very informative, witty and funny.  He warned us before entering to stay hydrated because there is on average one person everyday who faints.  Sure enough, a lady in our group fainted 1/2 way through the cemetery.  Bobby stayed professional and calmly guided her out and called an ambulance.  The history is pretty incredible.  I thoroughly enjoyed myself.

Salsa Verde has made some changes for the better I would say! We were in last night for taco Tuesday and they are now a sit down restaurant. No more ordering at the counter and having your food delivered to your table. Now when you walk in they seat you and take your order at the table. When seated we were served chips and salsa which before you had to pay for, works for me cause we always ordered it. 
It seemed like they have a larger menu now. We just ordered the $1 tacos  so I did not look at all of it. 
They have removed the salsa bar. But to me it not a big deal cause the salsa they brought to the table is the only thing I ever got off the bar. So it made room for two more tables. 
Our tacos were great like always. Keep up the good work Salsa Verde and we will see you soon!!

I visited Par Lounge late on a Friday night with a friend. We've driven by this place several times so we wanted to check it out. Par is right next to Hi-Pointe Theatre (which is awesome btw). And if you're a smoker, Par is the perfect place to go to after a movie. But only if you're a smoker....Par is a smoking bar. And even if there's no one smoking in the bar, the walls and furniture are still going to make sure you leave the bar smelling like an ash tray.

Other than the smoking aspect, Par is a pretty cool hang-out bar. The service was great. There's a long bar for you to sit and talk at. And there's several leather couches in the back that are comfortable to relax and drink on. There's also a jukebox that appeared to be pretty popular with the regulars at Par.

Another hesitation I have about Par is that there are ZERO draft beers. Everything is served in bottles. I probably won't be back to visit Par because I'm not a smoker and I really prefer draft beer.

The restaurant looks nothing like the pictures even the menu. The prices are higher in the restaurant then they are online. The food was decent but their special "butter sauce" is mainly oil, also the seasoning was a bit over bearing and messy. I got the jumbo shrimp which has shells so peeling them with the seasoning all over them was very messy. Probably wouldn't eat again but it's a good concept!

Overall this is a pretty good restaurant. Their burgers are good, and the environment is nice. Husband had the steak and said it wasn't his favorite. The toppings on the steak were good, though. The Brussels sprouts were good and their fries were alright. The fries are never crispy. They have amazing homemade ketchup though!

We tried to come to Morrow's on a Friday night. We called ahead and they couldn't give us an exact wait time. We arrive a little after 6PM and they told us the wait was three hours. We didn't have a reservation so we made one for the next day at 1PM. 

We arrived the next day at 1PM and we're seated right away. We ordered our drinks and food. Everything that came out was perfect. I had the fried chicken and it was crunch and juicy. 

The service was great and you would love the food here. I will definitely be recommending it to others.

Fine dining in a comfortable setting. Start to finish our meal was outstanding. My husband and I love trying new places so we tend to splurge when we have the chance. We started with the oysters, served raw with a delicious citrus mignonette, followed by the sea urchin which had the most amazing fresh ocean flavor. Next was my favorite course, a special that night, chicken liver on sourdough with caramelized onions.

Wow...I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised by Sterling's. I expected kind of a second-rate steakhouse but I really can't find anything to complain about.

The service was friendly, but respectful (our waiter, Lee, was great!). The food was very good: I started with bread (tasty rolls), swapped my house salad for a Cesar "with extra anchovies" (and was rewarded with a plate of the salty little buggers), a nice rib-eye cooked exactly as ordered, and enjoyed several glasses of wine.

Sterling's wasn't cheap, but I think it was priced better than many of the competitors from other cities. The place delivered everything I hoped for.

I was going to give Sterling's four stars (because I withhold 5 star ratings unless something blows me away), but I can't think of anything I'd like changed. It was a great dinner. Thanks!

Another amazing meal at Puckett's. Waited a whole year to come back again.  We have the good luck to live in NYC and eat in some of the best restaurants all over but Puckett's never disappoints. Catherine the manager was fantastic hn getting us a great table and accommodate us and the whole staff was fantastic. Did a rack and half with a friend and out 2 young sons with the baked beans. Not to be missed. Can't wait for next year

Definitely one of the best vegetarian restaurants I've ever been to.  And I love that they don't use any meat substitutes in any of their dishes!  Not that I have anything against soy or wheat meat, but the lack of tofu or seitan-based entrees just makes Blue Sage get that much more creative with their menu.  

I've eaten here I think 4 times now, and there are a few dishes that continue to floor me every time:

Green Curry BBQ Summer Rolls - holy crap, these are some delicious summer rolls. Filled with baby spinach, mango, Thai barbeque glazed veggies, smoked red onion, ginger & basil, these rolls were so flavorful they hardly even needed the dipping sauces that came with. (Those dipping sauces are phenomenal though, so I'm glad they are there).  The side salad is just meh, but who cares, the rolls are amazing.

Sliders - cute little brioche burger buns stuffed with avocado, mango, sun dried grape tomatoes, goat cheese and some kind of crazy delicious mango glaze. These little burgers are a complete taste explosion. In fact people I've dined here with have said they might just order a plate of these sliders as their entree next time, they are so good.  The pound of yucca fries that come with, however, aren't great.  So what I do is substitute the fries for the side salad/corn and bean salsa that normally comes with the Asparagus Tacos, and the kitchen has been more than happy to accommodate.  And THAT makes for the perfect appetizer.  Seriously, anywhere.

And last but not least - the Cubano Supper. Flaky plantain pastries stuffed with sunflower seed-smoked red pepper pesto, with a tower of yellow tomatoes & avocado corn salsa in the middle. Chipotle jicama slaw & mango-papaya relish surrounded the tomato mountain.  All I can say is wow.   There were so many different flavors and textures going on, each flavor complimenting the next so perfectly.  The plantain pastries (crispy on the outside, tender on the inside) were the perfect vehicles on which to pile the multiple sauces, relishes and salsas.  I wouldn't change a single thing about this dish. 

The East West Bento Box deserves an honorable mention. It includes lentil and pine nut dumplings, an avocado salad, and a cup of red curry.  It was good, but I found each component by itself was a little lacking in flavor.  But when I mixed everything together, now that was the flavor I was looking for.

Every carnivore I've brought here has left amazed.  My NYC friend even deemed Blue Sage better than most of the trendy Manhattan veggie spots, and I would agree.  Blue Sage puts the entire East Village to shame!

The crawfish poboy, shrimp poboy and seafood gumbo was delicious. We enjoyed the service and atmosphere. The fried food is spicy but don't worry, if you don't like spice you can get the yankee (mild). Nola Poboys has a variety of items on the menu so you will definitely find something that you will like.

The setting is very nice.  The decoration, lighting, music and space kind of give the restaurant a rather intimate setting.

The food is nice.  I ordered a Tom Yum soup, which has all the right flavours.  A hint of...if u ordered the soup w/ chicken, eat the chicken w/ the soup...it creates the balance and make the soup less "powering."  :)

The mango curry was very interesting.  It has the creamy curry texture and the mango balanced out the spiciness of the curry.

I recently visited with my husband for our third time. 
This time we invited friends to join us. We arrived around 12:30 to an empty restaurant. The owner - who is quite pleasant- told us that they do most business on the weekend. 
My husband and I both ordered the Jerk Chicken Scramble offered on their brunch menu. The chicken is so tender and flavorful. It's seriously like eating chicken from the islands!  The top the scrambled eggs with the same jerk sauce and it is FIRE! So good. 
Our friends shared the chicken and waffles. While the chicken was good, the waffles we believe were frozen waffles. 
Try out Da Blue Lagoon at their restaurant or follow their food truck.

I hate cold weather.. I hate it like a fat guy would hate a vegatable or a lean protein. The only good thing that comes w/ the end of summer and sub 80 degree weather is that I can shovel noodles and delious chopped up pieces of dead animal from a steaming bowl of broth. Why don't I eat pho in the summer? Why do girls wear shoes that they know are going to give them hammer toes or plantar fasciitis? Probably stupidity, the world will never truly know. But as far as pho goes, Pho 75 is tops in Filthadelphia.
     When you roll up to Pho 75 it looks like a place where my grandmother would play mahjong.. who cares. In a matter of minutes you get a big beautful bowl of bean sprouts, lemon, basil, and jalepenos  mixed w/ tendons, tripe and brisket ( my favorite combo) for under 10 bones. As I inhale the thinly cut meat with a mixture of sweat and snot running down my face, I don't even bother wiping my face because it would just slow down the consumption..disgusting yes...but tasty still. Sure I don't even know if Pho 75 serves other food besides pho, but when you do something so well this guy doesn't gives a shit if it's the only trick you know.

This is the BEST Taco Bell. Whoever started managing it after the remodel has done an awesome job! I wish I knew her name, but she is so kind and so is her staff. They are the only place on this corner open late and even with a big line it goes quick and they are seriously NEVER stressed or have a "I hate my job" attitude. Food is super great and they never forget sauce or napkins. :)

The food is amazing here  and Maz
Our server was the best! If you are looking for a good vibe and good restaurant this is the spot!! Don't go anywhere else

OWNER OF THIS BUSINESS, LISTEN UP:
You are not being represented well. Your server taking orders got several wrong in a party of four, including getting one person's order wrong twice. She was not apologetic, focused on making the customer wrong and overshadowed your delicious food. I ordered the Rose Benedict with garlic mayo on the side with alligator sausage. The order, while delicious, was lukewarm, the mayo was not on the side and there was no alligators sausage. I stood in line with my plate and ate my breakfast standing to avoid it getting any colder, waiting my turn to let your employee know about the error. By the time I got to the counter, my meal was finished. She stated I did not ask for the sausage, nor did she charge for it. Unfortunately, she did not give a receipt to anyone in our party so we don't know that to be true. She asked me if I wanted to pay for the sausage now and that it would arrive several orders down the line. 

There was no apology and nor offer to comp the sausage now that my breakfast was already completed. 

I strongly recommend some customer service training for your employee.

I got the pork tacos and the chicken tacos because i was really hungry. It was really overpriced for the portion. The pork was really dry and bland. The chicken was okay but that's the first and last time I'm going there.

Went here today after finding out about it through Yelp. We heard weekends are crazy here so we made sure to come on a weekday.

We were welcomed as soon as we were noticed and were told it'd be 10 minutes or the bar, which was available immediately...we opted for the bar, cause hunger. 

Our waitress Corinne was amazing! At some times maybe a little too talkative, but definitely better than the latter! She made our first time great by recommending some of her favorites and going over each drink and entrée. 

We went with the Reeses Hot Chocolate and the S'mores Hot Chocolate for our drinks and the Tropical Crunch Waffles and OMG French Toast. All were AMAZING! Very fresh and delicious.

I would definitely recommend stopping by!
Great food! Great price for the amount of food! Beef and Chicken hot pots are my families favorite. My families favorite and go-to restaurant. Great service! Never been disappointed.

Really really excited about the tasting menu at Double Knot. Everything we tried was delicious and the menu is so big that I would go back and try something different from each section. 
A few of my favorites: 
- cheese curds 
- duck scrapple bao bun 
- broiled seabass 
- black cod fried rice 
- beef kabob

I wanted to customize a sandwich and the lady was rude about it and grabbed the manager to help me and he wrote everything I wanted on my sandwich then as i walked to the register he said "eyebrows on fleek" and laughed rudely.
I guess this place has been open for 12+ years. I stumbled and found it on yelp. Definitely a cool place if you're into baseball and bar food. I definitely want to come back and do a few swings here.

Jane is a welcome addition to the restaurants at the Marketplace. The food is excellent and the service is attentive and outstanding. Everything is made from scratch in house, so you can't beat the freshness and the flavor. The desserts are exceptional and the coconut cake is a must-try. The atmosphere is casual-chic and relaxed. The decor is sophisticated but comfortable. There is both indoor and outdoor seating and space for large groups.

Happy hour is great here. However I am severely disappointed with the Pad Thai take out I recently got. It had absolutely zero flavor. None! Correction, it had flavor, but tasted more like Italian Spaghetti.

This is the best Mexican restaurant in Fountain Square! There is a lot of variety including more traditional and American-style Mexican food. The molcajete is pictured here -- it is big enough for 2 people to share with leftovers (ask for extra tortillas). The meat is tender and well-seasoned. There are also a lot of vegetarian options for a Mexican restaurant. And a children's menu. And water bowls for dogs! And good deals on giant margaritas.

Just stopped in here for breakfast after our flight into New Orleans while waiting for our hotel to be ready...

Very clean place, atmosphere is nice and wait staff is friendly...

We ordered the chocolate chip pancakes, and a crispy country omelette with grits and a biscuit. Overall the food was pretty tasty, grits were good but not made the way I prefer them. Omelette was good, large and very filling! And the pancakes were as well good, tasted somewhat dense/doughy but still decent...

Not a bad place to stop in and grab some traditional style breakfast!

Not what i expected based on what i was told it would be. 35 dollars for two burgers and fries was way over priced for what i felt the food quality was. Wasn't the worst experience Ive ever had but personally i will not go back

My boyfriend despises seafood but on a rainy afternoon, on the way home, he let me stop here to grab some take-out. I had the fried clam meal and an order of the smoked mahi dip appetizer. The smoked mahi appetizer was AMAZING! It came in a little dish and was served with the freshest lance crackers I've ever had. The fried clams were like none I've ever had before. You get a choice of two sides and I chose the cheese grits and cole slaw. Both were delic! The clams breading was not as heavy as I am accustomed to. It took a bit of getting used to but was thoroughly enjoyable. I live in Mira Lago so I drive by every day. They are only open Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays which breaks my heart because I crave the smoked mahi dip all week long. When they are open the place is always jumping! All seating is outside though and you sit on picnic bench type seating. Since I live so close I'd prefer to do take-out but on a nice day I could see sitting outside enjoyable.
went here based on good reviews, don't understand the hype. left a nasty taste in my mouth all day. mediocre at best. probably wouldn't go again.
WTF did I just eat? Just try basically anything here. You'll be amazed. Don't worry about the cuteness of the food, its awesome.

Decor - A little southwest with the colors and some of the wall hangings, mixed with a little contemporary with the fixtures and some of the other wall hangings. The restaurant layout is a little weird. You enter from the front side door to a nice bar area with 2-3 tables. The main dining room is down a narrow hallway.

Service - Excellent...extremely friendly, efficient, yet very relaxed and laid back.

Food - Starter - Escargot- just ok. It was cooked correctly in Burgundy and butter, but it wasn't that tasty
Main - My wife and I shared the combo plate. It allowed us to sample a little of everything. The stuffed cabbage was awesome...cooked nicely and very flavorful. The perogies were ok...nothing to write home about. The best thing on the plate was the kielbasa...smokey, nice snap from the casing and extremely tasty.

Overall - a great restaurant with good food and even better service....we will defiantly go back.

Does not have any happy hours right now.  Don't know if that is because of Covid or they got rid of it all together.  They do have a lot of tv for sports, including Dodger games. But if they don't have happy hour specials it isn't worth it. Can go to other places to watch Dodgers and get better drinks and food that cost the same expensive amount as at Sharkeez.
My fault for assuming they would still have happy hour. I would have gone somewhere else.

Went Sunday @ 11am. Great off street parking.  It was very busy however we were seated quickly.  The table was clean and no sticky silverware like last time, but our table swiveled on the base like a lazy Susan.  Service was good, the servers were very busy.  I got the Spinach & Avocado Benedict. It was okay, it seemed cold to me but I haven't had one before so nothing to compare it to.  Overall a decent place.

Perfect sports bar. The bartenders and wait staff are very attentive and respond to tv station requests.  Food is great for bar food. MUST HAVE THE GATOR BALLS!!! plenty of room and TVs, clean, friendly, good vibe. Great patio space on West side and love when the huge garage doors are open. Awesome location along Broad Ripple Ave (= great car and people-watching).

There's a healthy eating trend percolating in Philly, and these guys are on the front lines.

In a nutshell:  Quick real food, ordered via a touch screen (lots of customization), for approx 10 bucks.  Super casual.  Good choice for Gluten Free / Paleo folks or peeps looking for low carb options.  Nice.

The Food:  Two options:  Salad or Stir Fry

You order and wait for your food to be called.  Self serve, no tip, keeps it cheap. 

Salad:  I dig the cob.
Pro Tip:  You can ask for beef.  Beef is my preferred meat source, but it doesn't show up on the menu when ordering a salad.  Ask and you shall receive.  They'll probably hate me for writing this -- (assuming anyone reads it...)

Stir Fry:  I always do custom on this and just add just about every vegetable and I dig the Thai coconut milk sauce.  They couldn't close the lid on my stir fry last night and had to use two containers to make it fit.  They apologized;  I was happy.  If you are Gluten Free -- they have rice noodles.  If you are trying to lean out, get romaine lettuce instead.

Other Important Info:  I asked what kind of oil they use for frying and they told me Canola.  Could be better, but could be worse.  At least it's not soybean!  I'd love to see them have the option to fry in coconut oil.

Oh and they have complimentary water cups by the soda machine.  The soda machine also has a "soda" lever (similar to the water lever -- a couple to the left).  Chill out with some sparkling water while you wait for your food.

Love  Me Some Salem's ! Best Food In Tampa Whenever it's late night this is the spot! I don't care how long the drive thru line is I'm gonna wait and get this amazing fresh to order food they literally have almost everything so whatever you like I'm sure Salem's has it check them out !! My Usual is The 10pc Hot Boneless combo with a 10pc fried shrimp and There Gyros Are Everything!

Yuck! This location mad me wish I still had a dog. They would have appreciated it more than I could. The wings were unusually large. I am not particularly a fan of that so that was problem one. The seasoning was packed on so it turned my stomach. The fries tasted like they sat. Waste of money.

Came here after reading the biscuits were the best in town, served with homemade jams. Got the biscuit basket and I will say they were the fluffiest biscuits I've ever tried. I'd give 4 stars for the biscuits and selection of great jams. Only downside is I thought them to be a little underbaked, or maybe they are a tad doughey by nature. 

Rating 3 stars for lack of cleaniness and a 'beer bloody Mary' that I couldn't drink (not to my liking, but that might just be based on preference). The BOMB (hard cider mimosa) was tasty though and I would order again. 

Service was friendly and attentive.
Love this place as the food is phenominal and there are many gluten free options all clearly marked.  Our server even had celiac so she was great!

The sushi was just so-so and the wait for our food was soooo long. My friends and I went in like a group of 6 and not only did the food take forever, they gave away our sushi to the table next to us which was a table full of 14 year olds. The girls put their hands all over our sushi before they realized it wasnt thier order. The waiter came by and took the plate back and tried to give it to us after they had put their hands all over it. What waiter in their right mind takes food from the wrong table after he watched them touch it and trys to give it to the right table???? That's absolute garbage. If I'm paying like $10 to $15 a roll, I sure as hell am not getting already manhandled sushi. That's crap. I would never go back.

Review for casino only!

Strolled in here with two of my friends around 1:00 AM on a Saturday night (uhh..I guess that's actually Sunday morning...) and it was still pretty busy, considering. I get the feeling that someone with previous time/experience in Vegas definitely had a hand in the design and interior decorating of the place-- there is some very obvious similarity to resorts such as The Venetian and the Forum Shops at Caesar's Palace. Anyway,  we came to play blackjack, and play blackjack we did!! 

There were a few $10 and $25 tables and one $5 table. We managed to find three seats together and played. And played....AND PLAYED. We finished the rotation of the dealers and started it again. Between the four dealers, we remembered James-- fantastic and interactive dealer and is definitely the best one of the bunch! When all was said and done, we left at 3:30, all three of us up between $90 and $100. 

We actually went back the next night as we had a few hours to spare, and even though we lost some of our winnings from the previous night, we still had a good experience with the dealers and casino as a whole. 

A unique little bonus on the blackjack tables is the side-bet game they have: Straight Jack. Pretty much just try to make a run with the cards you're dealt. So, if are dealt two cards that build on each other (for example, 5 and 6, or 9 and 10), this pays 3-1. Three cards in a row is 25-1, 4 cards is around 125-1, and 5+ is 250-1. Definitely a house game, but a few other players at our table won A LOT of money with this side-bet option.
Also a plus: 12 oz. Blue Moon was $2.50. 

Casino of the Sun is extremely impressive for Tucson! Perhaps sometime this summer I'll stay a weekend there.
Food was excellent! The ribs were so tender and I love all the sauce options. The Mac and cheese, coleslaw and greens were delicious too. Great place would def recommend and visit again
Great service and a fun time. When you can order food, drinks, play some bocce, and listen to some good music you know you are in a special place. Highly recommend to anyone for a chill time.

I was really tired and drunk by the time we got here, but the Ferry ride over was nice and kind of sobered me up a bit. I didn't get seafood, though, but I did get an awesome steak.  The waitstaff was quick, friendly, and the place is nice and easygoing. I'd like to go back and try the seafood the next time I am in town.

If you have ever been to the Cheesecake Factory, you know the biggest complaint about the restaurant is the wait time during prime hours...so let's take that issue off the review.

The menu is about as diverse as they come...this makes the restaurant ideal for large groups with various tastes. The desert menu is ridiculous...great take home options.

The quality has never disappointed us...consistently outstanding. The portions are generous to say the least.

Service (even in prime hours) is quick, helpful, and efficient.

The price is right down the middle for mid-range national chains.

Simply stated, it is the best chain restaurant we have been to.

My go to meal when I am cold or feeling blue is always PHO!! I saw the sign from Fairview and I immediately had to try it.  The interior is refreshing, modern and open.  The service was first class.  My friend is celiac so we asked to see if soy sauce was used in the broth.  The server quickly checked with the kitchen and reported that the only seasoning they used was salt and sugar.  No soy sauce.  You know it's authentic!  Great place for people to go if they are restricted gluten free diet!  

The pho was amazing.  I liked how they had 3 different sizes.  I ordered a medium and it was plenty.   I can't wait to go back and try the other Vietnamese dishes.  Reasonably priced.  So glad this is here!

HALLELUJAH!

Some innovative, INTERESTING, DARING southeast Asian food in NOLA! (And in my neighborhood no less!) The food here is far different from what you'll get at your standard New Orleans Vietnamese restaurant, and light years away from a local Thai place. Everything we ate was aggressively seasoned (and by that I mean perfectly seasoned), cooked to perfection, and unlike anything else in the city.

I've been struggling with the new restaurants in the city because I feel like everyone is doing the same thing - crudos, pastas, flatbreads blah blah blah. Marjie's Grill is wholly unique, and wholly delicious.

Stand outs:
- The charred cabbage salad: This really reminded me of something that would come out of Grandmother's kitchen. Somehow managed to be cooked and doused in delicious sauce but still feel fresh.
- The charred pig knuckles: I always appreciate a restaurant that's ballsy enough to put stuff like this on the menu. If you're not an adventurous eater, I think this is a great gateway into all things beautiful and chewy. TRY IT!
- The half BBQ chicken: This stole the show. You get half of a *perfectly barbecued* chicken, a huge pile of herbs and a delicious sauce. You're instructed to essentially make your own lettuce wraps out of the herbs and top them with the sauce. So yummy. So so yummy. Dreaming about eating this again.

Other notes:
- The restaurant ambiance is very casual- they're currently building a back patio that will be a total game changer.
- Happy hour Tues-Fri 4:30-6:30

This Wendy's is the only one i have been to that takes a while to bring your food up but it be hot and fresh evry other Wendy's I've been to in the yrs of eating take out i can say it was terrible compared to them... Keep up the good work guys

I am trying to be understanding but this was not good. Waiter had mask but oyster person at the bar had it hanging or covering mouth or nose. Others behind the bar no mask. Hostess and waiter did have a mask. What is the point is signing in?  Dozen fresh oysters good. Barbeque Shrimp po boy band -little taste and fries soggy.

day 60...

is it bad to admit that you drink all the left over au jus???

Had an ice'd latte and beignets. They were fine, but service was VERY slow. An order of beignets took over 15 minutes. The high school aged workers spent more time talking with each other and a friend who came in to visit than serving customers. Similar quality at Cafe Dumond, but faster service there.

A Huge Thanks to Main Event Wesley Chapel for helping my Son Cristian pull off the cutest Homecoming proposal!! The bowling pin was adorable!! It makes sense since Main Event was their first date! They had so much fun bowling, playing video games, eating!! A memorable day for them and is!! This place is amazing!!! So much fun!! Seeing this kids happy faces melts my heart!!I love this place!!! Eat Bowl play!!!!Main Event it's the best family entertainment there is!!
Had good atmosphere, but we waited about 45 minutes for our food. The waiters and waitresses were really nice. The food was kind of bland and mediocre and not worth 45 minutes. I would not recommend

As much as I like to stay away from the retirement community-like streets of  Downtown Clayton, I will definitely be back for breakfast here! The space is laid out like diner with wooden furniture (I'm pretty sure). Your girlfriend/wife will think it's so cute (I'm sure). The entire staff is very hipster, something I found very strange for Clayton, but those hipsters sure do know their way around a skillet! I ordered the salmon hash, but every order at my table and every table around me looked pretty freaking incredible. My mom thought it was so great that she wanted to buy some souvenir coffee mugs. The server charged us $5, but I think he just made up a number.
Great food and great service! Thank you Michael for making our first dining experience great!

Whenever I am in Indiana I go to Le Peep for breakfast glad their was one across the street from my hotel.  The first time I had Le Peep was the Downtown restaurant and the food was delicious. It is a great restaurant for breakfast never done lunch. I had the Hen Pen eggs, sausage and potatoes. One kid of mine had the Lumberjack combo that comes with pancakes.   My other son had the very berry French toast that had granola mix into his French toast. He said it was very tasty he was glad we went here instead of the the hotel breakfast.

I've eaten here many times and and always enjoyed the pulled pork sandwiches. Today I had a late lunch and chose to eat at the bar.

I selected a pulled pork sandwich with salad bar and tea. As much as I always enjoyed the seafood salad, it didn't taste fresh. 

My sandwich had less meat than usual and it didn't have the smoked taste. Needless to say, this experience wasn't up to par for some reason. Bar tender was friendly and efficient. 

There is so much competition for restaurant dollars in North Pinellas. First off, servers need to be personable and make suggestions. No one knew if I was a regular customer or first timer. No one asked. 

Ratings for area Sonny's are average. There's got to be a reason. I've enjoyed previous visits yet after today Sonny's drops further down my list of available options.

When this place first opened it was top of line, fast seating, great service, food was served fast, the staff was always friendly, BUT it seems the past year, everything has declined. Take my most recent experience there. The once fast seating is done with, I recently called 2 hours ahead for a 15 person party, spoke with the manager and she told me she would guarantee our seating within 20 minutes of arrival. We showed up 15 minutes before our time as requested, waited the 15 plus the 20 we were told it would most likely take and then an additional 45 minutes on top of it. I asked the greeter about how much longer after an hour how much longer and she replied with a "We have a table, but the people are camping and there's nothing I can do about it, so I don't know what to tell you," and followed that up with an eye roll. It took everything I had not to lunge at her for that blatant disrespect. I asked to speak with the manager and she was very condescending with her attitude implying they were busy (it was a Thursday night), and when I informed her that 2 other larger parties arrived and were seated before us, she shrugged, and said "It happens." She then offered to comp 2 appetizers. Our appetizers took 40 minutes to get, and both were horrible. One of them, the rattle snake bites, were so over cooked that the cheese inside was nonexistent. The other (fried pickles) were so coated with grease from the fryer that they were floating in it. The salads came out all wrong, my chili never came even though I asked about it 4 times. When the main dishes came out another 35 minutes later, we were informed they had run out of sweet potatoes and were cooking more but it would be an additional 45 minutes to an hour for them. So those who ordered it were asked if they wanted something else and told that they would get a sweet potato to go. Half of the substitutes never came out and a quarter of those that did weren't right. My steak was completely burnt on one side and raw on the other, the onions I had on the steak were raw, 2 of the other steaks were all nervy but upon complaint ended up being comped. One persons chicken was raw, my brother found a hair in his french fries, and then low and behold, my chili arrived, cold, without crackers or the cheese on top. With out receipts came the sweet potatoes, 2 of which were not cooked all the way, and didn't have the toppings those in my group asked for. Drinks went unfilled, it seemed to take an act of God to get anyones attention, and to top it all off, it was my birthday dinner and everyone was now pissed from such shitty service. I don't understand how the restaurant I used to love and deemed my favorite in town went from an 11 on a scale of 1 to 10 to a -100000000. I will never again go to this restaurant, nor is anyone else in my party who went. I will drive an additional 40 minutes to the one on Wilmot next time. Oh I will give them one plus, the bread was the only thing that came out fast, and provided some sustenance so we didn't starve to death during the 3-4 freaking hours we were there. To the manager, if you read this, I'm seriously disappointed in your failure to motivate your crew, and your lack of concern for your customers.

DONT GO TO THIS MCDONALDS AFTER MIDNIGHT OR YOU WILL TURN INTO A GREMLIN!!! A Gremlin filled with Super-sized McRage cause this McDonald's McSucks Ballz!!Their "system" seems to constantly be going down, and other times they act like they're closed, when they clearly should be open. (I'm talking hours before their advertised closing time)  I have gone to this McDonald's over 20x cause it's right near my friends house. My point: ITS NOT A FLUKE, ITS A PATTERN! Look, it's McDonald's, I get it. . . But this is ridiculous!

We came here for dinner last night before the book of mormon. Good choice, I must say. I took a star mainly because their happy hour drink specials SUCK! They have 3.00 beers and 3.00 premiums....but that's it. The food on happy hour was fantastic though. To drink i tried the Rose something or other. I really enjoyed it but if you don't like sweet things, don't get it. I also had their "skinny margarita" it's not on the menu but it was freaking fantastic. You need to get it.  To eat we had the sliders, the nachos with guac, the goat cheese balls, and the pear salad. My husband ate the pear salad, so not sure how that was but he seemed to enjoy it. ALl of these things were fantastic though. The sliders were exceptional.....I don't know what they season/marinate the meat with but I want to cook EVERYTHING in it! The goat cheese balls were great and the nachos were huge and good. All in all, I'm glad we came to Fly!

I absolutely LOVE this place!!!! Came here for brunch with my husband while we were visiting NOLA. Everything we ordered was delicious, for drinks, we got bloody marys and I had to order the copper bunny (comes in a beautiful copper bunny) and it was great! For food, we ordered the hamachi everything doughnut, truffle fonduta egg dish, coconut french toast and banana zeppoles, and every dish was amazing. Highly recommended!

Famoso's Quattro Fomaggi Pizzetta and Napoli Salad are my go to for casual Saturday meals out. 
I have eaten here on numerous occasions and really appreciate that the quality of my meal is consistent. I am yet to have a bad experience here. It can get busy to the point that it becomes quite loud and cramped but only if you go at peak times. 
Both the staff and the decor are welcoming!
Try the Sangria or the Nutella Pizza - they do not disappoint.

Mid Peninsula Seafood is a spot of golden fried hole-in-the-wall heaven. And I make an effort to eat there every time I'm back in St. Pete.

So two years ago I was staying in St. Pete and was craving some fried seafood. And not just any fried seafood but two things in particular: conch and gator. Thanks to Yelp, Mid Peninsula was the only option (seriously how can you call yourself "Old Key West Bar & Grill" when you don't even have conch fritters on the menu?) and with high reviews it was worth checking out.

As you can see from the other reviews, it is worth it. 

You enter into a mix of Florida kitsch from the partial lobby seating, to the seafood counter you order everything at, to the main seating area with covered benches and even a corner for live music.

The menu is a huge mix of seafood options. It takes a while because some days have some crazy fish sandwich specials, but between plates, sandwiches, starters and more there are a ton of options. I usually get the following:

-Cracked Conch or Conch Fritters: I'm partial to cracked conch but the fritters are also great. They give you a good portion for the starter option, full of great breading and flavor. They also pound the crap out of it so it is chewy but you can still bite through.

-Gator Bites: Because I want to feel like an Alpha predator and not many places offer it. Chewy, tasty gator in good sized chunks. 

-Steak Fries: The pinnacle of fries.

-Slaw: honestly good slaw!

-Hushpuppies: depending on how much fried balls of dough you want, these are also solid.

-Sweet Tea: Really good and helps wash down the layers of fried food.

So if looking for a ton of fresh, fried seafood in a fun, laid back experience, I cannot recommend Mid Peninsula Seafood enough. I'm showing off the pictures and counting down the days until I'm back. Really should go in a group so we can try more!

Environment: For a place 20 min over the bridge from Philly, I would easily choose this place over any sushi establishment in the city. Very authentic Japanese-like restaurant, although owned by a Korean establishment. Great great place for an intimate, low-lit, low-key, romantic place to eat. Many people will complain about the low ceiling, but it only adds to the authentic experience!

Service: Excellent, they did everything possible to attend to us! Really gave you the full experience as if you blind folded your date to bring them through the door and have them feel like they "stepped into the streets of Kyoto." (Hint: You should probably do this if you bring your date here, haha!)

Food: Absolutely amazing.. I don't know where to start. Pretty authentic chirashi bowl (which you won't get the same quality as the ones in Japan, obviously!) Considering this is the East Coast, this is REALLY as good as it gets. You will not regret getting the chirashi bowl which comes with a few different cuts of sashimi, the sweet egg, layered over rice and their sweet seaweed seasoning to top it all off. 

Price: I wouldn't go here often; only for special occasions. After tax and tip you are looking at $35-40 a person considering you get chirashi and share an appetizer.
Love Boca! Great staff, atmosphere and food! Their farm to table menu is a foodie's dream. I am always a fan of their flat breads.

I've already reviewed Wawa (in my hometown in PA) so this is a bit of a cheat, but...oh well. Wawa gets 5 stars for the following reasons:

*One of the best chicken salads hoagies in the world (and I am VERY picky about Chicken Salad) I've had it 3 times since they opened 5 days ago (don't judge me)

*The nostalgia. I was born and raised in Bucks County, PA and grew up with Wawa...tastes like home!

*Herr's potato chips (esp the sour cream and onion)

*Wawa brand iced tea

*Tastykakes

*Clean, cheap and fast

*Good breakfast sandwiches


Love it---go there!

There are a number of things that I found satisfying about Grimaldi's. First off the music put in a 50's-60's mood, probably one of the most satisfying I've ever heard at a pizza place. Secondly, our server Wesley was very helpful and worked hard to gets us our food and refills quickly. And last off, the food was delightful, served in generous portions (whatever size you think you can handle order one below) all in all an amazing pizzeria that all should experience.

I really liked this place this was my to go Chinese restaurant in the city... but not anymore they have disappoint me so I ordered my usual general chicken and take It out to go enjoy at home i start eat my food and start chewing on a piece of metal looked like a staple and my food smell like it was starting to spoil.. not good the good thing was that I didn't give my kids the food or it would of been a different situatio.. step your game back up guys .

I'll start by saying that MacDinton's is a good bar.  They have a great variety of booze and beer and the staff is generally pretty good about helping you out with your beverage selection.  As a soccer fan (kind of) I think it's nifty that they're willing to show matches and that they carry a lot of the EPL , UEFA, et al.  Even during prime drinking hours (after 9pm on weekends) they'll often have important matches playing throughout the inside of the bar with sound.  Again, there's not much you can knock this on their ability to serve quality drinks.  

If only that were the whole story.  In my opinion this bar mostly suffers from being so popular.  Hear me out now. On weekends this place is absolutely packed, as in call the fire marshal packed.  At this point there you'll likely have trouble doing a lot of things, among them being: getting a drink or any kind of attention from a bartender, getting to the bathroom, walking around and forget about the ability to communicate with your companions.  As a non-douche I can also say that it is in fact filled with douches, they flock flock to this place.  But that's not without reason though.  Some of the most beautiful women in the Tampa Bay area also frequent this bar, so I guess they're just following the scent...

I love Reservoir. It has great coffee and a great atmosphere. The LGD has a plethora of amazing coffee shops, but Reservoir is the best place to sit and enjoy your coffee. The quiche is my favorite thing to eat there, but for lunch I really like the falafel sandwich.

Maybe 2-3 times a year, I reconcile my red meat craving, dislike for chains, and cheap budget to visit O'Charley's and order the Louisiana sirloin medium-rare. The sirloin is pretty decent for the price, cooked appropriately per my med-rare request, and rubbed in a generic Cajun seasoning and topped with butter. The portion is so huge that I always have enough leftovers to make killer steak & egg burritos for 2-3 people the next morning.  I typically order the loaded potato soap calorie/fat bomb as a side, and add heaps of black pepper and torn-up bits of the buttered rolls. The rolls are addictive, so we typically stick to one basket.  My visit to this particular location started off to be not very promising, a potential 2-star experience due to a longer-than-quoted wait and a hoard of screaming children in the waiting area.  We were luckily seated away from the hoard in the bar section, and enjoyed some privacy and average service while giving in to my semi-annual craving. O'Charleys is maybe one baby notch better than the comparable TGI-Chili-bees.

DISCLAIMER:  When in Chinatown, it would be a pretty good idea to bring a Chinese friend, or at the very least, somebody who understands how to read Chinese.  Not doing so could be considered foolish.  That being said, I'm evaluating this restaurant on those merits, it being a Chinese eatery in a Chinatown.

The food?  Unquestionably Chinese.  If you're used to takeout and Americanized food, expect something different.  You might not hate it, but at the same time, you shouldn't expect it to taste like Americanized Chinese.  It would be sorta like eating at Taco Bell all your life only to realize on your trip to a Mexican restaurant in Mexico that they don't really do tacos and burritos.  That being said, the quality of the food is well worth what you pay for, and very delicious.

The service is actually pretty darn good too, albeit a different type of service than most would be accustomed to.  Don't let the staff that speaks in sometimes broken English fool you:  They understand English well enough to take your order if you use plain language.  From then on out, they'll concentrate solely on getting food out to you as quickly as possible, without regard for the order that the food comes out in or whether or not you run out of water.
