But the manager definitely needs to train their employees how to be servers. I've been rushed to order, with the waiter literally standing there waiting for me to order. Or just completely forgotten about!

Loved French toast! There is limited seating so you'll want to get here early, but it was worth the wait. I got the breakfast sandwich which was delicious and my table split a king cake French toast. You'll definitely want to share this one or risk getting sick with how sweet it is! Will be back!

Tried this place recently on account of a flyer in the mail. Once I called n placed my order I had a good feeling about this place, the guy who answered had an Italian accent like what I'm accustomed to back home. 
Ordered my usual ( Sicilian str8 up ) and opted to have it delivered which unfortunately took over an hour. 
However once I received my box of delicious looking eye candy the angst of waiting evaporated.  
Good crust light  well balanced sauce with low acidity ( aka low agada occurrence)  and a generous slathering of creamy moozaell with a touch of goodness that unfortunately only us Italians can provide.  
I was very impressed and elated to find another pizzeria that serves the pizza I grew up back on LI.  Angelo and his staff very friendly and will treat you like famiglia.

I've only gotten take out from here but was pleasantly surprised with the food. The portions are decent, prices are good, and the food itself is great. The pad Thai and crab Rangoon are awesome. I would definitely recommend those. The pork fried rice, tom yum soup (sweet and sour with shrimp), and volcano tofu (fried tofu with green curry and veggies) are also good. The only downside is that they don't deliver. At least when we called for delivery they told us to use an online service, which wasn't working properly.
Hella greasy and overpriced. Standard French Quarter slice, I'd say. Won't be back unless in a super pinch. Ordering process was also super clunky.

We placed an order waited 40 minutes only to be called by the drive and told that that the restaurant manager told him they were to busy to fulfill the order. Really like there food but can't trust them to deliver. By the time
We found out that they refused to deliver it was too late to order elsewhere and eat at a decent hour. To make matters worse we won't get our refund for 5 days. This sucks.
Had buffet breakfast Brenda the host was phenomenal food was hot an fresh an omelet station was great for $20 an unlimited mimosas $12

Price: 2
Flavor: 5
Variety: 5
Ambience: 5
Service: 5

Amazing, simply done to perfection. I joined a group and we ordered appetizers (sushi and oysters), steaks and sides. Everything was delicious. 10oz filet was tender, well seasoned and flavorful. The 34oz ribeye was bananas. You could share between 3 people,but it was a little less than they wanted for the 3 male carnivores who ordered it. All steaks need to have accompaniments, or side dishes. We ordered truffled Mac and cheese (5*), mushrooms (5*), asparagus (4*), Brussels sprouts (5*), and garlic mashed potatoes (5*). The wine selection was ample and great.

It all began when I discovered our reservation for 10 had been given away.  We were running 15 minutes late so I called ahead, but apparently when I spoke to the manager upon arriving, this call never occurred.  After this, I was determined to go elsewhere, but my best friend who loves Italian and was visiting home from Vegas, had her heart set on this childhood favorite.  So I caved...I'm such a sucker.

The manager did scrounge up a table for us pretty quickly (maybe it was the laser looks we were giving him), and we were introduced to the best part of the restaurant: our waiter.  This guy was so cheerful and animated he immediately brightened everyone's mood, despite the murky-looking water and completely lackluster food.  

The interior of the restaurant is gorgeous, with high, beamed ceilings and a plush lounge.  But the best part, the waiter, stood on a chair to sing me happy birthday and got the whole restaurant involved.  No, it wasn't my birthday.  Not that we faked it or anything, but for some reason he asked us who had the most recent one, which happened to be me.  Guess he felt like giving out free desserts.  Anyway, this normally would have made my cheeks burn (which it did a little), but it was all in good fun and we ended up experiencing a pretty good end to a pretty crappy beginning.

Decided to try this place out with my hubby for a breakfast date! This place certainly doesn't disappoint. Charming quaint little space with 4 outside tables and two inside plus some. The frenchness & friendliness of the owners is noted! I had the ham and cheese croissant& a cinnamon roll , perfection! With a cappuccino of course and my hubby had the omelette with a side green salad and house handle bar coffee. 

The only downside is it doesn't have a restroom????

Oui oui, We'll be back!

So.. this place has strange hours. 10PM - 1:30PM. Welcome to the Twilight Zone. Aside from the food being pretty cheap, our group witnessed some of the most disgusting food preparation techniques we'd ever come across. The short order cook was literally buttering bread with his hands (like... fingerprints in the butter), sometimes immediately after handling raw meat. More often than not he was using his hands to manage the stuff cooking on the grill. It was gross to the max. Don't think I'll be back here anytime soon.

I have been to two shows here are both were amazing! The tickets for national acts are between $26.00-$30.00+ per ticket.
The openers are usually local and really entertaining!! Their is a two item minimum per person in the dinning room. Be prepared for your evening to cost you around $100.00 for a party of two plus tip (tickets, food, drink etc) 
That being said.... it is totally worth it!! 
My fiance and I went to see Natasha Leggero months ago and last weekend we saw Ryan Hamilton!!
 I just found out they do a Saturday Night midnight show with 12 local comics called the dirty dozen for $12.00... I will definitely be checking that out!!!
The food is okay... I have enjoyed the appetizers more than the entrees. The spinach dip and boneless wings are pretty darn good on the spectrum of bar food! 
If you have never seen live comedy... do yourself a favor and check it out!!

I went to their Supper Club after the daily market closed. Great place - excellent fixed menu and good wine/beer selection. It was also served at a leisurely pace (a good thing) allowing for plenty of time between courses and good discussion at the table. This is a nice contrast to places where it feels like there is 30 seconds between courses and the restaurant is focused on turning tables 3x during dinner. The food was outstanding and overall it is a GREAT value. The ambiance is very informal - feels like you are in someone's dining room, and it is not very noisy.

Recommended!!

I love this place. It is very italian inside with the faux painted walls, the clouds on the ceiling, the Frank Sinatra coming from overhead and the delicious smells coming from the kitchen. I highly recommend the bruschetta- big slices of bread packed with the tomatoe goodness combo on top. Usually the stuff falls off of those tiny pieces of bread when I have ordered brushetta out before. Not in this case! The service was fast and our waitress Megan was professonal, friendly and attentive. My husband ordered the tri colored tortilleni with crab meat and clams. I ordered the broccoli/spinach penne with olive oil and garlic. VERY good meal, large portions. I am particular on my italian restaurants and this one is top notch!

The workers were really sweet.They had a rude customer that was holding up the entire drive-through line till after closing but still served us all. They even gave me a free drink and extra spring roll and were very apologetic for something that wasn't their fault. Super sweet!

I'm surprised i'm only NOW writing a review for Nan Zhou! I've been a handful of times, loving every visit and excited to return.

My most recent visit was on a sunny, freezing day for lunch - so I needed to warm up with some soup. I believe i got the House Special Soup, which comes loaded with brisket and other delicious meats - with shaved noodles (I wanted to try them, but I think hand drawn would have been the way to go.)

Service was super friendly and speedy. I need to come back and work my way through the other noodle dishes, and check out the non-noodle plates as well.

We have visited Marsha Brown in downtown New Hope a few times because we love the atmosphere, décor, attention and great creole food offered here.  After attending the Bluegrass Festival at Peddler's Village on Saturday we stopped for early dinner with 6 family members and were promptly accommodated without previous reservations!!!  With our drink selections out of the way including wine from their extensive list we were ready for food.  The youngest member of the family chose the typical chicken fingers and fries which is one of the children's selections the restaurant has though it is not listed on the menu; among the other food choices made were Crab Cheesecake, Lollipop Lamb Chops, Lobster and Shrimp Bisque, Gumbo, Prosciutto Salad, and Surf and Turf.  We were all happy with our selections even though the Lollipop Lamb Chops was not what we expected!!! The chops were deep fried which totally messed up the dish!! The mint accompaniment to this dish did it no justice; something else is needed to bring up to the standard!  The Crab Cheesecake was as delight able as always, creamy and tasty but not over the top perfect!  The soups although served lukewarm were well prepared with the right combination of seafood and spices.  The winner dish was the Surf and Turf which was a combination of their delightful crab cakes and beef fillets accompanied by crawfish risotto; all well prepared and presented.  Everybody raved about the bread served with the meal which we found out came out of a bakery in Trenton, NJ!  Overall, I believe we all left content and satisfied for the time spent in the relaxing, attentive and superior atmosphere offered at Marsha Brown!

tl;dr this Italian BYOB just off of Rittenhouse Square might work for a large party just looking for a good time that doesn't care about the quality of food

I had heard mixed reviews for Melograno from a variety of sources. Some called it the best Italian BYOB in Philly, while others lambasted it for poor service and subpar food. If anything, all this controversy left me needing to find out the real deal for myself.

Walking into Melograno with my partner for an 8PM Friday reservation, I immediately took notice of the cozy decor. Melograno was lofted with exposed wooden beams overhead,  finished with heavy accent lighting, sliding barn doors, and knick-knacks around the walls (including a motor scooter!).

However, the coziness ended there. To say this restaurant was busy would be an understatement. Pop music playing in the background, which ended up being completely drowned out by how incredibly loud this restaurant is. It took nearly 15 minutes to be seated, despite our table having been ready for that whole time. We were seated next to the front window, with the hostess desk (and therefore a line of people still waiting to be seated) blocking us from any servers. And, to be quite frank, the service was awful. It took another 10 minutes after we were seated for anyone to even greet us at our table. Then, it took over 30 minutes on top of that just to get us water -- hilariously, we received our appetizers before our water! Finally, our "starter" bread came with our entrees, a full hour after we had been seated, despite us being promised several times that it was "on the way."

And I haven't even begun speaking about the food. We ordered the Calamari Puttanesca, the Polenta with Oyster Mushroom Special, the Pappardelle al Ragú di Cinghiale, and the Squid Ink Fusilli Special. The polenta, although described by our server as being served "crispy" was mushy and flavorless, with just a dab of red sauce on top. Any flavor that was in that dish came solely from the oyster mushrooms. The calamari was a bit rubbery, although the stew it was served in was really tasty especially with copious amounts of olives and capers. Onto to pasta dishes, I will say that, for both, the noodles themselves were clearly homemade and well-cooked. However, the fusilli lacking in flavor, even though it was served with a good deal of assorted seafood. Unfortunately, some of the mussels were sandy and inedible. On the other hand, the pappardelle, which had only a tiny scoop of the wild boar ragu, ended up leaving much to be desired. To top it all off, our waiter became defensive at the end of our experience when I told him our meal was only "okay."

Overall, I found our meal to be lackluster. In fact, I found myself complimenting the wine (which we BYOB'ed!) more than Melograno itself. In any case, I don't plan on coming back anytime, ever.

This is my new favorite breakfast spot. Just make sure to call ahead or check in on the app. Because this place is new, everyone is finding out how great it is and the place stays packed. I could order everything on the menu and be completely satisfied. Thank you to my wonderful waitress Cece!
This spot is serving takeout during Covid! Easy ordering and the pizzas turned out great :)

Great service! Food was mixed reviews, we loved the Brussels sprouts, the fig dish, and the pea dish, but the prawns were OK. Also this was a small plate restaurant so we all shared everything family style. Drinks were bomb and so was the service. Very cute atmosphere as well and we sat at the community table (which we reserved 20 minutes before arriving- pro tip!)

Would come back and a great place for lunch/ dinner.
great service.   Trish is the best.   Always fell welcomed and food service is great as well.

By far the BEST place around!!! 
Food - 5*
Atmosphere -5*
Service - 5*
Staff - 5*
The Butcher and Barkeep has been a blessing since they opened. You may have to wait for a table on a Friday and Saturday night but it's WELL worth the wait! You are greeted the minute you walk in, if not only by one of the staff, but also one of the owners, you'll always feel welcome and appreciated you're there.
My husband and I have probably tried everything on the menu and not once was there nothing but an extraordinary experience, yes, the food is that good!
I promise you won't be disappointed!
Beautiful eats! We loved the muffaletta, but nothing topped the fried Mac and Cheese with gumbo. Astonishing. Lovely service as well.

I went here with my husband after I purchased a Groupon. I loved the ambiance....I thought it was really romantic and classy. This is definitely a place you want to come dressed-up to. I'm not sure if they require it, but you should probably come in a suit coat if you're a man. They have about 3 people at any given time serving you, and all of the staff are really dressed up. 

The food was good too. They have some interesting items on the menu, such a dish that was cooked for Oprah and another that was prepared for Ronald Reagan's inaugural dinner. I tried the pasta dish from Ronald Reagan's inaugural dinner, and it was very good. My only complaint about this place was that the lobster ravioli was $16 for ONE square of ravioli.....even the waiter commented on it (too bad he didn't warn me before I ordered it though). Overall, very pleased (just wouldn't order the lobster ravioli again :) ). In terms of price, though, it may be a little expensive without a Groupon.
From the moment we walked in, the staff has been very pleasant. The rooms and bathroom are very clean and neatly organized. The pillows are AMAZINGLY SOFT!!

review is only for the bites menu. We had just gotten into town and was looking for a lite bite there is a parking garage close by and easy to get too. I had a beer which to me seemed pretty small i.e 10 oz and wife had a glass of wine. We got the Mormon funeral potatoes which were good. I had the beet salad which was awful way to much dressing and the beets slightly undercooked and my wife had the soup which she said was good. My main beef is the value of the meal and sticker shock of $55 with tip $63. You would think in a bites menu offering 5 items there would be some value. Big mistake we should have went to Harry and Izzy's next door and got the $13 burger and probably paid half for a better meal.

Holy burrito! My husband and I went for dinner the other night and it was excellent!

First the drinks, the margaritas were really good. A bit on the strong side but, no complaints here. Then there was the nachos! Oh,the nachos... we got the Hawaii nachos and the combination of the pineapple mango salsa with the avocado and the bacon - oh my goodness delicious! They were a Briton the cheesy side but overall we were very content. We split the bacon azul quesadilla. It was pretty much a blue cheese burger and the flavors melded so well. It was delicious. The service was good - not overly attentive but they definitely took care of us! 

Overall, would definitely go back and would highly recommend!

We have been to this chili's at least 1/2 dozen times and have been happy till last night.
We always sit in the bar for happy hour.
The table we got was sticky,
My wife was served a glass of wine in a dirty glass.
My fajitas were not sizzling but did have a burnt smell to them, my wife said what is that smell and I said I think it's my fajitas.
They had the smallest portion of meat I have ever seen on a fajita order.
They forgot to add the guacamole to our nacho order.
Considering all the problems we had i would shave to say they have a real management problem at this location.

Loved this spot. The food was great! The servers were friendly....heaven.com!

I went here for a friend's surprise birthday party. I was impressed by the friendliness of the servers. Despite taking orders for multiple people at the same time, after 4 hours, no one looked or acted flustered. The menu consisted of crab cakes-moist and well flavored, bruschetta-crispy toast well seasoned veggies, cocktail shrimp-HUGE (like the size of your head), egg rolls-great sauce and not greasy at all, and calamari-well seasoned not greasy and delicious. Did I mention the cocktail shrimp were  huge? Like really huge? Omg! 

Anyway after I large party you would expect some sense of exasperation with the party but the servers were smiling friendly and very willing to please. I'm so going back.....and I live 3 states away
Delicious Neapolitan style pizza, very friendly service. They have about 6-8 tables outside, a bar countertop inside to eat. One of our favorite spots to go to in St. Louis!

This place was unreal. The Mole poblano sweet potato fries were amazing. It could be the newness but they really may be the best fries in the city. I had the chicken and shrimp tacos and both were very good, and I'm what you may consider a bit of a taco snob. On top of that I had the best bubble I've ever had in Indy. Felt a little pricey but for this food who cares?

I was looking for Italian food but nothing like I've had before, I wanted to try something new. There were many to choose from but the pictures posted on yelp pointed me in the direction of Julian's Little Italy. This was my first time dining alone and what an amazing experience! I truly enjoyed myself. The establishment was clean, everyone was friendly, and my meal was amazing! I had the Chicken Saltimbocca a la Romana. DELICIOUS! The host at the front desk was very welcoming (he was shocked that I was dining alone) and my server Leslie was an absolute sweetheart! Thank you Julian's Little Italy, I'll definitely dine with you again!

The good, the bad, the ugly...

The good:  Cabbage w/Duck Bacon, yes get that!  Seasoned to perfection, a wonderful side dish.  Vodka Gimlet, their bartender is on point.  Would have loved to get several.  Shrimp Poboy, very good seasoning on the shrimp and the remoulade sauce.  I did take off 1/2 the bread though.  Service was awesome!

The bad: Mac n Cheese lacked seasoning and the appetizer Fried Green Tomatoes and Pickles was not a portion relative to price.  In addition to that, the Fried Green Tomatoes needed more seasoning.

The ugly: Beignets...now, to be fair, I'm partial to Cafe Du Mond in New Orleans, so, there's no one who can live up to them, however, Fleur wasn't even close.  Won't order these again.

Overall, I did enjoy the meal and I will visit again.  The music playing in the restaurant was great.  I wish I had their playlist.
This place saved us as we got in last minute before the kitchen closed for our sons birthday. The food and service was great we will definitely e back.

I was really excited to try this place . I haven't been Uptown much since the pandemic started. I have really been looking for a good Vegan place. I got a Chikn sandwich that was sopping with grease. The Seitan was bland and chewy. The fries were good and came with a honey mustard which was good, but nothing special. Unfortunately, this isn't the good Vegan place that I was looking for and that makes me sad.

The Capital Grille is a great American Steakhouse. The staff are very polite and even ask if you have any food allergies. They also have really good services like a coat check in and valet. Although pricey, the food is worth it. The steaks are cooked perfectly and the portions are large. Its a nice place to go for birthday's or special occasions, no matter which location you got to.

While the pizza is far from the best, the rib eye is awesome. I didn't want to give it 5 stars, but it met the criteria. Pizza: Check, Potato Skins: Check, Good Beer Selection: Check, Good Bartender: Check. Throw that in with a super cheap and good rib eye, you have 5 stars. Pizza is not great, but it's a bar. That is like going to a baseball game and expecting the best hot dog in the world. It has a little of everything. 

Don't confuse this place with the Turtle Bay on Bourbon. The one on Bourbon has crazy prices and seems to be set up for the drunken debauchery that happens there. The big difference is when you leave the one on Bourbon, you'll see drunken fools stumbling around. This one has gutter punks. Pick your poison.

I love the margaritas here. The low carb menu is superb and the tortillas and salsa is delicious.
The nachos are addictive!

Best Chinese food we have found in Indianapolis! It is also moderately priced. 

If this alone did not sell us on the restaurant, the staff is also very friendly and appreciative. The owners came out to make sure we were enjoying our meal.

Carry out is good, but if time allows I would recommend dining in. The decor is very cool!

Decent food.  Nothing to write home about.  It's definitely a hole in the wall but its super cheap and you can feed an entire family of 5 for under $50.  If you looking for some cheap greasy food after a night of partying this place will do the trick.

The worst dining experience I have ever had. The food quality, staff and service were terrible. Stay Away! The chef was unsanitary, inattentive and rude. In between dropping food in the garbage then serving it, he made inappropriate sexual comments about the waitresses/female patrons. It was very uncomfortable. The waiter was inattentive and got 4/6 orders wrong. The manager had no idea what she was doing. Several others already had complained to her. There was a fight at the table behind us. The manager watched a drunk guy about my age bully and scream at a family out for dinner. Both patrons remained and were continued to be served alcohol. The drunken patron spilled several drinks and feel on the way to the restroom. The rice was undercooked and I left after being severed the wrong order for the 4th time, that was dragged through the garbage slot. I could not be paid to go back. Avoid at all cost!!! Stay away! It's a shame that they closed Arriagatos, but this place is awful. Next time we will try eido's.

My mom always loved ordering from here. Very good Mexican food, always delicious and served in big portions. Staff is always friendly and attentive. Whenever you're craving some tacos, skip Taco Bell and come here.
Great appetizer, spinach artichoke dip chips were good. Awful stuffed baked potato with blackened chicken. The potato was bad and the chicken was as dry as jerky.
Great food. Plush booths. Great atmosphere. Crab cake was serious with no filler. Steak was cooke perfectly.  Will be back soon.

Short rib sweet potato tots - those alone are worth a second go!
I did a to-go order, and everything went smoothly. The correct pick up time was given, and everyone was professional and friendly.
The inside is kind of rustic decorated - it fit the atmosphere. 
Someone opened the door for me coming in, and going out (two different employees) - nice little touch!!

The food was delicious.  I had a mixed platter appetizer, lamb kabob and both were amazingly tasty!  Topped it off with a giant bowl of rice pudding.  The bill stacked up quick, but it was reasonably priced for the quality of food that we received.  Can't wait to go back again. I only wish it were closer to my apartment..

There is no way anyone could give this place than a 4 or 5 rating. For me, it's a 5. I don't think I'll ever go any where else for baked goods or pastry. Everything was fresh, delicious, and exploding with flavor. The inside of this shop was clean, trays of desserts kept churning out as we were picking out what we wanted. We wanted to try everything but this trip we tried the cream puffs, pesca alla crepe, carrot cake, pumpkin cheesecake. There's a large selection of sweets so I will keep going back to try more. Let's talk about price. CHEAP. I was shocked that i was only charge $16. Definitely going back. So happy we love so close.

Maybe I was expecting more of a Tavern-homier feel, but it seemed more classy than that. The menu is limited but offers some refreshing options that aren't generic bar food. I enjoyed my trout dip appetizer ($11). All I wanted was something small to munch on after touring the sites in Old City. Price is appropriate considering location and restaurant atmosphere. I didnt try any drinks though. A full meal at dinner time, (drink + entree) will definitely put you over $35. The service was quick and our waitress was sincerely nice. This seems like a good place to revisit if I'm in the mood for dishing out more $$$.
This restaurant is an absolute gem in a town where fast food seems to be all that is available.
The Best in Ruskin,FL hands down. And fast and fresh upon request. This is the only food my baby girl will eat
OMG!!! I only had the bandeja and it was delicious. The beans were authentic, just like my abuelita use to make . Highly recommend it

Wow, were to start. Was overcharged as a failure to recognize their own special, order did not contain all the requested ingredients, and had to wait longer than suggested. Overall, terrible. Take your money elsewhere if you can.

Ribs, hot link and pulled chicken were excellent. I would pass on the pulled pork. For the sides, potato salad was good, but the deep fried corn on the cob was not good. Deep frying the corn seemed to take all the flavor out.

Ok I have only eaten brunch here a bunch of times, as I stay in the neighbourhood when in town. The food is ok when not cold due to lack of motivated staff. I chatted with the manager once and she said good staff hard to find in Edmonton, everybody want $25hr, well a good waiter makes $25hr in their tips if they give even basic service, what shocked me even more was the manager never pitched in to set an example of what the wait staff should be doing. Hire them train them and they will make money or you will go out of business.

Reasonable price.....delicious....

don't forget to order beefstroganov ($18)  and mocha parfait.

What I had:

Split Pea Soup: um...yummy
Arugula Salad ($7): love it
Beefstroganov ($18): Tasty
Broiled Crab Cakes ($26): there are 2 jumbo crab cakes which you can ask them to split for 2 dishes......my mom shared this dish with my dad.

Don't show up a few minutes late for your reservations because you won't get in. We called a head to let them know there was an accident on our route and we would be just a few minutes late. We were told they could not and would not hold our table. Turned out good for us because we ended up somewhere with better ratings. Given this level of service we probably won't even give this place a shot

Terrible service. The old lady manager with the blue hair was rude. Waited 75 minutes for food. Instead of apologizing she invited me to the kitchen to see how small it was in justification for the wait.
Avoid it at all cost unless you desire to be treated as a nuisance instead of a valued customer. Very disappointed and dissatisfied

Even in Florida, it's a challenge to find a full menu of genuine, authentic Cuban food as the Cubans are partaking of right now in Havana. I found it at La Yuma, complete with full bar and live Latin music. Highly recommend La Yuma to all who want traditional Cuban cuisine and can't get over to Havana right now!

Under cooked bread was a terrible start, I'll see if I can upload a picture it was like play doe... The top of the bread was completely white, and not cooked at all inside. 

I had the steakhouse salad with Bleu cheese dressing, the avocados were very fresh, after the bread I was surprised. My companion had the wings and said that they were big but not to fatty.

I disided to use the bathroom before we left, but it was so dirty and gross I designed to hold it... 

It will probably be another 10 years before someone talks me into going here again.
Always fast and reliable. Good burgers and fresh fries. Not a whole lot else to say. Probably one of the better locations I've been to
Really a great value i love dots when i want something for a big cheat meal for a great price :)

Thanks to fellow Yelper (Ivonne C's.) review, we booked a reservation last night via OpenTable; glad we did as the place was quite packed. (especially the bar area). The inside has been nicely remodeled with a wood motif theme (lots of recycled wood from the previous restaurant). I like the solid wood  tables (kind of butcher block style). They have a 16-foot communal/large party  table in the center.  The bar looks the same/similar to the previous Cork restaurant.

Our server (Mark) was excellent. He gave us the perfect mix of attention and space. Our water glasses were continuously refreshed. Our plates were cleared in a timely manner.

The food menu is comprised mostly of small plate offerings. (good for tapas style sharing). The specials are written on a huge blackboard. They have 17 craft & belgian beers on draft. The server told us they have 100 bottled beers (the menu was quite extensive). Food/beer prices were reasonable. At first glance, the per-wine-glass pricing looked a little steeper. (compared to Treno down the street)

For our libations, I went with a 'Leffe Blonde' and Kate had the 'Duvel' Belgian, tasty as always.

- Cured Meat & Cheese plate: We chose the mix & match (5) of charcuterie and cheese off of the blackboard. We liked the items we chose, was tasty. We could of used one more toast point & maybe another tablespoon of that delicious jam.
- Chicken Wings: Were ordered the 'Thai hot' style. The wings were breaded (not naked). They were very tasty but had no heat whatsoever (did they forget the spice?)
- Spicy Tuna Tartare Tacos: We did not like these, the tuna did not taste fresh. (I am picky about sashimi, ceviche, tartare, etc.)
- Pizza: goat cheese, sausage, roasted spinach: it was okay, the sausage needed a hint of some seasoning & maybe one more item on the pizza such as marscapone, plumb tomato or olive oil drizzle, etc.  to 'bring it all together'. I felt the dough could be a little more crispier. 
- Asparagus fries: we liked these, had a nice crunch, tasty. The hickory- smoked mayo was interesting.

So, you made it this far in my long, drawn-out review? You deserve a beer for that. Go have one at the the Keg & Kitchen, we like this place. Until next time......

I have been to many Indian restaurants and this is by far my favorite!! My favorite dish to get is the chicken tikka masala. I also love the garlic naan and their mango lasses. I would definitely recommend this place to everyone :)

I'm in town for work this week (yes, during Covid-19) and finally got to try this place. I called later on a Saturday evening to order a pizza and was told they were out of pizzas for the evening! The owner sounded like she felt so bad about it and I told her I would try them the next night.

Well, I called in an order the next evening. When I went to pick it up, the owners informed me they had to make a substitution, which was fine. The owners were so nice and warm, and gave me a free (and really tasty) treat to make up for the trouble (which it really wasn't). 

Got back to the hotel and opened up the box to find a really nice looking Insalata pie...it was delicious. Crust was spot on, gluteny but crisp at the edges. Generous sheets of parmigiano reggiano and prosciutto. Very good pizza. I also got the chocolate mousse, which was absolutely rich and decadent.

I would highly recommend this place, and wish I could have eaten there in person instead of just having to pick up. The owners seem like wonderful people. Carpinteria is lucky to have such a place.
Nice little shop.  Good atmosphere/music.  Clean.  Good breakfast sandwiches.  Good service.  Sadly, didn't try the donuts, but they look delicious.  Def would recommend.

It's started fine with the cheese skillet and went off the rails after that. Five tacos and they were all bland and or so sloppy they fell apart. Nothing had an ounce of flavor. The tostada was so hard you could kill a man with a shard of it. The jus for the taco was tasteless. Pretty bad when beans and the appetizer are the star of the show. 50 bucks later  ........well.....we won't be back.

We read high reviews of the Gumbo Shop here, but I was not super impressed. The atmosphere was nice, but nothing special. The waiters seemed very rushed. The tables were too close together. The food was ok. I had jambalaya, and it was tasty, but I've had better elsewhere in the city.

I have been to both Cafe Beignet locations. One, off Royal, has your typical cafe feel with both indoor and outdoor seating. The other is off Bourbon street. This location is almost tucked away in a lovely outdoor area where statues of great musicians greet you upon entering. There is also a stage where live music is frequently played.

If it is the weekend, be prepared to wait. It could be a different culture here, but I feel that the cashiers/baristas could have more than one person taking orders when it is crowded (every time I was there, I only saw one person taking orders). Still, it is worth the wait to grab some beignets. 

I've been here about once a day for the last week. In that week, the beignets have ranged in terms of size, doneness, and texture. While I understand they have many customers, I think they should be more consistent in preparing their most popular item.  One time my beignets were slightly raw in the center. Still, I come back because I enjoy sitting outside and enjoying the weather. 

Food prices are reasonable, but I find beverage prices pretty high. $2.29 for a small bottle of water is a bit absurd. Food wise, I have had both the crawfish omelet and cajun potatoes. The grits leave something to be desired; they taste as if the box they come in has the quaker guy. The omelet itself was tasty and the potatoes had some great flavor. 

Overall, I think it is just sheer volume that causes these small issues and inconsistencies. If there was more consistency and perhaps a bottle of water was less expensive, I would give a higher rating.

Quick View:
Service: 7 out of 10 
Food: 6 out of 10 (ranges from 4 to 9)
Value (food): 6 out of 10
Value (drinks): 5 out of 10

We loved the down town location so yesterday we finally got to go to this one and we were not impressed.  We had a wonderful waitress but for the price, I think most people can do it better at home.  I ordered a Caesar salad with the dressing on the side and it arrived at the table with a half cup or more of cheese, way too many croutons and just a little, really bad looking romaine (no green).  I did not even take a bite it looked so bad.  They did remove it from our bill.  I also had the toasted ravioli that was not really toasted, it was fried.  The sauce that came with the ravioli was very good.

My husband had a medium-rare New York strip that we expected to have a good seared crust but it did not and was actually rare, which he enjoyed.  Mushrooms were overly salted but had a good flavor. The wine was very nice, perfectly chilled.

If we go back we will probably stick with the sliders.

My first dining experience in Indy and it didn't disappoint. Sat at the bar and had a great draft from the decent selection. Had the harvest salad and a side of brussel sprouts. Delicious. So flavorful and filling. Will definitely frequent on future visits to this city!

Well at least its food...about authenuc as Taco Bell...
Service was good but no flavor
Find something authenutic

I always go into beachside cafe to order food for years. Tonight was a shit show and the owner should know. The waiters were playing around like there wasn't a customer in sight. My glass of wine was served to me with other people's wine on the tray table that were a lot healthier than mine. Two good looking girls walked in way after my friend and I who had not been asked what we wanted but when those good looking girls walked in way after us they were served right away. I had to go up to the workers and remind them that we wanted to place an order to go. I was not told ahead of time that my 6 pack of beer to go was going to be $40 + dollars. The service was absolutely horrible tonight and I left with very bad energy not wanting to be a patron of this restaurant ever again. That makes me very sad.
First time ever eating here and I love it! I got the Mexican corn bowl with shrimp yummmm
Great place! Great food!! Awesome beer selection!!  Can't beat the prices and the wait staff is super friendly!!

I'm in Philadelphia for work and really wanted a steak. Oh boy did we make a great choice. We started with foi gras and beef carpaccio. The foi gras was so good it was like butter.  As for the beef carpaccio, well it's hard to go wrong with beef carpaccio.  I ordered the wagyu filet. It was amazing!  They bring out several knives and you get to select which you will use. I selected the knife made by Porsche. It was a great knife. The steak was so good I didn't want eating it to end. The flavor was amazing and it was a perfectly cooked medium rare steak. 

I couldn't eat the bread since I can't eat gluten but I will tell you, it smelled, looked, and sounded amazing. Just the way it sounded when they tore it i could tell it was great bread. They confirmed it. 

As for the service, Brian was our server and he was wonderful!  We couldn't have asked for a better server or a better experience.

I think this place is kinda a tourist trap. There was a long line to get in but the food was just meh. I tried the char broiled oysters there since I had such a good first experience at Drago's the day before but it wasn't up to par. We kept eating dirt or sand in each bite.  The po boys weren't all that either. Just fried shrimp and fried oysters in a roll with some lettuce and tomato. Nothing special. What we did like about the place was the waiter. I wish I remembered his name. He seemed like an old timer there. But he was very nice.

Great place for smoked baby back ribs.  We decided to try a full rack for takeout and were not disappointed.  They were not over smoked, dry rub that created a nice crust to the fall off the bone tender ribs.  Sauce on the side which was just right.  

We will definitely order them again.

I am not ashamed! I come by the drive through JUST for a vanilla ice cream cone. I am convinced though that they have changed their formula because it is now more of a frozen yogurt consistent and color. Where as before it was more creamy and white vanilla. Maybe it's just me... but i need answers.

I found this place on yelp! My friends and I went and certainly enjoyed the ambiance and food. I ordered a ribeye and finished the whole steak! It was cooked the way I wanted it. You guys have to definitely try this place out.

You looking for a good restaurant in New Orleans?  Keep on going.  Do not waste your time here - there are too many other venues with great BBQ shrimp, oysters, and ambiance to visit Pascals (think Mr. B's).  The service is HORRIBLE and the food is average at best.  The owners desire to rest on their laurels rather than provide excellent service and an innovative menu is the icing on the cake.  FYI, their specials never change..any given night you will be "lucky" enough to get drum with BBQ shrimp.  Seriously, save your money for the cab and go to Irene's in the quarter - they will show you great food, service and ambiance.
Great friendly and fast service. Nice inside and the food was SO good. Will definitely recommend them and come again when back in NOLA!
Fun, friendly, good time bar. Marie is best bartender in the FQ area (By far). Don't drink too many Hurricanes and get naked in fountain, they really frown on that! Terry, Terry, Terry!

My husband and I have given this location a chance several times. They regularly forget items in our orders and mess up dishes. This time, we ordered identical meals, but as you can see they were completely different - one bowl looks like it never made it past the first station (no salsa, cheese, lettuce, sour cream, etc). Cherry on top was the chunk of steak we found - we are both vegetarians, so it was gross to find red meat in the bowl and made us nervous to eat our meals. They also forgot our order of chips and guac. Thankfully used the app to receive a refund for the missing chips and a free meal for the botched order, but this will be the last time we order from this store.

books & brews are popping up everywhere! 

Things different about this location compared to others (not a ton, but): 
- I like this layout the most compared to the 96th St. location
- great location within the City Center shops 
- this place has french fries (!!!) and a quesadilla option

Things to love: 
- easy location to stop by during a shopping experience
- laid back atmosphere
- books upon books if that's your thing
- food is pretty darn good (especially the naan)
- they had a few guest taps for those not into b&b brews
- daily special (i.e. kids eat free on a certain day)
- random special events (pay attention to their FB page)
- the beer cheese dip was great (but replacing the pretzels with bread bites would be the ultimate experience)

Things to improve: 
- my Tomato Sawyer grilled cheese was very underwhelming - no flavor and hardly any cheese! 
- lowering the prices of guest taps ($7.50 for a local cidery was a bit much for me and not relative to other prices around Indy)
- wish that the bartenders would come out to you and take your order if it's not busy
- more stuff to encourage people to read the books. Every time I've been in a b&b, people aren't there for the books...they're there for beer and food (totally fine, but doesn't work well with the books part of b&b)

Food was good. Kinda pricey considering what you get. They have gotten my order wrong a couple times. The silverware was spotted and not very appealing at all.. Service was good. The pies are good and free on mondays!

Came here for my birthday dinner! They were very gracious on taking a reservation for 19 people! 

We kinda had a private room in the back, very well lit and funky decor, loved it!

I had the cucumber signature drink, very refreshing and delicious, decided to try the pumpkin soup (to die for) I actually wished I didn't order a cup and got a bowl, it was that good

I got the biscuits with prosciutto and fried egg...so good, but biscuit was a BIT dry

my friends ordered me a delicious fried chocolate balls dessert, so good and melty

will definitely come back!

The newly expanded Indian Garden is absolutely incredible. They have a spinach dish called saag which
Is to die for ! We also enjoyed the chili chicken. Our service was impeccable and the staff was very accommodating. I highly recommend the Indian Garden!

Heard about this place online, looked very promising so I gave it a shot. Showed up right when the doors open for dinner, promptly seated and served. Atmosphere is very good, professional looking, bathrooms could have better lighting and a bit cleaner would be nice. The bartender, Kate, was friendly and informative. Also it is nice to see the owner, Joyce, sight on scene. Food was good, sweetheart + filet mignon rolls, with mochi for dessert. The 50% off sushi is really the best deal you can get anywhere, regular price is a bit much for the area. The only thing I would majorly change is the meat in the rolls, there needs to be a larger quantity, it seemed as if I almost ordered veggie sushi. Overall a great place, good deals, and friendly faces, will be back.

I've not made it a secret that I love deep dish pizza, and specifically, Giordano's. I'm still extremely bitter that Dayton has one and Cincinnati still doesn't, but I guess that doesn't matter much for the Indianapolis review. Their pizza is consistently cheesy and delicious. However, this Indy location needs a bit of work.

I felt kind of bad because my friend isn't a big fan of deep dish but I REALLY wanted Giordano's. I rationalized that she picked dinner the night before and it was my turn. She agreed, but looking back she may have chosen a better lunch option.

We came in to a well air conditioned restaurant, which is absolutely crucial in this heat. I. AM. DYING. Anyway, we took a seat and were aptly greeted by our server. She wasn't exactly unfriendly, but a bit difficult to find. I have a feeling she wasn't a kid person because the two tables next to us had children and I watched the interactions she had with them. It was awkward.

Giordano's has an excellent lunch menu. For under $10, you can receive a personal pizza, pasta, or sandwich with a side and drink. I ordered the sausage deep dish with fries and my friend had the thin crust cheese with fries.

The food took a surprising amount of time to come out. They say to allow 45 minutes for the deep dish to cook. I thought that meant full size pizzas, not the mini ones. I never asked if my pizza was the reason for our extended wait time, but I assumed it was a good bet because my friend's thin crust was ice cold and our fries were limp and bland. Her food could not be enjoyed without a hearty addition of ranch. Luckily my pizza was hot and filling because I left a good portion of my fries on the table.

The saving grace for Giordano's is the ability to buy frozen pizzas and take them home in their insulated bags. I took a sausage and a spinach pizza home to Cincinnati safely and enjoyed them in the comfort of my house. 

I've never hesitated visiting a Giordano's, but I'd probably think twice about coming to this location. It's smack dab in the middle of multiple A+ lunch offerings, so if you really want the deep dish, maybe eat elsewhere and get some of their frozen pizza to go.

The best thing since sliced bread in the Nations. I love mustard- as in mostly no sandwich goes without mustard. Their Italian was incredibly tasty and needed no mustard. Save half for next day as it was that big. Also should note they don't put thin slices of cheese. They give a healthy portion. Love this place. Also tried the rueben breakfast sandwich  and the prolly cheese steak. If you have not tired this place yet. Do yourself a favor. It's that good!

We stopped here while passing though because of the high ratings. Although the place is on the pricey side ($10 mimosas) the quality is top tier. The omelettes were light and fluffy - perfectly cooked. The bread was thick, well toasted, and gently shmeared with a bit of butter that assume was artisan and locally sourced from a nearby farm. 

The coffee is bottomless and they even provide take away cups. 

Although it was busy, we were seated immediately.  The line formed soon after 10 am. 

It has a cool sophisticated atmosphere without being pretentious or snobby at all. 

I'm pleased I tried it out and would recommend it to anyone.
Great brunch here. Be sure to try the short rib hash. It's literally one of the best things I have had. The coffee is also great and the restaurant has a nice home-spun vibe.

Carley's Cake's is awesome!! I took my son after finding this place on Yelp to get some treats after getting 100% on his spelling test. We arrived right as they were locking up for close, but they still stayed open to let him pick his treats! The girl working was so nice and patient while my 7 year old gazed in amazement at the awesome unique candy selection! We got a bag of tons of awesome goodies all for less then $10! We will definitely be back! This week! 10 Stars for Cayley's Cakes!

I ate at the Refinery about 6 months ago and was frankly underwhelmed. I had a cold soup (I want to say it was squash based), an entree I can't remember (bad sign), chick pea fritters, and some sort of delicious peanut butter pie which is the only thing my friend and I  ate that did not leave us underwhelmed. The next day at work my friends who adore the Refinery asked how we liked it and my response was eeehh. I loved the roof top patio (the weather was good) and our server was great but the soup was bland and the entree was entirely unmemorable. My friend was equally unimpressed and has already given it 3 or 4 tries. After reading various yelp reviews tonight I decided to add my 2 cents. There are actually other people like me who have not drunk the Refinery koolade! All I hAve to add is Beard shmeared. Maybe I will give it one more chance, but it better be good.                            ----------                                                                                                                I posted the above review on 7/26 and today 9/7
I am amending it. I originally gave it 2 stars but today I had a 5 star experience. My wife and I shared delicious muscles to start, a roasted squash entree, and a tasty swordfish filet. And the brownie! The food was phenomenal and just like last time, the service was great. Instead of having wine I had the Tampa-brewed Jose Marti beer and my wife had a refreshing pear cider. We thoroughly enjoyed our meal. So, what's the lesson? The menu rotates so if you have a less than stellar experience, check out the weekly menu on-line and think about giving it another chance.  I am glad I did and opted to change my rating to sort of break even between my two dining experiences. We'll go back.

I had a fantastic meal at Henrietta Red and will be recommending a dinner here to anyone who mentions an upcoming trip to Nashville, it was that good. Their focus is seafood, with an expansive oyster bar, but the hands-down favorite dish of the night was actually a vegetable dish. Go figure. Just goes to show that they really know what they're doing in the kitchen. The amazing food made the meal one of the major highlights of my vacation with my mother.  

We started with the Red Snapper Crudo and Razor Clam Escabeche from the raw bar, and both were super-fresh. I especially liked the quinoa and citrus used in the former. At the server's suggestion, we also had the Green Curry oysters, which were unique but understated. Eventually we added on the more traditional Wood Fired oyster dish with dill and mustard, which I preferred.

On the dinner menu, we shared the Roasted Acorn Squash, Squid, and Scallops. That acorn squash dish was amazing, with creamy feta, crunch from the almonds, and a great harmony of flavors with the lemon, chili, and a hint of mint. It sounds like it would all cover up the squash, but it didn't. This was THE dish of the night. As for the scallops and squid, my mom was especially impressed by the great sear on the scallops but we both were underwhelmed by the squid, which is usually my go-to dish. 

We shared the Pumpernickel Panna Cotta for dessert, and it was a more generous portion than anticipated. The cherries were my favorite part, and there could have been a few more. 

As much praise as I would like to laud on this place, I have to make a few comments about the service. We had reservations, were seated quickly, and enjoyed the decor and ambiance. But our server only paid attention to us after literally all of her other tables had left. We went half an hour without seeing her or getting drink refills, and she finally came over when I was craning my neck to follow her around the dining room- coming up with a short, terse, "Yes?" when I wanted to add on to our order. I don't know if she was just overwhelmed by the workload or simply didn't think our tip would be worthwhile given our two-person party and lack of alcohol. This would have easily been a five-star review (and I don't give those out often because that indicates the best of the best) but for the service- the food very clearly deserved it, though. I would certainly come back, regardless.

Came here with a group of coworkers on a Friday for lunch. We work down the street and wanted to check it out. This was a while back so the menu could be different now. I tried the gumbo and it was pretty good but I was sort of weirded out by the fact that it had greens in it. It was also served with potato salad, which I thought was a cute, cultural nod to Louisianians who eat gumbo with potato salad. I got the catfish as my meal and it was pretty good. I wasn't wowed but it was a good lunch. My coworkers were all satisfied with their meals as well. The place was empty so we had it all to ourselves. I like the setup and the decor. I will have to go back for dinner and drinks and update this review.

Just got back from lunch at Jimmy Johns.  The sandwich pictures on the web site looked nothing like my sandwich.  I ordered a #2, no mayo.  I got 2 pieces of beef, 4 slices of tomato and not enough lettuce to cover anything. When I opened my sandwich I could see 1/3 of the bottom bun.  Really?  Publix makes a MUCH BETTER  sub for less and you get what you want on it and it is huge!  We had to ask for napkins, they don't have any out if you dine in.  Fooled me once, never again.
Food and service was great. I had the pork chop which was off the hook. Place is small but it was enough. I do highly recommend for a higher quality meal in Treasure Island. Ry the carpaccio.
Wifi is good at about 3 Mbps.  Coffee bar is nifty.  Service is friendly.  Served almost immediately.  Food is excellent.

I had my birthday dinner here this past weekend. 

This is such a scenic and beautiful restaurant! Gorgeous views of Butterfly Beach so sitting on the patio is a must. They have heating lamps so it was really comfortable even past sunset. 

Excellent customer service. Really attentive and fun wait staff! 

The food! On birthdays we eat pasta so I had the Crab Gnochetti - a gorgeous bowl of dense pasta with huge lumps of crab and sweet corn. My date had the Lobster Radiatore - huge pieces of lobster with perfect al dente pieces of radiatore. So delicious! To start we had the Kobe Beef Meatballs which were excellent. I had two Oprah Martini's to drink and for dessert we had the Some More Please! - their version of s'mores. Again, excellent! 

Very fun, romantic, whimsical place - perfect for a birthday dinner!
Texan here. In case you were wondering...this place knows how to bbq. Get the 2 meat plate with brisket and pulled pork. Excellent.

After 2 years Parc still seems to be going strong as evidenced by the 2pm visit on a Sunday when it was packed. Unfortunately, they were only serving the brunch menu, so some of my favorites from the lunch/dinner menu could not be enjoyed, but we liked everything we got.

The mushroom tart had a delicious flaky, buttery crust, topped with black trumpet and other wild mushrooms.

The warm shrimp salad featured perfectly cooked shrimp in court bouillon. 

The quiche Loraine had a gorgeous custard like texture and rivaled Thomas Keller's quiche Loraine I had at Bouchon.

We will be back to get our fix of the poullet with pomme puree (the closet thing to Joel Roubochon's on the East coast).

Got a loaf of their awesome walnut cranberry bread, which at almost $10 is still worth every penny.

Service was friendly and efficient for being packed. Crowd started to go down around 3:30pm.

Wow! I tried this place about an hour ago and I could walk back for another Big Rube right now. 

Food: I came for a biscuit sandwich and a biscuit sandwich is what I got! Big Rube is filled with chicken fried to perfection (they consider making this a stand alone), goat cheese, and pepper jam. I am not a huge fan of goat cheese yet somehow all of these flavors make a wonderful medley. The biscuits are big, flakey, and buttery. Pepper jam? Sweet with a tinge of spicy. The fries are also unique in their cut but are thick, crispy, and salty! The menu also has a number of non-biscuit items and ice cream for dessert. 

Atmosphere: I wouldnt care if this place was in a bathroom somewhere, I'd still risk it for the biscuit. That being said, there is limited parking and about 1.5 places for people to sit. Either walk there and munch or drive and go somewhere else. I would recommend calling ahead if youre trying to snag a quick breakfast. I believe they make everything to order.  

Great food! Great price!

Great place with great food! We will definitely be back in the spring! Shrimp, shark, fish tacos
were all  awesome!! service was also top notch!
Very good!! My first carry out experience was a great one! The pizza was A M A Z I N G. Very fresh and a really good size. I was super impressed! It is definitely a top pizza joint.

Waited until they were open for a couple weeks to experience the real feel of this new restaurant.  To say we were disappointed would be an understatement.  A very limited menu and both choices were a big disappointment. The Black & Blue Burger was tasteless, the beef had no flavor and the little bit of blue cheese also had no flavor.  The french fries were good and they came to the table hot.  The chicken wings were okay.  Our server did a good job under the circumstance...we had the feeling the kitchen was over whelmed, and the dining room was only 3/4 full.  We waited a long time before our waitress came to our table and then we waited way too long for our food.  Not  her fault I am sure.  I saw who I thought was  the manager or owner hobnobbing with some customers, I  think his  time would be better spent taking care of the kitchen problems.  We will not be returning there, the quarter pounders at McDonald's would definitely have more flavor than experienced at the Stackhouse.
The quality of food is totally just okay.  Prices could be a bit better too. But I'm really glad there's another "fast casual" place on Mass Ave. It's perfect drunk food.

I have died and gone to August heaven! Oh my gosh... Saying the food is amazing is an understatement. I had their signature trout dish with shrimp and wild mushrooms. I savored every single bite! My waitress Karen was so incredibly friendly and helpful. Her recommendations were the best. I loved the glass of wine she recommended and the trout dish was her suggestion. The restaurant is very nice but since I was alone, I ate in the bar area, which was very comfortable and welcoming. I wish I could afford to eat here every day that I'm in New Orleans. I'll save up and come back though! Definitely worth every penny!!! My favorite seafood dish, hands down is at August! Walk-ins are allowed in the bar. You get some treats along with your check from the pastry kitchen. I just adore August!!

The food here is good. However most times the food comes out salty or just plain nasty. They don't really offer to fix it or take it off your tab. Not looking for a free meal. But if I pay money it better be worth it. I come here all the time. Just be prepared to wait for a long time to have your water refilled. That why I ask for two glass when I got here. Some what good food just bad service!

So I've only frequented the downtown campo until today. I was skeptical on meeting my friend, as I had a few people give me some poor feedback for this location. Having said that, I was extremely surprised. (In a great way) Our waitress Reece was fantastic, our food and happy hour drinks were awesome and the atmosphere wAs perfect! I will definitely be coming back again and often.

The first time I ate here the pizza was great. I have since been back several times and the pizza just isn't good. The problem I think is that they prepare the pizza in advance with the sauce and cheese. Then when a pizza is ordered they add more toppings and reheat it. The pizza tastes like reheated leftover pizza. The crust is rubbery and chewy. And several times we have received pizza with burnt toppings, that had to be thrown away. The garlic knots are amazing the lasagna is good.  And the salads are prepared very fresh. Everything but the pizza is good.  Which is a shame since that is their signature item.

Overall the service was okay:( the food and golf were absolutely amazing but the bartender(tall with glasses) laughed when we didn't get the food we ordered  won't be at the bar anymore but will defenitly come back to golf!!!!

Ok, I admit it: I like Olive Garden. I'm normally an "eat local" girl, but I'm down with OG! 

First, their salad and breadsticks. They just just GOOD.

I really like their 4 cheese ziti al forno. Cheesy deliciousness. Always enough to bring home a to go box after eating salad and breadsticks.

Their drinks are pretty good too. I've had several, both alcoholic and non, and they always are good.

Service is always good at this location. We just want and our waiter got stuck helping a table of around 20 people, and he sent someone else to take care of us - no lapse in service. He apologized to us but it was impressive that he managed to get us taken care of despite being tied up.

Oh, and who doesn't love those mints they bring when you pay? Seriously.

So we headed to Sam's at old hickory lake because I wanted my friend to try a Bushwhacker during our trip and I felt that Sam's did them right. Plus we were escaping the crazy crowds on Broadway over the holiday weekend (and I mean CRAZY). We sat at the bar and had very good (and friendly) service from the bartenders. We actually ordered 3 Bushwhackers as my friend really enjoyed his and wanted to try the one with the peanut butter whisky. We also ordered the spinach dip which was also very good (and filling). The Laker game was on during our little stint at the bar which made us feel right at home. Nice relaxing bar at the dock on the lake.

I really need to frequent New Port Richey a little more.  I haven't really been up that way since I was a child in the 90s, so I still had the impression that it was still kinda podunk, but I was glad to see that I was wrong.

During my drive up there, I was starving for a new spot to eat and saw Grille 54.  It was around noon on a Saturday and it wasn't much of a crowd so I was happy about that. When we walked in, I already knew that I was planning to get a big ol' sammich. The menu is exciting to look at and it made me hungry for a little of everything; sushi, soup, burgers...all of that. 

Tes was our server and she was just a pleasure.  She told us about the special and made it sound so good that I could almost taste it and she just had an overall great vibe. I would definitely recommend trying to get seated at her table.

I was hungry and inconsiderate of carbs, calories or any of that lame stuff. I ordered the Homer J which was a blackened turkey sandwich with onions, mushrooms, aioli and provolone. So.Damn.Good. 

I'll be back up that way to see what's up with the sushi!
Good food and atmosphere inside.  We got ours to go.  Was not very covid compliant, no masks or table spacing.  Will return after covid.

This location always seems to have groovy music playing out loud. I can't help but sway to the sweet tunes as I wait to order my lunch. My go to is always the Southwest Cobb salad. I love that chipotle ranch dressing! Their soups are always nice on a cold fall afternoon. This location gets really busy around lunch time but the environment is always cozy. The mango sweet tea= highly recommend!
Greasy, slippery floors. Sticky tables. Food so salty it is inedible. Ripping off 20-somethings who don't get the difference between trendy and good.

We were on our day trip in Tucson, and I was starving.  Got the French fries and they were pretty good.  My partner got a pina colada eggee.  Not really a fan of that flavor, but we are glad they are opening one in Gilbert soon!

I love Velvet Cactus! Their salsa is unique and smokey which I definitely now crave! This time I tried the chef's taco which was coffee rubbed smoked turkey, baby kale, pumpkin aioli, and apple cranberry slaw. It was incredible and that's what I love about New Orleans everyone plays with flavor combos to make one of a kind eats! Even they're margaritas are unique I really like the cucumber jalapeño margarita! I also got the chipotle chicken taco, the habanero pineapple relish is awesome.
Only the best kept secret in the west side of Tampa Bay...! Excellent line of primo Italian goods....! Great foods to eat-in or take-out and a wonderful wait/serving staff..!

Grubhouse is the place to go for a hearty breakfast if you are near the Liberty Bell.  Everyone in my group enjoyed our meals.  The baconcakes were moist, loaded with crispy bacon and topped with a delicious bourbon-infused syrup.  The biscuits were freshly made and came with a creamy sausage gravy.  The eggs and pork roll were perfectly prepared.  The atmosphere in the reimagined Bourse is awesome.  And Yolanda and the crew's positive attitude is a perfect way to start the day.

I love the Reuben sandwich.  The burgers are great as well.  Great place to go later in the evening have an appetizer and adult beverage.  The staff is always pleasant and efficient.  Big Smiles everywhere!!!  We try to stop there at least 2 times a month.
Very nice restaurant. Food was amazing. Turtle soup was to die for, eitouffe was one of the best in the area. Strongly recommend this restaurant!!!

The service is terrible here -- 4 people working as a cashier but no one is taking orders, just talking to each other. The manager was nearby but didnt seem concerned and also was participating in the talking. I'm not really sure how this McDonalds stays open in the area, especially without a renovation and some new staff.  Lots of better 'fast food' nearby with workers who will actually take your order.

First time trying this place and was really looking forward to the pizza since I had heard great things.  Called in for a pizza for take out on a Sunday night.  Apparently everyone wanted take out last night.  Medium half cheese, half Hawaiian with a side of ranch.  Not too hard.  

It took over 45 minutes for our pizza to be ready.  After 45 minutes you expect your pizza to taste like liquid gold.  Now, I've never had liquid gold, but I was expecting some delicious pizza.  The Hawaiian side was mediocre at best.  I never go for cheese pizza, but at least it had taste to it.  I wasn't impressed, but I was starving.  They also forgot my ranch, but I forgot about it after the long wait and being so hungry in there with all the smells.  Total came to $13.33.

Had it on Thursday. Not only the flavor is not authentic w/ the  awkward chashu,but I also got sick after having the ramen w/ a soft inside boiled egg. The egg, was obviously refrigerated and was cold when I had it. That makes the fatty soup really just too heavy. Checking the other reviews I'm not surprised to find out that I'm not the only got sick. 1 star for it.

Yummmmy! I am not a frequenter of many restaurants, but we will definitely be back to this new northeast Tucson Treasure often! Commoner and Co. has outstanding servers, warm ambience and
most notably, the  offerings were beautifully presented and prepared to perfection. The fried Green Tomatoes were scrumptious,  the cocktails were original, and my date devoured his extra thick burger with pork belly. Can you say chocolate mousse? Lots of little delights await you. I highly recommend this new restaurant,  you won't be disappointed!
Not sure why the negative reviews.  It's not a 5 star dining experience but my meal was enjoyable.  The waitress was pleasant and friendly. If in the mood for seafood again I'd go back.

For an "on-the-go" deli, Julia's is ridiculous. While their sandwiches are perfectly fine, their customer service is so bizarre. No only are their hours all over the place, they have rejected orders because they're "too close to closing". If you won't make things after a certain time, why not just close earlier? Beyond this, Julia's parking policy is ridiculously strict for a small town. The fact that on a snowy day, they're still willing to boot cars parked in their lot for barely any time at all is unbelievable.

Ambler would be better off if a more courteous business were to take the place of this sad excuse for a deli.

I wanted to like this better. It's cute. The menu is great with lots of variety. My breakfast was good. But the service was too absent. My drink was wrong. My coffee didn't get refilled until the end of the meal so what was the point by then. It's worth a second try. Hopefully the older dark haired lady that seems like she owns the place won't be there. She's terrible...rude....inconsiderate to the diners....spacey and just down right bizarre. We were all shocked with her. Maybe next time I will like it better?

For now this is my favorite place to get Vietnamese/Pho besides my mothers. The food here is really good. The dinning area is fairly large and you can bring large group of people to enjoy dinner with. Servers are really nice and most are students and english speaking. They have a large menu with all sorts of dishes.

I enjoy this Pho Quyen out of all the other ones. It's a bit of a drive for me but it doesn't stop me from getting good food.

Was in town from Texas to meet friends.  Have been wanting to try out the New Connors Steak and Seafood.  We were greeted very promptly upon entering by Valerie.  After being escorted to our table, our Awesome experience began.  Grace was our server and could not have been more helpful on both our dinner and drink selections.  From our Appetizers to the wine to our main Entree.  We were never disappointed.  The service and Food were beyond Awesome.  What a great dining experience with friends and family.  Thank you Grace and Val for making our experience a memorable one.  Can't wait for our next visit to Connors.
Great food, I had the quesadillas which were well seasoned. But I wish that they had a bit more meat in them seemed like a lot of it was mainly cheese. But overall really good.

Good food. Had the habachi salmon and it was very good. According to my husband fried rice was not the best but still good. Steak habachi was good. Even though the price was a little high, the serving was large.

Probably my favorite place to eat in Nashville. Always start with a drink at the bar. They have a great selection of spirits. The food is southern upscale and fresh but is still comfort food. Most of the ingredients appear to be sourced locally. The beef tartar and seafood Johnny cakes are my favorite starters. You can't go wrong with anything on the menu. The service is upscale and friendly. Five stars.

I came here for brunch this weekend and it was a fairly nice brunch. I ordered a few drinks and they were all fairly good, nothing amazing. For the entree I had the seafood crepe which was divine. It was filled with shrimp and crab and had this amazing creamy sauce on top. My friend got the steak eggs benedict which they though was pretty good as well. The service was really great. Overall a fine time, I'll probably be back.

I should start by pointing out that I don't drink and I don't eat meat, so feel free to call my review into question based on those factors alone. A teetotaler vegetarian might not be the best person to weigh in on a restaurant known for its beer and burgers.  That being said, I enjoy Iron Hill. The items available to me on the menu are limited, but good. I especially like the Mediterranean Wrap, their pizzas, and the legendary sweet potato fries. The atmosphere is also nice as is the design of the building. The staff is always friendly and the patio is nice in the spring/summer. I only wish they would change their menu more often.

Used to be a favorite spot.
Now they are off our list.
While we were eating we heard the manager calling another employee over to an area he was cleaning saying "you want to see something really gross?"

The whole menu has been blown out.
A couple sandwiches, salads and appetizers.  No oysters at all.
It seemed like they were not even prepared to be open, even though it was almost 6pm on a sunday.
Host and waitress talked only about how they were transitioning to a new menu. 
No one behind the bar.
One server, a manager, 2 guys in the kitchen0 and a host. That was the whole staff.

We had lobster rolls.
It was not fresh lobster.
Tasted like they went to a local market and bought pre cooked lobster meat.

Sad to see how far this place has fallen in such a short time.

I was in last week and I asked the gentleman behind the counter not to put ham And he did it anyway I thought I was going to vomit after I took a bite of my salad in the employees there I need to spend less time on their phones and laptops and pay more attention to the customers

This is a place parents everywhere will love. Escape the conventional Nashville tourist spots and settle into this hole in the wall nestled away on a dock behind shrimp boats and an impressive cascading water feature. The catfish will make you believe in love again, and the hushpuppies might just have the answer to life's hardest questions. This place makes Nashville feel like a small town where everyone is family, and yes, they do serve Blue Moon.

After craving sushi for, literally months, we decided to stop in the the Sushi Bar - Broad Ripple.  This intimate, unsuspecting sushi bar provided for an excellent session of sampling fresh cuts of fish and sipping sake.  Here's what went down:

The ambiance: one word that comes to mind is 'homey,' it feels as though we are being welcomed into someone's Broad Ripple Avenue house to enjoy their Japanese delicacies.  Maybe that's what it really is?

The food: was spectacular for where we are globally located.  I frequently avoid seafood restaurants that are this far in from the coast, I have to say that the cuts here of Tuna, Yellow Tail, and Sweet Shrimp are delightfully fresh.  Very good rice base, as well.  I went with the Sushi Bar Special One - four rolls and five standard servings of tuna, yellow tail, shrimp, salmon; a great portion that is accompanied with Miso soup and a salad (next time I will get a side of Japanese noodles, they are excellent).

The drinks: the sake was pretty good - not the best I've ever had, but it was the house, which was exceptionally priced ($7).  The beer menu also peaked my interest - can you say $2 imports?  Oh yeah, next time I'll be enjoying one with my sushi.

The service: I felt very well taken care of here, the wait staff is very attentive to your needs are are frequently stopping by to make sure everything is satisfying.  I appreciate the attention to detail.

This is one of the best places I've gotten sushi in Indy.  Excellent food, authentic feel, reasonable prices; let's just say, it's worth it's salt.  See you next time the cravings hit, Sushi Bar.

I have been to Campbell's a few times now only for ice cream and frozen treats. I usually always get the same thing and like to keep it simple; vanilla ice cream with rainbow sprinkles. 

I decided to try the Dole Whip recently to change things up. What flavor comes to mind when you think of Dole Whip if you've even had one before? Well, I started in on the Whip while driving away and I said to myself "this tastes like Flintstones vitamins!" I looked down at the Whip in puzzlement as I was trying to determine what exactly I was holding in my hands. My eyes began to play tricks and I couldn't decipher if the color I was looking at was orange or yellow. I took another stab at the Whip. Hmm....what is this? Then the pistons fired in my mind. Flintstones vitamins...vitamins...vitamin C....Florida...Florida oranges...orange. The Whip was orange flavored. I was thinking it was going to be the flavor of pineapple as I've never had a Whip in any other flavor but alas, it was not. It wasn't disappointing but honestly, it just tasted like orange sherbet so it wasn't anything special. 

I won't be getting it again unless it's pineapple but otherwise, if you catch this place at the right time, the food it reasonable, and the staff is normally friendly. In the evenings they tend to be really busy as everyone wants an after-dinner dessert. Plus, you know how those "other folks" always seem to have their ice cream machines down historically at the peak time that people want dessert, so do yourself a favor and don't waste your time going to the "other folks". Just go to Campbell's.

The kids and I walked up from Chaifetz on a rainy Saturday between gymnastics sessions.  I checked in on yelp while we were walking and I'm really glad I did because we were seated immediately.  But we must have beaten everyone else there because just after we were seated the crowd hit.  Due to the influx of diners, our table got a little bit lost in the shuffle and some of the later arrivals were greeted and had their orders taken before us.  However, our server apologized for the delay and he was super friendly and helpful.

My kids chose Mac and cheese (which I typically discourage because it's often kraft and my kid never likes it and it is money wasted...but I digress) and say cheese, which is basically a cheese pizza on focaccia.  I chose the pesto chicken with a side of St. Louis city salad.  

This was one meal that we all really enjoyed and I heard zero complaints!  The Mac and cheese was not from a box and kiddo #1 devoured it with the intermittent "this is really good."  Kiddo #2 did not eat all of the say cheese but also said it was good.  The biggest excitement for them was the potato sticks, which they both loved and commented on.  I guess I've never introduced them to the canisters of potato sticks found at the grocery store.

My St. Louis city salad was super good (I might even try it as my sandwich next time).  The chicken pesto was open face on focaccia.  While I t was good, I doubt I'll order it again (but Kiddo #1 might as she finished off the rest of my pesto chicken while declaring her love for pesto).

What we really came here for was dessert.  By checking in on yelp, I received a free world's smallest ice cream cone (I chose coconut almond joy).  I also ordered a world's smallest hot fudge sundae.  Kid #1 chose a stutz sundae with vanilla ice cream and chocolate syrup.
