Kid #2 wanted dipping dots (?!) back at Chaifetz but I still let her get a world's smallest cone with chocolate ice cream.  Yummo!  Loved their ice cream and I really loved the small desserts.  Just the right amount to get a taste but not feel over indulgent.  

We will definitely be back and next time I want to try a house made soda.

The food was very delicious and the lady who I assume to be the manager as well as Ernesto stopped by to make sure that we were having a good meal which I appreciated. They seemed very friendly and wanted to ensure that we were having a good time! The waiter seemed to be a little unfriendly at times as though our requested bothered him and at other times he was very friendly so it was confusing. He added an extra charge on our bill but when we told him about it he was quick to remove the mischarge. I ordered a skirt steak and it was very delicious! Also I noticed that whenever my glass of was even half empty someone would always come and refill it which I really appreciated. The staff seemed to be very attentive!

Just picked up a croissant sandwich from Provence and I MURDERED the damn thing as soon as I took a bite! OMG! Delicious!  I love the coffee menu and the selection of desserts and breads! HEY! I'm gonna pay this place a visit more often.  Neat little gem in the Hillboro area!

I dig El Vez.  Their guacamole is kick-ass and the blood orange margarita is as yummy as the previous reviews indicate.  Also, an old school photo booth that actually works?!  Yippee!  Lounge-y background music and glittery decorations make for a fun atmosphere.

It's been a while since I've had dinner there, but hanging at the bar for drinks the other night made me want to plan another night out as soon as possible.
Had the meatloaf and macaroni and cheese, both items were very sweet. I was pissed, I paid $12 for it. I am a diabetic, beware, probably won't be eating here again.

Only go to this restaurant if you have all night to eat dinner-server was nice and felt horrible that it took over an hour to get our food. The owner apparently did not care and never apologized or came  over. Two of our party had to leave before the  dinner came. We were so upset that we could not enjoy the food when it came-which by the way was good. Will not come back.

My favorite place for oysters! They have great specials during the week. We love to go on Monday's when they have half-off bottles of wine and $1 Gulf oysters. Not a fan of Gulf oysters, so I skip those and go straight to their "boutique" oysters. It's a rotating menu, but selections are always ridiculously icy fresh. Service can be a bit slow, but if you ask for Kat you should be in good hands!

Wow!! What a great place in Tierra Verde!! It reminds me of those great bars in Boston. They have 2 huge bars, both with seating tables to eat, plus outside dining, with a nice water view. Now let me get to the food!!! Outstanding!! I had the short rib tacos that were to die for, tender and so flavorful served with fresh rice and black beans. Mom had the shaved Rib eye sandwich that was beyond words! Tender and so tasty, I took a bite of hers and wanted to eat that too! Best rib eye sandwich ever!! Our server Ashley was so friendly, helpful, she made our dining experience extremely pleasant. They have tons of specials, happy hour. You must go, love it and will be back for sure. Love it!!

So far, this has been our favorite place to try at The AMP. I thought the original (Southern Fried Chicken) was OK, but would probably be better with a dipping sauce. Now, I would recommend the wings with the lemon zest for those of you that like acidic flavors. They were very tasty!

Beer NV (pronounced like "envy") is a great spot to try a lot of different beers.

ATMOSPHERE: This place rests inside a strip mall complex with multiple stores and has a hipster-ish feel to it (good in small doses). FYI, this place does not serve any food but does have menus for the nearby Mexican place, which will deliver to the bar.

SERVICE: The bartenders working that night were very friendly and attentive. No complaints.

BEER: It was really hard to choose. There were 60 beers on tap, and all were displayed on their digital menu which stretched the length of the bar. I ended up trying a lager, a hefeweizen, and a cider. All of which were local (to the west coast) brews and tasted very good.

VALUE: This place offers a good value for what you spend. Prices are reasonable, and if you don't want to be stuck with full-sized pints, you can get pours as small as 4oz. This not only limits your expenditure but also allows you to try multiple beers in one sitting.

Overall, Beer NV is a nice place to sample many different beers without breaking the bank.

My husband and I went to dinner this past Sunday.  It must have been national steak day as they had over an hour wait on a Sunday evening.  Once we were seated we were greeted by Mary.  Very pleasant and thorough server.  She took our order and we received our salad and cup of chili very promptly.  then our entree arrived.  My husbands food was cooked perfectly and everything looked great.  When I looked down at my plate I was SHOCKED.  The entire plate, every square inch was FILTHY.  Beyond my food being placed in the middle (medium steak and baked potato) the rim, every inch where food was not and the bottom was completely filthy.  There was food or something hanging off the BOTTOM of the plate.  Our food was dropped off by someone who was NOT our server, which I know is common, everyone helps everyone when your slammed.  She placed the food on our table and said "here" and walked away.  When our server Mary returned to check on us I alerted her to my plate being a mess.  She picked it up and immediately knew it was DISGUSTING.  I explained that being in the restaurant business myself, my boss would NEVER allow food to leave the window on a plate like mine.  She offered to have my food recooked, and I didn't want that, I just wanted a new CLEAN plate.  She brought me out one, apologized and I took care of transferring my food.  I just want to see the BOH taking more notice of the plate before they place food on it.  The cook, the expo, and the server delivering the food are ALL responsible for making sure that plate of food looks perfect before it leaves the kitchen.  Mary is a FANTASTIC server who was gracious despite a very full, hectic, restaurant.  YOU can do better BOH Texas Roadhouse, I'm certain of it.

Things like this is what makes Yelp great.  When I went to Philly I had a feeling that the famous Pat's and Geno's were tourist traps that no real Philadelphian goes to really, and I was right.  

This cheesesteak is minimal with just high quality beef and light cheese on a long baguette style roll.  It was very good.  The atmosphere was cool except for the fact that the condiment area was disgustingly dirty and not covered with sneeze guard.  These guys are definitely selling out by opening up a lot more restaurants in ballparks, casinos etc. so we will see how long they stay good.

I ended up at this place for a work event, and I was shocked I could get enough vegan options on the salad bar that it was a nice experience. 

The people with me that ate meat seemed to like it and felt like it was a little better than average.

The service was nice and the beer selection was ok

This is the first and only Chipolte I've ever been to that was clean, and has smiling, friendly, fast & efficient employees!  Amazing service, excellent preparation of my order of two bowls.  Ingredients all fresh, very tasty.
I swear; I was in and out of here in less than five minutes.  Service and food, excellent.

THANK YOU to all the staff here.

It should be less than a one star but it was as low as I could go.  Once this was a great place to eat with consistent service and food quality. My last three experiences have terrible and the  last was our final time to eat here. 1. Food quality has diminished to the  point we would rather eat fast food. 2. Price has steadily increased and the  quality has as above mentioned decreased.  3. Service has gone from tolerable to amateur hour. Servers bring food out in questionable order and on out last visit didn't serve my entree at all and wasn't apologetic at all. I believe it is a direct reflection of the management as when presented with what happened the attitude became apparent. It must be contagious because it happened on another occasion with a different manager.  We do indirectly know the owner and will let them know our experiences. I would avoid and pick another restaurant as there many that do it right.
There aren't very many options in Rita Ranch for Mexican food. This restaurant has good food and service :)  I would recommend the pork carnitas or shrimp cocktail.

Simply the best Chinese in Clearwater!! Hands down! Get the coconut balls, roast duck and the salt & pepper shrimp with asparagus. Super friendly service here and a very clean establishment. Will come back again!

My friends in St. Pete took us here for brunch one weekend while we were visiting and we loved it so much that we now go back every time we're in town! 

They can get crowded but make up for it with a parking attendant, and they're well worth the wait. Great atmosphere with an industrial feel and a nice covered outdoor space. They sometimes have a DJ playing music which was awesome! Amazing mimosas and brunch items, would highly recommend the Southern Benny and Lemon Ricotta pancakes. Service is always friendly, and I love the added touch of getting a bottle cap magnet with the restaurant logo when checking out. Great restaurant!!

Had a great dinner tonight; the food and service was amazing! However, it went south when the music started. It was so loud!  My husband asked the manager if they could turn it down. We waited about 10 minutes, nothing changed so went ahead and paid our tab and left. Would like to try again but disappointed that the dining experience was ruined by the loud music.

The slowest service I've ever received at a chick fil a every single time I come to this location. The one in Avon is far busier & I wait for 1/3 of the time as I do at this location. Just a bunch of children playing around at the drive thru window instead of doing their job.

Just your regular Pat's Pizza (a chain here in Delaware and nearby areas). The area is right on Kirkwood Hwy, which is rather convenient. Bonus: On Wednesdays at around 4pm, a group of gentlemen come by with their hot rods to eat. It's like a mini car show!

I love the sandwiches and salads here, I highly recommend getting a Greek salad. For just 99 cents, they will add a large portion of grilled chicken. 

The cheese steaks were just ok, but not great. Too little cheese and meat, too much hard bread. I'd skip it and go for a sandwich instead. People come here mostly for the pizza, but I find the sauce to fairly sweet. I don't like it at all. Pasta is okay, but kind of bland.

The employees are okay, and the floors and tables are kinda sticky. They have 2 TVs which usually play CNN or a movie.

I was expecting it to be better, all the hype about this place and it was just ok, first if you can request a booth you will have less flies to deal with even though we were inside we really were not cause the garage door is all the way up right next to the outside seating area, White pizza was the best as the angry pizza was overwhelming with green chili peppers so we took some off nothing special with tomato pie little piece they give you for appetizer $4 bucks, so 1 beer 1 drink 2 pizzas 1 soft ice cream with tip $110.00, Manco & Manco pizza way better, and has to better pizza in phila then here!

This is a place owned by the same people who own NIckle City restaurant. Nickle city is known for their beef on weck (it's a roast beef sandwich people-that's all) and their infestation of cockroaches. The owner has known about it for years, has treated in on occassion but with no great effort. I have personally seen the "chef" flick a dirty german cockroach off a pizza and tell the server "servce it anyway" So yes, when you complain about the owner of this place turning off your music cause he doesn't like it, believe me it's the least of your worries and the least of his concerns! Avoid it like the plague people, it's a dive

My husband and I stopped in for dinner last night. It took about 13 minutes for our waiter to even acknowledge us. As soon as he came we ordered our food because we had sat for so long looking at the menu. It then took what seemed like a long time to get the food. I ordered the sliders and they were just ok...a little dry and the bun was hard. Husband had the chicken with mushroom risotto and he said it was good. They do have good beer though. We will try again but weren't impressed this time.

I really wanted to like this place. I have heard so many good things about it. Maybe I came on an off day? I first stumbled upon here when my colleague and I had to evacuate Scotia Place due to a fire drill. We decided to take the train back to our office since we were not wearing any jackets. When we entered Central Station, we soon discovered Burrow. I ordered an americano to go. It tasted fine but I felt it was a little steep in price. I noticed their food menu and decided that I would have to come back here sometime and order lunch. Yesterday I did just that and ordered the chicken stew with garlic toast. I  felt that the portion of the stew I received was small for the $9 I paid. I was still hungry after the fact. Second, it was quite salty and overtook any of the other flavours that were in the stew. I could barely taste the sage that was in it and I like sage when seasoned properly. The garlic toast was good - not too buttery and just the right amount of garlic. But again, the portion was small.
I will say this that guys who were working were pleasant. I think it's a great concept and convenient for LRT passengers but it has room to improve. I do not believe that I will not go out of my way to stop here for a coffee or lunch again.

Did not provide all of the food for my order, made us drive back 15 minutes to get it, wouldn't offer any kind of refund. Food was still not ready when I got back even though we called ahead to make them aware of the issue. 

When I asked for a refund for the food we had to drive a 30 minute round trip to get, they said if I drive home and bring back all of the food then they would give me a full refund otherwise it wasn't their problem. Terrible customer service all around.
I thought this was traditional Korean bbq and it wasn't. If you want to pay for every little dish and side dishes that you would get for free in Seoul come here.

Yum!! My hubby and I finally made our way here and are happy that we did. We both got the Village burger w/out the Russian dressing. I opted for gueyere cheese and caramelized onions at medium rare and it was perfect (I wanted more on my burger but it was already at $17!). I forget what the hubby got on his but he loved it as well. 

We split an order of duck fat fries with the cheese on the side and those were exceptionally good as well. Neither the burger or fries were overly greasy- a welcome surprise!

We also ordered the blueberry pie shake and it was just okay. It was a far cry from a milkshake, but if aggressively slurping pie filling laced with vodka and Tuaco up a tiny straw is your bag- go for it!

Service was great. Seating was limited. We sat at the end of the bar, facing a wall, but we were fine since we didn't have to wait. It was pricey, but we got a lot, so I'd say it was worth it in the end. Next time I'll skip the shake.

I live in Benton Park and want nothing more than to support our local establishments, but after trying Benton Park Cafe three times (at the old location and the new) I have almost never had worse food.  I've tried both breakfast and lunch and it's all grotesque.  Not only is everything mushy, but the pancakes taste like a combo of salt and cornmeal, the bacon is the size of a string bean, and the potatoes are loaded with sour cream.  Even worse than the food though is the service.  We ordered milk for my 2 year old and it came after the food.  I walked in with a newborn and a toddler and they seated at the only table in the aisle situated in the middle of the entire restaurant (versus a quiet out of the way spot).  And when we realized we left our toddlers hat behind and called to ask them to put it in lost and found we were placed on hold for 8 minutes, hung up on, and when I called back they condescendingly said they didn't have time to look for it.  I will never go back here ever again and will tell every one I know to stay far away.

This was our first visit to Chicago's pizza for a fundraiser for my son's school.  Overall five stars for a wonderful relaxing experience.  
     We ordered The Big Hurt deep dish. The pizza sauce is wonderful.  The pepperoni is a little extra spicy which combines for a great tasting pizza.
Balloon artist was also a nice touch.

The food here is amazing, the ambiance of the restaurant is beautiful, and the servers are so very kind. We came here for breakfast in the morning before a long business day, and it was so good to be treated to very modernized Southern food. We ordered some toasts, breads, and egg dishes, and it was fantastic. When we were on our way to the conference, I couldn't pass up the beautiful pastries, and picked up some intriguely shaped muffins and of course a chocolate chip cookie. Come here for some delicious and beautiful food - you can't go wrong!

Was there last night.  Nice ambiance & wait staff was terrific. Loved the biscuits they give you to start.  My main dish was just ok panko fried shrimp very heavily breaded & too well cooked.  My husband liked bus rainbow trout very much.  The flatbread appetizer was a big hit.  Dessert was nothing to get excited about had the 3 ice cream combo very ordinary.  The portions were very generous for sure.  All in all very pleasant & very conveniently located to our hotel. Really would only give it 3 stars not 4

I am suprised that yelp has given Modo Mio $$$, because if anything, this place is very affordable for the size, creativity and elegance this restaurant offers. $33 for a tasting menu is incredibly affordable, and you get to try dishes that are different and delicious. 5 stars for sure.

I've never been so disappointed in a place I used to love.  Service was terrible, our server was snippy with us(I think her name was Olivia) and they had changed the menu leaving off some of my faves. No more of that delicious cavatapi side dish, no more Mahi Wolfe which was the best fish I've ever had.  We ordered the new sangria that was highlighted in the menu and were told that the mix wasn't in yet.  No plates brought out with our bread.  Meatball app was cold.  It took forever to get anything at the table. Food was ok but such an overall disappointing experience.  Carrabba's need to quit messing with a really good menu. And great service can greatly enhance a meal which we clearly did not have.  I think I'll be done with Carrabba's.

Another successful Lulu's trip (ate in this time). Took my mom as she was excited to see what it was about! Awesome service as usual even when we had odd requests. The workers were attentive and kept the place clean! I got the chipotle black bean burrito with tater tots on the side and my mom got the chipotle black bean burger with tots. We loved it, zero complaints, so delicious. My mom isn't vegan and was blown away!!

One of the BEST meals I've had from any restaurant and definitely some of the best Italian food. The place is very nice inside but not over the top so you do not need to get all gussied up if you don't want to. The staff is incredibly friendly and polite. Our server, Liz, had such a great sense of humor and created for us a dining experience that went beyond delicious food. 

That said... The food is Amazing! My dad had the mussels which came in a great red sauce with chunks of garlic. The chicken abruzzi entree is just the perfect blend of all of my favorite flavors. You really can't go wrong with any of the entrees. 

Dessert.. Oh my. You have to come here for the seasonal caramel bourbon ginger gelato!!!!! It's the best gelato I've ever had and has ribbons of ginger snap cookie crumbs in it. 

Tip: come for the early bird dinner from 4 to 5:30 Any day and most likely you'll get seated right away and can also enjoy early bird pricing :) 

We made a special trip to come here and will certainly be doing so again.

Something for everyone.  The staff were amazing by not only providing great service but also making excellent recommendations.  TVs were a bonus to watch the game.   We will be back when we visit Philly again.  The kids enjoyed the pizza and the avocado grapefruit salad was delicious.

This is my go to late night delivery restaurant. The food is always good and fresh. I always get the pizza and wings.  The pizza is good and their wings are tender and flavorful. Delivery is quick and the delivery person's are always nice. Would definitely recommend this place.
The karaoke is great, and the bartenders are awesome! Cherri was our waitress and she provided excellent, fast, and friendly service!

If you are looking for a dive with great, fresh seafood, this is your jam. It's nothing fancy, not even close but that's the allure of the Crab Shack. They have all you can eat crab on Tuesdays and Thursday's. They also have every other type of seafood you can imagine, good prices on Stone Crab while they are in season as well. They have a full bar and also serve Jai Alai so they are upping their craft beer game :)  You will have to wait on a weekend or during all you can eat nights but the price and no-frills are worth it.

First time ordering from here, I got sweet and sour soup, egg rolls, crab puffs & general tso chicken with fried rice. Delivery was very quick and the customer service was excellent! Although the food wasn't the best I've had, it was good!

meh. It wasn't awful, but it isn't somewhere we'll go again. My boss sent me over for lunch, it was a (25m) drive which is no biggie. Got there and everyone seemed like they hated that they were there. Yes it's healthy, yes it's convenient, but overall I just don't feel like the price is justified. It was yummy but not holy wow def. worth it yummy. Coolest part was prob all the different drink choices.

We stopped here for lunch and had breakfast.  The bananas foster was to die for. We also had the Ruby Sunrise and their special Bloody Mary. Put this on your must-do list. Ask for Jay Acus. He provided outstanding service and was very helpful and responsive.
Could possibly be the best food in the Philadelphia area. Chef is amazing!!! Literally every single item on the menu is off the charts raw to meat to fish.

When you walk into Martin's,  the smell is heavenly. Tried the pulled pork cornbread taco - the cornbread was shaped like a tortilla and complimented the dish well. My friend had the baby back ribs, so tender and juicy. The potato salad was also really tasty,  not too heavy either. Very happy with the experience!

Very convenient that it is next to AMC Voorhees, fairly priced for Vietnamese in this area. Ordered the goi cuon (summer roll), very good and the sauce it. Ordered the bun dac biet, it came with a generous amount of meat and the egg roll it comes with was good too. Will definitely come back again to try the pho and other dishes.

Great atmosphere and service!  Really good pub grub & beer.   This is our third visit and so far, I've tried the avocado chicken wrap, the combo tacos and the avocado fries. The tofu tacos have been my favorite, but all were great!

If you live in the area, or stop into the area on the weekends, I highly recommend stopping into SSPB for a quick breakfast-- something along the lines of an egg and cheese on one of the many incredible bagels. It's quick, it's yummy, and it's local.

They also have Israeli newspapers, if you want to practice your Hebrew while you indulge.

One of the best breakfast spots in Boise! The service every time we have gone in was fantastic. The food was really good and fairly priced. Our favorites are the coconut scones and the raspberry scones!
Excellent, authentic food.  but be forewarned . . . this is just a stand.  Orders are "to go" only!

Coffee was ok, but You cannot get a French crueler at any time, but early AM, that's what I want the most. Pulling teeth to get a straight answer when is next baking??? Finally she said never again any day/// only once a day!!  Then she slammed window in my face! This place is so poorly managed, don't waste your time!!
We used to love this place, but it has gone downhill fast. The pizza is often cold, the staff is inept, and we have been overcharged several times.

This is the only restaurant that my wife and I go to in Gloucester County!
Definitely stop in and try it.  Do not be afraid of spicy food.  Not everything is spicy.
The food is great along with the service.  If you're up in the Riverside area, check out their other location on Scott St.

Super chill cafe. Perfect for those lazy weekend days. My boyfriend digged the burger - on the recommendation of fellow Yelpers. Fries were just OK. I had the Ahi Tuna salad which wasn't mind blowing, but was tasty. Also the Salmon chowder (which tasted just like clam chowder - minus the clams) was very good, only was missing any sign of salmon in there. My friend had the Sword Fish Tacos - which sounded really good on paper, but she gobbled it right up and was hungry for more. I guess her complaint was that it was a smallish sized portion.

The BEST part about this place are the outside patio heaters! The heat doesn't come from those odd spaceship heating towers - but from BELOW! It literally came up from the ground and the warmth was so lovely! 

They also have a full bar which is great. My friend said her Long Island was strong - so that's good. 

Inside seating - simple and cozy. Bar seating is no frills. It's a bar. All in all, this place is a nice little dive - nothing adorable or worthy of going out of your way for. But if you are in the area and you want relatively cheap and tasty and want someplace family friendly - but that serves alcohol... It works!

Yelp doesn't have you write a title for your review, but if they did, I have a good one:  Lost in Translation.   To begin with, I can't for the life of me remember whether the name of this restaurant is Shu Feng or Feng Shu or Fu Sheng or Sheng Fu (you need to know: I often write my reviews offline, then copy them in).  Besides that, what's funny about this restaurant is that each of my three visits has been made more interesting by a lack of English communication.  For my latest visit, I sat down and ordered the same thing I had the time before, the House Special Chicken lunch special.  After a couple of minutes, the woman I have deduced is the owner walked up to the table and I swear, said "Do Dee Do Dee Do Dee Doo Doo Dee Do."  I thought I was in a dream.  I just looked at her and said, "What?"  So then the waiter walked up, she said something to him in, uh, Chinese I guess, and he turned to me and said "How spicy do you want your chicken?"  How was I supposed to get that out of Do Dee Doo Dee Doo?  My wife always laughs at my inability to understand people with accents, but after this, I might just tattoo American Dumbass on my forehead.

Later, when I was about done with my lunch, another woman, who is kind of an assistant/bus girl, walked up with a pitcher of ice water.  I had about half a glass of soda, but no other glass on the table.  She asked if I wanted water.   I said "I had soda" and she looked confused and troubled.  I guess she was going to top it off with water.  So I just said "No water, thank you."  Satisfied, she left.

So how was the food, you might ask?  Strangely, it seems stylewise like kind of standard Americanized Chinese, like you'd get at China King or some other suburban strip mall place.  I'd rate it as good or better than any of them, but considering the lack of English spoken here, I'm kind of surprised it's not more, well, foreign.  The prices are fair, the place is clean and the food os very good, so I'll be back for sure.  Maybe next time I'll venture off of the lunch specials and try something more unique, like the Do Dee Do Dee Do.
AMAZING POKE! I got the half and half which was tuna and salmon and this might be the best poke I've ever had. My dad got a bucket of fries which were also really good. HIGHLY recommend

It might be good as a bar, but for lunch, it was sub-par. Granted, I had the special, which was orange chicken with rice and eggrolls (not exactly traditional pub fare), but I wasn't expecting something that looked and tasted like a freezer-burned package of pre-made Chinese food from your grocer's freezer. It was nasty. The chicken with pineapple was just covered in sauce that didn't help the taste of the chicken; the rice was dry; and, the egg rolls were overcooked and tasted only of oil. My co-worker had a burger and onion straws, which she thought were okay. My other co-worker had toasted ravioli and mini-tacos that both looked like they came straight from the freezer into a deep fryer. She loves toasted ravioli and barely ate any of these. She ate most of the tacos, but they weren't worth it in her opinion. Hopefully this place is better as a bar. As for lunch, there are far better downtown options. Heck, you'd be better off with TGI Fridays. That said, the order taker at the counter and the guys behind the bar were super nice and helpful. If this was just a review of service, they would get a 4.

As an aside, as other reviewers have stated, you order your food at a window, take a number, and they bring your food to your seat. To get your drinks, you have to go to the bar and order separately. Very weird setup. Tables were clean. Interior was dark - typical dive bar atmosphere.

Would I give it another try? Probably not. There are just better options out there. Bailey's is right across the street and has very good burgers and shakes, albeit quite a bit more expensive.

I love this juice place and I am so glad that it is located in Brentwood, where there are no other fresh juice places. I've visited a bunch of times since I discovered it about two months ago. The juice or smoothies are really excellent and creative. Most juice places sell the standards, you know carrot/ginger/apple juice some sort of kale pulp/ apples etc. The Juice Bar has the standards and lots of creative options that are really excellent. 

I will admit that the first time I visited, I got the Bunny Love aka carrot/apple/ginger/lemon. I'm sorry but if you can't get that juice right, then I don't want to come back. It's my litmus test of juice bars. The Bunny Love was really great. The Achilles heel of the carrot/apple/ginger juice is the ginger. There is either just enough or too much or too little. This juice was perfectly balanced and I happily sucked it down. My finance ordered the Mint to Be and now this is what I order. The Mint to Be is delicious. I love getting it after a really great hike at Radnor. There is honestly nothing more refreshing. The last time we visited my fiancé got the Blue Chocolatta and he really enjoyed it. 

They have started doing a punch card system, you enter your phone number when you order and after 9 drinks you will get a medium smoothie. This would probably happen in like a week if they were to start opening at 7:00 instead of 7:30, which is my only qualm. I have to be at work by 7:30 and if they were open at 7:00 I would stop here like everyday...which maybe is a good thing if your name is Morgan's Wallet. 

P.S. This juice bar is a little bit more expensive than Whole Food's Juice Bar. However, it's also a local business and honestly I would rather pay a little bit more to support them.

I needed a quick and cheap bite before I headed to a meeting. Dos Hombres was just what the doctor ordered. I got three chipotle chicken tacos. It was delicious! I loved the "build your own" concept of this restaurant. It let me customize my toppings after I picked a method and protein. All in all, a good eat.
Great pizza, the shrimp is the best. Try the whipped  ricotta appetizer. Pretty cool environment friendly staff.

The rock shrimp tempura is apparently one of their signature dish, BUT it is rather large (good for 3-4 people) and while flavorful, your taste buds get a little tired of dish after several bites. It's an 'a lot of the same flavor' type of appetizer. Worth trying but recommended for a bigger party (3+ people). 

Go for one of the carpaccios....the kobe beef will leave you happy =) 

Entrees are very well portioned...surprisingly so given the type of cuisine. 

The duck duck duck was delicious, and it may be one of the few times you'll get to eat lotus flower root. 

The seafood 'toban yaki' was amazing!! Plenty of prawns, clams, crab, & scallops, served in a delicious citrus butter. The meal comes on a traditional clay bowl, accompanied with a side of sticky pork rice. 

Delicious cocktails. The morimoto martini is a winner. 

Tried the mary jane brownies for dessert...nothing special. Brownie was kinda dry. The only thing interesting were the candied hemp seeds, but overall it was not a very good dessert. 

Aside from dessert, every dollar spent on appetizer, entrees, and cocktails is worth it!

***DON'T BE FOOLED IF THE PLACE IS EMPTY*** IT IS A GREAT PLACE TO EAT *** YOU WON'T BE SORRY***

My family and I visited this establishment about three weeks ago. We were immediately greeted by a friendly and warm face. 

The owner is able to do it all. He is the waiter, the cook, the busser and he does it all quickly and efficiently. He took all 8 of our orders without even writing anything down and nothing was wrong.

He is able to gauge what kind of person you are in a second and tell exactly what you aren't going to like and what you will like. So listen to him when he gives you advice on what to try. After all, he is the pro.

The Food:

The food was excellent. Freshly prepared and tasted amazing. I was not very happy that my family decided to try Mediterranean food, as I have never had it before. However, I was very impressed with it.

The Atmosphere:

This is a very quiet establishment in the heart of Euclid. It is a very "happening" place. You can go in and expect great, fast service while being able to think peacefully to yourself.

The Owner:

Excellent person. Very nice and genuine. We have gone in three more times in the past week and he was able to remember exactly who we were, our names and what we had had prior.
This is probably my favorite place to eat! The breakfast is amazing but you also can not go wrong with a delicious burger! I highly recommend Daily Eats, you wont be disappointed
Zivaz has the freshest  and most creative take on traditional Mexican food at the best value anywhere in town. They offer specials on the weekend and their margaritas rock!

Forgot my salad dressing. What a bummer. Can't eat my salad. 

Nothing is more annoying... can't they have someone check the order before it goes out!!!!!!

I was really looking forward to good food and drink, but the service was so bad it took away from the whole experience. Lots of unique menu items, Veggie Grilled Cheese and Crab Mac and Cheese are both outstanding. But... The hostess estimated a 45 minute wait for a table, we sat at the bar, and 3 tables opened up within 3 minutes. The bartenders didn't have a beer list and didn't know anything about their draughts beyond the name and ABV. Read all about it on my blog Kbc Eats http://bit.ly/1ULqT8I I tweet @kbceats

Sandwiches were amazing.  The "Batali" was great!  "The Goose" sandwich was very good also.  Gelato,  some of the best around.  As said in another review, the service will blow you away.  Everyone is helpful and seems to enjoy being at work and it really shows.  Also an amazing selection of specialty food items and meats.  Just go!

All positives for this place. It's a family run (byob) establishment and they're extremely nice and provide great service. 

They have a great Tues./Thursday special ($2 tacos). Portions are large so you won't leave hungry! I've had most of their taco menu and I honestly can't pick a favorite. Each one is unique and bursting with flavor. And of course, we all know a taco is nothing if the tortilla stinks. Theirs are fantastic.

Also, stop always ordering takeout and sit there and eat for a minute. It has such a positive energy in there (sometimes their little kids will be running around) you'll be happy you did. Support local and not just the new brunch spot that charges you $15 for some avocado on a piece of toast that you could make yourself for 2.00 flat. You'll order guac here and get two-three avocados worth of guac with your order. Eat half then take the other half home and save it to put on your toast in the morning : p
Oysters are to die for! Try the desserts as well. You can't go wrong with any of them.

Family style burger restaurant.  The burgers are always delicious and the fries are bottomless so that's a plus ..  the onion rings are amazingly crunchier and the Smokehouse sauce that accompanied them is amazing . The best thing though are the desserts, they are huge . The cheese cake is massive and oh so yummy .   however the service is rather dismal!  No matter if the place is packed our dead the servers seem to forget everything you tell them .. if the food wasn't so good I wouldn't bother going here but I genuinely love the food !
One of the best Italian restaurants in the city.  Everything there is excellent.  Make a reservation as you may not get a seat.
This is my first dining experience at Azul and the food was very decent for a resort restaurant. The menu were all decently priced.
I got the pint Gumbo and this is super delicious! Has a great authentic taste with lots of seafood. A lot of food too for so cheap...

Thank you taffys pizza 
Our family had an amazing time.
Sofia,lili,tommy,sugel;
 my family was  super thankful  for everything. 
Taffys pizza is worth more than 5 stars. They are the best!!

Whiskey Kitchen is a MUST for any lover of both Whiskey and great Contemporary Cuisine in Nashville, Tennessee. This restaurant is the authority when it comes to sampling whiskey and having great food with a contemporary twist. You can enjoy a flight, a straight whiskey, or a delicious cocktail. The location (in the Gulch) is not far from downtown and the decor is chic. The kitchen provides wood fired pizza, pub foods and southern cuisine with a delicious contemporary twist.

I ordered The Southerner with Hot Chicken. Upgraded the side to the Mac and Cheese. The hot chicken is great and the biscuit is one of the best I have eaten.

We enjoyed the open-air atmosphere, and the overall ambiance was great.

I absolutely love this place... their dishes are traditional Mexican fresh seafood but the way they are styled and prepared is completely out of the box and innovative. The only drawback is that the servers are not continuously coming back to the customers...we're having to wait to ask for another beer or ask for a napkin etc. I've also observed a few different times some of the servers not wearing their face mask properly and playing with your long beautiful hair putting it up in a bun behind the counter.! I just feel that I could give you five stars but I won't for that reason because you need to work on that... it's a simple fix .. I will consider the five stars if I see this issue resolved the next time I visit.

Located smack dab on South Street, Lorenzo's is a hotspot for some pizza after a night of drinking. Even without drinking, you can't pass up their huge slice of cheese pizza for just $3.50.

The pizza is pretty good for what it is. It's your standard cheese pizza that is relatively thin. Top it off with some parmesan and hot sauce, and you got yourself a great deal for a solid slice of pizza.

Ate at La Hacienda restaurant for the first time tonight. The chicken enchiladas with red sauce, rice and beans were excellent! My friend had the steak and mashed potatoes which were very good as well. Lots of chips and great salsas. All the staff were really friendly. We will definitely go back!

Let me start by saying these guys have BY FAR the best sandwiches in Reno. And when they're actually open during posted hours the service is amazing.

REASON FOR 1 STAR REVIEW:
Posted hours online and on the storefront state they are open till 9pm M-Sat. HOWEVER this business is CONSISTENTLY closed between 7:30 and 8pm. By consistently I mean 4 or more nights a week. The biggest reason this is such a frustration is when you're craving Capriotti's NOTHING else will suffice. And when you're there AN HOUR BEFORE CLOSE and they aren't open it ruins your night. If it weren't for how good the sandwiches are this practice would have more than likely caused this business to close years ago.

Summary: Great sandwich, good service, but never count on them being open because you will more often than not be extremely frustrated by a locked door.

I am new to the area and went to Fly Bar for the first time yesterday.  Staff was super nice and checked on us a lot without being overbearing.  Great cocktail menu - I had the Greyhounder.  A little minty for me, but that's just personal preference.  I'm normally not a Mac and Cheese person but WOW!  Best Mac and Cheese I've ever had.  The brussel sprouts were also pretty incredible.  I'm looking forward to going back and having dinner instead of just drinks and appetizers!

Completely disappointed!  The food is subpar and the mimosa is like drinking gasoline because they serve cheap champagne and OJ.   The management decided today to charge a guest in our party that clearly did not eat breakfast./brunch...  that is a new all time LOW.    They should have charged them for their beverages and that is it.   For someone who has been in the industry for over 30 years... this is not the way of keeping your clientele!   And, is clearly why your business had declined by over 30% this past year.  Completely disappointed and expected alot more from your management.  We are locals and frequent your establishment on Saturdays and Sundays... but, don't worry, no longer.  Competition has a lot more to offer and with alot better food quality and customer service.  Too bad management doesn't know that you don't need to charge for seats..poor, poor decision.
Amazing food, super friendly, great experience wait staff was polite and professional well worth the money.

The wife and I had breakfast today at @11am when one of the workers in kitchen walked past us with very bad BO. He was kicking like Bruce Lee to the point I was getting sick and left half my meal in which I as enjoying up to that point.    I did tell the tall male cashier about the worker kicking like Bruce Lee.

We had a horrible experience for our first time here. We were sat down in a corner booth and it took about 10min for the waiter to even come greet us and we saw him casually walking around the section. We set a timer and said if he didn't come within two more ministers we were just leaving and we had about thirty seconds left when he walked up and took a drink order. After that we saw him walking around doing other things instead of the drink order so we just got up and walked out. 
The prices are high so I expect great service. 
Will not be back!

FULL MOON YOGA!  Hubby and I just enjoyed our third Full Moon yoga date night at the Belmont and it was amazing. The price of admission includes a day pass to the pool and fitness areas, a small group outdoor evening yoga class and wine after class.  What's not to love?  Yesterday we kicked our day up a notch by adding a couples massage in the beautiful spa. The experience was seamless, the spa staff really knows their business and Ty and Pat (our therapists) were very skilled and professional. All in all this was a very romantic, intimate, relaxed day for this long married couple.

One thing this location has going for it is that there aren't many other options. But that doesn't really excuse the subpar service you get here. Even more problematic, it's hit or miss. Sometimes the food and service is great, other times it's slow, unfriendly, and you get served cold food. On my last trip I practically had my drinks thrown into my car by an unfriendly teenager. And it wasn't even busy at the time, which does happen very frequently here despite the questionable service.

My boyfriend and I went here for my birthday weekend dinner and it fell a little flat for me.  The atmosphere is nice- sort of loud, and we were sat promptly.  The service was great- very attentive and many hands on deck with above average speed from the moment we sat down.  They brought us a bread with sauce all over it which was just a bit spicy and mushy.  Next we got calamari- this I enjoyed- the sauce wasn't as spicy and it was just the calamari rings.  We both ordered gnocchi which came with soup or salad.  The pasta fagioli was decent.  For some reason a big loaf of garlic bread was brought out, it was delicious, so nothing to complain about there.  We were basically full before our main dishes came out.  The big issue for me was my main entree.  The gnocchi was just really mushy.  My boyfriend commented how he liked it since he doesn't like when they are too firm.  I guess I'm more traditional.   The sauce and seafood in the dish were tasty.  I didn't want to complain, as the only fix would have been to have the dish remade, and at that point I wasn't even hungry anymore.  Overall the place was decent, prices were pretty good, and it's a Byob.  You do get 15% off with a check in but they ask for your email also.  I would give them another shot, and maybe just request my pasta not be cooked quite so much next time.
The salmon udon is very good, fish is still juicy and fresh even in the hot soup. The tempora shrimp is the best ever, another item can't be missed!! Service is very good. Highly recommended!
There cheesesteaks are really good and there wings. I love coming here when I have a cheesesteak craving.

Tried going there for lunch to see how new sushi restaurant was. Got there, not crowded. Tons of video screens in every direction, heavy metal music playing for ambience. Ordered some rolls and nigiri. 40 minutes later, our waters had been topped up several times but still no sign of any food whatsoever. Since our brains were pounding from the constant stimulus and we were starving, we walked out in disgust.
Rione is the real deal! Delicious and authentic  Roman pizza. Can't wait to head back to try more flavors!

OK, I get it now.  This place really isn't one of the good branches of the Ruby Tuesday chain.  

So tonight, we came here because we had a gift card.  Like I said previously, I generally do well with Ruby Tuesdays.  The one I go to in Malvern near work has generally treated me well.  I usually appreciate the salad bar.  Some items on the menu can be pretty good, especially the appetizers and burgers.  Like a lot of chains, if you go into the entree world, it's hit or miss.  

Before I go anywhere, let me state that none of this review is indicative of the level of service by our waiter, Brian.  He was very good.  I made it a point to name him because I know that everything else isn't his fault.  

Now, on to the grievances.  

So, my first mistake was coming in here expecting to get something I wanted as a paying customer.  Case in point... order the Chicken Trio, and ask them to substitute the rice pilaf for another side such as mashed cauliflower.  You see, this particular item on the menu is stated that it is served with rice pilaf on the menu.  If you get the salad bar with it, you do not get another choice of side.  Apparently the three pieces of chicken must be served on a bed of rice pilaf.  This is a rule.  Don't question it.  It has been deemed so by the corporate suits who own the Ruby Tuesday empire!

You see, in my naive head, being the paying customer, it seems to me that you can just serve the chicken on the plate without the rice, and put some cauliflower on the side or in a separate dish.  Well, my server was nice enough to ask the kitchen if they would do it at least.  But he seemed mildly unsure if they would accommodate the request.  

I never managed a restaurant in my life.  But I have to imagine some requests, if simple, should be honored.  It's not like I was asking them for a more expensive side.  It's not like I was asking them to change the flavoring radically.  It's not like I'm Meg Ryan ordering dinner in When Harry Met Sally here.  I just wanted cauliflower instead of rice.  

The server came back out, and he told me the kitchen couldn't do it.  Apparently he told me they said it has to be served over a bed of rice pilaf.  He asked if I wanted to order a completely different entree instead.  

Well, since I really wanted the variety of chicken, and I just didn't feel like making a scene, I took the rice.  You see, perhaps I could have asked for a manager, but sometimes you just don't want to fight the battle in the restaurant.  Because in the end I have a simple credo.

Always Yelp about it later... that's the best ammunition!

So anyway, I imagine the conversation in the kitchen went like this...

SERVER: Hey, a customer wants the Chicken Trio with cauliflower instead of rice.  Can you do that for him?  

20 YEAR OLD COOK WHO ISN'T TRAINED WELL: W-w-w-w-w-whaaattt???  Ummmm, I don't know how to do that.  The menu says rice pilaf.  I can't ignore the menu.  The menu says so.  Can't go against the menu.  

SERVER: So you're going to send me back out there to tell the customer no, then?

COOK: *head explodes from the pressure*

I mean, if you're Georges Perrier, and you have lived your whole life learning about food and you win major awards in France for doing so, then you get to tell me how you will serve your dish.  Otherwise, give me my damn cauliflower and hush.  

So anyway, now that my rant is done... that Chicken Trio does indeed come on a bed of rice pilaf, a HUUGGGEEE bed of rice, with three pieces of chicken the size of two of my fingers each.  

You know, I really think they could have just moved the damn chicken over, saved the rice, and thrown some cauliflower on there.  It's not like real estate on the plate was at a premium.  These weren't large chicken pieces here.  

I know... I'm ranting.  And there are far greater injustices in the world.  But for some reason, this kind of soured me.  

Oh by the way, the dish I got wasn't too bad in the end.  But my wife's dish... for 12 bucks she gets a scrawny cajun chicken breast, three overcooked shrimp on a wood skewer, and sliced tomatoes.  The tomatoes were bigger than the other two items on the plate combined.  The flavoring on her chicken tasted bitter.  She couldn't even get the shrimp off of the skewer, it was stuck on there since it was so overcooked.  Literally, she tried to pull the shrimp off and the stick broke from the pressure.  The tomatoes were the only good thing on her dish.  Bottom line... one dish failed out of two.  

I just have to say this to the Ruby's kitchen... if you had just given me the cauliflower like I asked, I'd have kept this place at three stars and not updated my review.  But you compelled me to mock you after this experience tonight.  This failure is on the kitchen staff.  They just didn't know what they were doing tonight.  

Next time I get a gift card for Ruby's, I'll just drive to Malvern to use it.
I didn't eat here but had a few beers.  The place is big open and well appointed.  The Beer was good and from what I hear the food is great.

First time diners last night and it was a delight. The food was excellent, solid wine list. The food took a while to come out but it was a Friday night at 7 pm so that is par for the course, it's downtown St. Pete. The Short Rib Mezzaluna was delicious and the Bucatini Pomodoro was equally good. Was a little concerned portion sizes would be too small, total non issue, took home leftovers!

Named after the operatic composition by Bellini, this small attractive and romantic renovated rowhouse enjoys a steady and loyal constituency of well heeled Rittenhouse Square Dorchester/brownstone residents who come both during the week or on the weekend when the family visits.  Two expansions added little more than two four tops but there is a little more elbow room now.  The former chemical engineer turned autodidact chef turns out lovely pastas, excellent veal chop, boar and game as well as the mandatory pork and chicken dishes.   Ambiance conducive to elegant and quiet dinner but that mood can be difficult to capture when the room is teeming with patrons, which is to say every Friday and Saturday.  A best bet for a twosome would be to request one of the newer tables near the back and during the week if possible.  A definite maybe for Valentine's Day!

This place just won a Best of Delaware and they deserve it.  All the food was so fresh and delicious.  Don't miss this treasure in downtown Wilmington.  Be careful with google maps....it will take you to the wrong location....about a mile away.  May need to call the place first to get the cross street.  Worth the effort.
Came for lunch and was not disappointed.   I had the classic lobster roll and salad.  The atmosphere is pleasant, the food was fresh and the service was great!

Nice work, SPTR.  We came in for lunch on a Saturday.  The staff were casual and friendly.  The service was prompt and accurate.   I had the tomato lager soup, which was very good.  It was thick, tomato-ey, and a little tangy.  It also had two tiny grilled cheese sandwiches on it! That was a very creative touch! My dining partner had the gazpacho, which I tried and liked as well.  It had a smokey taste, but I still think it was  veg.  I also had the salt and pepper wings, which were a simple winner.  It was wings that were seasoned with, well, s and p, and then deep fried.  Deliciously simple.  The dishes were reasonably priced and had good portions for the price 

This is a tiny complaint, but it drives me bananas.  We sat at a high bar table.  It wobbled constantly, along with the table next to ours.  It is a simple fix.  I wish restaurants would check that stuff daily.  

Other than that, it was GOOD!

I have to preface this by saying that I did not have a meal in the dining area, I went here strictly for the Harry Waugh Dessert Room. I have never been to Bern's before, which is a little embarrassing to admit since I've lived in South Tampa for almost 20 years.

Tonight (01.20.2012) my boyfriend, best friend, and I were just in the mood for amazing dessert and a great drink. I was instantly floored as soon as we got it; the place looks unassuming from the outside, but is absolutely stunning inside.

We went straight upstairs and were shown to our table. If you have never been here, the thing you should know is that every table is in its own "pod" like structure. You're almost completely enclosed minus the entry way to get in and out of.

We started off with dessert coffees; I got the Steakhouse Cappucino which was...undescribably good. It had about 7 chocolate liqueurs and Kahlua, not to mention it was beautiful presented. For dessert I ordered the "Chocolate-chocolate-chocolate". It was a two layers: one was their "chocolate cheese pie" whih is basically just chocolate cream cheese mousse and the second was their chocolate cheesecake. It was on a dark chocolate crust and completely enrobed in a thick layer of chocolate ganache! It was the most decadent thing I have ever tasted. I had to bring two-thirds of it home with me.

My total was just under $20, which might be a lot for a coffee and a "piece of cake", but you at paying for the quality and the experience of dining at a world renowned steakhouse...deal with it!

I will definitely go back for dessert again, and more importantly for a STEAK!
I absolutely love Country Bagel. My friends and I go here every week. Service is great and the bagels are to die for!
When I'm in town I love stooping for their home-brews and Buttface cheese dip.

Beautiful restaurant . Great atmosphere for a family outing, dinner with friends , or a date night. Food was awesome. Very flavorful and great presentation. Our waiter was phenomenal. I wish I remembered his name. Overall, I will be back.!

This shake was one of the tastiest smoothies my taste buds have ever tried! I got the Mango Smoothie and it definitely will quench your thirst, the NOLA sun was draining my energy but as soon as I got this smoothie I was ready for the world! 
All shakes have banana, yogurt and coconut milk, which is a great addition to any flavor.
They have tons of alcoholic infusions but I left before I could try :(. If I'm ever back in NOLA I'm heading here for my daily thirst quench!
Great coffee and amazing cheese Danish. Clean. Cute store also. Seating outside is nice. Friendly staff.
The drinks and food were amazing! Blackened tuna was so delicious and the soft tacos were super yummy! Mojitos and margaritas were fantastic. Great happy hour from 11-7. Awesome atmosphere!
Awesome and tasty. The seafood beignet is really good. Plus the regular beignets here are way better the Cafe Du Monde!! Thin, flaky, hot, and made to order!! Yum!!!

The staff here is uber friendly. The food was decent, but what really made the whole meal was the courtesy of the staff. Biscuits and gravy were pretty good, and the waffles were okay. For the holiday season they have pumpkin spice waffles - wish I would have tried one of those!

Can't figure out why this place is rated so high. First it is just like any other low-end Mexican restaurant in Nashville. And once you open up the menu you are blown away by the high prices. How in the world does this place stay open in this part of town?? You know immediately about this place when you try to order a coke and they point to a fridge with bottles. I ordered the combination beef and chicken fajitas. The serving size was huge, but the quality of the beef was below average. Homemade corn tortillas were good. Save your money.

I love trying new food destinations, but when it comes to the special moments, Eleven Eleven is my place. The food is never disappointing and consistently delicious. The ambiance is lovely and allows you to be among many while feeling a sense of privacy with your party. The servers are experienced, well-informed on the food and drinks, and are attentive. Eleven Eleven is one of my favorites!

Wonderful breakfast!  Staying at the hotel next to the restaurant so super convenient.  I had the West Coast Omelet which was filled with delicious avocados, tomatoes, onions, feta cheese. It was really good.  My daughter had pancakes and eggs.  Very generous portions and they had sourdough toast which was a big plus for this west coaster!  Also had a lovely mimosa which was a delightful bonus to breakfast!  Very friendly and attentive staff!  All in all a delicious and delightful breakfast!

This is an amazing place within the city. Easy to ignore - hard to forget. 

I had two tapas: carrot mousse and gnocchi. Both were hearty. I could not finish them. 

Great find in City...
Robert was the server - he was great

My hub's has been wanting to come here for months.  We were out about and he pulled in and said, today's the day!  We walked in, only one other couple inside, we were greeted and told to sit where we wanted. Haven't been in since it was Benton Park Cafe, the place was totally different. Really cute. Seemed to have more seating.  Loved the ceiling murals.  It was bright and colorful.  The menu isn't big, but there's plenty to chose from. Some apps, salads, paninis and pizza.  The bar is nice, looks well stocked.  Sam was our bartender and waiter.  Nice and informative.  We kept it simple, ordered a couple Caesar salads and a couple pizzas.  I did order a cocktail, the Pink Italian lemonade.  It was ok, but I wouldn't get it again. The Caesar's were good, on the smaller side, but had a good dressing.  The pizza's were wonderful!  Hand tossed, crust had crunchy edges, but chewy too with a great flavor.  We tried the Momma's Meatball and the Sazizza.  (It's how they spelled it.).  I noticed they also have a Yelp check in special, a free gelato, so we did that as well.  You get two scoops and we chose the Strawberry and the Chocolate Hazelnut.  I've had much better gelato, but it was ok.  All in all it was a great experience.  We left full and have some leftovers!!  They are working on their website and are revamping their Wine Dinners that sound amazing!!  We'll be back!!

I love this place- though it is smaller than the Campbell location (or it appears to be). Nonetheless the same great food. If you are a pancake lover, I highly recommend it. The specials are always tasty and the regular menu has a variety of options too.

I have read the reviews here on La Patisserie Chouquette and believe that those giving it less than stellar ratings need to get their undies out of a wad. I mean, this place is incredible and the staff is uber-helpful every time I walk in the store. I have never had a bad or distasteful experience here, both figuratively and literally. Mind you that the store isn't in the most "high end" area, but I believe the McRee/Botanical Heights area is gentrifying so it doesn't really seem so out of place. The only challenge one might have is parking space, which can be at a premium along Tower Grove at certain times of the day.

The pastries are amazing, albeit on the pricier side, but such love and care goes into their creation it would seem almost a crime to sell them for less. The French macarons (not to be confused with the common macaroon) are the stars of the store. They are prominently placed up front as you walk in, which is NO mistake in my opinion. I mean, if you don't try these you are crazy. I have had the croissants and many different cookies and homemade marshmallows, all of which have never left me disappointed. The ice cream is amazing, so don't forget to ask for a sample. I ended up getting the wedding cake ice cream the last time I was there and dreamt about it the rest of the day. From other reviewers I see I need to try other things the next time, especially the coffee.
 
They do have a traditional tea during the weekends, but since I live out of town I have not done this yet...maybe someday. Also, the patisserie is now making Faux-nuts, of which I would kill to try. Unfortunately I live out of town during the weekend so can't make it during the Saturday's when they make them (get there early and get in line as they sell out FAST).
 
So, nothing bad to say at all about this little gem. I look forward to my next trip, much like a little kid loves going to the candy store. This is just a grown-up candy store. I also would suggest if you like this place, you need to follow them on Facebook since you get to see what they might have special on a day-to-day basis.

Went with a group of 8. The Tortellini on Broth soup with spinach was delish.  5 at the table got the Bronzini fish filleted tableside. Presentation was lovely and they all liked it. I got the stuffed pasted with lobster with baby shrimp in brandy cream sauce. Was tasty, but baby shrimp is never very good- only a salty addition- and sauce was too heavy on the brandy part, didn't cook off long enough and it overpowered the dish. 

The service was terrific. Wine menu is as big as an old set of Encyclopedia Brittania. Unbelievably wonderfuly, but best is the wine cellar! Worth a look. 

I would eat there again. Convenient location off Market Street.

We dined here for restaurant week and it was our first time! Decor is adorable. The restaurant is small and the kitchen was open, which I love! Great smells and you get to see all of the action. Restaurant week was four courses. First: we had the lobster pop tart (incredible) and the stuffed long hots (delicious and HOT). Second: gnocchi (gnocchi itself were so delicious and pillowy) and the lobster mac and cheese (one of the best things I've ever tasted). Third: mahi mahi (okay, wasn't blown away & didn't like the sauce and the fish was a little tough) and whole fish done scampi style (really good, sauce was good, but not great, fish was excellent and the mashed potatoes were delicious). Fourth: bacon bread pudding (delicious!!!!) and tiramisu (delicious as well!!!!!!).
    Overall, this place is really really good. The service was excellent and extremely attentive. At some points the would try to take plates before we were finished. But they were all great, really. The food is excellent. I wasn't a fan of the entrees sauce, but everything else was incredible.

11:40 Sunday, parking lot full, good sign. Seating for 50 inside and 24 outside. But, with the tables 50% full and people in line it feels a bit congested ... eight deep for one very kind order taker who was also taking phone orders so locals must know its best to order in advance. No chicken flautas unfortunatey. No public restroom. Carne asada taco was better than the burrito but both could use a bit of salt and hot sauce because the salsa is just ok. Horchata a bit stronger than I'm used to. Seems like an authentic place.

L'Espresso is a great alternative to teh chain coffee shops in the area, and solid competition for Three Bananas just across the street in Churchill Square. There is a solid selection of hot and cold drinks, sandwiches, soups, and other light fare. The place has a Mediterranean theme to it, and it is conveniently located amongst the attractions of downtown. Worth checking out if you're in need of a caffeine fix, are thirsty, or want a quick bite to eat.

Wow, what a total and complete disappointment. I would give 0 stars if I could. My wife and I live downtown and with the sunny weather yesterday we decided to ride our bikes somewhere for brunch. We picked Sunrise because for years we used to take the family to the Carmel location, and I used to eat at the Fishers location, and always enjoyed both. We locked up our bikes and walked into the building the cafe is located inside of. There was a group of 4 men in front of us and a restaurant that was only about 75% full. We stood behind he group of 4 men and waited for a good 10 mins before a gray haired gentleman asked me how many. I said 2 and looked and saw at least 5 open tables for 2. I wondered why they hadn't pushed two of those smaller tables together for the group of 4 in front of us. After being ignored for about 5 more minutes, one of the men waiting in the group in front of us yelled out to a waitress rushing past us how much longer before they could be seated. She just shrugged and kept walking. After another 5 mins of all 6 of us now being ignored, the 4 men left to head to another place. My wife and I stuck it out for an additional 5 minutes of being completely ignored before we also left and headed to First Watch. 

We ran into the 4 men who had been eating in front of us and they said they had waited at Sunrise for at least 30 minutes before leaving. My wife and I waited 20 minutes before we left. We all agreed that the waiting wasn't what had upset us, it was the combination of empty tables all around and being almost completely ignored.  One other thing we all agreed on, none of us will ever go back to Sunrise. I don't care how busy or understaffed they may have been at that time, there is absolutely no excuse to treat customers that way. Or should I say former customers!

Good, cute BYOB.  The food is predictable, but doesn't REALLY stand out to me at all times.  Oddly enough, my favorite things to eat here are the side dishes. I enjoyed the beats and the artichoke dish I ordered.  It's a really great spot for groups of people, and for first dates.  Especially when it is nice out, as they have great outdoor seating.  I recommend it if you have lot of wine you want to finish up, and don't particularly care about what you eat with your wine.
This is an awesome place. The donuts look amazing and so does the food. The coffee was great. The front service staff was a lot of fun and helped out a lot. Also byob.

Plenty of restaurant choices in Tarpon as far as the usual Greek fare goes. We walked up and down Dodecanese a few times and settled on Yianni's. Felt like it had the best bang for buck as far the lunch specials go. 

We were seated in the back of the restaurant and the place was fairly busy. Staff while polite seemed to be in a bit of a rush and not acknowledge new customers. Bread arrived promptly. But waitress to take our drink and food orders did not show up for a while.

The missus settled on the Greek Sampler while I opted for the Gyro sandwich. The sampler included one serving each of Mousaka, Pastito and Dolmades. The sandwich is served with one side: fries, soup or Greek salad. As luck would have it, they were out of the soup. I settled for the fries. 

The gyro was awesome. The meat tender, flavored and cooked to perfection. The pita bread seemed fresh and was soft. The fries certainly were a good accompaniment. The missus enjoyed her sampler. For the uninitiated, here is quick run down on what's what on the platter.. Mousaka is a layered dish with eggplant, potatoes and meat. Pastito is a baked pasta dish that contains ground beef and béchamel sauce. Dolmades was grape leaves stuffed with rice and meat. Very tasty!

The food gets a 5 star rating. No complaints. 

Yianni's loses half a star for the facilities. The restrooms were filthy. Water all over the place. Lights not working in the ladies room.
Another half a star for the staff that just seemed to rush through and not care that much about the customer. Might as well make it a "walk up to the counter and order yourself" place. 

Based solely on the food, we'd go back! Hope the service improves.

This is a great venue to hear great live music from the songwriters themselves. It's a quiet place so you can hear the acoustics perfectly that is different from the live bands you hear on Broadway. It is about a mile walk from Broadway or you can take a quick drive or uber/Lyft ride there. The food isn't bad either. I had the Alfredo pasta and it was great. Also has good ribeyes. A must stop to hear premium good music.

Amazing place! Wait Staff's customer service could be bettter but will still go back.

Thanks!

Everything we had was excellent wife had the tikka masala I had the lamb jonaf. Perfect spice and perfect portions. I also tried the appetizers the garden salad left a lot to be desired but was still good. The potato patties were absolutely awesome. The fried onions were good as well. Has a true indian taste and that is what I crave plus they have combinations of north and South Indian cuisine which suits me and my wife. Will definitely return. Only quam I had was they were out of mango lassi but it wasn't enough for me to downgrade the food. Service was okay but never a major factor for me.

Our favorite Thai food for take out! We live super close and they always have our food done super fast! Some of our favorite dishes are the pad Thai and fried rice! The spring rolls are yummy too! Their spicy is super spicy! I always order boba here as well and it's so delicious! Great food!
I went to the Moorestown location to have the express lunch. I odered the mozzerella and the Margarita Pizza. What a dissappointment! The food was boring and bland.Worst pizza ever!

I've been here twice and I still don't get this place.  The ordering process is confusing and long.  I found it difficult to visualize just what it was that I was ordering.   Food was fresh.  Just the same, This will not be a regular stop.
Tried to order through Grub Hub, Tried to call to place a pick up order.  They are not accepting orders.  Not sure if this is still open or not, but it did look interesting.

I think i can write a pretty detailed review about Heart of Oak.  We were regulars there for over 3 years.

http://www.baciristorante.com/index2.htm

Heart of Oak is a quaint, intimate english style pub in Buckingham, PA.  It's fairly close to Peddler's Village (2 miles) and New Hope (about 10 miles). Seating is minimal inside (one bar and about 10 tables) so don't be surprised if you go on a friday or saturday around dinner time and don't get a seat.  If you go there after 10pm though you're fine.  

The beer selection is superb for this area.  If you're looking for bud you're at the wrong place.  Beers on tap include: John Courage (a first for me, i love this amber lager), Guinness (especially good here), Boddington's, London Pride ESB, Carlsberg, Newcastle, etc.  They do have Yuengling on tap which downgrades them from 5 stars to 4, but you have to please everyone i guess.  I'm not a wine fanatic, but i was given a tour of their wine cellar and they have an extensive collection.

The prices are high...$6 for a full pint of beer....no head here.  The food is delicious.  They have a pub menu, but you can also order anything from the excellent italian restaurant upstars (Baci) which is owned by the same family.  The pub menu includes Bangers and Mash, Chicken and Leek Pie, Shepard's Pie, Hamburgers, Buffalo Wings and various other quick eats.  The Chicken and Leek pie is DELICIOUS, as is the Shepard's Pie.  Either one will run you about $10 but is more than enough to fill you.

The thing that drew us to Heart of Oak was the excellent beer selection and the people.  It is owned and operated by a great family.  The head bartender downstairs is Tony and he is hillarious.  Many a drunken night was spent with Tony as he was "practicing" making his famous shots.

Also great are the other bartenders and the regulars who are always up for some darts at 1am.

There also is music on friday and saturday nights.  An excellent musician "Graham" plays there twice a month.  if you're into alternative/folk music he's your man.  He plays everything from The Beatles and Bob Dylan, to Radiohead and Pearl Jam (we asked him to play a PJ song one night and he played a whole set!)

Anyway, if you're looking for a relaxing evening head to Heart of Oak and tell Tony i said Hi!

One final thing, they are no-smoking now.  If you're a non-smoker it's MUCH more enjoyable in there now.  If you are a smoker, bring a jacket.  There are table outside for you though.

ATL wings is my new favorite wing place in Tucson. I used to go to Wingstop but this place is a hundred times better. The staff is super friendly and the manager is great to customers. The wings are made real fast, I feel like you order and then they arrive in just minutes. Located on 4th North of the church. I would say I am addicted to this place, they even know my order lol. I highly recommend this place if your looking for the best wings in town

I lived in Thailand for a little while so I got spoiled by all the wonderful street food that is incomparable. However, this place really surprised me. Their flavors and technique made this take out dinner feel like we were enjoying it in a restaurant. 

The presentation was great and the everything was very fresh. I highly recommend this restaurant to Thai food lovers. I only wish I could have gotten it super spicy but I had to share with my husband and he can't do the heat. 

Surprisingly affordable and the portions are great!

Napolean House has a special place in my heart, as it was the first restaurant I ever dined at in New Orleans, before I lived here. It mistakenly gave me the impression that every place in New Orleans would present as ancient, dark, moody, and feature upscale service with cheaply priced food. Wrong on all counts. These features are fairly unique to NH.

Napolean House is one of the only places in the Quarter where you can just pop in, get seated, and have an affordable meal with upscale service and ambience. That said, the food is just OK. My favorite thing about the menu is that there are options for vegetarians - a rare thing in the Quarter. There are a few appetizers, salads, and sandwiches appropriate for vegetarians, and well priced 

My favorite thing on the menu is the rich and creamy spinach artichoke dip, served in a bread bowl. The caesar salad is fine, and the grilled cheese sandwiches are just ok, as is the potato salad. The establishment is known for their Pimm's cup. To me it seemed unremarkable.

It's very lovely, authentically Spanish, and darkly lit inside, and the walls are scribbled upon. There are portraits of past maitre d's. Service is great. Family-friendly.

Oh my gosh!!! The food here was amazing. I had the salmon omelet with cheesy grits. I've never had grits before, and I was very pleased with what I got. The wait was long, but the food came out really quick. Definitely worth the wait!
The Vampire tacos were amazing! The tacos had crispy cheese on the outside with mouthwatering chicken inside. Then had the brownie with ice cream. It was the perfect dessert to end my day!

Huge selection for vegans!  BBQ fried rice and Koloke are my favorites.  Once ordered the BBQ fried rice and realized after it was delivered they had put egg in it by accident.  We called and they came back with a new order and gave us the money back for the rice.  Exceptional customer service, would recommend to anyone, but especially vegans/vegetarians!
My father and I stumbled across this place and we were really surprised by how yummy it all was. Very healthy selections and great prices. My dad really loved it, I'm sure we will be back!

I went to the buffet for a basic breakfast because it was close to the cafes price.  I thought the buffet had good choices (although I didn't try everything and I realize that everyone's favorites might not be there).  I just had bacon, scrambled eggs, hash browns and a cinnamon roll.  Everything was at least satisfactory except the cinnamon roll, which was excellent.  It was the only roll I've found that is comparable to Cinnabon's.  Maybe the roll was a little soft, but that was more than made up for by the flavor.  I knew it would be bad, but I had to go back for seconds.  It took a lot of willpower not to just stay and eat roll after roll, especially since by that point they were effectively free.  I don't know how lunch and supper buffets are, which is why this os only four stars, but the cinnamon rolls are five stars in my book.  And the service was also very good.
Good to fair. I've definitely had better and worse. We came early which I regret - maybe if I came later in the day the broth would have had more time to develop and get richer.

So delicious! The garlic naan is fantastic, as is the paneer tikka masala, and the mango lassi. Got great reviews on the fish curry, the and the saag as well. Service is very friendly and we got to sit outside in the gorgeous weather which was great!

Shocker: this place is not a dive! It is nice inside but the real star is the bartender who was working yesterday mid-afternoon (I apologize for not getting your name) and the food was really good, too. 
We needed a drink while we discussed making a LARGE purchase for our home down the street and decided to go someplace close (like, just on the corner) and I'm glad we took the plunge and went inside. The bartender directed us to any of the many tables which are separated from the actual bar and pool table with short walls, so it makes it nicer. After we sat down, she left the bar which looked like it was nearly filled with many regulars and brought us the food menu and took our beer orders.
