Wings...wow, do they have the sauces! We decided on a mix of Cajun spice rub (yum!) and a Ghost pepper sauced set. She warned us of the heat but said they were both her #1 and #2 favorites. They were both delicious and not too hot but you have to watch the heat build up with Ghost pepper. Good thing I ordered another beer! We also ordered Potato skins which were stuffed with melted cheese and the works and really hit that mid afternoon munchie spot.
I was really impressed she would leave the nearly full bar and come over to see how everything was and take her time and talk with us. Did I mention we were the only people in the dining part? Yes, that is service that make you feel special. 
Being a sports bar, there are TV's all around but a mix of music is heard overhead. Could be the neighborhood place for Golden State Warriors games? I'm looking forward to returning and giving the menu a hearty try.

ok sushi, cool designs and rolls. My issue is the price here... for 2 people is was $100 and we brought our own wine.  We had 6 rolls, 2 soups, 2 salads. You can go to Yokohomo or Kabuki for half the price. For instance, there eel roll is like $15, but it should be $6-8.  Just a pile of leaves are $7. Nothing else is in the salad. Not much of an atmosphere except the beetles music and pictures. Probably won't go back just based on the prices.

My husband and I had dinner on the outdoor patio last night. The food and service are generally very good, and the patio is very pleasant. We had the grilled octopus appetizer which while pricey ($18) was definitely a large portion and was really nicely prepared. My dinner was a whole Branzino that I got already filleted. It was served with red potatoes, broccoli and red peppers. The fish still had a lot of bones in it but was fresh and very simply grilled and seasoned.  The surprise came with the check: the branzino cost $38. I didn't study the entree prices but I think they pretty much top out around $24. When there is that large a difference in your menu prices and your 'market' price, I think the server should include the price when telling you about the dish. I should have asked as well, and won't make that mistake again.

First time there. Got takeout and will b back - very flavorful. Both the chicken and beef with vegetables and pan-fried noodles were very tasty. The sesame chicken was too salty but good otherwise. The egg rolls r well made  - crispy.

Ordered delivery and the delivery fee was outrageous, $10! The delivery was supposed to be delivered between 1:10-1:20 and got it at 1:40. The fries are all hard and over cooked. The chicken tenders are disgusting and oddly squishy inside. The shrimp platter is lacking in shrimp and hard. The pasta is hard and the noodles are breaking as soon as you touch it. Will not order again.
Coffee is pretty good, I like coming here on the weekends. It's hit or miss on how busy it is and how long of the wait. Kind of expensive for what it is, but I do go here for the convenience.

Their pho is okay this place will do if your craving for some pho and do not feel like going to philly. Their banh xeo is good but it is very oily. I had one to go and my take out box was filled with oil on the bottom. They have good service.

Had the other Alambres dish (ranchero) this time and lunch guest had the chicken burrito. 

Both were good but both were too heavy on the salt. 

Free chips were one again appreciated. 

Request for water refill twice seemed to be forgotten.

Fantastic place in cool springs! I had the Angus Breakfast Burger (burger with fried egg) with duck fat fries. Both were great. I had been wanting to try this place for awhile and I am so glad I did. I will be going back soon to try the Nashville Hot Chicken Sandwich! Yum! Adam was our waiter and he was great! Met the owner too, Mr. Kelly Black. Very nice and welcoming. I recommend you stop in and give it a try soon!
Dam good food!The steaks & gravy fries are awesome!

My best friend and I went here for apps and 1/2 price wine night. They have these great booths off the bar that have a great atmosphere that allow you to be out and social but also give you space to talk. The place is a bit pricey but a really nice night out. The wine selection is decent and the margaritas are strong...can't get better then that!

Hubs brought me here for a late lunch early dinner on a Sunday afternoon. I ordered the Cheeseburger, Andy's Size with provolone cheese, with everything, and fries and sweet tea, the hubs ordered a double burger. Andy's size with mustard, ketchup and grilled onions, onion rings and Diet Pepsi. 
Our orders came out quickly and the burgers, they are take you back to flat top diner cooking amazingness! The bun, the juicy burger, the melted cheese, the fresh tomato, lettuce, it all works out perfectly! 
And I LOVE the music, reminds me of my Pops!! He would've loved this place! 
Emberlee was our Server and she was very attentive and sweet!
We will definitely be making the drive from Mount Juliet Back to Highway 55 Burgers!!

This place was great. I was having such a bad day and just happen to walk in. I ordered pho from next door but decided to get a few items from here. Food was great. The owner was very nice. Best part of my day. Will definitely be ordering more often .

Came here for lunch. As we have many times before. And again discovered that this place is at best, very mediocre. If it weren't for the atmosphere (and jalapeño poppers), I would not visit again. Come to drink...not to eat!!
The California Club was awesome!!! The wait was a struggle but the area had other areas close to hang!

I pretty much love all Indian food, seriously the spices and the cream sauces so delicious.  We came here the other night I was craving Indian food like no other. So we ended up here.   I ordered an appetizer mixer which included veggie samosa, veggie pakora, and some other things.  The samosa was okay but not fabulous and the veggie pakora was soggy. Which is always icky.  So then I ordered the entrees for all of us to share chicken korma, and chicken tikka masala.  The korma was much better spiced and the chicken tikka masala was okay. 
You do have to pay extra for rice.

Anyways it was awful but it wasn't fabulous.  Just kind of in-between.
Probably won't go back again the prices were high if we are going to spend money I would rather go to Saffron.

The smoothies are fantastic. I'm addicted and they are priced fairly at around $5.66 for a generous 24 ounces. Why the 3 stars? When I first started going there a few months ago I got the app which gave me $5 off my first purchase. I ordered a Mediterranean Bowl to go. When I got home the bowl was only a little more than half full. The young man who made it waited on me and knew I was getting it almost free. It's my opinion that he shorted me on purpose because it was free. That's the worst thing you can do to a new customer. I haven't ordered another food item since. I hope the owner of the franchise reads this and has a talk with his or her employees.

I loved their food but for some reason I believe me and my family was not welcomed here this evening.  We sat for 52 minutes after ordering our food and our order never came.  We were reassured our order was a coming but after 15 minutes...nothing. People sat after us received their meals quicker than us and were almost finished.  My family got up and left...never to return because we seen what was going on.

My husband had the BBQ oysters, and while he said the taste was good, almost everyone had grit in it. He did, however, say that his martini was REALLY good. And my seasonal cocktail, a Ruby Sour, was also very good. But nothing ruins rosters more than grit. Unfortunate; we might have stayed for dinner but for that.

I love love love this restaurant and the "old world" charm.  It's decor is romantic...reminds me of that "One if by land two if by sea" look.  We had the shrimp lejon, neptini cocktail and crab dip as appetizers...Crab dip was fantastic...nice and buttery...well worth it!  Had the stuffed broiled scallops as an entree...loved every bit!  I can't wait to try this place again.  : )

Really ok place good food good quality decent selection including delish Chicken korma. Doubtlessly about as authentic and healthy as General Tao's chicken and even more delicious!
The place costs more than Szechuan Mandrin and guess what - you get what you pay for!

Get the portabella mushroom sandwich!  It's a cheesy with alfalfa sprouts & it's amazing!  The fries here are da bomb!  

Excellent beers on tab and friendly servers.  

The only negative thing I have to report is that the upstairs bar/seat-yourself/order yourself thing going on is kinda confusing.  I wish they just had servers up there to take your orders... it's tough to pick out your beers from a chalk board on one side of the room and then go to the other side of the room to see the menu (on another chalk board).

This highly anticipated bar that so many friends recommended left me feeling sour. First the server didnt explain or offer anything.,Second the drinks were ok. I moved to the bar where we ordered a few appetizers, they were more like over salted snacks that were too dry and lacked finishing ingredients. The worst part was that we didnt get our complete order, We asked for pig popcorn which was actually a small amount of tiny pork rinds.was forgotten and no one took notice until I spoke up. Lastly there is a awkward silent treatment thing going on that overly pretentious for no reason, too stiff, and off putting. Sorry I wont be returning here.

Stopped for lunch today and was pleasantly surprised by the quality and creativity.  Had a Chicken Cordon Bleu sandwich that was nicely done.  My wife had a Jerk Chicken wrap that was also very well constructed.

All in all a keeper that I would like to go back to for breakfast/brunch, for which they are known.

So I fairly regularly order delivery from here. And food is pretty good. Not everything is my favorite, but that doesn't mean it's not prepared well. When I asked for a total, on today's bill, I questioned why it was so high, almost $8 more than I expected to hear? Ok. I asked for some extra veggies to be put in my pasta. But $4? For a handful of mushrooms and roasted peppers. Ok, folks its wasnt extra chicken or shrimp, its veggies, about $1 at best. But when I asked about the remaining balance I was told there is a delivery fee $3.50. So who does this go to i wonder? The driver?? In the future I will no longer tip the driver as I am guessing this 15% fee is going to them. Because my additional $4 that I gave to him makes a 40% tip. That's a bit excessive in my book. I think they should notify callers of this. As it is no where printed on the menu that a deliver fee will be charged. That's an unknown charge on my bill. In a restaurant that would be disputed and removed. In the future if they want my biz they'll remove that charge or give it to the driver as their tip. I've run restaurants for 1/2 my life. Never have I felt so inclined to make a complaint. And not have an ounce of understanding for the business. This is just shady. 

I would give their food 3 stars but their swindling of delivery customer deserves 1 star. Shape up folks. Or you'll be losing guests.

Who doesn't love felipes???? My favorite go to meal is the shrimp quesadillas and you get to add anything you want to it! And your sides get to be queso and chips! Love! Their queso is the domb! I also love their margs! Each location has their own feel. Mid city has a fun side bar, the one downtown is obviously wonderful because their bar is almost completely separate from the restaurant so you feel like you're at a real bar. And the one uptown is more of a grab and go type place. Everything's delicious!

DECENT BBQ FOR A GOOD PRICE!

I lived in St. Louis for a few months and luckily enough just down the road (within walking distance) from Bandana's. I am from CA and living in the midwest was obv looking for some BBQ. This place satisfied my cravings and let me share why:

1) FOOD (4/5): I've been here for LUNCH a few times because it's such a GOOD DEAL! I think the food is good/satisfying and it gets 4 stars because of the PRICE and PORTION size. From the lunch platter I can have 2 ribs and a slice of bread for leftovers.
- Ribs: tasty with that top rib layer CHARRED JUST RIGHT. The ribs are FLAVORFUL and have a good amount of meat to them.
- Beef: so-so. The beef is cut into pieces and SOFT. I prefer the ribs.
- Fried okra: plain and BLAND. Would most def have to put salt on this.
- Baked potato: served with a good helping of butter and sour cream
- Garlic bread: generally large slices of bread

2) SERVICE (4/5): FRIENDLY waiters and they're good about filling up your water. If it's your first time there, they will explain all the sauces to you. Something about how 2 of them are a thicker, molasses sauce. The food comes out relatively QUICKLY, as in I am not waiting a long time to eat. 

3) AMBIANCE (3/5): Standard chain restaurant; good for parties of any size with average noise level. It is nice to dine outdoors when the weather is good. They have MULTIPLE TVs with sports games on.

BOTTOM LINE:
Totally RECOMMEND this place if you are looking for GOOD BBQ for a REASONABLE PRICE and in a timely manner.

I decided to stop in for an early dinner after an appointment.  I had been here a few times before and for the dinner special prices, it has been worth an occasional stop.  

The waitress seated me in a booth, not very comfortable.  The restaurant is located in a shopping plaza and also has a small bar.  Two customers were enjoying drinks at the bar.  A small group was sitting in an adjoining room and what appeared to be playing a card game.  I decided to try the special, Calzone with a side Salad and Tiramisu for dessert.  The Calzone was tasty and for the price the portion size was appropriate, but I would have enjoyed more filling.  The house salad was nothing to write home about.  Plain bag lettuce with sparingly watered down dressing, this has been a repeated event.  The Tiramisu was not home made, but it was good.  I did enjoy my glass of wine. I would have liked another glass of wine, however the waitress never checked on me again until my food was all gone.

The hotel room looks clean, however the cigarette smell was so strong, like someone just smoking at your door even though we were at a non-smoking floor. Also the AC running sound was so noisy at night that kept waking us up.  Water pressure was low, there was two morning that we couldn't take a shower. Insulation was bad, we can hear people taking loud outside all the time. We wouldn't recommend it.

Tonight I ate dinner at Tucker's in South County and was very disappointed with my steak and baked sweet potato. I asked for my steak cooked medium and was nearly burnt, the sweet potato was charcoal. I have never had any problems with my food at this location before.

Some of the best real Chinese food in Saint Louis. Stay away from the "American style" entrees and try the authentic offerings. Beef with Cumin,  Beef Chow Fun, Eggplant with Bean Sauce, Beef Slice and Ox Tripe in Chili Sauce are real standouts. There are some daily specials available as well.
The sandwich was surprisingly good. Very tender pork and nice tangy sauce. The Mac and cheese was good, but heavy.  Wish they had another option besides canned beans.  A reasonable value for 10.00.

I swear everything they served was bought at Walmart and not even seasoned. The wait staff was fantastic. The food was so bad we couldn't even get it down. Ordered a pizza when we left so disappointing to wait all day to be served garbage

Have been to Fogo a couple of times and think Fogo is a good benchmark but this place is a-ok.  Quality of the meat in the barbecue realm is really a moot point.  it's ALL fatty, tendinous, unctuous, greasy goodness regardless of grade. They have a great salad bar which I get some things from.  Word to the wise, don't go all you can eat.  Trust me.  I can eat.  I have eaten two and a half full entrees at a restaurant and needed more.  

I have gone rodizio twice there for 25.00 each time.  They bring out the crap first.  by the time you get full, they bring out the Picanha.  Instead, tell them you want it by the pound, go up to the counter, and ask for the picanha.  5.00 a lb.  3 lbs of meat for 15.00  and it was all cuts I wanted.  I was just following the brazillians who all get it by the pound.  It's the way to go.  The whole bill for my wife and I, fully stuffed was 22.00, versus 50.00 for two, and we just got meat that we wanted, and salad.  

Give it a go.

got our table of 5 in super quick, service was great and all our food was really good. great selection of appetizers and the calamari was bomb.... sucks to pay to park, but at least you know there will be parking available.

Omg do these ladies know how to make a good Italian, boy am I a sucker for an Italian sub. 

Salami, ham and capicola I believe, with peppers and provolone. Mm mm mm. And it was 5.75, perfect for a day trip to Washington, even had leftovers that I added some Dominican avocado to for a midnight snack...cause ya can't keep the Cali out of me

Pretty stoked on this spot, can't wait to go back.I'm guessing most of their clientele are so die hard they don't even use yelp. 

And may I add.. it was Some of the best service I had in Delaware.

A month later and I find myself updating my review for this place once again! Anyone who lives in Philly will tell you that Vic sushi is a must-try, and they aren't wrong. A tiny place with only a sushi bar and one table, this place does not seem to have any issue bringing in customers. 

Vic Sushi has one of the best deals of the surrounding sushi spots. The Three Roll Special. Choose any three (regular) rolls for $10.75. My personal favorites are: Spicy Tuna Roll, Shrimp Tempura Roll, and Philly Roll. Also, you MUST order the spicy mayo on the side. I could literally drink it straight. Anyways, the spicy tuna here is bomb.com. If you are a spicy tuna fiend like myself, stop reading this review and go order one. 

Another Vic staple (that I have yet to try!) is the tuna dumpling. 9 times out of 10, when you dine in here you will here the sushi chefs going to town with a mallet. This is the art of tuna dumplings. They literally smash tuna into a dumpling shape and fill it with avocado and other tasty ingredients. 

So why not five stars? Well, Vic has some issues. For starters, they do not serve you water. You have to purchase a water bottle. Secondly, although minor, they do not care much about presentation. If you order steamed shumai, you will watch them stick a box of shumai in the microwave and serve it to you. Not on a plate, but in a takeout sushi tray. Super minor, but a bit odd. In addition, they do not provide dumpling sauce. My shumai has also been cold before because they failed to heat it up for an extra 10 seconds longer. 
And probably the most talked about issue; the size of the sushi rolls. For some odd reason, Vic creates full sized special rolls, but miniature regular rolls. They provide you with 8 pieces per regular roll, but they shrink down the size to fool you. If you order the three roll special, you won't be complaining. You'll be full regardless!

100% worth the trip. See you soon, Vic!

I have been to Sakana multiple times and have eaten from different sushi chefs when I'm there. They are one of the best places in town by far. They are on the opposite side of town from me but I happily take the drive passing many other sushi joints just to eat there. Always amazing food and service no matter who's there. They have the freshest nigiri in town. Plus they make there own ice cream just an added bonus. Go there if you haven't yet.

You're going to have to make a really phenomenal burger to get me to pay $15. I did not experience that on my visit...at all. Those sad, greasy, stale chips that accompany the overpriced burger should be removed from the roster altogether. The final straw? Those seats on the first floor that are so low you feel like a kindergartner when trying to eat.

I went to this place cause I saw all the great reviews but was utterly disappointed. This place is not worth the hour and a half to two hour wait. The omelet I had was overly spiced and was the worst one I have ever tasted. Their waffles tasted like eggo waffles and were extra crunchy and dry. Dispite the bad food their staff was extremely nice, their fruit was fresh, and their coffee was awesome.

Best Spot in South Tampa for Brunch! Excellent Hostess handling reservations and service was very good as well. Excellent spicy margaritas called The Tahona.   The Mill Burgers were top notch.   Friend has the Dirty Bird and I had the Sausage and waffle Benny.  It had egg.  Which did not show on the menu.  If not for that it would have been a perfect brunch!   Great decor.  Don't miss a visit to the restroom!  Will return!

This was the first restaurant I went to since arriving in New Orleans. My experience here was great. I had mentioned out loud there was an Alfredo dish and the waiter insisted I get an authentic creole dish. I thought that was so cute. My baby sister ordered the fried oyster po boy which was soooo good. My older sister ordered the catfish Po boy which she said was excellent. I ordered the bbq shrimp and grits which I liked a lot but I wish I would have chosen a difference dish. Lastly, I ordered the creole cheesecake. It was soooo delicious. I actually ordered one to go just to bring to my room for later. The service was excellent. All of the waitstaff were charming and sweet. I had such a wonderful experience. Good food, excellent service, and great people.
Delivery restrictions are a bit ridiculous, but the food is delish & affordable, and does not take long to be ready for pick-up!

A place that is easy to miss from the street as it is built in the side of a house basically, Brother's Old Style Deli offers breakfast sandwiches, a variety of specialty sandwiches, hoagies, hot sandwiches, cold sandwiches, salads, as well as tomato pie that they have brought in. They also have a few side orders - potato, tuna, chicken, or macaroni salad - and cole slaw. The decor in the seating area is surprisingly quaint, much like the Epicure Cafe a few blocks down the street. Seating is limited to about 10 people.

The store hours on the door read they are open until 6:30pm, but I was told by the girl working there that the hours are 5 on weekdays and 4 on the weekend. Don't mistake the door nearest the corner as the entrance even though it has the store hours on it - many people presume the store to be closed all the time because of this.

Today was my first time ordering there, and I must say the panini I had with smoked turkey, bacon, spinach, tomato, & cheese with cajun mayo was excellent. The bread especially was seeded and seasoned and had all kinds of flavor and chewy texture. I will definitely be back and will update my review when I do.

I liked Applebee's when I went in person but when we had it delivered it was disappointing. My mother and I got the same thing. The mashed potatoes and onion rings were great but the steak was very tough, hard to cut and had absolutely no flavor. My mother also didn't like the broccoli but I didn't see anything wrong with that. I, like her was just very disappointed in the steak.

This place is fun, reminds me of a vacation spot. I had never been and to my surprise it was fairly crowded for a Saturday lunch. The food was decent and the service was friendly.

Cons: 
We were asked if we wanted mimosas when we walked in. They offer: Peach, Mango or Orange. We ordered the mango and the peach. One would assume all of those were juices & champs. Wrong. What they didnt tell us is that the peach & the mango are some horrible flavored liquors of some sort which made these taste like odd perfume. One or 2 sips was about all we could take which resulted in a complete waste of $20.

The other complaint is that a lunch for 2 took 40ish min to just get the food after ordering. Yes, they were pretty full, but I just expected a quicker experience overall.
Love the ambience! Super fun if going in a group to play a few games of corn hole with an assortment of appetizers and great drinks

Stayed here for a business trip (my company is based in Tucson but I'm based in Los Angeles) and I've never had a worse hotel experience! The entire lodge perimeter looked very cozy and inviting but I had so many complaints. 

1) The front desk staff did not ask me for my Stash Rewards number. In fact, she did not bother to even ask if I was a Stash Rewards member. I had to call up the front desk the next morning to let them know that I'm a Stash Rewards member and my account was then put on the system.

2) I told the lady at the front desk upon checking in that I'd prefer to stay on the 2nd floor of the lodge, if there was any available. She completely ignored my request and proceeded to give me the key card to the room on the 1st floor, without any explanation if there was no availability whatsoever. It was too late at night for me to argue so I just head out to my room. 

3) The room itself was cozy but there were so many things wrong with my particular unit. The tv remote control was dirty and crusty (I had to physically clean it myself using Clorox disinfecting wipes). There was no microwave available in all rooms. There was no hot water available in the room to drink tea but I did request for a cup of hot water from the restaurant and they delivered. The coffee maker was disgustingly dirty (wouldn't want to make hot water in that piece of equipment). There were disturbing traces of hard water in the bath tub (especially the bath tub drain). The walls are somehow very thin, I could hear my neighbors talking and watching TV every night. My AC broke down in the middle of the night and I woke up sweating bullets--it was fixed by them replacing the batteries in the controller but I shouldn't have been awake between 12:30am-1:30am because of that, especially when I had important business meetings to go to in the morning! 

4) Pros: The front desk guy (Richard) was very efficient and accommodating. Sonoran breakfast was amazing, a lot of yummy varieties & table service. Cool ambiance of the lodge. Coffee packets in the room were Wolfgang Puck's so that was lavish! The robes provided in the room were incredible!

We have been going to Pizza Amore for 15+ years, the last few years pizza has changed, crust too thin , stale and always burned. Toppings are lacking. I am so dissappointed, when the mom and dad ran it, everything was 5 + stars. The sandwiches are very good, cant comment on the dinners as I never ordered. 
I did have to return a pizza one time, it was wrong and crust was burned and hard as a brick and the girl was so freaking rude, The owner though was very apologetic.  Since its convenient we will still go but not as often, I am exploring other options
Had dinner with stuffed chicken, fish sticks and crab capellini. Thoroughly enjoyed it. Amazing server

I will start by saying, the food is probably close to 4 stars, maybe slightly below. The service on the other hand, could have been better.

We started off with the bean dip. If we would have stopped here, I would have been satisfied to the nines. It was so good.

Then, for my entree, I got the friend fish tacos. They were pretty good. Not the best, but not far off from them.

My wife got the quesadilla. It was the one with chicken, mushrooms, and pineapple. She really liked it.

The disappointment was the service. Our guy was nice, but seemed to not look our way often. Shortly after the meal came, my wife needed salsa and I needed a refill on my drink. We grew impatient and finished half of our meal before we finally got our waiters attention.

Yes, he was nice and attentive once we got his attention, but he needs to pay more attention to his surroundings to avoid such along delays.

Shula has good quality burger due to selection of the premium meat. If you want to leave your name in the restaurant, you can accept the 48 oz 48 minutes challenge. It is huge. They do pack the left over if you cannot finish. 

We got the Swiss Mushroom Burger. I like the Swiss cheese than American cheese. It more chewy. The mushroom are developed from fresh mushroom with thick slice. Great when cheese melt on top. The burger is nice with entire package. We got meal and fried come with it. We also got the chocolate shake. I believe on Tuesday, the shake is only a dollar addition from meal plans. It great to have it. 

Service is great. Restaurant has TV that I can watch the games while I am eating.

It's been a long time since we've ordered takeout from this restaurant. Maybe two years even!! But the nice thing is that it is still owned by the same family. The same young lady that takes your order when you call still has the same no nonsense, unfriendly tone. 
However, the food is consistently good! Delivery is always timely and they are always friendly!! ( They have even delivered our order to the backyard while we were in the hot tub!! Lol!!).I would have given five stars but I only found 4 tiny shrimp in my large order of House Special fried rice.

3 stars I think :/ I really wanted to like this plave more, but the food and service was mediocre. Three of us came for a late brunch in the afternoon and sat out in the patio area to enjoy the beautiful view of the river and downtown... Unfortunately that was the highlight of the meal.

The décor and ambience was great when we stepped in. I was excited for a good meal and  service, but it started to decline from there. The waitress brought us our water to start, my friend kindly ask her for less ice, the waitress steps right behind my friend's chair and pours the ice out in front of us...ok!

The menu seemed to have a good variety from sushi, miso soup (what my friend was craving) to calamari. She ordered the miso soup to start right away. Ten minutes later we all placed our orders. We ordered tuna sashimi, hand roll trio with miso soup and ginger salad, spring rolls and spicy tuna roll. My friend's miso soup she ordered as an app didn't come early, but with the rest of our meal. Although, my friend's spring rolls came before the meal. When the soup finally came with our meal, it was the worst miso soup we ever had...bland, you can barely taste the miso, and the tofu was slightly sour...ugh very disappointing! The sashimi was good and fresh, the hand rolls was okay, my friend wasn't crazy about the spicy tuna roll, but did like the spring rolls.

All in all, it was just mediocre. We really wanted to like this place. Great location, ambience, and they had a Sunday buffet for $25 that sounded awesome that we wanted to try. Sadly, I will probably go else where.

A great little lunch spot on the corner of an Oro Valley strip mall, Street is set up as a walk-through order-line type of place, like Chipotle or QDoba. Although I like the flavors here better. Especially the salsa, which is a nice blend of roasted chile flavors with a slow, subtle heat. 

I got the shredded beef bowl for $8. Yum. Perfect for a quick lunch. 

The menu has tacos, burritos, toratas, etc. with a few beers on tap as well. 

I'm looking forward to coming back for a torta. The bread looks really good. 

Check it out some time.

Very good, have vegan options and everything seems really fresh - only side note the side greens are a little sweet for my taste but were good inside my sandwich ! Nice little place close to all the attractions in New Orleans !

Had an awful experience here. It took 45 minutes for our first drink to come and we were not given an opportunity to order another round when we were finished. The water on the table was consistently empty. The food was over cooked. My friends skirt snagged on the broken bathroom handle and it ripped her skirt. We informed the manager because it was very sharp and sticking out of the door so we didn't want someone to get hurt. The manager said they would send a drink over to the table after we had already paid the bill. We waited twenty minutes for one drink when a group of 6 had already paid and THE DRINK NEVER CAME. A total waste of time. We finally left and let the manager know at which point she just said "sorry." This used to be a place I would recommend to friends and family visiting Nashville but will no longer be doing that.

This is one if my favorite places to eat!  The atmosphere is casual and fun.  Some of the booths have beer taps at the table!  There is a great variety of original burgers to choose from and they are all delicious!

Bold Statement of the review: 360 St. Louis is as close to a Vegas bar as you will get out here in St. Louis...

This place is brand new, has great views, and has a modern feel to it.  There is outdoor seating available where you can pretty much see all around downtown!  

I've been here quite a few times with coworkers and although the drinks and food are pricier than other bars in the area, the food is actually pretty tasty.  I've never had to pay cover, but then again I am going during the week so I'm not sure if there's cover on the weekends!

Food: This is more of a tapas-style (small plate) restaurant/bar, where you are probably going to want to order a few dishes to share.  I've tried the short ribs, Korean BBQ pork tacos, mussels, lobster rolls, pizza, and baby lamb ribs.  Nothing really stood out, but I would recommend that you save the money and pass on the lobster rolls.

Drinks: I haven't had any of cocktails that they have here, but they have a large beer selection (6 on tap, ~10+ in bottles)

I believe they have the ability to accommodate large parties, because I saw a section roped off one of the times I went. 

Overall, I believe this is the new spot to be in St. Louis, especially during gamedays.  It does get cold/windy up on the roof if you're outside, so be sure to bring a light jacket or something to keep you warm!
Lovely coffee shop with delicious breakfast sandwich. I want to come back and work my way through the panini menu!

I am going to have to Agree with all who have said good things about this place. It is well worth the wait, the money, the parking sucking to be in a place that cares what they are serving- and know why they are serving it. Great wine list and beer selections ! I'd reccomend you try it anytime.

Fun lounge, except on $2 draft night, buy bottled beer. They bring out the draft rejects on $2 night. Sent back two beers and had to buy a 3rd, even though they continued to taste odd. Girl with pink hair is a sweetheart, She is why this gets 3 stars. Decor is fun too.
Either you are open till closing time or give up. Every time I go there within 30 min of closing they are out of dishes and not making anymore. Bad service.

Arizona Inn is an oasis in the desert, the only sounds I heard were the grounds keepers meticulously caring for the lush flowers, trees & grass that meanders trough this unique experience.

You can wander around and find yourself playing ping pong or relaxing at the pool with the trees tickling you with their shade.  The Library and dinning room wrap you in an air of casual sophistication.

This Island in the clouds is all about service and attention to detail, and shame on you if you do not take the time to embrace the historical significance of this location.

Please enjoy.
This place is great. It's great for everyone. We are vegetarians, and eat a spread every time we come to Tequila's. The rice and beans are so flavorful and their food is so fresh. Highly recommend.
Great local place to dine in and enjoy some good Chinese food!! The food is constantly good and the service is great!!

A little piece if heaven on earth! I have ventured from the tacos on their menu and still found it to be amazing! What a great addition to Mass Ave. I am thankful for the great service I have always received here, and the delicious Margs of course. Get the pitcher instead of just a glass, they make them better that way! You can not visit here without filling up on some queso or quac before your tacos either! I wish they had outside seating, but they have a nice area to enjoy a drink and nice ledge to lean on :)

We used to order from this location at least 2-3 times a month. The last several times we ordered the food was terrible. The thin crust was stuck to the box, veggies floating in grease, bacon was gristly just terrible! Even the regular crust that normally has such a great taste was hard and tasteless. I tried to tell the store multiple times but they never corrected the issues. We had Parmesan bread bites that were equivalent to small rocks. I even ordered a salad and wings from them. They sent the wrong salad with the wrong dressing. The wings were worse than what you could get at checkers. They were tiny and not even a full order. We ordered 8 but received 6. The last time we ordered the owner by the name of Anthony called to apologize. He stated that he put a credit on my account. I called to use it but the manager said he never put that credit there. I tried to call his number and left s message but he did not return my call. We decided to never order from this location again. We now pick up dominos from another location if we want dominoes. I just ordered 5 large pizzas on Monday and picked them up. I will not patronize this location ever again!

Good Food, Not So Friendly Service

We were visiting Santa Barbara and saw the Yelp reviews for Los Agaves and wanted to give this restaurant a try. This place was crowded and the tables are on a first come first serve basis. We were afraid we wouldn't get a table so we ordered to go. The cashier told us we should have called in our order and we told her we didn't know it was so busy and she said, "we're always busy" in a rude way.

I suppose if you were a local you would know that, but we were from out-of-town. It left a sour taste in our mouth, but we paid and waited and waited. After about 25 minutes we got our food. There were tables opening up, but by that time we were so annoyed that we just wanted to leave.

The food was good, but the bad service wasn't worth it.
A 2 hour+ wait for a to go order. Absolutely absurd behavior! This place is awful, steer clear!

The experience was very rushed and lacking. My son ordered a chicken sandwich that only had a little piece of chicken on each side the sandwich was only about 3 inches and cut in half. The bread was wheat and hard. The sandwich alone was pricey nothing came on the side, we ordered chips on the side which shot the price for the very lacking meal over 8 dollars. The restaurant was very tiny we sat near the register and had a line of people standing over us trying to order their meal. We had to shuffle around other people to get our own drinks and condiments. The iced tea was hot. I'd suggest running the line of people  to the side rather than down the center of people trying to enjoy their meal. Our meal was pricey and the eggs were over cooked. We had high hopes.
Love Hawkers with what it is.  The service is always great and the food is fun.  Sit at the bar for great service.
Great calzones.great pizza. Ordered double cheese large pizza. Very generous in size and toppings.

Came here rather than wait in line at Acme. Right across the street. 

We were seated as soon as we walked up. Oysters were delicious (pretty salty, but delicious) & the gumbo was GREAT. Would recommend.
Falda steak was perfectly cooked and was amazing. Ceviche is a must have. Everything was perfect down to the frosted beer mugs

So I actually told myself that I was gonna write a review for this place as soon as I got finished eating their food because the experience was so great, but I could barely stay awake after eating all of that lovely deliciousness. 

Let's start at the beginning. We randomly saw this place for the very first time a week or two ago on 'New Places to Try' here on Yelp and we wanted to try it. Badly. The only thing that stopped us that day was a Yelp picture of an insanely packed house on a Friday night. Next thing we know, we're getting an email saying that Caplinger's was #1 per Yelp. Well, they were absolutely valid in that deduction. 

We walked into Caplinger's and every seat had a bottom in it, so immediately we knew we were placing a to-go order. We walked past beautifully cut filets of super fresh fish as we made our way to the counter to order. I already knew exactly what I was ordering since I've been trying to find a lobster roll in Indianapolis for... well... too long. We ordered our food, and while we waited, several things happened. Every single employee was friendly, happy and even made us genuinely laugh a few times. Then we perused the refrigerators and cases spotting the most gigantic tiger shrimp and the freshest yellowfin tuna. There were even a few exotic items to be found. Then, the ever-so-pleasant employees offered us some samples of their storemade wares. Everything we sampled was delicious, but the smoked tuna salad was divine!

We got our food and sped home to eat. All you could hear throughout our house was, "Mmmm...", "You GOTTA taste this!" "Try this sauce!" So good.

You would be doing yourself a great disservice by not trying out this awesome little spot. It's a little pricey, but you get the incredible quality that you pay for. Oh! And don't forget to try the pineapple bread pudding -- served warm and over  custard!

Love, Love, Love this place. 

We have been to Phili several times a year for the past few years & this place is always on our list. I'm not  a beer drinker, but they have Lindemans Framboise on draft- that's all I need- plus they do have other ETOH drinks available. You MUST try the dijon mussels- they were highly recommended by the bartender & they are the best mussels I have ever had.

You gotta try this place on the weekend. There are dishes they only serve on Saturday and Sunday and they're worth trying. There's even items they only offer on Sundays! I love authentic Mexican food!
The Gringa is loaded with meat and cheese and goes really well with the smoky chipotle sauce they provide on every table. All of the sauces are really tasty. The tomatillo one has some bite but nothing was overly spicy. 
The Frijoles Charros Black Bean soup has good flavor and decent chunks of bacon and chorizo sausage but very little broth so it's more like a chili. It also had a LOT of black beans which is quite filling. I only ate half cuz I had ordered a main dish as well and wanted to enjoy it. It will be good with rice as a leftover though! Some think it's on the spicy side but I thought it offered a good amount of burn. My dinner date had the Tortilla Soup and finished it. There was a good amount of tortillas and cream in the soup. Make sure you ask for it piping hot! We seriously considered the Pozole soup which is only available on Sunday and I regret not ordering it now. 
I also wanted to order the appetizer Chiccaron de Queso which is a huge cheese chip with guacamole. After we ordered we saw how big the cheese chip was and realized it would be better shared with 4 people instead of just two.
The atmosphere is bright and inviting. I heard that the owners also own the Mexican grocery store at the opposite end of the strip mall. That makes sense and I totally support using produce and/or ingredients from their store in the restaurant. I actually think it makes a lot of sense. 
The restaurant is right beside an Adult Entertainment store which wasn't appealing to my date but such is life. The parking is also quite limited and can be difficult. If you're there in the evening at least you can park in stalls that are dedicated for other businesses that are closed.

Ate at the bar.  Completely over-priced paella at $28; it was sitting in too much rice water and the whole thing tasted like it came out of a can.  The waitstaff talked among themselves most of the time and were otherwise stand-offish.  Apparently one-off tourist visits keep the place going.

I have been at Public Markets all over the world, London, Mexico City, New York, Florence, and many, many others. 

I love going because it's very easy to get a feel of the place you are visiting, and what is important to them. Food is alive, artisanal, fresh, tried and true. A marriage of tradition and innovation.

Low and behold... the tremendous disappointment the Santa Barbara Public Market was. All the employees I interacted with, did not crack a smile, clearly not the owners (one would hope) nonetheless a lack of interest in their work.

Two of the venues had "run out" of what their specialty was at noon... they opened at 10:00, and there was not a lot of people. 

I am giving it two stars, because it was clean, and Rori's Ice Cream has one of the most delicious root beer flavor ever.

But you can skip the whole thing, if you want  a reliable, and polite experience.

Location of this restaurant is in a new building and very spacious and clean.
Service was great and actually had an opportunity to add a comment with Daniel, the manager/ cook.
Tried several items, fish ceviche tostada and the two taco, one fish one shrimp combo plate.
Both were excellent!
Also the home brewed iced tea and basket of fresh chips were both exceptional..
Great food, good friendly service and very affordable ...

I am a big fan of this place. I've been twice now-- once just to purchase a couple of bottles to-go, and then again for a multiple-bottle get together with friends. They have a great selection of low-moderately priced wines which are positioned along the wall. In addition they have wines by the glass and an assortment of snacks/cheese/charcuterie. You can open a tab, or just pay up front at the bar. There are friendly folks there to open your wine, serve you glasses, and bring your snacks to the table. They also are apparently the only ones who can physically remove the bottle from the wall (some weird law). I think what impresses me the most about this place is the fact that I can actually buy a bottle of wine at an extremely reasonable price (read: $10-15), and open it and drink it there. My only criticism is that the ambience is a bit echo-ey, and perhaps the decor could be softened a bit with more comfortable chairs and dimmer lights in the evening, but this is just a suggestion. It would also be nice for them to have a printed list of their wines by the bottle with pricing, to make it a bit easier to sort through, though I imagine this list changes often. I will be back for sure!

Beautiful restaurant. The food was okay. The service was bad. It was very empty (maybe 4-5 other tables tops). The server assistant was pleasant and refilled our water several times. Kept saying that our server will be with us "soon". Our server never came so the manager took our order. 10 mins later our "server" asked if we had ordered yet. He was apologetic but didn't offer to help us with anything else. When the food finally came out our burgers were not cooked the way we had asked and it took so long that we were afraid if we said something it would be another 30 mins. Getting the check took way too long. We were really looking forward to eating here... Sad that we probably won't be returning.

Came here as a pseudo-celebration now that the wife can drive again after a month off!  We were in the mood for tater-tots but did not want to have to drive all the way past the Philadelphia Airport for the best tots we've ever had, so a search for tater tots showed Yelp giving us Steam.  We were very happy with the restaurant!

We were here for an early lunch about 11:30am on an off-from-work President's day.  Only one other couple was in the brightly lit place (right next to the tracks...an old railroad car, maybe?)  Long and skinny with lots of TVs, very long bar, and nice wood floors with a lot of tables and a few booths.  Bathrooms are plenty and to the end on the left of the facility.  The place overall seemed clean, but I ended up remembering my days as a dishwasher many years ago and smelling the cleaning products used over the smells of the really good food.

We had too much to eat, but all of it was very good!  Started with the tots plain which were nice and crisp, and did not have an overdone grease taste or smell to them.  They went fast.  We also had a hummus platter which included a scoop (I'm pretty certain these were not scratch made) of three types of hummus on a platter of plenty of pita bread, and very fresh vegetables of roasted red pepper, nice long slices of cucumber, olives, and cheese.  This was very good, too.

Wife had a Caesar salad which was average, and she thought the dressing was not tasting like Caesar that much.  She also had a tomato/mozzarella flatbread which mostly went home with us.  She said it was extremely tasty with the balsamic drizzle on it.  I went with the signature burger medium rare which was awesome.  It came with fries or a side salad which you can upcharge to a "premium" salad which is what I did.  The Chop-Chop salad was great with a nice dressing with oranges, candied nuts, and I subbed goat cheese for feta.  

Again, we ate too much and brought some home with us for later.  Service was really nice and friendly.

With two Cokes (yea!) the bill came to about $60 for two.  A Yelp Check-In got us 10% off if we ended up sending $40 which we did easily.

Very happy with Steam.  Happy hour 4-6pm M-F, and they are starting a Sunday Brunch in a couple of weeks.  

We'll be coming back!

We only hung out outside and had a few beers (brewed by Ulele) but I was pleasantly surprised by the vibe. Everything I heard about this place made me believe it was going to upscale but when we spent the afternoon walking up and down the river, we were thirsty. We walked down the stairs to Ulele and into paradise. We sat outside under a rather large umbrella and enjoyed a flight of beer. The Wedding Beer and the Black Cherry Lager were two favorites. The outdoor bartender was very helpful and accommodating. I am definitely looking forward to brining out of town guests here in the next couple of weeks and I will be pursuing the menu until then!

I love coming to the outdoor patio to enjoy some great Mexican fare and margaritas. They have a sunset happy hour between 4-7 with some good specials on wine, beer and Margaritas. The service is always great and Ive always enjoyed my meals. Not sure if it's the tequila talking but everything always tastes great!

When I went to Belmont a few years back, I used to come here all the time.  It's so convenient to the college, and its a perfect place to grab some coffee or tea and do your homework.  They have free Wi Fi even if you're just into relaxing with a warm beverage and updating your brand of social networking site.  I think every group project meeting I had in college either started or ended at Bongo Java.  

They're not just about delicious and unique coffee and tea drinks, Bongo Java also serves up some tasty treats.  I love their fresh bagels for breakfast, and you can get bagel sandwiches all day.  Everything just tastes fresh and there's something about a cup of their coffee and a breakfast sandwich to start your day with.  An added bonus is they serve organic and fair trade coffees and are veggie friendly.

Don't let its popularity with the college kids scare you away.  Bongo Java is a hit with the entire neighborhood.  Drop in and you'll find people picking up a beverage on their way to the office or on their lunch break and neighborhood moms grabbing a caffeine fix before running errands as well as the college students across the way.  

I love their front patio, its one of my favorites in Nashville.  Belmont Boulevard is a little quieter than a lot of the neighboring streets and its very relaxing to kick back with a book or my laptop and enjoy my coffee in peace.

"Have a side of burger with your fries", or something like that is their moto. Which is pretty accurate.
This is a burger/fry place, but the lead is the fries. They offer many different types of potatoes (Russet, Yukon, some purple kind, and many others, and have them cut in various styles to (shoestring, regular, curly, etc).
There are several sauces (sauce bar) to accompany the fries.
Then the burgers. They offer beef, bison, turkey, and I believe a vegan option. The burgers were on the small side (fries the centerpiece), but very good.
We called in an order here for 8 people (business lunch) last week. We arrived 10 minutes early, and the place was just getting busy. The only critisism is that there were only 2 guys manning the place. One taking orders, and 1 cooking. as it got closer to noon, the place filled up, and they were swamped.
Our order was ready 5-10 minutes after the specified time (no biggie), but when I had to add on a last minute order, I had to wait in line, to order it, and then wait for the order, it was 30 minutes.
Not their fault, just think they should have another body there.
So in closing. Great place to get your fry groove on. Try the burgers, and the sauces too.

Authentic, Fresh, Homemade
We had a fantastic experience. From the lightly battered and fried smelt to the Tiramisu, this place was first class all the way. The smelt was light and flavorful. These are one of my favorites and they certainly did not disappoint. My son had spaghetti and meatballs and said the meat balls were delicious and way better than mine. I had the Puttanesca. It was spicy and just, well,  perfect. The chef served it with a side of his homemade spicy olive oil so I could add more heat. We finished the meal with the Tiramisu which was exquisite.

We appreciated the personal touch. This is a one man show folks...personal service from the chef and then he makes the meals to order. Although, this place is so good he may need to invest in some extra help soon!!!!! 

This was a great experience. He's doing it right...

Update
We are in last night and everyone had an amazing meal. The portions were excellent- enough to take home for lunch next day. Curry sauce was delicious. Best Thai food I've had since moving from Philadelphia and probably better.

This was my neighborhood grocery store for many years.  And then I moved away.  But I love to visit when I'm in the area.  The store has a clean and well organized layout, with a great selection of natural and bulk foods, and the friendliest checkers of any markets in town.  Shopping at the right times can help with the price points for produce and quality meats.  Sometimes it's the customer service that makes all the difference.  One of my most favorite checkers moved on to bigger and better things.  And another of my fave checkers, infamously known as Doc, has been counting his days to retirement for years.  He's funny and helpful, and seems to know the store like the palm of his hand.  Even if his line is busier than others, he's worth the wait!

I love this place. I have never dined-in, as my office is very close, but the breakfast is perfect for what I like. I always get the fresh fruit of the day (love) and sunny-side-up eggs with a dry English muffin and a small coffee. Yes, I could make all of these items at home and take them to work with me, but it's just so much nicer to have someone else make it for you so that you just walk in and pick up your delicious breakfast that's waiting for you. Yum, Sunrise Café!

So it saddens me because the food and service are usually good. I got the pork chops which came with a spoon full of mashed potatoes, my son got chicken and waffles which came with three small strips of chicken. My wife got the salmon which came out with a vegetable that was unidentifiable. My other son's burger was wet from all of the cheese and the bun fell apart. The waitress was okay but the overall experience was negative. The appetizers were average at best. All this for $96.00. Not worth it. #lackluster

Was so excited to try a new Gerard Craft restaurant! We had reservations on Valentine's Day but due to the weather had to cancel. We ended up going for lunch on my birthday. Woof. 

Pros: the space is nice, would be lovely to sit out on the patio during warm weather. Staff was very friendly and accommodating.

Cons: $100 for one appetizer, two cocktails and two very sad sandwiches. I get that this is the Four Seasons and I was prepared for that, but nothing about the meal made it worth that much. Mediocre at best. Got the lobster roll with the saddest piece of charred gluten free bread on my request. Husband got the coconut shrimp roll and said it was all bread and he's had better coconut shrimp at Red Lobster.  Cocktails and chips and dip appetizer were both just ok, flavors on everything overall were lackluster. Just expected a lot more from a Gerard Craft creation. We went directly to Ted Drewes and eased our disappointment with custard.

The chair tables could be more eating friendly. Love the drink (I can be a lush when baby free). Seats are comfortable, and nothing beats reserved seating, hence no line. Food is acceptable, satisfying.
So happy to find out Pho Garden was open for takeout during Covid!!! Their pho is a huge portion and so delicious every time.

Best burger in Boise.  I've tried smash burger and Boise fry company and 5 guys smokes them!  The burger tastes like a in and out burger - only better!  The try's are better other places but the meat on the burgers here is the best.  Their buns suck though..  Or rather nothing special about them.  Again, best burger in Idaho.

I've only been here for the lunch buffet but the food has always been delicious and fresh. I believe it is about $11.50 for lunch.. There are many different sushi options as well as hot foods such as chicken, fried rice and egg rolls. They also have a hibachi stand at the end of the buffet line which is included with your lunch buffet where you can request different meats or vegetables to be made. I also like that there is a worker constantly watching the buffet line to swap out the trays so you never have to worry about something being sold out, and you can see that it is constantly coming out of the kitchen freshly made. If you like sushi/japanese then this is a great lunch spot for you.
I rarely post reviews on any social media, but this place is lit! I came with 2 friends. We ordered 4 dishes but ended having to bring home a portion because the dishes were full of food!!

Our family enjoys coming here for the sliders and donuts and we've loved everything we've tried (especially the pork belly slider).  They even have parking. It was no surprise that our 14-year old daughter wanted their donuts for her birthday treat at school.  Not only were the donuts delicious (s'mores, glazed) and a major hit with the other 8th graders, but the folks at District went above and beyond to make them for her.  Melissa and the front of the house staff were fantastic.  They went through hoops to get them done in time with absolutely no sacrifice to quality. It is not often that a restaurant will make this kind of effort.  We were big fans before but this has taken it to a whole new level.  I would highly recommend it to anyone - an excellent place to eat!

This place is so good I had to start writing my review before I left. 

When you walk in, you're greeted by a 30-foot salad bar. They have premixed salads--the Asian wonton one was one of the best salads I've ever had--and also a wide variety of lettuces, veggies, and dressings to make your own. I did both. At the register I asked if I could go back through again (rookie question). You can--it's a buffet dummy--and the question prompted them to give me a free bag of cookies and a 15% off coupon since it was my first time. 

This place isn't just a salad bar, though that's what they advertise on the exterior. They also have Italian-restaurant-quality pasta and some great soups and bread. Ice cream too.

The layout is spacious and well decorated, and the windows allow for some great lighting.

I'm blown away at the variety of tastes and all of the options. The hot food was perfectly warm and the salad was cold and crisp. I thought I'd need a quick turn around meal when I got home--I like to devour--but I left feeling more than full.

The GM, Michelle, even came over over to my table. Apparently the word was out that I was a newbie. She asked me some friendly questions and we had a brief convo. The quick exchange and obvious appreciation for my first-time visit felt like a small-town restaurant, so welcoming. 

I'll be back, especially w the 15% discount. You gotta check this place out if you like buffets. I haven't been to a better one.
Best tacos in Tampa Bay! Don't let the hype of Taco Bus fool you..... Casita is the REAL DEAL!

Everything at this buffet was average at best. We came here on New Year's Eve because there was strangely nothing else open on the casino floor. Rim and the steakhouse were both only open for prix fixe dinners that day, and CPK was closed as per usual. So since there was actually no line, we decided to give it a try, and my mom even got a 20% senior discount!

However, everything in terms of the food spread was less than desirable. It had your usual stations - carving, salad, Asian, Mexican, Americana, dessert/fruit, etc. Some of the more exciting options included eggs benedicts on individual mini skillets, a pho noodle soup station, and a burrito/asada bar. But as far as the actual taste, there wasn't anything that had me clamoring for seconds. I think the best thing I had was coconut shrimp, which, well...either says a lot about this buffet or about my standards. You can decide for yourself.

Unbelievable value and  great tasting food
My steak was cooked medium rare as requested  fried Rice was excellent
Try  the spicy rice soup  too good 
Attentive  friendly service
They messed up our order and the food seemed a little bland. Maybe it was just a bad night. I'll definitely give it another go and post an updated review
I ordered a pasta online and when I came to pick it up they did not have the toppings needed for my dish. It was an okay pasta.

It always bites when you don't have family to spend Thanksgiving with, but that's the position I was in.  I called up a friend and asked them if they would fancy going to Boston Market.

We arrived about 1:30pm, and there was no line. We both ordered the Thanksgiving Day promotion which was: Turkey or chicken, 2 sides, 1 cornbread, 1 dessert pie.  They were all out of pumpkin pie. 

We both got the turkey. It was horrid. Tried the beans and potatoes. Horrid. 

Both of our meals tasted like they had been refrigerated for hours and then served straight out of it.  Obviously, it wasn't but it reflects about how cold they were.  Bloody hell.

I would be giving it 1 star; however, I thought the decor of the place was decent. Good colors and a slight sense of warmth in there. 

Not sure if our experience was in relation to the holiday, but it will not be on my list next year if I am in similar circumstances.

What a shame.
Very Good Ice cream.....on par with Handel's...but with indoor seating.

I was here in business and checked this place out for dinner. I actually visited this place twice in 2 days as I missed my flight home due to work. They have a great beer selection and full bar. I had a salad with grilled chicken which was pretty tasty. The service was greAt during both visits. I'll be back again if I'm ever in town for work. Great little pub.

This place is terrific! We flew in today from So Cal and thought we would just bit the bullet and test the mexican food in Boise on our first night! Pueblo Lindo did not disappoint!! 
The Chili Relleno and Carne Asada taco were terrific, as was the Carne Asada Burrito my hubby had. We will definitely come back on our next visit to town!!

I've never been one to finish a spring roll because I haven't really found one I like, but my search is over!! Their springs rolls are the best I've ever had! I had 2 but probably could've eaten all four on the plate! My boyfriend and I have been searching for a new Thai restaurant since moving from Muncie. Thai Spice is our new spot! He's a huge spice fan and he said the medium was perfect spice for him! I, however, am a spice whimp but quite enjoyed the mild! I highly recommend Thai Spice!

Four stars for price. 
I drive truck, so I've eaten bbq all over America. This place is better than most, but it's certainly not 4 star worthy. I'd say the food is more like 2.5 star. 
The cheeseburger was quite large and the meat was tasty. (Be advised: if you don't stop them they'll automatically put that disgusting invention called mayonnaise on it.) I got it plain so I can't comment on their lettuce/tomato game. 
The pork bbq sammich was soggy on the bottom. Moist is good, but this was just plain wet. The meat itself was bland but not bad. 
The bbq sauce is pretty good but not great. 
The Mac & Cheese tasted ok but the noodles were way overcooked. It'd be much better if it were baked and had a little crustiness to it. 

If I lived local I'm sure I'd come here occasionally.

I was in Tucson for the holidays and my wife and I decided we wanted to eat Thai food. Not knowing Tucson very well, we obviously Yelped it and found this place with good reviews. We ordered some very basics: pineapple fried rice (w/ chicken and shrimp) and pad thai. And that is where the goodness ended.

Problem #1: It cost $25 for two people to eat the most basic and cheapest food on the menu! Having eaten at many Thai restaurants around the country, this is easily the most expensive Thai I have had. Why though?!?

Problem #2: the food was not flavorful at all! The temperature of the food was fine, but the first bite was soooo bland, and of both dishes. My wife and I took a few more bites (thinking it just needed time to settle in), yet nothing changed. I immediately went to the pantry and found some spices that got the food to doable. But, man oh man, it was not good food as prepared. My wife didn't even finish her Pad Thai.

Problem #3: yes, it is takeout and no dine in (which is a bummer; one which I blame our gov't for). That was no the problem though, because they can do nothing about gov't regulations. However, we had to stand outside and wait for our food. This would not normally be a problem, but it was winter and cool with a breeze. I would have preferred that 4 Seasons had a covering or a outdoor curtain to help cut the wind because their customers have to stand outside.

All in all, this was not the most awful experience, but definitely far from great or even good. I think the prices just need to come down, the food needs more flavor, and the outside needs a covering.

Next time I am in Tucson and craving Thai, I will try some where else.

What a great new addition to Old City. Great ice cream, water ice AND kettle corn. It's nice to have a place that's not a 30 minute wait and cash only. 
We absolutely love the ice cream flavors, especially the Cookie Monster and the salty caramel. They pair nicely with a scoop of water ice - especially mango flavor. 

The kettle corn is a go to when traveling and giving as a present, definitely a crowd pleaser. 

Cannot wait until their full kitchen opens

Delicious pizza, AWESOME calzones!
They usually have coupons in the menu too, which is a bonus...

I have, on more than one occasion, gotten there after I called an order for pick up and it hasn't been made. They turned it around FAST though. Easily the best pizza in the area.

Sort of a theme restaurant - If you like going to the planet hollywood/hard rock cafe of oysters, then this is your place!!

Upscale and Fun.

Stopped in after a day at the beach for snacks. Had a couple beers at their outside seating and shared three apps. The calamari was lightly breaded and crisp, not overdone like many places. The crab cake was excellent, loaded with claw and lump meat with just enough breading to bind. I was particularly impressed with the Drunken shrimp as this is almost always a fail, but the shrimp were perfectly blackened and the garlic butter sauce demanded the bread served with it to sop it up. Service was friendly and efficient. Will be back soon!

Visiting family from DC and picked Mai Thai from an article I came across. I was particularly impressed that, while I'm not one, they have a whole vegan menu. We had a party of 6 and while I had a reservation confirmation, they didn't have it in their system. No problem though, because they flawlessly threw tables together and invited us into the dining room right away. We ordered the wings and fried chickpeas and both were great. Then came entrees. I got the half duck which was INCREDIBLE. I also got Garlic Noodles (no protein) to share for the table which were DIVINE. Seriously I almost ate all of both entrees. The lamb curry my brother got had a WHOLE lamb shank in it! My mom and SIL got the pad Thai and asked for a 1 for spicy (least spice) but had to send it back because it was really hot (like, not a 1). Overall, I was genuinely impressed by this place. I didn't know what to expect as a big city girl, but can say this would run circles around a lot of places in DC. The food quality and presentation plus the customer service made this one of my favorite restaurants in Boise.

Delicious oyster and shrimp po boys! They are huge so two people can easily split one but very yum and the first po boy I had here! Place is a little convenient store so seating and is cash only so just be aware of that but good place off the beaten path

Our first visit to the place went ok. It wasn't great, but it was ok. There is not enough seating in the place, but the service was ok. The second time we went the one employee bringing the food was extremely unfriendly and acted inconvenienced by the order being wrong. A group of customers came in and basically took over the place, where in turn my 11-month-old was practically assaulted by one of their kids. The establishment didn't care and neither did the parents. My basic take on the place was if you didn't look like them, then you weren't really welcome. We won't be going back!

I dined here with two friends for the first time yesterday, and I was not disappointed.  Even though it was lunch buffet hours, they had no problem allowing us to order from the dinner menu.  We had Vegetable Samosas (this comes with a trio of dips that were all delicious), Chicken Makhani, and Vegetable Korma with some garlic cheese naan (omg!).  Everything was extremely flavorful and had the perfect spice level (we ordered 3/5).  We all ate a ton and still had quite a bit of food to take home from that!  

Our server, Akram, was a pure joy and was so accommodating during our lunch.  We will definitely be putting this in our regular rotation.  Two thumbs up!

Amazingly delicious tacos. Being from Arizona, I'm glad to recently see some palatable Mexican restaurant  pop up in the city. This just happens to be one of them. The happy hour here is killer with $4 nachos and $2 taco Tuesdays. Coupled with the $4 beers and margaritas you seriously can't miss with this one. Fishtown in starting to be a Mexican culinary destination, which is exciting. If you are looking for satisfying cheap eats, this is a winner every time.

This housed in the Overland Hacienda building on Woodson Rd.

I have been here many times. The food is usually super fast and always delicious.

My go to meals are the steak tacos with flour tortilla. If I'm feeling like I need to add some good old fashioned fat and cholesterol to my diet I go with the Macho Chimichanga.  If you're a cheese lover...add some extra cheese. DELICIOUS!!!! You can regret it later but you will savor the moment.

Unfortunately I vannot comment on the margaritas.  Never had one here.

Eh, this place is OK. I only really like the guava/cheese empanadas and those were quite off the other day when I got them.

I won't be back. West Tampa Sandwich Shop makes a much better guava/cheese empanada than these people.

The service here was terrible. We came in for dinner around 7:00 and were one of the only parties in the restaurant. Our waitress hardly checked on us and we had to wait over ten minutes to simply ask for a bottle of ketchup after our food came out. The food is simply mediocre, basic bar food. The live music was a nice touch.

The food is mostly soups, sandwiches, salads, bagels, rolls, muffins, cookies, and bread. Everything is usually fresh. My favorite are the tuna sandwich, French onion soup, bravo bacon club. They miss a star because the portions are small, have inaccurate orders a d the price is a little high. Also,  the drinks Re are tasty.

Maybe I went on the wrong day, but I was underwhelmed with Middle Child. I stopped by on a Saturday for a takeout breakfast sandwich and was told it would be about a 25 minute wait because of how busy it was. I was totally fine with this.

I ordered a breakfast sandwich off their menu. They were out of potato rolls (what it's supposed to come on) so I went with oat toast.

When I finally got my sandwich, 45 minutes later, it was laden with grease. I'm assuming they butter the toast on both sides before toasting, and I really wasn't a fan. The eggs were decent but a little on the salty side. And, the cooper sharp was served in an overwhelming amount.

Honestly, I'd try this place again but won't go near that breakfast sandwich. Maybe something else ok the menu is better?

Horrible service! the bartender was sooo rude when I asked for a Bud Light. This is St. Louis home of AB headquarters right? 

The service couldn't have been any slower. It was a busy night and the bartenders had NO sense of urgency. also poured their drinks extremely weak.

Food was terrible! The spinach dip had obviously been scraped off the bottom of a burnt pan . Big black crusty , burnt chunks. Completely inedible. And wasn't taken off my bill.

Just an all around horrible excuse for bar/restaurant.
Having lived for almost a decade in DC, the land of steakhouses, I can tell you that Bern's is the best there is. Great value, experience, steak, and wine

Celebrating my 52nd Birthday here was absolutely enjoyable!  The service was phenomenal throughout the entire evening.  My girlfriends and I enjoyed the attentiveness of the bartender as we enjoyed drinks while waiting for the rest of our party to arrive.  I was so happy to see our table had birthday decorations on it!  My appetizer and entree selections were perfect & delectable.   I chose the Crab Cakes, Lobster Mac & Cheese, and Brussel Sprouts, paired with Rose', resulting in the perfect combination.  The finishing touch was the mouth watering Bread Pudding!  I am looking forward to returning again soon!

My family and I ate here tonight for the first time in over a year, and unfortunately the experience will not induce us to return anytime soon. The atmosphere is pleasant and quiet, and the waitstaff were friendly and attentive. Miso soup's flavor was good, but the pluses end there. They charge for everything, including green tea. A $6 order of gyoza yielded just THREE pieces - deep fried rather than pan fried - and with a dipping sauce that was more suited to bulgogi than gyoza. I understand they do Korean dishes as well, but when I order gyoza I really am looking for gyoza, not small mandu with a sesame-heavy sauce. Pork katsu arrived all in one piece rather than sliced as it would be in Japan or any other Japanese restaurant I've ever eaten in. Vegetable tempura was good, but a bit on the heavier side (and no, just because it's fried does not mean it has to be heavy) and at $13 pretty expensive for 9 pieces of fried veg. The staff seemed like really nice people, and the food wasn't bad, just mediocre. However, the lackluster food combined with what feel like disproportionately high prices will keep us away in future.

Called the day before we teachers wanted to put in a delivery order to double check that they deliver to our school. The next morning, we call to place our order and they tell us they're too busy to deliver and that they don't deliver to our school anyway. Spoke to the manager and she still wouldn't make it right. JJ's lost quite a bit of business as we'll be ordering from Lenny's the rest of the school year instead.

My wife and I were actually en route to a different establishment when I stubble across the Yelp page for this establishment. Based on the reviews and awesome pictures we decided to give it a try.
Of course due to COVID things are different. We had no wait for service but based on how good the food is once things start to normalize this is a place where no matter the wait I would still come. As far as customer service it was very refreshing how patient the front counter hostess was with my wife and I. She was generous with her time by answering all of our questions and was super nice.
We order 4 pork belly bowls and 1 shrimp bowl. Unfortunately I did not get a chance to take a photo of the shrimp bowl prior to my favorite devouring his meal. Needless to say it was really good by his account. He had the egg noodles which had a savory butter like sauce with it which alone made this really good. He added their "orange sauce" which amplified the great flavors. As for the pork belly it was sooooo tender and full of flavor. The pork belly looked like it was caramelized on a flat top and seasoned with a simple salt and pepper combo. I had the lee sauce on the side which added another layer of flavor.
Overall I will definitely come back to this place. Their food and customer service warrants another visit or two, three lol. Especially during this pandemic please help our small business owners such as this place.

I have been going to this location since it opened. At first it was a great experience. Busy, loud, plenty of good seafood served quickly and with a lot of energy. But in the last year, it has really gone down hill. The last time I went with friends and the service was just awful. It was so bad that for only the 2nd time in my life, I left no tip. That was a few months ago. I went back tonight with my free appetizer coupon that was given to me by the manager because there were so many mistakes with our orders. The restaurant was less than 33% full. The appetizer was cold and inedible. The server was nice and attentive but the food was just ok. The "melted butter" that went with my crab was some sort of clear oily liquid. It's really too bad. I had high hopes for this place. I think I'm done with Joe's.

My local go to for take out. Today I wanted to celebrating the Lunar New Year, so I ordered a ton of food that I plan to eat all weekend. 

I got steamed dumplings and fried scallops (so good!)  for appetizers, then the lunch specials of curry shrimp, kung pao chicken, and boneless spareribs. Lunch specials have choice of either white or fried rice, and soup, egg roll or a can of soda. So I got hot & sour and wonton soups.

The curry shrimp was a new one for me, not a ton of shrimp (5?)  but really nice retty large ones, and a lot of zing to the curry. The hubs particularly enjoyed that one. The kung pao and boneless spareribs are something  I order frequently. The hot and sour soup here I really like. I also like the rice noodles with shrimp; those shrimp are a little smaller but plentiful.  The amount of food for the price is abundant. 

#yum #ReviewsByRL

Good was pretty good. Terrible service however. Our server, Leslie took a while to greet us and wasn't the most pleasurable.
