Had to ask twice for her to bring my sons apple juice & my order was brought to me incorrectly. It was kind of busy but not enough to be as flustered as she seemed. Hopefully she can receive some additional training & tips to improve.

The sangria's are sad today I don't know who bar tending but between their sad ass drinks and the waitresses non friendly approach to her job I hope the food tonight makes up for the fails that I am encountering thus far. Not to mention so far looking at the table top bill they are attempting to charge me for two soft drinks I clearly didn't order foh with that shit. This will be a evening of the No Tip For You.

And omg the food first time around made me want to get up and just walk out. They cooked the food wrong even after taking the order and the potatoes were drowning in salt in which the manager says oh that's how we season them you should've asked for no salt "really" like I knew they would be bathed in it. I will say after unfortunately complaining they did get things correct but still makes me feel this is no longer the Applebee's for me.
More like a 3.5. It's decent food, reliable but nothing special. I do love their fried rice, but you can't get it as a side for dinner. Go during lunch otherwise it's not worth the price!

After reading some good advice from some fellow Yelpsters, decided to give this place a shot and I am glad I did!  Very clean, friendly atmosphere and food was very good!
My wife and I shared a spinach and cheese calzone that was very good, fresh ingredients set this apart from most other run of the mill pizza joints.  Give this place a try fellow Malvernites!

Having lived in the downtown district for the last 3 years this place is the go-to for pizza. The owner is always at the front desk and genuinely cares about the food that is given out. I'll also say the quality of the pizza is way better then others in the area... 

My go to order is pizza with pepperoni and a side of hot sauce, all good stuff! 

Plenty of room to sit down, it's only street parking but you should be able to find a meter. 

Highly recommend this place, if you're in the area cause you're a student, visiting the aquarium, BB&T center or recently moved then it's a must try.

Always a good crowd in here and for a good reason. The menu has so many great options, they tailor to everyone's needs/allergies. I've had quite a few things here, all in which I've loved. This time we had an awesome waiter named Keenan(sorry if I spelt it wrong). He suggested the magic mushroom latte iced with coconut milk and my god was it good. Not too sweet with that back of coconut, I'll be craving this everyday from now on. Then I asked a few of his favorite thing on the menu cause I was having a hard time deciding: he gave me a bunch of options and gave me some details. I went with the vegan Reuben sandwich (I'm not vegan) wow wow wow so so good absolutely recommend it. From the bread to the Tempe meat and Sauerkraut. All perfectly portioned and flavored. My boyfriend went for the double edge paleo bowl with tri tip. Let's just say he ate it so fast I didn't even get a bite. Over all this place rocks but I have to give a special shout out to our server He made our day and is definitely a special assets to this awesome restaurant.

best burger in new orleans! this place is not a fine dine restaurant so leave your blazer and shoes at home. the decor consists of old ship parts hanging on the wall and a huge fishing net hanging across the ceiling but who cares when you get an insanely delicious burger with a side of loaded mash potatoes and bacon bits! the port of call drink is not great, stick with sweet tea. 

also, lunch on a sunday consisted of a 35 minute wait and it only got longer as the day progressed. by the time we left, the line was out the door. sit at the bar if you're hungry!

I saw most very positive reviews, may be I am not lucky on July 4 th,. Time is not right I guess. Only 3 of us dinned at 3 pm , nothing really taste right, but service is great , send detail to the business mail.  Hope get reply back soon

Crabby cafe has the best scenery for eating a nice seafood dinner! The muscles in the red sauce are so good! And the shrimp and clams are also my favorite especially with the crabby mild sauce, so tasteful and delicious! The bucket packages are great deals when I'm in the mood for different things, like crawfish and shrimp or shrimp and crabs. I always get the fried catfish to start with the Cajun fries and that yum yum sauce that everyone loves! The service is wonderful everyone is so friendly and welcoming, overall this place is definitely somewhere everyone needs to try (:

I hate to do this but I really must...my husband and I went to Lucas for brunch today because the other restaurant we wanted to go to had a hour wait. There was plenty of room at Lucas...now I understand why.  
First off the wait staff was extremely slow and inattentive.  And it wasn't because they were understaffed.  It took an extended amount of time for anyone to even acknowledge our presence.  And then the time between our drink order and actually getting them was ten minutes.  No one came to refill our coffee.  We had to almost trip the waitress from the other table to give us some of hers.
Then when it came time to order our food we were told the oven was broken and our selection was unavailable.  She could have told us that thirty minutes ago...come on!!!  So we chose something else from the menu.
The food was average at best.  The toast was cold and so was the center of my omelet.  My husbands potatoes were undercooked and room temperature.
We have eaten here before for dinner and it was actually pretty good.  But if you're wanting brunch do not go here.  Wait in line at the better places. It'll probably be worth it.
Sorry Lucas
The best food that I have eaten in Indianapolis.  The Price  per value is outstanding and can't be beat in Indy. Thanks for the great meals
This place is the best. High quality food with friendly staff. Best gyro in town. Ask for Ari and tell him I sent you.

I was visiting from Florida and needed a place to eat before I had to head to the airport and found this place on groupon and went. It was so delicious and amazing. I would have paid full price for what I got. The food was out of this world, it was the perfect ending point to a great trip. If I go back to Louisiana I'm definitely coming here again. Loved the food and the spot. Me and my boyfriend couldn't stop raving on how good it was. We told people at the airport to go check it out.

We have been eagerly anticipating the opening of this place at work, since there is not a ton of fast options (McDonalds, BK, etc.) and we weren't disappointed. First - the fries - I could have eaten a whole pound. They were coated in pepper and sooo good. The pasta bowl we got with Alfredo and Breaded chicken - which was also very good - a little small (I was full - but I could see other people not - it was also only $6) and it also came with garlic bread. The other people in my party got roast pork, canolli dip, gelato (definition - water ice) and everyone was happy. 

Downsides - Stuff was a little salty (mostly the sandwich meats), The garlic aoili was more like mayo than anything else, drive thru was a little long (it was the first day)

We will be back.

This location opened up by our house and we were happy to try it. They have assorted old school fords as decor all through the restaurant. It was very busy when we came in around 6 pm on a Thursday. The restaurant was full and a wait was in the lobby.

The staff was friendly and moved quickly to serve the guests. I will say the menu is creative and they offer a lot of variety. Of course, the staple are the burgers. I appreciated the different burgers they had as well. They had unique flavor combinations to them or you could build your own.

I got the estate burger and you can switch out the protein option , so it can cater to vegetarians or pescatarians. I kept it simple and got the regular patty they offer. The burger itself was very flavorful and juicy.

As a side option, it comes with standard fries or you can upgrade. I decided to upgrade to truffle fries. I was a little disappointed they didn't have sweet potato fries (they do have tots but tots make me think of elementary school lunch.) I was underwhelmed by the truffle fries. They were just regular fries with Parmesan sprinkled. I got no truffle taste and the portion was small for how much extra it is. 

Other wise I think this will be a place I will come back to again, but come at an off time!

Went here recently with co-workers. Every Mexican restaurant usually gives out salsa and chips when seated, well not here. When I asked about the salsa and chips the waiter was nice enough to bring some out anyway. However, the salsa was no more than cut up tomatoes, like the dice tomatoes that come in a can, but worst because it was so dried out. The prices were a little high for the amount and quality of food. Check out senor salsa not too far away! It had great food and prices!

Two coworkers and me went after work we arrived about 8 pm. Only a couple people eating.   We ordered our margaritas and it took awhile to get them. But the margaritas were amazing!!  We each had one. We ordered our food and that took forever also. Not really sure why, like I said maybe two other tables with customers. But I have to say that the food was amazing also.   We will definitely go again.  I would give them a 5 but they were very slow.

I went here on 3/14...National Pie Day. I took a few photos. This was the right and wrong day (Not absolutely horrible day) to go for pizza. The pies were only 3.14, who doesn't like and want a deal??? Well if you don't want to wait in line, then you don't want the deal. I think I stood in line and waited for my pizza to finish, about maybe an hour. When I got home it was 6pm. The guy at the door Jessie, not sure how to spell his name, but was super cool. He kept us entertained the whole time while we were standing outside waiting to get in. I didn't feel it was a bad wait, I expected the crowd to be in abundance. The pizza (which I also took a photo) was ok. They have gluten free dough for those who can't eat it. You can create your own pizza as well as choose one of the options they provide. The most you will pay for a pizza before taxes is 7.25 or something like that...I don't remember, I just know that it is very economical for what it's worth, and it's more healthy than a few of the chains. The place is great on the inside (see photos), it was clean, crowded because of pie day, but still worth going. My only critique would be in regards to the monitoring of how long the pizzas are in the oven...mine was partially burned on one side and the bottom was pretty burned as well. It is a fire oven too so there is a lot of justification that I can understand completely, and it was pie day so there were a lot of pizzas going in and out like crazy. It was a pretty cool restaurant I will go back and try it again.

I've been to the Mercantile for Dinner and I have to say lunch was a downer.  When I got out for lunch and order a sandwich the first thing i expect is fresh bread.  Didn't find it here.  Other than that the taste was bland.  If it wasn't a business lunch, I would have sent it back.
First time in New Orleans. Great food! Great service! Quit reading all the reviews and go!
Amazing. Great choices for all picky eaters/foodies. Fresh food, GREAT coffee. Hope to go back soon!

A gem for sure in the City Center of Philly. The interior is well decorated, with a modern/asian fusion feel to it. Nothing feels overly clubby, but at the same time everything is in good taste. The wait staff is great as well, constantly checking up on us, very light hearted humor, and making great recommendations.

In terms of food, we got a good sampling of appetizers. The edamame dumplings were so good, we got a second order of them! A very butter taste to them, it's extremely savory and very well presented. We also get the crab rangoons, which were good as well, but the edamame was definitely the best in show here. We got a few skewers as well, mostly the wagyu beef and chicken. They were very good as well, and perfect for sharing, but not particularly filling.

For entrees we got the korean fried chicken, which was a slight let down. The chicken itself was very good, however the sauce it was in was a little odder than what I'm accustomed to. It was an odd wasabi type sauce that was somewhat sour but also savory. The short ribs and shrimp pad thai however were great! the ribs were so tender and juicy, although fatty, so watch out if you're not into that type of thing. The pad thai noodles were well cooked, not too hard or soft, and the amount of shrimp was sufficient. Together, it was quite tasty, and a good balance to the ribs/wings.

In summary, this place has a lot to offer and would be a great date spot! The food is made for sharing and there's so much variety that even picky people should be able to find something they want.
Best pizza in town. Always our go-to pizzeria for quick, delicious dinner!
Yessssss!!!!!! This place Rocks food was awesome  service was nice a lot of food all types of food 5 stars yup 5!
Went around 11:45 am and it was pretty empty. Seated quickly and they were very attentive. In the mood for some deep fried sushi so got the Las Vegas Roll. Really big selection on sushi.
The food is excellent and the owners are friendly, generous and kind. Highly recommend!

I used to come to this Don Pan with my family all the time years ago when it used to be good. What a disappointment it was today. From the bored cashier who has zero customer skills and zero knowledge of what's offered (she didn't know if there was a menu, did not give me a receipt and tried to overcharge for a cachapa, when I noted my frozen maracuyá juice didn't have any sugar or enough ice she made a comment that surprised me "that's the way I like it, I made extra for myself..." !! Then proceeded to add a lot of sugar to my cup that didn't dissolve- I expect a little more when I pay $5 for a medium sized juice that's cold but not frozen like ordered. 
She was the only girl at the store at the time and she had to do everything so the 5 customers that came after me were served while I was waiting for my order. 
Again, really disappointed and I would not come back. The Management really needs to make a lot of changes, including quality of the food (ingredients not fresh/greasy food and not heated through) and prices (some items are way overpriced compared to similar places) if they don't want to go out of business.

I have mixed emotions for one reason, about this place. I adore the ambiance and the environment of this great little local find. I think the food is quite good and the drink selections are fabulous. I'd highly recommend the A to Z Night and Day - it's delightful, especially on a cold winter day. The Welsh Rarebit is pretty delicious and the hamburger is pretty good too. I found the bone marrow to be minimal. My main concern with the Black Market at this point is the pricepoint. . . As I mentioned earlier, I love this place, but I think 15 for a burger and 13 for  glass of wine is rather high, for an Indianapolis establishment. $100 for two people with limited drinks, no appetizers and a hamburger as one of the entrees, is a bit high.  Again, love the atmosphere, the food and the wine . . . just wish it was more in the traditional price range for Indy. . . I think a $75 bill with tip would have been a bit more appropriate for the evening. I'll be back for drinks or for lunch - but probably not for drinks and dinner.

Love this place!! The employees are soooo nice. I've been there a few times and the carrot cake açaí bowl is amazing. Today I got a "the healthy heart one" smoothie. So delicious!! I feel great after eating here. Def recommend!
Food was surprisingly good, my first time having VIET food and I was impressed. Very tasteful and inexpensive totally worth it. Staff was great & very fast

I gave this historic restaurant two opportunities to show that they could provide what one would expect for a weekend lunch.
Both times they failed.
Both times we sat outside and  it could be lovely except service was horrid. The place was relatively empty. However there were  lots of staff milling about and congregating in the small outdoor supply house.
Finally the waitress came by and the order was given. 
Then the wait
The long wait. Where did everyone go? Are they all in the shed?
Where are the servers?? What can't a manager help?
Finally the busboy came by to remind the waitress that we ordered drinks. Bloody Mary was undrinkable.
A salad was never delivered but came out and it was a sandwich??
The burger delivered was fine, but in a party if two orders are given and when one meal (hot) is delivered and the other (a cold one) isn't what do you do? I started eating
We then heard there would be a shift change but the waitperson leaving did not come with the person taking over . 
I paid for what was delivered and (partially ) eaten /drunk and watched as another customer got frustrated and left.
I was happy to leave, meal half eaten and won't return.
Excellent buffet, loved the atmosphere and the service was excellent. Our family and friends go there quite frequently, It is the best place on the beach,
Food horrible. Salad small. My friends shrimp was frozen. Portions tiny. Overpriced for what you get. I don't recommend eating here at all. I'm sure the alcohol is fine.

My first time and I was pleasantly impressed.  The food was the right temperature, varied and really good, lol. Courtney was our helper, she was knowledgeable, professional and courteous. The price was a tad high ($30 per plate), but overall it was a great experience. And yes, I will be going back.

Don't bother!
Especially if you are not from  New Orleans, don't waste your time or money going here. Food was tasteless, overpriced and served at room temperature.  The place looks nasty, unkempt. Health Department needs to have a visit. on top of everything said  service is lacking and rude. The only bright spot was our waitress, I believe her name is Janelle, she was friendly and stayed on top of our food orders and drinks even though they it was hot and busy. When asking locals in the area they mention Mothers but many of them said they haven't been there in awhile. I see why!
The Italian beef is my favorite sandwich here. I have actually never been inside and just had take out, but the food is worth the trip.

Terrible accommodations. Could not handle a simple pasta sauce substitution of marinara for bolognese. Spoke to Manager, then General Manager who clearly had no interest in a customer leaving satisfied with their first experience.  Waitress was phenomenonal. Managers and cooks fully incompetent. Strongest recommendation never to come here.

No accommodation on checks either. Total water of money. Ate half the veal and none of the pasta!

I ordered the pork tenderloin.  It was hand breaded and thick.  The size was perfect.  It wasn't the huge one that you need three buns to eat.  It was one of the best I've ever had.  It was delicious.  I ordered the onion rings as well.  They were top notch.  The breading was fantastic.  They were fried to perfection.  The service was prompt and friendly.  Jimmy's is one of the best diners I've been too.  I would definitely go back.

My boyfriend and I have done takeout from Eclipse twice in the last two weeks.  I'm smitten!  I've never been in the restaurant (Darn you, Covid!) but hope to sooner than later.

I am crazy for their apple and goat cheese salad.  A large is more than plenty for two adults.  Both times I've eaten 75% of this salad myself.  It is just that good.  A salad?  Yes, it is true!  The goat cheese is not gamey at all and they add dried cranberries and walnuts that compliment it so well.  

Our first pizza was pesto with chicken and sun dried tomatoes.  We ordered a family size and devoured the whole thing.  Not because the pizza was too small but because it was too good!  

I am doing a month of vegetarian eating so on Saturday we ordered another family size pesto pizza but this time we asked them to add all of their veggies instead of chicken.  DANG but that pizza was magnificent!  My BF loves, loves, loves meat but said that he didn't miss it at all on this pizza.  We managed to save a few slices for breakfast the next morning.  Might I recommend a fried egg on top of leftovers?  YUM!

I'm hoping to talk the BF into making this our regular Saturday night meal.  I don't think I'll have to try too hard!

The service at this restaurant was excellent. The price was a bit higher than I would have liked, but the food was good as well. I think out of everything ordered, the Salmon Tartare was my favorite. Don't forget to try some of their signature drinks!

Food good!! :-), papaya slad,  thai noodle soup,  pad thai, pad see ew, red curry  chicken,  tom yum goong..that i like to order aet   ( Taste orignal thai food.  serve good  take care you good :-)  the best  thai food in phily  cherry hill..

Fast service and accomodating staff. Somehow I still feel like they haven't reached their full potential when it comes down to flavours and usage of different textures to their signature bowls.

I ordered a large bowl and I was satisfied with the portion. The difference in price between regular and large is not even two dollars if I remember it correctly. 

Fresh food at a good cost but I've had better poke bowls in the past.

Stopped in here for lunch with my father and the food was great. Best hot and sour soup we have had to date and the best general tso's chicken too. We requested extra spicy and it was delicious and super spicy. Great staff, quick service, we will be coming back for more!
came to this location before 9:30 am for breakfast and was told they aren't serving breakfast, even though the breakfast menus were clearly up. might want to change your menus, guys.

Wasn't that amazing- the food is OK but not as flavorful as french fusion should be. Maybe trying some of the asian dishes would be better, but we got the lamb and chicken, so so. The service was also slow, but it allows for a romantic slow dinner. I don't think its worth it for the increase of price- havn't been back since.

Stumbled by this place while searching for a place to stop for lunch. The staff was friendly and the service was quick. The chicken salad and Italian sandwiches were delicious. The bread they were served on was amazing. Outdoor seating. Will be back to try their donuts for breakfast.

Great everything!  We had such a great experience at this restaurant. The ambience, the live jazz band, the food & the service were top notch.  
I will definitely recommend this place to my friends and family. Thank you!

I was very impressed with this place. We had a little bit of everything. Jerk wings were awesome! Hand cut fries like my grandma makes. Cheese mashed potatoes, collard greens and cabbage was authentic and seasoned perfectly. I came to Nashville for work and decided to try this place specifically after a friend recommended. I will dream about the wonders of my awesome meal until I return.

After a Sunday afternoon of drinking beers at craft breweries, we needed something to eat, and so we visited Party Fowl. 

It's a bar and restaurant, and focuses in on lots of variations of chicken dishes. We all ordered the same thing, chicken dumpling soup. I added a Mac-and-cheese side dish. It was pretty good, and close to what my mom used to make when I was a kid.

It's smack dab in an area that is being developed as a drinking spot, as well as an entertainment and dining destination. It could serve as a reprieve from the craziness that is Broadway.

Where the heck was I?  I lived in St. Louis majority of my life and today was my first time ever coming here. 
I never thought there could be a restaurant that makes their own noodles and wonton wrap. Awesome!

Pictured menu for your convenience!  It actually made it harder for me to decide because everything looked delicious!

Appetizers I had:

Dumplings!! Perfect balance of chewy and soft. I like to mix some hot oil with the soy sauce for a little kick on my palate. 
Spicy chicken!  I probably could've ate the whole thing by myself, but I shared. Has a type of spicy pepper sprinkled on deep fried bite-sized chicken. Boneless! Delicious with sweet and sour sauce. 

As my main lunch, I got the fried Shaved noodles with beef. From just looking at it, it looks like regular flat noodles (chow fun), but you can definitely tell it's different when you take a bite into it.  Texture of noodles and the cook on the beef was great. I was disappointed with the sauce they used though.  Slightly bland and I got bored of eating, which is why I couldn't give that last star! 

Bubble tea:  Matcha milk tea was great for dessert!
They also have a good variety of fluffy ice and fruit smoothies!!! Gotta try next time.

Omicron DoorDash review:

I don't know what took me so long to visit Szechuan House, as several of my friends rave about it. I had been planning to order delivery from Food Hing again, but they were closed on Monday, which is typical for Chinese establishments, so I figured it was about time I tried some Szechuan, and was pleased to see them pop up as a delivery option.

I am an adventurous eater among my circle, but by Szechuan House standards would likely be considered a big baby. I enjoy a bit of spicy heat, but never at the expense of flavor, and I'm old enough at this point to know that I just don't want to dive into the world of entrails as a meal. I'm sure the intestines and kidneys and blood broths are as delicious as the other Yelpers indicate, but you'll have to take their word for it! I over-ordered (non-innards and non spicy options) so I'd have food for a few days (it's the week between Christmas and the New Year and I've had about enough of the kitchen, thank you!). I kept it bland with chicken and eggplant over white rice, some wonton soup, scallion pancakes, and a side dish of sesame noodles.

I knew I'd be saving the sesame noodles for the next day or so, so I focused on the rest, and I was very, very happy with the meal, which held up nicely during the trip across town - even the scallion pancakes, which, if you have not had them, are a laminated bread of sorts. They're shaped like a pancake, but are perhaps more like a flat croissant, with scallions mixed in, and then fried, yielding a delicious flaky, crispy, chewy, layer-y treat that you can use to shovel your food, or simply dip into the soy/sesame sauce provided. I haven't had a scallion pancake in years - they're a simple treat, I suppose, compared to other items on the menu, but this was good enough to make my eyes roll to the back of my head in joy with the first bite.

The chicken and eggplant was perfectly seasoned and was a dish large enough to also yield two meals. The eggplant are the long skinny, vibrant purple variety, which I prefer, and the chicken was very likely marinated and tender. A little bit of heat - perfect for me. The wonton soup, too, was excellent. Szechuan House uses a darker broth than what is typical in the area. Possibly beef broth? Not sure, and perhaps it's best I don't know. But it hit the spot. I saved a bit of that for the next day as well, though I was difficult to restrain myself because it was so good.

My only complaint is with the sesame noodles. I took a nibble the night they arrived because I was curious, but they were so spicy that my mouth burned, and they had a slight bitter taste as well, that I found unpleasant. I saw scant evidence of sesame seeds, so I may have received the Cold Noodles with Spicy Sauce by mistake. As I mentioned, I saved them - I just had them for lunch today and the extra 30-some-odd hours marinating in their sauce amped up the heat. I will likely endure some long-term consequences as a result, but to mitigate them, I added some sesame seeds, a splash of sesame oil, a little sugar to cut the bitterness and to take the edge of the heat, along with a smattering of French's crunchy onions. Sacrilegious perhaps, but it helped the noodles go down without burning my esophagus too badly. 

I've kind of settled into the habit of not giving 5 stars to an establishment I've only visited once, though I believe Szechuan House is worthy, for sure. The noodle experience is the only negative, and for what it's worth, I think if you are a fan of heat, they'd probably be great. I will definitely order from Szechuan House again, and look forward to it!
Food is what you'd expect from Black Bear. Our server, Nikole, was awesome. Very personable and attentive. Great job, Nikole.
New fav pizza spot in Indy. Good vibes and good pizza. Will def be back. There were 6 of us and we split 3 pizzas. The stinky Pete was our fav.

If you walk by this place you wouldn't think its home to the original muffuletta because all you see is spices and oils and a deli counter tucked off to the side BUTTTT.... hold the front door, the sandwich is delicious!  And you can get a beer as well!  There's seating in the back and its communal so you may sit across from strangers but everyone in NOLA is so nice, it's a nice touch. If you need a quick bite or want to try the best in town, pop in. They have the sandwiches lined up and ready to go!
My husband I eat here or order take out at least twice a month. Everything we've ever tried has been delicious, and the service is fast and friendly.
Once again, MrEd's NEVER disappoints...came for the food, drinks and to see my favorite bartender Tricia.
Hands down best place to eat if looking for buffet.  The staff very kind and courteous , very clean environment. Trust me when I say you won't be disappointed what so ever
Best thai in st Pete clearwater area. The sushi is awesome, the curry very flavorful and the ownership and employees are very nice

Ok... Went for lunch today with hubby. I ordered before hubby got there. We got pork chop with broken rice and tofu banh mi. Then another family came and sat behind our table. Waited 15-20min... Then the waiter told us the to go pork chop is ready. Seriously, why don't you come out with our food first then the to go one.... Waited another 5-10 min- still didn't get our food, but the table behind us did... I was getting very irritated and flagged down the waiter. 10 min laters- finally got our food. Very poor management. But, the food was very good to be in this area. The pork chop is a must try. Two big pork chop, very juicy and flavorful. I got the tofu banh mi- bread soft and warm. The tofu is probably marinated in some sauce. Very flavorful too. 
Just beware- food is good but service can be improve.

Average food, decent beers, but overall "meh" experience.

I went with two friends for dinner on a Friday evening. We got there around 6:20 and were told it was going to be a 30 minute wait, which is okay/expected for Friday night. We grabbed some beers (recommend Troegs Wheat) and headed to the 3rd floor, where they have pool, darts, dingy walls, and not enough seatery.

So we waited. 30 minutes went by. Beers were finished. And then we waited more. Until we got tired of waiting and asked the hostess about our table. We were told we were next (Yes!) and she would come get us. So.. guess what? We waited. By the time she came to get us, it was 7:50 and we'd already been there for 90 minutes. Come on..

We were seated on the crowded second floor, unfortunately right by the door, where it was cold as balls. We all had to keep our coats on the entire time.

As for the food..

Cheesesteak empanadas (I am told that this was featured on the Food Network) were pretty good, but overhyped.

Duck pot pie (another Food Network star) was alright. It's basically a bland starchy pot pie with a hint of duck flavor-- I think it's overpriced for what you get. Not to mention the pile of wilted greens on the side...

Baked mac and cheese was tasty and waaay rich. If you like cheesy richness, this is the dish for you. Enjoyed the blueberry cornbread too.

The latter two dishes were meant as entrees, but it was definitely not enough food (surprising for a dive-y place). I could have eaten both of them by myself, but maybe I'm a bit of a pig.

Sadly I did not get to try the burger, and I probably won't go back for it. Am I missing out?

This is absolutely one of my favorite places in Philly! I always have a good time and the atmosphere is part of the fun. It's vibrant and the staff are always nice, knowledgable, and ready to answer any questions or pronounce anything on the menu! Lol
The food is always good, I've never had anything there that I didn't enjoy...I've had a couple of sausages that were difficult to eat but u can just chock that up to my dirty mind. Rofl
Beer...so much beer.  That's really all that needs to be said about that. 
Oh, when u go, get a giant plate of the potato pancakes because they will change ur life!! Not just a side...it won't be enough, u gotta get the plate of potato pancakes. I might just eat that the next time I go...and I won't even be embarrassed...that's how amazing they are! They are like if potato were mixed with all the really good drugs...I mean the really good expensive ones that u don't mind being addicted to...then fried crispy and topped with sour cream...yea THAT...order THAT! Shit, now I need some...dammit!!
Anyway, any place that ends the meal with a shot of anything should be given 5 stars...
Drink up, stuff ur face with potatoes and sausage, and yell at the tv during any sports season with everyone else! This is a great place to do all that!

Excellent wine, excellent food, excellent service, Excellent Evening.  What's not to love?
Always order the tiramisu!

Wow!!! I can't say enough about how much my friends and I enjoyed everything about Southern Steak and Oyster! Great atmosphere- great Service - phenomenal food! Portions are generous and amazing! 

We loved the biscuit steak appetizer! Ordered 2 and then got a 3rd! I guess I should state there was 7 of us :) we got the Benne Shrimp - loved the sauce and the shrimp was perfect but I'd suggest the biscuit steak if you had to choose! 

2 of us ordered the Belle - so much flavor and my filet was perfect! The dbl cut smoked pork chop was awesome! Salmon special was a big hit,along with the brisket! There wasn't a bite left on anyone's plate! For dessert we got the whoopie pie and banana pudding - both .... Get both! 

I've heard about the Southern and how it's a local and tourist favorite - we all saw why!!! Go there you won't regret it!

Great chicken. Great horseradish potatoes. Great collard greens. Great service. Cool vibe. Kitchen open late. We loved everything about this place. It was loud and crazy when we went (bit after midnight after a concert), but the food and service was totally worth it.

Ambiance: 4/5! Maybe because my friends and I came at a non-busy time, but it was just a nice, clean, and a bit hip place. The place was a bit smaller than I expected, but the owners did a good job decorating the inside of the restaurant well. The seatings near the wall have cushions which was nice!

Food: The meats are really soft but I thought that the marinates were a bit weak/watered down. The vegetables as well, like the grilled onion seemed a bit lacking in flavor. The side dishes were great tho!

Service: 5/5. They attended to us quickly and we were able to eat our food comfortably! The owners are very nice and friendly.

I love noodles and company, they've never let me down. Every single one I've been to (and I've been to a few) has been clean and fast and delicious! I'm really happy I know I can always trust this chain to be up to standards.
Wonderful food - but a little pricy. The watermelon summer salad that they're serving right now (summer 2015) is a dream.

Located in the Radisson Hotel. I've been staying here on business for over ten years. Breeze is definitely an above average hotel restaurant. The draft beer selection is great(I'm always happy to see my favorite Moose Drool still on tap after many years!)  The pesto chicken pizza is my go-to meal.

Terrible service at the bar. Asked blond bartender if the nachos had olives and she didn't know. I said I don't not like them, if she could please keep them off. They came, 45, yes 45 minutes for NACHOS, later. Covered in olives. She didn't once check to see if we were ok with our meal. There's 6 people here, I can't imagine she is or the kitchen is that busy. 
After we were done, we sat with dirty plates in front of us for 15 minutes while she walked back and forth in front of us 10+ times. 
Will never be back.

Hubby and I stopped by for the first time for dinner a few days ago. We were VERY happy we did.
The server was awesome! I wish I remembered her name. 
 The appetizers were yummy...(lemon pepper wings and garlic bread sticks) and my king crab was delicious! I tried hubby's shrimp and loved  them as well!
We will definitely return!!!!

The worst dining experience I've ever had. The appetizer took half an hour. After we were there for an hour I asked the waiter how long our entrees were going to take and he said "I don't know. I can check if you want?". DUH! When the table next to us got their food (they arrived half an hour after us) we got up and we ready to leave. The manager finally showed his face. We finally got our food after waiting over an hour.  He had to hear it from three tables. Two of the tables ate the food because it was ready but one table was done and left. It was a complete mess!!!!

Expect long lines but they move very quickly.  We enjoyed the beef brisket which tasted like pastrami. Also had the pulled pork and the burnt ends. 

The sweet potato fries were delicious but the cole slaw was too vinegary.
THE BEST hot chicken in the world. Can't beat it.

I just went to the location in woodbine yesterday and I will be back!  I loved the atmosphere the coffee was to die for. Organic and small business what's not to love!  I wish they had a few more options but other than that I felt right at home in this coffee shop and can't for my second visit!

The Kobe burger is amazing, everything else is average. Let's face it this is a great place to go for a hamburger. But, if you know someone who makes good hamburgers, i.e. has watched a few food network shows, there won't be much difference. Unless the person you know only uses kobe beef.

Had a really great time here a couple of weeks ago. So many great food options, really high quality breakfast and lunch. I love the casual diner vibe though, everything came out quickly and the servers were incredibly nice. We signed up for the rewards program there and we already got a free slice of pie. Definitely try the pies!

Service sucks and an extraordinarily long wait for the first course

I decided to check this out for dinner.  It was Wed, around 7:30PM when I reached the place. Only four tables were occupied and there were six servers. I was directed o a table and then they seemed to forget. After a few minutes, had to call the server from one of the other tables to get water. 5-10 minutes later, someonre came for an order. I ordered a dosa for an appetizer and asked them to leave the menu while I decided on the main course. 
Few minutes later someone else came and took the menu. Aftera wait of 35-40 minutes, I got my appetizer and no one bothered to ask or seemed interested in my  remaining order.

Put off with the service and attitude, I left after the appetizer alone No one ever greeted while coming or leaving. The owners didn't even make eye contact. A real shame. 

Courtesy training and small business service management should be manadatory for the staff and the owners before they are allowed to operate.

The same Friday, our group of around 14 went out for Indian dinner and no surprises, this place was off our list despite being the second closest.  Won;t be returneing here ever

Maybe too much time in Philly restaurants with more energy. A beat up shopping center and a somewhat tired atmosphere inside the restaurant (although I love the Flyers stuff)
Food was good. Gnocchi was average. Pizza with prosciutto was good but did not expect the room temperature toppings. The veal Milanese was just ok. Too greasy for my liking.
At over $100 for 3 entered and 2 appetizers I know of much better values in the area. Still think Sapori is the best Italian in South Jersey.

Supremely delicious food and excellent service! I've gone here twice now and without fail, every time has been delicious. I especially enjoy the negimaki and takoyaki appetizers, which are savory and melt in your mouth. The entrees were good, but compared to the appetizers, paled in comparison. The chicken teriyaki and pork katsu were yummy, but I'd go for the udon for a more satisfying meal. I also highly recommend the schuykill sushi roll--very creamy and the flavors meld together so well. The waiters are excellent too, very professional and attentive. I love that my water glass is constantly filled (a small thing that a lot of restaurants overlook!). The restaurant ambiance is quiet, intimate and calm--perfect for a date night.

This was my second time ordering delivery from Taj Mahal, and I am definitely pleased with my experience. 

I ordered the Palak Paneer, and my partner ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala, along with some plain naan, and an order of garlic naan as well, since we had to hit the delivery minimum (which is a bit high, but I suppose this is the price you pay when everybody's had too many drinks to drive, but you need some spicy awesomeness in your life...and probably also some rice to help absorb some booze). 

My partner said he wished that there had been a bit more chicken in his Chicken Tikka Masala, but the flavors were spot on. The Palak Paneer was perfect--and spicy enough to give me the hiccups (which is how you know you're doing it right). All in all, a great experience, and the order arrived very quickly, especially for being a Saturday night!
Just had the best brisket sandwich. Stellar! Good prices too. So glad they are near my house! Do yourself a favor and visit Texas BBQ. Delicious sauce as well.

Every time I go to this bar I ask myself, why? This bar is only good for one thing young twenty year olds looking for some meat to take home. 

Its unfortunate because this bar/property has the potential to be something much better.

As a huge fan of organic and clean eating, Healthy Bites hits the nail on the head.

The cozy store and restaurant offers really tasty menu and produce items. This is not a grocery store, so don't expect to find everything you need.  Instead, there are some select seasonal and staple picks like milk, eggs, and cheese. 

Some reviews mention the prices can be steep, which is why I only go to treat myself.  For me it is worth it. Everytime I go to Healthy Bites I feel a bit more rejuvenated and inspired.
I stopped at Firehouse Subs for some "fast" food and my order was not ready in 15 minutes so I spoke with the manager. He covered the cost of my meal without any fuss. Thumbs up to Firehouse

Update* 
Talked with some wedding guests post wedding and was informed the following about the quality of the food: pork was undercooked (like very pink); macaroni and cheese was "cold;" and the turkey tasted like "they dumped salt on top of it." Some guests complained that they ran out of pulled pork during the dinner service. I'll continue to post updates as I receive more feedback. I guess you can say, I'm still pretty upset with the service and quality of Andrew's Bayou Ribs.

Came here to get drinks and lunch. Excellent variety of beers, great cocktails and other drinks. Service was good as well. But the food was equivalent to something I could warm up in the microwave. My glass for my beer wasn't very clean, our appetizer wasn't very appetizing. And the tables are kind of sticky and don't feel clean. I feel like they could do a better job at making this place cleaner. I'd come back here to drink but I wouldn't come back here to eat.

This is certainly one of my new favorite restaurants in the city. From it's simple but lovely decor to the amazing food and service, I had no hesitation in giving Spice Finch a glowing five star review. 

I had a 7pm reservation on a Tuesday night for me and my friend who was visiting from Canada. She just recently moved out of Philly and when deciding where to go for dinner, her only request was for me to choose a place that was new for both of us. Spice Finch had been on my mind for a few months now so I figured this would be perfect for the occasion.

Our sweet waitress gave us a rundown of the menu and told us that dishes are typically made for sharing. With that in mind, we both ordered fries to share but decided to choose our own entrees. I'm allergic to both chickpeas and lentils so unfortunately, I have quite a few food restrictions at Mediterranean restaurants. I shared this with the waitress when I ordered the peri-peri shrimp and she assured me that she would speak to the chef to make sure these ingredients were not used in this dish and there was no cross contamination. Thank you to the team at Spice Finch for making me feel so well taken care of!

The peri-peri shrimp was incredible. So flavorful and rich with well-cooked, plump shrimp. I became a huge fan of peri peri during my trip to South Africa last year and am so happy I got to enjoy it here. The dish came with a side of buttery flatbread that I dipped into the sauce. 

The fries that my friend and I shared were also very good. They were well-seasoned and the portion was huge. I couldn't have the hummus aioli they come with but my friend said it was delicious. Although the sauce looked great, I was more than content just enjoying the fries sans dip!

For dessert we enjoyed a slice of chocolate cake with tahini soufflé and blood orange sorbet. I was a little skeptical because I'm not usually a fan of fruity desserts but wow was this dish really something! The blood orange sorbet really balanced out the rich chocolate cake, but in my opinion, the tahini soufflé was the MVP. I could have eaten spoonfuls of that alone!

The restaurant is beautiful. It is open and airy with the appropriate lighting. It isn't too bright but not too dark either. Lighting can make such a big difference - it really sets the mood and Spice Finch does it just right. This restaurant is great for get-togethers, celebrations or dates. 

I can't wait to return here. I'm tempted to make my next experience a brunch outing, but with such an incredible dinner, it'll be hard not to go back for that!

Well, what can I say...? It's been a while once we've been here. I realize now the reason why. We waited 20 minutes for the server to come ( it was a slow Sunday afternoon with maybe 6-8 customers) And when he did... he went to the table that came 10 minutes after us. So we waited for another 10 minutes and he kept walking past us " not even a look our way". So, we went to the manager and said something then said we were leaving. The server just gave us a dirty look. 

That's all I needed... I will never go to this place again. This is poor management and poor service. ITS A WONDER WHY THIS PLACE IS STILL EVEN OPEN. Just

While I'm not a fan of beer, I loved Victory Brewing Company!  The restaurant is open and loud but the service is friendly and quick.  We began our meal with Skillet Fries.  The fresh cut fries are loaded with Summer Love Ale cheese sauce, scallions, sour cream and bacon.  They're an ooey, gooey delicious mess and I would never visit Victory Brewing without ordering them again!  I also ordered the Smokehouse Burger.  While I asked them to hold the house made bbq sauce, I enjoyed the bacon, cheddar cheese and onion straws.  My brother was with me at this meal and he ordered the chicken ceasar salad.  It was wonderful!  Victory Brewing has several locations locations.  If you're ever near one, I'd suggest you make it a priority to stop in!

I didn't try Pat's or Geno's due to the poor reviews.  Service was fairly quick and friendly.  It was busy prior to a Flyers game.  I had the standard cheesesteak with american and it was really fresh, hot and good.  Pickles at the side stand were good also.  Had a terrible time trying to catch a cab back to my hotel after being dropped off.  It's in the middle of nowhere.  Be sure to plan ahead if cabbing it.

What a joke of a restaurant. I ate here years ago, but what prompted this piss poor review is their non existent customer service. Called this location to ask aout delivery radius and was quickly put on hold .....for 9 MINUTES!!!! Ridiculous. Called back and got the same person who proceeded to nonchalantly tell me to call back later.... No worries- won't get my money....

A must-do for any fan of the Man in Black. Seeing the relics of his life and work, both musical and religious, was awe-inspiring. Don't miss this if you're in Nashville! (One star off only because it's rather small.)

First let me say that the competition for your food dollar is intense in New Orleans. There are so many choices it can be a bit overwhelming, but if you're in the Big Easy, try this charming place for breakfast. 
We started with amazing coffee and some of the best bloody marys I had had in NO, made by our delightful server, Dustin. It's a signature cocktail in the city and these stood out. 
Our breakfasts were served beautifully. My choice was a southern breakfast of scrambled eggs, fried chicken with biscuits, grits and gravy, which I highly recommend to anyone with a big appetite. 
One friend had the French toast made with amaretto butter and luscious bananas foster, and my other friend had the healthier white wash omelet made from egg whites and loaded with veggies. Each one of us raved.
In a city filled with great food, Monty's on the Square stood out.

Winckler' Ribs are the best. Mike Winckler is a great chef...and his"Ribs" are delicious. I love the Ribs,Chopped Barbecue and all the sides served there. Mike has a great personality...and always welcomes his customers with a smile and great conversations. You can smell the goodness when you cross the Trenton bridge and ride down East Bridge Street in Morrisville, Pa. Just follow the aroma, you'll be rewarded with good eats.

The service was good, but the food is very overpriced. I really don't like the practice of throwing cheese on everything to mask the flavor, or lack thereof. I found myself distracted while eating, thinking of what could have been done to take the meal from palatable to enjoyable. I ordered salmon with a Cajun cream sauce that looked like American cheese, but tasted like Velveeta, salsa, and a bit of cream. My friend ordered onion rings and a spicy beef sandwich. It was fatty, flavors were flat, and wasn't spicy at all. The onion rings were good though. The sweet tea was too. The people in the bar seemed like they were having fun, but I won't be going back for another try.

Simply the greatest dining experience I've had yet. The family came to NOLA to celebrate Mom's 60th birthday and we celebrated with dinner at August. WOW. The food was exquisite. The four of us all ordered the tasting menus- both with meat and without, along with the wine pairings. Everything was incredible. I told them I have a shellfish allergy so they modified one of the courses to accommodate me. I ate octopus and loved it (typically a chicken/beef kind of girl)! Robert, our server, was extraordinary- knowledgeable and friendly. He made us feel welcome and was great at explaining what each course was. The ambience is charming as well. HIGHLY RECOMMEND! Wish I lived closer so I could go back again!!

Proudly staking their claim as one of the few non-chain restaurants in the Castleton area, the Castleton Grill serves up good food with generous portions. The menus is standard American fare. I had the Beef Manhattan (billed as shaved Prime Rib) that was tasty albeit possibly overdrenched in gravy. Service was friendly and atmosphere was not much different than you'd find in a similarly billed chain restaurant.

My husband and I visited on a Sunday evening, hoping to quench our desire for some delicious Thai food. We had read some decent reviews, most of which stating that the food was good, but the restaurant was fairly empty for dinner.

We arrived around 6:00pm to a mostly empty restaurant, with one large table of diners celebrating a birthday. We were seated promptly in a booth with some pretty pictures of Buddhist temples under the glass top table. Overall the decor was nothing special, but it was not dirty or dingy either.

Our waiter was wearing street clothing (jeans and a t-shirt), but he was fairly friendly. It took a while for him to return to our table and take our drink order, but when he finally did, the beers were brought out in a timely fashion.

The menu had an array of options which were listed with ingredients, so people who are unfamiliar with Thai food can know what exactly they are ordering. We started with the Tom Ka Gai (coconut chicken) soup. It was served to our table in a flaming metal bowl with a ladle. Nice touch for appearance and keeping the soup hot as well. The soup was creamy and delicious, with a touch of spiciness. Just the way we like it.

I ordered the Pad Thai with beef, and my husband ordered the Massaman Curry with beef. The Pad Thai was a decent sized portion of noodles and meat, not brothy, not overly sauced, with crisp raw veggies and some chopped peanuts on top. It was good, but I felt like the flavor was missing something.

My husband received his Massaman in a soup bowl, and it was very brothy. Other Massaman dishes he has eaten were not soupy. The flavor was good, but the delivery was a bit odd. A bowl of white rice was served along side of the curry. He enjoyed his dish. He had asked that it be made spicy, and assured the waiter that yes, he actually wanted it spicy (because the waiter clarified that point). It arrived spicy. Although... if you like REALLY spicy food, you may want to drive that point home to your server. I think they are probably used to catering to more "American" tastes and spice levels, and therefore they are cautious about overdoing the heat level.

Overall, we had a good experience. The food was good. I would like to go back sometime and try some other dishes. But before I do, I will visit some other Thai places here in Tucson so that I have something to compare the food to.
This is our family go to place we love the whole experience any time of year oh and the foods not to shabby either if you're into home made food and baked goods. Definitely worth checking it out!

This Cheesesteak was surprisingly Bland.  Wednesday night, the parking lot was full, lots of events on the sign out front, big menu and diverse crowd had my hopes up for a much better cheesesteak.  $8.75 and it came with the potato petal french fries that were delicious.  The other food going past us smelled amazing.  The guy next to us at the bar liked his dinner.  Maybe our cheesesteak was a one-off.  We got the De Kalb cheesesteak which comes spinach, peppers and provolone cheese on it.  Our cheesesteak was the weak link in the Whitpain Tavern chain

When I suggested to my Korean-American friend Connie that we give bop a try, she said, "No, I tend to hate fusion places."  I said, "But we should still give it a try!"  I should have held my breath.  

Maybe it's because they just recently opened, but bop has a lot to learn.

While walking towards bonchon chicken, my husband suggested that we cut the walk short and try out bop.  We ordered drinks, wings, and a couple of entrees.  The drinks came out pretty quickly (they have no beer on tap).  Then we waited.  And waited.  And waited.  After approximately half an hour our server gave us a funny look and said that she'd go check on the wings.  After another 5 minutes the wings appeared.  The server exclaimed, "I don't know what happened!"  Well, I don't know what happened either since there was no apology, no manager, no nothing.  In any case, the wings were insanely huge and doused in sauce.  For me, the taste was too sweet and too one dimensional.

The entrees came out after we were done with the wings.  The bulgogi bibimbap was okay, but nothing remarkable.  I tend to like my bibimbap on the spicier side (otherwise it's just too bland) so I needed extra hot sauce.  I had to get up and hunt down our server to request the extra hot sauce.  She brought out a whole bottle, which I appreciated.  But overall, the bulgogi bibimbap wasn't anything special.  The "hot" stone bowl in which it was served was not very hot; no extra-crispy rice at the bottom of the bowl.  :(

The manager stopped by after we were done with our entrees to ask if everything was okay.  (He was stopping by all the tables.)  I relayed my frustration with the wait on the appetizer.  He said that the kitchen had been backed up but that they fixed the problem.  No apology, no offer to comp the appetizer, no nothing.

Maybe I've been spoiled by frequenting restaurants that know what they are doing or that are truly in the hospitality business.  I won't be back.

My family and I came here for dinner over the weekend and we had mixed feelings about the serves we recieved. Although we were seated immediately and the host was nice, our server was unprofessional. She came to our table and served us our drinks and food, but told us she was cut early because she had been there all day. For us we thought it was unprofessional that she just left us with a new server instead of waiting till we were finished eating, so we could properly tip. The second server was ok, considering she had just got us for the last part. The food was good, wasn't too happy about our drinks, because they tasted watered down. But they were ok too.

First and last time I'll ever visit this location. Service was absolutely terrible and the food wasn't much better. The breakfast I ordered tasted like it was warmed up leftovers from the breakfast made earlier in the morning. It was obviously not freshly prepared. The waitress Lacy S had to be constantly asked for coffee refills, napkins and anything else we needed never once coming by and checking on us. Spend your money elsewhere because this place doesn't deserve your business!

One thing I can stay is that is reasonably priced and has good variety. It is very chill and has a real serene atmosphere. The music is very up and down it can be regally good at times and then they'll play kids bop. If you don't make reservations on Friday or Saturday nights don't Expect to be able to sit indoors.

Holy. Crap. The Spanish Breakfast bites were TO DIE FOR and I'm like still upset with myself that we almost didn't order them. Highly recommend. It was my first time at Jamonera and I was so surprised! It was amazing. I just wish the place was bigger so we could have had a little more space...the people at the bar were like sitting on top of us i  thought my BF was going to get pink eye.
But the food was fantastic. It was intimate and cool ambiance so it made for a great date without breaking the bank.
Yet again, these owners are killing the restaurant game. I have loved each one of their unique establishments.
I'll be back.

Exceptional spa services and amenities. I've been here on multiple occasions and never left unhappy until yesterday. Made reservations for four people and one of the people in my party did not receive any services. We were all checked in at the same time and everything was fine upon arrival. Apparently they forgot about her and offered a very weak excuse about her appointment accidentally being deleted in the system. To make it worse the only offer they gave was to enjoy the amenities free of charge and to come back for services the following day. Absolutely not! Not sure if I will be returning. Bad service!

Horrible service. Inattentive staff and management. Did not get to eat. Left after more than 30 minuets (no exaggeration/probably closer to an hour) of no one coming after being seated with a menu. Not even any eye contact from employees passing our table by. Saw the manager back and forth without eyes on the entire restaurant. Complete tunnel vision. Finally left and tried to inform someone leaving and why. They were not concerned. There with my hungry family, kid included. Too bad because we like the beer menu. I will never come here again. It's like they think the brand speaks for them so there's no concern with the level of service.

My family and I waited a bit in line, but it went by pretty fast. Before coming here I heard so many great things about this restaurant... and boy were they right!! The food was soooo delicious and the portions are a lot for a good price. Also our waiter was fantastic. He knew the menu very well, very attentive, and well mannered. I ordered the red fish oceana, Cajun fries, and the gator bites. All of them were just sooo good!! True Louisiana food.

Went on a Sunday for lunch & got the pork lo mein lunch combo & my friend got the bourbon chicken lunch combo & both were very good. Fresh ingredients & none of the  msg or grease you get at a lot of takeout chinese places. The restaurant is very clean & the staff was very attentive. I will go back.

Lenny's is a small deli located right on the corner of Fayette Street / 9th Ave.  They're known for having the best roast pork sandwiches.  I'm not a big fan of roast pork but I do love a good Italian Hoagie.  Lenny's Italian is one of the better hoagies in the area and I give it a solid B.  If you are in the area Lenny's is always a great choice for lunch.
The charbroiled oysters are pretty good and the service was awesome. The server made me feel like family... That's how you get repeat business!

First of all, let me say about Nini, she took care of us with 5 stars customer service. She got everything, personality, service mind etc. 

Amazing food portion, quality and taste. More than that, You can get appetizer-main course and dessert less than $35!!! With that luxury look restaurant operated under W Hotel , it's unbelievable price. Awesome

Restaurant's interior is unique and very beautiful. If you think of place to take photo to upload into your IG, this is a place you are looking for

I had a great experience at The Stillery Midtown! I was visiting Nashville for work, and when I needed a dinner spot I, of course, checked Yelp for something in the area that looked good. The Stillery caught my eye, so I decided to go check it out. 

The location is nice, and it wasn't very busy when I visited. I was dining alone, so I opted to sit at the bar. I started with a Mason Jar Cocktail - the Blackberry Lime. It was made with Ole Smokey Blackberry 'Shine, lime, sour, and lemon-lime soda. It was good, not overly sweet. 

For my meal I chose the Mac & Cheese, which is cavatappi with their house cheese sauce, covered in buttery breadcrumbs and baked. I also opted to add Hot Chicken for an additional $5.00, and I've got to say it was totally worth it! I really enjoyed the mac & cheese, and I think the hot chicken really kicks it up and I would recommend that option to anyone opting for this meal. 

My interaction with the staff was great! The bartender was attentive and friendly, but she also gave me my space, which I really appreciated. Overall I had a really nice meal here, and I would recommend this spot if you're looking for dinner in the area.

The only time I've been disappointed was when there was a 1 hour wait for a table. Even then I was able to drink extra delicious beer while waiting. The draft list is always diverse and huge. And the food is great. In an area with more microbreweries than I can count, this is one of the best.
Fantastic!  My fiancé and I had dinner here twice this week. The chicken wings and mussels are banging! The staff is friendly too. This might be our new favorite spot : )

This place was taken over by someone else, other than the "Papas".  The quality has left as well....I had ordered one dessert and it was less than terrible, being the forgiver, I decided to try one more time for my husbands birthday cake, what a major disappointment!!  Drive around the corner to Lancaster Ave and visit Avila's bakery for tres de leche cake for that special occasion!!  Hey PAPA family, you were doing so well!!  Why oh Why!!

I ordered take out and was greeted as soon as I came in the door. The people here are friendly and when I tell y'all their food was to die for, literally. I tried some of my brother's chicken fried chicken (came with 4 tenders) w the sauce and it exceeded my expectations. My oven-grilled pork chop tasted amazing, and so did the corn grits and red beans & rice. The tiramisu was my favorite, except for the cocoa powder on top, but it was nothing to take it off. These plates were only $10 each and it came with a lot of food. The restaurant is a bit small, but those are the best places to eat at. I give it a 11/10.

I've been to several Five Guys locations and this one is by far one of the best.  What makes it the best?  The staff!  Everyone has a great attitude.  They all seem like they enjoy working there.  Burgers are what you'd expect from Five Guys.  I think you either love it or hate it.  In my case, I love it.

This place understands me and my chips and salsa needs.  When you sit down, you get a really big basket of chips and salsa to start off your meal.  I powered through it and more chips and salsa appeared.  It was like a dream come true.

The prices are good for what you order.  I got a combination of an enchilada and a tamale with rice and beans for $8.75.  The menu is huge so everyone is easily able to find something they like.  The issue for me was narrowing it down to one thing I wanted.  Mexican food quite possibly is the love of my life.  It's hard to choose just one delicious entree to consume!

The service was a little slow at times, but it didn't bother me as we were celebrating a friend's birthday and taking our time to enjoy our meal and the time together.  The waitress did take note that it was our friend's birthday and brought him a scoop of fried ice cream, complete with a sombrero to wear while eating it.

The atmosphere is so fun!  It kind of feels like you're outside in Mexico.  It's very bright and colorful.  I loved it.  This is the first time I really realized how much an atmosphere can impact a meal.

One last tip: Their margaritas pack a serious punch!  Bring a designated driver!

I will be back.  Chips and salsa, I'm coming for you!

This place was really good.  Further than we expected from the St Charles trolley stop but worth the walk.  The pizza was amazing.  The service was top notch and the ambiance was pretty cool as well.  Great pizza!

Oh yeah, this place is great.  Big tip, get here as early as you can!!! even on weekdays.  We got in at 8:15 am on a Friday and 30 minutes later there was a line.  I can understand why the food is fresh and delicious.  The service was efficient, but not particularly friendly.   Won't stop me from coming here again
Love love love me some crows nest. When I worked over there it was a twice a week go to. I miss it!

This place was dirty and smelled funny. It could have been because the toilets weren't working properly. It made me wonder if the bathrooms aren't up to snuff, how maintained is the kitchen. This turned me off and my party and I left the restaurant.
Probably the best Cajun/Creole restaurant in Nashville. The oyster poboy is on point as well as the étouffée and gumbo.

It took me forever to figure out a place to go for my birthday dinner but after much hemming and hawing, I settled on District Cafe. They're the newest of Nate Box's empire (Little Brick, Elm Cafe and Burrow are the others). I've never been before although people rave about their brunch and pastries. 

We came on a Saturday evening and surprisingly, it wasn't very busy. I'm not sure if people know they're open for dinner (my friends that have been had no clue) but it's nice to see they're open late (11:00pm Friday and Saturday!). I made a reservation a few days earlier and they set aside a few tables in the back for our group. The patio area outside looked great with 4-5 umbrella covered tables.

The service was friendly but slow. Must be because they're not used to big groups coming in. That being said, the inside is spacious with plenty of seating and decor is what I'm going to call refined hipster. 

- Blindman kettle sour #8 (summer & centennial) ($8.00) - light, drinkable and a touch of sourness. First time trying their #8 batch. I'm a fan. 
- Rattlesnake ($12.50)
- Cassis bramble ($12.50)
- Roast eggplant ($13.00) - ricotta was fresh. An interesting way to introduce eggplant to the masses.
- Hand cut pasta ($19.00) - Litaly said this reminded him of kraft dinner but everyone else, including me, thought it was good. Pasta was al dente and sauce wasn't too creamy. 
- Flat iron steak ($20.00) -guys, guys, guys; they BLOWTORCH the steak! The steak was a perfect medium rare. Everyone loved it.
- Sous-vide chicken breast ($19.00) - to quote Litaly: "this $hit's tender". I couldn't say it any better. You'll never want to eat chicken breast any other way. So tender and juicy. Another delightful dish. 
- Patatas bravas ($12.00) - a few people said this reminded them of poutine but with a tomato sauce. Good but quite rich. 
- West coast manilla clams ($18.00) - didn't have a taste but it smelled heavenly!
- Chocolate chip cookie ($2.50) - good but not what I would get from the pastry options. 
- Salted caramel chocolate cake ($7.00) - I'm not a huge chocolate cake fan but this portion was massive. I had a bite and it wasn't bad. Didn't taste the salted caramel. More chocolatey.
- Coconut cream pie ($10.00) - their pies change daily but damnnnn, this was SO good. Crust? Good. Filling was incredibly light, airy and not too sweet. Bonus, this was huge; you could easily share this between several people.
- Mocha ($5.50) - a couple people grabbed coffee drinks at the end of our meal. Mocha for Swanger.
- Cappuccino ($4.25) - Cappuccino for Litaly. They both had some neat coffee art.

Happy everyone liked the place and I'll be back again to try brunch/lunch.

Saw this new restaurant had opened when I was getting my nails done a few doors down and was pleasantly surprised with all the positive reviews for the first location in Boise.  We went for dinner and are so glad we did.  The restaurant does not take reservations but there was little wait.  Our waitress was super attentive, knew the menu well, and quickly had our food ordered.  The Caesar salad was delicious but I would not order if you don't like Parmesan..... there is a good amount of it in the salad.  Garlic bread is served while waiting for your meal.  We had the lasagna and scallop risotto.  Both were flavorful and ample portions.
The donuts were great at the Vegan buffet. Tuesday buffet is vegan. The family is very kind.

So very, very loud!  Music blaring so when you come into parking lot and hear the blaring music - it's that loud inside.  Grilled oysters are in shell with an array of spices.  Chips and an odd creamy salsa dip.  Different?  Mahi Mahi wrapped in bacon in a pool of green chili like sauce.  Food nice favors, staff knowledgeable about menu.  Many seafood selections are raw.  We left before finishing our drinks because our ears hurt.  Suggest carry out if you want to visit your dining mate.

Amazing onion rings.
didn't get a chance to try out the burgers or in fact any thing other than the rings. 
but as my infatuation for onion rings grew since my trip to santa barbara,
i am but a fan!

Worst Place ever! I've been treated better at a McDonald's on the wrong side of town. Staying two weeks on a business trip at Ameristar Casino and every time I've visited this place everyone acts as if it's an inconvenience to wait on me. This afternoon I tried to order two hamburgers to take to the room and was told that they quit taking to go orders at 6:30!! Saturday night 6:45 pm and I can't get something as simple as two burgers!!

Food is good, service is so so, depending on who you get on the or who waits on you.  Housekeeping is horrible!!  The washer / dryers are old and broken so don't do your wash there.  My guess is the privately held company doesn't put much money back into the place and it shows.

This was our first visit to Zim Zari and we were absolutely impressed!  Husband had a Sunburnt steak burrito with cheese & salsa and it was amazing!  Wife had the spicy Thai wok bowl, And that was equally amazing. We each had a draft beer that set our food off nicely. We thought the salsa that came with the chips to start the meal was the best we've ever had. And Eric, our waiter, did an outstanding job. We would definitely recommend this establishment and hope to return sometime from Michigan when it's possible.
My co workers and I decided to go to Meyers Front Porch for our monthly lunch. We were very pleased! The food was great and the sweet treats were delicious. I highly recommend!
Food was good and the place is decent enough, similar to other posts, it will do.

We are currently sitting at the restaurant right now. We had a 1:45 reservation and it is now 3:50 and we have not received one bite of food. We've asked to speak to the manager twice and no one has come to see us. The service is awful. No drink refills. No bread. This is AWFUL. I will never come to this place again.

Update..The time is now 5:40 and we just received our bill. This was an all-day event apparently. Of course, our bill is completely screwed up and we were charged for things we didn't even order. The manager still has not come to see us nor has attempted to make anything right. My uncle had to clean our table twice and remove all of the used dishes and silverware. We couldn't get drink refills so my uncle went and got the drinks himself. This is RIDICULOUS. Beware of this restaurant!

I went here with a group of Yelp elites for a devour downtown meal and it was absolutely picturesque and perfect. It might be one of the nicest, fanciest, delicious places that I've ever eaten. It reminded me of a restaurant that I'd see on the Food Network. The plates were small, but with multiple courses, and high-quality products, left me feeling fat and happy with lots to talk about to my friends and family.

The atmosphere is trendy, very pretty, and modern. The restaurant was dim, but it wasn't an issue while eating. It was the perfect amount of light and space and noise throughout the evening. We were eating a three course meal with wine pairings. Appetizers provided a wonderful prologue to the meal. I started my meal with an Old Fashioned made with Buffalo Trace whiskey and it might have been one of the best cocktails that I've ever had. Don Draper would have even been impressed.

For my first course, I decided upon the ham and grits starter. It was my first time trying grits, and I'm afraid that I'll be beyond disappointed with any grits after these. They were perfect. Made with Smoking Goose ham, grits, and other ingredients, it was the perfect combination of savory. For such a small amount, I found myself fighting towards the end because the plate was so dense. I absolutely loved it. My second course, the entree, I picked the fried chicken with cream, blackberry, and served with an egg. It was so delicious I can barely Yelp review it. It was fried chicken for breakfast, but without trying. Everything worked so well together. The end was the perfect touch to the meal. It was perfectly portioned and you didn't feel gross afterwards, something that sometimes happens when eating friend chicken. For my dessert course, I picked the Thai basil spongecake. I'm extremely glad I picked this. It was light, spicy because of the jalapeno/strawberry sorbet, but beautifully balanced by the basil gel. It was a really interesting and unique dessert. I wish I could get into the appetizers, but there were so many, and were so complicated, it would be hard to describe them all without writing a book. The wine pairings were all wonderful, too. If you are looking for a place to take someone special, impress them with Cerulean.

First time here and the kibbeh filling were pretty good. Outside a little thick but the yogurt was good and it had a lot of flavor. The mixed grill was tasty. Lamb was a little tough but the chicken was grilled to perfection.  Rice was fantastic and the pits could have used a little salt but great service. None of the serving staff were wearing masks which was a little weird to me but still tasty nonetheless.
The food is great and the food is GREAT. It's a must stop shop in new orleans. Get your oysters and po boy!

Yeah it's snowing like hell out. Yeah I'm hungry as hell at 8:30pm.  Maybe somewhat borderline hangry but the first 10 minutes in here spiked my BP a bit. 
I came in, saw the hostess, stated I'd sit at sushi bar.  I sat with my back to hostess, and now waitress, as the Snow meant someone was sent home early.  After peering over my shoulder several times over 5 minutes, the waitress finally came over.  I asked for a menu and hot tea. Another long period went by with no action so I got up to get a menu at the hostess station.  She then asked me if I was ready to order!! I snipped that I needed a menu first and she giggled all oriental.  Sorry, if that offends anyone but I bet you know what I mean with that description right? She then brings me the tea pot. Great right? Think I'm on a better course? No cup.  I have to wait until I see her to ask for one. More giggles.  
The bright spot was the sushi.  Without the soy dipping dish of course.  To avoid the giggle, I didn't ask for one.

They do a brisk business selling to drunk folks from 11pm-5am. The day time it's not so crowded. There really is no reason it shouldn't be packed either way. The hot sausage po'boy is good, a little greasy but definitely worth price, and it even comes with chips, which is not like many other places selling po'boys around the area. 

The menu is almost all po'boy along with some other New Orleans staples. What I like about this place is that the food is made right there but it takes so little time to get. The staff is pretty helpful, counter service is obviously not all the labor intensive but still friendly-especially since I meant one thing but said another and it was changed with no fuss. It's a nice change from the pizza places on Bourbon and definitely a good po'boy place.
This place was adorable. It was quiet, with great Italian food. Get the artichoke appetizer and lemonchello dessert!

Nothing like good ol fashion food and fun environment.  From the car shows to cherry coke with crushed ice. Its all great.  I have have been going here for almost 20 years and it's still the best burger and fries.  Check this place out. You will not be disappointed!

Consistently great food. Great drink and beer menu. Go to spot in west Chester. Their food is fresh and delicious. Rye rye birdie hands down best drink on the menu. I've also been here for brunch, just as good !

There's a first and a last time for everything. Not something I think I'd do again, but glad I did do it, and I think everyone should. It is a novel way to view our river valley from a very different perspective.
