Personally, I think it inspired me to find another watercraft to explore the river with, but I feel that this service does make the water-way more accessible to those who might find it very challenging to get out there, perhaps because they are not so able bodied to do so otherwise. There are ramps and a golf cart to ensure that everyone can get onto the boat

Speaking of the leisure cruise specifically, it would hold much more value for me if it was a tour. It could be a tour if it went a little further up and down the river (though I understand so that is dependent on the river level) and if there was some sort of guide to point out the sights and perhaps offer light entertainment with a few witty jokes and trivia about the sights and the boat itself. It could also use some kind of binocular service, either built in apparatus or rental/sale (for all I know, they might offer this in the office - it was not made apparent if they do). So, as a FYI, BYOB(inoculars).

I have some issues with the logistics of the design of the facilities. The second half of the load of passengers who boarded seemed to struggle to find shelter from the sun, and move around seats. Not just the last few stragglers, but about half. I think that's a lot of awkward discomfort that shows a bit of bad planning on the cruise company's behalf. Some of the chairs and tables could have been cleaner. I'm quite confident that the vast majority or passengers would agree that there are not nearly enough tables on board (perhaps those could be pre-booked, perhaps even at a cost). They'd likely sell more in the way of food if it was ensured that those who wished to eat had someplace to eat.

I tried the nachos and the sangria. I feel the nachos were over priced for what they are, very meh, large, but nothing special, and on par with nacho platters that are $5-8 cheaper elsewhere (If I'm paying for the cruise, don't gouge me on food prices). The sangria was alright and on-point for $20 for the pitcher, I have no idea why it's not printed in their menu though, they said it was a 'drink special', though seems to be an ongoing one and should be a staple. 

The staff was all quite professional, helpful and friendly.

So I know you want to have a great meal in a unique building that was once a Farriers, right?  Don't go running to Google yet, I'll fill you in.  Back in the days when Ben Franklin was walking the streets of Olde City a Farrier was a blacksmith that also had some veterinarian skills. This is where you brought your horse for new shoes.  Today you bring your hungry/thirsty self for delicious craft beer and inventive food.

I'm a sucker for restaurants that are rustic old buildings with lots of wood and heavy beams.   Olde City has quite a few and this is one of the best.  The front of the building has two huge barn doors (to bring in the horses of course) that can be opened during the summer.  This creates a unique experience that should not be missed.  It the winter there is a wood burning stove that's very nice.

These folks have a full bar but they specialize in unique draft beers.  They have about 15 taps and on a recent visit I enjoyed a delicious Troubadour Belgian Pale.  

So what about the food?  I've visited for lunch many times and dinner twice.  The lovely wife and I have also enjoyed Sunday brunch so I think I have a good handle on the food.  A lunch sandwich is going to cost you about $10.  It could be a burger or chicken or pulled pork, or even fish tacos.  There is a long list of extra toppings that go for $.50.  Of course the sandwiches come with good fries.  The Spanish Burger - $10.50 is to die for. A combination of ground beef and chorizo sausage with melted Manchego cheese and fries topped with sautéed onions, jalapenos and cheese.  Add a craft beer and I'm in heaven.  

Expect your entrees to be in the mid-teens.  I've enjoyed a pork loin dinner for $16.50.

When I was at Sunday brunch I tried the Huevos San Lucas - $10 which is three fried eggs served over house made salsa, grilled andouille, and nacho chips topped with melted cheese and fresh avocado. Delicious!

A word or two needs to be said about the service.  Several reviewers have commented on negative experiences.  My experience has been that while sitting at the bar my service has been excellent.  When at a table my experience has been mixed.  It appears that the servers are overworked and a bit undertrained.  

When I rate a restaurant I look at atmosphere, adult libations, food, and service.  Even though the service is sometimes a little off the overall experience is so great I'm going four stars.

Went here for brunch and got the buffet. They serve you gumbo and potato salad to start and both were very good. On the buffet they had fried chicken which was excellent, gumbo, jambalaya, grits, potatoes, and other stuff that I was too full to try. The neighborhood was full of very kind people as we left here we walked up to the back street cultural museum. In the day time it is very safe to walk around.

I come to CiCi's every other weekend with my boyfriend and his kids. It's definitely not super quality food but it's a great deal for the money. They have a salad bar and about 8-10 different Pizza choices. The thing that impresses me the most is that they will make a pizza for you if the kind you want is not on the buffet line. The staff are all very friendly. My favorite pizzas are the buffalo chicken and barbecue. They also have great cheesy bread.

My husband took me here to celebrate my birthday dinner in March.  Unfortunately I was really underwhelmed.  I really expected much more out of my dining experience.  It was really mediocre at best.  I think previous reviewers have all explained the menu extensively so I don't think I have to rehash it all....maybe it was just that we did not order the items that would make eating at Emeril's memorable?  They have an amazingly extensive wine list, but again the cuisine would not have matched up to such high end choices!  Some of the wines were in the $10k range?  

In gist we ordered the steamed crawfish as a starter.  This was a special of the evening and was okay.  My husband then ordered the Grilled Niman Ranch Double Cut Pork Chop with Caramelized Sweet Potatoes, Tamarind Glaze and Green Chile Molé Sauce and I had the Paneed Veal & Crisp Sweetbreads with Wild Mushrooms, Radicchio, Brabant Potatoes, Prosciutto, Sage and Lemon-Caper Crab Butter.  They sounded great on the menu, but from the actual experience it wasn't really anything mindblowing.  We actually ended up skipping dessert because we couldn't finish what we had ordered.  I think the fact that there was no real even minor attempt to treat a birthday guest with a small extra was also a slight off putting observation.  Not that I was expecting anything grand, but most restaurants do try to show some token of appreciation for customers celebrating a birthday.  As of now I will have to say that Emeril's gets a thumbs down from me.

What a cool place! I love the mission behind the business and their execution of a beautiful cafe is fabulous. The food is really amazing, the tea selection is great, and the space itself is gorgeous. It would be perfect for a very cool event!!

One of my new favorite spots! I went here this weekend to celebrate my graduation. We made reservations and were seated quickly. The service was good, but the food was even better. We took some of my family members who are extremely picky and even they had no complaints about the food. I would most DEFINITELY come back here. Can't wait to try out more items on the menu!

Tried again.

Excellent beer, perfectly chilled. Many choices.

Mega long line for cheap Amish donuts. The Apple fritters were glorious. Maple bacon, Nutella and glazed were ok but I would stand in line for another 30 minutes for the fritters and to try others. 
  I also made a couple of bucks since someone didn't wanna wait in line with his kid and wife so I bought his Apple fritters, haha.

Boulder Creek is perfect. Lauren is the best waitress there. We always ask for her. She is always so decorative with her cute buttons. If you want the best experience there ask for her as your waitress!

This place was amazing from start to finish. Their bacon infused bloody Mary's are perfect. I had the the cochon egg Benedict and the salmon egg Benedict (you can get 2 different kinds AKA the peace maker). Thinking about the cochon one has me drooling. The service was super friendly. Best brunch spot in Nola hands down
Third time here and quite possibly the last.. Service is slow, food is mediocre, staff not so friendly, beer watered down, I just can't wait until Winners Reopens..

We went last night and the food was great! My husband and I shared 2 vegetarian dishes which were incredibly tasty and our friends had a meat combo which they also loved. We shared a bottle of Tej which is an Ethiopian honey wine and is very sweet, goes great with the food. The service was great, very friendly and accomodating. Thank you for a wonderful meal!
Really friendly server who knew his stuff about beer! They got rid of the raspberry wheat but they added a new beer that has raspberry in it. The Golden Arm was good too, it's just like Golden Monkey
Always great pizza the family is huge it easily feeds 8 people when we have guests we get this have and it cut in squares.  Will come back again and again.

Not as good as the Main Street location.  Despite swimming in a vat of unknown fluid, the chicken was dry and flavorless.  And what's up with all these "Mexican grill" places charging extra for queso?  It's melted white American cheese with jalapeno juice and milk.  It doesn't make no damn sense.

Meh.

After a long drive from San Jose we were in search for a great restaurant. The FisHouse wasn't the best find, but it was ok since we were all starving. Tonya who was our waitress was good except for a mess up on one of our claim chowder orders.  I order the halibut ceviche. The chips were nice & salty, but the ceviche had too much lime juice. It overpowered the whole meal. It was so tart that I could barely finish half of it. My boyfriend had the New England claim chowder which he said was good. He also had the seafood pasta, which consisted of shrimp, scallops, and fish made with marinara sauce. The dish was huge, but lacked flavor. This was the same for the steam mussels & clams that were ordered. Such a waste of money I have to say.

Excellent! I got the Farmers Omlette, hash brown and biscuit. Big portions, delicious and fast! Coffee was fresh. My husband got a skillet. Said it was excellent and he opted for the diced potatoes and loved them! Service was attentive and safe.

Visited virago tonight with my wife in celebration of our 5 yr wedding anniversary and was majorly disappointed with the service. I made reservations for 9.15 and arrived at 9 and let the hostess know we were there, she said she'd call/text in 5 minutes as they were preparing a table. I got my wife and I a drink from the bar and left my tab open. We waited 45 minutes so I went back to the hostess and she said they're ready to seat us, no apology. When we sat down we had our drinks from the bar so I explained I had a tab open and asked if it could be transferred to our table she said "yes". Then she asked for my ID and I explained I have a tab running at the bar and she said, "well you could have just picked that wine up of another table". Considering the wait time and the fact that I had explained I had a bar tab running I found this insulting. We put an appetizer order in which ended up coming out after our entre and still no apology (the appetizer was terrible) This is my first yelp review but felt like I needed to write it as tonight was supposed to be a well deserved celebration which quickly turned into a waste of our time and $. I've dined at virago many times but I will never go back after tonight. If you get a girl with an English accent, be warned.

Update: after leaving the previous review Virago contacted me apologizing for our bad experience and they offered us dinner & drinks on them. We visited Virago yesterday eve and I have to say any bad taste that I had is now gone. The food, service & drinks were great. My faith has been fully restored in this place - I'll definitely be back!

No cover and not very crowded on a Thursday night. The waitstaff was pretty quick with our orders. Had a decent $8 dark and stormy. Philly totally needed a place like this. Being on the water right by the lit up bridge is really relaxing and made me feel like I was far away from city life. The music selection was a little confused. Besides the ambiance, the other best part is Little Baby's ice cream!

The hype is real for Shaya, and the wait for reservations is worth it. My wife and I like to pop down to NOLA in the winter as a quick escape from the cold north, and to enjoy some delicious food & drinks while down there, this time Shaya was on the list. It was incredibly tough to get a reservation, but we were lucky enough to get squeezed in on a Sunday evening for dinner. 

The vibe is trendy and lively, without an ounce of pretension, I dug it. We ended up splitting two appetizers and an entree, and as other reviewers have mentioned, you WILL eat too much. Come hungry! The food is just so flavorful and expertly prepared that you won't want to stop. It was without a doubt hands down the best Mediterranean food I've yet had, we both ate so much we woke up at 5am with raging indigestion from not wanting to stop once we were full. 

But it was sooooo worth it. We'll be back for sure.

Loved this bar. Everyone was super nice as well as fast service for how many people were in here. Security was very tight making sure no minors were able to get in. Loved having the juke box as well. Even when I didn't have coins for the juke box the bartender still played music we were all interested in!!!
Really fresh food, very attentive waitstaff, and the BEST falafel I've had in the area.
Just because you say you have gluten free food doesn't mean it has to taste like literally nothing. Awful...

I don't usually complain about service or give food service just 1 star but my experience with this location and their crew earlier tonight most likely will not have me return to this location again. If there was an option not to give any stars, I would have opted for it. 

It's an hour before they close and I pull up to the drive thru and order. I always butcher the deal (11pcs for $12.99) until the person manning the drive thru corrects me. I ask her if they have that same deal going on tonight and she said "no." I order something similar anyway and she ended her sentence with a total that was a little higher than usual and before I could say anything else she had already tuned me out. I drive up to the window and I hand her my card, I ask again as to how come the total is higher than it usually is (~$17 instead of ~$13). I'm assuming that she didn't understand the deal I was talking about so I ask her to cancel that and order a chicken tender meal instead. The total now hikes up to $25. She swipes my card before I could even ask her why the total was so much. At this point she's not listening to what I have to say and I just ask her to cancel the order and for my card back. I foolishly drive away without even thinking about asking for a receipt or proof of the cancelled transaction. 

I'm at the next parking lot over and I pull over because I had a sneaking suspicion that she and her nasty attitude weren't going to give me the refund for food I didn't receive or even want in the first place. My gut was correct and I make the decision to drive back over and go to the lobby to ask for the copy, hoping to resolve the issue and move on. Instead, I'm met with even more attitude. She saying and mumbling the "pleasantries" that you're supposed to say to a customer but with a scowl on her face and without even so much as looking me in the eye. I then get passed on to an employee outfitted in a blue button up shirt whom I assume is the shift leader for the night. He was a little better at attempting/ pretending to understand where I was coming from but by the end of the conversation, surprise surprise, he's also giving me attitude and not meeting my gaze. Not one apology for his employee's behavior even when she wrote "did not want to wait for order" on the receipt that was printed out even though I had asked her to cancel the entire thing. This tells me that she had NO intention of refunding me the money. He made it seem like the entire thing was my fault and that he was hurrying just to get me out the door. 

I would also like to mention that while I'm having this conversation with the "manager" the rest of the crew were speaking about me in Spanish thinking I wouldn't understand them and if that wasn't enough, they were snickering to each other and gawking at me. Having worked in retail and specializing in one-on-one customer service for nearly 10 years now, I have never been so baffled by the degree of indifference that this particular crew has for how they treat their customers. I've never been so disrespected by any place of business in my entire life as well. This location is in SERIOUS need of restaffing and training.
NEVER DISAPPOINT... If only they're closer!! BBQ, Kkanpoongi and their naengmyeon are yeshhhhhh!! Then dunk lemon or cucumber soju and you're all good for a while.

Waited an hour for our food to arrive. The waitress didn't seem to care after we asked about our food 3 times. We got the three stooges and the burger with a side of beef sausage....the burger was outrageously overcooked, potatoes were cold, scrambled eggs were cold and weirdly runny (couldn't eat them) and the beef bacon tasted like fish somehow. I'd really recommend NOT going...ever!

This place was totally fun for the atmosphere. The staff was cool and even forthcoming with shots of Jameson. I expected the food to be much more impressive, though. I ordered the fried crab claws to start (amazing), but the Coopers Taste platter that followed left a ton to be desired. I wouldn't go back for the food, but the bar tenders were kick ass, and for them, I would return. My advice? Come here after dinner for a few beers and kick back.

Just your average tex-mex restaurant. My friends and I decided to try this place out during our visit to Philly. The restaurant is really cute and they have some unique decor. The time we went was not packed we got seated right away. It wasn't too loud we were able to converse but it may be because there weren't many people there. I had an order of the carnitas tacos and they were good. The plantains con queso are a must if you like maduros. The tacos aren't anything out of this world but they're good. It's a bit overpriced but the food is decent. The waiter and manager checked-in on us a good amount of times. The food didn't take too long to come out. They were constantly refilling our glasses of water. The service overall was great. Not sure if I would go back there but it is a cute spot to visit!
Absolutely the best place to get breakfast at Santa Barbara. Amazing food and service.
Worst Moscow mule ever. The "ginger beer" tasted like flat 7-Up. The server just gave us more lime juice to make it "better". Try again...

Great dinner with friends..shared the punch, very refreshing. Bruschetta, all 3 were tasty. Flatbread was ok, lacking something but still pretty good. Trout w beet salad was excellent. Attentive service.
Best fast food place I've been to in a while. Very healthy choices, very delicious food! Had a lettuce-wrapped burger with fries and it was great.

A friend told me about Twisted Soul and I was pleasantly surprised! A hidden gem right on Market Street. The food was tasty and I picked up my food on my second visit for take out and learned that they have live music sometimes which was nice. Great atmosphere and nice setting. The only downside was the price. I found the prices to be a little high in comparison to other soul food restaurants locally. However the food was so good I soon stopped focusing on the price. Nice location for date night!

This IS the greatest Thai restaurant in St. Louis. My family has been dining here for years and the food is consistently amazing. The crispy spring roll appetizer is served with a lovely, tangy sauce and the vegetables inside always taste very fresh. The pineapple fried rice entree (with chicken) has a lovely combination of flavors; whole cashews, raisins, chicken chunks and sliced onion, to name a few. I would also highly recommend the Thai iced tea- yum! And DO NOT forget the best creme brûlée in St. Louis, my goodness! It is pure heaven served in an adorable ceramic mug. The torched sugar crust is unlike any other creme brûlée that I have tried, and I have tried many! The prices are very reasonable for the quality of the food, the restaurant is always clean and the service always fast. This place is a must-try!

I went to The Lark with my boyfriend for dinner last night. The service was great and the restaurant space is beautiful, but these were The Lark's only redeeming qualities. 

For such a pretentious menu, we were expecting to be blown away by the food. Instead, we shared three dishes (the liver and waffles, beef cheeks, and peanut butter mousse dessert) and we were disappointed with each one. The liver was fine, but the accompanying marmalade was overwhelming. The beef cheeks were tender, but extremely bland. The peanut butter mousse was oversalted and the caramel popcorn chunks in the dessert were nearly impossible to break apart. 

Perhaps we unluckily ordered the only three poor dishes on the menu. I doubt we'll be back to test that theory.

OMG I had the most delicious turkey sandwich here on wheat TOAST.  That's right, they toasted the bread without me mentioning it.  It was LOADED up with delicious turkey, not too salty, and they accommodated light mayo.  Plus it was fast - about 4:30 on a Sun., and they called me honey.  How sweet is that.  Fast check-out with 2 registers rocking.  They have to get you out fast, that place is so tiny but it gets it done.

I'm a huge fan of Suraya and was curious to see how a Lebanese powerhouse delivers Mexican food. The space is beautiful, and once you get past the host stand, does not feel like a hotel lobby restaurant. The menu is primarily corn-based, so this is a great spot for gluten-free options. I loved the Guacamole (which comes with 3 large Tostadas - you can get 3 more for $3 and will want them especially to try out the salsa selection) and the 4 Churros were probably the best I've had. I needed some translation help with the menu but the wait staff was friendly and patient and helped me pick the Suadero Chilango Taco, which was good. The food feels a little overpriced overall, but provides a solid option.

A abundance of crepes for my moms visit to town.

It's uncommon in Reno to find a true French cafe, French press and puffy crepes and all. 

Sparse in terms of space (5 tables), like a true French brasserie, nestled on the edge of a strip mall of all places.

For a second, you can be teleported from the suburban jungle to a quieter Parisian experience. 

They had a fair selection of French crepes (a bit thicker than a true French crepe) with both sweet and decedent option.

I went here recently because I've been seeking out places that are known for their wings. I'm gonna just say it, I don't understand what all the fuss is about. The wings weren't good. Not even a little. Lots of chewy, fatty pieces with little meat and the flavors weren't good either. I will admit the honey sauce was good (I ended up dipping my finger in the sauce a few times and eating it). I read that the staff is rude but that wasn't the case for me.

This place missed the mark for us. The place was completely empty on a Thursday night. We ordered a pizza, wings and a salad. It took nearly 45 minutes to get everything. I wouldn't call anyone who worked here friendly. The wings were rubbery and had barely any sauce on them. The sauce on the pizza tasted like chef boyardee sauce, weird and sweet. The salad was fine but it's hard to mess up lettuce that is dumped out of the bag. The kitchen staff appeared unkempt and unclean. I understand they were making delivery orders but it should not have taken that long for what we got, considering the lack of traffic in/out of this place. Would try again, but wouldn't get the same things we got this time.

I had to read the directions twice: are we really headed to a restaurant in a grocery store? Yep! Seating was quick and comfortable: those great plush booths that you just sink into. The service was friendly and professional. The menu, although not extensive, was creative and appealing. The cocktails were excellent - everyone tried one and everyone had a favorite. We wish we had room for dessert but left with a doggy bag. We will definitely return.

The boyfriend ordered IV Deli Mart delivered a couple nights ago, and it was delicious! I finally tried the wings from here he was raving about for weeks and they were GREAT. Super flavorful and I couldn't stop eating them! They're also cheap. We also ordered the honey and spicy chicken sandwich, which was also really good. The bread was kind of soggy (might have happened just to ours though) but everything else was tasty. The sandwich was HUGE, so we shared half and saved the other half for later. For the price, I would definitely recommend this place if you want a sandwich and/or wings!

One of my go-tos in Indy. I love it for brunch and dinner! Also a great place to take your folks when they're in town.

$14 bottomless mimosas can't be beat at a higher end spot like this.
Dinner options are also fantastic but I always seem to go back to the rockfish tacos! They seem boring and "healthy" but they really are absolutely incredible. And as basic as it seems, the house fries and ketchup are what dreams are made of. 

Don't forget to try the "mess" for dessert! Keeps me coming back.
Really enjoyed the food drive-in totally  great staff I was there a couple of days ago, corn dog mashed potatoes and gravy. Other day :I've had the  meatloaf sandwich was great:

The food is very good. I enjoy the service, at times it could be better but when it's busy you have to understand the servers can't spend as much time at each table. My daughter and I really enjoy coming here, to me it's a real nice addition to the Blue Bell area.

Worth the 45 min drive for me! I had a Caesar which was perfect with just enough spice, my friend and I shared a poutine (it could have had more cheese and thinner fries but otherwise it was very delicious), I had the beef bourguignon which was perfectly cooked and the bacon and mushrooms that came with it were very delicious. Then I had the molasses brown bread pudding. I was a little skeptical about the blueberries with it but it was just perfect. Service was great- my water glass was never empty, and the atmosphere is rustic and comforting with the lights dimmed. I thoroughly enjoyed Chartier and absolutely recommend it.
Their manager Katie made it very easy for me to pay for my sisters breakfast from California for her birthday! Thank you for making it so easy and being patient!
Bomb food but today seems long for them so they accidentally forgot some sauces/ silverware and I just went inside and got them in seconds

Great Tavern , Good draft beer , Good service. But unfortunately our food was not so good . The typical bar food was good, jalapeño  poppers, chicken fingers and nachos. (But you can get those anywhere) Sorry , not impressed with the wings, they seemed old., and the Mussels in red sauce were bad! They Smelled bad, half were mushy and not edible. The red sauce seemed like canned tomatoes poured on top. Not sure who was running the kitchen on this Friday evening. Sorry! 
Note : Our server did comp  us for the mussels.

What can I say about Eden that hasn't been said about heaven. If you are looking for traditional, home cooked hearty Korean food look no further. First off let's start with the atmosphere- don't come here looking for some super fancy setting. This is a restaurant that screams "we focus on food"
There's multiple TVs, booth seating, ample parking and clean bathrooms. The staff? Super sweet. The older Korean woman whom I assume is the mother of the two other servers is probably the sweetest woman on this planet. She's very attentive to your needs, has an infectious smile and a laugh that will make your visit enjoyable every time. The choices are great, I've had the kimchi Chigae, tofu stew,  and the galbi. Each time has never let me down. The marinade is ON POINT, the stews and soups are extremely flavorful, with huge portions, and the side dishes are to die for (especially the garlic stems). everything is reasonably priced for the amount you get. My gf and I are forever customers. Thank you for the amazing service and the amazing food.

Maybe we came in on the wrong night (Tuesday at about 6pm).  The place was jam packed crowded. We just wanted some pub food, but it was not to be had.  We stood around for an hour trying to get a table, but as soon as one became available, people were all over it like a hoard of locusts.  Yes, the beer was reasonable, but it's very difficult for me to stand for an hour when I'm still trying to get over a broken hip.  Forget about talking to anyone.  You pretty much have to scream in their ear. If you are taking someone on a date, go some place quieter.  If you are going with a group, find someplace else where you can at least get a chair or a bar stool.  We finally gave up and went back to the hotel. The prices were a lot higher but the atmosphere was a thousand percent better.

Holdren's is located on state street passed the freeway overpass. The area is full of restaurants and bars. They closed down the street and set up a bunch of open air tables and chairs. It's super cool and lively. Parking is a little difficult so it's better to park down a few blocks and walk on over. Holdren's has modern steak house vibe. Our waiter read friendly and really took his time with us. We ordered the bacon wrapped stuffed shrimp apps which was delicious. The sauce was a sweet chili sauce. It could've been a little spicer but complimented the shrimp well. We shared the Cowboy Cut. It was cooked perfectly and came with some amazing onion rings.

Steamed dumplings, pan seared dumplings, rangoons, and the shrimp tempura roll were good. Fried dumplings were good but had to remove some of the wrapping, and the spicy tuna tempura roll seemed a little heavy on the batter. Will go again and try other things since the price is good! Also I'm sure things fresh in store would make it even better than the 20 min drive home.

My fiancé and I came in last night (05/13/17) around 7-7:30pm. There were a few people at the hostess stand no one greeted us. Finally after the other staff cleared out we went up to the girl standing there ( I think her name is Cathy? Maybe) and told her we would like a table for two. She looked at us and walked away. Walked around the restaurant confused. Came back and said hold on I will be back. Walked up to the sitting area stood in front of a table for about 5 minutes. She came back and was like "uh we have to see if we have anything to accommodate you. But you can sit at the bar and order there. " she was making it seem like we were a party of 15. We were just two people. Give us a table with two chairs. It wasn't rocket science but she made it way more complicated. The place wasnt overly crowded. didn't let us know if there was even a wait or anything. Plus there was plenty of sitting at tables around the bar and a few in the seating area so I'm not sure why we weren't offered that. We never had a problem before but will probably not be back now.
Great food, fast and friendly service. Fried Cornish hen yummy. Dessert was amazing- the cupcakes:) Gin distilled here and yum. Easy walk from our hotel.

ok although we didn't actually eat here, just drinks, we saw how large the portions were and were impaled by the delightful scents wafting from the kitchen. based on that, we will definitely be back!!!
all that being said, I am writing this review purely based on my senses and the wonderfully friendly and attentive bartender that served my mother and I on our most recent visit. 
no one told me that shots in new Orleans are equal to a full glass NYC style but gotdamnit I appreciate it. to put it another way, the extra heavy handed bartender wowed me with his charm attitude and overall bar experience. the bar itself is pretty small and located directly across from the kitchen.  they had an exceptional variety of bourbon and that awesomely friendly bartender (can you tell I am a fan yet) offered me a taste of another bourbon I had never heard of!!!
cant wait to go back and taste, not just drink, on my next visit!!!

We went to dinner with anticipation to Copper Pig on Friday night, their 2nd night open. We live a block and a half from this restaurant and have been waiting for it to open.

We were not disappointed. Copper Pig is an upscale but casual dining restaurant that mixes Korean and American dishes into new and fantastic flavors, and also incorporates one of my favorite meats, pork!

Do you love it already? I know, it gets better. We dined on the bacon jam with melted brie appetizer served with toasted baguette chips. My husband thought the bacon jam was pretty sweet and is not a huge fan of brie, but everything clicked with me, and I declared it heaven in a bowl!

We ordered sandwiches, the bulgogi cheesesteak and the three little pigs, with fries and tatertots. Both sandwiches were very filling and the sides were fried to perfection, just the way you would want them. 

My husband's three little pig sandwich was a great blend of flavors. A pork cutlet, ham and bacon jam joined with a fried egg over-easy makes for a mighty sandwich! The great thing is that each part tasted great individually, and together, it is all a mouthful of goodness! 

I decided to write this review today after finishing the other half of my bulgogi cheesesteak, because it was really delicious the 2nd time around. It was a large sandwich with cheesesteak style beef bulgogi. There is also Kim chi and melted cheese. It worked well, and I will order it again after I make my way through the rest of the menu.

Our server was very nice and attentive, although forgot to mention specials, but those are also listed on a chalkboard by the bar, so check there too. She more than made up for it by keeping my water glass full, and doing a great job checking on us. Because of opening week, we were greeted by the owner and manager, and we were glad to give good reports. 

The atmosphere is clean and cool, and I noticed sitting by the windows that in the summer, they could open up. Very cool.  I can't wait to go back! After a few more experiences like this, I am sure it will be 5 stars in my book.
The sweet chili sauce is amazing especially with literally everything! The staff was very nice and they give great recommendations

So I visited Chicago in September and thought there is no way that Uno pizza could compare to anything in the city known for its pizza...Wrong!  Uno knows what they are doing, from the delicious buttery crust to getting a pizza out in under 15 minutes, the pizza is pure Chicago without the wait.  I found no difference from what I ate in Chicago to Uno, it's clear their heart and flavor come right from the Windy City!  Thank you!

Steak was amazing!  Food is awesome!  Little over hyped on the hotel tourist channel.  And is a expensive for sure!  Not kid friendly (aka a steak house with no steak options for kids).  We split a 22 oz ribeye, mushroom risotto, and brocillie.  That and 3 drinks came to $100.  Don't get me wrong, it was awesome food!  Just a little over sold.

We decided to go to Oceana for breakfast in our way to a swamp tour. Their menu said they had crepes, and all the reviews were good. I mean, how bad this place could be if they had an average of 4 stars? We are in New Orleans, and the food is great everywhere! Oh, boy, was I wrong. First of all, this place feels like a dump. We ordered crepes with shrimp, lobster, green peppers and something else. What I got was this huge burrito, the size of a new born baby. All good so far, but then I tasted it: it was greasy, salty, nasty. My daughter ordered a dessert crepe, and hers was old and cold. Huge, mind you. My daughter end up eating an English muffin. After spending over $50 on the most terrible breakfast, we rushed to our tour. 15 minutes later, my stomach felt funny, and I barely made it to a nearby bathroom. I ended up with the worse upset stomach, and I felt sick throughout the day. Needless to say, we regretted our decision dearly. So beware. I have no idea if dinner food is any good here, but breakfast is atrocious. So stay away.

Been going to El Rey Azteca since they first opened in Mt. Juliet. They have come a long way as far as the interior, bar, etc. One thing that has never changed is the food and service. This is the best Mexican food I have eaten and I have tried them all, even in Mexico. Service is friendly, fast, and competent. Memo and the boys do a fantastic job. I don't drink Margaritas very often, but let me tell you...their Texas Margaritas are the tastiest, most potent you will ever drink. Order by the pitcher or 1/2 pitcher; don't waste your time with a glass. The best chili rellenos anywhere. Also love their combo plates, house-made chunky guacamole, and the shrimp/chicken fajitas. Great place for us gringos to get our Mexican on. Best thing is that it is only 2 miles from my house. Highly recommended!
The view from this place is a must!!! Come to watch the sun goes down while you drink a glass of wine or a beer. I tried their food once and it was really yummy. It's a place everyone should visit!!!

This place is an unknown gem. I really hope it survives because everything was absolutely delicious and I can't wait to try more things! We got the bruschetta, my mom got eggplant parm, I got stuffed rigatoni in vodka sauce. So good!  Our waiter was such a sweetheart. We also got dessert, the carrot cake and the chocolate lava cake. They both had a awesome decoration on it and they were so good. I definitely recommend trying this place.
Just awesome... great authentic Italian market vibe. First time here, picked up a Hot Italian sandwich... excellent, quality and fresh!
Realllllllly great Italian style pizza and dishes (not Italian American style).  Cozy and hopping neighborhood feeling crowd.  Homemade tomato sauce was ridiculously good.
Left 10 min after sitting down. Horrible quality hookah. Disgusting environment. Ripped couches. Prices are ridiculous. Never coming back again
I love this place best food in town the chicken kebab is very good come in try for your self no Dout bout this place very very good
AMAZING!! The best Mexican I have had in Philly. The guacamole, quesadillas, and burrito were on point. We can't wait to go back to eat inside instead of ordering out!
Love this place, best Cubans around. When I am on that side of town always go by there. Prices are good.
The Key Lime Pie ice cream was amazing! Best ice cream I've had in Indiana, by far.

We were excited to try this restaurant! We arrived in the pouring rain and got what we thought was the last parking spot. Score. It was about 745 so I wanted to get some sponges from the precious soap shop on the corner. We started down there and were just about to cross the little street and an employee from costas ran out and told us the parking was only for patrons of the restaurant to which I responded that I just wanted to get some sponges before dinner. He said oh. Ok. That's fine then. I asked my husband to move the truck to the little road we were about to cross. Took 1 minute and we went on to buy our sponges, soaps and baklava to take home and then went to an amazing dinner at Mamas. When we left I was shocked to see a big empty parking lot for costas around the corner. WOW!! Still gets my goat today. In fact I joined Yelp just because of it. But on to reviewing all the other places we go.

I've been to this chipotle twice. The first time I went, the portions were very small compared to every other chipotle that I've been to. So disappointing that I didn't come back for months. I decided to give it another try and had the same result--portions so small that I should've been paying half price. Don't go here. Whatever manager runs this place is trying to cut costs by encouraging employees to serve tiny portions. Food tastes fine, and the place is clean, but you're not getting your money's worth.
The food comes out fast, hot, and the kids meals comes in this cute presentation with a snack! Kids eat free on weekdays 3-9pm. Nice family restaurant to grab a meal. Clean and awesome service
I love the cheese steak service is always great n fast

Try their soft pretzels, they're amazing, just kidding, they're really awful and they ought to get rid of them because they can do way better than frozen jokes. Everything else we had was great though!

I guess that's what I get for being slightly hungry for small salty bites and beer. My bad.
Good food and nice people.  They give out free samples at the counter.

First let me start by saying that we had a reservation for 8, showed up at 7:30 but wasn't seated till 8:30. But we had a few drinks while waiting at the bar and bartender (Amber)  made up the for the hour wait. Our waiter was Andrew, a cool guy! Made some recommendations to the menu.  For appetizer we had the MD crab soup and a dozen of oysters and buffalo shrimp. I also had 1.5 of lobster bake. Clams and mussels were ok. Not very flavorful. Enjoyed the meal overall. Happy with Andrew being able to bounce back from late seating.

Fries ok, ordered delivery and they sent me a different drink than I ordered oh well.
Burgers average to a bit better than but very pricy value/point

Update second order of cheeseburger was delicious, bump up a star

I don't really like cupcakes. Never had. They are one of those things in life that I've felt I "should" like, because they have some kind of intrinsic "virtue" or something like that, but cupcakes never did anything for me. I had heard a lot about Crushcakes, and thought "well, maybe this will be on another level, maybe this will be the cupcake that opens my eyes, provides me with the bliss of finally understanding why people love cupcakes.  I had hoped for a superior cupcake that went beyond the normal cupcake.

Didn't happen. The cupcake was just like all the others I've had.  It was.....ok......after I ate it I thought "why the hell did I just waste my money on this"?

The woman behind the counter served me with all the friendliness and enthusiasm of a DMV employee. I felt like I was a black guy walking into a Woolworth's in Birmingham, Alabama in 1948 with a big "Whites Only" sign.

I should have given the money I spent on that cupcake to the homeless guy in a wheelchair who wheels around State Street asking everybody for money.

OH, and one more thing: Why do so many grown people use the word "Yum" in these reviews? More than that, why, in the name of all that's holy, WHY WOULD ANY ADULT USE THE WORD "NOM" OR "NOMMY"??????????? I just find that really nausea-inducing, to read that someone thought the burgers were "Nommy" or "Nom". Why do people seem to revert to baby talk when speaking about food???

I just hate that.
One of my favorite spots for happy hour and appetizers. Love the shrimp tamale, Guinness cheese fondue, pork tacos. Good value. Nice vibe. Clean and well maintained. Friendly and helpful staff.

Decent. The room could be updated. There wasnt much of a view. Had to cut the trip short. Still had a few nights left, but the 24 hr rule applies, so i got a refund for just the last day. At least they didnt charge crazy check out fees.

Amazing food, seriously amazing. Every time I come to this part of Philly I go to Holme Circle to eat here. There is a minor problem, though: incredibly slow but sweet staff. I mean I've seen them comp a $75 tab because the cooks were slow. Takes forever to get out of there once you're done. And the manager just walks around scoping out the dining room and doesn't help at all. I'd be annoyed AF if he was my boss. But it's so worth it for that food. Mac and Cheese, those fries, the bread, and the duck: man, this place will fill you up.
Awesome place.  Ordered the bbq shrimp, don't be cool, where the bib...you be happy after you save that $100 shirt.  Food was fantastic and would order the same on my return visit.

Nice steak, great cocktails. There for a birthday dinner. The menu was printed with Happy Birthday ______! Nice touch! Before we left, the hostess came over and took a picture of the table and asked how many copies we would like of the picture.
What we didn't like-besides the exorbitant bill ;-) -it is very loud.

The food was horrible the garlic knots under cooked and the sauce on the side tasted burnt, the brownie was scorched on the edges and bottom, pizza was just sloppy wet mess. this is the worst food ever.

This place is okay.  It's a nice place to go meet up with friends and catch up, but it's not a place where I'll go if I am hungry and craving for a certain thing.  I like the smoke salmon with pumperknickle, but I like anything with smoke salmon. It's hard to mess up a lox. We ordered sandwiches to share: meatloaf, fried chicken, fish, and smoke salmon.  My favorite was probably the fried chicken.  We also ordered Lisa's Corn Bread as an appetizer.  IT WAS REALLY GOOD! I lied, if I crave corn bread, I'll come here and order to-go! I probably would come back in the future if my friends wants to go.

Friends and I all live right in the neighborhood, and Royal Thai is our go-to for quick and great Thai food. The curry dishes are hands-down the best part of their menu, and we can't go without one (or all!) of us getting one of them. Green curry is my favorite, but I've enjoyed them all. They're great about catering to vegetarians. Prices are pretty reasonable. Check out the lunch special for the best deals-- served until 3pm. Great for eat-in or take-out.

We've never had a disappointing experience at Royal Thai, despite what some others have said here about their own. It's always been dependable, and we prefer it to the others in the neighborhood.

So I've always been loyal to the store that I worked at for almost 8 years but my loyalty is gone. This store has just gone down hill so bad it's depressing. It's dirty, it's service is just awful and I feel so bad for my friends still working there because it's apparent management DOES NOT CARE!!! I stopped in there last night and the hostess is just so rude and unkempt, she sat us at a dirty table, pulled out the chair and hit me with it. Layed down the silverware and menus and walked away. We sat there 15 minutes and the server never acknowledged our existence. So we got up and left and went to the Cracker Barrel in greenfield much cleaner and more country fresh. Post road Cracker Barrel is a ghetto and like I said I feel bad for my friends that are still working there because management is so out of touch with the reality of the situation of this store.

I wouldn't bother to eat Spanakopita anywhere else.....these folks have the absolute best !!  It is crisp and flaky and rich, and the delectable center melts in your mouth !   It tastes JUST like it is supposed to taste.  Anywhere else I have eaten it, it is soggy and fairly tasteless.   The Harrira soup is fabulous, also.   It is chock full of flavor and vegetables!  I feel really lucky that Norma's is right on my way home from work !   They also have nice staff and service :)

I went in to this experience with no expectation other than the facade was pretty. Upon entering, there's no hostess or person to greet you,  to let you know the protocol to get a table. Approaching the bar, I was told to pick a table anywhere. So I picked a table in the courtyard(pretty weather with a lovely temperature), best part of the entire meal. The second best part of the meal was our server. He was prompt and attentive. The menu looks interesting and intriguing. The idea of using a sushi styled check box menu is fun, yet not needed for a menu that would easily fill half of an 8 1/2 x 11 sheet of paper. Next, someone needs to tells the kitchen, that restaurant is not sponsored by Morton Salt. Every item that was eaten had copious amounts of salt. So, we started with the radishes. Salted butter as a spread for raw veggies, not a problem tasted great. English peas were delicious seasoned appropriately, the cauliflower cream so yummy. Chopped salad with pickled veggies, at first was appetizing. Then we realized, that as we were encouraged to share our plates of food-tapas style- an additional salad was brought out that hadn't been ordered. Trust me one is enough. A salad vinaigrette should be used in moderation. I mean the restaurant took time to pickle their own vegetables, why not showcase them. Instead, the only taste to be found was an overly salted dressing that covered the beautiful colors and taste of the vegetables. Moreover, I'm not a fan of when a restaurant chooses to not list major ingredients on a menu(when a description/list has been given). So, we moved on to the Bolognese. No where on the menu does it mention fried chickpeas, at least I think it was chickpeas, there was at least a cup on top of the dish. The flavor of this item was similar to that of when you eat a Bolognese a day after it has been cooked by grandmother and then someone in the family, without any reason or tasting, chooses to re-season the sauce. The dish mentions spaghetti squash(it's puréed or whipped), it's not like the stringy spaghetti squash some squash connoisseurs may be used to. Either way, it won't matter what type of squash was in the dish because the only flavor that could be found was salt, salt, salt. There are culinary measures to correct these instances; though, I'm not sure those techniques are known to the kitchen staff. Sliding into the end of the meal, we selected the pork chop. I had real hopes for this item. It was the main reason I'd selected this location for dinner after looking over the menu. Upon arrival, the broccoli rabe looked charred(wasn't a great flavor-just burnt). The porkchop, which felt more like a pork loin, was not trimmed of it's fat. That is no a problem for me because that usually helps with flavor and holding in moisture. One bite is all it took to stop. It tasted like a salt. I stopped and that point my meal was over. My tongue started itching on the sides from all the salt. I hope this location gets some sense of salt levels with their food. They had some great products and wonderful platting. The flavors were just all over the place and need to reigned in. In closing, there may be another try here but I'm gonna need a bit to process all this sodium out of my body.

We wanted to be low key today for Easter.  Our friend Charles had been telling us about this restaurant and hearing from client's nothing but wonderful things.  All true.  We were able to get in short notice and service was friendly, quick and quite frankly we were very impressed. We ate downstairs, because we did call ahead to reserve a table, and if you do, they will seat you downstairs.  However, if you take your chances, they have a beautiful upstairs, outdoor patio that is covered.  The perfect day for it, although we choose to stay indoors.  Best ManMosa I've ever had, The bisquits were something my grandmother would make.  Besides the great food, ALL the STAFF enjoys working there! Friendly smiles welcome you and they are proud to let you wander through to check out the place.  VERY, VERY WELCOMING!  On my top 5 list in tampa now.  We will be spending lots of time there...Thanks for great EASTER brunch...

Love the ambiance of the place and the customer service there was good. We got seated right away despite it being pretty crowded on a Sat evening. 4/5 Star since I didn't think their selection of beer was super impressive .
Mediocre food, 1 hr wait for food, slow service, had to clean the table to sit down when we first arrived! Has potential! Could've just been a bad day! The manager Mike was really nice

I come here time to time for lunch I get the combo number 6 which is 15 wings. the food is always good but the wait time to get it is always extremely long. This stuff is nice and they have the games on when I go in
Great food and great service! Crab cakes are delicious! Everyone cleaned their plates!

It reminds me a bit of NYC pizza joints where you have to move quickly through the line, although the people are much, much nicer.  I had the Gladiator lunch deal, as that seemed the only way to go for my first visit to Joey's!  Excellent choice!!!  I look forward to many return trips, and I look forward to trying some of the other items, as they all looked really good.  Get there early.  1115a, and the line was already about 15 people out the door.  We were able to find seating for two fairly quickly, though.

Soooooo good! We waited quite a long time to get our order taken, but there was only one waiter... but besides that, the food came out super fast! And everything tasted amazing. I got to taste the pad thai, basil fried rice, red curry, and green curry and ALL of them were yummmmy!!

This chick fil a is definitely sub par.. I would rather walk into the mall and get my chick fil a than go here. Just overall better customer service , friendlier people and better food. Don't get me wrong this is still a chick fil a so I love it. But it's definitely not the same, the fries always seem to come out under cooked, which is annoying. They almost always seem to forget a straw when I go drive thru. But 3 stars just for them being a chick fil a.

What an absolute gem of a restaurant! While in Tucson for a meeting we found the Polish cottage. The interior of the restaurant is warm and welcoming, like sitting down and in your own dining room.  I ordered the perogie dinner with a combination of potato and cheese and sweet formers cheese perogies.  My husband ordered the half portion stuffed cabbage and it was delicious and a huge portion. It reminded him of the stuff cabbage that his German mother made, except better!  Highly recommend this wonderful restaurant anytime you're in Tucson and looking for a good home cooked meal.

Just a girl from Houston, Texas who LOVES seafood! Everything is truly bigger in Texas, but I have to admit the lunch portions are HUGE! I recently relocated to Hermitage and my mom and I decided to eat lunch here. The service was amazing! I just wish I could place an order togo when they are on a wait, but I promise I have "time"  so I can deal with the small things for amazing food and service.
So delicious! We always get the tacos and steak quesadillas. Their cheese is sooooo delicious!

The iced Turtle Latte half sweet is very good. The California is awesome. Love their sourdough bread. The Gail salad is delicious. The lemon garlic vinaigrette. Very subtle lemon and vinegar taste. Cool atmosphere and super friendly service.  Looking forward to trying more of their delicious food and drinks.

First time with the wife and kids and I will be back with friends. The people were very welcoming when we entered and the waitress was excellent. We ordered regular pizza, arancini, fries, and a cibo salad. I really didn't know what to expect but we were pleasantly surprised. All of the food was delicious. I love the brick oven pizza that was  crispy and well done to perfection. The cheese was excellent , perhaps a blend of mozzarella and other cheeses. The sauce was on point! Salad was fresh and dressed with a lemon infused olive oil... perfectly done and refreshing . You must try the arancini , unbelievable! You can tell they are home made , and I love the idea of incorporating pesto with rice and cheese... scrumptious!!

Wasn't impressed. Friday night was a bust here for us. I mean we did get in free and got a free Jell-O shot coupon but the music was WACK. Upstairs loud
Techno and downstairs --more like Spanish night--no hip hop at all so we left and went elsewhere. It would be nice to play a variety instead of just one genre and not a mixture.

Best new spot in STL! The trendy atmosphere sets the bar high, but the food far surpasses it. Not your typical menu with a great selection of cocktails. Be sure to explore the hotel and rooftop bar after your meal!

Had a few drinks with friends here last week and loved the vibe. Was really packed but managed to grab two stools at the bar. Beer selection is great in bottle but a little weak on tap, so that is a good opportunity for improvement.
Great place to relax and fight a hangover!! Food was great, and the guys behind the grill were super nice and funny.  Nice little find amongst a touristy part of town.

Overrated.

Now that Malvern is going through a revitalization/modernization of sorts, places like the local Christopher's easily give the Pig a run for it's money.  Sure, it has a certain charm.  Beer selection is decent.   But I've eaten here multiple times and darned if I don't remember a single dish I've gotten here.  Maybe the beer is to blame?  I dunno.  It's cool, worth trying once, but again, vastly overrated.

I'm not a vegetarian or vegan but this place makes food in such a way that I don't miss meat. Everything here tastes great. Staff is supper friendly, fast service and attentive as well. It's BYOB. Definitely worth the 30 minutes trip just to get here for me. Will be back
Had dinner here the other night. Food was not dissapointing. Everything I ate as good. Wife though the serloin was a bit under done for her liking but I was all over it. You won't go away hungry
Love this place!!!! Delicious food with fun options on the menu. And the beer is great!! Warm atmosphere with wonderful staff. Highly recommend!!!
Such a cute little place! The food is very good; some of the best Italian food we've ever had! The service was good too.

I'm a fan of this lovely french spot nestled under the oaks of Esplanade Ave in the heart of mid city. I don't think it has the best food in New Orleans but the semi outdoor atmosphere and the good food, warm service and consistency makes it a favorite spot of mine to dine in that area.

Short review: Go. Now. Order a bit of everything.

More words: Sometimes you have a culinary experience that is inspired. That would describe our visit to Setsun. Chef Jason Zygmont prepared dishes rich in flavor, interesting, nuanced, and restrained. My mom and two sisters were in town for our annual getaway and Setsun provided a perfect last meal in Nashville. We ordered two "bit of everything" tastings for the four of us, and we are still arguing over which was our favorite. The oysters had a green curry mignonette that did not compete with the oyster but held its own; the shaved meats were a nice beginning to our meal. Then came the long beans and the heirloom tomatoes with toast. Each was prepared with a sauce that required extra toast so we didn't leave a taste on the plate. The grilled baby corn was charred to perfection; the beef tartare showed the mastery of the knife with subtle flavor profiles that let the beef speak, and the ribs fall off the bone good. But, it may have been the fresh pasta that stole the night - the ricotta agnolotti and the spaghetti pomodoro took the meal to a whole next level. Whether it was the fresh pasta or the ricotta or the sauces that partnered with the pasta, both were dishes that hooked us on the first bite. Callie, our server, paired each course with wine from the selection of interesting varietals on hand; she also made the night fun. Finally the chocolate soufflé with the peanut anglaise brought it home. We left happy for sure!

Absolutely fantastic place. Customer service, food menu, atmosphere, drink menu, etc was all great. Pricing was: appetizer, 4 drinks, 2 entrees, and 2 deserts for under $100. Everything was high quality and unique flavors. This is not your average "Italian" restaurant.... Convivio is absolutely authentic Italian. It is equivalent to high end cuisine in Italy. Plus, it's in downtown Zionsville which is great to enjoy before and after dining. Don't forget the large park behind the town.

Great place! I would recommend!
Whatever free Indian chip thing they give you at the table are awesome.
The samosas are good. I liked the tangy, sweet sauce.
The spicy crab naan okay. Nice flavor but I might try a different naan next time.
Chicken saag and the lamb korma were really good. The chicken saag was very creamy! I loved it.
They had a complementary dessert. Was almost like sticky, Sweet polenta. Didn't have much of a mango flavor.
Service was excellent. They even have me extra rice to take home with my leftovers. Super attentive.
The restaurant is clean, comfortable, and nicely decorated.
I would definitely come back for the saag and to try other stuff.

If you're in the French Quarter, you have many more  options you should take advantage of, this shouldn't be one of them. The female bartender is openly rude, hostile and aggressive and the male bartender supports her in that behavior. She spent the majority of the time we were there taking shots with customers next to us which didn't help her demeanor. She tried to throw a guy out of the bar for simply waving at her, which she tried to justify by saying she has to put up with so much - well honey, you're a bartender in New Orleans, you should have an idea of what to expect going into the job. The bouncer seems like a reasonable guy but if you'd like to have a good night, I'd suggest you try one of the many other bars around the area.

Went with a group of 5 people....had multiple dishes.. and EVERY SINGLE THING was amazing. 

Not much else to say. Other than the (understandable) wait, this place was near perfect. 

Oh and I don't usually care about such things, but our server (cool guy w/glasses been there a while) was also an additional huge plus to the evening. 

Go here. Can't wait to go back. 



It's better in every possible way to Bayona...

Owney's BottomLine: Hey I'm drunk and I need some food....oh hey, pizza. 


Pizza is ok. Servers were cool, one was cute (bonus) and the crowd was from some post-apocalyptic world, except not run over by zombies, but by strippers and other sluts.

Needless to say I will be back for the beer and scenery, but I will eat elsewhere beforehand.

Went here for lunch today with my daughters.

The good: Hamburgers! Especially the guacamole bacon burger. This is what one of my daughters ordered. The only reason I knew it was good was because we ended up sharing it. My meal was so bad I ended up sending it back and the waitress did not offer to bring me anything else.

The bad: 
1. Chicken avocado wrap. One half had no dressing which made it tasteless, the other half was doused in it which made it soggy and overly spicy. 

2. Service. Our server was inexperienced and completely clueless. She got 2 out of 3 of the orders wrong...which had to be corrected by someone else. She came back and asked how everything was and left before I responded. I flagged her down and I told her she could take my plate because the wrap was awful and she took it away without saying anything. Later I asked her to take it off my bill and she asked what was wrong with it, but didn't offer to bring me anything else. She dropped off our bill and for some reason did not come back to pick it up. She finally came back and said she forgot about us. During our meal a lady at another table in her section came over and asked to borrow our ketchup because she could never get our waitress to bring her any.

3. The Iced Tea. I got nauseous after I drank it which means it was not freshly brewed, was from concentrate, or their equipment was not clean. Still a little nauseous the next day. Got the bill and it was $3. Wow.

The burgers are the only reason I give 2 stars...service was so bad I can't justify more. I'd  come back for the burgers...and maybe to try a beer flight...but I think I'll just sit at the bar. If that experience is good maybe I'll raise my rating.

OMG! I'm glad I found this place. I had the best fried chicken ever!, the best bread pudding ever! and the best customer service ever! The employees were very friendly and I even talked to one of the owning family members. Thanks Yelp!!! I will definitely go back whenever I'm in NOLA.

Found another burger place that found myself wanting to come back and try again. Meat quality melts in your mouth plenty of food no worries if you are going to leave hungry. Tons of food for a comparable price.

A solid 4.5 stars for Naan & Kabab!  Naan & Kabab is the first full-service Mediterranean restaurant to come to Reno.  There were a few small counter service Mediterranean restaurants, but none of them offered a full dining experience.  Of course, there are a few more Mediterranean restaurants these days, but we wouldn't have those without Naan & Kabab leading the way.  Located across from the Peppermill (and next to Ruby River), it may be a little easy to miss.  They have a huge sign, but it has very light coloring and may be a little easy to miss if you aren't actively looking for it.  I have never had anything less than fantastic service in this cozy restaurant.  The moment you walk in, you will be greeted with a warm, genuine welcome.  The wonderful aromas of saffron and spices will delight your sense of smell and will make you start salivating for this wonderful cuisine before you even peek at the menu.  Chef Maurice is always there at dinner, and he visits with each table to ensure that his guests are satisfied.  He is a very warm, genuine man- always offering a handshake and coupon for a free Awesome Dude on your next visit.  He is very passionate and loves what he (and his team, particularly Tom and Sam) does, and you can taste that love (and freshness!) in the food.  

The Awesome Dude is definitely awesome!  The pistachios in the saffron-vanilla ice cream balance out the sweetness of the baklava nicely, making the dessert a nice way to finish your meal without being too sweet.  It is also an ideal portion- not too much, not too little.  However, I ALWAYS get the Vegetable Combination appetizer and rarely have room for dessert.  Seriously guys, Naan & Kabab has the best dolmades (stuffed grape leaves) in town!  Ditto for their falafel, hummus and tzatziki.  The naan is freshly grilled, brushed with garlic and baby dill-infused E.V.O.O. and is the perfect texture.  The dipping sauce that accompanies it (I believe it is called torshi, but forgive me if I am mistaken!) is the perfect partner for this delicious naan.  I have never ordered anything at Naan & Kabab that I have not thoroughly enjoyed.  It is a wonderful date for an intimate dinner with friends and loved ones, offering excellent food at very affordable prices.  It's not really set up for large parties, though they can easily accommodate 6-8 patrons without a reservation.  They also cater!  Do yourself a favor and check it out!  (And make sure you check in on yelp for a free Awesome Dude on your visit!)
The lady who works the counter is so nice. Not a huge menu but enough good choices to please a variety of diners - in addition to subs, there are vegetarian options, soups and salads.

This place is unreal. I visited back in September and had a variety of appetizers including the grilled octopus, stuffed artichoke, and meatballs. Highly recommend all three. My entree was a gnocchi dish and it was perfectly made. Mercato is cash only so make sure you come prepared.

I am sad to say that even though the food is good the service is poor. The waitress was not friendly, no smile but a smirk . After ordering coffee my husband had to go up to the waitress twice before I got milk. No water at the table . I could have dealt with the slow service if the waitress would have been more accommodating. She never asked if the food was good or if we needed anything else.
After I ate I noticed the menu board towards the back of the restaurant which had specials that I would have ordered but never knew about as the waitress never gave us a special menu. Not a happy meal

I would give the nigiri we had (salmon and tuna) 4-5 stars--it was good. The seaweed salad was also good. However, for some reason, the sushi rolls just aren't my favvvvvorite. Though I have only ever been for happy hour, so have only ordered off of that limited menu. I'm guessing I would like some of the sushi rolls on the regular menu more. The prices during happy hour are great! Other than that, there were quite long wait times between getting there, ordering drinks, ordering food, getting food, etc. All things considered I'd give it a solid 3. Out server was very kind so that made waiting a bit more manageable. 

Xoxo,

Is this thing on?

Pretty disappointed that they closed the pho place downstairs of el dorado--that was our go to soup place while in Reno. We were surprised to find out they had pho/Asian food at candle central! My family and I decided to give it a shot since we were hungry. 
Many of us got their pho--the pho was actually decent and good although it was on the pricey side. I believe almost $15 for a bowl. Although it did hit the spot. We also got French fries on the side--don't judge lol and they were good as well. 
This place gets busy, especially later in the night. Some workers can be grumpy, but I get it. 
If in the hotel already, it's convenient--give this place a try! It's literally downstairs from your hotel if staying at silver legacy.

The Plav was very odd. It tasted like old dry rice mixed with oil. I don't know if that's how it's supposed to be but I didn't enjoy it. I wasn't a fan of the lamb liver either... I guess it's my fault for ordering it. The kebabs were good but the boneless beef one was tough. Everything was pricy considering that none of the dishes came with any sides besides onions. Oh, the red sauce was bland and awkward as well. I guess I'm just not a fan for Uzbek food. But the 2 star is for the server.... he kept asking if we wanted bread and salad??? Like it was complimentary. He asked do you want bread? And we said sure! When the bill came, we were charged for bread. Kind of feel cheated on haha. But whatever, the bread was the best "dish" we had tonight sadly.
I love ijji and this one was also great. Slow service when busy but still great. The mussels are my favorite.

We really enjoyed this location. 

I can't wait until the outside area is ready for the warm spring days. 

I personally don't eat it but the table said the corn bread was really good. 

My kids really enjoyed their meals. I think they had the steak. Cooked well and a nice portion for a kids menu. 

I am ready to make my next trip there.

A good small place.  Just remember not to go during prime times as the wait can get long.
 If your going for breakfast - get there before 9.  If lunch, 11:30.  Weekends for lunch - all depends.
Most of the time we have good food and service.  Even when something does go wrong with breakfast, they are quick to resolve.  
We'll be back

DIRTY and it smells like old beer.  Bartenders have terrible attitudes and bickered with each other about shifts.  I watched a waitress carry 3 breakfasts to a table,  all 3 plates were piles on one another after the plates had been on a dirty counter. Someone is going to get sick.  I don't even think  I would have bottled beer at this place.  Whomever is the manager he/she needs a new job and profession.  Oh, flies everywhere- we are in an airport?

Very delicious and they offer all of their crepes GF and most of them can be made vegan. I ordered the mozzarella, tomato, spinach, and houseware (vegan) pesto crepe. It was lovely. The crepe had a slight sweetness to it and the portion was consistent with the price. They over a good variety of sweet & savory crepes. Service was also quick!

Been coming here for last few years and food always good.  Dunno what happened  since our last visit but the mac&cheese was tasteless, oily and mushy, the Cole slaw, which previously was ok, has new recipe to some inedible variety.  The fried shrimp were skimpy, overfried and barely edible.  Coconut shrimp were ok, but those clearly went from freezer to fryer.  The burger looked ok, but nothing to write home about.  

Get a sense that the kitchen staff has changed. At least our bartender/server was pleasant and attentive.  Sad to say we won't be giving this a go again anytime soon. Too bad, we always enjoyed the location.  

(And if you're considering Shark Tales across street, their marquee has "EVICTED" across it.  Guess that's better than the closed for health violation stickers we saw last time we were over that way)

New Indonesian cuisine ,.... I went there today and ordered bakmi ayam jamur ,......and I like it ,the foods are good , the pangsit is reeaaally goood (I recommend) , the indoor lay out is nice, the service are good ,IS ONLY TAKE THEM 15-20 MINUTES TO BRING MY ORDERS ,so it quite normal (no worries). I definitely back for more .....!

Average supermarket.

Just avoid "welfare day" at the 1st of the month.  Tax payers beware!

Usually I somewhat agree with Yelp reviews and we have found sone really cool spots searching Yelp, but not this time. Don't understand the 4 stars at all. We had Garlic Chicken and Szechuan Beef. This is definitely the lowest-common-denominator, americanized, cheap take-out Chinese you can find. Neither of us finished our food. It was actually kindof gross. Cashier was really rude, and speaks almost no english I guess. Dont plan on eating in - tables are gross. Wont return for sure.
Wow wow wow! What a great experience! The sushi was made fresh and delicious! Our server was very friendly and knowledgable. The price was on point and we'll definitely be eating there again!
Happy Hour is now only Mon- Fri; they have added "The Loft" which sells beer to go. as well as coffee and such. Still a soild four stars.

My first review is unfortunately no longer valid as this local "jewel" has been transformed to the local "dump" under new ownership. My family used to walk to this restaurant literally every Saturday but now the food is terribly disappointing, the "fresh" baked goods are awful and there is no friendly service. If there aren't new changes soon this restaurant will no longer need to be reviewed for obvious reasons.

I went to first watch this past weekend and I was amazed once again. The BLTE was amazing and the chimichanga was absolutely delicious. Everyone there is super friendly and I always feel at home when I eat here. I highly recommend this place!!!

Overrated and overpriced. Has very good merchandise but I'm not going to pay those prices.
Read the link below. 
http://www.chicagotribune.com/business/ct-whole-foods-overcharging-nyc-customers-20151229-story.html

Went in at 9:15 on Monday night and had the GREATEST experience! Our waitress Mayla was fun, personable and completely on top of things. The food was delicious (could possibly be the best burger and fries in town!) and the Gumbo was just the right balance of heat and belly warming deliciousness. Often times service during slow times at a restaurant leaves a lot to be desired. SO not the case here, both service and food were exceptional. Thank you Mayla for making our late dinner one to remember, I will be back in soon :)

Tony's used to have the best pizza and wings in South Jersey, but it's really gone downhill.  The pizza had this great tangy sauce that made it great, but they've since replaced it with a generic sauce that has no taste whatsoever.

Their wings used to be made in a great tangy wing sauce that wasn't overly spicy.  But once again, they changed the sauce, and now it's a fiery sauce that's absolutely brutal.  In addition, the once soft skin is now crispier - Something that I dislike.

Bring back the old Tony's, and I'll happy come back!!
Best hoagies in town! This is our go-to place. Love the different options of sandwiches, and they are always amazing. Great sizes too.

I had a craving for a chicken sandwich and wanted to try something a bit different. After some research, I opted for the spicy chicken sandwich from Huda (via delivery). It did not disappoint! The chicken was crisp and juicy, and the sauce gave the sandwich just enough of a kick (though I would not actually call the sandwich spicy). As good as the chicken was, the best part of the sandwich were definitely the buns - they were extremely fluffy, and all around just super delicious.

I completed my order with a side of fries. I loved the chive topping on the fries, though I think the fries were a bit oversalted.

This isn't the cheapest sandwich in the world, but I would say the portion is fair and the quality of the food is high. I will definitely be back to try more of the menu.

Came here for lunch with my co-workers.  The express lunch was absolutely delicious.  I'm not a fan of raw tomatoes, but the Domata Salata was unbelievably good.  Give me those bright red tomatoes anytime!  I also had the moussaka which was nice, but the bechamel sauce created a hard and heavy layer on top that I just removed and ate the rest of the dish.  

We also shared the spreads, which were all very tasty, although I liked the red pepper one the best.  From other people's plates, I also tried the octopus, which was cooked perfectly and not slimy or tough.  The octopus was also much better than the fried calamari, which was rather plain.  

All in all, I will definitely come back and try more dishes.  The $19 business lunch is hard to beat.
Saw James featured on Fox and wanted to check it out. Cool neighborhood spot with a good vibe.  Food is solid and the bartenders are friendly. I'll definitely be back.

Came for dinner this week and I loved my dinner. My boyfriend was disappointed however citing small portions. He had the fried catfish while I enjoyed the chicken and dumplings. It was more like chicken pit pie and it was delicious. We also enjoyed the lemon pie.  Yum!

Came here for dinner on a Friday night. Seemed mildly busy but we were seated right away. 

Service was good. We were given bread which was crusted w sesame seeds and salt I think. That or the butter added salt. Either way it was good. 

For drinks, I got the wine from Italy which was really good if you like red wine on the stronger side. 

For small plates my husband and I shared the octopus. Had been the octopus alone, we probably would not have liked it but being paired with the white beans, nuts which gave it texture and a favor full aioli type sauce, it all came together. 

My husband ordered the halibut which was one of the specials. He really enjoyed it and after trying it, agreed. 

I got the angentinean burger. I know others noted that it was amazing but I thought it was average. The burger was juicy and fries were crunchy, but in the end i thought it was just okay.

Portions were good so unfortunately we were way too full for dessert. 

2 glasses of wine, 2 beers, app, 2 entrees (halibut being the highest but we enjoyed it) came to $101 inc tip.

Went here last night with a groupon. The restaurant is downstairs and has a cool set up. There is a bar area with big TV to the left and a small sushi bar in the middle, and the dining room to the right with tables and nice big booths.
