BBQ brisket. - hoisin sauce forward bbq sauce. Not a fan. 

Bang bang shrimp. - too sweet for me. But most people will like it. Sweet mayo sauce forward. 

Beef bulgogi. - way way too salty for me. But that's most off the food in Nola. I hate salt after this trip. Lol. 

Stake and egg. - again too salty but favor is nice. 

Overall. Best advice. If you are a tourist, Get a sandwich to share. Pick your favorite protein, If you like it order more. If not, no harm done. Move along. Hope this helps.

Finally got around to coming here. It was alright. Food was OK. Pricey and small portions. There are plenty of other options in St. Louis for same quality food, bigger portions, and cheaper. $12 cocktail vs $9 cocktail literally across the street with same quality liquor/spirits. There are many other restaurants that serve hummus and pita comparable to quality at almost half the price. Generally speaking, this fell far below expectations. You either want to be a fast casual restaurant or you want to be an upscale nicer restaurant. This was a confusing experience of neither idea being carried out. Also, difficult to get staff attention even though staff were literally standing everywhere. I do not recommend.

Had a fantastic dinner here. Everything was so good!

Server Matt was really nice and funny. He was great at keeping our drinks filled and the food coming out fast. If you get him then you know you're getting good service. 

The fried green beans were nice and crispy. So good with the remoulade sauce. Yum! And holy crap the nachos were huge! Covered in cheese, omg so much cheesy goodness. We got it with pork and it was great. Mom said they were the best nachos she's ever had and I have to agree.

I ordered the shrimp and grits, nice  large portion. I thought moms taco salad should have come with more brisket but she liked it. My friend got the chicken fried chicken. Luckily she let me try a bite and oh my it was good! Another friend ordered the catfish and it came out with two HUGE pieces. It was crazy how much food there was!

Of course we saved room for dessert and ordered the fried brownie with ice cream. Now I am a believer that everything is better with bacon and for this case I was one hundred percent right. Candied bacon! Oh this dessert is a heart attack on a plate but totally worth it! What a way to go.

Thought I wrote a review for this place last year until my friend made me realize I wrote it for the wrong Sakura! Gahhh... 

Th food here is pretty average. Why do I recommend this place, simply for the convenience of soup dumplings. (It's better than going to Dim Sum Garden which is a bit scary and ghetto).  Its a cute, clean restaurant with good service (can't say that about a lot of chinatown restaurants). Tried a few apps and entrees off their menu, can't say much about their food. Soup dumplings is the only reason we keep going back.

Great atmosphere!  Good pumpkin beer (four peaks)!  And great food!  Bruce was the bartender working and not only was he friendly but cute!  Great place for a group or sitting at the bar by yourself!  Chicken sandwich, Amazing!

One of the worst meals and experience in New Orleans! We were there for lunch.  The gumbo was watery and tasteless! The grilled oyster were greasy and tasteless! Service was abominable! We sat in an alcove and basically were forgotten by the wait staff! Our waiter, whom we asked for hot sauce and other things not only forgot our requests, he blamed the busboy, who occasionally did refill our water and gave us more bread, for the lack of service! Perhaps it was an off day for our waiter  Dustin but we will certainly never return to this over priced tourist trap because it certainly seemed like the norm for them! Don't waste your money, there are plenty of other delicious city's restaurants in the French Quarter!

While staying at the Hyatt came here for two late night visits: one for Oysters and the other for dessert. Both were really good. Very reasonably priced, especially considering that it's in a hotel, loved getting 6 oysters for $10 or so. Very good service and easy.

Just got home from here. The breakfast choices are abundant and it was hard to choose. I had one of their skillet meals, hash browns with meats and mushrooms (it comes with green peppers too but I'm not a fan so I asked for them to be omitted). It also comes with a side of 2 very large pancakes which were really good. The skillet meal was HUGE and delicious. I brought more than half of it home. Bessa is awesome and added to our enjoyment. So glad they have moved into a place close. Can't wait to try other choices as well as their lunch menu.

It's been a while since we visited IJJI because I always leave disappointed.  But I was given a gift card so I thought I would see if they would redeem themselves. To be fair, all of the employees were delightful. But the menu was bland. We ordered 8 long rolls and weren't excited about any of them. 2 stars for good muscles and great staff.

I took my partner here for this birthday dinner this month and we had an absolutely wonderful time.  We realized we haven't tried many steakhouses in Philly, and have heard a lot of good things about Butcher & Singer.  We definitely were not disappointed!  We really went all out and got everything we were interested in: we started out with some oysters as our appetizer, and they were delicious - super fresh tasting and the horseradish and vinegar sauces they gave with it paired really well.  We also got the escargot, and it was incredible - they were tender and also very rich tasting, the buttery and garlicky sauce they were marinated in was just so good.  We also got two sides, the stuffed hash browns was perfectly crisped on the outside and so creamy, cheesy, and delicious on the inside.  I mean, who can say no to a potato dish stuffed with more potatoes? The mac and cheese also was just decadent in a word.  Would highly recommend both.

We got the 32oz Porterhouse for two cooked medium rare as our main, and it was indeed perfectly cooked.  Super tender and juicy, and nice and peppery.  The seasoning was not too much and not too little, and we were absolutely stuffed to the brim.

For dessert, we knew we just had to get the Baked Alaska - I unfortunately didn't snap a pic, but there are plenty of photos of this particular dessert.  It was piled high with creamy and light meringues and the ice cream inside had a bit of a banana flavor and overall it was really refreshing after all of that steak.

The service was beyond incredible - we had to wait a little longer than usual for our steak, and because of that, the chef really kindly sent us a complimentary shrimp cocktail.  We really weren't in a rush, but everyone was just super attentive and kind and kept offering us the complimentary warm biscuits as well.  Servers were super knowledgeable too.

The atmosphere is very intimate and feels extremely upscale, and although there isn't a dress code, expect to see people dressed well.  So just as a heads up, you might feel a tiny bit out of place if you show up in shorts.

I would highly recommend Butcher & Singer as a romantic dinner for special occasions or really any celebratory meal, it will definitely be a solid bet for a good time.

Easily my favorite restaurant in St. Louis. The quality and flavor of the food never ceases to amaze me. The lentil Sambosas are super flaky and incredible, the veggie combo plate is worth the trip alone, and the shrimp tibs are something I constantly crave. Don't miss out, it's one of the cities most underrated gems.
Truly a cut above every other local burger drive in. Super fresh and not fried into oblivion. Some of the best chicken tenders in town.
My husband and I were so excited to try this place. However we thought the food was average. The concept is good but the execution lacked. The dessert was the best part of the meal.

First time visitors on a weekday afternoon. Our gourmet cheeseburgers were memorably succulent. A burger I could literally sink my teeth into. Attentive service.Ambiance is merely average, but we'll be back.

Being a vegetarian, I know fries.  I know fries in the way most long term vegetarians know fries...because their loved ones know burgers, cheesesteaks, etc.

The fries at SPTR are stupid delicious.  They are creamy on the inside, and crisp on the outside.  And the ketchup is pretty darn tasty too.

Frankly, the whole menu is pretty awesome. I've been for dinner, brunch, and drinks, and always leave stoked to have good veggie food in the city.  Mind you, the vegetarian/vegan selection isn't huge, but neither is the menu...if you're picky, check it out before venturing to this spot.
If any Mexican restaurant deserves five stars, it's this one. Good prices, good food, lots of options. Even in quarantine they have super clean hands-free packaged food.

Visited this Zionsville brick street gem fir lunch and dinner this week. They have really upped their game.  Their menu seems bigger than before. They are offering sandwiches for lunch and also dinner.  Several salads.  For lunch they also have combos. We had the southern chicken sandwich with a mini wedge salad.  Very yummy. For dinner we had the spicy shrimp appetizer. Many times I get it for dinner with a wedge.  Also ordered the wedge and added blue cheese crumbles to the dressing. Theirs is different in that they serve their wedge with buttermilk dressing.  Shared the 8 ounce filet which came with whipped potato and they subbed broccolini instead if asparagus.  I was previously skeptical of getting steak there but it is very good. Friends shared the mackerel special and they loved it. They nicely split everything we ordered.  We dined outside on the patio.  This is one of the nicest patios around- flowers, ferns, wrought iron, brick.  Really need to check it out!

Very good food and very nice menu.  Just remember if you order a special it's going to be expensive  up to $40 range, so stick with the menu so you are not shocked at your bill.  They verbally don't tell you how much each special is so I will ask next time.  I felt $9 for cake was a bit pricey.  They did not bring a dessert menu so I had no idea of pricIn all the food is delicious but our bill was way more than what we planned because of the specials.  The music is very nice and you can still have a conversation.   Very nice dining but ask pricing on the specials and desserts.  It's your money.

Meh, not a fan. Got a flight and the brown was the only one mildly drinkable. It's the first time I've left more than half the glass left for each of the 4 samples. Overall bummed by the beer flavors (my four and my friend's four). The location is really nice and the staff were helpful and friendly. Unfortunately, I won't be back.

Out of this world good. The dough. The sauce. The service. All spectacular. 

Recos: Margherita, Fraviavola (spicy), Pancetta, pizzas, in that order. Ask to have them brought out one at a time.

Off menu secret: Ask if they've got any Amatriciana. Incredible.

Enjoy!

So this location is kinda close to my home.  The women in my home are obsessed with the cheese sticks and fountain Cokes here.   So much so that my Sweets has earned the nickname "Coke lady" because she is here so often.    

They seem to have good luck when they go to the drive thru.  They get in and out pretty fast.  Not me.  I get stuck for sometimes 15 mins.    From time to time I'll partake in the cheese sticks.  Maybe even a burger.   Its convenient and decent fast food.  Aside from the wait.  I am an impatient person tho so pay no mid to me.

Stopped into the Industry for a quick dinner before seeing a movie with some of the fam and immediately loved the atmosphere in this place. Casual and cozy. Our waitress was really sweet and speedy with getting us both drinks and our dinner orders. Definitely a safe bet if you haven't left yourself a ton of time to get somewhere else because they can turn it around. We actually gave ourselves a couple of hours before the movie and were in and out in under an hour! The reason I am not giving more stars is due to the food. I ordered the burger to split with my mom and she ordered the whole grain waldorf salad. These were the only two entrees I tried, although the fried chicken sandwich, the Korean BBQ pork belly and pasta all looked good and my dining companions all confirmed that they were. The burger was SUPER tiny for $9. Think like dollar menu size. It came with a large portion of fries which were yummy, but the burger was done really rare. We told the waitress our issue who graciously offered to replace it, but we declined. She took the burger off our bill anyway, which was nice of her. So again, great service. The whole grain waldorf salad unfortunately was also disappointing. The salty/savory dressing did nothing for the traditionally fruity salad and the faro added a weird chewy texture to the mix. We both didn't finish the salad, which was portioned much better than the burger and the pasta, which was also quite small for $15. Overall, I would come back for drinks and I'd be willing to try some appetizers. As I said before, the service was really nice here and I'd like to give the Industry another shot based on this.

All-hours Carrollton grill
Black tie & white coat
Choice fare with NOLA patois
#NOLA_Haiku

I've been waiting to come check this place out and after a lot of hype I was still very surprised and how good it was! I'm not a huge fan of Italian food but I was really satisfied with our meal.
Firstly parking didn't seem to be an issue, there's lots of space and it doesn't seem to get too packed. 
The waiters and waitresses we had were extremely attentive and charismatic - there energy really made me smile! 
We started off with a charcuterie, which I would highly highly suggest if you're with a group of three or more OR a really hungry group of two! It reminded me a lot of croatian snack foods (but don't tell the Italians that).
Everything on the board was fresh and delicious! Full of cold cuts, cheeses, grapes, olives and so on!
For the main I ordered the Amore salad with chicken ( I know boo, I'm the salad girl) while my mom ordered the spicy sausage fettuccine and my brother ordered the mac and cheese. 
The salad, as much as I may be poopooed on for it , was actually very good! The chicken was well done, the balsamic vinaigrette was great and I would highly suggest! 
I got to try a bit of the other dishes and those were also really tasty as well.
Overall the atmosphere was adorable and gives you a little taste of romantic Italian dining! It's certainly a great date location or a great place to take the family for an afternoon lunch!

A perfect Sunday morning coffee bar with wonderful selection of food and treats. Macha latte and lavender latte are the best along with a sausage burrito.  Haven't tried the wine or beer selections but they are available along with appetizers.
I've been to St. Louis twice and here twice.  Love the food.  The Slinger is ridiculously good.
This place just beats all taco places hands down. Amazing ingredients and always great quality no matter what location I go to it seems. I won't go anywhere else for tacos. Treat yourself

Had a good meal, tasty chicken dish with a mango salsa, steak fries and a Caesar salad. My only complaint would be the salad was not cold, seemed like it was sitting out somewhere, one of my pet peeves. Salad needs to be served cold. Nice atmosphere, view of beach, would definitely go back. Service was excellent, our waiter was very attentive.

Bottom-line-up-front (BLUF)--If you live downtown or nearby, you can't go wrong with Mizu.

I'm gonna pile on the Eli-is-a-douche-bag bandwagon before I start my review.  I've lived in Japan (and been treated to sushi elite), CA, RI, VA, DC, FL, TN, MO and IL and enjoyed sushi in every one of my adopted cities at a local favorite sushi bar/restaurant.  I've also enjoyed sushi in dozens of cities around the world as a one-time visitor.  What I have found, is that sushi is sushi is sushi...and it's all pretty great (save for my first ever visit to Sushi-go-round in Sasebo, Japan...which almost ruined sushi for me forever).  
I have spent over $100 for one or as little as $29 for an all-you-can-eat experience...and it was all just about delicious.

I will say, that because of my above opinion, once I find a place that is close by and relatively low-cost, I'm not going to be too anxious to run all over the city looking for a better place.  They are all within small degrees of each other and driving 15 miles for minutely better but pricier isn't going to do it for me.

If you walk in the door with a chip on your shoulder, you're gonna find a way to be a hater.  So...stay home Eli.

Mizu is great to outstanding.  I've never been to Wasabi or Drunken Fish.  I suspect they are good/great too.  I just don't want to wait in line or drive 5 miles and sweat parking when I can walk or cab downtown and find ample parking.  

Mizu goes way above and beyond to ensure a great dining experience.  As mentioned, the daily Sushi Happy Hour means half-price drinks and apps from 2:30-7 p.m.  Large bottles of Asahi or Can of Sapporo for $3.50 is a great draw.

Plenty of interesting original rolls or standard sushi items.  Everything tastes great to me and I have brought in out of town sushi fans and they loved it too.

Darn it...I'm feeling a sushi crave coming on.

Went here for the first time. Ordered the brisket with baked beans as side 1, broccoli salad as side 2, and the habanero bbq sauce.  Came with Texas toast. 

The brisket would have been ok but they served it cold. The sides were ok, nothing special. All in all, not worth the money.

tldr: pretty decent ayce kbbq but it is lacking in menu options and has pretty poor service. In addition, it is pretty expensive ($24.99, $28.99 with short ribs) but given it's the only nearby ayce kbbq nearby, it will fill your crave.

Environment: Walking into this restaurant, you first notice the relatively small grills set into the tables and relatively few number of tables themselves. We had a party of 5 and were seated at a table with only one small grill (which was electrically heated). Overall, however, it was a pretty good environment as it wasn't too rundown neither too fancy/posh.  

Service: The poor service we received is enough to warrant a lose of one entire star. Though there was a good amount of customers on a Sunday afternoon, it was constantly a battle of getting the server's attention to order more food or even get more water. For some reason or another, there often was no one around in the dining room/only one person behind the counter. Especially for AYCE, this is extremely frustrating as at times my party just sat at the table waiting to order more food. When the servers came, they were friendly and willing to get whatever we wanted, so this isn't a criticism of their attitudes/personalities, but more of a criticism of their training/management (most likely management as they seemed to be actively looking for more servers). 

Food: Finally, onto the food. To begin, the beginning appetizers consisted of the usual kimchi, fish cakes, etc. which were pretty solid. In addition, the servers were more than willing to get more (when we could get their attention). We were also served two seafood pancakes, which was only alright since there wasn't a seafood flavor, two cups of soup, which was apparently pretty solid, and one cup of cooked eggs. Again, more of a criticism of the management/way the food was served rather than the food itself, it was just awkward to share two cups of soup among five people. Now onto the meat, it was a small selection but it was relatively solid. The brisket was frozen and honestly somewhat tasteless, but that's somewhat expected with brisket imo. The bulgogi was honestly pretty solid and was one of the top choices among my group. I personally really enjoyed the pork belly because it was extremely fatty but it unfortunately wasn't too thick of a slice. The spicy pork and chicken had good marinades making them also worth choosing/tasting. 

As you can see, really my qualms with this restaurant wasn't necessarily its food, but rather its management/environment. We honestly had a great time eating the AYCE option and the food was pretty good. However, there were many factors that if remedied, would make this a much better experience. In regards to food, the only thing I would want is a larger selection of meat/better quality of meat, but of course that would require an increase in cost which I'm not sure I would be willing to pay for given the other things I didn't like about this restaurant.

However, given this is the only AYCE kbbq place nearby, I would say it is still worth going to and enjoying. Having come from NYC, it is just a step down in many aspects that CAN BE IMPROVED. I would come here again if a group of friends wanted to get some AYCE kbbq.

Food was absolutely delicious! First of all, i really appreciate a restaurant with complimentary bread (knew it was gonna be great right then ahah) I got the lobster ravioli and it was wonderfully spicy and very filling. I found the service and overall atmosphere to be very good, it was my brothers birthday and the waiter brought out a special dessert and the entire restaurant sang. Food is a little on the pricy side, but I found it to be more than worth it.

Amazing amazing amazing! As a party of 4 coming during Covid, wearing masks, and in the heat of August, I couldn't say enough about this restaurant!  Great service, THANK YOU Mike B, and great recommendations!  The Crawfish Mona and the Ahi Fajitas were top notch! My sister and her husband got the lobster and mushroom fettuccine and again to die for. We had a gentleman ask about our meals and how they were more than once. Maybe the owner? Sweet as pie and genuinely wanted to make sure we were satisfied. We will be back SOON! Thank you for a fabulous time.

Full disclosure I was very hesitant to try this place as I'm not a big fan of small plates and especially not small plates when you share.  We went with a group of 8.  First we ordered a few different hummus and not a one disappointed.  In fact, the Turkish hummus was the best hummus I've ever tasted.  Phenomenal texture and just the right amount of flavor.  I'd go back just for this alone.  Then we ordered a ton of small plates to share.  They were all fantastic.  Our server was great and the price was reasonable.  Definitely somewhere I will go again.

As much as  La loconda is my fav Italian restaurant in Philly and therefore tell everyone to go try it out, this time I wanted to give it 3.5~4 instead of 5. 

There's not a single time when I came and not get the gnocchi dish. As always, it was perfect! The chewy yet soft texture was exactly what I wanted and expected. The gorgonzola sauce was perfectly cheesy enough to not overtop the other flavors. My friend's seafood pasta (sorry I don't remember the name but it started as "Cop....") was perfectly cooked with the perfect amount of sauce and seafood toppings too. This dish includes clams and mussels, which my friend does not like, along w/ the calamari squid and etc. We requested to not add on the clams and mussels and the waiter/cook had no problem in doing that and topping the pasta with more of the other seafood. 

Plus, it's BYOB! How wrong can you go w/ this! 

However, the reason I deduct one star time is because the younger server (there's always the same 2 guys- the uncle and the cousin) is so crazy and unorganized and not careful. He is such in a rush all the time and bangs the wine glasses down on your table. He will fill your water so fast it looks like he doesn't care about the customer. The tone of his voice is very rude too. Because of this server, I always start off my dining experience at La Locanda in a 'not-so-good' mood. Thank god the food here is so delish it overcomes the service of this one rude server!...I complain about him all the time,,,but I will come back for the food. It's that good hehe
Great Cuban sandwich!  Very authentic and price was extremely reasonable. Would come back.
Absolutely loved it!!! The tacos were delicious and the price was perfect. Try the bbq brisket taco and the shrimp taco. We will definitely be back!

This place makes the BEST Old Fashions I have ever tasted!!!!  Their food is spot-on.  The Beer Cheese Dip is a must!!  Great staff and the owner really cares.  My favorite new place in Ybor, GET THE WORD OUT!!!!

Very delicious but very $$. The have the best tasting $6.00 burger for $9.00. Lol!! Three chicken strips on a bed of fries are hardly worth $12.95 even if they are good. You average $10.00 per person but it's fun & funky and the service is always with a smile. I'll surely go again & again since I'm just up the road.

I was recommended by my friend, she said this sushi place has a great service and foods . And now I come , it turned out that this restaurant is just like she said , the sashimi is the best , a lot of appetizers, I will definitely come back !

The customer service in the place was horrible! My husband and I attempted to have breakfast here on Sunday. When we walked in to place our names on the list to be seated, the guy behind the counter not only yelled at us, but was EXTREMELY rude.. We, along with another couple decided we would take our business else where!!!! 1st impressions are VITAL..Never again!

Love this place! It's a small family owned restaurant, with very friendly people. I've been looking for a Pho place around here and finally found our go to place! Everything looks so good, can't wait to try the whole menu!
Amazing bagels and a huge variety of cream cheese and bagel flavors. Definitely worth the wait!

I loved it. The place reminded me on one of those long Brooklyn restaurant/bars with tile on the floor. The oysters were beautiful and my shrimp and grits were the best. I cannot remember what my wife ate but other than the oysters it probably did not have many calories. Felt very comfortable with the covid separation.
Greek salad and calzones are my favorites here. Service is always friendly and helpful

Stopped in on the Fourth of July.    I had the STL STYLE pork streak with potato salad grilled corn on the cob and some fries and a salad.   Everything was fantastic.  Great location.  Great atmosphere.  Great friendly service.  I didn't catch my servers name cause I hadn't slept in two days and there was music playing.   I just needed to get off the interstate for a bit.   My best friend was with me and he is the pickiest eater on the planet and he ate every bite of his also.  

My favorite thing about the place was our server.  She made us not only feel at home 1000 miles from there, but she made us feel like family



I definitely recommend this place to everyone.   The flavor of the smoke in the food was perfect.    Absolutely amazing.   The perfect blend of smoke and spices.  Everything was cooked to perfection.  Nothing I ate was Fancy or out of the ordinary but everything I ate was the Best of hat particular menu item I ever had.   Seriously check this place out.  Prices were very very reasonable.  


Get you some!

Ordered take out with the Eat 24 app. Our order was accurate and ready quickly. They even accommodated our request for veggie-only tempura and extra chopsticks. 

The food was pretty good! We ordered an appetizer and four rolls of sushi. Recommend the Dr. Pepper roll and Crunchy Crab. 

The 5 stars are for the great attention to detail tho.

I'm starting with I'm really picky when it comes to Mexican food & in general because I'm Mexican myself having said that ate at this place twice so far so good! The cook be putting some magic in that Ceviche  service was great I think the only mess up was I asked for Corn tortillas got flour no big was so hungry devoured Ceviche & some chicken fajitas ate it all.

Great family owned business. Delicious food and service. Quant outdoor patio. 
Highly recommend.

Service friendly, but slow and unorganized. The waitress who started us out didn't finish with us and our order suffered for it. Drinks took about 10-15 minutes and it wasn't even busy. Burger was great, loco moco was cold and bland. Get the burger if you're not in a hurry and you probably won't be disappointed.

My fav waffle house. Food is always good. Nights are the best Jeff always hooks it up in the kitchen. Customer service is always on the money and its very clean. Im a regular and this is the best waffle house.

As required by Tourist Law, I came to Cafe Du Monde on my first trip to NOLA. The staff was a little surly, but I got my chicory coffee and beignets almost immediately, and DAMN... they seriously don't play when it comes to their powdered sugar. Eating those beignets without getting any of that stuff on me was like performing open heart surgery. I felt like a caveman, crouched over the carcass of a dead gazelle, protecting my precious beignets lest the powdered sugar escape and wreak havoc upon me.

This may be blaspheme, but I'll say it anways: the beignets weren't life changing. They were OK. Perhaps this is because I wasn't at the original location, but the way people were talking it was like I was supposed to have some sort of relevation during this experience, which wasn't the case. They were mounds of dough, topped with an obscene amount of powered sugar. That was about it.

As for the coffee... I need to note that I'm not a coffee-drinker. So, you may not be able to trust my opinion on this one, but it was just extremely bitter. Not having had chicory coffee before, I'm not sure if it's supposed to be this way. I got the cafe au lait, as recommended by many here on Yelp, but it didn't really help (and neither did the copious amounts of sugar my boyfriend dumped in). I think if you need a gentler wake up call, this isn't for you (or me, really).

Far East deserves 5 stars without hesitation.  The food is amazing.  My go-to are the fresh rolls and the spider bowl, though all of the menu is on point.  This is definitely a neighborhood joint and not a tourist spot, and the type of service reflects that... which makes it that much better in my opinion!  Lunch, dinner, or late night food/drinks, Far East has you covered.  An East Nashville staple for sure!

Not very friendly at all. We went here on Sunday 9/12/21 thinking there was food but the kitchen in back was closed. My friend decided to use the bathroom before we got a drink and the bartender comes out from behind the bar and followed him into the men's room. My friend is very put off by this guy following him into the toilet to "check him out". My friend was upset and wanted to leave. I asked the bartender if he followed my friend into the bathroom and he became aggressive towards me. As he put it "I needed to check you boys out."  He squared off like he wanted to fight. He hoped to make me feel threatened as well but I found him utterly rude and disturbing and just said chill as I held up two fingers and walked out. The place is obviously just for locals. The tough guy bartender role is outdated and lame. There are lots of good eateries and bars nearby. Try one of them instead of this place. It's Their Bar.
Probably the best beef sandwich in Tampa!!  Get the beef martini sandwich toasted!  Incredible food and great service

I love the Panera chain. The food at this location is consistent with the quality you'd get at any good Panera location. We went for dinner on a weekday night. It was moderately busy, but we got our order quickly.

My husband and I use to go to Addie's all the time when they were at their old location. He loves the pancakes and I love the French toast. Since the locations changed we had not been there until today....The new location is nice and there is a lot of parking. So already, they earn a star. We sat outside, which was also nice. Our server was very friendly and quick to get our drinks. The only problem was we waited a long time for our food and when it came out I got very sad looking French toast and my husband got delicious looking pancakes (this is why I gave them 3 stars). I took back the toast in exchange for the pancakes. Attached are 2 photos. Not only was the French toast burned today but there are less slices! The other photo is from 2017 during the French toast glory days. Addie's why have you changed the amount of bread and amount of egg batter???!!!??? Sad.

I've been a fan of Hoang Long for years prior to their move downtown. When they closed the restaurant on the West end I was lost and heartbroken. I thought I had lost the best Lemongrass Beef Satay forever!

To my surprise they have simply just moved locations and I was astatic to find them downtown just recently. 

The new restaurant is well designed, looks great and feels new again. The beef lemongrass satay was so good today and I actually ordered a second bowl because I missed it so much! 

Keep up the great work! Best of luck in the new year!

Currently this is only 1 of 2 Chinese resturants in the city I will go to.  The food is good and consistently made.  They are very quick and I've rarely had to wait even when I show up 10 minutes into the 20 minute projected pick up time.  Parking is kind of a bummer, which isn't their fault since it's street only parking, but be prepared to park "creatively".  The only thing that irks me is the "we charge a fee if you use a credit card under $8.00" malarkey.  Technically no business is allowed to charge a fee to use a card for any reason per MC/Visa regulations but they ALL do it so... well, I guess it's lump it or eat pizza.

Heads up folks, the Philly area finally has a legit world-class brewery.  

The space is beautiful - smallish and lovely, with many thoughtful details: open tarrasse-style front windows, exposed brick and wood, reclaimed materials utilized throughout ... a far cry from the TGI-Fridays-esque ambience of many brewpubs.  

All Tired Hands beers are brewed on premises, and all range from "good" to "outstanding".  The focus of their brewing efforts is primarily IPAs and saisons.

The 'Foliage' double IPA is my favorite of the bunch...densely hoppy and floral, absolutely delicious, and highly drink-able.  The 'Tabel' - a saison brewed with various herbs and spices - is perhaps the most flavorful low (3.5%) ABV beer I've ever tasted.  The FarmHands - an homage to the FarmHouse roots of the style - is an unbelievably tasty saison brewed with wheat, oats, barley, and rye.

Also on offer is a small but high-quality selection of charcuterie, local cheese, homemade pickles, housemade bread, and paninis (utilizing the aforementioned).  I sampled the River & Glen duck prosciutto (from Warminster PA) and the Birchrun Hills 'FatCat' raw milk cheese (from Chester Springs PA) - both were wonderful.

Parking is easy, and the train from Philly drops you right nearby.  Insider tip: take a growler to go and drink it on the train ride home.  Make the effort to get out to Ardmore and check this place out.

The set up of the restaurant was awesome!  That's where it ends. Salads were ok..not impressive. EVERY SINGLE MEAT WAS A PILE OF SALT...except the lamb chops. The only saving grace. We took my 91 year old grandma there as a treat and she was so unhappy with everything. The alcohol was not even worth drinking. We never got a receipt to see what our bill total was. The two stars is literally attributed to the lamb chops. Probably won't go back with our "bonus" gift card

We enjoyed our selves at the Paris Bistro. The service was great. My husband and I liked our salads too. We also had French Onion soup....mmm good! My favorite. The jazz ensemble didn't start until 7:00PM which I forgot to ask about. The atmosphere was great! The music was simply perfect for our 18th wedding anniversary.  No complaints at all! Looking forward to eating there again. Patricia 11/24/17

My husband and I came here for our anniversary dinner last night.  I set up a 7:30 pm reservation on "Open Table" and requested a "romantic spot" and stated it was our anniversary.  When we arrived, we were abruptly told to sit at the bar and one of the hostesses would "come and find us".  I was surprised that we had to wait given our reservation and that it was a Wed., but we proceeded and ordered drinks and waited..... and waited.  We finished our drinks and heard nothing for over half an hour.  At this time, my husband was ready to walk out, but I inquired first with the bartender who called up to the stand and assured us that someone would be with us shortly.  We continued to wait.  I estimated about 45 minutes until one of the hostesses approached us and said "are you ready to be seated now?" with frankly a bit of an attitude.  My husband replied that we have been ready for 45 minutes and that we were unhappy with the long wait, to which she just said "sorry about that"... no explanation, no apology, and nothing offered.  Although not necessarily expecting free food, at least an apology and courteous behavior would've been appreciated.  She also stood there while we were closing out our tab with her clipboard seemingly annoyed and said "I'll just stand over here" like she had a problem with having to wait another 2 mins.  When we finally got to our table, I was a bit disappointed.  We were seated on the lower level in the middle, where it was quite bright - when I requested something romantic.  I was hoping for the mezzanine or a table on the side tucked away, but I let it go anticipating at least a good steak.  

After we were seated probably close to 8:30, we did end up with very good table service.  Our server was fast, efficient, knowledgeable, friendly, and helpful.  We ordered the porterhouse, strip, lobster mac and cheese, potatoes au gratin, and had the cheese steak dumplings as a starter.  All the food was indeed DELICIOUS and the steak was amazing!! one of the best we've ever had! 

In the end, my overview of the place is that the food is definitely worth trying, and the table service was great.  However, the ambiance is a bit obnoxious given the size of the place (although a beautiful building, it needs work on lighting and tables to soften it up a bit), the staff was discourteous, and the wait ridiculously long with a reservation ... the food did make up for it in the end, but we were disappointed.
1st time, delivery took 2 hrs. 2nd time, 2.5 hrs, and food was cold/congealed. Delivery driver called me a d*ck when I wouldn't sign (I had paid in full online, he slowly realized his mistake)

I'd probably give 3.5 for food quality if it were possible but the hostess staff all three times we've been in just really sours me. Also the bartenders two of the three times seemed disinterest and slightly annoyed as well. The first time we went for just drinks was ok but the beer seemed heavy on IPAs so if you don't like that there wasn't much else. 

Also I tried to make reservations three weeks ahead for a party of 8 and I got just nuthin' but attitude. It was a Monday night reservation so not like I was taking tables on a weekend. Whatever I guess but it really annoyed me how it was treated like such a hassle. We ended up canceling the week before because of the attitude we got when they called to confirm. A small group of us went recently. 

Some of the menu items are fabulous. Eggplant meatballs, Brussel sprouts, pretzel bread, ribs, for sure. Wings. Warm skillet cookie. 

Super disappointed in mashed potatoes (watery and unsalted), Italian meatballs nothing special, my friend liked the sausage but I didn't. I wasn't crazy about mac and cheese either. 

Drinks are expensive and the waiter pushed us into ordering far too many dishes. We had excessive leftovers and a huge bill.

We had to wait nearly 30 min for a table we reserved a month in advance, but the food was EPIC! I am not a regular at brunch, but, this place makes me want to start.....so long as my part can be seated in good time and not have to wait on the cold porch. That's the only reason I'm giving 4 out if 5 stars.

Service was great, I had the steak and eggs medium rare (perfectly cooked), eggs over medium were cooked a little more than medium but no complaints. Avocado toast was great!! My girlfriend had the shrimp and grits which weren't the best but still good. We also had bottomless mimosas which were good.
Lamb and chicken satay were great, flavor was spot on.  Pad Thai and larb mushrooms were way over seasoned.  Service was amazing!

Unique, delicious experience of more varieties of Thai dishes than you are likely to find in any restaurant.  Very well prepared by temple members and volunteers, mostly Thai and other Asian, but also a good mix of English speakers to help with transactions and describing dishes.   It is a bit of a mob scene with multiple waiting lines, and the longest (30 min. plus at noon) for the hot entree entree buffet & soups.  But other stations sell dried bananas/taro, sauces, salads, prepared curries, spring/egg rolls, dessert/sweet items and drinks.  All are very low priced as described by other reviewers.

Seating is on your own at picnic tables, with some under cover but more under trees overlooking the river.  A very scenic locale and the ornate, gilt Buddist temple is the centerpiece.  A few saffron-robed Buddist monks mingle some.   Parking is a bit tight at peak hour (noon) but parking attendants will find you a space.  

All transactions are cash in even dollar amounts, with no tax.  Today we had a family excursion and fed 5 adults and one child for under $50, with drinks.  And the left-overs brought home were another meal.   And there seemed to be no way to tip.........find me a similar high-quality, low-price, no tax or tip food emporium anywhere else in the area.

Amazing vegan options and absolutely tremendous food! 
Owner is very helpful and invested in your experience.

I went here based on a Phillyblog recommendation, and oh man, this is my favorite restaurant so far.  That might not be saying much, since I've only eaten here and at the New Delhi buffet, but I'm confident Kaffa Crossing will remain at the top of my favorite restaurants list.  I shared two appetizers (some kind of samosa-ish thing and a roll-up injera with tofu...something) and the veggie platter with my boyfriend.  We thought it might not be enough, because we were told the platter is for one (not two), but it definitely was.  Cheap, cozy, cute, great.

We were fasting & decided to try their vegan menu. I ordered the veggie pita pizza, hubby ordered the veggie kabobs, kids had chicken salad sandwiches w fruit cups. Food comes after 20 minutes & they tell my husband they were out of veggie kabobs. So they bring him the salad & beans that werw included, well it was covered in feta cheese so he couldn't eat it! They did refund (took 5 days to show) but I wish they would of told us upon ordering. Everything tasted good & they're new & busy so I'll give tgem a second chance!

Love this place! There's nothing like it in Nashville and if you're looking for authentic Greek food that isn't made up of the same typical menu, then you need to go here. The space is vibrant and fun with an amazing outdoor patio, and awesome Greek rap music! I got the Roka Salad and loved it, but next time I would add lamb or chicken. My husband got the Korinthian Lamb with fries and it was incredible! The lamb had so much flavor and was so tender. I'm still craving it! We went during the grand opening so it was insanely busy, but I noticed the entire family was working their butts off. I love that Greko is family run business and you can feel how much pride they take in their food and how much they want you to be a part of it. Great food, great service, and a fun atmosphere. The best part is that it's traditional Greek food, but not what you would get at all the other Greek restaurants, its truly unique!

Very disappointing, stopped for breakfast and it was not good at all. Didn't think you could screw up pancakes but they did. Should of known I was making a bad mistake by going to this restaurant for breakfast when the place right across the street ( flap jacks) had more cars in there parking lot 13 to 2 than this place....will not be back

Came with a large group for an early dinner.  I was excited to visit a brewhouse, but very very underwhelmed by the selection of beers. Nothing innovative or exciting here.

For my food, I ordered the fried chicken sammy with fries. My sandwich was so sad, ya'll! The chicken patty was way too small and didn't cover the entire bun. The fries were even hohum, IMO - even after adding salt and pepper they weren't tasty enough to tempt me.

It might depends on what you order, because my table-mate got a red fish, that was packed with flavor.

They did make a mean irish coffee for me, and our service was fine - I just wouldn't send someone here to eat with so many good NOLA options.

The food here is amazing, but they can sadly never get my order right. I've ordered guac in a burrito, that was left out but I was still charged for it. They also added beans into my burrito when I did not order them. 
The past time that I was there they gave me the wrong rice too. They've messed up my friends orders each time too. There is sadly always a few things wrong with my order. 
Very disappointing because I wanted to love them!

My husband and I went here this past weekend. We were served by Sam, who was attentive, informative, and fun. I don't believe in ordering meatloaf when you go out to eat, because, hey, that is an easy make-at-home meal. However, on Sam's suggestion, I gave it a try. What a beautiful decision! We started with the edamame ravioli. My husband loved it, I liked it. The truffle oil flavor was a touch heavy for me. We closed out with a vanilla bread pudding with a fresh whipped cream. We could barely walk back to our hotel we were so full. Our bill total (including 2 beers) was $70, which is amazing for this caliber of food in Old City. Give it a try. I can't wait to go back.

This is such a gem - esp for vegans !

There is an incredible, welcoming vibe as soon as you enter.   It's clear that food is made with Love.

I got the Jamaican Jerk seitan wrap and it was utterly fresh and delicious and was seasoned/spiced to perfection!   Kale and rice were added to the seitan to make such a filling wrap that I could only eat one half for my dinner.

I complimented the meal with fresh ginger brew (Real Deal).

I took home a vegan dessert that I couldn't resist - a raw pineapple-ginger concoction that was part pie and part cake.  It was lovely and light!

I will absolutely return!

I love this place. It's my go to for steaks and pizza. The management is very kind and helpful and they employees are amazing. It's a very localized place that serves amazing food for cheap prices. You should definitely recommend this to your friends and family.

Just left from breakfast here. Terrible service. Long wait for the worst pancakes and potatoes I've ever had. Had to keep asking for coffee re fills.   Expensive too    Skip this place go to breakfast nook or rt 130 dinner in delran
Eggs weren't even good

4 stars because of the expensive prices but the food is good. Try them for happy hour. Meat is really fresh and authentic 

I tried the oysters this time. They were okay. 

LISTEN TO ME: best margaritas I've ever had!

We ate here on a Sunday afternoon and had an enjoyable experience overall.  Five of the six dinners (2 pastas, 2 chicken entrees and 1 beef medallions) were well received but the pulled pork was too dry.  The salads were just okay (the Ceasar was too wet).  Overall, it was a good value for the price paid.

This place has a variety of options and the service is great. The view from the 6th floor is beautiful. The chicken parmigiana portion was exceptional. The plate itself was decent - not roll your eyes good, but not nasty either. I would say the best parts of the meal were the calamari with the banana peppers they were really tasty. Lastly, the brownie cheesecake is TO DIE FOR

Had lunch with my daughter here today. Jamie was our server and was friendly and attentive. 
It took us forever to decide what we wanted, the menu is bigger than I expected!  I had a fried chicken sandwich that was very good - juicy chicken breast, flavorful breading. The house chips were also a hit!  She had a buffalo chicken salad that she said was amazing, except she got the sauce on her chicken a little hotter than she should have. We'll definitely be back!

This place is so good! I wish there were one in Philly!

I love me some cheesy, greasy, pizza, but if you want something a lot healthier, refreshing, and really delicious, come here!!  I got a slice of veggie # 1 (feta cheese, kalamata olives, red onions, fresh chopped organic tomatoes, romaine, organic tomato sauce) and veggie #6 (artichoke hearts, fresh chopped organic tomatoes, arugula, garlic, mozzarella, cubes of fresh mozzarella, gorgonzola, oregano) and both of them were delicious! Veggie #1 tasted more like pizza that you'd get from a place a California Pizza Kitchen, but they both were yummy.  I didn't realize that a slice is more like two (they cut a large piece in half), so I'll probably only get one next time because I was really full when I ate two of them   But I definitely want to come back here and try some other slices!

Also a BYOB, so that's always a plus.
Great food, great prices, and staff knows customers by name. Well run family establishment. Love the new hibachi and my kids enjoy it as well.
Been by here 100s of times but 1st time we've stopped. Better than Pappys. Everything really good. Homemade chips best ever. Baked beans good. Pulled pork sandwich piled high.  We'll be back.

Overpriced. The salad had brown avocado. Gross. Lettuce was wilty. My friend's burger was way overcooked. My other friend got the chicken sandwich, which was dry and crumbly. Fries were soggy. Service was seriously lacking.
Nice beer selections, eclectic crowd, chill atmosphere. NIce to stop by after work in shorts flip flops and not feel judged.  I also had the grilled cheese with pear sandwich which was quite tasty.

When I tell you this is my favorite restaurant EVER, please believe me! I work nearby this restaurant and I probably order from here at least two times a week. Their curries and pad thai are sooo good and tasty! I especially love that they are able to make their food super spicy if that is what you prefer. Also, the staff is incredibly kind. This place is just so great, I can't express just how much I love it.
No good, stay away. Tourist don't know any better steaks suck, overpriced not enough meat and sometimes overcooked quick with the wiz, I said American. Check out Jim's, Phil's or steves

Heard a lot of good things about this place and finally got around to trying it out.  Everything we had was excellent!!  Crab soup, onion soup, mild wings and garlic parmigiana wings.  Wings were perfect.  Best I have ever had.  Staff was friendly, professional and attentive.  Will definitely be heading back here.  What a treat.

This McDonalds is the best McDonald's in the area. I live no where near it, but it is still worth the drive when I want some good fast food. The staff is the friendliest I've ever experienced at any restaurant and the quality matches. What are all you people doing reading this review? Hurry up and get over to this McDonald's and have a great meal experience.

Loved this place!!!!  I had the buffalo style grouper sandwich and it was amazing!  My friend had some type of chicken salad pita and it was the best chicken salad I've ever tried.  Atmosphere is great.  We ended up sitting at the bar to eat because it was over an hour wait for a table and our service was fantastic!  Can't wait to go back to Clearwater to eat here again!

Maybe I just picked a bad time to go here for my first visit.  I was not impressed.  Don't get me wrong, the food is good, but m first and only experience was at lunch, on a Friday, for their buffet.  I feel like I was set up for failure.  I would go again to be proven wrong.  It was just kind of crazy in here.  It was hard to get a server to even refill my water glass.  The food was good, a nice sampling of different Indian dishes, but truthfully my favorite thing was the naan, which I could have eaten as my meal happily.  The dishes did have some nice spice on them, perfect for flavoring without being overwhelming or too hot (I'm a wimp, no shame in that) but other than that they were a little bland.  I love Indian food, and maybe the problem is I know exactly what I want and don't need a Golden Corral-style spread of choices to try.  Heads up, its wildly busy in here around lunchtime, so take that into account when planning your visit.  I hear dinner is a better time to go so maybe I'll give that a shot sometime, but I'm admittedly not in a hurry.

Convenient to the convention center this is a dive bar type of place. I've stopped in here 3 times now. Things to note. 1)There can be a little bit of a wait. 2)Red Beans and Rice is awesome but I don't care for the Sausage that comes with it. 3) Fried seafood is good. 3)Jambalaya feel short for me. 

There are lots of awesome places in the city. If you on a budget or looking for a solid lunch spot this is a good one.

HAD to try this place, just for the cupcakes. :)

And the cupcakes were YUMO - much better than Bee Sweet!

The breakfast was ok, but nothing special.

I definitely will give them another try.

Three and 1/2 stars.

Enjoy!

This place is pretty tasty. We had the Maple Pecan, Peach Pie and Cannoli. The cannoli one is the greatest donut I have ever had. The filling is so good. The other two were great as well. We live in the west side of town and hope they put a location in Speedway or Avon!

Oh and what a refreshing breath of air to be asked what kind of creamer I want in my coffee!

Love the inside too.

The atmosphere wins us over every time. Recommend the fried chicken or any breakfast dish (always get the steer in potatoes with cheese!). Great mimosas and good local beer options as well. They have a few tvs to watch the game but it doesn't take over the atmosphere at all. 

Staff are always very friendly and do not discriminate. I've seen them treat many different people with the exact same kindness they would anyone else. Love them!

Excellent! Great food and great atmosphere.   We stumbled upon this place and could not have enjoyed the food more!    I had the freshman and fries.  Outstanding.   Service was great and our server advised us to check out the Colts kick off party happening down the street. We will definitely be back!

Locally sourced ingredients, cute patio and tasty food. It's a great combination for this little place in Old Town Goleta. I have had the roasted veggie sandwich twice and I am craving it again. Highly recommend!
Hip spot with great food and staff. Everyone who mentioned this place recommended the Cuban sandwich and it did NOT disappoint! Def will visit again when I'm in Philly!

Muy chingon!  

Our go-to place for the best burritos in Nashville.  I've heard the tacos are great too but I love the burritos so much I never stray.  

I get the fish burrito or the bean burrito.  With LOTS of green sauce.  So spicy and good.  You can get french fries in your burrito if you need them ;)

The only problem with this place is that Charlie closes the cart on Sundays.  Boohoo!

I had been to Karlton Cafe once before with friends and it was a very good experience. Food was great, service was fast. I was hoping it would become a favorite go-to since it's right in town and within walking distance. I was also very excited to take my husband for his birthday, raving to him for weeks about the place. But after today's experience, I don't think I can ever bring myself to go back. We walked and arrived around 10:05 am on a Sunday. It was far from being packed. We got right in right away and seated. Our order was taken approximately 15 minutes later and that's when things started to go awry. The couple who was seated at the same time ordered, ate and left and we still hadn't been served. A couple who came in 15 minutes after we did, ordered, and was served and we were still waiting. We finally asked our waitress if she could check on our order and was met with a "I put the order in immediately after taking it ma'am". I didn't imply that she hadn't. I was just asking for her to check on it since we were still waiting and sometimes things get mixed up. We ended up waiting approx 50 minutes before we were served. Two of the orders were wrong. We had ordered two omelettes with prosciutto, red peppers and manchego cheese. We were served something with asparagus and ham. Our other two orders were ok, but the pancakes were a bit burned. Finally our omelettes came out but the home fries were not cooked all the way through, to the point of still being raw/crunchy. We let the hostess know as nicely as we could that we were severely disappointed with our experience. That was met with nothing but a sorry. So we paid (full price, no comp or percentage off offered) and on the way out, my husband asked for the owner who happens to be the chef. He relayed his experience and that was met with a "then go find some place better". Needless to say, I don't think that is very customer friendly and I am severely disappointed by his attitude and unwillingness to keep us as paying customers. And overall, I'm really disappointed because I had a good experience before and hoped to make it a regular stop for us.

I finally got a chance to check out the Gold-N-Silver recently.  After walking by it so many times since I've been a Reno local, the old-skool Googie sign outside and the overall grunge of the place finally drew me in.  Gotta say that this place has the biggest assortment of newspaper machines on a single property that I've encountered in Reno yet!

Don't expect Caesar's Palace for the decor, as it's more like a throwback from the 70s.  It really reminded me of the Top Deck at the Cal Neva, one of my all-time favorites in town.

Friendly, attentive staff.  There appears to be a little slot/video poker parlor on the property as well.  The place touts itself for being featured on a previous episode of "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives."

For the food items, I went all out and tried the G&S Heartburn - tri tip, two cheeses, onions, peppers, chile, and creamy horseradish on grilled sourdough.  Awesome, especially with extra jalapeños thrown on!  I also got an order of fried zucchini, something only a few restaurants around here seem to have on the menu.

Prices were incredibly cheap, and the other menu items looked incredibly varied - everything from comfort foods like meatloaf, to pizza, steak, pork chops, and banana splits.  I was pretty impressed to see that there were lots of tri tip dishes.

The cherry pie was awesome, just not sure if it was homemade or not.

Don't let appearances fool you.  This place is old-skool Reno.  Give it a try!
Love the fried pickles and they have a ton of unique and vegetarian options.  Service is lackluster.

Tonight (12/10/21) at approx 11pm I walked in wawa that I've been going to since I moved to delaware county in 2001 so roughly 20 years. This wawa is located in drexel hill PA. It's at the corners of garret rd and burmont rd. So approx at 11pm I walked into wawa with a PA lottery cash voucher and i wanted to hand it in to receive cash from the winnings i had on acouple PA scratch off winning tickets. From previous predicaments like this I was under the impression if the cash voucher is under $100 then wawa shoulder honor that cash voucher no problem.when I handed the voucher to the cashier first she kind of looked past me toward where they make the sandwiches and everything else for I guess help or she had a question. Then she looked at her watch and told me "we dont cash vouchers past 10pm" I said "really" she says "yes" so I asked her" is it just this wawa or ALL WAWA'S. She said All wawas..I said ok and walked out. At that point i couldnt help myself but to go directly up burmont rd to another wawa and told them about my experience not 10 minutes ago...3 people couldnt believe what I just told them. My voucher was honored at the second wawa so questions or issues. I guess my goal here is not to get anyone fired or in trouble in anyway shape or form. Just gotta be a better wawa in the hiring process to test for laziness. Rant over

We showed up just a half hour too late to order breakfast. Y'know when you have your head (or stomach) set on something and you just can't move past it? I was craving biscuits like nobody's business, but eventually settled on the 'Lisa's Cornbread" with a side of collards (had to include SOME greens, so I could eat the cornbread guilt-free.) That cornbread was AMAZING! It was also ginormous. I was expecting a small-ish square portion, but it came out as a loaf. Delicious butter and some kind of cane syrup were the perfect accompaniments. The collards were very nice too, with chunks of ham and beans. It was also a pretty big bowl. Then again, for $8....

The space was bright and open with a modern rustic vibe. The waiters were really nice and very patient when I was confused about my lack of biscuit dilemma. Next time I'm in New Orleans, I need to go back for the biscuits.

Back again three years after my initial visit, and it's better than I remembered. We came here on an early Sunday afternoon and there was plenty of seating. Here, you order and pay at the counter, seat yourselves, and then they bring out your food. Subsequently you place your dirty dishes in a slot when you've finished. 

I ordered the standard beef bibimbap with a fried egg, and it was quite good. I've never had mind-blowing bibimbap.. since it's literally boiled vegetables and marinated meat mixed together with rice, but the ingredients tasted fresh and the portions were generous. Got like... 5 different veggies in this meal, so definitely not feeling guilty upon leaving!

great staff 
friendly ,food is quick ,coffee is hot and fresh
gas attendants are quicker than most gas stations
love my journey to this store more than others in the area
got to  give them props haven't had a bad visit yet
customers there are always friendly too
Love this place for my coffee. they are always pleasent. this is another gem of a find in Media.

We ordered buffalo chicken pizza. Absolutely do not recommend. Cheese was definitely cheap processed crap. Chicken was shredded, probably canned chicken. Also the buffalo sauce was basically blue cheese salad dressing which was disgusting to say the least.

This was our first time here. I have heard rave reviews of the pizza here, so we decided to give it a shot. I am left feeling very ambivalent. We picked a good time as they were not busy. To begin with the 3 of us were seated at a table where the 4th chair had been removed. After several minutes someone came around to fill our glasses with water. My glass had water marks all over it. Several minutes later a waitress walked by and said she would be back with menus. We sat for almost 10 minutes before we even had a menu to look at. We had fun conversation with the flies on the window. We ordered the garlic toast as an appetizer. One would have thought with as messy as toast is, they would have given us plates. Nope, just had to deal with crumbs everywhere. The pizza came, and it was good. The crust was crisp enough to handle all the toppings put on it. Napkins were rough on the face wiping the grease off. When waitress noticed us talking to flies she offered to get a flyswatter. Honestly I'd rather the fly on the wall then have fly guts in my food or on the window I'm looking at. Overall the prices are too high for the experience you get. They want it to be high class, but it's more like the BBQ place that was here before.
Food is just ok. It's not worth the long wait. I've had better food in and out of the French Quarter.

Salads got smaller but same price. Noticed that last night. Use to be our favorite place. Pasta dishes are not consistent with the great flavor we once loved. One day it's good the next not so good and other days it could be so off and dry and lacking flavor. Last night the noddles didn't even stick to the sauce or cheese. So you tasted a lot of just plan noodle and it was like the cheese and sauce were a separate dish.  This really sucks because I used to rave about this place to everyone and it being the only place I have ever had great home cooked tasting pasta from a restaurant. It used to be if only certain people were not working the pasta wouldn't be good. Now it's more than hit or miss. I really do miss the old taste and way it was made. I don't see my self every getting the pasta again. Not sure I'll go back because it's already higher priced but the taste was worth it. Now the taste has gone from 10 to 5 and the salads smaller. I'm not sure it worth it anymore.

I was in Conshy for a night and wanted to go grab a good meal and some drinks afterwards. Flanigan's was the perfect place. We went to the restaurant portion first that was connected to the bar and it was good. The food was good, not great, but good and it satisfied my hunger. A good price and a good variety.

What I learned with dinner, though, is that they had a draft-beer selection the size of Pennsylvania. It was extremely extensive and simply wonderful.

The bar was great. It had a college feel (I was there on a Friday), but also contained a good mix of people so if you're a little older you don't feel out of place. It was also crowded at points, but never got to the point where it was uncomfortably crowded and most of the time, there was room to move. It was a perfect size, I'd say.

It was a great bar, great atmosphere and just a good vibe. I really enjoyed myself and if I'm ever in the area again, I'll plan another nightly outing to the Boathouse. The reason it got four stars instead of five was based on the restaurant portion. However, heard the wings there are awesome, so I'd try those if I went again. The bar was 5 stars plus a couple!!

We drove around from Mount Juliet just to get our fix. Chicken is moist and tender, fried mushrooms are flavorful as well as the fries and seasoning. Atmosphere is clean and inviting. Our cashier Melissa was upbeat and friendly! We definitely recommend coming here if you get the time.

One of the best places for raw oysters. Nice and cold and shucked very well with no shell residue. I had a fried fish sandwich that was so large I had to bring some home. Like others have said, ambience is straight up bar, but that's what makes it fun.

Went there this morning and originally had a party of four but was actually five. So we told them we made a mistake and said we can take another table. Instead they brought us another chair. About 15 min later the manager came out and told us we had to get up because the chair was in the way and that we have to wait outside another 20 min for a different table. We had three young children already had our drinks and we originally asked before the waitlist grew. We have never been so disrespected by a restaurant! DO NOT GO THERE!!!
This place is so good. Very authentic in taste and super inexpensive. Best Thai food I've had in a while.

I have a new favorite place on Mass Ave! It's not a large place, although if the weather is nice they have a nice outdoor seating area.   The Tavern has a good selection of alcoholic beverages, and while the menu isn't huge, what they do have is delicious! Our group of four had: a salad with side of brisket, the crispy chicken sandwich with fries, the brisket nachos, and the pastrami Reuben with pimento mac. The entire meal was fabulous! The staff was friendly and attentive. The atmosphere clean and relatively quiet.  At a part of the Cunningham group of restaurants so you can earn points if you are a member.   I will be back!

Where the heck has Half Liter been hiding this whole time? Or maybe I should say: Where the heck have I been? Because apparently, lots of people have been to Half Liter, and lots of people love it. Though I'm late to the game, I'm glad I discovered this restaurant, and I'm sure I'll be back many times.

One important thing to know, right from the start, is that Half Liter is an offshoot of Liter House. They both occupy the same building, but they are on different sides. One side is the barbecue section (Half Liter), where it's a little more laid back and you order at the counter. This is where most of the families were (and where my family decided to go). On the other side is Liter House, where they serve German-style food, and it's a more traditional restaurant. 

We decided to visit Half Liter, the barbecue side, and the thing over on this side is that you find your own table, write down orders for alcoholic drinks and clip them to a stand at your table, and then order your food at the counter. This ordering system wasn't my favorite, because someone came to take my beer order as my husband was at the counter ordering food, so the server had to coordinate with the person taking my husband's order to make sure my drink was included on the tab. If that sounds confusing, it is, and like I said, it's not my favorite, but the food makes up for the convoluted ordering system.

The food! Specifically: the ribs! I could eat multiple racks of Half Liter's fall-off-the-bone ribs all day long. They were the best thing that we ordered, and I see myself coming back for future orders of ribs. They were smoky, slightly sticky and tender -- all of the things you want from ribs.

We also got the Eddie's Melt, which is smoked pork, collard greens, pimento cheese and caramelized onions. So much meat! If you're looking for a substantial sandwich with a lot of meat in it, get this one. It was delicious. 

We had kids with us, so we also ordered off the kids menu. The kids cheeseburger was fine: The server specifically made a point to tell us that it's not anything special -- just a burger between a bun that they keep warmed in a warming tray. But kids don't care. My kids didn't care. As long as it looks like a burger and it doesn't have anything spicy on it or anything extra, then they are happy. It wasn't the best kids cheeseburger, but it did the job.

This restaurant can get loud from all the people talking and enjoying their meals, but Half Liter keeps the music at a decent level, which I appreciate! (As I get older and more of a curmudgeon, there's nothing that ruins a dining experience faster than overly loud music.) The service is also very fast and not overly obtrusive.
Good, hearty breakfast food and not very expensive at all. There really isn't a bad item on the menu, they do everything exceptionally well.

First - the food here is fantastic. You can't go wrong with the breakfast, especially the Huevos Rancheros.

However, the service is just terrible. It takes forever to get coffee to start breakfast, forever to order, forever for the check to come, etc. The kitchen is actually quite fast. It is just that the servers are a) under-staffed and b) just pretty slow/"chill".

Lastly, the service was so bad on my last visit I tipped 10% since I usually am quite accommodating but the server was quite surly. I come to find out my credit card statement does not match the amount I signed for - it was only off by $2, but still.

I came across this restaurant because I was looking for a place that allowed dogs. I had a puppy with me and did not feel comfortable leaving him in the car while I ate, so I stumbled across this place on yelp's handle filters. 

I sat outside and the weather was perfect. The environment was very comforting with live music and other dog owners. I give this places four stars because the menu is very limited -see attached photos. 
Side note: food gets cold because you're seating outdoor, so keep that in mind when you want to dine outside. 

I ordered the spicy shrimp pasta and it was alright. The sauce was very watery, which I wasn't expecting. It wasn't as spicy as I would like but it wasn't bad. It was a big dish and they were generous with the shrimp. I was surprised that I had 11 shrimps in my pasta! 

My friend ordered the house specialty meatloaf. I enjoyed that dish a lot more than my own. The mashed potato was delicious. 

To top everything off, I ordered a key lime pie and it was delicious. I was very full but I made room for dessert. The key lime pie was delicious and the crust was subtle and not overwhelming sweet. I only wished that it was a bigger slice than a sliver. 

I would recommend this place on a nice sunny day, and if you have a dog! Big or small, they welcome them all!

The food is typically not bad, I think the Philly locations has a more authentic taste than the SoCal locations do but of course it does not beat the OG cart. The late night staff is pretty good, nice people. My main issue with this place is the afternoon staff.  I've had issues with them trying to get my order right such as asking for an extra pita and they do not add it until I confirm with the cashier that they included it in the bag. Sometimes the bread has been inconsistent as well, sometimes it's very dry other times they give me 3 instead of 4 slices. I've also scanned my halal card and have checked online and some visits were not registered. Lastly, they advertised having free fries on their facebook page once, it said to show the post to the cashier. I did just that and the cashier said he knew nothing about that promotion, he asked the "manager" which I doubt was the manager since she wasn't even in the restaurant she had just walked in from outside and was not wearing anything that identified her as the manager, the managers typically wear the blue shirt instead of the yellow shirt, she was simply wearing a college sweater. She claimed that her superior had not told her anything about the promotion so I left with no fries which was the only reason I bothered making the trip since I had never tried their fries before. Lesson learned: the social media staff does not communicate with the stores directly.

I'm confused about all of the 4-5 star ratings.

The service, atmosphere, and K83 pale ale while waiting were all fantastic, but the food is a different story.  I had 3 tacos - fried Mahi Mahi, grilled fish of the day (perch), and grilled shrimp. The fried fish had no crispiness/flavor to it, and the perch was under-seasoned. The shrimp were great, but I didn't want to ruin them by keeping them in the bland taco, so I ate them separately. The jicama/slaw were fine, but it's hard to make a good taco without lime and cilantro. 

I'm determined to find things I like here because it's in my neighborhood, so I'll be back to try the other things on the menu. But for now, pretty underwhelmed, JG!

Superb donuts!! I brought these in to work one day and everyone raved about how delicious they were. You can tell they're homemade (and well-made on top of that)! They have a good variety, but don't try to get too fancy with the flavors. I am so glad I found this place. Also, the woman working the counter was very nice and patient with me as I chose all of my donuts. Definitely recommend!

Great place for steaks. Explains everything you could ever want to know about beef cuts. I ordered the chicken was perfectly cooked, juicy and tender. 

I will be coming back!!

I absolutely love it here!! We have been to this location more times than I can count and have had a great experience!! I am not sure what the others on here are talking about?! I have had chicken parm, veal mozzerella and chicken sorrento...each one of them is amazing. The staff is friendly and the atmosphere is elegant. I higly reccomend
Castellis is a very nice place to eat at.  The chicken is very tasty and this last time ordered the chicken Parm.  Yum.  Must visit here!

Didn't hang around to wait one hour to eat microwaved food. I can't justify an hour of my time for flour food. My gut will thank me later. Got a good visual and there's nothing authentic in this chain.

I normally like the food here but picking up togo that I called in advance maybe 15 minutes and still sat around for 30 minutes and there are only 4 small tables. They also dont allow you to order food for the kids to go and have to get adult portions of everything.

Wednesday night me and my boyfriend went in for a nice and chill drink night and walked right out within 5 minutes. We sat down at the bar and the bartender asked us for our IDs (which is cool cause we look  young) anyway she had an issue with my boyfriend's ID because it was coming up in the middle. So she is explaining this bullshit reason why she can't serve him/us. Basically saying because his ID was raised alittle in the middle that it's invalid and putting her job at risk. Which I know is bullshit because I took the RAM courses and all. So as she's explaining this guy is standing behind us like he was ready to kick us out. Instead of kicking the CAT out that was drinking water on top of the station (talk about unsanitary) so we walked down the street to the thirsty soul to valid what I wanted to say to the cat loving bartender. And low and behold I was correct and the thirsty soul accepted my boyfriend's ID and even traveled  to center bars as well ACCEPTED HIS ID WITH NO PROBLEM

I understand the buzz. Loved this place. Clean, fun, wide variety of items on the menu.

What makes it stand out- the long and eloquent descriptions of different kind of dishes that spells things out for non-Vietnamese like me. Plus some rare dishes that I haven't been able to find since leaving Viet town in Orlando- they have them here, clear and plain as day.

Waitstaff is super attentive. Food cane quickly and was perfect. 

We will be back!
The best place ever. And I'm a burger snob. Their Nutella milkshake was one of the best things I've ever tasted.
Really cheap, tastes amazing, huge serving size. What more can you ask for? The place is cash only but there is an ATM machine in the front.

We came here and were so disappointed. We requested the rooftop and loved the atmosphere but wish we had a better experience. 

Our server Ari was not the friendliest from the moment we sat. We asked simple questions and were given smart remarks. 

One person in our party couldn't have alcohol and instead of mentioning their mocktail menu, they were provided smart remark for a Shirley temple and announced loudly as if we were 18. 

The limited menu was.. well limited. Which we understand but between the rudeness of our server and limited food item, we decided to leave. 

We fully understand COVID and 100% understand we were in the heart of tourist district Broadway but the service was what rubbed us the wrong way.

I am a picky Cuban-American and my friend is an even pickier Puerto Rican. We were driving by and decided to stop and try Mi Caribe since St. Louis's selection of Latino restaurants leaves something to be desired. What a find!

The owner helped us and was very friendly. He took a lot of pride in the restaurant and told us where each piece of art work came from. He informed us that the chef was Dominican and that many of the dishes were prepared Dominican style. 

My friend wanted the mofongo but was on the fence because she doesn't like Dominican mofongo. The owner assured us that that all of the Puerto Rican customers seemed very pleased with the dish. She ordered one for herself and we both loved it. We were so impressed that we ordered 4 to go to feed our families for dinner.
