I ordered the vaca con tostones and was equally impressed. The skirt steak was very well seasoned. Even though the steak was on top of the tostones, the tostones were crispy and delicious. 

I recommend this place to anyone who misses or likes authentic Dominican, Puerto Rican or Cuban food. We'll definitely be returning.

Phenomenal little gem outside of Philly. Great whiskey selection and great eclectic menu where you can't go wrong....from the burger with Lebanon bologna to the short rib with the beet juice soaked latke. Simply stated....can't go wrong....
The food is excellent, the atmosphere is open and fun with beautiful wood accents and boisterous staff!

Wow! Just wow! I am usually not a fan of doughnuts but Dotties definitely made me a doughnut believer. a friend gifted a half a dozen and within a day they were all gone. I side eyed it for a couple of hours, a vegan doughnut? I doubted that these doughnuts were going to change me, but my gosh! It did.

I love this place, I think they're reasonably price their drinks are always awesome. The food is outstanding.With all that being said, they have some really cool desserts. I would just like to add to this post because I just had a lovely seafood enchiladas at the Kingfisher. Wow, it was amazing their enchilada sauce is wonderful! If you get Chance you should go check it out because they only have it six months out of the year. So good!

This was our first visit to Roberto's!
We are in St. Louis visiting family & friends.
We had lived in St. Louis, MO for over 50 years, now in California.
The entire experience was incredible.
From Shannon the receptionist, to Sterling our amazing waiter, who used to work at the famous Al Baker's (no longer in business) to our chef Roberto who made a mouth watering, delicious dinner for the four (4) of us.  Yummy!  Can't wait to return,. We are telling all of our local friends, not to miss dining @ Roberto's.
Thank you for a wonderful experience,
Lilo Cooper
ps:  Mike Seidler gave us the recommendation to dine @ Roberto's.

I haven't been here since I was kid, so when Groupon offered a great deal I couldn't pass it up. Firstly, I never came here expecting to enjoy the food at an arcade, but their pizza is AMAZING. The games are also quite updated since the last time I was there. Lastly, the customer service is really good here too and they are more than happy to help with any question. Awesome!

Saturday night ordered takeout for 3 and was told it would be ready in 15 minutes.  Went to pick up order and had to wait 30 more minutes to get my order.  The girl was very nice but offered no reason why had to wait on food & the restaurant was not busy only a few tables with customers. So disappointing the food as it was mediocre & lukewarm.  The enchiladas were not tasty and needed some seasoning & the tacos were very, very small as if made for a 5 yr old child. The prices are high for what you get.   Reason for the 1 star:  Guacamole was very good, but just a small container so even that alone is not worth purchasing.  Overall, I would not recommend this place to eat as you will be disappointed in the food and the restaurant itself.
I was in Reno for graduation at UNR and had the entire extended family with us. They took in 20 of us easily and were polite with all of us. The food is good standard diner food in my opinion.

Sampan is a ultra modern, rustic Asian-fusion restaurant located in the heart of Philadelphia. I came here (on what might be the most humid summer evening) with a group of friends who were familiar with the area. I never would have found this place if I wasn't with a local. However, it is to be noted that we didn't go to the main dining area. We actually went through an inconspicuous alley leading to the outdoor Graffiti Bar hidden behind the restaurant -- mainly to grab a few cocktails and a quick bite. Both, the drinks and food, were just brilliant. Very well priced, fresh ingredients and a perfect combination of flavors. That is the simplest way to describe everything that arrived at our table. 

Despite arriving during Happy Hour on a Saturday, we were able to find a table near the bar after a few minutes of waiting. The decor is very rustic, and chic. The bartenders are very friendly and professional. As far as food, I ordered the Spicy Chicken Wings, which were pipping hot and came with marinated carrots and cucumbers. Mind you, this only came out to $4. Yes. $4. In regards to drinks, we ordered the Chapter II, Ming Mule, Cocktail of the Day, and the Mid Town Punch scorpion bowl. All of these were tasty, crisp and refreshing. I would highly suggest that you just try whatever you find interesting on the menu. Everything they serve will just leave you craving for more. Will definitely be back here again!
It's good, but too many of the sandwiches taste the same due to over saucing.

Not sure how they stay open. Second time I been in and told nobody to pour a beer, of course this was after standing at the counter without being acknowledged for awhile. No hi how you doing tonight we will be right there. Then when someone does bother to come take my order no greeting just whats your name. Only reason i keep trying them is they are the only place close for pizza. Guess from now on its the blind onion and see if their service has gotten any better.

The bagels are delish, especially the whole grain bagel.  the food  good, quick service, good prices, although the Cole slaw was iffy.   However, the place is so dirty,   absolutely disgusting.  Take the bagel to go and try not to think about the rest.  PS,  gas station bathrooms are much cleaner, do your self a favor and use the bathroom there.

I have been here a few times now, and have been extremely pleased with a lot of their menu items. The chicken kabob is excellent (honeslty, though, I am a sucker for a charcoal grill) and the hummus is tasty.  The only thing I was disappointed in was the chicken shawarma.  It was just kind of dry and blah-tasting.  But overall, I can't complain., and they deliver, too!

This is a very well known brunch location, but I have to say the options always leave me a bit uninspired. It seems to cater to sweets and baked goods, which are great, but the savory side- dishes like eggs and other brunch basics, lack the same touch. I've stopped getting the potato pancake dishes, and tend towards any options with smoked salmon because they get really good salmon.

By far the best place for sweets though and worth a little wait.

Loved everything about the place BUT...food great, service great, restaurant week.  Took 7 friends, good times..until the check.  For 7 individuals,  they would only accept TWO credit cards.  How awkward is that?   Never bring a gang of friends there again.  Very strange business policy.

PURE ASS. 

Decided to hit this spot up after the gym while I used the Laundry Cafe nearby. Big mistake!
My chicken sandwich was hard and the Whopper was cold and crusty! I worked in a BK in high school and it was never like this. Prolly cause I care about food. 

This was like I was biting into Asscheeks. 
And I'm not talking like Rhianna cause I'd eat those cheeks viciously... 
I mean Hermit gamer in the basement of his moms house eating Cheetos and beating off wearing the same draws for a week type of ass. 

Don't go here.

This place really surprised me ! 
Absolutely wonderful ! Food was amazing, very tasty and proportionate.
Bartender , Richard , was on point ! Service was amazing and his recommendations for food totally hit the spot. 
Very friendly and live environment! But also mellow and welcoming ! 
I would definitely recommend this place to any one that wants to be classy but have a good time !
Delicious salad, great coffee, as a visitor to the city I was very happy they let me dine-in.
Great food, GREAT chile relleno..  taco tuesday $1.00 for street taco.. beer is cold and its just one of out go to places

Just moved to the Northern Libs and starting to explore the local eats. First great dining experience was at North Third. The food was banging and consistent on my two consecutive nights. Highly recommend the Chicken, Shrimp dumplings, Pork tacos (special), hanger steak and the cauliflower flat bread. The hummus wasn't anything special but otherwise the menu is far above normal bar fare. Allagash White on draft to top it off.

 It's a bit pricey but worth it and they accept credit cards. Chill atmosphere, plenty of space with an area away from the bar. Healthy crowd but wasn't packed on Wed/Thurs evening. We were quickly seated and had great attentive service. Will definitely be returning.

Love this place! I wish their menu was a bit more creative when it comes to coffee drinks but their mocha is awesome and their teas are out of this world. Each tea is loose leaf and you can you taste the difference.
Just OK at best.  Mo's Southwest Grill is MUCH better in taste, quality and friendliness.  Unlimited chips & salsa too which Qdoba offers neither

We craved a sandwich for dinner. We went on Yelp to find a sandwich place. We were at Nora's within minutes. This place oozes charm in every corner. We happened to go on a very windy and rainy night and the lights inside flickered a few times BUT that did not stop us. 

I really enjoyed the atmosphere of Nora's. I loved that it was small and cozy. I like the random decor and the little tables. Even on a terribly cold and rainy night, people would saunter in, shake off the rain, order a meal and read the paper in the tiny lit corner of the restaurant like a true regular!! I one day want to be those people!

Nora's had a nice selection of sandwiches to choose from and they offered soup and salad. I settled for the Smokin Turkey and it was very delicious. It was exactly what I needed that night. The service, I give them a 10 out of 10 for being very personable and friendly. I like that Nora's provides you with a SpotOn app option to check in and receive rewards! You very rarely find little businesses that have this feature.

I cant wait to go back to Nora's and try out the other sandwiches!!

We are here touring UC Santa Barbara college. It was my birthday and we wanted go to have some desert and a drink. I haven't had a Banana Foster in a long time. I saw the description and it sounded good. But just because something sounds good doesn't mean it's good.  Don't go here for the desert or a drink. Banana's were old and mushy, didn't have a good taste. Even Baskin Robins has a better banana's for their banana split. It's not an original flambé. Ordered their blood orange margarita..... pretty bad.... bitter taste. They don't even have a blender to make certain drink. View is beautiful because the place is on the beach.  Not a very good experience.  Save your money and go to some other places.

I've been going to this event for years and always have a great time. I do miss the days when they gave out the tokens instead of having the 'all-you-can-drink' wristbands, it seemed like a better value. They did offer pre-purchase tickets this year through Eldorado's website that saved you $6.50. I was excited to see Smashmouth on the stage but their sound guy must have been drunk because they sounded horrible! We didn't venture over to the other stage to check out any of the other music. We stopped by the Yelp booth for some swag and took a gander at the scavenger hunt. But after an hour of beers the task at hand was lost and beer was the only mission. By the end of the day I was toast but still managed to drink my Brew Brothers beer for checking in, good times! 8 hrs of beer drinking can really take it out of a guy.
The selection of beer they had this year was really good. I always like getting to try new brews to keep in mind for when its beer thirty.

Easily the best menu in New Orleans. That has nothing to do with the food, if you've read it you know what I mean.
You won't find fancy dishes here, this is straight up diner food and I have no problem with that. Whether it be a burger, fries, and a shake after a night of drinking (they are open 24/7) or starting the day off after a night of drinking and getting a chili omelet with a lot of coffee, there isn't a better value in the city. 
If it's not too busy and you take the time to interact with whomever is working, you're probably going to be entertained as well.
A must try if you have picky eaters, or just looking for some cheap eats.

Visiting near here on business and tried this restaurant for dinner based on the reviews. Excellent food and service. Extensive menu - Japanese, Thai, Asian fusion. I had the seafood delight and it was very good. If I lived locally I would definitely return.

Yes, yes, and more yes! 

Delicious veggie sausages in a perfectly toasted bun with all the toppings you could ever desire! 

Ask for the cheese fries to be topped with pico de gallo and sour cream--you won't regret it! They're so good! 

I opted for the apple smoked veggie sausage (or apple something? Idr) with: cheddar cheese, creole mustard, Jalapeños (they're pickled), onions & then the mother-in-law slaw and blackberry sauce on the side.

One person in my group mentioned that they were so full after eating theirs but wanted another one because they wanted to "keep tasting it" hahahah. I had to agree! I stayed full for hours after that but low-key wanted to go back for dinner later that night! 

Seriously, if you're vegetarian/vegan this is your place while in NOLA. The service is pretty fab, to boot!

Wow! First words that came to mind! We brunched here during their first ever Sunday brunch and our group left giving them our unanimous "best brunch award", and we brunch weekly so that's high praise! Our server, Tim, was great...friendly, quick, menu knowledge (even with this being their first brunch), and putting up with our brunch group which is no small task! I had the biscuits and gravy and was absolutely blown away by every aspect of them! They have a menu that will please everyone, along with a Bloody Mary like no other! I will be back, and soon!

I used to love Caddy's , great place with great food! Seems like since it has grown so big the quality of food and service can't keep up.... it took over an hour to get our food and it was cold... Yuck!

Ordered online, after I got home and realized that they charged me for extra mango dressing and guacamole, however there's NO dressing or guac on my tacos at all??? Just dry tacos. Great. They charged me for the things I requested but didn't get. And only two pieces of steak in both of tacos. Very disappointed in this whole online ordering, won't ever order it again. Great way to spend $25 on some dry rice and beans. Oh and I tipped too, guess wasn't enough tips for whoever made this to actually care and look through what I requested. 
Don't order online. They either can't read or don't care.
Amazing idea and phenomenal follow through. Food is delicious and the service is equally as great. Have day dreams about the chicken pot pie

A+++ Establishment. This is a up and coming gem. From the indoor and outdoor seating, to the yard games, to the delicious tropical variety menu this place is sure to be a hot spot on the beach!  Don't pass this one by. You'll be glad you stopped. All of the dishes we tried were delicious.

This is about the service, not the food. Food was fine, no issues. They are VERY VERY understaffed, at least on a Sat night when we went. I mean wow. This guy was waiting for his to-go order since the time we came in until I wrote this review...probably a hour minimum. This is absolutely horrible service. They need more bartenders and more waiters/waitresses for sure. Also, they have zero craft beer, none. I spoke to the mgr though and he said he's going to look into it. Also, I was informed the menu is limited from other Fridays...I didn't know that but seeing the menu I can tell. I won't be back.
First time eating Ethiopian and I couldn't be more pleased. The wait staff were very educational and explained every dish and how to eat it properly! Very impressed!

We dined here while on vacation.  We read good reviews, although we mistakenly dismissed all the ones about the huge portion sizes.  We both ordered the hotcakes and they were huge.  We easily could have shared one order.  They came with 3 huge fluffy pancakes, that we both could only eat half of.  They were 7.95 each.  We also ordered a side of fried potatoes, that were just ok in my opinion.  My husband got a coffee which he said was good and which they came around frequently to refill.  I ordered a diet coke for $1.95 and got a can of it.  Service was average.  Order was correct and received quickly but my husband had to ask for water 3 times.  The atmosphere was friendly, although the tables were a bit crowded.  Overall we would eat here again, but we would definitely share a plate.

Cons:  Bland pizza.  Little flavor.
Pros:   Near university.  Moderate pricing.

Tried one slice of Pepperoni and Sausage.  
Good size.. about  $4 w/ tax.

Looked great...unfortunately sauce and toppings were bland.  Won't go back.
Food was good but only concern I found is location. I am not sure about this town but the way this is located was not looking comfortable to me.

I'll begin by saying there are places I find decidedly unimpressive; chain restaurants generally fit that category.  Bar Louie is certainly a chain, and it's certainly average, unoriginal, and makes a feeble attempt at providing a cosmopolitan ambiance.  Bar Louie fails the hardest at the latter.  To be clear, this is a reflection of the company itself - not just its Greenwood location.

My problems with Bar Louie began as soon as I was seated.  The restaurant is miserably loud. It's so loud that beckoning a server is impossible; ordering requires shouting, and conversation is limited.  As a result, I found the service to be unacceptable. Orders were incorrectly fulfilled, and I generally felt poorly accommodated.  While I would rate my server as average, I believe her blunders were caused by the noise - and not by incompetence. She was friendly and was sure to promptly refill sodas.

At a glance, the menu at Bar Louie is hip and "upscale."  In reality, it's a mere notch above Applebees.  We started with a round of "flash fried" calamari. It was decent.  I then had the "Gastroburger" and a side of French fries. With a "custom blended" patty and shaved sirloin steak, it was a tasty, yet mediocre sandwich.  The fries were also mediocre. If I were waylaid in an airport, it would have been above-average for that setting.

For a self-proclaimed "gastropub," I found the drink selection at Bar Louie to be uninspiring.  Other members of my dining party found their margaritas tasty.   The beer selection was retrograde.  There were a few microbrews interspersed with some ubiquitous European beers and a plethora of garbage brewskis typically found in rube's man cave (e.g. Bud Light, Blue Moon, etc).

My experience at Bar Louie was far from the worst dining experience of my life.  However, I have a finite number of days left on this planet (how many that is, I don't know), thus I won't spend another minute of it at this restaurant.

Thank you.
Really really good fried chicken.  Juicy and delicious.  Be careful, I ordered the medium and it was pretty dang spicy!

Great place, great value! Wonton soup was $8.50 and plenty for 2 people as an appetizer. Lo Mein was $10 (depending on protein) and plenty for 2 meals. Waitress was very nice as well. Highly recommend!

Super busy with a small amount of space. The managers never call back. Every time we go in and are able to sit down they never take our order correctly. Something is always missing and we have to ask repeatedly to have what we ordered. I just wish the location was a little bigger like the others. And it was run a little tighter. Everyone is moderately polite, but just needs to have more leadership.

Pork Belly taco - DO NOT EXCLUDE THIS TACO FROM YOUR PLATE. We each ordered three tacos. Big mistake on our part. We ended up ordering one-two more each. They were that amazing! My only negative was that I wish they had a better beer/alcohol selection.

This is one of the best meals I've had since I've been in new Orleans. I had the fried alligator it was super,I had the blackened red fish it was good too but the dusted shrimp in some kind of green sauce was the BOMB!! I will be back!!
Food and service excellent as always. Call ahead for a reservation to make sure you have a table since they are limited at this point in time. Best Italian food in the city!

Nice place--good, simple food. I was not sure I would like the cheese incorporated into my Crawfish Etouffee but I took a chance and it was to-die-for. Good comfort food. 
My only sad moment was to discover no booze served here...prefer a cold one to wash down the yummy hot sauce but oh well, the food is worth the trip. Cute decor, lively hipster crowd. I will be back!

The veggie Cuban from The Hot Tomato is the kind of sandwich I crave when I am in other parts of the country. It might be the perfect sandwich. During the pandemic, I have 100% driven to their restaurant, placing an order on the way, picked up take out, and eaten my sandwich in the car. 
This is the kind of sandwich I will drive an hour out of my way to get. Yes, they have other food. They have an immense bakery. Really, though, the Cubans are worth it alone.
We came here for brunch, and it was the most mediocre food I have had in a long time. It's hard to mess up brunch food- I just had a simple frittata and potatos but it had no flavor at all.
Great food! Great and friendly service! I would recommend this place for anyone looking for some wonderful Mediterranean food!
I have had a lot of grouper sandwiches in my 50 years and theirs was the best. Unbelievably fresh and perfectly blackened

Not the best breakfast in NOLA but very good

I had the St James crepe.   It comes with about a pound of shrimp and crab although it was missing hollandaise sauce.  this would really have improved the breakfast.

This place is all over the place. There is really no hostess. The line to pay is very long. The food is average but came up fast. They do have helpers delivering the food. One day our server was average, the next quick and friendly, next all over the place. I know it's busy but they need a hostess and to be a bit more organized.
This is a great Sushi place. Their food always fresh and delicious. I think this is one of the best sushi places I ever visit!

If you want to give the middle finger to the pandemic the communal stylings of fondue is an ideal way to kick that obnoxious bastard to the curb - with the extremely fun Melting Pot as your spirit guide to the bubbling crude.

Things sure have changed since we were dipping our adolescent forks into half-melted Velveeta from my mom's avocado green electric fondue pot (a housewarming gift from Carol Brady no doubt.) Now, cheese is just the opening act as veggies, meats and chocolates can all be submerged into the boiling goo. 

It's fun but please go with someone you really like because you'll be swapping spit all night, just like those carefree days BC (Before Covid) when lost, shared and mangled food led to shots and chasers and not a 911 to the CDC.

Honestly, this is a novelty meal and is priced accordingly - you can even watch your credit card melt down during dessert. But let's stay on point. If you're looking for a change of pace and want everyone leaving happy (unless they're a doosh) you could stick your fork into far worse places. The Melting Pot is an easy five stars.
Great place and great service!! All the flavors look and taste great. My personal favorite is Llama Licious. Over 100 choices! Awesome place for dessert

I have eaten twice for lunch at Ingatius.  The service has been pleasant and accommodating, the food excellent, and and location is great. When you finish, save dessert for Sucre a block away.  It's a great way to experience the "other" part of New Orleans.  It's not all about the quarter!

Another amazing lunch here. Tableside sangrias are amazing. We changed up everything this time, and once again everything was perfect. Think I need to rent out one of the many dining rooms here for a bash sometime.

Simon the bartender is awesome and I found my all time new favorite salad; the baby kale and beet salad. Pumpernickel croutons, goat cheesy, pomegranate seeds . And I finally found a bartender that can make an espresso martini that doesn't taste like the sweetest syrups

Dear Marilyn Hagerty,

I loved your earnest and glowing review of the Olive Garden in the Grand Forks Herald last year.  I am impressed that with your words you were able to capture the attention of Anthony Bourdain and have inspired so many people to re-examine American culture through food (whether it's our own self-criticism about bi-coastal elitism, the over-thinking of degustation, or rethinking restaurant chains in general).  I do believe, though, that if you came to Philly and tried Mercato, you would have a lot to say.

First, I think you would fall in love with the charm of the area around 12th and Spruce.  I imagine that you would come by around opening time for the restaurant to avoid the later crowds and wait times.  You would enjoy walking down Spruce Street, admiring the brownstones and older architecture, and up the steps to the restaurant and finding it to be a single room with an open kitchen where you can watch the chefs firing up dishes.  You may be surprised to find the host or hostess keeping track of seating via an iPad but then immediately look around to the simple yet elegant details in the restaurant's decor, complete with carvings on the ceiling tiles.  Yes, the ceiling tiles will make the Tuscan arches of the Olive Garden fade away like a bad dream.

You may be a little disappointed that the bread at Mercato does not quite have the same allure as the hot, processed white oil-covered breadsticks one gets used to at the Olive Garden, but you may be pleased by the herb butter and your ability to bring your own favorite wine here.  No, the waitstaff at Mercato do not wear the crisp black trousers and yellow dish towels you so love at the OG, but you would quickly become impressed at their knowledge of all the ingredients that go into the specials of the day.  

Now on to the food.  The few black olives offered with the unlimited salad bowl at your Grand Forks eatery would pale in comparison to the flavorful savory broth of the mussels you can start with here; no canned garnishes are needed to add flavor.  Although you found the chicken alfredo ($10.95) at OG to be warm and comforting on a cold winter day, you would find the short rib ragu to be the definition of comfort food ($13-14 for fresh ingredients for a half-portion that is more than enough for one person) with well made gnocchi and broccoli rabe to accompany the tender meat that soaks up the broth.  I would not judge you if you ended up licking the bowl clean and gobbling up one of the succulent seafood pyramids from your dinner companion's pyramid pasta plate.

After the ragu, you would thank yourself for wearing pants with an elastic waistband in anticipation for splitting the salmon dish, which again is so beautifully cooked, sitting on expertly prepared risotto and kale, all enhanced with the acidity of the lemon butter sauce.  At this point, you may pass out from a food (or wine) coma, but I am sure your dinner companion would inform you that the tiramisu was quite good.

Ah, Marilyn, how you would love this place.  It may inspire you to move away from Grand Forks, North Dakota and come live / eat / critique in Philly.  One can only hope and dream.

Much love from one of your biggest fans,
Jen

I arrived late in the night so I was very happy this place was open, I'd eat anything at that point so it was a plus that it was also pretty good! BLT was fresh/tasty.

Our server, Christine, was a doll! Loved her!!

With the overwhelming crowd, lines, and food choices of Reading Terminal I chose this place because there was no line and i typically love duck.  Ordered the special (roast duck roast pork wonton noodle soup) thinking I would get a little taste of everything and i did. I know there was duck. It actually had small bones which is quite annoying when trying to enjoy a soup. I didn't get to fully enjoy the duck because of those bones. Then there was the other meat. I couldn't tell if it was pork or a different cut of duck. It was team
really chewy. Definitely did not enjoy the meat component to my meal, but what i truly did enjoy were the wontons ,the noodles, songs the broth. Those were amazing which is how they earned 3 stars from me

Pretty decent burger place. I was in town for work and this place popped up on yelp and other sites as one of the best burgers in town, so I'm all in. 

I sat at the bar, it was early around 11:30am but there were a few seats outside. I assume they get busy because there were a ton of staff around. As I was leaving there was a steady stream of people coming in.

I was between the burger with stilton bleu cheese and the burger with a garlic aioli, the bartender (very friendly guy by the way), say get the garlic aioli one (it started with a P). I took him at his word and ordered that with a side of onion rings.

It came out pretty fast, almost too fast like it was back there waiting pre cooked or something. But, it was still a pretty tasty burger. Worth the price tag. I enjoyed it, big. messing and filling. The patty itself could have used a bit more seasoning in my opinion. The onion rings were few, but good. They weren't crispy at all more a soggy outside which was kinda disappointing, I like the just out of the fryer type onion rings, these were more like reheated onion rings. The marinara style ketchup that came with it was good.

Overall a pretty good spot, nice, clean, great service and pretty good food. I think I just got unlucky with those onion rings.

Wow - best Indian food I've had in a while!  We got the veggie pakoras to start with, and they were excellent.  The shahi paneer was also amazing - though we'd ordered it medium spicy and it came mild.  The dhal makhani was pretty good.  And the mango lassis were great.  

The service was very prompt and the staff super friendly.  

I can't wait to go back again soon!

Chyrill was great, with us and the kids! The Chipotle chicken wrap was a bit too spicy but the southwest ranch it came with was a great pairing. Kiddo had mini corn dogs off the kids menu and they were typical fried kids food but he loved them. We started with the creamy chicken and rosemary soup on Chyrill's recommendation and it was delicious! Kiddo had fries and we had the tots and we shared so we could taste them both as we are potato fans! Both were tasty but I think the crispy fries were just a touch better. 

It's a seat yourself place with tall tables and chairs, and a big football crowd that is a bit loud and can be rowdy during game time, but a casual atmosphere still. 

There are definitely a few things I want to come back and try (a few of the tacos, the Curb Dip). We will probably try to avoid coming during a football Sunday crowd but will be back! The service was what knocked The Curb into five stars, although the food was a solid four.
Good food and Friendly staff. We'd definitely come back. Really enjoyed the German Pancakes.

Love this place, we have been coming here for lunch for a year now on an almost weekly basis. Here is what they do really well: summer rolls, Pho, egg drop soup, dumplings (fried or steamed), their signature sizzling Clay Pot, and my personal favorite, Singapore Mei Fun. The only reason I give it 4 stars instead of 5 is price, they are roughly 25% more than a comparable establishment (but I am happy to pay for good food).
Awesome! It was a busy night but the line moved quickly and the food was delicious! If you are in the area you really must try Martin's!

Really a very pleasant surprise after reading some of the reviews. Loved the fish tacos and the mango cheese sause was the best I've ever had. So large a serving we took home leftovers for a full meal tomorrow. Our waiter did forget to put the bill on 2 checks as requested though.

We ordered dinner to take out tonight (4/26/14) Ordered egg rolls they were crispy & tasty. Entrees were red curry chicken which was very delicious and great flavors of south east Asia, Pork in garlic sauce, the pork was tender flavorful and sauce was tantalizing spicy garlic sauce which was excellent, then the orange beef was very tender & tasty with sweet & spicy orange sauce. What we really love is that you also have a choice of rice, from white, brown, or fried, the fried rice is amazing and the edamame in the fried rice is perfect. The food here is remarkable! 

We had a nice chat with Johnny, what a nice man. The service here at Oriental Pearl is outstanding all the staff are professional.  

We really enjoyed the crispy noodles & duck sauce :)

Thank you so much 

See you soon!

This is a small, yet busy place in Mid-City, New Orleans. It seems that their main thing is boiled seafood and po-boys, but we ordered Seafood Platters. We all agreed that the platters were large, perfectly fried, and nicely seasoned, but found that the tartar sauce had an odd citrus aspect (which could just be an unfamiliar style of it, to us). Sadly, the platter did not come with a green salad, but it did include a tasty potato salad. The fries, catfish, shrimp, and oysters were all good. I think we prefer the Metairie location, but we would recommend this one. RJT

Oh my the lines can get long, especially on a Saturday afternoon. The doughnuts are not as light and airy as you might think, they're a bit dense and have that fried dough mouth feel. The cremes and flavors used in these doughnuts are great though (especially the apple) - not too sweet and made with quality ingredients. Harvest apple is good. I wish the lemon filled ones were more tangy and lemony.

The Boat House might be deserving of a four, but if so, it is only because of its location, which is superb.  Right on the beach, great for a sunset time dinner.  The wine list is pretty solid.  Their seafood is not as good as you would expect from a place right on the ocean called the Boat House.  I had the seared mahi mahi; the flavor was decent but I didn't care for its texture.  I agree with the many posts saying less than complimentary things about the calimari.

Our waitress was very friendly but not very fast and she brought us the wrong check at the end of the meal, not that I was in a hurry.  All in all, it was a pleasant experience and I would think about returning if I ever have cause to be in Santa Barbara.

I was driving to the shore and stopped off at this Dunkin' for some breakfast.

I went inside, but there was a sign alerting customers that because of the worker shortage that they are drive through only. 

I ordered an everything bagel with cream cheese, strawberry frosted donut and a lemonade.

The donut was delicious, just like any other Dunkin' donut,  and so was my bagel. However, my lemonade was pretty terrible and lacked flavor. In fact, it was not even reminiscent of lemonade, too much.

The drive through was fairly long, but moved pretty quickly.

Altogether, this is your basic Dunkin' and you can't go wrong with it!

This review is mostly for the hot pot here. E-mei is a restaurant that I frequent all the time, possibly the one I go to the most when I eat out. I've gotten the normal Szechuan fare here, but usually I come here for hot pot.  This is the only place in Philly that I know that actually serves the cook-it-yourself hot pot and it is pretty yummy. One of my friends (who is extremely picky) raves about the soup bases - both the spicy and the non-spicy. We always get the yuan-yan (half- half). I would definitely recommend getting the fish and the pork balls for hot pot. The pork balls are different from the usual meatballs which are much denser. It is softer in texture and pretty tasty. They also give you a plate of free jew's ear, veggies, bean sprouts, pig's blood, pork balls, and some other stuff. 

The normal Szechuan food is pretty decent as well. This is definitely not a place for people who don't like spicy food.

My only quips about the place is that it is a bit overpriced. It's possible that my friends and I are just pigs, because our bill usually end up being $20 -25/person for hot pot. That is pretty expensive for hot pot considering doing hot pot at home would usually come to under $10/person. Of course, I wouldn't know how to replicate the soup base here. 

If you are can handle spicy food and enjoy hot pot, this is definitely worth checking out. It's a true Szechuan experience.

By far, one of the best chinese takeout place in Tucson. This restaurant, in my massively long search for the correct chicken with garlic sauce, was damn near perfect. I grew up next to the oldest China towns in the United States, therefore I am very picky about my Chinese takeout.

You get a lot of food for not a lot of money, but the service is not very good.  It took four times asking for sweet n low before someone brought me some.  Not sure why this is not just brought to you when they bring you  your coffee or why it's just not already on the table  like at most restaurants.
Without question the best pizza in the area. Friendly staff also. Just had the lasagna. Not bad. Not the greatest I've ever had but then again not bad. Cheesesteaks are great too.

The wait ended up being shorter than they estimated it would be, and the food was delicious again! Very friendly waitress, checked in on us multiple times to make sure everything was going well. I got one of their french toast things... apple something something? It was ridiculously good. Hash browns were great as well. I was planning to get a doughnut afterwards, but I was so satisfied just from the french toast that I didn't. But I'll be back to get a doughnut sometime in the near future!

This is not great pizza! I can't figure out why so many people like this . The atmosphere is good and the service is OK but the food is mediocre at best. It's not NY pizza! I was born and bred there, and this is not NY pizza. I can't recommend this food. There are better pies in the area. NYPie, joeys house of pizza, nicks Italian Deli, and pizza perfect on 21st.

We came for an early Sunday breakfast.
Trying to be a little more health conscious, I ordered the veggie omelette. It was good, and I liked the generous avocado, but I miss my bacon! 
Service was attentive and prompt.

After pouring through Yelp reviews of local Tucson restaurants I decided to take a business associate to The Parish. I always look for interesting local places that have good food and local beer. This place was hopping for a Tuesday evening but they fit us in. It was a great atmosphere with a friendly staff. We both enjoyed the Gumbo and an order of the hand cut fries.
The beer was good and the service was friendly. 
I definitely recommend this cool place to fellow travelers.

Okay- my husband and I went here for dinner with a gift certificate...WOW!  The place is wonderful.  Justin was our waiter and he was fabulous.  Really- super attentive without being annoying.  The food was outstanding.  My husband had a lamb dish that was out of this world.  I went for the bistecca that was truly the best steak I've ever had.  So happy to have tried this place and will DEFINITELY be back again.  Thank you!

I loved this place. As someone who gets chicken sandwiches at a lot of burger places, I can honestly say that bare burger has the best grilled chicken sandwich I've ever had. It has a lemon marinade and was delicious. I love that they have a create your own burger option where you choice your protein, bun, cheese, toppings, and sauces. There's a lot of options. 

The only reason I'm not giving this five stars is because the fries were just ok and the service was a bit slow.

Very cool place, great ambience, open feel with open patio but still good AC.  However bartender was more concerned with chitchat and wandering around than actual service.  I don't expect someone in 10 seconds, but it took 5 minutes for the bartender to even look our way. Then no knowledge of the guest taps/rotating beers... and after calling a server over to answer my questions she seemed overall disinterested in actually serving me anything. Very nice bathrooms, but oddly noisy.
Basically the hipster/millennial attitude of nonchalant service, although to be fair, pretty nice when actually engaged.  It's Monday night, I get it's the slowest night in restaurant world - just... try harder.

It was horrible, the chicken was dry, turkey was rubbery.  So disappointed, it was my boyfriend's birthday and wanted to have a special experience with the Preds tickets.  The only editable items were the desserts, delicious.

Whats to be said that hasn't been said? Never had anything from here that wasn't amazing and clearly made with a great deal of care and love. Always check out the monthly features but arrive early as lines can be terrible! Wish the location was bigger but one of the best places to eat in Edmonton hands down.
Not worth it food poor excuse rye bread for sandwich was white bread even when I called them on it chicken salad melt horrible French fries edible . Go somewhere else.

Update- I have been back at least 3 more times and with larger parties. Once, I called to let them know in advance that there was a party of 10 and if there were tables available. They spoke so fast and hung up at least twice that I wasn't sure at all if they heard me correctly. I gave up trying and just arrived to find out they already had tables ready. Food is still consistent every visit if not better.

Wow! So impressed!  Recently had Americas Pie catered our evening party and it was perfect in every way.  Working with Becky on the menu couldn't have gone any more smoother.  The food was outstanding and very impressive. From the charcuterie board to the filet on baguettes .... everything was so good! Every one of our guests asked who catered and also raved about the food all night.  We had Drew as our server/staff on site.  Very professional and fit right in with our company.  Highly rec AP for any catering needs. We will be using them in the future!

To anyone from Burlington NJ, the Prince Diner was a staple to your social life. Prices were cheap, and it was always a fun atmosphere, and the vast majority of people who went there loved it, and the staff. On the day it closed, the place was packed until the very end. Some of us even loved it so much we bought shirts off of some of the servers (mine is hanging up in my closet). 

After months of renovations, the Poseidon Diner emerged, which didn't last long at all, and now it is the Dolphin Diner. The place has cleaned up a bit. It looks more like a restaurant than a diner. There are TVs and flashy interior decorating everywhere- not what a New Jersey diner is supposed to be. 

The food is expensive for diner food, and the portions are smaller than usual. The quality of the food is nothing to write home about, but it IS a diner. I rarely leave not hungry. The servers don't go the extra mile, and half of them barely speak english- not that it's a bad thing, it's just hard to build a relationship with english speaking customers if your servers don't speak english. 

They have free WifFi, but I assume most people are in a diner to eat, not surf the web.

Long story short, I only go there if I have to, which is what I'd suggest to anyone else.

Staying overnight on Sand Key wanted a restaurant near the Sheraton. Saw Backwaters with a4.4 rating so gave them a try. NEVER Again We were seated after a wait to a table with no server. 10 minutes later a server appears to take our order. 
I had Mahi which was over cooked and DRY my husband had Pasta Margarita with shrimp and scallops. Lots of pasta. He later had an awful gastrointestinal event.
NO ONE from the door host, Manager, or servers
WORE MASKS or GLOVES!! The restaurant also appeared very full WAY over 50% occupied!!
Oh, yes the sea food (lobster) bisque was very good.

Have you ever had one of those places that you want to keep secret so it is just for you?  In your head, you think "If everyone finds out about this I will never be able to  get a table."  This is that place.  We went to to their unlimited brunch and every single dish was better than the last.  The Mexican Chocolate Waffles blew my mind, and the Biscuit & Gravy was a brilliant new take on a classic.  The $3 Mimosas helped wash everything down and we ate our fill.  This ain't your mama's breakfast taco...its a new mainstay in the crowded Broad Ripple food scene.
Bad experiensce for us. Limited food menu is way overpriced. Ignored by our waiter. The only thing we liked was the music. Never again!

I have been meaning to try La Calac for the longest time now, having lived a 10-minute walk away from it for almost 3 years now. Me and my girlies from work decided to take advantage of the happy hour. However, the prices for happy hour to me seemed a bit steep. $5 for margaritas and Sangrias I can live with but $5 dollar for a single taco I am not so sure about. Although $2 off draft beer was definite steal. 

The service seemed off. We felt forgotten because none of the staffs were ever in sight and not once we were checked up on. I never recieved a glass of water upon my arrival. Food was ok, but if the staff were a bit more attentive, I believe I would have enjoyed it way more.

We read the previous reviews and thought we would give a Franky D's a try. I had the meatball sandwich. It was very good. It would have been better if green peppers and onions were added or at least an option. I am sure I could have asked for them but I didn't think of it when I ordered. The French Fries were crispy and very good. I would have liked a side salad option instead and again, if I had thought of it in time I am sure it would have been no problem but the server didn't ask and it was not an option on the menu. Hubby had the Chicken Parmesan dinner. He said it was very good and the spaghetti was cooked to perfection. His meal came with a side salad and was crisp and fresh. He said the garlic bread was good as well. Lunch portions were a good size.  I know the owner reads these reviews so I am going to mention the one negative I have. There were multiple TV's on with a variety of sports stations which were fine but the TV in the middle had Fox News. In this very politically polarized environment, I would suggest owners keep to sports or the Weather Channel. It could otherwise cost you customers.

Omg! So, I've been here three times this month, including this evening. Nudoro makes the best ramen I've ever had. In fact, I've failed to even take a pic yet, cuz once I see it, I dig in and eat it too fast without even thinking of photos. I've tried a different variety every time - twice making my own, and once ordering the spicy tonkatsu but adding black garlic oil. I prefer making my own! Fun! The fried shallots and menma bamboo shoots are my fave toppings, of course along with the uber-tasty soft boiled egg! So good. I crave Nudoro now!
I love Ricks! I send all my pilots from work here foe food and atmosphere, and the waterfront view! Ricks is a family fave!

Absolutely amazing first time here! First of all, I would like to obsess over the ambiance of this place. Coming from the west side of the country, this beachy vibe is just what Nashville needs! We got there around a busy time but my boyfriend and I did not have to wait a minute for our table -- perfect spot for a chillax Golden hour dinner. 

Our server, Raven was very quick to accommodate us and explain the menu and happy hour menu. Surprised by how affordable this place is for how stunning it looks, I have always passed this place but always thought it would be costly. My boyfriend got the ahi poke, the portobello, pork belly and chicken pastor tacos. Let me just say that the Ahi Poke is absolutely wonderful. Coming from someone who just moved to Nash from Hawaii and growing up in authentic poke, their Ahi Poke is perfectly marinated and is very well complimented with avocados, cucumbers, and onions. I order the carne asada rice bowl and pork carnitas tacos. Although the rice bowl is far from an authentic Mexican carne asada plate, this dish is phenomenal and very filling. The brown rice that sits under the carne asada is very flavorful. 

Our server was fabulous and attentive with the service she has provided for us and Gray, the manager topped off our experience by swinging by to make sure we were having a pleasant experience. 

If this review has not prove itself enough, I am definitely looking forward to coming back again for another date night or even just a casual dinner with friends! Wonderful restaurant, spectacular food and servers! Mahalo

Sometimes at restaurants you may receive bad service, but at the Dennys on Hillsborough I received no service. My son and I were completely ignored. The waiter passed our table serval timed before even acknowledging us. He never once apologized for taking twenty minutes to take our drink order. Completely unprofessional. Not to mention how hot it is in here. Worst experience I've had in a long time.

Great food.  Decent wine.  So good, in fact I went twice in 1 day.  Once before shopping for lunch and again after 6 hours of shopping for dinner.  The shrimp and crab salad louis was amazing.  I could eat it every day.  Luckily my friend that was with me had recommended that I order double shrimp and crab since it normally comes with a very small portion of both.  I'm very glad I did.  And next time, not only with I order double shrimp and crab, but also double avocado.

There is a new Chinese restaurant in the Town Center Plaza that is giving it a go.  I believe it to be an independent restaurant, but has all the standard chain offerings that seem to be pretty popular in the area.  As part of a strip mall, there is plenty of free parking in the lot.  

Inside, they have done a complete makeover of the lobby and small shotgun style dining area.  Warm yellow walls, black and white flooring and wainscoting, and teal benches make for an inviting interior though it was kept rather dimly lit.

I decided to get my order to go and after placing my order and paying, grabbed one of the chairs in the lobby by the window.  I didn't see any wait staff, so I believe you are supposed to grab your own supplies from a counter where you pay if you are going to dine in.  Otherwise, you should have all the napkins, sauces, and plastic utensils inside your to go bag.

I was ordering for dinner, so I selected Egg Drop Soup (thick and yellow, but not much seasoning), crab rangoon (6 in an order and quite crisp with a sweet red sauce), and the peppered steak entree that comes with white rice.  The flavor was mild and okay, but the peppers were cut into too large of chunks to be bite sized and I wasn't supplied a plastic knife (which probably wouldn't have cut the peppers).   Fortunately, I was able to dump it out onto a plate at home and take care of it.  But if you were trying to eat directly from the little white box, you would have some challenge.  My wife sampled my dinner and thought that it was okay, but not anything special other than if you simply wanted a quick Chinese to go dinner.

I will say that the lunch specials are priced at only $5.50 and include fried rice and your choice of an egg roll or crab rangoon.   There are 25 lunch special options listed!

Anyway, the food was good, but nothing unique.  The service was efficient and easy to communicate with.  It's nice to have another option for dining in the area.

Review #2574

Hidden gem. Took me a minute to find it, I almost gave up, but really glad I didn't. The service at this establishment is top notch, Chuy himself was behind the bar serving but that did not stop him from holding the door for incoming/outgoing patrons and tending to the needs of the restaurant. 

The food was fresh and flavorful. 4 stars because I felt it was priced a bit high for Mexican food, however it was prepared well and the service left a memorable experience. Guacamole was delicious as was the skinny margarita. 

I love that they are dog friendly also!

This restaurant is a authentic amazing find! The owners are from Italy  We had the gnocchi sampler-Trittico di Gnocchi, Trio of homemade Gnocchi ( Sorrentina, Pesto and Gargonzola) we switched out the pesto for the Pistachio with no problems. We also ordered the Crudo e Rucola pizza, perfect wood fired crust, fresh prosciutto! Would highly recommend.

The food is poor, over priced and the service is horrible. You are better off going somewhere else than this place. I personally witnessed the servers harassing a customer that was totally uncalled for. Maybe they wanted to close earlier, I don't know but it was uncalled for.. Stay away!

Such a great meal. I ordered the pappardelle and the short ribs. Both were delicious! The short ribs came with a side of carrots, charred broccolini, horseradish au gratin potatoes, and a salad. The dressing on the salad was fantastic as were the rest of the sides. Don't forget to ask for bread and butter, simple yet WOW. I'd go back just for the bread alone. I am looking forward to tasting more. In addition, the service was fantastic!
Super fun place with great food but you have to time your visit carefully as it is very small. If the weather is good, there is outdoor seating...and when is the weather not good in Santa Barbara?

Giving this place 4 stars because the cocktails are yummy! Traditional prep, vintage glassware, well trained bar tenders. The place was decently busy for a Wednesday (looked like a crowd of locals which I like) and the seating options were diverse and comfy (couches, tables, and bar). The food though is NOT good. We should have taken note that no one else was eating (lol) but it was really bad. Bland, texture implied things were reheated, not super warm. Was very underwhelmed on that but will go back for drinks!
I got an iced coffee & an almond croissant. It is clean, and has a pleasant staff. I will be back!

Been a big fan since Blenders first started, never understood why anyone would consume a Jamba Juice. We had a JJ on State Street and Blenders easily put them out of business. If you want a delicious fruit based smoothie, this is the place to be. Every time I am back in town without fail, this is the first place I stop at especially for a fix of Berries Plus. This will be the first place I take out of towners before SB/Goleta orientation.

Host a variety of supplements which never taste powdery or leave a bad taste in your mouth (Jamba Juice). I get bee pollen and calcium.

97% of the time I will get the Berries Plus but everything else I've tried or tasted is also excellent. I do not like having bananas in my smoothies and Blenders provide plenty of alternatives. Soy is also a substitute for extra charge. Bring your own cup for extra discount.

The staff is always really friendly and working as quick as they can.
The only thing I'd slightly advise against are the random baked goods in saran wrap - they don't look very fresh. Have purchased on a few occasions and acceptable but you may want to purchase elsewhere. This place is about the drinks and they do a fantastic job on that. 

I've also purchased shots of wheatgrass for my parents.

just left this place - sent back both orders - Kristen was a great server - The guy cooking tonight was the drive up window guy working the griddle, according to her - he nuked my food twice, the poor cow that gave it's life remains are doing back flips in Alpo dog food cans as I type.this -  Probably would of been tastier.
This place needs a good sanitizing and retraining - My server was great - one other server literally laughed in our faces - send her to the curb.
Not a good experience at all.

This pizza is fantastic. I love a good cheese pizza and the cheese pizza here is stellar. Today they had a deal - large cheese pizza for $2.99. You really just can't beat that.  
I've previously tried a variety of their pizzas at an event and all were super tasty. Can't go wrong with pizzava!

Yume used to be our favorite sushi place but now that it has moved, Sushi Teri is our new go to place. It's cheaper and portions are good (they give more rice and generous slices of the fish as well). Will note that the eel and  mackerel were more fishier then Sushi 29 (We had just come from Sushi 29 (new yume) and wasn't satisfied-their rolls were costy for the amount given and we wanted a round 2)

We normally only order sashimi-so I can only recommend this place for sashimi and drinks as of right now.
Their Chicken Salad is absolutely incredible.  I seriously have cravings for it.  Love their potato, egg, and bacon salad and Greek bean soup, as well.  I am never disappointed!

While in college, I used have all you can eat sushi weekly since they were right by campus. As an experienced pro, I'm always up for trying new places. While up in Reno for the rib cook off, I thought I'd try this place since I heard good things about it. Plus, I wanted to see if my stomach still had the all you can eat magic that made it so famous in college. 

I'm pleased to report that my stomach is liking what I had here! It hit the spot for all you can eat sushi. I'll save you from the gory details of what I consumed and just tell you my favorites: Hawaii, Godzilla deluxe and Vegas. All the stuff I had was pretty good but these stood out in my mind. The service was also great. The waiter was super friendly and very attentive. He made sure the sushi kept flowing! Overall, I was very happy with my experience. Can't wait to come back!

I was pretty happy with our stay. I think if you travel with kids, this is a perfect choice for your stay. It is located across the beach, has a nice pool and healthy kid menu options. There is also a beach cafe across the street for breakfast with the view. It is a short drive to State street, the Zoo is just around the corner and playground at the beach. Overall, I would come back.

It takes everything inside of me not to eat her once a week. Everything on the menu is amazing but my go to is the spicy basil fried rice w/ tofu and a fried egg on top and the yellow curry. I can't say it enough but the staff and service is always exceptional.

Went here on 8/4 to get food and drinks for my kids. Ordered 4 freezes and was told that they weren't able to do more than one of each flavor because the machine freezes up. Weird, because we order multiples of the same flavor all the time.  Got to the window and the cups werent even 1/2 full of the freezes. Kyle, the "manager" ran my card for full price, i asked him why the freezes  Weren't discounted because of the fact that they weren't full, let alone the flavors my kids wanted. Kyle got a very unprofessional attitude with me and told me "what do you expect you go to fast food you get what you pay for".  I just paid $16 for for freezes and they're not even 1/2 full. He proceeded to tell me that I'm delusional and that HE himself IS reality and basically talked trash to me trying to start a fight with me, a 42 year old mom in a minivan. 
 I told him to cancel the order and refund my money. He told me he needed my card back, and I should have known better than to give it to him. Instead of doing a refund at the cash register, a he took my card in the back room for 8 minutes while  another team member proceeded to unwrap straws and drink the freezes meant for my kids standing in the window staring at us. 
 I then went across the street to the gas station to buy ice cream for my kids so they could still have their treat. When I went to the cash register my card was declined. I ran it 3 times. Not only did Kyle not refund my card but he somehow messed up my bank account and canceled my card. I will be talking to the police and corporate to try to get this resolved because not only was he rude and unprofessional but he has now messed up my bank account.
Great Bakery, been going there for over 15 yrs.  Definitely  worth checking it out !!  Their sticky buns are awsum, as well as their danishes.

I work in restaurants, so I am not always willing to go grab a bite to eat between shifts, but Sasha's not only serves food all afternoon (am I the only one who eats lunch at 3pm?!), but they do everything well. The staff is helpful with selections and quick to chat, their wines are extensive and they are well versed in what they are serving, and the food is great. Not too heavy and some unique items are perfect. I would not go their if I was starving for a burger, but some wine and snacks and Sasha's is worth the price.

I arrive at Biscuit Love to a small line of about 20-25 people or so. The line moved very quickly. I was in line maybe 10-12 minutes outside and then another 5-7min once I got inside. 
This place does not have waitress service, you order and pay for your food when you first get in there and then find your seat. Someone brings you your food and that's it. 
I honestly believe the hype was overrated but I truly didn't know what to expect. Everyone I talked to just said make sure I stop by there so I did. I ordered the East Nasty no gravy and add an egg. The chicken thigh that comes on that sand which is huge and actually takes away from the biscuit. It was to enjoy the sandwich because There was so much chicken. They should definitely use a smaller piece of chicken. 

We also ordered the bonuts which were really good. They were fried biscuits dipped in sugar with icing on top and sitting on a plate with blueberries.

Went on over, down the block, to eat. Called. Confirmed BYOB.

Arrived. Ordered just one main entree and a shared plate. Got the Moroccan tea.

This place has good flavors and allows you to order a la carte: a rarity for Moroccan places.

The owner tells me her family is from Tangier.

Keep this place alive so you don't have to go to places that force one menu down your throat and are run my non-Moroccans.

In case you like prix fixe, they do that too.
This place is the real deal!  A lot more family dining atmosphere than other places.  Al la carte taco prices are pretty good too!

It takes a lot for me to care enough to give any eatery any review let alone a  5 star review but Marjie's   Grill absolutely deserves it.
Everything from the kitchen was a delightful adventure in taste; a gustatory symphony of harmony and contrasts that is rarely encountered anywhere. These guys truly understand how to take what might at first seem mundane food and create something so sublime that presentation seems unimportant.
I dare say the food is so good I would eat there even it was located in dumpster. What's better is it's not. A real funky atmosphere and friendly staff make this place tops in my book. I will return here every time I am in NOLA.
Forget all the 'famous' kitchens and chefs in this town and eat at Marjie's.

I have mixed feelings about this place. Out of the appetizer, main course, and drinks only one was really good and the others were ok.

Drinks- I ordered the prickly pear and it was great tasting but very weak. Normally after 1 drink I feel something and was expecting it to be stronger for a 12-15 dollar drink.

Appetizer- decided to go basic and order the guacamole. It was more smoothy than guacamole. The chips are also very salty but I did like that they seemed made in house.

Main course- this is where this place redeemed itself. The pork belly tacos were really good. I also tried the chicken and that was delicious. These tacos are better than Bakersfield but Bakersfield has better drinks and apps.

If you want the best fancy tacos this place is it. If you want strong drinks and good appetizers you can go elsewhere. The environment is very touristy but it is a good place if you have large groups. Be prepared the wait times are ridiculous. 1-2 hours.

The place looks great and the food is really good.  However, the management and service is lacking.  I know they're new and we were a table of 10, but they really should have been more prepared to whip up more than one dish at a time before opening their doors.  It took longer than an hour and a half for us to get our food.  Instead of apologizing or explaining that we'd have to wait due to [insert reason/excuse here] , they just tried to avoid our table and then lied to us saying the food was coming right out.  30 minutes later, they're only able to produce 2 plates with the rest of the plates dribbling out for the next 30 minutes.  Luckily we were feeling fine from the wine but they really need step it up a hertz or 10.

This taco bell honestly has the best employees I have had the pleasure of dealing with. They are always very pleasant and friendly. If you wait any more than needed they always apologize and make it right somehow. Now and days its harder and harder to find people who actually take customer service seriously, and they do. It maybe only a Taco Bell, but with there service I had to put a review down. Keep.it up guys!
So disappointed, went for the Sunday Brunch- should of went to Hardee's or better Cracker Barrel- $15 per plate

A definite favorite of ours for breakfast.  The portions are large and everything is delicious!  One of my favorites is the omelet with crabmeat, spinach and cheese.  So yummy and way too much to finish. If you enjoy scrapple, they do a great job with that too - according to my husband - it's crispy and delicious.  My only complaint is that the coffee is not good - much too weak for my taste.  Service is good- very friendly and helpful.

I have only been there twice, both time sitting at the bar.  We got the nachos with chicken and jalapeños which we ate at the bar.  They LOADED the chicken on!  I got the Mexican steak (TO GO) for dinner which was delicious.  For drinks, I got the jalapeño guava margarita which was YUMMY!!!!!  The "to go" containers are great, perfect for the main entree, a side of black bean puree and Mexican rice.  

Next time I got the barbacoa tacos, and tried the guac and salsa.  Chips are definitely homemade, as was the guacamole and salsa.  SPICY and DELICIOUS!!  Happy that this place is so close to me.  It will definitely be a place I frequent again and again.  

The only reason I gave it 4 stars is b/c I haven't had a chance for a sit-down dinner, so can only speak to the bar service, which was perfect!
Got sandwiches to go for a meeting w coworkers...Godfathers and pressed cubans...lots of meat and good seasonings...its Boars Head so good quality...good size for the price!

Generally excellent food however this morning I found the chocolate chip pancakes to be mediocre at best. The mediocrity coupled with a lack of butter to use on the pancakes prompted me to write about it.

Some of the best food in St. Louis. Tonight was my second time in. We had a lobster roll, trout, asparagus, fries and apple tart--all were superb. We had my 2-year-old with us, and they were friendly and accommodating. I love nice restaurants that are kid friendly.

I like this spot for the beer and convenience to my apartment.  I could take or leave the food.

If you go during brunch or on a weekend night, expect it to be packed.  I love the addition of the upstairs, which allows for more wiggle room when trying to get to the bar.  

Their beer selection is awesome - lots of craft beers, which I appreciate, especially since Philly has made me somewhat of a beer snob (I cringe when my Ohio friends order Miller Lite's).  

I've eaten here a few times and while the food is good, it doesn't stand out as something you can't get anywhere else.  Then again, I've never been for brunch, which is supposedly the meal everyone raves about here, so I'll have to try it one of these weekends when the weather gets bearable enough to stand outside and wait!

It is lovely, absolutely wonderful. Did you step into a time warp that you feel both respectful and awed by? Absolutely. The amazing plaster walls, hundreds of years old, stretching 18 ft to the ceiling all yellowed and patched with oil paintings strung everywhere. The worn floors, the ancient bar. The wait staff spinning stories true or false of the history. Ambiance does not even begin to explain this little bar. We stayed, had a few Pimms and marveled over the history all around us.

Arriving at an unassuming corner on South St, my boyfriend and I found the way to our early Valentine's Day reservation at Serpico. We were greeted by friendly hosts and were able to be seated quickly at the chef's counter. 

Our server for the night was a perfect balance of friendly, helpful and prompt. I tend to ask a lot of questions (yanno, just to make sure I'm making the right decision!) and he was very patient. I ended up choosing the Gin cocktail with a strong, fresh ginger syrup. My boyfriend got the Rye, which he has announced as his new favorite cocktail in the city. He proceeded to have three. 

After reviewing the menu and munching on our complimentary sesame rice paper with edamame hummus, we opted for a few small and medium plates rather than the larger entrees. Starting with appetizers, the raw hamachi and mushroom tartare. The raw fish was a immaculately balanced dish with the perfect ratio of sweetness from the fish, acidity from the citrus, a hint of spiciness, and umami from nori strips on top. 

The mushroom tartare was not what I was expecting at all. The mushrooms were dried out and served with an intensely smoky seaweed powder and a soft poached egg. The flavors blew my boyfriend's socks off. If I was looking for a small complaint, it would be that the egg was cooked just one touch more so that the white was a liiiiitle more done. 

Next, we had the deep-fried duck buns and king crab ramen. These were definitely my two favorite dishes of the night. The flavors were intense and rich and buttery. The duck leg was cooked to perfection: crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. They were served on soft potato buns with fresh pickled vegetables and sriracha. Imagine if peking duck and Shake Shack and banh mi were all infused into one perfect little sandwich. This. Is. It. 

The king crab ramen is a dry ramen (not soup) in a butter old bay sauce. The crab is served in large chunks and the old bay and chili gives it the perfect simple kick. We both fell in love with this dish. 

We saw the Specials board and couldn't resist trying one. Since we both love lamb and it was served with greek yogurt and eggplant, we chose this one. Unfortunately it was not what we expected. The sweet hoisin-tasting glaze was a little much for us, especially on top of the fatty cut that was served. The natural flavor of the meat couldn't shine through. The greek yogurt sauce was also a curd-like consistency, not smooth. A little disappointed on the way the meal ended, we opted for another round of drinks we knew we'd like rather than dessert. 

My boyfriend described this meal as "wanting to have a little more of everything after the plate was clean," especially his favorites: the mushroom tartare and crab ramen. While the price tag was high, we felt it was definitely worth the experience because it's truly innovative food that you can't find anywhere else in the city. Though, stick to tried-and-true items on the menu that do change every now and then (seasonal vegetables, pastas, etc.) and skip the experimental specials that they're currently innovating on.
Wow. Pastrami reuben was phenomenal. Melt in your mouth quality. Just delicious. So much delicious sandwich. Find them at the Reading Terminal Market!

I've been here few times now and have been to their other branches many times in the past years as well.
I would say, compared to the Aman standards, this location falls right in the MIDDLE.
Again, this is in comparison to other Aman locations in the area.
Decor and food much better than the Norristown site.
But, we are die hard fan of the one in chalfont, PA - for the decor/taste/serivce.

The service here could use a little improvement compared to the chalfont location.

Overall, a great place for indian food near the Berks area.
First time in and I will definitely be back. It's clean appearance and colorful chalkboard menus was very appealing. The food was good and reasonably priced.

Ramen Ray YAYs:
-The staff at is cordial and friendly.  I had my dogs out in the car on a rather frigid day, and when I asked for my take-out to be brought out to my car so I be with my pups, the staff said yes without hesitation.  I was thankful for their kindness.
-The half portion option allows you to eat "in moderation" or--on the other side of the coin--try multiple ramen bowls.
-Ramen Ray has partnered with Grub Hub for delivery, so you don't even have to leave your house.
-The pork-based miso broth is RICH - this would be the one I'd get again and again.

Ramen Ray NAY:
-The vegetarian broth is quite dull in comparison to the miso broth.  I was pretty disappointed, as it reminded me of watered down soy sauce.  Therefore, I don't think I'll be setting a lunch date with my meatless friends here.

The miso broth ultimately saved the day on this review - puh-lease don't take it off the menu!
Usually go to Central Grocery then we found ourselves on the other side of the river. Saw Dimartino's and tried them last night for dinner. AMAZING! The Italian salad and muffuletta were perfect.

I tried the cuban sandwich when they came to Tampa General Hospital. They won best cuban sandwich in Tampa, but honestly i don't know how they did. The sandwich was good but it wasn't great. I gotta stick to Larrys Deli in Land O Lakes for having the best cuban sandwich.

I tried to try it again but when i went to the truck they ran out of cuban bread. I was craving a cuban that day but it is what it is. Overall i think they are hard workers and would go again.

This qdoba is very inconsistent when I visit. I always order the same meal, chicken nachos. Sometimes they add rice and beans, sometimes they just put queso and chicken. The portion size of the meal depends on who's working. I went in this evening a whole hour before the store closed and they treated me as if I had walked in 1 minute before they closed. My meal came cold and there was little to no customer service. I love qdoba food, but this location makes me want to stay away.

Improved flow with high-tops added and table service all the way. MidiCi does not need to be as complicated as it was at first. 

I just got a Margherita pizza with half pepperoni and      it was both light and filling. Flavorful; a hint of char. A Coke. 

There is more to had here, for sure. But, it can be simple and very satisfying.

Summary:  over 2 hours and several phone calls for a pizza to be delivered.

Ordered a pizza and some fried mozzarella.  The initial delivery window when we ordered was 45-55 minutes which is reasonable for a Friday night.   After the order was submitted it was bumped up to 1:25-1:35 minutes.  At 1:35 minutes I called the place, asked for an order update and was told ours was the next to go out.   30 minutes later... still no pizza... called again.  I was told the driver was almost to our house.... 15 minutes later, 2 hours and 15 minutes after ordering....after I would normally be in bed...the pizza finally came.   It was a pretty decent pizza, but I don't think we will be ordering from here again.

Great bar with a great history, beers are cheap and so is the liquor, place just could use a little clean up along with some air freshener.  I really enjoyed the few beers that we had there and the company of the bartender and would definitely return if we were in the area looking for a few drinks.

Had a 3:30pm reservation for a specific table (we were a party of 9). We were seated just before 4:30pm. Apparently, a group was seated at the table for over 4 hours. Policy prevented asking them if they would like to continue their conversation in the bar area. They were no longer eating or ordering drinks.  Risotto came out cold and undercooked. Service was slow. Some food items never arrived. Overall, we were disappointed. We've eaten here before and had no issues.

My husband and I went on a weekend getaway to Tampa from Ft. Lauderdale. We have been wanting to check out Steelbach for brunch for quite some time. We went there for brunch today - and what a disappointment. The hostess & waitress were both unfriendly. We told the waitress it was our first time dining there and she had to response for that. lol we thought she'd make recommendations or let us know what's popular. After taking our orders and giving our food (with a missing item), the waitress never came back to check to see if everything was ok. We had to call her over to tell her the eggs from our order was missing.. so that took another 15 min to come (while the other food that was supposed to be eaten with the eggs got cold). The waitress never apologized for the situation, all she said was they forgot it. She never came back to check in on us throughout our entire meal. We had to call her over again to ask for coffee refill.... and even after requesting it twice, she never refilled the coffee. Anyways, huge disappointment. Would never go back due to service at the location. Management needs to do a better job training their staff.

We have dined at Guadalajara grill on East Prince many , many times. Paul, Margarita and the staff have been phenomenal. We moved NW recently and decided to try Guadalajara in N Oracle Rd. 
What a mistake. In entering the restaurant we obviously interrupted the hostesses day. When she looked up and finally acknowledged my wife and I, it was with a look of "your bothering me." We asked for a booth at the bar( there were two or three empty)and she studied the map for 10 seconds , sighed and said follow me. She seated us at the outside door where servers were going in and out ( it was cold). I asked for another booth and here comes that look again. What a pleasant lady. The server thankfully chimes in and said "open seating at the bar sit where you would like." We found one of the three empty booths.  Food was not quite up to Prince road but the Margaritas were perfect. Not enough to bring us back.

Bella's was ok... the service I had was not too good, but I didn't come for the service! It was all about the food.
 
The place is definitely nice, a little dated but ‍ 

Anyway I got the... you know what I can't even remember what I got! That goes to show you how good it was. It was alright but there's definitely better places for Italian. I'll go back but it would be because I get invited.

Had Farm Burger for lunch today with the wife. My number #1 Farm Burger and bucket of fries was very tasty. I enjoyed it and it filled me up. The wife had the salad with chicken, which was a patty of some sorts. She said it was good, but will get a bun less burger next time. 

The price was a little expensive for what we ate I believe, but so is everything else these days. We liked the restaurant and we will return. I think the only reason I didn't give it a 5 was due to the menu was hard to read for me. May just be because I am old and can't see worth a crap any longer, but other than that thumbs up to Farm Burger and the staff. Go visit soon.
I love the design of the restaurant, I think it is stylized beautifully. The food was great for a group of girls looking for a hearty breakfast after a night on the town! Yummy drinks. Great spot!
