I'd take my business elsewhere. Their servers and  bartenders truly lack what the service industry is about, what a shame.

Great place for breakfast super cute girl works the counter on third shift. ;)

Love ma Waffle House!
Shrimp & Grits. Oily, 3 green pepper slices and just an overall bland taste. No flavor what so ever. Won't be back
i do like the breakfast. go between 8am-?. before that it is iffy. i really like the banana pancakes and the spinach feta omlette.

What a bummer. We used to love this place but not so much lately. The service was ok. We were greeted, seated and brought our drinks. My spouse and I ordered burgers. He had the Whisky River and I got a cheeseburger. We were asked if we would like them pink. I said no and my husband said maybe a little. Our food came out in a timely manner. The fries were cold though. Which sucked because that was the only part I was able to eat. My burger was raw and covered in relish. Not sure when they added relish but the last time I had a burger there it was not an included condiment. The burger was just nasty. Our waitress never checked on us or I would have sent it back. When she brought the check she asked if I wanted a box.... I explained what was wrong and she offered to have another one cooked for me. Too late, we had other places to be.  She should have taken it off our bill but she lamely walked away when I declined an offer of another burger. Oh well. If you like loud, overcrowded crappy restaurants with poorly cooked food, this is the place for you!

Mussels, mussels, mussels!! My favorite mussels in town. The service is a bit slow, but almost everything on their menu is worth the wait. Don't expect to dine with a large party, they can't accommodate it. However, this place is a perfect date night. I love that they added the outdoor bar that offers live music, but again, expect pretty slow service. We go back regularly just for the food, but know what to expect.
Food has no taste.  The chicken tastes like it was boiled.  Would rather eat at Fresh Kitchen.

It's nice to have vegan pho options that taste great but this place was a bit awkward. It's a great concept but it's perhaps trying too hard. It's great that pho came to the neighborhood, but let's keep pho pho, back to washington ave we go! 

Pho at $9 is a bit absurd, especially when I can get two large bowls for $11 on Washington. 

If you are a strict vegan or veggie and want pho, this place would work well for you!

I've been here twice and I have to say that the experiences were night and day. My advice to you would be to only come here during a very down time, not a lunch or dinner rush time and not on a weekend.

The place is extremely small, with I think perhaps four tables that seat around four people each. There is a very small kitchen with one chef working, and one person working the register/phone/tables.

The last time I came it was me and a friend, just after they opened up and on a weekday. This was around a year ago. The burgers and fries were pretty good, and everything was done in a reasonable about of time.

I came in on 1-26-19, a Saturday, at about 12 PM - lunch time. Only one table was free so I was seated there. Then it took my server over 15 minutes to actually take my order. She was so caught up with getting other orders out, phoned-in take-out orders and such. Once she finally took my order, it was literally another 30 minutes before my food came to me. My food being one hamburger.

Meanwhile numerous other people showed up, hoping to be seated but having nowhere to sit, putting in to-go orders and so forth. Once I did get my burger - the "cyclops" (basically a burger with a friend egg and garlic mayo) - it was nothing to write home about. Certainly it wasn't even close to being worth $9.25, especially with the unreasonable wait.

Add to that an underwhelming bottled tea by Joe's Teas (they ONLY offer bottled beverages) brought my total to $12.96 plus tip. For an underwhelming burger that took a total of 45 minutes to get from the kitchen to me, that's just not excusable.

I hear that the place has changed ownership since my first visit to my recent visit, and that may be the culprit for the downslide, but I also think they are just simply not equipped with the space or staff necessary to handle the volume in a timely fashion. Coupled with the overpricing, I can't suggest you bother trying this place.

UCBC is the new big boy in town and is incredibly hyped. I am not saying the beer is bad, I am just saying that I think they sold out a bit. The set up is really big. The beer hall is massive. But I believe that has created a problem for UCBC. It is incredibly loud in there. Almost to the point that one either struggles to have a conversation or is required to shout. This on a day where the place was only about 1/4 full. I am more partial to the smaller breweries in town that are still growing up. That said, UCBC's growth is welcomed and has certainly brought a solid footprint to the Grove neighborhood. I want it to do well. And it seems to be. The lady that got my beers kind of rubbed me the wrong way like she had better things to do. When I ordered, I asked for my tab to be closed out. I had to ask two more times before I got my card back. This on a sunday afternoon when the place was not terribly crowded.

This used to be one of my favorite restaurants but,due to the occurrence of new staff members this restaurant's rating has definitely gone down ,the staff isn't the friendly inviting, lovely people that used to work there ....they seem to be replaced with exhausted and angry staff which makes for a pretty unpleasant dining experience. The food is still consistently good but , it's served with a sneer. I will be giving back my duchess crown.
Good ol' deep dish pizza delivered quickly to our door. Just what we were hungering for

I popped in the day before Thanksgiving for the first time and had a wonderful experience. This was absolutely the type of restaurant/bar the CWE was previously lacking. I'll dub it classy sports bar. 

LOTS of TVs on the walls and individual TVs at the bar top tables. Diverse menu (limited for vegetarians, but still options). Good beer options on tap. We had great service when we were there. 

I know this place gets really crowded on game days, but I'll absolutely try and return.

What a gem! Honey's is a Philly staple - I've been several times for breakfast and never had anything bad. The 'Enfrijoladas' are amazing, so flavorful and fresh. They focus on using local and green products as much as possible, which is awesome. They are generally very busy for breakfast, especially on the weekends, but it's worth the wait!

It's been a long time since we have been here. It is still very good.  We enjoyed our food. The staff was nice. Glad we decided to stop by.

If you have not tried it you have not lived.

Food was very subpar, probably won't come back I only walked in here cause ciccio Cali next store was closed. My whole breakfast skillet was cold and when I asked the waiter if it was a substantial amount of ham in the skillet he said yes. I guess 1oz of ham is a lot to him. With good places to eat like boca and ciccio this place may last just because of the residual business but def not a good place If you want good food.

Classy, intimate , great location because it's not too touristy and the food is delicious. 

They have a very small menu. But the selections are not bad. Tonight was full house. Service is good. Parking is street parking. Definitely recommend this place for when you're on a date.
Pizza and house salad dressing are both delicious! Service was fantastic too, my drink was never empty!
Food was great!  Had the dry ribs, mac and cheese and the baked beans.  Everything was tender and not over cooked.  Staff were friendly and helpful.

I had read a lot about this place and decided to give it a whirl! First of all, valet parking is a bargain, unless you want to keep circling the block to find a space. Or you can use the parking garage half a block away. I liked the interior décor. It is very nice and eclectic and does not interfere with your meal. My wife had the panzanella salad, which is a mixture of various tomatoes and bread. It was very pretty and very tasty! I had the mixed greens with green apples and spiced pecans. Very nice, but could have used a bit more dressing. For entree's, she had sides of mac-n-cheese, spinach, and garlic potatoes. The mac was very cheesy and had a nice velvety sauce with cracker topping. The spinach seemed flash fried and very good! It had golden raisins and bits of green apple. Very Mid-Eastern! The potatoes were fluffy, but average.

I had the vege lasagna! This was not only beautiful, but quite flavorful! They must have taken a lot of time to make each lasagna by hand. Save room for dessert which is worth waiting for! Wife had chocolate pate'. A very artistic presentation that you don't even want to mess up. It seems that there is not very much you can do differently with the taste of chocolate pate' though. I had the famous banana cream pie! It is extremely good, even though I had the graham cracker crust and not the peanut butter cookie crust. I really enjoyed the caramelized sugar on the bananas!

Travis, the waiter, was attentive without being obnoxious. We had a very nice time!

Everything was delicious. It's a quaint little place with charm and old world. The shrimp app was good but the bean cake with it was kind of bland.

The lamb was oh my goodness delicious.

Chocolate crepes are also good if you like dense chocolate. I just wish you could order the number you want since I was dining alone.
I like this place for Pizza and sub sandwiches. It is family owned and been here for quite a long time. They are casual and consistent. You can get your food to go or dine in.

Love this place, great down home service/food/People; only wish is that it was a 24 hr dive...
But, unfortunately those days are mostly gone w/the lunatics free among Our Society...
One of my fav spots anyhow...
Mac

Love everything about this bar except the service. Sat at the bar on a slow Monday night for football and was constantly overlooked. Wasn't checked on or asked if I needed another drink when mine was empty. Instead, I had to flag down the bartender and  they made me feel like that was somehow an inconvenience to them. Will be back but hoping for a more attentive staff.

Tuesday May 6th was National Teacher Day.  If you remember it was advertised on TV and radio stations in Tucson that McDonald's would give teachers a free extra value meal. Teachers only needed to provide an ID OR a paystub.  
 I decided to stop at my neighborhood Mc Donald's at Cortaro Road and I-10. I have been a customer at this McDonalds' for 21 years.  When I arrived at McDonalds' I was greeted by a very pleasant young man behind the cash register.  I placed my order and told him that I am a teacher. The smile on his face grew, he thanked me for being a teacher.  The young man called the manager for the promo code.  I handed the manager my district issued ID.  This is the ID I am required to wear at school, and present at other schools and district functions.  My ID is issued once by my district and is not reissued unless it is lost or stolen.  The manager looked at my ID and told me it was too old, it was issued to me in 1999.  I have been a teacher for 25 years.  Prior to 1999 my school district did not issue teacher IDs. 
He asked me if I had a paystub.  My paystubs are issued electronically, I do not print them.  Frankly, the advertisement was ID OR paystub.  Since I had the proper ID I didn't think I needed my paystub. At this moment the manager of my neighborhood McDonald's, at Cortaro Road and I-10, became the authority, with detailed knowledge of the policies, procedures, and inner workings of the school district by which I am employed.  According to the manager I should have an email with my paystub attached to it.  My district does not issue paystubs via email.   The manager said to me "you have to understand that when we did this last year a lot of people said they were teachers and took advantage."  I was completely humiliated and embarrassed by the manager of the neighborhood McDonald's, I have been doing business for the last 21 years. The McDonald's located at Cortaro Road and I-10.  I politely said thank you and left the restaurant. 
I immediately called the corporate offices of McDonald's and filed a complaint. McDonald's corporation has not responded to me.  I called Gray Management the franchise owner of the McDonald's at Cortaro Road and I-10, I left a voice mail. I was contacted again by the manager of my neighborhood McDonalds. During our conversation he was arrogant, condescending, and unapologetic.  The conversation added insult to injury.   He told me, "You need to understand that this is a security breach." He followed that statement with, "You are the only teacher we had a problem with."  Perhaps I am the only teacher whose ID he so closely scrutinized.   I would like to add that I spoke with two colleagues who stopped at the same McDonalds, used their district issued ID that is as old as mine.  They were not interrogated and not have a problem.  I told the manager I wanted to speak with Gray Management, franchise owner of the McDonalds at Cortaro Road and I-10.  The franchise owner has not returned my calls.  
This is not about a $3 dollar sandwich and a cup of orange juice.  This is about the customer service I received at my neighborhood McDonalds. The one I have stopped at for late night snacks, quick meals on the way to work and activities, or just because my children wanted a treat or happy meal.  I have been a loyal customer at the Cortaro Road and I-10 McDonald's for 21 years.   
As a teacher I have served students and families in Tucson and the state of Arizona for 25 years. I was embarrassed and humiliated by the manager of McDonald's on a day when members of my profession were to be celebrated. Sadly, I'm not, "Lovin it."

Great burgers and great prices. Always always crowded. Not enough sitting room inside. The brown tissue paper they use to wrap the burger (goes on before the white wrapper) I think is unnecessary because it blends in with the bun and gets eaten! 
Very clean and friendly atmosphere.

We had an amazing dinner here. I highly recommend getting the gigantic martini shaker to share with friends. The Lobster Mac N Cheese was divine. 
We were so happy we went the next day for brunch. Not so much of a brunch scene. Sort of bright and the food was solid but not amazing.

One our way home we needed to stop and get dinner.  So we looked on yelp and Johnny Grits came up as one of the closest places the menu looked good so we said why not, and boy ate we glad we stopped.  They had thier fish & chips on special buy one for $10.95 get the second one for half price. We also wanted to try a Grits skillet with caramelized onions, andouille sausage, & provolone cheese. Everything was great the fish was REAL grouper and the breading was so lite and crispy. The Flys were crisp and very tasty, and the Grits such a combo of flavors. We will be back and will bring friends.  Give the place a chance. They lost one star because of bad parking.
My second time there this week food was very good again the clams was very good.  Will be back soon thanks again for a grate meal

Great little spot in a sleepy town. Seems a bit overpriced for the location but the food was stellar. Crust and toppings were delicious and the garlic knots were great. Don't confuse it with the upscale Italian restaurant of e same name just down the block. We spent $80 for 2 pizzas and garlic knots. Not what I had in mind so be careful. Prices on the menu in Yelp are incorrect.

My s/o and I love going here for any celebration! We always get the steamed mussels and we rotate between the sea scallops and the wood fired mushrooms. The service we've had has been exceptional-- once our waitress remembered what we were celebrating and greeted us at the table with a glass of our favorite sparkling drink. I feel like the staff really knows me and does a great job of customizing my experience so I keep coming back for future celebrations. 10/10 would recommend Union 50 if you're new to Indy or trying to venture out of your comfort zone!

I read previous reviews and found the negatives ones to be interesting because I decided to try the place for myself.  This place rocks, the food is fantastic, the wine is very good and the service is top notch.  Bridgette, the owner, seated and greeted us.  She check up on us several times and provided great care.  The veal and pasta dishes were perhaps better than the hill without the journey.  The salad was tasty as well.  This is not expensive for the quality and portions served.  A surprising find in Westport plaza.  Go here and judge for yourself

I've come here many times for happy hour since my first time (Sept 2014) and more often than not, the place is under-staffed. Tonight, we came with a large party during happy hour. Long story short, it took us ~1.5 hr from the time we walked into the restaurant to the time we got our food and drinks. And the food was cold when we got it, but we were so hungry we couldn't care. Also we had to sit outdoors because they had no space inside and none of the heat lamps were working. None of us were pleased with Pasco tonight.

The wait staff kept apologizing, which I appreciate. But it would be better if they staffed their happy hours to match with the demand of the place. I will be coming here more sparingly in the future, especially with large groups.
Been here twice. Would say some dishes are very good. Some are good. Slightly overpriced but nothing out of Wayne Normal. The goat has been very good.

Great place, great food, and awesome service! We go in regularly on Saturday's for dinner and the hear the live band.(we are going tonight) We have a a favorite server/waitress named Briauna that we request to have. She always takes care of us and we always leave satisfied! We have tried multiple things off of the menu and have yet to find one thing we did not like. We love the new look, the food, and the service! A definite "must go" and if she's there ask for our favorite server/waitress Brianna! Also, we really enjoy the brunch that they have over the weekend. My wife loves the "omelette station" that they have but my favorite is the "biscuits and gravy"!

We were in town for the weekend. Walked over from the hotel and into the bar. Best happy hour menu I have experienced in a long time. Fresh sushi, kimchi rice, brussel sprouts, several drinks all for under $60.00 Great staff, and excellent food. We ended up eating there both Friday and Saturday.
Usually when I go to this Starbucks they never get my drink right, but yesterday when I went there they were so much better then normal!!
This is by far one of our favorite spots! True authentic Mexican flavor with every dish that they offer. There agua frescas are DELICIOUS!!!!!

Oh my do I LOVE Silvergreens! There are so many wonderful attributes to this restaurant that go beyond the food, that I'll start with them and then work my way to the taste buds. 

First, it's a great location. I haven't had much trouble with parking and I love the layout of the dining room. Plenty of tables and seats to accommodate their numerous clientele. 

Customer service is fantastic! The staff is super friendly and very knowledgeable about the menu. 

Another detail I love as a health conscious customer, is that the nutrition facts for your specific order are printed right their on your receipt so you know exactly what you are consuming. For example, I ordered my dressing on the side and my receipt reflected that. My salad was only 200 calories without the dressing! 

For the food, I had a grilled shrimp salad that was to die for. So flavorful! Ripe avocado, goat cheese, slivered almonds, mango and a mango dressing that was wonderful (and I used it sparingly). The salad was large and very filling considering how few calories I was consuming. 

I can't wait to try more of their healthy creations!

This place has a couple things going for it:
1. Great atmosphere with cool lighting and dynamic seating options
2. Super friendly and attentive staff
3. A good price point for cocktails ($8) and wine ($7-$12) compared to other places on Mass Ave.

They have a pretty thorough wine menu and special limited time options on the chalk board.  It also looks like they will be having happy hour specials some days of the week, which I'm all about! 

We ordered lobster poutine and gooey Louie burger to split, along with a couple glasses of wine during our visit.  The gooey Louie is pretty good.  It has a nice flavor and it pretty unique.  I was disappointed in the lobster poutine though.  It is in a creamy sauce that makes the fries soggy and it lacks much flavor.  I wouldn't get it again.  

Overall I was disappointed in the food, which is why Louie's Wine Dive only gets 3 stars from me. I'd go back for after work drinks!

Our favorite burger and wine spot in town!  Alex was at the bar and his recommendations have never failed us.  This was the first time we ordered a shake with him as we were deciding between that and wine for a drink, and he mentioned the ability to make it an "adult" shake with rum - we were not disappointed!  The Santa Fe burger special for the month was amazing!

Legacy of Heidelberg Haus lives on throughout the generations. My mom's wedding cake, my kiddy birthday cakes, my whole family's birthday cakes, my significant other's cakes. Heck, it may even be my wedding cake. Probably the best German cakes, or rather the best black forest cake you can get in Indy.

Yes, they have a lot of knick knacks, snacks, and all kinds of crap scattered around which gives it's unique German experience without really being there. It's homey feeling, that's all that matters. Especially when you're having a sucky day working until 4pm on a Sunday, Heidelberg is like the light at the end of the tunnel. I'm glad this was on my way home when I needed something cheery to pick me up. They close at 5pm on Sundays, but to my surprise this place was still packed (with seniors) having their bratwurst, cakes, cookies, and coffee/tea. I stumbled in along with my boyfriend to grab a pretzel and looked around for other goodies. We left with a freshly made soft pretzel and a marzipan apple strudel for home. Both were equally delish. I like how German treats aren't so sugary compared to our American goodies covered in icing.

The next time I visit, I think I'll sit in and have one of their bratwurst meals. I'm not a fan of sauerkraut or sausages, but hey, gotta try everything at least once before you say you hate it. Who knows, it just may be that once in a lifetime, dang-good wurst that I'll crave for.

Can't beat the rustic open atmosphere of this joint that rotates musicians to please everyone's tastes. Even better, you can eat a Florida-style meal while enjoying the tunes on stage! Reuben grouper sandwich, anyone?

Today was my first visit here with my children and their father, and the food was great! Usually when I eat out with my kids and I ask for things to be partial servings or made simply so the littles will enjoy it too, I get some sort of back and forth about it but today was the easiest time I've had with i doing so in all of my years eating out. They didn't have menus to hand out but when I asked for something to view they obliged and gave us a tablet. I of course kept it with is to keep ordering more because everything we were served was sooo good! I will be returning in the near future to try more on their menu!!!!!
Always enjoy a good meal at Ooka. Their hibachi is entertaining and food is fresh and hot.  They have take out as well.

Dinner last night was FANTASTIC. The food was incredible, the waiter was attentive and nice, and the atmosphere was comfortable. We had penne alla vodka with chicken, prosciutto, and peas & eggplant rollatini. The bread was perfectly fresh and warm with a subtle crunch. Best meal I've had in West Chester and in a long while. I've been here for lunch before, too and I have always had great experiences.

Worst waitress ever. Told her we wanted to talk our time . She insisted on taking our entire order... We weren't even done our appetizers when she brought out our main course. I stated we weren't ready and that's why I didn't want to order and told her we wanted  to take our time ... She didn't say anything and just walked away

They were fast, courteous, and really tasty. We had a hard day on the paddle boards and needed quick easy sustenance. The phone etiquette was clear and concise and it arrived quick and hot. Would buy again.
I got a brisket sandwich and some mac and cheese.  It was amazing. Custmer service was great. I will be back!

Great place just down the interstate from us. Never had a bad sandwich here and the staff is nice. One thing I don't like is those new Coke machines with the touchscreen. Lots of options but none taste mixed correctly (soda to syrup ratio is off). Also, these machines create a bottleneck and make it take longer to get your drink than to get your food.

Wanted to try this place since arriving here and finally made it. The food was delicious and the service was great. We ordered several tacos in a variety of proteins and each were delicious. I also ordered the spicy chicken quesadilla which was a good shareable size. They included two sauces, a red and green both were very good, but watch out for the green it's extremely hot and tasty making it difficult to stop eating it.

LOVE THIS PLACE. Only coffee place in town that has a drive thru when you're in a hurry. AND their Java chip blendeds are BOMB. Not to mention their hot chocolates and mocha valencias are just plain awesome.

Umm... yeah, I loved this place. Like it's seriously so good. Immediately walking in, it's like the mood just changes. It's romantic. Sexy. This amazing guy I like to call my boyfriend took me here for like the best date ever. There are candles everywhere. It's dim. It's perfect. Seriously, take your girlfriend/wife/some person you like... whatever. I loved it. 

Okay, let's talk about food. 

Appetizer: we went with the curried crab dip. It was delicious, and I'm not even a curry fan. I loved the thin vegetable chips. It always makes me think I can eat more because it's a healthier element. When I go again, clearly from the reviews I need to try the biscuits. 

Food: I went with the fried chicken (mainly because I trust johnny's taste buds). It came with 5 pieces ($19)... delicious. You can't go wrong with this. My boyfriend got the duck. Also, not a huge duck fan, except maybe I am if it's prepared correctly? It was seriously fantastic. I could eat this all day. Yum!!!

Drinks: I mean, we're wine people. I say that but... ordered a Pinot noir and expected it to be red? Nope. It was a rose. The actual red Pinot noir, delicious though :) we also tried the sangria. A bit spicy. Not your typical kool-aid sangria which I appreciate. 

I'd say this isn't your everyday restaurant, but I'd say you should definitely check it out. Celebrate here. Something.

First time staying at the Silver Legacy Casino Hotel.  I have to say that it was great!  We were there for "Street Vibes" this past weekend and it was great!  The room was clean, quiet, comfy and the entire staff were great.  The restaurants, Sterlings Steakhouse, Flavors Buffet, etc. were great too.  It is also conveniently connected to the El Dorado and Circus Circus which makes it very nice.  We will definitely be staying at the Silver Legacy again!  Thank you!

The food and service were both really good. 

The location is great too and it was busy both days we went. It is on the main floor of an apartment complex. 

This is a family run place. The food was incredible. The Beef Steak Sandwich in particular was really good. 

They have a separate small hall for private events too.

COVID: Face mask required. 6ft markers on the floor for lining up. Although many patrons didn't not follow and were too close to us in line. Would have appreciated if workers emphasized the rules. All workers had face masks on. The hand sanitizer dispenser didn't seem to work. 

I got the large 24 oz tropical guava with the bee pollen supplement (all drinks come with 1 free supplement) for $5.50. I'm glad I opted for the large versus $4 for the small 12oz. It was a nice refreshing drink for the summer and I finished the whole thing. I loved how thick the smoothie was and all the fruit and supplement made it feel healthy a f. Tasty 10/10. 

Would come again to try the other ones and can see why this is a must stop.

I wish I could make the trip out here more, it's definitely worth the trip from philly. Great beer and great food. Prices are a little high for my budget but are absolutely fair for the quality of the food and drink. Pretty much never had anything I didn't like and the atmosphere is pretty cool. 

I haven't had the best service there, but most of the time I think it can be chalked up to how busy that usually are. Except the time  I brought my mom and she asked if they could cut her sandiwch into 4 pieces instead of two (she was going to share it with the 4 people there) and they told her 'she had a knife'. I thought it was pretty rude and it would literally only be one other cut for the guy making the sandwich. Dumb complaint, but my mom's really nice and they just made her feel like an idiot :(

Having moved to Nashville from California my husband and I crave In-N-Out often. Quick side note, for those that compare Burger Shack or In-N-Out burger to the likes of Burger Republic or Burger Up: you are comparing apples and oranges. In-N-Out is California comfort food. Moving on, overall the food is good, but there is room for improvement. 

Burgers - Great! 5 stars! Right in line with In-N-Out. I got a hamburger with lettuce and grilled onions. My husband got a double cheese burger with no tomatoes and grilled onions. Both of us agreed our burgers were as close to In-N-Out as we could hope for in TN. 

Fries - Decent. 3 stars. We just got regular fries. You could tell they were frozen fries. However the seasoning was good. The thing the makes In-N-Out fries some of the best ever are that they are fresh cut and thin. Invest in a fry cutter and Burger Shack could come close. 

Milkshake - Good. 3.5/4 stars. Milkshakes were good not great. The straws were pretty thin and made the shake extra difficult to drink. If I were Burger Shack I would invest in some thicker straws for milkshakes. 

Overall, Burger Shack is doing a decent job living up to In-N-Out standards and hits the spot when I am craving an In-N-Out burger. Just work on the fries and it will be a 5+ star place.

I have been wishing and wishing for a salad buffet and yeaaaah it is finally is. The salads are great, I recommend the Asian salad a little spicy but very nice. They have soups, baked potatoes with all the fixins, muffins, and other breads, and pasta and pizza. Great layout of food. If you want something light and also if you want something to fill you up this is the way to go.  Very nice service/people that come and take your plates and make sure your food is tasting good. My only complaint is the pizza, very dry not so good tasting.
The hubs and I have been here a couple times this week and have been very impressed. Great food and excellent service. Kevin waited on us both times and is just delightful - such a doll.

Went here for brunch with my sister today! Service was impeccable. We were seated promptly and were able to order pretty quickly. Staff were engaged. Food was amazing! My sister had an omelette and home fries & I ordered chicken and waffles. The mimosas were delicious as well.

Prepared foods (meals, soups, etc) for taking home and heating. Selection of cheeses, crackers, spreads, coffee.  We purchased the $15 cheeseboard that came with nuts, grapes, honey, toast, and a selection of hard cheeses). It was fantastic! Highly recommend. We also got crackers and a goat cheese cranberry spread. This was also very good. Very friendly and welcoming staff. Definitely worth a stop when in Kennet Square.

We want to try everything, but we only have so much room to fit food in our bellies. We know we love pho and we know we love vermicelli noodle dishes. I had the vermicelli noodle bowl with meat and it was legendary. My wife had a dish with sugar shrimp. For those who do not know the shrimp in this case are very small, ground up, and seasoned. The sugar is a four inch (or so) length of sugar cane. The shrimp mixture is packed around the end of the sugar cane and cooked. Think corndog-ish shape. The flavor from the cane goes to the shrimp and after you eat the shrimp  bite the cane gently for a taste of more real cane sugar. So so delicious, we are quite lucky to have a restaurant serving something so special. Pho street did this dish very well, it was part of a vermicelli bowl.

We tried the egg dish which is essentially an omelet. It had great taste, but we too greasy. Other than that the herbs, veggies, and sprouts that came with each dish were so fresh that I ate them the next day with our leftovers. I keep begging to go back to Pho Street, but life keeps getting in the way. Soon, my friend!

Meh just about sums it up - tried it for lunch today (we were grocery shopping, and it was right there), and it was not very good. For being right at lunch time, almost everything we tried was overcooked, and tough. But its a buffet, and i guess you can't expect much more. The price was alright; something south of 20 bucks for two people on the weekend seems to be at the low end for most buffets now.

So go if you want a cheap chinese buffet. Cause thats what you'll get.

I have ordered 2 pies from Tonito's and had two very different experiences. The first was a solid pizza. Not great, but good. The second was just bad. Dripping with grease and the cheese was all over the place. 

I had high hopes as Exton NEEDS some good pizza and I live right down the street. I will probably give them another shot, but if they come up short again, I will be back on the search for the perfect pie. 

2.5 stars

I got into this restaurant while returning to Chicago from a road trip, since they had an excellent rating on Yelp. Needless to say the restaurant didn't disappoint. The food and the ambience were great and the staff was friendly. Try their chicken boti, I loved it. One of the best Indian/Pakistani places at a great price!

Lively boisterous really cool room for enjoying a party with friends watching the game or hanging out.

A very nice extensive menu lots of choices sandwiches burgers pizza etc.

You better know what you want when the waitress comes up to you because they keep moving there's a lot of people to attend to the waitresses try to stay on top of things as best they can.

I definitely enjoyed the atmosphere and would recommend this place highly people looking to hang out watch a game and enjoy a brew with friends

Beer is the obvious drink item as their menu has about 25 or 30 different beers to choose from.

The pizza is incredible , generous amounts of fresh toppings brought out piping hot and just wonderful.

On top of everything else the staff is absolutely sweet as can be. I cannot recommend this place highly enough for people looking to have a good time!

Stopped into this new Tucson restaurant on Sunday night. I was surprised to find that we could be seated right away - I was expecting a wait since this is brand new to Tucson.  My guess is that people are not yet aware of it, so perhaps it will get busier as word gets out.

We were greeted quickly and served our drinks.  The coffee is good and strong. The menu is typical American fare:  hamburgers, meatloaf, chicken fried steak and lots of breakfast items.  They also are known for their cobblers and pies.  I opted for a breakfast, going for a meat lover's omelette with fried potatoes.  My father ordered the pot roast with mashed potatoes.  The first thing I noticed when our food arrived was that my breakfast was served on a platter!  Like a serving platter!  This was a huge amount of food!  It came with a homemade biscuit the size of a kitten!  That being said, everything was quite good.  The omelette was delicious, the fried potatoes good and the biscuit, with butter and jam, was as good as it gets!  My father enjoyed his meal as well.  The pot roast was moist and tasty and he said the mashed potatoes were some of the best he'd had in a long time.  This meal was a "twofer" - two for the price of one.  We both took home enough leftovers for a whole meal!

The prices were reasonable for this amount of food. On average I would say a meal would be $11-12.

Update:  Be forewarned!  The desserts are also a "twofer"!  

We tried two different items: the chocolate brownie/chocolate ice cream/chocolate sauce sundae and the coconut cream pie.  Both were very good.  If you are a chocoholic, like myself, the sundae will not disappoint.  The brownie is very chocolate-y, which I appreciated.  The pie has a graham cracker crust and appears to be more of a coconut custard pie.  Compared to our other favorite pie place, my companion preferred this one!  But, go prepared to share - we actually had to take leftover dessert home and we didn't eat dinner beforehand!  

I plan to go back just to try out the good looking pies when I'm not too stuffed!

If you like places like Cheddar's or IHOP, you'll like Big Bear Diner.  A welcome addition to Tucson.
Avoid at all costs - Food is decent, but our wine carrier was stolen right from under our table.  Nothing done about it, treated terribly.  Used to love this place, but will never be back.

Would give it 5 stars except for 2 things.
1. The bread was not real fresh. With Conshohocken Bakery so close, there is no excuse for not having great bread. 
2. It's really small and noisy, but so are a lot of BYO's.
The food is up there with Fond and Sycamore. Service was very good. We had a couple requests and the waiter was very nice about both.
Spinach salad with pancetta was perfect as were the Brussel Sprouts drizzled with balsamic glaze.
The flounder was on a par with what you would get at Blackfish, and the duckling with berry sauce was cooked to perfection.
The entire meal was well paced and will go back again. Next time I have to try the mesquite bbq ribs and chicken which a diner close by raved about.
They have parking right next to the restaurant and during the summer you can sit outside. They only take MC or Visa for plastic.

Really nice place. Ambience is pleasant and more fancy than other Asian joints. Good place to have a business lunch. I suggest the pad see you with chicken or the crab fried rice. The pho is also the best in the area. The grilled meats though are just ok.
Needed something to eat and place to watch Redskins...check, check! Got a chili burger. Got fries. Got an IPA, Skins down by 12 points in 4th

If you are a lover of flavors - garlic, mint, parsley, good olive oil - then make sure to try this hidden gem. My husband and I first ordered takeout from here because it's reminiscent of my grandmother's cooking and it does not disappoint. We've also eaten here and BYOB'd. The staff are so friendly and make you feel welcomed, even if you stumble through pronunciations. Our favorites are the Baba Ghanouj to start and the lamb platters. You can even substitute items in the platters to meet your diet (ie low carb or not so much). When you leave this place, your mouth stays filled with delicious flavors that you can tell were prepared with love and a passion for Mediterranean cooking. I hope this sticks!

Though I seem like THE customer to love Pure Fare, somehow this place just doesn't do it for me. Overpriced, small portion sizes, and lackluster food quality... and I've tried it a couple of times too. I keep going back with the hopes that I'll find something that actually tastes good and impresses me, but I have yet to find what that is.

I've tried a smoothie (sounded great too... matcha something or the other), some salads, some bowls, and even some of the desserts. Nothing has stuck. 

The worst part of it is the pricing. Everything is EXTREMELY pricey for the quality and the size. There's just no value, and I've found that there are several other vegan spots around the city that deliver higher quality food at lower prices. 

Sorry Pure Fare - there's nothing Pure about you for me.
This is a great walk on place. We've never had to wait in line.   Tonight's dinner was good. Some days are better than others.

My boyfriend and I were vacationing in Clearwater for 5 days, and by the 3rd day we were completely over the fried food selections and drooling at the thought of some "real" food. Steak was what he wanted and after looking for some restaurants this popped up and happened to be close by. We were BLOWN away. He had a new york strip cooked medium rare and said it could not have been cooked any better! As a side he got mashed potatoes and we were fighting over the last bite, they were so creamy and buttery! I got the seafood Alfredo, which came with lump crab meat and jumbo shrimp. The crab portion was extremely generous (was a bit surprised) and the jumbo shrimp were just that..JUMBO! I finished my whole plate (something I never do) and all we could do on the walk home was talk about how amazing the whole experience was. Service and all! It was just what we needed!

I came to Oxford Exchange with a friend for the first time. I had heard great things about their aesthetic and food. I made a reservation on Open Table and recommend it because it was so easy and I got the time I requested for two. I will also say there is a gated, free parking lot two blocks from the restaurant so don't get duped paying for parking next to the church or fighting for street parking. I got to the restaurant 10 minutes before my 10:30am reservation and was immediately seated in the courtyard area. If you can swing it or request it this was a cool place to sit. We were seated and immediately greeted by a server. Another note is that they can't sell alcohol until 11am so I had to wait to order a mimosa. For breakfast I ordered the eggs Benedict and it was very delicious. I like cilantro and this dish had plenty of it. I also got a huge portion of their breakfast potatoes and I couldn't finish it. I ordered a cup of coffee and it was good but I wish I had tried a cappuccino or a more craft coffee beverage. I eventually got to order my magnolia mimosa which was champs and cranberry juice. It was good but that $10 price tag hit my heart. I liked this place but it's definitely expensive and I'll likely come back for special occasions/celebrations. After breakfast we walked around because this place has more to offer than a vibe. There is also a bookstore, Warby Parker, and home goods store for you to browse!

This location has a lot of history for me. I went here a lot growing up when it was a Joe's Crab Shack and I was glad to see that it has been reincarnated since the storm. 

To me, Joe's was always about the view over the food. When I had heard Landry's had taken over the location, I had hoped that they would provide some better quality food. 

My one experience with this location since it became a Landry's was just OK. Granted it was late on a weeknight and we had a large group, so maybe what we got was not their A game. I was looking to get my fix of good fried seafood while in town, so I order the seafood platter. When it came out, it seemed soggy like it had sat up in the heat lamp for a while. The waitress was a little unresponsive too. 

I'll give it another shot.

Nice hotel restaurant and bar. The classic brother was well prepared and portioned. If you like craft cocktails get the JW old fashion. Excellent.  Cobb salad was really good as well served with avocado toast. Nice touch. Service was good as well.
In New Orleans for the weekend and found this awesome place to have a Margarita and watch the game. Martin the bartender was the best.
Great atmosphere! The carnitas was pretty good, and the quest dip was great! I'd come back again.

The restaurant is spacious and well decorated. The service depends on the server you get. I've gotten awful service (sat 20 min and had to ask for a serve to come bring us menus) to good, attentive service. The reason for the 2 stars is that the food just isn't that good anymore. It used to be much better, but now the food is just not tasty. The last time we ate there, we had the Pad Thai, which didn't have any peanuts or sprouts, and wasn't very good, and the drunken noodle, which tasted pretty much just like the not-so-tasty Pad Thai. I would recommend going somewhere else.

If you're looking for a family outing place consider hanging at Armature Works because they have it all! Come for the amazing food choices but stay to relax and people watch, take in some Florida sunshine and mingle with your guest outside. The best part is your kids can have fun too with the outdoor area and there are food choices that they would be happy with too. There are choices for the most basic appetite to the most eccentric! From pizza, to barbecue to sushi and everything in between this hall has it all. My family loves it not only for the food but they offer events and classes too. Kids cooking classes, Mr Tommy interactive fun and family movie nights to name a few. When friends and family come in town we always take them to Armature Works. I really like the location because its steps away from Riverwalk!

Stopped in to Café NOMA for the first time to grab some breakfast. I've been watching construction take place around it for a year or so. It looks so nice and new inside in the little eat-in courtyard. You can access the cafe without paying the entrance fee to the museum.

That staff were very friendly and masked up. Pineapple mimosas were a surprise as I've never seen that before. The lemon icebox pie was delicious. Sweet and tart with a chewy crust on the bottom. I bet all their pastries are great. The kitchen doesn't open until 11 so I'll have to go back to try some of the other things on the menu like Thai fries or Spicy Shrimp Poké bowl.

In a sentence: my favorite American-Chinese-Korean joint in UCity. 

Hear me out. I have a set of favorite dishes that I order every time, so I literally have no idea how some of the other dishes taste. But who cares? My review!

Vichet's All-Time Favorites for Getting No Work Done in the Afternoon:

1) Egg rolls (freshly fried - nice and crispy on the outside)
2) Sesame chicken (super crispy, with a nice, gooey, sweet/tangy sauce)
3) General Tso's chicken (same as above, but with broccoli and slightly more soy/ginger than citrus/sugar)
4) Beef lo mein (greasy goodness)
5) Beef fried rice (fried so hard that even the rice grains are caramelized - deliciously smoky)

I swear they put crack in their sesame chicken. Those little seeds? They're actually crack rocks. In fact, I'm pretty sure that any MSG that was originally in the food, naturally occurring (yes, glutamate ions naturally occur, look it up) or otherwise, has been replaced by delicious crispy crack rocks.

The service is always friendly (they recognize me and my coworkers by now), and the food always comes out quick. They have no problems with little additions to the order like extra rice, red chilis, sauce, etc.

I come here way more often than I should. And, let's be clear that this is probably one of the worst things you can do to your body on a given day. You WILL be sleepy and 2 lbs heavier after eating here. But, if you love comfort "Chinese" as much as I do, remember Won is there with their delicious spring rolls and crack-chicken.

Pro-tip: Their lunch combinations are huge, and come with one of the eggrolls I keep mentioning! Get it now!

I love World of Beer!  My girlfriend and I had just finished up playing an "escape room"  nearby and decided that we really needed to unwind and get something to eat. WOB couldn't have been in a more perfect location for us!  Now, my friend had NEVER been to WOB before, and this was MY first time at this location. When we were seated we were deep in convo then realized that we had not been been approached by a server in almost 12 full minutes!! NO ONE person came to check on us or take our order. I started looking around and saw folks who came after us were served while we just sat there looking for someone to give us eye contact. Now, there seemed to be some type of staff huddle happening in the corner - an employee noticed us looking around and fortunately sent someone over to our table before started to consider walking out.  
The rest of our experience went well. They made up for their mistake by constantly apologizing, bringing the food out quickly and constantly checking on us throughout our meal . 
I had the Oatmeal Raisin Cookie Ale which was great! I also tried a couple other shots- one being cheesecake; only downside to this flavor is it gets pretty chunky if you don't drink it right away :-( but it's also super tasty too! I feel like the price point for what I paid for was on point. I'll definitely go back for another round.

We were so excited to find out Korean bbq had finally made its way to Reno! Five of us stopped in on a Saturday night, We were seated right away. 

The server was awesome - she explained the whole menu and how it works. My fiancé wanted sushi but they don't serve sushi at this location but we were all blown away by how awesome the food was. We had a great time! The manager and owner Truman even stopped by and shared a few shots with us from a homemade liqueur that they made in house!  After being in the restaurant industry for 10 years I had to give them a shout out for their hospitality, ambiance and amazing food. 

They truly went above and beyond and we will be back and also will spread the word around Reno! Nice job Truman and team!!

Went here for brunch this morning for the first time. So glad I tried it! I had an egg white omelet with tomatoes, spinach and goat cheese, and it was delicious! The multi-grain bread from Le Bus was awesome, too. I'm a stickler for tasty coffee, and Green Eggs definitely delivered on the good coffee, as well.

Will definitely be back to try some of the other menu items. I have a weakness for red velvet, so I may just have to try the red velvet pancakes. Sounds yummy!!!

I've been here several times over the past 15 years. Today was the worst food I've ever had there. I had Swedish pancakes that tasted like paper. Completely flavorless. My boyfriend said his tasted like cardboard. He had eggs, sausage, hash browns and an English muffin. Very disappointing breakfast. We will not return.

Food no well prepared - eggs burnt on the edges, well done (no as I ordered) and very grease. Bad service, live music too loud for 11 am on a Sunday. My review is got one star just because of one of the staff members presumably the owner was very nice to usable welcoming.

Last night my friends and I went to Blind Pig to enjoy a nice drink on our Thursday evening. The manager seemed very heated while we were there and insisted only after being seated for 10 minutes that he needed to search our bags. We were so confused why he needed to do this, but complied because we knew he was authority in this situation. He found a flask in my friends bag after rummaging through her personal items and grabbed the flask, walked to the back, and emptied it, finally throwing it back on to our table. Last I checked this has never been a problem to bring a flask out when the bars charge about $12 a drink. Awful experience, and awful customer service, so unprofessional. As a large group of girls we all felt the need to comply, but this was embarrassing and I hope no other women ever have to go through something like this.

The food is good. I usually get two orders of chicken fried rice to meet the delivery minimum. I can eat it for like three days after because the portions are huge which is nice.
I've never had any problems with carry out, but delivery is another ball game. They are S L O W. Like waiting for paint to dry in the rain slow. I ordered my food at 7pm. The order portal said 40 minutes. It is now 8:50 and the guy just knocked on my door. At this point I'm starving and would eat a paper plate. I asked him what took so long and he gave me a blank stare.
Another really annoying thing is they always call me to go outside even though I put the gate code on the order form. I had to go out into the street in my Jammies.

Jess M. was my server and she was great!  The food is amazing...The Taste of New Orleans gives you a little bit of everything - gumbo, crawfish etouffee and red beans and rice.  A must try when in NOLA!!
Saki Endless Sushi in Clearwater has an excellent atmosphere. Excellent, fast and friendly service. Fresh sushi with a great selection of rolls and entrees.

This  is a true treasure for the appetite & a must  to try. The  owners , staff, customer service,  and best of all the menu, be you a meat eater or vegan or vegatarian( forgive me if I spelled it wrong) are definitely fresh & delicious.

I had been to F&M a few times just for beer, and it's to hard to imagine anything more ecstatic than three rotating cask-conditioned cellar-temp beers that are evidently brewed with precision and imagination.  

My wife and I have since eaten dinner here twice.  After both meals, I caught myself thinking about how good the food tasted for quite a few days afterward.  The fish and chips plate was nothing short of glorious.  And I am thankful that I don't live within walking distance of their kitchen because I would not be able to go more than a day without stopping in for one of their mouth-watering burgers.  Even the bread they sit you down with is perfect, sourced from the inimitable Baker Street Bread in Chestnut Hill.  

This place, hipster vibe and all, takes food and drink very seriously.  If you don't get yourself and your loved ones in here without further delay,  I am afraid to say that you're doing it wrong.

I'll keep it short and sweet.  The fries were amazing.  I wish this location had chili.  The burger was just OK.  The onions on it were good quality.  The lettuce was too leafy for me and I wasn't a fan.  The burger itself didn't have a lot of flavor.  The shake was made out of real ice cream but didn't have a lot of flavor.

The person that served me, I think her name was Jessica, was 5-stars and really sweet.  I will be back for the fries and maybe a soft drink.  I'd be a frequent visiter if this location had chili.

If you are ever in the South Philly area be sure to stop by this new bar-restaurant! It is amazing! The staff is incredible & music is great! let's not forget the food an Italian take on bar food that is to die for! cannoli pancakes , tiramisu French toast , lamb burger, scampi mussels were all out of this world! They have a drink that has sorbet in it and tastes like a flint stones push up pop! I think we found our new spot for nights out!

Probably the worst McDonald's in Philadelphia.  Slow service, COLD FOOD and ignorant employees. If your fries are hot you're in luck. If you get an extra burger or fries in your bag (from the ignorant employees) you're even luckier. More than three times I've drove off GLADLY with extra goodies. Not that its a bad thing on my part but they clearly don't pay attention. I'd hate to be the one who has to wait for food because they passed it off.

Dear Nashville, step up your game in the airport food department. There were slim pickings that day and we decided on Swett's. It seemed like a decent purchase, but the breakfast food was just ok. My recommendation: pack snacks.

This place is a great college bar.  Don't go here for any sort of lavish experience, go here for cheap beer, and good times with friends.  I never had the food here, but the beer is extremely cheap, thus making it good.  The bartenders and wait staff are very attentive, which always makes it easier to stay for one more round.  The decor of the place could best be described as "busted."  Everything here smells eerily similar to stale beer, while the booths, tables, and floors have probably not been cleaned in quite some time...but I really didn't care.  The vibe here was so upbeat and people were so friendly,  you'll forget that your foot is stuck to the floor in no time.  Go for the cheap beer, stay for the friends you'll make.

I used to go to Co CO Di's all the time on RHW, even though I liked that location better, the Jasper Ave location is great, if you leave that place still hungry, maybe you need to get a few staples in your stomach lol. As always the portions are massive, the quality of the food is of top excellence. The staff are super friendly, and Riad the owner, is awesome. BTW they haven't changed their prices in over 10 years, so you get way more in portion and quality than you pay for. The only bad part was the light above my booth kept turning on and off which got a bit annoying.

My husband and I were there last night. The restaurant decor is very pretty. Does not feel like you are in a casino at all. They have only been open for three days but the food was great and the staff couldn't have been nicer. Every person that worked there was very accommodating, attentive and pleasant. Great job, thanks again! Wish more places had the amazing customer service that this restaurant had.

Very happy with my meal. I ordered a full rack of St. Louis ribs (decently priced), and needless to say, it was the biggest portion of ribs I have ever had! Their side dish called Dirty Rice is very good as well. I enjoyed their food and my parents did as well. They have a good atmosphere with nice employees and clean bathrooms. Can't ask for much more!

The bar tenders here are great! So attentive and nice. Also when I was waiting for an Uber after having a bit too much to drink one of them came up to my table with a water and refused a tip for it!!! Such a nice change from the other bars I've been too
Best tacos we've had in Indy. The service was great, the tacos were great, the home made ginger ale and pink grapefruit soda were to die for! We'll definitely be back!

Today was definitely sushi day.  I stopped here on my way back and grabbed a spicy salmon sushi pizza and white tuna avocado roll.  They have a decent 50% off menu, although the variety of special rolls is not as extensive as Sakura's or Shogun's. 

 This is the only place in the area that offers sushi pizza so I had to get it, simply because I hadn't had it since visiting Toronto.  The version here was pretty good, although it wasn't the same as what I have had in the past.  The Toronto version has a thin, crispy, and chewy fried rice base topped with thin layers of avocado and salmon, drizzled with spicy sauce, and topped ith various roes.  The version here has a slightly denser, thicker rice crust, although the rice still had that delicious fried crunch.  The salmon slices were also a bit on the thicker side, but that actually complimented the desner crust, and the fish itself was fatty and fresh (I love fatty salmon and tuna - which is why my cholesterol is through the roof).  The spicy sauce wasn't that spicy but it was very flavorful and creamy with just a touch of wasabi powder.  Overall, a pretty tasty version of a sushi pizza.  Definitely gives it a try if you're in the area.  

My white tuna avocado roll was also very good and the rice was perfectly seasoned, sticky, and soft, even after the 40 min. wait time from receiving my order and actually eating it.  I also picked a pumpkin tempura roll and lobster tempura roll for my dad, who proceeded to engulf them almost instantaneously (no raw fish for the padre).  I managed to sneak a bite of the pumpkin tempura, which was crispy and creamy with just a touch of sweetness.  Definitely getting my own next time.  The lobster tempura looked pretty good, too, and the roll itself was very big.  The only thing is that I will probably request that they add mango to it should I get it next time because mango in a tempura roll really adds that sweet, refreshing splash of flavor to balance the fried component.  Not a big deal though, and judging from the consumption speed, it was pretty tasty. 

It was less than $20 for everything, and my order was ready in less than 15 min.  Will definitely be back soon, especially since they have a scallop tempura roll and hamachi kama that are yearning to be tried.  Will report back.  I haven't dined in so I can't really report on the service except to say that the takeout operation was fast and friendly.  While the roll quality is not as amazing as Bluefin's (yep...definitely setting the benchmark very high here), it is good, the fish used is fresh, and the prices are GREAT.

Stopped in for the first time tonight with my sweetie. I am a vegetarian, so I had my Velvet Hammer on a Boca burger with tots. Sweetie had a beef Hawaii 50 with onion rings.  Both burgers were fantastic.  We ate the whole thing and plan to go back.

Was fooled by the number of people eating at the bar. Ordered shrimp sausage po boy and jambalaya.  First order was incorrect and redo took a long time.  Jambalaya was not spicy at all and couldn't taste any shrimp in the shrimp sausage. Could have chosen better.

We love Chick-if-A we have never had an issue with an order.  However tonight when we got home with our order I found something wrong with the lemonade.  I called the store to report it, apparently someone had put straight lemon juice into the dispenser.  Then the gentleman asked if he could bring me some, I told him we were already home and he asked if we lived in Plainfield, I said yes and he said he could bring them to my house. About 10 minutes later someone showed up at our house with replacements.  You couldn't ask for better service. You guy are awesome!

I heart this place, yo. My boo and I rolled in on a random very very cold Thursday night and we were the only ones there. So I was a little suspicious because I usually associate places that are bumpin' with the goodness of the food. But lo and behold, the service and food were excellent. Definitely the feel of a family run business with like mom making the sushi, dad handing the bills and daughter serving you the food. And everyone was amiable (server was funny and sweet... wonder if she's single should i set her up with my friend?? hmm No, he's not good enough she was that cool). 
I was laughing because I felt like EVERYTHING had avocado in it and I'm sadly newly allergic to it, but obviously they let me order it without the avocado. Verdict: everything was fresh and pleasing to the tongue and eyes.
Best part about this place is that it was laid back and I could totally see myself going there with a bottle of wine (byob!!! awesome!), chompin' on some sushi and browsin the interwebs. A great find for those of us in the Art Museum.

While very trendy on the inside, the quality of the sushi nor the service lives up to those expectations. We ordered sushi to go from here and they told us 10 minutes. We arrived at the restaurant to find the two orders the place were rather overpriced, quality unbecoming, and we waited 25 minutes while ordering overpriced drinks at the bar. I don't think they have a legitimate sushi chefs. Rather a bunch of college students have taken some course on how to make sushi.

Three stars is generous. Iced coffee-not good; tasted old.  Tables and chairs-sticky and did not seem clean. Staff started cleaning early and walked past my husband with every full trashcan in the building-gross! We will not be returning.

This is a delightful spot to have a relaxing and enjoyable meal.   Everyone liked their meals and the consensus was tasty food authentic in nature.  Sapphire our waitress was so friendly and attentive and greatly contributed to our fun celebrating a birthday.

We had an awful experience at the taproom and were very unhappy when we left. We were seated at a small table by the bar, but it took 15 minutes for anyone to come around and take our order. I understand if the place is busy, but the upstairs wasn't open and there are only 6 or so tables downstairs. Once we gave our order to the hostess (since the waitress was so busy with the 5 other tables) it took another 10 minutes just to get our overpriced 12 oz beers. The beers were good, but not worth the price for the size that you get. I ordered wings and my boyfriend ordered the steak tip sandwich. The wings were way too breaded and fried, it was like I was at KFC. My boyfriends sandwich was pretty sad looking, and didn't taste much better. It was mostly bread and not real steak tips. A second round of beers took another 10 minutes to get to us and then they screwed up the bill in the end...The only food that looked ok coming out of the kitchen were the burgers (but how hard is it to screw up burgers). We usually love bars like this, but in the end we did not enjoy our time at the Taproom and will not be back.

The main hostess was rude seating us, but other staff members were friendly and helpful.  The grilled chicken varied in temperature, but was of good quantity.  Dessert of raspberry sauce surrounding white mousse filled dark chocolate was nice with chocolate writing on plate.  Prices were on high side, but makes one appreciate preparing food at home.  Wall paintings had mixed reviews from our group.  Location is away from main transients farther downtown.
Great drinks, great bar specials, great service, great location! Walking distance to our hotel was a bonus. We will be back!
Great atmosphere although inside seat in was limited and it was pretty cold. Didn't take long to get a seat though. Good tacos and chalupas. My favorite was the fish taco.

Food was good but what really stood out was Charles the waiter with a beard. Kind professional and attentive without overbearing. Food gets between a three and four star but service gets between a five and six. Best server we've ever had at an applebees. Ask for Charles by name. We came on Feb 11th at 7pmish so whatever manager is reading this go give Charles a pat on the back for hitting a home run for service. We'll be back!

$4 house margaritas that are heavy on tequila, and the good kind, Yes please! The service was great, the waiter was very helpful and let us in on some great tips for ordering. They have a great outdoor set up for COVID safe dinning. The chips are warm, perfectly salty and not greasy. Splendid home style salsa. The Papusas were decent but, I probably wouldn't order again. The fajitas were delicious. The tacos seemed a bit overpriced but, I might try them next time. This place is always busy, so make sure you have a reservation if you can.

Get in ma belly, Cheesesteak.
Best vegan Philly Cheesesteak I have ever had, and I've had a lot, all over the country. The staff is friendly, the food is good.
What more could you want?
(For a store to open in NY, please.)
Stopped by this morning for breakfast, the dinning room is closed due to the coronavirus, but the drive thru and take out is still open.

This location is located in inside the Silver Legacy or El Dorado Casino.  I am not sure which it is actually attached to.  But it is along the walk way which connects the casinos. 

Visited during my stay in Reno for the bowling tournament. 

I had a Gut Buster Burger.  And it lived up to its name!!!  Bacon, grilled cheese sandwich between a huge burger..  

We went back a second time for happy hour while we were there. Nice discount beers and discount appetizers.  Only had the stout beer, but it was exceptional. Friends also tried variety of beer and were happy.  Had wings during happy hour and they were very good.  Good bar wings....

And the nice thing is you can walk out into the casino with your beer.

This will be a go to place next time I go to Reno.

I went here on an anniversary date with my boyfriend, and really liked it. The restaurant was really packed since it was Friday, but we didn't wait long for our food, and our waiter was pretty attentive. The food is on the pricier side though, and I was a little dubious of how small my food portions was when my salmon came out- but it was DELICIOUS and I was really full by the end. Definitely going again.

The ambiance is very nice and relaxed with rich woods, a gorgeous leather booth down one wall and moody lighting. The cocktail menu is fantastic! I like the vibe of the music as well. Definitely recommend the old fashioned and the hot chicken boa. I also love the spring rolls and the impossible gyoza!

I stopped in here to when I had to kill a few hours waiting for my sister. I got an iced coffee and a blueberry muffin. The coffee is great, very smooth and not bitter at all. The muffin was a little dry, I wouldn't get it again. They had a ton of other options such as bagels and quiche. 

I noticed some reviews say there was a minimum of $10 to pay with a credit or debit card, but it seems they have gotten rid of that policy. I was able to pay my card no problem. There's a ton of seating with plenty of outlets for chargers. The service was super friendly and quick.

I'm dying to go here once more to give it the 5-stars I suspect it deserves. A friend and I stumbled in here and immediately turned to each other, jaws dropped and mouths drooling. The display case is spilling with rows upon rows of decadent lebanese treats. 

When we ask the guy behind the counter for some help, he without hesitation launched into an explanation of each. "This is like a chocolate cookie on crack ... some dates and honey on top... That's one's more like a shortbread on crack..." super-friendly. The food's delicious!

They have couches, a very nice outdoor patio, and free wi-fi!! I'll be back soon.

My husband and I frequently eat here, the food is delicious and the service is exceptional! They have such a great variety and so convenient in The Spanish Springs area, we try different menu items and have not yet been disappointed at all! If you want easy pretty quick, homemade taste this is your place!! 100 stars!!
Clearly they are not open until 11.  Should change your hours.  Party of 13 refused at 10:40.  Guess they don't need the tips.

Walked in after the Phillies game on Sat March 30 with my wife and 2 small children.  They told us sitting at the bar area would be quicker than waiting for a table.  Ok - it was getting late and we were hungry.  We sat in the middle at a pub table with  4 chairs. We waited longer than 5 min before a server finally walked up to us.  He apologized for the wait and said he didn't see us sitting at the table in his area.  Really? What??  It gets worse.  We ordered drinks.  I ordered a tall Sam Adams.  Kids and wife's drinks came first.  Ok - mine was from the bar.  Whatever.  So I waited...and waited...and waited.  Finally he brought it over - Not a tall Sam Adams.  Regular size.  I rolled my eyes - whatever again.  We ordered the food.  Kids got chicken fingers.  Wife and I ordered All American double cheeseburgers.  I can be a finicky eater - So I made it simple - Just make mine with buns, cheese, meat, bacon and lettuce.  That's it.  Easy right?  Not so for them.  Kids chicken fingers were dry and hard.  He brought my burger back with...mustard, mayo, ketchup and pickles.  At least he immediately realized that it was completely not what I ordered and took it back.  Then 10 min later he came back with a super greasy burger that still had pickles in it.  WHAT??  At that point I was upset and finally said something.  He was nice and did apologize, but they messed up so many things it was too late.  I ate 2 bites of the burger and some soggy fries.  Slop.  The manager came by and then offered us coupons for next time we come.  NEXT TIME???  I told her there would not be a NEXT TIME and was again upset by this weak attempt to make our experience better.  Then she said she would also give us 25% off our meal.  I accepted because I just wanted to go.  Awful.  The whole meal should have been FREE for that garbage food and service.  They finally decided not to charge me for that garbage burger after I told them it was inedible.  I was foolish.  I had heard bad stories about this chain in the past and thought "let's try it out."  HUGE MISTAKE - NEVER AGAIN.  TOLD ALL MY FB LIST - many said "yeah we heard horror stories about BWW too!"  At least the Phillies won.  HUGE FAIL by Buffalo Wild Wings.  PJ Whelihans in Newtown Square is like the Capital Grille compared to this hole.

Beautiful ambient setting, great service! The food was good but not $50 good. I love that there is valet parking and a great variety of choices on the menu, but I just felt as though The food wasn't as authentic and booming with flavor as I anticipated it to be. Maybe it was an off night I'm not sure? I would be willing to try this place again but my three star reviews definitely from the flavor of the food. Very bland but looked nice.
Great food, service and atmosphere !!! Hats off to chef and his delicious menu!!! Flourless chocolate cake was decadent !!!
We were going to Cracker Barrel but the wait was over 45 minutes so we opted for the tried and true Silver Diner. Never a wait to get a table. Now with their new menu there are healthy choices.

I'm prissy so going to a place that served in a paper bag was not at the top of my list. But baby let me tell ya I will never in my life go anywhere else for a burger. The peanuts are soooooooo good and they even have my fav drink Sprite Zero in all Flavor's.  Service is great and the place is clean

Food was good but do not ever bring out the main dishes while I am still eating appetizers. Barely minutes into our appetizers the hapless waiter brought the mains. We asked him to hold them in the kitchen till we finished appetizers. Of course the mains came back cooled down. I had the waiter reheat mine and it came back with the chicken dried out. Probably microwaved it. 
The waiter was no where to be seen after that for at least 25 minutes. Getting the waitress attention working the other side of the restaurant was nearly impossible since she was barely present. Thus our water glasses were empty for way too long. 
When the waiter finally appeared he was apologetic saying he was helping out in the kitchen. Say what? So you abandon your paying customers? He was young and inexperienced so I hope he learned his lesson with no tip.

The food here is always great! Especially the fresh cut French fries!!! The staff are really nice. They will bring your food to you when you order and dine in. The lobby is clean. The bathroom was clean. No complaints. I would come back.
Best Italian cream cake ever! Go in March to order St. Joseph's cake, available for one week a year. Great cannoli and coffee cake. Family owned and operated.

Quickly seated at around 5pm on a Thursday. Food was good. I had mahi mahi. Wife had crab cakes. Both were delicious. Service was quick and even though they were busy our server was great. This place is literally on the beach so the view is great from the patio.

It could have been that my group just lucked out and chose winning combinations, but we were three for three. You also can't go wrong with the white trash fries. What probably sets this place apart from other hot dog joints I've tried is the bun. Really, we all agreed that the bun may have been what made these dogs great.

Quality and variety. I love a traditional gyro but sometimes I want something different or maybe a little lighter. The Gyro Co. has a varied menu compared to similar places that I've been to. My particular favorite is the Cheesy Greek Squeeze, which could possibly be one of my favorite sandwhiches ever. They get extra points for crispy fries and having Orange Fanta in the soda machine so that I can make Orange Coke!

The prices a very reasonable and food is always fresh. Add in fast service and a quiet atmosphere to make for a pleasant dining experience.

We didn't eat here just stopped in for beers.  Service was very good, beer selection was all over the place, almost whoever's buying the beer is just going with what the Beer Reps are pushing.   We'd like to actually try their food, their menu looks good.

I was really scared to try Chef Dan's because I know a lot of these places use that obey seasoning I hate that stuff. But by my surprise they didn't use it on my fish. Thank God.. My Catfish, red beans and rice and yams were delicious.. Keep up the good  work..  Very clean and pleasant place.

This place is known for it ambiance and interesting concept. There are couches, bowling lanes , a bar bigger then most in Nashville etc. It's Creative, different , good food, however we came here at 12:20am and they say they serve food til 1:00am but they WOULD NOT serve us food . LAME! change your menu times please!
In summer my favorite place to watch the river and enjoy the wine and food.

Brunch and dinner all in one day. 

Took my pops for brunch this morning and was blown away with the amazing service, quality and food. Everything was high quality from start to finish. Want some amazing knowledge about your food and amazing personal service? Ask to sit in Samantha's section. She provided such amazing customer service (and sent me home with the dinner menu to drool over) that I went home and convinced my husband to take me back for dinner! Everything we ate was high end and delicious. The scotch egg (holy crap so good) duck and waffles (rich rich deliciousness) poutine (perfection, potatoes could have been cut ever so slightly smaller for a better potato to curds/gravy ratio) beef bourgnion (hubby says DELICIOUS!) and tomato tart (spectacular) all exceeded my expectations. 

I can't wait to come back and try more things off their menu. Honestly Samantha made our stay so enjoyable. In fact everyone who worked there really made you feel at home and it really seemed like everyone was happy to be at work. 

Seriously though, Sam - you rock. Thanks so much for an amazing day of indulgence :)

Placed an order and after an hour I still hadn't received it. I called the store and they said they don't deliver to my hotel! Then why did their own website allow me to place the order from their location for delivery?! I told her it would be nice to have received a call to let me know that my order had been canceled. She said I did call, twice, and I received a busy signal both times. You don't receive busy signals when you call my cell phone, it goes to voicemail. And I do not have any missed calls or any voicemails.

This local bar is really great! 
There's a view of the pier and the beach anywhere you sit. 

Late night kareoke and cheap drinks!!

 They have a large menu with great items like the lobster roll, crabcakes, burgers, or little appetizers at the bar to go with your drinks. 
All my parents neighbors love having their lunch get togethers here.
They always rave about the great food. Some things are a little pricey, yet worth the price. 

It's like a party everyday and everyone here is friendly! :) 

I'm a regular here when I come to Florida for visits!
The Thai curry pizza is excellent as is a bottle of the local root beer (big enough for two to share). Definitely one of my favorite pizza places in Tucon.
