Visited during Oktoberfest. I loved the vibe inside and the front porch area - perfect for people watching and enjoying the day. The Halloween specialty beverages were not only interesting, but very clever (Witch's Cold Brew, Scary Spice...) and the pumpkin latte art made my day :)

:: Parking - They have street parking. I believe a municipal parking lot, located around the corner is available for use as well.

:: Alcohol - They are BYOB. If you want, the art gallery located directly across this restaurant sells bottles of wine produced by NJ and NY vineyards. This restaurant will give you a 10% off wine coupon ('poker chip') that you can use at that gallery for a discount. 

:: Atmosphere - Unless it is for a date-night, I'm not too hung-up about ambience as long as the food is good. Upon entering, we detected a musty smell, often common for flood-prone areas such as Mt. Holy and Manayunk....the smell seemed to have dissipated as the night went on. The main room has an old'ish diner feel to it while the backroom was a little more cozy.

:: Food
- Cold combo spread - Each individual item on this plate (eggplant salad, hummus, olive spread, etc,) was very good. We would order this again.
- Octopus Sta Karvouna - Excellent. Nice portion, flavorful, not overcooked. Decent price. We would order this again
- Pistachio Crusted Snapper - Nice portion. Perhaps a little dry but very flavorful. Wow, the accompaniment of lemon potatoes were fantastic. So simple but delicious. 
- Salmon - Ok, nothing to write home about.
- Vegetable Moussakas - My wife enjoyed this.

:: Service - Excellent. The owner (Greek gent) was very friendly and seemed hands-on. Our server was great. 

:: Pricing - Very easy on the wallet. 

We will return

My god.  Reservation for 10 on a Thursday night at 730.  Arrived and looked at me like I was nuts when I asked to be seated.  Didn't not get my drink until food came out over 45 min later.  Mortified I chose this place to take friends!!  had to actually get up and ask if anyone was coming to take our order after 25 min of just sitting there.  Brought us food with out silverware, no big deal, but waited for 10 min for forks food, which eventually became cold.  When we nicely tried to approach staff, they either ignored us and walked away, or said someone will be right with you that never came.  Kicker is they weren't even busy!! Skip this place I will never go back ever!! Service was UNREAL bad.

First, this place is BRIGHT.. Like hurt your eyes kinda bright lol.  Not that I want a diner to be dimly lit or anything but I wear glasses and notice things like that.

The menu was probably the largest diner menu id ever seen in life. There's something for everyone. Literally. I also saw the extra value meals where you get an entree, soup or salad, dessert. Pretty typical diner fare. 
Our waitress, Judy was a hoot! Hilarious but not annoyingly funny. I'd come back just to sit at one of her tables. I'd been on a burger kick all week long so I ordered the All American Burger with lettuce  tomatoes and red onion. Ordered medium with Old Bay fries.  It came more well than medium but alright. The burger was still good. The bun, brioche I believe or a smooth knockoff was good! Buttered and toasted. Buns make or break a burger experience. This one hit the mark.. While the fries weren't hand cut, they still made my day. My date ordered a bowl of Claim chowder soup but was surprised when he got Manhattan instead of New England. Judy asked us if we still wanted it, we hesitated  bit but decided to eat it anyway. Great choice! It was tasty. However, I'm a New England Lady and like that one much better. He also ordered a Breakfast Chicken Sandwich. Came with turkey bacon and melted provolone cheese. He enjoyed it. Chicken looked moist and super juicy. 

There is a small bar with no seating. From what I saw, there was no real bartender, as I watched any waiter and waitress walk behind to grab beer, wine and make cocktails. Knowing that,  I'm not entirely sure how well a good cocktail woukd be made there. But hey at $3 a glass for house wine with your meal, I'll take it. 

Next time I'm in Woodbury, I'll be back.
Great Service. Good Burgers. Salads Ok. Other entrees Steak & Frites, Pork Tenderloin, Orecchiette Pasta were very average to low quality.
Both the food and the atmosphere is very good. I had pad thai and it was pretty good. Mostly I like the restaurant ambience. The service was good too.

This was my first visit to a p f changs.  We had good service, everyone who worked there was very attentive.  I had the salt and pepper prawns with rice.  I'm glad I ordered an appetizer because all that came with the prawns was rice.  My mom had the vegetables with tofu.  She was very disappointed, there was but a trace of tofu.  It was mostly broccoli.  There was about 6 quarter-sized pieces of tofu, and they were as thick as a quarter.  The appetizers were good, I had the curried cauliflower.  Not sure if we will be going back.

The security guard DEMANDED to see our service dog's papers and ID papers. There is no such thing, according to LA & federal law. I tried to help him understand this & he refused to listen. I asked for a manager, he refused to get one, told me I needed to get a police officer to prove myself. I refused to move until a manager was obtained, he started throwing the "f" word around, and got out his flip phone to call the police on me. I left to to call Bamboulas - while trying to leave a message, the security guard left his post to come down the street to harass us. I called for help and he replied "are you f***ing kidding me?!" We have filed a complaint with the ADA from Miason, a GREAT bar next door.

Fantastic experience. Staff was very friendly and welcoming. I had the chiles poblanos, my wife had the al pastor, and my son had a quesadilla. The al pastor and quesadilla portions were enormous. All of the food was delicious, and the al pastor specifically was the best we've ever had.

I hope this place lasts longer in this location than the previous occupant.  They have the classics of saurbraten, Wienerschnitzel, and sausages.  They listed an apple strudel with vanilla sauce and some optional whipped cream and ice cream which sounds great.  I liked the  saurbraten.  I will be going back to try the Wienerschitzel.

I caught Kung Fu Hoagies randomly on 38th and Sansom my first day back in Philly. I had no idea they were located there, as I always thought they were based out of Clark Park, so that was a pleasant surprise! They're a big hit among my vegan friends, so I've always been looking forward to trying them, and I was pleased.

I ordered a Banh Mi with vegan ham. It took about 15 minutes to make my hoagie (they make everything fresh and in front of you!) which was a bit painful in the ~100 degree Philly summer weather, but it was worth it.

Vegan ham = AMAZING. I've never had it before and I have no idea how they make it, but ohmygosh, it was just incredible both in texture and taste. The rest of the hoagie itself was pretty good too. The flavors of all the different vegetables and spices complemented each other really well, and the sriracha I requested was a perfect touch. 

However, eating that thing was a MESS. The crunch noodles they put in get everywhere, and (I'm not sure if this is how the hoagies normally are but) the toppings were kind of just places on the roll, instead of -inside- the bun, so it was a painful eating experience. The roll was a bit soft too, so it couldn't really support all the topping. Still delicious though! 

If I ever catch Kung Fu Hoagies again, I look forward to trying some other delicious item on their menu!

This was possibly the best location I've been to yet. I absolutely love Chipotle and cannot get enough of it. Everything was fresh and the employees couldn't be better! Very clean! I truly had a stellar experience! Thanks!

Great restaurant. Very cool and classy decor, a super nice waitress, and excellently prepared dishes. 

Food: The prix fixe menu prices were very reasonable with good choices. I especially liked the shrimp and goat cheese crepes - outrageously good. I also liked the pork chops - big, thick, fatty, and tasty. The bread pudding was delicious too. 

Service: super attentive and polite and personable waitress. 

Ambiance: very cool place, beautiful decor, historic building. 

Would definitely return.

Why have I never had this before? 

Everything is super cheap, super fast, and SUPER DELICIOUS.  I wish...I wish I still lived here.  I didn't try any of the pho here, but the banh mi sandwiches=OMG. Buy 10 get 1 free and all sandwiches are under $3. 

I also really enjoyed their meat pies and the bread was just the right amount of crisp on the outside and softness on the inside. 

Ah...*drool*

Speaking of outsides and insides (yes, corny, I know), they have outside seating, too (two tables with chairs).

Great little diner in T town. Not just donuts it has great hamburgers, breakfast all day, dinners like grill pork chops, white and red beans, etc. our waitress Autumn was great she did great job thanks! We will be back!

I can't say enough good things about this place. 

Food is amazing. Best veggie burger I've ever had, I don't even care that you need a fork to finish it!!

Oh my God the mousse and other delights are incredible. Vegan. Insane. 

The service is GREAT with big smiles and laughs. 

If you haven't checked it out. Please do. 

PS: I don't work here or have any stock in whether you go or not :) BUT GO!

Nom nom every time. I've had the granny salad with avocado instead of meat, the Cali wrap with steak, and the breakfast bowl with chicken (wished I got steak lol). All delicious! My fiancé got the broth bowl and loved it!

My boyfriend and I had dinner here a few weeks ago.. it was amazing! Their house pop corn is super delicious ..we ordered the punch bowl, octopus, fried chicken, wings , and corn bread... we loved it all! Also, the service was great!
This was a great hotel bar. The food and drinks were good, the bartenders affable. Great place to unwind after a day in the city.
Really great food.  The menu is extensive with items that are really great.  Happy Hour is 1/2 off apps and they have weekly specials so there's something for every budget.  Great drink specials!

Came here on 1/10 Sunday around 12 - there was a 40 minute wait but it was well worth it . The interior was for modern and the service was great . My girlfriend and I both had the French toast cannoli it was good , was it omg no but it was good and def served a lot . The bacon was probably the best bacon I ever had . Coffee was good . I have two complaints - one is parking and secondly is that they don't accept credit cards - cash only  and although they have an atm on site it sucks bc ur paying for the fee . But besides that goo for it

Perfect service, awesome drinks, good food. 

Burger was a little too well done for medium-well, but that's what I get for including "well" when I really just wanted medium. ‍

Good food, nice looking place, but waaaayyy too loud. There was a live band playing for a private event a few tables away from us (cool!), but they were so loud that I missed much of the conversation at my 5-person table (not cool). It actually nearly ruined the evening, considering that the whole purpose of the meal was to catch up with friends. Darn.

The food was good though. I liked how they kept bringing out those huge French bread rolls and whipped butter! I had the turtle soup (waiter recommended extra sherry; quite tasty!) and the crabmeat "cheesecake" - also good! Haven't had anything quite like that before (some people have said that it's basically a quiche, and it certainly looks like one, but the texture/taste is definitely from the cheesecake family, not egg-y like a quiche). I also got a side of the fried oysters, which were HUGE (and yummy!).

For dessert, we shared the bananas foster (obviously), and the white chocolate bread pudding. Both were good, but not super special (other than watching the table side flambe).

Overall, a fun place to be a tourist!

Great atmosphere.  Fresh Seafood.  Lovely lunch spot. 

Holy Grail - Maryland (love!!)
38 North - Maryland (awesome!!)
Hurricane Harbor - Virginia / very high salinity (not a favorite that will have me coming back for more)

Caesar Salad "Royale" - Good.  The blackening spices on the shrimp made it just a tad salty.

This place is just terrible. I will drive out of my way to go to a different BWW even though this one is much closer to where I live. The atmosphere is terrible. I have ordered to go and it's been completely wrong. Management is rude and I'm still waiting on a "gift card" to come in the mail for their last mistake. I have given this place a chance numerous times and they constantly disappoint. Save your money and skip this.

UPDATE:12/06/2019- tried ordering again with uber eats, this time it was my boyfriend ordering(which I had very high doubts and did not want to do). This location can not get an order right and they do not do the right thing by their customers. Every time they mess it up we contact them to try and make things right and they are not at all apologetic or willing to make it right.

I had dinner here on Friday.  Overall the food was good and the service good was well.  I will the menu were a bit larger with me choices.  The restaurant also had a decent selection of Evers on tap.  It's not outstanding but a solid choice for a meal.

My husband had dinner at this location 3 days after they opened and according to him, the line snaked through the restaurant. He said they handled the crowd with great efficiency and his food was really good. He couldn't wait to tell me about the great taste and value. Because I was out of town, I didn't get to try the restaurant when he did, so we went a few days later. What happened in less than a week, we will never know but the experience was the exact opposite of what he had a few days before!
When arrived around 8pm and waited 10 minutes while the cashier took care of the 2 people ahead of us. As we stood there, we observed the other employees laughing, playing, and joking around. We understand that these are likely high school or college kids so a certain casual behavior is to be expected, but not when there are customers waiting. After the 2 patrons ahead of us  completed their order we stepped forward to be served, but the cashier chose that moment to eat chips and queso. We waited patiently and watched her eat chips and queso. After her snack, she greeted us and we placed our orders. Then we had another 30 minute wait as we watched the employees have a good time and confuse the orders sitting in the window. My husband saw a to-go bag sitting in the window for several minutes before he then saw one if the employees interrupt her chatter to glance at some of the receipts to fill orders. By the time we were given our order we counted 13 employees in the restaurant and 11 patrons. We checked our order and it was wrong.  My husband requested no tomato but there was Pico de Gallo on his Spicy California taco. I asked for one beef and one chicken hard tacos on my Taco Plate. When we checked they were both soft and both beef. My husband was disappointed and embarrassed because he had highly recommended we go there for dinner and the service was poor, the orders were wrong and the food was lukewarm. Needless to say, I am not eager to go back!

Just loved it !! Great food and great place. It's off the beat and path and was just what I was looking for. The wait staff especially Leslie made us welcome and was fun to talk to. This is a true Nashville treasure !!!

I've been here a few times after hearing great reviews... unfortunately, I have not been super impressed. I keep going back though trying to get a really good meal- I still have hope!

We went for brunch and the menu was fine, limited compared to the full menu, which is to be expected. I ordered the BLUE CRAB CAKES, spicy green tartar sauce, mesclun green salad. 15 which were super tasty, but extremely small. I usually take home half my meals anyways, but this wasn't even enough to fill me up! Very nice flavor though. We also had the CASHEW CRUSTED HAWAIIAN FISH, ginger butter, Texmati rice, sautéed spinach, sweet potato chips. 15. which to be honest, was just alright. I was hoping that a seafood place would have something more exciting than Mahi mahi on its menu. Both of these options were on the brunch menu, but for some reason we were told that they were not available for brunch...in the end the server brought them to us with no explanation...

Our table also had the MAINE LOBSTER ROLL, caper mayonnaise, red pepper, celery, scallion, coleslaw, handcut fries. 16, which looked good, but the person eating it didn't comment.They also ordered TRADITIONAL EGGS BENEDICT, English muffin, Canadian bacon, poached eggs, béarnaise. 9.5..which they didn't like (I thought it looked good..)

We tried both the FRESH PACIFIC NORTHWEST OYSTERS and the GULF OF MEXICO OYSTERS. I enjoyed them quite a lot. I had a cocktail, but the server had never made it before and she seemed very confused about putting it together, and was even more surprised when I told her that it was actually very good!

After we finished our meal, we were all so hungry that we each ordered a dessert (we usually do not eat desserts)..when they came, we were shocked! they were massive! We had to box them up to take home and ended up sharing only one between the 4 of us. I thought this a bit strange considering the portion sizes of the mains to be so small..the deserts were all excellent-I had some bread pudding/run concoction- amazing. 

The next time we came was for Happy Hour (Daily 4:30-6:30). We entered the restaurant and the host looked at us like we were someplace we shouldn't have been and asked what we wanted!!! um...We want to sit down and eat!!!? 

We ordered the STEAMED BLACK MUSSELS (7), as did most everyone else around us, but we were really, really surprised to see that they arrived with the cling film still on them, and the bowl really hot- this obviously came out of the microwave! The clams and muscles (we got a mix portion) were all overcooked and rubbery! What a disappointment. The oysters, which were great on our previous visit, were all shucked incorrectly! Each and every oyster had bits of shell in. We attempted to get the attention of the bar staff, but there were so busy that it was impossible. We couldn't even get bread from bar staff/or servers...in the end we had to grab a bus boy who ended up serving us. To be fair, they were really busy on this day, but I felt really let down by the quality of the food. 

I did enjoy the Happy Hour vibe- there were tons of people there...and the patio is a great place to sit. 

I will give this place one more try...I am determined to like it....I hope they impress us a bit more the next time.

Wifey and I stopped in for an appetizer and ended up getting an app, entree and dessert. The Brussel sprouts were delicious. They were chewier than expected, but the bacon and butter sauce was rich and mmm, mmm good. Next we shared the broiled gulf fish, which was drum. It came with grilled asparagus and Brabant potatoes. All very good. I just wish the potatoes had been crispier like the ones Kenton's used to make. We finished with the chocolate ganache cake. It was so moist and chocolaty. It really hit the spot. 

Service was great. Our server was fast and very attentive. Ambiance was also great. It's a beautiful restaurant and great place to watch a game or for a date night. The only negative was that it was very cold in the building. We could have used jackets. They have outdoor seating and it was warmer outside, though. 

Looks like I forgot to take a picture of the fish. My bad.

Excellent food and service. We ordered a bunch of dishes and everything was cooked perfectly. The restaurant is dimly lit and seems more of a date place but don't let that stop you from trying their food. Tapas run $10-$13 amd mains run $20-28. And the portions are a good size. I really enjoyed it!

I would like to update my review after being contacted by Pizza Delicious. They explained the problems they were having and the growing troubles they have had. I would like to commend them on reaching out to me and being active with their customers on social networks / sites like Yelp. I will give them another try soon and put the rest behind me.

When this place opened up first, it was great. Good food, good service, great prices.

I'm not going to talk about the $2 dollar night because its pretty much their only thing they've got going for them. All I'll say is the bartenders are cool and nice and helpful. Servers and waitress' suck. Also, their tap/draft/keg systems are watered down. Guinness doesn't taste anything close to the REAL guinness. 

Any other time is not that bad. The waitress' that are there when it's not tuesday are friendlier, more attentive and just better than the tuesday crew. Food is decent.

Overdue review, I really need to be better about stuff like this, especially a place that is so deserving of a five star review. This place hits all the notes for me. It's not fancy, it's family run, it's stood the test of time because the food is really good. 

I love a good local place, with friendly people that know how to show an out of towner some good old fashioned hospitality. I was lucky enough to get one of the last available corner tables during dinner time, apparently they were holding the spot for someone that wasn't there on time, so my wait wasn't a long one. Big open room, reminded me of Club Lucky here at home. A good mix of people, young, old, couples and families. Everyone breaking bread and having a great time.

I had a glass of the house red, salad and the manicotti special. If you get the salad, do get the house made blue cheese dressing, you will not be disappointed, the three different sauces on the manicotti is a nice touch, however I think I prefer the traditional red the most. Even the bread was a treat.

If you're looking for a quiet romantic restaurant to gaze into your lover's eyes, this isn't it. But if you're looking for a great meal, it is. Of course you can still do the eye thing if you want :)

Very solid! I'd definitely come back!

Nice little place I found thanks to Yelp! Owner is friendly guy with a big Philly accent who may greet you while you enter. The downstairs is cozy and inviting and just what I was looking for. 

After my mother was done flirting with the owner, we sat down and had a delicious margherita pizza as an appetizer. Good choice for starters! I really like that type of Americanized Southern Italian sweet sauce which smothered the pizza!

The homemade linguini was excellent and cooked well! Bolognese was solid, chicken parm nicely cooked and my mother's caprese salad was as good as the owner said it would be. Also, she had a bowl of lentil soup that could kick the pants off nearly any other lentil soup. 

Sir Francis the waiter was friendly, helpful and not overbearing. Definitely worth your time for very decent Italian in a city full of solid competitors! Prices are just right as well.

Came in around 7:00 on a Saturday night with a group of 4 friends. There were 5 of us total, so we expected a wait. My friends have frequented this place and said their food was decent and it seemed like a new place that I might enjoy. Sadly disappointed.

We were greeted by a hostess within 2 minutes. We were then told it would be about a 25 minute wait, which we expected so that was fine with us. The time was around 7:00 PM when we first walked in. We were sat at 7:22, so 22 minute wait. Not bad considering it was earlier than the time we were told. We were sat in a corner booth which was private and spacious and the second best part of this whole experienced. We were immediately greeted by, in my opinion, one of the best servers I have ever experienced. He gave us the entire rundown of the place including history, menu specific details, and a mouthful about their "smoke shack". This guy was incredible and absolutely saved this place from a 1 star review. After the lecture, we investigated the menu. The smoke shack section was expensive, but my wife insisted on getting the smoked chicken, par fried. It was $14.99. I chose the 20 oz River City Chargrilled Pork Steak. It was also $14.99 but I've had an 18 oz pork steak from a BBQ place in the area called Penny's and it was comparable in price and very big. I couldn't even finish it and this was supposedly even bigger! We were told right off that it would be about 40 minutes before we got our food. We obliged because we were hungry, had already been waiting, and everything sounded so good.

First, the good. The booth. The waiter. The homemade onion rings. The smoked par fried chicken.

Now, let's get into this places downfalls and the reason why I will not be returning. I don't care that we had to wait for a table for 22 minutes. I don't care that we didn't order our food until 7:40. I don't even really care that the waiter told us it was going to be 40 minutes, because I assumed it would be worth it. It didn't take 40 minutes. It took an hour and ten minutes. We received our food at 8:50!! That is absolutely ridiculous. And I know what you are thinking, the 20 oz pork steak probably took forever to grill. I am here to tell you, that pork steak was not 20 oz. It was smaller than the pork steaks I grill up from Walmart. MAYBE 8-10 oz. And burnt to a crisp. I was visibly disappointed. There were 6 onion rings. They were decent sized, but 6?? AND they upcharged me for them?? Terrible. The pork steak was dry and thin and just disappointing. The sides were small and disappointing. $14.99 is a joke for that meal. The smoked chicken however was very delicious. BUT the sides were equally skimped on. And the salads...so petty. AND $1.00 upcharge. I feel like if I am paying $14.99 for chicken, I should get whatever side I want. But they make the menu. I have no right to complain about the pricing if I am getting what I order. However, when I am served extremely tight portions and being charged more, it irritates me. The server was very friendly the entire time. Asked us to be understanding and even brought us free donuts. He kept this review a 2 star. We walked out of this restaurant at 10:10. Over 3 hours in this place, for sub-par food.

Overall, this was not a good trip. I can buy 6 pork steaks, all bigger than the one i was served, for less than what I paid for the one, burnt, thin, small, pork steak. IF you come to this restaurant, get items from the smoke shack. They may cost more, but it's very good. It carries this restaurant IMO. Will not return most likely.

Came to I Hop for dinner. All waiters not wearing masks. Felt I should leave mine on when he was near. Saturday 7pm Place was empty. My waiter was Milton.
This is not a reflection of I Hop. The location on Bearss ave. Was 100% better.
First things first. Our server, Izzie, was amazing. Nice night in Tampa so we sat outside. The menu is varied with standby items and unique creations, like Boxtys. Awesome place. Be sure to stop in.

I'll play devil's advocate and say I'm not impressed. As a local (I've attend primary school and grew up here), i love the new New Orleans and what it brings. These upscale food courts are cutesy and offers a nice ambiance BUT the food is only okay especially for the prices. You're literally paying for a vibe. I've been here twice only because my friends dragged me and i ate at two different places, the poke spot and the salad place next to it. The poke wasn't bad nor was it anything to write home about. And the ceasar salad at the adjacent spot was good...i mean it was a simple Cesar salad. If there's a next time, I'll be ordering drinks only. On a good note, i never have a problem with service and the place is always clean. However, these upscale food courts are just not my thing.

My husband and I were in search of a new lunch spot on a Saturday, ideally a new sandwich place! We chose Nora's and will definitely be back. The sandwiches, served warm, were huge and delicious. I had one of their turkey options and the broccoli and cheese soup and potato salad, which was just okay. Great neighborhood spot!
Absolute worst. Took over two hours to get a single pizza.. Same thing happened last time I ordered from them, but figured I'd give them a second chance. My mistake.
Great italian home cooking from the region of Emilia Romagna. Great quaint atmosphere! I would definitely recommend it

Ocean Prime is an absolute treat.

I have been twice now (once for drinks only) and I have been equally as impressed both times. The first time I went was with my boyfriend for our anniversary. When making the reservations online, I denoted "Anniversary" when it asked about special occasions. I didn't expect for anything to actually happen, but we were surprised with two glasses of champagne AND a complimentary dessert (which had "Happy Anniversary" written on it)!

The service is exceptional. You will feel doted on by the host staff AND the wait staff. 

The atmosphere and ambiance is both high-end and romantic (especially in the evenings). 

The drinks are amazing!! Both our waiter and our bartender were extremely knowledgable and that is very helpful to a somewhat-ignorant wine drinker. The star of the show, though, is the "Berries and Bubbles". This is far and away the coolest drink I have ever had. Despite its fruity name, the drink is not too sweet but perfectly balanced. And did I mention that it is made with DRY ICE?! Which means that upon the pouring of the drink, it bubbles continuously for about 10 minutes. Absolutely blows my mind.

The food, of course, is astounding. If I didn't have a budget, I would have ordered everything on the menu and then come back again the next day and ordered it all again. Every menu item they have is served with intention and a story. Plus, they use fresh ingredients mostly from local farmers. Hard to beat that.

If you are celebrating for any reason (and aren't tight on a budget), you absolutely need to make your way to Ocean Prime and TREAT. YO. SELF.

I recommend this place for the beer list, the ambiance, and the friendly staff.  The food choices have been improving since when the place first opened, but I find that the entrees continue to have way too much salt.  If you live in or are walking through Bella Vista, Growler's is worth stopping in to grab a beer and watch the game.

Came here because all other restaurants had a long wait except here. Now I see why. 
The "host" had her back to people walking in and didn't speak or smile or change facial expressions at all. I had to ask her if she was seating people since she seemed too occupied in looking around and wiping a plate. A few minutes later she asked how many we had and a bit after that she sat my mom and I. 
Our waitress Courtnee was pleasant enough. Not bad, but not great. She seemed like she was just going through the motions and wasn't very knowledgeable of the menu.
The Caesar salad was good, no complaints. 
The house salad was explained by the waitress to be romaine and arugula to my mom. The salad that was brought out was chopped romaine and kale mix and my mom had to pick out the kale the best she could, but eventually gave up eating it. 
My mom ordered spaghetti bolognese (meat sauce) and she rates it a 4/10. She didn't enjoy the taste and the sauce was watery. We had been traveling all day and were very hungry so she managed to eat most of the pasta, leaving the meat and most of the sauce in the bowl as it was too watery to stick to the pasta. 
I ordered spaghetti pomodoro (tomato sauce, no meat) and the sauce was a 5/10, but the pasta was undercooked. I know al dente is a thing, but I tried my moms spaghetti and it was cooked fine. 
I notified the waiter and she had the manager replace it. The spaghetti that the manager brought back might as well have been the same as the bowl she took because it was underdone as well. At this point I was very hungry and just wanted to eat what I could and hope that microwaving it later on would cook it enough to make it more edible. 
Over all, the experience was below average especially for the price and I wouldn't go back. I'd much rather wait 45+ minutes at a different restaurant or eat microwave ramen at home.

Detailed.  That's the best word to describe Brick & Brew. They've got the three D's down pat: Decor, Drinks, and Dishes.  

Wings are confit'ed before fried.  Personally, doing this causes the meat to lose the "juice" necessary for a great wing.  It does however speak to the thoughtfulness placed in trying to re-invent the standard wing.  I would prefer the head chef X'ed this step out of the equation. In my opinion, one never compromises food's freshness! The brown-butter hot sauce is solid.  The side of blue cheese has a milky, thin texture with a nice sweet, I'm going to say, honey accent. Being completely honest, I put the cup to my mouth and drank what was remaining after wings and celery sticks had been eaten.  

The beet salad was a winner.  Simply stated, if your there and want a healthy kick, get this salad. You'll be very happy. For the more detail-oriented foodies, you'll appreciate that this dish is a 4-part construction.   

Part 1:  You've got a basic mixed greens and radicchio tossed in a light balsamic/olive oil dressing. 

Part 2: Freshly-boiled, golden beets are cooked tender and left undressed and un-pickled. This nicely preserves the natural flavor of the beets, allowing their flavor to remain prominent against the bolder sweet and sour accents.  They're tossed into the mix. 

Part 3:  Crumbled, creamy goat's milk chèvre and candied, I want to say, walnuts are also tossed into the salad.   This is a nice play between sour, salty and sweet/crunchy and soft-textured bites. 

Part 4: A second chèvre is painted onto the dish.  The chèvre is mixed with a sweetener, honey I believe, warmed (maybe it was the plate), and paint-stroked onto the dish.  It's a really nice touch falling in line with the rest of the dish's flavors. Again, nice attention to detail. It gives the dish an added dimension that many venues simply wouldn't take the time to consider.  Forking the beets and mopping up this chèvre leaves the mouth feeling happy, happy.  

As for drinks, didn't have a chance to try. However, I'll be back for round two at this place for sure.

I was impressed with the food, service and atmosphere!! I have been there 3 times now and have tried the ARTICHOKE TOASTED RAVIOLI WITH PESTO, the COPPA PIZZA and the PEAR SALAD! All delicious!!
Love the decor and overall vibe...perfect for family night out, datenight or drinks with the girls!

The service was really good and very attentive. The food was delivered to the table quickly and hot. The fajitas were good but the tacos tasted like store bought Ortega shells. Icky. The enchilada is filled with cream cheese., A little different. Overall not bad.
Good sauce, cheese and dough. Real authentic Sicilian owner and employees. We will definitely be back. Thank you for being open during the holidays.

Very thick cheese dip. Very slow service (even at 1:30 on a Wednesday with no other customers). Great atmosphere and friendly (but slow) staff. We should've went to O'Chucks instead. The waiter did bring my daughters iPod out to us when she forgot it there so that was very nice.

Limited menu 
Fishtown iced tea novelty*
No rush to return 

*I'll bring my out of state friends here for the fanfare of drinking out of an iced tea box

I visited Leo Sushi at the Nashville Farmer's Market on the advice of a co-worker and was really impressed with my meal.  I got a rainbow roll (which comes with Miso soup), and an order of vegetable dumplings.  All three items were prepared perfectly and tasted great.  The fish was very fresh, and had good texture and flavor.  The rice was nice and fluffy, and the sauces were perfect.

Oh, and they got a 100 on their health score!
amanda was the best server, we were hanging around the bar waiting for a seat and she got us margatitas while we we waiting! sbes beautiful too

I LOVE T&T!!! I love ethnic food markets but this one is so much more. 

They have several different ready-to-eat counters - the one along the wall near the bakery has a fantastic selection of food - you have to try the beef brisket stew with vegetable (can't remember what vegetable it is, could be Chinese carrot - and be warned - the meat is a little fatty and chewy but that it's my favourite), or spicy shrimp (I don't even bother taking the shell off), or try one of their barbeque combos, which is what I did today - got a mound of rice, veggies, a soy chicken leg, a good chunk of Chinese bbq pork, and a bowl of hot&sour soup, for only $6.99!! Can't beat that price for the amount of food you get!

Their sushi is ok - the spicy salmon roll is the best, and they have pretty good salmon sashimi and a pretty good chirashi bowl. They also have really good congee (I don't know what the seasoning is but it's soooo tasty), and chicken teriyaki bowls.

They also make a ready-to-go series that are different kinds of foods packaged in a little aluminum container and wrapped in plastic wrap, that you can bring home, steam for 20 minutes, and it's ready. My personal favourite is the black bean garlic spare ribs - better than what you get at dim sum - it's awesome with a bowl of steamed jasmine rice. The chicken feet and beef tripe are also very good, just like you would get at dim sum.

T&T is great for getting Chinese fruits, veggies, spices, weird cuts of meat (lots of organ meats), everything! They also carry Korean, Japanese, etc food stuff. 

Oh you can also buy bags of chicken and pork bones, which are great for making stock. Lots of live fish as well - they have great deals on the weekend on crab and lobster. 

So my point is... go!! It's awesome!

Beautiful restaurant with a great atmosphere,  a extremely friendly wait staff and friendly chiefs.   The sushi at hachi is superior then any of the local competition.  They take  great care and pride in the preparation and presentation of their food.  They also have wonderful new creations that I've never seen before and they make for a very enjoyable and memorable dining experience.  This quickly has become my favorite restaurant.  The chefs do a great job of explaining the dishes and highlight the level of quality  and freshness of the ingredients.  Highly recommended A+++

Came here for lunch. Very nice inside. Very spacious, bright, and clean. 

I ordered a poke bowl. I started with jasmine rice. I added ahi tuna and salmon. I choose the soy-yuza sauce for my poke sauce. My base sauce was the coconut garlic. Both sauces were very good and a nice combination. I added edamame and cucumber. I also added scallions, nori furikake, crispy onion, sesame seeds, masago, and black seaweed. 

The jasmine rice had an odd texture and wasn't sticky like normal. The portions of protein were small. Overall it was not a traditional poke bowl or flavors. Not my favorite poke bowl spot unfortunately.

Well, we've eaten here many times and it is always very good.  We live close so our visits have also transitioned to carry out.
Our fav's!  definitely Mussels Josephine and the fairly newer item added is the coconut shrimp app.  -to die for.   They are huge, fresh and perfectly done!  The bang bang shrimp are also good and very popular, but if you're looking to get away from fried and sugar, try these items.  I make a little salad and,    Well I think tonight would be good for a little seafood, just talking about it!

They do not open for dinner until 5, and when we showed up at 5:15, we were the first group for the night on a Thursday night. Around 6, another table arrived. It was a bit peculiar to be the only people dining there for such a long amount of time but the service was impeccable- with 3 waiters to ourselves, and all very attentive, though not overly friendly. 

The onion bisque was delectable, with a sweet and savory base and melt-in-your-mouth bread, crunchy bacon bits, and scallions. And our entrees were good. The shrimp in the shrimp and grits was large and fresh. 

Their scones were dry, however, even with the whipped butter on them. 

Overall, the atmosphere is classy, with 1920s music playing and fresh flowers on each table. The waiters pull your chairs out here... I would wear a dressy outfit.
The tacos were incredible. Everything was well season. Great service. The beans were also very good. The menu was very affordable. Would definitely eat here again!

This is a tough environment, most of the people are in a rush to make their flight and the adrenaline is already 3 notches above normal just because you are in the airport.

They are seriously understaffed and try to do the best with what they have.  My wife and I both had burgers and the bin fell apart on both of us, stake bread that wasn't toasted.

The burger itself wasn't bad, it came quickly after we ordered.

The seasoned panko onion rings weren't very seasoned or fresh.  The coated steak fries were just not good, far from fresh.

The lemonade is good, I just hope you're not too thirsty because you will probably miss your flight waiting for a refill.

I wouldn't want to take the staffs place, it's a horror show.  If you have time to spare (we had two hours when we say down), it's not awful.  Try to give the staff the benefit of the doubt because I doubt you could find a tougher environment to sling burgers and beers.

My Daughter and I stopped by The Kettle & Grille for late lunch after reading some great reviews online.  Honestly, we were not disappointed ! The restaurant was nearly full but we were seated immediately. A plus was as soon as we were seated the server brought us each a glass of ice water as we were handed the menus.  Normally in most establishments, one has to ask for ice water, but since it was such a hot day, I'm glad she served it immediately.b

We shared an appetizer of poppers, chicken tenders, onion rings, mozzarella sticks and potato skins loaded with crisp bacon and cheese. Each item was better than the previous one, lol. We ended up taking home half of it as we had our entrees coming up.

LB had a bacon cheese burger served with French fries, cole slaw and pickle.
Her burger was cooked to perfection, well done but not burnt. She ordered it with American cheese, lettuce, tomato and onion, with a side of mayonnaise .  It came out exactly as ordered. The portion was so large, she ended up taking half of her meal home.

I ordered the Reuben, with corned beef, sauerkraut and Swiss cheese on authentic rye bread. It also came with piping hot fries, cole slaw and a pickle. The sandwich was delightful, plenty of corned beef on a nice and chewy rye, no grocery store bread here. My only disappointment was the Russian dressing, of which I'm glad that it was served on the side. At first I thought that it was some kind of cheese whiz dipping sauce, it was that color orange and very smooth, not the kind I'm used to that has bits of pickle in it. It was, in one word.. Nasty. 

Our Server was very attentive, she refilled our drinks just before they were emptied, and she stopped by our table a couple times to see how we were doing. Plus as it was obvious that we'd be needing take home boxes, she brought them by without asking. 

Good food, large portions, clean and friendly environment.. We'll be back !

Sunday night rockabilly is great.

the live band really get you in the mood, the bartenders are nice, service is great, drinks are perfectly mixed. only downfall is the size of this place, its TINY :( which is the only reason it didn't get a 100% amazing star rating. 

parking - you can easily park in the train station lot (its across the street) or even just take the train.
Best location ever. Friendliest service. Best tasting food. Best overall experience. Cleanest restaurant!

I eat a bagel every day. No matter where I am. For the last 30 years. These are the best in the world. So... when there is a line it is because the products are so good. If you come in on Sunday and special order bagel sandwiches you are going to wait. In a hurry? go to Starbucks and have a cardboard bagel from the freezer and be on your way. But if you want the best bagel there is, from a Mom and Pop shop that takes their time to create bagel magic the old fashioned way, get in line. Or do what I do, call ahead on a Wednesday. They are great people, but they are busy and again, not a chain with a million employees. Many times there is no wait at all. 

In a town where everyone loves their chains, and in a hurry, Skyy's the Limit is a true treasure. The salt bagel is my favorite. The Kummelwick is a nice treat. They are all awesome.

I really wanted to like this place.  I had seen their signs during construction and it seemed as if they had a sense of humor. I hoped this would translate into a really fun experience, and it did not.  Now this place is not bad by any means, but simply "A-OK" and not a place I'm sure I'd even want to give a second chance.
I stopped in here on a Saturday evening to grab dinner before a show at the Murat.  It seemed like the whole town had the same idea, because every place was packed except Pizzology.  Maybe I see why now.  The space is nice enough, and it's got an interest concept.  Even with the big windows (awesome for people watching!) it felt cozy and comfortable.  
We decided to sit at the bar.  Their beer selection seemed to be very thoughtful and had some nice local options.  I enjoyed a few brews, but kept getting distracted by the TVs in the bar.  No big deal, people love watching sports and eating pizza!  
Now the pizzas.  The bartender/server explained that Pizzology specializes in thin crust pizzas with either a red or white sauce.  Don't expect to understand what any of the toppings are, I just took a guess and ordered a pizza and hoped for the best.  It was okay.  A-OK.  Definitely not bad at all, but not something I enjoyed or even felt the desire to finish.  
All in all: friendly service, nice atmosphere, okay pizza.  I don't think I'll be back, but this place would be nice for a small group of friends or a casual dinner out with kids.

I was extremely disappointed with my service here and would not recommend anyone to go out of their way to check this place out. Especially if you have dietary restrictions like being vegan or vegetarian or any food allergies. Though they claimed to be accommodating towards vegans, they are absolutely not. There were multiple instances in which the waitress was rude to us. I went in with my mother, aunt and friend earlier this evening. My found this place since they said they could accommodate a vegan diet, since my friend and I are both vegan. When my friend and I were ordering we doubled check that the bread they came with our dish was vegan and she seemed to be very annoyed by that question. She said she would go in the back and check for us and when she came back she told us that one bread was vegan and something else was possibly vegan but vegetarian. We asked if it was possible if she could read the ingredients and she, she said no she had other tables and wouldn't be able to do that. Keep in mind this establishment has about eight tables and only three of them were filled including mine. We weren't trying to be difficult we were just trying to know if we were able to eat that bread in case there were eggs, dairy, or honey in it. When we asked for ketchup or extra bread she took a very long time to bring over to the table and had to be reminded. In addition to this when she brought over the check you could see visibly that she was annoyed that I was paying for it and I was the one that she had a negative attitude toward throughout the dinner. She probably thought our older guests would be paying. I normally leave the tip in cash, and I normally over tip. I used my credit card to pay for the check and she handed me an iPad with the screen asking for a tip on the card, when I hit no tip she grabbed the iPad in a rude way and stormed off to grab the receipt. I intended on giving her cash so that's why I hit no tip. It was just an all-around terrible experience and I would not recommend anyone to go here. The quality of the food was decent and the portions were small.

Amazing food and amazing owner! I come here all the time and the food is always brilliant and consistent.

Look forward to getting their food everytime in order.
Excellent environment and experience. The seafood is great. Nice place for a late night meal and drinks. Webster location

As someone who takes pizza very seriously, I can't say enough positive things about Snap. The staff is always friendly, the ingredients are always fresh, and they make it easy to customize your meal to build the superior pizza of your dreams. 10/10 would Snap again.

4.5 stars. Awesome small, family run business, the food was delicious! I would call the vibe inside "rustic," not everything is shiny or new or modern, but stays true to the essence of a restaurant I would find in Italy.
Yes, the plates are a little bit smaller than American food business entrees, but this is all home made and fresh! And honestly, we were full at the end of this!
Chef came out to make sure we were enjoying our meal and wine! Chianti paired well with our pasta entrees! 
Kinda had to take a half star off as I don't think the waitress was really experienced, the young boy (I think he was considered the host), knew more about the food than she did, as she had to ask him a couple of our questions, but maybe she was in training and a little nervous? And she kinda splashed the wine during the pour, luckily, on to the napkin in my lap and not my white pants, yikes. My friend is Italian and pronounced the meals the way it was written in Italian, and the waitress only understood one of the orders, as we had to point to each meal we asked for. Otherwise, the staff were very pleasant and friendly and made sure we enjoyed our meals. Would definitely highly recommend Beccofino, we came for a girls night and enjoyed ourselves, so it's for anyone, but I think this would be especially wonderful for a romantic couple's dinner.
solid diner that's open 24 hours. Good selection of food and service is usually good as well. The guy at the register (owner?) is a bit ornery, but stay on his good side and you'll be fine.
Great place. It is a buffet style Cuban Restuarant with everything fixed fresh daily. The plantains are some of the best I've found and did I mention that it's very reasonably priced
Not bad. Service was a slow as usual but food was good. This location seems to always have new employees. Over all not bad
I have been having a hard time finding burritos that remind me of back home (CA). This place has been able to satisfy my burrito needs. The food is great and they have great bottled sodas too.
Not a bad experience. The food was pretty decent. I got biscuits and gravy, which wasn't bad and my husband got jambalaya and was very happy!

Love this place... I ordered the Bellicimo (lamb belly burrito). Being in the business, I was taken back by their pricing. It was worth every bit of the $9. The ingredients were fresh, quality and well prepared. The portion was huge. The flavors were robust and worked until the last bite. I bought a second to take home for my girlfriend... I knew she could only eat half (more for me!)

I really enjoyed the atmosphere as well. Staff was nice and despite the line, I did not wait long at all for my first or second order. Outdoor seating is very cool and creates a fun setting for locals who like to meet new people.

I highly recommend Heffe to anyone interested in a taco or burrito that is not of the cookie cutter variety. I only gave 4 stars because I didn't want a soda and no iced tea was available. I was told they had not yet received their order for that day. I will be back to find out!!

Husband and I came here last night while roaming the Queen Village area.  The decor is very warm and cozy, and the atmosphere was almost zen like. Lots of rich red and gold tones with some cultural items throw in throughout the space.   We were the only ones in the restaurant but I didn't mind at all, the service was wonderful, every attentive and friendly. Our server, just knew when to appear at the table and when to let us enjoy our meal. 

I am a Thai food novice so I can't really speak to what is authentic vs. what is not. I went for the typical Chicken Pad Thai, which I have to mention is the best so far in the city, that I have had.  Not to mention that the portion was enormous!! (I'm actually having it for lunch again today!)
He had the Chicken Thai Basil, and asked for the spicy level to be hot, he was not disappointed, the heat was perfect, leaving the lips a bit tingly. The portion again was large and the vegetables in the dish, were really fresh, not the usual soggy peppers and onions soaking in the peanut sauce, that other Thai places dish out.

All in all, I really enjoyed our stop in here. I did notice that there were numerous take out orders, which seemed to be quick and efficient.  I would stop here again, if we are ever in the neighborhood!

Wow! Haven't been into Brinkley's since COVID. I heard they had new owners answer so we met another couple for dinner. Our server, Carson was awesome. My cosmo was perfect. I chose the filet (it was a special) that was wrapped with bacon and stuffed with blue cheese. It came with mashed potatoes and asparagus. The asparagus was cooked perfectly and the mashed potatoes were amazing! The steak was juicy and I loved the blur cheese filling. My husband had the bbq pulled pork sandwich and fresh fruit. He said the fruit was fresh and the bbq was a a winner. We had truffle for fries for an appetizer-they are addictive! We will be back soon!

Five stars aren't enough to describe this place!

When my husband and I first walked by (still choosing a restaurant) and paused, a random person sitting at an outside table yelled to us that the cheesesteak is amazing. Since the place was pretty empty, we thought it must have been someone affiliated with the restaurant. We wandered around a couple more blocks, then decided to return there. The woman was no longer there; she had been just a customer.

As soon as I bit into my own Philly cheesesteak, I also wanted to tell random strangers how good it was!

It was perfect! Juicy and messy and cheesy and hot and delicious! The kind you need a small army of napkins for, where you have to go wash your hands in the middle of the meal before diving, full-face, back in. Tender meat, melty cheese, perfectly browned onions, bread with just the right amount of crisp in its crust. I never understood what the big deal was with cheesesteak...until today.

The place is byob (the helpful counterperson even walked us to the end of the block to point out the nearest liquor store), counter-order, and rather brightly lit. It wasn't as busy as the (overrated and similarly priced) Sonny's a block away (where we had gone for lunch. Meh.). But man, can they make a cheesesteak.
Very disappointing açaí bowl :( the texture was kind of icy and not smooth. Also I don't love that they use soy milk instead of almond milk. Stripp'd in old city is much better

What's not to love about this lil place? The beer list is world class, the menu has something for everyone and the staff is super friendly! I don't think there is a better spot in the city to catch a ballgame or just relax with friends. Be sure to try the dirty wings & the chicken strips!
We've been to Alfredo many times throughout the years. I feel the quality of the food has been going down and the price has gone up. the only reason I will go back is they are byob.

Pretty good spot for a bite and they have cask beer as well! 

We stopped in for lunch today and the menu had lots of nice sounding options and the beer list, while I couldn't enjoy (work) was nice. We had the special salmon which for the life of me couldn't find any of the pesto encrusting. It had a nice lemon and roasted red pepper topping and was cooked perfectly. The side of rice wasn't anything worth coming for and it also has a shredded lettuce and slices of tomato, it was a special but maybe try something else. All the other food was very good, the Hawaiian burger was real nice with a hearty slice of pineapple and the hummus appetizer was huge! Plenty of pita chips for dipping and the ingredients were really fresh as well! 

I would love to give it a try when I can enjoy the beer menu next time!
I really dig their ambiance & veggie burgers. Their service is a tad on the slow side, though.

Gale was an amazing server. She made sure we were attended to without being overbearing. Her personality complimented the environment. The restaurant is gorgeous. The food was pretty good. I did feel like May steak was undercooked. She quickly replaced it including the fries I ate. Which we appreciated as they were not the issue. I truly enjoyed myself experience.

Amazing!!!  The food was delicious (I got the #2) along with the tropical fresh squeezed juice and coffee made with cinnamon, honey, and coconut oil.  Service was kind and quick!  Definitely my new local fave spot!

Awesome place. Great staff and atmosphere. The games were actually free for the whole month of April. We had an awesome time. The manager we spoke to said they were going to make some more improvement in the next few months, can't wait to come back and see!

Holy almost NOLA....fantastic menu, great prices!    The food arrived and I was so excited to eat I forgot to take pic.  Then dessert came and almost made the same mistake.   My daughter and I split char-broiled oysters, crab cakes, and grilled shrimp in a cream sauce I'd like to layer myself in.   My go-to desserts are creme brûlée and bread pudding...they had the bread pudding and it is one of the best I've ever had.   Hot, thick with yummy sauce and great whipped cream.   We will be back.

Unfriendly service,over priced for what they offer... could not recommend!!
Cluttered Dirty ... floor filthy!!

strong martinis. just because a drink is strong does not make it good. the bread given before the meal was good but, overall it was WAY overpriced. I had the seafood pasta and it was so salty. low class food that is over-priced. skip this one.

I have been here several times, always with other people who choose this place to go to.  Although others seem to like it, it is just not a top quality AYCE sushi place in my opinion.  Although AYCE, sushi, and quality might seem like a funny joke to some even being in the same sentence alone.  The fact is is that Reno/Sparks has some fantastic AYCE places and have raised the bar on exactly what this kind of restaurant should be as far as quality.  I have sat at the bar and the table in this establishment.  Chefs and staff are friendly, but I always have a problem actually getting what I ordered. I know each time I go there that if I fill out a sheet with the items that I was that I will either get another person's order entirely or get several pieces missing off of my order.  Add that to the menu that features almost every roll deep fried and/or spicy and this leaves me seeking out places with better/more attentive service and fresher or more raw fish choices.

Peter's Planters Punch is fabulous! Very Citrus-y & refreshing with a nice rum kick! The spinach salad with egg and candied bacon was good but not great. The bacon was a bit hard to chew and not very flavorful. The Crab Cheesecake was shaped like a slice of quiche. Oh yeah, they also provide a warm and crusty baguette too. Good to go!

By the way, Chuck and Lloyd both serviced my table...both HOT! They were so attentive and had great senses of humor. They made the dining experience even more enjoyable because of their jovial attitiudes.

Ippolito's is my go to for fresh fish in the city. From sushi grade (made Thomas Keller's salmon coronets) to humble smoked trout (shredded into a cracker spread) this place always has what I need at a reasonable price. Quality is always high - just yesterday I picked up some great snow crab legs cheaper than what the local supermarkets were advertising (Ippo's had it on sale for just $3.99) for a great Valentine's dinner. Staff is always super knowledgeable + friendly as well.

Love supporting local businesses and if it's good enough for most of Philadelphia's restaurants (they also own Samuels + Son wholesale) it's good enough for me. Thanks guys!

Loved the food and the atmosphere.  Servers were great and even went out of the way to make additional recommendations for the area.  Fried chicken was great and so was BBQ sapler.  Great atmosphere.  Lots of room at the bar and live music a few nights a week after 9.  Definitely worth the visit.
Rose benedict is amazing and the staff is super friendly. The prices are very reasonable, will definitely come again.

My husband and I are regulars when it comes to ordering for take out from Miss Saigon. Their menu is awesome and we love the beef Pho so much. The portion size is Huge and the flavors make your senses come alive.
The sesame chicken is the perfect combination of crispy and tender, and the Pad Thai is yummy beyond compare! They package to go so neatly and never fail to disappoint. 
If you are looking to bring your taste buds from boring to ba-boom and get away from the norm then Miss Saigon is a place you have got to try!

So this was my first time in Philadelphia so I had to have a philly cheese steak. This was not what I expected. I thought it would be cheesy and juicy and it just wasn't. I ordered it the provolone and onions,  luckily I grabbed some random condiments on the way out. They were needed. Maybe I should have ordered something else on the sandwich..there are several options for additional charge but I was trying to get the authentic version. Basically we had 3 steak sandwich in the 1 day spent in Philadelphia and this was not the favorite.

This is reminiscent of the "fast food" Korean restaurants in Hawaii I frequented as a child. You basically pick a protein and get several vegetable sides with it. I got the bibimbap and my friend got the bulgogi plate. The bulgogi was prepared ahead of time and in a warmer, and therefore was kind of dry. The veggies weren't bad, I'd say the kimchi was the best of the selection. It lacked the variety of most "fast food" Korean restaurants though. Overall,  I wasn't too impressed with my meal but I'd be willing to try their kalbi, which I believe is made to order, and see if the meat quality improves. But it's a nice beginning of Korean food trends in indy, and I hope to see more of these types of restaurants pop up in the near future.

I love this place! I had a Mexican omelette and it was delish! My sister had the western omelette and she said it was delish! Our waitress was outstanding and I loved the way the seating is. I like this restaurant should get 5 out of 5! Me and my sister will be back in!
Always friendly staff and I'm able to get in and out on lunch break. Great selection of meat and vegetables. Keto friendly!
The only restaurant where the flies are so numerous around your food that they are bound to fly into your mouth.    Disgusting.     Go far far away from here.

My 5 year old picked Applebees for birthday dinner. We were seated right away, restaurant looked to be about 50% full. 10 minutes went by, no one ever came to the table, at all. So we got up and left. The hostess that sat us was talking to a server standing at the door, neither one noticed us leaving. I did interrupt them to let her onpw why we were leaving. We went one mile down the road to Chili's. It was great.

P.F. Chang's is a great place for Asian Cruise with a variety of options. I was in the mood for something light so I ordered a few sushi rolls. I had the lobster avocado roll and the shrimp tempura roll. The rolls were quite tasty however a tad overpriced in my opinion given the portion. I sat at the bar were I was pleasantly greeted. The service was average and the servers appeared busy with restaurant tasks. The restaurant lacks a vibe so bring your own company if your looking for a fun time.

I can't say I was wowed by the food or service at Mom's Place. Both are pretty average. That is both are generally good. The food is fresh and the ingredients used are okay. There's nothing that stands out as exceptional. I'd characterize it as dependable. Good, but not great. And for Phoenixville, that's doing better than most.

The French toast is equivalent to what you'd make at home. The  Breakfast Burrito was fine, but I've had much better. Lunch is about the same, dependable, nothing exceptional. 

It's cash only (which I wonder if isn't counter-productive --it's the suburbs, so many don't carry much cash anymore). 

If you go you'll be fed well, you just won't leave raving about anything.

Heard good things about this place but was disappointed. I couldn't decided between a burrito, burrito bowl and a quesadilla and the cashier recommended the burrito bowl so that's what I got. There was a little bit of rice and beans at the bottom but the majority of the bowl was sour cream. The parking lot is pretty small but there was plenty of indoor seating and the service was fast. If I were to go back next time I would definitely try a burrito or quesadilla instead.

This is a small but super cute spot right off of south street. Both times I've visited the service there is so welcoming, accommodating, and polite! First time I just got bubble tea and the second time I tried some food. I got the passion fruit bubble tea both times though because it was so delicious 

For food I ordered veggie dumplings and the shrimp tempura tacos since they were recommended on the menu. Shrimp was crispy, and went well with the spicy Mayo and slaw. Would definitely order both items again! 

Both times I ordered at the counter and waited and they were super fast to prepare. I ordered a few drinks the second time because I was taking some to friends, and they even asked which one was mine so I could have it to drink while I waited for the rest of the order which I thought was sweet. They also have good specials a few times a week. Definitely a gem of a spot I'm going to continue going to because I'd love to keep trying their other menu items!

Disappointed with the food and not terribly impressed with the service. 

Pick somewhere else.
Reopened under new owners, I liked my cheese steak and fries, the cheese sauce with old bay in it is really good

Definitely returning to this place.  My first visit was with my co-workers and we had a lunchtime blast.

Enjoyed watching the chefs use the ingredients I had selected to create a fabulously flavorful meal.  The concept is not foreign, if you like the Benihana-style, but this place has 4 of those chefs whipping up meals on a circular table.  

Great food at a good price!
Exceptionally good food and service! I really enjoyed the experience.  Must have espresso! Seafood is out of the world.

This is really a place for beer drinkers not for foodies, but eventually you gotta eat. The food is okay, but not great; the service is better. The restaurant is nicely located in downtown. I also love a good deal, so when we end up here we make sure we have a discount either with the axxess card or other.

There is a trickster ghost here... I am not kidding!...nothing to be scared of.

S.O. and I were at Drake's last night for a friend's 40th, it's a good meet-up place. Sucks I didn't get to taste their burgers or sushi tho'.. we had a buffet earlier in the day and was still feeling a little full. I did like their frickles and tater tots, good snack food. Was having a great time with the gang until a few slightly inebriated older ladies decided we wanted to parteyy with them and kept coming over to chit chat.lol May try a less busy night

Wow! We showed up without any notice, at noon on Saturday,  ordered 25 burgers, 10 fries and 10 nuggets to feed a hungry team. The crew rocked! They had our order ready in record time!
We will be back!

Living in Safety Harbor, Brady's is one of my favorite local eateries. The ribs and pulled pork are flavorful. The brisket is tender and the spicy sausage has a great kick. Love their cole slaw. They have a very large selection of beer on tap and also some bottles.

This place is the best. Food was cooked with pride, ambience was perfect, away from the crowds of bourbon street. Great for dates, romantic. The owner Poppie sets this place apart. His staff is top notch. The food is out of this world. A must stop for good food in NO. dont settle for the tourist trap of bourbon. Plus the building is historic built in 1732 I believe.
This is s nice little place with great atmosphere and quaint bar with live music being played at piano bar. Fine dining but in a casual atmosphere. I'll be back!

This restaurant is very poor the food is below average for OCB standards not the it's suppose great food the place smells your feet stick to the carpet as you walk the tables and chairs are sticky and wobble the wait for the trays of food to be completely empty before the refresh the food I really think that someone needs to pay a visit to this place either shut it down or redo the entire establishment

Very good food. Mussels were great. Ocean sauce was awesome but too rich. Couldn't eat it after several bites. I was also full and I have trouble eating rich food when I am too full.
But cajun italian fusion mix was surprising and pleasant.
Highly recommend.

This is the best lunch I've had in St. Roch Market. The owner was super friendly. The bibimbap and shrimp spring rolls were delicious. I'm used to tofu and kimchi coming with my bibimbap, but be prepared to pay extra here. Portions were about right, but the spring rolls were a bit small for the price. Overall, I'd definitely recommend this place if you enjoy Korean food, or just want to try something new. I left feeling very satisfied.

This place has to be my favorite gyro restaurant in the Nashville area. What makes this place different is that they grill food to order, and don't just have it sitting there, steaming all day. In addition, it's clean, spacious, and reasonably-priced. You get a good amount of food for the money you pay. I'm lucky to work so close to it that I can come here during my lunch!

This past Sunday we walked into National Mechanics for a brunch 11 people, there was a wait  of an hour so the hostess offered their sister restaurant, Lucha Cartel, right down the street.  A group of 11 starving people were willing to try it out, what a mistake.  When we walked in the place was EMPTY, we should have turned around and left then.  There was a table open that could have accommodated us but they were going to make us wait for a 2 top to get up to seat us at a longer table.  Finally the decided to seat us at the open table. 

A few of us ordered a Bloody Mary and it was by far the worst I have ever, it tasted like poison.  We waited a good 40 minutes for our food, I get it, we were 11 people but like I said the restaurant was empty.  The food was terrible, the only things that were remotely OK were the quesadilla and the chicken sandwich (It is hard to mess up a quesadilla and chicken sandwich.)  My dish, the Huevos Veracruzano, was so horrible that I took two bites and refused to continue eating it.  The service was slow, it took entirely too long to get our check and then for the server to come back and pick it up.  

The entire experience was so bad my friends and I are still discussing it 24 hours later.  Needless to say, I will not be returning to Lucha Cartel and I would not recommend it to anyone.

Excellent British food.  Particularly enjoyed the scones, real jam and clotted cream, but also the full British breakfast.  Serve excellent tea.  Nice service.  Excellent location in the heart of Philly.  Great atmosphere and decor.  Only disappointment was the lack of British draft beers.  If I want canned Boddingtons I would got to Wegmans.  How about adding Fullers beers on tap.  Highly recommend if you are in Philly.
Food was amazing, I had the sweet and sour stir fry and my boyfriend had the garlic stir fry .. we've bee ate the chicken wings for app and the veggies egg rolls ... highly recommended

Normally I don't review chain restaurants but had to give a shout out to them for one of their menu specials this month. 
Don't get me wrong first watch is always a solid and somewhat healthyish breakfast lunch place & a go to for us.  But I was super impressed with their Bahn Mi Bowl they have available this month. It's a savory faro & I think quinoa mix as the base. On top are two sunny side up eggs & a drizzle of sriracha. On the side are the traditional pickled veggies (needed more of those) but the piece de resistance is the cubed & caramelized pork belly sautéed in a Chinese 5 spice sauce.  It's a knock out & I'm hoping they add it to the menu. The service those trip was excellent as well. I'd give it 5 stars but my mom's scrambled eggs & potatoes kinda sucked. For some reason they can't seem to get the yolks & whites mixed they come in clumps of separate yolks and egg whites...weird.
Sorry for the half eaten food photo but it took me a few bites to realize how good my bowls tasted;)

I am not sure what I can add.  The other reviewers have got this place nailed.  It's the fantastic, energetic, colorful little sister to the upscale (big) Cafe Poca Cosa.  The food, in my opinion, is as good, but the portions are more reasonable, and more reasonably priced.  If I could I would make it there for breakfast and lunch more frequently.

Do yourself a favor. DO NOT knee-jerk order an iced tea or water when you sit down.  Have one of the incredible freshly made juices that are on offer (last time I was there, it was a mango-lime), or the Coffee-chata (iced coffee with horchata).  They are the perfect complement to the tremendous food.  And, as I would recommend with the big Poca Cosa, live dangerously and get the Plato Poca Cosa so that you can be surprised by whatever amazing dishes appear on your plate.

I have never taken someone to this place for breakfast or lunch and had them be any less than amazed at its existence.

And if you're sensitive to the loudness inside: it's Arizona, sit on the patio.

I can only describe Goody Goody as good, not great. I heard such great things about how wonderful Goody Goody was back in the day, but it just didn't live up to the hype. I will say the actual restaurant is beautiful, they did such a great job with it, so it's a shame the food isn't up to par.

If you're trying to decide between lunch or breakfast, go with breakfast. I really love their Hangover breakfast and their omelets are massive. While they're known for hamburgers, the POX burger with the special sauce is a let-down, it's a tomato based sauce which just swallows uthe whole burger. Doesn't taste any different than a McDonald's burger. Skip the fries and go with the onion rings, they're pretty good and the sauce that comes with them is excellent. I've had their Patty Melt too which was just okay, the bread was good though. But, definitely save room for dessert, their pies are amazing. 

As other reviews mention, the service is not great. The last time we dined here we were practically rushed out of the restaurant from the moment we ordered to the moment we got our check. Pass on the burgers, but definitely check out the breakfast and pie.

A great spot for dinner that's casual, yet nice and has great service and food. I stopped in with my boyfriend on a Saturday night around 730pm and although there were lots of tables available, we sat at the bar.  That have a really great menu (that's in a fun 'portfolio') and we opted for the white cheddar mac and cheese and biscuits appetizer.  The biscuits come in a set of 3 and they're served like sliders with pulled pork and chow chow.  Absolutely delish.  The bartender was super nice and I'm really glad we stopped in.

This is my go to place when I want something gourmet. I've never had something here I didn't like. The only down side is the service is honestly terrible. I feel a "you're wasting my time vibe from the cashiers and it makes me sad that for such a great place with history, the staff acts as though they couldn't care less.
It was amazing. The Nashville hot Flounder sandwich was great. The Groper and fries were good as well. Came hot and ready. I will be back for sure

Very impressive new entry on the ever expanding Oak Street scene of cafes, restaurants, shops and general funky places. While housed in a historic building DTB is its own self, respectful of Creole cooking but not afraid to chart its own culinary course.

In honor of the Tricentennial go for the Louisiana cocktail, a tasty riff off a Sazerac rye. For a darker taste the brown sugar Old Fashioned was surprisingly good and not as sweet as it sounds.

We did a mix of small plates and entrees. Thumbs up for the fried cornbread--a bit of heat, lots of crunch. The gumbo is dark and favorable--a wonderful roux that includes the chef's potato salad rather than rice. Sounds a bit odd I know but try it--it really balances the roux. The salad is fresh fresh and highlighted with bits of cheese, bacon, spices--light yet filling.

I believe I would order the Louisiana Rice Bowl every time I come here--everything about the dish, from the browned rice, the Tasso and the grilled shrimp. Just a perfect new Creole dish.

The dessert choices are limited but excellent: creative, beautiful presentation. The strawberry shortcake sounds boring but not here--do it: like many items the inventive approach just stands out. This place is close to a 5 but in New Orleans that's a tough number to reach.

There's so much you can say about a bridge but I will keep it brief.  

If the sun is out, you will probably be stuck in traffic coming into Tampa, you may get lucky early on the weekend.  The bridge dumps into a bottleneck and the exit only lanes seem to create accidents as people change lanes to avoid taking the exit.  

Going to Saint Pete, you are usually ok and won't be slowing down by much unless there's a major accident.  You may also get trapped in some delays if the weather is nice and people are heading to the beach.

As far as bridges go, this is a nice looking bridge, nothing too fancy, just that classic "bridge" look.  The best part of the Howard Frankland is the beautiful view of the bay as you cross (just don't look too much while you drive it).
I got undercooked sausage here and thought the service was generally poor. The rest of the food we had was mediocre too. Not a terribly nice place inside either tbh.

This bar is a very neat spot! The staff was very friendly and kind and the drinks were strong. The decor was awesome, very colorful. I didn't expect this bar to essentially be in a parking lot at the top of a hill, but there's a fence all around it which makes it feel more private. There is an unmarked parking lot up there street with plenty of spots. I hope to go back soon to try their food!

A friend and I decided on Wednesday morning brunch in order to catch up and unwind post-holiday. I'd passed Morning Glory a number of times while in the neighborhood, but hadn't ever eaten there.

I like the vibe - it felt much less pretentious than in Sabrina's where I feel out of place with only one tattoo and feet not shod in Converse.
