I have to say that I wouldn't attempt to eat here with your 10 best friends, though, as space is an issue. There was no wait when we arrived at 10am, but I was surprised at how quickly the place filled up on a Wednesday in January - does no one work these days? This also isn't  place where you can linger over a cup of coffee for hours given said lack of space. The staff will probably appreciate you much more if you pay your check in a timely manner and vamoose if there are people waiting.

That being said, my Irish oatmeal was lovely. I was grateful that it wasn't soupy, but just right. Baby Bear would have approved. It was topped with a generous helping of strawberries, bananas, and blueberries. I also ordered a side of turkey sausage which was delicious and fork-tender. Few people probably care about this, but I found it charming that they serve their coffee in large tin mugs instead of the usual white ceramic stuff. My friend ordered a hearty portion of eggs, turkey sausage, and biscuit - which looked thoroughly delicious, but equally taxing on one's gallbladder. Maybe I'll for it next time, when I'm not contending with post-holiday pudge. 

The staff was great and quick with the coffee refills.

Yes, this is a yuppy, hipster sandwich place that at first made me want to roll my eyes, but they have damn good, huge tasty sandwiches.  My husband loved the sardine sandwich.  Hard to find one these days.  Lots of meat choices, and veggie choices too.  Plus they have free bubbly water on tap, serve yourself.  (Why can't all restaurants have this?  Love it!)  Their sides were way over priced and did not look entirely appetizing.  Otherwise, I would have given this place 4-star.
Love the nachos.  Haven't had a bad sandwich there either.  Great place for lunch and dinner both.

Federal donuts is awesome (period).

This place never has wings, so while I wish I could try, and thus comment on them, they are always sold out by the time we get there. 

If you have not tried their chicken you are missing out.

I have driven by this place for the last 5 years and figured I'd finally give it a try. I was really excited for a nice Italian meal but wasn't blown away. 

The place was not packed when my party arrived and we were seated immediately. The sun was shining in directly on the tables and it didn't look like the cleanliest of restaurants. The chairs were also too short for the table? It was weird. 

I ended up with a bowl of capellini and marinara and the stuffed eggplant. My friend ordered shrimp penne in vodka sauce. He had no complaints  about his meal. I, however, didn't enjoy my meal as much as I'd hoped to. The meals were large in size and both my friend and i ended up leaving with leftovers. The sauce didn't have any kind of seasoning or flavor. It was also super chunky and I personally don't like chunky sauce so if you're like me stay away from the marinara here. The pricing was a little high for the quality of the food. 

Pasta Pomodoro was just ok.

I was disappointed after dining at Juicy Lucy's.  I am vegetarian and was so excited to get the veggie burger.  I have eaten tons of veggie burgers and I knew right away it was a frozen patty made by Morningstar.  This is the same burger vegetarians can get a Burger King (and its not 10 dollars).  My boyfriend got a regular burger and he said it was very good.  All and all I would not go back nor recommend veggie eaters but carnivores may love it.

Well, I had an akward experience. 

I was expecting sushi and basic bitch food. 
The outside was pretty, looked good so I went in with my friend Blair. 
She ate there and said to trust her, I'm like whatever. 
I was really hung over. 
So I thought the best thing would be to have more alcohol. 
I got a martini and there wasn't olives 
It was a mini corn on the cob! I said "oh god" 
Fancy shit! 
The drink was good. Our server was this guy, he looked like the guy from The Outsiders, the hot one. 
He asked if I wanted another 
I said no, I wanna try another awesome drink. 
But it looked like a margarita glass dipped in a mixture of dirt and cigarette ashes. 
More fancy shit. It was pepper! 

My friend ordered these crazy raw fish rolls that were decorated like we were in The Hamptons, or those places in Aspen where it's too pretty 
I couldn't find my phone or my fork. 
I thought it was in the car- whole time- it was in my bra. 
This sushi lounge wasn't an all you can eat, or a 50% off roll where you go for a quick bite. 
I didn't find my reading glasses but I told my friend and the server, "I'm racist against onions and peppers"

Their drinks were Asian fusion just like the food. 
I couldn't find the fork cause they gave me chopsticks and I didn't eat. 

I'm not too adventurous with raw fish, so Pony Boy recommended I have green tea and ramen. 
It was nice, but the steam from the soup was making my nasal passages drip. I just got my nose redone for the 2nd time a couple weeks ago. 

My friend knew the menu and when I took a piece of her 3 rolls they were done nicely.
Too much for me. I was impressed that I managed to use the chopsticks. I was so hung over that I had mascara running down my eyes. 
I looked like Courtney Love. But I had sunglasses and a scarf covering up a stain on my shirt. 
Plus I was carrying a LV bag, so I looked classy and very West Hollywood chic. 

This isn't the kind of place id be able to order from on my own, all raw fish tastes the same to me. 

I think my server, Soda Pop Curtis or whatever his name was cut me off! I wasn't drunk at the restaurant, I was drinking the night before. 
I should have showered and did my hair but I didn't know we were going someplace that nice. 
It was Las Vegas nice. Better than Nobu! 
I was a bit surprised and I wanted Mexican! Ha! 

My tip is either go with a sushi lover, who knows how to order, this is the kind of place you want to impress someone. 

I used the bathroom 3 times. It was clean
Pretty sinks. The seat was comfortable. 
Definite recommend a trip to the rest room. 
The bar stools were so nice. 
And they have the fried soy paper. 
I got Dallas Winston to give me some to go. 

Good salad, colourful, but I smelt onion so left that to her. 
We skipped dessert. 
I left my credit card, but they came out and said "man! You left your credit card!"
I was like "man!!! Do I look like a man to you?" And I whipped off my scarf like a feather boa. 
And he said "ma'am" and starts laughing 
My friend laughs with him
And I'm like Really?! -so I'm old now. 

That was fun.

Order some food from here through Uber eats on Monday night. Two bowls of tortilla soup, one with chicken, and a side of the there choriqeuso. Soup was decent, not worth $8-$10 a bowl but good. One bite of the queso and the rest was thrown away.
Great green curry! The buffet is nice as well... Other dishes I've had have turned out a bit on the sweet side. But you cannot go wrong with the green curry.

So the atmosphere is very romantic and the aquarium is beautiful, unfortunately the food was pretty bad. I ordered the charcuterie board which consisted of only 2 kinds of cheese,one a cheddar the other a huge pile of blue cheese. And only 2 types of meat, one was hard salami and the other a disgusting bologna type head cheese.... really gross, and only a few small crostini's. Overall very sad spread. For dinner I ordered the 2 lobster tail which had only about 2 bites of meat per tail TINY!!! The potatoes were dry and tasteless And $45!!!! Crazy. 

My poor husband ordered fish dip appetizer which had no flavor and for main course he ordered the lobster ravioli. Never in our lives have we ever had such bland food. I don't even know how you can mess lobster ravioli up! We were extremely unsatisfied and disappointed in this restaurant.

Absolutely delicious, from the flavorful hummus selection to each of the shareable plates. The wines were also quite good and overall amazing price for the spectacular service and food. Definitely worth all the hype and we would revisit again.
I dream of the Wild Boar Bolognese and the Rabbit entree. Well done with fantastic cocktails!

Sampan = a perfect happy hour destination offered every day of the week!! 

The good: Some friends and I wanted to meet up in center city and catch up and Sampan was perfect for that occasion. We got the chicken bao bun, kimchee fried rice, and the short rib chow fun. I personally enjoyed the chicken bao bun. It was slightly spicy, but very flavorful with the only drawback being I ate it to fast xD. The kimchee fried rice is a nice staple, but nothing that really surprised me. For happy hour, you typically sit at the bar which gives you a nice view of the kitchen, which I appreciated. It's also a nice place where you can show up casual or slightly dressy and not stand out. 

The bad: The wait can be long if you come on a busy day during happy hour. The happy hour menu isn't super exhaustive, but you definitely can swing by a few times before feeling like you've had the entire menu.
First time in New Orleans so if course I was looking for authentic LA food. Found it!! The place is small and parking is not good but it was worth it. I will be back.

A great place for brunch. I had the Egg's Benedict and a short stack of pancakes. Delicious. The hashbrown's were very tasty too. Service was fast and friendly. I'll definitely go back next time I'm in Reno.

Aimee Olexy and Stephen Starr must not have gotten the news that people like to relax and converse over their food or that people don't like excruciating noise. This one is louder than Jones, Buddakon, and Talulah's Garden. I don't care how good the food is -- and it was fairly good here -- I will not return to a restaurant that is deafening. Are you trying to turn the tables over faster or just clueless. I was here at the invitation of a friend last night and couldn't wait to leave. Having said that, the decor is quite nice. Too bad I couldn't spend more time enjoying it.

Ordered for the third time from Waitr today to celebrate Pi day with pie! In the past we have tried several of fry dishes. These are fresh cut fries with lots of fresh, interesting flavor combinations. They are good. 

The pies, however, are the real stars. These are little pies in unique flavor combos. Today to celebrate Pi day we tried the Woozy Suzy (dark cherry with a hint of amaretto in a graham cracker crust, the El Chapo...dig it (Carmel cream in a chocolate crumb crust), and the red eye (coffee custard in a chocolate crumb crust. All were topped with fresh whipped cream and garnished to match the pie. They were all good but the El Chapo was hands down our favorite. We rate it a perfect Pi score of 3.14!

My boyfriend and I have only been to this restaurant twice and I've enjoyed both instances. The place is clean, the service was efficient, and they serve a lot of appetizers while you wait for your meal. I have ordered the rice, vegetables and beef in sizzling bowl twice but I loved their rice and eel in sizzling bowl (which my boyfriend had). I can't wait to try their other dishes! :)

Food tasted okay while we were eating it, but within an hour after eating, both my husband and I had diahhrea....we were fine before we arrived, and both had the same results. Called the restaurant, and they called us back; said we couldn't have possibly gotten ill from their meal because that would have to take 8 hours to hit, and we would have to be vomiting. That's ridiculous for them to make that medical assertion and show such a lack of concern. 

I note another review noting their partner got ill as well....so maybe they do not keep their sushi cold enough on ice or have other food sitting out picking up bacteria. Who knows, but it wasn't up to snuff as far as I'm concerned.

I've been reading the reviews (just curious) and would like to share my imput. I've been going to the Hard Rock for many years and have been to many other casinos nationwide. The HR is a great place to unwind, people watch, and have their delicious steaks at Oak Council, they're the best in Florida, bar none. There have been changes and as explained to me by a former host, the valet parking went from $5.00 to $20.00 in January. This did not make me a happy camper. After being ticked off at the casino, I today learned that the valet packing is sub-contracted and they have no decision in what their contractor charges for the valet parking. Also, you used to be able to use your comp dollars at the food court and can no longer do so, as they are also sub-contracted out.
The Plum Lounge was one of my favorite places to sit back and relax after many hours of playing, and since I usually come alone (widowed), I didn't want to go to a restaurant and eat by myself. This is now set aside for the elite players and no one else. That is something management needs to reconsider. If I'm going to drop $3000 to $5000 bucks, I think I deserve a little more consideration. The servers are losing out on my $20 tips, too!
Paying for drinks. Okay, if you play the High Limit slots you'll receive drinks on the house. I play High Limit slots and have no problem with it until I go to a different area and play $3.00 a spin. In my personal opinion, if it counts, anyone gaming should be getting free drinks while gaming. Give the server a tip, always. If your not gambling, then no, you shouldn't be getting free drinks
The hotel rooms are superb and I enjoy staying the weekend. If you're looking to go somewhere nice and spend a couple of nights, this is all in all, a great place. I just hope someone in management takes my personal opinions to the powers that be, give a rebate on valet parking for great players and free drinks for those who are actively gaming. This will induce players to skip going to Biloxi and Vegas, and keep our gaming in Florida.

Terrible customer service!!!! Very rude staff, and the management doesn't respond to problems after many emails/calls! 
They got my order wrong, charged me for an extra pizza and when I called they kept bouncing me around to call different numbers, send an email to the manager and call the delivery service. After 3 months, still haven't got my money back.
Best steaks in town! Great people, great service! Friendly atmosphere and smoke free! Grilled chicken is awesome and The Tubby Burger is one of my favorites. It a must go to restaurant'

I come to Denny's often and the food is always good as well as the service. I come late night right after the bars close. I have a Town Car Service so its fits in perfectly. My favorite server is Matia. She's the best. Matia always greets me with a smile and knows exactly want I want all the time. She is a TEAM player and a Five Star server. I also like to recognize two other individuals and they are Joe McFadden (manager) and David Buchanan (chef). Both of them are a great team together. When I walk in I enjoy having David prepare my meal for me. He has that special touch. Joe is also a good chef and a great manager. So when you come into Denny's ask for Matia and make sure that David or Joe is there to cook for you. You will not be disappointed. Tell him that DAN THE CAB MAN sent you.
So good!!! Had a great selection of sushi. I get nervous trying buffet sushi but it was nice and fresh. All of their food was nice and warm... better than most.

We had lunch here on Mother's day and were not disappointed.  This place is a gem we were so happy to find.  Family-owned and run, and very kid-friendly.  For starters, they gave my daughter a little dough ball to play with while waiting for our food, which was incredibly thoughtful.  Everything we had was delicious.  I had a seafood fra diavlo with shrimp, clams, mussels, and calamari, that my 8 year old devoured.  My husband had the slow-cooked chianti marinara (which was out of this world) with meatballs.  They were able to accommodate my vegetarian niece and make a non-vegetarian dish vegetarian for her.  The creamy pesto was my favorite.  I normally do not like alfredo or cream sauces, but this one I loved.  It was not overly creamy, and the pesto flavor was spot on.  The clam chowder was great, and the pizza was also delicious.  Our favorite appetizer was the fried calamari, which was not greasy.  It had a light crispy breading, and was served with a sweet and sourish sauce that almost tasted a little asian.  Everyone loved it.  

We got there at a time that was not overly busy, so they let our daughter make her plain cheese pizza (at an empty table, not in the kitchen).  It was such a great experience.  They let us go back to see where the pizza goes, and got a quick tour of part of the kitchen.  We got to see the huge mixer making dough, and the walk-in refrigerator where we saw everything measured out and labeled.  We saw containers of chicken stock with pieces of chicken floating in it that was REAL stock.  We started asking questions, and learned that all of their ingredients are fresh and real, and their cheese comes from Wisconsin.  They also have gluten free pizza crust made with brown rice, honey, and water.  They told us they do a complete wipe down of the area and cook the GF pizzas in a separate oven.  Everything was so clean and organized back there.  I was very impressed.

The only thing I regret is not trying the salads.  We had ordered so many appetizers and had so much food, we completely forgot about the salad. We were so full that we could barely eat desert.  My husband loved the cannolis, and I really enjoyed the tiramisu.  However, everyone agreed their cheesecakes are the clear winner...and I thought I didn't like cheesecake!  

We will definitely be back.  The food was very good, but the excellent service and how much these owners care about their customers is truly priceless.
Best BBQ ever!!! Everything on the menu is delicious you can never go wrong with Nola Q!!

If there was one word to describe eating here, it would be uncomfortable. Don't get me wrong, the food's great, but the service was so bad my friend and I considered skipping out on the check just to avoid another painfully awkward interaction with the waitstaff. It was honestly some of the worst service I'd ever seen; no one knew what they were doing. It would have been funny if it wasn't so creepy.

When we got in, we tried to figure out whether we should wait for a table, go sit down, or order from the counter. We chose to sit down. My friend flagged down the waiter. I ordered samosas, a side of palak paneer, and naan - just enough for one person - and then the waiter walked off. My friend was sitting there, openmouthed, waiting for the waiter to come back. He did, to drop off the samosas, and then ran away. We finally flagged down another waiter, but his English was terrible - my friend said "I want to order" and he asked her if she wanted a bottle of water. It took another 5 minutes for him to comprehend that she wanted a veggie platter and I wanted to know if I should get my soda out of the case or wait for someone to bring it to me.

The food was amazing; I think the Yelp reviews and Craig LaBan have made that very clear. But the experience was greatly diminished by the fact that the servers couldn't stop staring at me and my friend. Strangely, we had a really hard time getting their attention when we actually needed them, since it took 10 minutes just to get to-go boxes and the servers would barely talk to us or look at us.

Come for the samosas, stay for the horrible service (and objectification, if you're female).

Also, they had the entire place shut down by 11:15 and it's supposed to be open until midnight. We left around 11:20 and saw 4 people who were turned away because they'd already cleared out the steam trays. If you're going to do that, close at 11.

Edit: My friend reminded me that there was a huge puddle of water (as in 2-3 feet wide and half an inch deep) near the entrance from a leaking pipe. In retrospect, we should have left right then.
The bartenders were rude, ignored you if you weren't a local and the place is dark. Save yourself and go elsewhere.
Best ribs I have ever eaten! Smoked for 48hrs. You can't even pick them up by the bone because the fall off! Manager Carmen is the most amazing, fun hostess! Go here!

Despite what the yelp page says from the business, the staff does not wear masks. Upon arrival, we were greeted outdoors by someone who wasn't wearing a mask, however with no distinguishable uniform or name tag, we thought it was just a patron being friendly. We were outdoors so it wasn't a big deal that he wasn't wearing a mask. 
   We were seated indoors, and noticed that the indoor space is quite small. Not more than six tables in a very small space sharing a full length bar. Ambiance was upscale and decorated quite nicely. We sat down and looked around and saw that no one on staff was wearing a mask in such a small intimate space. We were greeted by our waitress who was lovely and friendly. However, you guessed it, no mask. This gave us pause. Every staff member we saw in the front of the house was not wearing a mask despite still being in a pandemic with a very aggressive strain. So if the front of the house wasn't taking this virus serious, we can only imagine that the cooking staff were unmasked as well. 
    Unfortunately we didn't have a chance to try the food because the risk was too high of a price for us to take if the establishment and its staff choose to not wear a mask.

We ate dinner here and enjoyed ourselves. I had the pork tacos, which were good, and the amber house beer, which was also good. Can't say the food or beer was super exciting, but I wouldn't slight them for that. Fun atmosphere and even though they were busy, the service was prompt.

A little underwhelmed.  We ordered dumplings and they were good, probably the best thing on the menu. Everything else, papaya salad and skewers, were very much so-so and way overpriced. Service was ok, a would say it was a little slow. We also got a dessert and I was not impressed with it's quality at all.
Carne Asada tacos were so so good. Honestly some of the best I have ever had. I wanted to order an endless supply and sleep in a pile of them
One of our favorite breakfast places. Great Mexican breakfast food. I came here because I was craving chilaquiles and Cappy's came up when I searched for chilaquiles in Tucson. Recommend!
Their takeout chicken tikka masala was delicious. It's the best I've tried in the area. It's a little pricey. The decor looks minimalistic but nice. I'll try it out soon.
Party of six with every person raving about the good taste and service. Four stars because no one can meet my standards. I will go back

I don't see why this place has such good reviews. The food is just ok, not great, not memorable, just ok. No one at my table loved their food, it was just average tasting BBQ but an above average price point. I've been twice & both times my dishes were just meh. 

On my last trip my brisket was really dry & the sauce was way too sweet. The sides were decent & service was average. I seriously doubt I'll ever be back. It's just a bit too much for the quality of food I was given.
Had tasted it before for brought-in lunch at work but this was first time trying it in-person. Great pizza, tremendous service. Definitely coming back.

First visit I had the fried soft shell crab, second visit I had the Jambalaya, both times I had the Jalapeño Martini in Mason Jars, both times I got buzzed, both times I licked my plate, both times I ordered more jalapeños, both times I left happy, full, and service was so friendly. I can't wait for my next visit to wine country and end up here for great Cajun food. BTW there are tiles of naked people on bathroom walls :)

How can they be picky about not substituting menu items but not picky about following my order.

Eggs over medium.  Simple right? Nope runny.

Cinnamon roll...a day old.  Also, add some cinnamon too it. 

Sausage sampler.  Barely warm. Sent them back. 

Pancakes were good.  Fruit? Not ripe.

Also, men's restroom has a sign that says if you pee on the seat wipe it off...no! How bout you clean your restroom.

In a city of amazing food, Chophouse just doesn't make the cut. 

My partner wanted a break from seafood, so we decided to give this place a try based on Yelp reviews. 

Let's start with the good:  You can make reservations online which I always appreciate to avoid waits. The service was relatively smooth and all the staff was friendly and helpful. Oh, and the loaded baked potato was AMAZING! I'm always surprised how difficult it is for restaurants to make a baked potato, but they could take lessons from Chophouse. Crispy skin, hot potato, and truly loaded with toppings.

However, our main course, the bone-in ribeyes, were a true disappointment. All good ribeyes are nicely marbled with fat, but both my partner and I had more fat than meat on ours. With all that fat and a nice char, I was expected it to be full of flavor; instead, it tasted like...well... nothing. I've had $20 steak from the grocery store with more flavor. 

Overall, a very disappointing visit.

They will be closed in a few months. Came for my daughters birthday as she had a great time at the center city location a couple years back. The evening started off with the looks from other customers as we came through the door with 3 younger girls like we are dining at a steakhouse with an intimate setting..come on now. We were seated and everything started off great but then our server forgot to bring our drinks, waters and sodas. I asked twice in a 20 minute period about them, and nothing. I ended up going to the bar and getting them myself. Strike 1. As the food started coming out, the waiter brought the drinks with the food and never asked about the ones at the table! Whatever. The cheese fondue was going well up until the pots started burning/smoking on the table. 3 waiters/waitresses come out of nowhere and start removing the pots and switching them out with new ones. While doing so, they take our bread and some of the veggies in the process and never return them to the table. Great, I hope everyone had enough cheese fondue. To top it off they only brought back 2 of the three cheese pots. Strike 2. We are now almost 2 hours into our dinner before realizing our waiter never took the entree order. After taking it, that at least came out in a timely manner. I was talking to the other waitresses off and on and they were saying it was extremely busy that night and they were having a difficult time keeping up. The philly location was twice as busy on a Friday night and their waiters had waaaay more experience! Our waiter never came back to ask about refills or just to check in. As the dessert was coming out I couldn't help to sum up our experience...bad seating, mediocre service, and what seemed to be a staff lacking experience. Strike 3. The manager took money off the bill after I asked. In which her response was, "oh yea we were already thinking about that." No questions and no concerns as to why. So, to sum it up, 3 and half hours for decent food, but a bad experience, bad service and lax attitudes...overpriced! I'm afraid to say the melting pot just might melt away from that location.
Ordered cheese pizza, extra cheese. The worst I've had.  Crust was way too soft.  Horrible!  Don't get the pizza!

The owner is nice and the place has a great atmosphere, but you have to be a smoker to enjoy this one. Non smokers wouldn't last 5 minutes in this place even if there wasn't anyone smoking at the time. 

I love the decor and the live music that they bring in, but I can't go anymore because I can't deal with the smoke smell. It's worse then league night in a bowling alley.

The night started off arriving at the restaurant and approaching the hostess and we asked her for a table for four. Our friends weren't there yet, but we asked to be seated. She rudely let us know that they do not seat separate groups. She sat us anyway. Our friends arrived no more than 5 min. later. 
Secondly, we started to order drinks and when they came out, my friends wine glass was only filled to four ounces. We asked why it wasn't six ounces, which is standard, and again we received a rude reply. Not cool. 
Also the waiter guy came out and spilled soup on me and did not offer me anything to clean it up let alone an apology. 
The food was small portioned and not very good.

Needless to say we will never come back and not to mention we know a very large abundance of people that we share our experiences with. So they won't try hit out either!!!!

I went for Sunday brunch. The service was terrible. They told us it would be a ten minute wait. We waited at least 30 minutes before we could sit down. When we finally got our table, they ignored us for a while and even served people who came in after us first. Something as simple as water, they failed to bring to us until we asked twice. We spent over 2 hours there in all. The quiche (Mushroom and Caramelized Onion & Roasted Vegetables) were pretty good, but it may have been the hunger talking after waiting such a long time. I imagine that getting frozen quiche from the grocery store would taste about the same as what we had though. Pumpkin lattes weren't bad. The waitresses couldn't even answer basic questions. They gave my cousin my food and gave my food to her, even after examining it to double check. The person who makes the lattes has never even tried them and couldn't give suggestions. My main complaint was the service. For that reason alone, I probably will not return.
I had the gumbo and Catfish Treme. Omg it was sooooo good. The sauce on the catfish Treme was absolutely delicious!! Great taste, great presentation, fresh food.

Love it!!!

I happen to visit this place for breakfast on a Sunday. Super busy time for them. It took us 20-30 mins to get a seat. Our server was very nice and friendly. The ambience is good. Everything has an egg-theme for sure, may it be paintings, wall design or your salt and pepper bottle on table. Everything inside has 'wild egg' theme and is bright and clean. 

I went ahead and got myself a 'surfer girl' omelet which has 'fresh spinach, wild mushrooms, tomato, cream cheese and onion, topped with diced fresh avocado, pico de gallo, sour cream and fresh alfalfa sprouts' with a blueberry muffin on side:) It was very filling and tasty. 

My boyfriend ordered 'Mexico City Maria's Chilaquiles' which is 'mexican-style breakfast casserole with corn tortillas, refried beans, salsa verde, queso blanco and a sunny side up egg. Served with skillet potatoes and a shot of jugo de limon y chile'. And can I just say, this is DEFINITELY THE BEST breakfast I tasted EVER in my life. My surfer girl omelet was nothing compared to the chilaquiles. I had my first bite of it from my bf's plate and I was in HEAVEN. I loved loved loved this dish. So many amazing flavors. DELICIOUS. WOW.

If this is your first time or if you are a regular and haven't tried the Chilaquiles. Please do so ASAP. You can thank me (or my bf) later :P Hahhahahaa. I can't wait to go back and order myself the whole plate of chilaquiles.

I think they got a new cook! The food about a year ago was getting bad but, now as of 2018, it is really good and back to what I expect. The lobster was a little rubbery but, its hard not to over cook, other than that great.

Great food, first time going there and i was very impressed. Waitress was amazing very personable. Food was amazing and hugeeeeeeeee portions. I was upset they ran out of their cornbread i was really wanting to try it. Only thing that i was uneasy about was the staff dusting around our table and food... he was dusting the light fixtures and everything over the tables that had place settings already so that made me feel a little unsanitary.

What a find!  Make reservations especially for the weekend.  Food surprisingly good.  Portions VERY big.  Service a little slow, but waitstaff very warm and gracious.  Appetizers unnecessary.  I ordered a seafood salad - enough for two.  Beef and lamb gyro platters - ordered by 2 - was awfully big.  Quite tasty.  Ditto the chicken gyro platter.  Moussaka 5" sq was atypically prepared.  Waffled in my estimates.  BYOB. Worth while making the trek.  Lansdale much different than I remembered.  Charming town.

This location of Frothy Monkey has used records and (not used) books. Shop while you drink your coffee! Then wander over to Grimey's for even more shopping. (We only had coffee while we shopped, but they have food as well.)
Clean, hipster-y, and serving up delicious cold brew. The guest shawls were a bit too twee for us, but overall, this was a great place to read a book and enjoy coffee and a muffin.

My party of 5 stopped here yesterday for a birthday dinner. We were greeted by a friendly hostess and seated immediately even though only 3 of us were there.  We unknowingly made our reservation for 8 with the restaurant closing at 9.  

Service: The waiter "Matt" was very nice and checked in on us frequently while we were waiting for the rest of our party to arrive and throughout he whole meal. He was very attentive-constantly asking if we needed anything. 

Our dinner carried on past 9 PM and not once did they make us feel rushed to finish.

Food:  the portions were very big unlike typical tapas restaurants. I ordered the charcuterie tray, baked brie, poutine and mini chicken cutlets.  They were all very good but my favorite was the baked Brie platter.  It was loaded with fruit, jam and nuts which paired perfectly together.  

The dessert menu was limited and only features cupcakes or cheesecake.  There were about 6-7 cupcake options like Oreo, peanut butter cup and strawberry shortcake. I ordered the apple crumb which was basically a vanilla cupcake with apple crumb pie on top but it was very tasty.

BYOB: it's byob here so bring your drink of choice

I hope to visit again soon!

In a section of the city with so few places to eat, let alone cafes, I'm so psyched to have Batter & Crumbs in our neighborhood. I'm not vegan, just lactose intolerant, but it's awesome to not be concerned about the dairy content of anything in the shop. Our order consisted of an Iced Pumpkin Spice Latte, an Iced Lavender Vanilla Latte, and a S'mores Bar. I remember having vegan desserts in the past that were dry and crumbly, that is not the case here, I'd never have imagined that the S'mores Bar was vegan. The chocolate and marshmallows were delicious, and the cake itself was moist and had perfect texture. The coffees were also excellent. You can taste that alternative milk was used, but the drinks were made really nicely and mixed perfectly. Our favorite was the Lavender Vanilla, which was recommended by the barista, the flavors worked so perfectly together and they were really refreshing in an iced drink. The Pumpkin Spice was good, but we felt that it would have been better as a hot drink. 

Overall, I'm looking forward to making Batter & Crumbs a place I visit regularly. There are so many great looking pastries in their case, I'm going to have to slowly try them all. They also had a selection of sandwiches and other savory foods that they'd heat up for you, which I'll also have to try in the future. The staff was super friendly and helpful, and showed real love for the food and drinks they were serving. The cafe itself has a really nice, modern atmosphere that was relaxing on a Saturday afternoon. Simply put, I loved our little coffee break at Batter & Crumbs and I'm already looking forward to going back.

Watch Out!  Antioch Location:  Food poisoning from spinach enchiladas. Very sick for 2 days. When I called them they wanted to know why I did not call sooner!!!!!   Well ..... because I had food poisoning!!!  
Will never go back. Tooooo bad, at one time this was my favorite place to eat.  Times change....must move on.  Again, Watch Out!!!!

Happy chopped steak.  Cheese (whiz) on bottom, places like Pat's put it on the top.    Lots of big chunky onions (not finely cut) it'll get messy i think.   Restrooms inside, you talk to the chef cooking.  There's other choices too, including meatless option (my wife got it)   What's with this Cash Only thing in Philly? 

One thing - 8 or 9 dollar sandwich, i should be stuffed by the end right?  I wasn't, and i'm not that big of a guy.   But, that's sort of what the other guys do also.

PS don't bother with the bell peppers and mushrooms and pizza sauce, just get the onions, and cheese whiz and a hotpepper on the side.

This Chili's has really improved so I have to give this location 4 stars.  Their portions got a tad better and the food tastes much better than it did.  I don't know what changed but it's working.  

The 2 for $25 has been nice and their chili cheese burger for 10 bucks is a bargain down here.

This is the best Mexican restaurant I have ever been to..  The whole experience is quite extraordinary. The service was very friendly and the food excellent. We ordered the California burrito in dinner size. Very pleased. But perhaps the most intriguing part of the experience was the large and beautiful original art that covered every wall of the place.. I was told the art all came from Mexico. It makes you feel like your in a museum where they serve food! The price is also reasonable. Glad to be the first to get to rate this place and they did quite the job to deserve 5 stars.

Make sure you come here with an empty stomach. Woah what a delicious "not yo momma's grilled cheese" sandwich. I got the Seoul Brother, my husband got the Chuck Norris and my little dude got the famous Mac N' Rib. All super delicious, although I have to say mine was my favorite. Super delicious flavors and a huge portion. Staff was friendly and place was clean. Couldn't ask for more.
This place is phenomenal! Great burgers and the chicken sandwich too. Also love the dirty martinis!

Very awful service and very awful food.  Unfortunately for Fox and Hound almost all bars are stepping their game up when it comes to food.  To have greasy wings and limp fries because you are drinking is not appropriate anymore.  Someone please send them the message.  The drinks, as one Yelper noted, are watered down and not well made.  They need to step their game up, literally.

Pretty nice, definitely lives up to what us Philadelphians were expecting.
Music was a little "adult contempo pop" at moments, but besides that...over the top beautiful, but the music didn't match.

Attended the Wednesday Jazz event - very disappointed! Received several text to arrive early for seating - when we arrived it was half empty. The Jazz duo played 2 songs then sat with friends to eat and drink : food was good but not what we were expecting
Beautiful hotel! Love the atriums! Paradise!!!

I have enjoyed going here for years.  I remember when the main entrance was on the Olive Street side of the building.  Previous trips have always had great results.  Today I stopped in at about 2pm on a week day.  Employees outnumbered the guests but the service was very poor.  When my chicken fajita came out the chicken seemed very dry as if it had been sitting on the grill for hours.  I asked for additional salsa when my food was delivered and it was not brought.  As my drink got empty it was not refilled.  I finally went to the servers area where three of them were chatting and asked for a drink refill and salsa.  I did receive more attention after that but this is not my favorite way to start a dining out experience.  In previous trips here I left a $20 tip that exceeded the check amount.  I appreciate good service and recognize it, but this trip was not what I expected.  The server was one that has been here for years.  My advise would be to get a young or male server that may try harder and not a relic of the past.

We had a wonderful breakfast and experience here at Criollo!! We first of all
Loved the Hotel Monteleone and then had breakfast one morning at Criollo.  Our waitress Deanna was exceptional. She was just delightful, kind and was super attentive to our needs. We were impressed with her professionalism as well. Her helper( not an expo, but the water guy?) Michael was helpful and wonderful as well.  Just a super nice group of wait staff.  We will eat there again when back in town !

I went to Pappy's yesterday for the first time (ever) during lunch.  We had to wait in line in a hallway for about 10 minutes before they would let us wait in line...again...in the establishment.  Total wait was about 20 minutes from first in line to ordering at the window.

Nearly everyone around me was ordering ribs...which looked fantastic, but since I was with clients I decided to get something a little less messy to eat and ordered a brisket sandwich with potato salad and coleslaw sides.  

The side were good, above average.  Kudos on that.

The brisket was well trimmed, tasty, had a good smoked flavor, but was a little underdone for my liking resulting in it being a bit on the chewy side, but only enough to keep it from being a 5 star rating.   

The hot BBQ sauce was very good.  

Next time I am going to try the ribs.
The food has been pretty consistent since I ate there as a kid 16 years  ago. Chicken bahn mi and egg role have been my go to.

I was driving by and saw "Cheba Hut Toasted Subs". Just what I was craving. You'll notice when you walk in that the toasted subs almost kind of seems like a subliminal message with sandwich sizes such as "nug" and "blunt". Also, the sides are labeled "munchies" and drinks are "cotton mouth cures". I love all the posters and things on the walls pertaining to "the ganja". I also love the menu choices because they aren't what you'd see at any ordinary sandwich shop. I chose the Pakalolo. It consists of ham, swiss, and pineapple and then whatever veggies you want to add. It was excellent.

We came here for their ayce sushi but they hadn't yet opened for dine in. The waitress told us they were actually opening the next day, but that was our last night in town so I guess we just missed it. Nonetheless, they were running a sushi special for takeout during COVID-19, which was a sweet deal...$30 for any 4 sushi rolls and any 2 appetizers. Forgot to take photos, but it was all really delicious. Only disappointing thing was their spider roll. Every sushi restaurant does their spider roll differently, but this particular one was not our favorite. And unfortunately, spider rolls are my fiance's thing...lol.

Just visited for the first time. Amazing beer selection, I mixed two sixes. The snacks and food looked pretty good, and the cheese selection was big for that size store. It does seem a little pricey, but where else are you going to find the vast assortment of brews in that part of town?
Got the bacon sand which and it was amazing also the service was up to standard. I tried the bulgogi cheesesteak sandwich and it was one of the best I've ever had.

We have been ordering from them for about a year now. Their pizza rocked! But sadly they stopped making it. Last time we ordered i got pork tacos with apple slaw on top. So good!!! I would highly recommend this place! Their menu is very unique and doesn't disappoint in taste

We called ahead to make a reservation and was told there is 90 minute time limit for the table. Food was ok but not what you would expect from C&L. Ordered a bottle of wine but it wasn't kept cold. We left our table at the 90 minute mark, went to the bar. The place didn't appear to be 50%  full. Not sure why the time limit but I won't be back.

My wife and I pulled up and with the line out front we were even more confident that the food and service would be good. We weren't disappointed. The service was friendly and quick plus the food was delicious.

Small little grocery store not even an 1/8th of the size of most Kroger's or Publix stores. It is very crowded. It is over stocked and it is a little dark and dingy...but the prices are very good!!!
Can't beat the prices of the meats  here, they have a lot of the buy 5 for $20 ...and some really good cuts of meat. They have a meat cutter on duty so everything is fresh!!! I like that!
It is close to my home and easy to get to on my commute home from work, so I stop her fairly regular...the staff is friendly and the patrons of mixed means..so you will be safe here!!! They close about 8pm and have a big parking lot (larger than the store itself)

This is one of the most unique places in Tucson! A beer & wine garden with food trucks in the parking lot! And right at the base of the Catalina Mountains. They have a wonderful variety of beers and wines, so you are sure to find something that you like. And the outdoor seating is great for small groups of friends or family to gather and enjoy our beautiful Tucson sunsets. Check out their Facebook page to find out what food trucks will be there each day. It will take me several dozen visits to try all of the beers that they offer! Can't wait!

Glad I finally made it here!! My friends who are regulars, invited me to join them for 'Sha bu 'Sha bu'. We had that almost daily in Asia, this served the fun!
I was very happy to see each person has our own pot, with our selections of broth. Though the spicy broth was a bit watered down, it was still tasty, wish there was a real spicy and thick one though. ^^
The 'make it your own' sauce bar was just like in Asia, and good sauce made everything tasted good!! 
The next one, ingredients, vegi were fresh looking, tasted lovely, and I loved the fish and fish ball the best! Clam were full of sand, that's the only down side. Plenty of food!! If not enough, you may add any extra dishes for extra cost.
I had a great time and wish I came here earlier! Because even dinning alone, this could be cozy especially on a cold day!

I had TERRIBLE service this morning. I called in my order this morning and was told that it would be ready in 10mins. I show up within the 10mins and the food isn't ready, no big deal. I figured I was a few minutes early I would wait. At no point in time did anyone at the counter tell me that there would be a huge wait. After waiting there an additional 30mins and 3 people who came in after me and placed their orders in person received their food, and I was still stuck waiting, I go to the counter and say that I've been waiting a half hour and would like my money back. They say my food is being boxed up right now. Odd that I ask for my money and then it's ready. Then the people at the counter RUDELY proceed to tell me when I ask for my money back  they had 40 burritos called in this morning. Wouldn't that have been helpful information when I called in and was to TEN MINUTES, or when I paid for my food like hey there's lots of food in front of yours it could be a really long wait, so I could decide if I wanted to wait or not. I ended up being late for work on account of this.

The food at Zahav was incredible, and was truly a highlight of my trip to Philly. But be sure you come here with a plan (see final paragraph) and with an appetite. The Tayim ($45/person Taste of Zahav) is the recommended way to survey the food, but I cannot emphasize how utterly massive the portions are.

But let's talk about the hummus. It's so light, and so well seasoned to the point where I am now spoiled - literally every single time I've had hummus since my taste buds are sorely aware it doesn't hold a candle to Zahav. The other highlights of the meal were the duck and sirlion - both were very tender and delicious. Excellent all around.

A logistical note: Zahav is a tough place to grab a table. When we had checked in for a January reservation, we found out they were booked for the next month and a half. Fortunately, though, if you get there at 5pm you can roll the dice and hope to grab seats at the bar. (Tables were only for reservations.) This worked out well for us, since after arriving on the Saturday of MLK weekend at 5:10 (and already people were streaming in by tnen), we were able to snag some seats after a 45-minute wait. This will be our go-to plan for returning here in the future in the likely event we can't get a reservation.

If you live in Philly, definitely check out Zahav. If you live in NYC, I wouldn't blame you if you took a trip down just to eat there.

If you want to sit, go early.  Once you get a table you're better off ordering drinks from the bar - they come out quicker.  It's a fun place to hang out.  The crowd is usually diverse in age but usually ends up creating a great ambiance.  I've never had the food there but the Scoprion drink will knock you on your butt.

Definitely a place to visit if you are in the area.  Food is amazing.  They always have specials and they are accommodating with food requests. (Ie me lol) 
Service is super friendly too.

We placed our order on 2/26/2021, around 9:30pm, and had our food delivered.
It was a pleasure to speak with a polite and accommodating employee that answered the phone, and took the order.
We ordered a large pepperoni, black olive, thin crust pizza, and a garden salad.
I asked if the pizza is cut in triangles or squares. I happen to like triangular slices. I was told that on the thin crust pizzas, the crust is cut in squares but the person I talked with said they would be happy to slice the pizza the way I preferred. Our pizza was baked to perfection and very tasty!
The salad was pretty standard but arrived fresh, cold and crisp.
I had specific instructions for the delivery driver, and my instructions were taken and followed as requested.
I called the store back after my husband and I finished eating, to get the name of the employee that was so helpful.
I spoke with Chad, the General Manager of the Olivette location and was told that Sam took the order. 
Thank you Sam, for a good experience in customer service.
Sometimes, people can be quite rude on the phone. Not Sam though.  Nice going!!
I didn't ask the delivery drivers name but her employee # on the ticket was 6821. She too was courteous.
Good food, good all around experience. 
Will definitely order from here again.

Food was okay, but the staff and policies left much to be desired. Our server was less than pleasant, ignoring us half the time and frowning at us the rest. They refuse to play anything but Boise State games ok ALL televisions if the game is on. We wanted to finish the last 5 minutes of another game, but they refused. The table next to us had an altercation with the manager as well, and "the customer is always right" was definitely not his policy. He argued with them for five minutes about a glass of wine. I was rather underwhelmed by my burger, but could have overlooked that if not for everything else. I'll think twice before coming back here.

I picked up the two taco's and chip combo and was quiet disappointment at yesterday's food rally in Westchase.  The tacos were mediocre at best, the chicken and steak had no flavor and weren't authentic.  Both tacos were overloaded with sour cream and cheap lettuce to cover any taste..  I could off done a better job making them at home..
We need Taco Bus to make a visit over to our neck of the woods..

This place is amazing! As soon as we walked in we noticed the Mediterranean style grill modeled after the bistros and brasseries of Europe. The menu is seafood focused with an emphasis on fresh and local produce. The style is simple and comfortable! We had the Mussels to start which were amazing! I had the Duck and she had the Seared Salmon. The presentation was outstanding and the food was prepared just right. The manager came over to personally check on us. Everyone was clean cut. You really feel like you are at a 5 star restaurant. This is a very fine addition to the growing Tucson community. I look forward to trying everything on their menu. Great job...

Wow, SO impressed with Tupelo Junction's happy hour!  I just wrote a review about the underwhelming food at Jeannine's, despite the positive reviews.  However, I was so pleasantly surprised with Tupelo Junction!

They have a happy hour tasting menu every Tues-Sat between 5-7pm I believe (see photo).  I tried the Farmer's Market blackberry mojito and my boyfriend had the margarita, full with amazing fresh fruits.  Usually I opt for wine, but there was no way I could pass up these drinks!  Especially for $5/each!  They are served in cute little jars which is a nice touch.

We chose two items from the tasting menu - the bloody mary short ribs and the shrimp and scallops with grits.  WOW!  Both were so impressive!  Definitely generous portions for $5-7, and such quality food.  I wanted to try everything off the menu but we had dinner reservations shortly after.

This place made me even sadder that I am leaving Santa Barbara soon.  If I lived here longer, I would make this a meet up place with my friends all the time!  Santa Barbara has the best happy hours, and there are so many that I never got a chance to try!  I guess I'll have to visit frequently :-)

I tried their cappuccino. The place looked beautiful. They have many options for desserts/bakery. My review is based on the cappuccino. The cappuccino was ok. Not the best. I might be back to try their desserts.

I've been talking about coming here for over a year. Finally came and it was everything that I thought it would be. I love the setup. Very intimate setting. Food... AWESOME!!! Drinks... ON POINT! I definitely will be coming back. Highly recommend
I enjoy eating here it is a gem of a restaurant in South Philly. They have an spicy beef pineapple dish I love.

There's something magical happening in the area around Spring Garden between Broad and 10th Streets. The Rail Park, new restaurants, and new brewpubs like Roy Pitz make this stretch of the city a destination, in my opinion. RP is like any other brew pub; large beer-making equipment on view, house brand beers, and a short but decent food menu. The open seating and large bar area makes the space inviting. The beers are good and I think in my mind I would enjoy them more if I was more familiar with them (like any local brews, you gotta get to know them). I did a flight to find a favorite and while I don't need to run back to RP for that ONE beer, I finished them all. The wings were prepared how I like them--friend and no breading--but the sauce was too sweet and not spicy enough for me. There was a TV at the bar that only showed loops of RP ads. Seemed like a waste to me since you only see it once you're already in the restaurant. I would've much rather have seen the Sixers game while I worked through my meal. I'll be back. Probably before or after a trip to the Rail Park!
It won't fill the pit of despair in your soul, but at least it'll fill your stomach. Chicken's good. Liked the small basket with the chipotle sauce.
Excellent banh mi and very good boba drinks. My son is picky about his banh mi and after visiting Paris Banh Mi Cafe, he always wanted to stop by every chance he had. Highly recommended.

We just moved to the neighborhood and had wanted to try this place for a couple weeks. Delivery was on-time and the chana masala and palak paneer were both excellent. Nan and samosas were as well. Can't wait to dine in sometime. We moved here from NYC last year and were used to great Indian food so we were excited to find such great Indian food here in STL.

Good food, horrible service!  Arrived to a sparsely filled resturant at 5:45.  Our server started out nice enough, but obviously couldn't maintain it!  It took forever to get our drinks, only one loaf of bread for seven because the rest was still cooking.  Asked for butter with our salads, but that didn't show up until well after our meal came out and he had to be reminded.  Four of our seven entrees arrived and more than five min later the other three arrived. Worst part was it was two kids who were part of the waiting group.  My wife's meal came out with sauce on hers when she asked for it on the side.  I asked for spicy marinara, but they gave it to my wife instead.  I could keep going, but what is the point.  Talked to a manager who offered free dessert to make amends, but made no attempt to promote a return visit by offering a discount on a future visit.  Needless to say we will NOT be back due solely to the service!

We came to this place because of the many reviews we saw on line and we left extremely disappointed. The service was professional and good but not the food .
The fish was swimming in an unknown creamy  sauce and the fried platter actually was full of cooking oil.
Even  the dessert  mousse cake tasted like margarine . 
New Orleans have better restaurants!!!!!
Love this place. Wish for better deli quality/variety relative to cost (guest chef?);otherwise awesome!

We went to the Keg for an early supper this past Sunday. We thought if we showed up around 4PM we would beat the rush. Wrong! It was very busy even at that early hour (they had just opened at three o'clock). Fortunately somebody else in our party arrived before us and secured a table.

Our waiter was super friendly and completely unflustered by the busy ambience - calm and steady like he was in the middle of a storm, debris hurling past him. I ordered the Chicken & Ribs which came with fries. The food was very good even though the meat didn't slide off the bone of the ribs like I would've liked. The chicken was slightly on the crispy side just like I like it.

Even though I really enjoy the food at the Keg it's not my absolute goto place to eat because I'm not a fan of its busy, hectic atmosphere. There's always constant motion going on all around your table and it's noisy. I don't enjoy having to yell at the people at my table to make them hear my dinner conversation. Also, I never understood the fetish for sawdust and stained wood that seems to be permeating every steakhouse these days. Does it make your food taste better if you think you're eating it in a dimly lit barn?

Anyway - good food, good service. Eat here.

We enjoyed a very good meal with friendly people and a knowledgeable, helpful waiter. The bisque was good. Lana's ribeye steak was very good. My thick chunk of pork (cochon) was moist and falling apart, sitting atop a bed of spinach which sat, in turn, on a corn-bread base. The dish was smothered in a raspberry-dijon sauce. It was very good to excellent. The waiter suggested a Bourdeaux which was reasonably priced and complimented both entrees. The banana cream puffs were very good. In sum, the food was very good and very consistent. In addition, three other customers sitting apart from each other but near us engaged us in pleasant dinner conversations.

One note: I see that Luke is rated $$. That price range probably applies to lunch or perhaps to appetizers and a drink. Our dinner with tip was well over $100.00 and well worth it.

This is a great little spot to grab a quick bite to eat
they have several different food options available 
however they do not have enough seating and there
was NO SOCIAL DISTANCING you will spend between 
$5.00 to $20.00 on some really great food
Great environment everything was good I will be returning most definitely .. my waiter was really helpful as well

Can tell you several stories about Los Sarapes - but I will spare you & just provide the Cliff Notes...... FOOD is VERY GOOD. Why do I only give it 2 Stars you ask??  Two WORDS ----- The service. The people here are MEAN. They have all these "rules" about what you can / can't do ( there are many rules but one they are very SERIOUS about : absolutely NO substitutions, don't even THINK about asking - you will get a GLARE.)  It is over-priced. They always rush us. When it was byob - they used MY tequila & made margaritas with their mix and charged me $7 for each one..... I could go on & on - but I won't.  We still occasionally go there - b/c like I said - the food IS GOOD -- and we always come away with a story.......SO - if you DO go... at least you know what to expect.......good food, bad service.

Been going to Grazianos for over 20 years. NEVER had a bad meal or experience there! The staff are all friendly and the food is AMAZING. We aren't regulars as we live a pretty good distance away, but we are always treated like one of the locals which makes it an even better experience. Its a nice cozy place with an old school vibe...if you are looking for mainstream, look somewhere else. Grazianos is an old fashioned, welcoming, cozy, mom and pop restaurant with a knack for making great Italian food. I'd give 10 stars if I could.

Met my girlfriend here for dinner since I had business in Nashville. She'd been once before and raved about the food but said service was a challenge. We had a wonderful meal with fantastic service. My only regret is I ate too much of the appetizer to try the dessert menu but I could not eat anything else. Great experience!

Today was my first trip to the Basque Market. I've heard over and OVER how good the Paella was, and--due to the limited times they serve it--haven't ever had a chance to make it over. Today, however, was the day! Paella is served Weds & Fri at 12pm until it's gone and Thursday at 6pm. Let me tell you, it usually always sells out in about 10 minutes!

Food: I ordered the Paella lunch special. It was about $9.50 and came with a HUGE plate of paella (filled to the brim with seafood!) and a side roll. Tapas (pay per toothpick) were also offered, but I opted just for the paella this time. Boy, it was good! The flavor was bold and nice and salty. The meat was cooked to perfection (I loved the sausage chunks!), and the added green beans and peppers helped me feel like I was eating something "healthy." This will definitely be a return venture!

Drinks: n/a

Happy Hour Offerings: n/a

Atmosphere: While the interior space is small, it's cozy and suggests that it's a popular spot. I know the paella regularly sells out, so it's a "be there on time or you're square" kind of scenario. I'd give it a better rating were the space a little bigger and more inviting.

Service: The woman who took my payment was very helpful and explained the offerings of the Basque Market to me. I would have appreciated a bit more detail on their menu items and explanation of "how it works," and as they weren't busy, I should have asked more questions. The paella chef was very friendly and served me immediately, also reminding me of the other times he serves the dish. Smart! I'll be back!

Overall Quality: Absolutely superb. To be able to watch the chef prepare the paella and then enjoy a hot plate of it right away is great. 

Overall Value: A little spendy for a lunch plate ($9.50), but considering the heaping amount of seafood that was included in it, I'd spend it again any day.

TIPS: Paella only served Monday & Weds for lunch and Thursday at dinner. It sells out FAST so get there on time! You can also take it to go!

This spot was inspiring and I love how it is small and quaint. 
We were able to try a few things on the menu: chick-un and waffles, tuna salad, crab mac and cheese, bbq burger and oyster mushroom poboy sandwich.
The texture of the chick-un will blow you away. The chickpea tuna salad was a great twist and the dressing was refreshing. 
My favorite was the poboy sandwich, the mushrooms were so crispy and lightly coated.
I am excited to see this place grow and flourish and gives me hope for my cooking dreams too. 
Thank you for sharing your chickpea nuggets with us :)

first time having which wich (I KNOW?!?!?! i grew up in nashville and it took me this long to try it?!) 

omg. its. so. good.

first of all, get the hot sammich. its crunchy and fantastic and not too bready and great quality... omg yums.

so how which wich operates is you walk in, and you grab from their many little bins of sandwich brown bags that you want the base of your sammich to be. may it be turkey or ham or veggie or something else, you just grab the base of the one you want. then, you can customize it. you check on the bag certain things you want to add or not have on there. Then you write your name on the bottom of it (anything you want, i've seen some hilarious ones on social media). Then you pay for it, wait for it, and they call your name out super quickly. There are 3 sizes, and believe me, the small may seem small but it really isnt! 

I came here and got a turkey bacon HOT sammich. It was fast, they were incredibly friendly (shoutout to the register boy) and it was DELICIOUS!!! I will DEFINITELY come back again.

the small sandwich by itself was ~$4-5. definitely worth it!  I love which wich. now come to memphis. :]

My wife, daughter (16yo), and I stopped here for lunch on our way through Indianapolis; as we always like to stop at local establishments featured on the Food Network.  The Steer-In was on Diners, Drive-Ins, & Dives in 2011.  The restaurant looks very similiar to what it must have looked like in the 1960's.  From the counter and booths, to the large windows.  The service was friendly and the food was awesome.  My wife ordered that Meatball Sandwich (featured on DDD) with fries, and I ordered the Hoosier Pork Tenderloin (also featured on DDD) with fries, and our daughter ordered a traditional burger with fries.  We also ordered two sides of mac & cheese (also featured on DDD).  The main entrees did not disappoint, my pork tenderloin sandwich was big, juicy, and full of flavor.  The mac & cheese was very cheesy and good.  My wife's meatball sandwich looked delicious, and she commented several times on how good the meatball and cheese were.  My daughter indicated the burger was good, and looked like a handmade patty.  The only let-down were the fries.  They were just the standard run of the mill steak fries and nothing to write home about.  All in all though, if in Indianapolis, I would certainly steer in to the Steer-In Restaurant.

My entree, the steak and potatoes, was outstanding. Truly.

The bread was warm, fresh and wonderful (just out of the oven).

My dessert was not good at all. It was the chocolate pudding cake. It was a major fail  on their part. I think it was frozen and microwaved, because they brought it out within a few minutes. There's a great restaurant I go to in Soho, where they bake the molten chocolate cake after a customer orders it. You wait for it but it is worth the wait. This cake at Herbsaint was inedible.

 I was surprised that the server didn't offer to exchange it or take it back, since it was barely touched. Consideration of that sort is what makes a restaurant extra special and worth returning to. Also, for a restaurant of that caliber I expected the server to lightly dust off the table after he saw the bread crumbs. He just left the mess there as I sat.

So, definitely not deserving of five stars, but perhaps deserving of four.
Authentic, insanely delicious New Orleans food with great, friendly staff. Very popular, prepare to possible take the food home instead of sitting there. Wish they were open more than two days!

First time at Crabby Bills. They had reopened recently due to the pandemic. The place was like a morgue. They are really following the social distancing guidelines. No drink menu. I was surprised how limited the menu was. The food itself had good flavor. I had the sea scallops, red potatoes and slaw. Portions were adequate other than the red potatoes. I literally had 5 small potatoes. Like bird egg size. So I was somewhat disappointed. If Here again I would consider trying again. Especially when social distance guidelines are over.

"The Palace" as it is called amongst the pack that I run with is one of the best most succinct places to get a very good meal if you like spice and you like freshness when you dine.


The curry dishes are great and there is a papaya fruit salad that is really grand. Not to mention a coconut shrimp that is one of the best shrimp dishes I've ever had. 

Dining here is a warm experience, with both the servers, and for your taste buds!

Spicy!

My wife and I went there for a date night during the concert series at The Village.   I found the pizza to be moderately good, not knock your lights out.  The menu is really Ala Cart everything, even your pizza toppings.   So be careful if you're on a tight budget.   It's a thin crust pizza that I like, but would like better with more toppings.    Because of the price per topping I felt too restricted.
Excellent seafood and great service. Very good wine selection and if you get the right server you get great wine advice. Friendly staff.

This place looks like your typical corner store from the outside, and pretty much on the inside, too, but the staff is nice, there are a ton of options, and they will give you more ice cream than you know what to do with.  Seriously, it took me 3 days to eat a kiddie sized cup.  I'm looking forward to making more stops here.

My friends and I had lunch at 3 Margaritas yesterday. I just wasn't thrilled with it. Their prices are very high for the area and the quality. Some of the premium Margaritas are $18. And they aren't worth it! Just really sweet concoctions that don't taste at all like alcohol. 

The restaurant itself is kind of dirty feeling and the tables and chairs were crammed all together. The food was just ok. I liked the salsa and chips but the queso was pretty tasteless. We ordered the appetizer sampler but the quesadillas were greasy and the meat portion was small. Queso fundido served with the sampler was good, spicy and plentiful. They also had some yummy shrimp. 

But for 2 Margaritas and an order of fajitas, $38 is way too high. Disappointing experience!
Pizza was really good. Everything else is so so so. Get the traditional square tomato pie, well done.

Nearing the end of our meal so I will begin with dessert. Ok, I will try anyway. The coconut cream pie and key lime pie are extraordinary, and I bake! This is our second visit and in both cases the dessert was a topic of conversation for days afterwards. Tonight we had the special, a sea bass crusted with macadamia. Incredible. Nothing else to say-it was perfection. The seafood sampler was fabulous. The salmon has a great glaze, the crab cake light and airy and scallops perfectly seared. This is not inexpensive, but the prices are fair and the superb cuisine worth every penny. Great place to make an impression, indoors or out. Service is attentive without being overbearing.
Food is extremely disappointing just like all the food on bourbon at. Go to to Frenchman st instead.

Ahahahaha this place is a joke if you get there after 2pm. They literally run out of all their food and because they don't have a freezer you have to get potato salad and pulled pork without bread. It's not just the meat, they ran out of MAC AND CHEESE and BUNS. Like, buns you buy at the grocery store two blocks away. Nobody could order any sandwiches because they didn't have buns. ?!?!?!

Came here for lunch a couple of times and it was great, the food is awesome. But this is not a real restaurant once the sun goes down. No brisket, no chicken, none of that stuff. They had wings though.

Do not go here for dinner ever.

One of my favorite places to go for brunch as the food is really good and so are the drinks. Anytime the suggestion is made to go here I never mind going because I know I'm getting quality food and good service.

Enjoy a seat outside on the patio if the weather permits and drink one of their frozen mimosas or frozen pomegranate mojitos. They don't skimp on the liquor and both are extremely refreshing. Favorite apps include the crawfish cornbread which is a piece of skillet cornbread with a crawfish étouffée type sauce smothered on top. The fried green tomatoes are also really good which come with jumbo lump crab meat which is a plus. Favorite brunch entrees include the cochon de lait which comes with poached eggs, a heaping side of potatoes or grits and a biscuit for $13. The shrimp and grits are also surprisingly good as well, which come in a Tasso cream sauce. 

I definitely prefer Superior Seafood over the Superior Grill which I feel like is overpriced, mediocre texmex. I'm looking forward to coming back for their happy hour.

Not my first time to visit Fins and won't be my last. Other than slight misstep as we checked in for our reservation, the evening was perfect. We had several friends join us for some excellent cocktails and great food. Most chose the lobster dumplings and one had the soft shell crab. The flavor was hard to beat. The crab with cashews (everyone had to taste) was some of the best in the city. The signature dish Scalibut was the whitest and softest fish on the menu and definitely worth the trip. Swordfish, scallops and pork chop were also great. The wild red fish was my choice. That was surprisingly tasty even for someone that traditionally doesn't favor sweet potatoes. The dessert that we all lived before was not on the menu (apple pie), put the bread pudding, chocolate bomb and cream brûlée were great choices. I must mention the wonderful biscuits served while waiting for our appetizers ( wonderful flavors and moist and not hard). The service was very good as well. They were attentive and prompt. Lastly to mention they validate for parking on the Iberville lot so makes it easy to park. Try it you'll love it.
Wang's Table is great Chinese food! Moved here recently from Sacramento and have been looking for a great spot here in Reno, I think I found it!

This is probably my favorite restaurant in Chinatown! They open late, great food and the servers are very attentive and friendly! I usually throw my company parties here because they have private karaoke rooms upstairs where we can dinner and karaoke at the same time with no additional room charge.

Finally got the chance to try Bandit Coffee.  They are in renovation, so no indoor access, order thru the window so to give you the hole in the wall experience.  I asked to heat up the baked goods, they said they can't??? Also give you one napkin for the whole order, like our commander in chief said, come on man!  If offer one napkin, customers can only either use it to wipe their mouth, or clean up after themselves.  Other than that, the coffee is good and baked items are tasty.
Good and quick. Friendly and convenient. Clean restaurant. Never overcrowded. Great lunch specials, and Friday/Tuesday lunch buffet. No complaints.

First off WOW! I was blown away when we walked in and left even more impressed! This place is first class all the way. From the food, drinks, service and overall atmosphere this place is class! I would suggest the Icetini for a really amazing drink, it comes in a ice glass and is fantastic! 

This family owned business is truley a staple in all of Idaho! Thomas Keller better watch out because there's a new sheriff in town!

Great spot! We had dinner on a Friday night, service was great and so was the food. I had the tonkatsu ramen and was pleasantly surprised, I'm a noodle snob. My friends all had sushi and said it was awesome as well.
Omg. I loved this place. The food was amazing. So full of flavor. The service was quick. The staff was friendly. The rooftop seating was terrific.

Don't be scared away by the line. It moves fast and the food is worth it! Came here on a Sunday for brunch around 11 am and walked into almost no empty tables. But as we waited in line, tables slowly cleared up and my friend and I were able to grab a table pretty easily. Several groups of 4 and even 6 were seated, so it's possible. We ordered at the front and the food was brought to us in less than 10 minutes, even on such a busy day! 

OMG, the divorced eggs. Who knew that simple things like salsa roja y verde, tortillas, cheese, and eggs could make something so delightful? If you like eggs and typically order items like eggs Benedict, hold your urge to order the ordinary and go for the extraordinary. - 11/10.

Now regarding the rest of the meal: avocado toast, black coffee, latte. The avocado toast was exactly what I expected with toast, sliced avocados and a whopping serving of scrambled eggs on top. A little dash of salt and a side of ketchup brought this dish to a solid 7.5/10.  Black coffee - 7/10, Latte - 6/10. 

This particular Sunday morning brunch wasn't a poppin' bottles kinda brunch, but I will keep this place in mind when I'm in the BYO kinda mood.

This is a very tasty burger!  Stopped in post-dinner time, so I was able to walk right up and order.  One burger, medium rare, and a vanilla milkshake.  Perfect.  Oh, and the ice cream is Bassetts Ice Cream, what a treat.  Just goes to show they pulled out all the stops to make this place great.  I'll definitely be making regular visits to this place.

My friend and I visited this restaurant over memorial day weekend after a 3 hour tour of the city. We arrivedat 4:22 and we were starving!  The hostess sat us at a table for 2 which was so small that we didn't know how both our plates would fit on the table at the same time. I asked the hostess if we could sit at the larger table next to us and she told us no (even though at 4:30 they open up the upstairs portion of the restaurant for dinner where there were several more tables).  We sat down at our cramped table. The waitress came to take our drink order. We both ordered water. She brought us 2 glasses and some water in a glass container. it was about 80 degrees that day and the water was warm. no ice in the glasses. When we looked at the menu, we saw that it was the 'snack menu'. Apparently, you don't get a regular dinner menu until 4:30. While a little annoyed since we only had 5 mins to go, we knew we were only ordering salads so we didn't make an issue of it. We placed our order: a chopped salad and a Caesar salad, both with grilled chicken added (both were ricdiculously priced). and then we waited... and waited....and waited.... after a half an hour, we were pretty annoyed and started looking around for someone. At that point, I noticed there were 2 salads that had been sitting on the counter for quite some time. People have been walking by them, servers have been talking over them, one server was leaning against the counter right next to one of them.  Around this time the manager came over and told us that they lost our ticket and they were correcting the issue now. (i can only assume is that they basically forgot to cook our chicken, even though we were watching the cooks in the kitchen sweep, clean up and converse with each other).  At this point , even after we pointed out that we have been waiting half an hour for SALADS, the manager never offered us anything for the inconvience. Not a drink, not an appetizer, not even some bread for the table. (i should also mention that in all this time our waitress never even came back to check on us so that we could ask for some ice for our warm water). I asked the manager if the salads I have been looking at for quite some time were ours and he said 'yes'. i told him we didnt want salads that have been sitting there so long and people were talking and gesturing over. He said "if you don't want them, then you don't have to take them". We told him we don't want them and that we were going to go. He just walked away, no apologies, no attempt to get us to stay. 
We definitely will not be giving this establishment another chance since it is obvious they do not value their patrons all around experience. From the minute we walked in the door, we knew we should have left. Next time we will listen to our intuition.

I have been excited to try a Sushi place close to home however Sakura Sushi was very disappointing! One of my rolls had a very fishy taste but my service was worse. The waitress did not check on us once other than to drop off our rolls and we had a party 6.
