We would have to ask other staff for drinks or sides and one of them even cut me off and said "your waitress will be right by" I even had to ask if they had ice cream. Sushi is something we like to treat ourselves with fairly often but unfortunately tonight we did not feel "treated".

After much anticipation and the opening being delayed since August.... I was finally able to try the Chicken Spot today. For my first visit I just wanted to try the most traditional. I got the 3pc combo with Mac & Cheese. I'll start with the good.... The Mac and cheese was pretty good. It wasn't dry but it wasn't the ooey gooey type either. It was right in the middle with a little of the crispy topping in the middle and bread crumbs on top. The breading of the chicken was pretty good. It was crispier and sweeter than I normally like, but it wasn't bad. I was a little disappointed that for $10 combo you don't get a drink or a biscuit/cornbread... I think the owner must have heard that and threw in a biscuit. Thank goodness I did not lay for that because it was terrible! When I went to break a piece off it was so hard and just completely crumbles apart. The drumstick and the leg were cooked mostly ok... A little less done than I would have liked but better than being dry. The thigh on the other hand was extremely undercooked. Even after a warm up in the microwave it was still just too slimy and undercooked to be able to eat it, so it got tossed. Lastly, $3 for a fountain drink was a little excessive. More than likely I won't be returning. I've worked in the city for a really long time and I was a fan of Benjamins.... I was hoping for a decent affordable spot for lunch. Good luck!

What a great little place.  Visiting Galliton on business and wanted a local place and not a chain.  Found Alberto's here on Yelp and so happy I did. 

Walked in with 3 other groups and the waiter got a little frazzled but recovered well.  Ordered the Quibi and Chicken Curry and was not disappointed.  Both were excellent with the Quibi having just the right crunch when bitten into and the curry was a great balance of spice. 

I didn't have room for dessert but the dessert case looked amazing.  Overall excellent and will come back if in town.

Note:  That his is a BYOA (bring your own alcohol) type establishment. Don't let the wine bottles I show in my picture fool you.
Had the chicken fried chicken and it was great. Server was friendly and they were busy. Food was a little slow but nice and got when we got it.

over hipped... terrible wine list  I ordered a wine I couldn't drink, it was old and the last of the bottle.   I took one sip and ordered something else , they charged me the full price and charged me for both.  VERY DISAPPOINTED - this place won't last long.

Thank you SoBro Cafe for proving to me that Indy actually does offer some vegan options and can do them well. I've always loved buffalo anything wraps. Just throw some buffalo sauce on something and wrap it up and i'll probably be satisfied. Their buffalo tempeh wrap was the healthiest, freshest tasting buffalo wrap i've ever had and i do mean that as a compliment. The buffalo sauce was not overpowering and the flavors worked great together.
We also ordered a superfood salad which really is full of everything good for you and can make you feel better about yourself when you order dessert.

We sat in the front window seats which we enjoyed. We will definitely return.

Also, although the online menu doesn't mark which lunch entree items are vegan, the actual menu does.

This place was the only soul food place I used to goto until the other day I found a hair in my food . You would think they would comp the whole meal ,that wasn't the case. Most restaurant will comp your meal 100℅ ..  or give you a gift certificate .. this is sad cause I used to frequent there ... I will no longer eat there because of the lack of care for the customer .

On Sunday night, my boyfriend and I (out-of-towners) were looking for a fun place for foodies.  First of all at 9 pm on a Sunday night barely anything is open in the downtown area.  However, we found Fly, and boy am I glad we did.  I tried some amazing jalapeno infused tequila grapefruit dream drink (a palmina I think)...EXCELLENT DRINK.  We ordered the garlic frites, crab cakes (my personal favorite), and sliders.  Everything we had was delicious, and the service was excellent.  The waitress was very helpful in telling us where to go to see more of the excitement in Tampa.  

After being tired and cranky from a long drive, this restaurant was a wonderful experience. When we move there, we will probably become regulars to this place.

We came here after leaving another place that had poor, grumpy service. It was a relief to walk in Imperial to find open seats at the bar, our game on the tv, a very friendly bartender/server, and a lively environment!

We ordered a couple beers while we looked over the menu. My husband ended up having the 35¢ chicken wings - a special on Wednesdays. I ordered the Jalapeño Burger (roasted jalapeño, pepper jack, roasted jalapeño aioli) substituted with a veggie burger. 

While we enjoyed our meals, the wings were very tiny (understandable since they were only 35¢ each). My burger was tasty but I do think a bit too small for $13 even though it came with a side salad.  

Our overall take on Imperial is a positive one and we plan to go back.

Confused to why it's rated so high. At best, it's mediocre Cajun food. Went here based on 4 star rating from over 800 reviewers, but I'm guessing most of those hadn't eaten good food before. 

Ordered a mojito which was all syrup and no club soda, returned it and it was equally as bad. Jambalaya was dry and lacking flavor, mostly mushy rice with dry overcooked chicken mixed with a decent andouille. Only thing I really enjoyed was the redfish beignets (which are essentially just fried fish bites).  

With all the other amazing food choices in New Orleans, I felt cheated out of a good meal that night based on the high reviews here.   It's probably more 2 stars, but I'm giving it a 1 to balance out too many 5 star reviews. 

I would highly recommend looking elsewhere if you actually want a meal to remember.

If you like blues...take a minute to check this place out.   Intimate setting, great music and great prices.   4th trip to Nashville and I'm 4 for 4 on great times here.   

Also try to catch Stacy Mitchart.....his group is electric.

Surprised...
Well that was better than I expected.
The other location on 50st left a bad taste in my mouth...
As such...I wasn't expecting much from this one. As such...I am pleasantly surprised.
All in all...not too shabby.
Nice place. Very clean and presentable.
Friendly staff.
The donair;
Meat...decent, but sliced pretty thin which makes it less juicy than it could...and should be.
Veggies...fresh and good amount.
Pita - pretty good.
Sauce...
This one surprised me.
I ordered sweet sauce on donair and a cup of garlic on the side. The gentleman behind the counter said he only has a garlic sweet sauce or taziki and seemed confused when I mentioned most shops have3 separate sauces. To his credit I guess...he said he would "look into" this option.
Anyway...the sauce I did get was quite good. Thick (so it didn't run away...), rich and amply applied.
Value...fair.
All in all...
A pretty good experience.
I would be content if this were my local shop...though I may make a few requests whilst they prepare my meal...

Food was pretty good but we found it to be very pricey for what it was. Staff were friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. 
Quaint place with BYOB which can help when the bill when it arrives.

Yay another restaurant on campus that I can't afford! Yes, the food is delicious (I can only vouch for the fries and onion soup). Yes, the decor is cool (though a little blinding). Yes, the waitstaff was great. 

Unfortunately I can only afford to go here once a year due to the steep prices. Penn does not pay its employees enough to enjoy many restaurants and faster food choices on their own campus (they control most of the real estate and no doubt are involved in the launching of new businesses in said real estate). I can only assume this is meant to provide big bosses a place to hang out in private and to woo rich parents, donors, and other visitors. It's a bummer.

If you are looking for authentic food with fresh ingredients go to Thai Taste. I have never had a dissapointing dish! The servers and owners barely speak english -- I always enjoy that in a restaurant as it helps me feel even more emersed in their culture. Thursdays is the all you can eat buffet. I like to go occassionally as I can try new things on the menu that I might have other wise not ventured to try. The buffet is a little more pricey but I always leave happy and stuffed to the gills! The restaurant decor isnt the most appealing to me but dont let this stear you out the door!
Love the coffee with a dash of cinnamon and the organic chai tea latte was fabulous. Tip:  casa means you get the porcelain cup. The other sizes are to go. Totally didn't know that...

I want to give a better star rating, and I will definitely give them another try soon and edit my rating depending on the experience. I'll try something else next time, too 

To start their phone number wasn't easy to find from Google. I had to call the speedway location to get it, which isn't a huge deal, but worth mentioning. I called and was on hold for a while to place my order, again not a huge deal. I had to repeat myself a lot and it was easy to tell he either wasn't paying attention or wasn't by a computer. My order wasn't complicated.

I ordered a Jason vegetarian with no tomatoes, extra sweet peppers and mozzarella sticks. He asked if I wanted ranch, marinara, or both. I said both and only ended up with marinara in my bag. 

The food - the mozzarella sticks were delicious. They aren't the typical breading. Maybe they're beer battered? I didn't like the marinara sauce but that's personal preference only because I prefer sweet marinara. It would have been nice to have the ranch. My sandwich didn't have extra sweet peppers but it had about a million hot peppers. It was HOT. Way way too hot. I enjoy hot generally but the sweet would have been better. The bread was soft and very tasty. You can tell it's very fresh. 

I have a feeling the food is generally fantastic. I'll eat in the restaurant next time for safe measure. It's really nice inside!
My god! As soon as I walked in the vibe was radiant! The service was great! Price well worth it

I've been to this restaurant 3 times and feel like I've got enough info to properly review.  Here it goes:

I've gone on both the weekend and during the week around early to late evening.  I've never had to wait more than 10 minutes which is great.  Food is pretty good especially their table side guacamole.  They can get a little heavy handed with the lime but other than that it's really good guac.  The tuna appetizers are delicious too.  Enchiladas, tacos, and fajitas were good but nothing remarkable.  The desserts are dull and way overpriced.  I paid $7 for a slice of tres leches cake that was bland and boring.  My friend got chocolate cake and said it tasted like it was from Giant.  Bummer.  Lastly their drinks are ok but can get pricey.  The first time we went we all ordered margaritas and actually had to send them back because they were too strong!  I know, right, who does that?  This girl who doesn't want a DUI that's who!  

Overall Plaza Azteca isn't the best but it's not bad and is a relaxed fun place to grab food and a drink.  Just be careful of the strength of the drinks and pass on dessert!

Independence Beer Garden is the go to spot for a day/night out! I really like the fact that you can order online and they bring your order to your table fairly quickly. They have different food on their menu each time I go, which I appreciate! The vibe is fantastic and I would definitely recommend this place for a large gathering as well! They don't accept reservations but you can put your name on the wait list and order drinks while you wait and the wait isn't always that long!
Corn fritters were great! Grilled cheese was good. I would not recommend their baked beans as they taste like canned baked beans.

This is one of my LOCAL FAVORITES!!! They have an awesome selection of southern cuisine with great portions and a great atmosphere and vibe. 

In the evenings they dim the lighting for a nice candle lit dinner perfect for a date night! 

It's also a great place to enjoy a weekend with friends for brunch, lunch, or dinner.

The bar has a variety of bottled beers, wines, and awesome cocktails.

And the customer service is unmatched! True southern hospitality quality service. 

We stopped in on a Tuesday for a family dinner for a family of 4. Although, they don't have a kids menu my children (ages 7 and 9) still found something to their likings.
They took FOREVER to get me my online order. And they asked the lady next to me if she wants her change of $2...? Not coming here again, the dirty, awkward atmosphere turned me off.

I tried the all-you-can eat option. Overall I liked it and I could do it again. Nothing stood out as especially good. The link was a disappointment. It was badly overcooked and pretty much not edible.
Excellent place for a drink! Had a flight of some of there beers and some lemon cream cake. Will come back again and again!

I love this place. The owner is super friendly, and even accommodated my friend who wanted just a few falafels with her chicken plate. I'm not sure he even charged us for this bonus little side, but how kind. While the pita's are microwaved back to life, the rest of the food definitely fits the bill. I had the gyro plate with most of the fixings from the small toppings bar, including jalepenos, black olives, green peppers, red onions, pickles, cucumbers, cheese, salad, lettuce, and an assortment of sauces. Portions are enormous for a beautifully low price. Everything is under $10 from a quick glance at the extensive menu.

Atmosphere-wise, it's a bit cool for the winter, but tolerable. The seating is reminiscent of most fast food joints with small group seating arrangements. There is a large flat screen near the counter if you need some entertainment.

There's plenty of parking around the back of the restaurant, conveniently away from the hectic traffic on Charlotte.

Definitely worth a try for the budget gourmet in town.

Love the atmosphere, music and great things they do for the community.  I crave the Cheese burger deluxe & fries which happens to be the perfect size for me.  Killer baked beans and cole slaw to die for.  Today is Halloween- if you get my puns.. Can't do without my Biff-ster.

I am really not sure how this place gets any stars but... 
Giant portions of food don't counter the fact that the food is awful.

A group of us went there when we found out that there was a 2h wait for a table at Memphis tap room 2 blocks away on saturday evening.

The decor was 70s/80s, the atmosphere was airless.  It was not a comfortable environment.

My GF described the food best:

The fancy meal a 10year old kid made for his mom for mothers day.
A lot of love but very little skill or imagination. (Rotini pasta with canned veggies, rotini pasta with stew, rotini pasta with grated parmesan.)

My visiting friends where very quiet about it, but later where faced with carrying back with us 3 pounds of rotini pasta (literally 3 pounds), got in arguments over who would carry the gross stuff. arg.

Wasn't impressed.  Baked macaroni and cheese was actually spaghetti noodles.  Didn't enjoy crawfish plate, but I believe that may have been that I don't like crawfish this way.  Chicken dumplings were thoroughly enjoyed by partner.
Ordered delivery and I was impressed. It's tastey American Chinese but done really well. The Moo Shu is on point. It's my go to for delivery.

This is hands down my favorite sandwich shop of all time.  Never once have a had a bad sandwich from here. I've lived in Philly all my life and this is unquestionably the single greatest sandwich shop in the entire city and state. You have to get the fries with the truffle wiz, whatever sandwich you pick will be the best one you've had. I wish I could brown nose these guys even more but I don't know how.

Came down to Bison after a football game in a jammed pack 4th ave. Lots of eating establishments had waits, but lucky I remembered Bison Witches from back in the day and found a table inside. After not eating for many hours we ordered the chips and salsa as an appetizer, A whole sandwich and a bread bowl soup. Man everything was great!  The bread bowl was so soft and we ordered the cheese soup. Amazing. I loved how easy it was for me to tear apart the bowl to eat with the soup. 

I forgot the name of the actual sandwich but I believe it was the Hawaiian one. It was so good! Paired with soup really amazing. 

Also their beer selection was good and they had a good IPA. But after eating so much I could barley drink any beer.lol.

Cool music playing inside and a cool dark alternative vibe. A true tucson classic so this is a must place to try!

Nestled discretely between South and Bainbridge on 3rd, it's easily missed if you're "hoofing" it (pun totally intended). 

The menu rotates every four weeks, so if you see it floating around on their minimalistic, trendy  website, be sure to disregard and go with the chef's flow. We sampled barbecued octopus that was simply right with the world and amply juicy; a gnocchi  that was scantly served in a delicate, buttery sauce (is that a hint of cinnamon?) leaving you with a delicate impression; and a duck breast served over lentils that just came apart with each fork dab. 

The venue is small and intimate and yes you may sit close to another couple or group, but you know what? If you don't have ADHD and can focus on your date's conversation, you're ready for a very intimate, personal dining experience.

TIP: Stop in Southwark's around the corner for pre-dinner Apéritifs or a post digestif. Or fuck it and just get the Manhattan the bartender recommends (because it's usually pretty awesome).

having binged on reading terminal deliciousness during the day, my friends (whom i was visiting) and i decided on a late gorging on dollar oysters instead of a full on dinner.

and we weren't the only ones...the lobby was jammed with people, though many were waiting to be seated for dinner, freeing up the first-come-first-serve bar for us cheapies only looking for happy hour oysters.

it took a while, but we got seated and ordered our drinks and shellfish.  all of which came out quickly.  though clearly not the best oysters i've ever had, for a dollar a piece, my standards range lowers to somewhere around flavorful and edible to somewhere above bowel busting awfulness.  and i'm happy to report that i had no experiences of the latter after an experience at oyster house.

Slow service, and the main lunch menu is nothing special. If you pop in on a Friday afternoon after 1, do not expect to be seated right away or see your server in the first 5 minutes. Had the turkey BLT and I kind of wish I didn't waste the calories. 

That being said, amazing fries and Brussel sprouts. Also a good beer selection. Definitely worth the calories! The parm truffle fries were amazing, and the Brussel sprouts truly changed my life.

Will go back for beer and sides.

We ate breakfast there, because the pancake pantry had a line around the corner. The food was good. I had one of the skillets.  It was a little pricey for what we got but not to bad. I would eat here again but would not drive out of the way to get to it.

Ordered the vegetable kabob platter for lunch. It came with rice and completely burnt vegetables.  The portion size was very very small.  It looks like a small kids meal protion.
I guess I should have ordered some Pita bread, but they charge $1.00 for a piece, and I already blew $10 on the meal.  
I won't be going back here again.  I ended up going back home and making lunch.

This place is amazing! We weren't that hungry, but really wanted to try it out, so we just got the conch fritters and the jerked chicken salad. Both were insanely excellent, and we can't wait to go back and try more food.

Server rushed us to order our items and rushed us to complete eating our food didn't get refills on our water and then wanted to know if we will leave a tip. Server should never ask a customer if we will leave a tip. Tip is earned by the service  we receive , food we eat and how it is and the atmosphere of the establishment.

My first ever real Philly cheesesteak. We ordered a pork & beef.  The beef was better!  The cheese is put on the bottom, then layered with meat & whatever else.  Even though it was good, I think it would be better if the cheese was it into the meat. Just sayin...

This is a wonderful, warm, and inviting place.  It fits nicely into the charm of Media.  I have taken my two kids there on several occasions-sometimes for a meal, sometimes for an ice cream treat.  The service has always been super friendly and the food always quite yummy!  We really like it and sure look forward to going again.

This was my first visit to Sangiovese.  I chose it based largely on reviews I read here and I couldn't be happier at having chosen it.  Both I and my date had pasta dishes which were delicious and our waiter suggested an excellent wine based on our meals as well as our comments as to the types of wines we like.  The staff was friendly and attentive, the ambiance was classy and romantic, and the live music was a fantastic accompaniment and addition to the atmosphere - the music was such that it was very easy to converse but without worrying about voices carrying.   Being originally from central Indiana and having lived in and around Indy for many years before moving west, I was very pleasantly surprised to find this new (to me) restaurant in the area - and I'm glad I did.

Sho Wok has become our go to place for Chinese takeout and delivery in Kirkwood. If you want consistently good food, this is the best we have found in the neighborhood. We have tried every Chinese place since Steak and Rice closed down. The place is nothing fancy. But the kitchen is clean and everyone is very nice. Some of our favorites- the crispy chicken wings, sesame chicken, hot braised chicken boneless, shrimp lo mein, and egg rolls. Give it a try! We did and keep coming back!

I have been here a couple of times but there is a time I walked in and the guy at the counter was really cold and looked at me like I should not even be there. Their food is ok but I dont think I will be going back.

A great sushi restaurant in the Washington Square area! I visited Bleu Sushi on a Saturday night to celebrate the birthday of a friend. 

A friend and I split the signature roll special: 2 signature rolls and a miso soup or salad for $25. We chose the Temple and the South St rolls. I would definitely recommend the Temple roll! The seared peppered fish wrapping the roll added a whole new dimension of flavor.

The service was great as well! The owner of the restaurant came over to greet us personally, and wished my friend a happy birthday. My one complaint was that we felt rushed to leave. There was another large party waiting outside, and the owner kept telling us to take our time with the bill, but "Do you mind if we start cleaning up?" 

Overall, I will definitely be back for the signature roll special again; it's an awesome deal!

The location is great. However, the hotel itself is lacking. First, they'll send an email requesting information, ie are you celebrating a special event, etc and if so, to let them know if you have any requests. So we let them know we were celebrating a special event, and if possible, we would like a room with a view. They responded that it's probably not possible lol but sent us a menu of items we can purchase to make our celebration memorable haha 

This hotel charges around $800/night + parking (whether self parking or valet, it's $50+) + resort fees. And they couldn't be bothered to make it memorable. We got a room with no view and with broken items.

We stayed for 3 nights. The entire stay the television was broken and the water wouldn't get hot. It is winter, and 2 out of the 3 days, it was raining. A hot water shower would've been nice. When I told the front desk, kindly, she was condescending about my complaint. Like I was an idiot for even watching tv lol and she even didn't bother to address the lack of hot water, at all. Instead, she kept asking if I needed an envelope for my folio. No, I do not need an envelope for my receipt lol

Overall, I don't recommend coming here. There's hotels that cost 80% less that provide better service and actually has hot water and working tv's (if you watch tv lol).

Great Family restaurant! We love their brunch better than dinner but great neighborhood joint and they are great with kids!! 

Brunch- cinnamon bun special was amazing as well as the poached eggs!

We just celebrated my daughter's Baptism at Monalisia restaurant and the Management and Staff were absolutely amazing! They made living in Maryland and planning the luncheon a breeze. We were able to drop off the beer and wine the night before and they had it chilled and set up upon our arrival. Banquet Luncheon was 3 courses; salad, pasta and entree. The options we chose were Chicken Monlisia; Veal Alla Milanese and the Crab cake, everyone could not stop talking about how good the food was. They also put out the most amazing roasted peppers and delicious bread. It was delicious. I received so many complements on what a wonderful party it was I am so thankful for the Staff and Management you all really made it a wonderful day! We look forward to coming back for dinner on our trips to NJ! Thank you!

My friend recommended this place on THE HILL because his wife's great grandfather is the recipe creator of their famous hot salami sandwich.

We were greeted by friendly staff. They asked if we had ever been here before and we said no.  He gave us the run down.. Even though my mind was set one thing.

So of course I ordered the salami sandwich on garlic cheese bread and everything but peppercini's and jalapenos. Plus horsey mayo and mustard.

These sandwiches are huge!  I don't know what we were thinking. We should have shared one sandwich! 

With sandwiches in hand, a pop and bag of chips, we sat at the counter looking out on a huge rain storm that rolled in.

The salami was warm, the bread soft, the veggies crisp. I could only east 1/4 of it, but wow..what a taste of the old world!

The place is simple. There's indoor and outdoor seating. The staff is friendly and they are great at advising what is best!

Definitely a great place to grab a sandwich on the way to the airport!
I have passed this place so many times and finally decided to go in because I had a taste for breakfast. It was good I enjoyed it

First time ordering from here, got chicken parm, vodka penne, pizza and a salad. The sauces were very good, I did not expect a pizza place to have that good of sauce, clearly the chef/cook has worked at an Italian restaurant at some point because he/she knows what they are doing.
This will be our new go to from here on out.

This place was so not what we expected. Looking at the menu online, it seems like a nice sit down restaurant: however, it's more of a neighborhood bar. We were still excited to try it as we had been wanting to for a while. We were seated quickly and got our water and soda pretty quickly but were hardly attended to after that. Our food took about 30 mins maybe  more to come out to us. We still were trying to stay positive hoping the food would be good but we were very let down. The burger was ordered medium well and was served with red and blood in it & the fries that were served with it were cold as if they were done long before the burger. The bun to the burger tasted stale and was hard. The steak was ordered medium rare and it was served straight up rare. One side of it looked grilled and the other side looked like it barely took any heat and it also had zero seasoning on the steak. The food took so long originally so we didn't want to even send it back and wait even longer. So I'm an effort not to be difficult, we ate what we could of it and paid, but I ended up leaving pretty much a full plate of food behind. The steak was about $30 and the burger was about $17. It was not a good experience and we likely will not return.
Found this on yelp but unfortunately when you walk in it's very not up to par. Very dissatisfy

They say "you can't make a meal out of side dishes."  It's true. The service and fig salad were both phenomenal, but that's about it. Upon entry we were courteously greeted and made our way to the packed bar to get a drink until our table was ready. We were promptly seated and greeted by our friendly server. 

We started our meal with e delightful fig salad. It was light and refreshing and the vanilla bean vinaigrette was amazing. After that we had the "ricotta." I understand the limitations of ricotta with vegan meals, but they had used way too much lemon in the tofu mixture. The texture was there, but it honestly tasted like Trix cereal. Sorry, vegans, Trix are for kids. 

From there we an order of the chickpea fries. We were warned ahead of time that the portions would be tapas style meant to share ("to gain the full experience"). The fries came out on a plate that looked like someone just smeared aioli with their finger across it. The fries were stacked perfectly like a little chickpea log cabin... All ten of them. They had the taste, texture, and appearance of Lincoln logs. There was barely enough aioli to cut down the dryness of what I can only assume was reclaimed fried hummus.

To cap off our meal we had baby leeks with romesco (Which admittedly I was excited to read as romanesco... Not the same thing) and the heirloom beans. Both tasted wonderful but were laughably small, even as tapas.

Throughout this experience we sampled many of the drinks, all of which were served in glasses barely half full, is there a liquor shortage we're unaware of? Is this place supposed to be prohibition themed? No, they actually don't seem to have a theme. From their crystal chandeliers to the green lamps above the bar to the LED lights on the bar and book shelves, from the teal painted walls to the curtained wall with classic black and white films projected on loop, there's a whole lot going on without much to say. 

Charlie was a sinner, but he also probably had the appetite of a small bird. Guys, I think Charlie was a bird. It is their logo after all.

Kept hearing about this place so finally decided to check it out! I contacted them on Instagram and easily made a reservation. They answered promptly and it was no issue at all! I literally got a margarita and then some appetizers, the quesadilla and then the guac, bean, queso trio. All were so delicious, came out hot, on time! Service was great! Everything came out super fast, super attentive and never once did I feel like I was being rushed! Great spot to start out the night, prices  were very reasonable! I can't wait to come back! Oh also they play great music!

Took the wife here on our 14 year anniversary and it was fantastic. Our waiter Willey was great. He was knowledgeable and helpful.  He explained the menu in detail and help us pick an authentic German dinner and a beer the go with it. I will most definitely be coming back and this time with friends.

Pretty good pizza. Went there with some friends for a late dinner after drinks. It didn't take very long -- only about 15-20 minutes. The staff was very friendly, and they have a variety of pizza options.

You can probably tell from the pics but we got the Margherita pizza and grilled barbecue chicken. The pizza isn't super greasy -- it's just the right amount. I will say that they went light on the sauce though, especially on the barbecue pizza but it was still really good.

Be aware: the pizzas here are HUGE! Don't expect to cuddle up with a friend and watch a movie with one of these because half of it will still be there (especially if you get a big one)! And that being said, if you're going for a medium pizza, the large is only a dollar more a lot of the time. Go for it. Such a good value!
Had a great time with my son. We came here to kill time before our movie and after the movie we ended up going back before they closed and played some more.
Wonderful Italian food. The house salad is amazing. Sunday family style lunch is also great! I always recommend the daily special. It has never disappointed me once.

This Taco Bell is quick and the order is always right.  The staff is friendly as well, which says a lot for a fast food restaurant.  I always use the drive through  because I generally come here during lunch on a workday...

IOU Sushi isn't your high class sushi joint by any means, but it is a solid option.  I have been there once and I would probably go back.  We went with a group of 5 people and were seated pretty quickly, but like a lot of reviews state it goes downhill from there.  If there is one thing that needs work it is the service.  It is extremely slow, and almost feels like you're a bother to them.  We all ordered all you can eat sushi with the exception of one and it took a minute for the server to acknowledge.  When we finally got our orders we almost had to look around and see where she was and make eye contact while waving our order sheets to get our next round.  I wouldn't call it a deal breaker but it definitely needs some work.  Now the sushi like I said isn't high class or even pretty, but it was really good.  It wasn't blowing my mind, but it was good enough that I would brave the poor service for the price.  All you can eat for around $25 bucks is really good.  This isn't the cleanest place either,  but it wasn't dirty enough to make you cringe and want to scour the place looking for roaches.  I will happily edit this review when I go back if things have improved.  For now, I wouldn't make this your first choice but if it's convenient, and you want some sushi come check it out.

Great location and great price!

We got a good deal for a Saturday night stay - $49 after taxes plus $10 for a rollaway bed divided by 4 people = less than $15 per person.

The room was big enough to fit the 4 of us, but would probably be cramped if we stayed more than one night. 

Located in the heart of downtown Reno and connected to 2 other hotels (Silver Legacy and Circus Circus), this is a great hotel that is close to everything! 

There's a lot of options to eat around the hotel and bars to hang out in after dinner. We especially liked the Brew Brother's brewery for cheap beers and great music! There was a live band there that night and plenty of space on the dance floor. Good times.

I would definitely stay here again because of the convenience of the location and variety of resaurants and bars inside the hotel. It was nice not having to venture out in the freezing cold weather to look for entertainment.

Best Thai in Tampa. Amazing authentic Shrimp Green Curry. You can just taste all the wonderful spices in this dish. Made with love. Awesome service with a smile. Hard to find but hard to forget the food. Run as quick as you can if your a foodie like me, looking for authentic Thai cuisine. 5+ Stars.

Yellow Belly is one of my new favorite places. It always seems to be bustling but it has a cozy feel to it. There are two outdoor patios and a small indoor area. The ambiance makes YB seem more like a house than a restaurant. The beer is great and the servers are friendly. I had the brussels sprouts and Mac n cheese. Topped that off with sharing their delicious chocolate chip cookie with my friend. Overall, YB is a great place to hang out and grab a bite. I will definitely be back.

I took my friend here to celebrate his birthday so I wanted to treat him to the Sunday brunch. First, I want to highlight that the food was amazingly good. However, there were waaaay too much people the buffet line with such a tight space. It took us 20 minutes just to move through the line. It took so long we decided it wasn't worth taking a second trip back. Although I feel I didn't get my monies worth, I would definitely come back during regular dinner hours.

Love this place! Has been really enjoyable for many years.  The sushi is fresh and the tempura perfectly fried.

Have been coming here for years.

Food was AMAZING! Though, service? Meh. Whether you feel welcome or just lucky to be there is a matter of service. And, I have to say, we were made to feel just lucky to be there. Definitely worth the food. Ambiance is lovely too. This is not their first rodeo.

When I want a gourmet pizza, I go to Anthony's.  When I want something that is similar to the pizza style I had in New Jersey growing up, I go to Best NY Pizza.  It's not exactly like NJ Pizza or NY pIzza but close enough.  You can fold the slice.  My favorite here is a bacon/pineapple pizza, which my granddaughter is starting to like.

Interesting joint. Birdcage meets Red Robin. Food is a tad pricey but you pay for the experience. We didn't find the food to be overly flavored, it was bland at best. 
Not sure if I'll ever return. Just wasn't impressed.

A wonderful experience. The food, the bourbon and atmosphere were briliant. Tom out server went out I God way to give us a great evening. I can't speak more highly of the place. You must give it a go.

My wife and I had lunch today at the George Jones for the first time. We thoroughly enjoyed the atmosphere, restaurant, music, refreshments and the food. 

My wife had the pulled pork sandwich, Cole slaw and a glass of wine. She was pleased and couldn't eat all of the big portions. I had the full order of 10 wings with the sauce on the side and a basket of waffle fries. The food was hot, tasty and plentiful. I ate all of mine but should have gotten the half order! I'm stuffed! Washed it all down with a cold beer or two... 

The restaurant was clean, service was great. Left the server a 20% tip and it was well earned. The live Music was super, and it allowed us to relax on the river side with a view, and enjoy the tunes. 

It was not very busy at all on this Sunday at 12:30, but the Predators game was not over just yet. We came at a good time and enjoyed it! I recommend The George Jones... and check out the rocking chairs too. I do need one!

Great nugget in the middle of the lovely small town Carpinteria. It has a low-key, casual vibe that makes you immediately feel comfortable, and you can trust the beer on tap is carefully selected. There's also a sweet parking lot right behind that always tends to have open spaces, so that's a definite score for the girl who always has trouble finding parking (aka me). 

They were pretty busy on a Friday night, so my friends and I ended up sitting at the communal table with other folks. We weren't exactly given that much attention, so we had to wait a while to get our order taken. My friend and I had the tri-tip sandwiches (her's had pico de Gallo and I had the BBQ sauce). The meat was great, but was definitely a mouth workout. I thought the flavors were great and finished the entire thing without actually feeling bloated! Score. Plus I looked cool finishing it and drinking a beer after. Double score.

They have a wide selection of draft beers and some rotating guest local beers, and the prices aren't so bad. The bar is usually occupied by the old men of the town, so I got a kick out of watching them interact loudly while watching sports. Also, the patio is really chill. 

Great place to hang out with people and just enjoy a good meal with good drinks. I'm a fan!

I will never give this place another chance. Service is always horrible. They may be friendly, but they are incompetent and inefficient!! This last time, we went for breakfast and were there for 90mims for only 3 simple breakfasts! After 45 mins of no food and No server, I sought out manager to ask about food, it was almost another 10 mins before we got our food! The server took 10 mins after we asked for bill, to bring bill. He took another 10mins to bring back my credit card. Food is decent but by far NOTHING special. I ordered the crazy Karen has browns (hash browns w.peppers and onions and eggs).....the charge $7.29 which would have been fine had I got a real serving. There wasn't even a half cup of hash browns and only one egg on top! I am fine w.small servings but I am not paying $7.29 for a half cup of hash downs!!
We love supporting locally owned, but this place desperately needs new management or owners or staff or ALL 3
Great environment and food (breakfast and lunch only) nice selection of healthy breakfast and lunch menu as well. Hours is limited. Open 7 am to 230 pm daily.

This place used to be one of my favorites. A recent visit included chicken cutlet parmesan that was right out of a box with a single slice of provolone on top. I should have sent it back. Too bad, the sauce was still good ... but, I won't be going back. Not the food I expect for the price I paid.

Just has my boyfriends birthday party at the karaoke lounge upstairs of Fuji mountain. The red room comes with a bathroom and a doorbell (to order drinks when you want it). The servers came promptly and it was definitely a good time for the price paid... Perfect for a group of people looking to sing karaoke stress free in an enclosed area!

Gio's is a new addition to the Maple Glen Shopping center and is owned by the same people that run the Jarrettown Hotel.

As stated in other reviews their Pizza is THIN crust. (I haven't tried the pizza yet)  On this visit my girlfriend and I split a Grilled Chicken Panini with honey mustand and Caeser salad.  The salad was a good size for $5.95 and the Panini was tasty.  The bread was fresh and the chicken was very moist.

Although Gio's was clean and reasonably priced they didn't have anything that makes me want to make a special trip to go there.

I have to say I went in with HIGH expectation's.. I mean Guadalajara on Prince level expectations, and I'm super bummed to report this is not the Prince Rd location at all. Between the stale chips, our awkward and lackluster service and underwhelming food I will unfortunately be traveling to the Prince Rd location from now on.

I love this place. Spicy tofu is incredible. Spicy eggplant is heavenly. They have the best service, I have picked up carry out several times and eaten in. I've never been disappointed. My goal is to try everything on their menu! Probably my favorite places to eat in St. Louis. I guess I don't have pics bc I'm too excited to eat when I go. I'll try to add topics the next time I'm there.

Ordered the "Taste of New Orleans" (gumbo, jambalaya, and etoufee sampler), marinated crab claws, crawfish ravioli, and the oyster duo. The crab claws were by far the tastiest and most flavorful. Everything else was quite bland to be honest, and each dish came out lukewarm which was disappointing. The atmosphere is cute though, especially the upstairs balcony area. I probably would not come back though due to my lackluster experience.

Well, I wish I would have read the reviews prior to eating here.  I walked up to the first hostess bar and the lady is talking on the phone just staring at me.  Never makes eye contact, a manager walks by and doesn't say anything.  Um, I probably should have left but I'm still feeling good.  It's a beautiful Sunday afternoon.  Finally another hostess arrives and tells me it is self-seating upstairs.  I go upstairs and this is why they get 3 stars - the patio area is lovely!  Loved the view, great place to go on a date and just chill.  However, I waited 7 minutes and finally had to grab a server and ask for a menu and a glass of water.  Now, other people came in after me and were seated with menus but somehow no one noticed me!  I had to stand out, I was the only "solo" diner in the place.  The food was okay.  It wasn't great.  Soup was $5.  Purchased 2 entrees - fish taco ($8 - mango yum) and shrimp ($8 - very spicy with sour cream and rice, interesting).  Once again the food was good, but not great.  I like the Brewery (nothing like A-B at home, but still a nice touch).  Good selection of beer.  Service was very lacking....I like local places but I think I should have went to Joe's Crab Shack next door.....

The burgers are absolutely delicious. Like really delicious. The fries were absolutely delicious. It's a shame that the cashiers are so nasty and rude here. We were on our honeymoon and excited to try this place from many referrals but the service was so awful I would never waste my time again going here. If it was just one person with a rude attitude I would probably  just go about my business but it was multiple people. Talking to customers with disgust and attitudes acting inconvenienced. I'm aware it's a busy place but nobody wants to pay $60 somewhere working who can't be polite or even give a hello when people walk in.
That's just common business practice nothing outstanding. So while the food was actually amazing when I tell people about this place I have to warn them about what they will encounter. I just am dumbfounded by how the older gentlemen in front of us was spoken to and the rolling of eyes by the staff when THEY messed up the order. It's just sad because the food was so good.

My wife and I had dinner at the Hermitage Steak House tonight.  Service was excellent.  The salad bar was clean, fresh, and a lot variety and options.  Steaks were cooked to perfection.   Definitely the perfect spot for a Date Night
Always tasty and great menu items. I would give 5 stars but they fill their soap bottles in the bathroom with water and that's just gross in my opinion. So we bring our own soap! BYOS!

New place that recently opened in a former bakery space and some other prior business.  It's right next to Benny the Bums Seafood which has been around for some time, so I guess this space just needs the right tenant to stay open for a while.

For now, they offer their standard rolls @ 50% off, and special rolls @ 20% off.  I do not know how long this will last or it is a marketing gimmick.  They have it right in their take out menu so I think it is the latter.  I had a total order of $21 for 1 special roll (Red Lobster - Asparagus, avocado, crunchy inside, spicy lobster on top) and 3 regular (Crunchy Spicy Scallop, Shrimp Tempura, Shrimp Avocado).

All of the sushi was average with nothing to absolutely rave about, but it certainly was not bad.  I would go back for a sushi fix.    

The restaurant was dark inside with a wooden bench for waiting for take out.  It seats about 40.  Staff was pleasant and well tempered to deal with the jackass who had so many specifics for the $100 order he wanted for takeout.  Even I was getting angry with his belittling the staff.  I hope they got everything right!

I'll have to try the non-sushi offerings someday.
LNice, Saturday games are in Altamont. First game at git c:30. Sunday game are at hl lou lllit5lx5l it 5c

Love the food here, the service is wonderful!! I wish I could eat here everyday, but I was coming to this place a lot on my off days.. Lol  The prices for the food and drinks are very reasonable. I haven't tried to many dishes here, but my favorite was the white queso, the shrimp fajitas, and my kids loved the burgers,  chicken fingers, and the chicken quesadillas..  I had took a friend out to this place, and he just loved it. He told me this will be his go to place when he come back to visit me..lol he also had the shrimp and steak fajita and he also had the margarita with a Corona.. To bad I couldn't have any margaritas.. :(  next time for sure!!!

We really love this BYOB for very affordable and authentic Central American food, such as pupusas and Honduran enchiladas that we can't find elsewhere locally.  Don't let the fact that it is usually fairly empty scare you away...it seems they do a fairly active delivery or take out business.  Added benefit is that you can bring a fairly large group there for events and they can be very accommodating.
Great food, service and atmosphere. The food was amazing! Can't go wrong with any of the dishes. My favorite was the flat bread, grilled octopus and The seared scallops, gnocchi & soft boiled egg.

One of the best little skyline's I've been too.  Cafeteria style ordering, very clean, GM Jordan was making the food and was very friendly.

Love me some skyline and will be back to this spot!

I've been working in the area for about 5+ years now and must admit I had never stepped into this establishment until recently, and I'm glad that I finally did!  One of the new staff here recommended this place to me so I checked it out.  They suggested "the special" which includes a quarter of a sub sandwich, a really small soup, and a drink.  Admittedly I was overwhelmed upon entering as you need to fill out a form with small pencils and hand it to the first sandwich maker in the line of friendly women staffed there and they begin to assemble your sandwich as you head to self serve your soup.  I am not over exaggerating when I say that this may have been one of the best lunches I've ever had while working in this area.  The flavor of the meats and cheeses are fresh like the additional ingredients they use.  Their soup is OUT OF THIS WORLD! I recommend the Shrimp Corn Chowder. The atmosphere is also nice.  The only drawback of this place is that the price is towards the higher range for what you get.

They seated us right away and I now realize why. The service was mediocre and the food was not great. I had the Cochon and it was just really salty. The Mac n cheese side was bland and not incredibly tasty. 
   I don't often dislike everything about my meal but this time I really did. Oh wait , the bread was good. I paid a lot of money for good bread!

Heeeey! This place had a super cool vibe from the moment we walked in. Small place, limited seating, line out the door on weekends which made the wifey and I try it on a Monday morning. Walked right in, a hip waiter sat us down and was at the top of his game. Drinks were topped off throughout breakfast, helped with recommendations and the chef/mgr even came out to ask how everything was. Pulled Pork Benedict was delicious and the wife's Monte Cristo was "something special", as the waiter called it... the seating is tight quarters so be prepared to talk to strangers cause it may feel like you sitting with them. Social butterfly friendly. In other words, if you are a Debbie Downer or anti social you're better off hitting the IHop around the corner. This place ain't for you! But if you are a foodie, bite the bullet, sit your butt down and get to grubbing cause this was the biz!

Came back for breakfast and was not disappointed. I ordered the apple cinnamon French toast and my friend ordered the blueberry pancakes. On Saturday's, those two items have a special for $8.99 each. I preferred the pancakes over the French toast. I could taste actual blueberries in the pancakes and it was so good. Two pancakes can feed 2 people. They are also very generous with the amount of butter. The French toast was good, but I wish I tasted the apple. It was good French toast, but I wouldn't order it again. My special came with fresh squeezed orange juice and hands down the freshest orange juice I ever had! I want to come back and try lunch next time...and get the famous apple dumplings again!
Must eat outside! Not aware of that. Food was good. Churros great!!!! Best I ever had.

My daughter and I ate here before a show at the Mahaffey and had delicious meals.  We were seated promptly and our server was very attentive.  We had calamari which was very good but not the best I've ever had.  I had eggplant parmesan and my daughter had lasagne which were both excellent.  We would have tried dessert, but were in a hurry to leave.  We will definitely be back!

This is the sorriest excuse for what Popeye's was at one time!  We chose the fried fish combo and it was a disgusting example of over fried tasteless food ever!  The fish was fried to the point of being fragile!  I picked up a piece and it and the fried broke when I tried to bite !  The sweet tea a tasteless tan water!  Left the food here n the trash....   not even good enough to feed the dogs a treat!


WHAT HAPpENED to POPEYES????   Not my idea of "food"!!!!   The commercials are a joke!!!!!!!  Been a while since we tried but they will not ever see me again!


Here is what the staff did as we were leaving!  Walked to the window facing our car in the handicap spot and laughed and waved til we left the parking lot!  One black employee and two Hispanic girls!!!  Not many manors in their upbringing!  Race or color has no bearing on this...  mentioned only so hq knows who was on duty at 610pm on 15 August!  It isn't just your food that needs amending!  I do not care if you are stripped and polka dotted!  You belong to the human race and you owe some respect!   Really saddened at the experience!
Lesson learned!!!!!!

Really a pleasant experience. It is better once inside.  Great wait staff, good suggestions.  I will take friends there when going to the  downtown.  The asperigass appetizer was a great find. I'll try the bar next time since it looks like a great gathering spot.

Beer selection was good.  Staff was prompt and attentive.  Food was bland and unremarkable.  Salad that accompanied the entree was very small and lacked substance.  Shaved Brisket in crepes was overwhelmed by a nacho cheese sauce.  Added heat was odd since any real flavors were missing.  Cilantro amounted to a few flakes on top. Will not return- there is better food out there.
This is my Thai restaurant. The food is full of favor and well balanced with the spices. My favorite is the crispy curry duck. Yum

This is the best meal I've ever had. Our server was fabulous and had answers to anything you could possibly think about asking about the menu. We were vacationing near the beach and took a 5 min Uber to the restaurant but then just walked back bc it wasn't far. You can't make a bad choice on this menu, everything from appetizer to dessert was unique and special. I had the burger because I love burgers and it was the best I've had anywhere (and I've had a lot of burgers). It's quiet and super comfortable outdoor seating. FYI it's beer and wine only but fancy cocktails would honestly just distract from the beautiful and delicious food. We loved it and will def be back!!!

I made reservations to take my Lady out for her birthday this past Thursday Night before a Blues Show. The Four Seasons was very nice & classy the staff were very friendly & courteous. 

We went up to the 8th Floor to the Restaurant it was very trendy & romantic. The Host was very Friendly & greeted us promptly. We were seated at a scenic table with a view inside. We looked over the menu we were given bread and water galore.

We ordered our food she had the Chicken dish & I had the Ravioli. We had great conversation while waiting for our meal. The wait was very long and the Restaurant was not crowded at all. There was a forty minute wait and we had reservations so I would hate to see the wait time when it is very busy.

We finally received our meal & drinks it was well seasoned & nice to the taste buds. The waiter was very friendly & always asked if we needed anything. 

The quality of food was very good. My lady really enjoyed herself and she stated that she gives it a 8 on a scale of 1 to 10. But the only thing is the quantity of food for the price there needs to be more food provided. If you are paying more the food needs to be more.....Needs more quantity of food for the price.

Overall the Staff were very friendly and courteous. The atmosphere was trendy and romantic and we really enjoyed ourselves. We will go back again! She says next time she wants the Ribs! lol

Yum! Came for dinner, and would definitely come back. Started with some sweet and sour margaritas, and BLT bites. Fish tacos were tasty with a hint of spice, liver and onions (Thursday night special) was great, kids enjoyed the chicken strips. Key lime pie was sucked down quickly. Cheesecake was good, just felt heavy compared to the light fluffy key lime pie. Would definitely come back!

Tower Grove Park is the best park in the city. It has lots of gazebos and grills where you can celebrate holidays, birthdays, or just throw a sweet party. The park has a number of paths and roads that make it perfect for a bike ride or run. On July 4th, 2015, my boyfriend of 5 years proposed to me by the pond near the center of the park which is a scenic spot fit for a date or for wedding photos. Every Saturday during the late spring to mid autumn you will find the Tower Grove Park Farmers Market by the playground.
Absolutely loved the cheesesteak with hot peppers. Steak was fresh, the bread is amazing and service and friendliness makes me want to come back!!

Blue Sage has been my go to place during the Lenten season for the past few years! As someone who eats meat, I had doubts about trying it initially since it's a 100% vegetarian but I was pleasantly surprised and now I'm hooked! 

I love the feel of this place -- it's very charming. It's pretty small so I recommend that you make a reservation especially if you plan to go on a Friday or Saturday evening. Please also note that it's BYOB and the dessert menu changes occasionally. 

The adobo goat cheese nachos are a must try! I also recommend the black bean soup, the mediterranean sampler, the blue corn asparagus tacos, and the falafel wrap. 

The only dish which I'm not fond of is the wild mushroom risotto.

So.... this is my first time here.  
It's a BOB business and I always want to give a BOB a 5 star ...just because.  
But... I'm feeling some-kinda-way.
They are stuck in the 1970's
It's a place that my mom would probably LOVE!
a lot of 1970's music.
I'll start from the beginning 
We got here 5 minutes before our reservation and was told that we needed half of our party here to be seated... totally understandable, however once our party arrived we still weren't seated for another 30 minutes afterwards.  The service was fast after we were seated.  The server(s) weren't friendly AT ALL!  The food wasn't good to me.  Sorry, I really wanted to love it... I traveled 2 1/2 hours and only ate breakfast so I'd have plenty room.
I ordered the catfish, it came with greens and grits. I had a side of cornbread, sweet potatoes, and Mac &. cheese. I only ate the fish.  Nibbled on the other stuff but it just wasn't good.  I alway take left overs home...but nope not this time and I had plenty left over.
To the owners...
I could have easily written a 2 star review.
But I don't want to hurt your business and lower your ratings.   I hope that you will read this and make significant improvements.
1. Honor reservation times... or compensate  someway if you aren't able to. ( maybe free dessert or something) sometimes you have to take a lose to retain customers.
2. Make customers aware of the environment to expect.  I'm not a old school Gail.  I like today's music.  Your karaoke guys (team) are too much... overbearing and stuck in the back when... my opinion. 
3. Service ... maybe our girl was having a bad day or long day.  I get it but it can't rub off on your customers.  She was Flat , blunt , argumentative and generally grumpy.  Nothing friendly or pleasant about the experience. 
4. The food...is what it is... I'm sure some folks love it... I didn't. 


You have people traveling from other cities to visit your restaurant ... make it a memorable experience so that they can't wait to do it again.  Just my 2 cents!
Wanted to try a new spot for lunch. They have a stage for live music and an open seating area. Hubby ordered the wings and I got the burger. Both were good and service was quick and friendly.
So good. I'd take a photo of my food but I already ate it. Had the cauliflower omelette, sounds weird, but it was delicious! Come here, seriously.

This cool place has a creative, delicious, and healthy menu, not to mention a good drinks list as well.  Staff was attentive and knowledgeable.  Sit at the Chef's bar if you're solo or in a couple.  Don't pass up the opportunity to eat here!

Came here with a reservation but waited 20 min to be seated. We have the breakfast bite, seafood paella, and churros. All of them were well made and delicious. The lighting in the restaurant was soft and dark which created a intimate ambience.

I've been looking for a new burger place ever since the Motoraunt shut down and I think Sodajerks may be it. The decor is a mix of retro and sports bar, which was interesting. 

We ordered onion rings for an appetizer, along with a kids burger for the little one, while my wife tried the Macho Nacho and I had the Bacon Jerk burger. 

The onion rings were nice and crisp and had the right onion to batter ratio so that they were neither soft and greasy or too oniony. The little one had a rootbeer shake, but she said it tasted more like a sweet vanilla shake than rootbeer - although since none of us ever had one anywhere else, we weren't really sure how it was supposed to taste. I tried a sip and it was okay, but I'd probably go with chocolate or something else next time. 

The Macho Nacho is essentially a plate of nachos in a bun, and it was really delicious, with the cheese and bacon mixing with the nacho crunch. The Bacon Jerk was basically a huge Big Mac with bacon on it and was very filling.  

Next time, I think I want to try making my own burger, although it seems daunting, givne that each part of the burger: bun, meat, cheese, and veggies has so many options to choose from (at least 7 or 8 choices in each category) as shown on the burger worksheet. 

https://www.sodajerks.net/uniquely-creative-burger-worksheet/

They also have wild options like adding a Froot Loops, Doritos, Kraft Dinner or a perogy to your burger! 

All in all, Sodajerks is a solid choice for both families or groups to come and try something different when you're craving a burger.
This a great sports bar with great food and an awesome staff.  The nachos are great and the potato skins are fantastic.  I highly recommend stopping here for lunch or dinner.

First and only time I'll go.  Cold food dry brisket even though the sign claims you can pick which cut you want, you get what they give you.  For a smoke hot se there wasn't any hint of the meat being smoked.  Tasted like it came out of the oven at home. Also had the tri-tip sandwich on the order and it was raw.
The food is delicious, the decor is cute, and the restaurant is really clean. However, what I like most about Buho's is the friendly staff! Our waitress was so patient, polite, and helpful!
Fast sushi is a great concept but they should offer more "labeled" roll or description of ingredients

Tried this place for the first time and enjoyed it. We sat in the patio because it had rained and was nice out. 
The burrata was probably the hit of the night. Everything else was good but that was great. 
Drinks were good but they didn't have some basic staples. 
Service was solid. Will definitely go back!

Food was good, bus boy was great! However our waitress was terrible and tried charging us for games on the kiosk which wasn't even touched and to top it off she said that charge is always on there and they just don't tell anyone..WOW really?!?! Purposely ripping people off. Thank God I looked at my charges, zero tip for the lazy, worthless, slow as sloth waitress but tipped the awesome bus boy.

Walked in after seeing a line down the block and bomb reviews. 

I saw 2 roaches run across the floor. Waitress said it's an African tree bug that came in from outside and that the owner was aware of it. She gave us the option to stay and eat. We decided against it as everyone was starting at the bugs and eating as if it was appetizing. 

Not for me.  No thank you.

Our first stop in Tucson and it did not disappoint! Excellent tacos, amazing chips (they are free too!) and delish horchata. I think the al pastor tacos were my favorite. The corn and flour tortillas were both good but the flour was better in my opinion. We sat outside and it was lovely.

While the service was a little slow, the pizza was amazing and the server was very nice and helpful. It's not a place to go for a quick lunch but if you want a good homemade artisan pizza or cup of soup and have an hour to kill, this is a nice place.
Loved it. Great food, wonderful staff! The bring the sides right to the table, then you order the entree. All-you-can-eat fried chicken was great, whole catfish was perfect. Hushpuppies were awesome.
Went for first time today and sat at bar for lunch.  Grilled chicken salad was excellent and so was the service.  Think I found my new healthy lunch spot!

We had a lovely first experience here. We ordered steamed pork dumplings, which were made from scratch! They were fluffy and delicious and the sauce that came with them was also homemade and very good. We had sautéed shrimp and pork with broccoli next, all very good. Our server was Susan. She was so welcoming and friendly. I look forward to going back soon.

Sincerely amazed! It was a Friday night and the place was PACKED! I had this incredible bar tender! She was really something! Out of all these people hungry and needing drinks she gave me individual attention and made sure I had my drink and got my food almost immediately! I was blown away! I'm a bit on the buzzed side, so I'm hoping I left her a decent tip but I have to say the service was GREAT and the food was really good. I'm just a very happy customer and I'm picky. I sincerely hope everyone will try this place. I'm a Nashville native and for roof top dining (partying) this is THE PLACE
My Wife and I enjoy going here yesterday was the first time we had lunch there. Also first time we did not use the rocks. We had burgers and fries. The food was great.

Came here late morning on a Monday and it took over 50 minutes to get our food. It's toast and eggs, traditionally the fastest food to prepare. It would've been nice to know the wait time would be that long in advance. Just to be clear this was after placing an order and being seated, it's not as though we were in a crazy line up out the door to be seated for brunch on a Sunday like at other establishments. I'd say the place was half full. The couple that came in after us complained and was offered a free coffee cake. We were waiting far longer and weren't offered any such accommodation. 

The food was good don't get me wrong, but not at all good enough to justify the wait time.

I absolutely love this place!  It's a little pricy and the atmosphere may not be for everybody (skater/surfer), but the quality of the food is great.  Everything is fresh, daily.  No big walk-in freezer where things are stored overnight for weeks.  I always get a "bowl" and there's so much food I can't finish.  The selection of organic teas are amazing!  I did start to notice a decline in the restaurant but there appears to have been a recent management change.  The place looks better since the first time I went.  

So much better since Chipotle!!  It's one of St. Pete's hidden great places.
Went here for Fathers Day and my husband loved everything from the ambiance, service, and food. I would highly recommend this location

Stopped in around 10:30 yesterday morning (a non-holiday Monday) and was very impressed by 1) the friendliness of the wait staff, and 2) the quality of the coffee. The atmosphere is relaxed and I could easily imagine how it works well as a nighttime live music venue. Along with my dark roast coffee, I also ordered the potato + avocado + asparagus + poached egg food option, which I found tasty but was admittedly about 85% potatoes (for $8). I'm not sure this would ever be my top pick food option, but I certainly hope/plan to be back for more coffee and perhaps some evening music at some point.

Not as good as in years past, service has fallen off of late.

May strike from fav list unless they can regroup.

We were in the area just visiting & picked this place on a whim. Excellent beer, even better food. We had the pretzel, beef brisket, bbq sliders, poutine tots. The place is beautiful and clean. The owner & staff are very friendly & we didn't wait long. I would definitely recommend this place!
Good tea and nice place to study! They have a little quiet room to do work and they have a huge variety of loose leaf tea to choose from.

So my friend was recently tragically diagnosed with a dairy allergy. We decided to give this place a try for her birthday so she didn't have to worry about her allergy. We went for brunch and it wasn't too busy but I'd make a reservation for a larger party. The portions were just enough and the service was very nice but a little on the slower side. I think it was meant to make us more relaxed and enjoy our food more. Also no WiFi because it's an ~oasis~ (there's a sign here that will explain this comment).

I came here last week and ordered the steak and white cheddar panini and this is what was served to me! We called the manager and showed him and he said that was the regular portion but even he had to admit that it didn't look that appetizing. This can't be the regular portion. It looks nothing like the picture on the menu!  The meat doesn't even look like meat!!  This should not have even come out the kitchen to be served to customers. The manager did take care of the matter for us and brought out another sandwich with much better looking meat and a bigger portion. Needless to say I had higher expectations from Panera.

Food looks as good as the pictures! Had the cream brûlée French toast. It's was amazing! You have to order this!! Also enjoyed the dunk  your donut martini it was  also delicious. My little one ordered the mini pancakes and bacon off the kids menu. Unfortunately they were out of the monkey bread heard that was amazing have to try that next time. Also ordered the breakfast tacos tasted great but came out cold they took it off the bill. Overall everyone was very happy with their food and drinks we were there on Super Bowl Sunday! Go Buc's!!!

It's been a year or so since our family's last visit to this location.  Thought we would give it another try.  Bad decision.  Took over 30 minutes to get our food, service is painfully slow, and way overpriced for the quality.  A coke is 2.99!  Would love to have that decision back, I'd go to Culver's up the road all day long versus this place.  Moreover, there appears to be dust or grime on fixtures if you look closely, tables are poorly cleaned and my shoes were sticking to the floor...kinda gross.

Fabulous place nestled in quaint Nolensville.   Their chicken salad is amazing.  It has cranberries and pecans which make it extra special.  The Mac and cheese is incredibly creamy and delicious.   Terrific service!!  I will go back the next time I am in the area.

Enjoy the mediocre tiki bar above Felipe's! The bartenders got that sass but the drinks are on fleek. One can conveniently order food from the full Felipe's menu up. The hurricanes here are like no other, way more fruity and delicious.

One of my favorite sushi places..
GREAT sushi, CHEAP prices!

Right now it's still BYOB I think, but they are working on getting a liquor license.

I never tried their all-you-can-eat deal....

Restaurant severs processes cream   Any half healthy restaurant knows this is unhealthy. Serve real cream. My omelette was very bland without much taste. Would not return to many other better choices.

Had a mediocre dinner at the Italian place next store, so we came here for coffee and desert, which was very yummy and very filling. I also see that they've begun serving a dinner service, which I'm anxious to try.

Right on the beaten path, the Eagle boasts a wonderful well placed location. It was little hectic according to hostess, just missing happy hour. We sat at the bar. The helpful half hearted bartender insisted we got the hearty helping half chicken with hot honey. The chicken was heaping and hardly healthy, not hard, and very tender. The homey atmosphere, combined with food, which was all home made, made it feel like home. I'm now a habitual Eagle-goer

Il Granaio is 'practically' in my backyard (if we did not have a creek with wetlands running between us which is apparently the residence of a rangale or mob of deer) with no proper pathway to traverse to this fine restaurant except via Concord Road! We've been venturing over to dine here ever since it opened and in the past my hubs has taken multiple visiting international business partners with great success! Juan provided stellar attention when serving these guests and we usually would ask for him when making our reservation!  He has become a wonderful friend over the past years; and we certainly missed him and dining here during the upset of 2020!  
This past week it was delightful to see him again!  Although he was engaged  with other guests, he took a moment to stop by our table and exchange a greeting and update news since our last visit!

We enjoyed delightful service on this visit with charming wait-service staff, Catlille (sp?), who anticipated every need and graciously met them! That might have been the highlight of our visit, if the cuisine did not once again, ROCK!!  I started our celebratory dining with a Rossini cocktail, Proseco with purred strawberries, served delightfully in a chilled champagne flute; followed by the tastiest Beets & Burrata appetizer! I ate it all!  Too good to save a bit for leftovers! Golden beets are ALWAYS a treat and IL GRANAIO'S burrata is some of the BEST I've tasted, coast to coast in USA and even Italy!

All of my former favorites were on the menu and the Veal Marsala did not disappoint! Tender and succulent as always with a most generous portion which our son enjoyed immensel! I was planing on my former fav, their Chicken Parmigiana, until I noticed a new entree, Paccheri Alla Norma, which included the largest pasta (paccheri) I've ever seen, freshly produced in-house and lathered in a rich pomodoro sauce of stewed tomatoes with  garlic, onion and chunks of delicious eggplant topped with a generous dollop of herbed ricotta cheese! OMGosh! It was titillatingly delicious! I was THRILLED the portion was large enough to take home half the serving for a most satisfying lunch the next day! This dish is NOW my 'house specialty' from their menu!

I had ABSOLUTELY no room for their exquisite rendition of Tiramisu for dessert and will return swiftly later this month for DESSERT first to celebrate my birthday!

Tune in again to learn what the *others* in our party of 4 devoured because I have run out of room and enticing descriptors for their menu choices!  BUT, NO ONE left unssatisfied and none of us had any room for dessert!

Every time I go running along Delaware Ave, I have to seriously fight the urge to give up and get a hot combo at Johnny's Hots. The sausage is bursting with flavor and is spicy like a sausage should be. The bun is fresh and is full-bodied enough to withstand all the umph from the sausage. The fish cake on top doesn't look like much, but its salty goodness really drives the whole thing home. One might feel out of place standing in line here if they are not a trucker or other blue collar worker, but this is some real high quality stuff, and they shouldn't get to have ALL the fun.

You may have a desire to get a cheesesteak here after seeing that Philly Mag rated it the best in the city in 2010. Do not do this unless you enjoy the feeling of disappointment. If you're going to be on Delaware/Columbus anyway, might as well head south and make a stop at John's Roast Pork.

We order the antipasto plate with Italian salami, cheese and bread as well as the pizza pane, all of which was incredible. All the ingredients were very fresh and the perfect temperature. Finally we ordered the pizza with prosciutto, arugula and fresh mozzarella. It is one of the best pizzas I have had in St Louis. The service was friendly and ambience was comfortable. Really loved the Italian music!
My husband and I both had the Prime Rib and they tasted like a pair of leather shoes.
Staff here are great.  Food was delious.  I had the oyster and the grill shrimp sandwich And it was at a perfect price.
Whose idea was it to put velveeta in a chile rellano. Yuk.

Brand new restaurant,  went once for dinner and Sunday for Brunch.  Fascinating menu with very creative choices.  Chef Andrew was on duty Sunday and went out of his way to explain that the restaurant makes almost everything in house including growing their own greens.  For adventurous dinners this place is a must.  More beer choices than a pub and excellent coffees roasted in house.  The menu is a constant surprise and don't be afraid to try something different

It was really difficult trying to narrow our choices for takeout. Ultimately, we settled on the bird and jackfruit buns and for ramen, one shoyu and the other, veggie with red miso. My husband and I loved it all. The buns were delicious and maybe, were a smidge more outstanding than the ramen.

The buns were steamy soft and the chicken and jackfruit, respectively, were delicious - we seriously loved every single bite. The ramen should be ordered with the spice bomb if you want to add a little kick to the broth, and if you enjoy having egg on your ramen, the sous vide egg is also a great addition.

I guess I don't have more words to describe the flavors or how good the food is - it's all just really worth it.

I was really surprised by this place (in a good way) as I wasn't sure how they were going to distance themselves from the former lodge. The ambiance has totally changed! And the food is unique/versatile. I had the fammoro with chickpea Rojas, and honestly my favorite part was the Brussels sprouts! We had the baked nachos with jackfruit carnitas as well- a bit heavy on the cheese + queso but it was good nonetheless, seasoned well with onions and cilantro.

This place has a very versatile menu and you can make practically anything plant-forward. I'm curious about the paratha tacos and will be trying that next time.

Didn't try the etoh but the cocktail menu seemed very standard for a brunch place. But the bar was full service and I think this is really a place you can come for happy hour, brunch, or late night. Seems like it's got it all!
This place is just incredible! Husband and I love it! Love meeting friends there for lunch! Just wish it was closer to where we live.

The farfalle w/ crabmeat should just be on the menu like always. Its delicious and the crab is not skimped! 

The lobster ravioli was very creamy but quite delicious as well. What I loved about it was that it was plumb and actually filling. It wasnt overpriced and sad looking like when you see it at those fancy restaurants that want to make lobster ravioli sound like some gourmet special.

They had a burrata special that was on top of I guess it was farro? Some sort of grain. Wasn't sure if I would have liked it but it was an absolute love.

The branzino mixed grill was the only thing I wasn't all that excited about. Don't get me wrong, there was nothing wrong with it. But after bites of the other dishes, this felt a little bland to me.
Great food and deserts, but service could be better! Convenient location from Marriott!
