My coworker and myself ordered lunch/dinner for pick up from Armitage the other day, because we really didn't want AJs since we (as any mall employee dies) frequent there much too often and we wanted to change it up a bit. I ordered the Caprese Press with french fries. The bartender who took our phone order and checked me out was... uncomfortable? Cute but lacked some social skills. I usually can share some all-knowing laughs with other people that work at La Encantada, but he didn't even answer my question on the phone or greet me when I came to pick up my order. Upon receiving my food I was incredibly disappointed to see that my french-fries were Eeggees-esque except not as good. For somewhere like Armitage, I was expecting more than fries from the freezer section at Costco. That's exactly what they were. My coworker and I had to scarf down our food while watching our store because the fries were the kind that would turn to stone if left unattended. My Caprese Press was fine, but it was nothing to write home about. The pesto sauce they included as a side was 90% olive oil and separated no matter how vigorously I shook it, essentially inedible. That with the french fries, I was so happy I had a minuscule discount because it was in absolutely no way worth $11 full price. 

I'm a vegetarian and I didn't want to order a huge expensive meal or a salad (yawn). Maybe some of the other things on their menu are delicious, but I was seriously underwhelmed. Would I eat here again, sure. Nice, quick lunch food for work and easier than Sushi or over priced (yet yummy) North. On my ranking of La Encantada restaurants, I'd put it in the middle above Firebird and Blanco. Under Ra and North.
Absolutely delicious food! Outstanding service. Sit on the balcony for a great view of Jackson Square action. Great happy hour specials from 2-5.

I had French toast sausage and coffee. Dad had eggs grits and a muffin w/ coffee. Total bill $12.  Price was small but portions even smaller. French toast consisted of two pieces of what could be considered WonderBread made into French toast. Absolutely nothing excessive. Even coffee cup is small. This restaurant belongs in one of the hobbit movies because of size but then again hobbits like to eat. Honestly as a young adult I'd need to order at least two meals and sides to make a meal and by then it'd be cheaper to go elsewhere. If you are tight on funds, this is the place to go.
Love this place, I'm usually here on Friday nights with the Mrs.  Food is always great and the beer selection is top notch!

Super good, food is fresh and staff friendly. Fun place to go with a group or a couple. Great atmosphere and music. We love going here and will return again soon. Excellent food! Drinks to enjoy so UBER home for sure.
What a wonderful place this is, hands down 5 stars. Not sure why other reviews didn't think this deserved the 5 stars. Keep it up, if I ever return to NOLA again I will be back here.
Food was good, but staff weren't as knowledgeable about the wine as other high end restaurants.You'll end up paying about $100-$150 per person.
The place was clean, food was fresh, servings were generous and service was great. Nice alternative to the norm. We all had the Vietnamese selections. Great value. We will definitely return.

Wow! I'd heard about this place for years. Finally tried it. This food is cooked with love and all the right spices!!! I'm vegetarian and the tofu po-boy got things going and raised the bar unexpectedly high... then the pumpkin/acorn squash curry with popcorn rice jumped right over it! Wow!

My daughter was craving a pizza and we ended up here. They had some nice gluten free options and the owner was super nice.  While we waited Cora got to practice making her own pizza with some dough she got. The food was quick, service was great and we will see this joint again when in town.

Worst taco place ever. The food was disgusting and I found a bug in my taco. Also the customer service is ridiculous I had gotten kicked out of there just because I left trash on the table. I wouldn't recommend this place at all
The Homestead is a sports bar done right. The best place to watch the game. Good pub food, incredible beer selection, and great drinks.

How do I not have a review of this wonderful, wonderful coffee shop?

Only a tiny doorway leads you into Block 1912. Very deceptive indeed. Inside is an absolutely massive cafe. It goes super far back and the high ceilings really top it off. I'm not exactly sure how they got some of the art in there, like the one painting that stretches almost floor to ceiling.

I think the food is a bit overpriced ($6 for a really small salad) but you can get a good bang for your buck on coffee and tea. The cakes are definitely worth trying, too.

The staff here let you work all day on your laptop with free wireless. Too bad there isn't a single plug-in in the entire place!

Great location - perfect for hanging out between shows at the Fringe Festival or warming up after Ice on Whyte!
Second time here, this time was even better. This Salmon and Egg Sandwich should be on your bucket list.

Always a winner for a quick bite to eat we're sit down at the bar and have a good beer never a bad moment of any terminal. This trip around all I had was a smoothie but it was well worth the wait in line excellent quality excellent service. I will be returning to the wedding party tomorrow Market whenever I am downtown Philadelphia

Easily one of the best restaurants I have been to in any city. The oil with spices for dipping bread in was amazing as well as the monk fish appetizer. The menu changes daily but my girlfriend had a steak dish and I had lamb chops that were both absolutely fantastic. Wine was fantastic and service was great as well.

Been here a few times.  The most accessible deli in the area, and the food is really good, for a deli.  I've had better, like Jason's Deli, but there are a couple things that standout.

1.  Sweet tea is famous.  They give you big pieces of lemon another plus.

2.  Soups are outstanding, you have to ask for the bread bowl though.

Also, I like the decor, and ordering the ultimate nachos, because men enjoy names with ultimate in it.  Good place where everyone is pretty satisfied because traditionally people like a good sandwich or salad.  The quality is consistent.  

That said, sometimes you get really slow service, and sometimes it's really fast, Slow is extremely annoying.  They always seem to choose me for the slow service.

If Yelp had fractionated stars, I'd go 3.75 on my visit.  I went in one eve after a long day of Christmas prep/shopping for dinner and sat at the bar solo.   I hadn't been to this location since it had been a Cancun, which I really enjoyed.  Anyway, upon first glance the restaurant is very decorated festively in the typical Mexican-style bright colors.   It appeared to be the same general layout as Cancun (although the bar is in the back/far east end of the restaurant, so I didn't explore the front/west dining area during this visit).  
There appeared to be two bartenders working the small-ish bar, but after some observation I noticed that the one seemed to be floating around in and out of the kitchen.  It became apparent only one man was truly bartending, as well as making all of the other alcoholic drinks for the restaurant.  Thus, he was rushed.  It took him a few minutes to greet and take my order.  When I asked  a question, I could tell he was busy and it wasn't well-received.  Mind you, he was never rude nor inattentive but I felt as though I was imposing on him to take more of his time so I settled on a medium ultimate margarita and a veggie burrito bowl.  He made my drink, which was essentially what I expected.  Not too boozy but tasted like a typical (not so "ultimate") margarita.   I received a basket of the obligatory chips with salsa, which were probably above average for the standard Mex restaurant. Chips were warm and crispy and I liked the consistency of the salsa.  My burrito bowl arrived shortly thereafter. All of the vegetables were very fresh and it was artfully presented. My only complaint was that overall it was lacking in flavor/seasoning, perhaps some spices to jazz up the corn/rice/fajita vegs?  But I was definitely pleased with the fresh and healthy menu option.   
The bartender remained busy throughout my visit and checked on me a time or two after my food was served, but he was so busy I felt badly to ask him for anything else.  
I'll come back and give them another try again after the holidays.  Stay tuned!

Tried their chicken and beef tacos again, this is my 3rd time here. The beef is the better of the two. Their salsa is fantastic, I would buy jars of this.  Their guacamole is already spicy too, love it!

So, after a bad experience at The Gables, Dan K sent me this message a several weeks after my review.  I kindly replied acknowledging his apology and provided my address.  I never heard back from Dan K or anyone else from The Gables.  Looks like they were just trying to appear to be understanding with no follow through.  What a joke!

Hi Mike, Dan K. sent you a message on Yelp: 

Subject: Your Review 

"Hi Mike-
I apologize for taking so long to respond to your review. I was trying to get some more details about what happened that night, as I was not in the restaurant that evening. Secondly, I want to apologize for the miscommunication that happened during your dining experience with us that night. We try our very best to make our guests' experiences as seamless as possible, but we are human and make mistakes. I also apologize that the service you received was not up to our normal standard. Our server Michael is very good, but he was having a difficult day that day, and though it should not have affected his service, he is also human and makes mistakes. We do hope that you will give us another chance to win you back. It would be my pleasure to offer you a gift certificate to use towards your next meal with us. If you would be willing to accept this offer, kindly send us a message with your address and we will happily put one in the mail to you." 

Reply to Message

One of my friends loves this place to meet for drinks and lunch when we're in New Hope.  

The food and service have always been good the times I've been to Bowman's Tavern and it's nice to know you won't be breaking the budget.

I also like supporting the local restaurants rather than the chains whenever possible.

Great food and fantastic service.  We arrived around shift change which usually means poor service however a day shift server came right over and took our drink orders and then our food order. We ordered deviled eggs and bacon. Three perfect deviled eggs appeared with an order of deep fried chicken skins.   They were phenomenal. Our combo plates were ribs and brisket with amazing popovers and we ordered Cole slaw and creamed corn.   Other main order came quickly and served with several sauce choices.   The servers appear to work  well together as other servers refilled drinks and cleared our tables. Each one walked by and noticed something was needed.       Overall it was a great experience with great food

Service was great! Food + atmosphere as well! Wished the hostess was a little bit more friendly. She seemed to be annoyed when we asked her to take a group photo for us. Guess that book she was reading up front was really good.

I love this place. Small plates are my fave and they do such a good job here. The wine list is also great and to top it all off - the waiters are SUPER knowledgeable about the wine and food, which always makes for a better dining experience.

Definitely one of my top five pizzas ever. The margherita was superb, and the pepperoni (which was a pepperoni margherita!!!!) was amazing. I loved the extra kick in the pepperoni. The arugula salad was so simple but delicious. 
Very small, only maybe two tables and counter seating. Great spot to grab a quick bite to eat.

We stumbled upon this place after walking for blocks and building up quite the appetite. I got the pomegranate spritzer - so tasty and refreshing after a hot walk. Decided on the fried oyster toast with avocado, corn maque cheux, poached eggs and srihacha mayo. Delish! A great start to a bike ride along the riverwalk!

Brought a Taiwanese friend here and she loved the variety, which is a good sign. Lots of very unique sweets and teas available. Not as big of a variety of options as K&S up the road, but definitely a nice local market.

I've heard excellent things about this food truck, and I might give it another shot as the prices aren't bad. I did however order a chicken and broccoli dish. It was lunch hour so I understand that it took over 20 minutes, but the actual dish contained very little chicken or broccoli. Even a co-worker who eats from the truck regularly said he thinks they must have been really busy and just skimped on that dish and piled on the rice. So for $7.50 I had a lot of rice and a few skimpy bites of tasty side dish. Pass.

I love sandwich shops and delis.  So when I passed by the one while I was working, I had to make a mental note to come back at some point.  
  The sandwiches I got were decent.  Surprised this place isn't any busier.  I have been to better Firehouse Sub locations back in Texas.  Despite that I don't really have anything bad to say about this location.  It was satisfying.

Yes, yes, yes. Eat here. 

We came for Christmas dinner, which was a 3-course prix fixe. The things that really stood out were the prime rib, pierogis, asparagus soup, and the eggnog milkshake and banana pot de creme. So basically almost everything we had. The only thing that wasn't totally impressive was the braised pork shank because it was too salty. Cooked to perfection, but definitely salty. 

Great service from our waiter! Our dirty blonde bearded guy was nice and attentive. 

We can't wait to get back to SB and go again! Great meal great ambience and exceptional service.
The best turkey ribs i have ever had it my life !!!! Tender, good sauce and they havw something for everyone even rhe non pork eaters.  Check them out you wont regret it.

This is NJ, so there's no need to order from Pizza Hut as there's a plethora of great pizza joints around. However, sometimes you just want pan pizza and PZ's was always the best. Was. Our delivery order was 20+ minutes late, they brought the wrong drink, and the pizza was cold. Absolute crap. Never. Again.
These nugs are worth the drive from anywhere.  The staff is helpful and friendly.
Horrible service and the staff isn't welcoming at all! Sterling is their only hope! The staff needs to be more helpful and professional.

Everything about the Townsend experience was fantastic - the food, the service, and the atmosphere. 

We called ahead, and they said they were happy to accommodate vegetarians, as long as they knew they were coming in advance to give them time to prepare options. When we arrived, there was a menu tailored to vegetarians. They explained that the chefs were actually very excited to have vegetarians as it gave them a new creative challenge.

And I must say - they did a wonderful job!

The meal started with a couple types of bread (the sourdough was very tasty) and butter. They also sent out a small portion of complimentary potato and onion soup which was so good I would have ordered it if it were on the menu. Next, we had the Chanterelle Mushroom Ficasse which was sourdough bread topped with mushrooms, sun-dried tomatoes, microgreens, and saba - this was really delicious and well-balanced in terms of flavor. We then had the Fennel and Apple Soup which was not only tasty but a really unique flavor. For our entree we had French Green Lentils served with eggs - again, very good. It was a subtle but really delicious taste like comfort food. And lastly, we finished things off with their Chocolate Gateau - a dense chocolate cake with coffee chantilly that wasn't overly sweet.

The food wasn't the only great part - the service was outstanding. The staff was very professional, and our server (Megin, I believe) was a delight. She was very friendly and knowledgeable about the food and restaurant. In addition to having a great personality, she got all of the small details right - little things that make a big difference, like the fact that our water was never empty during the meal. 

The atmosphere was also very nice. It's a repurposed house turned restaurant, so while it has a polished, upscale look it doesn't feel pretentious. It's actually quite charming, as it has a lot of its original features like an ornate tin ceiling and stone fireplace. 

Townsend was without a doubt a 5-Star experience, and I can't wait to try it again.

My first review in Philly! 

Meat and flavor lovers, rejoice. This place serves up loaded sandwiches packed with freshly smoked meats and sauerkraut.

First timers, I would recommend Hershel's Famous Reuben with half pastrami half brisket, just to get the full experience. Sauerkraut and the Russian Dressing make the sandwich, and be sure to ask for it toasted.

It's a pricey sandwich (~$15 for sandwich + coke), but potentially shareable (or solo it, no one's judging). Would definitely recommend but more as a once-in-a-while thing.

I would say Paganini is a nice place to dine at. The atmosphere is warm and romantic somehow. It might be awkward as the stairs, but who cares, it makes the place looks elegant. About the food, i don't find any problem with the daily varieties food on the menu. It's not gonna be special if everyday has the same pasta. People can find it is an interesting thing to come visit different day in a week to try new thing. I can tell the ingredients are excellent as it goes very well with the food, especially the parmesan cheese and olive oil. The bread is freshly baked and served. I see some reviews complained about the long service. Some people should understand that freshly made food need time to cook unless you want your food come out from the microwave. It takes me hours to prepare the food at home, so be patient, people. One bad experience doesn't need to become the reason to jump in conclusion n judge the whole restaurant business. I would recommend this restaurant to everyone who loves hot food.

Diva Drag Brunch! This was the most fun I've had in a long time. The drinks at the bar had a kick -- one drink was included in the admission price along with a light brunch menu of about eight selections, i.e. Eggs Benedict, Omelets, Cobb Salad, Grits and Shrimp  were a few. Our food came out timely, and everything was hot. The performances were awesome. I will go back to see a different show in the future.

While the food was tasty, the place is severely understaffed.  People got frustrated and walked out.  It took 25 minutes for someone to come take our drink order.  We got our food over an hour after we were seated.  People at a neighboring table got their food the same time we did and we put our order in 15 minutes before them.  The manager was no help.  There was a nice young server, but she wasn't getting much support.

Good place for a quick breakfast, lunch or dinner or if you want to carry out. Overall decent value for money. They have it all from beer to coffee to bottled juices that you can buy. Dinner options that I've tried have ranged from just okay to quite good( recently Singapore noodles).

Small bar that appears unchanged since the new ownership took control of the Pontchartrain Hotel. Too many tables packed too closely together make for a loud and uncomfortable environment. I get the nostalgia--several people had ordered the Mile High Pie which was served with a flourish and it appeared spectacular. I don't know, personally, because we did not stick around for dessert. I was feeling peckish and ordered what I believed would be served quickly, the gumbo. It was served promptly, but was underwhelming "tourist" gumbo. Overly thick and under-seasoned, a very small portion at that, saved from one star by a couple of large shrimp and oysters. The craft cocktail menu looked interesting, and I had a rum-rye-orange concoction of which the fancy name ("Bayou" something) I cannot recall, that was well executed. The Duck Fat Sazerac (there's some sort of infusion) had a flavor that you could tell was "something" but not necessarily something to order again. Food prices were high and cocktail prices about normal for a craft-cocktail place. I really wanted to head up to the Hot Tin Roof bar but, alas, the Friday evening crowd meant there was a twenty minute wait for the elevator. That was at 7:15 or so and I'd hate to see the line later on.

The employees at this location are just awful. From the wait staff to the employees working the games, everyone is just bad. Food is not good and I don't think it's one of those situations where it will get better with time.

Service was excellent. The servers are so friendly! Food was good. We had deviled eggs, which were pretty average  the cauliflower wedges were tasty and different. Didn't love the sauce that came with them. The chicken bacon ranch grilled cheese was good, very large portion. The fries were crispy.  Everything came in paper trays, for covid I guess but seemed flimsy and we weren't given flatware.
This place is fantastic! The atmosphere, the service, and the food is phenomenal. I highly recommended this place for a romantic evening, birthday event or even just a Saturday night!! So much fun!!

When you ask for NO BACON & they stuff your crepe/omelette it with bacon anyways. Server was sweet. Offered to make me a new one, but everyone else at my table was done eating. So in my opinion, that wasn't an option. Didn't have to pay for the messed up order, but still. I left there hungry. Too many breakfast & brunch options in this town. First Watch is now last on my list.

What a great place. We have been here twice now. Once for brunch and once for lunch. The food they serve has always been excellently prepared, servers are very friendly and take care of everything you need and prices are pretty decent. A word about the food - I'm a bit old fashioned in my tastes, I like simple - my fiancé on the other hand loves a mix of flavors with all kinds of different things going. This is HER type of place. It's very very good, but there a LOT of different flavors going on. 

My suggestion - try the chicharron. You won't be disappointed.
Yummy pork vermicelli in a cozy and comfortable atmosphere.  Friendly owners!  Try the pork belly sliders.

We're greeted at the door and seated ourselves on the patio. After twenty minutes had still not been seen by a waiter. They walked past us many time and just ignored us. Finally gave up and left. Have been here plenty in the past but are now very disappointed.

This place was delicious! It had great reviews and it was all true. Nice farm fresh food. Cooked to perfection. It was located in a cute area downtown great for a stroll after breakfast. They could get rid of some of the gnats and the server could have checked on us one time during our meal, but other then that I would encourage anyone visiting to stop by.

Delicious and nutritious rolled into one! Try the Cuban sandwich or the turkey ham they're the best sandwiches I have ever tried! The avocado and bacon gives it an amazing taste, the sourdough bread is really delicious!

I don't leave bad reviews and this won't be a bad review.  I've been here several times in the past year off and on.  The place is cute.  It can get very busy and loud which is fine. The camaraderie is great.   People come and stay to talk or be on their laptops and people are in and out getting their coffees to go. I'm not a coffee aficionado by any means so I can't give an expert review on the taste of the coffee.   I generally get a latte and it's fine.   The food is generally good.   The thing that I can't get my head around is the staff is just there.  Not friendly which to me would bring much warmth and add so much to this place.   Try it though.  A lot of people are here and enjoy it.

I'm not sure why they have call ahead when they don't start making your order until you check in.  I thought the mac and cheese was very peppery for my taste.  I loved the brisket sandwich with the sweet bbq sauce.  I also tried the tangy sauce which was too harsh for me.  The ribs were just okay.  I'll only go back if its someones else's turn to pick the restaurant.

We were so excited to try Charlie's Roast Pork. We actually called ahead because we weren't sure if there was a dine-in option (there is) and no one answered the phone. When we got there, and not until after we both ordered roast pork, we were told the restaurant was out of roast pork - the only food in their name. This was around 5:00 PM. The waitress told us it happens all the time. For a place with roast pork in their name to run out of it at 5:00 and have nothing on their website indicating this is a frequent occurrence is a bit absurd, and also highly disappointing. I ordered the roast beef instead, which was bland, rubbery, and really only edible after the addition of much salt and hot sauce. The fries were mediocre, at best, but because of the inadequacy of the actual meal, we wolfed them down.
I highly recommend the shrimp and grits- when your plate comes out it has like 1/2 a pound of shrimp on it. The service was wonderful and the employees were very friendly!

There's a reason why locals (and former service industry people) don't go to broadway: they will scam unsuspecting people.

Ordered two lemon drops (customary vodka lemon juice simple syrup), not expecting sipping quality, but received 1.5 oz of country lemonade no distinguable vodka (which should be evident in a small pour) for $22. Seriously it looked like backwater of someone's drink for $11 each. Barely hit the plastic cup's initial line. 

C'mon guys.

They moved to a new location on Locust, yet the place still seems too damn small for a pair of pianos.  While the atmosphere is very nice, it is far to pricy even for the city.

It can get loud, not that that is necessarily a problem, and there isn't much of a dance floor with a packed crowd.  FYI.... There is a $5 cover on Saturday nights (or at least on their opening weekend).

This is a fantastic restaurant in New Orleans. We went for a light lunch and had the Louisiana shrimp taco, a pork taco and Brussels sprout salad. We sat at the bar and chatted a bit with the bartender Lyle. He was quite pleasant and offered great suggestions of what to see in the area, but onto the food. The pork taco had wonderful flavor however was just a little more greasy than I typically like though it (oddly) did not distract from the flavor. The shrimp was lightly coated and fried to a crisp coating yet succulent inside with a perfect sauce and complementary shaved carrot and radishes. YUM the Brussels sprout salad was crisp light and flavorful.the art is a bit eclectic with day of the dead style mural on on wall, and beautiful doors understated elegance on the other wall, interesting dichotomy.  If you can, make this a must while here!!

This place is the best thai food I ever had in Edmonton!!! The green curry is very good!!! The loft thai arancini is very good too, we try the drunken bucatini it was ok the only thing I did like about that dish was that is spicy other than that is just ok. I'm just so happy to have a good thai restaurant close now!!! My new spot to eat good food!!! Love new places and this one is worth trying!!

Filistix is at MacEwan University in the Robbins Building during the fall and winter terms and at the U of A in the ECHA building all year - for lunches only. Personally I love the South Pacific dish. Ask for extra sauce. Meals are served with rice and coleslaw topped with dried cranberries and almonds and there is always a vegetarian option. It is expensive with a half order at $8 and a full order at $12, but there is always a line up of staff, faculty, and students.

I wish I didn't love this place as much as I do because I'm sure my arteries are suffering for it. The burgers are awesome, everything a greasy cheeseburger should be. And the fries are so good, I wasn't surprised to learn that they are pretty much the least healthy fast-food fries out there. 

It's more expensive than most fast food joints but it's worth it.

My husband and I had dinner at Arnoldi's a couple of times and knew we wanted to have our wedding reception there and then Covid happened. We had already put a deposit down and were working with Arnoldi's event planner Sara, who was very helpful and accommodating during this time. We ended up having a small dinner with socially distanced tables the night we got married and it was perfect. Everything from the food and drinks to the beautiful setting of their outside patio area. The few guests that were there raved about how amazing it was. 
The only suggestion I would have for the restaurant is to remove the "recommended florist" you have listed on your website. Ruben from Elevate Floral is a crook, who stole our money and left town without ever providing flowers for our wedding day. 
Arnoldi's cafe is a restaurant I would recommend for a date night, a family dinner or when wedding receptions are happening again, a beautiful reception! Great food and great service and we will definitely be coming back for years to come!

I only gave this restaurant a 1 because Zero was not an option. With the exception of our server Love, the front of the house staff including the condescending rude Manager were horrible. My party had reservations for 2 six tops at 4:00pm which I had to endure my first encounter with the curt Manager to make. After she cut me off mid sentence saying "I'm not going to go back and forth with you" when I attempted to make sense of the policy to only hold a table for 15 minutes while refusing to seat those who had arrived. I was asked to make phone calls to the members of my party to obtain an ETA.  It takes 15 minutes to find a parking space outside of this establishment. The valet service ropes off 50% of the available spaces. While complimentary valet parking is nice, many customers are not comfortable using this service. I would recommend saving yourself the headache by selecting any of the numerous other local restaurants where customer service is a priority. Half price Happy Hour is not worth the hassle associated with the reservation process for a "Large Party" of 6 or more at Bahama Breeze in Cherry Hill, NJ

We ordered food from here for my daughters baby shower! Omg it was awesome! Nothing to complain about at all. Everyone was happy and the people that got leftovers even happier! Thankyou for making our day complete!

Old school  Italian restaurant.  Pretty much average what you could get anywhere.. Nothing bad but nothing truly memorable.  Toasted ravioli, Caesar salad , spaghetti  with red sauce, etc. Fettucine  Alfredo  had thin sauce and really needed to bump up the parmesan cheese and seasoning.

Very friendly staff! Calzones were okay. Just not happy with the pizza.  A good pizza place should have an amazing cheese pizza and theirs wasn't. We thought we would give it a try and everyone went to bed with stomach aches.
8am and they refuse to take my order.  Not open for breakfast she said!  Lights were on?  HORRIBLE

I've eaten here a few times in the past.  I don't love their food but they deliver, and I appreciate that.
So today I called to place a delivery order at 9:21 PM and was told that they weren't delivering anymore because they don't take orders for delivery past 9:20.  I said that I understood they have to draw the line somewhere, but I was planning to make a big order and offered them my business.  The lady said "The kitchen is closed!" and hung up on me.  Wow.  Horrible customer service.  If they didn't want to deliver the food, fine, but that was uncalled for.
I'll never go there again.  I'd rather give my business to someone who wants it.  Besides that, I'm a better cook than them.
Food great service sucks and slow as shit pur server was very slow at taking orders and everything else.

Super good, super fresh sandwiches. My friend and I both enjoyed the Rueben on rye. Simple, the bread was delicious and pickle spear spot on. Lots of variety as well as specials of the week. Indoor/ outdoor seating and it was packed around the noon hour. Dogs were allowed outside. Worth the visit if you want fresh deli style.

I call this place Ol' Reliable. Why? Consistent quality, tastes amazing! I always get the baguette, almond croissants, and waffles when I visit here. They have FLAKY croissants. The way it was meant to be, crunchy and soft. Not like the bready kind you get at the supermarket or chain coffee stores. The baguette is crusty and chewy. And my sister says the waffles to be the best. Also, the Vietnamese Iced Coffee is great too, strong coffee, sweetened condensed milk - what's not to love?

It's fast service if you come PREPARED. It is CASH only, but fret not, if you forget, there's an ATM inside. Highly recommend! Will definitely come back :)
Heaven. Vahalla. Nirvana. Xanadu. Nick's Pub Happy Hour. 'Nuff said.

The coffee is good, but they don't have much in the way of food- just pastries that sell out by the afternoon.  AND- if you want a refill on drip coffee, they charge you full price!  

The lack of food options and no-refill policy is really disappointing because it is an otherwise comfortable space- tables are large enough to spread out a bit, and they've set it up so that you have enough distance between you and the table next to you- it doesn't feel cramped like some other places.

Locations are great- right on campus and by Trader Joe's on Campbell.

This is the absolute best place to get coffee in Tampa. The customer service that I experienced from Karen was superb, and the hot white chocolate mocha had a nice flavor..not too weak and not too strong!!! This will be my go to place from now on to satisfy my coffee addiction!! I will gladly drive by numerous Starbucks to go to Sips!!

Where to begin.... I called after 9am needing a large flan for that evening for a celebration of life. They let me know it'd be cutting it close to have it ready by the time I needed it but they were willing to do it for me. I'm so appreciative of them going above and beyond to make it happen for me. And on top of that, it was one of the most delicious flans we've ever had, and the family I bought it for are all from Mexico. Thank you so much! Will be back!

Fun place to hang out have fun on the machines, etc.
I like the set up.

Drinks were okay, its more of a beer place, and I'm not a beer lover. 
Had the chicken Quesadilla, it was very tasty.

The new location for H&H is great.   It's connected to a brewery (just like before) so they can take advantage of the symbiotic relationship.    The classic Philly cheesesteak  ("Wiz with, please") is alive and well in Indianapolis.

Terrific place with marvelous service!  I have rarely found such a satisfying, healthy, reasonably priced option close to a convention center.  For  $8.95, I got a huge salad with chicken, olives, cucumbers, tomatoes and tatziki.  I was going to get the french fries, when Kyle (who was SO nice and helpful and kind) asked if I wanted some pita chips with my hummus.  Once I found out I could have free pita chips added in, I regretted the fries, asked if he had started him.  "Yes, but it doesn't matter--what would you prefer" and he served me babganoush, even though he'd already started fries.

I have only been to this location once, and it was at night.  I order breakfast, my sausage was pink in the middle (I'm pregnant!) the french toast was not good, it tasted like burnt eggs. Our waitress didn't refill our drinks, and someone else brought our food.  Our waitress literally was just walking around and talking. We finally had to ask for our check, she brought it back to the table and stood there until my fiance finished filling out the tip and took it. (RUDE) I will never go back to this location, who wants to risk blowing money on terrible service AND food.

Ok, last time must have just been an off night, because tonight was EXCELLENT! We had the same lovely server as last time and she seems to have totally got onto her groove. The service was fantastic, as was the food.

I got the steak and beet salad again bc I've been dreaming of it for days, and added the carmalized onion soup. My bf had the chili, which he was warned it was spicy, but holy crap it was HOT! Some sour cream helped temper it a little, but that was spicy as heck. So good though. And the accompanying cornbread!? Life changing. Be both said it was the best either of us had ever had. 

As a note, I appreciate that the owners reached out after my prior review. They refunded the drink and app from our last visit, which was awfully gracious of them. 

This place is a 10 minute walk from our St. Pete home, so we will for sure be regulars. I'm definitely going to need a weekly fix of that salad.
This is the nicest mexican restaurant hidden in a creepy area. The food is Amazing, Good mexican beer collection as Well. Will definitely Come back.

It's been my favorite but I will never go back since the incident yesterday.
The waitress that served us barely showed up to help. She was slow and didn't care at all. At the end, she also put the number of people in my party as 6 so the system can automatically charge 18% tip on our bill (she then used a pen to correct the number). We usually leave 20-25% tip. But we could clearly tell that she did that on purpose because she was afraid we wouldn't leave any tip. We will never go back

Great spot for a healthy bite to eat or a fresh coffee. I've stopped by before for a coffee to go but it's a smaller space so I've had a hard time sitting down. Today I sat down at their "bar" with a friend for breakfast. I had the green egg bake and they had the gluten free banana bread. We both got an iced latte with almond milk (75 cents extra instead of whole milk). Definitely will be back!

Tip - they're cashless so make sure you have a card on hand.

Went last night to get pizza. Had no idea it was by the slice. We were feeding 10 people and really needed a whole pizza. When we tried to buy the whole pizza, they were almost argumentative about it. We didn't care how much it cost, just fill up the box. For some reason this was really difficult for them to do. They have a menu with pizzas but they don't even make all those pizzas. Ridiculous!

I was wondering why this place felt familiar, I would miss Mangroves but Sunova Beach won me over for its specials and friendly staff. They offer 75% off hospitality and service members on Sundays and I got two cocktails, a burger with fries,and wings for around 8 bucks that day. My wallet and stomach was happy. Great food options and specials, the fish bowls were my favorite with little gummy fish swimming around. I like the little slice of beach atmosphere, good first impression. Will be back to check it out again.

The staff were very nice and helpful. The ice cream is beyond delicious! I got to milk a cow on my $2 self guided tour of the beautiful grounds.. also, the drive out was very pretty.

My favorite is the Dairy Bar, the strawberry ice cream and chocolate milk shake are soooo tasty! I can't wait to go back to try their brunch or dinner.

I've been following Mac Mart on Instagram for over a year and a half and I can now finally say that I was able to make my dreams into a reality. 

Yes it's absurd that they can charge 9 dollars for a small *reusable* tupperware filled with noodles and cheese. But are they able to get away with it? Yes. 

I ordered the jalapeno popper Mac and my sister got the Rittenhouse. I'll start off by saying that the classic Mac base is amazing on its own. A cheesy pile of beautiful noodles. Tbh I didn't order the jalapeno popper dish because I particularly like heat, but because it had the word cream cheese in it and I eat that shit with a spoon on the regular. Cream cheese on top of Mac and cheese? Sold. It wasn't too spicy anyway (I asked for no jalapeno oil, which apparently is where most of the heat comes from). Not once did my nose drip and I did not begin to perspire, which generally happens to me when I eat anything more spicy than a mild buffalo wing. 

My sister liked hers, which was topped with a garlicy spinach and artichoke dip. I had a few bites of hers and liked mine better.  

Although the tupperware is small, they do pack a lot of food into it. Regardless, I could have finished the entire thing in one serving. About halfway through I began to feel a little full, which is usually when people decide to stop eating. That's not typically the case for me, I often take it as a challenge to clear my plate. Also i have no self control. However, my sister did and decided to save some of hers for later. I didn't want to, but the idea of watching her eating more later with none for myself, inspired me to follow suit. 

You may be thinking to yourself "it's just Mac and cheese", but ok really there's no such thing bc all Mac and cheese should be idolized and imo no Mac and cheese is bad Mac and cheese unless you accidently step on it. 

This place is worth the hype and everyone should check it out at least once!

We love Dos Gorditos! Their steak they use in fajitas, burritos, taco salads, etc. is amazing! It is so full of flavor and you can tell they marinate it! Awesome place! This place is now called El Gordito!

Well well well. Nice to finally have some crawfish. We been jonsin' for some time now. Think it's been two years!! Spiced good and we each had the potatoes with sausage n corn. The corn was spicer I think. Worth the  $ coming here into where the locals come!! Great price point. Service was also great.

I am staying at the nearby hotel, and, wanting a nice (and early) dinner, chose Paul Mineo's on the basis of its very attractive street presence.  One of my treats when I'm traveling is a solo dinner - just me and my Kindle. How I am treated as a solo woman diner "of a certain age" says a lot about the restaurant. In this case, it cost them a star.

"Table for one, please." "Oh, umm, yes, please wait a minute." (the restaurant was 2/3 empty). Hurried conversation between two suits. "Put her at table x" (sotto voce). So we turned around from where I'd been invited to wait, and seated me at a table that essentially faced the entrance and the doors to the restrooms.  Every Other Table in the restaurant was tucked away in one location or another. Not this one. I went to say something but decided to wait and see. 

Service was . . . slow . . . I'm talking about that first service where you order a drink, not the length of time you expect a fine restaurant to prepare your meal. By the time the wine came, I was ready to order. Salad and one of their flatbread pizzas.  I should add that the waiters' attitude was -- there is no other word for it-- patronizing, with observable difference from how they treated the mixed groups at tables nearby.  This attitude, combined with the table selection, cost them one star.

The salad was the best part of the meal (see picture) - though the mozzarella was sliced much too thick. You can see from the picture, though, that it had many yummy additions to please the hungry palat. Thankfully I had ordered dressing on the side, because the dressing itself seemed to have no taste beyond oil. 

The 10" pizza was actually 12" (yes, I did measure - you know those fussy women diners) and should have been listed as sufficient for two average appetites. The flatbread crust was crunch at the edges and soggy from the mid-point of each slide to the center. Yum?  I managed to snag a waiter for a second glass of wine.

By the way, another reviewer mentioned that during happy hour the price for house wines was $5/glass. Either they've changed this or they now only offer beer at Happy Hour prices - my wine was $7 (and to damn with faint praise) "worth every penny."

I'm not likely to be back here again, so my opinion counts only insofar as it contributes to the Yelp conversation. So - have at it, friends and fellow Yelpers! What is your current experience with Paul Mineo's Trattoria?

Skip this place and go to another joint instead!  We had read the reviews and looked at the overall rating and were prepared to be thrilled with our meal ......but were extraordinarily disappointed. The burgers have no more flavor than a hospital burger (NOT SEASONED AT ALL). This burger patty was juicy and cooked perfect with no flavor. The mushrooms (standard frozen kind) were OK but the Mayfair dressing was AWESOME. Lighting drove me crazy, way to low for a lunch meeting. Servers seemed focused on the regulars, witch would be cool if we had not been first timers !

Don't believe all the hype.

I haven't eaten everything on their menu but what I have had so far is pretty good and you get good size portions. The only thing I've had there that I didn't care for much was their buffalo wings.They aren't bad really, just mediocre. A 3 out of 5. 
The prices are reasonable and they have great specials. The wait staff are pretty good also and I like all the wood. I get that warm, homey feel from it.
I would recommend going there.
The young female bartender will try to argue with you. The only great thing about this place is they have Great White on tap.

The pasta here is exquisite! The family ordered baked ziti, stuffed shells, and lasagna. The sauce was robust with that homemade "Grandma's Sunday dinner" taste. The ricotta and mozzarella were fresh, and the ricotta was especially creamy. The dinners included garlic bread, which was very liberal with the amount of garlic but thankfully not oily or greasy. We also sampled slices of pizza, which had a tasty, crispy crust and tender steak topping. The service was abundantly friendly. It's easy to see that the owner cares about his customers and giving them an excellent experience. I would most definitely order dinner from Candelario's again.

Boucherie is one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans. Located in the little house on Jeannette, which was most recently home to Iris, it is small and intimate, yet not too formal. Due to its size, you will want to make reservations.

Boucherie's menu features large and small plates. The menu changes monthly, but a few items remain constant. My favorite small plate is the blacked shrimp and grit cake with house made bacon vinaigrette. I also enjoy the grilled heart of romaine Caesar salad. Of the large plates, the scallops are always a star. The preparation changes monthly but this dish is a winner. Another great choice is the beef brisket with garlicky parmesan fries (a very generous portion and a bargain at $15). I crave this dish. My recommendation is to visit with a small group or at least one dining companion that is open to sharing, so that you can try many dishes. If you don't like sharing, you will be perfectly satisfied ordering one small and one large plate.

Boucherie has a nice selection of beer and wine. Boucherie also serves creative, refreshing cocktails, which also seem to change seasonally. In the winter, they serve a fantastic version of hot buttered rum. 

Leave room for dessert! All of the choices are stellar: bacon brownie, Thai chili chess pie, or Krispy Kreme bread pudding. There is some debate about which dessert is best. My vote goes to the bacon brownie or bread pudding but you can decide for yourself.

Boucherie is currently on vacation until September 7 but rest assured I will be back soon.

(Note: Boucherie was closed for the month of August, when this review was written. It is open now.)

For a place with such decadent food, you might believe you can't afford to go very often. Well, you might have also heard from the other reviews that the lunch specials are quite affordable. 
How many places will actually give you your money's worth on a ten dollar lunch? Because Farmhaus delivers. First of all, unlimited iced tea or sweet tea, that's a plus. Then the best spinach salad you will ever have. No seriously. How many times can you honestly say that you've uttered the words, "wow I totally want more of that salad" in your life? (In my life it's three times, but this is one of them!) The blue plate salad has a savory mustard seed vinaigrette, sweet caramelized onions, salty pickled vegetables, and a nice crunchy wheat cracker that they make in house. It's got all the flavor profiles and textures you could want in a salad. After the salad you get your main course, which changes based on which day of the week. Let me tell you, they are ALL great. When I heard on my first visit that it was different monday through thursday, I made a point to make it in each day. My favorite is Tuesday for knackwurst sausage on dirty rice. The sausage is made right there in the kitchen and smoked out back. It's hearty and the grind is just coarse enough for my tastes. The dirty rice is full of onion and peppers and has the amazing tang and texture that only chicken livers can provide. You love dirty rice? Do you wanna? You gotta try it. 
Hope you can find a seat on Monday, because it seems to be the most crowded day for fried chicken with mashed potatoes, gravy, and mac'n'cheese. The chicken has a crispy and crunchy spiced coating on the skin but is cooked in such a way to maintain complete moisture, it's really fall apart in your mouth tender and the texture compliments the gooey mac'n'cheese and the smooth mashed potatoes with gravy. I like to ask for hot sauce though, they have one that doesn't overpower the flavors, works great. 
Then on Wednesday is the "meatloaf", but honestly it's texture is far beyond what I'd call meatloaf. It seems like a disservice to call it meatloaf, and I already love me a good meatloaf so I'm speaking pretty highly of this meatloaf here. 
The last day they're open for lunch is Thursday and it's fish with red beans and rice. Let me put it this way, I'm not a huge fan of fish, but I'm a huge fan of THIS fish. It's crispy and buttery and has a light and pleasant flavor. Whereas the red beans and rice can probably hold their own against the best of them, they're like liquid pork belly. Left me licking my plate.

Every day they usually have an appetizer ready for lunch. It costs extra but they're all worth the five bucks if you're feeling fancy. The pork rinds don't sound special but believe me you just can't buy pork rinds as good as this from a store. They crackle and crunch then literally melt in your mouth into... delicious pig butter. I don't know how else to describe it. The porchetta bun is a fluffy piece of folded dough with some sizzling porchetta slices inside dripping with their own juices and the almost sweet sauce that compliments them. They're served with a very salty homemade kimchi that pairs well with the subtle flavors of the bun, and also goes good with your entrees if you have any left by then... I've also had a smoked fish dip that tasted like I ate an entire smokehouse of fish and a tray of pickled strawberries that confused me with how delicious pickled strawberries can be. The sweetness of strawberry reconciles quickly with the tart and salty flavors of the pickling brine. Really something there. I hear you can get a cocktail with the pickled strawberry flavor here, but I'm not bold enough to try. Day drinking I mean.

Finally, they have a desert at lunch typically. It's random every day just like the appetizer, and it's another extra five if you're going all the way, but their pastry chef really outdoes themself. Personal favorite is the dutch pancake. I just adore that texture of crispy outer layer with soft, delicate, pillow-like interior, spiced and slathered with a berry sauce and fresh soft sweet cheeses.
The food is good but price and customer service is awful. Communication is poor.  Parking is horrible.
Great breakfast and lunch food - friendly staff! We'll be going back again for breakfast with the family again - the kids loved the pancakes!
Never had a bad experience here. Great, fresh food every time, great employees with awesome customer care skills

OMG.
OMG.
OMG.

I haven't had Indian food this good in years.

No really.
It was that good.
Seriously, that good.

You haven't been yet?
You're missing out.
Seriously, you are.

What should you get?
Pakoras!
And Eggplant Masala.

Believe it or not, 
It's vegan.
Yes, vegan.

What are you waiting for?
Make the trip to Chapati...
...NOW!

Best ice cream shop I've ever been to in my life. Poke sticks in the ice cream and cake at the bottom. Very welcoming vibe great for the family. It is more of a froyo texture, but the flavor combos are great.
Good food old fashioned service. Place is immaculate. Just remember to bring cash. Limited parking and seating. My absolute favorite is the fresh roasted turkey sandwich. (Not lunch meat)
Delish Bulgogi Cheesesteak. Don't believe the haters. That's FIVE STARS, mofo.
No refills on regular coffee, bakery choices are few and most are stale. The prices are okay, but the atmosphere isn't very friendly.
Always good food and friendly service.  Can't forget Macs corned beef sandwich also!!!!!

The staff were great-friendly and very helpful on giving us recommendations. The environment is cozy. The pork buns were delicious, the fried chicken with spicy mayo were good too. The hero water was my favorite drink. However, the ramen did not impress me. I got the champon and my boyfriend got the miso ramen.I thought the miso ramen tasted much better than champon. The champon was a bit too salty for me. It was not bad but I've had much better ramen. I gave this three stars because of ramen. . I would come back if I was really craving for ramen but definitely not worth the hour and half wait. I thought the ramen were overpriced as well.

What I thought was very rude was our server giving us our bill before we even finished our food! They're rushing us out before we can actually enjoy our date together.

Ordered a chef salad to go. I know who does that at a beer hall but they actually have a good menu. I asked to leave off ham and bacon and just put extra turkey. They charged me $3 to do this???? Got home and ham all over the salad. Beer wasn't good enough to go back.

We have been dying to try Three Birds since we moved to St. Pete. The outside looks so appealing. Lots of outdoor seating which we would've chosen had it not been pouring rain. Instead we opted for indoor seating which was small but tastefully and obviously decorated to look like a pub. The seating was fine until we realized that though the bar to the outdoor bar area an opening freely allowed cigarette smoke to flow through to what should'be been kept NONSMOKING with a little more effort. Our five year old did not like the "stinky" smell and neither did I. It really put a damper on my appetite. We ordered some drinks, mules which were acceptable and some Jojos and scotch eggs. The apps were fair. The scotched egg was coated in a spicy sauce that didn't really compliment the food, but I suppose the restaurant was attempting to make it their own style--fair enough but the effort was lost. The jojos where essentially a series of vertically cut wedges of giant potato sparsely covered in salt with two plastic ramekins of decent jalapeno cheese sauce. Our meals where sandwiches with again were just okay. The service was friendly, but slow but the food did arrive quickly. We declined dessert because we really just wanted to get away from the cigarette smoke and the bartender who was inclined to sing along to the music loudly and off key. I didn't feel comfortable with the ambient noise which was another off putting part of the experience. We were near where the staff congregated to chat loudly.  It's clear we should've sat outside, but the rain was just too much. The menu may have items that are better than what we ordered. I suggest if you're looking for a place for dinner this isn't the place I'd recommend; however, the outdoor bar area which includes one pool table and a dart board might be fun place for an adult night out.

Evening meal on 27 Nov 17.  Worst food and check out service I've had there.  Mediocre  hamburger and the Oreo Ice-cream sandwich was soggy.  The place "stunk" like they are using soured mops and old pale water!  I noticed thru the meal that patrons were really getting mad because no one was at the cash register to take their money.  They just left cash on counter and left.  Same problem when I wanted to check out as I had to go find someone with threatening to just walk out.  This place has really fallen to new lows!  JUST GO SOMEWHERE ELSE!

I'm sad it took me so long to try this place!! It started with a Friday online order (spicy polenta loaf and a danish). It was so delicious that my husband and I were back the next weekend to try a cinnamon braid and take home a half loaf of miche bread. 
The spicy polenta loaf was so good and unique. On its own, it reminded me of bread dipped in hearty soup. The level of spice was perfect for toast or paninis. Our favorite combos were using it to make avocado toast or a turkey club. 
We loved everything we've tried so far and plan to make this a more regular weekend treat.

Couldn't even review the food, as I didn't even make it into the restaurant. As I walked up, a group of people were in front of me looking for a menu (i was planning to follow suit), when a person working the bar or stocking rudely directed people to the bar, and then shouted at the men when they asked for a menu. I get it if you are busy and it's not your job, but be a little more courteous. They lost my business.

My party tried Skybox for a Thursday Night Football game since they have NFL Network. It was wonderful! We were seated immediately and were able to choose a seat near one of their MANY huge screens and were helped fairly quickly after that. We started with a hot spinach-artichoke dip, it was heavenly. Warm cheese with some veggies to make you feel a little less guilty, plus it seemed to have some type of pepper or sun-dried tomatoes in the dip too. I ordered the Southwest chicken sandwich and couldn't get enough. They aren't joking when they say it has a kick to it... tons of jalapeños with the seeds along with a savory chipotle mayo, cheese, and a fresh bun. It was great! Our server was attentive, our beer and water glasses were never empty. Definitely check it out.

First time customers .  Very pleasant experience. Arrived Saturday around 12:30 -- 10 min wait to sit outside .  Ordered Cure Mimosa-- Delicious! 
It goes down refreshing - but 1 is the limit for me . 
We got the Grilled Cheese /soup and  Chicken/French toast .   Love the brioche grilled cheese -- nice crunch / chewy.  Tomato bisque is Delicious!!! Love the swirl of olive oil on top.  Chicken breading seasoning is very tasty.  No oily chicken here -  this was freshly battered and fried  .  French toast was good -- could have used more blueberries on top .   Ordered the blueberry scone -- the reviews don't lie .  The pastries go FAST.   We were lucky to get one the last blueberry scones .  Also nicely done -- sweet but still not overly dry .  I wanted to bring some back -- oh well next trip.  Oh and our waiter -- very personable and attentive.   Check it out !
This is a very nice place to have brunch. Great atmosphere, wonderful servers, unique menu items. Nice take on shrimp and grits. highly recommend.

Very impressed with the quality of the food at this place.  Wasn't expecting much from a laid back bar, but this place over-delivered.

I had the stuffed pork tenderloin and my wife ordered a personal size sausage pizza.  Both were very flavorful and the portion sizes were great.

The kids had pasta and chicken wings and there were no complaints there either.

We'll definitely be back soon.

I will NEVER go back. Went here last night for my birthday dinner with my family, we were a party of 8. I could only talk to my boyfriend sitting next to me and my cousin sitting across from me because it was so incredibly loud in there! There was a party of 10 behind us and a party of 20 beside us. The volume of the place put a huge damper on the entire night. I wasn't able to even move down the table occasionally to talk to my parents because the place is so small, they really cram you in.
Recommendation for the restaurant: put some foam in a picture frame like Green Eggs does to absorb the sound 

I ordered the special which was Mahi Mahi... It was eatable. Gave my leftovers to my boyfriend, but after 2 bites, he pushed it away even though normally he's a garbage disposal. 

La Viola gets 2 stars instead of 1 because the waitstaff is very good and attentive. Also, the mussels in white wine were delicious. 

Overall, a very disappointing experience after reading such great reviews. Did I mention I will never go back?

I tried this place out a few months ago during quarantine and now I go once a week. Great tacos! The chicken and steak "ribeye" are the way to go. The only thing I'm slightly disappointed by is that they don't sell chips and dip. However, it's still one of the best authentic taco places!

Outstanding service, dinner selections, salad and cheese bar. I had the beef medallions which were melt-in-your-mouth delicious! Hubby had a 22 oz porterhouse 1/2 inch thick and cooked to medium perfection!
Definitely recommend for a relaxing night out!

Can I give it 6 stars???? Sooooo good! And consistent! It looks like just a little cafe but they have so much to offer- whatever you're in the mood for. Every time I go there the food is perfect! Its a go-to spot for us and we love bringing people there because they always end up LOVING it too. Everything on the (huge) menu is delicious.. from pizza to salads.. or burgers, fish, wraps...  I'd recommend: The blackened salmon with the mango salsa, Mediterranean pizza, sweet potato fries, grilled chicken wrap, backyard burger, or fish tacos! Those are my favs!

I promise on my life, the calamari is the BEST I've ever had. It's served unlike anything I've ever experienced. The slices are thick and hearty and the seasonings are amazing. I wish I had ordered 2 servings of calamari instead of an entree. 

Great atmosphere!

The food is hit or miss. When it's a hit (the salted caramel french toast) it's a huge hit but when it's a miss (the soggy breakfast burrito) it's a huge miss. I would give this place another chance because it has great potential (even with the goofy hours)

I used to go their because I love their condiment, lol!
They started to serve less food very obviously, made me little sad.
Outstanding food! Tofu pho soup and tofu rice were both incredible! Fresh tasting and really good! Definitely recommend!

Upon entering I noticed that the service was Extremely slow, and no there wasn't a lot of customers at this particular time. When I was next up in line, the server stood away from the stem table and acted as if she wasn't interested in serving me. It took her nearly 3 to 4 minutes before she stepped up and asked what I'd like to eat.  The older lady then properly ate my food, but I had to wait a few minutes for the corn bread to be cooked, as well as the customers before me. 

When I returned to work and began eating my lunch, I found my food to be EXTREMELY salty. I even allowed a co-worker to taste it and they agreed the food was salty. 

This is the 1st time I've ever found the service and the food to be subpar.

Hands down, the best breakfast place in Nashville. We went on a random weekday and didn't wait at all, tried to go again on a Friday and laughed at how long the line was (no exaggeration - at least 50 people). Definitely get grits if you make it into the restaurant!!

I finally found my favorite Thai restraunt. My wife and I love Thai food. And this is the best one we have been to. The store front seems small but thers is a big table in the back that can fit two families. I tried many different dishes. They are all good but I really like eggplant with Basil. My wife likes pad se-ew and she orders that almost every time.

AWFUL!  Worst restaurant experience ever!  Went to get a salad dish out of the chiller and it was dirty.  My burger tasted like heavy cologne!  Horrible.  I sent it back and got another salad and found another dirty dish in the chiller!  Health dept should shut this down!

I have a love and hate relationship with this place. Almost every Sunday I'm there since that's the ONLY day out the week that they offer jerk chicken pasta and it is soooo good! But, the rest of their food is mediocre. I've had Jamaican food at various other places and all have been better, sadly. Also, I love spicy foods but for some odd reason their jerk chicken is STILL way too spicy for me. Spicy to the point that I can't even eat it and actually enjoy it. Lips burning and all  :(

Very friendly people and amazing comfort food. We went for breakfast and all the ingredients tasted fresh as well as great staff that made you feel at home. The decor was nice and definitely didn't have a diner feel but a place you go for some good food. I will definitely be back here and would recommend you to try this place you won't be disappointed

The thing about New Orleans, is if you are staying in-near The Quarter, do your homework on dining so that you can find an unpretentious delicious gem like Daisy Dukes.  The nook-and-cranny locals' places like this always have more character, besides.

Thanks to Groupon and another site, I was alerted to this restaurant, found very enlightening reviews on Yelp and dined there on September 1.  Long week, long travel day, compounded by miserable rain, and a quick tasty meal  was in order. 

My server, Jaz, was very friendly and patient with me (so much good stuff on the menu, and I was starving and couldnt decide).  The greeter and other staff were equally inviting and friendly, in person that day and also for my take-out order another day.

I ended up with a side salad (gigantic) and a fried oyster poboy (gigantic and delicious -- impossible to get good fried oysters anywhere but Nola and I dont like them raw).  A perfect comfort meal that hit the spot and I certainly was back on my weekend trip.  My lunch on September 5 made this 5 stars, hands-down.  

For a bite on-the-go, I thought I'd grab a shrimp po-boy and soem of the famous (per the menu) hand-cut wings.  I was absolutely overwhelmed -- the bag felt like someone had mistakenly put someone else's larger order in it.  

The po-boy was gigantic -- the the point that I decided to enjoy each large shrimp (you're talking 26-30-count or larger) individually -- yummy by the way with light and perfectly seasoned batter -- and make an impromtu salad of the lettuce, tomatoes, and pickles.  The wings were equally spectacular -- very large and meaty and the barbeque sauce/seasoning was out of this world (like what you'd expect in a BBQ specialty restaurant).  

Trust me, the folks near me on my flight were wondering where did you get "that?"   I certaily wonder why folks can't make the 2-block trek from Bourbon St for this great comfort food -- vs. straggle into a fastfood joint with nasty, cold burgers (just because it's on Bourbon) for a combo price that is the same as a po-boy or wings etc.

Thanks, Jaz, and thanks to Daisy Dukes for being you -- and getting my vacation off to a great start and ending it with a bang!  Five stars all the way -- if I return to Nola, I'll be here a lot!

Great steaks. I usually try a new place each time I visit Philly, but Dalessandro's earned a second trip. Cheesesteak with whiz is my go-to. They also have a decent selection of craft beer bottles - which can sometimes be difficult to find in Pennsylvania.

Had lunch there the other day. Less than impressed. I remember them having these great chicken strips and french fries and Italian beef sandwiches. So we decided to order the chicken strips. And let me tell you how disappointing they were. They obviously are frozen. Processed chicken,  it was entirely just rib meat. They were the grossest thing I think I have ever experienced in a restaurant. The fries were amazing as usual. And they have good ranch dressing. But do not, I repeat, do not order the chicken strips. Unless of course you like fake chicken. I don't think we'll be rushing back anytime soon.

Mark provided excellent service last night- helped us make solid food choices from so many delectable options! We did the dim sum sampler and loved them- especially edamame dumplings! Soft mashed edamame with truffle oil. Korean beef rice was great, and we loved the cauliflower and Brussels sprouts side dishes.

Pastry chef is amazing too-chocolate kufti! Orange cream!

The first thing you need to know about this place is that it is inside the Peppermill Casino, and that's the only way in. If you opt to eat dinner here, be prepared to be tempted by flashy slot machines and exciting table games on your way in.

I went here with a party of three on a Saturday night around 7pm. I was expecting a significant wait because we didn't have a reservation, but they seated us very promptly. Once inside, the atmosphere is surprisingly quiet, which made for a nice dining atmosphere. The service once we were seated could have been better, however. Immediately upon sitting down, food runners brought us (delicious) bread and water and told us our server would be with us shortly. The guy who told us that didn't know it, but it was a lie. More than 15 minutes went by without anyone coming to talk to us, which was strange because the restaurant wasn't all that busy. In the grand scheme of things, it's probably OK, because it saved us $30 on the drinks we would have ordered. I can't imagine the management would feel the same way.

Once someone finally did come and help us, the service was pretty solid the rest of the way. Our server made several suggestions and had a clear understanding of the menu and the wine list. I started with the kale and bacon salad, which was very good, though I'm sure the bacon negates any health characteristics usually associated with a kale salad. I also tried my sister's caesar salad, which comes in a taco shell made of burnt parmesan cheese, which is the best idea ever, obviously.  

For the main course, I got the Tuscany Trio, which is the best choice for people who are as indecisive about ordering Italian food as I am. It comes with small portions of lasagna, fettuccine Alfredo, AND chicken parmesan. All were pretty decent. A half step above Olive Garden for sure. My dad got the spaghetti and meatballs, which was good. Keep in mind though, spaghetti and meatballs is a pretty easy dish to make on your own at home. They get some points for presentation, as you can see from some of the photos of that dish posted in some of the other reviews. 

Overall, the experience was positive, but barely so. The service should have been better, especially because they're in a casino resort. The food was fine, but not amazing. Next time I'm back in the Peppermill, I'll opt for Cafe Milano instead. Better food, better service, better prices...and it's 30 yard away.

The owner/manager is really friendly and knew the customers who were there while I was. The food is great. I got a chicken pita and potato salad. Good prices and you get lots of food. Great for lunch or dinner. Everything I have tried from here was super good.

Great view and good food, but service has always been poor and the portion sizes have been reduced significantly.  Coupled with the high prices, Circles has definitely fallen off my "place to bring out-of-towners" list.

Plus the place was swarming, absolutely SWARMING, with flies outside.  That's sort of endemic of Apollo Beach, but they could at least try to lessen the fly situation.

I won't even comment on the experience here, because I've already discussed it in detail with the manager, who sent us two free meals I likely won't be using ... because the burritos here are just not good. Cold, a little soggy, and bland is how I would describe it. Being from AZ/Southern CA, I know my Mexican food, and this isn't it.
Without a doubt, the best hummus I've ever had in my life. I would literally hop on a plane to come back to New Orleans just to have it.
Good sandwiches that are made fast! They also deliver. Love their chips and hot peppers!

Dim Sum Garden you have ruined me...I can't eat XLB at any other place without thinking of these juicy dumplings ever again! 
I happen to have found this place through some instagram snooping and while visiting Philly, had to visit. I frequent Bob's Shanghai 66 in Maryland, it does the job for me but these dumplings were outstanding. 
The covering wasn't too thick and the soup inside had delicious depth and there was perfect broth to filling ratio. 
We also ordered the sautéed bok choy which wasn't anything to rave about. We just wanted to consume some greens to outweigh all the carbs we were gonna stuff down...
Another favorite was the beef brisket soup. I've had beef noodle soup before in the DMV and enjoyed it but this was above and beyond good. They didn't skimp on the meat which always adds points in my book. I haven't had these kind of noodles with cilantro and pickled veggies before and although the broth was already flavorful, this only added more deliciousness to the overall dish.
I can't wait to visit Philly and hit up this place again.

Hmmmmmm.  I like the concept, place your order and the fillings are assembled, pan fried sauced up before your eyes.  I had the butter chicken wrap, it was ok, but it wasn't as flavourful as I hoped it would be. Service is very helpful and friendly, prices are reasonable. Is it lights out great?  No.  Is it better than the fast food sandwich options of this style? Yes. Will I come back?  Probably.

Agreed, this is a gem and a great break from the crazy French Quarter area.  Found out about this place from a cab driver and my colleagues were wondering why we were going here since the outside is a little misleading.

Everything was great, good, atmosphere and service.  And yeah, who can you go wrong with praline bacon?  We ordered a bunch of different things, multiple sides (and bottles of wine), and it all came out great.  Lastly, man that Ooey Gooey cake was hands down the best dessert.

Worth the short trip outside the Convention Center area and a stop I will try to make everyone I come back down here.

Snob alert! 

Toucan Charlie's is a total rip-off. Reno isn't exactly the classiest city or known for it's great food... but at this price, at least try. The best part of the buffet was the soft serve ice cream... that should tell you something. Everything else was either salty or tasteless. The food was not warm.

The reason Toucan Charlie's gets an additional star is service. Our waiters and busboys were attentive and very speedy.

This place is great. There is something for everyone, whether a light snack, heavy meal, drink, or dessert. The mango drink is really nice and fresh. The Vietnamese coffee is good but not strong. The churros are crispy and delicious. We ordered pad Thai with beef. Beef was a little chewy and nothing spectacular. It's a decent plate. Not something I'd travel to order again. The garlic noodles were recommended to me. The noodles are good. But a little heavy for me. The beef with the noodles (maybe shaken beef) was the best thing I had. I think I would have enjoyed it better with rice. The beef was tender (I ordered medium) and flavorful. It was like your favorite auntie making you a homemade meal after you've been away for college. I would definitely get the beef again. 
It was busy, lines were long. But the staff were great and helpful.  We sat outside in the back patio area, which had a great view of a small pond fountain thing with ducks. The staff brought us water while we waited for our food and brought us to go containers when we were done. They cleaned the tables in between customers and made sure everyone got everything they ordered. Food comes from one station and the desserts come from another station. The staff made sure our churros came out after our meals so that it was fresh and hot when we were done eating. I had a great experience even though the wait was a little long.

The food is exactly what you would expect from an IHOP. The staff is friendly and the wait times are about average depending on when you go. My kids love the chicken and waffles. It's a bit pricey for breakfast food but not unreasonable.
Their food is amazing!  I've ordered the Cuban over a dozen times and it is always great!  Delivery is fast and the driver is very friendly
Meh, the wine and food are uninspired and very limited. Atmosphere lackluster and unoriginal. Service was fine but no reason to go back.

When a friend suggested a Barbecue spot for a breakfast treat, I was skeptical at best!   But I must endorse, with as much enthusiasm as I can muster, the Eggs Benedict at BJs. I've overcome the delicious barbecue aroma twice now to enjoy them. My seat at the counter this visit forced me to consider a trip to try either the pulled pork or brisket, if it's lean, and what looked like fresh cut fries on another visit. I only wish I could afford, by dollar or waistline, to eat all my meals out.

I can't tell you what a perfect end to a great day we had at Jill's Place.  

My girl and I both got steaks, a RibEye and a Filet ... both were cooked perfectly and the bearnaise and pepper sauces were delicious.  The dinners came with lots of good sides ... a great split pea soup and garlic bread, salad, and mashed potatoes.  We both love steak, and can be a little critical if it's not done right, but we were very satisfied by all the food.  We also had a margarita and mojito, which were good.

But, what really put the evening over the top was the live music that started up after we had been seated for dinner.  When I first saw them setting up, I admit that I was a little worried ... it could have ended up being a really bad thing, but they were actually pretty good, and the entire restaurant responded really well to them.  Apparently, the place was full of musicians ... there were two women who got up and joined them for a song each, one of whom I was very impressed by.

Anyway ... me and my girl went home fully sated ... thanks for a great evening!

Wow, great little find on Magazine street.

I had a birthday dinner here and can't say enough about it.

The bar is a bit small, but the piano player/singer really added to the classy feeling here.

Dining area is small but we didn't feel crowded at all...and the place stayed busy on a Saturday night.

Drinks were good and the food was excellent.  The chocolate cake is huge, popular, and could feed four easily!  However, to me it was the down side to the meal...it was just too dense and heavy for my taste.

Absolutely best part was our server, Danny, and his support.  

Danny did an amazing job and I would return just for his service...though the food is also worth returning for.

Overall excellent place for a great meal!

The shop was really cute and packed.
 The staff was great and friendly. I like the location and the feel of the coffee shop. It's hard for me not to be critical of food because I live in the heart of philly where there are so many amazing choices. All and all the food was ok but the vibe was great.

Wooooooow we were having a fantastic time. David and Jessica were amazing until this really RUUUUDE individual walked through and yelled at the top of his lungs "EVERYONE OUT!!" I was seriously finishing my drink. I will never go again.
