Prices are not bad and are about the same as other Viet restaurants in the area. We should have ordered some banh mi to go. They seriously had a huge variety of sandwiches. But yay! I'm glad we have found another Viet restaurant to come too! Service and food were both awesome during our visit and we will definitely be back.

Knowing my personality I had a friend who insisted that we go to this restaurant because they knew that I would love it. I eat vegetarian and am slowly inching my way to be vegan so they thought this would be the perfect fit for me. However the food was just okay. Don't get me wrong there were a wide range of options to choose from and they had plenty of items to get but it was more a place to go for a snack after walking on the trail rather than a full meal. I have tried other 'hippie' restaurants along the trail and like them much better. They did however have my favorite beer there, which is always a plus. One of my friends got a Bloody Mary. I thought it tasted good, you could tell they used canned tomato juice instead of store bought so I love it. However my friend was not as big of a fan and paying $9 for a drink and not liking it is kind of disappointing. They also used hand canned pickle in the Bloody Mary which was a nice touch that they didn't skimp out on any part of the process. 

One major thing I will applaud Public Greens for doing is serving organic and preservative free ketchup, bbq, etc from a local vendor. Many times you will walk into a restaurant that claims to have a clean mission and serve healthy food and then they will have Heinz ketchup sitting on the table. Which for me honestly ruins the whole vibe. 

They did have large tables that would make for bringing a big group of people ideal

Smells gross, dirty inside, service was awful.  I get its right at the entrance to the quarter, but come on!  I do have to say that the drinks were cheap and much stronger than most in NoLA, but maybe thats to cover the smell?!  Won't be going back here anytime soon.

I love Judge Bean's!  the brisket is my go-to here.  Texans know how to bar-b-que beef better than Tennesseans, which is a pork state.  The smoked brisket here is tender, juicy, and has that awesome bark on the sides.  I also love, love, love the The Original Shrimp Diablo. Give me a break, a Jalapeno Pepper Stuffed with Shrimp and Cheese then Wrapped in Bacon.  That is some good stuff.  Super friendly staff.  Small, homey atmosphere.  My kind of place.
Really great food at a reasonable price. The service is a little slow so make sure to give yourself some time but the food is well worth the wait!

Considering Sedona is a beautiful city in Arizona, a state where I lived for some time, I anticipated the food and ambiance would be comparable. Ehhh not so much. Really nothing special about either of the dishes we ordered. I was considering the Croque Monsieur but our server advised the Sausage Benedict was the better choice. Supposedly better than the Crabcake Benedict option too; and while it was hot, my potatoes on the side were cold and soggy, along with the overly well done asparagus. The french toast was way too sweet and it didn't taste cooked through. It also didn't come with any sides, nor were we offered anything to go with it. A nice, large restaurant and clean which was a plus but also fairly empty, so not sure why we were seated directly in front of the kitchen. I really could have done without smelling like cooked food for the rest of the day. Nice service but otherwise, nothing too memorable about this place for brunch any way.
Merlice has to be the worst server that I have ever had the displeasure of serving me. She should be fired for her total lack of customer service.

Food was excellent. Hummus was very tasty and smooth with several pickled treats and olive oil in the center. Would have been plenty for four. We both enjoyed the lamb shank that was flavorful and fall-off-the-bone tender. The salad that came with plate was a healthy mix of fresh greens and veggies. I dressed mine with the creamy Greek that tasted.Tastefully decorated with friendly service. Highly recommended.

The staff is always very friendly and helpful. My favorite coffee shop in Wilmington. The prices are reasonable and the quality of the food and coffee is out of this world. They open at 6am which is actually earlier than the others in Wilmington but normal time so people can get something to eat n some caffeine in the morning. 

The breakfast sandwiches are amazing my bf always gets the Asiago bagel with bacon egg and cheese. It's amazingly fresh every day and definitely hot when he gets it. 

Anyway when in Wilmington definitely stop to this place.

First time to Indianapolis. Looked for a local place that the locals go. Let's just say you won't be disappointed. This place was happening. Great breakfast or lunch anytime of day. I had the protein plate. 4 eggs to order and two meats. Added hash browns it was awesome. I will defiantly be back durning my current stay and if I'm ever in the area.
We didn't eat here, but my goodness is this a fun place to just walk around in.  Awesomely outrageous and just a fun stop!

This place was recommended by our Lyft driver Bob as a great place for seafood. My wife and I wanted an early dinner before heading downtown to the Ryman for a concert. 

We ordered two entrees the salmon and stuffed mushrooms with the intent of sharing. The salmon was done to perfection, served with mashed potatoes and asparagus. 

The mushrooms were served on a bed of arugula with some handmade goddess dressing. The mushrooms were flavorful with the stuffing filled with just the right amount of ingredients. 

My wife asked the manager, Matt, if he had pecan pie. He said his wife makes the pies and brought us out a piece of peanut butter chocolate. WOW!  Awesome crust, creamy sweet flavor and absolutely delicious. 

Service was excellent. We had a few of the California wines. The atmosphere was nice. If you get a chance to eat here, take it!

Great service and the food was phenomenal. The blueberry lasagna is a MUST try, absolutely delicious. The kind of dish that doesn't look huge but you want to savor every bite! The cocktails were unique and very tasty- worth the price!

Love this place! Bright,spacious and inviting! Great coffee! Excellent Service! Very relaxed vibe, that makes you want to spend time there. (I personally do not like hanging out at coffee shops) However, this place makes me feel completely comfortable and makes me want to linger. Their bakery snacks are legit as well! If you want to do yourself a favor treat yourself or have your next client meeting at The Farmhouse Coffee & Espresso Bar! I highly recommend it!
I order the Steele special. They know me by name.  Best NY slice in Idaho by far.  Plus BOGO slices last hour they are open.

Ordered on a Saturday night for a large family meal and everything was excellent! Will definitely return soon. We ordered the salt roasted cauliflower, swordfish pastrami and rye, big a** salad, roasted chicken, smoked octopus, whole trout, corn donuts, chocolate blood pudding, the basque style cheesecake. To drink we had the milk punch, the e&a black Manhattan, and the Rusty Rail IPA. Cauliflower was a great option for the vegan in our family.  As a meat eater I still enjoyed this.  Swordfish pastrami and rye was an adventure on my tastebuds. Probably one of the groups favorites.  Big a** salad was a meal in itself... guess that's where it gets it's name from.  The roasted chicken was amazing.  Moist chicken with a great smoked taste.  The greens with the chicken were excellent and rich in flavor. The smoked octopus is by far the best octopus I've ever had.  I would put it up against any octopus around!!  Trout was fresh and presented well.  Corn donuts had a great spice to them and were great for the group.  Both deserts were delicious.  Blood pudding was definitely a new try for us and we all loved it!   Cheesecake was great also.  All the adult drinks were excellent and were great to go!  We will DEFINITELY be back soon for this adventure!

Most authentic Chinese food in town!!! Treated like family on our first visit. If you enjoy home cooked spicy food, The braised lamb spine is a must try!! Also the Salvia chicken is incredible with such bold flavor! Just like I was back in china!

This place has been a favorite of mine for years, I go there whenever I want a good margarita. Not anymore. When our server brought our first margarita, I thought we simply got the wrong drinks because the Grand Gold margaritas we ordered were 1/2 orange juice. When we questioned it we were told, even by the manager, that that's how they make them. Really? It doesn't say that on the menu description and no margarita I have ever had there has had orange juice in it. The pulp was laying in the drink and coating the ice cubes! So another server comes over and suggests a different margarita that has Grand Marnier but no orange juice. That drink comes and there's no GM in it! On the third attempt we finally got ok margaritas. And they didn't even comp the drinks! Yesterday (8/12) they were out of Sauza Tequila according to my friend. Whatever's going on there I hope they fix it soon so I don't have to look for a new margarita place. Oh, and one thing I've never understood is why they don't have dessert, even though I've never been hungry enough for it.
okay BLISS!!!! best waitress i've had in a while. she was so sweet and great. also funny! and doing her job. we loved her!! come here just for her!!!! WE LOVE U BLISS!!!

Wow! This restaurant is absolutely incredible! My boyfriend and I love Mediterranean food and our very favorite place was in New York! We have searched high and low in St. Louis for something comparable and nothing stacked up until we found Jafra! We elected to have our food carry out, but when I entered the restaurant, it was spotless and the staff was incredibly friendly! I was offer Arabic coffee during my wait, which was stellar. Once we got back to our room, we were amazed. The portions were large enough that we shared everything and we were so glad we ordered lots to try! We had the labneh, foul, Arabic olives, eggplant salad and beef shawarma. We were fighting over who got to eat the rest of the eggplant salad! The food here is to die for and the staff are so nice! We will definitely return and will recommend to everyone we know!!!

Too bad I live in NJ and can't have these cookies all the time.  They are effin delicious and perfect in every way.  Their texture is firm, but gooey inside... no uncooked dough or overly buttery/greasy feel.  The chocolate chip with walnuts cookie was flawless in my book and I consider myself pretty picky . The cookie was warm,  freshly baked and slightly crunchy but yet soft at the same time.  The perfect balance of texture and taste.

My husband loved the oatmeal cookie and swears up and down that it is the best oatmeal cookie he has ever had in his life.  Service is ok -- don't expect anything spectacular but remember you're not there for the service, you are there for the cookie.

They have different varieties of cookies and they all looked delicious but the one that stuck out in my mind was the chocolate chip cookie dipped in milk chocolate... boy was it hard for me to walk away from this place without ordering tons of cookies.  Philly, you may have lost the World Series but NYC can't fuq with your cookies... or your cheesesteaks... but I'll save that for another review...

A quiet, not-overly-touristy place for a meal. We went to brunch during Mardi Gras and while they could accommodate our large group, most of the food came out pretty cold and took a while. A lot of the poached eggs came out soft boiled. It was okay brunch food. The best value was probably the egg croissant. It was good, filling, and fresh. Drinks and beer selection were good as well. Not the BEST New Orleans meal, but for its location near Bourbon, it wasn't bad. It's a good choice if you are near Bourbon but want to avoid the tourist traps and sub-par offerings.

I always enjoy trying out a new burger place and Burger Study did not disappoint! The black raspberry Moscow Mule is a must. SO good! I got the Double Standard with a side of onion rings and it was delicious. Our service was a little slow but our server (Keith) had a ton of tables and gave us a heads up right when we sat down. My husband got the turkey burger and tater tots and the other couple we were with loved their food as well. Location is great. Close to the bars and you can park at the mall. Great new spot to visit if you're downtown!

I'm absolutely obsessed with this place. I finally made my way to this shop three weeks ago and I'm kind of ashamed to admit that I now go at least once if not twice a week. I used to be a Bing's fan but I've fully converted and haven't stepped in there since. 

The best thing about Chatime is that there are literally hundreds (maybe thousands???) of drink combinations so you will never get bored and can always try something new. I've had the roasted milk teas, the taro pudding tea, lychee black tea , milk chocolate and they are all super delicious. I am usually the type of person who finds one drink and sticks with it but I can't help but want to TRY ALL THE THINGS. I was surprised with how rich their flavors were - a lot of bubble tea places rely on sugar, powder and milk and the flavor is kind of an afterthought. Since you can adjust sugar, ice, and add-ins they make a point to start out with a really good liquid beverage so everything tastes authentic. I also love drinking the add-ins and Chatime makes it a point to fill the cup at least a quarter full of sweet, sweet tapioca (or other stuff). After I finish drinking the liquid part I'm always left with a whole bunch of boba to vacuum suck up with my face which is awesome.

I too wish they opened just a little bit earlier since I'd love to stop buy here and get a drink before I run errands on the weekends. Other than that I have zero complaints and I will be back until I have tried as many things as possible from the menu.

Scramble Bowl was amazing! Customizable and a big portion. The staff was very nice and the manager came by to ask how I was doing. This is a great spot in Tampa and I can't wait to come back next time I'm in town.

So we came in for $5 breakfast, my husband and I said we would like to have that. The waitress said it was $5 brunch. So we chose from the brunch menu. The meals came in. They were okay. The French toast was cold but good servings. The bill came in and it was NOT $5. They did not properly explain this to us and said all they could do is offer gift cards for future visits. I said I would prefer the discount on the breakfast. She then said she would be back. After several moments the manager returned and took off the difference which we much appreciated. If you come in for $5 make sure you get the waitress/waiter to properly explain what applies. 

We live in the area and hope to return and appreciate the manager took care of it. We just wish it was clearer in the menu (look to photo attached). It's not even listed on the menu, how do you order it?

The barbacoa is a to fatty for my taste buds, the chorizo and pastor is very spicy a little too spicy to have more than 1 or 2. The carnitas is good flavor when they really fry it up well.  I dont know why but im not crazy about the carrot garnish they add, all in all good food!

I've been to a few restaurants in the French Quarter who serve similar food and this place was pretty good. We thought the wait was going to be long based on the line outside but it moved pretty quick and we actual were about to sit at the bar which was empty when we arrived. I had the fried green tomatoes with shrimp and remoulade sauce on top. My only complaint was that they put way too much sauce on top of the shrimp for me. It took away from the taste of the fried green tomatoes (which I'm pretty sure were just red tomatoes). I also had the bbq shrimp with white rice. For the amount of sauce they give you it would have been nice to have more rice. The sauce was good and the shrimp were cooked well. Overall everything was good but not great.

I was at Harry's recently for a celebratory dinner with a small group. Incredibly respectful with COVID precautions. The dinner was superb and the wait staff was professional, knowledgeable and attentive.
Excellent food and service. Thanks to Diego for making our first experience wonderful. He was outstanding.

The King of Burgers.  I meet up with a friend and mentor once a month at Burger King.  It is a nice relaxed atmosphere with a full selection of burgers including the Jr., Whopper, and Double Whopper.  The burger is served on a sesame roll with pickles, romaine, catchup, and mayo.  Sides include salads, fries, and chicken fingers.  I personally got a Whopper Jr. and a small coffee.  The coffee is quite good.

The regulars tend to be older men and a few teenagers.  It is just a nice quiet place to sit, chat, and grab a quick bite.

They are supposed to have WIFI, but every time I ask they tell me go to another location that actually has it.  It would be a nice addition to be able catch up on emails and write yelp reviews while eating a burger.

I rarely, if ever, comment about products and services even when I have been disappointed by them.  But I feel compelled to do so about the sushi I got from Misora.

I love sushi, and have it for dinner a couple of times a week.  I am a huge fan of Vic Sushi and other places in town.  Even though I live in the same block as Misora, I have never been able to convince myself to go there, until today.  I needed to grab something to eat fast, so I ordered a couple of their specialty rolls.

Big mistake.  Both rolls did not taste fresh.  The eel was tasteless and dry.   The tuna was rather insipid and of lifeless color.  It was almost unpalatable.  I was not able to finish eating it.

Whether or not there is agreement on how many stars this place deserves, I am pretty certain that for almost comparable price at Vic Sushi you are guaranteed to have some of the best sushi for your money.

They lured me in and now I'm hooked. Seriously, it was the blue cheese stuffed olives in my gray goose martini that did me in. Plus I love the interior decorations and the high vibe energy. The stuff was super great from host, to bartender, to server. 

I'm not a fan of the non-reservations policy but that is minor. My boyfriend hates (is their a stinger word for that?) fish; the smell of it and the taste. We were both wary Lure would smell like a rotting fishbowls and we're both surprised it didn't.

The ahi ceviche was bomb. The homemade tortilla chips were also nom nom. Omg, and the strawberry spring salad (add chicken) was nothing short of delicious. 

I will be back on another martini & oysters kind of night - can't wait.
I reserved a table for dinner the day before Valentine's Day and I was very disappointed. The atmosphere was wonderful but the service was horrible. The food was ok.

Great food at a great price.

Betos seems to be fairly famous around reno.  My wife and I stopped in to see what all the buzz is about.  She ordered the fried fish and I had some tacos; both meals were excellent!

I have been a member at North Shore Beach Club for the last 4 years and it was AWESOME. This year it's Monarch and it. is. the. WORST. The menu used to be varied and delicious; now, salads in to-go containers look like something you'd get in a school cafeteria, sandwiches are sloppy, and all the good things on the menu (like artisan pizza and tacos) are gone. The drinks are only still good because they had the sense to keep the same bartenders (but who knows how long they'll stay with this place going downhill). They reconfigured the space and now it looks like they're packing people in like sardines. The wooden chairs that were so comfy have been replaced with cheap plastic. The bathrooms are a gross mess. The list goes on.  The most terrible part, though, is how they took a great little slice of heaven - an oasis - and have turned it into a grotesque attempt at a lounge/bar/nightclub.  A friend was there in the evening and it was all the worst parts of a spring break frat party run amok.  "I'm pretty sure I saw someone inside someone." was how she put it. The cherry on top is that now anyone who wants to pay 50 bucks for the privilege of drinking enough to puke on people in bathing suits can do so.

Anyone who has something to do with how this place is run should reach out to the people that have been coming back year after year and try to figure out what made this place great before - there are a lot of people who really loved this place and want to keep coming back.
Nice decor, the food was delicious. But all together the experience lacked imagination.
Staple of New Orleans, top of the line service along with an outstanding menu, This is a must if you are in the area. My wife and I visited in May 2014.

Taro, gobo, big white daikons,
These make up the Asian icons
Which, with broth and miso mix  
Gave me a tonjiru fix.
Cut some  pork belly in slices
Added seven chili spices.
All paid at  T and T cash:
With twenty bucks. That's quite a stash.

Well I had too try this place since people were talking about it and what a waist. I could have thrown something on my grill and saved my $18 on ribs and sausage.  For 1 the ribs are not good and very salty dry and cold. The sausage was ok and cold as well. I live 2min from this place and there should be no reason the food is cold. 1st and last time eating there. Also someone please tell the girl that gets your food when something drops on the floor or she throws something out please change your damn gloves. Very nasty. Also paying for sides is just ridiculous when the prices are that high. If Dicks bbq was closer I would have went. They have good size portions that are hot and sides comes with the meal shocker!!

Best sushi I've ever eaten. Great service, super friendly staff thats happy to answer any questions you have. And the $20 all-you-can-eat eat meal can definitely be worth it, if your hungry enough and love sushi. Our group of 3 ate well over $100 worth, granted we hadn't eaten all day and were starving. I'd recommend looking over the menu first because if they serve it to you and you don't eat it, they will charge you extra for that dish, so if you can't put down some serious sushi maybe just order individual items... And be a little  adventures and try the desserts, the green tea ice cream is the bomb.
Great food, cocktails and service. We were a group of 8.  Our server, Jordan, was amazing and she took fabulous care of us.

Santa Barbara is one of my favorite weekend getaways.  State St is the "main street" of the city filled with great restaurants, shops. theatre's, and bars.   If you're looking for a breakfast cafe', I would definitely recommend Anderson's.  It's a very charming cafe with indoor/outdoor dining.  I love the European look/feel, with a menu to match.  Tasty crepes, egg dishes, and complimentary danishes.  A great touch.   Put this on your list of breakfast places.

Totally OK bowl of ramen. The Ai was about a million times better than the Spicy ramen, which tasted like a package of Top Ramen with spicy oil mixed in. A good option for fast casual lunch in Center City.
It's okay. The macaroni is bomb when it's made right lol the little crust on top is so good!
One of my favourite places in the city. Owners are amazing. Food is always perfect. For sure 5/5 stars !

If I took my Midwest-raised, almost retired parents to Shappiro's, they would give it 5 Stars. Thankfully, I don't have to do either. Although they make nearly everything from scratch, the mostly bland Midwestern comfort food like meatloaf and beef liver suffers from poor execution.

I really wanted to love this place, because I am a sucker for a quality Rubin sandwich. But, under-toasted bread with lukewarm corned beef does not a good Rubin make (especially for $15 without a side). Serve up that sando with my wife's (not) hot pastrami on rye and I probably pass on the opportunity to have it again.

+1 for the deserts. The brownies were great. The pies and cakes also looked outstanding. I might go back for that.
Was in the neighborhood and looked on yelp for recommendations for lunch. Reasonably priced, beautifully presented, very fresh and tasty sushi. Will go back whenever I am in the area again.

This Roy Roger's site is located within a New Jersey rest area food court. There are various menu readily available for customers to retrieve on their own. During my visit there wasn't any french fries present to retrieve. There wasn't a Roy Roger's employee within eye site. I had to literally yell towards to the food prep area for a Roy Roger's to appear and request for an order of french fries. There was about an approximately five minute wait for the employee to cook the fries. In the meantime, there was a growing line of hungry customers waiting for menu items.
Once I received and paid for my food, I observed the lack of condiments in their self serve stations. An employee eventually appeared to replenish the ketchup in various condiment stations.
Roy Roger's Management needs to stay abreast of their employees, and remind them of their customer base. They are at a major highway rest area, and a fast food area. A customer should not have yell out into the food prep area for assistance, and idle by the condiment stations for anything.
Good food - good service.  I had the bacon,egg,cheese on Texas toast with hash browns - will return when in the area....

I have the prosciutto pizza, it was very good!  I started with the caesar salad with crabmeat crostini.  The salad was average but the crab-meat crostini made quiet an impression and I would order it again just for that!  Girlfriend had the duck which was very good!  Another friend had the shrimp pasta which I wasn't too excited about.  But the warm salmon salad got good reviews from those who tried it at the table.  The chocolate gnosh for dessert was very good as well.

My husband and I went to New Orleans a few weeks ago for a 4 day weekend. We did not have dinner reservations the first night and happened upon Coterie for dinner. I can't really speak for the food as we were so unimpressed with the atmosphere we just got the firecracker shrimp and a drink and left. There was absolutely NO ambience...no music, nothing! The bar area was ok, but we were seated by a table by the bar in the main dining room. The tv screen next to us just showed local commercials. We were in NOLA and bored out of our minds! There was even a table  of about 10 that was seated before us and  left after they got their water. I am assuming most of their customers are on vacation and are expecting a bit more 'atmosphere ' than they give. What
 a fantastic location they have...I hope they can step up their game.

What an experience!! Amazing food incredible staff and the owner AJ is awesome! We had the salmon and pork porterhouse. Everything was so tasty and we even got a glass of complimentary wine! Truly a great dinning experience and I would recommend checking out this spot if you are in town. It is very clean and AJ makes you feel like part of the family.

This is one of my new favorite restaurants in St. Louis. Locally sourced meat through Mac's Local Buys (the guy we buy meat from, too!). Amazing platings. Delicious food. When they first opened up, I think we went three or four times within a month span....they had turkey leg nachos on the menu which were both my husband's and my favorite. We'd like turkey leg nachos for appetizer, turkey leg nachos for salad, and turkey leg nachos for dinner.....and maybe turkey leg nachos for dessert! (We're talking four different orders here!) They are THAT good. Granted, I don't know if they are on the menu anymore, but yeah, look out for those.

Everything else we've had has been outstanding, too. We've taken our friends and family here. This place is a gem in the SoHa neighborhood. So impressed!

We've been here a few times on the weekend only now.  Definitely seems like this place would really be busier during the week with the work lunch crowd.

On the weekend it's been pretty light, which has made ordering quick and easy.  All of the different components we've tried have been delicious and fresh tasting.  I've tried a few different of the pre-selected bowls and the combinations have been great.

It's definitely not your typical build a bowl place and I really hope to see it continue to succeed.

Don't waste your time unless you have to. Its an airport bar with transients in and out. show your airline ID and get a discount. for us saps that don't have one we get charged the extra 10% .... high prices hotel food. even the domestic beers are Vegas prices... com'on.... its a coors light !!
Great food, great service! Taste like authentic Mexican food. Very reasonable prices.

Apparently asking for them to toast the bread is too much of an inconvenience at 9AM. I'll have to find somewhere else that can take 10 seconds out of their day to make an enormous request possible. Very rude, find somewhere else to get a better steak.

Casual dining s as bd lots of fresh local fish 

Quiet and  clean restaurant, we enjoyed a relaxing early dinner

You're not going to find anything at Hella's you can't find at other Greek restaurants.  What they do offer, however, is above average in quality and reasonably priced.  The atmosphere is conducive to conversation, the service is fast, and there's rarely a wait to be seated.

The gyros are good size and the hummus is tasty.  If you do get hummus, make sure to ask for extra pita bread as they never bring enough with the initial order.   After the meal, stock up on mints because you will reek of garlic.

Hella's could improve itself if it wasn't located in the middle of a small parking lot.  An outdoor patio with a hookah bar would be nice but won't happen unless it changes locations.

Tried this place out twice. Although the food was fresh service was lacking. Went on a Saturday afternoon, close to 2pm. Only had two other tables so it didn't look busy as expected for late lunch. We sat ourselves after a server instructed us. The girl who sat us came by for the initial welcome but didn't come back to take our order. After 10 minutes a different girl that was sweeping came by and asked us if we've been helped. We told her that we haven't and we were ready to order. I don't know if it was there was a shift change but the other two servers, the girl who welcomed us and another guy, didn't take any moment to see if we needed any help, which was weird. I had the crab roll plate and my boyfriend had two lobster rolls, but they accidentally made two crab rolls instead of one, this mix up was noticed by the server who took our order and was an easy adjustment off our bill. I'm not sure if we will be back since our experience with service being so slow and the price of the food being so high (which was not a problem).
So much food, got gyro platter #quality. Pretty good portion and friendly staff. Definitely come here if you are looking for some good food!

Stopped here on a Saturday night with the family and glad I did. The place isn't too big but was about 2/3 full. Got right in and were seated quickly. Max was our server and he was awesome. We started with the goat cheese appetizer and it was one of the best we've ever had which is saying a lot because my wife is a goat cheese fanatic. My wife and daughter got the beef brisket sandwich and they loved it. Wife also had the jalapeño brisket chili and found it perfect. Just a little spice but not overpowering. My son and I each got the brisket fettuccine and were very happy with our choices. We all shared 3 desserts: bread pudding, lava cake, and walnut brownie. The bread pudding was the favorite. Will certainly be back soon!

This review is just for the spicy braised beef noodle soup which I get all the time! The broth is not too salty, but still full of flavor, and can be made spicy on a scale of 1-5. There are lots of noodles in the bowl as well as tender pieces of beef, and a decent amount of greens. When I can't make the trip to Chinatown or South Philly but have an intense noodle soup craving, I go to Jane G's.

On the third day the holy one led us to the best Italian food in StL. Honest, we've been driving around the country 34 days eating local and this was great. Started with the deep fried raviolis. A local favorite. We each ordered one of the daily specials. They really hit the spot. The best!

Been here a couple times never really had bad service but the other night my gf and I decide to come here just before going to see a movie, the place was empty and there was a booth open by the bar. It took 10 min before the bartender came and asked us for our drink order and we went ahead and order app and entrees. Well it Took another 10 minutes for the appetizer to come out, then after that 15 minutes went by and we still hadnt received our food or been asked if we would like a refill on our drinks. The whole time the bartender was occupied doing everything else except tending to us, but what broke the straw on the camels back was when I got up to go to the bathroom looked through the window of the kitchen and saw him eating and talking to another server, that really pissed me off, won't be back here ever again
Delicious bagel place definitely underrated I give it five starts very nicely decorated and serviced !!

Had a great Sunday brunch experience! There was a slight wait, but Katie ensured we could start our bottomless mimosas before we were seated, and everything was great. Once seated, Kelsey took great care of my group of three and we all really enjoyed our food (I tried the special (crab omelet with sides and my friends had menu items). I will definitely be back, and hope to be served by Katie and or/ Kelsey again soon!
Great stop on the way to AC. Fresh and good quality food. Clean bathrooms and lavender soap!

I got the Nana's Favorite.  I don't know who this Nana lady is, but boy let me tell you, I'd like to give her a big kiss on the cheek.  This sandwich is like an elite thoroughbred that comes from the perfect pedigree.  It has such simple ingredients that all just fuse together magnificently.  Salsiccia that is butterflied, then a layer of provel cheese, a sweet marinara, some flavorful roast beef, and a great Italian white bread that locks it all in.  Even if I use every adjective in the dictionary, my courier new size 12 font on this screen doesn't do this sandwich enough justice.  Bring a couple of napkins, a big appetite, $10 and you will walk out of Adriana's with a new zest for life.  You're welcome.

First and last time I will be here. If I could use one word to describe the place, it would be SLOW. The food takes forever and a day to come out. I understand you can't rush Greek (no pun intended) but this is ridiculous. I didn't complain about it but people before me and after me were asking and asking and asking where there food was. The people next to me were one order ahead of us and it took 15 minutes for their soup to come out. How hard is it to ladle some soup into a bowl and send it out? 15 minutes.....really?
On a good note and only good note my Gyro taste fresh. However it was tiny, I thought I had ordered a kids plate or something. I also ordered a side of Greek fries. What they brought me was a bowl of potato chips with some taziki slapped on it and called them Greek fries. I challenge whomever owns this place to do a little research and get your product right. It's pretty obvious that this place is Greek in name only.

I was highly disappointed in Jones. My boyfriend and I went here on a regular date night based on a friend's recommendation. The drinks were good and strong but overpriced and the food was ehhhh.

For an appetizer we got the baked macaroni and cheese which was good but I wished the baked crumbs had a bit more seasoning. Outside of the cheese there wasn't much flavor.

My boyfriend got chicken & waffles which is hard to mess up. The chicken was extremely salty which we chucked up to balancing out the sweetness of the waffle with syrup.

Since my diet is limited to poultry and seafood I didn't have many options to pick from the menu. I chose the turkey burger which was underwhelming at best. The aioli and turkey bacon were good and I enjoyed the way they toasted the bread but the taste of the turkey burger made the entire thing a miss.

At most, I would go back for their drinks. Overall, the total cost of the meal did not equal the total experience. It was highly priced with a diner ambiance and food menu.

Very disappointed yesterday. The French fries were very undercooked, hard to screw up crinkle cuts and the baked beans were terribly bland. The fried chicken was ok but greasy, don't understand what all the hype is about.

Oh and my Schlaflys lager was flat.

There's a lot of great restaurants in New Orleans. There's so much to choose from, you might forget why you came to New Orleans in the first place. If you want some great Cajun/Creole food, then go to Dick and Jenny's.

Stop buying those $7.99 pizza's and get a quality pie! I got a Meatball and a standard Margarita pizza. Fresh basil, homemade sauce, high quality cheese, Ricotta, sliced tomatoes, made these pizzas memorable. Do yourself and your family a favor. Spend the extra money, to get the real deal.
This used to be my favorite sushi place to go to.  Ownership has definitely changed, the menu is different, the service is horrible and the food is sub par.  Don't waste your time.
So nice to see such positive changes here in the past year.  The service is friendly and attentive, while the food is consistently top notch.  We are a fan of Lucky's

The speidi sauce that they use on all chicken has a little spicy kick to it, but it doesn't say this anywhere on the menu nor was it was described as spicy to us by the server. My hubby doesn't do any spicy food at all so the chicken was too hot for him to enjoy. BUT the chicken was cooked perfectly moist and not all dried out. The fries were nothing spectacular, in fact, should've been cooked longer. Onion rings were good. Prices were descent and service was great (except they need to tell people about the slight spiciness of the speidi sauce!!!)

I came here fully expecting the possibility of a lame, touristy meal. They say the waiters are in period dress, but it's not over the top and just seems right. 

The food itself though is the reason to come. Ordered the lobster pie, despite the listing of "market price". It wasn't cheap, but it was worth it. I would suggest splitting it with someone unless you can eat a lot of rich food by yourself. The sauce is the best part and eats more like a soup, spent a good minute just smelling the darn thing before breaking open the flakiest, most delectable puff pastry known to man. 

The bread is also good, though I think T. Jefferson's favorite sweet potato biscuit should be served at breakfast not dinner, but Sally Lunn knew how to make a good white bread. I thought the slice I had felt dry when I was buttering, but when you bite into it, it's soft and chewy texture knows no bounds. 

And get Martha's raspberry shrub champagne cocktail. Perfect compliment to rich food.

Ordered food last night.  Had the Combo meal, Shrimp Basket, and Wings.  All very good but especially liked the man taking my order.  Wasn't sure of what I wanted to order but was really patient with me.  Will be back.  Delicious food, large quantity, and very reasonably priced.

Best tamale we've had in years.  Our meal was flavorful, fresh, not salty, service was excellent, well worth the wait to sit down.  Once ordered, we didn't have to wait long.  

You may have to flag down your server.  I'd give 5 stars but the front of the house was in total disarray and physically laid out in such a way that customers leaving, waiting and paying were all in the way of the staff shuttling food both out of the kitchen and to the outside waiting area that doubles as a seating area...not sanitary in that regard, and very stressful.

But again, the food was well worth it.
The strip mall that it's in is kind of scary looking but the restaurant is not.  Delicious pho and nice, attentive staff!!

I have visited this Brentwood location and their Memphis one as well, and it's just not for me.

I am a spice wimp.  Trust me, really.  At Humdinger's, it is very tough for me to find something to order.  I had a half chicken with grilled sweet potatoes and grilled corn on the cob, and everything has a red seasoning sprinkled over it (everything, the sweet potatoes and corn included - did NOT see that coming) that while I could eat it, my lips were burning halfway through, and I found myself taking a napkin to the corn to try and dab off any excess whatever it was.

You would think that a person ordering who tells the cashier they are the biggest spice wimp ever (I always do), confirms what they are ordering is not going to be spicy, twice - that maybe they could mention the Cajun/chipotle/African whatever it is and not add it on top?  But no.  They had omitted for me in Memphis I guess and just didn't tell me.

Hubby can take some spice, but by the end of his meal he was struggling, too.  I realize the current in/fashionable/gourmet trend is spicy and garlic (I'm allergic to that, go figure), but it's just not for me.

Dined here with my wife and several other people who are part of a monthing dining out group.  This review should be a 3.5 - somewhere between the A0OK and I'm a fan.  The service at dinner was fine and the food was OK.  The bread was fresh and tasty, but the oil and balsamic presentation was very hard to get anything but 95% oil and only a little of the vinegar.  My biggest problem with the presentation of the bread is the lack of imagination - if you're not going to do anymore than just oil and vinegar, why bother?!  I had the lasagne at the recommendation of the bartender and it was OK, not great.  Large portion for sure, but nothing that will bring me back soon.  What might bring me back is the sea bass special.  It looked terrific and was reportedly very good.  There are so many other Italian restaurants in Tucson that I'll likely try a few I have not been to before I return to Caffe Torino.  Nothing really bad, just not good enough to bring be back that soon.

called order in, was there with in 10 min  (order said 15min) food was ice cold, other food was cold and did not seem fresh (was not cooked that day).  For the over priced food, will never order from them again.

My husband and I went for drinks on the terrace during the sunset on a Thursday afternoon. The atmosphere is low key, slow pace, but offers excellent service! The drinks were impeccable: ordered the Garden Gimlet and the Sage + "something" - it had whiskey in it! Anyhow, it was extremely relaxing and we enjoyed a fantastic cheese plate while there. Highly recommend- even if you're not staying at the hotel- go for a drink and enjoy the views!

Cool decor, nice atmosphere.

Food was great!  I had the scallops one night & the roasted chicken the following night.  

Pizza was fresh & tasty.

Service was a liiiiitle on the slow side - but this may be the fact that I live in NY & I am a server.  I just expect things to come at a faster pace.  

Our dinner was running late and this man (a manager, i think?) offered us a free appetizer.  I believe his name was VITO but I could be completely wrong.  He was so nice & made a great impression on us.  

I highly suggest this place.  Great prices, good food, tasty sangria, can't go wrong.

Talk about great tacos! The Brussel Sprouts and Bacon jam taco was amazing, (and I am not a huge Brussel Sprout fan). The Scallop Taco and Pork Carnita which I have had other times are equally creative and delicious!  Fermentaria had a big lunchtime crowd, enjoying the unseasonal snowstorm through the big windows. Our server, Bree, was excellent, stopping by occasionally to see what we needed. I love the friendly service, fresh ingredients and creative new taste combinations from the chefs!

Limited menu but I think they do everything well that is on the menu. Ordered a bologna sandwich with fries. Very good! A friend ordered a cheese burger and said it was also delicious. We also had fried pickles which were very good! Service was pretty good also.

Ordered traditional beef and lamb gyro, and my co worker ordered the gryo plate special. Both meals had a large portion of gyro meat and both of us were impressed. I would suggest visiting this place to get full on quick and excellent tasting gryos.
Very good beef and tendon noodle soup.  Ordered basil eggplant and tofu with bold Choy to go.  Been wanting to try this place, glad I did today!
Awesome pizza, great service, thanks to the Thursday night crew for the awesome experience! Def recommend stopping here!

We had an excellent experience here! We came on a Saturday night at 7:30 and the expected wait was 45 minutes, they do not take reservations. They take down your phone number and will text you when your table is ready, although I don't think there is much else around nearby to do while waiting.

Among the three of us we had the kale salad, blue bison burger, yucca fries and the no meatloaf! Each of us thought our meals were superb! The kale salad is definitely recommended and the red grapefruit paired perfectly with the other fixings.

Sandwiches come a la carte and you will definitely want to order a side to accompany them if you come for dinner. I recommend the yucca fries! They have several different seasonings that you get to choose between!

Will be returning soon! Would be 5 stars if they took reservations!
Love the drive thru and the sizes. Mardi Gras Mash is enough to put you on your a$$. But great drinks

I've been to Thai Orchid two times in the past 3 months.  Both times it was an overall superb experience.  Food was delicious and beautiful, service was courteous and attentive.  We will frequent this restaurant often

I think the food was okay, however, I didn't spend a whole lot of time there so I didn't get to taste everything. It had a pretty wide selection of food than I'm used to seeing at Asian buffets. When greeted at the door, the woman wasn't the kindest, and the set up wasn't too fancy or pleasant. It was quite bland and casual. The sushi selection wasn't as extensive as I hope, but it was pretty alright to quench a craving. The salt shakers were also sticky and dirty, as well as the table itself--which was very off putting. However, there are free refills, which is neat, but mostly, it's the customer service and hygiene that resulted in a lower rating.

Buttered mustard sauce
Covers porterhouse Pork Chop
Smile covers my face

Quite possibly the best meal I've had in years. 

This quaint BYO's one page menu is a list of American inspired all-star dishes. Our waiter rightfully called the braised short ribs their unofficial signature dish. This was proven true as the two in my party that ordered them quickly fell into a silent feeding trance as soon as the dish hit the table. 

The hanger steak and halibut dishes also were both as pleasing to the eye as they were the tongue. Yours truly went with the porterhouse cut pork chop with buttered mustard sauce. I know from years of experience with these monsters that cooking to a perfect medium is no easy task but our chef achieved his goal flawlessly. 

In my post pork bliss I agreed to share a vanilla ice cream topped strawberry & rhubarb cobbler that has since made me question what I've been doing with my life. Amazing food.

Final note. I was quite impressed by the way with which our waiter handled our party of six as well as the other 7 tables of various sizes BY HIMSELF! You hear that slackers. No busser, no front or back waiters, nada! He filled the glasses, opened the bottles, explained the specials, took the orders, delivered the orders (correctly)...blah blah blah all of it and it was perfect. 

As for prices, well here is where we get into the discussion of value. While the entrees avg. between $25-$30 range (not bad, but not cheap) the quality & skill makes it a no brainer. 

My reviews don't come as often as they once did because I feel I need to be effected either positively or negatively by an establishment to be inspired to write...I've been inspired by No.9 and you will be too.

Went for dinner on a wintery night and came away not quite satisfied.  The starter red wine shrimp were very good and a generous portion at $18. The tamarind chicken was OK, the favours were muted. The chicken satay were truly disappointing - no grill marks or char on the chicken and marinade was bland.

I was really wanting dessert but there was nothing that seemed fitting for a cold night.  

Service was good, food came up quickly.

So it was a pleasant meal, but there is much better Thai food around.

We love going to Seamus McDaniel's in Dogtown.  We go for lunch, happy hour and dinner and we love introducing newbies to the big burgers and big chicken sandwiches.  And the gooey melty provel cheese garlic bread is delicious.
This place is very small, but it has excellent food.  I know people who have also held small events here and they do a very nice job.

This is mainly a take out place but they do have a counter you can sit and eat at.   I have been here a few times and it is very busy at lunch.  For a quick supper, it seems much more calm.   Today I had the Singapore noodles.   Nicely spices with beef, chicken, and shrimp.   It was very filling and they could have cut back on the amount of noodles to make the noodle to meat and vegetables ratio better.   But all in all, very tasty.

We decided to watch the Monday night football game at this location tonight. We had a huge group and were taken care of beyond what I expected. Quick service, great food and our drink were never empty and the waitress always check on us to make sure if we needed anything. Also we requested the game for the night and the manager Chris Combs tuned the TV's for us and had the volume up for us as we requested without question. All around great time, great atmosphere, great service and wonderful time thanks to the service, management and cooks. I highly recommend this location for any occasions, chill, food, drinks, get together, date night and for sure any sports events. Thanks again soooooo much for a great night!!! Will be back this season that's for sure!

This is one of those "Everybody knows your name" place. They make you feel welcome from the second you walk in the door. Coffee was always free flowing and delicious. Very large selection of items on the menu for both breakfast and lunch. If I lived closer I would be there a few times a week.I had their crabcake eggs Benedict and my guest had a vegetable omelette both were superb, service was quick and very attentive. It takes a real treat to get five stars out of me and this was a real treat. I look forward to my next visit at Chia Café.

This is as generic as it gets without actually being a chain store.
Service was ok.
The chips were good, the salsa just ok.
The Nachos grande with chili con carne were pretty bland, with cheap tasteless cheese.
The chimichanga with pork and tomatillo sauce was banal with nothing special about it.
They asked for 2.5$ for a table spoon of tasteless, mushy guacamole. 

This place tastes like it serves TV dinner mexican food.
Wings were soggy not good. Blue cheese was cheap. Not worth the price. Fries were over priced and pizza was average.

I go here a lot whenever I'm in Tampa for business. The BBQ meats are average to above average, but their side dishes are outstanding and is what keeps me coming back. The spicy macaroni salad is the most unique style I have had anywhere and is my favorite dish. A close second would be the BBQ beans. The fries are good too and a lot of people seem to get those, although there is usually a wait while they make more.

There is usually a line out the door unless you come at an odd time. Ordering can be somewhat intimidating and reminds me of a black version of the Soup Nazi; the guys behind the counter all look like hardcore gangsters, and seem too high to say anything and just stare at you when it's your turn to order. If you're not paying attention they'll take someone else's order.

Running errands in the area and after my experience at The Washington House for brunch,  been to the Local a bunch of times... Wanted something different. Yelp delivered. For breakfast, I prefer lively crowds, and Stella had a lively crowd. I walked in just in time to take the corner table by the window. Great for people watching inside and out. The meat lovers omelette was perfect, just as I would have made at home. The rye bread was different but good.

I will try the cream chipped beef the next time and update my review.

I'll be back.

Have been here twice ready.  Once for dinner the week they opened and once again the week after for Lunch. We are vegetarian and ordered the Pad Kra Pow, Pad Kee Mao and Panang Curry.  The Panang Curry had a splash of coconut milk on top of it.  Different and unexpected.  Taste was good and flavor was not like that of other restaurants in the area.  We were 2 of 3 in favor of it.  The vegetables were fresh, the tofu on point and the spice level was great.  If you can't handle spice do not get anything above mild.  If you can take the heat then try extra hot.  Have not done thai hot yet but be warned on the heat.  Maybe try hot and take some hot sauce or dry chili powder on the side.  

For lunch orders you get soup, a vegetarian spring roll and your order.  We did not care much for the soup.  Would rather have more of the entree.  Spring Roll was great.  

Looking forward to having this option in the area.  Competition is a good thing and hope this helps being others up too.

Other reviews have commented on the *cough* interesting logo, but weird places like this are my favorite. We stopped in for a late lunch and I loved it. the ample seating and outdoor are a nice touch. The drinks were cheap and their drink menu is hilarious (seriously we read it aloud like poetry). The food was good. The tots needed to be crispier, but my Ruben was delicious. My husband go the pork shank- beautiful and delicious. So tender! We'll definitely come back when we're in the area.

Maybe you get a better quality experience dining at the restaurant...? With such good reviews, I was expecting a much better experience but...

My order not ready after 2 hours:
I submitted an order online about 2 hours before I needed to pick it up. However, when I arrived, I was informed that the order had not yet been submitted to the kitchen. I had to wait at the restaurant as they rushed to put together my order. The restaurant was empty, so it was not like they were backed up. 

Seafood pan fried noodle:
Mostly liquid. Lacked seafood. 2 pieces of shrimp and 2 scallops. The scallops were rubbery, and old. Normally my favorite dish. This was just disappointing. Definitely do not recommend. 

Chicken and broccoli:
Not as much flavor as other places. Sauce was watered down. Chicken rubbery. 

Potstickers: 
Mediocre. Not very flavorful, would skip these.

Shumai: 
The best item from my order. Delicious.

Excellent service, atmosphere, and amazing food! Their bread tho... Out of this world with flavor and creativity. I enjoy making toast again. They take time getting ingredients right and know where it all comes from, the quality of the bread shows.

Disappointed after online reviews. Super mediocre food and even worse service. Filthy bathrooms. And we were there mid day. 

Very cool space so hopefully they figure out the food and service side of things.

I'm trying not to kill my weight loss but...when in New Orleans...you must eat New Orleans food!

A friend suggested getting a shrimp po boy but I thought about the bread...I couldn't do it. But, I opted for the shrimp platter with the house salad and red beans and rice. The shrimp was plentiful and tasty. It was really enough for later or to share. I did neither! The house salad had romaine lettuce and tomatoes and was tossed with Italian dressing. The red beans and rice was fine. 

There was a nice crowd of people when I got there and when I left. I probably waited 15 minutes for my to go order. I had no problem with that. My hot food was still hot when I got to my destination less than 15 minutes later. I plan on coming here again.

Hidden gem.  Authentic.  Delicious.  Really can't believe we've never been here.  Had the Middle Eastern sampler and the tabouleh, falafel and babaganouche was more flavorful than I have had.  31 years - an institution in Lansdale.

I asked the bartender for a shot of 12 year Jameson. She looked at the regular Jameson and said "no, but I have the 10 year."  I get it. It's an "Irish" bar in Reno. 

$3 Stella's.  

$4 Guinness in IMPERIAL pints! That's terrific! 

They have tons of Scotch, actually a pretty good selection by anyones standards, but why?  It's an Irish bar. The best they have is Powers and Bushmills Black.

There isn't much Irish in here.  

Food was serviceable pub-grub but nothing to get super-stoked about.

I hate to give less than 3 stars but Santorini was a disappointment in just about every way possible. 

#1 the menu. I appreciated that it identified gluten free foods since I can not eat wheat. This was a positive +1

#2 the service. While our server was good he had too many tables.  This meant that every time I emptied my water glass it sat empty for a while and I had to drink from my wife's water glass. Even though other servers were standing around with nothing to do and/or had the water pitcher but only supplied water to their tables even though I was 5 feet away? Got the serious vibe that either the staff doesn't like each other. They certainly didn't care if people not at their table didn't have water.

And their was one waiter that looked like possibly the only Greek in the restaurant and he spent the most time just standing around. Pick up the water pitcher and make sure your patrons have water.

#3 the food. Just awful. Tasteless. I got the fish souvlaki. Never in my life has scallops, shrimp and fish been so tasteless. I don't know how the fish was cooked either but it was dry. And even though they heap tons of sides on the plate that too had little to no taste. Our friends who brought their 12 year old son commented the Pastichio was too spicy and the kids spaghetti sauce was too spicy too. 

#4 Between the lackluster service and bad food the total bill for 5 people was $135 which just seemed incredulous to me. Way overpriced for the poor quality meals.

Let me put it this way. No one at the table finished their meal (or even got more than half way through it) and no one took any home to go. That is how bad the food was. I won't be back.

Best Malaysian food ever! Staff is great and fast....make sure you give them good tip because they deserve it.

Try the golden fried squid and the mango chicken...the best combination.

This is a friend's favorite restaurant, and she chose Brio as the location of our first tete-a-tete since I moved back to STL. I read many reviews here on Yelp beforehand, so I felt well-prepared, but not terribly excited.

We arrived around 5:45, and the happy hour was hopping. Not my crowd; I used to work at Plaza Frontenac, not hang with Plaza Frontenac. Plenty of seating in the dining room.

We ordered cocktails, mine was the Raspberry Mojito, and my friend ordered something custom. They arrived quickly, and although mine was good, I didn't taste any booze. Had I not had a few the night before, I might have pursued this with the waitress. The triangle crispy things were good, as was the warm sourdough. Even though I always eat the bread they bring out at restaurants, I just wish the industry as a whole would stop this practice. It fills you up, you're not hungry when the entree arrives, and you have all sorts of misplaced bullshit carb guilt. Why not bring out some vegetables and salsa or hummus? Just saying.

Per a suggestion from another Yelper, I joined Brio's rewards whatever and had the $10 appetizer coupon. We wanted apps from the light menu, which has appetizers and starter salads listed in the same category. The waitress would not accept the coupon for any of the starter salads, saying the computer would not accept said coupon for ANYTHING but a designated appetizer. Splitting hairs like this annoys me, especially when the food is so overpriced. $4.95 - $6.95 for a side salad? Really?

At this point, it was becoming obvious that the waitress, for whatever reason, had lost interest in us. I actually began timing how long it took her to come back to the table. Perhaps she saw two women talking and lingering over drinks, so thought we were there for the long haul. We weren't, but the slow-ass service saw to that. When my friend ordered a second drink, it took over 20 minutes for the waitress to bring it. I was scanning the restaurant to find another member of the waitstaff to fetch her when I finally spotted her coming our way. Was it busy? Yeah...but not that freaking busy. It became a game and a source of exasperated humor between my friend and I.

When we ordered, the waitress didn't tell us about any specials, so I have no idea if Brio even does specials. I ordered the Pasta Alla Vodka and my friend ordered the Roasted Half Chicken. Many reviews on this site mentioned the massive portions. My friend had a ton of food left over, and I had zero. I tried to keep it light with the bread and appetizers, so that I was hungry for the actual meal, maybe that's it. I do know this: there was not $18.25 worth of anything on that plate.

The disappearing waitress act got so bad that my friend spoke with the manager, who recognized her from many previous visits. He was incredibly gracious, apologetic, and comped all of the food on our bill, leaving us with the tab for four drinks.

Bottom line: food was fine, service was definitely lacking. I would go back begrudgingly, but it would be someone else's idea and I would try to steer them to another restaurant.

I love Raijin.  It is by far the best Ramen in town.  When Raijin first opened I was a bit intimidated by the line that often forms out front.  When we first visited we found that the wait in line is frequently less than 5 minutes, and never more than 20.  That said, I would wait an hour+ for their delicious noodles. 

All of the selections are solid.  I am partial to the Tonkotsu w/ Black Garlic, but my son loves the Vegetarian.  The Japanese craft beers are also worth a shot.  The White Yuzu is especially delicious.  

Do yourself a favor and try Raijin.  You are missing out if you don't

I love the concept for this place: a community gathering place. There's food, drinks, bowling, swimming, bocce ball, and (reportedly) karaoke! We had dinner Friday and brunch Sunday--both were good. Best part: you can order fried broccoli at either meal. A gem of an appetizer. Also order the grits, catfish, or any cocktail. I recommend A Sidecar Named Doug. Tasty. Nice atmosphere, nice service, a tad slow even on the coffee and apps but worth the time.

Great French food at a reasonable price. Went there with my wife and daughter for our 50th Anniversary. The owner came out to greet us and congratulate us. He was very personable and kind. The food was excellent. Will be going there again. It is a pre fixe menu which makes is easier to decide what to have. Very good and, knowing French snobbery, a very affordable place to enjoy.
The food was great. Hannah was awesome and showed fantastic service. The maine lobster carbonara was excellent, creamy and the lovster was cooked perfectly.

A few friends and I decided to stop in here after dinner on a Friday night. So, this review is strictly for their wine, atmosphere, and service. 

When we got there, it was packed! But, we waited about 10 mins and were able to snag 4 seats at the back bar (at the raw bar prep station). I love the fact that they have half glasses of wine because it really allows you to try so many different types! We each tried several half glasses of wine and enjoyed each one. Two of us also tried the Tredici Standard cocktail and found it just a little too sweet. 

The service was exquisite. Everyone was friendly and could answer any questions we had about the drink menu. There was a customer next to us that appeared drunk and kept trying to talk to our group. The staff handled him in a very professional manner and made sure we felt comfortable. It was very reassuring! 

The atmosphere is very modern and chic. Sitting at the raw bar prep station is awesome because you get to see the oysters, crab claws, shrimp, etc. The restaurant also feels very open since there are tables outside and the walls open up to create that "open air" feel. All the food that we saw being prepared looked very fresh! I'd love to go back and try their food :) Overall, it seems to be a great place for drinks and small plates/appetizers! Definitely a great addition to the Philly food/drink scene!

Great place to go for some pints before a game.

The food is of top quality. The burgers are extremely fresh, the beef is fresh. The patties are made in house. Stay away from the nachos though they are small, you don't get what you pay for 18$. 

Beer + food + arcades = good times

Be prepared to be loud in there and have to scream to each other. Lol

You can reserve tables. I would suggest doing so if you plan on going there after 5-6pm. 

Overall I will go back, it's a great place to hangout and play arcades and have some drinks.

We went here early Sunday afternoon and found the food to be good. I was a little worried when, at about 2:30, the place seemed empty but the staff was friendly and the 3 of us were promptly seated and drink orders taken. 

We didn't order an appetizer, but after we ordered our meals, Carlos, our waiter, brought us the house salad and breadsticks, which were very good. 

Shortly after, the meals, Chicken Parm and Chicken Picatta arrived. Very healthy portions. The Chicken Parm had 2 large breasts, battered and baked covered in a flavorful red sauce and cheese over pasta. The Picatta was about 8 chicken medallions in a creamy sauce over pasta. 

My 2 kids (18 and 21) could only eat about half of their portion, but I finished. There was no room for dessert, 

The food was good. I'd gladly go back.

Stopped in on a Friday night with my boyfriend and a friend and was pleasantly surprised they had a happy hour on Fridays. Not only just a happy hour, and amazing happy hour! Drinks were super cheap- I had two mixed drinks and they were $5 each and we had two rolls which one was $7 and the other was $5 and the steak fried rice (not on happy hour menu). The rolls were incredible- superman roll and spicy salmon roll. The superman was my favorite- to die for. The service was decent and we sat outside. You have to sit outside or at the bar for the happy hour and it was nice out. Overall highly recommend for their happy hour M-F. It's amazing and a great value. Will definitely be back for cocktails and sushi.
The cocktails and the mussels were soooo good! The best part of the place was the ambience, the decor, and the service by the employees!

Pretty good stuff! Liked the food and service. Had the Turkey Reuben with sweet potato fries. Quite delicious!

The layout was very interesting, it's clean and sleek. No restaurant equipment visible anywhere. It's just a room with tables. Makes it very intimate.
Not too expensive for a new try out. Down a dark road. Feel like hanging in a neighborhood of close friends and relatives. ATM on site.
This place has a lot of potential but misses the bar on some points. Service was slow and food took a long time to come out. The food was decent but not worth the price.

Beer was great. Service was excellent. Food was underwhelming. I ordered pizza. The pizza crust was comparable to frozen. My friend got the burger. Again looked like bulk frozen patties. Maybe being from a "brew/foodie city" I am spoiled by the handcrafted foods in the breweries. Any hoo, probably will not return.

I liked this place earlier but the food now seems average. The general attentiveness of the wait staff is poor. I waited for 20 minutes before one of 3 waiters loitering around showed up to take my order. They seem disorganized since the front staff ask you to sit anywhere and then forget to communicate to the wait staff!

Overall a decent place. The shawarmas are good but if you have eaten good shawarmas and middle Eastern food before then this place is definitely average. Not bad for St Louis standards though.

I've had breakfast here several times now, and it's always been OK.  I haven't been wowed, but it hasn't been bad either.  The restaurant is clean, and bright, but the tables are close together, so when it's crowded it gets pretty noisy.  I feel like everyone around you can hear your conversation and you can hear theirs.  In the evening I'm more accepting of loud places,  in fact I really enjoy being in a booming environment when the sun goes down, but in the morning I just want a quieter setting.

The food is average, and I find the prices a little high for the quality.

I must, however, highlight the staff.  The folks that work here have always been very nice and my meal service has always been timely and super efficient.

This place is legit.  No longer need to drive to Nashville for an excellent prime steakhouse.  Prices are better too.   The grilled buttery garlic bread is amazing and so were the sides.  Steaks were excellent.  Our server Christine was very attentive, as were the rest of the crew.

Not worth my time.    Workers Don't Listen.  Orders are Never right Ordered a quesadilla WITHOUT any Sauce 


Of course my kid couldn't eat the jalapeno sauce.     Unreal Workers.     Fire them

Fast friendly service for good, not great  Mexican food. The place was clean and very busy.  What the menu they are charging small amounts for things that you woulld think would be free. Fee for carry out....

Been enjoying delicious, hot pho at Saigon for more than 10 years, starting at their Lafayette Rd location.  Service is always friendly and efficient and food always reliable and reasonably priced.  One of our go-to restaurants for a quick, filling meal.  Banh-mi sandwiches, potstickers snd goi rolls always hit the spot.

Such a rad little spot. 

Walking in and it's immediately noticeable that the owners and staff here take immense pride in this little cafe. Parking might be a little tricky but I'm sure there are plenty of spots around the block, I walked here while getting my smog done. 

The shop is clean, open, and super well decorated overall with a great modern vibe while being super comfortable. 

I'm a pretty simple coffee drinker but I had to try something new in a place like this. I got the burnout which is one of their signature drinks. At $7 it's not exactly super cheap but most certainly worth it. Along with that I got the avocado toast which you would think is over done in Santa Barbara but was perfect here with just the right combination of flavors  

Overall this cafe is a great addition to the area and I would definitely go here again for a treat. 

Plus they are super environmentally conscious and center around sustainability. Always a bonus.

The food was average... 
The risotto wasn't good 
My son ask for a sundae from the the kids menu and they serve him coffee ice cream,...
All the food we got was super good! Chili-cheese etouffe maque chaux and gumbo. SQUIRREL!!!

Everything was delicious!!! We ordered the beef roast, filet mignon country fried steak and the fried catfish. We loved every bite!! The waitress, Cora was very accommodating and attentive to our every need. He atmosphere was ambient while still kid-friendly. We will come back next time we're in the NO!!

We were on brunch here last Sunday. Restaurant was noisy and stuffed with people, but overall I like the place. Food is unique, delicious with excellent presentation. Portions are large, I had to share my red velvet pancakes with a sister. I like it's byob. I hate it's cash only.

Unlike a lot of the previous reviewers I had a good experience. Service was fast and efficient. Breakfast was hot and tasty. Prices are not too bad for an airport location.


Update
Tried to get a sandwich to go. OUT OF BREAD!  Are you kidding me!!! A deli that is out of bread may as well shut the doors!

Excellent food ! Everything on the menu is superb! 
The atmosphere is amazing ! Large open spacious for larger parties and they always play great music that sounds amazing !!! My go to on Sunday ' yes they will be busy so get there earlier than the Sunday brunch crowd and you'll be in and out with smile and feeling full ! Very very good food

Usually solid, but just got the most lifeless biryani I've had. White rice and chicken...disappointing.

Reached out and offered replacement. Very gracious.

My husband and I have been coming here for years.  We love this place.  It is not only our favorite restaurant in the city but one of our favorite restaurants of all time.  If you appreciate a good steak and excellent service, BP is where you need to go.  Don't leave without having the deep dish cookie for dessert.  We plan on returning as often as possible.  Our server this last time was Glen.  We will ask for him the next time we go.

Nice chic place, came for breakfast, and luckily checked in first. Wait was not bad but they were very busy. I can confidently say the wait was well worth it. I had the Monte Crisco which was very decadent, and different, they grill it here vs deep frying, and give you a side of strawberry jam for dipping, so good. Wife had the Lox and said it was excellent. Upscale chic decor, great service and ambiance. We will be back next time we're in town.

I don't understand the hype here. I can see where it's got a lot of potential...maybe a bad night when I went.

Pluses: 
Food is quick, it's BYOB, and it's cool that the tables are big and there's space for larger groups.

The pizza was lacking that good slightly burnt flavor a Neopolitan pizza should have.  Salads are small and overpriced.

Maybe it was just a bad night; based on the other reviews, I'd have to think so.

This is the best taqueria in Tucson hands down!

Get the red chile salsa.  Hot and declicious

Our server was friendly but not attentive in any way. It seemed like some of her friends or acquaintances were also dining there. She engaged in a 20+ minute conversation with them while we were waiting to pay for our overpriced, cold, lack of seasoning, sat under the heat lamp for hours, not fresh, frozen crostini, piss poor meals. We asked another server if he could give us our checks. He asked who our server was, we gave him her name and he proceeded to walk past her three times without saying a word to her about our request. Again, the service was poor and  the food was less than stellar. I would not recommend this establishment to my worst enemy.

I have never been to such a pretentious restaurant in all my life. The rules of this establishment are uncalled for. The hottess gave my party of 4 a time limit for our dinner, along with a cash only and a $18 per person minimum policy. These are the rudest and most disrespectful policies I have ever encountered. The prices and atmosphere are not worth that bullshit. Not to mention they don't take reservations, the food was decent but not worth the price.
Crispy tofu over soba noodles, mango salsa and peanut sauce with avocado. So good. Great texture and flavor.

For the first time in my life, I can say I've had flavorless Indian food. I'm really shocked that there are good reviews here.

My fiancee and I live in the neighborhood and came here on Valentine's Day. I was really excited for a new BYOB and a new Indian spot, my favorite cuisine! Checked out the menu beforehand since I was looking to avoid pre-fixe menus. There was just the regular dinner menu listed on Makhani's site and OpenTable, perfect! 

We arrived for our reservation at 8:00 and had to wait about 5-10 minutes--I'm totally okay with that, they just opened and it's one of the biggest dining nights of the year. Someone brought us each a glass of wine, which I assumed was because they were running behind. We were seated and had to wait another 10 minutes until someone brought us a menu. Again, I can deal with that.

When we finally got our menus, we learned it was indeed a pre-fixe menu, which was not listed on Open Table or Makhani's site. That explains the wine they handed us. Okay, so I guess we're eating off a pre-fixe menu. Except, what Indian restaurant has a pre-fixe menu and only one vegetarian option? The only vegetarian entree option was Aloo Gobi, which I think is delicious, but cauliflower unfortunately doesn't sit well in my stomach. Luckily the chef offered to cook something off the standard dinner menu for me.

My omnivore fiancee ordered the tandoori chicken wings and salmon begum bibhar; I ordered the veggie cutlet appetizer (only option) and okra (off of the regular dinner menu). Fiancee reported that the tandoori chicken wings were good. The veggie cutlet... oh my goodness. I've tasted few dishes in my life with that little amount of flavor. It was like the type of food you would feed to a toddler who is insanely picky. It was basically mashed up potatoes, battered and fried but with ZERO seasoning! It tasted like nothing! It was served with two chutneys which were also somehow lacking in flavor!

My okra dish was pretty okay, I have had better but I did appreciate the chef cooking it just for me. I ordered medium out of mild/medium/hot and it was definitely not medium or spicy at all, but at least had some cilantro, onion, and curry and cumin flavors. Fiancee's salmon... so bland. The server also asked if he wanted mild/medium/hot and he asked for hot. The server even asked "are you sure, I just want to warn you that it's really hot!" He reported that not only was it not spicy... there was no flavor at all. No ginger, garlic, herbs, spices, etc. Nothing! How can food be so bland, especially Indian food? I can at least say that the garlic naan was on point.

Since I read other reviews I was expecting the mango cheesecake to be a life changer! It was one of the better parts of the meal, which doesn't say much, but was doused in an overly sweet berry sauce.

They had a very unfurnished bathroom on the second floor with no trash bin and people were throwing their used paper towels on the window and floor. Just a mess.

I totally understand the chaos of a restaurant on Valentine's Day and can forgive some things like running late and taking forever to get menus. They also just opened, so the staff is likely to get more organized with more practice. But flavorless food? That's definitely not going to improve.

I love this place. We come here mainly for breakfast! I love the frenchtoast and the gyro breakfast wrap! And every time I get an order of the grilled biscuits  we have no eaten here too much for lunch or dinner items, but we have tried there gyro and taco salad. Both were good. But I would recommend this place mainly for breakfast.
Seems over rated. I stood in line for 45 minutes. I ordered one of the eggs Benedictus. The biscuit was dry. I would not wait in line again for that place. Not sure it was worth the wait or the price
