Cute little restaurant in Hyde Park. We have Been here for dinner before but today we came in for brunch. Honestly I like brunch better than dinner. 
We had the breakfast flat bread, yellowfin tuna and the boca cubano sandwich. They were all outstanding.  
The only problem I have with the restaurant is the noise. Makes it difficult to have a conversation without screaming. 


They also have take our for 2 for $29 dollars. I think it's pretty price for dinner and dessert for 2.
This place is great! I've always wanted to try Pho and finally did and now I can't get enough. It is so good. I've also had the strawberry boba tea and it was really delicious.
Don't do the extremely hot levels  - but overall a very excellent place - landmark to hit up in Nashville

Fresh quality food and great fresh breads.  The only complaint I had with the chicken Brazilian sandwich was that the cheese overpowered the rest of the ingredients and left them on the blandish side.  I didn't really taste anything but the awesome bread and gooey cheese. Best time I will order sans cheese.  Still super filling, good quality and very reasonably priced.  This is a food trailer so you will be eating outside or in your car.
Great food! The brisket is amazing, the sides are delicious and the desserts are so yummy!
Food was ok, not amazing! Service was thumbs down.  I know you're closing in forty minutes, but geez at least give me semi service. Waiter was all over the place. I asked to wrap the food

First time for us to go here, we are here for the winter from Michigan, we go by there quite often and kept saying we need to go one night.  The reviews that I read were good and I went on line for menu and prices, except no prices, that's not good!!  I read a good salad bar,so we tried it.  Guess what no more salad bar!!  They did have early bird specials all day, not bad, a salad with dinner.  Food was good, service was very good.

I come here once a year for my free birthday treat. This year I opted for a free creamslush. It was good (and free!). Be sure to sign up for their email thing to get a coupon on your birthday.

Other than that, I really don't go to Sonic very often. I prefer Wendy's when fast food is necessary. However, on my last birthday visit, I discovered something wonderful... Sweet Potato Tots. These are amazing. I may make a return trip for lunch in the near future to enjoy more tots.

Edible food/drinks, clean parking lot, kind of slow (but that's expected with car-side service), really cheap. A solid 3 stars.

We're always looking to try new places and couldn't pass up the great reviews for this place. It's basically half food store, half restaurant. My husband couldn't resist buying some authentic snacks that he couldn't read the label for but that looked interesting. Not a ton of space to sit in, but we were doing take out anyway. There's street parking and a lot nearby. We ordered enchiladas con pollo with red and green sauce, a molotes with carnitas, and a burrito with suadero. The enchiladas come as a meal with delicious rice and beans and avocado. It seemed authentic and had a good amount of chicken inside. The molotes was new for us. Not really sure what to make of it. The carnitas inside was yummy, but there didn't seem to be anything else inside. Maybe that's normal for a molotes. I think I expected cheese or something. There was some crema and cojito on top but I needed more. The suadero in the burrito was delicious. Really nice flavor, tender, and perfect seasoning. The burrito comes with a side of fries which was surprising but not unwelcome. They also give you two salsas, one red and one green (very spicy!). We enjoyed our meal last night and enjoyed the left overs again today for lunch.

Been here a couple of times and both times were great.  Both times we got the sausage pizza and the second time we got the seafood salad with calamari, shrimp and scallops, it was so yumdeliocious! Also a great place to watch the drunks stumble around.

I can't believe my girlfriend and I both had lunch and drinks here (we were on vacation - don't judge) and our bill was a whopping twenty-six dollars.  A great place to sit outside and soak up the AZ sun while waiting for our flight.
There was some confusion regarding where we order.  Our waitress told us to order from her, and when I went inside to see what the pizza offerings were the guy told me to order from him, and when I did the waitress ran up and said "Tell him what you want, but I can bring it out to you."  Um, I don't care who brings me the food, as long as I eat.
Other than that however, the Pesto Pizza was great, the Margherita Pizza was really well done (and the big thick meat and vegetable sounded great - I just wasn't looking for mushrooms), and the side salad was surprisingly fresh.
A very relaxed atmosphere for a leisurely lunch downtown that I would recommend to anyone.  I wish I could remember the name of the Italian beer I tried, because I would love to look for it here at home as well.

Tonight we went to Firebirds.  I had been contemplating going for some time and never had the opportunity.  So having read many glowing reports our expectations were set for an exceptional experience.
Sadly this was not to be the case.  Our server, Rob, seemed okay at the start.  Although we asked 3 times for lemon for my husband's drink.  We were prepared for a delicious steak dining treat.  We ordered the rib eyes because so many of the reviews had sung its praises.  The steak was excessively fatty and grisly.  (My husband actually vomited due to the meat. ) His baked potato came out prepared incorrectly and was sent back.  The subsequent offering was not warm enough to melt butter.  He wouldn't let me send it back again. 
Now the finishing touch was when we paid the bill.  We gave $100.25 so as not to have a lot of change.  The waiter overlooked or ignored the 25 cents and brought us change as if it weren't there.   When I corrected him he was rude slapping down a $1 and saying, "I will eat the 17 cents. ".  At this point we modified the tip to reflect his lackluster service and rude attitude.  
Oh did I mention it wasn't busy and we felt forgotten.   I asked multiple times for a refill on my drink.  And just felt adrift.  
Spoke with the manager on the way out, but...probably won't go back.  Not worth our money.
Amazing service and grass fed meats!  As good as I've ever sampled.  Exotic bar with live music playing above or over looking bar... pretty cool to see!
Great service, great food, great ambiance! Highly recommend the rib eye! Jared was an awesome server that kept it real and had awesome recommendations. Thanks Jared!

This place has some of the best and freshest Vietnamese food I have had in Edmonton/SP area.  I often go here for the vermicelli bowls and grilled platters (wrap your own with meat of your choosing) which are delicious and extremely well priced.  They also have amazing Kim Chi and onion cakes as well as lemonade soda.  The service isn't always the best, can be slow and a bit abrupt, and they always forget our Kim Chi.  However, the food itself stands out enough that it keeps me going back, and leaving full usually for about 12$.  Check it out if you are in the park!

DD doesn't have the best donuts but this location is awful. They were out of a lot of flavors and the one I did get was hard on one side and inedible. I've had bad experiences on multiple occasions and the only reason I've been back is because it's on the way to work. I think I'll save my money and stay away from now on.

It's very rare of me to order pho from a pho restaurant because mama makes it best at home, so I went with the Bun Bo Hue aka Spicy Beef Noodle Soup. The broth was spicy, but not overpowering. I was shocked that the amount of beef was so generous. There was pig's blood which not many restaurants who offer BBH have. Our server was also very friendly.

Great brunch of Vietnamese hash with baguette and "Good Morning Philadelphia" to drink. The hash was quite a bit heavier than anticipated, but flavor very well. The pork in the hash was cooked perfectly, but the corned beef was soggy. The drink was poured heavy, but was great. Overall, a pretty good brunch for somewhere I wandered in.

If you enjoy Indian cuisine, this is gonna be fun!  Less vegetarian, and more meat dishes, this place is a nice change from the samosa and chicken tikka masala you keep ordering.

Very clean.  Friendly staff.  I have not tried Pakistani food before, and the woman who seemed to be in charge of the front of the house was easy to talk to and get recommendations from.

I settled on the Nihari Plate, which was the shank of the cow, slow cooked and simmering in a stew of spices that was outstanding, and very filling.  With fresh naan and some onion and tomato, it was a great rainy-day lunch.  

The prices seemed very reasonable for the quantity and quality of the food I was served.  

While I'm not often this far north on 309, but when I am you can bet this is a place I will head back to if I'm hungry.  If you live up this way and haven't yet tried Bobo Lahori, head on over!

Great place with a good hearted manager who actually has ethics. Ordered a 20 piece boneless wing dinner and some came out smaller than a quarter. He saw it and stepped up to fix it and even agreed that shouldn't happened for the overall cost. Glad this manager Rick  was on top of his position. I recommend if there is a problem let Rick be fair and objective. This is a place I will continue to support and enjoy because Rick works hard to make his customers happy. He even acknowledged that he believes all customers 
"should get what they pay for" Rick I appreciate you and I will return

If you're going to advertise yourself as a pre- and post- basketball game venue, maybe actually be prepared for those crowds. Went there on a Saturday. Half our party ate 45 minutes before the rest of us because the kitchen was backed up. They had too few wait staff available. Our waitress was running around like a chicken with her head cut off. We couldn't have as many drinks as we would have preferred. And, even though my food arrived long after some of the rest of our party, it was somehow cold. And the food wasn't so good. Wouldn't recommend.

Best place in New Orleans! They have everything you can ask for!!! The $10 plates comes with a lot of food!! Enough for 2 ppl to share! This was my husband and I first time and the 2 ladies up front was so nice! They treated us like family. We definitely will be back! They even ordered for us!!

We drove 40 minutes to visit what seemed to be a seafood restaurant for a Friday late lunch. The place is clean, has a nice atmosphere and attentive servers. It looks like it would be a great party bar in evening. I'm not sure they feature live music, but I was there only for the delicious looking seafood platters featured on their web site. In particular, the mahi. For a "featured" dish it was over cooked and DRY! Way too much salt on half the fish, I had to spit out a mouthful in a napkin. I tried eating from the other end and while less salt, it was DRY! What cook salts seafood? Ugh. I've eaten mahi-mahi several times and I cook seafood at home. 

I was treating my son to a special day, and taking home a doggie bag ((FOR THE REAL DOG AT HOME)) that cost $17 was a huge disappointment.

I will say the coconut shrimp appetizer was perfectly delicious. I wish I would had ended my meal there.

We love this place!

We typically like go here for breakfast or brunch, but if you go on Sunday, try to time it out before church lets out...otherwise you may have to go elsewhere.  That's the only problem we've had there; there's no actual waiting area, and on a typical Sunday, folks tend to hunker down with a newspaper or their family for a bit...

But really, how can one fault a restaurant for being busy?  And to be honest, we've really only left twice due to a long wait for a table.

Give this place a shot.  The prices are good, and the food is tasty!
One time was enough for me. Other locations might be different but this place was completely filthy. I didn't even sit down. The b urger was okay and the fries were dripping in grease.
Yay for soup dumplings! And fried soup dumplings!  Only thing about them is it doesn't come with dipping sauce that I'm used to (ginger and black vinegar).  I would ask for some ginger slices.
The rating above is an absolute lie. Its the Mako's of Rittenhouse. Except you wont get shanked here.

Today a friend and I decided to come here to enjoy a nice lunch. The food was fantastic. We both ordered the plain and simple burgers with a fry to split. The burgers were cooked perfectly to our liking and the fries were exquisite. I also ordered the cookies and cream milkshake which honestly could have a had a bit more flavor. Though, I can't complain. The food was lovely. Though, I do have to file a complaint about the uniforms that the staff are wearing. My friend and I noticed the hostess wearing the shortest and tightest skirt possible, basically mooning the clientele. Also, spaghetti straps? Come on, I don't believe that is very professional. Especially for a fox restaurant, I expect there to be more clothes on a woman's body. I can just imagine what men guests are thinking when watching this girl walk around the restaurant wearing little to nothing. Don't get me wrong, the food was lovely. Though, for first impressions, a hostess should not look like she's going to the club, since she is basically the face of the restaurant when first walking in.

The sushi isn't terrible, but there are much better options in the area. To be frank, I would pick up some sushi from Publix for $8 or $10 before going back here, I'd probably only go back if friends insisted.

I pretty much always order an eel roll and a specialty roll when I go to sushi places. The eel roll... it was pretty bad. The eel was paper thin. There was actually no eel in most of the pieces. I didn't know it was possible for eel to be so thin, so I guess that's an accomplishment? I reported it to our waiter, and showed him the pieces that physically had no eel in them and his answer was "Oh, they use two pieces of eel." The other roll I had was the tempura lobster roll, it was all right. 

Before our rolls, we had the tori yakitori which was very, very good. Tasted fresh and delicious, I would highly recommend it. I would say it is the only part of my meal I really enjoyed.

My husband had a lemon sake cooler, which he said was okay. He also had some hot sake, which he said was terrible. I am not a sake person but my husband always makes me try his, and even I could tell there was something very off about the flavor. Maybe it was stored or heated improperly, but there wast just something wrong with it.

Overall, I do not recommend this place. The service is just okay and the food is below average. Not exaggerating when I say that you should just pick up some sushi & a bottle of sake at Publix before considering Samurai Blue... or even better, head over to Zen Bistro which is nearby.

Diwan (sp?) is eminently friendly and genuinely happy to work with you on crafting the sushi he prepares.  I eat lunch there, every week, and I will always come back, because these people work fast, the food is GREAT, and they follow up often on refilling drinks.  It is a clean place, with a comfortable atmosphere and great bar space for eating and drinking.  Cheers!

TRIED to go into Another Broken Egg for breafast on a Saturday morning. The six of us arrived about 8:30 am. As we entered we noticed a line. This isn't uncommon for the locations in other cities that we have been in. We were told it would be about forty five minutes.  Ok, we will wait. So after 30 minutes and a bloody minutes we saw a customer approach the counter and she told them that they have been waiting an hour for their food.  We started looking around and nobody had any food and the people that we saw at front of line had not been seated.  We waited another 15 minutes and left.  As we were leaving other people were leaving and a group of about 8 were walking in. Somebody told them don't waste their time as they had been there an hour and the line didn't move and nobody was receiving their food.  This is unexceptable and surley brought them down in my book.  Not up to the standards we are used to in the other locations, Santa Rosa beach and Tuscaloosa,Ala. I usually post reviews when something is good...but this was bad so I had to share.

At the moment, I am working nights, this place is just around the corner from my place of work.  It's nice to be able to have a place to go and just have a relaxing sit down lunch with coworkers. As far as 24 hour restaurants go, Mel's is not all that bad!

The restaurant is decorated in a 50's style theme, down to vintage posters, mini jukeboxes at each table (songs are 25 cents each), and neon lights. It's fun. Also, the restaurant is super clean and quiet so enjoying a conversation with your dining companions is possible. 

Most  of the times I have been here, the service has been great, but sadly this can be inconsistent because we have also had 2-3 times were the service was mediocre at best. One noteworthy point is that they have never tried to rush us out when we had a longer wait between shifts to kill. 

The food is diner food, nothing special. For the most part, I've ordered grilled cheese with french fries and had their milk shakes. The grilled cheese was cooked perfectly and the fries were crisp. The ranch sauce was of good quality (not any of that watered down stuff other restaurants serve). I've also ordered the vegetable omelet with no mushrooms, it was bland. ...however the fried potato side was very tasty (overcooked, but tasty). Also, while their garlic fries are not as crispy as I prefer, their flavor is awesome. 

But as with the service the food can be inconsistent as well in regards to quality and serving size and included condiments. If they worked on this, the restaurant would most like get better reviews.

The Greek salad is really good.  You get a lot for the price.   Service was great.  The wings are really good, but kind of pricey.   Burgers and sandwiches are above average.  Beer is served ice cold.

Just got the spinach, tomato and feta croissant and it was sooooooooo good. I sent my boyfriend in so of course he didn't ask for it warmed but it was still amazing room temperature. I also got the vanilla iced oatmilk latte which was perfect. I definitely will be back!
Not bad. Not truly thick enough for Chicago-style pizza in my opinion, but I like the taste of the tomato sauce. Pepperoni was good. Interesting that they give the choice of sauce or cheese on top.

I guess this is as good as it gets around here. I ordered my 3 rolls ahead of time for pick up.  Lady told me 20mins, got there in 30 minutes and to wait another 20mins... smh.. the sushi was smashed into the to-go container and was not very appealing but I was hungry.  Everything was 50% off so I guess I can't complain. Make sure to order from the discounted menu.
Terrific find, off the beaten path in NOLA. Great seafood and Italian specialties.  The mussels appetizer was fabulous!

The District Tap is amazing for literally any group size or event. I have been here just meeting a friend for drinks and with a larger group. The staff is amazing and our favorite bartender Frank, she is amazing and always comes up with delicious shots for us! Ask for her!

Service was painfully slow. The cold outside wait didn't help either . Food presentation wasn't a good quality in this establishment but the taste of the food was delicious  Even tho the red beans and rice wasn't what I was expecting by far , it still had a great taste

Hands down the best service I have EVER had! Josh, our server, was absolutely outstanding! Despite his packed s cation he was quick, efficient, friendly and offered amazing suggestions. As a former server for 8 years, I can be quite critical, but he blew me away!

The ambience of this restaurant is fantastic. Out-of-towners will love the tropical feel And locals will love the prices and the ease of sitting.

We sat out side and listened to the live music. For an appetizer we had the tuna nachos topped with jalapeños. They were a little sweet and little spicy. Our dinners also came complete with a salad and Caribbean cornbread. All the food here, is made fresh and in-house which I love. The only downside to our dining experience, wasthat we were so full from the salad, bread, appetizer, that we had to take her food home!

My hubby and I were looking for something quick to eat yesterday and remembered this nice little gem in Collegeville literally down the street from her Ursinus College,  there's parking in the back, just remember to turn right at the traffic light.  

The food here is good quality food I see the complaints about it being over priced I disagree if you want good food you pay for it nowadays people want so much for nothing and it's ridiculous. This is a small local business I always support small and local business owners.

Our meal was excellent I had the American Kobe slider cheeseburgers three of them perfectly done on a great soft roll my husband had a chicken parm sandwich and we had onion rings for appetizers so I can excellent simple meal well done and the service was excellent very nice sweet people. They also  have excellent entrees we just wanted to have a simple meal yesterday.  So give it a try they are well worth it
Horrible place !  This was not worth my drive, time or gas. Very, very limited menu.  Yuck
Like you I read the reviews and I figured I would try it out, needless to say some of the best fried chicken and pork chops I have ever had!!

My wife and I came  hear on a recent trip to Reno Nevada. We were looking for a little bit of a change in food selection based on the fact we were here for the rib cook off. We left this place feeling like wow what a great hidden gem in South Reno. From start to finish everything about this restaurant was exceptional.  It is a mix of Chinese and Sushi which would help satisfy anyone's appetite. Tonight we were in the mood for some Chinese so we decided upon the honey walnut shrimp and kung pao chicken with pots stickers to start. 

After a pretty short wait we received our food and by the smells of it this was going to be great. For one the chicken is real pieces of meaty chicken. Which is rare and the flavors mixed the right amount of spice. The prawns as well were so good and no skimping either this plate was chucked full of prawns and not shorted by unnecessary plate garnishes.  Then I guess you could call it desert were the pot stickers which we asked to all come out together.  Wow these stuffed little (I only say little but these were big) delites were amazing as well. So packed full of pork and pan fried just the right amount.  But one of our favorite things was a drink the bartender made taste sort of like a scaled down version of a pina colada and man was this good, but be careful can't have too many of these based on the fact the main ingredient is Bacardi 151. 

Bottom line Reno is filled with great hidden spots and we truly stumbled on another great one. Thanks local and non local Yelpers for guiding us to this great spot.
Outstanding food.  Outstanding service.  Delicious and priced well.  Bloody Mary was fantastic.
Stopped in for lunch and got P A N C A K E S!  Now all I want for lunch is breakfast...I love this newfound place.

I'm so happy to live so close to Chinatown. 
I have been to most of the good spots because my favorite foods are here.
 Considering the subpar atmosphere and okay service I give it a 4 for consistently having great food.
The noodles were mmmm and broth is nice but, I usually add spice and hoison.  The roast duck has that five spice sweetness, the oxtail is really tender and tasty. And those dang scallion pancakes gahh... and the sauce.   I've tried to make these at home but, whats the trick to the flawless flakery with the layered fluffy flakiness. 

You make it look so easy. Thank you for being pretty well priced too, it is appreciated.

I really wanted to love it here. The space is beautiful and the atmosphere is lovely. However, the service is absolutely terrible, comparable to a roadside diner. The server didn't introduce himself, talk about the menu or ask if we had any questions. He just walked up and asked, "you ready to order?". Then it took 30 minutes for him to bring waters for the table and he had us pass plates and silverware around like we were at a mediocre chain restaurant. 

The food is unremarkable and the portions are very small for the price and level of service. It takes 30 minutes to get a glass of wine even when the bar is less than half full.

Always enjoy the mudslides there. The best I've ever had. Visited there a few times over the past week I spent at the beach. Did not eat there in the past but food was average.  I always enjoy the atmosphere with live bands, plenty of seating, friendly staff. Will keep going back.

Went through the drive thru which I have learned is a big mistake when going to Eegee's. I went to this location because the location closer to my home often messes up my order and I don't find out about it until I am at home...I was hoping for the best at this location but once again was disappointed with Eegee's. I had to wait almost 15 minutes to get fries, which when I ate one 5 minutes later noticed that they were cold, and then when I opened my monsoon dog I noticed it didn't have BACON on it ....the main ingredient after the hot dog itself....sorry Eegee's but you have struck out...I will not go back.

My husband loves bbq, and we've tried most of Philly's joints with satisfactory results - but then I saw Sweet Lucy's listing and devised a plan to try them out. We don't own a car, but we had to rent one for a weekend and on our way back I directed him to stop by Sweet Lucy's to pick up a much-deserved bbq dinner. 

We got a lot of food - by my standards, at least, but probably not that much for bbq. Full rack of ribs (duh), pulled pork, hickory smoked wings, spicy collard greens, garlic mashed potatoes, braised cabbage, and cornbread. WOW. Do they know how to do bbq!! Ribs were so tender that meat truly was falling off of the bone, wings were still juicy, and the pulled pork was perfect and not overly dressed. Of the sides, the greens were definitely our favorite, but all of them were delicious. My husband loved the cornbread, which was cake-y, slightly sweet, and moist. I picked up their apple crumb pie, personal-sized, which tasted just like mom made it. My husband is so obsessed with their bbq now, he's made me promise that the next time we have to go away for the weekend, we stop by Sweet Lucy's on our way back. We still need to take his parents there - his dad loves bbq more than any other food. Sweet Lucy's will make him an addict instantly!

I got the 12oz Filet Mignon with the twice baked potato. It was super good, probably the best steak I ever had. I'm not in Santa Barbara a lot but if I am I will definitely be coming back if I want a steak.

If you're looking for the best skillet in town, with the best bartenders in Boise, come to Addie's!  This neighborhood gem is located right off boise ave and has so much to offer.  The entire crew that works here treats you like family.  The bottomless mimosas and bloody Mary's are unrivaled.
Very good service and food was very good as well. Not a formal restaurant but still very nice

I went to this place today and it reminds me alot of a place called Hulas in the town I went to college in. The food was the best of any Mongolian BBQ place since I was in college. However, two reasons why I give it only three stars: one the price is too high; and the portions are too small which I found to be quite disappointing. With an appetizer, the bill was higher than I would have got at a Fridays or Applebees and I would have had more food at those places. 

This place needs to work on the portion sizes!

Awesome! Right across the street from me, too! Their baked goods are fresh and made on sight everyday.  I'm usually up late and I see them getting there at 4am!! Staff is super nice and friendly. The coconut macaroons are big and just, omg, heaven!! I also enjoy the pumpkin pastry!  The steak torta was tasty as well! The prices are decent. Overall, a great place! 


It's May 27th and I'm chowing down on a Carne Aseda Torta with everything and a giant coconut macaroon! I'm in food heaven heaven! Absolutely LOVE this place! Again, great staff,  surprisingly low prices l, and the baked goods....just YUM! Definitely  one of Sparks hidden gems!! 
Support Local Businesses!
Great spot for breakfast lunch and dinner or just a drink with friends. I have experienced all meals and have always left happy.

Had the flame grilled chicken sandwich and it was probably the best chicken sandwich I've ever had.  You can get a chicken sandwich basically anywhere these days, but this was top of the list in flavor. Comes with homemade French fries.

So disappointed. Nice menu, outside dining, delightful and attentive waiter, but the food was inedible.  Had always wanted to try grilled romaine, so ordered that salad.  Gritty dirt in the romaine.  inedible.  "sauce" and "bacon" almost not there.  2 skinny pieces of avocado.  Expensive.  Friend had the butternut squash soup with apple.  Said the apple was good, but soup was ... odd.  Finally, the weakest coffee I've ever had.  Ordered expresso.  Don't bother.  Total washout for $45++
That said, the waiter was good.

The food is really good. I tried the calamari app, bruschetta, and meatballs. All were great. The dinner special was a steak topped with scallops and shrimp with melted cheese. It was perfect. I'd definitely recommend this restaurant.

Don't expect an upscale trendy dining room at Chef D's. Here they serve up home style hearty breakfast with Mexican options. The restaurant is located in an aging strip mall. They attract a wonderfully diverse clientele and do a robust carry out business.  I can see why...the prices are fantastic and the food is delicious. 

This was our first visit. I opted for the breakfast burrito which was larger and stuffed with scrambled eggs, sausage, cheese and hash brown potatoes. The burrito was served with side salad typical of what you would find in a Mexican restaurant and a small cup of green salsa. My meal was only $4.99 and I was full after eating only half of the huge burrito which was tasty and hot. 

My husband opted for the $4.99 eggs, meat choice, toast and hash browns traditional breakfast. His over easy eggs were cooked to perfection. The crispy bacon was generously served. He loved the hash browns. 

They offer a kids menu as well. 

Our service was good. She checked on us a couple times and refilled my husbands coffee cup.

Awesome !!! Her food , her personality 
And such a great service !!
Thank you . You Rock!!
Everyday Special! - Corn, shrimp, potato, sausage in the most amazing garlic sauce I have ever had!

Good atmosphere- boring food. Just the general compliant of the table was not enough seasoning. While I appreciate fresh, well-cooked food, there wasn't much flavor. Vegetables (squash) were bland and if it weren't for the capers on my fish, there was almost no other flavor. The dishes need a kick! Especially for the prices. Not sure id go back, especially with all the other seafood places in the area. Also, they ran out of the "all you can eat" sourdough, and that was a disappointment.
Love the lemon grass chicken, and the pho soups are very good. They have other Chinese food there that is very yummy I just get stuck on the soups.
Awesome pizza and bread sticks!  Carry out is very quick!  This place has been a staple in Indy for decades!

Ribs are something that I love, but simply to not get as often as I would like. However when I do, I tend to gravitate towards Andre's Ribs!

For my visit I ordered the ribs, which are served Julie's style. Apparently Julie's style is a dry rub perfected by Julie and Andre. Kudos to Julie, she is a miracle worker. Seriously these were the most amazing ribs I have ever had, just enough dry rub to not be overpowering, a solid smoky flavor and so tender that no knife is needed to cut these delicious ribs, they simply fall off the bone. The only problem I had was that they were all gone I mean I was full but I craved more, which left me licking my fingers clean. I also ordered some baked beans and a side of mac & cheese, both were amazing and homemade. In fact during my conversation with the owner, I learned that everything down to the sauce was homemade, however don't expect them to smother your ribs with sauce, that's not the way Julie intended so they will provide you with the sauce to apply yourself. I will say that Julie's style needs no additional flavor, so the use of the sauce was limited in my case. 

On additional visits I have tried a number of items, my favorites are the Ribs and Beef Brisket, which is so full of moist and full of flavor you will forget that those other bbq joints around town even serve brisket! Yes, it's just that good! Try it and you will be hooked. 

The staff here is super friendly and passionate about bbq, and it shows! Prices are reasonable, seating inside is limited so there is a heavy focus on carry out. I used to think that Pappy's had the best ribs in town, however I think the torch has been passed on to Andre's when it comes to the ribs. If you are looking for some delicious food at reasonable prices I highly recommend Andre's Ribs.
Love this place friendly staff and owners and great selection of spices and other great middle eastern need for their cocking!!!

I recently found out that I am gluten intolerant. And was recommended to try Red Robin's. They can literally make anything gluten free! With a separate kitchen area for the food to be cooked in! I was ecstatic. Needless to say I will be here often! The Brandon location is killing it!

Monsoon chocolate has some of the most delicious bonbons I have ever tasted!

They use delicious chocolate, local and natural ingredients, and they sell out quick! If you plan to sit and drink coffee while you enjoy your chocolates and read a book, this is a great place to do that. They also have options for you to purchase items like their take on a Choco taco. They also sell some specialty drinks using their chocolate. They also sell basic common coffee items.

If you don't live in Tucson, they have a website where you can order boxes of chocolates, as well as some of their merch.


They usually have some staple bonbons, but they also will rotate some specialty types. The decorations on top of the chocolates are amazing and so artistic! They look like little gems and jewels!
Had the elvis, peanut butter, banana and bacon panini. The bread was burnt, completely ruining the sandwich. I will return as the menu had plenty to offer for cheap.
Definitely worth a visit. Beer was good, affordable, and a nice selection. The service was very friendly. Seemed like a neat little neighborhood bar.

Love it! Their bread is my new favorite. I'll go weekly just to pick up a loaf of bread. The cookies (butter) are also to die for. The only reason I give it four is because it can be hard to find a seat because of the communal seating. It can also be loud. There are many students working, which is fine except that they take up a good part of the table with little turn over. Everyone is really sweet here; especially the coffee makers. I do love their unique coffee and brunch set up.

Great food!
Great people!
Great drinks!
Great vibe!
Shrimp, shrimp, shrimp. 
This is a must do.

I have been to Jade Garden twice, both for dinner.  The first time was a limited menu.  I had the chicken lettuce wraps as my entree as I was eating lite.  My husband had the mongolian beef.  Both were well prepared.  The owner came by to check on our meal.  The service was even a bit over officious...the bus boy came by to fill up the water glass numerous times even if I took a sip.

The second time was this week and the full menu is now available.  We had the Char Siu Quesadillas as an appetizer.  That was an awesome choice!  Very different and great flavor.  The salsa was a jicama base and went well.  We had the Hunan Beef as an entree.  It was as spicy as I like it, but we asked for some chili sauce to spice it up and got chili oil as well.   The owner again came by to chat....I had a nice gtass of Ravenswood Zinfandel.  Very reasonable at $6.00 a glass.

We live nearby and will return to try some items.  The atmosphere is nice and the patio is also open, which I love during summer!

OMG its the worst meal I have had in a while. I feel really gross having just had dinner there.  Where to begin...My chicken entre was smothered in a gross white thick sauce with mashed potatoes all over and the brocoli underneath so that I could not eat the brocoli because it was smashed. The chicken was disgusting.  I'm giving it t the racoon.  The brussels without the caramel were ok and the beet salad was beets and cheese..very few greens. The fried chicken sandwich was also bad and my dad's pork chop was too tough to chew. 
The servers were incredible but to spend 30 dollars on a lousy pork chop is just wrong.  I will never eat there again. Really bad food.  Super friendly staff !

Everything here was delicious. Started with a Caprese Salad and their homemade mozzarella and vinaigrette dressing. They have a $10 13" pizza special on Thursdays, so we had a chicken and mushroom pie with great garlic and spices. They also tout their cannoli bar, so we indulged and got a chocolate chip cannoli... Also delicious. They're currently in a "soft opening" phase, so their sign isn't done and some fixtures have to be placed. But a great meal and not too expensive!

Listen to me right now. If you bumped into Guy Fieri, and he said " WHO WANTS TO GO TO FLAVOR-TOWN" and he didnt take you to the funky taco. You would have every right to slap him upside his frosted-tipped melon.

Walk in order the Korean pastor, tell your peers how good the taco is approximately 3 times for each taco. Reevaluate literally every aspect of your life. Pay the people. And run home, leave the car wherever it is. Just run.

I tried ordering a Chicken Cheese Steak w/ sauce and  was told that's a "chicken parm".  At any other reputable hoagie/cheesesteak place in Philly, these are two different things!  That's a red flag!  At the counter they always mention that their mom makes the potato/macaroni salad, which is a great upsell on their part, but it's not good.  Unfortunately there's not a better alternative I've found in Old City forcing me to go outside old city for hoagies and cheesesteaks. I imagine this place survives on foot traffic like many of it's neighbors.

Traveling by myself in Tampa from Chicago.  Stopped in for a dinner at Il Ritorno.

Everyone in the joint was dressed nice and I was dressed pretty low-key in jeans and a hoodie... I was expecting to be turned away or at least catch some attitude.  They were lovely.  Lovely.

I had the Bucatini Pomodoro, Brussels sprouts, and a big glass of Pinot.  Everything tasted fantastic!

The bill came out to just under $50 which was totally reasonable for the really high quality meal and drinks.

I can't wait for my next trip back!

i'm a little surprised i haven't reviewed this place yet. over the past 2.5 years, i've come here (and dreamed of coming here) numerous times for their brunch. sabrina's sits right at the top of my yummy but accessible list of philly brunch places. 

the wait is LONG. but i love that sabrina's allows you to call ahead and put your name on the list. sure cuts down on the amount of time you have to stand around waiting in the cold.

french toast has been and always will be my go-to brunch item of choice. and nobody makes it like sabrina's. their challah french toast is fluffy and warm; their stuffed challah french toast is about 5x better, but almost 100x sweeter, which can wear on your sweet tooth about half-way through.

over the years, i've also tried their other breakfast items, ranging from the standard egg and toast breakfast to the omelets to the eggs benedict (and other monthly brunch specials). the quality and yum factor varies, but any breakfast/brunch item here is generally a solid choice at the very least.

but here's the kicker. this past weekend, i discovered something new: their huevos rancheros. if anyone can make me love mexican food, they deserve 5 stars. 'nuff said.

We went to Glass Monkey with a group of 10 for a friend's birthday. Overall the experience was very pleasant. The waiter did well with a large group and everyone seemed satisfied with their food and drinks. I will say our party may have been out of place in what I would consider a quiet (even romantic) dinner restaurant. 

If you order from the small plates menu I would suggest at least 2-3 different dishes (or you'll have plenty of room for dessert). 
Menu Highlights: Green Beans, Pappardelle, Bangers and Mash
Menu Lowlights: Broccoli, Caesar Salad (difficult to eat and romaine was very charred) 
(There were also daily specials that were a hit around the table)

Glass Monkey has an extensive bottled beer selection (local craft and imported) and a few goodies on tap as well. Their wine list is also quite impressive featuring a few of my favourites.

I see this restaurant is listed as a $$ price range. I would suggest a full meal with drinks would be more in the $$$ range.

I went to Supper for the first time two nights ago, and really enjoyed myself. 

We started with a couple bottles of wine, which was nice. I then had the Supper Burger. It was $19, which is expensive for a burger, but it was HUGE (10 ounces)! It came with three types of sauces: chipotle aioli, mustard, and thousand island. I kept rotating between the three sauces because they were all good, but the thousand island was my favorite. The burger was really succulent, and all of the toppings on it (caramelized onions, ham, cooked tomato) were awesome. It was a bit of a challenge to eat because it was so big. The duck fat fries that came with it were also amazing. 

The restaurant itself was really nice. It was small, but we were not cramped at all. I was there with a bunch of friends for a birthday, but Supper would also be a great spot for a date.

I just ordered the rib platter to go. Only after paying did I find out they don't have plastic forks and knives to go. How do they expect you to eat a take out meal. What a waste of 25 dollars. The vegetables were good but the ribs were tasteless. They could have used some salt, but oh yea, they don't give you that either. This was the first and last time I will order food from this place. Don't waste your money or time. Just terrible.

Used to love going here on a Friday night and sitting in bar area listening to music. Usually have to get there early but even that doesn't matter anymore bc bar and table reserved . We've been told a number of times bar area is first come. My daughter met some friends a few months ago and it was a full band. They couldn't even talk to each other. Unfortunately, Sacred Peoper is going from nice dining to a club. ‍ Don't know if we'll be back.

Nice neighborhood coffee place. Staff is VERY friendly. Good drinks. Nice decor. Definitely an asset to the area.

The main thing I think these guys could improve on is seating. Nice big tables, but if you go at a busy time, you'll be next to either big groups chatting loudly or people camping out with their laptops.

Overall, a great experience.

WOW what can I say but WOW !
Been here in Reno for a couple of days but visit often.
I'm not a big fan of their food but tried it out today since it was in GSR.
Superb customer service - unlike some dry by servers we've experienced over the last few months coming to Reno at many other establishments.
Tina provided services as if it was fine dining ! Other staff members were gooacknowledged us as we walked in.
Thanked Mgr Robert for taking his time to come and speak with us about our experience with their good food and service !

My favvvvvvorite. 

I'm basically obsessed with their chicken kabob sandwiches (get it with everything and spicy for the full experience), but really everything i've ever had from their grill is delicious and wonderful. I don't think I've ever had anything from here that I didn't like.

They're also a pretty sizable market that has a pretty extensive selection of items (my boyfriend & I often find random things here we are missing when we're cooking dinner) that are both your run of the mill sort of junk food & soda stuff but also a ton of healthy stuff. They're also the only place in the area I can find a stocked cold case of a variety of Vintage seltzer waters. 

We're too close to Liberty Choice to get delivery, but they will deliver - not just food from the grill but anything you need from the store. Staff are super duper friendly and will smile and make conversation with you while you wait or get rung up. 

Open til midnight on weeknights which is really nice when you're getting back from somewhere late and want a quick bite (though they do tend to close their kitchen before the advertised time so I'd get orders in before 11:30pm).

We went here for lunch, hubby ordered a crown and coke, I ordered a glass of Chardonnay (mirassou or something like that) I saw them opening a bottle of Barefoot. They didn't have the one I ordered and they weren't going to tell me.  By this time hubby was done with his drink, so we decided to leave as then menu sucked.  We paid for the one drink, $9. and change, paid with a $50 dollar bill, we were given back 2 $20 dollar bills and the coins.  Any server with common sense would break down the bills so you can leave a tip.  They weren't surprised when we left, probably happens a lot. I'd stay clear of this place.  The gourmet sandwich shop is very good just up the street.

So we were in Lakeland fla and wanted to see our friends in st Pete and they recommended this place ... being food snobs we were seriously impressed with the freshness and down home tastes of the place I had the steak my wife the chuletada can can ... the pics don't do the res tastes justice

Stopped in for a drink at the new location tonight to see what's up. Had to sample the chicken nachos and they were awesome, loaded with chicken and the pico was fresh and so tasty! Prompt, friendly, attentive service from the moment we walked in the front door. We'll be back soon for a full meal for sure.

I heard all about the gas station operated sandwich shop, and so I decided to give it a shot. My experience really proved to me that people will love some place if it just gives them a lot of food, no matter how mediocre the quality is. Really, it's all the same ingredients as a Port of Subs, except they give you and charge you twice as much. I think the only thing I like is the foccacia bread and the ability to buy my cigarettes, 40 oz and sunflower seeds all at the same time.
Great service and food.  Got a few sushi rolls and take out Moo Shoo pork for dinner at work.   Food was very good and sushi was made well.

To be honest I haven't taste the food yet. Got it to go buuuuuuuuut this review is on service. Wanted to take a moment and say just how great a server Trina is. It's Monday night.... Approx 1:15a and she's amazing. Warm, charming, attentive... She sent us on our way with smile on our face!!

Oh, Han Dynasty, you broke my heart...

I'd been wanting to try Han Dynasty for years, but never seemed to get around to it, so my hubby and I booked a reservation and headed down to Olde City.  We arrived and waited... and waited.... and waited.  We waited for 45 minutes, which wouldn't be a huge deal if we hadn't made a reservation.  The hostess was completely inept and would walk away from the podium for long periods of time, during which we saw several other potential customers leave out of frustration.  When we finally sat down, the manager apologized for the wait and offered to get us each a drink on the house (very nice).  However, when he came back, he threw two beers (the cheapest kind they serve, I should note) down on the table and ran off.  Since I don't drink beer, I tried to flag him down and when I finally got his attention, ordered a glass of wine.  He short-poured the wine (poor form, Han Dynasty, poor form--why offer a free drink, if you're not willing to oblige?) 

Anyways, though we were annoyed, we wanted to give the food a fair shot since we'd been hearing raves for so long.  The Dan-Dan noodles are very good--a solidly 4 star dish with some kick.  We were severely disappointed by our entrees though.  The dry pot beef was incredibly average and the crispy rice chicken was inedible because it was so sweet (and just plain bad).  Han, I had such high expectations for us, but it's clear that we just weren't meant to be.

My wife and I have dined in and ordered takeout from El Sitio many times throughout the past few years. The food is consistently good and the owners are very nice. There aren't many authentic South American restaurants in the area and they bring something refreshing and different to Collingswood. The appetizer sampler is delicious and we really like the chicken stews. Steaks and ceviches are great as well! And the imported herbal tea is unlike anything we've had elsewhere. The small patio is also an awesome place to enjoy a glass of wine and dine al fresco. 

We love it when they sell empanadas at the events in town and would love to see the empanada "cart" outside more frequently. As an suggestion to management... there aren't many places to grab a quick to go bite in Collingswood when the weather is nice. It would be awesome to have El Sitio's empanadas fill that need!

Staying at the hotel next door so we thought we'd give it a go. I ordered the teriyaki chicken with light sauce. It arrived smothered in sauce and the side of carrots were cold. The chicken was SO incredibly salty I had to ask them for another piece and requested just plain. When I got it back I received the same piece of chicken (I know cause my bite mark was still there) plain but COVERED in seasoned salt! Also the carrots were reheated in the microwave because they were now hot but squishy. My sister ordered the liver and onions. She didn't enjoy dinner because there was more gristle than meat. (And as I'm writing this my sister is starting to feel queasy)  The only positive point to the meal was they had warm rolls that were actually quite good. My suggestion is dine at your own risk!!

Excellent place!  This is a must for a date night with the spouse or significant other. From the very start the experience was great. Very friendly crew and we were seated promptly. We did have a reservation due to Valentines Day. They already had a 4 course meal planned for us. You did have choices for the first course and third course. All 4 courses were delicious!  Both my wife and I had the seafood scampi for our main course and it was one of the best dishes I have ever had. Our waitress made an excellent recommendation on wine although on the expensive side. It was well worth it!  Overall the experience was fantastic and would recommend it to anyone. We can't wait to go back to try the other dishes on a non holiday.

Great place for a quick simple tasty meal. My husband was hungry after his flight and it was around midnight. We didn't want to go into a bar or restaurant and found this place. He got the shrimp n grits and they were so good. Staff is friendly and she told us how the chef likes to experiment. He came up with a new dessert and I told her to name it the Sweet Boy- just putting that out into the universe Incase it becomes a hot trendy thing lol.

Terrible experience. This goes as a first for the many times I've been to in n out. They only had a few people in the restaurant and a couple people in the drive thru. They took over 20 minutes to see me at the window, then said they never input my order, then asked me to pay and took another 15 minutes. Terrible management, poor training. The employees didn't appear to know what they were doing. They offered me a free shake, but all I really wanted was my food and maybe a store credit. Bad job.

Took my family, all over 21, to this delightful restaurant in Hyde Park.
Started with glasses of bubbly and wines. Offered to let me taste samples of the regional whites I was interested in. We ended up with a Moscato which was delicious, a Malbec, a French champagne and a fine Yamhill Pinot grigio.
Shared warm tasty bread and brussel sprouts with cashew creme and pork belly, salads and an amazing potato gorgonzola soup with sunchoke chips.
Entrees were all interesting and well prepared:
Waygu beef, steelhead, and pork osso buco...with well thought out sides and sauces.
Shared three flavors of sorbet for dessert. Yum.
Our server was wonderful. She was informed and helpful. 
Will definitely come back. 
Aside: I can't eat dairy, gluten or eggs and they accommodated my needs with no problem. Of course, I couldn't eat everything is on the menu, but there was plenty I could. I didn't eat the soup.

The reading terminal is a must go to in Philadelphia.  The food at the little booths are always fun and adventurous.  If you can get a seat at the diner inside you are lucky but you must try.  A good place to grocery shop of you live I. The city near buy all the food is very fresh.  The bakery items are specially good a must have it the Pa. Dutch stand which only opens on certain days.

Pizza is fairly tasty when eaten immediately out of the oven.  But terrible acid reflux later.  Seeing the cheese become so firm in room temperature after just a short period of time leads me to believe it's very cheap.  The fact that it takes them so long to cook their thin pizzas leads me to believe all of their ingredients are junk.

Service is horrible.  Ridiculous waits both to place an order and then to receive food after ordering.  During my final visit, staff waited on tables without any consideration for who arrived before whom; and they ignored waiting customers (chiefly me!) to chit chat with other, apparently favored customers.  And again--why does it take sooooo long for them to cook their thin-crust pies?  Garbage.

As an African woman, I was really looking forward to it.  I was not disappointed.  The plantain starter was delish ... the egozi soup/stew with fufu ---- I was transported back to my childhood.  The fufu was soft, almost creamy tasting and not heavy (fufu is not the easiest thing to make properly).  I consumed almost the entire plate of it.  Mmmmm.  One of the best fufu I have ever had.  The spinach was also exquisite.  Good experience.
Lovely ambience, great selection of beers and cocktails. I was honestly surprised at how great the food was as well! Can't wait to return.

I knew of the name La Carreta from their place on the north shore. Now that they opened a new location next to my house I was excited to finally try them. I got the lunch special Burrito Supreme and a side of salsa. It was delicious. All the ingredients were fresh, the Spanish rice was delicious, and their homemade salsa is to die for. Everything I got was just the way I love it. Can't wait to go back and try some more of their exceptional food.

I ate dinner at the Lucky Dill yesterday night. I ordered the Waldorf chicken salad sandwich but when the order came out it was actually just plain chicken salad. The meat was dry and tough and the dressing holding the salad together was absolutely flavorless. The best tasting food on my plate was the pickle and cole slaw. When placing my order I asked if I could have the sweet potato fries as a side and they said yes but it would cost an additional $1.50. I asked if they were frozen and out of a bag not surprisingly the answer was yes. I decided to pass on that great upgrade. 

When the server asked how everything was I told her exactly what I wrote here and she called the manager over. He was very polite, removed the food from the bill and offered to get me another dish. Unfortunately I was working the night shift so I did not have time to wait for another meal. 

Overall the food was not impressive. I think they cater to an older audience that can't taste much so bland food is ok. Also the menu is gigantic. This may be part of the problem. No restaurant can make that many different dishes and have them all taste decent. 

I wouldn't waste the trip getting this spot.

This past Saturday I had my bday party. Service was awsome! Ordered the seafood dip and the food was great. Drinks were good for house well drinks. Best part of the night was kareoke! I have never seen such a hugh selection of songs. Fun time for all! Will be back soon

Just home from Buffalo Wild Wings. Went to watch the Colts Play off game. Expected it to busy and it was. 
The service was worse than I have ever experienced in my life. We sat for 45 minutes before anyone came by and we were seated at the kitchen door. I have always been partial to independent restaurants where the owner/managers had a stake in customer satisfaction. This visit reinforced my opinion. 

I have never seen wait staff that seemed to be annoyed that customers came in. Plenty of tips to be made. 

Some type of Manager ask about who was covering our table and we pointed to the guy she just past. She had just asked him if we were his table and he said no. 

She replaced him with another guy who was just as bad. Another 45 minutes to pay our bill. 

Horrible service model for the restaurant side as it is, standing in line to place your order... ridiculous . Wait staff on bar side. 

One good thing my wife will not want to go there again. 

The wings were good.
I was pleasantly surprised by Deke's BBQ.  With outdoor seating, its a great place to eat on a really nice day.  We got the buffet which they have daily for around $12.  A good deal

Cozy place with very friendly cashier and casual service (they drop your food at the table but that's it).  It's pretty small but we lucked out with a table right before the rush.  They mostly have salads, soups, and sandwiches; they offered quiche, spinach artichoke dip, and hummus as specials when we went.  Being able to sample the soup was really helpful. We loved the tomato bisque!  The turkey pesto on jalapeno cheddar bread was really boring.  I think it needs a stronger cheddar/jalapeno flavor in the bread (I couldn't taste it until I tried the bread by itself, and even then not much), and definitely a stronger pesto.  The whole thing was bland.  We were pleased to receive a tiny side salad, which was delicious! Also complimentary was a tiny oatmeal chocolate chip cookie, just the right size...and delicious!  We would like to return to try more of their soups!
The best customer service I've ever had at hot pot. Food was really good too, definitely will be back

The sandwiches and the salad I've had at Mugshots have been pretty decent. But of course, being a coffeehouse you probably want to know about the coffee and the atmosphere.   The coffee is pretty good, although it does seem to take some time to get your drink.  The atmosphere is fairly relaxed with a good mix of students, families, and the odd character or two. The prices for both coffee and food are fairly reasonable and they take debit/credit cards.

They have excellent free wireless internet.  And they have some wired ports(Ethernet). What is really annoying is that they have a limited number of outlets, so if you want to hang around you've got to find a spot that isn't taken. 

My only other gripe is that the staff seems to delight in cranking what ever music their whimsy desires.  So while I like punk music and metal, I'm not really fond of it while I"m trying to enjoy coffee and do some studying/reading.

It's located inside what looks like a little convenient store, so you definitely can't just sit around and hangout...regardless, the food is so good! 

I love Chicken Fried Steak but I think I found my favorite spot for it. The meat is thick, gravy full of flavor and after your first bite, you can't imagine having this anywhere else!

Muffuletta. Wow! I love the olive spread on this sandwhich!  

I don't like stuffing...but I will eat their Turkey and stuffing every week, if I lived there. They know how to do their stuffing. I can't explain it but the it's full of flavor and made perfectly with the Turkey!!
Forgot half my order but didn't forget to take all my money total inconvenience for my kids . But good food so 2 stars

Great local place.  Very fresh and best as far as Take and Bake goes.  I always get the house special Pepperoni, sausage, black olives, mushrooms, onions & substitute Artichoke hearts for the bell peppers.  Great stuffed pizza will feed a small army!  Super cool people too, love supporting local businesses.  Been going here for 20 years!

This was my second time at Tiffin very much enjoy the selection of food and desserts. Absolutely love their butter chicken. I definitely recommend this place for people who are wanting to try  Indian food or the Indian food connoisseurs out there. a good place to stop in for a beer and some great eats.

Chengdu Famous Foods is one of my favorite Chinese restaurants in Philly, and is definitely my favorite in University City. Everything I have ordered here has been so delicious and authentic, and I am never disappointed when I come here and order something different.

The Dan Dan Noodles is the best one I've had. It was the perfect combination of sweet and savory. The Pork Belly also blew me away, and I just couldn't have enough of it.

One of the best parts of coming here is that the menu is so diverse that I don't think I'll ever be able to try everything, and anything I do try, I know will be amazing. I definitely recommend coming here if you are craving flavorful Sichuan food. 

Side note: bring cash for a 5% discount!

Great authentic Mexican place. In an ocean of pizza places and fast food, this is a welcome island of tasty options. I've had the tacos and burritos Al Pastor (delicious) and the huaraches bordados (also delicious). For purists, there are some authentic Mexican entrees, as well as choices of head meat for tacos, quesadillas, etc. 

Service is good for lunch so far, and recommend calling ahead for takeout (obviously.  Do you even have to recommend that anymore?).

Fun patio and even better drinks! I came here for cocktails on a bachelorette party. It was the perfect place for afternoon cocktails. The patio is huge and has games if you want to have some fun.

We got drinks at the bar until they good set up a table for us outside. There are so many options for frozen drinks, cocktails, beers and anything else you can imagine.  The frose and hibiscus mule were top hits of the party. 

The waitress was very accommodating with splitting checks for our large party which always saves a ton of hassle so kudos to them.

If you are looking for an autenthic Philly Cheese steak experience look no further than Tony Luke's. Very tasty sandwiches with good quick service. Not too far away, only about 10 minutes from Downtown and the historic part of Philadelphia.
Great experience.  Service was great and food was excellent. I had the Karaage, and Miso Ramen (add the house made bacon). Both were tremendous.  Can't wait to go back.

Great Place with an amazing staff , Sawy, Mary Beth,and John are quite a team. The food was excellent except for one soup which was too salty to be consumed. This should have never left the kitchen. That is the only reason I did not give them 5 stars.
Dr. T

Yum, yum!!!  Either pay by the pound or get the buffet.  My preference is the "pay by the pound" as the cost means you'd have to eat 2.5 lbs to break even.  Who can eat that much or should???  Also when buying by the pound, you go to the meat counter and order what you want, when you want it.  I love the top sirloin, very rare and I'm not disappointed!  On weekends  the black beans come with sausage or organ meat laced in and over the rice is SUPER delicious!

It's a casual BYOB with friendly staff.  In fact, they know me by now as I eat there at least 1x\week, sometimes 2x.  And dessert - awesome selection easy to view and pick from in a special refrigerated case right there at the edge of the dining area.

And if you like soccer, the large TV's at either end of the restaurant will keep you occupied.

Family friendly and a separate room for overflow or large parties.  ENJOY!!!

I wanted to love this place since it got such great reviews from Sauce Magazine. However, when we walked in for lunch the music was literally blaring "Tongue Tied" by Grouplove. I love that song but it's not suitable for the crowd of patrons which were mostly in their 50's and older and it wasn't suitable to be that loud. By loud I mean we couldn't talk at the table. I was with my mother and aunt so I asked them to turn it down. They clearly were disappeared.

Then there was the menu, which had dirty spots of food dried on it. That was followed by the salad which had caterpillar poop on the leaves. My mom is a master gardener so it was easy for her to identify. The pork burger bun was so hard I couldn't cut through it with a knife for my aunt. The tacos I ordered were bland but the cabbage was a nice crunch. I brought this to the servers attention who said "Thank you for telling me.  We try to use local ingredients." I bet!

I also emailed the owners with the info and the pictures I took and they offered to refund me for my meal if I called and gave my credit card info over the phone to an assistant. No, no thanks. I'm not comfortable doing that over the phone. I emailed her back and told her this but never received a response. 

Based on my experience, I would not come back. We still laugh about paying so much to eat "caterpillar poop".

Wish I could give it 0 stars. 

Visiting Philadelphia and Geno's/ Pat's was mentioned to me by several friends who were vaguely familiar with the area. Let me say this: SUBPAR. I could get better cheesesteaks in California. 

Geno's clearly uses their reputation to get away with using only cheap/ low quality ingredients. It was not made fresh and was ready and wrapped in less than 3 minutes- essentially cold. If it didn't have the name/history this would place would no longer be in business as far as I'm concerned. 

If you want a good cheesesteak: DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY HERE.


For Philadelphia's own sake, they better have some better cheesesteak joints.

We had a great time listening to the Friday Night Mariachi band and having a great dinner! Our waiter Andres had a great smile and made sure we were well cared for, the service here is beyond amazing! It's nice to drive up a little further on Oracle road to get out of town and enjoy a Friday night out on the patio with great Mexican food with our puppy. I love this place. We will certainly come back again!

Great food and their sandwiches are pretty darn amazing. We always stop in every time we're in town. The first time I was there, the guy who served us- Brian- was so over the top in costumer service- he made the experience 100 times better. So kind. So welcoming. Really turned a yummy food experience into a must go. He was truly a big part of the reason we came back. Great costumer service. Most of their staff is also super nice! But most definitely count on great food.  love love love.

The food is good but waiting for it is another thing. We usually go on our lunch break and sit at the bar expecting faster service, not the case. In my last visit we waited 40 minutes for an order of sweet potato fries and edamame.

Hands down the best cheesesteak I've ever had! I am enviest of the locals, you have a hidden gem here y'all! Genuinely friendly service, affordable prices, and absolutely amazing food! The smoothies are also very delicious and well made, im from Cali and I know what it takes to make a great smoothie. Do yourself a favor and check this place out!

This place used to be a standby for our family. We could count on them for cheap, healthy, consistently delicious eats. They changed their name, but management & staff were supposed to be the same, so we didn't think twice about hitting them up for dinner the other night. 

Sadly, the food was terrible the night we went. My vermicelli bowl was full of limp, way past edible green onions & iceberg lettuce that was brown & tasteless like it was from a plastic package the was past its "sell by" date. The broth just tasted like salt & they didn't bring fish sauce until I found a server to ask. But the biggest disappointment was the vermicelli. It seemed like spaghetti instead of rice noodles. Maybe we just caught them on an off night, but I'm in no rush to go back.
Tbh, I don't quite get the hype. I've had tacos that were just as good for half the price elsewhere. Not to mention the crowd...

This place is awesome! I had their portobello sandwich was seriously one of the most amazing sandwiches I have ever had. They don't have a large selection of sour ales as there is usually only 1 on tap which is unfortunate because those are my fav types of beers. Prices are somewhat reasonable. The service could've been better but I think it's better if you sit at the bar. Over all, can't complain.
Fantastic! Best Indian food I ever had. I'm from out of town not one of the local rednecks so I have had my share of Indian food.Great atmosphere and decor. Services was great friendly and attentive.

Even though the food is pretty good, the service is TERRIBLE. Even for takeout they rarely get it right. They're always out of stuff. Their cuisine is very authentic and the sushi is very fresh and nice. Even the hibachi is good too. But the service is awful. What can you do?

Nice warm and inviting atmosphere as soon as you walk in.  Food was excellent.   We ordered the calamari,  and the chicken puffs to start.  The calamari was crispy, yet tender with just the right amount of spice.  The chicken puffs were light and flaky with a nicely seasoned filling. As for the rolls,  we ordered six different ones.  The gobe, sexy girl, old webster, white house, salmon skin,  and spicy girl.  The sexy girl and spicy girl were my favorites. The salmon skin was solid as well. Overall good food and great experience.  Will definitely return.
Great burgers and extremely convenient. I am disappointed when I call the phone and it's busy, only to arrive to order in person to see the phone is purposely off the hook.

Shatangi almost forgot to review this place.  I was reminded about it from a feature on Food Network last night.  This was one of the most memorable meals I enjoyed in St Louis.  Finally a restaurant that was just trying to be itself.  We went on a slower, freezing cold weeknight and the warm service made up fro the trek.  Soul food tastes much the same throughout the Midwest but when made right, the simplest dish can evoke memories of childhood  and summer that make the not-so-healthy combo of salt and grease a delight to the senses.  Mos def on my list of places to go to celebrate.

Shatangi told you...

My husband and I went with another couple at their suggestion. I was not attending with enthusiasm.  I have driven by this restaurant countless times and was never drawn to it due to the dated signage and building. Overall, I was very impressed. I am generally hyper-critical of things like comfortable seating, host greeting, lighting, and of course, food and service. All were very good here. I would describe the service as very good, although not sophistocated. Also, it is family owned and the bartender was one ofthe family and both a good bartender and interesting guy, striking the right balance between service and entertainment. The food and drinks (again I'm critical in this area) were great, and the steaks fantastic. Going back tonight.

Just picked up my lunch from here and I had to leave a review. I got the QT Special sandwich, which I was told was their most popular. It's a Banh Mi with a mix of different meats. Everything was so well balanced and very delicious. This isn't a sandwich that's overloaded with meat or overloaded with veggies to fill space, it's just a perfectly balanced sandwich. They included what felt like the right amount of every ingredient, allowing me to taste everything with no one ingredient overpowering the sandwich. The bread was ultra crunchy, which I imagine might be a turn off for some, it definitely caught me off guard when I realized just how hard it was, but those concerns were gone with the first bite. Somehow the bread is super crispy on the outside without being hard on the inside. 

The restaurant itself was small, but there are a few seats. I ordered takeout and I was in and out within 10 minutes. The staff was nice and worked quickly. The food is ultra affordable too, my sandwich was $6.50. This meal was excellent and I can't wait to go back.

Super strong drinks. No table service--order at the bar. You can get food from Felipe's downstairs and bring it up.

My favorite part about the bar was that it wasn't very crowded, so our group could relax and enjoy our food and drinks.

Having lunch here was just ok.  I had the 1/2 sandwich and 1/2 soup.  The chicken noodle soup was average, but did have big chunks of chicken.  The 1/2 turkey bacon sandwich looked a mess but actually turned out to be quite good.  My fries were dried out and warm, not hot.  Overall it was enough to fill me while traveling but I wouldn't stop here again.

Best crab bennies oh wow I finally found in Nola!!
Trust me this place hands down will change your taste buds!!
Delisioso and the iced coffee lol just try and see!!!
Spiked! Lol yum yum yum thank you Chef you are amazing !! 
Our server she is the sweetest nicest her name is Kelley she was amazing, knows everything on the menu and she's right on point, everything is just too good to be true!
A Must Try!!!!
My boy friends huevos ranchero were so good not even a bean was left on his plate lol!
Oh and the shoe string homemade fries and homemade ketchup. Come try!!!!
Forget Willa Jean!

Stopped in on a cold and rainy night.  Location is easy to find and just a couple minutes off of 465.  Ample parking which is appreciated.

This place is instantly the nicest tasting room in Indianapolis.  Like an upscale pub without food, really.  I liked the reclaimed brick.  They have some tables and a bar with TVs and the game on.  The only food on the menu looked to be pretzels, so be sure to check Twitter to if there is going to be a food truck there.  By the time I arrived at 8:00, the food truck had already checked out for the night.

Servers were very friendly  if not a little pushy.  I appreciated them getting me a glass of water while sampling their house beers.  I found their house beers to be a little bit on the safe side of their genres.  Probably a good business bet, but a little disappointing for a hardcore beer nerd.  Their guest tap list, however, filled in the gaps in their lineup - there was an excellent choice available for any beer lover.

If you're looking for a nice place to grab a pint, it's a nice option.  It isn't yet to a point where I would consider it a destination, but if you are in the area, I would recommend it.  I look forward to seeing how it evolves in the future.

What a waste of money. I will never return. Paid Steakhouse prices for a filet and rib eye that I could have beat with walmart discount meat and a smokey Joe BBQ. I thought it was too good to be true, a steakhouse in MJ. Driving downtown next time I want a steak because this place is not an option. Don't waste your money or time.

Only in America can you have New Orleans food in a restaurant owned by Europeans on the 4th of July. We were starving & we walked it bc everything was packed. We ordered a seafood platter & I wasn't really hopeful it was going to be good. Never been so happy to be wrong. The seafood was really fresh & tasted great. The owner was really nice & kept us happy. The only thing I didn't like was their  lobster bisque, it was very uneventful. Their salads going out to other customers looked amazing though! Overall, I'll def be coming back & trying the rest of their items. Def give it a shot! Love the chill atmosphere here.

Meh.  I was hungry and Parkway closed early because they ran out of bread so I ended up at Theo's.  The toppings were good but the crust was flavorless and I am not a fan of its crackerlike crispness.  I like all kinds of pizza, NY style and Chicago style and so on but I have yet to find pizza in New Orleans that I love.

Tartufo steak. It comes in a pizza. but more importantly it comes in cheesesteak form. For those of you not familiar with what a truffle is, my first list will explain what it is and where to find them in Philadelphia food. Don't discount it until you've tried it, TRUST ME. The Tartufo is a cheesesteak with truffle cream and caramelized onions.

I've also gotten the Old Smokey on a couple occasions, and while the pizza is great, the toppings are rather spaced out and thin, I remember being disappointed. The sauce, while great, overpowered the other ingredients, that little thing you pay extra for ;)

The sides/appetizers available are really just lame. Not bad, just a real fizzle. With every combination under the sun on their pizzas, an appealing appetizer shouldn't be too difficult. Cheesy garlic bread shouldn't be outside of the realm of possiblity, no? Per favore?  

Don't bother with the fries, they're regular variety and if you ask for cheesefries, it's a 50/50 chance they say they don't sell such a thing; else, you get a softball of fries and cheese rolled up in foil. NO. LIE. More of a speedbump than a roadblock, as I consumed said fried potato mozzarella ball.

The arancine looks awesome on the menu but don't get your hopes up, might as well be fried air. Far too much batter and microscopic flecks of pancetta.

To remedy the weak sides, I will every so often get an order of wings along with something bigger. The wings themselves are not fried, but baked and are of good quality, so no worries there. 

So despite the fact that I've never actually made it to Rustica to sit and have a slice, I've picked up food from there before and the establishment is nice. The inside seating is minimal and a couple tables sit outside along the street. I like this part of Northern Liberties, as this particular part of 2nd street is lively. If you plan ahead you can order your pizza, hit up the Foodery just across Poplar Street and grab a beer with plenty of time to spare.

As a Yelp sponsor, read this!
The fish sandwich was disgusting. Could bring myself to try!  Errs are good but will not be back!!!

The Good: the wine list is amazing and fairly priced. The staff is wonderful. 

The Bad: the food. Every steak was undercooked and had no seasoning. The sides were cold and flavorless. The Wagu short ribs were greasy and bland. 

The Ugly: over cooked Halibut sent back and a new piece sent out that you could smell from across the room. Really?!  That was sent back as well. 

Not a good representation of the Charle Palmer brand I used to know and WAY too expensive for the "quality."

I've been to Good Dog four or five times since I moved here three years ago, so I would hardly call myself a regular.  That said, I would say I have been enough to opine on this little gem of a dive.
