Personally, I am not one of these dive bar junkies, and I prefer a slightly more upscale bar if I am going to be eating food (for drinking bring on a good beer list and that is all I care about).  Good Dog delivers a much better dining experience than the surrounding decor gives off (and if you watch triple D, the kitchen actually looks in good order).  This is certainly not gourmet and I wouldn't compare this to the experience at, say, Village Whiskey, but it is solid.

If I was going to make a recommendation...this place is dark...the first floor may not have any natural light.  Given the rather cave like feeling throughout, maybe save this place for the Winter when hibernation and beer is a perfect excuse for a dinner.  

Other notes...great beer list and decent mac & cheese.  Watch out for the upstairs (third floor) where the real locals and insiders reside...I went up there to play pool one night and it looked like I was going to have to sell my kidney for a pool stick.
The food is wonderful and the owner is so personable. We had a fabulous experience here!! Highly recommend when in Santa Barbra.

We try to make our yearly family vacation here each summer. Plenty to do with our teen daughter and my parents love to gamble here.
We splurged this time and stayed in the players suite-it was so nice. Room a little outdated but awesome views. The spa hot tub worked great. In the past we stayed in the upgraded skyline part of the hotel which is nice and more upgraded.
We rec'd voucher for 2 free drinks on casino floor (house wine or well drinks) got 2 rum at cokes at Vitos Bar -woah,it was a strong drink lol! Awesome & friendly service from the gal working bar last night(around 7PM).
What we loved about the players suite is we don't really gamble it's nice to escape the smoky bars and sit in our room with our amazing view and with a nice bottle of wine to enjoy in our room.
I'm dinging it 1 star because although it was supposedly non-smoking our room reeked of cigarettes. If that will really bug you I'd suggest staying in a different room.

I am giving Bahama Breeze 3 stars because the food/service here has been very inconsistent. The first time I came the service was just okay, but my food tasted great. I got the jerk chicken pasta and a shrimp appetizer. The two times I've come after this, I have ordered the same exact thing. The second time, it was super off, but my waitress was great. The last time, it was just okay. This probably won't be my first choice of restaurant, but not a bad alternative.

My favorite place!!!

Delicious coffee and beignets. By far better than any other place in the city.

The live music and outdoor park topped off the visit!

Gotta have  the Red Beans and Sausage on Monday. Real New Orleans food!!
Good Service and Food second to none!!

Decent spot only because of this dish. They maybe better for the other dishes. I do not eat meat but I can tell you that the mash potatoes and corn were really good. The blackened salmon was a bit disappointing. It was ok. I excepted a flavorful experience however, it was cooked like I expected a blackened salmon to be. So I rated based off that salmon but the other dish looks fire, I just don't eat meat. Just another day on the road! 

Live, love, and laugh
- Sha

Pork rinds. Chicharron. Eat and love these when done well, but for health not as much as I'd like. These are so GOOD! House made. Grab a bag. Ate them with my homemade red pork pozole!  Chorizo breakfast burritos are great too. Chilaquiles are not worth trying though.

Overpriced, overpriced, overpriced. 

I have been waiting to experience this new CWE hot commodity for a week now and the perfect opportunity to skip the 45-minute line presented itself at 3PM on a Wednesday (we only had to wait 10 minutes to order!) The restaurant itself was clean and had an interesting decor scheme. The staff were efficient and what one would expect at a typical fast food restaurant. 

The food, while decent for diner food, is FAR too overpriced for decent diner food. I was extremely excited to try the vegetarian option: the fried, cheese-stuffed portabello Schroom' Burger. Unfortunately it was hard to taste the small mushroom with all the cheese and fried breadcrumbs, so the mushroom sandwich turned more into a mozzarella stick sandwich. It was also a little too small for what one would expect to get for $7. The crinkle cut fries were crispy. I wasn't a huge fan, but my friend, who loves crinkle cut fries, thought they were excellent. The 'pie oh my' pecan concrete was far too small for what one would expect to get for $5. 

All in all, it was a fun experience but I probably will not return unless others suggest it because of the price of the food compared to the amount and quality of food I received.

Please stop using Grubhub! Pizza was clearly sitting at restaurant waiting for the delivery person. In that time crust became like cardboard and then delivered lukewarm. I can't even fairly rate the food since think ruined due to delivery. 

Shouldn't take over an hour to get pizza.

Wats up people,  so this place is pretty cool. Very fresh and tasty food. The waitress I had was very nice although she was not much help when it came to choosing a dish. She had a basic response of "yah man, its all good." So here the man two dishes i go for, Chicken and Kubideh , and Chicken and Barg. Both are down right amazinggoodunbelievable. If you've never had falafels, please try them. And make sure to dip them in the cucumber sauce. In all ,this place is definitely worth checking out. Peace

Stumbled here with a few friends while in town for the Sugar Bowl and had a great experience. The service was very laid back and fun, with the server calling everyone nicknames.  The birthday boy even got a free beer! 

The menu is more of a "Create Your Own Sandwich" type, selecting the type of meat, bread, toppings, sauce and side dish. The orders came out mostly correct, with a few people missing some toppings and my order of grilled veggies being substituted for steamed (when they brought them out, he said they would be better. And they were excellent. Topping wise, I'm guessing they took some liberty because we selected too many options that would clash). With such a large amount of options, it seems some things are not always in stock, but they will make suggestions to enhance your experience. 

I ordered the Zapp's potato chip crusted chicken on french bread.  It was delicious. The side of steamed veggies with Cajun seasonings was a great complimentary choice, as the sandwich was huge!

The meal was a great value, as our whole party was full and satisfied for under $15 per person. The cost per sandwich is the same and there are only a few toppings/side dishes that required an additional charge.  

This place was very casual and laid back. It's a great place to stop for lunch while exploring NOLA!

We've been dining at Tastebuds for years and always love to go back.  The menu changes with the seasons, and there are always inventive, well-seasoned main dishes that are absolutely delicious.  Last night we had deviled eggs with crabmeat and jalapeno peppers, stuffed mushrooms,  duck, done just rare enough, with roasted fennel, blackberry vinaigrette and arugula and cod with horseradish panko crust (really crunchy) and risotto.  Yum!  I hated to see the meal end.  This place is a bit uphill from town, but certainly worth the short ride.  Free parking is plentiful and the staff will give you a warm welcome.  Love this place!

Ladies and gentlemen, I have finally found a true Italian restaurant in New Orleans. Though I have yet to try a couple of Italian places in the quarter, I can safely say that Domenica is far more authentic Italian than saaaay Vincent's. Their pastas are perfectly cooked, sauces rivaling those I've tasted in Florence, Italy, and the proscuitto buonissimo (that's awesomely delicious for you non-Italians). Service was friendly, atmosphere chic and classy and to top it all, it does opentable.com. Four stars it is.

Very good, authentic Mexican food. Fresh, tasty and made to order. Limited menu but amazing tacos. The rice and beans were delicious. The place is small but we were greeted kindly and the menu explained to us in detail
Hands down best Bloody Mary bar I've ever had (I've tried quite a few)! It can honestly be a complete meal! A must try when you're in St. Louis!!

Ok.  Every time I have been here it has been better.  Jessica was our overworked server tonight.  One of only two servers on a busy Sunday night.  We both had the filet mignon....like I had last time.  Tender, flavorful nicely cooked.  Great fries.  I worked at the Ivanhoe Restaurant in MA back in the day...they made the best bread pudding...until tonight.  OMG was it good.  All employees had masks and all the customers..except those of us eating outside.  Superb and highly recommended.

Honestly.. I really do NOT understand how some of the reviews were written here. My lady is VERY particular to what kind of food she eats and how it's prepared (frozen or fresh) and she didn't complain, I was amazed. Came here for dinner and had paneed chicken with Alfredo sauce, delicious. I had my breakfast just now (big easy) and it was delish. Staff is very professional and very friendly . I ate here twice, zero complaints. Might come here again before I leave. Some people on yelp are harsh, but I also can understand personal experiences not being good leading to those types of reviews.

Great neighborhood spot for a beer, a snack, or a few of each. They do a great job of rotating the draught and can selection to keep things fresh and the servers are generally friendly and knowledgeable when you ask about their current selections. The food is just as strong as the beer selection and there truly is not a single thing on the menu that does not hit the spot. The Buffalo chicken spring rolls and chicken fingers are fan favorites but everything from the kitchen is solid. 

The Collar is truly a gem and is worth stopping by any time you're in the neighborhood. Looking forward to being able to sit at the bar again as the bar tending staff are all exceptionally friendly. In the meantime their tables are a great place to start or end any night out with friends!
The BEST soup and sandwiches in town! Highly recommend the #11 Blue Bronco but can't go wrong with any of them.

I would say it is more likely 3.5 Stars, but I decided not to round up.  I found it weird that they claim home made ice cream, but half the freezer case is filled with flavors they do not make on their own.  So, definitely ask which flavors are "HOME MADE".  

Between the GF and I, we tried only the Home Made flavors of Butter Pecan, Nutter Butter and Chocolate Overload.  All were pretty good and of superior quality to large batch industrial ice cream.  

A good spot to grab a coffee or a scoop while roaming around Nashville's little downtown area (Sorry, I am from NYC, no offense intended).

So I got online since I'm from Utah and learned about Pizzalchik on Diner's, Drive-ins and Dives.  First - they ripped us off and I don't know why I didn't say anything, and now online I see I'm not the first person.  I'm into antiquing and estate/garage sales and not a snob about used plates at all, but they gave us two from the FREE PILE garage sale plates that were all chipped up - like the worst ever from any restaurant I've ever been to.  Pizza was good but the chicken - we got a half chicken and honestly, the rotisserie at Sam's Club kills it for a TON better price.  I wouldn't be writing this review if he hadn't completely ripped us off but I knew that he knew he had done it.  Later, I met people at the local wineries (great winery town, unknown to us!) and they said ya, not that great at ALL.  Again...we got one pizza, and said we wanted a personal pizza to split since we were also getting a half chicken and some potatoes, but we got a full sized pizza. No problem - but as I was sitting there looking over the menu I saw he had STILL ripped us off by 15 bucks.  We're happy to pay very well and we're the best tippers ever if you serve us well and give us GREAT food - but this was a complete rip off.  What is Guy Fieri thinking?  Someone scouted this place out for him so he got great service and got to eat for free, that's what!

One of my favorite happy hours. Even though I loved the steak medallion with mashed potato option the happy hour menu changed on me. 
 Steak and tomato was a refreshing change.  
If you love spicy and devil eggs this marriage is right up yours and my alley. One word Delicious!

As a former French Quarter dweller, I always was short on great spots to have more than greasy diner food late night in the neighborhood. St. Lawrence fills in this gap in the midnight hour, and during day light as well... with a varied menu that offers something for everyone. 

The arugula peach salad is delicious and though I am a equal opportunity eater (meats, fishies, veggies, unknowns), and there are plenty of great carnivore options on the menu (like the TURDUCKEN BURGER(!)), they have great offerings for the herbivorically inclined. The veggie curry is perfect and the sloppy joel (all veggie) is pretty awesome too. 

Glad to see some non-pretentious local talents heading up a spot that keeps it straight and simple: quality, locally sourced, wholesome, what's in season kind of foods, great service, at a good price point, serving into the late night hours. 

The cocktail menu has lots of great delights too. The fresh mississippi blueberry basil gin daiquiri will make you rethink what a daiquiri can be. mmmm....  

Oh, and don't forget dessert. I thought I hated pudding until I tried the banana pudding. It's all fresh mashed up 'nana's, with a POW! Ginger cookie, and a perfectly tinged cardamom cream. Not to forget the tempura fried double stuffed oreo. I almost never eat fried ... but my lord, this thing is a whole new dimension of dessert.

This place is tucked away in a strip mall next to a Publix supermarket but their sushi is excellent.  The decor is average but the plate and sushi presentation are very creative and imaginative.  This place is definitely a hidden gem in the area.

Good bar food and cool beer garden. Unfortunately the beer garden is a revolving door of inside patrons coming to smoke. They leave the garage doors open, so those eating inside and out have a terrible smoke filled experience.

I reluctantly stopped in this morning at my son's request, because he loves the food.  I say reluctantly because I've eaten at many IHOPs across the US and almost always have a lackluster experience, usually because of bad service.  We walked in and were seated right away.  The only negative thing I will note is that the greeter was a ridiculous mumbler.  "Howmanyyougot?" I'm sorry??  "Youwannakidsmenu?"  Huh?  Once we were seated, our waitress was quick with our drinks, and made sure we were not ever in need of anything.  She was outstanding, and it kills me that I lost the receipt with her name on it.  We were seated near the entrance on the 4th of July if that helps management :-) The pancakes, eggs, hash-browns and bacon were delicious, and met every expectation I had, but the wait staff were what made our meal outstanding.

Gordon helped me look for my first home. About one week after being introduced to Gordon through one of his satisfied clients and starting the search for a home, Philadelphia went into quarantine for coronavirus. As most business within the city came to a grinding halt, my stress of finding a new home within a specific time frame was now accompanied with the new challenge of keeping safe from an unknown, spreading pandemic. I was lucky that Gordon took to the challenge of a changing time by adjusting his own process. He adapted quickly to using technology wherever possible, which kept the search and closing process timely. Gordon is also very savvy in the Philadelphia market, and his perspective on different aspects of the home-buying process like cost negotiation really helped me as a clueless first buyer. Gordon has also checked in after the closing process, making sure all our goals were satisfied. With Gordon's knowledge of the area, his connections, and his professionalism in overcoming challenges, I can confidently say that Gordon helped me find a fantastic place. In the future, I will be able to say that meeting Gordon and buying my first home were a personal high point when looking back at the chaos of 2020.
Little Donkey...fresh Mexican food at a great price with a superb bartender. Ross, you made our night!

Was actually very surprised how good this pizza was. Sure, its not what you would get in NY but it's really not bad for Florida. Ordered through uber eats on thursday night around midnight. Got delivered to Carrollwood and it was still hot.  Will order again.
The place is awesome!!! The food, the bar, the ambiance, the dancing and along with the friendly staff, this is my go to spot every time I'm here in the city!!
All sushi is NOT created equal.  Very impressed with the unique rolls and happy hour pricing.  I can't wait to return...I wish they were open on Sunday :-( .

I would not go here during the weekend.  Last weekend, we went here for my girlfriends birthday.  BIG MISTAKE!  They were so unprepared for the large crowd from Oktoberfest.  We got there at 6 and by the time we got our food and drinks it was already 7:30, we ended up getting our checks by 8 so we missed half of the soccer game we were supposed to go to.  They also forgot numerous food items and drinks that people in our party ordered, which was only 10 people (Some people didn't even get to eat).  The manager and server kept saying they "think" the food is on the way after an hour when we ordered.  The food here is good, relatively cheap, but the service is absolutely awful, do not go here on the weekend.
TASTY FOOD - EXPENSIVE - NICE PEOPLE. There's nothing fancy about the place, but the food is pretty good. I felt like the specials were not that special, and for $13 I expected much more.

This place is DELICIOUS! I was planning a large (16 person) bachelorette party brunch and the people at Saint Anejo were so helpful and accommodating.  The space is really nice and has tall ceilings and the space for large parties was off to the side- almost like having our own room.  

The breakfast tacos, chilaquiles, churros, chocolate waffle, drinks, jalapeno cornbread and queso... it's all delicious!  

Definitely be prepared to wait because as we were leaving around 11:30am on Saturday there was a LONG line waiting for tables.

You can't go wrong if you're downtown Indy and want to grab a drink and some pretty good food. We were in town  and decided to try the bar because it was close to the hotel.  We were able to find seats at the bar, drinks were delivered in no time, and our food was surprisingly good.  I don't usually expect much from bar food, but I have to say it was very tasty - best burger I've had in awhile. The staff was busy but they found time to chat for a minute about other things to do and see while in Indy. Can't give it enough praise.  We will definitely return!

Update 8-11-21. The service is awful. When they first opened this place everything was great now it's gone down the drain. The male waiters are so rude. My husband and I use to love it. We would tell everybody about this place and even take our guest. We would go at least once maybe twice a month. We have experienced their awful customer service before but we ignored it. However, today was the last straw. My husband and I were ignored by our waiter the whole night. It was four tables around us. We watched and listened to him go to every table but ours. He came by to ask them "were they okay, he came back to take their empty plates, he came to ask them if they needed refills. He didn't once acknowledge us. The last time he came around he looked me dead in my face and kept going. Mind you we had empty plates but he always kept his back towards us. He even kept asking the people behind us that already paid if they needed anything. It was so bad I had to walk out the restaurant while my husband was still eating. I will NEVER go back. The hostess are rude as well. I will be spending my $75 elsewhere.

I placed a GrubHub order tonight from Cibo by Illiano and I'm so happy! Everything is delicious: the bread and salad are fresh, the rustic chicken soup was to die for (tortellini and big pieces of white meat chicken), and the chicken francaise is scrumptious. They delivered quickly and the delivery guy was very nice. I was lucky to get my order in minutes before they closed. My only regret is that I didn't tip more than the suggested 15%.

Great place!  Even BETTER than before!  I love the quality the new owner has put into the food they serve!  I always get the crispy sea bass, extra garlic, not spicy.  I get at least 2 meals out of it.  Combo plates are generous portions but the flavor is hit-miss - hubby likes it.  So far, the flavors of items OUTSIDE the combo plates have been consistently great.  We also tried the ox tail...good flavor.  I appreciate the variety of selections they offer...the rice plates, ox tail, shrimp honey walnuts.  I get a good bang for my buck while still be able to enjoy the Chinese flavors I crave. I can't wait to try the other dishes next time!

Laxmi's Indian food was really fantastic. We ordered lamb tikka masala and chicken curry plus an order of the plain Naan bread. 

The two curry dishes were excellent and uniquely tasty. We ordered them spicy and they had just the right amount flavor, plus heat. They were nice sized portions too with an ample amount of good rice! The curry was filled with tender chicken and peppers; the lamb in the tikka masala was also really tender. I love curry and am not a frequent Indian-food eater. Now that we have such a great place close by, that will change! The delivery was prompt and friendly. 

I called and asked for advice about what to order and they were so helpful and polite. They didn't rush me and I had quite a few questions bc I am not too familiar with Indian cuisine. 

We are so glad to have this new option for Indian delivery in Broomall. Give them a try! You will love.

I stopped by here today for dinner and ordered dinner. To be honest, most Mexican food is sort of the same no matter where you go. Not here!  Great service, and the food was seriously the best I've ever had.

Staff hardly acknowledged us. We stopped in for our lunch break, and a to-go order of a sandwich and salad took over 15 minutes to put together. When we finally opened the bag, we'd received the wrong sandwich altogether and the salad had no dressing on it. Way too expensive for what you get (even if you get what you actually ordered). Bummer.

I was pleasantly surprised with the food and drinks at the village pub. The menu is fairly large and has something for all tastes. I order the award winning wings, buffalo style, and a burger. The wings were great and the burger was flavorful.
The beer selection was pretty solid but mostly consisted of light ales and IPAs, nothing dark or robust. 
I sat at the bar and got great service. I'd recommend the village pub as a great stop for folks coming through town or staying around for business. I'll be back.
The food was absolutely amazing  cool atmosphere    Waiter wasn't super attentive but overall great experience
Nice Mexican joint in the city. This place has a great location and the margaritas were incredible. Hostess was friendly and escorted us even to the bar.

The food was over priced for the quality.  The wait was forty five minutes to be seated.  Furthermore, the service was substandard, once our server took the ordet we had to wait thirty minutes more for our oder to be placed on the table  and the food was cold.  I would not recommend this restaurant. I suggest the management at the restaurant execute  quality assuance and quality control.

This spot is AMAZING and the decor is so cute. Currently on a week long trip and have already gone two times because their food is so incredible. The service is great too and food comes out quickly. They have TEN different eggs Benedict to choose from and everything we've tried is incredible! Think we'll be coming back a third time before our trip is over.
Great and convenient Starbucks, always fast and good coffee. On this most recent visit, I was lucky enough to be staying in the Marriott, so it was REALLY convenient!

We came here today for dinner. We loved the decor right away. This is women owned business and all staff that we saw were women. We believe we met the owner as well. Very pleasant ladies. We got crab Rangoon for appetizer- it was hot, tasty, a bit on a sweeter side and that is what we like, they come 5 to order. My husband got beef soup that came with lots of beef, noodles, cilantro, bean sprouts and green onion. He liked it a lot, he ate the whole huge bowl but the couple pieces of meat that were too chewy. I got the wild rice noodles with veggie and chicken. The flavor is on a sweeter side but very good. Chicken was all white meat and to my surprise very juicy. I also visited the restroom that smelled good, looked nice and there was a huge single standing beautiful full size mirror there. Very cool place! We will be back and recommend to our friends.

I love this place. I went on a Saturday morning and didn't have to wait for a table, our server was very friendly and they had someone there playing a piano while we ate. The place itself is interesting in that the kitchen and the dining area are in one open space. You can see them cook everything, which I thought was impressive the amount of deliousness that could come out of such a small cooking area. I had the HUEVOS RANCHEROS and added chorizo and avocado. To die for! I can't wait to go back and try more. Go for breakfast and then enjoy walking to all the shops on Oak.

The food is very top notch here, so that definitely deserves a 5 stars. My group and I really did enjoy our different versions of Eggs Benedict. It was flavorful, very savory, and such a great dish. I personally ordered the version that included either the crab or lobster and it was really delicious. So, the criticism doesn't really rely on the food itself. It more so relies on the waiter that took our orders.

His name was Michael and he was a great guy, until towards the very end when he had brought our check over. We asked if we could split the check. To that, he slowly put his hands together with a slight heavy sigh so that we all took notice and replied with, 

"We are currently slammed at the moment. It would have been better if you guys had told me in the very beginning to get split checks", he said with a disappointed look. 

He just stood there while we took a quick glance at each other. We had told him that it would be no problem, and we could pay on one card and the rest of us would Venmo that individual. We were perfectly fine with doing this, but we were not okay at all with his approach to the situation. 

Isn't it standard work process for the waiter themselves to ask in the beginning if we are all going to be on one check or if it's going to be separated? Because that's what we came to be familiar with when working with our waiters. 

With that, our only critique is this. Please train your waiter(s) about proper standard work process and to follow suit to those of other restaurants. I honestly hope that the establishment takes this critique very seriously , because I wouldn't want another group to experience the same feeling of pressure that we felt from Michael. Other then that, we did thoroughly enjoy the food, just not the waiter.

First things first:  They are no longer open until 9pm.  They close at 8pm, Mon-Sat (I submitted the changes to Yelp but until they take effect--fyi!).  Also, they've moved.  They are technically at the same address but at the other end of the strip mall.   

Having cleared that up, let me say, The Shak serves up some amazing Hawaiian eats at incredibly reasonable prices.  All of the workers I've encountered have been friendly and welcoming in every way.  The atmosphere is ok, though not fabulous.  My preference is to do takeout  (and it seems to be their preference as well as whether dining in or taking out, they now serve all entrees in to-go box/trays).  

What I love:

-Their Chicken Katsu is perfect.  

-Their teriyaki salmon (I think is an occasional special) is just the perfect mix of sweet, tang, and salt.  And, more importantly, they don't overwhelm the salmon with the teriyaki.    

-My dining companion thoroughly enjoys their Mahi-mahi (also usually a special).  It's popular though...we've gone before when they've run out!

What isn't as wonderful:

-I'm not a fan of most of their beef dishes.  The quality just doesn't seem to be what it should be.  

-I could also take or leave their macaroni salad.

Honestly, the dishes I enjoy here, I love.  But, I don't love everything.

If I could, I'd hit it with 3.5 stars.  Since I cannot--4, it is.

i was super excited to have my birthday dinner here ... and an hour and some change into waiting for our food, kinda lost the enthusiasm. 

we ordered drinks and appetizers - the drinks came in about 10 minutes. 

they were out of most of the seafood for the boiler pots and the salads as well. so we ordered a caesar salad with shrimp and crab legs, only one appetizer showed up, maybe 40 minutes later with the promise "the rest of the foods coming" ... over a half hour goes by, drinks are empty and not asked if we want refills. 

more time passes and as i was using the bathroom dinner was dropped at the table and we were told the kitchen lost the ticket. 

my brother in laws steak was over cooked - otherwise i can't actually complain about my burger or my sisters eggplant parm. 

the server comped all of our food and we only had to pay for the 3 drinks. no manager touched the table about the issue.

don't waste your time - i'm sure you can get a better experience else where.

If I could give half a star, I would. The food is decent enough, not the best sushi in town. Service sucked! Only one sushi chef for the Sunday lunch shift? My friend who's the most easy going individual was upset about our experience today. She was served fatty salmon and unripe avocado. Never coming back here. Do yourself a favor and drive up McCarran to Hiroba instead.

Love the waiter who took care of us he deserved  a 5 stars very attentive even the place is busy he knows what he is doing our food comes in on time and very accurate 
The food is not that fantastic I can not rate it a 5 stars 
 the place is ok I feel that I will fall on the floor feels that it's slippery 
The atmosphere is ok though

We had such a nice meal. My salad was diverse, fresh, and delicious.  Beautiful presentation. Mr, had the panini and fries.  Crisp, super hot fries were seasoned to perfection. The panini was also delicious, grilled and we finished every bite. 
I know I'm in New Orleans with some of the world's best food but this is an excellent hotel restaurant and perfect.  Really.
The service was attentive and very gracious.  The chef checked on our food.  A lot of interest in making our meal a very good experience.  They offer both the lunch and dinner menu through the evening.

Cool atmosphere, with bands playing almost every night. Good Mid-City location with amole drinks including Abita draft beers. Staff friendly and establishment clean. Come check out a band, sit back, relax and enjoy the music in this cozy, Canal St. Bar. Also conveniently located by streetcar stop.

I went to Rich & Charlie's for lunch with a co-worker around 12:30pm.  We were immediately greeted by a hostess and seated immediately.   Our server promptly came to our table to greet us and obtain beverage orders.  The restaurant offers a lunch menu with prices that are extremely reasonable for the amount of food.   I went with the chicken spiedini which came with a side of pasta, salad, and bread.   

The salad came in a large bowl and we were given plates so we could self-serve the salad.   The salad included a nice variety of ingredients and a very flavorful, but not too overpowering, dressing.  The bread was served warm and fresh.   The chicken spiedini was cooked perfectly, with just the right amount of breading and a hint of lemon flavor.  The side of pasta was much better than I expected, as sometimes the side of pasta you get at Italian restaurants is not very flavorful.  

Overall, I was very impressed by the service, food, and the prices.  I will definitely return!

I love love LOVE Fitz's. It has everything a hot spot in STL needs...delicious food, unique desserts, and it's very own factory for it's home good quality made items.

I've had the pizza before and that was good, but the most recent visit I got a burger. And I was blown away! I didn't expect to love it, but I did. I ate almost every bite and it was a big burger! It had a good smokey flavor and was cooked well done but still tender and scrumptious. So delicious!

My husband and I shared a float with orange soda and vanilla ice cream. Oh. My. God. It was so good! It was HUGE for one so I would recommend sharing. It comes topped with 3 or 4 scoops of ice cream that in and of itself was delicious...then combine it with the Fitz's orange soda and it was divine.

I always look forward to going here (and interesting note: I don't even like root beer!) and I'll be back many more times. It's a must stop of tourists or regulars who may have never been.

Crazily Good Food-We've been there three times and each time it gets better.  The shrimp tacos are the best ever, ever.  The huge, crispy shrimp taste like they are battered to order and the slaw that comes on them is unbelieveably good.  That salad with the fresh greens and the fruit, with that amazing dressing is sooo good, also served with very decent rice, shaped in a pyramid and topped with a sprinkle of Mexican cheese- is also way above average.  If they had table service they could charge twice as much, so I'm happy to go to the counter and place my order.  The salsa bar has a great variety of salsas, and the interior of the restaurant is decorated with paintings and fixtures that look like they were custom made in Mexico.  This is no taqueria!

This steakhouse is very quaint. It's unique and roomy atmosphere make it a great spot for special occasions or just because you're hungry. The bar is neat and the prime rib is huge! French onion soup is a nice touch. Service was very professional and speedy. A nice change from chain restaurants.

I was so curious and intrigued by this place after having moved to the neighborhood. The experience was average. I was a part of a party of 3, sitting on the balcony, Wednesday evening probably 7 or 8, and the service was just terrible granted there had been a large banquet party downstairs that wrapped about the time we arrived. There was a 20 minute wait on that balcony before we had any attention at all so my boyfriend went inside to see who would be taking care of us. Our server acknowledged our wait and seemed distant, but apologetic. We ordered a round of Yuenglings and Cigar City's then waited 10 minutes to see our server again to put our appetizers in. Appetizers: Oysters Rockefeller and Zing-Zang Shrimp and a bottle of wine. I have never truly enjoyed oysters but have tried Rockefeller a few times, CDB's was bland. After eating our Rockefeller we asked our server about the shrimp and wine, he let us know that they were coming but it was blatant he had forgotten. Finally returning with the wine, he broke the cork inside the bottle-- lame. The bartender from upstairs came out with the cork-infused bottle of wine and a vinturi aerator-- no big deal, there's no sense in wasting wine. By that time we had also ordered our entrees, mom and boyfriend ordered the Lobster Ravioli special, I ordered a "pasta your way." Got our Zing-Zang Shrimp, it was truly outstanding-- get it. Fifteen minutes later, the manager came back to let us know that they only had enough Lobster Ravioli to give us one entree-- not the end of the world but another disappointment nonetheless. My boyfriend ordered "pasta your way" that would be on the house. Ten minutes after that, our server came back to let us know they were completely out of the Lobster Ravioli and couldn't complete the other order either; we were blown away that it could take so long for the kitchen to let the server know, or the server to let us know. After two hours our final entrees came (all 3 being "pasta your way") and were really delicious! The final blow came with the bill and that the manager didn't see it necessary to comp both entrees. My party and I had a great time despite the flukes. I left disgruntled, a little drunk, but knowing I would try it again-- at the bar where I wouldn't be forgotten.

I give them one star for the food. For the service, they don't deserve anything. The food is quite authentic I have to say, and the portion is good also. 
The service sucks so bad that we left a penny for tip just to make a point!!! We made an reservation, as we came in, there were plenty tables open, but some how we still waited for 10 min for who knows what reason. We then sat down and ordered, after that the service hell had broke loose, the guy came to deliver our dish, and he literally SLAMMED the dish on our table without telling us what it was, and left. We ate through the whole dinner without refills on water or hot tea, no one came to the table to check on us except to SLAM the dishes at us. The part was so amazingly ridiculous was that obviously the female owner was thanking everyone who came to dine, but she SKIPPED us!!! We felt very weird being Asian who dine at a Asian place yet being treated like we were crap!!! We paid for the food then left a penny to make a point, we sure never will go back to this place anymore no matter how good the food is!!!

What a charming little place, this cute little dessert place is! You should definitely check out Chinatown's newest little sweet spot. It's got a cozy wood theme going on inside, and the nicest barista to take your order. There is a lot to like here, with its many unique desserts and drinks.

After finding this place here on Yelp, I came for the Green Tea Mille Crepe--a 20-layer delicacy of which I'd never seen before. And let me tell you folks, it's as good as it looks! Your fork will cut through it like butter, and the firm, yet creamy, texture literally melts in your mouth with a nice Asian tea flavor. As I did, it's best to compliment it with the green tea ice cream & graham cracker crumbs for the full effect. It's not cheap, at $8.95, but it's definitely a treat!

I look forward to come back here many more times in the future, to try some of their other delicacies--such as their namesake mousee. And so should you!

Bud and Marilyns is truly fantastic! I had been wanting to make my way over for a while and I'm so happy I did. We had a party of 4 and a reservation and got seated right away. 

Bud and Marilyns has a funky old diner vibe. It's like going on a really good trip with great food- yeah!!

Our server was prompt, friendly, and clearly enthusiastic about the food. Cocktails were fabulous. 

I got the fried chicken ( I was torn between that and the meatloaf) and was not disappointed. My friend ( the birthday girl) ordered steak and it was delicious. Planning on coming back soon!!

Where do I even begin with this place? The food here is remarkable, not her way to describe it. We have eaten here many times and continue to come back because of two very important items: 1. As I stated above, the food is truly out of this atmosphere. 2. The service is hands down, the best. The servers are personable and very knowledgeable about everything on their large menu. The night bartenders are also amazing, James and Jeff, I believe. The owner, Jonathan, will come out from the back and greet his customers as well.

I could go on and on about the food but give these a try as these are my favorites:

Prime rib strips 
Prime rib w/ potatoes and veggie medley 
Escargot 
Filet mignon (can't go wrong!)

5 stars and two thumbs WAY up for Jonathans Cork!
Thank you, Yelp!  You found this gem for us! Great service, great food!!!! Superb home fries!  We will be back to try more of your culinary delights!

We just finished dinner here and our Server Tony couldn't have been nicer. 
The food was great, the ambiance was very nice as well. 
It was a cold night, and when our Server knew we were cold, he came back to the table and told us he raised the heat.  
The service was excellent and the Desserts were very good-the Sorbet was amazing.

A few years ago Harvest served small portions of good food at a high price.  I would often go to the McDonald's across 202 to "top off" after eating there.  Now Harvest serves small portions of bad food at a high price.  The second to last time I went there I waited 45 minutes for a burger that was totally dried out when served.  When I pointed this out to the waiter, he said "Next time order it medium rather than well."  Um, no, next time don't leave it sitting under a heat lamp for twenty minutes (to be fair they did comp me a dessert).  The last time I ate there I ordered fish, which (no lie) smelled exactly as though there was whizz on it, and I don't mean of the cheez variety; absolutely stomach churning.  From now on, I'll just get the supersized meal at Micky D's.

Quick drive-thru location (seating too, I think?) and good deals on chicken, spicy jalapenos, and macaroni sides, rice and beans, and they gave THREE tortillas for my $7 chicken meal with two pieces of chicken. Wow! Quite tasty and I like the value and protein. I'll be back.
I LOVE this place!  Out of the way but definitely worth seeking out.  Vegetarian food was outstanding.  HUGE portions!
The tacos here are hot, fresh, and good!! We all ordered another one even my 3 year old!  I meant to take a picture but forgot all about the review after the first bite!

I came with some good friends for dinner the week of Christmas.  Food and service were both great, but the best part was the nice bourbon menu.  Very nice selection if you are a bourbon lover.  I highly recommend it and will definitely be back again soon.

The wait here was long, but it's understandable during COVID. The hostesses were great. The food is good but not amazing - try the buffalo chicken dip! Overall a cool spot to hang out with friends and get a few drinks. Only downfall, they charged for water, which is a bummer if you plan on drinking.

We keep coming back because the pizza is usually delicious, but they always mess up in some way, and tonight was no exception.  The email said to pick up our pizzas at 630, but we went late because they are never ready when we get there.When we got there they couldn't find the pizzas, but the cheese fries were sitting there.  The manager said they were crazy busy and backed up, but there was one couple eating there, and not a single pizza in the warmer.  Turns out they forgot to make them.  He offered to make me an extra pizza for free, that's fine, but I'd rather have one that I ordered for free.  I asked him if he was going to remake the cheese fries and he argued that they were fine, I pointed out how long they were sitting there and he said fine and threw them across the kitchen and said "We have to remake this guy's f###ing cheese fries."  This is completely unacceptable behavior.  When I first got there and they couldn't find my pizzas, he told me he was the new manager, and that he was going to make this place better.  He needs to calm down and take care of his customers.  To make this all worse, we paid for extra cheese, and there is barely any cheese on our pizzas, it's like eating crackers.  I've thought about writing yelp reviews before, but this is the first time I've actually done this, but when he threw the fries and said the f word, I knew I had to.  The service here has always been bad, but tonight's service  is unacceptable.

A longtime valued customer of Rose Cafe. This is a local favorite. They know exactly what I like. I don't even have to ask. Being Mexican coming from the best Mexican cook (Grandma) their Wuevos Rancheros con Carne is the best. I take all of my out of town friends here for this masterpiece. And they all come away satisfied and happy! The restaurant is alway clean and inviting. The chips are fresh and yummy. The staff always has the nicest smiles. Food time is fast and the food well that is the BEST!

The 4 is strictly in support of the food quality and portion...on the Salads! To go order today for the Southwest Cobb and I was definitely wowed at the size of the salad when I arrived home. They provided 2 dressing cups, without me asking, which was great. Huge chunks of chicken in the salad, enough for taste in every bite.  I added bacon to my salad because why not. The fire roasted veggie soup wasn't the best for me. It didn't taste bad, but just not in my flavor wheel.  Took about 20 min for my order which was a bit long, so I think there's a need for improvement in that area. Didn't seem like there was a manager on duty to keep the staff focused. Otherwise, all good on the food front. Thanks for coming to NoCo!

From the moment I walked in I was met with an overwhelming sensing warmth and welcoming from the bartender. His name was Stu. I was squished (shoved) into a small corner of the bar. Stu was able to find me and my friend a place to sit and made sure we were comfortable. An amazing bartender.

Had a great time, great service, and a great meal; what more could you ask.
Lively bar setting, front window and back window were open floor to ceiling, great outside space out back w heaters (I was sorry we weren't out there), but the dining room has a great feel and is decorated w an homage to a butcher shop but in a very cool way. Small plates, tasty comfort food, and full plates are on the menu. The cherry cheesecake was to die for. Loved it.

A Great, family friendly & affordable restaurant. Yesterday I ate with my two daughters (3,9). We were full and very happy with the service & quality of food. My girls had the vegetarian quesadillas, I had the grilled beef burritos both delicious. The owner was very nice. I also tried the homemade salsa mild and hot, incredible. Will definitely come back soon specially during this cold weather.

We had a fantastic experience last night after not eating at Seasons 52 in a little over a year.
The restaurant was COVID safe with everyone in masks.  The tables were throughly cleaned and sanitized after each group left.
Our server Christopher was excellent without being annoying.
The food was delicious.  We started with Tomato Flatbread.
The spouse had trout which she loved.
I had Cedar Plank Salmon which was outstanding. Both dishes came with potatoes and vegetables which were prepared perfectly.
The mini desserts just hit the spot.
The manager came by to see how everything was.  That doesn't happen in most restaurants today.  We won't wait a year to go back again.

I live close so I come here a lot! The staff rocks, the place is clean, the prices are decent, they have 2 happy hours with good deals on really good appetizers, & I ALWAYS walk out having had a great time! 
I love the variety they have. When it comes to apps, nothing beats the tide wings & zucchini wheels for me! Their mozzarella sticks are pretty good too. 
MOST IMPORTANTLY-for me, I love a big hot bowl of fresh, gooey, French Onion Soup with lots of flavor & onions! I FINALLY FOUND it HERE! 
I have tried a number of their sandwiches & have loved all of them! Actually I haven't had anything I didn't like at the Flowing Tide III!
They do serve breakfast on the weekends but I haven't made it over for that! 
Give it a try, you won't be disappointed!

Great great restaurant! BFood was delicious.  Would highly recommend the pesto fettuccini with prawns or the prosciutto wrapped burger. Both were very very good. Gabriella was by far one of the best waitresses I have ever had. Make sure to ask for her
Great pizza. The crust is thin and crispy. The sauce has just a hint of sweetness. Servers are very responsive and friendly.
Small store, inconsistent service, food items "meh" and can get great donuts/pastry/coffee at Tyler's across the parking lot for less $$.

I just want to start off saying this is my first review ever. After today's experience I had the need to write this review. We had to wait 45 minutes for our breakfast to come and it was only half of our order. It took another 15 minutes for the rest of the food to come out and we were still missing some sides. The food was cold not even warm. If it wasn't for the fact that my family was hungry I would of told them to take it back. I asked the waiter to remove the sides from the check that we didn't receive and when I walked up to pay I noticed that  they  were still on the check. I complained to the lady at the cash register and she chose to  ignore  my words and just  grab  the cash out of my hand. We should have gone to a fast food restaurant the food would have been hot and half the price. If you're looking for bad service and cold food that wouldn't even taste good if it was hot this is the place for you.

Let me preface this review that I have never written a bad review about any restaurants. Usually I will give an account about my positive experiences and leave the poor experiences alone.  But I really feel compelled to write this review especially  before  any more of this years St. Louis Downtown restaurant week goes by.

My family and I decided to participate in this years restaurant week at 360 mainly for the view that many have described and less for the food. We fully knew we would be paying for the $35 price fixed option even though many of the other restaurants participating were charging $25 for their price fixed menu. The Cardinals weren't playing so we thought it wouldn't be that crowded and it wasn't. The view was great..and that was all. 

Let's address their reservations policy. Their website reads:

"Three Sixty is first come, first served and does not take or require reservations for small parties. However, if you are coming with a large party or wish to guarantee a spot for your group, you can reserve space by pre-contracting a food-and-beverage minimum for your party. Our reservation policy and minimums vary depending on the size of the group and the date and time of the event."

When we entered we were told that there was "open seating".  We found some seats at one of the free rolling bartop tables. We observed a party leaving a standard fourtop dinner table and move to a nearby bar top table and when we asked our server if we could move she replied that it was reserved.  We then observed a party of two being seated there.

One would think that during restaurant week you would want to show off what your kitchen can do.  My adult daughter ordered a wedge salad which was not a wedge at all. It turned out to be an adequate tossed salad.  On this same sized salad plate was served my shrimp and grits.  Lumpy grits poured to the very edge of the plate with 3 medium shrimp placed in the middle and a small amount of sauteed peppers and onions on top. At least I did detect some cayenne pepper to add some interest.  Their fried chicken entree was a wing and a small drumstick with a buttered biscuit drizzled with honey and creamy coleslaw. Both of two orders were that.  My dad ordered a lobster roll off the menu. He got this on a nearly burnt bun with a tablespoon of pickled onions and pickles. This being a sports type bar I would have expected a side of chips or some fries.  I have never had a chilled pea soup so it was ordered. I still haven't had chilled pea soup because it tasted  like a luke warm standard pea soup. The strawberry short cake was a thin layer of strawberry with some whip cream sandwiched between to stale pieces of cake drizzled red colored sugar water. The best thing were house made Kit Kat bars.

There were several errors in service.  I found it very anoying that entrees were being served before everyone had even been served their appetizers. This happened twice.  An attempt was made to serve our desserts before the appetizers were even served. One of the desserts was still served the middle of the meal. At the end of the meal we were given a bill for the meal and several minutes later were given the bill for the drinks and an appetizer(added $2 for extra chips for the queso.

I do know how hotel/hospitality money is so important to the downtown area. I hope this establishment finds the importance of running at a high level whether the cardinals are playing  or not.

We went for lunch on a Friday, relatively packed but the line moved quickly and there was a good amount of parking available.  Being Lent, we had a couple of seafood po-boys and didn't feel like we were missing anything.  The shrimp po-boy was terrific, with expert breading that maybe graces their fried chicken as well.  The French bread was perfect, soft and flaky as it should be.  My FGT/shrimp remoulade po-boy was the best po-boy I've ever had, bar none.   The remoulade was fresh and tangy, balancing its inherent richness.  The fried green tomatoes were crunchy and coupled well with the red tomatoes of the standard dressing.  The sandwiches are oversized and overstuffed, making them well-priced overall.  The restaurant is comfortable and I am definitely looking forward to coming back and exploring the rest of the menu.

Update from my previous review.  We hit RR monthly, at least.  Food is still solid, and they are doing a lot more local stuff, which is great.  The staffing issues seem to have been resolved, staff is pleasant and prompt.  Some of them still know little if anything about the beers they have.

My primary complaint at this point is the beer.  Whoever orders their kegs has a real hop fetish.  Hey, guess what, not all of us are hop heads.  The real shame of it in my eyes is that they have 30 or 40 taps, all with mostly US micros, but a LOT of the beers have too much crossover - there might be 3 or 4 beers on draft of a given style at any one time that are really similar to each other.  That's a real shame.  Want an uber IPA or two on draft?  Sure.  But free up a couple of those taps for different styles for different beer tastes.  And always, always have at least one good old traditional American lager/amber ale on...New Belgium Fat Tire would be a solid choice.

The primary motivator for me to go to RR is the food, not the beer, and that's a real shame.  Mix in some traditional Wit beers, a few Belgian style doubles or triples, some good, malty, chewy beers, and I'll be happier.

Had the Reuben, was quite tasty.  Service was good.  
Tried the beet salad, that was tasty.
Also had one of the duck sliders, it was good, but not as good as wild duck.
Ploughmans plate was good too

I saw Marlon Wayans here on 11/22. I paid $10 for a tiny glass of wine just for it to be served in a plastic cup. We waited a very long time for our food & it ended up coming towards the end of the show. I ordered a margarita next only because there is a two drink minimum. I never got the drink and received my bill before the drink! I reminded the server that we hadn't received our 2nd drinks and they still never came! The service here is extremely slow!

Perfect weekend getaway from L.A. or O.C.
My girlfriend insisted she brought the dog.
The Valet always has the finest cars up front 
Thank You
My first time eating Eritrean. I have had Ethiopian several times. This is very similar but still unique. Great food and great service. Very authentic. The injera was delightful. Highly recommend!

I'm glad I finally got to try their donut! I love a good cake donut and theirs were delicious. It was so fluffy and airy. You could tell how fresh they were. They also do have yeast donuts if that's what you prefer. 

My husband tried their mango fruit tea with lychee bobba and loved it. I tried their milk tea and it wasn't my favorite. I did come in expecting Taiwanese style bubble tea and theirs is Thai style. The straws they provide were not wide enough to get the bobba through which was unfortunate.

Such a cool and relaxing hidden little spot! The boyf and I randomly decided to check this place out and it has become our favorite getaway gem. So far we've tried their burgers, fish tacos, calamari, onion rings, micheladas and their margaritas. The food is surprisingly delicious and their outdoor seating area is the best part. Its not crowded and the beach is steps away. Love this place!!
Great food great price. I usually get the Chicken salad croissant, steak sandwich or reuben. Always delicious.

I had to choose between this place and another place and honestly only chose this one because of the design and atmosphere. Once I ordered and ate my food I was ECSTATIC with the choice. Delicious, fresh and fulfilling food. Happy I stumbled into this place and will definitely be back and recommend to my vegan and non-vegan friends :)
I thought this place was really cool and the food I had was good. But the hostess wasn't pleasant and glared at my kid through the meal. I was uncomfortable the whole time. Not good for kids.

After a day at the beach, the husband and I needed to refuel. Our search of  veggie burger and/or some non-meat options brought us to a strip mall eatery. 

Decked out in surf boards and all things Hawaiian, the menu options read burgers, kabobs, and plate lunch. 

We went w the fish (grilled red snappers). 

I agree with the other reviewers - good service; good service. This is somewhere we'd return for another meal when we're in the area.
How can you complain? The service was incredibly fast, it was literally an assembly line. Cheezewiz is a must, forget the other cheeses

The options and portions here leave little to be desired.  For the money, I can understand the reviews for this restaurant. Will definitely frequent this place again as the food is quality and the prices are below where they should be.  I can see how they would get very busy on the weekends so go early.

You must wear masks when entering the restaurant. There was absolutely, NO social distancing in the front as customers wait to be seated. But, at the dining area,it was social distancing. 

We wanted breakfast before I went to the airport, so we stopped here. 

The cooks all didn't wear masks, but the waitresses did. The one who prepared our breakfast was the one with the mask on. :-) 
 
Our waitress was Rose, and she was really nice and attentive. She took our orders, and made sure we had everything that we needed. 

The pancakes were cold, so we went them back. The rest of the food was ok, but I didn't eat all of mine. 

I ordered a steak and mushroom omelette, grits, and pancakes. They didn't have red potatoes and I don't like hash browns. My husband had a split decision. His food was delicious to him. 

We end up ordering for our grandkids, so we did a take out order. I dropped their food off to them, and I went straight to the airport. 

If I had to do it all over again, I doubt I will visit this ihop.

I would normally give Picasso's 5 stars.  I love this place.  It has great coffee drinks and eats.  It has a great vibe.  It's a nice place to sit, drink coffee, eat a bagel, and watch St Charles go by.  BUT.......the smoking right outside the door at the sidewalk tables is becoming intolerable.  I wish the owners would place small no smoking signs on the tables indicating the aroma of coffee and cigarettes and cigars do not mix.   Some guy just lit up a stogie at the table right beside me.  How rude.  I was forced to go inside.

Amazing food and service! Their tikka masala sauce was out of this world!! Their chicken tikka masala melts in your mouth! Our vegetarian daughter begrudgingly tried the sauce, and a wrestling match ensued from there until the bowl was clean.

The naan was good, the garlic naan even better!!

I appreciated the complimentary rice pudding to finish our meal-I can't stand rice pudding, except for theirs-WOW!

The rice is light and tender-we'll be back for sure!!

Positives: good food.  
Negatives: contrived theme bar vibe, password is a hassle, poor value.

The last time I was here I craved an old school gin & tonic.  The server mocked me for this simple drink request. Then she brought me something with cucumbers instead- it wasn't good. Thank you annoying server!

Blue Ocean Sushi is definitely THE BEST Japanese restaurant in the US. I moved to Los Angeles from Japan about 3 years ago, and I've been traveling and trying to find a superb Japanese restaurant that has the foods as good as the restaurants in Japan. It was Blue Ocean Sushi indeed, that brought me memories of my childhood in Japan. The ramens at Blue Ocean Sushi are super great. And the staff there, are really nice and sweet. If anyone has a chance to visit St. Louis I highly recommend Blue Ocean Sushi. As for the locals, you're very lucky to have Blue Ocean Sushi near by! 
If you think the sushi there is not good, then, you'd haven't tried real traditional sushi in Japan instead Americanized sushi.
Coco was an absolute angel & made the experience so much fun!!!! The shot/bomb choices were really cute & the atmosphere was amazing!

It's a decent place the last time I went during lunch. Service was good. Love the crab fries but the pork sandwich was dry. The time before that we got seated and no one waited on us for 20 minutes so we left. Overall food is decent. I like the mussels and their pepperoni pizza. Also I think their wings are good. The cheesesteaks are ok. Service is sometimes good sometimes slow.

Not sure why everyone hates this place so.


Each time, I go - although I average going once every couple of years - the food had improved.

The portions are BIG - take a look at the photos I posted.
The food itself is pretty good - not great, but what do you expect folks - it's just an average restaurant. 

Also - this place serves frozen cocktails - which is so hard to find. For that I gave it 4 stars despite the service which was very inefficient & disorganized.

Plus - it has an outside patio so you can people watch or motorcycle watch in the summer time.

So the 4 stars are for
1. Big portions
2. Frozen Drinks
3. Outside Patio

Relax & enjoy it for what it is in the hustle & bustle of South Street.

I've had pastries from this bakery before that were very good, so I decided to use them for large cannolis I wanted for a birthday party. I called and placed the order two days before I needed them & left my phone number. When I arrived to pick them up I was told they didn't have their large cannoli shells. I expected to pick up the order I placed, not be told after I walked in that they didn't have what I wanted! And not even a phone call to let me know, or to ask if I wanted  something else?? I ended up having to order the mini ones instead (I would have ordered cupcakes had I known earlier) because at least they wouldn't take long to make. Kind of a poor way to do business. The cannolis were good but I was left with a bad taste in my mouth, figuratively.

Terrible. We had reservations for a milestone birthday, but when we arrived we had to wait and then were seated way in the back of the courtyard, by the smokers exit. The food was okay, but not the quality we expected for the price. The steak was so tiny it couldn't even be classified as a petite filet. The service was not good. Our waiter was served our meal with a nice helping of attitude, and was even condescending to several members of our party. The best part of the dining experience was the stray cat that stopped by to visit, and the waiter promptly scared away. 

Our check was $100 more than it should have been and half of our party had to spend over an hour at the host stand with the manager to get it straighten out. The manager sealed the nail in the coffin of a night gone very wrong. Instead of apologizing and making it right, he argued with us until we finally got him to see what the mistake was. An apology was not offered. The worst part was I spent time away from my best friends birthday celebration.  Unacceptable. By the time we worked it out everyone was so upset it put a damper on the evening.  They never even wished my friend a happy birthday.  

Find elsewhere if you want a good dining experience.

Rollers is probably the most quaint little Chestnut Hill breakfast location. Probably the only one where you can get mimosas as well. 

A plus because at the end of the day it's yummy and people have been friendly to us. The location is cute enough and I'm glad we have it. Kind of similar to my other reviews of Chestnut Hill breakfast locations, there really isn't one that is a clear front runner. I mean that to say that no breakfast spot really does anything too special. 

You can expect normal sized portions at a slightly expensive price. I had bacon and eggs and my wife had French toast. We each had coffee and the price after an 18% tip was about $24. 

The location is small, it's laid out something like a long table against the wall. Not a good place if you want an intimate breakfast. 

That's a fair assessment I think. It's nothing too special, but not at all bad.
Amazing food! Chef and waitress are from Germany and make an authentic homemade German meal!! If you're in the Florida area and love Germany or America...GO!!!!!
Good fine dining food. But for the price, serving was small. Spring crab cake was very tasty. Filet au poivre was so tender and juicy. Chicken Paillard was flavorful. Definitely will come back.

This place was surprise - mostly for the food

I expected try to a couple new local beers (which we did).   They were fine, but nothing memorable.

However, the food was really memorable and good - full Hawaiian menu with a lot of unique offerings.
Great place. Very laid back. The boom boom shrimp  was great. Everyone loved their food. Our waitress was very helpful and attentive.

First, this review has nothing to do with their food, and everything to do with their service.   If you're like me, and would choose another place to have a pierogie based on service, then continue...

So...there is an annual hoagie fest in Port Richmond.  Let me describe this accurately...The line for a Pierogie was almost 1/4 mile long and they opened at 12pm.  It was super hot, sun beating down on everyone, and line moving at a snails pace.  They had 5 selections of Pierogis, 1 Kielbasa platter, and "wooder and soda".    The pierogi selection was sold out by 12:45pm.  The rest of their Pierogis (the main attraction) were sold out by 2:15pm.   I waited on line from 1:15pm.  Event hours are noon until 5pm.  

You would think they would tell people (who have been waiting over an hour on line...both hot and hungry) that they ran out of Pierogis, but no.  There was a sign up front when you get to their booth that they are sold out, however, that doesn't help when you can't see the sign from the herd of annoyed people waiting.

Total disappointment.  People were very upset that they waited a LONG time for the one thing they are "famous" for.   Wish they would have made an announcement after hearing constantly from upset people when they finally got to front of line.  

It's a Pierogie fest. Be prepared! They even said to me, "...You can go to their restaurant today (30 minutes away) if i wanted a pierogi....now why can't the restaurant bring the ingredients to the festival...there are 3 hours left?!?! 

Sweaty, hangry, confused, and annoyed.   If you want a great pierogi, try "Mom Moms Kitchen" in Port Richmond.   True neighborhood Pierogi heaven.  Ask for Serena, she was an excellent waitress.

The food here  is amazing..Helena and her team catered my wedding 5 months ago and ppl still talk about about the food and how delicious it was   !!!This place is a Hidden gem in stpete . I drive a good distance  just to eat here my favorite jamaican resturant.
Wanted to like this place, but the al pastor burrito was pretty bland. I'd go back and try their other stuff.

Living in/around NOLA for over a decade and just came here for the first time.  Just so you know the process, I used the top reviews to decide what to order--the Bananas Foster French Toast (sweet) and a Montana Plate (savory).

The Montana Plate is a nice portion of all your breakfast meats with 2 eggs to order, grits or home fries, and a biscuit with gravy.  The meats and eggs (over easy) were awesome, as were the home fries.  The biscuit and gravy were good, but not amazing.  I was hoping that there would be a little extra gravy for the meat and potatoes, but it was just enough for the biscuit, so ask for a little extra if that's what you have in mind, too.

The Bananas Foster French Toast, however, was incredible.  They split a baguette open length-wise, slather the inside with a cream cheese and banana concoction, then cut it into triangles, dip in egg batter, and fry it; served drizzled with a (rum?) caramel sauce worthy of the dish's name.  If you're on a low-carb or low-fat diet, this dish is your mortal enemy.

I will definitely return soon to try the Crab and Avocado Omlet (replacing the Montana Plate in my sweet and savory breakfast).  Update coming later in 2018!

I love the fact that this is not a chain restaurant and it is doing so well. The reason I am not giving it a higher rating is because I have had some sub-par experiences. The first time we went for a meal we hung out in the bar. It was not a busy day and the service was really bad. We had to go up to the bar and order our drinks after 10 minutes of waiting and watching 3 servers chat amongst each other. Food was not very good at this visit. (it was a 1 star visit for sure) that was about 9 months ago. 

I am so happy to report that things have changed a lot since that first visit.

I have met friends here for girls night 3 times since that first experience and the service has been great. The live music is pretty good and Fat Tire bier on draft makes me happy. The food is a step up from bar food, nothing fancy but I am not looking for fancy at a local pub. I have had to send food back for being prepared wrong, but the serves and owner went out of the way to make it right.
Like most people I am looking for a friendly environment close to home with good cold bier and decent eats at an affordable price. Georges meets all the above. Looking forward to spending some more time and giving an updated rating!!

Food was good but waited at least 10 minutes just a little surprised for fast food, when it's tacos. There were three staff members on break saying the F word multiple times as I sit with my kids then they are yelling talking to the girl behind the register as they sit in the last booth across the room. Last but not least they left drinks on the table when they were done, I'm guessing to claim the table for the rest of the evening.

Visiting Philly on a rainy day left me with not many options on the entertainment side, but when it came to lunch, I knew I was heading to Reading. When looking at the map I quickly headed to Fox & Son's for a taste of a child hood favorite. I purchased enough corn dogs and fries for a couple colleagues and I. The food looked great. Although expecting the same friers used to fry everything, it appears something was burnt prior to my order, or the oil hadn't been changed as everything tasted of a similar over done oil. I wanted to love this place, unfortunately we all decided to try something else for lunch.

I am a fan of Fuel. I really do love the options that offer healthy solutions while on the go or too busy to cook. I order from here a lot. However the last 2-3 times I have ordered salads and the sweet pea wonton, I have been disappointed. The salads are sparse and the amount of actual food in the container is SMALL for the price!  The same sadness happened with my sweet pea wontons. The amount of 'wontons' was so small, I had to use my own veggies to eat it. 4 pieces isn't an Oder. I do t have this problem dining in but only when I order take out. I am sad because I have been overlooking it since last summer but I think I am re-thinking ordering FRIM Fuel again. The food is always tasty but for the price, there should be more. I can go to Whole Foods and make a larger salad for less :-(. New option....

Well this isnt the first time I've been to this place and probably not my last.  I do frequent here alot of family birthdays and what nots.  This place probably is more known for the Bubble teas and smoothies.  Both which are very good, but the consistency has gone down for the fact they seem to hire different people to make them.  The last few times I've had it, which was yesterday, it was very watered down.  I had the peach w/conjack jelly and green tea.  The smoothies were up to par though.

As for the food here.  Its the typical chinese food, but not americanized.  Yes they have the General Tsao Chicken and chicken w/broccoli, but they also have frog legs!!!!  Actually its the whole frog and not just the legs.  Its batter and fried with garlic!  Yes it taste like chicken too! LOL!  The menu is self explanitory its in english.  So if you cant read chinese, dont worry they wont give you the chinese only menu lol!

The service is pleasant.  Also depends on who you get as the waiter/waitress.  Never really had a problem with any of them, but there is 1 with an attitude. 

They are open late till 3 am and also have karaoke rooms to reserve.  I believe they have 4 rooms.  Request the first one on the right, its got the best machine and system. Also the songs are current too!

Happy Eatings!!

Walking down Magazine Street in the early afternoon and realizing we were getting hungry, decided to stop in at Coquette. 

We were dressed very casual (shorts and t-shirts) which didn't seem to matter to them. Taking a seat at the bar, had the greatest conversation with the bartender and manager over the course of our meal. The soft shell crab was amazing as was the fried gulf shrimp. The greatest discovery?? The Jackson which is made with bacon bourbon and moonshine. OMG.... 

On the way out made reservations for the following evening which we were dressed much nicer and enjoyed table service upstairs this time. By luck, had the opportunity to briefly talk with Chef Michael who's passion certainly shows in his food. 

Cannot wait for my next trip to NoLa as Coquette will be on the list!!

An under appreciated gem. Do not go here for modern gourmet dining, this is comfort food perfected over decades of unwavering service to our community. Huge portions, simple delicious American Italian dishes, at very fair prices.  Service can be spot on or can be a hot mess, but if you're a regular you won't care, this is just an unpretentious, unassuming place to have a relaxing family friendly meal with all generations.
Food was great, pancakes were surpurb.  The staff was so sweet and accommodating, we loved the pace.  Our order was perfect and delivered in good time.  Woo hoo we have another breakfast place.

My son and I visited the food truck on Monday.  The employee who took our order was very friendly and helped us make selections.  The menu is quite large.  I had an Arizona burrito.  My son ordered a sope and a taco.  We shared rice and beans and both ordered an horchata.  The food came out quickly.  Everything was good and came in large portions.  I'd like to try dessert and some other menu options.  The only negative was spending $30 on "fast food."

I think the manager of this place deserves a shout out.  He is the nicest guy and always provides the most attentive customer service.  I like the food, especially the Russian sandwich with the coleslaw on top.  The soup is decent, too.  Hits the spot on a cold day.  But the guy, who I'm assuming is the manager, really goes out of his way for every customer.  I'm not really the type to enjoy small talk with strangers, but I enjoy coming in here because he has such a warm personality and could seriously brighten anyone's day.

Welcome to the new secret of Town N Country!

Now I am a bit upset that the fresh produce store and Cedar Lebanese is gone, but what has replaced it is great.

I've had issue with getting to Thai Gourmet Market because it closes at 8 pm. But now that I'm working from home, I can finally enjoy it for lunch or an early dinner. So on my first Friday on this new schedule, this was my first stop.

As I walked in, a bit late at 3, the staff was sitting down for their own lunch. However they quickly stopped everything to serve my needs. Just like Cedar's, the interior don't leave a lot of room, but there is enough for a few tables, a counter, and some additional chairs. The main hostess, as Lyman mentions is from Bangkok, was personable, friendly, and willing to explain everything, which I enjoyed.

So I got a whole table to myself, and looked over the small menu - which is the only reason this place gets 4.5 stars. Good news vegetarians and vegans - all the dishes come with a meat-free variant. On the menu was Basil, Pad Thai, Green Curry, Red Curry, and a few more specials of the day - a soup, a spicy pork dish which sounded really good, and a seabass dish.

I went with the Basil Prawns - which she mentioned is their most popular dish. Partially because I was the only one there at the time, the food came out in minutes with black rice. She explained that its just an organic rice, and I enjoyed the taste of it. On each table is the spice carafe, which I greatly enjoyed. The food tasted fresh, and there are signs that say no MSG, and she mentioned that there was no refined sugar in the Thai Iced Tea, only natural sugar. Score.

Before I left I ordered some dumplings - 4 for $5, and checked out the small market pantry. A few sauces, which good to know as I'll need to reup my Sriracha soon.
Had the worst experience EVER!! Asked to speak to a manger and she was so RUDE!! Lost a patron

Solid BBQ stop in St. Louis.  Made it by in the late afternoon and were sat outside on a nice day.  Service was attentive and the food was quite tasty.

The star of the meal actually came as an appetizer. The smothered fries were amazing. "Best cheese sauce ever" was among the comments at our table. We also gave the jalapeno cornbread a go, which was savory and complemented with a nice honey butter.  But, the fries... Mmm.

For the main course, we ended up splitting a three-meat plate with pulled pork, burnt ends, and meatloaf.  Now, I'm one to prefer my BBQ to taste good without sauce. I wish I could judge the burnt ends, but they were simply oversauced. Not that the sauce was bad, in fact the choices on the table were all good, but it was too much for me to offer a solid review on the burnt ends. Next time, I'll see about sauce on the side.

That said, the meatloaf (yes, meatloaf) was shockingly good.  Not a dish I would normally go for ahead of others at a BBQ place, but I took some Yelp advice and went for it.  Indeed, it was outstanding with a nice smoke flavor.  And, the pulled pork was good with any of the four sauce options available.  Overall, glad we made the stop for a very good meal.

NO meatballs in pho!? 

Good service but the food took a while to come out.

- Pho tai was excellent. A little bland but after I asked for the homemade xa te it made it a lot better! ( i need my meatballs though)
