- Eggrolls had a different twist! Chicken instead of ground beef? ANDDD BUTTON MUSHROOMS instead dried mushrooms? YUM!! ( i love mushrooms!!) Very delicious

- Pork springrolls........ BANGIN!

The front area has 2 Booths and lot of wasted space. No napkins on tables. Salt pepper n hit pepper all 1/4 filled not much attention to detail. Turkey club was ok. Said no mayo it had mayo, bread was stale.

After a long day of air travel I was ready to sink my teeth into something hearty but also fresh.  My steak gyro provided this.  This place is set up like a subway where you tell them what to load on.  I piled mine high with fresh cucumbers, greens, feta, olives, and tzatziki sauce. 

Sometime you need to eat alone because you make a huge mess. This was one of those times. I sat in the corner and enjoyed my food as it was falling  everywhere. The fries were also stellar. I didn't order them Greek style and was kicking myself about it later.

The bacon chicken burger was juicy and I especially liked the bacon being chopped so that I would enjoy bacon with every bite. The pickles were flavorful with a kick. I would definitely go again and also recommend the loaded baked potato salad.
Pretty tasty was satisfied was also told the Tequila & Margarita story by the bartender.

Oh man, I really wish that they give you a wife-beater shirt and a barefoot and pregnant wife upon entry, because that really would have rounded things out.

This place is a glorious dive--and they make no apologies for it.  That's exactly how you do it.

We were in town to do some research for an upcoming conference, and the concierge recommended we check this place out if we were looking for a greasy burger and PBR on tap.  She summed it up by saying it had the feeling of a trailer park parade.

The food is great.  I asked the cook what was good, and she gave the useless answer of, "Everything."  But you know what?  I think she was really just being honest.  The Patty Melt and Sweet Potato Fries were great!

The bar is great.  There are a ton of taps, and they will also make you a STRONG drink.  The price was right, too.  We actually came in on a 2-for-1 night as well as a $6 PBR pitcher.  So that meant that we got 2 pitchers for $6!  Awesome.

The bands we saw were great.  However, it bothered me how the crowd there didn't appreciate the way they were busting their ass to provide music.  I spoke with the lead singer later, and she told me that most musicians don't like playing that place because it's full of a bunch of college kids who come for the cheap drinks.  Kind of sucks for them...

So come on down.  Bring a Sharpie so that you can leave your mark somewhere.  AND BRING SOME CASH TO TIP THE BAND!  They are working hard and could use a few bucks.
$20 for two fish tacos and some rice, takeout. They were decent (and covered in cheese, which I've never had w fish tacos), but $20 is some bullsh*t. I've had three tacos better for half the price.
Food has gone down in taste and quality since they opened. There were Very few pieces of burnt ends in the chili. It was mostly water.and, prices are expensive.

This really is a special place and a gem. My wife and I discovered it yesterday for the first time and we were delighted with all aspects of service, food, and atmosphere. Please be  advised that although the food is Italian...it's more northern Italian. We could not find any dishes made with tomato sauce which some might expect to find at a more traditional Italian restaurant. Yes there is a pizza oven but it is for specialty pizzas. Most of the dishes are served over a bed of homemade pasta and with excellent presentation. 

Prices are reasonable, servings ample, and a great wine selection! Great place but don't go there expecting baked manicotti or other southern Italian pastas.

This review is based on atmosphere, service and drinks.  We did not eat, so I cannot speak for the food.  But I have heard the food is as good as you can get for bar food.  
Beer was cold, tv's were too many to count.  HOT servers and bartenders (just sayin'). Great service, manager was present and greeting tables, changing channels, talking to lots of guests.  Really great bar atmosphere.  If you want to watch a game or fight on a clean, fun local bar, THIS is the place!

Love Goodness!  I would go here more often if I lived closer.  Stopped in last week for perfect post-workout (to-go) goodies: Hot Tropic smoothie and bag of delicious granola.  I returned again...and typical me ordered the same items.  I need to return for an actual sit-down meal plus try out their infamous juices.  My only request...my Goodness, please extend your hours (5pm is too early for those who workout in evening)!

It wasn't that great of a scene on a Tuesday night but I bet this place gets wild. It has ample space to dance and get crazy and a dj booth just blasting bass pumped music. AND laser lights!!!!!! The bar is pretty long and on a Tuesday it was easy to get some drinks. The bartenders (men and woman) seemed friendly and were quick to get us some drinks. Unfortunately as I said it was a Tuesday and it wasn't that fun dancing among just a handful of people so I bailed early and went somewhere else just to chill. Still, when it's busy I can see this place being fun. If wild is your idea of fun.

Not great food but it's a great spot for after a game or concert.  No smoking.   Be aware they add gratuity.   My drunken friend tipped 50% even after I told him this.   Nice place to chill and people watch

The pizza here is very good, that's for sure. Huge, you ask? 18 inches is a big pizza. Is it expensive? Absolutely. Apparently you can buy it by the slice so maybe that'd be better. The first time I went here there was something funky with the beer so it was warm. Add the warm room and it's not a great mix, but in their defense it was hot and humid that day. It would have been nice had they somehow made the warm beer up to us but, alas, that did not happen. The second time it was taking a long time to get our food and it turned out the pizza sold per slice was somehow taking the entire oven and it pushed our pizza back, so it took a looong time. Then when it came out we were told it was because there were a lot of orders. They must have a lot of to go orders because there weren't many people there when we arrived. Either way it was too long for a pizza that expensive, especially considering it's not gormet food.

With an intimate, social atmosphere and an attentive staff (even on busy nights), The Bards is a comfortable place for drinks, small meals, and good times. Right after walking in, you're hit with the sports bar vibe almost immediately. Casual crowds in heated conversations or entranced by the many widescreen TVs playing a number of different games at any one time. The seating is comfortable (maybe not as much for the shorter crowd; a friend of mine had trouble getting on to a stool because everything seems extra elevated) and the place is always clean. In regards to pricing, it's all the usual fare with $4 to $6 drinks and the assortment of food like chicken fingers and such. My biggest complaint is that it doesn't seem suited for groups larger than 7. You'll find it hard getting everyone in the same area at a table without it being extra snug. Also, the establishment follows a narrow path so not much leg room on packed nights, so expect to bump into some patrons on your way to the bathroom.

Stopped into Nashville for a night and came here for breakfast.  Great atmosphere and amazing yet simple menu items.  I had a vanilla latte that was beautifully made and an everything bagel with bacon and cream cheese.  I'll definitely go back next time I'm in Nashville
I live next door, so I come here all the time. All of the cupcakes are good- you can't go wrong. But my favorite thing is the lemon bars.

3rd time at Rick's. Started with the celery slaw and it was excellent!  Went light this time and got the apple pecan salad with chicken. Very tasty and full of flavor. Another great outing in Meridian.

This is a small place with a clumsy indoor and outdoor atmosphere.Outside walkway to this place feels like you're walking through a gutter, full of trash. Coming to the food, Quantity is way much more for the price listed. But the quality of food is so poor that the meat is not properly cooked. I bought Lamb over rice this morning and found that the meat is not cooked and  tasted like beef instead of the one that i ordered (lamb). So tried calling the restaurant and inform them; so that no one had to go through the same experience like i did, but the one who received the call hardly understands English and did not understand my message to him. Feeling socially responsible made me walk to that place again and handing over the food bag to them , Finally I got my money back , but its a waste of my time and the experience made me not to eat at these sort of places anymore. God save Wilmington and Delaware.

Excellent little cafe with an amazing breakfast sandwich! Your know how sometimes when there is bacon on a sandwich you take a bite and the while piece comes out? Not here. The bacon seemed to melt. Add some of their zesty sriracha and YUM!!!  We also had their icegreen tea. It had a hint of some type of berry flavor and was great!  The staff was very friendly!

Went to iftaar there and the restaurant was considerate enough to put out punch, dates and pakora for all who were fasting Ramadan. Typical simple fair to eat and good. More like I would imagine Pakistani home cooking. Not too spicy and made fresh to order. Very friendly hostess and staff. Don't let the outside fool you (which is in need of a serious curb appeal makeover). Inside is swell.

This is the sushi place to visit in Reno! Great service and awesome rolls. It was quite busy but we had a chance to sit at the bar and have a refreshing cocktail. I had a savory margarita that was possibly the best I've had in years. I rarely order margaritas but I ordered a couple here and I'm very glad I did. 
When our area was ready we were sat at the sushi bar and our sushi adventure begun.
Our sushi chef Giovanni was spectacular. There were 4 in my party and we politely gave him our orders. He kept up with my hungry crew and we kept throwing back roll after roll. To our surprise our chef is still in high school but doesn't believe he is an expert. To us he was a Top Chef and we gave many accolades.

Came here for the first time with my friends and had the best food and best service! Matt and Oliver were outstanding and so personable. They made our day! We will definitely be back because of these two!! Our food was amazing and the restaurant is beautiful. 10/10 service!!

I'd like to start by saying, I'm from out of Province.  I was looking for a unique place to grab a coffee and some breakfast. Great little spot.  The atmosphere and esthetics are very lovely.  The roast beef sandwich was very delicious and I enjoyed my cup of coffee.  If I find myself back in Edmonton, I would definitely return.

Get the chocolate chip cookie cone! Mike's is especially great if you're wanting to experience Broadway, but aren't into visiting the bars. It has an old-fashioned vibe and so many classic flavors to choose from.

New Orleans needs more places like Vintage Garden Kitchen. Theres an ever growing need for dietary restrictions like Vegan and Gluten Free. This place covers both!  You can pop in for a smoothie and wrap at a reasonable price and leave feeling healthy and satisfied! They have a set up with an entire line of fresh vegetables and scrumptious house made toppings! If you're feeling like being a bit naughty after they also have some yummy house made treats! The salted caramel pecan bar, omg sweet sweet heavenly treat! The hummus is also to die for! I could go on and on about this place, but I'll stop myself here and leave you to it!

Found this place on a whim trying to find food that was open after 2. They had so many food options I was so happy because I was starving, so it all hit the spot!! We ordered mozzarella sticks, Mac and cheese bites, fried pickles, and garlic fries, all so tasty and just what we needed after a night on bourbon!!

We went here on our last night in NOLA, and it didn't disappoint. We tried the oysters, chargrilled, because we had had them like that at Felix's. They weren't as flavorful as the ones st Felix's, but still tasty. I had the gumbo, which was quite tasty. My sons had a shrimp poboy and an oyster poboy. The consensus was that the shrimp one was better. They were so stuffed full and overflowing with the good stuff, they had a hard time picking them up and eating them! The daughter had jambalaya and pronounced it delicious. I'd say give this place a try. Ask for Ty as your server. She was very sweet.
Went in and it was empty for a Saturday night...service was excellent and friendly...food came out quickly but the food was awful.  Won't be going back.

Love love love love love this place. They do everything right. Ambiance, decoration, class, food, drink, room choices, service, all of it. Very top notch. Been there a handful of times and they have always impressed. Be sure to try the squash puree soup.
This is a fun place .great steaks .great service (ask for perri).very reasonable .asked did I mention the bread? Awesome
I just went by this location this evening and it appears to of been closed... Everything is stripped to the walls

This is one of my favorite restaurants ever! The food is always wonderful here. I love the fact that on my first time here the owner came over and started chatting with me and my dining partner and ended up comping our drinks and dessert! The atmosphere is cool and how can you beat the make your own bloody mary bar on Sundays!!
Don't live in Philly any more, but I would go back to the Astral Plane everytime I visit.

Best BBQ in Edmonton. I find sometime the sides ar bbq joints tend to be bland but not here. Everything was so good. Ask for the sample platter so you get a bit of everything.
Service was excellent,  fast and friendly. The only suggestion I have is for them to buy some high chairs/booster chairs for us folk that can't get sitters. :) Can't wait to go back

We had a great lunch there today.  I had the chicken salad sandwich.  It was amazing!    The home fries were delicious with palmetto cheese.  Yum!  Would go back.  The staff was not very friendly thus the 4 stars.

The girl's meetup group I'm a party of decided on this spot for a Sunday brunch. While they don't take reservations, we knew we would have a large group and showed up ready to wait. 

12 ladies arrived, the owner (?) came out to greet us and give our large group some options for ordering to make it easy and keep everyone happy. She made it clear there would be no separate checks, but if we did a family style brunch they could split everything evenly. Perfect for all 12 of us. They sat us in one of the corners and out quickly came the food; big bowls filled with scrambled eggs, hashbrowns, sausage, bacon, grits, biscuits AND french toast (she overheard somebody say they were hoping for that). Not only were they overly acommodating with carafes of mimosas, coffee and waters they also added a small dish of hollandaise sauce!!! (I'm an Eggs Benedict fanatic)

Friendly staff/servers continuously checked on us and I've never seen such amazing service in any other restaurant. I look forward to tasing the entire menu on many many return visits & happy hours. 

Street parking in a little bit of a residental area. Uber/lyft if you're close enough!

Cute place and good idea but didn't get the hype. I love fries, all sort of fries but didn't get why this place was so highly rated as they don't make anything special. Their sauces are good, was not a big fan of the blueberry aioli (or ketchup? Can't remember).

Walked into the restaurant and there was live music.  We checked in and we were seated immediately,  by the window.  We were greeted by our server James, sans ink, was the spitting image of Adam Levine. He was extremely attentive, professional,  funny and knowledgeable.  Made our dining experience all that more special. We shared the shellfish tower,  which was fresh,  plentiful and delicious. I had the jumbo stuffed shrimp and my husband had the filet mignon and scallops, we shared the au gratin potatoes. We skipped dessert as we couldn't fit it.  We both had an amazingly fresh cup of coffee. We would recommend to try this restaurant and if we are back in Nashville, we will be visiting again!

Ok so I was here last week and gave them rave reviews. Just to make sure, I came back today and as I expect...... GRAND SLAM! You first walk in and think, hmmm easy dining area filled with customers seated at wooden tables & chairs. Looking at the food area, nothin fancy but here you actually get to see, pick n choose while looking at all the delicious items. 
Loads of vegetables to choose from, pork chops, fried chicken, pasta & more. Had a blast choosing my meat 'n three. We sat and as we were getting ready to dig in, one can't help but notice that so so many of the patrons know each other. Ya see.... that's what Franklin use to be; that down home feelin. 
That's what you get at Cool Cafe. You leave there with a full stomach and satisfied. As you start to leave, you can hear the staff sayin thanks and see you back! Ya know what..... they're right!!! 

Best meant n 3 anywhere!!!!

Will never be back to this place.  Family of 5 ate dinner.  Nothing spectacular.  Paid and left tip..  exited the building only to be followed by our waitress to our car demanding more money on her tip.  Where in America is 15% not enough?

Pissed us off to the point where we went back in to complain...  where the manager suddenly could not speak English.  Lucky for us....  my wife is Japanese.

Finally got a "gomenasai" from the guy claiming to be in charge.  Never got a return call from the real management though.

Many other places to visit and eat in Indianapolis without the complete disrespect we received from this dispicable establishment.

I wish you could give half stars on Yelp, because this restaurant is 3.5

This place is slllloooooowwwwwww to produce your entrees, even if you are one of three tables present, and even if you order something that is in a steam tray in the kitchen ready to go (tika masala or sag paneer).

Also, because it is a Suburban Indian restaurant, do not expect to have the same level of spice as in an Urban Indian Restaurant. Our food was sweet and savory, and could have used some heat.

I would actually go here again, but would request my items spicy next time.

The naan is a non-issue, and is none too bad . . . too bad there is no lunch special on weekends.

Popped in on Christiana mall  because we were craving pizza! Now the food on the website looked just like what we ordered and tasted as good as it looked minus a Lil salt which I need to watch anyway,  but the flavor was definitely the.  Rebecca was a great server and the manager was awesome thanks CPK.
Food was great and the delivery was prompt! Will be ordering from this place again--go check out my photos I attached. The Panang curry is just like I like it.

Went here on our way back frpom Florida. We'd been in the car for what seemed like a long time. Very hungry, very thirsty. First time in Nashville, concierge recommends this place because he thinks they will have music. One of our hoped for attributes.

Good news, they did. Heard a couple of good up and comers, including a fellow named Hunter Leath. Check him out.

Dinner was chicken fried waffles. First time for me so not sure how to compare it. But, the waffle was good. The fried chicken was good. I don't know about the combo, but either would have been good on it's own.

Place is cool, music stage is easy to see. Waitstaff was attentive and friendly.

Only been one time. First visit: liked all the healthy choices on the menu and decided on  vegan pho.
Service was a little slow for us and seemed especially slow for those sitting around us. Five stars because the staff was very kind and the outdoor seating was nice, too.

We stumbled upon this restaurant in its new location on Gay Street right after it opened. The menu, service, and food was just about as perfect as it could be.  The mussels in red sauce were unforgettable. The decor creates  a fresh, lovely atmosphere. I love having a good Italian alternative to the sardine-can crowded atmosphere at Limoncello's.
I order from here almost once a week. Only place to trust sushi in south Philly. Food is never a let down.
#TopNotch #GreatService and #FreshFood! Be sure to stop by and #EatLocal at this little #FamilyOwned #Restaurant! I'm looking forward to my next visit at this little #GoldMine! You will love it!

What a fantastic addition to our SB Funk Zone. This new beer garden space is  open to the elements, and with our beautiful weather it's a great space for dining and drinking with friends and family. And even on a cooler Sunday afternoon, the fire barrels generated some nice heat for all.

First of all, the Valet Parking makes it very convenient, which got us on to the queue all the more quickly. Wait didn't take very long, and we did get to enjoy some Ale before heading to our table.

Once seated we were greeted by server Sylvia, who was gracious and helpful, and made all of our Biergarten wishes come true. Can't wait to be back there soon.

At a comfy outdoor table we all enjoyed delicious Ales and Lagers, which paired well with the delicious Pizzas, Bratwursts, Pretzels, and yes, even a Schnitzel Poutine. 

Favorite of the day for me was the sweet and delicious Mother Earth Cali Creamin' Ale, followed closely by the Stone Buenaveza Lager.

This new beer garden is located in the historic SB Funk Zone building that also houses Love Worn, Skyenna Wine Lounge, Shine Up Men's Wear, and Lighthouse Skateboards. And also right across the street from Kunin Wines, Brass Bear, Corks and Crowns, and beside Flor de Maiz and Oku Sushi.

My friends and I stumbled upon the Clover Grill while walking on Bourbon from the Blacksmith bar a few blocks away. We decided to head here the following day for lunch.

The burgers and fries were great. The meal was much needed after a late night with many drinks. The food hit the spot! Some of my friends went back there 2/3 times during the trip 3 day trip.

The place can be a bit dirty (floors, counters, table tops) and can take a while to be seated. We had to wait about 15-20 minutes to get seated. There aren't many tables to sit at or space at the counter. The check took awhile to get to us after we finished eating. 

Don't expect great service, but you'll come away with a pretty good burger and that's what we were looking for!

Went to this donair shop thinking I would have a delicious donair, was I ever wrong! Awful meat, soggy pita, vegetables that looked like they fell on the floor, cheese tasted like plastic! As someone whose eaten at over 30 donair shops in Alberta this was hands down the worst! Fast forward 3 months and I'm willing to give them another shot as bad experiences are sometimes not the norm. Anyway I order through skip the dishes and 90 minutes later driver calls and tells me owner gave him 10 bucks to not deliver order because it's late and they are cleaning up kitchen and order was processed but unfortunately my food will not be delivered. People take your money and run, Swiss donair is the best alternative

This is usually a 4-star place for me, but today, u only get a 3! Came for late lunch (approx 2:50p) after my dr appt. Entree dishes were old, dried out or empty. Had to wait 45 min for the fresh fried calamari to be restocked....worth the wait tho! I love this place coz I can sit, read, eat w/o being bothered....free wifi too!
Brilliant! Incredibly fresh bread, unique sandwiches, gracious hospitality. Try the goat cheese, bacon and cucumber on a brioche bun!

I remember seeing this place on TV so I wanted to give it a try.

I got the roast pork and broccoli rabe sandwich. The roast pork was juicy and moist and the broccoli rabe gave it a nice contrast of a slight bitterness to the sandwich. I wish the sandwich had some kind of sauce to make the roast pork more tastier. The pork itself was a little on the bland side. And if the rabe was more mixed it with the sandwich, that would have made it taste better too.

Really fun concept - a bar with old video games. I was psyched to play T3 and other games. I was thrilled to find the prices were still the original ones. 
It was a bit crowded when we got there, but for the most part you could just wait a few minutes to get to any game you wanted to play. A few times people would plunk down a few dollars worth of coins and "claim" a game for way too long, but that wasn't the norm.
The pluses - no pressure to drink. I actually manged to sober up a bit here after Frankford Hall, so that was nice. Great assortment of games. A layout that actually made walking around the games doable. 
No so great - they don't take quarters, just tokens. This means, if you buy tokens you can only spend them there. 
Bad - A few of the games had broken controllers and no sign indicating that. Kind of sucks to pop in .50 to find you can't actually play. This was more than one game. 
I like that this is something different. If it was more crowded I could picture it not being fun, but for what it was (old video games in a bar), I had a great time.

Black Bear Diner is quickly becoming one of the local favorites among friends and foodies alike. The food is good and served in big portions with the exception of the baskets. I had chicken fingers and fries it was pretty average. I have also had breakfast here. The hash brown portions are extra large. I did prefer the breakfast over the basket. This place has been open just short of a couple months so like any new restaurant in town it is frequently busy. This being said while the wait staff is friendly when they get busy the kitchen can get backed up. First time I was here I  walked in at 5pm on a Friday. It was very busy and did take 20 minutes after we ordered to get our food. I do think it was good and worth the wait I just think they are still working out the kinks among the kitchen and staff members. You can watch this all unfold if you are seated near the kitchen. The decor is cute as they have wooden bear carvings throughout. We will be back again soon!

Came in here because my mouth won't open passed a dime... wrong place for that. Ordered a gnar burrito. Poured pepper plant hot sauce all over it. Now I got split lip and flaming mouth.

Just kidding. I love this place and their food. Custom order a sandwich or pick something off the menu. These guys are local and when you pick certain food they don't some of the proceeds to a local charity. 

By far my fave is their breakfast anything. You cannot go wrong.

I was far away from home in New Orleans, pulling license plates off my totaled car after having dealt with a food-poisoned boyfriend from 4-10 AM when I left for work, so generally having a crap day, figured I'd get us some pho while I was in New Orleans East.

There are no vegetarian or pescatarian soups, my only option as a non-meat eater was a grilled shrimp bun. Kind of bummed me out, but whatever, as long as there's something I can eat. Ordered that and a brisket pho for Sir Pukes-a-Lot. Minimal atmosphere and all that in the actual restaurant, but you're getting Vietnamese in the East for the food itself, not for the decor.

The manager ran my food over to me when it was ready, as I had taken a seat at a table, I said thanks and left, drove 30 minutes back to NOLA, and goddammit, my food wasn't in the bag. I hadn't eaten since the day prior, as I left my own job early and without shift meal to pull my plates off my car before the lot closed. I was somewhat irate, so I called the business in hopes that they would rectify it in some way, as it's frustrating to hand someone $10 to NOT give me the food I ordered.

The only thing they offered in response to their error was that they would "remember me" when I came in next. I explained that I lived 30 minutes away and have NO REASON to be in New Orleans East, not to mention that I'm car-less for the moment being. I'm not going to drive an HOUR within the next week or so to get stupid bun. I asked them to send me something in the mail that I could present the next time I was over there, as I anticipated it being within like, six months, but not soon enough where they would "remember" me. I have a dumb facial piercing, but I don't have a tattoo of an orca whale on my forehead or anything. I certainly wouldn't remember me. I asked to speak to a manager and was denied that? Really shoddy customer service after having acknowledged that "the manager forgot to run [me] the rest of the food." In retrospect, I should have asked them to write down my name and I could present an ID upon my next visit, but I doubt they would have cooperated with this idea either.

Boyfriend said pho was "okay."

I have had some inconsistent experiences, but overall I would say the meals are pretty worth it here. Steaks and seafood are what I usually stick to, but I have had the brunch also and it was a nice treat!

Just had their dim sum this weekend.  There are alot of components which makes this place the best in Philly for Dim Sum.   Again, let's do the good and the ek.. I've had better. 
Chicken Feet:  Very nice flavor.  Deep Fried just enough to make it the perfect texture.  Just enough Hoisin to make a very good sauce.  Wish it had less red coloring.  You know you put too much coloring when the chicken bone is red too...) 
Chiu Chow Fun Gor:  Very nice mix of pork, water chestnut, dried shrimp in a nicely wrapped rice paper.  Great flavor. 
Steam Chicken and Cha Siu Buns:  Perfectly steamed and very soft. Bun had just enough sweetness to compliment the chicken and BBQ pork flavor!  
Ha Gow (Steamed Shrimp Dumpling): Wrapped very nice and I tasted hints of bamboo shoot and water chestnuts.  Perfect filling along with Shrimp.
Siu Mai:  Put too much dried mushrooms.  As a matter of fact, why so traditional?  Just pork, pork fat, shrimp and binding agent like egg white and cornstarch.  That's all someone needs.  
They have other items that we see in NY's chinatown and Hong Kong.  Overrall, a nice gem off of Race Street!

not very impressed. Italian restaurant without a good selection of soup!!!  Only one type and it has ham. When I got to select a drink, they did not offer any flavored iced tea. Just regular iced tea.
The Lombardo salad is not that impressive either. Too much cheese. They put the whole salad in a small plate and every time I touched it, the cheese fell all over the table.
Waiting for my Fettucini Primavera. I will write another review for that after I finish.

Worst place to get a steak! Went there last night for my mom's birthday. Wait staff is terrible! I asked my waiter for my steak to be medium rare and my steak fries well done extra crispy. I get my food and my steak was well done and he gave me extra order of fries that are crispy. I know this place was a dump when I walked in but I figured the food would be good. Was I wrong! I knew it was gonna go south when I asked for a Coke and he said we have RC. By the way, my soda was flat as well. Don't waste your time! They ruined my mom's birthday last night!!!

I went here last Saturday for lunch because I was in the area and had always wanted to try it. Granted my expectations weren't that high, but I thought over all it was kind of underwhelming. The decor was really tacky, like early 90s tacky; the view from the patio of the river is nice though.  Pretty standard menu: fish, fried food, burgers, etc.  Only thing was for a place called the lobster trap there was a noticeable lack of lobster dishes on the menu, with whole lobster and lobster ravioli being the only items I noticed.  Kind of hoped for like a lobster roll, but I went with the ravioli, which tasted ok but looked a mess.  Chowder I had beforehand was good.  Service was fine, could have been a little more attentive. All in all, not bad but not good. Better than red lobster, but not by much.

Not sure what all the fuss is about. We both got the large chili cheese dog. The dog and bun were good. The chili left something to be desired. My onion rings were very good, but I think the french fries might have been from yesterday. The fries sucked. I'd eat here again, but only when it's not packed. Which it wasn't tonight, but still took too long. Lots of people standing around.
Excellent pizza, comfy chairs and great view. Top it off with Beignets for a perfect evening.

I don't often venture to South Reno but we were in the area and decided to give it a try.

The first time I came was for the very first official  Yelp Event in Reno. Our esteemed CM (Michael T) hosted a meet and greet with drinks and appetizers. I was very impressed by the food, the Margarita, and the overall ambiance of the restaurant. 

My husband and I came back for lunch to make use of the the gift certificate I had received at the Yelp Event. 

We were greeted warmly and were seated right away. Our drink orders were taken (no Margaritas for lunch) and we were given time to review the menu.  Chips and salsa were brought and are included in the meal. 

My husband had the Chimichanga with shredded beef and I had the two cheese and chicken enchiladas. (entrees were $10.99 each). Both meals were very good and generous portions. The ingredients are fresh and it was a nice balance of meat and cheese and vegetables. The enchilada sauce was just spicy enough to make it interesting, but did not overwhelm the mild cheese and shredded chicken filling. Great guacamole was served on the side. The beans were OK and I am not a huge Mexican rice fan, but the bite I had was good. 

Overall, it is a solid restaurant that consistently serves good quality meals made from fresh ingredients. It will most definitely be a repeat visit when we are in that part of town.

The bar food at Cajun Mike's is better than the gourmet version in other cities.  It is close to the Quarter without all the terrible things that means.  It looks and smells just like a bar should.  I recommend the burgers, the oyster po boys, the onion rings, and whatever I get next week because that will be good too.

Best food and service ever. I ordered the duck which was served with sweet potato polenta and Brussels sprouts and a southern comfort glaze. Best duck I have ever had. My husband had red snapper that was served with baby Swiss chard in a lemon reduction. We had started off with turtle soup and creole shrimp tomato soup and finished with bananas foster. The offerings were not only different than the usual restaurant fair, but excellently executed. The servers work as teams delivering each course simultaneously to all of your party. Water was refreshed constantly and wine poured as needed. Just impeccable. We sat in the upstairs room overlooking the trees with little white lights twinkling around the windows. A magical ambience. We will return each time we visit.

Loved this place totally completed me lovely stay in St Pete Beach....heard their Ukranian Violin player from my balcony across the street and was drawn in like a mosquito to a light trap...they pulled me in but did not disappoint...One man who I forget his name was insanely nice to me and the food was SPECTACULOUR literally amazing....I am leaving St Pete Beach tomorrow with a weary heart because I met some truly amazing ppl here.....
Good place to go for happy hour - prices and selection are decent. Service is always nice, but slow. Their lobster bisque is damn good.
The salads are amazing and flavor! The three cheese flat bread was yummy and flesh, will definitely recommend!

So, I'm trying to taste all the cheesesteaks in Philly! These were pretty good, but not the best. I thought it was funny that they put the cheese on the bottom, under the meat. The bread got soggier quicker, and I just think the bite would have been better if the meat was all cheesey. The block was very unique - it had a strong provolone cheese flavor, and the mushrooms were extra flavorful. Couldn't decide if it was very good or just ok though!

By far the slowest fast food restaurant experience I have ever had. I couldn't even get mad about it - I truly felt sorry for the employees. The manager was lost and just stood with his back to the customers, looking haplessly at the order screen. I wanted to jump behind the counter and give directions, as nobody seemed to know what what was going on.

Great service, great food, so so drinks.  I suggest you try the pears and prosciutto appetizer, incredible. 

Prices are a bit high but worth it.

Amazing food, try the paso style bacon and eggs! It's like a wish wrapped in a promise wearing a dirty vest. Ericka was not only kind but promised me her first born if the food sucked. No child this year grandma, sorry. @italianjapanese

Who knew a bar could do vegan so well. The only reason to hold back a five star rating is so I can ensure I get a table in the future. The attractive wait staff were impeccable throughout service. Recommend to order about 2-3 dishes per person to start, unless you're very hungry. Very Reasonably priced beers, and the cocktails were pretty good. The vibe is energetic and plays on the old saloon theme in a classy way. They def could use some sound dampening panels. Hard to talk across the table.
Best chicken tenders in town...hands down. Great beer selection too.

My husband and I went to Delosa's because our wait for the other restaruants was too long. Even though the place is perfect for people watching, we found the food to be awful. There were flies buzzing all over the restaurant and the top of the napkin holder was dirty. The slice of pizza that my husband orderd looked like a flat piece of cardboard. We both thought that the restaurant might be serving up pizzas that were frozen. The chicken parmesan sandwich that I ordered had a very small bun, and a small chicken breast that was soaked through with sauce. When I was eating at this place, all I could think of was Gordon Ramsay. Neither my husband and I could believe how poor the quality of food was.

The image I'd conjured was of the quaint location in the Heights being duplicated in the Burg as the new name suggested. Sure I could have the same great food here, but I wasn't sure yet what the draw was, where was the individuality? Well, this place turned out to be expansive in more ways than one! Hidden behind two large doors in some unassuming step down in the middle of dt I almost walked right by. I could see the staff bustling about in the kitchen below from the street and found my way in. Walking into those two tall doors you seem to forget where you are until you resurface on the city streets above years later all satiated. I was fueled by drinks that were a tour for the eyes and the taste buds. They each took a turn as a topic of conversation. The food is consistent, and still kills it. (as a GF foodie the octopus is my personal fav) The rooms take turns evolving from darlingly garish to quirky vintage décor. The dj booth, selfie corner, and the intricacies of the entire Station House allll the way up were THE experience. I hate to kill your discovery of the hidden flavors in the drinks offered, so I can't go into too much detail, but I couldn't try them all, and I didn't get close. Worth the trip? I'll be taking my ass across the Frankland again real soon. It's too much for just one night. Hey, is that a real bird in there? You tell me, I swear it just twitched.

Best tzatziki sauce on the planet .
Everything tastes fresh, with wonderful flavor.
The baklava is crisp and fresh, not gummy like at some other places.

Best pizza in Metairie. Sauce tastes great, toppings always fresh, perfect crust. Barq's in a bottle always a plus. My only complaint is the lack of parking. A few times I've wanted to stop but couldn't find  anywhere to park so I kept going. If they delivered , I'd order prob once a week.
Good COLOMBIAN food.  Sancocho! Need I say more?
The tri-tip noodle soup was 10/10. Would definitely recommend on a cold day. Staff is friendly and chill.

I like the inside/ outside bar seating at Noble. They have a decent beer list, only 2 on draft however, good cocktails and the food was good. I had a veggie burger served with beets and fries that was good. The chickpea fries were sopped in oil however.

Definitely different food from what I'm used to, but I was very pleased with the consistent service and great quality. Only complain I had was when I ordered beef and broccoli, it was a 5:1 ratio of broccoli to beef, but hey, vegetables are good... so I guess that's a win right there! I'll definitely come back to try some currys too! Recommend!

We had heard a lot about this restaurant and decided to try it.  The cheeseburger and fries were as good as you get. The fries were hot and crisp.  It was obvious the meat was hand patted and not a frozen patty. Our server  was Joyce and she was attentive plus quick to get our drinks of sweet tea and our order. I had the Blackberry Wine cake which I have never eaten and it was a fantastic dessert and very moist. We will definitely go back..

It looks like a great sports bar but doesn't taste like one. Service was excellent food was not, wings were tough, so that means they are old, freezer burned or cooked right out of the freezer in other words not fresh. BBQ sauce tasted like straight out of a open pit or Gordon Food Service container and not even evenly distributed among 10 wings. BW3 is much better than this, taste and wings. Fries were meh, I do better fries out of a frozen bag from the grocery store, would give this another try but no wings, too depressing to have bad wings, I made better wings last Thursday at home.

Good stuff. A little pricey but for tasty vegan Mexican fare I am down with it. I had the enchiladas; 1 spinach and nut  and 1 mushroom. Tasty but small.Great guacamole and tasty beans. My wife loved the chicken flauntas. Very nice help but I cannot stand the old smell of the place.
I still like the old one better,  the food is still the same, somethings are new like cotton candy! I want to say I  liked it darker it was more of a jungle, prices went up too!

I grabbed lunch here with a friend and it was pretty good. Staff is friendly and service was good. The food wasn't very memorable but it wasn't bad either. My friend and i got the same vegetables and mine tasted terrible and fishy even though she was the one that ordered fish. Our waitress took too long to come back though so I just ate my sandwich and had no side. I would go back again but it's not my first choice. 1 star for the employees, 1 star for the atmosphere/view and a star for the rest of the food.

Just went there for lunch today and really liked it. Extremely inexpensive and the lunch menu is out of control!! There must be at least 50 items on there.

I had the lunch pollo crema with rice and refried beans, and it was delish! 

The decor is really cute, especially the painted booths and chairs. 

The servers were nice and attentive. I will be going back again ... looking forward to sampling more of the menu!
Conveniently on the way home, good food, SUPER great service by Chayse, who ROCKED it!  Small wait to get in around the lunch hour, well worth the stop!  Thanks Chayse and supporting cast!

I ordered from DoorDash Food was old dry and cold. I should have learned from my last order but used to love mamas so much but it has definitely went down hill. This was the last time I will purchase the food is overpriced and dry everytime I ordered

Excellent drinks, food, and service. Our waitress Morgan was great. There's a little bit of everything for everyone here, and though I'm not vegetarian or vegan, I enjoyed the different kinds of burgers they have. I recommend the hummus, particularly the rotating special hummus. I'll be back for that in particular. Parking in this part of town is a little difficult, but that is to be expected. Definitely a cool, chill place to be.

This is the worst drive thru service ever.  My husband was in line for 45 minutes.  We have received incorrect orders more than once.  Don't know who runs this store but they should be they should be fired
Imma keep this short and simple. There is no other spicy chicken sandwich. Popeyes who?

My friend and I went to a late afternoon lunch on 6/23 and I can't come up with enough good things to say about our experience.

Eating out is always a challenge as I have two severe food allergies.  When I mentioned it to our server (Jessica C.) to inquire about the ingredients in a few items, she immediately noted my allergies on our ticket and offered to double check with the kitchen to ensure she was 100% correct on how each of those dishes were prepared.  She also went to speak to her manager (Thomas) to see what modifications were able to be made to accommodate my allergy.  Thomas personally came over to clarify what I wanted and let me know exactly how they could adjust the two dishes about which I had inquired. He also let me know about possible issues with the sides and offered up options.

Both Jessica and Thomas were extremely friendly, helpful, and willing to adapt several meals for me without hesitation.  The meal I did get (lemon parmesean shrimp) was outstanding!!

I truly appreciate the integrity and attitude of Jessica and Thomas.  Take note other dining establishments:  THIS. IS. HOW. EXCELLENCE. IS. DONE.

My husband and I went here this morning (5/23/21) for breakfast and had a rather poor experience due to our server. We are both vegan and are fully aware that many places cannot accommodate to our diet. However, the Yelp page states that there are vegan options and we ordered the one that was apparent on the menu (an avocado and tomato dish). I asked if there were other vegan side options, specifically if the hash brows could be made vegan, and he told me they are made with butter and then told me "good luck finding vegan options, you are in the south after all". A valid statement but the snark with which he said it was pretty off putting (not to mention there are multiple all vegan restaurants in NOLA, we were just out and about before any of them opened). We received our food and a few bites into mine I bit into something greasy and fried (in an all raw dish). After we received our check and paid, our server then said to us "sorry we didn't have your necessities" once again in a very snarky tone. My husband and I sat there for a minute stunned thinking "what the fuck did we do"?!, and we then left with a bad taste in our mouths, figuratively, but also literally in my case due to the mystery grease ball hidden in my food.

Nice view of the water & boats from the outside deck seating. Our server, Laura, was very accommodating and quick. We enjoyed our seafood dishes. I had the grilled shrimp with rice & beans, shared a clam chowder bowl, & also shared a half dozen of oysters. I also tried the seafood gumbo, which has lots of different seafood in it, & is less stewy than it is soupy. The bisque was extremely thick & almost had a "out of the can" taste to it, although my dad loved it. 
They give everyone hush puppies to start while you wait for your food.
The atmosphere is very casual & nautical themed. We got seated right away on a Sunday around 2 PM. 
Prices are average, at about $10-$15 on average per plate.
They don't have many vegetarian options, so my mom ended up breaking her diet to get seafood.
Excellent quality, taste and service. We stop in here every time we travel to Nashville. Staff is friendly and food is awesome. 5 stars!!
Terrible service....  Never again.  4 other couple left with the same experience.  Ehhh. Disappointed

Very disappointed with the Pineville Tavern.  The waitress, Kim, acted like she was doing a favor serving us.  The tuna was dry and the snapper soup thick and lumpy.  The most pleasant staff was the valet, working in 19* weather and the helpful, friendly bus boy.  We can't remember when we have had such poor service.

Came here for lunch, some of the worst service I have ever had, the Chicago thick pizza was served with undercooked dough while everything on top was burnt to hell. The sausages were burnt to hardened discs, spinach was oily and overcooked. We started with a short rack of boneless wings that came with an order of 5 wings for over 8 dollars?! The wings were bland and tasted like frozen grocery store Tyson wings. Awful portion sizes for the prices and quality of food. Would not recommend!

Sure...its loud in here, but it is because everybody is having fun.  Start at the bar while you are waiting for a table and enjoy a beer or cocktail while the friendly staff takes care of you.  Then, at your table, the chill staff will explain all of the unusual delights the chefs have in store for you.  Experiment with your order and you will be happy.  We ordered from the many tapas selections and got more than we needed and everything was nicely prepared and thrilled our taste buds.  Don't be in a hurry, but the tastes are worth the wait.

The food was great!!! It was a nice quiet jewel in metairie. The only thing i didn't care for was a server having an issue with his table, yelling at them and using profanity, telling them to eat elsewhere. There were little kids in the restaurant, and no one from the staff stepped in to at least pull him to the back. Other than that incident everything was great.

I have been drug into this place many times and they never disappoint.  They are always slow regardless of when youre in there, the fries are almost always soggy regardless of the type, and the burger is nothing special except for its price (high).  Most of the burgers I have tried were also very salty.  It is the type of place I bring out of state friends to because it is unique in its multiple potato  choices.

Food was excellent! Visited with my wife and children. Everyone's food was absolutely delicious. 

We were saddened that the service did not match the food. Our server was less rude to us as the table next to us. We came in at 3pm on a Saturday when the kitchen was about to close. The server was open and obvious as to her irritation that the table next to us was taking so long to order. The attitude, eye rolling, and overall unpleasant demeanor. 

We will certainly return to try out other meals, as ours were fabulous. We hope the service will be better and/or with another server.
If you care at all about your cleanliness just don't stay at a casino. It is so disgusting. Hair all over the bathroom and the shower curtain was so nasty. I could barely stay here for one night.

This is by far my favorite breakfast place! I love the banana bread French toast. I like to upgrade the breakfast platter so I have eggs, bacon and sausage. You can't beat this savory and sweet option. They definitely give you large portions and always offer great service. They have lots of locations around Indy!
Best Pizza in the area. Owners are great people. Very friendly and accommodating to all customers.

I was seriously disappointed in this place. I went in and ordered an açaí bowl but informed them i had a banana allergy and needed to make sure there was no banana in my bowl and they said they were "unable to make it with no banana," and proceeded to watch me leave without ordering a thing. I've had açaí at multiple places with no banana & they always inform me it takes longer to make but they'll do it, safe to say i won't waste my time at soho again.
we love this place. the food is consistently good. the service is always great too. the parking lot is sketchy but the mall is kept up nicely. i drive an hour one way just to eat here..
Food was solid. Very very slow though. Service was strange and made me feel uncomfortable.

We moved here 3 years ago and have never made our way here.... big mistake! The environment is fun and inviting, the staff was very nice and helpful... the food... spectacular! Authentic LA cuisine and so many good options to choose from. Can't wait to go back for dinner, as our last lunch was on the lighter side.

Door dash driver.  This is one of my favorite restaurants to pick up from.  There are times when they get slammed with orders and you might have to wait but they are always respectful and courteous.  Most of the times the order is ready quickly.

This was my daughter's choice for my 1st meal out in Philly and I'm glad she took me here. No waiting and a table by the window made for a great start as we were starving that morning. 

We shared the pork belly benedict with rosemary potatoes and Snickers brioche French toast. We wanted to start with something savory and end it with something sweet.

There were 2 large chunks of pork belly next to the eggs which was perfect for sharing. A very rich dish that we both enjoyed. We love pork belly so we're not put off alt all by it's richness along with the creamy hollandaise sauce. Who knew it would go so well together? 

The giant portion of French toast made us smile as it was beautifully presented and just so delicious. Loved the topping of honeyed mascarpone cheese, chocolate ganache and caramel sauce. We didn't finish this dish as it was gigantic. Took a couple of bites and it was just perfect to end our meal. 

Service was friendly and attentive. I also thought that it was a great deal for the amount of food that we had. It does get loud in there, but we had no issues where we sat. I will definitely be back on my next visit.

After reading the reviews here and subsequently going to Culver's on Thornydale for an early lunch with my husband and a college buddy, I am less than impressed. I had a burger for lunch yesterday, so I wasn't really in the mood for a burger, but all the reviews say the burgers are what you get here, and that's what I did. I hadn't seen my friend in some time, and this is the place he recommended, so this is where we went! The menu is overwhelming, which in itself made me just want to go somewhere else. Having TOO many options is not always a good thing for a food place. I got the mushroom swiss butterburger and my husband got the sourdough melt. We got the cheese curds as well. I'm not quite sure how a melt or something called a "butterburger" can be bland, but my husband and I both had to shake salt on our flavorless, paper-thin patties. The buns were pretty tasty. I have nothing to go on when it comes to the cheese curds, as I have never been to Wisconsin and I am unfamiliar, but they were alright for chunks of cheese that are battered and fried. As a cheese curd noob, I would describe them like mini-mozzarella sticks with no sauce. Nothing to write home about. The boys opted out of custard and there were too many options for me to decide, so I opted for no custard at all. Oh, note to others, everyone says that two patties are standard at this place and a single is a special order. That is no longer the case. Most likely to cut on costs in this economy (just a guess) all of the burgers are featured with single and double prices on the menu. If I do go again, I'll try just the custard. As far as the non-dessert food goes, though, I'll skip this place and head to In-N-Out next time I want fast food burgers.

I've lived in the south for many years and I put hot sauce on everything. Let's just say I like hot food.  I like some heat in my food but when you go here to Bolton's; when they say "hot chicken", they mean it.  Your lips will be burning, your tongue will be on fire and don't even think about touching your eyes or nose or anything else sensitive. Even if you think you are pretty tough when it comes to spicy food just be careful because you are going to get what you ask for.  Good food slow service kind of divey but legit.

I liked Cafe Du Monde better, even though Morning Call has been around for a long time as well. 

However, since it is located in the City Park, I can see why this can be a great break. The beignet sizes were not as consistent, and contrary to the belief that they are bigger than Cafe Du Monde, they are not. They are extremely generous with the powdered sugar if you get a to-go order.  I had half a cup left of sugar in the bag! The Cafe au Lait was good and consistent. 

The service was really rushed and not as friendly as our service as Cafe Du Monde which had a more chill vibe. As others mentioned, they seemed quite stressed there. Perhaps we just came at a busy time!

We went there last night for my fiancé's birthday. The  food was OKAY. The truffle fries and paella were awesome. However some of the other tapas were simply average. The service was adequate. Server was not that very attentive or warm. This is my second time here. I don't think I will be dying to return for a third.
Came here after a day of day drinking and had the beat dawg ever! So many different options of meat and toppings. Definitely check this place out if you're looking for some drunk foods
AMAZING! Not your typical greasy spoon. Attention to detail.... The atmosphere is great food is excellent.

I called two days prior to order a cake for my daughter's Confirmation luncheon.  Not only did Lochel's accommodate me but the cake was beautifully decorated (and tasted just as good).  I have been to this shop multiple times for cupcakes and other desserts and I can say that everything is so delicious.  Highly recommend!!!

Went to Atchafalaya while I was visiting a friend who recently moved to New Orleans.  He was told that it is a must go to restuarant so we did. I was visiting from Los Angeles and I was treated like a celebrity when Tony, the owner found that that I was visiting.  He sat at our table and jazzed up our night.  He hosted our dinner...described the food in detail, introduced us to some Louisiana cocktails, and invited us back for sunday brunch.  He made us feel at home and made the concept of "southern hospitality" come to life.  The food was scrumptuous, the service impeccable,  and the ambience was warm and exciting, not to mention the beautiful patrons and attractive staff.  On a final note about the food....the chef was able to transform their grits into a veritable gourmet delicacy that rivals the best pasta or risotto anywhere.  We will return.

I am a native Tampanian and have lived here all of my life. I've had some really good cuban sandwiches and some bad ones in my lifetime but this place had the worst Ive ever had. It was so dry, I had to look to see if it even had any mayo and mustard. I only tasted one pickel and after paying $8.14 for that crap, I expected it to be really good, especially being that it was located in Ybor City and the reputation it had in the past. 
I planned on taking their takeout menu back to my job, so others could have a variety to choose from but the only place their menu is going is in the garbage.
So, I hope they dont enter any cuban sandwich competitions any time soon, cause they need to go back to the drawing board.

We really like Rumba, the pineapple chicken is delicious as well as the citrus half chicken. I have ordered the half chicken a couple times and once I got a tiny "half" that wasn't a true half as I had got before on prior visits. 2-4-1 drinks all day, try the libation. Those little cornbread muffins are basically crack, so go ahead and order a half dozen of those too.... and a shrimp bisque. You can thank me later. Local spot for stone crab, and it's delicious. Served hot or cold (I recommend the cold), precracked, and with mustard sauce. If you go before 5pm (could be 6?) they offer a early bird menu is like half the price I believe.

Always top notch food and service!

We typically start out with the tableside chips and guac because its an absolute must!! Then my hubby and I will split 2 entrees so we get to try different foods. I haven't had anything that wasn't delicious on the menu and we've gone here more than 15-20 times. 

My kids love their food but especially love the tableside S'mores. I was really impressed with the wine list and the fact that the markup was within reason as some restaurants tend to overcharge on some of the common wines.

Overall we are still happy to have this close by so we can continue to go back!

If you haven't tried this place you must! I've been a fan since going to a Duck Donuts in the Outer Banks, NC years ago. I was happy to see one open close to home. They make the donuts while you wait and with the freshest toppings right after you order. You can make your own or pick from popular donuts on their menu. Everyone there is very friendly and very helpful. Check this place out!

Ugh, as I sit here and write this I am currently in I-hate-myself-so-full status. I left work for an early lunch today, as I didn't have any breakfast. As I drove by this section of town -- initially wanting a sandwich and then...oh hey, Sushi! -- I realized how early it was and that all the yummy-looking places were closed; most of which don't open until about 11am. Typical.

Aldertos is not, however. They open up at 7am, which is perfect, as I was starving. So, I use the drive-thru and am greeted quickly with a gentleman on the inter-com. I vaguely remember someone mentioning the carne asada fries (known as the Super Fries here), but I didn't want to hate myself THAT much, so I opted for a taco de carne and a breakfast burrito with carne asada and eggs. I tried the burrito first and it was immediately transparent that this place does NOT skimp out on the carne -- it was full with, what I would presume, was a 1:1 ratio of meat to egg. There was some cheese coagulated on one side of the burrito which kind of made me raise an eyebrow, but it was delicious and just enough cheese to not ruin each bite.

I will say, however, that I'm generally (see: try to be) a clean-ish eater, but I'm not hardcore watching my salt intake and this burrito tasted quite salty to me. I think for a breakfast burrito, they should just cut back on the salt, as it would be much better with less or it omitted completely -- I rather just have salsa for more flavoring if need-be.

The tacos are also FULL. They're a bit Tijuana-style with larger corn tortillas that they double and pack full of the meat, cilantro and quac. Folding the tortillas over almost caused a massive over-flow.

When I arrived at the window, the gentleman asked if I wanted any salsa, so I asked, "Do you have any hot salsa?". I think he looked at me like "Pinche quera. jaja" as if I was asking for just any hot sauce. No, I meant, do you have HOT salsa -- like make my nose run, man! What he gave me was some salsa de verde that wasn't that hot; I mean it had a kick, but I'm pretty sure Taco Bell's Diablo sauce has it beat in spiciness. I got my food in record time, but I wouldn't have expected any less with how early it was (10am, give or take) and the fact that I was the one and only customer.

Overall, it's pretty good authentic Mexican food, but the salt kind of ruined it for me. However, the service and expense for what was received was definitely 5/5 stars.
Delicious food! The service here is great and the atmosphere is awesome. If you have not had one of their bowls, you are missing out.

I meet clients around Oliver and this Brewsters is about the same as the others. Food is decent and service is generally prompt during the day.

It's not 5 star dining but that's not what it tries to be.  They have a good selection of unique beers that are exclusive to Brewsters (well they brew it themselves).

My second time at this place and I just love the Food and drinks!!! Couldn't get a table so ended up sitting at the bar. The 2 ladies at the bar are so energetic, and lovely and fun!!! I thoroughly enjoyed my dinner sitting at the bar. Michelada drink was very nice and so was Triple Spicy Margarita. The huge Nacho mountain full of cheese, beans, salsa and jalapeño was perfect with the drinks. Chips are very fresh and not so oily. Currently have special tacos on the menu..(testing a few new tacos and the best one gets on the Menu permanently). I tried the Fish & Chips (beer battered cod fish, potato shoestring fries) the combination was awesome. Fish was really good. Definitely needed some hot sauce with it as it was too dry by itself. Overall great place. I like their patio style seating at the end of the restaurant.
Kyu-don and other rice bowl are as authentic as it could be. Wish they have ramen but I am happy to settle on udon.
A great neighborhood sports bar.  They have full-liquor, craft beers, great food and they show all of the games!
Food is good. IPAs are good. Thats why you came on yelp, in telling you to eat and drink here. It's delicious.

Still good.  Still on the high side for "burger and fries", but the quality makes it worth the price.  A "regular" hamburger here is a double-patty.  And is big. If you want a single patty hamburger, get the "little" version.  No charge for any toppings, including sauteed mushrooms.

Stopped in here for the first time after a visit to the hospital. The guy running the counter owner was very nice but I was a little disappointed in the food. The lamb gyro seriously only had like one layer of lamb a little skimpy for the price and a small bag and chips and a small drink for three extra dollars? I don't feel like it was a good value . Good flavor- will I be back? probably not

The Mister and I have been to Cloud 9 twice now and both times have been very impressed by their wonderful small batch beers, fresh seasonal menu, and friendly service.  
The brewery and pub are both located in the same small space in a north end strip-mall; which is the rare combination of being both car friendly, with ample parking, and bike/pedestrian friendly with bike racks and well maintained sidewalks that lead into one of Boise's most sought after historic neighborhoods.  There is limited seating in the venue itself, this is a "nanopub" after all, with a handful of tables and bar stools.  Yet if the weather is nice they have additional seating on the "patio" which is basically the partially covered deep sidewalk out front.
Cloud 9 is a certified organic brewery and tries to source all of their ingredients locally whenever possible.  The menu reflects this desire to remain organic and local by changing often to serve what is seasonal and available.  So far I've sampled the Beet Salad, Street Tacos, Blue Cheese Fries, and Mac & Cheese and everything has been excellent.   As far as beer goes I haven't had anything I didn't like, but my two favorites were the Lemon Ginger Wheat (summer in a glass) and the Salted Caramel Stout (the perfect dessert).  
As this is a relatively new establishment I went in ready for spotty service, as I always think new restaurants need a couple months learning curve to get fully in the swing of things, but I was pleasantly surprised both times.  The service was excellent, efficient and friendly, and our food and drinks came out quickly.  
All in all this is a great local nanopub and we will definitely be going back.

I go here all the time for the eel and the squid! Best nigiri in town, and the Agedashi tofu is amazing also. Only reason I didn't give it five stars is that one of the owners is pretty rude, and almost seems dismissive of customers... I just keep tipping high in hopes of softening her heart because I don't claim to know her tragic backstory : /  great sushi though!
I love going here. They have great beers on tap and the people are awesome! Also, did I mention the food is delicious too?! If you are ever in Pottstown, stop by and check out this place!

This review is only based off our brunch meal. Husband and I walked over the bridge for an anniversary brunch. We had always heard great things about HLD but have never gotten the chance to check it out. We waited for about 20 minutes before we were seated, as it was packed for the Labour Day brunch rush. The brunch menu is quite small. I ordered the classic benedict with roasted potatoes. Hubby ordered the farmer's omelette with multigrain toast, and we ordered one of their legendary cinnamon buns to share (sidenote: Edmontonians really have a thing for cinnamon buns. And green onion pancakes. As a Vancouverite I always found this amusing). 

The food took awhile to come but service was otherwise efficient. Our waters were refilled throughout the meal. The benedict was all right, nothing special. I did like the back bacon, and the roasted potatoes were good with the home-made ketchup, but aside from this, there was nothing that particularly stood out about our meal. My husband was less impressed unfortunately. He wasn't a fan of his farmer's omelette and didn't even finish it; however he did compliment the multigrain toast. The cinnamon bun was all right too. But again, nothing to write home about. I was a bit disappointed because we had always heard about High Level's brunch and while there was nothing bad about it, I've had better in the city.

My go to when I forget to bring lunch or when I'm craving something out of the normal routine. Anyways this is probably the healthiest option on campus, it is about time there is higher quality dining outlet. They have avocado, Dutch crunch bread, and delicious soups which is why they receive a 5 star from me.

Sigh. 

I had a Groupon that was getting close to its expiration date so on a Saturday night the boyfriend and I made the trip to the Piazza. The place was packed, as expected. A Phillies game was on, it was warm out, so we knew what we were in for. Sort of. (Okay so admittedly, this experience is my fault for waiting until the last minute.) 

"How long is the wait for two people?"
"Oh, about an hour to an hour and a half."

LOLWUT.

Fine, we put our names on the list, thinking "There is no way on earth it would actually take that long!" 

Flash-forward to an hour and a half later: boyfriend's cell phone rings. It's PYT, asking if we're ready to be seated. We got up from one of the public tables and raced to the restaurant.

After we were seated inside we were a little pissed to see how many open tables there were - I guess instead of accommodating the many, many (oh, you know, two pages) of two-person parties, PYT was keeping its (empty) four- and six-top tables intact, I suppose should the need for such a large group arise.

Anyway, waitress was friendly and the food came out pretty quickly. The Philly Cheesesteak Pretzel Burger is good and I tried the Lobster Burger. Sounds a little strange but it is the bomb. The fries were done well.

Don't ever call in and order. A few weeks back I order a few things from Coplands, when I got there the order was completely wrong. Now I just tried giving them another chance by ordering again today. When I got there they couldn't find my order at all. Whoever I talked to on the phone didn't put my order in. I've also gone to a different Coplands before in Kenner and my waiter was absolutely rude. I'm tired of giving them chances, for a restaurant that claims to be "fancy 5 star" They slack very hard.

After standing at the counter going through the menu, you will probably find yourself overwhelmed with delicious Venezuelan food options. You will want to try everything and will be indecisive. Not a problem... do what my hubby & I did and get the Sampler plate. This is more than enough food for two, and it's only about $16. The food is awesome. There wasn't a single item that I didn't like. Also, the woman working the counter was telling us about the Venezuelan tamales in plantain leaves, and now I have to make a return trip just to try those, because they sound fantastic.
Wow. Rum, coffee, baguettes, pastries, and soooo much space. I'm going to be here a lot.

Amazing!!! I love this place the food is delicious and the owner is a delight, very kind,  very helpful. I look forward to eating here once a month for the food and for the amazing service and desert balls / bobas/ vindilu / tiki masala / rice PUDDING

The stars remain the same, but there is a dish worth mentioning:

PORK BELLY BENEDICT. Now this is pork belly done right: thick cubes of pork belly, smoked with maple, appropriately seasoned with salt and pepper...kind of like Korean BBQ pork belly. If you are a true pork belly fan, you must get this!

I would've bumped up one star just on the pork belly alone, but the Chicken and Waffles Benedict was horrible. Small pieces of fried chicken that wasn't even crispy. No thanks.

The Red Velvet Pancakes are huge like everyone mentioned, but it wasn't too sweet and the chocolate morsels were just enough and not overwhelming.

Mmmmmmmmmm!! El Gato Negro never fails me! The only thing I wish they had was their own parking lot. We drove around for at least 20 mins looking for a spot to park on a Friday night - it was worth every drop of that $4/gallon gas! Once again, I ordered my fish tacos with all the fixings. The seasoning they use is incredible! It's so flavorful and the fish was nice and flaky! J ordered the chicken fajitas and he loved them. Every time you check in here they give you a top shelf marg for 7.75, you can't beat that!!

Was hesitant to pull into this place at first because my husband and I have this silly criteria that reviews on Yelp must meet the criteria of at least 4 stars but with at least 100 reviews. This only had 27 reviews at the time, but was the only place for a quick stop in a hurry. 

Well, it's our 2nd visit in 2 days and we might be back for a 3rd before we leave this afternoon from a travel softball tournament at Carneys Point Recreation Center. If you need a quick bite between games for some amazing deli food and Italian favorites, this is a go to must!  If we are ever in the area, we will definitely be back!

I'm actually not from Tucson, I'm from the Phoenix area but really wanted to try some local restaurants while I was in town for the day. So I yelped it up and came across the Drunken Chicken. Obviously, you say 'Chicken and Waffles' and your girl is there! I bookmarked this place before I left and could not wait to get there. I love the location... I would say it gives me vibes of Tempe's Mill Ave. I know I'm boring you already, so to make a long story short. This place would probably be amazing to someone who's not very familiar with chicken and waffles, and maybe to someone who's not obsessed with fried chicken and fried chicken recipes! I would say this place is very OKAY... the waitress was awesome, but my chicken was a tad bit overcooked and my waffle cold and somewhat dry. To give them credit, their spicy  recipe really is spicy! I like the infused syrups, in which I tried the jalapeno and the rosemary flavors. After I was done eating, I felt a little bit amazed by the almost five-star Yelp review. I might have caught them at a bad time (Wednesday around 3pm), but I highly doubt I'll spend $13 again to find out if I misjudged or not.

This is a quaint neighborhood restaurant with an excellent drink selection. The staff are attentive and friendly. We love the cornbread appetizer. Unfortunately our dinner review was mixed. I got a dinner serving of the shrimp and grits appetizer (5 shrimp instead of 4). It was the best shrimp and grits I've had in several years. I can't say enough good things about it. The blackened, head-on shrimp was flavorful all on its on. The cheese grits, sofrito and lime crema complimented the shrimp without overwhelming them. On the other hand my dinner companion got the Jimmy Burger and was really disappointed. She asked for a single patty (ground chuck) because she thought two would be too much. While the burger has a good crust and flavor it was too dry. The skinny fries were tasty but cooled really quickly. 

We looked at the menu but decided we were too full to enjoy it. The table next to us told us to skip the chocolate cheese cake with coconut panne cotta. They said the flavor was good but it was dry. They recommended the Clementine's ice cream instead.

We left another establishment for having terrible food and service and came here for something light. It BLEW MY MIND. Definitely a Madeira Beach/ John's Pass hidden treasure. 
Our server (I have since forgot her name) was incredible, attentive, personable, and quick. 
The fries (the only thing we got besides beers) came out immediately and they were piping hot and delicious; the best I've ever had. The beers were cold, delicious, and they have a great variety of local craft brews along with domestic options. They also had quiet, ambient outside seating overlooking the water. 
Thank you for showing us what a place that cares about their food and local customers that also appeals to tourists. I can't wait to make this a frequent place for a laid back date night all the time. 
Thank you again!
Have always enjoyed breakfast here.  Pre-breakfast muffins are delicious with butter.  Really good pancakes and toast.  Eggs over medium always come out great.  Love sitting on their patio

You know you're in a classy location when you're flanked by both a Church's and a Lee's.  

It took forever to get our order.

It wasn't that cheap.

The fried shrimp wasn't that great either.  They should consider brining it or something because it had a slight mediciny taste.

The fried whiting was only ok.  I was hoping this place would be like Seaboat in Champaign, IL.

Again, another place that was almost Vess exclusive.  I was amused by that.

There was this dude with a portable DVD player selling bootleg DVDs.  Classy.

Love the bowls here. Brunch has a lot of egg bowls that are basically scrambled eggs, potatoes, and different add ins. Basic but delicious. Dinner bowls are where it gets more creative with lots of options for bowls and wraps. I highly recommend the fried artichoke appetizer.

They also have a bunch of handmade drinks that are awesome - agua frescas and teas.
Fantastic and personable bartenders and great food that doesn't leave you feeling gross or heavy

I'm reluctant to give even ONE star. Never staffed properly; I suppose that's why the service is so bad. Watered down drinks - you're safest ordering bottled beer. I can't prove it but I'm pretty certain they swapped out requested top shelf brands for well brands...or it may be our waiter really was that bad. The food is uninspired - heavy typical carb-heavy sports bar fare. I appreciate that they are trying to bring In live music but whomever is booking has no clue on how to promote that it or how to book the right bands for the clientele. Please get some solid advice before this place closes down.

6/11/2011 Update
--------------------------
To Pi's credit, after my initial review (see below), they reached out to me and actively investigated the issue and sent me a gift card. Good to see that they care and tried to address the situation rather than ignoring it.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Despite service issues on a previous visit my wife and I took a leap of faith and decided to give the Pi in CWE another shot. Bad idea!

So we sit at the bar for an hour and parties coming in well after us are getting seated while our pager refuses to go off. Finally, after reminding the hostesses of our presence we get seated only to find our server is AWOL.

The meal itself was OK but the coup de grace came today with the credit card statement - the bartender decided she deserved a larger tip than I had given her.

Never again!
