They also have 4 sauces on the table for people to use, a regular BBQ sauce, a mustard sauce, a hot and tangy sauce and their version of their hottest sauce which a lot of people said wasn't very spicy. There is actually a 5th sauce, their very own White BBQ sauce which was a favorite of my wife's, its tangy with vinegar and lemon. The service here was very welcoming and helpful. Their recommendations were of course the St. Louis ribs, the brisket and pulled pork. Their side recommendations are the white mac and cheese, herbed fries and their beans. 

My wife and I decided to share the Bestie 3 choice, we chose the ribs, brisket and pulled pork with our sides being herbed fries and the white mac and cheese. 

So first the meats, the ribs were of course fall of the bone good. Juicy and the sauces they provide just enhance the flavor but honestly you could eat the ribs on their own without any problems, the rub they use have plenty of flavor. The brisket was very juicy and tender and probably my favorite piece out of the three. The pulled pork was also tender and had a great flavor, a bit more salt than I would have liked but still good nonetheless. 

The herbed fries may look burnt but man they are far from it. It was cooked just right with it being crispy but still soft on the inside. Now personally I don't like mac and cheese at all, that is my wife's dish. But their creamy white mac and cheese was great. It was creamy and the noodles were cooked perfectly. They also sprinkled bread crumbs on the entire thing to make it taste that much better!

One of my favorites! Not surprised at all they have hour plus wait times!

Have fun everyone and eat well!

Friends brought us here to celebrate a special occasion.  We were in the back room because of a music group performing in the front. 
I ordered lamb chops. O M Goodness!!! They were out of this world!!! In the center of the plate was a heaping helping of homemade mashed potatoes. The service was great and I can't wait to go back   My friend had the Bronzino and it was beautiful. Highly recommendLava

Taiwan Tea House is my favorite place for Asian cuisine on the north side of Indy.  It's small, family-owned establishment with a wide variety of teas and a simple food menu.  The entrees are all roughly the same - Broccoli, onions, carrots with your choice of meat:  Chicken, shrimp, or pork.  The only thing different is the sauce that they top it with.  For example, they have  Orange, Sweet n Sour, General Tso's, Oyster sauce etc.  They have about 16 different sauces and you can get several of them spicy or non-spicy.  You get a ball of white rice and two crab rangoons as well as a bowl of soup. The soup is rotating - the only thing they seem to have in common is tofu.  I've had the turnip and miso soups and both were fantastic.  The crab rangoons are perfect. Small, crunchy, and the cheese/meat combo is just the right amount to not make it overwhelming. Not usually a big fan of crab rangoons but the Tea House's are wonderful.   My favorite part about the Tea House is the fact that even though many of the dishes are your traditional Chinese-American dishes,  the vegetables taste fresh, the sauces are a lighter and unique take on their more common counterparts, and the meat isn't heavily breaded/fried/greasy like most other places.  Everything actually tastes fresh, light, homemade and is probably far healthier than the Chinese food you're more accustomed to. They were closed for a few months due to a horrible family tragedy but now that they've reopened, I highly recommend giving it a shot.  The owner is super nice and she remembers faces.  Just one more thing that makes the Tea House a pleasant little spot to eat at.

FYI, they used to be closed on Mondays (don't think their hours have changed since they've reopened) and they do close for holidays so call ahead if you're going out of your way to try it on a day that typical businesses are closed.
Food is always fresh, hot and delicious. My children love the quesadillas and I'm a fan of the chicken fajitas.

Visit: 1/25/10 - Dinner.  Mongolian beef and kung pao chicken.

I just wanted rice after a week long rice shortage in tahoe.  These dishes suprised me.  I was expecting terrible food, but got good food.  Rice is cooked well, portions were hugh.  The kung pao chicken was definately our favorite.

Service was good.

Price was okay.

I would come back.
Went to a wedding rehearsal dinner here. Sarah was awesome and made up for lack of customer service from the bartender Michael. Great atmosphere.

I've been here twice now for lunch and it's really great. Coal-fired Pizza ovens definitely to a great job on the crust and having a buffet that comes with a salad and fountain drink for $12 is a great value. They display six or seven different styles and the wait staff is attractive, friendly and attentive.
Super cute atmosphere, very friendly staff, and quick service! First gumbo experience and it didn't disappoint! Crab cakes were delicious too!

Every time I've walked by, I've always felt "Tourist trap, don't do it" - Not sure why today was different. I mean Mexican food in SB is a dime a dozen and more often than not - the really "trendy" places are a raging disappointment.

The hostess mentioned that if we were cold to let her know and they'd be happy to turn the heaters on (it's in the 70's today but the section we were in was kinda drafty) and she even offered to hold our stroller for us.

Aliex is literally hands down one of the top 5 best servers I've had in SB. He was super attentive, great energy and kind. You can tell that he's passionate about what he does and truly enjoys it. He should give server training to literally every establishment in SB. The food could have been garbage and I'd still be stoked to have been there.

The food is NOT garbage btw - it was surprisingly different and tasty. I'm pretty confident that the steak for their nachos is braised in unicorn magic. It was unbelievably tender and flavorful and NOT salty (something hard to come by in SB).The burritos are incredibly large - I mean - enough to feed 2-3 people probably. He was also really nice about our odd food requests (usually servers get super annoyed - but it's hard to get kids to try something new).

The bussers were friendly - attentive and sincere. This was absolutely not the norm for SB. So glad we stopped in. Can't wait to go back again.
Great tasting food with a very affordable price. As a Peruvian myself i highly recommend meanchi's

This had to be the worst place for music and or a dessert.  My friend and I walked in because it was close to our hotel and ordered drinks and dessert. Well we listened to mediocre music and paid 50 dollars for the worst dessert and a cover charge we weren't informed of. The funniest thing was the two employees walking up and down working the crowd, urging us to clap constantly. We left and found Frenchmen Street. No cover charges and the best damn music in one music venue after another. Just go to Frenchmen street if you want good music

I have been here on multiple occasions and every time, I have to wait at least 30 minutes for a dang pizza! Though it is good pizza, it's not AMAZING and not worth the wait. There are plenty of other pizza places I would rather go in Boise that have quicker service and tastier pie. However, one of the quirks I do like about this place is when they put your name or a specific group on the board and it's your day to make a free pizza. If my name is ever on the board, that will probably be the only time I will come back.

Renovation tried but failed. Customer service total failure, if you need something plan on asking 4 or 5 times or just plan on not getting it. Definitely not enforcing COVID safety. Rooms by street (all of them) are noisy. Dog poop stains on carpet. Woof.

I ordered delivery as I was staying at a hotel near Tampa International. They delivery timely however forget one of my meals. Which took another 45 minutes. The manager offered a free dessert for the trouble. So nice right?!?! Well when the rest of my dinner was delivered, they forgot my free dessert. Wasn't worth the wait! Don't bother ordering from this place.

We have eaten here 3 times in the last year. We share a large Pho, beef, round steak and a bon vermicelli salad while there. Pho is doctor it your way and between the condiments and the garnish provided we love it. For $7.95 the Pho is a nice value. This was our first salad and we enjoyed it, pork was tasty. Then we take the Korean beef tacos and the BBQ pork bhan mi which we love. We have always had prompt and friendly service.

Horrible service! The bartender (Brent) was rude. I've been here quite a few times in the past, but never again. This place has gone way downhill....I'd review the food, but we got up and left before Brent had time to take our order. I guess we should have waited about half an hour.

Food was good.
Service was good.
I thought it was a little pricy for breakfast.
The ice tea was NOT fresh brewed, that's disappointing. 
Think about it would you serve instant coffee??

Ate here many times when in town for a conference. Short walk from the Marriott and much better food and prices. Fun happy hour specials and really fast service. Lots of business people go here for lunch and it is packed during that time but they still get your food out quick!

Dont understand the hype about this place. The beet salad was primarily bitter endives than beet. The farm board was nothing special . The zeppoles basic fried dough. The only redeeming dish was the lamb meatballs. Will never return

Excellent!!! Reading the menu, I thought it was just another overpriced fancy Mexican adaptation similar to Tacolicious in San Francisco: a good, but horrendously overpriced spot. 

We followed the locals advice and tried it out. 

Funky taco was nothing like the trendy overpriced spot in SF. Tacos here were super delish... generous portions, and simply to die for. 

I can especially recommend the Piggy Stardust and Macho tacos

Not that good. Came here with a friend and the pho was lukewarm. Pho should be piping hot! Lukewarm broth seems to be an issue with every Miss Saigon location I've been to. They also don't give enough bean sprouts and charge for any extras. You can get an entire bag of bean sprouts for $1 at the store. It's not like I'm asking for something expensive. Ridiculous. I've never had a pho restaurant in Cali charge for extra sprouts, not that I've ever even had to ask because they give you four times more at a cheaper price.

First impressions are lasting impressions. One and done for me. The customer service was not the best especially the bartender with the pink hair. She didn't bother to ask if we needed a refill or anything else besides what we ordered the entire time we sat at the bar. The burgers were good but was expecting much more. Also, the owner im assuming made his way to speak to everyone in the establishment which was not many but the only black couple in the spot..it was so obvious....but none the less I will keep going to Lakeview Harbor or my beloved Velvet Cactus....the bartenders rock over there!!!! Nice new spot but it won't last long in lakeview.

Fried shrimp, Halibut, raw oysters, garlic fries and clam chowder bowls! It was delicious. We came here during Covid. Seats were spaced apart and there was outdoor seating. We had dinner here and came back the next day to have breakfast which was fried shrimp and the halibut. The fries were so good too.

We heard rave reviews of this place and checked it out tonight! They ran out of one of their subjis so we only got the dhal, eggplant, rice, roti, raitha (they had vegan raitha for me!), and something like kheer. It was all pretty bland, but did taste homemade. I would come here again only if I wanted something less spicy and had an upset stomach  They also overcharge like crazy. Don't think they charged us less despite running out of food.

Great value, two piece dark chicken. Long line for Sunday lunch with some rain.  Took 50 from getting in line to getting food.

Food was worth the wait. Cole slaw and yummy baked beans w bacon bit. Slaw needed dash of salt and had some big thick pieces. I got medium chicken (level 3 of 5), goes from Non spicy to hottest Shut the Cluck Up. 

Didn't eat the bread that soaks up chicken oil. Medium was the right amount of spicy. Chicken was juicy and cooked perfectly! Fries were great, spicy but kinda salty. Ours were served at room temp. They kindly gave us fresh batch. 

Have sweet and brewed tea. Unlimited. Great friendly, customer service. Clean place, tvs showing sports. Big parking lot

There is a separate to go line 
And make sure you try the banana pudding!! Can taste the freshness and perfect ratio of pudding, banana and Nilla wafers. Also have peach cobbler t-shirts, hats and cups for sale. Black and red Jersey tees are cute, so soft, $25. Available online too

I first stayed here a year ago, and have now been back this year.  Both times it was for a conference that was held in the hotel.  The hotel is very nice.  It is up to date, clean, nicely laid out, and well situated in New Orleans.  Generally speaking, the food at the hotel is very good as well, although one meal this week of fish, had left far too many bones in it.

I recently went to Paris and did not buy one macaron while I was there because I knew I had Nathaniel Reid when I returned home! So glad we went here before Paris.  It was great preparation for our many Boulangerie stops.  Not a lie!  I can't say enough about anything you buy here.  The quiches, the sandwiches, the bread, but the brownies were an unexpected GUILTY pleasure.  However, I'm partial to French citron desserts and NR doesn't disappoint.  I seriously crave NR.  I wish we had one in Edwardsville (hint).  Worth the drive.  Get there early to snag a breakfast  sandwich.

When I first moved to the area everyone recommend this place so I tried it and was SO VERY DISAPPOINTED.  The food just had no flavor.  I tried it a second time in case the first visit had been a fluke but it was just as bad the second time.

Great vegan place with awesome vibe. Got the tofu tacos, chorizo mac and cheese, seitan steak and potatoes, hot chicken sandwich, and loaded potatoes. Highly recommend loaded potatoes as they were some of the most delicious we've ever had. Hot chicken was juicy and soft tempeh with a good spice kick, and tarragon chickpea salad was a tasty side! Seitan steak was good but pretty salty for our taste. Shout out to our waitress Anne who was super friendly and helpful! Thanks Graze for ending our trip to Nashville with a cool & creative meal.

Food was excellent, service sub-par.  The waitress was non-apologetic for the slow service, forgotten item and drinks that took 20 minutes to receive.  The host was great and responsive, but given the great food you can find elsewhere in New Orleans, I wouldn't return.

I have been eating at Delco's since it operated under a previous name -- LaSpadas.

These are the best cheesesteaks in Pinellas County--bar none.  If you really want Philly authentic, go with the cheese whiz, but they will make it however you want it.  The steak is great and the rolls are awesome.  You won't be disappointed if you know what a steak is supposed to be...

My tip -- bring cash because they don't take credit/debit cards.

Definitely a 5-star in my book!

The food here is great. We started with a 3 choice ceviche dish, and all 3 were amazing. We then had the marlin tacos and the sugarcane tuna. Both fantastic as well. 
The only thing that was disappointing was the noise level and the seating. It's more of a bar scene/noise level than an actual restaurant which is tolerable but be prepared. They are also not normal tables/chairs, kind of awkward but tolerable as well. 
The food makes up for any issues you may have there!

This new restaurant is in a great place and the decor and atmosphere  good. BUT if this place is supposed to be all about the wines, why don't they tell you more about them on the menu (i.e., region and not just country of origin) and have staff that know something about wine? As a previous reviewer said, the wines are common big names and it really is the starbucks of wine bars.
Had to go back to back days after eating their tacos for cheap(2 bucks per taco) on their Happy Hour menu. 9-20-16

Absolutely love this restaurant! My family and I come here frequently for family dinners. Great food, decent sized portions (I always have leftovers for the following day's lunch) and a good dining room environment. Waitstaff are friendly and professional. 

My recommendations: Potsticker appetizer, mu shu pork, yen ching beef, beef pad thai and hot braised chicken.
Another great STL bbq joint. Sugarfire has done a great job of adding their own unique twist to the BBQ experience. Try it. You won't be disappointed!!

We had a restaurant dot com certificate for this place so we decided to try it.  The crepes were very delish and we thoroughly enjoyed our meal.  I had the So Riviera. I will be back and based on previous reviews probably going for the smoked salmon dish.

Very cool spot on Mass Ave.  Great physical space as well as food and drinks. I like their mezcal margaritas but you can't go wrong with the classic! We got their short rib queso and it is quite possibly, the best thing I have eaten in a while.  It's a little heavy - I split with someone - but the portion is just right.  Enough food to be satisfying but not too much.

I'm a huge lover of Cuban food and this place did not disappoint! Kuba is located in Armature works right across from Astro and I found their service quick and friendly. I went on a Thursday which was not a busy day and they had happy hour $5 sangrias which was really good! I also had the Cuban Salchipapa that was very tasty and filling! I will definitely be back!

This place is convenient for people who don't want to drive to Chinatown and located next to a Chinese supermarket. However, a few times I've been here there have been huge issues with their sanitation standards and the service is atrocious. Most servers are okay, but one lady in particular, a tall middle age lady with black hair and a stank face always says the most nasty things and gives a horrible attitude totally unprovoked. I live near Chinatown so I don't come here very often but of the few times that I have, this has really stood out to me. Enough to the point that it prompted me to write this review. I've never in my Yelp history given such low ratings but just because they are busy doesn't mean they can treat people like crap. 

I came here and it was 10% full. It was my dads birthday, a big occasion and after a tumultuous few years regarding his health we decided to have our close family come out to a small dinner to celebrate. We asked for a small private room in the back so the kids could have their space. She said we "wouldn't spend enough money to get the room" I've been in the private rooms many times and have never heard of a minimum. The manager told her to bring us to the room and she refused. Not trying to argue with this lady we all left to the restaurant down the street and my dad is heated by the way we were just treated. Mind you, we never have a budget with food when celebrating special occasions. Regardless, we didn't have to explain ourselves to this lady let alone meet these made up requirements. 

This is the same lady that told a family member that she "shouldn't have worn flip flops" when she slipped and fell on their wet bathroom floor and also the same lady that brought us our check and asked if we were ready to leave as soon as our food arrived last time and the time before that. We have a family of about 45 people. None of us want to return here despite the convenient location. We've all been offended by her in our experiences. Nobody deserves to be talked to this way and I hope this business starts seeing the consequences of the horrible attitude of this particular server.

I did not appreciate this place whatsoever. 

First off, the DJ did not know his audience. He was placing songs with cussing, when there were young kids in the audience. He was also saying cuss words. All the music was incredibly loud. I had trouble ordering food because of it. 

Next, once I ordered my food the kitchen got it wrong, once they brought it out it was very dry. It was quite disappointing. 

Now for the very few good things, my waitress was very kind. Unfortunately that was the only thing. I do not recommend this place at all.

Am I missing something?? I would NOT even begin to compare this place to Texas de Brazil or Fogo de Chao.  

It is a tiny place that looks like a cafeteria.  Zero decor.  

The salad bar is a joke.  Very small and super greasy options.  Plantains in a pool of oil, black beans so watery it covers your plate and good luck trying to fish for some from the bottom of the liquid filled tray.  Those were the only 2 things I'd suggest getting if you actually went here.  The "salad" is leaf lettuce normally used for garnish -whole leaves layed on a tray - with slices of tomato on top of them. Unless there just wasnt any salad out the entire time?  There was white rice, a "greek rice" that I'm pretty sure was a version of dirty rice using left over white rice and random meat scraps, pot roast, "fajita" meat, fried yucca, potato salad, and some dry minced meat patty thing -  greek again. Golf ball size balls of doughy bland "cheese" bread.

All of the meat was way overcooked and not great quality.  The filet was tough.  Top round was so cooked you couldnt even cut through it - although the knives were super dull. Bottom round was the least dry/overcooked - probably due to all the fat. We were only able to take one meat at a time as that was all that was cooked. Constantly up and down for a piece or 2 of meat.  They must do that on purpose so you are full faster and can't load up. It was peak dinner time.  They should have everything ready or minimal wait for maybe one option. And again we sat and waited forever for the bill - actually had to ask for it.  The waitress walked by several times with no acknowledgment that we were done eating.

The Caipirinha was one of the worst drinks I've ever drank. SO sour I could not take more than one drink. It sat on the table and I had to pay for it. 

Even with the Groupon we left paying way more than this place is worth.  Not only do they charge you for a fountain drink on top of the buffet price but they charge you for every refill.  I would not recommend this place.

I come here for lunch 1-2 times a week. The food is delicious and I love that they offer the small plates ('mfavorite is lemongrass bed and brown rice). It is the perfect amount of food, perfect serving size. The workers are really sweet and always greets customers kindly. Love this place very mi

Having dropped into this place for more times than I care to admit over the years, I'll say that it has had its day in the sun and it's time to go the way of the chain it once buoyed as the original. The world's stage has moved beyond any place called "Sambo's".

Mediocre service provided stale old muffins before a breakfast sooner forgotten than described here. Pancakes were dry and tasted like a thick paper, cardboard. Eggs were dry and cold when they arrived. The saving grace, bacon, was greasy, cold and made me want to return to a vegan lifestyle. This place is great for the drive-through Winnebago tourists from Ohio where they can gloat "I ate at a place called "Sambo's! I swear to God!" but not for anyone that craves a delicious breakfast.

While occupying an enviable beach-side location, the cracked and fading paint, the chipped walls and broken lighting show its true colors, a relic in need of demolition. It'd make a wonderful competing location for a cleaner, newer B&B or even another surf shop to counter Yater's monopoly on the market here but hey, that's just my humble opinion. In truth, Yater has earned his place on this coast, Sambo's has not.

Very nice lunch buffet. Food is tasty, but not spicy hot. Tandoori chicken was moist and tender, not dried out. Most of the chicken that they had on the buffet that day was dark meat, which I prefer. My wife had some special needs, and they worked hard to accommodate her. Naan looked very good. Light and airy atmosphere, well maintained. Semi-patio seating on State Street.

Honestly best pho I can find, I used to live near this place and go all of the time but since I moved to the city I haven't been able to go as much. I went today for the first time in a while and I had the absolute best service and best pho AND delicious fried bananas with chocolate. Love coming here!!!

If you desire unique local cuisine, you need look no further than Red's Chinese. Red's is located on St. Claude Avenue in a neighborhood known as the Marigny. The exterior of the restaurant is reminiscent of a pre-Katrina neighborhood home with little identifiable signage beyond the empty red square that stands in front of the building. It is almost impossible foresee such a bright vibrant interior or innovative menu from just a quick glance at the exterior.This is a true hidden gem. Red's menu boasts an enormous variety of chinese- creole fusion, featuring dishes such as kung pao pastrami, crawfish rangoons, and even sweet and sour sweetbreads. When it comes to creativity and flavor, Red's does not disappoint.

Found this place via Yelp when searching for a good southern breakfast during my weekend visit in Nashville. There are no reservations, so try to get there as early as possible, as we arrived around 10:00 and had to wait for 45 min. The restaurant reminds me of an old timey diner - nothing fancy at all and seems to be a joint for a lot of locals.  I ordered a biscuit sandwich with country fried chicken, cheese, and egg. You can tell the biscuit are super fresh. Honestly, the food was good, but not so great that I'd go out of the way to eat breakfast here. My boyfriend ordered ham and potatoes and eggs. The ham was too salty. It was a little too casual for what I was looking for and the wait time was just too long for the quality of food that we ate. If you're in the neighborhood and it's convenient for you - go for it! Simple and straightforward breakfast.

I want to like this place because I love buffalo wings. Sadly after multiple visits this place has not measured up. The service is mediocre. You will randomly have to wait a long time for a drink refill then suddenly get more drinks than you need. All the times I've visited the food runner and server could not accurately tell us which wings were which sauce. They even admitted this to us one of our visits. 
Very disappointing.

Surprised the ratings weren't higher. This was one of the best dinners that my husband and I have had. And he's a picky eater. Definitely coming back.
Whatever they are doing with fish-keep it up.

Every time my friend comes into town, we try to accommodate her with vegan food. With choices such as bar bombon, it's hard to compete. Though, Charlie was a sinner, did not disappoint. There were 6 of us, and we shared 10 plates (tapas style), all from different sections of the menu. You couldn't go wrong with any of the choices. Not to mention, they're drinks were from another world. Each cocktail were $12, but SO WORTH IT. They had many different flavors, in one drink.. and many different styles and liquors to choose from. Most people are scared of vegan, but even our skeptic friends were in love. Highly recommend!

I was expecting a little bit better. I know a lot of people have told me great stories about their meals here, but I expected a little more.

The parking lot is pretty small, but we were able to get a spot. The restaurant is basically one big open room. The staff seemed friendly and attentive enough.

The Jasmine iced tea was pretty good. We ordered the Spring rolls for an appetizer. They were very big and odd. I was hoping to get the Lemongrass beef with vermicelli that I always get from 9 Roses, but they only had Lemongrass chicken, so I got that. My friend go the pho. I'm not sure what meat he got in it, but he liked it a lot.

When my chicken came out I was already a little skeptical before tasting it. It was a massive serving of whole chicken pieces that still had the skin on. -Not exactly what I had in mind. I tasted it, it didn't have much flavor. It was quite underwhelming.

I guess on the plus side, they give you large portions for leftovers. But, if you don't like it much to begin with, the leftovers are even less appealing later.

I think I'll stick with 9 Roses instead.

This is officially my new go-to for a lovely dinner! After drooling over their Instagram for weeks, I finally managed to make my way there with friends for a fun Friday night dinner! (Btw, if you aren't following them on Instagram, you really should be)

I did make reservations, not sure how busy they get on Fridays. Going early means there isn't a crowd, the crowd picked up closer to 7ish. We walked from Sparkman, so not sure how the parking is, they are on Harbour Island. 

The restaurant is super clean and bright. It's also, uncluttered and super cute! Our server was amazing. She was super attentive, made sure our waters were kept full (they leave a carafe of water on the table)  

We started with apps and a lovely bottle of wine. The wine list is brief and has some lovely wines on it, including a Tempranillo. 

The food is AMAZING! Everything is fresh. The server said there are no freezers. The menu is seasonal and changes. So pay attention. We ordered the calamari and mussels. YUM!! The two apps were plenty to share among 4 people. 

For dinner, we ordered an assortment of fish and red meat. Everything was scrumptious. Every single dish was perfectly seasoned, prepared and paired with perfect sauces and seasonings. We got all the veggies on the side so we could share. Best idea ever. Serving sizes where well-proportioned. 

I had the lobster tail and steak. Not overly priced and cooked wonderfully. I like my steak a rare-medium and it was a little more done than I like, that's fine, it's hard to get a little rare without going full rare. I know, that if I sent it back it would have been redone. I chose not to send it back so I could enjoy my meal with my friends and frankly it was delicious. 

We skipped dessert and I was a little bummed about it, they looked super good but we were super full. 

The prices are reasonable and not overly expensive. Totally worth it for the service you get and the fresh food!!
I highly recommend this place the ladies in the drive-through window are really  nice and friendly the food is amazing and everybody should try the new vampiro  taco is the best in town

needed late night grub. stumbled upon this on our way up north. BEST shrimp quesadilla I have ever had. ever!  and I lived in Cali for 10 years. the mix of onions, peppers, cheese with shrimp topped with a chipotle drizzle + guac on side was insane. no time to take a pic, I ate it so fast. FYI this isn't on the regular menu - late night appetizer

I got the pork chop entrée and it was beyond fabulous. It was incredibly moist and the sauce and sides were great. Waitress was extremely friendly and helpful. Fact is, the prices were great. The interior was really nice, although I only got to see it when using the restroom.

Great place with a large menu. You should definately check the menu out before going because it could take some time to read through it all. Not only is the menu large, but the ingredients in each item is extensive as well. 

I don't remember the names of the items we ordered and I don't feel like searching it right now, but I had something that resembled a quesadilla. It was alright. It needed more meat in it. My wife ordered this chicken and waffle meal. I enjoyed hers a lot more than mine. Of course she always orders the better dishes everywhere we go! The sweet potatoes in her dish were amazing. I think I ate more than half of her potatoes. The coffee here is also on point. 

Service was great also, but became a little slow near the end when I was close to finishing my meal and requested the check. I guess she got busy and kept forgetting??

Overall: I would come back again, but this time, I'll order what my wife is going to order and make her get something else. LOL

I'm always looking for good not fried "fast food" and I may have found my ideal place. You chose a protein, 4 veggies, a sauce and a base (some have extra cost). I had brown rice, chicken, veggies with black bean sauce. The food was simple but it had flavor and it's prepared in the kitchen not a buffet style place where everyone picks through everything.  I will say the portions are not big so if you are used to that you may be disappointed. Also you can ask them to go "light" on the sauce. If ordering take out... Call ahead. You will be grateful you did when you see the line inside!
Had to check this place out,  had the Cuban and was not disappointed! Delicious.  Made like it should be. Will definitely return.

For the quesadilla, they melt mozzarella cheese then add your fillings vs the burrito has no melted cheese and thats the main difference and maybe the addition of beans in the burrito.  We first fell in love with felipes when they had a booth at the audubon zoo one weekend.  But our visits never stood up to our first experience.   I find it rather bland. And of course you can douse it in hot sauce but whatever. The dessert menu says all homemade, well Ive made better flan out of a jello box then the crap they are selling.   The best things on the menu is the white queso and the flavored tea and milk.

We called ahead and reserved a table for 6.  It's our typical Friday night out with our friends, so we wanted to make sure that our little group was going to be able to get seats at this prime dining time of 6:30 Pm. 

I was the first to arrive and though seating wasn't a problem, Parking was. I had to use the Valet service, and while free, I just don't like someone else using my car.  Anyway, I digress. The rest of our party arrived, and we were seated outside. It was a lovely evening, so that wasn't bad. A few flies and mosquitos were annoying but this is Florida, you survive it. 

The food was good, My husband ordered the coconut shrimp and I ordered the Rumba Platter, which was a Fillet kabob, a Grouper cake & a few of the coconut shirmp, everything arrived quickly and hot, The food was tasty and the service was good.  We'd come back again.

We tried a sampling of the jerk wings, beef fat fries, meat pie, and boudin. Everything was fantastic! The jerk wings weren't the typical. They had a little sweet taste and some kick. The meat pie was by far our most favorite of the sampling (if we had to choose one).  Was staying in the French Quarters but caught an uber over, just a short drive.

The latest addition to the John Besh family of restaurants has finally hit Uptown. If you aren't familiar with Domenica then brace yourself for the best pizza on the planet. No one executes like these guys, and if you like to have a drink with your meal then you will find plenty of draft & bottled beer and cold spirits to accompany  whatever deliciousness they put on your table.

Terrible. Hamburger meat was not done sold me a raw burger actually two raw burgers. Called to tell Rick the manager and he hung up on me. Food was so awful my dog turned his head . I'm embarrassed for you and that you serve dog food to your patrons . If I could give you minus 5 stars I would

I'm on a mission to find something cool in my neighborhood, so I gave Pinky's a try.  I went for breakfast and was immediately dissapointed when I was told they were out of rye *and* wheat bread.  The service was perfect diner -friendly and upbeat, with plently of "sweetheart" and "hon."  

I ordered a breakfast sandwich on a croissant.  The croissant   was delicious, flaky and buttery, and so rich that I almost couldn't eat the eggs and provalone smothered inside.

This place would've gotten a 4-star, but like the rest of Philly, lose points when it comes to homefries.  Mine were still hard, as in still potatoes, and totally unseasoned.  If they could have gotten this right I would have breakfast here all the time.  

All in all, Pinky's delivers a no-frills breakfast experience.  Bring your own hot sauce though, as they only have little packets of non-hot hot sauce here.

Came here for lunch over the weekend. I was visiting with a group for a bachelor wite party from New Jersey. Our waitress was so nice and the food was delicious! I ordered the hot chicken sandwhich with a side of Mac and cheese. Also tried the baked cheese appetizer which was really good as well! Hoping to visit again in the future!
Best Chinese food in the city. I'm originally from NYC and am very picky about where I go. Highly recommend the white meat general tso. Yum

I love this place. I can go here and order dim sum anytime! They are very friendly, and the owner LOVES kids! People usually don't go here. I used to see the place being very busy. But lately it hasn't. Oh well no need for me to be having whispering conversations.

I'll be back!

The food was tasty - love that you can build your own gyro or salad - or just choose to get a ready to order menu item. The staff were super friendly and chatty, but efficient as they worked. I love the vibe inside this GORGEOUS historical building. When the building was renovated, they left a lot of the original ceiling, architecture, etc visible -- so cool. Prices were reasonable. 

The only drawback is tight parking. But if you are craving a gyro, you'll find a way. Don't let this little challenge keep you from visiting. You can walk a bit for good food, good service, and a cool vibe - you'll be glad you did.

Food is so flavorful and delicious. Portion sizes are huge. Could not finish half of my food because I was so full. I ordered the brisket nachos and they were layered to perfection. Their ribs are the best. You can tell they have been slow cooking forever. The chicken is so moist and delicious as well. A must try!

Very precious little cafe tucked away behind the ice cream shop in New Hope.  Great for breakfast items and desserts, although I wish I saw more savory opens for the morning.  Their pastries and confections looked great though...

I got the ham and cheese croissant and it was light, flaky, savory and delicious.  I was kind of wishing for a little dijon in there, but maybe that isn't traditional.  The guy that owns the place speaks with a real live large and in charge french accent, so I am assuming that I'm getting relatively authentic baked goods...

There is a cute little patio available for patrons to sit and enjoy their goodies, and it has a nice view of the river.  Next time I think I'll try the coffee here... if it's good, that might make it five stars for me :)

We have been eagerly anticipating our visit to House of Cards! My husband is a magician and I have been to magic shows across the country, and the magic at House of Cards didn't disappoint! The table magicians were lots of fun and did a wonderful job of engaging and holding the attention of spectators, despite the staff interrupting them for drink orders, etc. I thought that was a bit disrespectful to the performers, but that is a management issue. Jessica Jane, the theater performer, was delightful! She related personal stories to the audience and brought them along on a FAST 30-minute journey! She was refreshing and I definitely will go back and watch her on "Penn and Teller's Fool Us"! Being fans of magic, we were thoroughly entertained by the magic and the original pieces memorabilia adorning the walls. The theater was beautiful! The patio was a wonderful surprise! Who would think there would be a 19-foot waterfall in downtown Nashville! 

My reasons for not giving this 5-Stars lies in the details. For a venue to truly be magical, everyone working there should be excited to take you on a magical journey, not just the entertainment. The staff was very formal, and it seemed to conflict with the atmosphere. The food was lackluster. If I'm paying that much for entrees, why am I getting thawed bread and not fresh-baked? Why is my server not focusing on me getting to the 7:30 show instead of offering me dessert at 7:20? Why are the restrooms lacking feminine supplies, lotions, etc. like other high-end places?

I think this place has what it takes to be a world-class destination for magicians and those who love magic! Tweaks in the service and amenities will take my rating to 5-stars! We will definitely be back for more! Great entertainment is lined up in the upcoming months!

The people here don't know what a fucking cup carrier is. Went in and ordered 5 coffees to go, and the stupid bitch doesn't even think twice about giving me a cup carrier. Attempting to carry them at once, I spilled the damn coffee on myself. Don't go here, they are incompetent!!

In this water tower village, there's a little villa that packs a thrilla! 
Just off the 52 bustle, one can find Pancho's neatly tucked into the one-street downtown skyline. 
This is and has been the place for Mexican food for a lot of years.

Fab fiancée and I always enjoy the scenic back road trip to the best Mexican food this side of the Pasco border. 
By car, truck, horse or iron horse it's a great ride. 
No horse? No worries. You won't have to contend with saddle sores at least. 
No Oucho Gaucho, LOL. 
Today, believe it or not, I hit the trail alone. Without benefit of Fab one's beguiling beauty before me I was forced to contain my ooh's and ahh's and yums....people would stare!

For me, chips & salsa and guacamole are a good indicator of a Mexican restaurant's quality and authenticity. If those are good, the rest of the menu typically excels as well. The salsa? Absolutely delicious! Muy bueno! Chunks of tomato, cilantro and other goodies pack a lot of Pancho's punch! Heat wise, they serve you both a mild and a hotter salsa. I sometimes mix the two for a perfect heat note! 
Their guacamole? With its thick and creamy gooey goodness, it is the Goddess Gravy of the Avocado! Yum to the Yum!

Which entree comes to mind as the tortilla and tomato Tex Mex trophy dish? Lots of folks would say the Chimichanga. That funny name is hotly debated as to its origins. Some say that back in 1922 a Tucson, Arizona restauranteur accidentally dropped a burrito into her deep fat fryer. What she uttered next was technically some Spanish profanity; quickly followed by 'chimichanga', a Spanish version of 'thingamajig' (we shall never know the real story....)

So, naturally I had to order one of these flavorful deep fried fantasy delights! 
My wonderful server Debra D delivered the dish piping hot. These servers are always wearing an oven mitt or a towel and warn you 'Do not touch the plate, it's hot!' 
(How many of us go right ahead and touch the darn hot plate anyhow?) 
As heatproofed hand set said plate down, heatwaves of Chimi flavors freely floated about my face, tantalizingly tickling my nose! The measure of my pleasure put all things San Antonio out of my realm for a brief food interlude. 
In other words, I was in Mexican Heaven!

Pancho's Villa has just a few tables, so you may expect to wait at peak times. 
But, hang out to bang out some mighty fine eating!

Wasn't terribly impressed by C&T brunch. Carribean menu is  nice and intriguing. Expect sweetness, less  savory in the dishes.
We ordered biscuits and jam to start. Fantastic. Flaky, warm biscuits- cold butter, okay jam. Warming the butter to be spreadable goes a long way with me. Maybe next time. Our mains were the arepas and the C&T breakfast. Waitress helped decide the latter. Then later asked me if I i thought it was good as if  she's neveR had it. Huh? I was honest and said it was just ok. Pork belly seems re-fired as outer skin was tough and chewy. Everything else on our plates were just ok. One tone. Expected  more but left  full I guess. I'd say 2.5 stars. There's better out there and a pricey start to the day. One mimosa isn't  $9. Just sayin

Great!  Clean and friendly place with delicious food.  Much needed in this neighborhood, good quality fresh food to go (you can eat there too). I have to eat gluten free and this place is the ticket.  They have dedicated pots and pans and a section of the kitchen to avoid any mix up.  I had gluten free penne with cherry tomatoes, fresh basil, mozzarella, garlic/olive oil, and sausage.  The chef cooked the sausage in a separate pan, not on the grill, since they cook flat breads on the grill.  This is really great care and much appreciated.  Best of all, the food is fantastic, pasta was cooked perfectly and the whole dish bursting with freshness and flavor.  Very friendly people as well.  What else do you want?  Spread the word, this place is a keeper.
A roach ran across the bar. I alerted the bartender who said cavalierly, "this is New Orleans."

I definitely have a mixed review of this place. We just went last night, and while the food was really good the menu was strange. Only one of the schnitzel platters came with spätzle while the others all came with french fries. Some of the sausage plates came with potato salad, while others came with roasted potatoes. None of the sites were consistent and the menu was very clear that no substitutions were possible. It was very strange. Our waitress was also not very friendly and give us an incredibly hard time about having a party of seven. Making snarky comments about how we should've had a reservation and how it was difficult to put together a table like that.
Great Mediterranean food. Love the hummus and  tea! I wish they had table service but it's a nice place.

Ordered the breakfast sandwich with berries and Earl Grey tea yesterday - the sausage was super greasy, appeared to have been sitting in grease and then put directly on sandwich without draining it off; berries were moldy; and Earl Grey tea didn't taste like Earl Grey, possibly wrong tea bag or maybe the teapot wasn't washed well from previous use and had leftover flavor from another tea. Even when I told the server the berries were moldy, his only response was "sorry". I was sorry too that I came here and spent over $20. No offer to take off the $2 extra charge. I didn't bother with the other issues since he clearly didn't really care when I pointed out the moldy berries. Overall the food was disappointing. I won't be coming back and would NOT recommend Cassis.

Purchased from Garden Mediterranean for the first time. Got a variety from grilled fish to lamb, grape leaves, and baklava. The food was good. The price is a bit higher than other close by Mediterranean places but at least, it tasted good.

My favorite burger! 

The only place that has my combination I put on burgers at home- A1 and jalapenos!

This is my first time having dinner at Lemongrass. In the past, I would come here for their lunch buffet. I must say, their lunch buffet is much better than their regular dining. 

I ordered the chicken pad thai, calamari and fried rice. Portion size were generous but lacks flavor. I had to add extra fish sauce and spices to my dish.  

My water was left unfilled while the servers were socializing in the back. Servers were not friendly and never smiled. 

Overall, my experience here was ok. I ate, I paid and left. Nothing captivated me. I'll come for their lunch buffet but would not dine here otherwise.

Had breakfast here the other day while visiting Oro Valley. The food, staff and restaurant was all great. Food was tasty with many choices available. Was surprised that when we ordered coffee, we were asked if we wanted a light or dark roast! That's awesome. Also, they leave the coffee pot and carafe of water on the table, which I love! Three of us ordered spanish omelettes and a fourth ordered the veggie skillet I think. The omelettes come with your choice of a side (and there are numerous sides to choose from) as well as bread. I love that they include calories on the items, very helpful! Everything was tasty! Our server Anthony was very attentive and service was quick and accurate. The manager came by to ask how everything was. They have a nice outdoor eating area as well, which we took advantage of before returning to Seattle, where it will be at least another month or two before we can eat outside. :-)

I would definitely recommend this place for breakfast!
We love the food/ the service and really want one out on the main line in philadelphia

Stumbled on this gem while passing through town.   Oh.  My.  God!   Simply the best  pulled pork I've had in a long time!  Corn in the cob?  Yummy deliciousness!  Baked beans?  Oh yes bring it on!  Unassuming building hiding some damn good food.   Hubs and I will be  back!

My husband and I decided to try out this restaurant for our first time! The greeter was okay, and they were busy! The paper menus were sticky,  but the restaurant was clean! There was a wait for the waiter, and another wait for the food! The food was okay, but we're not coming back

When we walked into this wawa I thought wow this place is huge! So clean too! Then i saw they sell wawa apparel. Awesome, right? Wrong.  Nothing available. Bummer. Can you tell I'm a big fan of Wawa?

After looking around I realized they had no pre-made breakfast sandwiches.  That's odd. I've never experienced that in the morning.  I went to the screen to order one made but the selection was so limited. Disappointing.  Then I went to get a fountain drink but no cups. Huh? You have to purchase the cup first. Ok maybe that's how they have to do it here. I purchased the cup then argued with the attendant when she didn't give me one. I mean look at the receipt?? When she did, no apology. Ok maybe she was having a bad day or had something heavy on her mind... all my stuff on the counter as she said "next". Um.  I had to ask for a bag. Which she said was a quarter. I paid by credit card. Had she told me at the time, I would have added it. But now you want me to put $0.25 on a credit card? Does she realize it cost her store $0.10+ per transaction to process cc? 

Anyway, I got my drink, but the lid didn't fit. Are you kidding me? No small lids. The S/M lids were full of L lids. Ugh.  Picked up my sandwich and left disappointed.

Hubby and I came here for V-Day. The food was delicious and the service was great. He had the steak and said it was juicy and cooked perfectly. I had a pork sirloin that was served with blue cheese and various vegetables and it was so tasty. We will definitely eat here again!
Update November 2017:  Service is much better the chipotle chicken tips are very good & a light option for someone dieting.  Wish they would put the breaded pork chops on the menu for good

AMAZING FOOD!! This place is great and the service is excellent. I've only been there for dinner (and only lived in the area for about 3 months, but have gone here at least 4 times already). Good price too.
I hear their lunch buffet is excellent, but haven't had a chance to check it out yet. 
Definitely recommend!!

Nora's Mexican Grill has the best authentic Mexican food on South Street! I have ordered the Mexican Grilled Chicken over rice, Steak Tacos, Fish tacos. Everything on the menu here is really good and freshly prepared, cooked, or grilled. The owner and all the employees here are awesome, friendly, and very hard-working. 

The food is always made very fast and the staff does a great job letting customers know of any specials and new items. The customer-service focus aspect of any food/restaurant business is important to connect with your customers and Nora's does a great job doing that. I hope many people will continue to patronize Nora's Grill on south street we need good Mexican ethnic cuisine around to stay!

I had a meal at the Coachman last night and it was great. Ribeye with jumbo shrimp and baked sweet potato. The steak was requested medium and it was delivered medium, the shrimp were large and lightly breaded. Service was excellent. I don't understand why there are so many negative posts about the restaurant. My friend and I both enjoyed it very much.

Awful. Small. Freezing cold. Entire waitstaff seemed to be made up of very young high schoolers; too many with nothing to do. Many were hanging out at tables with friends, but clearly still on the clock. 
We were seated so close to the bathroom we could hear the toilets flushing. We waited a long time for our drinks to come but were visited 3 times by a staff member trying to get us to sign up for some membership card-who forgot he'd already been to our table twice before. And when he wasn't visiting tables he was tending only to a table of friends or family to get them more and more sauce and chatting loudly. I felt as if we'd mistakenly walked into a high school homeroom that happened to serve food. 
I don't expect a 5-star dining experience at BWW, but I do expect to feel like I'm in a restaurant. The entire experience was bad. I won't be going back to this location. Next time I want overpriced wings and beer, I'll drive to the BWW in Downingtown.

Rooms small old, overpriced and not enough staff.  Our room still not cleaned at 530pm so we went to the pool area to wait.  Unable to get a drink at the bar stood for 15 minutes and wasn't even acknowledged by the bartender.  Pool over crowed and small .  This place is definitely not worth $378.00 per night with $29.00 parking fee.

It seems like every week I end up at Vango for at least the early part of the evening. Ever since they got rid of the vomit smell by the entrance, I place has been pretty decent. I mean it is what it is, and it doesn't try to be what its not. Basically a cool place to chill at the bar with friends. There is a moderate sized dance floor, usually at least a few cute girls. There is an upstairs, in the summer its really cool because you can go onto the roof and chill outside as well. The drinks are usual center city prices, but not quite as expensive as G Lounge. Upstairs (you do need to have a drink in your hand to get up there) is more of a hip-hop vibe, down stairs is a mix. The crowd is kind of diverse, mostly white and black, but also a few indians. But while the crowd is comprised of actual Philadelphians, it mostly caters to adult who are looking to have a good time. I've never seen any tension or fighting, I see a lot of guys brings their girls there. I've seen girls in groups. A lot of college kids and grads. Its a nice place to chill, and I've never paid a cover to get in. The line moves pretty well (unless its crowded). Bouncer's are cool. I do believe that they serve food and have bottle service, but I wouldn't recommend doing dinner later than 9:30p, it gets to crowded and a little too boisterous to enjoy the food. All in all its a good stop en route to a good night out.
The pizza here is so delicious. They have the best combinations for their pizzas. The service can be somewhat slow but it's worth the wait usually. I definitely would recommend!!
The new space is absolutely beautiful!  Love the food and the staff, many of whom have been around since I started going to the previous location pre-rehab.  Everything is always fresh and delicious.

Meh.  Better than the Cafe due Monde for sure.  Light and airy.  Servers aren't friendly and the beverages are served in tiny glasses.  This place has 3 things going for it: location, location, location.  Tours stop here.

Vegetarian review:

The cheese used was too dense, sauce was tasteless, but the portions were large. They charged me $4 for a side of beans, which in my opinion was a lot since the smaller platters go for $6. 

But the people were friendly & the place is decorated well.

I'll get to the point right from the start...this place is great! I'm not an BBQ Officiando, but this was some of the best BBQ I've ever had in my travels. 

Spent a long weekend in the Big Easy with my wife and good friends and were lucky to happen upon this place. We actually ended up going twice because it was so good the 1st time. 

The atmosphere is of a typical bbq place (comfy & cozy), prices are quite affordable, the servers are pleasant and best of all the aroma gets your mouth watering.

We ordered the the 3 meat combo being a 1/4 chicken, brisket burnt ends, ribs and a side of baked beans m, totally Yummy!  ... and what goes better with bbq than a pitcher of beer! Helpful tip...for a group of 4 and depending on how hungry you are, the 3 meat combo may be a bit on the light side, again the prices are quite reasonable.

So if your in the mood for great BBQ on the out skirts of the city, then check out "The Joint"...you won't be disappointed. Enjoy!
This place is St Pete's original Thai restaurant. The food is great. The price is very reasonable. It's like home cooking from your Thai family.

I have order from El Purepecha and some items are a hit or miss for me. Today I got the pescado burrito (fish burrito) and the camarones quesadilla (shrimp quesadilla). They were both amazing. The fish taco was heavy and had a nice spicy kick to it! I've tried the shrimp burrito. It's ok but not amazing. But the fish burrito is AMAZING. I could taste the chipotle/ancho favor and the the guacamole. The shrimp quesadilla was amazing as well. I'll stick to these as my go to as well as the chimichanga.

I've visited Tampa twice, and both times I made it a point to visit Datz. 

The first time, we ordered the hemp mus, Memphis on my mind, and the cheesy tod. The second time, we ordered jacked up steak and eggs for my brother, reuben sandwich for my mom, and the fish taco for myself. 

Hemp mus: very interesting. The texture is not as smooth as normal hummus but it is still very good. Very pretty yellow color and had great flavor. They gave us a good amount of pita chips which was nice.

Memphis on my mind: this is essential a BBQ pulled pork sandwich. Average in my opinion.

Cheesy tod: you should probably order this only once ever in your lifetime. This is the infamous burger with Mac and cheese and buns. It was a fun dish but not something to get as a regular item haha.

Steak and eggs: cones with hash brown and sourdough. Hash Browns were okay, sourdough had too much butter on it. Steak was cooked perfectly though, and the eggs were huge! 

Reuben: just like the Memphis on my mind, nothing special. It is your typical reuben sandwich.

Fish tacos: this as actually my favorite! Highly recommend. Three very large tacos with big pieces of fish and avocado. Served with corn and rice. Very delicious and authentic in my opinion.

Overall a great place to visit once in a while as a treat. Food is good and portions are huge. It's a bit to greasy for me which is why the four stars.
Great sandwiches and salads, very fresh ingredients, homemade,will definitely go back.

In my opinion this was a very good burger. I loved that you were able to have the burger made to your exact specifications. The check list menus cut down on the time it took to order as well as eliminated the chance for a miscommunication. As a picky burger eater I was happy to see that the typical condiments that are usually put on my burgers (after telling the cashier to leave them off) were no where to be seen. The shop had a very nice environment and friendly staff!

I love love love this place.  I've had the burger, fish sammich, chicken strips, fried chicken dinner, pot roast dinner, chili, cheese curds, French fries, onion rings, cole slaw, taters & gravy, green beans, milkshake and numerous flavors of the frozen custard.... Not all in one sitting.  haha...

Everything was good, although they are not my favorite onion rings in the world so I won't order them again.   The chicken strips are divine, and the burger is one of my favorites in town now.  Five Guys & Burger Monger is stupid expensive and way too big for me to enjoy.  This burger is just right.  

Everyone is friendly, but I do think some staff is still getting used to the routine so some were quicker than others.  But when someone is new & trying, I don't mind.  Place is clean, but a little awkward in the design for ordering - sort of like Chik-fil-A where you kind of mill around near the counter and hope everyone is going to respect the order in which you came in.

There has been a pretty good wait several times, but they are cooking your meal, not just pulling it off a warming shelf.   It's also nice that they bring it to the table so you don't have to just stand there.  

I won't even try to describe how good the frozen custard is.  You'll have to try it to understand.  They will give you a sample of the flavor of the day.  The milkshake is just fabulous. Kind of a mix between the Steak & Shake & the DQ  -- it's a thick, but sip-through-a-straw consistency, and they have add-ons that can be blended or just added.  I had the chocolate shake and they drizzled a liquid peanut butter sauce in the middle so I got just a little pb w/ each sip.  Heaven.  

As for price - cheaper than the gourmet burger places; not as cheap as McD's... but who cares?  This is real food, cooked to order and worth it.  

Oh, and a heck of a little kid's meal for about $5, including a little coupon for a frozen custard you can redeem now or later!

Slow service, server was nice.  Terrible wine list, house wine is the only wine option by the glass, otherwise you can buy a bottle of which there are no good choices. Very bland food. For being an Italian restaurant on The Hill we were thoroughly disappointed. Olive Garden would have been a better meal. We will never dine here again.

My wife and I visited for our 11 year anniversary a few weeks ago. We have been to Ruth's several times in Louisville and were looking for a great steak within easy walking distance in downtown. 

The service was fantastic here. Our server was Derwin and he really did a great job. Very attentive and very polite/professional. They were busier than usual and he comped us a round of drinks for our wait and a free dessert for our anniversary. A+++

The food was as you would expect from Ruth's. The filets were sizzling and juicy and cooked expertly to perfection. Highly recommend!
Blyss is awesome! As is ML Rose...

Had the Bawarchi Special Boneless Chicken Biryani $10.90 portion big enough for at least 4 people, the butter chicken $11.90 which I found too spicy even though it did not have the spicy icon next to it but I was sooooo hungry and just kept eating with a tissue in my hand. It was really good once combined with the naam. The place was nice and clean. Waiter did not speak much English and only served us water and did not offer any other drinks. Make me wonder if the freezer with the sodas were for them or for sale. My daughter was like"mom they had Fanta, now why they only give us water" I don't know baby. My only suggestions to them-offer something else besides water and if something is really spicy put the icon next to it and try to offer small dinner portions because I spent $29 just on me since my daughter was sick and could not eat- side note

Just give me your wifi password, I had something really important I had to log onto the internet for. I even offered to pay.

Wanna be Latin food, stick to the local New Orleans fare. My first ever 1 star btw, they really hard to earn this one.

This place is the "BOMB" can't be beat when it comes to Hawaiian Food.   Service is awesome, food is even better, selections are beyond what most restaurants offers, portions are unbelievable and the prices are very fair.  Best yet, the taste "Broke da mouth".  Gotta give them a try, you really won't regret it.

We stopped in Saturday evening and had a great dinner. The service was fast and friendly. It is where the old King and I place used to be. It very much resembles the old place, just a different mix of dishes served. The food was very tasty and we were all very happy with the plates we orederd. Looking forward to our next visit.

One of the greatest finds on the beach!! The Cuban sandwich is in if the best around (Tampa) the menu has many great options. They serve my favorite ice cream brand and flavors. The only negative is the parking...just walk over it's easier! Love the Kooky Coconut!

Good food and fast service. For the most part they were large servings besides for the brisket where they definitely skimped on. We had the brisket, smoked turkey, half chicken, catfish, and an assortment of sides. We loved sitting outside and the servers were very nice and accommodating. Highly recommend.
Great New York style pizza.  Fast service and depending on who is working it can great or average service and the 1/2 price Monday 12 in is a deal!

The boyfriend picked up a Groupon for this place and it was our first time to visit. We both love French food, and so were really excited about trying Franco. Overall, our experience wasn't horrible, but it definitely was not our best date. The food was surprisingly uninspiring and the service was ridiculously slow - we are actually convinced that the couple next to us received our food by accident since they arrived after us yet some how got exactly what we ordered way ahead of us (for the record, we ordered a long time before them). The whole date lasted over two hours, which felt pretty long given that we were sitting there with nothing to eat the majority of the time.

Anyway, the ambiance is pretty cool, but the food and service was not so good. Based on my experience, I'm probably being generous with three stars, but I hate being that person who complains on yelp.

One of new favs!  Cozy atmosphere - although a bit loud.  Expect a wait - especially on Fridays or Saturdays - but the pizza is well worth the wait.  It's easier to get a table for 2 than for 3 or more (which makes this a good date place).  The pizza is thin, Napoli-style with fabulous charred edges.  The dishes of olives and bottled water add to the charm.

Yes yes yes yes yes !!!! This is how burgers are supposed to taste ! Absolutely delicious burgers, so much flavor, just wow. So far I've only ordered from here once but it will most definitely NOT be the last time. Looking forward to trying more items on their menu, I have no doubt they're as delicious. Highly recommend ! 


Ok so just wanted to update in regards to having only ate here once; my boyfriend and I have ate here 4 times in the last 8 days ! We gave the Hawaii 5.0 a try and OH MY GOOOOODNESSSSSSS ! Let me say that pineapple belongs on burgers, hot dogs, pizzas, and literally on everything , pineapple on burgers and hot dogs is very common in Colombia so when I saw the Hawaii 5.0 I knew they had to be on to something and boy are they surely doing everything right ! [Not to mention, very important to me as it has made me turn away from some restaurants, BTB has ZERO health code violation findings, WAY TO GO TO THE STAFF !!!!! This entire establishment is great vibes and just genuinely incredible food] We literally wiped the container clean with the fries because the juices from the burger with that Cajun seasoning they put on the fries is out of this world. If you have a far drive once you pick up your order just park and eat because the smell will have you driving WAY over speed limit !  might just order for dinner tonight, this post made me crave it

Met an old friend here for breakfast a few weeks ago.  Thought the food was average and service was lackluster.  Server could have been more attentive for beverages, and we didn't see her between meal delivery and dropping the check.

Great coffee, are really nice. I love that it's right off the Monon Trail, just a short walk or bike ride from the heart of the Carmel Art & Design District. The reason I give this 4 stars instead if 5 is the vibe. Very knick-knacky and grandma-ish. If vibe isn't your number one concern, or if you're just looking for coffee to go, check this place out. I recommend the siphon-brewed coffee.

Really great service, very friendly. This location is right off of the highway, but it was well kept. I had the cupcake pancakes, which were delicious, but sooo sweet. I like that there was a lot of variety. The coffee was served fresh and hot, and our mugs were never dry.

Heard a lot about this place and decided to give it a try.  First off, there is a real problem with good restaurants in the Quarter.  The play to tourists has really dumbed down the flavors and most Quarter restaurants are just mediocre.  This place is an exception.  It's not "great" food by New Orleans standards overall, but its "great" for the Quarter.  I had the BBQ shrimp. . it's different, but good.  Another local Quarter restaurant (unnamed) has the corner on the best BBQ shrimp but this was a close second.  My friend had the chicken pot pie. . to die for!   Great big pieces of chicken, gravy, vegetables. and the pastry!   You can't beat the pastry.  Definitely recommend the pot pie.  The place is charming, the service is generally good (a bit slow) and the prices are about what you would expect for the Quarter, though the side dishes are a bit pricey at $7.00 for collard greens.   I will definitely go back. . if for no other reason than to sample additional dishes (well, ok, and to get the chicken pot pie).  Their menu is quite eclectic.  The one complaint I had was that the BBQ shrimp was not served hot, just warm.  I'm not sure if it was from letting it sit too long before being served or another reason.  The chicken pot pie was just right.  I do recommend it for a satisfying meal and a great restaurant for the Quarter.  A little improvement and it can be great for any area in New Orleans.

I went to my usual spot looking for stone crab claws, but they were under renovation, and suggested I try here. Thank goodness for mapping programs, because I never would have found this place otherwise. It used to be a seafood house, but apparently due to road widening, now it's just a seafood market, which consists of two buildings - one you order and pay in, and the other one the food is cooked in, and you pick up your order from.  As someone else said - if you call and get a busy signal, just keep calling back.  The counterman was taking telephone orders almost non-stop.

The menu options are all hand written and displayed around the room on poster boards.  It is a lot to take in your first visit, but since they didn't have stone crab claws, I went with a snow crab claw platter, which came with a couple of crab clusters, sausage, corn, and potatoes, all cooked in a garlic butter and crab boil combo.  It took about 25 minutes for my order to be ready, so next time I would definitely call ahead.

I couldn't wait to get home and dig in, and it was all excellent.  The snow crab clusters were small but cooked well, and the sausage was fantastic. I absolutely loved their seasoning combination.  All in all it was a delicious meal, and I will definitely be back.

Nom Nom Nom!

My friend and I came here for the roast beef, but it wasn't ready so we opted for the club po-boy which included bacon, root beer glazed ham, and chicken with a side of onion rings.  The large po-boy was HUGE!  Even split between us, it was still ginormous.  You definitely get what you pay for because these po-boys are fully loaded!  It also doesn't help that I'm a messy eater! Haha.  The onion rings are awesome!  They're literally thinly sliced onions that are fried, and I loved it!  It's perfect for putting in your po-boy to add some extra crunch and flavor.  The sandwich was actually really good.  I like that you could really taste the root beer flavor, but it wasn't overpowering.

The only downfall was waiting for the po-boy.  It took longer than expected, but the wait was well worth it!
So delicious - I had stuffed bell peppers which were amazing and hubby had kufta with tahini. So good and excellent service

This place is terrible.  If I could give it negative stars I absolutely would.  The food is overpriced and incredibly subpar.  My boyfriend got a milkshake that actually had a piece of plastic in it.  Mine was slightly better but still absolutely terrible for the price.  We were so excited for this place to open and talked about how we couldn't wait to go there often; now we only mention it when we talk about places we absolutely do not want to ever go again.

Setting: The interior is pretty neat.  It has a full bar and an upstairs for additional seating.  Decor is outdated like many have said, but very comfortable.  I normally don't like sitting in booth seats (which I got), and they are not that comfortable.  Should've switched to a regular table.  The drinking glasses are tinted in dark blue.  I don't like it as I cannot tell if the glass or water is dirty.

Service: The servers are good.  Although ours disappeared after entre was served, but not too big of a deal.  Perhaps I was uncomfortable in the booth and wanted to get out asap.  Servers also recited the specials and seems to know what they are talking about.

Food:  This is the reason why this place only received 3 stars, instead of 4.  Now, I am no italian food expert (ate chinese food growing up), but the food there was just ok.  The bread they served was nothing special, butter is prepackaged, instead of softened.  

App: Fr. Calamari ($9)with warm tomato dipping sauce.  The sauce is decent, and the breading on the squid is nice too.  But the squid could've been cut a bit thinner, which will allow it to cook quicker and maintain its texture, and not as chewy.  Overall, I liked it.  I also wanted to order the Broccoli Rabe but didn't have the appetite I usually do.

Entre: Pascotora (sp?) ($16).  Basically its liguine in tomato sauce and about 4 pieces of big scallops, shrimp, squid (same as the ones in app), clams and mussels.  The pasta was a tad overcooked.  Scallop is also overcooked (its easy to tell as it will get rubbery).  Overall, I liked this dish.  The flavor was right on, the sauce is not overpowering and tomato-y.  Some items could've been cooked a little better, but the taste was there.

Special entre: Mahi Mahi ($22), grilled with shataki mushroom in garlic (supposely).  The presentation of this dish was good.  Must be the theme of this restaurant, but the fish was also overcooked.  The string beans had that "string" on the side that usually I take out when I cook them, so its more pleasant to eat.  The potato bits were delicious and goes well with the fish.  The sauce on the bottom was again not overpowering and tasted great.  Now, this dish would've been good if it wasn't for the mushrooms.  It was sour to the core.  The mushrooms were chopped length wise and "looked" fresh, so the sourness is not from spoilage.  I asked the server how the mushroom was prepared, I don't exactely remember what he said, but he mentioned it was cooked with garlic (which I did not taste much of) salt and lemon juice.  Perhaps it was the lemon juice as mushrooms tend to absorb juices.  A little acid on the fish is always a good idea, but not with pickled mushrooms.  I give the fish 3 out of 5 stars and garnish 1 out of 5 stars.  Overall, the dish failed IMO mainly due to the mushrooms.

Dessert: tiramisu cake.  Nothing out of the ordinary here.

Conclusion:  Seesm like the food here is fresh and clean, but cooking techniques could be better.  And that mushroom on the fish did not go well, don't make offer that garnish again chef, please.  Will I visit again?  Perhaps to try out other stuff on the menu, but I would not hold my breath.

This place and its amazing staff helped save our Father's Day! My family and I were having a rough day, but tried to find a good restaurant to turn things around. 
We were greeted by a cheerful host who sat us quickly at a lovely table by a window. Our waiter was Armando and he took excellent care of us; from making great food recommendations to making us laugh. 
We ordered a small Caesar salad which was perfect to share between four people and a 12' Don pizza on traditional crust. It was all delicious. It is safe to say our day was saved by delicious pizza and personable staff members. Looking forward to visiting again real soon!!
The breakfast burrito here is soooo worth it. The coffee is great and the atmosphere is super cute. I would definite recommend going. We even tried their bagels and they were wonderful!

If you've been to other Bravo joints, you really should check this one out. It is the best I've ever been to. The selection of meals is beyond what other Bravo's offer. They are extremely accommodating and will fix your pasta order exactly how you want it. There are always several salads available: pasta, greens, veggies. All fresh and good. Another thing I like about the place is the staff...friendly and competent. 
The chicken cooked with peppers and onions is great! If I ask the guys will heat up some pasta and toss it all together. YUM!.

By other half loves to come to Outback - while I stick with preferring more 'ethnic-fare' he sides with a baked sweet potato and salad w/honey mustard ;)
* On Wednesdays there is a 2 for $25 option we've been digging lately. You can share either a small version of an appetize or a dessert and 2 entrees for this price. This makes things more reasonable than the usual steak prices.

Food - My preference has always been the Outback special: 6 oz. steak w/a greens salad (w/vinaigrette) & green beans. Hubs digs the same w/a baked sweet potato and side salad w/honey mustard. The Ahi tuna on crispy won tons and the chicken quesadillas are our favorite appetizers!

Atmoshere - The Outback in Brandon upped the ante! The new decor and more 'chill' mood opens up the space and gives diners a more quaint feel than the hustle and bustle of the bar area - should you choose a more quiet surrounding.

Overall - we come back, it's a great place for dinner

Only set back: parking. That parking lot for all of the  businesses in the plaza gets crazy!

Had the Bestfriend burger with avocado and it was amazing. I didn't realize it was a beef patty AND a piece of fried chicken when I ordered but I have no regrets. Little hole-in-the-walls like this are perfect.
Gotta love the family style food. Never really had a problem with this place on any visit.

Look, it's an institution in St. Louis. You know it's not going to be the greatest but you have to at least try a small pizza, and think of it like a nachos instead of a pizza.

What can you say about Imo's? It's got average quality ingredients, and the promel cheese... the cheese is okay for the first few slices but it starts to taste very processed very quickly. And it sticks to your teeth which is unpleasant. It's more like a cheap queso cheese than anything. 

It's not bad but the crust could be crunchier. I want cracker crust if it's St. Louis style pizza, and Imo's just delivers a thin, semi-soft doughy crust. 

At the end of the day, you have to give it shot because it's Imo's, but in truth you'd be better off ordering a thin crust from Papa John's.
The lunch buffet is amazing ! large selection, nice restaurant, pleasant staff all around great dining experience

Food was decent and service was good. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because I found the price to be too high for the quality of the food. We got BBQ so it totaled $32 per person. It's all you can eat, so that would be the reason for the higher price and I am aware that Korean BBQ is generally on the pricier side. However, I wouldn't come here any other day aside from my birthday (free for bday person if ID is provided and review is written). The food is good but I found the price not worth it.
