My brother took us to dinner to try this place since we hadn't been here for a few years.  The wine and drinks were good and the bread.  Totally down hill from there.  Calamari were so greasy and the Asian dumplings were nothing to talk about.  My cod with crabmeat and was smothered in cheese that couldn't taste anything but cheese. My husband's broiled trout was so over cooked and drenched in butter... no lemon that it was tasteless.  My brothers Mahi-mahi was over cooked like shoe leather.  I couldn't believe how bad the cooking was.  The rice was glued into a ball and tasteless, Absolutely worst food I have had at a restaurant.  A diner would be better.  We try area places twice a month and this one is a no way we going there again.

Had a very good first time experience here. Drinks, food and service was all great.  Loved our waitress Ashley she was on point with taking our order and making sure or drinks were full. Food was really good as well. This is a place my family and I will be returning to.
Teriyaki  bowl was real good and my wife had poke bowl.  Shared the Macha and cucumber drink.  Very speedy and friendly service. No indoor dining yet. Highly recommend this establishment.

Depending on when you go in, there is a all you can eat buffet and the service is good.  Haven't been to the bar which is one wall/door away but looks to have a good selection of several things I would drink if I wasn't driving.
Wow, first time just wow! Everyone is wearing a mask, loads of room for safe distancing, and the pizza is OUT OF THIS WORLD!!! Wow!'n

I've been to Bernie's in University City before and the food was excellent. My most recent experience, however, was the exact opposite. First let me preface that this review is based on the food only. The waitstaff was fine. 

My wife ordered the ribeye, while I order the paella. The ribeye was mostly fat and tasted like it was microwaved. The paella was very bland and came with only 4 or 5 small pieces of shrimp. My wife also ordered a blackberry bourbon. It cost $12 and if there was any liquor in it, we couldn't tell.

I'm going to finish off this review with a photo of the  fatty remnants of the '14oz' ribeye.

I visited this restaurant bcoz it showed on my search results and looked decent enough. What I encountered though, well let's just say, I wasn't ready for it.

The lunch buffet had a huge variety of dishes, which simply stuns you. And if that doesn't, then the taste of those dishes sure will.

A must visit restaurant!

Had a beautiful and cozy lunch here today on a gray, rainy afternoon. The menu had all sorts of amazing choices; I got the Bella Burger, I'm a sucker for good angus beef, my sister got the fish tacos. 

We even decided to order the dirty mac and cheese to share. It was all very tasty and we had a nice big doggie bag for later.

David was our server and he was wonderful. Attentive, funny and always around without hovering.

I only wish we had room left for one of their yummy desserts. That's ok, we'll be back, to try some other great sounding entrees while hopefully sitting in David's section.

We had excellent cocktails today and absolute loved the mini pizza "flight" - what a perfect app idea! The cucumber mojito and ?? apple cocktail (fireball & hard cider) were truly fantastic. 

The service was good - almost too good. The host seated us and came back in less than a minute to say our server would be right with us and could he take our drink order - you just seated us literally one minute ago. The waitress came several times to check on us. The manager checked on us. I was trying to catch up with a friend and we kept getting interrupted. 

Looks like there have been poor service reviews in the past and they've WAY over corrected. When the place is slow, the customer can easily get your attention so there's no need to check every that often. 

Otherwise it was great and we are planning to come back for future movie nights.

Love The Fountain on Locust! The food is very good and health conscious! They mKe fantastic cocktails! It's definitely a sweet place to relax for a few drinks and dinner. Also the service is amazing! The staff seem to be happy there and go the extra mile!

We ordered from The Brass Monkey the other day and had our food delivered. Our wings and burgers and grouper sandwiches were all delicious. It's tough to find a meal on Pass-a-Grille these days, but we are so happy that The Brass Monkey was able to deliver our meals for our party of six. Thank you so much staff and crew at The Brass Monkey. PS. This was in the midst of the Covid-19, somewhat voluntary, lockdown in place at the time. 3/24/2020

One of Broadripple's best restaurants! Amazing vegetarian options; all the ingredients are so fresh. The portabella burger is delicioso!!! Oh and the place is family owned and operated which is always a plus in my book.

Po Le opened in the former location of Mina Cucina and Filippo's in a strip mall along Bethlehem Pike in Spring House.  The owner was formally a chef at San Marco up the street.

The only changes to the design of the restaurant was the addition of outside seating.  The layout remained mostly the same from how Mina was setup.  The buzz locally was that the food was top notch and I had to see for myself.

We made reservations 1 week in advance for a Friday night around 7pm.  We arrived and were seated immediately.  The restaurant was completely full shortly after we were seated.  Our sever came over after a few minutes to open our wine and get some ice for our beer.

The menu is rather compact which is fine but the specials list was about the same size.  After the server was finished advising us of the specials it almost seemed like there were more specials then entrees. 

My mother ordered an anti pasta for the table and we all shared an order of Calamari.  Each of us also ordered and entree.  I thought he food was good and it was obviously fresh.  While I did enjoy my meal It wasn't memorable.  I'm sure I will return again sometime but I didn't get what all the hype was about.

I have enjoyed dining at the Plant City location many times. I'm trying to get my husband on board with this restaurant.  We had a busy day and wanted Mexican food it was 8 pm on a Sunday so we ordered take out so we wouldn't keep the wait staff. We specifically ordered chips and salsa with our entrees.  My husband went in to pick it up and asked if they put the chips and salsa in the bag, they said yes.  We drove from Dover so by the time we got home it was 9 pm(closing time) I emptied out the bag and you guessed it no salsa for their delicious chips.  Very disappointing! The moral of the story please dig through your bag and make sure your order is correct before leaving the store. Wasn't a fan of their chicken verdes , I'm use to it having a sour cream cheese sauce over, theirs were a bit dry.  Love their fajitas though.

Awful pizza. I was so disappointed when I called Queens and this restaurant had replaced it. Claiming your pizza is NY style should be a crime when it's NOT and it's this bad. I'll try some of their other food, but the pizza was so bad we threw it out.

What's not to love about "And Pizza"? the perfect combination of fresh non-GMO produce, non-MSG ingredients, ooey-gooey cheese melted over fresh and organic oven-baked dough? More pizza, please.

After tasting five organic oven-baked dough pizzas, plus one dessert pizza, currently I'm obsessed with &pizza. And (fair warning) you're about to be, too.

1. Moonstruck: Delicious. Im so in love with the Moonstruck, and it will steal a pizza your heart, too.
2. Maverick: Created to please the meat lover. Salami, pepperoni, Italian sausage on a pizza. Not my type of pizza but it was a table winner.
3. Pineapple Jack: Very tempting. 
4. THE OG: Classic and healthier pizza. Yeah.
5. GNARLIC: The ultimate pizza. So what's stopping you?
6. Lori Lane 'dessert pizza': The whole table agreed it was out of this world.

Facts:
- And Pizza stay open till 3am on Fridays and Saturdays, to satisfy those late-night hungers.
- Amazing pizzas at a mere 800 calories per pizza ( Lori Lane 1060).
- At And Pizza, if you use you imagination while creating your own pizza, the possibilities are endless. 
- All pizzas are $9.49


Get pizza the right way -- Get And Pizza.
Four and Half Yelps.

Service was horrible!!!! Three people in my party, we ordered Irish nachos, onion soup and a Ruben sandwich. Irish nachos were good, but took a while to get to the table. The soup and sandwich took well over an hour and at least 25 min from finishing the nachos. After we asked where the treaty of our food was, it quickly got to the table, and had obviously been sitting under a heat lamp for some time. Moving to the bar wasn't much better. Bartenders were hardly friendly, and took a while to get another drink. Not to mention at least 15 min to get my tab at the end of a very long dining experience. Will not be returning.

GET THE CRAWFISH BENEDICT! We had banana bread, the Benedict, and the sausage egg pimento cheese biscuit. All of the above we delicious but the Benedict was my fave. We also had the Au Lait and vanilla latte. Highly recommend going to brunch here!
Everything was sooo good. Whenever I come back to the Big Easy ill eat here again....customer service was good as well

This has been a fantastic experience for us! Super friendly staff especially Rachel and the manager. After they learned we are here for a special occasion, they surprised us with the best tasting budino I've ever had. Tables are nicely spaced out and the atmosphere is just amazing. If you are ok with eating meat, definitely try the duck leg and the braised rabbit. I highly recommend this restaurant!!! Give it a try, you won't regret it!

I came here for the jazz brunch on a Wednesday afternoon as suggested by a local.  I was solo and was seated immediately without a reservation.  The courtyard was beautiful and it was the perfect day to sit outside.  Beware of the birds!  They may be hungrier than you are!

I was seated and waited quite a few minutes before anyone came over to my table to greet me, which I thought was odd and I felt a bit awkward for a while just sitting there.  There were a lot of staff standing around and not too many patrons.  Once I did get service, my server was very friendly and attentive, for the most part (waited again for a while to get my bill).  The brunch buffet has many items and all of the food I sampled was delicious.  The prime rib was so tender I was able to cut it with a butter knife.  The prime rib paired with the amazing garlic mashed potatoes was one of my faves.  The turtle soup was good....give it a try!  I am now addicted to Bananas Foster, although I doubt I'll find any as good as it was here (but its not going to stop me from trying!).  It's just not a dessert item I see too much on Pennsylvania menus.  Hmmm, perhaps I'll try to make it myself!  Love the history here as well, don't forget to touch the charm gates!  Can't hurt!!  : )

Wow. We stumbled upon Mario's and were excited to support a clearly locally owned family restaurant.  We love those kinda spots. The reviews are great and the staff was friendly. I just have to tell folks - no one is wearing a mask. Not even around their neck. The tables are on top of each other.  I'm sure the food is great. But we wouldn't know because we left. It was that uncomfortable...
Excellent experience! We were here for Sunday brunch. Complimentary fruit salad and mimosas. Surprise live music with Larry. Well done.

I am not a frequent visitor of Midtown, and after my night out I have no clue why. There's more space to move around, less noise to talk to your friends, and drinks are way, way cheaper. 

For a Friday night, DawgHouse was not very lively. But I really had no problem with it, we were able to sit at the bar with no problem talking, and got quick service. The music was kind of lacking, the DJ wasn't doing much to draw in too big of a crowd.

Overall I had a good time at DawgHouse but they had a lot of competition up and down the road and they were not seeming to do to well in terms of getting people in the door.

The place looks nice. 
The servers were friendly, but incompetent. 
The food was overcooked and poor quality.

Started with calamari. It had the consistency of a condom. 
Pesto gnocchi was good, but texture was a bit off.
Veal cutlet was good.
Pescitore was terrible. Overcooked clams, mussels, and calamari. Fish was bearable. One shrimp, but it was the only thing cooked correctly. 

Staff does not speak much English. If they spoke Italian, it would be fine by me, but they are all Mexican.

My first visit today with my daughter.  I had the Pink Dragon acai bowl, it was absolutely delicious. The only thing i would wish for was a little more fruit/nuts...other than that i loved it and am already craving more. My daughter had the breakfast burrito w turkey sausage, she really liked it and so did i (stole a few bites). We shared a smoothie and a coffee, both good and i appreciate the strength of the coffee. Woke me right up. Will definitely be back!!

This review is specific to the Panzarottis .  After all, this place serves the Original Tarantini Panzarotti and that is an important distinction to keep in mind when you have a craving for one of these deep fried dough pockets of goodness. Yes the baked imitation Panzarottis at other places may be healthier for you, but they lack the taste of the original, and whats more important then great taste in a meal. Just don't eat them for breakfast lunch and dinner as a regular diet.

I have enjoyed the Original Tarantini Panzarotti for years now, so when Franco's place moved even closer to my house, it made it that much easier to run out on a Snowy winter night to feed my Panzarotti craving.  Francos Panzarottis are consistent in taste and are stuffed with generous portions of mozzarella cheese and homemade sauce then deep-fried to a crisp, golden brown.

I ordered the steak Panzarotti and my wife ordered the chicken for take out.  While both were delicious,  I have to say the steak it is still my number one go-to when getting a Panzarotti. We ordered a side of extra sauce to go with both.  This was the only disappointment, tasted mostly like sugared tomato paste and nothing like a classic Italian tomato gravy. Only suggestion for Franco would be to change up his tomato gravy to improve the fantastic Panzarottis he serves up. I gave 4 stars for the Panzarotti w/o the side sauce.

The take out service was fast, friendly and efficient.

This is my new cravings spot. I went last night and had an appetizer of mussels. First time I had tried them and they had the garlic and wine sauce. While eating them I said something I have never said before, "I like these more than boiled crabs." That was until my girlfriend got her plate. She had ordered the fish covered half with their "missy" sauce and half with lump crabmeat. This crabmeat was THE. BEST. CRABMEAT. I had ever put in my mouth. I mean, I savored the flavor as long as I could. The "missy" side was equally as delicious. My girlfriend quotes, "this side is heaven... AND this side is heaven!" Then I got my crabmeat and corn cannelloni which was stuffed with a different crabmeat but still so good. All in all this is now one of my favorite spots and I will be returning... A lot. 

Thanks guys.

Sorry, it had a cafeteria feel but my group wanted an authentic Nawlins joint to eat at. Had the grilled oysters and they were ok but since we were sitting at a table away from the bar it lost its appeal as a bar food AND the reason I always order them. Too brightly lit and server wasn't the most attentive but the place was packed at 4pm on a Saturday. I've eaten at the Jackson Mississippi location at the bar and wasn't in awe of that place either. I don't know if it's trying to be like the Acme or not but it doesn't have the "punch" I'm looking for in a New Orleans joint. Maybe it's trying to please everyone.

Adding an edit - Reading the manager's response to my first review of this restaurant let's me know that my first impression was spot on. Rather than owning up to what was clearly very poor service and rushed plates, she is exhibiting petty and defensive behavior. If this is the management's attitude toward customers' reviews, there's no room for improvement. 
I hope others don't have the same experience. What a shame.

*****

This place was so promising before I went with a large party on a Saturday night... Although it has an overall high rating on Yelp, reading some of the other reviews, it seems that nothing about our poor experience is uncommon for Eastland Cafe.

I understand that it might be difficult to take care of a larger party (14 for us, but our reservation was pretty late, after most of the tables were cleared out or finishing up their means), but they managed to "lose" part of our ticket and forgot to make 3 of orders. While waiting over an hour for our food, I ordered a glass of wine, and it was one of the stingiest pours I've ever experienced. I had the shrimp and grits (one of the lost orders), and it was a flavorless mass sitting in a puddle of vinegar. Shrimp and grits is one of my favorite meals, and I've never tasted anything like this. A lot of people in my group ordered the steak, which was clearly a cheaper cut of meat poorly masked by over seasoning. It's never a good sign when people are reaching for bread at the end of the meal over finishing their entrees. The bread wasn't very good either. 

To apologize for the poor service, the manager did take care of the lost entrees and sent out desserts. However, it was a poorly carried out gesture too. They just keep sending out large portions of brownies (pretty good), strawberry shortcake (not great), and apple doughnuts (actually quite delicious!) - too many for our party, so just a bit wasteful and ineffective in making us forget about the terrible experience and dinner plates left half uneaten. 

In all this time, the servers never asked anyone if we wanted another drink. What a fail. 

Also, the restaurant space is cute, but they have some issues with noise level. I've been to many restaurants with open kitchens and high ceilings, but for some reason noises really amplify in this space. It was really hard to hear one another even when the place had pretty much emptied out. 

They have some work to do is all I can say.
Don't bother ordering in advance. I always place my order ahead and still wait 40 mins to receive it & something is always wrong. I use to think they were good.

Went here for my birthday back in September. Did not have a good experience at all. They wouldn't sit my party together even though the tables were right next to each other and could have easily been shifted. Took half of the tables drink order and just walked off and came back with double the alcohol drinks that no one ordered and then got mad at us. Again took only half of the tables order so everyone's food came out at different times. The waitress was very frantic and didn't seem like she could focus. The location was cool and the whole arcade scene but again, some of the machines took your coins and some didn't work. Overall i enjoy a good taco but the food was just basic. Gave it a two star mostly for the service, that really counts, i probably won't be back.
This is a great barbecue restaurant that has a marvelous brisket that is to die for. The prices are reasonable and they have a good selection. Seating is outside only at this time or take out.

Meh is the correct description for Arni's. My family and I have eaten at both the 96th St. and 86th St. locations about a dozen times and left disappointed each time. I don't get the hype. The pizza isn't that great, the salads are always served in warm bowls (I have a thing about lukewarm lettuce.. yuck!), and the service sucks. I'll take my family to Scotty's from now on.

Went here on a Friday night and it wasn't very busy. They have a great selection of craft beers on tap and the bartenders are very knowledgeable of the options if you don't know what you want. They also serve wine of beer isn't your thing. There is darts and a pool table here which are a lot of fun too. And don't forget the popcorn machine with free popcorn!
El servicio es pésimo.La comida sin sabor,Los precios muy altos y la espera es eterna.No lo recomiendo.

Have eaten there twice this month and both experiences were great.
Went for Sunday brunch first--cinnamon bread was warm and yummy, the biscuits with Meyer lemon jam was perfect (made a mistake and didn't get a jar to go that morning--remedied that mistake on my return visit).  Blueberry pancakes were fluffy and delicious and devoured by my 11 year old.  Pork hash with over easy egg was comfort food at it's finest.
Took my husband back for lunch two weeks later and had THE BEST BURGER EVER!.  Trying to figure out how to duplicate it at home since we live about 5 hours away...
Great, great food.

We have been going to Thida Thai for about 3 years and enjoyed every experience except for our past two. Both times we did an online order and have gone to pick up our order to find they didn't even start it after we waited the 25 min it stated it would take. Both times we got just an apology and asked us to wait another 10 min so they can make it. Ugh.. that is the last thing we want to hear being we did nothing wrong, they did. Tonight was the most recent experience. We went all the way home to find our food wasn't even at the heat level we asked for it was tasteless.
It's a McDonald's. This one has flashier menus and an inefficient kiosk ordering option, but other than that it's standard fare. Not good or bad, it's a chain and you get what you're supposed to.

I had really hoped Doson had moved onto Carrollton to fill the void left in the wake of Pho Tau Bay's failure to return to the area.  Like I had really, really hoped.

But alas Doson wasn't much more than slightly upscale Chinese with some Vietnamese on the menu.  Ah well, you live and you learn.  And i guess you can always drive to the west bank.

When my friend first told me he loved the fried rice here and I saw how plain it looked, I was a bit disappointed. But don't let that fool you! I took a bite and was instantly hooked. The rice is hard to describe, but it has a fluffy texture and it's addicting. Hands down my favorite. The chicken is good too. I don't like spicy so I've stuck with the ginger soy and the teriyaki. The orange chicken was really strong, even breathing it in can make me cough. They also have stamp cards where you get 6 stamps and you can get either free large fried rice or wings, so that helps my budget when I come here pretty often! I recommend trying it here at least once!

Great sushi and sashimi.
Super slow service. Disorganized (at least during late dinnertime).

The Oxford Exchange is such a cool place to go. It makes you feel like you are in a completely different place. There are a variety of different things to do there. You can have a meal, drink coffee or tea, get your shoes shined, or get some coffee that is really good. The atmosphere is unique and makes for a great place to study, work, or catch up with friends.

I basically came to Nashville with my wife on our Honeymoon for the hot chicken- and Pepperfire did not disappoint! Unbelievably delicious! The HOT chicken was perfection, as was the fried grilled cheese, crinkle fries, and green chile mac-n-cheese! I almost want to move to Nashville so I could eat here on the regular. The owner was super sweet and welcomed us too. Highly, HIGHLY recommend! Peppercheese Tender Royale for life!

We stopped in Boise on our way to telluride and stopped in at the white dog brewing for a beer and a bite to eat.  The beer was very good however the meal we got was very disappointing. We had the finger steak an Idaho original with a side salad of the 3 finger steaks only one was edible. The salad was typical spring mix with a few grilled tomatoes which tacked on an extra $2 to the meal. Unfortunately the wait staff hardly acknowledged the fact the meal was bad let alone offered to take it off the bill or offer a different option.  I am not knocking white dog too much because it is not their food but since they are serving it I would have hoped they would take some responsibility. I will definitely not be getting the finger steaks again.

Tyler's is just okay; no egregious issues, but also not memorable in any way. What keeps it alive and even crowded is decent happy hour prices and the fact that it's open late in an area that has very little else going on past 8:00pm. I've been here a few times with friends and service is consistently slow, even to just get a bottled beer delivered to your table. Servers seem a bit clueless as to what specials are happening and what beers are on tap. Sometimes they stand around talking to their friends, and more than once they've plopped themselves down at my table and  and expected to hang out with us rather than, you know, taking orders and serving customers... very odd.

There's a good beer selection, but it can be a little bit pricey if you don't stick to happy hour or drafts. Similarly, the food is way overpriced for what you get, and just generally isn't very good. I wouldn't be surprised if everything was frozen and microwaved to order, or else poured directly from a bag or can. If you stick to beer it can be a decent place to hang out with friends, as it is attractive and well maintained inside, but there are better places around town.

1. I enjoy a good drink. 
2. I like to do it in discrete locations sometimes.
3. The Mermaid is one of my new favorite discrete locations.

Nebraska Avenue may be known for prostitutes that walk up and down the street, but the only act of gratifying pleasure I would solicit on Nebraska is the wide variety of craft beer inside the walls of the Mermaid Tavern.

If you go often enough, the bartenders will get to know you by name.  They treat everyone like a good friend.  If you get hungry while you are boozing your day away, there is a small menu with delicious culinary confections.  

B. Major Grade:  A

More than I expected.  Hospitality, boasted chicken, great service and price.  A 5 star chicken experience for sure, albeit in a rustic but very clean setting.  Had lunch platter 1/2 chicken (breast + 3 large wings), unmistakably broasted to perfection, cob corn and broccoli sides served pronto.  Totally crisp, w moist, flavor sealed in.  $8.99 + drink.   Pizzas, Italian and country frIed classics as well.  Worth the cabfaire and a permanent stop on future visits.  Recommend without hesitation.  Bob from Texas

Baquet's did it, again. A meal to remember, and to want again. And again! The most scrumptious lasagna I've ever eaten.  Every mouthful a savored delight, and portions ginormous.  Fresh salad of mixed greens, brightened with their own dressing.  Crunchy crusted bread with pillowy soft middle.  Ended with a light and luscious strawberry layer cake.  All of this generously feeding 4 for just under $100.  Pre-COVID, we loved dining here.  But Baquet's continues to care for their customers with pick- up or free delivery of their fabulous meals.  Not only does it feel very right to patronize local restaurants,  but Baquet's also uses fresh local ingredients, boosting the TV economy and bolstering community.   They are the very best!

For an iconic New Orleans place, this didn't quite live up to the hype.  The Shawarma Pizza, Alligator Sausage Bao, Cobia Bundles, and Frog Legs were all highly creative and well made. None were that memorable that i want to go back for more. 

The service was excellent, as expected. The atmosphere was really lacking. There was a lot of energy and it was loud, but not in a cool way. There was too much exposure to the kitchen. I like to see them make my food, etc. - just not right in front of my face all night. Wolfgang Puck at Spago does the best job of combining the energy with the food. I expected more at NOLA. 

Pricing is reasonable for what you get - a decent value. I'll go again.
Great Lebanese restaurant serving halal. We tried the mixed grill with lentil soup and side of taboulleh. Everything was very flavorful.

One of our favorite stops in Fishtown! Not only are the people always friendly and welcoming, the beer flows as it should! What a wonderful beer garden filled with plenty of amenities such as ping pong and jenga. Would recommend stopping in if you are in the area!

Very good taste and efficient services.

Highly recommend oysters in all cooking styles.

Tang Bistro's been on my radar ever since it first opened. A lot of Northern Chinese spots seem to have opened up recently (South Silk Road, Blossom Northern China Cuisine and Chinese Crepe). TB specializes in Xi'an cuisine.

We came on a Tuesday evening and the place was half full. The inside is quite spacious and even has a patio facing out onto 109 Street (after all, it housed Urban Diner). The menu is beautifully done and more upscale than your normal Northern Chinese spot.

- Liang-pi (cold noodles) ($7.50) - crap, I didn't realize that you had the option of getting this non-spicy, mild, medium or intense! Would love to see how "intense" it really gets. The cold noodles had a chewy, slippery bite. Comes with the usual bean sprouts, julienne cucumbers and spongy gluten. Good but I prefer Noodle Feast's version.
- Cucumber salad with garlic sauce ($6.50) - the cucumbers had a satisfyingly crunchy bite. The vinegar/garlic sauce was bright and refreshing. Would get this again.
- Spicy pig ears ($9.50) - the spicy pig ears had a tasty chili oil sauce. Great texture but the portion was pretty small for the price. CC thought it came in a "ear shaped" bowl.
- Scramble egg & tomato ($10.50) with hand pulled noodles ($2.00) - the hand pulled noodles had a great chewy toothsome bite to them and the egg & tomato sauce worked well with the noodles. The combo felt like you were eating Italian with an Asian spin to it. The egg reminded me some sort of delicious cheese. I know that sounds weird but it was good.

The dishes are a bit on the oily side of things but everything was solid. Will be back to try more dishes. 3.5 stars.

Really fun spot.
Definitely a good start, but there does need to be some more entertainment options. The Nintendo was so much fun to play, but they need to snag more of them.
The drinks were all a bit sweet for my taste. But hey...it matched the SUGAR FUELED 80's and 90's...so fitting.

My boyfriend had food poisoning after dining here but I was ok... it took quiet a long time for the food to come out even the restaurant was pretty empty. Only one server was available during the time, food was good though.
I ordered the fish sandwich .. tons of breading and very little fish.. then I said well chicken tenders are error proof, wrong. The worst chicken tenders ever. I will forgo eating here again..
I love this place been going since I moved to Reno 4 years ago. Best service, best burgers..
While majority of business are closed early due to hurricane (Elsa), this business has no issues of having their pizza delivery still going. Sorry, but this is just WRONG.

Went here last night for nachos and sangrias for the first time in between doing an event with a friend. First time here. Smaller parking lot but the building is painted up pretty cool and unique which is perfect for downtown st Pete. They have happy hour Monday-Saturday 4:00-6:00 which include wine, I think beer and $3 house margaritas. Sunday's they have brunch 11:00-3:00 with bottomless mimosas for $12. 

Last night we had $7 sangrias (one of each) peach and the blackberry. Blackberry was my favorite. Nachos were $10 and added chicken for $3 and they were huge! My friend and I split it and were stuffed. We did get extra chips too. 

Service was amazing. She continued to come back and check on us and make sure we had drinks. Food came out quickly and a cool place to hang out.

Cute guys serving coffee. Big airy space.
East Nashville. There's a stage outside.
Artisanal chocolate. If you don't like tattoos, jeans, and artisanal stuff, go somewhere else. Iced coffee was delish.

I found this restaurant by happenstance while looking for good reviews on seafood restaurants on the beach.  The pictures looked good and I liked the disclaimer for 'fresh Florida seafood '.   I must admit I was pleasantly surprised. I thoroughly enjoyed my lobster roll.  It looked just like the picture and tasted better.  The SPECIAL tonight was crab cakes.  They were phenomenal.   I was mad there was no dinner (just appetizer).  If they ever add them to the menu that will be my go to.  Well back to the lobster roll...all knuckle meat.  I don't think any filler lobster shreds was in it. The staff was great.  My waitress' name was Hanna (Banana lol).  If you are lucky she'll be yours too when you visit.    I really liked this place...going back to sample their breakfast while I'm here.

Im gonna put this in short  i had  ordered a pie from here came with sour cream .buddy was at my door and he accidentally dropped it on the ground no biggy , i said id use my own . Best part he said he would clean it i said cool  tyvm . Closed the door he left  did not clean it . Called the restaurant and the manager told me to f-off because i wanted the driver to return to clean it . Real classy

Ad said there serving dine in seating. When I arrived after a 10mile drive,the chairs were all on top of the tables.,
I wasnt feeling it anyways. It seemed cold and dirty. Turned and left.

OK guys . . . this place is a gem.  The energy is high and the people are the best.  Great selection of a wide variety with a vegan spin on traditional New Orleans traditional recipes.  Great ambiance and they made me feel right at home.  Very reasonable prices.  The nachos were awesome and the eggplant poboy was delicious.  Thanks to Eric, Yimeil, Craig and Chef Ed for making me feel right at home all the way from San Diego.  I am going back tomorrow for lunch before I catch my flight back home to the land of the sun.

Namaste and the best of everything to you guys.

After a while walking through John's Pass, this was the perfect restaurant to end the day at. To start with, the people who served our food were very attentive and kind. The food was very good. The fries were some of the best I've ever had. I ordered the fish and chips and got three huge pieces of grouper. The fish was great batter was different than what I was used to. The restaurant itself was very clean and well decorated. Overall it was a good experience and I would recommend it to anyone in the area.

My friends and I came here for brunch twice on a 4 day trip to Nashville. The service was flawless, and the food was so delicious! The biscuits are the best I've ever tasted, as well as the grits, AND the jalapeño bacon ugggghhhh so good!  
The Blood Orange Mimosas and the Bloody Mary's were awesome!

Just went to Quinn's based on other reviews from Yelp.  I had the Pepper Steak, baked potato, bread, salad, and a beverage.  Everything was really good!  The steak was cooked to perfection. The service was friendly and fast. The atmosphere is definitely in the lounge or diner category, but it's clean and the place is pretty big.  I would definitely go back when in town again.
AWESOME!!!  Cheese fries were great!  I love how the were melted in the bowl!  My eggplant pesto and red pepper panini was GREAT!

Stopped in after a late change in plans Saturday night. One of the specials was a spicy  Bouillabaisse.  It was incredible! So much so that I asked them to email me the next time it is on the menu.  I wouldn't want to miss it. The chicken fajita salad was also delicious.  

The staff was right on top of everything.  It is a very friendly fun environment.

I shouldn't have been all that surprised, based on the brunch reviews, that this was a thoroughly disappointing experience, but I was. The two stars reflect the fun locale, the tea, and the pancake.
 
We did the buffet. I did not make the res, so I don't know if you had to decide ahead of time, but we were never offered a lunch menu or any other options. Our server was completely disinterested in the little bit of service that was expected. We had to ask for coffee and tea. The buffet never had plates at the ready, but no fewer than 3 servers were standing around doing nothing. At one point, the carver left his station to get plates because no one else seemed to care. It took forever for them to refill food items that had run out. And it was not even crowded. 

Pretty sure the chef did not taste anything. The eggs benedict was terrible, the jerk chicken had no jerk, and so on.  

In short, don't waste your money, at least for brunch.

Recommended by some locals.
Nope.
This place was okay. 
Ordered Frank's combo, filet mignon with shrimp drenched in a garlic butter sauce. 
I love garlic butter but this was overdoing it! 
All I tasted was garlic butter and I love garlic butter!
The sangria was okay.
The rolls and honey butter were okay.
The caesar salad was okay.
I can't believe this place has such a high rating. 
The service was so-so.
Won't return.
It is a nice place to hung out with friends and family.  I have been here many times.  It has a delicious dessert, especially,  Mas party

Went thrift shopping with some friends and we wanted something different for lunch I found twisted fork on yelp and everything that was order for the table was amazing I can't even tell you how crazy amazing everything that was ordered best place hands down our waitress was so kind and kept checking on us
They have some great dinners and sandwiches. Also some great specialty pizzas. Food and service is usually on point.

I am irrationally mad at their unclear and awful menu. First, brisket by the half pound is only two dollars more than pulled pork, but they charge you four dollars more to get it in the combo. Doesn't make sense. 

Further, the menu for the combo says "add brisket for 4 dollars" but no one would read that to mean "and subtract other meat option" which is what they somehow think you should understand. Family combos also don't say they will charge you four dollars more to add brisket, but they do. Made ordering a mess. I was angry and tired before even getting my food, which arrived cold. I hate to leave a bad review of a neighborhood spot, but dining there was frustrating.

Edited to add the business called me petty because I didn't like the menu but he didn't notice me saying my food was cold.... that is why it got a bad review.  I changed it to one star because of the yelp insult.

Second edit - Brian this is getting silly but I did tell your cashier about the problem. I told her your menu is awful. She shrugged and said that's the way it is. Why would I ask to talk to someone else when your staff has a bad attitude?  It was on her to say "we are aware and so sorry - let me get the owner to personally apologize and handle it." Just because I didn't rudely demand to speak with you when I told your staff I was unhappy doesn't make me the bad guy here. I did what I thought was appropriate to rectify the situation. Your staff chose to do nothing about it.

Had an amazing experience here the other night. Their salmon and goat cheese pizza is to die for! Service was great too and if you ever go, ask for Viviane. She was super friendly, attentive and knows her stuff. Loved their high ball glasses too. Very cool spot.

$15 agua de fresa and a chicken torta 
$12 for 3 tacos and a fountain drink 

Tacos were pretty good and sized pretty well 
Chicken torta sandwich was delicious 

Reason I took 1 star off is because this place closes at 10 and at 9:15pm we were still eating our food and they had 2 different people sweeping the floors next to us and even had a floor dryer on. There were atleast 10 patrons still sitting Down eating. Didn't like that.

Walked into Miel last night to buy birthday cake. Was staying at the Sofitel from out of town and it was recommended. I was in a great mood and was psyched for a birthday treat. Walked up to the front counter, was friendly, smiled and said hi and then "are these all the cakes you have right in here in this case?" motioning to the front counter. I wanted to make sure I was aware of all of the options before I chose. The cashier looks at me and rudely says "feel free to look around". Then goes back to her personal conversation. That's it. Just "feel free to look around." What kind of answer is that? How dismissive. There's 3 other display counters would it have killed her to explain oh here's our pound cakes but we also have this this and this. So at this point I'm offended and put off by the nonexistent customer service. I said "yes I can look around, but do you have additional cakes for me to look at?"  The counters are sprawling and I'm a customer asking her for service. I *could* aimlessly look around a shop I'm unfamiliar with. Or she could just answer my perfectly reasonable question. First she acts like I'm interrupting her personal conversation with her coworker. Then they look to each other like I'm the rude one. (Yes, I saw you mouth "wow." Which is hilarious given that you treated ME so poorly. Wow, indeed.) Completely unacceptable. Walked out. Got much better service and delicious cake from another bakery. I won't give my patronage to businesses that treat me like a bother and have no self-awareness about how they interact with guests.

The food here was excellent. My sister and I split a chicken dish that was topped with eggplant and mozzarella, and also a pasta dish. Both were delicious. My mom ordered a scallop dish that she really liked, and my dad ordered the veal shank which he loved. My only criticism was the service. The waiters weren't very accommodating, and not very friendly either.

Ok foodies, If you are in between Clearwater or Tampa or you don't know where you want to go?  head west on Hillsborough or East on Tampa Rd (same thing) and when you get in the middle, check this place out!  They have amazing tableside guacamole and reallly good drinks.  I had the shrimp and scallops with Jasmine rice,,, sooooo goood!  You will NOT leave here hungry!  But beware!  You will overstuff yourself cuz it is so good! It is waaaay better than Grillsmith.
Great Service!  Good prices
The corned beef sandwich is good but it definitely needed the dressing.  The meat on its own would be too dry.  I bet the pastrami is better.

First time in Chadds Ford for business, so I figured I'd try to find the best cheese steak I could. This place was a absolute homerun! I got the smaller size cheese steak, added onions and mushrooms with banana peppers on the side. Came with fries which were just as good and a pop to wash it down. Not just saying this, but I'd put this right up in the top list of best philly cheese steaks I've ever had.

Amazing ice cream, burgers, and sweet potato waffle fries. I was in town for a week on business and my co-workers took me here for lunch. I owe them a debt of gratitude because without them I would never have discovered this place.

Lines can be long around lunch and dinner... if you're able to take a late/early lunch/dinner then you can save yourself some time. Otherwise, be prepared to wait.

Ordered the chicken pizza, it was fantastic. 
Our server however was very sloppy and unfocused. Lots to improve there.

BEST BANANA FOSTER FRENCH TOAST!! I like to think I am pretty picky when it comes to food considering I attended 5 star chef events every year. This French toast is stuffed with banana cream cheese and I haven't had anything like it! 

PLEASE also order the Shrimp and Grits and eat them both together. These two dishes are the perfect balance between sweet and savory. 

Come here, order these two items and you will not be disappointed.
Amazing burgers. Try the bacon and peanut burger burger. Pretty good brunch dishes too. All the usuals plus some interesting breakfast sandwich options.

Visiting Tampa from western NY and was looking for some good NY pizza. I am very picky about my crust when it comes to pizza and am skeptical when I hear "NY pizza", because it rarely delivers.  Well Eddie & Sam's DELIVERED!!! The pizza was better than an I've ever had in NYC! Toppings were generous as well. Ordered wings also, and living near Buffalo I was wondering how their hot sauce would compare and I was pleasantly surprised. Amazing food! If/when I come back to the Tampa area I will definitely be hitting them up again!

Dined for breakfast only. Service wasn't too good and a little rude. Got the Irish Benedict (eggs Benedict topped with corned beef hash!) Although a little salty (hash is made in house) it was quite good! Prices are fair and the restaurant is set up nicely, very open.
Great pizza! I eat here almost once a week. Great variety of toppings. Quick and accurate service. Staff is very kind and friendly.

This is my favorite place to go. I love the sushi rolls and in my opinion they have the BEST fried rice. My favorite is the Hermitage roll. The prices are really good for the quality of food. The service is good, I really like the people who works there. They are nice to me and my family.

We were looking for a bar/restaurant to have some good seafood  and a view of the beach and we got it all. Seafood was delicious, tasty and fresh!! We had an amazing lunch. We didn't get to sit outside because it was full and we settled for the inside by the window and still enjoyed the view. Would definitely go there to cool off and have good food and drinks when I'm by the beach.
Tastes like regular takeout. Portions are okay. Didnt really enjoy it. Also gave us a stomach ache.

Recent first time visit, rather busy, but location isn't all that big, so it increases the hustle bustle vibe inside. Tacos are offered a la carte with many tasty options, as a result they add up on your bill quickly. Standard nachos were lacking in quantity and flavor, and also overdone. Drinks are tequila-centric, not bad overall but not up to par with the Philly cocktail scene. Sure, you don't have to cross a bridge, but the small location and near non existent parking make it a wash with going to El Vez, El Rey, Mission Taqueria, etc. for better fare all the way around. Decent for the Haddon Ave restaurant scene in general.

I've eaten at this Tijuana Flats location multiple times and have always had a good experience here. The service is always excellent and the staff does a good job of keeping the restaurant clean. My favorite thing on their menu is the flautas, and the last time I ate here I had their nachos which were good as well. The nachos I ordered could have done with more flavor. They should really salt their chips more. That aside, the food here is always good quality and enjoyable.
Tried to eat Zydeco Gumbo, but it was so salty I had to stop. Didn't mention it to waiter because I was with a large group. Others seemed to enjoy their selections.

Used to be a regular stop a few years ago, stopped by to try it out again.

Food is good and portions are normal. I have had better bread with breakfast at some of my other stops . 

They charge for refills of soda which we were informed after the second refill. Small cups, lots of ice. $1.60 × 2 small cups = unhappy. 

Passing by here as I can get better for less money.

This was by far the worst experience I've had at a coffee shop. I couldn't tell you how the coffee was because we never got that far. 

The barista who served us, and who we would come to know as the owner, Greg H., is best described as a surly snapping turtle, at best. We ordered our coffee and then began perusing the menu for sandwiches as we were hungry. Amidst our decision making, Greg informed us that breakfast sandwiches were only sold Friday through Monday, which contradicted what I had read when researching the cafe. No worries,  we'll just choose from the "exceptional lineup" of baked goods, which consisted of two types of bran muffins and two types of bagels, white and wheat. Slow down, not all at once! White bagel it is. As I go to reach for a bagel, Greg very condescendingly (remember, snapping turtle) points out that the sign in front of the bagels says do not reach into the jars. Should I mention that I have Stargardts disease(i.e. I'm going blind) and have trouble reading anything larger than cell phone sized text? Nah, Greg seems like he's got enough on his plate what with the four muffins he has to watch over. Ok I just want to get my coffee and leave at this point. 

As he starts to ring us up, my wife tells him that we bought the Groupon for $20 worth of products, to which he sighed and replied that it was only good for 4 individual visits of $5 per visit. Touché Greg, I'll keep playing the game. Well there were three of us so we'll use 3 of those and just forfeit the fourth one since we were just passing through NOLA and wouldn't be back. He refused, so we asked what we COULD get. He sardonically replied...$5 off everything. ...good ol' Greg. I said fine, but then I no longer want the hot coffee for myself, just the iced for my brother. He told me that he already made the coffee so I had to buy it. What?! I let him know what I thought of him and we went our separate ways. 

BE WARNED! When entering Cafe Luna you are exiting the real world and entering one which revolves around Greg H. and his complete incompetence when it comes to understanding basic social constructs. Or he could have been having a bad day. Either way, I don't enjoy coming across people like this in my life, and if I can gift to you all one thing, it would be that you don't have to either. Good luck!

I don't think I have ever given 5 stars before.  This little gem is probably the best restaurant in Reno and quite likely in a much wider area.  We loved it!  From the friendly greeting we were seated immediately.  Carol was great! We felt at home immediately.  Our server, Tim was quick, full of information, willing to chat but not at all pushy.  I ordered the special Fall drink, a nice fall pear vodka/apple/absinthe martini - perfect!  From there, everything arrived quickly and I could easily fill this small space with superlatives.    I don't eat meat, but do eat fish sometimes.  I was happy to see a vegetarian entree that looked wonderful.  After reading the entire menu, we had the fried cheese appetizer, shared a seasonal salad, then I went on to porcini dusted scallops (wonderful), he had the halibut and raved about it.  The accompaniments were perfect.  It seemed as though each dish was carefully thought out with regard to seasonings and portion, then cooked perfectly!  It's pricy, but worth it.  In fact, for a special occasion I'd consider driving there from the Bay Area just for dinner. 

Looking forward to going back.
Boil House was a great experience. The service was Great. Tim was excellent. Food was fair. I'd go back with out of town  friends.

Great food, great service! We had the vegetarian appetizer platter and everything was delicious. My kufta kabob was beautifully spiced and my friend really enjoyed her shish kabob. I loved that the waitress was attentive but did not try to rush us in any way-we had a nice long lunch complete with Turkish coffee and delicious sweets.
Love their omelettes and the fact you can substitute for an egg white omelette. Their mimosos are also yummy! Cute atmosphere and great service.

Well, DiNic's turn my blue eye black didn't they!

I returned here with a co-worker who was eager to try the sandwich with me.  We both plunged for the pulled pork, mine with greens and cheese, his just with cheese.  After STARING at the steaming piles of pork and fresh cheese slices, we finally had our meals after ponying up $8-$9.

After having a so-so experience with the roast pork, the pulled pork was like night and day.  The meat is more tender and with greens and cheese, they all compliment each other perfectly.  Whatever sauce they use, I could basically bathe myself in it, and it makes all the difference.  It's not too overwhelming, and accentuates the pork's own flavors.  Don't expect a heavy BBQ sauce by any means.

All in all, I'm very impressed, and am happy to have given DiNic's another shot.

We eat here nearly once a week
Highly recommend the egg rolls the rooster sauce wings and the Brussels sprouts and the shrimp tacos are freaking awesome. 
The guys are really nice.  Can get a drink at the bar. No kids though unless you sit out front.
The food was great! I had the barbacoa tacos, and were delicious. Good portions and reasonable price. We are definitely coming back whenever we come to Reno.

They are open for indoor seating, but it is very limited. So even on a Wed evening the wait was more than 1.5hr (we were told 45 min wait). They had a waiting list, but i guess all the folks ahead must have called in. The wait is shorter for non-BBQ grill, but for that i could have gone elsewhere. Its frustrating to be told we are next when there is an empty grill table that was just vacated. 

I'm sure the food is just as good as the last time we were here... but between the 2 workers.... service alone is sad. If you must have your korean BBQ fix, call ahead and expect long wait.

I am confused after reading most of the posts. I think the food is sub par for the price. I have tried several times. After each try I had to remind myself that I have yet to find something that I think is good. Why did I go back you ask? Someone keeps giving me gift cards. I have told them to stop because of the food quality. 

The one thing that they do have is a great patio / view when eating the sub par food.

If I could give a 1/2 star I would because to me that is the best that I could give them.

Another hidden gem - but this one is very specific. The rest of their dishes are pretty good but the one that really stands out is their calamari.

If you like the deep fried asian calamari, this place truely is the master.

Came for lunch on a Saturday and the place was empty. We ordered the pork belly baos and BBQ pork skewers. I wanted to enjoy the food more but the pork belly was all fat. The minute I picked up the the baos the buns were falling apart from the sauce and fat. For $8.50 we were only given two BBQ skewers and they were pretty small. I recommend KaBao Food Truck for better and tastier baos.

This is a great place to get lunch or dinner with friends. Affordable lunch specials and all you can eat sushi on Tuesdays! The staff is friendly and the sushi is prepared fresh. The atmosphere is relaxing and there is plenty of seating... With that being said it can get very busy on certain days so be willing to wait a few minutes and you won't be disappointed!

Ever since they first opened, I've been a diehard fan of this pub. They offer an extensive array of excellent food, beers, and cocktails. The staff is always friendly and helpful, and the service this business provides is always top notch! If you're in the Croydon area, I highly recommend the Dog and Bull.

The moment I first saw a big sign saying "MEAT", along with the words "beer, brisket, bourbon" underneath, it was lovely at first sight! 

They did not disappoint: the brisket is everything it should be, and the selections of both beer and bourbon are good. Go there, get yourself a pound of brisket and some Mac'n'cheese and a beer to wash it all down with.

My one caveat: even when not very busy this place is incredibly loud.

The food and service here was simply the best.  We had a large party and we were able to be seated quickly. The food came out hot and the server was very helpful in making meal selections. Would visit again!!!

I thought the tacos were three stars, but the prices, ambience and sauces were four stars. We passed through here hungry driving down the PCH. There was a perpetual line out the door on a Sunday afternoon -- clearly a favorite among the locals. The line moves quickly; these guys are efficient, which is also why I give them four stars for service.

This place is GREAT!

Come here if you want bare-bones, affordable, but perfect Mexican food. As far as quality-for-price, I don't think you can do much better in Tucson.

Seems family-owned, and like it is run by people who take pride in doing things right, being friendly, and in sourcing super-fresh ingredients. 

My recommendation is the Ceviche Tostado. Super-fresh! Squeeze some lime juice over that baby and you're good to go. Also, anything with the Al Pastor pork is good.

Keep up the great work, guys!

Ok so I'm slightly biased as I love Waffle House! We had been planning this trip for a couple months knowing we were stopping at at least one Waffle House! (We actually stopped at two!) We stopped for dinner. But of course we were eating breakfast! Can't come to the Waffle House and not have a Waffle?! The service was fantastic! Friendly and engaging! Very helpful like a small town buddy! I ordered the two egg breakfast with scrambled eggs, white toast, bacon and hash browns. We shared a pecan waffle. The bacon was perfectly crisp! The eggs were light and fluffy! I like my has browns crispy and drizzled with ketchup and they were the exact amount of crispness I wanted! I ignored the toast because let's face it! If I'm having a bread product at the Waffle House, I'm eating a waffle! So pecan waffle yes please! Omg the wonderful browned tastes crispy waffle with fluffy middle and crunch of pecan! Wow! All day long wow! I wasn't not disappointed! The only let down I have is I'm still two plus hours away from a Waffle House!
My favorite pizza place, I'm glad that you can still get it despite all the other locations closing
Excellent food for what I'd consider to be well-priced. Shocked for the quality of food that it was only $80 for a charcuterie board, 2 glasses of wine, and two entrees. Definitely coming back.

The food and service were very good. The bad review is for the manager with the short blonde hair barking orders at her employees like they are slaves. It actually made me sick to watch the way she talked to them right in front of customers at the bar. The employees seem miserable, no wonder it takes a bit longer to get drinks and food, no one can concentrate because this lady is constantly shooting down their confidence. The bartender was super friendly and attentive and at one point left the bar crying because the manager told her she wasn't making drinks fast enough, clapping her hands vigorously in her face as if to intimidate her. 

The tater tots and the drinks are great and the service is friendly, a little slow, but very accommodating and you can tell they care. I would never recommend sitting at the bar, solely because of the short blonde hair manager micromanaging and reprimanding employees right in front of the guests. As someone who has been in restaurant management myself for years it literally makes me sick to my stomach to see the way the employees are treated here.
My boyfriend and I ate here we had the breakfast Burger (I forget what it's called on the menu). This was exactly what we were looking for the food was great and the service was good!!

I am sooo upset I didn't take photos of the food! This review definitely deserves photos of their food! We were so happy with their eye pleasing dishes we just couldn't wait to dig in! My family a party of 9 went to this restaurant today. Nothing planned we drove to this area to visit Peddlers Village! Oh my goodness, the food was fantastic! Every single thing we ordered was so delicious! It's a little place way set back from the street, but it's always my experience that little places like this make up for the size and understated decor with their incredible food! My Compliments again to the chef!

The food was good but the service was terrible. My waitress left without saying anything in the middle of my meal. No one noticed that I had no server. My to-go order hit dat in the window. When I finally said something the exec chef came over. He said they would deal with her (whatever that means) but made no offer to discount my meal. I wasn't going to spell it out for him so I just paid and left with no intention of ever going back. Too bad too, I liked the ribs
Delicious, fresh and healthy. Never been disappointed. Very reasonable. Many vegetarian choices

I have been a happy Lucha Cartel customer for many years before I moved out of state. What made me white this review is our brunch experience during my recent visit to Philly.

We arrived at 11 o'clock in the morning, and the place was surprisingly packed for such an early hour. We were seated promptly, and our very personable waitress informed us it was an unplanned post-wedding celebration of 50+ people.

We ordered drinks and food and prepared ourselves to wait, given the number of customers. To our surprise, the food started to arrive before we knew it and was as good as always.

You could tell the staff was a bit overwhelmed serving so many customers but handled it very professionally. Not only our waitress but a manager checked on us multiple times to make sure we were doing all right.

Lucha Cartel did not disappoint once again, and will remain one of my favorite spots everytime I'm in Philly.

decided to give this place a shot.   already a bunch of taco places on 4th so wasn't sure we needed another one.   but holy amazing tacos Batman!!!   this place blows all the others away.   first off they have the softest tortillas I have ever experienced.   absolutely delicious.   I tried several different tacos.  huge menu so easy to do.   fried pork.   grilled shrimp.  steak.  thry all have names but I just remember that each one was better than the last.   it was crowded but line moved pretty fast.  girl at register very helpful and made good suggestions.   had my first Florida snowball.  won't spoil the surprise but definitely have to get it.   won't disappoint.   overall this place is now not only my favorite taco place on 4th but my new goto spot in st pete!

Best pizza in Nashville.  In fact, it's probably the best brick oven pizza I've ever tasted.  My favorite is the Pomodorini pizza but everything here is spectacular.  The only downside is that they close as soon as they run out of dough.  So, make sure you don't wait around to go if it's a busy night of the week.

I'm staying with a relative who is a patient at East Jefferson General Hospital. I ordered the Crab and Corn Bisque. It was delivered right to my grandmother's hospital room, by a very courteous gentleman. 
The soup was DELICIOUS! The gigantic lumps of crabmeat definitely made me happy! I would definitely like to try more from their menu!

We went here for my daughters birthday. Wifey had a great time and loved all the food!
Service was awesome and prompt!
Food was excellent for a good price!
A must try!

My immediate impression when walking inside: one part Japanese video game, one part Hoarders episode, one part passive aggressive notes a coworker leaves on the office fridge. 

They really like to decorate with little notes telling you not to do things (no dining in for under $10, no waiting on a large group at a table when everyone isn't there yet, no breathing -- OK, I made that one up). The same notes are posted in 3 places in every single booth. I was kind of scared I'd accidentally do something to anger whoever wrote these notes, but I was able to eat here without incident.

Also, there is pork in the ramen. They make this abundantly clear in the 50 notes posted around the restaurant saying this. Maybe just put that on the menu?

Honestly, the crazy notes kind of make this place charming. I can't help but make a little fun of it though. :)

The sushi is pretty good. And quite cheap. No rolls were over $10. It's a decent place to grab sushi if atmosphere doesn't matter much or if, like me, you feel like skipping out on the gym and eating sushi instead (it's located next to Gold's).

The servers were really friendly, and the place looked really nice. I enjoyed the traditional Japanese feel and the seating where you could view the cooks!

However, this may have been just by chance but my ramen soup was salty, the noodles were hard and slightly undercooked, and the meal itself was bland. I got their signature dish, which I believe was called Terakawa.

The Takiyaki wasn't bad though.

Initially we tried to hit Anthonino's Tavern nearby, but we weren't about that 1 hour wait life. Being in "The Hill" area or essentially Little Italy, there were plenty of other options so we decided to check out Zia's after calling in to see if there was a wait for a table for 2. "No wait you say? Be right over!"

From the get go, I had really high expectations for this spot and was looking to carb up on some hearty Italian food. Initially I was quite impressed with our toasted seafood ravioli stuffed with shrimp and crab meat and a generous side of melted butter, but from here it kind of was a downward spiral. Our starter Dinner salads were pretty good the first initial bites but had way too much house Italian dressing. By the time you got half way through, the salad was swimming in dressing. 

For entrees, the lady did a seafood pasta which tasted amazing initially, but once you got to the seafood to find imitation crab meat and the itsy bitsy shrimp it made me wonder how quality that toasted seafood ravioli we just had really was. For myself, I did the Pesce Maria ~ 8oz filet of Icelandic cod, breaded, baked, topped with white wine butter lemon sauce, Italian cheese, red peppers, artichokes, broccoli, tomatoes, & mushrooms. While it looked good when it came out, the first thing I noticed was how damn fishy it smelt. Not the most pleasant thing, when you're starving and just want to dig right in. After a few bites, I was convinced the fish wasn't fresh and didn't have the sort of tenderness and delicacy you'd expect. I suspected the fish was previously frozen and possibly old. Needless to say only made it through half of it as it was really unappetizing to eat. The sauce was pretty bland to be honest and the veggies... Those artichokes and mushrooms... Canned for sure. After that, the only thing I could think about was where else did they skimp out? I didn't even bother with the side of pasta it came with. This has to be the first time in awhile, I've refused to finish my meal and even take home the leftovers. 

So to recap... skimping out on fresh ingredients for a less than mediocre meal and an $80 bill for two. Ouch.

'Til next time. No cheers for you Zia.

234/365
The very best of New Orleans.  Great entertainment and drinks every night.     Enjoy the dialing piano bar at night and the courtyard by day.
Best place in my area for seafood- short of driving into Philadelphia. Fresh, great selection and very helpful staff.

I'll keep this review short and sweet. This place had fantastic service. The bartender was friendly, professional and fast. I had the French dip sandwich and it was fantastic. Prices aren't too steep (considering its on coast village). Great for a sunny afternoon outside and the interior is very well done.

If I could give this a -1 I would. The new owners obviously have no idea what they are doing. 
The gluten free ideas on the menu are no longer gluten free even tho it's advertised that way. Be ware as this will make you ill. 
The condiments are a mess, so badly so that  I'm not sure they are even sanitary. I'm not sure about anyone else, however, I sure don't want to hear the new owners yelling across the restaurant what people need or ordered. Pretty sure that's what the wait staff is for. 
I give it 3 months before they are closed.

I went there on Sunday.  Prob the first nice day this year so far.  The atmosphere was nice, the service was horrible (very slow).   Also, I didn't expect the place to be an app and sandwich place.  We ordered the lobster rolls which were good but very small. At $13, I guess you get what you pay for.  We also had to order cheese fries because NOTHING comes with your sandwich.  Free refills you ask?  NOPE!  We never got our refills we asked for, yet were charged.  We brought it to the servers attention and it was fixed, but $2.50 for a drink with no refills?  For real???  

Needless to say we left there still hungry.  I guess if you are looking for a place to have a few drinks and apps with friends, then this would be a great place to go.  As for dinner?  Nah... unless you'd like to spend an arm and a leg for the additional apps and fries you will need to go with your sandwich.  Oh and the $7.50 on iced teas you will need throughout the meal.

One of our fav quick & tasty ice cream stops! So delish, and it's a Pokestop!  The Twirls are so good, the medium is pretty big, and you get 2 toppings included, additional toppings are $0.75!  The ice cream is so... "smooth" idk how to explain it but every bite is just so perfectly smooth, I just want to keep eating it!! They do a points system for rewards, and free cone ON your birthday. I haven't tried any of their other fun creations like the waffle taco or anything, but they look pretty good!  I really need to branch out and try new things but I am stuck on getting what you see in my Yelp pics here, the medium Twirl made with chocolate ice cream with toppings of Heath, Pecan Pralines, and sometimes cookie dough.  I have tried my husband's small Twirl made with vanilla ice cream, Oreo, and cookie dough, and that was so good I might have to switch it up and start putting Oreo in mine too!
It's adorable shape, pumping tunes for cool, fun hang outs, sassy lights, and adirondack chairs make this a frequent stop for us for a quick dessert treat.

One of the best phos I've ever had! Houston has great pho and I've tried pho in many a places, cities, and countries and this is by far one of my favorites now. I got the filet mignon pho andOH MY so delicious!! And how it's served! The broth, meat and noodles are all served separately. The meat was filling,tender and juicy, broth was piping hot in a clay pot and plenty of noodles. I'd suggest to cook the meat to your liking first, take it out then add it to your noodles (in portions). I slightly cooked mine in the piping hot broth, took it out, added some noodles and divided my meat (in the pot and on the plate to eat separately).

I love the Ugly Crab. I have been here a couple of times and the food is excellent every time. Love the crab legs and shrimp. And the Potatoes and Corn on the Cob also. The seasoning is great and actually is spicy, which I love. The employees working are always so kind and sweet and excellent at recommendations. If you want good seafood near Indy, go here and you won't be disappointed!

Only giving two stars because I feel really mean leaving one. We waited a few minutes to sit as the waitresses all just kinda looked at us like who's gonna sit them? We were seated in a booth beside a large table that had yet to be bussed. There was trash on our table from the previous customers but we were hungry and were sat in the mostly empty restaurant. We did however have our eventual waitress bring out a trash can right in front of our table for her to bus the table, but it just sat there before she bussed the table. Super appetizing. We waited another 10 minutes for our waitress to take our order and I even said nicely, oh I thought you forgot about us!" My husband ordered our food and my food came out rather quickly but his didn't come out for another 10 minutes at which that point I had finished my food. Our waitress checked in on us twice total. The restaurant was dead but all of the girls there were more interested in speaking to each other or the tables with guys (I was the only non employee female there). My experience in the past has been super friendly waitresses who are super attentive and I felt like baby if I wasn't there my husband would have gotten better service. As my hubs said as we left, food wasn't terrible but the  service was awful. Never going back.

Such a gorgeous space with amazing small kitchens lined up along the walls. We loved our Haitian breakfast and can't wait to go back to try their fish meal. I splurged on oysters for my baby and they did not disappoint located at the seafood counter. This place houses so many tiny food delights such as gourmet Thai, BBQ, a bakery that makes giant cookies, tacos...and so much more! I don't know if they have closed b/c of the pandemic and we probably won't go back anytime soon sadly but will do once the all-clear to hang out in public spaces is declared. This place is a treasure. The building itself is so pretty and well-lit. It would make a great date night too.
We love this place! We always come when we are in town! Great food, drinks and atmosphere! Definitely worth the wait!!

My wife and I went to A Taste of Thai for lunch on Monday. We were quite impressed right from the moment we walked in. The place is very clean and nicely decorated, I had the Drunken Noodle lunch (all lunches are $7.95) with pork, prepared Hot, and an egg drop-like soup. It was absolutely fabulous and everything tasted very fresh.  My wife had the Tempura appetizer with shrimp ($14.95). It was easily enough food for two people. It came with a house salad, which featured a vinegarette-mayo dressing that she couldn't stop raving about. Service was excellent. We will definitely return soon.

If you want great quality sushi and personable service- go here! Small little sushi bistro with very knowledgeable sushi chefs. Probably some of the best sushi you can get in Clearwater. Very fresh and  solid options!
Yet another amazing Cuban place . Very authentic food, friendly people and the fresh food market is neat. Wish the county didn't put their foot down on the fruit trees they sold

Took the family here tonight. Ordered 6 main courses and each one was fresh, flavourful, and not greasy or salty. Recommend:  Ginger beef, chicken curry, wok vegetables, oat chicken. Appetizers:  curry puffs. Will definitely be back and will tell our friends.

CPK is my kid's favorite resto. It's sort of automatic for me as far as what to order. I always get the same thing pasta with garlic cream sauce with chicken and mushrooms. The difference is in the service. The particular day that we came by we were seated immediately, orders taken right away, our drinks refilled promptly... Good visit for us this time :)

We went there with a party of 9. They said it was going to be a hour weight,  which was fine because we didn't have a reservation.  An hour and a half later they said if we wanted to be seated soon we would have to split up to 2 tables nowhere near each other by the way. If we wanted to do that we could have been seated an hour earlier.  So for that they comped us a order of tater tots.

Great atmosphere, great staff, and awesome food! I visited a week ago and still am thinking about the pizza! I loved the Drunk Duck drink as well! I would recommend this place to anyone who wants to go watch a game, have a beer, and socialize.

I'm not usually a coffee drinker so I tend to get a little overwhelmed in coffee shops. I just don't know what I like. 

At Steadfast, I've ordered the coffee soda twice and have very much enjoyed it. Foodwise, I've tried the polenta porridge with a poached egg and the gravlax platter. I was impressed with each, but I wish that the gravlax platter were served with a little bit more substantial bread. I found myself hungry a few hours after eating it. On my last visit, my friend had the egg sandwich, and it looked insanely good. I'll definitely try that next time.

The workers are very nice, but they definitely take their coffee seriously to the point where it is almost comical. 

It's very well done on the inside but does not give the coziness that I would want to spend a full day working there. It's also slightly pricey.

You know that a place is pretty awesome if I leave downtown and drive all the way to the north side to go. 

So here is the problem with Big Lug: I can never decide what to order because the menu has so many tempting options. What's even worse is that the weekly specials are even more tempting because you have to order them before they disappear forever (once there was this pork tenderloin on a tarragon waffle with pancetta and herb mayo...). Whatever I finally decide to order, I know it will be a generous portion of really good food. 

Besides the food, you can always count on solid beer, excellent service, and a great atmosphere. 

Now if only there was a downtown location...

Food was absolutely delicious and the drinks were amazing! Very varied drink and dinner menu! There was definitely something for everyone. The only think I think they need to improve on is timeliness. We had a dinner reservation on a Wednesday night and it was quite empty. Drinks took a little too long to get in between and the food even longer. Other then that, it was a good experience!

We continue to visit because it's never a disappointment.  Last night we stopped in for dinner to find the restaurant seating had been rearranged which is really nice.  And there are new items on the menu. Great changes and additions keep up the great work!
I usually get the tuttomare but tonight it was horrible. Only 1 shrimp few mussels and noodles were clumped together. Totally not worth the money. So disappointed

Vegetarian Spicy tofu stew was delicious.  Kimchee as well.  I ate everything.  The cooks were so thoughtful, and it is very much like eating in someone's kitchen.  Realized there is likely fish sauce in the stew and also anchovy in the kimchi but I let it go.

If you're looking to take classical dishes and add layers of flavor and emotion to them, then I think Edison Food Lab is the place where you want to eat. Their classic signature dishes, as the pork belly braised kimchi amazingness or their mixology selection, such as the Violetta, are all amazing and will definitely surprise you. Overall, definitely recommend this to any adventurous food lover, 10/10 would definitely repeat.

Fantastic beer variety, which makes a small selection go a long way. The atmosphere is on the upscale side of casual. Rabbit was fantastic. Pepperpot soup could have used a bit more kick.

I ate  here shortly after they opened. Service was top notch. Meat and cheese plate looked good enough to tempt me, and I never order those.

I went to Percy Street back in January for Restaurant week, which was an amazing deal and one of the best barbecue meals I'd ever had.  We had the brisket fries, mac and cheese, combined to a full rack of ribs, tried four of the sides, and two desserts and we were stuffed with food left over to spare.  I was ecstatic and couldn't believe they gave us a $10 off coupon for our next visit.

My boyfriend and I went last night to use it before it expired, and I was really disappointed to see that the menu has completely changed.  Our waitress was really polite in explaining that it was so people could have appetizers instead of being forced into sides, that the little shot glasses full of sauce were more sanitary than the four bottles they used to bring you (especially with regards to gluten contamination); all of these were good points (although I loved their sweet barbecue sauce!).  But the menu now feels like some bourgeois barbecue place, with $10 sandwiches and $4 sides à la carte.  Whereas before at Percy Street everything felt generous, now it feels really sparing and not ideal.
