There was no napkin and no silverware.  Minor details but quite frustrating after a very long day at work.  It was being delivered to an office address so you'd think they'd include a napkin and a fork!!!
I called the restaurant and was told the driver would return with the dressing. Twenty minutes later, I had waited long enough and wanted to go home. New Haven, see you next week for pick-up!
I go here more times than I can count! Great soup dumplings. Super inexpensive! My son and I go here often. There's always a long line for good reason. Worth the wait!

Buckle up ya'll, this is going to be a bumpy review. 

After reading a rave editorial about Sangrita on the Indy Star website, a fellow yelper and I decided to drop in on their second day of biz to see what the buzz was about. 

Crazed for tacos and tequila, we were greeted by the sweetest hostess who took our phone number and told us she would text is when our table was ready (yay, technology!) So, in the interest of tequila, we went to the bar to check out the libations. And whoa. This was the best part of the evening! I got the La Pipa, a refreshing mixture of classic margarita and coconut/pineapple juices. Guys... Mind blown. My friend got the blood orange margarita and it was equally mind blowing. 

After a few sips, we were seated (rather faster than we expected which was nice!) Here comes the disappointing part. We were seated in the bar area (essentially a long L shaped couch with square coffee tables as the pace settings.) Promptly we ordered and received our house salsa (because you always have to try the house salsa) and it was a little lackluster. We added some of the orange hot sauce (yum), which brought some much needed flavor to the mix. 

We ordered our main dishes within ten minutes of being seated. We both ordered the skirt steak tacos, but I chose the crispy rice and pinto beans for my accompanying sides whereas she chose the black beans and the elotes. The waitress, god bless her, at the 75 minute mark of waiting for our food to come, came to offer us some fundido on the house for our wait, which we accepted. This fundido was probably to tastiest portion the meal. The oil they drizzle on top was excellent. I would absolutely order the fundido over the salsa any day!

But alas, we were still an hour and a half into our food order and still no tacos. All the tables around us, who had in fact been seated after us, had received their food. But we poor lasses were still without taco. We had essentially arrived at the point where we were just going to pay for our salsa and leave, when lo and behold our food arrived. 

I expected that after waiting an hour and a half for our food, that it was going to be some damn good tacos. But it seemed our disappointment was destined to continue. The steak was overcooked and tough, seemingly flavorless besides the crema on top. The crispy rice was also lusterless. The pinto beans, however, were the saving grace. Spicy and savory, exactly what I was expecting from a place boasting their culinary superiority. 

At the end of the day, our meal was comped since we had waited so long for our food. We never did get a solid answer on why that was exactly. We suspect they lost our ticket, I'm chalking it up to the fact they had only been open two days. I suspect once they get the kinks out of the system, they'll have 4 and 5 star potential.
If you're military and used to getting a temporary pass all other locations.... this location isn't military friendly and will not allow a temporary pass.  GARBAGE

Olivia is an exceptional server; a real asset to this establishment!
The meal was rather tasty. I ordered the Alfredo with blackened chicken; which was very delicious.
It was a great way to spend an afternoon among friends!

As far as food trucks go, this one is okay.  They make  comfort food which  is good but nothing that will blow you away.  The best  thing that we had was the chicken quesadilla.  The triple  grilled cheese was decent but nothing you couldn't make at home for a lot less. We were not a fan of the mac and cheese. Just had a funky taste. If you are looking for great mac... try Mac Mart!

We had an amazing meal at this place!  The steak salad was to die for!!!  Perfectly seasoned and grilled sliced steak, in a blue cheese dressing, With deviled eggs. I had a grilled chicken, bacon and avocado wrap. Every thing was delicious! But even better, was the service. We had an awesome server named Marina. She made us laugh and helped us with our meal selection. She did not steer is wrong. Will be going back for sure!

We are frequent visitors of boardwalk pizza in Clearwater... I still like their pizza but their service can be down right bad. So we have been on the look out for a new New York style pizza , after driving by Big Romans many times, my boy friend finally decided to give it a try! Boy am I glad he did! This place is spotless and the cheese pizza hits the spot for me!  And the staff is down to  earth n friendly, score ! We ordered  a large cheese pizza for 12 bucks! Delicious ny style! I really liked the sauce n cheese n crust, oh that's everything isn't it! The have a special for two slices and a drink ... at the lunch hour on certain day! I think that is more then far! We will be back for sure

When I first walked in, I was impressed by how fancy it looked.  With such decor, I expected this place to be first class Indian food -- I was waiting for  the best Indian food ever.  However, it was ordinary.  Not bad food & servers were really nice.  I can't say I have plans to come back.

If I were to leave this review solely based on the taste of the food, I would give it 5 stars.  Unfortunately, everything that leads up to actually being able to taste the food leaves so much to be desired.  I understand we are living in "different" times, but COVID has been going on now for more than a year.  You'd think they would have worked out some of the bumps by now.  Ordered through the website.  Easy!!  Received an email within seconds confirming the order and letting us know that it would be ready for pick-up in 20 minutes.  Waited, got in car, drove to Manayunk and went in to get our order.  Was greeting by a "hostess" who informed us that it would be another 45 minutes before food was ready.  We were told that there is a "problem" with the website and that estimated pick-up times are not correct...but that the problem "cannot be fixed."  We were also told that it was "the dinner rush."  I complained and asked to speak with a manager since the "hostess" seemed less than interested that customers were taking time to drive over to pick up food that was not even close to being ready.  After waiting about 3 minutes for anyone to come back, the "hostess" returned holding a bag with our entire order.  I will say this - based on what we ordered, it would have been impossible for the kitchen to have prepared our entire meal and pack it up in the 3 minutes she was gone.  Sadly, this was not the first (or even second) time that we have expereinced issues with an order.  From food not being ready to food being cold, we probably won't return.  It's really a shame since the food is tasty.

Apparently the staff can't use a clock. Every time I place an order ahead of time I'm still waiting 45-60 minutes for my food.

This has happened multiple times and today is the last straw. I won't be returning.

So my and my guy have decided that each time we go out to dinner, we would try something different.  So we get on yelp and see what's nearby.
I would have never picked this place because it is just off the main road and in a strip plaza with an auto tire shop and a music center.  
Looks are deceiving.
This place is a gem!!!  
Italian and Greek came together and had a baby and it's called Romanos Restaurant.
The palm ceviche was chunky bits of hearts of palm, grilled shrimp...so so good...radish, grilled pineapple...o.m.g. it was good.
I then had the bruschwtta and salmon and honestly it was very different bruschetta but I'm down for new things....so so good...the salmon was cooked perfectly...the chicken parm was to die for good...the sauce was perfect and it had grilled tomatoes in it that I fell in love with.
The Baklava was probably the best I have ever had.  My guy had never had it before and the ice cream with what I think was crushed pistachios was the best compliment to it.  They also had a Ukrainian layered cake but there was no way we could have gotten two desserts.  I was full when I left.
Danyelle was our waitress and I'd like to give a shout out to her!! Awesome through and through.  It's so nice to get a competent, efficient waitress and she did not disappoint! Give that girl a raise!!!

Thank you so much for great food. Y'all were so sweet too. I'll be back. I live in Salt Lake City but when I'm home it's great to have a place you know has food you like and can eat. You're not over priced but perfectly priced. I more than enough food. I had the smoked almond wrap. So tasty and full of flavor. Thank you again.

We stumbled across the restaurant because of being hungry, in pain and exhausted  (aka it wasn't too far from our hotel).
Fans were on full blast when we arrived,  a welcoming feeling after being outside in the hot humidity! 
Our server was Evelyn! I don't know where to start when it comes to her! Let me put it this way, once Evelyn began catering to us, I didn't take notice much on the details of the restaurant! Yeah it has plenty of televisions for the sports fanatic but what made us TRULY APPRECIATE THIS PLACE WAS DUE TO EVELYN'S DESIRE TO PLEASE!
The grandson saw there was BBQ ribs offered here on the menu, one of his all time favorites! When he asked for ribs he was informed they couldn't offer it because they were out of their house BBQ sauce. Holding back the tears and trying not to quiver his 7 year-old lip he opted for shrimp instead. Evelyn took notice and went into action! 
She said she would see what she could do because she didn't like how disappointed he was. I told her if it could or couldn't be done to not mention it but rather surprise us all because I couldn't bare to see him disappointed again. In the meantime, she took the remaining order and we asked if we could sample the Yaya Gumbo as none us ever had gumbo before and we were definitely curious. She said no worries and returned with a small bowl for us to sample! Now I know why the call it Yaya ! Ya I want it again and should have ordered that instead of pork chops! 
It appeared our meal was going into 40 minutes to arrive but when it did oh my!
What did Evelyn do?! She walked out with a plate of ribs for the grandson! She told one of the cooks how upset our grandson was when he was told he couldn't have the ribs. The cook decided to take it up in himself to whip up his own BBQ sauce fro. Scratch to ensure the grandson got his ribs!! 
Evelyn you are truly a SAINT!! She ended up with a double tip because my husband and I both wanted to express our appreciation!!!

Seriously understaffed on a Thursday nite! The evening started well enough, 6 plates came out at a decent pace ..shoshito peppers were delish, as were pork tacos, teriyaki chicken wings, garlic chick wings, seafood skewers and yummy fried rice. But then a party of 20 came into the back and the restaurant filled up and our server Josh B could not keep up. We asked for a 2nd plate of wings and it took 40 min - we asked for water 5 times before getting any which was discouraging as Josh set  6 bottles of water on the table of 20 even after we asked and still hadn't received any. The second plate of teriyaki wings was not as good as the first, the sauce was not as rich and they weren't cooked with the dark sweet edges.. One wonders how the same dish on the same night could taste and look so different. Come early and don't "add on" after your original plate count - drinks were very good and I might have ordered another had I been able to drink a glass of water in between. I'm happy that they are doing so well, but the poor service made the experience underwhelming.

Little Thai stall, decent variety, great taste, even better price! Hard to beat LEMONGRASS CHICKEN SOUP for only $3!!! It was packed with so much of flavor & the quantity was killer for that price!

Returned a 2nd time to try out some entrees. All the food displayed on the counter looked appetizing! We tried the SALMON CURRY ENTREE- grilled salmon with steamed broccoli over steamed white rice with yellow curry poured over top of everything. You can get steamed shrimp as an additional $3. 

Overall, the experience both times were satisfying and the food tasted great. Definitly will keep this place in mind when bringing friends.! The line apparantly usually wraps around the block - probably on weekends.

This place was a drive for me but it was so beautiful.  I can see why this would make such a nice wedding venue.  Eating outside on the deck was a pleasure.  Even in the heat, it wasn't that bad.  The huge fans they have set up everywhere helped with that.

The food here was pretty solid.  It took a while to get to the table, but the wedge salad was really good.  Generous amount of blue cheese and everything tasted fresh.  The gator bites weren't bad but didn't really blow me away.  

I didn't try the wine but the beer list was more than enough for me.  

The people here were nice enough to set up a large table for my friends and me to play a game of Dungeons and Dragons.  Great environment for friends and family. 

If you're willing to make the drive to Plant City and you need a nice venue for a get-together outdoors, I'd say this place is perfect.

Food was good (a little pricey) but the service was slow. Took 3 requests to get a water and my wife's food came after everyone else was done. Plus, they tried to charge us for a $20 rack of ribs that we did not order. Gave 3 stars because the manager made it right and discounted our bill.
By far one of the best sushi restaurants in town. Love the funky margarita. No one else can get this right. Stuffed mushrooms are beyond tasty. Food is super fresh and the staff is super nice.
This place is outstanding! We absolutly love it and enjoy this place being located in the neighborhood...BEST CUBANS

I've been to Sunda twice now and feel ready to give them a 4 star review. They did a great job with the interior and it definitely feels like a large upscale restaurant and not Cantina Laredo revamped. Our first experience was the week they opened and we sampled some sushi, the miso bronzed cod, and sashimi. It was a good sampling but everything was pretty pricey and the service was a bit too much where someone was checking on us every few minutes. But it was their first week and I know they are new and a bit more hands on the first week. 
Our second visit was on a Friday night and we sat at the bar. We ordered the devil's basket with crispy soft shell crab on an odd bed of crispy noodles that weren't edible and a ton of hot peppers. It was a strange dish and one I wouldn't recommend. But luckily the tuna truffle pizza was absolutely delicious and I wished was double the size because it was so tasty. I would highly recommend this! We also had some dim sum options, the lumpia was similar to fried egg rolls with a sweet dipping sauce and butter leaf lettuce and that was great and a large portion. The shiitake edamame dumplings were also delicious but we ended up sending back the oxtail pot stickers because they were odd and not our preference. I decided I needed more food so we had the spicy "tale of two tunas" roll that was a great decision because it was highlight of the meal. It had just enough fresh fish mixed with the unhealthy stuff (spicy mayo) but didn't feel too fried or too mayo filled. It was the perfect balance which can be difficult to do. I would highly recommend that you get this roll if you are looking for sushi. 
Overall the dishes at Sunda are very hit or miss, but the hits are really great and delicious! The biggest downside is that you are paying a lot of money for the misses. Like the devil's basket at $22 for some fried soft shelled crab that isn't that great. Overall I think they are good but be prepared to spend some money and be wary of what your order. If it sounds weird it may be more about appearance than taste.
This place is delicious! We had the hummus and the Gyro salad. The salad was excellent and the hummus could've used more flavor but the consistency was on point.

We always have great service but Friday evening we joined the waitlists for three and requested a booth. The girl that sat us took us to a table. I said we requested a booth can we move to one of the empty booths, there was at least three. She said no, booths are for four or more people. We assumed it was a new rule and sat at the table and had awesome service from Sarah. As we left there were four booths with three or less people. It just turned us off because we have eaten here several times and had never been told that.  We request a booth for a medical reason so if you really need four or more I guess we can't eat here again.

This was our first time going to Toma. I've heard amazing things about it for a while and am so glad we finally made it happen. We called the same day on a Tuesday
for a 7:30 reservation and the female host was so nice and accommodating. Gabriel was our server and was so knowledgeable about the wine list and food menu. We had the ahi tuna cones, the rigatoni, and the scallops and I can't stop thinking about how amazing all of our choices were. The food runners/bussers/support staff were awesome as well. Can't say enough good things about this place.

Terrible experience. You would expect that a recently remodeled location would want to provide an excellent experience but this was far from the case. It took nearly thirty minutes for our drinks to arrive, they were amazingly slow to be refilled, our orders were in complete shambles. To top off this awful experience, our friend's ticket was charged a ten dollar tip when he had left a two dollar tip. Stay away from here. You are better off going across the street to McD's than to waste your time and have your money stolen.

Some of the best value for food in all of Nola.

Felipe's follows the highly popular Chipotle fast casual choose-your-burrito-fillers checkout model but THE FOOD HAS FLAVOR.

Every potential burrito stuffed item is seasoned very well, and most of the non-burrito items, such as nachos, tacos, taco bowls, etc. are great value as well.

Go with the Chicken Tynga in your burrito over the classic Chicken. Chicken Tyna = shredded chicken soaking in a spicy chipotle seasoned sauce that is delicious. The queso and guacamole are as good as you'll find anywhere.

I would definitely recommend this place to anyone coming down here. Filet was phenomenal, as were the potatoes au gratin (just don't ask how much cheese & butter goes into them). Not in the French Quarter, but totally worth the cab ride! Both the manager, Glenn, and the owner, Matt, were super nice and our waiter, Steve, was great too! Cannot recommend this place enough!

I'm not sure what happened to this restaurant, the food used to be really good and there was good service and it was pretty cheat. It used to cost about 9-13 dollars a person depending on the time of the day and now it's 20 dollars a person. You only get one drink now that's in a bottle instead of when they used to bring you drinks with refills. Hot wok also used to be my favorite sushi place to go to where I could eat all my favorite rolls but now there's only about 6 rolls that barely stay together and taste disgusting. This restaurant has seriously gone downhill bad.

Service was horrible! We were not greeted when we walked in the door. They just stared at us and pretended to look busy. After five minutes I went to say hi and they didn't say anything just stared and talked to each other. A family came in after us and they helped them right away and walked right past us. I decided to leave after this and my boyfriend told them "Are you seriously going to ignore us this whole time?". The girl looked at him and said "Oh I thought you were here for takeout".   She said this right when we were pretty much out the door. Worst experience!

I first heard the term "pork belly" in the 1983 film "Trading Places", e.g. breakfast bacon. This pigbit has become trendy in recent years, but a recent visit to Asian fusion restaurant Creazion presented more expressions than I've had in a single meal. Along with many other tasty tidbits.

Pork belly pops started us off on a high note, cubes of braised fatty meat on skewers, glazed in maple and ponzu sauce. The sweet was matched with salt and spice, with lightly crisped, tender, succulent meat ($9). Next, orders of calamari--tempura-fried baby squid mantle and tentacle--both tender and crispy, tossed in sweet chili, lemongrass, scallion, and chipotle aioli ($8). Loved 'em.

Stir-fried chicken, mushroom, and crispy noodles were served with leaves of iceberg lettuce to make lively chicken lettuce wraps ($6). Flavors of garlic, ginger, soy, and a hint of fish sauce were enhanced by a side of cilantro and scallion. Next, a rice flour and turmeric crepe--banh xeo--stuffed with pork belly, prawn, bean sprout, scallion, with a side of cilantro, basil, and pickled daikon/carrot ($9). Usually a light, savory dish, the crepe itself was sweet and quite oily. A pair of steamed lotus buns stuffed with braised pork belly, cucumber, pickled daikon/carrot, possessed a near perfect contrast of flavors and texture ($7). If you've got room for just one appetizer, don't skip this.

My sister-in-law's banh mi sandwich of French baguette with BBQ pork, Vietnamese pork sausage--cha lua--cucumber, cilantro, jalapeno, pickled daikon/carrot, and house spread, was just OK ($7). The bread was nicely crusty, but the pork was a bit dry and included more than a few gristly bits. 

Her husband's seafood noodle soup--pho do bien--with prawns, calamari, blue crab, veggies, egg noodle, and chicken broth was pretty satisfying ($13). The seafood was tender, the broth hearty, the noodles and veg on par. A kid's order of beef pho with rare steak, flank, brisket, veg, rice noodle, and beef broth was well received and quickly consumed ($9).

My bowl of tonkatsu ramen with soft pork belly, 7 minute egg, wood ear mushroom, garlic chip, and scallion was close to being great ($12). The broth was rich, the fungi and meat plentiful, but the noodles were in a bit of a knot requiring disassembly. Worth it. The egg yolk was a bit runnier than the jammy consistency I love with proper Japanese ajitsuke tamago, but still yummy. 

A pair of poke bowls were ordered by our friend and her son, one salmon, one ahi tuna ($12). The fresh, cubed fish was available on a choice of rice--brown or white--or organic mixed greens. Toppings included crab salad, seaweed salad, edamame, sweet onion, jalapeno, wasabi, chipotle aioli, and ginger ponzu sauce. The fish tasted fresh and the seaweed salad was quite good. Both enjoyed their meal.

A goi ga salad of thin-sliced chicken breast, cabbage, cilantro, basil, pickled daikon/carrot, crushed peanut, and nuoc mam dressing was my wife's selection ($8). The fish sauce dressing was fine, but the chicken was dry and the shredded lettuce quite limp. I think this dish works best when the traditional cabbage is used for more crunch. Orders of lo mein for the niece and nephew were a hit; thin egg noodles loaded with plenty of stir-fried chicken, pork, prawn, broccoli, bok choy, and carrot ($11). The veggies had crunch and the meats were tender. As it should be. Overall, our lunch invited a shot at the dinner menu.
Absolutely no negatives.  Maria was super with the fires. Ali our server was fantastic, got all our drinks perfect.

I was craving meatballs and found this new little gem on yelp.  The reviews were all positive and absolutely right!!!  We went for lunch today and it was seriously so delicious!  We had the chicken parm plate and meatballs and spaghetti.  The portions were generous and delicious.  The red sauce was exactly what I was looking for.  Each meal came with a side salad with that classic Italian oil vinaigrette.  I was in Northeast Italian heaven!!  Make sure you order the Italian bread, it's only $1 and comes out hot.  It was gone in 2 seconds between the sauce and dressing.  We will be back to try the sandwiches!
The best pizza, very tasty. I am taking a pizza every week. Too good. . Well maintained place, employees are wearing Masks. Taste .....
Love this place. Authentic Mediterranean food (verified by my Jordanian fiancée). Fun hookah service, and beautiful out door dining. I try to come every time I'm in Santa Barbara.

First timer at this restaurant, and stopped in for brunch. I had no idea what to expect, my husband was just hangry and I needed to fix that quick. Up the stairs, about 3 other diners were seated. The drink menu is 4x the size of the brunch menu. I was a little anxious about this. We ordered the poached eggs and the scrambled eggs, and they gave us a free beet appetizer and a free panna cotta dessert. Talk about a great first time experience. The poached eggs, the Eggs Benny, was SUBLIME. Hollandaise was velvety and flavorful, and the marriage of kale and butternut squash under the eggs was perfect. The scrambled eggs were buttery soft and held shape, and the accompanying sausage and hash brown (which was more like a superstar latka) was superb. Both dishes shined in their own way. It just depends on whether you want a straightforward dish or a leveled dish. My husband and I shared bits and pieces here and there and it made for an incredible brunch. I would def be back for brunch and will definitely consider dinner.

Food was decently good. But I feel this particular location is understaffed. I would not recommend coming here if you have places to be. Coming in I had to wait some time to be seated and even longer to be checked out. The wait for being cashed out was uncanny. The guy who finally did help me was super nice though. And the service overall was good and friendly. Idk if it's just me and my paranoia, but I did feel uncomfortable after I heard some of the coworkers laugh when I came in.

Ask for Steak Tartare under the "Build Your Own Appetizer" option! The meat is butchered fresh and David blends ingredients that bring out the flavors in the beef. Such a treat, thank you!!

P.s. this was part of a search for Beef Tartare in Reno, we couldn't find it anywhere until someone tipped us off to this secret item...

My home away from home. Rue is a great place to study and people watch.  Free wifi and a ton of large tables to do work. The coffee is pretty good and fairly priced.  The cookies are awesome and the sandwiches are a bit above average.  Most of the 'baristas' are nice enough, but occasionally you'll have to deal with a hipster who thinks he's Ethan Hawks character in Reality Bites.  Will warn that the place gets a bit crowded Saturday and Sundays, and is cash only.

This place was wonderful!  The food was amazing and just as delicious as described on the menu.  The staff was welcoming and warm, as if they had invited us into their own homes.  The ambiance was lovely and the food and  pizzas were perfection.  We came with our little daughters for dinner and they had no problem and were very accommodating about our kids and even taught them to speak a little Italian!  So sweet!

I wavered back and forth on whether to give this two stars or three. The food saved this review from being two stars. I came in after a Saints game on a Sunday with my brother and it was pretty full but had empty seats at the bar and one empty table. The sign when you walk in says "Please wait to be seated". So we waited. And waited. And waited more. 3 different waiters passed us by and just looked at us without saying a word. Not even a "someone will be with you shortly" just glances. I don't know if they had an actual host/hostess or what. But we were starving and Walk-Ons wasn't serving food (eyeroll) and Reginelli's next-door was packed. So FINALLY the man working the bar came from around and asked if we'd like to sit at the bar. So we did. This was about 10-13 minutes after we arrived and were standing in the door being awkwardly stared at by waiters and customers alike. So we finally get seated and get our waters. Then it takes the fella forever to come and get our order. I ordered the chicken tenders basket with fries and my brother ordered a veggie omelet with cheese grits. That is not what we received. After waiting about 30 minutes, we were brought out a chicken wing basket and a veggie omelet with hash browns. I sent mine back. My brother decided to keep his because he was so hungry. I waited another 8 minutes or so and finally got my tenders. They were very good and hot and fresh (as they should be). They had a good amount of seasoning and weren't over fried. The fries were good as well. The biscuit that came with it was very flaky. My brother also said him omelet was very yummy and full of shrimp. And he said the hash browns were great. The server did apply his employee discount for the mishap with the food so I really did appreciate that. He was a very nice man. I think their service definitely needs some fine tuning but the food is good and it's a cute little spot so I believe they'll be fine. I would return to give it another shot.

Nit Wit is back! Thank you Pat Cronin! If you are looking for a restaurant with a group of friends that have eclectic tastes in food, this is the restaurant for you. Plus, they are a brewery that utilize local brewers. My favorite thing on the menu right now are the Mahi Mahi Tacos grilled. I have yet to have a bad meal here though.
Don't eat much before coming here!  The food is delicious and always causes me to overeat!  The pineapple and brisket are amaaaaaaazing!!

I came to New Orleans on a late night flight, after i check inn my hotel and everything i saw it was after 10 PM and most of the restaurants were close so i walk in to a CVS and they told me Daisy Dukes was right by it and it's open 24/7 so i went here and when i walk in it was not very busy.

The food was alright had the New Orleans Sampler was not bad but nothing to talk home about but it's good for a late night place if you need food.

The service was great set by a lady that help me find a hotel cause little did i know most of the hotels were booked the next night and help me find one and the stuff was very friendly and take good care of me.

Overall i will give this place a 3 and a half stars.

Poor quality here. The entire facility smells like cigarette smoke and my eyes burned and teared the whole time I was here.  My room was in the "non-smoking" tower, yet certain guest would be smoking in the elevator, the hallways and the rooms.  The rooms were old and out of date with no refrigerators or microwaves.

They also charge you a resort fee of $22 per day and a $100 deposit that you are not informed of until you check in.  You also have to park 1/4 mile away in the parking garage (very inconvenient). I have felt cheated since I got swindled at this "resort". You would be better off staying at the  Motel 6 down the street!

I was looking for a local place to get some wings. I found the reviews of Rockhill on Yelp and decided to give this place a try. I ordered 10 Buffalo wings, onion rings and a brisket sandwich for my roommate and I to share. I drove over to Rockhill to pickup the order and everything was ready within a few minutes. The drive home however was torture with the wonderfull smells from the backseat.

The onion rings were the first box we opened, and they were incredibly crisp and tasty, and not the slightest bit greasy. They were a little too salty for me, but that is my only partial complaint. The wings were cooked very well and the meat fell off the bone. The brisket again was very well done and fell apart if you tried to pick up a piece. 

The actual restaurant looked clean and inviting. The opening into the kitchen was a nice touch and everything looked clean and well taken care of. This is definitely some place I'll be returning to!

The atmosphere is awesome....but the service is lacking. We've sat here for like 30 minutes at the bar  only to see how selective the bartenders were in selecting who was next. Our beers have been empty for 15 minutes...not sure what the reason is

I just order pizza from this location. I placed my order around 11:30, right when the store close the store calls me and tells me my delivery can not be made because of the rain. I ask can a drive deliver once the rain pass the pizza guy said no. Advised from the store manager! Bad first experience and bad customer service! Highly pissed I have to drive to the store since my order was suppose to be delivery. Not ordering from here again! Pizza is great but the store is not

Amazing every single time. Can't go wrong with anything g on the menu, the agaves burrito is delicious and the pork/salads verde burrito. Also they have the best salsas in the game. Portions are very generous
Great food.  Be prepared to wait in line but well worth it.

This is a St. Louis pizza institution. I ordered a pepperoni and olive pizza online for carry out. Pizza was ready in about 25 minutes. The crust was nice, crispy and thin. The sauce was tangy and delicious and there was a generous amount of toppings on the pizza. ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS. Also only 15 bucks for a large. It's a must try when In St. Louis. 

PS: Order the crust well done for that extra crisp!

This gem is a nod to "Aunt Adelaide" better known to the rest of us as Adelaide Brennan. This place is a sister restaurant to Commanders Palace and lives up to the family name. I had the pork loin rolled in praline and wow. Also this not one of those places where the protein is amazing and the sides are ho-hum. The sides are knock outs, there is just all kinds flavor and it is all so well balanced. the wait staff was attentive and gracious, the kitchen even made an off menu vegetarian plate for one of us. I'm not talking whatever sides they were serving that day this was a whole other thing and it was delicious. An all around wonderful experience

It's like Chipotle, but with Greek food! Such a cool idea. I've tried several things from here, and everything was wonderful. My friend was disappointed that they didn't have spanakopita, but they do have the spinach and feta mixture, which they can give you as a side along with pita. I tried it and actually preferred it to typical spanakopita.

Wasn't what it was cracked up to be. We ordered General Powell's Chicken and Sesame Noodles and it was 18.90. Was it worth it? NO! The General Powell's sauce was not that good at all and the chicken was really dry. The cold sesame noodles were very watery and it was rather disgusting while eating. We barely ate half and had to throw it away. The almond cookies that were included were good though. I'd definitely not go back!!!

Since there is so much pizza in the world, I feel it is only fair to be picky. This place is pretty good. We ordered the JJ's special which tasted similar to a combo. The pizza was made from scratch and the young employees were fun. A good place to get pizza, beer and watch any game.
Service is fast and server explains the menu clearly. Ramen is very flavorful and unique.

Ducked in for a birthday party and it was a fine time, here's why: 
* Excellent Service
* Cool and artsy decor
* Innovative menu 
* Fairly priced

I loved it, I had cauliflower, some mushrooms, I tried the Steak Tartar, and loved the egg served with it. 

Good stuff, see you there. 

Cabeza OUT!

First real philly cheesesteak as a Texan.

First visit, ordered double meat w provolone because I'm a food snob and can't imagine eating "cheese whiz," much less putting it on good steak w mushrooms and onions.  Mistake.  Provolone didn't have flavor.  But bread, meat, onions and mushrooms were amazing.

Second visit, ordered double meat with whiz and cheese fries.  Amazing. A-MAZE-ING.

Third visit, double meat w whiz, onions, and mushrooms and of course, cheese fries.  Amazing.  A-MAZE-ING.

Service was outstanding.  Friendly guys.

I'll keep coming here as long as I'm in Philly.

The food at Epice is as phenomenal as you've heard. Quite honestly, my meal here was one of the best I've had in Nashville. Stunning. I can't say enough good things about it. And it almost didn't happen.

One of my nearest and dearest friends -- whom I hadn't seen in 13 years -- was making her way back to the States from South America and I wanted to make sure she had a meal to remember. She requested Lebanese food so, duh, Epice was a no-brainer. I made reservations for four at 815 on a Friday and went on my way planning for the night. I arrived at 805. The small waiting area was stacked with people. A walk-in party of 3 wanted a table and were whining to the hostess that they wanted to sit. My Spidey side-eye sense started tingling. The one hesitation I had with coming here were all the review mentions about problematic service and Real Housewives-level attitude. I can't and I won't. Truly, I'm not the one. I gave my name to the hostess and tried to make myself small so as to not be in the way. Another party of four came in at 810. They were early for their reservation (830?). The owner/manager asked if my party was here yet. I replied that they weren't (mind you, they weren't late, they just weren't early). The other party was seated. Defcon level started to rise... The rest of my party arrived at 814 for our 815 reservation. Between seating the early party and another party who didn't want to get up from their plates, we were table-less. My friend had flown over continents to get here and this was her welcome to Nashville. Even better, we were directed to stand at the bar and wait. Mind you, there was no room at the bar, so our party of four hovered at the edge of the bar, moving out of the way for servers and bartenders alike. The owner/manager implored us to get a drink -- on us. Yes, their decision to sit a party early and our discomfort = us paying for our own drinks while standing in the way and in the corner. That was the last we saw of the owner/manager. We were finally seated at 832 and I was concocting my scathing review in my head. My friend's mother asked me to dial it down and be fully present. After all, we hadn't seen each other in 13 years. Reverting to teenaged deference, I did as asked. The Fayrooz cocktail was helping to calm me... as long as I didn't think about how I was paying for it. The vodka cocktail had a light green color thanks to the lime and cucumber. The orange blossom water added a unique & authentic element. Very refreshing.

Our waitress came over to the table and did her best to stem the bad vibes I was emanating. It sucks that she was thrown to the lions while the people who put her in this situation hid out but dammit if she didn't turn my frown upside down. I hope she's taken care of by the restaurant. Like everyone else who comes here, we started with the Al-Raheb and an order of Kibbeh. As I have mentioned time and again, I am not a beef eater but when presented with beef like this, I'm all in. Delectable. Wonderfully crumbly texture. Seasoned just the way you'd imagine a placed named 'Epice' would be able to provide. Outstanding. The Al-Raheb was delicious as well but the Kibbeh reminded me that I'll never be able to fully give up animal proteins. Up next was the peasant salad as a prelude to our entrees. A basic salad of fresh vegetables and lemon dressing was made all-the-more enjoyable by whatever subtle spice profile the kitchen introduced to it. The salad is as good as mentioned. Now we were ready for the main event. I ordered the Sayadeya and it silenced me... that is when I wasn't moaning with delight. The generous fish filet was aggressively spiced and seasoned and topped with caramelized onions. If you tend to enjoy your food on a more pure (basic? bland?) level, the presentation would be a turnoff. And, honestly, at first smell I thought the kitchen had been a bit too heavy-handed with the spice. But when I tasted it? Oh my dear goodness gracious... I haven't had food like that in a very long time. This food is why people put up with hiccups, attitudes and eyerolls. I can't adequately describe what I tasted but know that it took me to a very zen place. With every bite, I became more and more chill, less and less angry/frustrated. This was transformative food. The vermicelli rice wasn't a forgotten side. It was an essential component of the plate and after I savored it on its own, I coupled every bite of my fish with the rice. Divine. The tempranillo I picked to accompany my meal was a standout as well. It balanced the spice profile but didn't overwhelm the fish. Heavenly.

Despite the late hour (and still a bit annoyed by our delayed start), we opted for dessert. The date tart sounded very pleasing and appropriately Middle Eastern (a term I am trying to use less and less given its relational origins) but I couldn't pass up the pot de creme. Neither should you. I'm hitting the word limit so I have to stop. That's how good Epice is. 5000 character good.

It had been a LONG time since I'd eaten at La Trattoria and it's changed a bit. It's no longer the crowded place I remember. Our server told us that a few years ago there was a kitchen fire that pretty much gutted the restaurant. The result is that they remodeled and now it's much more open. I dig it.

It's pricey and you need a reservation, but it's so worth it. 

I had the chicken Alfredo and it was perfection. And the portions are huge, I couldn't finish it. Which meant I got to have it again for dinner the next evening. 

It's a shame it took me so long to come back, but I won't make that mistake again.
Good Hamachi Kama. Sushi can be a hit or miss. Never great but usually okay. Generally overpriced so the all you can eat is the best option.

What a delicious treat. I went to the Shaker Mill with some friends from out of town last night and we had an amazing time. A great representation of the Santa Barbara nightlife. I really enjoyed their beer selection and my fiancé loved the mango lassi (a little too
Much haha). 

I really like how there are different food options that you can bring to the Shaker Mill area (both Cubaneo and modern times restaurant). 

Our friends visiting from LA had a great time.

My wife and I were here back in April for a friends wedding and this is where we went for breakfast the day after. Excellent little breakfast joint. The Bee decor is waaay out, I mean there are bee knick-knacks everywhere. I wish I could rate the food but since I can't remember what I had, I'll leave it bee... lol. The owners were very outgoing and new all the regulars. If ever you're in Carpinteria... buzz on by for memorable experience.

The food was very good. The staff was stellar. They where short a sever and it the first k a couple xtra minutes but she let us know and was attentive. I had the eggs Benedict with steak. Next time I'll just get the regular and the steak wasn't that great  but let's talk about the homemade hollandaise sauce. It was so amazing. And the chunked potato's wher fresh and wonderful. My son had eggs and pancakes (he is a adult) and it was fresh and perfect.

love it. service is great and food is delicious. i always get the lean brisket pho and sometimes sneak in a crab rangoon app. both are phenomenal every time. highly recommend this place if you're looking for some vietnamese cuisine.

Great place to go in the Seminole Heights area. The vibe is a combination of hipster and New Orleans Cajun. They have a great happy hour for drinks. The place is very clean and customer service is good. My complaint is that there isn't many options in the entree section but the food that is delivered is very unique, tasty, and something that you have never seen before. I also feel the prices are a little high, the main meals are over 20 bucks.  Overall, great restaurant that I will be returning to.

The first thing I noticed was, of course, the decor. It looks like Picasso threw up on the outside and Warhol gave birth on the inside. I wouldn't normally critic a diners decor but here it literely distracted me from my meal. (which may not have been a bad thing)

My meal was a omelet with spinish and Swiss. The omelet was 90% Spanish some egg floated in and absolutely no cheese.

The two stars are for the servers.
Love this place! Yummy! Great choices for kids! Delicious tuna melt! Would recommend this place to everyone!

I'm reading some of these reviews from the "locals" (by that I mean NJ'ers that stay within NJ and never make it across the bridge to Philly), and I find it hilarious that a lot of the complaints are consistent:  Pricey and didn't taste good.  First, if you know anything about Jose Garces, the Distrito in Philly is one of his first restaurants ad that place does very well.  The food in the Philly and Moorestown location is very good.  So if you want to eat at an establishment with a world class chef's name attached to it, go here.  Second, folks that say "tasted horrible":  I'm sorry that your taste buds have been ruined by the likes of Taco Bell, Panchero's, Don Pablo's or Chipotle.  If you've been disappointed by Distritro, then just go to places that you're used to - $12 for a taco bowl or something.  And FYI - you pay what you get for at those other places:  low quality ingredients and absolutely zero creativity.  

As for my review of Moorestown Distrito:  I love it here.  I've been here for Brunch, Lunch and Dinner.  I've even had several work dinners here and everyone is always delighted.  The staff is very attentive and polite.  The only con is how busy Thursday and Friday evenings get.  If you go there just for happy hour during those nights, then get ready to wait.  I'm not sure if the bartenders are not used to that type of volume or what but they tend to be overwhelmed very easily especially when its more than 5 bar patrons per bartender.

Had dinner with my lovely dinner pals and arrived early and they had no problem seating us and giving us time to prepare for the gastrofestival that was about to take place.  This is a midsize and very open restaurant/bar with seating along the wall and bar ends to the back side.

We chose to try the chef's 5 course blind tasting and it was amazing.  What began with a slight hesitation and concern quickly turned into excitement of the surprise of what was next.
We began with cured meet and sorbet that cleared the pallet and prepared us for the delightful onslaught of flavors.

I am not going to give away the surprises that followed but the gnocchi (***** stars) has now made it a requirement, that my future companion knows how to make these.  The dessert was full of technique and complexity but I was expecting a more decadent traditional dessert.

I would also recommend the wine pairing.  The chef's choices clearly enhanced our dining experience and help me set aside some prejudice I had towards white and rose.

Now the chef's blind tasting is not for the faint at heart.  Dinner for three and drinks for two was almost $125 p/p and while I am more than ready to do it again, its clearly not a weekly adventure.

Parking is heavy on Magazine and while I enjoy the ambiance, when I am hungry and have to find street parking it can become a bear.  The only reason that it is 4 star and not five is because I did not like being so close up to the bar while we were dining and it was difficult at times to hear my companions with bar conversations taking place right behind me.  I didn't know there was a upstairs seating area so maybe that would be a more quiet environment.  

The food is CLEARLY 5 star but the overall experience was a 4.7 and I dont round up.

I first tried Sauce on the Side in March of 2014.  It was wonderful.  I had the figgy piggy and my husband ordered the Fatty-B.  I loved the combination of flavors they offer.  The calzones are HUGE.  You can definitely eat 1/2, then save the other half for later.  I didn't use the sauce that much, because the calzones are so wonderful on their own.  They recently expanded to a new location in Clayton.  I haven't tried that one yet, but it is on my to do list.

Nikki's has been around as long as I can remember and for some reason it took me this long to finally give them a try. I visited them for breakfast on a weekday morning and it was surprisingly busy. There weren't many open seats and the seating that was available was tight. 

My girlfriend and I could hear both of the tables next to us pretty easily and it kind of felt uncomfortable. Our order was placed and our food came out very quickly. My girlfriend's food was good and mine was just ok. It was nothing special. Certain parts of my meal had no flavor and tasted bland and needed some salt and seasoning. 

I ate rather fast because I really just wanted to leave due to the very small sitting space. I was starting to get uncomfortable due to the table next to us analyzing our meals loud enough for us to hear. It was awkward. 

I've had worse, I've bad better. Nikki's got the job done and that's why they are getting 3 stars from me.

We ordered two crunch wrap supremes and some Doritos Locos tacos. When we got home I commented that everything looked "thin". So we unwrapped the crunch wraps and there was no meat! One had mostly tomatoes and the other was just over loaded with sour cream and cheese. The tacos all had a very very sparse amount of the correct ingredients so that when the taco was closed both sides touched each other! Worst food. Get it together, it's really not that difficult!

I wasn't super wowed here, the place was beautiful and the staff were great. I enjoyed the environment the ambience was nice. The decor very nice.
 
    I tried a bowl of the smoked duck and jalapeño chili. The flavors were unique, I didn't get any jalapeño flavor though. I don't think I would call it a chili. More of a bowl of beans and some shredded duck. 

    I also ordered the two meat platter with tri-tip steak and burnt ends. The tri-tip steak was very good I enjoyed the flavors. The burnt ends were kinda dry and stringy, and smothered in a lot of sauce. Not horrible just not what I expected. 

     The mac and cheese side was ok, it was shell macaroni, with some cheese sauce and bread crumbs on top. 

    Overall 3 stars from me because the portion size was kinda small for how much they charge. 15$ for a two meat plate with like 4 or 5 thin slices of tri-tip and 5 small pieces of burnt ends.

I have a ton of stomach issues that prevents me from eating at normal smoothie and açaí bowl places. But sweet soul has been only good to me. With all natural ingredients, I feel amazing after eating soft serve which I never thought I would be able to say. The flavors are amazing and it is all super healthy!

First time I have tried this place after years of not wanting something new. The place is really cool and always busy but they move customers and there's always a place to sit. The pulled pork was pretty good but the brisket was a bit dry. I loved the squash side and unique sodas they had. Thought they were a bit over priced compared to the serving size. Sauces were pretty cool except the coffee bbq sauce which was weird. Orval not a bad place and I will for sure come here
More often.

I had never had this place before but it was recommended to me for catering my wedding reception. Holy crap I was impressed. The food was incredible. All our guests raved about it. Brisket was so right, the mac n cheese wow!,the green beans are everything and finally, they said they hadn't had the best reviews about their pulled chicken but it was soooo good. I didn't eat the salad because who eats salad when you have incredible BBQ but it looked real good. Aside from the food, the girl (I believe her name was Nicole) was incredible and with ease took on my panicked phone call and everything was no problem. I am not sure who the caters were that came and stayed to make sure everything was great but they were in and out unnoticed. Everyone was so kind. I can't thank them enough for being apart of one of the most important days of my life.

Absolutely wonderful! The food is fantastic. I had a Grilled chicken sandwich and chili cheese fries! The grilled chicken sandwich was made to perfection the toasted bread was to die for & the chicken cooked perfect it was juicy and flavorful. The chili cheese fries were so cheesy and loaded with chili they were delicious! The best location to have lunch or dinner it is amazing. The train passing by the beach, the waves crashing  on the sand. Beautiful and delicious!
Great menu! Weather was perfect. Sat outside! Lots of great drinks and food. Tracy was a great server!!

Decided to try a different place for brunch on Sunday and had driven by Mimi's on North Oracle at the Tucson Mall. Standard name on the list at the door, seated within 15 minutes...not bad. Once seated, our waitress finally got to us for a drink order. My companion got his lemonade within a few minutes, a coffee and a mimosa took an additional 10 minutes. Bread finally arrived a few minutes later, lovely carrot mini muffins and mini baguettes, warm and crusty. Service was very slow though the place was not bustling busy. I also noted that the table behind us that was seated and ordered after we did got their food before we did. Hash Benedict with a salad and crepes with a salad shouldn't take longer than a burger plate with multiple substitutions and pancakes...just throwing that out there. 
Now on to the food, the true star of any brunch. The herbed potatoes were very good, the hash Benedict was as expected with a nice hollandaise that was not overly lemony. Eggs on top were cooked perfectly. The brie, bacon, Turkey and spinach crepes were passable but nothing to be ordered again. We prefer cheese to
 be inside a crepe melding with the other ingredients, not melted on top by a broiler. That last step toughened the crepes and put a hard blanket over something that should be light and delicate. Disappointing. After finishing our meal, service was once again very slow and inattentive. This is not a place to go to if you have anywhere to be in less than 3 hours. 
I would love to give this place more stars because the decor and atmosphere were nice (though there was visible dust clinging to the wooden columns on many of the booths) and the waitress was friendly but the inattentive and slow service and mishandled crepes brought down what was an otherwise pleasant experience. We may give it another try as there were several other tempting offerings in the menu that are calling our names on a weekday for lunch or another weekend outing. Also of note, the house mimosa is yummy and you can add a side Caesar or garden salad plus dessert to any entree for $5 more to make it a 3 course, even if your late lunch is a breakfast selection.
Not the best but definitely not the worst. Give it a try when you have plenty of time.

Love love this place!!  After driving past it since it's conception, we decided to look online to see what was going on. I have only had the French dip and would like to try something else... But, I would have to forgo the French dip!

This is my favorite place to get Chinese food and I still make the trip after moving out of the area. They just consistently have slightly better food here than the other Chinese food places that serve the same crap that they serve everywhere else. Their crab Rangoon aren't those little paper-football shaped things with almost no filling. While this might look like all of the others places on the outside, the food is worth trying at least once.

The inside is always so dirty and grimey. It's really dated and always needs to be cleaned. Customer service isn't really a strong suit for this location anymore. I believe it's still run by the same family, but their kids are likely off to college and they used to work up front. I've never been sick from eating here or anything like that but I've been pretty underwhelmed with my last few visits.

My girlfriend and I went on a Sunday night.  Apparently there is a happy hour during the week, but you must sit outside? Not sure.  Anyway, the hostess was dressed for the club and looked out of place in the restaurant.  I wouldn't have trusted any of her recommendations so I didn't ask for any.

They start by trying to sell you the wine on the table and if you don't order any wine, they whisk away the drink and dessert menu.  I thought that was odd because people might change their minds, but maybe it was a one-off.

I ordered the chicken marsala and my gf had the chicken parm.  The chicken parm was a large portion of chicken and a huge pile of pasta.  She enjoyed it, but couldn't finish it.  The chicken marsala was the best I'd ever had; one of the best meals I've had anywhere in a long time.  The vegtables and mushroom risotto it came with were also very good.

They show you a platter of desserts to choose from at the end, which I think really helps sell it.  I was full, so I took tiramisu to go.  The waitress assured me they were heavy on the amaretto.  It was a very large portion of dessert for $5 and very, very good.

One of the owners came by to shake hands and say hi, which reminds me of restaurants in small towns or in Europe, which I love.

Overall the ambience is kind of strange, the hostess out of place, but the food was amazing.  I would definitely come back to this side of town for more tiramisu!
Great atmosphere. Food was below average! Service was slow. Location is perfect. Nice restrooms.
Amazing!!! Had the founders favorite for lunch and I already want to go back. Yes, I'm going back at least once a week.

As someone whose family hikes to Lansdale to eat at Greater India (scrumptious cuisine) every time we want Indian food, I was very excited that an Indian Restaurant was coming to Red Hill.
We went for the lunch buffet and were disappointed to find that children were the same price as adults ($10) which seems a bit steep. Kids 10 and under are free at Greater India.
Since I knew my children would not eat that much, my youngest 2 ordered off of the childrens menu (about $6 ea) instead of getting the buffet.
The food was good, but chicken was the only meat option on the buffet (no lamb or beef) like what we're used to.
I must say, that although the food was good - my family and I will still travel to Lansdale for the Greater India buffet. 
The bill for 2 adults and 3 children was $50. At Greater India my entire family can eat the buffet for $35, not to mention the food is better.
I think Sawaii is on the right track and with a few improvements could really be a great restaurant. 
Improvements:
1) more buffet variety (less chicken dishes)
2) a lower buffet rate for children
3) Explanation of what's in the dishes on the buffet so people know what they're eating.
Best pho I've been able to find in the Boise area after looking for so long. Fast service.

We come to this place time to time for  their pho and rice platters. Their grilled beef is one of the best in flavors. For today's post and review, we have tried their Ube Milkyway smoothie with added boba and lychee jelly. No further comments needed but it was awesome!! Make aure to stir a d mix it up before drinking it to mix the contents well... yeah, the looks will not be there but hey, you'll not regret it unless you like eating the boba, the kychee jelly, the whipped cream and the ube separately.  strongly recommending this and we'll definitely order this in our next visit especially that summer is upon us. A very good way to chill and cool down the heat.

Excellent local hoagie shop. Always a friendly welcome. 
Hoagies are well sized for the price with Dietz & Watson meats and cheeses. We're a pretty standard family- Italian & Turkey hoagies have always been on point. Also, really enjoy their hoagie dip if you're looking for a sharable snack!

Okay so I was back here this Sunday for my sisters birthday. The service was fantastic!! They specially made a number of items for our table and brought out so many extras that were requested. However the food was overall pretty mediocre. Nothing extraordinary. And the Brunch selection was dismal. They probably had less than half of the selection as they had my last visit. I understand that times are tough but really the buffet looked pathetic. It was so disappointing.

So happy they opened down the street from my house.  The soft serve icecream is the best! The young lady was really nice and signed me up for the rewards loyalty program.  Will be back at least once a week.  Prices are reasonable compared to DQ and the other icecream spots.
Got their lunch special which was a sampler of three different curries. One was decent, a second was good, but their tika masala was one of the best I've ever had. Delicious.

We loved the food!  The smothered chicken, mashed potatoes, corn and macaroni and cheese were so delicious.  It was an A plus for the food.

The staff was super friendly and helpful.

So Outback is a pretty decent restaurant all around. I would say it's pretty good for a chain restaurant. What I can't understand is the service. Why does it seem like every time I go to an outback the service keeps getting work. I think the management at this outback needs to get there act together. The restaurant was nearly half empty and our service was terrible. The waitress was nice and was on the drink refills and that's were to stopped. It took nearly an hour to get our food. The appetizer probably took about 45 minuets. So if you go to this Outback you may want to bring a air mattress and a pillow, because it is going to be awhile.
nice place and good eats.  my fish was a bit undercooked but I will just ask them to make it more crispy next time.  a good find.

They have really good bagels, stop there and leave. Ordered two of their signature lunch specials, the Ellis Island Hot Pastrami & the Manhattan Cheese Steak. Horrible, a complete over priced ripoff. The hot pastrami consisted of two thin over cooked deli slices with little cheese & mustard. Not edible it went in the garbage. Go to Ben & Irv's if you want the real deal. The Manhattan cheese steak was a joke. Tiny roll with almost no meat, gone in 4 bites. I can't believe that they get repeat business selling this over priced crap. Don't waste your money.

This is the second day this brix and mortar location is open. 

I couldn't wait. My temperament is also very forgiving today. Dying for true ramen in Nashville and my gratitude may overwhelm, so take this review with a grain of salt. My boyz and I are kicking it up this Sunday. Supping on ramen and topping off the day with Star Wars. It doesn't get any better than this. 

Starting off with a glass of cava and a Japanese white ale. 

They are already out of duck buns and out of gyoza. We were warned and so I'm not grumpy. Well-being still high and intact. 

Our server today is a pretty young woman who used to serve us at Zushimaki in Franklin. And she says the ramen is great. She's Thai so I'm going to hold her to a much higher standard with that endorsement. 

The okonomiyaki were pretty darned good. We ordered two. It could have done with a little less tamari/sweet soy sauce, but otherwise, very tasty. Served in cast iron skillets--another nice nod to humble Southern cooking. 

The hot chicken buns are excellent. Perfectly fried, crispy, respectable heat inside steamed folded Chinese bread (bao) -- exceptionally pillowy, with a slathering of mayo and piquant pickles, respectful nods to Nashville's famous hot chicken, a la Japanese bar food style. We ordered another one. It was as good as the first. 

We all ordered the Tennessee Tonkatsu ramen, two without egg. Another nod to Tennessee--the pork is pulled pork rather than braised, seared char siu. I get the nod of respect but didn't want pulled pork in my ramen. 

We ordered these add ins that cane in ramekins-these let you doctor your broth, like pho. 

-miso butter--this transformed the broth and gave it depth--a little salty, buttery miso
-Sichuan bomb (floral, sichuan peppercorn paste)--be careful and taste this. It is floral, a hit of black pepper
-spice bomb (sriracha hot and a little sweet)
-karashi takana (salted pickled mustard greens) -this should be a pickled counterpoint but was saltier than it should have been
-chili oil

The broth was nice and hot but could have been hotter, steamier. Black garlic oil put a ring of char in the bowl. Wood ear mushrooms come in the bowl--dark, blackish brown, a toothsome counterpoint to the noodles. 

The broth is almost neutral tasting and begs your adornment. Mouth feel is a bit thinner than I like but the miso butter gives the broth a smooth, fatty deliciousness and is just salty enough. 

The ramen noodles are thin spaghetti noodles. I like my ramen noodles a little thicker and a bit more toothsome. These tasted just fine and were cooked nicely. 

Missing for me were: raw chopped garlic and sesame oil. Garlic is on the dinner menu but not available at today's lunch--too bad. Garlic transforms a bowl of ramen. Also missing was sesame oil. My broth would have exploded with garlic and sesame oil. 

The cocktails look excellent but I was told Otaku doesn't serve these until evening.

All in all, this is a damned fine bowl of ramen for Nashville. 

We will be back.

This place is fantastic. The flavors are Indian/Asian influenced and full of complexity. The service is top notch, the food gets to the table in a flash, and the presentation and  combinations are amazingly creative and complex. We stopped in just for a nosh and kept ordering dishes  because it was SO MUCH MORE than we expected.

The night started out nicely, Amber, our waitress was pleasant and accommodating  the Aussie fries were good

The appetizer plates had not been washed properly and were were dirty

There were three 'Premium' chopped salads ordered with dinners. 

There wasn't one with 'chopped' characteristics, see attached photo. 

The manager was requested, showed up on a few minutes, told me that what we had ere 'Outback chopped salads' that he would take cared of it and returned with what is pictured. Leaf lettuce, 1/4 teaspoon of bleu cheese, no visible pecans, with a sweet vinaigrette. 

The Managment for this franchise has a problem  and is not handling it properly. 

I will not return  until there are major changes.

6/26/16 --- Sister was up from Richmond.  She wanted some fried oysters, unfortunately these were undercooked.  My fiery shrimp was really good though.  I ordered a Lagunitas IPA which took entirely too long to get because the female bartender was too busy talking to her friends at the bar and wasn't too concerned about her other customers.  Also, I prefer to get a beer in a pint glass.

Came into Blanco on 5/9 and had Sofia as our server for dinner and she was fantastic!! We had never been to Blanco before but she made the best recommendations! We took her word on the hibiscus margarita and nachos and both were absolutely amazing!! She was always making sure we had everything we needed and brought everything at a timely manner! Very respectful and friendly! Made our dining experience amazing!!

A friend from Taiwan got my colleagues and  I take out from here to help share a taste from home. We walked in and placed the order. The wait was nominal, the staff friendly and the food was great. A bit greasy at times but overall worth a taste.

We had the best dining experience at georgine's last night.  It was our 50th wedding anniversary celebration with 22 friends and family.  The food was delicious and our servers, Christine and Ally, couldn't have been more pleasant, attentive and efficient.  Everyone, including management, bartenders, wait staff and busboys, we're totally accommodating and made our dinner party a wonderful success.  Thank you all.
Ordered soup from them and it was delivered so hot it burnt the whole inside of my mouth.

I got a pizza cheese steak with onions and my girlfriend got a regular without onions. Both were unbelievable! Totally worth the 20 minute wait. I'm not really sure whether the sauce they use on the pizza is nacho cheese sauce, but it doesn't matter. Be prepared to want to nap for the next six hours.

Also, I botched my order but the guys at the register were nice about it. Don't necessarily buy into the soup nazi stories about the staff.

So why one star?   Because their ice cream is still good.  But that is where it ends.

I have been to this Twistee Treat at least 40 times since it opened.  I might be the TT Duke on Yelp with more check-ins here than anyone, but that will likely change.  I rated this place a four star a couple weeks after opening, but it has gone down hill, a lot.

With the last ten visits, service and quality has gone down so much, I might never return.

Let's start with product quality.  In the last five visits I have had a stale cone three times...the once perfect cone shape is now nothing but a swirled ice cream mess pressed into the cone and leaning to the side....and several times the sugar cone leaked from the bottom.

Then there is service, or lack thereof.  My only complaint at opening was slow service.  I thought service could not get slower, but it has.  

I fully support giving young adults the opportunity to work, but the culture at this restaurant lacks any customer care.  They seem more interested in socializing with friends at the window or their very exotic fingernails, than they are about customers.  And, the managers lack any empathy or ability to resolve these problems.

So...Back to TCBY for now...
They got the best fresh garlic pizza in town. They deliver too, so I don't have to cross 301 anymore for pizza.
Great diner atmosphere and passable American fare.  Will go again, but it's not my favorite.

'Milkiest Chocolate in the World' is where its AT. Everything about Jeni's is a perfect experience, from the sweet homemade waffle cone smell that wafts through the store, to the genuinely friendly employees who stay friendly when I ask to sample every single flavor (yikes, I was THAT person!). I bring any and all visitors to Jeni's because it is simply the holy grail of ice cream experiences.

This tiny, little, sketchy place packs the BIGGEST flavors! Me and hubby have been here a few times and we love it. My husband's quite obsessed actually.

Staff is always friendly and super down to earth. We had one waiter who didn't know the menu too well, but he was probably new and his super cool personality made up for it haha. 

The burgers are delicious. Portion size is great. Like too great that my brother and I were thinking about sharing the next time we go..and I usually never share burgers lol. It's soo filling, so if you like a big burger this is your place! The mussels and frites are always a hit-we want to try the Cajun flavor next time. They also have wings as appetizers and they are scrumptious as well. Good size and great flavors. We tried the emergency and ICU flavors and they are perfectly spicy. If you can't handle spicy, it's NOT for you. As for sides, I love potatoes so I'm sooo happy they have tots and fries which are both so delicious. 

Definitely one of the best underrated burger spots in NOLA! Can't wait to come back and try some new stuff!
Cute little place. They use local foods and serve it up Scandinavian style. We had the salmon toast, bread pudding, honey toast, and breakfast pizza. All delish!

Glad to see the Hendersonville get a finer restaurant, too bad that the food isn't that fine.   The food isn't bad, it's just overpriced. Hamburgers are great, mac and cheese was awesome, and the pecan pie cheesecake was great.  However, just not sure it's worth 50 for burgers and dessert.  Go for the gift certificates on restaurant.com

What a great sushi place!!  The fish was fresh, and they had great rolls.  There were also plenty of other items to choose from that were not just regular rolls like salads and such.

I would definitely go for the poke salad...
The best pizza and pasta. My favorite is penne pasta with vodka sauce and the margarita pizza or primavera pizza.

okay for soup dumplings! ive been craving soup dumplings, so we came on the weekend, around 4pm-ish.  theres always a wait here, so if you come at odd hours you're in luck!  ordered the SCALLION PANCAKE (pretty chewy, standard size, but not really much filling in it. not bad), BOKCHOY (standard veggies with garlic. not bad as well), and PORK SOUP DUMPLINGS (8 pieces for the price, pretty worth it. but after a bit, the soup dumplings get cold pretttty quick. it is really doughy, and the filling isn't plump, but its not bad for its price), and PAN FRIED SOUP DUMPLINGS (this one is more of like a fluffy dough bread with the filling.  its pan fried, has a different texture than your normal soup dumplings because the dough is more like a bread than a wrap. i would probably get this next time over the regular soup dumplings).

i wish they had the fresh ginger with the vinegar and soy sauce many typical taiwanese soup dumplings places have, but it doesn't have it here.

worth it to come during odd hours with no line! but not worth the wait if theres a long line.

ALSO CASH ONLY

My favorite pho place in Goleta and Isla Vista-- the food comes out quickly and the service is good. I always come here in the mornings, where there is not much people. It does get busy around lunch time. #42 on the menu, is the best bun bo hue, the meat is not too thick of a flavor and the soup is just barely spicy. The spring rolls are also good, comes with thick peanut sauce, which serves as a perfect appetizer.

Ms. Tootsie was great! The food was great me and 2 other females went here and our food was great. I got southern fried chicken with okra, corn and tomatoes and candy yams. My waiter was great August was sooo sweet     And she has great customer service.

Let me state that I usually 1-2 days before writing a bad review. Lots of buzz about this place, dig deeper and the really good ones are about the bar. I had a beer, guest 2 had Horchata, guest 3 had a margurita. By the way I , at least do not pretend to be a good speller. Food, taste salt, then ??? Oh the corn tortillas are real good, the filling(s) so so. I usually will not talk about decor, but, Was the designer on sale ? the glassware, nor the dinner plates go with the Industrial decor. Theres more but just go get a drink and go elsewhere for food.

Moving from Boston to Tampa, I was not expecting much to be the same. One day driving to work, though, I saw Chipotle. A must have! I walk inside and order a chicken quesadilla. I then go to pay for my meal, although it seemed a little high, and voilà! My chicken quesadilla was done and put in front of me. Confused, I politely told the woman whom rung me up, Lisa, "I'm sorry, but I did not say what I wanted on the quesadilla." Apparently, in Tampa it is absurd to ask for lettuce, tomatoes, and all of the other usual's on a quesadilla, because "wanting items on it is not a quesadilla, but it is now a burrito." I then remind Lisa that I do not want a burrito; I want a quesadilla. She then proceeds to walk away from the counter. Never have I ever ordered from Chipotle and a) had a ruder employee, b) was never asked if they could fix the problem, and c) honestly, who simply wants chicken and cheese on their quesadilla? To top it off, I was charged extra chicken, when I never asked for that. I ended up leaving frustrated and with a $7 cheese and chicken quesadilla with no sour cream, no Chipotle sauce, and nothing in it. Needless to say, I will not visit Chipotle anymore, but instead I will find a Moe's and/or Qdoba.
Ta-Korea tacos were just ok. Not great. Service was pretty fast and friendly. I will return at some point to try some of the other menu options.

Worst management I've ever delt with. Bought a Groupon under their location but then the manager told me that the  voucher was for a restaurant in a different state. Wouldn't take it, wouldn't help us, still had to pay full price even though we didn't eat our hibachi. I've never heard of such bad hospitality. I left feeling embarrassed and scammed! I can't be the only person that has falling for this, he knew about the Groupon and still hasn't done anything to contact them and have it taken down!

Pros: 

Cocktail shrimp appetizer was fresh and tasty, side of peewee potatoes were delicious, but the salad was an experiment gone awry.  They just didn't pull off whatever they were attempting with the salad.

Visited for lunch, it was after 2:00 so we thought they'd be slow but they had a steady stream of folks. We decided on the tuna sandwich (husband) and I had the tuna stuffed tomato on salad. They give you plenty tuna and it was good-pretty standard.  The salad was was a good size too. Husband had the potato salad as his side, he liked it okay. 
There was only one waitress so she was running around waiting on quests and cleaning tables. She's friendly and acknowledges everyone as they arrive. 
It did take multiple trips for the table to be cleaned off, order taken, silverware delivered, etc.
You're going to order it anyway because you're drunk and hungry, but they've screwed up my order more times than they've gotten it right. One time the cheese was missing from half my pie.

So not worth the hype.   Yelp finally failed me.  I was in the mood for Japanese and was thrilled to see a 4 star place so close to me.  The food was eh, the service even worse as I had an Thompson Twin clone as a server and the wait too long once the order was in.  Skip.

Upscale atmosphere in the lounge.  Numerous TV screens and some for betting on the races. Wings are huge and can come with veggies.   Happy hour specials.  Meals otherwise expensive.  Servers were pleasant.  Music not to loud.  Free parking.  Nicely padded seats and booth seats.  I would return.  At least for lunch!

Used to love this place but my last two visits from out of town have been disappointments. The tenderloins are not the same and taste store bought. Onion rings and root beer are still good but I would pass on the tenderloins.

Great little gem for great chinese! Can't go wrong! Definitely my new go to spot! The fried rice and Lo Mein are delish! Also they have awesome apps, the pot stickers, crab Rangoons, & egg rolls are awesome!

We stopped by here after shopping and a desire for something sweet and cold struck us. Neither of us had tried boba tea before so we arrived here with some excitement. 

This is a small place with some limited seating, food and drinks are serve from behind a counter much like a coffee shop. There's and extensive menu with different kinds of crepes, teas and exploding boba. 

I told the staff we were newbies and they explained the menu choices and made recommendations. I got the Thai milk tea with boba. The most traditional item on the menu and my wife got the apple chai with mango exploding boba. While we both liked what we ordered, we liked each other's order even better! The traditional Thai tea was less sweet than I expected, and the apple chai was too sweet for my wife but perfect for me. The tea had plenty of boba and hit the spot on a warm afternoon. We will return to try out the other types of tea and boba on the menu.
