My wife and I ate here when we stayed downtown for a night.  Food was really good, location was great and neat, older building.  We were the first ones there and they opened a couple minutes later than they had posted but quick service and would eat here again.

I've always had high expectations of this place based on reviews from friends who are regulars so I finally went to check it out for myself. I wasnt extremely hungry at the time of my visit so I didn't order a full meal. We started off with bang bang shrimp which is one of their most popular items and it was fantastic. Great flavor and decent portion size. Also got the edamame which was tasty but nothing special. Next I ordered a bowl of lobster bisque which is usually my favorite soup, but I wasn't crazy about theirs. The soup itself had a good flavor but the lobster meat is where it was lacking. It's Better when served shredded and mixed in with the soup, but this was 3 large pieces floating on top, which could not be cut easily and weren't very tender or easy to chew. I had to eat each piece all in one bite and it was what I would call "fish overload". Our server was professional but not exactly warm and friendly. At one point I witnessed another server blowing his breath all over a dessert that was about to be served to another table as some sort of a prank. "Ew" is all I can say about that. 

Because the environment was really warm and enjoyable and the bang bang shrimp was delicious I would probably go back again for that (especially on Wednesday when it's only $5 instead of $9) but I won't be a regular guest. I think I must be one of the few people who isn't head over heels crazy for bonefish

The host and server greeted me promptly.  Nice atmosphere.  The appetizer plate was tasty, way too many fried pickles, wings were highlight, but only 3 of them.  Coke was semi-flat tasting.  Music was low, heard more of the traffic and Spanish speaking family.  The cheese pizza was tasteless; needed ranch dressing for flavor. Shrimp po' boy sandwich was an embarrassment.  I'm not even Creole and mine taste way better and have more flavor.  Sorry u r in NOLA your food should have FLAVOR.  Please stop by a nearby seasoning shop and buy some seasonings guys.

Soho Sushi never disappoints. We ordered several rolls, appetizers, dessert, and a bottle of wine for our party and all was good. Their spicy tuna and fried rice are always regular orders for us and those were great as expected. We did order the crab rangoon and shrimp tempura this time and those will for sure make their way into our rotation. The crab rangoon has green onion or the like in the mix that gives it a really nice flavor. Loved the addition of the valet because parking there was a dread in the past.

My favorite brunch place in the city! Cute, simple decor, and never more than a 15 minute wait on the weekends. I've gotten the breakfast nachos the last 5 times I've eaten there- my absolute favorite dish. It's incredibly fresh, crunchy, and bursting full of flavor. Large enough to share for two people. It comes with chorizo, but I actually like it better without.  Side note, I can't love a brunch place without loving their potatoes, and these are absolutely delicious. In addition, it's great that you can order a single pancake or waffle on the side. It solves the savory vs sweet brunch dilemma that we often find ourselves in

Just moved to Tucson and so lucky to have this place near my home! This place is the real deal when it comes to authentic Vietnamese dishes. This is what it should be in my opinion, just fresh real ingredients in large portions. The place is small but very clean and cozy. I think I just found one of the best kept secrets in Tucson!

The staff was very kind and nice to interact with. The rooftop pool and rooftop gym room is neat. The lobby is stunning and fun to take in for a few mins. The hallways feel grand just like the lobby, but then you eventually have to head to the inside of your room....

Room 921 had the wall paper ripping off in the bathroom and the room was filthy. The carpet was dirty and well over due for a replacement. Noticed the blanket had black flecks of something on it so shook off the cover and checked the mattress itself for bed bugs and was appalled with how filthy and old the mattress had to be. They cover the mattress with a mattress topper. Why can't the mattresses be newer and clean and actually comfy to sleep on? Sleep is the most important part of a person's life and is crucial for a fun vacation. I did not sleep well at all and now my sleep schedule feels completely off. Very disappointed in the bed and in my stay at Le Pavillion. I get that I signed up to stay in an old hotel that was supposed to have vintage charm and antique flair, but there is no reason the bed itself has to be an antique and there is no reason cleaning should ever be skimped on.

I've been here a few times. Just not that great to me. It's like hit or miss with items. 2 apps I enjoy are the fiery honey shrimp (when the shrimp is crispy) and their fried pepper jack bites. What's cool is you can get tap beer at your table and the overall atmosphere is nice, plus they play good music. Their burger buns are branded which is cool but we weren't impressed with the taste. Our entrees are never really good its just ok. Even my boys didn't care for their chicken strips, just mediocre.

5/5 stars is an understatement. Voodoo Gumbo was HANDS DOWN the best restaurant we visited in Nashville. The Food, the atmosphere, and the customer service was nothing but amazing. 

Make sure you visit!!!

I came here for lunch with a friend. I would say I had better sushi but we decided to come because of the 50% off. When we went in there nobody was at the front to start us so we thought it was closed. But they finally came and seated us. The interior of the restaurant is pretty decent, they done a good job with it and keeping the place clean. The menu has a big selection of different types like specialty or 'hot' sushi. I kept in simple by ordering the shrimp tempura, tuna, salmon and shrimp dragon roll. My friend had the double crab, crab and Angel roll. The portion size is pretty small but the place is cheaper than other sushi place I've been to. Overall been a good experience. Customer service was good after they finally seated us and saw customers.

Real southern seafood. They Fry they're fish like my Louisiana family. No sauce needed because the seasoning is on point. The kids meal was enough to fill me up. My kids loved it. The seating is very cozy and snug. They deliver too.

My boyfriend, Matt and I were in the city at the Barnes Foundation and wanted sushi for lunch.  Most of the places we knew of are only open for dinner.  So we turned to Yelp and Dasiwa was open for lunch and everyone was giving it great reviews.   We were not disappointed and loved everything!

We walked in and were greeted promptly and were seated.  We were told to look at the lunch specials on the board.  Matt and I both decided to get the maki trio for lunch.  It consisted of a california roll, salmon roll, and a tuna roll.  Matt also ordered miso soup and I ordered a sashimi salad.  The salad was served in a martini glass and had a little bit of heat to it which I liked.  Matt's soup was also great and he enjoyed it.  We both enjoyed our maki trio and it was priced at $17.  While we were there a few customers stopped in for coffee and a pastry and there were 2 other tables.  The staff was friendly and our waters were kept filled.  Dasiwa is a BYOB and would be a great place for a nice dinner.  

I will definitely be back!

As the only customer at the counter, It shouldn't take 15 minutes to get medium fries and shake (to go). Maybe if the horseplay was kept to minimum..:. 
And the fries were soggy. The shake was good though.

Ashli's bubbly personality welcomed me when I walked in the door. She described the menu very well, including the great pies. I ate the farmer's frittata. Really enjoyed the mushrooms as they really provided great flavor. Craft beer and liquor available; bottomless mimosas on the weekends, so I will check that out at a later date. Finally, Zudar's provides a great location as it's close to Bayshore and next to a Publix.

This is the place for some wonderful food. I get the opportunity to visit them a couple of time a year and always ask myself why I don't come here more often.  The steak modiga is great -  the sauce is not overpowering the medium rare medallion cold perfectly. Highly recommended!! The staff is always very accommodating and pleasant. 
Always busy - call ahead to be safe.

My go-to place for my annual trip to New Orleans!  We always go as a large group and close the place down, but the staff is friendly, knowledgeable and accommodating.  They manage to get all of our food out at the same time, everyone's entree cooked perfectly.  On my last trip, I apologized to the owner's daughter for our party taking so long and she was so gracious, telling us it was no problem whatsoever and filling us in on some of the history of the restaurant and the building.

A Fantastic BBQ place. Great service, nice atmosphere, broad selection and amazing food. I'm no BBQ connoisseur but this is probably the best I've ever had and would highly recommend checking them out.

I reeeally wish I would have remembered to take pictures of the food before our table devoured it all :-(

 Anyhoo, there was maybe a 20-25 minute wait when we came. When we finally got in, it was PACKED but that didn't affect the service, thankfully. Our server was very nice, attentive, and accommodating. My uncle "needed" (lol) to watch a particular game on a particular TV and she made it happen for him.

I decided on the fried platter which was pretty good, although it made me realize that I don't really care for fried oysters. I definitely enjoyed the fried fish & shrimp that came with it, though. 

The chargrilled oysters...Get them! Eat them! Love them!...& thank me later ;-)

Really delicious!  Burmese food is so good.  We had their tea leaf salad, which was really unique and tasty.  Chopped lettuce with peanuts, it had a sweet and sour taste, very refreshing with crunchy nuts.  We also got their thousand year bread (fried dough, how can you not like it?) with potato curry (curry is key so you can dip the bread!).  

We also got their jungle chicken which tasted like key lime pie, creamy good- chunks of chicken in this creamy, lime sauce.  Their chicken curry was pretty good, but would try something else next time- it was just chunks of chicken in a sauce.

Definitely try their tea leaf salad and their thousand year bread!!  Their dessert is pretty good too, lots of coconut flavored good stuff!

I never waited 45 minutes for a California roll , but I sure did here . They place was not busy with customers , but they where 2 busy filling to go orders . I've never waited this long for basic sushi rolls in my life .

If you want to wait indefinitely for someone to come to your table, you have found the right place. If you desire coffee, but never want to taste it, you have come to the right place. If you want to leave after 20 minutes of no service, you guessed it, this is your place. Not a one time thing either, tried it twice anf both times, complete lack of service.

THE BEST PHO EVER!! No place can beat the pricing, portions, or taste here.

Other places have good pho too, but, whenever I'm really craving pho, all I can think about is pho ha.

**warning(?): cash only

I had the avocado blt ans it was delightful. The perfect lunch that wwont weigh you down and came with lightly dressed greens on the side but I i wouldn't consider it a salad. I would return for sure.
Food is good and delivery was timely, but when the pizza arrived it had been crushed on one side by the box and the pizza was only partially cut.

There are lots of fanciful names for simple classic breakfasts. They do however have some more "progressive" options like turkey sausage. My experience was very average but not bad. Our waiter was a bit impatient but ultimately accommodating.

I wouldn't describe myself as being well-versed in Korean cuisine, but I am definitely a fan of Bibimbop.  I came to Miga on a Friday night with 2 bottles of Cabernet Sauvignon thinking I was going to eat with 2 friends, only to find that the reservation was for 10, much to my surprise.

FIRST IMPRESSIONS:
I was instantly greeted by a smiling hostess who invited me to wait for the rest of my party at the sushi bar.  They do not (yet) have a bar, it's BYOB.  Shortly after, the waiter who was to be serving us that night introduced himself to me, asked if I had any questions, what kinds of wine glasses we would like, and directed me to some entertainment while I waited-- a fishbowl on the sushi bar filled with male crabs fighting to the death (they had nothing better to do).

THE ATMOSPHERE:
Visually, it's pretty modest, but that's a good thing I suppose.  Just the right balance to give it some personality, separating it from lower-end Asian reastaurants, but it doesn't try get too artsy or give off heavy vibes.  The choice of music should be reconsidered, the trance and vocoder-heavy soundtrack comes off tacky and totally doesn't match the setting of the restaurant.

THE FOOD:
Using my experience with the delicious dish known as bibimbop, I felt that Miga's was delicious, definitely in my Top 3 spots for it in Philly.  Served in a hot stone bowl, with a fried egg on a separate plate, the shredded beef was tasty, and I love it when the rice forms a sort of baked crust on the bowl.  I think I would have enjoyed the meal a lot more had I gone with a less dry wine, but that's my own damn fault.  It's also my own fault for drinking entirely too much of that wine.  But I digress, I was admittedly unadventurous with the food, but I really enjoyed what I had.

THE SERVICE:
Delightful.  I must be getting lucky with the service I've been receiving recently.  Our waiter, I believe his name was Young, was very friendly, displayed a sense of humor, and was courteous, even stepping up to pay for one girl in our party's entree when it came out of the kitchen a bit late.  The man who I assume was the owner or manager was also friendly, joking around with us as we were reading the menus.

THE PRICING:
Incredibly reasonable.  I was surprised how much food I got (I couldn't finish my entrée), for so little money.  It's really great to be able to go out and enjoy some international cuisine like this without breaking the bank.

THE BOTTOM LINE:
A great experience, good food, friendly service, I don't eat much Korean, but I would definitely go back to Miga, and I would definitely recommend it for people seeking tasty, reasonably-priced Korean food in a relaxed setting.

We came here as an alternate to our loss of FlapJacks...  The coffee was very good.  We ordered Hoosier Bread and had to return it, as the outside was brown, but middle was raw dough. My guest had French Toast and Indy Skillet. The French Toast was not evenly cooked. The one side was lightly seared only. I got the belgium combo, which was just a std round wafle, not the deep pockets and batter was not Belgium with light airy mix. It was more like pancake battered waffle. The balance of the food and execution was similar to the Hoosier Bread starter, where the temperature of iron and fryer temp was too high. They deep fried my fresh sausage, which made casing like plastic. We may return, as out breakfast options on Sunday have decreased locally for goo homestyle options, but not without reservation. The home style potatoes, b/c of fryer temp were good.  The balance of meal was just poor execution in the back at a time that was not busy. Only four tables seated.

The Galley is a solid addition to a block that badly needed SOMETHING to happen there. 

This bar is located on 4th Street one block south of Williams park. If you're driving, its pretty easy to find it because there's a huge, beautiful mural painted on the second story. If you're walking by, you'll notice a passthrough bar, a few tables outside, and the door is usually open. The space inside is decked out in a hipster/nautical theme. I wouldn't say its a fully immersive experience, but you get what they're going for. The tap list is impressive, although one of my primary complaints is that its a little bit pricey (~$7 for a local craft beer... frustrating when you can walk down the street to the brewery and pay $5). Wednesdays are 1/2 price bottles of wine, and this is when we went. It was surprisingly busy and we got good service seated at the passthrough. 

They have a Yeti club, where you pay $100 and get a yeti mug (worth ~$40), plus discounts on drinks- they pour you a 16 oz beer for the price of a 12 oz, or a 1.5x pour for a the price of a single. There's no system in place for wine. I'm told you can take the yeti with you, but I'm not sure. I think it makes sense if you live nearby, or if the Galley is going to be "your spot", but assuming the value of each extra pour is $3, you need to consume at least 20 drinks there to pay for the markup. 34 drinks if you can't actually take the cup off premises. I don't go out enough to make it worth it, but I can see where it could be.

The biggest knock on the Galley is its location. Hopefully this improves over time, but having the spice selling corner store as your neighbor makes for an odd outdoor environment. While we were seated outside we got to watch a few drug deals, were accosted for money by a few panhandlers, and watched a homeless person try and steal a patron's bike. The Galley needs to take a stronger stand against this (like Crowley's used to), or its going to kill the outdoor environment. 

Overall, its a solid addition to DTSP.
Good was ok. Skip the gumbo. Get the cracklings but make sure to get a small. Chewed so much my jaw hurt but they were tasty.

I think they have the best tasting ribs in the area.  Unfortunately, they didn't have a ton of meat on them (since my guess is that they were cooked for days making them tender and smaller) but they were priced at the high end for a 1/2 rack rib meal locally.  I wouldn't get them if you are starving, but they were still awesome and more fairly priced if you only get the ribs without the whole dinner.  I can't imagine a better $10 appetizer than a 1/2 rack of these.

Had spinach (for diet - rather than enjoyment reasons) and a taste of the mac and cheese for sides.  Both were outstanding.  Even ate all the spinach :)
Quick service even when the place is packed on a Saturday at 6pm. They have all the Louisiana classics and they all taste amazing. Definitely recommend!

The tortillas are so good that I got them delivered to Brooklyn for the 8 years I lived there.  The small jalapeno tortillas make the best breakfast with eggs and chorizo and I can never leave without buying tamales.  When they have the green corn in stock, buy some!

My order from yelp didn't get to their system. They still made my food quickly. The food was okay, but I still had a slight allergic reaction. It's very hard to find restaurants that cater to my allergy.

Note: this is my memory from years ago, and I still think it's the best fried chicken I've not only ever had but actually changed my thinking about fried chicken in general

Coop's doesn't look like much. It is dive bar-y. The bathroom, if you have to go, should come with a warning label. The "service" has some serious attitude (fine with me, whatever). But you're not here for any of that. What you're here for is the fried chicken. I don't even know they made fried chicken like this. I don't know what they do to (and I don't want to know) but it is like, like, heaven if heaven is full of fats and meats and deep fried goodness. No wonder Southerners are fat, if it all tastes like this. God damn. And the rabbit jambalaya (which my sister still curses me for eating - years later, "poor bunnies," well poor bunnies taste delicious sometimes) also really damn good. This is a local's place. Good food. Good drinking. Who cares if the table wobbles?

Charming neighborhood delightful gem!  The service was outstanding - truly as good as it gets.  Our server knew exactly what was in each dish.  I absolutely cannot eat cheese, I have a very strong aversion, she knew it was in the meatballs, but said she could substitute sausage.  She brought me special bread they had just baked, without parmesean.  She was amazingly thoughtful and knowledgeable.  

The food was sooo delicious!  The bread was crusty yet soft and warm.  My pasta was cooked perfectly, and the marinara had clearly been simmering for hours, it had a deep, rich, vibrant, tomatoey taste.  We were too full for dessert, but lingered a bit over our wine (great wine list at all price points!).  

This is a great special occasion restaurant, we just happened to be celebrating an average Tuesday.
Incredible hotdogs, great for any meal, but particularly satisfying for a late night nosh.

A pleasant surprise! We got a bunch of cups instead of bowls so that we could sample more of the menu on a budget. The jambalaya goes away very quickly when you add the house hot sauce, the chicken andouille gumbo is off every chain, and the seafood gumbo is nice and light yet very filling. Go here!

I stopped by this location for a quick dinner before heading back to the hotel in the evening. It serves breakfast omelets, salads, soups and coffee. They have a large selection of hot and cold soups that can be paired with a full or half salad. I ordered the gazpacho and Summer Salad half salad. The gazpacho was very fresh, spicy and pureed; it was perfect for the hot day.I wish I had gotten the full bowl of the soup. Everything was served quickly and all the soup seemed fresh and not merely reheated. I also tasted the Chicken Velvet which the server said was a classic Indy soup. It had a creamy base with hint so lemon and bits of fine chicken. Tasty, but I prefer more vegetables and a broth base.

The salad was tiny but also light with the balsamic served on the side.  I would have liked to try their breakfasts or other soups but ran out of time. They have a couple bar stools and outdoor seats if you decide to eat in.

Some of the best wings I've had. Also, get the loaded fries and thank me later. The staff was super nice and even with a party of 5 ordering 80 wings between us at walk in, the food didn't take long to cook. Cute resistant setup that also has a beer garden and serves dessert!
The wine list is extensive and the waitress was kind and helpful. We got a cheeseboard, which was incredible, the burrata pasta, meatball, and ceased salad. I will definitely be back!

Out of this world!  I am a fan of BBQ.  I thought I knew good BBQ, but this place is absolutely next level.  Most places soak their meats in sauces.  Not here.  The rib tips came out with salt and pepper. They did not need any sauce!  They have a burnt end that is a cube of meat off the moist end of the brisket.  Do not use any sauce.  It does not need it.  I am gluten free and Keto.  This place fits the bill for both.  My wife LOVED the deviled pig.  It was a lightly fried ball of goodness.  Now, if you like sauces ( not needed!) They have a white sauce that is crazy good.  The mustard is perfect for me being on Keto.  Wish this place were closer!  Any time I'm with 30 minutes I'll be by.  The local population does not know how lucky they are.

Wowowow this was the best sushi I've had in Philadelphia by far. Umai Umai is located just off Spring Garden Street. Its modern and intimate decor matched its equally modern take on Japanese food. I could not have been more impressed! 

I came with a group of 5 on a week night. Umai Umai is a BYOB (!!!) so plan accordingly. We ordered fried calamari, seaweed salad, rock shrimp tempura, and the oyster and sea urchin shooters to start. The shooters were excellent; we were instructed to pour the contents of the shell into the shotglass full of sauce, chew, and then swallow. For dinner, we ordered the 4-8-15-16-23-42 (shout out to any LOST fans), Henrietta, Eternal Sunshine, Godzilla, and a spicy tuna. The Godzilla, which contained shrimp tempura, avocado, macadamia nuts, strawberries, and honey, was my favorite by far! I would definitely recommend any of their "designer rolls". All that we tried were unique and delicious!

Ever since brothers in Cinnaminson closed i've been looking for another pizzeria that I can call my new standby however his place just didn't cut it. The pizza wasn't bad or it wasn't good it was exactly a slice of mediocre pie. I also attribute this to a very poor location though it's located on route 130 it's an absolute pain to get out of the parking lot which can deter customers. In due time I will give this place another try however it will not be for a plain pizza
Service looks kind of like they don't want to be there. Other than that, they're fast-- probably the fastest Wawa in North Wilmington.

Went here on a date with my husband and we were both very disappointed. We got the pizza and listened to music. Well let's say we listened to the music because we couldn't talk. The music was sooooo loud we could do nothing but look at each other.  The waitress could barely hear us to order and she disappeared. When she reappeared with our pizza she set it down and took off. The cheese on pizza was not even melted and tasted bland with no spice at all not to mention cold. We couldn't find our waitress to order drinks or have our pizza cooked a little longer. Meanwhile while we waited the couple next to us got steaks. They looked delicious. Oops said that too fast they both sent their steaks back. But that happened only because the gentleman got up to get his waiter. They were both burned on the outside and raw in center. When our waitress finally showed up 20 min later we had one drink and one piece of pizza each while unable to have a conversation. We got the bill tipped accordingly and left the overpriced pizza. This dinner of 1.5 hours was an AWFUL experience. Oh by the way the couple next to us still didn't have their steaks back and were getting up to walk out behind us. Can't believe this place is still making it.

Pretty good. I've been here a few times and I'm always pretty happy with what I get. I only get a bagel with cream cheese now though because every time I get a sandwhich I notice there's always 1 thing incorrect with the order. Won't hold it against them. Good bagels.

Boyfriend and I came in for lunch before our road trip. I expected more as this restaurant got 4 stars but it was ok. I ordered Bun Bo Hue and boyfriend got the Pho. Nothing about the place was a wow. Food/service/price was all mediocre.

This place is amazing. We have been twice and both times been amazed. For one, I am vegan, so in order to go out to fine dining anywhere I am usually relegated to finding an Italian place and getting plain pasta, something that gets old very fast no matter how good the place is. I have always been a fan of Indian food, but the food at Tashan is unique. It is a perfect blend of Indian inspired dishes with French finery. I had so many options of dishes and they were all unbelievable. My partner, the carnivore went on and on about the boar that melted in his mouth. On top of that everyone in the place went above and beyond to be at our beck and call, from opening the car door outside the restaurant to catering more to my dietary needs than any place I have ever dined before. Last night our server, Bennett, was also serving a huge party of easily 20 plus people, yet we never felt neglected. He was amazing, explaining each dish thoroughly and pointing out what I could eat and what could be modified for me. Back on New Year's Eve, when we tried this place for the first time, Virginia, modified the tasting menu for us so that my partner could have meat dishes, while I had plenty to eat that was vegan. Both servers were so nice and outgoing, that it added to the atmosphere of having everything and everyone at our service. Also, we had so much food both times, that we brought much of it home, too stuffed to eat another bite and for a very reasonable price considering the classy atmosphere. It is quickly becoming my favorite restaurant.

I gotta admit that their food they serve is top notch. I highly recommend it to one of my friends, and the service there is fantastic. As a fellow yelper, I had no problem with how the service is ran. I would give it 5 stars for the food, beverages, fries, and shakes. I have 2 reasons why I had to give smash Burger 5 stars. 1. The food and beverages are fantastic and 2. If anyone should try smash Burger, it would be my friends and colleagues

This is our first visit to Tried & True Alehouse. We arrived right at 5:00 pm and it was already getting busy. We received a friendly greeting and seated immediately. The bar seating was full when we arrived so we sat in the family area. 

Zach greeted us immediately, brought our drinks, and gave us ample time to checkout the versatile menu. 
The beer menu is extensive and they serve many local craft brews and cans.

My husband ordered the Octoberfest, grilled tenderloin and skin-on fries. The tenderloin was good, nice flavor and the fries were terrific. 

I ordered the BBQ Bacon Chicken dinner. It's a tender BBQ Chicken breast topped with slightly crisp, smoked bacon, Swiss cheese and honey mustard dressing. Served atop a pile of scratch made, red skin mashed potatoes. I subbed a cup of chili for the broccoli. The flavors blended nicely and was delicious served with the mashed potatoes. The mild chili was flavorful and very meaty. 

The menu had several appetizers and entrees I'd like to try in the future. I can see us returning soon with friends who highly recommended Tried and True Alehouse. Our first impression was positive with good food, attentive and friendly server, lots of craft beers and a fun atmosphere.

YES -- I am an avid fan of Babalu. We typically sit at the bar and the service there is friendly and fun. I really enjoy their brunch and their belinis ($4). There is always a crowd of regulars that are fun to chat with and happy to be there.

Regarding the food, Babalu's makes a wonderful egg-white omelet, consistently great pork chops, excellent mashed potatoes, and solid wings. I do not like any of their desserts. They have a lot of misses on the their menu (like their side salad and broccoli bites), but the neighborhood/local charm and warmth make me return over and over. It's definitely a "diney diner," so don't expect too much and just have fun. 

They also deliver, which is a wonderful resource when you've come in off the boat and want food without the hassle of leaving the house.

This is our go-to brunch spot in Carp, in fact, we would go every other day if it was appropriate! Standard meal is the potato skin hash which is amazing (gotta get the jalapeño bacon upgrade)! My husband has gotten everything from their omelets to the biscuits and gravy and everything we've tried has been filling and delicious. We keep bringing different sets of friends here and everyone leaves happy. 

Coffee is hot, bloody marys are spicy, Rick and Rick are always super welcoming! Once you go this will be your regular breakfast spot.
this is a great breakfast place and had wonderful food. Try the Sunny eggs benedict if you can.
Tasty gem in an otherwise dismal downtown area.

The cafe is at American Airlines concourse. It occupies the prime center location. We are glad that finally the airport has some great restaurants for people. Mise en Place is one of them. 

The menu is simple. They have flat iron steak sandwich or hanger steak dinner plate. This bring up the standard of the airport dining. I did not order any of that and I got the Mahi Mahi. It is grilled mahi mahi with sweet potatoes, corn and spinach. The stir fry veggies is great. The mahi mahi need work. It need to have burn a bit with less wash sea taste. Unfortunately the Mahi Mahi doesn't standout. If not it can be better. 

Service is good since the bar has easy access to food he server. Food came out quick and allow me to boarding with plenty of time.

Staff was friendly although my time was brief because I only order 2 desserts . Baby let me tell you that brownie was delish with all those amazing layer  you got the pretzel on top , underneath dark chocolate, go deeper you got the whip cream and the star of the show brownie yum ! . FYI their chocolate chip is great but microwave that bad boy chocolate dripping! Love it definitely going back

We were really excited to come to Luna Cafe! But sadly it wasn't that great! Service wasn't good at all had to go inside for refills on coffee and silverware. Are food came out wrong and no one ever came out to see if there was any issues. When we went to pay we asked for separate checks but was told they didn't do that and since its cash only we can just split it ourselves. Over all not a great experience! But the mugs are cute!

Waited inline at register for almost 10 mins while a manager (yalawnda) (female) Heavy Set an two female waitresses stood there talking about another guest they where yelling at. I spoke up and said we're waiting to be rang up, the manger turned around an said where busy and went back to talking. How rude talking to a paying Guest like that. I spoke to our Waitress after we got Seated and asked who the manager was standing at Register she gave me the information. and Made sure we had a Good dinner and kept on apologizing to us about the Managers Behavior.  I have Emailed Golden Corral's Corp Office twice over this Matter and still haven't gotten an email or Call back Regarding this issue.

The Good
 + excellent friendly service
 + good prices
 + great food
 + nice decor and plants
 + excellent green curry
 + non traditional som-tum

The Bad
 - too mildly spiced
 - plastic table cloths
 - poor location
 - no drunken noodles dish

The Food
 * for an appetizer we had Thai Treasure which is a combination platter including several dumplings, fried tofu, satay chicken (on a stick), spring roll and som-tum.  All of this was served with a side of satay sauce, a sweet flavorless red sauce (duck?), and sweet n spicy plum sauce.  The som-tum was the best part, although it's not a traditional som-tum (they replaced papaya with cabbage and didn't use shrimp or fish paste.)
 * Green Curry - this is the creamiest and most complex green curry I've had anywhere.  The lemongrass aroma is fresh and distinct.... absolutely delicious, but they should have used more hot pepper.  Also, It wasn't very spicy although it was marked on the menu as their hottest dish.
 * Evil Jungle Princess - this was also a very good chicken, vegetable and rice dish and was about as spicy as the green curry but was  flavored with a red curry and had large mushrooms in it.

Overall it was a good experience and probably worth the 21 mile round trip drive, but I think I'll try to make it back to Thai Tida (Lamberville, NJ) before revisiting White Elephant.

Come on, Rae. We could have had something, you know? My friends were saying such good things about you, and seriously, you looked REALLY good on paper. My mom would have been so proud. So when we finally met at last, I have to say that I was more than a little disappointed. Sure, you looked gorgeous, with your beautiful dining room and high ceilings. And you were super convenient, since I was picking my friend up from the train station and all. It could have been so good between us.

But from the moment I sat down, things went south, and not in the kind of way I'm usually hoping they do on a good date. The server seemed like she was doing us a favor by taking our order, and would have preferred to be anywhere but where she was. And those famous Rabbit Nachos I've heard so much about? Not only should they be re-named (they're much more similar to rabbit empanadas, but what do I know, I just eat out 7 days a week?) but they were just ehhh. I had a shrimp Caesar salad, and while it filled my belly, I walked away feeling a little unsatisfied and a lot let down.

But don't let it get to you, Rae. Just because it didn't work out between us doesn't mean that there's not somebody else out there for you. Just look at all these other glowing reviews. And just so we end it on a positive note, your lemonade was delish. Tart, bitter and a tiny bit sweet...just like I like it. See, maybe you get me after all.
We had a great lunch on the deck~fast service, great food of which we had fish tacos and shrimp tacos and a wonderful view. We will be back

Today was my first time to try Honeygrow and I will definitely be back. I tried the Stirfry with whole wheat noodles, chicken, egg, and vegetables (broccoli, spinach, and squash). The textures and flavors of the combination of fresh foods were perfect. The crunch of the added cashews completed the delicious meal in a box. 

I may have to return tomorrow for the salad that my daughter raves about so often.
Burnt okra and had to pay for the honey. No bueno. Not the establishment they use to be
try the lunch menu. the bulgogi was amazing. must go and must try. always a pleasant meal everytime we go here. 5/5

Do not pass by without stopping here!!! This place is delicious! The bagels are a great texture, and the muffins are cooked daily and so good! The cranberry orange muffins are my fave! Definitely try the cheddar herb bagel!

We walked past this place over the weekend, it's in my daughter's neighborhood.  I was so impressed!!  I can't wait to come back!!  WOW!  Fresh homemade empanadas, the organic native salad was FANTASTIC!!  I could not believe how good the cholla buds tasted, and you wouldn't think chilies would be good in salad, but they were!  Nuts and seeds, just fantastic!!  I had the molletes - it was open-faced with hibiscus flowers that were sautéed in chipotle! It tasted so good, it was lightly sweet and you had the texture of the actual flowers!!  I want to bring everyone I know here and try everything on the menu!  Just so local and such a good vibe on the patio!

The Tap is not my favorite beer bar, but I always enjoy it. The service is fast, the beer list is ridiculously extensive, and the food ranges from OK-to-good. For someone who knows little about beer, I appreciate the work they've put in to make it accessible. They provide note cards with their flights so that you can make notes on your favorites, and have a 2-way sweet-bitter/light-dark spectrum on their menu to show you where each beer falls.  

Also, this place is humongous and has a gorgeous, dog-friendly patio. During the weekends, they have live music at nights. Like I said, it's not my favorite, but it's a staple because of it's size (i.e., it's not as hard to find a seat as some other places on Mass Ave) and because there's something for everyone food-, beer-, entertainment- and ambiance-wise. Non-beer drinkers beware though--they do not serve hard alcohol.

My mom has been getting cookies and baked goods from Gianino's for some time. I recently went there myself and found the Italian Rum cannolis incredibly delicious. I find rum cake far too rich and it spoils but a cannoli is the perfect erving size. My son loves them!

Their recent renovation makes the place look sleek and really nice.

I've been here before and loved it but today it started out bad when we got here and they didn't have our reservation.   They had a very poor system for taking them... a sheet of paper without lines, dates, times or any organization but somehow this was my fault.   I know it was my fault because the hostess told me her system was good regardless of the evidence to the contrary.   They smashed us into a corner and brought out something resembling chicken but cut in a way that it's impossible to eat,  I couldn't even stomach it since it was all bone and skin,  very little meat.  Mushy green beans,  and the dessert was very unappetizing.  Not sure what the dessert was supposed to be... maybe cake but it didn't have icing it just had chocolate chips and white sugar mound on top of it.  Will never waste a trip here again.   Maybe they had a change in ownership, management or something.  Do not bother coming here.
Great causal brunch spot. Creative menu. Reservations are suggested for busier times.

i call to order and who ever picked up the phone was mumbling I could barely hear the person...and sounded annoyed and very mad like he had a attitude. i usually get a cheesesteak from here i dont really like it tho the last time i ordered it was dripping and so soggy as if it was dipped in oil...the fries are okay.
  ...just letting yall know.

I went here the other day with my younger sister for a late dinner, around 9pm. When I first saw the restaurant It didn't make me think Greek. However, when you walk in the dim lighting, stone floors, marble style countertops, as well as the diner style seating with copper colored chairs helped create a cozy warm welcoming atmosphere for me and other guests. 
Our service was welcoming from the minute we walked in the door and were greeted by the host. Our waitress was just as friendly although it did feel a little rushed (Possibly because it was later at night near close) however she was really nice got us our food quickly and kept my water glass full. Which is a big deal for me if my waitress/waiter can keep my water glass full it always leaves a very good impression on me. 
For an appetizer, we got the 'OPA Flaming Saganaki', which is an absolute must. A mild imported cheese they cover in Brandy and light on fire at your table which gives it a good Smokey lemon flavor it is served with pita bread. The pita is softer than crackers and very bland but mixed with the cheese its better than breadsticks with cheese sauce. For an entree, I had a classic Gyro with Feta Cheese. A classic Greek delish that is simple yet delicious. If you order it I suggest you get it with the Feta cheese it just melts in your mouth. 
Overall I had a fantastic experience, a little pricey for a college student but not bad at all. I will definitely be returning as well as recommending it to friends.

I may have just eaten my last meal.  I anticipate having a massive MI at any moment.  But it may have been worth it.  

I had the Commerce Special.  Basically biscuits and gravy but the gravy had cheese, sausage and jalapeños in it served with two lightly fried eggs on top.  I expected something like pump cheese but the gravy was actually a well made mornay but with sausage and jalapeños.   I orders hot sausage as well.  When it all came I thought of this is not bad I'll eat a third of it.  I scrapped the plates and am writing this in my car almost catatonic. 

The place is NOLA old school cool.  What I had was superb and something special.  I am going to buy aspirin.

This little greek owned spot is definitely worth a visit. We were staying nearby and it was recommended. The staff was friendly and efficient. The owner and his son were on site. The Greek omlete was incredible and the waffle and eggs was great also.
affordable, friendly and serving top quality food! Do yourself a favor and go,

Not completely sure why there's such low reviews for Mainstay. I personally thought the food and service was fantastic!

I recommend trying the cauliflower bites. I've heard of this thing where you can make vegan buffalo wings with cauliflower, and I imagine this is what it tastes like and I support it 100%. You can also choose any of the wing sauces they offer to get them tossed in. Perfect appetizer 

For my meal, I went with the signature Mainstay Melt and it was delicious!! It was your typical patty melt with steak, American cheese, an onions all melted down into a beautiful gift of heaven. 

Can't wait to come back!!

First visit to FBC. Good place and I would go back. They were a bit in the weeds and it took them some time to wait on us. They were apologetic though which is what matters in that situation. My son and I had the Franklin burger. It was very good and cooked medium as we asked. You could tell the patties are hand-made and the bun seemed "local" as well. The Franklin burger included a house sauce which was terrific. It reminded me of a Caesar type dressing - which was great. The burger came apart and slid around some, which is a bit nit picky. Again, great burger and I'd go back to try another one. The fries were thin, hand-cut style. Some kind of homemade ketchup was also a plus. Very dark and smokey. My son had a chocolate milkshake which he said was delicious. FBC gets thumbs up from us and certainly glad to see another good local place.

I wish I had more time to try all of their sauces! The ones I did try were mostly incredible. I've had better garlic parm but the bayou sweet heat, teriyaki and especially the pepper jelly were all out of this world. Can't rave about that pepper jelly enough! The wings could be a little bigger but the amazing flavorful sauces make up for it. I also tried my first frog legs here wish were pretty interesting. Good overall. I can't wait to go back.

Paul, our server wasn't attentive.  My food was good.  I was given coffee in a dirty mug.   I had to ask a different server for a clean mug.  She seemed irritated.   She brought me a second coffee.  The mug had something crusty near where I might take a sip.  I guess that was personal.   This was very disappointing.

Very good food but it took more a few visits to figure out what would be my regular order. I love the beans coming out with chips and salsa. Good bar area. We noticed several couples on dates sitting in the bar. Chicken Fundido is the best thing I've tried from their menu.

Tortas are delicious,  come with fries that are crispy,  and at a very reasonable price. The homemade Verde is very flavorful. The soda are all in Spanish and the grocery store has snacks and basic cooking ingredients. My only qualm is that the guacamole has too much cilantro abs onion which masks the avocado. I'll be back again!

My centrally located pick for my birthday dinner with friends, and I'm not gonna lie, Crow's Next wasn't even on my radar until my brother started bartending there.  I read a few reviews and thought it sounded up my crowd's alley, so why not patronize those that pay my family member's bill, right?

Overall, I'd say The Crow's Nest is pretty appropriately labelled with 3 stars - A-Ok for this trip.  Would I go out of my way to visit again?  Probably not.  Would I stop by if I were looking for a bite in the area?  Sure.

For my entree, I ordered the mac n cheese, which was good, but when I make or order a mac n cheese, I tend to like the creamier, smack me in the face with some cheese varieties.  This stayed on the drier cheese end of the spectrum.  Good enough, but not my favorite.  I did try a bite of a friend's grilled cheese w/ bacon which was good and another's BAT (bacon arugula and tomato) that I had waffled back and forth choosing myself, and I should have gone with the BAT!  My husband ordered the pulled pork which he said was good, but the sauce wasn't his fave.  I'll chock that up to personal preference.

We didn't order dessert, because the offerings didn't sound all that appealing to me.  Perhaps the Pear Gorgonzola Bread Pudding would intrigue me more post-finicky pregnant belly.  I had read a stltoday review referring to some sort of chocolate-y bread pudding concoction that sounded awesome.  Alas, it wasn't on the menu.  Sad day.

The service - eh.  Our waitress seemed a little out of it, and the guys once or twice just gave up and ended up ordering beers at the bar which I never take as a good sign of service.

Perhaps a future visit will result in higher marks.

I want this place to work so bad. The seats are great and I love ordering tickets online. It's just staffed and run by buffoons. They're lazy and rude. Theaters are never prepared on time.  I keep coming and hoping it will get better but it just doesn't.

I took my kids to a kids movie and they showed an ad about donating to help kids with cancer. The ad literally said "' help make sure no kids DIE of cancer."  WTH? Wrong audience for a theater full of children.

So we went to the new location after having a so-so experience at the old location.  The moment we walked in the difference was tangible. The new location was clean & neat and we were greeted immediately by a waitress.

It was seat yourself so we grabbed a booth & the waitress came right over with menus. Of course we had to order a slice of their famous French toast.  I ordered the mexican omelet & my date had corned beef hash with two eggs. Standard coffee & water to start with. 

Not long after placing our order the food arrived, talk about quick! The omelet wasn't huge but it was still a decent size along with a good quantity of hash browns and a side of regular toast. Standard omelet stuffed with veggies, meat & cheese within.

Of course I had to try my dates corned beef hash & that was pretty awesome. None of that canned stuff, this was big chunks of real corned beef that the menu bragged they're famous for & I could taste why. 

Speaking of famous,  let's talk about the French toast.  Years ago Yanny's was known as "The French toast king". Now I'm not sure if they got that tag from advertising this on their own or if that's the nickname they earned from this dish but it's definitely true. This was the best damn French toast I've ever had. Served with the extra egg wash cooked on the grill with the French toast sprinkled with cinnamon & powered sugar you almost didn't need syrup... almost. 

Needless to say we will be returning soon!

They make the best root beer floats!!! 

Obviously the dessert menu was my favorite part about Cafe Manhattan, and I can't wait to go back and try all of their dessert menu. Now on to the rest of my experience... 

- The waiter we had was terrible with a capital "T." Barely spoke when he came to our table, rude, looked like he hated his life being there, and messed up our orders. To top it off, our food and drinks were extremely slow on getting to us. I don't know if it was a bad day here or what, but I was not happy with the service portion at all. 

- The decor was way cool, all Elvis and classic 50's memorabilia. They have an old style diner counter too that you can eat at, which looks fun! They also have an old jukebox that I hope still works! 

- It was very clean and seemed organized besides our waiter's portion. 

- The food was pretty good. Don't get a salad though...they were not fresh at all. Yuck! The pizza was good though and so was my mom's beef sandwich. And their cream soda....mmmm!!! 

So I would love to come back again, but next time the service must be better or I am crossing Cafe Manhattan off my list of places to dine. However, I may come back for their desserts no matter what!
Whenever we visit 6/10 brewery, we order from Lolis. The food is fresh, delicious, and well priced. We are never disappointed with the quality or taste and 100% recommend!!!

The east side needs this place badly. But we also need it to step up its game a little. I'll start with the good: pastas are fresh, amazing Italian beef (Chicago vibe), late night menu is cool (and you can eat at mickeys) - friendly staff and clean as a can be. Priced reasonably, but by no means cheap. 

Negatives? For starters, their Marinara could not possibly be more forgettable. Watery, bland, etc. Caprese salad is light on basil and the balsamic reduction, which basically makes it a bowl of tomatoes and mozzarella balls. Caprese is the simplest dish. How do you screw this up? Portillos is a fast food joint in Chicago and even they have decent marinara. I'm giving it 4 stars because I feel like compared to the other crap in East Nashville, this place is solid.
There is so much to choose from. So far everything that I have tried is amazing. I will definitely be adding this to my regular lunch spots.

Loli's is wonderful! Don't be intimidated by the line out the door. It moves fast and so does the kitchen. You'll be eating fantastic sopes and tacos in no time!

As soon as I got out of my car, the amazing smells hit me. This is the defining feature of what makes a great restaurant. It didn't smell like a fast food grease trap. It smelled fresh and tantalizing.

As this was my first time eating here, I wanted to make sure I could give it a fair review, which in my terms means eating everything I possibly can!

I ordered a rib eye taco, carnitas sope, and a pork tamale with red sauce. Admittedly like a 700 calorie lunch, but I have no regrets! The sope was piled high with meat and cheese and topped with just the right amount of cilantro. The cilantro dipping sauce it came with was the perfect complement. I would definitely order this again.

The taco was probably my favorite. The steak was very flavorful (more so than the carnitas) and went really nicely with the hot red sauce that comes with it. I will go back to Loli's just for this magical taco!

Lastly, the tamale. I'll preface this with: I LOVE tamales! Sadly, I wasn't a huge fan of this one. I really wanted to be, but I couldn't get over how tomato-y the sauce was. I was expecting it to be tomato-based, obviously, but it was overpoweringly tomato with nothing else to really deepen the flavor. The tamale itself and the filling were great, if maybe a little under-seasoned. It was just the sauce I wasn't into. I'm still giving Loli's 5 stars, because my experience was great and the sope and taco were DELICIOUS! 

I wish they would expand their dining room to accompany more people, or even extend the deck! It would be a really great way to make the restaurant more inviting. A lot of people get takeout, because they know there's nowhere to sit around lunchtime when it's busiest.

Yesterday was me and my honeys first time ever eating at a Culvers ! Very awesome staff and awesome food ! We signed up for their email list online and if you do that you get a free buy one meal get another value meal for free . The food was super super good and inexpensive and the staff treated us just like family ! Best place ever ! We loved it so much we had to go again the next night for dinner !!! To top it all off we waited maybe like 3 minutes and our food was already ready and hand delivered to our truck window !!! I highly recommend Culver's !!!

Clean, comfortable rooms. Impressed with the complimentary breakfast which had yogurt & cereal to make your own waffles to eggs and sausage to biscuits and gravy. Great spot just south of the busy downtown area. All in all more than pleasant weekend stay here.

Love love this place.. haven't been in many years but was her a week ago and I'm back.. my tostado ceviche de Camarones es deliciouso (the one shrimp ceviche tostado is plentiful and delicious) and is only $3.75.. the 2 waitresses both remembered me.. they were friendly and helpful..
Lunchtime was jumping but I'm here on Tues @ 4:15 and just a few customers so far.. I'll be going back.. next best thing to being in Rocky Point

I came in looking for a medium iced coffee.  After I asked the person behind the counter, she gave me a weird look and said, "we only have small or large" before rolling her eyes.  Sure, okay, so I ask for a large and they tell me they have a $10 min to use a card.  I can understand a restaurant having that high a min, but for a coffee shop, it just seemed silly.  So I used the ATM, got back in line only to hear the person in front of me place an order that was $8.50 something.  The person behind the counter then said, "We have a $10 min, but you're welcome to tip up to $10".

I've never thought of a coffee shop as pretentious until I went here.  Coffee was alright.

went here a few days ago, ordered a buffalo chicken cheesesteak, and the boyfriend ordered a chicken steak with bbq sauce. both were served on a soft amoroso roll, with a generous amount of tender juicy chicken, and a good deal of sauce 
got a "huge" drink... it was rather large, a definite pro. 

overall, a pretty damn good place with decent prices, the only cons being that its a small place, so it may take you a minute to get seated [well worth it in my opinion] and that the parking lot spaces were also limited.

I am from NEW YORK and live in LOS ANGELES and am an avid restaurant goer. Here's why I give 3 stars...

Positive
Ambiance was amazing with a woody yet classy vibe and the server was kind and patient.

Negative
The menu looks great but dont be fooled.
These chefs don't know the meaning of balance; everything was over salted. My family and I ordered the steak, coconut+lime drum (best dish) , and a bunch of sides including the beats, oysters, brussel sprouts and lamb skewers. 


Also, it took 45 minutes for our main dishes to be served and the restaurant was half full. 

So much potential here but damn, Im not a picky eater but the wait was not worth the wild amount of salt.

After a long day of traveling, my friends and I were hungry for a great meal. Our dining experience at Ye Olde College Inn was the perfect start to our trip to New Orleans. Our server, Jimmy (if Jimmy is your server, you are SO LUCKY!!), welcomed us to New Orleans with all of the southern charm and hospitality we could ever dream of. I ordered the Fresh Catch, which I highly recommend. Ye Olde College Inn is a bit out of the way of the French Quarter, but it is worth the journey.

Worst experience EVER! We were too tired to go drive anywhere so we decided to just check this place out. 

We got seated immediately and that made me happy. However It took our server about 15-20 mintues to just greet us and take our orders. We got water and bread from the busser/bus boy. Once we order we noticed there were 3 empty tables. So we're eating our bread and the tables slowly starts to fill up. The tables are quite close together, so I coudn't help but notice how we got our soup the same time the table next to us did. 

Worst of all is when the server dropped off the soup. So the tables are really close, she decides to place herself in the middle of the two tables, stretch her arm out, and she facing the wall while she's doing this and she lowers her arms to put the soup bowl down without trying to see if it would spill or not. Why did she do that? Why can't she face one table, put the soup down and turn around face the other table and put the soup down? I just don't freaking get it..Anyhow luckily the bf grabbed the bowl from her before she completely let go because she placed it on his silverware. The soup was about to topple over. 

So beside the fact that she didn't think correctly why is our soup 25 mintues later? So as we sat the two other tables have already received their entrees..Um wth? We were here first. This is a total about maybe 35-40 mintues later, the waitress comes by and stated that the Chef didn't like how my salmon was cooked so he had to recook it. WTH? 

I was thinking off the bat "Alright if he's actually doing that I better get a salmon that is not overcooked, because I'm going to throw some elbows". Okay not literally, but you know what I mean..

Anyhow of course when I received the fish it was super over cooked. I thought it was me just upset since we waited an hour for our food. The bf tasted it and we cut the fish apart to see how it was cooked, it was SUPER OVERCOOKED! How can you do that after making me wait for 1 hour? 

I super upset, the waitress didn't offer to help me out too much, I just told her that this wait is unacceptable and she just said ok. She didn't apologize. Another person came along, I'm not sure who she is but I saw her servering other table but she apologized and asked if I wanted another dish, she even offered me dessert. They took the fish out of the bill. I did not eat it after my one bite, I was super upset about the service. 

So Never AGAIN! How do they even get four stars?

Idk I mean Zahav is just THAT good. I've tried to get reservations here sooooo many times for my family and I with no luck on Open Table or by calling 60 days to the date I'd like to reserve. My mom and I came up with a plan to get a seat on a Sunday night during the Eagles game, which turned out to be THE MOST GENIUS hack ever (maybe I should keep this to myself?!). We wait for a Sunday when the Eagles are playing during the time Zahav opens on Sunday, bc duh this is Philadelphia, stores, bars and restaurants with no TV's are ghost towns when the game is on. Not being sports fans, missing the game was no skin off our backs!

Anyway we arrive at 4:40 to wait outside the door, they let us in at 4:55 and seat us immediately at the bar. WAT. Is this a dream? The bartender is super friendly, welcomes us in immediately explains the menu, gets us some drinks and off we go. We did the popular tasting menu of the Israeli salads, 2 app courses, a charcoal grill course and a dessert. It was a great amount of food for us and a cool way to try so many menu items. 

The highlights were the Lemonana drink-- basically an iced tea lemonade with bourbon, delicious! the haloumi OMFG the haloumi-- it was served with nuts and jam the textures and sweet and salty combined to perfection, the branzino was incredible, hummus-- duh this was good, the brussel sprouts were insane, sorbet was incredible (I've never said that about sorbet) but the highlight of all of this was honestly the Israeli salads and the Laffa bread (made by Solomonov himself I've heard). The Israeli salads mainly consisted of pickled veggies in all kinds of cool sauces and spice blends, there were beets mixed with tahini, spicy green beans, eggplant of some sort, pickled fennel and a few others I can't recall. The bread was soooo well seasoned, I could exist on it. 

A slightly less positive side note: Everything is quite salty. I did not find nearly anything to be over salted aside from one dish, but a warning for anyone with a sensitivity/aversion to super salty foods. I was reaching for water for a few hours after this meal. Despite the salt Zahav is worth the wait/time/pain/effort of getting a reservation and even more of a delight if you sneak in like we did for a seat at the bar. It lives up to its reputation.

As with most here. Got in early for a flight and decided not to have fast food or Chickie and Pete's. So this is kinda your only other actual food option. 

I saw some mixed reviews so I am happy to report that I was one of the ones that lucked out. I ordered the miso soup and chicken pad Thai. The soup was a little too hot and the flavor was juuuuust a tad off, but the pad Thai was really good. Nice spice and good flavor. 

Overall, actually one of the better places I've been to in an airport so I would probably go back again and try something else or the same pad Thai
Food is good and service is extremely helpful. Only improvement would be controlling the lunch time lines.

Good food, not as much wait time as other hot chicken spots.  The hot chicken isn't the best in town, but it's more than serviceable.  The Deconstructed Cobb Salad is excellent, and will be my go-to meal when they open their Donelson location.

Recently, I posted about Fuel's healthy options - available on 12th and Chestnut. They've actually got several other outposts, including one at 16th and JFK Blvd - Fuel To Go. This location offers a quick option for lunch - they have a bevy of fresh options available for pick up.

There's some seating as well within the establishment - about 10-15 seats in total.

Recently, they've been offering a great $10 special which includes a wrap and a smoothie. So after work, I picked up two of these for the GF and I. 

Fuel Stacker ($8.95)
Portabello, eggplant, zucchini, squash, tomato, house made mozzarella, and pesto 

The meaty portabella and eggplant helped to make this a substantial wrap. The zucchini and squash adds a light, vegetal element. The house made mozzarella adds some creaminess to the wrap, while the pesto helps to tie everything together.

Eggplant & Goat Cheese ($8.95)
Roasted eggplant, goat cheese, pesto, roasted peppers, and arugula

The eggplant and goat cheese was hearty as well, with the tangy cheese brightening up the dish. The peppery arugula added some bite, while the roasted peppers added a subtle sweetness to the wrap.

Fruit Fusion 
Strawberry, raspberry, banana

The fruit fusion smoothie was really sweet - the berries helped to make it tart, while the banana brought some ripe creaminess to the drink. Still, a bit too sweet for my taste.

Pineapple Power Lunch
Pineapple, strawberry, banana

This pineapple smoothie was slightly less sweet, but still brought up the ripe flavors of its respective ingredients as well.

Overall, Fuel to Go offers a quick, easy, and healthy option for lunch. The smoothie bar is a nice option for those who want something sweet as well.

I don't typically express my opinion on food because I'm not an expert, but the pork belly slider made me see God. If their wifi worked, they woulda got 5 stars easy.  I got my eye on you next, coconut basil donut.
Amazing homemade corn tortillas. Went with reviews and got the corn, it was out of control!! Shrimp tacos were fabulous! Loved the salsa as well.  Warm chips great service.

As you wonder around Busch stadium neighborhood and want a cool place to grab a cold drink or good creole, you must go to broadway Oyster Bar. 
I highly recommended the voodoo chicken wings, "Aunt-Hallie's Crawfish Étouffée" and "Chicken Tchoupitoulas"
I'm not an oyster person, but I hear they're great. Lol. 
They have about a dozen craft beers on tap and a tall, cold, "Abita - Purple Haze" is an excellent craft beer that is made in Louisiana. Very light, easy drinking wheat/fruit beer with a hint of raspberry. 
The decor inside is truly that feeling of the French quarter in New Orleans. Dark, and comfortable on the inside with some big tables and a very cool bar. Every bar in nawlins has a patio and so do they. The courtyard has its own bar, wrought iron fence that is covered with vegetation for privacy, and a large stage for live music. It's hard to imagine the downtown buildings are nearby when you're kicked back on the patio, you just feel secluded. Good for groups and a must for a pre cardinals game warmup.

Tried the shrimp schiarcha appetizer. They were Excellent! Would recommend adding a salad or fries to make it a meal. Hoping this become a permanent item on menu. Service was slow but in their defense seemed like a lot of large parties and not enough waiters.

When I worked in on Olive Blvd. in Creve Coeur, my co-workers and I would frequently Kim Cheese for lunch. It was one of our go-to regular lunch places. I just wished we had discovered it sooner! Kim Cheese had been open for over a year before we finally decided to try it. I would drive by it all the time and wonder if this place had any potential. The restaurant's exterior is not at all representative of the amazingness that is inside this place! The restaurant is in an old fast food place (Taco Bell maybe?) that has since moved. And "Kim Cheese" is displayed prominently on the front the building in giant yellow almost Comic-Sans style font. Kim Cheese also has a drive-through, although I've never used it.

What made me finally decide to try out Kim Cheese was the amazing review written about it in The Riverfront Times. I usually order the Kim Cheese burger or the Spicy Pork Burger....but you really can't go wrong with ANYTHING you order off their menu. It's all delicious and mouthwatering. Kim Cheese describes their restaurant as "fast food, ethic style" and it's a mix of American, Korean, and Mexican. Very interesting and unique! 

The staff at Kim Cheese is so friendly too! Sometimes they get understaffed because this place is so popular, it'll get busier than what their kitchen size allows. On one occasion when we had to wait slightly longer for our food to get made (we didn't even complain), the owner apologized and brought us a giant chocolate chip cookie to share with our table! I was very impressed by their service and you can tell they really care about the customers experience at Kim Cheese.

I'd highly recommend Kim Cheese and I'll definitely be back to visit this place whenever I'm in the area.

Ahhhhhhh Domino's, Its 1245 Sunday morning, football is about to kickoff for the day, what do I always want? Papa Bless? heck no I need some freshly tossed dough pizza from Domino's. Now ill admit I am a huge Domino's fan as a franchise and this store is close to a model store. They freshly remodeled the interior of the store and besides the cash register being annoyingly as far away from the door as possible it looks great. The 5.99 deal or 7.99 large pizza deals are my bread and butter (literally). I would give this Domino's 5 stars but my favorite part of my pizza is the garlic herbs that are usually put on the crust, and unfortunately a few too many times they have completely forgotten to put it on. However that is just the smallest complaint and will continue to come here often!

Updating my review because of an experience I had yesterday. It had just snowed, hailed, and rained for two days straight. The Manayunk streets were disgusting and most Main Street businesses were closed. I was wandering around in search of lunch because I was early for my train and wanted to curl up somewhere warm. Lo and behold, Derek's was open. I ordered my Rhuby Slipper and the mussels and chatted with the bartender, Caitlin, about the weather. My drink was excellent as usual and the mussels in white broth were even better than the first time. At one point, Derek himself was walking around the restaurant. I thanked him for being open and he laughed and thanked me for coming. Another employee told me he has closed twice in 23 years. It is that kind of commitment to serving the community that makes me really like this venue. I will continue to come here because of the good vibes and great cocktails.
Great food. Knowledgeable staff. Never disappointed. Kind of tucked away in a hidden shopping center on the outskirts of town but worth going to.

I hate to admit how much I enjoy McDonald's every now and then. I saw a commercial for the new "artisan" grilled chicken bacon sandwich and went to go get it today. The cashiers were laughing and looking at me like there was some inside joke I wasn't in on... Then I opened my bag and glaring me right in the face was a long black hair sitting right on top of my fries. It was OBVIOUS. Their laughing and looking at me with the smiles that weren't friendly smiles make sense when I saw the obviously placed hair. Trashy and immature. 12 noon Monday 4/38/15

Much improved since my college days. Many healthy menu options engaging staff (thanks Juan!). Tried, recommend, & loved: turkey sausage patty, Frittata Rustica, BLT Benedict, Kale Tonic! Can't wait until we can visit again!
We love this place!!!! Food and staff are amazing  this place is in the forest down a long road which was used by the stagecoach back in the day. It a must go for so many reason. It stunning there

Surprised the reviews on yelp are not better. It's such a reliable spot in the hotel that opens 24 hours a day. The menu is very expansive and the food is pretty good. It's not the best food you'll come across in Reno or even in the hotel, but they have so many options to choose from and they also serve alcoholic drinks all night long. 
Highly recommend the chicken fried steak with over easy eggs and rye toast. Had this two times while I was here. Also recommend the Rueben sandwich with a side of coleslaw and or potato salad. Also good is the spicy Bloody Mary. The service can be a bit slow, but generally would recommend to come here after a night of drinking, or for brunch.

I love this place! I usually come for their lunch special and always leave satisfied. The service is great and their fish is always very fresh. Oh and their kimchi fries are so good!! My go-to sushi spot!
Love the atmosphere and food, can't wait to come back! Great addition to Trolley Square!

I must have gone to Sawatdee on an off day. i'll have to give it another go, but my first meal here was not the best. Pad thai noodles were... linguine noodles.  Maybe they ran out?  My salad was salty and overly-seasoned...I took a few bites and then called it a day.

Left the restaurant feeling hungry for thai food.

I really enjoyed the dark tenders and the multiple sauces. The fresh cut fries were great as well. My husband did not like the wings. The breading seemed to be a thick double dipped type and was the same on both. It worked well on the tenders but not on the wings. They may want to revise their recipe and stick to a classic fried chicken recipe that is much thinner. If you don't enjoy dipping chicken in the sauces, I can see how it would be bland. Some people just don't like any sauce on wings. If you are like me, where you love all types of homemade sauces and flavored mayos, this place is for you.

Having recently moved to the Nashville area, I had a plumbing issue with my water heater. I called Jack Ward plumbing twice, based on yelp reviews.  Both times they were able to squeeze me in at the last minute and accommodate my schedule. The second time, required a complete replacement of a water heater on a Saturday and Jamey responded to my house and busted his rear get in the water heater replaced and up and running. Would use them again and highly recommend.

Enough has been said about this place...there is no other like it in the world!  The Famous Ferdi Po-Boy lives up to the hype & breakfast was homemade and delicious.  The ham truly melts away...I know that sounds strange, but it does.

This place is great! When we came in they told us it was all vegan and mostly raw/non-processed. That's just what we've been looking for so we had a couple of wraps (the one wrapped in collard green is really small) . Overall, really good though. We'll definitely be back. I wish they were open Saturday afternoons. Evidently that's when they do vegan cooking classes.
This place has cheesesteak in their name so you think they'd good but they were pretty awful.  Bread was too soft, the steak didn't really taste like anything, and I could barely taste any cheese.

Very good based on a brunch visit. Disclaimer: they do NOT have bottomless brunch. Drinks are on the pricey side and this is more of a bougie brunch option. That being said, portions are pretty large for a gourmet experience and the interior itself is very nice. Waitstaff are very friendly and efficient. Stopped by here recently with a party of 8 hungry gals and everyone was happy with the experience. I had two cocktails and the smoked salmon pizza ($17). Wouldn't order the pizza again because it was mostly bagel dough. Get a salad or the meatballs instead. Had a really nice time though! Nice place for a fancy date.

Awesome (slightly divey) BBQ spot! Glad we stopped here. Great food great service. Try the Carolina Gold BBQ mustard based sauce if you've never had it. Good stuff.

My daughters (5 and 6) had corn dogs with a mac n' cheese side. I had the brisket dinner. My son (13) had the Pork sausages dinner and my wife and dad both had the Thursday special, which was a pulled pork sandwich topped with smoked sausage and bacon. Yay meat.

Food was ok at best.  Part of the reason was our waiter(AJ).  He was not very helpful as we were trying to figure out the best choice for us vegans.   Also - he never brought any chips and salsa out after we ordered it.  We wanted more tortillas and could never find him.  He was just not very good.  Disappointed in general.

Absolute rudest employees ever!! Would love to try this place, but considering I've now called THREE times trying to place an order and they pick-up the phone only to not speak and hold it off the hook. The first time, I heard them screaming and cussing and what was it they called me again...a dumb a** hoe...all while still refusing to say "hello" or take my order. The other two times, they just flat out ignored me. I am disgusted. Get your employees in line and on board because this is the very first time I've ever felt the need to write a negative review on Yelp.

The lounge is in the lobby of Marriott, near the entrance to the restaurant   Not a bad place  to wait for your event to start in one of the ballrooms upstairs as it is a great place to people watch. The lounge has an airy feeling to it.  And there are plenty of TVs if there is no one to watch.  Prices were what you would expect for a Saturday evening.  Table toppers mentioned Happy Hour specials during week.

Stopped in for lunch and got a Torta Milanesa. It was a good sandwich, but not standout. The bread was fresh and soft, the avocados ripe, but on the whole it lacked some spark. 

No tap water available, so you have to buy bottled water or a bottle of soda if you want anything to drink with your meal. 

Ambiance and decor were a little dark and cold.

Incredible dogs!!!

Note the Winter Hours: M-Sat 10:30a-3pm

Awesome food.
AWFUL parking.

Warning!!
Watch out for the "premier parking scam located directly to the left of this place. No signs or meter anywhere. You'll walk out to a $50 ticket.
I legit thought this was jack Browns parking lot.

Food was good. Service not so much. Was there for 4 birthdays same as last year and multiple past years. That's how we got our discounts for this year. They wouldn't accept all 3 bday discounts only would take 1 because we came all together (again).  So our entire bill was over $500 and they wouldn't accept the other 2 birthday  discounts a total of $30.  We have been repeat customers over the years with parties of 9 plus people. Not anymore. Mrs An made it very clear that $30 was way more important than our repeat business. Im very sad to say that we won't be returning.  No more happy hours, football games or special occasions which we paid full price.  I hope that $30 was worth the repeat business that you lost from 9 loyal customers   By the way this also should have been made clear to us prior to not AFTER we had our meals and received the bill. Ohhhh and the tip was added in....not that it was the servers fault but if there was a concern it should have been brought to our attn prior to our meals.  We provided our discount cards prior to ordering and was told it was fine.  Very disappointed

Great quesadillas...enough to share! 
Lots if grear choices...Thai peanut and Texas are my favs so far!

It wasn't the most authentic Mexican I've had, and it was more like a fast food place than I had anticipated, but the food was good. The atmosphere was kind of basic, so definitely not a date place. I was disappointed they didn't have rice so I'd have beans and rice. For a place like this, I was pleasantly surprised they had tamales. And better yet, they had a choice of chicken or pork. Some of the chips were a little greasy, but not all. They were borderline too salty, but still tasty. The salsa wasn't really your typical red colored tomato-based salsa, but it had a good flavor and I enjoyed it. I didn't love that the chips and salsa cost extra, but I understand it can't be complimentary at every restaurant. I could see myself frequenting this place if I were a local.

On my recent trip to Philly, I put together a personal cheesesteak challenge to find my favorite cheesesteak in Philadelphia. The three contenders were what I think are the most famous cheesesteak restaurants in Philadelphia, Pat's, Geno's, and Jim's.
