I will start off by saying that I enjoyed the sandwiches at all three spots, very much. I ordered the cheesesteak the exact same way at each restaurant so it would be a fair comparison, with Wiz and no onion.  
I will rate the cheesesteaks on their own, on each restaurants individual Yelp page.

In my personal opinion, here is how they finished.

1. Geno's
2. Jim's
3. Pat's

Why did Geno's finish first?

With only three ingredients making up these sandwiches, there wasn't a lot to compare. 

The steak on the Geno's sandwich was the only one of the three that was in larger pieces, which I liked better. The steak on the Jim's and Pat's sandwiches were chopped up into finer pieces.  

The Wiz on the sandwich at Geno's was a generous volume and evenly distributed on the sandwich.

The bread at Geno's was comparable to the bread at Pat's, but wasn't as good as the bread at Jim's. I'd say that this was the only ingredient of the three that Geno's didn't have the edge.

Best steak, best Wiz volume, and pretty good bread gives Geno's the crown of my cheesesteak challenge.
I stop by for the first time today! The smoothies are refreshing and tasty. Clean environment with hair nets and gloves. Friendly service!

Had my birthday dinner at the Boathouse and the food was amazing. They do not always accept reservations but we were able to walk in and be seated quickly on a Sunday night since they had seating on their outdoor patio and 6 feet apart indoors. The restaurant is directly on the beach so you can walk on over after dinner. 

We ordered the Steamed Manila Clams as an appetizer, which was well portioned and filled with buttery goodness. I got the Grilled Scottish Salmon which had the most amazing lobster mash potatoes on the side. My partner got the Pan Seared Scallops which came with another amazing side of lobster and crab risotto. Overall, probably some of the best seafood I've ever had. 

Our waitress Danielle was also great. There was another party celebrating a birthday as well and they were crowding the indoor bar without masks, and our waitress proactively moved them to an outside area away from the inside patrons. She then comped our drinks as an apology (totally unnecessary but greatly appreciated) for the minor disturbance. Always great to have staff who go above and beyond for their customers and really create a safe and enjoyable experience.

Definitely look forward to coming back to Boathouse when I'm in the area.

I really enjoy Santuccis pizza and have made it my go-to pizza spot in Fairmount. Their sausage pizza is a favorite! Their chicken fingers are also worth ordering as they are crispy with a nice batter but not overly fried. My only disappointment has been with the french fries. Knowing the fries are fresh cut, I was excited to try them. Every time I've ordered them for takeout or pickup, they've been extremely soggy. Wish they would keep them in the fryer longer!

We tried the quesabirria tacos and the carne asada fries. 

Everything was delicious. 

We went in, ordered, and ate in the car. They have some seating inside if you're into that. 

We will definitely be back.

I can't believe we found this hidden gem! The food was excellent and well seasoned. The staff was super friendly and it felt like we were going to a friend's house to eat. What made it even better is that we came an hour before closing and all the food was fresh! The only bizarre thing is that they don't have menus to hand out; everything is posted at the entrance in front of the service line and the specials are written on the chalkboard wall behind the line. However everything else was excellent. We'll definitely be back

Very disappointed of the service I've gotten today. I ordered a salmon steak and asked for NO CHEESE BUT ADD SPINACH, SHRIMP, and ONIONS. I gotten the complete opposite. They gave me cheese, broccoli, carrots, and added cinnamon on my fries. Do not repeat my order and still get it wrong: my stomach hurt so bad. I'm so disappointed!
I think the food is amazing here!  The paleo bowl is a must!  The service isn't always on point.  But the food is worth it

We came here based on Yelp recommendations and are not sorry we did! My son and I each had brisket sandwiches, the other two had kid meals and killed them. My husband had the brisket platter and was a big fan. We had baked beans, mac and cheese, cornbread, skillet corn, and an app of fries. My non-cornbread eating boys devoured it! And I could eat that mac and cheese everyday. Highly recommend!

We were there Tuesday late afternoon.  We found  on Tuesday there is a special deal- two scoop of ice cream for $3. We jumped in  for the deal.  I loved my choices - chocolate and peanut butter . It was good. The cupcake girl sells adorable mini cupcakes. There are 16 different kind in the display case. The cupcakes were not only beautifully presented as well as no lack of imagination in taste. We got a pack of 4 cakes to take home. My top favorite was the s'more. The marshmallow top was fire torched and released a charred  flavor, the cake was moist and just right amount of sweetness- very delicious.  The bacon mini cupcake  received high praise in my household. I thought the mini cupcake was a very good idea- you got a little bit of sweet but don't need to worry about high cal and ruin your weight control plan. On Monday they have a special deal of 4 pack cake for $4 , and so on.  Why not make Monday a mini cupcake day! The service was good and the ambience was inviting.  This dessert shop definitely worth visit.

Stopped by for some takeout and was a little apprehensive. There was only one patron and it smelled a little funny, but it was the best Tom yum soup I've ever had. This is a great hole-in-the-wall find. Check it out!

I went in for a to go. First the restaurant is drab and no music. I got a Caesar salad and the dressing was not good. I also ordered lasagna and I cannot describe the flavor but I did not like it. I couldn't find the ricotta cheese and way too much mozzarella cheese. I will not be returning. Throwing the to go menus in the trash. Don't waste your money. There are better places around. Wow!

Service is great and food is also good. Love the vibe and ambiance. A bit dark but trendy , intimate and cute. 

Food: The salsa is amazing with the yummy chips, it's the perfect combo to start off the meal. So good we bought a pint of the salsa to go.

I got one of the Asada dishes for dinner. Flavors were great, pretty "saucy" but in a good way. Mom got the Poca Cosa surprise. We should have known better because we're not huge fans of mole, which was one of the chefs choices. Her Asada dish was also creamy but good flavors. She felt the meat was a little chewy. LOVE the beans and rice. Only other minor gripe is the plates are filled with fruit and lettuce which they call salad but does not have dressing in it, soooo.... Having fruit on my dinner plate was a little weird and made it hard to poke around.  All of that to say, you should definitely try it, a great spot to dine in Tucson.

I have been here for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.  Personally, go for breakfast/brunch.  Lunch is good.  Dinner can be skipped.

Breakfast is always tasty and is way more food than anyone needs.  They do offer a lot different options for those with dietary restrictions.  The service is good, and the patio is very nice.  Actually, if you go, only sit on the patio.  I am not a fan of the actual dining area.

The shop is cute and offers lots of fun things to look at if you are waiting for a table.  But the best part of the shop is the baked goodies at the cashier counter.  They make a very large Neiman Marcus cookie that I have to get whenever I am there.  I am usually leaving there absolutely stuffed, but will still get the cookie to eat later.   This will continue to be a go-to breakfast spot for me.

I love this location the staff are always so nice and seem to be in high spirits. The location on Clearwater beach is closer but I'd prefer to go the extra distance to dine at this location. The food is also always amazing as well and comes quick.

Upgraded review!  We got pizza last night and had light on the sauce meat lovers.  It's was very tasty and tons of pizza. The light on the sauce helped it be less soggy.   We really enjoyed the toppings and the way it was cooked.   The pizza overall was very good.  Only thing I would change is having it cut into less pieces next time.  They were a little small for the 20in.

Plenty Food - Good Service

Haven't been here in years so I gave it try though it's not a close place from where I live. I ordered the kung bo Chicken ding and egg rolls. The egg rolls are huge with plenty meat filling and veggies and one egg rolls had more meat ingredients than the other one. Flavor was mediocre.  The main entrée looked much better than the flavor I'm accustomed to for this dish. It really had more ingredients in it than I have ever seen. Flavor wise for this item was good, but not at the top of the best. I liked the wait staff, most of which are Asian and accommodating.

I order food from here twice...They gave us plenty to eat and it looked very good...  The first time the food was ok but the last time the food was bland, tasteless and dry... I don't understand why there was such a difference between my first order and the second... 

I will say that the staff was very friendly...
Food was great! Tried the alligator and duck gumbo based on reviews. It was delicious. I also go the crawfish cheesecake and it was very rich but yummy. I would come back.

I was excited to see this place open up near me. Usually I go for revolution taco or El Rey if I'm feeling tacos, so I wanted to scope this place out. We ordered 3 types of tacos: al pastor, pollo tinga, and pescado from the list of special tacos. All the tacos were stuffed to the brim, just the way I like it. Al pastor was our favorite, the meat was cut thinly not shredded, and the sauce was sweet. The fish tacos were not particularly memorable, but maybe the shrimp and Korean tacos may be more special. Service was great and this place is perfect for a quick bite to eat- we were in and out in under half an hour. Will definitely be back!
Food was fantastic service was outstanding. Only thing that could compete with that is  the ambiance. I mean heck you're right there at the beach!
The slowest Dunkin' Donuts ever! They never get your order right and it takes 15 mins for one cup of coffee every time

One of my favorite Indian lunch buffets in town, right behind India Palace. The lunch buffet has limited choices: usually the only protein is chicken and there will be a couple of vegeterian entrees. However, everything I've had in my more than a couple of dozen visits here had been fantastic. The food is well spiced (although not spicy); the service at lunch has always been courteous and prompt. They keep your water glasses full and ask whether you need naan refills almost right when you run out of them (they bring naans onto your table). 

I have never had a bad experience dealing with the servers or the food at Saffron, and I'm thankful it's so close to work that I can visit on a bi-weekly basis.

We popped in the place on day one for the opening dinner unknowingly, and it was a complete disaster for service. However, the food was extremely tasty regardless of the wait.  I have waited a  couple months to order again to allow the place to settle in and not suck.

I just called to place a to go order and had to call three times to get someone to pick the phone up.  It was a treat for my lady as she was to pick the order up on her way home from work, and I had intended to pay for it over the phone. However, the girl that took my order informed me that they cannot process cards over the phone which I think is a complete joke. I'll wait another couple months I guess.

I will not comment on the food, because I could not enjoy my food. I had to eat it so fast, I could not chew or taste it. Here is why: We had tickets for a performance at Mahaffey on a Sunday night, went to Frescos for dinner an hour and a half before the show started. The first problem/impression was that the hostess walked by us twice before she greeted us and sat us at a table. The second problem was that our waitress seemed busy, so we did not see much of her. An hour after we were sat down and put in our orders, I asked her (Allie-?) what is going on, and she said the kitchen is backed up. Really? you couldn't tell me that 30-45-60 minutes ago? Needless to say a manager did not check on us at all. We finally got our food 25 mins before the show and had to eat as fast as we could, so that we can rush and make the 10 minute run to the theater. We finally made it to the theater on time, sweating and out of breath. That was not the way I wanted to spend my Sunday night.

All of a sudden these coal-fired and stone-oven pizza places are hitting the Indy area and I've tried all that I know of. The locally-owned CRUST gets everything right including its location in a Carmel spot that could become the town's version  Mass Ave. 

Chicago-style pizza chains are grabbing the headlines, however. But what was 1995's Pizzeria Uno is 2015s Giordano's. They're too top-heavy to endure. God-forbid profits dip by 3% for one quarter and they high-tail it out of Indy until the next fad slices in.

Crust got the crust right! Which is to say "the pointy end" doesn't droop like a tossed banana peel as Blaze does. But hey, I'm a guy who will finish his son's Subway flatizza crust if he leaves it for longer than the agreed-upon 90 seconds.

The staff was shiny and pleasant and they serve Coke instead of Pepsi THANK GAWD.
Best margs in town. Been up and down the menu and it's all good. Fun to sit at the bar and hang out!

Good measures taken for COVID, outside dining only at the moment. Service was really good. 
Food was mediocre, I found the pork knuckles too fatty but the shrimp and wings were delicious!
What an amazing burger with the best bacon around. good customer service. some the best tater tot's in the valley I highly recommend this place to anyone. I eat there about once a week.

great pizza, great beer; snotty, entitled bar-staff!!! Stay away from thi joint if you don't want to be insulted or to actually get you food or drink in a timely fashion. Cat/Kat is the worst; insulting and beligerant, you can gat a pizza or drink with more of a positive attitude from  tons of places on Magazine or St Charles. Total trash; food was good; drinks cold but don't expect friendly service with cat/Kat!

Yum!!! This place is the real deal serving fresh fish which reminds me of being back in San Diego. Yes, the prices are higher than fast food, but remember this is fresh high-quality fish. You would pay much more for a couple sushi rolls. The sauces are great! I created my own bowl with the traditional poke, white rice, house piranha sauce, and all the toppings available. It was mouth watering good. Excited that Boise has a poke place now and it meets and exceeds my expectations of goodness. One suggestion I have would be to keep the pickled ginger on the side. The taste is quite overwhelming if you get a big chuck of it in one bite ;). 

Can't wait to come back! Good Job!!

Crab beignets for the win! These delicious crabby and fluffy tummies were the best thing we ate during our trip to NOLA! I could make a meal out of a few orders of these babies! 

Entrees were expertly prepared and plated. I had the seafood stew - subtle, light and perfect for a light supper. My boo had the turtle ragu which tasted good but we couldn't tell it was turtle! Neither of us have had much turtle in the past but we were slightly disappointed in not finding a more distinct flavor from the protein. For dessert, we shared homemade ice cream - consistency and texture was spot on and the rounded out our meal very nicely! 

But seriously, those crab beignets! Worth coming back just for those!

Service sets the bar in Franklin and Brentwood. Pete and Ichikawa upstairs have great table-side energy and knowledge from food to wine.

Good tonight:

Buffalo Cauliflower (great starter)   

Grilled Caesar is fantastic

Beef Medallions spot on

The food is very good and the service makes you want to come back....

The staff here is super friendly and accommodating; a nice, neighborhood store that a lot more people than 'just in the neighborhood' visit. So ,they have a great following, while also remaining a neighborhood staple. I really like that.  

Nice selection of middle eastern groceries, dry and canned goods, frozen selections, as well as butcher counter and fresh foods. A great market for middle eastern goods and sundries. They even have cooking utensils, cosmetics, soaps, etc. It's like a mercantile - a little bit of everything. I love it; very nostalgic for me because I grew up in the middle east as an ex-pat. 

I often order from the restaurant for take out. They have a large menu selection and the food is always fresh, well cooked, generous portions, packaged well, orders are correct and prices are fair. I've never had a bad meal there. 

I use them for catering often. Sometimes I find the prices a bit high for catering/if I'm picking up. I could see the higher expense if they deliver and set up, but not if I'm picking up. I once told them the price quoted was out of my budget and they worked with me, which I appreciated. 
The food was as good as always. Super fresh and elegantly presented. They also work with your timeline to ensure the food is fresh cooked and hot. Which is great! 

But the next time I called, the price for a platter of rice was almost double. I chose to skip the rice due to the price. They don't seem to have set prices for catering/catering prices aren't published online. You call to get a quote, which I understand. I just found that price too high for a platter of rice, which a lot of places throw in free when you order 3 meat/entree items for 20 people. They also don't provide gratis condiments/bread, sauces, etc. Just FYI. 

They also charge $35 delivery fee for catering. I'm less than .30 miles away, so that seemed excessive. I can totally understand that charge within over a certain mile radius. No problem. But, I'm literally .30 miles and had an event planned with multiple scheduled time constraints and food that needed to arrive by 6 p.m. and i'm less than 1/2 a mile ... so, I had one of my guests go pick it up. It worked out just fine. 

I love the Tabouleh, Shish Tawouk, and the Beef Kofta Kabobs. Their hummus is very tasty, and I like the thinner version of pita bread they serve. I prefer Greek Tzatziki but, for such a small place, they do pack a punch! 

My only negative eating experience was with Falafel - it was very dry and hard, not too tasty and seemed not too fresh that day. But, any restaurant can have a bad day. 

It's a great grocery/sundry market for international items that are tough to find elsewhere, and a great place for some savory, well cooked, flavorful take out for lunch or a Friday night with Netflix. I really do love this place. So glad I can walk there and get whatever I want! 

Pros: Location, convenience, selection, friendliness, variety, global, ethnic, fresh, tasty, decent prices. 

Cons: A bit high priced for certain catering menu items and delivery fees/no published catering prices or options. But they work with you.

We stumbled into this place after seeing the line for the restaurant we really wanted to go to.

This is a semi upscale restaurant.  The food is just okay but the prices are high.  There are better options.

I will say they have an impressive selection of bourbon if you are into that.  The service is also great but not enough to elevate the food.

The salad was good but too much dressing for my blood.. the pizza was fine but soggy, greasy and floppy. I prefer no grease and crispy call me new school.. had loud customers goin wild for the baseball game, not my scene so it's just a bunch racket to me.. will I be back? Perhaps...

I came to visit as a tourist and it didn't disappoint. To be fair, I feel like this is a tourist trap but it definitely met my expectations. 

I ordered a spicy shrimp po boy and loved how perfectly toasted the bread was and how flavorful the shrimp was.
Do not trust the prices quoted on this rip off of a restaurant. Upon calling I was quoted double the price for each item as advertised on their website. These people are pieces of shit

Small place tucked away in an industrial area.  My first time there.  Clean interior with plenty of room to sit.  Got an Italian Beef hoagie.  OK but nothing special.  Not very flavorful and hot peppers not very hot or peppery.
This place has great food! But im only giving this place 3 stars only because they have the worst service. You are better off ordering take out.

After seeing its episode on DD&D, I decided to give this place a try on my way through Hendersonville. Similar to the other reviews, I found the service to be severely lacking which was weird as only myself and one other table were in the establishment. I had the cheese plate as an appetizer as it was one of the featured dishes on the show. To be honest, I hated it. For a ten dollar appetizer, I expect more than three slices of cheese on a bed of lettuce. Plus the cheese was extremely salty. My main course was good, but for a Mediterranean dish it was way under seasoned. Overall, food is good, but overpriced. Service leaves much to be desired.

My husband and I came in on a Monday night and I was thoroughly impressed. First off, I thought the decor was adorable but not overkill. Love the checkered table cloths. Little tealights in the jars on the tables would have just set it off but I can't complain. 
We ordered a BBQ chicken pizza with no onions. It came out with onions and we told the server and she was super apologetic and said she put it in wrong. She was great and redid our order and it only took about 10 minutes for the new pizza to come out. Due to the mistake she brought us out some complimentary garlic bread to ride us over which I appreciated. 
Our corrected pizza was done within 10 minutes and it was delicious! Definitely the kind you need a knife and fork and you can tell the crust is homemade and not frozen. I'm looking forward to coming back!
Come for the beer and stay for the pizza OR come for the pizza and stay for the beer.  Either way, it's a win!

Went on a busy Friday night so there was quite a line. The chicken was pretty good we got two chicken sandwich meals with the heat level hot and fries.The fries were really good and the "comeback sauce" was pretty average. I think it is a spicy ranch. Overall it was nice but make sure to go at a less popular time if you don't want to deal with a wait/large crowds. I felt the hot wasn't terribly spicy so if you like heat I'd go with a higher level.
Waited in drive through lane without moving for 10 min. At Kesey move the line so I can leave if getting fast food takes so long ;)
Not good food. Staff was rude n not good service. Not recommend. I order vegetarian food n server looked at me strangely.  It was from menu n not sure if they actually have it as vegetarian

Yes it's as good as it gets and ALWAYS consistent. A gathering of girl friends were there on a recent weeknight. Walter is the best waiter/bartender around - doesn't need to write down orders, gets em right the first time and makes good suggestions for food and wine!  Their pizzas, especially the shrimp (only place I know in town to get one) is fabulous! Even the gluten free smaller ones are yummy. Pasta is always done to perfection. Love the new layout - works well for bar, small and larger, private parties. Great to support a local restauranteur. Daniel knows how to please at the right price points whether here or at Vivace!  We'll return.

I'm increasing my review to four stars because my last two visits have gone well. Service has improved.  Their salads and boneless wings are really good and priced right. My friend really likes the burgers and he's a bit picky, so try one.  They food specials that are pretty good. I will be back.  Ps: It is always good to see a restaurant improving their building...a new ceiling is being installed in the game room as I type.  Good job!

Always fun to sit at the bar when it's not too busy. They have some pretty decent entries. Good look getting service when it's busy though, they don't know how to mange lots of people. You're no one to them.

Two Words:  Banana Milkshake

I love the vibe that Finch and Fork gives off. Impeccable service and dining exprience.

They executed my Lamb Burger - it was my second time trying one. It had this slight sweetness to it because there was chutney added to it. It complemented the flavor of the lamb and goat cheese. Finch is making me fall in love with lamb, again!

The banana milkshake was the star of the evening. They have graham crackers mixed in the drink and topped it with peaks of meringue. 

This is a fine dining experience, I suggest you all try it!

Tip: Park in the 90 minute parking lot behind Saks on Carillo!

So I decided I wanted lunch but going out was not an option.   Playing the "Oh what eat" game with the refrigerator was not what I was into today either.  I decided to try out a delivery service for food and a new place to eat.  A double whammy.  I am kind of selective about not going into a restaurant to get my food and having it delivered is something I have not done in a looooong time.   I cannot remember the last time I ordered a pizza for delivery.

A few places offered free delivery for first time customers and after spending way too many minutes drooling over the offers, and playing the "Should I or Should I Not" game, I decided on Mimi Blue Meatballs.  I would never probably had ate there because my original thought was, "Oh it's just meatballs and there is a gigantic store up north that has those too."

I am so glad the games stopped long enough for my taste buds to be happy and my stomach sated.  

I love meat.  Forget the veggie stuff.  Give me meat!   And Mimi delivered.  But not just in the meat department.  Oh the sauces!  Geez who would had thought that beside the usual tomato style sauce, sweet savory or swedish sauce you could put some zing on meatballs?   I ordered 3 sliders with brioche bun.  Mushroom gravy, garlic cream and barbecue.  That garlic cream is something special.   I also decided to try the Truffle Creamed Gnocchi and was not disappointed with order at all!   

My order arrived in big enough tray that my 3 sliders were not cramped together and sauce mixing did not happen...yay!  I admit that I am a bit pretentious about my food touching on my plate so this was pleasing to me the way they packed my food.  The containers were nice plastic ones and not cheap Styrofoam.   Everything I was needed for lunch was packed nicely in a brown thick sack stapled so I knew my order had not been tampered with.   I loved the attention to detail they provided with my delivery order.  

I definitely plan to visit the restaurant in person for lunch based on my delivery experience.
Great place to come hang out!  Great food, great atmosphere.  Myr is bomb!  She makes the place!

So good! The hype is real. I ordered mild through Postmates. I'm a wimp when it comes to spice so this level worked great for me.  It arrived hot, fresh, and the fries were crispy and the bun was not soggy. But I live nearby so I'm sure that helped.  The flavor was great and the sauce was really good. Thank you, Crazy D's for not disappointing me!

Met with a friend for dinner this evening. I am not a regular so I was looking forward to trying a different place. The atmosphere was nice and pleasant when we walked in, but when seated at our table along the wall the light above was blinding. Mentioned it to the hostess with no response. When the server arrived and our friend asked a couple of questions about a drink and then an entree, his response both times was that he had never had them. We had the crab soup and cheese steak appetizer and they were very good. Our friend and I decided to go with the black and blue salmon special and my Husband had a burger. No complaints on the burger and was even cooked as ordered to medium well. The black and blue salmon was a different story. First it tasted very Fishy. I order salmon everywhere I go because I love it and this was not even close to good. Instead of coming with blue cheese as described it had what looked like melted chedder and tomatoes only with no taste. I had two bites and couldn't eat the rest. the broccoli and carrots were room temp and quickly became cold. The rice had no taste at all. When the server checked back and we said we didn't care for it and wouldn't order it again he did offer to take it back and in hindsight we should have let him. For some reason I thought I would eat it because I was really hungry, but I just couldn't in the end. We ordered a sandwich to go for our friends Husband at the end and the manager brought it and never asked if we enjoyed our meal or gave any indication that he had been told we didn't care for the salmon. I can remember the days when if someone didn't care for their meal, especially two people with the same meal it was a big deal. It kind of felt like take it or leave it service. My Husband waited and had a drink at the bar after dinner while I ran an errand and when I picked him up he mentioned that while he was sitting there a group at the bar was dropping F-bombs constantly. Again, I remember a time when that language wasn't tolerated in nicer places. I don't really like writing bad reviews as I feel not enough people get praise, but this had to be written.

Decent little restaurant in the outlet mall area east of the Galleria (which houses Crate & Barrel and PF Changs). The food is all decent for the price, and they didn't skimp on the avocado on their brunch. 

Nothing about the food sticks out, though if you're looking for a light brunch or lunch and you're in the area, this place should be on your radar. They have wraps, sandwiches, and scrambles that are great for anyone arriving early-ish to the mall before making the dreaded trek over (which have been every instance I've been there). The interior is surprisingly roomy and they have some outdoor seating. The coffee is also pretty good, and they have a few generic varieties that you can get to-go. Basically, Nadoz is a way to make your shopping visits start a little nicer than they otherwise might.

Right off the bat, I love the look of the Mercer Tavern.  It's old wood and industrial feel really adds character to what is basically a fancy, upscale joint.  
Now down to the nitty-gritty.  The food was pretty good.  Had a rather large burger that was quite tasty, but with a very different and unique bun.  At first I wasn't a fan, but I was so hungry (this was an after work trip on a Wednesday night) I dug into it, and it grew on me. 
We did have a small problem with the service.  We were seated as soon as we got there, but it was at a tiny table crammed in the back.  The whole point of going to this place was to enjoy the old-school look, NOT to sit in a tiny corner, surrounded by drywall.  We asked if we could have another table in the main area and was told that there would be a 45 minute wait, but we could sit at the high chairs along the thin, narrow counter - not cool when you're there as a couple (having to sit next to each other instead of across).  While we were sitting there, waiting for our hostess to find  us a better seat, two great tables opened up but were immediately grabbed by people who just walked in off the street and bypassed the hostess.  If you are going to have a gatekeeper, it's best if they actually do their job.
The next time a table opened, we politely asked if we could move and were told we could - only to have our new server get angry with the old one for not letting her know we already ordered drinks.  Probably best not to do this in front of customers, eh?
And speaking of drinks.  I LOVE(!!!!) a place that has a huge selection of beers on their menu.  I HATE(!!!!) when you order one and it is not in stock...and even worse when your second choice is not in stock.  List 'em AND have 'em; the system only works when you do both.  If not, you have beer anarchy!  Will I go back?  Probably not - I rarely hit downtown and with so many great places on the southside, it takes a lot to get this boy across the river, and the Mercer just doesn't quite have it, despite the great physical atmosphere.
Been here couple of times and everything was amazing! Had a Banh Mhi sandwich and coffee. Very good.

The waiting staff is hit or miss. I have eaten here a few times and sometimes the servers are great and others not so great.. However the food is awesome!!! I always get the fried grouper sandwich and it is to die for!! If you are looking for fresh seafood this is the place to go!!!
Fantastic food and atmosphere. Very friendly staff!
Aesthetically amazing.  Master crafted drinks at the bar.  No better place to start or end a night.  Sadly I have not tried the food but I have heard nothing but goos things.

Food was good and cheap, however I have a big problem when you offer delivery and my office is literally right down the street you can't deliver because the driver gets confused when he goes there. I had to leave work and go and pick up the food and waste my lunch time because they don't know how to use Google Maps or Apple Maps. I'll go back for pickup and I'm not on a time crunch, but seriously they need to figure out their delivery system. Also the woman who answered and helped me at the restaurant was a little rude. Finally make sure you have a backup plan with your ordering, their hours are always changing with no warning.

I walked in to a casual atmosphere and ordered a Rock n Pork Roll. 
Scrumdillyumscious!!

5 stars for food quality and taste ; 2 stars for service:
Really good food but it comes with bad service.You must be patient and ask for what you need bc it won't be brought to you as it should be.Sad bc the breakfast is very good. I have been to this place about 6 times and is always the same.
I needed a quick vegetarian hoagie & I got it. It was made well, quick & tasted great. It lasted me through my coast to coast flight.

UPDATE from after my review below: According to the owner, who left a very kind response to my review, the Trolley Car Cafe is still under the same ownership as when they opened in 2011, and the General Manager has been with the company for several years. His response was extremely professional and thoughtful, and these sort of things matter! Thank you so much, Ken! We'll be back for breakfast.

----

Normally the service is pretty good and the food is always good. Our most recent visit left a lot to be desired. According to some of the more recent reviews, it seems like Trolley is under a new management or new 'team'? Can't confirm this, but maybe that explains a few things. Our second most recent visit hasn't been since late springtime of this year and back then I would have given this place 4 stars.

Firstly, we sat outside because we had our dog with us. They were very accomodating to the dog, as there was an area where you could go get a water bowl and fill it for the dog and they even have a little doggie menu that you can order off of for your pup. We got her the chicken jerky and peanut butter biscuits and she thoroughly enjoyed them.

Our food was good--we ordered the catfish and waffles, meat frittata, and cucumber & melon gazpacho (very refreshing on a humid summer day!) We also ordered iced coffees and fresh squeezed orange juice, and they provided us with water as well.

The service was the main problem. The waitors/waitresses were nice enough, but they forgot to bring our drinks out and were serving others who got there well after us while we sat and waited. They admitted they forgot, and we said it was no problem because really, it wasn't a problem at the time. And then they never brought out the orange juice when they did bring out our drinks, so I had to ask for that again the next time they came over. And then one girl went from table to table to tell everyone their credit card machine was out and they could only accept cash, which definitely put some customers in a tough spot since they didn't have cash on them (luckily I happened to have just enough.) And then they served, not one, not two, but three tables that came anywhere from 15 minutes to an hour later than us. We waited almost 2 hours for our food (we arrived at 9:40something-AM and did not get our food until after 11AM.) There was no apology for the wait either and no acknowledgement. Then before we were about to pay and leave, we asked if the credit card machines were working yet, and the waitress told us yes, they were. We did think it was a bit thoughtless to not go around telling the tables that the machine was working since they went around telling everyone that they weren't woking in the first place. So my partner pays for breakfast inside and then we had to leave tip, so I went inside and asked a lady at the register to break a bill for me. She asked, with an attitude, if I was buying something and I said no, this is for the tip, and I thanked her twice and she didn't even look at me or respond to me, just handed me my bills and walked away. Okay...

So all in all, some things to be desired. We like it there and we will be back as it's conveniently located near us and the food is good, but we're going to wait a while and hope that things get a little better and the staff gets better mentoring/training before then.

Let's keep this quick and funky: this ain't traditional Asian food. It's fusion from all parts of Asia. Eight hat being said, do not get the pad Thai. It is watered down and just not good relative to all the pad Thai I have ever had. This one definitely stands out as the worst. The good thing is that the Mongolian beef was on point and the quality of the meet was on yum yum level. Come and check out this spot.

Was walking thru the FQ with a friend waiting to go to lunch at ACME when my friend says "lets stop in there for something to drink, it looks nice in there - and air conditioned." The staff that greeted us were really friendly and escorted us to the bar. The place is beautiful in a really classy way, but for some weird reason, we didn't feel underdressed because the staff were so nice. We sat on these nice barstools and the bartender (who I was wanting to hug when we left) offered us a menu along with making some recommendations for drinks. We decide to just have sweet tea. I watched the bartender make the tea right in front of us, fresh brew poured over ice with syrup/sugar...nice!

We notice their cookbooks and ask if we can look thru one. The front cover has the most gorgeous photo of BBQ shrimp and when we look around, it seems everyone is eating it. We didn't know that was the thing to order, but we knew that we had to get on board. We ordered a  plate to share. While we waited, the bartender made sure that our tea glasses were full, then starts telling us the history of the sazerac (because we were looking at the sazerac page in the book) and shows us a bottle of absinthe and a bottle of herbsaint...it was a cool lesson.

The shrimp arrives and the smell is spicy, buttery, ocean-y....then I smell fresh bread. WOW! This was by far the best BBQ shrimp I have ever eaten. It was amazingly good. I know that it was indulgent, but it was so good I just couldn't feel guilty. When we used up our bread sopping up the sauce - the bartender then brings us a brand new fresh loaf - hot out of the oven. We were in heaven!

When we were done, we decided that we were going to have to come back with our group because it would be rude to keep this amazing place secret from anyone. We then went to ACME to meet our friends (couldn't eat much) and they had no idea why we had silly grins on our face. I decided I wasn't going to say anything, and just take them next year...have them be surprised like we were.

Add this place to your bucket list people!......and get the shrimp!

This place is just minutes from my apartment and I couldn't be happier.   Love it!   I've only been on a Saturday or Sunday morning (I actually went yesterday, Monday July 4th, but that might as well count as the weekend) and it's always bustling.  It's a little on the small side, so it gets a bit crowded during the busy hours, which I would imagine are anywhere from opening until after the lunch hour.  The crepes are very large and delicious.  I always get the nutella and fruit one and am never let down.  It's absolutely wonderful!  On my next visit I plan on trying something new, but I can't make any promises...nutella and fruit are hard to beat!

Me and my friends reallllyyyyyy enjoyed the food,  it was finger  licking good literally lol. There were no complaints.  Portions are good, prices are reasonable.  It's BYOB for now,  they have a set up for a bar area, soon to come.  What more can I say,  just check crafty crab  out you'll like it.

This hotel is one of the best I have ever stayed at.
The hotel its self was very nice. Plus the staff was great. 
The boyfriend was spending the semester in Biloxi (designing and rebuilding post Katrina) so we met in NOLA and stayed here for the weekend. Everything was perfect from the service we got, our room, the food, etc. 

One of the best things about the hotel is the PBJ and hot chocolate bar they have at night. It was a great way to end the day. It was not really a social gathering as much as a fun way to end the day.

It was hard to look out our window and see the dome and know what happened 2 years before but the it is great knowing how the city has rebuilt itself. 

I know that the next time I am in NOLA (and I will go back!) I will stay here.
Great service,  excellent guacamole!  Very casual laid back atmosphere.   Live music and pretty good food.

Stopped here without reading reviews and I've got to say this spot is worth stopping for. The service was always done with a smile. Mike J. Was our server and he was very approachable,  so attentive and helpful. For the food I would say try the coffee it is very flavorful and bold a coffee you can do without the creamer. The food was cooked to perfection. I had the crab cake Benedict's.  They were a perfect blend of flavours all working together without overpowering any of the ingredients.  The bacon was delicious to the point my husband almost asked for bacon only plate. Haha. The potatoes were okay nothing to rave about. I will definitely come back for the crab cake Benedict's.  Enjoy!
They have good food for a reasonable price and they give HUGE portions. Get the Grilled Chicken Plate all the way! Mmm.
Best fried chicken I've had in a while and that mac and cheese doe

5 stars??? Yes!  So much fun!  I'm a kid at heart so this is my kind of place.  The service was awesome and everyone made sure we had a great time! Thank you!    Food and drinks were so good!  This will be our go to place for Birthdays going forward.. Highly recommend for a group of people or family outing. So yes 5 stars!

Waiter messed up order
Ordered chickpea burger, got chicken burger. I'm vegan... 
Also overheard he messed adjacent table's order
#S**tforEars waiter

Bring a pad n paper make waiter sign ur order...in waiter blood
Ps
Messed up bill too

Food not that great...

What could you not like about this place?!?! The atmosphere is amazing and the service is superb. Not to mention that the food might as well have fallen from the heavens. Seriously, despite it being labeled as a "vegetable restaurant," this place would amaze even the most uppity foodie. I often pop in for happy hour, as the drink specials and food selection are great and the prices are very affordable. However, when I'm really looking to indulge, I come in for dinner. My partner, who isn't vegan, loves this place as well. We have never had anything here that wasn't absolutely to die for. Oh, and for dessert, GET THE STICKY TOFFEE PUDDING!!! Hands-down, this is not only the best vegan restaurant I have ever been to anywhere, but it's also one of the best restaurants in general -- vegan or not!
One of the best burgers I've eaten in a while. Friendly staff, great service, and awesome portions for the money!

My coworker and I discovered this unassuming spot straight through Yelp during a short business trip. My Gaucho Chimichurri sandwich was outrageously good -- tender rib eye steak slices, grilled onions, some sort of cheesy goo and of course the green garlicky chimichurri sauce. My coworker also praised the Brat. The local lager beer was a perfect complement to a reasonably priced lunch. Will definitely visit again.

The food here is decent, and of all the touristy cheese steak places, this is the best I have had. The rolls are fresh, the meat has a good balance of tender/stringiness, and the steaks have a good cheese-to-meat ratio.  The prices are a little high, but that comes with the location.

One of the few places I frequent regularly. Great food- local, organic, you know the drill. Highlights: trout, potato salad, Cuba sandwich and savory bread pudding (Gorgonzola, rosemary & bacon!) which has a cult following in the city.  Best beer, wine & liquor selection in the city, first date upstairs by the lamps = good.

OK, OK.  5 stars for an airport restaurant is a bit much, but given the setting, this place is perfect.  Wonderfully nice and accommodating staff, and good food.  You can order three "sides" here for 12 bucks, including fresh steamed vegetables, roasted potatoes, sauteed spinach and other choices make a large tasty meal.  Cheeseburger is fantastic.  Fried Green Tomatoes were very good.

Really bad service to get gas!  Waiting and waiting while others coming way after getting fueled up.

Step it up!!!

I'm a New Orleans local and I don't believe in good Cajun cooking outside of the home but this place proves me wrong every time. Server Chris definitely made the experience worth it. Will continue to visit!!

Kids vote yes!!  You can order your pizza up to 20 minutes in advance - which I recommend if you're dining with kids.  Glass windows let the kids see the bakers toss pizza dough! The sauce on the pizza is incredible. Staff members are awesome.  I can't wait to go back.

that the place was cold (no heat) and empty should have been a warning sign: don't eat here.
very expensive, almost no food served, very unsatisfying
the mint tea is watered down
the portions are almost non-existant
no plates, no opportunity to wash hands but you gave to eat with your fingers
terrible place, avoid!

In my short 37 years I have never had a breakfast this amazingly good!!! I had country fried steak & gravy, hash browns, over easy eggs, and white toast. My boyfriend had corn beef hash, hash browns, and over easy eggs with Texas toast. We walked in sat, greeted immediately served our large orange juices. Placed order. We got our food within 7 minutes of ordering. It was hot, perfect and delicious. The hash browns could be eating with nothing added not to crunchy or to soft. Flavor AMAZING!!!! The steak and gravy hit the flavor spot I was looking for!!!! The over easy eggs whites not runny and yellows perfect for dipping. I will bf back again.

SERVICE: Terrible for groups that want any attention at all. Took over 30 minutes to be approached by a waiter after being seated. Staff was rude the entire evening. 

FOOD: Decent appetizers, but main course left much to be desired. Quality ingredients used, but did not come together well. 

Highly discourage anyone who is close to a "foodie" or Italian to visit. Will never personally entertain the thought of going back.
LaPizza is that rare pizza place that excels at both delicious crust and sauce. Highly recommend it.

We waited 25 minutes to be checked in only to be rushed and no explanation of charges and resort fees. She handed me my keys and told me to take the elevator for our floor but no room number. No free wi   fi and outdated room that smelled like stale water and mold! Casino was dirty and outdated and shirt staffed all over. This place is run down and very poor customer service! No one cares about my complaints. We would never stay there again! Horrible for a Harrah! Even Laughlin Nevada Harrah was better than Reno one.

We first went to Bridgid's about 15 years ago, and back then they had the menu only on the chalkboard/verbal, and it was a seasonal rotation of surprisingly upscale items for such a humble converted row-home.  Add in the amazing Belgian beer selection, and it was a favorite.  We hadn't been recently, so had a nostalgic pull to go back last night, and boy what a surprise.  The menu is now Italian in nature, but the atmosphere and friendly vibe is still the same (as are the funky tables).  The beer selection isn't as expansive, but they have more cocktails and wine to choose from.  I had the "Judson" cocktail - vodka, lime juice, ginger - and it was one of the best darn drinks I've ever had.  Ever.  We started with a pork belly appetizer with crab, goat cheese, pine nuts and plum, and it was divine.  So interesting and for the complexity, a decent size where we didn't feel short-changed after the first wonderful bite.  We then shared the prosciutto wrapped asparagus with mushrooms, and something about the delicate frisee and tangy light vinaigrette balanced the heaviness to make it just delicious.  I had the pasta special - a bucatini with pancetta, fresh peas in a carbonara sauce - and we licked the bowl as the sauce was again balanced, with the perfect amount of garlic and salt.  He had the crispy fried quail, and the maple syrup sauce was a perfect pairing.  My only slight criticism if I reached for one, would be that the sauce was thin, and a tad too sweet for my liking, but we again finished every yummy bite.

All in all - what a nice discovery to find Bridgid's updated menu, but with the same neighborhood charm it's always had.  We'll be back soon.
Strong hurricane drinks. Piano musicians that play customer requests. A unique experience

Best burger place I have ever been to.  Great selection of burgers including several different meat selections.  I had the PB&J Bison burger and it was incredible.  In addition to the burgers they have a wide selection of sides (including homemade fries that are amazing), sodas, homemade ice cream, and beer.  All of their beers are from the microbrews popping up in STL.  I haven't seen a better local beer selection in the city.  The prices are a little high but definitely worth it.

Arrived in NOLA for my 40th and we were staying at the Avenue garden Hotel next door. 5 of us just flew in and were starving! We were supposed to go to Willie Maes for the fried chicken but there was a line wrapped around the building. So we decided to check this place out because it was convenient and it was worth it.

One thing I like was you could get ANY type of pizza they had for a slice! Most places have limited selections when it comes to the per slice. The pizza was pretty freakin awesome! Ny Style like I love it and full of flavor! 

We were so impressed we managed to squeeze this place in a 2nd time. 

The second time we didnt have pizza. Garlic Bread was great. Mushroom Crostini was very good, Caprese Salad was decent.. The pasta was a heaping portion and filling but it was kind of bland. However, the item I was least thrilled with was the bread pudding.. it was definitely cake not bread pudding. The only reason I wasn't impressed is because I was expecting bread pudding.  

For NOLA I expect an overabuncance of flavor so for the pasta portion I was left a bit in the "meh" category but the pizza.. SPOT ON!

nummy nummy jambalaya. and breakfast 24/7! I love breakfast, so any place that serves breakfast all day gets extra props from me. Their jambalaya also comes with a biscuit! I love biscuits just as much as I love breakfast (mostly I love breakfast with biscuits and gravy), so any place that serves biscuits with their entrees also gets props from me.

Sadly they do not split checks, which is mildly irritating. But besides that one minor fault, service wasn't mind-blowing but it wasn't like I had high expectations either, food was hot, filling, good, and fast, they had plenty of hot sauce, real good stuff.

Stopped in for a quick snack slice. It's always tough to judge a pizzeria by their slice pies, but Boardwalk impressed. No screens being used, Baker's Pride ovens and Grande cheese!  Shit was good and hit the spot something proper. I look forward to going back and trying a fresh pie with an ice cold beer.

Used to be good, not the same place anymore. Cut backs on quality and quantity of meat in pho. Bad decisions on staff hires. Atmosphere is too loose and not professional. When the owner isn't there things aren't up to her standards. I don't trust the kitchen anymore.

Our first time here & it's pretty tasty! I ordered the Cod Burger (added cheese too), the kids had the grilled cheese (it looked pretty good) & my hubby had the Texas Style Double(nice n spicy) with an order of onion rings  We will definitely be back! Next trip to try the "Indy's Best Milkshakes"
Excellent. Made reservations ahead of time. Service and food outstanding. Worth the price.

I live right around the corner from this place.  Just incredible ambiance, service and high quality food and drink.  The brunch on Sundays is particularly good.  Solid place for happy hour, or to start at the bar for a drink then move on to dinner.  I've never been disappointed there

Ok.  So I ordered online for delivery. Apparently that comes up as "pickup" on their end.  It was supposed to be delivered at 1 pm. 1:30 rolls around and I call...only to find out that it had been sitting there for 45 mins.  After speaking with the twenty-something employee, they informed me they weren't going to remake it.  After the delivery guy figured out he was at the wrong address,  the amount of gyro meat with my "fork style" (aka salad) meal was laughable.  Oh, and when they called me back, instead of announcing the business, he said...simply..."hey". As if we were long time friends catching up.  Pathetic.  Don't go here. Oh, and they will charge you $3 dollars for delivery, and argue with you whether you actually clicked on the huge "DELIVERY" button on their website.

I've been going to Lamberti's on and off for years now. I'm not sure if management has changed, but the quality has significantly diminished. Recently dined in and noticed for starters the lack of staff and service. The food also left me unimpressed, I ordered a pasta dish with chicken and noticed it had little to no flavor. Lamberti's has potential to do well and be great again, but management really needs to take note of some short comings and take ownership of them. Overall, I will not be coming back to this Restaurant.
The food was ok. We asked for our wings well done and they were not even close. The service was abysmal.  At least the margarita was good. Will not be returning to this terrible version of Hooters.
My favorite is Jersey Mike's Famous #17! I love it served as a wrap!! :)  It's sooo good! when you take a bite from the wrap, you just see a web of cheese that looked like it exploded inside.

This place doesn't get the recognition that it should, it should be packed almost every night. My friends came here after playing tennis. After ordering the sample appetizer dish, I was ready for more food. I got the skirt steak with yuca b/c I LOVEEEEEEE steak and yuca. 

Friend got the beef stew and it smelled delicious!!! I think I want to try that next time!!!

Great service, awesome beer, fun trivia nights! You can't go wrong with Redemption Alewerks! My hubby loves the Indoctinator they have on tap. I go for Amber Waves. Pair that with awesome burgers and you get an affordable awesome meal.

Johnny Brenda's,

It had been too long since our last acquaintance! Just about two years, to be exact.

I don't have any worthy excuses for what took me so long to return to you, and I am deeply sorry. I won't neglect you for so long again. I promise.

In both September 2012 and September 2014, I had the honor of consuming the crispy chicken sandwich and french fries while in your fine building. In both Septembers, I very much enjoyed said meals. I also really liked your selection of local craft beers!

A sincere thank you for two great visits, and I truly hope we can keep in touch.

Your friend,
Kathleen

Located in Mid-City on Carrollton close to Canal, step back in time, watch the streetcar go by and get your dessert on.  Locals already know, so visitors hit this institution up on the way to or from City Park, for some of the best dessert in town year round.  It's been for generations, that's a great sign all on its own.  Unlike most snowball stands, Angelo Brocato's is open all year round so you can get your fix of gelato or spumoni anytime, yeah you right!  This place can get busy and parking can be tricky but don't let that be a deal breaker.  Also it's right on a streetcar line so that could be an option.  The prices are reasonable and the taste is big.  I love the spumoni, I get it every time!  Enjoy!I

being new to the area, i checked my yelp android phone app to see "what's hot" near me, and i found this restaurant close to where i was staying.  i loove thai food, and they had a killer lunch special, so i dropped in one day for lunch.  i ordered the coconut soup, dumplings (i know, not very thai, but i can never resist dumplings), and pad thai (my usual go-to when trying out a new thai place).

- coconut soup: yum. normal. as expected. downed the broth, left the veggies.
- dumplings: soggy, mushy, fell apart.  disappointed.  my bad for ordering chinese at a thai place.
- pad thai: from the first bite it just tasted too soy saucy.  it didn't taste like pad thai to me.  very, very disappointing.  

i might try this place out again to give it another shot, but if a thai restaurant can't get pad thai right each time they make it (in my opinion), then i'm not sure it's worth trying out a second time :T

My husband and I just moved to the area, and at the moment we're living on Scott AFB in temporary housing. I was excited to see that something other than pizza delivers to on base locations, especially since we're still getting established here and the husband has the car during the day. I decided to give this place a try for lunch and it was great! 

The gentleman who took my order was patient and very nice, repeated my order back to me to ensure its accuracy, and informed me of the wait time of 45 min to 1 hour. When it arrived at my door, it was on time, piping hot, and delivered with a smile! The portions are very generous and everything tasted great! 

Obviously it's not a 5-star spot, but waaaay better quality than what I got at Panda Express a couple weeks ago. I had read a few lackluster reviews about this place but decided to give it a chance and I was pleasantly surprised!

I can't believe I've lived in Tucson for 10 plus years and never ate here in til today. Fresh tortillas made here and it's delicious. I eat it with there tasty salsa. Shrimp ceviche is made fresh as well, so it took 20 minutes , well worth it. I had chicken fajitas and it came with beans and zucchini and corn, so good. My  husband got the Chili con carne that he liked , and he also had a Michilada that he said was excellent! This place is now our favorite Mexican Restaurant. I can't wait to go back.

Excellent food,  great service,  secret menus.
Best kept secret in Fairview Hieghts, it is not
the easiest place to find and would probably 
do much better at a more prevelant location.
But the food is awesome and who doesnt love
a secret menu (Korean)

If you know me, you also know that I just LOVE meat.  So I have always avoided vegetarian restaurants like the 2 week-old wrinkly tomato in the back of my fridge.  And whenever I've ignored my better judgment, I've always been sadly disappointed (with both restaurants and tomatoes).

But the reviews of Vedge have been so mouthwateringly good, we finally broke down, and I'm very glad we did.

In the old days, Vedge's 1890's townhouse (on the National Historic Register) was home to Deux Cheminees, one of the luminaries of Philadelphia's fine dining scene 20+ years ago.  Today, the dark wood interior, stained glass windows, charmingly cozy lounge and contemporary bar have as striking look that still preserves those past memories (although I did feel the dining rooms were a bit on the dim side). 

Upon arriving (parking is easy in one of the nearby lots) ~15 minutes early for our 7:30 PM reservation for 5 people on a Wednesday evening, we were shown to the charming, tiny lounge off of the bar.  Although we had the option to order drinks and snacks, we were eager to get on with our dinner.   However, we were not seated until almost 8PM.  Now, maybe I'm spoiled, but we never seem to have to wait at any of the other Philly restaurants we frequent, so I do admit to being a bit annoyed (no explanation was given).  But this was essentially the only damper on a fine evening.

We opted to for the 5-course tasting menu. However, if you very carefully peruse Vedge's website, you might find the hidden small print saying that the tasting must be ordered 24 hours in advance, which we only realized that AM.  But, to the restaurant's credit, a few hours notice did secure the tasting menu for us.  We also decided to bring our own wines, despite Vedge's liquor license and interesting wine list, which resulted in a $25/bottle corkage fee.  High by Philadelphia standards, but very reasonable considering that every bottle on their list is only marked up $25 over wholesale, a true bargain.  We did order one bottle from their list, which ended up being wine of the night, and they also kindly waived the corkage on our half bottle of dessert wine.

Tasting menu & wines:

Amuse bouche (complementary due to the delay in seating us):

Potato fritters with Chinese mustard--if there is one thing Vedge does well, it is fritters, as this was my second favorite dish of the evening, after the hearts of palm fritters below.  I could pop these things all evening.  Fantastic!

1st course:

Salad of spring greens & peas, coal-roasted carrots, shaved asparagus--a very nice, clean, simple salad, with a light dressing.  I wouldn't drive out of my way, but it was much better than your typical fancied-up lettuce salad, and it looked beautiful on its wood cutting board (see photos).

~2007 Cédric Bouchard (Roses de Jeanne) Champagne Blanc de Noirs Les Ursules--a big and unusual grower Champagne

 2nd course:

Seared tofu on a bed of braised Savoy spinach & black kale, smoked mushroom stock--This was the most controversial dish of the evening.  I admired it as possibly the most delicious tofu I've ever had, obviously imitating a seared scallop, and doing a fair job of it.  But not everyone agreed.

~2011 Arnot-Roberts Touriga Nacional Luchsinger Vineyard (Rosé)

3rd course:

Green & yellow zucchinis (imitating fazzoletti, which doesn't make any sense), heirloom tomatoes, basil, dried olive, fresh hearts of palm fritters--Everyone agreed: this was the dish of the evening.  In part, the fantastic fritters (Vedge rule of thumb: order fritters), and the perfect tomatoes, but also because of the wonderful, accidental pairing of the Radikon orange wine (a white wine made with extended skin contact, so it has the tannins of a red wine and the exotic spices, orange rind and cider of a Christmas wassail).  Food/Wine pairing of the year!

~2005 Azienda Agricola Stanislao Radikon Collio Ribolla Gialla (500mL, $70 off list)

4th course:

Seared Maitake mushroom, gold & candy-striped Chioggia beets, black lentils, pickled leek salad--All I can remember about this dish were the beautiful Chioggias, and the big mushroom, crispy on one side and meaty on the other.  Unfortunately, the big fruit of the wine overpowered the mushroom.

~ 2006 Beaux Frères Pinot Noir Beaux Frères Vineyard

Dessert:

Strawberries, cheesecake, shortcake, ice cream--Being a vegan restaurant, presumably soy was used in this dish, but you'd never know it.  Perfectly ripe strawberries were a good match for the Black Muscat.

~2000 Philip Togni Black Muscat Ca' Togni (375mL; a wine with a fascinating back-story: http://www.bowlerwine.com/site/wines/3716.html )

Service was outstanding, and I especially want to thank the manager, who also served as our sommelier and was very accommodating. $124/person counting tip and the Radikon off the list.

4+ stars based on 1 visit.

Would I go again?  Definitely, but given my carnavorian proclivities, maybe only a couple of times a year.

Sláinte!

Great mid priced steakhouse.  I went on a Sunday and was seated right away.  I had a rib eye steak and it was good.  Not the best rib eye I've had but for the price point it was very good value.  I will be back to try more entrees in the future.
Tiny, crowded, but nice spot to see some music and really get a Nashville neighborhood experience.

I would only come here during Happy Hour Monday through Saturday from 2-7 PM. Otherwise it's over priced for mediocre food. The Happy Hour menu includes 1/2 off select appetizers. I recommend the margherita flat bread which is enough to share with 2 people. I would pass on the calamari because it's mostly breading and is surprisingly a bit spicy. There are select sushi for $5 but there are meh at best. I had the wave roll which was very small pieces of spicy tuna and tempura. It's a good spot for after work to catch up but won't be my go to dinner spot.

First and last time I'll be eating at this place.

Food is mediocre but if you're on the road and need a place to stop this could work. However, I would never come to this place if there were other options. 

The minute I walked into this place the rude manager said it would be a while before someone could take our order. We waited for 10 minutes without water or anything. 10 minutes later the same manager asked if we wanted drinks but when we told him we were ready he replied by saying "I thought I already told you it would be a while." 

What doesn't make sense to me is how he wouldn't be able to take a food order but would take a drink order when they both have to be placed in the system??? 

The management here has forgotten that people are not going to their establishment for free and because of that they have to actually work to make their ambiance enjoyable. Maybe they should reconsider their staff and give a proper etiquette training.

Safe to say I won't be back.

Brunch was perfected at Milktooth. This fountain square gem has discovered the secret to culinary breakfast perfection. With unique food pairings and eclectic decor, I find peace with my inner hipster when I dine here. The coffee selection is nothing short of a caffeine addicts dream. Even just the brewed coffee is swoon worthy. 

Vittles are served on an array of vintage dishes, including coffee cups that I'm sure came from my grandparents house. Every time I come I branch out and try something different because I've yet to be disappointed. Though, I do always get a side of the sorghum glazed bacon because... let's be honest here... it's really freaking good. The Belgian waffle toppings change, but the waffle itself is a fluffy doughy delight. I just had the gruyere and ham Dutch baby pancake and it may be new favorite dish. 

I've always had excellent service. The staff is always up to explaining the unique ingredients they cook with. And I always know my food is going to be cooked to perfection.

Great idea - poor execution.  Everyone loves donuts, rights.....but waiting 30+ minutes won't win back a return visit.  Understaffed and inconsistent product are a problem.  One person is making custom donuts for each order and can't keep up.  Coffee is low quality and watered down.

Just left there. I get everything costs more and staff is limited but I just paid 6.11 for two tacos that were cold and soggy, ugh
At least make me happy a little!

The quantity of food is above average. Though, the coffee seemed a bit watery in taste. The place did have quite a bit of people, but we acquired a seat quickly. It's an ok restaurant. If they could improve anything, it would be the coffee.

Holy cow! This place is delicious and I wanna come back for more!! First off, I should say my hubby and I were driving on the westside to do some furniture shopping. We were both needed a little snack to get us going for the expedition ahead. Somehow we both had the same idea. GASP! Go to The Tamale Place!!

So after turning sharply into the parking lot and rushing inside-dude we were starving. No one wants to go furniture shopping on an empty stomach! We ordered our tamales and enjoyed very very much. They look small but man they pack a lot. They are super delicious with all kinds of meats or peppers in them. They are such a hot commodity that by the time we were there, they had sold out of a lot. Which is cool because it tells me people dig this joint.

Either way, I think I have to say every time I drive Rockville to go to the westside, I'm going to have to stop here for a little tamale action!!

The sweet potato fries and decent drink menu are pretty much the only things that bump this from a 1 to a 2 star review.  My boyfriend & I were looking for a place to get some good pub food for dinner on a weekday and found this place on Yelp.  First of all, Red Lion should not be listed as a Gastropub - that would imply that the food is above your average bar fare. Maybe something else on the menu is decent, but the 2 things that we ordered were downright awful.  

The meat in my boyfriend's burger was chewy. Gross! The chicken in my Hawaiian chicken sandwich was tasteless (seemed like it went straight from the freezer to the grill with no seasoning), the "Canadian bacon" was replaced with small pieces of undercooked, fatty regular bacon, and when a logical topping of "grilled pineapple" would be flat pieces of grilled fruit, instead they threw on a few cold chunks from a can that kept falling off of the sandwich. 

We had higher hopes for this place but were sadly really disappointed.
I love, love, love San Antonio Taco Co. It's ridiculously addicting and always good. I've never had anything there that wasn't great. Plus, it's pretty cheap and right next to Ben and Jerry's.

I ended up at Wudon twice in 3 days and both times it was great! The first time was for lunch on a Sunday. I ordered the Bulgogi Dolsot Bibimbap and my friend ordered a Vegetarian Bibimbap. We were both very happy and we liked the Banchan selection. Our request for Doenjang was honored.  My favorites both times of the Banchan have been the kimchi and the fish cakes. My second trip to Wudon was on a Tuesday night for dinner. I ordered the spicy beef stew. My dinner dates ordered Japchae and a Tofu Soup. We were all thrilled! It was loud and crowded in there by the time we left at maybe 7:45 on a Tuesday evening.  My observations are as follows 1. They need a liquor license. Everyone was going to the market next door for soju and Hite. 2. If it's nearly full it can be loud in there. 3. If it's nearly full and a good portion of the patrons are eating the BBQ it can get a bit smoky in there. Perhaps some better ventilation might be needed...
Otherwise I love their food. Service has been friendly and speedy. Their menu is huge. It's going to take a while to work through it. I could eat Korean food everyday. I don't think there's an "if" I'll be back. I think it's more like "when" I'll be there again. I need to try the BBQ. YUM!

Such a sweet and wonderful atmosphere! Food was great. Cake and cinnamon rolls were yummy! The best part is the staff! We danced and sang and clapped and hugged! We felt loved from the moment we walked in! A family affair all around.
Their hot chicken and Mac n cheese is INSANE. Please order this. I dream about this dish. Their cocktails are also fantastic. It's in a great location too!

If I could give Table 3 zero stars I would. My boyfriend and I went there for lunch and shared the fromage appetizer which was decent but underwhelming, then ordered a burger and panini. The burger was flavorless and fast food quality. The turkey panini was dry and arrived to the table not even warm with brown avocado. There seemed to be a lot of waiters but the only one really doing anything was the bartender bless her heart. Will not be returning sadly.
Everyone knows chick fil a is amazing. Delicious food and amazing service. I've never been unhappy here.

Outstanding Argentine/Italian food.  I lived in Argentina for 2 years and became a fan of this unique blend of South American/Italian cusine.  Cafe 943 does it right.  Outstanding empanadas (among the best I've had), great Churrasco steak and Raviloi -- just like in the better places in Buenos Aires, and a fish special that was just outstanding -- perfectly cooked, buttery and well complimented by a rice and fava bean side.  Service is friendly and attentive.  Decor is a little spartan but comfortable.  It's BYO, cash only.  The "wine glasses" are small water glasses, so if stemware is your thing, bring your own.

I travel a lot for work, and so I told my coworker before I called that we probably wouldn't be able to understand the person on the other line.. turns out I couldn't.  I tried to order General Tso's, some fried rice, and some egg rolls...I ended up getting an egg roll, some chicken that may be General Tso's. *as I'm typing my coworker just informed me it is not*, some real yellow rice and some chicken wings, and let's note that not once did I ever order chicken wings... When we went to pick up our order I hadn't noticed but my coworker saw and employee working the grill "blowing snot into a trash can".. he said it was a "double barrel, snot rocket" so I can only imagine... Him telling me this just as I was about to take my first bite made me more than weary but it tastes fine so I'll give it 3 stars
Great breakfast spot. Really enjoyed the skillet. The service was a bit scattered, seemed like we may have had 2 servers. I hope they split the tip

Between the good service, the good food, and the good view, Summerland cafe is always a good stop. I enjoyed a wonderful lunch after the lunch hour, and the servings are always more than I can eat.
With the patio overlooking the Pacific Ocean, they have made the restaurant dog friendly. 
A must stop if traveling up and down Coastal California

I heard they just opened up here on Grant Rd and Oracle, they were previously serving in the Tohono O'Odham swap meet. Was bored staying home so decided to come here for take out. Got the Parillada (1 lb meat + fixing) for $23 and one goat taco ($2.50 +$1= $3.5). We were allowed to choose hot to 3 types of meat for the Parrillada so we picked Carne Asada + Carnitas + crispy Tripas. She did ask us what tortillas we wanted, we said flour so we assumed we were getting tortillas with the paradilla but when we went home no tortillas to be found. I guess they forgot it, no worries, we got our own tortillas at home and put the meat in. I mixed in a little of the carne asada, Tripas, and carnitas in one taco and it was good! They asked us if we wanted the Tripas soft or crispy so we said crispy! Crispy Tripas is good just a little greasy. The carne asada is ok, could be better if they had wood/ charcoal grilled it. The goat taco was good, the meat was tender, it is an acquired taste, so if you don't like gamey meat maybe this is not for you since it cost $1 more than regular taco. The lime provided was tiny and dry, hardly any juice coming out but no worries, we grabbed some lemon from our backyard and we were good to go. I'm glad to support local mom and pop shop during this difficult time, will you?

Very small, a little kid runs around and makes a lot of noise, and the lady taking orders is rude and nasty.  That being said, I get my sushi to go and enjoy it every time.  The prices are better than Publix or Kroger and the sushi is much better.  I will continue to order my sushi to go and remain very happy.

Do you every stare at a menu for hours debating whether you want the calzone or the burger? Well stare no more! TBBC has a unique dining experience that will satisfy anyone's calzone burger fusion craving. The Bomb is a burger topped with smoky hickory bacon, aged (probably) cheddar cheese, freshly fried onion straws, all wrapped in their delicious pizza dough. 

I could only eat half of it during my visit, as to not significantly exceed my caloric intake for the day all in one sitting, but it heated up surprisingly well in my GE Microwave (High for 73 seconds). 

8.4/10 - Will frequent this place.

My husband and I went to Fleming's for dinner for a date night last Friday.  I hadn't been in a very long time and was nothing but impressed with the food and the service.  Rob A was our server and was very knowledgeable about the menu and provided us great service and attention the entire meal.  When we left, a kind gentleman on the staff even brought me a handmade paper flower which was such a nice touch!  I'd highly recommend!

I had the duck thing and the quail salad. Poultry is wonderful here, my girlfriend's pork chop was OKAY but it's pork what are you going to do? Maybe I'm just not the guy to ask about non-bacon pork. 

The cheese plate had very odd crackers but the bleu cheese bites like a tiger and it was great. 

I had a 2008 Pinot which was so good I forgot what it was called. 

We were seated at ~6:50 and were able to order food at ~7:10. I enjoyed the ambiance and never mind waiting for good food, but don't come in starving, the waitstaff takes their time with each customer and you'll need to wait your turn. Once they found their way to our corner, our waiter knew everything about everything on the menu, so no one is slacking off.

Would love to eat here again, probably will wait until I'm trying to impress someone.

Very impressed with every bite of what I ordered! Super happy with the goat cheese appetizer could not believe the balance of savory and sweet. My meal of the Havana entree was divine. The sweet of a mango within this quesadilla was just out of this world. I was very impressed and I cannot wait to take another trip!

Our local Favorite!! My Family loves this place  fried green beans is our daughters favorite and I love fish fry on Fridays. We had relatives coming in from Vegas, Chicago, Tennessee, California and Ohio and we all ate there. They loved it!! We tried different foods from the menu and everyone was satisfied. My husband and I love to go have drinks here and they made my favorite on point. Always leaving smiling and giggling

I tried the Chipotle Cheese Steak on Rosemary Bread. It was amazing. The meat was wonderful and very fresh. The onions were great too. My sub were very messy (in a good way) and had cheese oozing out of everywhere. The subs were out to our table very fast. I can't think of anything wrong with my whole experience. That was definitely the best Cheese Steaks  that I've ever had. I can't wait to try more of there menu options.

Very good barbecue!! Very loud, noisy, and crowded restaurant!! Not able to have much dinner conversation with our guests, but the food was delicious!!! The ribs were my favorite. Brisket was too tough for my liking. Pickles were incredible!!! Sides were excellent!!!
