Tomato Pies (aka pizza) were ok, the traditional with cheese on the bottom and the white broccoli were both better than the grandma pizza which was surprisingly salty and not great.  The sandwiches were very good, we had an Italian beef and an Italian pork.  However the Italian pork was super spicy and I didn't expect that or see it anywhere in the description.  Finally, price was fair for what you get.  3 pizzas and 2 sandwiches for $83 feels expensive to me, but so does everywhere.  Main reason why I am giving 3 stars instead of 4 is that they forgot the pepperoni on our cheese on the bottom pizza, yet I was charged for it.

This class-act BYO (a wine store and beer distributor are a block away) flagged slightly after it was "discovered" by the Inquirer newspaper some time back. Thankfully, it quickly recovered and went on to become even better than before.

Rouget is in a stunning Addams Family type Victorian building overlooking a large grassy corner with an old stone springhouse. There's lovely seating on a glassed-enclosed porch facing the corner. However, bland touches like acoustical tile ceiling and boring carpeting rob the interior of vintage charm. Too, some interior tables, resting as they do on thick carpeting/padding, can be tipsy if leaned on hard.

A really great value is their $35 four-course tasting menu Tuesday-Thursday, with cheese course optional if you call hours in advance. A pricier six-course menu is also available, and calling the chef a day or more in advance helps here, too, so he can obtain the most interesting ingredients. Fresh foie gras with figs (call the chef a week or so in advance for this exceptional treat) and wild mushroom bisque appetizers are world-class; ditto selected mains offerings and white chocolate dessert. Service, which briefly generated complaints, is now back up to snuff.

Bottom line, Rouget offers excellence in fine dining normally associated with Center City standouts. Yet -- weekdays, at least -- at prices from an earlier and happier time.

Ordered the Cajun fries and the Catfish PoBoy Togo. Big mistake.m, because if I would've ate it there I could've asked for a refund for being served bad fish. The catfish was bad fish that should've been thrown out and not cooked and served to guest as if it was old fish. I took 3 bites and was like yeah this is bad fish. The crawfish in the Cajun fries weren't fresh at all. I've had better food and service at McDonald's
Terribly slow drive through service. I know they're new but they really need to step up their game!

Came here for a team dinner and went family style. In general, the food was decent Indian fusion - emphasis on fusion, don't come here looking for authentic Indian food. The sesame crusted salmon and butter chicken were a bit dry. Winners were definitely the saag paneer and shrimp vindaloo. Definitely eat the naan while it's hot! Flourless chocolate cake was super chocolatey, key lime pie was nicely tart, and mango cheesecake took the gold when it came to dessert.

Pretty good, had the spicy hushpuppies ane they werent spicy but had a great flavor but hard to eat more thwn one.   Ordered the blackened redfish, and thought it was very light on the blackening but also a great flavor.   If you have high blood pressure dont eat here though, alot of salt

Used to be the lazy brew and only been there a couple of times and I wasn't thrilled about the food..it was OK but NOW...food is unreal...Spicy pork absolutely unbelievable...and their wings are awesome and I think are better then coppertop...I officially found a place to watch football every sunday!!  Owner is cool and they definitely make sure you are happy with your experience A+

We had a marvelous dinner at La Placita this evening.  The sweet green tamales were excellent.  There were seven of us and the waiter made us feel special and welcome.  The chicken mole enchiladas were very tasty and the mole sauce had a kick to it which I thought was delightful.  The Maria's Margarita was well blended and fresh.  The Tres Leche Cake was mmmmmmarvelous.  Oh and the homemade chips and gaucamola are the best I have ever had.
Amazing cheesesteaks! Always fresh, hot, and tasty. Super convenient place to pick up beer with dinner also.

This place was disgusting. I ordered grilled scallops with fries. For a seafood restaurant on the shore, you'd think the seafood would be exceptional.  The scallops tasted and looked frozen. The fries were actually the worst I've ever had. Limp, soggy and greasy.  Save your money. No indoor seating either.

We're from out of town and were very excited to eat at this restaurant. It was a shame to learn that this restaurant has gone back in time-  to those of discriminating against people who are different. Since we're unvaccinated, we were told "you can't sit in the main dining area, but you can sit on the patio." We even had negative covid tests showing we do not have COVID. Discrimination at its finest. Super sad.

I had panzarotti's here for the first time. However, they were way to oily. They do not compare to the consistently good panzarotti's I have gotten from Sal's Pizzeria in Marlton, NJ. The place is spartan, with security windows. However the service was friendly. Not much room to eat here.

I have been a fan of Pizzology since they opened their Carmel location.  The Homemade Sausage is amazing.  It's my go to selection along with a large chop salad to split.  We have tried a variety of their pizzas and haven't had anything we didn't like.  

Seasonal selections on the appetizer menu rotate.  They used to have zuchinni fritters that were awesome, wish they would bring those back.  

Order the sidecar of sauces to help use up that last bit of crust.  Mix the garlic and mornay together...perfection.  

Good selection or wine, beer, and drinks.  

It's kid friendly, but I prefer to enjoy without my toddler.

Family was in Reno visiting from Sacramento for a day trip, wanted pizza and found Rick's. We ordered 2 pizzas and Bread sticks. They were the best pizzas, we have ever had, can't think of a better pizza! Owner was excellent, great service, friendly, nice, helpful. Perfect space for dine in or out or takeout. Quick, hot food, drinks. Clean & safe. Would go back everytime in the area!

Delicious! Just checked out Rene's for lunch. Ordered a carne asada burrito for myself and a barbacoa taco for my 2 year old and they were both amazing. The carne was had a nice outer crust/crunch from the grill, but was so tender that it melted in my mouth. Combine that with the pieces of avocado, onions and I can't remember what else they put in the burrito, but just say yes if they ask what you want in the burrito. The barbacoa was super tender and my 2 year old ate it up quickly. Definitely recommend trying it for yourself.
Love this hidden gem. I always eat here when I visit NOLA!!! Good home cooked food!!!

Ben A.
The first time was great! Party of five was received with red carpet treatment. Service was prompt and food was amazing! 
Second time around for party of 2? Not so great! Waiter was very welcoming and interacted well but the food was lukewarm at best. Staff appeared surprised; however, the food was replaced with hot food. It just took too long. 
Third time? Party of four, including 2 first time customers! Food was lukewarm for three of us. One of us sent the food back but the replacement was colder than the first. Supervisor came out and stated that he "felt it" before it came out and that it was hot! He was encouraged to place a finger in the food and after doing it he the stated that he actually  "felt the bowl" earlier and that it was hot. He apologized. Will not recommend this place again.
A bit of a wait but totally worth it. I got the buttermilk Pancakes with bacon and pork sausage links.
This place is horrible, they are always out of BBQ sauce and now they have no chicken nuggets. Horrible service.

Best Indian in Nashville. Small restaurant so call ahead. They're lunch buffet is great because you get to sample a bunch of dishes before settling in with something you love! Onion bajees are really good but you might want to make two orders because you only get a few with the appetizer portion. Chicken tikka masala is off the chain!!! Great service and you'll leave full!

I loved this nice little Korean restaurant. My friend and I were greeted immediately once we walked in the door. They have a relatively big menu that will satisfy your Korean food craving. Their small plates before meal were all very good, loved their kimchi. I ordered a spicy beef soup stew, it was fantastic! A little spicy, but with all the vegas and food in the soup, it really hit the spot. Our server kept checking on us to make sure we liked our food, she was very friendly. 

Overall, it's a nice and neat restaurant, the price is very reasonable, great food and service. Can't wait to go back and try more of their food.

Every time I go there around 8pm it's closed. I see people in there and the door says open till 9pm but it's closed. Today I went there at 6:30pm and again it's closed. I live in the apartments right behind it so I go there often and theres a kid in there that must be on something because I went to give him my order and he rudely tells me to wait till he puts his code in the register and 2 seconds later he ask me for my order and it was 2 sandwiches and he rings it up and he charges me for 1 so I figured he got it wrong and when I said 2 he goes oh like it's my fault. This place has to lose money because all the people that get there to find it closed and on more then one occasion there were people getting out of the car and I tell them it's closed and they say isn't it open till 9 and I say that's what the door says so again they are losing money because of it. Try going there around 8 or a little after and see if it's open.

I was working in South Philly today and decided I wanted to go out for lunch. So naturally, I used my trusty Yelp app and looked up some local places. San Miguelito popped up at the top of my list, had a 5 star rating and was a 7 minute walk from my job. Perfect! 
This restaurant was definitely a diamond in the rough. The food that this little hole in the wall was putting out was amazing! I ordered the Al Pastor tacos, which were served on fresh tortillas with cilantro and onions. The meat was juicy, flavorful, authentic and cooked to perfection.  Yum yum yum yum yum! An order of 3 only came to $6.50!!!!! This restaurant is a little hole in the wall and I would have never thought about coming in here. Thanks to Yelp, I was able to find this gem. Another successful food adventure! I hope after you read this you make the decision to try this place out too. You will not be disappointed.
Food was very good so was the service. I would recommend this to everyone. Not cheap but worth the price.

I see some reviews mentioning the prices, but you are paying for the equivalent of white tablecloth technique that is barbecue here. Straight-up protein isn't cheap even in raw form, and at Central City you get a flip ton of it done right. This is certainly a special occasion place for me to order from, but worth it. 

This past Saturday we ordered online at 11:30 and the brisket and ribs were already sold out, but the ribs tips...I picked one up by the bone and it slid right out, meat so tender.  Sweet chicken wings were just as good as the Buffalo style we tried before.  And as always, the Brussels sprouts and spoonbread and coleslaw. I can't wait until we are all vaxxed up and can eat in person again, even when the place is (rightfully) clogged with tourists.
Great value.  Genuine hospitality.  Feels like you're grabbing breakfast with grandpa as a kid.

Very solid Thai food with spacious seating and fast. friendly service at the corner of W. Wayne and Conestoga.  It's tucked away in Wayne but the food is good and the portions very generous.  I really liked my Pad See Yew and Asiana Veggie Lover with additional jumbo shrimp.  The dishes were very flavorful and not very salty, with plenty of crisp, fresh veggies and just the right balance of savory and sweet.  The Thai eggplant with chicken was also very good and I really liked that the eggplant was not mushy and overcooked, which happens very frequently with this dish at other places.  The portions are also huge!  Our food was served in less than 10 minutes and our servers were very helpful and attentive.  Definitely returning to try more of the menu and will update accordingly.

Recently we hosted a company dinner at the Wild River Grille for 40 of our employees and a plus one. Working through the planning of the dinner was easy (mostly through email as I live in another state). The WRG staff was very responsive and helpful through the whole process. When we arrived at the WRG the staff was ready for us and did a great job of handling the drinks at the bar and orders. The food was prepared well and came out in a timely manner. I would definitely recommend using the WRG for future events.

Nice casual atmosphere and good red fish. I figured that I should order the red fish at red fish grill. I had it with the lemon vinaigrette dressing which was flavorful but not too heavy. It was served with eggplant and several other vegetables such as squash. Presentation of the food was what I would expect from this type of place. Fresh veggies nicely laid on top of the red fish with sauce in the side. I enjoyed that the sauce was on the side so I could customize it to my liking. They also brought out complimentary bread on before the meal which was fresh and addicting. My coworker stated that the cornbread he got with his meal was excellent.

The restaurant had a very modern decor with fish art hanging from the ceiling and an artsy palm tree. Ceiling was high, so restraint felt very open and even though it was crowded, it never felt like the place got too loud.

Service was terrific. Our waiter was very friendly, answered our questions, and consistently refilled my water without me having to ask. The restaurant is a little pricey, but good seafood usually is. Overall, red fish grill is a solid option in the French Quarter of New Orleans.

Potential to be a great local BYO with great service and extensive menu but there were fundamental issues with the food.  Balsamic calamari was tough and rubbery.  Pasta sauce had no taste and the linguine with clams promised garlic but again was tasteless.  Too many specials to chose from and most attractive main courses were priced above $32 to $40.  The biggest issue was the pasta.  It was not fresh and tasted like a generic grocery store box.  Bread was fresh and desserts looked great but everything in between was disappointing.

My husband and I gambled on a good night's rest at the Golden Nugget in Sparks/Reno, and we lost.  We stopped there, exhausted, while traveling, having seen okay reviews as a 3.5 star hotel.  We got a 'deluxe king room'.

The space in the room and the sitting area were good, even if the upholstery and furniture were a bit worn.  I could nitpick a number of minor issues, but there were three which ruined our stay.

1) The toliet was not totally functional.  It would not flush the first try.  Instead it would make an awful noise for a while.  You could then flush it later on a second try without difficulty or noise.

2) The bed was not a king!  While management did check into it the next morning and assured us that their linen company had measured it and told them it was a king, it was not 76' wide or even the 72' wide of a California king. It is 66' wide, a 'super queen' or 'olympic queen'.  They swore to us all their 'king' beds are this size.

3) The mattress was a horrible, squeaky, springy thing that bounced horribly with any move my husband or I made.

Management was polite and removed the resort fee, but I still feel like we would have done better to go down the street to any of a dozen alternatives offering rooms at similar  rates.
We love tuk tuk thai! The food are very flavorful and authentic. The portions are great too!
Great food and service .I am not a big fan of Greek and I even loved it ! Highly recommend!
The best tacos and Menudo soup! Ridiculously good! I live in Clearwater and would tell you if I have a taco crave - it is the place!

I always order for delivery  so I can't really say anything about the actual place but the guy on the phone is always super welcoming and warm!!! Hands down best eggplant parmesan sandwich in Tucson. The mixed cheese is good too but they skimp on the lettuce and tomato. I usually try to order somewhere else each time but there are just a few yummy places that deliver so u dont mind being a valued customer here.  I just wish the sandwiches were a tad cheaper but other than that, no complaints!

You could go there a million times and always have something new to eat. Never disappoints and besides lunch time it's pretty relaxing to sit and enjoy your food. The donut place is my favorite and the roast beef place is my second. Really easy access from suburban station.

This is our first time in New Orleans and we arrived at our hotel after 9 pm. Our concierge gave us a coupon for a free dessert at the Cheescake Bistro, so we thought, what the heck. 

The restaurant was clean and the atmosphere nice.

We ordered the eggplant fries as an appetizer with the seafood sauce. It was just ok. I love eggplant so maybe my expectations are high. 

New Orleans is definitely a place for seafood lovers. There wasn't really any vegetarian options. Shame too, because their build your own burger would have been good with a veggie burger option. 

My husband ordered the crawfish ravioli (note to all, I won't touch shellfish ) and I had the Cobb salad with salmon (sans bacon). My husband loved his ravioli. This was his first time trying crawfish. He thought it a stronger fishy flavor, but he said it balanced nicely with the sauce.

My salad was excellent. It was a huge portion and the salmon was cooked just right. 

For our free dessert we decided to try their white chocolate bread pudding. Heaven!!!  This was a large portion so I definitely recommend sharing. 

Our server Anthony was very nice and the best surprise - they give a 50% military discount!!!  I was so surprised!  I will definitely stop by here again before we leave.
One of the BEST burgers I have ever had. This was not just a burger, it was an experience....fries were awesome too!

When my class mate told me of this place, she described it as a Thai restaurant that also served American breakfasts - strange combination right? Naturally I was skeptical of how authentic the Thai food would be. 

I am happy to report that this place was surprisingly delish! I ordered the pad see ew and it was ok. The beef was dry and the seasoning was not nearly as spicy as I was hoping. However, the pad thai was amazeballs! One of the best pad thai dishes I've ever had. The tom yum soup was also very tasty! 

My friend also order some chicken lo mien - a very safe dish for a very white boy with unadventurous taste buds. If you're looking for something mild, that would be a very safe dish to order. :) Don't get me wrong, it was tasty, but it was definitely not what I would think of as authentic Thai. It was like a much better version of Panda Express lo mien.

The restaurant is small but very clean. Something about it is very charming. I liked the ambiance immediately. I look forward to coming back and dining on the porch in the spring when the weather is nice. Definitely enjoyed this Thai place more than the one down the street (Singa Song II or something like that).

Such a cute place and right next to Creole Creamery! My friend and I shared everything! We got the chorizo with almonds; steak with potatoes; scallops; and the mixed roasted mushrooms! Scallops & mushrooms were a little on the salty side but other than that everything was really good! Highly recommend.

Had a really great breakfast here. There was a decent-sized crowd waiting, but since I was solo, I slotted in at the end of the counter (the advantages of being a loner are many). It's a pretty small place that takes advantage of the spacial perception advantage that mirrors give.

Diner waitress - a sweet middle-aged, gravelly-voiced woman who was extra nice. Diner coffee - not the finest of caffeines, but it's familiar and gets the job done. Diner menu - but much much higher quality. 

I had a mixed fruit bowl, which pleasingly was not the usual cantaloupe and grapes in a cup. Bananas, mixed berries, tangerines, etc. It was fruit. In a bowl! Just as advertised. Main part of the meal was the Tomato Pesto Mozzarella Omelet. So good! The eggs were fluffy, the flavor was great, and they use small tomatoes, which are the best kind of tomatoes. Sides were home fries - flavorful and not greasy (!!!) and wheat toast. You know, warmed up stale wheat bread. Excellent!

Great neighborhood spot. Service is always prompt and friendly and I love their bagels, especially at the price! I've had my order messed up a few times (wrong cream cheese, etc) but I've never even cared or complained because I love all of their options!
Great bar food with some traditional irish dishes. The wait staff was slow but other than that its a pretty good time.

We originally had planned on going somewhere a little further down the road but, after a day poolside, none of us really wanted to walk any more. Besides, the street construction was a bit daunting in slaps.

I must say, this was a wonderful find! The service was friendly and prompt, but not hurried. The wine list was respectable while not being absurd. And the food was delicious and fresh.

Hubby's ribeye was scrumptious and cooked to perfection. My wasabi tuna was delectable and light. I WAS asked what temp I wanted it and, after being assured it was VERY fresh, I opted for rare with a light sear. Our friends had the stuffed grouper, which they could not stop raving about throughout the next day. All items came with a delicious potato souffle-type side and veggies. The salad included with our meals was large, for side salad standards, and the dressing was wonderful. Even the fried zucchini sticks were plentiful and crisp.

I suppose the only boo moment was the wait we were told we would endure for a seat outside; it was a Sunday. We were, however, seated immediately inside and, though it was a tad dark, it was pleasant and cool.

Stop in next time you're in St Pete. If you're a seafood addict, you'll be hooked!
...pun intended ;)
It's okay...

The PHILLY-RRITO (cheesesteak burrito) was absolutely delicious. It had the perfect combination of ribeye steak to cheese to fried peppers and onions to french fries. As a fan of quality Philly cheesesteaks like Dalessandro's and Jim's this burrito more than met my expectations. The meat was flavorful and juicy and the addition of the hand cut french fries really took this thing to another level. Sometimes you see places that make "fat" sandwiches with french fries, mozzarella sticks, or what have you into their sandwiches as almost a gimmick, but the fries in this cheesesteak burrito added the perfect amount of crunch, oil, and salt. Normally I would say $14 is on the higher side for a burrito but this thing was massive and more than worth the cost.

I would wholeheartedly recommend this place to my friends and family. The girl working the counter was extremely nice and polite and allowed me to get extra sauces to try at no charge. I used a 10% Yelp check-in available at the time, which is an extra bonus and I encourage you to contribute it towards a tip as this place deserves it!

Cafe Du Monde is at the heart of New Orleans, probably the most iconic location in terms of artwork around LA. It's beautiful seeing that you can walk down the street and go to the cathedral and take a tour of the French Quarter. Whenever I went in today, the place was absolutely packed, and you can't blame them. The beignets were made fresh, and the coffee is absolutely delicious. 

The only problem is that the place is so packed that you can barely hear yourself talking due to the numerous amount of people. Sometimes it's so busy that you can barely ever get a clean table without having to hustle through a large crowd of people.

In conclusion, I guess you could say that coming here is a great experience, especially if you're a tourist. Mostly for historical value and a taste of what New Orleans is about.

This place is great. I was on a road trip and stopped here for dinner. The food was super fresh and the octopus and cauliflower were insanely delicious. Outside seating was charming...loved the ambience.

This review is for Terraza, the bar portion of "The Grill at Hacienda Del Sol Resort." 

Let me start by saying, I love the setting of this resort, as it makes me feel like I'm in Santa Fe, New Mexico. The grounds are beautifully landscaped, and the views are some of the best in town. It was a cold evening, and as we stepped out of the car, I immediately noticed the distinct fragrant smell of mesquite wood burning. If only the rest of our experience tonight could have been half as good as the mesquite wood smell coming from the kiva fireplaces! 

My husband and I had missed happy hour, which runs from 4-6 PM, M-F. When we arrived at the Grill around 6:30 PM, we decided to just have dinner in the bar area, since we didn't have reservations, and we weren't up for the formalities of the main restaurant on a Friday night when we were both tired. It had been about two years since we've eaten here (in the bar area). We used to come quite frequently on the weekend nights when they had great live Spanish (Gipsy Kings style) music. Tonight we had wanted to sit outside on the patio since a band was starting at 7:00, but  we were informed that all of the tables were "reserved." No matter... We got a table inside, and we got our table just before the rush hit. 

Maybe they weren't prepared for the big gem show crowd? Whatever it was, I don't want to make excuses for their lack of service, and lack of food quality. They had about 3 bus boys, and 3 hostesses, but sadly- only one cocktail/food waitress for an entire bar area filled with hungry and thirsty patrons. The poor waitress... It wasn't her fault. I felt sorry for her, and I couldn't help but sense and feel her eye popping looks every time a new table sat down, or every time we'd ask for something else. Add that to her practically running through the bar to pick up drinks for the nearly 10 tables. Where was the manager? 

Sigh, and double sigh!!! Onto the food.... Let me say that for bar food in Tucson, it's pricey. I know it's a resort. And if the food had been better, I wouldn't mind paying these prices. We started with chips, salsa, and guacamole, which for $6 sounded like a great deal. It was a big white bowl filled with two colors of cold tortilla chips, literally one lowly tablespoon of salsa, and one lowly tablespoon of guacamole. Twice we had to ask for "more salsa please." Hmmm... To serve it like this in Tucson? A chips and salsa town we are, and know our chips and salsa- we do!  Maybe the resort guests have no idea that they should expect more salsa, and if this is their first intro to the chips and salsa staple- they may not be seeking it out anywhere else. I have to say this: two BIG thumbs down on the chips and salsa. Guys, how about fewer chips and more salsa and guacamole? As it was, we ended up leaving half of the chips uneaten. 

For our main courses, my husband and I ended up switching. He had ordered the "Double Check Ranch burger," ($14) which was supposed to come with blue cheese, green chiles, and cherry wood bacon- but somehow- the chiles were left off. The fries... Do you really want to know how bad the fries were? I've had better fries at McDonalds'. Unfortunately they tasted like- day old & cold McDonalds' fries. Sad. Really sad. I had been excited to come back here, but once I got the food, my excitement dried up pretty fast. The reason we switched plates was because the blue cheese on the burger was overwhelming for my husband, and after a few bites- it was overwhelming for me too. 

I had originally ordered chicken enchiladas ($12), which were soggy on the top and hard on the bottom tortillas on a bed of black beans that (I kid you not) filled the entire plate, and we both decided had to have been nearly an entire can. (They tasted canned- not fresh). We switched plates because we were both disappointed with our food, but (again) the poor swamped waitress didn't even have time to come back and check on us. When we finally had to track her down for more water, she didn't even notice that we had switched plates. 

Saving graces were a good glass of Zinfandel, The Federalist ($10), and my husband had a pint of English Black Stout ($7). The wine list has only two glasses of white wine for $8 per glass. There is only one red (an Argentine Malbec for $9). The rest of the wines range from $10 to $15 per glass. Sadly, there was no one around to express our complaints to. We left with the feeling that this must have been an off night for them.

This restaurant was extremely disappointing. Size of the portions is very small.  that included the tacos, the rice bowl and the nachos were awful. There was hardly any meat and the tortilla chips were stale. This is going to be a one and done. Sorry I hope they find someone that likes their food and the size of their portions but it's not me

A Carrollwood main stay, this is a great Friday night escape, solid food, fresh ingredients, they are friendly and have a fast deliveries. Definitely beats the pizza chain restaurants and open for lunch, highly recommend Slice Masters.

Nuvo Burrito = Creative (in their menu, marketing and decor)

If you go there expecting something like Blue Coast or Baja or Moes, this is not that kind of burrito place. The burrito combinations that Nuvo offers are unique, well thought out, FRESH and addictive.  Some of them are a little on the experimental side.  

My favorite is the Plymouth.  In fact, I love it so much, I don't order anything else, because I crave it all the time.    

If you get salsa, make sure to try the green (tomatillo / salsa verde).  They make it themselves and it's one of my favorite salsa's in town (close tie with Rose Pepper's).  

The staff is incredibly friendly. Make sure to get a stamp card from these guys and join their emailing list, facebook and twitter, because they are very active and creative with their marketing and do post coupons regularly.

Wonderful atmosphere, employees, and food. You're definitely getting what you pay for and definitely worth the trip here. A lot of nice vegan and vegetarian options, which is nice also. I had the palak paneer and would definitely come back.

While waiting for my family's table to be called I decided to shop around the store and I notice I'm being followed by a lady worker. I would look at the toys and there she was watching me, I would then look at the clothes and there she was watching me, I would look at the candy and there she was again. I started feeling uncomfortable because here I am, the only MEXICAN woman shopping amidst the other white women shopping and I'm the only one with an escort. It was so uncomfortable for me, So I decided to end my shopping and pay for my stuff and wait outside with my family. As I'm walking out the worker escorts me out too!!! 
Our table gets called and we all go inside to get seated, this lady sees me and makes the comment "I see you're not done shopping", at this point I'm upset and my brother is upset because he can also see that I'm being targeted by this racist worker, he asks her if there's a problem and if we're in her way because she keeps looking our way and she responds with "no, I just like to stand here and look at the discounts, they have such great stuff here!" First of all, you're supposed to be working and not shopping but also have the decency to apologize and admit that you truly are being racist and following me around because I'm not the skin color you would prefer in your store.

I have loved this place for years!  It is delicious, well-prepared, un-fussy French cuisine.  Food is very tasty without being over-done and over-sauced.   The atmosphere is simple and warm.  It is calm and quiet (unlike a lot of the "hip" Center City restaurants).  It is a go-to for holiday luncheons for my staff and a great place to keep in touch with special friends.

You say Kahlua Banana French Toast, and I say HYPE!
Kahlua Banana French Toast! ... HYPE!!!
Kahlua Banana French Toast! ... HYPE!!!
Kahlua Banana French Toast! ... HYPE!!!

Sorry not sorry to be in the minority opinion, guys.
----------
Prior to our hike to Inspiration Point, my friends and I were inspired to come here to grab some breakfast... because nothing says "We're ready for some strenuous uphill activity" like stuffing our faces with heavy, sugar-laden carbs. LONG LIVE AMUUUURICA!

I ordered the beloved, infamous Kahlua Banana French Toast, and I wish I could say that sh!t was B-A-N-A-N-A-S, but I was McKayla Maroney-level not impressed (http://imgur.com/H9bWuCf). The food pictures and menu description made this french toast sound heart-stopping heavenly--"authentic challah bread topped with bananas sauteed in Kahlua, brown sugar and butter"--so naturally, I played up my expectations to the tune of other people's praises.

At first, when the food was brought to the table, I was really excited because it looked as amazing in person as it did in pictures. Then after I had finished snapping a million food pictures in true Asian fashion, I opened my eyes and saw that the challah bread pieces, which were already drenched with the caramelized Kahlua sauce, were basically sitting atop a puddle of even more sauce... and then I wasn't so excited anymore. To be honest, I was a little turned off by that abominable discovery.

The first two bites were okay, but each bite after that was a little painful; my throat literally hurt as the sugar glob passed through it (as with all things too sweet). The goopy caramelized Kahlua sauce was so overwhelming that it killed any flavor that the french toast might've had. I tried to eat some of the banana slices in hopes of cutting out some of the sweetness, but that too was covered in sauce... aiyaaah. I ended up finishing only one of the four slices on my plate, of which I'm actually really proud because consuming this dish was a bit more difficult than I had originally imagined. 

In conclusion, it was like as if someone had ejaculated caramel sauce all over every inch of my breakfast, thereby rendering it nearly inedible. I don't really know what I was expecting, but I'm surprised that I didn't let the words "sautéed in brown sugar and butter" deter me from ordering the Kahlua Banana French Toast. I guess, no more sweet things for this bitter girl. Ya live and ya learn (even if it's for the hundredth time).

LESSON LEARNED... for now.

// PS. One of my friends ordered the huevos rancheros, and it was AHHHH-MAZING. It comes with corn tortillas, fried egg, beans, cheese, homemade salsa, and avocado. The salsa provided a nice, spicy kick to slap me awake from the oncoming food coma. If I ever make my way back here again, that's what I'm getting!

Located inside the AMP at 16 Tech. On my first visit to the  AMP, I was looking at all the vendors and this is the one that caught my eye. I used to live in Miami and haven't had arepas in a while. Also, I LOVE fried plantains.

I ended up ordered the pabellon, which is white cheese, black beans, plantains and shredded beef in the thick corn pancake (arepa), for $12.  It was good except that it needed some salsa or something a little sauce or liquid because the overall effect was a bit dry.  But the flavor was otherwise good and my plantains in particular did not disappoint.  

#yum #ReviewsByRL
9 am on Sunday, plenty of open tables and still a 30 minute wait. I understand when it's crowded but we came here as early as possible to be beat the crowed and still waiting.
Really good experience. Food is good quality and good prices. Beef doesn't have any hormones ( according to their disclaimer ) . Our server, Jeremy, was great and so pleasant!

I have never wanted to leave a restaurant so quickly... TO WRITE A 5 STAR REVIEW
How am I possibly giving 5 stars to a pizzeria?!  Seriously guys, my taste buds just went on a roller coaster ride and I can't wait to go back for more. I really don't know how else to say this... but I'm pretty sure I just experienced a TASTEBUD ORGASM.

Each dish we ordered was a symphony of unique flavor.  I was extremely shocked at the presentation, textures, and taste.  When we saw all the servers walking around in untucked blue collar button downs, grey dickies, and red tennis shoes, the LAST thing we expected was to be blown away by such fantastic quality food.  

**I encourage diners to be prepared and open minded to the unique tastes, aromas, and flavor combinations.  If you're looking for an experience, not just a meal, eat here.  You can't go wrong with what we had this evening:

Whipped Ricotta Vasi
Crispy Beef Cheeks Antipasti
Goat Cheese and Pancetta Pizza

Sunday brunch...

First time at Adelphi's and never realized how big this place is. It was nicely decorated for the holidays.   

I ordered the bacon egg and cheese croissant which was light, flaky and delicious.    

The side of bacon is huge.   At most places you get three pieces here you can at least 6.   

Everyone enjoyed their brunch.   

The blood Mary was weak and lacked heat.   However the hot chocolate despite being on the small side was very good.

I'm giving it two stars just because their staff was awesome and the bloody mary's were good. Other than that, their bacon has literally made my husband and I, never want bacon again. Do NOT order the Bacon Sampler. Like, how do you mess up bacon? All of the flavors tasted like rotten feet or dog treats. I just threw up in my mouth thinking about it. Not to mention, I wish someone would take Berryhill down a notch, not exactly the nicest person. 

If you're a bacon lover, don't go here. You'll be throughly disappointed as we were. Barf.

This place proved true to what I was expecting: A DECADENT HEAVEN! Walked over from &pizza across the st and it hit all the right spots for my dessert craving. We sat at the bar area where we could still order the desserts. They also have a dinner menu which makes this a complete experience if you're looking for a perfect date night or a friend gathering.  We ordered the surprise tiramisu and it is the best I've ever had! The smooth and rich texture just melts in your mouth - and the fact that they add biscuits submerged in the tiramisu which gives it a little crispiness to it. We also ordered the big party platter with white and milk chocolate fondue. There were 10 of us and this was the perfect size (and we still had leftovers!). 

Have to give a s/o to the bartender who accommodated us. We were a party of 3 at first but slowly everyone started walking over from &pizza and it got very loud very quickly. But the bartender was very friendly and very  understanding of our frequent requests! Definitely coming here again, amazing desserts and very friendly staff

A+ place, a secret gem of Boise. I would dare to say Goldy's is the best breakfast spot in downtown Boise. I had their malted waffle (yes.. a malted waffle) and it was out of this world. 

100% would recommend if you're looking for a good quant breakfast spot.

I understand Walmart fast food will not be the same as a standalone. While the service was nice, the resteraunt was disgusting. Not a clean table to find, the condiment section was gross, and the floors horrrendouse.

Normally when we do this type of restaurant, it is a lively chef that interacts, with great food. Our chef literally just looked at his order sheet, he couldn't seem to get portions down. Three people order chicken and one vs another had twice as much chicken. 

I ordered a bottle of clear sake and a cloudy unfiltered bottle came. Then the server knew she made a mistake but was trying to "lie" her way out of it. She is telling me that the bottled I ordered is unfiltered, when it is the fifth one down on the list saying clear.  She had no idea on anything related to sake, and her lack of knowledge was very disappointing, especially for a expensive bottle of sake. There need to be an experience there, instead of just filling up everyone's water.

They just opened so the wait is still long... They serve craft ramen. It is a little pricey. I got the most expensive Ramen they currently offer which is CHAMPON* served with 
pork/chicken broth, head-on gulf shrimp, chasyu asado, ginger tempura, scallion, corn, shiitake, sesame.. Priced at $16 to start. When I got the bowl.. I was not impressed. They put 1 slice of pork, a few sliced of shiitake mushrooms, tiny pieces of corn and scallions, noodles and broth. I was excited for the head-on gulf shrimp.. But mine was served without the head which was disappointing. That's what I came there for. I'm Asian.. So I love that stuff! ... When I asked the server, he told me that they somehow just literally changed the menu an hour before I got there.. So they don't serve the shrimp head anymore. Just my luck. Then you have to pay $2 extra for 1 poached egg, $1 for hot sauce.. And extra $ for everything else.... Who charges for hot sauce ? 

Well, all in all, I paid $19 for a small bowl of "craft" ramen I could have made myself... I'll make it even better. 

I might try it again in a few months.. When they get all their ducks in a row.. But in the meantime .. I'll be making delicious craft Ramen at home

I've never been a believer in online reviews, however, I felt the need to create a profile after visiting this establishment. My girlfriend and I just dined here earlier tonight, in celebration of our 5 year anniversery, to see what the fuss was about. Let me tell you...CIROS DELIVERED!

The night started by a knock on a huge wooden door (speakeasy appropriate). The gentleman (which we later found out was the manager) opened the eyehole and was very animated. We gained entry after the password for the evening was presented. He asked us if it was our first time here, and our first time at a speakeasy. He was very accomodating, and really played into the part of the speakeasy.

The cocktails were superb. Im a bourbon drinker and I had the best Old Fashioned Ive ever had. Ive had quite a few Old Fashions in my day as well. My girlfriend ordered a Moscow Mule. Although it did not come in a copper mug, it was still outstanding. After trying the cocktails, I personally had to make my way to the bar to shake the bartenders hand. He was very courteous and gave me the historical run down on both cocktails. I did not know my dining experience would also include a history lesson. Best history lesson ever.

We ordered a few dishes. We had the cheese fondue, chicken and waffles, and beef tartar. the tartar was highly recommended and I can see why. Not the biggest portions but full of such unique flavor and fusion.

Just when we thought the night couldnt get any better, the manager (Eric),   came to our table with 2 glasses of champagne! He really didn't have to, but he said on behalf of himself and the house Happy Anniversery. 

Our dining experience was flawless, and the staff made us feel so welcomed. I highly recommend this establishment to anyone living or visiting in the Tampa area.

This restaurant is conveniently located right across Plaza Frontenac.  My department's holiday luncheon was held here last year which was my very first visit.  The place is big, clean/orderly, but a little too dark inside for my taste.  We had our party in a large room next to the bar area with a nice fireplace and a big TV. It's nice that they actually were able to accommodate about 20+ people, however, we were only assigned 1 waitress (we will further discuss).

The restaurant created a fixed menu for us. I think the person who made the reservations dealt with the menu issue but it was pretty cool because it actually had the company's name and it definitely felt quite special. We played some raffle games and they were nice enough to let us have free use of the space. Appetizers were being delivered to a side table when I arrived and I tried one of each.  We had some Bavarian pretzel bites served with bacon cheese sauce and I believe some potato cakes with accompanying sauce.  Both were quite delicious and freshly made.

This place has a large beer selection, however, while in the process of ordering we were told that some were unavailable. The waitress then brought over a big menu book of drinks. I had a glass of cabernet but did pick a German beer that sounded interesting for my buddy and he said it was pretty good. For my main course, I had Oma's meatloaf served with green beans and mashed potatoes with brown German gravy. It was actually good as far as the taste goes, however, they seemed more like Salisbury steaks than meatloaf. The portion was quite large so needless to say, I ended up with some leftover to take home. We had 2 options for dessert: bread pudding and apple strudel.  I had the bread pudding and thought it tasted fine.  My buddy had the apple strudel and I was curious so I tried a little bit of it.  I don't like apple pies or apple strudel and theirs did not really change my mind.  

Someone in our party did have their order forgotten which was the down part of having only one waitress.  Also, getting a refill on drinks or ordering a new drink proved to be slightly difficult due to only having one person running everyone's order.  Overall, the first experience was fine and slightly successful.

Not long after the first experience, I went back for dinner to try something different and see how this restaurant runs under normal circumstance.  Got seated at the bar side since there didn't seem to be anyone at the time and drink orders were taken right away, water glasses were brought to the table and there were buckets of popcorn for patrons to enjoy.  The personnel by the bar did inform us about the happy hour if you sit in the bar area instead of the dining room.  This time, I wanted to order the wiener schnitzel due to the high praises by some of my colleagues during the holiday party.  The dish tasted good but the sides were nothing to write home about.  They were also 2 small portions of meat which was not what I expected since my lunch portion was quite large.  For dessert, I wanted to try their chocolate molten lava cake which was very good albeit small.  The service was faster than the first time and our waitress was wonderful and very accommodating.  

Would I come back here? I would not discount the possibility of coming back for another happy hour, perhaps.

I adore the Bubble House. Well, more to the point, I adore their bubble tea. I make the trek west just for their syrupy sweet technicolor concoctions chock full of chewy tapioca goodness. I've eaten there a few times and the food was tasty, but more often than not I grab a couple of cups to go. It's the best bubble tea in town.

This place is one of those local gems that has remained special because it remains authentic. No pretense, no hip vibe, just legit local food. There were three in our party and we all had different types of Po' Boys. Everyone was quite pleased with their choices. I had the Shrimp and Oyster Po' Boy, and it was OUTSTANDING. The shrimp was battered and fried just right and the French bread was on point. They have a small bar inside, so I was able to wash my huge sandwich down with an Abita Seersucker Summer Pilsner served up in a heavily frosted goblet. Bam!!

I have had several dining experiences in New Orleans, mostly in the French Quarter and the Garden District. This is the only place where I felt like I was having an experience that one could only have in New Orleans. 

Good stuff at reasonable prices, given the ingredients they use and the amount of food they serve you.

Hubby and I came here with friends for a birthday dinner. The place is nice, but not  what we expected. The restaurant is very noisy and crowded. It's very close to the water, but not the least bit romantic. The food was overpriced and just ok. The staff was friendly. We sat on the first floor and I enjoyed being able to watch the chefs prepare the meals. The overhead music was great. This is a 1 and done spot. It was interesting to experience, but I doubt we'll be returning.

The place was tiny..but super clean and inviting.I love the way it looks,The lettering  of the menus displayed allover look is super cool. I had to order off menu, which caused a Lil grumblings, but you can tell they love food and care about quality.because my Lettuce,Tomato Onion,Pickle sandwhich was really good. With quality produce. The carnivores in family had a hambuger,hotdog.They said it was super yummy.
  They also offer an extensive array of bottled drinks..Vernors,Rc, Ale 8..drinks you cant just cant get anywhere. But it would be nice if they recycled all that glass..
Amazing food! Creative and Delicious. Paradise for vegetarians and vegans.

Good old southern home cooking here people! I am talking fried chicken, smothered cabbage, white beans, gumbo, fried catfish, boudin, just to name some. Best baked bronze tilapia I don't know how they do it but I have yet to taste better baked tilapia. I eat here a lot, maybe as much as once or twice a week. They change up their items some everyday. Good atmosphere, good service, good food, great price and even good music. Places like this are the reason I enjoy eating out. Oh and they only charge 99 cents for drinks, yep 99 cents. Do yourself a favor and just eat here and be disappointed that you never tried it sooner. My famous stamp of approval. STAMP!

I bought take out on a Thursday night ~7PM. I ordered 1 egg roll, fried dumplings, and a shredded pork with garlic sauce at the recommendation of one of these reviews. My favorite part is the fact that their website is easy to navigate and the menu easy to read. However, my review is solely on the food itself.

Egg roll: This was just okay. I've had tastier egg rolls. I wasn't a fan of the filling combination and had to pour duck sauce over it in order to enjoy it. The outside wrapper was crispy, and the second inner wrapper was soft. It has a very overwhelming cabbage taste and you don't get much of a shrimpy taste. 2/5

Fried Dumplings: These were awful. I felt like I was eating russian perogies with mince. The filling was decent, and you get a lot of filling in these dumplings. The dumplings themselves are larger than average in size. However, the pan fried sides of the dough were not crispy whatsoever. The entire thing was soft and doughy. The dough is very very thick, especially in the spots where they crimped the dough together. The dipping sauce was just okay, it was missing fresh scallions and some acidity.  1/5

Shredded pork in garlic sauce: This was awful as well. If you can envision the taste of average chinese food... this dish is certainly below average. It had no flavor whatsoever. I could barely take 5 bites out of it because it was that bad. You don't taste the "garlic sauce", I'm not certain there was any garlic in the dish at all. The vegetable combination lead to an overwhelming cabbage taste (carmelized/overcooked soft red peppers, green peppers, onions). The pork itself wasn't horrible.  This dish tasted extremely mild and lacked flavor that I enjoy in chinese food. On top of that, the white rice that came with it was hard in certain spots and a bit dry.  1/5

Overall, I wanted to like the food here since there aren't many chinese restaurants nearby and I hate driving 20min to pickup takeout. But my experience was not good. It was the first time in several years that I've been truly disappointed in chinese food.

Spent the morning driving, then fishing in the punishing Florida heat, so I needed a cold beverage and a quick bite for lunch. Popped in with my boy to Thee Burger Spot and ordered a frosty Coke and Thee Glazed One.  A life altering bacon cheeseburger served on two Krispy Kreme glazed donut buns. I ate this thing way too fast, and probably could have eaten another four or five of them, but I just finished my one burger and left with my dignity intact. What can I say?  Fire. This thing was cooked perfectly, well seasoned and exploding with flavor. It was like a sweet/savory hand grenade, seriously. Loved the burger, loved the atmosphere, service was prompt and professional. Five stars, two thumbs up, we loved it and will definitely hit this spot next time we're in town!

First time to this establishment. I had a totally different idea of this restaurant when being built and driving by. I thought with the size it would be a real restaurant. It is one step above Wendy's and I probably would have done better going to Wendy's. It is fast food plain and simple.  Maybe a 2 rate as I did not eat the full menu ! Italian beef sandwich was dry. Nothing on it but cheese and peppers. No ah jus. Supposed to be dipped in a gravy. This was not dipped.  French fries are commercial frozen. Stacked up by at least 50 under a warming light waiting to be served. Not even freshly made. Same with the Onion rings.  Chicken pieces are commercial again, frozen out of a box.  The only condiment available was ketchup. I asked for honey mustard, out, blue cheese for salad, also out or does not carry. I am not sure about the rest of the menu. I see cars waiting and waiting in take out. They must be doing something correct, but I did not have it. With so many restaurants out there, I will continue to go to those others and not go back to this one.

I was highly disappointed and underwhelmed. We went here for lunch on a Friday and they were almost literally out of everything. The lady taking our order was pretty embarrassed as well. Its a friday people not a monday or tuesday after a busy weekend. Aside from that every table was dirty and I'll add there was probably 6 empty/ dirty ones out of the 10 they have. Must have been from the big breakfast rush they got who also ate all the food as well. On a positive note the coffee was solid, so that  I would recommened.
Big place.  Lots of beers.  Ok.  Service was pompous for no reason. Slow, etc. I was excited to get here but nah

Having a good dinner tonight. Staff is very attentive and our sushi chef is taking care of us very well. 

We have had service issues here in the past, but tonight they are totally on their A game.

My husband and I went with our 1 year old son yesterday and we were really impressed. The inside was very clean and the menu had a lot of options. There is ice cream, crepes, and other food like tater tots and mozz sticks. My husband got three scoops with a waffle cone and he really enjoyed the flavors. They don't have a ton of flavors to pick from, maybe 12 or so, but they did have a good variety. I had the ore-Oreo rolled ice cream. It was so good and it was like having an ice cream sundae but something different than I'm used to. It was really fancy too. They have an area that you can watch them doing the mixing of the ice cream and roll the ice cream. Our son got a free scoop, we picked vanilla which was yummy! Our son still sits in a high chair and they had two available. I normally dread putting him in it at most places because they always look dirty and gross but not here! It had a nice insert that was very clean and I didn't feel grossed out with anything about the high chair. It was perfectly clean. The seating was very nice. They have options of normal chairs at a table or a booth set up almost with a nice couch setting. The couch was a little low but it was comfy. It was not busy when we went around 4ish but slowly people were coming in and out. They do have some deals like $3off the ice cream snows during their happy hour until 5pm M-F. I think my favorite part was how clean it felt in there. As soon as anyone left the nice young lady working there wiped and cleaned the tables off. The staff was very nice and checked in to see if we needed anything and how it was. We will be going back to try something new next time!

I have probably eaten here a dozen times since moving to the Ft. Ben area! 

Pros: fast and friendly service, great queso, and fantastic food!
Cons: the ground beef is only so so...I recommend the shredded or grilled chicken with meals. 

Overall, the restaurant is festive and clean. It's located in a cool, historic building. The food is great and I'm tempted daily to stop in on my way home from work! Check it out if you are in the area.

I had to call Modo Mio to get a phone number for Monsu, which has moved into the 9th and Christian location that housed Paesano's.

I snagged a table for that night, and ended up sitting between two parties who were both talking about the soft opening, which had coincided with the thundersnow on Wednesday.  Despite the quiet opening, Monsu was packed, with what mostly seemed like either Modo Mio regulars or McAndrew's devotees.  Nothing wrong with either one of those, and there wasn't much wrong with our dinner either.

The pastas were the definite standout; the gnoccolis and ricotta raviolis were great, and for those who are used to the Modo Mio turista menu, these are much larger portions.

The only hiccup came with our check, when the addition didn't quite add up.  Actually, it added up a little too much, not in our favor.  It was fixed quickly, and I've got no doubt that Chef McAndrews will have another hit on his hands.

Best Mexican food EVER!!
Not only is the food amazing, but the service is above and beyond. This place never disappoints from the moment you walk in, to the moment you walk out.
Who would think a Mexican restaurant would have such amazing burgers?! That's not it though, they have the best enchiladas and salsa in town. Such a great variety of food to order from and everything has always came out delicious. Highly recommend

Anyone who rates this below a 5-star went for the wrong reasons. This is NOT a place to go if you are a stuck-up snob who can't eat anywhere that isn't beautiful. The restaurant looks like it was furnished in the early 90s, but WHO CARES! Also, the menu CLEARLY states that all orders are made to order, and to bear with them. The motto, which is true as can be, says "Its Worth the Wait." Because of this I can't bear to listen to people complaining about the time it took for their meal to come.

This food is HOMEMADE, and it is AMAZING! It is homemade to the point that I asked Mamma Jovan where she got the cheese inside my friend's Stuffed Schnitzel, and she said "Oh, I made it." This is above and beyond the call of restaurant duty. It was a minor part of a dish, and it was homemade.

I had the stuffed cabbage, and it was brilliant. The meat inside, pork and beef, was cooked perfectly. It was cooked so perfectly that my lunch companion lamented that he didn't eat beef after tasting the cabbage shell, because he wanted to order it the next time he was there. I was also given half a loaf of homemade bread to take home with me to accompany my leftovers. 

If you have at least an hour to spend at a restaurant, definately go to Jovans. you won't regret it!

I absolutely loved the food and service I received.  We had 3 sushi rolls (habanero tuna roll, coconut shrimp roll and shrimp and lobster roll. Everything was fresh and the rolls were rolled tight and easy to eat. 

We ate the lobster mac and cheese and the macadamia nut chicken. Both were awesome. I'm not a Mac &Cheese person and I might order this as a meal. The macadamia nut chicken was rich and with the marmalade puree it was a great combo. 

Dessert was the "Spiced apple bread pudding". It was big enough to share. It was really good and I can't say more than that. 

The drinks that were ordered were Sam Adams cold snap, tropical Mango Punch, Fiji apple sake and several Kentucky Mule. They were all great. The Kentucky Mule is light and refreshing. I think it is my new summer drink.
Cool spot, definitely in the patio area!  Good food and great service!  Our server was a total Megan Fox look alike - hotness!!  She was really cool!
food was just okay nothing out of this world for the area, there are many other better options, our service was very slow, but at least they acknowledged us. It a trendy spot ! I would go again,
Over priced for what you get. Food was not that great. It's been in business for ever and not sure why. Always seemed to busy at old location. Won't be back
Very good Indian food infact its delicious, good location right in the heart of State Street,  great service and generally a better ambiance than its only rival in SB

Yum yum yummm! I love their whole menu and I want to have it all in my belly. 

As far as the bar menu goes, Whiskey is their thing. If you are like me, you might say, Whiskey? What color is it? Brown-ish maybe? is that what Don Draper drinks? If so, I need to have some so i can be uber awesome. Being that I am not a whiskey connoisseur I was apprehensive when I ordered, but I always like to stick to things that places specialize in. I want to fully embrace their culture and let it live in me. I selected the French 95, because I like French 75s and this drink was a whole 20 numbers higher than that so obviously it will be delicious. I am so happy I presumed the correct notion. The drink was freakin delicious and I could have drank them all night. Hello whiskey, it's me, your new bff. 

I tried both the wings, because I like to compare apples to apples. Here is the verdict. 

American wings: bland, not that flavorful except the bites with the blue cheese and overall a disappointment. 

Korean wings: ding ding ding! We have a winner! These wings are worth having your face covered in kimchi sauce. Full of flavor, spice and everything nice! 

The sweet potato poutine was like butter in my mouth. I don't even think I chewed it. I just let it slide down my gullet like a snake. 

The service was great too. The server knew the menu front and back and offered some great suggestions. Even though it was busy on a Saturday the wait for the table and the food was nonexistent so these folks got all their ducks in a row over here!
We went for brunch and bluegrass while visiting Nashville. The spinach croissant was delicious, and the atmosphere was laid back. I'll definitely be back!

The food was delicious and the atmosphere was very cool.  When we arrived, they brought us 4 difference breads with butter and all were very good.  I ordered fish and chips and my husband ordered the gnocchi and them we finished with the caramel, apple, bourbon bread pudding.  We loved everything that we tasted.

Wait time absurd 20 mins at least drive thru...ridiculous amd its always like this. Food is usually decent sometimes the fries are extra salty but the service is so slow. They do not know how to manage well that usually managers the one running the food they don't have enough staff restaurant is usually clean though
Omg the food there is AMAZING! And also love the self-serve order screens! Just makes things faster and easier
very friendly, the food was bomb! would 100% recommend. although the people that takes you in were unprofessional

I love live music.
I love to be able to breath
Chickie Wah Wah is perfect for both.
What more do I want from a venue? Oh...free food but COME ON!!! That's just asking too much.
It helps that this place is only a few minutes walk from our house. 
Come listen to good music and breath good air...well...as good as it gets. You know that as soon as you are all up and bopping, a hypster who doesn't believe in deodorant because it kills seals or something and who hasn't bathed in months will suddenly think they are your soul mate....

Amazing food amazing service!

Me and my family went here for brunch today and it was outstanding.

I ordered a breakfast dish with the popovers and macadamia sauce and it was Delish.

My brother and my parents are vegetarian and vegan. They all had an amazing experience and commented on how tasty their meals had been. 

Our waitress was really friendly and had great knowledge of all the dishes on the menu!

Thanks everyone

I love to cook and try new recipes by combining additional ingredients to make it my own. Mongolian BBQ is like a playground for me. 

A plethora of fresh ingredients and a creative mind equal a great meal.  Veggies and meats are set out buffet-style to add to your own bowl.  You can pick and choose what you want in your own unique concoction.  Then at the end, there are also oils and sauces you can pick from to finish off your dish. 

Then take it to the cook station where you watch your meal come to life on a huge flat 'Wok'. It is tossed around by the chef with what look like GIANT chopsticks.  After a few minutes on the 'Wok' you are set to experience your own creation. I feel like a proud momma once I taste it and realize I made the perfect meal all on my own!!

Sometimes, the combination you pick may not turn out the best.  If you don't trust yourself in choosing the right ingredients, they do have recommendations posted. They also have a very large buffet with various pre-cooked items.  My advice, don't fill up on those.  

Take a 'Wok' on the wild side and let your Mongolian BBQ freak flag fly!!! Do the BBQ!

If you're looking to eat Italian, there is no need to search for any other place. This is the only Italian restaurant that I will choose to eat. Superb service with even more superb Italian cuisine. Today I had ordered black linguine with shrimp and scallops that were so large and so fresh that I had not had scallops this fresh before. The pasta, there are no words to describe it. Made in house silky smooth  and fresh infused with squid black ink. I will definitely order this dish again. Mangia!

This is the best place to go for roast duck in center city.  The meat is seasoned just right and is still excellent after being refrigerated.  It may be a small store with a questionable store front, but they're specialty is duck, pork, and chicken... and they haven't disappointed yet out of the many times I have shopped there.

Rack of lamb was excellent, the service was remarkable, the ambiance was classical, the deserts were incredible and the wine selection was phenomenal. . A must resturant to visit when you're in the big easy, bring your gold card..

For some reason in 2017 someone decided to change the menu and the dressed hummus has taken a major nose dive. Previously accompanied by roasted red peppers and sundried tomatoes, someone made the horrible decision to substitute these items with cold tasteless cherry tomatoes and similarly tasteless roasted cauliflower, which in no way goes with this hummus. I love my neighborhood Reginelli's and eat there at least once a week, but this is a fail. Not sure why anyone would mess a classic winning item, but I would like to place my plea for the good ol original. Sometimes, change is bad.
Always love stopping in at Arigato Sushi when I'm in town. This time we ordered to go since we had our dog with us. It's just as great as I remembered!
My fiancé and I have ordered delivery from here several times. The food tastes divine! We just moved to the area and decided to try them out. I'd recommend their food to anyone!

Nice experience. Chairs are really comfy, environment is cute and the margaritas are pretty good. Got the mexican street corn nachos and they were delicious. Our server was very sweet and she was quick with bringing us drinks and food. Only giving 4 stars cause we had to send the nachos back the first time since i'm vegetarian and they put the carne on top of the nachos and not on the side.
Authentic New Orleans Sno-Ball experience with some hoot treats like Shrimp Nachos.   Looking forward to trying this place again when in town. Try the Key Lime Pie Sno-Ball flavor with cream.
Got the Bayou Platter and it made for a great lunch. The fried gator is fantastic and the oysters on the half shell are tasty!

Fusion Bowl is a nice laid back spot. This is the second time I have been here. I must say I do love just sitting on the couch. Last time around I got the breakdown from Rico Suave Mel R. on dominoes. 

Last time around I had the beef teriyaki, and this time I had the Japanese udon noodles, chai tea latte, and a nice sample of vanilla ice cream and Vietnamese coffee. All were delicious!

I can't say enough thank you's for the owners of Fusion Bowl. They are very friendly and welcoming! This is a great spot that I will definitely come back to!

This is a new restaurant that rolled out their full menu on Saturday. We are a large party. We ordered and our food took an hour to arrive. It was served in pieces. There were 3 hot meals and 9 salads. It was ridiculous. No apologies and very lacking in service checking on our table.

Best bar-b-q in St. Louis. Big portions and reasonably priced. The only drawbacks are the long lines and limited seating. Of course the long lines are because the food is so great. If you go on a nice weather day, you can use the outdoor seating.

This is a great place to grab a bite before the theater. We stopped in before a show at the Academy of Music and were lucky enough to grab a seat at the bar, despite not having a reservation and it was a busy Wednesday night. Loved the view, being able to watch all the delicious dishes being prepared. We wanted to sample every one of them!

We started with some shared apps.  The Butternut Squash Arancini (rice balls) were great, very light and delicious.  The Sweet Potato app was good, but not my favorite.  I think there are better choices on the menu.  We then shared the Tagliatelle with Duck Leg, and that was also excellent.  None of these dishes were heavy or overly filling, and that would have likely been enough for us.  But the pizza looked excellent, so I wanted to give that a shot.  So we ordered a Margherita pizza, to eat a piece here and then take the rest home.  And it did not disappoint.

The service was pretty good.  We had plenty of time to make our show.  The waiter checked on us frequently (until we wanted the check and to leave. . .don't you just hate that?).  But all in all he was good, and made good suggestions on what to try.  We'll definitely go back here for a pre-theater dinner.

This place is not a Diner, not Drive In, and not a Dive. It is a hole in the wall in an old shopping mall.  If you are looking for fancy this is not the place to go.

But WOW the food is so good. On my first and only visit so far, I got two pupusus and I was not disappointed. The prices are really good and the lady who helped me (I think the owner) was incredibly helpful. They have your typical bar of pickled jalapenos and salsas.

I look forward to my next visit.



20/3
This is probably my favorite Chinese restaurant in town! Very authentic! The owner is very friendly as well!
AMAZING SERVICE and AMAZING FOOD. You can bring your pups outside to eat which is wonderful ! This is the place to go on Mass Ave !

We were looking for somewhere we haven't been before and decided upon the Purple Parrot at the Atlantis for lunch. It's located near the bottom of the escalators leaving the skyway. We were told it was a 30 minute wait so we put our name on the list and decided to try our luck. It's nice because they announce your name over the loud speaker in the casino area just outside the restaurant. 

After quadrupling the cash we put into the slot machines, we waited closer to the entrance and they called our name in a short time.

We were seated in a half circle booth and our drink orders were promptly taken.  The menu is extensive with all day breakfast options available. My wife was happy to see a pho option and I decided on a burger.

Our meals arrived in a timely fashion and looked really good. The western burger was huge. Everything was very tasty.

Kathy was an awesome server and took really good care of us even though they were very busy.

Overall it was a good experience.

A beautiful restaurant with top notch service and hearty rich food!

Ambience: 5/5
My boyfriend and I visited during Christmas season, so the restaurant was beautifully decorated and classy. I also liked the open kitchen layout since it was fun to watch the cooks and it also added a fun lively vibe to the date night. Service was great. We had multiple wait staff who had different duties (ex: water refilled, bread server, server, etc). During your dinner, you will be helped by at least 4 different people.

Food: 4/5
I decided to make a reservation for Emerils since my boyfriend grew up watching his show, so I knew he'd enjoy the sentiment. We ordered the following:

Emerils shrimp: very tasty, but I wish the shrimp were bigger 

Seafood gumbo: this was yummy and not too salty. I'd recommend this. There were mussels in there, which were a nice touch as well!

Hanger steak: good flavor, but a bit chewy

Andouille crusted drum fish: this was executed well. The fish was delicate, flakey, and moist. The crust was flavorful as well, and I can see why there's a lot of hype to this dish. My only complaint is that it's pretty rich with both the crust and fried string potatoes underneath the fish. I wish it came with rice or steamed veggies instead to cut through the richness. But I get it, that's New Orleans cooking! (Can't help that I miss my California LA cuisine haha). In sum, I'd recommend this dish. 

Banana cream pie: A must! It's a a beautiful dessert that isn't too sweet or heavy. The banana cream is deliciois and the Graham cracker crust is crisp and thin. Don't miss out on this one!

After my first review, Tyler (GM) invited me back to make things right. I came with my husband, his brother, and his brother's girlfriend. This time our experience was pretty stellar. We got the burgers again; this time they were juicy, delicious, and cooked to order. Tyler talked to us for a while, and he told us they were about to put out a new potato salad. He let us try it, and we all loved it. We also tried the fried green tomatoes, which I thought were cooked perfectly. Their iced tea needs to be stronger, but otherwise we were pleased with both the food and the service. We will definitely be back when we're in the area!

This restaurant is one of my best memories of New Orleans.  With no reservations - the line is long to get in.  For a good reason.  Fortunately, we can hop across the street and purchase a bottle of wine while we lollygag outside waiting for a table to open inside Lola's.  Favorites: family style paella and the lamb is incredible.  My friend had the soup with almonds - I'm sorry I don't recall the name - but it was delicious.  As was the sangria.  This is where I have my "last supper" with my friends who are locals to that neighborhood.  Save the best for last.  :)
This is the worst Little Caesar's I've ever been to. The staff is rude and I wouldn't trust any food that came from this location. New ownership and management are needed.

All I ordered was cold sesame noodles and an egg roll. Seems hard to disappoint. The egg roll was good, but teeny tiny. Unfortunately the cold noodles were 80% lettuce and carrots and 20% noodles. The container wasn't even full. Not worth it.
We love all of the appetizers! Fried chicken hummus with their hot bread is a must try! Great atmosphere and the service is wonderful.
This place is a must try!  You'll love everything about Kimmies, from the staff to the food.  One word... Pleasantly "full" of love!

COOL place. The beer wall is great and well organized so it's easy to navigate. I love being able to use the bracelet to pour anything from a sample to a half glass to a full pour and not have to commit to one beer. Service has always been good despite this restaurant being very popular. We did get seated at a dirty table once, which was awkward, but the hostess made it right pretty quick. I had the meatball and mozzarella pizza and it was absolutely awesome. Everyone loved their pizzas from a simple pepperoni to the Eggs Benny. I look forward to bringing guests here often!

Inexpensive and overrated, but I don't want them to close hence 4 stars. It's not bad; there's just so much better out there. I'm not a fan of the ambiance in their dining room. Last time I was In there, it seemed kind of tight.
Love this place! The cold pressed juices are healthy and tasty. Finally tried the food and I am obsessed with the vegetarian cheesesteak quesadillas. Can order on line and deliver by Door Dash.
This is my place for avocado bobas. Very worth the value and the shaken beef is yummmz

So...  have been going to Hellas for over 10 years.  Used to love this place as it used to be on par with Greek islands, Parthenon etc. in Chicago as that is where I am from.  Unfortunately, something changed since we were there in April.  The portions accross the board are noticeably smaller.  The Greek salad used to be served on a large glass platter, now it is served only on a large white serving plate approx 1/2 the size.  One of my daughters had the scallops and the other had the broiled octopus.  Both of which were a little more than half the serving size we had before.  I ordered the leg of lamb and not to mention a small serving size it was as tough as beef jerky.  We have spent over two thousand dollars a year at this restaurant every year and will never go back again.  So disappointing as we used to look forward to this meal every time we visit family in the area.  I am writing this while having a turkey sandwich as I am still hungry from not being able to eat the "lamb" that I had ordered.

Second visit here yet the same poor service! The food is really good local home cooking but the service is terrible; from the owner to the wait staff. If you want a good meal but treated like crap, then this is the perfect place. Me and my party of six won't be returning - ever!
I love this place. I'm gluten free and they take it very seriously. Their tofu green curry is my go-to.

Last night we dined here as a group of four. We chose the chef tasting menu after the waitress heavily suggested it was the best option. Halfway through our main entree, another waitress told us our table was needed for another reservation so we needed to finish quickly or box up our meal. We were still waiting for dessert, had another bottle of wine to drink, and were never offered coffee. The food was okay. For an Italian restaurant we weren't impressed with the pasta. Incredibly disappointed in the service.

Friendly staff, great assortment of bagels and coffee! For those with lactose intolerance, they do offer oat milk! Perfect place to grab a bagel and coffee in the morning and sit outside in their patio area if the weather permits.

E+Rose has food for all occasions, as long as all of those occasions are living longer and healthier.  I go here every day for a smoothie, soup, or a wrap.  Usually take some home also.  In a city with very few solid vegan options, this is a bright spot.

Wonderful dinner last night.  Great menu, service and ambiance.
Been here a few times, and has never disappointed us.
Highly recommend for a date night or special occasion - though, also great for just anytime, too.
Kudos!

Being from New York, it is hard to find good fish in Nashville. Fin & Pearl has done it. Everything was superb including the octopus, tuna poke, branzino, and beef tenderloin. Friendly service and a fun environment.
