I had been trying to try this place for some times.  I have seen the pictures of their specialty meals posted by several friends and knew that I had to see this for myself.  However, their hours were not very convenient to us getting to try it.  Plus, we knew how busy it is on a regular basis so we were trying to find a good time.  Finally, we had the opportunity and took it.  The place was indeed very small but thanks to a friend who is always early we did not have to wait long before we sat.  The service was not very good. The waitstaff all ran between the inside and outside tables and it was very chaotic and confusing who was serving us.  

The food for our group of 6 was very slow to come out and came out at very staggered times.  The fried food was average.  I believe that this did not really stand out from the fried seafood anywhere else in the city.  The crawfish was had by one person in our party and he stated that it was good. I enjoyed the shrimp and corn bisque.  It was a white base not a seafood base as I have had in other places but the large shrimp that were obviously out of the shrimp boil in the back were excellent and added a great flavor.  Finally, the dish had been waiting months for.... the Tuna Volcano!  It was exactly like the pictured and better tasting than I had imagined.  I am not usually not a fan of crab salad but this was excellent and fresh.  The tuna was well done and the addition of the shrimp and sauces made the dish out of this world!  

We will be back.  But I know that we will be looking to go earlier or later in the night so that we do not have to deal with the chaos of the busy time.

Stopped in to grab food to go before leaving town. Nice concept, and I love the selection of house made meats. I found my Gambino sandwich (house meats + herb vinaigrette) to be a bit underwhelming for $12. It didn't look as big as the muffaletta, and while the bread and meat were pretty good, it felt like it needed a more flavorful sauce to tie it all together. It's like it was just missing that umami component. Seems like I ordered the wrong sandwich. However, I also got the mac & cheese, which was absolutely amazing. Creamy, rich, with a little bit of a kick.
The best hoagie spot in Philly!  You won't be disappointed.
I would not recommend this place they've had bugs in their food and if it's busy they will not make any drinks. Do not expect to get boba if the line has more then 3 people.

Not bad for a late night Chinese take out joint. I each with foods that we vegetarian instead of vegetarian versions of meat dishes. Order was ready quick after 9 pm.

Vegetarian fried rice was good. Tofu with vegetables was with brown sauce and veggies. Also good, but just because it's vegetarian food doesn't mean it's healthy. Must've been a good amount of sugar in the sauce to make it so tasty.

Would order pick up from here again

Delicious, hot and crispy! Yum! I almost walked on by them, but a friendly patron had just finished her pizza and told me about Nicoletta's. That they are from New York City and make everything fresh from original Italian recipes. My mouth was watering as she described the crispy crust and all the different tasty dishes she has tried. Her recommendation sold me. My recommendation to the owner is to make sure this type of information is coordinated in your signage and marketing. I realize you just opened. I hope you have plans to make the most of the white wall to the left to tell your story to drive your business. You deserve it! I love mushrooms so I enjoyed the Tartufata pizza with prosciutto cotto, truffle cream, and mozzarella. If you are at the KOP mall, definitely try them out.

Drove an hour to pick up take out from here tonight, got the 2 entrees from here and drove home with the sense that our order was correct the first time. Drove the hour ride home just to open up the incorrect order and then called to figure out if they could refund or give new food. We were not going to drive back to philly for one meal so they agreed to replace the entire order. We drive the hour to the restaurant the second time just for us to be greeted by 4 workers with no respect. Claiming we hadn't called and they could NOT refund us for the incorrect meals.... honestly didn't cade about the money at that point in the situation but they continued to act as we were the problem and could not even refund or replace the incorrect food that their disrespectful staff messed up.
We will never be going back due to the lack of
respect and responsibility.

I visited this place earlier in the week. My food was pretty good and I received a good portion of food. It was enough for two meals. The service was superb. The owner was very personable. My pound cake was very tasty.

We visited Retreat while our kids were in town. There was no crowd because it was the afternoon. It is very small so I can only imagine how loud it gets at night when they are busy. 
We ordered cocktails and lunch. The drinks were tasty but a bit overpriced for me. We tried the Farm house burger,  pork and fennel Flatbread,  mac n cheese and the poutine. The Burger was worth the trip and I highly recommend it. The mac n cheese was tasty but nothing special. The Flatbread had great flavor and I liked the dressing on the greens. The poutine, that came highly recommended,  was a real disappointment. No distinct flavor to speak of and it was way too soupy. I asked the waitress if that was how it was supposed to be and she said yes. I returned it and she took it off our bill. 
Our waitress was very nice and the food is hit or miss. Nice neighborhood bar though.

I was very impressed with our wait staff,  however, we made a reservation but had to wait 15 minutes after. The food was good and prices were expected. Overall we had a great experience, but it might be a while before we return with their "reservation" policy.
The skate wing with parmesan broth is an experience not to be missed.

What an experience. I came here a few weeks ago after finding them on Yelp and had one of the most wonderful brunch experiences ever. Aside from the food and drinks (which we'll get to later), the staff and atmosphere of the restaurant was so great. As soon as we walked in, we had multiple people greet us, tell us about the process here of ordering and find us a perfect table outside. Even when bringing our food and drinks, our waiter was so pleasant. 

Now onto the food, we got a giant Bloody Mary and 2 for 15 dollars bellinis. The Bloody Mary was good but wow, the peach purée bellinis was definitely a huge hit. 

Overall, this was a great experience for us and I'll definitely be back!

Sonny's was great, just what a Philly cheese steak should be.  Service was fast, place was clean and the cheese steak with cheese wiz was perfect.  We also tried the cheese fries and onion rings which were good also.  Cheese wiz over provolone hands down.

We just moved to town and were looking for a good authentic Mexican spot. I'm sad to say that Que Pasa didn't even come close. I know this area isn't known for its Mexican food, but I was at least hoping for freshly made food. The tamales were clearly store bought and reheated. The rest of the food was either canned food or reheated from a few days ago. We will not be returning.
The best pizza in Quakertown!   We get take out from Frank's at least once a week and always find there pizza or pasta to be excellent.

Once you step inside you are immediately greeted with that southern hospitality which is terrific. There is lots of seating inside which is great, and helps the waiting time go fast! I ordered the crawfish and grits which is served with a slow cooked egg. This was my first time trying crawfish, and I wouldn't want to try it for the first time other than New Orleans. I also got the fried chicken sandwich to split wit a friend, and it was delicious. 

The cocktails here are on point as well. I suggest getting a frozen cocktail you will not be disappointed! The bakery offering looks to good to turn down. I ordered the banana bread after I was clearly full, but I'm glad I did it was amazing!

Got the Gaucho steak which was good but would have been better if it was served with the chimmichurri sauce as indicated on the menu. They were out which I wasn't told upon ordering. The red beans were old and tasteless, and the wait staff wasn't very capable. Basically, a less than impressive performance for a good chain. Sorry that it took the place of Mizado which was excellent in all categories.

Me and my husband tried vijaywada biryani and gobhi manchurian, good taste.
The gobhi manchurian sauce nice and spicy just the way I like .crispy cauliflower Florets 
Vijawada Biryani spicy and different kind biryani than dum biryani. I like the taste of it. 
This Indian restaurant has unique flavors must try

We came to this location on Mother's Day with the impression given to us that it is one of the best ones in the area for many reasons.  It did not live up to all the hype we were given.

We were seated right away, which was great with our group of 10.  Drinks were promptly brought out and rolls presented.  Ordering for a group our size has its challenges, the first one being that my MIL wanted the potato soup that they are known for and apparently on Mother's Day they were not serving it (but they serve it every other day of the year).  Once that was figured out, we all got our orders in and everyone was happy with the loads of sauce that each entree was given (one of the hypes we had heard about).  Everything was eaten up as it arrived hot and ready to eat.

The waitress was super nice, and did the best she could with the loads of questions and people she had to deal with at our table.  Everything was boxed up perfectly at the end, and she even threw in a box of rolls.

Big fan of Bar Hygge!

I have visited twice, once for dinner and another time just for drinks. The first time was for dinner with my brother and his girlfriend when they were visiting Philly. The friendliness of this establishment was the first thing we all noticed. We arrived in the evening, I think it was about five minutes before 11:00pm. As is the case with most bar/restaurant combinations, the kitchen isn't open as late as the bar. The first question we asked before even being seated was if they were still serving food. The hostess checked the time and said that they close the kitchen at 11:00 but they would still serve us. The owner or manager overheard our question and immediately came over to say that he would notify the kitchen not to shut down so that we could place an order. After he walked away, the hostess told us that he makes sure that if they say the kitchen is open at a certain time that it stays open. I appreciate this since a lot of places try to close before the actual posted time. We already had a good impression and we hadn't even sat down yet.

They have a dining room, a lounge area with sofas, and bar seating. We chose the dining room since we were eating and were seated at a nice half circle booth. We quickly checked the menu and ordered Hygge Frites and Beer Steamed Mussels as appetizers. Then I chose a Clam Strip Po Boy and the other two ordered a Grass-Fed Beef Burger and a Pork Chop. The fries were very good and came with both ketchup and gremolata mayo (herb mayo). The mussels were also quite good and came with a big piece of a baguette for sopping up the broth. My po' boy sandwich was delicious with super crispy clam strips on top of buttery bibb lettuce and a soft hoagie roll topped with what looked like house-made pickles. One of the best po' boys I have ever eaten! The burger was a nice thick burger covered with melted cheese and had the most perfectly pink center ever seen in a burger. We all tried a bite of this burger and it was fantastic. I will definitely be ordering it for myself on a future visit. The pork chop, while still good, was honestly the item I was least impressed with. It was topped with a blueberry mustard seed compote and while I liked the creativity of mixing mustard seeds into the blueberry, it was still a bit too sweet for me to enjoy on top of a pork chop. Overall, the food was impressive and delicious.

Beer from the in-house Brewery Techne is available and I ordered multiple during both visits. While not every beer was a standout, some of them were really good. My favorites so far are the Kickin' Ash and Gristy Business. The Kickin' Ash is a German-style smoked lager that I really enjoyed and am absolutely hoping is still available on my next visit. Delicious smokey flavor in a easy drinking lager. I loved it! Gristy Business was a tasty IPA with more grain flavor than a typical IPA. Lemon Meringue IPA was another good IPA with some nice citrus flavor. Perkuno's Hammer is a Baltic porter which was decent but just not as good as others I have tried in the same style. Exaggerator is a doppelbock that was my least favorite. It was quite sweet and really malty and I'm starting to think that maybe this style just isn't for me. 

I highly recommend visiting Bar Hygge for food and beer and will definitely be returning many more times.

Fun to play pub poll and trivia Tuesday's and Wednesday's 
Food is great and staff is awesome 
Only Shuffleboard in town 
Highly recommended

I am normally not a fried chicken fan but I am noticing we are having more and more places in town where it is appearing up on the menu and has truly made me a convert.  I had read multiple reviews about this place so thought it was time to head over and I was fortunate enough to have my foodie friends join me..

First recommendation.......this place tends to have a long wait on the peak nights on the weekends so I recommend downloading the No Wait app on your phone.  It is a free app that allows you to get in line well ahead of time so that you can literally walk in and be seated without the hassle for waiting for hours.  

In our case, when I put our name in at 6 p.m. before I had left home, it had showed close to a 2-3 hour wait with 13 groups ahead of us.  Therefore, our group decided to have a drink first at one of the nearby establishments (Sasha's on Shaw) before we headed over.  That was one of the best moves we made as they always serve up great cocktails, beer, wine, and snacks.  

Once the No Wait app indicated that we there were only 3 groups ahead of us which was right around 8 p.m., we headed over the restaurant which was only a half mile away.  Parking is limited mostly to street on Tower Grove with a few spots just east of the building.  I was lucky enough to grab one of those spots.

When you enter the place, it does remind you a walking into a cafe in the heart of the Delta that you happened upon during a road trip.  It is set in a small building that I think used to be a auto garage/gas station.  Walls are whitewashed with some additional unfinished beams as well and the seating is all in unfinished wood as well.  There is also a bar along the east wall that is stacked to the gills with whiskey, scotch, and other spirits.

As we walked in, our hostess greeted us, checked us in on the No Wait app, and showed us to our table within maybe 10 minutes of arriving.  After perusing the menu, beer and whiskey drinks were the order of the day, we got our beverage order in first.  They do have several local beers on top (Urban Chestnut is well represented), many in cans, local sodas and beverages, but they have quite an extensive whiskey and scotch selection list plus a few cocktails that are infused with them as well.  I had Maker's Mark which is always a good standby.  One in our group had one of their whiskey drinks, Gold Rush, which was outstanding.    

Once our drinks were settled, we went to the business of ordering the food.  We ordered the boiled peanut hummus and the bread basket.  The hummus was great and came with a small amount of olive tapenade in the middle and a few peppers around sides and we ended up having plenty of pita bread to go with it.  The bread basket was a great choice as well......two kinds of biscuits and two kinds of cornbread with up to 3 types of butter/jams that you can pick to go with it.  We selected the Molasses-Pecan and the Honey-Lemon butters and the Strawberry Blueberry preserves.   The preserves were great along with the Honey Lemon butter.  The Molasses-Pecan was just a little too sweet but still a good accompaniment.  

Now onto the main course.....the fried chicken was amazing.  The outside was crispy but not greasy and flavored very well.  But what was great was that the chicken was not dry but moist and seasoned well on the inside.  We also did get an assortment of sides (if you do the half chicken or whole chicken from their menu, 1 or 2 sides come with the group.  Otherwise, they are a la carte if you do individual chicken pieces).  I admit that I have an unhealthy obsession with mac and cheese.  However, I wasn't overly impressed with theirs....the sauce was too runny and never seemed to thicken up as it cooled.  I did get to sample the sweet potatoes and homemade chips.....both hit a home run out of the park.  We also ordered their mashed potatoes and it is my understanding those were great as well.

There was a little confusion initially with the sides when they brought them out but that was resolved quickly.  By the time we got to the end, we were stuffed.  When the hostess mentioned about dessert, although all looked tempting, we originally said no.  But just as we were getting ready to head out, she decided she would bring over their banana pudding for us to share......it was indeed amazing.

Overally, we enjoyed our dining experience but the one thing they need to work on is perfecting the sides......some did well, some not so much.  But definitely it is a place worth checking out.....
You can split pancake orders and get two kinds. So why wouldn't you? Tennessee Ham? Yes please! Punny sayings about pancakes, you got it. A line worth standing in? For sure

I really enjoy coming to circles. The menu is your typical bar food menu. During my visits, the crowd was mainly couples although there were a few "girls night out" groups as well. We usually arrive around sunset and there is always a wait. Never longer than 30 minutes and there is a waiting section with comfy seat.  Speaking of seats, if you have a full tushy like me, the little  orange wrought iron seats may not be very comfortable for you. They're usually located along the pier. The gray/silver seats are much more comfortable. It's nice to watch the boats come and go. Very nice scenery. Two negatives:  Our Server did not wear a mask nor did he keep adequate distance. I also witnessed him in the prep area as the only employee with no mask on as well while preparing food. Not cool at all.  The other negative is the allowance of animals. Dogs shaking their hair next to where you're eating is not sanitary. The atmosphere is too crowded and tables are too close for dogs to be allowed. One older gentleman allowed his dog to come directly up to our table and start sniffing our legs. I am a dog lover but not everyone is. Dogs should not be allowed where an abundance of people are dining.

Very small local joint within walking distance of East Beach. It wraps around the batting cages, which makes a nice show to battle your friends or even people watch others!

I would suggest to park on the street as there are only about 8 parking spots for both the batting cages and east beach tacos combined. And you're not allowed to park next door at the Habit. But it's an easy walk across the train tracks and then you won't have to worry about blocking traffic trying to get in and out of the small lot. 

I would recommend getting the "triple play" as this allows you to mix and match three tacos of your choice! I personally got the Bahn Mi, Spicy Shrimp, and Ahi Tuna! Very delicious and all so different. In the past I have also tried the Carnitas and Carne Asada. Honestly there is no wrong decision because I haven't heard one bad thing about them. I would also suggest the chips and guacamole. Always made fresh and you just can't stop eating them once they are in front of you! So addicting!

This place is worth the trip alone for that truffle egg toast! My only suggestion would be to dress the bed of arugula...sure, the egg yolk helps but I think the greens are missing some oil or lemon at the very least. I also had the asparagus salad which was a great size to share. A bit predictable in terms of flavor, but very hearty with beans, artichoke hearts, tomatoes, lots of pine nuts and toast. Great beer and wine selection - although, am I crazy or was there no rose? In any case, I'll definitely be back to try more of their small plates, cheese and beer. Sizes and prices align perfectly. Lots of options for meat eaters and vegetarians.

Kind of small in here - probably not good for groups eating but better for couples or maybe up to four people if you can snag some seats. 

The host at the door was the sweetest!
The waitress forgot our appetizers and then my grandma's BBQ wrap was so spicy she couldn't eat it.  Food over priced for the quality...
Love many things about Pizza Domenica.  Just one request, please.  Bring back the White Clam Pizza.  PLEASE!

Been to Stateside 4 times, first 3 times drinks only,  dinner with last visit.  The space is small but decor and vibe are spot on.  During summer months, the huge windows open up and you're seating from outside at the bar.  We stopped in for a drink after dinner at Le Virtu.  Had a whiskey sour and a boulevardier.  Loved them both.  Their cocktail game is solid.  The bartenders were friendly but really didnt engage us but it was busy and it was a cocktail hit and we all know how that goes, ok, maybe not all of us.   All in all service and cocktails are solid.  Last visit we decided on dinner.  I thought dinner was ok.  Nothing bad but nothing great.   I'll still stop in at Stateside for my night caps.

Got #1. Tomato, Whole Milk Mozz with sausage and mushroom; #2. Swiss chard, Calabrian cream, old gold. Such good pizza! Have been wanting to try for a while and was definitely worth the wait. Definitely order ahead!!

Really yummy. Loved this sandwhich and was craving bagel and lox. Definitely hit the spot and would go back again :)
Their coffee is very tasty and outdoor deck is a great vibe to sit outside with a friend or three as well!
The people are also very friendly too
Wine list is good and decor is beautiful,  Service was very poor. Our waitress didn't know anything about the menu and she was less than attentive.

May 2016. This restaurant has shut down.

The rib eye sandwich was tasty. Their fish and chips are delicious, lightly battered. The jalapeño cheese dip is very good. They have great nightly specials.
Being a brand new restaurant they still have some improvements to make. However, the service is good and friendly.
For the night life, the other half of the restaurant offers live entertainment and dancing.

May 2016. This restaurant has shut down.

I ordered from here through GrubHub and they never showed up. BUT...

They reached out to me via Messenger, and sent my my original order on the house. (I of course tipped the driver well in cash.)

They made the situation right. Can't recommend highly enough.

I would say this pizza place has its charms in terms of decor and selection. By far the most tasty slice is the diavalo and the potato pizza. The only reservation I have is that it gets redundant and almost salty at times. This business model has a selection of pizzas out for display and they will reheat the pizza upon ordering. My preference is something straight out of the oven made to order. There's something missing in this pizza in terms of delicious for myself. I think it might not be the most tasty, but the best looking. You should try this place out for the selection.

I have also tried the restaurant option on the other side. Try it out too and have some of their deserts. I wasn't the most impressed but check it out just in case.

The heat didn't feel like it was on and I run hot. The chips are tri-colored and not even cooked onsite. I recognize they are complimentary but would've preferred to have paid for warm and fresh ones.

The menu has no descriptions... eg what's on the nachos...what do the fajitas come with. Had to ask. Didn't ask about the chorizo corn chowder but do have to state why would you purée it all including the meat. That's not a chowder and I wouldn't have ordered if I had known. It tasted only of celery and made my date taste because the texture looked sketchy. Still paid for it despite not eating and sending back. At first didn't think I got the right soup. His lobster bisque had no lobster and I'm raised in Maine...that's wrong but guess you get what you pay for.

Grilled calamari appetizer was cold when served. Dinner was pretty unappetizing. He had the Mexican special which consisted of enchilada, quesadilla, baby chimi, and tamale. I watched him taste and just move food on the plate, not in his mouth after he tasted each item.

I got flank steak and chorizo fajitas-not worth the price. Tacqueria Felix flank steak fajitas were less and far better quality. The tortillas were weird too... almost as if they were over cooked in a microwave. My meal was luke warm at best. The amount of 'things they give' to build your fajita are enough for one tortilla. I paid ~$8 in sides which doesn't bother me but at $19 for fajitas at least include enough to match the 3 weird tortillas. 
Margaritas were meh so glad we didn't get a pitcher. Martinis a lot better but no price in the menu.

I can fairly say our server was nice but nothing driving me to go back and spend $120 thinking I need to hit chipotle on the way home.

This place is really nice. There's one area with the bar, and another section for more formal dining setting.

Mushroom soup: highly recommended. It has a lot of chopped mushroom.

Crab Salad: pretty big size and fresh. A lot of crab meat 

Crab cake sandwich: really delicious. Pretty big and all are crab meat . Not overly seasoned. 

Key lime pie: beautiful charred meringue, really good and not overly w.

Great place for brunch, drinks, and snacks! Big fan of their cornbread - it's so moist and perfect drizzled with honey.
BBQ shrimp toast was quite delicious as well.
Their fried chicken and sandwich also hits the spot without being too heavy. The biscuits were flaky, the fried chicken crunchy and not greasy at all, and it came drizzled with Tabasco honey which gave it the perfect amount of kick.

They also had many amazing sounding desserts (cookies and milk looked great!) But was too full to try them. Also have a number of cookies and pastries that you can take to-go!

Great Pho . All the ingredients were fresh. I ordered the chicken Pho and egg rolls to go. The parts of the dish were packed seprately and the server told me how to put them together when I got home so that I could have an authentic Pho experience. It is LARGE. I had to use one of my mixing bowls to put it all together. But it was good, I will get the Pho again. Egg rolls had ingredients I couldn't identify. It tasted good but will probably skip them in future.
I went there and had the Gyro and it was excellent, probably the best in town. Personal service, friendly and comfortable atmosphere, I will dine here again for sure.

Absolutely fantastic service! We got a dozen donuts and a half dozen bagels. Everything was fresh, delicious, and very inexpensive. Will definitely be back soon to try the coffee and sandwiches that I've read so much about on here :-)
Good, authentic food  in a big restaurant. Very  friendly service. A big plus is the live band every night.
Excellent corned beef and pastrami sandwiches. Was probably he best I have ever had. Fast service also and friendly waitresses.
They have very weird hours which is odd giving the fact that they have been at their same location for over a year now. I had the food it was mediocre at best.

Bagels are very good and service exceptional. Of course, I'm a local customer so they see either me or my partner at least once a week for a breakfast bagel sandwich or bagels. My partner likes his egg sandwich well done so they know how to make it when I say his name and it's right every time! Great local place, tables inside and a couple outside too. Always have specials like free coffee and a "bagel club" so you earn points towards free sandwiches and cream cheese.

Square 1682 was a last minute decision on a cold Sunday night in Rittenhouse Square.  I am so happy I made the choice, well my dinner companion did.  I had the custom blend burger and fries.  The burger was done to perfection.  It is rare for me to gush over a burger but I am GUSHING! The burger was seasoned and cooked well and the fries were just an added bonus.  I also had the kale salad which was good.  I would definitely return here for the burger.

We visited little octopus last night. The ambience is great along with the food and drinks! My friend (who is pregnant) ordered the steak. She asked if she could have it slightly more cooked than medium rare. The waitress replied that they would not change it for her because the it's the "chef's preference." We asked her to double-check and explain the situation. 
She returned and said that he said no.
To me I don't think cooking a steak a little longer for a pregnant lady with a queezy stomach is that much to ask. 
To me this seems slightly pretentious and honestly was a turn off. We probably won't be revisiting.

Simply love and frequent as much as possible when visiting NOLA.

Chips are fresh & tasty served with delicious queso and can be included with a meal of burritos, tacos, quesadilla...pick your favorite style.

Margaritas...hello friend insert loopy smiley face...;-)

Tried this place yesterday, nothing special, overrated and overpriced, service was very very slow, wait forever to get a roll, everybody was in a slow mode, won't go back, there is so many sushi place that way better then here.

By far the worst dining experience that I have ever experienced. I would not encourage my worst enemy to visit this establishment and here's why: 

To begin, the waiting staff had bad attitudes and did not want to serve our party. They were very short, rude and unpleasant. It appeared our server had a preconceived notion regarding the party that I was with, whom by the way was comprised of all persons of color. However, we continued our dining experience. Later, one member from our group overheard a conversation between two servers negatively talking about our group. Mind you, this group is comprised of doctors, lawyers, nurses, educators, entrepreneurs, and business professionals. Not that it matters but that is what happens when you believe black and brown people cannot spend money in your establishment. What Mesh reminds us that the Confederate South is not only still alive, but very much present on Mass Ave. 

We have heard a lot of negative things about the experiences of persons of color on Mass Avenue but we believed those to be in the past. Unfortunately, this is not the case. The Assistant Manager refused to allow more than 25 people into the restaurant, requiring that we needed to have a reservation! Now, last time I checked, Mesh was not by reservation only. It does not even say anything about it on the website. The manager informed us that they don't cater to groups more than 12 people when in fact, you can use Open Table to reserve a party of 20 people. Yes, we had a party of no more than 30 people, but were told that we could not have more than 25. 

There were five guests who were refused service and were not allowed to enter into the establishment. Treated like criminals when bringing business to this place. Later, we find that we were characterized as "people who don't tip" and "people who wanted free drinks." Are you kidding me?! 

The manager then decides to tell his wait staff to "Call the 'Po Po' on them." The bottom line here, we were a group who decided to have brunch at Mesh. Not believing that it would be such a difficult task to eat and commune in the same dining space. Furthermore, there were 5 booths and 3 tables that surrounded us. Management told us, they were reserved. We were there from 11:15 AM - 12:45 PM (not one table was used during this experience).

Finally, this place is not a good place if you're in town visiting. Their treatment of patrons is despicable. Never, ever, have I been told to leave from an establishment and had the police called on my party. Unbelievably nasty experience and the Assistant Manager could have chose to handle this matter in a different way. 

I can only imagine what he told the General Manager about our party. Fortunately, everyone has an experience and can share with others. 

Beautiful place but the people are not nice nor welcoming.

Went there today, staying at the Ritz Carlton, so I took a little walk. Went in to ask for directions to somewhere else, and was swept away by awesome menu of items. Wound up getting a black beans and mango burrito, oh my God deliciousness!! All employees were super friendly, and some of the customers were very helpful to me as I am from out-of-town. I would go here every day if I lived in this town it was fabulous!!

I have been going to Iron Abbeys for years. Service used to be great, and just recently the customer service has began to be absolutely HORRIBLE!!! Last couple of times I been there the same Host (the guy who always wears a bootie) never greets us and and just ignores you when you walk in, and when he does acknowledge you he is very ignorant and rude!! Also servers have been taking forever to come over and greet you and take your order for drinks or food!! First time this happened I figured they might have been short staffed, but it has happened the past 3 times I have gone there!! Only reason I continue to go there is because they have a great beer selection!!

Service was fine, even good. Business lunch, AYCE sushi with a large sake. Was pretty sticker shocked at the sake price at $10 for lunch, should have asked. The cost on a large sake is roughly a dollar, so pretty much a giant rip off. 

Anyway, sushi I would put between medioce and subpar. This is the issue with a lot of AYCE sushi situations, but I was expecting far better from Oceano. Specifically asked for my eel to be hot and crispy, and it was cold and mushy. Gross. 

But this request is almost always messed up no matter where I go for some reason. Positive note, clam chowder is included and it was pretty decent for west coast CC. 

Paying for two AYCEs and a large sake, was expecting a bill around $50/55 with tax or so, but it came up north of $70. 

Not in a hurry to repeat the experience.

The most lively Karaoke spot tonight! Not only can you sing but if you sing poorly, everyone is super supportive. What a nice place to grab a drink, relax, casual sing, and comfortably make a fool of yourself! No worries in sight here. Beer is cold and the mic is hot. Come on down, join the fun.

My friend brought me for my inaugural visit and was really surprised that I had never been, given that I'm a huge Italian food fan! I started with a Barcelona!  The house version of a sangria cocktail recommended by our very friendly and attentive server. We share a house salad, perfectly crispy and tangy, then shared a margarita pizza, which was also perfectly crispy crust goodness, with a tangy tomato sauce and fresh basil. Both were authentic and delicious!! I can wait to come back to try the chicken parm and the tiramisu - both devoured by a couple we knew that happened to be at the next table!! The casual yet familiar atmosphere coupled with the homestyle Italian tastes makes you understand why this has been a long standing favorite in Edmonton!
Great for a date and for a family outing. Very underrated kitchen with a friendly staff. If you like un-breaded crab cakes this is your place.

Super fresh and super yum. The owner and staff are friendly and welcoming as well. Brought back memories from my childhood. They've got some pretty delish chocolate dipped biscotti too. Garlic and shrimp stuffed ravioli is a must buy! We can't wait to visit again and splurge!!

Attended a very socially distant baby shower here last weekend.  I was never here before and I was very impressed!  The room we were in was a nice size and we had less than 20 people at the shower.  The room didn't seem too big at all because of the way the tables were set up, along with the gift and favor tables.  Plus they had limited seating at each table.  The service was absolutely wonderful and the food was good too!
We ordered the beef skewers for apps and they were delicious. Sushi was very good and service was equal.

It is a fun time place.  I have been to other dueling piano bars and this one wasn't the best I've seen.

My recommendation is to stick to the other bars in the area the music and entertainment is much better.

My family of 4 ordered breakfast food (eggs & pancakes) at 7pm.  The restaurant was not very full - maybe 7 tables w/ customers.  After 45 minutes we still did not have our food.  Nor did at least 2 tables that were there before us.   After asking the waitress (1 of 2 on duty) when we might get our food, she told us, 'I don't know - I can't make the chef go any faster'.  Other tables were complaining about the wait as well.  At that point we finally got up and walked out.  --  On a brighter side, we drove to the IHOP near Grant & Swan.  There we had a perfect service and had our food on the table exactly 11min and 30 sec after placing our order.   We will NEVER go back to this Coco's.  Coco's used to be a great place.  The Coco's at Campbell Plaza was a favorite for many many years before it closed.  Sad.

Hubby had the Cuban which he enjoyed a great deal.  I had the best ruben I've ever eaten. Sweet potato french fries were outstanding.  Service was quick and friendly.  Very busy but no one seemed to mind the slight wait.  The iced tea was cold and wonderful.

First time visiting this location and I give it a thumbs up. I love the fast casual vibes here with plenty of communal style seating. It is located in a small alleyway but I don't mind that at all.. you're coming here for the food, not the view.

Ordered the rotolo and the fennel sausage pizza. The rotolo is great flavor wise, but my only complaint is how hard the bread is. When looking at this menu item I expected it to be soft and flaky.. but it was quite the opposite. I know many people recommend it.. but I don't really get the hype. The fennel sausage pizza was delicious and I definitely recommend it!
Seated promptly and the food was good. The waiter was very nice. This is clearly a chain style restaurant. Not an issue but that is the atmosphere.

I went there again with my friend from NYC and we both agreed it was definitely good food.  
They offer a variety of spicy levels from mild and sweet to really spicy.  I love spicy food so this place actually offers me the option.  I think it would be interesting if they offer a spicy curry challenge like they do in Brick Lane in NYC. 
Word to the weak stomached, order mild.
Wow!  Before I changed my diet, I had a difficult time finding quality places to break bread, the. I found this gem in Yelp!  The veggie enchiladas were fire!!!

On 12/23/20, I visited Luncheonette for the second time. I ordered the Cubano sandwich ($13). Slow Roasted Local Pork, Housemade Local Ham, Comte, House Spicy Pickles and House Creamy Mustard on Griddled Acme Baguette. My sandwich came with this side. I ordered the Turkey Stew. I've had a few Cuban sandwiches over the years, but none that I enjoyed more than this one. The difference is the exceptional quality of each individual ingredient, most of which are made in house, and how thoughtfully it was constructed. Initially, I was disappointed to see the sandwich was not made with Cuban bread, but the griddled baguette was a worthy substitute. In fact, I think I may prefer it. I liked the more pronounced contrast between the crispy outside and the soft inside. I also liked the proportion of meat to bread in the sandwich. For those with dietary restrictions, you can substitute gluten free or keto bread for $1.

The Turkey Stew was light and healthy. It was full of turkey, tomatoes and root vegetables, which made for a filling side. I I probably wouldn't order it again. Although it had good flavor, it wasn't what I would consider a knockout dish. Even so, I like that the menu provides healthy options like this.

I also ordered the Taylor Shellfish Oyster Chowder ($12) for lunch the next day. It consists of 16 oz. oysters, bacon, milk, potatoes, carrots and herbs. It Luncheonette's Taylor Shellfish Oyster Chowder ($12) 
16 oz. Oysters, Bacon, Milk, Potatoes, Carrots and Herbs. Served with buttered Acme bread.

I love a good oyster stew, but I had never had oyster chowder before. I enjoyed Luncheonette's version. It had a slightly briny flavor, and was chock-full of oysters and potatoes. 

I always post my own pictures of food, but this time I'm sharing a cropped photo from Luncheonette's website because I only ate a half portion at a time, which didn't photograph as well. My photo is in the comment section. It was served with buttered Acme bread. I love a good oyster stew, but I had never had oyster chowder before. I enjoyed Luncheonette's version. It had a slightly briny flavor, and was chock-full of oysters and potatoes. 

Highly Recommended!!!

I am a big fan of Rubios!  Totally sold!  Aside from their salsa/condiment bar the food and service are great. I used to come to this location on Sundays and although there is usually a line 3 to 4 people deep they are fast! I love their beer battered fish burrito and rarely depart from that choice because its all I need in a burrito! They have an awesome chipotle salsa too! If you sign up for emails you get a free b-day meal I look forward to every year! Thank you Rubios!

Not that busy, but surprisingly slow to get seated (40 min) and to get served (60+ min) on a Wednesday. Server wasn't sharp... blew two out of five basic drink orders, wasn't attentive to table, and didn't check on food progress despite being prompted.

Raised from 1 star to 2 stars based on food quality and temp, which were good.
Great Place to dine...FOOD was awesome and price very fair! I love the place and the Server was out of this WORLD ...Johnathan N.!!!!!

Simple deli filled with the smells of fried deliciousness. 

We walked in at 5:45pm on a Thursday and didn't realize that they closed at 6:00pm! We walked out a few minutes later with an Italian hoagie, a cheesesteak, a couple bags of chips, and a couple sodas. 

The sandwiches were super yummy! Well made, and lots of meats/cheese/veggies.

I appreciated that they stayed open a few minutes longer for us.

Since moving from Korean food heaven (aka. Los Angeles) to Philly a few months ago, I've tried over a few dozen Korean restaurants and I've been fairly disappointed in every single one of them. All of them had ok to terrible tasting Korean food and they were all overpriced for the quality that they served. I was about to give up on all Korean food in the East Coast and write it up as a hopeless endeavor.

And that all changed when I came here.

I was told about Jong Ka Jib by a friend who knew I was looking for good soon doo bu and how I'd been so disappointed in all of the Korean places around the area. I honestly didn't think this place would be any different but I was thinking, "Hey, at this point, I might as well start conditioning my mind into thinking this is good Korean food." and I went.

I was blown away. Not only is Jong Ka Jib the best Korean food I've had at a restaurant since moving out from LA, but I would definitely consider it one of the top ten soon doo bu places I've ever been to in my life. Granted, it's not in the top 3 in my opinion but it's definitely up there. I had the pork soon doo bu extra spicy and ordered a side of kalbi ($15). The soup base was very tasty and it wasn't too watery or thick. And the tofu was cooked to perfection. They give out perfect portions too so after you finish eating, you should be pretty full.

Don't be surprised or put-off when you come in and see a ton of non-Koreans eating here (white and Chinese) if you're not used to that. I myself, coming from LA, if I went to a Korean place and saw the customer base were mostly non-Koreans, I walked out because from experience, the food did not taste like Korean food but very Americanized. This place doesn't follow that trend.

The service here is just ok, or maybe even below ok but that's what I've come to expect and experience when I was in LA going to good Korean restaurants. It's rare to find a Korean place that has great service and great food. The galbi was terrible though. Don't get it. First off, it's not marinated very well and the flavors come across a bit funky. Second, it is way overpriced for the amount and quality of the meat. I shared the kalbi with two other people and we didn't even finish the galbi. That's how bad it was. As long as you stick with the soondoobu, and the occasional pajun (Korean pancake), you'll be very happy.

After my oh so amazing experience here, I came here two more time thinking maybe it was a fluke. And no, it wasn't. I think I've found my home here.

Parking: Limited lot or street
Price: $10 per person
Wait: 10 mins after order (during rush hour you will wait an hour to be seated so beware)

Absolutely delicious!! I had the oyster Benedict and I can't think of a better combination of ingredients. The poached eggs and oysters were cooked perfectly. Our waiter was very attentive and so personable without being annoying. My husbands meal was equally as great. I almost don't want to post this for fear that this quaint bistro will become too touristy.

This has to be one of my new favorite restaurants. Not only was the service great, the food was amazing. I tried their lobster Mac n cheese and crab cakes. Currently I have not been able to find better crab cakes in St. Louis. It is quite expensive but definitely worth it.

My husband and I ate here and we split 3 different sausages. The waiter was nice and cut them in half and put them on a plate together to make it easier to share. However I noticed we only got 1 portion of chips, even though we ordered 3 sausages. I thought oh well maybe we'll get a few dollars off the price or something. No we got charged the full amount. We didn't say anything cause we didn't want to bother our waiter and maybe we didn't want them to bring out a huge amount of chips and charge us if we asked. But still,  if you're paying for a meal you should get everything it includes. Luckily one of our friends that ate with us didn't want his chips so I ate some of his. Next time if we go back we will order each meal separately and just cut them in half ourselves. Their prices are a little bit high also.

It certainly has slipped over the years and I read they were going to close. But I was driving by and I saw a sign saying New Ownership!. I stopped thinking a return to its heyday. Nope. It the same. It might even be more run down. The food is just ok. You can get a better hoagie or cheese steak almost anywhere. I can't say I'll ever bother again. And $9:50 per, it's not even a bargain.

Fair disclosure: I'm a Texan. I've been to San Antonio many times. And I know tacos.

When a good friend decided to bring me here, I knew it was mistake.

The tacos were flavorless. The guac almost had some flavor, but really it was tasted like processed avocado. I would have preferred Taco Bell.

The cashier was friendly, and it does seem like a great place to hang out with friends and have some beers. Parking would be nice too.

I guess the best way to put it is this: It will probably be OK for most people in the area. It's not *bad* food by any means.

But if you're a foodie, or if you know what tacos should be, keep on movin'.

All you can eat Korean BBQ means way too much food! By the looks alone the place is nothing special, simple. You choose the proteins you'd like to eat, they bring them to your table raw and you cook them yourself. Don't go in too hungry or with too many people because you'll end up frustrated. The concept is fun though, communal cooking and eating. In terms of the quality of the meats, I would say they were pretty good but I don't really have much to compare it to. The ventilation overall could be better. By the end of our meal the last pieces of meat were getting burnt not just BBQed. Server was nice and attentive.
We found this place on Yelp and are happy we did. We loved the comfy vibe in the restaurant. Food was great, staff was super friendly and attentive. Definitely recommend.

If you're coming here for the oysters this place deserves a full 5 stars. My boyfriend and I are coming from VA and came 30 mins before they opened (11 am). We sat right at the bar ordered a dozen raw ($20) and half chargrilled ($12). The restaurant immediately started filling up as soon as it opened.

I was kind of weirded out at first when our chef put the oyster directly ON the bar, I was like FOR ME?! The thing was as almost as big as my hand. I ate my first fresh raw Louisiana oyster and I was blown away. I felt like I was eating the ocean. Sounds crazy but it's the best way to describe how fresh they were.

Don't forget to make your sauces which you can get on the side or at a table. I mixed the horse radish and ketchup together. I filled a  cup full of lemon wedges. The nice couple next to us gave me some of their hot sauce which brought the flavor from the oyster from here to HERE. 

We left feeling super energized and wanting more. A def must go in NOLA!

We came for the "famous" Shrimp Cocktail, but we were WoWed by the steaks!! We traveled from our home in Louisville just to visit St. Elmo's Steak House and, without a doubt, this was the best steak I've ever had! 
Our party of four enjoyed the Strip steak,  a Ribeye and Prime Rib. The bone in Prime Rib, was shared by our companion couple, because it was two pounds! (32 oz.). This was Prime Rib as it is meant to be cooked and served, like days of yore.  Both the Strip and Ribeye were grilled as ordered with a wonderful, flavourful taste that is often missing in steakhouse steaks these days. The baked potatoes were freshly served and were a perfect accompaniment. 
Just when we thought we couldn't eat another bite, we relented and shared a White chocolate blueberry bread  pudding with vanilla ice cream which hit just the right note of sweetness. Thank goodness we were spending the night in Indy- we would never make the drive home!

Stopped into Nine Irish Brother's last weekend with friends and family.  It's a great spot on Mass ave, made to look old but actually brand new.  The service was good, the beer flowing and the food didn't miss a beat.

A worthwhile place to have dinner if down on Mass Ave in Indianapolis.

Neat place for drinks and live music. Indoor and outdoor seating area. Clean bar/restaurant. Employees were friendly. Grilled Grouper sandwich was really good. Wife liked the shrimp and pasta.  BBQ pork sandwich was not very good. Kinda salty meat didn't taste very good
I stopped in yesterday and tried the hot dog. Not fully cooked and did not taste good. For $2.50 save your money and go elsewhere.

Tonight was my first time being in this building since last year (it was previously Sukho Thai).  I went in with two of my friends for a late dinner, and did not expect to receive such great service!  We were the only table in there at the time and he asked if we wanted to play music, so I requested Pantera and our server had no problem doing so.  When I ordered my dish, I asked for a vegan ramen bowl and he told me his go-to order for vegans and it was SO DELICIOUS!  He was really nice, and I wish I could remember his name so I can give credit where it's due!  I had a great time there and I will definitely return! 
You can never go wrong with metal music and delicious ramen.

Went for lunch before a Sunday Reno Aces Baseball Game. This place is all about LOCATION. Right across the street from the ball park. Not really busy but the service needs some work or else they were just understaffed that day. Beer selection is adequate, food was pretty good. The Pizzle (Pretzel with Mozz cheese and pepperoni) was devoured immediately. Wasn't sure if it was the food or the fact it took so long to get it. Also had a sausage on a pretzel bun, little pricey $7.50 but much better that inside the park. Others had the cordon bleu grilled cheese (excellent) and pizza melt (also excellent). Overall food was good once we got it. Will be coming back (Season Tickets).

Crazy! That place really feels like an urban market. Different food stands provide you with all options you can imagine. Im top of that is a bar in the back. High-Class food with the regional influence delivers #yumminess! We had the breakfast and lunch there and never got disappointed. We are still talking about the Quinoa Bowl, the Haitian Breakfast plate and the shrimps'n'grits. But the best was the street corn with feta and creole seasoning. Really cool market flair made it to an full on experience that doesn't disappoint.

We went on a Saturday morning and we were seated fairly quickly considering how packed it was...

The prices are very reasonable and the portions are HUGE. The staff was most excellent and I can say that we will definitely be back whenever I'm in Indy...

Great dinner with my husband! Had the chicken fried steak. The gravy was awesome! The mashed squash was sooo good! It took a while to get our food because of a party going on. The manager came over to explain and apologize and offered a free dessert. Our waitress was the sweetest and said to choose the carrot cake which was awesome!! They also serve a good glass portion of wine. Will definitely go back. Would be a great place to bring the kids!

I stopped into HK while on an afternoon stroll in Doylestown. The brisket and ribs were quite good. There were several table sauces that, although a little sweet for my liking, were not bad. My favorite was the mustard bbq sauce. Sides were somewhat hit or miss. I would skip the Mac and cheese which is rather bland and more like buttered noodles than the creamy, cheese saturated MnC I prefer. Beans and collard greens tho were tasty. My favorite fare were the French fries with chipotle mayo (I'm a junkie for this kinda gastro pub fare). This is a nice, casual restaurant situated across from the court house. The staff are very friendly, as well. Worth a visit if you're in the neighborhood.

MUFFIN & COFFEE BREAKFAST REVIEW ONLY

Stopped in the Vincentown Diner after court in Mt. Holly this morning for a late light breakfast. It has been at least a decade since my last visit, and aside from the new sign out front, the inside looked basically the same with two main dining areas, a long counter with spinners, and servers in black.  It also has signs referring to local sourced foods, craft beer, and french press coffee.  The lighting seemed a bit dim which felt more somber than comforting. 

I sat at the counter and was promptly approached by a woman in black offering a menu and asking if I wanted something to drink.  Coffee, please.  It arrived in a larger cup, about twice the size of the normal diner serving.  Nice touch. Felt generous. 

I inquired about muffins, and was advised they had corn and blueberry.  A toasted corn muffin was exactly what I wanted.  The menu called them, "The Real Deal!"  It arrived cut in thirds and well grilled on top and bottom.  I small cup of butter and two jelly containers came along for the ride. I spread some butter on the heated surfaces, but pushed the sweets aside.  

First bite was a small surprise.  Rather than having that expected corn muffin flavor, the mix included Lemon Zest, making the taste more a lemon corn muffin, than the traditional rich corn flavor and texture.  Disappointing, but certainly an acceptable variant if notified beforehand.  That was not the case here.  

All the above would have resulted in a three star review, but for the heartburn I have been suffering since leaving the diner.  Whether the coffee or the muffin were the "Real Deal," or not, that was an aftertaste I could live without.
I love this place! Amazing Food. Friendly Staff. Really great options for burgers, like Bison, Elk, even Ahi & Cod sandwiches. Try em all!!! Don't forget about shakes & Malts too.
Always great food and amazing wait staff!  Traveling to New Orleans, we plan our day around food at Ruby Slipper!

This place is cute but not overly noticeable.  Saw that it had good reviews so I had to check it out.  

The first time we tried to go it had about an hour wait.  Tried to go again today and it was still def busy, but we were able to get seated pretty fast.  It seems like this place is always pretty busy and can be a little loud.

When you walk in, it's not overly clear what you are supposed to do, so we initially stood by the door behind another couple, but were motioned to the back of the restaurant.  It would be helpful to have a sign indicating what to do when you walk in.  We were quickly given menus and got our order taken pretty fast.  Food on the other hand was a little slower.  They apologized however and said that they were slow because they were out of a lot of stuff.

We order the falafel plate for an appetizer and it was served with hummus and naan.  It took a while to come out but was overall pretty good.  For dinner I got the chicken kabob and my husband got the lamb kabob (he wanted the lamb shank, but they were out of that).  Food took a while and was pretty good, but could have used a little more spice. I wanted to ask the waitress for hot sauce, but unfortunately she didn't come back to the table to check on us so I wasn't able to do so.

We were done eating a good amount of time before the check came, but they ran the card pretty quickly.

Overall food is good, particularly the falafel, service was okay (not sure if it was lacking due to them being busy or bc it was New Year's Day).

Went here for Mother's Day Brunch. For $65 pp and an ocean right there you would expect crab legs. They didn't have much to choose from. A small room and an even smaller dessert table. No variety or special foods you would expect for $65 pp. The Universal Hilton for the same price has 3 huge rooms of variety including king crab legs. 

The mimosas and champagne were included however for people that don't drink that, it was extra for every drink. I was pregnant so I just wanted an OJ and my son got cranberry juice. We asked for refills and the server said it was extra charge. I thought that was odd seeing how the orange juice for champagne was included, but not just the orange juice? We ended up just getting water. 

I wouldn't recommend this place. There's a great seafood place a few minutes away, Enterprise Fish Co. way cheaper and much more worth it.
We had the sliders and waffle cheese fries. They weee the best I have ever have. I will be back to try more on the menu. A true gem!!!!

Had some very good oysters but that has nothing to do with  cooked food     My father and I each had shrimp poboy. Super small tasteless shrimp also over cooked   Really unbelievable from a seafood market restaurant. I guarantee the shrimp were not from the USA
This is such a great Greek restaurant Sean is an awesome server. He kept our drinks full and answered any questions we had. He was pleasant and efficient. We will be back and will ask for Sean.

My Aunt and I decided to got to the New China Buffet on Tuesday, April 3rd 2018. We were walking in with high hopes but unfortunately it did not fill them. Many of the items were lukewarm and others were cold. Steam can be seen coming the tables but they weren't warming the food up much. 

Other than the cold food, it was okay food. Nothing really special but some items were tasty. There were many different things on Buffet but nothing stood out as amazing. The price is $10.99 per person, working in the restaurant business I know that isn't bad for "all you can eat" but my aunt thought different. 

The buffet had a good amount of people coming in and out, so they must doing something right for some people. My aunt and I probably won't be coming back for a while but I will not say never.

Giving this 5 stars because I was pleasantly surprised. Unique/diverse crowd from "A-Listers to Hipsters." Guys behind the bar are mixologists! The hospitality was top shelf. Very good small bites to eat, there's a coffee shop in there, and even a small bowling ally! There's a little bit of everything at this social club. Well done.

We don't usually order Americanized-ish sushi rolls (cream cheese, cooked fish, imitation crab c'mon =D) so I cannot review those rolls. If you like sashimi like we do, definitely order the sashimi plates. They were so fresh. Our friend had teriyaki beef and it came with tempura, salad, rice on top of the edamame and miso. It was a full meal ! I've found another excellent sushi restaurant.

This. Place. Is. Amazing.

I have lived in Japan on and off for 5 years, and this place is legit. I have tried any number of places in both Indianapolis and Chicago, and nothing comes close. I would come here even if the prices weren't amazing (hello there happy hour sushi!), because it is just so freaking good.

Obviously, the sushi is great. And cheap. What is even more exciting to me is dishes that I don't see often outside of Japan. I am in love with their oyakodon and dishes with unagi. Also highly recommend a grilled salmon collar. 

You really need to make reservations. They make it super easy, and I always do so through facebook. 

Come eat all the sushi!!!!

This place will go into my to-go restaurants list for sure :) the food was just as I had expected - delicious and made perfectly with just the right spice level. The waiter was quick and friendly even though it was a little packed in there. As soon as you walk in you can smell all the deliciousness and you know you won't be disappointed.

Awful food, terrible wait staff. I will never come back to this place. The waitress was nasty from the moment we sat down because she was the only one with 7 tables. She made this known and wanted sympathy. I even called ahead and asked if it was busy/if we needed a reservation and the hostess said no. The food was terrible too. We ordered a few things that were on the menu and were told they didn't have them. I ordered Mac and cheese for my son because they didn't have something else and she said she never put that order in. I will never come back to this awful place.

I did a lunch delivery today from Puccini's through Yelp and it was very convenient!  It did not take a long time and the Greek garden calzone was very good. I have had Puccini's before and their pizza is terrific!  I have not had a bad experience with Puccini's to date, so I'm grateful to be able to order lunch through them.  Puccini's has great quality food and the prices are reasonable,  so I would recommend this place to all of my friends.
My favourite Asian restaurant in Saint Louis. Right amount of food ..flavors are awesome.. rightly priced.

My kids and I dine at Carlitos at least once every couple of months. The patio dining across from the Arlington provides great people watching and the food and drinks are fantastic. Probably our favorite dish is the chicken pozole. The stew is fantastic and its served with an array of accouterments such as fresh avocado, shredded cabbage, onion, cilantro, dried oregano, fresh tortillas, etc. so that you can customize the dish to your liking. They also have a good kids menu including some fun drinks like a virgin lime margarita and smoothies with mango or strawberry. Chips are complimentary and served as soon as you sit down with two different kinds of tasty salsas. My only complaint about this fantastic restaurant is they have a live band that usually starts playing around 7:00. While the music adds great atmosphere, it's often too loud making it hard to have conversations with your dining partners. Although we like the idea of live music, we usually book an earlier reservation so that we leave before the music starts.
The food really was tasty but I'm clearly not cool enough to eat here. And for the price, I'd like a plate. But in terms of flavor, Moar is spot on.

I love their diablito but I ask for mango flavor for the ice instead of tamarind. Really hits the spot like the places back home. The esquite is pretty decent.. mix well because all the Mayo is on the top! Sad because last time I stopped by the place was unlocked .. but .. no one was there ? !
Cool place, nice vibe. Solid bar tenders. Main negative is the young crowd puking in the bathroom.
Sushi was delicious and presentation was spectacular. Waitstaff were very attentive .

Just ok... with so many other choices near my hotel should have asked first.  Server was blah... no excitement to start.  Wasnt really listening.  It 2as super slow and she probably wanted to get cut to go the Made in America... but I digress... 

Quinoa and Kale salad - bland at best with over cooked salmon.  

Philly wonton - greasy, hot sauce not a compliment. 

Matso Ball soup - ok. 

Mac & cheese - hot and cheesy but again blah. 

Overall if your starving and other choices are packed. This'll pass.  I won't go back.  Ever.
Fun place to go for a quality burger. Has a lot of history and enjoyed the low key atmosphere. Has a nice historical aspect to it's franchise. Had an Elk burger that was really yummy.

Came in with some friends for the Fight , we only had reservations for 7 people but ended up showing up with a group of about 15 at around 9pm. We Purchased tickets at the side door for the extra people with us, and based on the demeanor and blatant "screw this and all of y'all" attitude that we received from the lady with green hair giving tickets at the front door, I without a doubt would have said, this is going to be one horrible night... thankfully none of our party (nor the rest of the employees we encountered after entering) let that rotten apple spoil the bunch!! We all proceeded to where our reserved table that was in the back of the bar upstairs, although being a tight squeeze, it was not too packed where our table was located. When we found it.. We asked the lady that helped us find our reserved table if we could have the table next to it as well because our party was bigger than expected and the sign on the reservation was for 7 pm.. she told us she wasn't sure but would find out, returned with another employee which told us that she could not make that discussion, but would ask her manager. She returned with the manager and although at first she seemed a little agitated, (totally understandable on a night like it was) upon hearing our plea that the paper on the table said the reservation was for 7 and it was now 9:30, she took the paper off of the table and told us no problem at all enjoy your night..  and what a night it was moving forward!!!! Despite a few hiccups involving  some of the friends that were in our party, the 2 bartenders Andrew, Katt, and also the female manager on duty, (I cannot remember her name) went ABOVE and BEYOND to make sure we were okay and well taken care of throughout the evening! Those 3 HANDS DOWN, made what I thought as I first walked through the front door would be a horrible night with disgruntled sports bar employees, one hell of a night!! And I will recommend American Sports Saloon to any one I know in the future, that might be traveling that way.! We all had the best night, and gratefully appreciate the hospitality shown consistently throughout the night (especially in leu of some of our parties indiscretions) I know without a doubt, we will be back so to see you all soon!! Not sure if anyone employed here monitors this page , but if so, on behalf of our whole group, please let Andrew, Kat and the manager who helped us out all evening, that we truly appreciate all of their hospitality shown!!!!!!  Thank You American Sports Saloon

2 of the workers were super nice so sweet and easygoing. there was this one girl at the end who was super standoffish and made me pay too early when i was waiting to add xtra stuff after he got the meatballs and then i asked after i paid and she basically said no. then i went out to the car and looked in the bag and was missing sauce and i went back in to ask for it and she was very rude about it all. Now since i got home i'm eating and i got the ahi tuna and it is nowhere near fresh. it's super super fishy which if you know anything about fresh seafood basically raw it shouldn't taste like this. I'm pescatarian so i eat seafood quite a bit. Wouldn't come here again super pissed i spent 46$ on 3 bowls. :(

This bar is okay. They have a few good happy hour specials (they used to have more, but cut back), the food is your average bar food. The bar staff is nice at times, other times,  they're very rude (including management). Sometimes it's dead, other times it's full of young drunk kids. It's better on week nights- quieter and better service. Basically, it's hit or miss. It's not called Barristers anymore, but everything seems to be the same.

Writing this review as I sit here at the restaurant. This will be my second time coming here and I was hoping for a better experience but......no. First roll came out and fish quality tasted questionable, still waiting for the second one. 10 min later... second roll has arrived. I took one bite and already feel my stomach grumbling. My bf is devouring it but that doesn't say much because he eats my a** on the daily. O sushi off swan and speedway is way better food and service, go there.

This meal was so dry and terrible: the gyros, the falafel platter, the rice, everything. In New York, the cart gives you hot sauce and white sauce. All three items I ordered did not come with white sauce. Or hot sauce. The falafel was flavorless as was the rice. 

My delivery was delayed twice. $45 later for 3 "meals," I wish I chose a different place for delivery. 

Save your money and appetite for a place worthy of both. Like the Halal Guys food cart on 53rd St and Sixth Ave in New York.

Omg! My first time here. I passed it twice on our way to sassafras and today i decided to turn around and come here after looking a the pictures posted on yelp. I always judge by the pics rather than the reviews even if it has 4-5 stars pics tell it all and omg i do not regret it! U have to come here. chef Ruiz u are amazing. Pure comfort food. For appetizer i ordered the fried shrimp but instead of the buffalo sauce i asked for the thai ginger sauce that comes on the salmon bits and it was Amazing! .

My mom ordered the plain chicken wings and the gourmet potato skins n LOVED it. The wings were perfect tasted like my homemade fried chicken yum. This is definitely authentic NOLA Cuisine. I ordered the Pork chop w/ mac n cheese entree and omgggg  delicious. I rarely eat pork chops but the picture i saw of it on here made me want to get it and i was not disappointed. The baked macaroni was dream tasted homemade like something we'd eat at thanksgiving with a stuffed bell pepper or dressing lawwwddd! N my green beans were sautéed to perfection. .... And the food was sooo good i had to try the dessert which is also made from scratch too btw. Jesus take the wheel i dont even like or eat bread pudding my mom ordered it n i ate some of hers n its THE BEST IVE EVER HADDD lawwwd like seriously yall im not even exaggerating. I ordered the key lime pie n it was really good and flavorful but that breadpudding won my heart. seriously id give 10 stars if i could im so impressed and thats says a lot coming from me. N ill pay anything for great food and the prices r reasonable and worth it!!! Wheeeew... I already know what i want to try on my next visit. And FYI i was born and raised in New Orleans so i know good food when i come across it. Ohhh and i cant forget the sweet and verf attentive server Alexis. Thanks girl u were great. Very good attentive, knowledgeable and was even playful with the other guests kids. Great Job Chef Ruiz! Great restaurant.

This is one of my new favorite spots. My boyfriend and I split the guacamole, soooo creamy and good. (The plantain chips were to die for). Next he got the oyster taco and street corn, which he loved although there's only one taco per order.. I got the chicken enchilada and rice, rice was okay but the rest was awesome! On top of that the decor and paining on the wall was stunning (pic)

Tried this place out today because of the awesome reviews and it really is amazing! It's probably one of the best Thai restaurants I've been to. We ordered the dumplings as an appetizer (which were the best Ive ever had), yellow curry, and pad Thai. The pad Thai was average but the curry and dumplings were delicious. We plan on going back to try a lot more off the menu. Almost forgot the Thai tea! It was perfect.

It only took one visit to become one of our favorite food joints, and we've been dreaming and salivating about returning ever since. I sincerely appreciate that they carry the impossible burger and have several plant-based options. My fiance eats meat, but he will always get an impossible burger over a beef burger if it is offered. Burger Fuel has their own take on their burgers, fries, and milk shakes. I appreciate the vegan shakes as well! Meat-eating milk-loving fiance approved! The restaurant has a unique vibe and an electric atmosphere. Their personal parking lot was very convenient. I adore their unique outdoor seating that is shaded for those extra hot days.

I love the small plates that you can get here.  The food is well prepared and the menu imaginative.  It is right next to 30th Street station and you can get in and out quickly if you need to.  The wait staff is very friendly, well trained, and knowledgeable.  
The down side is the bar menu which is bourbon heavy.  If you love bourbon, this is your place.  If not, you are out of luck.  It is also very expensive for what you get.

The food here stands out above all the rest.  I've never had an egg roll/shrimp roll that was lightly crispy but not oily.  When I say lightly crispy, I thought I was eating a puff pastry...it was fresh and the shrimp was fresh and cleaned and it was huge.  It was about 40% bigger than your average egg roll.  I had the Bourbon chicken lunch special and the fried rice was fried darkly brown like I love it.  I don't like yellow, beige or light brown fried rice.  It was perfect.  And although they are priced higher than other restaurants in the area for lunch, it's worth it.  The Won Ton soup has 4 Won Tons in it, instead of 2 or 3.  You don't have to pay extra for the crispy noodles and the fried rice has meat in it also without paying extra.  It was enough for two of us...I just can't complain at all.  This is not my first time eating here.  I've had their egg foo young and their bbq spare ribs....always cooked just right.  China Palace puts others in the area to shame and I won't even talk about mall Chinese food.

I love this place! If you like BBQ pork steaks, you will love the pork steak burger. Its basically pork steak removed from the bone, mixed with yummy BBQ and cooked as a patty. The coleslaw as an addition on it is perfect. I also have had the veggie burger. Great flavor. I only wish it had longer hours so I can have lunch AND dinner there. :)

Awful eggs Benedict. The Hollandaise was basically yellow mustard. Also the business only accepts cash which is a pain in the butt these days. I can see why there was a short wait on a Saturday morning during peak brunch hours. Will not be back.

Thought the food was alright. I was disappointed to see that there weren't that many healthy options on the menu and my salad that I did get was very average! Overall great vibe thought and the costumer service was great!
This place is 24 hour!! It's fast and pretty decent the quality is alright although I har had better but for that late night snack this place rocks

Came here tonight with a friend in search of good Caribbean food outside of the USF area. Was pleasantly surprised with this spot in Hyde Park. It's on the side of The UPS Store and a bit difficult to see from the street so beware. While I was on the way I came across a photo from another Yelper about them not being open every weekend. Their website didn't state this so I called but got an outdated message instead of a live person. We almost didn't come because of this. They were open though so on to my actual review...

The restaurant is very nice looking inside and the ambiance is great. I consider it Upscale Caribbean. We were immediately acknowledged but it took 20 minutes to be seated for a party of 2. They were not full, but there was only one person serving tables. I expected this due to the reviews, so no complaints... but I wouldn't come if I was pressed for time. 

Drink prices are a bit high. No free refills because everything comes from a bottle. Don't let that deter you because the food is good (Im picky about my Caribbean food). I had the oxtails, rice & peas and coco bread. All good, only a bit spicy. My friend doesnt like jerk chicken but liked theirs. The menu doesn't state this but entrees come with a side salad... they also give complimentary bread which was nice simply because that's not the norm for this kind of restaurant.

The owners came and spoke to us prior to leaving and they were very nice. I can appreciate their desire to improve. They take feedback seriously which is good. I enjoyed dining here and I will return.

Stop right now. Go to RTM and buy yourself one of these amazing doughnuts. Laugh at all of the people who go on and on about how awesome Krispy Kreme is. 

You'll find all of the classics you would expect with a couple of novelty choices, all 95 cents each. The line moves quickly, and while you wait, you can watch them being made.

My personal votes go to the apple cider, pumpkin and chocolate mousse doughnuts.

Had my hopes up but left disappointed.  Lasagna was bland, ziti was bland, the lobster and fillet was really good, the ravioli was good.  They have a very bright tv in the "romantic" dining room with ads and  the weather showing.  Very friendly staff and the owner stopped by our table but I've had much better Italian food.  Oh, and at 10:15 they turn the ugly lights on to hint your time is up and you need to leave

This place has gone WAY downhill. It is now using old ingredients and cutting dangerous corners with seafood and spoiled products. Just threw an entire dinner some 100$'s in all rotten and or home-spun American-ized Asian cafeteria food crap- 

Crappiest-coconut shrimp- crispy fried with coconut in the breading....not this time it was  batter fried old shrimp in milky coconut gravy- mushy filth. @nd place to the worst Black bean fish and vegetables ... nope not standard poached with green veggys- this poop version was breaded and served with red sauce and both old and again mushy filth with those tiny square carrots and frozen peas that come in school lunches. Wanton soup- old rotten- mush. Fried rice.... oh they failed here too- terryaki sauce poured over whice rice. Glossy shiny DARK BROWN not the golden fried rice you always get this was special too this was BM dark burgundy brown like covered in bbq sauce- ugh!
