The food is delicious and reasonable. The owners are an amazingly nice and customer-driven couple from Vietnam. Vietnamese, Thai and Chinese favorites, along with unique and delicious coffee and other drinks. Went two days in a row. Will be back.

BEST breakfast in Tucson!!  We probably eat breakfast here 2-3 times a week.  The servers are so awesome every time we are here!  It's a great place to bring young kids if you want to eat breakfast or lunch with them. They do a great Cheerios set up for them that distracts them until the food gets here.  The breakfast is always cooked perfectly to order, is hot and the bacon is delicious!  And really, the best priced breakfast in Tucson!

This location used to be kind of a mess with late orders, et al., but they've really come around.  I've ordered here no less than a dozen times in the last few months, and it's always on time with a great, friendly staff.  They had some issues with the app, but I won't blame them for technical difficulties.  Great job taking a poorly managed place and turning things around!

This class was a great experience.  The chef demonstrated how to cook the native New Orleans cuisine and provided us with our own copies of the recipes to follow along.
The biscuits that they gave as a snack were amazing.  They also let us have more than one helping of all of the food.
I would recommend buying the fresh pralines for all of your friends at the attached store because they are much cheaper than the prepackaged pralines you find in all of the tourist shops.
My only complaint is that they used basically the same meats for the gumbo and jimbalaya.  I would have liked one of the dishes to have had some seafood.

I absolutely love the food here. Well composed dishes at a reasonable price. The atmosphere is cool too. That is where the good stops. There is always a wait, even when there's visibly empty tables and I've been 15+ times. Hostesses are always rude. Service seems unempowered and flakey. Tables don't get bussed quickly. I go back for the food and sometimes do takeout to avoid the service issue.

So happy to see this stylish new wine bar open in Hyde Park. 70s vibe, soul/blues vinyl, fantastic charcuterie board, and a lovely red made for a fantastic evening just two days after they opened. They have a surprising variety of food available, and what I tried (French charcuterie, watermon) was very tasty. Service was excellent, and the owner's passion is very apparent after a short conversation. This place has class out the ass.

Always a winner.  Small, hidden, quaint, and unassuming, but the food packs a punch!   Try the chili dog wrap, which was recommended to me and I highly recommend to you.  My wife had an Italian grinder and was just as phenomenal.

This is still my all time favorite Mexican restaurant!  Just wish it was closer to home! Best chips and salsa...the chips are so light and crunchy! 
Several menu items I've never seen offered at any other Mexican restaurants. Very nice decor and atmosphere. Again everything was delicious! ! The only down side to this years visit was our favorite waitress wasn't there.

We ordered about two months ago and want to try again. They are a little pricey but most meats are expensive. My hubs ordered the ribs with a few sides. The mashed potatoes were very good along with the corn bread. The ribs were good but needed to
Be warmed more. We understand they cook everything before just heat it more :) 
We will be trying again!

Delicious and refreshing boozy drinks made with love!  My group tried the Almond Freeze, which was a bit cinammon-y the Flaming Monkey, which was pretty much amazing, and the Bloody Mary was spicy and had a Louisiana kick.  There's a bit of a wait to get your order taken and receive your drink but it'll be well worth it!

We have been here several times but this last time really compelled me to leave a review. Everything was perfect. The waitress was friendly and super helpful and the food was straight delicious. We went on a Sunday so the place was packed (yes there a wait times around 45 minutes at peak times.) and we were all shocked how fast the food made it to our table. They have some "fancy" breakfast dishes but also awesome comfort food. Breakfast burrito on chili? Yes, please. I love this place, the food is sooo good!

I go to Tuscany café all the time. I love their breakfast says and it's a nice quiet quaint place to go with your family. The coffee is great.The food is very good and the portions are nice. The servers are friendly and tend to your needs almost immediately. I will be going back to them. Even my son liked Tuscany. And he is hard to please

My friends and I went to Cafe con Chocolate for our Sunday brunch.  We went in a fairly large group with 7 people, but were seated right away.  Our server was an adorable and friendly young lady who was very familiar with the menu and explained all the dishes to us.  There was no tofu or Japanese food that day.  I ordered a cafe con chocolate, breakfast burrito, and homefries.  Food was delicious.  Cafe con chocolate was delicious, and HUGE.  Only complaint was how slow the food took to come to our table, and how long we had to wait for the check.  I figure that they are only busy on-and-off and can't afford to hire another server.  I would come here again!  They seemed happy to have us there to keep them in business.

I called in reservations for 8 on Friday the 31st for a bunch of  hungry golfers.  Talked to the owner, and our server Jade did an outstanding job.  Food was 5 star fresh, homemade, and plenty to eat.  Fantastic thin crust wood fired pizza, great wine selection, apps., and entrees simply fantastic, and the desserts were great..  Love a well run Family restaurant, and this one is a big thumbs up.   It is a must go to place, and being Italian, and a caterer, they exceeded my expectations.

We went there for brunch while doing paperwork in the downtown. The people are very friendly and nice. I should say that the place is good for delivery or take out. Not many seats for eating in, you can figure out when the food is ready and receive the food in the disposable dishes (which I personally like as they are cleaner and you are sure never been used before :) 
We ordered Colbey and Shaughnessy. Both were good and delicious. I personally liked Shaughnessy more. There were some things like the coffee was finished and we waited couple of minutes till they prepare. And they were out of Ketchup sauce!! That's why I am giving 3 stars. But over all it is a nice place for the price.

I grabbed brunch with a friend around 10am Tuesday morning and there were plenty of seats available. The food arrived reasonably quickly and was pretty good. I order the huevos rancheros and found it very tasty. My friend got the stuffed french toast and was pleased as well, although in retrospect we figured that it was probably meant to be shared as it was huge. (It's hard to give a sense exactly, but just take my word for it.) I also have to say I particularly enjoyed the coffee. (Pretty sure it's La Colombe. I recommend getting it black since it's got a pretty decent flavor on its own.)

The only reason I'm giving the place four stars is that I didn't find it to exceed expectations. But by all means, I was very satisfied.

Tip: While the seats outside are somewhat pleasant in their own right, I don't recommended them as the street nearby is very busy and noisy.

The Eagle is exactly what Mass Ave needed. I've been there several times and now when friends come into town, it is one of our go-to meeting spots. 

The environment is urban chic with rustic yet modern decor and some good ol' southern dishes. The one downfall for me now that I am gluten free... there are very limited food options. Thankfully I like sides and sweet potatoes so I usually find something that will work for me.

If you're planning to go on a Friday or Saturday when the weather is beautiful, plan ahead and go for drinks before dinner. It does get crowded, but it usually moves along quickly.

I've had two experiences with The Pop Shop in the past month.

My boyfriend and I stopped by on a Monday night a few weeks back. Service was prompt, the food was great with crazy big portions and my ice cream soda was awesome. Pleasantly surprised with my initial visit, I opted to bring my mom along for a visit about a week later.

The Pop Shop is known for having open arms toward children, I just didn't know that as a college graduate, I'd be treated as one by my server, who I'll refrain from identifying. He was arrogant, rude, callous and topped it all off by bending down at the side of our booth and asking me in a voice usually reserved for a 5-year-old: "Can you allow your mom more time to decide on a dish?"

Basically, he had apathetically stopped by our table while my mom was stuck between two dishes. Rather than helping at all, he simply said, "They're both good." Knowing I had yet to eat that day, and being that she had wanted some direction from him, she had jokingly said that I would want her to choose a dish.

I'm sure Mr. Arrogant knew that he ticked me off, as he never acknowledged me again through the meal, other than once as a complete afterthought since I needed a box.

All in all, despite living around the corner, I won't be back to The Pop Shop as long as he's working there. There are far too many other restaurants in Collingswood to still check out.

I have been here a few times. Great service, strong lunch menu with reasonable prices. 
Yesterday, my fiancé and I met there for lunch. It was his first experience. He had the basil pasta and I had the Rueben sandwich with sweet potato fries. We ordered the lobster dip as an appetizer. It was delicious. Perfect spice. The dipping chips were light fluffy rice spoons(I think). But it doesn't matter what they were. Light crispy deliciousness. 
After eating ALL the dip, I was only able to eat half of my Reuben, but no worries, it made for an excellent dinner too.

This is a nice addition to Mass Ave with its fast casual setting. You order at the counter (takeout or in-house) with booth and tables inside or outside seating due to pandemic precautions. They do have a full bar but seating there is closed due to pandemic. The service is fast and the seafood is fresh and tasty. Lobster rolls, fish tacos, and huge salads are what I usually get there. They have fountain drinks plus naturally flavored teas. As for alcoholic drinks, the watermelon mojito is very tasty. 

I eat here a lot for lunch as I work downtown and it's within walking distance. Quality of service and food has been consistent. Definitely recommend.

This place is great. Service is great, environment is great, food is great. I ordered the prime rib and it was perfect. They give you these really yummy pickled vegetables for appetizer. Also, would recommend the garlic and herb fries. Good restaurant if you're looking for a nice night out.

We tried their famous dishes. 

The grilled oysters were very good! After we were done eating them, we dipped the bread in butter 
We had their sample of jambalaya-delicious!! Seafood gumbo- very good, red rice and beans- delicious, and sausage was very good! We also had raw oysters and they were good.

Wow, so absolutely delicious. Eric and I were starving after going to Cigar City and we went here because we were pretty sick of "American" food in Treasure Island. This did not disappoint...2nd best Pad Thai I have ever had (after the restaurant in DC a few months ago) and Eric's penang curry was also wonderful. The Tom Kha Gai was also top notch. Eric got Tom Yum and it was an excellent iteration. 
The service was very good and the waitress was super nice and friendly.
I think this place is OK. But do have pretty good Mac and Cheese and ice cream but it's pain in the butt to fine a parking in downtown, tho.
Needed some good traditional Chinese dishes that didn't cost an arm and leg. Small family own, but service was friendly and warming we had a huge party and they were very accommodating.

I love this place. However the main reasons I go frequently are Tara and jt. They are the absolute best!!! They are very attentive and quick to serve you another drink. They are always friendly and there to make you laugh even if they are having a busy night! Customer service is their strong quality!!

Nice addition to Main Street in Speedway. It's a small space but the food was quite good. I had the taco special which came with many options including two types of fish. I went with the fish tacos and was quite happy. Having recently moved here from San Diego I have become spoiled on fantastic fish tacos. These were quite good with a variety of hot sauces on the table. Service was excellent. Definitely check it out

Overall i give this place a solid 6/10. the prices reflect that of a restaurant with a lot to show for their food. Most meals start upwards of $11. Their lattes were pretty misleading with the titles "stuffed french toast latte" but tasted about the same as a regular vanilla latte. their pancakes are tasty, but the texture is very chewy and rubbery. the best part of the experience was the scrambled cheese eggs my boyfriend got. he also got french toast that had the same chewy texture as the pancakes. the service was fine and everything tasted good, but i feel like i could have gone somewhere else with the same prices and gotten a way better experience food wise (i.e. "honeys, sit and eat" in northern liberties is about the same price but the food there is way better). probably wouldn't eat here again.

Stellar fresh made to order Lebanese cuisine! Ordered the baba ghanoush, lamb shawarma, chicken shawarma, and the lentil rice special. So flavorful! We wrapped it up with a delicious tres leches cake.  Don't hesitate to stop here!

This is my new favorite breakfast spot! I've lived in Fishtown almost 6 years now, not sure how I missed this joint. Amazing staff, food, and coffee. I try to hit all the local coffee houses and this is one of the best. The hangover hoagies are huge, delicious, and really reasonably priced. Multiple people (not just our waitress) made sure we had plenty of coffee and didn't need anything. The owner checked in with us at our table and on our way out. Couldn't have asked for a more enjoyable breakfast. I'll definitely be back!

Loved, loved this place for lunch today in first floor of the Thompson Hotel. The drinks were good, the Rose' wine tasty. 

The gumbo was delicious, just enough spice. The server was kind enough to get us small side salads which weren't on the menu. They were crisp & the vinaigrette dressing was good. We asked for bread & it was yummy as well. 

Highly recommend this restaurant!

It's been a few years since I came to Yellowhead but went on a weekend afternoon recently.  I remember the last time it was to volunteer and the room was nice and the food was good.  This time I didn't eat here but the restaurants at the back were pretty empty.  They have a large sign advertising the daily specials and the prices seemed decent.

The layout is large and spacious and fairly modern unlike a smelly, old, casino.  I found there were plenty of walking around and the machines weren't so close together that you feel cramped.  It wasn't too busy inside so lots of selection of machines for those feeling lucky.  There were 2 self serve coffee stations to keep customers awake so they can keep plugging away at the slots.  The washrooms are large and clean.

Too bad they don't have a venue for live entertainment as it's a nicer place than some of the other local casinos.

Admittedly I'm not sure how NY style pizza should taste, but this here is good eats, imo. I've ordered the stromboli and the pizza and haven't been disappointed. Stromboli was very good. The cucumber salad is my favorite.  The chocolate cake is multiple layers of amazing!

The pizza by the slice is enormous! Ordered a slice of the veggie lovers minus onion and a small custom pizza so I had options. If I'd known the veggie slice would be so large I wouldn't have ordered anything else! 

I haven't been into the restaurant but ordered delivery. The time in delivery was much faster than the estimate and went without a hitch. Definitely my new go-to for pizza delivery.
This place has really great food.  The General Tso's is delicious.  I order from here at least once a week and the food is very consistent. Delivery is also very quick.

I have reviewed this place before, but it deserves another 5 star review after my experience last night.  The pizza was delicious and the salads were perfect.  Our food was ready exactly when they said it would be.  Perfect experience once again.

This place is fun and right in the heart of Ybor! Great, unique wines & delicious food!! The eggplant salad is savory and not too heavy, and saganaki is a must. Joe is a great server and we had a great time :) Opa!

Mmm! Their pho sure is tasty. Good broth similar to Tau Bay (my current favourite). The large bowl is $8 (I think.. forgot already), and it's a standard large bowl of pho, maybe just a tad too many noodles for my liking but that just means more food for me! I ordered #14 which was 'brisket, tendon, tripe, and crunchy' possibly also 'fatty'. They give you a good amount of all the bits (though not as much tripe) - the 'crunchy' was my favourite - it's the white-ish piece of chewy tendon that sometimes comes attached to the brisket (I know this will gross some of you out, but for those of you who are like me and like weird textures, you'll know what I mean) - I've never seen in served in pho anywhere else and thought it was a great addition. The broth comes with onions and green onions, no parsley, which is great for me. Garnishes included fresh bean sprouts, a wedge of lemon, and a good bunch of thai basil. In addition to the usual spicy and sweet sauces, they also had some chili flakes in chili oil, which added a nice smoky kick to my soup. Yum. We also had the green onion cakes to start - two large, fluffy cakes for $4-5 - pretty good though not enough green onions in it for me. I'd recommend getting a small pho if you're going to order the green onion cakes. 
Service was good and fast, even though it was pretty busy (more than half full). They accept credit cards here which is nice. I'd definitely come back here again - in fact, it may take over as my new favourite pho place due to its location (easy to get to on Kingsway, ample free parking), the 'crunchy' bit, accepting credit cards, and being open pretty much during regular restaurant hours (vs Tau Bay, which closes pretty early on the weekdays I think and sometimes closes for weeks at a time).

I have been several times since they opened a few weeks ago. The food is fresh, well cooked and delicious. The owners are very sweet people with great pride in their food and service. What an amazing addition to Frazer!!!
I called and was automatically put on hold, and after being on hold for five minutes I was greeted with nothing but someone with a very unsubtle attitude screaming "we're closed"

Service is poor. Food is decent.

Server never brought Gluten Free Menu after it was requested at table. I had to get up after approx 7 min of waiting and get one at the front. Kids never got their "included" Chocolate Milk after clearly ordering it with their meals. After we asked for additional napkins, Server comes to our table with a roll of paper towels like you would find in a residential kitchen and starts unrolling it, asking me to let him know how many cut sheets we want..."1,2,3..." I was kinda caught off guard and just responded saying, "that is good". I have never seen this type of performance at a restaurant myself...maybe some restaurant locations provide napkins this way but to me it is sloppy. In total, our server made approx 4 total visits during our visit (one to take our drink order, one to take our food order, one to ask if our food was good and one to drop off our check). Other 2 visits were done by drink runner and food runner. Server had no personality, no interest on how we were doing, no attempt at light conversation, no drink refills, no closing statement like "thank you for coming by", "have a good night", etc.

Anyway, our food was decent and nothing special. Service really disappointed us. Would we come back(?)...probably not. There are other great restaurants nearby that we would choose over "Good Wood".

we were there saturday evening and had a fantastic meal..started with baked portobellos and carpaccio, both outstanding, my wife thought the carpaccio was one of the best she's had..split a terrific penne putenesca and then had the special branzino and a wonderful chicken..we were greeted warmly by Anne and Franco, served amazingly by Marcos and visited often by the the superb chef Giovanni..also enjoyed a couple bottles of Vernaccio from their very nice wine list..and outstanding dining experience..we live in Redondo beach, so a bit far to become regulars but definetly will return as often as possible, thank you for a great evening
Down from Brooklyn. This places' pork Mei fun makes me want to move here. Exceptional service too!

Usually solid but everything is dropping off. Waited 45 minutes and our food wasn't even out yet. The waitress was more concerned about getting the 20 people who showed up afterwards by at least 10 minutes their beer and spending another 10 minutes putting in their orders into the computer. Ran by once telling us it would be out shortly and then nothing for another 15 minutes. The owner is allowing this place to go downhill quickly. I use to be a regular, now a last resort.

OK, apparently this place was super well known and had a super amazing reputation! ( That's always a bit scary-- will it measure up to its  big rep?) 

For one  of our meals out we decided to wait the time it took to get in ( an hour and a half.) Luckily there are bars and coffee shops around the corner and they text you when it is your turn to get seated. 

Our waiter was super nice. Our appetizers were a bit delayed. He apologized like ten times, comped the apps and gave us dessert on the house too!

I ordered the blacked redfish with an amazing hollandaise sauce. It did not disappoint. My husband had BBQed shrimp which were pretty much the best thing ever, so delicious and spicy. Our alligator cheesecake was creamy and savory- not to miss. I mean, even the salad was delicious. 

I was so impressed that it lived up to its hype and would absolutely do the wait again.

Five Stars!  Pretty lofty....here is why: 

1) We ate at the bar and were welcomed warmly, offerred suggestions on the menu, immediately made to feel at home and enjoyed the time there. 

2) Had a wonderful meal but we will get there. 

3) Had an opportuinity to meet with Chef John Besh (picture is to the left!!) This guy is the best.  First his perspective on food I just get and love.  Second he doesnt try to shove that perspective down your throat in every construct.  Third he got up from a friendly lunch to spend time with us and was happy to do so.  

This third point speaks to Chef Besh as a businessperson and a man.  How great is it that his staff knew they could ask him to do that and it wouldnt be an issue? !  

On to the food.  Wonderful!  My most lovely wife had the grilled ham and cheese and the tomato soup.  She raved.  Served in a can they pour the soup over a basil aoli.  I had the pulled pork "sloppy joe".  Vinegary, saucy metling into the bread.  All the things you want in a sloppy joe.  

This was Besh experience number 2 of the trip and it was altogether wonderful and a significant highlight of the trip.
It's the wine (Red Romance) that brings me back every single time. Although, I tried the short rib risotto this time...and it was delicious!

This restaurant is amazing! You can sit outside and enjoy the water or sit inside the friendly-family restaurant. We ordered the chocolate chip pancakes and they were delicious! The food was amazing and came out quick. They also had very good prices for big servings. I would definitely recommend this restaurant for breakfast!
Had a really nice time. Good food nice cocktails. Was there on a first date(tinder). Would recommend it had a nice decor and feel to the place.

Isn't there an option for a rotten tomato?!?! They don't even deserve one star. I find it hard to believe people actually spend money in this place. The owner is rude and is horrible to his customers, and the bartenders are right there with him. I'll never spend my money there. Avoid this place.

Everything they say about this place is TRUE. After trying nearly every "famous" cheesesteak place in Philly, I've crowned this one the winner. Steak, onions, mushrooms, and American.  Thank me later.

My go-to delivery place. Excellent pizza and the french fries are cooked perfectly every time. Desserts are pretty good as well, your standard Italian pizza place fare (cannolis, slices of chocolate cake, etc.).

Brophys restaurant & clam bar is a must if you're local or visiting the Santa Barbara area expect weekday wait times 15-25 minutes weekends are a different story 30 mins plus but it's worth it.
Hands down Cioppino, Hot Combo is a must. 
Seafood pasta is a hit here just like the famous Brophys New England Clam Chowder.
Enjoy

We went here with a Groupon and dang it was good! I am always a fan of those build your own pizza for one price places and this one did not disappoint. 

The guy who helped us was freaking hilarious! I can't remember his name, but he was great! He was incredibly funny! 

All the ingredients looked good. And they tasted even better! I got lots of veggies and cheeses and the red sauce with the traditional crust. I ate half of it there and was very full! It re-heated well which doesn't always happen with pizza... We were both very, very happy with the pizzas!

The restaurant was very clean. There was a good beverage selection. Tim got some soda in a glass bottle. He liked it. If we are in this part of town again, we will be going back!!!!

I've been to Tacos and Beer many times.  Food's good and service was fine.  Recently (a week ago) they did away with their $1 happy hour tacos. When my wife and I went in on Thursday, I ordered a beer and looked at the menu for tacos.  When I went to order 5 tacos the waitress then says that the old happy hour specials are no longer available.  The sign on the wall says $3 draft during happy hour.  OK, fair enough, I'd ordered a draft.  Then the waitress tells me, "Oh, sorry, the beer you ordered isn't $3, it's just a select few. (This fact is not mentioned on the sign).  The bartender explained that they didn't charge me more than the regular price.  Wow! Imagine how thrilled I was.  He also mentioned that their signs were wrong, but they hadn't changed them yet.  So, I guess customers are supposed to know the price by osmosis.  Imagine ordering a $10 burrito and being charged $15 because they hadn't changed the menu - but meant to.  They have the right to have or not have "happy" hour, but right after making a change they might want to let people know.  The place was usually fairly full at this time of day and we were the only ones in the place.  Except for the four waiters all waiting for customers.

Quick service - fast service.  Very kid friendly.  Company burger was a little greasy but tastes great.  Fries a little salty for my taste but rest of family liked them.  Onion rings - very lightly battered, great flavor.  A bit pricy for burgers ($30 for 2 burgers, fry, onion rings and 1 drink).  Didn't leave feeling overstuffed.

This is a nice AYCE BBQ and hot pot place. We came here on Saturday and it's almost packed. Ryan was our waiter. He's nice and helpful. Basically  most of meat are marinated. For me, all marinated meat tasted more sweet. Besides, the seafood was fresh. The price is fair.

Overall, it's a nice experience.

We were blown away by the quality of the sushi. I wasn't expecting much but was overwhelmed by the service and presentation. They have an excellent selection of sake and have limited inside and outside seating. Overall we will really loved this place and will return again!

I Love Sushi is just like the name sounds. Cute. Fun. Honest.

The restaurant is tiny with just a few tables - the perfect place for a lunch on your own or a dinner with a few friends. For the ultimate experience, try to go outside of the downtown lunch rush or during dinner time when the downtown core has quieted down.

The menu is considerable and offers everything from hot food (appetizers, tempura, soups, teriyaki chicken, etc) to sushi (maki, sashimi, cones, etc). The pricing is great for quality sushi. I love that they don't try to impress anyone with their decor, or their presentation - they let the food speak for itself. Fresh ingredients, great customer service and no frills - in a good way.

Aside from dining in, they have great takeout service - you can even call in your order and then come by to pick it up later. If you're looking for a quick sushi fix for a great price, I Love Sushi won't disappoint.
Happy mouth!!!  Everything you have heard about their greatness is true.  Go there and wait in line if you have to because yes, it is worth the wait.  Best enjoyed hot at the counter.  EnJOY!
Michelle was our server and she was so attentive to us and our 15 month old son. Food was spectacular. Definitely a must stop place when you're here in Reno

Great atmosphere and love the salsa and queso dip! If you order the queso dip make to to devour it fast enough because it will get cold pretty fast and then it will start thickening up.. also I ordered the arroz con pollo and I was a little disappointed since the waiter told me it was very good and flavorful and I mean I'm no expert here but I am Hispanic and I'm not sure this was up to standards... kinda tasted pretty basic and needed some touch of some sort... my boyfriend ordered the shrimp salad and he LOVED every bite of it! I will be back again to try something different though to see what else is out

Definitely a great sushi restaurant with a great selection, very fair prices and excellent service.  The icing on the cake is that they have $2 domestics and import beers everyday.  Their jalapeno roll is really good, and they always have specials that aren't always on their regular menu.  I highly recommend this restaurant!
Love their breakdast. Get there early because thry get busy. You need to get the danish basket.

Had a great meal and great service!  If you are in a hurry let them know and they will accommodate, service was impeccable and plates beautiful.  This menu is very creative and eclectic, not a good place for the picky eater. I am a retired chef and would go back in a heartbeat! The absolute best chocolate pana cotta I have ever had!  I sat in the main room of the house but they have seating upstairs and in a garden area that is beautiful. Signage is small and the entrance is on the side, so be looking for the street address. 
So glad I missed the parade to go an eat here.

I kind of have to agree with Scott on this one..
Was not impressed and severely disappointed.
1 - Smoke filled the restaurant and didn't expect that
2 - Slow meal delivery and potato side was cold
3 - Ordered medium to have a sizzling hot plate delivered with the filet nearly well done
4 - Side salad probably had more dressing than lettuce

I may try this place again, so you never know

Formerly El Sol, think they had to change the name due to legal reasons. Same great food different name. It's a tad overpriced but this place is the best authentic Mexican in town. Doesn't matter what you get it's all very good, the interior atmosphere is nice as well. My only complaint is I don't go very often since its in kind of a ghetto location and off the beaten path. If you're feeling adventurous give this place a try!

We had lunch at On the Border today. We were a little disappointed because it was such a beautiful day and we wanted to sit outside, but their outdoor seating area was not open. That's the only reason I'm giving this review a 4 instead of a 5. Our waitress, Katie, was outstanding!!! She was super attentive and very pleasant. We had ordered sodas to drink and she had refills to the table just as we were finishing our first drink. She checked on us several times to see if we needed anything. She held up our lunch order just a bit so we could enjoy our appetizer before our lunch entrees came out. Honestly, the best dining experience we've had in a long time.

While I understand that there's some hurdles business have to overcome because of the state of the nation (pandemic) it really doesn't excuse the lack of certain customer service.  Used to be a regular before the whole pandemic.  Since they've reopen I tried it out 3 separate occasions.  On all three occasions I've walked up to the bar and I'll stand there trying to get someone's attention (I assure you on 2 of those occasions it was not busy). They've gone as far as look me in the eye but not even acknowledge me.  A simple "I'll be right with you" would suffice.  Now if I call for their attention they seem bothered.  Again, I'd understand if they were extremely busy and didn't see me, but that has not been the case.  Don't want to think it's a "race" thing because that's not my "go to".  But I'm truly at a loss. Like I said, I was a regular, always tipped 20% or higher, was always considerate to my servers.  It's a shame, this place was convenient and walking distance from home and I did enjoy their Cannon Burgers.

Second time eating here since August, when I moved to Tucson. First time was fine. This time, not so much. First, the menu has changed in format and seems to offer fewer options. Stephanie, our server was nice, but slow. We had the Spanish Omelette and Eye-Opener breakfast. Omelette was fine. Asked for crispy bacon on the Eye-Opener, didn't get it. Waited to eat until bacon came back and when I did, I noticed pancakes were uncooked all the way through. Whole plate was taken back and returned with crispy bacon and cooked pancakes but way overcooked eggs. I'm not a picky diner, but the eggs had a brown crust and were really rubbery. Manager and server apologized and offered to remake again. My friend had already finished her meal, so I was over it and asked for the check. Nothing comped, not even my soda. I didn't ask for it to be, but just assumed if you've messed up my order twice, I should at least get a free soda. The cashier, however was very nice. He gave me a fully stamped diner's card so I can at least have a free entree on my next visit. He salvaged the experience.

I've been here twice. Once for lunch a couple months ago and once for a birthday dinner two nights ago.
Both times were equally average. There's not a lot of redeeming qualities about this place to justify the 10-15 dollar entrees.
For lunch: ordered the butter chicken that everyone seemed to be raving about. This butter chicken was unseasoned and boring. I think I also got some sort of eggplant appetizer that was overseasoned. Not good at all.
For dinner recently:
I got the Mekenah (lamb in ketchup sauce is what it ended up being). It was about 13$. Nothing interesting at all about the dish. Lamb was cooked okay. Texturally uninteresting. Flavors were just not developed. I also got to taste my boyfriend's chicken kabob which was the driest thing ever and also lacked seasoning. I also got to taste my friend Will's combo kebob plate and the lamb was cooked well and juicy on it, all the other meats on the kebob plate was underseasoned.
Also the waiter bothered me. We were in a giant group of like 14 or so but 2 of us, myself included, ordered 10 minutes before everyone else. My friend who ordered her food early with me got hers about 20 minutes before I finally got mine. I asked the waiter for my food and he's like: "you will get yours with everyone else" like really sarcastically.  
This place is REAALLY BLAND. Spend your money elsewhere, like at the Meskerem, the ethiopian place kind of across the street, or Wei Hong or the Vine if you're going to be on South Grand. This place seriously has average, expensive food.
Super cheap and solid Chinese food. Delivery could be a little faster but definitely great

Date of Visit: 2/26/15
We visited about 4:30/5pm on a weekday so seating, parking, and traffic was easy.

We enjoyed everything about Mimi Blue! The atmosphere was intimate, but very laid back. Clearly it'd be a great spot to meet with friends to share some delicious food! 

Our server was Max, who was very attentive but not overly intrusive to interrupt our dining experience. We shared the the mixed green salad and Mac and queso. Next, my daughter ordered (2) sliders Classic w/ Marinara sauce and Special (chicken ball) w/ spicy cilantro sauce. I ordered the Juggler sandwich that included (3) classic balls w/spicy bolognese  and Parmesan cheese. Then, we shared a pecan toffee oatmeal cookie topped with vanilla bean ice cream and chocolate syrup. The meatballs are filling and neither of us could finish them, but they tasted good warmed up at home. 

Because everything, and I mean everything, was super delicious and I can't wait to return and I fully recommend a visit anytime of the day or night.

Maybe it was because I was way too tired to eat..I don't know. But it wasn't what I thought it would be. I ordered fish tacos with sweet potato fries. Fries were awesome, crisp and delicious. Fish tacos? I loved how they put lettuce instead of cabbage. But I hated that they put red onions in it. It just was not what I would expect from fish tacos. My friends ordered steak and lamb steak respectively. Lamb steak came out perfect. But steak was overcooked. She ordered medium rare but it was medium well done. Of course they didn't charge for it, after my friend declined to have it fixed. 

Food was fine. Service was acceptable, except when the waitress spilt water on our table, dropped a lemon wedge on the floor, and spilt my friend's sweet tea. 

The place was nice...except the tile floor just didn't go with upscale looking interior. 

Overall it was OK..I probably won't return. The menu didn't have the variety I expected.
I really like this place! Great small plates, creative cocktails, nice wine selection and great ambiance.

I try to stop in at Cold Spring Tavern anytime I am in the area.  I recommend it to anyone who is driving through Santa Barbara.  The drive is pretty but the roads can be a bit windy. It's only about 20 minutes away from Santa Barbra.  There is so much history to this little old tavern.  It was established in 1865 as an old Stagecoach stop so it's very fun to visit and see how things were back then since it's been well preserved.  There is a tiny museum where you can purchase souvenirs, a bar and a small restaurant.  The food is very good.  I have had soup and wine at the bar while sitting at the fire when it was raining out and I have also been on a Sunday for the tri-tip sandwiches and beer. Sundays are so much fun because there is a very eclectic crowd sometimes lots of bikers and good people watching.  There is usually live music and a BBQ that serves tri-tip sandwiches for about $10.00 but it comes with fries.  People are friendly and everyone seems to always be having a good time.  I would say this is a must do on a Sunday for lunch.

Great little neighborhood place, near my parents' condo.  Great food, good beer list.  Just a nice little place if you live close by.  I probably wouldn't go out of my way to go here, but I'm happy to go when I visit my parents.

Good little breakfast place in Tucson. 

Eclectic decor but fun and friendly. 

Breakfast menu diverse. 

Food came fast in generous portions. 

Coffee always filled. 

Waitress very friendly.

Recommended!

La Villa just moved and is actually closer to my house now! I'm thrilled! I love their enchiladas and the guy who rated them poorly obviously has never had authentic Mexican food. They are amazingly good and I like the combo enchiladas 1 with tomatillo sauce and 1 with a yummy creamy cheese sauce. They also have the BEST soups ever! The tortilla soup is fabulous, the tomato soup is very unique and delicious and she also makes a great chicken and veggie soup sometimes. My kids love the tortas and my husband likes everything on the menu! For those looking for a healthy option, Estrella the owner will make you a chicken breast salad and it's yummy! 
The family that owns and runs this restaurant is very kind and they make fabulous food!
So glad to have this resturant 5 minutes from my house now! 
Lithia and Valrico aren't known for their family owned restaurants (most are chains) we are so lucky to have yummy authentic Mexican in our neighborhood.

I always heard about the great food  served here but wow what an experience. I guess I should've read the reviews and no go by word of mouth.
The service was poor and the food was poorer!! Let me explain: My waitress and the manager got in a fight in the front of the restaurant. Yes a fight- cursing, the waitress stormed off....totally unprofessional!!!
Oh did I mention this was after my order was taken so someone else had to complete my order. The food was not as described when it was recommended and I was told it would be discounted. I thought that was fair. I was then told that it could NOT be discounted, I swear the second waitress waited until I ate some the food to tell me that. I felt bad for her so I let it be as she has her own issues going on. I just packed up the food and left. 
I was truly truly TRULY disappointed in my visit and will NOT be back.
GET YOURSELF TOGETHER!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

This was my second visit to Mockingbird, and I was quite disappointed. My husband and I ordered the tots as an appetizer. They were pretty good, but quite greasy. Husband and I planned to split the chicken and a side of fries our waitress told us it was a huge portion, so splitting would be perfect. It was pretty dark in there (they sat us in the upstairs outside area) so we couldn't see our meals very well. I cut a piece of chicken- it was pretty tough. As soon as my husband put it in his mouth, I noticed it was TOTALLY raw. Like purple. Totally raw. Husband discreetly spit it out, and we were both nauseated. We didn't make a scene. We told our waitress, she took it back and asked if we wanted another. We had lost our appetites so said no. I expected our entire meal would be comped, they'd offer us a free dessert, SOMETHING. We were charged for the appetizer and the side of fries, which we didn't eat because we didn't have an appetite. $25 (including tip) for the app and side and raw chicken. I was shocked that this sort of establishment didn't even try to make the situation better.
Awful food, dirty glasses.  Steak was chewy and greasy.  Tuscan chicken had a pool of oil on the plate.  Really nasty.

Came here for a company dinner and had the best experience here! At Korean restaurants, if you want to get the wait staff's attention, you click a button and it signals to them that your table wants their attention (important to know if you've never done this before!). Their quality of meat is great, and especially if you're going with a large party, many times the restaurant will give you small free items as "service" for being great customers and ordering a lot. We had round after round of pork belly and I think that's something you should definitely try if you go here. They cook all the meat right in front of you too. Overall, great experience and awesome food. Great for big dinners.

This is a great American restaurant. They have a great burger and fries. The food is good but the service is amazing, friendly and caring. They  accommodated our dog, brought water and made her feel at home.

I've been to Delmonico's in Vegas before and had a great experience, so I had high hopes for Emeril's.  The decor is nice, but it was a little noisy.  We were seated right by the kitchen so you could see what was going on inside.  It was slightly more casual than I was expecting, but still with high prices.  

For appetizers, we started off with:
Homemade Andouille and Boudin Sausages - just OK
Lamb Spareribs - YUM! Def a fav for everyone.
Rabbit Remoulade - Good, but nothing to rave about
Abita Root Beer Braised "Fresh Bacon" Salad - Pretty good portion, and tasty.

Entrees:
Grilled Niman Ranch Double Cut Pork Chop - can a pork chop be any thicker?  it was like a triple pork chop!  cooked perfectly, tasted great, but nothing special.  If you're really into pork chops, go for it.  Oh and the caramelized sweet potatos are amazingly good.  Can I just have an order of that?
Saffron-Chili Dusted Jumbo Gulf Shrimp - The shrimp was boring... but everything else on the plate was delish!  I loved the sweet potato grits

Dessert: 
Sticky Toffee Blueberry Bread Pudding - i must say, bread pudding in New Orleans is fantastic!
Sweet Potato Cheesecake - Honestly it tasted like pumpkin cheesecake to me... pretty boring

Overall an OK meal.  Most of the dishes were good, but nothing blew me away and I definitely expect more from a restaurant with prices like this!  

One thing that bugged me was the disorganized staff.  When they bring out your plates, they wait until there are enough servers to place everyone's food at the table down at the same time (we had 6 people).  But since we were sitting by the kitchen, we could see them waiting around and trying to flag down other servers that were passing by.  Trying to figure out which dish goes where.  It's like they were trying really hard to provide good service, but it just wasnt showing.

Would I go back again? Probably not.
Great service every time. Food comes out quick. Really good Pho broth. My favorite lunch break spot. Kung pap chicken is also a good one.

Biscuit love has a great atmosphere and draws plenty of people in each day. My friend and I had to wait outside in line because of the crowd. Walking into the restaurant it is really awesome how it is decorated and set up. They had a great patio area for outdoor seating. 
As for the food, I wasn't really impressed. My friend and I started off with the Bonuts. She loved them but I was not feeling the blueberry compote with the lemon. It didn't blend well flavor wise for me. For my entree, I had the biscuit and sausage gravy with a side of potatoes. The gravy didn't have a lot of flavor like I was hoping for. I kept having to add salt. I did however love the potatoes. I also enjoyed the mimosas. The prosecco and orange juice were balanced perfectly! The service was excellent and staff wonderful. I will give it another try in the future and try some of there other food options.

I've lived in Italy and had divine Italian in Philly. La Baia is just "meh". Its a no frills, home cooked decent place, but the food is too hit and miss for me. The killer is the awful attitude put on by the owners who feel they're doing the world a favor for having this eatery. Bottom line, that even with barely decent food, the attitude and the jacking up of prices, you'd be much much better off going to other places. 
Philly is full of AMAZING italian food. Skip La Baia. They overcharge and give you such attitude it's not worth getting up to go there even if you lived in the area.

This review is geared towards the dance club section referenced by anna marie c. There are a couple tables and loungey sofas around the edge of the floor and the DJs have played requests for us in the past. Mirrors line the walls, probably to make it feel bigger, but useful for checking out the room to dodge creepy guys dancing out of your field of view. D'angelo's feels pretty under the radar, which I don't mind b/c it means there's a little more space on the smallish dance floor. We find there are usually some small groups and couples on the floor (no bachelorette parties here), but enough elbow room to feel comfortable and to run away from people we don't want to dance with.

Favorite Ethiopian place in town. I have had the coffee ceremony which is fabulous. I really love the veggies here - greens, green beans, etc. Four people can go and easily split the "combo for 3 people" and be out well under $10 a person, and so full you all will think you will never eat again. I also prefer the injera here to everywhere else in town.

For anyone who hasn't tried Ethiopian, it is very different and some of the dishes can be very spicy. Right up my alley :)

Found this quaint spot when looking for pho. I saw the menu and was delighted to see they had a small portion of the sooo without the noodles yayyy. I figured if I had the spring rolls and it had noodles it helps balance my meal without overloading on a huge bowl for lunch. Awesome spot and the staff is very accommodating and quick. The place was super clean and spacious. I'm definitely coming back again for my small portions. Great spot.

It was our first time at Chavas tonight & we weren't disappointed. The service was great. The food was great. The fried tacos were good.....the margaritas were light & tasty. The queso dip was just ok. There wasn't a lot of taste to it. But it was an overall nice experience.we can't wait to come back!

I'm a regular here. We just went to the weekend brunch buffet again and thought I should update my review from 2+ years ago.

The food here is fairly authentic spicy Sichuan/Szechuan food and is in the same ballpark as Tony Hu's famous Lao Sze Chuan in Chicago's Chinatown. Lao Sze Chuan is still better, but this is Indy and that is Chicago - let's keep it real. However, Sichuan is about as good as you get in Indy for Sichuan food and, in many ways, Chinese food in general.

To address some of the negative reviews, which are mostly variations of "I wish this were more like P.F. Chang's". I find these sad and reasons for why there are not more great, authentic ethnic restaurants in metro Indy and why Indy has more chain restaurants per capita than any other city in the US:

"...much of the meat was inedible. Grisly, fatty and not appetizing. Avoid chicken." Translation: "I wish the meat were only the clean, lean, and flavorless chicken breast they serve in chain restaurants." Authentic ethnic foods use almost all parts of the animal.

"...I was horribly disappointed with barely any seafood/ chicken options, no cards indicating dishes..." The menu has something like 6-8 pages of single spaced dishes and she couldn't find seafood / chicken options? And did Sichuan fail to give her the obligatory flash card version of the menu for gringos?

"The ambiance leaves a lot to be desired..." Translation: "I wish they had the pretty horses out front like PF Chang's. It's a hole in the wall authentic ethnic restaurant, not a pimped up chain restaurant that you're used to going to.

"Really don't recommend going to this lace if you 
1. don't eat red meat.
2. Have food allergies, coz i would at least expect labels." They have many non red meat options. Ethnic restaurants generally don't put labels regarding food allergies - it's a foreign concept to them. Back to the chain restaurants with you!

To me, this place is just OK. Nothin too special about it. I visited on a Sunday afternoon with the wife and kids. First, it took 20 minutes for water to arrive. Second, tables are way too small for AYCE. I had to ask for two tables to be joined together. Service was a little slow to start, but was ok after things were going. Sushi was ok, nothing too special, nothing memorable for me. Appetizers were same ol. Calamari rings were OK, but comes out in very small servings. I will not return for a while, maybe next time the service will be better and more spot on.

Why a place that specializes in crepes only has one crepe cooktop I have no idea. It took 25 minutes to get one. Completely inefficient system. The eggs were very over cooked. The fruit side was frozen melon and blueberries that had no flavor. The staff seemed confused and annoyed to have to be working. On the scramble the cold cheese they put on top was never melted and again the eggs were over cooked and they charged $.75 for each add on which was just like a couple leaves of spinach and a few chopped onions. Ridiculous. The side salad was just a few leaves if mesclun with a raspberry vinaigrette. No options for dressing, that's just what you get. If you're not going to give options then maybe use something a little less specific. And just leaves? I mean add something else. At least some other veggies. I can't see a reason I would ever go back.

Gogos Greek Grill is a Greek fast food place that's a combination of Chipotle for  Mexican and Subway for sandwiches. You walk down a cafeteria line and pick whether you want a gyro, wrap, or salad, and then tell the staff how you want your meal stuffed, topped, and splashed.

The food is served fast, but it's honestly not as good as other Greek eateries around Tampa. One thing they do have going for them is their location. You'll find Gogos on Kennedy just east of Westshore Blvd in a small strip mall.

My first time at Gogos I ordered a gyro, and I was quite underwhelmed. The meat was sitting in a warming tray, rather than being sliced fresh off of a spit. As a result the combination of beef and lamb was dry and overcooked. The pita bread was warm, the veggies were fresh, and the tzatziki sauce had a nice flavor, but the crunch of the dried-out meat was blah.

On my second visit I played it safe and ordered a standard Greek salad with lettuce, tomato, cucumber, onion, pepperoncini, Kalamatta olives, and feta cheese all sitting on a bed of potato salad. The salad was better than the gyro, but not as good as Greek salads that I've had at other places around town. I also ordered a side of hummus with pita chips, and that was pretty good.

If you're near the Gogos location then it's a safe spot for a quick lunch, but if you're looking for a good Greek meal than I'd recommend that you keep driving.

We came here based off many suggestions from locals. Let's just say they did not disappoint! We went for taco Tuesday which makes all the tacos $2. We got the fried oyster, duck, the Carolina, and the calypso taco. They were all beyond delicious. Our server Daisy was welcoming and informative as well. I suggest stopping here if you can. It's well worth it. Out side seating  was nice and shaded too!
I've gotten food here several time and never had a problem. Staff was always quick and polite. Food was always tasty and relatively quick(not as fast as McDonald's, but equivalent to Burger King).

I love love love this spot!!!!!!Enjoyed everything about this spot on a beautiful Monday for lunch. The only thing that was crazy is we stood @ the outside booth to be seated & no one came.Then eventually a server told us to go in to be seated outside. That was weird because there was always a hostess to seat you outside. They need to have signs so the customers will know. But when i mentioned it i was told that the hostess are only outside on the weekends & the weekdays you have to walk inside to be seated outside...makes no sense but we still enjoyed our food!

My son and I come here every week for sushi. He says "it is awesome and yummy!"  They have great prices for all you can eat for kids under 11 and if you don't like sushi they can accommodate as well. The service is usually pretty fast too! And surprisingly they have a pretty good wine list too!
Fantastic food at reasonable prices, especially considering the generous portions. Great atmosphere for dates or small parties.

Fool me once, shame on you.  Fool me twice, well, you know...  I first went to Latin Fusion a year ago, close to when it first opened.  The food was quite good, but I was extremely disappointed with the service.  Everything was slow and once our food was delivered, our server never approached our table to check on us, which prevented me from ordering an enticing cocktail I had eyed up on the drink list.

Tonight I decided to give this restaurant another chance, hoping they had gotten their act together since their initial opening.  At the time we were seated, there was one other party (granted, a large party) in the restaurant, and it took us a long time to even have a server approach our table.  After ordering drinks, the beer we ordered was quickly delivered, but my glass of wine took about another 10 minutes.  After about 20-25 minutes of being no where near placing a food order, we decided to cut our losses and end our experience with the drinks.  Both visits have been very disappointing.  I will not be returning.

Met a dear friend here for beers and a bite and was completely surprised at how great it was.  I had probably the best grouper sandwich I can remember in a long time, along with the dreaded bu efficient shoestring fries.

Tiny and on the water tucked inside a marina, this is the place to go to eat in or to buy fresh and take home with you.
Wow!  This is a gem.  Make reservations and enjoy.  Can't say enough good about the Red Pony.  It's amazing.

There are so many things I love about this place. My company held their Christmas party here one year and it was amazing. The steaks were cooked to perfection, the service was great, and all the drinks were well worth the money paid. 

The cheesesteak egg rolls were the best I've ever had, and the Banana Cream Pie Martini is something I would order every time I go back.

It was really crowded on a Wednesday night when I went (FYI for some reason they have a rule of no falafel sandwiches at Wednesday lunch).  I ended up getting to sit in the front window bar seating area which is a bit tight with tiny metal stools to balance on.  I had the lamb flatbread and while everything was good, fresh and great quality I found the portion size to be way too small for the price.  I've had far better lamb and rarely such a small portion size of lamb.  I was sitting right next to some folks that got the "Falafel Feast" which for $28 gets you falafel, flatbread, hummus, baba ghanouj, yogurt, pickles, slaw, house salad, tahini, cilantro chile sauce and toum which made me quite jealous of how awesome their food looked.  The hibiscus iced tea was flavorful and nice but a bit expensive at $3 for iced tea.  The only meat dishes currently are the lamb flatbread, chicken salad and shrimp.  For the price and small selection I'm probably going to prefer another Middle Eastern restaurant most of the time but this place has a unique flair to it that will give it the occasional appeal for something a bit different.

Generally I liked this joint and would rate it around a 3.5 except it does lack a bit in value for the meat dishes and they are quite lacking in delighting carnivores here but they make some amazing looking and tasting salads.

Okay so I found this place on a whim this morning. My love from Indiana is in town visiting and she requested coffee this am. So rather than hitting up Starbucks, I prefer to find somewhere local and share some love to small businesses owners instead. Most shops were closed this Sunday morning but Bowtie was not! Oh my lanta! I loved the overall pleasing atmosphere of this place. But what really got me was my latte. Absolutely amazing. I got the honey lavender latte and quickly there was a small party in my mouth. Did I say this place was amazing?! I got mine with almond milk rather than whole and it still was so good. Please if you get a chance stop by and have a latte from this little coffee shop. You will not be disappointed. I can't wait to return next week!

With such great reviews, maybe I was expecting  more but for one I had to keep my coat on the entire time I was there because it was freezing! The coffee was ok, the tea was very good and I love that they give you a pot. Getting on wifi was easy but most places are these days. For as many coffee shops as there are to choose from, I would go somewhere warmer.

I can't believe I've lived in Nashville for 26 years and have never tried the magic that is Five Points Pizza. Talk about hitting the spot after having a few drinks at a nearby brewery! We got a slice each, which is all you need to have a savory pizza experience. Clearly the joint is popular, as the main restaurant was pack to the brim. We walked over next door and discovered a 'to-go' area where you can also buy by slice. This place brought back lots of delicious New York-pie style memories -- authentic and flavorful. Thank goodness we only stuck with a slice, not that I would have been ashamed to walk the streets of East Nashville donning a major food baby. So good. So tasty. Get thee to Five Points.

I popped into Le Bar Lyonnaise with the GF for an after dinner drink and was pleased with the space almost immediately.  It's dark, quiet and comfortable; ideal for warm glass of wine at the bar.

We had only been there 10 minutes or so when the GF started elbowing me in the side in an effort to point out that Chef Perrier was sitting a few seats away from us at the bar.  Chef Perrier, who is almost a caricature of himself, was fantastic company, and after a bit of conversation, he insisted on ordering us a dessert plate and a plate of petit four.  Needless to say, the desserts were delicious.

In addition, we had several glasses of wine, all of which were delicious.  The only concern is that the list isn't huge and the cheapest glass of red I can recall was still $12.

I can't wait for the opportunity to return for a proper meal and update this review to 5 stars!

Very pretentious crowd(for breakfast!!). Fresh ingredients with very little flare or flavor. Banana Pancakes were overly sweet, Benedict was boring, and potatoes were potatoes. A "cafe " for rich people I suppose.
Really great healthier food when I needed a break from the heavy new Orleans eating. Great staff and decent prcies

Great food at this place, but I saw some review herein that claims this restaurant is "quiet?!?!?!" I thought to myself, "Are you serious?" The seating is atop one another. The restaurant plays music with far too much bass within the EQ. Diners literally are nearly atop one another. This place has great, amazing food, but to see reviews on YELP that state this restaurant is "quiet.." is grossly inaccurate. Sorry. Great place, great food, but not at all romantic or quiet. It's not as loud as Macaroni Grill or similar places, but it's pretty loud once inside. Great food, again. Know it will be a bit loud, but the food will be amazing. The service is at this place is very inconsistent. If you have a bald, male waiter, unsure of his name, ask for a different server. he's among the worst we've had in years.. not kidding.

The rudest bar tenders in Tucson Mark is a giant stress mess every time I've been in and can't keep track of orders or paid tabs. JOJO is a real I can't even say the word on here..... After serving me an appetizer with uncooked bacon decided to pay to try something else tried to order sliders without the burger and she said " does this look like fucking Burger King?" I will never come back here worst staff of any establishment I have ever been to.....

If you are looking for some amazing soul food.  The Praline Connection is the place to go!

We had friends in town and we wanted to show them what good cajun-creole style food was.   We went for an early lunch and we were the first ones there so the service was great.  My husband started off with a bloody mary and I had a taste.  It was so good that I got my own.  

For an appetizer we shared the fried chicken livers with sweet hot pepper jelly.  Now, I am not a fan of chicken livers...but OMG these were INCREDIBLE!  The serving was HUGE and definitely enough for 4 or more people.  I popped so many of these perfectly fried chicken livers in my mouth that by the time my entree came I was full....Of course, I made room and enjoyed my stuffed crab plate too.  Our entrees were also served with corn bread and it was delicious.  

Some other items we ordered:
BBQ Ribs
Crawfish Etoufee
Red Beans and Rice with smoked sausage

We definitely left happy and full and all I can say is if you have a chance to visit here you must at least try the chicken livers if anything!
Good food, nothing we ordered was incorrect or not tasty. Good selection of adult beverages at pretty fair prices, which was surprising for Hyde Park. Friendly and attentive service.

Well was headed to an old reliable restaurant when we saw a new restaurant so decided to try something new. 

The valet was available but decided to park ourselves. Just nice to know it's there if needed.  From the moment we were seated we were impressed. The staff was very attentive. We are seated and when I tell you the happiest server in the world came to great us. Jenna C. was an absolute pleasure all night. 

The Martinis were perfect (and I'm picky). Started off with Caesar salad, followed by a perfectly cooked Ribeye and 2 lobster tails. Leave room for dessert. We split a Carrot Cake and it was very good. 

This place is not your cheap steak house but the food and service justify the price. 

I do suggest asking for Jenna C. to make it the perfect dinning experience (even though she is from Chalmette ).
The Pho is so delicious! The egg rolls and spring rolls are so good! The Boba is amazing! I definitely recommend this place!
Under new ownership, but same great food with addition of Greek dishes that reflect the heritage of the new family.

The Legend won the 'which one restaurant do we visit coming through Indianapolis' lottery - myself, my honey and my two kids headed over there this evening.   I had done a search on the 'Good for Kids' filter and after quickly perusing reviews it appeared a good choice for comfort food.  While the food was very good, I would not recommend it as a kid friendly venue.  It's not that anyone treated us badly for having the kids there but it's really a bit more upscale in ambience than I feel comfortable bringing the kids to.

Two of us had the Dad's Crispy Chicken, one pork tenderloin, one beef tenderloin marsala.  Everyone liked their entrees.  The garlic mashed potatoes were particularly good.  The chicken wasn't crispy but was very moist and flavorful.  The baked mac and cheese side was good but not spectacular (it wasn't a pepperjack mac and cheese as others have commented about, this was different).  

One comment is that they were out of several items when I got there and from listening to the wait staff talk to others who came in that list got larger while we were there.  So, go early if you want to be able to pick from the full menu.

Prices were reasonable for the quality of food though there were some higher priced items.  All in all, I'd certainly go back but without the kids.

First the good stuff:  Biscuits, jams, sausage patties, hashbrown casserole = very tasty, good texture. The location and country ambiance are welcoming and engaging; wait staff are genuine and attentive. Prices are fairly reasonable.  Less satisfactory were the ham (dry, tough), garden omelet (veggies are set inside a finished omelet and folded over, nothing to hold them in; very little cheese), red eye gravy (basically watery au jus). Also of note, even if an infrequent faux pas, was the eggshell in the omelet!  I'm glad we came but, having checked it off my bucket list, I have no need to come back for breakfast ; maybe to get the biscuit sampler to go.  Might try their BBQ.

I always past this place on my way to my house and I finally decided to stop in, the smell of the smoked meat was overwhelming and I had to try some. I normally never eat red meat but the smell of the beef brisket sandwich was tearing up my nose. I ordered it and a side of mac and cheese, the mac and cheese I would pass on in the future, but I will be breaking my non-red meat eating habits every time I come to Tom's, the beef brisket was out of this world, and the portion was more the generous, the smoke flavor was present throughout the brisket but was not overwhelming, and the hot bbq sauce was a perfect combination (its not hot at all but with a little kick at the end). I would 100% back a decision to purchase a beef brisket sandwich, you will not be disappointed, I would just say stay away from the sides.

I would not recommend this location every time I've been they've had something either broken or out, this time it was the freeze machine was broken and they were out of fire sauce. Also they cut my quesadilla very awful and do this most times. I may add this is the slowest one I've been to.

Best be bringing your A game when it comes to this hot chicken. With a twist on an East Nashville staple Pepperfire brings you succulent  hot chicken that brings southwestern flavors to mind. 
If you don't like spicy food, ,don't even eat the mild.
The mild is hot in normal food standards, and the Hot is atomic. 
I have yet to eat anything above Hot, and at the moment I don't plan to. Im the guy that dares the Thai food joints to gimme Native, gimme what you got! So Hot is hotter than Native Thai. If you're like that. 
The sides are okay. Nothing to write home about, but it's all about the hot chicken anyway, right?
Best to order before you head there online, with their app, or phone. They make the chicken fresh to order. 
When it comes to attire no shoes or shirts are required here. 
If they cater, it would have to be to groups of people who like to dare each other to eat extremely spicy food.
Great food, great ice custard, super clean and friendly staff. My son loves this place. Highly recommended!

This is a good place if you love spuds! Their menu is amazing! From simple spuds to shrimp/crawfish super spuds. The people working here seem nice and attentive, the place is a bit small but i think that makes this place special. They also have salads, sandwiches and other dishes. Another thing to mention is that the place is suuuuper clean!! There's an app you can download and it will give you rewards (free wedges) and a coupon for $5 off $20. GOOD JOB SPUDLYS

Meh.  I've been here twice and I'm not impressed.  The food is average to below average Mexican food.  Our first time here the server was so rude, I swore I would never return.  The second time a large group talked me into going.  The service was better, but still nothing outstanding.  If you do go, definitely don't get the cheese dip.  It is flavorless.
If I could give fewer stars I would. Service at the bar was absolutely awful. Will never go back. Too many great establishments in NO that want my business.

Southern hospitality at its best. 
The restaurant is so welcoming. The outside is inviting and cozy. The staff is just delightful. The fried chicken is delicious! I had not been here in a while, but I sure will be back very soon!

I am an avid breakfast lover, any time of the day. In the past few months I have changed my eating habits, eating clean and increasing my exercising. Prior to this healthy change I was addicted to McDonalds Big Breakfast. However on this day I wanted breakfast after my workout (protein and fresh veggies). I asked a friend if there was a place in the area to get a delicious omelet. She recommended Tower Delicatessen. After my workout I went immediately to Tower. They have a wide array of meats to choose from from the deli; however today my heart was set on an omelet. I got the Tower Omelet, and had them add some spinach (small fee for the addition) surprisingly, Tower's omelet was delicious. The staff was friendly and healthy. Not sure if breakfast is sold all day, but I will definitely be dining there again. Great to have a nice place to eat "real eggs" and not that powdered, manufactured breakfast that McDonalds provide. Sorry McDonalds, you have lost a customer. Can't wait to try another meal at Tower.

The food was great. The service was fast and kept checking on us. I had the lasagna and the wife has lobster ravioli. The house made lemonade was very good!  Enjoyed a great meal. We will be back for sure! The menu is limited but still has a good selection.

No.8 Grilled Fish in Dried Pot！

The taste is sooooo good！The fish is not Tilapia（all Chinese restaurants here just make Grilled Fish by Tilapia），and the fish tastes tender &smooth. The skin   is my favorite that isss sooo flavored！They put sichuan pepper in it and it's hard to taste it in the Chinese restaurant here， i like the sense of sichuan pepper！ And the we only ordered this meal， and combined with the free appetizer， its definitely enough for two persons. And  we even packed the left fish to home

Not sure what happened to this place.  It used to be good.  Menus were old and gross, saki bottles were the smallest I've ever seen (it's house saki you cheapskates), the sushi was 70% rice... almost like they were loading the rolls up with rice to save on fish and ingredients.  The service was good though.  Tell the chef and the owner to stop skimping.  It's painfully obvious what they're doing... at least at my meal

I just left there about 30 minutes ago and they didnt give me my sandwhich but they did charge me for it. I attempted to call them and complain but they either leave their phone off the hook or refuse to answer it.

I want to keep this place a secret for selfish reason, but I can't. I must spread the goodness. 

Teriyaki Madness is absolutely delicious. The staff is courteous and friendly. You literally must go NOW.  Well, when they open.
Wasn't able to eat here because the wait was 1 hr and 40 min but the drinks, esp the two for one are pretty good.
Excellent sushi and great prices! The grilled halibut cheek and tuna sashimi were both outstanding. The halibut cheek was cooked perfectly!

After visiting Baileys breakfast restaurant and loving it we had to try their burger joint. We were seated upstairs along the rail where we could see everything going on below. I'll get into why this isn't 5 stars first. The sweet tea. That's what got me. It's not Southern sweet. If that's the norm for St. Louis, that's fine, but it deflated me. No other restaurant we have been to has sweet tea and I was excited. Our Server Elena was awesome! She gave great recommendations and has a great personality. She wasn't overbearing and that nice where it feels forced and she didn't try to push the sides or dessert on us. When you see $6 for Mac and cheese, it's worth it! They make their own pickles and the fried ones were pretty good. They are battered, not breaded, so if you don't like them that way you have been forewarned. The Chop House burger is phenomenal, our 6 year old finished his chicken strips before we could even ask if they were good and my wife loved the basic burger. Hot chocolate and marshmallow ice cream, brownie with ice cream and the chocolate shake were all amazing as well. I may be diabetic now, but it was well worth it.

Terrible experience. I ordered a vodka and Red Bull, and ended up paying 9 dollars for basically just a red bull. The drinks were barely alcoholic and there was maybe two or three single bathrooms which had 20 minute waits each. Bartenders were rude. All around not a very enjoyable experience. Would not recommend.

This place is great! Everything was flavorful and fresh, and we had enough food to take home for another meal. I ordered the saag paneer, which was exactly how I like paneer, and my husband really liked his chicken tikka masala. The staff were also super nice and helpful. It's awesome to have such a good Indian restaurant so close to home, especially one that we can get takeout from in the future. We'll definitely be back.

Average indian restaurant, prices are on the higher side and they charge a steep amount for delivery as well.  Their chicken curry tasted old and horrible.  I hope they improve their quality because this area needs an Indian restaurant.  I will not order from the again until I see a review saying their food tastes fresh now.

This was our first time here. We're snow birding in Palm Harbor and was recommended this restaurant by an U er driver. It di not disappoint!

My husband and i shared the Slab For Two, it comes with deviled egg, bread and two side dishes. My husband is a big eater and we didn't eat the whole slab. 

These ribs literally fell off the bone, they were delicious!!

Japanese restaurant but not really authentic. This place was Korean restaurant before it became Japanese, but the people are all the same.  Sushi rolls are ok, and the ramen does taste good; good enough for Boise area.  I haven't found any good ramen yet.  The menu is weird, it has 2 different prices but it is not driven by time.  "When the lower price is listed, then that is the price you pay."  So why not just remove the 'higher' price from the menu?
Sorry you're having a bad morning. Mine was less good when I left. Great product. Not great service.

First time visit and I live within walking distance. Excellent menu, very good service and the sushi was well prepared.  The Bento box is well worth the price as it was more than I could eat. Great addition to the west fishers food scene.

Ran by kids, this has actually happened multiple times where there is a big line around 8-9pm then all of a sudden they close down. I think the staff gets lazy and doesn't wanna deal with the late night rush and decides to close it down.
I absolutely recommend the Asian muscles, the best I have ever tasted! Great atmosphere and prices!
My first burger in Philadelphia. I got to say, it's pretty scrumptious. Juicy, meaty, fun and satisfying. My only complaint was the long wait for my food to come.
If you are looking for a step up from a relaxing bar scene and wanting to dance a bit this is the place for you.  Drinks are alright nothing special but there are tons of people in this place.

I enjoyed a dinner here with friends on a Monday evening a few weeks back. Likely thanks to the pandemic we were 1 of maybe 4 total parties in the entire restaurant. I really appreciated the touchless menu option (you have to scan a QR code on your phone to view the menu). Not only does it help reduce the spread of germs, but they also have free wifi. I've experienced other restaurants with a similar setup since the pandemic began and rarely do they offer free wifi so this was huge to me. 

As far as other safety measures go there were plenty of clear and wooden dividers throughout, seating was arranged so folks could socially distance (if, in fact, there were to be more people dining at the same time), cashless payment was required, and staff wore masks at all times from what I could see. 

As for the food I was completely disappointed. I'd heard SO many good things about this place and had always been curious about the cuisine as it always looked packed out there (*pre-pandemic that is). 
I ordered chow faan and the pork shoulder dish. Frankly it just lacked flavor and didn't taste like much of anything. Despite the portions being a  considerable size, even for small plates, I really didn't find it to be worth the price. I was pretty disappointed in the variety of options on the menu. They call themselves "Asian Street Food" and that is not what I gathered from the selection on the menu at all. 

If anything I'll be back for happy hour as the mule I had with my meal was pretty standard and the overall vibes were good.

Crawfish Etoueffe and it eas Excellent!  Service was outstanding as well!

A Must Try when in the Quarter!

It's been a very long time since I was here last. Like 15 years or more. This past week I joined my wife and two friends for a night out and I was completely thrilled by the quality of food and atmosphere.
