I opted for their early evening 3 course menu and I was glad I chose this option. For the price, it was a bargain. I started off with the tomato bisque. Great depth of flavour and the side grilled cheese was a perfect pairing. 

Next up was the Main course. Cedar plank salmon with a crab crust. Resting on gnocchi and mushrooms with asparagus. Wow. 

The salmon was well cooked and the rest balanced well with the fish. It wasn't too heavy. It was just right. 

To finish the meal I got the peanut butter and jam cheese cake. OMG. Very cool take on a classic. 

This place has survived for 20 years and I can see why. Their menu is amazing. The atmosphere is fantastic. Service is also amazing. I'll be back here once again.

I've been here a couple times and both times I've been disappointed by the size of the dishes compared with the price. It's a hit or miss with the portions and quality. I don't know, I just expect more out of a bbq place. It's okay but would rather go somewhere else.

Great wings! We had parmesan garlic, regular buffalo, & KC bbq. They were all absolutely delicious and very fresh as well. The lady who checked us out and brought our food was very kind, friendly, and great attitude! The owner (guessing he was owner I may be wrong) was very kind and friendly as well! Very glad we tried this place and we will be back!

You can't really mess up breakfast food but there are some places better than others. This was just 'meh'. The food lacked salt, the pancake was alright, and the eggs were bland. The only good thing about our breakfast was the green sauce on the southwest/Mexican breakfast omelette! I would actually LOVE to have that bottled for every day use! 

Come if you're hungry but not in search of a culinary creation. Stay for the dependable and attentive service.

The woman who took my order left me at the counter to sign my receipt without getting my beverage. Then I waited 45 minutes for the buzzer to go off, to no avail. I went back to check on it and they finally found my food, as it was under a different order number and had been sitting under the heat lamp for a hot minute. She didn't offer any apology or anything, just pushed the food at me. And the food just wasn't good. The California Heat taco was so salty (and I love salt; this was inedible). The chicken enchilada was tiny (three bites), there is no cilantro in the cilantro lime rice. I won't be back. This was unacceptable even for Covid related labor challenges. What a shame.

A hidden gem in the Santa Barbara mountains! Amazing food, great atmosphere, and beautiful scenery. Sunday brunches are fantastic! This is a local favorite, so if you are eating at the restaurant on a weekend, make sure to book in advance.

This is a terrible experience, since we travel all the way from Texas, and planing to go explore the city later night. But the whole dining time took more than 2 hours, each dish took at least 40mins to get on the table, I don't know if the waitress is racist, they give other table fried pig sink as appetizers (as the restaurant's tradition). She didn't give to us even we ask for it. When we check out, they miscounted our happy hour dish to regular price and argue with us about it. NOT RECOMMEND AT ALL! And the food is very salty!!!!

This place is a complete joke. Several reasons to not eat here. I was on vacation last week and me and my boyfriend were pretty freaking hungry. We heard that this place usually has a line out the door, and we figured it must be for a reason. I ordered the ham po boy because they were supposed to be known for their "oven baked ham" there was nothing special about this sandwich just bread ham and a tiny bit of shredded bagged lettuce. I paid r $40.00 for two sandwiches and two soft drinks! What a rip off. The soda I ordered tasted dirty and I didn't take more than a few sips.. for three dollars a soda someone should regularly be cleaning the line... To make matters worse you order at the register but then they have waitresses bring the food out to you... what is the point of that? As if it wasn't bad enough I spent $40 on two lousy sandwiches .. I mean SADwiches..  Now I have to tip the waitress who cant even keep a clean restaurant? After eating half of my food I realized the place was filthy, and if I wasn't so hungry I probably would have noticed sooner. Long story short I ended up feeling like crap the next three days, and my guess it was probably due to this joke of an establishment. I am warning all those who read this do not waste your time or money on this place, because they don't deserve either.

Here for lunch today. We had grouper fingers comma soft shell crab sandwich, and a grilled grouper sandwich. All of them just right boys and with the fried foods crispy batter. Wait staff is very friendly and we were served quickly. I also must mention a very nice view of the river.
There are no words can't explain how delicious they are...yummy . From the foods to service all awesome. I'm telling y'all perfect place

I finally got around to trying this place... Food honestly was good... But I think it was a bit tooooo salty. Catfish was amazing, again too salty!! My favorite has to be the Mac and cheese.. Yummy cornbread! Sweet tar sure was sweet, maybe too sweet for my liking. Peach cobbler was not what I expected. The consistency was very thin and watery... And oh my was it sweet... Customer service though... I must say they were very nice pleasant people!!

Yes, yes, yes.  Everything about this place is great.  It is by far the best Italian food in Tampa, and from what I have experienced from the four times I have been to this restaurant, you cannot go wrong with whatever you order!  It is tucked away in a strip mall (per typical Tampa) and is pretty small.  They typically do not take reservations, so while you are generally okay Sunday-Thursday, I would try to get there as early as possible on weekend nights (they open at 5:30 and any time between 5:30 and 6:00 is okay usually).  

These people are true Italians!  They have Italian accents, it seems to be family owned, and they are so freaking nice.  One time I went on my birthday and they gave me my meal for free, which I thought was very kind.  

My favorite dish has been the pink lasagna.  It tastes incredible!!! I took part of it home and reheated it the next day and it was even better somehow.  I have also tried the lobster ravioli (amazing) and the beef carpaccio (also amazing).  

To sum things up: Great people, great service, great food.

After coming here a few more times since my last post, I have to bump this place down to three stars. Mostly because I find it completely frustrating that one cannot put a comment or request into the computer from which you order and the cashier/shift manager (who, ironically, avoids the cashier counter like the plague) is quite unyielding when requests like "can I get a side of lettuce with that?" or "can I get less noodles in my stir-fry?" Sometimes, I don't want a pound of noodles in my stir fry. Sometimes, I want  lettuce in lieu of noodles in my stir fry. Not only can you not substitute in lettuce for the noodles (which you pay for), you also cannot even pay EXTRA for the lettuce? What do you mean I cannot pay you for something?! Very frustrating and inflexible ordering system. Not to mention how the entire meal prep process would go MUCH faster on the meal prepper's end if they had a display screen showing them what goes in an order, rather than having to squint down at a receipt with size 6 font to read what goes into each persons order. 

Simple changes like adding the ability for special requests and a better order display for their employees would go a long way. The food is still real good, but perhaps equally frustrating to get. I'm still coming but may just get too peeved one day...

Came here for dinner on a Friday night since it was the only place that had reservations available. Clearly that was for a reason. The bread served was more like Texas toast drenched in butter. The "paella" was just seafood on top of some rice on a plate. Overall it tasted bland and rubbery but the mussels specifically tasted like I might have food poisoning in an hour. 

When it came time to get the bill, we were thrown off by the fact that we could only split between two cards and we weren't told the tip was included (we were a table of 5). As we were trying to figure it all out the system timed out and charged the first card without our approval. 

There are a myriad of great places to go in the Gayborhood. Don't go here.

I believe that when you ask a local for a recommendation, it's probably worth listening to.  Especially if that local is someone you trust.  That's how we ended up at the Rockaway Grill.

It was a sunny Wednesday morning when we found ourselves on the beach at Clearwater, right near Frenchy's Rockaway Grill.  Although not hot, it was a warm March day and prompted us to decide to get a cool beverage at the bar, which was very crowded.  We were fortunate enough to find two seats just opening as we made our order, so we naturally slid right into them.

As we sat, cooling off with our beer, the smell of the food overcame us and although we hadn't entered hungry, we quickly became so.  Another recommendation from the local was to try the grouper, so we decided to see if he could be 2 for 2.  One of the offers was for grouper nuggets, which came with fries and coleslaw.  Since we weren't starving, we thought it would be a good choice to share.

My local guide was now 2/2.  Frenchy's, of course, exists in multiple locations, so I don't know what all of them are like, but if this is any recommendation, I'm game to try all of them now.  The grouper was battered, fried and light.  The outside was crispy, with a moist tender chunk of meat inside.  The fries were just right and it's pretty hard to beat washing it all down with a cold beer.

If that's not enough for you, you're sitting right on the beach with about a 200 yard walk to the water.  It was early spring break season so the beach and restaurant was getting crowded already, and in speaking to the bartenders, it sounds like that's pretty much here to stay for the rest of the summer.  Time your visit intelligently, but if you can manage to find parking and a spot on the beach, this should be your next stop.

Arrived right after opening on a Saturday. Too small of a location. Waited. No service, no pizza, not worth it... I'm going to Cheesecake Factory. (Which is saying something considering the wait) 
Try again Giordanos, you're not ready for Indy. #Disappointed

This was the first stop on a pastry and bread crawl through town, and it was a great beginning! The croissant was perfect - baked dark, flaky and buttery, and not doughy or bready at all. We also got a chocolate macaron. I'm not a fan of macarons, but this was a good one. And finally, a peanut butter cookie, which was enjoyed by all. Great work!

First time eating there was last night. Great Place for fresh HOT foods. Plenty of choices. Good Sushi, has Hiachi for your selection too.  The place was very clean. Staff very friendly. 
I will return again for sure.

Good for family and friends. Plenty of seating if large group is needed. Carry Out Available

Since Cafe Mingala in New York City closed, Rangoon became the third bucket-list item when we went to Philadelphia yesterday because we want to have some Burmese food. Our trip was largely a success, but this seals the deal. I couldn't ask for better food and Crystal even said that she would dream of the food. Yeah. It's that good. 

We got there shortly after 5pm (Friday) and it wasn't that busy. There were customers piling in as we ate. As for the menu items? Phenomenal. Even though the menu items were generally inexpensive, the two of us splurged a bit knowing that there aren't that many opportunities to have Burmese cuisine. The best part about the menu isn't the prices. There are no surprises here. They will tell you what's on the dish, what ingredients there are. So God forbid you are allergic to seafood, peanuts, sesame, etc., you know you should avoid them or ask for special arrangements. 

FIRECRACKER LENTIL FRITTERS: The menu describes the dish as some grounded lentils with blend of onions, int and chili spices. In other words, it would probably remind you of a falafel patty. There's three of these little patties, which just fit inside my palm. They are by themselves not very spicy, unless you add the sauce to them. They're not deep fried like a falafel ball, but fried enough for a good texture. I'd recommend. ($6)

ASIAN TEA LEAF SALAD: Neither of us would usually eat salad, but this is always an exception. The tea leaves are combined with cabbage, tomatoes, sesame, peanuts, garlic, fried onions, and dried shrimp. You're expected to get a wild fusion of flavors and textures. Therefore, the taste of the tea leaves may be a little subtle. But it's still good, fresh, crisp. Very yum. ($9)

SHAN HIN LAY FISH: This is a steamed fish, not sure what kind of fish it is. It's fileted, but marinated and steamed with various ingredients such as onions, tomatoes, coridian, and hot peppers. Subtly sweet, mildly spicy, it went great with the...

GOLDEN RICE: We ordered two of them, expecting that they would be served only in a bowl. Instead, our server gave us two round plates of the rice. The fried onions and sesame really impacted the fragrance and the flavor. Add in the turmeric, which gave the rice a distinctive golden yellow color. I'm a big fan of rice, but she who normally isn't, enjoyed the rice a lot. She didn't finish hers because she wanted to try... ($3.50 a plate)

THOUSAND LAYER BREAD WITH COCONUT MILK: This. Get this as your dessert. The bread resembles a roti pancake that you would see in Malaysian restaurants. It is slightly chewy, but surprisingly not flaky. It comes quartered with a layer of a cream made coconut milk. They served it with a cherry on top. I had a slice of it and let the bread lover dreamingly munch on the three remaining pieces. ($4.50)

Our servers were very nice and friendly. Would definitely return.

This place is fun! Large selection, and delicious!

I was in line trying to decide, and a nice man that worked there came up and offered his opinion. I got the turkey sandwich with cole slaw and fried corn on the cob. So good!

You can't go wrong here and a must if you are in St Louis! A+++

I kept getting signs that I need to try a beignet. Signs as in 2 friends posting beignet pictures on facebook, so maybe more of a craving for something I've never had. ha. Yelp brought me to Nola Cafe.

It's a cute little decorated place. My friend & I halved our Shrimp Po Boy & Roast Beef Po Boy sandwiches so we could try both. Nothing too fantastic, but still good. Lots of shrimp, roast beef, lettuce.

The real shining star was what I came for: beignets! Overall service was a bit slow (especially for just sandwiches), but this made it all better. We had to wait a while for our dessert, but they're made fresh so that they come out melt-in-your-mouth-hot. MMMMM. Originally, my friend & I were going to share, but after our first serving of 3, we wanted more! 4 people in our party, 4 servings of 3 beignets: 1 for each of us.

My quick tip: don't share your beignets!

Only gave one star cause I had to but I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone We had a party of 19 and they absolutely refuse to seat us even at our own tables. With so many restaurants around save your money and time go somewhere else. Good way to lose business management I would say you need to be replaced by the owner you just let a huge party walk out the front door with our money. Not to mention management wouldn't even give a reason why he wouldn't seat us he just flat said no. That's ok we found another restaurant to take our money and our celebration tonight.

This was a return visit for me and a first for my husband. I continue to be totally impressed and awed by the food at Rawr. This is food like nothing else I have ever eaten. 

We decided to start off with the beet ravioli - I had had it before and knew it was a save bet for my meat and potatoes guy. Solid hit here. It has texture, flavors and spice that mingle delightfully. It tastes like pasta stuffed with ricotta but this is pure vegan - totally nuts and veggies.

We then went with an animal based product and had the pate. I am not a huge fan of pate, but this was amazing. Small discs of light, slightly sweet, rich, creamy pate with persimmon slices (one dried to a chip and another pickled) and lentil crisp. Sweet, spicy, crunchy, and velvety all in one dish.

We finished up with a final vegan dish - trumpet mushroom "scallops" on sprouted lentils and a sauce that I could have sworn was made from caviar. The mushrooms are soaked in a brine that makes them mimic scallops without the adverse reaction I get with eating mollusks. 

Every dish was beautifully presented and very much lend themselves to sharing and savoring. We washed all of this down with a nice light sauvignon blanc by the glass.

This is not cheap. Our total tab, with three glasses of wine, was just under $70, but so worth the cost. I got my food skeptic to try it and he loved it. We will most certainly come back again.

There are few BBQ joints in Tucson and even fewer that would be worth your time, this however is not one of those places. To really have a good gauge on a restaurant that you are going to for the first time you must order something typical of the cuisine to see how well they can do the basics. So i had the brisket meal with 2 sides and my fiance had a pulled pork sandwich with one side. both the brisket and the pork were very satisfying i think the mac and cheese is lacking but then again i am a fan of bold flavor....which the sauces do have with out taking away from the meat. I recommend the spicy chipotle  if you enjoy a little heat if not go there other mild sauces are worth a taste as well.  Anyway, if you are in the are and you have hankering its worth stopping by!!!!1

Ok, so I've only been here once but liked it (for the most part)! I thought the seaweed salad was a bit petite. I was also a tad upset it was not a BYOB.

The sushi "boat" was fun. (It was more of a tray than a ship.) The fish was fresh, especially the sashimi. The special rolls were ok. My favorite was the one wrapped in avocado.

I'd come back here again, but I think I'll stick with more BYOB places!

Brought my girlfriend here for her birthday lunch. She got the ahi tuna and I got the Hot combo and the clam chowder. Everything was served promptly and as fresh as seafood can get! Shrimp was so soft that you could eat the entire thing without peeling it. The clams, mussels, and oysters just topped off the entire dish. 

The service is impeccable, very fast and professional. And you cannot beat the view of the harbor and the hills of Santa Barbara. Will definitely be coming back again!

Always a pleasure coming here! The staff is wonderful and the food is amazing! My husband and I love coming here. The short ribs are to die for and I just found out they have a short rib panini on the lunch menu will be back to try it!

Awesome raw and chargrilled oysters!  THis is a great place to just stroll by and get some awesome seafood in the market.  THey said they just started up and I hope they are still there when I return.

The food was medioker here for the price, but the service was what stole the show! The bartender was friendly and attentive, and I had great conversation with the other patrons! Normally a single girl would feel uncomfortable going into a place like this alone, but I felt welcomed and not like a peice of meat! Cheers to Bliss restaurant!

So this is my first post ever ... visiting my mom & ordered some takeout for dinner , was charged $47 for shrimp dinner - are you kidding me. Love to honor the old school places but this is ridiculous upcharge.  Menu posted it at flat rate not market rate, should have been disclosed when ordering . Be warned!

While staying at the Westin for a weekend event at the convention center across the street, we had four separate experiences with Shula's.  Both mornings we went to the breakfast buffet.  These are always risky and this was decent the first day and far less than that the second.  Eggs that taste like they come from a box and on the second day the buffet stocking was non-existent and the table service to match.  The seating area was not full yet folks were forced to use saucers to get what food was left.  And this was at 9am, not close to the close of the buffet.

We also tried for a 'quick' lunch.  2 people, both ordered a salad.  One Caesar and one Chicken Salad.  The food was actually good.  The poor server has his hands full however with a full ball area and part of a dining room with no help.  Apparently there was only one cook as well because our two salad took 50 minutes.  Everyone in the place was frustrated while a couple manager looking types walked around and seemingly did nothing to help the situation.

The last encounter was a 9pm order from our room to be picked up at the restaurant.  Chicken strips and French fries for my daughter.  56 minutes.  She liked them but they were nothing special and certainly nothing that should have taken that amount of time to prepare especially since they appeared to have come from the freezer and dropped into a fryer.  At least they were still warm.

I would expect a restaurant like this to have pretty darn good service and maybe even great.  Highly disappointed and it's unfortunate that the hotel does not have more options.  The management staff of Shula's needs to look in the mirror and try to make changes to salvage this place.

I liked the atmosphere, service and food. I actually enjoyed my meal and the building. The location is absolutely terrible to get to. I think I would take my family there if it were not for the parking and the homelessness downtown. I looked both ways crossing the street and made eye contact with a homeless man who decided to confront me because I looked towards him as I crossed the street. Smh

Unhappy with the quality of the food. Stopped for a late lunch, and the food was less than dead average... the quesadilla was good, but the salad was old and almost slimy, and my husband's combo of taco, chimichanga and enchilada seemed to have been reheated all together on the plate it was served on. The servers were nice and attentive, but the food was a disappointment.

It's decent. I'm not as crazy about it as a lot of the people that I've known that have eaten there, but I don't have anything bad to say about it as much as just a little indifference. The food will probably be really great once they've grown into it a bit and I'll try it a third time(s a charm) after they've been open for about six more months. 

I do have to give them a lot of credit for their drinks. They made a perfect manhattan and their drink menu kept us all trying new things all night.

While watching the Rockets game, we were looking for Italian that delivers and found Ponzo's. The pics and reviews sounded strong. When we called to order delivery, the experience was solid. That's where the good ended. The pepperoni pizza tasted like what they serve at kid's pool parties.  The cheese ravioli looked good in the pan but once you dig in, it's like the ravioli was cooked and then the sauce was added at the end just before they closed the lid. The meatball sub was average at best. 
During the delivery, we were told that we are outside their delivery zone and this is the only time they will deliver....that is ok with us. Maybe eating in-house is better......

The decor is great here, I'm bias when it comes to the music choice here since it's Motown nonstop. We came during happy hour; which to my surprise was amazingly priced. The appetizers were good but I think our choice of entrees wasn't that great, I got the veal & tuna which is veal sweet bread and tuna tartare. The sweetbread didn't have much flavor but was cooked perfectly, I might have added more capers into the tartare. My girlfriend got the mussels and frits which was pretty good. For apps we got the goat cheese Arancini, escargot, and pan con tomate with anchovies. Drinks are worth the price .. we will frequent for happy hour for sure and Want to Explore the menu.. for the first week of the restaurant being open; I think it's great 4/5 easily. The price is exactly what you should expect when coming to place like this. Thank you

This place is terrible. Don't eat here the menu sucks. They have crappy sandwiches that are toasted and are cold in the middle. They claim to have over a 100 soups, but they don't. They have about 30 soups on the menu, and at the end of the night they will freeze the left overs to serve, which is fine until they freeze it again for a second time. There is truly one soup that is good but they really never have it, Maryland Crab. I would rather eat a stale bagel with day old chicken broth. I recommend eating Campbell soup from a can. Do your self a favor and either bring your lunch to work or go to a real restaurant and not a place like this.
I live in NY and Mexico. Came here with relatives. Food is amazing. Javier was a wonderful waitperson. Great evening all around.

Darts are great. Very divey. Cheap beer. Good music.

Definite minus: place reeks of smoke. Like leave your clothes outside for 2 days smokey.

Loli's has been on my list of places to eat for a while now and my wife and I finally drove down this past Saturday for dinner. Like already described, this is literally a hole in the wall with a few benches for outside dining. Once we got there, we were told
they sold out their tamales which I really wanted to try. The person taking the order was super friendly, answering all our questions including giving us a sample of their drinks. We got the chicken taco, chipotle chicken sope and chicken torta. The food was out in under ten minutes and everything was great. My wife and I both liked the sope the best and felt the tacos could have had a little more kick to it. Overall a good experience and like the name suggests, we will be back when we have Mexican food cravings.

We had brunch at Atchafalaya this past Saturday after a solid recommendation. We figured we would have to wait since we did not have a reservation. The 1 hour 15 minute wait was accurate and bearable given the Bloody Mary bar. That unfortunately was the best part of our experience.

Once seated, our waitress came by pretty promptly to take our order. We asked her what the soup of the day was and she told us "I'm not even going to tell you what it is because it's that bad". We then asked about the omelette and the empanadas and to both of those she told us they aren't very good. So we asked her what is good and her response was "everything else on the menu". This had to be the weirdest restaurant experience any of us had ever encountered.

We ended up ordering the Egg Treme, Eggs Atchafalaya and Salmon Club. The food as ok, but unfortunately by that point we were so put off by the experience we just wanted to eat and get out. Too many other better choices in town then to have to put up with this treatment for so-so food. We'll cross this one off our repeat list.

I am not vegan. Might not ever be. But I picked up some of their Mac and cheese with the herb bread crumbs and man was it good. I don't really have anything bad to say about it as I always try to honestly review all of the restaurants I review but let's just say I will be back!

Definitely a great place to dine! They serve the food quite quickly and the waiters were friendly. The food itself was delicious and we ended up ordering more food. Overall, I'll say this restaurant deserves a 5 star rating.

I think that the portions were relatively small. We were a group of 6, two adults and four children. We ordered 8 dishes.

First impressions outside...very cute house, good parking, Feb 2nd your Christmas decor should be down. 

Walking in...glitter over load! Like Tinkerbell exploded all over the cakes, pies and walls. Inside could be beautiful if it were just toned down. 

The cakes...I ordered Red Velvet and Chocolate Layer Cake. The Red Velvet cake was dryer then expected. The icing on the outside of the cake was beautiful but tasted too much of shortning. The icing used on the layers was diffrent. It tasted like it may have been cream cheese. The icing on the layers was really good the outside layer was not. I threw away the outside layer. 

The Chocolate cake was not dry but the icing was good but had a gritty sugar texture. 

Presintation...The boxes they were put in to go were very nice. A thick stark white paper with the beautiful Cake Bake logo. Piece of cake layed on a piece of parchment paper. 

$25.07 for two pieces of cake is a bit much unless they make you cry from tasting so good. I did not shed a tear. They do not have prices posted on their items. Typical way to show if you have to ask you can't afford it. 

Would I go back? Not likely. The cupckes from the Flying Cupcake are expensive but so much better. Their Velvet Elvis almost makes me cry. Happy Birthday to Me is also awesome.

UGH - Horrible food - and this is supposed to be the new "in spot" to eat. I ordered the chicken off the lunch menu which is given the ever so "helpful" following description: Chicken - mushrooms, Marsala sauce, preserved lemon.  What I got was a fairly non- descript piece of chicken - I think it was a de-boned thigh - swimming - and I mean swimming - in a broth of chicken with some mushrooms and no sign of preserved lemon.  I must assume that the chicken broth - while it bore no resemblance to it - was meant to represent Marsala sauce. Just Horrible food.

Great Tacos! Not sure about the juices. But they have excellent taco-related presentation.

A piece of lime and packet of Cholula hot sauce with each taco. Not a bad wait time, and you can people watch down Gay Street at all sorts of pretty people.

10 / 10 would taco
Just moved to the area and went here for the first time, their bagels are amazing!! Nice employees and affordable! I will definitely be back.

FIVE TIMES. We were here for 4 days and we came here 5 times! The other cafe beignets in the French quarter had the same quality of beignets but lacked the same ambiance. The beignet here is the most delicious donut I've ever consumed, but the ENTERTAINMENT was the cherry on top. I love the openness of the cafe and how they share the magnificent jazz with pedestrians walking by the cafe. It's definitely a draw! I had the most amazing time every time there was a band playing; I enjoyed  authentic, fresh, hot, crisp beignets alongside their cafe an lait and listened to some of the best music I heard all weekend (besides preservation hall, which I highly recommend). This cafe is the definition of New Orleans culture, and this place helped make me fall in love with this city. If I find myself back in town, I will definitely make 5 more stops.

We've now stopped here twice (market, not dining room), for the exact same reason: it's the only place you can get to in the 30-minute-or-so stopover you get taking the Texas Eagle through Tucson. As a place to stretch your legs on their patio and have a coffee and sandwich not produced by Amtrak while also avoiding a train platform enshrouded in cigarette smoke, Maynards functions admirably. Really, you get sick of Amtrak food by day two of any trip, so the world's biggest breakfast burritos and 12 Arizona craft brews to take back to our sleeper car were like tortillas from heaven sent to nourish us until we got to San Antonio. 

The market is set up with a giant coffee bar in the middle where you order food at the counter. Nice selection of coffee, craft beer on tap, and breakfast/brunch/lunch items at reasonable prices. There are coolers on the outer wall with to-go beers and soft drinks. It's a carefully thought-out c-store/cafe combination that serves its niche as a quick-turnover place to restock your train goodies before continuing east or west by rail.

I love this place because I can take my parents here for a good beer, or come here with friends on a Saturday night and still have a great time. The food here is also surprisingly good, with a good pasta special on rotation at all times. The space is very well designed, to boot.

Great neighborhood bar!

Gary rocks .. " fresh and hot" customer service master. 24/7 breakfast, conveniently right next to Walmart. Silver Dolphin has a pretty cute gift shop and mural for a nice family photo but if you're looking for a meal you can count on Denny's is always a go to!

Have tried breakfast a few times at the Grind and while I'm glad they're here in Westchase (we're in need of more options), the overall coffee and food experience is rather generic.  One of those places where it's not really worth it if there's a wait, but if no wait and you're feeling lazy, this place will do the job.
When we walked in and the place was empty we should've known then. This place is a total dive and the owner was so rude and unfriendly. Don't even bother with this one. Not worth it.

This place is sexy! We snuck onto the main floor without a reservation and had an amazing dinner. The craft cocktails are top notch-smoked Manhattan, garden party, espresso martini are MUSTS. The food was orgasmic-get the spinach Gouda dip! No complaints, priced well, will be back for SURE.

Hurray for tofu that is actually cooked before being added to the curry!

I'm so glad I found this place.  I loved my first order of Massaman curry so much that I actually branched out and ordered something new the second time.  The Massaman curry was perfect, and like I said, the tofu was cooked to my liking, so it didn't fall apart and make a mess in the curry.  I also loved the yellow curry in my most recent order, although the potatoes seemed quite undercooked this time around.  The spring rolls were okay, although they were a little overcooked.  I loved the roti, which was greasy and heavenly (I like greasy roti; I can understand if others don't appreciate it).

Luckily for me, there is a lot of other stuff on the menu which sounds pretty good!  I'm excited to try everything else they have to offer.

Came in on a Saturday during lunch to find out they were out of burgers. My appetite went out of the window immediately! I ended up having just the lobster bisque. It was too rich for my taste but wasn't terrible either. My friends had the steak and eggs, fried egg bagel and scrambled eggs. They said theirs was good. There was a girl performing an acoustic song when we got there but she only sang two songs. I forgot her name but she was extremely talented. 

The service was terrible. Our server was extremely slow.

Great little happy hour!

A friend kept checking in here on Facebook so I went to check it out.  They pour a nice black n tan and the fish n chips and Irish Cuban are wicked good!

The half fried chicken was dry and unseasoned, and the shrimp was from a box you can find at Walmart. The shrimp was very hard, I threw away the shrimp and chicken. I only ate the fries, what a waste of money.

If you're in the mood for pizza, a sandwich, or a panini this is the place go. I'm from California and I've been to so many pizza places there, but this one tops them all off. There customer service here is also spectacular. The server was very knowledgeable and helpful in making recommendations on what to eat. If I'm ever in AZ again, I'll definitely be back :)

I came here for drinks last thursday with my friend Claire, due to her own recommendation. The vibe was very casual, but still someplace I might bring my parents for a meal. We arrived in the early evening, but after happy hour. The place was lively in the front by the bar (there was a group doing shots!). Meanwhile, in the back area there were tables in a more calm setting. They also have outdoor seating! 

Claire and I just got some brews which led us to an interesting discovery. Kite & Key's beer selection changes quite frequently. Basically, when the keg kicks they replace it with something completely different. Our server (shout out to Chelsea!), explained that they always have Allagash White, Yuengling and a few other beers, but for the most part the selection varies. Before I found this out Kite & Key was just barely 4 stars, but with this information I felt comfortable with my decision.

And like I said Claire and I just got drinks, but all of the food I saw looked delicious! I am interested in trying some of their flat bread pizza.

If you haven't tried Kahwa yet, you are sorely missing out.

This is a beloved local coffee shop chain that originated in St. Pete. I was ecstatic to see that a South Tampa location had popped up.

I'm an espresso fan and Kahwa's lattes have the perfect caffeine kick and the espresso actually has flavor. I love jus getting a cafe latte here...no flavoring needed! Plus they have almond milk! Take that Starbucks!

The staff is also super nice and genuine. The space is, we'll, spacious. Outdoor and indoor seating. Perfect place to meet up with a friend or set up shop to work for a few hours.

I didn't try any of the food when I was there, but e erythema I made fresh with local ingredients.

There's also a drive thru if you're in a hurry!

We showed up sort of at the end of the night and had a couple of incredible burgers, really excellent flat bread and some wine.  
The Wine
Flying Goat Pino
omg I'm in love.  Enough said, can't wait to come back.  Fine wine selection and very good service by an overworked server-she did great though.  I love the cozy, dark atmosphere on a chill night and oh that Pino.

Only one word, WOW, The best fish I ever ate.
You're not going to be disappointed, cooked fresh while you wait, and the display case has so much to choose from, If you're into exotic foods.
My meal was amazing there was no wait. Updated upscale breakfast in the heart of downtown! My waffle was absolutely amazing!

It's a pretty good place to chill with friends on the patio or inside listening to music. They upgraded their menu and now it's on an iPad or something similar. They have a large variety of drink options and their food is moderately priced. 

If you're in a group, I highly recommend the mixed meat and cheese board! It was delicious amongst my friends and I.

Good vibes. Good food. Good times.

Came here last Saturday with my entire family. Food was great, but the service was the worst I have ever experienced. Our server Brett was rude from the second he took our beverage order. We asked for sugar for our teas and he acted annoyed like we were bothering him. My sister had arrived late and we were going to ask for another iced tea but when he came to drop off the sugar he put it down on our table and immediately turned around before we could ask. Other than taking our food order not once did he return to our table to check on us throughout our meal. Our appetizers and entrees were brought out by other people. My mom really wanted to try their tiramisu but because Brett was no were to be seen we flagged down another server Jennifer who took our dessert order as well as our check request. She came back with the check and informs us that due to Brett's poor service she comped the tiramisu. Brett finally shows up at our table along with another server to pick up some plates. We asked the other server if the desert was being brought out. As Brett picks up a plate he turns around and rudely says "if it's on the check then it's coming out". I'm sorry but who in the service industry treats people this way. That was the last straw for us. We were mistreated from the second we sat down and honestly felt discriminated. We asked to speak to the manager. The manager comes out and we relay to him the horrible service Brett provided and he hears us out. He asked what he could do but by that point we had already paid and even tipped because other servers NOT BRETT did provide us service. He apologized and gave us a complementary bottle of olive oil. There are plenty of other places in Santa Barbara that have great food and great service. If you are looking for a good night out this is not the place to go.

This is written for all the visitors to St. Louis on the south-side of Saint Louis County. 

I just had the best time at Sam's Steakhouse. We took my uncle while visiting the area. Even as we came in VERY early for our reservation to celebrate my uncle's 85th birthday and 65th anniversary as an ordained priest, - -and even with needing ADA accommodations for him - - the owners and employees were very accommodating, attentive and generous of spirit. We began at a bar area table and moved to the main dining room. Each was set with candles, tablecloths and cloth napkins. It was a lovely setting for such a family celebration. 
Besides everything above, the steaks were great. Also, we were able to identify a few appetizer items that accommodated a gluten/wheat allergy. Additionally, the portions were generous and the zucchini was nicely seasoned. Yes, do order the garlic mashed potatoes!  The funniest part of the evening was was how the additional forks for my uncle's celebratory cheesecake (delivered with a lit candle) were not needed! He loved every bite and we created a memory. 

THANK YOU, Sam"s Steakhouse.

A true hidden gem. By far one of the best all around bars in center city. Cheap food and beer is always on the menu. Prices are much better than other places in the area. Also a decent selection of craft beers. There are daily specials which makes it a great place to go on week nights. Love this place.

Good food and a beautiful restaurant. I rated four stars because I felt it was slightly overpriced. Though I will say, we got a ton of food- more than the menu stated-so I think this is not a usual occurrence to get so much food.
My favorite was the ribs, which I rarely order anywhere and am very picky about. They were huge and fall off the bone tender. The blue cheese slaw was also a good, different side that you don't see everyday. 
FYI..The parking lot is small, so it can be tough to find free parking if there is an event happening at the Trop.

The manager ( cannot remember his name started with B) was over the top and sanitary towards taking our orders. Even though my husband made his life more difficult than needed he kept his composure and never broke professionalism. We will definitely be returning to this location thanks to his patience and orderliness.

Great place to be. Bar is always clean. No food sales but thy allow dogs and can bring in outside food. No smoking inside so I can enjoy a night out without having to wash cigarette smoke out of my skin. Delicious craft beer at good prices. Staff is fun. Plenty of seating and free popcorn.

I've know this place since a was a child and everything is delicious! I've just started ordering my cakes from them and the job they do is amazing. Prices are good and the staff is super friendly. I will continue to return here for years to come!

A "top chef" like restaurant. Each dish we tried was so full of flavor and the sauces that came with each were amazing.

We started with the cheese board, which changes every so often. We had etorki, idizabal, valdeon, fresh fruit, mixed nuts & local honey. The bread that came with it had a hint of garlic on it which topped it off. 

They're plates are "tapas" ish so we ordered 3 to share. The oysters which were lightly fried with honey and aoili sauce. The buffalo cauliflower, which came with a blue cheese dressing and a carrot celery date salad. & finally, the lump crab squash blossom rangoons, which was paired with blood orange ginger jam and toasted macadamia, which was perfect with the crab. Also, the ragoons weren't super cream cheesy so you actually tasted the crab, which was a plus in my book.

Can't wait to return.

First let me say: the wait is DEFINITELY worth it.

I love breakfast, so after I heard that it was a Nashville staple I had to try it. Especially since pancakes are my favorite food!

The 23 varieties made it hard to choose, but eventually I decided on the sweet potato pancakes. It sounds odd, but honestly these were the BEST pancakes I have ever had. The cinnamon cream syrup on top complemented the pancakes so well. 

We had to wait 50 minutes on a Monday morning, but I would do it all over again. This is a MUST, especially if it is your first trip to Nashville.

Loved it here. Great quality gyro, super fresh pita. Wasn't sure about putting fries on the gyro but it worked.  Desserts were very authentic, rich and delicious. My son asked if we could go back the next day.

I wanted to love Chabaa so much. When I looked at the menu, I thought it sounded great. When I walked into the place, I thought it looked so cool. I couldn't wait, I thought it would be great. When my server greeted me, she was so sweet and did a good job serving me, I thought it would be so great. I ordered one of the specials, which was a game fish wrapped in banana leaf with peppers and onions, mushrooms, baby corn and rice with a sweet and sour chili-lime sauce.

Then I tasted it.

And it tasted like what can only be described as the food equivalent of water. Evereything but the chili-lime sauce was completely tasteless and bland, not to mention cold the minute it hit the table.

I was very disappointed, but I still see the potential and hope to one day return and be swayed to a positive review.

This place is our new favorite for a quick meal or mostly to-go. The staff are always friendly and you can't find a better breakfast sandwich around. I love the ECS (Cuban style sandwich with sausage, egg and cheese) and my wife really enjoys the Oatmeal. Please go support this small family run business. It's great.

I use to love it, but past 2 times we ordered food to pick up it was inferior. 
Not worth the money. I will spend it at HOUSE.

Owner was really nice, you can order almost any pizza and they'll make it for you. Depending on who's there depends on the service and quality you receive. Lucky for me the owner was there both times I've gone and even recognized me! So that was nice. The soda machines need a good cleaning tho.

I love this place because of the fact that it's not a chain and the breakfast is really good. Sometimes the service is slow which is ok on weekends but when you are on your lunch break it can be an issue. Also the menu is 3/4 ads which makes it cluttered. Other than that the most important aspect is the food and it's good.

I would give a 2 1/2 star if possible. 

This is the second time that my family and I have ordered from this location. Both of which orders were incorrect and charged improperly. However, we are not big on the whole complaint process with businesses. 

Cleanliness 4 out of 5
Seemed fairly clean

Staff 2 out of 5
Cashier seemed very young and untrained 

Food quality 2 out of 5
Food was fresh but bland. No toppings or trimmings came with the food(lettuce,tomato,onion)

Portions size 3 out of 5
Different portions I guess with different people. As far as the jumbo part, food was definitely bigger than average size but not crazy big like everyone makes it seem.

I've enjoyed Tony Luke's roast pork and provolone from various locations in NJ and the ball park but the Oregon location by far is the best! Set apart as more juicy, tender and flavorful!  If your getting take out don't bother with the fries. They just don't travel well.  If you're in the neighborhood you've got to give it a try.

Great atmosphere in the courtyard, really romantic atmosphere and great ambiance throughout the restaurant. Cocktails varied in quality but were overall pretty good. Staff was nice and attentive. The food was great, try the duck confit dirty rice and the lamb!

Food was excellent and the service was wonderful. What a great place to spend a Sunday afternoon. When we made the reservations, I made a mistake and reserved the wrong date. Nevertheless, they were very busy, yet they made an accommodation that was perfect. I would highly recommend the restaurant for the service and the food.

We were looking for a place with vegetarian options and this came up. It's in a beautiful quiet alley way with tables outside. We ordered half salads of the Green Goddess Wedge and Pressed Watermelon Burrata and Kale, both were good portions and delicious! We also ordered the Crimini Escargots (no snail) and Sausage Sampler Appetizers. Everything was delicious and well presented! Service was wonderful. Highly recommend!

It's roots are in the Tamales, and there's no mistake in saying they're arguably the best, Green Corn and Beef tamales in town! You can pre-order by the dozen to take home, or they're part of their humble, but very, very good Sunday buffet. It's a quaint setup but it stands big on those tamales.

Clean buffet with more options than a single person can sample in one visit.  I would venture to say that this is currently the best "Asian Buffet" in Indianapolis.  

They restaurant should of had 5-stars, but I needed to deduct a star because the waiter kept interjecting pointed questions after eavesdropping into my highly personal conversation with long-lost friends.  The waiter also told our entire table (females included) that he had "never seen anyone eat that much sushi in his whole life."  Bad form bro - minus one star - for initiating early mid-life crises centered around accusatory over-eating by a disheveled young buffet waiter.
Liars ! Promised to, refund some of my money and never did. Food is just ok and overpriced for the quality. Found a new place for Chinese food, Green tea restaurant is way better.

How can this place not get a 5/5 when they do such good work for people in need?
Our "go to" place for Donairs. Every time.
Delicious!!! Ambiance and drinks are phenomenal and the staff is very friendly.  It is a bit of a small space and there was a slight wait but definitely worth it!!!
Slower then shit waiting  30 mibs now, lost my order omce i got here  almost 45  now.guess they had to catch the chicken in the back yard

Awesome Pizza. Best I've had in a very long time. There large pizza is LARGE   Most of pizza places today serve a 16" which is really a medium. 

There's is 18" and loaded with the very best meats. Their meat lovers is one of the best I've had. 

Not to mention they have really good fresh brewed ice tea. 

I will be returning again. Plus with a few new customers for them.

This place is amazing! By far my most favorite place to get tacos in South Philly. The food is super flavorful, and they have really great salsas that taste very fresh. Really nice people as well. Definitely order from them, you won't be disappointed.

Waited 1 hour for a simple salad.
This place takes forever to bring out your food!
The service is slow and horrible.  I had to ask for my salad to go since I had a plane to catch.  When I was able to finally eat my salad, they forgot to put a side of salad dressing, needless to say my salad was awful!  There are plenty of other restaurants you can go to, don't waste your precious time and hard earned money on this dump!

Brickhouse is a chain that markets itself as a "man cave," replete with dozens of flatscreens showing the latest game, as well as plenty of under-25 female servers clad in daisy dukes and cleavage-exposing tight tops. They may not be the most experienced servers, but they are some of the best-looking outside the strip clubs that adjoin this outpost along North Dale Mabry Highway.
Inside, find lots of reclinerr-style stuffed chairs, with arm holes for beer, around a fireplace. Outside, the patio has a fire-pit for cool nights, and plenty of comfy chairs. They're even doing live music in the summer on Saturday nights.
The burgers come in the shape of hoagies, and they are quite large. The pizzas are good, too, thin crust concoctions, large enough for two.
The best things about Brickhouse, though, are the beer sizes and pricing. You can get a 22-ounce Jai Alai, the Tampa-made craft beer IPA, for $4.50. That is cheaper than at the Cigar City brewery right around the corner! For that, I am a repeat customer. They have a few other craft selections, as well, along with more normal suds, also available in 16 ounces, as well as a humongous beer tower that serves about 10 people. The towers do not keep the beers cold, however, so don't order unless you can drink it all really fast.

Crowds. Many, many crowds.

Also, Expensive. Very, very expensive.

I think that the market is a great resource for the community to have, considering the next closest Christkindlmarkt is in Chicago.  However, there were limited food options (due to city policies), the booths were too close together, and there was not room for seating.  I think this event could benefit from a second stage to have more options for entertainment, and could also benefit from having more space.

A little disappointed. Got the yakisoma with shrimp. The noodles didn't have much flavor and the shrimp were overcooked, rubbery, flavorless. Definitely not worth the price and made my stomach a little sick. I did like the decor of the restaurant. Maybe their other dishes are better?
Just a quick 5 star rave.  This is my favorite local restaurant.  I have never had a bad experience.  The food is great. The servers are attentive.  Try it....the food will not disappoint
Delicious food including the most yummy pastries and loaves of bread. We get the Cali Bowls and it's so cool that they add a fried egg. Their sauces are tasty too. Great add to the neighborhood!
If you want great bbq pork or beef, this is the spot. Service is always spot on and the sides are delicious, particularly the okra or baked beans.

An amazing lineup on the food menu. Sit down or take away. The grocery mart has so many great items. A go to for when I'm looking for cotija and oaxaca cheeses. There is even a meat and deli in the back.

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this truck yet - the first time I ordered here was like 5 years ago. And they've been improving ever since! They now accept debit/credit so now I don't have to worry about pulling out cash during the lunch rush, and they're open later than they were when I was a freshman. They also have new items on the menu - today I tried the Enzo's avocado - not as much avocado as I would have liked, but still an awesome crepe nonetheless. My favorites are the Nicole's Southwestern (or Dozer, if you prefer rib meat), and the Mediterranean. For dessert, anything with nutella or honey is awesome. Fresh fruit in a warm crepe is a go.

The wait does get a little long, but they are really systematic. If you do wait long, it's not for lack of trying. The truck is just that popular. But it's all worth it, 5$ for a delicious, filling meal.

When I had heard that the world-famous chain was opening up in Edmonton, I was super excited. Nando's originated from South Africa but their food has Mozambican and Portuguese influences. They are very well known for their peri peri chicken. The restaurant is currently located southside but another one is planned for a northside opening (yay!). I came during their opening week which would explain the kinks throughout the night. The service was very inconsistent and unorganized. 

To start the dinner off, we each had a glass of their housemade sangria. It was deliciously refreshing and fruity. The taste of the wine wasn't too strong either. The first appeteaser (appetizer) I tried was their Portuguese garlic bread. It was a baked Portuguese bun with a garlic and herb spread. The bun was a bit too chewy for my liking. On the other hand, the spread wasn't overly filled with a garlic taste. Next up I tried the Peri-Peri fries. These fries were served with a Peri-naise sauce. It was a creamy blend similar to an aioli but not as thick. The lightly crispy fries had the right amount of salt on it. My friend and I tried out both types of sliders that Nando's offered. Found as an appeteaser, you have a choice of chicken or mushroom sliders. The chicken ones used Peri-Peri chicken with cilantro dressing and chili ham. The vegetarian option used roasted portabello mushrooms and halloumi cheese. I preferred the mushroom sliders better because the chicken sliders were very bland. There was barely any flavour or spices in it. 

All of the chicken at Nando's is marinated for 24 hours in their secret sauce. The timeframe allows the flavor to be soaked right to the bone! After, they are flame grilled then basted in one of Nando's Peri-Peri sauces. Their chicken is ordered based on a spiciness scale. I tried the lemon and herb chicken, which is further down on the scale since it's not spicy. After taking a first bite of the lemon and herb chicken, I can see why they are well known for it. The chicken was deliciously juicy and tender. There was a bit of zest from the lemon with a balance of aromatic spices and herbs. The freshness of the chicken came through with every bite. The other flavour of Peri-Peri chicken that I tried was the mildly spicy chicken. Maybe my tastebuds are weak but I found it to be too spicy for me. I had to take a sip of water after every bite! 

Dessert offerings at Nando's include pasteis de natas (Portuguese egg tarts), New York cheesecake, Nando's kisses, and bottomless frozen yogurt. I had the pasteis de natas, which I was excited to eat. I'm a big fan of Hong Kong egg tarts so I wanted to see how the Portuguese version would compare. They have a custard in the center similar to creme brûlée. The crust was buttery and flaky. It was very tasty!

I feel like Nando's is worth a try once or twice. There is a lot of hype surrounding it though, but that's not necessarily bad.

It's absolutely the best sushi in st Pete. Always fresh and tasty. At one point , few months ago, kitchen was slow but  they improved; our food was on the table within 10 minutes. Portion of the fried rice is rich and big for one person. Service is good too! All together great place; highly recommend!

I've been going here for six years, mainly because it's on my way to work. For as long as I've been going there,  I have never received any attitude or nasty service until today. I'm not sure if it's just an off day for the lady, and she has a lot to deal with, or she's just plain old rude. Then proceed to come back to me after she give me my meal to ask me, "do you need anything else?" with the same attitude. Even my employee was taken back witnessing her attitude. Maybe the MOD can coach her on how to interact with the customers, or simply retrain her.

What a wonderful find!! My wife of 30 years is a constant nay-sayer, but even she had nothing bad to say. "Designer dive" atmosphere with "bougie" food. We had 4 different plates and shared everything. Will definitely be back. Very happy with the whole experience

Very good daily specials. Get the fish taco special if they have them. Fantastic craft beer selection and the bartenders were great. Service was average - our waitress seemed a bit scattered but it was quite busy at the time.

We chose this place for Valentine's Day, and it was a great choice.  When we arrived the lobby area was extremely crowded and the hostess seemed a little overwhelmed but very pleasant.  We had to wait even though we had reservations so they made it up to us by giving us free cocktails and comfortable seats, which I thought was a nice touch.  The food was good but the veal osso bucco was insanity.  I would definitely return!

I can't speak for others that have rated below a 5 star or below for this place, either standards are too high (the individual might be also), maybe the service wasn't to their standards or they're not into some 90's and earlier rock and roll. Either way, the Trabue that I had was on point, great flavor from the beef, to the bun, the egg and bacon on that burger. In addition, it came out and was on the table after I set my menu down and washed my hands. Hot, tasty and ready to be eaten up just like I did. You can see the last few bites left before I made my stomach happy with a hamburger and french fries just like I had sought out for.

Would have never known this cute little place was in this shopping center if it weren't for Yelp. Brought my family here to try it for lunch and it was extremely good food, quick service too. We got two happy bowls, a tuna sandwich and the veggie sandwich, all were 10/10. Would definitely come back.

Great spot to grab a fresh, delicious brunch on Mass Ave. I also always enjoy feeling like the food I'm eating has "cleaner" and generally responsibly sourced ingredients. I'm not a big juice person, but their coffee/espresso options are great and I always enjoy trying a new drink! 

Also great if you are vegetarian/vegan - the yam bacon is delicious and a fun substitute for regular bacon. I also routinely go back for their biscuits, they may be the best thing on the menu. 

Solid selection of brunch basics but also plenty of more adventurous options to choose from, I'll definitely keep coming back.
Order wasn't correct and fries were cold. Seems like only two people were working, because the guy that gave us the order, came out the back a few mins later with the trash

Food was delicious! Staff was super nice, super fast. Their covid procedures were seamless and made everything comfortable and easy: they have sanitizer stations, everything is constantly being cleaned, you get seated with menus and then order behind plexiglass, then food is delivered to your table, all while distanced. It was decently busy for early evening, yet the food was out pretty quickly. My husband and I will definitely go again!

Went here for hibachi with my family and it was really good! Our chef was very fun- doing things like squirting sake into my dad's mouth for his birthday.  How could you not love a performance like that?! 

The food was all around delicious.  I'm a huge fan of hibachi shrimp but other delicious entrees were the scallops and lobster tail.

This place is BYOB, which rules.  Hibachi is kind of pricey but, in my opinion, worth the money because you know it's fresh and MTO.

I've eaten here three times now, and have tried their grilled cheese (the recipe of which has changed for the better since my first try), pizza, a passion fruit smoothie and the Blue Moon Ice Cream. 

The service is a little slow, and we've had to correct and repeat our orders a couple times. Twice we ordered to go and sat down for the wait, only to have our food brought out on plates to eat there. 

The food isn't bad, but it didn't quite impress me either. The passion fruit smoothie wasn't great enough for me to want to order it again - I'm pretty sure they use frozen fruit or concentrate for it, it just didn't taste fresh. The grilled cheese was ample in size, and definitely much more cheesy with the revised recipe. And the pizza was decent, but I think they're still working on developing a distinct recipe and style for it. 

The primary reason we've returned to this place is the Blue Moon ice cream. It tastes like someone took the milk at the end of your bowl of fruit loop cereal and turned it into ice cream, and I haven't experienced anything else quite like it. 

So if you're visiting and you just need a cheap and easy meal, this place is definitely one of the more affordable places to grab a bite in town, but while you're there, try the Blue Moon ice cream, because that's what will make you want to come back.

Not even worth one star!  We spent the last 1 1/2 hours waiting for our dinners.  TWICE we were served RAW salmon!  This place has a major problem!  Now we're home trying to fix something to eat for dinner.

Holy burrito!
My boyfriend and I each got a supreme burrito. The guy at the window was suuuuuuper friendly and made it such a chill place to go. We got our bag (with tons of salsas AND a lime) and took it home. We then opened up the mammoth burritos, took a bite and fell in love. Probably the biggest burrito I've ever seen. How can they put all those ingredients in and charge only $7.10?!? 
Great job, Nico's. We'll totally be back.

Like some others, I'm an East Coaster (exit 4, NJ Turnpike!) so I've never quite found the perfect pizza that reminds exactly of the pizza that is so prevalent back there.  I ate at the original Nu Yalk Pizza and was so turned off by the nastiness of the staff and how dark and uninviting that hole was that it's taken me 9 years to give them another try.  I remember not quite liking the sauce.

I finally swung by the new location, and I must say I was pleasantly surprised. Huge slices with an extra topping came out to be about $2.50 each.  And I'm with total agreement to the one topping rule - with thin crust, crispy pizza, you can't really support massive amounts of toppings, and it works best with a light layer of whatever topping you choose.  In my case, I went with the mushrooms.  And HELLO!  Fresh mushrooms, not from a can.  I don't normally first pump, but I did one anyway.  

Yes, I folded over my slice.  Crispy base - check.

Yes, I checked for orange grease.  Check.

My one minor complaint was that there wasn't much cheese on mine.  It must have been an abnormality, because I checked out other people's pizzas and theirs seemed cheesy enough.

One nice touch - I had ordered two slices, not knowing how huge they would be.  I asked the guy up front if I could have some foil to wrap mine up later, and he gave me a big smile and said, "Hon, just bring it up and I'll do it for you."  I thought that was sweet.  And for that, I instantly forgave them for the cheese scarcity.

Scott and Co has the secret feel of a Speak Easy as you find it nestled down a side street of busy downtown Tucson. The bartenders have the best personalities and can craft amazing cocktails. I have never had any food here and am not even 100% sure if they have any. A great place for a night cap or low key night with exception ambiance.
I'm obsessed with their Sunrise Bowl and a couple of their juices.  They are a lil pricey but when it comes to eating/drinking clean price should not be an object.

Stopped in yesterday to get some chicken.  Went inside (didn't know they aren't using inside). This place starts with liquid on the floor in the entrance.  No no one wiped up the ice cubes but put up one of this floor is wet signs.  Very dangerous walking in. Two employees could not help me but they sure could yell at me something about how busy they were and they didn't have time to...  Place is filthy.  I am going to try to contact who owns this particular store to find out if they have any cleaning policies in place and wonder how they could serve food out of there.

What is happening at TGI Friday? Came into a line at the host desk. No one there. Waited a few minutes and decided to go the bar. Could not sit at a table as they were doing a change over. What is that? So we opted to eat at the bar. I HATE eating at the bar. Wanted a beer. No Blue Moon available. The keg needed to be changed and there was only 1 manger there. They are the only ones who can change it. We waited about 10 minutes for that to be changed. They did comp the beer for the wait. 
Maria did an excellent job of accommodating us. Took our order with a smile and polite conversation. She was in charge of the bar and the surrounding tables. She was making it happen. Thank you Maria for the awesome service. 
My husband received his food a good 5 minutes before I did. He was almost done by the time I got my food. 
There were dirty tables behind us the whole time we were there. Not sure what the manger was doing but he/she was not front and center supporting their staff. 
We had some gift certificates so we used them but will not frequent this location.
I come here a lot and get there Rice and Beans Bowl. Staff are always friendly and consistent. The atmosphere is great too!

Really nice anniversary dinner with the wife. Very attentive service and the food didn't disappoint. Once I informed the hostess it was our anniversary, she made a hand written card and put rose  pedals at my wife's seating. Next time in Santa Barbara, we'll be back.

If ever there were a reason for me to join Yelp, it was most certainly to give Pietro's a bad review.  

It has been a few years since I went to Pietro's, and there's a reason for that.  First of all, I never would have gone to Pietro's on my own.  I think the place looks like a chain restaurant.  And it's not!  (Yes, they do have two locations).  I think the main appeal is probably outdoor seating on Walnut Street, and everyone gets their attractive-looking pizzas, which you can see when you're hopping between Arden B. and Knit Wit (two stores on Walnut Street I've never considered shopping in).  But the outdoor seating undoubtedly draws people in.  
I had a friend who SWORE by Pietro's.  Every time she came downtown, Pietro's was her place.  She loved the pizza, and always ordered the same exact thing.  I went there with her once, and I thought it was nothing to write home about.  I wrote it off as "Meh."  I thought it was overpriced for what they were offering.  I wound up getting dragged there with her a second time, and I ordered a salad, which was pretty much a $7 pile of lettuce.  I told her I didn't want to go there anymore.  But, alas, ONE MORE TIME, I was persuaded.  "We're just going to get dessert," she said.  Okay, dessert, I can handle that, right?
This was the WORST experience:  We got there maybe at 7 or 8, and there were 3 of us.  It was sort of crowded.  We told the hostess we just waned dessert.  She sat us outside, which was fine.  A guy brought over complimentary bread and olive oil and we told him that we were only having dessert, but he said it was complimentary no matter what, so we starting eating it.  The waitress came over to take our order and we started ordering dessert items, when a man came over and started flipping out at everyone.  "You can't sit here if you're only getting dessert!" he yelled at us.  "And you don't get bread if you're only getting dessert!  Take away their bread and find them a new table inside!"  The waitress looked at us, with the bread in our mouths, and embarrassingly cleared away the bread and oil.  The man continued to yell at us... "You can't just sit anywhere you want, especially when you're only having dessert."  We explained that, obviously, we hadn't seated ourselves, and that we had informed the hostess of our dining plans.  He huffed and puffed and told us to get up.  We started to get up, when the hostess came over and explained that that was the case, and that she wasn't aware that there were stipulations for dining outside.  The man rolled his eyes and told us to sit back down.  Then he told us not to sit there again if were were just getting dessert or appetizers.  Then he walked away.  
The waitress and the hostess apologized for him.  After we ate our dessert (which we had already ordered, or else we would have left), we asked someone if we could speak to the manager.  We were lead to the back of the restaurant to wait for him to come out of the kitchen.  We waited at least 25 minutes before our original hostess walked by and asked us what we were waiting for.  We told her we had been waiting to speak to the manager.  She told us that the man who yelled at us was the manager.  We asked her to get him for us, and she came back a minute later only to report, "He said he's not going to come talk to you."  She apologized repeatedly.  
And THAT is why I haven't been back to "Pietro's Mediocre Pizzeria with Complimentary Awful Service"
Their spinach and artichoke dip is awesome! It's true that some of there food options are better than others but their delivery is super quick.

Mind blown. We are vegan foodies who have been to almost every vegan restaurant in the LA area, so on our wedding weekend in Santa Barbara, we knew we had to dry Mesa Verde. Not disappointed! The food was almost too beautiful to eat and the flavors were absolutely incredible. The baklava was out of this world! Thank you for one of the best meals we have ever had
Tasty burgers (and fries), nice staff, and a cool atmosphere. Great place to eat dinner on a Friday night.

I am only giving it three because it would of had 4.5 if it wasn't for this time. I normally come here often for the rainbow bagel, poppy, and a few others. I normally enjoy it. good breakfast sandwiches. i ordered the rainbow bagel and this is what came it looks half blueberry.

I had actually been to this restaurant years ago. I went again last night. I would say that this restaurant is probably the most authentic I have had in Tampa. The staff was pretty friendly and accommodating and the service was fast.

Since the last time I was there, their prices have increased dramatically! There were 3 people in our party and we spent over $90!! That is really high. 

The food was just okay and could have been better. We ordered the jellyfish, pan-friend tilapia, mixed veggies, tofu dish, lo mein, and other items. The jellyfish tasted good but the texture was kind of weird; the lo -mein had these really thin noodles that I am not really used to and it tasted kind of weird, the veggies were the best dish we ordered. The fish was okay.

I agree with one of the other reviewers-you really can't get any better than San Francisco for awesome Chinese food.

Absolutely love Lindy's! The place has such a cool atmosphere, and a menu that is sure to please almost anyone. The first time I ate at Lindy's was because a friend had a gift card. However, it was for sure one of the best burgers I have ever had. And the fries were amazing! I was so excited when the east side location opened up. Would absolutely recommend!

I went to this place for breakfast. It was on the "Trendy" side. The menu was limited and extremely pricey. I sat at the bar and ordered a bloody mary and the staff seemed confused (the bartender wasn't in yet supposedly). They got one made, but it took a very long time. The food tasted good, but again was quite pricy for what it was.

The new, trimmer menu is a winner. The baked mushrooms in rich gravy are not to be missed, and I haven't enjoyed brussel sprouts so much in my life. These were fat flavor rockets, and my grandma would have been proud. If the restrooms weren't in another hemisphere, I'd tack on another star.

This place is still fantastic. I haven't been here since the 90's when I used to go to Santa Barbara more often. And even though it's coveted 19 they have lovely outside tables and fantastic service. The drinks are still outstanding and strong. had a calamari appetizer that was excellent as well. Saw some daily specials of people eating dinner but wasn't quite ready for it. I definitely would stop in here for a meal or a drink or both.

The restrooms are clean and I'm not sure about parking since it's right on State Street and the street is closed for cars which is nice because everyone on State Street has put up an outside dining area.

Terrible service. We were sat in a back table and ignored. Half of our food didn't come out, the waitress ignored our empty glasses and eventually we got up to ask for someone to fill our water. 3 out of 6 deserts had hair in them. They then took an 18% gratuity. So the crappy service and the crappy waitress still got a 25$ tip. Been visiting for for four years, safe to say we won't be back

We went to Hickory Lane as part of Fright and Bite package to attend the Eastern penitentiary Horror Tour. The restaurant is small but clean, causal and has a terrific staff.  We were served a different pre-fixe menu as part of the package but the choices were varied and all the food was good.  This was straight forward food - beet salad, onion soup, burger, etc - the onion soup was fine - though not enough sherry or cheese for my taste.  The burger was excellent - perfectly cooked and well seasoned.  The waitress kept the meal moving - but did not rush us.  It was a very good experience overall and we all mentioned that we wish we had a restaurant like this in our town.

Loved this place. Came here with the hubby on a Tuesday trivia night. We were thoroughly entertained just watching. Trivia unlike most places. They shake it up with game rounds so it isn't just a bunch of questions. Great beer selection, free popcorn, nice local vibe. Really enjoyed this place!

One word: Omakase.  I had the lunch one and was blown away, thus trying the dinner omakase in Waikiki twice!  This place had an interesting  ambiance to it.  

Weird to say this, but check out the restroom!

This place is absolutely the best vegan spot we've hit in St. Pete, so far. Try their vegan cheese plate, and definitely don't skip dessert. The atmosphere is so quaint and cute and the service and staff are so nice and welcoming. We had a really great time on our little date night, and will definitely be back.

Frank's closed for good... Out of Business.  Sad.  
New restaurant and bar scheduled to open in early 2022 according to sign on door, called OTR (On The Rocks LLC).

Daisy Dukes, feels like a biker joint with reasonably priced food.  Open all night.  Recommend the po boys with creole in different varieties: 3 fried oysters, fried medium shrimps, alligator sausage (different and kind of fatty for my taste).  The creole with rice was just spicy and good.  Drinks start at $3 but water is free.  Great intro to casual New Orleans food.

Yummy pizza after you've been walking around all day and having drinks in the Quarter. HUGE slices, bigger than your face- and the crust was so good. Only downside is there is not much seating, so don't plan on coming to visit with a group. There is a bar with about 5 stools to sit and eat. Great if you're by yourself or with one other person. It wasn't busy when we were there, not sure why! It was excellent. We would definitely go back.

So, this was our first return since the Solomonov crew went on their merry way and it just deosn't seem like this is the same restaurant. 

There were four of us for dinner. We arrived slightly before our 5:30 reservation. the restaurant was half full, but they only had ONE menu for us to read from. Not a big deal, but who runs out of menus with only a half full restaurant. 

There were several other small mis-steps during service. My drink came one time garnished and one time not. The sliverware was reset differently for half of the table than the other half. These are all small details which would get a pass at most restaurants but for the prices they are charging ($24 for chicken, $38 for Rib Eye) service must be perfect and food must be impeccable.

The food is no longer spactacular as it was before. The food is just "fine" but again just fine doesn't fly at these prices. The game hen ragu was too brothy and a bit flat to be a a ragu. The Artic Char was just unispirred. Why is it even on the menu? The trout with smoked hummus was very good as was the roast chicken (more chicken liver crostinis please). 

My "Tea & Sympathy" cocktail was delicious!

Since this place is in/next to the park, they have a sculpture inside as well as an outdoor patio. I was hoping to see more breakfast options since that's what I was in the mood for. I ended up w/ a smoothie & pumpkin bread. I guess this place has more lunch items so maybe that's what people should go for. Everyone has different preferences so I guess find out for yourself.
