Went here for an end of the semester wind down. Parking was easy, they have a huge menu of beers, and the food was pretty good. Prices are reasonable, too. It felt like more of a younger place, but I would return for a quick pub bite.
First time here  since I'm from Houston Tx. Great place and food. The staff was helpful and very sweet!

Every meal I've had at Chapati has been amazing. I love the modern atmosphere and as a vegetarian there are so many great menu options. I love that they will customize your food to your desired level of spice. Definitely one of my favorite restaurants in Indy. A great place to go with a big group of friends!

We arrived, sat down quickly, and waited for our waiter. To start, he didn't understand really anything on the menu. We ordered 2 grilled chicken sandwiches, some soup, and some chicken tenders. He looked almost dumbfounded when my girlfriend was asking him about what comes on the sandwich.  Fast forward about 40-45 mins later (we went on a Monday at around noon with maybe 15 others in the restaurant) and our food arrives.  The bill arrives and it comes to almost 40 dollars. My mom pays some in cash, and I put the rest on my debit card. We wait for him to pick it up, and he goes to take care of it. Another probably almost 35 minutes go by, and he comes back, sets the bill on the table and just stands at the end of the table. I pick up the tab, and he ask's 3 times if everything is ok, did he do something wrong, etc. I say no(because at that point, everything on the bill looked to be fine), and he walks away. As he's walking away (my back is facing the front door so I can see him walk away), he turns twice and looks to make SURE we leave him a tip. Fast forward to the next morning, and I check my account. I WAS CHARGED FOR THE ENTIRE BILL. I call and speak to the manager (who seems like he doesn't know much about managing) and he said the waiter "does not like to make mistakes, and when he does, he gets really awkward." I tell him I was charged for the almost 40 dollars, plus what my mom paid in cash (which meant the server picked up a 20 dollar tip!!). He gives me the run around for 15 minutes about the bank this, the bank that, and how when the waiter realized what he did, the manager came over, canceled it, and re-debited my card for the 20 dollars. It's no big deal, it was an honest mistake I say, but why wouldn't the manager come over to our table and let me know? He kept saying things about the bank and I told him he wasn't answering my question. Why wouldn't the manager come over and tell me my CARD WAS CHARGED FOR 40 DOLLARS? They knew about the cancellation correct? He says yes and with a response of "We don't normally go and talk to the customer because of how fast it goes through" So you take 40 dollars from someone and you don't let them know? I told him I'd never go there again because it's too much of a risk, and the waiter was an idiot, along with the service I was getting from the management.  Food was mediocre, but the service was HORRIBLE.

We've eaten here for breakfast and dinner. Food has been great both times! It definitely has a diner feel and the decor isn't my favorite but the food makes up for it. The pancakes were wonderful and the lamb burgers were amazing! We will be back. :)

An old friend of mine was in town one Friday morning and wanted breakfast.  By breakfast I mean, coffee and Bloody Marys.  I live in the northern suburbs and am no longer welcome at the country club and there's nothing else that would fit the bill so I tracked this place down, based on the positive ratings and the fact there is a full bar open for breakfast.

Well, there is supposed to be a full bar open for breakfast.  It wasn't open when we arrived at 9am and ordered Bloody Marys, which are featured prominently on the pretty website.  The server explained the bartender hadn't arrived yet, which begged the question of why the well-staffed joint couldn't find a spare waitress or maitre d' to mix vodka with a little tomato juice more vodka, Tabasco, Worcestershire, lemon juice, salt, pepper and olives.  They figured it out eventually, after I mentioned I was an Elite Yelp member and picked out Pinewood Social for their 'full bar' at breakfast time.  I have to say I even think the pour was generous, which I haven't said since...well, I can't remember the last time I had a generous pour outside of my own home, where my kids know to pour using the count method, "One Tennessee, Two Tennessee...." until the kid reaches his/her age.  

Was the Bloody Mary worth the $10 price tag?  It was close enough, I guess.

I was also frustrated by the parking situation here.  I circled twice before finding a spot in the lot directly to the north of the building, which interestingly enough, is located next to a lot with approximately 1,000 empty spots, none of which are available for parking "at any time", according to the sign posted prominently.  Poor property management by the lot owner, or typical government diktat?  Who knows.  Nashville is booming right now so that covers lots of negligence. So be prepared to park at the lot to the south of the building, which is a paid lot with no shelter to pay when it is hot, cold or raining.

Otherwise, this joint is fantastic.  It's exactly what I had in mind from the descriptions.  The maitre d' at front is chipper and well dressed, the wait staff is gorgeous and do a wonderful job of pretending to be happy, if their smiles aren't genuine, and the environment perfects the cliche`d "hipster" scene which has NashVegas in its grip right.

Price was okay and ambiance was interesting considering it's a converted old house. Chicken was extra crispy and super brown, but not necessarily great or special. The red beans and rice were meh too. Cornbread was good. We went at lunch and it was packed but considering most reviews indicate it is frequently this packed you'd expect they'd have some system in place to prevent this. Instead, I saw a lot of people standing outside waiting and not being noticed and meals taking forever (about 45 for 2 fried chicken plates). Not to mention, it was hot and there were lots of flies. People say to try it but honestly I'd skip it and opt for something else.

It's been many years since I've been to one and is a first for the area! Great, fast service. You get what you pay for and is a great addition to the area! Online ordering and pick up is coming soon, and while they just opened, the place was well staffed and clean! Can't wait to come back again!

The food here is absolutely wonderful! I have deducted two stars for the small size of the place, which results in a lengthy wait. My friends and I love to go to brunch on Sunday mornings, but the over an hour and a half wait for the  6 of us (plus the lack of parking in the area) deters us from going very often. I would love to try every item on the menu!  The lemon donuts they bring to the table are amazing!  Would love to see another location open with a larger dining area and much better parking options!

Update March 2016:  Found out that the donuts I mentioned in my original review are not something they typically bring to the table for free and had probably been brought out due to the super lengthy amount of time we'd had to wait when we were there.  This time, for 2 people we "only" had to wait for 50 minutes at 11 am on a Sunday because we were seated at a 4 top with 2 people we didn't know.  Awkward!  Plus we were really wanting mimosas and they were out of orange juice - seriously?  How difficult could it be to make or go get more?

Well a Coworker took me to this little gem and I loved it. I had the country ham and eggs with red eye gravy, had never had red eye before...described as bacon juice and coffee, but it was great for dunking the country ham.

Will I be back...absolutely!
Great food, great service, delicious beer!  Not the place for a quiet meal on live music nights.

Visiting Philadelphia, coming to Tommy DiNic's was #1 on my boyfriend's list of places to eat. He has eaten here in the past but I never have! We were conveniently located at the Hilton Hotel right across the street, so popping over to Reading Terminal Market was our first stop! I was also a newbie to the Reading Terminal Market and loved the experience and atmosphere here!

When we found our way to DiNic's the line was so long which kind of made me nervous because I was getting super hungry. But, we had a minute or 2 to look over the menu and was quickly greeted by someone behind the counter. After that, it took about 4-5 minutes to pay and get our food- I was very impressed with the efficiency here! There was no room at their counter to eat, so we went to the area in the  Reading Terminal Market with tables and Christmas music being performed. Very festive!

As I said before.. I was super hungry (and a little hungover). One bite of this sandwich changed my day! I ordered the pork with provolone and hot peppers. The bread was super fresh and light- which to me is sometimes to most important part of a sandwich! The pork was cooked perfectly, and the hot peppers were HOT! I have a high tolerance to hot food.. so if you don't.. be ware! Chris got the same thing as me but he got the broccoli rabe... which I regret not getting! The best part of this sandwich was that I didn't leave feeling super full or gross from it because it wasn't super greasy. I look forward to coming here again on my next trip to Philly!

My friends were trying to pick a place so I suggested this as a small attempt. We go in not really sure what to expect. The atmosphere was very nice. We were seated pretty quickly and the service was nice. Very clean. The food was delicious. I had the brisket (which we all agreed was the best thing to have), one friend had the CHOW burger (tasty but a bit greasy and huge!) and my other friend had the General CHOW chicken which was okay. We all shared and their mashed potatoes are fantastic. They had an interesting take on calamari but tasty. The dessert was pretty good too. The portions LOOK small but really fill you up! 

Will definitely be returning here!
This is the best Mexico food I ever had. I and my husband both love it! Want to come back before we leave Santa Barbara.
They have a really nice staff! Ordered $200 in pizza/apps/salads, and we were able to all enjoy a beverage at the bar while we waited. Nice ambiance and bartender was very nice and helpful.

Everything is very flavorful and fresh.  The portions, as others may have noticed, are pretty large.

The lunch specials are quick choices and you will not leave hungry.

Only thing that needs to be improved are the french fries.  They are limp and soggy.  The spices are good, but please learn how to deep fry a potato correctly.  It's really the only thing that keeps me from coming multiple times per week.

Never heard of this place until today. Food truck came to my job and I ordered the Chicken arepas and the pequenos (mozzarella cheese bites) and let me tell you it was AMAZINGLY delicious. Good portion size and decent price. The owner was friendly and I would definitely go visit his restaurant in the future.

This is just a great neighborhood spot, every thing we've had has been fresh and delicious. The butterscotch latte is perfect for cold mornings, we've had a couple of the breakfast sandwiches that were all great and the lobster po'boy is a favorite. The juices are all super refreshing and made to order.

If you're looking for quality homemade sandwiches and pizza Cafe Carmela is the spot. I've been here twice and feel good recommending this place to my friends/family.

Their pizza is really good and tasty, the fries are fantastic with their cheese whiz they make. As far as the cheesesteak the roll was amazing but the insides didn't impress me one bit. 

Pizza 8.4
Fries 9.1
Cheesesteak 6.6

Maybe they just have an off day with the cheesesteak so I will give them another chance. 
The staff is also super friendly and accommodating.

Came back with my family this time, I was praising how good the place was to my sister and she couldn't stop talking about it so we came with our brother and mother. My mom is very hard to please when we go out to eat but we knew she enjoyed seafood and this place gives you a bucket of it! My sister and I got a pound each of crawfish (I got shaking sauce/ extra hot, my sister got garlic butter/medium), I got an extra side of corn on the cob and red skin potatoes, they both come with 3 if you add extra sides, if not it already comes with one additional potato and corn. My mother got a pound of black mussels (shaking sauce/extra hot). She LOVES them, probably the first time we heard her say amazing things about her meal. My brother got the 6oz lobster tail, he really enjoyed it, the sauce was soaking into the meat and he ate it with his rice. We finished everything and left very satisfied! My family will be back.

This was quite possibly the WORST service that I've ever had at a restaurant. I would recommend avoiding this place at all costs- just go to the Gumbo Shop which is a hop and a skip away. 

My boyfriend and I made a dinner reservation on Open Table and arrived on-time. When we got there, the hostess/server Ava (not her real name) was completely unaware of our reservation, which was the first sign of unprofessionalism, but was able to seat us anyway. When she seated us, we weren't given a menu or any other attention. After 5 minutes had passed of us just sitting there, my boyfriend got up and asked Ava if we could please get a menu. She said that our server would be with us shortly and that they would give us a menu. After several minutes of no attention from another server, Ava came over and finally gave us menus, with no other attention. Please note that the restaurant did not seem overly busy at this time- there were several empty tables, so they weren't at capacity. 

We looked over our menus and decided pretty quickly what we wanted. We sat there for at least another 10 minutes with no service. My boyfriend got up and asked the other server on duty, Matt (again, not his real name) if we could please get some service, as we had been waiting a long time. Matt said that ANOTHER server would come serve us shortly. That "other server" never came- after an additional 5 minutes of waiting, we decided to just walk out, despite being very hungry at that point. On our way out, the man who I presume is the manager there confronted us- my boyfriend explained that we were leaving, and we were upset that we hadn't gotten any service. The manager assured us that if we sat back down, we would get proper service. WRONG!

It was a mistake, but we sat back down, since we were really hungry. It was only after the manager talked to Matt that he came over to serve us. I was completely STUNNED that Matt had the nerve to say, "Sorry guys, I didn't notice that you were here." My boyfriend had LITERALLY just spoken with him and asked him for service sometime in the past 10 minutes. Matt's flippant and jerky attitude was incredible, and something that I've never experienced at a restaurant before. 

To make matters worse, I'm a vegetarian, and the one vegetarian menu item that they serve was unavailable that night. Matt checked with the kitchen to make sure they wouldn't make it, but he didn't try to see if they would make some other vegetarian substitute, as any other restaurant would. I'll eat fish in rare circumstances such as this when I can't get something vegetarian, so I opted for a fish dish instead. 

When my dish came out, the side rice dish had chicken and sausage in it. Matt knew that I was vegetarian (pescatarian for the night) and failed to tell me that the rice had meat in it. After all our trouble there, it was really really disappointing to not even be able to eat half of my meal. 

Matt was of course barely apologetic about the whole experience, but luckily they did not charge for my meal. I will say that the food that I did eat was good. My boyfriend and I left the restaurant as quickly as we could, and were very upset by the whole experience. We felt like we were treated in a terrible manner, and in a way that no one should be treated. We felt like we were intentionally being ignored, and can find no reason why they would have done that.

We came to this restaurant the day after Christmas. It was packed and they only had a few servers. It was the slowest Steak and Shake service I have ever experienced. Wd waited 30 minutes to be seated yet tables sat empty while we were waiting. We ordered and waited 35 minutes for our food to be delivered. The floor under our table was so sticky that at one point I almost pulled my foot out of my shoe because my shoe was stuck to the ground. The floors were dirty throughout. I am giving them two stars because the food was good and typical Steak and Shake food. We had a customer next to us wait 35 minutes for a hot dog. She then cancelles the order and told them just to bring her sundae. 15 minutes later they delivered it and it was wrong....she walked out.

Went for my first time today and the food was excellent!! I got the shawarna wrap with lamb and it was so good. We also got the chick pea snack, which were pretty good. The falafel was amazing and the dessert donuts were good, but the icing was the best thing I have tasted! We went during lunch time and it was very busy and we had to wait a long time for our food, but it was worth it for sure! I will surely go again.

I LOVE pizza and Ponzo's delivers good pizza! This spot is close to my office, so I usually swing in during lunch time- if I'm on a crunch, I call ahead and my order is usually read within 15 minutes. Large parking lot, it can get busy during lunch hour and beware of other business's reserved spots!

The slices here are large and the topping options are plentiful! But my favorite is the pizza rolls (orders of 3, 6 or 9) with ranch! They are like mini-calazones, little pouches of heaven aka- cheese & pepperoni. Dip them into ranch and you have yourself a mind blowing mouthful of deliciousness. Perfect order for me is 3, then I add a side salad. The salad is just enough for you to get some greens in your system, but get the balsamic dressing. Everything is made fresh, so even your pizza rolls will come fresh out of the oven! Canned sodas and waters for drink options. 

The only downfall- they aren't open on Mondays! I find myself craving their pizza after the weekend is up and I'm back at the office. Customer service is fabulous and the guys are super friendly. The shop is small but has that warm feeling. Come by Ponzo's and get your fingers greasy!

Best donuts I've ever had.

Friendly service - wanted a sugared donut and the they only had cinnamon sugared ones. They made me a batch on the spot.

The chocolate mousse donut is also great.
Terrific coffee, calming atmosphere, good options for seating, very reasonably priced.

We went here for my birthday dinner.  I had the table side guacamole which was really good!  Highly recommend.  My friend had the lamb it he felt sick most of the night dinner.  I had the scallops which were fantastic.  We decided on this restaurant for the view and ambience but when we got there, there was no outdoor seating at all.  It was not open. Very disappointing because we drove so far to the resort.  Dessert was not great.  It was a good meal but for $150 it was not worth it.

This is one of the best Indian food places I have been to. One of the main reasons why is because of their paneer bhurji. I am not sure what they put it in but it literally melts in your mouth and the cheese is stringy when you spoon it out. Another reason is their yummy spinach chaat. I would recommend you going for restaurant week because they have a good selection!

This spot is a must for experienced foodies or anyone who wants to try Korean food for the first time. It's nestled in the same plaza as H-Mart. The inside is immaculate and clean, the staff are curt and friendly. As for implementing safety precautions to Covid, they did a great job of distancing everyone. Offering bottled water, sanitizer and rules when it comes to wearing masks. 

Now for the food. You'll enjoy their array of food that their menu offers. I've tried the marinated crab, mandoo dumplings and kimchi soondubu and wasn't disappointed. The crabs were tender, sweet and the sauce complimented it. The kimchi had the right amount of vinegar and spice to it.

If I wrote a review when this place opened, I would have given it closer to 5 stars. However, over time, the burgers seem smaller, lack flavor, and are no longer worth the price. My last visit, the burger was bland and dry. The fries were overcooked and undercooked at the same time. I'm not sure if I'll make another trip to It's "Not" a Better Burger "Anymore"
Great place for a concert. A chance to see the smaller bands up close.  Drinks are good.  Get the "Cowboy Mouth."

Let me paraphrase on what I have read on restaurant's website first. Bacaro - a place blessed with its own unique atmosphere that is ideal for friends get together over a glass of wine and home made small plate of food. That is  Ristorante Acqua Alta, a brad new Italian restaurant serves Venetian food.

I invited my girlfriend for lunch. Total bill is 50 dollar for two because we decided to order today's special ($19.5)instead. I had clam in white sauce over spaghetti and my friend had Carbonara with salmon filling. Both dishes tasted very different from Americanized Italian food. The salty pasta revealed the natural flavor of the clam itself instead of heavy garlic sauteed sauce. My friend's Carbonara is a slightly hearty dish but the salmon filler has a delicate flavor that soften the "mass". We also shared a roasted pepper and eggplant vegetable stew. It tasted like a fine ratatouille. 

I was very happy for trying authentic Italian food despite of paying premium price. I would like to pay the same price for a non-Americanized Chinese food. Authenticity is the premium. Food prepared with pride and heritage worth the respect. 

Owner and chef are very friendly and approachable. Do chat with them if they are not too busy. I learned a lot about their food and why they chose to open this restaurant in Pinellas. I will definitely go back to try more dishes.

Picked this restaurant for dinner to celebrate two birthdays with the in-laws. I have been here once for lunch when while it has been Washoe Public House and it was average. The dinner menu and reviews looked intriguing so we showed up on a Friday night in the fall, really one of the first colder days of the year. We were sat in the back, in a room that was freezing, luckily after asking, the waiter turned off the air which helped a lot. The atmosphere inside was much more "sports bar" feeling than what I anticipated, which was maybe a bit more upscale, considering the prices for meals for dinner. And I am not afraid to spend money on good food. 

Between us all, I had the duck dish, my husband has the schnitzel, and others in our party had the rock candy short ribs and the daily selection of grass fed beef steak, which this day, was sirloin (M.P.) 

The duck had bamboo rice risotto with kumquat gastrique, and honey. The risotto was good at first, but the bitterness became a bit overwhelming for me. I think that is me though, because it reminded me of orange marmalade, which I am not a fan of due to the bitter taste from the rind. I only ate about a quarter of that. The duck was cooked perfectly, except would have liked crispier skin seeing as how the duck sat on top and didn't have any juice on top. 

Husband liked the schnitzel, he is picky too I guess, b/c he felt the pickled mushrooms were a weird combination, even though I told him it was an asian fusion restaurant. I thought the mushrooms were good. The schnitzel was super crispy, except where they poured sauce on. his suggestion would be to have the sauce on the side, to preserve the crispiness. 

The grass feed beef was a hit, and was raved about, it was served with potatoes and zucchini. The short rib, I think was enjoyed, the only other person to taste it said it was a bit dry, but the man eating it, prefers his meat well done, so I don't think he would have had the same complaints. It was a nice huge portion of beef and he ate every bit of it. 

The service was adequate and everyone was following covid protocols. I would hit this place up for some apps and happy hour, but didn't hit the mark for me as far as a nice dinner out.

Great meal.  Employees were professional and friendly.   Food came out fresh and at a good temp.  The portions were huge.  Had the ultimate fajita and they did not disappoint.  This dish could be shared depending on how hungry you are.  Would definitely recommend.

Great service, nice drink menu. The food was absolutely excellent. As a top rated restaurant in Edmonton I would have expected the menu to be a bit more innovative and creative but found it to be more on the traditional side. I will plan to go back but to keep up with a hot food scent in Edmonton they will need to stay interesting to keep customers in the seats.
It wasn't crowded, so decided to grab a gin and tonic. Happy hour just $3.00. They charged me $3.50 and cheapest gin possible. Oh well. I won't be back.
Been going to this place since it opened.  The best sushi on both sides of the river...better than tani's......delicious and fresh

We showed up as the restaurant was opening and waited in line approximately 5 minutes at the most. We were offered inside or outside and promptly sat. We were short of time because we had a show at the Granada Theatre after. Without even warning, our services was quick and the food was amazing. We had the popcorn tempura shrimp with had a great "bang" to it. My boyfriend had the Dracula roll and the pro melt. He preferred the pro melt, but both rolls were good. I had the sashimi. This by far is the best sashimi I have ever had. The albacore was topped with a minced garlic and thin green onions and the salmon, yellow tail, and tuna was very decent in size and delicious! This will definitely become a favorite of ours only 5 minutes from home!

Favorite casual dining restaurant. Kyle is our regular server and does a great job! Good food (love the lean bison alternatives to everything on the menu), talkable atmosphere, good service and reasonable prices.

If you are traveling to the Indianapolis area, or around the East Washington area I would avoid dining here. The food had a puréed texture, the chips in the nachos were soggy and the food was cold. The guacamole had no flavor whatsoever and there was a visible layer of grease on top of the food. On a scale of 1-5 I give this a -4. The only reason I chose to give it a 1 star was due to flan that was actually pretty tasty. But, I do not go out for lunch just to eat dessert.

One and DONE!!!!

A reservation was made for a party of 11 to celebrate my 61st birthday on December 4, 2021. Crescent City Steaks was chosen after deciding that we would try somewhere new, local, and had good reviews. In the past, I've eaten steaks at Ruth's Chris Steak House, Fleming's Prime Steakhouse, Chophouse of New Orleans, and Sullivan's Steak House, all of which were worthy of my time, palate, and money! This place, Crescent City Steaks, was absolutely HORRIBLE!!! The staff, the service, the food, the restrooms, the chairs, the water glasses.... all low level, no, I digress, make that no level!! I know this establishment is used to handling large groups, so I'm not sure what the problem was with my table, which consisted of family and friends. We were all well-mannered and dressed appropriately. Our group consisted of 4 males-ages 19, 31, 36, and 40: 7 females-ages 28, 29, 30, 34, 58, 60, and 61. No teeny-boppers, no troublemakers, no celebrities, no scam artists, no clowns! Just decent, educated, working, hungry, regular people expecting to eat, drink, laugh, celebrate, their loved one's birthday. All we wanted was our food and drinks delivered to our table as ordered. However, that is not what happened. There were (2) glasses of water that was compromised/dirty. The group order consisted of (5) different cuts of steaks, all cooked well done, as per the menu description. All (5) steaks were brought to the table with pink centers and blood drippage on the plates. When brought to the waitress' attention, she replied "when 
the steaks are thick and ordered to be cooked well-done, they should be requested as butterflied". She then proceeded to pick up the plates and return them to the kitchen for further cooking. Keep in mind that had she mentioned the disclosure about the well-done steaks being thick and needing to be butterflied, that's what we would have requested. A few minutes later, the steaks returned and guess what, still pink centers, still bloody! The waitress saw and heard our disgust about the steaks still not being correct!!! She offered no apology, no explanation, no empathy, no nothing!!! She left the table and we decided that we'd just take the steaks home and cook them further. The night was a bust! When she returned, we asked for go boxes and the check. Our food bill was $691.00, and the bar tab was $195.00. Since it was a large group, the 20% gratuity was included. Needless to say, none of the staff that we encountered, specifically the waitress/server deserved a dime!!! But even paying the bill was a problem! Since we had a large group, we wanted to pay the food bill with half in cash and the other half with a bank card. We were told that couldn't be done. Now once again, I'm more than sure that at some point, this request has been made by others and processed as such. So, after seeing that was an issue, the bill was just paid in full and with cash!! Luckily someone in the group was foolish enough to have that kind of cash on them at that time of night!!! The quality of food and method of payment were the biggest issues, however in addition to all of that, the greeter/hostess wasn't very friendly or inviting towards us. It seemed as though we were in the way as we sat in the lobby area waiting for everyone that was included in the group. The restrooms are small, one toilet stall, one sink, unkept, no changing table for infants, and no locks on the entry door. The chairs at the table are rickety and not very sturdy. 
So, like I said at the beginning of this very long, true story and disappointing birthday celebration (or lack thereof), "ONE AND DONE!" Crescent City Steaks located at 1001 N. Broad Street-New Orleans, LA. 70119 will NEVER see me or any of my family and friends again!!! PERIODT!!!!  This business deserves "no stars". But since I had to make a selection in order for this to post, I chose 1 star. But honestly, the time has come. The doors should be closed and locked permanently! After 87 years in business, it has run its course, literally!!!

We have gone here several times.. The food is good and to our liking- wish we could say the same about the service. I ordered Chai which is meant to be hot .. When I said it was cold, the waitress had the audacity to blame me for it being that way. (My husband ordered it while I was in the restroom) A simple hot replacement was all I expected. Don't expect much from the Rude waitress here.

We decided to stop here for a quick lunch on our way back from Catskill. Ambience looked nice, the place was busy and the service was first grade. Ordered a cup of Clam Chowder, Flounder for main dish and off course some beer. Pretty happy with everything we are back on the road and here comes the headache. The pain increased over the next few hours and I threw up immediately after I got to the home. My face was swollen and I felt pretty sick. A case of food poisoning and probably fish was the culprit. It was served well cooked, but probably not well refrigerated before cooking. Typical histamine poisoning which arises from rotten fish. I'm a scientist by profession, so I have my strong reasons to suspect that It came from that fish meal. The only food I had before this was my usual break fast. You guys should be careful, such food poisoning can be serious for few people.

I walked past The Artful Dodger about a jillion times, sneering as I went, probably muttering something under my breath about it being a pseudo-ye-olde-english-whatever tourist trap.

As she often does, April smacked me out of my snobbery and forced me to finally walk in for dinner one night and I'm glad she did.  It's not gonna set the world aflame, but if you're hankering for some good old-school English Pub food (read: fish & chips, shepherd's pie, etc.) you really can't go wrong here.  Very solid and reliable, if somewhat uninspiring and weak in terms of service and atmosphere. 

But hey:  when you want good fish & chips, you want good fish & chips!

Such good food! Also, some of the best pizza I've ever had! The prices are good and the owners and staff are so friendly. The portions are amazing, well priced and I have never gotten something from here that I didn't love. The restaurant is clean, including the kitchen. Would highly recommend to anyone looking for a delicious and reasonably priced snack or meal.
Great way to try a variety of unique seafood dishes! I loved the music to and all the proceeds go to flood victims this year!

We went out for brunch on Sunday morning looking forward to a stellar omelet.  We arrived and there were only two other tables occupied.  The restaurant got busier and we observed 4 other tables had received food when they had arrived at least 10 to 15 minutes after us.  When we finally got the server's attention, we asked about our food.  He told us that they were experiencing a rush.  We reminded him that we had arrived well before said rush.  He said he would check on our order and eventually came back with more coffee informing us our food was on its way.  Much later, still no food and we asked a different server who was also going to check into it.  We finally left after a 45 minute wait with no food or explanation for the deplorable lack of service.  We have patronized this restaurant in the past experiencing reasonable food quality and variable service with a side of arrogance.  Arrogance is never palatable, especially when the service is poor.  We will not return - zero service, zero food and zero stars.

There is no other cheese steak better, by far than the cheese steaks at Michael's. If you ever talked to Michael, he is passionate about always searching for the leanest, most tender, less fatty steak in the world. Yes the WORLD. He is always challenging his suppliers about getting the best for his customers. Have the conversation with him, and you will feel his passion - how he searches for nothing but the best for his customers.     

oh, try his Prosciutto Italian Hoagie. It is equally "the best" if you like all the great Italian ingredients that surround it - you will love his hoagies, too.        Nick Cirilli, Wallingford

Wow this place is great. We live in Philly but this was our first time there.  I got the traditional and my wife the vegan traditional.  The fries and gravy are great, but cheese curds make it spectacular.  The staff was friendly and explained the options.  Now I want to try everything on the menu. If your on South St. go there, if not get there.  Maybe I'll see you there,  "let's get squeaky."

Great place for lunch - the portions are reasonable and tasty. A word to the wise - stay away from the Caprese Sandwich.  The tomatoes and mozzarella are sliced paper thin so it ends up being a pesto sandwich.

Our wonderful Server Stephanie really made our lunch both delicious & memorable!

Visiting from out of town to discover the Hyde Park District and stopped by this Pub & Grill, atmosphere is casual & friendly.

Items ordered: 

The Grinder: American Wagyu Beef is layered with Swiss Cheese, Onion, Mushrooms & Grilled Red Peppers. Dip into the Au Jus or the Creamy Horseradish completes this symphony of flavours!

House Salad comes with my Wagyu Burger and I love the Lemon Tahini Dressing, the slight lemony taste lightens the whole meal!

Full Caesar Salad add on Salmon & Shrimp. Both seafood were grilled to perfection without being over cooked. Caesar is dressed well with a balance of garlic and lemon juice.

Thanks again to our super friendly Stephanie! Making our visit to the area so much more enjoyable!!

I moved here from Wisconsin where we often had Papa Murphy Pizza. This is the first time I have ordered in Boise and I chose the Apple Street store for convenience. We got our pizzas at the correct pickup time and the order was correct. My problem is that the toppings were pathetic. We ordered half pepperoni and half artichoke heart. There were about 6 pieces of pepperoni and the "artichoke hearts" were 2 anemic leaves and no hearts and even with this they were so skimpy!  In Wisconsin I would see the pizza assembled and they would weigh the toppings so it was consistent across customers and so newbies knew how much to put on. I hope it is just this location because I like PM pizza, but I will try a different location next time. PM headquarters should have a talk with the manager.

Came in here for a snack at the recommendation of a friend who lives in Philly.  The decor was super cute - the outside looked like a 60s diner, the interior had a more modern feel. They had a different menu between 4-5pm. The lobster mac (no mac, just orzo rice) n cheese was legit. Also had the Cheese steak eggrolls were a little on the salty side. Loved their cocktail menu - the hammonton cocktail was delicious.
Wasn't sure if I would be a fan of this bar especially since the girls only wear lingerie. But it actually wasn't that bad, they had a band, the bartenders were cool. I'll def be back.

This is the FOURTH time they screwed up our food this month. They read our order back to us correctly but apparently you need a college degree to make a HAMBURGER correctly. Not hard to leave cheese off. 

Tonight, they made two burgers... both times it was screwed up. 

I left having eaten my tots and drank my drink before the third burger even came. Never again am I coming back here.

I did not get reimbursed. I'm mad as hell. Of all the Sonics we have been to around the country from Minnesota to Texas... this one is THE WORST.

The Red Lobster in Port Richey is WAY better! I have worked at this Red Lobster in the past and I will warn you it is very unsanitary! Silverware is not clean most of the time and sometimes on a busy day when silverware is being cleaned, Servers will get impatient and run silverware UNDER THE SINK with warm water! This place is DISGUSTING!

This is a wonderful restaurant!  Very nicely decorated, with a large bar at the back which serves appetizers or an entire meal.  We were there with 2 friend and all of us were hungry. Each couple started with the crab cake appetizer...delicious with lots of crab!  We then each shared a salad and all of us had the Chilean Sea Bass as our entree. All I can say is PERFECTION!  We will definitely be back!

Ended up waiting 20 minutes with a group of five. Once we got seated, our drink order wasn't taken and we waited another 15 minutes to get our order taken. Once we got our food, they messed up each and everyone of our orders. Our server didn't write any of our orders down either. They forgot our drinks still, and forgot my order that took another 10 minutes to get out. Our food was cold and the meat was dry, and none of us ended up eating half of our food. They claim for "new cooks" but if there is, it shouldn't of taken that long to come and check on your table. Absolutely ridiculous.

I'm so excited to have a new brewery in the downtown area. Although I wish it were within walking distance from other downtown spots, it's a great space with awesome beer. Big fan of the open mic stand up nights that they've been hosting and i have a feeling that Ellison will be great for the Indy community! 

I recommend trying both of their sour beers!!!! Planning to come back soon!!!
Always consistent, my favorite is the rum ba ba. Also love the cannoli and the Italian cookies.

For the price, go to The Journey instead. A lot of the food trays were empty and the floors were sticky/slippery with grease. The sushi bar was completely empty of everything nothing was restocked before I had to leave.

One of my favorite gastropubs! Delicious kale salad, Mac n cheese, fries, and burger. I literally get those items whenever I go for dinner. The cocktails are refreshing and very tasty. I recommend trying a few of their speciality cocktails, they are definitely work the price. The ambiance and overall experience is always very pleasant.

I was here with a friend for happy hour a few months ago. It was great- crowded but service, food, cocktails, beer selection, ALL good. We went back last night for a birthday dinner with two more friends. DIFFERENT EXPERIENCE.
 
(I am a former bartender, expediter so I have some point of reference here)

We arrived 45 minutes before our reservations to have drinks at a table around the bar. This turned into one drink before dinner because it took 40 mins to get them.  

After we were seated, ordered another round and some apps.  20mins later, 3 of the 4 apps came but drinks didn't.. The waitress said the bar was backed up and extended her apologies. Which was possible, however, the bar by this point was not packed, normal crowd. 10 mins later, we ordered dinner and at the point our 4th app showed up and finally the drinks. 

Dinner comes (we ordered one more round of drinks). I had the NY Strip so I was expecting a NY STRIP, right? Wrong.  Instead, I received 6 bites of overcooked steak, a smear of spinach puree and 6 quarter inch squares of beets for $28. My friend received inedible, greasy fried chicken and fake slaw. She let the waitress know it wasn't to her liking and sent it back. 

15mins later, the waitress gave us the crappiest version of a funnel cake I've ever had. She was trying to be nice and it was appreciated but don't give me something terrible to make up for terrible service. Oh, that's when our next round of drinks finally showed up. 

Whether it was the kitchen, the bar or the wait staff, who cares, It took a party of 4 three hours to get 3 rounds of drinks and an overpriced, sub-par dinner. The bill came, ($200++). No courtesy of even a comp drink or plate 

never again..

We had never heard of Sharrott but, since it was on the list, visited during Barrel Trail Weekend.  What a find!
First, the barrel tour/tasting experience - wow!  The owner of the winery took us back to the barrel aging room, all the time humorously and fascinatingly teaching us about many of the skills, work and science that go into making a good bottle.  Once there, we got to taste some wines (white and red and their Wicked Port!!!) that he pulled right from the barrel, in the middle of the aging process and then the same wines that had finished and were bottled.  What a great experience and opportunity - we learned so much and thoroughly enjoyed both the wines and the experience in its entirety.
We will absolutely be back.  We will absolutely be purchasing from Sharrott again, and I highly recommend giving them a try.

Pretty solid pizza, friendly yet sometimes inattentive staff and  fashionably quaint décor.  

There are different types of pizza in the world, and I tend to fancy the NY sort.  My second favorite is the fire/coal oven sort, and that's what they serve up here at Cristino's.  

Once you make it past the smelly garbage cans leaking dumpster juice into the alley, you're immediately welcomed by a large patio area with a bar and plenty of outside seating.  I imagine that during any other time of the year, it looks great out there.  However, it's fall and the patio was littered with leaves from the looming oak trees.  I saw a few employees doing a whole lotta nothing, and I think they should have been sweeping.

Inside, La Chica and I walked past the hostess, who appeared to be taking an order over the phone.  She looked like she wanted to help, but couldn't, so we went straight for the bar.  We were greeted by a kid who said, "If you're ordering drinks, I'll have to get you a real bartender.  I'm just making a drink for the owner."  During my visit here, I saw and made eye contact with the owner 4 or 5 times.  Not once did he acknowledge me, ask how I was doing or inquire about my perception of the staff or service.  Just a side note.

While waiting for a "real" bartender, it was hard not to notice the pizza cook standing by the ovens eating.  It was just gelato, but I don't think employees should be eating in the area where pizzas are slapped out, topped and baked.  Go grab a seat dude!

A "real" bartender came over, greeted us, took our food and drink orders.  The kid was friendly and very sociable.  Problem is, once he dropped off our food, he disappeared.  My drink sat empty, and was never refilled, despite two separate employees stopping by the bar area to make drinks for other tables.

As for the food, we ordered a 12" pizza margherita with sausage.  The pizza came quick.  Those coal ovens must burn at 600 degrees or something like that because the pie seriously came out in 6-7 minutes.  It was hot, fresh and delicious.  There's nothing like coal oven pizza crust.  My only suggestion would be just a tad bit more cheese.  I realize that with a margherita, the pizza doesn't get complete cheese coverage, but I found the cheese serving on mine to be sparse at best. 

Would I go back?  Probably not.  The pizza around the corner at Bellini is cooked in a similar over, and the service is a bit more attentive.  Plus, the manager there almost always talks to the guests.
It was just okay. The onion rings were the best part.  Fires seafood platter wasn't crispy, the batter was on the verge of soft and mushy.

Was looking for a place near where we were shopping and took a chance with only one review up. However, when I saw it had previously been a food truck I figured it should be good and I'm glad I stopped by. The queso birria was awesome, the right amount of cheesy and the crema on the side was delicious. I will be dreaming about those nacho chips for a while! They almost tasted like fried wontons to me, which I'm totally down with. They were the right amount of crispy and not greasy at all. The meat was good and tender, although there is some gristle so don't be surprised. I got a mix of the strawberry and watermelon aqua fresca and it was amazingly refreshing. Highly recommend giving this place a try!

To start with this bar pub has over 50 beers and the best of this side of Mississippi bartender,MORGAN . I seriously don't know how she runs the bar and the all the drinks for this restaurant/ bar . She is always happy and after the first night we came back again for happy hour and she remembered our drinks and served them within minutes. Very pretty , classy and has this bar in complete control. She a bataAsk for her and tell her Dawn sent u !!!

Just had lunch here with my folks for the first time. Walking into the place it has a great atmosphere with pleasant decor, a spacious room and good laid back music. After getting seated we were helped promptly. I ordered the smoked salmon benedict and some hibiscus tea. My parents got the giant pancake and a chilled soup with avocado, serrano-chilies and yogurt. We also shared a cup of chia pudding with walnuts and caramelized bananas. 

I would say that my dish was the best of the ones we ordered. The poached eggs were done perfectly over just the right amount of smoked salmon, with a touch of balsamic on the english muffin. My dad got the pancake plain (you can add blueberries and/or walnuts) and quite enjoyed it. My mom got the soup, which she said was missing a little something, albeit quite tasty. 

The desert was ridiculously good. The chia pudding itself had a touch of sweetness to it and a nice creamy texture which contrasted wonderfully with the walnut and bananas on top.

On a side note, our server mentioned that they're expanding to having drinks and dinner available in the near future. All in all I'll definitely be back the next chance I get.

First time eating here and the Friday special (pulled pork) was recommended.  It was unbelievably great.  I also got the cole slaw and barbeque baked beans.  I'll be going back to try other things.  Highly recommend this place of you're thinking about trying it.

I can see the appeal to this place.  I mean "AYCE" sushi  who doesn't want in right? However, they don't serve sushi  grade/premium fish.  So if you're looking for fresh sushi grade fish this not your place.  It wasn't ours either.  Service was great, staff friendly and ambiance was nice.  Though food was less than sub-par.

As you will read, get there early. Business before 9a is robust and donuts fly out of the display.  Bavarian/Boston crepe filled long Johns are awesome - my wife's fave. She also likes the raspberry filled donuts.  I'm more of a glazed cake donut or bear claw kinda guy. These are terrific as well. Add the cheese or cherry danish and it's a home run.

Very unassuming location but so worth the stop because the food was delicious and a very friendly and comfortable atmosphere. The staff is super friendly and very attentive making you feel like old friends enjoying a relaxing get together. The chips are thin and crispy, salsa is perfect and the margaritas are excellent.I had the  Barbacoa  chimichangas (perfectly cooked and spiced perfectly) with cilantro rice and beans. Husband had the LA special which was a grilled chicken breast topped with shrimp, grilled onions peppers and cheese, served with cilantro rice and beans. This may be my new favorite go to place for Mexican food and if you decide to visit I know you won't be disappointed.

Ok so the first time around I didn't have the best experience , (food mixup/customer service ) but the owner quickly messaged me on the app and told me next time I stopped by lunch was on them . It was very nice of the owner and they clearly care to make it up for their customers. Anyways I finally got the acorn squash curry chicken salad and it was delicious . Clean , healthy serene place to eat at . Simple !

I've had the breakfast buffet a couple of times and lunches a couple of times. Always a great experience. It's not cheap but it's what you'd expect from a place that's downtown, fancy surroundings, room to breathe, creative and excellent food.

One of my favorite date-night spots. 

Cozy up with one of their fun cocktails or delicious glasses of wine and prepared to be blown away. I've been here with my family, just with my boyfriend, and for their NYE prix fixe night, and had a little bit of everything on their menu.

All the food is beautifully presented AND delicious. For date night, we always spilt a few of their toasts; a pasta, raw dish, or salad; and then a dessert. And if you're only going to get one thing here- make it the toast with beef tartare. Easily one of our favorite dishes in the city. And if you're going to get two things, add on the tuna poke....and if you're going to get three things, order their fruit crisp of the evening...and, well at that point, you can walk home happy.

Made a reservation on OpenTable for a dinner our last Sunday night. We are new to the Nashville area and are slowly trying to try everything out!

Pemrose sounded good based on reading their menu. We used the valet parking out front, which is a nice touch downtown, and were immediately seated once we got inside. Our waiter come soon after and brought water and took drink orders. The coke fountain line was empty or something and also their drafts weren't working and they only had beer on bottles available when we were there.

We ordered the crab dip as a starter and also the sourdough bread and butter. I don't particularly like Fritos so I ordered the bread to use the crab dip on... bread costs $6, and is not complementary. The dip was really good and I can see how it is one of their specialties. I wouldn't say it's as good as the crab dip I've had in Maryland... but it's up there!

For meals, I ordered the warm lobster roll and instead of fries, tried the Mac and cheese. My meal was really good. Being from New England, I know a good lobster roll and this was really good! The Mac n cheese was also really good too!

My husband ordered the burger with crab cake on it. He said the burger was average and the bottom roll ended up getting super soaked with grease, but he did enjoy the crab cake on top. You don't get that everywhere!

Overall we enjoyed the dinner but it wasn't a place we would necessarily rush back to with so many other options around. If you do decide to go here, get the crab dip!

loved the 1950's vibe from the place. food looks and tastes amazing. when we walked in it was very loud and noisy, the hostess couldn't hear me speak even when i was next to her. we had to wait 5-10 minutes to get a table but that was understandable because it was lunch time. when we finally sat down our waitress took our drinks but she was stacked with tables that she seems a bit stressed. we tried to ask to put in our order but she said she had to take another order then ours. she didn't have much of an order so it was easier on herself. as soon as the food hits the window they send it out which is weird because we didn't get our whole order together, we got it in parts so by the time i finished my eggs that came with my food, my pancakes had just come. food overall was amazing and i would definitely recommend it

I like this place! They have a good selection- for as much as they are compared to Chipotle, they have a wider selection of food items. Between me and my boyfriend we have tried the veggie, chicken and pork in tacos, burritos and a quesadilla. All are good and at a decent price point. The chips are fresh made (and free) and I love ALL the salsas in the salsa bar. The street corn is crafted to perfection, too! The beer selection is impressive and, honestly, overwhelming! This place can fill up quick, but the indoor/outdoor seating area seems to turn over just in time! This is becoming one of my favorite downtown places - quick, fair-priced, tasty and customizable!

Delicious food and great curbside service. Ordering online was confusing at first but a text was sent after ordering and all was good! Pulled up and they had food ready to go. Food was delicious. Pad Thai is awesome.
Food is ok. Chips and salsa were good. We ordered the chicken tostada, vegetable tostada, and fish tacos. All were average.

Food: 4 stars
Service: 3 stars
Location: 4 stars
Ambiance: 3.5 stars
Price: 4 stars

Recommendations:  The Good Dog Burger is excellent.  Its one of the top 5 burgers I've had in Philadelphia (see TOP 5 BURGERS LIST).  The highlight of the meal are the french fries which are served as a combination of Sweet Potatoes and Yukon Gold Potatoes.  The beer selection on tap are unique and fun to try.  My fiance got the Fried Tomato BLT which she loved as well.

My only critique is that service can be a little bit more personal and that the ambiance is a little too dark for my taste in a pub style restaurant/bar.  They have so many great pictures of dogs on their walls; I wish they would feature them a little bit better.

Overall: 4 stars
A great place to get dinner and drinks and kick off your night with a little pre-party.

An absolutely fantastic bagel spot/deli/restaurant.

Their breakfast sandwiches/bagels are fantastic. The bagels are freshly made and delicious. I went there two days in a row for a Taylor Ham, egg, and cheese sandwich. The first time I got it on an everything bagel, and later a poppy one. Both were equally delicious. 

A few days ago, I also swung by to grab lunch and got a turkey and cheese on a bagel. These bagel deli sandwiches are delicious!!!  Lots of meat and cheese and 10000x better than any Wawa sandwich or bagel.

The coffee is good - strong and bold Colombian roasts available. They also offer free (and amazing) biscotti and other baked goods on a small table near the counter, for those who wait.

Lastly, they  have done a wonderful job keeping the place look cute and clean. Unlike most bagel places, they have an entire back area with booth and table seating. 

Five stars - a clean and cozy atmosphere, fantastic deli, and amazing coffee.
This place hit the target right on! Great and friendly staff and very enjoyable dinner.  Our host was knowledgeable about the food and culture.  Would definitely go back again.

I'm a fan. If for nothing but the amazing baguette and the ham and butter that makes it a perfect sandwich. The vibe and building were awesome too. 

But what's with the service? No numbers on our orders? A mass stands and waits for their drinks and food around a counter, and a random person yells out "ham and butter," and of course half a dozen of us have ordered that, so what are we supposed to do? The assertive extroverts win again (I'm one of those, but still had to wait longer than I wanted!). Moreover, my friend's drink was forgotten about. And another reported to me it took a longer time to get his coffee than it would have if he rode his bike home and made his own cup.

Very cool spot with high quality food, but please, get it together!
Amazing place, brand new with the signature coffee. Delicious and beautiful presentation.  Kids friendly.

This place is energy! Amazing decor and good music. Salsa is good, fiesta bowls are okay, but the TACOS AND APPETIZERS ... Perfectly balanced and full of fresh flavor. Portions are big. Gluten free and vegan options. Reasonably priced as well. The server, Alexis, was on point. So nice!

Great food great people ! Perfect neighborhood gem . We have heard great things about this place , so we finally went last night and we were beyond happy we stopped . If you want authentic Italian you should hurry in .
I love QuikTrip. For a gas station they sure have a lot of great food choices and drinks. I love buying my breakfast from there and my drinks. Great place.

Absolutely amazing food.  We started with the Mix Cold Appetizer Plate for the 3 of us, but it could have served six easy.  Babaganoush, humus, Russian salad (kind of like a potato salad), an eggplant side and 2 more served with warm bread.  Each one was so mouth wateringly wonderful and that would have been a great meal, BUT of course we ordered MORE.  We ordered the Mixed Grill of shish kebab, chicken kebab, lamb gyro, chicken gyro and Inegol kofte served over a bed of rice.  The luscious & juicy meat highly flavored the rice.  Just sublime in every way.  Maria was our server and she was so friendly and attentive, we are asking for her next time and that will be soon. All three of us HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!  My mouth is watering now, LOL.

Really happy with this option in the mall's food court. It's one of the healthier options (if you leave out the fries). 

I've eaten here twice now. The first time I had a chicken wrap (pita bread) and the second time I had a gyros wrap. Both times the food was fresh, salad crunchy and the meat warm. 

The last time I was disappointed. Apparently they prepared my gyros wrap without asking me which vegetables I wanted, so I ended up with lots of raw onions. Yuk! 

Their baklava looks good, so I'll have to try that soon. Large pieces though! No one in Turkey or Greece eats them in that size, but hey, this is America!

Holy moly, I was not expecting this place to be so good! We went for dinner and had the Malai Kebab and the Rogan Josh, with sides of Mushroom Poriyal (AMAZING!!!), garlic naan, and one of the stuffed naans (server chose for us, and I have no idea which one we got). I ordered a spice level of 5 out of 10 (medium salsa is sometimes a bit too hot for me!), but next time I'll try a 7. I already can't wait to go back! Yes, the pricing is a bit high, but each dish is huge. We had enough left-overs for two lunches today, and all of it was still divine heated up.

I was skeptical when we first sat down, given that it was mostly empty, the decor was a bit odd, and they had a QR scanner on the table instead of actual menus (which annoyed me). Fortunately, the food speaks for itself. Loudly.

I've only gone here once when I was craving hot spicy soup. I saw a food vlogger video coming here and it didn't disappoint. Fast service, clean restaurant, reasonable prices, flavorful soup. Will definitely come back.

Miss Amy at the front is the sweetest host as can be. The Mac and cheese was super moist and the pork was so tender. I love this little place with an adorable upstairs bar as well. Perfect for game days with your people. Very respectful due to covid. Love this place feels like a little treasure.

After the long 2 months of staying in and now that restaurants are opening back up. The fiancé and I were in need for a date night and we decided on Murrietas since it was close by and wanted something different from our usual Mexican spot at La Fuente.

When we got there it was actually a little busy and the wait was supposed to be 20 minutes but we went to the bar , got our drinks, and they called us up pretty quickly.

The micheladas here are pretty good ( we got it with Modelos) and served in a huge glass , which is great!  I ended up getting 2 because they were that good!

We were seated outside kind of near the doors which was fine because it was quiet and peaceful where we were sitting. 

As far as the food goes: DELICIOUS! 
I found the food to be really flavorful, great portions, and really filling. 

We ordered a side of the mango salsa and calamari and the calamari was seriously delicious. I also like the fact that it was in strips so it was easier to eat and dip into the sauces. 

For the main dishes my fiancé ordered the carnitas rancheras and I ordered the Baja fish tacos. I had a taste of my fiancés food and the meat was so tender and flavorful. The fish tacos were delicious also , it was crispy and had some kind of coleslaw/cilantro sauce on it but either way it was so good!

I also wanted to say their rice was really good also, i find some Mexican restaurants rice can be really bland on flavor , but this place really knew how to make their dishes very good in flavor and i ended up really liking the rice from here.

Overall, i'm impressed with Murrietas and happy we chose here as our first dine in date night after all the craziness. Its close by to us also which is super convenient!
Beautiful rooms, though expensive. Very nice staff. Helpful. We had a queen suite with jacuzzi. The jacuzzi was wonderful. Nice patio off the jacuzzi room. Two gas fireplaces. Great location.

Food was really good.. I had the chicken salad.. It was fresh and amazing.. I ordered a Lemon Drop martini and it was to die for.. Could only have one.. LOL.. My waiter was awesome.. I had ordered a special menu for my boyfriend due to the fact he was on a NO CARB Diet and he accomodated us to the tee.. He did exactly what we ordered and my boyfriend was content with his steak.. The waiter was super attentive to us and that made us feel good.. Wish I remembered his name.. but between the martini and the great company I was with it completely slipped my mind.. I do remember that he mentioned that he was studying to be a school teacher and he had a lisp.. I also remembered had a hearing aide on both ears.. Super nice guy.. Look for him when you guys go there.. You won't regret it..

So very glad I stopped by here today. Was recommended by a local (after I saw his takeout). 

This is off the main drag but totally worth the stop of you are looking for a awesome Rueben sandwich.  A true delight and the freshest of ingredients. This kosher deli and marketplace has lots of choices when it comes to food. Fresh, canned, dry, breads, etc. 

I was very happy with my meal and it arrived very fast. Most lunch plates in the $9.00-$11.00 range. 
When back in St. Pete, I'll be back again!

After paying 35.00$, it took over an hour and a half to get our food, and when we got it we had cold, tasteless pizza with canned mushrooms and greasy, undercooked breadsticks with cold dipping sauce. The wings were alright, and they're generous on the extra sauce, but we will never be ordering from here again. We were really hoping for a nice independent pizza place to order from in the future. Too bad :(

Picked up the MOST amazing and delicious *vegan* meats and treats from Poppy The Suffering Vegan  I got: 2lbs if mac & cheese, so perfect for a quick easy delicious meal to heat up at home! 1lb each of the turkey deli meat and gyro meat. I sautéed up the gyro meat with some onions and had the BEST *vegan* meaty gyro I've even had! 1lb (4 big links) andouille sausage that I am so excited to try in a gumbo!!! And so many other treats, I can't express how happy I am with it all!!!!!  See the picture of me with the raspberry coconut layer cake, that about sums it up.  Thank you Poppy & Derek for making amazing vegan food accessible and affordable for your FQ and local NOLA fans and friends. I love you!!!
Went back today, the service just keeps getting slower! There were only 5-6 other tables and we waited 40 minutes for the first plates to arrive.

Acceptable room. 
Remodeling? An extreme loud banging next door. 
Children screaming and running in the hallway by 11:00pm. 
Pleasant checking-in/out.

We went to order take out for our family and were told we could not order kids meals for our kids unless we came in and sat down to eat. We were not allowed to order kids meals through the drive thru or carry out. The manager advised it is a new corporate policy. I can only assume it is to prevent adults ordering kids meals. They are apparently losing so much money from adults trying to get one over on them through the drive thru that they are willing to lose entire orders because of it. We ended up at Cheddars instead where my six year old and 22 month old can get meals designed for kids. Yes, we could order an adult meal and split it, but we shouldn't have to. We will give our business to a company who is more family oriented.

Limited tables and the music is too loud and I wish they would also play  Filipino songs instead. The foods that we ordered were a little bit salty except for the talangka rice. Talangka means crab in Filipino  but I didn't taste any of it in my rice but I still liked it. I mean,  there's always a room for improvement. I would still gonna go back in here and give it a second try.

Food was amazing! I am so happy they have a veggie version of the smothered fries! Service was quite slow and inattentive for as few customers as there were at the time we ate. We were finished eating for over 20 minutes (table already cleared) before our bill came.

Food was unique and executed very well; I had the pheasant scrapple which was super.  Decor is open with lots of light.  Pricing was fair and accommodated both big and small budgets.  I was there for Sunday brunch which also featured a live band.  I thought the sound was great, maybe a little loud if you were hoping to chat with friends, but the band (bluegrass) was perfect for the setting.

Parking is not great, but nothing unusual for the area.

Great food, but the wait staff turns tables too fast!

The food at Cafe Giovanni is good, but part of a dining experience is being able to take your time, have a conversation, and enjoy the food.  This is not possible at Cafe Giovanni.  When I was there for French Quarter Music Fest, we had to ask our server three times to slow down and give us more time.  The staff wants to turn tables quickly, and I'm sure they have been instructed to do so, but this doesn't make for a pleasant dining experience when you have to shoo your waiter away, and they hover by the table, waiting to turn it.  I won't go back for this reason, there are too many great restaurants in New Orleans to put up with this kind of service.

I always come to the Mall at Green Hills-I love the environment, store selection, and the level of customer service.  I was really excited to try Coco's because the menu looked great.  I was immediately a little irritated because the man working at the counter (a tall older white man with a moustache) was very rude from the beginning.  He was acting like he was bothered to take my order and answer my questions about the sandwich I wanted to order.  I ordered the sandwich, but when I got it, I did not like it at all.  He added something that he did not tell me when I was asking the questions.  I approached the man again to see if I could order something else because I did not like that.  He basically argued with me and accused me of wanting it for free, stating he would not make me anything else.  He would not even listen long enough to hear that I was not expecting it for free.  I was willing to pay.  I just wanted to order something else because that sandwich was not good.  I was honestly shocked by how rude and aggressive he was.  I asked to speak with the manager, and I was even more blown away to find out he WAS the manager.  It is pretty shocking that someone with that attitude and complete lack of professionalism was able to retain that position.  I'm disappointed in my experience, but I'm also discouraged that a business like that is now at the Mall.

We came here for a drag show last night and were impressed!  The drinks were good and it was a very well organized event.  I wish the seating was a little more spread out and the traffic of servers during the show can be bothersome.

Best waffle cone and best ice cream I've had in a long time. Simple, but original flavors with perfect texture and taste. The waffle cone had just enough cinnamon and sweetness. Staff was helpful and ET me sample just about every flavor. Wish I lived close... LOVED the place.

Really cool spot. The variety of good food was impressive. Duck wontons were one of the best things I've ever had. Had a pizza with Brussels sprouts on it that was amazing as well. Definitely look forward to another visit.

My vegetarian husband and I went here for dinner on the advice of my coworker and we brought along a non-vegetarian friend. It is the type of restaurant where you order at the counter and then they bring you your food. They also have hibachi entrees, but do not make the food in front of you (they make it in the back and then bring it out). 

It was a fun experience as we tried a lot of different menu items for a fairly inexpensive price - we tried the vegetable soba, vegetable hibachi, the spring rolls, the vegetable tempura, the sweet potatoes tempura roll, and the Japanese donuts. Of all of the menu items we tried, the vegetable soba was preferred by both my husband and I.  Next time, that is what we both plan to order. I did appreciate having lots of different options to choose from instead of just one vegetarian option.
The atmosphere was great, but the food, not so much.  The menu was promising, but the results were just so so.  Needs improvement.

Excellent food, cocktails, and service. We had scallops and drum, which were both lovey. The lobster dumplings are amazing. We had creme brûlée for desert, perfect! I would highly recommend this place, one of the better meals we've had in New Orleans.

So I'm not going to sugar coat it: In case you didn't already know, Grand Lux Cafe is an upscale version of the Cheesecake Factory. (They're run by the same company; the dessert menu even features some of the Cheesecake Factory's more basic selections.) We went for the training/sneak preview event before their official opening next week, so despite having a hugely extensive (and overwhelming) menu like Cheesecake Factory, we were given a limited menu comprised of certain items so that the kitchen could practice preparing different dishes. 

We were allowed to choose 2 appetizers. My dining partner picked a calamari salad and I got Vietnamese Chicken summer rolls. The summer rolls were AMAZING! I love eating them at Vietnamese restaurants and I love making them at home. They were the perfect treat on such a hot day! The menu states that it's served with a peanut sauce but they also gave me a Thai sweet chili sauce; both complimented the rolls perfectly. And for being an appetizer, the calamari salad was ginormous! It had me nervous about what my entree salad was going to look like. (NB: The menu on their website lists it as a "small salad"; it was easily enough for 2 people.) My only complaint is that the calamari was fried and warm. While it does state this in the menu description (crispy calamari), I just think a cold calamari salad might have been a better fit with the "upscale" environment. (But I guess I don't create the menu, lol!) 

Then things went downhill when it came to entree-time. We get it - this is new for everyone, the kitchen was very busy, etc. So while our waiter kept assuring us that our food would be out shortly, we expected it to at least come as we requested. My dining partner ordered his burger medium-rare; it was fully cooked to slightly well done. And my southwestern salad (which was also super big, and served in an awkward oval shaped dish as opposed to a big bowl like the calamari salad) looked promising... until I moved my tomato wedge around to slice it and saw what appeared to be a tiny green string of lettuce, but upon closer inspection, seemed like a piece of plastic - perhaps from a prep item or a scouring pad. And then, I found another string...and another string. 

One of the 'seasoned' wait staff who was present for the training process noticed my confusion with the salad and came over to inspect the foreign object with the manager, who then apologized profusely and promptly removed my salad. He asked if there was anything else that he could get me in the meantime; I was ok at the moment so he said he was going to bring me a brand new salad to take home - and then we were given 2 $25 gift cards as well for our trouble. The situation was definitely handled tactfully and he went above and beyond to make sure that I didn't leave with a bad taste in my mouth. 

Oh! I almost forgot - Dessert! We were allowed to choose 2 desserts but the one dessert my dining partner wanted, they had run out of earlier. (A banana caramel bread pudding which sounded amazing!) I wanted to order the "create your own cupcake" which consisted of 4 cupcakes, 3 frostings (peanut butter, vanilla/coffee? - not sure. I kind of got a hint of coffee, and a rich chocolate) and assorted toppings (sprinkles, chocolate chips, peanuts, toffee chips) - so that was more than enough for both of us. The peanut butter frosting was out of this world and our waiter, the pro-waiter and the manager kept coming over and telling us that was their favorite too! 

While I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here again (especially since Cherry Hill is kind of out of the way from my neighborhood in Philadelphia), it's definitely a perfect fit for the suburbs, and a nice dining experience for anyone who has a lot of picky, indecisive eaters in their family or social circle.

Being from Detroit, this is one of the most authentic Coney Island restaurants I have ever been to. Just like home and the original Lafayette Coney Island. I work in the area and stop by tonight for the pre grand opening. Excellent staff all from Michigan great restaurant, good service, and excellent food. Not only do they serve original Coney Island dogs, they serve Faygo Saunders hot fudge and better made chips, if you're from the D you know what I'm talking about.! This is my new favorite restaurant, and will be yours stop by and check it out.
The Australian guy who works behind the bar is rad.  Everyone else is pretty cool as well.
Excellent customer service and delicious BBQ. Loved the pork and collard greens. They make you feel right at home here.

Third Lincoln square we've eaten at. 
1) food is better than you'd expect. Omelets made in traditional French style. Eggs are soft and omelet rolled.
2) have always had good service. 
3) always clean. 
4) great coffee. 
5) eggs Benedict was perfect. Sign of a place that knows breakfast.  

Highly recommended.

This restaurant has been my best experience with Mediterranean food here in Indianapolis. Other places, Sam's Gyro in particular, have left me with terrible stomach aches and nauseous feelings after eating there. The Parthenon is under new management and my boyfriend and I frequent often. All of the staff know us by name and are very helpful, in fact, if they have something new or it is new to us they serve it to us on the house. I couldn't ask for better service at a restaurant! They have a rewards program through a mobile app called Spot On that allows you to earn a free entree. Every time we have visited, there are people dinning but it isn't over crowded and the musical ambience is always traditional, relaxing and never too loud. The only bad thing I have to say is, as of late, there have been some smells causing your clothes to smell like smoked meat when you leave. However, their incredible rice pudding will make up for that, IF they haven't sold out of the fresh, home-made batch already that day- because it is that good!!!
My husband just brought home half of his burrito for me to eat tonight. My first bite had a CHICKEN BONE in it! Glad I didn't eat that! Ended up throwing the rest away.

Yumm.  I was turned on to this place by my Sister.. So glad I went. I was greeted by the lovely owners which I loved. I was in a rush heading to the airport so I ordered to go. They got me n and out and brought the food to me as I waited outside. The place was packed with patrons! In a good way. I went for the chicken and OMG was it light, crisp and tasty. It was so good. The mac n cheese was good too but I cannot stop thinking about the chicken. So flavorful and soft n juicy on the inside.  I will be back for sure.  Love the fact that it's family run as well. So motivational.  Boom.

We went for the fondue experience.  When we walked in we stood around at the near empty restaurant and watched the staff look at us and keep doing whatever you do in an empty restaurant.  Finally being seated, we literally waited another 10 minutes before someone popped from around the corner to see if we wanted drinks.  Long story short, we had never been there for the fondue so we were hoping for an explanation as the menu is horrible.  It was like pulling teeth!  The server would stop by the table for one second, enough to ask and get a answer to one question then they would move on.  Like a said, it was empty so I'm not sure where they were going.  2 hours later we had a decent meal but highly overpriced.  Knowing the setup now I wouldn't mind trying it again but the service assured that I will not enter that restaurant again.  

Note to staff:  If you make eye contact, say HI.  Tell them you will be right with them.  WHAT A JOKE!

Not sure why all the hate for this Chili's!

Sometimes going to chain restaurants is a guilty pleasure I enjoy when I am traveling for work outside of LA. 

I usually get the Grilled Chicken Sandwich, no bacon. As usual, sat in the bar. I like how they have the thing in the bar where you can pay at the table. Sometimes the sever forgets about you because of this, but not here! Tye came by to make sure the food was good, brought some badly needed extra napkins before I could even ask, offered me my watermelon lemonade to go, and brought a printed check in case I didn't want to use the table thing.

All of the employees seemed friendly and this experience satisfied my Chili's craving!
