The food is seriously amazing.  Everything comes out seriously, piping hot! I couldn't decide what to get, so I made a split second decision and went for the Canelloni(sp?).  Oh. My. God. I honestly wanted to lick the plate. It was that good....everything about it is utter perfection: the portion size, the sauce, the cheese...oh so good!

As for the others: Diver Scallops - they looked SO good and I hear they were delicious! I'll be getting those next time!; Parpadella with lump crab meat - Looked amazing, and my friend, who is a bit of a foodie, said it was divine; Rigatoni with Sausage - my friend, Brian wanted to lick his plate, need I say more?!; Veal Medallions - I'm not into veal, but apparently it was seriously good stuff! 

I can't wait to go back!! It may be tiny, but it packs a serious punch! It's definitely in my top 2 Italian BYO's in the city!

We came across this place really hungry. After waiting for some time we noticed it was really hot, first downfall. Service was bad. The waiter only came to ask how we were while waiting on the bill. The girl who brought our food had a terrible attitude and when we asked for sauce she rolled her eyes and never brought it. Hot, terrible service and on top of that the food was bland.

The customer service was top notch. I think I have had better S. Indian cuisine but our party of 3 ordered chicken biryani, paneer tikka masala and the vegetable lunch (the one that comes with various mini small plates). For drinks the mango lassi was awesome. The chapathi was good but the other buttery bread they had way better with the sauces. Their paneer tikka masala was probably the best meal since it was very rich and the food was quite a lot. The biryani was good too and also spicy and did I mention top notch customer service? Will come again but I will try a different meal.

I have to update my review from several months ago.  

Just got back home and needed to write this review straight away.

The management of Good Earth need review the staff at this branch. The two staff on duty today January 28th at 2:30pm need training in people skills.  They need to learn to smile and engage customers no matter what their night before entailed.

I was served by a very tattooed young lady who appeared not interested to engage herself in my conversation.  Once my tea of Earl Grey Latte was ready I went to collect it at the end of the counter I ask the young man Jaimi where are the stirrers he did not answer just pointed in the direction of where they were.  You would never receive such service from Starbucks or Tim etc, or the branch of Good Earth downtown which I frequent regularly.

How do they know that I was not a safety inspector, a CEO or a Manager from one of their head office.  They should always serve a customer with this in mind as first impressions count.

If there was a selection for 0 stars I would have selected this for their lack of customer service which not only spoilt my visit but also my families.

Extremely disappointed.

Lionel Richie, Gloria Estefan, Kool and the Gang, you'll hear them all at CR Hero's. While the music is god awful, the food is not bad and reasonably priced. The kids menu is fairly large and includes shakes. This menu is not the healthiest but if you're in the mood for some junk food then this is your spot. The restaurant is well staffed and after 7:30 it is easy to get a table. Fried mozzarella app is really good.

Glad I found a good Ramen spot in Philly! Service was great, seating was great and so was the Ramen. I really hate comparing places, but I think this place should be giving Terrakawa a run for its money! Try out the house Ramen it's delicious but pass on the bubble tea. I will definitely be back

SUPERB experience there last night. It was crowded, but we were seated immediately and menus were delivered, drinks orders taken at once. Our waitress explained "how it works", then followed the plan to every detail. Food comes out as it "hits the window", sizzling hot, nicely seasoned and perfectly cooked. Great variety for all appetites. Our server was so attentive, we felt as if we were her only table. She even brought us a complimentary dessert (cinnamon ice cream with fried 
wontons dish), and I tipped 40%, which I rarely do. We'll be back. Only downer to me was acoustics of interior -- concrete floor, metal ceiling, you can hear every conversation in the room. Management, there are easy ways to deaden acoustics with ceiling-hung banners/upholstery, etc.
Food was flavorless, and my husband got the beef noodle bowl and got terrible food poisoning from this place, will never go back to this location ever again. Also service or lack of, was terrible.

If you visit Yards, you must do the tour. Our tour guide, Christian was wonderful. He kept our attention and kept us laughing the entire time. I highly recommend this tour. Remember make sure you get Christian as your guide

So, true to my word, I gave this place another try after they've been open for a few weeks. I am so glad that I did!

The falafel recipe seems to have changed a bit and my wife says that it's much better and is no longer dry. The tabouli had bulgur in it this time, and was just delicious. Seriously. I don't often like tabouli, and I ate the entire portion. It was just that fresh and wonderful. 

They had the shawarma this time, and it was amazing. Even my 13 month old approved (also worth noting, she had some of the rice and shoveled it all into her mouth, and then demanded more - 3 times!) The pita was so good!

All of the things that I liked before were still delicious - the rice, the hummus (which my kid also ate, by the spoonful!), the grape leaves, and of course that BAKLAVA.

The staff is still friendly and accommodating, the place is clean, and I will definitely be back.

Oh, also worth mentioning, I did try the french fries. Not something I would normally order from a Mediterranean place, but glad I tried them here. They are seasoned perfectly and I'm pretty sure they were hand-cut.

We are NOT from NY but from NJ & have been lucky enough to eat bagels in Manhatten many times. Clearwater Bagels is the closest thing you'll ever have to a REAL NYC bagel outside of the city. Yes, they're more expensive than Costco but they are real boiled bagels. The cream cheese is very good as is their coffee. Don't forget to try their rugelach....cinnamon is my favorite

As far as cupcakes go, Buttercream Cupcake Truck slams it out of the park.  Not too sweet, no overly complicated flavours, and just the right ratio of frosting and cake.  The chocolate peanut butter cupcake I had was perfectly chocolatey and moist, and the peanut butter frosting had a great deal of flavour without being overly dramatic.  Reese's peanut butter cup, anyone?  Yum.

Students around UCity get the first non-fancy cupcake for $1, which is a sweet (pardon the pun) deal.  Sadly I'm not a student in that area, but she cheerfully let me use my SJU ID for the deal and made a joke about supporting her fellow Jesuits.  Thanks!

Rumour has it that she's planning on opening a permanent location soon... cross your fingers, folks!

First Time Visitor based upon Nevada Magazine "Best of Nevada" recommendation.  Will have to be cautious of the magazines future recommendations.

Was not impressed and severely disappointed.
1 - Smoke filled the restaurant and didn't expect that
2 - Slow meal delivery and potato side was cold
3 - Ordered medium to have a sizzling hot plate delivered with the filet nearly well done
4 - Side salad probably had more dressing than lettuce

I normally don't write reviews and complain.  I just don't go again.  We did dine on Easter and it wasn't that crowded -- maybe that had something to do with the poor experience.
Horrible.  Took an an hour and a half to get my unseasoned luke warm food.  Management runs from issues.  Avoid at all cost.

A no frills pasta and pizza joint in Clayton for a quick and cheap lunch.  I don't gather that there is supposed to be an atmosphere - it's an in-and-out kind of place.

I've never ordered the pasta. The pizza is just ok - it'll suffice.

In all honesty, the only thing I regularly order is the side salad just for the creamy salad dressing - it is just THAT good. The best Italian salad dressing I have ever had. I also like the provel cheese and the croutons (as other reviews have spoken about).  What I don't like is the iceberg lettuce - it has no nutritional value when compared with greener lettuces. It's time for Pasta Plus to face the facts - we order salads for nutritional value - and make the switch.  Once I asked them to not use iceberg and sub in their greener lettuce (which I know they have for their other salads) and they up-charged me - that was disappointing. 

Have never experienced disappointing or unfriendly service. The place is usually buzzing with customers. It's really A-OK.

All and all, I will be back because I work in Clayton and there are limited lunch options for reasonable prices - we're kind of a captive audience.

Disclaimer:  The person writing this review is a huge fan of Korean food and Mexican food.  

All right, now that that's outta the way, I am ready to rave about the MaFooCo food truck.  It was so conveniently parked outside Borderlands Brewery last night for the brewery's grand opening.  Many people were drinking beer, but we were also hungry!  This is where MaFooCo comes in.  This steel food truck was like a beacon of deliciousness luring us in.  

The menu was simple, which was perfect:  Korean tacos, Kimchee quesadilla, and Korean burrito.  My fiance moved through the crowd inside the brewery to get to the food truck and came back bearing gifts.  We tried the tacos and the quesadilla first.  For those of you who have not had Korean food or don't know what kimchee is, this food is a wonderful gateway drug.  It gives you a sense of familiarity with the Mexican flair, but then it takes you on an adventure by adding some Korean seasonings and some chopped up kimchee.  It's an amazing combination.  

(Kimchee is a Korean staple at every meal.  It is fermented napa cabbage with Korean chili powder/flakes and minced garlic.  I love it.)

The tacos were so fresh, with a nice heaping pile of tender, cubed beef, some minced kimchee, and a little pile of chopped romaine on top with a mild sauce that reminded me of almost a sweet ginger soy sauce mixture.  Simple.  Elegant.  Delicious.  

The kimchee quesadilla was new terrain for me.  I had never eaten anything that combined cheese with kimchee; it sounded like blasphemy.  But it was very well made.  There wasn't an overwhelming amount of cheese like generic quesadillas are commonly guilty of (sorry to end a sentence with a preposition).  A bit of cheese, nice amount of beef, and once again, some chopped kimchee.  The ingredients were all the same, but the different permutations were unique and exciting.  

Lastly, before leaving the brewery, we went back for SECONDS.  This time, we ordered the tacos again and a burrito.  The burrito was a nice surprise, there was a different ingredient in there:  seasoned sticky rice.  For an Asian like me, the rice just elevated the burrito to soul food status.  I'm craving it right now as I'm writing this review.  

In conclusion, MaFooCo serves as a delicious reminder that it pays off to be adventurous with food.  You never know where you might find a great meal...for me, it was the MaFooCo food truck.

YUM! First time in philly and just stopped here for an early lunch. Had the falafel with harissa add fries and the Turkish coffee date shake. It was all fresh and delicious. Anytime I'm in town I will be stopping here.
Well it's 11:49pm on a Saturday. I went to Wendy's at 11:15 and they close at 1pm. The people ignored us and wouldn't tell us why they were closed .... got A&W instead... better choice.

I called to order a French toast bagel with honey pecan cream cheese. After picking it up ten minutes later, I realized they gave me an everything bagel and maybe honey pecan cc (couldn't exactly tell). Why didn't she tell me on the phone that they didn't have any French toast bagels left or when I picked it up that my bagel would be different?? It was my first time getting their bagels and besides them cheating their customers, the bagel was nothing special. Everything bagel was especially too salty. I threw it out after a few bites. Honey pecan cc with everything bagel?! Horrible mix.

Taqueria la Flama serves surprisingly excellent Mexican food.  From tortillas that are made fresh to order to the tasty salsa bar; they offer the best mexican food that I have had on this side of the border.  The food is great!  All their flavors are spot on with nicely seasoned meat, rice, and beans.  Their food is generously portioned, they dont skimp on the meat, and the food is priced right.  
When you walk in, the setting is misleading as it seems to be a counter service, which can be a turn off if there is a line, however once you order, food is served restaurant style with freshly cooked food delivered hot at your table.  While the interior lacks the tradional Mexican restaurant decor, the food makes up for it in authenticity. If you can't get to Mexico for some authentic Mexican food, don`t fret, give Taqueria la Flama a try for Mexican food as good, if not better than what's served over the border.

Been to Tokyo Sushi a few times now. Love the sunrise roll. Good service. Good food. Love the selection of app's, rolls and desserts. There is a great deal on beer and sake during the week. The only problem is the don't stay open very late so make sure you check the times.

Cool spot downtown, pastas were good & cooked properly (Cacio e Pepe was lovely). For drinks- the Old Fashioned was delicious. While some items were tasty, some weren't great. (Im finding a recurring theme with the M street restaurants). 

We were seated by the windows, which were gorgeous but my god, it was a cold night & it was so drafty. If you are like me, I have trouble enjoying my meal if I'm super cold. Bummer. 

Service was pretty good. Definitely give it a try if you are looking for a cool vibe. 

I'm feeling like this place is a solid 3.8 (but I'll round up).
Tasty croissants, low key and charming atmosphere! Downgrading a star because they messed up my sister's order. Otherwise delightful!

Being from Medford my entire life I have always loved otts! It has indeed changed over the years however the new outside addition is terrific, especially the fire pit! I must say the crowd that comes in now a days is definitely different but that hasn't stopped me from coming in. No the main reason I return to this bar is the staff! The bouncers, wait staff, and of course the bartenders! Everyone is so friendly and makes you feel at home. They actually strike up a conversation rather than just pour a drink and walk away. Personally I am not one to walk into a bar by myself however when I've had a long night at work I have no problem stopping by there. I love when my Asian persuasion (along with all the other wonderful bartenders) is behind the bar, I can always expect a relaxed, fun, and overall enjoyable night! I love this bar and all of its staff! And due to its reputation rising if you come here and it is busy be patient, because unless you've worked in this industry you have no idea what they go through!

Whenever my family is is St. Petersburg, they love eating here. The last time I was here was 13 years ago, but after this visit i can see why they keep coming back!! The food is delicious, the mariachi band was hilarious and great, the staff was friendly, and if you are not sure what to get, i reccomend the "Mexican combo" which has a bit or everything. Overall, not a bad experience.

Loved it here.  This was just the atmosphere and type of place we were looking for in NO.  Ordered Red Beans and Rice with sausage.  Super tasty - sausage was amazing.  Hubby ordered shrimp po boy and that was great too.  Definitely recommend this.

Not worth the hype. Came in here a couple weeks ago and the service is horrible ! They are under staffed , only one waitress running around the whole restaurant. We were there for half an hour and they didn't even take for our appetizers we had to ask the waitress place an order for them, after an hour we received our mussels and they were over cooked almost burnt around the edges. The sushi wasn't very good, not fresh at all. The salmon and hamachi had a funky old taste to it . Couldn't even finish it . Overall it wasn't a  great experience and my husband and I will not be coming back. Don't waste your time here

This is definately a treasure that could be missed if you blink. I found this on yelp under bakeries so I decided to try it out and OMG I am so glad I did. This is amazing little cafe on Drew St. I will even compare this so far to Frida's only on a smaller scale. The food is spot on perfect and tasty and huge for the price! The owner is sweet and the staff is very friendly. They are so accomdating to change up the sandwich if you have an allergy or special preference. I definately love the food and I am working my way through the menu. I am so glad that I tried it.
This was hands down the best nachos and burrito we ever had! We plan on going back for more while on vacation!

Worth the effort to find in the back of an industrial strip mall.  Excellent authentic Mexican taqueria, lots of variety.  Tongue (lengua), tinga (marinated pulled chicken), and al pastor (pork with pineapple) were my favorites.  Tacos very tasty.  Sopes a real treat.  Plentiful parking.  
Downsides were watery free magarita, and smelly accessible restroom; regular single restroom in the back was fine. 
Service is polite and attentive.  Very relaxed casual atmosphere where you can enjoy a good meal.

This bar is very nice and local.  My friend had invited me here because he lives nearby and I love local bars.  When we came in, there weren't that many people so we sat ourselves down and the bartender gave us our drinks and made a little chitchat.  We also became friends with the girl next to us.  The drinks are high quality for the price that they charge and the atmosphere is very serene.  Later that night more people came but it was never crowded or crazy.  Just people enjoying a nice weekend drinking and talking.

I would definitely go here again.

Well we had great hopes for meatball U and we were a little disappointed. 
After seeing a news report on them, we decided to take a 30 min drive and give them a try. 

We did buffalo chicken balls 
Mac n cheese with meatballs 
A pan of meatballs in marinara. 
And Caesar salad

The stars of wHat we had were the salad and the Mac n cheese. 
Salad was fresh and crisp with a good tangy dressing. 

Mac n cheese was excellent 

Chicken balls were mushy and soft terrible consistency for a meatball and the buffalo sauce was disappointing.  These should have been pan fried. Especially needed with chicken and turkey balls since the meets tends to have no body to it. 

The regular meatballs in marinara were ok. Have had better at most Italian places. 

If we were in West Chester, we may go back to try some other things but not worth the 30 min drive
The chicken in my opinion is gross but do not take my opinion unless you are a picky eater because I don't like certain kinds of chicken. But the fries are amazing.

The host was a little standoffish, but everyone else was really nice and accommodating. Our waiter was very personable; we loved him.

We were seated in the courtyard, which was mind-blowingly beautiful. Both my husband and I fell in love with the quaint atmosphere in there. Absolutely loved it. If we ever get a house in NOLA, we want a courtyard just like it.

The food? Meh. Very bland. We weren't impressed at all. Our best course was the appetizer: alligator sausage. It was flavorful, but both of our entrees were in dire need of seasoning. The food definitely wasn't worth the high prices. 

If we ever come back (which might be never, but still) I think we're just going to stay in the bar and maybe sneak out to the courtyard just to soak in its atmosphere.

This Taco Bell was quick, inexpensive, and fresh. The food was steaming hot when I received it! I truly love not interacting with the employees but still being able to sit and eat here. They have updated seating to where you can plug in a charger. Also I like that there are high chairs available (family friendly). In addition to all of that the food was good. My friend got a crunch wrap which had holes in (see pictures) but that was nothing to the service and quality.

Ordered dinner take out for the first time last night. A little pricey, but we were full and satisfied. We got the chicken lettuce wrap appetizer, brussel sprouts side dish and 6 maki rolls (Philadelphia, yellowtail scallion, spicy tuna, soft shell crab California, salmon avocado and tuna avocado). Everything was quite yummy! we noticed that the sushi rice was properly seasoned unlike many other sushi places in the area. The brussel sprouts were delicious, I will definitely order those again. The chicken lettuce wraps were okay, left something to be desired but tasted fresh and fairly healthy. We will return!

Best steakhouse in Nashville, hands down. If you're going to splurge this is definitely the place to do it. Such a fantastic view of the city, top notch staff from servers to management, and not to mention the most important thing, the food..absolutely phenomenal! I definitely would recommend the Wagyu steak, black truffle Mac & cheese, and to top it off the banana tarte tatin. Lastly, a shoutout to our server Godfrey. He was very knowledgeable with all the menu questions we asked, great personality, and took top notch care of us. Without doubt, I highly recommend asking for him when you go in. No ifs, ands, or buts about it, Bourbon Steak will become a regular go to. Thanks to all for an incredible night, and even better experience!

We go there for their $5 hot and ready pizza sometimes. Often we still need to wait for our pizzas! The employees are trying but they need to be trained to know the tricks to keep the pizzas stocked so people can just come and pick up and leave.
Great selection of meats, and the service was perfect. Asked us if we wanted more of any specific cut. The price is great too. Much better than Fogo.
Fresh, fresh fish and fast service! I highly recommend the Volcano Roll and Firecracker Roll if you are craving something spicy.

Sunday brunch. Wonderful service at the bar and great fun watching all the action in the kitchen. My wife and I had the clam chowder, half dozen Kumamoto oysters, and split the lobster tacos. Overall just a fantastic time. Highly recommend if you love shellfish.

I have had the pleasure of dining at Zahav multiple times over the last five years and every dish every time has been delicious, inventive and beautifully plated.  Everyone knows just how wonderful the food is so I am writing this review to give a shout out to the service - it is warm, knowledgeable and courteous; no request is too much (for instance, we found out yesterday that some friends would also be eating at Zahav tonite and the manager was kind enough to seat us together; at such a busy restaurant with a carefully orchestrated seating arrangement, it seemed like a nice gesture to me).  Additionally, while you have a primary server, you probably come into contact with an additional 5 or 6 other servers throughout the meal, who all help to make sure your needs are being met.  Combine the food experience with the attentive and considerate service (and the ridiculously low price point for the Tayim tasting menu) and Zahav is epic indeed.

Consistently good, if you're looking for Thai/Asian food in the area pick this place. Only complaint it sometimes on large orders they'll forget something but they always are happy to refund it and honestly the food is so damn good I keep coming back every week.

Came 30 min before restaurant opened... on a Wed night, and there was 15 people already waiting in line.  Recommend coming early like other yelpers advised

Quality of the sush and sashimi-- 4 stars.
 Price:  Overpriced for what you get!
Size of the sushi rolls:  are you kidding me?  i swear  some of the rolls were the  diameter size of Half Dollar Coin!  And they would be only 6 pieces...

Service : SLOW!

I used to live in San Francisco, and i think you get much better bang for your buck there..

but I guess it's Santa Barbara...

Service is really really slow  took for ever to get us seated the drinks took long to come out also conch was hard and rubbery had to send it back the bill was kind of high for what we ordered   the waitress super sweet .

Worst bar service ever tonight. Sat at a high top in bar for 20 minutes before being approached by bartender. When she did saunter over it was to tell me that I'd have to move because of COVID restrictions. Apparent my table was next to a couple diners. Meanwhile, complete strangers were walking in and sitting right next to each other at the bar.  I'm all for keeping everyone COVID safe. But I think I was asked to move to save the bartender from serving me at a table.

The fam and I came here on Fourth of July for lunch. Parking was super easy. There is a lot with a free 90 minute parking right when you enter the harbor. It's a small burger joint where you order inside and grab a picnic table outside. They bring your order to you.

As a vegetarian, I was highly impressed!! I had the black bean patty / burger which was so yummie. Cooked to perfection and topped with a delicious chipotle mayo. It's on the spicier side just FYI. The pickled onions were a nice touch! All of the burgers come with fries or homemade potato chips. Both were tasty! 

Even though that was one of the few if not only veg options on the menu, I'd definitely come back for it!! 

The only reason they get 4 stars is because I ordered a $5 fruit cup but they never brought it. I forgot with all the other food but still, they forgot too!! Also, I asked for no guacamole on my burger since it's listed as an ingredient and the man said they ran out so it wouldn't be an issue (I still mentioned I had an allergy just in case) - I thought he should have deducted $1 or so from the burger since most restos charge extra for it but they didn't. Also, most bizarre of all, they put guac on the burger!!!!! 

It's a great location though bc you can walk out to the beach within a few minutes. Burn off all those calories :)

Worst McDonalds I've ever been to. Don't have high expectations anyway...messy...water all over the ground... Employees don't seem to care. If I was the owner I'd want to know...if I knew, I'd be embarrassed. Yikes. On the bright side the air conditioning works & so does the Coke machine.

I can't say enough good things about the food here. The bibimbap in the hot pot is delicious, and I especially love the variety of bottomless side items that automatically come with all entrees. The wait staff are generally friendly and attentive. This is a regular place for my wife and I, so I hope it stays in business. It's definitely the best Korean food in town.

We selected Mambo's because we wanted to try some classic Cajun/Creole food- with a vegetarian. You do need to ask for the vegetarian menu (also gluten-free I think, but we didn't look at that menu), but this is one of the few places we were able to find that had anything vegetarian that was similar in flavor options to what the carnivores were eating. Most places just offer a Caesar salad. Our food was great. I had the red beans and rice with chicken, which had great flavor, two of our companions had the redfish and enjoyed it, and the vegetarian had Mambo's favorite and loved it. Was it the best food I have ever had? No. But it's good food, is right on Bourbon street, and the service was great. Shoutout to our server Joshua.

As to getting a table- we tried to reserve online and the only openings were for three hours in advance- but when we called the restaurant said they had available space right then. When we walked over we waited in the res line for 5-ish minutes and got in (Wednesday 5:30ish). From what we saw going down Bourbon street several times during our trip, most people wait in the line, and it didn't get much longer than 7ish parties anytime Weds or Thurs. However they did take down our phone number when we got in line, so there may have been parties out exploring Bourbon street who were in line.

The worst part of our visit? A boy playing plastic buckets was seated directly outside our open window, which made it hard to talk. But that's part of being on Bourbon Street.

In a nutshell: Great location, decent food, slow service.  It takes an extraordinary amount of time to get your food once ordered.  This location offers a strange menu mix between Italian and Sushi.  Outdoor seating is a nice alternative on a nice day, but it is noisy due to high traffic volume.  The food wasn't good enough to offset the time it takes to get your food.  The wait staff is friendly enough, but kitchen needs to pick up the pace.

I like this big restaurant that's just west of the border of UNR. Apparently lots of college folks flock here (which makes sense) since they have daily specials. I like the fun atmosphere with the random trinkets scattered along the walls. Service was great.

My friend and I enjoyed a couple cold brews and I had a burger. If you're looking for a unique bite, try their Jiffy Burger. Yes, there is peanut butter in it--not sure if it's Jiffy as implied in the name of the burger, but it's there. Now, just imagine: bread, beef, and peanut butter. It's actually not bad. I mean, it's worth trying but I'm not sure if I'd get it again. You might have one of those moments where you're just like, "ohhh, this is interesting," and then just finish it. The fries were typical--but the good typical.

I'd definitely come back again if friends wanted to! The parking lot could get tricky (could be more spacious) so beware if traveling in a caravan of sorts.
Wow, it was amazing authentic Mexican food. Chicken quesadilla was delicious. Their red and green sauce is so hot but worth it. The el pastor torta  was delicious!!

WARNING DANGEROUS HEALTH  CONCERN: I have been to La Indita a few times before but this was an absolutely awful experience. I ordered 2 chicken tacos on 9/29/17 around 6:15 pm and  a cheese enchilada and the 2 chicken Tacos had MULTIPLE (4) CHICKEN BONES  IN THE TACO. I almost choked and when I spit out the bone it was pointy and could have punctured an organ( eating chicken bones can cause bowel perforation)  if I would have swallowed it. I informed the waitress and she took the meal from me and brought me a new one ( after 20 min) and charged me for it anyway. I was totally disgusted  and didn't wanna finish it and ended up throwing it out. This is inhumane even to feed to a dog, why would you feed it to a human? This is a major health code violation and I will NOT BE RETURNING.

After waiting 2 hours for my delivery because I had to call and check on my order since the delivery time was 90 minutes!  After finally getting my order which I specifically ordered thin crust pizza and received thick crust cold pizza! Specifically requested honey barbecue wings and received hot spicy wings! Cold cheese sticks! The delivery driver said someone should have called to tell me they didn't sell any other wings besides spicy, well guess what I never received a call! Order #10231483

Very clean Wingstop in a bit of a tough neighborhood, but the employees are great! They're personable, friendly and willing to carry conversations. One is a bit slow taking orders, but I figured it was her first day. Like always, they make great wings!

Got the crab omelette with Swiss cheese/spinach. No flavor. EXTREMELY bland. $30 for decent coffee and very bland food for 2 :/ Great atmosphere, but that doesn't make it worth it. They will succeed via yuppy followers who need IG photos, but foodies... avoid.

The corn muffins were very dry and did not taste good. The shrimp was average, and it tasted like frozen shrimp from a bag. All the food in general served at our table seemed old and just heated up for us. However, the service was really great, and the waitress was nice. I will not be coming here again.

My sister-in-law bought some sourdough bread, which we've yet to try. I was going to buy some cookies, but one of the employees made it seem like it was so inconvenient for her to answer my *one* question that I decided to pass. Customer service counts, people - maybe trying too hard to emulate the French? Super cute place, though. Hopefully the sourdough is good. Three stars for quaint location and promising looking pastries. Still, I wouldn't go back. Hate being treated like a nuisance.

Oh I so wanted the food to be better but it was lousy! we got a pizza with sausage, mushroom and pineapple and it was barely mediocre! Also ordered a calzone. Both lacked flavor, the crust on the pizza seemed like it came from frozen, too thick and dense and while there was plenty of cheese it could not make up for the poor lack of flavor. The calzone was only cheeses but I swear they don't season it at all. The sauce tasted like it came from a jar. Im sad cuz I know it's a family business and I would like to support that but when I can get better from dominos well that's kinda pathetic.

They refused to fix our taco order, after charging us to have a topping added_ salsa. Then hung up on us, refusing a refund as well, telling us to buy more tacos. We were polite. And now late to work with no food, as we do not eat meat beyond fish. Zero stars, will not return.

My favorite spot ever.  I love the guava mojitos and the nachos.  I wouldnt recommend this place for a first date because it's noisy and superrr crowded. You could sit outside in the warm months and that would make this a perfect date place.  Either way, I am regular and i will continue to frequent El Vez

The dishes are OK and the waitress is nice. We are glad to see another Chinese restaurant opening in Indy.
We went there with a 10% coupon on a newspaper. But when we checked out, I forgot to show the coupon. Yes, that's all my fault. The waitress kindly helped ask if we can get the money back. Actually I did not expect to get the money back. But what surprised me is the excuse we got from the cashier--the coupon expired. We took a look at the newspaper, it's from 2 days ago, and there's no expire date on the coupon. So we got another explain from the cashier, "You should show the coupon before checking out next time!". Yes, she was right this time!  Probability not, I mean, shall we go there next time?
I had the red, white, and bleu burger. It was decent, but just tasted like a burger you'd grille at home. The atmosphere is unbeatable, just recommend something other than a burger! Ha

EGGCELENT!! Loved the ambiance and service. From the mimosa to the french toast and breakfast potatoes an easy 10/10!

I will be back for sure!

Absolutely love this vegan ice cream spot in Nash! One of the places I miss most since we moved away. It's the cutest spot near some great restaurants (including Avo which I also recommend), and I loved that during covid you could order & pick up these cubes on ice cream. Made me happy!

What a beautiful, open restaurant with great natural lighting! 

We started off with three appetizers that were all decent. The Boudin Egg Rolls were pretty disappointing though. I love boudin and these just did not do it for me. We also got the guacamole, which came with a tiny amount with a huge portion of chips. The fried green tomato was the best of the three!

For my entree, I got the chicken and biscuits! Huge portion, the sauce was delicious and the chicken was perfectly crispy! Definitely recommend this dish!

Went to Reno and stayed in western village inn in sparks all I got to say is we're coming back, clean comfortable beds clean rooms , Casino has really good service and Panchos restaurant is delicious!five stars.

I was there last night for "Monday Night Oyster Nite" - what a deal and so delicious! Flown in fresh from WA they serve them either grilled or raw, keep going back n forth about which I like better, and at a $1/oyster I can keep trying to decide and not break the wallet! Oh, and they have some wonderful new whites that really paired well with the oysters. This makes Mondays not such a hard day to face, knowing you can end it with such a treat!

Traveling for work with 2 dudes, I knew I had to feed them something good. When I told them we were going to a place for lunch that served sandwiches on paper plates, they were skeptical. But of course, I won them over. 

I ordered a roast beef with cheese and peppers, the other 2 ordered a philly cheese steak and a meatball sub. Let me start with the fact that the small sandwich is actually huge. Its a big-ol-sub! 

The meatball sub looked the best to me, and my coworker was very happy with his selection. There were 4 meatballs and they were very large! He said it had good flavor. My other coworker got the philly and he was concerned that since we were in DE, it would not be good. However, he was thrilled. 

My sandwich, however, was disappointing. It was overly salty, i don't know if it actually had cheese on it and they forgot the peppers. I eventually asked and was told to just take them out of the cold fridge that was in the lobby area. The peppers are worth the extra $1! 

The seating inside is limited, there are 3 tables with 4 chairs each. At lunch time, its hard to find an empty spot, which is a good sign. They have soda in bottles as well as a customized Coke machine (LOVE THOSE!!). lots of chips to choose from to go with your massive sub.

Overall, I would still send people here.
Omg they have the best Happy hour specials not to mention that Phils Pineapple Martini. Service is great must try the Broiled Stuff Crab Portabello very nice size for Bar appetizer special $5

One of my favorites! Love going when the cream of asparagus soup is the daily soup, nothing like it. Tastes soooo good! Parking can be very difficult as the lot is shared by several large restaurants so often times it's easier to valet.

This was our second time trying koto. The first time we ordered hibachi take out and this time we dined in. We reluctantly dined in after our take out experience. Both times I had to actually fry our leftover rice at home. First, the restaurant was extremely hot to the point we were sweating. We moved to the bar which was a little cooler than the booth. One plate came out well before the other, which was a cold plate of hibachi. The rice was far from "fried" even pouring yum yum sauce over it didn't help. The hibachi veggies were still raw. My shrimp was cooked but was still cold when I got it. The ginger salad was good. The service was slow but otherwise very nice as they seemed understaffed. We won't be back unless management or something changes.

What I like best about this restaurant was that the food was portioned so that you will have appetizer, main course, and desert without your stomach exploding. I had the pumpkin ravioli (because of all the good reviews on yelp) and it was nice with a slight sweetness. It had a bit too much olive oil in the dish for my preference but I can always get rid of it before eating it lol. 

Also, the place will have a long wait time because the place is so small and there are only 2 servers.
They already include 20% tip in the bill so you do not need to add it yourself.
Best Chinese around this area. Prices are low and the food is great. I've tried much of their menu and have never been disappointed!

I would not call Two Bits as much as  bar as an emporium of all that is good in life. Walking into this garage style emporium of all that is good, I immediately saw two grown men playing Jumbo Jenga- the classic sign of good times ahead. I think my head nearly exploded when I walked into this place. I've heard great things about Two bits... but really, you cannot capture how incredible this place is (well I will because Im THAT good).  Two Bits transported me back to a better time...a time when trouble shooting your video game meant blowing on the cartridge. It was like being a 10 year old kid again.. but better yet.. this ecstatic 10 year old kid could play Galaga while drinking a Tennessee Brew Works IPA-legally. Life don't get better then that folks. TKO. Foreal.

I think I almost died when I saw their console selection. Super Nintendo, N64, Xbox... blah blah the new ones that I could care less about. (I bet they even have that complete failure of a gaming system- Sega Dreamcast). Anyway, let me tell you about the games. They have your classics- Mario Bros, mario kart, smash brothers, andddd GOLDEN EYE. AND ITS FREE. I came with a few guy friends and they choose to play shuffle board.. but everyone in the fun emporium is super friendly so I had no problem scooting up to some strangers in a booth and starting up a game of Mario Kart with them. (Of note, Two Bits has an interesting mash up of characters. There is a mix of young professionals with your occasional college student types. But as any place that carries classic video game consoles... well, lets just say I had some run ins where you can imagine the scenario would be captured by NATURE or National Geographic... First Encounters of the Female Kind).  Anyway, back on track (if you are still reading)...

Games: Classic Arcade- Galaga, Pacman, Hunter 2, NFL Blitz, WHERE IS TEKKEN?!?!?!, A bunch of board games 

Games Needed: Skee ball, TEKKEN

Beer: Such a solid solid collection. All your classic TN brews: Yazoo, Mayday, calfkiller, TN brew works... Happy hour specials from 2-7 where you get $1 off drafts or get $3 Coors Banquet/Miller Light. I have to do a particular acknowledgment at how awesome their Bar team is. I met CAS tonight and he was so great. We talked quite a bit about the brew scene in Nashville and he was so helpful in regards to educating me more about brews.

Events: Tuesday night is BINGO. I cannot possibly be more excited about that (I am completely being honest). Wednesday night is trivia hosted by Nerdy Talk who I hear is a hilarious woman.  I thought that meant trivia was all nerd trivia-- its not..but if it were.. I would win. 


BEER CLUB--- This is a new program that they are rolling out at Two Bits. Essentially you get a passport of 39 beers (physical book where you get stamps). If you try all 39 (no more then 3 stamps per visit) you can attain ETERNAL GLORY on the Two bits wall with your name and a personalized Stein. I have always identified myself as a high achiever and ETERNAL GLORY is something I strive for.. so clearly you WILL see Chalupa Batman on that wall.

Overall, I will be back. As a regular.

My favorite Vietnamese restaurant in New Orleans so far.
Sure it doesn't have the hype of Lily's.
Sure it doesn't have the decor and ambiance of Magasin.
Not does it have the prime location of Pho Noi Viet 
But the food is excellent and the service is just as great.

What is good:
the menu is extensive. 
The menu is also color co-ordinated. So everything in red has meat, everything in green is vegetarian.
The portions are great. They have an option of smaller Pho sizes and Larger sizes.
They have a vast menu, more options than any other Vietnamese restaurant. 
If you like Meat, Onions and LOTS of flavor I highly recommend the number 38. 
Their steamed bun tacos are also exceptional.
I had the veggie pho and it was light and delicious. 
Next time I will get the number 38! The meat was flavorful and the rice was airy and fluffly. 
Our server was very attentive. She brought water for my dogs who hung out on the front patio and she always refilled our waters and iced-teas before our cups emptied.
The prices were fair. The decor was simple. The ambiance was chill.

We enjoyed lunch at kingfish. The steak salad is brilliant. The chicken sandwich is a bit much. The cocktails are well thought out and very well made. A good representation of old classics and interesting new ideas.

Ambiance: casual dining 

Food: 

Chicken spedini - 5 stars - so good! Perfectly seasoned and grilled chicken chunks on a skewer served with toast points with a garlic parmesan butter dip.

garlic chicken wings - 4.5 stars- not greasy and so well seasoned 

Pizza: trio pizza- 4.5 - Great crust and tasty toppings. The sauce was the star of the show, well seasoned, not too sour and good thickness.

Drinks- 

Grapefruit mule - 4 stars - light and refreshing

Red Hammer - 3.5 stars - good but could have used more horseradish and be spicier.

Everything was absolutely INCREDIBLE! The rolls melt in your mouth. We ordered 5 different dishes and they were all absolutely amazing! Zero complaints! My personal favorite was the stuffed pork. I highly recommend the turtle soup!

Well we should know by now that if you go to a place called Galley pizza you should probably eat pizza!  Kids got spaghetti and the sauce tasted pasty like flour was added for thickening!  The tea was bitter.  The garlic knots were out of this world which is why we decided we should of had pizza!
Oxtail was excellent , very rich. Enjoyed the Sorrel drink. Met the owner/chef and his son..very nice people. I recommend.  It's a BYOB, too btw.
A little stingy on what they will put in a growler, but nice selection of beers from all over.
If you're in the mood for a great burger, this is the spot! There won't be much else on the menu but what is offered is delicious.

We were looking for a good FroYo place after catching a movie at the Ritz and stumbled upon this joint courtesy of positive Yelp reviews. 

While their selection of flavors isn't huge, the ones they have hit most of the things you could be looking for, with the Nutella being my favorite. Unlike some places, they do offer you a little cup for free samples as soon as you walk in, which I really appreciate since I'd rather not drop $6+ on a cup of FroYo that I don't like.

As others noted, the topping selection is similar in that it's not the biggest spread you've ever seen, but it is definitely sufficiently varied and gives you plenty of options. I was surprised how good boba works with the FroYo -- give it a shot!

They have a ton of other menu items to choose from if you don't want soft serve (smoothies, waffles, creme brulee, etc.), so it's a good place to go with a group of people with different preferences.

Finally, the service was fantastic and both people working (assuming one was the owner) were extremely friendly and seemed to sincerely want to make your experience there a good one.

Will definitely be back any time I'm in the area and looking for a frozen treat!

What a revelation! This is the kind of Mexican food restaurant that could thrive in Mexico City. Everything from the Nachos to the Sopes to the Molcajetes was prepared with an almost artisinal flair. 

The sauce enrobing the enchiladas was sublime. The husk on the tamale was like your abuela made it for you at Christmas. The guacamole retained the nutty goodness of the avocados it was plucked from.  

The tortillas de maiz were so chewy and of such a consistency that they tasted nothing like the corn tortillas we are so accustomed to north of the border. They soaked up the various salsas (beware...there was one at the salsa bar that would make a vaquero cry) with a sponge-like quality that only added to the greatness that was our meal. 

They accomodate vegans well and the service was up to par for such a busy restaurant. 

This was one outstanding meal and I'll count the days until I can get back there for another run at the menu. 

If you're in SB and you want Mexican, GO HERE!!!
Decent local fare food and drinks. Good place for sports watching. Plenty of big screen TVs.

By far the best food in IV and the best of its kind in town. Way better than the beloved Zaytoon. The lamb platter is to die for, the vegetarian platter is to die for, the dips are amazing, the beer is abundant (20oz glasses) and cheap. I want to try all of it!!!!

I am ashamed I haven't thought of boudin egg rolls stuffed with cheese; it's a genius dish. 

I had the No Animals Were Harmed" sandwich. The herbed goat cheese spread brought it from boring to very good. 

The Delicate Lady was the best chicken salad my dining partner had ever had. A rave review by any account. 

I'll be back to pick up their house made guanciale-the only I've seen in the city. A must have ingredient for bucatini all'amatriciana.

Honestly, Ive really been consistently disappointed by the service here, which is unfortunate as there is no other place serving this particular kind of food. 
I have seen on multiple occasions staff dressed unprofessionally (baggy sweatpants, dirty -houseslippers-, etc.) and unhygenically.
Today I came in (admittedly close to closing but not by much) and they told me they arent serving food, just smoothies. Now, I understand being out of a few things, but from this interaction I am fairly sure the employees had already cleaned everything and just wanted to leave early. I get that, I've worked in the food service industry. But its still your job to serve food with a smile on your face, opening to close, regardless of how much you want to go home. And this is just the latest in a long string of negative experiences with this restaurant. I truly hope the manager can step up and motivate their employees to do the same, because it'd be a shame for this unique menu to go out of business.

We put our name on the list for a 20 minute wait, sat at the bar for a drink and was never acknowledged.  There was no bartender at the bar the entire time we were seated and when employees went behind the bar noone even looked our way.

Good dinner, great flavors, reasonable
Price, sidewalk tables. My waiter allowed me to substitute fish for the pork and shrimp, no upchrahe.

We decided to try EatNic because it was advertised as farm to fork and we like to support local businesses. The menu was small but had a good variety.  I tried the grass fed burger and for the $17 price, and I expected a premium burger.  What I got was a dried out, tasteless burger on a slightly toasted (and yes dry) roll with only lettuce as a fixing (no tomato or onion?).  
I could only eat half of it as i needed to drink water with each bite to wash it down.  I expected a tasty, juicy burger for the price and the menu description of grass fed beef.  the others were satisfied with their meals (scallops, duck).  I do like that it is BYOB.  However, I do not plan to be back.

4 stars becuz of the patio sitting with the fire place, the live steel drum entertainment, drinks & happy hour prices 4-6p!  
also note that they take expired coupons (at least thats what i was told buy the last manager that approved ours over a year ago).  dont b afraid to ask!
Service was slow and the food was cold each time we were there.  So many better places near by to dine.

TOURIST TRAP!!!  The most watered down drinks I've ever seen!  Go to Joe's across the street if you want a real drink for the same price. Food was ok but nothing to write home about.  The kitchen got my order wrong or it may have been the bartender I'm not sure. It took 20 minutes for them to bring it back and it wasn't even busy. Plastic forks and cups and paper towels for napkins. The worst thing of all is the smell!!!  If you sit at the bar be prepared for overwhelming stench of stale alcohol and bleach.  On the upside there are at least 40 televisions and the staff are very friendly and willing to change the TV to the games you want. Frank the bartender was very friendly and helpful as were the rest of the staff.  Frank even took 50% off of my burger since it was so late.

Let's start with low quality chicken burrito and then  charge $3 bucks for sour cream on it?!?!?!?!

Skip this place at all "costs" ...  Let them close and a new restaurant.

The diversity of cuisine in Indianapolis never ceases to amaze me.  Just when I think it couldn't possibly get better, it does.  I was intrigued when I heard of Che Chori Foods' opening.  Having never traveled to Argentina, my understanding of their foods was nascent: succulent, perfectly cooked steaks were the first items to come to mind.

I'm a sucker for small, family-owned eateries - which is exactly what Che Chori is.  The restaurant's space is mostly kitchen, and if you want to dine-in, you'll be dining out - outside, that is.  While some picnic tables are available, Che Chori is mostly serves takeout, delivery, and drive-through (yes, they have one of those) diners. Service is relatively fast, considering the food is freshley prepared. I've found ordering online a swift process.

The beauty of the Che Chori's fare is in its diversity.  The owners, one originally from Argentina, and the other hailing from Central Indiana, create a paradigm fusion cuisine. The diner will choose between delectable Argentinian "street food" items - as well as American favorites with an Argentine twist.

Che Chori's menu is large, as are the meals. There's nothing I hate more than going to a restaurant and getting a thimble-sized portion; I want to eat a grotesque amount of food, and I want cuts of meat large enough to send frightened vegans back to their soy farms. That's what I get at Che Chori.  Our plant-based friends can relax, as there are plenty of options for them, too.

Start any meal at Che Chori with an empanada or two.  I've had the beef and chorizo options - the latter being the more magical experience. If you like sandwiches with a healthy portion of meat, try the bondipan or the "El Vacio." The bondipan is a large portion of Argentine-spiced pork and two fried eggs served on a baguette.  Eating it can be chaotic, so be sure to have napkins - and perhaps a knife and fork - on hand. Try it with the chimichurri picante.  The "El Vacio" is a delicious flank steak sandwich, and it is topped with chimichurri.  It is served with a mess of fries.  Delicious.

Che Chori Foods is a peach of a place. It deserves awards, and it has my highest recommendation.

Large serving portion and eggs were very good. Even my picky boyfriend liked the wheat pancakes. Wheat toast was dense, but not in a bad way. Also good coffee and atmosphere. Would certainly go back but it does get crowded, so might not be fastest place if you need a quick meal.

I've been coming to this mission since it's been open, including durning covid this year. The staff has gotten progressively worse and in the past few months it's so bad we don't even want to dine there anymore. Try any other mission or Mexican restaurant for that matter. Somewhere they actually appreciate your business and support.

This is an excellent coffee spot -- the coffee is the best that I've had in St Petersburg (in the same quality level of, say, Panther in Miami, and at a different level from the local brand, Kahwe, and from Starbucks); owners/staff are professional and personal; the physical spot is "minimalist" - plenty of room, simple tables (some 2 tops, one common), counter/stools along the street-facing window, 20- and 30-something clientele, often busy with a buzz, usually good music - good place to sit, drink coffee and talk or write (or whatever) - only negative is eats, very narrow, sometimes only (designer) doughnuts, or (very good) highbrow gluten-free this-or-that.
old go to spot!! live this place!! sangria is amazing, guac is ridiculous, and the food is soooo goood!!!

From the outside it looks like a office building. I tried to enter in the front. But the entrance is on the side. Strange, but I'll go with it. Once you enter the restaurant you're greeted by the hostess who was extremely pleasant. This establishment is bright, cheerful, and clean! The food is DELICIOUS. I went there based off of they're reviews and I wasn't disappointed. Try something new and enjoy the experience.
This is our favorite pizza hands down!!  Fresh ingredients crispy crust. Cooked perfectly every time.   The Tuscan  Salad  is delicious. Great selection of beers and service is awesome.

Happy Grover treated us like royalty .... The food explodes with flavor from all angles in your mouth . The food hits on all senses , the presentation is sizzling , the aroma perks up your pallett and then as the food enters your mouth it explodes with flavor...
Had the hot garlic naan , tikka chicken , Malala or something like that all made it an incredible dining experience thought I was in New Delhi somewhere but then I walked out the door and realized it's just limerick.... I challenge you to come taste the flavors of of the house of India.

Hours on Thursday 10/5/2017 12-6pm, 12:15-12:33 no show! 

Note: I checked social media before venturing out! No update on change of hours provided.

My review is as empty as that open spot on 38th Street between Walnut and Sampson! 

On to the next open establishment!  (ICI Macarons 230 Arch Street, Philadelphia PA 19106)
Came here based on yelp reviews. I did not really like it neither did my husband. We went on a weekend, place was not very clean and we thought food was less than mediocre. Will not go back.

Joe and I had been wanting to try this place out since moving to Meridian. We finally hit it in time for happy hour! Joe and I appreciate a nice, descent size happy hour menu with some variety since we tend to go during these times of the day to save some cash money! :) With plenty of flatbread, oils to dip, beer and yummy cocktails to try we had a great experience. The atmosphere was awesome and you kinda wanna just hang out. Our table was tucked a little in the back but the employees were attentive. The manager even stopped by and asked if we'd been in before. He informed us a little about the restaurant  and their popular lunch special they have. The flavors and the deals are bringing us back for sure.
     P.S.
       I cant  wait for it to warm up so I can sit out on their super cute patio. I love me some outdoor seating!

Ok so i need to do this before i actually forget her name...i think it was Bea or Beee or along those lines...anyways so yeah i made a huge mess and there was an employee who contributed her efforts to make things right again. No joke tho i made a legitimate mess, like if my mother was there she would have totally grabbed a broom and whooped my ass but thanks Bee for helping me make it right

Had a very mediocre experience here recently.  Most surprisingly, my steak (their specialty) was not cooked properly.  Initial attempt at medium rare was so clearly rare-center was red and cold.  Manager even exclaimed that is clearly rare.  Next version was well past medium.  Disappointing to be sure.  Partners dinner was ununspiring at best.  Unlikely to return here.

Horrible service. Customers order on iPads, which does not have an intuitive interface, takes way too long, and cannot accommodate special requests or questions. The servers won't pay attention to you unless you select that you need their assistance on the iPad. Even then, they will not come over. There's no reason to tip 20% since the servers don't interact with consumers at all.
it was great except everything was  clean  they were kind but they gave me the wrong beans :/

Delivery was quick especially for a Saturday night. Their pizza crust and cheese is amazing!! The garlic knots and what I call the real deal marinara sauce will definitely have me come back for more!!

I love your pizza! 

Is there a chance you guys will ever be available on DoorDash???

Had the burger times two. They got to the table warm. Fries were the same and just ok. I had he orange blossom beer and it tasted flat - missing a crisp finish. 
All in all not bad - good pleasant server but slow to bring food and a little disjointed it seemed.

First off, the building is incredible. Like, just stunningly beautiful. The architecture is totally lost on most coming through. There's an enormous vault inside, too. Bathrooms are always clean!  It's a great place to study, read, or people watch. 

I've never eaten there but I've always gotten a coffee and lemonade. Can't explain why but I can't refuse a lemonade. The coffee is always perfect.

The upstairs is warm so be wary if you're staying a while. It can also be hard to find a plug for your laptop.

Fun place near the convention center! Food and service were excellent. The greens, baked beans and Mac and Cheese were great sides. I enjoyed the fried pickle spears and fried okra too. 
The chicken was crisp and juicy and had a good crunch. The chicken is spicy but flavorful. 
There is a unique root beer float made with Not Your Father's RootBeer. Makes a cooling drink after your chicken dinner!

This restaurant is a gem tucked away with so many Southern staples. It's not really a 5 star but deserves more than a 4-star. The chef is from Alabama and adds greens to most dishes and pulls it off! The pork shoulder is the best dish and I've been dreaming of it since. That says a lot for a girl who does not often eat meat. We went with friends and also tasted the Drum (on special), the shrimp, and the country steak. The champagne and fries were a nice way to start the meal! The fried were fried to perfection and the contrast made me laugh but was oh-so-yummy. This was well worth the visit!

Some obvious inexperiences when it comes to a Sunday brunch. Kitchen apparently was backed up and didn't tell the people up front. And after waiting 45 minutes (exercising patients after being told 20-30minutes) I was told "I don't know how long your wait will be.". I'll stick to the meridian street location.
Stayed for a business trip and really enjoyed the resort.  Definitely need to come back with my family.  Good mix of adult only and family friendly amenities.  Certainly a relaxing atmosphere.

I have never written a bad review before, but I would stay away from this Dickey's location. I had ordered lunch for myself and my partner and when i got back to the office, realized both of my orders had been messed up. I called back to see what they could do since I was unable to make it back during my lunch hour. The answer I received from Steve, supposedly the boss at the time, was ridiculous. Without even so much as an apology, he instructed me to disassemble my sandwiches and rearrange my meats to get it close to what I ordered. He also said I could bring back the sandwiches at a later date so they could remake them. I paid for this and not to have someone tell me how to rectify their mistake! I also would most likely return knowing mistakes are made, but the way that Steve handled the situation was very unprofessional and has caused lost business! I will not return and it looked like others had the same thought as there was no one even in the store!!
Love the space! Love the drink menus, fries, service! Go! Stay! Great lighting, acoustics, and overall ambience!

Not only is the atmosphere kickass, the beer selection is KILLER! Literally, they have the widest selection of specialty beers I've seen in Indiana. They've got loads of craft beers from Hoosier breweries, favorites from across America, and plenty from all over the globe. You'll always find something new and exciting. 

The atmosphere is cozy and intriguing and you'll find yourself checking out all the neat nick-knacks, prints, and taps whether you're on the first or second floor. It's warm and kitschy, and you won't want to leave. 

The service s always stellar and they are super accommodating. I have a mother who is a very picky vegan and even though there was nothing on the menu that was vegan (save the salad) our waiter offered to come up with a pasta that would be vegan and went down to the kitchen and made it himself! He used oil instead of butter, wheat pasta, fresh veggies, clean, un-meatified cooking utensils and everything. He went above and beyond. It was amazing. I wish I could remember his name. 

So basically, Shallos is amazing. Whether you're coming for drinks or diner (or both) you won't be disappointed.

Excellent customer service. Everyone is extremely friendly and are always willing to help. Every time we come we usually wait about 30-40 minutes ( we come on a Saturday) but the wait is so worth it. 

They are known for their 1 pound homemade Burger, AKA Terminator. 

I personally get their turkey dinner, slices of Turkey covered with turkey gravy, homemade mashed potatoes, veggie and cranberry sauce. Hits the spot! 

This place is inside Western Village, and the ambient is very casual/ Romantic!

Everything was great (atmosphere, food, service). One of the best cheese plates ive ever had was here. A little pricey but all the food was superb. Staff was very attentive and treated us very well. The reason im giving 4 stars instead of 5 is if you are seated outdoors near the washington square park you have a chance to encounter roaches near the sewer cover on the sidewalk. I probably had to kick 2 or 3 roaches away from my girlfriend just to get some peace and these are the roaches that are domesticated and are not afraid of people unless you physically kick them. The table next to us was also disturbed by them as well.

A nice little cafe tucked away from the bustlin' of the CWE, housed next to a greenhouse...rustic touches abound (old books serve as checkfolds), and homegrown to boot!

After a bit of boutique dabblin' in the Central West End we found ourselves famished. With a few quick blips on the Yelp app...we found ourselves trekking over to Olive Street...to find the lucky little lunch stash AKA Osage Cafe. 

My lunch: 
*A fresh, flavorful (yet simple) micro greens salad with ranch dressing. 
*A piping hot cup of the (organic!) bison stew with a dollop of creme fraiche. YUM. 
*Gardener's plate: Cheese, bread, fantastic fruit (fresh! not hard!), asparagus, and bison sausage (again, this is what they are sort of known for...This was probably more of a plate to share, but I found it to be a very filling and somewhat healthy lunch option.

I do have to agree with other reviewesr...the service is a bit slow, and the lunch is definitely done at a more leisurely pace. Our server was very nice, but it did take some time. 

A really wonderful lunch spot...I was quite happy to have stumbled upon it, and enjoyed it immensely. Everything tasted very fresh, and a nice pop on over to the nursery while waiting for a cab made for a nice end to our meal.

*closed between 2pm-5pm.

Looking for something a bit off the beaten path? Stop in!
Painfully mediocre. They ran out of syrup and eggs. Dry pancakes are weird. The setting is very white. Over not the worst for a new spot

I like TF in general and may have given a 4 star review in the past, however the last 2 visits have been disappointing. I'm not too eager to return to this particular location again anytime soon. The past 2 times I've gone, they took forever to make the order. Much longer than they said it would be when I placed my order on the phone. Last time I had a to go order and asked for an extra side of chips. Guess what happened when I got home and opened my bag?! No extra chips :(  

Today I ordered a burrito power lite with no jalapeños. Again it took forever to be ready. This time there were indeed jalapeños all up in my food and the burrito was wet and soggy (no, I did not order any sauce on top). It really had very little appeal due to being soggy.

Boo, what a let down. This TF location needs to step their game up a notch
I guess I never have to go back to Burger King again. The crispy chicken was as hard as a rock and impossible to eat.  It was awful!

This place just opened a few weeks ago in Fishers. We've gone there every weekend since! The place looks nice, the wait staff are all great, the menu has a lot of different variety and options, and the food is  delicious. I can personally vouch for the strawberry pancakes and the heuvos rancheros with green chili!  In full disclosure I always get their breakfasts, so I have not tried their lunch options yet.

Long wait and mediocre food. I would not come back here. I got fries and a grilled cheese. I didnt know it was possible to have bad fries but they have them here. Go somewhere else for late night food.

Golfed here today because it claims it's on the water and it was only $15 at a certain time for some reason. 

My friend and I go to tee off and we don't hit them too good. We hit about two balls each and then the man working behind the desk of the pro shop comes out and asked what our handicaps were. We've both have played golf before and have even held memberships at a golf course before but we tell him we're not sure. He starts telling us that the black tees we hit from are challenging and based on what he saw he recommends we hit from the white tees.

 I found that very rude and embarrassing considering there were other golfers around and that this man also watched us from inside the pro shop and left the pro shop just to tell us that. Based off that comment alone he lost two customers. We say yeah ok and don't let it bother us. We saw maybe 2 black tee boxes that would've been challenging. I ended hitting several drives close to 300 yards as well. 

I felt like I was playing Plinko on the Price is Right every time I went to put because there were holes in every single green. You got it straight, and it ends up going left and right and left and right. Maintenance is normal on a course, but every place I have played at has discounted their rates and even put a notice on their website when they do so. Cove cay did nothing. It can't be said that our tee time was $15 do to this. Even if it was, it was the only $15 tee time (every other one was $30), and they didn't say anything on their site. 

Will I come back? No. Why? Because I did not like the comment that was made to my friend and I about how the pro shop employee was watching us and based of that he recommends we hit the closer tee box.

I realized recently that my husband and I eat out at Mexican restaurants an average of 2-3 times a week. So I think I can safely say that we are big fans of this style of food. He loves everything spicy, and I'm into rice and guacamole. Qdoba is definitely at the top of our Mexican "quick service restaurant" list.

When I describe Qdoba to people who have never been there, I say it's like a Subway (sandwich shop), but with burritos. Choose your meal from the menu, and it is assembled in front of you from ingredients set into the counter. By using this method, everything is also completely customizable - choose your favorite type of salsa, ask them to leave off the cheese, or have them add peppers and onions.

The employees are generally quick and courteous, and do a good job of preparing your food correctly. There has been more than one occasion where my burrito was "overstuffed," and rather than serve me a tortilla literally bursting with beans and rice, they either double-wrapped it or "transplanted" the filling into a new tortilla.

The menu offers a variety of tacos, burritos, nachos, and salads, as well as tortilla soup. Everything can be ordered "naked," meaning you get just the filling in a bowl, either without a tortilla or with the tortilla on the side, and this has become my preferred burrito style because you can make sure all the ingredients are mixed together, and it's a little neater to eat with a fork than to bite into a burrito the size of an infant. Though the flavors are pretty standard for Mexican food, they also have some interesting options, like poblano pesto.

Compared to a fast food place like Taco Bell, their dishes are on the pricey side. But I think the high quality of their food and large portions makes it worth the cost. They pride themselves on the freshness of their ingredients - for example, they used to have signs out with a photo of an avocado, saying that this was what your guacamole looked like this morning. The bins of ingredients at the counter are constantly being replenished, and at this location, you can watch other employees in the kitchen grilling meats or roasting vegetables. Even your tortilla is freshly steamed when you order.

A few ingredients I recommend you definitely try: the cilantro lime rice (which comes in almost every meal), the queso (a spicy cheese sauce), and the corn salsa (deliciously seasoned).

Fantastic burgers, decent beer selection, inventive dishes. Everything is just top notch. I've ordered a couple burgers, and they were exceptional. However, I would ask that you not overlook the wings. The sriracha wings were life changing. I can't have buffalo anymore. I get mad that everyone isn't doing sriracha. The duck wings are also delicious. I can't recommend this place enough and can't wait to go back. Oh, one more thing- try the sweet potato fries!

Mother of god! If you are looking to strain at 45 degrees on the toilet for 25 minutes and then throw up, this is the place for you.  And I only had the bruschetta. The wait staff are friendly but that's it. The appetizer immediately gave my wife and I such bad heart burn and indigestion we didn't even order a main meal. Not to mention it was drenched in oil and still tasted extremely bland. I'm talking the plate had so much oil on it  that the BP oil spill in the gulf was put to shame. Now being a resident of palm harbor I had read the reviews of this restaurant and never eaten there, however the parking lot has been extremely full these past few weeks so I incorrectly assumed that his place had changed. What a fool I was to believe that theory of mine. Not sure where those people are, that those cars belong too, maybe they are owned by former customers who have died on site and are buried out back?, because that place had about 5 people in there and no one was looking like they had just eaten a meal worthy of this place's prices. Next the wine. We happened to hit happy hour....not so much. Prices for wine that was obviously repoured into the carafe numerous times from different bottles.   Anyway if you want to try it. Go for it. But you have been warned.  And stay close to a bathroom.

Drove by yesterday and stopped by today.  Was in the mood for something light. They did not disappoint! 
Very impressive display for the flaming cheese! 
The soup was filling and hearty and a huge portion. The seasoning combo of flavors was lovely! 
The hummus plate with the dill Greek yogurt was delicious! 
What a great local gem.
Will definitely return!

Hangry Hikers  Tucson!

One of the best things about hiking the Arizona Trail is learning about all of the best places to eat at across the state from local, fellow hikers who are glad to suggest places they would take their out of town guests to.  

The Sausage Deli in Tucson was a fantastic suggestion off Grant on the way over to the Catalina Highway!

We got the Legendary Bismarck and the Breathtaking Omar with a Meatball Sub to-go as well.  Even Wilbur the Wildcat recommends this place.  Then on the way home we stopped into eegee's for the flavor of the month Watermelon!

The food was pretty good and the service wasn't bad ether but the server over charged our card over 50 dollars and neither the sever nor manager notified us when it happened, instead I had to find out from the bank. Then when I called and spoke to the manager, Frank, he repeatedly denied the charges before he even went to his office to check; even though my bank already verified it was an extra charge from the restaurant. This manager was wildly inappropriate and unprofessional and clearly is incapable of delivering acceptable customer service. Don't go here, especially if this manager Frank actually does run it. How do you argue with a customer after clearly making a mistake on their card charge? When I told him what the bank said he replied with 'that's bullsh*t' Not even an apology or even any assistance in getting my money back. This man is pathetic and doesn't deserve a job whatsoever nevertheless a management position.

Best place to catch a big sports game in the Belleville area (huge Blues crowd for the game I caught there last week). Affordable drinks and menu. Pizza is delicious. The chef's three meat chili is the best chili I've ever had! 

There are several cool things there as well. There was a  live band on the stage in the back room (the acoustics were AMAZING!). You couldn't hear the band at all in the front, main room. That worked out because they have a jute box there that you can use a smart phone ap to play discounted music. Oh, and the draft beer tapers are frozen solid, resulting in the coldest beer ever.

I noticed the opening kinks their first week (end of Feb '12 i believe), but they've all been ironed out since. The food is delicious for the price, and the service is fun friendly and smooth.

Solid New York style pizza in Midtown. Probably 90% of the pizza here is sold by the slice, but if you want a whole pie, be prepared to wait at least 15 minutes.

The cashier didn't tell us until after we had already paid that they were out of jalapeños - would have been nice to know ahead of time so we could have ordered something different.

We tried "The Kitty" aka Hot Chicken Pizza(!!!) and were super disappointed. If you've read my previous reviews, you know I'm a huge fan of hot chicken and Hattie B's in particular. Cue freak out when I saw that Two Boots offered a pizza with Hattie B's chicken on top. Sounds like heaven, right? I was so let down! I was expecting crispy and spicy bits of hot chicken covering my pizza - not the bland, dry chunks of chicken tenders I received. Seriously, the chicken just tasted kind of old and had absolutely no heat whatsoever. Tastes nothing like hot chicken. I'm also just realizing that the menu says that this pizza is served with a side of pickles, but there were none to be found.

We also tried "The Clyde" - spinach and artichoke dip pizza. The crust was crisp covered with a generous amount of creamy artichoke dip. I'd definitely get this again! 

As I mentioned earlier, they didn't tell us ahead of time that they were out of the jalapeños that usually come on both the pizzas we ordered. The Clyde, while already very tasty, would definitely have been improved by the inclusion of jalapeños. I'm not sure they could have helped the hot chicken pizza, though.

I plan to return to Two Boots and try out some of their other pizzas. The crust and cheese were both delicious, but the toppings we tried left something to be desired.

Had the stuffed fish which is basically a fried fish rolled up with veggies and a cream sauce. It was delicious. And ordered the black beans and yellow rice. Also good, but was even better as cold leftovers.

I really love this place. I've been here twice and go for the sweet stuff, so I can only attest that the french toast and pumpkin waffle are fantastic, but my sister loved her wild mushroom black truffle cheese scramble. And my friend said the biscuits and gravy were very good, for those who like that kind of thing.

Two issues: The service isn't great, as others have said. Also- I basically go to brunch for the mimosas, and was really excited that theirs claim to be "fresh squeezed." But... they are so not! I know freshly squeezed oranges from store-bought concentrate, and this was definitely the latter. Very sad. (Somehow I managed to drink it all, anyway... there's still champagne in there!)

This place is tucked away in Metairie not in a touristy area at all. Local shops and other restaurants near by. 

Parking: 
The parking is Horrible, it's a small parking lot directly in front the building but with the amount of traffic this restaurant receives it stays packed.
