The other nearby restaurants have signage of restrictions to park in front of their building. As their parking is for their customers only and enforced towing of vehicles. 

Greeting/host: 
Not much of a host stand. I believe the staff takes turns greeting guest. We made reservations and upon entering the owner was at the front. He greeted us and we informed of a reservation but he simply pointed to a table where we can sit. That was very odd to not be brought to our table of a fine dining restaurant. But once our waiter actually came he was very nice (Jordan) and recommended different entrees and drinks. 

Food: 
Corn and crab bisque- it was good however the crab wasn't very present as the corn took over in taste. The flavoring of the soup was perfect just not much lump crab meat. 

Salad-I was expecting the salad to be a little more appealing than it was. It was simply a bed of lettuce with a sliced tomato on the side. The dressing was already on the salad with an overly generous amount. 

Lamp chops- this meal was cooked to perfection. The flavoring and the pairing of the potatoes made this meal even better. 

Stuffed chicken breast- this is more like chicken roll up's. The meal consist 5 breaded and stuffed chicken roll ups with heavy Marsala sauce and plenty of mushrooms. The stuffing didn't do the overall taste any justice in my opinion. 

Dessert: 
We order the chocolate layered cake. I love chocolate so this was perfect for my sweet tooth. However, If you dont care for death by chocolate this is not the dessert for you. 

The owner greeting: 
I thought it was pretty cool that the owner went around the restaurant and greeting his guest. He didn't do the standard greeting like most restaurant owners/managers. He held a short conversation, he made it authentic and it didn't seem like he was simply checking a box on his to-do list. 

Overall: 
I would visit this restaurant again but I would try a different entree. The service was impeccable and the owner was authentic and appreciative.
One of the dirtiest places I've ever set foot in. The girl at the counter is horrible to deal with. Sorry to bother you , but I'd like to order. Not too friendly. It's a no for me to go here again

Seated immediately and the place was pretty full for lunch. This place has decent local craft beer selection but its similar to just about all places that say they are craft beer bars...(Two Hearted, Sunking Cream Ale, yada yada) I got a chicken sandwich with guac. Which was pretty good but not $11 good. They have some burgers or you can make your own also. Waitress didn't know a lick about beer and was unsure about things on the menu, messed up some orders, had to ask multiple times for things etc. Dropped glasses and dishes happened multiple times while we were there. This place is new and really just needs to get it together. Food is good and what you expect but I would hold off going here for a few months until they find a solid staff and tweak the menu a little. Has good potential!

Breakfast buffet was a bit disappointing. Mom said eggs were gross and didn't eat them. Fruit was super fresh. Bacon was ok. No service pretty much. Potatoes had no flavor. Go somewhere else for your breakfast instead.

They didn't know what they were doing. The cashier wouldn't allow me to switch breads for my grilled cheese when I work at a panel at another location and know for a fact that they are able to. Moreover, he selected for me not to have a side when I specifically asked for a baguette.

Had a fantastic breakfast here! Everyone was super friendly. I ordered the special which consisted of country fried steak, incredibly sausage gravy, two eggs, I had mine sunny side up. The eggs were cooked perfectly. On the side came a green salad with a delicious, citrusy vinaigrette. Also ordered a side of hash browns and biscuits and gravy. This was hands down one of the better breakfasts I've had in some time! The coffee is great too!

For our first delivery in Indy, we decided to go all in and order Indian food. Haveli's serving size was quite generous for the price and both meat-eater and vegetarian agreed that it was some of the better Indian food we'd had.

Delivery was quick but at some point I'd like to get the full experience and eat in the downtown location. Yum!

I forgot to check in when i came...but regardless this was a nice experience. Quite pricy, but it's a fancy place. We ordered four dishes, rather small(that's the point of the place...order multiple small dishes so you can try more). Everyone really took care of us! The desert was truly the best i have ever had!! it was a chocolate ball filled with ice cream, neatly placed on top of a cookie, and hot caramel was used to melt the chocolate...seriously to die for.

We moved back to the Southwest from Seattle and one of the things I looked forward to was the nice chain restaurants that weren't readily available up there.  How sad to see Macaroni Griil has gone WAY downhill.  Calamari was cold with zero taste the other appetizers were equally dull or over cooked.  We didn't even order dinner.  Being understaffed on a Friday night may have contributed, but sadly I think the attention to details had left this establishment.

Can never go wrong here! The best Italian I've had south of Boston's North End. Clean and simple decor! Great service! Huge portions! The flavors are over the top!!!
Boom!!!

Fast and friendly service, which I like. The sandwiches are big but a bit pricey. They were out of roast beef - not good - so I had the capastrami. It was good, but more bread than meat. If you are stuck on Greg street in Sparks, this is a good option.

We had a great experience at Condado. When the server found out it was our first time, he took the time to explain their novel ordering system and was on the ball with drinks and taking our order. 

The food is pretty amazing. It's a lot of fun to choose exactly how you want your tacos prepared and the portions are definitely ample for the price. Three adults ate for $50... and that includes a beer!!!

I highly recommend this location. Sitting by the open windows next to the sidewalk in bustling Broad Ripple while you munch some tasty tacos is a great way to spend an evening!
Ok they win I'm so done with this place! I have had some many problems here it's almost comical. Food is usually good but they can't get an order correct for some reason!
I wouldn't even give this place one star. Let's just say it's disgusting, egg rolls soggy and food was just bad overall, will Never order from them again.

I am ashamed of myself for taking so long to review. 

I eat here any chance I can get or at least as much as I can without feeling guilty. Anytime I have guest in town...chimmies is where we go.

The Margaritas are by far the best I've had in the lou. I've visited nearly every Mexican food join in the stl city limits and many out of that and I've yet to have a better Margarita at a better price. The only Margaritas that can match are easily double the price and a quarter of the size. Yes, I love my Margaritas. 

The food is great! Always consistent and always delicious. Chips always fresh although the salsa could have more of a kick or a spicier option. 

My favorites are the enchiladas, the chimichangas and any sizzling platter. The deserts are delicious but far beyond my expectations these days is the service. Everyone is friendly, attentive and even better remember your face and orders when you come back in. Granted I do visit often :-|

This place is obviously a local favorite as its always busy. That doesn't stop the staff from making good food and offering great service. 

When my hunger for mexican food falls on a Monday, I wonder out and am always dissapointed. Thank you chimmies!

Attended a wedding reception here over the weekend and it was absolutely wonderful.  There were about 40 of us in attendance and we started in the back patio area.  It was very well shaded and they had a bartender outside serving up drinks as well as having a cheese, meat, and veggie platter to snack on and also some roasted mushrooms.  This was the day after valentine's day and the owner brought out some baked oysters that they had from the night before which were absolutely out of this world.  I hate oysters and tried one which also had chorizo, cheese, and spinach.  Now I may never eat another again because it was so delicious.  

Dinner was served inside shortly after and what a meal it was.  A stuffed caprese chicken breast with a balsamic sauce on top, spinach pecan salad, an assortment of roasted vegetables, and fresh baked bread.  The staff continually kept drinks filled all night and cleaned our plates up promptly so everyone still had plenty of room for the champagne toast and cake when it cut and passed around.  

The service was top notch, the food was incredibly delicious, and the venue was small but quaint.  Located as part of the Tucson Museum of Art, this may be a small little place but big on ambiance and customer service.

Only thing I can't comment on is the pricing of food as it was a catered event but from what I experienced and ate, I would easily have paid $30 a plate not including drinks.
Great little sandwich and breakfast spot with tasty pastries. Service was very friendly. Even our kids ate more than usual.

Me & my friend made a last minute decision to eat here after Southern Women's Show...avoiding rush hour traffic.  It was well worth it!  My food was cooked to perfection & my waitress was awesome.  She was so good at explaining things from the menu & accommodating with our request.  I can't wait to go back!

I was quite unpleasantly surprised by Sabrina's Cafe, based if their ratings.  First, I want to give them credit for their cubed home fries with cheese.  It's nice and crispy in the outside (my favorite!) and warm and fluffy in the inside.  The chicken noodle soup was ok, not too much flavor.  

The also had lavender lemonade, which I don't recommend if you love lavender.  I couldn't taste the lavender.  

The pancakes were ok.. Pretty forgettable.  The challah bread French toast was pretty good.  I appreciate how it's not too dense.  I do recommend the French toast.

The service was on the terrible side (by Molly).  Waters were not refilled.  Finished plates were not cleared for incoming plates.  She didn't ask how everything was.  All this one did was bumble around like a bee except not busily.  

I suspect this place has such high ratings because everything else around is pretty much university dining hall food.  I most likely will not be returning, but I don't necessarily regret trying it.  Green Eggs is the way to go.

Food = 3 
Service = 2

The best thai food I ever ate. I love the pho brisket soup. The best soup highly recommended. My next favorite is the red currie with chicken. And the dessert mango sticky rice. I have been eating here for years and it's still my favorite place. The owner is wonderful. She is always at her restaurant going to the tables with her beautiful smile making sure her customers are happy. And we are very happy!  I just love the service and the food. 5 star very much deserved

Free Coffee Day Review

I visited this Wawa for the first time today for Free Coffee Day around 7:30am. When walking in, I was impressed with how clean the location was. I immediately went to the coffee area, where people were waiting for fresh coffee to be made. I'm not sure how long they were waiting; however, fresh coffee was being put out when I was there. The vanilla coffee was already available, so I got that. When getting cream, the creamer area was very clean. The location was not busy except for about 10 people who were getting coffee. There was no line at the register. Also, everyone working was very friendly! I didn't buy anything or look at any other products, but I would definitely go back!

Absolutely amazing! Gorgeous atmosphere, delicious food, and wonderful service! Large patio with great views of Germantown. 

Lots of candlelight and flowers/plants. Multiple seating and lounge areas, also has a waiting area surrounding the bar.

This is THE place to go for happy hour in the area. They have multiple food specials for $5-$7 and drink specials that are super cheap. I'm a wine drinker so I cannot comment on their beer list, but it seems extensive. You can also sit anywhere in the restaurant for Happy hour with is a huge plus for me.

We live here. We called all day after 11:30 am NEVer answered phone . We left our neighborhood at little after 5 pm got down to parking lot across the street from Nash House about 5:20. Walk across the street after paying for parking $10 and restaurant was little quiet but tables had people .... hostess says do you have a reservation?! I said we called ALL DAY and y'all never answered the phone !? So we came early - she's said we're booked full sorry ...I said you are not allowing 6 people early on Saturday to eat and leave which is all we wanted !!! NOPE. I will never recommend anyone will never eat there again will never say anything other than BETTER PLACES TO EAT IN NASHVILLE. Too Bad ... I'd give ZERO STARS FOR THE F*CKS THEY GAVE ABOUT OUR BUSINESS :(

Public greens amazing as ever.  I've had a long love affair with Public Greens, part of the Patachou empire they're just an amazing organization.

They've really stepped up when it comes to dining in a 2021 circumstances.  They offer heated outdoor dining either next to the outdoor firepit or if you get lucky you can snag one of their private indoor greenhouses.  They use a 3 step cleaning process un between each sitting so I feel super safe.  Each greenhouse is also outfitted with a space heater and twinkly lights perfect for a romantic lunch or dinner.

They're takeout options are also wonderful as all of their to go containers are 100% compostable.   

They offer a wide variety of food including sustainably sourced meats - local produce - and great vegan / veg options.  Not to mention Circle Kombucha on tap,  a variety of local spirits, and a full coffee bar.

It's quaintly placed right on the monon so perfect for taking in the local atmosphere.   Public Greens makes my heart (& tummy) very happy.

@twainindy

This place was very interesting.  By the name we didn't know what we were walking into.  But it is a pizza a beer place. 
We had a brown and a biere de garde.  They were pretty good.  The menus are in books which is pretty cool.  It was pretty busy when we were there.  
The bartender was very nice.
We had the Rueben flatbread which was awesome!  Def will be back for the food.
Cheers!

Enjoyed a great meal last night after attending an event. We ordered the Dan Dan Noodles, Sesame Noodles, Spicy Cucumbers, and the Garlic Tofu. I enjoyed the Dan Dan Noodles so much that I got them for take out. I highly recommend this place not only for their food but for their exceptional hospitality.
Really great spot.   Interesting food, great drinks.   The special appetizer was so good we tried to order more for dessert!   Ambiance is fun and relaxed.  Will definitely go back

I would have given this place 5-Stars except the seafood platter wasn't as full as other NOLA seafood eateries in the area of the comparable price of 25$ the Beignets where WONDERFUL! I had the powdered sugar on the side so I could lightly dust them myself! The CHARGRILLED OYSTERS were amazing! The butter has white wine in it and so it's such a delicately balanced flavor over other chargrilled oysters that I've had at more famous oyster houses. All in all, this little spot is very good! I'd suggest them over The more famous restaurants anyway! If I lived in NOLA this would be my go to spot for chargrilled oysters!

This place is one of my new favorite spots ! ESP for brunch anywhere they have bottomless bloody Mary's has my heart and they are good! The place is small put has such an old but fancy charm to it . The menu is full of the city's classics such as shrimp and grits , eggs Benedict with a Nola flare  , and chicken and waffles

I'm a big fan of Calvin Fletcher's because I'm a big fan of pretty coffee drinks! Also, the environment is very welcoming and conversational. However, this past time I was a little disappointed with my order. While my coffee was great, I ordered a egg white sausage sandwich without cheese since I am lactose-intolerant. Unfortunately they forgot to take the cheese off making the sandwich inedible for me. They did apologize but I would've perhaps liked a refund or compensation of a different item. Yet the people who work there and the friendly faces will make me continue to come back when I visit! Everyone has their off days!

Probably the best customer service around! The owner makes you feel very welcome and is so sweet to everyone. The food here is always delicious and tastes super fresh. The homemade sauces that are brought to the table are amazing! I love them on the potato chips that come with the sandwiches. I highly recommend the pesto sandwich, but everything I have tried so far has been great!

They use cheap pork hot dogs which are absolutely revolting.  If the menu had SAID pork hot dogs, we would have ordered something else.  My daughter and I threw them out.  My husband enjoyed his cheese steak... that item was 4 stars.

Started with the boudin balls appetizer and - wow - really tasty!!  Had gumbo, jambalaya, and the Amberjack Special.  My business partner has been here 3 days in a row - lol.  This place is outside of the mainstream area, but it is as authentic as you can get!!   Don't pass this place up --- sooooooo good.
I only ordered tamales, and they were a little dry and dense. I will give them another shot to try other items to update my review.

Ah-mazing!! Simply the best homemade crepes and French Toast to die for! Friendly and knowledgeable staff, who keep a very chill vibe. There's no rushing you out as soon as your food comes, but they don't lack in quick response to your needs either. Hands down best breakfast in a long time. Plus, added bonus- mimosas and bloody Mary's!! Need I say more? Check it!! You won't be disappointed.
Food is good better than the other Thai place in Browns burg. Try the curry it is very good!!

Wowwwww, really good place. Great service, the owner of the place really helpful. The food really good. Nice concept and great design. 
Definitely we  will back.

Took the boy there for a calzone. Two personal calzones and a soda about $35. They charge $3 per topping, but they were so skimpy with the toppings. My son's was $16, it was suppose to have sausage and pepperoni, maybe 5 pepperoni and sparse sausage. Would have been great at $10-12 felt cheated when we saw the bill. The food is good  just not for what they charge.

This was by far the best service I have received...ever. The staff, food, and presentation was impeccable. I had the ribs and they were delicious. The hubs had the pork chop and he loved it. I can not wait to come back to Truffles. The wine list is expansive. We got to hear the live band since we were there on a Saturday evening. I could not have asked for a better location for  birthday dinner.

This is the best bakery and breakfast place in Franklin. Finally a place where they serve excellent espresso! The croissants are like they should be - fluffy like in Paris! The bread here is really good, the best I had so far in TN. The cakes look amazing. Glad we found this place!
Nothing to write home about! Visiting from Atlanta. I really didn't like this meal. I had fried oysters & fries. I expected more since the photos were nice.

My wife and I were in the mood for BBQ yesterday, so we ordered from Sweet Lucy's (takeout).  I thought the food was great and appropriately priced.  I had the ribs/pulled pork with corn bread, mac n cheese, mashed potatoes and cole slaw.  The meat was unbelievable and the sides were top notch.  I even heated up my wife's leftovers later on and it was still good.

The food here is bomb.com! My favorite restaurant to xo.e to. I always order the yellow curry with fried rice 1 or 2 stars its spicy.  The staff is always kind and I've never had a bad experience with the food or the staff! I would definitely recommend anybody to try this place!.
Beautiful atmosphere with amazing food and lovely customer service. Also very close to some cute shops! Lots of options for any diet type.

This was a great dining experience: really delicious food in a beautiful setting with 'easy' service. We had four in our party and all got the tasting menu. Two were pescatarian and two ate meat. To me, when you can be creative and cook vegetables well, you win in my book. The first course of snacks was amazing. Carrot tartare with an egg yolk? Yes, please. My favorite course was the course out at the grill: grilled mushrooms/chicken thighs, whipped goat cheese, pear mustard, and grilled sourdough flatbread. Unfortunately we were all so stuffed that we couldn't eat as much of this course as we wanted. If I could change anything about this dining experience, I would not have added the scallop course. It was delicious, don't get me wrong. But it added another course of food that we didn't need. I also didn't really love the roasted/charred beet course. If we could have eaten the first 'snacks' course, the out-by-the-grill course, and dessert, this would have been 100% perfect. As it was, it was a solid 95%. Two of us also got the wine pairing. I highly recommend. It was not too much wine but the wines were all delicious, unique, and paired perfectly. The sommelier was helpful, professional, and friendly. Our server was absolutely amazing: she was there when we needed her but she didn't hover. She was friendly, professional, enthusiastic, and knew the menu so well.

My second visit to Philadelphia and my second visit to Parc. This is the perfect lunch place, and a very popular one. Luckily my friends had made a reservation and we only had to wait a couple of minutes until we got our table for three, close to the window. 

Our waiter, Adam, was very lovable and helpful. He allowed us time to explore the menu and helped us find the best combination for us. We landed on Oysters for starter and he made sure we got the sorts we preferred. I had white wine along with it, a type that would also go well with the moules frites I chose for main course. 

The oysters were fresh and delicious. I prefer them with lemon only or with a good vinegar sauce, and the one provided at Parc were delicious. The moules were served in a white wine sauce with exquisite flavours and with thin, crispy fries and majo. 

Being a large restaurant with many tables, Parc provides a hectic atmosphere and much activity from people arriving and leaving. The restaurant is for all kind of people and our fellow guests were ranging from babies to couples in their 80's. All were heartly welcomed and all seemed to enjoy themselves. So did we, and I am certain I will be back the next time I'm in Philadelphia.

Just had another great meal at The Drunken Fish! We got right in even though the place was packed, and our server Kendra was awesome at giving recommendations and keeping us hydrated! This is one of my favorite sushi places in St. Louis, and it's our go-to Valentine's dinner date. Highly recommend!

I first walked in and noticed the decor, very quaint and accepting, and the only reason why I am giving this place a two star instead of one.

The food was cold, plain, and over priced. I ordered the nachos and added beef for $4, and there was barely any. I also had the Fried Mac n cheese bites, cold and plain.

They also do not have condiments laying out, so you need to wait in a 20 minute line for a pack of ketchup.

Basically just sampled the menu from this place a few hours ago, which isn't that difficult to do as the menu is simple and straight forward.

I recently became vegan since falling in love with my wife in september. Since then I have lost 3 belt loops in my waist without really excercising at all. There's my two cents about being vegan. Moving on...

The menu features a black bean burger and a chickpea burger. I asked the girl at the counter what her favorite was and she replied with the latter. My wife and I decided to get both and halve them. She added a small spicy salad to hers while I opted for the energy soup.

The food came out quickly and it looked so fresh. Both burgers were good. But one was AMAZING! The chickpea burger, the flavors and texture of that thing was incredible!! On top of that they have delicious gluten free buns, I could not believe how good it tasted.

The sides were strong and complimented the burgers very nicely.

My dad ordered a salad that had the vegan tuna salad - which tasted remarkably close to the real thing - next time I will have to try it on a piece of bread.

At the end of the meal we grabbed a couple of the cookies which were a lovely finish to the whole experience.

The dining is cozy and would be a great place to bring a girl for a 3rd date without breaking the bank.

You get a burger and a salad for 9 bucks! Wha whaaa

Definitely feeling the LUHV!!!

MANY THANKS!

This is and will be main Raman spot in STL!  The food is so good and fresh!  I wish I could make the broth at home but I can't :-(. The portions are huge and the staff is so friendly. I have also had several friends get the lunch box and you get a ton of food as well!  The location is great and the food was worth coming back time and time again!!! If you want something fun get the pork belly Raman and you will not be disappointed!!!

Just amazing for brunch. 

Shrimp po boy -- winner 
Carnitas -- winner 
Lemon ricotta pancakes -- winner 

Even the coffee was amazing.

ba ba ba banging sandwiches. we were in the neighborhood and i remembered hearing the name from a guy at work, so we pulled in. i got the fat daddy and my fiancee got the viablo. $16 w/ 2 sodas...i wouldve paid 20+!

I have been walking past this place for the last 2 years almost everyday and always wondered. Funny thing, I didn't even know it was a restaurant for the longest time, anyhoo, that was my laziness.

So me and my friend decided to get thai takeout, and we almost ordered from Erawaan, and then I decided to check out the reviews of this place and went with it. SO HAPPY i did. The prices were way cheaper, will not lie, always helps. Placed my order through the phone and the person who took the order was super patient and helpful [ I happen to be a mad indecisive soul...] 

We got the 

Steamed Shrimp and corn dumplings
Seafood Pad Thai
Create your own Salmon dish with vegetables in Penang Curry  Sauce.

Amazing! I won't lie, I loved the Pad Thai, only problem was, where it looses a star, was the seafood was not the freshest of all, the scallop was a bit questionable, but nothing major. I would still go there in a heartbeat and order the same thing! Steamed dumplings came in a bundle of 5 and were creamy from the corn and had a great spicy kick to it! Dear god the Salmon was DELICIOUS! I thought they would be small pieces, turns out they give u a huge piece from the best part of the salmon, with beans, peppers, carrots and pineapple in the creamy rich sauce. Wish I could lick the plate. If you are sharing food, this salmon could easily be split in two. 

Point is, I would order from here in a anytime and food was plate-licking worthy! The salmon was $14.95, who could beat that? For Vegetarians, they have this thing called Mock duck and many other alternatives and will modify any entree for you too. They definitely put a smile on our face by the time we were done :]

I'd give them 0 stars if I could. Anyone who thinks it's okay to have a sign by their register that says, "This is America, please speak English" on it, does not deserve to have a restaurant. If I had seen this before paying, I would've just left and walked across the street to Pat's. What about customers from across the world who cannot speak English? It baffles me that this place still exists and has a long line around the building.

It's a joke cause their cheese steaks aren't even good. Meat is dry and they give you a lot less meat in general. If you ask for onions, they'll probably forget since they forgot for me. Maybe my English wasn't good enough, not sure. All I know is that this place has garbage cheesesteaks and a garbage attitude. 

Pat's all day, everyday (way better meat and a lot of it!! All without racism too!)

Buffet food was ok. At the end of the buffet they automatically charged a 20% gratuity for a party of 2 adults and 2 kids. Despite our objecting the server was adamant that this is standard practice. Then he said this was because it is holiday week and the staff rely heavily on tips to get their money.

Have never known this to be the case for lunch buffet wherever we have eaten. Our objections fell on deaf ears and what should have been a pleasant lunch experience left a bad taste in the mouth. 
The owners should take note and either pay their staff enough so that they do not resort to forcing a 20% gratuity on patrons coming in for a lunch buffet. 

I have no objections to tipping but do not like the way they are implementing it at this restaurant.

All and all not a bad place.  Didn't get to try the pizza during this order, but might have to come back and test it out.  Ordered a sampler platter and buffalo chicken salads.  The salad was very run of the mill with a couple of pieces of buffalo chicken, an inberg/romain combo, croutons and parm cheese.  Nothing too exciting.

As for the sampler platter this was a kick of fried food.  Prob one of the best varieities I've ever seen on a menu.  For seven bucks and change this sampler included, 2 chick finegers, 2 mozz sticks, 2 fried eggplant, 2 broccoli bites, 2 stuffed mushrooms and maybe one other thing.  My order came with 2 honey mustards which was great but should have opt for one and one marina.   Descent place for apps, not so great on the salad front.

Came here for pliney the younger which was handled well however the pours were small. They have a great beer selection on draft and bottles and I had quite a few while I was here. I also had a brisket sandwich which was really good. The service we had was very good and the waitress was very friendly.
Very clean.  Nice waitress. Good food!  I can't believe after all these years, I finally came here last Thursday.  Their garlic noodles was so good.

We tried an order from Big Roman's tonight. A two star may be generous. We ordered the Meatball Knots. It's a good size order for the price. Not awful, but the accompanying marinara was weak. Smoked wings, garlic Parmesan flavor, were a disappointment. They are smoked and then fried. Whoever fried them must have fallen asleep. They were so dried out that they became sawdust with each bite. (Also didn't receive an extra sauce we paid for). Where was the garlic Parmesan flavor? Not on these wings! The biggest disaster was the Sausage and Fries. It sounded SO good but the same person was on the fryer. So over done that they were bitter. After reading some of the good reviews, I was surprised. I never give up on a place after one order. I'll try again. Hope I'm not being a glutton for punishment.

We were at Barnes Jewish for the birth of our 3rd child, and I needed something besides cafeteria food. So I checked Yelp and found Oasis. Solid, solid Mediterranean food. I tried two things, because it all looked so good. Falafel Plate and Deluxe Gyro plate.

The gyro was top notch. I will definitely get it again. I also liked the falafel wrap, but the taste of the falafel was a little lost in the rest of the wrap goodies, but the falafel and hummus in the wrap were great. So next time, I'll probably just get a side of falafel with hummus, and call it a day.

Will definitely be back!

Well.  So far: cute ambiance.   Plus one Star . Bad attitude twice so far from waitress from California (just bc you are from a place doesn't give you the right to ignore a straw request-had to ask twice for straws and then be told after the 2nd time that she only gives them when asked.  Had to ask for water twice - minus 2 stars . Food- ...all our omelette were excellent.   Grits ok.  Potatoes ok.  Biscuits ok.   Three stars for the omelettes.

Gnocchi is an obsession of mine, so a random Internet search of "Philadelphia Gnocchi" yielded this restaurant, not surprisingly, as its top hit.  The week day two for $25.00 special described elsewhere (salad, pasta dish, and Tiramisu for two) is a great deal.  The food was great, with the gnocchi being light and fluffy and the sauces (we tried three different dishes) quite superb.  We arrived right before the dinner rush hour (I was visiting from Baltimore), so we had the place all to ourselves. The service was very nice, and I would definitely return.
Food is fair but both times i was there and they were out of many items. They claim to have famous biscuits but were out of butter. How can u be out of butter!!
They take doordash orders, in person orders and phone orders, with one cashier, if you want food from here be ready to wait 30-45 mins.

I traveled to TN to attend a course, and my instructor recommended this spot for all us out-of-towners. I love spicy food and wasn't familiar with hot chicken, so a group of us decided to go Saturday night for dinner.

As other reviewers pointed out, there was a line out the door, even at 7:30. It took us about 15-20 minutes to get food ordered, but it is definitely worth it. I ordered a LG white, which is 2 breast/wing quarters (with the intention of having leftovers), with one medium spice and one "shut the cluck up," the spiciest. I underestimated how spicy this stuff is! Even the medium has a decent kick, which I personally feel was the perfect amount of heat.  After a few bites of the hottest level, my eyes watered up, my throat burned, and I joked that I would have to finish it later when not in public. The heat is no joke, coming from someone who   cooks with ghost chili pepper flakes at home.  When I ate the leftovers later with honey mustard, I found that the mustard helped cut the spiciness quite a bit. The chicken was perfectly cooked, crispy with lots of flavor on the outside and juicy on the inside. It comes served on slices of white bread, which I didn't plan on eating at first, but they accompany it so well and soak up flavor from the chicken.

For sides, I chose the pimiento mac and cheese and collard greens. For $1 more, I added an extra side of mac and cheese to take with. I thought both were delicious, and although the flavors were a bit mellow, they complimented the spiciness of the chicken well. 

I had to save room for the peach cobbler, which was a perfect way to end the meal after burning my tongue on chicken! The serving size is generous. 

There's beer on tap, and I saw that they serve a boozy arnold palmer, which I will definitely try if we make it back.  I wasn't familiar with the beers here, and the gal at the counter was super sweet helping me decide.  I was going to just trust her recommendation, but she even poured me a generous sample to make sure I liked it. Overall it's an awesome little joint, and although I can't compare to other hot chicken in the area (yet), I'm happy that we were pointed in this direction.

Absolutely loved this place. Decorated so nice inside and perfect for brunch. I split the Hickory Town and the Beet Cured Salmon with my friend and both were equally amazing in their own way. The Salmon sandwich was beautifully presented and very tasty. The Hickory was very hearty and more like your typical breakfast sandwich with a unique take. Also had the Bloody Mary, couldn't taste any vodka in that though. I would definitely recommend!

Best tacos around! 

My friend and his family own this place so i'm a little biased but you can't get tacos like this anywhere close! Yes sometimes they are super slammed and it's hard to get a table or have FULL attention of your server but that's a busy restaurant for you. Everything always comes out fast and fresh, never any problems. 
Bring ya family here for a nice meal and good atmosphere !

For some unknown reason I hadn't been back here for many years but tonight's meal was excellent and service outstanding. I had the Mongolian combo plate, mother had the sweet and sour pork combo plate. The egg drop and hot and sour soup was very good. The egg rolls extremely good. We'll be back.

Jabari made our experience both  memorable and fun! 
He introduced himself, greeted us warmly, made excellent menu suggestions of his favourite pairings. Laughed and smiled with us and was extremely accommodating. 
We come to NOLA every year and always stop at Le Bayou...this was by far the best experience.  

Thank you so very much Jabari for taking pride and being the best at what you do. You're an Ambassador, and one kick ass  human being!!

My boyfriend and I have become regulars & we are always pleased with the fantastic service and amazing food! It's our usual go-to & sometimes the wait is long but it's always worth the wait! Kay and Emilee are two fantastic servers!

This is a very popular spot after a football game on a Sunday. We got there early enough to be seated right away. A nice high booth in a secluded corner near the bar and the restrooms. The atmosphere was very cool and inviting. The service was good and quick even though it was a busy Sunday afternoon. I took the servers recommendation after explaining what type of beer I wanted (and it had to be local). I got the Mill Creek Lil' Darlin' which is a very light wheat ale with citrus undertones. It totally hit the spot for me.

We started with the Trio and a small iron skillet of queso. It was all very good. Especially the hot queso. We ordered 3 tacos each. It's a very similar concept to bartaco. The tacos are small but full of ingredients. I got the Bistec, Hongos, and Baja Shrimp tacos. The Baja Shrimp was the best of the 3. I really liked the flavors in that one. The other 2 were not that special. The bistec was kind of dry, and the hongos (mushrooms) needed more seasoning. I probably should have chosen the short rib taco that everyone raves about. I think my husband had mixed feelings on some of his tacos too. 

All in all, it was a very good visit. I feel that the tacos at bartaco have better flavor (with the exception of the Baja Shrimp taco). But, I do like that Bakersfield gives you way better chips to dip into the quac and salsa. I love the concept, and I'd go back again to try other menu items. It was an enjoyable and relaxing visit.

for Midway Games only

decades later and this place looks almost the same as when I visited as a kid.  Some big differences:
Fascination is gone. 
They added a ticket-redemption area since there are lots of games that give out tickets.

Games have not changed, prizes are a little newer.  Shrek and Despicable Me were some that I recognized, that's how "current" they are.

Some games are still 5 for $1 but many are $1 to $2.  $1 for the "Horse Racing" games where you roll a ball into the hole to advance your number.

The center circus performance area still doesn't have a viewing area so people just crowd around the side watching, that can be a major pain.

I have to update because they catered our wedding and it was SPECTACULAR! They are the reason our wedding ran so smoothly and wonderfully and magically. I can't say enough about the Duos truck and the lovely folks who run it.

What a refreshing oasis after walking this hot, dusty, (sorry, I'm from back East: we're not in Boston anymore, Toto, WHEW!)  artsy little district and draining your brain at the mind-boggling selection of used clothes at Junkee Clothing Exchange (right next door to UnCork'd). 

We stopped in at around 4pm on a weekday, so our experience won't be relevant to most people's visits, given that we were the only two people in the place.

But having said that, we found the service to be wonderful,helpful, and attentive. We found the interior bright and colorful, the walls covered with brilliantly colored neon art. 

The waitress told me they'd only been opened 3 months. I hope they're doing well and manage to survive, because I thought it was a gem. 

They have a simple menu with a tasting approach to cheese and meats, which I love from a low-carbohydrate/diabetic standpoint. i.e.: $3.99 to choose 1-3 selections of meat and/or cheese. I chose the brie, the fresh mozzarella, and the chorizo, the last of which arrived having been grilled, so it was hot and had a nice crunchy browning. Delicious. 

We also got a plate of smoked salmon, olives, and more cheese: roquefort and I forget what else. Very nice. 

They served everything with delicious garlic bread. Bad from a carbohydrate standpoint, but the little nibble I allowed myself proved it was crunchy, fresh, grilled and seasoned to perfection. 

The outdoor patio seating area looks like it would be a lot of fun at night, too. They're offering wine samplings, too, though we didn't partake. 

Thanks for the refreshing break, UnCork'd! Best of luck to you.
They used used overnight rice for my combo, the rice was cold and disgusting, never diet here again!

This place is FABULOUS!! And they DELIVER!!!!! The food is better than most eat-in Chinese restaurants and the family that runs it are just as fabulous as their food!! 

I've been having them bring me my favorite egg fu yung and other yummy food for almost 2 years and they are prompt, courteous and the food is always still so hot I have to let it cool before I eat it!!

Thank you China Garden!!!

Oh my goodness! We were in Tampa for a quick family getaway and we went to this place two days in a row for breakfast. I'm actually a little glad there isn't one in Miami because then I'd be in real trouble. 

Quite possibly the BEST WAFFLE I've ever had in my life. My mouth is watering as I type. 
We ordered off menu for a biscuit sandwich with egg, cheese and sausage. Wow wow wow. 

If you're anywhere near this place while it's open - you MUST stop and try it out.

We are so thankful to have Turchetti's whole-animal butchery supporting our family's meat needs while we quarantine. The city ham makes for great sandwiches - or as a fried topping on an egg sandwich. We also loved the ground beef (large grind with big flecks of delicious fat) in our burgers. 

I like knowing that they buy animals from Indiana farmers - which keep much needed money in our state during these crazy times. Thank you!

I love this place, how lucky we are to have had a true Mexican Taqueria move into Riverbend area. I grew up in SoCal & hence on real Mexican food as well as having travelled extensively through many parts of Mexico. If you want authentic Mexican food for a quick bite at a great price this is the place for you. The owners & staff are so nice also!
Noticing here most of the lower star ratings for TL are from due hard Felipe fans....if Americanized mex food & a trendy spot to eat your tacos is what you crave for your Mexican food experience, stick with Felipe's. 
The rest of us craving the real deal will be at Tacos Locos :)

Went here for happy hour, wow, great specials and really good food, not your typicl bar food, refreshing to have some differenet selections. Our bartender was fun, she was pleasant and was attentive when our drinks were getting low. Will be back.

I was at Jasper's a few weeks ago.  I met my sister there on a Friday night and was really looking forward to it after hearing about the transformation from the former  Jasper's Cafe.  I got there a bit late and the patio was packed.  It was an amazing Tucson spring evening and I was a little sad there were no tables left on the patio.  However, my sister had gotten us seats at the bar..... which was just so oddly placed.  No Feng Shui goin' down in The Jasper.... just sayin'.

Anyhoo, I sat down at the bar and was surprised to see that a friend of my favorite niece was a server at Jasper.....  she seemed pretty busy so I just waved at her. (I mention this because she was a key player in us getting some semblance of service later).  So, my sister had ordered a margarita (interesting and different) and I began perusing the menu.  What I really wanted initially was some water while I decided what to order.  The bartender was obviously too busy doing....uh.... I have no idea.  While the patio was full, the interior of the restaurant.... not so much.  There was another couple at the bar who were finishing up when I got there, so it wasn't like he was waiting on them hand and foot so to speak.... and so I waited.... and finally he acknowledged me.  I asked for some water which he obliged me with and then he was gone..... not literally, because he was still behind the bar, but trying to get him to actually serve us was almost impossible.  Finally, I flagged down my niece's friend and asked her if she would order us some appetizers.  We ordered the ceviche and amazingly, right after that the bartender decided to pay attention to us.  How convenient!  The ceviche was really good and something I would definitely order again.

I decided to order the gin mojito and it was pretty good but not something I'd go out of my way to order again.  We also were able to order some food from the bartender instead asking the poor servers walking by to help us out.  Honestly, the other 2 appetizers were so unmemorable, I can't even fairly review them a few weeks later.  Needless to say, due to the lack of respect and service from the arrogant, inattentive bartender and the not so exciting food I doubt I'll be back to Jasper.  I'd rather drive 10 miles farther and sit on the patio at The Abbey or go across the street to Armitage.  Jasper definitely has potential but right now, I'll skip it.
Cute place! We got the mushroom bruscetta with truffles which was very tasty!

So darn good! We went in the middle of renovations but they still made some perfect food! We got the family non vegetarian meal because we wanted to try a little of everything and it was a great idea! The tikka was amazing and the naan so good! Can't wait till the reopen in a couple weeks after the renovation is done!

Red Fish Grill: Burnt not Blackened. Last day in NO and I was really counting on a great meal and was willing to spare no expense. I've been to the Red Fish before and had a wonderful red fish in lemon butter sauce. That was no longer on the menu but they did have a blacked version of the same fish. Well that was far from the truth. It wasn't blackened it was burnt and not just the fish. The potatoes were so hard and crunchy they were worse than your most over cooked French fry. All I could taste was char and the butter sauce had no hope of making it any better. There is nothing really good I can say about this trip to the Red Fish Grill. Even the staff was totally confused by the two waitress process they have in place. Oh well. Back to the pizza joint.
Prices have gone up a ton and while the food still has good stuff, I feel like most pieces are not up to par. Roast pork only had a few crispy pieces. BBQ pork is still pretty great though.
The food and drinks are really good.  Great outdoor area. Every time I've been I've not been disappointed.

Food was excellent! They were extremely busy and the manager took the responsibility of helping by hosting, serving and bussing the tables. We will definitely add this to the rotation. Highly recommend fish and chips!

Barnabas is an incredible server, the service assistant was prompt, & the whole experience was wonderful. Truly great dining experience and so much to choose from. The scallops were absolutely perfect and the cannoli & chocolate pyramid were exquisite. I want to go back again and again to try new things. Thank you Barnabas, for a great belated Mother's Day dinner!

Delicious and fresh organic food and coffee with non dairy and gluten free options just a short walk from the beach! If you like a strong brew, try the Turkish coffee! Was great getting to know the owners and hear their story. Can't wait to come back!

Today's visit was meh. Had a bad meal. 
I ordered medium well delmonico.  It arrived charred and well done inside.  Same thing happened before and at that time they were determined to get it right, which was nice, but of course it would take some more time. This time I just didn't want to bother to get it fixed. I hate sending food back at restaurants. 
I think the quality has gone down in general.  I frequented Firebirds in Richmond.  It was great and that was my "norm".

food- Rack of lamb was awesome, sea bass was a little salty. Ambiance- small room , candle light , good date spot ... My pet peeve about byobs is that they make you order everything at once..that just turns me off. It's a little expensive too but Byob makes up for it... Overall good Byob in the city.
I got a calzone here for the first time today. I did takeout for lunch and ordered the Five-O. The overall flavors were really good but they skimped quite a bit on the other fillings.
Simply delicious! We ordered a lot and finished it all. I thought there would be leftover but it was too good. Excellent service, wish we had this restaurant near us.

The raspados are good but the service sucks, the workers are rude and stuck up which makes your experience bad. I would come back if my experience was more delightful. A short lady that was working was almost mimicking me when I ordered.

Wow! Holy smokes - we are so in love with this place. The veg is so fresh in their dishes, the taste is spot on, and the owner and staff are super friendly! We went here because our regular place was closed on this particular day, which is unfortunate for them! We are converted! When you go you have to try their homemade taro ice cream - out of this world!

Second best Thai food joint in Boise! I frequent this place and they've got friendly staff. Food is a little pricey though. Thai is always a great option when you have many vegetarian friends. I'd definitely suggest this place to friends!

Came to Royal House on a Sunday night, around 10pm. I ordered the seafood pot and my bf ordered the snow crab legs. While his meal was delicious I can't say the same about my food. First off, my meal was overly salty, all the clams and mussels were just empty shells with the meat no where to be found and then I barely got two-three shrimp in my pot. The only reason I didn't give this place a one star is because when I told my waitress that most of my order was missing, she brought me a dish with more mussels and clams. I was very disappointed with this meal. Wouldn't come back again

We just accidentally found this place and I have never had better catfish than I had over here. The catfish Lafitte is to absolutely die for and so are the chargrilled oysters. You won't go wrong with this spot !

This taco stand is open and ready to serve amazing food, to go or on their covered open-air dining patio.

The parking is minimal. You walk up to the building and order your food, then stand around and wait for it. In COVID times, I wish they'd come up with a better way--maybe a text when your food is ready? It was a little awkward. They also only accept cash or Venmo, which meant I had to end up paying for everyone in my party and they paid me back later--also awkward.

The food was pretty dang good and they have a lot to offer. We got street tacos and Mexican street corn-both solid choices. It's definitely a neat little spot that I'd come back to for a quick lunch during the day if I'm in the area.

Don't get the Ribs!  (everything else is good to go)

Coming downtown on a Sunday evening we were hit with an 1hr-1.5 hr wait for 2 people, after walking around the area for a bit we squeezed back by the bar to grab a few drinks to help the rest of our wait time pass, the true wait to be seat was at 50 minutes. 
For cocktails I went for the newly released Ole Darlin' Bartlett (Pear moonshine with vanilla lemonade) and OMG it was soooo smooth! Tasted exactly like the juice of a perfectly ripe pear. 
For my meal, as you might assume, I went for the 1/2 slab of ribs- though they had a far amount of meat on them, they were rock hard, I couldn't even pry the meat off with a fork, but had to bite the bone to get the meat to release! I substituted one of my sides for mac and cheese which was a nice gooey flavor kept warm my whole meal time in their little skillets. My husbands choice of the Pulled pork was much safer and showed that they really can make good barbecue. Our service was a little lacking, with our waters not even coming until our meal was out, but all and all it was a very filling meal that just took a little work to make it through.
My husband ordered an extra sauce for his Cheese sticks and was charged for funnel fries but was told y'all didn't have Any. They always mess up our order!! So double double check your order!

This is another rest. in a bad section of town and no parking lot.  What's up with Philly and parking spaces????  

I paid $21 here for ribs, collards, potato salad and cornbread.  They made me pay extra for mac n cheese because they don't allow it as a side option.  
The sides and cornbread were all ok, but I did not like the ribs.  They weren't quality ribs and were too mushy.  
The young girl running the counter had an attitude problem but she was very detail oriented. 
  
They do have a buffet style going and the food looked pretty tasty though excessively greasy.  I might stop here again if I were in that area otherwise, it's not worth the long drive I made just for home style southern cooking.

I've been coming here off and on for years and I actually really like this place. I was initially skeptical because when you see Irish pub you think ok this won't be the experience you want but it really is almost every time. Food might be pricey but it's center city and it's pretty good. I like coming here early on the weekends to be amongst real soccer fans. That is an experience this place was made for. The place gets packed but the atmosphere is fantastic, and they know how to properly pour Guinness (may have to do with the fact the staff are a majority from Ireland). The one thing I can say that keeps me from giving it a 5 star is the evenings on the weekends. I made the mistake of stumbling in one Saturday night and the place turned into a freaking dance club and that ruined it for me. So if you avoid those times and scene, I can only highly recommend coming here.

Food is great - margaritas (at least the $2.99 house special Lime Marg on Wednesdays ) are awful.

Great nopalitas salad (Marinated cactus leaves) - fresh veggies and a light dressing.
Shrimp Ceviche was HUGE and tasty.

Serive at the beginning was great - but the server messed something up with my dining pal's credit card and we waited, and waited, and waited to pay our bill.

Nevertheless, we'll be back.

Muy delicioso!
Best papusa hands down in a 50 mile radius, we stop every time we are in the area. Bring cash they dont take cards and expect service to be slow but it's worth the food

This is the real deal. When I lived in Chinatown I used to come here every week to buy fresh produce, meats and eggs. Iovine is awesome. Always fresh and always affordable. The dollar bags in the back are a steal. Also Godshalls has quality poultry and the guys that work the stand are super friendly. A rather new favorite of mine, is Guintas for both poultry and red meat. The smoked turkey and pig parts are fresh and taste great in soups. Perfect place to shop for groceries and ready to eat food. Highly reccomended - but be prepared for the crowds on the weekends.

Great location and there's parking in the building's garage. The interiors is nice and dimly lit for a nice romantic evening.

Hubby and I ordered the rock shrimp tempura as a starter. It was good with a lil kick in it. We then ordered the cabo roll and spicy salmon roll. I didn't like the cabo roll but the spicy salmon was pretty good. 

What I didn't like about this place is the very limited menu. They should add more nigiri choices and add some Maki roll with baked choices. Other than that, it was good overall.

Great non-traditional breakfast.  We have been for breakfast a few times and always enjoy it.  The service is always fast and friendly.  They are always very attentive to anything that you may need to go with your meal.  We have never had lunch there, but the menu looks like it has some good options as well.
Just good Chinese take out. Always easy to order and always ready when they say it will be.

This was my second visit to the Tucson location, my wife and I have been to the Scottsdale location several times and both locations have fantastic, service, food and decor. 

We meet the owner in Scottsdale and he is a warm wonderful person. The menu is huge with something for everyone vegan, vegetarian and lots of meat choices as well. 

They a full bar with a nice wine list. Not only is the food delicious the portions are huge AND a great value. 

If you have have Persian food before you're going to be impressed, if you have never had Persian food you are going to be transformed.

Horrible serivce!  Terrible  attitude by our waitress  Christina! And the drinks from the bar were like giving a child pacific sun juice.  I mean the only thing crappy's  had going for it its  unfortunate wast of a locations  which should've been used by a better resturant!
I have had my share of restaurant  experience this one by far is the worst ever.
Really good wings!! But the brisket was definitely overcooked and a bit dry. Homemade ranch was good too
I never leave restaurant reviews, but this place is by far my favorite restaurant in Nashville. Everything about it is perfect. It's a win win every time.

We will never eat here again. We ordered a side salad and asked for a side of onion and they charge 40 cents for 1 sliver of an onion. Really, Bazbeaux!!!  Plus, they only gave us two teaspoons of dressing and guess what, you guessed it, another up charge of 50 cents. They must be really hurting for money, to treat use to be, loyal customers for something that all restaurants would give FO FREE!!!!!

I ordered the three fish sampler where the chef chooses which fish to give you. While the fish was fresh, I felt that the flavor was uninspired and dull. I don't even remember what they tasted like! For the price, I would have expected the restaurant to find pairings that bring out the natural flavors of the fish they serve.

On the other hand, the clam chowder was pretty good. It was the right thickness and didn't have a starchy taste.

Perhaps I should've ordered wine. A bottle of alcohol is bound to make anything taste better.

I don't write many reviews on yelp.  Things have to be either pretty bad or pretty good for me to spend the time to do this.  Unfortunately, Baan Thai is one of the former.

My fiancé and I were excited to find the place as we have always felt that Fishtown (in all of it's glory) lacks decent Asian delivery.  We were sadly disappointed.  We ordered delivery one Friday night.  Specifically the fried sweet potatoes, fresh rolls, a chicken dish and a beef noodle dish. 

All of the food was brought in plastic containers.  The first bite I took made it clear that the food was packaged whole still hot.  Everything had that plastic tasting airplane food quality to it.  Even the dipping sauces (and I don't know how that's possible).

We also ordered the spiciest dishes (we LOVE spicy food).  And yet everything was totally bland.  Aside from the plastic flavor. 

And the best part?  We love 0.7 miles away and were charged a $3 delivery charge.  Forget the "free delivery" championed on the website.

Avoid at all costs.  Stick to pizza.

We have made several trips over the last few years and I must say that I have never been disappointed. The service is Rockstar outstanding and the food always leaves room for surprises. From the cheese selections to the aged beef, pastas , and very creative small plates you should find something amazing. We really enjoy the atmosphere and every time we have been it has been memorable. It's a great value for the outstanding craftmanship that goes into every bite! Enjoy.
Awesome Restaurant Great Food and we sat next to The team Captain of the Indianapolis Colts Super Bowl Champ!!! We had a great time great service and great food!!

I've been there twice. In both cases the chicken was dry.  In fact, the dishes tasted like they'd been sitting awhile like leftovers from lunch.
Other people seem to like the place, but my personal experiences haven't been good.
There are several other Thai restaurants in town and I've had good experiences at all of them.

This is my neighborhood go-to for good, cheap quick pizza and italian sandiwiches. It's everything you're looking for if you want to eat, not spend a ton of money, have something filling. And when nothing else is open because you spent too much time partying or goofing around downtown, they'll still be open. Their drinks are unlimited refills.

You can get a half sandwich and drink, tell them to "make it a combo" and you can literally be out the door less than six dollars... (Make sure to tell the newbies there's a button on the screen for that special price.) And let me tell you their "half" sandwich? It would be a "whole" one across the street if you went to subway, and these are freshly made, toasted, and served with Parmesan cheese and all the fixin's. The full sandwich can easily feed two people. Can't beat it!

If you want a pizza slice, they have them. Several whole medium pizzas are for less than $10 dollars. Delivery is quick and they bring it to your door with no problems. You get to know the staff if you're a regular and they greet you by name.

Oh yes, and they have cheesecake. One time I spent an hour roaming around on a Sunday with everything else closed as far down as California St. searching for cheesecake and these guys were the only ones open that had it. It's served cold in a little plastic covered tray thingy, but it's cheesecake nonetheless.

They're also very kind to the local homeless people, which is more humanitarian than other places I've seen.

The food quality, authenticity, and price are all worth the 5 stars. I'm not sure why people would complain when their prices are so cheap compared to other areas. The food was tasty and did not get me sick so I would say that's already a step above some other restaurants. Their grandpa's chicken, pork fried rice, noodles, and hot and sour soup was delicious.

I first went here on a Friday night out looking for some food after already having a few cocktails. Santa Barbara, for as much good eating as there is, can be a tough place to find a bite to eat after 10. Roy, however is open til midnight (I believe) every night, which is great.

The cocktails are nice pours, and they have this great $10 entree deal going for a seemingly unlimited time. I've only had the chicken marsala, which is delicious. It comes with potato pancakes and vegetables.

The service is touch and go, sometimes it's fine, sometimes it's painfully slow, even if you're the only people there!

Anyway, I've almost made a trip there a weekly occurrence.

This place is fantastic. As someone that lives downtown I'm always surprised when I stumble across amazing food for a good price. I found this spot in my search for Cafe Con Leche and was more than impressed with the Lechon sandwich. The bread is toasted perfectly, the garlic mojo makes the roasted pork's flavor pop, and the portion for the price is perfect. Downtown St Petersburg definitely lacks in Cuban Cuisine but with the future expansion into a juice bar and the currently amazing sandwiches, Bodega is a great start.

Just not the smash burger I enjoyed the location.  Just not the best.   The fries are never fresh and the burgers just don't taste as the other locations.    Not sure this location is the best for smash burger.

We are on vacation, had a late start to dinner, and found this restaurant just down from the hotel opened till 11pm online. We arrived at 10:10pm. As we walked in, the bartender announced they are closed. I said your sign states 11pm and online it said 11pm. She just said, "yeah, I know, sorry."

Fido? More like Delight-o!!!
The honey-sugar-coffee concoction I ordered may have been nauseatingly saccharine, but I'll never turn down an opportunity to stick it to my dentist. I just hate him so much. 

I recognize that this is just my taste, and I won't say the barista didn't warn me. I understand that not everyone likes to taste coffee in their coffee. Aside from my mediocre beverage experience, I found the ambiance to be quite pleasant. Plenty of open space and silent enough for me to imagine successfully reading a book on my tablette. I found the canine motif to be quite fetching. 

PUNTENTIONAL.

It was super packed but I decided to wait anyway... the estimate to sit was 30 minutes but to my suprise we were sat in 10. They had really good specials on their oysters and they were delicious. The service was great as was the fried calamari. Only complaint was that it was a tad expensive but all in all it was worth it. I deff recommend this place. Stay away from Doc Mcgrogens !!!
Hugely impressed with the food ..The dahi poori was legit keep it up ..Chole batoore was great and the other curries were also up to mark..sambhar was a bit bland but still not bad ..

So many choices it's overwhelming but in a good way. We got food from fourth street cookies, BECK's Cajun and two other places I wish I could remember. All was so good! Even though there are tons of vendors, everything is clean and organized. A must visit

This is a really interesting place. I have heard of it for years, but never got around to visiting. Last week some co workers made it a lunch run and I was very pleased with the food. So, today, I went there for lunch. Huge portions, that's for sure. I like the idea of how they do things and the food quality. The area, 10th and Post Road, is a little, shall we say, "sketchy"? But, in the day time, not a big deal. The food is the real star here. And if you opt to dine in, you can order unlimited side dishes!!!! I had the chicken over rice, a spicy Creole side, (5+++ Stars!!!), a side of their Chili, very good, and their bread pudding for desert. Can't wait to go again and try the other sides. I was too stuffed to order more sides today. If you are in the area, or even just near-by, make a stop, you won't regret it.

So we drove to Philly over the weekend and wanted to experience what all the rave was about at both Pat's and Geno's (you can find my review for Geno's on their page). Well where do I begin? The location is horrible, such an unsafe neighborhood in an unsafe city, parking was horrendous (we had to park nearly 3 blocks away) and I for one felt really uncomfortable leaving my nice car parked in such a torn down neighborhood. So, we walk over to the stands (they're not restaurants.. just stands where you order food) get in line and wait approx 10 minutes which wasn't bad for a "tourist trap" food stand. The service was horrendous, if you don't know how to order or have your cash in hand you will get scolded told to move away for others (who does this?!?). Once we ordered we walked across the street to an open field and sat on the fence to eat (not enough tables or counter space). We got a "wit provolone" sandwich which was OK at best... the meat was under seasoned and the cheese wasn't properly melted, the bread was the best part, especially after it soaked up some of the juices from the meat. Overall, it was very disappointing, after all the talk and hoopla about this place it truly wasn't anything special. People say "well you go there for the experience" what experience are they talking about? horrible parking, bad smells, rude people and mediocre food?

This place used to be the only place I would go to get matar paneer. However, after this experience in will never step back inside. I have often purchased this one and only dish here at the brandon location. I'm unsure if they are under new management, but they provided me with 3/4 full  container of my meal. Even the staff noticed that it wasnt full. When I asked to have it filled up, I recieved an attitude and saying that most people want more rice. I never want more rice as that is not the reason to purchase this item. I was very insulted and they kept walking my container back and forth and speaking about it. Once they brought it back up, it looked like they swishes it around the container and gave it back. I promptly requested a refund and walked out. I will never come by this place again. The manager should know better than to say that people want more rice than the actual specialty dish they make. Ridiculous.

Cool place to hang out for lunch or happy hour. The food is great for people who like brats and also gives the more adventurous some options. The beers are great, but a bit pricey. I downgrade any place that doesn't have happy hour on Fridays so really this is a 4.
Cool Springs was missing a nice micro brew place like this. I think I've figured out that they water down their beer to get you to stay longer.
Ok sandwiches. Excellent bread pudding. Dirty restaurant. In sum, the recognition precedes reality.
The chicken Philly with Cajun seasoning is awesome. Shrimp po boy was also great.

Went on a Saturday so we could try the weekend only dishes and the place was packed full. We waited a half hour to be seated and ordered an appetizer while deciding what we wanted. Unfortunately that meant that by the time I ordered the Pastor tacos they had sold outWound up ordering Cochinta Pibil (Mexican style pulled pork) and Suadero (slow cooked beef). To share with my husband while the girls had the kids menu. 

Kids both got quesadillas which came in a cute face design with two folded quesadillas for only $4 each (or add meat for 2$ more)

We ordered the 4 tacos for $16 however the tacos were not much bigger than the kids and were double the cost. Add drinks, dessert and the appetizer and the bill added up quick. 

Service was slow due to the business of the place, our server was new so didn't really know much about the food when asked which were spicy. When asked if something could be on the side I got a funny look. 

While the food quality was great I won't bother with going on a Saturday evening again. Too busy, didn't get what I came for.

Portions are extremely small - containers are teeny as well making it difficult to eat. I'm at a poke place in California right now where I know it's common and I can't believe the difference in portions!  The pricing is way cheaper here too for better size and quality. I really hope poke bowl makes some changes because im a huge fan of poke and there aren't any other places in Philly.

Unfortunately, I discovered this place AFTER I moved away from Tucson.   But it's a great place to get a tasty beer.  40 on tap, you're bound to find something you like.  They also have a pretty decent bloody mary.... just enough heat to put my hangover to ease. 

Tried the pretzel... it was... a pretzel.  Nothing too awe-inspiring.  That beer mustard though.... I would like to coat all of the things with it.  Delicious.

Definitely check them out -- great addition to Downtown Tucson.
Sometimes their customer service is not excellent, they don't keep restaurant clean, alot of the employees are standing around.
Great customer service. Horrible quality frozen lobster tails. I feel I was ripped off. I should have went to costco instead. Step up your game with the lobster tails.
One of my favorite St. Louis spots and a place I'm sure to visit when I ever I come to town. Warm and welcoming with a great wine list and good food.

The best sandwich shop on Tampa!!!!  Everything is fresh and amazing. They have fun and quirky sandwich combinations that are scrumptious. Really small shop, totally worth the wait. The owners are so nice and pleasant and really eager to help you have the best meal!!

Goldies still delivering the best, now following spacing guidelines and with full mask compliance as you would expect.  If you'd like to get out of the house consider one of Boise' best, you know ... the place everyone recommends to a visitor.
Food. Delicioso! Ambience. De bienvenida! Dessert. Cambia la vida! Service. Jackie is THE BEST! En serio, la mejora. Cannot wait to return to Los Gallos.

This is not the first cheesecake factory I have been too, but this is probably the last time I will be going to this location. My husband and I went here yesterday for the first time to have a early dinner. We arrived and waited 15mins to be seated, when we were seated we noticed that we could see about 14 open tables around us, I only assume there wasn't  enough staff so I didn't think to much of it.

Our waitress came and got us drinks and brought us bread, while we sat there my husband pointed out that the table had a bunch of caked on gunk on it. Now I know that no restaurant table is super clean, but I would like to think that they could get the chunky stuff off at least.  After he pointed that out he pointed me to the floor of the table next to us. Now this table along with 5-6 more next to them were all bussed and set up to seat people, no one was using them. But the floor underneath the one next to us had flood under it, and not just bread crumbs, but some decent sized pieces. We looked  around us and there was a lot of old food pieces, some dirty napkins, and just filth. I get that floors get dirty but the place wasn't that busy and if you have all these open tables you would think someone could grab a broom and just do a quick clean up to get the big stuff.

As for the food. I had the club sandwich which was good, but it is hard to mess up a club. My husband had some sort of spicy chicken sandwich which wasn't spicy, had almost no chipotle sauce, and the cheese looked like it just sat out in a warm place instead of being melted on top. We both had fries as a side which were insanely bland.

The services was ok. The waitress and hosts were nice and friendly, but our waitress wasn't super attentive and didn't get drink refills till we were done eatting, which was kind of a waste. In the end we left disappointed and slightly grossed out.

Consider this your home away from home. Walking into this cafe, I felt like I was walking into the living room of a family member. I love the cozy, mismatched furniture and the homey decorations, and they had the place decked out for the holiday season, too. 

They've got awesome specials, including seasonal rotations, but I had a french press to see how their coffee was on its own - I was not disappointed. They served it to me in a real mug so that I could settle in and spend time with my friends while I enjoyed the brew. 

My favorite thing about this place is how intentional everything is - they partner with local organizations and businesses (like Seeds of Happiness and animal rescue groups, they leave used coffee grounds outside so people can take them for free and use for a variety of purposes, they offer crayons and coloring pages for kids, and they even have events like open mic night or painting classes. 

Basically, if you want to have a good cup of coffee, and feel really good about where your money is going, swing by this place. 

Tips: they do have food (pasties, breakfast burritos, chicken wraps, etc.), there is outdoor seating, there is a water bowl for dogs out front, and there is free WiFi.
Will not return. After waiting 8 minutes to order ... number 3 in line but drive through comes first, got grilled cheese too oniony to eat. Grilled chicken not much better.
Service slow and food quality has slipped. Waited a long time to get served and the food was nothing to write home about.
Great down home Philippine barbecue. Was offered samples as we came in, chicken is out of this world!
The Bacon Blue Cheese Burger was the stuff of dreams - I wrote home about it.
I came in for brunch, and I definitely plan to be back. The server (Chelsea), paced everything well, and my friends and I enjoyed the mimosas. Glad that someone took that old Pinnacle spot!

They didn't expect and they aren't ready for long weekend like long weekend. They aren't ready for a big party. Whenever there is a long weekend they should get ready for big crowed but they dont. The food was so slow (we waited for an hour for our food to come). Food come to the table that they remember first, so if they forgot about you remind them otherwise they will forget. When the resturant gets busy with big tables, they forgot about small tables. There is no refill the water or anything you have to ask for it. I have never experience this bad service before.

Cheese wiz on my burger. CHEESE WIZ ON MY FUCKING BURGER. Luxery to say the least. My crew strolled in there after a steezy win on the Bocci court. Clean sweep no big deal. Anyway me and Dizzy Double D sit down for some suave grub. 50 chicken wings later and I got to experience the motion of the ocean of the bathroom. SUPERB. Double ply toilet paper? You gotta be tuggin on my ball bag. Service was kinda slow though. Took like 45 minutes to get my burger. Did I mention there was cheese wiz on my fucking burger?  It's okay though. The waitress was kind enough to give us step by step instructions on how to get to some strip club called Double Vision.  She said it was dirty. Idk how she knew but that's none of my business. Hopefully I won't have to wait 45 minutes for my lap dance from Phoenix. I wonder if they'll have cheese wiz. Waitress with the glasses was exemplary.

Brought here by some friends during a recent trip to Phila for a wedding, and I was duly impressed; the service was top-notch, and while every other joint in Passyunk was crammed to the rafters, they managed to find us a nice table for a group of eight with hardly any delay.  The liquor selection was solid if not particularly creative, and the food, likewise, was better than standard gastropub quality but not enough to make it a memorable restaurant in its own right.  But overall, it was very good, and really went out of its way to make a good impression on us.  It's always hard to judge a place based on a single visit, but I'd love the chance to go back again and confirm SPTR is worth those four stars.
Such a fun relaxed atmosphere. Perfect for groups getting together for food or coffee. Living room feel.

The noodles here are amazing, but everything else about this place was terrible. The veggies were questionable and the egg was grey. Waiting for a table was a mess, vicious even. Other people will snatch a table out from under you if you wait for the dishes of the former customer to be cleared. But again, the noodles are starch heaven.

We went to RSC for lunch on Sunday and had an absolutely terrific experience. Andre, who waited on us at the bar, was gracious, pleasant, and knowledgeable about food; the service here is nearly on par with that of Zahav! The food was wonderful. I tried the beet-pomegranate borscht and the biscuit with egg and cheese, both of which were perfect. My companions ordered the brunch special, a sausage and cornbread waffle, which was also perfect. Overall a wonderful experience- will be back very soon!
THIS PLACE IS AWESOME!!!!!!! So good. I'm so excited to get it today for our weekly office friday lunch.

I am disappointed with my panzarottis latley. They are pre made and you can tell they just throw them in the oven to reheat....gross! Makes the grease linger and pour out when you dig in. What happened to fresh made?  Booooo!
