We had the feeling we were guests in someone's home. This was reinforced when the owner came over to introduce herself and ask about our meal. This is exactly what we were. When you're next in the mood for some succulent chicken or a creamy kofta, do not hesitate to try Haveli. We can't wait to go back.

Good food. Hamburger and fries are terrific, husband had the French dip.  You can sit indoors or out. We sat indoors.  While we were here they opened garage style doors so it was nice and airy.  Looks like a great place to hang out with old friends. I always like a place offering Fat Tire, so that was a plus.  Would come back again for sure.  Saw a pizza go by that looked very crunchy and full of topping.

The rooms are outdated. The homeless overtake the entire garden and outside area. It's embarrassing. Staff was friendly. The elevators are extremely slow and there are so many of them so you would expect them to be quicker. Probably would stay somewhere else next time around. Just seemed run down
excellent pizza, despite it not being what I ordered lol. The wait for delivery is pretty standard, about 60 mins but I'm grateful they even deliver to my location so hey, thanks.

Neat coffee spot in an unexpected spot. Was surprised to find a caje in the area. Definitely a lot more low key then the one near state street. Drinks here are a bit pricey, but look amazing once you get them. Everything on the menu is presented beautifully like a work of art. The rosemary Thai tea that I got was pretty good. I expected a more traditional Thai tea taste to it, but still really enjoyed the soothing flavor of the tea. Overall very cool and chill spot!

Overall very Bad experience. 

Worst Thai Food & to top it bad service. 
Visiting Santa Barbara from Bay Area where we have a plethora of Thai Restaurants - so we are spoilt with Thai cuisine options the Bay Area has to offer. Nevertheless- based on other reviews - we decided to order take out from Zen Thai. 
- we ordered 
Tom Kha - overpowered by Coconut milk. Lacked the galangal, Kaffir & lemongrass flavors in it. Very watery too. 

Green Curry - very spicy, and again very watery gravy with cut jalapeño in it.  We asked them to keep it as mild as possible. So disappointed. 

Plain vermicelli noodles for our toddler. Over the phone we asked specifically if they have them as our toddler loves it. Instead the take out had flat write noodle! 

To go with the green curry - we ordered 3 serves of rice. Ended up getting just 1 serve!! Since we were staying at a hotel - we couldn't make extra rice so instead ended up having the green curry as a soup! 

Overall very Bad experience!

The coffee is good but somebody stole my sunglasses off my table while I was in the restroom! After ordering a coffee I set my sunglasses on my table and--after quickly using the restroom--I came back and my coffee had been delivered to my table, but my sunglasses were gone. I asked all of the employees and customers in the area, but no one saw anything. Watch your valuables!

When you're looking for a classic New Orleans Po-Boy. Guy makes it the best. 

Their 11" po-boy is big enough to feed two hungry boys. 

We had the fried shrimp po-boy with everything on it. They asked if we wanted it split in half and they did. And individually wrapped it for us too! 

The sandwich was AMAZING. 

Two things thought. 

I wish they didn't use so much paper to wrap the sandwich. I felt like one paper was enough. 

Secondly, wish they had fried oysters :( but did they not have it. But the fried shrimp did not disappoint! 

Cash only.

I don't know if they hire people and don't train them or what's wrong there. When I ordered a King jr menu for my dAughter this dude had no idea what I was talking about not was he able to clearly communicate. They forgot half of my order and then acted as if I never ordered that. Absolute idiots working there
Great service, amazing FRESH oysters, and free valet! cant wait to go again! Valerie, Tabitha, Brad, & BJ are always the best!
Delicious empanadas. Highly recommend. When we are in the SB area we love to stop at Buena Onda to get some empanadas. I love the Humitas and the Serrano with some fresh chimichuri.

These guys are the oldest family owned Italian in the USA for a reason. Great food in a laid back setting. A taste of the old world pasta and gravy. Not overly expensive but not cheap either. Regardless a good meal every time.
We are weekend regulars and this is our favorite place for a delish crab omelette and the best mimosas in town! It gets crazy busy so call ahead or use the app to get on the waitlist-worth the wait!
Very nice place, good flavor and good price. I recommend the picanha and yuca frita, very good.

I really enjoyed their food! Place is clean and small, but I didn't mind. I had jerk chicken, rice and peas and cabbage. My friend and I really enjoyed it and this is the only place we swear by in the downtown area to get Jamaican food.
Love love love Valente's! Their homemade delicacies are the best!

This is strictly on what occurred in our way out tonight ...server was sweet: not pushy, attentive, food was exactly what we were looking for: fast, sandwiches, easy, tasty...on our way out the entire staff seemed to be at the service bar area and all said goodbye to us as we did to them and thanked them...one little snark in the bunch (not our server, another male server that also made a comment after we sat down to a fellow server: "I'm not taking them.") said goodbye and something after that was snarky and rude which both embarrassed and amused the gaggle of servers standing around. Now my husband and I are both in the business and have been for quite some time...I should have said something to him or the manager who was at the host stand but I didn't...I wasn't even going to write a review but it aggravated me as the night went on...I tried to think if we did something? If we sat down late? But we were done and out the door by 9pm and they close at 10...this server wouldn't last an hour in one of our restaurants...he should learn to shut his mouth until customers are out of earshot.

Went there sunday 3-11-12, in the afternoon with a friend, it wasnt too busy. We ordered sodas to drink. The waiter, a young male, brought them quickly.  A few minutes later, we ordered. I ordered a turkey burger, my friend a 'Shroom Burger.  It wasnt the 1st time we've eaten there, been there a couple times before.  We finished our sodas, and were waiting for refills....for a long time.  Maybe 5-10 minutes. Finally we got refills, after the waiter finished talking to 2 young girls.  We overlooked that, and fortunately we got our food.  Our food tasted good, and we ate, then left. The price was good.  Well, about a 1/2 hour later I started feeling like i had a big lump in my stomach....NAUSEOUS... took some bicarbonate, and it didnt help.  Had to lie down, and had a STOMACHACHE for the next 24 hrs. Had DIARRHEA, and couldnt eat.   Finally 2 days later I felt ok.   I dont think I will ever eat there again.  This was the 1st time I got sick there, but the restaurant probably has cleanliness issues in the kitchen.  Dont want to risk it again !

I know I know... the line... but honestly if I am on South Street it seems like I am cheating myself if I don't get a cheesesteak for the road. 

I first had Jim's during my college days, when waiting for a piercing appointment at Infinity, my friends and I were told to get something in our stomachs and circle back. 

Jim's has earned its reputation, and is definitely a beloved Philly treasure (check the walls inside while you wait and you will see autographs and photos from a million and one celebrities). 

Some tips to Jims are to know what you want before you get to the counter (for those visiting or unsure, just listen to the previous patrons who order), and be ready to move quick once you are at the cashier. You don't want to be that guy who is holding up the line wrapped round the building on a hot August day (no one likes that guy). Also seating is upstairs - narrow staircase on the right just past the cashier.

Like this place friendly neighborhood type feel which is hard to find in camel. Very open and lots of natural light in the bar. Love their habanero sauce ask for it with the fish tacos. I have not had anything i did not like. A lot of regulars seem to come here also. Beer is not my favorite of local variety but do enjoy several especially champagne velvet pilsner on a hot summer day. I try to stop by here on a monthly basis. Some of the menu choices are a tad high would be perhaps a slight drawback for a cheap lunch. Staff is younger and most of the time very attentive occasionally there have been a few misses. All in all it is a solid place and has a super nice deck.

I've been to several Wing House locations and have to admit that they are by far my favorite wings. With that being said I also must say that they are not all equal. 
I visited this location last night and enjoyed myself immensely. I was promptly greater and seated by a very friendly staff. The waitress was very polite and attentive.  Once our order was taken it was delivered in a very timely manner. The food was exceptional, hot, flavorful, and appealing to the eye. Even when the restaurant began to get busy week were not rushed to leave. 

This has become my new favorite.  Good job Ladies!
I love this place!! It's just everything tasty, fresh and clean!! I loooove the sushi and sashimi. And the staff is super friendly.
Food and drinks were average. We ordered a bunch of things and they were all missing seasoning or taste. It's located in a great spot, it's just the food could be better.

Food was as close to Spain as you can't get on the west coast!! Sommelier was helpful and our waitress was amazing as well. More importantly the food matches their service. Try the ham croquette, Japanese sweet potato (although something I've never had in Spain it was my favorite dish.) i can have this over and over!!!, their kale salad also filled with flavors ;something I'd never order but my partner loves a good salad) and I was stunned it was my 2nd favorite dish. Loquita is a must try!! Food, service and ambiance is worthwhile

u gotta take your drink upstairs u can watch the bands and enjoy the beautiful view . inside is solid food &drinks are alittle expensive but with the location its worth it. dont b afraid to ask to bring your drink on the balcony upstairs its worth it.
Great ambience and awesome happy hour selection and prices. The bar is large and has room to move around, which is rare in the area. Will definitely return!

Renata's Kitchen is a classic UCity eatery that everyone loves! Although they are known for their brunch, I came for dinner and was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food and service!

They had just revamped and added a dinner menu recently and so I was a little apprehensive. However they did stay true to their Middle Eastern/Mediterranean roots! I ordered the Turkish Eggplant appetizer and the Chicken Mohammar entrée. 

The Turkish Eggplant, three pieces of Italian eggplant covered in a thick parsley tomato-based sauce, was good! It was yummy but nothing outstandingly special though.

On the other hand, the Chicken Mohammar is a MUST GET! You guys, IT'S SO GOOD. According to the menu, it's cooked for 18 hours and boy does that actualize in the dish. The chicken was so tender and still remained juicy after all of that cooking. The true star though was that sauce (pretty much got lost in the sauce ). The sauce was tomato-based as well but had a bevy of flavors and spices. It was spicy but right below the threshold of discomfort. The sauce was beautifully balanced and complemented the chicken (which is cooked in that sauce) and potatoes. My only desire was to have more of it!

The service was great, but the food was quite pricey. Honestly though, this is a worthy place for your money!

This was quite the surprise, but I'm so happy that their dinner menu was great and not basic! I'm definitely coming back for more!

Had some very bad service here. For a slightly expensive restaurant, my expectation is always service that goes above and beyond. This was no where even close to what I might get from a 16 year old stoner kid at applebees. In fact it was much worse. 

First... we waited 20 minutes for a reserved table. Then they finally sat 8 of us at a small round table meant for 4 at the very front of the room next to the bathrooms and kitchen entrance (aka worst table in the restaurant). Our server was a complete dick. He made several huge mistakes. 1 - initially only took drink orders for half the table, then walked away. 10 minutes later he came back and asked if we had any questions about the menu and I said how about take the rest of our drink orders... no apology. He hated me from that moment on. Also didn't fill my beer up all the way when he brought it out (really?!?!) 2 - brought out the wrong appetizer. 3 - brought out the wrong pasta entree for a vegetarian who hadn't eaten meat in decades and accidentally ate it this night (thanks dumb ass!) 4 - didn't bring us bread until after our salads were finished and we had to ask about it 5 - never apologized for anything never offered anything free, and had a completely awful attitude. 

Really disappointed. My lasagna and salad were actually outstanding, but the ridiculous table location w zero room for 8 people and asshole service overshadowed any of the delicious food. Never going back and that waiter should be canned.
Best Vada Pav in town, a must try.  South Indian Dosa, North India Dishes, and so much to explore at the Philadelphia Chutney Company, all topped with a friendly service!!!
Lauren our server was excellent. Very friendly, professional, and knew everything about the menu. The restaurant was very clean and romantic! We will eat there again!

So let me start off by saying this was an awesome experience , over-whelming (in like a really good way) . The meat that I tasted was really juicy and fresh and I paired it with a Merlot that I can't remember the name of but it was also really good!  The only reason I give it 4 out 5 stars is because  I don't know if it was my position in the restaurant but my entire table was full and I had barely gotten any meat . I mean it was like by the time the server would get to me he'd be out of meat . Sooo I was like not getting full at all . I kinda felt a little robbed because it was like I didn't really get as much as everyone else but I still paid the same amount . I was just kinda watching them enjoy everything . But what I did get a chance to taste was amazing!
Good margaritas, good guac and good tacos. Service was also great! Would recommend to anyone

So here's what's up: I had a concern about my receipt showing incorrect tip %s (basically the suggested tip % at the bottom was off--it said "20% is $X" but it was actually 40% of the total--this also happened to my friend's receipt), I didn't think THAT much of it (like maybe it was some software issue with their receipt app or whatever) but I emailed Datz weeks ago to let them know of the error because I thought they'd want to know--esp since at the bottom of the receipt, they say to please email them for any concerns/suggestions... but I never got a response. I also messaged them on social media and never got a response, which I think is p darn unprofessional, esp if you specifically ASK for feedback ON your receipt? It's like, claiming that a manager will reach out to you on Yelp but they never do (happens a lot LOL). Like, how hard is it just to reply with "Oh wow, we had no idea that was happening! We will look into the issue and get it resolved ASAP! Thank you for contacting us about this so we can fix it." Datz, if you're reading, you can copy & paste that as a response to my email, but I'm still waiting for a response.

OK besides that whole skadoo, I enjoyed my meal. They did mess up my order (I don't eat dairy and specifically said "no cheese" twice but both parts of my meal came with cheese on it) and fixed it. The food was good, but I think they need to work on their managerial skills...
Great chocolate almond croissants but the service can be really slow and it's a bit pricey. Worth the wait when you need a yummy treat.

I can say my first road trip to Philly was highlighted by Pat's. The entire experience was great. Plus I thank y'all Yelp reviews for helping choose between Pat's & Gino's. The line wasn't too long & the whole sit outside neighborhood feel was perfect. The cheesesteak was everything I had heard Philly's cheesesteaks were.

Great business for the west side. Often busy. Good portions sizes for the prices you pay. They heat and make the tortillas fresh. The bar is pretty good, could be better. All and all worth a visit if you are on the west side looking for some Mexican food.

The sushi is amazing!! To be located in a state that is not surrounded by water the sushi is very high quality. Also, the rolls are a very decent size and quality so you definitely get the bang for your buck! The sushi tour is a little pricey but so worth it and could fill up a party of 6-8 especially with some appetizers. Also the drinks are very well priced and delicious.

UPDATE-We returned for the beginning of my birthday weekend with our dear friend Deniece from San Francisco, my husband and our wonderful friends John and Nick. Jesus was our server and he did not miss a beat. Vicente a Managing Partner stopped by the table to say hello and Chef Wesley and the staff presented me with a desert platter fit for royalty.  The service, care and culinary delights of On Swann are truly unparalleled. This is our second visit and I cannot wait to return. We were treated with such amazing care and kindness...and the food, gosh the food is simply divine! What makes this establishment so different for me, is the true heart in the staff. It is remarkable. We cannot wait to come
back!
Went there with friends for dinner, the atmosphere is amazing and relaxing, and the food was absolutely incredible! Vegetarian soup is to-die-for!

Great views. Whole restaurant rotates slowly. In about an hour you went 360 degrees. Good food and good service.  Kitchen is downstairs and food is brought up. Some renovations were going on when I was there. Making outdoor bar and dining area. Drawings looks really cool.

Went here for brunch with a group of friends on a Saturday.  The food wasn't very good, but the reason I am giving 3 stars instead of 2 is the brunch special they offer.  $25 for all you can drink bloody mary's or mimosa's which include an entree.  So if you're looking for some daytime boozing with some OK food, this is a great spot.  Outdoor seating is a little small, but we got there right as they opened so we didn't have a wait at all.  The staff was also very nice and checked up on us VERY often.  Perhaps the food at other meals is better than breakfast, so I'll definitely go back to this place.

Great breakfast for the price!  You get a great big plate of food for $8, and it's way better then fast food.  I come here whenever I'm out in sparks around breakfast time.  You order at the register then they bring it to your table.  Usually very fast for made to order good.
I've eaten the pizza here a number of times and never found it to be all that good.  Boring sauce, and boring crust.

We thought we'd try Wilko's because we were attending a event at Centennial Hall. They were out of the first two bottles of wine we ordered (really? on a busy Saturday night?) We started out by ordering the mixed pantry board.  It was served with a few cubes of cheese and some meats that looked like packaged cold cuts. For $20 we expected more! We  would have left at that point, but we were pressed for time. My husband ordered the Marguerita pizza which was mostly sauce with little cheese and I ordered the pasta which was served in a watery, bland marinara sauce. We should have saved our money and gone to Gentle Ben's for a burger and beer!
Everyone agreed that Pats is better than Genos. I had the veggie sub loaded with mushrooms, onions, peppers. Huge! The pepper/sauce bar was the best part!

Ok so I want to start this by saying I know times are really hard for small businesses right now. I have eaten really good food here before. Today was not the case. I love Baba ganoush. It's o e of my favorite dishes to make, so I admit I'm picky about it, but it is just so so good when it's done right. There was hardly any eggplant in this dish today. Way too heavy on the tahini. When mixed in beef shawarma it was a little more ok. The beef was pretty good. I asked for it on top of a fattoush salad. The salad was not good. The dressing was premixed and it was not flavorful. No taste of pomegranates or lemon.  Very soggy. I will eat here again for sure. It's a wonderful family place. I cook a lot of Lebanese food at home and I will admit it's a cuisine I am very picky about!
My friends showed up 20 minutes to closing and they wouldn't make more food even though they were all ordering the same thing. This place is so analog

The sandwiches are mediocre. I had their spicy chicken sandwich and the meat was microwaved. I tried their turkey sandwich before and it was underwhelming. No bueno and not worth the price $9-11. 

On the other hand, their sushi and breakfast burritos are delish.

Well the food truck revolution has finally hit Tucson.  About 4 years late folks.  Well lets talk about Serial Grillers.  Being from the Philadelphia area I don't usually eat cheese steaks outside of Philly.  Having a couple beers at Dragoon and my buddy convinced me to give them a try.  They had some unusual combinations for a cheese steak but all sounded good.  I chose the Kalifornia and added bacon for a $1.  That's 4 strips of bacon for a $1.  How do you pass that up.  

The Kalifornia is steak, cheddar cheese, pico, and french fries.  Oh and the bacon.  I am a sucker for sandwiches with french fries.  Why not just get all down in one shot. The sandwich looked a little smaller than I'm use to but it was packed with rib eye steak.  I was stuffed.  The french fries seem to be hand cut, I didn't ask.  They were perfectly cooked and have tons of flavor.  

I am giving them 5 stars great food and the excellent communication on Facebook where they are going to be.

I GOT VERY SICK: I ordered the traditional pork belly ramen this evening. When it arrived, I noticed the ramen was almost cold (lukewarm), but it was a very busy night, so I stirred and ate it anyway. 

About 8 hours later, at 2 AM, I woke up with extreme nausea, chills, and a fever. About 30 minutes later, I threw up everything I had eaten. This was all closely followed by diarrhea as well :( 

I would highly recommend that this restaurant be very careful with their food's holding temperatures and that the customer be mindful of this... for your own safety.

I typically don't eat at the hotel, but this restaurant breaks that rule. Steak comes from a butcher, sauces are next level and the chef comes out and personally delivers your meal.

This beats any capital grille experience, the sauces are next to none, very excited about this place

John B makes some of the best cocktails in St. Pete

Loved this place, for the staff if nothing else.  Packed on a rainy Saturday night, we came in for most of the bluegrass band's set (our destination), but made enough friends throughout the night that we stayed for the hour in between, and a good amount of the jam band too. Seriously, for every beer I bought, a worker or band groupie bought me two. And that's not a usual night.

The staff were really amazing, especially Kerri, Michelle, and the woman in the "New Orleans Needs..." t-shirt, talking us up and keeping us there for hours on end. The music was cool (though bluegrass sans banjo), and the other patrons stuck to the rule on the door and uniform 'Keep your attitude at the door.' 

The menu was not vegetarian friendly at all, so we stuck to beers to fill us up, but try as we might, we wouldn't leave. Definitely one place I'll relay to friends who make it to that side of the Mississippi.

We also have a special liking for beer n' booze specials, though I wasn't partial to the one they had. My friend was, though, and fell in love with the PBR off-brand that was her mystery can and always loves Soco. The Broadway Oyster also introduced her to the local Schlafly beer, which is one she'll remember. Me? I always hope for whiskey or rum shot deals, but they don't have them on weekends (understandably).

When I go to Heaven (fingers crossed) it will be sitting on the porch at the Columns with a dirty martini... watching the streetcars pass by.
The garden district is beautiful in itself, but with a cocktail and great clientele and this porch, you just cannot get a better time.
Love the bar in the back, very speakeasy-style. Decor is old NOLA.
Highly recommended, not so much to bring your A-Game, just to relax and have some laughs while spending time in one of the most beautiful places on earth.

The fried chicken is tender and flavorful, the gumbo was pretty solid, the shrimp creole was bland for us (we had the coop's sampler), the smoked duck enchilada was very smoky (as per their in-house smoker at the back) but a bit too chewy. But damn, the biggest downer is how slow the service is - it takes 45+ minutes to get any food to come out.

Wow. Amazing seafood. 

My husband had the fish with fries. I had the pick 2- whole belly clams and fried shrimp. And spicy tuna sushi-fried!

We we're both iffy to try this place. We are from out of town and were looking for something close by. So happy we found this place. Staff were all friendly, including the manager who we spoke to before we left. We had to let him know how much we enjoyed our meals. 

The whole belly clams were a bit different. I love clams, despise oysters. These were a mix between the 2. I enjoyed them and encourage everyone to try them if you visit. 

The batter on our seafood was light and crisp. Perfectly seasoned. I just wish we lived closer.

We chose this restaurant because it was right across the street from our hotel. I wrongly assumed it was the same Abuelas as the ones in Wichita and OKC. At first we couldn't find the entrance, but once inside we found a lovely, contemporary space. This is definitely not your usual Mexican restaurant. There was a limited menu with a lot of dishes I've never heard of.  I ordered the cochinita pibil. Don't. The food and service were disappointing. We left through a side door and ended up ina dark courtyard with no exit.

Amazing. The meatballs and bread. I'm drooling thinking about it. The pasta was also good, but the meatballs and bread man, they were other worldly. Service was incredible. Wine was fantastic. Bridget Foye was there lending a hand.

I had a terrible experience here. The staff isn't reliable and management doesn't show respect for individuals or for patrons. There is one individual in particular that has no business in customer service. I watched Jamie (an employee) bite her fingernails at the bar and then serve beverages and food to customers. I observed her berate fellow employees with verbal aggressive behavior and general bad attitude and bark "just do what I say and we won't have a problem." When this employee went to three separate members of management she was brushed aside and ultimately reprimanded. I noticed there is no "employees must wash hands before returning to work" sign, which clearly wasn't implemented in this case. Jamie asked a couple "will you still eat this?" When their food went out wrong, which it goes out incorrect often and Brian is an inadequate inexperienced manager. Clearly customer service isn't the bottom line, which is unfortunate.

Party of 4 dined on Saturday 9/17, total tab between the tasting menu and 3 people with the wine pairing - over $900.  Wanted it to be a special dinner for my son and his new wife celebrating both their wedding and their birthdays. However, we were stuffed into a cramped space next to the coffee/water station in the middle of the dining room, repeatedly bumped by waitstaff as they tried to squeeze behind me - what way is this to treat a diner unless it's just about how much $$$ you can get from diners stuffed into a small room seeking a great meal?

I was expecting something memorable based on rave reviews by Vetri's colleagues and other diners but the food was just not anything exceptional.  All four of us felt the same way.  I wanted to love this place because I love Philly and this was supposed to be our flagship. 

Maybe it was just a bad night but when you're charging these type prices - $130 for tasting plus $130 or $90 for wine pairing (50% of which are so obscure (highest altitude vineyard, macerated oranges stored in clay pots for three months., blah, blah, blah) they didn't seem to have anything to do with the food and were just plain bad) you can't serve average food.  Nothing was exceptional.  

A real setback for 'fine dining'.  I'm not a restaurant hater.  I wanted to love this restaurant and give my son and his new wife an experience to remember, unfortunately we'll remember it for all the wrong reasons.

This place was horrible.  The food was bland, undercooked, barely warm, and overall horriffic. For the amount of money spent on my order and the time I had to wait for it to get done, I was disappointed in the quality of the food.  Good riddance to this place because it is obvious that the owner doesn't care about quality of his product anymore.  Thank you for leaving and do not return.

OK I have to start by saying I am a vegetarian, so of course I am excited to have a restaurant choice that is so veggie friendly. That being said it is also nice to go out to eat in a place that offers options for ALL kinds of eaters.  

This is now my go to place for lunch or dinner. Their "wasabi bowl" is one of my favorite options as well as their vegan sandwich choices. Sandwiches are served with a choice of quinoa salad, slaw, or chips. You can't go wrong with any of the sides. For the meat eaters there is a BLT, pizza, Salads with choice of meat or salmon, and daily seafood specials (just to name a few). 

GG's staff is always friendly and will do as much as they possibly can to serve all dietary needs. They are almost always busy so be prepared to wait if you are in prime hours of lunch or dinner. But trust me the wait is worth it!

I used to be a big fan of the cupcakes at Naked Chocolate, the one on Walnut Street. Then something happened -- change of ownership, mission creep, I don't know -- and the cupcakes got bigger. Much, much bigger. They also got less tasty and slightly more garish. I was sad. I stopped getting cupcakes. 

But now there are no complaints here, because now I can save up all my cupcake energy for Sweet Box. I appreciate the slightly more petite size, because they are packed with proper flavors. No powdered-sugar taste in the frosting, just a rich creaminess that is harder to get, but so worth it! They are also more complex than the average cupcake. Often it's just one note, sweet + fat. These are more delicate, more interesting -- and like I said, the perfect size. 

My only complaint is that they don't set up often enough! 38th and Walnut, please?

Swordfish was fantastic. My mom had the Parmesan crust fish ( I can't remember the name) it was delicious. I tried red snapper from my friend and it was taste too. The warm biscuit that they bring are really good. They keep bringing every time is out of the oven cage white chocolate and caramel bread pudding is wow!!!

Merchant takes itself a little too seriously.  We stopped in for a quick, to-go coffee and yogurt parfait.  Ten painfully slow minutes ticked by and I felt like I was watching a yogurt parfait making class as the staff went through the process of placing individual fruit slices around the rim of a plate, scooping perfectly shaped yogurt balls out of a tub with a fancy ice cream scooper, and then delicately drizzling honey in an artful swirl to top off the masterpiece.  I wanted to scream as I saw each new step in the complex process begin.  Come on people, it's just yogurt.  My time is far more important to me than a strawberry cut and fanned into a flower.

A must go to restaurant in Nashville! It's located in 12 south. We went on Sunday night for dinner when we were in town. Got the crawfish to start with and it was as great! The shrimp and grits are hands down the best that I've had in my life! The waitstaff was awesome- we talked with the manager for good amount of time! The building was a car wash back in the day and for sure awesome building to check out. Call ahead and make a reservation!

This place is so great. They had valet parking because that is always a chore in itself. The portions are huge so be prepared. I think almost everyone in my group had a Togo box. The sauce / gravy that comes with the food is amazing. I had the veal parm and the veal was extremely tender. The prices are actually reasonable which because this place a perfect combination of great food and great prices! You can't go wrong here

Ploy Thai is VERY hit or miss for me. There are day days I go in and it's spot on and then there are others where I wonder why I go in at all.

Now, I've never been in for dinner so I can't speak to that, but the lunch portions are fairly priced and taste pretty darn good on their good days.

I order mine "Thai hot", but I need the spice rack in addition as it never really comes out with any spice at all. AT ALL. 

That said- the duck soup lunch special ($8.95) is THE BOMB EVERYTIME.

Good, cheap coffee in an airy, big-windowed, marble-tiled establishment. Stopped by for a refuel after po-boy overload after yesterday's Po-Boy Preservation Festival on adjacent Oak Street. Great place to linger with a cup and a paper.

I'm a little scared after reading about the cockroaches (did I miss them?! ew!) ..but I just didn't have the same experience at Selam!

I'll agree that the injera is a little different. Maybe they're trying to cater to a less adventurous crowd? In any case, it's  not as..well..sour-ish as other bread I've had. It's much milder and maybe even blander. That said, it sops up the food perfectly and is tasty!

I won't do a play by play of what we ordered (working lunch with the boss & several co-workers), but it was all really tasty and filling. 

It was also really nice being able to share a meal with my boss, since she's gluten free. Injera is made of teff and people with Celiac's etc can it without worry!

4 four people, multiple dishes..and we still had leftovers which were a tasty lunch the next day!
The sandwich was fresh and delicious with the right flavors.  The pho was flavorful and had plenty of fresh ingredients and healthy portion of meat.  Yum!

My husband and I stepped in for a quick drink. They were so good that we ended up having a couple different ones each. We also tried their spicy wings and bruschetta. Both were excellent. To top it all off, the atmosphere is amazing as they have a great outdoor patio. I'll be excited to come back for a full meal soon!

This was our second visit and we may not come again.  First of all, they did not have our reservation and they also lost the reservation we had made for Mother's Day Brunch, so I made it again.  When we arrived for dinner, we said the people we are meeting will be arriving soon and please bring them to our table.When that couple arrived, the hostess told them we were not there and sat them outside. Until we finally called each other, we were sitting in separate areas unaware that the we were both there.  Servers from each area gave us different "specials" for the night.  Service was very slow and the meals were mediocre.

We went here for dinner and the food was delicious! I had the kettle chips without meat and they were amazing! It was piled with toppings and melted cheese! So good. I highly recommend it. I loved their bbq sauce that they used too. I had kettle chips at another restaurant, but I liked how Luke's kettle chips melted a lot of cheese on top. We also ordered the cheese curds and it was SO GOOD! I love how lightly battered the curds are and I liked the dipping sauce it came with. I highly recommend getting them. My friend got the margherita pizza and she did not like it. Everyone else got other food and it was all good! I definitely recommend this place! 

Oh- and they also were super accommodating on giving us separate checks! There were 7 of us but we were paying separately. Make sure to ask when you order so the waiter knows ahead of time! He also was able to split the 7th person (the bachelorette) on all of our 6 checks which was awesome!

Smooth latte! Love that it doesn't need a lot of sugar to mask the bitterness. Great open space inside that doesn't have the same cramped seating as a typical coffee bar. Also thumbs up for the super sized choc chip cookies with flax and oatmeal for my kids. Always nice to sneak healthy ingredients into a treat.
The food here is average to good, but we were treated very rudely. It happened before, but we gave it another shot. Four women will not return

Changing my 5 star review to 1 star. Terrible reservation system and customer service experience. I have been here several times without an issue and love the restaurant and usually the experience. I called yesterday for a reservation and was able to get one for 6pm. We show up at our reservation time and they all the sudden can't find my information in their reservation system. They question if i called another restaurant by mistake, i pull out my phone and show the number i called to confirm that i wasn't mistaken. They confirm that's the phone number to their restaurant. Instead of apologizing and trying to accommodate for THEIR error. They say they wouldn't be able to get me in til after 10. My issue with this is that i shouldn't have to face the consequence of an employee's error. I show proof that i called the correct number for the reservation, accommodate me for your error. Not that difficult. Don't tell me there's nothing you can do because your technology failed or the person taking reservations yesterday put me in wrong. Whatever happened was your fault not mine. Someone please make this right so i can enjoy coming here again. Otherwise you've lost a customer for life.

Little diner in the heart of Philly! We loved this place, traditional diner food was fast, service was GREAT, food was good. I had a interesting plated eggs benedict it was in a small iron skillet and was a healthy amount! Everyone was so nice and helpful!!

So we were the first customer of the day with one person behind us. We ordered the chipotle chicken quesadilla, roasted poblano quesadilla without pico, a kids chicken taco, and kids quesadilla. Roughly 30 minutes later, we got our food... some of it... and my wife's had pico. 
They took back my wife's to redo it. I also had to go ask again for the guacamole and sour cream I had paid for. About 5 minutes later, the food rearrived, as well as my daughter's taco. 
My chipotle chicken was more like a salted Dobie sponge with not even a hint of chipotle. At least the guacamole was good. My wife's roasted poblano may have seen a roast once, but it was not. 
After this meal, I feel terrible, because this was our last lunch date for the summer. From now on, we'll stick with Mercado.

This restaurant used to be the old "Chopstix" but recently underwent a change in ownership. I normally come here when I'm craving seafood because most of the seafood (lobster, clams, fish, and shrimp) here are kept fresh. I don't particularly like their dim sum as much as the old place but their normal order off the menu dishes are delicious.

Plan to Save Room for Tiramisu.

I selected this restaurant for a group dinner as one of our members had an allergy to shellfish and was concerned about a reaction if we dined at one of the many seafood restaurants.  We were seated in the back of the restaurant in the wine rack area which gave us a sense of privacy.  Our server was very pleasant even when we let him know we'd need separate checks.  I can't speak to what everyone had, but I can tell you that everyone was very happy with their meal and all plates were empty. I had a glass of wine, the lasagna and tiramisu for dessert.  Both were heavenly.  I highly recommend this restaurant for a great meal at a reasonable price.

I don't think this is the kind of pub to write home about. There were a lot of things I didn't like about this place. The cole slaw was too peppery, the honey mustard was oddly stringy, my mom got the sliders and they came to her without the buns pulled apart.
Behind us was a painting that looked like some food had been splattered on it and never wiped off, so it dried there. There was also some tape left on the wall from multiple banners hung that they were too lazy to take down!
Not gonna come back to this one.
If you've been to a Midtown, you've been to them all. They have decent food and service. This one also has fountain soda. Yay.

Super yummy. Really friendly staff. It's comfortable inside too, big booths for the whole family! The salsa is always really good. And their guac is AMAZING. I love their tacos but my husband loves their fajitas. Yum yum!!

Went to pick up dinner and when I arrive and picked up food was over charged for the whole Bill. The online food menu is really half the price and then they add it once you order it on your card. Reporting to BBB beware! Also food serving was small and still can't believe they are even open. 

I even tried to settle it nicely and she then said online price can be different then other prices she was all over the place. #badfood #badservice #closedownbadbusiness
The Fountain was a stop after Pappy's for a cool quencher to that great BBQ. Their home made ice cream was tasty and did the trick. Well worth a visit.

DISAPPOINTING! I was in Santa Barbara for the weekend and stopped by hoping for a great breakfast. The food was only okay and the service no better. It took WAY TOO LONG to get served and everyone in the place was complaining about this. It took at least 40 minutes for our food to arrive.  It took another 10 minutes to get a Latte. All in all it was certainly not worth the $20.

Disgusting and poor quality: 
pork in the vegetable roll (I don't eat pork and it wasn't listed as an ingredient).

seaweed salad tasted rotten. 

sushi rolls over stuffed and completely disgusting. poor quality, poor taste, bad flavor combinations. 

Edamame over cooked and no salt even though it was requested.

none of this is eatable.

Excellent hummus and falafel...
Very good and always fresh. 
The sandwiches are excellent....

All I can say is wow.  In terms of tapas and sushi places this place is on point. Upon entry I sat at the bar and bartender into introduced himself to me with a firm handshake told me his name and asked mine.  The beer is all local crafts on draft (which are excellent).  The menu is on the trendier side of sushi and tapas.  I had a roll, the Donald tacos, and the filet mignon over potatoes and black eyed peas.  Everything was made to perfection and was in front of me within minutes.  The manager (guy in the suit) asked me how I was doing a few times and made sure everything was going smooth.  This place is a five star joint hands down!

We ordered burgers, truffle fries and Mac and cheese, all the food was really good only downer was the Mac and cheese was bland it was ok but wouldn't order it again the truffle fries were amazing and the service was really good and personable

So disappointing. This location recently went "corporate" and the quality has decreased enough for those of us who were regulars to start bailing. My last visit included watching the kitchen cut open bags and pour soups and dips into bowls and serve. I don't think I had ever seen them use the microwave as often as they did that night. Not sure if we'll go back. Such a bummer!

Good God Almighty! I was really hoping the "Executioner" heat level was the perfect step up that I needed from the "Stop Drop and Roll". SDR heat was awesome but not quite got enough for me. I'm a chili head so rarely is anything hot enough for me so the average spicy lover would probably be content. 
Well I just tried the Executioner level whole wings and it's not a step up in heat; it's TEN friggin steps up.  I've never found anything that I couldn't eventually eat despite sweating, tearing up, and burning pain but after one bite I was all done!! I'm hoping that somebody just made an accident today and tripled the pepper power cause there ain't nobody that could eat that. For a point of comparison I would give the usual SDR level about a 7 and in today's case Executioner would be a 12. I could smell the pepper when I put my order in the car. Even if it wasn't inedible because of the heat level, the flavor sucked. Way overpowered by the pepper power to the point the chicken wasn't good. It was also over fried which is a common problem here. (I try to specify "light fry") But when they are on their game there is NO other hot chicken placethat can touch Big Shakes. 
I guess I got two wings that will be thrown away.  Thank goodness I at least got 2 SDR that I could eat. I would have bet $1000 there ain't nobody that could have eaten the wings I got today! I dont care how bad ass you think you are.  
BIG SEAN, you got to put a heat level b/t SDR and the E if this is truly how it's gonna be every time.

Would highly recommend visiting here to try a variety of foods while in PA. I flew in from San Fran and loved this place. So many different places to try! Will definitely be coming back to try some more delicious food and drinks!

This was one of the worst dining experiences I've had in recent memory. It took over half an hour to take our drink order, and longer for our food order. The food was dry and below average, and dinner with an appetizer for two, with two sides and a drink each cost us $180. I'm shocked, disappointed, and logged into Yelp just to write this review.

I used to frequent Bar Louie when I lived closer to the Gulch.  Recently I went in after a City Council meeting for a date and it will be the last.  We ordered drinks an appetizer and entrees.  I ordered a double Hendricks and Tonic and my date ordered a Jamison and Ginger Ale.  My double was made in a lowball glass.  When I asked why I was laughed at as though I was crazy.  A double is a double...two drinks.  My dates drink ended up being Jameson and Carbonated water.  Our entrees came...Mine came out fine and theirs had a nice long hair in it.  

We were given a crap apology and a bill for our entire meal.  I went ahead and paid it and I will not return to Bar Louie.  This isn't the first bad experience but it was certainly my last.

Probably will be the last time I order from here. The stuffed cheesy bread was basically raw dough when it arrived to my house and the hand tossed pizzas dough was so thin in the center it was almost non existent and although the pizza itself was cooked more it still had undercooked dough as well. Tried speaking to a manager at this location and all they wanted to do was send a gift card. I will more than likely not order from this location ever again. Wouldn't refund my order either. Waste of money on food that could not be eaten. And no that is not cheese in the photo it's RAW dough.

NEVER SUPPORT THIS PLACE!  IF I COULD GIVE ZERO STARS I WOULD!

First of all let me say I live a block away and have been in here several times as a repeat customer.   Last night, I was treated the absolute worst as a customer I have ever been treated anywhere in my life.  I ordered two slices of pizza.  Apparently that was a huge mistake.  I sat down to wait for my pizza, and a few minutes passed until they called me up and gave me my total: $7.45.     

This was quite confusing to me, as a slice from Uncle Nicks is usually $2.50, so I replied to the server questioning the total, who had a difficult time speaking English.   I felt for the guy, but we were having trouble communicating so I bent down and tried to check out the screen to see the breakdown and figure out how my total was so much, but I don't have very good vision so it was difficult.

At this time the owner chimed in.  

Owner:  "What's the problem?"
Me: "How is it $7.50 for only two slices?"
Owner: "what do you mean? What's the problem?! Is that a lot?!"    *getting a slightly irritated tone with me
Me: "um... Well yeah, how is two slices that much money?"

It's at this point that he told me I ordered three slices, which i contested and told him i only ordered two, which he argued back and forth with me three to four times, as if I didn't know how many slices I ordered when I clearly only ever wanted two slices, getting increasingly rude with me, then started all out SCREAMING at me to get "take my fucking money and get the fuck out of his store", getting up in my face in a rather violent manner, which I can only assume to be the behavior of someone who does a lot of cocaine or other hard drugs.  I even tried to shake his hand and apologize and tell him I wasn't trying to be a dick or anything like that, but he wasn't having it.

As I was leaving I even heard him call me a "fucking faggot" on my way out.   Pathetic.

Absolutely INSANE response to a simple miscommunication and quite frankly COMPLETELY inexcusable behavior for ANY worker to treat a paying customer, especially the OWNER of the restaurant.

As if this isn't bad enough, I told my friend who lives in the neighborhood about what happened and he told me one time he tried to order delivery, it took an excessively long time to get there so he called in to ask how it was taking so long when he only lives 4 blocks away.   The owners response?  "Oh you only live floor blocks away?  Walk."    And then hung up on him.

People like this should not even have a job let alone be allowed to run a business.

Sushi selection is pretty decent. Portions are good and quality of food great.

We had a few different rolls for dinner and thoroughly enjoyed them. 

There's a bit of wait if you come later so be sure to leave plenty of time. Seating indoors and outdoors is quite small.

If you are hungry inside the c terminal this looked like the best option and the pizza was really good. One problem it's expensive for pizza but big enough for an adult and kid to share so there is that. I would eat here again if I was back at the terminal but the price

Cheap and delicious. The pork soup dumplings are by far my favorite item on their menu! They're juicy and flavorful, the best I've had in Chinatown. Also a BYOB! However, it must be said that the quality has diminished since their popularity has grown. I find that the soup dumpling skin is not nearly as thin as it used to be, and their other dishes are often inconsistent, too salty or too bland. 

Unfortunately, the service here leaves something to be desired. I always have to remind the servers of missing entrees, and it is clear that they are drastically understaffed. The last time I tried to come here, they actually locked the door to prevent more customers from coming in! While I respect that they were not in a position to take on any more tables at that time, I also find it incredibly rude. 

Until I find a comparable soup dumpling place in close proximity, I will return. But if one appears, Dim Sum Garden will definitely lose my business.

Memphis is still in the upper echelon of beer bar in Philadelphia, but newcomer competition and Memphis' ironclad management have dropped the place down a notch.  

Things I still like: Great beer, honestly some of the stuff here isn't available anywhere else in the city.  Great brunch.  Nice outdoor space.

Things that bring it down a notch: Ever increasing beer prices (especially now that tax is not included).  No prices or pour sizes noted for drinks (I should not be asking the bartender for this information).  Menu is small and does not change too often, so if you are a regular you may get a bit bored.  Cash only outside, as well as a separate menu and drink list with no cross over allowed. 

I still like what Memphis does, but it is now my 3rd, 4th or 5th choice when it used to be an unquestionable first choice.

Best hot dog I ever ate in my 65 years!  Had the pleasure of this meal, and it is a meal, at an outside flea market in Tucson last weekend. Great guys making great dogs. My group had four different dogs, all of them Excellent ! Don't remember the name of dog I ordered but it had bits of Perfectly grilled home fries, onions, "grilled cheese" and bacon, good bacon! Top of the line bacon!  Thanks guys, I'll be back!
The food, decent; the service, poor: the owner or the manager.
OMG!!! Best pizza next to my New York Pizza. Cuz that's where I'm from!! Wings are great!!! Joint is jumpin!!!! A+

We visited Roxane after a night out with friends at Cardwell's.  I guess it's one of the only late night bars in Clayton.  It wasn't that busy, and they had moved the tables out of the dining area to make room for dancing.

Oh how I tried to refrain from singing the Police song with the same name.  But liquor took over, and I belted it out for no reason.
The food is consistently delicious and fresh! I love their Teriyaki Tofu Poke bowl. Husband loves the Salmon Poke Bowl w/ house sauce, and my kiddo loves the shrimp hibachi w/ noodles. It's all good!

Randy and Tina Van Osten run a great little shop. Mostly geared towards kids, but perfect for lunch and a cup, of tea especially!
That is, if you don't mind a crowd.

Service was quick as usual and the tables were clean. I always like munching on the peanuts while I wait (not that the wait is too long). 

You can get your burger the way you want it. Any toppings available. The burgers can get quite but sometimes. Fries. Order the small or you will have a huge paper bag of fries OMG.

Some would say I should have known a pancake house hamburger and fries would not be a good choice. I am staying at a hotel that has a Ihop attached. 
I returned to the restaurant 32 minutes after picking up my order for a missed beverage. The cashier initials L.P. at store #3119 5:42pm, who actually gave me my original order, acted as though I was trying to get a free $3 unsweetened ice tea. when she finally brought my drink 12 minutes later, it was a small. She stated, "I don't know what you got." despite having provided the kitchen ticket and offered my electronic receipt from my online ordering app.
mediocre burger with terrible service.

Very nice experience. The restaurant itself is beautiful and has old time wall paper plastered on the wall which I thought gave it a nice vintage and authentic feel to it. The staff was great and the food came out very quickly. The gumbo is delicious of course but it does have a strange consistency to it, almost stringy. Aside from that, everything was great and the jambalaya was definitely a must try. The daiquiri's were yummy and I like that they're freshly blended with real fruits. A little too light on the alcohol though.

Staple of the new Fountain Square restaurant scene. The menu is varied but heavily tilts toward English pub food. Chips (fries) and curry sauce are a great way to start your meal. I like their English dishes the best but had this amazing Chicken Pot Pie with a flaky crust and creamy filling. Ultimate comfort food for a cold night.  Pair that with a Smithwicks or Guinness and you are in heaven!

Nice neighborhood bar that fills up quickly. Menu is interesting and the wild boar tacos are great. I have never had an entree here just bar snacks. The draft list rotates frequently and can be hit or miss. Kind if off the beaten path if you do not live in that neighborhood.
Great Ambiance, great food and great service!! I would go back in a heartbeat!!

I order from this place all the time! Sometimes delivery can take a while but that's to be expected during weekends from a popular Chinese/sushi restaurant. Highly recommend pickup if possible.

Items to definitely try: hot and sour soup, spicy tuna roll, any of their specialty rolls, and the bbq boneless spare ribs. 

Staff are always courteous and friendly on the phone and in person. Great place!

Deliciously delicious.  Our breakfast was the best meal of our trip! The service was excellent too.  Smokehouse and the cinnamon french toast were what we had, but every plate that went by looked awesome.
Yummmmy!!! Biscuits melt in your mouth and bacon very delicious and not fatty! Coffee is rich, not bitter. The service was amazing with friendly and accommodating...thanks for being outstanding!!
Ordered food from 12000 miles away for someone!! And they loved it.. i am so happy. Keep up the great work!!

Do not go to this place for a shrimp poboy. These were the smallest most flavorless shrimp I have ever had. I couldn't even finish a third of the sandwich because they shrimp were fried too hard and they look like dried shrimp when I took the batter off. A complete waste of time and money. I wish I could give no stars. I spent $11 on something that was inedible. If you want batter on French, this is the place. If you want fresh actual fried shrimp, try some place else. Sorely disappointed! Not what I expected at all.

I want so much to love Diablo. The wall-mounted Vespa, gregarious owner, and wide open world-facing windows beckon hipper-than-thou downtowners. The uber casual jackbooted servers are sweet and attentive. I like the grilled muffin texture of these signature burgers, but my veggie pattie literally disintegrated into an unwieldy mess. Maybe I ask too much from masters of ground beef, but the quality of a veggie burger speaks volumes about the nature of a restaurant these days. The fries were inexplicably chopped into mini shoestring micro niblets, and if I'd had a fork I might have managed to get a decent bite for dipping. They were sodden as well, and off color. My partner's med rare burger was on the red side, although he managed to polish it off with aplomb. The hanging lights along the front windows glare like operating room spots - I don't need to look at anything this closely. I'll be back, but would like to see a few adjustments.
Perfect spot for a drink with colleagues and friends. Happy hour wines are very good. Walking distance to businesses in downtown. Beautiful decor and friendly staff. Love it!!

First visit so I tried two sandwiches.
  Reuben - 4 stars.  I liked this a lot. Real corned beef (!) on marble rye, good sauerkraut, not enough dressing. Would love to have an XL option with double the meat.
  Satchmo - 2 stars. I was very surprised that I didn't like this. It looked good and smelled good but I didn't care for the taste.
  Service - 5 stars. Super nice people. 

I'll be back.
Worst service. Waiter way overworked. Food was awful. Canceled our entree and hated the oysters. Would never recommend

Came here yesterday to study and use the wifi and even with all the bad reviews I decided to come to this one over my usual spot in Soulard as it is closer to my daughters school. It was packed on a Tuesday around two. Hard to find a seat that didn't seat more than 2 and had an outlet so that was the only downfall. I had to use my phone for the internet because I couldn't find a seat with an outlet to plug my laptop in but that was okay. As always the iced green tea was amazing!! I don't really like the set up of the parking lot as it was a bit confusing and not much parking but more than the Soulard location. I love sitting outside but it was way to hot and the sitting outside was sub par. I like the Soulard outdoor seating 100% more. I will come back though is I ever am running out of time and need to be close to my daughters school. All in all not a horrific experience but not an amazing.

I took friends from out of town on a Saturday morning. I anticipated a line and a long wait. I was pleasantly surprised. Within 10 minutes we were seated in the front dining room and had coffee served.
Everyone ordered something differ not and we all shared to make sure we had the full Biscuit Love experience. We all left full and happy.

Just had brunch at the Mercer for the first time in too long. This place is one of the best kept secrets in Philly. All the food is freshly made with fresh ingredients. The place has a very local vibe and you feel right at home there for breakfast or lunch. There is never a huge wait, no pretentious hostesses, servers, or design just amazing food. Standouts include bottomless La Colombe coffee, crab and asparagus omelette, their famous mascarpone and berry french toast, egg & cheese on a fresh crossant, and the best eggs florentine I have ever tasted. This place is truly a gem and the perfect cure if you have had one too many the night before.

Chickie huh what? Attempted to go on multiple occasions because of proximity to my hostel, but was met with 8- 15 $ cover prices. Awfully steep when all I wanted was a bite to eat and a couple of beers. Cool graffito near the restaurant with my name.
Food was good. Server had good personality but was not terribly attentive. Had to ask for every water or coffee refill we needed.

First time for me when it comes to Jamaican cuisine.  I ordered the Jerked Chicken, and it was so good.  It has a nice smokey flavor with some nice heat.  I ate everything on my plate.  Definitely give this place go when your in the mood for Jamaican cuisine.

I've ordered delivery through total takeout here before but this was my first time dining at the restaurant.  Other than the girl at the table beside me talking way too loud it was a good experience.  We sat outside which was nice right by the water.  It was one of the first nice evenings of the year so very relaxing (minus the loud girl).  The complimentary pita and seasoned oil was a happy bonus you don't get with delivery so a good surprise.  The whole menu sounded delicious and it was hard to choose, but everything we got was very good.  I highly recommend the feta fries!

'Big Food' was the comment from my family. And that it was. The burgers were huge! They were tasty and my California Cobb was great. The nachos were mediocre. For the 4 of us, our bill was over $70 plus tip, with no alcohol. So kinda pricey for best part to be 'big'.

Most things are vegan, and dishes are creative, delicious, and affordable. Lovely wine selection too. I would go here every day if I could and just work my way through the menu. Love the white interior with the colorful pillows, well designed and cozy. They use stainless steel straws, so cool! And they have veg chicken. Hope I am back in this city soon.
Great stop for lunch. Staff was super friendly. Got the seafood nachos which were good, but next time I'd get something else 'cause the food looked incredible.

We had such high hopes - but not at all what we expected. A friend recommended this place. I followed the Brickwall on Facebook this summer and saw the great drinks and specials. Finally we made the 20 min drive to check it out and I wish we hadn't. Cool atmosphere. Friendly waitress but not much knowledge of the food on the menu. We had some drinks - they were fine. We ordered clams - they were out of them. I found the menu very overpriced for a bar and for this area. We had a cup of very watery clam chowder ($6). We ordered the shrimp taco's ($16!) It came with three of the teeniest tiniest tacos I've ever had in my life (about 4 inch round soft shell)! They each had 3 small shrimp and some slaw. It came with a tiny bowl of bland cold undercooked rice. The entree was the size of an appetizer. Although tasty - it was not $16 tasty. We also had the Filet Mignon sandwich, again tasty, again such tiny portions. When our food was delivered it was borderline funny how small everything was.  It, no lie, looked like a slider bun. With a ton of potato chips! --- ready --- $20! for a sandwich the size of a slider and some potato chips!!!! We agreed it was a one and done visit but beware that if you are hungry, this is not the place to visit. So disappointed!

Hey, we get the shrimp grilled or some of the house specialties and manage to get there as often as possible. Decent tequila selection. Good salsa. Good margaritas, plus No waiting to get in, plenty of parking. A plus. Side patio, with outdoor seating. Not too fancy, not too fast, so you don't feel rushed...but feel full and happy.

I recently had the best customer service experience here. Our waiter Damon treated us and all the other tables near us exceptionally well. He was very attentive and gave us suggestions that fit our needs. He is the best waiter I've ever come across in all my years. He made it a pleasure to come there.

Stopped by after a shopping at Soft Surroundings a few doors down. Spent 10 min waiting for Ashley the bar server to acknowledge me. There were dirty dishes from prior customers next to me and the counter for both my seat and adjoining seat were covered in something sticky. 
Ashley spent the 10 minutes chatting with a customer. She came over and i asked her if she could wipe the counter. She begrudgingly did then handed me sticky menus.  I informed her they were sticky and asked for new ones. She shoved another one towards me to use - all this while not saying a word. Never saw her again. LOL. I guess this passes as service. We left. There used to be terrific front of house people there. Vastly different and dirty. Bring some Purel. Mike and Cornelius, (the managers) should do something.

Let me just say right off I'm not a fan of this chain. My wife and I tried another location and weren't impressed. Between the goofy yelling "Welcome to Moe's!" as you walk in, the school cafeteria setup, and the bleh food there was no real reason to go back again. 

However this was another location and I was starving after a couple hours shopping at Lowes. I was by myself and in the mood for some tacos. Not enough time to go do Don Pablos, and hoped to do better than the Taco Bell. 

So I pop into this location without high expectations. Just want some chips and a couple tacos. 

Thankfully, no one yelled at me when I walked in. I don't know if they quit doing that or just didn't feel like it. Fine by me. 

The first thing I noticed was the appearance. Dirty tables unattended and no one in an apparent rush to clean them, and they weren't cleaned in the time I was there. It was the slow part of the afternoon and there were people standing around. I should have walked out but I was really hungry and too tired to care. 

In line you could see the work area was a mess & they had no control of the work space. Doesn't inspire confidence. I push ahead anyway. 

Sat down at one of the clean tables, and the food wasn't any better than the other location. You may as well just hit the Taco Bell on the other side of the mall. Moe's isn't any more satisfying and this one seems kind of dirty.

A wonderful restaurant with a wonderful family. The food is excellent. The owners are so kind and considerate that it feels like you are at a neighbors for supper. 

The interior is more like a cafe, but it is one of our favorite spots. We drive an hour away to get there. I hope as they grow it gets the recognition they deserve.

UPDATED MAY 2020: Ok ok ok I HAVE to tell you about the "revamped" menu at The Mill OH MY! We LOVED  that spot before and now  YOU MUST GO! We stopped in last night after the amazing storm and our stomachs & palates were "blown". Staff is amazing! Funny, welcoming and kind. We started with a coupe perfectly crafted Old Fashioneds. Then we pretty much ordered everything on the menu and it was worth every calorie! Yum! Some
Photos follow but here are some highlights: the "Not Yo Mama's Grilled Cheese" (wow) and the Tenderloin Frites with Duck Fries, Sherry Cream Sauce (the sauce!)* & the Roast Beet Panzanella with aged balsamic drizzled POUND CAKE Croutons (yes you read that right! OH MY!) & the beets! & the burrata! (I'm salivating again). Seriously recommend this place! They call it tapas but the servings are more generous than a taps (we finished everything except just a couple of bites of the poke (which was also amazing!) NICE JOB The Mill!  *I don't eat beef/poultry/pork so the beef & duck fries reco is via my husband and his mind was blown; said the cream sauce was outtacontrol!!!




I've  been trying to eat at The Mill since they opened 1.5 years ago but every time I looked at the menu online, there weren't enough vegetarian options so we went elsewhere. Well, I kept trying and last week the menu showed something about a trumpet mushroom entree and we were IN! Went on a Sunday night (GREAT IDEA!) we were immediately warmly greeted & seated. Our server arrived promptly and was so incredibly nice and helpful with the menu. Really nice guy just to chat with. My husband got the (special??) pulled pork hash casserole thingie and he had to totally restrain himself from devouring the entire thing and filling up before our entrees arrived. Since I rarely eat fish, I was torn between the seared king trumpet mushroom and the tuna. I got the honey seared tuna and honestly, I don't know if I've had a better piece of tuna before. The blood orange beet purée was devine! My husband had the pork tomahawk & while we expected it to be ridiculously large (too much) in size as previous "tomahawk" cuts have been dinosaur sized, this was perfect. BIG portion without being gluttonous. Husband said cooked
To perfection and savored every bite. The yucca was a great surprise side as was the street corn. Overall, GREAT spot, loved the food, the staff and oh, the decor is fabulous (look in the bathrooms!) looking forward to going back!

Yes yes yes!

Environment: I loved the open, classy, clean feel of this place. It was really nice to not feel on top of anyone here. On also love the size of the tables. One thing that stunk was we went as a large group, but had to split up the tables. But other than that it was a larger open area and the flow of servers to table was quiet nice. 

Product: LOVED IT! This is hands down one of my new favorite places. I had the devour Indy and it was an app, the meal, and dessert and I split it with someone and I was full at the end. The vegetarian tacos ( easy to make vegan. Just remove the cheese) were to die for. I'd eat them everyday if I could. 

Service: our server was very attentive and charming. He kept up on out water but didn't feel intruding. He knew she  was a good time to ask if we were okay. He was very knowledge able and accommodating for my vegan friend!
Lobster cheesesteak was amazing, The Cheesesteak was good but the creamy lobster on top just finished it off. Crabfries were seasoned well, and you just crave more of it as you eat more of it.
The BEST Burritos. My go to is the Sausage Burrito, no beans, add sour cream. Their salsa is hot but goes so well with it. ALL of their drinks are great.

Mungo's is STL fine dining tucked away on the other side of the river in Illinois. Food is fantastic. If you are looking for authentic Italian dishes from a place that prides themselves on great customer service then you have found it. We will be going back again soon!
I had a horrible experience yesterday! I went to this tgi on my lunch break.  One of the employees wasn't sure at all on the food that you had! I'll never go back !! Highly disappointed!
First time eating at Flamez got the pizza half pepperoni and it's beautiful brick oven cooked thin crust delicious
The seafood platter was great..came out hot! However, the oysters had shells and the poyboy' s bread was too thick and dry.. The service was nice and the rest of the meal was okay!

Fantastic little family run place. We came in after church around 11:45 am and even though we were past the breakfast time on the menu, they offered it anyways! The corned beef hash was homemade. The waffles were fluffy (chicken and waffles were excellent). I am excited to be back again soon!
What a great GastroPub. Great SERVICE imcredible food. Jeff is amazing. What,a great place, totally reccomend!

God is this place random. Please don't be thrown off by the fact that you need to drive down into the lot of a nearly abandoned children's amusement park to get to their establishment. I came here on a Sunday with my family for lunch and am glad I didn't let the scenery scare me away. Although the food took quite a bit of time from ordering to delivery, (say 30 minutes and we were the ONLY people in the place) - it was well worth the wait. I can tell that they make everything to order which is hard to find! I ordered the veggie burger (for all you vegetarians and vegans out there) as I believe it was the only item on the menu my diet allows me to eat. Despite the fact I didn't have many choices - it was delicious - black beans, onions, fresh herbs and spices, coconut milk on a housemade bun (the bun alone made it worth it). 

Will I be back? YES. My only suggestion - don't go when you are starving as the food takes some time to be prepared and bring a good friend because they weren't playing any sort of music or TV shows while I was there (insert the noise of crickets chirping in background)...

I would have ate here, but the owner acted like a total douche. If your customer service isn't there, then your food is irrelevant.

Go to Jumbo and Delicious a couple doors down.

Was in town for work and wanted food without leaving my hotel. Ordered on Grubhub despite a handful of negative reviews, and was pleased with both the quality of the food and the speed of the delivery. The double hamburger was substantial, and customization was easy. The Philly cheesesteak was a little smaller than I expected, but delicious. Onions rings were a bit cold, but that's to be expected with delivery. The driver brought the food directly to my room on the 4th floor. Would definitely order from them again.

We ordered Uber Eats, and the driver arrived and they cancelled. They repeated this three times. Waited for almost two hours. Attempted to call the store on four occasions over that time. No answer. Went and ordered in person the next day. Staff standing around out back on their phones. Didn't notice we had placed an order. Order was cold and wrong.

Two star review only because the takeout refrigerated and reheated was much better as far as the inside and initial quality of food is pathetic to put it nicely me and my girlfriend dishes both combine for $36 the price of the food is ridiculous when you consider how terrible the food was but that all being said the lady up front was nice and polite

Great experience all around from the wine, food, atmosphere to the service. Amber was absolutely fantastic. She made our dinning experience one we will remember. We will definitely be back, and are now members.

Kojaks was recommended by a friend. It was a great recommendation. At our table of six all all of Kojaks meat options were represented. I had the ribs. They were meaty and smoky, but not overpowered with smoke. Nice smoke ring present. They are served dry and 4 homemade sauces are available. The chopped pork and chicken is cooked and served wet in their custom sauce. The pulled pork is served classic style, no sauce. I didn't have the brisket but my wife did. She loved it. I sampled it and it didn't fail to please. 
The great food doesn't stop at the meat. The sides deliver as well. Cole slaw is one of those foods that is either good or bad, rarely is there an in between. Kojaks slaw is AWESOME! The parsley potatoes are tender and buttery. The baked beans are hit as well. 
Don't pass up on the sangria. 
Finally, the service was awesome. Super friendly and knowledgeable staff. Very attentive.

Good food. Excellent selection.  Everything seemed fresh.  Service is sloooooooow.   Like old people driving in the fast lane on Sunday slow.  The waiters all seem to be Korean k-pop d listers who just do not give a shit about much of anything.  Well.  I guess it can't all be a win.
Lamb chops are the only thing I come here for. So freaking good! I always have a tummy ache though when i leave

This place is my go-to on the bench for Vietnamese; I'd recommend it to anyone looking for an affordable bite. Most reviews have hit the positives well enough. I'm taking one star off because the tables are left a little dirty at times, and the pho lacks some common options.

Impressive decor and super comfortable and chic inside kimmel center. We had the prix fixe which includes first, second and dessert. The hamachi was really balanced with acidity except it was very very salty. Halibut was perfectly cooked. And I love the black sesame panna cotta except the yuzu ice cream was melted. I love the open kitchen. What I didn't love was the chefs on their phone texting and looking at their phones in the open kitchen. It was a slow night after 8pm on Saturday. But c'mon...please don't look at your phone in the open kitchen and then go back and prepare the food.

Do not waste your time and money here! I have never experienced such rude management and poor service in my entire life, especially for this price point. Starting with the snobby/arrogant hostess who would not let us be seated in a group of more than 6 or to occupy the bar space because it was against covid protocols, as it only had six spaces. But, an hour later we go inside to see 12 people at the bar and a table of 7 having two tables pushed together. I am fine abiding by health and safety protocols and would not have a complaint if they didnt blatantly lie to us, while violating it to serve a different "class" because it would mess up their "flow". Also, after someone had canceled and our party was then 6, we were seated outside and they forgot one chair and wanted 3 people to squeeze onto a love seat bench. But after much protest they gave us another chair without a cushion and when asked they refused to provide one, even though there were at least 7 other empty tables with chairs. I am still appalled by this experience and recommend anyone to look elsewhere in the city for an upscale experience worth the money.

Worst service 
Every time, anytime.
Got to be the worst  Subway ever open in all of the world.
Where ever they hire their employees, it must be the true bottom of the barrel minimum wage people. 
Rudeness and incompetence must be part of their training regimen!!!!!
I only gave them one star so I could write a review.
Yelp needs to add negative stars then they would count for maybe 130,000 negative stars.
Whoever owns this location should just go ahead and close.

Being from San Francisco (where there are Filipino restaurants at every corner) I am very happy to have this new place opening up fairly close to where I live.  I passed by during Sunday Brunch to have Lumpiang Shanghai and Sinigang.  The food was great and the people working there were very nice and attentive.

I'll be adding Filipino Fusion Bar and Grill to my rotation of place to go
Always incredible snacks and bevs. The vibe lets me pretend I'm in old New Orleans and the balcony is my fave.
Literally everything I've had from Chiquitas is absolutely delicious. They blow some other well known south Philly pizza joints out of the water.

I went there yesterday to get the veggie delight. The girl and the man that were waiting on me never smiled never said anything only asked what I wanted on my sandwich. This sandwich is over six dollars she put one slice of jack cheese on a 6 inch roll in the veggies I asked for.Don't go there lousy food. No customer service.
