Waited for an hour and a half for a cheese pizza. Turns out it was the second worst piece of pizza I've ever had behind a slice from a gas station. Do yourself a favor and pay for delivery from somewhere else. 

Severan, I appreciate the apology, but the sad part was I didn't order delivery. I ordered at the counter, and then sat in the restaurant for more than an hour and a half.

I was so excited to try this place out purely based on the creativity of their menu! Every item sounds absolutely drool worthy and I love the innovation on classic dishes into pot pies, empanadas, and balls. 

I ordered online and scheduled a pickup for 6:15. Unfortunately, I could not find the spinach  and artichoke empanada on their menu, although all their other menu items are listed. When I arrived, the food was waiting for me and the pickup process was really smooth. The girls behind the counter were really nice and the whole process was so easy. 

Once we got home, the food was still hot and crisp. The pot pies had little symbols on top to indicate which were which, but I wish the boxes were labeled cause it was a little hard to decipher the symbols after the baking process. I think this is a cute concept, but the meatball pie filling had overflowed a bit in the cooking process and you couldn't tell what the symbol was at all.. 

Once we dug in, everything was delicious. The empanadas were large and stuffed with a good amount of filling. I wish the cheeseburger one was cheesier, but the beef and mushroom was super flavorful and the pork and sweet potato was a surprising flavor combo with curry spices. And the sauce line up adds a little extra oomph to each bite. I really enjoyed the spicy Mayo and their pickled onions. 

The risotto balls needed a little salt, but the loaded mash balls were so dang good. Definitely the best balls that we ordered. 

Overall the food was really good, but the prices are on the higher side. It does seem like they make everything from scratch though, so you have to take that into account when you consider pricing. 

I'll definitely be back when I have a craving for that rich and delicious miso chicken pot pie again.
Like always the pancakes were great. For a Sunday late breakfast the wait time was not as bad as other times. 15 minutes to 20 minutes wait time.Service was good. This is my go to spot.

There are so many things to eat and see and buy here. I like taking out-of-town friends to this location, setting them free, and telling them to buy food until they burst. The only thing that I always forget to take into account is the hours--it's best to go around lunchtime or the afternoon, because the Terminal closes at dinnertime. In addition, it can get a little crowded, as space is at a premium here. Be prepared to maneuver delicately.

Must stop at: the Asian smoothie place near Bassett's (another must-stop). The Termini Brothers satellite shop and the Fourth Street cookie place. Also at DiNic's (obviously). Oh, and there is a great Middle Eastern place called Kamal's, as well as a fantastic creperie a few aisles away. Finally, the Lancaster merchants always have amazing baked goods (like cinnamon buns!).

Soooo goood! I love this place. It is only place that gets me to eat brussel sprouts. They have a new chorizo meatball with poblano cream. There is nothing more to say besides you need a make a visit here.

The soup I got, Autumn Squash, was very good but I had planned to get soup and salad. The woman said vaguely, "you get your salad over there". After she gave me the soup she said she would ring me up back by the cookies. When she got there she started to talk to another customer about milk options for her coffee. As she was about to go to the back about the milk, she decided to ring me up. I wasn't about to wait for the salad so I said I would just get the soup and a drink. Since this place is basically identical to Panera and I have never had poor service at Panera, I will stick with them.

Deep sigh, Macca' Grill was always a favourite of Pablo et moi, our first trip back since it reopened after the flood, it has now gone from Cut-Above to Cut-Below.  The big wide open space feels too cafeteria like, the greeter was charmless, she tried to lead us to a table with babies and children next to us, not going to work ever for this middle age couple, especially when the place is almost empty.  The menus we were handed were very grubby.  We sat at a booth in the bar and  the waiter came over, deep sigh, zombie and completely disinterested, took 10 mins to get our drinks, sodas,  then the calamari came, the recipe has changed, it was bland super dry and minus the peppers.  The portion was small.  The seafood linguine, usually a favourite was completely overcooked, shrimp were rubbery, linguine stodgy and the mussels mostly empty, the scallops a hair from overdone.  All this for $49, not very good VFM, we felt cheated...on the way out - the father from the aforementioned table was carrying one of his children out screaming damn you to him, my instincts about seating proven once more.

Cafe Audrey is a hidden Indy gem! I live close by, so we frequently go for breakfast or brunch. It's small and cozy, very family friendly  with options to sit inside or out. I love the cute coffee station with all of the different mugs. It's like getting a mug out of your own cabinet but with more coffee choices! The menu has just about everything to satisfy whatever breakfast craving you're having. The omelettes are fantastic, and definitely try the hash that comes with your order. Plates are plentiful and easy on the budget. There's so much to love about this place!

I was coming home from work last night and made.a stop. Ordered large fries. I paid my money and, when the guy was about to hand me my food, I asked for some dipping sauce. He copped an effing attitude, got the sauce, put it in the bag, shoved the bag in my face, and shut the window. When I got home, the fries were effing stale. Nasty food and a nasty business.
Wonderful place full of good vibes and excellent customer service and a short wait time

My hotel was just around the corner from this lovely cafe in the French Quarter.  While the hotel had coffee, I am a tea drinker so I ventured a few blocks away to Envie to get my day started.  Envie is a charming cafe with indoor and outdoor seating.  It has an eclectic aesthetic with some bar seating in addition to the regular floor seating.  They had a great selection of tea but since it was hot and humid I wanted to go with an iced tea.  I had a black peach iced tea and it was amazing.  It was perfectly refreshing without being too sweet or sugary.  The fruitiness was mild, which I liked since I didn't want something super sweet.

I also decided to try their breakfast and saw that they had a few vegetarian options but when I saw a Brie Croissant on the board I knew I had to have it.  It was a Brie Croissant Omelette that initially came with ham.  They were nice enough to take it off and the barista kindly asked me if I wanted something else instead of the meat such as spinach, arugula, etc.  I chose spinach and I was so happy that I didn't have to ask to have a substitute, they kindly offered it.

However, the service was better than the food.  The croissant was good but the omelette was basically dry and dominated the entire sandwich.  The brie was stuffed inside of the omelette, but its flavor was drowned out by the intense omelette that wasn't very flavorful.  It was a heavy sandwich that was bland.  There was a generous portion of hash browns and they hit the spot, I would have liked them to be crispier.  I did return here for iced tea but I decided to eat elsewhere.  Perhaps they have better items on their menu for food but I'd come back here for some Peach Iced Tea.  The barista who was working there seemed genuinely kind and thoughtful.

The Olive Restaurant. I give them 5 stars for having the strength to open a new restaurant during the pandemic. I can't wait to try the full dining experience inside. For today, it's takeout. Looking for a place to order lunch. The Olive has two menus on line. Lunch and dinner. The lunch menu had lots of great choices. 

We choose the turkey club and the chefs salad. The turkey club was big, the way you want your club sandwich to be. We missed the note that all sandwiches come with fries. Extra treat when we opened the container. The fries were very good the turkey club also very good. The chefs salad was loaded with luncheon meets. Like the club sandwich it was a big salad. The blue cheese dressing very good.

We have leftovers for tomorrow as there was no way to finish all the food they gave us. Based on the serving size the pricing is good. At the counter a very friendly server invited us back to try them for dinner. His suggestions were the chicken parmigiana with a blush sauce and the clams with a saffron sauce. We plan to order both and let you know how it was.
Everything we ordered was really good especially the curry. Will definitely order from them again.

Tonight we went to Baldini coffee shop for dinner.  After the hostess (a Hispanic lady with eye glasses) took us to the table, I tried to ask her what are the specials on weekends, she said, "Just a minute" and walked away.  We waited for 15 minutes but she never returned.  When she walked by our table again, I asked, "May I ask you a question?"  If looks could kill, I'd be dead right now. She looked so annoyed and snapped at me, "I AM VERY BUSY,  WHAT DO YOU WANT?"  

My goodness how could someone like her to be the hostess of a restaurant.......so rude and disrespectful.

Just a heads up, even though this restaurant's post on Yelp and their official website says their happy hour starts at 3, when our bill dropped, we were told it didn't start until 4. When we asked the bartender what the charges were he was unapologetic and when told that this is what their website stated replied, "well that's just wrong." It's not about the money but about the fact that there is wrong information out there posted by this restaurant and the staff there seemed unwilling to acknowledge or remedy it. There are plenty of other mexican food restaurants in the area with food on par with this and better. Go to one with better customer service.

What happened to this place??
We used to be a frequent diner here when we lived a little closer. Since we moved, we do not get the chance to get here as often. However, there is a vast difference in this place from a couple of years ago.

I will comment on my last 2 visits:
About 2 months ago:
We always sit at the counter areas. When we walked up to the first area (where pizza station is), we noticed a tray of dirty dishes and a dirty counter. Maybe people just got up and they didn't clean it yet. There was also a laptop on the counter at the far left seat. We asked for the counter to be cleaned and sat there. The lap top remained as well as the tray of dirty dishes. We were told that they ran out of bread. REALLY??? It was not until our dinners arrived that the tray was removed. I ordered something that was not on the menu. It was a FETTUCCINE WEESIE with Salmon instead of shrimp. The Fettuccine Weesie with shrimp is $18.99. They charged be an adder of $3.00 for the change to Salmon. This was ok and the dinner was good.

Our most recent visit was this past Thursday:
When walking up to the first counter area (pizza station), it seemed that someone had taken over this area. There were chairs with a jacket, laptop bag, laptop on the counter and a tray of dirty dishes. Later we found out that these items belonged to the manager. Doesn't he have an office? We did go to the rear counter area to find that it was also dirty. A tray of dirty dishes and very dirty counter that was sticky. We asked for it to be cleaned and sat down. After waiting for about 5 minutes with no one greeting us, we asked if there was a server for this area and someone came to greet us. I once again ordered the same Weesie with Salmon entree. This time when the bill came, I was charged $25.99. How could they charge me an up charge of $7.00? My check came to about $44.35. I gave the waitress a $100 bill and received back $55.00. Why would the waitress round off the change in her favor? This was WRONG! My tip did reflect this.

With so many choices of restaurants in this area, I do not see going back to Carrabba's in our future.

I'm gonna be optimistic: food was delish and waitstaff very sweet. We had burgers and fries which were great! We spent under $30 on a beer, two burgers and two sides.

I'd give this joint four stars if we had been serviced and had received our food sooner. After we were seated it took about 10 mins before we were greeted, 45 mins to receive food, but definitely no delay in getting us our check and running our cards.

We will be back after things settle in for a few months - and if things go better I'd love to give this place five stars. Lots of potential!

The people who work here are EXTREMELY rude. I absolutely loved the atmosphere and vibe of the bar but I cannot justify going back due to the extreme rudeness I encountered here. Literally every employee that I encountered, and everyone I talk to encountered, was rude. Even the bouncers. Unbelievable

It's a gastro pub with New Orleans décor.  They have a New Orleans style brunch on Sundays.  We went for dinner though and the comfort food hit the spot. We were visiting from out of town and who knew Philly would rock this down home cooking! I recommend the brisket, mac & cheese and big ass biscuits.  The beer selection is good as well.  The prices are really reasonable.  The staff was friendly and attentive even on a busy Saturday night.  The restaurant noise can get quite loud so I wouldn't recommend if you're trying to have a quiet, romantic dinner.  I can't wait to get back there.

I had a great dining experience for breakfast. Our PWBN group was served in a timely manner and the service was friendly. The open egg omelette was yummy and I liked the coffee too; plenty of fruit in the fruit cup. Great choice for a meeting on an early Friday morning in Chestnut Hill. See you next month.

Went for early dinner on Sunday 5/28.  It wasn't very busy and we got seated right away.  Service was good overall but the food took a nose dive!  We've eaten here several times over the past few years and have previously enjoyed.  This time, nothing on the menu sounded interesting at all.  My daughter ordered the Crab Grilled Cheese which was super greasy and tasteless.  My wife and I both had the Mesquite grilled lettuce seafood salad.  The lettuce was a soggy mess and the shrimp and crab were luke warm due to the warm lettuce.  Poor presentation and the seafood was mushy.  I had the Manhattan Chowder which had the texture of baby food didn't resemble any chowder I've ever had. 

I get that we were in Santa Barbara on State St. but the prices were ridiculous!  We spent over $120 for a grilled cheese and 2 salads w/ 1 beer, 1 glass of wine and a lemonade.  Was it coincidence that the only one of the 3 Pinot Grigio by the glass choices was the most expensive one and the others were sold out.

Time to check out the other restaurants and not rely on what was.

I was super excited to see the change in their hours. They are now back open at lunch. I got there a little for lunch. They had a list of about 5-6 rolls on special. Those are really a great option. The diamondback roll and baked salmon roll were awesome. All the sushi rolls I got were great. Reviews were a little mixed but don't buy the hype. Service and food were excellent on point!! We also got edamame and miso soup included so that was a plus. Very reasonable price for what you are getting. Glad to have tried this place and looking forward to getting back.

The 4-star reviews must have been the owner's friends because from a food blogger perspective, my experience here was just meh. Service was fine but food lacked seasoning. Onion rings and fries from frozen. Burger seemed small for a half pound. The patty melt was made with marble bread (what??)  with processed cheese thrown on it. Now who does that? The place lacked the warmth of-- what? A sports bar? A local restaurant? This place wants to be both and the result is no clear identity.

We stopped by this place by accident...Glad we did... They recently opened up and place was empty. We tried half of their menu - escovitch fish, curried goat, roti bread and stewed chicken. Food was really yummy, even rice and service exceptional.

Always enjoy coming here but Sarah W was our  our server tonight and she did an EXCEPTIONAL job!  EVEN MORE THAN. she made our evening memorable and fun. We wouldn't ask for any other sever, and we love this establishment! Will continue to be regulars until they OWN AND COMMAND INDIANAPOLIS FOR ALL ETERNITY!! MWAHAHAHAHAHAHA

Although it is not evident from their simple sign and exterior,
Hanjan surprises you with its spacious interior and hip atmosphere.
My favourite spot was upstairs by the fence, where I could look over the first floor
and was closer to the beautiful row of lamps they have installed over their ceiling. 
This place is like a have-it-all, it is a Korean-style cafe during the day 
and very authentic Korean restaurant/bar in the evening. (They even have Karaoke rooms upstairs!)
From their lunch menu, I recommend their tteok-galbi sliders - those patties made with Korean-style beef ribs are to die for. Their coffee (although I wasn't expecting it) was very well made, full-bodied and not overly acidic. But on warm days, I recommend iced plum tea. It's different but definitely worth trying. 
The waffles from the dessert menu was impressive as well. I tried their nutella banana waffle; the waffle was fluffier than others ones I have tried in yeg, but it was perfectly paired with the ice cream topping. The staff were very attentive to our table so I got to try the waffle when it was still very warm! I found the pricing reasonable as well. The server told me that they were soon to be open to sell liquor at night to so I am excited to go back and try more of their dinner menus!

I really didn't enjoy these donuts. They are expensive for what they are, I paid about $17 for half a dozen. They are also very dense, heavy, and slightly greasy. The denseness was similar to bread which I don't really prefer in a donut but the thing that really bothered me is that they didn't have a lot of flavor or really taste like anything. I also didn't know what the flavors were in the box because it doesn't show it on caviar. 

Maybe I caught them on a bad day, maybe I didn't. I will not be buying donuts from here again.
Very friendly service. Terrific appetizers! Their pineapple and ham pizza is a great! Especially during happy hour for only $6!

My fiancee and I had some brunch and beers while overlooking the Mummer's Parade on Broad on New Year's Day - that said, they were running a limited menu and we did show up, literally, as they were unlocking the doors to open.

I had a pair of decent beers and a similarly decent, simple burger. We split a $4.50 order of 3 deviled eggs, which we agreed was way too expensive for 1.5 eggs. Our server was noticeably busy with the holiday crowd, but still friendly and attentive. The location was perfect to watch the parade: we could see every group going by without freezing in the cold (or having to use port-o-potties).

Overall, it's a nice place for a beer and easy meal, but unfortunately, there isn't really anything over-the-top about Perch Pub.

This place is perfect for a quick snack while on the go. The sushi was servicable. Small, compact sets of two rolls in each plastic wrapper made the process very easy. The pieces were small and a tad on the bland side and the selection wasn't too great, but for a quick stop sushi joint I didn't expect gourmet sushi chefs behind the counter. I also tried the seaweed salad and was disappointed. I guess they store it in a refrigerator somewhere before its put on the shelf, because mine had a slight freezer burn taste as if it was frozen and thawed. As for the yogurt, I wasn't able to try it but the selection looked good. Different flavors and a mix and match option, plus the toppings bar was well taken care of and had all the necessary froyo toppings and then some. 

Staff of two was very friendly and the store was kept very clean. Always a plus for me. Considering I'm on the road all day, I would come back here without hesitation, if I was in the mood for sushi.  But if you have the time and money, there are better sushi restaurants in the area.

Great Pizza in the beautiful Downtown setting a  large open Free parking lot  across the street that's free on weekends. The pizza is good also the chicken wing appetizer Is great along with the salads. Daiquiris are a must try, you can even get one to go any walk around old Gretna or get a pizza and daiquiri and go sit up on the levee and watch the Mississippi River traffic.

I'm so happy to report that Burger Monger is back on our list!

For a couple of years, this was our go-to local burger spot. Dine-in or Takeout, it was always fresh, well cooked, and endlessly customizable to meet everyone's preferences. And a good value!

Then the pandemic hit, and... I'm not exactly sure what happened. We noticed the staff change entirely. Burger temps were all over the place, and a couple of times we got home to find out to-go order unappetizing. Favorite items began disappearing from the menu.

Tonight, after a few months, we gave them another try. Yes, unfortunately the Akaushi upgraded patties are still gone. But the burgers we got were fantastic! Cooked perfectly medium, abundant delicious toppings, and satisfying challah buns. The sweet potato waffle fries are a must-order side, and they were properly cooked. This is a huge relief after a disappointing year or two, and we're excited to put Burger Monger back in our take-out rotation!

I'm not sure over ever had anything less that stellar from the chefs at Peacemaker. This time, it was an off menu app that had turkey, bacon cured shrimp and some delicious sauce!! I think they called it Hot Brown. Loved it! Crawfish poor boy on every visit, hush puppies, sprouts, all were spot on. Our waiter Lucas was friendly, attentive and seemed passionate about the food! We'll be back!

We used no wait and got in almost immediately! Had to rush over in the Uber.
Really really good. The serving sizes are plenty and the customer service is awesome. You get to pick everything you want with a combination of sauce. Highly recommend.

This place used to make amazing croissants - they changed ownership some time last year and since then it's gone quite a bit downhill. Their croissants are no longer flaky or crispy, more like dinner rolls. So sad to see them go...
A decent enough Indian lunch buffet but nothing outstanding.  Really little spice in the food, especially the chicken and the goat curries.  Good service and a good price.

Went on Sunday evening and the place was not busy. Our waiter was not good!  First he did not offer us water. Then, after looking at the menu, he asked for our order, totally neglecting to tell us the specials...we had to ask him. The food was average at best. The sweet potato gnocchi was gummy and bland. Unlikely to go back.

Living in North Jersey, we were 10 min from Balthazar Bakery and never worried about good fresh baguettes. After moving to Exton, I've looked far and wide to find a decent baguette. Been here for 3 months now and could not find any place. All reviews on the web were just lies until this place. As soon as you walk in, the smell is intoxicating. You're greeted with a "bonjour" which just adds to the authenticity. Their baguettes are $3 each and does not break the bank. Nice hard crunchy exterior with soft chewy interior rich in flavor. I definitely will be back to try other items. Dont bother with other bread places unless you really like bland texture less baguettes.

I was there on a Sunday afternoon before catching a flight. I was happy that they were open, as most restaurants in the area were all closed. The service was great and everyone was friendly. I tried the baked ravioli which was delicious and a filling portion as well.    Pleasant surprise for a bar/pub.

Taco Bell is not open until 2 a.m. in the morning unless you are in a car! Taco Bell for people who want to dine inside is only open until 9: 00 PM This is why I'm only giving Taco Bell one star! Because nowhere on the app, nowhere on their website, nowhere online at all does a Taco Bell franchise declare they are only open until 9 p.m. for people who want to dine inside!

We came to Trips this morning for brunch for four at what seemed like the busiest time of day to be there (10am). This spot is busy, but the meal was well worth the short wait. The staff was kind and helpful, the coffee was delicious, and I was more than happy with my eggs Benedict. My wife had the French toast platter and was equally satisfied. We will definitely be back again during our other trips to Tampa!

Our basketball team plus parents had lunch here. While we didn't think about the size of the restaurant before we arrived, Beefy's was able to accommodate all of us (20 or so) indoors. Ordering on separate tickets is never easy but the guy who took our order did so without complaint and without mistakes. 
Food as served up quickly, (always a good thing when there are hungry teenagers involved.) I overheard several of our group compliment their meal. Milkshakes in particular were a big hit. As were the wings and garlic fries.
Spectacular meal made better by the excellent and professional service of Errol. Highly recommend!
We've been here about five times since Covid started. Never again will I go to this location. Every staff member doesn't wear mask or if they do, they don't wear masks properly.

I had been craving the gluten free lemon bars they are so yummy.  The sign outside said under new management.

This bakery has a large variety of Gluten Free items breads, soups, cupcakes, cookies, lemon bars etc. They use to have the best GF lemon bars ever. I mean the kind you would drive clear across town to get in bad weather for even if they are pricey. 

I got 4 lemon bars one for each person in my family. I couldn't wait to try them. Upon arriving home I tried one of the lemon bars. The crust was stale. The lemon curd was not tasty and way, way to sweet. Freshness is important for pastries. This is not what I drove across town for. So sad I threw them all away. What a waste of time and money.
Good not great.  Our favorite Japanese place is Kyoto, my favorite sushi place is Happy Fish.  so I guess this falls behind those in my book.

I need to know who i can speak with or complain to, to get my issue resolved and figured out. This casino has charged me $85 on my card but says "they dont have any record in their system about the transaction" so im out $85 for idk what reason. help.. and its not from a third party.. my statement says "Nugget casino" ... confused...
Wow.  This place is awesome. Best falafel, beat baba ganoush, lamb kifka... hummus (or as my friend calls it "hamas"... awesome.
Best Carne Asada tacos I've had!  The Sonaran Dogs are also a must try.  Quick service, easy in and out for lunch.

I have been looking forward to checking out Chatayee for a while! It's a big space, easy to book a reservation, and the food was great! We got the roti appetizer, and I got a tofu dish, and my companion ordered off the omnivorous menu. I just love that they have a vegan menu! It's what made me want to come, and now that I've been, really excited to come back. Great location in the gayborhood/midtown. We also got cocktails that were delicious too! Recommend.
Got food poisoning from eating here. Sharp pains, burping the taste of the food. Terrible experience.

Always the best place in town to go if you want to watch a Hoosiers basketball game, just make sure to show up early. I had the wings (lemon pepper and hot sauces) and my wife had the breadsticks and brisket sliders. The food was decent, but the service was subpar. The waitress forgot the soup I had ordered and the service was flat out slow. I'm not completely surprised by the service because when you head to Kilroy's on a Saturday for an IU game you should expect it to be chaotic since they are so busy. They do have a good selection of beer and long islands which is a plus. Overall, not a horrible place to go, just don't expect the service to always be fantastic.

Why, with their bar full,  would I not be able to sit at an empty table by the bar and order drinks ? I was informed that the bar tables on the patio were for diners only. I Guess they expected my girlfriend and I to stand there drinking overpriced drinks while there were plenty of tables empty . It would be one thing if it was a Friday or Saturday dinner rush but this was Sunday night at 8:30. We live in the neighborhood and wanted to get out on a nice night and watch the cards game but McGurks is a little too snobbish for that ! We won't be back and when people we know ask for recommendations about soulard I will say if you want friendly go anywhere but there .

Definition of a standard bowl of pho. I prefer my pho broth on the cleaner side and this pho is definitely on the more oily and dirty side which is a preference for some. In terms of meat quality, the beef balls did not quite pack enough taste. For noodles, they were a bit on the soggier side. They don't have the best ventilation either so the restaurant is moist and steamy. Overall, not very impressed but am willing to bear it if others prefer it.

I completely agree with the other reviewers- this spot is the real deal!
As you walk into the counter service setting- it looks like a hole in the wall (not as much as some other spots in the NOLA but still).  You wonder- hum, is this going to be one of the best po'boys I've eaten- and the simple answer is YES.
With all of the variety of choices of fish, shrimp, oyster, crawfish as well as non-seafood sandwiches there are options for all.
I personally had the shrimp po'boy (non fried) and I have to say the seasoning was on point.  We were actually with a group of 7 and everyone enjoyed their meal which is always a challenge right?
TIP- call ahead if you have a large party- we did wait for 25-30 minutes for food because of a large order in front of us

A Tampa standout in the local ramen scene, Ichicoro is expanding and that is great news for all Ramen lovers. Opening up in the Armature Works, think of this place as the lite version of Ichicoro. This place may be small but it was buzzing during Saturday around lunch time. Although this place is known for their ramen, don't pass up the rice bowls. Today, I decided to try out their Karaage Rice Bowl. Those tender prices of Japanese fried chicken, man, they blow all other types of fried chicken nuggets out of the water. Crispy but not greasy and flavorful but not overly salty, they provide such a good textural contrast to the rice it's sitting on. Top it off with some spicy mayo, fresh green onions, and house made pickled cucumbers and daikon radish, this is the perfect combination of flavors and textures. I just wish there was more seating and a shorter line. But you know what they say, if you want good food, follow the place with the longest line. Following your nose is a good alternative too haha

The building (from the outside) is beautiful but the decor (inside) can only be described as..godawful.? I had an overwhelming urge to rip off the recessed ceilings and the strange coiled wires around the light fixtures. Also the service: painful. Bloody Mary's: salt is an essential ingredient. Use it liberally. 

Giving it 2 stars so that hopefully it lives up to its full potential one day.

This is probably my favorite restaurant and bar in the Tampa Bay! It is arguably the best location for this type of restaurant in the entire Tampa Bay. It is in the heart of downtown Tampa across from the convention center and where the Tampa Bay Lightning play. It has a great brunch menu, one of the best bar menus period! The service is what you would expect in south Tampa! Great location to watch sports, have a few drinks on the weekend, have a date night or brunch. This place is taking over! Can't say enough good things.

Food:

Ordered the chicken sandwich - it was very flavorful and tender. The 'grilled' flavor came mostly from the bun which they put on the grill too.The fries were generic/frozen - try a different side if you go. Maybe the sweet potato fries are better. I would/will definitely order the sandwich again though - the flavor in one bite is unlike anything I've had around here! The bun could have been a little smaller for the size of the chicken. Got 5 regular wings to try as well - they were grilled and fell off the bone; we ordered plain to test the 7 different sauces. We also ordered 3 tenders to try - they were juicier/just as tender as the wings in my opinion - we'll be coming back for them + the sandwich! They have a digital soda fountain with 200 options, and beers are about $6.

Restaurant:

The grilled concept is a refreshing change from the plethora of fried chicken options we have. They shouldn't be compared against each other in my opinion. The only thing that surprised me was the ordering process. You are first seated at a table by a server, and handed a menu.  You then decide what you want on the menu, and walk up to the counter to place your order and pay. They give you cups and send you off to get your drink. The food is then delivered to your table by the server that sat you. Looking back it didn't hurt us in anyway and didn't really have any negative effect, its just different/new to me! I agree with other reviewers too - the timing of their dishes coming out of the kitchen needs some work (and we only had two people)

Being able to buy a liter of Duvel would have sold me just on its own. But then the french fries and the lentil soup (two of my favorite foods on the planet) and the fact that it feels like el dia de los muertos in here...amazing.

Another foodie friend recommended I try this restaurant. Upon hearing the name I was really confused. Biscuits Cafe? I would never in a million years think this would be a mexican food restaurant. The best thing about this place though? ...I could literally get an order of biscuits and gravy with my chilaquiles! and that is exactly what I did! 

We walked in on a Sunday afternoon for Brunch and we're seated pretty quickly. It was busy so we understood the bit of a wait for food and drinks. We ordered the chilaquiles with shredded meat, the sausage scramble, a breakfast burrito and an order of spicy biscuits and gravy. They were all huge servings and we even left with leftovers for the next day. 

The only reason why I'm giving 4 stars instead of 5 is because service could have been a bit better but that is not going to stop us from coming back because the food is delicious! 

Overall, this is a great brunch spot with delicious food and good vibe. We will be back!

The first time I went the sushi was so so, and the service was horrible.  
I was persuaded to give it another try a couple weeks ago, and I have to say...It was really great.
So maybe my first time was just an off day.  
The service was speedy and dthe sushi was really good.  Our chef was creative and made stuff that was unique and to our preferences.  
I'll be back!

I really love the food here, but the last few times I have come the service was awful. Super slow and server forgot multiple of my items. She didn't come check on us and I had many issues with not getting everything I ordered. I understand they are very busy, but it is frustrating to only get half my items.

The food are so good and fresh.  We ordered the red curry duck with rice and the chicken pai thai.  I love the curry because the sweetness and the spicyness balance very well!  Also the duck is very good!

Went here with my Mom before her work shift. There was one woman behind the counter who was working both the drive-thru and the dine-in. She took our orders which were pretty basic meals, and then we waited. And waited. We waited for about 15 minutes and they finally brought out our food, but forgot the Lobster Bisque my Mom had ordered. After another 2 or 3 minutes she brings out the bisque and it is MOLTEN HOT. It was in a Styrofoam bowl and the inside of the bowl was brown and crusty around the edges where it had been obviously scorched in the microwave. My mother ate her entire meal, and afterwards the Bisque was STILL too hot to eat. After bringing this attention to the woman behind the counter, she shrugged and said "It's always made like that." At first, I was kinda stunned, then I said "It's always served with brown crust and burn marks around the rim?" and she said "Oh, he [the cook] must have cooked it too long." Still, she offered no apology. So I continued "Ma'am if someone orders this and spills it on themselves, they're going to have 3rd degree burns. It's literally dangerous to serve it that hot." and she said "Yeah thanks. I'll tell him [the cook]." I get it, it's fast food, but c'mon...take a little pride in your work and the quality of the food you're feeding your customers. The only reason I go back to this establishment is because my Mom loves their Whitefish and hushpuppies, which is why I gave this place any stars at all.

Greatest staff of any Starbucks in the area. 

I've been going to this Starbucks for about ten years and I'm not exaggerating when I say this place has seen me grow up. They have the best baristas in the game. If you're new: they'll make you feel welcome and if you're a regular: you can be sure they'll make you feel like family. In fact, when I left for college I told my mom they would be some of the people I missed most. 

Since the location change and addition of the drive thru, new hires were made and they're the same type of wonderful as the veteran baristas. 

Speaking of the move, the place now boasts a larger, shiny, new interior (although if you roll through at a busy time you may be hard-pressed to find a seat), wonderful outdoor seating area, and the benefit of being a test location for Starbucks Evenings- a development that offers wine, craft beer, and small plates in addition to the Starbucks coffee drinks and treats (the truffle popcorn is a must-have.)

The drive thru is a great addition although, if I'm being honest, I hardly ever use it because I don't want to miss out on the great experience of talking to my baristas. 

Basically, if you're in the area, make this your go-to Starbucks and you won't regret it.
Can't really comment on the food.  Been here for an hour and still no food.  I expect more from a John Besh property.

Wow.  Wow.  Wow.  This place is doing everything exceptionally well.  Ask for Adam R for a server.  Knowledgeable, personable and a real joy.  Oh, and did I mention a FABULOUS Happy Hour.  We will be spreading the word and wish the more success.  One last thing.  Save room for Vanilla Gelato with Extra Virgin Olive Oil and Black Sea Salt.  Sounds funky but it works on so many levels.

Yeah, I like this place because it's convenient and a cheap way to feed the kids a semi-healthy meal. Where else can you feed your tweens crab legs, shrimp cocktail, steamed rice, salad, or even a vegetable stir fry for under $10. Ok, maybe they don't have as much variety as other buffets, but it is super clean and the price is right compared with going to lots of other places.

(Located inside the Harrahs Casino)

The other day my family was up in Reno for Thanksgiving weekend. Our visit here was a Japanese turkey dinner.. lol We found this place by looking on yelp of course along with my younger brother's recommendation (he is a Reno resident). 

My first thought before coming here was 'Oh great not another Benihana experience.' I was kinda surprised and enjoyed our visit here. Our chef was "Manny" who is a hispanic character and was very entertaining. This cat was speaking tagalog to my mother in-law and make jokes as he kept pouring Saki in our cups. This guy had some cooking skills to go with his jokes.

Oh speaking of Saki, if you check in here on Yelp for the first time you are suppose to get a FREE bottle with your order. I did show it to our server who indicated that she would bring that out to our table. I requested it to be warmed up.. I got it as requested. So I shared it with my father and younger brother. It tasted like it was watered down a little bit, but the cold Saki that "Manny" was squirting into our cups did not taste watered down at all and he was not shy with it at all.. At that end of the meal my mother in-law fought with me and my brother and picked up the tab.. Due to the dark lighting she did not notice that we were charged for the Saki. So Heads up everyone. 

On to the food.. My only experience with these type of places was Benihana where the flavor of the food is kind of uneventful. Not this place.. The fried rice was legit and so were the meat and seafood offerings. The showmanship of "Manny" was an added bonus.. He did this thing with an onion and squirted some flammable fluid that warmed the table. Trust me.. You could feel the heat!! 

All in all our experience here was decent. I was not disappointed with the food or the service. I did minus brownie points for charging us for the "Free" Saki though. Before I go let me leave you this heads up.. Its kind of on the pricey side!!

Sat outside on a beautiful day. Lisa, our server, was fantastic. Had a couple signature cocktails which were great. We tried the crab cake salad and turkey club on special. And of course could not resist dessert. Wonderful stop for lunch or dinner!

It's a small place so large parties may not fit.

Otherwise beware of portions, they're huge so you may have leftovers for a few days, but they are delicious. And when I say delicious I mean St. Louis Italian delicious, so if you don't like St. Louis Italian you probably won't like it.

You can order a half size which isn't mentioned on the menu.

Garlic cheese bread comes out in cast iron. Large salad easily feeds four ( if you're ordering entrees too).

I am sure you saw but it is BYOB. Which is nice because you don't have to deal with restaurants overpricing drinks, especially wine.

Even better the second time around. Tried their new prix fixe menu with the vietnamese meatballs as an appetizer while my husband and friend had the kobe beef carpaccio. All very good. Then we did the beef short rib....very tender and melts in your mouth. Of course we ended with the choc souffle which was just as orgasmic as I remembered. I was tempted to try the pumpkin mousse but why miss out on the choc souffle. The great thing about the night was that it was my friend's first night in Philly and we were talking so much we didn't realize our entree took almost an hour to get to us. The waitress apologized and the manager came to our table and said he could take off a discount off our bill. I was like well we already got the prix frixe why don't we get some drinks instead?? He offered us 2 free drinks each = total 6 and boy were we happy campers. That made our night and the food was to die for :) Can't wait for next season's prix fixe menu.

Stopped by for dinner with the family last night , and sorry to say we were greeted by the women who would be our waitress , she was informative but dry and very pushy 
seemed she wanted to up the the check amount. the food was tasty but if you are hungry this is not the place to go ,for the portions are small, the initial bread basket was served (size of a small roll) and never refilled again..nor was there an offer to not form the bus boy or our waitress there were only a few table's at the time. over priced for the size of the dishes!!  ordered a pizza afterwords! ONE AND DONE!

I stopped into town to visit a friend as I made my way to California. She really wanted to eat here so I gave it a try. Immediately upon entering we were greeted with smiles and helped to our table.

Our waitress was Amairani, she was an excellent waitress. She constantly checked to see how we were doing and always had a smile on her with the most helpful attitude. She even put up with our requests such as trying different salsas that they had. She was a big reason for the rating.

My friend got the octopus while I got the El Berraco. The El Berraco was excellent. It was so good I wish they had given me a bigger portion. My friend enjoyed her octopus as well. Both dishes were elegantly displayed and tasted as good as it looked. Next time I am in town I am definitely stopping by El Berraco again. 5- stars for this place!

This place is amazing! Came on a Tuesday afternoon so it was quiet. The bread was fresh and hot and the sauce taste amazing I never had anything taste just like it. The dishes tasted unique and authentic. Waiter was amazing and made sure we were good on refills. Atmosphere is nice, restaurant could use renovation but the flavor and atmosphere balances it out. Service was quick and definitely will be back!
Amazing food and great service!  Chef Maurice always comes out to visit and check on each guest.  Try the kubedeh and the awesome dude!

Huge portions.  Split one sandwich with one person.  The debris is the best part of the sandwich.  The Jambalaya only has sausage and chicken, not the Holy Trinity.  Nothing special as far as taste, but huge portions though!

System is funky- order and pay like a deli, get your drink at the counter, scout out your own table, waiter/waitress comes to your table to get your receipt to bring your order.

There are three rooms to choose to sit from.  They said they won't sit your party until you are all there, but honestly you can and save spots for your party.

Get a load of this - MacDinton's had a policy - DURING GASPARILLA - that guys couldn't wear tank tops. I was wearing a basketball jersey, well, because that's what you do at Gasparilla. They let me in the bar, took my $10 cover, then 10 minutes later some douchebag bouncer that probably makes $12/hr and goes home to his wife who is beat to hell, asks me to leave because I didn't have sleeves on. Yeah, so does every other girl in the entire bar, not to mention about 5 other bro's that were wearing tanks, but failed to confront them. Listen, I get it if it was a high class club at midnight and I was trying to get in being a slouch. But this is God-foresaken Gasparilla, in the DAYTIME, in 75 degree weather. I know what you're thinking reading this - the manager of MacDinton's, who came up with this joke of a policy, should have been out of the game years ago but can't go home because he hates his wife, and probably has to come up with this sort of policy to make his fat-ass self feel relevant around guys who take care of themselves. I hope a hurricane hits Bayshore Blvd and wipes out MacDinton's and all of its useless, jackass employees. And the hurrican's name will be Hurricane Sleeveless Scuffy McGee.
Don't ever go to this place. Very unorganized! They took 45 min to make my burrito and it wasn't even the correct order! This restaurant is unprofessional and subpar. DO NOT EAT HERE

If you don't try this one You ARE GOING to MISS OUT on a gem here in Nashville. Creative Farm to Table with great Southern flair. My second visit and the Pimento Cheese Begniets were even better than last time. Red Snapper on grits to die for and Desserts like the 'Almost Moon Pie' will satisfy the most intense chocolate craving you could ever have. Service matches the excellence this establishment displays. Next time I'm downtown you know where I will be eating!!!

Stopped here for lunch on a Friday while in the area. They have an enormous wine list but not much off the beaten path regarding beer. 

The food was delicious. I got the Shoreline Salad. It was a spring mix topped with filet mignon, roasted red peppers, and blue cheese. Holy crap - amazing! If that wasn't awesome enough, the waiter asked if I wanted to add crab for additional charge. Hell yeah, sir! The crab pieces were HUGE. The charge was kind of huge as well but it was justified. 

My fiancé ordered the Parmesan Crusted Chicken. He liked it but it was served with a blush (vodka) sauce. He wasn't crazy about the sauce but ate it all regardless.

I can't speak about desserts because we didn't order any --- I was stuffed after my salad. The server was very personable and attentive. The view of the Delaware River and Philadelphia were an added bonus. It was a very relaxing time!

Nina (our bartender) was awesome.
She made terrific cocktails and wonderful conversation!
Spent a pleasant 2 hours just hanging out.

This place has become a favorite for Lisa and I,  A hidden gem!!  BBQ is awesome, the creative samwich's they make (pulled pork grilled cheese on garlic toast & the Mac &cheese boneless rib samwich)  worth going out of your way for!  Don't miss out!

I have been to Hamburger Mary's a few times and have always had a great experience! I have been to the drag show a couple times and each time was a different show and kept me laughing. I prefer to come for the entertainment, but the food isn't bad. I have tried their mac n cheese balls and mac n cheese burger and both were tasty. They also have smores that you can buy and you can make the smores at your table. I thought this was a pretty cool concept and have never seen a restaurant do that. They also have a good drink selection. I ordered a sexy on the beach and it was a little strong, but not undrinkably strong. I got the souvineer cup which is a leg with netted stocking and is super cute.

This past Sunday, I came here for bingo. It was a blast! 10 bingo cards for 10 dollars, and the winners receive a prize. During the game they have you engage in fun things such as shouting "It's on bitches." 

Overall, great entertainment, food, and service. Definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a good time. Just be careful about bringing your kids because the material is likely to be inappropriate for them.

I get serving hearty stick to your ribs meals but this was over the top.  We asked if we could downsize an omelette to two eggs and our server's response was "unfortunately we can't do that, because if other customers see your plate, they will think that our serving sizes are inadequate."  OK, so instead we have to order breakfast dishes that could feed a family of four and in the end only eat half or less to see the rest go in the garbage all for appearances sake.  Got it.

I watched as my biscuits and gravy order sat steaming on the service shelf. Service was slow.  Gravy no longer steamed when the dish arrived.  I mentioned this to our server just as an FYI for the future.  Meanwhile, my eggs in a pan were hot so I turned my attention to it.  This skillet was BIG and crammed with vegetables like mushrooms, potatoes, broccoli and onion, plus cheese, sausage all topped by about 4 scrambled eggs.  As I dissected my entree, the server walked by and swiftly took my gravy off the table.  He returned with a "fresh" batch which oddly enough was just lukewarm.  The meal was good, lots of flavor with well sautéed vegetables.  However, the biscuits were forgettable and the gravy unremarkable.

My dining companion's omelet with ham, mushrooms and cheese was well executed and well received, but again, the serving size was ginormous.  After the server saw the amount of food left uneaten, he was ready to wrap the left-overs when we told him we were guests of a hotel and had no opportunities to keep and eat the items later.  I liked this place, it was kitschy, homey, and had a large breakfast selection.  But unless I knew I was splitting an entree with someone else, I couldn't possible dine here.  Seeing so much food go to waste was just too difficult.

A bit disappointing. Food -- Most of our party of eight ordered either the filet trio or the New York strip with several different sides and either apps, soup, or salads. The salad was blah. Nothing special and certainly small for the ~$10. The steak had good flavor; however, half of the table's steak was over cooked. Worse yet, the steaks, including the sides (other than the potato gratin), were lukewarm to cold. 

Service -- Staff were pleasant however the service, particularly for the price, was subpar. Not once did the server or assistant come to check on our meal once it was served. Also, drinks were not regularly filled and, when they were, they weren't filled the entire way. One guest had an empty glass for more than 25 minutes. 

In summary, taking into consideration the service, quality, and price (EVERYTHING is a la carte), we are unlikely to return. 

Recommendations for management -- Improve the attentiveness of your staff and ensure food is cooked to order and served hot. (The flavors were decent. All the other factors diminished the experience.)
The wait staff are amazing and the place is beautiful. The food is amazing and their dark beers are perfect. They played perfect music as well. Would recommend to everyone!

The good: How about everything?  The food is fantastic, although probably out of quite a few people's comfort zone.  I've had bone marrow, crispy pig's trotters, sweetbreads, amongst other awesomeness there.  I can't remember a dish I've had there that I didn't like.  The happy hour is killer: dollar oysters (and they are good oysters), five dollars house sandwiches, five dollar prosecco, five dollar cheese plates, three dollar Yards, et cetera.  Stellar.  The service is great, too.  One of my three favourite restaurants in Philadelphia (see also: Little Fish and Sushi Vic).

The bad:  Not much, although the squirrel collection sometimes creeps me out.  Oh, and the fact that it's not in Lawrence, KS.  That's bad, too.

As I've already said, one of my three favourite restaurants in Philadelphia, hands down.
Excellent place for burger and fries.  We had the Dam burger and the Belgian burger and both were great.  Fries have very tasty dipping sauces.  Quick, efficient service.

The photos on Yelp are unfortunately  outdated and from the previous owners... We got the lemongrass beef after seeing photos on this Yelp page and thinking it looks pretty good, saucy, grilled nice chunks of steak. We were very disappointed when we opened the box. It looked like boiled beef from pho, mixed with some onions and bean sprouts. Very GREY colored. I Took photos but accidentally deleted them. 

Get either the pho or the pork chops instead.
Phenomenal food, phenomenal service, phenomenal dining experience. We left feeling spoiled!

Been there on several occasions. I like their soups and sandwiches, although find it a bit pricy for what you get. Bacon turkey bravo is my fav. Cheddar broccoli is yummy soup that I go for. I like that one can come and work/study there all day if they wish. Comfy chairs, small tables that are easy to rearrange for different size groups. Many plugs for laptops. If I'm hanging there for a while, I get green tea. Refills are free and it's a refreshing drink.

We get takeout here fairly frequently, but have never eaten in.  I can say that it travels very well and is above average for takeout Chinese in the area.  It has become our go to place for a Chinese fix, I just wish they delivered.

dined here at 8:30 PM on Friday evening. Staci was the gal at the register and one of the rudest employees I've ever dealt with. Food was dry. We spent 30$ so we could taste test a variety of items. The only item that was fresh were plantains. I think this place has potential, if they replace employees that clearly have no desire to work in a service industry. Won't be back.
This spot is very good! We had 2lbs of mix meat: carnitas , buche, best of a mix of meats and tortillas! Reminds me of family style taco Spots in Mexico . I will definitely stop by here again!

You know, this place is more often than not probably deserving of five (5) stars but a few small glitches on my visit made me feel that things could have and should have been better. My best friend found the place and we were very excited to try it. The atmosphere seemed warm yet trendy. The whole place was teeming with activity when we walked in we tried to anticipate that being a potential problem with a reservation. Despite having a reservation, we still had to wait a good 30+ minutes. As much as I liked marveling at their collection of Bourbon (locked behind a beautiful glass display), I felt 30+ minutes when we already had a reservation, was too long. When we finally got seated, the table was rocking and there was some moderately high traffic by our area. 

Take all of that with a grain of salt. We were there during Jazz Fest so I'm sure the restaurant was dealing with a LOT more patronage than normal. The high traffic area and unstable table were probably coincidental. All of that notwithstanding the food was GREAT and the drinks were awesome (Lightweights beware: Some of their drinks were strong!). 

Bottom Line: "If you're early, you're on time. If you're on time, you're late." Ask to be seated away from high foot traffic areas. Follow these rules and you're in for a really good time!

I absolutely love Akira, I'm here at least 2-3 times a week. Not only do they have amazing sushi and prices, they also have hibachi.! Their lunch hibachi prices can't be beat. The staff is so friendly and they take notice of their repeat customers and really take care of them. I've tried other sushi places around the area such as sushipop and little Tokyo, and Akira is far superior.

My husband and I had seen this place a few times and finally decided to stop in for lunch. There were probably about 8-9 tables seated and two waitresses on staff. We got a table immediately. Ordering our food was bizarre. I used to waitress for 5 years so I definitely get what it's like to be busy, but our waitress couldn't even stand still long enough to take our order. She was walking away as we ordered our food and was a few tables down when we told her the last part of our order. It was so strange. I get that she was super busy, but she needs to at least let us finish ordering before leaving the table.

While we were waiting for our food I saw a few items went out to wrong tables. A waitress would bring the food, the table would say it wasn't theirs, the waitress would look confused, and then the other waitress would tell them where to drop it off. Our California rolls got dropped off at the table next to ours and sat there for a good minute before making their way to our table. 

My husbands food came out first. I never really like the bring it out as it comes style of serving because I don't want to sit there and watch my husband eat. He got the ramen and it was mediocre at best. He was disappointed with the two small pieces of pork. He barely ate any of it and most of it went wasted. The California rolls were okay. They were edible but not very good.

When my order came out it was wrong. The waitress thought I had ordered something different. She dropped it off so quickly and then left immediately, so I had to call out as she was already a few tables away. A bit awkward. She went back to the kitchen and I waited for the correct order. Mine wasn't very good either. The yaki udon only came with 2 shrimp, which was disappointing. It came with crab meat, but it was overly salted. Out of everything we ordered mine was the best, though it wasn't good, just more edible than the others.

When we got the bill we saw that the waitress had charged us for the incorrect item that she had originally brought. Unfortunately we had already given her our card to run since our 6 month old was getting fussy and we wanted to get her out of there before she started crying. We decided that waiting around to get it fixed wasn't worth the $3 we were overcharged. 

It's been a long time since I had a really poor dining experience and that's exactly what Ichiban provided us. Sub par food and poor service. Obviously we won't be returning.

We were so excited to experience this iconic place and left extremely disappointed!

Our group is a mix of foodies and those who simply enjoy a good meal, and with a limited number of nights in New Orleans we made sure to add the "oldest family owned restaurant in the county" and "inventor of oyster rockerfellar" to our must see/do list.

We entered the restaurant to a very stark white, brightly lit room.  It felt like a cafeteria.  We were sat in that room and immediately felt a little disappointed.  Nothing about the decor felt luxurious.  We asked if we could perhaps be moved to a room that was a little more dim or private, and they said all of the other rooms were booked for the evening. Really, I made this reservation weeks in advance?  Perhaps that should have been mentioned.

Not a good start but we carried on ordering the famed oyster rockerfeller and asked our server (who's name I won't mention) for recommendations.  All we consistently got was "everything is good here."  Come on buddy, work with us a little!  We want to know favorites.  We want to hear about the things we must try!  We got nothing.

We ordered oyster rockerfeller and Escargots a la Bordelaise for appetizers.  We knew from reading reviews to expect an oyster a little different that has been modified over the years in other restaurants.  Both were ok. No complex flavor profiles.  Very basic and felt like I was eating a lot of breadcrumbs (which I like, but again was expecting more).  Dinner half of us ordered Crabes mous amandine and the other Cote de veau Rossalini.  The soft shell crabs were terrible. I basically cut it apart and pushed it around my plate.  No one at the table enjoyed the soft shell crabs.  The veal shank was ok. Again, prepared as ordered but was not flavorful. Our side was Pommes de terre soufflées.  They describe it as "The classic Antoine's fried puffed potatoes."  They should simply say it's hollow french fries and that you get 10 for $8.00 Bleh.

We were so disappointed at this point that we opted out of dessert and skipped the tour of the restaurant.  Finally, it says on their website that "jackets are preferred but not required."  We dressed up for this dinner and was sat next to a diner in khaki shorts and t-shirt.  So yeah, you definitely don't have to and nothing about their food, atmosphere or service would indicate a reason to dress up!

We had 3 nights in New Orleans and were disappointed we wasted a night at this place. The only reason we gave 2 stars and not 1 is that we enjoyed the wine we had, but really we could have gotten a good bottle of wine anywhere!

Excellent white table cloth Mexican arrives in Tampa.  After attending Besito's opening charity event (benefiting the Pediatric Cancer Foundation) and then again for dinner this past weekend, I can highly recommend Besito for wonderful authentic Mexican cuisine. This is not your typical Americanized Mexican chain where everything is drowned in processed cheese and the margaritas are mixed from boxed ingredients, quite the opposite.  Besito's menu does include the staple items you may be looking for, like tacos and enchiladas, but is much, much more. We enjoyed the table-side guacamole followed by the Pescado Veracruzana and Filete de Res al Chipotle.  The fish was wonderfully tasteful and light.  The filet was marinated in Negra Modelo (dark beer) and was not only very tender but had a terrific mix of flavors.  Really unlike any filet I have ever had; simply excellent. Of course we also enjoyed some of the handmade natural margaritas which we truly excellent. Although we were too full for dessert, we did enjoy the complimentary churros and tried one of their many fine sipping Tequilas. 

We will certainly be back and look forward to Besito opening for lunch after Mother's Day.

Delicious burritos!! I've had the carnitas and the carne asada burritos (super and combo)... And both were made with quality meats, and packed with the right amount of fixings. You can't go wrong with getting your Mexican grub on at the Super Cuca.
I love pho when I can get some.  This place offered a brisket pho for $7.95 that was fresh and tasty.  The brisket was cooked well and not fatty.  I'll be back on a cold day

STOP!!!

Ok so now that I have your attention.  I would first and foremost say I would NOT allow you to try this this place.  I've eaten my fair share of dives and don't get me wrong the food is good.  But this food, yah, "take it away and go" did not taste good for my order.  This is my story...

So monday morning, i thought to myself..."Self you were craving dim sum all weekend...walk yourself to the Bird's Nest and order some."  So at 12:00 noon i strolled 2 blocks to this restaurant.  This is what I ordered:

1 Rice Roll Long Donut
1 Rice Roll Fresh Beef
Steam Shrimp Dumplings
Deep Fried Wontons

this order was approx $16 dollars.  Yah...not worth it...The donut in the rice roll was frickin stale and they didn't even pour sweet soy sauce on it.  The rice roll with fresh beef, the beef wasn't fresh it was mushy texture and the rice roll was mushy too.  The Steamed shrimp dumpling looked store bought and steamed, not freshly made and the deep fried wontons are store bought and deep fried.  Don't places ever cook from scratch anymore...sheesh.

Good thing i took this food to go, i would have caused a riot.  

i guess other information about this place is they do a daily buffet, guess I won't be trying that anytime soon and also they do menu orders as well...now if you excuse, i will be throwing up...BLEH!

Went back to try their Om Nom Nom beer, yum! Really does taste like an oatmeal cookie in a glass :) Got a growler to go, I'm sad that this is only a seasonal. I called ahead to make sure they were actually releasing this tonight, and the girl I spoke with said they'd be serving it at 5:00...I made a reservation for 5:15, but when we arrived and promptly ordered the beer, we were told by our waitress it wouldn't actually be ready til 6:00. We were bummed we wouldn't be able to get it right away, but figured we could wait since we were planning on having dinner anyway...shortly after, the manager came by and told us that he heard we'd come specifically for the beer, and said our 1st two beers were on him! Sweet! Good food + good beer + great people = win!

Loved this experience! There was a wait but I found a spot at the bar. The bartenders were engaged with everyone, knowledgeable about the menu and made some killer cocktails! When the food arrives it was delicious! Probably the top 2 shrimp and grits I've ever had! This southern guy will be back!

Yas Yas and Yas! This place truly hit the spot, I don't know what to say, I order grits, eggs and turkey sausage oh and some silver dollars pancakes. My husband order eggs, potatoes and turkey bacon. Everything was amazing except the pancakes they were dry and basic. The smoothie was perfect and had cut mango and pineapple at the bottom of the cup which was a nice treat.  The grits has me feenin'  from New York. #soreadytodrivetherejustforgrits

Ordered delivery and I received the food in about 30 minutes. The food was okay. I asked for no veggies on my lo mein and still got veggies on it. Other that it was good. Not the best, but defiantly not the worst.

What a cozy and romantic little place.  I've driven by this place so many times and said "I gotta go there sometime".  Well I finally decided to go and I am impressed.  Everything was very very good.  I was talked into (by the server) getting the fettuccine Alfredo which was supposedly voted best in the city which was odd to me from a Moroccan place.  I had to try it right?  Well it was definitely delicious, but it was also fettuccine Alfredo which can only get so great before you realize it is a simple dish.  My wife however, got a Tagine dish which was phenomenal and I will definitely get one of those next time.

Keep in mind this place is a bit pricey and might be a better fit for a date night, anniversary, or birthday.  Dishes here were in the $20-25 range which I would say is on the high end for the style of food.


I would come again!
Hands down one of the best places in Philadelphia to eat. I've eaten here a lot, and it is always consistent and very good. The service is nice and quick. They always have the best specials.

Had lunch with a customer here, the food was wonderful.  The salsa was possibly best I've ever had! I had fajitas and they were very good, friend had a taco salad which was plentiful and another had the Hawaii boat, it sounded amazin and he really liked it too.

I don't really know what happened to this restaurant because it used to be one of my favorites. I have been a long time Hibachi Steak fan but it has been awfully inconsistent as of late. Ive had undercooked meat, meat that tasted like it has been sitting in blood and was on the verge of spoiling, and last night both of the meals, including my Hibachi Steak were overcooked.

Anybody that knows anything about cooking, knows what happens to meat that has been recooked. Maybe they felt the need to conserve and use something older and throw it on the grill to resemble a fresh meal, but I know the difference. Even with delivery, the meat should taste that way. My steak was charred. Like, all the the black burnt parts on the meat tasted so bitter it was inedible. I used to order medium, but after tasting the bloody flavor last time (it was totally med rare btw), I knew I couldn't do anything but Med Well moving forward and I would leave the medium temp for steakhouses like 801 Chophouse. 

The potatoes? That's a whole other story. They were hard, lumpy and were not even mixable. You know how potatoes can get when they have been sitting and cool down? They kind of just clump. Who wants mashed potatoes that you can't even blend? 

My husband got the Jamaican Chicken and Shrimp. It was pretty sad, think the only thing they got right was the white rice. The plantains seemed a bit undercooked and the chicken was so dry and hard, there's no way it was made fresh. Truly disappointing for a birthday meal at home! I filled up on the bread, so yea I don't know if I will return again, which is sad. RIP Hibachi Steak.
No flavor... just nasty ass wings! All the sauces are horrible. I don't know  how it's possible to mess up on garlic Parmesan but they found a way.

This place is okay. The food is actually really good, and it's the only good sushi anywhere near campus which is why I keep going back. The street noodles were good, but had more heat than flavor. It was as spicy as wilko's shrimp if you've ever had that. The poke bowl was very good. We passed it around the whole table and everyone loved it. It was a little pricey for the bowl though. The main reason I'm only giving two stars is because the service sucks. Don't bother asking for silverware, because you will need to ask four times for someone to give it to you. Maybe bring your own fork in your purse so you don't have to wait 10 minutes once your food has come to start eating. And one of the waitresses there lies! I didn't get her name down, but everyone at my table had gotten their food and she said mine was "on its way out." A few min later, another worker came over and said they forgot about it and it won't be out for a while. So this home girl thinks "starting to make it" means "on its way out"???
First hangout spot after a long day and we were not disappointed.  We stayed 1 Block from here and just happened on it, so glad we did.  Staff, ambience, and drinks were spot on.  This is a must stop

Amazing vegan food! Amazing food, period. Even if you're not vegan, you'll find something you love. I recommend anything with their buffalo sauce. They give you a good amount of food for the price too!
Best Philly cheese steak I have had in awhile. Brought the parents and my dad is really picky, he ended up liking it. Service was not bad and the wait staff is friendly

We arrived about 4:30 PM on a Sunday night.  As there were very few people, we were seated quickly.  We waited and waited.  Finally a server came to ask if anyone had waited on us yet.  We asked for a couple of beers ... and waited and waited.  Finally, I asked another waiter to please ask our waitress to bring our drinks.  (We never were served with water.).  We finally got our food, but there was no cutlery.  When it became apparent that the server was not coming back, I got up to get our own cutlery.  By that time, my shrimp was cold.  I noticed that our server was often busy bussing her tables, even if it meant that her customers had to wait to order or pay the bill.  When she fInally arrived with our bill, I asked her for the cornbread that was supposed to come with my platter.  If she had checked on us sooner, I could have asked for the cornbread to go *with* my meal instead of just to go.  I gave two stars as my husband thought his shrimp po'boy was good, but my food was just okay and the service was TERRIBLE despite the fact that there were several staff members with not enough to do.  This used to be such a popular restaurant.  It has certainly gone downhill.

Going to breakfast restaurants, you generally can expect the same foods, but Yolk has some very unique dishes up their sleeve. I've been here a couple of occasions and it's  difficult figuring out  what to order. I'd definitely recommend the banana bread French toast if you can't make up your mind. Delicious! The food is good here and the portions are huge. The only thing that keeps me from a 5 star review are the variable service we've received. Our service the recent time we went was great, however the time before that we had problem after problem with getting our orders wrong and having to send things back. Overall, if you need a twist on traditional breakfast, stop and try Yolk.

Ok I am not going to lie I had my doubts about these tacos. Yes , I came all the way across the country and still need tacos #tacosarelife I just want to say these tacos were amazingly delicious. I got pork belly, shrimp and carnitas. The guacamole was definitely fresh and to die for! Salsa  I definitely recommend it. Especially for anyone missing home on the west coast! Demetrius was super knowledgeable and helpful with the drink menu and the food menu! Not to mention Dominique the manager was super nice and made sure all our needs were met! I love this place. 


Visit 2! I had to go back one last time before my visit in PA was over. I have to say the service just gets better every time! I tried the Asada tacos and they were just as amazing as the others! All this food is made with love! I got to try a new cucumber jalapeño mint margarita! (ARIZONA MARGARITA) Man it was delicious especially if spicy is your forte! The half sugar half tajin rim really lets you choose your hotness level! I like them so much I had 3! Made with fresh jalapeños and cucumber it's definitely this Arizona girls go to place every time I visit!!! 
I love Bartaco! Ps. The plantains are to die for! Thank you Demetrius and Dominique! You made my visit to PA super special! Tell Larry he's amazing too! You have a great team!

This place is quickly getting a good rep in Boise- it's not bad. The service is great and very friendly. My wife LOVES the fries. Honestly, I don't really think they are that great. I like my fries hot and crispy. maybe it's because they use all kinds of potatoes, but all of the fries I have had here have been soft and frankly, pretty greasy. I have had the buffalo burger here a few times, and really- the burger itself is great. However- it's $7 just for the burger, and this is an order at the counter place. The bun is delicious- I think it's a potato bun. However, everytime I have ordered it, there is much more bun than there is burger. When I have to pay $7 for a burger at the counter, I want the burger to be the same size as the bun. All that said- it is a fun place to check out, and I love that it is local and the service is really good. I think it's great that they were willing to compromise with the potato commission on their name, even though the commission was morally wrong. Good on you, Boise Fry Company.

No one likes being ignored at a restaurant, especially when there is no good excuse.  I spent a long time sitting hungry, thirsty and menuless despite being 1 of 3 patrons in the restaurant at the time.  I spent 25 minutes just waiting to get a menu while the staff milled around.  I guess I should be thankful I got a seat.  The food was good, but I had to wait another 20 minutes after my plate was cleared to get the check.  For most of that 20 minutes, my server was at the other end of the restaurant checking his phone.

Unless I'm looking to squander an evening, I won't be going back.

If you dream of driving by Krispy Kreme drive with the neon orange hot now sign on, this is the place for you. Not every Krispy Kreme makes there doughnuts on location anymore. This Krispy Kreme makes all the doughnuts for the Tampa area locations and all their vendors. If you are looking for made on the spot warm and delicious glazed doughnuts, you want to visit this location between 6-6:30pm any night of the week. This was the time frame the employee who helped us told us they bake the glazed goodness daily. The staff here is super friendly and always willing to go above and beyond! It's usually pretty busy, but the staff makes you feel welcome as soon as you arrive. A drive through is a available, but I would recommend going in and socializing with the staff and watching the delicious donuts being prepared.

Vegans: The seitan wings are on point. Vegetarians: quesadilla is on point. Fries are good too. Great ambiance and chill place. However: about 75% of the time we come in, it smells like fish. Vent the kitchen pleez.

Edit.
Good news. Last few times we came, it smelled like a bar instead of a Vietnamese fish market. Bad news: the fried foods (seitan wings for example) had a distinct fish taste to them, as if they were fried with fish.
Great customer service, the bang bang shrimp is simple and tasty! Fish were a little overdone and not as fresh as I imagined, still a good experience.

This is their second location on Whyte. It was our first time trying this restaurant and we were very pleasantly surprised. We tried the Lamb Ragu and Lobster linguini. And wow the portions are super generous! There was a huge lobster tail included in the linguini- I've never really seen that large of a piece in a pasta before. The lamb Ragu also had a good amount of protein in it. There was plenty of pasta and the sauces were good. A nice addition on whyte, will be back!

I have such fond memories of eating at Drago's. My HS banquets were held here.  In fact I had dinner in that same room on Saturday night...definitely not for private parties any more.  

The pros: 
The chargrilled oysters were tasty and fresh.
I sampled the fish special that one of dining companions got and it was delicious.
Lots of variety to the seafood dishes.
They have a Chandon sparkling split for a glass or so of bubbly.

The cons:
They do not take reservations, even for large parties. So my group arrived at 5 pm. We were seated immediately. By the time we left, the hordes has descended. It was craziness.
The crabmeat au gratin dip tasted like velveeta.

The weird:
Drago's is no longer an inexpensive restaurant and the server was very much...the jokester nephew of the owner style.
I found an oyster shell under my chair....remember we were seated at 5; had it been there since lunch?

The verdict:
