My entree (an fine but not remarkable shrimp & pasta dish) fed me for 2 additional meals since Saturday. I would rather pay less and have an entree that doesn't feed 3.  I wish the meal had been better and that our waiter hadn't disappeared so we could pay the bill and escape the gathering hordes of people.

[ food ]
Have stopped by here a few times for breakfast before the Amtrak. Egg/cheese squagels and the TBM melt usually hit the spot. Love their whole grain flatbread. 

Coffee is okay. They will even do soy drinks, which is cool.

Today, however, we got a basil tomato soup and it was cold. We asked them to heat it up and they microwaved it...came back and it was lukewarm, so we had to ask them to microwave it again.

That's been my only bad experience here.

[ seating / atmosphere ]

Clean and spacious. Nice cushiony chairs, heavy, sturdy tables. Plenty of seating, big tables, a nice place to camp out and get some work done. WiFi and outlets if you snag the right table.

[ overall ]
Nice for a break, a quick rest, or doing some work. Music is a little loud but not  overbearing. Service speed is reasonable but not lightning fast. Decent spot.

So far so good! I definitely underestimated this place in fletcher place and I definitely recommend. Look at how soft the porky belly buns look! 

My friend and I got the momma thang cocktails, which were okay, and we split the karaage. I loved this entree! The chicken was amazingly good with that sweet chili sauce! Didn't care too much for the egg because it made the rice mushy but overall loved it. 

Average price at this place is a bit high ( $14-18) but overall pretty good place to share.

It's hard to miss Molcas while driving down Grant Rd. at night.  There are bright neon yellow lights that illuminate a covered, outdoor seating area in front of the stationary truck.  Unfortunately, these yellow lights do not give off heat if you were to eat on site on a nearly freezing December night.

I ordered the quesadilla molcas, which came out to $5.30.  It came with steak, lettuce, tomatoes, cheese and avocado.  The quesadilla was the perfect amount of food for me although I had expected it to be bigger due to the price.  The meat was good but not amazing.  My friend had the 3 carne asada tacos, which he really enjoyed.

The condiments were not that great.  They had salsa verde and a spicy salsa.  The spicy salsa was not spicy.  The jalapeno and carrots were also not that spicy.  They had some of the usual condiments but did not have cilantro, onions and radishes.  We ate there at 8 pm, so maybe they had run out, but this is not confirmed.

While eating there, some people after us ordered hot dogs.  They have a special stand next to the condiment stand especially for hot dogs.  I didn't try the hot dogs, but the lady making them was definitely loading up condiments on the hot dogs for the customers.

The food was good, but the food and pricing were nothing spectacular.  The service was very friendly and no frills, which I appreciate.  There was no line at 8 pm, but there was a steady stream of customers while we were there.

Absolutely delicious food in an idyllic historic setting. We chose outdoor seating, shaded by blossoming trees, listening to birdsongs (We went in early May, when everything in the canyon was fresh and growing). The tri tip, ribs, pulled pork, and burgers are exquisite! The onion rings are seriously the best I've ever had, generously battered, golden, with a delicate crunch so perfect it makes you close your eyes in bliss! Dipped in ranch, they're the epitome of indulgence. The desserts were all excellent, the service was great, and we left stuffed and happy. If you're hungry after a hike or a long drive, this place will make all your appetite's dreams come true!

I'd eat here again just for the garlic bread! 

At reaonable prices, good food, and great ambiance, what's not to love? I ate here this past weekend with a few friends and we were all thrilled with our dinner selections. You gotta love a place that offers brown rice and wheat pasta options for no extra charge. The greek pizza was delish, and the scampi and salmon were also yum. Get the sampler platter of appetizers, for $12 you get a ton of tastes!
Very good good, good atmosphere, owner can play some ping pong.  I suggest getting the Mac and cheese

The first few times that I walked passed this little cafe, it was closed. Now, that was a given since it was around 11 pm and I was there to meet one of my friends who just got off of work. So flash forward a few months, 3 to be exact, and there I am: hungry, cold, and in need of something other than bar food. So I walked into Happily Ever After with a couple of my friends and despite it being almost closing time the owner was very kind towards us and even made us the ramen we wanted (which btw is the best ramen I've ever had in Philly). This surprised me since it was marketed as a dessert cafe, but now I happen to go there whenever I have the chance. Also I've told several of my friends about this golden establishment. Keep up the great work !!

Dmitri's is the best Greek food in town. If you're a seafood lover, go for the shrimp pil pil and the octopus. The grilled lamb and chicken entrees are the only non seafood items, but they're fantastic. Make sure to get the hummus - it comes with unlimited warm grilled pita and baguette.

Also - BYOB! And they don't take reservations. Kitchen closes at 10 so make sure to get there by 9:30.
Great food. The wait has gotten ridiculously long lately, however.

This place is awesome! We had dinner and can't say enough positive things about our experience. Very clean, welcoming restaurant with a small bar. Well made margaritas with black salt(nice touch) got us started along with their shrimp ceviche. This was made to order, not scooped out a tub made who-knows-when. So fresh, so delicious.
They had more seafood being offered than most Mexican restaurants. Deciding that was their thing, we dove in and were so happy we did. The Faro de Mariscos, sort of a layered seafood aguachile, was outstanding. Spicy, tangy, and unbelievably fresh.
The owner spoke with us and offered us something special. Sinaloa scallops and Robalo(Snook) aguachile.
This was phenomenal! The scallops were like tender abalone and Robalo is now a fish I will seek out in the future. 
A nice selection of salsas and hot sauces are available, but the food was so fresh and well prepared, it didn't need any help.
Great service(thanks Nelly!) and genuine smiles all around. Can't wait to come again.

The front of the business is barely noticeable, but it is worth finding. The iced coffee and giant chocolate chip cookie I got were amazing! The prices are very reasonable, and they take cards!

The basement has a very large seating area. It is easy to relax without feeling cramped like most cafes. The menu seems to have a good selection of sandwiches, cramped, and other items I hope to try soon!

This little place is an absolute gem!  The server was so sweet and personable.  The chef is very talented we had the French toast bread pudding, avocado toast, biscuits with gravy and mimosas. We loved it so much that we are going again for dinner tonight!

Such a cute and fun place in a great area. We went on a weekend for their Sunday brunch and this seems like the place to be! Everyone (and their dogs) came by, they've got great covered outdoor seating which allows for a lot more people to enjoy their food on site and the food itself is amazing, delicious, affordable and plentiful. Definitely going to come back, and I would like to try their other (non-breakfast/brunch) menu.

DO NOT ORDER FROM HERE!!! THEY ARE THIEFS! Took an order my order at 10:15 at 12:30 was told it was on the way. NEVER DELIVERED!! Had no problem charging my credit card. Impossible to get ahold of a manager, and was told they have a NO refund policy only exchange!! LMFAO!! THIS PLACE IS A JOKE! How are you not going to refund me for food that wasn't even delivered!? Hung up on multiple times after waiting 2+ hours. I was only staying a mile away at a local hotel. DO YOURSELF A FAVOR, AND NEVER EVER EVER ORDER ANYTHING FROM HERE!!

I'm giving this place a 4 star because the atmosphere is AMAZING! So fun! The margaritas are great, prefect margarita you've been waiting for. They have a lot of different flavors as well. The food is just okay. The guac is small. Service was great.
Great late night pizza spot in the french quarter. Cant beat it. Good location near convenience stores and xheaoer than most other tourist spots.
The sesame and Thai tea are good. Bite size cake is pretty moist and tasty, but can do without it if you want to save a couple of bucks.

Fantastic.  We were so happy we took a chance here- my drunken noodle was delicious, and my husband, a curry fanatic, was deeply satisfied with the red curry here.   Lovely staff, funky comfortable room.  Bravo!
My family and I live so close to this restaurant so we are eating here pretty often, we love this place! The food is always so great and the service is always accommodating and friendly!!

Found this place on Uber Eats and it was a pleasant surprise! I have tried a few different things and have yet to be disappointed. Their wings are so yummy and each sandwich I have tried has been fresh and delicious. I definitely recommend trying them!

Big Al's is where it's at. Prior to coming to Nashville I took the time to look up different places I wanted to eat and Big Al's was on my list. A real hidden gem in a residential area outside of downtown with some indoor and outdoor seating. Really pleasant environment. We walked in and were greeted right away and had the pleasure of meeting Big Al himself. We took a couple of minutes looking over the menu while the people from Big Al's asked us questions about where we were from (we must have looked like out of towners!). 

I ordered the shrimp and grits and my boyfriend ordered the BBQ chicken plate with mac & cheese and mashed potatoes and we washed that down with a couple of sweet teas. Why can't LA have sweet tea everywhere!? I took a bite of my food and it was so flavorful and full of spice. The creamy grits balanced out the spicy shrimp and it was served with a biscuit that I used to sop up that delicious pan sauce. Hands down the best shrimp and grits I've ever had. I picked at the potatoes on my man's plate and they were so flavorful. They reminded me of the mashed potatoes my mom used to make, so much flavor that gravy is not needed. The food portions were huge! It was a good thing we had a fridge and microwave in our room because we had to pack our leftovers to go and ate them later. Food too good to go to waste!

Big Al and the other workers there made us feel very welcome. They told us to come back for breakfast the next day, but unfortunately, we just didn't have enough time. I know this won't be my last trip to Nashville and I will return to Big Al's for that breakfast!

Such a cozy place! Coffee is okay, staff is welcoming, kind and lated-back, by the vibe is the best - copy couches to sit on, tables to play chess or work at, and sometimes live music! I love sitting in every place of this coffee shop.

Amazing food and good service. I went to eat with a friend and we were able to get a seat right away at the bar (I do know they had said it would be a 30 minute wait if we actually wanted a table).

As far as food went it was delicious. I got ravioli and it was amazing. They also had great drinks there.  

Definitely recommend it and will be coming back again!

Late lunch on beautiful sunny coastal day while traveling. Several other diners were with dogs on the large patio with seats in both sun and shade. Warm welcome by hostess, who brought bowl of water for our poochie. Service was prompt, and food arrived quickly. My wife had delicious seared tuna dinner with tasty chunky vegetables and astonishing sweet potato fries. I had excellent salmon burger on fresh brioche bun with really good salad inside. Tomato vegetable soup was peppery and better than average. This is a destination restaurant for locals and tourists, and we can't wait for another chance to eat the amazing sweet potato fries.

Fun place.
Family Friendly. 
South Tampa Hallmark Restaurant. 
Good Prices. 
Cheap beer. 
Plenty of parking. 
LOTS of TV's. 

This is a great dine-in OR take-out pizza joint in south Tampa. Nothing spectacular but the pizza is good and priced right. Personal pitchers of domestics are $5 with $3 refills. Definitely a great choice for family pizza night. They have a huge room with lots of TV's to catch your favorite team and plenty of outdoor seating as well.

I eat here often, as it is right next to my work. I have NEVER been dissapointed. Their burgers are very delicious and staff are all very friendly and courteous. The place itself is always clean. There are a wide array of sauces for your burger or fries that are to die for. Curry ketchup, Sriracha mayo and sweet red chili being among my favorites. They have a few menu options like grass fed beef vs regular, although their regular beef patties are very high quality and taste delicious as well. The buns are never over toasted, very soft and delicious as well! Left overs can be saved for later, as they are just as good heated up!  It is a tad pricey for a burger meal, but its well worth it.

Wow! This place was great. I would recommend making a reservation though as it is pretty busy.  The portions are great and me and my friend left feeling very satisfied. We started with the small antipasto and ordered the 20 layer lasagna and the family jewels pizza. Everything we ate was great and I would recommend this place to anyone who likes Italian food and a up to date atmosphere.

We had a reservation at the Tyrone location 2/23/21 @ 8:00pm to celebrate our 18th wedding anniversary. Missy was our waitress and she was great. App's were good (the Brie & the firecracker shrimp). We Received a complimentary bottle of wine and later a desert to share, all good so far. Then came the the Prime rib, which my wife and I both ordered, after reading many positive reviews on various groups on fb we decided to give it a try. What a mistake that choice was. My wife ordered medium rare and received the end heal of the prime rib and it was unbelievably overcooked and dry mine was ordered Medium and was just as dried out. I usually don't order prime rib medium but did this time based on others reviews of how rare theirs came out. Although it did have decent flavor it was inedible. It ruined our meal to say the least. The reason I gave a 4-star review was due to the service and friendly staff and the fact that they did all they could to make it right for us. Missy sent us home with 2 complete prime rib dinners to go, hopefully they will be better than what we were served in person. I understand it's unreasonable to think that everything is perfect  of the time for that reason I'm willing to give them the benefit of the doubt that it was just a "off" night and give them another try. 

-Greg & Deb K

I took my 9 year old daughter to the new Wayback Burger in Plant City for some Daddy/Daughter time.  The burgers were delicious, although a little small (she ate a double). It's like those other "Guys", I think there are 5 of them, but with a better menu and without the peanuts (as a parent of a girl with a peanut allergy...thank you!).  Oh and milkshakes!  Don't even go in there unless you leave with a shake!

I had the mushroom burger, she had the double cheeseburger.  I was impressed with the friendliness of the staff.  They actually bring your food to you and seem to enjoy their job (kinda like that chicken place with the cows).  Since they make the burgers to order, it does take longer than you might expect,  but the awesome 50's music makes the wait easier. 

I may try their online ordering...but one way or another, I'll be back..way back (see what I did there?)

Welcome to Plant City, WayBack!

I had the white pizza delivered via Uber Eats. It was amazing, I forgot to take a photo. I will order again I may try the Grandma pizza. The cheese tasty very fresh best I have had. I can't say enough good things about the crust. I usually don't eat all the crust with this one I did. The pizza lasted me 3 days size was big great value. I can't wait to try again.

I really enjoyed the decor and feel walking into this place-some areas reminded me of Saved by the Bell! Ice cream is one of my joys in life. I was very excited to try this popular favorite due to the exciting flavors I heard about. I sampled almost all of theM & decided on the Chocolate Salt Malt and the Sour Cherry & Honey. It was very good for the first few bites, but it's the kind of good that doesn't take you all the way, it gets a little tiring. All in all, fun experience, like the creative flavors, but didn't satisfy to the last lick!
Awesome taco bar! The tortillas are home-made fresh. You have to try the Elote Del Mercado.
Literally THE best place in town. This is a staple for any college student at Villanova

Workers are never on times. The store states 7 am as the opening time and it is still dark at 7:15 am.  I've pretty much given up on my morning meal here guess I'll go to bread company down the street.

Had a great workout this morning and found this cute coffee hidden in the west side of town. Instead of going to Starbucks in the same parking lot, check out this place instead. Very small, good for a personal convo, Has their own coffee (what it's not tinker ) and sells local merch. I got an iced latte with salted Carmel and oat milk. $6 is too much but it was delicious.
Some of the best tacos I've ever had!  The only negatives I could come up with is that I wish there were more options!  I'll be trying the corn next time and also the Frescas are on point, must get.

I always do delivery. They are so fast with their deliveries. I love that. We order about once a week. The food is consistently good. I rarely have mistakes with our order and when we do they fix it and deliver it quickly. We don't have many delivery options in Sahuarita so I'm glad we have a place like this. The prices are great and the staff is friendly.
Fabulous stay! Very nice room, super comfy bed, excellent service. Our room was quite a long way from the parking garage but that is our only complaint. We will be staying here again.
Food was 100% crap. Wings, wood grilled salmon, coconut shrimp, and service all super bad at the moorestown nj location. Biggest waste of $90 ive ever spent, i will not even go back to try it again

This was my first meal in Canada.  I was pleasantly surprised!  The hummus was probably the best hummus I have ever tasted.  I'm a fan of garlic, and that hummus sure packed a garlic punch!

I ordered the lamb skewers which were not gamy at all (I don't mind gamy, so there was something to be desired).  The zucchini in tomato sauce was excellent.  Also got to try some meat balls with minty cream sauce.  Not really into the minty mouth wash flavor in sauces or drinks, so I wasn't digging into them as much.

Over all this place was very good and I would highly recommend it.

This bakery is co-located with a small gas station/convenience store. I believe that it has been around for over 60 years. The bakery has a few parking spots that it shares with the convenience store, but I don't see a lot of people being here all at one time. The store is small and has an old school look and feel. 

It may be a bakery, but they do not have a big donut selection. Their pastries are were they make their money. They have a bunch of cookies, cinnamon rolls, danishes, pies and cakes. They have some awesome fruit danishes. I got an apricot, and blackberry and creme one. I threw in a lemon bar and pecan roll for good measure. Mmmmmm, I was hooked. My only issue was that my danish was cold, as if it was refrigerated or frozen. So, I cannot attest to their freshness. They are however, still pretty good. My favorite was the apricot one. Their prices are reasonable.

They also offer a limited selection of sodas, milk, coffee and cappuccino.

The staff was very nice and I was only there for about 3 minutes. In and out, easy peasy.

Yes!!!!! I found the best thai food at here.
I love this place, great Thai Food, 
good service.
Recommend to everyone to try this place.
Great pizza and sandwiches.  Worth the trouble trying to place an order.  Surpasses the hype.  Have had a cheese pizza, grandma pizza and a couple cheesesteaks.  Philly special !
Took my girlfriend here on a date. Nice atmosphere and dining experience. Good music, food and clean bathrooms.

Very good! I had the lamb and meatball sandwich with potato salad and greens salad and everything was delish. Love the Tabasco honey dressing, and the potato salad made with smoked bacon blue cheese was a nice twist to this American favorite. Definitely a must try.
Best gluten free crust hands down! Real food, fantastic flavor. You can't go wrong here.

I visited Frey for the first time last night with friends, and I liked it so much that I decided to return today with my family for lunch. The brisket is delicious, and this is what I opted for both times (I've had it both in sandwich and platter form).

Last night we enjoyed 3 flights of nice bourbon, each of which came with the delicious Pork Belly Popper appetizer for a very reasonable price. Overall, last night was great.

Today, however, my sisters had different opinions and did not like their pulled pork sandwiches. I tried a bite, and I have to admit that it was not very tasty. 

OVERALL:
Service was great both times, great alcohol selection, inconsistent food (some is good, some not; be sure to order correctly).

Y'all. I live 5 blocks away and I can't tell you how many mornings I've woken up and thought: 'I don't want to drive to brunch.' Finally, brunch has come to me!!

Toast is officially open on Gentilly and the food is good and the prices are great. I had the ratatouille and ricotta toast with a side of grits and my fiancé had the hangar steak. My toast was awesome and despite the fact that you're just ordering toast, it was very filling! My fiancés steak was perfectly cooked and before I could taste, every last bite was gone. 

The staff is very nice and they all seem really excited to open up the new location. At $27 for two meals and a coffee, and walking distance from the house, we're also stoked and will be back again!

Visiting the Columbia is probably the closest I'll ever come to visiting the mansion in "Clue." All of those immaculately designed rooms, and c'mon, that one with the staircase and the suit of armor! But it's an easy game of Clue, because no matter which room you pick, it's always Mr. Me with the gazpacho.

Yes, I love gazpacho and it's a little disappointing how rarely you run across it in Spanish/Cuban restaurants. It has a great taste, and I love the Columbia touch of adding the vegetables tableside. Truth is, I'm a pescatarian and rarely come here with a group, so this and the house bread usually sets me up. If I'm feeling the urge for something more, house coffee and the crema Catalana which is another tableside attraction - always fun to watch a dolled-up waitron torching up some caramelizing sugar.

Of course, this place is a classic "you haveta eat here when you're in town" kinda place. And we all know those places usually aren't any good. I just went to the Miami equivalent of sorts, Versailles, and felt "yep, ticked THAT one off the list" as I walked out. But the Columbia is one you can actually return to and enjoy every time. But then, I always have been a sucker for "Clue."

In NOLA last week and spent several hours at WWII museum and we were starving!!!!   Got the double and the waffle sweet potato fries.  Also got a hurricane from the bar.  Hubby got double and onion rings and a Corona.  The burger was awesome!   I am NOT a fan of sweet potato fries, but they looked so good I HAD to try them!  We also sampled ALL of the mayos on the bar and those house pickled jalapenos.........DAMN GOOD all the way around!!!!!!

Food was great. It was during covid, actually a birthday brunch my daughter took me to. We were 1st seated near the curb which sucked but they were rearranging the umbrella for us. Once a couple left we were able to change our table. It was much better, minus the bugs. They can't control the outside. My French toast was so delish. I didn't use syrup and finished it all. The fruit on it was fresh. My turkey bacon was SUPER thick and good. The Bellini carafe was good as well. My daughter also enjoyed her food. Service was quick and I was stuffed.

I wanted to add my two cents since we went for lunch, and most other reviewers reviewed coffee and breakfast. You can have breakfast menu options at lunch (which are great) but there are also many great salads and sandwiches on the menu. I had a super yummy Waldorf salad with curried chicken, and my daughter had an enormous quesadilla. I also happen to be there on a Monday and they are currently running a promotion for "Free Muffin Monday" which you get when you order just about anything. Don't know how long it will last, but their delish lemon almond muffin became my dessert! The restaurant has lots of charm and is large and open with lots of seating in and outdoors. They are also situated right in front of a pretty play fountain. Great option when you want quick, fresh, healthy and yummy meal!

Awful.  You walk in and are assaulted by cheap furniture and a equally awful decor.  It is more like a poor version of a imitation of Mexico.  The food is terrible.  It is inauthentic.  The pork burrito was greasy.  The rice was dry.  The salsa fake.  The only thing authentic was the bottled beer.  The waiters were nice.  They were even nice even to correct the overcharges on the bill.  This is a NO.  Any restaurant that has a tv is not a restaurant, it's a fast food joint or a bar.  And selling junk candy at the cash register is tasteless.  Seriously, this was among the worst experiences I have had in a long time.  NO SECOND CHANCES.  Plus I was queasy the entire day awful.  -1 review.

Very thin crust.  Wasn't what I was expecting. Had some kind of cheddar cheese mix or something other than real mozz on it. If you like an Imos style crust with this kind of cheese on it, this may be the pizza for you.
Great place and love the name!  Yummy fries and very tasty burgers.  Heard about this place from a friend and we will definitely be going back.

I am a loyal customer of ACME OYSTER COMPANY....on Iberville at Bourbon

Here are some personal highlights...

*community tables are fun, standing in a long line outside should be fun and you should encourage a communal gathering
*Portions are large, read the menu...you'll find fried foods...you'll discover broiled oysters
*Prices are well below other seafood meals in NOLA 
*I've always had extremely professional, attentive and deserving of high gratuity wait staff....ask questions because they like to share their favorites
*Bread Pudding....Bread Pudding
*Thoughts like...consistent, welcoming, quality, professional, inviting are key to me

Baby, I love the smell of freshness and how it triggers my tastebuds.....

Edit begins here...

2 DAYS LATER AND I'VE RETURNED.....because of friends recommending the CHARGRILLED OYSTERS I did go back for them.     A dozen freshly sucked, chargrilled in the half shell oysters with garlic, butter, parmesan cheese et al is a hit.   PLEASE TRY THEM OVER THE RAW.

Personally, I prefer the RAW....these were unlike Amy I've had before.....they were so so so rich that it really was too much for me.   

I ALSO ROLLED AWAY A FAT HAPPY MAN AFTER A CUP OF THE OYSTER ROCKEFELLER SOUP.....I can't believe that this could be replicated...thick and creamy, adequate spinach, extremely large fried OYSTER....a definite must for me from this point forward.

Last night we were a group of seven celebrating my son's 30th birthday and decided to go for drinks at El Vez - somewhere my son frequents often. We arrived at 11:30 and ordered drinks etc. at 1:45 they announced last call so everyone around the bar ordered another drink.  At 1:50 the GM announced in a loud crass tone that everybody had to finish their drinks and leave the bar by 2:00. Everybody looked at each other in amazement- why do last call at 1:45 if you want your bar cleared by 2:00. At 1:55 he bellowed "everybody clear the bar!"  Let me say this - it will be forever before I ever go back there!

Jimmy John's is as freaky fast as they claim. I come here at least once a week. I prefer it over Subway, even though they don't offer as many choices as Subway and no hot subs. The bread is really fresh and the meat tastes better here than Subway's, although I wish they added more meat and cheese without the upcharge. I tend to order either  tuna, turkey or roast beef. All good but It would be nice if Mr John can equip his restaurants with salt and pepper. Is that too much to ask? 

Service is very fast and friendly here. They typically greet you immediately and wish you a good day/night as you leave. They also have free bike delivery if you live or work around Ybor.  Pretty clean inside with outdoor tables with umbrellas. It's in the heart of Centro Ybor facing 7th Ave so a good place to chill while sipping on sweet tea, which is excellent by the way.  Oh, one other note...Read the signs scattered around the walls, they provide words of wisdom, humor and life advice.
Good local spot, nice service and hospitality.  Have desserts too although didn't try.  A bit pricey though.  Club sandwich, chips, drink with tip was $18.20
My fave lunch spot for the spicy pork Kogi bowl! Service is great and very affordable! Will be back soon!

Currently in Tucson for training. Came across this restaurant and I have to say it was an amazing experience! Started off with the order to Chips and guacamole. Then followed with the catch of the day (highly recommended!). The service and atmosphere was the cherry on top.

What a sad experience. I was excited for this restaurant and am new to the area. The food took forever and when I finally did get my food it was cold and I had a plate full of uncooked broccoli (I ordered kabobs, mashed potatoes and broccoli). I sent it back and it was returned to me, on a different plate but still the same. Service was also chaotic and the cleanliness if the restaurant was questionable. There was garbage on the ground under our table with a puddle of water near the booth base. Will not be returning, and I recommend to stay away. Many other quality restaurants down Gulf Blvd.
Great food nice interior.Absolutely amazing  seasoning.We'll be back again.Be prepare your hands will be messy .

I had the Bulgogi- fried thin sliced beef marinated in a special sauce & sliced onions for $12.99. It's served with steamed rice & side dishes. Service is quick, staff is friendly, and they can speak English. According to the plaque on the wall, this place was voted Nashville's 2011 best.

Yeah okay.
My wife likes this place. And sometimes, as a man, you gotta watch Steel Magnolias or Twilight. Or The View...not with Whoopi, with that know-it-all Rosie O'Donnell. Ugh. It's not that I'm suffering, it's just not my scene.
And Pita Jungle is that for me...not my scene. And that's cool.
It's a clean open dining space with an open kitchen and rather large bar. Bonus for having Torpedo on draft. Heck I'll watch the whole darn Twilight trilogy with sufficient enough good draft beer. 
Go team Edward!
My wife declares their jalapeño/ cilantro hummus superior to any other hummus in the world. Except for their red pepper hummus. She digs that one also. But for me, I like my hummus to punch me in the palate with chick pea, garlic, cumin, tahini and lemon. Paprika. Olive oil. 
Pita Jungle hummus is okay. Their pitas are okay. 
Just okay. Oh well. It's made for the tastes of many...not the few. 
I had their falafel pita, and it was okay. But if I'm going to do middle eastern/ Mediterranean I want to feel abused and dirty. Like Midnight Express dirty.
My wife had the vegetarian chili and she loves that, and she isn't even a vegetarian.
Service was okay too, nothing horrible- nothing spectacular. 
But I kinda feel a little cheated- I read down through many a yelper's yelp and the scantily clad servers must not be there on Mondays. Honestly that would have been a selling point for me. But there was nary a bare arm, let alone a braless coed slinging pitas. Maybe because it was 70 degrees today- almost Ugg weather in Tucson.
Anyway, Pita Jungle you're okay. I got no beef with you.
Get it? Because it's mostly vegetarian stuff.
This stuff practically writes itself.
No. Really.
Love this place for lunch. They have a great lunch special. Their kimchi fries are a great appetizer!

My husband and I held our wedding at Cafe a la C'Art. It was spectacular! The staff went over and beyond to make our special day nothing short of amazing. Especially the bar manager Galen Adams. They were all so accommodating, gracious, attentive and pleasant. The food and cocktails were fantastic and delicious. The venue is beautiful and the atmosphere is great as well. I highly recommended this hidden treasure for a special event or just a nice time with friends or that special someone. We've already been back several times and plan to continue.

You must try the steak tacos!  We happened upon this place a while ago due to a review of the best tacos in Indy and La Parada was at the top for their steak tacos.  There is a reason for this.  They are awesome!  Nothing fancy, just steak, onions, cilantro, and squeeze some lime juice on there....DELICIOUS!!  

The chips and homemade salsa are always good and hubs is adventurous and always tries other foods which he always enjoys too.  

Only bummer is that since they moved to new location they still do not have their liquor license so no yummy beer to go with the delicious food.  But the new location is nice, much more space.  Just wish they would get the liquor license....

The prices were ok and the staff and service were very friendly and quick. My issues were with the food. 

I ordered a potatoes and egg breakfast, as did my wife. She added bacon, I added ham and a hot chocolate.

The hot chocolate tasted of everything, but chocolate. It had a heavy nutmeg taste and was more like a cup of hot ginger bread. 

As for the food, the potatoes for both orders were room temperature, almost to lukewarm. The ham that arrived on my plate was not even a ham steak. It was ham lunch meat that had been thrown on the grill for a moment. It too, was lukewarm, at best. 

Not sure if this is the normal fare, but it could use some work. They are very much trying to emulate a cafe in San Francisco, but have missed the mark. And the target. And the tree holding up the target.

Visited Nudy's for brunch with my parents on Sunday around noon and had no trouble being immediately seated outside. The menu is large, offering both breakfast and lunch, and the service was friendly.  I was fully satisfied with the portions of grilled chicken and avocado on my salad and not hungry again until dinnertime.  Although it's a bit down the road from the "main" section of Bridge Street, there's a decent amount of parking available behind the café and on the surrounding streets.

Nothing about Nudy's put it into the running for best brunch I've ever had, but it's a solid spot and I am sure I'll be making repeat visits.

I recently went to Slidell for some business trip and stayed in Double Tree New Orleans. Mother's is only a minute away from the hotel so it's a no brainer. First night I had the famous special po'boy, and crawfish etouffee. Regardless of the portion (which is more than enough for a person), the po'boy was too wet for me. All I could taste is mustard. The etouffee was not hot enough and frankly, I have better at Davis Street in Schaumburg, IL!!

Second night I had the fried chicken with bread pudding. Now, you may ask, "if first night was awful, why did you go back for second?" Well.... I was tired and lazy so give me a break!! I had to wait 20-30 minutes for fried chicken. I have to say... it is probably the best fried chicken I've ever had. Better than Popeyes. Better than Church. It's crispy, full of flavor, juicy on the inside, and most importantly, not oily!! I totally dig that. The bread pudding made the dinner a complete meal. It may not be the best bread pudding but it's good enough to make me happy.

Two words: Fish Tacos   

We ordered food here a couple times during our stay at Windsor Suites and both times were on point. Great food & awesome service... what more could you want?
So good. Ordered the original crust w/ garlic sauce, Italian sausage, green onion and olives. Mouth watering goodness. Was made in just a short period of time. Definitely will be coming back.
This is the worse McDonald's I have ever been to! Rude people talk to other customers about you and back talk the managers in front of customers !!!!

I'm from the south, and a breakfast combo should come standard as 2 eggs, choice of meat, and hash browns, grits, or home fries, plus toast or biscuit. Price is usually around $6 to $8 then add a coffee or drink for another $2... 
I had to order bacon separately as a side here. My tab ?   $17.09
The food was so good and the inside was adorable. This is a hidden gem in the USF area. I'm definitely coming back.

I had never been to Maialina before and after my visit this weekend I will certainly be returning! The website was easy to navigate so it made making my reservations incredibly easy. Upon arrival to Maialina my party only had to wait a brief moment before we were taken to a freshly sanitized table. Although there were a fair amount of patrons in the restaurant at the same time, the tables had been spaced out enough that there was not a great deal of concern in terms of COVID. 

Once we were seated we were immediately met by our waitress wearing latex gloves  who provided us a water jug. We were able to get our appetizer order in quite quickly and even though it was a busy night we received our appetizers quite quickly. After being served the delicious tomato bruschetta, we placed our main course order and it certainly did not disappoint. 

When our food arrived at our table it was piping hot and looked incredibly fresh. I can easily say this was some of the best pasta I have ever had. Maialina is definitely a gem in the fountain square area that I will be returning to. 

In terms of parking, there is an abundance of parking spots within a short distance of the restaurant. The staff were incredibly friendly and efficient. The food was delicious and the ambiance perfectly matched a cozy authentic Italian restaurant.

Awesome food. Try the pork belly. The BBQ sampler is great as is the desert cookie. 

Pretty great craft beer selection though wine is either Sutter home for the little bottles or a full bottle for anything decent. 

Highly recommend.

Hail to the pig!!

Conveniently located less than half a mile from the convention center, Butcher delivers a lunch guaranteed to put convention goers to sleep for their afternoon sessions.

I tried the pork BBQ sandwich done up with coleslaw, Carolina style with a kick of Cajun spice.  Delicious.  

We beat the lunch rush by getting there at 11:30.  Mind you, even on a holiday the line backs up to the door.  Order and pay at the counter and then your food will be delivered to your table.  It's a fairly small dining area both inside and out so consider taking your food to go.

Great lunch spot in NOLA!

The pho here is okay and is one of those things you order when you have a cold and it is February, but the mango milkshake, oh the mango milkshake!  It is a bit pricey, but it will change your whole outlook on life, especially if mangoes are in season.

My boyfriend and I just spent an entire day cleaning up my place for a visit from his parents.  We were dirty and cranky and finally I just said the magic words, "mango milkshake", we dove out of my apartment and down the street, got the milkshakes and sat on a bench in the school yard drinking them and watching the fireflies.  All was good with the world.
We LOVE Thai Basil! From the lettuce wraps to the pad Thai noodles to the red curry, everything is always delicious at this family-ran business.

Friendly service. 
Decent prices from a huge menu selection of all American food. 

Worst thing was it took me a while to remove the paper wrap from the napkin and flatware. Must have glued it closed!

Worth the stop if you are in the neighborhood. 

I would note that there are not many good restaurant in this neck of the woods.

Golden Dragon at the corner of Liberty & Franklin, Trenton, NJ., looks like a new entry in the Chinese Take Out Wars.  The shop is cleaner than many, with room for four tables for those who prefer to eat in (like me).  The young family that runs the show seem to know what they're doing, with the wife at the counter taking orders and money, and hubby wok and rolling in the kitchen.  The third wheel, perhaps a brother, helps out and does deliveries.  

The lunch specials are the standard pork, chicken and shrimp in a variety of overlapping goopy sauces.  The fried rice is made in one large batch and has the yellow dye of most other chicken broth based steamers.  Unlike many of the other houses, this one is full of chunks of pork, peas, onion and carrots.  It actually tasted good.  My Pork Egg Foo Young was two pancakes, crisped edges, and loaded with meat, veggies and spouts.  The brown sauce was decent and packaged separately to keep things firm and able to be used at will.  It was a decent version of this old time dish.  

Service was as limited as you would expect a basic take away store to be.  No accommodation for customers wanting to eat at a table.  Everything packaged in styro and plastic, with thin fork and spoon to handle the mouth shovels. 

Still, at under $6., with soup or soda, it was a good deal.   

Nice quality for a take out joint, even if they don't really want you eating there.  Offer hot tea in addition to soda, and put the food on a real plate with better plasticware for those who eat in, and Golden Dragon could easily be a four star experience in take out cuisine.

UPDATE: MAY 3, 2017 -  Have to say that my second visit to Golden Dragon has put me in a generous mood about the quality of their food. Today I sampled their Hot & Sour Soup and General Tso's Chicken.  

The soup was surprisingly good.  It contained fresh cut mushrooms floating on top, and two types of soft tofu beneath.  The vinegar quotient was just right, and with the other veggies within, was about the best Chinese take out hot & sour I can remember tasting. Sucked all of that plastic container's contents dry.  The Chicken was also mostly meat and less shell, with a nicely balance spicy/sweet dark brown topaz sauce. The fried rice was plentiful, and although mass produced, still granular and full of pork, pea, carrot, etc. chunks.  

Overall, an impressive lunch from this far flung outpost of the Chinese Empire at the corner of Franklin and Liberty.  

Do it again, and you could find yourself the recipient of a full forth star.  But, for now...

3.5 Stars, with a bullet!

What a disappointment. It's a beautiful building and I loved the decor. If only the food was as impressive. The menu wasn't exciting and the prices were steep. We don't mind paying for a good meal however and were looking forward to our dinner.  The pork-chop was over cooked and the beans raw. The wedge salad was mediocre at best. Worst of all our server asked if we'd like some biscuits while we waited for our meal. Only when the bill arrived did we discover we'd paid for the tiny, hard attempts at a biscuit. The manager came to see if the pizza we ordered to replace the $28 pork-chop was okay... It was also mediocre but by now we just wanted to get out. The manager asked if we wanted another glass of wine.  Ummmm... Not sure if this was an attempt to compensate for the bad meal or if he was trying to sell 2 more glasses. We won't be back unless they change the menu and the chef. 2 stars for the decor and the hope that Gray's lives up to its potential.
Brunch on a Saturday....... ughhhhhhhh no Redfish.....however the Chicken and waffles, were great. Crispy filet boneless breast, buttermilk waffle and the pepper jelly was very tasteful.

So good.  I saw yelp reviews and decided to try.  Not cheap-- plan on $25-40 a person, but delicious.  I had stuffed grouper.  The scallop and shrimp stuffing was wonderful.  The whole presentation and flavor was wonderful.  A puffed pastry potato came with it, and I couldn't resist.   My wife got snapper and shrimp that we also shared and loved.  Excellent meal and really great personal service.   Bravo, this will be a place we visit.

We just moved to the area and are SHOCKED  by the awesome prices.  We got a huge shopping order for extremely decent prices. While there we had lunch. Their pizza is a great value and delicious, and so were their hoagies. We will be shopping here from now on!

Great service and absolutely wonderful food.  Touches of unique sauces bring the dishes to life.  Our server Dereck was extremely polite, helpful, and attentive with the drink refills.

The dumplings were the best I have ever had with the house made ginger soy sauce.  The fresh rolls were delightful and extremely fresh.  Our favorite dish was the chicken pad see ew, which was bursting with flavor with plenty of chicken.

Highly recommended!!

I love the caipirinhas!! The original lime--so fresh and crisp!
The food is wonderful.
I've been there for dinner 5 times and everything was fabulous including the service.
The decor and lighting inside is very interesting in each room. Dining outside is nice as well- you get a show! I've seen some real characters walking by!

The burger menu is quite extensive, with an innovative array of toppings that make the act of choosing what to get quite exciting. 

I got the New Mexico burger, which came with pickled red onions and queso and green peppers - it was quite messy to eat (not a great first date location), but was flavorful...not the best burger I've had (might be because of the texture of the bun, it seemed a bit limp), but decent. You also have the option of crunchifying the burger for free (which basically means adding chips in your burger, which seems like an unusual concept but 1) it's free chips and you can get it on the side and 2) chips make everything better!)

Also ordered the sweet potato fries, which were good but not as amazing and crunchy as I remembered - the horseradish mustard sauce that comes with it is quite yummy, so worth a try! 

They also have spiked milkshakes, which is great for a casual midday celebration when you want to drink but don't feel like ordering an actual alcoholic drink. 

Overall, I like the menu selections and the innovative nature of it, but execution seems to have gone down a bit from the first few times I came here.
This local Cinnaminson place is wonderful! The staff is friendly and the chicken soup is insanely good.

Brownies and fudgies are great.  Service was so incredibly slow.  They were in no hurry to help the next customer.  Perhaps my impression of their slow service is because I compared it to bakeries in Chicago.

Friday night we were craving Chinese food but did not want to go out in the cold.  After looking at several reviews on Yelp, we chose the Red Door and ordered crab rangoon, pot stickers, wonton soup, orange chicken and hunan beef.  Everything was great.  The chicken were nice sized nuggets and not overcooked, the vegetables still had some crunch, nothing was swimming in some unrecognizable sauce.  The heat was just right and the portions were generous.  Finally, everything arrived when expected by a very nice person.  The only advise I would give to this restaurant is that when you are getting this size order, you may want to send more than one set of chop sticks.  : ) Also, we got a really tasty rangoon but it was not the crab rangoon we ordered. I wish this place the best and many years of success.

First time in Santa Barbara, first time at this restaurant. It was nothing short of amazing! The seafood gumbo was incredible!!! The staff were all very friendly; side note: I went on Christmas Eve and I'm not sure if this is a regular occurrence but they handed out little music booklets and the entire restaurant sang "What a Wonderful World" as the staff went around toasting everyone, it was so cool! But the food was beyond good, and that dark chocolate souffle! My goodness! Also, if you're a non-drinker like myself, they have Buckler for their non-alcoholic beer option, which thrilled me to no end. Overall, I would absolutely recommend this restaurant and if I find myself back in Santa Barbara in the future, I'll definitely be coming back. Thanks for the memories!

Where else would we go on National Meatball Day!? I love Mimi Blue...I have been here several times and I have never had a bad experience! Tonight was no exception... fantastic service, delicious food, wonderful atmosphere. I ordered a variety of meatballs with a variety of sauces...they were all amazing! I highly recommend getting the "Special Ball" and the "Special Sauce" to go with it. It's a rotating selection... always an adventure! We felt totally safe here and safety measures were in full force.i would definitely come back.

Hi, guys! I want to share my experience because we just wasted $20.  
We ordered a regular greek salad, 3 skewers and gyro meat, no pitas. We've received no gyro meat and three pitas. That's fine. 
The size of the salad was good, I was so excited. Unfortunately, 95% of a salad in the box was an iceberg salad(the cheapest thing you can put in the salad). There were 2 pieces of tomato (not chopped), 2 rounds of cucumber, 3 tiny olives (worst taste ever). $6,99! Have they ever seen a greek salad before? It's a greek place they've got to know how it looks like. 
Skewers were tiny. Meat was overcooked. We ask for medium, got a well done. Chicken was dry and tasteless. Sauce got warm.
That was our first experience and the last. Most of the time I'm to lazy to write reviews. But these guys well deserve it. Save your time and your money.
As always food was great and service was also   Sampler platter for friends from out of town was excellent and they were pleased and full!

Great coffee house.  Coffee was fresh and the breakfast sandwich was tasty.  Give this place a try - you will not be disappointed.  My husband and I enjoyed it so much we ran there the following day but sadly, they were closed (they are closed Monday and Tuesday).  Check their hours before going.  We will go there again the next time we are in St. Petersburg.

This is apparently the best Indian food in Tampa... and if so... everyone there is missing out... bc this place sucks! The chicken tikka masala was inedible, the masala dosa was only okay and I didn't even enjoy the garlic or cheese nan. It's a nice gesture to provide free dessert with your meal but even with that, would not recommend this place at all as far as food is concerned.

I have been here twice: for my mom's birthday and for an anniversary with my husband. Both times the food was delicious and the service was exceptional. The warm bread with butter is wonderful and a great way to start the meal. The onion soup is the best onion soup I've had! Simply exquisite. The steak with fries, although it sounds simple, is amazing as it comes with a creamy sauce. The beef with vegetables is my favorite dish because the meat is incredible soft and flavorful. Be sure to save room for dessert! 
Although it is on the pricey side, it is completely worth it!
Happily surprised to get New York style pizza close to home! This will be my go to now that Grimaldis closed..
Breakfast packages are amazing! Quite possibly the best pancakes ever. Sausages are fantastic. Everything bagel breakfast sandwich with pork roll. Can't go wrong.

Whoa! Do not let these photos fool you and do not waste your money here. Unbelievably bad, over priced and skimpy sisco food. Our waitress was amazing which is the ONLY reason we did not complain. We will not be back. I should add, this is the F Terminal in Philly airport-  
SAD!

I'd been wanting to check out Chateau Thomas for a couple years, and when I found out that this weekend they were having their Grape Harvest Festival, it gave me the extra boost I needed to use the gas to drive out to Plainfield. It's not that far of a drive, and the gas was worth it! A couple girlfriends and I went and had a great time. 

When we pulled up, I was a bit thrown off guard - the winery is smack in the middle of a commercial development with hotels, Steak & Shake and Subway. This is, in my opinion, the biggest detractor to the winery. I thought it would be in a different setting, away from other businesses. Call me crazy, but I thought it might actually be in a vineyard! I was wrong, but don't let that stop you from going. 

They make the wine on-site and have some great selections. We went for the 2006 Dry Riesling, which I highly recommend! I'm a fan of sweet wines, so I also tried the Sweet Aubergine because it is their best seller. Only go for it if you really like sweet wines - it was way to sweet for me! I also took home a bottle of Muscat Canelli - it's light and fruity, with just enough bubbles. They also have a great variety of cheeses, spreads, meats and crackers to accompany your wine (sadly, no baguettes or other breads). 

If you are in Indy and debating taking the drive out to Chateau Thomas, do it - Plainfield isn't too far away and the wine is well worth it!

Pepo's is hands down my new favorite breakfast spot! $3.99 for two eggs, HUGE serving of Cuban toast and killin cafe con leche... although I went option #2 with the added Cuban ham for $1- well done Pepo's!!! 

Ask for the homemade hot sauce, it's more like pico. 

They're a counter service restaurant serving breakfast and lunch following traditional Cuban fare options with fantastic flavors.
they wrote the wrong address down. waited over an hour for our food ... also paid for a cannoli that we didn't receive. won't be going back
The staff was great..I went on 12/26/15 .it was insanely crowded, raining and cold.  This was my first time and they gave me A+ service.

What a wonderful experience here! The food was mouth watering and perfect! I had prime rib with a loaded potato and they were exactly what I needed! The atmosphere was chill and welcoming. The smells were delectable and the service was efficient. Also tried their fried mushrooms and zucchini, delicious! Going to have to come by here again when passing through!

The name fits because it is certainly not gold.  The food was better than the unattentive service however. I should have gone into downtown Boise, but was tired from a flight in for business.   Don't bother getting a drink unless your cutting back, because they are watered down in my opinion. However, the liquor stores close early in this bible thumping state so I had no choice but to quench my thirst here. Maybe the bartenders pours light to save the juice for her regulars. I've seen this before and think it's very tacky. I won't be back.

I have  issues with Milkboy ( both locations).  I am glad  there is a cool independent  coffee shop/cafe with two locations ( Ardmore and Bryn Mawr in front of BMFI).   This Milkboy is  big and spacious with  good seating and good lighting.  I appreciate  that.  Easy parking nearby.  I like that too.  I also love the fact they  use hormone  free organic  milk in  their  drinks.  Nice menu with   good  healthy  eating options.   The things I do not like about this Milkboy.  The staff  has a MAJOR  attitude problem.   Every time  I  go up to the counter I feel like I am   bothering  someone by merely  ordering a hot chocolate.  The  staff  seems permanently  pissed off and angry     No one  asked me if I wanted  whipped  cream.  I  smile and say thank you.  They barely respond.   So  that  immediately  makes the  vibe of the place LESS  friendly.  The prices here are  high too.  More  expensive  than Starbucks for the  same  coffee drinks.    I  don't  come here very often ( about 3 times a year).   Attitude of the staff  needs to change.  Hoping the owner(s) read  their Yelp reviews.

The food was a separate experience from the service. The plates were pricy but I thought worth it. The service however was as if taken from a family chain restaurant. Many times we felt as if we should be teaching her about the menu. If they would tighten up on the service and the owner dress a bit cleaner and possibly shaven this restaurant would receive all five stars. A great location, atmosphere, and product. Will try again in a few months.
Out of business, drove by 6/10/2014 and stopped. Vacant, with signs on the door. Stinks, just started to enjoy the place.
I went her and i did not enjoy it i got coconut shrimp and it was not fresh and they did not have seasonong

Worst service ever. If there were negative stars
 they would get them for sure. Not sure what to even think or say further other than don't go and waste your money. Even got chicken, which I dining order, in place of some of the fish. Speechless!!

Really good sandwiches and cheap the old number 7 is my favorite, like a trip to Roma and of corse wash it down with a cannoli only $2.50
Eat here once a week , love it

Tried to hit this place up on a Friday at 6pm. No way. It's packed.  Went Sunday at 6pm. Was told the wait would be 10 minutes for inside. Wait was 30 minutes. That's cool. Got seated. Took server about 10 minutes to say hi and when he did he said he wasn't actually our server and would just be bringing us water. Um, ok. So we wait. For awhile. All employees look chill. But who is our server? Same dude comes back and is asking about our order... and I'm like "so ur our server?"  and he goes "sure". Wtf? We order. It's basic. It was weird y'all. I spent 20 years in the restaurant biz and I could have turned this table 3x EASY! We got no attention and when we did it was so fake. Like when my server was like "oh let me get u a little to-go box" I was like "yes plz thank u" and it took the dude a HALF HOUR to get that to-go box for me. I even put my credit card out to signal an SOS. Service was pathetic. Also, yes I'm petty... I asked for my burger to be medium and it was rare AF and I was waiting to tell someone but NOBODY came to ask how it was. Ugh. Am so disappointed. The place is so cool but the service was sooooooo bad.

Well what an awful experience at the BP's by the Manning Cineplex. 

Starts off with our waitress arguing with us about a schooner beer prices, when we were asking for clarification on the price. Once we receive the beer it comes to us flat! 

We then proceed to order our food, spinach dip as an appetizer and then wings as our meal. 

Spinach dip comes out quickly and fresh. Then literally 3 minutes later; our wings are on the table. Without even a bite of our appetizer. The manager offered to take them back and put under the heat lamps, but we don't enjoy our food being cooked under the lamps. The wings were supposed to be fried, but mine came out soggy and not crispy. With 1 celery and 1 carrot shaving... not even a full carrot. 

The best part of this awful experience is ... How many servers does it take to do roll-ups on the bar side. Yep that would be 4. And how many tables were occupied on the bar side only 4 tables. Our waitress was more interested in the roll ups and conversation amongst the other servers, as Snapchat is a perfect conversation to have to listen too. 

Then it was time to pay our bill. No apologies about the food coming out, or how the flat beer tasted. Cash / credit machine. When the waitress saw what we paid at the end she ripped the customer copy receipt and basically threw the it in our faces. With no good nights , good byes, have a great evening. 

We finished our conversation off amongst the 2 of us, and dealt with death glares and unpleasant side way glances. 

Note to self - before sitting in the bar glance and see who the servers are on that evening to deem a good or horrible experience.

What an awesome choice for a unique Santa Barbara restaurant! We were able to make a last minute reservation for a weekday dinner and they sat us at a fire pit table. There was four of us and we decided to split a bunch of food family style! 

Cheese halloumi: delicious! my favorite thing we ordered! grilled sheep's cheese with watermelon, cucumber, and mint. Never had anything like this before but the salty/sweet combo was tasty, kinda reminded me of cantaloupe/prosciutto. 

Vegetarian feast: lots of lots of yummy veggie apps like hummus, baba ghannouj, falafel, tabbouli, cheese sambosik, labneh. Portions of everything was big and perfect to share with the table! I loved the variety, but the baba ghannouj and cheese sambosik were my favorite. 

Kebab combo: grilled beef, lamb, chicken, came with a side salad which had a delicious lemony dressing, and rice pilaf. It also came with some sort of whipped garlic sauce which was also delicious 

Overall: 5/5 would recommend Zaytoon! We spent about $35 per person for food and a drink, including tax and tip - very reasonable for the tasty large portions! I loved the fire pit in the middle, and it kept us warm and set a nice ambiance for our dinner.

Very creative and vibrant menu. I enjoyed my food and my dreamsicle mimosa. Unfortunately, we were seated at the bar where we had a clear view of the open kitchen. This was mostly a delightful part of dining but it got a little turned off when I noticed that one of the cooks had dirty fingernails. It distracted me from my food and I couldn't think of anything else after that. I would've given this place 5 stars if it weren't for that.

from the rasperry bellini to the final bite of sashimi, this was probably the single most decadent night of eating in my entire life.

if i could eat the toro tartare every day, i probably would.

I wouldn't make a special trip here, but if I was in this Virtua facility for a few hours this is a good choice for a quick bite. Trish is very experienced here so after an X-ray appt she convinced me to give it a try. 

We both got chicken quesadillas and I have to admit they were good. Not authentic Mex good, more diner-ish but meat was tender and there was plenty of it as well as peppers, onions and cheese. Rounding up slightly but a huge leap ahead for hospital cafeteria food. 3.75 convenience Yelps

Great lunch specials!  I usually get the $10 spicy salmon roll and 2 pieces of nigiri ( I get the eel!). I love that you order at the counter and they bring the food to you. It's still presented really nicely and you have actual plates and nice chopsticks, but this allows us to go there and have a nice meal and be on the road within a 40 minute timeframe at most. I'm hoping to try the bento box next time I'm there as its only $10 as well.

Gin martini, oysters , crab cakes and philly sandwich.  I am from OC CA. First time in Philadelphia and this is the food list I was sent to try.  I was not disappointed with fresh  blue points 
Thanks for the home pub feeling

TL;DR - Incredibly delicious food. Cheap prices. Great staff.

Center city needs more places like this!

Although modest in size, Tuscany Cafe is big on flavor and value. All the food tastes homemade; like it was prepared with love by someone who genuinely cares about the quality of their product. Everyone raves about the chicken salad--and don't get me wrong, it's great--but my favorite is the PROSCIUTTO, EGG & CHEESE BREAKFAST SANDWICH (get it on one of the most massive croissants you've ever laid eyes upon). I don't know where they're getting their prosciutto, but it just tastes better than most places. It should also be noted that their lunch panini are large enough for two meals; I regularly save the second half for the next day (and no one would accuse me of being a scrawny guy).

Tony and staff are warm, welcoming, and kind people. There's often classic rock, oldies, or classical music playing when I visit. A welcomed respite from the hustle and bustle of city life.

As an added bonus, I once went there late in the day (3:30ish?) and was given a free muffin in addition to my order.

Just. Good. People.

TL;DR - Incredibly delicious food. Cheap prices. Great staff.

my husband and I brought our 2 young children in and I appreciated the staff being quick, efficient and accurate. I forgot to look at name tags but the young lady and young man that helped us were very nice and a pleasure to speak with.

I love ikea but they might as well shutdown small land if they're never going to have enough help to watch the kids that are being brought there.  Every time I've come they have a few kids there but claim a 1 hour wait.  Why have a daycare that never has open spaces?
Bread tasted old and was dry. Beef had no flavor and there was hardly any provolone. This is a big disappointment and will definitely hurt the brand name over this airport excuse.
Extremely slow service. Brought some food out and then took 10 minutes for rest to show up (and that only because we asked hostess to check on it). And silverware was dirty - yuck.
A little pricey but well worth it! Had the BLT and alpine cake......freaking awesomeness!

Stopped by One Shot yesterday morning. Not my first visit, but the first time I really made it a point to take in the whole experience rather than just grab something and go. 

I definitely dig the vibe and character of the shop itself. The old Frogger machine, book selection, bike wheels as shelf-ends, and hodge-podge furniture make it super homey. I can't say anything good or bad about the service, really. There were four baristas behind the counter, two of which helped us and two seemed to be training. They certainly weren't abrasive or rude as some reviews have claimed, but didn't make much of an impression either. Both of the bagels we had were great - mine had an amazing pumpkin butter on it.

As for the coffee, we had mixed results. My girlfriend had a pumpkin latte, which looked worthy of a magazine cover or advertisement of some kind. One of my favorite things about independent coffee shops is the creativity and craftsmanship that is allowed to go into such works of art. I couldn't taste much coffee flavor in her drink, mostly just pumpkin and milk. But that's why it was her drink. I ordered a double macchiatto. Appearance was pleasing. The foam was velvety smooth, no bubbles. The barista making both our drinks was clearly an ace with the milk steaming. Unfortunately, the espresso was the worst I've ever tasted. Not sure if it was the beans, barista, or the equipment but I was very disappointed.

Cozy place to hang out. I'll have to give the espresso a second chance another time.

So, where do I start?
Had to flag down the bartender to order beers and an app. 15 min later received beers 45 min later received app. We also ordered 2 burgers. Over an hour later (probably like an hour and a half) still no burgers. Asked for the check (because now I'm hangry and still no burgers) and charged $20 more, not for the burgers, but for the 4 beers. Told our waiter and as he is changing it directly in front of us he is cussing under his breath. His name tag said Frank and he was inattentive and rude. The cheese steak egg rolls were good though..

The atmosphere here is outstanding. The walls are covered with paintings and relics attributed to the cowboy style. Our waiter was very attentive. The food was great. They served us free bread with butter. I had lobster soup and chopped steak with brocolli. All was very tasty and the wait wasn't long. The person I was with had a full rack of ribs which were very good too.
I would certainly come here again and implore you to come as well.

I came here with a few friends that said it was delicious. Meh, I'm happy I came though. They service is great and friendly but the food is not. Very bland and flavorless. We had a lot of the dishes that were on the menu as we were a lot of us and I got to try all of them and I was not I impressed. Not sure if it the food from the country that is like that or it was just this place. I've only been to another Guatemalan restaurant but it was in Atlanta and I don't remember it been bland. 

Overall, I would not come back or recommend it as something I liked but something that is available.

My friends stayed at the hotel and not wanting to leave and lose our parking spot, we decided on the Signature Grill.

We sat on the patio because the weather was nice and our waitress was very friendly. We ordered our drinks and it came quickly. However when my friend and I asked for an orange slice for our blue moon, it took a long time to get it and we had to ask someone else. I'm assuming it must have been busy or she must have forgot.

When asking about the menu, the waitress was very knowledgable which helped out a lot. We got our appetizers really quick and they were really delicious. Our food came by quick too and everyone seemed to be happy with their food. I had the posole which was really good and filling.

Overall the place was nice. It overlooked the desert landscape which was nice. Not really something I would look forward coming back to but it was a nice experience.

I do have mixed feelings about our experience here. I feel like the staff was not really in sync and it was noticeable. The 2 older gentlemen were very gruff and business like while the younger wait staff was more personable maybe didn't pay enough attention to what was going on in the restaurant. Our food was good. I did ask if the palak paneer was spicy and the older waiter told me he would make it not spicy. I can assure you it was spicy even for husband. I still could eat it though. We did get Kashmiri nan which was delicious. Kinda sweet so surprised they have under appetizers. Chicken korma was great.  Chai tea was lukewarm and just okay. I am anxious to try their lunch buffet sometime in order to try different dishes.
Wonderful beer, food and service. Kid friendly. They have shared parking with Target which is nice.

Oh my, this is one of the best places I've eaten at in a long while. Came here on a visit to family in Clearwater. Super friendly staff, absolutely delicious food, and the prices are ridiculously reasonable for what you get. The pigeon pea rissoto and the churrasco were outstanding. I even pilfered my daughters' "kids meals" of chicken, rice, and tostones. But what I will remember the most is the flancocho - worth the trip by itself. Will make every effort to come back. In the meantime, I hope they add a few more options on the beer menu like Jai Alai and Medalla.

I saw online that they had gluten free options. The gluten free rating is 100%. They are clean which is key to be gluten free not just by ingredients but by attention. I think if you can keep a gluten free kitchen then you are clean all around and a great choice.
Great little family restaurant. Really friendly and helpful staff. They serve some of the best empanada I've ever had.

Love the habit! This location gets so busy! No iside seating so it gets pretty crowded. Good quality burgers. I have not tried their salads or chicken, however their regular cheeseburgers and so good.

Still find the food comforting & consistent. However; I don't enjoy a very warm atmosphere, where there are no ceiling fans to circulate the air & when you ask your server to pls tell management, they act scared to death. The manger scares me too. lol we don't go as much

Had a meal here with my high school friends right before our last winter break ended.  Great food, great service at this family-owned restaurant.  The two daughters are hard working and provide excellent customer service.

The pho had very authentic taste, and this restaurant even had mini melts ice cream, much to my friends and my delight.  Fun fact- you don't see those ice creams in supermarkets because they are kept at a lower freezing temperatures than normal ice cream.  Another fun fact- mini melts after pho is a great dessert option.

5 star pricing if you ask me!! A hidden gem of sushi! My friends and I really enjoyed it this restaurant and man do they feed you! For $15 you get to pick three rolls (8 pieces each)! I will be returning!

We bought an entertainment book from our son and this place had an online coupon in there.  When I presented it to the waitresss she said she couldn't accept it. We read the fine print and there were no restrictions. When I questioned why she couldn't accept it she became very rude and insulting.  She must be a relative of the owner. Never again will we go here. The food is only soso. There are better Greek places.

Absolutely love this place! Great place to have a drink, be social, and enjoy some local Nashville flavor while feeling safe. A group of 5 of us sat outside. There's a lot of seating and we went on a Friday around 6:00pm (happy hour!) and there were plenty of tables available and live music! I got a flight of beer which is generous amount for only $12. Great way to try new tastes!
Nice change of pace for a quick bite to eat. Tri-tip and Reuben Piadinas were tasty and reasonably priced.

So I am here for some work in the area. I left work pretty late tonight and their kitchen was already closed. Over an hour closed.. and the owner Lee made sure I had a meal. Hospitality like this is was drives a great business! Thank you for accommodating me while working in the area.  This is my second visit in two days and love the atmosphere and food!
Service was amazing. Staff was very sweet. And food was to die for. You need to try the octopus appetizer and the Buratta! Great atmosphere and strong drinks!

I think this restaurant is considered "good" because the portion sizes are incredibly generous. Sometimes people overlook the quality of the food because it's such a a great value. My family and I weren't impressed with the service and food. The "rolls" were way too big. They were tasty, but why do they have to give the equivalent of a softball and a half of bread to each person at the table? Other restaurants--better restaurants--provide a small loaf or two for the table. It makes no sense! And the butter cups are huge as well. Just seems so wasteful!
My wife ordered the quesadilla and was told they were "premade" when she asked if they could make it without the chicken. The cheese sticks were clearly frozen and the tomato sauce had a "vomit-like" aftertaste. The beef sandwich was nearly 20-24 inches long and thrown together. We won't be back. Menu is huge, don't think it's manageable to execute anything with excellence when there is too much to make.

Ordered take out here for the first time. Went to get my food right when it said it would be ready and it wasn't it. Brought it out. I checked it and it wasn't even my order. The girl at the front took the French fries out and then took back the other food but didn't confirm what my order was supposed to be. Brought it out again and attempted to give me cold fries that were sitting there for 10 minutes. Refused the fries. Checked my order and it was incorrect AGAIN! Asked for a manager. He confirmed what I wanted and what was originally ordered. 10 minutes later, had the correct food and it was "on the house". Got it home to eat and the burgers were burned to crap. Charred so badly that I couldn't taste the other ingredients on the burger. I didn't ask for it well done. Even if I did, it shouldn't taste burnt. Threw all of it away and ate cereal for dinner instead. Don't rush my food because you messed it up. I'd rather wait and have it be correct than taste like crap. The girl at the front was more concerned about her cell phone and gossiping with her friend who was a waitress, as she kept leaving in the middle of people walking in for a table, to gossip about whatever was on her phone. Don't bother going here. Three people in front of me also received incorrect orders as well...waited 30 minutes past my promised time to get food that I ended up throwing away.

I'm just echoing all the other 5 star reviews at this point... this place is good... dang good.   The line will be long, it will be hot and you will be sweating by the time you place your order. You will just want to eat and then realize you have to wait another 20 minutes for your food. By the time it arrives you might be a little hangry, just relax and take a bite.  

The breading is crispy, the meat is juicy and the flavor is spot on.  My 5 month old son had a bit of an accident out of his diaper (I won't go into details) and I kept on eating.... that's how good it is. A must when in Nashville.
Best food. Been here few times in 15 years and always great food. To be consistently exceptional is not common, esp in SB.

Best pizza in the city. Awesome Italian beef sandwich. I can't say I've ever had a bad anything here and I've been dozens of times. This place saved Irvington by singlehandedly starting the revitalization. So many great places now. We love going down and making a night of it.

I live in Jacksonville FL and was there to see my father for a week and went in to order 8 pizzas to bring back with me they made all eight and wrapped them up for me and froze them for me to transport to Florida Awesome people and great pizza Will be doing it again

Hmmm... how would you describe this place?
A. "the Chipotle of Pasta"
B. "Sneaky way of serving Cafeteria style food"
C. "Ethnic food without the culture"

Tough, but I choose "B."

It's just another Pei Wei, but with cheaper ingredients.  Not to mention, when would it ever be appropriate to serve Mediterranean Asian and Italian?  Were they expecting regular patrons from the U.N. Council?

Good service, clean place, food is so-so.  The major downside is how cramped it feels.  Even when it's not busy, the tabletops are the size of trashcan lids and it still feels claustrophic.  

If you're there to shop at the mall, it's probably the right place to go if you're saving your money for Nordstroms (however, Nordstroms has their own restaurant).  

Meh... 

But really, is there any place worth eating around Greenhills?

I had a gift certificate from my dear friend so I decided to go last weekend with the fiance. I wasn't really sure what to expect but had an idea based on the Yelp reviews. When we got there we decided to try 3 small dishes for $14 instead of a full plate. That was a great idea because we loved the variety of options. 

I got in line and a lady who worked there came up to us to explain how things worked at the restaurant. We asked for recommendations and got everything she recommended. We shared chicken tenders, kung pao brown rice, and fried sweets. The chicken tenders were plentiful. I cannot believe how filling they were and quite delicious! I would order that again but I would also like to try new things. The fried sweets (sweet potato fries) were a bit on the soggy side. They tasted good but they were a bit disappointing because of the texture. The kung pao brown rice blew our minds. I can't even explain it because so many things were happening in my mouth and there are no words. I tasted soy sauce, rice, quinoa, walnuts, and other delicious things. Trust me, if you're adventurous go try it!
