Now obviously they are in completely different categories -- Shaya high end dining, and Cleo's basically a low budget eats type of place. But the food here is fantastic. Super fresh, light, and flavorful. Tonight I went with a friend and we had the Egyptian salad and the Greek salad -- both excellent, through I preferred the Egyptian which was perfectly balanced diced cucumber, tomato, green onion, and parsley dressed lightly with lemon juice and olive oil. We also had the lamb kebabs and the chicken shwarma, both which came with rice and hummus and pita. The hummus was so fresh and lemony and delicious. The rice was perfectly cooked and actually flavorful -- normally I hate side-dish restaurant rice as it just tastes industrial and like it has been sitting around forever. This right was light, fluffy, and lightly spiced -- so good. The meats were cooked to well done, but the seasoning was perfect on them, and I didn't mind that they were cooked well since the hummus helped keep them moist. The three of us all had sodas, and left full for $56. Can't wait to go back!

I have wanted to see a movie at Roadhouse Cinemas since they opened, and unfortunately I never plan anything far enough in advance to get tickets. They only show the most popular, mainstream movies and I don't tend to see a lot of those... so when my friend asked me last minute if I wanted to catch the new Star Wars film with her last night because she had an extra ticket I jumped on the chance to go with her. 

This movie theater is a little overwhelming for me, I get easily overwhelmed by large spaces with crowds, and walking in was breathtaking. For some reason I had imagined that this was a relatively small movie theater with intimate crowds. The entrance has a full coffee, ice cream, and popcorn bar, as well as an actual full bar with fun liqueurs like Bailey's and Frangelico. The fresh caramel corn smelled and looked amazing, but we split a bowl of the jalapeno popcorn and OMG it was SOO good. From what I could see the snacks and food was a little pricier than average snack price, but not nearly the cost of regular movie theaters. I think the point here is that they want you to eat and gorge. LOL
The screen itself was HUGE and the seats were so nice, they lay almost all the way back and the seat tables are perfect. The little lights with menu and condiments are also great and there are plenty of napkins, elbow room, and cupholder space.

This theater totally changes the entire movie experience, and takes watching a film to a whole new level. I would definitely come back here to see another film if I can get my act together to buy tickets in advance!

I tried the chicken kabob with rice. It was fresh and flavorful. I also picked up a couple other meals to try later. There were a lot of healthy choices and the calorie content was listed on each package. The lady that helped me was very knowledgeable about the different meals. I would recommend this place if you are looking for a healthy lunch, dinner, or you like to food prep and have a variety of choices.
Excellent lunch, Cajun Cobb Salad with shrimps and sausage. Small but comfortable, quick and cheerful service. Worth a trip, easy to get to from Uptown, CBD and Mid-city.
The eye candy is great... the food is flavorless and tasteless.  I only gave three stars due to the average of the two extremes mentioned previously.
Stopped for Lunch. Friendly atmosphere. Had BbQ salad and my mom had waldorp  salad. We enjoyed them and our $5 Margarita special. Will come back.
A bit overrated, whiz and onions on steak are good, steak has nice flavor, portion was weak though and its overpriced. Jims is much better.

Been there three times, and food was good, tasty, and hot. Very good selection, you just have to ask for lettuce, pico de gallo, and some of you small garnishes you get else where, I find that is good cause most people don't eat that stuff so no waste.  
The tomatillo sauce is excellent and spicy thumbs up.  Will be back for sure!!!!

I love this place! For one the tacos are thee BEST in town. Golden to perfection. Two the service I get when I go is even better. The girls at the counter are nice but there is a guy who is just great! He is a true asset to Kanaloa. Super knowledgable, helpful and genuinely happy to help! I basically depend him to pick out my dinner. Anyways they are a little tucked away and hidden but well worth the visits!

I am very upset now with the business on 2 occasions. 1) about a year ago it was around 9:30 pm and I called to order a pizza for me to pick it up.  The lady said i couldn't pick it up because they could only do delivery even though on the store app it says you can pick up until 10:30 pm. so i asked her again can i pick it up because i live right behind them not even 20 seconds walking and she refused again. so i said well can i get it delivered and told her where i lived which was not even 20 seconds walking and she said i would have to wait 45 min to 1 hour. so i told her never mind and she told me to fuck off which was totally rude and uncalled for. i told my self "first and last time". 2)Usually i order from domino's because they have better tasting pizza and everything else especially the wings and cookie brownie, plus they have good deals and online coupons and better prices too, but today because of the weather i guess the phones weren't working. so tony's pizza closed early today because my boyfriend works there and got off early so i didn't want to drive anywhere because roads are still bad because of the snow. so i said to him "okay lets try ordering from papa johns" so he said "okay". i then ordered online to have it picked up. i order one medium pizza with 6 toppings and an order of 16 piece wings. when i went in i had to wait 10 minutes because one of the guys didn't notice me. when i got my order it all came up to 38 dollars i was so shocked because at domino's i dont pay not even 30 dollars for the same things, so i paid and took my stuff and walked back to my place and when i open up the pizza box only 3 out of 6 toppings were on the pizza i was so pissed off i called to try to get my rest of the toppings but they said i couldn't . i hung up, then i tried the wings and they tasted so bad we had to throw them out because first they weren't cooked well and second the hot sauce tasted DISGUSTING. I was so angry I went back to the store and they told me i couldn't go in.  I am done with them. I will never ever come back again. i rather eat dirt than their food. Please don't order from here it's not worth the money or time.

If you want a great steak, this is the place. Had a T-bone special and it was like my Dad used to make 30 years ago. Didn't care for the ambiance as it was noisy and we were close to a trip of alcoholics but we were there for a good steak and we got it. Reasonably priced and great drinks. Oh, and they gave us a slice of cheesecake for my Birthday with none of that restaurant fanfare. Perfect topper to a good meal.

Make sure you check your order good! I ordered about $25 worth of food for my family and we were missing several items when we got home. The restaurant was clean (brand new) but the staff was new and not confident enough in their jobs yet to provide excellent customer service. I will probably give it another go in a few months. Other than that, its a typical Taco Bell.

I'm in lovvvvvvvvvvvvve with Goldy's.  I would die and go to HEAVING if these guys decided to open a spot in Los Angeles somewhere.  Good thing my parents still live up in Boise, because I seriously crave the Spicy Eggs Benny weekly!  Does Postmates deliver out of state? (Just Kidding)  They serve nice big mimosas that aren't straight orange and it is just an overall FUN and lively place to be with significantly better food than ANY other brunch/breakfast place in all of Ada county!!! Goldy's, I love you!

Do it. The food was very good however the oysters took 30min to show up. When they arrived they were great. Stay away from the blackened boudin. Not to tasty. The crab ravioli was good and spicy  as well and the shrimp and grits were great. The stuffed shrimp was very good but small. Only three. Bread pudding is good but hard to share. Will return.

A great addition to downtown Fishers! I had the surf n turf burger, and bacon cheddar for my wife with truffle parmesan fries. The owner and staff were friendly and helpful! 5 stars. Cool layout and concept.
Slow service. Kitchen closes very early. Live music is good. Very small and cramped. There are better options in Music City.

We used to come here often...but I won't be coming here after my experience last night. When I bit into my burrito, it had glass shards or meth crystals in it...it's Reno so it can honestly be either one. Also, there was a huge ass piece of sharp bone in the burrito. Eat here at your own risk.

I went to this restaurant based on the menu and a few reviews on yelp. I had the duck and it was dry, that is very difficult to do.  The food was just OK, in a town with amazing food OK is just won't cut it. Just not worth the calories

What a wonderful find this restaurant was! Delicious vegan Indian food and kombucha and incredibly friendly service in a lovely brick courtyard. My husband was especially pleased when our server offered extras of any of the dishes on his plate.

Awesome food and great staff. I had the ribs and potato salad. The potato salad was made with cream cheese and was great. The ribs had a great smile flavor and with the tangy sauce it made it even better. Best part? Kid friendly. There's a spot out back for the kids to run around and play. Completely fenced in and they have soccer balls. Great selection of drinks from the bar. I also had the root beer float and it hit the spot. Will go back for sure.
Cold beer, lots of Irish themed decor, and a bag piper on a Saturday night. Can't speak to the food quality as I was just there to drink. Standard Irish pub.

The food and service was excellent, I'll definitely be going back.  

One small note, get rid of the butter-like substance that came with the bread before the meal and go with real butter.

My new favorite place for tacos! I like Tijuana Flats on 4th, but it always upsets my stomach. I want to like Casita Taqueria, but they came up short on my last visit, but this place nailed it. The veggie & especially the Original Fish taco was excellent.

Went again the other night & had The Original fish tacos and the Shrimp & chorizo - they were both awesome!  Make sure you get the chips too - they're homemade.

Dry rubbed ribs. EPIC! I am a rib lover and these had it all. The two foot long slab was tender and super meaty. They were tasty without sauce but the sauce really compliments the ribs. Other sauces sometimes overpower the flavor of the ribs but this was a perfect match. If I had only gotten a half slab I would have kicked myself. I might have to move here from Chicago to get some more.

I have visited this location on a few different occasions, and this review reflects an average of my experiences. Also, 3 stars equals A-OK on the yelp scale. In the past, this location used to have issues with not being open during posted hours and lower quality than the norm for subway. It has been a few months since I visited this location, but a year ago I among other customers was somewhat dismayed by this.

My most recent visit was during the middle of the day as opposed to morning or later evening, which in the past was when I had found the location closed when they should be open.

With that said, during my most recent visit, I did notice a major change for the better. Better attitudes, fresher foods on par with subway standards, prompt service. I liked my food and will come back in hopes that this location has made permanent improvements.

Great spot to come to if you're able to get seating. If you're coming in with a ton of people on a weekend, good luck, the place gets mobbed with moderate waits involved, but oh is it worth it.

The beers are plentiful, the wine isn't bad, and the food is absolutely scrumptious! The portions are sizable, but not overwhelming, and the cooks get it right the handful of times I've been there. since the menu is rotating, it's always been a different experience when it came to the food, but I never found myself complaining once, it's really good grub.

The beers are abundant! So many kinds to choose from, and you can get little pubbers at 8oz each to try a bunch of different beers without hurting the wallet much, all they way up to 40s if you found one to hit home enough to get absolutely plaster off of it... or to bring home to share, we won't tell anyone :D

Kraftwork looks great, too. Dark ambiance with fantastic details to really push the industrial look without encroaching the actually dirty, greasy mess that actually comes along with it. Awesome place I've no qualms bringing people to!

When I'm in town, I have a list of greatest hits that I must visit. But I love being introduced to new joints! Especially when delicious coffee is involved. My friend had suggested this place because of the delicious pour-over coffees and unique sandwich combinations. 

This place is tiny with only three stools inside but picnic tables outside(perfect for the summer!). But it has a chill aesthetic inside with some t-shirts and pour over contraptions for sales. Plus some signage about a coffee club for those passionate about good beans for home. The menu was small but written in chalk, so I imagine a lot of changes in the menu and high quality!

I decided to stick to the original Grick Middle(I was tempted to get the surprise grick but I wasn't THAT hungry) and the phil & seb(honduras) pour-over coffee. The sandwich was on a delicious bun with the most perfect cooked egg, slightly runny, tasty bacon and fresh arugula. I was not disappointed! The coffee tasted great black and I added a little cream for richness. It was divine. I also grabbed a rice crispy treat with the blue whale candy... it was a delicious late night snack while I wrote this review.

I would definitely come again! Tasty and fresh eats & coffee. Mmmmm
Great spot for delicious Mexican food. Terrific service, staff are super friendly and helpful. Great queso and hot sauce bar.

Wandered in here after a hair apt across the street and now we just can't stop coming back! The pizza is amazing.  The flatbreads and inventive and equally as delish.  Fries are the best in our area and we love that the burgers are big and charbroiled.   Anyone looking for a low carb option the cauliflower crust is surprisingly delish!!!
Be prepared to wait!!

This place has one of the most interesting and eclectic menus I have ever encountered. It is a celebration of Southern food and cooking. Much of the produce and herbs are grown on site, and the meats come from local providers like The Hammery in Murfreesboro, where their hams are cured like they were generations ago. Some vegetables are heirloom varieties that have all but disappeared from modern usage. Our appetizers were crisp fried chicken skins with white BBQ sauce, and a charcuterie of cured meats with a type of black pepper biscuits and house made mustard. Both of these vanished within minutes. Each entree was served by several waiters simultaneously, with each waiter taking the time to explain the dish and its sauces, etc.Many of the dishes harkened from generations past, and are prepared the way our ancestors cooked them. My beef was cooked over a wood fire hearth. The drink menu spans an extensive wine list, down through artisan beers and ciders, to Nehi Orange, Grape, and RC Cola. Dining here is an experience that goes beyond just eating. 
     The service was excellent, and the food presentation unique and pleasing. The atmosphere is casual, yet chic. Dining here was both very satisfying and educational. Put this restaurant at the top of your To Do list.
Best tacos around! So glad they finally opened in Oro Valley. The staff is super friendly and the food is just awesome. New favorite spot in OV for sure!

YES - OYSTERS!!!!!
Stumbled across this place later in the night after dinner and drinks and figured we had a little room left for some oysters. We had to wait for about 30min for seats at the bar (which I did not think was bad on a Saturday). We had Oysters, Soup, and Beer & Wine. All were excellent. The oysters are fresh and the service was great - even for sitting at the bar. The place itself is fun/trendy/upbeat and it was the perfect place for us to end the night. 
If you are looking to get an oyster fix in - aren't we all - this is the place to stop in.
YUMMY!!!!!!

Service by Kim was outstanding. Knowledgeable and able to accommodate dietary restrictions with ease. My steak was perfectly prepared. Ambiance was outstanding. IPA recommended by Kim perfect. 
We are from DC and have high expectations. We will come back often to this comfortable and well appointed establishment.

Spent a delightful evening here dining outside on their lovely patio.  Friendly, helpful servers explained menu options well.  Had the heirloom tomato plate and picked 3 meats from the charcuterie selections, which were served with a wonderful locally made mustard and bread.  It was all delicious, would definitely return on my next visit to Indy!

Let me start off by saying, I converted from a regular Starbucks user to The Haus. The son is also a partner and quickly learned my name.  I have been going there at least twice a week at a minimum and frequently for the last 6-7 months and have one of my employees meet me there every Monday morning.  I have also brought several groups of 4 there for lunch and provide continued recommendations for them, as I am local to the place.

This am, the mother of the place sat down at my table with my employee and I and asked us not to move the tables together anymore.  Ok, fair enough.  At that point she began to speak to my guest and say that he needs to by something there every time he comes and not just sometimes!  Mind you, I buy coffee and breakfast there every time I am there including this am.  As I look around I notice that there are maybe 8-10 people in the whole place that holds probably around 35-40, and I am being told that my guest does not buy enough??? Bad call.  

I go there so often that the son knows me by name.  I am one of the few regulars that this business has on a Monday morning, and I have just been told that I am not buying enough? 

The coffee is decent, and the food is average.  This being said, I would recommend going somewhere else, as the mother has no idea what loyalty is.  I am sad to say that I will tell this story to anyone that asks moving forward.  

I am writing this while sipping my second coffee of the morning, back at the Starbucks down the street. Who might I add, is happy to have my business.

A great little hole-in-the-wall place. You'll never find a better burger for $5.95. Heck, I've paid 3-to-4x that and have been disappointed. Not here! Now this isn't the cutesy, ole 'how can I help you'  joint. But if you want a great, no frills/all taste burger- Willy's is it.  Weird thing is- they don't serve fries- only Tatar tots.

Moseyed in for the $15pp Sunday brunch.  There had to be at least 20 different offerings, but I found them to be hit or miss.  

Example hits: the coffee, the fact that there's chocolate thunder cake as part of the buffet (so you can preview the chocolate cupcake... it was way too sweet and WAY too rich with the ganache), bacon, scones.  

Example misses: the chicken salad, tomato slices (not fresh), a few of the cheesy, non-descript looking hot offerings (I really wish they labeled what everything is!  It's really hard to tell... and what about for people with food allergies?). 

Of course, I did not leave without trying the cupcakes!  K got a sundae one, and I tried the bee sting (vanilla cake with lemon curd and honey, and almonds lined around the frosting).  Each cupcake was about $7 after tax!  Yikes.  In a nutshell, they were more quantity than quality to me.  The lemon curd in my cupcake overpowered everything, and I thought it was a powerful lemon cupcake vs. what the description revealed on the sign.

Kayak's is now officially a Kaldi's!  They serve Kaldi's coffee, offer free wireless, and still offer the same menu as before.

This might soon become the Best Coffeeshop in St. Louis.

Also - bonus! - they put shades in, so no more crazy direct sunlight in the main room.  Yay!

Good food. Jack Daniels grill is a win. 

Let me be clear though. Depending on when you go, this place turns into Club Friday's.  From Thursday night on, this place becomes more bar than restaurant.  So, if you're ok with that, then cool. But if your wary of commotion, thirsty dudes and even thirtier chicks, then be warned. 

Now that you've been warned, I must say that I like the place when I decide to go.

We've eaten here three times over the past two months and have had consistently good food and service.  They have a great selection of beers...whatever your preference, they have it. My husband raves about their burgers...cooked the way he requested and delicious. I had a sandwich one time and chicken oriental salad another time. Both were large portions and tasted great. We did appetizers another time and they were all great, as well. Each server we had was friendly and attentive. Can't ask for much more ... Good food, good beer and good service!

This is a very cute little place, very nice place to chill in the morning. I got the strawberry stuffed french toast, and it was delicious, with strawberries and blueberries on top (but it was HUGE, get ready to share). I forgot what my friend got, I'm going to try to get a omelet next time and some other sweets too.
They have a hand written blackboard with dinner menus, it seems interesting, want to go try it out some time. I think they also have some dessert menu.
Excelente comida, todo muy limpio, le doy 4 estrellas y no 5 por que les falta una buena salsa mucho mas picosa para los para los de paladar exigente. Los mejores tacos en toda la área de SB.

This was the worst dining experience I had in New Orleans by far. We were immediately greeted and sat. Our waiter brought us water to drink, and then went M.I.A. for the next 15-20 minutes. Then he took our drink order. Drinks came and he disappeared yet again for another 20 minutes before taking our food order. We had the alligator appetizer, Mac and cheese casserole, boucherie plate, and the pork cheeks. If there was anything good about this place, it's that the food was excellent. However, we ended up waiting 45 minutes for our food. Normally, I would've thought they maybe they were just running behind or under-staffed that night. But that wasn't the case. Other tables around us were receiving much faster service. In fact, I counted 10 tables that were served and seating new groups while we just sat there mostly ignored. We also never got the complimentary rolls with our meal (which they provided other tables quickly) until I had to ask for it when our food came out. Our water was refilled only once throughout the entire time we were there. I found it funny that the only time they were quick on anything was when it came to the check. The food was also rather pricey for what we got, but I can't complain about the quality. 

We spent around 90 minutes in this place being absolutely ignored by the serving staff. As we were running late for a tour by that point, I didn't get a chance to speak to their management about our treatment. This was one of the worst dining experiences I've ever had in my life, and ended our New Orleans trip on a very sour note.

Went here for my birthday dinner tonight and thought everything except the pizza was very average. We started off with the pepperoni pizza which was delicious and the thin crust and tons if pepperoni made it awesome. The "small" portions are huge just so you know, I don't think it is necessary to get a large. None of our pastas had hardly any sauce on them and they were very dry. It was nice thief because our server ended up bringing is extra sauce, it did take like 15 minutes though which was kind of unfortunate because by that time the pasta was cold, and kind of hard from the lack of sauce. The environment is very cool though and I do like the restaurant all in all. Oh, and the meatballs are awesome!

Visited Spasso for an early (4 pm) dinner on a Sunday night.  I haven't spent much time in Media but my initial reaction was that this restaurant is in a really cute area of town.  If the weather had been a little better, I would have liked to take a walk around after dinner.  One thing to note- parking is very limited in this area (we parked in a garage a few blocks away that was free on Sundays).

Once arriving in the restaurant, I was impressed by how nice the space was-- it felt like an old mansion.  This is also a great location for a group dinner. There were two parties of 10+ people in the room we were seated.

Looking at the menu, there is a wide range of options- pastas, chicken, beef, seafood, as well as a number of vegetarian options.  Again, another reason this would be a great place for a group.  In addition, no entree was over $25 (cause you KNOW you have that guy in your family who orders the most expensive item when someone else is treating...)  

The meal started with some bread and this delicious mix of cold marinated vegetables (eggplant, squash, peppers).  I could have eaten an entire plate of that!  For my entree, I went with the crab ravioli in a cream pesto sauce and it was very very good.  The stuffing in the ravioli was excellent and definitely was real crab (sometimes crab ravioli uses fake crab and it tastes nasty- not the case here).

Overall, everyone at our table enjoyed their dishes, atmosphere was pleasant, and service was good:  if I am looking for a place to get a meal in Media in the future, Spasso will definitely be on my mind!
Totally loved this place! Fun friendly crowd! The music was awesome. Highly recommend. It's a must stop in Nashville.

Great service and very welcoming. There wasn't a wait. I was able to sit immediately at the counter. I had raw oysters and a cup of their clam chowder. It was delicious. I recommend you try this spot if you are a seafood lover.

This was a pleasant surprise! The outside looked inviting so I stopped in around lunch time not knowing what to expect. There is a sort of bar/restaurant vibe going on with a great draft list. The bartender was friendly and knowledgeable and suggested a few brews to me all of which ended up really good. But what really surprised me was the food. Not your standard bar fare and the quality you get for the price is really great. I had the catfish sandwich and it really was next level good. Will definitely be back to try their other food selections and to put back a few more brews.

They really have great sushi. The mark of good sushi is the rice called ...wait for it ... Sushi. This place does it well.  And each time I get it the rice is slightly warm which tells you that it's fresh
Really neat place, but good is overpriced. Got the salmon dish, which unfortunately was covered with a hash brown layer. Not bad, but not the ideal way to enjoy salmon.
Food is delicious! So are the drinks! If you sit at a table the wait staff is not that great. Sit at the bar, Tara is awesome!

I decided to try this place out since it was nearby, knowing nothing about it, and was pleasantly surprised to receive the best pizza I've had in a while. Castrillo's should be a frequent stop for anyone in the greater Sylvan area.
Amazing good , super accomodative of food restrictions. If you around the area should definitely try it :) friendly staff too

The pizza is just ehh... I should have just ordered from stogies..The girl on the phone was short and rude on the phone. The buffalo shrimp had little to no buffalo sauce on them and they were made of mostly breading. This place should cut the menu down and focus on perfecting each menu item. Quality over quantity. Possibly hire someone with personality to answer the phones.

Second time here, will most certainly not be the last. Nothing bad to say. Came here to celebrate the Missus' [xx] birthday. SIL is visiting as well to help little sis celebrate. Highlights--
1) the cheesy biscuits in a basket served with a generous serving of whipped butter. 
2) libations...SIL and I had the Crowning Achievement (Crown Royal, sweet and sour mix, and pomegranate, nicely layered), wifey had the Island something, a rum, pineapple, frufru combo. 
3) we passed on the appetizers, but they have some tempting offerings, including giant onion rings and bbq quesadilla with roasted mushrooms and serrano peppers. Next time. 
4) entrees...Mrs. G got the loaded baked potato. This baby was yooge. She ate half, brought the other half home for later. SIL had the pig on a roll, a pulled pork sandwich she said had a quite pleasing heat. I ordered the Lil Baby baby back ribs, a more "modest" 4-rib portion, but packing a good half pound of meat on dem bones. I sampled both the original bbq sawse and the habanero sauce. I feel it's my duty to inform you. The original is sweet and tangy Memphis style, or almost Carolina sweet. Good. The hab left my lips ablaze, which for me, is an essential part of the experience. 
5) dessert...we each chose different items. The ladies opted for pie, SIL had lemon, MRS had coconut cream. I think they approved. I took the signature banana pudding. It didn't taste like someone had just opened an envelope of a premixed powder. It smells and tastes like something made from scratch. 
6) service...shout out to Cierra, she was great, kept checking in to see if everything was good and if we needed anything else. 
With drinks and dessert, we got out for under $23 p/ person before tip, so I think this is a pretty good value.

Great fresh Thai/Fusion. Service was impeccable with a good amount of suggestions and quick but not rushed feel. Of the 6 dishes we ordered, the lettuce wraps stood out the most but every dish was spot on!! I was honestly surprised of the flavor profiles since Hendersonville I dint exactly known for its cuisine. BRAVO

Been here a couple of times when my friends and I are too lazy to go elsewhere and I'm always surprised at how good the pizza actually is.  Loads of toppings and flavor.  I believe the owner hangs out here a lot in the outdoor seating or maybe he's just a regular who knows everyone who works here.  The service is good and I had no complaints.
Great atmosphere and tasty signature drinks. The food was sooooo good! Every bite of each dish has an explosive flavors. I definitely recommend and will be coming back.

We had an Open Table reservation on a busy Saturday night that went exceptionally well. The beautiful hosts were pleasant, knowledgeable and seated us quickly. The menu had selections that were simply amazing, and the entire family was thoroughly satisfied. We had to indulge in the array of desserts and a cappuccino that was so good. The waitress was pleasant and attentive and the management has that operation running at a 5-star level. Looking forward to our next visit!

Our tourist stop of the morning! To start off, they only accept cash, i didnt see it posted anywhere until after we ordered and it was at the bottom of a small table top menu. Luckily I did have cash on me. 

Also this place looks packed all the time, but don't let it discourage you from waiting, the line goes very fast and there is lots of seating. The table turnover is very quick as you only have the beignets, coffee, and cafe-au-lait. My wait was less than 3 minutes.

The beignets are delicouse, soft, and crisp and the cafe-aa-lait was perfect. Very good, and well worth the calories.

Wow this place is busy! The service is like a cafeteria but I feel like I'm at an Italian market! 
They make the best mushroom risotto! !! And the pastries are AMAZING! The pizzas are made to order. And if you want you can order FRESH pizza dough on certain days and make your own! 
Well worth the wait!

The Rusty Pelican is a great example of a restaurant that is successful because of its location. There are some beautiful views- but overall it felt like an upper class Applebee's. Check my reviews. It is rare that I give such a low review. Rusty Pelican slowly worked hard to earn it. 
First, we called the day before our early reservation and asked for a water view. We were told our party of 7  could not have a water view due to social distancing despite us being sat in an entirely empty dining room. That was empty for a good 45 minutes before they ended up seating all three tables in front of the window that they refused to allow us to sit at. 
The food is average. Everything drowning in sauce or cheese. I ordered the lobster tail and requested no sauce. It came basically poached in butter. The broccolini?-same. I ended up just eating the cornbread which was actually really good. My husband ordered the crab stuffed grouper (40$) and described it as average. Overall it felt like banquet food but the kind that was just ok. 
The two stars are solely given for the service. of our waitresses who were great and brought a complimentary dessert for our special occasion. But no amount of customer service could make this lackluster culinary experience worth the near 600$.

A purrfect concept for coffee and cat lovers!  Adorable locally owned cafe with a separate section that allows you to interact and play with friendly kitties from the Humane Society.  And all the cats are adoptable, which is a bonus.  My sister, her family, and I made reservations this past weekend to attend.  I have always owned cats but this was a great way for my niece and nephew to interact with them to see what type of cat their family will be best suited.  By the time we arrived in the afternoon the kitties were most likely worn out from playing with humans all day since a few were sleeping or just enjoying us from a distance.  It was nice to just sit and pet a lazy kitty while the kids played with the active ones.  Very friendly staff, good coffee, and yummy pastries.  Definitely a spot to visit if you're an animal lover!

I've loved this building and am glad Schlafly moved in so you can finally get good beer here! The space is so interesting. It had been a few years since I had been in and I still love it. A very unique environment. It was raining on our visit and the roof was leaking though. Two different tables and water coming in at both. 

The staff wasn't very aware and were kind of off-putting.  Bartender/server was grabby (of plates and glasses not body parts ) and curt. Didn't care much for him. 

But Schlafly beer is great and the building is cool AND they're open during COVID so why complain? 

The menu is similar (not the same) to the bottleworks. I had a pretty good burger. Another in our group had the garden burger and wasn't a fan. Someone else had chicken nachos and LOVED them. 

4 stars for now. Although if I were picking between locations I might choose Maplewood (bottleworks) for a better all around experience.
I had the royale and it was amazing! If you are looking for a good burger goody goody is worth the drive.  Enjoy!

Excellent pizza, over a dozen interesting beers on tap, full bar, nice wine selections, and very friendly staff...what more can you ask for in a pizza joint? Seriously good pizza coming out of a wood fired oven. Don't miss this place!

I only tried the frozen yogurt so far but I like that there weren't a ton of flavors being offered. HEA focused on maybe five flavors and it wasn't overdone like a chain restaurant. Same with the toppings. Scaled down when compared to a chain and you could tell that the fruit was actually fresh and hand cut. The candy toppings were legit (like little Reese's PB cups that actually tasted like they should, as opposed to tasting like stale little lumps of plastic). The place is cute and nicely decorated. Good view and fun to people watch while eating something sweet.

Seriously good sandwiches- we grabbed some a few days ago for lunch. Tried half a fried shrimp po boy and half a crabcake po boy. Whoa, way too much food. Crabcakes were really rich but I loved them. Shrimp was good but not as special. Do yourself a favor and split 1 sandwich between 2 people! The place was packed and there was a bit of a wait to get our food but it was worth it. Seating inside looked crowded and uncomfortable so we headed to the wharf and enjoyed our food sitting on a bench overlooking the Mississippi. 

Cash only!!!

This place has some of my favorite sushi around.  What I like about this place is even when you get it to go the presentation is always on pointe.  The sushi is fresh and the variety offered is awesome.  A few places around seem to have la limited selection but Bonsai Sushi has so many different rolls to choose from.  They have raw, cooked and sashimi.  Pretty much anything sushi lovers may want.  Plus it is delicious .  I love this place and highly recommend it.

Highly recommend the penne alla vodka, so good! Excellent service. We also got two apps which were almost as much as our pasta dish each, they were also good but couldn't compare to the main pasta dish. Extremely authentic Italian!
Nice little Italian joint. Was in town for tournament and a group of us wanted a bite. The chicken Parm and hone made deserts were great! If your in the area try this place

Great seafood! Had the fish and chips with black beans and rice and it was delicious! 2 huge pieces of fish. Really tasty! And our server, Steven, was very good, attentive, and quick. Awesome place! I hate that I live so far! I'll have to come back.

Overhyped garbage. Would be OK if everything on the menu was 30% cheaper, but as it stands, it's a restaurant whose only claim to fame was that they were on the commercial called "Drivers, Dine-In's and Dives". I don't think anything here is as home-made as they would like you to believe. If your grandma cooks like this, your grandma is a lousy cook.

I tried breakfast the other day. Their home fries are like pan-fried mashed potatoes. My eggs were overcooked to hard yellow yolks, when I asked for Sunny Side Up. My hash tasted canned, smelled canned and looked canned. Probably canned. 10 bucks for canned hash, 2 eggs and a small amount of potatoes. Not exactly value-town. When the waitress asked me if my food was OK, I said, it was just OK. She asked for more detail and I told her my hash tasted like cat food. Instead of offering to fix anything, she just gave me a watery smile and walked away. Don't ask me about the food unless you want an honest answer, and don't ask me unless you're willing to do something about it. 

The Toast? The toast was OK.

Delicious! I arrived and the wait was only 5 minutes, the waitresses were very kind , the food was delicious. Their country bene is out of this world! I will definitively be coming back. Also, did I mention breakfast is cheap? Oh yeaaaa!

Absolutely love the spicy beef and pork pho! My boyfriend gets the chicken pho which is so delicious as well- choice of bone in or boneless- comes with the most delicious side sauce of lemon garlic and some other spices to dip the chicken in. I would recommend eating in, the food comes out so nice and hot and you have different sauces on the table to add while you eat. I put a lot of the spicy chili oil in mine, and then add hoisin for certain bites to add the sweetness. Service is very good, I would have to say it's my favorite pho I have tried yet!
Delicious pretzel bun sandwiches!!  Lovely sandwich shop with fast service and good food.

Wasn't feeling well and in town staying with my friend who lives in the building. Our server, Ally, was beyond patient with us. It is obvious she not only likes her job, but believes in the food she sells. She was spot on with all her recommendations to my questions. She easily convinced me to try the wings, which were basically some of the best wings I have ever eaten!  The Hot could have been a little hotter, but just amazing. The fried pickles, my first time trying, were amazing too. For my entree, Ally recommended the Bangers and mash. Simply the best I have had since I lived in England. My friend got the bacon burger and it looked incredible. Did I mention the prices for most things are about $10? 

Now it was quite slow and I'm sure the flawless service had to do with that, but...when you go in, ask for Ally.
Tacos are amazing. Everything is fresh and sooooooo worth the wait. I love this place. The employees are extremely nice and helpful. I can't say enough great things!

Chick, chick... chick chick chick chick chick, chicken salad chickkkkkk! You are welcome for your new slogan song!!!!

First of all. Why is there no location in my location?! , hummm... should I franchise?! (If I had the cash) 

I super love this place. Yes I know. 4 and not 5 stars but listen, I don't want to drive to Tampa or Clearwater for a fix ok. Geeze!!!! Give me my Fancy Nancy close to home will ya! Two scoops, with crackers sometimes a Sammy which I get on a croissant. Super wish it could be warmed or toasted and just agua to swallow all that yummyness down. 

I'm a muy caliente "spice girl" no, not scary spice ok, i was more like a mix of them all but baby spice but with a little sass!  but I love the sweetness of the grapes in the chicken salad vs the spicy.. idk ‍.. oh, and they give you pickle and their signature cookie which is good but I'm a chocolate chip cookie girl so I'll pass. 

Anywhoooo, either way, however you prefer, you can not go wrong. Mix, match, Patty wack give chicken salad chick a chance!
Great BBQ and friendly owners/employees. This is a local hidden gem that I will put on my list of places to return to next time I'm in Florida. Thanks for making solid, flavorful and meaty BBQ!

Giving 2 stars mainly for the view!  We stopped by Whiskey Joe's for the first time a few weeks ago on a Friday night with a party of 6.  We tried a variety of alcoholic drinks that were all mediocre definitely for the price and a few shots of fireball which were warm.  Our group ordered fish taco, the grouper nuggets, and burgers.  I did not think any of them were good.  The items that were fried tasted like a pound of grease, and the burgers and fish tacos were gross.  The view was nice, our waitress was friendly, but unfortunately since the drinks and food were not good we won't be back.

Feels like a hotel bar/lounge or a long forgotten country club that's trying to stay with the times.
After arriving we decided not to eat and only have a glass of wine.  They seem to use overpowering cleaning products and it made us not want eat anything. 

The service was also exceptionally slow especially given that only 2 other tables where seated.

This space has been transformed many times over. Anyone remember that seafood place?

Well, it looks like they've finally found a tenant that should really and likely will stick around. While the ambiance remains largely the same as Lazy Lanigan's, the likeness ends there.

The main thing to know right off the bat: They have an excellent beer list. Look up and you'll see it rotating on several TV screens across the pub. They even do you a favor and put all the unfortunate domestics on one screen together. That's the ideal moment to bite into your food!

On my visit a few days after the pope left the area, they still had PBC's Holy Wooder on draft. This made me happy since I had popecationed and missed the pope brews.

If you like IPAs, especially the local ones, you'll love this place. They have a crapton of 'em.

As far as food? We started with the mac and cheese balls, and since I'm 5, I had to choke back a laugh when they arrived. Despite their funny-looking appearance, they're really good! Formed with bacon and shallots.

For my main meal I had the chicken tender club sans tomatoes. It came with kettle chips, and the whole dish was huge. I could hardly even eat half of it. The rest was yesterday's lunch.

Keep up the good work, Village Pub! I'll see you the next time I visit my hometown.

Wow what a great find! My wife and I was spending some time in New Orleans a few days of our honeymoon before our cruise shipped out. While waiting for the Witches Brew Haunted Tour to start we decided to go get some coffee and beignets! Let me start with the coffee I had just black coffee and wow the flavor and notes in the coffee was out of this world. The wife had chai latte and said it was amazing as well. Then of course we had to try the beignets which is one of the greatest deserts of all time.
I miss Moby Dick in DC but this is almost as good. Fresh ingredients and good size portions, good price, Wish the flat bread was home made and cooked in a clay oven like Moby Dick.

Awesome first time experience here. 

Dropped in yesterday (wednesday) around 8pm with my pops looking for some fish and chips.   Limited parking in the lot but not an issue when we were there as there was only a handful of costumers.  Got Phil's Fish dinner and it was excellent.  Crisp brown crumbs over a moist and tasty large slice of white fish.  Brown rice and steamed veggies on the side were perfect after the lemon was squeezed over. Price was fair for the portions. Beer selection was pretty decent and decor was fitting, mostly fishing themed.  2 TVs hanging over the bar playing sportscenter made for a chill delicious dinner.

Major props to the waiter/bartender remaining ever attentive to our table even with a cute blonde lass vying for his undivided attention at the bar.  

Ill check this place out again.  Could see it being hectic in there when busy, but when it was slow, it was darn good.

The last time I was here it was under a different name and management. As soon as I walked in I got a good look at the salad bar. I should have made a 180 right on the spot. Wilted/brown lettuce and items just kind of pieced together with no attention to detail much less freshness. If this is the first thing customers see when they arrive, you would think that you would make a bigger effort to make a good first impression. I ordered the baby back ribs. What I got was beef ribs that tasted like they were on the verge of turning rotten. The sauce did an ok job of disguising the bad flavor, but not completely. On the up side, the waiter was very friendly.

I have been here a few times and generally have found the food to be okay until today. The galbi I ordered at first glance looked like a lot of food, but the bottom was covered with large meatless bones. Last time, my portion was so large that I had to push what remained on my plate away to a lucky friend. This time, I was still hungry and had to fill myself up on free pickles. Very disappointing.

Worst service today Sat at drive thru waiting for several minutes to arrive at window and yet wait even longer than at box... Order in correct no receipt in bag and no onions on my Whopper! I asked girl at window who is always there if they are having problems today and she says yep and we will be all day!

I looked on Yelp to find a new Chinese restaurant to try and Here I am. I called in my order which was the hot braised shrimp lunch combo. Comes w rice choice of crab Rangoon or egg roll and a soda priced at $5.50.  You receive a very nice portion which I was very pleased with. My hot braised shrimp was tasty..the crab Rangoon was also good and the restaurant clean. I will return to try something different on the menu.

Great food and super friendly and helpful service. I tried it for the first time, ordered the half and half allowing me to try two dishes for $8.75. The Red Beans w/ Smoked Sausage and Spinach Mushroom Etouffee were both great...the only improvement I'd suggest is a to be a little more generous on the Sausage but otherwise really good!

Went this AM for a snack,  ordered two tacos and asked for mild sauce. The tacos were greasy, and had been made and let sit, , , lettuce was wilted and the tortilla was actually stuck to the wrap. And of course I was given HOT taco sauce.
Terrible!

I am not the biggest Ramen fan but this is a place that I have come back to twice. The ambience here is great, very family friendly as well a great date spot for a night out for dinner or a quick lunch with co worker. I don't eat any other meat so I got the chicken but my friend got the duck ramen and it looked soo good. I highly recommend any of the ramen dishes and you won't be disappointed at all.  Portion sizes were decently sized and the service was great. Truly recommend this place in the st. pete area if you are in the mood for some ramen.

My friends and I came here on New Years Eve to celebrate a birthday. I hadn't been here in a while and was excited for some Steak and fine dining. 

We started with cocktails. I had an Old Fashion and my partner had an SV5 (fun fruit and vodka drink). Everything was good there. We then began ordering wine by the glass. The Tempranillo we ordered tasted old, we like wine, it shouldn't taste like it did. But we left it alone. We finally ordered a Pinot Noir and there were no complaints there. 

We moved onto entires, we both ordered the Crab Stuff Lobster Tail (Oscar Style). This entree was to die for, everything tasted great and was presented well. 

This is where it starts to get a bit rough. Our waiter, after serving our meals was MIA except when he brought out an on the house dessert for my friends birthday. Many of us wanted to try their New Years special cheesecake, but didn't have a chance to ask before a check was being sent to our table. We asked if we would be able to split the $1600 tab we were told they can't do that. Instead they gave us a piece of blank receipt paper and a pen. If we wanted the check split we would have to write down what we ordered and the price, then give them our piece of paper with our credit card so we could be charged. 

On top of that there was no mention of a tip being added to the total bill. Instead when we all divvied up what we were going to pay, each couple added a tip to their totals. However we found out later that a tip was added into the final bill. To top it all off I was charged twice that night. When I called the next day to see what was going on I wasn't really given a satisfactory answer. Still waiting on one of the charges to be dropped off. 

Overall the food was great, a bit pricy, but I did enjoy or meals minus the first glasses of wine. The service was fine, but bad service like we started to experience at the end of our time there can really make you question coming back to a place like this.

Made it to the Carmel restaurant with a group of 8 on a Sunday evening.  We were greeted warmly and the 2 guys behind the counter were very friendly and helpful to our group which were novices in creating a poke bowl.  As expected, the protein offerings were more than what is available at my work. They also had tofu, cooked pork and beef in addition to raw salmon and tuna plus cooked chicken.  They also had additional marinated proteins too.  Nice atmosphere and they do have kombucha and local beers if desired. Whole group enjoyed it!

We ordered food to go and we had to wait longer than usual because they did not have enough people working. The quality of food has gone down and the prices have gone up from the last time we visited.

Decided to try this place out since they have been supporting our community hospitals with food during pandemic and recent fallen officer. I was not disappointed! We ordered wings and buffalo wrap- both were great!

If you are from South Jersey or the greater Philadelphia area, then you know a good hoagie when you see one.  Never ever call it a sub though, you will be corrected!  We often get sandwiches from here for lunch at work, about once a week.  To me, the roll makes or breaks a good hoagie, and Primos nails it with their freshly delivered rolls.  We have a few people where I work that aren't a fan of the crust being so crunchy and hard, but to me it makes it that much better.  Who wants a mushy hoagie?

We even get the party trays once and a while and they go fast!  But why not 5 stars?  I've had to stray away from the broccoli rabe, which I enjoy on my hoagies.  Too many times it's been bitter or very stringy.  And they've forgotten special orders, like no cheese, or extra peppers and such.  I contribute it to it being very busy during the lunch hour, so slip up's happen.  But this will not stop me from going back time and time again.

Yummy yummy! We had a really nice dinner at the Tamarack Junction tonight. The food was great, the service was wonderful, and to top it all off my kids ate for FREE! And after dinner the kids played in the arcade and I had a cocktail. I think this might be my new lazy mom hang-out.

Great food, everything is so home made, staff, cashier is very nice, from hummus to pita bread, so FRESH....try their platter, got everything on it, found this place by accident, wish they have this restaurant near by my home.

What makes locals visit a Holiday Inn restaurant? Well it's pretty much midway between my house in Indy and a friends in the middle of rural Indiana so it seemed like a good place to meet for lunch. The menu was very limited- 4 burger options, 3 salad options, and 1 BLT wrap choice. The decor itself was modern and fresh, the service was friendly, and the food was good. I went with the Lone Star Burger with bacon, bbq sauce and an onion ring. The flavors were great and the price was reasonable. The bar doesn't open until 5pm. Definitely worth the stop if you are staying at the hotel, otherwise there are better burger options in Indy.

I haven't enjoyed a meal this much in a very long time. Everything was excellent. We were lucky to go on the third Saturday of the month when the do a full lamb de lait and it was amazing. 
Thrilled to have finally gone to Mopho and utterly delighted by everything we tasted.

Since Yelp has become so critical, I really just want to begin my review by saying the efficiency and service here is not the problem. The employees that work here as for as I know are more then fine, however it's the quality and bizarre atmosphere at Tijuana Flats that has me absolutely puzzled this place is a four star "Tex Mex" place. No way over my dead body.

I have been here three times. All three times I had an awkward experience. I rarely even use that word socially, but beginning with the menu- There isn't one item that sticks out as a seller. Since it's a fast casual category, I of course didn't know what to get each time. 

The quesadilla = probably the worst I ever had. Those are my favorites, Qudoba Mexican grill's is literally 10x better. Awful taste in my mouth from it.

Tacos . Just ah: whatever. The hot sauce bar. Might be the strangest thing I have ever seen in a Mexican restaurant. The tastes? All the same. Too many spices that aren't even authentic (vinegar for example) that just turns me off. Taste was way off. Too many options? Yeah. This is just the icing on the cake. I love hot sauce but literally what? 

Okay, so I am not Mr. Politically correct, but the names of the sauces have cuss words on the labels. I mean I don't really care but I just honestly genuinely do not suggest going here, unless you want to keep eating the average food in your life and put money down the toilet.

Excellent food.  The crab cakes, coconut shrimp, seafood bisque, and linguini and crab (on the take out menu) are a few of my favorites among many.  You can't go wrong with anything you choose. Drinks from the bar are always on point.  Never had a bad experience.  Definitely one of my favorite places whether it's a solo dinner at the bar or at a table with family and friends.
I have been here many times and have enjoyed the food each time. By any standard and locale (even NYC) this is fine food and always look forward to eating here when I visit Tampa.

My fiancee and I ate breakfast here because our hotel doorman recommended it, and we were very glad he did!

The place was busy on a Saturday morning, which is a very good sign for a downtown restaurant not in a hotel. The food was very good, and the service was excellent.

Very confused by the 4 star review...Stopped here with my family on our way up to Los Olivos and was disappointed with the subpar quality of the food. I ordered the eggs Benedict, the eggs were so undercooked that when they were placed on the table they ruptured. Completely inedible and so much watery yolk it made the dish repulsive. The eggs whites fell apart into gunks of slushy egg. The potatoes were cold and not fully cooked and lastly the ham was a massive slice of ham which was very bizarre (i.e.: Easter slab of ham). The room was hot and sticky, we were placed at a corner table that had bussers and waiters hustling in and out. The slamming and opening/closing of the door was very distracting and no one could focus on their conversations. Also, not serving tap water is a joke. Being forced to buy bottled water is absurd. One star for the waitress, she tried her best to accommodate us and was very attentive to our needs. She tried to reseat us in a different section, but it was sweltering hot in the alternative room.
My fiancé and I come to On The Border every week. Nancy is, by far, the best bartender. We love coming just to see Nancy!

Sadly, a pass for me.

$10 for a mediocre 1/4 glass full of Prosecco (draft) is No Bueno & seriously lacked bubbles. Their Red Wine blend is no good & cheap! 

I can go to Bar AW, which is around the corner for a craft cocktail for nearly the same price or a couple bucks more!

The Hibiscus popsicle was the best part of the drink - def. worth it on its own for $3-$4!

I'd like for Graze to deliver if I'm paying $10 + $2/tip for an adult beverage. 

I ate 1/2 of my friend's Burger while semi tipsy - this would be a reorder when I go back because it seems they make decent ones.

The sweet potatoes with a marshmallow glaze & cinnamon is outstanding & worth the upgrade for $2/more!

We love the food and they are always very friendly when we come in. The reasoning for the 3 stars is because the kids areas are gross... like gross gross. Dried milk and drinks on the seats of the games ( which has been there for over a month) candy thrown everywhere, food etc
We will be returning but i wish this area would receive more care. A nightly cleaning is needed.

DO NOT DRINK THE COFEE! 
My friend and I came down to New Orleans for a 4 day trip to explore this beautiful, culturally significant area. While here, eating beignets was of the utmost importance to us. Well, the beignets were great (as was the alligator sausage) -- but I'd ordered a cafe au lait (for close to $5) -- it tasted like something from a gas station machine. 
Very disappointing. I took one sip of the coffee and informed my waitress that it was beyond bad. She refused to remove it from my bill. Oh well. 
I hope you don't make the same mistake I did!

There is no need to write paragraphs when this sushi is summed up in one word AMAZING.

Always fresh, good vibe solo or with a group. Great service. Beautiful presentation. My goal is to try every roll.

Great restaurant at a great location (upper Garden District) with elegant surroundings, friendly staff and superb food - all for a fairly reasonable price.

Had a fried catfish and crawfish dish with fettuccine - both really nicely done. The chocolate bread pudding dessert was the best!
Fun spot for drinks and dinner. I like the atmosphere and the friendly service. It's also nice to go for a walk by the river after eating :)

Excellent menu with very affordable prices! Found this place looking for a better option than fast food and could not be more pleased. 
Perfect gyro pita and really good Greek Potatoes. Will definitely be back in the next time I visit family and need some great food for a simple dinner!
Very good food!!! Great experience! I thought the customer service was good too! Very relaxing outside and I love all the decor! I would love them to build one in the o'fallon location though.

I don't know what's up with this place but I won't go here anymore. Waited so long, way too long. Then other people were also complaining about waiting too long. They left stuff out of my order. The employee at the counter was polite. He was the only saving grace.

I asked for a couple of slices. They were old. It is a Friday night. It was as they were made two days a head of time. Service was either order  or get the hell out. Was there with wife and two kids I felt rushed and unappreciated. They were not even that busy. Overall a below average experience.

Cant write a review of the food because on a TUESDAY at 6pm with the place half empty we were told that they couldnt seat/serve us since we didnt have reservations...there were just 3 of us and there wasnt even a 'hey, do you want to sit at the bar?' or 'sorry; please come again' thrown in.  So while the setting was beautiful I probably wont venture all that way again.

Street tacos are the bomb!  I dropped in with my husband for drinks and late lunch.  We both loved the carnia asada and carnitas street Tacos.  I had a mango frozen margarita... the 12 ounce is plenty. I have a favorite local Mexican restaurant!

Get it while it's hot outside!  Who knew that ice could taste so sweet and delicious!  Imperial Woodpecker gives NY a new meaning to the word snowball.  It's shaved ice served in containers we might only be used to seeing in Chinese restaurants. The ice is topped with a flavored syrup of your choice, in fact there are over 20 different flavors of syrup to choose from.  The larger the size the more flavors you can choose.  For a mind blowing sweet treat, top it with sweetened condense milk.  I recommend the Mardi Gras King Cake, but don't worry there is no baby to bite into with this cake.
http://www.eatsomesweets.com/west-village/imperial-woodpecker

Well this was a new chain for us to try. It is okay but, I am not overwhelmed by this place. My ribs came out cold so, I had to send them back and the replacement ribs were dry. 
The chicken with cheese and bacon was better than the ribs. The hot croissant with pecan were different and good. 

This would be a good place to hang out and watch sports but, I doubt if this will be the restaurant that we go to after service on Sunday.

I went through the drive thru this morning- first time ever going. The service was amazing. It's always nice when a stranger can make your morning even through masks and distance. Easiest drive thru ever. I used the STL Experience booklet to get a free coffee and dessert with an entree. Went with the biscuits and gravy for my partner who has had A LOT of biscuits and gravy in their life. I asked for the gravy on the side so it was easy to reheat (for my on vacation sleeping in until 10am somehow partner!) and delicious! The brown sugar pop tart and the chocolate cake were great- don't skip the sweets here. I look forward to going back and 'making my own' breakfast sandwich with their sausage or turkey chorizo.

Justine has a cool modern vibe with eclectic decor. Everything is made from scratch here. We went for a birthday dinner with a group of six. We started with the field pea hummus and naan bread. This was pretty good black eyed pea hummus but could have used more bread pieces to go with it. We also tried the shrimp cocktail which was quite a different sauce than expected but pretty good. We also got the braised short rib appetizer and that was excellent! For dinner a few of us ordered the steak frittes. They do a cut of the day which our server told us was a cut called bovette and similar to skirt steak and served with excellent French fries and Austin poive sauce. The sauce was rich but not over powering. Hubby got the bouillabaisse with shrimp and sheephead fish filet. This was garnished with a long bruschetta toast with a red pepper sauce that was to die for but you really needed a basket of bread for the broth! You could tell the restaurant was struggling with social distancing and not enough staff. We waited quite a while in between courses and waiting for more drinks. For dessert they brought the birthday girl the granita dessert and we also got the lavender creme brûlée that was perfection! Overall it was a nice dinner.

Came here for brunch on a visit to NOLA. It's located in a quaint neighborhood right off Canal Street. The atmosphere is what you would expect from a brunch place and is very homey. Our server was amazing and extremely attentive throughout the entire meal. I had the White Russian Cappuccino to start with. It was great and combined two of my favorite things. I decided to order the Crabcake Benedict for my entree with the breakfast potatoes. It was one of the best benedicts I have had and that is one of my go to brunch entrees. I would highly recommend it to anyone. The potatoes were also very solid and well seasoned. A great place to grab a delicious brunch in NOLA.
We had a fabulous dinner on Valentines day 3 yrs ago highly recommend , all our food was delicious! Sever were very pleasant ! Love this place.

Went on a Sunday for lunch. The lady at the register was friendly and extremely helpful! The food was great! Had the gumbo which is on their special menu. The jambalaya was the bomb! I'd choose the jambalaya over the gumbo any day. Parking was right in front of the restaurant which was tucked in a corner of a shopping strip. A gem in a city notorious for shrimp, pork and crawfish.

Famous place so we had to try it! I got the Planter's Punch which was good but not very strong. The bartenders seemed a little tired/annoyed with us even though we didn't do anything wrong. Maybe just a bad day..? The bathrooms are not clean so go somewhere else if you need to. It's definitely a dive bar! Not bad but there are better places nearby.

Meh...this really isn't my kind of place. 

Helen Fitzgerald's is owned by the same people who own Sybergs, which means a lot of their menu items are the same.

I came here on a Friday night for a friend's birthday party. There was a group of about 6 of us, which isn't a terribly big party. But our waiter seemed to have issues taking care of us. Not sure what was going on there, but he kept forgetting drink orders, not keeping our water glasses full, etc. Eventually we just asked him to keep the water pitcher at our table. 

The food was mediocre and overpriced, IMO. I ordered the shark bites appetizer, and it was just meh. I remember the shark bites being SO good at Syberg's when I went there years ago! Maybe my tastebuds have changed or the quality has gone down, because these weren't impressive at all. 

Coupled with the inattentive service, I doubt I'll come back to Helen Fitzgerald's anytime soon.
Usually good, however this time we were ignored throughout the entire trip. We almost (and should have) walked out because we couldn't get anyone to take our money. Food was cold, waitress was rude.

It's a sweet place to have lunch.  I really think part of the draw is the limited hours....you just HAVE to go when they're open and you're downtown.  The food isn't going to win any awards but it's good...and it's a pretty place for a ladies' lunch and there's nothing wrong with that!  

You won't leave underwhelmed or overwhelmed...

This place is a gem. The first thing that caught my attention was the space itself. It is so open and inviting. Everything looks so clean. When I walked in the people I was eating with had ordered juice flights. They were absolutely beautiful. When I went into this place I was under the impression that everything was vegetarian, which I was totally cool with. But I was super happy when I saw bacon on the menu. I opted for the BMT and added bacon and had a side of greens. Everything was amazing! I also got to try a bit of the sweet potato and brussel sprout hash with chorizo. After I was done with my main meal I had to get a side of the hash it was so delicous. I cannot wait to come back and bring all of my friends!

We came for lunch just as they opened for the day. I liked that they were ready to serve us as we arrived. Two bowls of chips, two salsas, and some guacamole came ASAP and our ice-cold drinks came immediately. Now that's service! We sat in the side patio with our small pup. They even brought water and a nice bowl for our dog. 

We ordered a variety of things: chicken fajitas, pork pozole, and an enchilada and hard taco combo. The food we ordered was more than enough for the four of us and our little pup. The entrees are shareable. The combo was a beautiful plate of black beans, rice, enchilada and taco (and the frilly lettuce and Cotija cheese sprinkling). I had the pork pozole which had tender chunks of pork, lots of hominy, flavorful broth, and a plate of the fixings (red radishes, oregano, cabbage, chunks of avocado, cilantro and onions). The fajita plate was as expected - plate full of onions and bell peppers and tasty chunks of grilled chicken, along with the fixings. No skimping here! The best part of the meal, aside from the company, were the homemade corn tortillas - we ate every single tortilla and even fought for the last piece. 

The restaurant is warm and inviting. The spanish decor has lots of warm colors like gold and orange. It's a classy date-night kind of place. At night there's live music where the bar and dining room meet. The service here has always been wonderful but the food... It's bomb!

I've had the Mole here too and its AMAZING! I recommend trying the spanish-style (Catalonian) tapas Pan con tomate and the torta espanola (takes 20min to prepare). You wont regret dining here!

Its been a long time since I went to a Friday's restaurant. Last time I went out was great. Decent priced, good portions, decent service. Now it's all changed. The menu is a confusing. They have two for $15 which like most places we thought it was two can dine for $15. Boy,  was I wrong lol. So we ordered the new hamburgers they have. Double stacked American burger and another different one. For the price, $12, we were excepting a good size hamburger. Nope. The burger was small and they give you a bag of fries. Which has like 20 fries in it. Not worth the $12. The bathrooms are nasty. Barely lock. No paper towels. This place has before overpriced for the little food you get. If you want generic American food, I suggest just sticking to Applebees or Chili's. Very disappointed. :-/

After searching around and visiting several of the area Thai restaurants we keep going back to this place. They are in my opinion the best. The food is fresh and consistently delicious. I've been here for lunch, dinner, and take out. Each time the food has been good. I've had all of the curries and traditional red and panang are our favorites. The kids like the pineapple fried rice and pad Thai. You won't be disappointed at all. Is it the best?  Well I'd like to think there are others out there that are, but so far no one has consistently had better food as this place has. It is also family owned and if you are a regular they remember you each time you come in. The place is simple and food fantastic. You won't be disappointed.
I had the jalapeño lobster bisque and blackened fish tacos as a lunch combo. Just stumbled onto this restaurant. Great lunch.

So good! So FULL!  Cheesesteak was tasty and juicy. Meatloaf special was huge, and the kids spaghetti was enough for both my littles (and then some). Everyone was friendly. Will definitely be back when we make our yearly trip out here.

A well kept secret, the MFA of St. Petersburg is a small but exceedingly well-curated museum located in a beautiful neo classical building reminiscent of the old Getty Museum in Malibu, CA.  Indeed, it has many similarities with the old Getty.

Each room seems to bring a different era into focus--buddhist, Indian, classical Greek, American School, impressionist, wondrous sculpture, Rodins, Manets, a magnificent Georgia O'Keefe, spectacular photography, et al.

All in all, breathtaking.  

There is a neoclassical courtyard open to
the public adorned by several sculptures, also reminiscent of the old Getty.

The museum store is cute and full of surpises such as Keith Haring Dominoes.  

The Dali will always be the big attraction in St. Petes, but the MFA is a big cleanup hitter.  Definitely stop by!

Good atmosphere, decent beer selection....bud light was $6.00. Chips and salsa $8. 
Things are a bit pricy but that's what you get for this tourist trap.....
Not bad but not my first pick unless I'm staying here

***DISCLAIMER: 'Rona review - UNSAT experience.  ***


Would have been 4-stars and an overall quality experience - except for:

Everything was going good, nice table good service, though surprisingly not great?!?...  Our primary server was just not that good.  Not really personable or friendly.  I would have expected better.  All other auxiliary servers (bread/water/take-home box etc...) everyone else was money...  Perhaps our primary was "having a bad day"...

The food was excellent.  Under different circumstances this would be a 4, maybe 5 star review.

So about half-way thru (enjoying) our meal one of the staffers brought the full-capacity dining room to a silence by hitting a water glass with a spoon, then a room full of 50+ people bust into a HBD sing-song for one of the tables.  (no masks...)

When singing your respiratory particles can travel up to 30-feet, that coupled with being in the same room, same ventilation system...  really, really bad idea.

My ole lady and I were real uncomfortable with this.

This was a real bad move.

To management:  PLEASE don't do this again.

We can all sing in a year or two, but for now lets not and say we did.

-The "sub-par" service = minus one star
-The singing inside a very full restaurant during a respiratory pandemic = minus two stars

End of yelp review.

We came in early on Friday evening for happy hour and sat at the bar. Our bartender was Joseph and he was fantastic!  Happy hour consisted of buy one get one free house margs (originally $8) and Mexican beer. The margaritas are homemade but served on draft. What a neat concept. We ordered the lobster roll which was tiny, but unique and tasty.  We also had the queso which was really good, but a tad spicy for anyone who is sensitive to heat. The chips it came with were delicious. We also ordered for tacos: Carina asada, fish, cauliflower, and pork belly. Our favorites were the fish taco and cauliflower taco. Lastly we had the nada salad which was fresh, flavorful, and delish!
The service was fantastic. The bartender remembered our names, and was very knowledgeable and attentive. One of my favorite parts of this experience was how Joseph, the bartender, presented the buy one get one free margaritas. Instead of making the two cocktails and giving them to me, he made the first cocktail as usually, but left the ice out of the second, so the drink didn't get watered down!  I've never seen this concept and reallllly appreciated it!  When I was almost finished the first cocktail he added the ice to the second one. I wish ALL bogo places did this!  We will definitely be back, and will ask for Joseph!!!!

I loved this place!  It was easy to find a table, and the service was EXTREMELY friendly and helpful.  The food was exceptional for a Chinese restaurant, and also reasonably priced.  Will be back again when in Philly.

This place is definitely overrated. Don't get me wrong, this place is good but after a few visits now; I just don't get all the hype?

Eat a snack before arriving because it will take you at least 15-20 minutes just to find parking. As usual on a Saturday / Sunday, we had to wait a good 30 minutes at the downstairs bar before being seated. Most of the time, you're stuck standing when you wait for your table. The air vents at the downstairs bar are covered with dust. Not sure why the manager and/or staff hasn't noticed this or done anything about it? It's right by the kitchen doors where many employers pass by. The Guinness I ordered tasted funky and watered-down. This was either from the tap not being cleaned, or leftover water left in the glass, or just the Guinness being old in the keg? On the other hand, their Blood Marys are excellent. A big, tasty strip of bacon - coarse salt and pepper rim on the glass. For only a $1 more, I recommend to upgrade to the Square One Basil Vodka.

The menu is diverse and the prices are decent. The Monkey Bread is so good and comforting. But the other food is...eh, alright. But the main complaint I have is that for my 2nd visit in a row both my food and significant other's food has been cold. What looks great on the menu, winds up coming out just so-so and like stated before - cold. They have cheese grits, but the grits were bland and the cheese tasted like it came from a pre-packaged bag and they were cold. Their Datz Potato Chips are lacking the taste and pop they once had. Plus, the blue cheese they used was water-down and had no chunks of blue cheese. The rest of the food is decent, nothing to write home about.

Cool ambience at certain locations of the restaurant. And an overall decent experience. Would come back but they need to step up the quality of their food. More helpful hints - keep the food warm when served and clean-up the restaurant (vents, floors, etc.) and beer taps.

3.75 stars

First ever food review for me. I had the cravings for pizza and beer one night and decided to stop into Pasqually's, where hundreds of beer selections are available (not your standard Corona or Coors Light varieties). I usually stop in to buy my favorite beer, Victory DirtWolf, and discovered that their food is just as excellent as the beer. Everything I've ordered from here, whether it's been pepperoni pizza, French fries, or a cheesesteak, has not disappointed. The ingredients are fresh, abundant, and flavorful. Stop in, ask for a beer recommendation based on your tastes (read above), your favorite food, and prepare to be impressed. The prices are fair making this spot one of the best in Philly. And I've been to a whole lotta pizza joints. Five stars all the way.

Probably one of my favorite places to go! Food is always delicious and drinks are always 2 for 1. Great family place or hang out spot with friends on lunch or after work. Staff is nice and I'll definitely be going again.

Sat down 2 other people at bar - took 15 min for bar tender to address me. Then he left to wash dishes before getting my drink order.   This was my first visit but I think I'll stick with the Tampa location instead.

I give the food a 5 star!  The concept is very unique. I think their only chance of making it is to turn into a fast casual establishment. It would be great to go up to the counter and choose either bowl or sandwich then choose ball and sauce and lastly choose from a selection of sides. The bowl should come with the same size roll as the sandwich. People should pay the same price for the meal and then there can be add ons. I fear keeping it like this will lead to a closing soon. No need for wait staff, ours was poorly informed and not enthusiastic.

Nothing on this planet cures a bad case of the 'spins' like Wild Bread. 

Say...do you miss me as much as I miss you?

This place is awesome. 

First off, the service was super attentive and well versed. I don't remember her name. But she was short, had a ton of tattoos, a nose ring, and sweet shades.

I started off with the Sunday School Special wine, which happened to be a Malbec. An excellently smooth selection. I promptly ordered three plates: Figs & Prosciutto, Truffled Egg Toast, and Lamb Terrine.
