I will describe them in reverse order of my preference.

Lamb Terrine
Served with a dry, nasaly mustard and some sweet cabbage relish, the terrine itself lacked very much flavor. I was hoping it would really highlight that funky lamb taste I've come to enjoy. It did no such thing. It was disappointingly bland. Not a bad dish, just really nothing special. 

Truffled Egg Toast
I love truffles. It seemed like this piece of buttered Texas Toast with a truffle cheese. Was it real truffles. VERY unlikely. It tasted like it had some truffle aroma in there. But it wasn't the nasty stuff. This dish was really enjoyable. Really because truffle flavor is just so darned good. This was a nicely balanced dish. I really enjoyed it. 

Figs and Prosciutto
This was the standout. Truly an incredible blend of flavors: figs, honey, and prosciutto. The figs were perfectly cooked, the prosciutto perfectly meaty and salty. This flavor blast isn't really describable. You just have to experience it.
I ordered dry pot. Extremely salty, almost inedible. Please measure during the cooking. Mala tang was good.
I was super impressed with this place! The food and drinks were really good and super reasonable. We've been a few times and the best was when we sat on the roof top with friends.

I really like Ryan's pub! The atmosphere is relaxed, it's clean and there are plenty of TV's to watch games. It's a solid spot on main street.

The food is always good- solid bar food! I've never been for an actual meal just for drinks and apps but was looking at the order the couple next to us had and it looked delicious! 

They also have an upstairs which is great for private parties (went to an engagement party there).

Good spot!

Delicious!!!! We've had Lupton's cater and cook out on their truck for company BBQs & luncheons at the office, and they are amazing. From the rolls to their amazing chicken. All I can say is YES PLEASE & MORE PLEASE!!! the mashed potatoes are to die for, and everything I've had (ribs, burgers, every side) has been better than the item I tried before.

Now that I know from viewing here on yelp that they have a brick and mortar shop, looks like more BBQ will enter my world :)

My Uber Eats delivery person said the front desk refused to hold my delivery.  As a result I will no longer stay at this hotel.  I travel on weekly basis to Philly from NYC, have Marriot Platinum and stay there 4 days a week, which ends up being $800 - $1000 each week or roughly $47,000 a year.  They're going to lose all of that money just because they don't want to hold my food delivery for a few minutes so that I can come downstairs to pick it up from the front desk.  Dumbest policies and service at this hotel.

If you're going to claim to have the best wings in NV, better step it up. Not even the best wings in Reno. Actually I didn't enjoy any part of this place. Sauce sucked and medium buffalo wings were sweet. No heat at all. Asked to try a little of one of the beers on tap and I got a pint instead.

I describe this place as a bar that has a couple bowling lanes attached.  

Good luck getting a lane on a Friday, though.  I know that people shouldn't feel rushed but they have a tendency to get a lane and stay there.

Still, it's cool that there is even the option considering the high price of land and whatnot.
Horrible Pad Thai.  Ordered vegetable Pad Thai spicy.  It was salty, with no spice or flavor, and frozen vegetables.  It was sent back and not paid for.  Try one of the other Thai places in town!

I wouldn't go to a restaurant like this if it were not for geocaching events because I haven't been impressed by a family-type sit-down restaurant in a very long while. On this visit, I had a sausage biscuit bowl for breakfast. It looks good but it's overly gooey and probably not too healthy. I also can't give full marks for service because they got our orders mixed up.

I would describe this place like a fart in church - not appropriate at any time.

The food was just bad.

The service is terrible! Me and my girlfriend were ordered food and the first dish came in roughly 10 minutes which isnt bad. The second dish came an hour after we ordered our food which is terrible. Everyone around us got their food already and finally when I asked them if our food was ready they said yea its here. The person next to us got the same exact dish, yet they got their food within 10 minutes. This place seems to dislike people who do not speak mandarin. I've been there multiple times because I like a certain dish. Every time the food takes very long. This time I've had it and I'm giving this place a one star because the food is decent. The best thing they have is the lamb hot pot.

Whew....my wife me I shared the fried plate, choosing shrimp and catfish, with green beans (instead of fries). About half of the shrimp had shells, and the catfish had an after taste. Just before we asked for Boxes to take the fish home (why? I dunno!), the waitress took the remaining four potatoes away. We could've packed those small potatoes in our little blue boxes. Maybe that's it: we were sharing instead gorging and not spending the normal amount to make the waitress happy?
I cannot recommend this place.
Overall, we were disappointed and are not planning to return.

What a neighborhood bar should be. Great cocktails and excellent food. Not $2 Bud Lights. Not frozen then fried mozzarella sticks. That's garbage. This is a bar for folks that have not given up and desire quality without pretension.
Used to love the pizza but now it's meh. Sauce has changed, and the pizza dough isn't french anymore-looks like pre-made frozen stuff.
This place is super cute! The drinks were amazing! The food was great! I loved everything we ordered!

I had a very bad experience here ordered the​ spicy alligator chili for $10 waited an hour for it and it turned out to be just a tiny cup of chili with some oily chips not worthy of the price nor the wait

Good place for some unlimited pizzas. Plus cheap to at $6 plus taxes it's a good deal alright. Though my only problem is they have too little toppings on their pizza, like for e.g. Today's Buffalo chicken pizza barely had any chicken on it.  But then again crying about toppings doesn't really makes sense since for $6 unlimited cheese pizza also works for. One thing which came to my attention, this location is clean. The buffet table area is always clean, someone is always looking after that. Another good thing is the salad bar, has lots of veggies, which I just take and place on pizza slices to make up for the little to none toppings on them. Overall would visit them every now and then.

We got here late on a Friday and the three of us each got different bowls. This isn't real "hot pot" food where you cook it yourself in a pot built into your table, so if you're looking for that you'll be really disappointed - as was one in my group. It's great that you can really customize what you want added to your dish. Ordering took a bit, we three were all first-timers to this place, but our food came out relatively quickly. The ingredients seemed very fresh and the taste was great! I got the beef with the miso/ginger sauce with Thai rice noodles and selected veggies. Perfect! The prices were good because the portions are huge, like these are really double portions. We sat in the dining room on the first level. The interior decor is inconsistent and amateurish, service was fine. We'll be back.

The food was not bad, we ordered the sampler, burger, fish with rice and the lobster pie.

I would have give a higher rating but there were 2 major problems . 
1. The chips and fries were wayyy too salty, to a point where I cannot eat them. We didn't ask to return them since they were just chips.
2. The waiter, Keith , seemed to be not interested with his job. He never refilled our water until we asked him to come over. The food was so salty we needed more water badly! When Keith bought out our entree, he dropped some of the chips on the table and seat. Then he said he will bring us some more chips but he never did. Ridiculous!!! Terrible service!!!

The address is actually the Independent Hotel on Locust, but just go around the corner and the restaurant entrance is on 13th St. Energetic vibe inside; some would say loud.  Décor reminds me of 1970's diner with retro items on the shelves behind the bar. The food was excellent.  I had the fontina and chard stuffed meatloaf with roasted carrots and peas. Portion size was just enough. The only thing I did not like about it was the "ketchupie" BBQ sauce on it. It comes with delicious mushroom gravy and the BBQ sauce interfered with the flavor of the gravy. My husband had the fried chicken. It was a huge portion with a half chicken, 2 biscuits and pickles. He loved it, including the homemade hot sauce. Service was super and the food came out fast.  It's definitely an eclectic mix of people, many who looked like they were meeting friends for drinks and dinner after work.  Lively and fun atmosphere. We would definitely go back.

This 2-level eatery is as good as it is eclectic.
The menu is in the form of a newspaper. 
The first floor is part restaurant and partly a store selling different items from sauces to baked goods.
The second floor is all table seating. 
As far as the menu, there is a wide array of
Items such as chicken, burgers, salads, steak, sandwiches & a variety of cocktails. My favorites are chicken & waffles, steak salad, reuben and pulled pork sandwiches. The best side is a marscapone cheese garlic mash potato. Their starters are many and unique.
Service is excellent, and the staff can explain the menu. Atmosphere is casual and pub-like!
Parking can be a challenge on the weekends. 
There are small lots in front and behind
the restaurant. But most parking is on the street.

The food was good, but not great for the price.  The fried zucchini appetizer was probably the best thing we had there.  I had the shrimp and scallop gnocchi.  They use flour instead of potato in the gnocchi which made them unpleasantly pastey.  My son had the filet oscar style. Probably shouldn't order oscar from a restaurant that doesn't otherwise have crab on the menu.  It was mealy and didn't taste like fresh crab.  I'll be going back to Sperry's for my next special occasion dinner.

Heard about this gem from friends and stopped in to pick up a lunch To Go order. Before I picked up, I stopped into the little story they have next doors. Lots of great Japanese products. Found my favorite iced green tea, matcha Kit Kats (from Japan) and also some Japanese wheat cakes! They had curries, sushi grade fish, prepared pickled dishes and salads and so much more. Small placed, packed with great products.

Went next door to pick up my To Go order and customer service was great! It was lunch and they were busy. For $14 I got this amazing lunch Special Bento Box.

The box had fresh sashimi (salmon, tuna & scallop) on top of sushi rice, 3 spicy tuna rolls and 3 veggie rolls. Box included a delicious miso soup and salad with a nice dressing. Plus some small portions of  pickled items that were good. All of the sushi was delicious and fresh. I wasn't a fan of the spicy tuna or veggie roll, but everything else was outstanding and a very large portion. Also, well packed for a To Go order!

The food here was great, I ordered about 9 rolls and shrimp and crab tempura and I also got desert, for the price and the amount of food you get since it's all you can eat, is very good. I enjoyed it tremendously! The service was great and the food came out pretty quickly. When I got there (around 5:30) it was not busy so I would suggest going around this time that way there isn't a much of a wait but after 6, it was crazy crowded! I'm so glad this place opened up. $25 per person for all you can eat sushi?!?! SENSATIONAL

Not impressed with the food or prices. Their version of bahn-mi was 1/6 the size of a normal one. The bun was nothing like the usual French roll that this Vietnamese sandwich famously uses - it was not crisp, but distractingly chewy and dense. Proportions of filling to bread were off.

The tiramisu is nearly $10 and not like other vegan tiramisus that I've had and loved at other cafes. It was too heavy, cloyingly sweet, and simplistic. Not enough layers and airiness.

Atmosphere is cute with plants and wooden seating. Giving an extra star because it has vegan and gluten-free options.

Covid-19 info

You can order online, but I see no way to get your to-go Covid margaritas. So we opted to call in an order. You can go and have it delivered to your car or up to five people can be in the business to pick up their food.

Cashier is behind a sneeze guard, there's a bottle of hand sanitizer if you want to wipe your card after his gloved hands touched it, and you can exit the building purely by pushing doors with your butt.

To-go margs are awesome. Only thing I'd mention they might want to do is they have a box entry area. You enter door 1 (exterior) into the box. Door 2 (directly ahead) goes into the restaurant area, door 3 (on the left) goes to the pickup area.

What should have happened as I was exiting (door 3) and a woman was coming in is the woman in the box area go through door 2 and walk around. What did happen was she pressed herself to the back not realizing I think that it was a door.

Just needs a sign that says "enter here and walk over" and "exit only" and I think you'll have no chance of bumping into someone.

This restaurant is: a) a sorry excuse for a japanese restaurant, b) a sorry excuse for a chinese dim-sum restaurant. The first/last time I was at Takenoya was on a Sunday, when they were promoting their weekend "dim-sum" special. I don't remember how much our meal cost, but I do remember the dim-sum entrees tasting like frozen food products from 99 Ranch. If I've never had real dim-sum in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Malaysia, maybe I'd think their food was edible. Unfortunately, I know that even shwag dim-sum shouldn't taste like this. I think they're trying to get away with serving Chinese and Japanese food to people who don't know the difference. People, know the difference between Chinese and Japanese food, please! If you've eaten here and thought it was good, please go elsewhere and try something better.

All too often this place seem to be in drama or chaos. We have been here when the entire crew walked out and there were only 2 people working total, the restaurant was cash only because the credit card reader had been down for some extended time, when only 2 people were scheduled. This is just the times we have been there which is not that often.  
Each of these issues are more than we want to get involved in as we come here as a meeting place to grab a quick bite and a soda before we go to Tahoe for the day. 
Slow service, bad service, good service, and correct or not so correct orders, you just never know. But as they say, location, location, location.

This place was great. I had roast beef debris fries with provolone at the server's recommendation. They were incredible. Crispy fries, unctuous beefy gravy, veggies and beef with tons of melty cheese. It has heaven in a basket. My dining companion had the Roast Beef Po-boy. We didn't speak for the 20 minutes or so it took us to eat. It was so so so delicious. The Saints were playing so there were hardly any other patrons. Service was good if a bit inattentive.

Amazing drinks and views. Such a shame that the service is terrible!!!! We were seated for 20 minutes before getting waters. The food was decent. The wings and fish spread were good, the fritters were ok. This place has amazing potential and bad execution!

Calamari salt and pepper was perfect!! The tofu salt and pepper came well over cooked.  Not even close to the picture, and missing all of that the flavor the calamari presented.  Terribly overpriced crab fried rice.  It was a nice dish, but average at best, and the udon wasn't anything to write home about.  Nice place, great service, but more pricey for lunch then is appropriate.

This place has the worst food I have ever eaten. I never write yelp reviews. My food came out cold and tasteless. Absolutely the worst. When I asked for something different, I was given attitude. All I wanted was fresh food and it was slop. Absolutely unacceptable.

I love this place. Probably THE best asian food around. I like to get the jumbo fantail shrimp, Satay beef, seafood soup, and sushi. Ribs are great too...hell, everything is great. Highly recommended.

While studying at UCSB from 2010-2013 my roommate and I dined at Saigon Noodle House numerous times and always enjoyed our experience. We were lucky to discover the grilled pork pho upon our first visit. We agreed it was the best pho around and ended up ordering it almost every week. We'd typically split a large and always leave satisfied. Nearly 10 years later and the grilled pork pho tastes just as I remember it. Absolutely delicious. We ordered it during covid-19 for take out and it survived the drive all the way back to LA. Highly recommend it.
Great Irish bar with a fun atmosphere and amazing food. There's always live music or some event going on. Plenty of TV's for all the sports. Service is excellent!

The moment you walk in it is absolutely packed. The wait was 40 minutes but once we were seated it all went swimmingly. The complimentary bread was delicious, nice and dense. It paired well with the olive oil. We ordered the squid ink pasta, my usual pick if it is on the menu, it was good but could've used a little heat. The amount of crab really is plentiful. For the pizza, we ordered the one with mushroom, bacon, and egg. My problem with a lot of pizza is that they plate it hot which in turn can make the bottom crust very soggy. Exactly that happened. The flavors of the pizza were good, but I like my dough a bit on the crunchier/harder side.

Came here for thanksgiving dinner and have to say it was one of the best meals I've ever had and can't wait to go back and try the regular menu. Location is awesome, on a smaller alley in the quarter, away from all the craziness of Bourbon. The Gumbo was amazing.... The perfect amount of thickness and flavor. Steamed pork bun was also awesome as was the Turkey. We are already ready to go back for the regular menu!

Good pizza but we waited an hour even after we showed up on time for our reservation. Prices were not listed. Turned out to be $20 / pie for not super filling pizza. Bought 3 for 4 people. No leftovers.

If you need a simple last American breakfast before embarking on hours and hours of flights to a far away place, Sam Snead's fits the bill. 

I always sit at the bar, since almost nobody goes to a bar for breakfast except me. I'd recommend staying away from the omelets since they are not made with real eggs as sagely pointed out by @Michelle. But, they can do over-medium quite well and real eggs are fundamentally required for that preparation. Also, I'd advise requesting your hash browns extra crispy to avoid a soggy inedible mess.

Now you know the secrets! Over-medium, extra crispy, and bar for breakfast!

Now this place is both in my neighborhood as  a purveyor of goods to both EBT and cash paying customers. 

I have ordered from here several times to which my seafood has been over cooked and my sides undercooked. 

The very last time that I ordered I called and asked to speak to a manager. Diamond, whose name was on my reciept was incredibly rude and refused to put the manager on the phone. 

After rereading my order and announcing my payment type, she conceeds that my order will be fixed even though it is about 10:20pm. When my husband arrived, he was not only refused his food, but they attempted to harrass him due to how I needed to handle the rude and callous behavior from Diamond. 

They only thing they succeeded in was losing a customer in Med School who always can use a late night meal. I will be reporting to all necessary agencies
Had lunch there yesterday.  Great sandwiches.  Good beer.  Friendly service.  And live music.  What better way to spend a Sunday afternoon.
The food here is amazing and they have great drinks too especially the orchata. My favorite is the shrimp burrito it's really tasty. I been going here for years and they never disappoint!
Amazing breakfast! Everything is very flavorful! They have tons of options to fit anyone's preferences! Definitely stopping in next time I'm in town!

This is a must- great vibe, amazing service (ask for Natalie) in the dining room or have a great time with the best bartender around (ask for Alex)!  If you have not been here - make a reservation now!!

First time here and the food was amazing. My Reuben was perfect and hubby's pulled pork was delicious. Rocky, our server, was great. We've been driving by this restaurant and are now sorry we didn't try it sooner. We will be back!

Everything said previously about the rudeness of the manager/hostess/waitress is true. Really disgusting bathroom with no light (creepy) and a faucet that won't turn off (ridiculous). Were it not for the manager and the bathroom I might give three or four stars because the place is cute and food is pretty good, but with someone like that working there I'm afraid the place is DIRTY.
First time here, and would definitely return. Service was a little slow, but the meal was great and reasonably priced.

I don't normally review a place after only one visit, but i am so impressed with Downtown Olly's that I just had to say something. I also don't normally order fried food, but the fried green tomatoes and breaded mushrooms here are delicious AND fried to perfection. The Black & Bleu salad was my choice. Again....delicious. Kat took care of us at the bar. They didn't have Squirt so she made me the best Paloma with fresh grapefruit juice, club soda, fresh lime and tequila.

Excellent service, ambiance and music.

We sat inside, but there is an outdoor patio and sidewalk cafe service.

This place was absolutely amazing. My wife picked up a steak burrito, ground beef tacos, chicken tacos, and a cheese quesadilla. I don't know which was best. I was hoping my kids wouldn't finish their dinner so that I could steal from their plate. I ended up racing back before they closed after dinner to get another burrito and 3 more tacos. I'll be adding this place on my radar AT LEAST once a week. Amazing food. They were closing when I went back and let me sneak in my order. Very friendly.

Yum!  This seems to be a very under-appreciated sushi place in Tucson.  There is never anyone in here when I go, and I don't hear about it much.

But this sushi is amazing.  Really.  They have very unique creations, including my new favorite thing, the Sweet Potato Roll!  Ugh!  No fish, just sweet potato and I think eel sauce.  Dear lord, it really is delicious.

They have special rolls that seem to change some what frequently, like the Greek Roll, which we tried and it was darned tasty.

The prices here are very affordable.  My husband and I comment, every time we come, that the sushi is WAY better than Sushi Garden, and even though they don't offer All You Can Eat, we wind up paying the same amount for the same amount of food, and the sushi tastes so much fresher!  The Happy Hour here is great, too.  Hooray for sake!

This is one of my favorite sushi places in Tucson.  Good prices, amazing sushi...yum!  I smell today's lunch!

How could you NOT love this place?!!!

Grilled cheese and tomato soup?! Ummm yessss!! Staff is friendly and alway know what to recommend!

How can you go wrong at The Ritz? We went for NYE and had a fantastic time. The hotel is always gorgeous l, but they really go all out for the holidays. The Christmas decorations are gorgeous and the live music bar area is perfection. 

The service is always impeccable and the staff is extremely friendly and helpful.

SERVICE: 7.9/10
FOOD: 8.25/10
AMBIANCE: 8.25/10

Get ready to spend. 80% of the Tapas are awesome. Menu changes. Saturday nights are lively and LOUD. 

A good first date place.

I've been a loyal customer to Bobacup for a few years now and it's been long overdue that I give them this review. Whenever I am in Tampa, my boyfriend and I have to make a stop here. When we were doing long-distance for 2 years, he would pick it up for me on the way (even though it was completely out of the way). The staff here is so friendly, kind, and professional. They always go above and beyond to make sure that I enjoyed my drink. The way they have enforced safety measures for their staff and customers has made it possible for me to enjoy boba during the pandemic. If you made it this far, please pay them a visit so you can know what you have been missing out on. Some of my favorites are the Thai Tea Mochi, Pumpkin Cloud Thai Tea, Tie Guan Yin Milk Tea, and the Matcha Milk Tea!

I've never eaten here before, so the review is for the gambling portion only.

The inside of this place is beautiful!  Blue skies, columns, it feels open and inviting.  They obviously spent a lot of money figuring out how to decorate this place to make people want to stay for long periods of time and spend money.  The blackjack tables have a sidebet called 'straight jack' which is fun to play (though I wouldn't recommend putting more than one dollar on the side bet for every five on the main bet, it isn't cost efficient).  The poker room is spacious and clean and has interesting promotions running most of the time.  Almost every employee that I've met there has been friendly and helpful.

If you're determined to lose your money, lose it here!  At least you'll have a good time!
Bartender is so rude and pretends to make drinks that he doesn't know how to make then rude when he finally gives it to you. Never wrote a bad review until now

Went to Capital Grille for my birthday dinner and settled on the Porcini Rubbed Bone-In Ribeye, I must say it was one of the best steaks I've ever had in my life!  The aged balsamic accented the steak perfectly....could not be happier with the meal.  In the words of Arnold Schwarzenegger....I'll be back!

Wow, quite the eclectic decorated little ice cream shop.  

Located at the south end of the Junkees building, you just can't miss this place. Nice area of outdoor seating and a half a dozen spots inside. A very small case of about nine different flavors of ice cream to choose from. You can have it in a dish it choose from 3-4 flavors of freshly baked cookies to smoosh the ice in. At $4 there were two pretty good sized cookies and a large scoop of ice cream. And it was delicious!  Cool little concept and the area really needed a dessert spot. But keep in mind they close at 8 pm. 

In the area - give them a try. You won't be disappointed.

I went with a friend for dinner soon after their opening. We both shared the Diavlo and Prosciutto di Parma pizzas.  Although the Diavola was delicious, the Prosciutto di Parma was the best i've ever tasted and was by far my favorite.  The appetizers were delicious and the gelato never fails to impress me, if you've been to any of their other Capogiro locations. I would highly recommend dining here.

We were in town to visit older relatives and I found this place on a search. The only downside was the noise level in the main room. There was a large group at the time of our visit so it was very noisy. Once they left it did get quieter and we realized there was music playing. When we left, I saw there was another area at the back which if we had realized, we would have asked to be seated away from the noisy area. I will say the noise did not really detract from our enjoyment of this lovely restaurant.

Our waitress was attentive and explained the various dishes to us. My aunt and I had the mussels which were phenomenal. I also had a cup of the wild mushroom soup. The flavor of the mushrooms was perfect and balanced with the cream base. My husband and uncle had the salmon. The portions were large on a bed of risotto with glazed carrots and greens on the side. They ate every bite!

My husband and I shared the lemon cake for dessert - every bite melted in your mouth. Our aunt and uncle shared a tiramisu and absolutely loved it. They told us this place was a great find and they plan on going here again. When we come back for another visit this place is now a must do on our list!

The food and service are beyond amazing!!! This was an absolutely amazing experience. My mom and I just arrived to Philadelphia, and had a terrible experience with checking in to our hotel. We just ran across the street to grab a bite to eat. And everyone was so friendly and uplifting. The food was awesome. And we even mentioned we were in a rush to catch the tour bus, and they were helpful and quick! I don't come to Philadelphia often, but I would definitely recommend this place! They made our trip a LOT better!

Not being from the O'Fallon area, I jumped on the opportunity to try somewhere new for a lunch meeting.  Hemingway's was a gem from the moment we walked in the door!  The eclectic atmosphere & "general store" feel made it very inviting.  We were seated instantly & greeted by a server who took our drink order.  I had a hard-time deciding on what to order as quite a few items sounded delish!  They offered a few daily specials as well as a daily soup that were written on a white board.  I opted for the bison burger which was cooked perfectly & a side of applesauce which was tasty as well.  Our food came out very quickly for it being more than halfway full & at the peak lunch hour.  The entire meal was moderately priced & an overall delight.  If I'm in the O'Fallon area again, I will make it a point to stop in Hemingway's!

This place has decent views as well as a solid vibe and atmosphere.  My piña colada was refreshing whereas my girlfriend's blue margarita was extremely watered down.  Our waitress kindly brought her another drink which she was pleased with. The grouper tacos were very delicious but were challenging to eat on stacked plates due to the lack of space on our table. My girlfriend ordered sushi, which she said was good, but she had to wait another 5 minutes after we received our food for her sushi to come out. Not the greatest experience but I would potentially return.

I've been to Metropolitan a handful of times. Can't beat their happy hour specials! My favorite place to go with family for a good meal. Not the best restaurant ever, has been hit or miss at times depending on what you order. But happy to report more hits then misses. Staff is friendly and it's close.  Would skip for a date night but perfect for after work with friends!

We had sushi it was awesome. Had a California roll, spicy tuna roll and shrimp tempura roll. All were very good. I got the chicken pad Thai it was so good. The best I've ever had. My daughters both got the chicken ramen.  It was very good and had a lot of flavor.  The service was awesome. And Saturday night is free edamame. And is was good too.

This place gives donut shops a bad name. The donuts was hard and tasted old the customer service was bad the person at the front counter was rude and didn't want to assist me. I normally go to the Jupiter donuts in largo but was in Palm harbor so decided to go in there. The store was dirty and the donuts look like bad knock-offs.i wouldn't suggest this place to anyone. Dunkin taste better than this place. I will keep going to the largo store.
Everytime, for years this has been a reliable place to get good and authentic mexican food!

Everything here is great from the service to the food to the ambiance. If you are wanting to take a break from traditional New Orleans cuisine you need to stop here! It's soooo good. The menu is extensive, but the servers do a great job explaining everything. We ordered meat a la carte, garlic noodles, pork bibimbap, nachos and s'mores. I'm missing a lot of food pictures, because we gobbled everything down before I even thought to take a photo! Everything was delicious. I will definitely be back when I visit New Orleans again.

Rarely do I arrive home and instantly want to write a review for a restaurant.  This place deserves to be reviewed while the whole meal is still sitting awesome in my belly.  A coworker and I looked at the other reviews to solidify our interest we were impressed so we went. Found out when we got there that the menu changes daily so everyone else's reviews were obsolete but one suggestion we could not overlook. The 5 course option where you take the entree price and add $20.00.  Do it you won't be disappointed.   We started off with the French Onion soup, while I wasn't overly impressed it was tasty, the broth was closer to a gravy than a broth but it had a nice balance sweetness from the onions & pepper.  Then I enjoyed an appetizer of wild  mushroom raviolis accented with a balsamic reduction, Parmesan cheese and truffle oil.  This was awesome. I'm a sucker for truffles and truffle oil.  My coworker had the cheese plate of which I sampled and the one cheese that really stood out for me among the rest was the "Cahill's Irish Porter Cheddar" Fantastic!  Next I had what I dub the "inverted omelet"  It was a fried egg and bacon salad on  baby spinach with tomatoes and a maple onion vinaigrette.  The egg was cooked to perfection with just enough uncooked yolk so that when broke it ran out just a little.  The sweet and tangy vinaigrette was excellent and this was my favorite dish of the five courses one, of which was lamb. (which I love and will get to but seriously the salad was that good.). Then the rack of lamb came out. Two beautiful cuts cooked to medium rare perfection.  On a pile of red bliss potatoes, artichoke hearts, roasted red peppers, full garlic cloves & toasted almonds all bordered by a sauce that can only be described by saying this. "It was the perfect mix of lemon, aioli & spicy mustard you can fathom."  This paired with the lamb and the other aforementioned veggies was completely out of this world.(but still not better than the salad)  Last was desert.  A vanilla and orange flavored Crème Brule. While it tasted great my one real critique of it was that the sugar was not torched thoroughly/properly.  It lacked that satisfying crackle that I'm so fond of and had more give to it than expected.  It merely separated and not that oh so gratifying crack like ice that forms over a puddle that has dried out beneath it. Then you go step on it and ahhhh "victory over the elements".  If you love Crème Brule like I do then no simile is needed but I wanted to use words to paint you a picture of  just how important this one step is to me.  Taking everything into consideration this place is a solid 5 stars and you'd be remiss to not go.  So go eat, drink and be merry.

Went here for restaurant week.

3 course meal $35 per person.  They included like an extra appetizer and some extra chocolates at the end so it was more like a 5(?) course meal.

Overall the experience was positive.  We had some wine with our meal and the waiter asked me the try the chardonnay.  I had to bust out my newly acquired wine-swirling nose diving wine tasting skill.  I said it was ok.

The food itself was pretty good, we split scallop sashimi and this peach soup (which had a lot of spices and kind of tasted like curry...)  Our second course consisted of shellfish roast and the bacon-wrapped pork loins.  The pork loin was great and very flavorful, but the shellfish roast was quite the letdown.  The "shellfish roast" was literally two shrimps over some carbs, and one of the shrimp's head was black.  Upon removal of the head, black juices oozed all over the entire entree... gross.  The dessert was probably the best part of the meal, we shared the sweet corn and a chocolate cake - both were on point.

Heard the rave for the weekend brunch buffet at this place, will check back for that - but probably not for dinner dining.

I like food trucks. 

I like food trucks that have Poutine. 

I may just be a little biased here, but ALAS, I have found poutine in New Orleans.   For those of you who don't know what poutine is, it's actually a canadian dish originating in quebec.  It is composed of fries, with cheese curds that are sprinkled on top and they melt into a gooey mess as brown gravy is poured onto it.  It's a heart attack in a cup.

Back home in Canada, they have a a lot of different variations of poutines, and there are specialty poutine shops. I often think about poutine, so I was especially excited when I saw it on Foodie Call's menu as they were setting up.  I was so excited, I couldn't wait and I ordered it immediately, I had to wait about 20 minutes for the poutine because they hadn't even started up their burners yet.

Although it didn't taste like home, the poutine was still good in its own New Orleans way.  A little bit of seasoned fries, gravy with debris, and cheese curds.  Cheese curds weren't quite melted into a gooey mess, they were still sort of square and not totally soft.

Plus side, I know where I can poutine for my cravings, I just have to chase this truck down, and now I also know where I can get cheese curds in this city.  As we all know the grocery stores don't carry them.
Best food EVER. the chicken in my salad was sooo tender, I almost cried. super great

I've had a few strikeouts with this cute little diner a few times mainly with rude servers. I decided to give it one last shot because I love the food here, my server was Morgan and she was an absolutely amazing. She was super bubbly and sweet. I came with a larger party (We had 6) and she did everything to accommodate everyone's picky eater requests and managed to check on us a few times while she ran around trying to serve her other tables and help another server who asked her for help. We will be returning in hopes to have her again! 10/10!!!!!!!!!

Needed a home cooked meal! I wanted to try a new place with a some great friends and I'm so glad I went here. Great home town food with a great atmosphere. Totally recommend this place. Really excited to come back to try their happy hour.

Such a cute place with great decor and atmosphere. Finding a quiet place to get lunch in this area can be such a pain with most places being rather loud and busy but when I stopped in here on a Friday afternoon, I was pleasantly surprised by how laid back the environment was. The staff was very friendly and helpful and the food was great. I hope to come back again soon to try more things off their menu.
So happy I noticed this Lol coffee shop in my neighborhood. I have been several times and will continue . live the whole atmosphere, very relaxing

Simply outstanding food & service! I ordered the Veggie Hash and tried the Salmon Benedict (breakfast is served until 2pm!). They were both excellent. No corners being cut here, and the prices were fair. Very friendly service & plenty of outdoor seating including seats by the fire heater along the patio.

The food is fantastic. I travel a lot for work and usually have a burger since it's easy/cheap. Lou Bird's burger was the BEST burger I ever had in the Northeast. Just to think it was almost literally in my backyard! Another plus is the drinks are strong. The service was slow,but they were nice. Highly recommend

Amazing spot. Somehow I've become a huge egg snob, and I'm always looking for fancy fresh eggs- these are definitely A+. Also probably one of the best biscuits I've ever had, with amazing bacon and pulled pork too.
We came in pretty close to closing time and our server even offered us the last of the hot coffee as she was switching to a new pot. I always appreciate nice, friendly things like that. :) 
Also the bathroom is strangely beautiful? Very important.

Food was cheap both in price and quality and ok at best. 
Probably more of a local thing than a place to seek out and no public restrooms??  Or at least that's what we were told so either they didn't understand the question or didn't have bathrooms??

Atmosphere is like grandmas living room, very 70's

Incredible! This historic and beautiful restaurant is a must when visiting New Orleans. Set in the Garden District, you can't miss the bright aqua blue exterior. Inside, the decor is more subdued and elegant. 

The service is extraordinary with a careful orchestration of servers - it was a gastronomic ballet. Our server impressed me by providing us with a choice of black napkins since our group was donned in black pants, instead of the standard white linen napkins. Each server in the corps of servers was excellent - professional and friendly. 

We started off with a cocktail. At lunch, they offer $.25 martinis with an entree, limited to 3. The drinks were perfect and refreshing while we enjoyed our garden location. Our salads and soups were served first. There was a server for each plate. My gumbo was brought to me in a stainless cup and then graciously poured into my soup plate. The gumbo was a nice dark base with sliced mushrooms and bits of meat. The entrees came out shortly after with the Cochon Cassoulet, deconstructed and elegantly presented. I was impressed with the presentation. The shredded pork sat atop grilled bread in a sea of white bean puree. My friends enjoyed the shrimp and grits. The shrimp and sauce were light and delicate. The grits were creamy. The best dish was our vegetarian friend's mushroom risotto. You could smell the freshness of the cream in her dish and taste the delicate nuances of mushroom. That was a divine dish. 

As we ate lunch, tall, thin women modeled clothing sold at Canal Place. It was interesting as they stopped by the table to let us know what they were wearing. Perfect for the ladies who lunch or a busy career woman who doesn't have time to shop. 

We couldn't leave the table without trying pecan pie. It was a nice piece of pie but more delicate than I anticipated. It was nice but not the best piece of pecan pie. Come her for the service and the food. Stop in for lunch for a less formal dining experience.
You had better kno2w what you are looking for, or you will get swept up with hyperchodriac syndrome!! Very pricey, but great all Natural foods of all culture.

Great menu, food was really good. Lots of outside room to eat. If you have little kids you'll love this...they have a sand section where kids can play while you enjoy your food-easily within eye sight of practically any table.

I have ordered from here a few times. I like their Cuban sandwiches and deviled crab. They are very friendly and they also deliver. I do wish they had a bigger menu, but they do make  a nice Cuban sandwich. I will also say that the person who has delivered my food to me always does it fast and is also very nice. Anymore to get a delivery person that is nice is kinda hard to find. :)
The chicken is always crispy. Great sauces, I just wish they cleaned it because there is a lot of fat on the thighs.
Not very good. Meats are too salty. And they changed the brownie (used to be great; now just good). Beer to expensive.

We had come here on the soulard eats tour and the sandwich was really good so we wanted to try their Burger Week burger. The burger was really flavorful and very thick and also very juicy at the same time. They ran out of the smoked jackfruit so we didn't get to try they. Fries were good. The street corn was so sad. It tasted like canned corn that had been cooked for too long and then the toppings were not very good. Wouldn't get this item again.

Just walked into this place and glad we did! The positive experience started with nice outdoor seating and our fabulous server Erin. She brought out the yummy focaccia with garlic Parmesan oil and took our order right away with personal recommendations to help make it choices easier. We ordered the jambalaya which had just the right amount of spice with perfectly cooked shrimp and chicken and not too many vegetables...the best I've ever had says my hubby! Chicken parm is a favorite for me and this flavorful dish did not disappoint. Although the breading was a bit on the dark side there was no burnt flavor with just the right amount of cheese and sauce on top. I really dislike it when the chicken is bathing in too much sauce or cheese! And the homemade red sauce was delish!  We finished off with "the peanut butter thing" and key lime pie for dessert just yum....give this place a try!

Just stumbled in here, but it's a really awesome bar! Good mix of locals and visitors, so it's like not too weird, but also different from home. Everyone's super friendly. And they're watching the World Cup here!
The food is delicious but the lighting is horrible!! Way to bright!! Bad atmosphere!!!

There are a few choices in Donelson and for take out Gyros... However no on beats Sam's!!! The food is great- always fresh even on the buffet. 

Sam keeps the entertainment coming with his lighthearted jokes and friendly banter. 

I never leave disappointed and without a smile on my face.

Very good breakfast. I had the bananas foster pain perdu. Brioche bread with bananas, raisins and syrup. The bacon was one of the best I ever had. Cooked perfectly and excellent flavor. Wasn't sure about using a bread for what traditional pancakes or waffles are used. But it works very well.

Overall the food is average and service is average. The decor and and outside seating area is lovely. They had live music on the patio when I was there and it was very pleasant and relaxing. I think the place could really be great with proper management. I enjoyed the salmon. They have a nice cocktail menu and the drinks are mixed well.

This place is consistent, efficient, and yummy!  We love their taco pizza (if you can handle the filling toppings), and have ordered a variety of their Italian pasta dishes as well.  It's definitely better than your run of the mill pizzeria, but I must say they douse a lot of their pasta dishes with much more butter than they need to.  Eggplant parmesan, spaghetti, etc... those are all solid.  Antipasto salad can totally be an entree.  

It's a local's place, and they never disappoint!   Friendly service and decent prices, I recommend checking it out!

I was disappointed, I can't lie.

I love the atmosphere, I love the feel of the place, but the Po Boy was really pretty average. The meat was dry, the sandwich wasn't great overall. I had Po Boys at Jazz fest that were 10x better. There was no messiness to them. The slaw was incredibly flavorless. I just really wasn't impressed. Seems to be more of a tourist trap these days than much else.

I'm glad I tried it, but don't have any need to go back the next time I'm in New Orleans.

I tried Foodie Fleet at the last Tucson Food Truck Round-Up and while I enjoyed what I ordered I still feel there is something missing.  Maybe my food truck standards have been set high after going to places like Animal Farm and Planet of the Crepes.   

I tried the goat cheese sandwich with granny smith apples, arugula, and whiskey pear jam.  It was pretty tasty, I wish there was more of the jam on the sandwich due to the fact that arugula is pretty overpowering and I could only catch a hint of the jam and what I did taste I loved.  I will definitely give Foodie Fleet a few more tries.  I think there is potential for them to be great.

Based off of the reviews and location was very much looking forward to trying this place during my time in Tampa. We came here during the gasparilla festival as they have a excellent view of the bay and the invasion. 

Upon arrival we saw "booze" tables outside on the balcony area. We spoke with the hostess outside and she let us know she was one Cabana table left for 1500. Of course we took it, I mean if your going to do such a festival having a table is worthy it in the crowds. The table came with 3 bottles of alcohol, mixers, 10 grill tickets, and 10 bottles of water.  The restaurant had grills set up outside serving lays potato chips and either hot dog, hamburgers, or chicken sandwiches. There was some misunderstanding when we got the table as we thought it included gratuity, but it did not. Gratuity was 21% so over all it was a little over 1800 total. Seemed like a great deal. 

The catch however is you can't order food from the restaurant at the table. You pay 1500 dollars, tip the waitress (who even though she was very nice was SOOOOO busy that we often had to go to the bar to get mixers. It was very busy) almost 400 dollars but CANT get sushi in the cabana outside. We spoke with the Miles the general manager and he mentioned that basically there kitchen isn't able to handle such a busy day outside of the tables they have inside so if we wanted to eat we would need to sit inside, have another waitress, and basically tip again even though we paid to sit at a table outside at the same restaurant. The General Manager proceeded to say this was specifically written on the flyer they had (flyer is attached.. it is not) overall wish all the facts were disclosed prior to spending so much money for mediocre food. I even asked for just an order to go, but the kitchen was unable to do that as well.

Overall very disappointing to not be able to get food from a restaurant that you go to and are sitting at. The grill food simply wasn't good, burgers were under cooked, and just did not want that. There were several other restaurants offering similar deals with food included one of which being American Social right next door. There special actually included a brunch. Will do that next year. 

The ambiance of the restaurant is nice

I don't really have much to add to these reviews, except watch out for the pad Thai if you're vegetarian. It  does have fish sauce in it. Also, I think the quality & temperature of the food here is the best of the locations in Indy, 2nd being Broad Ripple, & the last being the one on 10th by the hospital. I normally go to the BR one, as that's by my house, but my doctor's up by the 86th street one. After an appt last week, I darted in here & was pleasantly surprised at the difference in this location's food.

We visited this restaurant based on the reviews about the Caesar salad, and it did not disappoint! We had such a great experience, the hostess and server were amazing. We loved the bonus complimentary appetizer, It was a small piece of breaded flounder that was tender and crispy. It was paired with a slice of garlic toast that had beer cheese on top. Both tasted great. 

We then ordered the Caesar salad, which was AMAZING!!! The gentleman made the salad table side and provided a little history to go along with it. As we were first timers, the gentleman got the other people in the dining area to tell us and he also informed us we'd "never be the same" we laughed but it is so true.... the salad was fresh and tasted amazing. It even included house made croutons which were very good!

The Chicken  Parm with angel hair pasta and Potato Gnocchi both had fresh sauce and were amazing!!!!! Truly great experience and we WILL definitely be back!!!!
Lunch here was good. Place is very clean and so were the restrooms. Waiter was good and gave us a small discount. Food is very delicious. I recommend the egg rolls and the crab cake!

Thanks to apple maps/yelp, we stumbled upon this gem! The banana pudding donut was unreal!!! Everything I imagined it would be. We only went for donuts but the atmosphere is great and all of the food looked good.

Don't know how this place has 4 stars. Most of the food is no better than average. That plus the rude service by the waitress knocks it from a solid 3 to a weak 2. We had multiple dishes. None of which blew me away.
This is my favorite breakfast hangout ever. My grandson says "The eggs are the best I've ever had!" I agree. And try the loaded toasts as well. Delicious. Going back really soon.

I heard this place through the newspaper and I was dying to try it so I stopped in. The Chef and the Waiter were very nice and the grouper sandwich was AMAZING! And you must get the shrimp tortillas. It was sweet but had a little heat. Pit was OUTSTANDING  Easily the Best Seafood in Tampa! I will BE BACK and soon!

If I want to get pizza delivered from Royal I have to get it from the west end location. It's never as good as when I pick up and get it from the Hamptons location. Always inconsistent with their quality. Last night I ordered and barely any sauce on the pizza and undercooked. From now on I will just pick up from the Hamptons!
just like I remember it!  great food, great place!!  the wings were awesome!

Only been once to this place, and from reading the other reviews, this place appears to be VERY hit-or-miss.  We went in on a Saturday evening around 7ish, and it was surprisingly dead.  The first thing we noticed was that they had a guy playing blues guitar with a drum and bass track that he ran from his laptop.  SUPER cheesy.   It was distracting to a fault.  (although at least it was something that kept us laughing, as the guy was SO into it) It also didn't make any sense to me.  Blues guitar at a sushi place?  Huh?

Food was decent.  Service was just fine.  We sat right at the sushi bar.  I imagine it's easier to get good service when the place is dead.  

PLEASE, SOTR, cancel the way-into-it white blues guy.
Loved the pizza and the nightly specials! The teenager was happy to have sub choices. The staff was friendly and attentive. I definitely want to come back and try other menu options soon.

The food is good.  I'm not sure why there are gnats flying around though which is a turn off from wanting to eat there.  Last time I went there were 5 employees and not one picked up a rag to wipe the dirty tables.  I wiped my own table.

There are not many chain restaurants you can rely on for decently prepared and priced food. However, Black Bear Diner has it all figured out. I've only ever ordered breakfast here, but what I have had was hands down 5 star quality food. 

First off, Black Bear Diner doesn't exactly provide what you'd call "lighter fare." You're gonna walk outta here with some extra calories, no doubt. The value is out-of-this world. All their platters are huge. There's so much food, and it's always cooked perfectly using fresh ingredients. 

If you're really in the mood for a big heavy breakfast, you gotta get The GRIZZ! (2 sweet cream pancakes, 3 eggs, 2 slices of thick-cut smoked bacon, 2 sausage links & a smoked ham steak). It's absolutely huge, big enough to feed both my husband and I, and we're still always having to take some home. My all-time favorite, however, is the Chorizo Breakfast Burrito (Chorizo sausage, country potatoes, scrambled eggs, cheddar cheese, diced red onion all wrapped in a warm flour tortilla. Served with housemade salsa, fresh fruit and your choice of strip-cut hashbrowns OR country red potatoes.) I mean talk about a breakfast fit for a king. This damn thing weighs more than my French bulldog, I swear. 

In sum, Black Bear Diner is a quality establishment if you're looking for a familiar menu, good prices and tasty breakfast.

As both an Uber driver and consumer at this restaurant. I gotta say it has been a nightmare. As a consumer the service is found wanting and the food keeps getting more and more disappointing. As an Uber driver this company truly is horrendous. The guy holding the door got into an altercation with me and kept making disrespectful remarks when I told him I would not be waiting outside for the order but instead be canceling it. He wouldn't give me his name to file a complaint and wouldn't let me in the store to talk to management about his attitude, which would've been pointless if my previous encounters with the staff and owner were and indication of how hopeless a resolution would've been.

 In conclusion I don't eat or pick up for them anymore. This isn't much of a problem considering you have both Tampa Bay Pizza Company and New York New York Pizza in the same area as much better picks than marinas.

We went for a work function and we had the private room in the back. We also had the back of the patio reserved for us as well. The view is great, nice and relaxing. Dinner was excellent. A limited menu was preselected for us, but there was something for everyone. I had the chicken dish that came with mashed potatoes and green beans. Everything was delicious and everyone at our table ate everything on their plate. The timing of the salads, meals, etc was great. Servers were pleasant and helpful. I would definitely recommend. I plan on going again to relax on the patio.

This place is a great find! Especially for happy hour when it's warm enough to sit outside or by the windows when they're open. The have a nice 3 hour happy hour with wine, beer and summery cocktails netween $3-$5!!! Brunch is a steal too mostly ranging from $5-$8. For dinner and food the cranberry turkey foccacia, sesame tunasteak and spinach and artichoke dip is phenomenal! Wine and cocktail list is aptly priced and they have a large range of drinks on their drink list. Go for the brownie a la mode or bread pudding for dessert yum!!

Wish I could give it 6 stars!  On vacation to Busch Gardens and wanted to continue Sunday morning donut tradition.   Found this place with a line out the door and knew it was going to be good.  The staff was extra friendly  and the donuts some of the best anywhere!  Get the special dozen!

Maybe the people who give this restaurant a lot of stars don't eat out often. The service was poor... but well meaning. Mediocre would be a compliment for the food, which used to be sort of continental and now is totally Mexican.  And a Mexican Karaoke going on outside was... most annoying. This used to be a good restaurant.. Used to be. No more.

Meh.

Ever been to Rosarito/TJ in Mexico? I'm from Los Angeles, so it's a thing.
Anyway, this place was good for the "hey, i'm in the mood for an alcoholic refreshment" occasions but we got fried chicken from here as a quick bite and I wasn't impressed by it.

Grilled chicken you can get anywhere really. The sauces were pretty good though, so that was good.

BUT, not bad for a quick spot.
That and they're EVERYWHERE around the French Quarter.

If your interested in spending money on awful,bland and tasteless food this is the place to go. Service is mediocre at best. Furthermore, this place looks like it was designed by a fourth grade boy with a love for fishing. Definitely two thumbs way dow

This was all about location for us. Our hotel was right across the street from the market and we had to have cheesesteaks. Came here twice over 4 days. First time was with whiz & onions. 2nd time was with whiz, provolone, sweet & hot peppers, & onions. Both were good. The 1 with all the toppings was seriously messy. I think next time I'll stick with the whiz and onions. I can't rate this against other cheesesteak places in Philly since we didn't go to
Any others but these were definitely better than those I've had elsewhere. Finely chopped meat, no fat chunks, not drowning in cheese.

Great place with great vibe.  Bar food was upscale and nice.
Lots of games for adults to engage with.

Customer service alone is 5 stars. I wanted to send a dessert for an anniversary party and general manager Robert made it possible. We went by email, he even printed my message to them and gave it with the dessert, and sent me back the formal receipt. He mentioned he had to "run downstairs to computer" which made me realize he was putting extra energy to help me make it possible. Nothing short of 5 stars! 10 if I could.

The best of the best pho . As a French Vietnamese I am extremely picky with my pho, and having tried in major cities (LA, San Fran,Houston,Dallas,Pittsburgh, NY, Cleveland,Toronto, Ho Chi Minh, Singapour and even Paris in France ) , I am so glad I found this restaurant . You can tell the broth is high quality. Always getting extra bao to go for my work lunch .Very clean , staff is nice and friendly . Also how fast the food comes is so impressive. Just thinking about it, makes me crave it .

What an incredible brunch spot. I had a "biscuit flight" which came with four different types of biscuits and four types of spreads. It was phenomenal. The coffee was free flowing and good quality and the the space itself had an inviting vibe. I'm sad that I'm leaving St. Louis because otherwise this would become a regular brunch spot.

The food at Baru is amazing. I've only eaten tapas here but everything was heavenly. 
The atmosphere is great, probably one of the most visually pleasing restaurants in New Orleans. I love anywhere with good outdoor dining. 
Try the mazorca and/or the ahi tuna, no disappointments there. Also they just added a few more dishes to the menu, the ostras tapa is an exciting take on traditional fried oysters.

Really fun place.  I have been there a couple of times with my family.  We (adults) get to try different beers while eating pizza (which is no Chicago pizza but good) and playing board games.  I am excited that warm weather is coming so we can try their outside space.

3.5 stars for the gumbo and service. Gumbo is 1 of those foods that everyone has a definite opinion on what it should taste like and I loved the gumbo here cuz it tasted like my mom's  (very pronounced file flavor), but my dining companion said it wasn't to his liking.we both agreed that the shrimp etoufee wasn't something we'd order again (shrimp is fresh but the flavor wasn't there - I suspect underdeveloped roux). The jambalaya was okay.
Unsweetened tea had a good flavor and was refreshing.
The waitresses are the gems here along with the gumbo. We were sharing everything & our waitress brought all the necessary bowls and serving spoons without asking and refilled our drinks promptly.
Come here for the gumbo and iced tea; find etoufee & jambalaya elsewhere.

A 4 for now because I have yet to to try the food. But with a solid bar menu, and a good sounding brunch, I'm destined too in the not too distant future.

When it comes to nightlife and good drinks though, Little Bar offers BIG possibilities. While one portion of it is perfect for drinking a good brew and catching up on sports, another is the perfect up and coming music venue for loud & local bands, and while small the downstairs area can have some pretty awesome dance parties.

From a few to drafts and bottles, to an extensive amount of canned beers Little Bar has a legit variety. it also has a good mix of shot and beer specials. They also bring in DJ's who spin a good variety of music that has people dancing in a frenzy in the basement, or chillaxing over a brew.

But where Little Bar really shines is the live music. Phongraphic Arts (Pat Troxell of Creepoid which is another Philly band you're seriously missing out on if you haven't heard yet, and his crew.) brings in does a good job of lining up some crazy shows on a weekly basis. The stage and sound are on point, and as a bonus it brings in some solid musicians for guest DJ spots between sets. 

Combine all of the above and you have one little spot that's big on potential!
Racist, racist bartenders and servers.  Honestly don't know why any people of color patronize this bar.

This is a great little local gem!  It reminds me of the many family owned Mexican restaurants in San Diego.  Everything is made from scratch, and you get an amazing number of choices.  Beef, pork, chicken, seafood, vegetarian, you can get it all here.  And it's Byob!  My son's favorite is the fried cheesecake.

Absolutely delicious. It's simply good food. We got an Italian sandwich on rosemary bread and my husband couldn't stop raving about it. This is exactly how a sandwich should taste. Great food, great place, great people. Definitely come and support this place. Can't wait to come back and try more of the breads and cinnamon roll.

This restaurant is nice cozy and very bright on the inside. The food is delicious. My favorite is the quack and cheese. I also love the duck fries. I have been here several times, typically on a Saturday afternoon with friends. Another good thing about it is that it is a BYOB. The service is great.

I love popeyes, but its kind of weird to see some employees to start eating in front of you while you order.

I mean they were licking their fingers and didnt wash their hands after.

Had a wonderful time this afternoon sampling different stouts and enjoying lunch. Our waitress was wonderful and patient with us as we decided what we liked more  (so many choices!) just can't go wrong with friendly service good food and great beer!

Have been wanting to try this place for some time now.

If you planning to drive here, you can park in the hotel for $10.  The entrance to the parking garage on Common St.  It is valet parking only.

Make sure you make a reservation because they get very busy.  The hostess and servers are very friendly and helpful.

The reason I am giving this place 3 stars is because of the food.  The meat, that they come around with, was too salty for me.  Also most of the meat was undercooked.  I don't mind some red meat, but some of the meat wasn't cooked at all in the center.  That was a big turn off for me.

Overall the service was great, but the food was ok at best.  Not sure if I would go back.
Excellent food, very authentic. Service is also very good. Has a really nice local family owned restaurant ambiance.

The food was very good also the cornbread muffins were excellent our waiter Terrance was very good and on point with everything. Now the Hostess suck she was straight special. We waited at the Hostess Stand for 10 min and when she came to greet us she was looking like a dear in Headlights that's because she was trying to figure out if we saw her eating behind the bar Yes I saw you feeding your face while there were 3 party's waiting to give u their names. We were told it was her first day well after all the complaints it's going to be her last. First impression mean a lot and if I wasn't hungry after at 2 hr ride in traffic I would of left.   But Terrance made up for the special ed Hostess and so did the food

Summary- Excellent atmosphere with very meh food.  

Food- 2 Stars
Chili Omelette was just all around meh. Waaaaay too much cheese inside of it. The chili on top was out of a can. Hash browns on side were OK.

At least the coffee was very good.

Atmosphere- 5 Stars
Just can't get better than the big bar style counter top eating area.

Service- 5 Stars
Just awesome service, playful, funny, welcoming.

It's pretty good. As cookie-cutter American-Mexican restaurants go, this is a good one.  I've been here five or six times.  There is a full-service bar and lots of tables, so you won't have to wait for a table at lunch on a Friday in Brentwood.  Service is pretty quick.

Again, it is standard Mexican/American stuff, but it's pretty good.

So I asked a Facebook group I'm a member of for recommendations for a Chinese restaurant near my work. A lot of people recommended The Wok so we decided to check them out. The wait staff was very friendly and had no problem answering my questions and we never had to ask more then once for anything. I'm a sucker for spicy dumplings (in Vegas there was a amazing noodle shop that made them fresh) so I had to grab an order. We settled on Orange Chicken, Mongolian Beef, Sweet & Sour Chicken, BBQ Pork Fried Rice, Pan Fried Noodles and Chinese Broccoli with Garlic. Really enjoyed everything. The meats were good quality and weren't cooked to death or too tough. Sauces had great flavor. The orange chicken had really good flavor and didn't have that overly sweet taste you sometimes get. The Mongolian beef had good spice but also good flavor, not just hot to be hot. The noodles didn't have that overly thick sauce sometimes you find at other places. Good amount of sauce to crispness. I usually get Chinese broccoli with oyster sauce so when they said they could stir fry them with garlic it was a great change. For dessert we ordered the fried bananas. Most times fried bananas are served with ice cream, whipped cream and looks more like banana split. I was really happy to see that they were served simply rolled lightly in granulated sugar. I could have ordered 4 orders. They were great. It was a great end to a good meal. My only complaint was the lack of more tofu dishes but other then that it was a good meal and we will definitely be back. As always.....Stay Sweet.

I've been to Renzos 4 times, and every time it's a slam dunk. I might be shooting myself in the foot here, but it's hard to understand how they keep their prices so fair while maintaining such high quality meat, service, and cooking, but they do. The meat is cooked to perfection every time, service is quick and friendly, and the atmosphere is great. Maybe it's the location - tucked in a strip mall off of Kennedy - but it doesn't really matter. The point is that Renzo's never fails to deliver (no pun intended - they actually deliver, too), and even my Argentine friend, who's very picky with Argentinian restaurants, fell in love with the place. As long as they keep this up, the place is here to stay.

Not cheap, but well worth the experience.  An omakase is a must (i.e., the raison d'etre for visiting the Iron Chef).  Complement it with their outstanding sushi selection to complete the experience.  Don't forget a good sake to complement the food.

A friend who works with Vietnamese grad students overheard them say this was the best Vietnamese restaurant in town.  I am not qualified to make that call, but I haven't eaten anywhere else since! Best vermicelli.  Delicious BBQ pork. The bang mi is quite good when they aren't out if it. I also love the spicy beef pho (ask for it sans pigs foot if you are squeamish). It is my go to for takeout when trying to fight off a cold. 

The avocado smoothie is made with sweetened condensed milk. I love it, as didn't 2 year old.

Good place But the place is insanely cold, we ask for the ac to be lowered down but NO LUCK. 
I brought my family of 18 but I guess not again.

I got a vanilla latte and chocolate croissant here. The croissant was the best I've had in Tampa. It was on that Paris level of pastries. The only reason I gave this place 4 stars is because they were not on top of what they had versus ran out of. So I paid for a type of coffee that they ended up not having ingredients for and I had to figure out something else to order at the last minute since I already paid for it. It also took forever, but it was good so I will not complain about that too much. However, it was also about $14 for the croissant and coffee so a little bit pricey.

I was shocked to see a four star average for this place. When we sat down I had to have heard "Vest Thai food in town" mumbled across from two different conversations. We ordered the soup and it was amaaaaazing. Best most flavorful and delicious and warm and puzzling soup I've ever had. Gotta give it a million stars because it's just the best. It confuses your taste buds because it satisfies every flavor pad on your tongue : salty, sweet, spicy... SO GOOD. Please go and order it.

This is what I expected it to be, good service average food. However my biggest disappointment was portion sizes, it's like everything was shrunken. Ordered the spinach and artichoke dip and boneless buffalo wings (bites). The flavor was ok but small. Then I gotta half rack of ribs and I couldn't believe how small it was. They have definitely changed their serving sizes, which is a shame.
Tasty baked goods but the women that work there are so unfriendly and snide that it makes the experience so miserable

First off, the inside of this place is ADORABLE! It is so cute and perfect for anyone who wants a good Instagram photo! The staff was kind and really sweet! Of course we got the peanut butter candy pie which is out of this world (but prepare yourself, it's very rich!). We also got the peanut butter fudge bar which was less exciting. The layers came apart and the bottom layer was so hard we couldn't even eat it. The top layer was tasty though. My daughter loved the pumpkin bread, too. I didn't love the pecan pie, but that's honestly probably due to my not eating it for several days. I'm going to try it again and eat it immediately next time! All in all, it's definitely worth a trip and I can't wait to try their savory pies.

There's Chic Fil-A, Popeyes, PDQ, all the other fast food chains, and all the restaurants and pubs that serve chicken tenders. And then there's Guthrie's, now conveniently in S Tampa. I had the absolute freshest tasting chicken tenders from there today. Even the last couple strips I ate still tasted so fresh after cooling down. They told someone to let their chicken rest for a minute since they were so fresh. Simple menu, simple concept, but very tasty. The breading is light and crispy. The garlic toast was pretty salty though. The line should be here, not Popeyes.

We went on a Sunday morning, on our way home from Key West. We had mojitos to start (traditional, pineapple and mango) and my wife had the mimosa roja (with watermelon juice) and all were delicious. The cuban coffee was just as good as the Cuban Coffee Queen in Key West (sorry CCQ)! We had the all-inclusive ($28 per person) brunch, as the plates are tapas-style. The four of us probably tried 14 different dishes, ranging from the french toast, cinnamon waffle, and churros to the seafood soup and grilled octopus. Everything we tried was delicious! Mango Butter? Dulce de Leche? OMG! Our server paced everything well and she was super attentive, even though the place was busy.

They have specials for lunch and dinner, and if you're inclined to just sit at the bar, that is a good place too. There is street parking (if you're lucky) and public lots nearby. Reportedly there is valet parking for dinner.  The decor inside was like being on the street - a two-floor high ceiling made it look like outside with tables on or near balconies. Big fans turning above resembled all of the ones I've seen in movies or tv about Cuba. This place is a must if you are in or near Philly, and great to feel like you've escaped the icy grip of winter, if just for a little while!

Michael from the Front Desk is the quintessence of professional cordiality and efficiency.  Seriously.  He even looks the part.  If there were a magazine entitled Dapper and Considerate Hospitality Professional, he would be the cover model.
And Anja the manager is super responsive, and she has her operation smoothly under control.  Thanks, Anja, for the courtesy you showed.
And one last shout out*... to Patricia, the housekeeper (that I never met) but who left me (A) a card with her name on it and (B) a crazy spotless room that redefined "tidy".  You know how the first blast of a cold shower can refresh the senses?  Amazingly, the room Patricia prepared for me had the same effect... a visual splash of order and crisp linens etc. that actually refreshed.  Thanks.
        * I'm gonna pioneer the Unsung Awards, where the folks who are normally unsung and unseen get the props they deserve.  It's funny/sad that a housekeeper who puts TLC into her work is someone you often never even see.  Keep ya posted...
Excellent drinks and food, sometimes line is a little long but well worth the  wait. A welcome addition to my childhood neighborhood.

A great spot with great decor and food. I try to stay on the healthy side with my meals and usually get the grilled chicken salads which are excellent. The lettuce and vegetables are always fresh, and the grilled chicken cooked to perfection. And when I'm not eating as healthy, the cheesesteaks are excellent and well.

I don't think this is authentic Thai food at all. My Mom's best friend is Thai so I ate a lot of Thai food growing up and it remains one of my favorite types of food. 
That being said if you go and don't expect your fav Thai food dish to be there, and just have expectations of Asian-esque kind of dining than maybe you might enjoy it?

Gotta say i grew up on Johnny's pizza definitely the best in the area. But besides the great food and the great counter girls. The people in the back could give you PTSD any counter girl ive known that worked there feels unsafe and disturbed by the comments some of the other workers make. Someone i had known who worked there left because she felt uncomfortable and when she told the boss was asked to leave and not paid. 
Could be a really awesome spot but they'd rather employ creeps who cant mind there own business and have 8 of there kids in the eating area screaming. But good food if you can put all that aside. 

Haven't been there since she told me that. Probably a year ago couldn't tell you if the food changed. Hope it didn't because thats all they got.
This place is amazing! If you haven't been drop what your doing and go. Everything is great you can't go wrong. Also ask about the Sunday meal, which is a really cool and unique experience.

Awesome food, drinks, and service! We visited during taco week for the first time and they were some of the best tacos we've had in St. Louis!! For drinks, we had 2 of their fall cocktail specials and both are great. We can't wait to come back and try more of their BBQ!!

This place is so good.. the atmosphere.. the hookah.. background music.. pasta.. cocktails.. just loved everything about it.
Our server was Dean and he took such good care of our special request for the food and drinks.. it was a lovely dinner an evening well spent!! Thanks Dean!!!

This review won't be very helpful, but I am trying to catch up on my recent dining experiences in Nashville.  The Park Cafe offers an excellent menu and service.  We have dined here several times over the last few months.  My only complaint is that there is no self-parking nearby (I refuse to hand over the keys for my car to a stranger.)

This place really disappointed, but in my recent return to NOLA, I am shocked at the caliber of foodstuffs found within this hallowed foodie locale. I've always know to avoid the french quarter if value and flavor is what you're in search of - shame on me, I suppose. We tried a sampler platter of étouffée, gumbo, and Jambalaya. Not impressed with any dish they brought out. 

The gumbo tasted more homogenous and sweet than muddy and interesting, and was much more refined than you normally would expect in a gumbo - as though they strained out all the wonderful bits that developed through time. I was told that a full cup of each soup comes with the platter of three items, but I would summate that if I had the ability to combine all three dishes, I would find little more than a cup of soup between all three. The rest of what I purchased assuredly was rice, so ask for rice on the side if you order a cup to be sure of your quantities - save for the jambalaya. 

The jambalaya was mildly flavorful, and the sausage was fine - but not what you would expect in NOLA. Hell, I get better Andouille in Kansas City at a place called Fritz's Smoked Meats, on State-line Road. 

The étouffée was the most interesting, but still tasted like something other than seafood. I couldn't place it, but it's not what I expected - I could not eat it after a few tastings. They also seem to use some sort of thickener that has nothing to do with time and love; the soups were bordering on gelatinous. 

I would never return to this place, as the value gained from the purchase price is far too unbalanced; the death knell for me however must have been the flavors; they aren't revolting, but just not at all what you'd expect. More refined and subtle than the strong, dirty creole seasonings you search out for in NOLA. This experience serves me right, as in my travels I've come to take mark of establishments with "sandwich wranglers" hustling just outside the door, obnoxiously inviting patrons to dine within.
