We shared the family-size Red Bass served in a poblano sauce. The fish was cooked beautifully the poblano sauce was not that impressive but paired well with it. We purposely ordered less small dishes because we thought the $60 family-sized fish would leave us with an excess of leftovers, but this was not the case. We were a party of two and this was enough food to be satisfied but definitely not family-size proportions. 

All in all, the food tasted excellent, the service was efficient, and our waitress was friendly.
Yes, do have breakfast here. Breakfast burrito was excellent. As well as the French toast. Not to mention that it's serve yourself gourmet coffee.
Asking customers for tip is not okay,  especially when left 20% already.  Food was mediocre at best, no service.  Shame on you.

FUCKING NOMZ! I will forever remember this place because of that one night I got stranded, locked myself out, lost my phone, lost my friends, lost my dignity, and... well nevermind, we've all been there before. You know, that night you feel like you're on the Maury Povich show. Pretty much the same story.

Anyways, I'm not sure what was worse: Freebird's being closed that night of all nights or me having to watch and smell Bagel Cafe making food until 6:30 AM ESPECIALLY WHEN I HAD THE DRUNKEN MUNCHIES!? They wouldn't even make people do that in Guantanamo. I was almost bath salts status. Eat fucking Pirate's face off. Eww... I'd do anything for [food], but I won't do that.

My husband and I stopped by the Crepes Your Way which is next to Neiman Marcus at International Mall in Tampa. If I could give this place zero stars I would because the crepes were that horrible!  We ordered the vegetarian crepes which had disgusting frozen spinach, canned olives, canned mushroom, and hardly any mozzarella cheese and one tiny piece of a unripe tomato. It was basically a canned sliced olive crepe because the rest of the ingredients were cut in tiny pieces you could barely taste it and the ingredients were not mixed together. 

There was absolutely no taste or flavor and it was grossly put together.  There was no seasoning, no herbs and cheap quality ingredients! The crepe has balsamic vinegar on top of it which was all I could taste was the sourness of the vinegar!  When I cut into the crepe it was so thin in cut into the paper that was underneath it.  The owner had his wife and two sons working there.  The older son probably in his teens was behind the counter while his dad (The owner) was showing him how to make the crepe and the the other son around 10 years old served us the crepes, I was served my crepe first than 10 minutes later my husband got his and we were the only ones in the store. 

The owner came to our table and asked how we liked the crepes?   He noticed that the crepes were barely touched and  I told him there was no flavor and the ingredients taste like everything was out of a can and he said "you ordered the vegetable crepe that is why it has no taste!"  I was shocked at his reaction and obviously he is not a good business person when it comes to customer service.  If that's the case than tell us next time not to order it because it is a horrible tasting crepe and save us a lot of money because the crepes were very expensive and they were horrible tasting!  We will definitely not be back and we definitely do not recommend. Shame on the owner for serving horrible tasting food and very poor customer service!  AVOID AT ALL COST AND STAY AWAY!
Ordered the brown stew chicken and curry chicken via GrubHub. It was DELICIOUS. That brown stew sauce is out of control yummy.
Food had wonderful flavor. It took over an hour to get our main course and they forgot our Ceasar salad.

This is the best outback i have been to yet! From the minute we walked in the door our host was holding the door open for us with menus in hand and a booth ready for us to be seated at. Our waiter, Matthew, had great attitude, charisma and charm and provided us with EXCELLENT service down to the tee. Despite one of our steaks coming back very overcooked, Matthew took the steak alone instead of taking the entire plate of food away... Big plus!! The steak was then personally brought to our table by the manager who made sure that the steak was made right and was courteous enough to remove the entree off our bill without us asking, as compensation for the inconvenience and the wait. Overall, this team was working as just that... A team! 5 stars to our restaurant experience at Tarpon Springs! Keep up the good work everyone!
Very consistent. I had to wait several minutes one night at the drive-thru because they were making fresh food. I love that the quality there is always excellent and the service is friendly.

OVERALL: this is something to do and show around out of towners. I've been here at least 3 times, but twice was more than enough for me. A OK rating for me. I'm not a big plant person but I think if you are then you'll love this place. 

WHAT: Inside is basically a jungle garden forrest with a man made river running through it. You can take a boat ride on it during business hours and they take a photo of you that you can purchase. I think it's better to see inside during the day. But better to see outside at night especially during the holidays when they have all the Christmas lights decorating the trees outside. 

KIDS: Every time I've been here they have some kind of children's exhibit fun activity for them. It's usually during a range of hours though. 

EAT: Restaurants are definitely over priced but it is a hotel so that's expected. Ice cream place was yummy. Nice bathrooms. I thought this would be a more happening place at night with the bars, but they were empty. 

PARKING: $21 for self parking. Free if up to 20 minutes but I swear their clock tacks on an extra 10 min so you have to pay the fee.

Stopped by during a snowstorm and the place was still open! My friend and I had the sandwich and didn't try any of the desserts/baked goods so I cannot comment on those (although they smelled amazing). I had the egg white/spinach/feta wrap and tried my friend's grilled cheese. Both were delicious and I highly recommend this place!

Only downside is limited seating but I am writing solely about the food (which was great!) 

Will be back to try the baked goods soon!

Server Emily made our experience good from the get go! Provided us tons if info on menu suggestions and she was very personable and attended your needs. Recommend the Pretzel crusted New England Cod. Hefty portion size and needed a to go for the meal it was overwhelming but absolutely delish. Will definitely go again for service and food

I've been to this place a few times now and each time is great. The typical NOLA food, which a lot of times is not as good as your favorite place. Here they make everything good, that I've had anyway. I've had fried seafood poboys and boiled crawfish, and all have been very good. It's a hole in the wall type place with great food, who doesn't like that?

The boiled crawfish are a definite highlight. I have never had boiled crawfish from a restaurant that were that good, usually have to wait for a family and friend boil where you can put whatever you want in. Restaurants usually don't want to make them too spicy for tourists or people that don't eat crawfish. Portside does it right. I didn't want to go back to work after eating them, just relax out on their porch. I've had their poboys as well, most recently the catfish poboy, it was great. 

The staff is very friendly, and it's easy to blend in and feel at home. It's a popular lunch spot for sure, and I'll be back again, especially for crawfish season.

We went there last fall and have been raving about it since.  As far asI could tell, everything was home made from scratch down to the butter.   The bread was warm and soft like it was just made. I got a chocolate martini and it was strong. I got the baked cheesy fish dish and although on the rich side I could taste how fresh the fish was.  With one waitress, she divyed up her time well with 4-6 tables to serve we never felt neglected.

Delightful dinner at this cozy spot. I came for one night to Philly from NY and was recommended to try this spot. So glad I tried their "Let us cook for you", which is a 4 course tasting menu where the chef chooses everything. I was a bit scared of "blindly" ordering this option as you don't know what is coming, but they ask if you have any dietary restrictions (I asked to avoid fried food). Everything was delicious and ingredients were super fresh.
The whole table is required to get this option, so for two we had:
- Chicken liver pate: not very fond of pate in general, but it was good. Bread was amazing! One of the Chefs worked 8 years at Balthazar Bakery, so no wonder... Also, you need to have this butter!! It's like they brought it the same day from the farm!
- Roasted beets, lentil and feta cheese salad: dressing was great, not too much, but still full of flavor
- Shrimp ceviche: my favorite of the three apps. They even finish the dish with a topping of dry corn which is how the Peruvians do it 
- Gnocchi with pork ragu, broccoli rabe and tomato sauce: not on the menu, loved every bite and I'm not a huge fan of pasta
- Skate wing with German style potato salad and creamy sauce: also not on the menu (potato salad does come with trout, agree is great side with fish). I was very excited to try this as I had seen skate wing in several menus of trendy NY restaurants. The sauce had mustard and was just amazing!
- Dessert was a pear tart with vanilla gelato and pear sorbet. Liked the pear on pear idea.

Overall, I 100% recommend the "Let us cook for you" menu for those a bit more adventurous. I discovered things I liked that I would normally wouldn't order. Also if you are two it is great because you can "trade" whatever you don't like with the other person. It is a lot of food, so if you skip one course, you will still be satisfied.

PS: the wine on tap is great too. Get the Malbec!
I love this restaurant. From their burgers to their steaks. All delicious. I love the brisket ravioli. Service is friendly and great atmosphere.

The grass fed burgers are so delicious.  Their range free chicken sandwiches are tasty as well. I'm very particular when it comes to quality of food; in every bite is juiciness, texture, and a richness in taste.  This place easily (in quality) out does the 5Guys, In-n-Out, and other hamburger/sandwich proclaiming restaurants.  Staff is super friendly and place has a good environment.  Over all, great experience.  Oh and for the critics, they just opened and with time they will expand their menu.  To start, with what they have now is enough to partake of the Graze Premium Burgers experience and know what they are about. They have my business and my stomach.

This small restaurant located in the Pan-Asian Market has excellent food for reasonable prices. The Pho broth is well seasoned and beefy. The add ins are super fresh so the cilantro and basil add aroma and taste instantly when added to the broth. Caution, the Jalapeños do the same and add heat too. Yum!  
We
Have tried the Singapore noodles, Chow Fun and Fried Rice and they are tasty as well. The Firecracker Green beans are crunchy, spicy, porky deliciousness. 
Fast and easy even when busy.

I really loved "Lucky Bamboo".  They are smart to have chinese menu in addition to the American one.  Very clever because people need to try menu items that are more authentic  but can also choose something they are more familiar with.  Someone should have done this a long time ago. 
I thought the service and food were great!  I love the bean sprouts and chives.  The five flavours chicken was very good and I loved the salad dressing.  It was a creamy dressing made with ginger, carrot and apple.    The atmosphere was great and there were a lot of live plants which was refreshing.  I can't wait to go back!

I've never eaten here but Dave's clapbacks are worth 5 stars. I'm definitely making this my next  dinner destination. Slow service noted, but the food reviews are fantastic so I'll clear my schedule to enjoy a proper pizza experience.  See ya soon!

Ha Long Bay opened up in the old Ivory Chinese Restaurant location. Upon noticing this, I decided to go try this place out. I had decent expectations for this place because the Ha Long Bay in Pinellas Park was rather good, especially the dim sum choices. Upon entering, I noticed that the renovations were rather significant. Gone was the old cramped and slightly claustrophobia inducing dining room. Instead, the renovations opened up the space and made it much more modern, with nice tile floors and modern wall paint. Some old dividing walls were removed which further enhanced the open feel. But while I was impressed by the renovations, I was less impressed with the food. It was rather discouraging to find that they were using the old Ivory menus without even removing the old restaurant name. The dim sum choices were limited and were at least a full $1 more expensive than most other dim sum places in Tampa and St. Pete. The salted fish and eggplant clay pot, while of a decent portion size, was definitely on the saltier side. Based on my first impressions, although I was somewhat disappointed with the food, I do also believe that this place has lots of potential. I will give this place the benefit of the doubt that because they just opened, they have some issues to iron out still. But my hope is that given time, if and when I do come back, I'm expecting much better the 2nd time around.
This place is a dive with a great ambiance and chilled vibe.  I ordered an egg burrito with chorizo.  The tortillas were homemade along with the anejo sauces.

One of our crowd said this was the best bar b que she's had in her life. I say it was in the top 5 of mine, which is great. Who knew that great que exists in bywater?

I loved the mix plate and the bartender was so cute, I embarrassed her by complimenting her tattoos. 

Everything here is delicious and cheap. Get your ass out of town and check this place out. I rode a bike here, you can take a damn uber!

Peanut butter pie and booze. Do it!

Fast and efficient service, every time! 
Food is amazing, service is even better.  yum!

Loved the nachos at this place. I have no idea how they make them so good each time but they do. Its so good. They have good drinks  and the ambiemce is nice small place but its got a great vibe. Only downside is that its a cash only business.
We had the breakfast pizza and it was absolutely delicious!!! Our kids loved it and so did everyone in our party! We had to order another breakfast pizza because it was so yummy!
Great Place.  Good simple fresh food at a good price.  I stop here with my kids, I used to stop here with my dad...he used to stop here with his dad.  It's still good.
The chips here are so freaking good. The queso is my favorite thing ever. I'm so obsessed.

This place has amazing food and great service. Sometimes crowded on weekends. I recommend the Johnny Cash - - French toast sandwich with fried banana, bacon and maple praline butter. The biscuits are sweet and delicious but if you order biscuits and gravy make sure to ask for extra gravy. The only reason I didn't give them five stars is because the coffee kind of sucks. If this place could get better coffee they would deserve five stars. You can't really be a breakfast place and have bad coffee. I look forward also to trying their craft cocktails. Will definitely return.

We were there for breakfast on a Friday morning and it was quiet.  Service was good and the food was excellent.  Had the avocado toast, very original.  Great flavors combination BBC and the right seasoning.

SO LOUD!!!! SO LOUD!!!

The staff was very friendly and food delivery was quick.  I have to admit the Fried Pork Tenderloin as pretty darn good.  A little greasy but very good!

Potato skins had flavor but again greasy :(

I would come back and hope that the greasiness was a one time thing as the taste was there

Weekday atmosphere is nor bad for a cup or two at night.  Not very many guests and the (cute) waitresses were a plus.  I live around the delmar loop so it was a nice change of pace from the noisy college bars.  The tables outside makes it feel odd for a single person doing a crawl but inside was not odd.

Delightful cafe blocks from St Charles with outdoor seating and a sunny interior.  There is also a snowball stand in the front.  We stopped in for a quick breakfast and everything was fresh and delicious.  I have the veggie omelette and my husband has the french toast that was served with a side of authentic New Orleans hot sausage.  We are locals and this tops some of the other more established breakfast spots.  We will definitely be back!

I was wary of this place after reading the reviews. I was worried it would be too generic...not at all authentic with bad service, but I was wrong.

The restaurant was pretty empty and we had attentive service. The food was pretty good! I can't say it was super authentic, but it wasn't like something you'd get a Chilis (that's a good thing to me!). And there's free chips and salsa!

This won't be one of my new favorite restaurants, but I'll surely return if the mood strikes me.

I thought the chicken fried rice was "good" and the sushi was "fine." One of the rolls (with tuna) seemed so sketchy, I was afraid of getting sick! The dressing on the salad was a bit bitter and an unappealing color; not the vibrant orange it usually is. The menu seems fairly limited, yet has several hand-written modifications as if it's constantly changing. I found it fairly tacky. Not exactly a place you'd go for an impressive meal or a meal with company. Pricing was decent and service was mediocre, though not bad. My server also had a bit of difficulty with English so some of my questions were lost on her. Overall, there's just better sushi out there. I wouldn't return.

This may be a chicken restaurant,  but I had the best Swiss mushroom burger there I've ever had in my life..pepper sauce, crisp bun, real mushrooms, sauteed onions...so many different choices on the menu..YUM!

My experience here today wasn't great. I'm going to chock it up to the fact that it's new and they recently had a decent write up in the News Journal. They were pretty slammed. My buddy and I came in at 12:30 for lunch and waited  about 15 min for a table. We waited another 10 before the waitress came over and said she'd be with us shortly. She never came back. Thankfully another waitress came over about 10 min after that and took pity on us. We placed our order and probably waited another half hour for the food to arrive. My buddy had a Reuben and fries which he said was good. I had creamed chip beef on toast. Honestly I've made better at home. Lots of creamed, not much beef. After we were done and ready to pay I was informed that the credit card machine was down and I didn't have enough cash. I had to walk next door to rite aid and pay $3.75 (loan shark charges) to use their ATM! The waitress that eventually waited on us was very sweet and apologetic so I left a good tip for her. I'll wait 6 months before I go back to see if my experience was just growing pains.
Great just walked in and got a table in the balcony no wait fr and the apps I ordered was great

As a native of Michigan, I have a pretty high standard for Middle Eastern food. It's one of the few things that I miss, the ability to get fresh hummus or tabouli at just about every deli and a Middle Eastern restaurant on practically every block. When I found this cart, I knew I finally found the real deal. This place lives up to its name. I absolutely love their falafel and hummus sandwich, and it's so cheap! They're not at all stingy about the portion size, and they serve it in the proper wrap--thin, flat pita, not the bready kind found elsewhere. The hummus consistency is perfect, not too thick. And falafels are the perfect crunchy texture. 

Both the man and woman (husband and wife??) are friendly, though I saw him more often. I have no idea how they work in such hot quarters in the summer, so I hope they're at least getting a good profit out of it. If you're around Love Park at lunch time, grab a sandwich and head to a park bench and prepare to enjoy a delicious meal.

Saturday night my husband and I had the opportunity to give Rapscallion a second try...and so begins my review redux!
The restaurant itself hasn't changed, the staffing hasn't necessarily changed nor has the menu, HOWEVER, our experience was much different this time around.  We were seated at Table 16 which is a very private booth across from the (real) wood- burning fireplace as opposed to the booth by the kitchen we had last time.  The fireplace was so calming and my husband enjoyed the live music that we could hear from the bar...not in a loud obnoxious way.  
Our server (Amber) was awesome...she was personable and knowledgeable.  I feel confident that had we found plastic in our meal, this server would've handled the situation much differently than our previous server.  We get it...sh*t happens...but how you clean it up is what speaks volumes.  Our last experience was so awkward that we almost fell over laughing when that server walked by on Sat!  
Our meals were amazing.  Of course, we started with the Roasted Garlic appetizer...is was ridiculously yummy and had the 8 pieces of flat bread as described on the menu.  I think they could add a few more pieces (comes with 2 whole garlic cloves) but recognize that I'm a carb-o-holic!  I ordered the Alaskan Halibut and my husband got the New York.  Both meals were delicious!  I even requested a modification and it came out as ordered.
Moral of the story:  Raspscallion has been voted Reno's best seafood for a reason.  An average meal for two is $100...add in the cost of a babysitter and a movie and that's a pricey evening out.  If we hadn't had a reservation on Saturday night, we probably would've had dinner at a truly sub par restaurant.  So...thank you Rapscallion for giving me the opportunity to update a bad review!  Although we only get out once a month, we've certainly added you as one of our top choices!  
Sincerely, 
Parents of Twin Toddlers...

So I've lived in Santa Barbara for over 3 years now, and I'd sort of given up on finding a pizza place that was as good as my favorite LA joint. I do like Rusty's, but it's no Mulberry Street Pizza. 

I dream of the big, floppy slices that you fold in half, with a slightly crispy crust, tangy/spicy sauce, gooey cheese, and lots of garlic. Little did I know that my perfect slice was right there on Figueroa Street the whole time. 

It could be that most times I'm down in that area, Gino's isn't open. But I lucked out last Saturday night -we needed a quick bite before a show at the Arlington and every other place was packed. Gino's was open and only had one patron, so we ventured in. My slice was like the pizza I'd been dreaming of ever since I left LA. It was perfect, and I probably could have eaten half a pie if I'd had the time. My salad was also delicious with the perfect amount of what tasted like homemade dressing. My fiance got a panino sandwich with meatballs which looked really cheesy and delicious. 

What made the experience even more wonderful was that we were both satisfied for only $11 total. That is unheard of in Santa Barbara.  The only bad news is that I will be craving Gino's constantly now and will force my fiance to eat there all the time.

This is where TSA agents come to
Work when they get fired. Service was horrible!! I wouldn't come if it was the only place in NOLA. Food was airport  quality.

Popped in on a Friday night and sat at the bar as all tables were full. Bartenders were very friendly and knowledgable. Ordered two cocktails off the menu both delicious. Ordered an appetizer to share and taco's, which was the perfect amount of food. Atmosphere made for a great evening!

Not bad.  Not bad.  Wanted quick and easy, and close to the hotel, before leaving NoLa.  I had the roast beef debris po boy.  Of course some oysters.  And some fried gator.  And an Abita amber......because what else do you wash all of that down with?  You really can't go wrong with any of these items I listed above.  I particularly enjoyed the jalepeno slaw that was served with the gator.  Service was good.  Ambiance is somewhat average, but definitely not bad.  Convenient Canal street location.

This was my fourth experience at Circles, the first for take out. I had been pretty impressed with the food and service while seated at the restaurant. This takeout order was a big disappointment. We ordered Summer rolls and fried calamari as appetizers. The summer rolls were fine. The calamari was tasty too, although the sauce was so salty as to be inedible. So we ate the calamari plain. We ordered a Pork Green Curry and a Chicken Red Curry. The take-out bowls were totally deceiving. What looked like it would be nice portion was all liquid in both orders. After fishing out the chicken, peppers, bamboo shoots, etc., there was not even enough to satisfy a child. Were it not for the side of brown rice, we would have still been hungry. As take-out, it would have been a burden to return all the way to the restaurant for replacements, so we grumbled and chalked it up to experience. Had I been in the restaurant and served this meal, it would have gone back.

There's a pizza place 20 feet from my door and yet I walk many extra blocks to get to Lazaros Pizza. Football (soccer for you Americans) is always on the TV when you walk in so this place is pretty legit. I'll say this up front: I'm not a huge fan of their pizza by the slice - does anyone else think the tomato sauce is too sweet? Luckily I never just get a slice - I'm a huge fan of ordering an extra large white pizza to go...delicious! 

A large white pizza will run you about $13 - cheap compared to just about every other establishment. Big slices of well cooked pizza with the perfect amount of grease and crust that is to die for....for a while my roommate and I were ordering Lazaros about once a week just to give you an idea of how much we like the place! 

Word of caution: cash only and expect longer waits on game days.
Beef's is my favorite spot whenever I go home! Chicken wings from here are always going to be my fave!

We have been dining at the Chop House since they opened and have never been disappointed.  Favorites include any steak and the calamari.  They have a good selection of beer and an excellent wine list.  By far my favorite when I'm "baching it" is the bar at happy hour; Kona beef tips with mushrooms and onions, fresh rolls, butter and an interesting people watching population.

While waiting for my flight back to Seattle I stopped for a bite at Ducky's, I was pleasantly surprised by the fresh grouper sandwich I ordered.  The waitstaff were very friendly and attentive, keep in mind the place was very busy and still the staff were on point!  If in the Tampa airport stop by and have a bite.  The menu is somewhat limited, but the food was ok.
A little pricey but the seafood is soo good. Customer service is A1. I will definitely go back soon.

Best Italian sandwich I've ever had! Came here for lunch, everything was super fresh and tasty. Tomato soup was awesome and obviously homemade. Super cute atmosphere with a great array of local goods to purchase as well.

We wanted to check this place out after seeing the great reviews. 
Arrived on Thursday (New Years Day) around noon and the place was packed with a hour and a half wait. We put our name in and went next door for a drink, 
The restaurant texted us when our table was ready and also had a cool app that you can check your place in line. 
Only had drinks and a few apps. The tuscan fries were good but had a LOT of garlic.
My friend loved her Kale salad. 
If you like a bloody mary, try the cucumber mary made with cucumber vodka. It was unbelievable. 

This was hands down out favorite place in Nashville and this place had the BEST service we got our whole trip. A+ to the staff. We were really really impressed. 
We went back on Friday night around 1am and it was pretty empty. The guy sitting next to us said its really a better brunch or Sunday Funday bar and not busy at night.

I randomly ended up picking this restaurant. I'm visiting from out of town and really just wanted something fresh. I had the Supreme Nachos and they were so very good! Wait staff is friendly, attentive, and laid back. It was great to go in there alone and sit at the bar. Clean kitchen, tasty food, welcoming environment, and great staff. I recommend checking this place out whether you are vegan or not.

This place is a little pricey, but they have a lot of unique burgers that make it fun. We ordered the zucchini fries and fried avocado. Both are absolutely delicious. The zucchini fries come with a black pepper sauce that is one of the best dipping sauces I've had in awhile. I had the Walk of Fame burger, which is more of a classic burger, but they have several selections like hot chicken or ahi tuna. I also really like the atmosphere as it's made to look like a classic "study" in an older home.

This is the worse place for eat. Sunday the 22th we when to eat there, was a party of 10 people in total we have that reunion because one of my coworkers move. Anyways be careful with the waitress name Hanna she likes to charge over 15 % in a check of 62.00 ending to pay 73 plus change, and her services is completely bad, also she keep changes one of my friends, she has to ask her for her 20 dollars change and Hanna look at her tips and pull 20 dollars to give back to my friend, also she do it with a lot attitude and whisper about what? Who's knows no mention she didn't do good job in our table two more people are upset because of her. I work for a big company and most of my costumers ask me where is a good place to eat, because they are out state and of corse we live in Reno, so far I sent them to Miguel's, or scapollinis I never going to sent them to this place because I don't want they have bad experience like me.. btw (i talk to the manager from there and its 3 days and I dint heard nothing from them. my ticket supposed has to be fix and in my bank account still show 73 plus change.) i will post it fb. Good luck!! I'm not happy with this place!
Amazing. We tried the jambalaya and red beans and rice. Wow. Out of this world. And so reasonable. Plus we got to meet Norton! In the flesh! Such nice people. Can't wait to go back.

There were pre-built options on the menu for the pizza and you can also build your own. The appetizers and salad section looked good too. They happily do half and half for the large and jumbo size pizza. We got the cherry poppins and spuds Rodriguez from the menu. The choice toppings on each of the pizzas was tasty and the thin crust was definitely the highlight. 
They had an assortment of fire sauce for heat lovers and 60 beers on tap as well as a few wines. I thought the beer was on the expensive side. I would certainly try one of their cocktails next time. 
The place was noisy but that's not a deterrent for us. We'll come back here for more pizza. Happy about this new addition to the grove.

Note:
The menu mentions gluten free and vegan options.

I'm a little puzzled by some of the negative reviews as many contain variations on the phrase, "Not as good as the Chinese restaurants in Chicago." Really? You think? Using Chicago, the third largest city in the US and the city with the fourth highest economic output in the world (after Tokyo, NYC, and LA) as the standard, how many restaurants (or any entertainmen/recreation enterprise) in Indianapolis of any kind would stand up?

I give it five stars because the food is fairly authentic, there's a huge selection, and you would be hard pressed to find something better in *Indianapolis*. The dim sum is also very good - again, probably the best in Indianapolis, especially after Shen Yang closed.

Yes, there are better dim sum places in Chicago, LA, NYC, Toronto, Vancouver, etc. etc. etc., but that's like telling the parched traveler in the Sahara that the water in the oasis he just found is not as clean as bottled water in North America. Not helpful.

You just can't compare Indianapolis restaurants with Chicago restaurants, especially ethnic restaurants.

Quite possibly the best restaurant in Santa Barbara. Off the Main Street, this hidden gem is one of a kind. We made our way through 3 appetizers, the eggamuffins were our favorite. Their tri tip special easily melts in your mouth. Such a great place with eloquent elevated dishes. 

Very spaced out for covid and cozy outdoor seating. Thank you for a one in a life time meal!
A must go! for only being open for about 2 months, they have the best pho around, not to mention the egg rolls. They're nothing like you've ever had. Excellent food, quality, atmosphere, and service

This is by far one of my favorite places in Nashville. It is a "gay bar" but that doesn't mean that you have to be gay to go in and enjoy yourself. It is very casual, yet quite upscale at the same time. Even the smokers are not relegated to freezing in some outside corner. The staff is very good (Brandon is a great waiter) and the drinks are great (check out TJ, he makes some of the best!). I highly recommend Tribe for meeting some people and having a good evening out.

This is my go to Chinese restaurant. Granted, I only live a block away but I would probably still come here if I lived further. I ate here (take out) tonight for probably the 20th time in a year, and finally decided to write a review. They have dinner specials for $7.95. How awesome is that?  I can't figure out how they do it but the food is always pipping hot when it arrives. Even after I forgot I ordered and picked up 45 minutes late. This is not five star cuisine but they never pretend it's supposed to be. Anyways if you want good Chinese American food at a great price, New China cant be beat.

Super polite in the drive thru! Food was hit and fresh, I always order the same thing and it's a modified menu item. One of the best times I've received it.

Thanks for the hard work!
Best Korean food in Nashville. Banchan we're super flavorful, squid & mackerel dishes were fresh and just the right amount of heat & service was kind & quick. Going back soon !

Real Texas BBQ. I came on opening day and there was a line down the street.  I was very impressed at how the staff took our safety during the Corona lockdown with cleaning the laminated menus between guests, having a hand sanitizer station, the employees in masks and every guest I saw there had a mask on.
I got there a little later in the day and they were out of a couple of items, but that is the price you pay for having quality fresh food.  They open at 11AM and stay open until they sell out.   We ended up each getting the pulled pork sandwich, one with potato salad and the other with the beans.  The meat was amazing and the sides were great.  I really liked the sauce that came with it too.  
I can't wait to go back and try more stuff.

I wish so much that I still lived in Nashville so that I could eat here weekly again. The tortilla soup is better than any other I've tried. The bar service is always excellent. I would love to say I've tried all the tacos, but the California Club and Sloppy Jose are so good that I never get anything else!

Lovely spot, seems very authentic in aesthetic, and the food is phenomenal. As a vegan I don't always have many options beyond the same old soups, salads (seaweed, house salad) and vegetarian rolls (avocado, vegetable, cucumber, etc.) that you find in any Japanese restaurant. Yet at Horinoya there are many choices that I have yet to find at any other New Orleans' Japanese restaurants. Like natto (a type of fermented soy bean), oshinko (pickled daikon), and yamaimo (Japanese mountain yam), to name a few. There are the regular options as well, but to have such authentic vegetarian choices on top of the same old ones is great. Plus this diversity lends itself to the rest of the menu, not just sushi. There are many veggie appetizers, soups, and salads as well. Horinoya isn't cheap, but for the vegan the selection it is unparalleled in New Orleans and the food quality and freshness top-notch. My boyfriend is not vegetarian and he was similarly blown away by his seafood and meat-based dishes. Hands-down my favorite Japanese spot in New Orleans, and for vegans it blows the others out of the water. They also have a private dining room that appears to have a traditional Japanese-style low-table and seating on the floor; it would be great for a private dinner event (prob seats around 12, at least). Service is also very good, food came out quickly upon ordering, and the atmosphere is casual with tourists eating next to businessmen eating next to locals. I highly highly recommend Horinoya, to both vegans and omnivores alike. So worth it.
Me Hacienda has great chips and salsa and wonderful food on their menu!  Great Mexican beers tried the Victoria - yum!
The food is always amazing. The macaroni and cheese is one of my favorite items on the menu. The service is super good.

This place is super fun. When I think of sushi/karaoke bars, I automatically think "not for me." I was wrong. It was pretty awesome.

The food is really good and the menu is fun to look at. I am a tough critic when it comes to sushi and I had no complaints. The yakitori was pretty awesome too. Just imagine -- gizzards, giblets, hearts, livers, chicken skin (my fave), meatballs, etc grilled and on sticks! God is good.

As soon as I walked in, I knew I should have turned around and walked out. There was an awful smell pervading the entire place. Like an old folks home that hadn't been properly cleaned. Getting a scent picture?

As I was hungry, I ignored the flight reflex and sat down to eat. First thing I ordered was a glass of Malbec from the pre-printed corporate menu. Five minutes later the waitress returned to tell me that they, "no longer carry that wine." Really? So I ordered. Syrah. Got a healthy glass of wine, to their credit. 

Salad bar was well stocked with fresh ingredients. My steak, however, was tough and very clearly microwaved. Yes, they nuked a steak. Blech!

When my check came, I had been charged for the Malbec they "no longer carry." Had to tell the waitress to change the price. And, making matters worse, I woke up at 3AM with an upset stomach. 

I guess I should have followed my nose, after all.

Just ate here for the first time and it's fantastic. Full of flavor without being overly salty or sweet as can happen with vegan food. Great variety and I'll be back to try their daily switch-ups. Friendly and quick service and super affordable with huge portions. A four item plate gave me three meals, no lie. If you want soul food thats healthy with flavor this is it!

The atmosphere and simply the smell is great here, so comfortable. The food is always changing, I usually like to order the special especially if it's fish, there's always something fresh and light. I've also brought three different people here, 2 from New York and one from Boston, and all said that the Burger is one of the best they've ever had, one was "top 5 burgers" he ever had. The NorCal flatbread is really tasty but not too heavy, and not too much balsamic which has ruined similar flatbreads for me.

My husband and I discovered this place during my birthday weekend in NOLA in March.  Walking to the French Quarter I noticed the sign on the sidewalk that had WINO on it and it piqued my curiosity and then we happened to "peek" in the doorway and were greeted with the coolest wine dispensing machines we had ever seen on earth...ENOMATIC!  COOL was all I could think!  We walked in and had a ball after we got our little "credit card" to purchase the wines by the glass with.  The beauty of the whole system is you can just grab a clean glass hanging from the racks and try EVERYTHING!  No waiting, no flagging a waitress down for your next glass...just skip on over to el machino et voila!  We happened on WINO on Friday and came back again the next day it was so fun!  We just wish to death there was a place like this in California!

Stopped in between sightseeing for a quick dinner with the kids. Staff was friendly. Pizza, fries and chicken fingers were tasty and a very good value! Would recommend to anyone heading to the nearby museums.

So this is my third time here and I must say that this place is amazing. Ashley was my bartender she recommended the wings & pb&J sandwich the food was amazing and I can't say anything else. I also had the drink with the CBD oil and it was revolutionary. I will be back to the Thee Tree House and I can't wait to see what's in store for the future
Found on yelp for a quick place to grab a bite and it did not disappoint!! I wish it had inside seats but it's amazing.

Finally a place to get fresh crawfish. I lived in Louisiana before and I have been missing crawfish for a long time. I was hoping that Jazz Louisiana Kitchen would have fresh crawfish but even when they got the crawfish from Lake Tahoe they ruined the crawfish by cooking them then freezing them. Crawfish are a delicate dish that can only be thrown into the crawfish boil live then served fresh. If they are frozen and dead before being thrown into the boil or if they are boiled live then frozen, they lose their "magic." This is the first place outside of Louisiana, Alabama, or East Texas Gulf Coast that I have found good fresh crawfish. I love the Thai sauce intermediate even though it isn't the "traditional" Louisiana crawfish boil seasoning. The muscles are excellent also although I would ask that the restaurant get the larger New Zealand Greeenlip type of muscles which are larger an more awesome if possible. (Red's 395 Grill in Carson City and Sushi Pier Original get them so it is possible in the area.) A great addition to the restaurant options in Reno. I'll be back!

An amazing tapas place!  We have been here twice (the last time to celebrate our 12th wedding anniversary). The food and presentation is already top notch. Being close to Philadelphia, this is a place that would be at home even in the most upscale neighborhoods. If you are a foodie and want a very flavorful meal (and BYOB) then this is the place. Cheers!

One of our top usual Szechuan restaurant!! 

Casual go-to dish: Cold Noodles w/ Sesame Sauce 
For spicy lovers: Cold Noodles w/ Spicy 
(There's sliced cucumbers on the bottom so don't order a cucumber appetizer if you are ordering this one) 

Century Eggs w/ Eggplant: SO GOOD especially if you are a fan of hot oil, garlic, century eggs & eggplants. The flavors is just so perfect 

Cumin Lamb: YOU MUST TRY THIS. 

They also opened a spot called General Tsao in Center City, Samson St. It is also worth trying, but be aware it's slightly harder to find parking

If I keep going here over and over and over do I need to keep writing the reviews? 

Its not gonna change. I love this place. Great food, friendly staff, awesome service.

YES its that good.
Great food, service and location. We had the burger and a salad with grilled chicken.

They DONT SERVE BLACK PEOLE!!!! 

I was sitting at the bar for more than 30min
Not 1 person offer me a menu or cup of water,(the waiter & the manager saw me sitting there the whole time, then a white couple walk in & greeted them, offered them water & took they order, another couple walked in they did the same thing
Excellent food!  Love the atmosphere!   Highly recommend!   The Cauliflower dish was very tasty!   The oatmeal fish was a big surprise!   It was wonderful!

Peg Leg Porker is my all time favorite restaurant for ribs.  Their dry rub ribs are the very best I've ever had.  The sides are also great.  I love crinkle cut fires and theirs are very good.  The beans have great flavor.

Omg this place is amazing.  My first thought was, how amazing can a sandwich shop really be?  Well, let me tell you, it can be.  The place is very chaotic, as in, SUPER busy.  You might want to call in ahead of time your order.  The devil cake was so beyond not fishy, which is always a hit or miss with crab.  The buffalo chicken, ahem, tasted just like home.  I have looked everywhere in Tampa for a place that serves REAL chicken fingers, let alone a sandwich.  And this nailed both.  I love you Brocato!

Local Nevada FTW. Yea, so my girl and i make it on over to Great Basin off of Virginia, this is after a full 5 course meal after PF Changs (DAAAMNGOOD), and the food STILL LOOKED GOOD! WTF?! Ok, the bar is the only part we went to, so i cant really give u an honest assessment of the food, but it looked SO GOOD, so there is that. 

The older guy at the bar, suggested a few beers for us, and when he was able to, let us sample them. Some, like the Belgian Beers, you could not sample, and i totally understand why, they come in bottles. He suggested we try the Cherry Beer (name forgotten) , and DAMN, i would have that for breakfast, im serious! Another beer we tried was the CuVee Van De Keizer Blauw (i have the bottle on my desktop now) and it was a beer worthy of being poured into the Holy Grail. Serious. Jesus himself would have ended up drinking a few more than Mary Magdalane would allow, and still would have been forgiven! 

Seriously, if you want a variety of Muy EXCELLENTE beers, go nowhere else. Im not saying their selection is the biggest in Nevada (that goes to the 100+ beer place near the University), but for the best, accept no substitutes. Yea, maybe there are some hipsters, but F them. Drink your pints here, and scowl at them if you must. 

I think they make the pizza here with crack. I cant stop thinking about it, and im bloated on Excellent Chinese food.

The food was incredible! So delicious and would eat here again for the food. Unfortunately I had to give 3 stars due to the service. We got take out and I was told 30 minutes until it was ready and it ended up being an hour. So I waited 30 extra minutes once I got to the restaurant to pick up the food. If i was told it would be an hour wait on the phone, this wouldn't have been a problem. The staff also seemed like they did not what they were doing, clueless, and overwhelmed even though there were only 2 parties dining in. Sorry, but train your staff better or hire people who know how to work in the service industry!
This is my favorite Chinese restaurant to eat at! I love their orange chicken, but it sometimes is a little over cooked. This place is now my go-to Chinese restaurant.

Yum and yum again simple restaurant not simple cuisine. Amazing thoughtful flavors from bread to dessert and everything in between !! Surprised by the experience. The surroundings are fine but really do not match the level of the food or personal service! Drove 2 hours will come again

Oh hell yes.  An iconic Nola institution, established in 1840.  Of all the times I have visited this magical city, somehow I had not yet stepped foot into Antoine's until this last visit. 

I particularly enjoyed touring all of the many themed rooms of the restaurant.  The cavernous interior seems to keep going on for days.  I love the narrow, dimly lit wine cellar.  And the Rex room, a tribute to the Mardi Gras kings and queens over the years.  And of course, the escargot room, with a big snail adorned on the wall.  

Much like Commander's Palace, Antoine's serves up a 25 cent martini with the lunch menu. Limit of three, but they are strong, so that's about all one needs for a lunch cocktail.  (Seriously! Why doesn't everyone do this?!)  The prix fixe menu is $20 and my dining companion and I both opted for that, as well as an order of the Oysters Rockefeller, which was a dish originally crafted here at Antoine's.  It tasted so rich, the only thing they could do to adequately describe the rich flavor was to call it a Rockefeller.  Knowing that, how could we pass them up?  Iconic dish at an iconic restaurant. 

I chose the crawfish bisque, the petit filet, and the strawberry cake for dessert.  Nothing disappointed me.  

After I left, my friends who saw my photos and check-ins all kept asking me why I didn't get the baked Alaska.  Well shit.  I don't know the answer to that.  Why *didn't* I get the baked Alaska?  That goes perfectly with lunch on a Tuesday afternoon.  Next time....

Oh, and the cherries jubilee, served flaming!  

Very friendly service by a talented black-jacketed, bow-tied waitstaff who certainly know their way around the FOH.  

The best part was talking to my dear friend after my lunch, whose father was a waiter at Antoine's for 20 years.  His uncle was also a chef there, and created their bread pudding recipe. So incredibly cool.  He writes movie scripts, and he wants to write a script about the intricacies of the restaurant world at Antoine's.  The staff dynamic; the history; the celebrities, politicians, and dignitaries who dined there; the restaurant's relationship to Mardi Gras; and although I didn't ask him, I'm sure the ghosts.  Because how does a restaurant from 1840 not have a ghost or two floating around?  (Aside: if I were a ghost, I sure as hell would choose to haunt a restaurant that has oysters, creole gumbo, escargot, bananas foster, cherries jubilee, and bread pudding.  No abandoned old home for me.  I'm going to haunt the venue where the FOOD is!)

The Little Bacon Cheeseburger was large and I had it topped with lettuce, tomato, pickle, grilled onion and mushrooms, mayo and ketchup; VERY good, filling burger. Fries were amazing with perfect amount of salt. Got the large fry and shared it with my family of four, which was plenty. Clean and friendly.

They had to remake the pulled pork.  Guess the first batch was bad.  Nice quality control.   If you come, get alcohol or beer, burger is good but don't stray from those items.  Service is beyond slow, I'm talking dirt slow! If your car breaks down, stop here, if not drive on by.

I am being generous with my 1 star.  I will not be dining here again.  The service was slooooooooooooow.  Had to find our waiter EVERY time.  Need water?  too bad.  Want another cocktail?  Not happening.  We were never asked or given an opportunity.  Appetizers came and needed additional sauce on Corn Fritters.  Yup, you guessed it.  Never found anyone to ask for more.   The fritters were over fried, filled with dry filling, small in size and VERY dry.    New England Clam chowder needed salt.  We will never know if salt helped because none was on table and waiter did not appear for another 50 Minutes.   Dinner came and was ok.  No one raved about anything.  You know how at lease one person in your party will say,"  Wow, this is really good, anyone want a taste?"    No one said that.    Do your self a favor and eat at one of the million other places in Philly.   The bugs flying around the table, which was in the far back of restaurant, was the final straw.  Goodbye Devon Seafood.

The clam chowder was fresh and delicious. The side salad was big enough to be a salad as a entree. The shrimp Diablo had a great flavor, not to spicy. ( Gluten free) There was a garlic spinach as a side that was fabulous. Our waiter Louis was very attentive and helpful. This establishment has air conditioning, music and great food, it a must visit while visiting Treasure Island.

My second favorite cheese steak next to Stevie's prince of steaks

All in all - its pretty good

Three stars because workers are nice and there are some benches on a small lawn so you can eat your ice cream someplace other than the parking lot (no indoor seating here). 

However, it's disappointing that the exterior of the rather large building advertises "Hot Eats - Cold Treats" and you go in and find the menu is 98 percent ice cream.  I stopped here hoping to get a burger - I've had DQ burgers on the Ohio Turnpike and they're pretty good - only to find that this location only had hot dogs and one special item which was a brisket sandwich. To make matters worse, if you look their menu up online it looks like they have a lot of hot sandwiches.  Don't be misled.

A must stop in STL! We randomly stopped for appetizers and drinks and could not believe the atmosphere. Incredible ambiance and a great date night spot. You simply cannot beat the variety of craft beers and fine wines.

Our group recently had brunch at Louie's in Broad Ripple and it was fantastic! The "almost bottomless" mimosa deal is really great ($14 for a 1/2 carafe which holds 2-3 servings and $1 for each following glass) or you can always order the cocktails individually or a full carafe to share - also with generous servings! I like that they have the option of classic orange juice, grapefruit, or cranberry. No two of us ordered the same thing and the portions were perfect and the food delicious. I had the Mac Daddy omelette which included some of the best, creamy, tasty mac n' cheese *inside* of the perfectly cooked omelette. File under: things I didn't know I always wanted. I also couldn't resist a 1/2 order of the praline french toast. They were very accommodating of additions and substitution requests and service was extremely attentive. The prices were also VERY reasonable! I was glad we made a reservation as a party of 5, even they were not extremely busy on this particular Sunday. I still would recommend reserving a table if you have a larger party. Louie's gets my enthusiastic recommendation!

I had a wonderful first experience here! The sushi is very fresh and one thing I honestly loved about it were the size of the pieces. They weren't too big so I wasn't sitting there chewing on them for forever! LOL! Our server was very warm and welcoming. A friendly server makes all the difference in the world! Their menu is also very extensive, so they have plenty of options for you to find something to your taste. I will definitely return here.

Haven't been here in years and I could kick myself in the ass! The turf burger deserves every award it has ever received. It is so amazing...even in a wrap! The flavors work so well together...you will not be disappointed. Best burger in Philly hands down! Add a side of regular or sweet potato fries or get both like we did :). Both are paired with delicious dipping sauces. Cannot wait to go back and try other things on the menu. Oh and they have hell and high water on tap! Keep up the great work Mike!

Best healthy option in the area hands down! Great place for families ... the combination options are endless ... can never get tired of this place. I highly recommend getting the breakfast bowl w steak.
worst chipotle i have ever ordered from. they always get something wrong and leave out items. no salt or lime on the chips. their ratio of bowls are always off

Food is overpriced and very very mediocre- be careful they'll seat you in their back parking lot if you don't specifically request to be seated on the main patio for outdoor seating- the inside of the restaurant looks like it hasn't been updated since 1982 - dark dismal and disco - a landmark for New Hope but sadly disappointed with the low quality and ridiculously high pricing - spent over a $100 in total with tip for two entrees one appetizer and three beers - food is really very bland and mediocre- wish it were nicer but won't be going to Havana again.

I always have a huge craving for poco and moms on a Monday! And my heart breaks because they are closed on Monday's. 

Poco and moms is one of my favorite breakfast places. The chips and salsa is amazing, the coffee is delicious, and all their staff and food has been wonderful. 

I love when the weather is nice, setting on their patio area outside by the fountain. People can even have their dogs out there. I get the Huevos rancheros majority of the time, but I've had their burritos and French toast/pancakes and they were delicious too. I've gone multiple times. Today we had Bailey as our server and he was perfect. Sweet, attentive, without being to much. Love love love! Always will go back!
Order pizza for delivery.  Pizza was way under cooked.  Still doughie.  Pizza was also delivered 30 minutes late and was cold. Disappointed.

This place never disappoints- the food is delicious and burritos are packed full and tight. The coffee is also delicious along with their baked goods. Tacos and coffee who would have thought? Thankfully they did and perfected it!

I ate here years ago, before Yelp was a thing and this place was a jacket required kind of place.  While time has moved forward, this place has not.  I came here recently for another try some 10 years later and nothing has changed except they no longer require jackets.  I had a little confusion with my reservation but the front end host and hostess did a really good job of being accommodating which was nice.

The food wasn't as spectacular as I remember it to be, but that could be that Prime Rib was also one of my first fine dining experiences of my life so at the time I was relatively easily impressed.  We ordered the special of the night, the soft shell crab, and it came out an oily mess.  The actual prime rib was well made though so I'll give them that.  Dining experience wise, my friend had bought me cake for my birthday from outside the restaurant and they charged me a whopping thirty some dollars to put it on a plate and cut it into small pieces so that definitely left a sour taste to end the meal.  On top of that my waiter seemed totally disinterested with life, let alone the table and showed up once to recite specials and take orders, the seemingly one required visit to ensure we liked the food, and then finally to present the check.   

With an aging clientele (everyone but my table was over 55) and a wait staff that seemed to care less and still want to charge you top dollar, I don't think I'll be coming back unless there is a major overhaul.  You and I could be spending our hard earned money elsewhere in the city with a much more enjoyable experience for the same if not a fraction of the price.

Once again The Blue Owl out did themselves! The strawberry salad had my taste buds soaring. My Quiche Lorraine was exquisite, my mile high lemon merqrine pie was the best of the best!!! The service was right on!! She one of the best we have ever had!

Sincerely,

Linda Higgins

Just tried Pretty Girls Cook for the first time and I'm soo happy I did!!! I had the salmon and rice and all I'm in love with it.
I can't wait to try something else .
I'm just sorry that I couldn't remember the actual name of the dish. And the next time I get it, I'm going to try it with the shrimp.

I really dig Bertucci's and had a day of mourning when the one on Locust closed.  But, this one is right around the corner from my house so everything is okay.  The bread is always hot and awesome, the mussels are phenomenal, the antipasto is big, and I really enjoy the pizzas.  I have yet to have a bad experience...
I can never get out of there for cheap though, and that's what annoys me.  I mean...I had two glasses of wine and a pizza...why is this so expensive? I've never had an entree there so no clue how decent they are.  So, while I do tend to stick to BYOs and Forno when I'm looking for za and wine, every now and then on a late week day night, we'll pop over for dinner.  I avoid during peek hours as I do every chain for sanity's sake, and I have driven by and seen the hoards of people waiting outside of a table.

Stopped in for lunch.   What a beautiful space!!!

I got the Fish & Chips (to go) ...

The fish was delicious as it is hard to screw up cod but the batter was soggy and there could have been more fish especially for the price you pay.

NOTE:  The french fries were really good and abundant.

I am defiantly going to have to go back at some point to try some thing else as most places who do a beer batter for fish ends up soggy since beer is not really meant for deep frying which is why it does not get crunchy and flaky like how I make my fish ... don!!!

First of all I had their specialty burger (I forgot the name) all I know is it was huge and sloppy. I don't normally eat like this but this burger, I'd definitely eat again!! I'll limit myself to one every5 months though but it was amazing

Wow! I ordered Uber eats from this location and it was absolutely incredible. I made a couple special requests in the notes section of my order, and the restaurant called and made sure they got it exactly right. So impressed - I got the nachos and the chips were homemade and so freaking delicious!!! I travel for a living, and finding gems like this one make everything worth it. Thank you so much Mayana! Delicious hot salsa, too!!!


*****hooooly crap the guacamole is life changing. Love the garlic flavor. Home run!!!
This is a nice bar to hang out . It's more for single people. But it has nice balconies and is huge!!!. Not the best price in drinks but have diferent groups playing in each floor.

This is my go to healthy pre made meal location! I was looking for a healthy alternative to my frozen weight watcher meals and this place is perfect! I would drive all the way out to chesterfield to grab my meals for the work week, but now this location is available and it's even more convenient! It makes eating healthy, not as difficult. I have also found that small individual meals are easier for me, especially when I don't like left overs and am only typically cooking for myself, I end up wasting a lot of food. With the individual meal options, I don't end up wasting anything! I have tried almost every meal and there are only a few that I really didn't care for. There is a chefs creation weekly that adds a different variety to the meal choices. But, once you find a few that you like, they are so good, I don't mind eating them a few times a week! I usually get the small plate meals for breakfast and lunch and a larger plate for dinners. Most of the time the large ones I can split in to two meals and that ends up saving some money. For a healthy alternative, this place is awesome and the prices are no more then what I would spend at the grocery store and it saves me time because it's already made for me! If you are looking for low calorie and high protein meals, are interested in healthy eating and nutritional health, this place would be a perfect fit for you!

This Subway location is usually clean and the staff is always very friendly.  The food is mostly fresh although they often take knives that have been in the trough behind the cutting surface with the cuttings of vegetables and other leftovers and they wipe them with a rag and use them making me wonder what bacteria may be on the knives.  They should provide tea through closing time.  My wife and I have often arrived after 6pm and the tea is often gone - taken down for the night (this is pretty early).

Atmosphere is wonderful, but don't go for the food, at least not for anything blackened - cook does not know the difference between blackened fish and poached fish.  Bleh, sent it back and he sent it right back out as it was.  Seriously??? We usually take company here when they come to visit - looking for a new place!

Too bad I can't  give a negative star.(s).  Food was nothing to write about and service was horrible was horrible.  Dark corner of the  bar area tables.  Don't see myself going back.  To top everything off was listening to the wait staff talk bad about the customers.
The food was excellent but the service could of been better . I didn't really get a refill till the end of my dinning but overall the food was delicious

Ordered the carne asada fries and two mini tacos, tell me why ONE mini taco had 2x the amount of meat in it than the carne asada fries??? Paid 9 something for the fries and $2 for the mini taco, such a rip off.

Despite the negative reviews out there, I still wanted to check it out...I made a mistake.  Food portions were unbelievably skimpy.  We ordered the recommended 2-3 plates per person, and found ourselves on the way to the Iron Hill for something to eat AFTER our dinner!  I could go on and on about the food... but I don't want to sound like a negative Nancy.  I have had the pleasure of some wonderful dining experiences in the city... Osteria, Barbuzzo, Vetri, Distritos, Amada, Vernick, etc... Stateside cannot compare to any of these places.  Food was average, service was average, plate size was down right poor, and should not be acceptable.  On a side note, they get two stars b/c the speciality cocktails were creative, refreshing, and down-right good.  Might be worth a drink at the bar, while you enjoy the view of the hustle of the neighborhood.  But, save yourself some cash, and general annoyance of wasting money.. trust me, don't eat here.
East nasty was tasty! A bit of a line but well worth the wait!! Service was great and the ambiance was very photogenic

Good tasty flavorful but overpriced, brisket good but 1/3 of it was fat. Nice atmosphere., if you check in Yelp promo for free fried pickles delicious. Tried the salmon special it was ok but the sautéed bed of kale carrots and Brussels sprouts were great.
Ordered the beer cheese steak sandwich.  Very bland and underwhelming. Sirloin had  no seasoning.  Grilled peppers were nice, but again, not seasoned

So we saw the write up in Indianapolis Monthly. We had a horrible experience here 15 years ago. So we figure that we give it a try again. Maybe it was just a bad night. Boy was I wrong. This place is horrible. How can they even be compared to high end steak houses? Maybe a step up from Ponderosa. The salad is about as plain as I have ever seen. The meat is tough. The prices are in line with a high end steak house. But what you get is backyard grilled steak that the neighbor had in their freezer for a year. The attitude of the hacking, smoke smelling waitress is horrible as well...Hello we are the customer...That is why you got no tip at all. Hint...try not spending so much time texting on your phone. I will gladly drive downtown and pass and flip this place off on the way.

Oh, baby.  The Parish isn't as sexy as I imagined it to be.  I get that the Parish is going for a New Orleans style, but lime green walls stick out in a weird way.  And for being a gastropub, their menu emphasizes a lot of terrible domestic beers :(

Although they were bone dry on a handful of beers that sounded good, Mr. Food for Todd and I did manage to find some tasty beers, including a delicious dark amber.  Todd also ordered The Doctor, which was really strong!  

As for food, we ordered the bacon popcorn, the steak salad, and a parish burger.  The bacon popcorn was a little heavy on the bacon grease (hahaha), but the steak and tomatoes on the salad were seasoned well and the fries were definitely memorable.

Can't wait to go back and try more beers!  Mr. Food for Todd and I went alone, but they have seating in the back for groups, too!

This place was amazing! Great vibe, GREAT FOOD, friendly! 

Absolutely LOVED the seafood Benedict brunch. Fried soft shell crab, fried oysters, and fried shrimp with poached eggs and hollandaise sauce - to DIE for.

My husband, son (15) and I recently visited Chronic Taco for the first time.  We were all excited because we all love Mexican food and expected at least  something out of the ordinary.  I had a large chicken burrito and it was big, but wrapped so that you could only eat 1 ingredient at a time.  The chicken was so salty, I couldn't even finish it.  My teenage son (who eats any and everything) took a few bites and ended up throwing it out because of the salt.  My husband had some fish tacos and some soft tacos which looked incredibly greasy.  What bothered me more than the food was the dirtiness of the place.  Food everywhere, dirty rags being used to clean off food trays and the floor was filthy both behind the counter and in the eating area.  There were also 2 employees supposedly standing outside smoking that the guy working inside was complaining about.  Very unprofessional.  I don't think we'll be back.
This place is as good as they come. Simply a 10.........
Probably the best brisket I have had.  I would have liked a little more smoke flavor.  BBQ sauce is fantastic.  Decent service.  Fried green tomatoe sandwich was good too.

Morning Glory you used to be lovely, but now you're a rude, frustrating, disappointment.

A friend and I have been going to Morning glory once or twice a month during the week for breakfast for the past 8 months or so. We always get there at 7:30 and order basically the same thing, so the usual morning waitress recognizes us and knows our order. That was great and breakfast was delicious for months.

However, this morning we showed up at 7:30 and the gate was still locked. They open at 7. 

There was a couple and a child sitting at the counter eating who looked and acted like they were be the owners. (The woman, I believe, was Shannon who owns Chapterhouse.) We waved. They ignored us. We walked around to the other side of the building to see if there was a notice posted about late opening or anything, but there wasn't. We walked back and the woman held up her hand to indicate 5 minutes. She didn't come out to talk to us or apologize.

We sat on a bench to wait, annoyed. And then it started raining. No joke. We left at 7:40, they were still sitting at the counter eating, ignoring their customers waiting in the rain.

When I was searching for the owner of Morning Glory online I found that Sam passed away recently, which I was very sorry to hear. And this must mean that Morning Glory is under new ownership and/or new management. 

If this new management intends to open at least 40 minutes late without notice and leaves paying customers outside while they eat at the counter, then I don't intend to ever return - to Morning Glory (or Chapterhouse). I'm all for the staff eating, but at least let the customers come in out of the rain for coffee. Her behavior showed rude and inconsiderate business ownership, and I would rather support a local business that values and welcomes its customers.

Made a special trip to Daddy's Dogs as we headed home from Nashville.
I had the Carolina.  I've never been a big.fan of hot dogs but this one was soo very good!!
I loved the coleslaw and the sauce,  soo good!!!!  We also ordered tots and got way plenty to share!
The atmosphere was relaxed and everyone was friendly.  Keep it coming!!!  Loved our lunch!!

Fresh hot chips with house-made salsa, guacamole made table-side and a delicious tomatillo salsa started our meal. Then I ordered the best fish taco I have ever eaten. Tilapia (of which I am normally not a fan of this relatively flavorless fish) seasoned with sea salt, granulated onion, pepper and paparika (might be missing an ingredient or two) on  a house-made corn tortillas was the bomb. The margaritas, however, were ok. They said it was made with fresh-squeezed juices. However, they had the very sweet taste of being made with a mix. 

Nevertheless, if you're in NOLA and understandably pigging out on the delicious Cajun or Creole food, El Gato Negro is a very nice break. I highly recommend this place.

Came here a couple times on some bar crawls in Philly and I'm a fan. It's like any Irish Bar in Philly, decent bar food, late night drunk dancing and always a good place to go with friends. The bathrooms are fairly clean and the music is usually good, a mix of top 40s and oldies. Sometimes they have a band playing as well I believe

While the food and drinks at Roy's were delicious, the service was spectacular.  We went for my friend's bachlorette party, and the restaurant went above and beyond to accomedate us.  In each of our menus they put an insert welcoming us and congratulating the bride to be.  It was a simple gesture but definitely left a lasting impression.

As far as food goes, I had the Szechuan Pork Spare Ribs.  They were fall off the bone tender, which is necessary when you're trying to eat them with a fork and knife! 

The Hummingbird was such a light and fresh drink, perfect for the hot FIorida summer.  I recently discovered St. Germaine's and cannot get enough.  It's St. Germaine's, sparkling wine and club soda... I definitely plan on trying to recreate this drink at home.

The restaurant can be a bit pricey, but it is certainly worth it.  Would definitely recommend Roy's, especially for a special event!

Wife and I are on vacation. We love to eat at unique places. We found just the place, YATS!  Squirrlie was great. He walked us through the options and gave us a sample tasting. 

What a feast!  The food was awesome.  I could eat a whole loaf of their bread! Then we finished it all off with some peanut butter pie. 

Go!  You will not be disappointed.
Friendly, nice spot, quick service & a pretty great & super filling burrito. I had the steak

One word - underrated. Sure, the spotlight outside might be trying to attract attention, but for me, it was a calling. Overall, this is a chic and casual japanese restaurant with comfortable seating, upbeat and sick music, an impressive menu, and late hours (open till midnight, 1 AM on weekends). 

Let's start with the drinks. There are various "bubblefish specials", from which I tried the lavender oolong milk tea. It was delicious, substantial, and the boba was soft and chewy. They also use lactaid milk for their drinks (shout out to all the lactose-intolerant peeps). There are at least 3 pages of drink options to choose from, ranging from oolong teas, black teas, green teas, hot teas, juices, milk shakes, and smoothies. While it was just my first outing, looking at the other drinks from surrounding tables, I was tempted to order more...

For food, I tried the tonkotsu don, taiwanese beef noodle soup, and a couple of specialty sushi rolls. The tonkotsu don is a helluva dish - you get a big pork cutlet katsu (perfectly crunchy on the outside with juicy meat) upon a bed of white rice sitting in a castiron. Great value meal at $12 and filling. The beef noodle soup was rich and had great flavor. However, they use thin beef slices (which were kind of tough) instead of the traditional beef chunk cubes. The signature sushi rolls have plenty of flavor, mainly because they often come with tempura, some avocado or fruit, and a miso or spicy mayo sauce. 

Of note, they also have "Bubblefish boxes" (around $13-14), which come with a protein teriyaki of your choice, with california roll, shrimp and vegetable tempura, vegetables, and rice. I saw a few tables that ordered these boxes, and they looked massive!

I would definitely check this place out, there is bound to be something on the menu to make a great meal for anyone!
Tasty little tacos with clever names, unfortunately they're overrated and overpriced.

Looks a little shady but is actually a fun little place. Lots of good beer. Lots of good food. I had the pulled pork chimi and it was awesome! Corn hole in the back. Live music in the front. Within walking distance of a lot of places if you want to do a pub crawl. Nice place to hang outside in the summers. I keep hearing about the corndogs so I'll try that next time.

Great food and drinks but hospitality sucks. Tonight we had a dinner party in there private room. Three weeks ago I paid to reserve a room which was suppose to be returned tonight. But they claim that is not true...you rent the room and money is not returned. When myself and some other family walked in...they made us wait until the rest of our party came...yet I am renting this room. I repeatedly ask why can't i go back there if i paid to reserve it until i had to beg. It was a surprise for my parents on there 40th wedding anniversary so we wanted to surprise them in the room. They claim they were getting the room ready. If i reserved the room for 6pm then why are you just now getting it ready? After the surprise we took pictures then sat down. I noticed after, about 35 minutes, that they just turned the hot tables on. It's two sides so we had two chefs. One came out but apparently the other hot tables were taking to long to heat up. Again repeatedly, i had to ask what was going on. One side was almost done eating before the other even got their rice. They offered free ice cream but that never came for my parents. We voiced our complaints but they didn't care not one bit. Hospitality and care for their customers are non-existent. The floors where very slippery and the windows seals were disgusting. They claim the room fits 25...that's a lie because we had 19 people and that was a tight fit. Will never go here again or recommend it.
It's located in a strip mall, but the interior's nice. The beers are delicious, though. We just went for appetizers and a pint, and I was pretty impressed with the place. Very good service, also.
Great sports bar with awesome food.  Staff was very pleasant.  I hope to stop again when down that way.

The storefront bragged "Wings and Raw Bar". 

We drove past it all the time. Finally, we were compelled to give it a try. 

We parked and noted on the window "Happy Hour all Day Monday". Sweet! 

The place was empty at 6 pm except a few ppl at the bar. 

The seats were torn up or looked like someone with a staple gun and zero clue about reupholstering had attempted to fix them. 

The waitress came over and I asked what was on the happy hour menu. She didn't know, and she said she needed to check to see if Happy Hour was going on. I pointed to the window. She said, "oh sorry it's my 3rd day here". Ok. I can accept that...

She came back and said all they had was beer. And 2 wines, but she couldn't name the wines. She said, "we are applying for our liquor license". 

When it came time to order, she said today was $0.80 oysters and $0.50 wings. So, we ordered a dozen oysters and 16 wings. We also ordered steamed clams. 

She came back later and said, "we are all out of clams. Also, I was wrong, the oysters and the wings are $0.80- is that ok?" Uhm sure. I guess. I wouldn't say it was an intentional bait and switch or anything.  

The food comes out and the oysters are steamed. ??? I thought it was a wings and RAW bar?? So, we say, "wait, we wanted raw oysters" and she responds "oh well, they were raw before they were steamed. We have cold ones in the back."

What the...? I'm sorry, even if you are new, what kind of response is that? 

A good while later, the manager comes over with 6 raw oysters and says they are on the house because of the waitresses mistake. While I appreciate the attempted gesture, we didn't want steamed oysters...so shouldn't we have gotten a dozen of them?

The salad was not fresh, the mussels were only steamed with a little butter and when I asked for more to dip, by the time it came out, the mussels were gone. The chips with the cheesesteak sandwich tasted like the oil they were fried in. The wings were mediocre at best. 

They charged for ranch dressing, which normally comes with wings, there were no celery or carrots. 

And the bill, with no alcohol, came out to $60! 

They really should not tout themselves as a wings and raw bar. I won't be back. Go to Surf Shack next door instead.

Yummy! After years of sticking to the lunch buffet at any Indian restaurant, we finally tried dinner off the regular menu (a challenge), and this place DELIVERED (literally). Great food! Don't be afraid of Indian cuisine! Shrimp curry: delish! Lamb saag: wow wee! Saag aloo: yes please!! Naan, naan, oh naan! Thanks curry house for bringing it to Smyrna and to my front door!!!
