Charred pie is amazing!! I love the atmosphere the drinks the pizza was so good! We sat outside and the view from our table was so pretty. Thank you Charred pie for the amazing dinner and service! Will be coming back soo

Noord was such a pleasant surprise on a date night during the winter! Going in, I had no idea what to expect from a Dutch restaurant. Turns out, it's just lots of seafood, plus a bunch of flavor-packed supporting ingredients like mustards, vinaigrettes and pickled vegetables. 

The bread they start you out with is truly magnificent. I'm not even a huge rye bread person but I was addicted from first bite. We shared the bitterballen, the Dutch version of meatballs, and a salad with bleu cheese to start. Excellent choices which didn't leave us too full for mains (if anything it's multiple servings of that bread that will get you!). The shellfish stew was excellent and I know my husband was happy with his entree as well, though I can't remember at this point what it was. 

The vibes at Noord were very European, with tables fairly close together and a nice din throughout the restaurant that seemed to suggest a fun night out was being had by all. Our server was as gregarious as he was efficient, adding to the atmosphere. Can't wait to do it again!

I want this place to do well - as its close to our house and a welcome addition to the ho-hum restaurants on 96. 

We've been there several times since they opened and have tried the pizzas and burgers and a few apps. The pizzas are pretty good. The burgers are usually overcooked and somewhat boring. I would encourage the owners to add more variety to the menu and perhaps to the appetizers (think:bar food. Maybe some nachos? Buffalo chicken dip? 

The beer selection is good (I appreciate the truck stop honey brown!). With a little tweaking this would be one of our favorite local haunts - just none of their current menu items are enough to bring us back in week after week.

Pizza is still good but new staff at store overcharged me and neither the cashier nor the manager knew how to correct the issue so basically they just to told me since the register said that was the amount then that was what Id be charged.  Anyway, simple math proved I was correct yet I was charged anyway.  And I saw another customer get charged incorrectly and the manager actually told him that the manager didnt know how to provide a refund so he did nothing about it.  And the toppings on the pizza were sparse and not evenly distributed. It appears this location is having some staffing issues. Very frustrating. The manager should call the owner and figure out immediately how to use the register so people aren't overcharged.
Possibly the best Sichuan restaurant in Philadelphia, is named after a mountain in Sichuan province. Quality ingredients done authentically, this is the place to go for aficionados.

Have been here before, and had a lovely time. However, today was not the same. Upon walking in, we were not greeted, had to walk up to bar tender and ask. He so rudely responded, and we went to a table. He then came to take drink order, and forgot one of the three drinks. Another member of the party ordered a beer which was never received. We then informed him we were going to order food, which he then took our menus from the table and walked away. He never came back, we then had to walk up to him and ask for our check, which I had to remind him we never got the beer so it needs to be taken off check. He delivered check to table, we waited another 5-10 mins and had to walk back up to bar and ask to pay for our bill. Very upsetting as we love this place!
Best Thai place on the beach. Relaxing atmosphere and great location.  Enjoyed the noodles and the fried ice cream!

This is one of our places on our work lunch rotation.  So much better now that the smoke is gone.  The staff is very friendly and attentive which is nice!  The food is good and varied.  I can get a salad when I want and the other guys can get good old fashioned pub food.  They have a nice frequent eater card too!

Best Mexican food in New Orleans. Authentic vibe that has a great energy as soon as you walk in. The selections are wide, unique and all delicious. In combination with the powerful marg it's a perfect meal.
always good food, beer, and service. Gena is awesome!
It's always so amazing eating here! The food and drinks are the BEST! My hurricane was sooo strong. Service is really good too. We had no wait and everyone was social distancing.

Rusty nail is my favorite neighborhood dive bar. It's very affordable, they have a large selection of liquor so they can whip up just about any drink. The staff is always super friendly, makes you feel at home. They started doing a pizza pop up on Mondays called Only Pans (love the name ) the pizza is awesome! Perfect crust! On Tuesdays they do trivia on the patio and Daddy Hot Bird sells hot chicken from his truck outside! The hot chicken is addicting, it has become my new Tuesday ritual. They take social distancing seriously which is such a relief to me, I love that I can still feel safe while going out in public.  I can't say enough good things about this place!

I am confused why this place is not in the top 10. The food is fresh ,healthy and TASTY HEALTHY. Prices are moderate for the ingredients used. Look, i am very picky .This place makes eating healthy DELICIOUS ! A MUST CHECK OUT!!!!!

I'm giving Red House five stars because when it's good it's very, very good and when it isn't very good it's fine.

They have a dish, "Hunan-Style Lamb" which seems very authentic and is very delicious. I've successfully gotten the same dish made with bean curd instead as well. Their hot-and-sour soup is also above average.

Unfortunately, dishes which usually are very reliable are very strange here. I wouldn't recommend any of the mixed vegetable dishes; occasionally it seems whoever is making them adds butter or something like it. As a result it comes out with a strange flavor that does not blend well with the other ingredients.

Some of their more fusion dishes are also less predictable. Their sushi, however, is also pretty decent for a delivery place, especially the vegetarian options (Sweet Potato, Cucumber/Avocado, etc).

Again, the reason I'm giving them the 5 stars is for their incredible Hunan Lamb dish (and bean curd variant) which are a must-try if you like spicy food. I would recommend ordering on Thursdays; for some reason that is when their food is the best.

I've had some good food at Xi'an Sizzling Woks and I'd be curious to come back to try more dishes.  

- The Biang Biang noodle with ginger and scallion was very nice.  Just a perfect simple bowl of noodles.  Definitely recommended. 4 stars

- Pickled pepper wood ear was okay, nothing special. 3 stars

- The pita bread soaked in lamb & beef soup is tasty.  My only issue is there wasn't quite enough soup to balance out all the bread in there. 3.5 stars

- Chinese hamburger was so-so. I probably wouldn't bother with this one again since there are better options to be had here. 

Somewhere between 3 and 4 stars.

Best place to catch live music in north Tampa. Eclectic crowd, fun to people watch, grab a bite and a cocktail or two. We loved March forth last night and made plans to be back for Reggae night which is always a blast. Too bad the crawfish is off the menu, my husbands favorite. Skippers sampler was an excellent replacement option. Bring a group or meet friends, very affordable fun evening for all ages.

We came here for brunch. They have a great menu with lots of diverse flavor profiles to choose from. I got the beef cheeks with grits. It was so tender and flavorful- a perfect dish. I also got a fresh squeezed orange juice. The fries we're pretty good, but the fried mashed potatoes balls were the best. Great fashionable ambiance and waitress.
Just tried it and it was good. Plenty of meat on the sandwich and drive through was reasonably quick for non-fast good restaurant.

I know the French Quarter location feels like the one you "have to go to" when you're in New Orleans but it's honestly the worst Cafe Du Monde for so many reasons. 

It's ALWAYS sticky, the area smells awful, it's cash only, it lacks the "mocha" flavor coffee that the other locations boast, the lines can sometimes be up to an hour wait, and it's generally just an overrated tourist trap. 

I'm giving it as many stars as it has because the coffee and beignets are delicious and simple. They can make all the other awful stuff work BECAUSE the staple offerings are just so dang good. Curse their amazing formula. 

Go to the other locations and get the same thing with way less hassle. If you insist on coming to the Quarter, please REMEMBER CASH and just go to the pick up window on the other side of the street so you don't have to sit in the sticky goop.

I was excited to see a new Indian Restaurant open in the city. I have my go-to spot, but I was curious to see what 722 had to offer. The prices here are not out of the ordinary. Spice levels can be varied if you let them know. They make it easy to order online on their website. 

Overall, their food was good. The chicken vindaloo was spicy and probably my favorite. The chicken tikka masala (which is always what I order to really tell if an Indian place knows what it's doing...) was great too.

Great atmosphere...a good place to just sit and work on your computer you don't fee like you have to move. I also like their food--delicious! I look forward to going here on Saturday mornings and just hanging out! I love it!

Typical Chinese buffet with the not so typical value of really good food. 
They have a normal spread and service is so so but the food makes it worth it.
I went to Dan Dan while in town for work and have been craving the Dan Dan noodles since! If you love peanut butter the noodles are a must! Amazing food and service was great!

This is one of the NICER locations, right in heart of Rittenhouse Square, very posh, huge inside, nice cafe , etc.has couple floors with security, Who knew? Guess you cant be too safe. Nice for college students to sit , read, study , get on their laptops, quite nice. Wish this was available when I was in high school, or college. I just had public library -so sad!! 
The personnel are helpful, huge assortment of books. Depending on genre you like, they have end displays with helpful suggestions or Book of month-great tips!! When I am in area, I like to stop at this one. Lots lots to see & read!!

OUTSTANDING. Came here a year ago, sat at the oyster bar & had a total blast.  The food was amazing..the oysters as big as my hand & fresh AF. Back a year later... the two master oyster shuckers - Cyrus & Carl - actually remembered me from the year before &, once again, treated me like royalty. The oysters were fresh (& still enormous), the drinks on point, & the service & atmosphere second to none. I even got some lessons on shucking this time. Stop in & sit at the oyster bar for some hella good fun & some amazing food.  Do it!!!  *Pro tip: use the Tabasco Chipotle sauce (liberally) on everything, try an oyster shooter, & ask for some crab on your chargrilled oysters. 
You're welcome.

My husband and I had come here for dinner and everything was quite good: food, service and ambience of the restaurant. Today just after noon, it was nearly opposite. My soup was good, but the chefs salad, although tasty, was made of strips of deli sliced ham, turkey and cheese, reminiscent of Denny's fare. Still, not bad. However my friend had a seafood roll which had a thin layer of bits of crab, lobster and shrimp (though it was difficult to recognize the meats) on a giant sub sandwich type roll. The meal was mostly bread with French fries on the side. This was so disappointing for a seafood restaurant. However the worst part of our experience was lack of service. The waitress asked us if we wanted bread, but only was is served after asking her twice and another server once. Never was ketchup offered for fries. She was quite unfocused, and we generally got the impression that she didn't care. Interestingly, the man at the next table over spilled a drink and quickly 3 other servers rushed to his rescue! But it took him waving his hand in the air for about 5 minutes to have someone help him with the payment of his check. It wasn't like they were busy either; servers just stood around talking to each other. So basically, I don't recommend this restaurant simply because their food quality and service is highly inconsistent.

This place is basically fast-food for sushi.  It is made right in front of you and ready quickly which is great.  The quality is just ok though.  Nothing I ordered stood out.  I didn't care for the garden salad because of the dressing and should be skipped.  Self serve soy sauce, ginger, and wasabi was pretty nice.
We love it, it's amazing, service is a little overwhelmed for brunch, but get a bloody mary, you won't regret it!

No thank you! Absolutley a horrible place for Italian cuisine, just plain nasty and horrible customer service. Since when does the bartender dig his nose and stick it on the counter nasty nasty nasty!!!!!!!

Excellent service. No wait for lunch on a Wednesday. We absolutely loved the Steak Frites, cooked and seasoned perfectly the Cabernet butter was amazing and the pomme fries are spectacular. We also enjoyed the spicy buttermilk chicken sandwich. Great experience. Highly recommend.

I have no idea how people are giving this place 5 stars. I go to take a bite of the chicken tender sandwich and it was absolutely terrible. It was way over cooked and it was cold. And of course that made the chicken dry and rubbery. The fries were cold too. Not sure how this place stays open. Don't waste your money here.

Might I suggest any other restaurant on main street. Until Bernie's opened you couldn't go wrong. The best thing about this restaurant is the building. Absolutely gorgeous, I could see sitting here for hours enjoying some drinks and delicious food. Unfortunately, while you will sit there for hours, the food and drinks may take that long to arrive. When the food does arrive you will certainly be disappointed in the flavor. I had a burger which might have been good if it arrived warm.

After searching and searching for a good sushi place in New Orleans, I'm happy to say the search is over! Origami is reasonably priced and generous in proportions. The sushi is always fresh and they have such a wide variety of flavors that I've never experienced at other Japanese restaurants. Among a long list of other things, my boyfriend and I always get the Poke Salad and the Mussels (Sake or Curry? It is always a debate because they're both great!) We recently tried their special, Oyster Shooters, and they were a huge hit at the table. They don't come with cocktail sauce but don't worry, there is plenty of kick! We sent a compliment to the kitchen and the chef came out personally and told us the ingredients, which included a wasabi oil. MMM definitely been dreaming about those :) Looking forward to our next visit soon!
I love their burgers and their custard! Never have had a bad experience. Also I love their coupons they send out! Highly recommended...

First time at Rockford and it was delicious!!! I got the pesto chicken with fries and tried the garlic aioli sauce. Ingredients were fresh and really great quality. The food was great! Can't wait to try more. Friendly staff and great customer service! Will definitely visit again

It all started with great service, and it never stopped!  What a great concept for a bar!  You can bring your own food to grill, enjoy a BBQ outside with and ice cold drink from the full bar (prices seam high, but it's worth it considering they supply the grills, plates, silverware, and I heard rubs for your meat but I can't verify that part).  Very fun experience and I can't wait to go back and show the place off when I have out of town company.  Living in a townhouse doesn't leave space for a grill....problem solved.  Inside is a nice bar and pool tables, and very cool decor,, great vibe.

It was acceptable but didn't knock my socks off. The sashimi was really good, but the rolls left something to be desired. My caveat is that I don't like fried anything in a sushi place, so the fact that most of their rolls had either cream cheese or fried something in them was off-putting. I also had to scrape the mayo off the top of the roll. I never saw mayo once in Japan, and especially not at a sushi place, so i don't really understand why American sushi places have such love for it. Yuck.

Prices are fantastic. Service is decent. Food is good. I've had a few instances of myself or someone else finding something disturbing in their food (e.g. french fry in the drink, piece of rubber glove in the burger).

This restaurant is an overcrowded
Dirty version of an old fashioned
Bennigans or applebees.
You are forced to sit at tables
With people you don't know.
Service and food quality
Were below par.
Will not return

CHEESE-OLOGY!

Although the owners have been Stringing us along regarding the grand opening for a while, this brand new restaurant on the Delmar Loop really Bleu my mind.  As we walked out of the summer Bries and Headed into the restaurant, we knew we were in for a great time.

The line was a little bit long, but we understood it was the grand opening and didn't get Feta up.  We dropped our Cheddar and ordered our meals and began to Edam --  I ate my food so fast I felt like a Muenster!  As soon as I saw there was an item on the menu called "Bacon Bacon," my eyes glazed over and I ignored the rest of the menu, because that's what I wanted to eat.  It was traditional mac and cheese, more or less, with a hearty sprinkling of bacon on top.  Needless to say, it was very very Gouda.

Other members of the party ordered "The Hill," which featured salciccia (sausage) and marinara sauce.  It had a sharp and tasty sausage taste that permeated the entire dish -- delicious!

The one thing that got my Goat were the prices, which seemed a little high.  A small helping, which is practically a side order, runs about $6.00 or $7.00.  Large orders, which are almost three times as much food, can't be found for under $10.00.  The food didn't really come out at one time, but we all ordered separately and that's about as good as you can get for a fast casual (i.e., no table service) restaurant like this; it's Nacho fault, Cheese-ology.

A lactose-intolerant friend who was along for the ride was pleased to be offered a Lactaid pill before digging into her noodles.  That's unusually generous of the management, thumbs up for that!

Definitely stop by Cheese-ology as soon as you can.  This restaurant is the Cream of the crop and surely an excellent addition to the Delmar Loop.  Not checking it out would be simply... un-American.

Just left this place. Unsure where to start. It took around 15 minutes for anyone to ask us if we wanted to have any drinks. We were also sat in the bar area and were not given happy hour menus. When we finally got someone to acknowledge us he had to go back to get us the HH menu and barcode scanner for drinks on tap which took him two separate trips to do so and he left after we could give him our order. Servers in general looked lost and confused with orders. 

When my fiancée finally got his drink the server had forgotten to put in my order so I had to wait even longer. Not once did anyone check in on us and I didn't appreciate getting slapped with the bill and having to pay as this gentleman impatiently stood holding the device. 

Let me be clear that the place wasn't packed; no wait at all and our server not once introduced himself or was courteous to us as we patiently sat around waiting. 

Food was pretty good. Carnitas nachos were great. Chicken sandwich was good as well but based off of this experience and what I paid, I will not be going back.

We went for dine in outside on the patio and had steak and Mac and cheese. Both entrees were delicious and the waiter was really nice. The tables were spaced apart about 6 feet and we felt comfortable eating there

Very good.  Got the rare steak Pho and the broth was very tasty and the steak was tender.  The noodles were also solid.  I will def go back to this restaurant.  Jannice the manager was very nice and welcoming! Try it out man, try it out!

Cute little place in Germantown . I've been here several times & nothing has WOWED me ... It good but never like oh , I want to come back her tomorrow ! Nope.. Not at all . I have a couple of cocktail favorites ; like the curry salmon but haven't found the wow entree . 

I've been here for brunch .. Lunch & dinner . On my last visit I stopped by for a quick lunch . It was busy at all so we were able to sit by the window ( to people watch ) . The service was great & prompt . I ordered the speciality raspberry lemonade & the salmon club . I passed on the complimentary bread since I was eating a sandwich . My meal came out quickly .. The taste was very bland  but hearty . The salmon wasn't seasoned at all ... Let down . It doesn't take much to give salmon a kick *palms face* I wasn't impressed with my meal but I'll just check that off my list .. Still on my quest ..
Excellent food, great service, so-so location (I've actually had to wade outside with my pant legs rolled up and my shoes under my arm because a heavy rain flooded the entire restaurant.)

Came here for the first time with my husband on a Sunday night. Neither of us had ever been to a Texas Roadhouse before so we figured it'd be something new to try. We went online and added ourselves to the waitlist as we were leaving our house. The website said our table would be ready at 6:20 PM and we got there right on time. Once we checked in, we were told it would be another fifteen minutes. We ended up finally getting seated twenty five minutes after we arrived. To drink, I ordered the Armadillo Punch, it was tasty but had very little alcohol in it. To start, we had their famous buttery rolls, which, yes they were very good. I will give them that. We both got steak entrees that came with two sides. We both chose Caesar Salads to start with as one of our sides. The salads were good, no complaints there. Our steaks were not great. Mine was cooked correctly, but was the filet I have ever had. My husband had a sirloin steak he ordered medium rare and it was WAY overdone, no pink at all. I know this is a lower end steakhouse, but I still expect better than that. I have enjoyed Longhorn which is at about the same price point. But, here it just felt like a waste of money. Our waitress was nice but service was on the slow side. Overall, I don't see the hype with this place and wouldn't come here again.

A bit of a one-trick pony.  There is one, highly inspired dish - if you must come, do not leave without trying the salt roasted gold beets with avocado, smoked tofu, rye, capers (which the waitress mentioned is influenced by lox and cream cheese).  It is really, really good - a combo that unexpectedly works.  

Everything else feels like an exercise in plating raw ingredients for a Gastronomica photo shoot.  The fancy radish dish was $9 for literally 2-3 sliced raw radishes served on a fancy black plate with some soy sauce.  The portabella carpaccio was $9 for maybe 1/4 of a portabella mushroom cap sliced thin.  The roasted maitake mushroom and the cioppino were better - at least there was more work involved than just cutting - but still were tiny and not justified for the price (would it be so hard to give us two 1/2 pieces of toast with the cioppino?).  At one point, I felt like going to the grocery store and bringing back something of a reasonable portion size for them to cook for me (like, say, one whole portabella mushroom cap)!!  I understand getting full may not be the primary point of this place, but honestly, if I want art, I'll go to an art gallery, and if I want to satisfy my hunger, I tend to go to a restaurant.  Sigh... maybe I'm not trendy enough to "get" this restaurant. 

As for dessert, strawberry sorrel bread pudding with saffron ice cream was interesting.  It was novel, for sure, but it felt like it was trying to be different purely for the sake of being different.  It was definitely not comfort food and definitely not something either of us would want to try again. 

Even though we ordered six dishes for two people (which, plus one beer, was about $85 after tax and tip), we were still hungry but feared ordering more due to the mediocrity of every dish after the beets.  If two people want to actually leave satiated, I think they would need to order one of each plate off the regular menu.  Yes, that means 13 plates of food.  (And for context, we are thin people with normal appetites - not world champion eaters or gluttons.)  So sad... I had high hopes for this place when I looked at the menu and really wanted to like it, but it just didn't live up to the hype.

I love, love, love Rustica. They've always been my go to place in NoLibs for a great slice. Unlike some other reviewers, I don't think their crust is awful; it's standard Neapolitan style with a nice crisp. (In fact, I sometimes buy dough from Rustica when I make pizza at home.) I love their unusual toppings, like the Reuben (corned beef and sauerkraut, drizzled with Russian dressing and topped with a pickle spear), the Mighty Brussel (white pie with brussel sprouts and caramelized onions), and the Bistecca del Tartufo (steak and white truffle cream), but the simple pepperoni is my favorite (so perfect, so picturesque that Philly mag used it as the cover model for its "Best Pizza" issue).

Please no one come here. I might not have a place to sit. What great pizza and wings. Lauren who was training a very nice young lady. As a bartender with all the specialty drinks and such. Was very cool and professional. She explained the origin of this Florida chain. And all the ways the owner takes. To make sure we all enjoy our experience at all of his 157 restaurants. Will definitely come back again soon. My mom loved it also

It's always exciting when a new pokè bowl spot opens in the neighborhood. I'm addicted fo it! I love sushi, but poké bowls are way more convenient. And fun. On my recent visit to Poké Fish, I ordered a large bowl and it was massive. Shrimp were nice and plump, salmon and tuna was fresh and flavorful. Love how you have a choice of unlimited toppings. And I love the variety of toppings too. The staff is always super helpful and knowledgeable of the menu. They're always eager to help guide you through building your bowl. With the amount of options, it can be a little intimidating to a newcomer. All in all, Poké Fish is a big hit for me and will likely be stopping in once a week on my lunch break to get my poké fix!

It was ok.... the only thing I liked was the hush puppies they tasted so fresh so good n so light n fluffy.... the chicken tasted burnt like the oil hasn't been changed in months... mash potatoes was boxed not fresh and tasted like it was made yesterday.... idk what the Mac n cheese taste like because I was charged but never received it.... green beans were ok.. at least they didn't taste like they came out of a can but hold the green peppers... I've never had green peppers in my green beans.... n the biscuit omg it was so hard I could brake a window.... first n last time here... next time I'll try the Mexicans next door.... sorry not sorry....

Love all Wawas as a South Jerseyan, but this is my home-base store that I pass on my way to work, so it has a special place in my heart.

Workers in the store and at the gas pumps are cheerful, friendly, and helpful. There is a big morning rush around the time I head into work (7:30-7:45), but they have all hands on deck to try to accommodate all of the un-caffeinated commuters.

Store is always clean, and there's plenty of parking. For me, this is always a go-to stop when I begin a road trip.

It's a chain and its big and the decor is what it is. They have a big selection which I like and the prices, which waver between seeming reasonable and not cheap, give me hope that the quality will be there. It is good but it just isn't the kind of place to which I'll keep going back. 4Rivers lacks the comforting authenticity of a real BBQ joint and yet somehow doesn't entirely satisfy my infrequent desire for the anonymous chain restaurant dining experience either. It was fine and you should definitely try it and see for yourself. They have a separate "Sweet Shop" venue with cupcakes and there was just something about the eating unhealthy food and then tempt 'em with cheap processed sugar products that grossed me out.

Awesome! Got a two pound burger and tried to eat it all with my son. We couldn't finish it. Great experience. Came with a LARGE soda like close to 40oz, didn't finish it, HUGE side of tots or fries both taste excellent. Best Fry sauce I tried so far in Boise. Nothing bad to say about this place. Went twice. Also had a reasonable sized regular portion burger and chicken sandwich both were great.

3.5 

The evening started off on a very bad note.   The Manhattan only came only half filled and the beer (not shown) came in a lipstick stained glass.   My French martini was also poorly made.   The bartending staff needs much better training.  

Despite the start the food was extremely good.  We started off with the zucca chips which were crispy with a pinch of salt.  The farmers plate was filled with fresh vegetables and a delicious pesto sauce.   

Dinners included a spicy meatball pizza which had good flavors and a nice crust.  The scallops were cooked perfectly on top of a wonderful risotto.  I got the Bolognese Pasta with a fresh Burrata.  The pasta was cook properly and the sauce was meaty and seasoned just right. 

The Italian butter cake was amazing, soft, moist, buttery ... it just melted in you mouth.  

I would ago again but would probably not get a drink from the bar.
Yes, this is a chipotle and yes, I love this food.  Part of my staple diet :-).  My only two cents are that they should be open at least until 11pm.
Westmont Diner is great. I enjoyed the French toast, Scrapple, eggs, and breakfast potatoes. The food is delicious and the diner is very clean and the service is great.

I came here on a Thursday night with a couple of friends. We originally started out at a restaurant across State Street, but we were lured in by the sight of their patio dining and the promise of delicious Mexican food. 

Our presence was barely acknowledged by the hostess, so we just grabbed a couple of menus on our own to peruse their offerings. The prices are a bit on the high side, but they also offer a wide variety of appetizers for smaller appetites. Luckily, the service improved from that point. We basically seated ourselves at the edge of the patio, and it was ultimately a good location choice because not too much later, two musicians set up on the other side of the patio to play. The music was surprisingly NOT Mexican. I recall them playing a lively version of Hava Nagila at one point.

The service was quite good, with our server bearing with our requests. Apparently this is a more Americanized Mexican restaurant, so we had to explain how we wanted our Chavelas made. The refrigerated glasses are nice, but way too small to fit a proper beer. Might as well give me just the bottle! While some of the shrimp offerings on the appetizer menu were tempting, I ended up ordering the Carlito's Combo with a chicken enchilada and a chicken tamale. It was NOT cheap at $18.50, but the portion sizes were massive. I did find it a bit cheesy that they stick a bunch of toothpicks with Mexican flags on them into the food. Not sure what that's all about. I definitely had a lot of food leftover to take home, and it heated up pretty well as my lunch for the next day.

So why the three stars? Well, the portion sizes were gigantic, but it wasn't very authentic. For example, I've never had an enchilada before that had NO sauce on it. Mine came covered in rice, and was quite dry. Nor did it have any cheese on it. I did ask for the cotija cheese and the drizzle of sour cream to be left off, but I did miss the melted cheese in my enchilada. The tamale was also pretty gross, way too mushy and without any flavor. I'd have to say that my favorite part of the meal was actually the rice, which managed to be nicely seasoned. 

I would say one of the highlights of dining at Carlito's is the people watching. In the time we were there, the most entertaining aspect was watching an older gentleman with his wife in the passenger seat almost plow into the valet guy's stand as he attempted to park. And then he finally got his Prius into the handicapped spot, but it was at the craziest angle. While we sat there, I realized that the car was never turned off as the engine kept turning on (from electric mode) to recharge. I asked the valet to track down the dining couple, but ultimately, he just got into the car himself to turn it off...which means that the key was in the car the whole time and the doors were unlocked. Santa Barbara...such a trusting town!

Great meals with the added advice from the servers.  Enjoyed the entire time.  We ordered the Red Shrimp, Oyster Slider.  Along the way we had a special watermelon cocktail and the special of the evening , 16 0z. Pork chop.  We finished with Banana Pudding. We had a difficult time trying to rank the three choices and came up with you can't go wrong with any of them. Bob and Jane

wonderful products...too bad they are frequently out of their baked goods on saturday afternoon and sunday mornings.  I love the fruit  scones, but have stopped going there as there is a fixation on baking only raisin scones.  They would be better off over baking and donating the excess than not having enough for their customers.  Their products, when available , are excellent.

Went here after a shopping day with my fiancee. Walked in to the pizza place and introduced with the gorgeous interior design. You build your own pizza which was fun. The only confusing thing was the name cards were correctly paired with the items on the building place. The man behind the counter was extremely friendly and joked with us a bunch.
I am always in search of Tapas, my favorite way to eat, I just wish I was not alone tonight.  Small and intimate, sports playing, music playing.  Super friendly service.  Very casual spot.

It's good food but the portions got smaller! I the burger doesn't fill the entire bun any more and I used to get so full.

Also my friends don't want to go there anymore because that guy in the kitchen is a sexual predator idk the details

Queer bands stopped booking here so it's just bros and the comedy burlesque night is embarrassing 

The burger with the ham is pretty good. Used to be bigger
Fun place for drinks..don't under estimate potency of beverages...love the location....able to have fun, have a few drinks, and then walk around channel side which annexes to the historical Ybor city

Hands down it is still the best damn "Philly" Cheesesteak with Fried Onions, American Cheese that you can find anywhere & everywhere! Perfectly seasoned & cooked steak nestled in a poppy-seed Kaiser roll layered with fried onions & American cheese.

Thaitanium is one of those places you want to like SOOOOO badly but you just feel like something is missing.  I went for a dinner one evening with a friend.  The food was good, standard Thai food.  The seasoning was a little light...so make sure you order a step up.  I asked for my food to be seasoned at the "Hot" level...it was barely a "Medium".  The service was just adequate, no checking in on us to see if we needed anything (huge pet peeve of mine).  I probably will try it again when a group wants to go there but it is definitely not someplace I will go out of my way for on my own.

I was told this was a good place for hot chicken went here on a Friday around 7 pm. It was packed so I sat at the bar. I ordered 3 tender meal and it took about an hour to get the meal. It was t a big deal as I was drinking a few beers and watching the sports games, but that's way too long for tenders and fries. It was good but nothing special at all.

Came here visiting from Miami. The truffle crab claws and oysters are amazing. I hope everyone gets Ashley and Anthony as servers- they are amazing  and an asset to this restaurant and to the experience as a whole.

We loved everything about the experience!

The hot focaccia and knot rolls along with the olive oil and tapenade were brought immediately to the table followed by our bottle of Montepulciano d'abruzzo.  YUM!

We ordered the special version of a caprese for our appetizer....prosciutto, tomato, lettuce, pesto, balsamic reduction, and burrata mozzarella di bufala. The richness was palpable. The milkiness was there. The fattiness oozed. Each ball, each bite, each shred screamed fresh burrata mozzarella di bufala. 

My husband ordered lasagna and I ordered the meatballs and ricotta for a meal and extra parmesan was offered. A nice salad accompanied his meal. While my husband says it wasn't his favorite lasagne of all time, he said it was delicious and I concur as he didn't leave one bite of the huge portion. The portions were huge and I brought back a meatball and sauce to our hotel after filling up on wine, bread, and salad!

All the other meals that came by looked as scrumptious and hearty as the next. From pizzas, pastas, and pork osso bucco! Compliments filled the air from nearby tables.

Our waitress was attentive and the environment was appropriately lively for a Friday night!  If it hadn't been summer storming, we would have loved to dine outside. We will definitely be back to do so!

John, aka Grizzly Bear, helped us with parking as well, and gave us great advice on ordering!

Verducci's is a gem!

We tried me Mian Sichuan as alternative to our usual noodle place. We found the food to be different and  really not to our liking. The cost of the food for two dishes and an appetizer was quite high, over $30. There may be many people who enjoy going to the Mian Sichuan. I really can't say where would be one of them and we will travel farther to go back to our usual place.
No bueno

Had a killer lunch on a Saturday afternoon. Nice little spot on Fairmount st. Patio seating as well as some indoor spots. We all ordered paninis. Everyone loved their meal. I had the special - jerk chicken. I substituted the provolone for sharp provolone. Great sandwich. Gf had the San Diego. Chicken, sharp provolone, roasted red pepper and pesto. Served on a panini roll. Also very good. We will definitely go back to try more! Eat it!

I could eat Asian food every day...I would consider myself an Asian food snob. This place is really amazing. My buddy and I shared fresh rolls. They were delicious and so pretty to look at. We each got vermicelli bowls and we loved them. There are some really interesting dishes to come back and try. The ambiance is really upscale/casual. I am already a fan!
The best BBQ sandwiches and sides in Nashville! They need additional locations in Bellevue and on the Strip!!

Went there twice this week... Once for breakfast and had the Chicken and bacon waffle tower... AMAZING!
Had Dinner there last night and had a Duck breaks over yam end prosciutto mashed tater... GF had the Stuffed meatloaf.  I can honestly say this is by far the BEST food I have had in Reno.. I love people complaining about HOW LONG food takes... Yeh don't you hate it when things are cooked fresh to order.. GO back to Claim jumpers yeh Maroons... This is Fresh wonderful food and it takes a few extra mins... Plus waiter let me know to go get a Harrahs card and get 25% off from now on.. Did I mention I had a Living social deal so i received about $50 worth of food for $25. So Good even if its a little out of my price range I will be back!!! and i cant WAIT!!

Stopped in South on a whim. It is super cute. Has a garden feel on the inside. Amir was our server and he started off as service perfection(we later had to look for him several times). We went for brunch, which is three courses. I got the peach Bellini didn't love it, but the food made up for it. The blue crab toast was delicious and so were the fried green tomatoes(my first time ever having them). I had the chicken and waffles which was excellent. The corn bread was also very good. The place is very cute and the interactions with the staff were great when they were available. I think they need to add a few extra servers and this place will be perfection.

Not bad. Pizza tasted fresh, easy to cook at home and not a tomato sauce soaked lump of dough like some others. 

Trying to be trending, they also offer crustless pizza. Forget it. It  was a glob of toppings in a pan. Kind of gross for those of us that don't like our food all mixed up. 
Mediterranean pizza was good as was another chicken one.
Store looked a little messy, but they could have been busy and hadn't straightened up yet. 
We still go there, but not ordering that pizza nacho looking dish.

Food was excellent. I had the bread basket and chocolate croissants. Bread quality is delicious and upto European standards.

My friend had poutine and it was good as well! The yoke off the egg wasn't how it was asked for. 

There was a 45 min wait and we got seated in 30. We ordered a coffee while waiting but it took us exactly all 30 min to order and receive.

I think it's a great place but great food, but could use some more structure.

This is your average run of the mill Bertucci's.  I went here for lunch because my Grandma refuses to eat anything besides Italian food or the Cheesecake Factory and this is closeby.  I got the margherita pizza with shrimp on top and it was pretty good.  The waiter was a bit confused and got my aunt's lunch very wrong- but he was trying.  We were celebrating two birthdays so he brought out a slice of cheesecake on the house.  Overall, I wouldn't go out of my way to go here but it's decent if I'm going out to lunch with Grandma.

This is a really authentic Cantonese Dim Sum place!

It doesn't get a high rating on Yelp because many Americans don't have an idea of how traditional dim sum place works -- there will be no menu. The waitress will pull out a cart carrying all kinds of dim sums so customers can choose from. Tea is free: you can have Pu'er, Oolong or jasmine. 

Chinese people should definitely try out this place!
Fooda lunch last week and I got a burger. Sauce was great. Burger ok. But sooooo small!

All the ads are true. The green corn tamales are really tasty here. A little sweet a little savory and pretty perfect. The combo plate came with 1 tamale, 1 cheese enchilada, and beans. The enchilada was solid. And the plate was definitely a good portion size. There was not much left over after I finished dinner. The guacamole was mediocre, I felt it was too salty and didn't have enough cilantro. The chips were tasty however. So all in all a solid place for Mexican but nothing stellar. I felt that the room was small and echoed a lot. So I felt like every other table had to listen to my conversation which I felt bad about. The wait staff was friendly however I never got a refill on my water.
eww. gaad! they should rename this place the dirty wok buffet. and buffet stands for big ugly fat fuckers eating together.
we ordered thai curry and some rice but it was very watery & greasy n service was also too slow... the place is ok.. may be its better with vietnamese food..

I loved my trip to Postcorner. My mom went twice on her visit to Clearwater Beach and loved it both times. The best part is the service! They are extremely friendly and gave off the great "family owned" vibe. I have a 16 month old son who was kind of a handful while we were there and the waitress couldn't have been more helpful and sweet to us. She let us know that we were no trouble at all. 
The breakfast pizza is awesome as well as the Greek salad. I can't speak for the whole menu, but it is a nice little place to give a shot!
Friends and I ate our first New Orleans dinner here and it was decent. We had a nice view of the street from a table on the porch upstairs.

I'm a big fan of brew pub food but for some reason the Manayunk Brewery was a solid meh for me. 

The atmosphere, the staff, the food, --and yes, even the beer --all suffer from the same 'so what' factor. Add in the trek we had to make to get here and it's just not worth it.

The Squeeze is a great place for breakfast. Steve and Lisa are awesome as well as the rest of the staff. At the squeeze you are family,you are greeted by your first name and everyone is accomidating. My wife and i are both on walkers and they make us feel so welcome. The omelettes are great!!
Try the quintana foo or roo. Highly recommend this place

An amazing world class property. From the moment you check in you feel pampered. 
The last time I stayed there was 17 years ago. They remodeled the entire property to perfection. 
The service was on point. The rooms big enough. The gardens fully manicured. 
Although the food was amazing , they need to add more selection to their Menu. 
I would defiantly go there again.

I'm not in this area of Lafayette Road often but decided I needed a cup of coffee before an appointment. Drove into Star Bucks parking lot and could not find a parking space plus the drive thru line was wrapped around the building.  As I was leaving the parking lot, I noticed a small Bjava coffee house sitting in the corner of the strip mall. So in I went and I'm happy I gave it a try. Good coffee with beautiful Latte foam artwork. 

It is a small, privately owned coffee and tea shop who's been here for 9 years. I had no idea since the sign doesn't face Lafayette Road. I was the only customer in the store so service wasn't an issue. I found the owner to be warm and friendly. After explaining I was a new customer she preceded to explain their coffee was roasted in house and the coffee sizes they offer.  As I was waiting, I checked into Yelp and was surprised to see a 10% discount off of my order. Love that!!  Then she brought a pan of freshly baked cinnamon rolls to the counter, still hot out of the oven. Cinnamon rolls are usually served on Friday or Saturday only. Further explained pans of rolls were forgotten in the freezer on Saturday so she pulled and baked as a Monday treat for customers. Stop in for coffee and support the private business owner.

Perfectos has the most authentic tasting tamales, refried beans, posole & menudo. I've eaten here over a dozen times and they never disappoint. The staff is prompt and courteous. Definately recommend.

Based on my first and only impression, which was for Sunday brunch.

Nobody can compare to the brunch at Oystercatchers, so I'm really trying not to do that. But there aren't many options on the menu, and everything is a-la-carte.

For brunch I like to mix it up a little between breakfast and lunch items, but these guys have mostly breakfast items. It's really breakfast, with the addition of fried chicken and a burger.

The breakfast was fine, BTW. I had eggs benedict and grits, and they were fine. My dolly had an omelet and she said it was "OK" (she looked a bit disappointed though).

If I had the option of paying maybe $25 - $40 per person and could try any of their items, I bet I'd have been more pleased. And probably would have spent more money too.

The ambiance and service were good, so I think we'll return for their dinner and extensive wine list.

The three course meal here is a fantastic deal!

One soup, one appetizer, and one entree for roughly $10!

The overall quality of the food here is pretty average, but for the prices they're charging (especially for the three course special), there's really not that much to complain about. Every dish is a little bland or greasy or over-sauced, but everything is still edible.

Pattaya is definitely not a place I would go to frequently, but it is a nice restaurant to get a cheap Thai dinner every once in a while.

This is a really great restaurant.

The location is right outside Forest Park, and there is parking alongside the building. The building is a residential building and looks like an old dorm building. 

The restaurant was not crowded, and the service was great. They serve their full menu all day, and it is definitely difficult to make a decision about what to order. 

We ended up ordering the Pyro burger, a waffle, and dirty fries. (Yes, the waitress laughed at the combination too.) 

The Pyro burger was fantastic. We ordered it medium well, and while it was a little overcooked, the flavors and spice level were phenomenal. 

The dirty fries were just so unique. I definitely recommend ordering them to try. The bistro fries themselves are awesome with a hint of sugar in the salt, but the addition of the gravy-like component is so different.

The waffle was great. It was slightly sweet and the perfect texture. 

Overall, the food is inexpensive and great. I would definitely come back.
This place has some pretty delicious food! My husband and I had the Spicy tuna don & a ramen bowl and both were fantastic!

This one is not as good as the other magasin that closed on magazine. Portions are smaller. Dishes are different. It's still good but not as good as the one that was on Magazine. Oh and I feel like it's more pricey!

Arrived at 11:30am for lunch.  Ordered chicken wings and a house salad.  Received utensils with only a knife wrapped in a napkin.  5 minutes later out came my wings and salad.  Salad had no cheese and wings were room temperature.  Sauce was good but when I asked why they came out so quickly the bartender told me they like to cook them early.  Well, I don't know about you, but when I order something I expect it to be cooked for me...that's why I am going to your restaurant!  The cooks were just interested in watching a NBA game that was played the night before...and the main tv was on the afternoon today show...cmon people...this is a sports type bar in a great location...YOU CAN DO BETTER.
Excellent food, great service. Will definitely go back. The only downside is that they don't serve alcohol, but the wine bar next door is very accommodating.
Probably my favorite restaurant in La Vergne. Their curry or pineapple fried rice never disappoint! They have a ton of vegetarian options and great service.

Loves and Madmen is an oasis on its block!  It is everything I love in a café - light and airy (there are huge windows everywhere) with friendly employees and a great drink selection.  While the drinks don't particularly stand out, they are made with great care and taste fine.  It's more the atmosphere that appeals to me.  It's a great study spot (free wireless) and feels like a community place (there are fliers for local events and the employees seem to know the customers).  Definitely my favorite Sunday morning study spot!

Like most Thai restaurants, I start with the Pad Thai. However, my new favorite after dining at Spice 28 is the Drunken Noodle. Any Pad Thai lover needs to give it a try.

Also, for a different appetizer, try the Spicy Cucumber. The sweet, salty soy concoction they soak the cuc pieces in is to die for. Once I was done with the cucumber, I finished the sauce to the last drop.

KEEP  AWAY    FROM     this    Dump......        Took  my  sons  for  dinner  last  night.    What  a  disaster.......Poor   quality  food    nasty    service.   rude   management......  The  fried  flounder  tasted  like  shoe  leather(  had  5  coatings  of   cornmeal)    where is the fish.?        My  sons  turkey   croquettes     looked  and   tasted  like  last  nights  vomit.      Our  waitress   Lisa  was  obviously  stoned  on  drugs   and    had  no  teeth.    She   kept  putting her   head  down on  our  table    and in our  face........The  food  was  so bad  it  wasnt  even  edible.   Nothing  tasted  normal.   The  final  kicker  was  when   Lisa   ran  outside  and   chased  me  down  for  her  tip........Wow   how  bad is  that,,,,  Go  to  Ponzios or  Silver diner  if you  want  a  decent   normal  meal...........KEEP   AWAY   THIS  PLace IS     Really    bad,    !!!!!

On your way back from Violet or up from Plaquemines and need a non-fast food fix in da parish? Charlie's is the spot, especially on Sunday when Rocky & Carlos is closed! 

On our way back from the Los Islenos Christmas celebration, we were those people, Yelping by phone to see if Rocky & Carlos was open (I really wanted some mac n' cheese!) Fortunately, Charlie's came up, and I remembered that I had met the owner several months back when they provided food at an Urban League fundraiser we had attended. Their gumbo was standout and a real motivator to come check out the restaurant itself. 

Fair warning, in the dark, it can be a little difficult to spot. My left turn was a wee-bit dangerous. That Sunday evening, there were maybe 3 or 4 other diners, mostly families, intently watching the Saints game as were we. The interior is spacious, with a large dining room, bar, and a separate smaller room. The menu is large and reasonably priced, with most items being in the $10-20 range. 

We ordered: 

1. Breaded eggplant with red gravy. I'm used to getting eggplant in sticks but these came in slices, and they were huge! The eggplant was tender although the breading was bland; dipping sauce was a necessity. 

Large serving sizes would turn out to be a theme.  

2. Catfish Almondine. This was not exactly what I expected, but still yummy. Deep-fried catfish rather than sauteed, topped with toasted almonds. The fried catfish was some of the best I've ever had, light and flavorful. French fries were standard but the green beans with bacon were delicious. 

3. Veal Swiss - paneed veal covered in gravy and swiss cheese. I didn't love it, probably gravy smothering just doesn't do it for me. The mac n' cheese was awesome though; a nice crust of cheddar over penne pasta and a sticky milky cheese sauce. The side of corn didn't taste like it was from a can either. 

There are daily specials (red beans on Monday, etc) and catering options. During the meal I counted no less than 5 people come by to pick up takeout orders. 

CASH ONLY. There's an ATM at the entrance that charges at $2.75 fee.

Recently saw this place and decided to give it a try tonight, since we were in the mood for Thai.

I like the fact that you can choose to sit on the floor or at a table with chairs.

We both had Thai dishes, both delicious.

All of the staff were friendly, and the place has a good vibe as far as ambience goes.

Great little place, great food.  We will be back!

I really wanted to like this more than I did.
My boys rave about this place so my review is not relevant if you ask them.
However!
For the price, my review is accurate.
There's a wait for food once ordered. (Not a big deal)
But if one waits for food, you'd think it would be hot...warm at a minimum.
My fries were straight up cold.
In hindsight I should have ordered the cheese fries. After viewing other people's order the liquid cheese on the fries looked amazing and probably would have added some warmth.
The burger?
I don't understand the rave?
I prefer smaller portions but for the price this burger kind of through me off.
Aside from it being cold, the onion slices (which were huge) overwhelmed the burger.
I'll give it to them for the freshness of the onion (and likely all of the ingredients) but as much as I appreciate onion on my burger I did not order an onion sandwich.
The milkshake...or malt?
Whatever it's called was ok but for average it's overpriced.
In full disclosure I'm likely to be back since the family won't pass up the opportunity to eat here, but as a bit of a foodie I don't get the rave.
Tasty and customizable! Similar ordering style to a Chipotle. Went here for lunch with friends and definitely want to come here again. Simple and easy!

The entree was good..although overpriced. The drinks were not very good. The waiter claimed the bartender was great, but not in my opinion. Both drinks were weak, and almost watered down. Blah. 
The food was tasty, but I didn't think the prices were appropriate for the portion size. I don't think i would come back here.

Friendly staff. Excellent hot dogs. You can get them steamed, fried, or grilled. They have a bunch of good combinations of toppings. My crew got the buffalo, the chi town, and the classic chili. All were delicious. The fried jalapeños were excellent too. Cool atmosphere - like a little house that was turned into a casual restaurant.

Went for dinner on a Sunday evening, there was no wait. The corn muffins served while you order were very good. Ordered the seafood platter and it was perfect. Crab Mac n cheese was definitely my favorite! Very friendly staff! Will definitely be coming back when in the Clearwater area.

Always a pleasure when we dine here! Our waitress, Agne,  was extremely polite and very efficient! They revamped their menu so we were pretty sad to see that the smoked salmon appetizer was no longer on the menu (insert sad face here). She suggested the jalapeño cornbread and it was a hit! Im very picky with my salmon and they made it perfectly! We also had the grilled artichoke, everyone said it was really good (especially with the sauce it came with). I'm not an artichoke heart type of girl so I can't really comment. The steak was also amazing but a little too rich for me but the piece I ate off his plate was delicious! We ate ourselves into such a food coma but definitely left satisfied!!

The atmosphere was great, the food was good, but the service was what makes this place.  The staff and the managers were all so friendly and accommodating.  They offered up very honest opinions on their own menu and really seemed to genuinely care about making the experience a positive one.  

I loved the alligator bites and sauce but the entrees were nothing overly special.

First of all let's talk about how toxic this place is as a business. The body shaming of a close friend of mine because she was a bit heavier than the other workers is uncalled for. For this to be a black owned business they definitely don't lift up or support other black people. Over worked and under paid!! The food is OK but they were out of majority of the thing I wanted on the menu and I was not able to add additional items to my meal or substitute. The drinks lemonade was diabetes in a cup. Constantly losing staff making customers wait even longer. Imma pray for this business because sis actually has potential.

I like this place.  It is cheap, and the food is good for what it is.  My favorite item here is the whitefish salad on a bagel.  Service is good.  Atmosphere is pretty basic and minimal for a diner.  The vegetables are very fresh, which makes a big difference.

This is a good place for breakfasty-brunchy food.  In spite of being a pretty small space, it's surprisingly good at accomodating our oversized group that meets here regularly for brunch.

Terrific bagels (I tried the salt and the rosemary, both were great) and spreads (dill pickle was terrific, my kids loved the strawberry on the French toast). The lox was like butter. Solid coffee. My service was pretty quick, but if things don't move as fast as you like, remember that they're brand new. I think they'll work out the kinks pretty quickly.

Went to Tito's with my cousin for a late lunch and were pleasantly surprised and content with the two different Ceviches we ordered along with the Rice with Shrimp and the Hanger Steak. Everything was delicious and so were the Pisco Sours. We'll be back!

It's far out but beautiful! If you have allergies I would stay away! We went for a wedding and the setting was beautiful and the food is maybe a 6 out of 10...the room was crowded with 150 people....small dance floor but the people that worked at the front Desk, Andrew Fine was AMAZING and very helpful and our waiter Arturo was very good! I was disappointed that after getting back to our room at 12 the maid came knocking at 8:20am....the drapes were shut and our car was parked outside the room so I thought it was obvious we were in there sleeping but maybe not...HA!  There was no "do not disturb" card to put out.  You can hear EVERYTHING that is being said or done in the rooms next to you so be aware of that if you are going for a romantic weekend with your honey!

This is our favorite Chinese spot! Delicious Crab Rangoon & egg rolls!! Jason always gets the General Tso Chicken.. and I switch between seasame chicken and sweet and sour chicken. Can't go wrong with the classics!  So glad to have found this place.

Instantaneous food love! 

This cute little place just opened in February 2016 on Jasper and was on my list to try. I was hoping for something different from all the other Korean BBQ places that you normally find and Soy and Pepper did not disappoint.

I found the restaurant to be super cute and cozy with a really welcoming atmosphere. The staff were super friendly and helpful and provided some great suggestions for our dinner. We started off with drinks, which were made with Soju and were super light and refreshing.  We ordered a full order of the Korean fried chicken (half chili pepper and half soy garlic) and a small order of the bulgogi and they were both beyond delicious. So much so that I tried to bring my family back the next day so they could try it. 

Even though we were so stuffed and didn't finish our food we still had to try the dessert. We tried the Korean pancake with ice cream and just like everything else it was so good. It wasn't to sweet or heavy and was the perfect way to end our meal. 

Like I said, instantaneous food love! I can't wait to bring my family and other friends to Soy and Pepper.

It is always something at this Starbucks.  Yesterday and today it was a lecture about requesting a straw for my drink.  They have started putting sippy cup lids on the drinks.  The lecture has something to do with saving the planet.  The girl that told me this yesterday was so rude and awful that I shouldn't have gone back today.  I did. My mistake.  Got the same lecture in a gentler tone.  I find it hard to believe they are trying to save sea life when they are still using plastic cups and even bigger plastic lids.  Not to mention the straws come wrapped in paper and my mouth is only touching something I touched not 2-5 Starbucks employees.

This is a cute little comfy bar with great service and delicious food. The dumplings are amazing. Great music! Upbeat and great vibes and energy in here and yummy cocktails :) if ever in Philly again I will be back!!!

I really had some high hopes for this restaurant, however, this was a truly ridiculous and overpriced experience unlike any other. 
    The customer service: terrible. We had reserved a spot at the sushi bar, but upon arrival, the waitress just pointed in the direction of the bar and told us to sit there.
  The sushi was actually decent, though a little overpriced. We ordered off the menu for our main.  I have to say that the waitress was pretty rude.   My husband got the steak hibachi from the kitchen. The steak was just fair. I ordered the Beef Soba, which is a Japanese buckwheat noodle, and the menu even described it as "Japanese brown noodle".  What arrived was a huge plate of mushy thin egg noodle with overlooked beef and a store bought, way too salty sauce. One waitress stopped to ask how things were. After I politely stated my disappointment with the noodles and why, we were subjected to three lengthy encounters with wait staff and the manager... Not to address my concerns or to ask if there was something else I would like for dinner, but to scrutinize the menu and prove to me that Soba could mean just about anything at any restaurant. The manager even went so far as to bring out a cellophane package of  Yakisoba noodles, kind of like cheap ramen, which can be purchased in any Asian market for 99 cents. To cap off an already epic evening, we were told by our waitress that we would have to pay two bills because  we ordered sushi from the bar where we sat, but the main course from the wait staff. 
     Since we went in their first week of business, we were prepared to give it another try, but after reading these other reviews, it's highly unlikely that we will risk wasting our money here. The one star rating is for the sushi only. This business will not last. Too bad.
I worked at Ben's as a teenager.It was great back then(in the 70's) and still is today.Always great food and good price. Also Joe the is a great guy.

Second time here. Packed, as should be expected on a Friday night. First available had us seated indoors and not on the lovely patio.
We ordered a bottle of Malbec and eggplant rollatini which tasted good, but should have been served warmer.

The Margherita pizza was hot with a well done crust, but there was little basil ( my sole purpose in ordering this type) and not evenly distributed.

Saved room for gelato!! My husband was pleased with his Nutella and strawberry gelato. My coconut was creamy but coconut flavor could have been stronger. Cappuccino was "very tasty" ( I don't drink them!)

Our server hustled and was excellent.
A bit disappointed over the quality of the food, but will return at a later date.

Ummm NEW FAV place! I'm so happy to have stumbled upon this gem. I was originally just going to get a bubble tea at tea do, but got distracted by this place and ended up getting a massive mango shaved ice and a matcha millicake. Everything was sooo good, it reminded me just like home. I love everything about this place, from interior design, their advertisements, to their actual dessert. I live an hour from here and i only came here twice this month. YUUSS cheers to mango mango. You will definitely see me here again soon. I've also tried the matcha ice cream waffle sandwich, that was pretty good as well. I was low key hoping the waffles are the actual Belgium waffles though. Those super sweet ones. But it was still delicious. Tip: if you get the mango shaved ice, you probably can't finish it by yourself! LOL

5/5 Service! Our waitress was amazing and so funny. We had great conversations and she made our visit a whole lot better.

5/5 Ambiance! A nice vibe where you can just come for girls' night or a date. It's not too overwhelming and is just the right amount. The couches/seating are SO comfy too.

5/5 Food. We just came for dessert but from the visuals to the taste, you cannot go wrong.

I love me some capital tacos. I usually get the augari and it is so delicious and unlike any taco I have tasted before. I have been to the original capital tacos and wondered why they haven't expanded, but I am glad they did. This place is in a plaza and doesnt stand out to you, so you have to know it's there. This location is very spatious and nicely layed out. The workers were kind and they give you a license plate and deliver your order to the table you sit at. The augari tacos were just as delicious as the original augaris that I tasted at the other location. Still has the same great taste! I also had some chips and queso which did not disappoint either. I enjoyed my experience at this retaurant. Overall, the sutomer service was good, the layout was nice and the food was amazing! I wish I had a portable capital tacos with me everywhere I went.

i figured i would try this place as i was running errands, i was impressed and i gave it 3 stars but  only because the first time there and i want to go back and see if its consistent with the food. anyway i went in for lunch and had 1 of the lunch specials; a salad , two slices and a beverage. the salad was pretty good size and was enough for 2 people. the pizza was tasty and the sauce had a nice balance of tomatoes and spices. the only negative i would say was the crust was a little thicker then i like but not too bad or thick. overall i would say was a good value for the money and 2 could have shared so i will be returning to try not just pizza but the pasta and appetizers

We picked this place because of convenience, there are better options I'm sure.  We ordered the olives and dates, olives are spicy, too spicy, we like spicy but that seemed excessive. The dates were good, had a nice maple flavor. Then the meals were not so great, my fish was over cooked and had no flavor, no one enjoyed the burgers and the tacos were just ok.  Service was great and sitting on the covered patio during a thunderstorm was beautiful.

We ordered a variety of items and they were all delicious and fresh! The rice was cooked perfect, sometimes it can be dry but this wasn't ! The sautéed broccoli from the veggie menu was amazing ! We will be ordering from here again

First time we came here 2pm on a Wednesday. They said they're known for the Clooney, so I got one, and a butterscotch shake. I did not choose wrong. The sandwich was PERFECT warm, bread wasn't too thick and a little crispy and the avocado was like a spread instead of chunks. The shake was yummy but next time I don't need the whip cream. I will be back!
Food was horrible. Service and drinks were ok. $8 for 1/6 of a wedge salad that tasted funny.  Wings were rubbery and

Cute little place in East Nasheville. Loved that we could walk here from our airbnb.

The layout is adorable and the food is pretty great. We did wait for a table for awhile even though there were empty spots, and they did serve me a BLT with no b (?!) but the servers were very sweet and did a good job overall.

The grits were not as mindblowing as everyone stated they were but the BLT was pretty incredible. The kefir was so odd (was expecting yogurt) but so fun to try. Their juice is also awesome. Super fresh.

Solid brunch spot!
Steak n Shake is like In n Out in CA. Wonderful burgers, wonderful fries and great atmosphere. I loved it!! I have pictures to prove how much I liked it too...haha.

This was the best Italian food I've probably ever had.. the restaurant atmosphere is awesome and the fact that it's a local neighborhood makes it even better. The wait staff and bartenders were awesome. The hostess wasn't the nicest but maybe she was having a long day

Whenever I'm in town in business, I stop here for lunch
Service was stellar, always there but no intrusive 
Tonight was first time for dinner - 20 buck a head is kinda spendy but the sushi was fresh and the selection was good - definitely not on par with Sushi on Oracle but decent
Good eats!
My favorite place to eat. I love the crab cakes and the strawberry cheesecake. Service is always excellent and well worth the (inevitable) wait and difficulty finding parking

I fear these types of restaurants.  Hibachi *can* be done well but every one that I've been to (this one included)  muddles it down to "if we set things on fire, perhaps they won't notice that the food is bleh drowning in some form of sauce.".

Well, I noticed.

We sat at the bar and had the whiskey flight. It's so cool the whiskey is actually distilled and bottled in house. The whiskeys were creative and super fun to try. The service was great, too! The bartender helped us decide which to try and was obviously knowledgeable. We also had the pretzel which was good. It came with cheese dip and honest mustard dip. We would come back to try more cocktails for sure.

Super disappointed I just ordered via Uber eats. It doesn't look like they added spirulina which I paid extra for and I asked for granola on the side and didn't get it which is basically my favorite part.

Phone number on the receipt is invalid so can't even call to let them know.

My husband and I have been here twice this month, once for lunch and once in the early evening. The food is VERY good.  The tater tots are great and the Gastro Burger is amazing. Our service was excellent on both occasions. Looking forward to checking out Happy Hour specials and their weekend Brunch.

Decided to try this place after reading lots of good reviews.  My wife and I ordered take out - me- lemon chicken, her - broccoli beef.  While I would say it was decent, I wasn't super impressed.  I found the broccoli beef to taste fairly bland.  The lemon chicken was better but still I don't think I would order it again, it was must ok.  We will definitely try it again with different dishes and update this review of our experience is different.  One more chance, then the search continues for a go-to Chinese place in central tucson.  On another note, the young man that helped me was super friendly.

This is a bright and cheery place that's always full of energy and plenty of buzz. It's a good place to go with a crowd that enjoys traditional breakfast/brunch fare, and also those that may crave a little more than the usual. 

I always go on the weekend, and only once was I seated immediately - it was at 8 am. Anytime other than that, and my wait has always been at least 30 minutes. If you have managed that expectation beforehand, plan to chill outside while you wait, grab a coffee or mimosa (multiple flavors available, try mango!) while doing so, and you'll be just fine. 

The food and service are ok, nothing to knock my socks off, but it's good enough that it's something that everyone can agree on and be happy.

The burgers are great! Definitely top 3 in Nashville. We argue about the rank. The sides are good, my favorite is the black bean corn salad. My only consistent complaint is the loud music they play. You can't hold a conversation very well. Go if you need to eat and run, but not have a conversation.  Good beer selection.

So my wife and I have been ordering Benitos wings and their quesadillas for years now.  Tonight we decided to order a quesadilla and an order of tacos al pastor with a side of guacamole, cheese and sour cream. After waiting 45 minutes for our delivery( which is the usual wait time for Benito's) the driver arrives at our door.  We open our order and quickly realize there was no side of guacamole( which also was not on the receipt).  We opened the tacos which looked to be ok until I went to squeeze the limes they provided and the limes were dried out.  When my wife opened up the quesadilla, it was a long thick tortilla with cheese and crema on top.  The tortilla felt like a crumbling cookie texture.  We called the location and "the owners daughter Stacy" answered the phone and was very arrogant.  She stated they have always made their quesadillas with that tortilla she than stated she would give us our money back as long as we didn't eat any of the food.  We explained to her that we did eat 1 taco but the rest of the food was there.  She stated she would have someone, "she didn't know which driver" come back out to get the food and give us a refund.  Shortly after we received a snotty voicemail from Stacy stating it was not her problem that we didn't know we had an option between flour or corn tortilla on the quesadillas.  Which she never gave us the option when ordering.  She also told us that her father stated we would have to drop off the food to get our refund like it was OUR(the customers) fault.  She than began to get loud with my wife asking where my wife worked.  Which was really unprofessional as if she was going to pay a visit to my wife's job. They never ended up giving us our money back and we were left with this food.  If there is a way for me to put up the voicemail left on our phone I will.  HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE and I understand she is the owners daughter but she may need to take a class in customer service because she knows nothing about it and they should NOT leave their business in her hands.

If I could do a two-and-half star review I would because Sauce is a definitively average pizza place. The only reason I went with two stars rather than 3 is because the place is very over-hyped. Whenever I would ask what the good pizza places in Tucson were, one of the first mentioned would be Sauce. My wife and I would drive by it constantly and we decided to check it out one night. Considering the great places we've found since (Zachary's, Picazzo's), we won't be heading back to Sauce in the near future.

I'm not a fan of the layout of the restaurant. It's self-seating which is a big problem since the place is constantly packed, and there's usually a considerable wait to order food. Of course, once you've ordered your food you have to hope that there's a table available to eat. I could get over the whole ordering and self-seating format if the pizza was worth the wait but sadly, it's not.

I like thin pizza but this is far too thin for my liking. Others might disagree but considering the price is a little higher than most pizzerias, I think the pizza should be a little thicker. The menu is also extremely limited. But they do serve mac and cheese as a side, which is a plus. It's not the greatest mac and cheese but any opportunity at indulgence is well-noted in my book.

This pizza is amazing!  I have been there 6 times since they opened 3 weeks ago!  They make your pizza how you want it, right in front of you.  Everything is fresh and it just tastes great!  I even have my parents eating there at least once a week.  Cannot say enough good things about Pionic!
Food was awful. Tasted like microwaved meat! Also customer service was was non existent

This is one of the worst cheesesteaks I have ever had. I can list 5 restaurants that make better IMO. Maybe there is a secret menu I did not look for or maybe I just don't know how to order but for the cost and what you get, I will not go back.
Super bomb place for good eats at good prices.  Lots of different types to try.  This place is a great addition to a diverse culinary option for Boise.

A nice dinner place on Magazine Street! =)

I ordered the beef brisket and my friend ordered the stuffed bell peppers. Our orders came with corn bread. Everything tasted really good and the service was great. The restaurant is a couple blocks away from the Bulldog pub. Great ambiance and location, and good prices.

I haven't been to this location for a few years and I'm glad to say the service has improved immensely. I used to come here with a group of friends and getting a drink was hard enough. Getting service of any kind after we'd get our food was nearly impossible. The waitresses would just stop coming by.

Last night was the UFC fight, and it was very busy because there were two championships on the line. Our waitress was quick and attentive and actually smiled (!) at us. Someone came by and charged us $10 each to stay for the fights, but we each got a drink ticket. It's all good.

Wall to wall TVs and good enough sound. The menu isn't very big, but it has the standard fare. My friend had a chicken club and I had loco bread. The bread was delicious, topped with tons of cheese, but the tomato sauce dip tastes like tomato paste and the garlic aioli tastes like mayonnaise. Gross.

Would I come here to watch another UFC fight? Absolutely! Would i come here otherwise? Nope. The menu isn't interesting enough, and I'm still leery of the service.

Only a matter of time before the droves of people turn their attention to a new fad. My hash was greasy beyond normal consumption standards. That being said I don't understand the fascination with this place either. I was utterly displeased.

Enjoyed our visit. We were early on Monday so there was no wait time. My husband had the grouper dinner and I had the shrimps and both were excellent. Portions were very large. The side order of coleslaw was small but the serving of beans was much larger. I would have liked a little more coleslaw and my husband could not finish the beans.

Best pork, rice and beans in town.
