Sauce is a big deal to him and did not meet his expectations. The wine list is extensive if you're buying a bottle, by the glass is limited but good selection. 
I seriously expected more due to higher prices and all items a la carte. 
Overall very disappointing and will not return.

A cafe in a garden centre!  My, times have changed.  Busy indoor outdoor cafe that is good for brunch.  Massive garden centre with a lot of parking.  The food is very good and bistro style with the fancy dishes.  Prices are reasonable.  Get there early or you won't get in. They are licensed and have cocktails too.  Patio overlooks the perennials and shrubs.  Nice.
I have dine there before they were closed for months.  The soup that I always ordered was a little pricy but it was good. The place is a bit small and I believe they don't take credit card under 10
LOVE yats!! the good is always so fresh and full of flavor! highly recommend the chipotle alexio

My friend recently moved to Wayne and she heard this was the Chinese restaurant to go to. She loved the Hot n Sour Soup , but, was disappointed in the chinese sesame noodles. I had the Vegetarian steamed dumplings and they were homemade and delicious. They give you fresh chinese fried noodles and hot tea, which was fitting on the day we went. The Staff was very nice too.  They deliver, which is great as she sometimes wants delivery. I would come back. I think she will too.

Been here a few times. There are only two reasons I continually come back: Sizzling Rice Soup and Shanghai Street Dumplings. I've always been a fan of sizzling rice soup and its hard to find. Shang Hai's is very good. The Shanghai Street Dumplings are (really) the reason I come. Xiaolongbao are very difficult to find. Are they the best I've ever had? No (that honor goes to Din Tai Fung) but they satisfy my appetite plenty while I'm not in Los Angeles. Their tea is very delicious. Their appetizers are also very delicious. However, the rest of the food (entrees) are nothing special to me. So I continue to go back for the soup and dumplings. Those are the only reason I give it four.

I was looking for quality tacos and heard good things about Tacos del Cartel. They did not disappoint. I got 3 tacos pastor, shrimp, and brisket.  The shrimp and brisket tacos were very good, but the pastor blew my mind. High quality ingredients across the board, and the combination of flavors was sublime. I definitely will be heading back there in the near future, and if you do, do yourself a favor and grab at least one pastor taco.  I grabbed takeout due to COVID, but I was impressed by the interior decor and ambiance. Well judged music that wasn't too loud, a very nice vibe all around. After I get my vaccine, I will definitely be dining in.

The most incredibly delicious can complex salsas that I have ever eaten. The flavors are pitch perfect - a bit sweet, a bit caliente or spicy warm [not too much] with added flavors of cilantro, roasted peppers/tomatoes, onions and ??? And this is the table salsa before and with your meal.

Tortilla Chips from Heaven ... Fresh yellow corn tortillas made into fresh chips - blowing your palette with flavor of roasted yellow corn. Yes, you read that right.

Lovely atmosphere. Outside St Phillips Plaza is like Europe meets Southwestern Plaza. Inside it is very clean and surprisingly not too loud given the tile floors. Rich wood interior.

Great staff, very well trained and attentive.

The World's Largest collection of Tequila and spirits ...... seriously, I think. My table had a little tablet with gorgeous photos in an app that displayed their massive collection. I would love to do tiny taste testing. In Mexico I discovered their are some very delicate and wonderful tasting Tequilas .... not the harsh bottom of the trash barrel stuff most people drink in the states. I think it must be distilled in the gas tank of old buses ..... haha.

I chickened out and got the Carne Asada tacos - not very creative on my part. Nice big chunks of tender meat that was well seasoned. Tasty corn tortillas... I bathed them in the rich flavors of the table salsa.

The menu is quite different and refreshing. The prices seemed reasonable. 

Would be a great place for a date, out of town guests, group meeting or ???

Enjoy mi Amigos!
Bad service, long wait, small portions for a $200 meal for two. Food is decent, drinks are decent.

First time here 
Chicken bites amazing 
Atmosphere fabulous 
Wait staff off the chain will I come back
Absolutely 
Are they recommended come 
Eat enjoy 
Happy hour rocks 
Don't walk run these guys are fun and the food is amazing
The food tasted terrible-- ordered several stiff but nothing tasted as the dish was named. Even the plain rice was not good. But the service is good.

We tried to go to Cafe Fleur de Lis for breakfast, but they were closed for the day due what appeared to be an emergency. I air boxed the sky because it's one of my favorite places to eat breakfast. This place is next door and it was raining cats and dogs, so we decided to wait the 30 minutes for them to open. Yelp showed us that all of our other faves had waits well over an hour.

The doors finally opened and we were the first seated and last served. How? I asked our server as well as the manager and they both told me that they didn't know why or how it happened. If you don't know, who does? No, really. Who?

My meal finally comes and has the nerve to be cold. It was this strange red beans and rice soup with a piece of andouille and fried chicken swimming in it. Who came up with this and why? Who asked for this? The beans lacked flavor and were soupy. I was suffering from the night before, so I tried to eat it. I couldn't get through it and left 3/4 of it. Hubs' pasta was a tiny portion and he said it lacked flavor. He ate it because he needed to. 

The manager stopped by and offered us a dessert. It was more of a punishment than a perk. The brownie was bland and the ice cream was meh according to my husband. My taste buds had been offended enough. I'll save my calories for Cafe Du Monde. 

It appears that this place is brand new. I can't say I'd give this place another try. There are amazing places to eat in the quarter. This is not one of them. Let my experience save you the time and energy.

When I want good coffee- I head to Lulu's. Love their iced vanilla lattes. Their espresso drinks are great but I was sadly disappointed in their brewed coffee. Their espresso drinks have me taking a sip and closing my eyes in appreciation for the depth of flavor, but their brewed coffee didn't do it for me, maybe I just needed it stronger. Haven't tried their food yet but look forward to it. It can get pretty crowded around lunch which makes it hard to study. I can't seem to find the perfect balance of study spots and good coffee around here just yet.
The guys from Brooklyn NY had a great time in BBQ ribs were the best ever, great portion nice bbq  sauce done right.Great time by all and fair prices.Great service and a excellent menu.

We stopped by for their outdoor beer week shindig. It was good for a quick beer but there wasn't too much excitement or socializing. The dj was playing some good music and the drafts were great and only $5 no matter what you ordered. I probably wouldn't go back for drinks with all the places to go in Philly but I hear the brunch is good so I might try that.

This place is amazing and serves delicious authentic food. We got the pasta special with pesto, penne vodka and tiramisu. The owner was so welcoming and we really enjoyed speaking with him. I see people's other reviews mentioning the decor but hello you are there for the food not the decor! Also anyone who has an Italian grandparent- this is how their house is decorated! I will definitely keep coming back and am so happy to have given them my business.

Atmosphere: super cute spot in Chinatown. They have steampunk like light fixtures, an old movie projector playing in the background, and cleanish. 
Drinks: it's really good considering the competition in the area. 
Food: this is where they lack finesse. I felt that they just put mayo in every roll. I found it to be overpowering to the actual taste of fish and rice. 
Service: slow slow slow

Got the goat korma dish, and was served tough and rubbery meat. I ended up sending it back and they came back with the same tough and rubbery meat. I felt bad for the waitress and still tipped her. I've eaten here before and the chicken is not that bad, but they definitely lost me as a customer

This is a delightful place. Everyone is very friendly and the salad I had last night was amazing. My hubby thoroughly enjoyed his seafood risotto as well. The only reason for four stars instead of five is the pomme frites were lukewarm when they brought it to my table and the veritable dearth of vegetarian items on the menu - but the fellow who was serving us assured me he could make any variety of items vegetarian if I desired. Also, the only table they had that would allow us to have our dog with us was right in the doorway which is not ideal but we would definitely return.

Fun and lively atmosphere at 6:30 on Wednesday evening.  Pretty busy , staff at upstairs bar was attentive with great dirty martinis.  I would not recommend the duck confit rigatoni,  was more like duck jerky and very salty.  Everyone else in our party enjoyed the grouper, scallops and tenderloin.  Tenderloin pizza appetizer was very good. Great staff.
Came for brunch and ordered The Crabby Shrimp omelet. It was incredible! Loads of crab, tender shrimp, delicious and creamy sauce. I would've licked my plate if I could have. Yum!

Where to begin; I've been coming here for years ordering the same exact thing every time I come. A chicken quesadilla, side of queso, 2 large bags of chips and 3 sides of steak on soft shells. It's a weird order, I know.
This visit was very different. They told me that if I get a quesadilla it has to have two sides, so I thought whatever I'll just get rice and beans if I have to, but it was the cashier who wouldn't ring it up as normal. I got charged for the sides that I didn't even ask for but was told I have to get. Then he wouldn't charge me for the 3 sides of steak, which typically comes up to around $11. Instead, he charged me for full orders of steak tacos. It jacked the prices up. I tried to explain that this isn't normal and it's literally just 3 sides of steak, I order it all the time but he said since it's on a shell and not in a bowl it's considered tacos, not sides of steak.

Just very frustrating to see my normal meal Jack up in price by $14. The chips were also surprising stale.

Wanted to grab a quick lunch before sending my daughter back to college so we dropped into Chilis for Soup salad lunch combo. Our waitress was enthusiastic and had a trainee in tote. The trainee was humble and sweet. I ordered the house salad with chicken tortilla soup and my daughter ordered the spring mix salad w chicken enchilada soup. The lunch included a generous portion of tortilla chips and salsa. The chips were a little greasy and the salsa watery but I shouldn't be eating chips anyway. The salads were ok. The spring mix salad was tastier with a citrus honey dressing and probably the healthiest thing we ordered. My soup was creamy w small bits of chicken and topped with tortilla chips and cheese.  Comfort food. We were offered additional helpings of both. The food was good for the price (inexpensive) and was served fairly quickly. I think they could leave off the chips. The trainee kept our glasses full of water which we needed as the food was salty.
There seemed to be a booming lunch crowd of business types also having the soup salad combo. We were able to pay at the table with a credit on a table top device that also had games on it which we did not play. I took a look at the kids menu for future reference and the healthiest options included fresh pineapple and salad.
The restaurant was clean.

This was my second visit to Popeyes, first visit got nuggets, not impressed. They were no better than any other fast food joint.
I was driving by on a Tuesday, and they advertise 2 pc dark meat for 99cents. So I got some of the Mild Chicken through the drive thru.
I was very impressed with the Flavor. I have always been a huge KFC chicken fan, but I actually think I prefer Popeyes. I got fast service in the Drive thru.  I don't know about anything else about the food here, but Tuesday is definitely a good deal.

They have now raised their price on Tuesday to 1.49 up from .99. So not as good a deal as it was.
Great location on the loop. The staff was very friendly and the food was great. Had the brisket chili and brisket meat and it was fantastic!

Went here for dinner for the first time on Easter Sunday. The food was subpar at best. Got a pizza and it came out cold. The restaurant itself dirty and dimly lit. The service was ok. The busser named cole did a very good job and was very helpful.

Some people will not like this opinion... but it's my opinion... so there!

A co-worker told me (before my trip to NOLA) that in his opinion, Cafe Beignet was better than ANOTHER very very very popular beignet locale... that being said, I and my merry band of traveling companions decided that the only way to judge for sure was to try both... and so we did.  Cafe Beignet won by a landslide.  Now, yes, they are both fried dough covered in powdered sugar which equals something amazing... but that's not the point.  These were decidedly lighter, fluffier, and had a satisfying slight crunch to the outside.  They get ALL of the praise and glory as the best beignets on our trip to NOLA, and I will be recommending this place to everyone headed that way!  Lovely!  Thank you!
Honestly the best boba I have ever had and is definitely better than Hana Kitchen!

Thank you, thank you, Thank you!!! 
I just hosted my grand daughters college graduation dinner here. A table of 4 and all the guests were just blown away. No sense going into greater detail the food, service and ambiance converged to make one of those unforgetable meals.

The bad news is my family expects to dine like this all the time.

Ok, this is a chain, but beer selection is excellent. Food is pretty good...dont make it complicated...But service was excellent...though it wasnt crowded  the recommendations were relative...I admit you've gotta be a beer a file to REALLY know beer and be spot on descriptive ...if you enjoy beer and simple well prepared food you will not go wrong...
Cozy, casual, study spot perfect for bringing a book & your dog - fav place to come still since moving home to LA, but always stop by when I'm in town! :)

I visited Local Public Eatery after a movie at the Cineplex and also the day of the last hockey game at Rexall ring. So the place was packed, but we were able to find a table without delay.
We started with Szechuan Edamame, covered with garlic chili sauce, toasted sesame and soy sauce, delicious. 
A press burger with cheddar and a portion of house salad. 
A tortilla soup with a little bit of pulled chicken, avocado and crispy tortillas
2 Baja Chicken Tacos without cabbage ( I don't like cabbage and the tacos tasted perfect)

The service was great, the server was friendly and always checking on us.
This is a good place for large groups, to celebrate birthdays or to watch a game.
Tons of space for parking, bathrooms were perfectly clean and it's location is perfect, close to the theater, shopping mall and main highways.
Great dining close to the beach. Perfect location and great food. Yummy onion rings. My husband loves their philly cheese steak sandwich. Bacon cheeseburger is simple but tasty.

Not happy. Ordered plain pizza and fries with whizz on side. A lot of the cheese slid off the pizza on it's way to me which made the barely edible pizza, inedible. The fries had whiz on the side AND on the fries. WRONG! Called to let them know and was promised fresh fries right away. Guess what........never came! I'll be dropping by after work tomorrow for a refund. I'll post the outcome

It's okay. Not the best place to eat. I usually go eat when my boyfriend wants to eat there burger. Be ready to order everything at once because its so hard to catch ur waitress after that. I ordered the salad, it was the worst salad I ever had. The chicken had no flavor at all. Milkshakes are good there. But the food takes a long time to come out.

Best pie in town. 
As a testament, if it's still great cold out of the fridge the next day, you know they're doing something right.
Small menu. Know what you want. Busy place. Friendly workers.  Try the soup of the day, in season.
Food was mediocre at best. It's byob, sat outside on Main Street. The service here is terrible, our waiter was mia the entire night.
This is probably one of the best barbecue chains in Tampa. The food was pretty good. The fries were delicious. I loved trying the different sauce options.  I will definitely be back!

We managed to get a reservation during Jazzfest weekend and it was a great meal.  We sat upstairs and everyone seemed very helpful and knowledgeable.  We order the rabbit appetizer and it was good.  They brought out 5 different kinds of delicious breads and we all got stuffed on that before we got our meals.  The server mentioned that they didn't have kids dishes but could do chicken fingers if we wanted but my daughter ordered the rabbit and gumbo and all was good.  We all had different dishes and each one tastes better and better.  I've wanted to try this place for a while and glad I finally did. After our meal we were too stuffed to try any deserts.  Maybe next time.

Customer service was really disappointing. The bartender seemed really stress and not aware when new customers are standing at the bar. Finally flagged him- he offered water and then said well get our order. Well we order some tasters and still no water. Wasn't until he grabbed a seat I went back to ask for the water. The bar didn't appear too busy.  Food didn't look appealing so we decide to just finish our beers and go downtown to a gastropub.

Cheeseburger Eddie's has a standard burger joint feel.  Plenty of tables and an extensive menu.  I do like that there is a selection of sides without an additional charge.  

My guest and I had a bacon cheeseburger and the crab burger.  I really wanted the gulf shrimp burger because it sounded wonderful, but alas, they were out of shrimp.  The crab cake burger was huge.  It was a lightly breaded crab pattie that was seasoned just right and went well with sweet potato fries.  I was told that the bacon cheeseburger was really good and it was a pretty good sized burger as well.  The service was very quick and it was pretty quiet even though we ate there around 12:30 PM.  

The outside seating looks really nice.  It's covered deck type of seating with ceiling fans to keep it comfortable.  I was actually surprised to see diners outside since construction is taking place in front of the restaurant.  Next time, I hope to dine outside since it has the comforts of eating indoors. =)

The only thing that was weird to me was the setup.  When you walk in, you think you are going to be acknowledged and asked to wait to be seated.  Wrong.  You will see a stand that you suspect to be "please wait to be seated" sign, however, it is a stand with 50 menus in it.  Upon review you walk ten steps to the register/bar and place your order.  Makes sense, but if this place is crowded, the line can extend outside the door.  The other thing is, people can enter from the side door, which creates confusion on who orders first because everyone stands in a general area or right in front of the bar to study the menu.  It would just make sense to place the menus on the table and people get in line and approach the clerk when ready from their table....that way, there is no risk of a fire code violation.  Win win, right?  However, I'm there to eat, not improve the experience, so hopefully, you're more patient than I am and have no issues on your way to the register.

This is hands down the best pizza I've ever had. Fantastic hand tossed dough and the freshest ingredients you'll ever find on a pizza pie. It's a refreshing change from the norm and since trying Mellow 5 years ago, I cant stand eating shitty delivery pizza. The pizza alone makes this restaurant top in it's class but throw the hippie influenced workers with a psychedelic 60's image and personality and you have the perfect recipe and ambience for a cool date night. And boys night out... Did I mention that they serve several dozens of hard to find beers from around the world.

Expect a long wait but definitely worth it. The fish tacos and grouper sandwiches should be top of the menu. Our kids ordered a few appetizers which were large enough for a meal. 

We did not have any beverages but there was a huge full bar with some very pretty fruity drinks being made.

Akio is my new favorite place to go for sushi. My husband and I have eaten here on two different occasions and were blown away both times. The food is gorgeous. Their selection is plentiful. You will be able to find something that piques your interest if sushi is your thing. The service and ambiance are also nice. It's not too fancy, but it's nicer than I expected for a place located in a strip mall. When I last visited, hubby and I got a vegetable gyoza appetizer, a special roll each, and a tempura fried banana for dessert. The price for all this was right in line with what was expected. Don't be fooled by the atmosphere...it's actually reasonably priced. The next time I want really good sushi I know where I will be going.
Best Cajun in town! I always get the pulled chicken wrap. It's so good, but massive and way too much to eat for lunch.

It has been a while but no one understands customer service like the Brennan family. I have never had a meal at Commanders that wasn't top notch. The service is impeccable. Every New Orleanian should eat here at least once.

Sooo freaking good. Definitely the best pizza by the slice place in Indy. I go here at least twice a week on my lunch break. :) The people that work here are super friendly, and they're so fast. I don't ever have to worry about long lines when they're busy.

What a nice change of pace with a fresh approach on the burrito market. This place is like Pei Wei meets Chipolte and every day after has been a holiday. Its also nestled into a comfy spot on California, just south of Russell Blvd. Good, clean, heathy fun in South City and I didn't have to use chop sticks... i used my hands! Thank you!

I'm almost hesitant to give this place 5 stars, but when I think back on my meal, every morsel from service, to seating, to food and drink were perfection!!!

We were a large group, midday on a Friday, which meant the restaurant was near-empty, and we were seated in a quaint little room with a large wooden table and sun-filled windows. Our server was casual and efficient with excellent recommendations.

The bread and olive oil with sun-dried (mash?) was outstanding. I had a late-day, perfectly spiced bloody-mary. 

We had the Salmon di Capri, which was really delicious. I've been into horseradish lately and was pleasantly surprised when I saw this combination on the menu. But it was subtle and well executed.

The Bruschetta was heaping with fresh tomatoes!

I had the Di Rucola e Parmiggiano and added shrimp ... just fantastic. Everything was so fresh, and the shrimp was warmed, added bonus for attention to detail.

Other highlights included the La Primavera, Pesto Rosso and the Lasagna.

I didn't have dessert or coffee, but my fellow diners seemed quite pleased.

Overall, Gulfport Florida is a sweet and cute little area I highly recommend.

this place was straight up amazing.  We had the watermelon/radish salad, the meat board, the pasta with asparagus/english peas/mushrooms/pancetta.  Every bite was delicious.  Service was on point and professional, attentive but not over the top.  salted caramel budino totally lived up to the hype.  price is very reasonable too.  you don't find many places like Barbuzzo in the US.

We are making the rounds to all the Jose Garces restaurants in the area. This was the second on the list. Linda picked as a V-day gift! 
Distrito did not disappoint. It is very trendy given the area. Set like an old style drive in movie. There are swing chairs next to picnic benches. Specials are up on the movie display signs. You feel transported to a chic NYC location.... That is until you leave and remember you are in Philly. We  chose from all the tapas to get a good selection of tastes.  Started off with guacamole it was good but still does not beat my favorite from NYC. Linda had the carna-Kobe soft tacos, I went for the recommended yellow tail hamichi tacos.( I did steal one of the Kobe tacos. They were both incredible.
we split a salad kind of like a Cobb salad with flar. Then we split a chicken enchilada and a pork tamale YuM YuM!!!! Churros and espresso completed the 
Meal. Everything was delicious. My only issue is with the small table where we were seated.  It was definitely an enjoyable time hoping to get some friends to venture into the city with us next time for margarita and sangria pitchers. BTW- white sangria is awesome.

Hands down the best steak I've ever eaten. Not gonna lie, the entrance is hard to find and basically hidden behind a tree. When you knock, they open a window in the door and ask if you have a reservation before letting you in. Seemed kind of gimmicky but I understand them only taking people with reservations so as not to crowd the restaurant. The space was very intimate and warm. They were late with our reservations so they gave us some free champagne, which was nice. Also a waiter spilled a tray right by our feet, and they gave us a free appetizer even though we didn't say anything. Waiter was attentive and courteous. Tomahawk steak was definitely the best on the menu. We probably tried every single dessert on the menu and they were all phenomenal. Bottles of wine are expensive. I opted for two whiskey cocktails and they are much stronger than they taste. Overall one of the best dinners I've had, and worth the price.

I made a yelp account just to write a review on this restaurant. The service was so shockingly horrible that it took us well over an hour just to get dinner. The waiter asked us THREE times what we ordered just to write up a check for us. The drinks we got were so delayed and so warm that they ended up having to just not charge us for them. The people sitting behind us straight up got up and left after making a comment about how bad the service is here on a regular basis. Food was alright, but not even close to being worth it. Good luck, everyone.

Been here 3 times just to get beers, nice outside bar & seating plus they have Bud Select in bottles, may be the only reason I drop by to get a Select. Never had their food & never had a problem with anyone of the bartenders, they always seems attentive. Will go back & may be try their food.

My friend and I checked this spot out for lunch today and what a delicious meal we both had. There was no wait and we were promptly seated. Plenty  of choices with the menu;  I was torn between the breakfast and lunch options. I went with the classic cobb salad and my friend chose the breakfast burrito.  My salad was enough for 2 and all the ingredients were fresh and flavorful. I took 1/2 home to enjoy later. No complaints with the breakfast burrito. Reasonable prices. Cash only. I would definitely be back.
This place is awesome and super beautiful. The price is perfect for high quality. Handmade with care and they taste amazing! I wish I got more to take home! I will be back for sure!

First off, there was a plethora of drunken, loud golfers. That should have been a clue. Not impressed with my first dinner for my first stay at this JW Resort restaurant. 
My niece spilled water and we used our cloth napkins to clean it up. Our waitress was nowhere to be found so we got fresh napkins from another table. When we finally did track her down, we told her we had spilled and showed her the napkins and asked for more water. She brought the water. Those wet napkins sat on the table the entire meal.
Then my pulled pork sandwich arrived with ice cold meat and no barbecue sauce. I've never had pulled pork without barbecue sauce.  I never been served one cold either. We had already waited an eternity for our food & couldn't find the waitress, so I ate the coleslaw & chips. A hamburger ordered medium rare was served pretty darn rare.  It also took  30 minutes to get a beer while they changed the keg. (Drunken golfers?) Do yourself a favor, go out of the resort for dinner.

The restaurant doesn't look very appealing from the outside, but I feel that is part of it's own appeal. The beer list (the beer bible) is tremendous and I've also heard that they offer tours of their beer cellar.

I always get the mussels.  They are about 6 varieties of the mussels and they all come with fries and this AMAZING dip. (don't really know what's in it)  I've also had the Spanish Flies, which are these crazy spicy and crazy huge wings.  Warning - these wings can burn your tongue and ruin your dining experience for the rest of the night.
The BEST pizza! Very small menu, but everything is delicious. I generally like topping on my pizza, but the best way to enjoy the red pie at Gennaro's is plain. Cash only and BYO.

I have been here several for both brunch and dinner, and both times my experience was fantastic.  My main complaint is the price - even though the quality of the food was very good, I'm not quite sure it was THAT GOOD (Cafe Ponte, for example, has lower prices on their food and I find that the quality between the two is comparable).  I imagine the extra $$ is for the view.  I can handle that. 

For the most bang for your buck (but still a huge chunk out of your wallet) is the brunch.  While extravagantly expensive (at that same price - or cheaper - you can go to the Wynn Buffet in Vegas and have the best buffet of your life), if you have the resilience and persistence of a person deadset on getting their money's worth (aka me) you can make this brunch worth the price. Things to do to get ready: 1) exercise in the morning or the night before to get that hunger up, and free up that stomach space.  2) But going to a buffet on a purely empty stomach is a big no-no. Be sure to eat a little something so that you can stretch out your stomach to fit in more. And 3) Get someone to DD because nothing gives you more for your money than bottomless champagne and bloody marys.

That being said, the all you can eat brunch is filled with tons of amazing stations: pasta station, omelet station, seafood station (raw oysters, shrimp cocktails, yum yum!), breakfast station, and an entire room filled with dessert. 

I would say that the brunch at Oystercatchers is a go-to must for anyone in Tampa.  It might not be reasonable to come here on a regular basis, but everyone should try this place at least once.

AMAZING service!!!  Surely our waitress was the restaurant owner, as she saw my wife and I skeptical scoping the place out.  She came outside to greet and invited us in to the only available table.  There was a rather noisy community meeting going on directly next to us, and without being asked, as soon as another table opened up our waitress moved us to a quieter area.

The food was phenomenal compared to the price.  Very welcoming and homey feel.

Great food, huge servings....and I mean HUGE.  These guys put Cheesecake Factory to shame!  Knishes were the only bad thing we had.  Kreplach and Latkes were amazing...and the noodle Kugel was phenomenal.  The Reuben was large and in charge.

We ordered a PIECE of German Chocolate Cake to go.  The  waiter told us not to get two slices and that 1 would feed us both with more to spare.  Took the cake home, weighed it on my shipping scale....any guesses how much it weighed?







The slice of cake was 2.8 lbs.

Waiter also gave us 4 cookies since it was my girlfriends birthday.


WOULD COME AGAIN....and AGAIN....and AGAIN!  TRUE NY-style deli.

Not terrible, not great. Pretty solid. Service is pretty hit or miss. We had a subpar waitress. Our salads were fine. Chicken caesar salad and fajita salad were good. 
Our table was near the kitchen and theres a double door that separates the kitchen from the public. We could hear the servers and bussers talking shit about eachother, the customers and their heavy periods. 
You guys might want change that design flaw or just have them stand somewhere else...
Orange Blueberry pancakes- on the 100 best places to eat for breakfast. GREAT FOOD ON THE BEACH!

Really simple to the point a lil dressed up but yes...yes...yes...sandwiches
Made well. Grilled cheese looks like they have down to an art. Slaw was perfect fries flavorful but I like mine crispier. I prob could've asked. I got ranch dressing for dipping fries and that was perfect and I think made fresh there. I want to go back again

I like this place. There is a little bit of everything: bao buns, steak; seafood, pasta, ribs. 
I tend to go at night sit at the bar order a couple of drinks and appetizers. But the other night my BF and I decided to have dinner here. He ordered the ribs, they were good and the meat was so tender it fell off the bone, the ribs were full of meat and a good size rack (no skimping here). I ordered the Tavern steak it comes with mashed potatoes and carrots plus mushrooms. The steak was ok, the ribs had more flavor I think it was the tangy sticky q. But overall everything was good and the portions are decent.  

They also have daily specials which are worth checking out.

I thought I hated guacamole until I had it here; these people do the work of angels. I'm a carne girl and can't say enough good things about it. I won't though because I would sob uncontrollably if all of you began ordering it and they ran out while I was there for dinner. The portions guarantee you're taking leftovers home, the service is good and did I mention the guacamole? Never disappointed.

Great shakes but the burgers are getting thinner and thinner every day. The triple is touted as 1/3 pound pre-cooked weight (about 1/4 pound after cooking) which means each patty is less than 2 ounces and after cooking about 1.3 ounces. They are doIng this to keep from raising their prices but they should raise their prices and keep their reputation for quality. I've been a fan for years, but it's better to have slightly higher prices to maintain the integrity of your brand than to lower the quality to keep prices down.
May be the best tamales in Tucson, and the sides are great.  The burritos look good also,  but I am full.

Service was great.  Went in to order my dinner.  I asked for a suggestion on a burger and the Brisket Burger was recommended.    I got that, some tator tots, and a Carmel shake. 

Sandwich was so so.  Didn't care for the bun, so I ate the brisket and bacon, which were good.  Tots with a little catsup was good.   Shake was good, but on the thin side....too much milk. 

Should've had a regular burger on a regular bun

Went there for dinner with the wife last night because she was wanting French Onion soup.  She got that and loved it.  I got the French Onion soup and a chicken salad sandwich.  Delicious!  The bread for the sandwich was extremely fresh and tasty. The service was great.  I recommend this place and look forward to going back and trying other dishes.

Was never a huge steak fan, ever. And then I received a gift card here and now I'm hooked. Love it, love it, love it.  The salad bar is huge, stocked, and phenomenal. The steak is juicy and absolutely amazing (ask for extra au jus, it's totally worth it). I'm not a huge drinker, so the alcohol prices don't really affect me. I really enjoy this place and the service staff is pretty great, especially the bus boys. The wait can be long on popular dinner nights, but for steak like this, you'll know why. Yum!

Our Favorite Neighbourhood Sandwich Shop! 

Me and my Husband frequent this place ALOT! They have the best BLTS in the City hands down. So much bacon and such friendly service!!! The Rueben Sandwich and donairs are also worth trying. Soooo good  We will keep coming here for a long time and continuing to recommend it to all our friends!

I've never been to a place that felt more like home and truly embodied 'Philadelphia' the way Perch Pub did. This place was where I came with REAL friends and family to drink good beer, play pool, and catch-up with some of the city's best bartenders. While everyone offered top tier service, it was James who consistently went above and beyond. Thank you sir for sharing your amazing stories, beer choices and friendship! After I moved away from Philadelphia, it became even more of a treat to visit Perch with family and friends and re-live that experience. I hope the owners are working towards re-opening in another location, even if it's under a different namesake. Perch was legendary and legends never die. Thank you for being my favorite Philadelphia Bar. Cheers!
It's smallllllll. Food is great though and you get plenty of it. Wouldn't take a large group over 6-8 I'd say even that would be large. Really good food

I really like it here! it's close to my house so I've stopped in a couple of times now. they've got a great turkey sandwich - I love sprouts. I also had a pan seared fish dish w buerre blanc that was pretty tasty and v reasonably priced. it still kinda has that new-ish feeling like a little bit bland and not settled in yet or something, but everyone is very nice and I plan on coming here routinely. 

I've yet to thoroughly investigate but there's also charcuterie and cheeses available for sale independent of the food menu. 

a great addition to the area.

Great pizza and great service. I've ordered pizza twice in as many weeks and it's fantastic. Best pizza in town and the service has been way above expectations. I ordered curbside each time and they have staff wearing masks outside running back and forth bringing the food to your car. Very organized. Will definitely be my go to pizza joint!

the service was horrible , the server was overwhelmed ,no manager could be found we started with appetizers and the server got lost or something then it took forever for our food , then they took our payment and when they came back asked if we were ready to pay , what duh the food was actually pretty good , but the service being so bad i wont be back .

I parked right in front of the restaurant and a staff person came out and yelled at me for parking then berated me about how long I was going to be there. My son attends music next door and I had planned on catching a solo bite to eat at Mythos while he had his lesson. Instead the utter rudeness of the Mythos staff completely turned me off of dinning there. The Mythos staff missed turning the increase of visitors to the strip mall into an opportunity and created an unwelcome and angry vibe dissuading people from checking them out.

Place sucked! They use mayo to reduce cream cheese! Also rolls are huge larger than .50 piece! The only good thing is the included appetizers! Oh also rolls real loose and fall apart! I hope the Korean food is better!
We tried to go to Charlie's. But they had a $30 cover charge per person because of a band and they were having. Doubt it will ever go back because of that

An ABSOLUTE YES!!!!!
Famous for their Sonoran Hot Dogs: oo la la!!
Try the Caramelos!!! Super yummmy carne!!!
Will never swing thru Tucson without stopping here!!!

Mediocre food and service, at best. The location of Cafe Pontalba is what gives it foot traffic but I'd rather spend the extra few dollars at Tableau across the street to have great food AND excellent service!

While I felt that the price should have yielded slightly higher quality fish, I did enjoy my lunch here.  There side salad is a nice portion, although I prefer ginger or carrot dressing.  The nigiri was okay (I had Japanese snapper and Unagi), and the roll I had was tasty (New York roll if I remember correctly).  I wasn't very excited about the hand roll--it was bigger than it should have been.  
Bottom line: it wasn't too bad, but not my favorite sushi, especially for the price.

Great spot for brunch. Love the patio and enjoy the biscuits and gravy quite a bit. 

Show up early, almost always a 45 min wait
Way better than Clw location. Will make the drive here instead. Philly Cheese calzome and spinach dip is awesome!!
Great pizza!  I love the fresh mozzarella slice, it's yummy!

They have amazing handmade pasta. Please do yourself a huge favor and go here. They are a byob spot however they do have a bar so it's ok if you didn't bring anything. The Cacio e Pepe and bolognese were AMAZING. Phenomenal!

I brought my friends here, on separate occasions I brought my family and everyone was impressed. The food is delicious and I mean all of it. 
Just had to update this review, so like I said this place is amazing, I feel like family there. The dishes that they serve in are also beautiful, my rice comes in a heart shape, they cut carrots into flowers the service is phenomenal what else can I ask for?  

So I'm sick right now and my mother said she is gonna door dash me and my son Rayshawn food for a week OMG! I am sooo loved :)

We went there after visiting Marigny several times.  The service was good, but the food was so-so.  I had the barbecued shrimp, and they were extremely small-pretty much popcorn shrimp.  My wife had the redfish, and that left a lot to be desired.  Way too fishy, almost oily.  You can do better in New Orleans.
This is a great little lunch spot! Spicy gyro was amazing! Very friendly staff. They even let me hang out for a few hours while I worked. Highly recommend this place!

Went to this Panda Express and stood in line for 30 minutes. The orders of the customers ahead of me had been lost....meaning the employees were so confused and there was no order or efficiency to the process that the customers were missing orders and orders were mixed up.

To make matters worse, the employees moved with no urgency. They acted as if they had just rolled out of bed. The food was not being cooked at the same rate it was leaving the restaurant. As a result, customers had to wait a long time because their selected dish in the buffet was empty. 

Noticing this failure to cook food before it ran out, me and my sister selected what was available so we wouldn't have to wait an additional 30 minutes. 

I gave it one star because the food was actually good but I would never go back!

I really enjoyed this place! The lattes were delicious! The prices are very reasonable. My 12oz latte was less than 5$. We tried the lavender latte and the mayan mocha. They were both great. They had alternate dairy free milk options as well. I had the toast and eggs, and the eggs we cage free, which I appreciated it.  

The environment was clean. Dogs are welcome on the patio. 

The only question we were left with was whether we should bus the tables or leave them dirt? 

We will definitely be returning the next time we visit tucson.

Jet's is a good choice when you have people that just cannot agree on what kind of pizza is best.  They offer both thin and thick crust and have a variety of choices AND they are probably one of the better choices if you are buying budget pizza.  I don't mean this as a bad thing but just basic pizza to grab and go.  It is not a ladies night out sipping cocktail type of pizza.  This is hearty, tasty, affordable and I have had nothing but positive experiences at this establishment.

One of the best rated pho places around Nashville. Coming from a huge Vietnamese community with a ton of options, I was disappointed by the pho. Personally I thought the broth was a bit bland and not as flavorful as I'm use to. 

The service is more like a take out, dine in option. You pay first and grab a table after. Servers bring out the food but essentially that's it.

Great Korean food with the feel of an authentic gimbap nara. I've been to this place a few times and have liked everything I've had. The prices are also decent and as inflated as other Korean places in the city.

It's been a while since we've been out to Sasquatch but it is as good as I remembered it being. This little bar/restaurant is spot on.  The atmosphere, the service, the food. Everything comes together for a great experience. Even my picky eater devoured the cheeseburger sliders and French fries without a complaint in the world. My burger was perfectly cooked at medium rare and had massive amounts of grilled onions on top of perfectly toasted sourdough. So good. My husband was also very impressed with the Dog Valley Tacos and was shocked by how huge they were! You definitely don't leave this place hungry!!  The seating is limited but the charm of a close knit restaurant makes you forget all about the wait, it's definitely worth it.

I don't know what's up with all of the negative reviews.  The staff was ok and the cream puff was heavenly creamy richfullness.  My fruit tart was pretty good too.  The pasterys run between $2-&6.  They're a diner too.  My coffee was pretty good.  I'm from orlando were every dinner serves Folgers or Maxwell so I feel spoiled to be served something better.  The breakfast was good.  $5 For a pile of scrambled eggs, potatos and buscuit and homemade perserves. (the best perserves i've ever had in my entire life!!)

I've been here twice now. I've only ordered coffee and pastries so far. I ordered the cinnamon vanilla latte which was delicious ! The red velvet cookies and almond joy cookies are great too. I will come back and try breakfast and/or lunch. Everyone is friendly here also. I would recommend this place .

We indulge on Rib Rack a few times a month . Wings for take-out, ribs eat-in.  I cannot eat wings or ribs ANYWHERE else without being disappointed, they're that good. Prices are great for the quality of the food!!

Happened to be in the area and hungry for lunch.  
Located at the old 73 circle (where Olga's used to be, or well still is kinda) Ragazzi's is nestled in a small shopping center in Marlton.  We stopped in for a quick bite on a Saturday afternoon during our shopping day.
The menu was large, I had a difficult time at first deciding what to choose, I always do when the menu's are so large at some places, but I settled on a tuna hoagie and it was delicious.  The roll was fresh and tuna was good, not all crunchy and weird like some places.
Staff was efficient and friendly.
Wife had a cheese steak and french fries and she said it was quite tasty.
This is a nice sit down type of place, next time we'll go for the pasta and try the soups that I hear are very good.

We will return.

Reservations only though you can sit at the oyster bar and enjoy the full menu. Everyone was so nice including everyone working at the oyster bar we felt at home. The catfish was amazing!! Definitely will go back there service was top notch.

Ahhh...what's not to love about dining alfresco!  Especially when the temps just right and you're having lunch with your besties.

The minute we arrived we beelined it straight to the patio. I don't even remember saying anything to the hostess...other than smiling and motioning to the patio as she smiled back and gave us a thumbs up.

It was really quite lovely out there.  The tables were nicely spaced (always a good thing when your gearing up for some good girl talk) and the large market umbrellas were a plus as the sun peeked in and out of the clouds. There was also an outdoor bar which was super cool to see.

As soon as we grabbed a table and got situated, our waitress promptly greeted us with menus, told us about the lunch specials of the day and took our drink orders. When she returned, I decided on the Strawberry Balsamic Chicken Salad (Mixed greens, thinly sliced grilled chicken, grapes, spicy pecans, Gorgonzola, herb vinaigrette) and my gfs got the Lobster Bisque and a Wedge Salad.

YUM!  All so delish!  My friend raved about her Lobster Bisque and I loved my choice in salads...it was such a fresh and tasty combo...my tastebuds savored every single bite!

Bottom line...dining al fresco with your besties is the best. But enjoying great food and convo all while getting friendly and attentive service? That's the bestest! ;-)
Place is literally empty with a 35 minute wait. BS asked to sit at the bar. But no. No one sitting there either

Brilliant food... The lamb/beef skewer is one of the tastiest things I've eaten IN LIFE. I marveled at all of the Russian pop/techno Christmas music videos they played throughout our lunch. Mind you, it's October. Still, I found the odd, out of placeness of it all kind of charming. Oh, and the sweet/spicy tomato sauce that goes with the meat pancake? WE ARE HOARDING IT. I want to buy a gallon of it and use it on everything I ever eat for the rest of my life. The waiter was rude and unenthusiastic but I just pretended he was playing the character of a stoic Russian military leader who got forced into restaurant duty. He could've been 40% ruder and it still would not change my mind about this place. Will take everyone I know there. Next time we will bring vodka. Woohoo!

This is just one of those places that demands the authentic visit from a foodie nerd. It's around eight miles outside Nashville, but worth the Uber ride for that long wait for some very interesting fried chicken. By comparing my wait to that of others, I think I came out pretty lucky. We arrived at about 2:15 or so, 15 minutes after they opened. Luckily the line was confined to the inside of the place, and not out the door, as so many others have described. In one of my pictures the line seems long, but it's actually longer. When you get close to the ordering counter it switches to the right and loops back. It's slow to be sure, as they make everything to order, and everyone is ordering. The line was about 35 minutes, with another 30 waiting for my number to be called out. They hand you a sack with the fried chicken wrapped in wax paper, full of grease and a sticker identifying the heat level. Apparently this is very important, as the heat can be pretty damaging to most. If you eat there, be sure to ask for plates, as they do not readily offer them. 

The chicken: Now this really is good chicken, but it is also very unusual, in that the spices are fairly intense, without being too hot up front. It's a slow build burn that catches up to you by the fourth or fifth bite, building to a nose-running, whole mouth fire that has staying power. This was my experience with the "hot" leg quarter, which came topped with a couple of pickle chips and sat on two slices of white bread, perhaps toasted at some point, but steamed to a soft, subtly spicy platform to take in the extra grease, making it quite good on its own. 

The other chicken: My brother had the "medium," which he enjoyed very much, but did state that he could have handled a level higher. I agreed, and would myself go the "xhot" next time, not minding destroying myself for the experience, which is exactly what happened to him later that evening. Think... five plus trips to the bathroom that night, lingering suffering into the morning. 

My wife had the "mild" with no ill effects, and declared her chicken the best she'd ever had, and we've all eaten at New Orleans' Willie Mae's Scotch House a few times, so that's really saying something. I tried hers, and it was some very tasty chicken with just the right texture to the skin, which I could eat a whole plate of all by itself. 

Slaw: Just slaw. It was nice having it with the chicken, but I wished I had remembered to order a side of pickle chips.

Fries: nicely seasoned but not crispy. Wife absolutely loved them, while I don't care for a too limp fry.

Prince's isn't located in the nicest of areas, and the restaurant isn't sparkling clean, but the character of the place can't be beat. Old locals storytelling about being ruined by the medium chicken, a homeless fellow stinking of urine walking around asking for money, concerned eating faces concentrating on the danger of their meals, and a vibe of intense contentment. What a great experience.

Eh. The steak pho is OK, but there's much better to be had around town. The green curry chicken was flavorless. Not sure what part of the chicken was being served, but several pieces were inedible. The egg rolls were very good & fresh. Very expensive - $30 for two people for lunch We probably won't be back.

This diner holds a special place in my heart.  I've been here about a million times during the span of my 24 and a half years on this earth, and I've never had a bad experience.  Some of the best diner waitresses in the world work here (some, not all).  And maybe I'm just a lucky orderer, but I can't recall a meal I didn't enjoy thoroughly.  Their breakfast is especially delicious (I love their "Hungry Lady" special, I hope it's still called that).  The french toast is amazing because they bake the bread for it themselves.  

It's just a diner, not gourmet cuisine by any means, but as far as diners go, this is one of the best, so that's why I'm giving them all five stars.

Went here to sample as a Yelp elite event. 
Then I realized OMG this wasn't just another middle eastern spot but a solomonov israeli eatery. How did I miss out on this place?
So I've come back again. They need an app like at Goldie so I can build on the rewards from draining my bank by eating all of their stuff... now I'm craving K'Far pastries again 
I haven't tried any of their meat dishes but I loved the eggplant-Sabich, and the cauliflower shawarma and was recommended from all the salads the carrots and chickpeas as was told they are in limited rotation. 
I was browsing my cookbooks Zahav and Israeli Soul and see so much of the menu can be recreated made at home too. 
My Moroccan friend was super happy with this place and it is well worth the $10 for sandwiches and $5 for salads. 
The pitas were stuffed generously with cucumber salad or cabbage and the sauces paired deliciously with the ingredients. 
I didn't miss meat at all. The only thing I wished I had was a Tehina shake from Goldie to go with this 
I will be back when craving more!

A great breakfast spot with a nice,  clean vibe. Loved the soft and delicious cinnamon roll. The hash browns were perfectly crisp. 

It's so refreshing to see the beautiful smiles of all the staff. We will be back!

The faculty club was great. They were prompt with email replies and was very flexible. I was able to change the dinner table set up to match what I needed. They set up the table cloths for me the night before and also allowed me to bring other stuff in two nights before. The food was delicious and my husband and I were able to come for a tasting before. The staff poured wine promptly all night and friendly. Good price for the quality we received with no hidden fees. Highly recommend people to have their wedding here. There inside upstairs room was a beautiful spot for our inside ceremony as Edmonton weather is unpredictable.

I ordered delivery and it was faster than expected which is nice.  However, the food was over-cooked, so everything was just brown, the broccoli, the green beans and not appetizing to look at. The shrimp were small and as overcooked as the vegetables.
Still searching for good Thai food in Philadelphia.

I will review on the service because I strongly believe this is as important, if not more, than the food. I am one that goes back for take out rather than sit down if the service is lousy. With the Beast, this will probably be the case moving forward. 
Here is my experience. So I and the misses are on our vacation and thought it would be a grand idea to try the Beast BBQ since we were in the area. It was at the tail end of lunch time so not a full house. Mind you this is our first time here so was not sure which end of the building is dining and which was self serve bar type. Went in and was greeted by a young lady believe name is Breanna or something around that name. W
Am not sure cause someone else yelled her attention by name. So anyway, she asked with a friendly greeting "dine in or take out". This should have been when I chose take out but, instead, said,"dine in". She led us to the counter which you have to order before any of your party members sit. No big deal cause we have been to Pappy's in St Louis. ( THIS PLACE BY NO MEANS CAN COMPARE TO PAPPY's). As soon as she gets behind the counter to take our order, the switcharoo personality changes. She became less friendly and more annoyed. Again, this is our first time and not familiar with the menu so we had to scan and think for a moment. She seem annoyed that she had to wait. This was at the tail end of lunch and we are the only ones in line. No one was behind us. I asked a question and received a negative attitude. There's this huge menu behind her and she seemed annoyed that she had to be questioned instead of me reading the menu. The wife could not make up her mind cause the menu look so good. The worker just looked away in disgust. I almost thought she may have rolled her eyes is the reason she looked away. She did not make any recommendation or assisted at all in helping us decide. She kept silent. No smiles!!!!! 

Ordered seated and waited for the meal. I was glad to get away from her. I thought she was gonna grow horns and spit fire at us. Now from that experience came an angel in servant clothing. This lady, much older, brought out our meal with a pleasant smile and checked on us every so often. Okay, she may have been the waitress and was her job to do so but at least she played her role correctly. The one behind the counter forgot she was working as a customer service and a representative of The Beast establishment. 

I hope and pray management reads this and have a talk with her. Shame cause I truly enjoyed the food. Brisket was dry but wife loved the pork steak.

Best music venue in Philadelphia. 

I previously hadn't been here in almost 15 years to see Oasis with my cousin. With that said, and at that age, couldn't appreciate such an awesome place to see a show. 

I appreciate and prefer smaller venues over larger stadium shows and festivals. It's significantly better to see a band in a more intimate setting. The decorative and ornate nature of the theater feels like you've stepped back in time and there's not a bad seat in the house, literally. Transportation to and from couldn't be simpler via the MFL line with a 2 minute walk from 69th St Station to the venue. A stop pre or post show at the Waterford Inn is also a must.

HAIM rocked. Completely surprised and impressed.
Awesome food, cool atmosphere! Didn't expect it to be as good as it was because it's very unsuspecting from the outside! We'd visit again next time we're in town!

I have driven up and down Olive a countless number of times, and the bright, bold red neon sign "Ocha" has always caught my attention. Yet sadly I had never checked them out until last week. My visit at Ocha can be summed up as this: good sushi, good cocktails, good prices, and great service.

I was in the mood for a cocktail and sushi, and unfortunately had just missed their happy hour, which ends at 6pm. I was in the mood for something fruity with rum, and asked my waitress for pineapple and orange juice with rum. The waitress took my order and soon after, she came back to my table with a guy who worked there. He politely said that he wasn't sure what I was asking for and asked me to clarify. I told him I just wanted something fruity with rum. He then offered to put grenadine in it with the juices I had requested and I accepted. My drink was great and I appreciated how friendly both of them were and how courteous they were to make sure that they understood what I wanted so that I'd enjoy my cocktail. 

For my dinner I ordered an Angel sushi roll and a basic California roll. I found it interesting that Ocha offers two different types of Cali rolls - one with "real" crab meat and a regular one that was cheaper which it's safe to assume has imitation crab meat. I ordered the cheap one. Eh, who am I trying to impress, right? Both rolls were great.

The restaurant is very clean and spacious and there are TVs throughout the restaurant to watch. I will definitely come back to get more sushi, check out the happy hour, and to try other items off of their extensive menu.

Got a to go order today. Little hole in the wall. Clean. Very friendly staff. Got a cheese omelet and rye toast. Hard to mess that up, but I did say well done and it wasn't quite there. Good prices. I'll go again.

The band was good, but the servers and the incessant "get a drink now" in broken russian was the phrase that would marr an OK evening at a fairly generic off bourbon street bar. Not a fan. Very smoky and expensive drinks comparatively.

The food was so great! We smelt the food first as we got there (smelled amazing) but even before we got our food, Tadarius greeted us and recommended the mac and cheese. He did NOT disappoint! Sooo good. George got me my food and I told him "what ever you would get, I'll take it." I was not disappointed at all. The potion sizes were great too! I'd give it 6 stars if I could.

I drive past Blind Owl a lot and most every time I pass the parking lot is busy! This must say something about this establishment. I have very much enjoyed both visits. They have their own brewed beers and few other on tap. The bar is impressively designed and I enjoy the decor and surroundings. The food may be a tad overpriced for mostly bar type food. They do have a few specialty meals but I have yet to try them. Overall, I really like Blind owl and have enjoyed both experiences. I think this area needed a Brewery and a good place to eat or watch a game. Try the honey brown! They have their own beehive and use the honey when brewing the beer.
Great dinner and brunch!  Vibrant atmosphere and friendly staff.  I LOVE the mushroom tarte!

This trip was our first time in New Orleans. We hit the French Quarter and did the tourist thing. I wasn't impressed with the incredibly expensive experience, nor the homeless population or the outrageous filth. However we did find this little gem on our last night. Thank you to Corine of Ugly Dog  to give us a reason to actually come back. The food was delicious with the exception that the stuffing was missing from the stuffed chicken but the bar service was great.  We didn't make a fuss about the problem with our food because we didn't realize it until we got back to the hotel. I would recommend double checking your food but it was good. The smoked sauage and the jambayla was delicious but always check your food! Given the price, quality of food ( very good), and service, we we're very satisfied.

Decent. I would come again if it was the only breakfast place in town... however its not. The patrons stared us down as we came in. The restaurant wasnt very busy and we were waited on right away. Big menu. Slightly over priced. Ordered the eggs over medium and and hashbrowns extra done. The eggs were hard and hashbrowns soft, so not as ordered. The pancake was huge but was not cooked in the middle . My coffee was almost empty until we looked for my waitress then she got up from sitting. Then the check was not added right it was 6 bucks over and I don't know if they would have corrected it, if we were not already checking... This place was a bust for us. Try your luck but there are better places very close by.

Ive been coming here for years my brother introduced me to the place since he knows that I love Jamican Food and whenever Im in town coming from Sarasota its worth the stop but the last time I was there was very disappointed in the meal that I order Jerk chicken and it used to taste like Jerk and now her "Son" or Nephew is cooking now taste like just Gravy was pissed because I spent over $10 on that meal to be disappointed well will try the Golden Krust I hear that got good real authentic food

I have been eating at the Taj Cafe on downtown State for several years. Over time food at the Taj has changed in quality much like at any restaurant. When I first started eating at the lunch buffet here in 2004 I was impressed with the solid variety and sauce and meat quality but saw some downturn after a couple years. More recently, however, since early 2008 I have been most impressed with the quality of almost every item in the buffet.

The highlight has been the vegetable korma which uses large chunks of vegetables and potato. The sauce of the korma is really well spiced and balanced with level of cream. In combination with some of their excellent garlic naan and basmati rice it is crave-worthy and has been the focus of many lazy Saturday brunches. Their curries have similarly improved using large tender chunks of white chicken meat which I look forward to each time.

The buffet has an excellent variety with a thorough salad bar and many excellent desert options. The rice pudding is subtly spiced and goes perfectly with their irresistable carat desert (Gajar ka Halwa). Other options include sliced melon and those brown colored dumplings of dried milk and flour soaked in sugar syrup (Gulaab Jamun).

Forget ordering items from the menu as the buffet has plenty variety at a reasonable price. Bring a big appetite and friends you want to impress.

Best Italian food....even better then carrabas! 
So glad I tried this restaurant using Uber eats!
Nice atmosphere. Awesome service. A little pricy but I loved that they had a full bar and a good selection of wine. So delicious. I love sushi !
The food here was very good and the portions large... you definitely get your money's worth! Kind of a strange vibe and decor but the service and seating were excellent. Bring your own wine, though.

Came here on a late Saturday night and it was pretty lively, but not packed at all. we were visiting from NY and staying a few blocks away, and saw that this local Mexican spot had great reviews, so we decided to check it out! both me and my bf ordered the 3 tacos set; i had  the chicken and steak tacos, whereas my bf had the more adventurous beef head, tongue, and tripe. i enjoyed my steak taco a lot, but the chicken tacos left a little to be desired... just a tad bland but i still enjoyed it. i took a bite of the beef head and it was tender and juicy! we also ordered a side of guac (because, duh) and they did it right. perfect texture and a small kick of spiciness.

The best part about this place is that they serve the mexican juice Boing! i LOVE these juices and the mango flavored one is sooo good. i wanted to try the flan but we were so full by the end of our meal that we decided not to. 

One gripe about this place is that the menu prices are not up to date. we were surprised to see everything we ordered was $1-$2 more on the bill (ex, tacos were advertised at $9, but we were charged $11). please update your menus!

Their Mac Daddy was delicious as well as their pancakes. Their staff was friendly and always checked in on us to see how we were doing. I also ordered their orange juice and it tasted amazing. Overall, I liked it there. I just hope that next time I go, there won't be so many people.

Much better burger than places that claim to have great burgers.  Fresh ground and made exactly the way i wanted- very unusual. And the burgers are legitimate size- if it says 1/3 pound it really is that size not some shrunken shriveled up piece of meat.

What a welcome addition to Fountain Square, and to Indy.  

Our server  (Who we recognized as working at another local restaurant previously) took his time explaining the menu to us.  We didn't feel rushed at all, and felt like the staff really appreciated that we chose them for lunch.

Our burgers were cooked to perfection, the toppings were plentiful, and I must say, those are some of the best fries I've ever tasted.

Their choice of music fits the atmosphere, and we really appreciated the fact that it was loud enough to hear, yet not loud enough to interfere with normal conversation.

A great selection of drinks, fantastic food, and top notch staff.  I highly recommend it.

The food truck came to our neighborhood for take out Thursday. We ordered 4 pulled pork sandwiches with chips. Wait was 5-8 minutes. They were delicious. Nice tender juicy pork.  BBQ sauce was very tasty. Not enough sauce but that can be easily remedied. None of us could finish our sandwiches. ( yay leftovers for tomorrow!) buns are just basic and not near big enough for all the pork they gave us but considering how much pork there was I'm cool with that. 
Will definitely eat from this truck again.
Love this place! We love the make your own stir fries. Been coming here for at least 6 yrs!

The food here is amazing... I've tried many different po-boys they have and they are all great!
The crawfish is to die for. Normally when you but crawfish from places, they make it too salty or it doesn't have enough flavor.. But the crawfish here is perfect!

First of all... I hate going to a restaurant on Mother's Day. Not bad... Not great. The service is very good. Very attentive. But it's hot in here. It's in the low 90s today and doesn't feel much cooler inside. 

The food is average. Nothing special. Didn't find anything that I would rave about. But the staff is very nice. Maybe we will try it again when we are in the area. Maybe the next time there won't be screaming kids running through people.

The food is excellent, however the service needs work, my husband and I are in our mid twenties and the last 3 times we have been we've been treated like children. The last time was the last straw we waited 50 minutes for food and drink refills. Won't be back.

Long awaited , amazing quality sushi to Island Estates & the Clearwater beach area!.
Very well known local chef who makes everything with perfection and love.  Best fresh fish hands down!.

I went here last Friday with my sister for her graduation dinner and it was a wonderful dinner! It's a pretty small restaurant with both indoor and outdoor seating. It has very modern decor; minimalistic with clean lines.

Our server was sweet and recommended the Fleur Delice cocktail, since I like fruity drinks. It was a great fresh, citrus-y drink. I am also a sucker for bread and it was amazing... I filled up on three slices! The bread was fresh and moist and had slight spicy kick to it. Some olive oil would have been nice but that didn't take away from the bread at all (and less calories in the end, too).

I ordered the lobster appetizer.. and it was a good-sized portion of lobster. It was in a light cream sauce with thin strips of pickled daikon and lightly toasted chunks of squid ink bread. The daikon was a nice juxtaposition to the cream sauce and the squid ink bread complemented the dish nicely. My sister order the crawfish dish which came with a strawberry sauce; i had a taste and liked it well enough.

For my main course, I ordered the pork shoulder dish. It was pretty tasty, but I was blown away by my sister's entree: the filet of beef. Hers was delivered as three pieces of medium-rare beef on mashed potatoes and leeks on the side. The beef was a perfect medium-rare: pink all throughout, with just the outside browned, and not bloody at all. Kudos to the chef! I doubt I'll be back in St. Louis anytime soon, but if I ever were, I would definitely revisit this restaurant!

Where to start???  What an amazing experience we had, this has been my third time @ the restaurant and I can say that it gets better every time.
The service was amazing, the waitress spend the perfect amount of time with us to make us feel that she care for our needs without becoming overwhelming.
The owners took the time also to stop @ out table a couple of times to make sure we didn't need anything :), in my book they get a 100% for service.
Now the food, the food was amazing!!!!! i recommended anytime. We were a large group, and our appetizers, am main dish arrived on time and EVERYTHING was delicious, the coconut shrimp appetizer has been the best I have had . We had pizza, pastas, salads and dessert; the flavor was on point, everything fresh and delicious!!! 
hands down BEST Italian restaurant @ St. Pete Beach
Very generous oyster poboys.  Boiled Shrimp were unusually small. Crawfish were mostly good and meaty with some small ones in the mix.
I love Rosario's pepperoni pizza. It's so good I've never ordered anything else (lame, I know). I've ordered a large pepperoni pizza approximately a billion times, and it's always good.

Disappointed.  They claim to be "the worlds greatest hot sandwich".....which it even says on the door and on the menu.  Saying that makes me more skeptical, and they shouldn't make those claims if they haven't really been rated that way.  Anyone can claim to be the best at anything......but who said they were the best?  

They are probably a step up from Subway and Firehouse subs.....but I have had much better sandwiches before.  Also, their sandwich menu isn't really that big, and it doesn't have what I would consider to be the typical "hot" sandwiches.  When I think of hot sandwiches I think of Reuben's, hot pastrami, corned beef.....but they don't have any of those.

If you were going to go to subway, this would be a better choice....but I wouldn't recommend going here otherwise.  Basically a typical fast food sandwich place, and nothing special about it at all.

Loved it ((but I'm also a huge fan of all Marcie Turney restaurants))!!! We had the burrata/beet/grapefruit salad- very good and seasonal. We also had the spicy fried chicken biscuit sandwich- must have. The flavors in the slaw were great (tarragon and maybe mustard seeds?). And the biscuits themselves were awesome with a crusty, salty top. The slush was a frosé! Apparently it's not lasting for much longer so definitely get it while you can. Lastly, we shared the funfetti cake. It's a huge slice, not dry at all. We of course wanted the cinnamon bun but it was sold out. Not surprising since we went later in the day. Will definitely be back. Our waiter great too. I didn't catch his name but he was prompt and chatty.

As a local (I wasn't born here but raised in the area since I was 3) I have heard several stories of Antoine's.  The stories of snobbery, how the menu use to be in all French and if you could't read it, it was your problem, and of course all of the history.

Antoine's had intimidated me.  I didn't think I was refined enough to dine there.  I felt as if though I needed practice at other restaurants in order to be worthy of dining here.  Antoine's was on my short list of must eat restaurants for years and until this Saturday I still wasn't sure if I was up to their standards.  After dining there, I don't think they are up to mine.  

There is no longer the snootiness that once existed.  The waiters are personable, friendly, helpful and make the experience enjoyable.  My waiter was somewhat aloof but nothing too bad.  He would just give me my lady friend's food and vice versa and read us the lunch menu instead of dinner for the Coolinary.  

We started off with the Oysters 2-2-2; Rockefeller, Bienville and Thermador.  They invented the Rockefeller and will remind you of that throughout your meal.  They even give you a card telling you what # order you are of the dish as a keepsake.(It's not very accurate as they have probably sold twice as many according to the waiter)  The oysters were pretty solid with the Bienville being really good!  The Bienville are baked in a white wine sauce, onions, and peppers.  Delsih.

After that we did the Coolinary menu.  I had the Shrimp Au-gratin to start.  The portion is quiet small but being as it was a pre-fixed 3 course menu, it's understandable.  The cheesy shrimp flavor was really good and au-gratiny.( I made up a word)  My entree was the French Pork chop.  The description has it as a '10 oz. French-style pork chop with apple port sauce and served with Brabant potatoes'.  If there was a sauce on mine, there wasn't much of one.  French style must mean bone in but in this case could have meant over cooked.  I love a thick cut prok chop and have gotten them at several places in the city and this was my 1st time getting one that I'd call mediocre.  It was like when I 1st started grilling and was afraid of undercooking them.  It was borderline burnt.  The Brabant potatoes are a fancy way of saying home fries.  The desert was Peche' Melba.  This was candied peaches, ice cream and rasberry sauce on top of a crushed almond cake.  Simple but delish.  The girlfriend got the drum fish dish that was suppose to be in a rich cream and white wine sauce but was quite bland.


Being as the Coolinary menu is 3 courses for 35.00, I didn't feel cheated but if I had paid normal menu prices for the same dishes, I would have.  Antoine's lives on it's history.  They talk it up as they should as the oldest restaurant in America but while their history dates back 174 years their prices are 74 years in the future.  Entrees start in the high 20's and go upwards of 50.00.  All sides are a-la carte and are about 7-9 dollars each.  Appetizers are in the 15.00 range.  I say this not to seem like a cheap ass but to say that their food isn't good enough to charge those kind of prices.  The atmosphere is great, the history even better, the oysters were solid and the sazerac was spot on.  However when I'm dropping the 175.00 for a meal for 2, I want to be WOW'd.  I was not.

I had their All-You-Can-Eat sushi lunch special ($16) which includes AYCE miso soup and seaweed salad. Delicious! Both the Nigiri and Roll selections were extensive. Really, the only problem I had with it was that they were out of Ika (Squid) that day. The restaurant itself has a great atmosphere along with great service, especially at the sushi bar. I anxiously look forward to going back.
Love the chicken fajitas and the empanadas.They also have pretty decent happy hour specials.

I've been to the Original Pete & Shorty's and this one doesn't disappoint. 

The Shorty burgers are the best. They're basically a slider on a Kings Hawaiian Roll bun. Are you kidding me? They're $1/ea unless you order a dozen. I have to be honest I haven't tried much else here. I know the Turkey Ruben is excellent as the folks I was with raved about it.

This is Pub Grub, but it's done right. P&S is owned by the folks who started Hooters. If given a choice I'd eat here 10 out of 10 times...just for the food alone. 

This particular P&S seems to be a hub for Iowa State football fans. So, if you're an ISU fan - I'm sure you already know about this place.

They have a very clever fountain out front made from an old bar tap. It's probably one of the neatest outdoor decorations I've ever seen at a bar.

This is a great place to stop on your way to a Rays game too!

Maynard's is a great date place for the following reasons. They have a huge bar and it's great to people watch, you can buy wine, sweet treats, breakfast lunch or dinner and they're open really late. There's an awesome patio to watch the train go by with live music of all different kinds, and a more intimate ritzy dinner section if you like cozier quieter dining. I've tried the salumi plate with meats and cheeses, the cheeseburger with French fries, and the pizza all of which were very good. The staff is always busy, very helpful and attentive. I appreciate it when I'm finished with my drink another is offered without even having to ask.
