The margaritas are fresh and potent. Have two and you may want to Uber. 

Fresh is the underlying theme here. Everything is fresh and you can taste it. 

When you go ask for Asia. She was perfect and fresh lol.

Today was my first time trying Falafel and I was extremely impressed. The staff was courteous and knowledgeable and helped me build my sandwich. The food was piping hot and very tasty. Definitely lives up to it's great reputation and long line. I will be back soon!

Y'all run, don't walk here! The smell from the seafood boiling is so enticing! It was love at first smell for me I wanted one of everything on the menu! We ordered the shrimp and crab dip that only lasted ten minutes as my hungry family devoured it! Hubby had the oysters Rockefeller which he gave two thumbs up. I ordered the red beans and rice with catfish. The beans had that nice smokey flavor of a hamhock in there and tasted like that pot had simmered all day! The catfish was flaky and light. It was so good I asked for a second piece! We ordered the gumbo which for some folks may be a little spicy but it was right on point for us! We also had the barbecue shrimp which was lovely. Even though you needed to roll us out the door, we still ordered dessert. That bread pudding will haunt me in my dreams until I can make my way back. And our waitress was so attentive and very sweet! She anticipated our every move and I can't remember her name to save my life! But thank you so much! Again don't let this gem slip by you if you're in NOLA! We'll see y'all soon!
Excellent quality and service. They really know how to take care of the customers. Family owned and it shows.

Impeccable service from beginning to end- starting with hostess offering to take our coats, to table staff, to chefs. iPad of beverage choices with ability to flag drinks your are considering. Dining area is cozy, seats are comfortable lounge chairs. Quiet atmosphere allowing conversations with chefs but also intimate conversation. Sat at a table facing chefs and watched the teams prepare each course meticulously- almost each one used tweezers to perfect presentation. Table staff was attentive but not overly so, perfect timing of courses arriving and removal of objects from table (never too long and never too soon). We had a main waiter but it was a team effort to make sure we were well cared for. While each course wasn't large, we left perfectly satisfied- not over full. Each course offered a variety of flavors and tantalized the taste buds. My favorites were the tuna (which I've had often before but not with this combination of accompanying flavors), the beef (melt in your mouth- which I didn't believe until I found it to be true- perfectly cooked with slightly crispy/sweet on the outside, tender, and dashes of sauces to compliment nicely, the potatoes (white truffles brought to table and shredded on top - amazing!), and the creme dessert in eggshell (sweet with the perfect zing of salt). The chefs were fascinating to watch and very friendly/open to general inquiry.  I'd highly recommend and look forward to an occasion to return with friends to share the experience with.

WTF happened to these guys???  Years ago when I lived in Philly, this place used to be the best cheese steak place in town.  With much anticipation I went there in early Jan 2014 after many years.  What a bummer it was!   The meat was thick and chewy, the bread was cold and chewy... it was just horrible.

Sad to see such a decay... hope it was just a bad day for the cooks and suppliers.  Would really like to see it revived.

Small diner type feel with nice staff. The food is par at best. I consider this a greasy spoon type restaurant where the plates are greasy and done fast. Prices are ok but I have had better breakfast throughout Clearwater.

Vero Amore e il mio amore. 

After a recent trip to Italy, I decided to revisit Vero Amore to see how it stacks up to my memories. I would just like to start by saying they are doing everything right. 

This place has a charm and quality you wouldn't expect from a restaurant located in a Bashas' shopping center. Their food here is great and the wine is just as good. The ingredients are always fresh and tasty. 

I usually stop by during lunch and the staff at Vero Amore definitely know what they are doing. They are always friendly, efficient and very knowledgeable. A huge plus for this tiny Italian eatery.

This is possibly the worst McDonalds in the history or fast food history. 

My wife stopped by to get a 2 Cheeseburger meal and Big Meal meal for supper. She ordered and pulled up to the pickup window. We needed another cheeseburger so she asked the lady at the window if she could add a cheeseburger. The lady at the window screamed at her and said well its going to be a while. Now granted there was no one in the restaurant eating and 1 vehicle behind her that it should have taken like 2 minutes. 

She then came back to the window slammed the debit card down and said you'll just have to pull up. So my wife did, waited, and waited, and waited....10 minutes later we did not have our food. Meanwhile, another employee came out and gave a bag of food to the vehicle behind us. My wife waited for another 5 minutes and watched the other vehicle eat and finally went in. 

When my wife went in, the lady at the drive thru said, what do you want? My wife told her she had been waiting 15 minutes and did not receive her food. The employee said yes you did and my wife was like no you didnt, in which she didnt. Her next comment was classic..."well, your not getting any free food!" Meanwhile another employee came up and said oh yeah I took out that food that had been sitting on the counter for 10 minutes to the truck out there...that was the vehicle behind us. 

So at this time, my wife had had it. She told the female employee that she wanted her money back..the lady reiterated that she wasnt giving out any free food. So the lady rang up some arbitrary amount on the register. It was less than what we originally paid and the lady employee had thrown away the receipts. So my wife made her print them out again....that just set off her rudeness and anger. So we paid for meals and food we didnt get, she tried to refund us less than what we paid, and now I am waiting on the charges to come through so I can make sure that they did reimburse us the correct amount. 

My wife texted the manager's number that is on the store window and did not answer. So much for the any customer complaint please call the store manager. To this date, she has not called us. 

There has been no apology, no admittance of wrong doing, or no food. Was it too much for them to do the right thing and refuse to do the right thing and just say sorry and replace the food that they NEVER gave us. 

Going to send this to McDonalds and see if we get anywhere. Its not too much to ask to do the right thing.

Being a spoiled Chicago beer guy I really wanted to check out what Indy craft beer was all about. First off their set up is pretty cool. You feel like you are in the middle of their operation... wait, you really are! You get 6 free sample (2-3 oz pours) which is very generous. You don't see that very often. To be honest I want to see them continue to thrive; so if they start charging for the samples I wouldn't complain. The people pouring are very nice and enthusiastic about beer. Some weren't very knowledgeable but  in his defence he started less than 1 month ago. Their beers were very good. Being a home brewer and coming from a family of beer judges I am happy to say their beers are to style and by the book. From color to clarity, aroma to taste, their beers are probably the best Indianapolis has to offer. Keep up the great work!

I visited the Isla Vista, CA store which I understand serves primarily students in the surrounding community.  However, as a 53-year-old multi-year gold card holder, I could not have possibly been made to feel more unwelcome.  The manager was far too busy chatting with his friends and running around behind the counter doing part of everyone's job in a vain attempt to train, he took only half of my order, left me standing at the counter awaiting checkout while orders from the other register continued to jump in front of my poor cup, languishing unattended beside the register.  When the young lady at the other register finally rescued me, she helplessly explained she was "just in training" and promptly put my cup behind several others that had been ordered by customers coming in long after me.  More than ten minutes after my initial order, my grande nonfat latte was finally served, about 2/3's full.  Despite the lack of customers at the time, I had no interest in asking the hapless barista for a redo nor did the manager offer anything but a "your drink is coming" during the entire wait (though at least he pulled himself away from his buddies in the store long enough to dismiss me curtly).  Unless you're the manager's "bro," don't bother...

One word describes the Tyrone Restaurant: EXCELLENT. There is no other diner that I've been to in this area in the past five years that can compare. 
I know this sounds like hyperbole but it's not. Let's talk about the food. Just a simple two egg whites toast sausage patties and sliced tomatoes. The food was so fresh the eggs just came out of the chicken! 
Wait staff was friendly -nice -joking around on this April Fool's day. It's just a great place lots of camaraderie. 
It's my first time here but when I'm in the area it's certainly not my last. 
Highly recommend it- can't say enough good things.

This is the best mall in Tampa it has a good selection on high end items.  They have sadies photography we really like.  We like Neiman Marcus and one of my close friends loves Louis v.  I love nordstrom and so do the kids. When we need  something this is were we usually shop

I REALLY always have a superb time here and the food is truly remarkable. You are always welcomed in with a great greeting & feel welcomed by the extremely friendly staff. I usually sit up at the bar and the bartenders are superb and knowledgeable and attentive and open. The food is unique, delicious and plentiful. It is a bit expensive for the casual atmosphere but not enough to affect things too much. I happened to havevthe sea bass with chestmuts on a butternut squash puree and it was perfectly presented, flavored and cooked. Their truffle fries always get things started for me and reslly are just plain GREAT! There is an upstairs mezzanine and  a large bar downstairs with a few tables. Both areas are well laid out and comfortable. The only aspect that  keeps it from thst final star is that i would like to see some more variety in a craft beer list. It is a bit single layered....just take it up a notch.

Okay let me start off by saying, its definitely not a place you want to stick around to long. Although its worth being asked by alcoholics for a dollar to go get some of the food.

It's basically just a regular store, but they serve food in the back. Everyone goes here for some gumbo, its absolutely great. One of my favorite items is the shrimp past and club poboy. You have to try it out. It's beyond cheap!

oh SNAP I love this pie!! For $8-10 you get an awesome, custom-made, fresh and filling pizza. Even on a busy night at 7 PM, I've never waited more than 15 minutes. These guys are efficient without sacrificing quality. If you're a thin crust person, Snap is for you!
May I suggest my all time favorite custom creation?
1. herb butter sauce (but their tomato is awesome too, very fresh!)
2. shredded mozz (AND fresh if you're feeling extra cheesy)
3. ricotta
4. artichokes and carmelized onions
5. lemon oil drizzle as the finishing touch
BOOM, PERFECTION. So refreshing and delicious.

First and foremost, kudos to management. I was there 12ish on the first Saturday of the opening week. The place was mobbed and they still had the shit running like they had been open for months.

So it's Cafe Lift... everyone knows what they do with brunch. They fucking nail it. Period. I had the Frittata. Execution was on point. The fresh mozzarella was the superstar... even outshined the prosciutto. The fried potatoes were seasoned to perfection: delicious.

Yo, but the real king... the cocktail menu is a superstar. The drinks are very approachable and user friendly. Definitely crafted with the masses in mind... I could seriously see this menu right at place at Talula's Garden or another of the like.

First thing I went in on was the 'Barista's Negroni'. The perfect mid-day Negroni: the Campari was just enough to let you know it's there. Not gonna lie, I generally like them big, bitter and boozy, but this was well-balanced, slightly sweet and refreshing... dare I say a Negroni that's thirst quenching?!!! At that very moment it was perfect.

Next sampled the bloody. It was solid and well-made. If you like em', you're good.

The 'Bees Teas' is dangerous as fuck. Seriously... drinks like a gourmet soda. Fair warning... they only taste like there is no booze, if you're not careful, you could easily go too deep on these.

Anyway, I'm tired of writing. If you're out that way, go. Great food. Amazing brunch cocktails.
I really, really want to love Mo's. Our server gave it his all, but you can only do so much with just okay food.   Good Luck Mo's I hope you can get it on the rails.

I really enjoy the deluxe beef pho which is number 9. I personally think it is the best in the city for the price. You can get two bowls of pho with free jasmine tea for twenty dollars. AMAZING. I recommend you try it out. Parking can be tight on Saturday afternoons but Sunday's it's free everywhere so that is the best weekend day to go.

We wanted to go to Big Shakes, but they were closed. BOOOOO to Big Shakes for only having a handwritten note to indicate this. BUT, it was a blessing in disguise, as this place is closer to Brentwood, where my dad lives, and it's awesome. They've only been open for two months, but I highly recommend giving them a try. I had the biggest leg quarter of my life. The cook even came out and asked us to reconsider our order because it would take so long to cook it, but we weren't in any hurry. It weighed 2-3 lbs and was cooked to perfection. Granted, he made it sound like they weren't normally this big. I got "hot" and tried their hottest flavor (it had some cheesy moniker) for the wings. i couldn't tell much of a difference between the two, but it will definitely make your nose run, and I have a high tolerance (very high). The crisp to the skin was great. The heat didn't penetrate down to the bone (which is why I'm docking them a point). Somehow, Prince's makes their heat permeate better throughout the meat, so they may still be my favorite. I really liked Rooster's sides, too; their fries were even seasoned with cayenne and some other spices....so even they were hot! The beans were meat heavy, which I like. Like most hot chicken places, each piece is cooked to order, so make sure you have a least 30 minutes free, even for a take out order. BTW, the wings are HUGE. $7.50 sounds like a lot for three wings, but wait until you see them! Highly recommended.

We were staying at the Bourbon Orleans and had a couple vouchers for free breakfast, it turns out was for the buffet.

They have a great spread and Tim was a fabulous server. So cool. The first day I got lots of smoked salmon and their egg bake was divine, especially the homemade salsa! Amazing!

The second day I had more egg bake and a fabulous crawfish gumbo. Tim brought out some fresh squeezed OJ, I haven't had that in years. Sooooo good. Also, crazy good.  If I were paying $20 for it, way expensive, but for some vouchers and a tip, this was awesome.

My 1st experience here  was dinner!  Staff is delightful and friendly.  The atmosphere here is a bit more casual than we expected but no big deal we are fine with casual.  We went for an early Valentines dinner we don't enjoy going out on Valentines so we go a day or so early.  We started with signature martinis which we really enjoyed and were priced well at only $9.00 and enjoyed 2 appetizers.  Note 1 would have been plenty we took most of one of them home.  They were both yummy ( fried artichokes and Spicy cheese balls).  Then moved on to a salad which was just ok I thought it was a bit over loaded with pimentos and a little heavy on the Italian dressing.  Main coarse. We had the ribeye which was cooked to perfection and melted in your mouth and the salmon both were yummy.  Baked potato as one side and pasta as the other.  Dinner was not disappointing.  We took home cheese cake to split later, awesome!  We had a gift card I had saved from Christmas.  If the salad had been better I would have rated this a 5.  The other reason I didn't rate this a 5 was the ladies room was awful!  Doors to the toilet broken, duck tape covering drain holes on the floor and it just wasn't clean!  This will keep me from not returning!  I hate ghetto restrooms!!!  This place is to nice to not take care of the restroom, YUCK!
I cant find another Italian spot like it! I am from SF Bay Area and I travel all over the US. This is it! Pick one of their specialty pasta dishes, you cant go wrong.

One of the neatest restaurant buildings in St. Louis. Lots of history and love poured into this renovated building. I have eaten here for lunch and stopped in for beers several times, and my cousin also held her wedding rehearsal dinner in the upstairs event space. 

You must try the crispy spare ribs, the poutine, and the rarebit. I like that The Tap Room and Bottleworks (both owned by Schlafly Beer Company) have different menus and different beers on tap. We bring out of town guests here and they always love the food, beer, and atmosphere. Great exposed brick throughout the whole building, and a side bar and game room in addition to the main bar and dining hall. 

The cuban, reuben, and shaved prime rib sandwiches are also all worth trying. Again, the food isn't cheap but it is high quality, locally sourced ingredients. In terms of beer, you can't not try the American Pale Ale, the Coffee Stout, and the Cask Oak Aged Barleywine. Actually be sure to get a sampler platter and try any beer they serve from a cask. 

The Tap Room earns an A.

When you need your fix of fried chicken and you want to just belly up to the bar and get a fried chicken plate in a hurry, Hodak's is the place to go. If you want to wait in line for a table, that's ok too, If you want faster service with a big smile, belly up to the bar and Lenny will take care of you. I have been eating Hodak's for about 51 years that I can remember.It is moist and juicy. Never greasy. And always piping hot. It is always a great meal before or after a ballgame.

Something feels really wrong about leaving a 5 star review after only eating a doughnut but what can I say this mornings grapefruit brûlée doughnut was excellent. Soft and fluffy with a grapefruit aftertaste.  The brûlée texture was much closer to a glaze than a hard brûlée.

Went back the next day and got strawberry shortcake. It was great, grapefruit brûlée was better.

I cannot believe I have not yet rate this place ! I first came here on a "lazy date" and actually got some good beers out of it . The atmosphere was very "classic" and I loved it so I decided to bring my sister here to try the food . AH-MAY-ZING . Fresh food that's so authentic . My sister and I had the tartar and the carapaccio for apps and for dinner , I believe she had fish and I had the half chicken (it was quiet a while ago) . I don't remember the food exactly, but i remember the awesome taste ! I also brought my boyfriend here who reminisce on the food constantly, and also brought my parents here for the past Thanksgiving ! They never try anything new (they're so used to their Asian cuisine) , but they LOVEDDDD this place and I was shocked !! We had an amazing time . Staff are always attentive and friendly . I just love it and wish I could dine here every single day if I could afford it . Fellas , if you're trying to impress a lady , bring her to Parc ;) (then Tria afterwards right up the block)

First time at this chain and I was very pleasantly surprised! Large breakfast menu with many options, super nice staff, and they leave you with a carafe of coffee on the table (these are my favorite kind of places!). Will definitely be back next time we're in the area.
One of my favorite breakfast places. Uptown location is great for locals

The Wheelhouse is my favorite bar in St. Petersburg. The service is incredible from everybody, especially from my favorite beer-tender, Brett. He's incredibly knowledgeable about all of the brews and is always warm and welcoming. I always leave the Wheelhouse with a smile on my face. The beer and food items are ever-changing. It seems as if every time I come in, which is often, the menu is all new. It's a fun low-key vibe with amazing beers and great company.

The food tasted good, and there was good Friday. My primary concern with the place is that some of the food was not hot. The warming tables were not working adequately. This creates the potential for food poisoning.

Came here on a Saturday morning when another favorite bagel shop of mine was closed. It was pretty crowded and the line was long, but it moved quickly. 

I intended to order a breakfast sandwich - bacon, egg & cheese is my to-go! - but when standing in line, I saw that the eggs were microwaved.  I quickly changed my order to a bagel with sundried tomato cream cheese. The spread was very good, but the bagel was not memorable. 

I will likely not return since I am not in the neighborhood... but if you're in a pinch it'll do for a quick and simple breakfast!

This is a fine lunch spot, although of course very busy for Sunday lunch!  My wife had very tasty salmon on toast with side salad, and I had a delicious 1910 Burger  with cheese on a brioche bun! Sweet potato fries on the side with a cinnamon glaze were especially good!

I'm a firm believer that my taste buds could write a better review about Thee Burger Spot. It's a reason why it's Thee"  and not "The". If Johnny Gill were to try this place he'd sum his experience up with "thee" following words: "My, my, my..." And James Brown would join in with "please, please, please..." Do yourself, your significant other, and the boss you don't like a  HUGE favor and share a scrumptious mouth-watering burger at Thee Burger Spot.
Went for the first time tonight for a family birthday. All 5 of us loved the place, food, service and very fair prices. Entrees we're BUG and we all needed boxes for leftovers. I'll be back   100%

I ordered a chicken pesto crepe. I really didn't like the taste. The pesto was really salty. I also ordered a coffee that came to me luke warm. The others at my table were satisfied with their crepes, but not blown away. The prices were reasonable, but I'm just not sure I'll return.

We were staying at the Marriott so it was really convenient for dinner. The hostess was very friendly and inviting although the server was ok. The food is definitely over priced- it's a bar setting with pub like food at a more higher end priced restaurant. The food was good but not that good.

Pimms cup was fantastic!  I had 2 smalls should have just ordered the large.  We had the Fried Chicken. It was good. If you have ever eaten at Babes in Roanoke TX in DFW its not as good.  babes is the best!  But if you have not had Souther fried chicken it was very good.  The bacon cheddar jalapeño burger was very good and large.  The wings were very yummy!  The jelly sauce on them were spicy and sweet.

This is my office away from my office. When I want to keep working but do so in a place with bottomless coffee that I don't have to make and amazing pastries I go  here.  It's  very comfortable place, one that was clearly designed for people to linger in.  The coffee is awesome in particular the hazelnut (I prefer it to 'bucks).  They don't have iced coffee on the menu but they'll give you a big cold drink cup and you can make it yourself.  Their breakfast sandwiches are ... eh.... they keep introducing different ones trying to find something that works.  The problem with them is always the rubbery eggs so I get them without the eggs.  But they have great little breakfast casserole things. Their salads, bagels, lunch sandwiches, soups (available in a bread bowl)  and pastries are very good. They also offer fresh baked bread.  They do tend to run out of things a bit sooner than I think they should and that's what takes them down to 4  stars. But if there's a particular loaf of bread or pastry that you want if you call them in the morning they'll set it aside for you. They box up some of their breads and pastries to make them appropriate hostess gifts so if you need to take something when you go a calling swing by and grab some yummy pastry or bread.  They do have outside seating  but smokers be aware that even their outside seating is smoke free. It is not, however, dog free so if you want bring the mutt. They give all their leftovers at the end of the day to charity that in and of itself would bring me there again and again. There's plenty of parking and it's easy to get in and out of.
Edge Brewing is a hidden gem! I love the food and the prices aren't bad. The staff is usually great, and the atmosphere is wonderful. Definitely recommend giving this place a try.

This location is fairly new, I had a handful of promotional coupons and was in the area, so decided to try it out.

Located in a small strip mall in busy North Dale Mabry, we walk in to a very clean, welcoming shop. The menu board is on the wall directly when you walk in. I use the B/O/G/O sandwich coupon and get their Chicken Avocado sandwich. 

While awaiting the preparation of said sandwich, I look around to the bright, clean surroundings. It was later in the afternoon, and only a few other patrons were present.

My sandwich is served. It was pretty good: ample avocado, white chicken and veggies, as I like them.  

I learn from my dining companion that the sandwich chain is owned by the actual of the Earl of Sandwich in jolly, old England!

I do recommend dining here, if you haven't tried any of their sandwiches. A good value for the money.

And, tell Earl I said "Hello".

Went here with a large group of people on a Friday night at 6pm, and I was expecting to wait, but we barely waited at all for our food! It was great because I was starving! I got 2 adobada 2 carne asada, and definitely could have ordered another 2, but 4 was just right. The meat is super tender and they give you a lot for each taco. I liked the adobada more in my opinion, but the carne asada was still delicious. The toppings also add more flavor, the red salsa is perfectly spicy. The menu is super simple, so everyone got their food within 10 minutes after ordering. Great for big groups because they have large tables. Will come back here whenever I'm in SB and in need of tacos!

Very expensive for Mexican, but completely worth it. Never had a dish I didn't like. The chips and salsa are even exemplary. I like the wood-grilled shrimp salad, the mushroom quesadillas, queso, street corn, and the brussel sprouts- you MUST get the brussel sprouts. My least favorite was the shrimp ceviche but still did not dislike. The drinks are good and the atmosphere is lovely. Service is fast and satisfactory.

I'm ashamed I didn't write a review many years ago.  That's what happens when you live so close to such a great place to eat.  I have eaten many a burger here, but I must admit I can't eat one of the big ones.  I have to ask for a take out container.  I always enjoy the atmosphere, friendly service, and pictures on the walls of all of those BSU football players that can eat the big burgers.  This is the only place I have ever brought my eldest son that he couldn't eat the whole thing.  I did enjoy watching him try.  But eventually he raised the white flag and gave up.  Our family of four kids and thirteen grand kids still love to go here for lunch.  You'll agree this is one of the best anywhere.

I very much enjoyed this establishment. I came for happy hour with a few friends. The happy hour consists of both a food/ sushi menu as well as a drinks menu, and everything is $3, $4 or $5. I had multiple hand rolls, all of which were wonderfully flavored. The restaurant was more than accommodating when our party count doubled and we had to add tables. The server helped with food suggestions, and the happy hour finger potatoes are FAB. I'm not sure I've had anything like them before.
The bathrooms are individual stalls with a common area for sinks.
I realized later that night that I forgot something at the restaurant and called them, and they even stayed there passed regular hours to let me come get it! So nice.

My gf and I were looking for an Italian place in the Treasure Island area. Luckily we found this place which was right across from the beach hotel were staying at. Even though some of the reviews were bad we wanted to still give it a try. She and I both had huge portions and the food was very flavorful. She had the spaghetti and meatballs and I had the shrimp scampi. We both have big appetities and ended up taking some home with us so you know you wont leave hungry! The ambiance was kind of dated and the service seemed to want to "turn and burn" our table (thats why 4 stars not 5). We will def hit this place upp again the next time we are in town.
The food is great, the service is amazing. It's authentic mexican food , they cook delicious and tasty.We will definitely recommend it.

Nice location on the ground floor of the Alexander. It's a beautiful space and well designed. The menu is focused on Southern Italian. There is a good wine selection and they do have a sommelier on staff to assist. The staff is well prepared and knowledgeable. There is a good selection of proteins and pasta. The food is very enjoyable. Overall a very nice spot to go without braking the bank.

My husband and I have been ordering from the same place for years. We decided to venture out so we ordered from here for the first time. 

we ordered from their website, which was super easy and convenient since we could put "special instructions" in there.  We ordered the wings, which my husband loved (he sucked the bone) and pizza which was pretty good. We'll order from here to further explore the menu. 

I knocked off a star because of the time it took to deliver. We're literally less than a mile a way and it shouldn't of taken over an hour for the food to come. I knocked off another star because the food was barely warm when it got to my house.
Awesome food, great service.. This place is everything you been told it is...well worth the line which moves fast and orderly.. Best Bbq

Love the breakfast there.  The prices are very reasonable, the food is awesome.  I had the Philly cheesesteak omelet: chopped steak, onions and homemade whiz sauce, yum.  My girlfriend got the Belgan waffle, it was fresh and thick.  Definitely a great spot.

Lunch today at this deli inside Silver Legacy on the casino floor. Order at the counter and your food is delivered to your table. All fresh cut meats by the deli chefs.

Today I had the Soup and half sandwich. Very reasonable at $8. Minestrone and Turkey on Rye.  Delicious! Delivered fast to the table. Crackers for the soup and a pickle accompanied the meal.

The menu is large with deli favorites.  Beer is served as well as Pepsi products.

Check them out, worth the trip.

Stopped in during happy hour for some apps and glasses of wine.  Sat in a booth in the bar arran and service was very good.  We had the gouse Pinot and sampled 4 different apps.  Great prices during happy hour.  The food was just OK, but the ambiance and service go a long way .

What a great vibe walking into this new spot in New Hope!  It is an exciting line of spots to try out, similar environment of the Stockton Market. Just now a produce and enthusiastic eatery spots in town.  Only tried Moose on the Loose and enjoyed a flavor packed veggie quiche and butternut squash soup for lunch. It was fantastic! A perfect addition to an already amazing place!

Excellent tacos. I'm from CA and I've had many tacos in my lifetime so my expectations were high. These guys know what they're doing and they're really friendly. Not the best tacos I've ever had in my life (their sauce is holding them back, I've had MUCH MUCH better) but they're pretty good and I'm glad they're in Philly.

Great neighborhood, fast service (although the wait staff didn't check in with me too often). The chips are served warm (and you can tell they're fresh), and the salsa has a nice kick. I ordered the enchiladas with ranchero chicken, and it had a solid flavor profile. Not the best I've ever had, but far above many, many others. Margaritas are good-sized as well!

We had nice time at Bardenay.  The atmosphere was wonderful.  I will say that I felt that it was over priced but it was such a lovely atmosphere I guess that is why the food and drinks cost so much.  We had a few cocktails and shared a meat and cheese tray appetizer.  I wold not return again because despite it being a beautiful restaurant and the waitress being a lovely lady, I can get drinks and appetizers elsewhere for a more reasonable price.

While the restaurant itself is very attractive, the server was great, and my specialty drink was delicious, it is inconceivable that my husband's filet was $39, and my halibut was $38, and we were not even served bread. And that was after the waitress explained the restaurant makes its own bread. Not quite sure why they do not serve bread, and I would only return to have a burger or sandwich next time.

I went to Five Guys last night moments before they closed.  I was actually intending on getting Chipotle next door but they closed at 9:49. Anyway, Five Guys were actually OPEN for business at that time so tried them. 

The service alone was worth coming back for. I figured it was about time to close and I would be making them cranky coming in so late. They didn't care one bit!  They were friendly and jovial and sincerely glad that I was there.  

The burger, well, I wanted a BIG burger and their patties are a bit lacking in size, even ordering a double.  It was decent though and all of the toppings are free; mushrooms, too!  

I'll be back for sure. I'd give them a 6-Star for service and a 4-star for food.  The place was very clean though.  Step up on those burgers to get one more star.  

I forgot to get the name of the guys working, sadly. Info is in my receipt photo.  At that hour of night, had I received crappy service, I would never go back.  The employees won me over. See receipt. 

Thanks.
Great food. Been going here for more than 20 years. Always great food and good prices.  Service is top notch.

This spot is cute little spot, you may pass it up the first time but don't be alarmed just look for the Columbia flag! The food is delicious, I got a steak arepa, your taste buds will burst with flavor as the savory taste of steak, avocado, and cheese melts away in your mouth. Come and get a taste, you will get a little taste Columbia here in the states! To top things off masks are worn by all employees, and the temperature is taken before steamed, as well as sanitizing stations.

Grand opening today! Nice layout inside, although no much seating. 7 tables... seats about 24 people. Guess they plan on a lot of takeout business.

Staff is friendly, and menu is easy to navigate. Pick a type of food (Taco, Burrito, Bowl, etc..) and then a Protein, and then whatever beans, rice, condiments you want.  Price for Tacos is $3.25 per taco... so a decent 3 taco meal with a drink will average 12 to 13 bucks or so. About average for lunch in the area.

I had two Al Pastor tacos and a beer batter shrimp taco, on corn tortillas. They double the tortillas, always a good idea to prevent messes. Tortillas are packaged, and heated up slightly before serving on a press. Tortilla's are not as flavorful as some others I have had recently, maybe a little on the sweet side. 

I love Al Pastor... and have had the real thing in Mexico, sliced off a vertical spit and grilled up with fresh pineapple. This was pretty good for a restaurant version... you can taste the Guajillo Chili in the meat, and it has some pineapple flavor also. Not much heat... but that is pretty normal too. I would eat them again!

The beer battered Shrimp taco? MMMmmm... it was good. The batter has a nice flavor, shrimip was not overcooked, and there was a fair portion served. The Gaucamole here is pretty decent too... I doubt that it is made fresh.... but it is better than many other places in town.

They have Jarritos soft drinks (Mexican Soda) and I love them. The only problem here, is that they are considered a "premium" drink... and run $2.75 per bottle. A bit high for sugar and carbonated water, IMO.

Girlfriend had Beer Battered Fish taco, and a Carnitas taco. She said they were good also.

Service was good, especially for a first day type of thing.... and they were getting busy by the time we left. The manager (owner?) came by to talk to us about the meal while we were eating which is always nice too.

Give 'em a try ... you will probably like them.

It was a good sandwich but I am not sure what the craze for muffulettas was for. 

Portions are huge though and a half took me three (albeit light) meals to finish b

I have been craving good falafel and hummus for months now! Now, nothing compares in my mind to a hot falafel sandwich on the streets of Israel, but on the streets of Philly, Mamoun's did the trick. The restaurant was clean, the staff was friendly, and the food was hot and delicious.

I went pretty basic with the classic falafel sandwich, fries and mango juice.

All in all, if you want a quick, fresh and yummy lunch, Mamoun's is your spot!

So I'm a little frustrated, after having my mouth tuned up for a specific dish at Manhattan Bistro, I have passed several other amazing options to come here and be told that even though they open at 4pm they don't start service at 4pm. What then does open mean? I'm beyond angry that I have wasted my time to come to an establishment that clearly doesn't understand customer service or value my patronage.    

So this is notice to all don't go to this place when they open cause apparently they expect you to be tardy for the party and won't serve you until about 5 or whenever they are ready!   

I called the owner and he said its true even though they open at 4pm, that's when the staff gets there so you can get drinks but not food until about 415 or 430 when the grill and ovens are warmed. 

If your mouth is open in amazement then you look just like me. What?! The owner ... enough said I'm done!

This place is alright, not too crazy over it. Been here like three times. Most of the times it was only to drink. Last time I asked for the same thing I have asked for when I've been there, Ciroc peach and sprite. The girl that was our waiter was quick to say "oh we don't have that here". Mind you, this was on a Saturday and I had just been there Friday. I didn't want to be like "ohh I came yesterday and you do have it!" I asked "are you sure?" She then replies with "ohh I know for a fact cause I have worked here for ____years and we don't have that." I asked nicely if she could check cause I knew they did sell that there. She. Comes back and is like "ohh guess it's a new thing they started and I was never told about it".  I tried their wings and they were not good at all, so don't get them. Also asked for their "famous chili" not sure why....but definitely seemed like they heated the chili in the bowl they gave me. So don't ask for that either. Lol. Other than that I guess it's ok for those of you that like to go there with your pets. Saw a lady with hers that kept getting on the table and all I could think was "is that sanitary?!" So if you're allergic to dogs, do not go there.

When we first sat down, we were told we could only order rice bowls or a bento box if we weren't ordering all-you-can-eat; however, a very helpful employee named Neil came over, clarified things, and took our order. He returned several times to our table to make sure things were meeting our expectations. We started with the tempura calamari rings--hot, fresh, light, and tender--then moved on to tempura vegetables the quality of which matched the calamari, and neither was oily. We ordered cooked long rolls: miyuki, umbrella, crystal shrimp, and FBI rolls (2). Along with the appetizers, this was more than enough for three people. The rolls are rich with texture, visually appealing, and very tasty. We ordered a large hot saki, and Neil added a flavor enhancer that made it super smooth. All-in-all, the meal was excellent. A five-star experience--they just need to be clear on in-house dining guidelines. After a 30 minute wait, no one wants to be told they're limited in selection.

This place was highly recommended and boy am I glad I gave this place a primo spot on my vacation itinerary. We rolled up after a long morning walk ready for some delicious eats. My first breakfast in New Orleans did not disappoint! I had the Shrimp and Grits. The BBQ sauce on the shrimp was unlike anything I've ever had the pleasure of sampling! It was so rich, like Thai peanut sauce rich but with this really unique kind of indescribable flavor! Maybe they started it off with a beef brisket roux? Anyway, epic! Will never forget this! My honey had the Fried Chicken biscuit with honey tobacco. He also gives it five stars. The biscuit was a bit crispy and so unique in this way. Oh and the service was top notch too. Next time, I'm going to sample a piece of their coconut cream pie which I longingly looked upon from afar.

This place was a life saver/hangover preventer. I had maybe had one or two too many, and made my way over to try this " awful awful burger". Boy did it do the trick! The wait was quick, they got my order right, the price was right, and you get a lot of food! It lacked some sanitation, and the ketchup was a little sketchy but it's all part of the awful awful $8 experience. Overall I'd say I'd be back ( well drunk me will defiantly be back)

Tried the CP this evening for dinner and was pleasantly surprised by such a fashion forward decor as we walked in. The tall windows in front were opened out to the streets and it was a beautiful evening. I had high hopes....

I started off with the bacon jam and brie appetizer. In my opinion it was a greasy strange tasting goo. I tried a second bite to make sure I was getting the full flavor and I didn't go back for a third. I personally wouldn't recommend it. 

The beet fries were good but lacked salt.

The avocado tacos were average, they were lacking something maybe a bit of heat or something salty like a pickled cucumber would have made these go from average to great for me. 

Our server was in la la land just slowing walking around staring into space. A different server finally took our payment that had been waiting for more than 10 minutes. So the service was average as well.

We hurried through our entrees because as the place got busier it was HOT HOT HOT in there and I had sweat running down the back of my neck and  noticed several tables AND the hostess fanning themselves with drink menus.

Nothing wow'd me which was disappointing because I've heard such rave reviews on this place.
I may try it one more time so I can hopefully revisit this review and change it to 5 stars.

We have passed this place many times and decided to stop for lunch today. Ice cold beer and huge sandwiches served by a friendly and efficient server. Prices are reasonable and parking is very good. We will be back!

Years ago I worked in Los Mochis, Sinaloa for several months. While there I fell in love with the Mexican interpretation of the hot dog, particularly those made outside of the Iglesia Fatima.  Since recrossing the border I have longed to find a place that could recreate this humble, yet blissful, offering.

Enter El Guero.

This place is the cultural food item de jour in the Southwest.  I had seen it on several of my favorite programs.  I decided that on my next visit I'd give it a shot.

I have been burned in the past so my expectations were low. Was all this attention merited?  I was wrong.  This hot dog was great.  Not quite as good as those from my Mexican memories but very worthy.  For me the good Mexican hot dog is all about the bun and condiments.  El Guero succeeds on both accounts.  The bun is soft and better then any of those used to dress their cousins north of the border.  The toppings were also great.  A good mix that complemented the ensemble.

Great spot.  Now might I recommend that you set up a franchise in Phoenix.  I'll even help.

I miss me some Monks!  Those delectable Spanish Flies (unbelievably make-you-sweat-and-cry chipotle hot wings), the insane selection of mussels (all types of tasty broth), the Trappist burger, and all those lovely Belgian beers on tap!

I'm guilty of taking the train back to Philly to "visit with friends and relatives", when all I really wanted was to go hit Monks.

Great location right at Ballas and Olive.

I used the online ordering the last time.  Worked awesome, they made it just like I asked.

Menu is VERY simple.  Burgers, Dogs and Fries.  What you see is what you get.

Regular fries easily feed two people.  I prefer the cajun fries, they make your lips buzz a bit, but it's a good burn.

I always order the Bacon Cheeseburger with Mayo, Mustard and A-1 Steak Sauce.  It's marvelous.

Best chargrilled oysters in New Orleans! It comes to your table sizzling. I drove in through town and heard recommendations about this place and I wasn't disappointed. I shared the oysters and got the shrimp po boy (1/2 grilled and fried). We also got the hush puppies. I would recommend all of the 3. It was the only seafood place I've been where I've left truly stuffed!

Nice location, interesting decor. Was difficult to get the attendant's attention for a simple order. 

But Worst cold brew coffee I've ever had.

So, overall okay place. But I wouldn't chance the food based on the quality of this order.
DELICIOUS!!  Finally tried Loli's at this location.  Flavors are the same as the original on Benjamin.  Sauces are superb!

Was in St. Louis and wanted to try out a local restaurant that would be quick. Crusoe's Original fit the bill. Tasty burger and good selection of sides. I went with a baked potato, which was small but worked just fine.
Nice ambience and a place worth checking out.

So far the worst place i have been in The french quarter, i had a 1/2 docen of raw oysters wich were already separated from the shell wich made me realize is these are not fresh just opened oysters. besides the texture of these oysters were just... Not to be eaten. I gave them back and waited for my bbq shrimp, to get another dissapointment, bad seasoned, it didnt taste fresh either and you get just two little pieces of bread to dip into yr shrimp bbq, no lime, it was kinda gross anyways, i just had a couple of the shrimps.

This being said, Go to Acme, Deanies, and Felix's oysters, they will have much better food than his, i just came here bcs it was the only place opened, and i guess they used to be good at some point, thats what my friend that works at a club in front says.

We really used to love it here. I mean who can say NO to a Bloomin' Onion?!? Last few times we have gone service and food has been so-so. I always get the twin lobster and last time it wasn't cooked! It was mushy and slimy! Time before that it was cold! Seems they have trouble getting everyone at the table their food at the same time and still hot. Hopefully it will get better!

It was okay.  I should have been worried that the menu really needed an index and chapters.  If you serve 250 dishes, you can't be serving quality.  It was what I get at any number of Mexican restaurants in the area that I visit once and move on.  

Chips are bought not made, salsa recipe consisted of 3 ingredients: pureed tomatos, water and sugar.  Is was a little less spicy than Hinez.  The queso was melted cheese with no spice.  I will visit a Mexican restaurant several times if they can get the chips and salsa right.

I had a huge special thing served in a molcajete (big hot rock vessel) that was actually very good and flavorful.  It's the reason for a second star.  Only serving 3 store bought tortillas that were barely warm was a shame.  Wife had the sad fajitas steak burrito.  Throw fajita stuff in a cold tortilla and top with cheese sauce.  Hard pass.

Service was rather inattentive and slow.  Decently busy and a lot of employees standing in the front talking.  These are not the Mexican dishes you are looking for.
Great meal and great atmosphere--highly recommend! My wife had the junk salad with chicken and I had the salted caramel pork chop and they were excellent choices! Don't miss the margaritas either!

Pastries to go!
Plethora of delicious pastries to choose from.. haven't seen a selection like this outside of Europe or DC. Amazing! Coffee and sandwiches are a bit pricy for what it is. Place is packed all the time (like sardines) so it's best to grab your goodies and go. Definitely will return for pastries & cakes to celebrate special occasions but not for lunch fare.

Loved the location and how it was set up inside. Really nice atmosphere!  The food was pretty good, but nothing to go crazy about. We had the pork skewers and the crawfish Mac and cheese. Could hardly find any crawfish and it lacked the creole flavor I expect from a New Orleans dish but it was nice.  Staff was great!!!

What a great find vacationing in St. Pete. We had a short wait even though nearby places had open seating.  However the ambiance from the patio to when we walked in the door, made us want to wait. The brunch was awesome as were the drinks.  I had the steak and eggs and the Russian Around to drink. I was uncertain when I read the menu on if I would like what I ordered but I am a huge Yuca fan so decided to give it a shot. I was totally blown away at the flavor combination. Don't miss this place if you are in the area!
By far the best meal we had while visiting Clearwater. Friendly, fast service, excellent food, not too crowded. Will definitely visit again when back in the area.

The pizza here is good. Its a great spot to get a quick slice to go. The guys here are cool. Last week when everything was shutting down with curfews they went out of their way to get me a pie. Much appreciated.

AVOID! This place serves, quite possibly, the worst fish and chips I have ever had. Greasy, soggy, and it took 50 minutes at 3 pm on a slow Saturday, with only one other seated party. My husband had the grilled shrimp platter- $16 for six greasy shirmp and a mediocre bowl of cole slaw. They serve a really small pour on a truly crappy $10 wine, and they also make a virtually non-alcoholic margarita. We should have known not to go when was no one else there, but other restaurants nearby were packed. The best part was leaving. Do not go here.

One  for the karaoke. Grumpy, leather faced man behind the bar was the rudest, most disrespectful person I've came across since I've lived here. Completely embarrassing considering I was bragging about how fun this bar was to my family that was visiting at Christmas. He was definitely an 'Angry Elf.'

Ok, this is a BUFFET so you have to expect Chinese-American buffet food.  I went here for an early brunch one Sunday so the food was all hot and fresh.  I think it is better than your average Chinese buffet food and there are lots of choices.  I tried several of their steamed dim sum and it was good.  I did not like the pork bun though -- too much dry bun.  There was a lady making sushi so I tried several kinds and it was actually pretty good.  It may not be good if it sat there for awhile, but it was really fresh when I was there.  I think this is the best buffet in Boise and I will be coming back.

Well, just to put it gently WOW! Wow.. I am talking out of the park! Steak medallions were a little spicier than I'm used to but the kick the Blu cheese made helped even out the flavor. The salmon was stuffed with a REAL CRAB mixture. The potatoes were mashed perfectly and everything was from scratch. I'm not sure what to make of the Brûlée , I can't believe I've lived this long with out it. I shall return! You have a repeat customer! Thanks for the great service! I think her name is Trish , and our food runner Danny? Or maybe Andy? I think, either way they both need a raise!??? Either way we will be back!

We thought we would try this place last night and we were pretty impressed. Most of the tables were filled which is a good sign. The servers were friendly, although very overwhelmed. I had the humus with pita, and veggies over rice, and it was all to-die-for! I can't describe the spice used on the vegetables, but if I could spice up my veggies everyday with whatever they use on this dish, I'd eat them with every meal! Their fries look tasty, so we'll have to try those next time. Save room for a piece of chocolate baklava!

Worst pizza hut ever. Don't order from here, their customer service is awful. Ordered a pizza for delivery waited 2 hours and still did not get it. Trying calling the store 10 times and their phone doesn't work so I had no idea where my pizza was. I had to leave my event to get the pizza that was supposed to be delivered. The staff was rude. We were told our pizza had been ready an hour ago and yet it still was not delivered. So we ended up with hour old cold pizza. I had to ask for a discount as they tried to charge me full price, only gave us a few dollars off. Also I didn't see any of the staff wearing hairnets or gloves. I was disgusted. Will never ever come back. Stay away and go for dominos instead.
The prices say it is gourmet pizza, however, the quality is equivalent to little Caesars pizza....

Tried this place tonight for the first time and definitely will be going back. Prices are great. Food is even better! I got the C N burger and Kumara fries. My burger was juicy and the cheese was an excellent addition to it. The fries while good weren't as good as my boyfriends just original fries so when I go back I will likely switch that up. The aioli that comes with the fries is amazing!! 

Atmosphere was great! Decor matches the ambiance perfectly. They even had a live dj in there playing music. It was packed but we still got our food within a few minutes. Local beer options also kept us happy. 

Def recommend and I will for sure be going back. It's a fun new place for the area that I'm sure will be a huge hit.

Great local spot right next to Publix on GTB and Belcher. Ordered the large Greek Salad and it was both delicious and fresh, not to mention HUGE. When the server brought it to the table I immediately asked for a Togo container, lol.  Place is clean and organized and the staff is friendly and the service prompt. Highly recommended!

I purchased two gift certificates here on 2/13/14 and mailed them out with Valentine's to my daughters in college. The manager who sold them to me did not activate them and my daughters found this out trying to use them.

Rip off! Overcharges without explanation. Caveat emptor
We like to get a small coffee in a large cup and add more milk. He charged for a
Large but no warning.

Breakfasts are pretty good, packed on the weekends. Interesting pairings of Crab cakes with hollandaise and poached eggs. Dinners, not so great. Last experience would make me not want to go back. Sour tomatoes, tea tasted like pot hadn't been cleaned in a couple of days, or it was left over. Not sure if I'd go back.

BEST GELATO EVER! I literally have to stop here every time l'm in NOLA. It's my main priority! I'm pretty picky so I've only tried the basic flavors lol. But the gelato is super creamy, not icy at all, and the service is PHENOMENAL! I love this place and know you will too!

Had an awesome dinner at Shells! You wouldn't know it by the outside of the restaurant, but this place was amazing on the inside. The entire inside of the restaurant was decorated costal style. It was so cool! I had the clam chowder as an appetizer, and it was some of the best I've ever had! I then ordered the shrimp pasta which is what the restaurant is know for. That was excellent as well. The server was extremely nice, and I had a great experience! Definitely a great spot to check out.

One word describes TacoSon: excellent. Overall environment here is so great. Everything was very flavorful and I can't wait to go back already. The people are super nice and it really is so pleasant to just be there. TacoSon is certainly worth checking out.
I had a smoked pulled pork sandwich special that was surprisingly good. Burnt ends, delicate mustard sauce, hot and crispy fries fries. Looking forward to trying other regular items, too.

A coworker and I stopped here for lunch on a Thursday afternoon. There were perhaps four tables full, plus a couple of guys seated at the counter. Everyone was already eating, so we figured this would be a quick lunch. Not so.

We ordered omelets (mine was veggie, hers cheese). I asked them for no mushrooms on mine as I just don't like them.

We waited, and waited, and waited. I kept looking around, trying to catch the eye of our waitress, who finally came over after 20 minutes or so to tell us our food would be out in just a few. Meanwhile a table of two was seated and ordered. 

We finally got our food after another 5 minutes. The waitress said nothing about our wait.

The omelets were hot, though mine was a little too brown and stuffed with mushrooms. Not wanting to wait any longer, I didn't mention it to the waitress. The shredded cheese on top of both was just sprinkled on and not melted. The omelet was okay, though it tasted like the cook hadn't bothered with salt or pepper. The hashbrowns tasted like they were from a box.

We noticed the other table received their food right after ours, making us wonder what about our eggs had taken so long.

I had a biscuit with mine that was small and rubbery. 

Overall, the food was not great, and considering the quality, I'd say it's a bit overpriced. It's certainly not like that classic, greasy spoon, savory diner food you'd expect - even McDonald's has them beat.

When we paid at the counter, they took our money with no "How was everything?" or even a "Thank you." When my friend said "Thanks!" the waitress simply replied "You're welcome." Um, shouldn't you be thanking us for patronizing your business??

Ordinarily, after such an experience I wouldn't return, but it's nice to be able to get breakfast for lunch within walking distance of the office. I'll give them one more try, but next time I'm sticking to just eggs, bacon, and toast. We'll see how that goes.
Had the Shrimp it was excellent nothing else like it in Tucson, service was very good. Reasonable prices too

I ordered takeout Saturday evening.  The burrito had partially cooked (hard) potatoes and no seasoning, the salads had lettuce and 2 small cherry tomatoes.  Seems like they put zero effort into their food. I want to support local businesses during the pandemic but the food needs to be better than Jack In The Box

This place is decent. I was sort of expecting the best mac and cheese, of my life, so perhaps my expectations were set too high, but it just didn't rock my world. I got the buffalo chicken mac, which was good. The chicken was kind of processed seeming, I would have been much happier with some grilled chicken breast. However, the noodles and sauce were tasty and went nicely with the buffalo and blue cheese accents.

The service here is incredible! We were told that there would be a short wait for our table, so we sat out on the patio. While waiting, we were offered a drink from the bar (seems small but we appreciated the offer while waiting). We ordered the Oyster Rockefeller to start and it was delicious! My mom tried to compare it to New Orleans (I wouldn't take it that far but it was good!). I ordered the trio pasta and I literally scraped the plate. My mom ordered the ribeye and it was seasoned to perfection. We finished our meal with a to go order of the key lime pie. Everything was delicious & the service was impeccable. 

I would definitely recommend this place while in St. Pete!

I had the piggy back ride , a Burger topped with pulled pork and coleslaw. Delicious, this is my new favorite burger place. The waffle fries were hot, crispy, and seasoned well. The sweet potato tater tots were served with a vanilla cream and a raspberry sauce and were great! I will come here again many times. The server was also attentive and upbeat.

Penrose has quickly become our Go-to diner when we want a quality meal with the convenience of not going too far! The staff is great you almost feel as if you're an extended family member . My last visit I ordeee the chicken cheese steak with fries and the server suggested I substituted the bread for a wrap, what a great decisión ! The wrap was tasty not too much cheese just the right amount of fried onions and the fries were crispy and delicious.
Decent ramen. Would have enjoyed some more traditional toppings to add on such as bamboo shoots. Great flavor broth, will return. Drinks are a bit overpriced.

We went here for breakfast around noon on a Saturday. It was a really good experience. The staff was kind and helpful. The food was as expected, never anything super special but good for a chain restaurant.

We come every Tuesday for Taco Tuesday and often one other time a week. Their happy hour specials are very good. The $3 hh poppers are so delicious and a great value. Their queso is amazing. Other favorites are the habenero beef enchiladas with the salad, the guacamole wings, all the fish tacos, the carne asada taco on bibb, and the banana churro dessert is incredible. Favorite spot in town hands down. 

Their management, hosts, and servers are all really nice and care.

Restaurant has two kitchens
Mexican and sushi. Ordered 3 sushi rolls and 2 items from the Mexican kitchen.
Salmon with mango salsa and chipotle cream sauce. Camarones a la diabla.
Everything looked and tasted excellent. Also great and pleasant food server Jim added to the experience.
Chef Ramon came and greeted us at the table.
We will come back with friends from L.A.
Great food, eclectic ambiance...wonderful experience.  We are traveling from California and found this lovely gem.  Take some time and treat yourself.

The food was outrageously delicious and fresh. Service was top notch. We can't wait to come back. Tip: I tried getting a reservation 2 months before we came and it was impossible. I put myself on the  waiting list and got a call back the evening before. Can't wait to come back!!!

For casual Italian fare in Philly, Fiorino is as good as it gets! (I'd even venture to say better than some trattitoria's in Italy) I've been a regular at Fiorino since 2011 and am mildy sad that my recent move out of the area means I'll be visiting less. If you are dining on a weekend, I'd advise that you make a reservation as the dining room is very small. The highlight of the meal for me is the pesto they give you with the bread....it is a red (tomato based) pesto that will just knock your socks off. Though it is difficult, don't fill up too much on bread as you'll need room for their many delicious entrees. My favorites include: the spaghetti scoglio, rigatoni amatriciana and the chicken siciliana. For dessert, the bomba is delightful. Be sure to bring your favorite bottle of wine, because its BYOB. If you're lucky, during your visit you may meet Franco (owner & chef) and share a shot of limoncello. Insider tip: go for lunch, the prices are significantly less and protion is comprable.

What a pleasant surprise!  I was stopping by Home Depot for some condo stuff when I noticed Rocco's right in front.  Smelled so good so I went to yelp to check on the reviews.
I ordered spicy sausage with peppers and onions and it was so good!  great sandwich.  Really good bread.  service was nice and quick.  Made it an extra worthwhile trip to Home Depot.
Ordered smoked brisket salad but got burnt. Literally. I usually don't write reviews but this made me so sad. Wouldn't want anyone to experience this.

Delicate, subtle, and delicious Indian cuisine!  Last time i enjoyed indian food this good was in New York.  This place is hands down the best indian in Metro New Orleans.  Nan is thick and soft, spices are not overwhelming like some Indian restaurants in Metro. I ordered the eggplant and a chicken biryana and both were perfectly seasoned, with a light kick.  The raita is very balanced and not heavy on the cumin!!!  Worth a drive to Gretna!!!

Went here on a date and left feeling like it was an average dinner. 

A lot of the 3 star review comes from my confusion of what the restruant is going for. Are they trying to be fancy? Are they trying to be hipster? I could not truly pick up on the vibe based of decorations, plating, colors, and food.

However, almost all the food was delicious! We ordered the huspuppies and Calamari as apps. Both of these were delicious and very filling. (If it is just two people, 2 apps is not needed, they will fill you up before the main course). 

Girlfriend ordered the fish and it was basically perfect! Super flavorful, fresh tasting, and complemented well with the other side items. 

I ordered the cajun pasta and felt that it was lacking in flavor... which should never be the case for a "cajun" pasta. The pasta itself tasted fresh, but the meet was covered up by the bland pasta sauce and no spice could shine through. If you are going here, would not recommend any of the pastas. 

Overall, this place gets a 3 star because of their confusing theme and bland pasta.

The bbq wings are quite good but suspiciously different every time I order them 

The pizza tastes okay-- better than anything else I've tried in the area-- but they never cut it all the way through. Last time we ordered a pizza it came in three pieces: one tiny sliver, one regular-sized slice and then the rest of the pie. How is it even possible to get an odd number of even odder sized slices with a pizza cutter? Incredible.

It also takes at least an hour to get your pizza which means that it's always cold by the time i get it (I live 6 blocks away). 

The delivery people also generally refuse to get out of their cars. Recently I've been playing games of "Chicken" with the delivery guy to see who will make the first move. 

I once had the pleasure of an elderly couple delivering my food. They chastised me for not answering my phone (they had called the wrong number) and wouldn't let me walk away until they had scoured the order paper to make sure I had left a tip on my card.

Oh, and sometimes the delivery guy will call and tell you he's outside when he's actually 10 minutes away.

..but the wings. I really like the wings. Don't get the mild ones-- they're just soaked in orange grease.

I just gave them 5 stars!  It might have been that I was really hungry when I ordered 6 different plates for 3 adults & 2 children at a "family style" restaurant.  Let's just say there was plenty of leftovers to eat for the next day. 

Ok the details... Everything was awesome!!! Seriously, EVERYTHING!!! Service included. Never said this before: Gladly paid $232.00 plus tip.   

Tiger

Came here for a work Christmas party. This was my first visit and it was great. The food was great and the service was good, but o was disappointed with the refilling of my drink. The server did not put more ice in it. I was a server before and I know you always give more ice unless they asked for no ice. 
One negative to a lot more positive things.

Still have never heard from the bakery over a year later except for a Facebook post telling me to call them. Uhm no you call me. I did my due diligence by calling for over a month. I feel like it is your responsibility now to reach out to me but I doubt that will ever happen. I still would never recommend this bakery to anymore not even my worst enemy. Shady business dealing that's for sure!!!!

What an amazing place!  We tried quite a few appetizers and loved them all!!  The peppadew peppers stuffed with herb cheese and an almond was such a great mixture of flavors, the Wagyu Carpaccio was phenom on the bed of truffle cheese & the Maine lobster on a crostini-drool material with its freshness!!!  Can't wait to go back and try some entrees!

After spending $80.00 for lunch, enjoying the shade at a picnic table, we were suddenly approached by the outside bartender, whi began cleaning our table.  Then I believe it was the owner/chef David Cox, who aggressively approached and told us to leave the premises immediately because my dog had been barking at too many people.  The bartender asked if she was a "rescue dog."  As if they are the only dogs who bark.  Then Mr. Cox became aggressive.  He threatened that he would sue me if I ever brought the dog back again.  We were so taken aback that we coukd not get out fast enough.  This establishment does not understand dogs, let it allows them onto the premises.  Trust me folks, this is not a safe place for your dog, and the owner is unstable.  Had he asked us respectfully to take my dog off of the premises, I would have no problem with that and I would not have been scared.

Soup, Sandwiches, and Cakes sized for a Giant is what you'll find here.

Established in 1923 and easily rivaling the NYC Delicatessens, this is the place to be if you are in Philly and craving a (non-Philly-Cheesesteak) sandwich. 

Like any other authentic Deli, you get a bowl of Pickles and Health Salad (Coleslaw sans mayo). I can live on just these alone, Mmm! We ordered the Famous Chicken Soup (w/ Matzo Ball) and let me tell you, its no soup, its a tub, it was so HUGE! We drank and drank and drank, it was so delicious! The matzo ball, the chicken, the pasta, the veggies, the BROTH ~ Mmm!

We ordered the Pastrami and Chopped Liver Sandwich. The Famous Chopped Liver has fried onions, horseradish and chopped eggs in it - also good but doesn't stay as long in the fridge, maybe 1 day. 

These 2 sandwiches, along with the soup fed 4 AND we had leftovers to take home. They are seriously that big. We've never ordered the cake but the samples were delicious and the slices were nearly a foot wide!

This place is small and makes you feel at home with the friendly staff and cozy atmosphere. It's a must try!

* Check out my pics and you'll want to go there TODAY!

My boyfriend thinks this place has the best bacon he's ever eaten. Enough said right? He and I shared a breakfast plate (we got 2 eggs, bacon, potatoes and then also split a scone). I think if we're ever back in Santa Barbara we'd definitely stop in again. It's good sized portions and reasonably priced. The wait wasn't really anything at all on a Sunday during brunch.

As two SB residents, we felt El Paseo was the perfect location for a classy, festive, and all-around Santa Barbarian wedding; the venue did not disappoint.  The manager Paul was very thorough, which was really reassuring during the planning process.  I'll admit - I'm a little Type A with my planning, so knowing that Paul was organized (but not overbearing) was great. We met multiple times and he provided lots of sample photos and ideas.  

When the day came, he knew exactly what we wanted and orchestrated everything with the DJ to ensure the day went off without a hitch.  He also kept us abreast of our bar tab throughout the night (so we could switch to cash bar and have no unpleasant surprises).  

Alex, the chef, worked with us to ensure we picked unique entrees that we liked.  The guests loved the food and we received lots of compliments.  

The venue had so many wonderful photo-ops and everyone had a blast.  We'd highly recommend El Paseo for your event!

The "Shack" part of the name is no joke! Restaurant has a classic old Florida-beach-bar feel to it (complete with picnic tables indoors). 

Oysters are always fresh and delicious! Garlic butter blue crab claws (appetizer menu) are a necessity. All-you-can-eat crab legs (with fries and cole slaw) during snow crab season is the best deal around! Cole slaw is fabulous, as well. Their blackened grouper sandwich is perfection. Garlic butter steamed WHOLE blue crabs are awesome, if you know how to open them! 

Service is hit or miss here. A few great servers, and one or two who couldn't care less about their tables. Have had to ask for water, silverware, and my check repeatedly on more than one occasion. Food is still worth the trip, though!

The hookah is reasonably priced and the variety of flavors is good. They allow mixing of flavors which is nice given some places charge more to do that, and there was no up charge to have multiple people per pipe.
They have a wide variety of food options but we didn't try anything.
The atmosphere was fine, they were watching a soccer game with the non-English announcer shouting the news but it wasn't too distracting.

I like the McCrossen's as an idea better than I've liked it in actuality the few times I've been there.  It's a pretty low key neighborhood place. On the one hand, unpretentious.  On the other, a little pretense (bone marrow!).  I'm writing now based on a visit yesterday during happy hour.  The bar is comfortable and for a Friday evening, was empty in a pleasant way.  The beer prices for the happy hour specials were great.  The beer selection is not extensive, but totally good.  The service was adequate; but it had a cliquish feel which is to say that though the bar was nowhere near full it looked like folks who were getting the good service were those familiar with the bartender.  I'm not saying it was unwelcoming, just uneven and slower than it needed to be given the lack of crowd.  The menu is pretty unfriendly to vegetarians;  I'm not sure why.  With bone marrow on the menu, I'd think the kitchen could come up with something other than hummus for the vegetarian option.  That's the only choice if you don't want a cheese plate or salad.  (Actually, in fairness, there was a vegetarian soup on the specials board.)  The hummus was fine; smooth and standard.  Not really spiced (i.e., no garlic) but fine.  The plate was nice with olives, peppers, garlic and some vegetables.   My partner had the chicken sandwich.  It was lackluster.  More bread than needed for the size of the chicken, he reported, as he left half of the roll on the plate.  The french fries weren't fully cooked and weren't great, either.  I would go again if in the neighborhood, but I wouldn't go out of my way to go there.  Also, one other thing I thought was curious.  They have a drink on the menu -- the purple orchid, or something.  The ingredients are listed as including white wine.  It didn't appeal to me.  But, then I watched the bartender make one, and Lillet was the "white wine."  Sure, I see the connection, but having Lillet as the base isn't quite the same as having "white wine" as the base.  I thought it odd the menu didn't specify.

Omg! Omg!! I never had a Banh Mi until someone introduced me to it and I was able to taste a bit of theirs. I had a hankering for a half n half shrimp and oyster poboy with fries. Browsing on the UberEats app, I saw Banh Mi Boys offered poBoys, and I also saw they of course had Banh Mi's. The bang bang shrimp looked so yummy, and their oyster Rockefeller fries intrigued me, so I ordered those. I was basically getting everything I was looking for. 

Once my food arrived, everything was still hot... from Metairie, to LGD! The Rockefeller fries came in a brown to go box with ventillation, and one set was closed, one set was open to make sure the fries stayed warm, but didn't get soggy. Genius! The Rockefeller sauce was served on the side in this huge container; unfortunately, I don't remember what the sauce consisted of, but it too was hot, thick, and flavorful. 

So, the bang bang shrimp banh mi was so damn good!!! Everything was fresh, and I was able to taste every ingredient. Nothing was overpowering. I was able to taste the spicy fresh jalapeños, and the cool cilantro cooled my mouth from the spice, the crisp cucumber and pickled carrot provided some crunch from the soft duong bread and shrimp. The shrimp itself was seasoned to perfection with a slight kick. I debated ordering extra shrimp because I saw it was served with only 5-6. I passed, and with good reason, this meal was quite filling and I feel that more shrimp would make the sandwich fall apart, and be a bit overpowering. 
The oyster Rockefeller fries were so yummy! There were about 6 fries in the container piled high with fries seasoned with cheese and green onions. Since the sauce came on the side, I used it sparingly, along with a bit of ketchup. The fries were $8, which is not bad because it would cost $8 just for oysters.


All in all, I am a fan of Banh Mi Boys, and cant wait to try the restaurant dine in experience.

I stop in to this mini-location when seeking out local gifts for loved ones.  The selection is not as huge as at the airport location or online, but they typically have a unique flavor or two that are of interest (you can never go wrong with the Smoking Goose cheddar-caramel-bacon mix).  My favorite product is the "Indy is for Lovers" 4-pack of small bags, each a different flavor reflecting a local Indy business (Sun King Dark Chocolate Osiris, 4 Birds Oatmeal Cookie, aforementioned Smoking Goose, and Bazbeaux Tomato-Basil). Unfortunately, Just Pop In tends to only have these stocked in-person around Christmas.  The store assistants are always friendly and efficient.  Just watch out for that huge front step as you enter...I've tripped on it once or twice.

Really good Thai! I had the chicken red curry and the husband had Pad Kee Mao and Thai Tea. All were really good and perfect amount of spicy for the stars ordered. I'm a wimp and the 2 made my neck sweat - as expected. 2 for 1 wine happy hour daily 3:30-6:30 too. Staff was really friendly!

I literally jus left this place!... This place is nothing but awesome!!... I love everything I had ordered tonight.. everything was great!!.. even my eef salad Togo.. the sauce, the beef, and the veggies all came in separate container... how awesome is that?!!... had drinks.. salad.. fried banana wit coconut ice cream.. fried red snapper wit  sweet chilli sauce.. yummy roll n a salad togo.. that's alot of food for $50bucks!... good food.. great service.. n reasonable cost!.. Def. coming back!... n I live in lutz!!....
Delicious and amazing all around . Especially to Jerry at the bartender he was excellent and made our dining experience above and beyond .. a must eat in NOLA!

Bredenbeck's designed and baked the cake for my father-in-law's 500 thousand party. Yes, that's right...the party we threw him when his '96 Chevy Impala hit 500 thousand miles. Bredenbeck's baked us a cake that was an exact replica of the car. It was gorgeous...almost too beautiful to eat! But we did eat it...for a whole week. And that chocolate pound cake hasn't left my thoughts since.

We ate at Mopho twice while vacationing in New Orleans. We live in San Francisco and have access to great/cheap Vietnamese food and we had high expectations for Mopho based on its history. Our first trip was for lunch and it was really, really good. I had the vegetarian pho and the broth was beyond excellent. It was one of the best bowls of pho I've ever eaten.
