No apologies. No refunds. And $35 later I decided no food was worth the frustration that is their customer service. 
I really hope the owner(s) sees this and either retrains their staff or hires new members. Everything else they've done with the place is amazing. I would love to start coming back here again, but I can't afford to throw away my money.

I love this place. love love love it. Great space, great food, great beer. While the menu isn't ALWAYS perfect, it's 99.9999% and that is good enough for me. The beers aren't cheap, so the bill ends up being pretty high each time we go, but it's so worth it. 

This time we had dinner, but Varga has a awesome BRUNCH MENU, but you can't find their menu online. So i posted 2 pics of the menu so you can read. 

WHAT WE ATE
*truffled mac 'n cheese
i heart truffles (the mushroom and the chocolate candy). i heart mac 'n cheese. so, honestly... HOW could we resist the truffled mac 'n cheese at varga? you're right - we couldn't. SO GOOD.
Don't get it twisted. it's not my ultimate favorite - that title still rests with the mac 'n cheese at silk city. however, this was pretty damn close. the cheese sauce was creamy and the top was crunchy in the best way - with BACON pieces. this tastes like TRUFFLES like WHOA, though. so if you're not a black truffle fan, you will not like this.  

*jumbo lump cheese fries
personally, i didn't enjoy these that much. the fries themselves were awesome. they were thin and crispy and, at the risk of angering foodies everywhere, i must say, were similar to mcdonald's fries. even the cheese was tasty. i am a sucker for white cheddar so that is not surprising. the sad part is that it was the lump crab meat that really detracted from this dish. i understand that the crab meat is the gimmick- the thing that makes this so different and FRESH, but... it tasted... CRABBY. maybe it's not like this all the time, but ours definitely had a fishy taste to it that wasn't really that pleasant. i found myself taking fries and avoiding the pieces of crab.

*duck confit chicken wings
THESE. WERE. A-MAAAAAZING. serious contender for my favorite wings. the pomegranate molasses-bourbon-chili (isn't that a mouthful?) sauce was incredible - sweet! tart! tangy! they were a bit on the heavily sauced side, but it was such a tasty flavor that i did not mind one bit. and the wings... they were just falling off the bone. you could literally take your fork and pull of pieces! super tender and juicy. PLUS, bonus - they actually give you a good number of celery sticks. in most places, you get three sad little ones.

*kobe beef sliders
AWESOME. something about that soft, creamy boursin with the chewy salty bacon and juicy kobe beef... * drooOOooOOOool * ... okay, i've pulled myself together now.. is SO GOOD. the onion rings were a delightful crunchy, salty side to this burger. this order usually comes with 3 burgers, but we asked them to add one extra slider and they did. 3 sliders are usually $12, and they only upcharged us $4 for the 4th one.

*kobe chili-cheese dog
MEH. hot dog was juicy/flavorful, but everything else was not noticeable. There was VERY LITTLE chili. sad. i suppose that is what happens when you make your chili out of kobe beef, but STILL.
IMO, in an optimal chili cheese dog combination, i'd say the serving ratios are as follows: 3 parts chili : 2 parts cheese : 1 part hot dog.
Good, but not great so we'd probably skip it next time

*beers
varga bar's beer selection really is remarkable. the four of us represented a wide range of beef affinities - stouts, pale ales, wheats, pilsners - but we could all still find something we really enjoyed off of the list. and the server, dour and sullen though he was, still had great knowledge of the beers available and what we might like.

Stopped in for lunch. I'm surprised by the 5 stars given, my burger was warm and really no flavor, was lacking salt. The fries were ok but then again no flavor. Our server was very nice but she was helping the bartender make bloody Mary's so let's just say service was ok. I don't think I'll be back, the menu was ok but nothing really stood out.

This is a cute place to hang out and eat.  The ambiance was warm and cozy.  The food was decent, but in my opinion, a little on the bland side.  I had the carbonara, and I've definitely had a lot better around the same price range.  With that said, the food was still good and the service was good.
Great Mexican food and atmosphere. Slow service but a must try if you live in Tucson.

Amazing service. For such a busy large place everyone was awesome. Brussels were awesome as was the hanger steak.  Only reason 4 stars was the pork belly dish was tiny and one of the pieces was 100% fat. Great pot de creme.  Would give 4.5 if I could.
Here for big ten championship game...massively understaffed. Really, between msu and osu fans you thought ONE bartender at 4:00pm for the top floor was sufficient? Hire some damn bartenders

WOW. Everything was absolutely splendid at Moto. We had a reservation and were quickly seated. Our waiter was incredibly friendly and gave us great suggestions. We weren't sure how much to order, but started with Brussel sprouts and the spaghetti pomodoro. We also ordered a pizza, but he waited to put in the order until after we had eaten our pomodoro then asked us if we were still hungry. We ended up being full and decided to not get the Margherita. How nice was that of him to do that?! Not pushing us to order more food, he truly wanted us to enjoy the whole experience. He split the pomodoro for me and my mom to share too. The Brussel sprouts were so good. It had a strong balsamic vinegar taste with the right crispiness. We couldn't stop eating it. The pasta was so fresh and a good portion to leave me full but not overly stuffed. I will definitely be back!

As others have noted, the food was incredible, but the service was leisurely. In Bayona's defense, the pace of life in New Orleans is more laid back than my home region of New England, and slow service seems the norm here. That said, several people in our party were uncomfortably warm in the attic dining room where we sat, and the server was not quick to help remedy the situation.

Oh, but the food was really good. I shared a gratin appetizer featuring oysters, greens, and sausage, then moved on to the special rabbit dish. I had initially ordered the red snapper special, but the waiter let us know he did not have enough of them for the several of us who'd ordered it; I switched to the rabbit and did not regret it. My sister-in-law let me snag a smoked quail leg from her salad and it may have been THE best thing I tasted at Bayona. The bread and sweet potato muffins served with dinner were also fresh and delicious. Desserts were the culinary low point, despite being pretty good themselves; we shared a chocolate hazelnut tarte, deconstructed carrot cake, and lemon buttermilk pie. The pie was the best of the three by far.

I also liked the rioja we drank and the glass of sherry I enjoyed with dessert. Bayona has an extensive wine list and I liked the decor of the open wine shelving around the attic dining room, although I was curious how they keep the bottles at temperature in such a warm space.

Overall, I'd recommend Bayona for a special meal. The food is too good not to try. I'd probably ask to be seated downstairs in the hope of a more comfortable environment.

Another great dinner! With so many great restaurants in Philly, I don't return to the same restaurant often. But for Italian, this may just be my fav (and I live in the Italian market). I love the servers here and the owner is always there and takes great pride in delivering a great meal. The bread and olive oil is perfect. I've enjoyed every meal here a little too much. My only problem on my most recent dining experience was that I practically licked my plate clean before going dancing so it kept my belly very full and slowed down my buzz. I love that it's byob.
Best mexican food in PA. Tacos al pastor traditional are my favorite. Nachos and fajitas are awesome. Service is quick. Prices are affordable.

So let's talk about their croissants... so crispy so fluffy and the blueberry preserves are such a great +1 to this mouth party. Also another great addition is their blueberry coffee. I am normally a regular black cup of coffee guy but this blueberry brew was so good! Definitely a must try. I thought the avocado broken yolk sandwich was like a 7/10 but the wheat toast was great and the egg lived up to its name, it exploded right when I bit into it. All and all I will be having a cup of joe and a bite to eat here again.

This restaurant was okay. I had the Blackened Chicken Pasta and it was good, bugging out of this world but it was good. The crab cakes however were soo salty and soo fishy. We didn't return them cause we are not ballsy but we did not eat them.

Good food - struggling with customer experience. I discovered this new restaurant (which looks vacant even from the sidewalk directly in front of it) a few weeks ago and have gone back several times. The food overall is pretty good -- our favorite meal  so far was a perfectly toasted bacon and grilled cheese sandwich on really yummy bakery bread with fries cooked to perfection. The menu seemed a bit...pretentious, however. What sort of restaurant charges "market price" for a salad??

Another typical visit was for Sunday brunch with my family and it was obvious the staff had not been properly trained. The large restaurant was nearly empty, but the hostess tried to seat us immediately adjacent to another (full) table which would have been noisy and required squeezing in. Although nice, our server was not able to answer basic questions like "can I substitute a salad for fries" and when she told us she'd have to ask the kitchen it was necessary to gently suggest she do so and come back with the answer. (No salad  but they did grill vegetables).  When I asked for decaf I was told they don't have it. (Were they out? Is it beneath them? Can they not afford two coffee pots?)  The brunch items we ordered were decent, although this time my grilled cheese was not perfect - the cheese had mostly run out into a gloppy pile at the edge of the bread and the edges of the bacon were significantly burned. A good meal, but not an excellent one. 

The fourth time I tried to go to this restaurant was when I called for takeout. (My son really liked that grilled cheese sandwich.) There is NO phone number on their website. I thought this was crazy until I called and was told they don't do takeout,  (seriously??) but I was welcome to order there and sit and wait for my food. Needless to say, I called my standby, Le Buzz, and this small, struggling restaurant lost what might have been 1-2 lunch orders a week and a great deal of customer goodwill. I'll probably go back, but my enthusiastic wish to support a new local business has pretty much evaporated in the face of their rigid business approach.

i had doubts but was convinced to get a burger from here.  I had the mushroom swiss add bacon.  it was DEFINITELY ONE TO TELL EVERYONE ABOUT!!!! IT was delicious!!  A bit pricey for the "broke-folks-until-payday" like myself but i will be going back!

Can't afford to have some drinks and dance here since I was DENIED WATER! Like any responsible adult I alternate my cocktails with a glass of water, however I was told by the rude manager that the OWNER has a policy AGAINST serving water in the night club, where people are dancing and drinking alcohol. As a bartender, I know this is unethical. As an informed citizen, I'm surprised this hasn't lead to a lawsuit.
Food was cold, portion was small. Worst Ethiopian food I have ever had, and I have had plenty of Ethiopian food in my life time.

I've long been used to playing the All You Can Eat game. You get less fish, more rice, but you still walk away feeling satisfied.

Today boundaries were crossed. Sadness was generated.

I ordered my first of two plates and it took thirty minutes to arrive. So I handed over my second form, figuring it would take a while for more food to arrive. In this case it took less than five. No big deal. Service wasn't awful either so the place gets a 3.

But what that gave me the opportunity to notice was just how much rice had been added to the second batch of nigiri. These pieces were loaded up with so much rice that it was almost impossible, and somewhat uncomfortable, to eat in a bite. I removed some rice from each piece to make doing so possible again, and waited to see if they'd implement their per-piece charge for leaving food behind, which they didn't.

So, yeah. If you like rice, this is the place to go.
Great food and super friendly! Had chicken and pulled pork. Would recommend all sides!

Good lunch specials!  

About $10 for a good salad, soda and 10" pizza.  I opted for the Caesar instead of the house salad and I'm glad I did as it looked better than the house salads at the table.  Not overly dressed but with a nice hint of black pepper to wake up the flavors.  Very fresh!

Next up was the pizza.  I asked for sausage & onions.  The onion slices were uniform and about 1/8" thick such that they were very easy to see, slightly sweet from cooking and not overpowering.  The sausage was of the finer, crumbly variety.  A little different than what I unusually like but a decent enough substitute.  Vaguely reminiscent of some of the flat pizza I had in a few dives in Chicago.  For some reason, STL pizza needs to come with a very basic tomato sauce and this place was no exception.  The crust was slightly salty and a little bit chewy - just about right as far as flat pizza goes...

Nice atmosphere.. Ok food... weird wait staff...liked this place better when it was old location.... Marginal foid... Marginal service... Goid location... Nice seating outside... Fire most wait staff keep buspeople and hostesses...

Well that was more than disappointing. Had to go back because the ahi I ordered smelled so bad it was not edible. Returned home with a beef bowl and brown rice. 90% of the veggies were broccoli and cabbage. Yeah! Very little carrot or zucchini. Staff was great just wish the food was as good. Save the money find a good Mongolian place. At least it will have flavor.

This is my second time at this place, and it might very well become a required stop each time I travel int he Tampa area!  Food is delicious, service great, and if the weather is noce (as in not too hot and humid...  It is Florida after all), I'd recommend eating on teh patio outside!  Best view ever!
Makes for a very relaxing and positive eating experience!

I attended Gentle Ben's on gameday (ASU vs. UA nonetheless) and like fellow diner Kristen S., had the worst possible restaurant experience of my life.  I used to serve tables so I was used to making sure that customers got the best experience possible and if the service or food was not up to par, they were compensated for it.

However, this certainly was not the case for my experience here. 

My drink did not come out until the meal (40 min after I ordered) and I was forced to chug it down in order to make gametime. Unfortunately, I should not have chugged it down because it turns out that due to the extremely slow service, I would not make it out of the restaurant until 6:15. Fifteen minutes after kickoff and about an 1:45 minutes after we were sat. (We ordered as soon as we were sat at 4:50).

The food that my table ordered did not come out the way it was supposed to and even the food that did come out ok was horrible tasting.  I spent 9 dollars for a dry hamburger on a week old bun. Absolutely not worth the money.

My table also spoke to management about the issues we were having and they did not seem to be in the least concerned that their customers were disatisfied. Never had I ever been to a restaurant that didn't put their customer's concerns first. 

If you are looking for a good experience on University, DO NOT GO TO GENTLE BENS. You will only receive mediocre food AT BEST.  I would highly recommend Frog n' Firken for a much more enjoyable meal as well as better customer service.

I always thought this place would look like an "old fashion dinner" with lots of fried food and was I wrong. Came here on a Sunday morning there was a long line of people waiting outside to be seated so I assumed that meant the food must be good or there is no other place open at this time. We decided to go on the wait list which was approximately 20-25 minutes. The wait  to sit seemed shorter than the time we waited for the food but the food was great. I love that I can order just one piece of French toast or pancakes and not be forced to eat a full plate. I ordered one French Toast topped with chocolate chips (fantastic), the smoked salmon (not too salty) and a pink grapefruit mimosa. The waitress was very friendly and definitely knew the menu. great place for breakfast, the burger in the lunch menu was also good and if you like Bloody Mary's you should try theirs. I found this place to be very loud so if you're looking for a quiet, conversation place this may not be your to go spot.

Extremely pleased by how my event went at the Napa Room at Seasons 52. Ellen was incredible helpful while planning and the two dedicated server and manager who helped with AV were all very attentive and helpful. The room as we layer it out easily sits 30+ and we had a great deal with the flatbreads, wine, and apps such as truffle Mac and cheese, hummus, Greek salad, and avocado toast
Thank you so much Dax for the great service!!!!! Super attentive and friendly. Plus everything was delicious

Last night my boyfriend and I decided to stop by due to friends meeting up here. Immediately you notice the male bartender is rude, obnoxious, and literally yells at customers. We've all been to a crowded bar where you wait forever for your drinks but this place wasn't even packed and people are just standing with money in their hands patiently and he's yelling at them "You aren't the only guy in the bar!" I just kept staring at him in disbelief. (I've been in the restaurant/bar industry for almost 10 years) The female bartender was super friendly, funny, and seemed to have no complaints about how her night was going. 
We ordered the same two types of beers and one type of shot the entire time we were there. So every time we paid it was $3 per beer (we bought two at a time) and 1 $5 shot. At last call the male bartender was even mad we ordered one more round and when he brought us our two beers and a shot it was $12 instead of $11. Now, here me out. It's a $1 and what can you really do with a dollar besides tip a bartender? Not much. But I politely looked at my boyfriend and said that's not right the male bartender (who I wasn't even speaking too) freaked out and threw the dollar back at us. Almost like we hadn't tipped all night. (We tip a dollar per drink, every round.) I slide the dollar back towards him and stepped away. He continued to yell and make sure the entire bar knew we where "worried" about a dollar. The female bartender came to me and asked what happened and if I was okay and I said I'm fine and didn't want to explain what happened. Needless to say, I've never been a fan and try not to go to the bar but I definitely will not be going back again.

We LOVE THIS PLACE!!! Food always fresh and unique, margaritas are delicious  you only need 2  
Awesome services and food, high recommend!

Definitely not the best cheese steak in the area, but it's a fun touristy place to stop. Just bring gobs of cash.

Basically, you walk up to one window where you order your steak (my fave is whiz with onions). You fork over $8.50 - then you wait on line at the next window and order fries and a drink - and fork over another 8 bucks or so. Then you try and hold the steak, cup of fries and soda while wandering around looking for a free table or loitering in front of people that appear to be finishing up. It is a bit of a juggling act. There is no indoor seating or bathroom to speak of.

They do take credit cards, but it takes longer to process and you get lots of dirty looks from the cashier and people in line behind you. Tip: Have your cash out and ready for when you step to the window.

I get hoagies at Al's all the time. I never had a better hoagie in my life! The price is low, and the hoagie is PACKED! It's the BEST hoagie place there is!  :D

~Cindy!  :)
..

Love the view and atmosphere !! 
Too bad don't accept reservation!!!

I went there for my BD and got a free ice cream (: super thick and was able to share with all my friends (total 11ppl ) lol

Recommend their signature breakfast -had crab cake !!!

This place is just fantastic! Used to go to the one in Northern Liberties all the time for sandwiches. This location is just as great. The hoagies are the BEST! Seriously, great bread, great Boars Head meat...you can't go wrong

I was referred here this afternoon by my usual car wash, AutoWash Express, which was bought out by Miles.  They are redoing the Cool Springs car wash.  
I drove up to the automated machine which gave different options for quick washes.  There was no explanation what the various Express Washes consisted of.  I chose Express Wash 2. When I got the attention of an attendant, he told me what the wash included, stuff I didn't really want.  I and was told to drive through and go to the right.  I was expecting to have the car towel dried at least, but no one was there.  You turn to the right and exit.  I need to find a new car wash.
Great Peruvian food. Love the lomo soltado and the comfort food that is served. I would recommend this place to anyone that enjoys Peruvian food.

The employees here are the best. They are so nice. One time I only had $5 on me for food and my total was $5.01. They rustled up a floor penny so I could eat like a King that day. My fav employee is Carolyn, u go girl! I've been here a dozen times and love coming in here for some grub.

Went here for the first time when they opened and we received excellent customer service. The crab naan is amazing and you can choose your spice level for any of the food. 

When we returned last night, the staff remembered us and presented us with the same great customer service. 

The food is really good!! I would highly recommend trying here if you are a fan of Indian food!

This is a solid restaurant.  The portion sizes are large and one definitely gets one's money's worth.  I ate breakfast with my host here many times, often getting their breakfast discounts (Mondays through Thursdays, I think), which are a great value.  I got waffles with eggs and bacon.  I got gravy biscuits with eggs--excellent.  And, some other things.  I ate dinner here once this trip.  The portion of salmon was huge with a sauce with capers, and lots of mash potatoes and corn.  At first, the price seems reasonable to high, but with the amount of food, it is really two meals.  

The service was pretty good.  Funny and nice lady server.  She was grouchy once.  haha.  Pay at the counter.  Plenty of seating and enough privacy.  Walk in and seat oneself down.  Fast service and food comes quickly.

The menu is large and it's open 24/7.  If you like gambling, locals come here and you could do that too. I don't know about the deserts.

I will definitely be returning.

Very nice beer selection.  Bison Burger is great and recommended. 
Service was just ok.

I do not really enjoy eating at this restaurant. The tables are very close to each other and there is not much room people walking by brush against you while you're eating. The food is okay but if you go in the evening it is very loud and there are many people who are drunk I have even seen people making out on the Dance Floor and throwing up outside on the sidewalk. It is really more of just a bar and is not a place I would want to go back to
Love aunt pollys salad.  I thought the pizza guy was OCD, but it turns out that "consistency is key"- he probably would never franchise out of fear they would ruin his creation.

Two of my sisters and myself  drove over to St Louis to vist Sweetie Pies  Upper Crust on Thursday, 07/12/12 and it was well worth the trip.  The staff was upbeat and friendly.  They were taping while we were there so Ms Robbie, Charles and Andre were all there.  Charles is cute enough to be a model and Andre is a doll, as well. Ms Robbie is a fabulous old girl like myself.  The chicken wings, mac and cabbage was to die for and the southern styled cornbread was wonderful.  I tried the Pear Cobbler but I didn't fall in love with it.  My sisters and I enjoyed our visit so much that  we went back on Saturday before we drove back to Indianapolis and bought some dinners to bring home for our families to try.  We put the dinners in a cooler for the 3 1/2 hour drive home.  This time, we tried the banana pudding and it did not disappoint.  It would be nice of the City of St Louis would invest a little money in upgrading the sidewalks and the streets at the front of the building but in a nut shell--Bravo for Sweetie Pies' Upper Crust. Thanks for the good food, good time and the pictures.

Nomnomnom definitely satisfied my sushi craving, its pricing was pretty standard but that lunch special though ! Pretty cheap for a lot of food :) the service was good the waiter was super nice! If you have a semi big party I would definitely recommend getting a private booth!

Soybean beckons guests with an elegant decor, friendly wait staff and excellent service. We're huge fans of Thai cuisine, and were more than excited to find Soybean right in our neighborhood. We've never been disappointed with the meals. The kids love the Pad Thai, while hubby and me indulge in Thai curries which are just great! Try their roti canai, the sizzling Tom Yum Koong and Pad Kra Pao. A complimentary, authentic Thai salad with peanut dressing comes with your lunch order. At times, they offer steamed edamame... YUM! A small bar is within premises - they offer domestic and imported beers, along with house red and white wines.
They have a pretty good cheesesteak but that is about it. The rest of the food is just average at best. They are okay with their pricing.

Person answering the phone taking orders was rude. French fries was over cooked and the burger was not all that. I had to wait for my food and it wasn't fresh. I don't know if the place has changed owners but there food used to be really good. I don't know what happen.

Their chocolate bombs are fantastic (giant cookies that are super chocolatey and a little salty--perfect!). My favorite dish is their Thai peanut salad with grilled chicken added on. I always love everything I get there. Great place!
Very good service, surf and turf Benedict had a very small piece of steak. Chocolate chip pancakes are just topped with chocolate, not baked in.
This place is great.  Kareoke night is loads of fun.  Friendly bartenders and cheap booze.  Gotta love it.

Pretty fun picnic casual atmosphere but with great service (oddly except for the person taking orders at the register).  The food is seasoned well and several sauces are at the tables to try with it.  The sides were pretty good and the drink selections were also interesting.  Definitely would come back.

Ugh Freaky SLOW!! Pulled up to drive through, placed order no problem. One car in front of me waiting. Took them forever to get their sandwiches. So when I pull up the cashier (Jessica) just stares at me. I said "how much" and she says "I don't know what you ordered". WTF Didn't I just place my order like 5 minutes ago....So I tell her and pay and I sit and I sit. See another chick stocking supplies and I finally beep my horn "uhm is someone making my sandwich". Jessica looks at me - "Yeah" I sit and I sit, finally after 10 minutes I get my sandwich. Not Rocket Science folks!!

Sometimes, it seems like the stars align for just an instant.

At least, that's how how it seemed at Union 30 in the lobby of Hotel St Louis. I'll admit that I'm a guy of particular tastes. As I've said before, I'm often disappointed when trying a place about which others rave. Sometimes I'm just in a mood. But sometimes, just sometimes, things strike me just freakin' right. Enter Union 30.

Ok, yes, I only had two items in this happy hour setting. But y'know what? They nailed it. NAILED IT. And by "they", I'm referring to Lucas and Danny behind the bar, and to whomever is responsible for the wondrous alchemy back in the kitchen.

So, the two items?

Smoked Manhattan and Spam Fries.

That's right, I said Spam. Don't judge me. Or, as they used to say back in the '70s, Don't knock it 'til you've tried it.

Typically I'd exhaust my storehouse of adjectives offering up an impressionist's image of the dish, but this time? No.

Just go. And order them. And smile. And silently thank me.

Way behind on this but I still can't stop raving about this place.  Visited here with family for an Easter brunch and it was divine.  I was absolutely blown out of the water by the interior and exterior of this space.  From the construction-filled Frankford Ave. entrance you wouldn't expect something like this.  Gorgeous tile/ceilings, plants, shelving, knick-knacks, lighting, inside to outside open air space...everything is so pretty.  But the best part was that amazing garden/patio space out back that's so massive it has its own outdoor bar, fire pits, couches, restrooms, etc., and reaches all the way back to the El.  Crazy.

Now enough about the ambiance, on to the food.  I came here on the recommendation to just try their homemade pastries and coffees, so we obviously started with a sampling of that, as well as some herbal teas.  Teacups, coffee mugs, and china were all lovely and ornate.  We all loved our flavorful pastries that were baked so delicate and fine (strawberry galette, labne coffee cake, linzer bar and one with green cardamom), but we all agreed our favorite was that wonderfully spiced, moist coffee cake.

For entrees, we did a mix of breakfast and lunch items: kafta kebab platter with hummus & pita and tabouleh, kafta kebab sandwich & spiced fries, lahm bi-ajeen man'oushe flatbread with a yolky egg on top, and the gravlax man'oushe flatbread. Everything was delicious and seasoned perfectly.  My flatbread with the yolky egg was the perfect hangover cure.  Sampled my guests' dishes and that hummus was probably the best I've had in recent memory.

Staff was very professional and welcoming and I spotted floor managers and bussers and waiters zipping in and out of the kitchen on their A game.  

Foyer/bakery area has even more seating for dining, but I highly recommend making a reservation.  The place is huge but fills up fast with large parties.  There's a bonus little gift shop here with all sorts of cute stuff for everyone on your list.

I'm dying to go back on a hot summer night and have cocktails in that romantic & gorgeous outdoor patio strung with lights.

First review, only for the beer side of the bar:

If you're a beer geek - or even if you're a novice - GET ON OVER HERE.  The beer list is impeccably crafted, and the bartenders know what they're   talking about.  Tons of stuff you've never heard of, but you will be guided through the options.  Stopped in for a Cuvee Des Jacobins Rouge and a Mikkerler Limencello IPA.

The free sweet popcorn at the bar rules.

Will probably be here a lot during Beer Week, so i'll return with a review of food, but so far, so awesome!

Complete awesomeness! If you have ever traveled to Hawaii you know shave ice! These are super authentic and the real deal! So many flavors to choose from, my children love pink and blue bubble gum, cake batter, blue vanilla and blue raspberry! My husband really enjoys flavors like coffee with a snow cap(condensed milk) and chocolate! Oh and you have to get with the scoop of vanilla ice cream on the bottom! The establishment is very clean and the staff and owners are very nice and accommodating. Prices are great too! Definitely worth visiting over and over  
 Added note: if you are from New York City, these are piraqua's, icees like you get from the street cart, but now imagine if that man had flavors like cake batter and bubble gum? So yeah..these are pretty awesome

We LOVED everything about our meal last night. The waiter was super attentive and kind, the atmosphere was great and the food was awesome. We ordered the escargot to try something different and it was SOO good. Not what either of us expected at all, but I will absolutely get it again. I dipped the rest of our bread in it to soak up every last drop. I ordered the paparadelle based on others reviews and was really happy with it. My husband ordered the gnocchi in vodka and added crab and shrimp to it. I can't say enough about how happy we were. We love to go to Philly to try new places and I feel like we had that same great experience in our backyard. We will absolutely be back!

Not sure why, there are so many reviews, or management has made adjustments from the past. In town visiting from Los Angeles, and staying at the hotel next door. Came in last night at 8.30, with a party of 8, and when we get to the door, there was a sign that the restaurant was closing at 9pm that evening, instead of 11pm. Not wanting to be rushed out the door, I've checked in with the host, and he said that we were welcomed to stay past 9pm. The host and waitress were very welcoming and very friendly. After reading some reviews, I was afraid about the quality of the food. But I have to say, that everything was excellent! Came back today, to watch a football game on tv, and everyone was wonderfully and accommodating!!! The manager Ernie has been going around the restaurant, saying hi to patrons, and stop by us, to chit chat about our staying in Nashville. The staff is working hard and I highly suggest this great place!!!

This is a hidden gem in downtown Boise with a very simple idea: you choose your pasta type and you choose your sauce, both of which are made in house with great skill. The food is delicious and the service Antonio provides is first rate. Check this place out, you will be glad you did.
Affordable buffet with great spread of veg and vegan dishes. Come in, stuff your face, it's great :) humble little restaurant
GREAT experience here. Got the "America's best" biscuit and a Bloody Mary and it was at my table within 3 minutes. Super yummy and affordable!
The only place that I could find online with liver and onions on the menu. Very clean and cute restaurant and friendly, sweet staff.

Decided to go to cap off a night in Old City before going back over to Rittenhouse Square with my boyfriend and am glad I did.

We ordered steak quesadillas and a bacon cheeseburger which were both to perfection. Our waitress, albeit eccentric, was also on par and a sweetheart despite it being 2:30 in the morning. 

Remembered why I love this place. fer sure.

If I could give this place a half star, I would, but the description of "A-Ok" doesn't quite do it for me. It seems a bit TOO positive.

When this location was Tapioca Express, I think the service was just a little better - the girl that NEVER smiles and is always rude was still working there (and still IS working there), but there were enough OTHER smiling faces to make up for it. My first impression of the place (I got a milk tea with large boba/tapioca balls) was that it was over priced. I remember getting these delicious drinks all of the time in San Francisco when I lived there, and not paying so darn much (and definitely not getting a drink with SO much ice, like I did here). Then I had to remind myself: They can have their prices higher, because they don't have competition in this silly little town of Reno.

When they switched over to Nam Van, I gave them another try. I saw a few of the same faces, but the service seriously dipped - no one ever smiled, people were rude and rushed you, they didn't care to give explanations for the rising prices if you were curious about some items going up while others didn't - they just didn't seem to care that you were there, and definitely didn't want to talk to you.

NOW it's right in between. The cranky girl is still there, lips forever pressed into a line and never allowing the smallest smirk to pass... but there are a few other employees that liven the place up.

The crepes are good, but boring and uneventful; the best thing about the crepes would be the smear of Nutella, which can be done at home on your own (if you know how to make crepes). The teas and snowbubbles are good, but if you ever ask for them to double blend the blended snows, you'll get dirty looks. The pho leaves a little to be desired in that the broth is either bland or too salty, but the ingredients that came out with mine the two times I got it seemed to be a bit fresher than other locations. The other items on the menu that I've tried (squid balls, fried tofu, spring rolls, spicy tofu, and a few other noodle dishes) are all tasty enough, but there's better entrees in the same shopping center at CJ Palace or whatever it is. The spring rolls seem VERY fresh, though - I will give them that. The peanut sauce, however, is runny and bland. Sad.

Unfortunately, due to the grump behind the counter and only a few things being something to write home about, this place will probably never get a three from me. It's good enough to stop in when someone else I'm with wants it, or if I get a hankering for boba, but I'd almost rather just wait for a road trip to SF.

Had lunch here with my husband and the food was delicious! I prefer the southern fried chicken; I also ordered the Ella's favorite and they were both very good. I also had the green beans and Mac and cheese...TASTY!!
You'll recognize it as the place with the Statue of Liberty out front (those things never look as big in person).  Casual atmosphere, strong drinks, and a great old look to the bar.

The quality is slipping - unfortunately.   The last handful of times I have gone has been disappointing.   I kept going because I guess I was in denial as to how things really were.  
The all you can eat veggie sushi is what keeps me coming back.    Lunch pricing is always the best value.

I just happened to stop by here after an Orangetheory Fitness workout with a friend who was in dire need of coffee. I opted to order a Strawberry Salad. That first bite I put in my mouth was like a slow motion fireworks in. my. mouth! It was sooo good!!! I couldn't believe how the strawberries, the candied walnuts, goat cheese and the arugula salad all mixed nicely together to make me sooo happy! It was a match made in heaven! I have to say, this was back in early June and I just checked and they have a new salad on the menu. I want to go back just to taste how good this new one is! Next time I visit NOLA, I'm definitely going back!

To be honest with you, this place is really overrated.  I used to think the steak here was good and don't get me wrong it's not bad, but there are much better options in Philadelphia for a cheese steak, take for example the less known Chubby's across the street.

Atmosphere is great, old school, service is good, no problems there, the quality of the steak is just lacking a little bit.  The meat seems often overcooked, as it sits on the grill for hours on end in a pile before they move it over to warm it up and put cheese on it when you order your sandwich.  The onions are done well, and add to the sandwich and the roll is good to go.  Cheese consistency is good, but not the best.

Overall, it's a good cheese steak, but it doesn't compare to some of the greats of the city like John's Roast Pork or Tony Lukes.  Don't get fooled by Pats and Genos neither of them are anything special either.

Delicious Italian style pizza. Dough and crust very tasty. 
A cut above the rest. Fast delivery. Our new go-to spot.

We waited an 1 1/2 hours for delivery.  When it finally got here the  order was wrong. The food we did receive was cold and horrid tasting.  I called, but customer service and satisfaction clearly are not a priority at Asian Village.   I ended up tossing the food that I paid $25 for and cooking dinner. Save yourself time and money and don't order from Asian Village!

Finally had time to come in and check this place out! It seemed as if my wife and I came in after a big lunch rush since about 75% of the tables were not cleaned, but there were other tables available to seat us when we walked in. We went straight to the simple Pho and Bun Bo Hue dish for our first try here. We were pleasantly surprised on how flavorful the broths were with both bowls as well as receiving a good portion. I also had the Nuoc Mat which is a concoction of jelly and fruits. My drink was overfilled with all the jelly and fruits which was left with a little bit of juice to drink. I would probably ask to have more juice than other jellies in the cup if I were to order it again. My overall experience there was nice which they would find me back there again to try out their other dishes.

It's  a shame how this place has declined over the past three years. 

They used to be so good at everything: food, service, sanitation. But now, they are cr u de, rude, busy on their phones, and not attentive. 

I ran in for some garlic knots and saw a boy who just seconds ago took my money and then proceeded to pick out 6 garlic knots with his unwashed. Ungloved, dirty hand. 
Gross!!!!
I went here for the first time last night and have to say this place is amazing! The beer menu is great and they had the best fish tacos I've ever tasted I highly recommend it.
Hidden in a strip mall but great place to eat. Pizza is very good but the Italian Wedding Soup is the best I have ever tasted!!!

Alright so was looking for a spot to grab some lunch and why not a joint that does both salads and subs. It was also a long Monday morning of work so I felt that driving a bit to find a spot would be the right play to make. This is where Pickleman's on SLU campus comes into play. This joint is essentially a pot bellys with no real difference. The spot is pretty big so you can definitely bring a large group and parking is pretty easy with meters available in the spot. Once you walk into this joint the smell of subs just hit you and trust me, you will walk out of here smelling like a sub. 

The big three sections of the menu seem to be the subs, salads, and pizzas. I am trying to keep it healthy lately so I decided to go with the Italian Chop Salad. They do not skimp on the veggies here and it's actually a really well made salad with the perfect balance of protein and veggies. I got the Italian vinaigrette which was great with the salad. The sandwiches look pretty solid and I am definitely eying the Buffalo Chicken salad for next time. The folks working here are efficient and are able to keep the line moving which is always a plus as well. I thought it was great that they had a PICK 2 option deal where you can essentially get a half and half which is not something is common. Big fan of this move. They also deliver I believe within a certain radius and I know I would definitely pick this spot over Jimmy Johns.
 A fan of this spot and will be back to try other options.

This place is OKAY. Nice patio, but not always much in the way of atmosphere. The menu is good, but could be better -- more veggie options, please (and veg options that aren't charred on the wood).

The schnitzel isn't what I would consider schnitzel -- schnitzel is pounded thin with a distant, bubbly breading. This is more like breaded cutlet.

And the fries.. well, they're delicious, but they're not what is typically served in Germany, nor is it the right choice to pair with sausages or schnitzels.

I'll return, probably not for a full meal, but I'll get the Wursts of the day and the spaetzle. And bier.

The Clover and the Bee is a café and bistro located in Old Webster Groves. It's nicely decorated, very simple, lots of natural light. I went for lunch and it was filled with lots of women, some with kids, sone on a work break, some in groups.   I had the Mediterranean quiche with feta and it was delicious.
The food here is tasty and the service is quick even when there are lines forming out the door.

We were walking through the quarter on a cool October day with no plans other than wander and day drink.  We walked past MRB around 11 am and it looked promising enough, from the street you could see straight through the back door into a courtyard.  It was the perfect day to be outside so it seemed like the place to be.  

They had 6 different local beers on tap, I got a Ghost in the Machine and the lady friend got her usual Abita Amber.  We then went to a table outside and enjoyed each other's company, the weather, the beer and the college football game that was on 1 of the 2 outdoor TV's. It honestly had the feel of a cool backyard.  There was also a small building out back serving food but we weren't quite ready to eat at the time so we passed.  

Inside there are probably 10 more TV's, a pool table, and the coolest bathroom that I had seen in awhile.  The urinals had dividers made in the silhouette of Alfred Hitchcock and the urinals themselves had little soccer fields for your pee stream to score goals with the little ball.  My only regret was waiting until we left to go to the bathroom. I'll definitely be back just so I can score more goals.

Gratzzi has been extremely generous and kind. Today I was able to pick up a free industry meal made fresh by their staff and it was amazing. Not only did it taste delicious but they were so generous in their portions of what they gave out. I can't wait to come dine in at this restaurant and pay it back to what they have done for me today. Thank you so much for your support to us who have lost our jobs due to Covid 19.

I made a reservation for a Saturday night a few days in advance. I really enjoyed it here, overall.

1. Food was awesome. Super reasonable prices considering all of the pasta entrees we ordered had fish, seafood, or meat in them! ($75 for three pasta entrees and an app). I especially love that there's Roman options (cacio e pepe, amatriciana) that you can't find at other Philly Italian places.

2. The charcuterie/cheese platter was amazing.

3. Our server for most of the night was awesome. But at some point in the night, he left. (But he didn't tell us that he was switching us over to a different guy, which I thought was weird.) The new server sort of forgot about us and didn't come back. 

4. BYO is obviously great.

5. Super cute place, with lots of outdoor seating. Decent sized inside too! The location is definitely an underserved area, and I like that's in between Rittenhouse and South Philly.

6. The fire alarm went off twice during our dinner. It's an open kitchen concept, but they definitely need to figure out their ventilation.

Surprised to find this restaurant in Isla Vista, an area of mostly college students.

I dined at this restaurant on a Saturday afternoon while  visiting my daughter at UCSB. She and her bf wanted sushi for lunch but we were short on time and a trip to Santa Barbara would not have worked.  At their suggestion, we ate here.  I wasn't expecting much since it was located right next to the school and the word "Express" is in the name.  

Fortunately, our experience exceeded my expectations.  They've dined there before so they knew what to expect thus the recommendation.  Here's what I experienced.

*A small to medium sized "order at the counter" sushi restaurant with Japanese decor. 
*Indoor and outdoor (communal) seating.
*A small parking lot with easy parking since most walk or bike there.
*Street and city lot parking readily available.
*Good amount of options on the menu.
*Pricing comparable to more traditional sushi establishments.
*Friendly service at the counter and table. They bring the food to the table. 
*Tasty food and decent portions.
*Fast service.
*Functional restroom with key.

We ordered 2 veggie rolls, a rainbow roll, a dragon roll, a spider roll, edamame and unagi sushi. Our meal came with miso soup.  The rainbow and dragon rolls looked very similar to each other and appeared to resemble the shrimp tempura rolls over what we ordered.   But they were good so we had no complaints.  Our taste buds were happy and our bellies were full. 

I loved the convenience.  I will definitely be back!
Best doughnut bites and brunch!! The wait is always long, but well worth it. There are so many amazing things on the menu it is hard to pick what to order.

This was our first time to Craft Street!  From the moment we walked in to give our name to the minute we left, it was amazing! Zach was our waiter and knew what beers went with what meals, everything he suggested we got and he didn't not steer us wrong! We will be back again and again!  Great experience!  Make sure you ask for Zach!!
Great sushi and awesome presentation. Staff were attentive as well. Thanks to GroupOn for bringing this to my attention.

If you have been through college you learn a few things. Algebra, Shotgunning PBR, bongs made from faucets/apples, and where to get a great burrito. Obviously we can't keep up with a lot of these skills after college, but one that stuck with me was the ability to analyze a good burrito. A burrito is a simple thing, meat, beans, cheese, rice and a tortilla. Simple right? Done right, it is true artistry. Growing up in Santa Barbara County is was what led me here. It is the Louvre of Burrito joints, not because it is a beautiful venue, but because the burritos they create here are art. Carnitas cooked to perfection, beans like none other.

This is the real deal. I've ate countless burritos in my days on this earth. It's a place I always go when I go back home.

We've been to Carlucci's a handfull of times over the years each time I hope it get's better. It's clear the ownership is making an investment in the facilities. I don't think you can match the outdoor fine dining atmosphere. I also think the menu is great for a high end Italian/Steak/Seafood restaurant. The service is very good as well. I gave it 3 stars instead of 5 because in my experience the kitchen doesn't live up to the menu. We've ordered all over the menu from pasta to steak to seafood. All I can say is that we haven't had a consistent experience with some appetizers/entrees were great others we were disappointed. For the atmosphere and menu choices you should take a shot.
This is my favorite ramen/sushi spot. The veggie ramen and shrimp tempura is a 2-3x's per week meal. It's a family owned business. If you want delicious ramen/sushi check them out.

Yikes! Silly me, I forgot to write a review about the Califonia Tacos. It was back in 2011 and I was dating this guy...Anyway, whatever.  Basically, I hyped it up for us because we were somewhat foodies.

I was looking forward to this place for so long because it had been closed for awhile. So when we heard it had been reviewed by the Food Network, we had to check it out ASAP.

I met the owner of the place and he seemed pretty enthusiastic and friendly. It was somewhat busy so it was a good sign. We didn't have to wait long for 2 fish tacos.

Well, I like fish tacos. They're supposed to be simple, flaky, and packed with flavor. Unfortunately, I'm not a fan of grease. Ironic, because it's fried. Well, at California Tacos, I opted for their famous fish tacos but it was packed with an overly greasy battered fish and some crunchy cabbage filling. It didn't look so tasty like in the show. It tasted fresh, but the grease filled my palate and I could barely finish it. But it's definitely filling.

Sadly, I haven't been back since...lesson learned. Don't hype anything too much.

went here to meet up w/ friends, even after reading the reviews. The food, eh. I liked that they offered boneless wings, (in addition to regular boned wings) and I recommend the chipolte dip for it-I dipped my hand cut potato chips in it. YUM! 
I had a Cesar wrap, it was tasty enough, and my companions had the bar pizza (looked pretty good) and the roast pork sandwich which looked and smelled great. the wine-a house pinot grigio was tasty. 
After wards we split a lovely brownie sundae which was probably the best part of the meal!

A GREAT Thai restaurant in Santa Barbara! This was my first time having Thai food in SB since moving from the LA/OC area a few months ago, and I am SO glad that I found out about this place. This restaurant has such an inviting atmosphere, with nice and big clear windows. I came here with a group of coworkers on a weekday for lunch, and we were promptly seated by the friendly staff. It was definitely not busy at all, with just my group and one or two other parties in the restaurant. 

The lunch special menu has a great selection of cheap items. I got the pork panang curry, and it was delicious! So creamy and full of flavor. It was a perfect portion for a working lunch. You can choose the level of heat/spiciness you'd like, otherwise, it will be medium. I felt that medium didn't have as much heat as expected and felt a bit on the milder side (think a little milder than the hotness of Sriracha), so I may go for 1 star hot next time. The white rice was great for eating with the curry. To drink, I had a Thai Iced Tea, which was quite refreshing and had just the right amount of cream in it, not too heavy.

For dessert, we shared scoops of the corn ice cream and coffee ice cream. Both were excellent. In particular, the corn ice cream was a very nice surprise: the corn is quite subtle and not overpowering.

I will definitely be back soon to try the Pad Thai and other noodle dishes! Great place for a relaxing lunch and to get your Thai food craving satisfied.

Wow. Wow. Wow. 

In a city of sea food and daiquiris, Cochon is THE stand out with the smoked meats and spirits. This is my favorite part of southern cooking and man every bite and sip we had was unforgettable. 

We ordered the pork ribs with watermelon salsa and whiskey flight. The sauce was tangy and spicy and the meat was tender, smoky, juicy, fall off the bone. The watermelon bites were a surprising but refreshing addition. I loved the pepper sauce they have the tables - the one with real red peppers soaking in a vinegar solution. Sharp taste that adds a great kick. So good I even put it on the bread. 

The whiskey pairings were great with the meat and showcased a diverse selection of flavors. Good serving size too. We came during an off meal time - around 3PM and were seated immediately. Next time I'm back in Nola, Cochon is first on my list.

If you want to know where to go,
To get the very best tacos.
Take a walk around the block,
And talk to my boy El Guapo.
He'll tell you a story that's true and no fib,
You need to try Spare No Rib.
Their carnitas the bomb, the fish make the list.
I'd never eat salads but I'll bet it's the shit!

This is my boyfriend's favorite pupusas spot. Pupusas are authentic here! Tasty fresh and their plate with two pupusas rice and beans is like 8-9 dollars. It's a lot of food!!!! Their curtido on the side tastes  mmmm mmmm good!!!! Next time I'm in the area I will definitely stop for pupusas.

My family and I came here from California on a road trip. We were staying at the Best Western Inn, which is not even 50 paces from the steak house.

Upon entering the place, I noticed something that was a little alarming... The floor was CLEAN! If you have ever been to a Texas Roadhouse, you know there are barrels of peanuts in the waiting room, and small trash cans full on every table. People are encouraged to help themselves while they wait, and throw the shells on the floor. The floor was immaculate! I wasn't the only one that was hesitant to throw my shells on the floor... You could see people meandering around in the lobby with shells in their hand. This was very disappointing. This is one of the novelties of Texas Roadhouse. The floors at every other franchise I have been to have been COVERED in peanut shells.

We called ahead because we are veterans. There's no way I would take my children here and wait in the lobby without calling ahead. The average wait on a busy night is 30 to 40 minutes. A table was ready for us when we arrived.

On our way to the table, we noticed that this particular location was very cramped. Our greeter attempted to seat my one and a half year old at the end of our table, in arms reach of another family's food. We had to ask to remove a chair instead and sit the high chair in it's place. This seemed like common sense to me. We ordered waters for the kids, and margaritas for the wife and I. While we were waiting, I noticed there were TRASH PAILS on the table for the peanut shells! There were very few shells on the floor, and in the spirit of the roadhouse,  I threw all of mine on the floor, and encouraged the kids to do the same. Some others were following suit.

A new family came to sit down, and two of an existing group of customers had to get out of their seats so the new customers could get by. There was NO way they could squeeze by. The chairs had to be pushed all the way in to allow safe passage.

It was at this point, before we placed our order, that I heard another lady at the table next to ours talking about her steak. She had returned her first portion because it was too rare.  She ordered medium rare, and in her words, "It was still mooing at her". I saw her meat, and it was bright pink, soggy, and tore loose from itself in a shredding action rather than a tender, red, juicy rare steak. It was clearly cold and raw.

This lady was a portly woman, about two and a quarter, and her husband wasn't far behind. He had finished off his chicken and was grimacing at his wife's pile of cold flesh on her plate. It looked like something out of a horror movie, or worse, something Rocky just finished punching for an hour.

She sent her food back a second time, and the waiter was very apologetic, and hurried to the back with the cold dripping slop. You don't go to a steak house and order a hot dog, but It was at this point that I decided to order my steak medium well to be on the safe side. I figured it would arrive at the table medium rare, and that would be fine.

The poor portly lady's steak arrived for the third try, and... It was raw. She boxed it up and took it with her, no doubt to finish the cook's job at home herself.

My steak was presented to me on a nice hot plate, with fries and jack cheese on top. Then I saw it... The nightmare of every chef... STEAK SAUCE on the table. No self respecting steak house provides steak sauce unless a patron asks for it. A steak should stand alone on seasoning and inherent flavor brought out by proper cooking.

My steak was leather, with some shoe strings mixed in for good measure. It might have been gristle, but I wouldn't have bet on it. I am not one to complain (although I do like a tell a story here and there) but I had to tell the waiter how horrible the steak was AFTER I paid the check. She wanted to bring the manager over, but I told her no, that's why I paid it first. I don't want my check discounted. I just wanted the manager to talk to the cook.

The restrooms were not air conditioned. Enough said about that.

The service was good, and the rest of the food was great. The margaritas were not strong enough. They were more like smoothies. My wife ordered chicken and mushrooms, and her meal tasted great. For this reason, and for the good service, I give this location two stars.

Rude! That's all we can say my boyfriend and I came in for an early dinner after wine tasting... The server was great, however when we ordered we asked for one of the dishes to have the cream sauce on it and the server's response was the Chef does not like to mix seafood with cream sauce... 

Ok so we said fine, we asked for the sauce on the side after we received our meal.. Mind you we can see the chef from where we were sitting while my bf and I were eating we saw him making faces in the kitchen... Never again do not come here...

Great food, friendly staff.

It's nothing out of the ordinary or exceptionally exceptional, but the best in the area.  Not much seating, so definitely take-out.
Beer and food are remarkable. Not too pretentious, a great place to hangout. Had the braised short ribs and the nachos.y wife had the lobster rolls. All of it was excellent. Highly recommended.

Went in to fill my water bottle with water, asked the cashier if that was alright. After looking at the prices of their smoothies, I decided not to buy anything. I went to my car in the parking lot and an employee came out yelling that it's not a public place and "you have to say something". I responded that I did indeed ask the woman at the counter and he replied that I didn't. Rude and disrespectful.

1933 is hands down my favorite place in the city to get a craft cocktail. Having a list of 8-10 specialty cocktails, their options aren't as large as some of the other places with similar draw, but their prices are on par and they are always delicious. If you want the best thing on the menu, it's definitely the Makers Mark infusion that they make served on the rocks. I could down an entire jar of the cherries that come out of that mix. They also have some beer offerings, and plenty of wine choices. Along with these drinks, the food menu is second to none when it comes to upscale menus in a bar setting. The filet sliders are delicious, and they are served with a creamy horseradish sauce that is perfect. If you want something more of the comfort food variety, they have fried bacon infused mac and cheese, and even offer a combo of the sliders and mac and cheese to those who can't decide. And of course, the crème de la crème, the St. Elmo's famous shrimp cocktail is available as well.

The thing that sets this place apart the most from the other cocktail lounges in the city is the atmosphere. It's a step above any other place I've been in. They keep the lights down low, and have a lot of ambient lighting. The bartender and servers are dressed up, and while not required, the patrons are usually nicer looking than most crowds anywhere else in town. I've been in a few times when they even have live music, usually one or two people and an acoustic guitar. There is a bar, some high top tables, and even some lounge chairs that are all open seating. If you're lucky enough to get there early, you can grab a seat in front of their fire place to enjoy your drinks. This is the ideal place to bring a date either before or after a night out to a show.

Really disappointed with the pizza and salads offered here. With the great reviews we decided to give it a try. Pizza was totally soggy in the middle, toppings slid right off. The beet salad was meager and hardly dressed with a giant blob of cheese on top. Not what I expected with the reviews I read.

Tavolino continues to be one of our favorite Happy Hour locations in Tucson. Kudos to Benjamin, our waiter, and to Jonathan, the resident sommelier, for their exceptional service!

Bob & Candi H.

I love love love new Asian village! I like the butter chicken a lot and the coconut naan is awesome! It is really heavy and fills you up, but that's a good thing if you're really hungry. Point is, I LOVE this place.

We stopped in here for lunch on our last day of our trip for a hearty sandwich and a cocktail. Napoleon House is known for their muffuletta sandwich and pimms cups. This sandwich is massive. Between the two of us, we shared a half and it did not disappoint. It is hearty and, as someone who doesn't like olives, the tapenade is delicious and super fresh tasting. We both ordered a pimms cup to wash down the sandwich and left with happy bellies. Definitely stop by and try to sit outside in their cute courtyard, this is definitely a spot not to be missed.
Has a lot of character, with what apparently is a Flying M characteristic: a gift shop.  Old sixties tables, decent espresso and great hours.  Wi-fi was in the neighborhood of 5mbs when I went.

We came here on Sunday afternoon at around 1. It was pretty crowded. We were lucky enough to find a seat but I wouldn't always count on it. Its pretty much deli set up. You order at the counter and pay and then they call your number to pick up the food. We ordered a 1/2 Shrimp Po-Boy with Gumbo and a full Crawfish Po-Boy. The food came out in about 5 minutes. The shrimp and crawfish were both fried crispy but did not feel greasy. The bread is super soft and crispy, typical NOLA style. We opted to pay the .60 cent extra to get all the fixins. The gumbo was alright though.
I love this please, excellent service, excellent food, My favorites are the fish taco and carnitas tacos but everything is good here
I love this place! Great for kids or date night. Service is always good and food is surprisingly tasty for the prices. The best way to catch a flick.

The perfect Spanish style tapas place! Every dish was simple but with a dome of flavor. I loved everything we ordered and loved the tapas style setup. Perfect place to order a bunch of things off the menu and share everything! The restaurant had great service and I will definitely return.
As always, a really special meal and experience. I had the beef stroganoff and my wife the scallops and we both loved our dishes. Look forward to going back.

I was in the Italian Market area of Philadelphia and got a sudden craving of tamales. I Yelped a few places  and  found great reviews here. Definitely not disappointed!

I was running low on time so I ordered a few. The person who tended to me explained that their menu is a mix of Hondurian and Mexican cuisine, but they only had Hondurian tamales. I wasn't familiar with them, and he explained the difference. I decided to give them a shot and placed a take out order. Once I got home, I opened them up and they were still warm (tamales were very well wrapped in several layers of aluminum foil and a takeout box). I opened one up and saw it was very soft (not good, not bad, I thought. It was very flavorful and  soft. Sometimes tamales turn out too dry, but this one was the opposite. There was a very generous portion of chicken inside too! Very satisfied!

I would like to revisit and eat there next time! As I walked in and out of the establishment I saw soups, steak, and tacos that all looked delicious (and again, generous portions).

Whenever we fly into Tucson International, this is the Mexican restaurant that we go to. Cheap and delicious with lots of choices! Love the guacamole tostadas! My sweetie can't resist the red chile sauce.
Service is friendly and prompt. Looking forward to trying more things on the menu. Anyone need an airport pickup? ;-)

This place has great breakfast.  Weekday special is a very fair price for two eggs, hashbrowns, and bacon. The bacon is a mixtured of juicy and crisp.  The hashbrowns were delicious. The eggs were also good.

I call this 5 stars, but you have to know what you are in for...

This is basic southern comfort food -- VERY well done.  We have only been for breakfast, but the eggs, grits, ham, biscuits, etc. are all fantastic.

It's table service of a sort.  You order at a counter, pay, and carry your own drinks to your table.  Then your food is brought out by a server, as well as any re-fills or special requests.

This place gets busy fast, especially on weekends -- so there can be a line.  Don't fret too much because the line moves pretty quick and the restaurant is HUGE inside.

Prices are quite reasonable and the food comes in great quantity.  I definitely recommend having something with ham in it.  They say it is the "world's best ham" and they can't be too far off.  Also, the blueberry muffin with pecans is wonderful.

One giant caveat that almost spoiled the 5-star rating -- no bacon!   The have ham, roast beef, and sausages for breakfast--but no bacon.  I wish they offered some thick cut bacon.

Mother's is a must-eat place while in the Big Easy.

Fabulous Cookies, but they could add a few more choices in the pizza department. Cheese or Pepperoni isn't exactly on my list of pizza choices. 
However they serve it up really fast. Which is a plus when you just came off the hiking trail and a little bit hangery.

We have not been to this Steak n Shake in a long time. We thought that we would give it another try. To our disappointment we had a bad experience. We ordered a double steakburger with cheese, fries, and orange freeze. and a doublestack bacon  steakburger with fries. Our fries were cold, limp, unsalted, undercooked. Our burgers were smashed and the buns were soggy and cold .Burgers were not good at all.  We decided to order online, but when I tried to send feedback it wouldn't submit it would say a error and I had all info correct. NEED TO FIX ISSUE!! So I came to yelp to write this review. I will Never come to or  eat at this location again. I hope that we do not get sick off this food and if they had a below 1 star I would most certain give it a below 1. EAT THERE AT YOUR OWN RISK !!!!

Dined at Luke on a busy Saturday evening and was so very impressed with the service (ask for Anthony) and cuisine.  My ribeye was cooked perfectly, the fois gras stunningly delicious, and the overall ambiance way cool.  Loved it!

Tasty, organic, healthy, reasonable prices, great selection!!!! Choose your own or select from large list of smoothies. Pre-made sandwiches in fridge opposite deli counter or made to order. Salad bar, vegan soups, hot bar, grocery store with organic produce.

Trust me when I say this is some of the best and freshest food I have ever eaten. You leave this restaurant feeling refreshed and satisfied. It's hard to explain the feeling if you've never experienced it before, but you just feel clean after eating here. Would 100% recommend to anyone!

We were not impressed. Really cute place, loved the patio. However the service was terrible. Very slow, and not friendly. The food was ok, but not good enough to make up for the poor service. Unfortunately we will not return.

I ordered the lunch special through the Yelp app with Grubhub for takeout. So this may have played apart in my main disappointment. In the special instructions(extra sauce, no onions, etc) section of my order, I had asked for "no peanuts, please" yet there was still a lot of peanuts in my food. My advice is just to be sure they pay attention to this part of your order. Since they were mixed into my food, I did not notice them until I was home and eating. The lunch special I ordered was the Massaman Curry with chicken (hot.) This also came with a cup of soup, a small salad, and a spring roll so it was a lot of food for $7.99. My curry was good, but a little sweeter than I would prefer. Overall, it was delicious for the cost!

So decided to stop in and try a cheese steak at ginos steaks, what a disappointment figured coming from NYC it would be better than anything I could find back home. NOT!!

First off the meat is sliced not chopped, had no flavor, the bread was weak and really didn't stand up to the steak, not even toasted, the onions , tasted like they came outa a can , the cheese ( got provolone ) again no flavor and not even melted, Oh and where are the peppers man, cant have a cheese steak without peppers!
All in all very poor , I can get a better tasting cheese steak from papaya king on the corner of 42nd and 9th for $7.50 with fries and a drink.

And to be fair I went across the street to try Pats king of steaks same crap! 

Final word can get a better cheese stake for half the price in NYC

We came here for an early dinner and chose to sit outside on the patio. It was a warm and clear day and we could enjoy the setting of the sun while partaking in our food. We shared one order of chips & salsa. Since it was Tuesday Steak Night, my partner-in-dine and I ordered the angus beef steak. Sadly, the steak was a bit tough and was mediocre in taste. The portion was on the smaller side. We would come back but maybe just order the chips and some drinks and enjoy the view. Service was friendly.
First time here and won't be the last. I felt welcomed from the moment I walked in. This place is very cozy. The food is good and tub people are sooooo nice

Very enjoyable. Pulled pork gumbo special and jambalaya were delicious. I found the crawfish pie too oily and having too few crawfish. The bananas foster bread pudding was tasty and the portion was generous, though it could have used more bananas.

I'll spare the details on the food and menu because they are fairly standard at any Panera (or St. Louis Bread Co.).  The service is quick and attentive.  Although there was a huge crowd when I went there on a Saturday afternoon, they had our food out within a few short minutes.  The staff is extremely sweet and I enjoyed coming there.  The only reason I couldn't give this location five stars was because of the location.  Although it was super convenient location, parking is extremely difficult.

Loved the food and the friendly staff and the layout. I wished I lived a little closer to NOLA. I am happy I was able to experience some good southern cuisine here. I had the chicken and sausage gumbo, and the bf had the pulled pork nachos (pretty unique) both were delicious. 

Prices were reasonable especially for the portion size and the fact that it's located in the middle of the French Market. The cool thing I found was that they have Jolly Rancher soda! I haven't even heard of that before.

We wanted to walk due to indulging for days on our first trip here. Was told by my cousin this place was a must do. We come upon the restaurant, nothing to look at except holy cow look at the Disney line! She says an hour or so. So we wait. And wait. An hour and minutes later we are seated, finally! Menu is no fuss. Just fried chicken and some sides, so they can move people pretty quickly. And the chicken... was complete worth the wait. My hubby was in heaven. Fried chicken is his death row meal, and this chicken measured up! We would do that all over again!

Giving this place 3 stars. Came in with moderate expectations. Ambiance is good. Seating would have been nice if they offered vision on these wood benches. I've tried more than a handful of ramen joints and I give this place a 2 star. The broth is way to salty and it seriously taste like the packets that come in the ichiban ramens I use to eat when I was a kid.

We stopped here after walking out of another place for extremely slow service (previous place was practically empty) boulevard burgers was packed & we were still greeted immediately & had our drinks in hand in minutes. Food was great our server was wicked friendly & kept checking in & the game night atmosphere was awesome. Everyone there was friendly & having a good time. We'll definitely be back

We order two lg pizzas & a salad.  The pizzas were HUGE!  Yummy crust and out favorite was the cheese and basil. Delicious. I will definitely be coming back!

Only downside is there is really no inside seating for a family of six.

Perfect place to grab breakfast in South Philly.  Food was well prepared albeit a bit pricey for what was served.  The only reason for not giving this place a better review/rating is simply that our waitress (wearing a Eagles T-shirt?...perhaps it's time to institute a dress code for your servers!) was snarky, sarcastic, and disinterested.  I'm not sure whether or not servers remember who the actual customer is, but the server at Hungry Pigeon the morning of our breakfast, certainly did not.  This person belongs in front of a dishwasher rather than in front of customers.

Not only was the pizza delicious, the customer service was top notch! 

We had never been to this place and ordered over the phone. When we arrived, they had our food ready to go, and asked us if we were aware that there wouldn't be cheese on the pizza. We were definitely surprised by that; I have never seen pizza with no cheese, but because we ordered over the phone, we didn't realize exactly what we were getting. 

We were willing to take our pizza, considering it was our mistake that we didn't fully read the menu, but they let us take the pizza AND gave us another pizza with cheese. They certainly did not need to do that, but we were so glad they did. 

The food was SOO good. Highly recommend the sausage pizza  I would definitely go back next time I am in the area.

The pizzas here are made with really fresh, really creative ingredients.  There are a variety of pizza options to choose from, each with a unique appeal and flavor profile.  There are pizzas to suit a variety of different tastes, and each of the ones that I've chosen have been very good.  You can't go wrong with the Cowboy Poetry pizza, its won awards for a reason.  Only two pizza sizes are offered (8" and 12").

The beer selection here is good, too, along with the appetizers.  I've been treated well on all of my visits, and for all of my takeout orders, by the staff.  Orders can get a little pricey if you are hungry, or in a large group, but the quality of the food offered makes the experience at Black Rock every time.  Cool place.

We finally just made it up there today and it was worth the wait and the drive. The pizza was definitely made with love and was the best pizza I've had in years hands down. Plenty of toppings and the crust was made just the way I requested. The staff was friendly and couldn't do enough for you. We will be returning.
Yogi
PS Open a store in Atlantic County

The thin was PERFECT, as close to Vito & Nick's as you get. In fact, Vito & Nicks is a bit greasier so we actually liked this better. We are far northside lakefronters that would drive all the way to the far southwest side (84th & Pulaski)  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=94aYUljniPI  to get that treat on occasion. so driving to Indian Rocks Beach from Holiday isnt too bad in comparison. The stuffed was like a cross between our two all time favorites, Giordano's and Edwardo's. No need to order "extra sauce" here.
The first time we ate here in October, we were blown away and loved that they had TBB's pumpkin on tap, even though the glass size is small. We wanted to try it again before leaving a review and the pizza this time was even better than we remembered. The Shipyard Island Time Session IPA (tropical) was a perfect pairing! 
WARNING: IMO, the deep dish (pan) is NOT what I look for in that style of pizza and be sure to "season" your pies with the shakers of parm, crushed red pepper and ask for oregano

This is easily one of my favorite places to eat in Tucson. I am not sure why some of the reviews are negative, but what you see is what you get. Do not go for the lunch buffet and judge it on the buffet alone. More than just a restaurant, this feels like the home of the owner. That is what makes it most authentic. I would highly recommend this place to anyone who wants to give authentic Indian food a try.
The best BBQ in town!  Great new location in the de la guerra plaza. Had lunch today and it was delicious!  Steve and Lori

I was in town for a National Guard conference in August. Staying at the Hampton Inn I thought I would eat there. I ordered the shrimp cocktail, steak and scallops special and a side of creamy spinach. Everything came out average, nothing was over the top. When I got my bill of $150 I about died. I also had 3 glasses of wine. But a solo dinner with my tip for $180 and I never ordered dessert. Not cool. While in town I also ate at Fago & St. Elmo. Twice the food, half the pice.

Just went last week, took my Mom with us as well. Have to say in all honesty I think they serve the freshest & best Mexican in Reno/Sparks. May not be exotic, but good tasty Mexican.
