I feel they they have the best chile relleno in town, my favorite. I don't think you will be disappointed. The new location is on a Sparks Blvd.

Pete's Place is a new casual Korean takeout concept run out of the Serpico kitchen, and unlike other Korean concepts we've seen this year (looking at you Char Kol), this one doesn't pretend to be fully authentic (it's Instagram handle is @petesplace.kindakorean), but it has a Korean chef, and the food is all comfort and heart, no frills. Ok, that's a lie, there are some frills, it is no Korean kimbap takeout or fried chicken joint, and the prices reflect that. But the food is exactly what you want to be eating as the weather cools down- noodles, soups, stews, and sticky crunchy slightly spicy delicious wings.

We got the wings ($18 for 7), potato salad ($6- more like mashed potatoes with crunchy stuff on top, this wasn't our favorite), steak ssam special ($29 came with rice, lettuce wraps, carrot, cucumber, broccoli a delicious spicy sauce and the steak was cooked and marinated perfectly), and the tsukemen style dipping ramen ($18 noodles come separate from the thick flavorful kimchi broth with pork belly and pork shoulder so tender you'll forget it's meat). The noodles were sticky and hard to pry from the takeout container, but that's the takeout life we live, I guess. For 2 hungry people that was too much food for one meal, but it was so good that I ate all of it and was uncomfortably full the rest of the night. 

Loved the QR codes on the takeout containers; "scan me" seemed like an Alice in Wonderland-like invitation, and the rabbit hole led us to adorable videos of the chef and his daughter thanking us for ordering and giving instructions for how to dip the noodles in the broth and add the starchy water afterwards to drink the broth. In this sad period of shuttered restaurants and masked waiters, and contactless delivery left on your doorstep with only a text, a video message from the chef feels like such a welcome treat, and a way to make takeout more personal. So glad to see Serpico back at it, and bringing comforting Korean fusion and flavors into our kitchens and living rooms.
Don't show up because she might not be there. I've done that twice and was highly frustrated because it's a 30-40 minutes drive. She doesn't consistently post modified hours. Good luck!

You can pick out your own beers and they add it to your tab or you can bring it home...so many beers to choose from! They even have them organized by type of beer...local, lager, etc...so you can always find your favorite style and drink tons of beers in that style. 

We had two women who helped us out while we were there, Anna and Jenna and they were super helpful. 

We didn't eat a lot of food but we did order the General Tso's cauliflower and I highly recommend it. They have a bunch of small plates that you can share with others which is something I would do with others or even by myself.

They had tables outside which was great for people watching and a lot cooler in temperature than indoors!

A must-visit in Tampa! Excellent food with the highest quality ingredients. All of the seafood is delivered daily from local sources. The building is very nice and has a lot of character, the waiter will explain the history of the restaurant to you at the beginning of your meal. Very interesting! As for food, we began with the crab Mac and cheese. Not as much crab as we hoped, but it was delicious. A perfect portion to share between 2 as an app, even the regular Mac and cheese is worth trying. We ordered the lobster stuffed shrimp, and the shrimp and grits. Both were excellent! Good portions and very fresh tasting. The shrimp and grits comes with grit cakes which is a nice twist on the dish. Would highly recommend Ulele, we will be back with more dishes to try.

Yes, the argument can be made that you can get some of the things here in different and arguably better styles at other places within 20 miles.  But as an entry point for some of these dishes, Hawkers does perfectly fine.  There are things I like, things that are close to what I've had in the source countries and some things that just don't work.  But on average I've been satisfied so that is the 4 star reason.  The Laksa is pretty decent and actually it has improved since they first opened.  Also, like the Char Kway Teo.  Similar to what I had in Singapore. Now if they could make Singaporean carrot cake, then I would be happy!  Fried green beans are fine, had better but good enough.  I think the big miss has been the duck small plate.  supposed to be roasted duck that they then threw in the wok.  It is that last part I take issue with.  Just wrecks it and doesn't taste like duck any more, more like the Char Kway Teo!  I'm betting this about reheating things roasted earlier but just doesn't work as a dish.  Stick with the pork.

Good selection of craft beer, but be sure to check the little flip menu for what is on draft.  While the bottles and cans are fine, there is a lot of good local things on draft so give those a try.  Some of the Sakis are good and not too over priced.  So a nice selection of drinks.  Prices are pretty reasonable as well.

Been here once before and the service and food were good.  Just stopped in again and could get no service.  Only 4 other customers and the bartender made eye contact with me twice but never would come take my order.  Hate it, but they lost me as a customer for good.

Again, a Wendy's in Philadelphia which is completely and unnecessarily slow - unbelievably slow in fact with zero people in the line or the dining area.

After fifteen; twenty minutes- I finally receive a burger which is not even warm

What's going on with inner city Philly Wendys? It is not somewhere you'd want to be as a client or employee- any of them.  They are all very poorly run here in my opinion and this city's franchises are giving a bad name to the chain


RE-VISIT 8/31
Oh yes, this one's a solid one - star

TOTAL GARBAGE LOCATION

jesus. They cannot get anything right. Staff of complete mental retardation patients, living in 50 IQ LAND.  #jesustakethewheel

Wasabi serves fresh, made-to-order sushi for prices that would be great for inferior rolls from a refrigerator at a grocery store. I appreciate that it's kind of like a chipotle of sushi... You can choose the proteins, vegetables, toppings, and sauce drizzles for your sushi if you want to customize it. For a small up charge, you can get double protein, etc. And the quality of the ingredients is pretty good.  And the service is pretty good, too: quick, polite, and prepared to ask questions and call audibles to make sure you get what you want. 

A few of the negative reviews seem to be from people offended that a quick serve sushi restaurant isn't Morimoto. I guess it isn't. But, if you get sushi at Whole Foods, Giant, etc., Wasabi is much better and a couple dollars cheaper. If you go to local table-service sushi places, Wasabi's still above their average. 

If I worked nearby, I'd get Wasabi's sushi for lunch at least weekly. This place is a local gem.

A nice spot for dinner.  Love the outdoor seating (under cover mostly).  Food was good.  My son and I stuck to simple sandwiches/wraps,  but the menu was interesting with a Paleo diet flaire. The staff was friendly; our waitress from the other night waved hi to us on her way by, a nice touch.  My only 'complaint' is that it closes too early,  but probably appropriate for the location.  I give it 3 stars only because I didn't sample enough to be impressed or unimpressed with the food, but I'd certainly go back (and did).  Atmosphere is important to me,  I like the vibe there.
Went for meal in afternoon after being recommended by the barman at our hotel... food was good and reasonably priced... went back in the morning for the breakfast and was great again.

*Update* 4/4/16 We ordered about 20 pizzas from Marco's for dinner at the fire house.  It was the traditional style pizza and we all enjoyed it.  The thin crust they have on display must be a 2nd style that they offer

Marco's pizza just opened in the strip mall at the corner of Bethlehem Pike and Loch Alsh Ave.  The location was formally a seafood / produce store.  The interior has been completely renovated and they have several booths along the front glass wall for dining in.  

The front counter along the back wall is filled with several different types of specialty pizzas.  Their pizza is thin crust and its cut into squares.  I was picking up an Italian hoagie for lunch but  decided to try a piece of their buffalo chicken pizza.  It was very crisp and had a good amount of shredded chicken on it.  I think they went a little heavy on the hot sauce but overall it was pretty good.  My hoagie was made on a fresh roll and was filled with meats and the normal lettuce, tomato and onions.  I would give their hoagie a solid B.  It wasn't anything I would be dying to come back for but I would order it again.  

The staff was very friendly and I will be back.

Jill's place was very good. But if I could I would probably give them 3.5 stars. The portions are very generous.
For starters, the free garlic cheese bread was crunchy and flavorful. 

I ordered the short rib which came with a salad, which was nice and crispy but not super flavorful, the split pea soup was just okay but I don't really like split pea. The short rib was huge and pulled apart easily but it was a bit chewy and tough sometimes. VERY GENEROUS PORTION. I paid $2 extra for the scallop potatoes, NOT worth it. The rice pilaf was better. I probably would not get the short rib again.

My dad got the ribeye early bird special that was VERY tender and flavorful. The mashed potatoes were okay nothing special.

My boyfriend got the fried chicken that was very good.

My mom got the chicken breast meal, that was cooked perfectly. It had a tasty crispy skin and was not dry. Huge generous portion. Rice pilaf was amazing. 

The vegetables were very good and not too salty cooked just right.


THEY DO NOT SUBSTITUTE. I TRIED TO SUB MY VEGGIES FOR RICE AND THEY SAID NO. it was not a big deal though because the vegetables were really good.

Overall I would give 4 stars but my short rib was just okay. The staff is nice and service is medium

I was initially hesitant to go in as the giant "KOREAN BUFFET" sign gave me pause. I didn't want a buffet, but my desire for kimchi propelled me on. Thankfully, they don't offer buffets at lunch time (or at least not at lunch time on weekdays - not sure of the weekends).

They have really good lunch specials - I had soondubu jigae (soft tofu spicy stew) that was I think only $7.99 - and it came with a whole host of banchans!!

The service was really friendly and attentive, which made sense since I was the only person here eating at 2pm on a Tuesday.

I promised the server that I will be back if ever in the area again!

I buy mostly cooked food. Their prices are considerably higher than Superstore for the same items in groceries, but obviously there is a greater variety of Asian foods here. Their variety of cooking sauces come in handy for home cooked meals, if you know what to do with them.
Pre-COVID, this place had the best brunch events on the weekends mixed in with a live atmosphere with a DJ and hookah. I miss this place!
Awful experience ordering through Uber eats. A whole item. missing in order and then burnt burger and soggy fries. Was first and last time eating from this restaurant

Love this place! I live just right up the street on poplar. I come here at least 2-3 times a week for my morning coffee. Their customer service is great btw! I advise anyone who is in the area or even just visiting the city to take a visit. You won't be disappointed with their menu. Btw their lounge is a huge plus! Great place to study when trying to escape the noise of the city.

Food & service were very good.   We had 24 in our group & they did a great job.   We had the CHICKEN SALTIMBOCCA, eggplant Parmesan, and fettuccine Alfredo.   All were cooked well & flavorful.   The Caesar salad was great as was the bread.  The chocolate chip cannoli was creamy with a crispy crust.   We really enjoyed our meal.   Would love to go again when I'm in Indy.

Went for the all you can eat seafood on Wednesday night. The seafood was fresh, not frozen and nice and hot. The Buffalo Shrimp wasn't that bad it was loaded in Tabasco sauce with celery on the side. There beers were ice cold!!!! Just the way I like them. The atmosphere was nice too...so will be back

I am a big fan having moved to STL three months ago.  The staff is extremely friendly and the owner typically mans the register.  Whenever I am in the area, I always stop by and have a pork sw or muffa.  Stop in and you won't be disappointed.
Alas, it seems there was a change in management and I need to update my review. Dry and tasteless tamales. Tasteless soft tacos. Not going back for a while.
Get an Italian hoagie. MUST get the hot peppers. (Put in on the side if you're a nance.) SO GOOD!
Dollar tacos on Tuesday can't beat it dinner drinks for 2 only 20$ and tasted great especially the beef tacos I will definitely go again and try other things on the menu

Beautiful evening enjoying a delicious dinner on the vibrant wrap around brick patio! Table for 10 girlfriends overlooking the main street in Skippack. The live acoustic guitar music served as a perfect backdrop to the delicious specialty drinks like the Cosmo, red wine Sangria and the Cucumber Chill (highly recommend the last one...crisp yet subtly fruity and you cannot resist having more than one)!
Dinner special was a ravioli in a cream sauce topped with spinach, blackened shrimp & salmon...a slice of heaven! Our server Laura was amazing! Her customer service expertise shone through every interaction with the table: explaining the menu, offering recommendations, and being just the sweetest most personable server...ask for her when you come to take your dining experience to the next level. She truly cares!

This place is awesome!  I would highly recommend stopping by for one of their burgers.  I got the El Diablo , no bun, which was spicy heaven. We also got the zucchini fries which were excellent as well.

Wow! I just spent over 40 minutes waiting for a cheesesteak and fries.  

How is that possible ? 

Seven customers in the joint with eight staff working.  40 minutes is unreal. I probably won't ever go back. 

Tried to phone in my order but nobody answered. Now let's see if my $29 (yes one cheesesteak and one order or fries) sun dial order is tasty. 

Update to follow....let's hope the food is MUCH MUCH better than the abysmal service.


Update. 

The order was incorrect.
So I'm from Michigan. Don't judge me. I enjoy Skyline and their unique chili. I get the 3 way potatoe without cheese.

Dalessandro's is one of my top cheesesteak places! It's a must try if you are anywhere within driving distance! I've gone here a handful of times and it gets better every time.

It's a very small place, so when you first walk in it will most likely be crowded. Chances are that most of the people inside are waiting to get their meals. Go to the right side and see if the people in front of you have ordered yet. You will be greeted with someone in the front who will ask if you want to eat inside, eat outside, or take out. The person taking your order might seem a little rude, but they're just rushing because they're so busy, so have your order ready. Once you order, go to the left side or outside and wait for your name to be called. You pay(cash only) when your name is called.

I went again Memorial Day weekend. I went on a Saturday nigharound 8pm and waited about 15 minutes to order and waited 30-35 minutes(which was what they estimated) to get my name called. 

My friends loved the cheesesteaks so much that we went back on Memorial Day. They were open regular hours. We went around 3pm and was able to order pretty quickly. We only waited about 10 minutes to get our food. 

The cheesesteak is consistently delicious. The meat has great flavor and there is enough cheese to go around. If you like a cheesy mix for your cheesesteaks, you should stick with American cheese, which is their standard choice. I also tried it with Provolone and it wasn't as cheesy. You will need to pay extra for other cheeses and toppings. Make sure you get the crushed red hot peppers(for free) on the side to add a nice sweet kick to your meal!

Came here while passing through SB on a day trip - wanted seafood for dinner and needed a place open later than 9pm. Chose the place for logistics alone but the food turned out to be fantastic, the service friendly, and the portions HUGE. Two of us split the grilled trout dinner and the shrimp and spinach salad, and it was more than enough even though we were starving. Will definitely make this a go-to stop for future coastal drives!
Very nice small meat market. The Salami is the best!

I love this restaurant because of the Japanese, Chinese and Thai choices.  The Pad Thai is excellent!  The dumpling and ribs are delicious.  The ambiance is upscale and the staff is pleasant and attentive. They are always packed which definitely tells you something about the restaurant!

Had dinner here twice the other week while in Reno for work. The Ahi salad was excellent and good portion and not to filling. Ahi was seared and cooked fair, but the dressing was great. The other night I had the strip steak salad. Not so good. the steak was over cooked like beef jerky and not a big plate. Stick with the Ahi salad with seared Ahi, skinny noodles, greens, and dressing. Beer was good, but service kind of sucked. The bartender was kind of a scattered and could had been better.  On Thursday nights its $7 all you can drink beer night. More of a college night, but great people watching from what I hear.

BEST CAESAR EVER.
Im Italian and picky but red sauce, burgers, pizza, pasta all great!

Thanks Mehdi for keeping this neighborhood tradition going!
ice cream is amazing, extremely rich though. really great interior. I wouldn't comment on anything else as the food is eh and the service is creepy.

I have just received a (gentle) slap on the wrist for my previous and only review of Shane's. The offense seems to be that I did not really express my experience there. I said, "I came, I looked, I left." I thought that was pretty succinct but I will flesh this out a bit and hope it flys.
I went into the restaurant, checked out the menu, looked at the food behind the counter, noted the absence of any patrons, and left without ordering anything.  Maybe I missed out on a fabulous meal-can't really say. This is not the first time I will have walked out of an establishment without sampling the wares.

I pop in here sometimes to treat myself to a cookie sandwich and, generally, the staff has been professional. This afternoon, however, I stopped in and asked for a cookie sandwich. After I asked for a cookie sandwich combo that wasn't already made (there were only two options in the display), the person working the counter rudely asked if I wanted her to make it. I've been in here plenty of times when staff volunteered to make a cookie sandwich combo that wasn't already made, so I think this is something they normally do. I said yes. She took my money, then walked to the back. When she returned, she made the sandwich with her bare hands. I was a little distracted and needed to get home, so I didn't think too much about it at the time. I thought that maybe she washed her hands in the back. On my way home though, I started thinking about it and really don't think she had time to wash her hands. In hindsight, I should have said something at the time, but I needed to get home and there was someone trying to pick up an order. Cannot eat the sandwich! Who knows what else she touched before the cookies - at a minimum, the cash I paid for the cookie sandwich. After the attitude and cleanliness concern, I won't be back here.

My date and I dined in The Little Lion Sunday 7/9/17 and while the food was good the service was horrible. We arrived around 4:15 and did not receive our drinks until 5pm and food until 5:20pm. Our waiter forgot to input our order and when asked by the manager how was everything we expressed our disappointment and was told we would be "taken care of". We received a random free dessert, not of our choice, which we did not eat as my date is allergic to chocolate. Unfortunately, we spent most of our date expressing to each other how hungry we were and how long the drinks/food were taking. Overall experience was not good and the manager made it worse by offering a dessert that we could not even enjoy. I am not sure that I will be back. Very disappointing experience with the service we received.

Friendly staff and you feel welcome right away. 
Had the blackened duck and creme brulee for dessert. 
Both were incredible and I can't wait to come back.
This place is a hidden gem!! The staff is so nice and the food is delicious... also it's very reasonably priced.

The Journey is me and my sister's secret spot. We come here once a month to get our fill on crab legs, Sushi, and other great Asian Delights. The restaurant is usually packed with folks that are doing the same. The buffet is about $22 which is a good deal. 

I was just advise folks to be cognizant of the lunch and dinner times. They do close their doors for an hour to switch over from lunch to dinner. It also might not have the same offerings at lunch that they will at dinner. Me and my sister try to always go to the dinner special right on time at 5 or 6 because that's when they have the crab legs.

The Journey restaurant has always been clean and their customer service from the servers have always been nice. I try to best to get people in and out as again they are always packed. If you are lover crab legs this place is having on our because they have unlimited crab legs.

This place is consistently one of my favorite go to sushi restaurants. I have eaten here several times both take out and dining in, the quality of the sushi is always incredible. I have a hard time ordering simply due to the extensive nature of their menu, and usually end up ordering way too much! If you're a sushi fan or not this is a place to try, they also have several non sushi options that are excellent.

Wow! Met Janet the hostess with the mostest! And Jennifer was a fabulous server! She recommended Dungeness crab 'all the way' and OMG the best crab I have ever eaten! Their shrimp and crab chowder was amazing! Shrimp cocktail was perfect - crisp and cold. 

I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND this place! Freshest seafood I have ever eaten!

We have been able to overlook the bad service in the past because of the great food but no service? Don't know if it is because they are short staffed or just badly managed. Noticed that we were not the only ones unhappy, another couple got up and left after waiting for approximately 5 minutes without even getting a menu despite trying to get a wait person's attention. We hung on because I was craving the cheese soup but gave up shortly after the other couple. And the topper, the place was half empty.

Oh how I love this place! Every time I leave here I am happy, sleepy and full of wonderful food :) 
Their bruschetta is absolutely mouth watering and tastes just like it did in Italy! The crispy bread gives it such a perfect crunch and the balsamic glaze was just the right amount. The shrimp scampi there is so good too! A bit on the soupy side but the flavor of the Parmesan crust makes everything much better.

If you come here often and like wine, join the wine club!! It is so worth the money for the discounts and the bottle of wine every month  Usually we come early to do a wine tasting and then have dinner which is the way to do it!

Will be back many many times I'm sure.

A deux pas de Chesnut, la grande artère commerciale de Philly, ce petit restau est idéal pou manger un bout à midi et se régaler. Nous avons choisi deux sandwichs, l'un au homard du Maine, leur spécialité, l'autre aux crevettes. Tous les deux excellents, avec du pain moelleux et beaucoup de homard juteux. Un régal ! L'endroit est BYOB (bring your own booze) donc je vous recommande de passer avant acheter une bonne biere du Maine au magasin spécialisé tout proche dans Samson st. Un petit bémol : le sandwich au homard à 15$ est assez petit et ne reussira pas à caler un ventre affamé.

We searched for a brunch place on out way out of Philly from the Army-Navy game and came across Rhythm and Brunch!! Great food!! Ample portions and great service!! Will keep it in mind next year when Army beats Navy again!

Great as always...cotton candy flavor was ok....I was impressed by the young lady behind the counter when a little girl who was with her gma and had some gummy worms in her bowl and then took them out of her bowl with her bare hands and put them back....the worker behind the counter QUICKLY took the container to the back and dumped it and brought fresh non-touched gummy worms.

Found this place by searching Yelp. Had never been there until this morning. 

Service was great! Food was great! I will definitely be back. 

I had the Olive Street Slinger. This chili used on it was flavorful. And in the center was some delicious candied bacon. You might question that, would a sweet bacon work in a slinger? And the answer is yes. I've seen more and more candied bacon type items popping up in restaurants, and if you've never had any you are behind the curve. 

My wife had one of their Benedict variations and was quite pleased with it.

First off, this place is exceptionally consistent. Second, the managers and employees are genuinely nice folks and hard workers. I've been getting big takeout orders here for a couple of years and they're just really "together" for a restaurant. The packaging is fantastic compared to a lot of other places and the wait time is pretty low considering their consistantly-packed lobby.

Now the food - Bonefish is great because you can really get a healthy meal that still tastes fresh and very flavorful. I tend to judge a restaurant more on the quality of things like vegetables, and Bonefish gets all high marks in that area - they have interesting seasonal vegetables, along with a tasty medley (carrots, peppers, broccoli, squash), plain broccoli, green beans, asparagus, and some very tempting mashed potatoes. The Florida Cobb Salad is a huge favorite for my office and is intensely filling and flavorful. I can't really finish a whole one due to the generous portions of cheese, pine nuts, and grilled chicken, but it's a really wholesome meal and lunch, too. 

Another favorite of mine is their mango salsa with grilled fish. So tasty! It has a spicy, sweet, salty flavor that doesn't overpower what it's on at all. Also be sure to try the Ocean Trust martini - it's one of the smoothest mixed drinks I've ever had. 

The only possible downside is that this place is packed just about every single night - but they seem to handle the crowds fairly well.

I really can't say enough in praise of this place. Great employees, great food. Bravo, bravo, bravo!
Small little restaurant but got busy very quickly. I ordered the pollo di giovanna and It was pretty good. There was an older crowd so probably not a good place for kids. Would go back again.

Moved to Tucson from a cold-weather climate ~2 years ago, but every time I go to La Cocina, I still feel like I'm on vacation. The intimate mix of outdoor seating, the shops surrounding the courtyard, and the live music all combine to make this one of my favorite places to be in Tucson on a Friday night. The food has always been great as well.

Authentic? Yes come here! Such an amazing little Mexican spot. I had enchiladas (tinga de pollo) and it truly hit the spot. In love in love in love of this place. Music wasn't too loud that you can hear your friends across the table from you. I will definitely recommend this to anyone in this area looking for a nice authentic Mexican "taco" spot.

There weren't many options for vegetarians, but that's usually expected. However, even with the lack of options, the portobello wrap I got was fantastic. The portions were rather large, too. Also, their fries were very very good! It did smell a little while I was in there, but it was from the water, so I can't complain. Our waitress was very nice and attentive. Overall a good experience.
Good Korean fried chicken. Wish they had given me pickled radish when i went. Little on fancier side for me but over all very good

The Culinary Adventures of Tom Coghlan
Yesterday at 1:03 PM  ·
I was driving down 4th St. on my way to Shoprite to decide on my dinner for that night. I just left my Doctors Office, where I had a series of tests that left me a bit drained. As I approached Ritner St. I saw a Mexican Restaurant that had just recently opened, La Canasta. I drove by the restaurant several times previously, and it peaked my interest. As fate would have it, there was a parking spot directly across the street. A new adventure was in the making... I entered La Canasta and met my server, Pola, who seated me at a table for two. La Canasta is a BYOB, so I asked Pola what   her favorite fresh juice was. Strawberry Lime was her choice. It was as delicious as it was refreshing! I was pleased... While I surveyed the menu enjoying my fresh juice, I ordered Guacamole and chips.  The Guacamole was fresh as were the chips and were the perfect preparation for my main course. I noticed on the menu,  something new to me. Something different! Spicy Mango Salmon. Salmon Filet sautéed with Broccoli, Cauliflower, Carrots, Bell Pepper and Onion. I ALWAYS enjoy trying something new and ordered it right away. It was uniquely delicious. and very nice. The Salmon was perfectly cooked and drizzled with a sweet and spicy Mango Sauce and served atop the vegetables and  a side of rice. I enjoyed every bite!

I've been staring down this place ever since it opened, but I never got the chance to actually go in and try something because I was always in a rush to work. However, today, I finally got to taste it. My friend and I purposely came from college touring just to try out this new place. 

When you walk in, the decor is superbly put together. The theme, as stated in the name, is green. All the walls are painted green. The tables are white, but the chairs are what gives this place a pop. they have highlighter colored chairs. On each table, they put down board games such as Chinese Checkers. Another plus was that this place offers free Wi-Fi. 

The employees were really friendly. As my friend and I were circling around, wondering what California Tart tastes like, an employee asked us if there was anything he could help us with. Instantly, he knew we wanted to try a sample of the California Tart flavor, so he took a sample cup and put some in. Turns out, the tart flavor was the original flavor that you'd get at Yogurino's. 

I was a bit saddened that they did not offer more toppings such as mango popping bubbles, but the toppings were still very good. They have two sections, one which is just flat out all fruits, and the other which have other toppings such as mochi or chocolate covered pretzels. 

When I was paying for my cup, the girl behind the counter offered me a 10% off coupon for my next visit. I thought this was a very nice tactic to attract returning customers. 

As we were walking out the kitchen if you will call it, the male employee who helped us with the sample yelled to us "thank you!" I thought this was a really nice gesture. This place will definitely be seeing my face again.

It's a diner, but a very nice one. The salad bar is fresh and varied. The entrees if a bit overpriced, are very good. I took my wife here on our first date to give you some idea of how I regarded this place in the past. I haven't been there in a while, but I imagine, like a lot of the rest of Bensalem, it has not changed (very) much. I have a special place in my heart, but I'm not overtly biased. If you like Diner food, you won't likely be disappointed.

Outstanding food best pizza in bucks county great sandwiches friendly service found this place by dumb luck really great find  every one should try this pIzzy. Bought a large pizza last night and reheated two remains pieces today it tastes just as good as it did when it was made. Dino if I could you ten stars I would this is truly the best I've ever tasted.

What makes it good:

Great lunch specials
Great "late" night app/drink specials
Good tasting food
Fairly prompt service- sometimes

What makes it poor:

Unengaging "chefs"
Price
How they handle allergies
Managment's unvinvolved attitude

My ultimate bottom line: Lunch is great, dinner is terrible

I went for a birthday part just last weekend and this was my...fifth or sixth time there. FORTUNATELY this time we'd made a reservation because the lobby was packed. We couldn't move through it. Everyone was irritated and the staff didn't seem to know what to do.

Furthermore, once we sat down our order was taken incorrectly for at least 3 of the guests in our party. The habachi chef looked like he was ready to leave, I had to wait for 15 minutes for the chopsticks I asked three different people for, and when we did finish our meals they sort of hovered over us waiting for us to leave. 

Now, I understand wanting to turn tables, I was in the restaurant business for a lot of years and most of adult working life, BUT! We had a birthday shindig going down and we wanted a few minutes to finish our food/conversation without management breathing down our necks. Literally, I could feel the hot breath. On my neck. CREEPY!

I'll go back for lunch when it's less crowded, loud and overall a terrible experience.

there really isn't much more for me to say that others haven't.

tria has one of the most perfectly curated wine and beer lists that i've ever seen.  there is a choice for every palate, and they really know their stuff.  it would be too much to list every drink i've tried, so i'll refrain, but i've never been disappointed.

i tried the sicilian tuna with black olive/red pepper tapenade and arugula sandwich.  i don't usually eat tuna, but this was magnificent.  

finally, i love how unpretentious, yet still refined, this place is - you can come in your post-work business casual or jeans.  this is the kind of place that makes me so happy to be in philadelphia!

Few months ago I started a ladies brunch club and it changed my life. My first brunch was in March of 2018.  Since then, we have tried to get together on weekly basis for a good meal by a chosen restaurant. 

Last Sunday, Sazon opened up its doors to relatively big group of foodies for a home-style Venezuelan brunch. We were excited to explore a new  South American cuisine. The majority of us ordered the Fish Omelette (Cuajado de Pescado) and it became the hot topic of the afternoon. If you've ever ordered this omelette, then you know it's something very unlike the omelettes you know. This fish omelette tasted better than it sound, and I'd easily go back again to try other dishes.  

Side facts:
- B.Y.O.B. 
- Cash only. 
- Gluten free & vegetarian friendly dishes are available daily.
- Dishes are cooked with corn & olive oil.

P.S: Don't forger to get the Churros for your dessert. 

Four and Half Yelps

The clam chowder is really good and the rock crab is really meaty.  I ordered from the window and ate on one of the benches outside.  The onion rings looked like they were cut too big but they were actually really good.  Also had the calamari and that was good too.  Only thing was, they overcharged me for the calamari and I didn't realize it until I left (they didn't give me an itemized receipt, just a credit card slip). Oh well.
Love this chain, great food for adults and kids. Typically great service and zero lines

Service sucks. We sat down for at least five minutes went by before our server came to our table.  I've had her before I was impressed she was still here. Normally a server will come by before your meal comes and after and she only came by because I had to get up after our meal was delivered to get another bottle of ketchup. It was a Friday but her section wasn't busy. It took her 20 minutes to get me a water. Do you have to pump the water yourself?

Yummy sandwiches! We came later in the afternoon on a VERY cold day, so there wasn't really a line... win! We ordered the bologna and the lamb. My boyfriend loved the bologna, but sadly I did not. The lamb, on the other hand, was AMAZING. We both agreed that was the star of the show. 

For dessert, we ordered the soft serve with key lime pie chunks. It was delicious! 

I would come back for sure if there was no line, but with a long line like I've seen in some photos, I'm just not sure it would be worth it to me.

From the outside, it looks as if this place is could be    some junky lunch spot. It's a bit isolated and it's between two other average/below average franchises.

When you get inside, the atmosphere hits you and you feel the german vibes, smells and sights. This location is fantasticly clean, swift and delicious. I admit I was surprised to see such a nice collection of beers on tap.

Overall, as far as german places go around here, this is a great spot to come to. If you stay too long, you might notice that the german music plays on a short loop and you'll wonder how the staff don't go crazy. Otherwise, I highly advocate a visit here.

Walked there from french quarter, took about 45min, got to see post Katrina results...local action, nice day. Even at 3pm midweek, slight line out door. Order double chicken and as many sides as you can eat, you can always take chicken out . Very good worth trip, i assumed grandson of Maes helped us and conversed as a fine young man, and on his way to another job, give us an insiders list of 4 other great places

Very good pizza, I rarely stray from the Potato and Bacon or Pepperoni, but many of their daily specials are great. The atmosphere does make me feel dated though. I don't know if I am hip enough to enjoy the music and clientele. Two slices (big) will cost you less than five bucks.

Absolutely incredible sushi place with incredible service. Gena was a great server - easy to talk to, took our orders in a timely manner, and checked on us to make sure we were good. We will be back!!

Great food. Gigantic portions. I had the fruitti de mare and it was delicious. Others had chicken parm and chicken marsala and their portions were just enormous. We all were very satisfied and had take home meals for the next day. It was crowded even though it was relatively early on a Sunday (4:30 - 5 pm). We had to wait 15 minutes. Very worth the wait.
This place is great. I've been coming here for years. The staff and owner are friendly and knowledgeable. You must try the wraps!

A fantastic  menu selection of all of your Italian classics without being overbearing. Good price. Huge entre portions. Eggplant Parmesan was extra cheesy and delicious. Skipped on cheese garlic bread since bread, olive oil, and parmesan was complementary. Veal Parmesan was good but a little tough. Yet I'll be back.

Mad scientist or creative chef. Do you have to decide the final outcome for the food lab. It is actually experiment food?  Mmmm. Let see the dinner out come. We have our company holiday dinner there with design menu. It is not cheap but very worth for the trip. 

Our request menu is a four course night with starting the cold appetizers at the first plate. My wife have the almond coconut gazpacho - it is coconut rock shrimp with Fuji Apple salpicon in green curry oil. This a cold soup. The rock shrimp is nice and creative in the soup. The soup base is not normal gazpacho and is white. It is good. I have the avocado leaf seated yellow fin tuna. This is the best of the cold app. It come green mango salad, aji amarillo sorbet, fish sauce caramel and tamarind peanut crunch. It creative that the sorbet replace the wasabi and the fish sauce caramel replace the balsamic reduction sauce. Now you know why they call themselves food lab. 

The second course are the hot appetizers. I have smoked maple glazed pork belly. It top with hoe cake, black eyed peas, green tomato chow-chow. Usually I don't care about hoe cake but sauce and other ingredients combine, it is great. The pork belly is cook perfectly. If you are not good chef, do not try this dish because it need three part meat harmony. My wife has Serrano ham zeppole. The slice hams were place on top of rosemary doughnuts with compressed melon, Saba and Parmesan snow. Interesting dish. The rosemary was deep fried to crispy with seasoning. I have not have it this way before. 

Our third course are the main dishes. I have the red snapper a la plancha. It is fillets snapper with sautéed and glazed on top on avocado coconut grits, baby spinach, mergers marmalade, avocado chutney and mango harissa purée. This best main dish tonight the purée go very well with the fish. My wife has the painted hills short rib 'sancocho'. Usually the Caribbean sancocho is a mix of meat and veggies soup. This is an overhaul design for the short rib with boniato, yuca, sweet potato, and sweet corn, green plantain,avocado toss watercress, and cilantro sweet garlic juice. I only can said - it is good. 

The final course is the sugar crusted butter cake or chocolate peanut butter bar. Both of them is great. I the butter cake because the cake form the caramelized sugar crust on all expose wall. The cake is syrup and is good. 

The only thing is the food take a bit time to come out for the first dish. The rest are good. The service is great. The drink you have to refer to the pic since we don't know what they have created.

If I could give zero stars I would. This place was terrible. Awful customer service, very dirty, people were packed in like sardines and not following COVID guidelines. Waited an hour for a table even though I had a reservation and left because I still wasn't being seated. I will not be returning
Their cheesesteak is so good it don't matter what you get on it I just don't understand why their not named phillys best cheesesteak ever

Not the most visually appealing place to visit in the city but I already knew what to expect when going. As expected, the food didn't disappoint. Chicken is sooooo good! The rice is decent too. Very filling for the cost. Can't go wrong with Manchu.

Horrible experience. Ordered the deluxe bento box Waited 20 mins for the food. The people came in behind me already got their food. So I walked to the counter asking for the progress.  the cashier give me a dirty look as It is my fault for being impatient. Never once apologize for it. The food is cold and very mediocre. Rice is dry. Never again return.   Warning: really slow and cold service. The cashiers are just couple of high school kids. So If you like bad service and crappy food. Please drop by.

I had dreams of it perhaps being about the Biltmore, San Ysidro Ranch or something a little more swanky. But it wasn't meant to be...

So, here's to you El Zarape! My 100th review.

Had the mixed plate that had all of their different meats combined with peppers, onions, mushrooms and cheese. All of this resting on top of four fresh made tortillas. Shared some of this along with a plate of chicken enchiladas. These aren't some premade enchiladas that they reheat in a microwave. No, sir...they are freshly made with those handmade tortillas plus some tasty rice and beans.

Nice folks running the place, and for entertainment, a jukebox and tv showing some cheesy novela. It's a locals kind of place serving great food without all the hype.

Try it!

Ribs, brisket, mac n' cheese, homemade pickles... This place is great, especially for meat lovers!

I met someone here who says he comes to The Joint every time he's in New Orleans, and I see why. The food is understated yet delicious.

The weather held out, so it was really nice to sit outside on the back patio, despite the heat from the ovens.

Definitely check this place out!
This place is awesome! The staff is always friendly and helpful. And I love love love the new patio! It's a great addition to this fun neighborhood bar.

Great ambiance and bar service.  The lobster rolls were like eating bad smelly seafood. One bite one smell.......NO WAY. bologna sammy yuck. The chicken skewers the girls said the sauce was over powering and over cooked. Place was packed and I realize that Nashville could use an awesome chef.  They could kill it here.

This place is open, very good customer service and great drinks (peach mimosa). My food was okay, they messed up my order (the tacos) but my waiter gave me a free shot for the inconvenience. I tried my friends food, she had the French roast bites and they were excellent. Would definitely come back again.

Just a pit stop for the ladies in our group to grab a quick bite to soak up all those cranberry Grey Gooses.

It's tiny, but clean, and the food comes out quick. The staff didn't even give us dirty looks for coming in six minutes before closing or spit in the food! Yay!

Onward...

So I ordered a bacon cheesesteak & it was good, wasn't the best cheesesteak I've ever had but it was still good. Only problem is it later left me sick.... :(. My stomach in soo much pain it hurts to move, then when I'm able to move has left me going to the bathroom way more than I should be. I've only had this experience once before after eating a McDonalds cheeseburger (which is why I've never ate a cheeseburger from there in years). I looked at some reviews and didn't see any similar situations, so I hope this was just an isolated incident....kinda scared to try them again though....
Bruschetta is the best! I walk 2 miles to come eat their bruschetta. It's by far the best I've had

My friends fancy me a South Philadelphia Italian BYO cognoscento. And have eaten (often) at my fair share of them. L'Angolo, Caffe Valentino,Scannicchio, Pesto, even wine list joints like Le Virtu' and Paradiso, are all well deserving of the praise they receive.  But my undisputed and longstanding favorite is Tre Scalini.  I have been a regular since they opened, so part of the allure for me is the 'familiar' feel of the place.  I sometimes say to myself on the way in "I must be stuck in rut.  Why do I keep coming back to the same place?" only to hear my own refrain on the way out: "that was one of the best meals I ever ate!"  It is consistently excellent and I never tire of the food. Franca DiRenzo, the owner/chef, is a genuine artist, transforming the simple into the delectable. 

I recommend that you do the multi course meal here. 

Start with some appetizers (family style if you like) like the Melanzana Napolitana (perfectly pan fried eggplant with simple marina and grated cheese; so simple yet so fantastic) or the Bruschetta Molisana (white beans and calamari in a simple tomato fish broth served over a crust of bread). The mussels are also fantastic, as is the burrata. 

For the pasta course, the signature dish, squid ink papardelle with crab meat and prawns, is sure to please. But I like the simplest food here;  spaghetti alla chittara with a delectably understated tomato and basil sauce, or my favorite, aglio e olio with garlic, olive oil, capers, anchovies, and a touch of hot pepper. Recent additions include papardelle with quail and another with lamb ragu, both deliciously inspired offerings from the central Apennines. 

For the secondo course try the daily fish special, usually a Branzino Livornese (steamed white fish with tomatoes and black olives) or their signature veal dish is the 'filet mignon' medallions of veal with wild mushrooms and the veal juices. Even a stereotype dish like chicken piccante dissolves tenderly in the mouth with its perfectly fused flavors of olive oil, capers, and lemon.  It's really impossible to make a mistake in ordering.  And every so often they have special fare like rabbit, wild boar, or my favorite, baby goat (capretto).  If you are so lucky to be dining on one of those rare nights, DO NOT pass any of these up.

This place was mediocre at best.

We were there tonight and the service was poor. They did not seem to have enough staff and our waitress was absent for long periods.

As to the drinks from the bar - the Long Island Tea was awful, very tart; I've never tasted one that tasted like this attempt. The "Hurricane" was far too sweet and bears no resemblance to what you would get in NOLA.

The food was below average. We had Boudine balls, boiled shrimp, etouffee, and seafood gumbo. None were anything to write home about. The shrimp was not fresh and boiled as tough as rubber, the etouffee and gumbo seemed as if they were spiced with something out of a jar off the Kroger shelf. The Boudin Balls were fairly edible but don't compare to the real deal.

If you think you'll get authentic Cajun food here forget it. It's more of slightly spiced pabulum for midstream diners. I'll give it a survival date of September this year. Skip it.

PS: The room is very loud, all hard surfaces, nobody was speaking too loudly while we were there but it sounded like a megaphone in an empty garbage can. The seats were hard and uncomfortable, Hang a blanket or something for God sake, soak up some of that bouncing sound!

Unfortunately, a few things colored this experience for me.

I want to say that I like the general state of things here. The service was good, and the decor is befitting a gastropub. People were generally here to eat and hang out, which is perfectly my thing.

But my chicken was burnt. My potatoes were so badly exposed to fire that I thought a few were mushrooms. My quinoa, on the other hand, was delicious. Occasionally it looks like the place fills with cliquish university students, but that's the tradeoff that comes with being right there on campus.

I'd give it another try.

The staff is very attentive.  The Flamenkutchen and Heirloom Tomato Salad are marvelous.  The Heirloom Tomato Salad has all the flavors of summer.   A relaxed French bistro atmosphere makes for a relaxing place to dine

A step above Mod pizza, but similar in pricing. I prefer the service at Fired, they bring your meal to you instead of calling your name. 
Mod has more choice of toppings, but I thought the quality at Fired was better. 
I had a Mediterranean with thin crust, and the topping flavors were excellent. The crust is very thin, almost crepe paper thin, for good or ill. I liked it, made for a nice light lunch. 
Service was fast, but there was no wait when I arrived. Pizza arrived at my table in maybe 5 minutes. 
Ambiance is nice - metal chairs aren't conducive to sitting long, but everything was clean. 
I'll be back - want to try the Mac n cheese and maybe a salad. 
Good pizza, fast service, nice place to sit for a meal. Great lunch spot.

Cute little neighborhood place. Put down your phone, enjoy the music, listen to the conversations around you, check out the funky stuff on the walls (can you find the guy wrapped in rope?). This is a great place to enjoy some food and waste some time. I had the eggs bennie, which was very good. Perfectly poached eggs, crispy ham, and a decent hollindase. Mimosa was a bit pricey, but excellent! Service was polite but not intrusive. I'll be back.

I'd like to say how great the food was here because the menu sounded good, but that would mean I would have had to had their food, and that would have meant I would have had some kind of service to order their food! Instead, we sat down, got our menus, and then that was the end of seeing any staff. They must have looked at us looking at them in their huddled corner chatting at least 15 times, yet they must have been having the most important conversation ever because they couldn't be bothered to actually serve us! No waters, no order taking, nothing. And this was at 4 in the afternoon, they weren't too busy! After patiently waiting 20 minutes with an infant, we got up to leave. The chatty group looked confused and so I stopped to tell them why we were leaving and they just stared with a dumb look like I was speaking chinese.I saw our would have been waitress not too much later on State St shopping. Guess she figured if she actually helped us it would have cut into her shopping trip.

Dissapointing in an economy like this where you would think your business would be appreciated you can't even get your order taken to spend your hard earned money. On another note, this crap experience led us to the Santa Barbara fishhouse and I can't say enough about how great the food was and how attentive and nice the staff is.

Leave your personal convos for your time off work and maybe actually work when you are at work...!

Found this little gem while hunting for some good ol fashion Mexican food. Not the tex mex stuff.. I mean real Mexican food. The taste of the food is fresh, vibrant and savory. Even the chips and dip when you first sit down is home made and delicious. The owner greeted us and sat us down right away. The place is clean and well lighted. Even the music is Mexican. Looking for great Mexican food? Look no further.

We just had brunch at Jackie's this past Sunday and found it very good. The food was fresh and of good quality. We particularly liked the shrimp grits and the bottomless mimosas.

The staff was kind and went out of their way to make sure we had everything we needed.

We will definitely recommend and come back again.

Krueger's is a solid new addition to the Mass ave food scene. It's lively atmosphere and solid food make it a great fit for the area. I look forward to coming here when it gets warm to enjoy their outdoor patio. 

This is a place to grab a burger and beer with friends. The dining room is a fun space to be in with great music. It's a tasty mid-tier-priced burger joint that is a great way to start out a night.

We started our meal with the beer cheese. It was excellent for sharing and I'd highly recommend it. We also split a side of fries to dip in the beer cheese. Very tasty! I went for the Bleu Gruyere burger which was a satisfying blend of sweet and savory. My buddy went for the Spicy burger which was super good but, buyer beware, really spicy.

Overall, Kreuger's Tavern was a great experience and has been added to my short list of meet-up spots in Indy. Look forward to coming back.

Like the other guy said, don't bother! Went for lunch buffet last weekend, food is so not flavorful! Ewwwww ! They call this Indian? Where did old owners goooooooooo? Drive to Amans Chalfont for the best!

Food and service were solid 4 stars but the noise level in this restaurant (we sat upstairs) was the worst in my entire life and I have dined in several thousand restaurants in the past 40+ years.  It was so noisy that I had trouble hearing my co-diners sitting next to me at the same table. I will never go to this restaurant again because it was uncomfortably loud. If so loud is what you want that you can't hear your friends sitting next to you then this is the place for you. The restaurant should hang some more drapes and mount sound absorbing material on the ceiling perhaps.

Its close to 4 stars...but they dont take credit cards so i cant go there when im out of cash and i had one bad experience with their food.... but if you have cash and you live near green lane try it.

I love Mediterranean food, it's always fresh and flavorful! Luna Grill is not this. It is a super plain version of the Mediterranean food. 

Additionally, there is no real lunch menu. Pretty much the cheapest thing you can get is a wrap for $11 bucks. Luna should consider having a lunch type menu. Wouldnt be as annoyed at the mediocrity if it wasn't a $12 dollar to go lunch with no drink.
From now on i'll make the extra trek out to Alladin Cafe that has one of the best (and well priced) shwarmas I have ever had, plus its local and not a chain. :)

I really, really, really am not a fan of this place. But my boss for some reason likes it here and will pays for my food, so I really can't complain. The service is usually pretty quick and it's inexpensive (probably why he likes it.... he's a little cheap). But you get what you pay for and the quality of Mexican food isn't good. I'd almost rather sit and my office and eat a Lean Cuisine. However, us admin girls would come here after work for drinks and their drinks are usually pretty good and strong. Just what I need after the end of the month is due at work.
Hands down the BEST shrimp cocktail in the world! I know, land-locked middle America, but it is all about the fresh grated horseradish.

So unhappy with my experience. I love the food, hands down one of my favorite places, HOWEVER, the customer service that I received (and have been receiving from Stephanie on multiple occasions) was appalling. Stephanie was rude, unapologetic and frankly a deterrent as a customer.  Again, the food is delicious and always prepared in a timely fashion. After speaking with my friends (who also swear that this is one of their favorite places eat) agreed that Stephanie's customer service was far below what should even be expected from a Mc. Donalds employee, NOR is this first time we were taken back by her comments to us. If I were the manager of this store I would highly suggest employing a new front staff to work hands on with customers who love your food so much. Stephanie, as the first impression of your store has accumulated an extremely poor representation of your company.
Great service and delicious food. I love that they have molcajetes here for the colder weather. Their chile relleno is really good too. Also, the salsa bar is amazing
Great service and food! We've only sat at the bar but have had a great experience each time.
Morrisville hidden jewel, best chinese food in town, I wouldn't go anywhere else. This is usually my go to place. They also have delivery.

This a new and happening place in our area and rightfully so.. it's by the water, Hawaiian tiki feel, outside deck seating as well as high cathedral main dining area with a big bar..

We came on a Thursday thinking maybe it's less crowded.. and it was packed (we drove by a few Fridays prior)  wait was about an hour @ 5:30.. we found seating by bar and there were social distancing there as well..

Pros: ambience, food was decent.. the oysters were very fresh and clean well- not sandy or gritty.. the raw bar was also in the bar area.. the fish/chips - was decent, not crispy like I expected, looked awesome but not crispy..

Drinks wise: I had the house margarita, pre-made in one those kegs like setup you would see for beer, same with a lot of their other drinks, served in a plastic glass.. was ok, a little too sweet for my taste and price wise.. south tampa pricing.. 

Cons:  disappointed by the changes to what was posted not too long ago by another yelper. I ordered the tuna poke and it showed up with 2 halves instead of 4 halves and with chips instead.. not what I expected.. 

Overall, fun ambience..it's definitely a place you come for ambience and oysters/beer..beyond that.. it's not foodie awesome, at least not for me :)

DISGUSTING FOOD AND POOR SERVICE

The wait was not worth the pricey,small portioned and gross food.
We had a party of three for lunch and our food was cold and VERY salty.
My spouse was given shrimp that had gone bad and my father was given a beer that was well over its expiration date.
We did not bring this to anyone's attention because or server was MIA for our entire dinner other than to  present our check.
The place is VERY tiny so all the LOUD patrons most of who were consuming alcohol were ridiculously obnoxious.
If I could give them zero stars I would.We will NEVER be back to this location and I will let anyone I know be made aware of how subpar their food and service is.
Went for my birthday with a party of 10! Service was great! We did not have to wait too long for our food! Our food is so delicious and fresh! I had a great birthday! Thank you!

I didn't get a chance to eat so I can't say whether the food is good. I went in last Tuesday night at 7:50 pm and there were a few people in line. The two girls working there told all of us that they are "closing in ten minutes" several times while I was looking at the menu. The person in line in front of me asked if we would have to eat in ten minutes or if we would have to take the good to go, the young girl rudely responded "well, we close in ten minutes so do whatever you want". I really did not want to be rushed so we left. There we're only two teenage girls working in the front unsupervised providing terribly rude service.

Great menu, certainly the best gyro in Boise, they're well sized and worth the price. Had the Lamb-beef combo in the Athena style, was juicy and delicious. Great beer selection at reasonable prices. Excellent tzatziki and pita, strongly recommend the hummus plate. The baklava was tasty, think it could do with a touch less cinnamon. Ambience is great, cool light fixtures, just hope they switch to warmer-colored light bulbs-the ones they currently have are very white, a bit intense when you're there at night.

I wish I had the experience others had I didn't eat my chicken it looked extremely under cooked (especially for it to supposedly have been smoked) the cabbage was old and I didn't even think twice about the plantains. Will not return.

This place is amazing for Brunch.  Everything on the menu is delicious but I particularly like some of their simpler dishes like their dips of the day.  

The dinner is also very good but I thought it was a bit pricey for the meal (e.g., $21 for a stuffed pepper seems excessive, and the fish I got was sparce, presented in a thin broth for something like $28).  

Still, don't miss this place.  Excellent food and the service is great too.

This store is close to me so I find myself there occasionally for quick trips or replacement of single items. The staff is always quite friendly and I think they are the best part of the operation. But the produce is always on the cusp of spoilage. Honestly, I've never seen anything like it at any other store. No matter what the fruit and veggies look like at the time of purchase, they are rotten within a day or two. EVERY. SINGLE. TIME.
Yummy sandwiches! The fried chicken breast banh mi is the best! The bread is just bright too!

Amazing ranchero omelet!  I loved this place, but I will say that I have heard many negative reviews from friends.  Not about the food, but the service.  My service was great, but I also did go here during the week.  I've heard that the weekend service can be very slow.

I have finally found what I have been looking for, since I returned to Saint Louis 13 years ago.  La Tejana Taqueria is an authentic Mexican restaurant.  It's not fancy, but the food is excellent; the chips and salsa so FRESH!  They have never seen the inside of a bag or a jar.  I will definitely be back.  I am happy!

Fantastic all around! What a great experience this was! Tried to visit last Tuesday during happy hour, but realized then that reservations were needed. But once all that was in ace, I'm happy to say it was all well worth the wait. The food was delicious and very well priced for the happy hour, and despite the large crowd, came out to us very quickly. The staff was so nice and helpful, and it was exactly what I needed! We're set on making this our new place for Mexican,  and can't wait to return!

I called to ask if it was possible to make reservations for a large party on a Sunday. The young girl who answered said that for large parties they DO take reservations and took down all my info saying that I just needed to wait for a call back to confirm. Never got a call back so I called and was told the total opposite. Apparently they DON'T take reservations for large parties on a Sunday. So now I'm a day out from my event day and do not have a reservation like I thought. When I asked how/why I was given the wrong information this rude man on the phone just said I don't know. I will definitely never give this place my business.
Delivery is always on time and food is hot. The delivery time is always quicker than the time reported. Best cannolis!

I don't like donuts.

That statement was true until I came here. Damn you, Federal Donuts.

I live a half a block away from here and regrettably this place has become a staple of my hangover diet. The fancy donuts are quite good - I really like the blueberry marscapone and the chocolate sea salt. I was underwhelmed by the dark chocolate coconut.

The coffee is quite good - they have their own branded beans that brew a strong and smooth cup.

Decided to head to Rippy's to try out their BBQ. We arrived at the door and showed our id's. I was then promptly asked to show the contents of my drawstring bag. The door bouncer proceeded to search through my bag and came upon my prescription. He then decided to violate my privacy rights and ask what they were and what I take them for. I declined to tell him and said I don't need to share that information. I don't need to share my privacy, nor medical information with a door bouncer of a BBQ restaurant. Seems like all he was trying to do, was interrogate me so he could confiscate my prescription. 
We decided to leave after that awkward confrontation and won't be returning. 
Hey, btw, what medications do you take and what are they for?
Just Kabob has the most amazing meat dishes with the best flavors!  I also absolutely love their tabouli salad!

We've stayed at several RC properties: half moon bay, lake Tahoe, marina del rey, laguna niguel, and palm desert. Santa Barbara was by far the worst experience we've had.

Check In: Crazy long lines. Not nearly enough staff. If you're a marriott titanium elite (like us), good luck getting early check in or late check-out here

Rooms: if you want a decent room here, make sure you book an ocean view or better. Regular rooms and suites are "meh". Most of the rooms barely have any light coming in and feel very dark.

Food: Most RC food I've had is overpriced garbage, and SB was no exception. I never go to a RC property expecting decent food, and will normally get food delivered. This property is built on a giant hill, so for half the rooms it's a 10 minute hike to get to the lobby (this is not an exaggeration). Food delivery people aren't allowed to deliver to your room and the RC staff will not do this for you. 

Views: Beach is not nearly as nice as half moon bay or laguna niguel. The view at night when the moon is bright is kinda magical, though. That was the silver lining of this trip

Staff: Most of the staff here is really nice, but one experience kind ruined it for us. My wife left her wedding ring in the hotel room. She followed up three times with the hotel with no response. I followed up with the the hotel three more times and they finally responded. They said they were unable to find the ring, but they would follow up with us to fill out a report for the missing item. We never heard from them again. I would have expected more from a RC property, but I guess this is what you get at Santa Barbara. 

One more thing - you can expect random golf carts zooming past and honking at you around the property. It kinda takes away from what should be a relaxing experience.

One of my favorite places to go! Love their breakfast and lunch options. Especially their banana pancakes and Melba French toast! Also love their cinnamon bun French toast! It's huge but it's delicious because it's an actual cinnamon bun not just a piece of toast that tastes like it.  

One good tip is that you can get a short stack with their pancakes and most of the French toast options. A great place to go for a quick meal. Gets pretty packed at peak hours. It's one of their smaller locations but I think one of the best locations. Also great place to sit outside in the warmer weather.

Normally I wait till I visit a restaurant 2-3 times before I write a review but this place right here... CAFE CARIBE they are in the building slaying a slinging breakfast, coffee and sandwiches. I called my order in and thanks to Doug P. I ordered the SUNRISE WRAP and added a side of home fries.

Now I should have known when I pulled into the parking lot and there were almost no spaces that this was a clue that this spot was jumping. I expected maybe three to four people to be in this little restaurant but when I got in it was busy and full of life just like if it was in a small neighborhood eatery back home in in New York. The smell of the place was delicious with the aromas of fresh food and cafe con leche. you could hear lots of conversation buzzing, people meeting each other and it was so cool.

When I got home and tore into my breakfast it was so good! The sunrise wrap has bacon, ham, eggs, green peppers and thin slices of potato wrapped in a pressed pita bread. I added American cheese but I could have did without it,  it was perfect by itself. The home fries were hot the home fries were hot, crispy, seasoned and delicious I thoroughly enjoyed everything. 

Sometimes you want fatty creations with an elaborate name for you first meal but most times you just want eggs, bread, meat and potatoes made right! That is what Cafe Caribe provides. Simplicity made to perfection!

This is a hidden gem and you have to dig deep into a little strip mall to find this place.  Staying away from the national chains and patronizing local businesses was the goal on our Yelp coffee shop search.  

There was plenty of free offstreet parking and inside the shop was clean and nicely decorated. There were also bistro tables out front.  Since the outdoor seating was situated in the shade,  we took advantage of the beautiful December weather. 

The Columbian coffee was spot-on, bold,  flavorful and smooth to the palette.  The baked goods were made fresh and they had a wide variety to choose from. We had biscottis with our coffee making this session more of an Italian experience than Colombian for us. The eclairs looked amazing.  I was thinking about trying them on my next visit.  The young lady who served us was friendly and clearly looking to please us. This was a Colombian restaurant she had a Spanish accent - she was wonderful. 

I'll be back - they have a full menu and eating breakfast or lunch there looks like it would be delicious.

Came in for dinner in Monday night. Server, Houston, was awesome. Super spunky and was right there when we needed him. Food was great, and the beer selection is phenomenal. They were out of the beer that I ordered, but had my second choice which was just as great! We will be back for sure!

Absolutely the best pizza in the city. It's old school and classic. The service is outstanding and food is always fresh.  The location is perfect right near all the sporting events. Must try the pizzaz pizza there is no one that makes it better.

I walked in at 3:39 pm Thanksgiving eve. Every other deli in town was closed! Trust me I know I had either been there or called. I needed fish for breakfast Thanksgiving morning. I don't know why this slipped my mind until the very last minute! But!!!!!
I got in line at the deli counter. People are picking up previously ordered , orders! Turkeys the whole deal! But they had their act totally together! Taking care of everyone.
I ordered sable, hand sliced nova, 2 white fish chubs,  (which he let me hand pick!) chopped liver
Pastrami, pickled tomatoes, ( he threw in 1 extra for free because they were small), and half sour pickles.
Now during all of this I'm being fed by them. A piece of pastrami (and not a small one)  a pickle, some teriaki wings, all because I said I had never been there before! No!!!! They were giving everyone little treats! All on single sheets of wax paper, wearing gloves, very sanitary! It was divine!
And this morning all the food was just spectacular! These guys are my new go to!!!!!!
Unparalleled in middle Tennessee. Best pizza south of Mason-Dixon. Used to be Nashville's best kept secret.

My husband made reservations for my Birthday here on Sunday October 16! We had pizza which was really good to start I got a house salad with grilled chicken which was ok and a side of meatballs which were pretty good although the sauce was not what I was expecting it was very tasty! My husband had the grilled chicken entree which he said was good as well minus the artichoke because he is not a vegetable kind of guy . We sat outside it was beautiful the restaurant was pretty empty inside so at least outside we could people watch. I would give them 5 stars if they had made an any effort to make my birthday feel special. Some restaurants give you little cards or desserts or just even a Happy Birthday wish for spending my day at their restaurant. I will definitely return just not on my birthday again ! The pizza  and meatballs are a must try!! I did express to the host it was my birthday not sure if my husband mentioned it when booking through open table FYI.
Pretty good, price is little bit higher, service is perfect. Quality is good, quantity is smaller, you may need to order 2 entries.

We have been going to Luigi's for a couple years. It has been our go-to pizza shop for the last year or so. In the last few months things have been very inconsistent. Pizzas have gone from overcooked to undercooked and back again a few times. We used to dine in regularly but we've stopped altogether now. Service is always friendly but it has become painfully slow. It shouldn't take an hour to complete a meal. We are going to take a break from Luigi's for a while and give them a try again over the summer.

The service was very slow and inept. Drinks went dry and we would have ordered additional beverages had we been offered. 
Our order was incorrect as well as our bill. 
Server was not attentive at all and did not seem to care when food and bill was incorrect. 
Very disappointing. 
Rating: will not return.

I've been here several times to try to eat and, despite the empty dining room, I've been repeatedly told that it would be a 30-45 minute wait. I hope they eventually deal with the problems, because I hear the ramen is good, but I can't say because I don't have time to wait 45 minutes for ramen.

Mmmmmmmmmmmmmmm try the papardelle with creamy tomato sauce, porcini mushrooms, and pancetta... the pasta was perfection and the sauce was among the best I've ever tasted! I highly recommend it!

The other couple of dishes we had were pretty good but not as memorable... and the ambience was a bit on the louder/brighter side, but the staff were friendly and prompt.

I would rate the papardelle alone at 5 stars plus!! But yeah, the experience as a whole was probably 4 stars, or maybe 4.5. Not bad at all!

This place was once fun and a must-see. Gone are the glory days of this place being full of shops, bars, and restaurants. If you're a history/architecture buff, go and see it *once*. Seeing the few damaged and disheveled skeletons of trains in the back train yard will make you cringe slightly (tetanus, anyone?). Why the heck does this place charge for parking? Is that what is keeping the bills paid? Anyways, here is how your visit will go: overpriced parking, feed some super fat fish, see the Hard Rock Cafe and remember the 90s when those were cool, go inside, find the Fudgery and have some songs sung to you, pay $30 for fudge, hike through an empty train station, check out the Whispering Arch at the front entrance, awe at the "Allegorical Window" in the Grand Hall, and then decide that was fun enough for an hour and leave. Side note: there have been four hotels in that place since 1985 (three different ones since 2008 when I stayed there). Hotel chains don't even want to stay at Union Station for too long.

Let's all pour one out for what Union Station used to be...
Had steak and shrimp hibachi and it was amazing! Great flavor, good portions and customer service was very welcoming. I found one of my favorite neighborhood spots! I'll be back for sure!!

I ordered via Doordash the mushrooms panini and Honey BBQ wings. Thankfully the wings were decent so it wasn't a complete waste of money but I will never order to go again. The mushroom panini was so soggy, I could not eat the bottom piece of bread because it was soaked. The fries were also stale

My husband and I have been going to Nacho's since they opened two years ago and have generally enjoyed their food and service.  We went to lunch there today and I ordered the lunch enchilada plate while my husband ordered the fish.  

They delivered my meal, twenty minutes later I was finished and my husband still hadn't received his plate.  The server avoided us and when we got up to leave and asked to just pay for what we ate, he said it was "almost" done and that we would have to pay for it so we might as well take it home.

We walked up to pay our bill and the person at the cash register said we were responsible for paying for it.  I refused, my husband agreed to pay half.  I expressed my disappointment and told him that I would never come back and would write negative reviews on food web sites and he said, "Fine, don't come back again.  I don't care." 

I think I can safely say I won't be going back and I would advise you to support Las Palmas across the street instead.

Great seafood place. Very casual, nothing fancy. One of the most impressive things is that you can see into their kitchen and it is spotless and you can tell very well kept. Food comes out very quick also. Only complaint is food portions could be a little bigger. They have the best key lime pie I have ever had. Many of the staff have worked there for decades so they are attentive and know how to do their job properly.
Awsome place, great selection of beer, Belgian beer- try it it's awsome

I love this big, spacious patio. Probably the best in IV. However they have "the chair." That super trendy chair that only fits size 2 people for more than 15 mins at a time. 

Anyhow, I thought the popcorn chicken had an excellent spice to it!! I loved the seasoning and was ups to try out more of their Shnacks. 

I also ordered the teriyaki chicken rice bowl. It was decent. There was a LOT of steamed cabbage. And lots of rice too. I didn't mind the over abundance of rice so much as all the cabbage. The cabbage looked bland but the needn't try it so I can't comment on the cabbage. The teriyaki chicken itself was pretty decent.  Nice big cuts and not overly doused in teriyaki sauce.  However, I'd prefer to go across the street to Hana Kitchen for a better chicken rice bowl. It's possible I overlooked the condiments , but this bowl was lacking. 

A lot of the menu was not in English, so I definitely intend to go back and try some items that aren't so American. I'll keep an eye on Yelp for suggestions!!

I went with a friend on a Thursday evening and they REFUSE TO SIT US even though there were two EMPTY tables. We were told we could sit at the bar in the mean time and that the wait would be 25 mins. (No one else was waiting to be seated beside us).There was no space at the bar. 10 minutes go by and the tables are still empty so I asked the waitress if they took reservations, she said no. I asked her why couldn't we be seated at one of those empty tables and she said that those were for parties of four and those were the rules. Totally ridiculous to have customers waiting when you have empty tables! Never again!
This place is one of the best kept secrets in Tucson Arizona! If you want Bomb food that is going to leave your mouth watering than you have come to the right spot.
