Locals have a new reason to crawl through piles of tourists, beads, and T-shirts to get to this new gem in the French Market. I've eaten lunch here two days in a row, and let me tell y'all somethin': it's FANTASTIC, and I don't say that lightly. I say to these people: WELCOME to the Quarter! 

MENU: 
The menu is small and diverse. The current veggie sandwich (beets, goat cheese, spinach/cilantro) should be a permanent fixture, because it will be a permanent staple on my lunch menu if it is. If I were making it, the ONE thing I'd add are a few candied walnuts to give it some crunchy texture. Other than that? Perfection. I love the grilled cheese, love the fromage fort, love the juusto, and the house-made pickles are delicious. The ingredients are clearly fresh, and a certain amount of love has to go into making a sandwich as good as the 3-4 of theirs I've tasted in the last couple days (we each bought different sandwiches and tasted them all). The bread choices are phenomenal, and I haven't even been able to scope out their artisanal cheeses yet. 

$: 
The prices are low enough here that my $10-per-lunch budget at work (including tip) can be accommodated with leftovers in hand. 

Sidenote #1: At long last I finally have somewhere to send people for the quality of food that I enjoy without a $3-4 tourist tax added to each price tag. This is the perfect place to pair with its delicious neighbor, Meals from the Heart. 

Sidenote #2 : That one-star review down there is pretty sketchy, y'all. No previous reviews on the account, no mention of any particular menu items eaten--- in short? Don't pay any attention to it. Try it out for yourself. 

Note to the owners: I think the most important part of my review is that your quality to price ratio can be the perfect marketing tool for y'all -- I'd bring menus, and more importantly, introduce yourselves to every business in the Quarter if I were you. Offer yourselves up as a delicious, healthy, and AFFORDABLE option to the service industry folks, maybe with some kind of incentive, and y'all will have more pick-up orders than you can handle. Kudos on the menu and its execution. The FM Corp. should be proud as hell to have y'all on board.
Very good food and service. Love the small plate options.

Tables are as squished together as possible, but service is great and food too.  Gumbo is good, blackened redfish was nothing special (but when is it ever?), ettouffee was greenish (?) but good.  Macque shoux is not bad.  Nothing outstanding but nothing to complain about either.

Some of the best service I've ever seen. Food was great too, but over a year later it's the service that still stands out as being extraordinary and would make us definitely return on our next visit to New Orleans. We arrived for our reservation after a day of sightseeing and walking so we were dressed more casually and were slightly disheveled. We received the same top notch service and consideration as the tables around us that were full of suited men and women in fancy attire. I was even offered a velvet stool for my purse which amused me to no end. The food was delicious, the service smooth, and we were even offered a complimentary selection of desserts that were presented in an ornate wooden box.

Really good authentic Mexican food. It's a small place but it's decorated beautifully and very cozy. It's a byob but the margaritas were amazing, one of the best I've had, and the food was great too. I would recommend getting the appetizer sampler to try a little of everything.

Used to come here for the taco Tuesday but now we go for the Sunday kids eat free. The specials are usually our go to because they are always changing but so good. The edamame is our favorite appetizer and no matter what we get a side of their cilantro ranch to go with the chips and salsa. We try to always make it a point to go here when family is visiting.

One of the best meals that I've had in a long time. We were a group of 8, so got the $75 per person tasting menu. Tried so many great dishes (too many to list). Excellent service and very friendly staff...The only drawback to this place is that the kitchen and dining area are one room and it's very loud. If you live in South Jersey, I totally recommend going to Zeppoli for dinner.

My husband and I decided to try this place out. It was a Monday night and not super busy for dinner. The food was good but not great. You're paying more for the presentation of the food in my opinion. The best thing we ordered was the gumbo soup. Very good! The rest of our meal was average for duck and scallops. You have multiple waiters and unfortunately my husband and I didn't have a good experience with one of ours (our main waiter), we felt ignored and unimportant, almost as if he was purposely not treating us like the other tables he was waiting on. This made my husband and I uncomfortable nearly the entire time. We spent good money, got the bananas foster for dessert, also average. This place is good... worth the money? No. Experience may depend greatly on your waiter(s).

I went and ordered food for take-out. I ordered a flat bread pizza and a piece of quiche. Things just didn't seem to go well. First, the quiche came out in a plastic container ready to go before the young lady had even started making, much less cooking, my pizza. Upon making mention of this, the girl told me that she would keep my quiche warm. Finally, my pizza was ready and I went home. Arriving home, I discovered that the bottom of the plastic container had melted into my quiche. (Inedible at this point.) I called and spoke with the owner and was told that I would be receiving compensation via email. Well, much to my dismay, the email never arrived! This truly is a shame since I had such high hopes for this establishment.
Los chilaquiles están muy ricos, me gusta que tienen refrescos mexicanos. Y los precios están muy accesibles y nada caro.

One of my favorite places to stay in all of Nashville.  Unique, stylish, super friendly staff, cool and perfectly located in the historic Lockeland Springs neighborhood in Nashville.  I loved it so much I moved down the street from this place!  Fire pit in the back is awesome, great beer selection.

Amazing! So glad I came here finally ! Love the outdoor seating and service was very good as well!! Food was incredible wow and so many different options for whatever mood you may be in 
Food : 
Starters - 
- Grilled eggplant : really good! Was more of a salad. Very light with amazing flavors. 
- Warm Seafood Salad : This is a main, but four of us split it as a starter and it was PERFECT!! The amount of seafood was so good. Highly recommend 
- Mushroom Pizza : the four of us also split this as a starter, and the flavors came together so nicely. The mushroom with the goat cheese, and it was baked to absolute perfection 

Mains : 
- Opal Paella : Wow this was insane. The seafood was cooked amazingly, and the seasonings were perfect
- Vegetable Napoleon : I was shocked with this one, but it was actually so yummy. The mixture of all the different layers worked so nicely. 
- Grilled Ribeye : Really good cut of meat. Had a lot of fat, but it wasn't in a bad way. It added lots of flavor and I just ate around it. The meat was cooked exactly how I wanted it too 

Cocktails :
Only had 2, but I got the Ginger mint Paloma and the Passion Fruit martini. Both were very good!! I liked the martini better, but would definitely get both again!! Cant wait to try more 

Do yourself a favor and come here if you've never been! You won't be disappointed

First time here and absolutely loved everything. They have so many sandwiches and wraps to choose from. The highlight of my meal was the soup -- the chicken barley was so good I ordered some to go for later on. Their dessert selection is over the top as well. I ordered an oatmeal/caramel/chocolate bar concoction and it was one of the best things I've ever heard. My boyfriend enjoyed his choc cake as well.

The only reason I can't give it 5 stars was because of the service. Everyone was super friendly but took forever to fill simple requests/needs. We were one of only two tables in the quaint space and it took forever for our server to come check on us. I could see she was just chatting with a co-worker.. we weren't in any rush and really enjoyed our meal / atmosphere so again it wasn't a problem but definitely noteworthy. We could hear the table beside us complaining about it as well. 

Check out their menu! Will def be back to try something else!!!

Visited La Vallesana during an exploratory outing of Cherokee Street.  The majority of the building had just been renovated but they were still working on another room.  The best part about the recently finished construction were the restrooms.  I have never experienced such nice restrooms at a Mexican restaurant.  My mom used to always say you could accurately judge a restaurant by their restrooms.  
La Vallasana does not sell alcohol so those expecting a giant margarita may be disappointed.  However, we were satisfied with the large glass bottles of Mexican coke made with real sugar instead of corn syrup.  
We opted not to start with guacamole which I soon regretted.  La Vallesana does not provide bottomless free baskets of chips so we were left with nothing to snack on while we waited for our food.  When I later tried a dollop of guac served with my meal it was the best I have ever tasted. 
We order chicken enchiladas and fajitas.  The enchiladas came with four covered in a green chili sauce and melted cheese.  The sauce had a kick to it but was deliciously tangy.   The fajita chicken was great quality and a generous portion.  The chicken was sauteed with various peppers and red rice.  We were only given three fajita shells which was not enough for all the filling.  We ended up taking some of each meal home rather than stuffing ourselves there.  
This was definitely the freshest and highest quality Mexican food I had ever had with no mystery meats and murky brown sauces.  However, I don't know if this is worth sacrificing free chips and alcohol.

This was the greasiest food I've ever had! I was literally mopping the grease off with my napkin. The salsa was so hot it was inedible, and they only have one, no medium or mild available. The guacamole was so watered down you can barely tell there was avocados in it. Also, they don't even have chips! What taco place doesn't have chips??? Bottom line, this place is horrible!

We had been wanting to try this coffee shop for some time and finally had the chance this morning.  I have to say it could not have been more disappointing. We ordered 2 lattes and a breakfast sandwich. Not super complicated in my opinion but not one thing was done correctly. We asked for a plain bagel for the sandwich, we were given an everything bagel. I ordered a butterscotch decaf latte and my wife ordered a grande latte which were completely undrinkable.  We paid for our order in cash (bills and coins) and the girl who was checking us out acting like she had never counted money before in her life.  When they somehow made the latte a skinny latte(the butterscotch was supposed to be skinny), and were corrected, she literally just added more milk and espresso to the same cup instead of making a fresh cup!  Place was empty on a Sunday morning when the cafe across the street was filled. We were hoping for a unique coffee shop, and I would really love to support local business but...looks like we will be sticking to Starbucks for now - they seem to have more quality control than this place.

The Worker Bee never fails to delight. The service is impeccable and the food is truly made with tlc.

We have been coming to this place for over two years on our visits to Carpinteria and look forward to our breakfast at the Worker Bee every time!

The restaurant has a beautiful atmosphere--that's about it.  The food left a lot to be desired.  

I've been there twice and Cuba Libre left me disenchanted.  The drinks are weak, the food is blah (kinda fatty, heavy, and over-salted).  I've had the pumpkin ravioli--they were ok, and the levantamuerto, or "wake the dead," soup (it wasn't levanta anything-- a thin little broth with a dash of coconut milk).  Traditionally, these soups are full of veggies and resemble a more soupy goulash or a stew with latin american vegs, like yuca. My friends had some pork dish and the cuban sandwich. The pork dish was really salty and the cuban sandwich was difficult to chew... the food wasn't worth the cash paid.  

Also, the bathroom was gross (there were waste papers on the floor and the sink wasn't draining the water)...

First time here. As soon as you walk in you are greeted and they seat you immediately, if seats are readily available. We didn't have to wait. Perfect. The hookahs are reasonably priced and they are good! I had the white gummy bear with mint and it was everything. They don't serve alcohol :( but I had a chai tea which paired nicely with my hookah. DJ played hiphop with a mixture of house, but mostly hip hop which I enjoyed. I'll def come again when I'm visiting Tampa.

I venture in Harry and David every time I'm at the outlets. I love the "foodie" type gifty things. There are many unusual things to choose, but I tend to window shop.  On my last visit there was an array of every kind of Moose Munch you can imagine, so I enjoyed the samples! That stuff is dangerously delicious!  Also they were sampling the Red Velvet coffee. It was ok. 

What we were blown away by though was the smell of the Banana Cream coffee in the bag. I felt if it tasted 1/5 as good as the smell I would be in heaven.  It was steeply priced at 13.99. They were running a special, 2 bags of whole bean coffee for 22$. We caved, bought that and the Toasted Coconut Vanilla. The coffees did not disappoint. The banana is the most scrumptious flavor I've ever tried and I've tried them all. I am a coconut fiend and while I liked the coconut, the Banana Cream was theeee star!

The staff was very kind and friendly. They told us they offer samples of everything in the store- no matter what! We were chatting with the staff and they were so personable & very enthusiastic of Harry & David!

Starbucks ain't got nuthin on Harry & David's incredible coffee creations

David and I discovered this place, around the corner from our house, just a month ago and it's become "our" restaurant.  The food is delicious, the service attentive, and the garlic knots (only place I know in Tucson that serves them.) are plentiful and tasty.

We like their pasta dishes best and don't think you can go wrong ordering any one of them.

The lunch deal, $5 for a huge slice of pizza that seems to equal half a pie anywhere else plus drink, is hard to beat both in price and quality.

The only problem you may encounter is that the place is sometimes crowded--even at 4:30 in the afternoon!  Seems David and I aren't the only ones who've discovered Dominick's.   But if you do encounter a short wait,  don't let that stop you.  I promise you the food will be worth it!

This place is good, I gave it a 4 star cause I know this place can be better. I had a hurricane for 5 dollars and it was worth the 5 dollars! I also asked for a cup of gumbo, I did not expect it to be that small but it was good. If you're not much into spicy food then I suggest you ask for something else. It was very spicy but that's how I love my gumbo. I moved to Florida 2 years ago from Houston and trust me, gumbo to me is everything! It was a bit salty but it was something you could still enjoy. As my entree I had the boiled shrimp. This is why I gave it a 4 star, I know the  flavor to it can be better knowing they can actually season their gumbo that way. What I enjoyed about that entree was the corn. I had gotten my braces removed and I wanted to celebrate it eating corn!!  lol if I'm in westchase i will definitely stop there again. A must try!!! Ohh, the device was great!! 

4/16/18 (deserves a 5 star)
I WAS ON THAT SIDE OF TOWN AND STOPPED BY. DON'T THINK TWICE, TRY THIS PLACE OUT. YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT. HAD TO GET SOME MORE GUMBO AND I HAD THEIR BOILED SHRIMP WHICH I LOVED. THIS TIME I TRIED THEIR VOODOO DRINK. ILL BE ON THAT SIDE NEXT MONTH AND WILL DEFINITELY STOP THERE AGAIN!

I was so excited to walk up to Parc, have a seat outside - a meal and a nice drink.  However - when they brought my water (no ice?)  It's warm out, who wants water with (no ice?).  

My iced tea had 2 cubes (2 more than the water).  I had the omlette - it was fair, a bit too much cheese for me, but overall good.  My husband had the shrimp and pasta and said it was good.  We sat on the Locust Street side which was not as nice as the 18th Street side.

Overall I would go back, but probably just for drinks (and I would ask for ice this time).
Fantastic food at Luke. Strong, custom cocktails too. Spaetzel, beet salad, shrimp and grits.

Been here twice for drinks but this time we decided to try the food. There were 7 of us and we ordered 2 of the meat combo platters to share. Plus an order of fries as an appetizer (very garlicky). We did bring a little bit of the meat home.  The platters included 2 sides each which were decent sized. Meats included a couple of ribs, quarter chicken, pulled pork, brisket and a piece of sausage for $40. You can get just the meat with no sides for $35.  Our favorite was the brisket.  Sides we ordered included Mac and cheese (decent), vegetables(zucchini and tomatoes-just ok), 5 mini corn bread muffins, baked beans(good).  They sometimes have a band in the events space adjacent to the restaurant/bar, but tonight they just had music over the speakers and they were really fun tunes. We all even commented on that!  Great use of an old building too. They just announced a new chef so the menu may be changing a bit. Will be back.

No bueno.  Three of us decided to give this little place a whirl after a relaxing beach day.  I decided to go with just simple tacos, which were gringo style(lettuce, tomato, and cheese), something I normally don't do unless I am hitting taco bell up but I went for it.  They were dry and flavorless.  The chicken was just terrible.  I've had more moist beef jerky, and it was big chunks making eating the tacos very awkward, which I wouldn't care if they tasted good.  The beef tacos weren't even as good as previously mentioned taco bell's, and we all know that they are more fast service/ cheap food than any Mexican joint would bill itself as.  The black beans were ok, again lacking any real flavor, and the rice at least wasn't bad.

The only good thing there was the salsa, which was admittedly very good, saving them from a dreaded one star.  The service was about as bad as it can get too, there were two tables(including is walking in) and it still took over 5 minutes to get a drink order taken, and longer for chips and salsa.  I am normally willing to give places a second try, but there really were no saving graces to get me to want to go back.

This was my third time dining here for lunch. The food is spectacular -- I've loved everything I've ever tasted! I highly recommend the edamame dumplings. Their sushi meets expectations, as do the desserts. Some of their soups are seasonal, but when they offer the mushroom soup, that's another gem worth trying. Yum!

Love the high ceilings, rich decor, and overall atmosphere -- including the music. It is pricey, but not pretentious. Large variety of beverages. Ample free parking. 

I did not love the hostess, who lacked warmth or personality...but maybe she was just having an "off" day. Overall, the service was good. Our waiter didn't give us a hard time when we requested substitutions, our water glasses stayed full, and everyone's dishes were brought out promptly and together.

Wonderful dining experience! I would absolutely return if given the opportunity.
I really enjoyed this place, the food and staff were great! Please-U Restaurant is my go-to spot when I'm in New Orleans!

I really wanted to like this place, the staff are friendly but the food wasn't very good.  Tzatziki appetizer tasted sour. The lamb and chicken on the salads were dry.  Canned  black olives no kalamatas.
Coming from a FOODIE, I will say save your money and go somewhere else.  The food is good, the service is PISS POOR.  Long wait times and low quality staff for price point of food.

I was alone so I decided to eat at the bar. Lucky for me I sat next to a local couple who worked around the corner at another restaurant and eat there once a week religiously and insisted I order their suggestions. They said that while they're entrees are wonderful, 3 particular appetizers were AMAZING and were NOT TO BE MISSED EVER! Soooo glad I took their advice!!! All I can say is I thought I was in FOOD HEAVEN!!! I must have been a very good girl! Lol! If nothing else, EAT THESE! Thank me later! :)

I started with the Tuna Tartare, (Tuna, mango avocado, wasabi)...DEELICIOUS!!!

Followed by the Tempura Fin Wings with the crispy noodle salad and Korean glaze! YUMMY!!

And finished with the Crispy Pork Belly with compressed watermelon!!! MOUTHWATERING!! 

Lauren & Ryan THANK YOU! For making this girls tastebuds dance with happiness!

The only sushi I tried in Florida! Per another Yelper's rec, I made sure to add Samurai Blue to the rotation. It's in an awesome, historical shopping strip called Centro Ybor. Some pluses: 

1. Fish was very fresh
2. Pressed sushi was amazing
3. Relatively inexpensive for 3 people (we ordered a total of 7 rolls)

Some questionable things: 
1. I think the space was being renovated, but bar seating experiences a leaky ceiling. The entire time we were eating, we were getting showered on. 
2. There was no regulation for folks who sat themselves at the bar instead of waiting for the hostess...so even though our party got to the restaurant first, this couple who came in after us sat themselves, got all their food first, and left before us...
3. Service was partially friendly

Regardless, the food was still pretty good. It gets pretty busy during dinner time if you don't make a reservation!

Goodfellas is a chain, but it's the only place to get a classic New York slice in Indianapolis that I'm aware, so therefore, it makes this place the best! And not just by default, it is very good. The quality of the cheese they use is palatable, and you can see them hand tossing the huge crusts when you enter. 
The entrance is narrow, and you can choose by-the-slice from what's available in the warmer or wait it out for a whole pizza. The slices are about $3-4 for one, but it covers the span of two paper plates so it's worth it to me! The salads are lackluster, so I would skip them. 
There's a cool lounge bar semi-hidden in the back that has couches and bar seats for seating. The bar has a nice vibe but is overpriced in my opinion. In addition to the lounge seating and few tables indoors, there's also some outdoor seating for the warmer days. Overall, the place is generally close to full in my experience, so sometimes finding seats for your crowd is kinda difficult - as a heads up. 
This place is open super late too, so if you're out bar hopping or late from a concert at the Old National Center, this is a perfectly viable option to hit up.

LOVE this place. It gets very busy at lunch so prepare yourself if you have to get back to work in a timely manner. I eat here weekly and have come to know the staff. They are always accommodating to dietary preferences and if a mistake is made, they go above and beyond to correct it! I am eating low carb currently and there are many options. I like that I can get spaghetti squash as a base instead of rice or noodles. Everything is always tasty and I look forward to my weekly healthy lunch here! Highly recommend this restaurant for everyone!

mice and fruit flies!!!!
Sad. We have been to 5th and Taylor so many times. Tonight w sat in the back room. Great jazz band. Initially we were excited but soon after sitting down we're Inundated with fruit flies. Soon thereafter so a mouse running around. We notified multiple wait staff. They were disturbed and apologetic but very hard to enjoy a meal with a mouse running around behind us!! Manager notified but offered a gift card- so sorry don't want
To come back and watch the mouse and flies at play
They refuse to wear masks while preparing food and only put masks on if Customers walk in.

Went here for the first time w my friends upon arrival in NOLA. We all ate something different and everything was tasty. Service was excellent. Our host and waitress were both so nice and gave us great recommendations for our visit to the city. Took away one star because a friend of mine got grilled shrimp with her salad but it still had a raw fish taste to it. Otherwise everything was great. Pics are of the French toast bites and the egg Benedict trio

One of the best byo restaurants in the Philadelphia area. My wife and I have been here 5 times and every time the food and service were both exceptional. Well done to the team that runs this restaurant, not easy to consistently put out an exceptional product. We've tried almost everything on the menu, and it has all been solid. Highly recommend
Great crowd.  Chill.  Open all night which is a big plus.  Great beer selection but I only drink Abita anyways.  Spent many nights until the sun came up at this bar.

I think with the recent construction on Waldron (for the past 2 years) it made this place harder to get to, and so their business has suffered. At least it feels like that, as most of the staff didn't seem to want to be there.  Food was typical of an Arby's, and unless you have a coupon, it can get pretty pricey (that goes for any Arby's).

I tried the beignets at Cafe Beignet and Cafe Du Monde on the same day. The beignets at Cafe Beignet are crispier and lighter. The beignets at Cafe Du Monde are chewier. Hands down, I liked the beignets at Cafe Beignet better.

Really enjoy coming here to get my Bbq smokiness on. I love the nachos. They are a fav of mine. Perfect split for two people. The best deal is the meal for 4. It's a great price and loaded with lots of food. My favorite is the beef brisket and pulled pork with the chipotle sauce. It's delicious and I keep coming back for more!!
Average food and average service on a non busy Monday morning. We won't be back, very disappointed.

I love this place. The service has always been pretty good and the food always spot on. They have a decent happy hour from 3:30-7:30...wines, beer, sake bombs, select cocktails and spirits. I always get the plum flavored sangria. Wowza! 
My friends and I enjoy coming here quite a bit. They have a gentleman that plays live music on Friday and Saturday night. The sushi rolls are a little on the pricey side, but well worth it and the sushi has always been fresh. Plus, you get a lot of bang for your buck. 
You can make reservations through open table which is convenient. 
Great place for happy hour, groups, families with kids, and even dates:)

This is a casual, low-key pub and restaurant that has good affordable food and is gay-friendly.
Our server was kind and attentive and checked up on us multiple times. We used a yelp coupon for a free "jethro" a rum-based cocktail and ordered the mac and cheese and burger to share. The mac and cheese is a smoked Mac and cheese and is creamy with a pretty smokey flavour. It could have been a meal on its own based on the size! The pit burger was delicious and the fried egg cooked perfectly. It also had a delicious garlic flavour to it. Honestly, I'd come back here just for the burger!

You will spend the best years of your underaged life here, find solace in its strict adherence to the rules of head down drinking: long, dark and narrow. Dig into a 23oz lager for 3 and change, admire the way the waitress moves between tables, conversationally, think for a moment that you might marry her, remember that it's Tuesday and there's probably a few pretty girls at Fox & Hound for pint night--but karaoke's over, so why bother--and turn to a friend to make a point on Chase Utley's on-base percentage, stab your finger on the table to prove you're serious, and spill a bit out of your glass by accident.
Great menu! Pizza is terrific.  Wonderful bar staff!  Nice selection of craft beer.  Live music, what else could you want???

Yes, this is a big giant tourist place but I will tell you it is hands down the freshest seafood in New Orleans. All the seafood platters are amazing . Its nice to sit at the oyster bar sometimes too 

go for seafood, you wont be upset

Zemam's and Zemam's too are basically the same thing, for anyone trying to decide.

Food: consistent and always very good. If you're not used to ethnic foods, this is a good place to start! Always order one less thing than you think you'll need.

Atmosphere: the one on speedway seems almost always empty. Both locations seem to be houses converted into restaurants. Servers are very friendly and helpful in the ordering, but service itself is VERY slow. But I think that's part of the charm :) 

Great for long, lazy dinners with a group of friends. Also, very cheap for an authentic ethiopian meal. One of my favorites in Tucson!

Their hush puppies are to die for. So good! As a whole, the restaurant is on the upper end of affordable. However, you eat what you pay for. The shrimp was freshly caught and tasted perfect. I had scallops that were so tender and flavorful. It can be hard to find a perfectly cooked scallop but Rusty Bellies did it. The grouper was pretty good as well. The only thing I didn't much care for was the rice and the dill sauce. The rice had no flavor and just seemed kind of like that boring lettuce you get under an appetizer - presentation was nice but not fun to eat. The dill sauce would have been good if it didn't feel so oily. But that could just be my preference. We will be returning for sure. Gotta get more of that shrimp!

Located on the 3rd floor of the Hyatt regency. At first glance the menu seems weird because it has sushi listed and the bar food but it kinda works well for the all types of taste buds you get
Coming in and out of a hotel. The chargrilled oysters here were way better than expected. I really got aquatinted with this place when I was here for a week for work.

I've only tried the soup a couple of times, but always lacks flavor!  The bagels are decent, but always seem to mess up the order.  They are willing to fix anything that is messed up though.  Staff is friendly enough.

So...wow!   Started with Lemon Ricotta.  Citrusy and creamy on grainy bread.  Excellent.  Lasagna different from any other with Citrus Cream and Veal Ragout.  Then Chicken Marsala never before seen.  Side carrots and beets  perfectly done.  Dessert Apple Slab and Ice Cream Sandwich were fresh and homemade.  Perfect wine pairing with Pinot Grigio    As for the staff, the friendliest and most helpful I've come across.  Kudos to Tim and Jacob.
The jambalaya was terrific. The service very good and friendly. The bread pudding was out of this world.

It's the only other German place in Indy. Compared to the Rathskeller, this place is much simpler, cheaper, but yet lacks that certain something.

The restaurant is located in the basement of the German-American Club, in German Park. Driving down the divided, big road that is Meridian Street south of 465, it's easy to not notice the simple sign proclaiming the club's existence in front of cast iron gates and a plethera of trees. Once located, you have to drive about a quarter mile back past playgrounds, tennis courts, and other park amenities.

Once inside, we were greeted by a half a room full of retired folk playing cards. Definately a welcoming, homey environment. They try to decorate in German nick-nacks, but it seems to be a losing battle in general, excpet for the giant mural hanging over the stairs upon entrance.

Freshly baked pretzels make for a good appetizer. A giant bowl of cheese sauce was wasted on us, since the spicy mustard served was much better than the imitation cheese. 

My friend's reuban was obviously made in house, including the corned beef. The meat was thickly sliced and extremely tough to cut, or take a clean bite of. But it was tasty.

The potato pancakes I had weren't great. They were served with apple sauce, probably to hide their lack of flavor. The German potato salad was unimpressive, the saurkraut was decent, but nothing to write home about. My wienerschnitzel, like most of the German dishes, was the most expensive thing on the menu, but it was good.

Good, but not great. I'd much rather spend the extra 10 bucks at the Rathskellar for the atmosphere and better (in my opinion) food.

Absolutely love the dinners here so decided to try them for catering and was so glad I did. The food was ready when promised, fresh and delicious.  I was provided with extra sauce for the pasta I had ordered but my guests didn't even need extra sauce. So bonus!- now I have some of their magnificent marinara in my freezer :) The garlic knots were a huge hit--try them if you have the chance!

Fantastic Food and line moves quick.  
I had the Currito, Paneer Tikka Masala with avocado, it was so much better than expected, so much bigger than expected, came out faster than expected.  It was so much food and tasted so good I didn't mind it was vegetarian. My friend had the bollywood bowl. Came here on for the Saturday market in St Pete, they were pretty busy, had a line but it seems you barely have to wait, the foods gets ready within a few minutes.

Tried the everything and sesame bagels and both were delicious! We definitely plan on going back. We also tried the matzah ball soup and loved it! Cannot wait to go back and try some more bagels and soup.

Brought my kiddos and their friends here on a Monday afternoon to play after they brought home some good report cards. When we first walked in, the smell of litter box was STRONG.

We were greeted and checked in promptly and given a rundown of the rules. The staff was very nice and accommodating. The kiddos started to play, but unfortunately we came hungry. The only options for food were some chips, muffins and moon pies. I wished there was something a little more substantial. We ended up going to McDonalds for Happy Meals afterward.

Many of the cats here don't like being held. And a few of the cats are downright mean...one of them was scratching pretty aggressively anytime someone approached him. I get that the primary purpose of this cafe is to get these animals adopted, but keeping mean cats seems like a poor business model. Maybe keep those in a different area or something?

Overall, I'm glad we came here to check it out, but the kids were ready to leave before our hour was up.
Delicious food and really wonderful owner. Everything was delicious and they are even adding a vegan sausage option! Try the Apple knodle!

When this restaurant first opened, I looked at the menu but thought maybe one day I would try the unique sides.  Recently, I came across a $5 off any burger coupon.  Oh, how I love to use a worthy coupon!  So I ordered the $9 The Wannabe Goat burger (mix of chuck and short rib meat) with upgraded sweet potato fries with caramel sauce (added $1).  The food came out with an enticing aroma.  Maria, the a.m. bartender, was very attentive and asked me how my food looked.  I was more interested in the smell but the food looked delicious.  Most importantly, my food was prepared as I customized my order.  The food was just the right portion especially the fries with the sauce.  

I greatly enjoyed my visit at Prodigy.  They have excellent service and food.  It was refreshing after my previous night experience at McAlister's Deli, on the other side of US 37, where the servers defensively kept denying with false assumptions and quoting food measurements (but almost half my food order was very noticeable missing to me) and did not completely correct my customized order.

Although the menu prices at Prodigy seem above my desire, it may be due to the better quality than I am usually ordering.  I will return to try the duck frites (as I have more coupons).

*le sigh* It actually pains me to write this review, I used to LOVE this place, it was once the go to hangout for my brother and I, we even made some great friends here. Oh how the once great has fallen. The whole vibe of the place was "We don't want you here"

Walking in and being "greeted" should've been a clear message. I didn't listen to that voice that said Just turn around and walk away now, you'd think I'd learn to listen to it by now. I stood there being ignored by the people who were talking about take out and who the new guy in the kitchen is hooking up with......I think he's hooking up with Michelle if you're interested (I was not) after about three minutes, which is an eternity when you're hungry. 

My waitress Alex was attentive enough but came across very corporate, it could be the fact that the place was so overstaffed for the night. At any given time there were three of four girls standing around and they all looked MISERABLE. Energy is palpable, and unhappy workers lead to unhappy guests. Also one of the managers was doing this weird thing where he was doing laps around the place. I'm pretty sure he was trying to hatch pokemon eggs because he never addressed any of the guests. At one point a woman from another table looks at me and mouths is he ok? I shrugged back because I didn't know. I've seen attentive managers that are engaged with their guests but this really did come across as kinda creepy. And now for the food.....

My appetizers and drink came out fine (so long Huckleberry lemonade you will be missed). Now I'm used to the Tuesday specials is was fun, so when I ordered six wings and was told I could only get them in multiples of 5, it wasn't the end of the world but it took some of the fun away and all but guaranteed that I wouldn't experiment with any new sauces because I didn;t want to get stuck with 5 if I didn't like them, so far it was only champagne problems and little nuisances but it DID feel like they were all adding up. Then my wing order came out and I became a mom (you read that right, no typo). My asian zing were great but my go to wing, the parm garlic, came out barely dressed. Seriously, I felt like walking back in the kitchen, holding my wings, and saying "Now you knew this wasn't right when you sent it out." I'm super annoyed now but let's try to handle this the right way I thought and asked my waitress for some extra Parm garlic sauce, then I found out why they came out that way as it took 15 minutes before I got the sauce to put on my now cold wings, apparently they'd run out and had to make more. I finished my (cold) wings and got my bill just to get out the door, I even skipped dessert which I usually like but since they'd messed up everything from my seating to my fav wings, I was just ready to leave bad enough alone. 

I'm not the kind of person that gets a manager and demands things be stricken from my bill, I just pay and choose to never set foot in the place again, and that's the case here. Oh and new kitchen guy, if you ARE having sex with the waitress by the dumpsters close to the bus stop, everyone in the place is talking about it!

A great place if you're looking for a fancy asian restaurant.
I say asian not fushion because they only have a few fushion dish.
Others are thai, malaysian, and sushi; therefore, it's more to international I would say.
I love pad thai and always try one everytime I see on the menu. This is one of the places I would get pad thai. P.S. ask for Chef Lee to make it.  
Some of the rolls are expensive but the size are double than the regular roll.  If you don't like raw and want a fancy roll, get their Lobster Cha Cha or Happy Friday.  Their good and huge, can't eat it all in one bite.  It wasn't the original chef that made the roll so some of the sauce are missing, but it still acceptable.
Come for lunch they have a great price for sushi rolls (hoso maki) that is served with soup or salad.  Their lunch special is also good.  As for fushion, I would not recommend.

I was really excited to try this place after a friend said they have good margaritas. The margaritas were just ok in my opinion. The salsa was pretty tasty and definitely my favorite part of the meal. I got the fish tacos and after going home and puking 4 times, I really regretted that decision!
Stopped in on a whim fabulous, outstanding will definitely be returning great drinks awesome menu and friendly staff Like bed It!!!!!

Oh my heavens. This place is.. Ok.. I mean it's ok if you are already drunk and don't care about your time. We were very sober upon walking in and even more sober when we left. The service was very kind, but wow was it slow. It was like they cared more about smiling at you than they cared about actually serving you.. Which is a bummer, because part of why you go to a place with a bourbon street view is to drink and watch the crowd. Nope. Just watch that crowd, but your drink will be empty for some time. They are probably busy off folding napkins and ignoring your requests (happened). 

Your food will be underwhelming (happened) as you peer down over the balcony to watch tarot readers get scared away when the state patrol shows up (happened). But you do you, ok? Food is as average as they come (if you're willing to wait that long for your food to come). I recommend something else if you're in a rush, this place is good if you're drunk and want to waste some time before you go somewhere else for better/faster food. In the meantime, they make a decent Hurricane...

I went to Butcher & Bee for a drink and appetizer with my friend, and this place was great. The bartender was able to make us 2 drinks off the menu and they were outstanding! I also had the Thai Brussels and they were delicious!! We sat at the bar, but there is a nice outdoor patio space here too. I am definitely excited to go back and try more food here.

Stopped by to pick up lunch; great service, efficient, friendly & polite staff and the food was just right. Usually, I'm worried about the fries -please see my review of McD in Silver City, NM- but these were great! ;)

All in all, my visit was smooth, hassle- free and I got fed.

Thanks! :)

So. Dang. Yummy. They're wonderful every time I go. They're quick and friendly. 
I get the Honey Chicken and Orange Chicken. 
So delicious every single time. Good portions too.

Yup, this ramen is good. Soup is killer. Noodle has great texture and chew. Soup options are varied, but not ridiculous.  

Pork or chicken based soup, variations from there.  Pork based is creamy, nap inducing luxury. 
Chicken based is clear, pure, not heavy. Biking afterward? maybe.  

Accouterments like the black mushrooms, bok choy, bean sprouts, crispy renkon make sense. They looks good, taste good. 

Complaints?  Its lined-up early! Come with a friend, not a group. And the gyoza... I don't know.  Its focused on the wrapper, not the filling.  Can't endorse it. The math doesn't work.

Fun place, delicious ramen, lineups. Reminds me of a country I know...

Went to Eddie Merlots on 96th street for my Birthday last night and it was the first time we had eaten there and wasn't impressed with the food or atmosphere. The food was mediocre and the chairs were stained and uncomfortable. Customer service was pretty good but could have been better. We heard some employees complaining and seen them roll their eyes about a party coming in that wanted tables pushed together in the sunroom area, pretty unprofessional.

Food was mediocre at best. Biscuits and gravy tasted like they dumped an entire bag of pepper in it...inedible. Pancake tasted old and rubbery. Hash browns...eh...eggs...eh...nothing special. Giving 2 stars based only on their prices (you get what you pay for I guess) and the friendliness of their staff.

I just wanted to get the word out to yelpers that this location is NOT closed!  It has re-opened for business after a long remodel and still has the best margarita in St. Louis.

I have never had a disappointing meal here.  Try the brisket, it's unbelievable.

I would eat here every day if I could. I live my life by the motto "treat every day like it's taco Tuesday" and this is my favorite spot. The tacos are amazing. Agua frescas are amazing too. The soups are fantastic. The corn is awesome. I actually should leave a horrible review so the line will be shorter but it's just too good to do something like that!!

The B-Line is consistent -- not outstanding but not terrible. Time for a pros and cons list!

The pros: the ambiance is nice, intimate, quiet, and classy, lending itself to good conversation. The crowd is more upscale and older than the rest of 4th Avenue. The food is good -- I've had the steak salad with avocado dressing (my favorite, healthy yet filling), the quesadilla, the fish tacos, all without complaints.

The cons: the menu is rather limited, especially the wine and beer list. Last time I was here, I only saw two wine options, a red and a white. The wait-in-line style of order and pay can create long backups. The food and drinks are also too expensive, especially for the European-bistro-sized portions. A cup of soup for $4.50 better be like liquid heaven, and it's not -- it's just soup.

There's talk about the desserts here but I don't have a sweet tooth myself so I can't speak for them. They look good in their little rotating case, though.

In all, not too bad. A better happy hour, better wine selection, or something more to distinguish itself would bring me back to the B Line for sure.

Our first time here. I've been wanting to stop in and try it as soon as I read they had opened.

We were greeted with a warm welcome and seated quickly. The menu is unique and interesting but also chart and easy to understand even with dishes that may be new to some.
We ordered the chicken fried rice to share so we could taste it along with it dishes. Really good rice with a unique and tasty twist, a little bit of pickled mustard greens on top. Stirred it in and it added a little acid to some bites that worked well. The chicken in the fried rice is pulled chicken which felt a little more upscale than what you get elsewhere. Great flavor too.

For my meal I got Khao Poon, a red curry and coconut milk broth with noodles, ground pork and some other veggies. Really good. They have two things I used to add some heat to my dishes.
1. Toasted chili oil with toasted garlic
2. Dried Thai pepper
Both added some really nice heat. I used the dried Thai cookies in the Khao Poon and the oil on the rice.
The Khao Poon flavor was robust and really great. Only request I would make is for more pork in it. I felt my bowl had a limited amount. But, great flavors and no other complaints.
My wife got the chicken red curry. Very similar flavors to the Khao Poon but thicker and with some additional veggies. Really good with the jasmine rice they served.
I how they do well, we'll be back soon.

Me n my daughter ate n had drinks in here been here several times but they renovated the inside nice and clean. I was here on a Wednesday evening not very crowded n we got our food quick it was hot n good drinks are a little pricey but most places are today

Thought we found a hidden gem here in Reno for Korean food. We love Bonchon and the first time we came here we were stoked on a place where I didn't have to actually cook my own food. First time we did the bbq and bonchon. And it was amazing so we were set. Today we left the lake and were craving just wings. So we came here and they was too much batter and the wings weren't drums and flats. It seems like the bits and pieces left over. A little disappointed the second time but still a great environment and service. Not going to give up on it because of the second trip.

In short, the food was very good but the drinks were a let down and the experience was a bit weird.

I brought two out-of-town guests here for a late afternoon drink and appetizer. Our waitress was very friendly and attentive, but did not seem very familiar with the drink menus. When we asked about their beer selection, she encouraged us to get up and go over to the bar to see what they had, rather than tell us (they did have a very extensive printed list of their wines).  When I asked about their Hot Buttered Coffee cocktail she said she had not tried them before and would have to ask the owners for information. She also wasn't sure about the happy hour special, and wrongly informed us that the drinks we ordered were eligible (which she explained after we received the bill).

The food menu is also very strange. They have have a full menu, but have drawn red lines under the items they are now serving (I'm not sure if the ones not underlined are upcoming or expired), and the back of the menu is an old menu they have scratched out. Our waitress said they had opened last June but were still "figuring out what to serve". Bizarre.

We ordered a meat and a cheese plate and both were very tasty and nicely presented. I also ordered what they called the "best hot buttered coffee in town" and my husband ordered a hot cider cocktail. For $10 each, I was shocked to see them both come out in styrofoam cups. My "coffee" did not seem to be made of coffee, had no trace of butter or alcohol and was syrupy sweet; it was very disappointing.

The decor is a bit eccentric, but nice, and the overall atmosphere is good except for the gigantic TV they have on the dining room wall. Luckily we were able to find the remote and turn off the sound, but the video was distracting and unpleasant.

I will give the caveat that we were here on New Years day, so I don't know if our service or menu was representative for an average day. I would go back for the food, but skip the drinks.

Being in Nashville for the first time, and with kids (8 and 12), this left us with a dilemma.  We wanted to experience the Nashville music scene, have some good food, and go to a lively yet appropriate venue for kids.

In doing research it became clear that Broadway was the place for this.  The avenue is full of restaurants and music and we happened upon the Wildhorse Salon after reading it was kid friendly.  

We could not have made a better choice.  This place is huge--three floors.  First floor are tables to eat at and some bars, plus the main stage and dance floor.  Floor two has a bar, some booths, viewing spots for the stage, and games such as pool and Foos Ball (all free to play).  The third floor we did not get to but it just looks like a vantage point to watch the stage.

We arrived to the place around 4:30.  We sat and ordered the fried chicken, piggy grilled cheese, and the kids Mac and cheese and kids burger.  We started with fried pickles and drinks as well.  I had read that the food here was at best average but we absolutely loved everything as it was all very tasty and filling.  

While waiting for the food there was free line dancing lessons (every 45 min or so) and the first band also came on.  The kids danced and then we ate and it was an absolute blast.

After dinner we grabbed a seat near the dance floor, had some more drinks and danced up a storm as the band played.  The kids even ordered a lemonade that came in a big plastic cowboy boot!

This is the perfect family place if you want good food, Nashville music, and a lively environment that truly satisfies both the kids and adults.  We stayed until about 8pm and it appeared that at that point the crowd was getting older.  I would think any time after 8 or 9 it would not be as kid friendly.

I have been to Pour House twice.  The first time was for Flicks and Food Trucks.  The second time was on a random Friday night for pre-dinner beers with the fiance'.

Flicks and Food Trucks:  This place is CLUTCH.  The fact that I can go in and promptly be served a beer or a glass of wine to walk around with is great.  For as crowded as it was the time I was here for Flicks and Food Trucks, the service was still good.

Random Friday night:  Really chill vibe.  We sat outside and enjoyed the nice weather.  It was refreshing to see so many regulars and dogs walking around.  Definitely a good spot to relax.

It looks as though you can order food from the restaurant across the court yard, Cena, and enjoy it at Pour House.  Definitely a spot I'll be back to.

What a disappointment.   They use to have the best calamari, but with a new chef they changed the style of cooking it and the sauce.  The menu said a lemon caper but it came with tarter sauce.   When we pointed this out to the waitress she claimed she told the manager and chef but didnt offer to replace the sauce or even apologize.  It was just awkward. And of coursd they charged us for it.    As a former restaurant owner I am surprised by the lack of customer service   And don't bother ordering the ceasar salad for $8.  It was half a salad plate....maybe 50 cents in product!  The Rap has been a great place for years, but not anymore.  You have to maintain quality to retain you reputation these days .

Yummm.

This place was very authentic and very affordable. I have gone here once so far, but will definitely see myself coming back way more often when I crave good pho and when I am in Philly next. So far I have only eaten the #1, and the soup is definitely flavorful, meats were good quality. 

The only down side about this place is that it is cash only, like most Asian places unfortunately. It's nice also that it has a parking lot in the plaza so parking is usually not too hard to find.

All in all, will definitely come back. Definitely worth the trip!

Excellent spring rolls - large, crispy and tasty!

Pho on the other hand is pretty standard in my opinion. 

Decor is unchanged and old since I can remember but you generally don't go for pho to admire the decor of most places. I don't mind the old decor gives it a bit of character.

Service is fast and efficient. Parking free outside in the parking lot.

You can ask for your bean sprouts to be steamed prior to arriving (that's how I prefer mine)

All in all a decent option for pho when you're craving some in the south side

Tens of visits and many menu items later, China Pasta House deserves an update. Their dumplings still deserve a strong endorsement. Yes, they all generally taste the same but, with the exception of the bland-loogie-textured leek and egg dumplings, the taste is a good one. The chicken and peanut sauce noodles are quite tasty, but the buns are perpetually disappointing. Oh, and never order the ice tea--it tastes like uncarbonated, Lipton-flavored soda.

The food is pretty decent much of the time with a few highlights and a few failures, but the service is terrible. On good days, it is a combination of brusque and apathetic, but they can usually get most of the leftover food off your table sometime after you sit down. On bad days (which aren't necessarily busy days), they are so incompetent and flustered that their movements have the aimless quality of fruit flies. The last time I was there we waited for almost ten minutes to order before walking out--we never could get the waitress to make eye contact and she seemed more interested in restocking the fridge than attending to any of the tables.

China Pasta House, you're okay, but not good enough to warrant another visit.

They make delicious food! I live right up the street from Franco's, and it's one of my go-to spots. They're incredibly kind too. I go all the time, and I haven't had anything less than an awesome experience! 

If you're looking for recommendations, definitely try the enchiladas!
Great quick Asian restaurant in Parx casino with great service. We'll definitely come back again when visiting Parx.

The size of the menu makes Fiesta unlike any of the other pizza places around. The wings are awesome... And so is the pizza, of course! Both service and delivery are quick and the staff is very friendly.
My family and I went there today and had a great experience ! The "coned pizza" was delicious and the staff was very friendly! We will be going back very soon!

Best. Tacos. Ever. And this is coming from someone who isn't super crazy about tacos in general. They got a vegetarian loving chorizo. And don't get me wrong, their veggie options are equally mind-blowing. Would recommend for a fun dinner with friends, since they have plenty of happy hour deals at the bar.  You better go!

I recently moved into the Irvington area and used to make special trips when I lived further awayfor to visit. Everytime I go, I pick something different and have never been let down. 

My last visit, I ordered the California crab sandwich. The server was knowledgeable and suggested I try it with hummus...great suggestion! When it arrived the kitchen accidentally forgot the crab but was realized by the manager on duty in a second. He retrieved the crab in less than a minute and the sandwich was fantastic. Quick problem solving and an awesome staff make this local place sustainable. If you live out of the way, I suggest going the distance to dine here. It's unique and original with a cool atmosphere. Don't pass up their black-board art by the host stand.

OH.  MY.  GOD.  If you want to try the best donuts in the world (at least in my eyes) you HAVE to go here!!!  Literally melt in your mouth.  As I type this review, my mouth is watering and now I want donuts.  I love this place.  My dad has been taking me here since I was old enough to eat donuts.  I love telling everybody about this place and hearing what they think.  And they all agree.  

My personal favorite is the glazed cinnamon twist.  YUUUUMMMMMYYYYY!!!!

THE BEST DONUTS EVER!!!!!

After leaving I felt like I just ate a salt lick. 

Needless to say...I was not happy. 

The beef was good but everything else was not...
We got the meat lovers for 2 along with a mushroom platter and spinach.

- The spinach was not edible and we didn't even touch it because it was basically green mush with white garlic paste that likened the texture of spit. 
- The mushroom was more soy sauce than mushroom. 
- The chicken pieces were so big that they were dry and burnt and we ended up having to cut the rest of the pieces ourselves. 

+ The rice was fantastic! I would just go here for some rice. 
+ All the beef was amazing, so tender and easy to grill. They also marinated it to perfection!

Dynamic place. Quirky joint yet knows it's niche. Reminds you of an old filling station and the staff is a hybrid of an independent record store worker crossed with a Whole Foods clerk. Punk music was blaring while the cast of chefs delivered amazing brunch lunch options. Sampled the cold Cafe de Olla. Dove into a sticky bun and chased it with sorghum bacon. For my encore I selected the ridiculous grilled cheese topped with a duck egg and maple syrup. I left in a coma. But straight up, we need more joints like this across the country. They don't take each other seriously but they deliver the goods with a flare matched by no other. Bravo.

This place is filthy!   Everything was sticky and fruit flies all over the place John Taffer would have a shit fit!  I cannot even imagine since it's underground the rodent situation!  The only reason why I'm giving two stars is it's CHEAP!
ALLERGY ALERT:  If you are allergic to hipsters, mom jeans on 22 year olds, long lines or overpriced food, I highly advise steering clear of Milktooth, and their Portlandia worthy brunch experience.
Nice restaurant at the main pub street. But it's pricey for  w $51. ramen was good first taste after that too salty. Sushi was so so. Fried squid was good, crunchy.

My husband and I were so impressed with Barclay Prime last month.  We went on a Friday night and made reservations for 5pm.  It wasn't busy at all when we arrived and we were seated immediately.  Everyone that we encountered was super friendly & kind. 

My husband got Filet and I ended up getting the roasted chicken, which was delicious!!  We got a side of asparagus that was plenty for both of us.  They were really accommodating with my dairy allergy.  The wait staff was extremely attentive and made it a great experience for us. If we ever are back in Philly this would be a must!

Absolutely the worst bbq I have ever had. I'm still trying to figure out how they can have our food out so fast and it be ice cold! The fries were hard, the potato salad and garlic bread were dry. Their sauce was pretty good and that's about all it had going for it...when I was asked how the food was I told him terrible, he said Whaaattt and walked away. Didn't ask why we felt that way or apologize.
Not a location you would expect a sushi restaurant! So glad my daughter turned me on to this place! Great sushi! Fresh, interesting choices and wonderful service.
This place is disgusting! Overpriced and the sushi looked old! The sushi was slimey and gooey. Threw it away

Once again best vegan mac and cheese ever! It's the only thing that hits the spot. Also the Ocean protein was very good give it a try. All the food is very good though, and they are very nice here. :D

First visit was lunch with a woman whose opinion I really value.  I noticed this place while it was being renovated, because they sure did put in a LOT of windows!  Little did I know I only knew the half of it...
A first glance at the menu online peaked my curiosity enough to suggest this for a Friday lunch date with said cool lady.

Lunch happened at high noon on an extremely cold winter day, but even so, I expected more of a crowd. " Hopefully it's the economy and not the quality of the food/service," I thought to myself.  We were greeted and seated quickly at an unsteady table upstairs.  It was no match for 6 sugar packets and the napkin that was already doing duty under the table leg.  Service staff was also attentive and pleasant.

The food was less than I expected because I was very impressed by the skylight and the decor, which I considered to be minimalist but cool.  I ordered the pulled porked BBQ sandwich, which admittedly has tough competition from what my brother in law makes at home, but it was a little dry and didn't have as robust a flavor as I might have hoped.  Cool lady friend ordered the cobb salad, which looked decent.  I was trying to be good and got a side salad, which wasn't remotely fresh or interesting.

I'd go there again to try some of their other food and for happy hour.  It is a nice open space and ADA accessible, so it possesses qualities I like in a happy hour bar.

Formerly a neighborhood grocery store, the restaurant is welcoming and cozy when you walk in.  Think of refined food in a very comfortable setting.  Service is attentive and helpful in offering advice, etc.  The food is absolutely outstanding.  Like others have commented. the blue crab beignets are an absolute must get.  Even if you don't like crab, get them.  If you don't like them, give me a shout and send them to me!  Yes, they are that good.  They are rich but paired with the malt vinegar aioli, they are perfect orbs of goodness.  The pickle jar (yes, a jar of pickled vegetables) also help cut through some of the richness.
You can't go wrong with any of the entrees either.  I thought for the quality of the food the price points were very fair.
Just a great dinner in a great setting.  What more could someone want?
My sushi is always fresh and its really clean. Everything is just delicious!!! I wish we had a place in my area with a hibachi style. Since the place on Quaker bridge road closed
Very rude bartenders and very rude staff. Literally refused to take my order despite my group of friends being well behaved

Immediately left once we were seated. The hostess/waitress didn't greet us, much less mile. She seemed disgusted that she had to serve us, And her bad attitude really rubbed us the wrong way. Very unprofessional.

We went here for my birthday which was on a Saturday. There was a typical wait of 45 min (normal at any brunch place) I got an omelette which was HUGE, but not as flavorful as I wanted it to be. My husband got the red velvet French toast which he thought was fried red velvet cake. There coffee was cold, and the restaurant was as clean. I don't think we'll go here again unless it's someone else's idea.

It's such a shame these days ! Super dirty inside and the food is no longer to "die" for. Whole situation is disappointing now. I would go weekly and the covid happened. Kept driving by and finally stopped. Wish I hadn't.

Plenty of seating for an airport restaurant. Servers were very attentive and the food came out quickly. The chili wasn't bad but I ordered a club that more closely resembled a regular turkey sandwich. I guess I was expecting a little too much

Had a great dinner with equally great service. Prices are very reasonable and portions are large. We started with the wonton soup and appetizer sampler for 2. The soup was very flavorful and the wontons were good. The sampler was much larger than we expected and more than enough for 4 of us to share. 
I had the green lantern roll which was huge and delicious. My husband had the best friends burrito and loved it, such a great deal as it was packed with fish and only cost $11. My son had the pineapple fried rice with chicken. Which he happily said was the best friend rice he'd ever had.

This is ridiculous. I drove OVER an HOUR to get my wife honey sesame chicken. At 4pm. They were OUT. It's insane how an establishment like this can be out of a certain food, especially when it is there special that only comes around once in awhile.  I need someone to call me 727-401-9900. Not acceptable.
Update: still no one of my knowledge has called me even though they said they would.

Well, it was another Covid night and I suddenly got a craving for Greek Lemon Avgolemono  soup (creamy lemon chicken soup with orzo). The absolute best around is from My Greek Corner, so I had my fingers crossed they were open.  Upon happily learning they were indeed open, I decided to load up on Greek food to last a few days: lamb kabob, a quart of the lemon soup, dolmades (stuffed grape leaves), tiropita (cheese phyllo pie), village salad and baklava. It has been a few days now and I have to say every time I've had a meal from my stash of Greek food I have been super happy. I grew up next door to Tarpon Springs when the original Greeks lived there and the local lore was that you never ask a Greek person for their recipe because they'll change it just enough that your results will never match the original. I miss truly homemade Greek food-- so much of it is now bought from a distributor. But My Greek Corner's Lemon Avgolemono tastes like it was made by YaYa herself. Chunks of chicken, creamy orzo, and just the right tang of lemon. The Village salad was mostly tomatoes, but they actually were ripe and delicious. I appreciated the small scoop of potato salad included with it (yes, I know that's not authentic). The slab of feta on top was pretty flavorless however. I would prefer a smaller slab of higher quality feta. The other big surprise was the baklava. I'm sure this is purchased from a bakery, but it's a good one.  I've had their tiropita before. In the restaurant, it is a stand out-- it manages to be crispy from the phyllo and creamy/tangy from the cheese all at once. Texturally, It didn't hold up so well with delivery, but taste wise is was still great. The dolmades are in the frig for a quick lunch during the week. So thank you My Greek Corner for delivering the delicious taste of comfort during COVID-19.

A little on the expensive side. Good food and atmosphere. Annoyed that it took forever to pay even though I was sitting at the bar and there were at least five other employees around but apparently only my assigned person can cash me out. Meanwhile she is busy with other tables.

Oh, dear.

After a promising start, I believe the restaurant now known as 43 Cricket, FKA Gillane's, may be losing their old customer base - the over 65 crowd.  

Took the Queen Mother and the Patriarch there for lunch today.  The dining room has been renovated, with the spaces formerly used to divide the bar and display the collection of creepy/charming clowns removed so now they're open 1/2 walls.  Also removed are the high backed booths which made the room seem a bit smaller but also acted like excellent sound buffers.

That means that without them, the room is much noisier.  Seniors don't like noisy rooms.  

The menu has been revised quite a bit, and mostly for the better.  One of us got the french onion soup and a grilled cheese sandwich, one got the house salad with grilled chicken, one got a burger with a wedge salad.   The biggest hit was the house salad, which was quite  yummy.  Grilled cheese was fine as was the soup. Wedge salad was just OK.  The burger was juicy but the bun fell apart and the tomato served with it was mush.  Ugh.   Portion sizes on everything were adequate, not ginormous, not 'small plates'.  

Service was fine, reasonably quick and very cheerful.  

Now, for the price.  $57, for three, for lunch, with no alcohol. I thought the Seniors were going to pass out.  On that alone, this place, which has been a mainstay of theirs for eons when it was Gilane's, is now officially Off Their List.  

I thought it was kinda pricey too for the food served.
Absolutely atrocious, but what did I honestly expect? The bacon was circular and soggy. I needn't say more. No one deserves respect when they disrespect bacon. Just don't.

I can't say I'm that big of a fan because the place is always too jam packed and not enough places to sit and eat in comfort without elbowing someone on accident. Other than that, the quality of food served at the various restaurants and other eateries is typically pretty good.

In short: I came to conclude that this place has an unrealistically high rating due to a steady supply of fake reviews.

The details: based on tonight's experience I say this is a tourist trap. Long story short, I ordered two steaks in a row.... First a dry aged New York strip listed at undisclosed price ("MP") and had to send this back for lack of any flavor.

Then I ordered the dry aged rib eye for another undisclosed entry of "MP" and it wasn't much better. I can get a regular ribeye from a supermarket and get better quality than in this place. That's two low quality steaks down and with steak having the most weight in a 'steak'house review I can only issue two stars. 

To be fair, the ad-on foie gras was to die for and I don't understand how they don't make that its own appetizer dish. 

Some places here on Yelp thrive on fake reviews no doubt and I called that out only once before in another review. Between Los Angeles and New York, this is the second fake I came across. And it won't even matter because this review will soon be buried. Yikes.

You gotta love it - This place screams upscale Northeast Philly. 

This place has certainly evolved since it first opened. I remember when it first opened, they were still working out the kinks and their menu selection was very limited. Since then, the restaurant has thrown up everything sports. 

They also expanded the place, and there is another bar in the back which is catered for the "night scene". It is an outside patio that is covered and smoking is allowed. It gets crazy smoky in here because everyone in Philly smokes. You will find a young Northeast crowd here. 

The drinks are good, the food is ehh. Standard sports bar fare - oily and good size portions.

My wife and had our order delivered and we really enjoyed it! I really like Thai and Laos food, and I'm pretty familiar with the flavors of this cuisine. 

The two menu items we had were Banh Mi and Tom Kha. Both of these entree selections were delicious, and I'd definitely order them again! 

The Banh Mi is a sandwich with grilled BBQ pork and vegetables on a baguette roll. The baguette roll was fresh and really complimented the sandwich. The crunchy vegetables were refreshing, crunchy, and tasty. Fresh cucumbers, pickled carrots, daikon, cilantro, and jalapeño are a perfect combination with the BBQ meat and baguette.

I ordered the Tom Kha soup, and it was my first time trying it. The first spoonful was so surprisingly flavorful, and the first flavor that gets your attention is the coconut milk base. This is blended with the lime leaf, chili, and galangal pastes, and with mushrooms, cilantro, scallion, onions, lime juice, and shrimp. The flavor profile is very complex and unique, and this is something I wish I'd discovered a long time ago.

I'm looking forward to enjoying a dine-in experience in the near future, and Thai Papaya will be at the top of our list for delivery as well!

This is my favorite place to go for (Americanized) Chinese lunch specials! 

For under $10, you get soup, salad, a wonton, an egg roll + an entree with a side of fried rice. My order of vegetarian orange chicken was super tasty and filling. 

Located by Zodo's, it's a small shop which somehow doesn't feel crowded despite its size. The service here is pretty quick and friendly. Great place for a decent lunch!

When I was here we caught our server as he was headed out the door and because of that, he sucked. I won't name names, because, well I like this place. 

They have great wings, thats undeniable, the draft selection is good and generally speaking they have a pretty good beer selection over all. They have a pretty cool atmosphere and the other servers are pretty decent. I had the pleaseure of working with Mary Kate at my restaurant and I have to say she is a great person to work with, and I mean to stop by Chatam sometime when she is working to see how she is at her tables...

Check this place out and grab some wings (just wings though, I haven't had much luck with other things on their menu).
Don't have the most popular menu item (bb wings) available.

Just a great restaurant. Nice ambiance. Owner greeted us at the door along with the greeter. He acted like he really appreciated us. There was a lot going on in the area and he thanked us for choosing his establishment.
Got there at 4 pm. By 5 the place was packed on a Friday.
Food was great. Menu is HUGE.  Maybe a little too big. Owner came by table 3 times to make sure our visit was up to standard. Super nice guy.
Staff was great. Lots of TVs. Full bar. And the most unusual thing I thought, but unique, was the fresh flowers at every table. Lilies I believe. Not sure.
Definitely going back
Brunch time is best. Make sure you sit outside for a gorgeous bay view and order the French Toast platter. TO DIE FOR!!!!!!

This is probably the worst bar I have been to in a while. The food is megerly portioned and overpriced. The service is terrible and the workers mess around. I got the fish tacos and they were oddly sweet, uncooked, and only came with two for a price of $7. The mozzarella sticks were also bland, and lacked of flavor along with its sauce. Would not recommend.

I have eaten at multiple First Watch locations and have always loved the food and coffee. I was excited when they opened one close to home. 
That being said, I was super disappointed in the service today. Every staff member was frazzled as they tried to keep up with a busy Sunday morning, starting with the hostess staff. We then sat at our table at least 10 minutes with no water/coffee and no acknowledgement. The 2 waitresses that ended up helping us were super kind, but it was obvious they must've been short staffed or didn't have much help. We were told that our food was running behind, so we didn't eat until about 45 minutes from being seated. (I'm thankful they at least communicated with us about the food running late.) The food also came out in increments, with half the table being served a solid 5 minutes before the other half. 

My farmhouse scramble was fabulous - the carmelized onions and peppers were cooked to perfection. The toast was perfectly toasted and the compote that came with it was yummy. The pancakes were also great - a large portion with a nice compote for dipping.

I wish I could say I will return soon, and if it was about the food alone, I absolutely would, but it was very clear that the service was significantly struggling, and they have lots of kinks to work out before it will be satisfiable for us. We have a toddler, and waiting 45 minutes is not what we would prefer to chance again anytime soon. The food prices are also more expensive ($11.95 for my farmhouse scramble, and $2.95 for coffee). I do hope they figure out their service issues and succeed at this location, but it will take some work!

Union Jacks used to be best deep dish Pizza in the city.... After Sunday's experience that can't be said anymore.  The bottom was burnt, given the fact it takes 40 mins to back we didn't have time for them to make us a new pie.  They reluctantly took the price of the pizza off the bill.   Not sure I will give them another chance.

Just went to Maple Glen Pizza. Almost $16 for a plain pizza with no toppings. Are you kidding me??? What a joke. Cash only??!  What a joke. Sorry, the pizzas not good enough to charge $16.  And definitely not worth it enough to go to the ATM/bank. I'm done with this place.

This ice cream shop opened in our neighborhood.  With Franklin Fountain nearby, we thought "uh oh, they'll never make it"...

Forget that thought, their ice cream is much better, and I shutter to say this, no 40 people lines (for now).  Once people find this gem, I am sure the lines will form down Church Street.   

Excellent taste, and great prices.

Make sure you make reservations for this place b/c it gets busy. There are two menus here - one for upstairs (finer dining) and downstairs is more casual. we ate downstairs.. We loved the seasoned popcorn that they start us off with on the table. It was very yummy. We got the pork fat tater tots as an app, and it was salty goodness. I got the fish tacos and it was really good. My friend got the burger and said it was ok. I would go with the tacos again..
Our waitress was very friendly. Also, we had a 45 minute wait, but they text you when they are ready for you which is great b/c we went next door to honky tonk for a drink while we waited since there was no room at the bar here

Cool vibe.  My table was sticky though.  Service slow but all restaurants are these days.  Lots of staff but many just standing around oblivious.  Food selections kind of limited. Its a beach bar mostly.  No beer selection at all.  No porters, no stouts no local craft beer.... gee whiz guys!!!  A couple weird things: Only cups of soup, no bowls.  Violation of my big pet peeve is those damn grind your own salt and pepper shakers that should be banned -- they dont work and I came to relax, not work out.  My bacon burger and side salad quite good . I did not have the fries cause I am allergic to shrimp and waiter advised fries cooked in same oil as shrimp---- yech... there should be a law on that. Fixable errors.  I was looking for cool water view restaurant.  This works but the view marginal.... but it ain't Hawaii :). Best wishes to owners to execute better.
I have been to a lot of Mexican restaurants and I can't believe the portion size. They really fill the fajitas plate with a lot of meet.

Very much enjoyed our experience here. This place has an awesome vibe and is very clean. My husband and I both ordered drinks, a burger, and chicken and waffles. We were not disappointed! Based on the food alone we will definitely be back.
