I was very impressed with the service. Our server Lauren was fantastic, along with the rest of the staff that we came in contact with. Everybody shared a friendly face and had kind words. You can tell they take service very seriously, which is a pleasure to experience. 

This is a fantastic establishment to bookmark and give a try!
Great service, great food, and great atmosphere!!! Great spot in Metairie to have a nice meal!
Langostina Quesadilla is a must. A bit of sweet and paired with the spicy salsa (ordered chips and salsa), it is perfect!

First time here. My phone does not really do that scan menu very well so they gave me paper menus one for drinks and happy hour and another one for food. In general the service is really good. The food is good as well but once I finally decided on a beer which came from a taste of two different beers it took forever to get there I was almost finished with my meal. I noticed that it was between the happy hour time and I noticed that you could get a second beer for $0.25. I asked her if the beer that I had was included in that and she said they weren't doing happy hour because of covid because they weren't making that much money. Wow. The menu said they were doing happy hour. She took the menu and she threw it in the trash. That was very strange to me I might have given them a 4-star or 5-star review had that not happened. If they're not making money then I think a happy hour would be even more important than normally.. I wouldn't even have ordered the extra beer for $0.25 for a second one except I had to wait for my sister to come and meet me. So while it was a good place it was kind of disappointing in the end because they should have handled the whole thing a lot better

Great Peruvian cuisine! Good food, great service. Will be back again to try some more food. Tried the calamari appetizer, chicken fried rice, Laquoma ice cream and Purple corn drink. Wonderful experience! Cozy little cute restaurant.

Stopped in for a quick lunch after an appointment.  I was feeling like a burger and they had a few options, of which I opted for the Bacon Burger and had them swap the swiss with bleu cheese (at no extra cost).  The burger seemed to be taking longer than it should for a medium rare burger, and before I could say anything the bartender told me they had overcooked it, and had already started another which would be out asap.

This is a pro move.  They didn't try to pawn it off on me and hope I wouldn't notice.  I gladly waited the extra few minutes and it came out perfect, just as I ordered it.  Their sweet potato fries are also really good.

One thing I did notice, was that it was absolutely freezing inside.  This should pan out when those lovely extra humid Indiana summer nights come back for good.

This was my first time eating at a Shake Shack, and I thought it was good. I had the SmokeShack burger. The cherry pepper relish was interesting, but I probably should've gone with the standard to start. Luckily, my wife got the original, so I at least had a sample. The biggest thing that struck me about the burger was the heavy char flavor. That could be a good thing or a bad thing for you, depending on how much you like eating charcoal briquettes. Personally, I'm a fan, so that part didn't bother me. I had the cheese fries, which was a poor choice. The fries themselves were ok. They couldn't overcome the cheese sauce though, which had a consistency somewhere between Nickelodeon's Gak and Crayola's Silly Putty. It tasted nearly the way cheese tastes. The chocolate shake was delicious. Also, puppies are cute. Nobody gets bonus points for making a tasty shake.

Overall, it's a solid burger and I'm glad I ate one. I think the biggest reason I won't be clambering go go back is the price. $30 for two people at a "fast food" joint... we might as well go to Whole Foods.

Great trendy restaurant. Reasonable pricing. The grilled cheese pop on a stick to dip into the tomato soup is delicious. Their burgers are very, very good here too. Can't go wrong with any choice. Lots of tables and full wall windows to look out into the streets. They let me put my bike inside behind the counter so it wouldn't get stolen, forgot my bike lock. It's kindness like that which makes it a 5star for me.

Ah Bar Louie. I love going here. They are a tad pricey, however, so I try to go on dollar burger night (Tuesday) or from 4-7 when drinks are a bit less. They have ladies night on Wednesday and their $10 martinis are only $5. I go for the location and atmosphere. Blue Martini next door is too frou frou for me and Too Jays close by is not a happening spot for hanging out and having a drink. Their tator tots are my fave thing to order at Bar Louie. Their DIVA martini is pretty tasty, too. If for some reason you haven't been yet, GO since you're missing out!

As a visitor to Tucson, I wanted to experience authentic Tucson Mexican food. The bland salsa served with the chips was the first disappointment. Next I was told that they have no horchata, a sure sign of the Americanized bland cheese food to follow. 

Then came the Chili Renjo, a tasteless green chili that was fried in six inches of batter, covered with a pound of cheese, served with a pile of chopped lettuce and some ok refried beans. 

My Nieces cheese enchilada was a pound of the same generic "Mexican" grocery store cheese with a couple of tortillas buried in the mess.

This bland cheesy excuse for Mexican food may just be authentic to Tucson, if this is true then please no more Tucson Mex. food for me!

El Minuto earned a second star because of the decent service and the pleasant atmosphere.

Laid back atmosphere...Good scotch...movies playing on the wall, silent with subtitles...Or live music. Lots of couches, dark lounge feel.

Worth checking out. We've been back a few times, though I wish the live music was not so loud. Its good, but we can't hear each other.

We had some time to kill before Costco opened so we decided to get some breakfast and chose The Nook based on the mostly positive Yelp reviews. 

The waitress was very friendly and attentive but the food wasn't so great. I had the "Hash Mountain" which consisted of hash that tasted like it was from a can and the center of one of the patties was still cold when I bit into it. The coffee was pretty weak and not very hot. My wife's breakfast sandwich was also just so-so.

The prices were reasonable but I don't think I'll be going back

Loved our server. Very laid back setting. I must say whoever has to clean thoose peanuts they allow you a to throw on the floor better get paid doubled definitely something fun they do for customers but what a mess!!!! Food is good. The loaded mashed potatoes are amazing definitely generous with the butter but whenever I come here I dont order very healthy. The steak is exactly what I expected when I ordered it juicy and delicious. I added on riblets to my meal for five dollars more and they were also great. I added a little extra bar b q sauce for extra flavor and devoured majority of my meal. I definitely recommend you sign up for there email club they are always having all kinds of specials and great deals and if you sign up they send coupons etc. I just got a 10off for my birthday from them. Also they have a kids eat free day. A bogo on fajitas once a week. There killer salad really is..
Country fried steak is good too. Give it a try you might be surprised. . ;)
This is not for the restaurant. It's for the bakery and deli. They sell too much old food out of the bakery. Stuff that should have been thrown away two days earlier, it seems.

cant get enough of this place. the burger battle is a great way to spend your lunch time. Sneak in a cold Urban Chestnut then saunter back to the rest of the day. Good spot before Cardinal games and they are open late. if they have the candied bacon you have to try it.
Great vibes, the staff is fantastic. They have 50 cents wings everyday. Usually go for the wings and the vibes. Definitely recommend this place to watch some Bucs football as well.

Atiya Ola's is awesome!! I'd heard about this place a lot but didn't get a chance to go check them out probably because they close at like 7p which doesn't work out so well for me. Finally I got chance to go this past week and the experience was totally worth it. 

The owners are very friendly and the service is great too. I had the sausage sandwich (vegan) and it is the bomb. I also did try the chili -- delicious!! There is this unique herbal taste that you get in the food which is awesome. They're pretty generous with spice so you might want to ask them to tone it down a bit if you're not used to all that spice. Oh did I mention their vegan cakes? I had a chocolate cake and it was mind-blowing. 

My only wish is that Altiya's was open for longer hours.

Great for a healthy lunch on the go. I probably stop here about once a week. Lots of local and organic food, and finally they recycle, which is great considering all the places around here that DON'T! The salad choices are extensive and always fresh. And the paninis are full of cheezy gooey goodness. The petite girls behind the counters can be snooty, but all in all a high recommendation.

Nonna rosa is a very good family restaraunt.. They have entrees as well as pizza and always a boat load of soups to choose from.. I recommend the stuffed pepper soup!  It's italian cuisine  they also make a pretty good cheesesteak for lunch.  I wish I went here more actually!  Chicken Marsala, fried mushrooms, and fried calamari are all pretty good! Always friendly wait staff too !  It's not fancy but very comfortable.

Great byob in the northern liberties area. Really a 4.5 star experience rather than a 4.Same owner as monsu which is another great byob! Went on a Tuesday which I found out is the night the owner is the chef. It gets very popular so reservations are required on Tuesdays. 

I had the turista menu.-4 courses. I did the grilled calamari. It was good but very lemony. Next time I would try a different appetizer. I then had the fettuccini. It was a spicy fettuccini with sausage. Very good!! Then I had the cioppino. Again delicious! Tried some of the lamb which was seriously amazing also. And agree with other reviewers, get the tiramisu. Some of the best I've had!! 

Overall amazing dining experience. Can't wait to go back!

If I could give 0 stars I would!!  The past three times I've been here the drive thu has been closed.  One excuse after another.   Someone actually came on the intercom and said the cook left early!!  I don't know why I keep coming back to this location, I guess  bc it's the only one by me!  Just drove out of the drive through after sitting for over 10 min, it was 7:40, clearly they are open and yet unable to handle the one lone car in the drive thru. 
THIS LOCATION SUCKS!!

Those horrible review about hair is  bull and people are mean and vindictive.  Trying to protect others or be protected should re commended. I love Sopfias and it has  always been great.  Food is awesome and service is wonderful.  It is my go-to greek restaurant in Boise.  If you are new to the area stop by!

This is the worst tasting P.F. Chang's that we have ever had. There was nothing fried about the mushy, flavorless rice they brought to the table. I would have said something except we didn't see our server until they brought our bill. To top it off, the parking situation here is terrible. We literally witnessed two women get out of their cars and have a verbal argument over a parking spot. We won't be back.

Headed over to Teca to celebrate our good friends anniversary. Very nice restaurant, plenty of seating including an outdoors section. The bar had pretty much everything you could want including a vast wine selection. 
I had the Penne Alla Vodka which was on the al dente side but very good.  
Nothing really bad to say about this place expect for it being a little on the pricey side. And after your done you can always head up to the cougar bar upstairs (Mezzanine) lol.

Poor Charlie's.  It's true what the others are saying; it's easy to forget it's there. And that's sad, because it's a small, dark, cozy pub.  The food is good, sort of a gastropub but quiet about that. It's more expensive than a lot of pubs, but it's a nice dining experience.

It's easy to overlook Charlie's when you walk past, but if you want a quiet place that is a bit more grown-up, stop in for a pint or dinner.

Would give 0 stars if it was an option. Ordered the lemongrass beef bowl. Cant say enough about how disappointed I was in the half bowl being vermicelli noodles, the other half bowl is bean sprouts and the ten overly thin pieces of flavorless burned beef jerky on top. What a joke, I can only hope this place goes out of business soon!!!!

Just visited for the first time toaday 3/16/13, I had a great experience the staff was very very friendly. I enjoyed the hot dogs  ( LONE RANGER )  and one with pepper hash and mustard very much it was fast, soft rolls and hot and fresh.
I have read some of the negative reviews but I found no such conditions during my visit.
I recommend trying this establishment and form your own opinion.
So good and fast and affordable, I tried chipotle across McCarran and it's not even close to this place. Fresh ingredients and it shows

I have been to this place twice now. Very good fried chicken. Friendly waitress. I did have an issue with my meal. I ordered 2 chicken wings and a thigh with a drink, that's all Total was
. $9.00 plus I tipped the waitress $2. My complaint is the chicken pieces were  VERY small. I feel they are way over charging for the small amount of food. I am not a big person so for me to complain, its bad. I never said a word to the waitress, its not her fault. I understand it cost money to open a business but over charging will catch up with them and it would be a shame to see them closed up down the road. I wish them the best but don't think I will be back. I could only give them 2 stars

Entertaining meal!  We ponied up to the bar to place our afternoon lunch order.  Great service, and you'll be at once of those places where the bartender actually talks to you, jokes around, and you've made friends with everyone in the vicinity by the time you've left.  
Everything we ordered was consistently well-prepared, and while it won't knock your socks off, it is hearty and delicious, home cooked cajun food.  Be prepared for bigger portions than you typically expect.  The crabcake is pretty good, as are the gumbos, crawfish, etc.  Well worth a stop.

I come here MAYBE once a month as a treat for brunch cause it is a bit pricy for a regular weekend spot, but since it's so close to my apartment and the food is delicious, I really don't mind.  They also serve dinner during limited hours so I'll have to check that out sometime.

I figured I'd update my review now that I've had a few more breakfast/brunch items.  My absolute favorite item on the menu (and maybe across ALL brunch places in the city) is, hands down, their special of Huevos Rancheros.  I hope it makes it to the regular menu, although there's only been one time they were out of it.  It is absolutely effin' amazing.

A GIANT fluffy homemade waffle (not too sweet, but sweet enough to counteract the toppings) smothered in smooth and creamy eggs hollandaise with the perfect breakable yolk, crispy thick cut bacon, fresh made guacamole and pico de gallo, black beans and a generous portion of cheddar cheese.  Holy hell.  My mouth is watering thinking of it.  It's the absolute perfect balance of sweet, savory, spicy, crunchy and chewy - and I make sure to top it off with some Cholula.  (That's another thing I love about this place - the choice between Frank's, Cholula and Sriracha!).  It's so big, I can only eat 3/4 of it no matter how much I try to finish the whole thing.

The egg/meat/hash/toast combo is always a good classic staple to order if you're not feeling too adventurous and everything is fresh, locally sourced and served farm-to-table, so you know you're getting top notch ingredients.

Although it's a little pricy for breakfast (keep in mind I came from Scranton where you'll pay, no lie, $20 for a family of 4 at breakfast places), I find it's entirely worth it with the quality of the food and always on-point service you're receiving.

Their coffee is fantastic (they serve only good brands...I think this weekend it was Rival Bros) and the cucumber water is perfect for when you get a seat outside in the blazing sun and you're mildly hungover.

During pandemic, Yamato considered has good customer traffic during difficult time. This has to thank to their simplicity of menu and more combo price dish. It is more attractive in compare to my first visit. The combo menu make it more affordable and the customer can try more items. 

I got the Yamato Special. It has shrimp, chicken, and steak. The side dish includes fried rice, veggies, noodle, salad, soup. This is the first time I also bring home the left over. My wife have the steak and calamari combo. We like our food. I think the chef make it a bit too salty. 

We always like the show. It includes the egg roll and toss. I also like the big fire in the beginning, ops check your eye brown after the show. Did it burn off. The volcano onion is classic. We enjoy the entertainment. As usual, this is seat close to the tepan cook top. Expect the food smell will stick to you. Just wear easy to wash. Cloth. Avoid bring and leather items such hand bag, clothing. The food smell will be difficult to remove from leather items.

The only thing that we had here was the bread pudding, but we'll definitely come here for more the next time we're in town.

The thing that impressed me most, is that we came to the totally packed restaurant on a Saturday night after having a very disappointing dinner at the Royal House. I'm pregnant and I couldn't bear to end the night without some real New Orleans bread pudding. When we got to the front door, we saw that there was a dress code, so instantly we thought "snobby". But, we were pleasantly surprised when the host told us that it would be no problem to come in for bread pudding.

He directed us to the upstairs dining room and the host up there was just a pleasant... as was our server. My husband and I shared 1 traditional bread pudding and he ordered a glass of red wine. The bread pudding was ABSOLUTELY AMAZING and the waitress was more than happy to serve us despite the small bill for her.

We tipped her very well and drooled over the delicious looking food all around us on our way back outside to the French Quarter.

Un menú completo y un sabor unico de nuestra isla. Si deseas comerte un plato tipico o recordar los chinchorreos de la isla te recomiendo este lugar. Los mariscos son frescos, el pescado un 100% en fin variedad y todo con buen gusto.

I ordered the ying yang rice ...half shrimp, half chicken..I think they ran out of shrimp and sauce it was mostly the red sauce and chicken and it was awful!!! They coulda said so and at least gave me a chance to change my order. AWFUL! Will never go there again

LOVE this place. Get lunch here at least 3x a week. Two massive slices and a soda for 5$ is a perfect deal. The slices are huggggeeee, thin, and the garlic butter they put on the crust is to die for. Honestly, one of my favorites in all of Tampa... Their buffalo chicken pizza is easily some of the best I've ever had. 

The baked spaghetti and chicken/meatball parms are very different, and totally worth a try. I try to switch it up whenever I go there so I don't turn into a pizza myself, but overall this place is worth it.

Not sure why people say it's expensive, you get so much food for what you pay for, it's worth every penny.

Anyone who's comparing it to Papa Johns or Dominos needs to talk a walk, this place is exponentially better, and not even in the same category as fast food pizza chains. There's a reason those places are 5$ a pie, and authentic NY style pizza are not.

I got the lunch special, including a turtle soup and the shrimp and grits entree. To be truly in the spirit of the town, I also ordered the bread pudding and a 25 cent Cosmo. The Cosmo was great, even though I don't typically enjoy vodka. The turtle soup was good, although I failed to accept the extra splash of sherry and seemed to suffer with a soup that was overly salty. Otherwise, it was interesting: I imagined a green goo, but it came out like a meaty beef stew (couldn't tell what turtle actually tastes like). Portion size was decent. 

The shrimp and grits were good, though somewhat of a smaller portion. I believe it came with 5-6 shrimp over a lump of cheesy grits. They were the tastiest grits I had ever had, though the dish overall was a bit lacking--compared to some wonderfully perfect shrimp I had had a previous evening as an appetizer at a wedding at the Audubon Zoo. 

The bread pudding was fun, though I am a dessert fanatic and found it difficult to take more than 3 bites of this overly sweet gooeyness. Perhaps it's my love or chocolate or my knowledge that you need enough fat in a dessert to counteract the sugar, but this was way too sweet and a virtual waste of $9 and only 2-stars. I did try my friend's pecan pie, however. And although overly sweet as well, I think I could have managed at least 5 bites of that. It was a 4-star dessert. 

What was absolutely 5-star was the service. As soon as you walk in, you feel the attention on the customer... From everyone having about a 10' awareness of you walking around (so they can let you pass with great ease) to pulling out AND PUSHING IN your chair when you sit, to laying the napkin on your lap... damn! Great service. And, beautiful ambiance. 

Note: go for the lunch to save some dough. It's typically a $16-$30 entree for lunch and about a $20-$40 for dinner.

You know one thing all cats are good at? Hunting. You know what this cat, this cat right here....is real, real good at? Hunting high quality product. So I'm gonna strut on in here and set the record straight, as most cats out there aren't really sure what they're meowing about in reference to top-notch product. 

This cat strolled through this alley, came across this Taqueria piece, and sniffed his way on inside. Once inside, took a look around. Saw my neighborhood cats chillin' at the bar. A few on some meowtch.com dates. And decided I was feelin' the scene and figured I'd give this Taq a tastin'.

First order of business? Need some of that seafood, so I went with the shrimp ceviche. Talk about umami...definitely refreshing and flavorful. Taste buds were poppin'. Receptors were receivin'.

Next order of business? Now you might laugh, but any time I can eat a Dog and not have to run from one? That's a guaranteed 4-paws-up and a purr-purr from meow. Very unexpected, but the perro caliente is on point. Forget about mustard and catchup....the pico de gallo / salsa verde combo? Damn that shiz had me hoppin'.

Last order of business? Yeah you guessed it, those fish taco jumpoffs. Might as well just chop those up, throw them in a can, put a Fancy Feast label on 'em, and sell those pieces nationwide. No for real, they're that good.

Washed all that down with a few 'ritas (particularly the Three Chili and the Santana) and next thing I know, I was feline great and ready to get my strut on. 

Any time I can eat a meal like that, feel a little woozy, and keep all my puurrchases under fifty beans?? Psssh....ain't no thang but a chicken wing. Or in this case, a fish taco.

- Esquire

I visit my sister once a year and we like to discover new places together, and I am so glad we discovered this great restaurant. I went in November 2013 around thanksgiving and it was freezing, but we still decided to sit outside next to a heater since it was crowded inside. I love the crawfish beignet and LOVED the shrimp and artichoke bisque. I will definitely be going back here when I visit my sister next year!!!

I like Popeye's. This one has only been open for a couple of weeks and I stopped by on a weeknight to pick up dinner for a small crowd. I ordered the Fried shrimp combo with mashed potatoes and a 12pc Family Meal (spicy) with Cajun Fries and Red Beans & Rice. I ordered an additional small side of Cajun rice. I went inside and it took over 25 minutes to receive my order. Apparently the problem was they were out of spicy chicken but had lots of regular. All of the employees were very nice but 25 minutes at a fast food restaurant isn't acceptable. When I got home with the order we had received a second mashed potatoes side instead of the Cajun rice. Not a huge deal but get it together new location! Orders should be right and shouldn't take 25 minutes!
The best pizza in Nashville by far. If I'm in town I always try to stop by. Great service, and great pizza. You can't go wrong by choosing this place. Come and check it out.

Go to the one on Belcourt Ave near the Grilled Cheeserie! We went Sunday morning at about 11am and only waited about 15-20 minutes! The one downtown was ALWAYS wayyy busier! But the food was absolutely amazing.

From the moment we set foot on the property, we were impressed. Greeted at the door with historical information about the house, we were then welcomed by the owner personally as she showed us to our table. The ambiance was lovely and the service superb. Between us, my husband and I shared calamari, fried green tomatoes, rack of lamb and sea bass and found all of it absolutely delicious. After dinner, we retreated to the enclosed porch area for dessert by the fire, a yummy baked chocolate chip skillet cookie with ice cream. 
What a gem of a restaurant, especially for celebrating a special event!
Good family owned, authentic shop. Great Horchata.

This is the second time we had an order that was screwed up. The first time or several months ago when we ordered a calzone and they left out half the ingredients we requested. This time, I got the veggie flatbread which was essentially pizza without the sauce, the crust was so thick, not the way a flatbread should be. My daughter got the chicken chipotle panini and they forgot not only the coleslaw and pickle but also the Chipotle sauce! Our meals tasted good enough but they were not as expected or as listed on the menu.

Needless to say, we are not going back. This place used to be good but it's completely unreliable now.

Been going to gators for more than 10 years but in the last two years the food quality has gone down the tubes. The location is brilliant down by the water and the staff are friendly but alas the tools they have to work with are second rate. I'll keep checking in the coming years to see do things improve and report back October 2014.

Excellent Q in Midtown Reno!

Dined for lunch on a Thursday.  Ordered the pulled pork plate with two sides (beans and spicy slaw) and a slab of cornbread.  Lunch companion ordered the three rib plate with beans and potato salad.  Service was incredibly efficient and friendly.  Interior of the restaurant was well organized and clean.  Meals arrived piping hot within minutes on a reusable plate with an actual metal utensil.  My pulled pork was outstanding, and honestly, enough for two.  The beans were well seasoned with a hint of heat.  The slaw was fresh, with a bit of a kick and not overly drenched in dressing.  Cornbread was excellent as well. Really appreciated the roll of paper towels and house made sauces at each table.  Service staff delivered the meal, checked in to see how we were enjoying our food and to see if we needed anything additional.  They also removed our dirty dishes when we were finished eating.  The restaurant was very busy but there was plenty of help and the operation ran like a well oiled machine.  It was my first visit but it won't be my last.  Well done, very well done.

Kylie was our server on a Tuesday she sat and explained every detail of the burger deal and was patient with my group as my grandpa is hard of hearing she was so nice and made our experience very fun! We will be coming back soon!

One of my top 3 sushi spots in Tucson! Love the all you can eat, there is something for the whole family. Ordering off the menu or all you can eat, you just cant go wrong. Always nice friendly service.
Delicious food amazing tortas tacos and horchata! I love this place amazing friendly owner and staff very clean and nice to sit out and enjoy food!

What a restaurant! Bistro Romano is one of my favorite restaurants in Philly. It's rare you find restaurants as intimate as this with reasonable pricing. Even with a packed room there's something about this place that is just relaxing. You can enjoy a meal and not worry about screaming over the table to friends. They have a simple menu, attentive service and great food. A great spot for dates as well as dinner with friends. 

One thing we thought was cool was the tableside caesar salad. Definitely worth it

where to start.... 
my boyfriends dad went to the bathroom and he was washing his hands, saw a severer leave the bathroom stall and walk back into the kitchen. gross. anyways  got there at 7:30 didn't get food until 9:15 ish 
my boyfriend got someone else food first 
my shrimp cocktail had maybe 5 shrimps 
most of it was tomato
my boyfriends burrito was no better than a burrito from cucas. 
asked for water and didn't get until i asked another waiter for water. 
wow. just wow.

Fantastic (as expected) lunch.  Dining experience was 5-star.  Menu is above expectations, service (with Austin) was stellar and the food is totally delicious!  Finally a fantastic place with great vibes to eat downtown.

Great place for local food and NOLA beer. Off the beaten path of Saint Charles Street one block over on Magazine. Get away from the tourist trap restaurants and find the good stuff, like Roux.

Service was good. We were served by one of the owners who recommended some amazing food and beer. NOLA Blonde Ale was a great match with the BBQ shrimp. Delicious!
Hidden gem. Not much to look at but it's clean, very reasonably priced, and the staff are super friendly.  And, most importantly, the food is fresh, attractive, and yummy!

Thank you for the great personable service Madison! 

I was sick this am and just wanted something light and a quick drink. Great recommendations and a nice stiff drink! 

She usually works nights at bar but has a Saturday am shift. 

#checkforMadison

Probably the best asian food in the area having grown up in the NYC area and eating in Chinatown on the weekends.  Very authentic and if you go, ask for items off the "Chinese" menu.  Food is extremely authentic.  The food on their regular menu is very good but love the other items better!  Go early and eat in as the food is much better when it's pipping "hot".

Saw this spot while riding by & thought it looked so cute. Well, at least it did from a distance. Food was actually pretty good, but the restaurant seemed like it needed a thorough deep clean & some love! Waitresses were nice, but I felt really bad for them because they were being scolded by their boss the whole time. Been trying to give small businesses/restaurants my money since most are hurting right now from the pandemic, but there are much better, cleaner options in the area!

I don't know if we walked in at the wrong time or something but the experience I had was way different than the other reviews. Mussels weren't fresh and the lamb chops were rare. Drinks were alright but did not walk out the place satisfied. Probably not going back.

I wasn't super into the idea of a tehina shake but it was so so good! The falafel sandwich is pretty great, maybe a tiny bit too salty but the balls are fluffy and fresh tasting. Good service and nice that it's vegan too!
Second time here and just as great! All around one of the best BBQ places. The brisket was absolutely perfect this time also. Took my girlfriend this time and she was equally impressed.
This place is so yummy!!! The corn beef is the most expensive but treat yourself don't cheat yourself  the samples are delicious!

Jimmy Johns may be freaky fast, but I was freaky fast too as I plowed threw my Turkey Tom. Turkey, lettuce, tomato, alfalfa sprouts, and mayo. I added all of their freebies that weren't already in my subwich; onion, sliced cucumber, Dijon mustard, oil & vinegar, and oregano. It was as freaky good as it was freaky fast. 

My Dad got their J.J. Gargantuan; Genoa salami, sliced smoked ham, Capicola, roast beef, turkey, provolone, onions, mayo, lettuce, tomato, & Italian dressing on their thick sliced 7 grain bread. It was freakin huge! Even the man who invented the clean plate club had a hard time putting this subwich away...I had to help =) 

It's a lot of meat, almost too much for me. I couldn't really differentiate between which meat was which, there was so much flavor going on. 

J.J's is really only good for subwich's, they don't have much other than that.

One of the best chicken strips you will ever find. Seasoning on the chicken makes your taste buds pop. They are meaty and crispy it's amazing but the fries and honey butter biscuits are out of this world. Nothing like them. I could eat those biscuits for days they literally melt in your mouth with the sweet buttery flavor and texture. I wish I found this place sooner. Such an eatery gem in the French Quarter.

This little gem pulled off the proverbial "hat trick" with us.  Great unique food and drink.  Great service.  Great Design.

Nice job folks.  Really.

Went there today for brunch.  Alexandra was our server.  She answered questions and made recommendations with poise and genuine enthusiasm.  The food was exceptional, well plated, fresh, and flavorful.  The interior is a relaxed rustic vibe blending conventional sit down dining, dine-at-the-bar, and a unique "Old Fashioned" bar area.

It was a little dark lighting-wise for a brunch, but considering the number of novelty menu items named in recognition of those nursing Sunday morning hangovers, I could argue that the dimmer lighting was entirely intentional and benevolent!

This is one we're going to return to as a destination.  I'll be sure to update with my 'tales from the Old Fashioned bar" if I can remember any of them next-day.  (hic)

The food was so flavorful and fresh! Hard to pick from so many choices. We went for an early dinner and enjoyed socially spaced out tables. Outdoor dining was open still too. Attentive and friendly service. Most portions are meant to share so that allowed us to try a variety of things. The biscuits with au jus sauce, flaked sea salt and seasame seeds were tender, buttery and flaky. The creamed corn and roasted cauliflower sides were both winners. I was disappointed with the ribs as they weren't as tender as I hoped for, but I'm also not a ribs person. My husband enjoyed them. The bbq sauce however was very nice, with a little kick of spice. My favorite part was the warm dehydrated towels they dropped into a tiny bathtub of hot water after eating the ribs  Adorable.

The. Best. Lunch. This is such a beacon of light, just a real treat in St. Petersburg. Well-Priced Lunch or Dinner. Great Business Catering. Fresh and Light Salads. 
Light Lunch - Got Em' 
Fresh Fish - Got Em'
Tasty Drinks - THEYYYY Got Em'

I just hope the line doesn't get longer.

Hitting the touristy spots were going to be inevitable...one in particular was Cajun Cabin. After passing all the drunks and the skanks down Bourbon St.(2 days before Mardi Gras..so Bourbon St. was crazy chaotic), I came across Cajun Cabin where there were some empty seats...it was great because all the other restaurants were either too packed or pricey...We came inside and our hostess was totally nice to us. The lighting was dim and a live band was playing in the back of the restaurant...pretty awesome and fun! I didn't know what to order but eventually I ordered the blackened tuna (Ok so I should've ordered some authentic Louisiana food like a po'boy or something but i still wasn't used to the meat and the grease yet...) Well...the tuna was FABULOUS...I loved it but couldn't finish it for it was a huge portion and the crawfish etouffe plus gumbo added on...oh and swamp water (I forgot what type of alcohol they mixed) was STRONG! Overall, it was a fun experience except for that creepy drunk who tried to strike up a conversation

Short on time but definitely worth spreading the word. This place was 100% awesome on all of the metrics. Environment was good. Service was good. Great little ginger salads came out before the meal. We got Pot Stickers which were head and shoulders way better than most places we have gone, and the dinners were great :) 

Loved it.

Went for a quick meal for my grand baby.  Went through drive through.  Long story short, they forgot to fulfill my order.  I called them went back and management and employees were very sorry about it the tried to give me a whole meal.  I declined.  Mistakes happen.  No biggie.  Gave me my sandwich and some pies.  Didn't need the extra stuff.  Just thought it was nice that everyone was kind about it.  And I know that's just good customer service.  It was the whole attitudes and manor of all.involed that made it a pleasant.  Big ups Hatfield pa. McDonald's!!!

I've only ever had Clarkville to-go, so I can't comment on the service. The prices are definitely on the high side for pizza in West Philly, but the food I've tried is delicious.

My favorite pizza is the Eggplant Pie (roasted eggplant, tomato sauce, cream, cheese blend, black kale, roasted peppers, and parmesan). I also love the Honey Pie (shaved brussels, cheese blend, grilled onion, and sriracha honey). It also comes with bacon, but I asked them to leave it off.

Overall, it's a solid choice for unique pizza flavor combinations.

My friend and I stayed here last weekend and I must say that we were very disappointed! I know I got heads up that there would be evacuees due to the recent hurricane, but the fact that the staff doesnt care to set rules on the evacuees loitering throughout the outside of the hotel is a bit outlandish. The place looked like a homeless shelter from the outside. That's not even the worst part of it all. Our room had NO HOT WATER! We called the front desk and they told us to let the water run for 5 mins. We let it run for 30 mins and nothing. They said they would send someone to check it for us and the guy showed up at 1am. He apologized for coming so late, but by that time we had endured cold showers and were already in bed. And this cold water issue was for our entire stay yet it never got rectified. The very few good things were that the room was clean and they did supply us with request such as toilet paper and towels pretty quick whenever we requested it. I'm just glad that our trip didnt consist of us having to spend much time in our hotel room. I don't think I will be returning to this location again, unless I can be guaranteed that the issues wouldn't occur again of at least having the ability to have a hot shower.

We waited to be seated at the bar and we had the cocktail special of the night. We met the sous chef (very polite and friendly from Cuba) who suggested the best dishes. Modern atmosphere and cool dishes. Must try the chocolate cake with olive oil and salt.

My friend and I had the chicken tika masala with the garlic nann. We shared one of each along with the tickki chaat for apetizer, which was recommended by a friendly waiter :) It was a bit pricey but the food quality was worth it!

I've never had a bad meal here.  They don't have a huge menu, but they don't need one because everything they do is fantastic.  I keep trying different things and am never disappointed.  The creole meatloaf is the meal that hooked me.
Nice, clean bowling alley, full bar, pool tables, decent bowling alley food, nice staff.

If you have good morals and hate pornography then don't go here! They have a child's menu on the window which is outrageous to advertise as family friendly and then have nude and nearly nude images all over the walls! What on earth are theses people thinking!?!

Our group of 4 ate here on a Saturday in October 2013. The place was quite crowded at 5:00pm, but we called ahead for seating and had zero wait, which was awesome. The place is very large inside and could use a little remodeling (especially the very dimly lit smaller-than-a-breadbox ladies bathroom at the front of the place) but it did have a certain rustic charm that I enjoyed. They also have ample outdoor patio seating - which I'm sure would be quite lovely in warmer weather.  Started off with the French onion soup, which was probably the best I've ever eaten ANYWHERE, and the buffalo chicken eggrolls were homemade and to-die-for. For dinner I had the homemade cheese ravioli - the ravioli were very tasty, but I think their sauce could use a little work. Hubby had the veal parm, which was average. We sampled our friends' plates - baby back ribs and chicken cordon bleu - both were exceptional. While there we took notice of some of the plates being served at other tables nearby - and when we go back I'll definitely be trying their prime rib (it was nearly bigger than the dinner plate) and the burgers also look incredible.

Had dinner tonight at miro
It did not meet my expectations for the amount
of money we spent 
Was told the wine pairing was going to be 45
For the tasting menu 
Really it was 65 
Times 4 people that is a 80 mistake 
When brought up we were told we were misquoted
But oh well we were to pay for the whole 
Mistake 
Waitstaff forgot to bring bread 
Food lacking
Next time I will look at other options

It's a great place to go accept for a Saturday or Friday night. The bread is amazing, you can taste it's fresh. Service was over attentive and great personality. I can tell when it is not the servers fault but I had ordered the spaghetti and meatballs. It came out with under cooked pasta which was no big deal just sent it back for a new one. Forty minutes later came out with the same dish, and it was still undercooked chewy hard noodles. Every other time I've been here I've really enjoyed it but avoid going on busy days

I was there last night with a friend. We were playing darts and sipping on wine. We befriended a couple and started talking about 90s songs. We began playing them on the juke box. No harm. There were about 3 other people at the bar. The manager on duty proceeded to skip all of our songs that we paid for and gave us the bill. He told us he took two drinks off to Compensate for the money we spent on the skipped songs and told us he did not care to ever see us again. Over what? Mariah Carey and Britney Spears songs?? I informed him that I too manage a bar and I would never ever do that unless the songs were in any way directly changing the atmosphere in a derogatory way. I asked for his name and he said don't worry about it. I told him we have been here only two times and liked the food and drinks and told him I'm industry and I know a lot of people who now will not be patrons to this establishment. His reply? I'm not worried, there is only two of you. I was disrespected, robbed of my money, and asked to leave because of our taste in music for those 10 minutes. I gave 1 star because I had to. Very disappointed.

I wish more such places exploded all over Nashville. This is what a community needs. A detachment from commercially mass produced processed food and an emphasis on local mom n pop businesses that take the time and lovingly create gourmet foods. The prices are on the steep side, no doubt, but you get what you pay for. Their raviolis are superb and so are their choices of Olive oil and cheeses. It's buried away in the nook of Germantown, but it's worth the drive.

I took my mom here for her 60th birthday and was very happy with our overall experience. I had heard from a few co-workers that Carmel was very good. The staff helped me set up our table with birthday balloons and stored the cake in the kitchen for me. The food was very good. I had the braised short ribs with polenta. My sister had the steak frites which was also delicious. The staff cut the cake for us which was very nice. I will definitely be dining here again.

I stopped in here for a quick to go drink. The place has a great patio for day drinking and you're allowed to bring dogs!! The drink was delicious and I could barely taste the alcohol in it (even though it was incredibly strong). I will definitely be back for an another drink and some food.

The food is good. The scene is casual and relaxed. The waitress service is slow. Then this happened...the waitress who was maybe overwhelmed spilled a bowl of wing sauce into my wife's new white purse. She said sorry and then disappeared forever.

Stopped by here while driving to see what the crazy lines were about. Well, the hype is for real and the food is delicious. The employees are so friendly and did I mentioned how good the food was? I got the spicy chicken sandwich, which was delightful. Wl definitely be back.

I admit it - I am a  pizza snob. 

As a boy growing up in North Jersey I cut my teeth on New York style, thin crispy crust. I am sorry that there was a time in my life that I thought ALL pizzas were great ( college years primarily, where mass quantities of beer and possibly other things were involved). I am older now and hopefully wiser. 

Having been to mecca - New York City's greatest pizzerias -  and specifically, the best pizzeria in the USA - Di Faras in Brooklyn, I have been ruined as far as most pizza sold around here. 

Dont get me wrong - The City of Brotherly Shove has undergone a  pizza renaissance with Nomad, SLiCE,Beddia, Pizza Brain and many others.Trenton's not far and a trip to DeLorenzo's is worth the travel time as its delicious. It's just in Delco, top pizzas are hard to find. Many are subjective, acquired tastes (Gennaros in Springfield, New London in Prospect Park, Rennatos in Swarthmore are all stellar locally). NY Style is just not found in Delco.

But if you look around, occasionally you are surprised as I was at Goose Creek Grill in West Chester.

They have several cold beers on tap - required when eating pizza ( great pizza and cold beer...one of life's finest pleasures). I ordered a ice cold Stella. It was great.Unfortunately that is it for alcohol so my girlfriend was out of luck as wine is BYOB. She had a coke.

She ordered the pulled pork sandwich and liked it. She also liked the sweet potato fries. I had the Caesar salad which was tasty - heavy on the garlic flavor.

Of course, I had the margarita pizza and was really impressed. The crust was light and crispy(order well done). The tomato sauce was thick.Could have used more cheese. Overall, this was a good pizza.

Service was good as well.

Honestly I swear this place use to be a lot better in terms of food and service.

My last visit was horrible, but I will not give them one star because I have been here many times in the past and the food and service were much better.

I came here around  2:30-3p.m meaning: slow time, not that many customers.

I came by myself and was promptly seated.

Minutes later waitress came up and I gave her my full order: bottled water, fried oysters (they dont have that but she allowed me the child's fried oysters plate), and one of the blackened grilled fish specials/entrees.

A very long TIC TOC................................waiting................waiting..................I mean my goodness how much more waiting..........................I am about to cancel my order................

20 minutes later I get my water....................tic tic toc........................

30 minutes later I get my caesar salad that was part of entree.  Upon inspection I notice a big, nasty, black ROTTEN CHUNK of romaine lettuce, a chunk of the heart was disgustingly slimmy, nasty, black, rotten, gross.  So, I take that big chunk out then inspect the rest and throughout the lettuce there are rotten black pieces that I pull out.  The waitress comes up to me and takes the pieces that I placed on a napkin on the table and apologizes for the rotten pieces and giant chunk.  So, of course I do not eat the salad.

40 minutes later I finally get my entree of blackened fish which was barely blackened, if at all and probably defrosted and grilled.  Not that tasty, average.

Overall a very horrible experience.

I was meeting some friends to listen to music on Dilla day. I wasn't planning on food since KWNK was serving up donuts, but I realized that I needed some healthier eats (since I am on this silly diet). I placed my order at the counter and made myself comfortable in a nearby spot  and saw that there were lots of options around me, including pizza, wine, beer, Thali . . . and we were all sharing the same space.  Which, is super nice because people can ordered from different places and share in 1 spot.  I ordered 2 mushroom tacos and tempura veggies.  Now, I realize that tempura veggies aren't technically diet food, but I was planning on splitting these tacos with my husband who was on his way.  
When he arrived, he was not into the mushrooms tacos (we thought the mushrooms would be battered but they were not) so I quickly downed my yummy taco with avocado ($2 extra) pickled onions and cucumber and placed the other in a to go box.  I was pretty satisfied with 1 and the side veggies.  Wish I had MORE pickled veggies because they were the star for me-so yummy! The total meal cost me around $10 which is pretty fair.  Service was kind and the food came out in a reasonable amount of time.  They had a nice selection of beers as well.  
I will definitely be back to get that hand salad and hang out again-next time with some wine from next door.

After receiving a message via Yelp mail from the MTM leadership organization (name of the individual removed at request) I would like to add an addendum.

It was pointed out that in my comparison of MTM to the Brockway Pub or the Stacked Pickle that I did a one-to-one (apples to apples) comparison as if they were the same in menu.  Not wanting to make a statement that was described as "...way out in DEEP right field."   I would like to clarify.

I was asked in the message, 

"[At the other pubs] Can you get a choice cut fillet mignon?  Can you get a choice Ribeye?  Can you get a panko crusted Fresh Walleye entree or sandwich?  Can you get an Ahi Tuna Wonton or a Shrimp and Grits?  Can you get an Ahi Tuna Flatbread?  I don't think so.  And, more than likely, you do not have two culinary chefs in either one of those kitchens like we do at MTM."

-Don't let the previous verbiage make you think that the person who emailed me from MTM Senior Leadership doesn't like the Stacked Pickle or The Brockway Pub as in a second email they told me they do like these two establishments and have dined there on occasion.-

To continue...
You are absolutely correct sir. Many of those items are not on the other pubs' menus. However, I was at your establishment for a work lunch not an intimate dinner and the rectangular shaped fish was tasteless, however, I won't reiterate my last post for either the negatives or the many positives. I hope that your dinner service and food doesn't reflect my two lunch experiences. If and when I return to MTM's I look forward to improvements in your food and hope for your long success in Carmel.

The MTM leadership offered to send me gift certificates for my next meal and the meals of my coworkers. There's no need. I don't write reviews to get free food. I write reviews to inform. All I want is to come into MTM, order, have a great meal with exceptional service, pay the bill and repeat. But that hasn't happened, twice.

I'll try one final time, perhaps, in 2013...and update my review shortly after.

Visiting for CMA Fest and saw great reviews for this place. All 6 of us loved the choices, what we ordered and the service! We all tried each other's and it was so good - hot tenders, best BBQ pizza we've ever had & the salads were so fresh! Will definitely be back!

This is probably my favorite restaurant in Indiana. There Pho is best (Other than my mother's Pho) Pho I've ever had. There's also a wide selection of Vietnamese food. There is a fish tank, and the place smells extraordinary. I'm happy I found this place and wish others do too.

This was my first time at The Root. The ambiance was great, a nice quiet place. I had the smoked scallops at the suggestion of the waiter. When the dish first came out, I thought the waiter had made a mistake because the dish came out in what looked like a cigar box. Once the waiter opened the box, it was indeed what I ordered. It was absolutely delicious, although by the end my mouth did taste like I smoked a cigar. The service was a bit slow which was surprising because the restaurant was not busy at all since it was a Monday. I would definitely return to this restaurant again.

We eat across the street at Inn of the Hawk often and forget to try this restaurant out. Its great! The falafel appetizer was one of the best tasting falafels I've every had. Served with tahini sauce and a freshly made, out of the oven ,puffed up pita. The falafel had a unique spicy taste to it I have not had before. I had the chicken pitza which was tasty.  You can go inexpensive here or go for an entree at $19. Food is amazing. Only draw back was the temperature of the place-cold in the winter, even by the kitchen there was a chill. Hope groupon gives them a shot. This place deserves to be busier.

What a great breakfast. Save room for the rhubarb pie!! 

Servers were attentive and all smiles.

This location used to be good. I almost always just order take out. When you dine in for the most part when you dine in they get orders correct. Staff is friendly. Resturant is clean. However for take out, check your order before you leave. I have got the wrong order the last 3 times. I ordered buffulo chips and got chips and salsa. The salsa trust me is not good, so I wouldn't order it anyway!  
Bad take out service plus order is almost never ready on time.

Mine and my boyfriends favorite place to go to in nashville for a special night out. It's great food and always love music, only thing I dislike is I feel like the tables are on top of each other, if you're looking for something a little more private or romantic I would suggest somewhere else

I wanted to stop in to this cafe for a while now and I am glad I did. I came on a Monday evening and it wasn't too crowded. On one side, you have the cafe which has pastries, smoothies, etc. and on the other side is the restaurant with a full bar. 

I really wanted a seafood dish which had shrimp, scallops, and more in a bucatini pasta but the waitress told me they missed a seafood shipment and it wasn't available. So I had to choose something else and it led me to the mushroom pappardelle and I added some chicken. When I say it was good, it was good. I really enjoyed it and probably ate every mushroom in that bowl. The noodles were just right, the amount of chicken and mushrooms were proportionate. The flavor was great. I am not mad about having to reroute my choice. 

Happy hour until 7 is also a good deal, despite getting there at 6:50. Still managed to get one round in before the time changed. Just as we were leaving, we decided to check out the upstairs where we heard music. Lo and behold, open mic night! Okay Front Street Cafe...good food and entertainment...you might just have to see me again.

Love that they have vegan options and authentic Israeli style food. The falafel is absolutely delicious. My only gripe is that a side of french fries costs $8!! And they're a perfect complement to the falafel pita. I think the price may have increased?
I wish if you ordered a sandwich/pita, it would come with a side of fries or a side of fries for no more than $3. Then it'd be the perfect meal. Unfortunately, the steep price is a deterrent, so I can't order too often. If they changed this, it would definitely be a 5 star place for me.
The appetizers and entrees were average, but the dessert was decent. Nothing to write home about though. For the price you don't get as much as you would at other Italian restaurants near by though.

This is one of the Best Steak Places in Town!! Took my Wife there For our 11th Anniversary. We were Greeted at the door By the Manager Troy who Promptly seated us at our Table. We were treated great by all the staff. I had the Lobster Bisque soup, shrimp & Steak witch were all very Amazing!! I would highly recommend it!!

Almost every restaurant has Tacos on the menu. Nada just does them better. They have created their own twist of flavors. The food is delicious and they have parking right in front of the restaurant, with an option to park in the Circle Center Mall.

I don't drink coffee but occasionally visit Starbucks for other items.

I paid more than six bucks for a Strawberry Acai Lemonade Refresher at this location and after a few sips through the straw, I started getting air.  It turned out that the glass was about 80% ice (see photo).  What a rip-off!

I had a better experience when I ordered hot chocolate.

I love this place - Boba tea is excellent and has best tasting boba around.  The only problem is that the service is TOO slow -- even before the pandemic I would normally be sitting here waiting over 20 mins for my crispy samurai chicken order to come out.  I stopped by today and not only did their system not take my mobile payment but I sat in the parking drive through service spot for over 30 mins.  Very disappointed- they need to figure out a better system - it defeats the purpose of fast food.

I feel like I need to try this place again. I liked the look of it and I was very intrigued by their items, such as a smores bar (swoon) and chocolate butter cake (remarkable). I was most attracted to the lavender cupcake so I just had to try one. Not impressed. Too much lavender flavoring and my frosting was straight butter. I let the cupcake sit out for atleast 15 mins and you would think the frosting would have come to room temp by then... Nope. It was like straight butter. 
I feel like this was the wrong choice of item for me but I wasn't blown away by the ale either. 
I will go back and try something different.... Perhaps that chocolate butter cake.... Swoooon....

My boyfriend brought me here for dinner on a romantic getaway to Santa Barbara for our anniversary. Bella Vista is located inside the Four Seasons Biltmore directly opposite the beautiful Pacific Ocean. 
We had reservations at 5:30p.m. in order to view the sunset, but unfortunately it was a cold day and the sun decided not to come out (bastard!). We were seated at a table for 2 right next to one of the two fireplaces which was lovely. Our server was friendly, quick, and efficient. I ordered a glass of Pinot Grigio ($12) and my boyfriend ordered a glass of Syrah ($14). We were brought a basket of bread after our server took our order. We decided to pass on appetizers since nothing was really jumping off the page. 

We ordered the following:

Grilled Halibut ($26)- This was in the section of the menu entitled "From The Grill". You are able to pick the type of fish/meat you would like along with two sides and choice of sauce. I picked garlic sautéed spinach, truffle whipped potatoes and a lemon caper butter sauce for my fish. The fish was amazing and the lemon butter sauce went perfectly with it. 

Main Lobster ($38)- Served with Cavatelli Gratin, Spring Onions and Micro Baby Vegetables. My boyfriend ordered this and said the lobster was wonderful but wasn't a fan of the Cavatelli Gratin. I ended up sharing my truffle whipped potatoes with him. 

Dark Chocolate Soufflé ($14)- Served with a side of Vanilla Crème Anglaise and Raspberry Coulis. The soufflé takes 20 minutes to prepare, however ours took about 30. They were very nice about the added wait time and gave us a plate of petite fours in the meantime. The soufflé was perfect. It was light and airy yet oh so decadent and chocolaty. 
In honor of our anniversary they also gave us another complimentary plate of petite fours with "Happy Anniversary" written in chocolate and two candles. I thought that was very sweet.

English Breakfast Tea ($7)- A nice pairing with the Chocolate Soufflé and a great way to end the meal. 

Our total bill after tax and tip came out to $147. 

The overall experience at Bella Vista was right in the name- Bella! Beautiful! If it's nice outside I would definitely recommend requesting a table near the window for a great view of the ocean at sunset. If it's a little cooler out I would certainly ask to sit next to the fireplace- if you're on a date it's quite romantic. 
We'll definitely be back!

I have been coming here for YEARS just for the LEMON BARS!  

They have a full lunch menu, coffee, donuts, cookies, macaroons  and cakes. I have tried several of their baked goods.  My favorites are the lemon bars, chocolate macaroons and some kind of strawberry cream pastry....the best.  They are on the higher end pricing for baked goods but worth a treat every once in a while.

I made a reservation in mid-January for dinner for 4 and was very excited to try Black Horse. The menu looked promising, however, I will never know. When we arrived at Black Horse, we stood in the entry for about 5 minutes before being acknowledged.

Then we were told to move to the bar area. When I mentioned to the host that we had a reservation he replied with 'That's nice, darlin', but some people are as considerate [to the fact] that you have a reservation and its going to be awhile.'

First of all, don't call me 'darlin'' and use such a snide tone. Secondly, Black Horse had my phone number. Why didn't they call to tell me that there was a delay?
We left and had an amazing dinner at Duck Sauce.
Awesome comfy tavern without smoking in BG. Food is good,  drink specials are good, owners are very nice. Trivia is fun, open mike night is enjoyable. Try the fried portabellas--they are fantastic!
This was a great find!  delicious food and rival to other Korean food in the area. It's a great lunch spot, fresh, and I particularly enjoyed the Bulgogi and Kimbap.
Food was ok not worth the wait the bloody Mary on the other hand was worth going to get and walk to another establishment
Get the cardamom gelato and coconut basil sorbet. AMAZING!

When it comes to restaurants, this is my #1, hands down, favorite place to be.  I don't even live in Indy, but I try to make the trip down from Chicago at least twice a year for St. Elmo Steakhouse.  Usually around my birthday, and then any random time I need to get a fix for St. Elmo.  My family has been coming here my whole life and they don't live in Indy either.  I'm not sure if it's the nostalgia, the amazing food, the dark, comfortable wood on the inside, or the extensive wine list that makes this place so special to me.  It's been around for over 100 years, so they are doing something right.  I get the same thing every single time.  A bottle of pino noir, their famous, face melting shrimp cocktail, the navy bean soup (someone else at my table must get the tomato juice so we can share), the 14 oz. Ribeye, medium rare, a side of sauteed mushrooms, and creme brulee.  I don't eat again until days later.  It's worth every penny.  The service is impeccable.  I came here just the other day and the Pacers were having dinner.  Probably trying to get their dinner on before the big NBA strike.  Who knows.  The walls are covered with pictures of famous, and semi-famous people expressing their gratitude for St. Elmos.  No matter where my life takes me, I will always come back to St. Elmo.

This place is the worst. Their customer service is garbage and the crew doesn't care what you ordered, they're going to short you every time or just give you whatever they feel like getting rid of. I order them through Uber Eats, and they leave out the Happy Meal from our order every time. Every. Single. Time. If you want a Happy Meal, order it separately from all your other food so it's the only item on the ticket so they HAVE to give it to you, or better yet, go to any other McDonald's - no matter how far away it is, I guarantee you it's better than this one. Tonight, I was temporarily delighted when I opened the bag and saw a Happy Meal box inside it; then, I opened the box. It was empty.

Exton has a total of 5 Indian Restaurants all in a 1.5 mile radius-- this is overkill and eventually one or  two will have to fail.  I ate here for the first time recently- I give all places a benefit of doubt.  I didn't get to order what I wanted- they were out of ingredients for at least two items I wanted.  For what we ordered the food was good and everyone in my group ate everything without complaint.  They charged about the same as the other competitors in the area-- they were good on the portions (more than enough of paneer, vegetables, and chicken for the curry dishes).  Chicken 65 is not Madras style-- it's Andhra style with yogurt mixed in but still very good.  I can sacrifice ambiance if the food is made like at home, served as such, and there isn't a fast food mentality to push you out.  I'll go back and see if the rating can be raised.  Also, would suggest media and marketing materials. There should be take out menus, mailed as well or coupons included in mailers to drive customers.   If they have catering they should push those marketing materials so people know.  Also, if they're struggling they need to price better or have specials to drive in traffic.  Also, for the S. Asians the theme is 'Non-Veg' in nature but they do a great job on the vegetarian dishes.

This is my spot!!!...I go to a lot of breakfast places but this is the one I go alone to and feel comfortable to handle other things like homework, bills, etc. I am at home here and the coffee & food helps too...

Nice ambiance, get a table upstairs if you can. We had po' boys, they were good. Service was excellent too. Be sure to go to New Orleans on a weekday. Oh, almost forgot, the Bloody Marys were excellent too, pickled okra...etc.

Love coming here. During Covid-19 there is ample space between tables and staff very diligent in wearing face masks. Tried the Lobster bisque, daily soup on Friday. Very tasty with a few pieces of lobster. I always order the Beef on weck, theirs is one of the best.  When I order their Greek salad I always request the potato salad to be on the side, rather than on top of the green salad. Wide variety of beer, wines, and special cocktails.

Pleasantly surprised! Breakfast was excellent. My eggs over medium were perfect. Husbands eggs benedict was perfect too. Bacon and hash browns were crispy and not overly greasy. Service was great. Coffee was topped off with out asking. Music was awesome. Next time we might take advantage of the free champagne.

They make some of their salad dressings in house. Their thousand island dressing is on fire!
Their stuffed catfish is delicious. It's a whole filet. It's fried perfectly. It comes with new potatoes and a vegetable medley. 
The service is impeccable.

Food was delicious. I had been craving boudin balls so we ordered those for an appetizer and did not regret it! I also got the redfish, and it was cooked to perfection. Then we had creme brûlée for dessert, and I couldn't stop thinking about it the next day. Our server was prompt, nice, and full of information. Would recommend this place to anyone who wants to have a nice meal. We managed to go when it was quiet and got to take some fun pictures with the truck outside. We will definitely be back!
Place is awful. Very simply put...the service sucks, food is just ok and they are clueless and rude. Had an awful experience recently and don't know if i'll be back.

I have been to Claim Jumper on several ocassions in California years back and the food and service was very good so I was excited to hear they opened one in Nashville. We arrived at 7:45 pm on a Tuesday and were seated quickly. Our server seemed new but I cant be sure. When ordering our food we were told that they would have to check on several items because they were closing soon(WTF it's7:45 and they close at 9PM). 

We were told they were out of butter and they had to get more because they were closing soon
We were told they were out of bread because they were closing soon
We were told they would have to check on chicken pot pies because they make them ahead of time and they may be out of them since they were closing soon.

When our food arrived it 3 out of 5 plates were cold and the food was just MEH

Bottom line there are too many good restuarants in Nashville to get MEH food at $$ prices.

Skip the Claim Jumper in Tennessee

Odd.
Tacos & Donuts???  

I did not have any donuts but they looked good.
I got a Chopped Salad with overcooked (but tasty - great spice on it) steak.

Would have been great if the meat were at least pink.  (It was well, well, well done.)

$8.47 for a cheap lunch.

Not rushing back though.

I've had pretty good experiences (namely 3) with the Clock Bar. The drinks are awesome it's always lively and the food is amaze-balls and not too pricey. 

So the obvious question: Why do I give it one star?

Well, I ordered my food one evening and while waiting patiently for my food I was able to get a pretty decent view of the kitchen and how the food was being prepared and I spotted in the kitchen a cockroach.

Granted this was maybe 3 years ago, but it was enough to put a bad taste in my mouth and I refuse to knowingly pay for food (which is VERY good) where cockroaches are able to roam freely.  Even if by some fluke that was a rogue roach I would never be able to dine there again, which is a shame because the food and drinks are very good.

Hands down one of my top brunch experiences, and I'm a foodie from San Francisco. The ambiance, menu, and service were above and beyond. The Portland-esque hip decor and lighting with communal tables that are divided into groups of four seats - just enough privacy and just enough people watching. 300+ whiskey selections and a separate Old Fashioned Bar. Some of the best farm to table cuisine. 

My friend and I ordered fried green tomatoes, farmer's breakfast,  whiskey-braised short rib hash, and whiskey cake. My favorite savory dish was the farmer's breakfast - a combination plate of eggs, potatoes, bacon, grits, and jalapeno cheddar biscuits. Seems simple right? Not at all. This is one of the breakfast plates I've eaten with the best execution and quality. The eggs were fresh and perfectly fluffy - just what you would expect from top-notch local farm eggs. The sweet and spicy thick cherry cut bacon was chewy with a burst of equal parts sweet and pepper at the same time. The thick chewy texture of the bacon made every bite explode with flavor. This wasn't one of those typical crunchy, skinny, easily broken pieces of bacon; this was bacon that you wanted to take time to eat, to savor. Equally delicious was the grits - buttery, creamy, and exactly what you would want from Southern grits. Lastly, the jalapeno cheddar biscuits were cheesy, not too spicy, and the ideal texture mix of flaky and bready. I just ate this plate yesterday and am already dreaming to go back.

Definitely order the whiskey cake while you're here. Infused with whiskey, the cake is dense and tasty after a savory brunch. When the whiskey cake was served to us, the server scooped some vanilla whipped cream onto the cake, and I thought it was just that one scoop. Boy was I wrong. He set down the entire bowl of freshly whipped whipped cream right next to the cake. A sweet, creamy, whiskey-infused deliciousness of a cake. I liked that it wasn't too sweet or too rich. Even after the farmer's breakfast, I still had appetite for cake.

I'd like to finish off with a shout out to our server, Frank. A little bit sassy, awesome humor, and convinced me to order the whiskey cake. Frank is a natural and is one of the most personable servers I have had. He saw me going on Yelp at the beginning of our meal, and here I am, Yelping after my meal about this restaurant. I used to write a food blog, but I haven't written a Yelp review or blog post in years. I chose Whiskey Cake to start writing again. Yes, brunch here is just that good - so good it's worth writing about, so go try it for yourself.

Ribs, Tri-tip, Chorizo and Eggs, so many healthy meals. What's funny is I get that same overwhelming healthy feeling I get when I eat sushi. Skip the grease and fat, do yourself a favor and try these meals. Can order online or visit the store/kitchen if you are in northern Nevada. Filling too, really enjoy the healthy meal alternative.

P Square Lounge - The Servers constantly have to run in & out to the main restaurant leaving the doors ajar. Customers have to keep pulling them closed.  Easy fix that needs to be addressed. Staff, service, food, drinks, & atmosphere are always great!
Three visits. All great food. Good to ok service.  Always swamped after 5:30, wait list ahead of time!

I love it here. Ate twice and invited my girlfriend. Only tried two meals. Looking forward to trying more. I love the fact that it's a friendly feeling and a lot of different types of people walk in. If you're Asian, expect the lady to treat you like you are her son or nephew, and not at the ratio of a customer of potential influence. The place is clean. The flies has been in the restaurant every time I come in. But maybe because that was the summer time. Haven't ate there in the winter time. The food was great! It's located in a plaza not too busy. But it can be crowded for those small parking areas. It has nice blinds to protect your Japanese zen environment

I went last Friday with lovely friend of mine for restaurant week. We changed reservations on them like five times and the hostess was SOOOO nice about that! Once we arrived, she explained it was going to be a wait but then sat us 15 minutes later!! Champagne cocktails are delicious!! I had the "Bubble-Lee".. Ordered Calamari and crispy beef which was cooked meduim and DELICIOUS!!! 
When the waitress brought our second round, she accidently shattered the stem of the champagne glass in my plate! She offered to bring a WHOLE new one but I had already eaten 2/3 of the plate and did not want to be toting food around for the rest of the night so I declined. However, she did not COMP a blessed thing! I thought she would at least offer a free $10 cocktail! Even with sharing paltes, this evening can get pretty pricey! We had the restaurant week special $35 for app, dinner, desert and two cocktails each and each spent $70. 
Also, the bathrooms are unisex and even though I LOCKED the door, I was totally walked in on by some random man who proceeded to tell me that it wasn't locked with the door open while I am HOVERING over the toilet! I don't know that that is a reflection ont he restaurant per se.... but it's funny in retrospect! "CLOSE THE DOOR!"
Swanky Bubbles was A-ok!
Cashier Emily hit the nail on the head! Warm friendly smile, allowed me time to put my tomato bank number in, eye contact! Look out earth fare I'm loving you!

This place is well managed.  I could tell walking in the door.  
The cashier really knew his stuff, and cranked out my order with a very non-cheesy enthusiasm.  Definitely the guy of guy you want running your front end.  I was impressed.

Yeah, it kinda sucks that the line is almost constantly 10 people deep...but this place is pretty good, thus it's popular.

My food came out quick.  A Large White (plate) with pimento mac&cheese, southern greens, and red skin potato salad.  

First, the Large plates are really for 2 people, or eating half and taking the other half home.

Second, unless you are REALLY REALLY into hot spice, stick to medium or mild.  I went with HOT, and it was really on the line for me.  I'm positive that I would not be able to enjoy the 2 levels that are spicier.  But even though the HOT was testing my threshold, it was still pretty good.  It took me a lot of napkins...but they are in rolls on every table...i guess it goes with the territory.

And the sides.  They were GREAT.  The Southern greens, which to me means collards were seasoned well, didn't even need hot sauce as I usually douse them.
The pimento mac&cheese was unique, creamy, through I generally prefer the homemade, baked variety.  The pimento part is something I'd like to see more places experiment with.
The red skin potato salad was great as well, maybe my favorite of all.

Anyways, great place.  I'll come again.  And I'll know better what to order next time!
amazing spicy chicken sandwhich. phenomena mayonaasoe . amazing. the cheese stick are good toov

This restaurant is inside of the iconic Monteleon hotel in New Orleans. I was in town for work meetings and we had a fixed menu. However, the food and service were excellent. The gumbo Chef has been there for 30 years and just does soups. The pastry chef has been there for 20 years and the crème brûlée is excellent.

Wow had a plate chicken enchiladas with red sauce!!!

Excellent had some tomatoes, avocados, lettuce

Rice and retried beans awsome.  Then the owner brought us some tamales without asking and they were homemade and fresh.

Highly recommended
Absolutely fantastic. The red snapper was one of the most memorable dishes I have ever tasted, and the pork shoulder absolutely blew me away.
Great food. You will definitely wait in line, but they move the lines pretty quickly. French toast was amazing and I recommend the mimosa!

Quality sushi for Missouri! Everything was fresh and full of flavor! Sometimes service is a bit slow but still very friendly and I've left my Fitbit there once and they kept it safe for me until I returned :)

No kidding you could feed a family of 4 with the pork steak here. Service was fantastic. The waitress was just the right amount of friendly. She was right on time with the drink refills. Everything was delicious even the sides. The atmosphere was fun and family friendly. We came by on a night when they had a guitar player who was real good. Definitely coming back here.

I ordered the southern chicken sandwich, and the pizza Mac. This place is in a cool location the atmosphere is pretty cool, and the food is great. The pizza Mac was sooooooo good, and the southern chicken sandwich was made very well.

Another great experience at Sonobana. As many of you probably know, Sonobana is owned by the family of Moon Sun-myung - a significant Korean industrialist who is known for the Unification Church and his many commercial endeavors including the Washington Times. They also own a sushi purveyor and that explains the quality of the fish that they serve.  Moon died in 2012.

Sonobana is easily the best sushi that I've had outside of New York, San Francisco and Chicago. Their sushi menu is diverse and includes things you don't often see such as ankimo and awabe - uni is also available if you ask. For Americans who don't understand or appreciate tratditional nigiri sushi or sashimi there are also fru-fru rolls. My guests all enjoyed the dinner and the excellent service we received, I'm looking forward to my next visit.

Awesome place..... always hard to find a seat because it is always packed.  That's a good sign.  Food is very good!  The staff are good ole country folk that know how to cook, and know that country charm.  Will come out and sit and talk with you.......... go here weekly - especially Friday night for their awesome fish.  Sunday buffet is also great!
best cheesesteaks in the world!!! ate there many times. always good. keep going back Everytime I am in Philadelphia! you gotta try it if you haven't. you will love it.
