We went to Cody's yesterday for the first time and we were very impressed with our meal.
My wife ordered the bacon wrapped filet and I had the salmon. 
The price of the meal includes a soup or salad plus two sides. My wife ordered her filet medium and said "yummy" when she bit into her first piece. My salmon was cooked perfectly and I was happy with my selection. 
Overall a great dining experience and the owner/chef even stopped by our table to ask if everything was okay (that impressed the wifey)!
 If you haven't tried Cody's, let me recommend it to you.
Ive traveled the world, these are the best carne asda tacos.... on earth.  Ive been coming here for a decade and more than one location, and I will never stop while they are still servring
Great setting with multiple food options , a must go to if you are in the area . Indoor and outdoor seating and very clean !

Fantastic - our server Tabitha was on the ball!  So hats off to that superstar!  I had the pear and Gorgonzola pizza - yum!  Spousal unit had the Greek pizza - unbelievable!  We ordered the caipirinha and the aviator - the aviator was delicious and fresh.  So great service and great food - you know pizza, kind of like sex, even when it's not so good it's pretty good- but this is really good, memorable pizza!
Best Irish coffee on the planet, ask for Brent to make it! Awesome food too. Cool building that is over 200 years old!

Recently moved to NJ and ordered a King Cake to surprise my fiancé. I spoke to Cindy from the shipping department and she was incredibly friendly. The cake arrived fresh, well packaged, and even came with beads! We used to live down the street from Haydels and loved everything! We can't wait to come back and visit!

When this Verona location first opened my household ordered from here many times and the food and service was normally very good. Over time the food quality has dropped down and after our most recent burnt Stromboli, dry gyro platter and soggy salad, we are no longer customers.

Our experience started with us standing in line to order our meal for over 15 minutes.  This was not what we were expecting.  We should have researched more.  Meal felt expensive for 2 people.  It was almost $30.  We each had a burger and fries, I had a beer and my wife got a Diet Coke.  I had the Stromboli burger and only got through half of it.  Except for the sausage on top of the burger, there really was not taste to the burger.  I think the entire taste is based on what is on top of it.  The picnic table we sat at was very sticky because of thousands of times it's probably been wiped down. Noise level was high because of the high ceilings.  Again, that bothers us, but it might not be a big deal for others.  We were just expecting bigger things....

Loved this place. Service was excellent (and we had a party of 8).  The seasonal drinks were delicious and artfully prepared. Everyone at our table raved about their food. Fresh, skillfully prepared and presented beautifully. Portions seemed on the small side, but they were just right. We left happily sated and not uncomfortably stuffed. Would def go back and highly recommend.

Probably my favorite Chipotle location near me because the staff already knows my name and what I like to order, plus, since it's one of the newer locations, not that many people know about it so it's less crowded than the other Chipotle's I've been to.

This location is a bit difficult to find because it's not visible from the street and the only way to get here is by driving here so if you see the CVS, it's behind that.

Great service with great attitude and they don't skimp on the burritos. Most Chipotle's get 3-4 stars (unless it's the 86th St Chipotle in Brooklyn, that place sucks).

Parking: Lot
Price: $7+
Wait: Little to none

Husband and I wanted to just have dinner in town since we were kids free for the evening.  Didn't have a particular place in mind.  Walked around Doylestown and came across chambers 19 looked at the menu and it looked decent.  I wanted a steak and lucky it was steak night.  Went on a Wednesday evening so there wasn't a wait.  The flow was steady with patrons.  We sat in the dining room towards the back by a small window.  Our waitress was super nice and came over quickly to offer us drinks.  I ordered a lemonade and my husband a beer.  I was hoping for real lemonade but it was a mix.  She had to go remix the drink cause it was too sour.  I am not even sure what they used but I was turned off by the artificial lemonade.  We ordered the duck egg rolls and the crab bread.  Food came out pretty quick. Our waitress brought out the crab bread and told us that the cook JUST informed her that they are out of the duck egg rolls so we decided to just stick with the crab bread.  It was meh.  I wouldn't order it again.  The cheese dip was watery and the lump crab on top was only a few lumps.  Came with one roll of bread.  My husband ordered another beer that they had on their list.  Waitress came back saying that it was JUST tapped out.  That's 2 for 2. I ordered the ribeye special since it was steak night and my husband ordered the scallops and crab with wild rice and veggies.  It should of been called seafood swimming in butter gravy.  He usually eats anything and everything esp with butter but he didn't care for the meal at all.  My ribeye was decent.  I think 40% of it was fat that was discharged.  But it was cooked perfectly.  I didn't care for the mash potatoes or the veggies that came with it.  We didn't order dessert.  If you were to ask me for suggestions on where to eat in Doylestown, I would NOT recommend Chambers 19.  Sorry, not sorry.  Oh yeah there was an annoying gnat that would not leave us alone through out our entire dinner.  we looked like fools occasionally trying to eliminate the bug, but was never successful.

AMAZING BLOODY MARY/MARIA (vodka or tequila, pick your poison). I'll say it again AMAZING. The perfect amount of spicy. Service was fast and friendly. I would recommend a reservation unless you plan to get there EXACTLY when it opens. The piggy chips are good but add that white BBQ sauce and it was a spiritual experience. We considered eating there every morning. Really sad we didn't try the Bloody Mary to share but it's on the list for our next visit. Do yourself a favor and don't waste time waiting at another brunch place. This is the only one you need.

I am a vegan from Washington D.C and was so happy to find this place on a weekend getaway. I got the tacos and they were just amazing. My boyfriend ordered a noodle dish and they were also exceptional. The flavors are so yummy and unexpected in the best ways.

This is the best Thai food in the city! The service was great as well. Get the crispy duck pad thai and seafood curry. The prices might seem higher than a typical thai place, but its well worth it. The prawns were 5 inches long and the curry came with big pieces of scallop. This is the first place I ordered curry that came with more seafood than curry. Keep up the good job Chabaa Thai Bistro!

Wow, I tried to come here 4 times. Always a line out the door. I thought this meant it was exceptional?!?!
      Today, I made it in and ordered a small white and 3 wings hot with Cole slaw and beans. Hot flavor was greasy/ spicy and beans were sugary . The Cole slaw had someones hair in it as a bonus flavor enhancer, they were very nice and refunded us, great customer service, BUT-Done.... never again!

The Squeeze In restaurant is a lovely place, whose walls are etched with the ghosts of past visitors from years ago. Any doubts about the quality of the food or service are quickly dismissed by reading some of the stories from satisfied customers who felt the need to make their mark on the restaurant's walls, following the tradition that has become a regular part of the experience with this establishment. Excellent service, great food, and mediocre coffee, made better with creamer and sugar.  The ambiance is great and could not be more comfortable, accompanied by furniture that makes the restaurant look like you're back at home, and your parents are doing the cooking.

I know this place is very known around Tampa Bay but for me was a total disappointment. The bread was way too toasted, the black bean soup almost looked like someone opened a can of beans and put it on a plate, it was too thick with zero liquid, the main dish was also average and the waiter was either too busy or preoccupied since it took a while to get a hold of him. The highlight was the Sangria. 

Perhaps I'm a bit more strict with my "Spanish food" but both me and my friend agreed we would choose a Spanish whole in a wall type of restaurant with better prices and less decor first.

Let's start with the positive. They seated us quickly despite how busy they were at the time. The Moscow Mule was the BEST I have ever had. Just so good.

Now, the rest. The food was only so-so. We didn't have anything worth mentioning. We were disappointed. The service was lacking. It seemed like we were a hassle. Apparently our presence was an inconvenience. 

I wanted to LOVE this place, but it just didn't happen. I would return for some drinks and to socialize, but it wouldn't be a spot to dine again.

Horrible food and service. Every Shareable we ordered was dry. The wings were overcooked and extremely dry. The fingers steak were  more like dehydrated meat nuggets.  The pretzel was over cooked and the queso tasted what a locker room smells like. And last not least the floating stuff in the pitcher of Blue Moon. Just telling the truth. It was 50 bucks I wish I could have spent elsewhere.

Ybor- Sunday dinner: Cabernet, Sanctuary my love affair has begun...salad with bleu cheese crumbles, pine nuts with a lovely vinaigrette and then tortellini carbonara, perfect! My cousin had the veal lasagna, not a drop left... Needless to say, I'll return. Agree on their bread, it's terrible but the ambiance is lovely even with the football game on. Btw- thank you Sam, you were lovely as well!

I had lunch a Super Cuca's today. There was a customer who decided to give is a loud and protracted political rant and would not stop.  After 10 minutes of a ruined lunch I asked the manager help us enjoy our lunch. Failure to intervene ruined my experience. I understand this is not "fine dining" place but a modicum of peace is expected.

**I want to start off by saying I was here in June.  Looking at the other reviews, it appears they may have worked out some of the kinks.**

I was so disappointed by Hearth.  I was planning a day out in New Hope and wanted to find a restaurant that offered a lot of vegetarian options.  The Health menu looked interesting, so I was excited to try it out.  I got the Roman Cambodian sandwich. First, the sandwich was tiny; barely a lunch portion. The description said there was an aioli on the sandwich, but did not taste anything.  The Nicoise salad my boyfriend got had not a drop of dressing.  

We were the only customers on the second floor and the entire time a woman kept coming up to put glasses away in a cupboard that was right behind us.  She obviously could have waited until we were gone, it was really uncomfortable.

Omg the best pad Thai I have ever had! This place has amazing reviews and I can definitely see why. They are also open for takeout during these difficult times which I am so thankful for! Will be coming back here again want to try everything on the menu my picky boyfriend also loved this place as well :)

I was in New Orleans for work for about two weeks. My co-worker friend and I made a list of places and things we definitely wanted to try. When it came to Frenchman street, we were looking for a place with good food and music. You would think this is an easy task for a the famous music filled street in the notorious foodcentric town. Most bars that have live bands do not serve food, if they do, it's bar food. (avoid Snug Harbor, what a waste of a meal) After more than a week of everything fried, my LA self just couldn't handle it anymore. We read about Three Muses and decided to give it a try. 
The first time we attempted to come here was on a Friday night. We didn't get to the restaurant until 10:30 or so. The hostess (Andrea) was very sweet, but told us they just couldn't fit us in and the kitchen was closing. She offered to put us down for the next night. We reworked our schedule and arrived on Saturday around 6pm. The place was already packed, waiting for the band to start. Andrea told us we would have to wait so we decided to get a drink at the bar and try the pickle chips, which were REALLY good. We were seated at a table shortly and the food came very quickly after we ordered. The lobster egg rolls were my favorite. The flavor was good, but not overpowering the lobster meat inside. The shrimp with polenta cake was slightly salty for my taste, but the flavor was still great, especially with the slaw and fresh strawberries. My friend (vegetarian) had the bulgolgi bowl and the Mac n' Cheese. I have to say the bulgogi bowl really was a miss. If you have had any decent type of Korean food, you know bulgogi comes in a clay bowl, the rice is crispy from baking in the oven and the dish is topped with layers of veggies and kimchi. This bowl came with a couple slices or friend tofu, a tiny amount of flavorless spinach and two pieces of kimchi and the rice was cold. This is the only reason I'm giving the place 4 stars. The mac n' cheese was amazingly rich though! 

The atmosphere was lively but not obnoxious. The wait staff/bartenders were busy but very helpful and friendly. The music was the cake topper, it made our entire dinner more enjoyable. While we were there, a cute little old man walked around offering portrait drawings. He was so cute I decided to get one. I'm very happy with the result and it will be a nice memory of my New Orleans experience. 

In summery, this was one of the best meals we had in town, in a perfect New Orlean setting. Go early, grab a table and enjoy your evening!

This is tough to write, 
The last time we visited, I and my two teens ordered all you can eat lunch.  The quality of food seems to be going down.  I started to notice after the ownership and name change, but I gave it a few chances.  The service was still good with refills of drinks, happy helpful chefs and staff, and somewhat speedy delivery of the sushi.  What turned me off, in addition to the lower quality throughout most the meal, was the last roll we ordered was a bit ammonia, and fishy smelling and one bite told the story.  Luckily I did not get sick due to stopping after the first bite and not swallowing.  My daughter did get a bite down before we noticed and did not feel well.  I just can't bring myself to go back.  I know All You Can Eat is a Reno institution, but maybe I have finally leaned my lesson.  More is not better, quality is worth the price.  

One more side note, the cucumber salad even seems old and wilted. 

I don't like posting things like this but It had to be said.  

I have had better luck buying my own ingredients lately and making the sushi at home.  I purchased a sushi Bazooka a few years ago.  Sometimes, I use the poke from costco, to make salmon and tuna rolls, sometimes I buy tempura shrimp to make SF rolls.  I cut all the veggies thin, make or buy all the sauces required and have all the sides ready.  It is a ton of work, but I know the quality of what I am putting in the roll.  

I will go try other places again but this turned me off local sushi for a while.

I love this bar so much - really, I just want to wrap it up, check it with my luggage and take it everywhere I go.

First, the insides are very fetching - the wall covered in mirrors of all shapes and sizes always gets my attention... there's something about the Oyster Bar that gives it this vintage Parisian feel, and I think that the stylistically-haphazard display of mirrors might be a big part of it. 

Then there's the cocktail program... I mean, c'mon - a limoncello mule? You had me at first glance of your copper mug.

But most of all, I like this bar because it's easy. So many things in life are difficult, but our downtime shouldn't be. So rest easy and know that the perfect date place really does exist. That neighborhood bar you haven't yet found? You can stop searching; you have arrived. A special somewhere where time doesn't exist and you'll never overstay your welcome?

World, meet your 'just one more' - as it turns out, the nightcap is very much alive and well.
Amazing burger!!! The service was very good we ordered the fig burger according to the waiters recommended and it was wowwwww!!!

I visited from out of town, thinking it was going to be this great local farmers market in small-town PA, but after asking for directions from the very friendly gentleman at the college information center, I arrived at this red barn with high hopes, only to enter a rural version of Whole Foods. There was nothing really spectacular about this market. I credit them for offering unique gourmet sauces and fresh produce that I'm sure was procured locally and the wide variety of gardening supplies and plants on the patio. I looked like a dope browsing the sparse aisles, searching on my phone for the quickest way out of there. Maybe I missed out on what the rest of the market was supposed to be, but for what I saw, I was very disappointed.
Love this place! The best oysters and service from Nairobi, Tasha and Ryan!!! Amazing in the Quarter!!

Beignets.

That's all you need to know. Just do it. It's a must to make a pilgrimage here when in the Big Easy. It's sacrilege if you don't.

Those sugary doughy puffs of powdery goodness are magical. Along with cups of delicious cafe au lait. Sure, it's a tourist spot, but it's part of New Orleans history. Have a seat and take it all in.

Oh, and we were here pre-covid so we got to have a real experience. Take all those giving bad reviews who visited during the pandemic shutdown with a grain of salt. It's not the same.

I haven't tried everything from their menu, but there hasn't been a thing I haven't like yet.  They have a wide range of food as part of their menu.  It's not just a snack shop.  Certain orders can be meals by themselves.  And they also have these yummy desserts!  

I love their spam musubi - the regular, super, and katsu.  The spam by itself is salty, but having it with the rice just balance it out perfectly.  The mochi nori fried chicken? A meal in itself and totally worth the $8. Perfectly spiced fried chicken bits, two scoopfuls of rice, delicious mac salad, and this wonderful sauce drizzled on.  Their various butter mochi - I've only had the chocolate and coconut ones so far - has a good balance on sweetness and chocolate/coconut.  The fried donuts (without the holes, and more ball-shaped) also have a hint of saltiness.  

Also, their congee (rice porridge) and peppermint hot chocolate w/ marshmallows are perfect to warm you up this winter season.  They won't be around this coming January, but catch them at The Porch this February!
3 of 7 workers wore masks..  i turned and walked out! are you kidding me!!! we are in a pandemic and chinese restaurant doesn't care about safety??!!! do not support this business!

Great food truck. 

The service is great and quirky. Since they make the food on the spot it does take a while (approximately 10 minutes) to be served. Other than that great. Their menu switches up frequently, so no telling what they will have in store. Make sure to follow them on twitter @guerillastreet because that's the best way to find out their locations. I had a Adobo burrito, it was very filling!
Lots of activities, beautiful vibe, looks like little mexico vacation spot. Lots of parking, beautiful design
Excellant food. Great service! Big portions. I had a gyro that I had to eat with a fork too big to pick up.

We  don't live in the area, but happened to be nearby and found this spot on Yelp.  I had Eggs Florentine and it was very good.  Expertly cooked poached eggs on buttered muffin with lemony hollandaise.  Husband had Greek Omelette which he also liked, although his was cooked a bit more than he prefers.  On Sunday morning the place was rockin' with families with children and I enjoyed the loud, lively atmosphere.  Service as outstanding!  Constant hot coffee and attention.  One thing that I appreciate is that the portion sizes here are reasonable and perfectly sized, not the huge plates of food often served at breakfast that often results in waste.

This place is amazing. Simple menu with the freshest ingredients I've had at a Vietnamese restaurant. We will definitely become regulars here. I can't even describe how flavorful the meat in the pork bao was, absolute perfection! The bread on the bahn mi was hot and crisp fresh out of the oven. The pho broth was robust and savory as it should be.
One of my wife's and my favorite new restaurants! The 12 Cheese Chicken Mac and Cheese is great!
Delicioso!   Got the special rosemary waffle Benedict and it was Phenomenal. Service was good.  I'd definitely go back.

This is by far the best Sushi joint in St. Louis. The sushi is out of this world good. I just moved here from California and let me tell you how mush sushi I have tried. This particular location is by far the best I have ever had. The sushi is so tasty and full with flavor it's unbelievable. Super fresh, so much goodness to comprehend. They have an all you can eat, as long as you finish it, for $20. What can you ask for more? I remember in California about 4 rolls, plus appetizer, and drink would be close to $100 per person, this place has redefined purchasing of sushi. LOVE LOVE LOVE. I've been here 50 plus times and took me this long to write a review. (Shame in me)

was going to eat there today i seen they had good reviews on here, so i thought it would be good, it might have been good but they were out of half of thier items, not really a way to run a business, I've worked food all my life and a trip to the grocery store would of fixed that, i guess making new customers is not worth it tho.
Damn it. Wanted them to succeed.

Typical townie bar.  Thankfully it's huge so you don't feel too packed in.

Cheap food, made cheaply.

The best part is that the drinks are cheap!  And there are a ton of TVs, so it's the perfect place to go watch a game but nothing more than that.

I have gone to Gino's twice now and the first time it was just okay, nothing memorable.  The second time I couldn't even eat the food and was $20 for nothing.  The Alfredo had zero flavor and the noodles tasted like what you'd get from a box.  My friend sent back her food and didn't seem to get any sort of remorse from the staff.  Our waiter was nice however.  As an actual Italian myself, I don't get why everything thinks this is the real deal but alas for people around this area who don't know better its not.  Personally I think Olive Garden is better and that's saying a lot.

Went there for the dosa. Tried the maysoor masala dosa which was on point. Chicken 65 was good as well. Went again few days later and tried the chicken dosa and the pani puri. Both were good. The staff is super friendly. This will be my go to spot for dosa fix.
Long wait but worth it.  Hidden gem.  HUGE oysters.  Very local.  Lots of mud which makes it pretty authentic (i guess).  Good place to take people from out of town to have a local feel.

Service and food were great 
We sat at the bar add nd the girl working the bar was right on point we had raw oysters which were delicious than we had a new york strip cooked perfect and great flavor atmosphere and service great

We have been longtime diners at the Belleville location and really enjoy dining there, but the new Clinton Hills location needs some time to gel.  We dined there yesterday around 11:15 am and had a mixed experience.  Service was fine.  I ordered the Thai Chicken Salad and it was very good.  My wife ordered a Vito Corleone pizza with pepperoni and sausage.  There must have been a fire at the meat supplier, because there was a paucity of meats on this poor Vito.  Server had disappeared.  Wife took the pizza over to the bar to ask about the meat shortage.  They remade the pizza.  The guy at the bar said the pizza cook was from the Belleville location so how could the pizzas be so different.  The server told my wife that the cook was new, but the kitchen manager was from the Belleville location.  The remade pizza was up to spec!  I suggest that someone act as Manager at Clinton Hill, because no one was in charge on Sunday.  Now, I will sound grouchy: There is a large table as you walk into the dining area.  It was occupied by three generations of one family.  This must have been the Loud Family.  We could barely hear each other above the cacophony, particularly with kids who lacked "inside" voices.  I wish they would put that table way back in a corner so families can caterwaul without disturbing others.  And the music in the dining area was more bar music than dining music. Sorry to be a grouch.

NEVER AGAIN..I ordered a whole pizza steak and repeated it twice because the guy was so short on the phone. I get there and the woman said a whole cheesesteak?  I said "No" pizza steak extra sauce on the side. She tells the grill boy and he is fired up. Get this, as I stood at the counter, he unrolled the cheesesteak and put it back on the grill. 
Are you freaking kidding me???? I said, "No freaken way, I ain't taking that steak" and started  walking out. The grill boy with a beard said "That isn't your steak, we're making you a new one!" Really? So someone else is getting that fucked up steak? This is the difference from a Philly steak and a self voted "Best cheesesteak in South Jersey" it's a joke. I just feel sorry for the people who don't venture out of area and think their steak is legit. It's eatable at best, not even travel worthy. Hey guys, keep serving your steak-umms, we all need hang over food....

One of my favorites. I used to love coming here to get work done or even read. Big windows, lots of tables, annd outlets galore. The coffee was good. The drinks Ive tried have always been delicious. The ambiance - just perfect. Loved sitting here at night - bright lights, big tables, just the right background music. Open till 10 pm. Plus less crowded in the evening hours.
 I love my coffee shops and this is def one of them.

Outstanding! My family and I were staying in a hotel nearby. It was raining so we needed something close. Nomad was a half block away. The pizza is incredible. Everyone will talk about the thin and crispy pizza. I want to talk about the incredible flavors. We had two different pies and each was so flavorful. The deserts are just as good. Many great beer choices and a full bar. So happy we were forced to stay close due to rain.

I came with pretty high expectations, but was a bit disappointed. I got a recommendation of the Pork Chop la Place, a hefty $32.00, which I was told was their best offering. Andouille stuffed double cut smoked pork chop... pretty great sounding. While it looked amazing, it also looked to be a meal for at least 2 people. I ate probably less than a third of it, and being there for business, wasn't able to save it and eat later. Sides were not even that great, and server seemed a bit annoyed or frustrated by some allergies at our table. For a hefty price tag, this definitely left me wanting more.

Excellent in every aspect!
Everyone is sooo friendly & sooo helpful!
The menu is very extensive & great choices for everyone 
We  all had excellent delicious meals
Service is excellent 
Food is 10 stars 
Highly recommend this gem of a restaurant

I have been waiting to try this place for a while. I always stare at the menu of the Whole Foods location (which is now gone :( ) and think to myself, one day I'll make it over to the full menu location. So, I finally had an excuse! Given that it was a cold day, I opted for the ramen, but because I don't eat pork I couldn't get their standard ramen. They told me I could substitute the meat but if the broth is pork-based it kind of defeats the purpose. So I went for the brisket option. I honestly thought that I did not get my money's worth. Sure, there was a lot of food but taste-wise it just wasn't cutting it for me. I thought that the broth was lacking an umami flavor and the cuts of the brisket were MUCH fattier than I was expecting. I thought that they tried to make up for the lack of the umami flavor by drowning it in unnecessary spice. Don't get me wrong, I love some spice, but I don't appreciate when they are using it to cover up for something else. I think for all my noodle needs I'll stick to the places in China town and South Philly that I know best (and/or my own kitchen) to get that ramen that I'm still craving.

The food was mediocre at best. Black bean soup? Talk about black bean POOP. D-I-S-G-U-S-T-I-N-G!!!!!!!!! SO DISAPPOINTED YOU GUYS. Plus, the TABLES. Don't even get me started on the tables. They're wobbly as earthquakes. Don't recommend. -10 our of 10 y'all. And that's not good. Thecookies were dry too.
Wonderful place. Love the atmosphere but the food is even better. There are options for many different diet types including vegetarian and vegan.

I will start off by saying that without a doubt the food here is really good. If you want something a little bit more elevated than classic American brunch, the food delivers in both presentation and taste. The biscuits are buttery, flakey, and come with really delicious spreads that compliment the flavor of each biscuit perfectly, and is very good for sharing with the table. 

For sweet, I love the lemon ricotta pancakes. They are fluffy and creamy without being heavy, and the homemade compote is tart and sweet. The savory shrimp and grits come with a bed of arugula that make them pretty and also lighten up the buttery grits. The sausage and shrimp are cooked so that the inside is tender but the outside is crispy, and the onion and pepper really make the whole thing rounded aesthetically and taste-wise. The seating is adorable; both inside and outside seating make you seek like you're in a little secret café in the countryside, very homey and intimate, but still casual. 

The service is god-awful. Honestly so terrible that every time I want to go back so that I can order the shrimp and grits, I decide maybe it's not worth it. I've been three times, thinking maybe it's just a fluke but there's no going around it: the service was abhorrent each time, for a laundry list of different reasons each time. One waitress forgot to bring out one of our plates, then insisted that the person had never ordered--which seems like doubling down on a frankly stupid mistake. She begrudgingly put his order in and it came out well after or party was done eating. In the same visit, she forgot our mimosas. When at the end we decided not to have them, since they never came out, she got huffy about it! All to finally be insulted when we didn't want the candy at the end because she'd "brought us extra to make up for it." Candy is no substitute for never getting your food or drinks. The second time I went was just standard bad service, from forgetting condiments to never checking in or refilling water or coffee. The third time was the same as the second, except so bad that this time we actually got up and got our own ketchup from another table and had to walk up, ask for our bill, and pay at the register, since our waitress brought our food and never came back. Then when we were finishing or drinks and just generally trying to enjoy breakfast (still had food!), they asked if they could take half our table, two put together when we got there, since a bigger party was coming and we'd already paid. We would've been done in ten minutes, and had waited double that to be seated. So two stars for the food. It's great. Order it to go, or go to the hundreds of other superior brunch places in the area. You can find food just as good, with service that far outshines this place's.

If you love the smoked barbeque taste, then Sonny's is the place for you. Sliced or pulled beef or chicken. Delicious sweet tea and a salad bar that goes with any meal. One of my favorite restaurants in Ruskin area.
The tacos were very good; the homemade tortillas were a nice touch.  The service was very friendly and accommodating.  The fried ice cream was different, but delicious!!!

Love their steaks and their fries. Just had them a week ago. I was surprised to hear they deliver. Took them up on it.  They were so cute quick and its delivery. Everything arrived hot and delicious. I also liked that you can pick what kind of cheese you want and though they normally do slab steak, you can ask them to chop it which is how I like it.

Our party called in advance, 5 days in advance. Was told to speak to Anthony only.  We spoke to Anthony,followed up with Anthony and confirmed with his team. Our party arrived at our scheduled time only to be told that we can not guarantee you will have a table at your set time. 1.5 hours later we were sat.

 My dish was below average. I had the Mahi Mahi dish. It was extremely dry and bland. Several people ordered crab and they were pleased and The crab and lobster that  I tasted was very good.
Service staff is hilarious.  God was great also. Would recommend this place. Line looks like a long wait.  We were about 40th in line. Waited 15 min. They have it down to a science
Finally. Good chinese food in Stl. Steamed entrees and moo-shu were amazing. Very fast delivery!!! Will be my weekly go-to!!

We have eaten here a few times as it is close to our house.  . We love the Mackerel Sushi. So nice and oily. The Korean Seafood Pancake is killer. We will get one to go just so we have more to share at home. The wait staff and Sushi Guys are very nice and take pride in the Sushil they serve. The best is the Mackeral along with the White Tuna Sushi. Like Butta!!  
 We go at lunch mostly. I like lunch prices and this lunch menu is varied so you can choose from Japanese and Korean. You can't miss either way. Bento Boxes are available at lunch. Never had one but have seen then and they look pretty bland. 
   We will return over and over again. Five Stars!!!!!

This is really a nice restaurant with an interesting menu. I love that it has vegetarian options for those who seek to eat a plant based diet. I would give it five stars if it weren't for two issues we encountered on our last visit. First, the spicy cauliflower rice dish was TOO spicy. I mean I like spice, but this was challenging even for me. The dish was great otherwise. Ask the chef to dial it down and you won't be disappointed. Second, the small  Israel couscous stuffed squash was a tad lonely looking on the plate even on the bed of greens. You might consider ordering a side dish if you're hungry as you'll be too tempted to get desert and undo to benefit of eating plant based in the first place.

Brand new Burger King just opened today 12/26/17! Being brand new it's very nice. Of course, it's clean, the staff are very nice, and just like other BKs the food is good. It was nice and cozy on this cold winter day, because they had the heat on unlike most fast food restaurants do. It's also quite roomy in this BK compared to most of the newer BKs. Can see my family & I revisiting this BK again.

Yes!  24 hour place downtown and they serve food!  Did not eat, but had a fun time here (but they need to fix the right gun on the hunting video game).  Decent band, jovial bartender, free pool.  The $6 pictcher of PBR was a pretty smaill pitcher but still a decent deal.

Bought the Groupon and checked it out...Crawfish Po'boy (only available on Saturdays)  was pronounced excellent by my son and everyone loved the Fried Chicken. Strip mall location on Watson Road never would have found without the Groupon but would definitely go back to try other things.

We stoped by on Friday afternoon, there are 4 tables include us at that time but the food and services is terrible. The spring roll is too big and too much bean sprout in there, which rice paper could not completely cover. They also serve the spring roll with plastic wrap on it? . I I ordered noodle with grill beef and egg roll but the beef looks rare. I left all the beef. Last but not least, the server forgot bring our water and did not check out us anytime during our dinner.

Joanie's to Go is your best option for delivery in the Soulard area.   They have decent homemade pizza (thick and thin) and are best known for their Margherita pizza.  They carry all of the casual St. Louis Italian standards like toasted ravs (not  my thing, but hey), a variety of salads, appetizers, sandwiches, etc.  I'm not a vegetarian, but after sampling their veggie lasagna at a catered event, I'm hooked.  Spinach and red sauce don't sound like a good combo to me, but this dish is awesome!.  The roast beef sandwich is really good, as well.

We've eaten at Chili Mac's Diner twice this week because the food and service are outstanding. The prices are very reasonable especially for being located in the heart of downtown St. Louis. The breakfast is great and the chili is some of the best I've had at a restaurant. Great value, great food, great service!

The search for a great creperie in America continues...

I had hopes for Le Cafe Creperie to be more authentic but I was quickly dismayed. Upon entering the restaurant you see the workers there making crepes right in the center of the restaurant and some small tables all around. I love Paris and French things but the decor was even a bit tacky for me (not to mention the overly instrumental "French" music and La vie en rose...) 

Moving on from that... I came with a few friends to try a few of the savory and sweet crepes. My biggest thing is that I have yet to see a restaurant create a proper savory buckwheat crepe and when I saw it was an option on the menu to have a buckwheat crepe for $1 extra, my heart rejoiced! (Gluten-free friends, you too, can have a gluten-free crepe for $1 extra too)
Typically, people here use the same batter for savory and sweet crepes and that's just not right!! I ordered a crepe Breton with chicken, arugula, and almonds and wasn't totally wowed by the experience. The buckwheat crepe was wholly not what I thought it would be; it actually made my crepe more like a pancake than the thinner regular crepes. It was alright... the flavor was a bit lacking. My friends ordered simpler crepes such as Le Parisien, baked ham with jam and too much, overpowering, Herbes de Provence. 

The sweet crepes were pretty nice. The crepe sampler was a cute idea but it was more whipped cream and fruit than it was crepe... But the real winner of this Sunday brunch was the Crepe Suzette - shoutouts to Yelp reviewers for pointing this out. This is the real deal!! Very tasty and not too sweet for crepe slathered in orange marmalade. 

All in all, if you want to grab some sweet or savory crepes, there's a spot in town now. Sweet crepes are quite good but savory crepes leave something to be desired. It's a tad pricey for me but it is on par for crepes overall.
The food was amazing and worth the wait. The Robster was incredible. The service was amazingly friendly and efficient despite the long wait for the table.

As an old fishtales regular I've been waiting for this place to open for awhile. Got the blackened fish tacos, asked for no pico or jalapeños. First of all they forgot the cheese and secondly the coleslaw left the grilled tortillas soggy when they came out. Fries were good, except the soggy ones sitting in cole slaw juice. Also took 40 mins to get my order. Was very disappointed. Also thought it was a little rude being that I sat 4ft right in front of the tiki bar on the bar top along the handrail, every time I ordered a drink I had to get up and ask, and the bartender would call me over to get it instead of walking his lazy ass 5ft over to give it to me, once while I had my hands full of food. He did the same thing when the check was ready also, "here you go bub". Very poor service. Hipster looking guy with hat on backwards with glasses.

Prior to this coming here, I had only ever been to the Acme in the French Quarter. The only reason we came to this one at all was because our flight arrived before another member of our party, so we came here which is reasonably close to the airport to kill time. The location is different in that it's more like a Friday's than the other one. But it's still cute. Checkered tables and definitely not as loud. 

We got some beers and they come in a huge goblet. They're also dirt cheap so I could sti there for hours just drinking beer and knocking back oysters. Every one of us ordered a dozen chargrilled oysters. We were sat right next to the kitchen so we could see them make it. I guess the cook saw how much we liked them so he made us a special tiny batch made with a different smoked chipotle Tabasco. Southern hospitality for ya. 

We liked them so much, we ended up ordering a dozen of his special oysters. I'm pretty sure we wouldn't get that special treatment in the popular location, cause it's so busy, so we were really grateful. We tried to go back on the way to our return flights home but it was noonish and it was PACKED. 

Everyone I was with seemed to think it was better than the French Quarter one, though those oysters were meatier. So definitely check it out if you're in the area.

Only Cuban restaurant in the New Orleans area, but it is the place I'd go even if there were others. The food tastes better than the Carreta in Miami. Though I wish they buttered the Cuban bread. They even have Materva.

Authentic and delicious. We had the goulash and Romanian cabbage rolls and they were outstanding. We shared the fried zucchini and eggplant and the creamy mushrooms which were extremely flavorful. We ended up ordering the Romanian doughnuts to go because we were so full and they did not disappoint! Cozy atmosphere and friendly staff!

Did not like to be greeted with someone yelling "did you order yet". You have to stand at the counter and hope someone sees you. Mom ordered a turkey club, it was 6 ins high on 3 slices of rye bread and not cut in half. Impossible to hold or bite into. Asked the not so friendly waitress if she could have it cut in half. Sandwich had to be taken apart so you could eat it. A turkey club is cut into quarters anywhere you go in the USA. It's rare someone complains about a sandwich being to big. A turkey club should be able to be eaten as served. My Jewish Cheesesteak was delish. Mostly self service. Tables to small.

Worst service ever. I think the staff was high. It took forever to place a drink order and even longer to place our dinner order. When my dinner arrived the chicken was raw. I had to get up from the table to get the waitress to address the issue. She assured me a new plate was in the oven and would be right out. It never ever came. I never ate and the staff was clueless. If I could give zero stars i would

Part 2: they sent my dinner home with me: see the photo of the Chicken foot with CLAWS that they included. This place should be shut down

Wow, someone said the service was friendly? I don't think I've met such bad bar staff. Obnoxious would be the word. Anyway, Limeys or whatever it's called now, became an American Sports Bar many years ago. Food bad, beer so so, staff dreadfull. I understand its under new management, hopefully they can see how run down this great old pub/restaurant has become over the last few years, and bring it back to a real traditional drinking establishment!!

My wife & I went there for a birthday lunch and had some vegetarian dishes (falafel wrap and pita with hummus and baba ganoush). The food was absolutely amazing (their spicy sauce was REALLY spicy and tasty) and the hosts are very friendly. The lunch was capped with a chocolate pudding shared between us, which was one of the best desserts I have had. 

Will I come back and try their chicken/lamb dishes sometime? ABSOLUTELY.

I would gladly recommend this place to anyone who asks me about a Mediterranean place.

I just had the most perfectly cooked extra cheesy burger with sautéed mushrooms & onions!  It was awesome!  No wonder they won at the Burger Showdown!  I love this local joint and their staff!  They always make us feel like family!!!  Everything on the menu is delicious!!

Moved from Seattle to St. Louis with a definite apprehension about the food scene here relative to the PNW. This place definitely gives me hope that St. Louis can hold it's own. 

Had one of the best Bi bim baps I've eaten in some time plus a smoothie that was lights out. Space is also pretty cool. Keep up the great work guys!

I usually avoid pan- Asian restaurants as they rarely have good, authentic food in all of the styles.  Sams is the rare exception. I went here with my family after finding another restaurant nearby was too busy on Father's Day. I'm so happy we did! As others have mentioned, the roti canai is very tasty and the fried rice noodles and rice with chicken and salted fish was yummy too.  We also tried the salmon sushi roll and sashimi which was fresh and excellent quality- better even than some of our other restaurant staples.  We will absolutely be returning!

I finally joined yelp today since I've been mooching off of the reviews for a while now and felt it was time to be a good person and give back instead of just take take take.  Most of the reviews on yelp (in San Francisco) have been pretty accurate.  This one does not fall into that category!  I was visiting a friend who just moved to SB and we yelped fish restaurants and this is the one we chose to go to.

One star for the beautiful view of the harbor.  The food was absolutely terrible - we should have known what we were getting ourselves into after being in what seemed like the most touristy part of Santa Barbara (we were the only people not wearing fanny packs taking pictures of everything in sight).  Clam chowder was the worst I ever had, shrimp wasn't even seasoned in both the shrimp dishes we ordered.  

They will prob never go outta business b/c of their location and naive tourists will def dine there (we did).
One of our favorite places! Best egg flour soup in Tucson!! We have tried a few different entrees and appetizers and they are all delicious! Fast and friendly service!
Definitely something to go and see while in New Orleans. No longer get the glass to take home with your drink.

I took my boyfriend here for his birthday dinner and it was incredible, both service and food.  We started off with the Alaskan king crab  and half a dozen oysters from the cold bar.  The crab came with two legs, with half of the shell perfectly sliced off.  All you had to do was just peel the meat off the bottom half of the shell. Hands down the most convenient and delicious crab I have ever had.  Feel free to spritz some fresh lemon and cocktail sauce on it

As for the raw oysters? Amazing.We had three from east coast and three from west,all of which were fresh and juicy. Their vinaigrette was amazing.  No buck a shuck here though :(

Crab cake was pretty good, except I don't care for crab cakes so I don't have anything fair to say.  Birthday boy devoured them so that says enough.  It came with 2 generous lumps of crab meat with very few of this corn meal filler nonsense most other places try to pull off.  It was perfectly seared and was super juicy.  I would say this is a must if you are a crab cake lover. Not to mention it came with avocados.

There is also a complimentary Gruyere and chive bread (puff) that is so freakin' good. It's so soft and fluffy and with their whipper butter... so damn good.

Lobster bisque was great.  Rich, creamy, and a chuck of lobster meat or two with every bite.  Generous portion too for only $15.  I would say it' close to 12 fl oz.

The steaks, were just wow.  First, you get to chose your own cutting knife.They had 4 or 5 to choose from, which is super cool.  The steaks were grilled to perfection and very tender.  You can cut the steak with a spoon. The 24 oz 29-day aged porterhouse was amazing.  It was well seasoned and very flavorful.  The 12 oz filet migon was also delicious, but not quite as flavorful. The cut was very thick, so only the outer portion was bursting with flavor and the inner portion just melts in your mouth.  I could definitely get used this.  

We also got two sides:  sauteed mushrooms and butterball potatoes (pretty much just fancy home fries) with garlic aioli, both of which were great compliments to the juice velvety steaks we had.

We also had a bottle of red wine (Camino de Navaherreros) which was amazing.

The hazelnut bread pudding was amazing.  It was warm, moist, and very fluffy. It came with warm cream on the side and you pour it onto the plate.  

The service was amazing.  The table was constantly kept clean and water and wine glass were always well attended to.  

Perfect everything!
Seriously best pizza ever. If you have never been here you HAVE to stop in. The service was excellent. The staff was all smiles. Pizza is cooked to perfection. Toppings, fresh, the bomb.

So when you have a picky eater in the family you tend to frequent places they will eat. This isn't the case here, we all love this Red Robin. I've been to some where the service is sub par but here, we are definitely welcomed. Our food always comes out hot and fresh. I try to get something different every time and I have yet to get something I haven't absolutely loved. You can tell this is a well ran establishment....we have coming here at least monthly since moving here a year ago and that's saying something for us. Well done to this Red Robin.

This is the most normal meal I've gotten to eat in the last 5 months. 

They allowed us to have the all you can eat salad bar.  We were just requested to wear gloves at the salad bar with our masks,  they provided disposable gloves and brought us plates and bowls.  

We got to have a booth all to ourselves,  and the one behind and next to us were corded off so easy 6 feet between people.  

The staff was super friendly.  
They wore masks. 
And gloves. 

It was a completely delightful visit.  
I missed it so much.  
They made coming back so totally worth every penny.

I was surprisingly impressed with this place and not sure why I didn't try it sooner. I stopped here on a weekend afternoon for takeout and it was pretty packed, and again surprised by this. It smelled delicious inside and although I didn't try the pizza, the pizza I was eying up on other peoples tables looked so good. I only ordered a meatball sandwich, cheese fries, and a garden salad. The meatball parm sandwich was delicious. The roll was slightly crispy, just how I liked, and still had a good amount of cheese. (I hate when anywhere skimps on the cheese). The cheese fries were steak fries which I didn't know before ordering and was so glad I ordered them because I love steak fries. The cheese was just a cheese whiz but good enough, although could have used a little more. The house salad was standard and fresh. I didn't wait too long for my order to be ready either, despite the business of the place. I can't wait to come back here, and I definitely will, and try the rest of their food and see if it meets my expectations from this takeout order.
Onto dessert with pastry from Cafe du Monde.  Staff was great and beignets were not dry like some other experiences I had.  It's cheap, but not to die for.

Wonderful ambiance with cloth napkins soft lighting interesting decor with  well stocked and beautiful bar. Best shrimp and grits I've had in a long time..not runny and just enough spice with ample shrimp sausage and peppers. Husband had perfectly cooked steak and potato. Large side salad with homemade vinegarette and soft bread with pesto. Wait staff attentive but not overbearing. Prices reasonable and portions large. We will be coming back and bringing friends and family

Really good restaurant. One of the best in Santa Barbara. Hands-down they serve GREAT food!  It is very fresh. Plus, they gave a good cross section of choices. And, they have very reasonable prices. 

This restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating. The tables and booths are well-spaced and the atmosphere (both inside and out) is open and airy. 

They serve both beer and wine. They have a nice selection of local wines and microbrewery brews, plus some very good non-alcohol based drinks. 

There is a couple of things to keep in mind about this restaurant, however. Depending on who's at the helm, taking orders, this can really effect your initial experience here. Some staff are very good, some not. Meaning some take a lot of time to do a simple job. I have experience both, so you may experience an unnecessary wait to order. The other thing to think about is that they just have one restroom for men and one for women. These restrooms are often occupied by the locals who sneak in though the side door to use it, so there may be a line. 

Overall, Silvergreens is one of SB's best casual dining experiences.
Stopped for ice cream for our granddaughters. Just two small vanilla cups. This was really really good ice cream. Had never been here but certainly will be back.

A little more than your typical corner pizza joint.  Along with the staple items, this place opens early enough for breakfast, offer delicious, home made desserts, and both Greek and Italian items.  Be warned!  Their pizza slices are large enough to use as a sail!  Seriously!  Biggest slices in the city!!

This is usually our fall back spot for office happy hours.  It's almost always a large group, so the size of F&H makes sense.  They carry a lot of games, which is nice.  But that's about where the compliments end.

The service is slow.  The food is bad.  And the crowd noise can get overwhelming.

Unfortunately, your options for sports bars downtown are limited.

First time from out of town, and I had a great overall experience. I arrived at four so I was able to seat myself at a high top with my guests. We ordered from the happy hour menu which was from 4-7 I believe. Appetizers were good (calamari, salt and pepper shrimp, lobster and crab bites) for my entree I had the Alaskan lobster tail, I also ordered the truffle mac, crab rice, and mash for the table. Entree was so full of flavor and fresh! My guests had NY Strip and Prime Jumbo Shrimp. No complaints. Dessert was good too (banana foster and Godiva chocolate cake). Server was Steven, good service I have had more prompt service but he was knowledgeable!

My wife and I ate at Cochin a couple of years ago. I returned to the more casual Cochin Butcher during a recent trip to New Orleans. Both places are wonderful.  I had the muffaletta, coleslaw and a beer on my recent visit-all delicious. The restaurant has seating inside and out, plenty of televisions to watch a game, and great tunes to accompany the great food. A must stop spot in New Orleans.

What a FANTASTIC deal - Sunday buffet!!!

Went for the All your can eat Buffett. We made reservations, which I'd recommend, but I think we may have gotten in, this time, at the same time even if we'd not had reservations. 
Hostess seemed a little frazzled or unsure of where to seat us. We were welcomed by our server right away, got our drink order, and pointed us in the direction of the buffet. 

On the buffet we had breakfast and lunch items. 
Breakfast: eggs Benedict, scrambled eggs, sausage links, hash browns, bacon, biscuits and gravy, waffles and French toast. Breakfast pizza. 
Lunch: meatloaf, green beans, Mac and cheese, 3 types of fried chicken, French fries, stir fry, breadsticks and dip, make your own nachos, pizzas, halved sandwiches (which were not refilled), 3 premixed salad options, 3 mixes of fruits. And desserts of brownie or bar cake. 

I ate mostly from the breakfast offerings. Benedict and French toast were delicious. And everything else was tasty as well!! 

Adults $13.99, kids 11-5 $7.99, Kids under 4 years old are free. 

Service was good. Facility was clean. Nice space. Decide of old barrel slats is pretty cool. 

Highly recommend. 
Also a large drink menu!!


We've had brunch at 2 locations. Like the one off 86th near the monon the best!!

This location for BJ's has given me a few good laughs since it opened. The first time I went here, the service was the single worst thing I've experienced in my life at an established chain restaurant. Food was old, stale, sitting under a heat lamp and dried out until tasteless. And their servers were incompetent at best, weren't even familiar with their own beer menu (They tried to tell me they didn't carry Rogue's Dead Guy Ale, even after I pointed it out to them on their menu, took a manager to finally figure out that they did carry it). 
This time around the service got a lot better, but I keep feeling like my food is sitting under a heat lamp for a half hour before it comes to me. I think it was the fact that my Sante Fe Spring Rolls were lukewarm when they arrived, kind of gross. 
I think the funniest thing that happened to me was this last time I was there: I ordered a Union Jack IPA (mainly because their indigenous beer menu is OK at best) and 10 minutes later, some random waitress comes up to our table and says "Who ordered the Union Jack?" 
I raised my hand, then she attempts to hand me what appears to be a screwdriver or some other type of orange juice based cocktail. I said "no, no, I ordered the Union Jack IPA" 
She said "Wait, what did you order?" 
"Union Jack IPA" (then looks confused and again attempts to hand me the cocktail) 
"No, I ordered a beer...that is definitely not a beer" 
(Walks away without a word) 
About 20 minutes later, after I actually got the beer I ordered, I still see this waitress walking around the restaurant with the same drink in hand, trying desperately to pawn this thing off on someone. It was so sad, I couldn't be upset, so I just laughed. 
I guess the point I'm trying to make here is, go to the other Tucson location of BJ's, they actually know what the hell they're doing there.

Here's the thing about Southgate:  I didn't think it was Korean enough!  Let me explain.  

The wings are excellent.  Can't complain about perfectly fried (multiple times) jumbo wings with good sauces.  I preferred the spicy version better, but it's up to your tastebuds on this one.  For some reason I thought that there would be some mind boggling Korean flavor burst that I've never had before, but to my slight disappointment, they were just really good wings.

As for the burger, which was just named a Philly's Best, I had a similar problem.  It was cooked perfectly and had nice flavor, but I was expecting some Korean fireworks.  I liked it better with some extra pickles.  Same thing goes for the fries: good, but not what I was expecting.

Service was perfect.  They were attentive, well spaced and very friendly.  I like the space, and there was a nice local vibe going on.  It's a place I would drop in on again if I were in the area, but not one that I would walk all the way across the city for, like I did tonight.

The pizza is pretty good and very large. Someone in front of me who ordered a whole pie had to stick it in the trunk of his SUV because it was too big to fit anywhere else.

My slice was pretty tasty and filling. It tasted pretty much like any other good slice of pizza in Philadelphia, just bigger. 

My only complaint is that it wasn't really hot. The slice was warm at best, which negatively impacted the texture of the cheese. This is the first time I've tried it, but I imagine the cheese would have been more smooth and gooey if I got the slice hot.

Noord was a ton of fun for an impromptu date night. The ambiance was cozy and romantic. The service was good. The food was good as well.

For the appetizer we got a liver moose that came with savory donuts, pickled onions and pickled eggs. It was beyond delicious. They also served house made bread with sweet potato butter. It was unique and delicious. The appetizer was definitely my favorite part of the meal.  

For the entree I had haddock with creme fraiche, corn and crab meat. It was tasty but lacked color. I also felt that there was too much creme fraiche and not enough variety of textures. My boyfriend had one of their seafood stews which was very good seafood with a nice smokey flavor. 

For dessert, we ordered a bread pudding and some chocolate to go with out dessert wine. The dessert was tasty but just wasn't very unique. 

Overall, Noord was a great experience, a great place to check out for date night!
I've lived near here for a long time but never stopped in.  Pizza is pretty good - nice people - quick and  easy.  So far so good for Nick's and I'll definitely try it again

Dissapointed!
 Johnny's has been in Reno forever and considering that, we felt our first visit would have been more exciting. The flavors were light and boring, the steak was way over cooked and the cannolini was filled with a meat paste that tasted and felt way over processed. The decor is nice and updated. Perhaps the food should be too. Just because it's been in Reno a long time, doesn't mean it's great.
Price was fair and the wine selection was great. But no beer on tap. Really? Want great italian in Reno? Try La Famiglia or the Tuscan Tomato.

We just finished having breakfast for Mother's Day.  We had made a reservation through Open Table, though apparently it was not acknowledged (I just received an email from OpenTable stating that we were a "no-show.") We indeed were there.  I did check in a bit before 10am and requested we sit outside (though I had messaged to sit inside as the weather was not great this morning).  We were told we could not go outside (the restaurant was virtually empty when we arrived). We  read in the restaurant's profile that seating preference was done on a first-come basis....so not sure why our request was not honored as there were many seats both inside and outside at 10am.  This initial confrontation made the beginning of our experience unfortunate.  Thankfully the wait-staff was excellent.  The food was good, but my poached eggs (with the veggie and grits item) were absolutely hard-boiled....unfortunate again.  We plan to return, as the atmosphere is lovely and hopefully we will be greeted, in the future, with more grace and professionalism.  A work in progress.

Just tried Sofia's for the first time. I ordered take out and was told it would be ready in ten minutes. When I arrived, I was warmly greeted by the owners and was able to look over the desserts which looked absolutely amazing. I'll have to try them next time.  The restaurant is small. They have a few tables and the menu is on two big TVs. 
I ordered a cup of chicken lemon soup, spinach pie, a gyro, and baklava. 

The soup was pretty good. I would have preferred a more lemony favor. The spinach pie was delicious. The outside was flaky and the inside was warm, meaty, and full of flavor. I'll be ordering the spinach pie again and again. The gyro was huge! Plenty of meat and the onions, tomatoes, and tzatziki sauce tasted fresh. Last but not least was the baklava. It was just what I was hoping for. I'll definitely return.

We really liked this place. If you're looking for a place you can feel comfortable visiting in your pajamas, with great coffee, large portions, quiet neighborhood, great for a walk around the block (maybe not in your pajamas), this is the one.

A neighborhood cafe, but a little bit on the pricier side. 

My wife had the eggs benedict, and I had a platter. Large plates, flavorful food, great service, excellent atmosphere.

Yelp has to work on adapting to a grading outside of the symbol five stars. We've come a long way. This pizza is a 6.3, and it's a generous one. That being said 6.3/2= 3.15, round it down. It's not worth rounding up, it's not even in the top of the list for me or the middle. Reminded me of a 711 theme or something inside. Not a place I'd go back to, that being said its standard pizza. Nothing special. See photo attachment for clarification from a longtime pizza expert.

One of my favorite go-to's in the area. One just can't go wrong here. The food is amazingly fresh and seasonal. The dining room is adorable. And the outside dining area is fabulous. I just love this place. If you're passing through Bucks County near New Hope and in the mood for an exceptional lunch, make this place a MUST!

Oh, WOW!  So glad The Taste of Havana moved p from Broad ripple  so I can go there more often!  don't let the shopping center fool you- the food is delicious!

Walked in- immediately greeted by the owner who is the nicest guy.  Super friendly and helpful.  The place has a cool Cuban vibe and is clean.  Eclectic but out together.  This isn't a chain- is is the real deal.  Folks in there talking Cuban make you feel like you stepped 90 miles south of Key West .  

The food.  WOW!  So delicious.  I don't remember what the sandwich was, but it was the owner's favorite.  Best plantains EVER!  I'm telling you, this place is authentic. If you like Cuban food, you will not be disappointed.

If it was possible to give NO STARS, I would!  Having recently moved over to Prater and McCarran, we have yet to find a GOOD Chinese restaurant in the area and this surely ISN'T one of them!  We ordered Mongolian Beef and Broccoli Beef and where's the beef?!  If I wanted my Mongolian Beef to be ALL green onions or the Broccoli Beef to be ALL broccoli, I would of ordered it that way!  WON'T be ordering from them again!
This place was great.   Loved the food - very fresh and a good presentation.   Bonus - frozen lemonade drink.  So good.  All the rave reviews are well earned.

We first tried out this restaurant several years ago and had a pleasant experience; pretty good Greek food and great service. But we tried it again this week and were disappointed - this place has definitely gone downhill. The food was not very good (one of us liked his meal but the rest of us were underwhelmed at best - fish not cooked properly, mushy vegetables that seemed to come out of a can, etc., etc. The service was subpar as well. Worst of all, they blasted disco-type music throughout the night - the music was so loud that we had to scream just to hear each other across the table. We won't be coming back.
1st they allow smoking in here. Not sure if that's legal. Got the pub club super dry small and smoky. Gross don't come here.

I like their food. But I'm not sure if they offer ordering ahead by phone. I have tried two different times and their cell goes straight to voice mail. It will be great if I could order ahead during my lunch time from work.

Yeah, it's small. 

Oh well, this isn't suburbia. 

Anyway, I like it that way. That's kept it somewhat local. We've seen a lot of the same friendly faces for years. 

The service can be slow, but I'm usually there for breakfast on a Saturday. Trust me, I'm not in a hurry to finish breakfast and get to the Home Depot to go shopping for bathroom fixtures. 

The food usually ranges from "good" to "outstanding." Our last trip was of the latter variety. Local eggs cooked just right, tasty bacon from Goose the Market, and some of the best black bean ravioli I have ever had for breakfast. 

Come to think of it, it's the only black bean ravioli I have ever had for breakfast. Those are the kind of differences that keep me coming back.

It was hard to find as it is tucked behind the thrift store. We are a o glad we found it.  We tried String Hoppers - tasty and different but not on my love it list. Stuffed Roti had lots of flavour - we got one each flavour! The Cucumber Salad was fresh, light and tasty :). Condensed Milk Tea was perfect the way it was - no need to add sugar. It reminded us of  regular tea but perfectly sweetened with Condensed milk.

Here for breakfast and got a sausage biscuit and a hash brown. Not too impressed with the hash brown at all. It's my favorite item at McDonald's but the one I got was soggy and not really appetizing! The biscuit was sub par...bread was hard but the actual sausage patty wasn't bad!

I personally love Chipotle for takeout. It is healthy fast food and it tastes great! If you come during lunch or dinner hour there will probably be a line just as there is anywhere else. Seating is the standard stools found in most chipotles. 

I purchased two burritos because you cannot go wrong with them. They also reheat very well. I purchase two and ate the extra one the next night for dinner. I leave it wrapped and put it in a pan covered pan on very low heat for about 15 minutes. It comes out throughly heated, tasting fresh. I highly recommend this over microwaving.

2nd time at Chi, service is second to none. You must get the pretty polly roll, it is amazing. We also ordered the Firecracker, just so-so and the ugani, which is also pretty good. The location is unbeatable and the prices are pretty reasonable. By far, the best part of Chi is the service. Our server was fantastic, he was very prompt, entertaining and very helpful. Will definitely go again.

BEST bakery in the area. Anytime I need something for an event or special occasion this is the place to go to. This is a wonderful family owned business that cares for each and every customer. They do EPIC sheet cakes with custom designs. For my 30th birthday I was surprised with a Dr Who themed Tardis black and white cake. IT WAS AMAZING!!! I pop in a few tomes a more the to get something on my way to work as a great for my coworkers and they absolutely LOVE whatever I bring in. This is my number 1 place for a sweet pick me up!

Checked out this bar for a Seahawks Monday Night Football game!!  Great little bar with all kinds of drink possibilities.   Great assortment of Bourbon, Whiskey, and others!  The atmosphere was nice and rustic for a Craft Bar.  We had some of the food and that was good too.  The fries were surprisingly some of the best I've ever had... and that's saying a lot.  My wife's salad was awesome.  I had a flatbread and it was on the upper number scale, just not a 10.  Overall a really great place for a quiet night with a loved one or small group of friends.  Service was excellent.  Michelle took good care of us.

My favorite local pizza spot. If you yearn for the glory days of Pizza Hut when they actually made amazing pizza this place is for you! Always super fast delivery and consistent pizza. For those not familiar with pan pizza, class is in session!

While they are not exactly bad at what they do i just cannot bear to eat here again, hot dogs ,french fries , and grilled cheese are just not something i want to spend more than two bucks on no matter how fancy the toppings are which some of your sandwiches do sound great but lets get real three slices of cheese on bread is not worth ten dollars out even at berns..But good God man here is my real dealbreaker if you are going to serve people french fries for nearly 8 bucks you better have some fresh cut fries not ones that look like you went to gfc food mart and got a giant bag of ore ida crinkle cut fries...This little mistep honestly blows my mind that you would make everything else so well then mess up on such a small  yet so important little detail. Read this change buy a bag of potatoes and thank me later king. A lot of times i dont leave reviews for places that i would like to see succeed that have a cool idea or are real old time places that i just dont want to lay into on you have a really cool idea here and i wish the best to you but i would highly advise re thinking a few things.

Normally, I would avoid this TB and drive down to the downtown one, due to past experiences.  However, on a whim I stopped by and was really impressed at the changes that have been made.  Sharlise was WONDERFUL. Friendly, and had my order together in a timely manner.  Def will be going back!

The katsu is actually not that bad. But they really need to work on their sauce. It really doesn't hit the spot. I think they make their own sauce but the sauce sold in markets might actually taste better.(probably cheaper for them too) 

I love how they serve all the mashed potatoes, soup and salad. It's great.

But about the portion size.... when they first opened, the portion size was a lot! I was genuinely surprised by the portion size of the katsu. But within few weeks, they cut down the portion of the katsu. The portion used to be a big plus for this restaurant, just enough to cover the bad sauce, but since they reduced their portion size, this restaurant is mediocre at best. Still pretty good katsu though.

This food might fly with the tourists, but people who live here should know better. Chargrilled oysters should not come with a mountain of canned "Parmesan" and stale bread. Gumbo should not be made with frozen, dime sized shrimp. Drinks should not take an hour to get to the table and contrary to what the owner might tell you, a roach crawling on the wall past your table is not just "part of New Orleans." There should be special provisions for vacation reviewers. Sadly, there are an abundance of this caliber place around and some people just don't know any better.
We got delivery for two. It was on time, hot, and yummy. This is our new go-to Chinese food in the neighborhood!

Excellent service , food even though it was crazy busy I was very surprised . Saw the manager walking around keeping tabs . I been to a lot of Boston pizzas this food is one of the best I have had to date . Place was clean and service was fast . I will be going here again !

This is a very cool German bar. Everything on tap is mostly German but it is a great selection. I have not tried the food but everyone at a table looked very pleased with their meals and this place is always packed. The only reason I'm not rating them at 5 stars is because I have not tried the food. It is also right across the street for McGillins. The bar is big with a lot of seating and there are plenty of tables.

The burgers are good but the fries are just okay. The service is also lacking and I'd recommend paying with cash bc I've had some concerns paying with my debit card in the past ... it's usually the same girl but she's always there so just pay cash.
The onion rings are good and the bread on the burgers is super soft.

I honestly can't think of a bad thing to say about this place. Great service, atmosphere, and friendly all around. Funny story though... there was this homeless looking dude outside, and he was super nice... even asked how our meal was in the back parking lot. I was like..  it was really good. And as he walked away I went for a few bucks in my wallet... then the dude hops in a Mercedes. I think it was the owner. Damn hipsters,... ya just can't tell any more. Lol

Weekday early dinner.  The finest German restaurant I have found in the US.  Doesn't look like much from the street but you step thru the door and you are in a different world.  The schnitzel was awesome.  Large servings and perfect service.  Make reservations.  Seemed like they have loyal, regular customers.

Muffuletta Sandwich is great if you like olives. Even though, i am not the biggest fan of olives, this sandwich wasnt half bad. You can both taste and smell the olive spread within the sandwich. The salami was fresh and potent. The bread is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. The sandwich is worth a stop.

Bellagio has proven time and time again to be the hands down best pizza joint in Nashville. Prices, amazing. Food, astounding. Service, extraordinary. Great hours, outdoor seating, speedy delivery, and lovely people. 

I recommend the spinach artichoke pizza, Italian Stromboli, and the fried mushrooms.

One of my favorite spots! Everything was AMAZING!! The service was perfect, the food was phenomenal and the portion sizes were spot on! Michaela was so promt and had great suggestions! The new menu is awesome! Sesame noodles and short rib skewers are a must have! The cheesesteak egg rolls are revamped and better then ever! AND the cocktails are so on point as always! Endless summer was my fav! This is a must stop in Philly!

I've only been here twice, but I absolutely LOVE this bar! The drinks and shots, are perfect and you really can't go wrong. I love how on the wall by the bar they have a huge list of drinks- so many it is impossible to choose what to get! I got the electric pink lemonade and of course loved it! The prices here aren't horrible, and the service is quick and friendly. The music is fun and typical radio music, with some country. The crowd is older because it is downtown, but it has its fair share of college kids. Definitely a fun change of pace from Purdue bars! 

Pros:
- Great drinks
- Awesome ambiance
- Quick service
- Convenient location with plenty of close parking

Cons:
- Can get crowded, but it is a bar...
- Sometimes there is a cover charge

A sign said we are open for dining in.... I went in.... it was true. First time eating inside a McDo. Ordered Oreo cookie ice cream mix. The place was clean and service timely. Few other customers came in. At the end of my meal while I was checking Facebook about to put a review, a man sitting in a quarter in a corner started coughing. Even though there was social distancing and he was 7 meters away I decided to leave. Another customer did the same. This is why I did not take any pictures.
Parking is decent fir this small but strategic McDo.

One of my favorite coffee places in Nashville and I don't even really drink a lot of coffee. Clean well well-kept with a wonderful variety of delicious coffees make this place a wonderful early Saturday morning favorite of mine. It's independently and locally owned and they do a wonderful job of keeping it staffed with friendly people.

This place in good EVERY SINGLE time. Best Mexican restaurant in town. The polo loco is great, but so is everything else they have. Chips are almost always fresh and hot. Great service and fresh food.

The food is amazing, the service is awesome, and the atmosphere is purely wonderful. One of the best restaurants Santa Barbara has to offer, if not the best! The wine selection is vast, with a the staff who are all very knowledgable and willing to help you find the perfect pairing with your meal.

Great grab and go lunch spot. Italian pork is amazing and definitely my favorite. All the Portions are huge, of good quality, and prices are excellent. The staff here are efficient, and nice. Good job, will definitely be back

This is a delicious, friendly neighborhood place. My family and I have eaten here for years. We enjoy the friendly, consistent service that is attentive and polite without being pushy. The restaurant is clean, consistent, and just a nice place to be for a variety of events and groups. Of course, the food is great and it seems to me that their food and drink menu can please just about anyone. We particularly love their salads and their fried chicken wrap. We just tried the hot roast beef sandwich last week and it was awesome and on great bread. Thank you, TJs!
ABSOLUTELY LOVED STATESIDE KITCHEN!! The food was immaculate and our bartender and the DJ were even better! Grant knows how to keep the brunch vibe flowing all day, I feel like I never left EDC!

I haven't been to this Carreta's in a while.  I should of stayed gone.  I feel the food was a glorified copy of Taco Bell.  My taco was so wet with the chicken from my enchilada, that I could hardly eat it.  The enchilada was a dissapointment being served in a flour tortilla?
