Best onigiri I've had! The service was very good and kind and I really enjoyed my time there even though my party didn't eat much!

Good Dog might be the epitome of my favorite kind of Philly bar. Anywhere else it would just be a hole in the wall with 6 domestic taps and a menu that makes you want to cross the street to Applebees. But not in Philly. Here, we've got a cozy unpretentious bar with great beer and food. They've got 3 floors to enjoy, with a long bar and booths at ground level, more tables on the above and a pool table and dartboard on the 3rd.

The beer list isn't as long as other area bars, but it's a well curated variety of craft beers. The food is excellent and creative. There are great appetizers; the roasted onion hummus with house-made veggie chips is a nice change from pita wedges and and a ball of bland chickpea paste, just as the cordon blue tenders will trump everyday frozen chicken strips. The cheesesteak empanadas and mixed sweet/regular fries are also standouts. The roquefort stuffed Good Dog burger is one of the best in Philly, but their other sandwiches prevent it from being an automatic order.

Not that pizza hut is very good anyway, but this location can never get deliveries right and cancels your orders after over an hour waiting with no notification. This us the second time to happen. Not only that, they really don't care about it either. Never again

My family and I just ate at St Elmo Steakhouse. We have been trying to get in for months since our son moved to Indianapolis for a job. I ate there once in the early 2000's and from the reviews our expectations were high. The beginning to middle of dinner was fine but after that the waitress didn't come back until I had to go find someone to pay our bill. It was a solid 15 minutes waiting for the bill and even longer since Emily checked on us. There was a shell in the crab Mac n cheese that I couldn't tell anyone about. She finally brought out our bill and not one word or apology for our long wait. With the reputation of this establishment I would have expected more......won't be back. I can find somewhere else to spend 250.00 for a dinner for 4

Don't bother unless you don't mind a rude hostess. She chewed (like a cow) as she leaned  and  arrogantly informed  us of a long wait. (Ms. T  has a  VERY small dinning area) She could soo... care less!  What fool gave her this  job,. I'll assume the fool is/was   a family member.  Later I was informed we didn't miss much anyway.

I come here for the cheap dollarita's (which I'm going to stop getting because all they do is make me sick), and to hang out with friends. The food is very disappointing. My most recent trip I got a southwest salad something and it was good, but $9 for a tiny little salad seemed high. Also, the service can be a huge hit or miss. I've waited as long as 10 minutes on a slow day before someone even came and took my drink order. Some of the workers are super lazy. I don't think I'll be coming back here any time soon.

If this is how bakery treats are in France, what am I still doing here??

Everything I've had there is delicious. The molasses cookies, cheese croissants and butter tarts are my favourites but I can almost guarantee the other stuff there is just as good. If you're looking for a tasty treat with an authentic French flare, this is your place!

With all the blogger attention on this place I was really excited to check it out. Unfortunately it let me down though. I came with my parents who are not from a larger city and so to them $12 for a drink is pretty outrageous. I definitely felt they should be more around the $10 range but also if they are going to be priced like that they need to be good. They were just ok. Food was the biggest issue we had. I ordered the nachos which I was extremely happy with but my moms order came out wrong and the kitchen took so long by the time they brought it out we were already done eating and told them we didn't even want it anymore. The waitress then asked my dad if he wanted a box for his leftover fried seafood platter but all that was left on his plate was the breading. Literally there was so much breading on the items it looked like the actual food hadn't been touched after he picked out the actual pieces of fish and vegetables. I have never seen something so ridiculous and the manager mentioned she had issues with that and had a conversation with their chef about that dish before! Service was the biggest negative I heard about this place before going but our server was very personable. Bottom line, don't order the seafood platter and expect to pay too dollar for decent drinks.

Poor food in a nice atmosphere. Service was friendly and attentive. Calamari apetizer, which was supposed to actually be mixed fried seafood, was missing components and was way too salty. Fish entre was overcooked and completely bland. There's a reason it wasn't crowded on a Saturday night.
Enjoyed our dinner here.  I had the crispy duck and it lived up to it's name.  It was moist and juicy inside and the skin was crackling.  Just perfectly done.  Very impressed with that.

For the previous reviewer,

Ahem -- there was no lack of planning on my part.  My review was based on my experience.  That is really great that you love Cool Hand Luke's.  No, really, that's great.  Honestly, you should not take it personally that I thought their food and service sucks.

I am also sure that the readers do not take these reviews as gospel and should they try it and love it, great.  For your information, I used to plan monthly association events for 20-plus people at various restaurants here in the valley once a month for a couple years.  Big whoop.  All I am saying is I know what I am doing.  

I have lived here my whole life and visited other places as well -- oh my!  And have eaten at restaurants in those places too!  Golly jeepers. 

Which leads me to my next point, why does it matter that you have lived in California your whole life and that you have eaten at some "really great restaurants"?  I think it is safe to say that since we are fellow Yelpers, we have all eaten at, what we deem, some really great restaurants.

I also don't need a dictionary or menu to tell me how a steak is prepared, as I am sure all menus in all chain restaurants say the same thing.  And I am well aware that there is a little wiggle room with the preperation -- but trust, not that much wiggle room.
  
I am a little bit blown away that you have never seen a wilted salad.  How is a "wilted salad" a ridiculous description or thing?  You have never had a wilted salad?  Wilted means limp.  My salad was limp.

You have never had terrible service at a restaurant?  Well, good for you.  I am not sure where you are eating, but do tell.  I expected to have decent service from two waiters.  And I did check to make sure our large party would not be an issue and that they would not be busy.
We ate there at 6:00 in the evening, and it was a Thursday night.  

I guess I shouldn't expect decent service, food, or the consideration that maybe -- just maybe -- it was a hellish restaurant experience.  
Being a lifelong Idahoan, it has never occurred to me that someone might actually think to write that just because this is Idaho, we may have a slightly different scale of what is good and what is bad.  In other words, we either have less expectation or, worse yet, don't have an expectation.  I implore the rest of the Idahoan Yelp reviewers to dare not  be insulted by ignorant comments such as "don't think that just because this is little ole' Idaho, you can't have a good restaurant, dawg gone it."  Like, whatever, like -- I mean, that is how ALL Californians speak; right?

A piece of advice, try a few more restaurants, non-chain preferably, so as to directly support the local growers of our teensy-weensy hickville dot on the map, and get another perspective of what this town has to offer.

It is sad that you only get one chance at a first impression.  Their first impression on me was just bad.  That's all.

And I am curious, if you have never had the bad, then how in the world would you know what is good?

So good. Service is great. Food comes out fast and hot and done to perfection. I got the spicy chicken sandwich and it was the perfect balance of heat and flavor.Real juicy chicken. My bf got the Philly cheesesteak and said it was the best he ever had. I would skip the fried pickles tho they had too much batter on them and the inside of the batter was raw-that's where they lost a star.

I've been visiting Crescent Steak now for the past three months regularly, planning to go orders. Sadly, I've been so disappointed in the attention to detail in getting their customers order correct, hot, and punctual. After several frequent visits of poor customer service, I decided to complete a review after waiting 40 minutes for my food. This is unacceptable for a 4 Star establishment.

A friend discovered this place last summer.

He convinced a group of us to go here after class, for their 12.99 lunch special all-you-can-eat. Depending on how much you can eat, the price is definitely worth it. An order of 4 rolls and 2 appetizers definitely sets you back over 13 dollars. However the sushi is not exactly the best, nor fresh, and to me, every roll seems to taste the same. I'm most likely biased from the sushi joints back home in California.

This same friend is ecstatic about the place; he always raves about coming back here for their all-you-can-eat. After a while however, I begin to diverge from their buffet menu and order from their normal one.

Glancing past their sushi and rolls off their regular menu, Sushi Ai has a satisfactory selection of bento boxes and side dishes. While this place advertises serving Japanese food, the workers and selection of music playing overheard begs to differ. The whole environment is a mix of Chinese and a little Japanese. Their Orange Chicken (??), Teriyaki Beef and Chicken all do not have any resemblance to true Japanese food. In a way, the food tastes rather dull and not worth the $10+ price.

I've since been here at least 10 times. Sometimes my friends drag me along for the sushi but I've found the quality and service to be inconsistent. Sometimes the rolls taste fresh, whereas sometimes it's obvious that the ingredients have been sitting out for a while. Moreover, the first couple of times I came here, there was this one particular waiter that lingered awkwardly over us, and objectively cut in to ask if we needed more water. At the end, he even stopped us before we went out the door asking for a tip. The hell? However it seems that Sushi Ai has let that particular waiter go and their service has seen been improved. 

The atmosphere is average, nothing too special. My friends and I are always seated at the same exact table. Nothing to really complain about though.

After passing over their all-you-can-eat menu, I have found the Shrimp Tempura Dinner specialty to be the best thing for me. The order comes with 6 generous pieces of shrimp tempura, along with 4 pieces of potato, broccoli, and cucumber. The batter is nice and crunchy, the sauce is sweet. It is also served with a side of miso soup and sub-par tasting ginger sauced salad. 

Overall, Sushi Ai is ok. They do have a 10% discount for students of neighboring schools such as Wash U, STLCOP, and SLU. It basically waives out the price of tax. After coming here a number of times, each visit seems to be more and more drawn out. I know that I am spoiled by the taste and delicacy of California sushi/Japanese food. Coming to Sushi Ai makes me reminiscence of better and cheaper food elsewhere.

We ordered our food and they told us to pull up because "they were on a timer" we said okay we waited for like 15 minutes and nothing so we had to go inside and the manager said "I didn't put the order in". Worst service ever if you don't want to wait for 15 outside then do not go to this area

I finally tried 4 Seasons. They have both Chinese and Thai food. Last time I went there they were closed for remodeling. Just 5 minutes from the office I took orders from my coworkers. Sesame chicken, sweet and sour pork, orange chicken and beef Penang along with egg rolls and the best spring rolls I've ever tasted. Lunch specials were fairly priced and large but not excessive portions. The Orange chicken sauce was very light and full of flavor. I just had carry out so I don't have a review on the service at the restaurant but overall very friendly and accommodating. Definitely worth trying!

I really love this place! The coffee is my favorite and the employees are all friendly. Prices are reasonable as well. Like others have mentioned- if you want to eat at peak hours, expect to wait a little for a seat or grab takeout. Small deck for outdoor eating when it's nice out too.

The food here is surprisingly good! I wish I worked in this building so that I could mosey on upstairs for this goodness! They have creatively put their menu together with twists on every dish to make it different then Joe-next-doors and their prices cannot be better! I tried their cashew ceaser salad and their version of a club sandwich. Both were great and I hope to come back soon. Maybe when its warmer so I can sit on the balcony and admire the view with a wine of beer in hand :)

They are pretty good, the food is cleaner then most other Chinese restaurants. Their general Tso's chicken is really good IMO. They used to be on Aramingo but they have since moved to Richmond and Tioga a little down from Bonks Bar. The aramingo location always smelled because of the carpet and the fish tank, fish tanks don't belong in restaurants, especially if they are not kept right, the pH level gives off a foul odor. I will say that I haven't been in the new location yet, dying to see what it looks and smells like. The owners are very nice and hard working people so give them a try. They are definitely better then the Aramingo buffet and the Wok n Roast nearby.

This place is ok. If you like wings that are fried and then have the sauce poured on them then this is your place . We got the hot garlic and parmesan wings . The hot garlic wings just had a little bit of spice and no taste of garlic . The parmesan wings just had parmesan cheese poured on top of them . I wasn't impressed . The staff was ok not very inviting . I probably won't come here again . Just ok wings

Very pleased with Silo this past Friday evening.  Entering Silo you find an a very cool design with effective use of woods, lighting and light that reinforces the locally sourced and farm raised theme.  While not that expert on Southern cuisine, we found the food distinctive and ably prepared.  We were impressed by the unusual wedge salad with tasty greens, turnip and topped with a fried egg.  The pork chop with sweet potato and apple was the best I have ever tried.  We also had the shrimp étouffée that was well prepared.  We ordered the cornbread and noted that while good it had was not the "sweet" variety that we had expected.
It was easy to see Paul (the owner) involved in all the details that are critical to the operation of a successful restaurant.  Friendly and helpful, he helped guide us to that evening's entertainment at the Station Inn where we were fortunate to hear the SteelDrivers.  Thanks for making our one night Nashville visit so nice.

Golf course is very nice. If weather has been dry for awhile, then course does get "poor". But when watered it is very nice.
Restaurant is fantastic. Great food and very nice atmosphere.

The best restaurants I visited this trip. Very pricey, can't compare to the other restaurants in the area. 
The architecture of this place is very unique and really reflects the history on NOLA. Staff were very professional but slightly on he slow side for a place like this. Also a mini point that I would generally not mention, but the silverware were put out in the wrong order in front of us, and my steak knife was very dull, had to cheng it. 
Everything else was amazing. My ribeye was perfectly done, great texture and taste. The other dishes as depicted were equally great. Dessert, bread pudding was one of he best I've had! Everything down to the coffee was delicious making this a great experience. 
Make sure to make reservations for this place. Ask to be seated in the back room close to the kitchen for the full experience. 
Will definitely be back!

I know everybody seems to have a mediocre opinion about this place. And I would tend to agree, but I don't think it's at all a bad experience. 

$2 pint Tuesdays are more than a worthy weekday experience. I always get the nachos and they are easily some of the best nachos I've ever had! Now, having said that, the hot wings are different just about every time I get them. Sometimes they are great and flavorful and the sauce is just the right level of hot.... And sometimes they are dry and sauce taste different and it's either super mild or super spicy. So, yes there's definitely some inconsistencies in the kitchen. 

Also, the staff seems to have a high level of turnover. There's always new faces working there and some servers are really friendly and knowledgable while others seem like they were hired literally yesterday and have no idea what they are doing.

But the good news is they seem to be really trying to re-vamp their menu lately. They have been making a lot of changes and I think most of them have been for the better. Granite, I go here to mainly drink some beer, maybe play some pool or watch a game on TV, and order a nibble on the side.....not necessarily to "dine." So maybe my expectations are a little lower than most. 

But hey, with all the new restaurants that just boomed up around them they seem to be really struggling with all the extra competition. I personally want to route for them because I have had some great times at the ole fox and hound. 

I hope they keep improving :-)

I couldn't wait for this place to open and when it did I went for their lunch buffet. We went for lunch just the other day and I must say, their choices were good but everything wasn't as hot as it should have been. The lasse was extremely thick when it should be thin but that's ok I still drank it because I love lasse. They had a chili chicken dish and to me it felt like they put wing sauce on the chicken and baked it. The food was dry and room temperature. It should have been hot. Overall I think the food should have a stronger flavor of the spices India is known for using. I have eaten at other Indian restaurants and their flavors of the cumin and coriander were quite strong in their dishes. The staff was extremely friendly! They offered us desert when we didn't ask which I thought was cool. They were yummy but I preferred them warm. I thought the ambiance was quite cozy and warm. I liked how they have a projector of different countries playing. Make sure you watch out for the floor. I almost tripped walking about because the floor wasn't glued all the way down. This was only a lunch buffet so I am basing my review based off of that. I have not gone for dinner. When I go for dinner I will post again. I will give this place another try in the future.

I brought one of my pitbulls here yesterday. She was the only dog wearing a muzzle, which I think put some people off. The staff however was great and there were SO MANY dogs for her to run with. We were there for 3 hours. Bartenders and our server were so kind and upbeat. My dog is a hugger, especially when she is nervous or excited, so she jumped on a few folks. Most people reacted very well and nobody was unkind because I had an energetic pitbull. I followed her around for about an hour, but after that I felt very comfortable leaving her for brief times with the handlers. Be sure to tip the handlers! They are so wonderful. There are QR codes on signs you can scan to tip them. The food was better than I expected. I had the French fries with variety dipping sauces, of which the honey mustard was the best. I also had the ahi tuna salad. There was too much dressing that made the greens soggy, but it had good flavor and quality fish. I will definitely be getting a membership and coming back. Another thing to love about STL!

Love the Prosecco mimosa. The croissant sandwich  with apricot chutney was lovely. 


Daryan was by far one of  most amazing servers in Reno.  With bottomless mimosas. Servers are key.   She is amazing, sweet and lovely and attentive.

I was there with my service dog this afternoon and we were denied access. I was surprised by the owner's lack of know knowledge or care about law and regulations regarding service dog, and she was extremely rude. 
I won't recommend this restaurant for anyone with disabilities.

This bbq place's only attraction is the big milkshakes. If you come here you will be instantly disappointed with the attitude and enthusiam pf the wait staff. 10 minute wait just for a beer order while sitting at the bar, the waitress with  blonde hair has a terrible attitude and runinng out of food by 6:30pm at night I would say is kinda unacceptable. No wonder blue oak is still better. Coming here twice so far and being disappointed, I know I will not be back. I only wish yelp could give me the option tp give zero stars

Kimchi Guys coupled my love of Kimchi with Spicy Chicken Wings, so I thought it would be my new take-out jam.  **Insert disappointment sound effect here** I ordered the smothered waffle fries and two orders of wings for boyfriend and I to indulge our inner fat camp kid - took one bite of the fries and threw them away.  The chicken wings were okay, but nothing to tell the friends about.  $50 down the poop shoot with this one

The chicken shawarma sandwich was alright.. garlic sauce could use a bit more of a kick. Overall, it was decent. It was a little bland, but alright for Mediterranean in NOLA. The pitas were pretty awesome.

The El Bar is an awesome place. Based off of how I dress, one could assume I would not "fit in" here. However, that is never how I felt. I loved the outdoor patio. I loved inside. i loved the pool table. I ALWAYS had fun. And it is cheap.

Oh yeah and the beef jerky is pretty delicious.

Nothing to complain about, just go. Especially outside when it's nice.

The good ole' egg roll house. When I was young and lived in Metairie, my mom used to take me here at least 3 times a week. She always ordered the Moo Goo Gai Pan for me or the chicken with broccoli. 

I feel for the family that runs this place because I can tell that they work so hard. I wish them the best. They've been in business for a long time. I mean if I'm 22 and my mom took me there when I was 4, then that's what's up!

One of my favorite recent discoveries, Felix's is a great place to get your drink on.  Swing by after work and pick up your "Pizza and a Pint" deal -- for somewhere under $7.00, you can get a whole-pizza-sized slice of pizza plus a Schlafly pint, which should keep you busy for a good hour or so.  Then you can move on to the reasonably friendly service and more food and drinks that'll surely follow.

There's always an interesting crowd here which is hard to sum up -- local Dogtown residents, college students, and more.  We've only ever sat in the restaurant section, which gets pretty hoppin' after the dinner hour; from what we've seen, the bar area next door is even more the case.

They advertise a bunch of live music here, but I've never caught any, so it's hard to say whether the gigs here are fun or distracting.  I'll report in a little later on.

Give it a shot!  I can tell Felix's is an important cornerstone of the heart of Dogtown.  That's for a reason.

Came in here with my girlfriend for dinner, we had a super fast server who was on it and we had our food within 10 minutes of ordering it. Not to mention it was delicious. The guacamole was fantastic and tasted super fresh. Everything was spot on. Would definitely consider coming back here again! Excellent service and food

I am an American Born Chinese and love all "authentic" ethnic foods, but lean towards the foods I grew up with.  Also a native Chicagoan, they have some pretty damn good Chinese restaurants in Chicago that I've yet to find an equal in the Saint Louis area.  Honestly, I would have never considered this restaurant because of its dismal exterior, but a friend mentioned this place as a favorite for some sports celebrities.  After reading the Yelp reviews, which were all over the place, I had to try it and judge for myself.

So with an open mind and low expectations, I went in on a Friday 6PM.  The interior was as dismal as the exterior, but seemed sanitary enough.   I opted for take-out, but not because of the atmosphere (rather lack of it) as my primary focus is the food.

The menu is surprisingly brief and simple, definitely catering to Americans.  I was acknowledged fairly quickly by the staff that was neither friendly nor rude.  I went with a few items raved about in the reviews* and a few Chinese staples**:  Egg rolls*, Yen Ching  beef*, tofu and black mushrooms**.

While waiting for my order, several patrons came in to join the handful that was already seated.  This place appears to do okay business, though I must point out that aside from myself and the staff, there were no other Asians.  As they say and in my own experience, a good sign of an ethnic restaurant is to see lots of patrons of the same ethnicity as the type of cuisine.

Looking at the dusty bottles of liquor in the bar area, I recall one reviewers disapproval of his drink.  I'm not sure if liquor has an expiration date, but that looks like some well aged booze.  Observing the accolades on the wall, I couldn't help but notice not one within the past 10-years.  12-minutes later my food is ready.  A little pricier than what I'd think, but not unreasonable.

First impression:  This is American food with Chinese influence.  Hence the all American patrons and I'm fairly certain that most if not all the raving reviews were from Americans that do not venture far from egg rolls and sweet & sour, egg foo young and other American invented Chinese food.  Did you know that real Chinese cooks actually need to be taught how to make sweet and sour recipes?

The food itself isn't bad and everything appeared to be fresh, but hardly what I would call real Chinese food.  More like a Panda Express in an old building.  If you're a typical American that considers egg rolls, Chinese food and don't mind a dingy atmosphere, you'll love this place.  If you're looking for authentic Chinese cuisine go to Chicago, New York or the West coast.  If you can't go to Chicago, try the Chinese restaurants in University City on Olive.  Look for the restaurants filled with the most Asians :-)
Good classic dinner food.  Good burgers, great breakfast.  Best corned-beef hash in the city.  Also go for dinner and get the beef and noodles, you will not be disappointed.

Nestled in the heart of Gayborhood, More Than Just Ice Cream is a delightful brunch spot and ice cream parlor! I had been following them on Instagram when I saw they posted a brunch special called 'Biscuit Head' and decided to treat myself and ordered this. It is a buttermilk biscuit bowl filled with scrambled eggs, sausage, scallions, cheddar cheese, and red peppers. It's served with an arugula side salad.

This dish was scrumdiddlyumptious! The biscuit bowl was infused with butter and it was carb heaven. The scrambled eggs and sausages inside were the quintessential breakfast comfort food. The arugula salad was so fresh and drizzled with a light vinaigrette; it nicely complimented the protein heavy dish.

My waiter was also very attentive and courteous. Overall, my dining experience at MTJIC was very enjoyable and the perfect way to kickstart the weekend!

Still a good bagel and I see more people coming in for coffee to go with it -self service for the coffee.   Parking can be challenging but they open at 5 am in case you want to bring some to the office.

Real Jewish bagels - not the fake ones you get at the chain stores

Mmm the reviews are pretty bad..., sexy building from the outside, nothing wrong with the inside.  Staff and Service kinda mute robots, me I like my students perky.  $6 for a small juice, don't know if this is good or bad, I had carrot juice -carrots a carrot right!, my friends Kale thing tasted just like she gets in in Brooklyn.  Food seemed to be wraps - boring - but hey on the whole it was a nice pitstop but a charisma bypass.  Since 8th will be the new 12th in the near future they are probably in a good spot.

A welcome addition to the neighborhood. The space has probably the best outdoor seating setup in Wayne. The food is good, we tried the curry fries and the hummus, both were very good. The drink menu is nice, and the beer selection is not bad, but not great. Our waiter was attentive too. If the plan is for this bar to specialize in whiskey, they probably want to up their selection and have a whiskey menu.

HORRIBLE LUNCH!

I do not eat meat and they refused to substitute anything for me!  They told me in order to do so I would have to order from the dinner menu which I was handed.  Then the waiter told me that I still had to pay extra for the substitution!  

Who the hell ever heard of chicken fried rice anyway??!!  GROSS!  They should just serve basic fried rice then everyone is happy.

Just at brunch at the hotel. Our server Stephen did an amazing job! He was extremely attentive and fun to have a conversation with! The food was delicious as well- highly recommend the French toast fish and the pimento cheese omelette!

Great salad and the pizza is even better! 
Service makes the experience exceptional. 
Can be a little loud, but that is no fault of the establishment.

3 months living in Malvern and I finally made it to Malvern Buttery and the only disappointment I have is why didn't I go there before ? Food was delicious , flat white and green tea latte we ordered were perfect. Loved the urban hipster feel of the decor. Friendly for kids. Enough space for strollers to move around. You are going to see me and my daughter here often.

Panda has been open for about 6 or 7 months. Not sure if it was just a rebranding or if it's entirely new. I never ate at the old place that was there before them.

The first thing that I noticed walking into this place was the condition of their carpet.  For being only 6 months old, it is very stained and worn. Definite need of replacing immediately. 

I didn't have any food expectation going into this place, and I was lucky for that.  Got my plate of assorted food, came back and my first bite was met with a cold oily texture.  This was supposed to be hot.  The majority of the 7 things I put on my plate where luke warm at best.  I really dislike cold food.

The remainder of the food was very bland and without flavor.  All the soups basically tasted like water, and the food was a bit like paper.

They're getting 2 stars because their staff really made an effort to be friendly and engage in conversation.  The hostess came over at least 3 times during my 1 hour there to check and see if we needed anything. 

This type of attention is not usual for a buffet place, and it made the place somewhat memorable. 

Also their Sushi was very decent for a buffet.  I believe this is about the only thing amongst the buffet that I enjoyed.

The problem with buffet places is that if there isn't enough people in there eating then there isn't anything to warrant them changing over the food. Thus, most of the food had been sitting there for what looked like near 2 hours (especially the salmon).
Good if you want some hooka, but it can sometimes turn into a popular hangout for the 18 year olds in town.
The planet Hollywood of soul food minus the soul and flavor you are used to in New Orleans. I get the appeal because of the location but it was not flavorful. Nice people but bad food.

Incredible amount of omelette choices. Food was great service was ok.  Plenty of other choices besides omelettes- food did not disappoint at all.  Only complaint was table was too small for the group size and the place was empty.

This is wonderful spot for a relaxing breakfast and cup of coffee or a casual lunch.  I believe they have evening activities and entertainment as well, but I've not experienced that.  It is located in an old Starbucks space that is in the "Merchant Square Mall".  The food and coffee: excellent!  The staff is very accommodating.  Each of the three times I've been they have gone out of their way to make me feel comfortable.  The chef makes it clear that if there is something you'd like that is not on the menu, they'll make it up for you.  The prices are unbelievably reasonable....I don't know how they can operate at these prices.  Support this locally owned, non-chain, breakfast and lunch spot.  The same center houses a Panera Bread, but I'd put this place way out in front of Panera and you will pay much less for the better meal!  Of course they have free WiFi and a nice toasty fireplace.  I am somewhat concerned that iCafe is destined to be a casualty to the franchises/chains....I hope not.

I'm a fan of this place simply because the tickets are a bit more affordable than a few others in Philly area I'm assuming that may have to do with the fact that they're expecting you to dine and spend money.  However, you should definitely take advantage of $5 Tuesday movies during the day. I've gone without purchasing food and enjoyed myself. 

Movies in the evening are a different experience because those are the high traffic hours which means you might wait a long time for your food. For the most part the servers are doing their best to get to orders during the movie but there does seem to be some disorganization at times; for instance my pretzel bites took really long to come even longer than my mom's chicken nachos. I'm pretty sure all it just took was the cooks warming up the pretzels and the cheese, that said, when I got my pretzel bites they were tasty. My mom's order of chicken nachos was just okay, not incredibly hot and all the cheese was kinda plopped into one area. We did finish the nachos together because we were hungry at that point.

SMG is hit or miss. In the daytime you will have an excellent experience most likely as there's no one there and the servers are not bogged down. In the nighttime you might not. There are a lot more moving parts when the theater has more orders to fill which leads to bad service.

Everything we had was delicious.  We decided to order two meals to share. The portions were very generous and we weren't able to finish it all. The Oceana Redfish was melt in your mouth goodness and the greens served with it were very good. Shrimp and grits wasn't on the menu but I asked for them and the chef made me the best shrimp and grits I have ever put in my mouth. Topped it all off with a hurricane. Delish! The service was superb and fast! We had Alex and he was amazing. I will go here every time i am in New Orleans no doubt! It's a winner!

Tonight the hubby and I needed a night off from cooking, and wanted really good food without the crowded scene of a downtown Reno restaurant. So we went to Campo - in Sparks. 

The ambiance is cozy yet chic, with the feel of an Italian winery.  We were well taken care of by Cristy, who was very knowledgeable and able to answer all of our menu questions.   

An oil and balsamic focaccia snack came shortly after our drinks. We only wanted water, and they offered to bring both naturale and sparkling water. 

We skipped an appetizer, though they all sounded delicious, and opted for the daily pasta special, as well as the Campo Pizza. The pasta special, a house-made spicy spaghetti with sausage and eggplant, received mixed reviews from us. Hubby, a native Italian, loved it, despite the fact that the pasta was cooked just a little bit past al dente.  He loved the spiciness of it. I felt it was a bit too spicy and would have liked it a bit less done. The eggplant was cooked perfectly and actually helped to balance out the spice.  The Campo Pizza was a definite "Yes!" from both of us. Italian hubby says that Campo's pizza dough is easily the best tasting and best textured pizza dough in all of Reno!  The meats and cheese on the pizza were also to die for!  
This time we were too full for dessert, but next time for sure!  

Overall, a great experience, which will be even better on a night when we go all out!
Love their tacos. Drinks are strong and burgers are big. The staff is just the whip cream topping! Awesome :)

Pros:
Decor was really neat! (even the bathroom!) And even though every table was occupied, it wasn't too loud, and easy to hear each other talk. 
The quality of the crust on the pizza was pretty good. 
My friend enjoyed her meal- bruschetta and the salad special 

Cons:
Waiter was kind of rude and cocky, I did appreciate his honesty in saying that the margharita pizza .
Ordered the goat cheese pizza with caramelized onions, roasted peppers, and mushrooms. The proportions of ingredients was way off first of all. Although I enjoy a thin crust, this crust was so paper thin in the middle that it made the middle of the pizza soggy and just taste like goat cheese. Second, there was way way too much goat cheese, which also was not of great quality- tasted grainy and sour, not smooth, tart, and creamy (in my opinion). The vegetables were good but the pizza could have used twice as many if the crust were a little more sturdy in the middle. 
Ultimately, this pizza was just pretty boring. I thought it would be exciting since the waiter said I should order this one if I wanted to be adventurous, but was definitely not much of an adventure. 

I might return to try a pasta dish, as those looked good as they were coming out to other customers.

The baked eggs in brioche was the most amazing breakfast meal I've ever experienced.  The quality of ingredients and way it was perfectly prepared was amazing. 

I saw people having other menu items that also looked spectator, but the brioche was so yummy I'm not sure I could ever order anything different!  Oh, the coffee was also wonderful. 

This is a gourmet breakfast not a diner type experience. Don't miss this awesome dinning experience.

We really like their pizza, but for the second time now they were under staffed and with countless empty tables there still was a long wait. We walked down the street and ate elsewhere. They need to employ more wait staff?

Ordered takeout because of covid, it was terrible. They forgot to give us wasabi (oh the irony), the ginger was non recognizable rolled in plastic wrap and they jammed all 4 rolls into one styrofoam box. I understand it's a pandemic and not all places have mastered takeout, so if it was just those issues I wouldn't complain. But the rolls tasted like they had been sitting out all day. They forgot sauce on one of them, they were almost inedible. We threw most of it away. It's a bit tough to take when we spent almost $60 on it.

Who goes to Bluebeard with a full stomach? Unfortunately, this girl. Seriously, the day we're invited to meet up with friends at Bluebeard for dinner is the same day that I had eaten a ridiculously late lunch. 
I ordered their salad of the day, of which each ingredient tasted crisp and freshly picked. While I didn't get too adventurous with my meal (which was actually an appetizer), I made sure I tasted bites of the other food ordered at our table, and it was delicious. The big surprise was how wonderful their bread pudding was. The first serving was so delicious, our table ordered a second one to share.

I really enjoyed the beautiful outdoor seating. Very urban, hipster, industrial vibe going on. And more than anything, our service was top notch. He was knowledgeable and incredibly helpful, especially when ordering drinks. They have an intriguing twist on their mixed drinks from the bar. And man, do they serve up some strong drinks! Beware if you're stopping in for drinks. Make sure you have your ride sharing app at the ready!

This is a cute little lounge place. Ordered an eggs Benedict with ham. My eggs were over poached. Looked more like a hard boiled egg halfway cooked. Was given thin pieces of ham and placed on regular wheat bread. All in all it was okay. I wouldn't order the same thing again but maybe I'll try their lunch.

exceeded my expectations

got the taco lunchbox

can't remember which taco stood out but the tortillas stood out as i think they were homemade.

the tacos are TINY FYI - TWO BITES EACH

also some of them had some white cream sauce on them which i wasn't a fan of so they aren't like gas station or taco truck types, a bit more foo foo

elote was stellar if im honest but has some cream sauce or seemed like it at least

queso is legit

the chips are amazing. they are like double stacked and fried well

JEANS: OK by far
ORDER: wait staff

they validate parking fyi, garage is in same gigantic building attached to it

Mothers was recommended by several people. I have to say I was not impressed. I ordered the shrimp poboy and the turtle soup. The poboy was dry and the bread was stale, the soup was extremely salty. I think the draw is the ham but I was told to order the shrimp poboy. I probably will not eat here again, I had a much better poboy the next day at another restaurant.
Been there twice , excellent food and service both times.  Chorizo pizza was great. Glass of wine was mammoth!

The buffalo fries were a revelation. I got very hot with the special sauce (chipotle style ranch) and everything worked well together. Then you add the reasonably priced beer. A Dos was 4 bucks which made my meal 13$ and wow was it worth it. This place has like, 15 different sauces that I'm gonna need to try! I saw that on Tuesdays they have a boneless wings special that I'm going to have to hit, Can't wait!

Food and drinks were great. We can a bloody Mary, blood orange margarita and the house margarita. With 1205 next door and visible because of the glass wall it adds a lot to the restaurant. 
Brisket tacos are on point. The shells did split apart on one of them.  The chili was great. And the thai peanut burger was amazing. 

Would go again
Worst winghouse wings I've ever had. I don't ordinarily complain about food but these wings tasted worse than Walmart chicken.  Horrible. I wouldn't return and definitely won't recommend this place.

My first time getting food from here was awesome! Very fresh and seasonal. The Pork Bun was delicious. The Cod bun was so fresh and the homemade Tartar Sauce was phenomenal. With just the right amount of saltiness from the capers. They ended up giving us an extra salad and the tomatoes were easily the best tomatoes I've had in 2018. Greens were also incredible. The meal is a little bit on the pricier side but the quality makes it all worth it and you do not leave hungry.

Found this place on Yelp!!!  If there had been regular chairs instead of stools and easier parking it would be a 5. But it is the perfect marina spot!!  Lunch on the dock! Wings give Spillway in Bowling Green a run for their money!!! Husband loved the catfish, I had the cod. Asked for French fries VERY WELL DONE and they were perfect! 4 Yuengling, 2 entrees and a huge appetizer. More than we could eat and was less than $50 before tip. Don't be an ass, tip for great service!!  Big military presence for guard weekend - go troops!  Server Hannah is the BEST!  Go Army Guard - we forgive you, Hannah. Air Guard here! Weekend breakfast in summer if you want it!  Live music every Friday and Saturday night!  While sitting here for lunch we heard Joan Jett, Journey, Cyndi Lauper, Foreigner, REO Speedwagon, and others that were pleasing and understandable.

I ordered the onion bhaji and the aloo papri chaat (veganized). 
Thank you for having vegetarian and vegan friendly options!
I had no problem with anything I consumed. 
The price is good considering the portion sizes of the appetizers. My two orders cost $9 and I couldn't even finish them.
The samosas are HUGE; I'm pretty sure the two that you get will fill you up if you aren't splitting it with other people. The onion bhaji (comparable to vegetable fritters) was great on its own but with the tamarind sauce it is amazing~
I really enjoyed the aloo papri chaat that i ordered as my entree. I usually don't like cold potato dishes but this was very tasty! 
The waitress did a great job checking up on is and refilling water as needed. 
I'm overall a very satisfied customer with the experience I had at this location.

Just finished lunch here with my brother in law and nephews.  I'm an avid yelp user who does not take the time to really write reviews.  However, this lunch was so good I had to join the other users singing their praises. My burger was easily the best one I've had in years, and I've been around a bit.  Better than Blue Duck, Ambler Feedstore and Grub Burger.  It was covered in bleu cheese (not just a few crumbles), bacon, tons of caramelized onions and a healthy dose of the chipotle mayo.  It came out hot enough to burn the roof of my mouth.  The messy tots with the cheese sauce, bacon and jalapenos were also piping hot, and enough for 4 people.  My brother in laws wings were huge (I'll be getting them next time) and looked and smelled excellent.  The salad my 1 nephew got probably could have fed 3 people.  Our waitress was perfect, and she had more personality than the last 10 servers I've met combined.  Just an all around excellent job.  Thank you and I will be back.
The authentic Philly Steak and Cheese. Hole in the wall, my kind of place, but they have a much larger place down the street. Very generous portion!
Wow Ronnie is the worst bartender ever. Learn how to bartend. No wonder why I hate this bar. Only a couple awesome people work here. Everyone else sucks.

I came  here with a large party of 15, the space is great and the servers were very nice. I expected more from the food, though. The Mozzarella Al Basilico didn't taste fresh. The veal medallions lacked flavor. I chose a cake for dessert but it was too dry. This review feels mean, but I just wasn't impressed. I won't be back, since there are plenty more impressive Italian BYOs nearby.

Took the family for a Friday night dinner.  Family of 5.  Place was packed which we expected for a weekend. 

4 Italian entrees and a burger ordered. We couldn't even get a 10" cheese pizza in less than an hour (seems rather poor service for a dine in customer) so our youngest opted for a burger. 

Salads were drenched in dressing, and small at that.

Seafood soup...a number of the mussels weren't opened, and couldn't be opened...which means they were bad.  The rest of the seafood was rubbery and just over cooked. 

Chicken Alfredo...taste was off and needed seasonings (salt at a minimum) which we didn't have at the table and couldn't get from our waitress. 

Ravioli with meatballs, decent dish although the meatballs were slightly off as well. 

The chicken parmesan was the only decent meal. Even the burger tasted like it had been pulled out of the freezer and cooked.

Iced tea had a weird aftertaste. It tasted like raspberry iced tea, even though I ordered a straight iced tea. Wife had an Arnold Palmer and said she noticed the same thing. 

We really had high hopes for this place as it's close by and has rave reviews...we were extremely  disappointed after spending over $100 for 5 people. 

We may try their pizza for takeout, but won't be going back.

Had to visit since we saw the oyster challenge on man vs food. You have to get there before they open as there is a line all day long. I recommend the chargrilled oysters over just raw oysters as their raw oyster we just ok and I was a little disappointed. Butter Bean dis with alligator was really good. Happy we visited but was not really impressed.

Very tiny place just a tiny bit off the main strip.
It seemed like it was a college buddy who swore he could make you the best gyro's you ever ate. So he starts cooking in his dorm room closet on his bunsen burner as you sit uncomfortably on his milk crate ...trying to ignore the flies, the unwashed furniture around you and the fact that the gyro really isn't that great but you want to be polite as you are sitting so close to his cooking area that he is looking at you with every flip of pita, as his hopeful eyes wait for approval of his basic cooking skills.  A longer sentence you ask? Simply not possible. 

You can ask for a cup with your can or bottle of soda. 
They do not have ice. (?!?!?! How do you...? Forget it.) I"m an ice person. *shrug*
The gyro was Ok. 

Bottom line: There are SO many places to eat within sneezing distance that are better by far.  
Little or no effort was put into this restaurant.
It's a mini fridge, a tiny stove, and a cash register.  
-----------------------------------------
Note ... there is another Gyro place that has as similar name so is constantly being mistaken for each other.

Food: 3
Decor: 4
Ambiance: 4.5
Service: 2.5
Value: 2.5

This place had really good entree salads. It was a decent spot for the mall, and felt less chain like than the other dining options.
Tacos were awesome- they were out of Patron so couldn't get the margaritas we wanted. Service was really friendly. Salsa bar is great too

Sorry to say IT was the WORST food for mexican EVER, first The ICE TEA, What can you do wrong with ICE TEA, IT was grainey, Still see the chunks, Bottle powder, Terrible, Then I asked for CORN TORTIAs with warm butter, I got Flour tortia COLD with Hard cold butter, Then I ordered Enchilida, and taco, The taco came on its side on the plate with all the stuff hanging out, ( THE TACO SHELL was for sure store bought,) HORIBLE, fell apart on plate, The Enchilida, ORANGE SAUCE, HORIBLE, NO FLAVOR, Should have onions and be a good quality corn tortia with a red sauce so you can taste what is in side, Sorry Guys but it really was horible, NO FLAVOR and after pay $41.00 for our food, NOT worth 10.00. IF Gordon Ramsey from Hells Kitchen was there he would shut you down, OR Robert Irvine from HGTV Kitchens He would run you out of town, Get some Help, Do some good research on REAL MEXICAN FOOD,,,,,

My boyfriend and I ate at Romanza's on a slow Tuesday night.  For being an upscale place , we were very surprised at how cold and  rude the hostess Jasmine was to us. Not a good start. Then appeared our server Susan. Susan had such a great personality. She was delightful and provided us with excellent service. I had the italian trio and my boyfriend had the lasagna. The food was wonderful !!! I would have rated 5 stars if not for the beginning.

I'm sorry, is it impolite to take a bite, exclaim it's splendor, and repeat? If so, I don't want to be right. From the fresh baked bread with accompanying dippers to the handmade pasta (cacio de pepe will give you chills it's so fantastic) make this newer hot spot a great place to gather and dine. The lunch special is wonderful. Be sure you have the chopped salad. Like do it.
Very good quality ingredients. The pita was a bit small but very good. The baklava was excellent.a good choice for a light meal.

Great place to pick up Indian food on the go!

It's conveniently located right by Jefferson. There are tables to sit at inside, but they have a buffet that is really popular, especially at lunch time. I usually go and pick up from the buffet, but they have a much wider selection on their menu and that food is also excellent. 

They are closed on Mondays, so keep that in mind. Be sure to get their rewards card which they stamp each time you go - after 10 stamps you get up to 1lb of food free. 

Note: in order to cash in your free meal, you must choose food from the buffet. I made the mistake once of ordering food off of the menu and then having to pay full price because the voucher was only for up to 1lb of food from the buffet. It was frustrating to find that out at the register (that rule was not clearly stated on the rewards card), so I say that here to give you a heads up. 

Overall, it's a great place!
I didn't eat here, just had drinks. The service was really bad. We would have ordered another round of drinks but we gave up. I cannot speak on the food.

Best food ever; never had a bad meal here.
Prices are very good and size is bigger than they need to be.

I love this place!!!!

Walked in for breakfast, super cute, clean, great music (they were playing b b king). I ordered the breakfast sandwich and was very surprised how much I liked the blood orange jam. Very chill atmosphere. I would definitely come back for lunch. Photo is of the Eggs Benedict.

Always willing to try Mexican food anywhere I go!! I definitely will recommend Mony's if youre in SB!! Order inside & sit outside or take it with you. So the tacos are a good size-3 bites & youre done. Lots of onion & cilantro and the best part .....LOTS OF SALSAS!!! Mix & match or go simple! The carne asada was on point - big chunks, little chunks, crunchy chunks - oh yea!!! Al pastor - too sweet for me - they cook it with pineapple....not my cup of tea but others may like it :) Chips, jarritos, & complimentary water...nice touch! Sorry no pictures...we just couldn't wait to dive right in!! Lol!!

Beer was mostly tasty.  Liked Rock 'n Rolla and Hand of God, but Training Day and Death from Above left something to be desired.  

Food was solid.  Bar food style which is fine and appropriate.  Burger a little over done.  Wife and son liked their bugers and chicken wraps.  Pretzel bites and Fried Green Bean were pretty good.

Loved the atmosphere with the open garage doors and outside seating.  Seems like a fun place to hang out.  Staff was friendly and helpful.

This review is coming off of a phenomenal New Year's Eve date night dinner. They had a special menu for the holiday, which differed from the everyday dinner menu. We had a salmon starter, which was delicious and so unique. I had the New York Strip and my partner had a Mahi Mahi Tuna plate, both of which were enjoyed heartily. The apple strudel dessert was perfect to finish off the meal.

We've been here for brunch as well and it didn't disappoint. Graham has been our server both times and has been so kind and attentative. The food, the service, the cute atmosphere, there's nothing not to like here! Definitely would recommend.

All these people are way too picky!  I don't know what they are expecting but for my family Knight's is perfect.  We've gone a few times for takeout and eat in.  Every time everyone has been pleased with their food.  Their calzone was delicious and freshly prepared (unlike other establishments that have them pre-made and sitting out all day).  My favorite is the spaghetti with mushroom sauce.  I do wish it came with a salad free of charge instead of bread but overall it is satisfying.  I also love that there are always leftovers that I can pack up for lunch the next day.  My husband has gotten sandwiches and chicken Marsala.  He enjoyed the sandwiches and thought the Marsala was just okay.

   Every time we go the staff are courteous and helpful.  It's my favorite . . . I don't feel like cooking dinner let's eat out fare in town!  Give Knights a try, I'm hoping you enjoy it as much as my family!

When making the reservation, we were not informed that it was restaurant week. We purposely went to this restaurant to try the crab cakes but they were not on the menu due to the restaurant promo. It's also not a family friendly menu and the waiter would not allow any subs for our 5 yr old.  We felt rushed and wouldn't recommend for a next visit.

Ambiance:  Inside is bright, clean and decorated traditional Greek style in whites and blues.  There is outside seating as well, but is near a very busy and crowded street.  The owner has tried planting flowers to reduce the noise, but people have either stolen them or vandalized them.

Staff:  Friendly, relatable and quick with service.  I ended up moving inside because of the loud street and they were nice about accommodating me.  My server was excellent and very efficient.

Food:  I ordered the special, fish kabobs.  The lunch portion was huge.  I have plenty for at least two additional meals. It included grilled salmon, grouper and shrimp with tomato sauced green beans and rice.  The salmon was slightly on the fishy side.  The shrimp a teeny bit rubbery.  The grouper was the best.  It was thick and tasted very fresh.  The side salad was okay.  It had a nice flavor, the feta cheese was a nice addition,  but the lettuce was a little on the warm side.  I prefer it much colder.  For dessert I had the warm custard with the philo crust, drizzled honey, powdered sugar and cinnamon with dipping sauces of chocolate and raspberry.  It was very good.  I didn't care for the chocolate sauce combined, but I liked the raspberry.

Overall, I had a wonderful experience.  And will definitely return.

Ok this would not usually be my kind of place to dine since I'm not a big meateater but a friend had some type of VIP card and asked me to go. So why not try it since they have salad bar.

Well the salad bar has an assortment of salad type items and cold appetizers. Sushi, tappas, roasted veghies, salads, pickled items, seafood salads, veggies . There's something for everyone. I enjoyed most of the cold salad items except for the potato salad, it tasted store bought and texture of the potatoes were off. As for the hot items in the salad bar area, they have soup, beans and rice, and potatoes gratin. I had the potato especially again and the texture was off again but this time it reminded me off an cold baked potato and the sauce was soupy.  Everything beside the potatoes were good and great flavor.

As for the meat I tasted some of the items. The pork tenderloin had good flavor but was over cooked,  the pork rib  had great flavor and was tender, the chicken good flavor , hot and juicy. Overall the meat was good including the lamb chop but the pork tenderloin was overcooked and that could have been because it was close to the end of it. Lastly the rolls on the table were delicious and the service was great.

The only reason Cafe Eau is getting three stars instead of two is because they have a lovely pool/patio area - which is where I dined last night. Other than that, this place is overpriced and the service is "meh".

Went up to the Chase Park Cinema last night at 6 pm and purchased movie tickets for a 7:30 show. This should give me and my companions plenty of time to eat and have a cocktail, while still being able to find a decent seat in the theatre, right? Wrong! Service was sloooooow! Our waitress was very nice, but I'm pretty sure she was the only one working the patio area, and there are a LOT of tables to cover. She should have had help, especially on a 80-degree evening. 

Service was so slow that we BARELY got out of there at 7:35 and ended up having to sit separately at the theatre. And there were only 3 of us. Granted, we were seeing the new "Twilight" movie and it would have been packed regardless, but still. We planned accordingly and the service at Cafe Eau sort of blew it. 

Maybe dining inside is a different experience, but I won't be coming back here if I need to be somewhere else within a 2-hour time frame. Time suckage, indeed!

We were visiting from Los Angeles for a wedding in New Orleans and happened to go to this place near the hotel we were staying at in Metairie.  For a random find, this was one of the better pizza places we've experienced.  We've always looked for pizza of the kind they serve at Princess Cruise ships and this was like it and very much better.  Its unfortunate we discovered this on our last day - otherwise we would have eaten here more than once during our visit.

After ordering, I waited a good 15 minutes before anyone came back out. But it was not to place food in front of me. It was the waiter giving me the phone so that I could spell out the website of the menu to a customer. o.0 

It wasn't like he asked me to do so; he just handed me the phone. I felt bad for the guy that his Chinese accent was probably too strong that someone with an equally strong country accent couldn't understand. I may have a useless degree in linguistics, but translation was not my field of study.

I rarely order appetizers, but after the nice complimentary dish at Chinatown up the street, I thought the Zing Zing Plate would be similar. It's just a bunch of deep fried won-tons, filled and unfilled. While I am still weirded out by cream cheese in my Chinese food, the plate was decent for 99 cents. What I did not like was when I was asked for what type of sauce I wanted and he came back out and gave me the sauce in packets. 

For whatever reason, I didn't order my usual go-to dish (anything with a sweet sauce). Instead, I ordered what I was hoping would be some sort of slice roasted duck on a bed of greens. Instead, I got what was obviously duck from a previous dish, deep fried, and sliced on overcooked carrots, a few broccoli, and water chestnuts (which I loathe). And in a nondescript brown sauce. It was horrible, but I ate the bits of duck that I liked, and pushed the food around the rest of the time.

Lots of booths and tables. For 5PM, there wasn't much of a crowd. A few people had takeout. But overall, it was empty.

I noticed a buffet area, but I think that was only for set times.

I politely took the leftovers with me, but then walked several blocks up the street to dispose of it next to my bus stop.

Decent food and cold draft beer. Wooden countryside interior , lounge style sitting, plenty of TV's, free parking, walk in- you probably will find place to sit it is big enough. Outdoor fireplace with wooden sitting was great and nice to look at. We stayed for hours!

The wife and I visited Mixto on Sunday for dinner. We have had drinks and bar bites here previously and enjoyed the restaurant. The venue is decorated beautifully with paintings and decor highlighting the Latin culture. We made reservations for 6:30 but arrived early to enjoy some drinks at the bar. Love that their happy hour is available Sunday. The bartender was swamped having to make drinks for the tables and take care of the bar orders. We observed that he was working alone and remained patient. Once he took our order the drinks were made quickly and were delicious. We enjoyed some bottles Dos Equis light and dark, caipirinhas and margaritas. At 6:30 we left to be seated for dinner. We sat in the upstairs dining area. Our waitress Maria came over took our drink order and gave us time to order. We started with the Calamares Fritos. 
When the calamari was brought to our table I thought it looked overcooked. The breading reminded me of deep fried chicken . I was pleasantly surprised to find it was not over cooked! It was light cooked to perfection and served with a tasty marinara...  I chose the Bandeja Tipica Seared top round steak, ground beef, crispy pork rind, arepa, avocado, egg, rice, beans, maduros and Colombian chorizo. The missus ordered the Paella Valenciana Saffron broth, rice, whole lobster, chicken, shrimp, squid, octopus, mussels, Cuban sausage scallops, green peas, fava beans, clams, maduros. We also had black beans and pinto beans on the side. My rice in my dish was mixed with black beans, one of the things you can customize and I ordered my egg sunny side up.
My dish was Amazing! The steak was so tender and delicious. The ground beef was more like chopped brisket and was yummy. I pulled the crispy pork rind apart and enjoyed the fatty portion and then the meaty part. I mixed the egg in with rice YUM! The maduros were soft and sweet. I was stuffed and didn't make it to my chorizo. I did have a piece out of my wife's dish and it was good. My wife thoroughly enjoyed her meal. She said everything was cooked to perfection nothing was over or undercooked and it was all seasoned well and very tasty. The portions were definitely enough for two.  To her delight she has enough leftover for lunch. She did experience a few pieces of shell in some bites. 
So glad we finally experienced dinner!
Love the ambiance of this place. The bartenders are always on point with  their drinks and recommendations. I highly suggest the truffled popcorn and the espresso martini.

This review is for delivery only: The food was very tasty & came in generous portions. This is probably the best Caribbean food I've had in Philadelphia. The main problem is that it takes forever to get the food delivered. Many thanks to Yelpers who warned about this issue so I could order the food well in advance.

Food Summary (I use ^ to indicate a half-star and * for a full star. So, ***^ means 3.5 stars):
****^ Jerk chicken was great: marinated and flavourful 
****^ Oxtails are tasty, and include beans & potato in the stew
***^ Candy yams are good 
**** Collard greens are super flavourful, salty but tasty
*** Baked mac & cheese is fine
*** Broccoli was steamed & simple, plain
***^ Callaloo and saltfish: tasty, callaloo was silky in texture. This came with ripe plantain, dumpling, green banana, yellow yam. I liked the sweet ripe plantain, but wasn't a huge fan of the others, especially not the dumpling which was very dense & plain. I'd prefer the option of getting other sides instead.

Delivery
Got delivery through Uber Eats & it took quite a while. From time of order, the food took ~1.5 hours to arrive instead of the 45 minutes originally quoted on the Uber Eats website. Uber Eats kept updating with a later and later delivery time, so I'd recommend ordering well in advance before you're too hungry.

Found this little gem as I was coming home from a trip and I'll definitely be back! There is a nice variety of foods on the menu, the bagels and spreads are freshly made, and the service is fast and friendly! I got the hangover cure as well as an oatmeal raisin cookie and both were AMAZING!

This place doesn't sell any fries!! I was flabbergasted when I tried to order fries and I couldn't ! The donair was pretty good but the super seemed like a small at other places. I was hungry after it so get a jumbo if you are hungry. The guy was really nice and service is quix

The food is amazing. We love the machaca breakfast tacos. There is plenty of meat n eggs in the taco. The cheese quesadilla with machaca was great again plenty of meat n eggs as well Price is great too. Go and try..

Can't say enough nice things about this place. Service was AMAZING, they made us feel like family, spent time with us, never made us feel rushed. Food was so good, everything tasted fresh and homemade. Portions were generous, margaritas and mojitos were delicious and not over-sweet. Restaurant was clean and bright, doesn't feel like a tourist trap. Such a great find in New Orleans.

I probably would have given a 3-star had it not been for our waiter.  Aarran S. was our waiter.  He was excellent.  He was friendly, knowledgeable and attentive.  That's what I look for when I go to a restaurant -- which is a LOT!  My wife always makes her favorite thing for dinner -- reservations!  We probably eat out about 4 out of every 7 evenings.

The food was good, but not enough to rate a 5-star from me.  My wife and I got the cheese ravioli.  Our friend opted for the shrimp scampi and shrimp Alfredo.  They liked their food, as well.

The break sticks and salad was great.
Worse service in the city. Has been this way since I was a kid. Hoping with future expansions in the area it will increase their level of service and ability to serve large lines.

So so so good, brings back a ton of childhood memories of my adoptive parents encorporating Russian foods and cultures into me and my sisters upbringing so we'd still have our Russian roots and memories! Fair warning the Latkes are quite greasy so I'd pat them off a little before eating them. Otherwise 10/10 recommend, I love when borscht is vibrant red you know it's fresh if it's a beautiful red color! Adding this to my list of lunch places when I'm hungry at work!

I must say this place never disappoints! The environment is always so chill and the music is good. My guy and I have been here twice and both experiences were great! The menu has a lot to offer depending on your taste. I had the Caribbean Bowl and my guy had the Blue Crab Bowl and both were delicious. Both dishes were flavorful and tasty! I will definitely be back to The Hall on Franklin!
After a chardonnay glass lined with dust, mediocre sushi, and the average price of a roll being about $2.00 more than what we've experienced, we won't be going back.

Cracker Barrel is the same no matter what city or state.  Just plain ordinary.  Now, wouldn't you expect a place that specializes in breakfast to include omelets?  Well, the do have them - just not on the menu!!  Must be saving money!!
Although, based on their origins, I understand them not having bagels BUT, for a national company, you would think they might want to include such an outstanding staple :)
Cracker Barrel is the place to go for breakfast when you can't find another place.

We just left this restaurant this morning, we were a party of 6. The service was HORRIBLE! My son recommened this place so that's how we went there. The waitress gave us wheat toast, (really? )She never asked us WHAT we wanted, gave us the wrong orders,  had to get up and ASk  for water, to go containers, and the bill twice. I'll never be back, too many places to go to..figure it out guys.
Such a cool place!  The building is beautiful and it has a great New Orleans atmosphere!!  The owner went out of his way to take care of us.  I will definitely go back again.

Ate inside at the bar. Bartender was friendly. Burgers were amazing. We were in town for a wedding and needed a bite to eat so we stopped here because Siri suggested it. It was a win! would go back just not sure next time we will be in the area! lol
A nice alternative to Starbucks. If you wak into a coffee shop and over 80% of laptops used are Macs you know you're in good company!

Flying Pie marked its return to Broadway Avenue with the opening of their new store at the former Buster's location. For years, Flying Pie operated a hole-in-the-wall shop next to the Suds Tavern. They left that location after they were evicted due to someone buying out most of the businesses along that strip just down from Boise State University. That company's plans were disrupted when it turned out Cobby's had a long-term lease and they weren't able to get that last building. Meanwhile, Flying Pie had gone and was later replaced by the Pie Hole.

The Buster's location gives the Pie a lot more room inside -- room for at least 100 diners -- and they've added an outdoor seating area, a first for the Flying Pie. There's even an outdoor standup counter. 

The Pie hosted a soft opening Sunday (ahead of their 3 p.m. Tuesday grand opening) as a benefit with the $10 cost donated to the Life's Kitchen program, which teaches culinary and life skills to at-youth risk. That program does a wonderful job.

During three serving times, each accommodating 100 diners, Flying Pie debuted a new personal size lunch pizza with a thin artisan crust. I found the crust superior to their regular dough. It had a lighter, crisper texture.

There were also new pizza offerings, including a Thai chicken and an El Diablo, with Basque chorizo and Cajun andouille sausage and a habanero sauce. Both were excellent, along with a roasted mushroom pizza. 

The building is unlike any of the Pie's other Boise and Meridian locations. it has an industrial look, with lots of stainless steel and even a roll-up garage door that I imagine will come open when the weather warms up. Also new for the Flying Pie is an outdoor seating area and a stand-up bar with a fire pit over the edge of the counter.

The downside will be parking. There's limited lot parking and nearby businesses and apartments have signs telling customers of the former Buster's at that location not to park in their lots.

This location looks like a winner. Welcome back to Broadway Avenue. You've been gone too long.

I returned for lunch two days after the official opening and had one of their artisan pizzas, which I learned will only be served at the Broadway location. I ordered the Carnivore, with red sauce, pepperoni, ham, Italian sausage, linguica, mushrooms, red peppers & sliced red onions on the artisan thin crust.

The pizza was great. I didn't realize they were offering table service at this location. No more listening for your name to be called and going to the counter. They also brought metal silverware wrapped in a napkin and at least two employees walked the floor, talking with diners and asking whether they were enjoying their meal.

The Broadway store is using a gas oven, different from the electric ovens used by the other locations. It fires hotter and cooks the pizzas quicker.

I downgraded my rating after a disappointing lunch experience. I ordered a Carnivore on the thin crust exclusive to the Broadway store. 

When the pizza arrived, it was lukewarm. That meant one thing: It came out of the oven and then sat forgotten for 10 minutes before it was brought to my table. That's the only explanation I could fathom.

The temperature was more like it would be if you had a few pieces left over at the end of the meal, not at the beginning.

It was funny, too, that the server brought a spatula but no plate. It would have been easy enough to get up and ask for one. Instead, I used the spatula to move pieces from one side of the serving pan to the other. Sometimes, you just have to laugh at the absurdness of it all.
Great place for a hot and delicious meal. My go-to take-out spot. They have authentic and Americanized Chinese food.  Try the dumplings in chili oil...mmmmm

First I should say that I love flatiron buildings. I want to give Old Point an extra star just for being in a charming flatiron. Indeed, the ambiance at night is great with the big windows and the glow of the neon shining in.... But, like Benjamin, I think I want Old Point to do just a yittle bit better. 

The food is good but it's not great. There are a decent amount of veggie options. The deluxe veggie nachos are excellent drunk food and the chili is pretty damn good. The Greek salad, veggie sands and veggie burger are just okay. They have a decent micro beer selection (last night I had a nice Upland amber on draught).

The service is spotty--sometimes it's fantastic and sometimes it's just weird (never awful, just off). It also gets terribly smoky when it's crowded and sometimes the music is just too loud. I think of this as a conversation bar so why is somebody's bad iPod soundtrack blasting at 9 p.m. on a Thursday night? 

Despite my complaints, I've obviously been to Old Point a lot. What can I say? I do like the atmosphere. With just a few tweaks, this place could be awesome so I'm trying to give a little tough love!

I'm so glad the awesome sales woman who knows her pastries and loves sharing the joy of them with others helped me pick out a chocolate ganache mouse with almond paste and a buttery crust tart.  It was delicious.  I hate half right away, but actually preferred the second half which had reached room temperature.

Perenn Bakery, the flagship location (even though this is actually the second location), has a slightly larger selection of pastries and breads and an actual menu of "entree" items. I already loved Perenn's pastries, and was so excited to taste the brunch. I honestly would only make the trek to Rancharrah for this particular location for a nice sit down brunch.

Now the food! I've gone with the Soft Scrambled Egg on a croissant each time I've visited. It is so good--why change it up if you've already found the winner! Based on an employee recommendation I added bacon jam--definitely do it!! Also, my favorite drink pairing (and perhaps favorite hot drink in town) is the chai latte with oat milk. Happy to report this location prepares the chai latte just as well, plus I get to drink it out of a mug rather than a paper cup. That's classy. 

Some notes if you haven't been to Perenn or are unfamiliar with their business. Be prepared to wait in line to order your food before sitting down. The time can be passed quickly by examining the menu on your phone--be sure to scan the QR code that is on the wall right as you walk in. Oh, and really read the menu--it's a bit confusing to read and determine which meal is right for you. Expect to pay a little bit more than expected, because the employees are compensated a bit more than expected. (Read the little sign by the register for more info). Be prepared for some deliciousness!
There food is good. But I think it's priced a bit on the high side . I think Steak & Shake has the same quality for less money.

Went here around 11-1130am for a brunch. Ended up ordering a hot chicken sandwich with a Caesar salad. 

The Caesar salad was pretty good- I don't like a ton of dressing and their wasn't a ton on it. 

The hot chicken sandwich was very good. I liked the sauce they used and the chicken was perfectly tender with the right amount of crispiness. 

We also had mimosas and they were good. This was a reasonably priced restaurant.

Ate here yesterday, after an exhausting shopping day. I called to check in for a group of five and a high chair. I was told brusquely, "Just tell us all that when you get here." The person who seated us, in the practically empty restaurant, tried to put us at a table for four. (Maybe he couldn't count?) When I objected, he said, "We can't put the high chair at any of the big tables." I had to suggest putting two smaller tables together. Would you really put that inexperienced a person in the reception area? 
Interesting menu, several of us ordered the steak and wedge salad. A lovely wedge of lettuce was plated with a small tender steak, roasted asparagus and GOLDEN beets. The lettuce was dressed with blue cheese, real bacon and extra SLICES of cheese. $17.95. Outstanding! Other members of the party had the shrimp tacos and a grilled chicken salad, both very good. Service was perfect, except for the guy up front. Would've been 5 stars without him.
I don't usually shop at Castleton, ended up there with family. Thought of Houlihan's because of many fond memories of meals at the old Glendale location. I will now add the Castleton Mall to my regular rounds, looking forward to ending at Houlihan's.

Being health conscious, I wouldn't really say that they have a lot of healthy options. We ended up getting the Mediterranean plate, grilled octopus and my BF splurged on the wings.

The Mediterranean plate was pretty good, I'd like the option of having veggies to dip into the hummus. The octopus was alright, I wasn't stoked on the idea that it came out already cut up instead of coming out whole. 

Not too bad for bar food.

Wow! Wow, wow, wow, wow, WOW! This place has such a good breakfast burrito - maybe the best I've ever had! The Protagonist Cafe is a coffee shop, but on Saturday and Sunday mornings, they sell breakfast burritos. (They also sell booze and some small gifts.)

I ordered a breakfast burrito with chorizo. They took a while to cook it bc they made it with love. It was outstanding, and it was huge! You can get two meals out of the burrito. I recommend getting the burrito to go bc after all that chorizo, eggs and cheese, it's time for a trip to the hopper, know what I'm saying? :) Plus, there was no room to sit inside or outside that Sunday morning. The place was packed. (Lots of cute ladies in there. :)) The staff was incredibly nice. They couldn't have been any nicer.
