Also, if you can, do not have Charity as your server. She really didn't pay any attention to us. Took our order, brought the food, brought the bill.

Lincoln Square is our favorite low-key place to visit for brunch.  This location is very similar to Lincoln Square's other local spots; busy atmosphere, friendly staff who know how to flip a table quickly, and a great menu that creatively tweaks the traditional stereotypical breakfast dishes.  Lincoln Square recently redesigned its menu to a large 2-sided sheet (versus the multi-sheet book they used to heave at you).  Menu favorites are still there, like Martin's Breakfast Bowl (eggs & chorizo over jalapeno corncakes) and the West Coast omelet (bacon, avocado, feta, tomato and onion). They still don't charge for egg white upgrades on omelets; score! My newest favorite dish is "The Alex" skillet; it has all the meats (sausage, bacon & ham) with a spicy Mexican twist (avocado, queso & pico), all drizzled with this delicious smoky chipotle Spanish sauce. The creamy chipotle drizzle is to die for and it ties all the flavors together well.  I definitely recommend this Lincoln Square location just as strongly as the other ones. It's a great place to take a picky eater; something for everyone on their menu!

Shrimp poboy was a 3/5 for me, the shrimp batter could use some heat from cayenne or something to that effect. Added Tabasco, oversight by not having Crystal sauce, and it was improved. Service was good, we sat at the bar. I understand the goal of the menu is to offer food from various places, but maybe trim it down a bit more? So many options caused a delay in ordering (slows the turn) and I would guess it elevates food cost. With 5400 sq feet in the square, rent can't be cheap and I'd like to see something survive in this space. A couple facility issues that can be easily addressed and not part of my rating: Lighting at the bar was distracting as it was dark behind the bar then very bright behind our seats. House music was way too loud but when the band returned, their volume was fine.

Our second visit to Clear Sky Draught House and it didn't disappoint.  The brisket (in any form) can't be beat.  Shared the brisket sliders with a side of mac and cheese.  But not any old mac and cheese--- instead it's build your own mac and cheese. We went with smoked Gouda and pulled pork in the mac and cheese.  

Amazing beer selection (I suggest trying  the Kentucky Bourbon Ale). Vibe was tight...  terrific live music and exceptional service  -- thanks Tiffany!

After having a horrible experience at Flap Jack, I decided to try this place since it's 3 mins away. 

The place is huge!!!!! I mean humungous! Tv's everywhere n a nice huge bar in the center of the restaurant. The booths were huge as well n everything is made out of wood.

I ordered the Fried Mozzarella, Jumbo Wings with Honey BBQ Sauce n my kid ordered the Fried Shrimp. Nothing was special about the food. Nothing at all. I ate it because I was still hungry from the Flap Jack Waffle Debacle smh... Nothing really impressive to say about my experience. Our server was nice but my overall experience was blah. 

There's really no need for me to go back.

Have been here in Houston & the food we received in Nashville from start to finish was under seasoned & not representative of what Tex-Mex is. If you add the fact that it's over priced... you'll be just as disappointed as I was. If you don't know Tex-Mex, this is a good option. But if you're from Texas....pass on this even though I know you miss good Mexican.
Amazing!  If you want healthy food that is out of this world, this is the place to go!
See the attached picture for what their idea of a serving of orange chicken is. This is literally the worst panda location I've ever been to. And I've been to them all over the country.

"Real food done real good" - I'd have to agree. We stumbled upon this place while staying in Bywater on holiday between Christmas and the New Year. Our party of 8 was directed to the bar upstairs for a 30 minute wait for a table. We were able to order drinks - excellent bloody Mary's - and even found spots to sit in while waiting for the actual table. I'm glad we were seated upstairs as I strongly preferred the ambiance to the downstairs area. 

I ordered the bubble and squeak, which I loved. The duck hash waffle was yummy, and the only disappointing meal was the crab cake breakfast special. 

Overall, Elizabeth's is great and in a very up and coming area with a ton of other fun places to bop around to. We will be back! Especially for the bloody Mary's.

Definitely give this place a try. The shrimp and grits ordered for an appetizer - excellent. Risotto with sirloin tips (cooked perfectly...shared, enough for two). Caesar salad was lacking in dressing and flavor. But overall, will return!

This is one of the best Asian markets I've been to! I know this may take away from the "authentic experience" aspect but the market is extremely clean and doesn't smell like most international markets smell. I am always eager for an international shopping experience and in many cases it's a full sensory experience but I really appreciate this particular market's cleanliness.

Though it seems a bit small, they appeared to have most of the main things I'd need from a Chinese grocery. They have a large meat/seafood selection in the back as well as produce. They have a wide variety of noodles up front and those are always well priced and fun to try!! There are kitchen utensils and supplies, teas, spices, decorations, and even cold beverages up front. The lady working was extremely friendly too. It was a great experience and I'm looking forward to my next trip through Nashville so I can stop by!

I eat at this place more than is probably healthy. Yes, it is essentially the local version of some chain that starts with a Q and ends with a Doba. The menu and style of the place are all very similar. I'm partial to Fast Burrito though. Much more flavor in the salsa and ingrediants. Essentially though, it is the same. So if you like the idea of places like Qdoba and Chipolte but don't like chains and waiting in line and not having anywhere to sit this is your spot. 

Hint, venture past just the burritos. The quesedillas are great and the nachos are probably the best downtown.

Met a friend for dinner and drinks tonight. Had the farmers market salad: fresh arugala, grilled corn, tomatoes and vinaigrette =yum. Dinner was the crusted sea bass, forbidden rice and asparagus. They can happily accommodate special diet needs with no fuss and no mistakes. Thank goodness for that because I have to be a pain and always ask for a special request. The drinks were amazing and dangerous! Fresh strawberry cosmos =o.m.g  I've eaten here many times before, always have left with a full, happy belly. This time was no exception. Thank you, chefs at Bistro 7= you know your stuff. :-)
Bring back .75 wing mondays. This was the best deal you guys had far. The new special is not very good.

This small French restaurant is easy to get to on the 40 bus. The staff are very nice and the food is amazing. It's a small restaurant and clearly popular, so you may have a wait. There's outdoor seating as well for when the weather is nice. I got a goat cheese, oregano, and roasted red pepper sandwich on crispy baguette which was to die for. My cafe au lait was very good as well. My friend got the red lentil soup and goat cheese and fig quiche. I tried the soup and it was very tasty. We are definitely returning because of their varied menu and delicious food, for a very reasonable price.

I got into an argument with the delivery driver because I didn't answer the phone and he was force to knock on the door.  

It took me less than 10 seconds to come to door after hearing the first knock, so I don't know why he was triggered.  

It's kinda fucked up 'cause the food was good. I just refuse to order from them again. He might remember the address and do a house special ball drop in my wonton soup.
I spent $68 tonight for 4 plates for dinner. It was incredibly gross! I won't be back.

if there is an option to put no stars that will be my rating for this sushi bar.  we came in and ordered our food, sashimi miso soup and bento boxes .  Another customer walked in and ordered their food and got served first with their food.  Their tea was just a lipton tea bag not a traditional japanese rice /jasmine tea.  We are visiting from California their food is horrible , bad customer service, slow and not i would consider sushi place.  Will definitely not coming here anymore.  I don't know how they get 4.5 yelp stars but this is not accurate.  The server  gave us the cup and put her finders inside the cup.  What is that!!!!  That is unsanitary, did she took the food handler test?  this is not a Japanese food ,  i'll say a copycat!!!

Armpit of cheese steaks, my wife wanted to go again, again cashier had gloves on tendered my transaction and then continued to wrap up food without changing them again. A customer was handed a thin paper bag in front of me, it split open and the cashier just flung her a plastic bag which she struggled to open, I helped her.They handed me my food and the cashier said have a good one, oh my God these individuals or absolutely awful, actually management is!

The steak was great as usual from Jim's. The line cook was on point. But the girls behind the counter were a bit preoccupied with talking and phone calls. So they had to ask the same question a few times. It was not busy but I could say if it were this could slow things down. This Jim's takes cards also. Parking is easy, it's in a strip mall. As usual awesome sammich.

This place was superb.  We had oysters six different ways, and Shrimp Arnaud for appetizers.  The bread was fresh and delicious and I had to dip it in everything I could find.  We ate two big loaves of this stuff (which can partially be the reason I could barely move when we left).   I had an assorted green salad with hearts of palm, micro herbs, etc.  Really tasty.  For the entrees, I had Filet of Beef Charlemond (with mushrooms and bernaise) and he had a steak with a soft shell crab.   Both were very good.  And, for dessert, we had the Banana's Foster.  It's probably not the best Bananas Foster I've had, but it was definitely good, and the service was great.  Thanks for a wonderful birthday dinner.   Best fine dining type meal I've ever had in New Orleans to date.  I would come her often if I had a lot of money and lived closer.

My favorite Indian restaurant in the midwest. The staff is very friendly and remembers my husband and I every time we visit. We lived in England for 3 years and once we didn't visit for 1 year - and the owner still remembers us! The spiciness is amazing and flavor complex! The atmosphere is pretty and their vegetarian dishes have a great depth of flavor. I must reiterate, when you go to an Indian restaurant in the United States and you see British, Pakistani and Indian people in the restaurant, you know it is authentic!

If you are a wheat beer lover this is your brewery! Tons of different beers to sample and at a reasonable price. My only complaint is that I wish it was closer to Philadelphia (although it is close to the outlet mall which is how we found it!) the food is good too! ($1 tacos are basically unbeatable!) a little out of the way but totally worth the drive! I do wish, however, there were more frequent tours of the brewery itself (only at 2 pm and 4 pm on weekends)- we will have to return for the tour!

Prices are affordable and portions are generous! However, the food wasn't too impressive. We ordered the beef stew thick noodle soup, the Beijing signature noodle, and the dan dan mian. I think a big issue for me for all three noodle dishes was that I wasn't a big fan of the noodles themselves. They just had a very flat texture, and they lacked bounce/chew? It's hard to describe!

#20. Beef stew thick noodle soup was a pretty standard beef noodle soup. The beef itself was quite tasty, but the soup was rather bland. This was my least favorite dish.

#19. Beijing signature noodles, aka zha jiang mian, was the best of the three dishes, but overall not worth returning to get. The name of the dish on the English menu is rather unrevealing, but it's essentially a meat, veggie and bean paste mix. I was a bit disappointed at first, only because the picture on the menu looked like jajangmyeon, which is the Korean equivalent of these bean paste noodles. Those are thicker, saucier and sweeter than the Chinese version, which can be less saucy and the taste of bean paste is usually stronger. This dish definitely could have used more sauce, since the sauce to noodle ratio was a rather low.

#18. Dan dan mian. The spice did overwhelm the other flavors of the sauce though. I've had better!

Jeannines is ALL about the people that work there who make you feel so welcome and special!!! Sundays are all about a great breakfast and ordering with the lovely and talented duo of Michelle and Renee. Martin is best barista ever. Love this place

I would give this place 10 stars if I could. Upon walking in, the smells from the pizza oven enraptured my taste buds. The menu had a variety of specialty pizzas but if you're feeling creative, you can build your own.

I had the Link In, which has sausage and I added fresh cut grape tomatoes, it was heavenly. Just the right amount of spicy and sauce was extra fresh, not from a can. My cousin had cheese and pepperoni and she loved it just as much as I did. 

I wish they had this close to home, I would probably go at least once a week... bring it to Miami! Cheers

The burg diner is INCREDIBLE!! Amazing food, amazing service, all around amazing! 
Love that they are NOW OPEN TIL 9 ON THE WEEKDAYS!! Will be back for much much more!
Wife and I the fish and chips and the bean dip to start with.  Nice place and atmosphere.  Waitress was very nice and the food was tasty.  Will come back!!

FRESH. And brilliant. Are the words to describe this experience. I never knew fruit and sushi would pair together so well! Hubby and I ordered the "Feed Me - all raw" omakase (6 courses $70) and each course shocked my taste buds. I don't recall all the specific names but please feast your eyes on these photos. Drool. Each dish was creative and beautifully plated and by the end we were definitely full. We also ordered the Curried flavor dumplings which I expected to feel heavy but was surprisingly very light and delicious as well. 

Based on Yelp photos the menu and omakase items change every so often so you may not get the exact same dishes as these photos. But trust this chef! This experience was amazing and I'd recommend it to anyone for a special night out. 

*also, service was great. We had reserved a table outside (because covid) but didn't realize the table was on a small porch and directly in front of a loud street with cars zipping by - not exactly what we had imagined for a nice omakase experience - and the ambience inside was too good to miss. Staff was so kind to arrange an indoor table last minute (even though they were spacing out seats and it was very limited inside.) thank you!

Fast service, always in stock of what I need! Thank you!

Even during a rush they are quick with making food. I've never had a problem with what they've made for me.

I must say that I was pleasantly surprised by Rizzutos. I tend to not venture too far from Uptown, Mid-City, and the French Quarter. I was craving Italian. Several friends recommended Rizzutos. So, off to Lakeview I went. The exterior was beautiful. At first, I thought it was just a nice house. Then, I saw the sign. The interior was upscale. The menu was nice. Not only do they have a nice selection of pasta, but they also have various steaks. I had a dirty martini that was AWESOME. I was pleased that they have blue cheese stuffed olives. For my entree, I had Wagyu Bolognese. It was rich and meaty. It was exactly what I wanted. With my entree, I had a glass of Terra d Oro Sangiovese. This red wine was amazing.  I was so pleased with dinner I treated myself to a piece of chocolate cheesecake.  I will diet tomorrow.

This is my new favorite restaurant in New Orleans! The service was phenomenal, food was fabulous, the wine list is fantastic! The Chilean sea bass (fresh today) was so darn good I wanted to order it (a second time) for dessert! The wine list is eclectic, with a great price point. Our waiter, Jason, was great. He even walked out to the curb to help us catch a cab! We will be back in December, and will be back at this restaurant for another awesome meal!

Stopped in for lunch because I was craving wings. I'm not a big sauce guy and usually prefer dry rubs. The only dry rub available is the house dry rub, which our waiter said was really good.

Wings came... nice, golden, and crispy... smoked not fried. 

The house dry rub was on point. Definitely worth trying.
Guys are super helpful and friendly. Will return when ever i have a bike related question or need work done. The Coffee shop next door is pretty awesome as well!

First I want to start off saying coming in the hostess was very dry and didn't make me feel like my experience was going to be great we sit down our waitress was nice but very slow taking our drinks we waited at least ten minutes for out soda, after the drinks came we waited another twenty minutes before our food order was taken. The bread we were given while waiting was stale and cold it was nasty. We ordered the monty cristo and when harry met sally ......both sucked and I'll explain first with the monty cristo my fiance has had it before so he was excited to try it here. Foul one the fries it came with looked like they sat under a heat lamp for eight hours they were hard and burnt tasting the sandwich was over buttered and greasy I squeezed it to find about a pint of oil and butter ooozing out of it!!! It literally gave my fiance a stomach ache!!!! NOT A GOOD SIGN! So on to my sandwich... When harry met sally the pastrami was amazing but not hot enough and the brie it came with was not smooth and creamy but very cold and hard it was hard to eat! Over all I gave this place a two because of our horrible experience but I am willing to try this place again and review again and re rate I know not every place will serve perfectly every time but I hope next time its a way better experience!!!!.....BTW free dessert doesn't make up for crappy food or service please work on this!!!!

Found this little gem along our way from Cali to Kentucky on our Whiskey Tour.  This is a distillery, brewery AND pub.  Steve, the owner and head distiller, went out of his way to give us a tour upon our request.  We got to see the brand new Vendome still, which is replacing their older, smaller still.  After the tour we sat down in their pub.  They only had 3 Whiskeys available for tasting, but they sure were good!  Also had a fresh salad and a good burger.  Left with 2 t shirts and a bottle of Hopskey Hop Infused Whiskey.

Use to love this place. Theyve changed some things and made it formal. Not sure why they did it but might have to stick to other places from now on.  Great place for a date but make sure to arrive early.

My friends and I stumbled on Cafe La Maude on Labor Day looking to grab a bite to eat before we all went back to our respective cities. We were in town for the Made in America festival.

The place was packed! The owner greeted us and told us he would try to seat us altogether in a short amount of time. He checked on us regularly while we waited. We thought about leaving but he was so hospitable we wouldn't dare leave. After about 20 minutes we were seated.
 
I ordered the Parisian Zá and it was incredible! Even the fruit and salad was good - so fresh. 

The next time I'm in Philly, I'll be sure to have brunch at Cafe La Maude!

They have such great food!!! I have never had a bad meal there. Some of my favorites are the 66th St. chicken, Cobb salad wrap, and breakfast quesadillas. I also love their broccoli, coleslaw, Bd sweet tea. We go often. The staff is always so nice!

Absolutely the best!  I enjoyed some of their yummy desserts for the first time yesterday and will definitely be back!  Their wedding cupcake was the best I've ever had and I have done a good bit of traveling throughout the U.S. and internationally.  Their creme brûlée was delicious!  This place is totally worth the price and a short walk from all the hot spots in Old Gretna.  My how that street has changed over recent years :)  I need to make another stop at Amore before leaving town Monday!

Amazing Mexican! We were seated right away in the beautiful patio right next to the fountain with beautiful white lights overhead. Perfect ambiance! The guacamole and chips were delicious (and totally addictive!) and the fish tacos were incredible! Highly recommend. Definitely worth it!

Excellent. The best gulf shrimp and crab. The desserts were the best... bread pudding, pecan pie and banana foster. And don't forget the BBQ oysters and alligator bites!!!! The service was outstanding..... Cici was the excellent

My first experience with Saige was good. I had a large pick up and the cashier was friendly and patient. The food is good, they have a large selection to choose from. Their smoothies are decent, no artificial colors or flavors. However the second time the cashier was not as friendly, and forgotten my friend had paid for her food and attempted to charge her twice. Was not crowded so confused how she had forgotten, but everyone has their days.

Highly recommend!! I was beyond amazed by the quality and craftsmanship that was put into making my meal. Absolutely incredible. Milkshakes are hands down best in the area. The customer service was fantastic, throughout the whole experience they were kind, courteous, and ready to help with any questions. Had the pleasure of meeting the owners while I was there and they are very dedicated in running their business and hands on involved.

I would like to give the place 1/2 a star. This is my first review EVER writing bc I hate to say bad things about places....BUT this place deserves it. My husband and I were there for 1 hour and only got our drinks (his drink was half way full). We left without getting our food! DO NOT go there! Waste of time. We left and went to Waffle House and got our drinks AND FOOD within 5 minutes of sitting down!!!

Paolo and his staff were amazing! 

Right when you enter you are greeted and addressed. the atmosphere was great, it smelled great, it felt nice to be inside.
the menu was simplistic yet very descriptive, there is a mixture of all time favorite dishes and new ideas. My self and my family absolutely loved it.  

The Vodka sauce that he makes is by far some of the best I've had! 

price wise, it was very reasonable. 

over all I had a very good experience, and I will be going back. 

I also ordered some pasta he has ready to take home. BEST PASTA BY FAR!

its hit or miss here.......... great one time and lousy the next.

ordered pizza and 45 minutes later, waitress says, im sorry, what kind of pizza did you order? we need to reorder because i think the cook messed it up........

another time came in for the lunch special, which is 2 slices and a soda. girl behind the counter started arguing with me that there was no such thing. i showed her the menu and she proceeded to pick out the two tiniest pieces she could find. wtf????????????

Never have I been so insulted in life here in New Orleans until visiting this place.  I'm always bragging on how nice and friendly people are. The bartender  Paul (don't think is his real name) was so rude and I could tell he was not in the mood to really serve. After speaking with him and asking if he forgot about us in my nice and friendly tone.He coped an attitude and decided that he will not serve us. I'm now waiting to see how the night manager Victoria will handle this. Will provide another update soon

HORRIBLE MANAGER. I repeat. HORRIBLE MANAGER.  His name is Tom and he is a rude, and horrible man. He told the wedding decorator and the band to shut up, it is his business and he do what he wants when the band told him to arrange a space for bride and groom to do their first dance. He even told the decorating staffs he'll give her money to shut up and stop speaking when she tried to explain to him that he needs to move the tables back for dancing space.

This has been a fantastic place. Started at the bar for cocktails. The bartender had served everyone else and asked what I would like. From about 15 feet down the bar. No reason he didn't come down to where I was. It was weird and felt a bit rude. I ordered a cocktail. Taste was meh. Then we went to our table. The truffle soup tasted good but needed salt, which was not on the table. Ate it as is. Server seemed really flustered from the moment we arrived, which I attributed to her being a new server. The awkwardness did not diminish as the meal progressed. She plopped a plate of bread meant for the table in front of one of our women friends as if that was her ordered appetizer. Very strange.
Me and one other ordered the Bouillabaise. The bowls arrived with about 1/4 of the broth you would expect. Essentially a blend of seafood pieces standing in a quarter inch of broth. We asked for more broth and waited for it before starting. Once the rest of the broth arrived, we started eating. It still wasn't what I would consider an adequate amount of broth but okay enough. The flavor of the broth was delicious and interesting. If I didn't have to deal with the drama of having to request the rest of the broth, I'd get it again. As it happened, no I wouldn't bother. The seafood in the Bouillabaise was kind of boring. Not bad, just okay. Everything here really wants to be great, they just didn't come close this time. Which was disappointing. The service really should have been better. I'm hoping the server was new which just indicates the management needs to follow through on training and orientation better.

Second trip here! Last time was spring break. Amazing fresh food! Takes a while for them to make it but worth the wait! Have tried the crab cake sandwich that was juicy and fresh, the Tampa Cuban and the Chicken Cuban were all amazing! If in the area it's worth a stop!

Would like to give 4.5 stars overall. Food excellent although I think cafe Ponte a little better, very loud...true. Service amazing.
Atmosphere not all that but good vibe..I am being very picky .Overall you WILL NOT BE DISAPPOINTED.  just not absolutely perfect.
Will go back often as it is one of the better new restaurants.

Ugh... Consistently confused and poor service. What a shame. One of those places where you wonder how awesome it could be if it was run correctly. Food was fine, but service and attitude was really sad. Indifferent staff, a store full of frustrated customers... Doesn't the company care? Guess not.

I had a good experience came when they were closing she still served me my beer.....chatted with Leasa, I really like the involvement of the family pulling together to make it happen there. We need more business like this in NPR...I was amazed at the decor of her establishment, you can tell there was a lotta thought put into this place...I would have gave 5 stars...but, I never do that...definitely a refreshing change from the scene...I liked it and will definitely go back although I am not a real wine drinker they have like 5 or 6 craft beers on tap including Reef Donkey.

Stopped in for lunch the other day.  Menu was nice and varied by I zeroed in on the chicken lemongrass bun vermicelli. First, though, we started with spring rolls with pork.  Very tasty and larger than most Vietnamese restaurants we've visited before.  The only thing different, for us, was no peanut sauce, but instead the nuoc cham (dipping sauce/fish sauce).  While it was tasty, we prefer the thicker peanut sauce with our spring rolls.
My main entree was the chicken lemongrass bun vermicelli.  This is where it went downhill for me.   The bowl was plentiful and large but there was so much lemongrass and so little chicken (pieces) that it was very difficult to find the chicken. Thing is, I do really like lemongrass, but not when it it is so overwhelming as this dish was. Maybe the kitchen made a mistake because my meal arrived several minutes after my dining partner's meal so he was almost finished when I got mine.  Rushed, maybe?  I did have a bit of his ban mi sandwich and really liked it a lot.  Bread was nice and chewy and the filling was very tasty!
The wait time is definitely worth it!! Plus there is so much you can do around Jackson Square while you wait. The food here tastes sooo good!

This pizza spot was great, the food was delicious and the staff was so nice! We got a pepperoni pizza and the cheesy bread. The pizza is brick oven style and the cheese is so yummy!!! I highly recommend you check it out.

I've been to Hugo's many times, and I've always enjoyed their food. Since my childhood they've expanded this location to about twice the size of it's original iteration. It's a lot brighter than it once was inside, which for some is a bonus, but I preferred the sort of dimly lit "Cobby's" feel of the place. Here's what I like about them, in list form:

1. My favorite JoJo's in town. Salty, with bits of crispy/flaky coating. Unique flavor.
2. I always order the Italian on the french roll, it's always good. 
3. Ketchup with horseradish mixed in.
4. Unique fry-sauce
5. Decent fried Chicken

It may not be the cheapest deli in town, but I go there infrequently enough for it to not be a hindrance. Worth a quick trip for the JoJo's alone, in my opinion.

I was excited to try this place bc 1: it's Korean food and 2: it's in the city. I love the décor and space of Bop but the experience we had was mediocre. It took a while for our waitress to introduce herself and ask us for our beverage; the menu was already on the table so we know what to order when she arrived. My husband asked her how the beer was and she had no clue what it tastes like. I also asked her how many wings come in an order and the taste of it, and again, she had no clue how many or if it's sweet, spicy and whatnot. We just decided to order:  buddha beer for him and spicy rita for me, wings for the appetizer, bibimbop and the sea bass to share. We waited a while for our drinks and when I got my drink, she gave me a bloody mary! I asked her and she said she didn't know that it was bloody mary? She offered to give me a new drink and that took awhile, it was okay. We kept waiting for our food right after that, the tables that ordered their food after us got their food first. I finally asked one of the runners about our food and he went to check and came back with the bibimpop and sea bass. We asked for our wings and they were not even aware that we ordered it so they rushed our wings order so we have three dishes at the same time. The wings are too battered and it was smothered with gochujang sauce, I prefer the Southgate's is much better. The bibimbop was okay; it was served in a hot stone pot but it was more for presentation bc it didn't even give you the crunchy bottom. The sea bass was good but  it was small and the seaweed broth that came with it (it's usually a soup) didn't mesh well, I'd rather have the seabass by itself. We were going to give the place another chance until we got our bill, we are charged for an extra entree we did not order! It needs more ironing and we don't want to go back unless we're too lazy to go to North Philly for some Korean food.

There are plenty of great, inexpensive Mexican restaurants in this area. This is not one of them. Way overpriced, small portions, slow service, and unimpressive food. The chips were stale and the food had no taste. We had to add extra sauces to give the food some flavor.

My husband and I ate here because we were walking by and the patio had such a nice atmosphere about it we couldn't help but eat here. My husband even hates Italian food but he wanted to eat here because it was so lovely with the waterfall, heaters, and soft lounge music.  We were very happy to see it was well priced and had a lot of vegetarian options.  The food was really good, so good my husband liked it.  We had the tiramisu for desert and it was five star fantastic! They also have a really good well priced wine list. Very nice romantic night.
I miss the the great buffet. However, the food a la carte is great and it was a very tasty and enjoyable meal.

This is the kind of Mexican Restaurant I've been looking for! Love the food and the atmosphere. 

My hubby and I had our date night here and it was fabulous!
The food was ok but the dessert was excellent. The server was extremely slow but glad to see a restaurant open and have staff during this pandemic.

Food was hot, fresh and came out quickly. Price was just right. I'm not often in the Plainfield area but if I'm in the area and craving authentic Mexican food I would definitely stop by. I would definitely recommend.
I was here first time and I can definitely say that this is one of the best places where you can eat in St. Petersburg. Recommend to everyone

After reading about this eatery in Philly Magazine, my brother and I stopped by on the way to the Flyers game on 2/12.   

The venue is a tiny "shop" in Fishtown, with a few spaces to sit at the counter and some standing room as well.  After talking briefly with the chefs (both were extremely nice); my brother and I both ordered the "Arista", which consists of thin-shaved slices of house-roasted suckling pig with broccoli rabe & long "hots" (peppers to those not in the know) soaked in jus and put into a long roll.  

The sandwich was just the right amount!  The pork was fork tender and the rabe was perfect....I would've preferred a little more peppers in mine but that was my only tiny complaint.  Bonus!  The sandwich comes with a free soda.  

I will be going back to try some of their other sandwiches and sides (the potatoes "side" sounds awesome).

The French toast is the best by far.  We tried eachothers dishes and everything was great.  Their cornbeef hash of course was wonderful and the chicken and waffles were good too.  The only negative is they ran out of tomato juice so we couldn't get a bloody Mary!!
Heaven!! What more can I say? I haven't had food this good in. ....we'll can't remember! Must try!
Very poor service. Worst experience That I have ever had at a chick fil a. Waited over 20 minutes for food. No apology.  Will not be back here.

Cameron poblano asada. Those three words caught my eye and those same three words changed the game - the mall restaurant game, that is. What can I say about Cantina? It's a great spot. It isn't very large but it's not too small either. There's a section for larger parties I assume, some booths, a few high tables, and the bar seating area. I was there on a Thursday evening and it wasn't very loud (despite the game being on) so this is nice spot. 

Okay, enough about that. On to the real reason for this review: cameron poblano asada. The name caught my eye (I LOVE shrimp) and the description sounded interesting. A steak dish that comes with a shrimp-stuffed pepper? Yes, please! My tastebuds thanked me even hours later. I almost cleaned my plate. I will DEFINITELY be back for more!
Tasty food and great prices. The service was also very pleasant. It's not a large place, and it isn't fancy, but it is perfect for casual nights out.

I had my wedding there and  the food was excellent, the service was  great and most of all  Felix and the staff makes you feel like family. They did an excellent  job on that special day. No matter whether you  come for Lunch , Dinner  the quality is the same and  Felix is wonderful to all  people   Thank You

The noodles are fantastic (especially the Pad Kee Mow). The curry is sub par. The delivery process is really bad, I'd never order again if the noodles weren't so great.

On Grubhub, the delivery estimate is always fairly slow, but more often than not it arrives well past the estimate. Not unusual to take 2 hours. The delivery driver always calls and says he's outside while he's still several minutes away.

Reserved two rooms with verandas on Bourbon Street for a full week and had a lengthy conversation directly with the hotel ahead of time as my sister and I were traveling with our 80+ year old folks.  My sister is their full-time caregiver and it was important that our rooms be next door or very close to theirs for health reasons.  After a long trip from the West Coast and arriving late and exhausted, we were forced to go into fight/protect mode as the hotel didn't have our rooms.  After well over an hour, they managed to come up with the right room for our parents, but stuck my sister and I on another floor in the back of the hotel where we had to take two different elevators to get to our parents.  That was just the beginning of our bad experiences staying at this hotel.  Way too numerous to go into here.  This is not a cheap hotel, so if you can afford to stay here, DON'T.  There are way too many other nice hotels in NOLA whose customer service far exceeds what you get at the Royal Sonesta.  If you do decide to stay here, don't pay extra for the concierge level; it's a joke!  Plan on washing your own sheets and cleaning your bathroom.  Don't expect the front desk, the concierge, housekeeping and even room service to answer the phone, because they don't.  Watch out for rude bartenders in the Desire Bar.  Finally, if you need to talk to upper management because you're experiencing issues, be prepared to hear "he's not in today" for 5 days in a row!

This place was tasty but I didn't feel like it was a very good deal.  I got the weekend special with the apples and lamb and it was the BOMB but i got a massive plate of white rice and a little bowl of main event, and it felt like I was being ripped off for the $17 bucks I spent on it, even though it was yummy and left me full.  I think if they might have plated it differently I never would have noticed.  It was a nice cozy meal to beat a surprise chilly day though and I think I will go back if I get a hankering for a down home afghan meal hehe.  
The service was nothing to write home about, but whatever.

A colleague of mine and I decided to give Ulele a try and realizing that their lunch service was brand new, we thought that this would be a perfect opportunity to sample the fare and experience the restaurant.  I made a reservation on Open Table, and after reading some reviews, was a bit hesitant that our reservation time of 12:15 would be honored.  Have no fear...we were seated immediately upon arrival.  The menu is full of temptations.  That said, I ordered the meatloaf and she had the Gouda Grouper.  We also opted for a few additional sides.- the Jalapeno Cheddar Grit cake and Carson's Jalapeno Corn Beer Quick Bread or as I would like to put it- Ulele's take on a corn muffin.
We ordered and waited a fair amount of time for the meal to arrive.  We arrived and were seated at 12:15 and our meal arrived at about 12:45.  That is a bit of a wait for a lunch order, so we decided that a 2 hour lunch was necessary.  For those in a hurry, I HIGHLY encourage you to look elsewhere to dine, because if you cannot afford to wait, don't do it.  That said, they just began lunch service on Monday so perhaps they don't quite have the "quick service" routine down to a science yet.  Back to the food-
We were offered sparkling or still water, and we chose the still with lemon.  My lunch date was very happy with her Grouper entree, but was overjoyed with the grit cake.  She had two, so we shared.  They were nicely flavored and we added a bit of butter to top them off.  Her Grouper was served on a bed of wild rice with three sprigs of asparagus.  My meatloaf was very tasty, 2 slices were nestled on a nice serving of mashed potatoes accompanied by three sprigs of asparagus and topped with fried onions.  The mashed potatoes were described as "white popcorn cheddar" but I neither tasted nor noticed a resemblance to the description.  That said, the potatoes were good.  The meatloaf was presented as two slices about 1/2 in. thick each.  For the most part, very flavorful.  The corn muffins were delightful with just a hint of jalapeno, and sweetness.  I did not notice a beer flavor at all, so I just chalked it up to a very fancy description for a nice corn muffin.  We opted for no desert because our time was up.  The service was wonderful and attentive and I cannot wait to try the restaurant for dinner.  I give it a total of 4 stars for the combination of ambiance and presentation of the food and the overall flavor, though if I had to rate the food alone, I would probably give it 3 1/2 stars.  Looking forward to a trip to Ulele for dinner!

Active construction on the property and you can hear the construction all day even out on the beach  (no notice on website or during booking,) noisy rattling AC in room, and internet doesn't work. Made many trips to the don over the years and this was my last.

More like 3.5, but I'll round up.

We stopped in on Friday night on a whim. Nice setup with an open kitchen where you can watch them make the pizzas. The place was packed, but they space the tables out nicely so it's not too loud or crowded.

We started with the artichoke fritters, and ordered two pizzas, the Homemade Sausage pizza and the Old Kentucky Rome. The fritters were a tasty start to the meal. Five fritters with a spicy sauce. It was kind of like artichoke dip in a croquette form.

Between the two pizzas, I preferred the Old Kentucky Rome. The funky taleggio cheese complimented the figs and prosciutto marvelously. The Homemade Sausage pizza was pretty good. The sauce was on the sweet side. The sausage was tasty, and the raw fennel slices on top made the pizza interesting. The crust was wood-fired, and stood up to the toppings well (no soggy or flimsy crust here).

Two pizzas were plenty for our table of three. In fact, we probably could have gotten by with just one. Four slices came home with us.

Beer selection was pretty good. Two 3F beers on draught, I chose Alpha King. Next time I'll try sitting at the bar (seemed to have a nice atmosphere there).

Ordered the shrimp penne vodka. Pasta tasted a bit under-cooked, as it was a bit hard, but was a tasty dish. Tried ordering a cannoli at 6:30 PM but the restaurant ran out... what Italian restaurant runs out of cannolis before 7 PM??? A few hours after dinner my stomach was upset and I ended up vomiting. I believe I had food poisoning. A nice place with a limited menu, but I would never come back after this experience.

Great variety 
Busy but they move you through in timely fashion. Bakery department has many choices and the Ciabatta is awesome!

Stumbled upon this place because the restaurant we planned had a long wait. Ordered the shorts ribs that were so tender that the meat just fell off the bone with the slightest touch of the fork. Mac & Cheese was an outstanding side. Live music was a nice added touch. Solid BBQ joint.

Person at the front desk was irritable, and openly showed her displeasure with my questions. The meatballs were cold in the middle, and so was my HOT sandwich. We also did wait 40 minutes for our food. Easily one of the most unpleasant food experiences I've had in a long time.

Randomly found this place in yelp - mostly because it was close to Cafe Du Monde . It reminded me of the Hofs you find in Seoul (except they don't have their liquor lol else yet). The quality of the Kalbi meat could have been better but it was still delicious. Ample side dishes and tasty amount of heat to the spicy chicken. Service was good and fast, which I appreciate. I brought my non-Asian friend with me and she loved it. I'm a little more critical seeing as how I'm Korean but I would recommend this place if you're in the area.
Best salads. Friendly staff.  Very accommodating also. One of my favorite places. Prices very reasonable too!

Very disappointed with both service and food. The Caesar salad was simply romaine lettuce with a bland dressing, croutons and Kraft-like grated Parmesan cheese. The calamari appetizer had absolutely no taste and the marinara sauce was watery. The glass of wine tasted old and smelled moldy. The meal was almost $30. 

The bartender acted put out that he had customers to wail on - all 4 of us.

Very disappointing. It was recommended to us for the wonderful steak and seafood, but when we asked about non-dairy options (my wife is lactose intolerant), we were told the only options for her were chicken or pasta. And steak was only available 'for 2'. 

When pressed, they said the chef could only make tile fish and not the wahoo, dairy free, and what came out was bland. And who puts slices of ham on top of seafood? 

My squid ink pasta was just OK, and the special fried oyster appetizer had 4 small oysters dwarfed by large tomatoes in both size and flavor.  It says a lot when your favorite part of the meal is the bread and olive oil, and you leave still hungry.

I was quite pleased with my first visit here! The pizza was spectacular. The lady who took our order was not very friendly and made it seem as though she did not want to be there. It was definitely not the best way to get my experience started. However, as I went down the line and chose UNLIMITED toppings for my 6" pizza ($5.97), the people were a lot more personable and more than happy to help me out! You are able to choose different sauces, toppings, spices, etc. They have MANY options. The pizza was cooked well and I had no left overs. It was delicious and their prices are pretty good for pizza! Their other main option is an 11" for $7.97 with UNLIMITED toppings! That's awesome. I will definitely go again! If you haven't tried this place out, I recommend you do!

Great service and ambiance. You have indoor and outdoor seating area.
Waiters are well trained and very very friendly and attentive.
We had the eggs Benedict's with lamb and the burrito together with the feta cheese dip.... a must!!
Ac is a bit cold... everything else is perfect!!

We were upset when the Tavern closed in the CWE, but we want to support local businesses in our neighborhood so we decided to give it a try. We arrived around 5:30 and were seated immediately even though the restaurant was quite busy. Our server was very friendly and attentive. They had a bourbon flight that was delicious and I also recommend the Manhattan. The pulled chicken sandwich was very good and the side of Mac and Cheese was outstanding! I could've eaten the Mac and Cheese for my meal. My date had the fried bologna sandwich and it was incredible! I will definitely order the fried bologna sandwich next time. The food was outstanding and the service was terrific! We are so happy to have Salt and Smoke in the neighborhood. We will be back often!

The best steak anywhere! This is the second location of Bobs we have been to. We got the same quality and service at both locations. You can't find better food or service. We go to a lot of restaurants to compare to. The steaks are perfectly cooked and so flavorful and tender. I would highly recommend Bobs to anybody.

I used to live near the intersection of Bay to Bay and Macdil and the thing I miss most about living there is being walking distance to Datz. It is one of my favorite restaurants in Tampa and where I chose to have my birthday dinner there this year (it fell on a Sunday which would have been a problem in the past, but they are now open until 8 on Sundays).

For drinks, they have a full liquor bar of course. I've had their Bloody Mary before and it's fantastic. However, I'm a big craft beer fan and Datz always has a huge selection of good beers to choose from. And it's not always the same which is even better.

Food is where Datz really shines. The menu is always changing and I always like to try something different when I come here, so while I can't recommend one specific dish, I can pretty much recommend everything. I have never been disappointed by anything I've ordered here. And as if I hadn't had enough to eat already on my birthday, they gave me a free cupcake for desert which was, of course, delicious!
Finally! A Hong Kong style Cafe in Philly. The food was great and authentic. The staff was friendly and attentive. The only suggestion I have is a bigger menu to include some more of the staples.
Great place to real food with good flavor...5.25.19...good prices with great food.  Sports bar at its best.

A holiday dinner at Wine Exchange Bistro was wonderful. We had a party of 6 and sat outside. Food and drinks we highly, highly recommend to all of our friends and family. Everyone of my party will recommend this restaurant; however, the server was not someone whom I would recommend.
Checks were just plopped on the table, a tad bit on the sarcastic side when asked to explain degree of spice, response was a bit short tempered and condescending at multiple points of the evening.
All things being equal we will be back but definitely
never again in her station.

I have been wanting to go to Keel & Curley since returning to Tampa from college. It's been 2 years and I used my sister-in-laws reintroduction to drinking after a 9 month hiatus (i.e pregnancy) as the occasion to get me out to the country. 

We headed out on Saturday. It couldn't have been a more gorgeous day. We arrived about 5 minutes before our vineyard tour, which the lady warned on the phone, "Tractor leaves at exactly 3 o clock!" We grabbed some peach Chardonnay and hopped in the trailer behind the John Deere tractor. All of this felt right. We were at a vineyard in Plant City after all! The tour guide was great. He was informative and told cheesy jokes. The ride was too short in my opinion. The air felt great and the wine was delicious. Everyone on the trailer was having a great time.

The tour of the... Not distillery... Hmmm not sure what's it's called... Anyways, it was great. I had no idea how fast the fruit wine process was. When I think of wines I think of the aging process. From picked to bottle it only takes the blueberry wine 6 weeks. It's pretty crazy. We got to see the bottling machine and learn more about the Keel family and how they came to own the vineyard, it was all kind of cool. I just wish that you got to see more of the property. There really no need for the tractor as it moves about as fast as you walk and only takes about 5 minutes. I would have liked to take some pictures with the blueberries but or maybe try some wine straight out of the big containers. In short, I wasn't really impressed (This is me, doing my best Maroney impression). 

The tasting was a lot of fun, and wine. They take your taste buds on an adventure of fruity design. There were only 3 wines I really liked but I enjoyed giving them all a shot. I don't love sweet drinks so it's definitely my palate, not their skills, that were to blame. The lady that was pouring for us was like a ninja, swooping in to give us our next sample just as we finished the last. 

Do they have room for improvement? Sure. But, it's definitely think it's worth an afternoon trip. It's a fun thing to do that I never thought I'd have an opportunity to do in the Florida. I also hear that the music festivals they have out there are fun as well. I would go back and sip peach chardonnay on a picnic blanket any day!

I went to this place for lunch the other day! I have had their food before, but never ate in the restaurant. The restaurant is very small inside, but it does have some seating. The workers are very nice. The establishment is clean and it is modestly priced for a pizza place!

This was our first time here and we loved it! 
The drinks were delicious and fresh. The food was amazing! I had shrimp queso and tacos. I can't wait to try more! To top it all off, the bartenders, Julio and Diego,  went above and beyond for us tonight! This is definitely our new "go to" Mexican for many reasons and we can't wait to bring our friends here.

A sparse but semi shoplike decor greets you as you enter the bar, which is well spaced and open-sensed, yet cozy and hospitable nonetheless. A portrait of Conway Twitty, the true "Slow Hand", subtly smiles from behind the bar. A warm and welcoming feel drifts over you, typically unprecedented in a spot where one sees so much chrome and copper.

There is an exquisitely comfortable upstairs space, open only on Fridays and Saturdays at this time. Magnum and BA Baracus cast a baleful eye back from decades past. 

Two drinks began my explorations: Rum Punch; which was very fruity and light,  with a spirity accent. Delicious! Dos Besitos: lusciously fruitful with an jalapeño afterbite! Revelatory!

Shift change, two different bartenders and fantastic drink consistency for my second Dos Besitos.

Heavily infused with gruyere and fontina, the Ham Croquettes do not disappoint, especially with the saucing of local honey and dijon. Magnifique!

The food is a bit pricey for the serving size, but so very satisfying to the palette! If you are trying to stuff the void before drinks; well, don't! Eat and drink over a long period here! Pay for pleasure, my friends!

$45 for an app and 3 drinks for one fellow. Not bad, and an immensely blissful experience for my mouth! 4.5/5, with extra kudos given to the immensely amenable staff!

I love this place. Probably go twice a week. The only thing I've had that I wouldn't recommend is the hot ham and cheese sandwich. The meat had a lot of fat and cut too thick for my liking.
The pizza crust thickness is a perfect compromise between thick and thin. They have a wide selection of toppings and sauces. The beer selection is very local and rotates frequently. They also have really great lunch specials!
Great service. Love the variety of burgers and condiments. Wonderful atmosphere and service from Eric was excellent.

The man-friend and I stopped in here to have a drink this past weekend, and while we didn't have anything else besides the one round we were impressed with the service we received from the bartender.  He was extremely attentive, and when a suuuper schwasty face man came in and sat down, he had no problems refusing to serve and removing him from the bar.  

I always appreciate when bartenders can put the welfare of their patrons first despite losing business.

High five!

Wonderful Mexican Restaurant has everything you want!! Great chips and salsa and even better Patron Signature Margaritas!! Service and management are great!! The short rib entree is always over the top!! Atmosphere, great food and over the top service spells great evening out!!  Bestito is easily one of Florida's best Mexican restaurants and is one of Tampa's jewels:)

Pizza was delivered earlier than estimated. It was a bit greasy for my taste and some of the toppings on our supreme pizza were scarce/poorly distributed. Overall the pizza was delicious, good consistency and a tasty crust, definitely not too crispy but certainly not doughy. After 4 pieces I'm still craving another. The pizza could have been a little hotter upon arrival. It was an enjoyable temperature but not hot out of the oven. 
       I ended up eating the 5th piece despite the temperature and poor distribution of toppings because the flava was just that good. My girlfriend loved it too and she has impeccable taste, obviously. Solid 3.5 out of 5, but definitely not a 4, so I'm not rounding up.

Ha long Bay......party of two, we got there. look at the menu order 2 waters. place was nice and clean.
Our waiter was great very attentive service.

order...Vietnamese crispy spring rolls, came with lettuce just put spring roll and wrap it then dip in sauce. like it really good.
order main course.....fried rice pork, I always like fried rice. born to eat it. Never bored. Second one is roast pork w/bean sprout.
that roast pork was good, taste that have not eat that kind before. need to sneak in their kitchen.
last she order was Grill lemon grass shrimp bowl, lots of flavor. what in it, come to Ha long Bay food exceptional.

Our water service kept refilled, excellent service. 

We will come back for more.

Jen, the manager, lacks professionalism when addressing customer's problems.

PROBLEM:
Our order of Fried blackened wings came to our table as Grilled without any Seasoning.  
Our party of three voted them as some of the worse local wings.

THE QUICK FIX:
Amy, our waitress, offered to discount them since we only at half the order.
We agreed that would be acceptable.

THEN, 
The $100 bill comes and we're ready to leave.
There is no discount!
Amy said the manager refuses to discount it.

OF COURSE, 
Then we ask to speak to the manager, Jen.

This is where it gets a bit odd and uncomfortable.

Jen comes out and says with a bit of an attitude and no smile, 
"I hear you wanted to see me.  What do you want?"
WTH?

WE RECAP the Problem to Jen.

We hear her excuses for 
*   "What I told Amy was.....".
*   "I told Amy to replace the wings...."
*   "I've already comped $300 today".
I guess that last one was to let us know other people are worthy of being happy customers - but not us.

Jen, please leave customers out of the "She said, She said" politics there.

OUTCOME:
Since Jen was spoiling our nice day out, we finally said, 
"Just bring us the replacement order To-Go.  We're out of here."

We will not be going back while Jen is there.  
$100 is too money to spend for this customer service and to leave b*tching about what just happened.

And, heck... we're in walking distance of the place!

The 2nd star is for the Gyro Egg Rolls - they were pretty good.

Have you tried to Bar Fly in Safety Harbor?  
It's awesome!


UPDATE:
After posting, I went to read other reviews.
Take note the owners are not replying to the 1-star reviews.
That's a clear sign as they do not care.
It will have new ownership by the end of next year.

Alllllllways a pleasure! As soon as someone mentions New Orleans in conversation.. whether talkin abt an upcoming trip, reflecting on a previous story, or just talkin... I always immediately say "BUT HAVE YOU BEEN TO STANLEY???" 

If not, GOOOOOOOO and get the fried oyster po' boy!!!!! BEST IN THE CITY! Hands down!!!! The bread is so good, the dressing slaw, and of course the oysters!! Goodness!

I also had the gumbo which is delicious.. and the pancakes with a ice cream scoop on top is one of my husbands favorites. We looooooove food and this spot never disappoints!

I LOVE going here. However this was the first time going to curbside pickup and the lasagna was not the same size as the normal entree as dine in. I must say, the manager offered for me to either come back and pick up another but since I go to dine in all the time, I figured I would just get one to go next time. Customer service is fantastic, to say the least. Very happy with the outcome, but just know if you order lasagna for 15.99 it's very tiny. I would love to give them 5 stars, but that's the only reason I gave them 4. Just beware... fellow lasagna lovers! Better deal to get the combo meal with chicken and lasagna with a side.

A wonderful experience! I was in town on tour and my parents had flown to meet me for a few days. We weren't able to eat until late because of the show, but the hours were great! Serves until 1am! 
Our waiter was very knowledgable. Wine was wonderful and the cheeses were delicious. I recommend the hummus dip and the olive dip. Both were made in house and were very tasty. Lots of great beers on tap! Local cheeses! The decor is beautiful. A very cool place to sit, chat, and enjoy some tasty bites! Cannot wait to visit St. Louis again!

I have been visiting Capogna's since I was a youngster. I once truly enjoyed their food; pizza and pasta,  and as I got older, their sports bar atmosphere.

My visits have dwindled over the years though the Hubs and I stopped in for lunch, drinks, and to watch some football a couple of Sundays ago.

While the service is friendly and attentive, the food is definitely not what it once was. I had the ziti with marinara sauce and paid extra for baked on cheese ($3.49 up charge!). The menu states that it comes with bread and soup, salad or garlic toast. I requested garlic toast. When my food arrived it was not included. When iI asked the waiter for it he said that it wasn't available, but that he would get me some bread; white, thick, soft bread. Seemed to me it would have been easy to throw some butter and garlic salt on top and toss it in an oven for a couple of minutes, but whatever.  Either way, the bread was the best part of the meal. My daughter makes better ziti using store bought ingredients. The Hubs had a meatball sub which he did not enjoy. I hate spending money on bad food. 

Sadly, this was probably our last visit here.
Went for Mother's Day and it was great. We were a big party and they had a limited menu but we really enjoyed ourselves and the food was delicious.
Got out of lab hella hungry. Wanted to see if I could get some pizza. Google said they were open. The person there just ignored me so I'm not going there again.

Service was great
Setting and ambiance is nice.. pretty dim and there was a live jazz band.. music was relaxing and everything today is great for a date

Food was great and fresh but I just wish it was more on the menu.. its very limited

I ordered the Brussel sprouts and burger

Their pho was on point. And the wait staff was very nice.  They put more meat than the other pho places around there. The price is alittle bit more higher than other places.  I liked the fact that they seem to be very clean.   I will be returning again so I can try their rice dishes. Hope they don't change anything .  
  If they do maybe their egg rolls. It was on the skimpy side. Not much meat in it.

My friend and I have the tradition of getting Mexican food and margaritas every time we get together. Since she moved to Indiana, we had to find a new place. In comes El Rodeo.

They have your typical Mexican options on the menu, nothing out of the ordinary. But their margaritas are probably the strongest I have ever had. Totally worth every penny. We got the biggest one you can get...and that was enough! The food was good, the service was pretty good (there was a period of time where were didn't know where our waiter went), but overall I would say the servers were very nice. We spent a decent amount of time talking with them (we were there when it wasn't busy). 

Basically, if you want to get some good food and an excellent margarita, this is your place!

Fuck yes this place is FANtastic. I'd been craving Indian food like no other - my college town had been rife with mouthwatering Indian restaurants, and I'd been feeling the severe lack of paneer in my life. Truthfully, the Yelp atmosphere description that Rasoi is "intimate" turned me off a little - I'm looking to shove as much curry, rice, and naan in my face and you're telling me I gotta bring a date?

Thankfully, the bombtastic Food Pedaler service - for serious, use them liberally; they're fast, unceasingly cheerful, and brightly dressed in skintight cycling suits - listed Rasoi as places they deliver from. So I scrolled through this page to look up recommendations - and man, Yelpers are awesome, you all never let me down - and proceeded to order a batch of food that was so tasty and so satisfying that I made obscene noises while I ate. 

I ordered the paneer tikka masala, makhani dal, methi malai mattar, and an order of garlic naan. HOLY JEEBUS. My new favorite thing is the methi malai mattar, a thick, creamy spinach dish that takes all the best parts of saag paneer and serves it up in an overflowing tureen of slightly spicy, beautifully green taste explosion. The tikka masala was absolutely terrific - creamy, spicy, tomatoey, and with an awesome smattering of perfect paneer. The dal was more soupey than I'd been expecting, but hey, its spiced lentils, and with the right amount of rice, I was good to go. AND DON'T EVEN GET ME STARTED ON THE GARLIC NAAN. Holy crap on a cracker, is this the stuff dreams are made of. Pillowy and garlicky - man, I'd do anything for a lifetime supply of that particular naan.

Next stop is to try out the lunch buffet, so I can sample Rasoi's chicken dishes and gorge myself on as much curry and naan as allowed. You keep on doing you, Rasoi, cuz it be gooood stuff.

Two words: Kombucha bar. I'm normally not the type to shop at places like this, but kombucha is the main reason I'll be coming here in the near future! It's also nice that if I ever am in the market for natural foods/products, I will at least be here on a semi-regular basis! I did look at their pet product area, and I found myself wishing it was better stocked. It's a fairly small store so it's possible they have to pick and choose what to carry. 

I've met the owners, and they are fantastic! If you've never tried kombucha, stop by! Find out what all the hype is about! They also have cold brew coffee on tap here as well as additional espresso bar drinks so you can't beat it!

Amazing bar. Great specials. On Friday nights the owner boils seafood, usually shrimp or crawfish, and it's amazing and reasonably priced. The bartenders are super sweet and remember you! Steaks are well
Cooked and seasoned! Visit and you won't be sorry!

Party of six, on a Saturday for hibachi-style lunch, in honor of Mother's Day.

The chef was LOVELY: charming and entertaining, and made a little extra so that each of us could try what the others had ordered.  The food was delicious.  The mothers in the partied felt honored.  ;o)

Tip: try the Japanese fruit soda -- it's tasty and if you're a curious sort you can spend quite a while studying and contemplating the design of the bottle.

This is a burger buff's dream restaurant. The choices are vast and delicious. This place has awesome salads (I recommend the Health Nut), a glorious selection of French fries and sides, and a medley of meats that will bring customers back to try out different variations of burgers.  

I had the Salmon Burger and fries on this visit. It's one of my favorites on the menu. The salmon is super juicy and the fried egg adds a nice flavor. 

This isn't a fast food joint, so expect to wait a little bit for your burger - even when it's not particularly busy. Totally worth the wait every time.

Love this breakfast spot! Definitely a staple if you're in Bellair Bluffs. They have a lot of seating both inside and outside which is nice. Overall the experience if 4 stars because the staff is pleasant and it's a place to go when you're not in a hurry. Just relax and enjoy your breakfast! I would say the food is better than typical diner quality, but not extremely remarkable. HOWEVER, you must try the hash brown casserole!!! Definitely legendary in its own right. I also enjoyed the vegetable omelet, very fresh and a huge portion for the price.

It was good! Def worth the try. The pros - fast service and the cons - my bowl of bun rieu had very little meat and veggies. Actually i wished the menu stated size small as cup size bc i would have ordered the large. My coffee was not good....actually one of the worst. Very tiny place to dine in - only a table for 4. The soup was descent and the service was fast.

Yasssss!! Seriously, I've been waiting years for this place to reopen! 

My first trip back was great! Prices increased a bit, but who cares, it's as delicious as it ever was.

I dined in with my parents who were disappointed with their first trip when they first reopened.  My Mom had the veal parm sandwich, my Dad, a half order of the red mussels and I ordered a half of the white mussels with a house salad. 

Although I miss the salad bar (olive overload), I enjoyed my salad with the house dressing. I loved the mussels, Dad did as well. Mom loved her enormous sandwich, great leftovers. Those fries, I almost forgot how yummy they are! 

Both the red and white mussels are delicious. My one issue...is why are they now served with garlic knots?! I asked for the old rolls and I was charged. The knots didn't taste too fresh, and the juice is meant to be absorbed by those rolls instead! Don't mess with perfection Coppa.

All in all, it was a great dinner!  Welcome Back 82, I'm glad to see the famous pan survived the fire!
I LOVE it here. The scenery, the atmosphere, the food, the drinks all around is amazing! We love doing Girls night's out here!
We love this restaurant--it's become a staple! Great margaritas, quality food and ambience and always plenty of seating. Great Friday night date spot!

Seems alot better now that it's reopened. Service used to be dreadful, long lines barely moved. Now, the food seems even better, but service is alot better! The workers seem to care, move things along, much more organized. One worker even opened a little early on a holiday recently, and was really helpful and friendly. 

Much better than it used to be, worth a return to give it a second chance!

Came to El Camino for the first time over the weekend. Loved the ambiance and vibe within the restaurant, however I cannot say the same about the rest of my experience. My waitress, I think her name was Hannah, made me feel unwelcome. I also noticed other staff members having some problems which the costumer should never be aware of. The food was okay. Disappointed.

My husband and I used to love this place. It's difficult to find good Chinese food nearby without going to Philadelphia. We've ordered food and had it delivered quite a few times. We called one night for delivery. (they have our address in their system) The lady even read our address to us. Then she proceeded to say that they don't deliver to our address. After stating that we've had food delivered many times the woman the. Says that the driver "doesn't want to deliver to our address." Needless to say Orchid has lost us as a customer.

Unfortunately, I would not come back here on my own accord. For starters the menu doesn't really make sense. When asking for a nigiri combo I was told I'd get sashimi not nigiri ... the service was not the greatest and at the end the head chef interrupted the server talking with customers right next to us and ordered him to pick up our empty plates. He wasn't our server and literally in the middle of talking with a table. The sushi itself was ok. All in all there are much better places to go in nashville in my opinion..

This spot was pretty average, nothing too special but nothing too horrible either. Crunchy rolls had fried onions on the *inside* which was very interesting? They weren't that crunchy and were hard to discern from the regular California roll. We also tried the Rock n Roll which had shrimp tempura and it was good! But was definitely more of the type of sushi you'd get from the grocery store than a specialty sushi place. I think the prices were pretty decent though! And if you're feeling yakisoba, they were also pretty average.
Just arrived in Nashville and decided  on our first meal here. Great decision! The food was so good. We had cod fish and chips and a lager. Also not much of a wait for a Friday night.

You can't go wrong with anything at cajun kitchen, it is seriously the best.

Went there last week and had the cajun chillequilles, not sure if they're new on the menu but they were amazing! Such a good combination of chips, spice and andouille sausage, in the future I might add another egg to the mix to keep the dish balanced.

In the past i have had many of their scrambles and omelets, all of which are delicious.

Beware on the weekends and expect to wait a while for a table especially with large groups, but service is usually quick.

I've been an Ernie's customer for about 10 years.  In the past I'd compared it to a really good nyc style pizza, with really reasonable prices. During  the pandemic summer of 2020 I
Purchased Ernies pizza for takeout to eat poolside with friends. I was disappointed multiple times , with too much oily drippy cheese and undercooked crust.  I ultimately stopped buying Ernie's. I recently went back and ate inside. It was the old perfect slice... crispy, with a crust that supported the perfect amt of cheese and allowed me to taste the yummy sauce. I asked about last summer and was told that occasionally they brought in other pizza cooks to offset the weekend demand. That person is no longer there. Ernie's is back, and so am I.

Matt the Miller's Tavern was a welcoming environment during the COVID times.  They definitely followed guidelines to ensure guests felt welcome.  Moreover, they played to all guests demonstrating this again by its eclectic music playing.  Music ranging from Bob Marley to The Killers to Maroon 5 to Nora Jones circulated through the speakers.  

They stayed with the safe theme with the food, too.  It was good but not fantastic.  The salad was definitely worthy of a high review with the main courses average but worth eating.  

In all, this was a nice experience for the family visiting from out of town.

Order was wrong, food was cold, wrote them on the only email to contact someone and no one responded . 

Pass unless Chick fil A is closed and then eat pizza or go to Five Guys
It's OK.  Seems like a place in need of a Gordon Ramsay to come in and clean up the menu and decor.

Three stars for SMALL portions. I spent $9.50 for a single piece of bread with cream cheese, egg, and arugula on it. Advertised as coming with lox... Oh wait, you mean the flecks in the cream cheese? I guess that must be what you meant. The coffee is fine, the food tasted fine, but I left here starving. Do yourself a favor and go to Cake Cafe if you're actually hungry.
You would not expect this much flavor at this location! Authentic, delicious, and fair priced. Won't regret it!

Something magical happens when you move south of the Mason-Dixon, you discover Chick-Fil-A.  Despite crossing that boarder years ago it has only been recently that I have savored the true value of "EAT MORE CHICKEN."

It was Friday night. The hubs and I were hungry. Chick-Fil-A to the rescue (referred to as Jesus chicken by some)! Not only is this location new but it is fancy-new. I mean double ordering in the drive through, quality speaker systems for ordering and everything is shiny. No, seriously.  I love having a location on the West side of town! One 12 piece chicken nugget #5 combo later and we were greeted at the window with our food. The nuggets are delightful but make sure you hit up the waffle fries! We also noticed that all the men have ties on. It is like everyone is a manager. Classy. Anyway, I'll certainly be going back whenever the hunger pangs for a quick meal. 

My pleasure, Chick-Fil-A. My pleasure.

Brand new eatery! The food is DELICIOUS!
We ate at the bar, where Nicole and Alyssa were spectacular. 
Won ton soup, char Sui, Sui yoke, pot stickers, spring rolls, and dumplings all were ON POINT!

Best Chinese food in Media! Best soup dumplings outside of Shanghai! It's a bold statement but it's mine! Double cooked pork unbelievably delicious. I'm a fan. Took 3 visits to get a table but we lucked out coming early tonight!

There is no cooling here! Just two ceiling fans and an open layout. The restaurant itself is super cute and very Chicanx hipster. We had to wait about 20 minutes for our food which was a bit upsetting because i was on a time crunch. I wasn't able to eat rolled tacos for yearssss but i finally found a vegetarian alternative so it was worth the wait. I ordered the queso rollies with cauliflower and a quesadilla in case I didn't like it (I ate the quesadilla). Bf got the cubano sandwich. I think my expectations were a lil too high. The queso was not a good match for me. I was hoping for something more real cheesy less saucy. (Their salsa verde is delicious!!!) Someone did come by to check on us, which i greatly appreciated. I will be back to hopefully add 5 stars.

For a $9 buffet lunch, Tandoor is pretty good.  I really like palak and it was pretty decent here.  Their samosas weren't bad either.  Fellow diner enjoyed the chicken.  She had been a frequent customer a number of years ago and everybody working remembered her and was extremely friendly.  

The actual restaurant and buffet display leaves a lot to be desired.   I felt a little gnarly all day after eating here.  BUT, for a once a year cheap indian buffet lunch, I'd go back for the annual visit.

This place was the best. We came in from out of town and we were looking for some delicious food. That is what we got here. The outdoor patio was the best! We had the cheese dip, the corned beef sandwich and the shepard's pie. They were all delicious. I wish their was a place in CA just like this!

The restaurant was awesome, great food, great service, ask for Freddie!

However, the casino is like every other...cigarette smoke everywhere, rude people walking into you and the shops along the casino had the worst customer service.  

If you are looking for a night out, a few drinks and slot playing, you'll have fun...just don't loose too much money!

First time, and won't be the last to Global A'Fare' with their great concept of global offerings, not just one....there's Mediterranean, Spanish, Thai, it's all over the place, a very well thought out global concept.

We started with the Global Tasting Board, a generous array of cheeses, spreads, meats, naan and lavash.....the three of us had a party with it, the stand out to me was the skordalia, which I've never had the pleasure of, this was something to write home about.  By the time it occurred to us to photograph the tasting board, it was almost gone, but Chef Dustin saved the day, he sent us photo, one of same and as you can see, it's totally inviting....

 The starter didn't leave us much room for full entrees, so we ordered up some Blue Point oysters raw and roasted, the sweet ocean breeze arrived with the platter of raw oysters, indicating the freshness, big kudos for that alone.  The roasted oysters with parmesan, limoncello butter and mignonette was equally as good.   we left just enough room for the deep fried baklava with ice cream, this was the killer coda to one fine meal at a very new, up and upcoming dining establishment along the Kennedy corridor.....Our server, Robin was on the ball, we wanted for nothing....totally on point.  You won't get any complaints from me.  To Chris, we raise our glass to you, you run a great show....and thanks to Lisa for recommending Global A'Fare

Wow. This was literally the SINGLE best meal I (we) have ever had. 

Came here for a birthday dinner. We ordered the chefs choice selection called "Black Sheep" that toured the chefs choice dishes that night. Ended up with 7+ courses including appetizers and desert. Not only was it the best food I've ever had but the experience was just perfect. Every waiter was so friendly, Sam, who described the food was extremely knowledgeable and got us excited about every delicious dish. The head chef was a culinary mastermind.

If you have a single dinner in Santa Barbara - and want something perfect - food, ambience, and people wise - it's gotta be this place. 

Wow.

Amidst a crowded, high-quality food truck scene in University City, Magic Carpet emerges as one of my favorites. Excellent vegetarian fare and great cultural food options make this a go-to for lunch. The long line says it all about the popularity of this spot.

I particularly enjoy the daily specials, especially the Bella Donna wrap. It's convenient to eat and absolutely delicious. Only caveat: make sure to get there before noon if you want to snag a daily special!
