The only item I don't order is the Foo Chow. But you can't go wrong with any other dish!

Went for dinner on a saturday night. Service was quick but my server did nothing when i complained about my over cooked food which he recommended to me. My buddy got some pasta swimming in sauce and over seasoned.we shared a bruschetta appetizer which was bland. I found everything overpriced for the quality and dont plan on ever returning.

I have to say the sauce is fantastic. Place is definitely a hole in the wall, and that part is ok with me too. But the sides are very small and I found bones in my pulled pork. The ribs were tasty but seemed to contain more bones than most..
Will we be back? I'm not sure..Still looking for great BBQ.

I love the burgers here.  The truffle burger and the spicy guac are both so good, I have a tough time picking between the two.  However, the management here is pretty terrible.  I've been here twice during lunch hours and it took 30-40 mins to get my food.  After multiple apologies and some free coupons, I eventually got my food.  On Sunday, we were there at 11 and they opened late and no one was ready.  Can't imagine how successful they would be if they cared and applied some common sense...

The AC was broken on the day we tried this place. Their kitchen was also closed for some reason even though it was midday. out but the weather wasn't too unbearable to still enjoy our time here.  There plenty of seating inside/outside/as well as upstairs. It's a pretty intimate setting but still great for groups

We ordered a bottle of wine and relaxed in their front corner. It was either the wine or the gradual (or both) that got us all feeling really tired and sleepy but the place was pretty much empty the entire time we were there (12~1). The gentleman who was serving us was dripping with sweat due to the broken AC but was really nice, however, he was really aggressive with trying to get us to order more bottles. He would come by every 10 minutes (even when we were in deep conversation) and interrupt to push us to get another bottle. We happily denied as we were still working on our first bottle. 

It was awkward when my friend was paying and the two managers/servers literally hovered over her as she was paying... it's hot enough without the AC but even more awkward when you can feel someone else's breath right behind you...

Great place to lounge (would be better if their ac was working) and they have a very large wine selection as well.

Went here on a Saturday night for dinner and was blown away with the food. We were a group of 5 and the small plates concept worked perfectly as we were able to sample a whole lot of dishes. I wish I could remember the exact names on the menu. To describe a few, we got the beef sliders, fish tacos, truffle Mac N cheese, snapper and scallops. All of the above were 5 stars and the snapper was the standout. We ended getting all the three desserts on the menu and I fell in love with the chocolate pavlova. Will definitely be back.

Have been here several times, but tonight's meal was impeccably bad. Tried their tri-tip and it was more like tri-rubber and should have tri-something else.

I actually returned the meal and asked for a 1/4 white chicken. It was okay, but lacked tenderness and that slow-roasted rotisserie flavor. The mashed potatoes and corn bread were cold. 

$17.00 for two meals. I could have purchased a bucket of chicken from KFC and would have enjoyed it more and had enough for the balance of the week.
I had a noodle bowl and it was phenomenal! I ate every bite ( to my later regret). Service was friendly and good too.

Out of pure desperation one day, I ordered delivery from Gondolier because they're the only place within delivery range of my crib that uses Grande cheese.  I ordered a small cheese pizza and an Italian sub.  The pizza was good, nothing special, but the Italian was the shinning star of the delivery.  I surprised at how good it was, and for that fact alone, I'm bumping up my review from a 2 star to a 3.  The sandwich was on either an 8 or 9 inch hoagie roll.  I know that every inch matters for the ladies out there, but in subland, it doesn't.  The meat was stacked pretty high, and the flavor of the meats was above average.  I give the sub a solid 4 on my Italian sammich scale.

My boyfriend and I have lived in Nashville for about a year and have always talked about going to The  Chef &I... well Saturday we went and had an AMAZING experience! We sat at the bar so that we could enjoy the full experience by watching how the chefs prepared the food and getting to interact with them as well. We wanted to try everything so we decided to split the $75 Chef experience, which is 8 course tapas style.(small plates) We were planning to get something else if we weren't full after that.. we ended up being full and did not need to add more. Everything we had was to die for!  This is by far my favorite restaurant and i cant wait to go back! they also offer cooking classes which i will for sure be taking! If you haven't been here make a reservation so that you can sit at the bar!
Great brunch. Duck fat tater tots. Dry rubbed chicken wings. Was surprised because it is right on Broadway. Service was excellent. Very friendly.

Guys, I had a rough day. I had to think long and hard about how to turn it around. So I went searching and landed on Almaz Cafe. 

From the outside, it don't look like much but the inside triggers a smile. Bright green paint patched with shiny tin panels. Super modern, super huge light fixture. Non-pretentious tables and chairs. Friendly employees.

The menu is eclectic: American breakfast and lunch items, ice cream, espresso, Ethiopian platters. Anyone who orders a turkey and cheese sandwich here has no sense of adventure.

Rough days call for a break from the mundane. My first bite of Ethiopian foule (spiced beans smashed with tomatoes, onions and peppers accompanied by a side of sour cream, vinegar-tinged pancake-textured bread and turmeric-hued cabbage) was just what I needed and when it was gone I wanted more. 

If it didn't take so long to prepare (really, it was only 15 minutes but I was stressin'!) I would have ordered another. Next time I'll call ahead, as the pleasant guy behind the counter suggested.
Superb coffee and espresso. Favorite is their cafe Miel latte, local honey latte. It's wonderfully delicious without being oversweet. Parking sucks tho.

Was a pleasant surprise to find this place randomly while out and about with the Mrs.  Snagged a few delicious treats for a day out running errands.  The service was quick and friendly and the selection was pretty diverse given the size of the establishment. Would gladly return.
You are so write my apologize for the mistake use do got the perfect sandwich and everything is fresh sorry for the mistake

The best place around for a great taco. I visit often. But today only days after hurricane lrma their phones and internet were down when I got here today for lunch. Instead of turning me away because I did not have cash like most people don't these days. The manager Frank said that my lunch would be on him no questions asked he wanted to make sure I got feed. Lol They truly are awesome both food and staff. Thanks again Frank you're  awesome!

Been coming here for years. Now we come weekly, sometimes 2-3 times per week. The food is AMAZING (Must try the Devil Eggs and the home made pickles) and the drinks will leave you speechless. The entire staff is friendly and AMAZING. Go see Mark, Jenna and Eric at the bar. Each one of them will make you feel at home and as part of the family. 

Cheers

I used to think this was a 4-star, but the fish and chips I had recently were "eh".  They say it is a frozen fish from Indonesia and it's a customer favorite.  I screwed up, should have had the fried clams, which were fresh, not frozen.  The fish and chips fish was the consistency of baby food, kind of mushy, not what you'd expect for fish and chips.  The fries were ok, not the best.  Dining companions had steak, another had chioppino, which were both okay, but not stellar.  Anyone else have a similar experience?  Now that I think about it, I might give it a 2.5 stars.

9/7/11  I changed it to 2 stars.  After my initial rating, I was contacted by the Brophy Bros. management and they said they wanted to send me a gift certificate and they take their business seriously.  They asked for my name and address and I never heard from them again.  I guess they just blew me off.  Oh well.

I have been here twice in the last two weeks. I have also been to their Nashville location. I was thrilled when I learned they were opening a location only 15 mins away from downtown.

This is a brand new building and it's GORGEOUS! The patio is huge. The interior has a clean, rustic feel with all the exposed wood beams. This place is also huge. At least 3x the size of their original location. First time here I couldn't help myself. I ordered the pulled pork nachos. They are amazing. Loaded with cheese, big chunks of house smoked pork, dotted with black beans and jalapeños, then drizzled with BBQ and ranch. It's a life changing nacho dish!

My second visit I opted for the mixed grill platter since I love their pulled pork so much. I was not disappointed one bit. In fact I already know what I will be ordering the next time I am there! Their smoked chicken has amazing flavor. It's so smokey it's almost salty. I have never tasted such delicious smoke flavor in a chicken before. It doesn't need sauce because it's tasty and juicy!

I have heard rumblings that this place isn't as good as the original. Maybe I have been lucky because I think it's just as good and I will be back, soon!
This is a great breakfast place, especially if you are really hungry! Food portions are huge!

I love Jeannine's but it was a little disappointing this time around. My boyfriend and I went at around 10 or 11 AM on a Thursday and it was not busy compared to how I've seen it before.

I ordered the pancake breakfast with a vanilla latte and my boyfriend got the breakfast burrito (which he found was great!). We found a table and sat for about 2 minutes when the gentleman that took our order told me that they couldn't make pancakes (that was the only reason we went there). I wanted to eat a sweet breakfast so I decided to sub with the french toast. Also a no-go. 

Disappointed, I just decided to go with the chicken pesto sandwich. I decided to not get grumpy over their lack of pancakes and french toast (you would think they would some bread and eggs for this?) but it was odd when one of the managers or supervisors yelled at me from across the room that my latte was on its way. 
Don't get me wrong, the sandwich was delicious and their lattes never disappoint. But the main reason I wanted to go was for their pancakes. I guess we shouldn't go on Thursdays anymore as they run out of the sweet stuff!

I work at a high end hotel in town and I always recommend this place to all of our guests that are looking for a great breakfast/ lunch outside of the hotel. Hopefully what happened to me doesn't happen to our wonderful, high-paying guests!!

Yes, it's a chain restaurant but the food is incredible.  They have free refills on the tortilla chips and soda.

My kids are super picky and always find something they love when we're there.  I'm a big fan of the tofu bowl, but have had great burritos too.  The food is made to order and you decide what you do and do not want on it.  Total customization.  They often have specials like kids eat free or buy one get one free burritos.  We often eat there as a family of 4 for under $20, and are never dissapointed with the food.  Fresh ingredients that are good quality.  Join their email club and get coupons and discounts.
Great and fresh. Casual and priced right for what it is.

Chips. Salsa. Queso. Arroz con pollo. Margaritas. Patio. Yep, this is my Broad Ripple happy place.

Though this isn't quite my favorite Mexican in Indy, it's still pretty dang good. I usually don't even attempt to come in during the months the patio isn't open due to extremely limited seating inside. Regardless, the service is fast and efficient and all the wait staff is really nice.

My only real complaint is honestly about the margaritas. They're good, not great, some times they're more watered down than others. This won't deter me from coming and I'm actually texting a friend to make plans to come here this week after writing this review.

Not great. Ordered saganaki (which has a really thick breading here) and calamari (which was rubbery) the meat in the gyros wasn't great and didn't have much flavor. Service was really really slow, the servers were really nice and we appreciated the dog friendly patio. Just kinda disappointed because Greek food is generally incredible on Dodecanese.

Parking during the week is horrid, but the weekends has valet. On the flip side, there wasn't a wait for seating when we came.on a Thursday.

We were promptly seated, and I ordered a peach bellini, which was quite tasty.

My husband ordered an omelette, and I had the skinny miga. We shared the NOLA 'Nectar Snowball French Toast. The skinny miga was perfect since I rarely eat eggs and satisfied my craving. My husband LOVED his omelette, but he felt that the French Toast was too sweet. I loved the the sweetness.

Ate here a few weeks ago on a business trip and the food was good but not the best I have had. The squash blossom appetizer was hard to eat and most of the cheese fell out when I picked it up and the blossoms were soggy. Personally I would have stuffed them, chilled them down a bit then lightly battered them and fried them. This is how I thought they were going to come but the description on the menu was vague. The cold melon soup was really good. It was mildly sweet with a bit of kick on the back end from tabasco. It had a nice marsala reduction on top that complemented the sweetness of the soup. For my Entree I got the braised lamb shank. I have eaten a lot of braised lamb shanks at lesser known and less expensive restaurants around the bay like Chalet Basque and been much more satisfied. The meat was kind of tough for what I expect braised meat to be and there was no sauce on or around the meat. You can take the braising liquid remove the fat and turn it into a nice pan gravy/sauce to spoon over the meat.  The decor was also very outdated in my opinion. The setting seems like a country home but they are serving modern food so ?

My rating is actually 3.5 stars but since yelp doesn't allow it 3 have been given. Had the lamb shank been more tender and had a sauce I would have given at least 4 stars. I think it was worth checking out but I would rather go to Harrah's Steak House for the money I spent

Still the best Mexican food at the price point in SB. 

The steak tostada (tostada del pueblo with steak) is magnificent. It used to look different, though. Now more like a tostada salad. 

Also the salsas are THE BEST in Santa Barbara, which is saying something. 

Wonderful people at the De La Vina location, where I go now that I'm over in this part of town. 

Enchiladas suiza a favorite of mine, too.

New to the area Fat Boys Pizza is a good slice. They are large like Mo's Pizza on the Westbank. I had the meat and pepperoni slices (had to box up the pepperoni to go). 

The crust is crisp but there isn't much flavor to it. It does hold up to the insanely large slice you get. The sauce is ok, it could be sweeter and a spicier. 

Overall it is a good pizza a a good deal for the price of $6-8 bucks a slice depending on your toppings. Take a trip down and get a slice or maybe try the two foot slice challenge.

I'm an avid foodie but seldom write reviews.  This will be the exception because Savanh of Laos is exceptional.

This is a family business and they treated us like family.  Service A++

Don't be fooled by the lackluster exterior.  The interior is lovely and clean.  

We ordered the Duck Larb (with a soup on the side), Papaya Salad, and the BBQ Chicken Laos style.  Everything was flavored perfectly.  The greens and herbs were so fresh I wouldn't be surprised if they had gone out to their garden to garnish our plates.  The chef came out personally to make sure everything was to our liking and was very friendly.  He is an artist who loves his work as is evident in the wonderful food and service.  

Thank you Savanh of Laos!

Took a cab right from PHL to this place. I was starving upon my 1pm arrival. The staff was very accommodating andxwelcoming and made some wonderful recommendations for me and my friend who lives around the corner and is a regular here. I'll definitely come back again. Love the gelato and the ambiance

Absolutely love Shalhoobs, what a gem.

Not only are their tri tip sandwiches (which come with amazing fries) delectable, they also have a wide variety of other food. Anything with tri tip at this place is going is going to make you happy as it melts in your mouth and gives you a flavor explosion. 

My other favorite is their avocado salad. It comes with lots of chopped avocado, crunchy broccoli and it is just really well put together and flavorful. To add meat it does get a little pricy to around $17, but if you want a healthier alternative and still get the tri tip, it's well worth it. 

Other things I've seen that are so exciting but I haven't tried on the menu are their street corn apps, their falafels, and a crispy chicken sandwich.

The atmosphere is so great and inviting, perfect for larger groups, and the food comes out quick!

Definitely drop by whenever you're around, you'll be happy you did.

- J
Soo much flavor in every bite! Everything thing we had was delicious, ate every last bit. This is being added to the must bring visitors to list.

This is one of my regular Mexican restaurants of choice. Everyone in my family loves the wet burrito and we get it all the time. Also their margaritas are very good. Strong but not overpowering and lots of flavor options. I love the black raspberry and some of the other berry flavors. Good size and portions for the price! I was so glad to see them get a lot of take out traffic during covid because it would be sad if this place went out if business. 

Staff is friendly and attentive. I have no complaints!!
Love them!  Best food and priced right. Love the familiar faces when picking up food and it's always hot and flavorful!

Overall it is a beautiful property in a prime location. Friendly staff and and room's themselves are beautiful. There is not much more you can ask for in a hotel room. There was one negative of the trip however and that was the temps of the rooms. I couldn't use blankets at night because the room was so hot. It never got below 73 no matter how low we tried to set it. Overall almost a perfect stay minus the heat.

Delicious! I can't say I'm a cheesesteak connoisseur, but Jim's was a great cheesesteak experience! Make sure you know your order going up. My boyfriend and I went together and got one cheesesteak with whiz, one with provolone. Both with onions, mayo and ketchup. They were both really delicious, soft bread, tender meat, gooey cheese (esp. the one with whiz). I liked seeing who else had been to Jim's (there's tons of memorabilia on the walls), and the upstairs seating area was definitely a nice place to sit (the back kitchen area you have to walk through to get there..not so much). But who cares? Jim's clearly isn't trying to impress with service or decor--they don't have to. There was a line out the door  on a Sunday afternoon around 1 PM, and for good reason--Jim's has delicious cheesesteaks! Mine definitely hit the spot!

Also, the streets around Jim's looked pretty fun--some cool bars, sex shops (always fun to wander around in), funky stores selling clothes, hats, etc. Go Go Go!

This pizza is damn good. You can tell it's made with care, great ingredients, a chewy crust that is baked until it is barely blistered and topped with fresh park and basil. I really liked their thick cut pepperoni. I'm looking forward to trying their other pizzas and subs which look awesome. 
They don't have a phone number, so you gotta just go there. Cash only.

GOOD LUCK GETTING YOUR ORDER. Wingstop is usually my coworkers and my  first choice for lunch when we go for wings but not anymore! This time they dropped the Ball big time you see we understand that multiple orders may take a while longer to prepare so we usually call 2-3hours in advance so they can have it ready by our lunch time and they usually do but not this time. The problem wasn't just that the food wasn't ready it was also the fact that when the food was ready they didn't bother giving it to us until 15 minutes later because they forgot we were waiting on more orders and the place wasn't even busy at all!! The cooks in back were joking around half the time. This whole ordeal wasted our whole lunch time giving us no time to eat, we're definitely not going back.
Update: manager contacted me and apologized for the experience and offered a complementary meal, although I didn't take the meal it was a nice gesture and I appreciate the fact she took the time to reach out to me and make things right.

This WAS the go to spot for the best fast food burgers ever!  However after I contacted Culver's corporate about the owner's attitude, the latter called me and profusely apologized for what had been a bad day for him and his store. Well: I can understand that and I certainly appreciated the call so we decided to give the place another try. The look on the owner's face was priceless and genuine when we walked in. Handshakes and pleasantries all around.

So the missus has her usual butter burger deluxe and upgraded to cheese curds. This time I tried the limited-time pretzel haus burger. Pickled onions, bacon and pub sauce with two kinds of cheese. I wouldn't get it every time but wow, was that sucker delicious. Good char as usual on the patties and a great bun that held up nicely really did a good job rounding out the sandwich.

Those cheese curds, you ask? I am not a big fan of fried cheese as a rule (nor of cheddar), but these things rocked. Lovely saltiness of the warm gooey cheese made a great contrast with the light, crunchy breading. Overall, food came out at a good temperature and we both enjoyed the hospitality offered by Parrish and his employees. Thanks, Parrish! Glad to be back again..

I really wanted to like this place better than I did.  A couple of positives--the service was amazing.  I really like the atmosphere, too.

The mediocre--my meal.  I got the breaded tenderloin, which I'd heard good things about.  I found it to be quite bland, and all the breading slid off the meat pretty much immediately, so I was left with a pork tenderloin sandwich and a plate full of breading.  I chose onion rings as my side, and the were considerably burnt.  (Like--I'm no chef, but I would have been ashamed to have let them out of MY kitchen)

That said, some others in our party had different meals and they looked amazing, and they were all quite pleased with what they got.  Although I was disappointed in my meal, the atmosphere and service make it so I'll return.

So we went back here to try the cheeseburger sliders for dinner tonight. We both got the brown bag meal which comes with sliders, fries and a drink. THE SLIDERS WERE AMAZING. They were so tender and cooked medium-medium well so they were still pink in the middle. Aka cooked to perfection. The buns were also SO GOOD. The only thing I can't speak to is the sauce because we got the sliders without the sauce since we don't like any sauce on our burgers (aside from ketchup, obvs). 

The only part of the meal I didn't like were the French fries. They are waffle fries, but they were just too dry and hard for me. I like greasy, softer fries. With that said, my boyfriend loved the fries so it's just a matter of preference, not necessarily quality. 

For dessert, we had to get the cinnamon roll given how much we loved it the first time we went. We loved it just as much, if not more this time around.

I bought four cheese ravioli, pecorino cream sauce and a package of pancetta for around $20. It took around 20 minutes to make. My husband, who prefers meaty tomato sauces, LOVED this. Everything is so fresh and easy to cook. It's cheaper and tastier than going to a restaurant and so quick and easy for a weeknight meal. Love this place!

Everytime i visit Tampa, this would be on my priority list. Its a hole on the wall restaurant serving authentic chinese food. The best fried fish, calamari, fried crabs I've tasted! It is not expensive too. Just dont expect too much of their interior. But the food is soooo good.

Went in tonight with my boyfriend craving a good Bloody to share.  Ordered from bartender:  "ok, if we have it."  What??? They run through their bloody mix by lunch & then don't make more for evening?  This was @ 6:30,   "Sorry we don't have it."  I am still in a state of shock.  I was a bartender once.  I should have ordered each ingredient individually and then stirred my own.  My guy had a beer.  Sorry he gave in & patronized them.   The Restaurant was not so busy that he could not have made some mix then & there.  What if they ran out of Jameson's

HORRIBLE SERVICE!!! LACK OF COMMUNICATION!  I went to this location today (the day after Christmas) and was surprised that there was only one person in line as this location is usually always busy. I waited patiently as the woman in front of me was asking a bunch of questions about the syrups and sugar free items. I glanced at the board and noticed a huge sign advertising a FREE drink when you sign up on the Starbucks rewards app and register your card. I waited until the woman in front of me finished her order and when it was my turn I asked the cashier about the advertisement. I asked, "If I sign up right now, will I receive a free drink?" The cashier acted as if she didn't know what I was talking about so I pointed at the sign behind her and stated my question again. Again, she had a puzzled look on her face, then another worker chimed in and stated that I would receive an email of some sort with a coupon. I said, "Okay, I'll step aside and register now." As I sat in a chair right by the register I noticed a young woman and a homeless man. They were talking to one another, and to quickly sum up their conversation, she was in there to buy him (the homeless man) a drink and a sandwich; which I thought was a great gesture for someone in need while most people are celebrating the holidays. The young woman ordered the drink and food and I hear her tell the man that everything is paid for and that the worker would call him when it's done. She left the store after that. I'm pretty much done registering my card on the app and waiting for an email with my coupon. As I wait, one of the workers yells a woman's name and is holding a food bag. I just observe for the moment and say to myself "that was clearly the girl's who bought the sandwich for the homeless man." I began to feel a little antsy because it started getting crowded with people and I still had no email. I then hear the homeless man (he was speaking loudly every time he spoke) he's asking a cashier about his drink and food. Mind you, there are now two new cashiers at the register. I see the situation escalating because the cashier explains that he did not ring the man up and he would have to wait a second (as he was ringing another customer). The homeless man just says "what do you mean? It's already been paid for. The girl, the girl bought it for me! a hot chocolate and a sandwich." I no longer could just stand by. I got up from the chair and I asked the male cashier where the female cashier went who was just on the registers. I said "I saw everything, a young woman was in here and she bought him food and left!" and as I'm explaining this the female cashier peeks her head around the corner and I point stating "she rung her up" (As I did this, I see the food and sandwich sitting off to the side together, unclaimed). I was just fed up, I yelled "There's the food right there! What is the problem? Why are y'all not communicating? This is horrible service, I'm leaving". So I left, with no drink and no further explanation of this supposedly FREE drink they were advertising. I hope that man was able to get his drink and sandwich, he clearly needed it. It's really a shame that the young woman took the time to help him, trying to do a good deed for someone, and the workers there just totally ruined everything. I will never return to this location, it's not the first time I've had a bad experience.
This bar is fabulous. We loved the food, beer and cocktails! I've told several friends about this joint as it's a great date night spot.

Went there for lunch Monday and had a portobello pita and friend of mine had the seitan gyro. Both were great! The flavor of the seitan was perfection and my sandwich left me feeling satisfied but not weighed down. So healthy and good! I'll be back!
If you want a place where the waitress is a jerk because she had a long day ask for Becky!
Superb service and amazing food. Highly recommend. The raw oysters were super fresh and the shrimp and catfish platter was straight awesome. We will be going back before we end this trip.

Amazing meal, best fra diavlo I've ever had. Perfect amount of spice, rich flavorful broth, and the soft shell crab and other seafood was perfectly cooked. We went with the fixed price menu, the salad was also great.  Don't normally order dessert,  but made room for the pistachio tiramisu and it was worth it. 

Service was also great, perfect evening.

Bricco has almost 2 of everything, 2 bars , 2 seating areas, with completely different ambiances and both a wood fire stove and a coal fire stove.

Popular/crowded night here is Wednesday night is half off pizza night. Great pizzas with a lot of options. 

Great place to go for Happy Hour, appetizer and drink specials. Appetizers are not quite half off but a good deal, well drinks are around $4.

I eat/order food from here at least once a week. Their queso dip is crack in a cup, and their burritos and nachos are amazing. I also LOVE the fact you can customize anything to your liking, because it's made right in front of you.

This was my first time trying this place out and my experience was great. The service was fast and we got our food pretty quickly and efficiently. We ordered the salad rolls and green onion cakes for appetizer and they were pretty decent. For main course we ordered the grilled meat with vermicelli and that was very good and delicious. The meat was moist and shrimp was cooked to perfection. This place is recommended if you are a vietnamese food lover.

One of the best restaurants I've ever been to! Quality service, perfect ambiance with a 1920s type feel, and the best meal of my life. My Delmonico steak was cooked to perfection and my drink made to match! They even gave us dessert on the house for my birthday. Couldn't have had a better time if we tried!

My mom and I were out doing some shopping and noticed the sign pizza by the slice. So we stopped in for a bite! This gem of a pizza place was unexpected. The slice was deliciously cheesy with a crisp crust. Enjoyed the relaxing seating and talked with the owner while we ate. Word of mouth is the old school way so I'm leaving this review spreading the news to please try this little slice of heaven family owned pizzeria.
I'm really not a pizza person but given the hype I had to try Pizza D. So glad I did. Excellent pizza and Caesar salad, lots of variety in the menu, and casual upbeat atmosphere. Definitely recommend

Food was good, had the oysters Rockefeller, the bar upstairs on the outside patio was nice but couldn't make specific to order drinks (orange crush) because they weren't equipped with the ingredients but they did have the ability to make what was on the menu. So as long as u don't stray from the menu ur good. Food came out hot, and tasted good. Good view of the sunset and great live music.

It's a very popular breakfast place in Nashville so I decided to give it a try. Their menu is very small and so is their location. I ordered three dishes so sample and all the food was decent but nothing excelled or stood out. The fried chicken is just okay, my sunny side up egg had runny whites, French toast was decent, and everting was just lukewarm not hot. Iced coffee again was just okay, if you're looking for exceptional flavors and service I would go elsewhere.

Coolest bar on Bourbon street! This place is massive and has an awesome feel to it. Each room and each area has a different feel which makes it fun to bounce around the rooms and check it all out. 

They make pretty good drinks but be warned that you will have a hangover after the hurricane ‍
the only vegetarian item on the menu is soup, well, that's of course if you like chicken broth. they would have gotten 1 star, if a solution wasn't thought of. we got steamed vegetables.

So good. Ate all vegetarian food, all with amazing different flavors. Every dish delicious. We had golden mushrooms, chili potato, tomatoes with egg, Bok Choy with soybean, chili cucumbers, and Xi'an Liang Pi. Loved it the first time I went a year ago; loved it even more the second time.

This Mexican Restraunt is the best I love there breaded chicken called a Minalesa and there stake burrito I Would  totally recommend this Mexican restraunt and I have been to different Mexican restraunt's across Indianapolis but this is the best I would recommend you guys to go have some food. Go have some burritos and enjoy your visit at Los Portales.                                    

          LOVED IT                 Best food Ever

Delicious, inventive food, great service. Yummy cocktails as well! I've been several times and was never disappointed with any dish. I wish the restaurant was a little bigger to cut down on waits but maybe if it's open longer that will calm down.

What happened to the customer service here. It seems like once the el dorado took over, the staff at SL gave up on customer service. El dorado Managment need to refresh this crew on what customer service means. If they  need someone to refresh them I would gladly by up to the challenge to train the crew to show them how to treat a customer

I love this place for a nice weekend American brunch. Everything we ordered was delicious, and the price is reasonable. Most importantly, this restaurant is only 2 or 3 blocks from the independence hall. So, it could be a good choice for tourist as well. They don't have private parking lot, so either street parking or garage parking.

This was the only restaurant we could find that would return Yelp messages or phone calls about taking a reservation for sixteen people.  Robyn from Marriott at Treasure Island recommended this establishment to us.  We took our family here for a dinner after a beach wedding.  The food was exceptional and the service was superb.  Beautiful ocean views from the dining room.  If trying to find it, it's inside the Treasure Island resort.  If definitively go again.

This has become my favorite store in the area. Not for the food or the products, but for the customer service.  The entire staff works towards treating each customer as a friend. It's not selective and it's not forced, it's genuine. Over the past two years, I have managed to meet some very caring members of this team. I have watched them deliver the same care and concern and happiness to see each person come through their door.  I come from a background with over 20 years in retail management. In order for this type of atmosphere to be present in the store starts from the top down. They have a great leadership team who lead by example and must show it to their employees too and daily.  I've tried to go to other locations and even other companies, but no go. Love this store and team.  It shows in all they do.   Job well done.

This place had decent breakfast, the omelettes are great. Good prices, however it's way too crowded, the service is not that good, only one bathroom and depending on the day there's a line to get in. I'm not sure what I'm missing but it's not that good were I'll stand outside to eat there.

Disclaimer: I'm reviewing Bobby's Burger Palace as a vegetarian.

I came to this BBP late on a Sunday night with some friends on a whim. I used to be a big follower of Food Network, so I was excited to try a Bobby Flay restaurant, though I knew my options were limited as a vegetarian.

The interior is cool--a bright, colorful interior, striped bar-like tables, and nice shots of burger food paintings on the walls. The line was short, and it wasn't too crowded since it was a Sunday night, so we only waited about 5 minutes to order. I got a Griddled Cheese--which is basically a bunch of different cheeses and tomato between white bread--and Sweet Potato Fries, which came with Honey Mustard Horseradish Sauce. My friend who was eating ordered a Palace Classic Burger.

We sat at our table, and the food came out about 15 minutes later. I was very underwhelmed by the cheese sandwich I really could have made at home, yet paid almost $6 for. It was boring, bland, and randomly oily. The sweet potato fries were a bit better, but not outstanding by any means, and the honey mustard/horseradish sauce was watery and sad. The only thing I really liked food-wise were the variety of sauces at the table, ranging from Chipotle Ketchup to Jalapeno Sauce to Burger Sauce, which were all actually really interesting and made the food substantially more tolerable. 

Maybe the cool burgers are better, but my friend said he was just content with the one he got--he said we might as well have just gone to the nearby McDonald's to get a burger instead of wasting money here. Overall, at least from my experience, don't go to BBP if you're a vegetarian unless you feel like blowing a ridiculous amount of money on a basic cheese sandwich. Hopefully the celebrity chef restaurants I go to in the future are more up to standards.

Well I was shopping on New Year's Day and lunchtime came. Drove by quite a few places but most were closed. Luckily So Italian was open. I looked at the menu board and saw they also have several lunch specials ie pick two items and get a drink as well. Looked like a good deal. The soup that day was tomato basil. I picked the half sandwich soup option. The sandwich was a bit smaller than I would have liked, but with the soup I was satisfied with the two items. They have several sandwich choices as well. The bread was quite good. But in reality the place is best know for pizza and luckily my son has been eating non stop so I had them make a large pepperoni mushroom pie. There crust is truly outstanding. Chewed but light. The cheese is a good quality tasty mix. Toppings fairly generous without being overdone. Sauce just right. Keep in mind these are thin hand tossed pizzas so if you want a different kind they mainly offer those. Albeit as it was winter so I ate inside, but they do offer outside tables for dining as well. It wasn't too busy at lunchtime and the food came out quickly. Overall quite good and worth stopping in.
Best of the best.   The hidden gem of new hope.  Love the food here.  If you are in the area stop in.

Nice place.  Great food.  The waitress/hostess really prompted the 5 stars as she really took good care of me.  I'd give the food a 4.5 star only because the calamari was kinda crunchy but that's all personal preference.
Great food (amazing Detroit Style Pizza), great beers on tap and a very friendly staff.  A MUST GO TO spot in Philly.

This place has incredible food which is made of high quality ingredients. Food is served hot and is fresh. They have apparently changed the tortilla chips they use with the chips and salsa. While those chips are still good they aren't as good as the ones they used to have. They even have real butter for their baked potatoes, cornbread, etc.. The bourbon bacon burger is phenomenal (but tough to say).
The staff is super friendly and nice but the food is not great. It seems like a Fridays imitation, not so many options to choose from.

Everything about this place is amazing I love the food, the service and even takeout is just as good as eating in. I come for dinner and my family also had a party here and I also get takeout from here on a regular and i can't express enough that THE FOOD IS AMAZING!!!

This is my favorite taco stand. In. The. World. I've had alot of tacos, but I've come to crave certain dishes here, like the rajas, sauteed pasilla chiles with melted cheese and herbs, and slow cooked onions on freshly made corn tortillas, and the #16 which is grilled chiles and cheese together on fresh handmade tortillas. They know what they are doing here, they keep it simple and nothing changes except for the fresh turquoise paint in this old Orange Julius on Milpas.The salsas are just how I like them, the proportions are just right and not too overwhelming, I don't give out 5 stars very often but this place deserves it. Ive probably been here 100 times and its been good every single time.
Slow slow slow. Serious this place is on the decline. Be prepared to wait 20mins for 3 tacos

Four friends and I had dinner at The Block this weekend. We met there around 6:30 on Saturday and had to wait about 15 minutes for a table. We waited in the bar area and were very happy with our cocktails. 
   Once we were seated, we ordered 2 appetizers, the Ale & Cheddar dip with house-made pretzels and the brussel sprouts.....you heard me, a brussel sprout appetizer. Don't turn up your nose, it was fantastic! It will make a believer out of you. Seriously. We also demolished the pretzels and dip, stopping just short of licking the bowl. Which, by the way, one of my friends has been known to do in a restaurant.
   We all ordered a different entree: fish special, rib-eye, sirloin, scallop salad and a hamburger. Again, we were all very happy, except for a small mishap with the burger. There was a bit of inedible gristle in it, which my friend mentioned to our waiter. He apologized, manager came out and apologized, comped her dessert. Aside from the gristle, the burger was really good, cooked exactly as described by Jason, our waiter. I had the walleye, which I wasn't sure I was going to like, but I'm trying to eat more fish, so, what the heck. It was delicious. Cleaned my plate, which I usually don't do at restaurants because I like leftovers.
   We each ordered a different dessert. The best was a potted chocolate with toasted marshmallows on top. Coming in a close second was a brown sugar-coconut ice cream. Apple tart was also good. Our two least favorites were a dried cherry-chocolate bread pudding (a bit dry) and the chocolate-bacon ice cream (too much chocolate, not enough bacon).
   Although the place was busy, our service was good. Jason, our waiter, was extremely knowledgable and did not steer us wrong on any of his recommendations. 
All of us were pretty happy ladies when we left. I know we will be back!
The tea is a bit weak but the ginger snaps are amazing and the scones are pretrybgood as well. Next time I'll have to try the coffee.
Great place, nice selection of beers for anyone's taste, awesome service and nice vibe.  Will frequent there every time I'm in Reno!

EDITED: 
I've had to knock Demo's down a star. The last two times i've been there, the food has been really bad.   Had the Greek-style spaghetti (my staple) again... terrible. Chicken was obviously cooked the day before; sauce was bland. No cinnamon. So bad, I complained.  They gave me a free dessert. Great. Thanks.  I would have rather had the entree the way it used to be. 
The time before that, I had a steak; overcooked and not seasoned the way it used to be. 
What's up with you, Demo's? You were awesome for years. YEARS UPON YEARS. I don't want to come back and have another bad meal. 
Your reputation should make you strive to provide what people expect. C'mon!


ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Demos' has been a food staple for Nashvillians for years; read the reviews and you'll see what's in store for you...delicious steaks and Italian food for a great price!
I'd just like to add a few personal notes: Jim's famous spinach is an amazing appetizer. Fresh spinach, egg, olive oil and garlic. My god. It's to die for. 
I've read a few negative reviews about the Greek style chicken sauce spaghetti...but honestly, it's my favorite dish at Demos'. Heads up: you'll have to love cinnamon! If you do, then this dish is spectacular.; very unique in its flavor with chicken, cinnamon, onion, garlic and tomato. 
One last word of advice: very rarely,  the steaks tend to be a bit overcooked. A few times over the past few years, I've asked for medium rare, and I've gotten medium. They'll fix it for you if that ever happens. 
All in all, it's one of the best eateries in Nashville for a very affordable price. Try it and you'll be a fan.

I love this place, and Charles Chen! (and not just because he hugs me when I see him.) Mr. Chen really bangs it out in the kitchen. Every time my boyfriend and I have been here it's nothing short of severely awesome. If you cant decide what to eat he always offers great recommendations. This is absolutely my favorite place to eat in china town. Charles makes you feel very welcomed and seems genuinely happy to see you when you come back ( which of course you will). The vegetarian won ton soup is basically life changing, as is the vegetarian orange beef, i feel like its safe to say there probably is not really anything bad on the menu. By far the best Chinese food I have had. ever. seriously.

My guess is Casa Del Matador is going for the fine dinning/upscale Mexican restaurant vibe. It is a beautiful restaurant and I bet in the spring/summer the patio would be a great place to people watch and enjoy a drink and maybe some chips and salsa. They do have a wood burning fire place in the middle of the restaurant that was wonderful on a cold winter night. I left with my hair smelling like campfire though. Not a bad thing, just something to be aware of. 
We missed Happy Hour, but from the menu it looks like they have some very good deals on select appetizers. 
Nothing bad to say about the service, except a little on the slow side. But our waitress was very friendly, offered suggestions and handled our large group very well.
The food - just okay. Some good and some not good. And on the pricey side, at least for Mexican food. But it's in The Village, so this isn't surprising. The chips and salsa are very good. For another appetizer we ordered the Queso Fundito. It's melted cheese with pablano peppers and caramelized onions and comes with your choice of warmed corn or flour tortillas. We choose the flour based on our waitresses suggestion. The queso had no flavor at all, especially for all the peppers and onions that we could see in the dip. The tortillas were good and nice and warm, but even dipping the chips in the dip didn't help much, except to add some much needed salt.
For dinner I ordered the carnitas tacos and my husband ordered the braised beef tacos. Both plates came with two tacos, Spanish rice and black beans. Both of our tacos were very good. The pico that comes on them was spicier than most places, but it was delicious. Sadly the tacos were the only thing on the plate that had any flavor. The rice was undercooked (crunchy) and flavorless and the black beans tasted like they'd just been scooped out of a pan of boiled beans. There was a little cheese on them, but not enough to add any flavor. So we each had a plate of two tacos for $12 each, because neither one of us ate more than a bite of the rice and beans. Good thing we filled up on chips and salsa.
Everyone at the table who ordered the Cadillac margaritas enjoyed them. Not overly sweet. The menu shows a lot of specialty margaritas that sound interesting. So I might try it again for Happy Hour and a drink. I'm a little more open minded than my husband. He said never again - unless we have a gift card or someone else is paying.

I have been in three times.  Once with a friend for dinner and once alone at the bar and of course a happy hour!  All were fabulous. Have had a few different cocktails that were all fabulous, including their daily punch at happy hour which was delish!  My only negative would be they have a few spicy dishes which are pretty conservative on the spice. Both the pizza and the crab pasta, turn 'em up a bit or give people the option to turn them up. Spice is something I look forward to, and when it isn't there and I was expecting I get :(.  Service was on point all three times, with a small exception.  The bar very obviously has regulars and it took a while to get someone's attention both initially and when I wanted food or refills. Remember those first timers, could, turn into regulars with the right attention.

Why is it when chains start to become popular they start cutting corners?

Their queso used to be really good, now it tastes like they got it out of a can from Costco, yuck. 

I got nachos and the cheese wasn't even melted on it, the little cheese there was.

Last time coming here.

Horrible experience . The food we did have was disgusting . Came in with a party of 6. Once they came to bring the food they let us know 2 of us wouldn't be getting what we ordered . Why would you bring out food for some of our party and what are the rest of us suppose to do ? The manager/owner was at the bar having a beer . He was already drunk so who do you complain to ? Wouldn't recommend ever , my fault I didn't look up the reviews on Yelp before I dined there 

Avoid at all cost not worth it !

Anyone who gives Mom's Place less than four stars should be blacklisted and shamed of themselves. This is what a great American diner should look like, smell like, feel like and taste like. Excellent breakfast food [check], big portions with low prices [got that], waitresses that are friendly and efficient [yes, ma'am], comfy booths and interesting memorabilia as decoration [oh yeah], unbelievable location [FTW], and a strict CASH ONLY policy [why mess with what works]. 

Mom's the perfect place to grab a bite to eat if you happen to be in the area - sometimes it's even worth going out of your way. The menu is basic diner and the quality is outstanding. Ned a place to grab a bite before a Yankees spring training game? Check out the dozens of autographed pictures along the walls near the restrooms! Dis you just pick someone up from the airport? Or are you dropping them off and have time to spare? Their first (or last) memories of Tampa should be of the omelettes and iced tea at Mom's (with a side of biscuits and gravy). 

I wish I lived close enough to become a regular ... but then I would eat here all the time and woe-betide my cholesterol and waistline.

Cocktail Lounge Side:
Forgot about PA's archaic liquor laws until my recent visit, when I walked all around downtown at 7:00pm on a Sunday looking for beer or wine.  I used to live in Philly in 1995 and I thought the laws would have been change since then.  

Anyway, I finally remembered the "take-out" beer thing and went to this place.  I was in and out very quickly. Of course there was a little back-and-forth from the drunk regulars inside (who else would be there at 7:00pm on a Sunday), but it was all in good humor.  

Restaurant Side:
The next day, my conference buddies were looking for a nice quick greasy-spoon breakfast and I suggested this place.  Midtown III is the epitome of an old school urban diner. The welcome was warm and the service was very attentive and friendly. The food was well-prepared, well-presented and well-seasoned.  This is your go-to place for a hearty affordable American breakfast (though they were out of Scrapple that day :-)

When we lived in Hi-Pointe, Par Lounge was less than a block away.  My husband and I liked having a bar within walking distance.

Upside:  It has a friendly atmosphere, and Gina (one of the owners) is very sweet.  The drinks are relatively inexpensive.  Great sofa area and large screen TV.  The Jello shot syringes are fun.

Downside:  Too much cigarette smoke.  The spinach dip is greasy and tastes like it has that abominable Provel stuff in it.

Breakfast or lunch 7 days a week, dinner weekdays only, very good authentic Cuban food. No frills order at the counter service and they bring you your food. Fresh, hot, and super delicious. 
There are tables both inside and outside. Not super crowded during lunch today, good steady business and the ladies behind the counter are very nice. Like a happy family serving their own recipes.
I ordered the deviled crab and it was the size of a junior football. Loaded with crab and plenty of flavor. 
Authentic Cuban beverages from the cold case and a soda fountain with the usual Coke products.  
I don't live in Tampa anymore but if I did, I would get lunch from here all the time.

My friends and I got there right when they opened on a Sunday and there was already a line. The line went by fast and most people past the time by having a beer or 2. I would say we waited 45 minutes but it's worth it. The chicken was flavorful with the right amount of heat. I really enjoyed Hattie B's and can't wait to go back.

Oh my goodness gracious the food is good. This is a true mom and pop, he does the meals, she does the baking. We both had lasagna I had traditional my husband had the chicken, we couldn't get over how good it was, and then there's the dessert - key lime pie just like grandma's and I had carrot cake -really special. They also do takeout-we'll be back to stock up!
So great to see Maynard's open again. Elevated and delicious new menu. We came in late in the evening and Tony and the team took great care of us. Definitely come visit.

Great place. You gotta try it!!!

Oysters are the Best....
Every thing is Great.
Great Happy Hour...

I went here with the kids for a birthday party on a Saturday afternoon.
First, it's great to have a bowling alley on the westbank.
Second, the service was good and the staff was friendly.
The kids said the pizza was good.
All-in-all it was pleasant and very family-friendly.

The place to go for hoagies and cheesesteaks.  We've had Italian and tuna hoagies, chicken cheesesteaks as well as beef cheesesteaks. Always consistent with their quality and taste. I grew up in DelCo and this place is the real deal. Don't get confused by that other place with a similar name!!!

This place was a wonderful surprise. I moved to St. Pete, but would still make the drive for their delicious Thai! I had chicken panang and egg rolls and it was absolutely amazing. Can't wait to try more!

15 microbrew taps, order food, pretty nice little bar but the Wi-Fi is so so slow slow slow. I love whole foods and have been to most of them in the western United States, it's a good bar but not a good value---come on, growlers $20 to $40????
The braised pork bowl came with a pretty pitiful amount of pork but it did taste pretty good. Had a taiwan beer for $3.50 which is pretty cool.

Had a late lunch here on Saturday, we ordered the fried tofu, fried bacon, beef satay, Szechuan chicken.

The fried tofu is rolled in Panko, and then fried. My family ate it, but I could handle the texture, and I in general like friend tofu. The outside was crunchy but the inside was squishy and flavorless. 

The fried bacon, isn't bacon at all...it's pork belly. I was hoping for salty tasty goodness fried but got something different. Possibly my fault I shouldn't have expected bacon in an Asian restaurant. 

Beef Satay...once again I was expecting those happy little skewers BBQ'd and then dipped in an accompanying sauce. What came out was a dish that had been stir fried in only was I could surmise as a mound of ground cumin. It smelled so bad that I couldn't eat it. When my partner tasted it he said "it tastes better than it smells but that's not saying much."

The Szechuan chicken though? THAT WAS FREAKING AWESOME!!!!!!!! super tasty, loved ever morsel. We ate it all! It wasn't to spicy so it lacked flavor, in fact the opposite was true. I'd get this from there again any day!

Sweet Potato pudding was good. I enjoyed the taste and texture.

My experience at Divvy was okay.  First, I'll lay out the facts.  Our reservation was for a large group (fourteen people) on a Saturday night at 7:20 pm. The restaurant was busy, but we were seated prompted (which I DO appreciate, especially when there is a large group because that can be difficult on a busy night even if you have a reservation). Our server was very nice, and she explained how ordering typically works; small plates...everyone shares...there are typically four rounds of ordering...start from the front of the menu and work towards the back.  That was fine but it's difficult to coordinate that amount of organization with a group of fourteen. Nevertheless, we tried just the same. The food was good, but I felt (and I sensed other in the group as well) rushed to get it on my plate and pass it around to the next person as quickly as possible because there was so much coming out of the kitchen at once.  I can't say if this was because we were ordering and passing it around like the server told us to for sure, but I think that was probably the reason.  Had we been able to order for smaller table sections (groups of four or five - having discussed what that set of particular people wanted) I think it would have been less pressure to pass so quickly and we could have just enjoyed the four courses of small plates within smaller groups of our large groups. 

Anyway, the decor and setting is very modern. It's a pretty hip place. It lacks acoustics and it was pretty noisy. I struggled to hear what the person across and two seats down was saying.  After an hour or so, I stopped trying to engage in conversation because I was getting tired of talking over the crowd.  

So, all in all, it was okay. I will go back.  I may have just had an off night.  I may have just been because our group was so large.  The food was good, and there are items on the menu that I want to try next time. 

I do recommend the bacon wrapped apricots, beer cheese fondue, olive tapenade, and calamari. The coffee and beignets were enjoyable after dinner as well.

I usually get take out. Service is fast and friendly. The wings are often on the small side, and overcooked for my taste.  I thought the prices were better than most till I had to pay extra to get blue cheese and celery.  Many sauces to choose from all flavorful.  They do hot chicken breast, boneless wings, chicken tenders, and popcorn chicken, but I have not  tried them yet.

Amazing and affordable! Loved this place. Food choices  on the menu were excellent. Try the West Side Shrimp! We had the special of the day which were sea scallops in a pea purée. Heaven! Free valet (what?!) and staff was so friendly and accommodating. Away from the hustle and bustle of Nashville. Can't say enough good things about this place.
Ravioli was delicious. Excellent cocktails and wine. And our waiter Rodney was wonderful :)

My wife and I stumbled on this location a long time ago. After six years of driving by (because the one in our hometown back east was terrible) we finally tried it out. I'd say we have a dozen visits in, thus far.

We're usually here around 4:30-5:00 for early supper. Most of the time Susie is here. She's great. She gets our order perfect every time and visits the table often. Drinks are topped and all requests are met, immediately.

I can't rave about ihop food. But they do a pretty decent cheeseburger and fries. The special I like to get has the burger and two good sized flap Jacks. I don't know how Chicken and waffles started, but I suggest chicken strips and flapjacks, and I suggest trying them here 09/21
Walked in never being there before. Ordered the jambalaya extra spicy and could not believe how good it was I mean, seriously amazing!

QUIZZO QUIZZO QUIZZO!  We have a great time here playing quizzo with friends.  The happy hour prices are really good for beer and $.50 wings are sadly now the norm... but still a good price.  The teriyaki flavor is our favorite very sweet and savory.  The beer selection is very crafty, just check the big chalk board and get your selection at a decent price.

I like to eat here for the nice environment and setting, and the food is pretty good too. Its a big pricey but you pay for eating on the water and the bands, which are normally decent. You do get plenty of food. Service a bit slow but you should never be in a hurry when you are going to a place like this. The salads are huge and fresh and they have a lot of really good appetizers.
I love this place! I would go here everyday after work. Fast and on point. The employees here always jave a smile on. Thank you

These are found every 6 feet all over New Orleans. I've yet to try the fried chicken, but I did sample some "Cajun tenders" I'm not sure why they are called Cajun, they are GOOD- above average as far as chicken tenders are concerned, but when I hear Cajun I think spice/heat/southern seasoning galore., Nope, but they are crispy decent sized, well cooked and tender so it at least lives up to half its name. The shrimp and Cajun fish platter were also good, but again not very "Cajun" in my non creole non Cajun opinion. Crunchy, crispy, golden, and delicious?? Yes! Cajun??? Well you be the judge cause I don't get it. Their signature Cock-tail is no joke!!! Everclear? In a frozen drink? Sure!!! It's probably the only frozen drink in NOLA boozy enough to be worth an 11$ price tag. You won't have to look fat if you want to check it out.
Pizza and breadsticks were fantastic. Place seems a bit sketchy being next to a gas station, but it has more of a "college town hole in the wall" vibe. Nice people too. Will definitely go back.
They forgot my mobile order, the fries were half filled, and the employees  were rude. Go down the street to the other Chick-fil-a.

After driving by this place nearly everyday, I finally tried it.  Fantastic flavor in both the falafel and lamb combo plates. Veggies are fresh and the meat is cooked perfectly. Vegetatian and vegan friendly. Definitely will be back!

Got off work, took the puppy to the Vet and wife and I didn't feel like making anything. So we head to BJ's which is close to where we live, and easy to get to Summit mall. Ever since moving back here 12 years ago, and I haven't reviewed them yet.... What is wrong with me. They are usually constant and the beer they make always taste great. They are a corporate place, but usually stick to bringing out new items (Hello Wheat Soba Noodles with Ahi Poki). 

The beer we got introduced to some local brothers that used to be their brew makers. They took us back to see the production, and took the time to show us the process. Back then we were new to beer coming from Bay Area and learning about Wine. Glad we got to do this as it always makes going there great to bump into the brew masters and shoot the turds (keeping it PG) with the guys. As for the beer they have something for everyone on tap, but the Nutty Burnett is my go to. Nice brown beer with a little extra hops.

When it comes to the food, it has usually been very good. Ya we go a lot so we usually get something wrong, but the wait staff or bartenders are usually super friendly and always help us out. I think when you go to BJ's you know it will be busy, and for years it has been this way, but you will always get something you like on their large menu of items.

You kidding me? Had me at the first sight of food. Was looking for New Orleans style food, and found this gem.
Wow, just wow. Tried the Rica, and boy was it Rico! Cool vibe, and view. Just real cool, chill and laid back. The food being good doesn't hurt.
My favorite sandwich place of ALL TIME. I go once a week at least. Miss Jessie and Jim Rome are my personal faves on Dutch crunch of course

Great seafood and atmosphere. I like most of their food the bang bang shrimp is my favorite. I thought the sushi was just okay. The inside is nice with tables and a very large bar. The inside bar has lots of tvs. It open up to a great view of the lake. There are also tables outside!

This place has been a family favorite for almost 30 years. My grandfather was a regular here so I felt like we needed to pay tribute when we visited PA. The food is good and the staff are all so friendly. The place could use some upgrades but that's also part of it's charm

I came here by a suggestion of a friend and was deadset on going after seeing such rave reviews on here. I don't believe it's lived up to its name. 
One major plus: it's halal for all the Muslim folks- YAY! Walking in we were seated immediately and the decor was modern and the restaurant was tidy. The potted plants on the wall with rustic dining tables and chairs gave a very unique garden feel to it. 

Looking at the menu, I had seen rave reviews about their doner kabob. We arrived at 4 pm with the place empty besides my cousin and me.

We tried to order the doner and the Adana kabob and the waitress had told us that both of these meats were not prepared yet. I was shocked, their best sellers not prepared on a Friday? We settled for the chicken shish that was tender and juicy throughout but had little to no flavor. The dish came with a small side of chopped salad (cucumbers, tomatoes, onions), yogurt sauce, a tortilla (since when do Mediterraneans eat with a tortilla?), and probably half a cup of rice. The yogurt sauce was what really gave the meal any flavor since things were quite bland. The salad was nice and refreshing to balance out the protein and carbs but nothing groundbreaking. We also ordered a side of french fries which was the only thing that went well food-wise that evening. The fact that french fries were the only thing that worked out for us, was a little disappointing.

I also had asked for garlic sauce on the side (i have never gone to a Mediterranean/Arab restaurant that doesn't offer it) and the waitress looked confused and said she had never heard of that. she asked the manager and said the yogurt sauce was all they had. Everything was priced reasonable but it just didn't seem to be our day.

Leaving 3 stars bc the waitstaff was courteous, the atmosphere was well decorated and inviting, and everything was decently priced. I wish their popular dishes were available so I could see what the hype was about. 

since everything was relatively underwhelming, I most likely will not be coming back again.
Eh, it was ok. Most of their arcade games were racing of some sort. Not a ton of choices in my opinion. Not the worst place either. A fine spot to keep the kids busy for an hour or two.

When I heard that we were getting a sushi restaurant that wasn't AYCE, my first response was GREAT! Finally, I don't have to pay high prices for a la carte, and I don't have to "get my money's worth" by making myself have a stomach ache. And with all these great reviews, I knew I had to give it a try!

My first impression was about location, it's a little bit confusing as far as where to park, but once you find it, it's a comfortable parking lot out back. It's also a smaller restaurant, which isn't a negative but I can imagine it getting pretty cozy at peak hours. 

From the moment I walked in, the staff was so friendly and welcoming and helpful. As it was my first time, they explained how the menu worked. One thing that I loved is that, as someone who doesn't really eat desserts, I was able to double-up on appetizers instead of getting dessert at the end. I LOVE THIS! So I went with mussels and calamari. The calamari was pretty standard but YOU HAVE TO TRY THE MUSSELS! Nothing like any mussels you'll get in town. I got mine baked, not sure what the fried option is like but...so so good. 

I also went with the 2 roll combo, opting for 8 pieces of nigiri and one "Sunrise roll". Both were very fresh and tasty with beautiful presentation. 

Everything here was incredible and I guarantee this will be one of my new hangouts. 5/5 food, 5/5 service, 5/5 ambiance. Just a great business to have new to us in Reno!

The first thing I think about when I hear about The Pint is WINGS! 
There is a great selection of different wings on the menu and it is hard to make just one choice! The happy hour is certainly a joyous time with really good beer specials.

A couple things to note though however is that from 4-6 it gets busy and you have to go quite early on Wednesday's to find a table. It also starts to turn into a "club" after a certain hour so if you're not into that sort of thing you might want to leave when you see the staff start to move tables and chairs to make a small dance floor.

This place was amazing.  Super hipster vibe in the middle of Boise.  They had a very friendly staff and everything just felt easy.  The rooms are small but super comfortable.  The only downside was that with such a small amount of real estate, peace and quite is hard to come by.  I highly recommend the the sazerak at the bar.  Super tasty.
Best Italian beef I have ever had out side of Chicago! The thin crust pizza is outstanding as well.  This place is the real deal when it comes to Chicago food.

Just had this delivered and was pleasantly surprised!! I assumed the ramen and spicy tuna roll would just be chain quality kind of good but there was some real spice and flavor! The spicy green beans, kids honey chicken, and lettuce wraps were all great as well and good portion for cost. I should've given this place a chance sooner!

i love visiting fellini's with friends!
it's loud, crowded, but ever so delicious! often times other parties are seated at your table, creating a very cozy, intimate space. the staff are as accommodating as possible--they once sat our party of 20 within 15 minutes!

the food is always fantastic--i've never had anything i didn't like. i especially enjoy their pasta dishes with mussels. fellini's is definitely a main line favorite and have yet to see someone leave the restaurant not smiling!

Went here with my family the Saturday before Fathers Day. Service was horrendous from the jump, from the hostess who wouldn't have cared if we stayed or left to the waiter who was overly agitated for no reason. The waiter was annoyed that my father had basic questions about what was in an entree and if he could have cucumber in his water. He actually raised his voice and spoke sternly.  We should've left then. We did not and we paid the price: average food, a rude and inattentive waiter, and a mandatory 18% tip for our party of 5. I love supporting and believe in supporting black business, but I will never be back to this establishment. It's a shame because Turae's comedy show is nice and he supplies excellent customer service.

We ordered delivery from here for the first time tonight.  

The service was quick and friendly.  Food was GREAT! 

I ordered the fettuccine that was homemade pasta, so tender and light, not a heavy dish.  The serving size was huge!  I couldn't even finish it all.

The service was horrible this chick Shelisha has the worst attitude, she is nasty and she should not be working in the food industry. 
The food is nasty and favor less, it's like they fry the chickens with no season and then put salt less sauce on it when it's done. Fries are cooked in old grease.  Just close and start over with a new staff and Lawry seasoning!!

As much as I would like to give this place 5 stars they just fell short on my most recent visit. I have been to this brewery a handful of times and it has always been good. The beer selection is great, the food is delicious, my issue comes to the service. Most recently made a 2 hour call ahead reservation for a group of 18 (they don't take regular reservations). When we arrived we were seated in 2 different sections, only 1 section was given menus, and by the time we all ordered our food and it started coming out an hour and a half had passed. To bring out dinner orders for 18 people it was left on one server. This woman did her best to get everyone their food as quickly as she could but she was one person serving 18 and only coming out with one plate at a time. I really feel like management should of stepped up and had more staff assist with our party or given us a heads up that they really couldn't handle such a large party. Either way I will still be going back but no more groups larger than 4 for me.

Thank you, House. Thank you for being a bright light in my day of torture (i.e. jury duty). I needed to pick up a quick lunch during my short jury duty break and House completely came through. The place is simply and beautifully decorated. The host was very friendly and helpful. He reassured me that my food would come out quickly...and that I would still make it back in time for court (I guess the red button gave it away). I decided to go with the King Kahn panini and it was absolutely delicious. I am definitely going back and hopefully this time I can enjoy my food at a slightly slower pace.

Great venue for watching the featured game on the many screens.  Great beer selection.  Not good for conversation or for hearing the game - way too loud.  Food is mediocre.  I had the crabcake platter and the crab cakes were completely devoid of flavor.  Fries are marginal.  I have had a very good burger on a previous visit.  Service is pretty absent once they take your order and deliver your food.  You see them standing around talking to themselves a lot

This place does have some good stuff and a cool ambiance but it has some issues. The food was pretty good, but the pork loin was overcooked and overpriced and the tres leches cake was a bit grainy. The service was not great. Went to the hostess stand and stood around, while all of the employees avoided eye contact. Service for the rest of the night wasn't great. Waited for the check, while all of  waiters and waitresses were chatting behind the hostess stand during a peak of business.
If I went back, it would be for the Sangria pitchers.
Stopped here after seeing the small place driving to work, it turned out being a hidden gem !!
Reds is the place to go!! Especially if you have Ceci for a bartender!! She is amazing and always has a smile! Come to reds and ask for Ceci!
Good size smoke free party room in the back. Waitress serving our private party was awesome! Bar is smokey (yuk!) and place is kinda falling apart everywhere.

The noise level is anything but average. We are a party of four, VERY hard to hear each other and the waiter description.  Looking forward to seeing how the food is. Btw the on line menu does not align with the current menu. No T Bone. No 24 oz bone in rib eye. Both reason we selected here.

I love love love the tuna kimbap! I find the kimbap here taste better than other place because they use high quality ingredients. Their pickled radishs are very crunchy, and everything else is fresh. That quality for $7. You can't beat that. I also tried beef bulgogi and chapchae nooodles. I'd say good price, good portion (and of course good flavor!). The owners were very nice and polite. I highly recommend.
Best Mediterranean food in Philly. Loved the wine selection. Amazing for meat-lovers and good for vegetarians too! Can't wait to go back....

We ordered pizza for delivery, it was amazing! It was a Saturday night so we expected a wait, but it was delivered on time and so fresh. Tonight I'm trying some of their baked dishes. I'm so glad we decided to try it. My honey is a chef and relatively hard to please so thumbs up all the way around!
Stopped by here the other day for $2 dollar yuengling on saturdays  and hot wings.. pretty decent place for cold beer and some hot wings..

Service was horrible had trouble getting check and having it rung up. Seems the Manager on duty, bartender, and 2 waitresses one being ours was more interested in play cards then the customers. Some of the wings were undercooked as well.

I walked into five guys around 9:55, right before they were about to close (10:00). I expected a simple order and go. However, when I placed my order I could not help but notice how friendly the staff was. Usually when a store is about to close you get a feeling of the staff being tired and just ready to go home. However, that clearly was not the case. I felt welcomed and had a genuinely nice time there. Their burgers are fantastic, their milkshakes are mouthwatering, and their fries are simply amazing. 

Thank you five guys, your food is delectable and you truly know how to value a customer.

First, I want to respond to some of the other comments made about the poor customer service. I went tonight, and either I lucked out or they had a change of staff, because our waiter (Four Eyes) was quite pleasant and attentive! He even hustled back out of the kitchen to make sure he wished us a good night at the end of the meal! 

Now for the food--the thing to get here is definitely the glazed tofu with the pistachio cream sauce....to DIE for. As another reviewer pointed out, that dish alone is worth it. For the entrees...my friend's pad thai was terrible, but my phyllo dough stuffed with mushrooms was okay. I think the entrees are lackluster, but the appetizers will definitely make me want to come back.

Reasonable prices for some seriously delicious food. Friendly staff. Had some new flavor combinations I had never had before in the Dan Dan noodles and chili oil dumplings. Visiting from west coast and was really impressed.
Amazing! Food was excellent, very nice restaurant with a family vibe to it. I highly recommend eating here for top of the line steaks, service, and other menu items.

This place is amazing!!!!!!! I'm so happy they have a new place on Davis island that came up to every expectation, staff is amazing food was incredible can't wait to be back tomorrow? Thanks Dean for being so awesome!

A bit off the beaten path for most tourists, as it is in the Marigny, but worth the trip. Sure, the place is not perfect, but there are ultra-expensive restaurants in the FQ that are also not perfect. Look, cheap food, especially food this good, gives "wiggle" room for imperfections.

Breakfast served all day is a bonus. Sometimes you just got to have a lox omelet (under $10) late in the day. The restaurant boasts vegetarian and *gasp* vegan dishes, but someone needs to tell them that cheese doesn't fit into either of those categories. That aside, the french fry poboy, and the mac 'n cheese sandwiches are amazing. So is the Saturday Blue Plate of BBQ Chicken legs. 

Every entree is under $10, well except for the Friday Blue Plate, but why quibble? And who can argue with $5 Bloody Mary's, especially ones that are this good?

This will not be a place that I will ever return to. The service was incredibly bad. There were three other tables with people and the rest of the place was deserted - for a good reason I was soon to find out.  My glass of water had black floaties and I had to finally get up and go to the waiter (who was playing on her phone) and ask for a replacement. When the food finally came it was cold. Not one of those places that say "be careful, these plates are very hot".  Mediocer food, very bad service, and questionable cleanliness.

This is a great option for Asian cuisine for the Longley area. They have a lot of Vegan options including the avocado spring roll, and the vegetable chow mein. They have a little bit of everything so whatever you are in the mood for they have something. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, and I like how they updated the interior of the building.
