My friend and I went out on a search for cupcakes near Broad street and found this gem!
You might miss it if you aren't looking! 
They had a nice selection and we chose chocolate peanut butter and pumpkin chocolate chip.
They were divine and we are cupcake snobs! 

The cupcake was a little dense, which is great because it doesn't fall apart when you bite it! The icing was rich and thick and perfect.
I cannot say enough, you have to go here!
Chiliquiles were great! Enchiladas were excellent! They even made machaca for us, that wasn't on the menu.

I had a wonderful experience at The Egg & I and it was all because of our server Dee Dee. I was seated at the table and while waiting for a friend, she talked about the menu since I had never been there before and talked about the cleanliness of the restaurant FOH and BOH and the freshness of the food. Being there 3 years and also having a long restaurant past, she said she loved working there and has tried everything. I asked about the seasonal juice and she quickly not only told me about it but offered a sample. Once my friend arrived and we ordered, she had a great amount of "table touches" and was spot on with approaching often enough without it being too often or disruptive. The food was fantastic and fresh, and it was a great experience.

This was my fist time here and I loved it. I am from Texas and in this area working, walking down the road I saw a gentleman enjoying his smoke and asked about this place, turns out hotsauce worked there and recommended it. The service was great and the food even better. I will eat at this place every trip I take to this area!

Great place for breakfast and lunch! Great prices too. The food is fresh and made daily. I love the servers, they are all sweet and provide great service.

Favorites include:
Omelettes- huge and always have fresh ingredients 
Chocolate banana nut French toast (crazy good)
Mexican mess
Chicken salad (made with chunks of chicken breast) 
The coffee is good too! 

Solid spot, you will not be disappointed!

Both Geno's and Pat's are tasty, but I preferred Pat's more--I tried them back-to-back. I won't go into detail, as you'll have to choose your own alliance. Choose wisely and draw your cheesy steak line in the sand.

Visited this spot during my weekend stay in Nashville. Great place. We loved the food, atmosphere and staff. I ordered the French toast and it was delicious. The coffee was definitely one of the best we had all weekend. It was pretty busy (30 min wait) but definitely worth it. Truly recommend!!

This place totally hit the spot today. I wandered in really craving some Chinese broccoli in a garlic sauce and made it perfectly. I left totally stuffed. The service was super friendly, the place was clean, and the food was good and reasonably priced. They had a lot of good vegetarian options on their menu, but if I ate duck, I'd eat it there. The skin looked perfect and crispy. 

I would eat here again!

Dine here often and always take out of town guests here. Dined there last night. 

Got there just in time for early bird specials. I had a salad and  grilled Chicken Breast with pineapple salsa and grilled pineapple slice, wasabi potatoes. The chicken was rather drab but the salsa and pineapple helped. Hubby had the Sweet and Sour Fried Pork and a salad. His dish was very good. 
Our entree was served a little quick. I took last bite of salad as server took my salad plate away!  Our server had told us earlier that bread would be out of oven soon and she would bring right away. We had completed our salads when bread was brought and it was barely warm? 

As I said we eat here often, and love their desserts as well as their food but feel with EB either no dessert or just a sliver of something you serve on your menu. 
The tiny cherry cobbler with a mini scoop of ice cream was not very tasty. 
You have fab desserts. Give a little taste, then they may order more!  Just sayin' ! 

Do love the atmosphere and the food.  Outdoor seating is great. 

Worth the $$.

A usual stop for me and my family when at RTM. Consistently delicious and fast service. We have steam many times at the restaurant in China town, but stop at this location often for orders to take home. 

The Peking duck, pork wontons, duck wonton soup, and roast pork and bok choy are favorites.

If we're running through really quick, we'll usually grab a Peking duck roll or a spring roll! I would also recommend these if you are "eating your way" through RTM.

I come for the food when I work nearby, everything I have tried has been really good!  
Definitely a place to try, they also have a great coffee, wine, large deli and other European grocery items.

Incredibly fresh, flavorful, authentic, and delicious Mexican food. The Queso Fondido was dense, melty, cheesy goodness. The fresh made chips were thin, light and crispy. The enchiladas verde was amazing! The pickled onion and radish make are a great compliment. The beans were full of flavor. And even the iced tea was dark and dense. Service was excellent. The entire place is ultra clean and pleasant. While the price is a little on the high side for Mexican food, it is totally worth it. This is high quality cuisine, not gut filler food. Go and try it. You will love it.

Chinese food tends to be hit or miss for me, all too often you'll ask for extra spicy and the food comes out bland.  Enter Jay's - Most Excellent Cafe.  I sometimes go into my office on a Saturday and thanks to GrubHub - I have ordered delivery from Jay's roughly five or six times.  The food has always been completely to my liking.  spicy, crispy, yummy, flavorful in every way.  As a 20 year vegetarian I appreciate the meat free choices.  I've had spring rolls, fried veg dumplings, the Chinese pizza and General Tso's Tofu - extra, extra, extra  spicy.  Everything was cooked to perfection and delivered piping hot.   I would recommend Jay's to anyone who loves delicious Chinese food and is in the Cherry Hill area.  (Get the Chinese scallion Pizza.....get two!)

My husband and I are from out of town and we stumbled upon Brunchies.  We eat breakfast at Brunchies every time we come to town now. The menu is a great mix of traditional breakfast and gourmet options for picky eaters.  Michael is our favorite waiter.  Spot on.  And, here's the best part...the outside tables out back are always open!  It's shaded and comfortable but no one goes out there.  Skip the line and request outside!  Highly recommend.

After a long annoying day, I went to Good Dog hoping the mac & cheese and the blueberry cornbread would be as yummy as they were the last time I was in town. They were! The mac wasn't overly cheesy, and the cornbread was the right combination of soft/crunchy and sweet/savory. It was the perfect meal on a cold blustery night. 

The waitress didn't charge me for my drink, and when I pointed it out, she said she'd done it on purpose - I must have looked like I could use it. (I added the value to her tip.)

I'm not in Philly often, but Good Dog is staying in the rotation when I'm here.

We're here on vacation and came to Grand Hacienda for lunch. 
The food was really good and you get such a big portion. I'll be having leftovers for dinner. 
The cheese dip was on point

I live right by Union so it's a great place to grab a drink with the girls or run over to for whiskey Wednesday. The patio is beautiful, decor is nice, bar is spacious, but I've never had awesome service... going to a place like Union and not having upbeat, knowledgable service is a let down.

Our scooter club used this place for our Meet & Greet for a recent event. Jay was very accommodating.  He has worked in the Tucson pizza biz for many years and really knows his pies.  The pizza is very good and prices are amazing. I've been there twice already and I'm looking for an opportunity to go back.

June 1, 2018 Friday - 5:15 PM for dinner
1 adults

Atmosphere - 5 stars
Food - 5 stars
Service - 5 stars

Background - Time for a beer and a bite.

Atmosphere - Classic sports bar with an actual dining area.  

Food
  Drinks - Lots of beer taps that is what I am looking for in a bar.  

  Dinner - Two tri tip sliders for $6, a steal.  I had the greens with balsamic reduction and goat cheese on my tri tip sliders.  Okay this is classic Nevada dish, and for $6 it is a steal.  I probably could have ordered another two sliders they were that good.

Service - My bar tender was great.  No rush here, enjoyed watching the games on TV.

Future - Yes and I see a future Beer Club event.

Admittedly, I've only had their pizza, wings, and chicken fingers, but everything I've tried has been consistent. The wings are crispy and delicious. They give you buffalo sauce on the side, so by time you pick them up, the wings are still crispy. Nothing is bad, but it's not in my top 10. The customer service is hit or miss. There have been times when I've walked in and stood at the counter being ignored because of the "not my job" mentality. There were at least 5 people working behind the counter, but not a single one acknowledged me until a girl came to the register all the way from the bar. The place is alright, and they always seem to have good weekday specials.

Live band and beer selection were the best part about this place, the rest, not so good.
The food left A LOT to be desired.  The fried green tomatoes were buried in so much cheese, that's all you could taste.  Scraping the cheese off made them slightly better.  My wife had the Griot with Ti Malice & Pikliz, fancy name for pork with a whole lot of fat attached to it.  If it was indeed fried, they only fried one side because the other side had a thick layer of fat attached to it.  The only decent part of this dish were the plantains.  I had the hot chicken sandwich and although it was a huge portion, it was over fried.  Now I do like spicy but this was way too spicy to the point you could not even taste the chicken.  Hotter doesn't mean better.  The fries that came with the sandwich were literally soaked in oil.  Limp fries sitting in a puddle of oil.......not good.  Don't think we'll be coming for dinner at Acme again.

This place is disgusting and the service is terrible. I'm sure there all nice people, however they clearly don't care about there employment. To serve cold food.. offer no napkins and eating utensils is unbelievable. You walk past the kitchen and some are in their phones or EATING FOOD. I won't bother with anymore comments because this establishment should be shut down
Terrible! They forgot our extra cheese sauce, gave us blue cheese instead of the ranch we ordered for wings, and the pizza was cold, greasy and tossed all over the box.

Visited today for the first time with a friend, and absolutely loved It! They are BYOB so we brought a bottle of champagne and ordered a carafe of orange juice to make mimosas, the ONLY complaint I have is the carafe of OJ was $9 which seemed a little pricey to me but it's no biggie and I would definitely do It again! We ordered the breakfast poutine and the seared tuna avocado eggs Benedict which were both SOO good. I'll probably still be thinking about how good the breakfast poutine was for atleast a week, lol. But overall our experience was really great, our server was super sweet and the food came out really fast and was amazing! I can't wait to go back!

This is my 4th time to Zemam's and this restaurant NEVER disappoints.  Food is always spot on.  Service is always patient, informative and very friendly.  I went with a small group of friends.  We ordered sampler platter of meats and vegetable dishes.  So good.  I would eat here every day if I could.  We ordered #4,5,7,11,12,16.  This was a variety of spicy and bland dishes.  Those listed spicy do have a kick if you are sensitive.  

Feels like home cooking.  We brought our own wine to drink, which was welcomed.  

I CERTAINLY recommend Zemam's for a great dinner.  I will visit again.

Was lucky to grab a last minute reservation on NYE with my girlfriend at Lou Bird's. I had heard great things and was excited to try this place, however I don't know what was going on that night but our experience was just not good. 

We had an early reservation and the restaurant was not that crowded, however it took a couple minutes to be seated and about 10 minutes before we were even provided waters. The wait staff was super friendly, but seemed very busy and unprepared for the NYE rush.

My girlfriend's cocktail was solid and our arugula salad was a good started. I went with the chicken pot pie through recommendations on yelp, which was good, no complaints there. However. My girlfriend ordered a BYO burger without cheese and pickles. It came out with cheese on top and they had run out of pickles already that early in the night. Also the fries had potential but were undercooked. 

Again, the staff was super helpful and friendly, but something was off that night and I'd like to believe on another night our experience would have been better.

There are plenty of other restaurants in the area I will be trying before heading back to Lou Bird's.

My mom's favorite place.. and it really does deserve the buzz it gets.  Everything is fresh and so many items you can't get anywhere else in Pinellas.  Their deli sandwiches are some of my favorites.  It can get just a little tiny but crowded.  Anyone who has been here gets that joke!  If you're in need of a quick in and out, this is not the spot for you.

We normally like this place but with few issues, I don't think me and my family are ever going to dine here again. First of all, there is no website, the one you click goes to the Hillsborough address which is a different management and thus, its so difficult the reach the manager with a complaint. For our recent visit on Feb 13th, we did a carry out of 2 dishes for dinner, one chicken with basil and another chicken with lemon grass,bell peppers. Though very good in taste initially, but as night progressed our stomach started to churn and eventually me, my wife and my daughter all had food poisoning the next day. We normally don't eat out a lot and it was the only dinner we had outside our home cooked meals that week. Thus, I am 100% sure its from what we ate here, plus all three having food poisoning same time, is not coincidence. I called them to speak to the manager or if he/she has an email ID because for sure they don't have a website. The only other way to convey was to write a review here. Previously we found a metal nose ring kind of stuff in our fried rice, though disgusted we kept eating for the taste but not anymore. Bye Bye Pho Quyen, Fowler location, Tampa.
This is one of my favorite spots for brunch. Their food and drinks are delicious. And the server Emily is sweet and super attentive. You have to come here!

NO WORDS - just perfect - GO

Our family had:
Brisket platter
Pulled chicken sandwich 
Pulled pork sandwich 

Brisket Fried ravioli (not the best)

Be prepared to sit with strangers- make new friends!

My friend and I were here last night and enjoyed the experience. The main dish prices were pretty decent for being next to the pier w the view. Really loved the clam chowder that came with my new york steak. However, I wasnt sure how my lemonade pricing was $4.50.....  wasnt on the menu and I wished I knew the price before I got it too. Other than that, service was friendly and great; pretty loud environment but it was enjoyable!

We have eaten at this restaurant in Philly China Town several times. The food has always been excellent. They offer a wide range of Chinese dishes, from the familiar to the unique. This is not a fancy ambiance place and service is not the anything special, but the food is very good.

Same story--boyfriend is vegetarian and I'm not. Here we are visiting New Orleans where there are so many great food choices and we need a place that we will both enjoy. This is the place. Great menu choices, service was awesome, nice location and the food is great. We started with chili cheese fries. My boyfriend got the special which was a seitan and mushroom po boy. I had gumbo. All were awesome! Def put on your list of restaurants to visit while in New Orleans.

What a great place. Went in with a big group got in without a problem. Staff was super nice and inviting. Food was great beer was great. We'll be going back again next time in reno! Have to get the lava bowl!

Highly recommend--what a treat for a special meal. Nice noise level, allowing for conversation, lovely art/decor (love those acorn cap lamps), tv in bar & in private party space upstairs. Robert = waiter was very attentive and enthusiastic with advice. We tried a little of everything, except the salads...cocktails, raw bar (yum, especially the roasted Rockefeller style), crispy pork belly on delish sweet potato hash, sides of glazed carrots/Brussel sprouts/mushrooms, red wine, NY strip with bleu cheese topper, short rib, pear cheese"cake"(more like cheese pie)/ chocolate cake, cappuccino/espresso. Hours of fun. So full! Richly decadent. Crispy edged, deep & meaty flavors. Bathrooms have hipster flair with asymmetric wood framed mirror, loooong white sink, cement tiling interspersed with mercury-glass-like mirrors, very sleek & gender neutral. Comfy seating up front at either the bar or the luxe couches. Tip: valet park at Westin next door for four hours of free parking!

We have tried MANY items on the menu but when we found the Zacatecas burrito we were overjoyed!  It really is enough for two meals, even for my husband.  The red menudo on the weekends is fantastic as well.  Best of all the staff is so very friendly and accommodating. Great find!

Love this place.  Take the kids all the time.  We can always get right in and they have something for everyone.  From hard core sushi lovers like me, to chicken nuggets and fries for my daughter.  The prices are very reasonable, but I often feel compelled to over eat because of the big selection.  If you go for lunch, schedule a later afternoon nap into your calendar.

Very good food and a clean and modern decor.  I had the mole poblano chicken, which is usually my go-to to test how good a Mexican restaurant is and it was very delicious. The menu is very affordable. Around probably $10 per person. I highly recommend this for Mexican food in the Fenton area.

Two visits now, and you all are very pleasant- the staff shines.  Our breakfast and lunch items are all as expected - will be back for hopefully many more dines.   The place is small, clean and well run.  Good Job- and see you very soon!

I've been here a few times. I've always enjoyed this place, the food, the drinks, and people who work here are really friendly and nice. My husband is a big fan of this place. Last time we were here we ordered chicken pesto panini. Oh it was lot of love in that panini...it was sooo good. I know what I'm ordering next time at Old Chicago.

I would have given this place half a star but that is not an option. We waited for much longer than quoted for a seat. No big deals this happens, but then when we were seated it took 15 minutes more for a menu and that was after I flagged down someone. Then, we waited an HOUR (no lie or exaggeration) for our food to arrive only to be all wrong. So, I asked to speak to the manager because I was starving and the meal was wrong. He promised to fix the situation and get me something to eat ASAP. Well, I didn't see him again for 10 minutes AND no bread was sent over. When my meal did finally arrive it was subpar at best. I've eaten all over the French Quarter and I've never had this experince before. Especially from a place as crowded or as popular as this plac is supposed to be!

This place is complete bullshit. I can tell from the reviews that out of town people think they are getting some "real" New Orleans experience or something by going here. What a waste of money this place is.  Went there this morning with friends and ordered 4 mochas. The mochas tasted like they were made with hot water, a splash of coffee, and some cocoa sprinkled on top. After complaining about the lack of coffee in them (they really should have been made with espresso, but whatever) they told us that is pretty much exactly how they were made. Then the OWNER told that if we didn't like it then we didn't have to come back there. Rudest woman I have encountered in this city so far.  In fact, all the women behind the counter were extremely rude.
We love them. We live around the corner so it's convenient and the fish & chips and shepherds pie are fantastic!

I visited Rudie's on a recent girl's trip to Nashville. The food was fresh and delicious and had a little edge to it! I got the lobster roll and was not let down. Drinks were great, service was quick and friendly, and all around inviting atmosphere. Fun place to dine for a group!

Good restaurant in the heart of Lambertville. The white bean dip served with the bread is excellent. Entrees and desserts are also good. Service is exceptional during the week but may not be appreciated by first time diners in a rush.

I ordered via Uber eats. I got an estimated delivery time of about 1 hour. The delivery person got to my house about 20 minutes late, which I was not too bothered about. I ordered the Salmon cheese steak which was absolutely delicious! I also ordered chicken wings and waffles. The waffles were a bit soggy at the time of delivery but they were still good. The wings were ok. So overall I give the experience 3 starts. I would give them a try again. Hopefully next time I can give 5 starts. I took off 2 starts because of the soggy waffles, the just ok wings and the delivery time. I really liked the Salmon cheese steak, though.

If coming here for the steaks alone, you wont be disappointed one bit. This place serves one mean steak. As far as the rest of the food?? it's just ok. I've tried the Spinach cream, Sweet potato casserole, and the bbq shrimp (not so) orleans, among other things I can't quite remember. wonder why?? Just wasn't impressed with any of it. When you consider the amount of cash spent to eat at a fancy restaurant like Ruth's, I guess you expect everything on the menu to match the quality of the steaks. The establishment and the service are top notch, they also make great drinks at the bar. When you put it all together, come for the steaks, the ambiance, and drinks. 3.5 stars.
Love love this little hidden gem.  Food is great and the guys that work there are really nice.  Highly recommend.

I ordered a water, a drip coffee and a cafe egg sandwich. The sandwich was delicious-came on a Philly muffin with a light pesto spread. Wonderful location with a pleasant atmosphere. Food came out to about $7.50.

My mom and I went here on a Sunday night and had a good dinner. The dan dan noodles were delicious-- tasted very nutty and creamy. We also got the wontons in chili oil as an appetizer which was very flavorful, full of garlic and the perfect amount of spice. For our entrees we got the scallion chicken and the spicy garlic chicken. The spicy garlic chicken had a thicker sauce and was much more flavorful than the scallion chicken. 

The service was fine but not overly attentive other than to take our orders and give us our check.  

I'll return for the dan dan noodles and the spicy garlic chicken.
Always kind staff here. Never have a problem with wrong drinks, but I am sure if I did they would gladly replace it. Big fan.
Ordered tamales for a large Mexican party I was throwing...delicious & authentic.  My guests raced about the food.  Could t be happier!!

The pros: 
Lots of tourist cups (been there series) 

The cons: 
1. Can't walk inside and yes I know COVID, but all other Starbucks stores have accommodated and followed regulations in order to have guests inside so why hasn't this one? Especially with how huge it is and it's in prime location. 

2. No connections, no third place environment here you're more of an inconvenience to them. 

And lastly and most importantly, these baristas don't know their recipes...please refrain because at $6 a cup, the drink needs to be right. 

Partner to partner , get it together

The wait for pizza is insane. The quality isn't there either. Not worth it unless you are just really hungry and mediocre food will do. Waited over 30 minutes for a couple of slices of pizza! They get busy and somehow they have 10+ staff members but they can't seem to manage the place properly. Also, get rid of those gross buzzers. No one wants to touch that before eating.

A group of 8 of us dropped in for a late dinner on the Saturday Dec 29th.  The restaurant was not too busy, 3 or 4 tables, and we waited for about 10 minutes to be seated. My husband and I ordered a Veggie Burger (no Mike's sauce) with salad (dressing on the side) and the Bruschetta (no parmesan) to share. The burger came with Mike's sauce, the salad came with dressing, the bruschetta came with parmesan and the ketchup that I asked for at time of serving arrived after we were finished.  When the waitress checked in with us and we indicated the order issues, her response was 'okay' and a blank stare.  No apology or offer to fix the meal. It could have been either a kitchen screw up or waitress error but regardless, it was an unsatisfactory response and we won't be returning.
Ordered a cheesesteak 2 foot long packed with meat and fries delicious the food was perfect

This Yelp entry is confusing.  Franco Luigi's is both a take out/delivery pizza place as well as a sit down restaurant that has live opera.  I am reviewing the take out pizza side.

This place has a very solid cheese pizza.  A nice crust, on the thinner side with a crisp bottom, but not paper thin.  Nice cheese and a flavorful sauce; in general the pie is well spiced so you don't need to drench it in garlic powder.

The standouts for me are:
1) The tomato pie, which is a regular pizza crust, but topped with only their homemade red sauce (like what would come on spaghetti, not the normal pizza sauce) and a sprinkling of grated cheese.  Their sauce is a chunky, garlicky, and full of flavor.  Plus, a large tomato pie will only set you back $4 once you spend $10 (or somewhere around there) on anything else.  You can also get this same pie with some slices of fresh mozzarella (not $4) and that is also delicious.

2) Their meatballs.  These babies and definitely homemade and are so good.  Great texture and flavor on these.  I recommend getting a side of these (2 come in a side, they are slightly smaller than a baseball in size).  The meatballs come with more of that homemade red sauce, which is so good that I can (and have) just eat it plain with a spoon.  I actually never eat ground beef out, but I make an exception for these meatballs.

The other menu items I have tried (cheesesteaks, hoagies, etc.) are all good as well.

I took a trip to Florida to visit my sister for her birthday and she chose this restaurant to celebrate.  

First, I have to say this restaurant is huge.  It covers an entire square block and has lots of different areas/entrances.  Our waiter informed us that it's the oldest restaurant in Florida and the decor reflects a long standing Spanish tradition in the community.

We started with a pitcher of sangria and Croquetas de Pollo (Chicken Croquets).  The sangria was delicious and since there was four of us drinking we needed another pitcher.  The croquets were good as well - sometimes they can be greasy or dry but these were perfect.

For my entree I ordered the "Jesse Gonzales" (Stuffed Shrimp).  It came with yellow rice and a vegetable - we ordered a side of maduros and tostones for the table.  I thoroughly enjoyed my food.  It was delicious - well cooked, well seasoned and beautifully presented.  Others in the group had Grilled Salmon Santa Clara, The Bambino and Roast Pork "a la Cubana".  Everyone enjoyed their entrees and we were stuffed by the time we left.

Columbia is an absolutely beautiful restaurant that I wouldn't mind visiting again.  It's definitely worth it!

My wife & I wanted to take our family out for a nice holiday dinner this past Saturday night. We were a party of  7 incl. our daughter, son-in-law 2 grandsons & our niece. I called at 5:15 to see what the wait time was for a party of 7. I was told 45 minutes so off we went to Longhorn and waited, and waited, and waited. Finally were seated at 6:45 after a 90 minute wait. I realize it was a busy Saturday night but if you tell people it will be a 45 minute wait a 90 minute wait is really not acceptable. Little did we know the worst was yet to come.
We were seated & given 3 menus for 5 adults?? (the kids had their own menus). After a few minutes our waitress came to take our drink orders. After almost 15 minutes our drinks arrived & she took our food orders. My son-in-law & I each ordered an appetizer for the table & everyone ordered their entrees. Our waitress left saying she would be right back with bread.
After another 20 minutes or so it is now 7:30. We have been seated for 45 minutes & all we have are drinks. To our left is a party of 8 that was seated about 10 minutes after us. They have bread but no drinks (same waitress). I finally see our waitress & ask for bread. A few minutes later she brings bread & says our food will be out shortly. About 10 minutes later here come several people bringing our food. Yay! But wait...these are our entrees! Where are our appetizers we ask? They have no idea. Apparently our waitress has joined the witness protection program as she is nowhere in sight leaving these two poor souls to bear the brunt of our frustrations.
Not only are the appetizers MIA, my wife's salad is nowhere to be found & out of 5 adult entrees only one is as ordered. My wife's loaded sweet potato had only butter, the steakhouse mac & cheese side my son-in-law & I  ordered are missing & my daughter had no entree at all! We also had no silverware or napkins!
Finally the manager came over to apologize & we let him know in no uncertain terms what we thought of the service. My daughter eventually got her dinner, at no charge, the appetizers & drinks were removed from the bill & a 25% discount was applied to entire check. We will never set foot in this restaurant again.

I think I had my expectations set too high based upon all the rave reviews I heard about this place before tasting it for myself. My friends and I ordered Dungeness crab legs, shrimp, potatoes, boiled eggs, and  spicy garlic butter (comes on the side) and were highly disappointed. The food was spicy but bland and unfortunately the sauce on the side did not help. 
The parking lot was extremely packed and the line on the inside lead us to believe that we had found the secret treasure and we were so excited to give this place a try after so many recommendations. I understand that everyone's taste buds are not the same, but if you were expecting tons of flavor, this may not be the spot for you.

This is my first review on Yelp , which should say something ... This place was terrible . My boyfriend and I sat here and basically got ignored by our waiter . He seemed like he didn't have any idea what he was doing. Got the eggs Benedict and it was cold. We aren't from Philly but I can say that if we were to come back , we wouldn't come here...

Visited Nashville this past weekend and when we got there they charge $10 for guys I guess and ladies are free.. We were seated right away.. Was given a menu and the waitress disappeared for longer than desired however came back and took our order nonetheless.. Once we got our hookah the mouthpieces that we were given didn't fit so we got the attention of another waitress who then told us basically in so many words that it is what it is and to bend the pieces and force them on the hose of the hookah? We were a little pissed but anyways other than that this place was coo.. When you check in on yelp you can get a 10% discount off your entire bill. I think this night be new because our waitress was a bit shocked when I showed her the YELP coupon and took her forever to make the change on our bill. In the meantime we were patiently waiting for our $1.33 to be taken off haha!
Great motorcycle pit spot, great sandwiches, & great environment. The drive in here was beautiful! Definitely wok be returning!
We came all the way from St.Louis to eat here. And we didn't waste one second at a time. The people are amazing. Food will make you cry.if u live here... get here.  If you don't... get here anyway.

When in Chinatown, its time to have ramen! Well at least for the bf anyway! There was a little bit of a wait but that's expected since there is not that much seating inside and also because of the great reviews. I tried a rice bowl with chicken and egg and it was really good! There's plenty of options if you don't particularly want ramen. Our  server was really nice and he food came out pretty quick.

The number of ramen joints in Tampa has been exploding recently. I've heard a lot about this place from friends so I decided to drop by and give this place a try. Word of advice, carpool or get here early because parking is nearly nonexistent. But upon conquering the parking hurdle, you are rewarded with a delicious bowl of ramen. The ramen broth is rich with a good balance of salt that keeps you wanting to come back for more. The noodles are cooked well, with a nice chew and spring. All in all, an excellent experience. Will definitely recommend and will definitely come back to try more items off of the menu!
Best Thai food we have ever had. Been trying to find a place in St Pete with no luck until this gem. This is the best I've had after living in three different cities.

Ok. So first of all, this is the best restaurant I've ever been to. The service and food is always great.I'd recommend the steaks or tuna. ALWAYS get the truffles Mac and cheese as a side. Come here now!

This is my first Uber Eats order and it was ok. I got a promo for $20 off so I figured what the heck? I decided on O' Charleys! The steak was ok and the loaded potato was just ok as well. The only reason I can just say "OK" is because this is the main reason I don't use services like GrubHub, Door Dash, or Uber Eats. My food is never as fresh as me getting it myself or just plain eating it right when it comes out the kitchen. I love my food HOT! And getting cold rolls or a loaded potato with hot and cold spots just doesn't do it for me. 

When I dine in I always have a pleasant experience so a part 2 will follow this review

Big Lug is my trifecta of brewpubs: good beer, good food, and nice atmosphere.  I enjoy getting a flight of the beers (grab the king's jive).  Try one of the 1/2 and 1/2 combos.  The bahn mi is a good grab, and they do a Nashville hot chicken that will sear your innards.

The lattes we ordered were pretty good and we agreed that the espresso is pretty yummy, the barista working was friendly, and it was clear that the coffee shop is a neighborhood friendly.  Overall a decent experience with good, smooth espresso. The decor is a little plain but some people don't mind that.

We really like Farrotos. Great food. We have ordered online several times. They have a box online for special instructions, but they don't read it!!
We will go there again but will never order online!!!!!

Paul and Wendy have done it again with another incredible spot in St. Louis. The place is big yet cozy and the staff is always friendly. I've been a few times and have never been disappointed in the food or the beer. 

I love their loaded fries! The portion is huge and great for sharing. I also had their jumbo hot dog and it was jumbo all right. 

The craft beer selection and great and the Paul's Pils is my current fave. I highly recommend this place.

I was coming to try this place out for the first time and come to a surprise that they had closed early. I got there by 6:18pm since their website says 7pm, but here's to my luck. When I called, the lady that answered said that they closed due to no business for a "whole hour". . I guess businesses now a days work this way.  
Then she hung up after I asked if it was privately owned or corporate, clever. 
Terrible experience. #ShitList for sure.

Ambience : 4 for a warm hip family to romantic spot.  Works well with either group.  Interiors are welcoming with warm woods

Food: 4 to 3.  4 for the grilled artichoke and the meat plate with the hot spicy pepper spread  pizza a 3.3 ..I agree with reviews it lacks pizazz...bland .  At least bring a bottle of infused hot oil like they offer at Tre Lune (yummy) 
Gluten options available.  

Favorite pizza in town is till the Ode to dan Russo at Lucky Penny for its spicy tang.  However the seating availability and vibe here is more conducive to a relaxed longer dining experience.

In all fairness, I have only ever tried their lunchtime buffet so the menu items may be totally different in quality which is often the case.

I find their appetizer sections one of the best I have ever come across. Everything I tried was fresh and very flavorful. I was not as impressed with the main entree section. I did not enjoy their tandoori chicken at all and both the curry chicken dishes were average. I also did not enjoy their Naan, it seemed a little greasy to me and I would prefer to have it as part of the buffet rather than have your waiter bring it to you.

As it it just around the corner from home, I do intend to go one evening and see what it is like with the menu items. Hopefully I will be able to raise the rating a little if what other customers on this review is true.

The food is pretty standard for breakfast and reasonably priced.  The view of the pier and the ambience of the location is worth it.  It's a stop on every trip to Pass-A-Grille,  I would 'pass' on the coffee.

Today was my first time visiting Ford's garage and I will say it's not going to be the last. 
I came here today with 4 other ladies for lunch. We were greeted immediately by a friendly staff and seated in one of their many large booths. The decor is clever and eye catching. They use clamps for napkin rings and oil rags for napkins... I came from Detroit so I can appreciate this type of detail. 
I ordered the grilled chicken salad... the house dressing was a garlic vinaigrette and it was delicious. It came with an abundance of toppings, egg, bacon bits ,blue cheese ,tomato and the chicken was grilled perfectly. However the avocado was not ripe so I didn't try it. 
Everyone else at the table ordered one of the specialty burgers and all four ladies commented on how wonderful their lunch was including the sides. The service was quick and our waitress Brie was delightfully friendly and knowledgeable with menu items. 
After lunch the manager Billy approached us for our opinion... of course we were all very pleased and he answered all of our questions. Our most important question was .... "where is the next Fords garage going to be?" 
I'll admit I didn't expect much knowing today is only the second day they've been open... but they surprised me with a full knowledgeable staff and a tasty menu.

Oh my god.  This is an insane place to get a drink.  Order scotch, they'll pour you half of a bottle of the stuff.  If I could remember the place, I'd tell you that it's pretty good sized with a whole variety of menu options (various types of french dips, yum).  The drinks are a little pricey, but given that one drink is the equivalent of maybe 3-4 somewhere else, it's a deal.  Good food too.

They are still new and learning the ropes.
A few lesson's learned
1. Make a reservation (last Sunday was a 30 minute wait with many open tables b/c we did not have a reservation
2. Right now just a few beers.  The server did not tell us, but I noticed on a walk to the restroom that it is BYOB currently for wine
3. My son loved the Mac and cheese
4.my husband liked the burger and fries (extra)
5. Chicken and waffles - the chicken was HOT and the waffles were cold and had too much syrup on them
6. Pay attention to your bill, we were overcharged 
7. There are a few versions in the menu pile with various prices (I told the manager)

Hope to return when they get over their growing pains

For now will go to Montesantos, Eagle Tavern and Liberty Union

My boyfriend and I went again tonight since they are offering Summer Feast for $40 (app, entree, and side). While the service was spectacular, as always, the food was lacking. We were greeted immediately upon stepping in and seated right away despite not having reservations. The onion rings were still delicious, light and crispy. My boyfriend and I both chose the filet which was tender and cooked to perfection. The steaks were very under seasoned though compared to our previous visits when they were perfect. We opted for the potatoes au gratin and crab au gratin for our sides. Both sides came tremendously salty and the potatoes too peppery for my boyfriend.
Order the Recco pasta (creamy tomato base with curry, basil, garlic, etc).  You will not be disappointed!

Food was good, I lost the reason why my soft shell crab was put on a bed of corn. 
My big complaint was their rush to turn the table over when you are paying 40.00 a plate. Bus was constantly trying to remove our plates, at least three different times while we were still eating. We weren't slow, in and out in 40 minutes, but was pushed out the door. Food is only half the battle.

Typically I take a photo of my food to share here but I was too ravenous. I had jumbalaya and boyfriend had the sampler and both were FANTASTIC! The food here in NOLA is so good and this place didn't disappoint. The bread they serve is so fluffy and light - I normally try not to eat bread but f@#$ it. I'm on vacation and it was delicious. Def come here! Boyfriend had a beer with the word NOLA in it and he liked it -it was light. Abita is the local brew here and it's good too (I have to take his word for it as I detest beer. Yeah, I know)

I'm new to Indian food (don't judge me, I've always been a baby with spice) but a friend ordered takeout for us once and I LOVE bawarchi. 
I've only ever ordered takeout but everything is always amazing. Every order comes with a side of basmati (ordered the mistake once to order sides of rice not knowing it already came with). The basmati is always cooked perfectly. I typically go with chicken tiki Marsala and the buttered chicken. NEVER forget to order the garlic naan.. so good!! They are conveniently on doordash if you're looking for takeout.

My favorite hotel in downtown Boise. Staff is super friendly, rooms are clean, bed is comfortable and the hotel is walking distance to everything downtown. Best of all, within the walls of the hotel, resides Chandlers Steak House. One of the best establishments in Boise.

Good food and service! The Zacatecs (spl) is great and the chips and salsa are delicious. The fried were not great and the tacos were average. Cheese quesadilla was good and we will go back again for sure.
Not really much to look at inside- but worth it for the food! Again, not fancy at all, but delicious sandwiches and fried bar food. For sure get the roast beef! YUM.

Service was nice but overwhelmed.   Recommend not going here during busy times.  Besides service being very slow I specifically asked to have wine BEFORE the food and they did the opposite. By the time the wine got there the food was ice cold.  Ravioli was ok but too rich and not a delicate sauce at all.  Overall food was fine but nothing special.   Ate outside to the combined smells of disinfectant and truffles.

WARNING: My Yelp star score is only for the food, drinks and waiter service. I had a fairly unpleasant experience with the hostess at the front. I made a reservation for four people and I arrived on time but people in my party were running late. They arrived one after another and when one other friend arrived, the hostess came over and asked us the eta for our two other friends and we said they were definitely still coming just running late. She then told us they only hold reservations for 15 minutes and they needed to turn the tables for more guests and reservations. Which is fine...but why sit us down at our table already then tell us this? I literally asked her, so are you trying to kick us out now? Or what? So we decided to order (I guess before they had to kick us out?) even though our two other friends weren't there yet but came like 10-15 minutes later. The worst part for me, was that at the end of our dinner when we were waiting to leave, the restaurant was not filled to the brim. There was literally an empty table next to us the entire time we were there. So I'm really not sure why we were rushed or frankly why they were being so rude to us at the beginning. This experience would have brought my score completely down if it weren't for the actual food at the restaurant. 


We ordered a lot of the major tapas and all were delicious. I think my favorites were the Brussel sprouts, the steak, the croquettes and the patatas bravas. They had very classics tapas options and all were really cooked well and tasted pretty amazing. The portion sizes were not too small either. The dishes were rich so I felt like I got the perfect amount of full after sharing several dishes. 

We also got cocktails and wine. I really appreciated our server giving us recommendations for wines and letting us sample them before we ordered. We also ordered the churros and olive oil cake. I love churros, but wow, I was really impressed with the olive oil cake. I would 100% order that again.

This spot was our first eating stop in NOLA and it set the bar for everything else. My seafood Benedict was AMAZING! One of my poached eggs was over cooked but it was still so good! My boyfriend had the shrimp and grits and man the grits were to die for. So cheesy and full of flavor plus with the sauce from the shrimp! I ordered a bacon Bloody Mary even though I don't like bloody Mary's, I'm more of a michelada gal but I still gave it a try. It was very flavorful and SPICY! It would have been the perfect Michelada! There's just something in Bloody Mary's that I don't like the flavor of but this one was good. Nice environment and nice staff. Quick service and great food!

Sunflower Cafe is cool little spot in a great part of town. I stopped in for happy hour before heading to the airport, which allowed me to get a decent sample of some different menu items. The hummus plate was a solid choice, and the pita was delicious and warm. I found myself wishing we had gotten more veggies, though, because there's just no way we could eat all the hummus we got unless we just scooped it up.

The nachos were really good. I loved whatever chips they used and the queso, which I assume was cashew. The only thing I'll say is that as with most nachos, it was impossible to get to the chips in the center and the chips just got soggy and inedible. In hindsight, I would have gone for the double dip since it still had the queso and black bean corn salsa.

I was unimpressed with the quesadilla. The buffalo tempeh was a little weird texture for the quesadilla...yes, all tempeh is weird texture, but I usually like it and just didn't feel it worked inside the quesadilla. The carrots and such were fine to, but I honestly couldn't even tell there was cheese in it, which was a bummer.

the chocolate chip cookie dough was great! The texture was slightly grainy and not as "solid" as I like to see from a typical cookie dough, but I wouldn't say I minded it. It definitely hit the spot for some sweetness after the rest of the meal.

I really wanted to write a great review, because the staff is friendly and responsive and the owner/chief Steve is extremely attentive to the needs of his diners.
Unfortunately, my impression after two dining experiences is that the food is just "average", so I was hoping to get some insight from other reviewers.

Onmy first visit, I tried their Friday night prime rib special and was less than impressed. The look of the meat was odd and the flavor was very plain. It was clearly more cooked than the "medium" I ordered and I had to use alot of horseradish to make it edible. Tothe chiefs credit he offered to cook another for me, which I declined because I had already eaten a good part of the meat and didn't think it would be right to waste food I knew I wouldn't eat at home. I can't really fault them.  If I want a tasty prime rib, then I know I need to pay more at McMahons, Flemings or Firebirds (another hidden gym).  

On my second visit, I ordered the tuna tartare and the jambalaya. One of my regular "haunts" is BJ which I think is a very underrated bar and resturarnt. I couldn't help but compare the two dishes. The tuna tartare was okay, but a bit dry.  The dish is accompanied by some chips that have their own seasoning (I couldn't place the taste - perhaps cinnomon??) that i didn't think complimented the taste of the tuna.  (If you get a chance, the more flavorful Tuna ahi poke at BJs is wonderful).  

I also ordered the 1/2 portion of chicken and shrimp jambalayaon Fettuccine.  The sauce was quite tasty and the fettuccine was well cooked. However, I had ONE shrimp in the dish.  I know the staff recognized me from my last visit, so I didn't dare complain - least I be labeled as a high maintenance diner.  There were little cubes of uniform looking chicken which made me wonder if they were using processed chicken or if it had been freshy cooked. Again, it was just an "okay" plate and I was really disappointed about the lack of shrimp given the $9.00 I had paid for the dish. (Again, try BJ's jambalaya. It is filled with shrimp, large pieces of chicken and Andouille sausage.)

I really, really want to like this restaurant.  I eat out at least 5 times a week, and Reish is close to home and convenient to my route home from work. The staff is quite friendly and Steve works hard to ensure that customers have a great dining experience.  I was glad to read recommendations from other reviewers, so I might be willing to give it one more try now that I have a lead on other dishes I might find more satisfying.  

This is a neighborhood restaurant and I really hope they are successful!

For my first blog, I was in Philadelphia for New Years Eve so I went to my favorite cheesesteak place, Geno's.  While many debate the best cheesesteaks in Philly, my personal perference is the ultra-American Geno's.

One thing that I love about Geno's is the hours of operation.  Given that I went on New Years Eve, one might expect Geno's to be closed, especially given the fact that the cross-street rival Pat's was not serving.  Instead, the hardworking Geno's staff is open 24/7/365, ensuring that I can always get my favorite cheesesteak and that the neighborhood is always aglow thanks to the massive neon signs adorning the outside of this landmark spot.

Although the lines tend to differ depending on when you go, we hit a peak time and the line wrapped partway around the block.  However, the system of serving up the cheesesteaks helps the line move along at a rapid pace so it only took us about 25 minutes to get to the window.

Upon arriving at the window, you notice the bumper stickers they have posted illustrating their support for police, ordering in English, and contempt for anything un-American.  The  establishment is cash only and they prefer you to order a specific way, stating simply the type of cheese first and then "wit" or "witout" onions.  Thats it.  Don't bother asking for mushrooms, lettuce, or any other silly condiments on a true Philly cheesesteak.  You can, however, add a few limited condiments yourself after getting your food.  The service is not exceptionally welcoming, but the setup is built to get the customer their food promptly so that is not a major detractor.  Geno's is also a cash-only place, so don't expect to come with just a credit card in hand.

The variety on the menu is limited to cheesesteaks and roast pork sandwiches with fries, cheese fries and sodas available at a separate window, but come on, when your going to Geno's, everyone is getting a cheesesteak.  The prices are not cheap, with a cheesesteak costing $8.50 and a cup of cheese fries putting you back $4.50.  

I ordered a cup of cheese fries to eat while waiting in line.  Given our hunger and the thick coating of cheese, we downed these in no time.  I cannot tell for sure if it was my hunger and anticipation but I felt that the fries were great.  We then went on to order our cheesesteaks, her getting a Whiz With, while I ordered a Whiz Without.  One thing I love about Geno's Steaks is the fact that they offer whiz, a cheese that too few restaurants offer outside of Philly.  The cheese was nice and gooey like whiz should be and though it could have stood to be a little heavier on the cheese, the mixture of cheese, bread, and meat really worked.

Although I do not usually like grilled onions, Geno's makes it work well on the cheesesteak.  The onions were placed on the grill but hardly grilled giving them a nice crunch that worked well on the cheesesteak.  The meat was well prepared using nice, thinly sliced ribeye pieces (not chopped up though) with a little bit of fat on it to give it some juice and flavor.    

The bread was the biggest difference between a Philly cheesesteak and a cheesesteak from elsewhere.  Delivered from up the street, the amoroso rolls they use do not overpower the sandwich by being too thick but instead offer a soft roll that is at the same time firm enough to handle the cheesesteak.  The sandwich really comes together with a perfect blend of meat, cheese, and a terrific bread roll.  Everyone has their favorite cheesesteak place, but mine is definitely Geno's topping its cross-street rival Pat's King of Steaks.  That being said, look for blog reports on some of the other well known Philly cheesesteak joints in the future.

Ratings:
Meat: 7.5
Bread: 10
Cheese: 9
Cost: 6
Overall Combination: 10

This was my first time at the cherry hill location and it was just as good if not better than the Mount Laurel location. Definitely more room (a lot more) if you don't like feeling crammed. I got the vegetable spring roll as with their homemade peanut sauce which is to die for. Salty, say saucey, peanut buttery greatness. I got the Pho Tom (shrimp noodle soup) but asked for it in the vegetable broth because it it phenomenal. The waiter was a really nice kid and very attentive. I will definitely be back to this location from now on because it is way closer to home and I didn't know it existed !! Not to take away from the mount laurel location because they are VERY similar quality and food wise but totally
Different atmospheres. Their wasn't a huge crowd and it was a very nice quiet place to enjoy a bowl of soup on a Friday night
Food and Service are always top-notch. Highly recommend the steak and scallops pick 2. The Mac and cheese is a few dollars extra but an excellent side choice. Can't wait to go back!

Deluxe Pho, #42, for $6.50. Yes, I realize this restaurant is surrounded by other Pho places. Yes, I realize I have not yet completed my life mission of trying every one. And yes, I realize there is more to Vietnamese food than Pho. Did that stop me, no!  So why should it stop you?
Total treat! Coffee equaled the best we tasted in Bali. Wait staff was wonderful. Meat combo platter made me wish we had "come to this country" years ago !!!

Enjoyed a splendid lunch here with my best friend. The service was good and the establishment was very clean. Not very busy for a mid-week lunch period. The only complaint I might have is that the music was a little loud.

We ate outside during the summer. We were blessed with a hail and rain show! Happy hour - Asian pear salad with chicken. The perfect combo of
textures and flavors. The boysenberry smear was a delightful accent. The dirty martini is a definite for pickle lovers. The pear tart should be listed as dessert!! The shrimp cocktail had beautifully well ripened chunks of avocado. If we lived in Tucson we'd be back often!!

I'll sum it up because all has been said by others. Way overrated. Food was good but nothing you would say to friends, "you gotta try this place". Service was lousy.. had to ask for water and then all four at the table ran dry. Waiter not engaging.. he was just there like you could expect him to go home and drink himself into oblivion to forget his miserable existence. Ambiance is a tad formal but loud.
Good coffee, made perfectly. $2.50 for a double espresso is sensible.  A little rickety looking but it is actually charming.  Good wi-fi

My husband, son and I went out for a family dinner. After being seated right away, we sat for 15 minutes without being greeted (we were seated closest to the server ordering station), with multiple servers standing around chatting. Multiple tables were seated after us, drink orders taken and delivered. When we decided to leave, we asked for the manager, who did not seem bothered or concerned with our experience.

Opening day happy hour (3-6!) was fabulous. Lively crowd, plenty of locals (it's mid-July!), excellent and inventive food, pleasant working waterfront setting, an exciting brief summer downpour, helpful staff, well-priced (especially HH well drinks). We'll definitely be regulars.

Upscale BYOB with casual prices.

Really like the wedge salad and filet mignon here.

Pork chop was very good, also the Chicken Parm with gnocchi. Filet mignon egg rolls were also pretty addicting.

BYOB so bring your favorite bottle(s) of wine.

The East Nasty is more savory, but I think the princess is better. 

The princess with the pickles, hot chicken, and the honey is great combination. The chicken is not very spicy at all, but it was still a good meal. Ask for extra honey on the side for the biscuit! 

The jam that comes with the Bonuts is what makes it good. It's not something you have to try, but it's good if you're craving something sweet.

Went here for lunch in Saturday when we discovered Bosco's had closed. Bad decision.

Service was generally poor. First thing I asked for was a particular local beer and of course they didn't have that one. We shared an appetizer of fried green tomatoes which were ok but nothing special. Then the fun began.
After three attempts to actually cook a simple omelette my wife gave up and just ate the part cooked mess. The first attempt was so undercooked as to be dangerous. The second attempt (allegedly a completely new omelette) wasn't much better. They took the second one back and apparently showed it a lit match or something as it was still undercooked but now browned to appear cooked.

They took her food off the bill and offered free desserts. We declined. If you can't get an omelette right in 3 tries I don't want more of your fare thanks.

Won't be returning.

Oh, one tip for you servers...have your girlfriends dine somewhere else. It is infuriating to be unable to get service while you are playing lovebirds at the next table while I am looking at undercooked food and trying in vain to attract the staffs attention.

It's been near impossible to find an egg bagel since moving to Florida. My search is over! They make me he most delicious egg bagels I've tasted in years. Sorry I can't tell you about any other of their many flavors!

Awesome little place on 19, smells amazing every time you drive by!  Today's special was a pulled pork grilled cheese. Very good. I also love the porky pie. The meat has a great smokey flavor but is still tender and juicy!  They also sell smoked fish spreads.  Food comes out quick so it's a great place to go when you're in a hurry and super hungry :)

**There's a car detailing place directly next door- so I also had my Suburban completely detailed during lunch.  I left full, happy and with a VERY clean truck!!

Service was great! But the burger I had was mediocre. 
I would honestly return for their delicious in-house ketchup (with a side of fries haha).

Great service, but food and drinks are "meh"...

We were met immediately upon sitting down, and waters brought right out.  Drink orders taken right away and brought to the table very quickly.  My drink, Maple Pear Sour, one of the featured cocktails, tasted like a muddled mess.  I couldn't discern any of the ingredients other than the frothed egg white on top. My husband had the Adios Amigos, with mezcal and Domaine de Canton ginger liquor, and proclaimed it good and smoky. 

It was fun to try one of the hundreds of whiskeys they have available, as a Manhattan, and this drink was much better.

For food, I had the lobster roll, and I realize we're in TN, but this didn't taste like any other lobster roll I've ever had.  I thought the sauce holding everything together is supposed to be mayo, but there was barely any of that, and overwhelming lemon juice.  The hot chicken "sammies" were 3 small bao buns, and my husband was still quite hungry after that - our fault that we didn't notice these were considered appetizers, and not a sandwich entree.  The fries were fantastically crispy and tasty, but it sure makes them look cheap to offer a number of different sauces to have with the fries, but you get only one choice, and have to pay $1.25 for a little cup of any other type.  Overall, a very mixed experience - there's too many other great restaurants to try, that I doubt we'll go back.

The volcano tots were amazing!  I love that the cheese sauce was made with butternut squash.  It helped me feel better about my decision to eat out. Sure, tots aren't healthy, but it was sooo good!  I also had the sweet potato falafel and wasn't disappointed. The service was courteous and swift at a very busy time. Definitely visit this vegan hot spot when you're in St. Louis...you won't be disappointed!

This place is just great. The food is like that of any other Subway, but what makes this place great is the staff and the building. It is always clean, and the staff are always so nice and accommodating. I always get the same sub when I'm there and every time I do, it is delicious. The gave me a water cup so I could put the Monster Energy I got somewhere else, in ice. The view is pretty nice, and it is handicap accessible. They even took the time to point out a coupon on the back of my receipt. Overall great service and great food. I will continue to eat here!

We held my grandmother's 75th birthday party here on Saturday night; reserved the private space on the second floor for dinner.  The space is absolutely beautiful and held our group of ~35 with room to spare.  

We had two really great bartender/servers - Melanie & Amanda.  They took care of the group during the cocktail hour and then served dinner to the four tables.  Dinner was served family style.  We had chicken marsala, salmon, and sirloin with mashed potatoes and mixed vegetables (mostly broccoli) for sides.  I had the steak (perfectly cooked - medium rare) with a small serving of mashed potatoes and veggies.  The potatoes were too mashed (100% smooth) for my liking but the vegetables were seasoned and cooked well.  

Everything was perfect about our night at Iavarone's.  We had a wonderful, relaxed dinner party with good food and great service.

Holy. Friggin. Crap. Best meal I've had in years. 

4 of us came in on a Tuesday evening and it felt as though we almost tasted the entire menu. 

Our waiter, Gavin, was Divine. So attentive. Very kind, can offer excellent suggestions, and you can tell he's passionate about the food. We had an individual with a gluten sensitivity in our group and they were able to accommodate this without blinking an eye. He was a big factor in why our experience was so fantastic. 

We began with the hummus sampler. Had falafel, lamb, onions, etc. Came with fresh pita you could see baking in the oven. Delicious. They were also able to accommodate the gluten sensitivity by bringing out vegetables for the hummus as well. 

We had several vegetable dishes to share and then also got a few entrees. We had the beets, broccoli, cauliflower, chicken, octopus, and 1/2 rack of lamb. My favorites were the beets, broccoli, chicken, and lamb. So basically everything. The crust on the lamb was perfect. The chicken was in a bowl with broth and chickpeas and was so hearty and warming. The sauce on the beets...so good!!!

We also had several cocktails and all were excellent. The waiter even whipped out the menu from a recent event where they were doing fall drinks. The bourbon drinks were my favorite. 

Do yourself a favor...come here and have one of the best meals of your year if not your life!

Best Pho in middle Tennessee. 
Meatballs are home made! Always fresh ingredients and great service. Nothing better on a cold or rainy day or to help get over the sniffles than a large bowl of pho!  I eat here as often as I can. It is a bit difficult to get in and out of the parking lot, but I found that there is an access to the main road behind the building that leads to the stoplight intersection ( essential around rush hours)

Came down to the oyster house on a quiet summer Monday. The bartender was very friendly!
The food is amazing! The oyster shooters and the mussels were amazing!

my husband and I have been 2 this location a few times for breakfast recently. We were pleasantly surprised- the  omelettes were very good and the pancakes were delicious. It was very crowded on the  occasions we were there. The restaurant is clean and the waitstaff is on their game. this is going to be our go to spot for breakfast from now on.

This place and everything about it is A-OK. The dim sum is good, but falls short compared to Joy Tsin Lau, Ocean Harbor, etc. Prices are fine. The parking situation in theory is good and is one of the few reasons I venture here, but it consistently takes me 10-20 minutes to find a spot during dim sum hours (10-1 PM on Sat/Sun) in their seemingly spacious parking lot! With such a long wait, I might as well be in Chinatown!

Sometimes going off script leads to greatness, and that's exactly where we found ourselves last night. Stumbling onto this Broad Ripple gem was meant to be. After some recommendations from our waiter Brad, I chose the Inferno Burger (Angus beef cooked medium, topped with pulled pork in their chipotle bbq sauce, two onion rings all on a brioche bun). My wife decided on their fish sandwich (Trout fillets, with an aioli sauce on a multigrain bun)  The burger was cooked to perfection, and the onion rings where . A date night isn't complete without dessert; we ordered the Fudge Brownie S'more. Needless to say, this will not be our last visit.
Worst parking lot ever!!! And you're not allowed to park on the street anywhere near it!!! I love their pastries but jeez almost lot worth it!

Decided to try Irie for lunch today. Can I be honest the lady that run the front is very nice but the food is horrible I order the Oxtail meal the meat was tender but NO Jamaican flavors at all.  The sweet plantains taste like they were cook in old oil and no flavor on the cabbage. I will never go back. I rather go to Trust Me or somewhere else

This has to be one of our favorite restaurants in St. Petersburg. So much to offer: 
Unique Menu and Delicious Food! Their food is simply the best. The menu has changed a few times which could be frustrating because you go in wanting one thing that isn't on the menu (which by the way, they will make for you if requested), but seriously try something off the new menu you won't be disappointed! 
Amazing Leadership - stopped in today without calling ahead (party of 12) and without any hesitation they took our name informed the floor manager who quickly went to work planning our seating arrangements. We were seated in less than 30 minutes and had our food 20 minutes later. 
Amazing Staff - We have never had a bad experience with their staff. Always pleasant and accommodating. Our waiter today was Will. He is fantastic! Fun, personable, energetic, and efficient, and if that isn't enough he's great with kids and make a delicious chocolate milk too!

IOU Sushi IV is the place for all you can eat sushi. 

A clean interior with friendly staff a large bright windows make this restaurant feel homey. 

The dinner menu offers their more high end sushi rolls, but whether you dine for lunch or dinner you are able to custom order your own rolls and hand rolls, just write down what you want and they will make it.

I love that they make a nice tempura sweet potato which I put in a roll with avocado and cucumber. 

I haven't tried much else off the menu than sushi and tea, what can I say, I go there with an intention. 

And based on how often I go, you should already know, it's five stars from me!
Great Spanish restaurant in Santa Barbara.  Difficult to get reservation, so plan ahead otherwise try for a seat at the bar.

I wish I could give a good review, but I just can't. I've ordered by going there and through door dash. Both times I ordered a grilled cheese (in person and through door dash) they gave me a breakfast sandwich and the bread was soggy. The latte I got on my first visit wasn't very good, but my husband ordered champurrado with espresso and it was awesome.  Another visit my son made was to get a specialty refresher for us, they didn't have any, so we got mango smoothies and they were awful, they were not blended enough and had a weird aftertaste. Since the only drink I've enjoyed there is the champurrado, and I want to support local, I've gone THREE times in the last few weeks for champurrado and every time they don't have any.   You would think that if you are running out of something regularly that you would make more accommodate request, nope...

Side note: turn the music down, it's way too loud.

I used to go to the Rusty Pelican quite often & for no specific reason, it fell off my radar. Rusty Pelican is located at the far end of the Courtney Causeway, right on beautiful Tampa bay. They defiantly  have a lot of windows & let you have fabulous waterfront views from almost any vantage point. I love the upscale ambiance and posh vibes I get from the establishment.
I recently returned for an after work evening of pure decadence. 
We imbibed in the beat wines and started our evening with an overflowing amount of seafood appetizers for our table. Everything was fresh & properly prepared. After an abundance of appetizers, they still wanted full dinners...LOL, hey who am I to argue, I wasn't getting the check.
Between all at the table we had some great steaks, seafood & various other dishes.
Did I mention the service was excellent...outstanding. I will admit I don't think we were the easiest table to wait on, but I will bet, it had the best tip. We chatted over our food and the overall concensus was very good.
Going into gourmet  desserts & tawny ports, all remained high caliber & no major complaints.
It is a great date or special occasion restaurant, but it can also be a regular restaurant, that is defiantly going back on my rotation.
Everyone had a wonderful & enchanted evening. Don't know about the check & don't care, just glad I was participating! 
What's a girl to do? Luxury comes in many forms & I found quite a bit tonight!

I absolutely love this place! I started off trying different dishes which were all good, but then I tried the fattoush and was blown away. It's fresh, packed with flavor, and I can't get enough of it. It is the only thing I order there now and I could eat it every day. It's honestly one of the best things I ever ate. 

The owners are so gracious and genuine and they treat everyone like family. The food is made to order, no preservatives, lots of organic options, and they even have organic or gluten free wine and beer. Their fries/chips are made with coconut oil and they're so good. The baklava is simply amazing; it's light and not drenched with honey like I've had elsewhere.

First time in Reno and we were looking for sushi. Found this place that had all you can eat sushi.

Priced at $21 per person. The sushi was good and the service was great. The owner recommended that our 4 year old just eat from the buffet so we saved paying from the kids meal.

I would return again with the family. The food alone would put it at 3 1/2 stars but for the price and service, they get 5 stars. 

And the Mochi green tea ice cream at the end was a perfect ending to the meal.

What a great way to wrap up Spring Break for my family. We choose to go for the lunch buffet! This is the place for my family because I have 2 vegetarian/ vegan eaters. They offer plenty of non meat options as well. * be sure to get the lunch punch card to earn a free meal* Honestly, the buffet here is the best route to go. Indian food is great! I just don't know the names of half the dishes I eat. This is because I eat off the buffet verses ordering directly from the menu. I also like to try different dishes and embrace it the flavors so an Indian buffet is just a good option.  It has well know items such as tandoori chicken, honey balls, curried goat and basmati rice.. just to make a few options.. On the buffet this day they had tempura vegetables which I loved so much I asked them to bring more out when they ran out. They brought us the freshest Naan to the table! Pipping hot with chunks of fresh garlic on it. They offer a few desserts as well (as in 4) so definitely don't get your hopes up if you have a sweet tooth. there was so much more to be seen and eaten.

This was a last minute decision to eat here and it was such a great surprise! The inside is decorated so nicely and has a really pretty view. But best of all, the food was delicious!  We started with the calamari which was perfect. All four of us got the Lobster Roll and it may have been the best I've had (although admittedly I've not been to Maine). The Mac n cheese was great and the lighthouse salad was too. I also was a big fan of the house Rose which is apparently made just for them. My husband was impressed with their Old Fashioned and he's pretty picky about those!  Lol.  I would absolutely return next time in Nashville.

Vegan quesadillas, YES!  
Everything is fresh, mostly local organic, and the selection of vegan options seems endless.  Try the kale salad with vegan cheese and it will rock your world.

I have been going to the VIP for years and always enjoyed it but that changed last week. I went for a light dinner with the family and the service was BEYOND bad. The server was just down right rude. I kept thinking it had to be a joke because she was being so rude. To top it all off at the end of the meal, She asked if we could go ahead and leave because she needed the table. We had not even paid yet and the only reason the table was cleaned is because I bussed it.

However, I do enjoy their Mexican Pizza.

Really loved the ambiance and decor, they did a great job decorating for the holidays too. The fireplace and set up was very cozy! I ordered the Sherlock latte and it was just ok, the flavors didn't really compliment each other..too much going on. We also ordered 2 paninis and the another one bites the crust pizza. The pizza was the best of the three, but even that was not great. I know it's a cafe pizza, so I wouldn't expect pizzeria quality but it was very average.

Great to finally have Ramen in Boise.   We always try Ramen in Vegas, Seattle, Portland ....   Ramen Sho has Miso broth that is good (probably 3.5 compared to other cities).  Menu should provide options to add additional items.  Try this restaurant.

NEW OWNERS AND A POOR PRODUCT!!!! After having great tacos last year at this location, a friend and I looked very forward to returning as we were back in the area.  Sadly, a total disappointment!  Although we had each purchased groupons separately, as we approached the window, the young woman working tried to tell us we could not both use our groupons!  After patiently and repeatedly telling the employee that these were two separate groupons several times, she finally agreed to let us use them.  Between the two of us we ordered 8 tacos, a mixture of carnitas (shredded pork) chorizo/shrimp, ground beef and skirt steak ( carne asada).  We were told that this year, would have to pay 1.00 per taco for cheese and sour cream???  Lousy policy.  Worst part was when we opened our orders at home, all the tacos had NO SAUCE, ( we ordered mild and medium) and were dry and almost impossible to choke down.  Sad, because there was potential - the carnitas were very good and plentiful, the chorizo and the ground beef were seasoned well.  Skirt steak was burnt and not seasoned at all.  We won't be returning and after reading the recent reviews, it seems the new owners need a reboot.

Ok. I'm sure it's supposed to be fine dining but wow it's not good. Tiny overpriced portions and infuriatingly odd in the way it's prepared and served, one item at a time.  Three TINY meatballs for like 15.00 or about five pieces of okra for 12.00. Even the "entree" options are barely even enough for one person much less to share with others.  One of the vegetables we had was corn. And it was supposed to be a creamed corn but it ended up being more of a sauce. Light brown baby poop looking sauce we referred to as goulash because it looked disgusting and didn't taste like corn.  The lamb was served on top of what looked like quinoa but it was some type of strange fat grain but had no taste and a yucky texture.  The quail was about the size of the palm of my hand and was greasy with a thick skin. And the cocktails were terrible. The one I had tasted like it had Worcestershire sauce in it. Bleecgh! 

Short version... Way overpriced. Tiny tiny portions. Food not that good. Sharing tiny portions made it even less enjoyable. Cocktails sucked. No chance I would return.

The waitstaff was really nice and the place looks great and there were a few things that were fun like the fact they bring you your check in an old book. That was cute.  The appetizer we had of whipped fetters cheese and pita bread was delicious.  And the spicy habanero sauce for the meatballs was good and the taste of the meatballs was delicious but they were so unbelievably small!!  But those few tiny little details could hardly ever outweigh the bad food and cocktails so over priced.

We came to Edmonton to visit a friend, and had to visit this Canadian pizza chain. Upon entering the location right across from West Edmonton Mall I was very pleased with the decor and ambiance of the joint. We were promptly seated in a booth and given menus to go over. We settled on two personal pizzas and a calamari app for the three of us. I was impressed when the calamari came out in just a couple of minutes after we ordered it! The calamari was fried to perfection and the dipping sauce was very good as well. Really complimented the oily calamari. The pizzas came out soon after the appetizer and looked amazing. One was their spicy Perogi, and the other was a smoked ham. The perogi pizza was good, but lacked a lot of flavor. The smoked ham pizza was very solid with the sweet marinara complementing the Smokey ham perfectly. The crust was pretty good, but once again lacked flavor. Overall this was a solid choice and I am happy we came! I would say don't run to get here, but if you're looking for some pizza while visiting Canada give it a try!

We came in with a big group at 3pm. No one was there the first bartender Serena was great. Then the second bartender came in. I ordered an appetizer. Over 15 min  later it wasn't there yet. My big group was ready to go. I told the bartender to cancel my order because we
We're leaving. She says. I still have to charge you. Oh you're gonna charge us for food we didn't get? The 18 yr old manager didn't seem to care that 20 of
