Cute diner spot. Took kids. Friendly and quick service. Free wifi. Boys got classic grilled cheeses w fries and loved them. I have blue pig grilled cheese with funnel fries which was super yummy. My hubby had a salad which was a nice size. All in all super happy. Are inside but they have outside seating as well. Will definitely go back.

Pros:

creative and extremely well prepared food, decent portion size,  fair prices, excellent service, nice atmosphere, BYOB

Cons:

Loud, desserts just OK, hard to book reservation

So great.  You will not be disappointed.  A wide variety of sandwiches.  The French dip and Rueben is awesome.  Always a good experience with the friendly staff.  We go there all the time and I have  never been disappointed.  Too bad there are not more of these.
To die for...Irene's oysters, amazing wine selection and the new location is beautiful olde world style.
Excellent! Everything was absolutely delicious from the wine to the fries to the sandwiches. Service was great too. Coming back tomorrow before we leave for breakfast!

So...It was my birthday a couple of weeks ago. I was on the search for a good breakfast place near my dad's house to start my celebration. I came on yelp and found this place. I was surprised that I hadn't seen it before given that it literally a couple stores down from our neighborhood safeway and some of my other favorite restaurants. 

My partner and I went there around 11a. There were a handful of folks there. We picked our seat and were immediately greeted. Everyone was really friendly and wished me a happy birthday.

The food came an it was awesome! I thought because of the low price, the portions would be smaller. I was pleasantly surprised. I ordered the chicken fried steak and eggs with a hash brown. My partner got a basic bacon and egg breakfast with a biscuit with gravy...see...that's the thing...not only is the food cheap but you get your choice of huge side orders with your breakfast...And let me tell you the food is incredible. It was probably one of the best chicken fried steaks i've had next to when Iron Skillet is on it's A game. Everything was fresh and seemed like it was homemade. We also got a cinnamon roll. It was tasty too. Not quite as good as one from a bakery but close.

I don't really know why you wouldn't choose to go here if you were looking to have a great breakfast and are in Oro Valley. It's not like there's much up here anyway :D

This is the best Thai food on the north side.  Their lunch meals are economical and the food is fantastic.

The restaurant is in an unassuming strip mall (like everything else in the suburb of Fishers) but the food is as close to authentic as the midwest gets.  Our personal favorites are the Thai Spicy Basil with chicken, the Crab Rangoons, and any of their fried rice varieties (bonus points for serving the Hawaiian Fried Rice in a half pineapple).

We eat here often and we never have any complaints with wait time, service staff, or quality and quantity of food.  One word of warning; do not order your food at the spice level "Thai Hot" unless you're ready to sweat it out the remainder of your day.

You know when you are about to do something, you know it is not a good idea, but you do it anyway.....this was what we did the other night when it was dinner time, we were hungry and walking out of a store next to Bonefish - we knew it was a chain, we knew this one had bad reviews, we gave it a shot anyway.  A mistake.
Had the muscles as appetizer which were good - however about 45 seconds after they hit the table someone brought out our entrees and said 'oh guess you don't want these yet' and left.  Ok so far - however ~10min later when the appetizer was finished, they brought out dinners again -  THE SAME PLATES - yes, everything on both plates was cold, steak, shrimp, fish, fries was all cold - it was obvious it was under a warming lamp, but thats about it.  Horrible - best part - the waitress came by to ask how things were i said 'cold' and she just walked away.... love it.  So - wont be back.
food and service was great, atmosphere was nice and even the music was good we enjoyed our meal and definitely get dessert if you go soo good

This is a unique place because their menu is so dynamic.  When you want to bring in a bottle of red and enjoy a great Italian meal, you can have that experience.  If you want to go for a cheesesteak and fries and watch the Eagles, there you go.

Regardless of your final destination for entree - please get the Antipasto - an amazing array of flavors and textures such as mushrooms oreganata, roasted red peppers, red onion, italian sausage to name a few, all served with a homemade rustic Italian dressing, chunky and bursting with garlic, oregano and olive oil.

My go-to is their White Spinach pie with fresh tomatoes.  The crunch of the crust pairs  up the creaminess of the fresh mozzarella and perfectly sautéed spinach and finishes with a burst from the tomatoes in every bite.  

Their chicken sandwiches (try the #4!!!!)  are totally unique and are perfect with one the best side dishes ever - broccoli bites - batter dipped and served with real deal Philly cheese whiz.

I have tried it all and always have a warm, family friendly experience every time I go back.

The owner is stumbling drunk at 3:30 pm and just groped a female employee.

All of the employees are great. Used to come here twice a month and will not be back

I'm a huge fan of Vietnamese cuisine and I have my favorite spots for a great bowl of pho, but Mopho is just not one of them. That said, the wings and the brussel sprouts are bangin'. So, when I go, those are always a must and now the only thing that I will order. 
For whatever reason, every single time I have had the pho here, I've been very disappointed and usually end up with a belly-ache an hour after. Don't know why, but because of it, I cannot recommend it. Besides that, I just don't think it's great pho. I could spend half the money somewhere else and walk away completely satisfied which isn't the case here. 
All in all, I think this is a good spot for a group of people to go, sit outside, and snack on some sprouts and wings while enjoying some decent brews and wine. But if you're looking for a great bowl of pho, I'd have to say to skip Mopho.
Excellent all the way around!! Service, food, ambience, all great. You can tell they put a lot of love into their food. The salsas are amazing too!!!

Lunch buffet is reasonably priced at $8.50+tax+tip but food is mediocre.  There was quite a variety but food was  insipid and not warm.  Mexican restaurant with colorful decorations but food quality leaves much to be desired.

Add me to the list of customers who thinks Gaudiello's Italian hoagies are a gastronomic work of art.  I was somewhat skeptical after reading all the five star reviews about how great the Italian subs are.  I had to find out for myself and I'm glad I did!

Very helpful staff. I asked for their recommendation since this was my first time. They started reading the entire menu and I quickly realized they are very proud of the food they serve. 

I had the Buffalo Pulled Chicken Sandwich and a couple of turkey ribs. The food is amazing.

The jambalaya risotto was one of the best things I had to eat while in New Orleans!!! The flavor is lights out and the poached eggs throws it over the top.

We liked it so much we went back for dinner the next night. They can be pricey but well worth it! We had the Cracklin' Pulled Pork nachos-amazing, the Marinated Blue Crab Claws-sauce is so rich, and the Shrimp n Grits- it was so amazing!

Drinks- we had the Bottomless Mimosas for brunch because that's to good to pass on! With dinner my wife had Ana amazing blueberry cocktail and I stuck with an Old Fashioned. 

Will definitely be returning to eat at Kingfish!
Waited for 2 hours for a pickup order (4 rolls) after being told 40 minutes. Sushi was mediocre.. the raw salmon in the rolls were horrible.

We were hungry for Pizza, thanks to fellow Yelpers, this place was awesome. We had approx a 20-30min wait but in Nashville, no problem, always something to keep you entertained. Service was great, polite staff. PIzza was just perfect, nice crust, delicious toppings.
Loved their food. The staff is very helpful and friendly. We had eaten Indian food but never ordered it so they helped us through the menu. Definitely recommend it! Delicious!

First off...not to bash any ones review of this place, but somebody obviously doesn't know wings. 
I've been here multiple times and I love the wings. More flavors then you can wrap your brain around. 
I've had the dirty nelly, spicy gar par, something medium and maple...and more. I've had atleast 10 flavors and loved all of them. The wing itself is actually large and in charge with enough meat on them to satisfy the price I paid for them. 
Sure the service isn't the greatest but i have water and wings and flat screen tvs to watch sports...so who needs someone asking "hows your meal today" every 3-4 minutes. Leave me alone with my face and fingers filled with tasty wing sauce.
I love this place and will continue to rant to everyone about how it is "the wing place" in Edmonton.
Love it!

Tonight was our first time here.  I had received a gift certificate, otherwise we would have never known about this restaurant.  First off, the salsa for the chips is the best we have had in Tucson. I ordered a Prickly Pear Margarita and it was delicious.  For dinner I had the chicken enchiladas, beans and rice.  I ordered one enchilada with the green chili and one with the red sauce, and liked the green chili one a little bit better.  My husband ordered the chicken fajitas with flour tortillas which are made in house. He said they were really good. For dessert we had the churros and it was the perfect way to end a delicious meal.  As my husband said, we have found a new Mexican Food Restaurant to take family and friends too! We are definitely looking forward to coming back!

Mia was an outstanding server. So friendly, attentive & had great recommendations. Would come back if for her service alone!  Thank you for great service and radiating positivity!  

The hostess on the other hand had us standing at the door to be seated while she took a personal phone call.  Though she had great coworkers who tried/did make up for her rudeness :)

Loved the skinny spicy marg. It was strong and delicious!

I LOVE LOVE LOVED this pizza. This is another place we have been meaning to try forever but it took until lockdown for us to order as takeout and I am so glad we did. The crust was cooked to perfect and it was spicy, sweet, tangy, and cheesy in all the right ways. Absolutely delicious and SO many to choose from we are sure to be ordering again and again till we sample all the options!

God is real. Journey down to the heart of Louisiana to enjoy this Mecca of a Louisiana kitchen. Yo C Baby, I am now speaking directly to you. They got drum legs for days. The breasts belong in the busty category and the tenders got that water. C, I will personally drive you down here just to get a plate. This is the pinnacle of life. Strong rec from the team.

I joined the waitlist 20 mins ago before checking in. I came to check in with the additional wait of 30-45 mins. 45 mins go by and we are still 4th in line. We decided to leave and go to Two Chicks. Squeeze In isn't squeezing in nothing!

Súper bueno, no tenías pensando comer aquí pero fue tremenda elección toda la comida estuvo fresca tienen buena atención u sobre todo limpieza y seguridad por el COVID 19 los pastelitos ummmmm no puede esperar regresar de Miami para comerlos!! Súper satisfecha

The pizza is way too pricey and bland, and it takes forever to just get a slice.  I used to be a huge fan of this place and was always excited to eat here, but then I had some truly excellent pizza in my food adventures.

I came to realize this is basically a greesy spoon pizza place with a ton of hype behind it, and it has an ultra premium price.  It's just not comparable to other similarly priced pizzas.  I would definitely put it in the same category as Dominos, Sabarros,  or Pizza Hut in terms of flavor.

This was a special day for me!  I just became a grandma again, so I decided to take my fiancée out for a special lunch to celebrate!  We decided to come to Columbia, after watching traveling Robert on You Tube.  We are RVers now and  like to sample the local restaurants.
Columbia is a beautiful Cuban Restaurant in Ybor City.  It's tastefully furnished with wood, terrazzo floors and Spanish tiles. There is a beautiful display of wines where we were seated.  Carol our server helped us pick out delicious things to eat. She brought us warm loaves of Cuban bread accompanied by whipped butter. We both started with the Gazpacho Andalusia.  I had a cup and he had a bowl of this creamy tomato and vegetable soup, topped with fresh cucumbers, peppers, tomatoes and onions!  Delish!  My date had the Empanadas de Piccadillo, made with ground beef, tomato, onion, raisins, garlic and olives wrapped in pastry.  They were moist and delicious.  I had the Eggplant Riojana, plantain crumb breaded eggplant with a rich sauce of tomatoes, garlic, capers, olives and red wine topped with a mozzarella type cheese called Tetilla Cheese.  It was more than ample and I gave my date half.
We finished our dinner with Cuban Coffee.  Carol made mine foamy, the way I like it, with dark espresso.
''Twas a must memorable and beautiful day.

Food-4 Stars
Service-5 Stars
Price-$$$
Atmosphere-4 Stars
The service was good and food was good. The drinks had two fruit flys in my glass . That comes from a dirty bar john taffer would say. Calet guys were best part of experience
Average food. Super pricey. Small portions. Go elsewhere.

From start to finish, it was an absolute delight!! The steak frites was amazing!! Every bite was full of flavor. The steak was filet and was so juicy and delicious. The fries are double fried and mixed together with the steak and dipping sauce (horseradish ) so yummy. For an entree I had the salmon and he had the scallops and pasta. Both dishes were so fresh!! You could taste the freshness in every bite. Nothing frozen here!! The salmon was crispy on the outside and so juicy on the inside. With fresh spinach and mushrooms over a blue cheese mash. Forget about it!! His scallops in a fresh cream sauce with homemade pasta. If you could even pick a winning dish, because everything was a 10, it would be the pan seared scallops. I cannot describe the flavor. The delicate seat and juicy scallops with the perfect seasoning. The homemade pasta was the cherry on top with cream sauce thy was full of flavor yet not heavy at all. The service was amazing and they space out apps and entrees perfectly. It is such a gem!! I cannot wait to go back!!

The manager Tony does not speak English very well and messed up my order. When they gave me the wrong pizza they tried to convince me that it was what I ordered. Even after talking to another manager, Gary, the establishment was unwilling to reconcile the order. The employees appear to be a ragtag group of miscreants who do not practice healthy sanitation habits. Beware Sal's Pizza!

Stopped in based on a recommendation of a local. It was worth it. The grits are to die for...there wasn't a huge line or wait either- which was a major issue with most of the places we stopped by during our stay. The Bloody Mary was good too!

We dined at Oak Steakhouse on Saturday evening, September 14th and just loved it!  The concierge at our hotel recommended it. 
The atmosphere was great-- it was warm yet airy with beautiful woodwork and lots of windows. 
We were so happy with our meals- we had the Ribeye Steak and New York Strip as well as the crispy brussel sprouts, aligot potatoes and roasted mushrooms and sautéed onions. All absolutely delicious... and the steaks were cooked perfectly. 
Our server Heather helped make it a perfect evening-- very professional, knowledgable and so pleasant!  Sam was the manager that evening and she stopped by several times just to make sure our experience was wonderful and it really was!

So they got knocked down in my book for actually charging me more to make my romaine/iceberg salad all romaine because romaine lettuce is more expensive.  Seriously!  I get all romaine salads at Wendy's for Pete's sake!  No nice restaurant should be serving iceberg. Ok my steak just came and it's ok. I've definitely had better (I had to ask for A1 which I don't do when i get a really good steak) I wouldn't say they verge on underdone with this one - needed to be pulled off a minute sooner I think. Id come here again, but now know to expect a basic decent steak. On a good note their asparagus was cooked perfect!  And their service was top notch!

First time here. We made a "to go" order. 14" Margherita Pizza, 20 Wings and Stuffed Mushrooms $45 The honey BBQ were good but the sweet mild were just dripping with grease. Mushrooms are good but a bit too much cream cheese, in my opinion. That's all you can taste. Now the pizza...TERRIBLE! I LOVE pizza and this has got to be the worst pizza I've ever had. The crust is so thin there is hardly anything to it! The edges were chewy and not edible. The worst part, it was drowning in olive oil! We ended up just throwing it away. I will not be back. There are tons of places in this area to get great wings, pizza and stuffed mushrooms. Schiappa's is NOT one of them!

This is not Pizza. Its cheese and sauce flavored bubblegum. That being said, I love it if its 2am and drunk. 

Slices are insanely large. You get your 2 bucks worth.

Its located by the sports bar in the Atlantis Casino, and it really is a Deli!! Matzo ball soup, huge pastrami sandwiches and entrees that come with soup or salad. The bowl of spicy pickled veggies as an opener were superb for me. Too spicy for my pal, though.

I thought the prices may be a little high, but the servings are enough for two, or a part 2 meal later. The corned beef and cabbage was juicy, a huge almost quarter of a cabbage, potatoes and carrots. So much meat, we ordered 2 slices of bread for $2 to make a late night sandwich.

I got the huge bowl of chili, so much! It was like a thinner chili, but not the soupy kind. It had pinto beans and fine hamburger. I was offered Tabasco and Tapatio, which brought the heat level up to my level. It wasn't salty or garlicky, at least for me.

Great server and hostesses. Everyone works well with each other.

extraordinarly bad value.  basically they have a 10000% markup.

everything about my angel hair pasta with alfredo and grilled chicken was 3rd Rate crap.
Yum. This was old school diner that was typical New Orleans. Great oysters, served many ways and GRILLED! Great cocktail sauce. They add Worcester sauce.  Great prices.

Honestly this is my new favorite spot. As a vegan i love finding places where i can have a great meal as well as my friends who are not vegan and this place is perfect. Their tofu is delicious. I went there once and was sold. Great quality food, fair price, and oh so tasty.  The girl at the front desk is so sweet and always so welcoming. Call ahead and your food will be ready by the time you get there every time. I have not had one single issue with Thai 5. Great job guys!
Very good sandwiches and friendly service.  Would go back again.  Everyone in the family found something to enjoy and I appreciate fresh brewed ice tea.

Just like its NY/NJ counterparts, it has old school video games and a nice selection of craft beer. Not as much variety, but still enough to keep beer drinkers happy.

It has a couple of newer games like TMNT and a shooting game, but still not enough for someone who grew up playing mostly 90 games like me. I would love to see Street Fighter, Pitfighter, Lethal Enforcers and especially 6-player X-Men (which alone would bring in as much money as any beer).

It also has a nice outdoor area which its siblings up I-95 lack.

LESS THAN IMPRESSED. We made reservations for Valentine's Day for dinner on OpenTable and received a call the following day saying the had a set menu and the dinner was $75 per person.  We then ordered a very nice red wine since we both chose the beef entre. The appetizer was Russian caviar served on a tiny crepe-like disc with a small dallop of crème fraiche (great concept, however the disc was cold?) Room temp would have been ideal.  My husband got the lobster bisque which he enjoyed and I had the featured salad - nothing exciting about my choice.  Then the entrees arrived - wow what a disappointment.  The beef (5 thin slices) was cooked as I ordered, covered in a mushroom gravy with three thinly sliced mushroom shavings, the potato side was completely inedible - thinly slice potatoes with a "window screen" texture, flavored with parmesan cheese (so the server told me) and the veggie side was nothing more than 2 tablespoons of shredded carrot and shredded zucchini.  The dessert was good. This was the most disappointing meal I have had in awhile - especially, especially for the price. Absolutely no plans to return.......ever.

are you in the mixx?  Well you should be...(I couldn't resist)

Mixx has been open for three weeks now and it is another success brought to you from Win Signature Restaurants (Teikoku, Mikado, Thai Pepper, Azie, Parkers Prime, etc..)

In an economy where small individual businesses are closing, Win keeps opening new restaurants...it is because they know what the people want...great food for cheap...

Mixx was designed to be light on your wallet...which I think will make it perfect since it is a stone's throw from Villanova's campus...but it is trendy and hip inside, so the mainliners will be at home too..

Mixx lets you know that even though you aren't going to be spending a lot, you still deserve to sit in a posh setting, be waited on by an extraordinary staff, and sample some yummy comfort foods...Who ever decorated Mixx somehow went into my brain and picked out all my favorite things...modern black chandeliers and black and white damask everywhere....the pictures on the website do not do it justice.

We had a good sampling of their offerings...the chop salad, ribs, and nachos were good...the fried chicken and cheesy mashed potatoes were great....we also tried their apple pie dessert which was warm and gooey....but what was by far the best was the chocolate souffle....

our main bartender was pretty attentive, but when he got distracted by another couple, in swooped Juan, another bartender who was good with the drinks, but better with the charm...which is the perfect combo for a bartender...i nominate him for mainline's bartender of the year...

I was there last night and I am going back on Tuesday for my birthday dinner...and then who knows how often I will go back...with Mixx's prices, I could dine there every night.

This restaurant just changed hands and is under a new name. It's definitely not as good looks like I need to find a new place to eat. If you're looking for an Indian restaurant start looking somewhere else

I think opening Stella was a brilliant idea for Stephen Starr, I think he just missed on a few things, mainly the pizza.  But before I write a review on the pizza, I would like to comment on the staff and atmosphere.

When walking into the newly renovated Cosi, you instantly feel as if you walked into one of your favorite low-scale restaurants when you were a kid.  Not to stay the decor is bad; it's actually the opposite.  For someone like myself, walking into an upscale restaurant that attempts to make you feel like you aren't dressed formal enough, can be intimidating.  Walking into Stella is a breath of fresh air, nothing special about it, humble and attractive.

Each time I have been here, the staff is always ready to greet you, super friendly, but not overbearing.  There has been one occasion on which our server, a male server, neglected our table for about 20 minutes, but compared to the other excellent service I have experienced, I guess everyone has their bad days, just like the rest of us.

I enjoy sitting at the bar, you get to watch the sous chefs work on each individual pizza as if it was their first day, trying to impress the chef.  It's quite amazing how carefully they handle each pizza.  I ordered a margarita pizza once without basil, and it came out with basil.  I watched as the sous chef caught this before it was brought over to me, and instead of taking off the basil, they prepared a new pizza.  The sous chef, not the server came over and apologized and within four minutes, I had my new pizza.

If you are lucky to go there without a crowd, your food comes out fast as lightning, as each pizza takes about five minutes, start to finish, due to the wood burning stove. If there is a crowd, you will wait a little longer, but if you make it known to your server that you are sharing everything that you ordered, it will come out one by one as it's done so you're not just sitting there waiting for everything.

Ok, the pizza.  I have tried the margarita, the four cheese, the pistachio, the picante, the clam, the pepperoni and the tartufo (truffle).  The crust is perfect and the amount of olive oil drizzled on the crust and the top of the pizza is perfect.  The flavors, need some work.  Painter has the four cheese and margarita down to a well executed science.  I am a huge fan of clam, however, this pizza was almost inedible.  The clams tasted like they came out of a spaghetti clam sauce jar - they were tuff and had a foul flavor.  It seems as if the clams were baked, which leaves them pretty tough, especially sitting on the line all day.  If Painter was able to figure out a way to steam the clams, maybe drizzle a spicy butter sauce of the pizza, I think it would rock my world.  

The picante pizza had a great flavor, a little spicy for me, but I can never handle heat.  I think one of the most exciting pizzas on the menu is the tartufo, the truffle pizza.  This has obviously truffles on top, and what most people find interesting is an over easy egg cooked in the middle.  The server comes to break the yolk and smear it over the pizza.  I was so excited for this pizza, but I was left only tasting egg - the rest of the flavors were lost.  The pepperoni was pleasant, but nothing too special about it.  The pistachio had too many onions which lost the pistachio taste.

The appetizers were good, I recommend the asparagus.  I also recommend the gelato.

I'd love to see Painter put out a mushroom or pineapple pizza.  I'd also like to try the other 4 pizza's on the menu.  Either way, I will make my way back soon!  All in all, a great place to take a date or the family for a smaller budget.  Hope this helps!
I had the rabbit and dumplings which was quite good. They also have a great brown ale.

I would like to start off with staying I am from the South. like born in the south and have eaten BBQ all my life. I am giving Fette Sau because this is the best in Philly but not best I have eaten overall. 

Ambience is awesome, you walk into a hipster vibe (next to Frankford Hall) and get into line where you tell the guy behind the glass case which meat you want where he proceeds to weigh the meat and serve it on a cafeteria plate. service was a little slow and there were only a few people in front of me. We ordered the brisket (a little fatty but the best thing we got), pulled pork was pretty dry, St Louis style ribs was pretty good but meat didnt fall off the bone like it should (could have stayed on the smoker for a few more hours). We were given free bread, pickles were not that great alongside the potatoes which tasted not very well cooked. Beans also had a lot of potential but werent cooked to completion as well. great place to go with a group, desserts looked delicious but i didnt have any. 

overall, 3 stars maybe 3 1/2...i think fette sau has some stuff to work on but yes, better than sweet lucys and percys.

Ok, so we made it on My Granddaughter's birthday! Confirmation is in order for cleanliness and customer service! Great! If you look for coupons and online deals, you will save considerably on the buffet. We ordered a veggie pizza fresh and they did it up for us. The dessert sticks and salad was fine. It wasn't gourmet but that's not what we came for! There are two TV rooms in the place; one for ESPN and sports, the other for Disney Channel! I enjoyed the cartoons this trip! :P As far as playing games, my 6 year old G-daughter did about $40 worth of game card damage. Sorry, she had a great time and that's all that mattered to me! We shall return. "Chuck's" is dead to me!

Talk about serendipity! 

We decided to walk from bourbon st to the Frenchmen st and got hungry/ needed a pit stop. When we put our names on the list the wait was 90mins long! The restrooms are tiny and if you're claustrophobic you won't be happy. After everyone took care of business 5 spots opened up at the bar. #blessed 

Everyone recommended their famous drink and friends said they approved it. 

The burger, OMG that burger! I am not big on red meat, but they didn't have much healthy options. The burger was so good, I may have waited those 90 mins if needed. 

#leslieapproved
I've been here several times and the food is ok but the service has always been terrible. Tonight, the food was mediocre and the service was terrible.  Not sure if I'll be back.

Upscale and nice place to grab a bite or some drinks.  I travel a lot and hate eating alone so usually sit at the bar though I don't drink.  I ordered a delicious wedge and a burger medium rare and cooked to perfection.  Homemade potato chips - think whole potato length potato chips.  Others ordered steaks and various types of martinis and mentioned how good it was.  Service was efficient so all the boxes were checked off that add up to a great meal.

Amazing! I am bicoastal from Houston and have been trying to find a restaurant to measure up to the great food in Texas! This is a great find and we enjoy eating here regularly. Food is fresh and so good! Love the ambiance inside. A hidden gem for sure. Picking up as we speak!
This is my favorite coffee shop. Nice variety, reasonable price, great coffee, and nice people work here!

It's quite a bummer to go into a restaurant that is all lit up outside, without any hours posted anywhere and they say, "uh, we closed 30 minutes ago". Do they just close whenever they feel like it? Do they leave the stupid light on outside so you pull out of traffic into their parking lot because they don't care how much of your time you blow on figuring out if they are open or not?!! Boo on you Cheddars!

My wife and I went with our 2 children and our 8 yrs old said it was a 5 star and I agree! We went at dinner time and got right in and had fast friendly service. We ate for half the price of a restaurant up the road and the food was also superior. We may go a 2nd time while we are here!
We arrived just before 9 after a long flight home.  They stayed open.  Made us feel welcome - it was our first visit since moving to Carp and can't wait to go back!

This has to be the most DISAPPOINTING EXCUSE FOR A RESTAURANT I have been to in Santa Barbara in the recent past. Firstly two Salmon Cakes with a few potato chips and a spoonful of very mediocre Slaw all on paper plates, together with two sodas,(served in the bottle without a glass or an offer of ice), costs almost $40.00 Yes, you heard it right $40.00. We also had to order this overpriced offering from a desk inside the kiosk and pay up front. The kiosk doubles as the kitchen with one table, as you can only really eat outside here and on the cheapest and most uncomfortable metal furniture available. Eventually someone came out with our food on paper plates together with our soda bottles and did not even offer us a glass, ice or any flatware because you have to go back into the kiosk to collect your own cheap plastic flatware from a table which also has paper napkins on it. The Salmon Cakes were just OK and the Slaw was not memorable and the $2.00 portion of potato chips, such as they were, came in a small brown bag. ZERO SERVICE, PATHETIC PRESENTATION and a complete RIP OFF, all on uncomfortable tables and chairs.. Clearly THIS RESTAURANT WILL NOT SURVIVE IN SANTA BARBARA, as the people here are very wise to being SCAMMED  and RIPPED OFF by places like this. REMEMBER THE KINGS NEW CLOTHES,,,,!!
DONT WASTE YOUR TIME OR YOUR MONEY ON THIS PLACE- THERE ARE MUCH BETTER PLACES IN THIS GREAT CITY- "YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED".

I can't give that thorough of a review, because they wouldn't even let us in, despite the fact that we were guests at a birthday party being held there.  There were two lines to get in.  We were told one of them was for people on the guest list, so we got in that line.  But they never let anyone in from that line.  When I went to talk to the bouncers about why they were only letting people in from one line, they instantly became hostile and unprofessional.  They said there was no difference between the lines (after we were told we were in the guest list line).  He wouldn't provide or attempt to find any explanation for why no one was being let in from the other line, refusing to talk to any of his coworkers or entertain our questions at all.  After waiting there for 20-30 minutes without anyone being let in from our line, which was allegedly the same as the other line from which people were being let in, we just left.

Clearly, I would discourage anyone from attending this club because of the rude and incompetent staff.  And I'd even more strongly caution against having any events there, because in cases like this, they won't even let your guests in!  What a waste of your money.

My wife and I came here on a recommendation. Once we were seated at our table, we were greeted by our waitress. We told her this was our first time dinning at this restaurant and asked if she could provided us with her personal recommendations. Once she went over her personal favorites, she continued with the most popular/frequently ordered dishes. My wife ordered the eggplant parmigiana with angle hair pasta, I ordered the pasta bolognese and we both split the Caesar salad. The food was absolutely amazing! I have dinned at many "Italian" restaurants and grow increasingly frustrated with the lack of authenticity. However, this is certainly not the case at La Locanda. We were both surprised at how authentic and fresh the food was. 
In addition to the fantastic meal, the service was the best that we have received in awhile. Looking forward to many more meals at La Locanda!
Went to eat tonight, and it looks like it has closed for good!  I hope not, but it looked that way to me.  Website is Down, too.

You have to be in the mood for this place. I vote LATE 1am - 2am ...ish... when you barely know what city you are in.

You will hate your life if you are there any earlier... Drinks can be cheap if you know what to order.

Don't expect to have any breathing room.  There are also signs for Watch Out for Pick Pockets (?) .. questionable.

I do LOVE the cards all over the wall from the people who forget to close their tabs.. CLASSIC COLLEGE.

I really wanted to love this place, it has a nice atmosphere and interesting food. I went with my co-workers, and I feel bad that I encouraged them to go with me. We were supposed to go to Su Xing instead. I ordered the shrimp tacos, yucca fries and a ginger ale. The best thing about my meal was the ginger ale. The fries were tasteless globs of fried potato the sauce is necessary, and the tacos had very little flavor. The worst thing is that one of my fries had a TOOTHPICK fried inside of it. Never again. As my co-worker put it "a costly mistake"

Went to Sassafras last Sunday for brunch. We got there a little after 10:30 am and were seated right away. By the time we left, the place was full of after-church diners.
I had a basic breakfast of eggs, grits and hot sausage (which they make in-house), and it was delicious. My partner had a hot sausage omelet that was excellent! Great food that seemed like home made, at a good price in a relaxing atmosphere.
The service was terrific. Our server, Akilah, was attentive and friendly.
Will definitely go back next time we're in the area.

I like Starbucks because of the consistency between stores all over the country. This one is close to my house and the drive thru is always fairly quick! I get the Strawberry Açaí refresher with lemonade instead of water  with a chocolate croissant!! Yum!! The guy working the drive thru this morning was super friendly and upbeat, which really gave a great start to my day!

Worst Experience! Whiskeys Joe's is not worth it. It was my first time entering this grill & bar, and I was extremely disappointed. The photos online do not justify what you actually eat or drink in person. The bartenders in the big tiki hut outside by the beach are rude and have no structure of order during these Covid times. There is no social distancing and majority of people weren't wearing masks waiting in line. The drinks are poorly done & tasted like outdated liquor, unfortunately I got sick. I do not recommend people to come here it literally smells like throw up! It is way too confusing for anyone to enjoy anything.

I was first introduced to The Corner through a Yelp Elite event and I told myself I had to come back. Funny enough I went back two days in a row.

Saturday I came to The Corner and got to experience the ambience of a notable Bluegrass band playing in the lower level of the establishment. It was a great time. Even though the place was packed service was timely and the servers were friendly.

I turned around and came back on Sunday to experience the brunch which was very good and again the service was great. I ordered the shrimp and red pepper grits with a side of bacon and the hibiscus mimosa. Everything was delicious, however, there wasn't as much kick to the grits as I would've expected and they were a bit stiff. The thickness of the bacon was very appreciated and the hibiscus mimosa was refreshing. 

I can't wait to try other things on the menu.

We went after a lot of walking and it was beautiful!! The design of the restaurant created an incredible scene and the food was just as great. From getting seated, to getting our food it didn't take long at all. We had the Apple Pie French Toast, a berry french toast, apple crepes, and sausage and biscuits. Everyone in my family loved it and would definitely go back!
Unbelievable seafood paella! My wife and I have been coming here for years. One of our favorites.

A unique English pub with excellent food and atmosphere.
Lots of beer choices on tap. My favorite was Guinness.
The fish and chips were truly exceptional and I highly recommend it. The batter was light with perfect seasoning and not a bit oily. The fish was perfectly deboned and perfectly cooked.
The bangers and mash were very satisfying and enjoyable.
Portions are very generous.
Always tasty boiled seafood ready to go. They have a whole kitchen that cooks poboys, chicken, seafood, you name it! Right off the highway and easy to get to.

The food is pretty good but service is terrible.  We don't have a waiter but "a team" that collectively ignores us.  When we compliant to lead waiter he blames on managements distribution of waiters.  The food is good but not worth poor service

If you're looking for mediocre elementary school food at late night gouged prices, all while getting treated unwelcome and being made fun of by the workers, than look no further you have found your place. i came here on behalf of my mom since she lives near and was the only place with "plate food" open. seemed fine at first but once ordering, one word of what i ordered came out with a spanish accent and the woman behind the register looks at me and blatantly says "wow he only speaks spanish when it's beneficial to himself" and the worker and her laugh at me. i'm not 100% comfortable with speaking spanish in front of people who aren't my family or in an emergency. She made me upset and uncomfortable to where i didn't want to eat my food in the restaurant and to end on a hint of irony, her english was not much better than my spanish so i'm not sure what point she was trying to make. If you come here and look like you don't speak spanish, keep an ear open. you might end up being the topic of conversation. :)

Mediocre food mediocre service.

Been here several times but it just gets worse and worse.   

And to make matters worse when they answer the phone they say  "would you like to hear our specials?"

Give them a call and say no and they will have no idea what to say!!!

My sister and I were very hungry and since we were shopping at the mall I recommended the Yard House since I had eaten there once before and the food was ok.  Very nice inside but it was the worst cheeseburger I have ever had. We decided to split one because we always split a meal when eating out. We ordered their cheeseburger that had truffle cheese and ordered it medium with sweet potato fries. When our waiter brought the food it was very small and was raw in the middle. The fries were over cooked. When I lifted the whole wheat bread you could not see any cheese. There was no lettuce or tomatoes with it. It also came with 3 little round pickles, the kind you would find on a  Mc Donald's hamburger.  We should have returned the food so they could fix it but since we are both diabetics we needed to eat.  There was no taste, undercooked and very small for the price of $15.00 with tax. We drank water. I did report the dissatisfaction to the waiter so that the manager would be aware that their food was coming out like that. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone.  I was embarrassed because I am the one that recommended the place.
I have been here for lunch several times. The food is delicious and so ridiculously cheap, I want to tell the owner to raise the prices so he can stay in business!!!
Wow..just had the best sushi in town. Had sushi at other places. But this is the best. Fresh and clean tasting. Friendly server and owner. Will be back for sure!!

I was surprised to see such low reviews...but after eating here three to four times I have lost interest in going back...

My friend and I witnessed quite a bit of unprofessional behavior by the general manager, at least that's who I believe it was. She greeted me at the podium and seemed very unimpressed and did not attempt to smile (everyone has those days). When I asked for a booth she looked quite annoyed. Later that evening her and other staff members were talking crap loudly in front of several tables and our waitress had to shush them and apologized to everyone. Yikes...

As for the food, everything was pretty good minus the dish I ordered. My friend ordered steak and lobster ravioli. The steak was juicy and seasoned well but he said the ravioli seemed to be dry on one side and moist on the other side.

I told the waitress that my meal was dry and overlooked. It legit looked like a TV dinner (image attached). Our waitress took it back and we could hear her telling the chef everything... other than that, our waitress was sweet and recommended a good dessert.

Getting up, the same woman at the podium followed behind us and announced that we had left and our table would be open. Just... idk...the overall experience made me take note of too many unprofessional moments... behind the scenes should not affect someone at their table..

That said, I cannot give this location 1 star nor 5. I think 2-3 is fair.

Traditional luxury hotel with impeccable everything. The service, rooms, food, bar, location are all five star.  And the club-level accommodations and perks are even better.  Take your wife here for an anniversary trip and book a club level room facing the river.

We arrived at the Lobby bar at around 10:30PM, delighted by the fancy cars at the valet, and decor unlike anything else in Edmonton. That's where the fun stopped, I had been invited to an opening party for a bar called the Alchemist earlier in the month, but was not able to make it. Assuming that The Alchemist would be open we decided to try it out, it was not. Upon arrival we are were greeted to a packed lobby, and met our first, and unknowingly best, manager of the night Julian. He informed us that there was no open tables but if we sat at the bar height table, we could enjoy our night and watch for one to open up, which we did. After 20 minuets, an order for 2 bottle of wines, and a special order for champagne not on their menu, we were set. Another 10 or so minutes go by and we see a group getting up from a near by table in the corner and we rush to grab it. All of our drinks are brought over and things are great, soon we are met with a server yelling "Get up, that table is only for our best customer and it is reserved 24-7. You don't belong here and you need to move immediately." Not the best way to be greeted by a server, obviously if asked nicely we would have understood and moved, but this lady had just screamed at us in a crowed restaurant drawing attention from everyone around us. She brought a manager over and we were promised a new table if we moved this instant. What we were brought to was a small bench by the front door, without our bottle of wine and no one offering to bring our $400 in drinks over. Julien spotted us and realized something was wrong. I pulled him to the side and explained the situation and he was very apologetic and almost immediately set us up with a new table in the center of the floor, just amazing. I had expressed my concern about our wine sitting out of our site for 20 minuets and he promptly brought us a new bottle and took care of our whole situation for the rest of our evening. As someone who has been in the restaurant consulting and management profession for over 10 years, I would recommend our sever and the manager on duty, Julien, with all of our compliments. They truly made our experience memorable; but the other sever who yelled at us obviously does not fit into the upscale brand or atmosphere that the JW Marriot or Braven fits into, very disappointing and almost experience ruining.

We ordered Saturday lunch for the studio from Wrap It Up and they did not disappoint. I myself had the falafel wrap... twas amazing! Also ordered the sampler tray which was also glorious. The flavors were on point. Everyone at the studio was thoroughly impressed as well and it's hard to please a bunch of tattoo artists, hahaha. The service was great, we phoned in a large order and it was done when they said it would be and everything came back fresh and awesome. We will definitely make this a frequent flyer in our Saturday rotation.

I really want to love this place but I'm still waiting for more.

I've been here 3 times so far and have found the following:

Pros:
-daily pierogis are great, they do not disappoint
-gnocchi basket is also a tasty snack
-other entrees that we've tried (most of them) are good but not particularly memorable
-BYOB is a plus 

Cons:
-Menu is very limited & does not change - offering daily specials or switching up the menu frequently would encourage us to try this place more.  Otherwise, our choice is to order the same 3 items every time we dine.
-Price always seems to be a bit too high considering there's no alcohol included & we often leave feeling a bit hungry (typically $120+ for 2 people)

Overall the experience is not bad but also not good enough to return.  For the cost we will often choose another restaurant which offers a bit more.

Hoping to see the restaurant evolve and we would love to try again :)
Great friendly service. Food is okay. French fries are fresh cut. Onion rings and fried pickles have a thick batter coating. Fish tacos were not great. Other sandwiches looked pretty good.

What a great little restaurant here and at the other locations as well.  Everyone is always friendly and their portions aim to please!  The Monte Cristo is one of the best I've ever had And I always have to take half of it home.  Their skillets or scrambles are huge and they have a great assorted menu that you won't find at the average joe breakfast joint. They make a killer pumpkin pancake in season And have many substitute choices for sides. I love their sourdough toast and they always give you extra for no charge. Great food,  portions and menu!

The pizza is really horrible here.. I don't know anyone who thinks this place has the best pizza but it is cheap and my kids love it. Their salads are just simply horrible but the desert pizza may be worth the trip;-)

Came here during a bachelorette party for some lunch. We went to the second floor and sat down and listened to the awesome live music that was happening at the time! 

We ordered some beers and fried pickles to start. There were 8 of us and more than enough for all of us to have plenty of fried pickles so that was great!
Not all of us ordered lunch but those who did got some wraps and I got a salad.

The food was pretty average nothing over the top stuck out but it was very good and the overall experience was definitely worth stopping by! 

Definitely somewhere you should come if you're visiting Nashville even if you're not coming for food, it's awesome how there's live music on the different levels and a great place to just take it all in! Plus the windows give you a nice view of broadway so you can take it all in!

The view is wonderful, but the restaurant is maybe a few steps above Olive Garden, which may be fine for the tourists but unimpressive, especially given the price. The service was similarly disappointing. We did not stay to enjoy dessert.

Went last night for New Year's Day because paddy whacks was crowded beyond belief. Cavs wasn't too bad, def crowded but could still move and get a drink. Bartenders were nice and quick. We ordered food which was the highlight of my night and just what I needed - fried pickles (AMAZING), chicken fingers and a pretzel with great dips! The food was surprisingly so amazing. Would def go back one night for dinner.

I was very happy to FINALLY be able to try Vui's Kitchen!  I had their pork belly bao buns ($6) and the pho ($11).  I did feel like the buns were a bit pricy for the amount you get, but they're very tasty.  The pho was delicious as well, though a bit heavy on the jalapeno seeds.  I prefer a bit less spice so you can add sriracha or whatever to taste based on your preference.  It was really tasty, but I think I prefer my go-to spot in Cool Springs a bit more.  I won't hesitate to come back if my friends want to go!

Ate at BGood for the first time with my family. Menu selection is about the right size. Good kid options too. The person taking our order was unsure of a few things and instead of turning around and looking at the menu or asking she kinda blew us off. It took foreeeeever to get our food, almost 40 minutes, and they were not that busy. I had the El Guapo and it wasn't bad. I got the fries and I had to remind them twice. The best thing going for them is the all natural soda fountain. It won't be at the top of our list anytime soon.
Absolutely love this place! Have been eating here since they opened and have yet to be disappointed. They now have soy bean wraps for their sushi if you request it!

I knew when this placed opened a few years ago it would be a diamond in the rough. Located in a old strip center that is highly overlooked. I waited wayyyyy to long to finally try it out. But I can officially say this place is f$&@#% AMAZING! Only tried a few things such as the chicken kabab, chicken Bahari kabab and chicken tikka masala. All great! I pretty much threatened my boyfriend for the last piece of the bahari chicken kabab. I have never been to the actual location as I always send my live in postmates to go get it. But my postmaster, I mean boyfriend, said the place is clean, basic and the people have always been friendly. He also said both times he's gone, the front has been flooded with people waiting for take out (always a good sign). I urge you to not make the same mistake I made by waiting to try this place out!

1 chicken bacon quesadilla (green chili, Mexican creme, bacon). 1 al pastor quesadilla. They each came with a bean soft shell taco. The flour tortillas are home made & you can definitely tell! Yum! This place is a great hole in the wall with awesome food, great people, great service!
The bean tacos are very good too.

We live close and we were exited to try it out!! First, let me tell you how nice the owners and servers are! Second. Complimentary fried bananas for all at the end of the meal. Yay! And yum! They came with a side of honey to drizzle over them. 
We started the meal with fresh spring rolls and pot stickers. Love Thai pot stickers that come with a side of panang sauce. They were excellent. The fresh spring rolls were good, but I think I prefer Vietnamese spring rolls textures a bit more. 
My friend ordered the Tom Yum noodle soup. She's adventurous. It had shrimp, squid and fish balls in it. She liked it and there was plenty for leftovers. I had the chicken panang curry. Spice level 2. Their panang sauce was wonderful! The green beans and carrots were cooked yet still crisp. I also had enough for leftovers. 
We were talking with some other folks in the restaurant and they had just ordered the Mango with Sticky Rice and he let us each have a bite! That's a must for the next visit. 
The location is in a strip mall so its nothing fancy. The prices are reasonable as well. 
We will be visiting again for either dine in or take out.

I have only visited Noi's once and had a pleasant experience. The staff was very nice, but don't be surprised if your server is a child! It is definitely a small, family business. I ordered the small chicken green curry which was the perfect size for me. It was loaded with fresh veggies and good flavor. I also tried the tom kha and spring rolls which were also good. I couldn't leave without dessert (a cupcake) which was also wonderful. I have had better Thai food in the area, but this is one of my new favorites. I will be back!
Great service, awesome margaritas and amazing Tex/Mex! I loved my Jerk Chicken Burrito.

I learned a very important lesson: if someone says "go to this place for breakfast" do NOT go there for lunch first.  Disappointment is the most likely outcome.  I'll sum it up this way:

Lunch at Blue Willow = meh.

Breakfast (or brunch) at Blue Willow = Huzzah!

No more need be said about the lunch.  It's just not worth it.  But the breakfasts they have here are to die for.  Eggs benedict like I've never had before.  Some of the best chorizo I've ever had in an omelet.  And (maybe I was just caffeine starved that time) really good coffee.  The last point being something I feel breakfast joints overlook all too often.

And it helps that the shop is a cute little place too.  It's fun.  Enjoyable to poke around either while you wait for a seat or afterwards when you're paying for a great meal.
Nice service and fresh ingredients. A friend recommended the tinga tacos and they didn't disappoint. I'll be back.

This is a great example of a seafood store. 
The staff is very knowledgeable and very helpful. 

They have a nice selection of fish and other seafood. 

They crab cakes are very good. If you like crab cakes then try these. 

They can be a little pricey but I have never been disappointed.

I have been a long time customer here. The food is always very good. I have always been able to accept the disgruntled service from the employees because I knew the end result would be positive. Unfortunately, I was not available to pick my order last week and my wife and son had to go in my place. They were met with the usual poor customer service that has been the reason why I always go to pick up. Again, the food was excellent but I will have to find a new location because of the typical anti-female, anti-children, anti-customer service that is the (poor) standard at Roy Tweedy's. The place where they butcher customer service.

Its soooo close to home and we soooo want it to be good, but our hopes and reality never seem to click.  Beer is beer, you pour we drink, but you gotta do something about the food, please try and do something about the food.

I don't know why I come to this Del Taco. The workers aren't friendly and they rarely get my order right. 

I ordered a Macho Nachos with no beans and extra cheese and a Deluxe Chili Cheese Fries. The nachos were correct, but the fries were not. Since I went through the drive-thru, I had to park and go back inside to get the order corrected. The counter attendant was nice, but obviously new. The drive-thru attendant was snippy and told me, "There aren't any beans on the fries." She rang my order correctly, but I didn't ASK for no beans on the fries. I asked for no beans on the nachos. The manager was working in the back, making the food, and she was polite and offered to make a whole new order of the fries (they were missing the tomatoes, onions and sour cream). I assured her that I didn't need a whole new order, just to add the stuff on that I had paid for. 

I'd really like to give two stars to this restaurant just for the manager's service. But the fact that the drive-thru attendant was so rude and snippy makes me unable to give an extra star. I will be visiting the location on Eagle in Meridian, even though it's farther away and more difficult to get in and out of.

Amazing family owned business! We've been going there since we were kids for about 25 years. The house special is our go to every time. We've never once been disappointed. The service and food is constantly exceptional. We love this place and the family that runs it.

Had a really good experience at brunch. There was about a 15 minute wait and only took a few minutes finding a parking space. First they sat us at a high top that was partially in the sun, but as soon as one was open in the shade, we moved to it. My daughter had the pancakes and breakfast potatoes and I had the French toast with strawberries and potatoes. The food was really awesome. I thought that the syrup could have been thicker, but it had a good taste. They provided Heinz ketchup which is always appreciated.  The service was also wonderful. All around good experience!

So much fun! My friend and i were the first bar customers since the shut down.  The food was amazing.  The portion sizes excellent. 
The bartender,  "Susan" was classy and sassy!! Thanks for a fun visit!!!

Not very good.  Pizza was just ok and the lasagna was disgusting.  There are too many great New Orleans pizza options out there to choose this product.  Take a look at Slice, Pizzicare, Naked Pizza, or Reginellis if you want good pizza.

Super friendly service ! 
Food was good & they accommodated my order with ease ! Fast & clean place

Went here last night for a late dinner. Service was very slow. Had to keep asking the hostess to grab our waitress. I asked for my steak well done no pink it came out medium rare. I had them cook it again and still pink. Steak was flavorful but very rubbery. My daughter ordered the chicken fingers. They looked great but she wouldn't eat them, so I tried them and they were very rubbery as well. Will not be coming back. If you're visiting the city for the first time or don't come often I wouldn't recommend this place. I am always in philly and there are many good restaurants so don't waste your time at this one.

Loved this placce when it first opened ... they had a soup and small Greek salad that was perfect....then  they recently cut the portion in half on the salad, for the same price.  I didn't find out untIl I got home, and didn't have enough to eat!  Poor form
Everytime I have been here the food and drinks have been great. The service is always good. The food is just a little to pricey.

Food was fresh and delicious.  Place was nice and clean.  The reason for the 3 stars is because we went there with a coupon.  The very personal and helpful cashier did not know how to apply the coupon to our order so he called the manager or owner, who does not speak English, but was well aware that our $5 off coupon was valid.  First he implied that he wasn't going to honor the coupon (it was like he had no idea it existed), when I questioned him, he said indicated to the cashier to take $3 off because they "don't have a button for $5 off" and walks away.  Even the cashier was dumbstruck.  So yeah, eat there because the food is great, but don't expect them to honor a coupon.

My beau and I decided we were in the mood for ice cream and decided to give this place a try.  While the portions are huge, the ice cream wasn't amazing.  We both agreed we would rather have better ice cream and less of it. We are sticking with gibbys as our local fave.
Expect to be waited on the weekend but it's worth waiting. Bring champagne too.  Order anything you want on the menu.  So good. I think Im going to go back this week.

Came here tonight with a party of 4 and enjoyed several items off the menu. The drinks were exceptional- the industry sour was a favorite of the group. 

Stand outs were also the pimento cheese, duck liver mousse, manhatten drink, hanger steak, Brussel sprouts, chicken was great and largest portion of all dishes. 

1 beef with this place: the charcuterie tray didn't have any cheese! What's up with that?? Beyond that all good!

Went there one time drunk off my ass with some friends. Hipster Paradise. $5 bottled beer. I asked the bartender if the place was called "Rabbit Pig" because the pretenious prick owners thought it would be cool to not have a name anywhere on the building. The bartender then asked us to leave. Place sucks.

Amazing food. Our go to place for take out. We've tried others in the area but nothing comes close to the flavors and freshness.
Dumplings, sesame chicken, pineapple rice, etc all amazing !!

The fried chicken was good, but the corn and crab bisque was a bowl of cream. There were no pieces of crab or corn. The chicken gumbo was so-so and had chicken bones in it. The red beans and rice were mushy. 

The floor in the restaurant was extremely sticky.

Ehhh no.... this is the first time visiting New Orleans and this place wasn't great. I thought getting creole and Cajun food meant tons of flavor and some spice. This place was not it. Service was great, portion size was great and we were seated immediately which was a plus but the food was way to bland. Don't recommend it at all.
One of our favorite places to come back to for breakfast / brunch. Good food, friendly staff, and great little neighborhood away from the craziness of the French Quarter.
Been going to Jerry's since it opened. Great breakfast. Great service. Love those biscuits and gravy.

We love this place. The food has been consistently delicious and we love that is has the casual diner atmosphere with a retro feel. Love that the menu has diner staples and also more creative items, too. Menu descriptions are fun to read. Bar (featuring only Dogfish Head beers I might add, nice touch) an added bonus!

Went with a private group of 40. Service was painfully slow, meals were mediocre at best. We had a limited menu to select from and no preference options on how food was cooked. My fish was terrible, flavorless and over cooked. I didn't hear anyone give a complement to anything we were served. Disappointing. 

It may have just been a result on the kitchens inability to serve a large group all at once.

I ate here for lunch, and the food and the service were excellent. The helpful and friendly waitress steered us to some excellent choices for a heavy appetizer lunch. Our table enjoyed turtle soup, chargrilled oysters, barbecue shrimp, and crab cakes followed by a creme brulee dessert.

The crab cakes were a tough sell to someone coming from Maryland, the home of blue crabs, but the waitress said we couldn't miss them. She was right, they were excellent. They are different from Maryland crab cakes, but very tasty, and served with a crawfish and mushroom cream sauce. 

The oysters were a real stand-out, and this is coming from someone who isn't an oyster fan.

The turtle soup is definitely worth a try. It's tangy and sweet, and the meat is really good.

The creme brulee was served cold, which isn't my favorite way of eating it, but it had a nice lightly-burnt sugar taste to it.

I would be happy to return.

First of all I want to say that I do not consider this a bad place, for all of you that think three-star ratings mean "hated it."

I am also quite conscious of the fact that I would be viewed by many as a poop for criticizing an all-vegan coffeehouse for not having any dairy whatsoever.  One could have a valid argument in saying this is like criticizing Chanel for not carrying cheap handbags, i.e. "it's just not what they do."

Nonetheless I would humbly suggest to the folks at Grindcore that having some non-vegan options would expand their customer base.  It's possible that's not what they're interested in and maybe the business serves a dual purpose as some sort of vegan activist community hub.  At the end of the day, though, everyone has to make a living and I just can't deal with soy lattes.  Even B2 is "too vegan" for me, but I know that I can at least go there and put cream in my coffee.  Why not have some locally-sourced, organic milk and other dairy around?  Well whatever, Grindcore, go on with your bad selves.

There is certainly a preponderance of dreadlocks here but I found the atmosphere to be welcoming.  Friendly baristas.  I guess I wasn't even thinking about how my latte was obviously going to have soymilk in it when I ordered it.  For what it was it was alright, but not as good as a normal latte.  I also ordered a peanut butter brownie, which was sweet in kind of an unnatural way and the texture of the thing was a little "off."  I sampled my boyfriend's bagel with sundried tomato "cream cheese."  This is a product that lends itself to veganization more easily and wasn't too bad.

The total of my items came to $7.02 and I paid with a $10.  When this sort of thing happens at coffeeshops usually they give you the penny or two, but not here.  I received exactly $2.98 in change.  Again maybe this is a thing I can't strictly criticize them for but I was annoyed to receive all that change.

If I were a vegan punk activist I'd happily pedal there on my bike, ignoring any stop signs that might get between me and my soy.  But since I'm not I'll respectfully stay away for the most part.

Went here for drinks and appetizers and then back for brunch. They are very gluten free friendly which was the first reason we stopped, but my non gf friends wanted to come back for brunch because it was so good! They have great drinks and the service was great. Highly recommend the fried tomatoes (gluten free) and the pulled pork plate for breakfast (gluten free).
The Cubano is fantastic.   Smoky, crunchy and spicy.  And one of the best in NOLA.  A must visit every time.

Portions were HUGE! I ordered the antipasto salad for $7.95 and barely made a dent. Husband got the baked ziti (all 3 of us could have shared) and little guy got the kids spaghetti.

My biggest complaint is there was nothing I saw on the menu (except the side salad) that was not butter soaked, cheese topped, or fried. The salad was nice, but it had about 2 C of cheese on top.

I left without receiving any service.  For some reason I was sat at a table for 6 (I was by myself but didn't want to sit at the bar).  Saw a server visit  a couple tables near me over the period of several minutes but never acknowledged me.  There were 4 girls standing around at the front door doing nothing.  Disappointing since I was really craving the Buffalo chicken salad.
Hey they closed! I just ate there a few weeks ago. Granted it was a shell of it's former self but wow, cant believe it's gone.

First time here last night. Came around 11-11:30 and it was a light crowd. Nice mood lighting with candles lit throughout the bar. The food is unbelievably good. If you're a bacon fan, you have to try the bacon fat popcorn. Their mac & cheese is amazing, too. The location is just a few blocks from city hall in center city, but not the nicest part of town.
Yum! Hit the spot for an authentic Greek lunch at a reasonable price! Delicious green salad with Gyro platter and stuffed Greek leaves.
Our family likes going to Cinder Bar. The atmosphere is fun, the craft beer menu is great but their menu is lacking. If they had better food, it would definitely be a 5 star restaurant.

Why do I even write a review for a chain fast food restaurant? 

Luckily, for them, I checked in on Yelp (yes, I was clearly drunk since I checked into a fast food restaurant) and managed to remember a small glitch in my weekday festivity. 

When I asked the manager (who was working at the register) for my Frosty, he said, "that's not my job."

Do not deny a drunk girl her Frosty.

Imagine;

You got out late because of whatever reason. It's 1 am, and you know most places close in an hour or two, Not Richeez! 5 am liqour license! great food till 3!  Theres a coat check on the weekend. Dress code is no hats, casual. As soon as it hits 3 am you can expect a bunch of fresh faces to pour in. The bartenders work hard, and theres a good amount of security, multiple big guys, not just one.

Terrific hole in the wall taco joint.   I'm tired of these pseudo-fancy taquerias that think if they have hardwood floors and chevre cheese on their menu that they can charge $4 for a tiny taco.   When I get tacos, I'm not looking for arugula.   Give me goat.  Give me tongue.   Give me tripe.   For under $3.  That's exactly what this place does.   My wife and I had dinner here for $20...tax and tip included.   Can't beat that.

I would advise against getting their quest fundido, though.  It's just microwaved shredded cheese.   I do highly recommend the chips and salsa though.   It comes with green tomatillo salsa, tomato salsa and pico de gallo.

Fresh, delicious, fast and friendly. This is my first time ordering from Poke Bros, I'm a grubhub driver and I've picked up orders all the time, they are always nice and welcoming and decided to give them a try tonight . I ordered online and my order was ready when they said it would be. Made it home and opened the container and was pleasantly surprised on the amount of food given. I ordered a create your own bowl filled with sushi rice,spicy salmon, edamame, the spicy aioli and a few other fixings. It was simply delicious, I'm a sushi girl and this hit the spot like my favorite roll would. I had so much I couldn't finish it all and now I have leftovers for tomorrow. I definitely will be back, looking forward to trying the other bowls. Great price for the fresh quality ingredients and the amount of food given.

CJ Muggs is a pretty good bar and grill located in downtown Clayton. There's a lot of TVs showing sports and a full bar. The menu carries a wide variety including standard bar fare, burgers, sandwiches, and specialty entrees. I've been here twice. The first time was a long time ago and I remember I had a burger that wasn't bad. The other night I came with a large work group and I had the shrimp and grits. It wasn't bad but I've had better, granted, CJ Muggs is not a Cajun restaurant so it was a worthy attempt. Our group was able to reserve a large party room which was secluded from the rest of the restaurant, which was nice. If you're in the downtown Clayton area, you should consider CJ Muggs for your next casual outing.

They  made us wait for 2 hours. we kept asking every 15 min and they would say it's nearly ready. they took 1 hour to give us a table. once we got inside we saw that there were many tables but they were mismanaging the seating. they didn't know how to prioritize between those who placed a takeout and those who were waiting as it was quite unfair. The communication was lacking. overall a terrible experience

Brats and beer: one of the greatest pairs in the world. At Brat Haus it's kind of a weird place they just tell you to sit wherever you want. I'm not sure exactly how it works or if it works often enough but the servers do find you and they do take your order.

The brat was delicious, but I don't have the credentials to say whether or not it was legit. But it felt legit. The garlic fries were good, I enjoy the cheese and extra garlic. My only complaint was the garlic distribution was no bueno. Too much garlic at the end meant the last of the fries were difficult to eat. Beer helps though. 

Brat Haus was cool but it didn't blow me away. I would say this is a better place to drink than to eat.

Been here twice for lunch.  Both times shared the Blue Duck fries, which are very delicious, though the cheese could be more flavorful (maybe a sharp cheese mixed in) and the fries less greasy.  There's a puddle in the bottom of the tray when they're done.  The flavored teas and lemonades are good.  The first sandwich I had was the fried chicken sandwich.  The chicken, while it tasted good, wasn't cooked well.  It was hard on the end that was thin and not cooked the whole way on the thick end, so maybe trimming the pieces to be more uniform would help. The big chunks of hard red cabbage were impossible to eat. A pickled cabbage slaw that has finer pieces would be a lot better.  The second sandwich I had was the portobella sandwich.  Again, it tasted really good but the execution was not so good.  It was difficult to eat and just made a mess.  Sprinkling corn and black beans all over a sandwich just leads to them all falling out.  There's no friction on the smooth mushroom, so everything basically just squeezes out when you try to bite in to it.  The greens, which were listed on the menu as kale but seemed to be broccoli rabe, were burned and had stalk material which was sort of tough.  I assume they were sauteed rather than braised as the menu stated, because they were blackened and crispy in parts.

The place has a nice, clean, country decor.  But, it's crazy loud in there.  The (I presume) manager that stopped by said after we mentioned that that they're adding carpet to the underside of the tables and counters so hopefully that will help.  It wasn't even full and was too loud...I can't imagine a full, BYO dinner night.

Overall, pretty good and definitely a good addition to an area that has next to nothing for decent food options that aren't chains or bar food.  I'll definitely go back and hopefully get there for dinner some time.

Do you have that "go-to" place?  

You know what I mean, when you and your significant other are both asking each other, "What do you feel like eating tonight?"  You might deliberate the question for 5 minutes or 50 minutes... the odd thing is, you know that when this dance starts, the conclusion is inevitable...  It's almost a compulsion, a gravity well inexorably pulling you in.  You're almost certain to eat at that 1 spot, your "go-to" place.  

Where do you want to eat when you've been away from home for a long time? Eating at your "go-to" place is a part of the process of getting comfortable and truly "feeling" like you're back home - a lot like sleeping in your own bed.  

For my wife and I, Asuka has become our "go-to" place.  Enough philosophizing, let's get to the review!

Sushi: High quality & very good value.

Chinese dishes:  Although their Chinese dishes may be critiqued for being less than "authentic", my Chinese wife looks forward to bringing her parents to Asuka - high praise indeed.   See the photo of the chicken with vegetables lunch special; it includes egg roll, fried rice, and a main dish comprised of chicken (lean, juicy, & boneless) stir-fried with an abundance of assorted fresh vegetables (carrot, broccoli, sweet peas, some root, mini-corn, etc.).  Tip: I sometimes ask for them to go light on the sauce - that really depends upon whether you like to use the dish's sauce to season your rice. 

Ambiance: A relaxed Asian café.  

Service: How & when did the hostess start greeting us by name?   Table service is efficient and helpful; if you need something, don't be shy about asking.  

Top Tips:
#1 Takeout!  This place is awesome for takeout and they do a lot of it - both Chinese and sushi.
#2 Lunch specials = tremendous value.
#3 Reservations.  The dining area is relatively small, so you are encouraged to make a reservation.
#4 BYOB

I originally gave this place 4*.  I really liked it but wondered if it had that "something special" to make it worthy of a 5* rating.  Over time I've come to realize that Asuka has evolved into our "go-to" place because of a large number of little things - all of which make Asuka a very special place.

Sigh, look. I'm not a whiner. The food is fine, though unremarkable. I've been here several times and the service has been slow but friendly and I've been ok with it. But last Friday evening, I popped in for a quick bite an hour before another appointment in the neighborhood. I just wanted a quick bagel and some coffee. The cafe wasn't busy - maybe 10 people altogether. Food trrrrriiiiiicccckled out of the kitchen at the rate of one dish every 5-7 minutes. After waiting 35 minutes for my bagel, I went to the counter to inquire as I was running out of time. The woman at the counter was just plain mean and snooty about my question, "Yes, I KNOW you've been waiting a half hour but you can see there were MANY tickets ahead of you". When I first arrived, I watched a man wait 15 minutes for a cup of coffee because she had to brew another pot. (?!? for realsies?). I like this place and being a very long-time super vegan, I was so thrilled to have it as an option. But this kind of casual attitude towards customers makes the shop feel like someone's hobby instead of something to be taken seriously.

We visited the "Thirsty Marlin" based on advice from a native Floridian (yes, there ARE some native Floridians, but not many!) We arrived about 5 PM on a Friday night. The establishment appears to be in an old house, and we were quickly seated in what may have been a bedroom at one time, with just 4 tables. (There apparently were other dining areas, but they may have been full). We ordered grouper sandwiches, and they were delicious, some of the better grouper sandwiches in the area (and we're on a quest to try 'em all) Our server (I think he introduced himself as "Smiley"?) was attentive without being overbearing. So...Food=Excellent, Service=Excellent, atmosphere=OK our "dining room" would be awesome for a romantic dinner, but we felt we were eating in a closet. Price=was about $45 for two grouper sandwiches and a beer. This is about the going rate. Another negative was the small selection of craft beer on tap. This is NOT the place to go if you're a craft beer enthusiast. Fortunately, they had Sweetwater 420 on tap, so I was good with that. We'll be back to try the fish tacos!

The sandwiches tasted good, but when trying to complete the kids meal for my 2 girls it was chaos. First when I asked for the apples and milk the girl tried to charge me extra for them, then after arguing with her she directed me to the refrigerator unit to help myself. There was only one bag of apples and they were moldy. It took over 5 minutes to get 2 fresh bags. Near the end of our meal my girls, after drinking almost all of the milk said that it tasted funny. I looked at the expiration day and it had expired two weeks prior. I told the uninterested worker and we left. Thankfully my kids didn't get sick. I wouldn't go back to that particular restaurant, but I still like Subway.
