I would consider the quality of the lamb to be high if I ate it at a restaurant costing 3x as much.
My order was over priced and very disappointing! Service better. No one there seemed to be hurting by pandemic and the totally raw food showed.
Came to Philly for the Cheesesteaks, ended up loving Fette Sau instead. Super chill vibe, and the brisket sandwich was amazing.

At Last, Santa Barbara has a wonderfully new restaurant that truly offers extremely delicious Ramen.  This is coming from someone that lived in New York City for six years and grew up in The Washington D.C. Area and has been to the top Ramen Shops in both cities often.  I moved to Santa Barbara in 2003 and quickly realized that Ramen would not be a weekly dining option as it was when I lived in the East Coast.  My love for a delicious bowl of Ramen was put on hiatus as I explored my new city and enjoyed what this city had to offer.  I adapted quickly and found my new dining staples, The Shellfish Company, The Santa Barbara Chicken Ranch, Arrigato, The Boathouse, and City Kitchen(I miss you so much!).  Fast forward to March 2016, and I now have Yankee Noodle in my top 6 must support restaurants.  Let's start with Yankee Noodle's service.  When you come to Santa Barbara from restaurant rich cities like Manhattan and D.C. you have to realize that you are simply not going to get consistently good service that's offered in these cities, simply because Santa Barbara can't sustain service industry professionals.  Therefore, the restaurants mostly hire college students.  That being said and having adjusted my grading of service accordingly, I was impressed with the staff of the newly opened restaurant.  They all were very friendly, made me feel welcome, and offered great suggestions on drinks and dining options. Anyone who knows me will tell you that I ask a lot of questions. I had a really nice conversation with the Bartendar, Mirch, about the high quality Beer, Sake, and Cocktail offerings on the menu. Mitch the Bartender came to Yankee Noodle from The Goodland in Goleta.  I started with the "Lemon in the Grass" cocktail.  It's Lemongrass infused Vodka with Ginger and Kumquat syrup. It was the perfect start to my dining experience and gave me something to savor while I examined the very unique menu.  For my first dish, I choose the "Umami Fresh Corn off the Cobb".   I enjoyed every spoonful of the r.  Next I had the "Rich Savory Smokey Pork Broth".   The Broth is hearty, rich, smokey and buttery delicious.  The noodles were authentic and perfectly prepared in soft and chewy Al-dente style with big egg flavor.  You can definitely taste the complexity of flavors from the broth that takes 24 hours to make.  The toppings it came with were excellent.  The Chasu (Pork Belly) was prepared nicely. It was an ample portion that I greatly enjoyed and the cost $12.95 was typical of what you'd find in a top Ramen shop in NYC or D.C.  I took home leftover Ramen and it was just as enjoyable heated up on the stove the next day.  Yankee Noodle occupies the former Space of Union Ale.  They did a nice job on the conversion.  They fashioned a community table from a "Chop Suey" sign that was from a Santa Barbara Restaurant on State Street in 1949's.  It's a great lunch spot while enjoying the Funk Zone or dinner spot Apres Wine with friends or solo.

Gangnam Style joke.

Alright now that's out of the way, I can move on to talk about H Mart. With high quality produce at laughably low prices, there's no reason not to do an immense amount of grocery shopping here. 

In addition to the grocery store, they've got a great food court and a fantastic cookware selection upstairs. The woman who helped me pick a wok was the sweetest lady I've seen in days.

Ate breakfast today with a party of 20. We called ten minutes before to inquire about wait time and they said they'd figure it out, to head over. We were able to sit in a long booth and a round table. We had one server and she did a phenomenal job taking care of us. 
I personally have not found a dish I'm crazy about. My kids ranging from 15-23 all ordered the Crack Chicken. It could be with a K but I'm not sure. They really like that dish with fried rice instead of white.
Restaurant and restroom are always clean and service was good. We had 5 checks for this party and it was no problem for them to disperse it that way. We really appreciated that.

I heard good things about this place until I actually tried it myself. 

This place has a pretty sorry Buffet. I should have already known from the name. "The Buffet" how generic. Anyway, the food here was not good at all. The carving stations had super dry meat which tasted like it was sliced from bouillon cubes. Everything was bad, even the seafood. Find a better buffet elsewhere.

Burgerfuel is in the heart of Broad Ripple. And it's a great addition. I ordered the Bacon Backfire gourmet chicken sandwich. The chicken was well-seasoned, the brie cheese was gooey and delicious, and I would be happy putting that aioli on almost anything. My sandwich was missing the bacon though, which was a major bummer, especially since I ordered the "Bacon" Backfire. 

But I quickly got distracted by the doofer, so all was good. The doofer is this little cardboard contraption that wraps around the bottom of your burger and collects all the messy burger juices. It's amazing, and it should be in every restaurant. 

I went with my sister, who is allergic to ginger, so unfortunately we were unable to try the motobites. We ordered the spud fries instead. They're thick-cut and covered in sea salt. Delicious. I typically don't like thick-cut French fries, but I'd definitely order these again. And the aioli was, of course, to die for. 

My standard for burgers is Bru Burger - I'm in love with their food. And I've never had anything that even comes close to a Bru Burger burger. Because of this, I'm giving Burgerfuel 4/5 stars. I would most definitely go back, but it is not better than Bru Burger.
Solid spot and great staff. I've been going here since I was a kid. Also, after moving out of state, whenever I do visit AZ, I make sure to hit this spot up every time!

Great place to hang with friends. excellent service. Very friendly and helpful. Order the hummus plate, plain bagel and cream cheese,French toast and a vanilla latte. It totaled around 30$. The French toast was my favorite. Trust me. Get it! Gorgeous hummus plate. A ton of hummus with fresh veggies. Could have used a few more pita chips. Perfect iced  vanilla latte. If you love bux this vanilla latte will show you what real coffee is. Great setting with plenary of seating inside and out as long as you don't mind sharing tables with people you don't know. We had a wonderful french man sit with us.

Went here for dinner while in Webster groves but didn't end getting anything but an appetizer and leaving.

1. Drinks are terrible, thursdays are 'margarita night' I'm pretty sure my margarita was Minute Maid Lemonade mixed with tequila, whatever it was tasted like sugar and nothing like a margarita. My fiancees Mojito was a sugarbomb, basically tasted like a glass full of simple syrip wiht mint leaves.

2. Menu has essentially nothing on it for someone who is lactose intolerant and doesn't eat meat, everything that wasn't meat was full of cheese or cream and when you pull those out of dishes that center around it they typically taste terrible.

We ordered some Hummus because we felt bad and it was good although the tapenade that came with it was not.  Its sad that places feel like they can't make good food without adding lots of fat to a recipe (heavy cream&cheese). I certainly wouldn't come here for drinks, I'm sure some of food is probably good if not run of the mill and uninspired.

If sitting and enjoying a cocktail or wine is your thing this place is great for that assuming there is no gun play or riots from groups being shoved down from the main part of the loop. Parking your car within eye shot is not a bad idea either. The food is fruffy with goat cheese and all that. The pizza is over rated although better then most in St.Louis. That being said St.Louis has about the worst pizza in the country. The few times I have been there and only because friends insisted the service has been slow and slower. Personally for the money(it is not cheap)  I would rather go somewhere else.

I am in St. Louis for a work meeting and decided to explore the area and came upon Brio.  This is a great restaurant -- as a woman dining alone, I was treated wonderfully.  I ate in the bar, and the bartender Paul checked on me, got my order in quickly, and was just super friendly and nice.  Anyhoo -- the pasta portion was enough to feed a family of four, while the asparagus side was enough to feed...me.  I cannot give the place four stars as they allow people to smoke in the bar, so when I got home my clothes, hair, coat were smelly.  Thanks Paul and staff for taking care of me.  BTW, it is dark and very cold but i did notice a Bocce ball court outside!

My first Philly cheesesteak - ever!  This place is small and cramped (A REAL HOLE IN THE WALL) so we ordered to go and only waited 10-15 min.  From all the people waiting I was sure it was going to take at least 20 min for my hero.  I had mushroom and cheese and it was delish!  Bread was nice and soft; meat was very flavorful.  Will definitely drive 1 H & 45 min for this (from northern NJ)!

Love the sushi at Hooks!!!  

Hooks Sushi Bar has such an amazing selection of sushi.  The specialty rolls are awesome and the prices won't drain your bank account.  It does get extremely busy around 8pm so be prepared for a wait (but it's worth the wait!).  I have sat at the bar a few times when we couldn't get a table and have really enjoyed talking with the sushi chefs (very friendly and informative).  My husband and I love spice so we usually order the Spicy Tuna rolls, Never Say Never rolls, and the TNT rolls.  

Arrive early for Wednesday's $1 sushi night!!!

Checkers is my fave but this location has the worst customer service. It is down pouring and no one is answering the drive thru telecom. My car and I are soaked. So I wait in line and just going to order at the window. They tell me, "We was busy makin other orders. Pull back around. We gots another order we makin now so you gots to go back around." Then the punk kid slams the window. I left. This is what life has come to. So sad.

Service was very poor. Waiter took forever to take our drink order and appetizer order. Our shots took forever to come. Food came out cold, and when asked to be remade it came out cold again. A manager didn't even come out to apologize. Service was horrible!!!
Great German restaurant in Horsham.  We all ordered the Weiner Schnitzel and various sides.  Loved their cream of spinach.   Service was good!

Wild Ginger sits in the corner of an aging shopping center (Justa Farm) and is easy to miss as County Line Road goes on and on with numbers that don't make sense.  It is much bigger inside than it looks and always seems too empty, considering the huge menu that is able to accommodate any kind of diet.  But we haven't gone there on the weekends.

All of the vegetarian items are vegan, and there are quite a few appetizers and entrees.  It is nice to see such balance on a menu.  No MSG either.

A beautiful fish tank greets you when you enter, and the fish will come over to you if you put your face close to the tank (of course you know not to tap on the tank).  Try to sit on the cozy banquette in the middle of the room, against the fountain and under the tiny neon lights.  

We had scallion pancakes and some hot and sour soup.  There is a large vegetarian section with vegmeats, which to me are a treat, especially seitan.  I got the Forever Young ($12 and quit snickering), which was like an Asian hoagie, a crispy pancake wrapped around green beans and veggie ham with lots of steamed broccoli on the plate.  He had the Mango Duck ($14) which was just ok, but being able to choose brown rice is a plus.  We took much of the food home.  It was a mistake to order a fried appetizer as well as a fried entree (did not realize the pancake was deep fried for some reason).  Our entire meal was $34 before tip, so it's very affordable, and as other reviewers mentioned, BYOB.

For some reason, it wasn't as good as the first time I ate here, and I cannot really determine why, maybe the lack of wine, haha, but we were already a bit intoxicated from a beautiful day.  I would still go back because of the diverse menu and low prices and would just not overdo the fried stuff.  Wild Ginger certainly does a brisk takeout business and is open 7 days a week.
Krista is an Awesome server!  Food was great!  We'll be back. Shrimp and grits-yum. Wife had blackened salmon-she loved it!

My dad saw Casale's on the Travel Channel so we decided to check it out during our trip to the snow. Definitely worth the drive from Truckee. 

We had four adults and three kids (1, 5 and 7 years old). We ordered the garlic bread, antipasto large plate, a full plate of lasagna, ravioli with meatballs and spaghetti with meatballs and one individual cheese pizza for the kids. We ate family style so everyone could try each of the entrees. We almost ate everything (after a ski day, mind you). Even our picky kids ate the spaghetti with their pizza.

The whole bill (including one beer and a few sodas) came to $85. Not bad at all for the amount of food we ordered. 

Andrew Zimmern did not steer us wrong!

Top notch deep dish pizza at a reasonable price. Plenty of options for toppings and side items. Pick up, delivery and dine in. I'm from Detroit where this pizzeria came from and it's bigger there than every other pizza place you can think of. Quality ingredients and dough made fresh daily. The managers are friendly and the staff is helpful and happy. I wouldn't be surprised if this was your new favorite pizza place after you've tried it.

Delicious!!!! We ordered 5 dishes and lived each one of them. Got to enjoy eating outside. Meals weren't huge which allowed us to get a few different selections
 Definitely a place to try out for brunch!

Great place. Best chain restaurant burgers, fries, and onion rings I've ever had. This location just opened, so the waitstaff was a tiny bit overly attentive at first ( day one), but today I went back with kiddies ( day four)and everyone had chilled out a bit. It's a very cool place to come after work, on a date, or with the girls/guys. I'll be back:)

One question: am I supposed to tip the people that check on you while you eat? You pay in advance, and I didn't see anyone leave a tip on their table when they left. I just need to know what the proper etiquette is in this pseudo-cafeteria setting?

We didn't end up eating here so I can't review the food, but wanted people to be aware of the atmosphere. Reviews were really good so we thought we would check it out. From the outside you can see beer signs in the window, but we didn't realize it was actually a bar that also served food. The bar is in front and there are a few tables in the back. Being from out of state, we didn't realize smoking was permitted indoors, and nearly everyone inside was smoking. We would have been ok with eating in a bar, but since our daughter was with us, the smoking caused us to leave. Disappointed because the menu looked appealing.
This was really good food. I still remember the garlic spread with the free bread seven years later. The service was amazing.
Food was good, price was very reasonable, and good service. Better than your average Mexican restaurant. Enjoyed the 2 for 1 draft beer (was a Mon night)
We went in for dinner. The music was great but what made the meal was the server. She was honest and attentive. The food was yummy too

I ordered the lamb kebab. It was overcooked and overseasoned, I never really tasted the lamb. It also tasted like it was precooked and was saturated in oil. The oven potatoes did not taste like greek lemon potatoes, tasteless. The only thing I liked was the greek salad. My husband got the mousaka and it was bland. They charge a fee for using your credit card, what??!! We will not return.

Natasha ,has been a fixture in the Copeland's business for numerous years. I am appalled that she is no longer an employee . She has been a loyal  , professional, and devoted employee for years nearly 10years . She has given her best of the best service to your company and the loyal customers . It saddens me to know Copeland's has no compassion or appreciation for loyal and dedicated employee.

Went for dinner on a Monday night, for not being too busy was disappointed by the delay in service and being able to order food. Good range of options on the menu, beet salad was solid and chicken was well prepared, on the pricier side for quality, overall would not go out of my way to go back.
Their menu is a little pretentious and the service can be spotty, but anything lacking is made up by truly excellent food. Very comfortable physical space.

My husband and I ate here for dinner and then breakfast the next morning. It was so delicious! The Chicken and Waffles were amazing. We had the ribs the night before and they were just as delicious! We added the updated menu as well

You don't have to go to St. Louis for great Japanese food. This place is it!

When we came in, the restaurant was very dark. It needs more windows. I'm not sure what that building was before they took over, but they really need better lighting. 

Anyways, the food was very tasty. I liked the stir fry udon and the shrimp tempura roll. The prices are super reasonable during lunch time. The sushi presentation is not very elegant or imaginative, but it tastes great. 

There was only one woman waiting on people so you can imagine how slow the service was, but she came when she was flagged down. 

My favorite part was the little pineapple boat that they gave you for free at the end of the meal. It had wedges cut out and was a great way to end a meal.

Tonight's supper was excellent!
My husband had the basa blackened meal. It was tasty, not too spicy. It came with chicken soup ( very very good), and a vegetable and choice of a potato !
I had the immense taco salad minus the jalapeños. The shell was scrumptious!
The meat was not over-spicy. And SO MUCH meat! A protein lovers delight!!
I enjoyed a house red. It was excellent & a good size glass. 
5 Stars. 
OH
 Immaculate clean. All re-done. Comfortable booths   No saggy spots. Bathrooms were superior!
What more could I ask: 
great food
Good portions
Happy atmosphere 
Clean restroom 
OH our waitress, Krissi, was SO helpful, friendly & smiling! The hostess also checked on us quite a few times!
BRAVO 
GO there. See for yourself.

I went previously to another McDonalds that was advertising the Shamrock Shake inside and outside the building that said they didn't have it yet, so I called this location first to make sure they had it before I drove there, they said they did have it. I get here and absolutely nobody is in the drive-thru, it's a weird time of day to get food anyways. I pull up to the speaker ready to order. And I sit there, and sit there, and finally I had to say "hello?" for anyone to come to the intercom to get my order. Finally someone answered and had obviously been joking around with coworkers and not doing his job. As I was ordering, he was still cracking up and laughing and I had to repeat myself because the order was wrong. I then asked for the shamrock shake and he says they have it but the ice cream machine is broken. Why did nobody tell me this when I called specifically to ask for it? Or they were lying, who knows. I get to the window to pay and he's still laughing. When I get to the second window, I wait and wait and then a very unfriendly women hands me my stuff with the ugliest look on her face like she could care less and says "here". No wonder this location has less than 2 stars.

I ordered a large thin pizza with several toppings, it was delicious! I also ordered the large caesar salad with chicken, but what a disappointment! Looks like they forgot to add the correct amount of chicken! We always order the salad and I know this was not enough! Did they ran out of chicken? Unbelievable! 
I paid almost $46 and this time not satisfied!
Best Mac n cheese. Great atmosphere and great service !!! Awesome beer choices.  Comfort food. Lengthy menu to choose from.  Cool spot in the city.
Good food. The roasted veggie antipasto was delicious. Chicken Marsala was also good, if not extraordinary. We also has a swordfish special that was really good. Be aware it's BYOB.

This place was great!!!!  We stopped for brunch.  Had the pork scrapple.....oh my gosh...lil party in mouth. Just FYI can't get cornbread til dinner-we will come back!
Actually came back for dinner same day cause just had to have cornbread...it was delish!!!!   Would highly recommend the place-u won't be disappointed.

Stopped in for a quick lunch on Friday. It was dead! I guess everyone was away for Memorial Day. Service was great as was the food. I ordered the crab cake melt, it was very tasty. My wife ordered the salmon. She was raving about it. Never a bad meal here. Solid 5 stars

We ordered pizza from this place through Uber Eats tonight. The total for two 12' pizzas came to almost $50 dollars. When the pizza arrived, it was clear that the margherita pizza was not even close to 12'. We also ordered a pepperoni pizza that was a complete abomination. First off, some absolute genius neglected to put the pepperoni on the pepperoni pizza. Second, another big brain at Anthony's forgot to put the sauce on the pizza before putting it on the oven so they brilliantly just plopped gobs of sauce all over the pie. Third, Anthony's clearly was trying to save us from America's vampire epidemic by putting FULL CLOVES OF GARLIC on the pizza. Fourth, one half of the pizza must have been shoved into the fiery depth of Krakatoa because it was burned to a complete crisp. And, for the pièce de résistance, Anthony's took some notes from Chuck E. Cheese and combined multiple slices to create a Franken-pizza. In my years on this earth, I have never seen a pizza so mangled and destroyed. It's an insult to pizza to even call this mess a pizza. Do not waste your time or money ordering from this place.

So, the restaurant is tiiiiiinnnnyyy. But, it helped add to the jovial atmosphere. We stopped here on a whim because we got caught in a major storm and the area is unfamiliar so instead of driving, we ate. Haha 

There is an outdoor eating space, however the weather kept us from utilizing that but it looked like a great place to eat. 

We got calamari and two pizzas. It was so good. 

So good. 

I mean, I love brick over pizza, but this was one of my favorite experiences. The crust is thinner, unlike our local brick oven pizzeria, and you could fold it like pizza tacos. Best of both world, am I right? 

If I lived there, it'd be a regular place we'd go. We really enjoyed our experience.

I'm obsessed with this place. Dude is a legend. Also: THURSDAY NIGHT RIBS!!! You'll wait a bit for your order, but honestly so worth it. I don't get the hype with Hattie B's and all that jazz, but the wings here are ace.

Don't go here! The worst staff ever! They never double check a bag and if you wait at the window to check your order they snarl at you. But they always forgot something! I got all the way home to find one of our meals were missing. Called and all they did was pick up the phone and hang up and then leave it off the hook. Spend your money somewhere else!

The location, atmosphere and food are all great! Wishing I could find more coupons but the prices are good. I love the soup and everyone was very nice and helpful. I had the catering at a wedding and it is awesome!!!
Taylor rocked as a server and as always the food was amazing! The 1905 salad and Spanish soup was delicious and one can never go wrong with the red sangria!

Came here for brunch before heading up to chop our Christmas tree down. They are the perfect little breakfast stop! I had the pork belly Benedict and as a Benedict lover I was thoroughly impressed. The bread they use is amazing. Great service from the waitress who helped us- we had a good laugh about a handsy couple just inches away from our table. Thankfully it didn't ruin my appetite lol! I told my bf from now on that needs to be our tradition before we get our tree. And will definitely be back before then!

We dined at FarmTable a couple of timea during a recent visit to St Pete, once for lunch and once for dinner. We enjoyed it.

VIBE: We dined on the outdoor mezzanine overlooking the mall plaza both times. Very pleasant (except at dinner, when the noisy artificial snow machine turned on every 20 minutes or so). Tables were well-spaced and brightly lit. Not romantic, but practical.

SERVICE: Service was attentive both times. Our lunch server, Will, was particularly knowledgeable, engaged and helpful. Food was delivered in a timely manner (the place was not busy either time). 

VERY GOOD: Lunch was outstanding. The Florida grouper BLT was fabulous - easily on my list of top five faves anywhere (right up there with the porchetta sandwich from Tartine Manufactory in San Francisco). Luscious fish, artisanal bacon, green tomato served on a tender bun - a little messy, but heavenly! And oh - those duck fat fries were 9.9 out of 10! Focaccia was excellent - tender and tasty, with a slight crackle to the crust. Fried cauliflower was also a treat, as was iced coffee latte. The lone dinner standout was hazelnut semifreddo - delicious and nicely presented. The wine list is compact, but well-chosed and affordable.

NOT AS GOOD: A margherita pizza sounded promising, but was too bready (good crust, just way too much crust for the topping). 

I'd certainly return if I was in St Pete again, especially for a nice lunch. The menu is appealing, the execution was generally good.

I'm really kicking myself for taking 6 years to try this place. To be honest I haven't been a fan of any of the "soul food" restaurants here in St. Louis so I just kind of gave up. This place completely changed my perspective! The food is so good I really don't have any words describe it. They have all the food I grew up on and didn't know to appreciate. It brought back so many memories of me sitting in my grandmother's hot kitchen. The food was fresh, non greasy, not overly salted/seasoned, didn't taste rushed or made as if it was in bulk! They do it right here! The sides alone is worth the trip! Whoever is preparing this food has spent a lot of time cooking for people they love. The line servers, and table servers and overall services was spectacular! It really did feel as if my family opened a restaurant. I felt at home....

Very nice experience at Cunetto's again. Had the tiramisu this time - it was out of this world! I wouldn't call myself a tiramisu connoisseur, but I know what's good, what's bad, and what's so-so. And this tiramisu was freaking amazing!!

Your basic Americanized Chinese food, but always hot and tasty. The Crab Rangoon are fantastic and clearly house made. The potstickers are doughier than average, but I find them quite good. The sesame chicken is always a good choice. If you're looking for a cheap, fast, tasty lunch, I suggest the Orient.

This place is amazing.

 They bake bread daily, have a rotating menu of breads they bake weekly and they have a day old bread shelf.

You can ask for samples of the breads you're interested in buying before you get them. 

Very friendly staff and amazing bread recipes. I want to try it all!!

Live this place well worth the wait. Can't beat the ribeye. Best service ever love the Margaritas.
The manager made us feel like family.

This is my favorite place downtown to go for coffee or chai. I love the vibe and I've loved everything I've ever ordered. My favorite thing to get is the chai- I don't know what brand they use but it is SO good. It is the perfect balance of sweet and spice, creamy but light. Perfectly refreshing. I do wish you could get discounted refills (maybe you can, but I'm under the impression that you can't.) I've also loved the iced teas, special lemonades made with house made syrup and coffee, of course. I've gotten various toasts and enjoyed them all. One time I happened to be there while they were baking vegan chocolate chip banana bread, which made the whole place smell amazing, so I had to get it while it was hot. It was incredible. Just melt in your mouth delicious. Also, everybody that works here is nice and helpful.

When I review chain restaurants like the OG there usually isn't much to say (I'm no Marilyn Hagerty). This one isn't any different. Olive Garden has changed up their logo and menu, which is fun. I didn't order anything new, but it's good to see them trying to update things. Our server was ok, but did seem to have a hard time keeping up with the busy restaurant.

What more is there to say? It's exactly what I expected. And I'm ok with that.

Good was delicious. We went for restaurant week and the dessert was delicious. We got the almond cake and coffee dessert. The presentation of our food was also so beautiful. The chicken was juicy and filling and I ordered the catfish which came with so many different flavor sand textures. The restaurant is small and cozy and service was great. Love the pumpkin seeds at the end! We left full and enjoyed our time!

Definitely will not be returning my food that I had was fine but my mother didn't like hers at all  within 2 minutes she said that she didn't want it when the check came they didn't take her food off so my mother said hey I noticed they didn't take this off and he response was so rude and disrespectful with so much attitude I'm not sure what her problem was I've been going here for years with my mother NEVER EVER has my family had a issue with this restaurant I WILL NOT BE RETURNING SINCE YOU DONT CARE IF YOUR DAD FINDS OUT ABOUT YOUR CUSTOMER SERVICE! I even tried to talk to this woman and she did nothing but cut me off and yell JUST DISRESPECTFUL

I really enjoyed the Chef and I. I came in for a cooking class, which was scallops. Now come on, something so easy can sometimes be so hard to get perfect. Chef Matt was awesome in his instruction showing us all the knife skills and cutting. It was so interactive and we met some really cool people there, which is great because sometimes you just want to have some nice convo while sitting and watching amazing food come together. The drinks were wonderful. Of course I  prefer something a bit on the sweeter side so I went with a Riesling. Everyone was laughing and chatting while the food was being prepared. We got to eat those scallops up, and it was a fine experience. I recommend this place based on friendly staff, good food, awesome atmosphere and I will be back to eat their chef's menu.

Cure is a pricey place, without a doubt, but what you get is worth it. The bartenders here understand what makes a cocktail, the way ingredients come together. The results are singular flavors, not the muddled and syrupy sweet mess that passes for a cocktail just about everywhere else in this city. I went on a Sunday night and the place was fairly empty, so I had a chance to talk with the staff. Everyone was friendly, and the bartenders seemed like real professionals. Of course things are probably different on a crowded Friday night, where the attention to detail could result in long waits.  When they say small plates they mean it, the food is good (I had the crab salad sandwich), and the menu carefully designed, but it's not enough for dinner. Overall I'll definitely return, but only around payday.
The hostess, a woman, said they had, "no seats" when they had 4-5 seats open outside. Not too busy inside either by looking at it. Wouldn't recommend if you are looking for walk up service.

Everyone keeps asking me what's my favorite Chinese restaurant...this one. Here's what I order on a normal day:
Hot and sour soup. It has a slightly farmy smell, but the taste! Oh my! I have noticed that recently this soup is less chock full of goodies like mushrooms, but it still holds its own in my book.
Dan Dan noodles. I like their version soooo much more than any other Sichuan place. They use a toothier square noodle. Blows other Dan Dan noodles out of the water.
Beef with chili peppers. Not the lunch special! On the main menu. It has a nice burn to it that is just right. Lets the flavors dance on your tongue but doesn't require tons of water to cool your mouth.
Snow pea leaves. One of the most delicious things I have ever had. Think of spinach but sweeter.
Dry string beans. Whatever they do to make them "dry" is amazing.
I've never had a problem with he service and we can get in, out, and done in 45 minutes for lunch.

Got a variety for the team working on a Sunday. Great food. Chicken Thikka was awesome. Naan was soft and yummy. GrubHub delivery. Everybody was well satisfied. I need to stop by there sometime and enjoy a meal in their restaurant.

I ordered the cheese steak with half whiz and half provolone. I found the meat to be bland, but maybe next time I should season it more with salt. There was a long line but went by pretty quickly since people knew their orders. There is seating upstairs!
Amazing!!!!  The meat is moist and flavorful. The rice and sides are perfect compliments.

Amazing place. Food is simply delicious here. High quality ingredients in all of their dishes. 

This place is most certainly a diamond in the rough. 

Hole in the wall but great food.

Ordered basil fried rice with Pork 3*, beef salad 4*, pad woon sen 5* & basil chicken 4*.
Enjoyed the sushi.  Also tried the pad thai on another occasion.  A bit overpriced.  Will go back.

I loved everything about this place so I don't even know where to start: 
Decor: very cool and smart, mason jar with up to date bill with all the prices for what they have on top and bottle. Cool idea. The menu is a newspaper.  Overall I wish I thought of it
Drinks: best Bloody Mary I have ever had so much that even my husband couldn't stop drinking it and he doesn't even like bloody Mary's
Also a great selection of beers on tap.. Love the milk stout.
Food: u must try the smoke salmon dip even if u don't like salmon dip. It's nothing I have ever had. It has hickory bqq, creamy, and a hint of smoke salmon that just goes well with even the tots they have.  The salmon dinner was good too. Perfectly cooked  salmon on top of a creamy corn. So the pound of Blt.. Wow it was huge and we had bacon for breakfast but the bread was perfect with a nice thick cut heirloom tomato and super crispy romaine and mayo.   Then for lunch we had these amazing ahi tuna taco.. The pickle onion on it was just perfect with their slaw. If u love french dip.. U will love it here the bread is light and airy and the prime rib is full of favor and tender that u really don't even need to dip it.
Price/service: very nice staff and owners have put in a lot of love as they are passionate about what they offer. Super kid friendly place. Good menu for kids and super accommodating as they add ground beef to my son pasta.  Prices are almost too reasonable for the quality of food... This would be three times the price if we were in Chicago.

My new favorite place and place to look forward to if my husband is working in the area or if I need to work in st.Louis. It's worth the drive.

Enjoyed an early dinner at El Cortez. Guacamole and chips were generous. Tacos were good. Why is it that "mexican" places make tacos with non-mexican ingredients like feta cheese? I love feta with Greek food but not necessarily with my taco. Shared and tried steak, ground beef (tasted like a taco), pork and chicken. 

Expensive, but likely due to location near Whyte Ave.

Ordered chili and baked potatoes; neither was edible, the baked potato was cold and hard (half baked) and the chili was undercooked with hard beans and very little beef.  Too bad; it used to be a delicious chili that was enjoyed in cold weather.  Plus the window clerk blew his nose on a napkin then handled food before getting up and going to wash his hands.  When he got up, his pants fell down in the back giving me a view of his underwear.  100% totally unappetizing experience and I will never visit this location again.
All around great Thai food and friendly low key atmosphere...attentive and kind servers and some interesting apps with classic American Thai dishes - great job!
Great food-good atmosphere! Menu will blow you away!

I simply can not say how amazing this place is. Huge venue that would be a great place to watch a game, amazing food and huge variety of drinks including moonshine, cocktails and of course beer. A white duck tacos on site makes this even better

Love the food and atmosphere! Fresh seafood and good cocktails. They have a bakery right beside the restaurant with delicious desserts. Nice little town with lots of stores and restaurants! Cool Greek people

On Friday and Saturday nights, this place is packed, and if you want an actual table to eat at or smoke at, you need to call and make reservations ahead of time.

That being said, Friday and Saturday nights, the place turns into something like a dance club.  Exotic music and exotic men are all over the place - especially Arab guys, and there's a lot of drunkenness and dancing on tables.

Definitely a great location for the occassional change of pace, although I know plenty of people who frequent the place several times a week.  It just depends on your tastes.

The decor is dark greens and purples - everything you'd expect to create an Arabian-like setting.  The front area has great comfy chairs surrounding tables for larger groups (and those are generally the tables people dance on) and beautiful stained glass windows.

I just got done taking 2 bites out of my crunchy chicken sandwich and throwing it away. The sandwich didn't just taste bad, it was disgusting. Complete waste of 10 bucks. After seeing all these other negative reviews I'm kicking myself for not yelping this place before i got food from it. The customer service wasn't bad but it also wasn't good.

Probably some of the best Italian food I've ever had. The portions are definitely big enough to save some for the next meal. Love the quaint and cozy feel as well as the outstanding service from the staff. My new favorite place as a newcomer to the area!!!

Great bread, great tomato pie, great hoagies, great pastries!
Corps is a long time favorite of my family. The only thing I would change, would be a bigger store with more selection.
They are always courteous and polite in the store.

This is such a great restaurant. If you haven't been, stop by, you're missing out. The servers are amazing and treat you like regulars (tonight we had Katie). Food is phenomenal at a great price. Drinks priced and poured well!! Ambience is super laid back and chill. A good change of pace from the overpriced restaurants around Indianapolis. Not to mention their food gives those places a run for their money! Great neighborhood bar not to miss.
The decor was great but the food was just okay. My sweet and sour chicken was Luke warm.

We came to R and R after a long day of driving. We were starving.  David was our server and he made a few recommendations that were spot on. My husband had the scallops and I had the chicken and both were beyond delicious. 
Great service and fabulous food. We were really impressed because we live in Seattle and the seafood is hard to beat in Seattle. The scallops were very big and very juicy and prepared so deliciously.

Where to start....   This place is exceptional, and I couldn't think of anything not to like here.  You walk in, and the atmosphere says "Family Style, Home Cooked".  The waitress was super friendly and the service was great (we heard later she is the daughter of the owners, thus reinforcing the truth that this is a family place).  Ray Charles, Steve Wonder, and Ben E King are playing softly in the background, and sweet smells drift in from the Kitchen.  We haven't even eaten anything yet, and I love this place.

We started off with cornbread cooked in a little cast iron skillet.  I have to confess, that I am a cornbread junkie, and fancy myself as quite the aficionado when it comes to this line of baked goods.  This may very well be the best cornbread I have ever had.  I've had other southern style cornbread that is dry and lacking in taste, and I know that some people love it this way.  The cornbread at Shanaz however is sweet and buttery.  It is soft and delicious, and I can't wait to go back just for the cornbread.  Yum, yum, yum!

I ordered the Jambalaya Stuffed Pepper, and my wife got the Fried Chicken & Waffle.  We traded bites back and forth, and we both agreed that both dishes were delicious.  The Fried chicken was cooked perfectly, and the Jambalaya was, well, amazing.  The spices tingle on your tongue as you eat, and the sausage was soooo flavorful.  I love it all.

I can't wait to go back to try some catfish and gumbo, but beware; we were told that the seafood gumbo is only available on Friday and Saturday (as I recall).

So what more can I say.  This hidden gem in Meridian served us up a perfect dinner, and we enjoyed every bite.  We will be back.



[  One shouldn't use big words when a singular unloquacious and diminutive linguistic expression will satisfactorily accomplish the contemporary necessity.  ]

I so want to love you, Abuela's... I've waited a year for your opening and have come in at least four times, each one more disappointing than the one before. The service is truly abysmal - it should not be impossible to request dairy-free items in a modern restaurant. I make a BIG fuss about it - once a manager even went into the kitchen to confirm that there be no dairy in my order, and yet our came my tacos smothered in cheese. The servers have no idea what ingredients are in the food, are incredibly slow, don't refill the water bottle they leave on the table, and don't bring you the check once they clear your table. Plus it is way too expensive for the caliber of food - $40-50 for lunch for two should mean I can get quality vegetables as my side, not undercooked chunks of squash. Please get better!  The location is so beautiful!

The Cheesecake Factory here in Clearwater next to Macy's at the Mall!  Sizeable restaurant and very clean!  The Staff here are courteous and knowledgeable!!  No appetizers today with Lunch we saved up for desserts after our lunch entrees!  For lunch we ordered Chicken Marsala, Spicy Cashew Chicken, and Carbonara Bow Tie Pasta!  Phenomenal lunch and we all had leftovers because of the Size, yummy tomorrow!!  We all had desserts: Very Cherry Ghirardelli Cheesecake, Original Cheesecake, and Tiramisu Cheesecake!  All were great in their own way!!  Hey The Cheesecake Factory here in Clearwater FL is a Home Run and deserves 5 Stars !!
Trying a new spot for our anniversary. This was a pleasant surprise. Quaint dining, friendly staff, all round good experience. Not your typical menu and the food is bomb!

my girlfriend and I went there yesterday and I must say they have one of the best hamburgers you would ever what to eat.  the garlic spinach top I had was truly wonderful.  thanks for the experience and the server was so pleasant.  we'll be back :)

I used to eat here a lot.  The food is major comfort good but really rich stuff, heartland style.  The Moe Joe potatoes are large cubed fried.   Hollandaise and gravy abounds and it smells like hash heaven in there.

It also has proper wait staff.  None of that downtown froufrou pour your own coffee and drink BS here.  The coffee is not gourmet but solid and dependable. Waitresses are cordial without being obtrusive.

Formal dress is optional.  Also rare.

So come on down when you can accommodate the calorie load.  Just consider skipping lunch and dinner if trying to fit into a smaller size.
Absolutely the worst service ever!!! Wow 35 min for food,  Not even busy!  Huge contrast on to go orders- food has always  been great!

If there were negative stars for rating I'd rate that.  
I ate there last night with couple friends and the waiter was rude.  We didn't even finish eating and he already started cleaning our appetizer dish.  Not to mention, when our pad thai dish comes out.. there was a freaking FLY on it.  It was disgusting and nasty.  We called the waitress/manager out to let them know and they didn't even apologized.  All she said was we'll replace this dish okay?  I am like, WTF, we should have just left but we were too nice and indeed we stayed there and continue our meal.

But of course, after knowing that there's a fly in one of the dish, I was freaked out and started checking the other dishes...  It was just a horrible experience in general.  I will never go back to FLY PENANG again..  Just NASTY.

This restaurant has exceptional quality in it's dishes. Instead of the usual chips before being served the main course, they serve a hot Gordita. 

Their pork is tender and delicious. I tried both a pork enchilada and tamale. Both were perfect. The tamale was not the usual minimal amount of filling. It was well balanced and moist! 

Don't pass up a margarita. They are huge and favorable!

My friend and I will definitely be back!

Thank god this exists. Nothing else in WC even comes close to Carlinos. I strictly rely on Carlino's at lunch time. Never had any complaints. Nice, friendly staff (they always seem in a good mood), great food, so much variety and originality in that little place.

Yummmm love the cool new flavors, 
"Home means Nevada" and Licorice my Favorite!!! Fresh and creamery!!

Last night was my first visit to Osaka... Not the city, but the place.  This is THE PLACE for great sushi.  I started with miso soup, which was standard.  I ordered hot tea, and I was very pleasantly surprised by its perfection.  Its heady jasmine aroma instantly transported me, calmed my jangled nerves from a busy week, and readied my taste buds for the main event: great sushi.
     I ordered two raw rolls, both were menu item house specialties.  They were skillfully prepared and very artfully presented.  The taste was truly excellent.  I could taste the fresh tuna and salmon, which was well complimented by spiciness and the flavors of perfectly ripe avocado, toasted sesame seeds, and fresh roe.  The wasabi and pickled ginger were perfect, as in these standard accompaniments did not at all detract from the main course.
     The restaurant was clean, tidy, nicely decorated, active, but not loud, with nice sight lines, interesting tiles, and comfortable lighting.  Nice atmosphere!  The restroom was clean, devoid of odors, and well-stocked on the Friday night that I visited.  
     Will I eat there again?  YES!  Who knew such a pearl would appear in Langhorne?  It is worth a drive from Oxford Valley, Neshaminy, Newtown, and Yardley.

Umm, I guess I don't get it?

I've had this place bookmark for quite a while, and kept meaning to try it. I had something to do around the corner from here tonight, so finally decided to give it a go.

I wasn't in a burger mood, so was deciding between a salad and a stuffed flatbread. I ordered a flatbread. In hindsight, I think I should've gone with a salad. Maybe I would've liked it more?

Specifically, I had the barbecue chicken stuffed flatbread. There was a lot of chicken. A lot, a lot of chicken. I guess the flavor was good? Kind of indistinguishable.

My other half have a barbecue chicken sandwich. I will say that the homemade - I think they were homemade - crisps that came with it were delicious! A personal opinion, but he was not fond of the sandwich. The chicken didn't have a whole lot of flavor besides sauce. Like it wasn't seasoned at all.

I would give the place another try -- for a salad or a burger -- but I'm not sure if I can convince my other half!

Note: they do have two TVs outside and inside that patrons can watch. 


2017: 56/100
The tacos are amazing! The shrimp and fish tacos  Highly recommended, especially on $2 taco Tuesday specifically.

I've never been treated so rudely my entire life at any restaurant ever..... Do not go  to  this restaurant  the food is marginal and Service pathetic ... especially the bar !!!I moved here from Los Angeles  and been here close to 20 years ...typically go to the Red Pony and  cork and cow ...In town love them!!!!thought i d branch out ... it was a bad idea
Not bad at all! They are somewhat friendly, but probably the most expensive hole in the wall Chinese restaurant, but they will be my go to close by Chinese food.

I really wanted to like this after a recommendation from  a local. But for 16.95 I had the worst grouper rueben I've ever had. Just a sopping wet sandwich with a fish that tasted more like catfish. And for $8 a small side of fries with a side of Heinz beef gravy. Not what I wanted for local fare. Ate half the soggy sandwich because I was starving and left.

I tried benny's earlier this week and I loved it! I got three pizzas delivered and they arrived exactly on time (I preordered). If you're in the area, the pizza is worth trying. The crust is crispy, but fluffy and light. The ingredients are fresh. We especially loved the entire sprig of basil that came with the pizzas.
A perfect breakfast. Yummy food, family friendly service, and terrific coffee!  We're coming back.

We come in and sit down and it's pretty busy which is okay but our waitress ignored us for 10 whole minutes. We sat here with no drinks no hello or anything. As I'm writing this we have been here twenty five minutes and she just came to take our drink order. We ended up leaving after thirty minutes of no drink or no apologies. I spoke to the manager and she was very apologetic however it was too late. I will never return to this establishment. Customers are not to be treated in such a way. The waitress even served others who came in after us which was totally rude. I'm very disappointed.
Awesome food and awesome service, the owner was very nice and the food was great. I highly recommend

Craft Street has been consistently awesome since my first visit a year ago. I bumped up my review to five stars because everything I've tried has been absolute perfection. 

My most recent visit was actually a day they weren't doing brunch. I had a late lunch with two others and we sat at the bar. Bartender was Ashley and she was friendly, attentive and helpful. This was my first visit since realizing my wheat allergy. I requested their "gluten friendly" menu. Difference between gluten friendly and gluten free is that friendly implies some items are cross-contaminated while cooking. Biggest culprits are foods that use the same fryer. Potatoes and french fries are out if you have celiac disease. 

Not a huge salad fanatic but the Figster caught my attention. Grilled chicken, marinated figs, Bartlett pears, candied pecans, blue cheese crumbles, mixed greens, spinach, and vinaigrette dressing. One bite and I was completely blown away by it. I ate the entire salad and it was pretty big! My party ordered the Avocado Hummus appetizer plate and a gluten free cheese burger with side of garlic mashed potatoes. They loved their dishes as well. We also shared a round of shots. 

I was a brunch junkie but Craft Street works any time of day. I would love to see them expand their gluten friendly menu and make solid allergy free options.

Cunetto's is one of my favorite places to eat. Every time I am in Saint Louis I stop by. But instead of telling you why I love the place so much, let me instead address some concerns of others.

Quality of food: the food is excellent, Michelin star quality food. But it is fair to insult some of their dishes. The only thing more ignorant than ordering a crab dish when there is only one of the menu, is having it on the menu itself. This is a great Italian restaurant with great homemade dishes, order something that it makes sense to order, not something that you know will have canned crab on it. The truth is they do simple things magnificently. The garlic bread is eye opening, the pasta is fresh, the tiramisu is delightful.  

You had to wait a long time: HOW DARE THAT HOSTESS MAKE YOU STAY AFTER TELLING YOU THERE WOULD BE A WAIT. Shut up.

Atmosphere: I am a food snob. But I am not a decor snob. If you serve the best apple pie in the world out of a truck I don't care about the kitchen on four wheels as long as it is free of little critters. This place is stuck in the early nineties and looks just like a restaurant out of season one of the Sopranos, but the staff is pleasant, the service timely, and the price reasonable. 

Overall give Cunetto's a try. Don't order something that is clearly not fresh and enjoy the pasta.

This is our second time eating here. The meat and the pineapple off the spit were excellent. The feijoada(sp?) the black beans, with meat was, by far, my favorite item on the buffet. The vegan beans were good, but if you eat meat, why bother. The fried fish and cod stew were also excellent. The ceviche was a little iffy, but spread on a piece of bread like lox was actually pretty good. Everything on the dessert table was excellent, from the fruit to to the chocolate.  The key lime could have been toned down a little. The lime overpowered the pie. It was good if you really love lime, but it would be nice to get other flavors there.

This place is amazing. I get takeout as often as I can. They adhere to my strict dietary restrictions and I feel safe eating here during this current pandemic. Excellent quality food, great staff, and affordable prices. Definitely worth checking out!

This place is LEGIT. Service is always good, prices are even better, plenty of tv's for watching games, and they have really good food. It's not what you'd expect from the outside. Don't get me wrong, this is a dive bar but it's a dive bar with awesome food. Definitely a hidden gem worth checking out. It's quickly becoming one of my favorite places to go in St. Pete.

I've been twice, the food has always been good and the menu items creative, but the staff and the "ambiance" are something to be desired. Tables are always dirty., garbage cans full, flies everywhere. Staff has always been somewhat rude. Our inquiry about drinks was met with a very curt "I don't know, whatever is in the cooler". I'll take my business elsewhere.
Excellent Chinese, Japanese, sushi and pad Thai. Very clean facility, good service. This will be a regular go to place for us.
Excellent food! Their mole is soooo good. I love the portions and quality. They are great for travelers and locals. Such good food for on the go people like myself.

Once again delivered an awesome event for corporate dinner. 
We had 13 this time. Enjoyed nice drinks and some shared apps - shrimp bruschetta yummy and calamari was quite good as well. Very light. 

Dinner got rave reviews from the team. I enjoyed my tuna seared. Boss liked her snapper filet and coworker enjoyed her filet Mignon. Cooked perfectly. 

Bob our waiter kept us entertained and never broke a sweat no matter how much we flirted with him. 

Thanks again. Will always return

Champagne & Sazerac Cupcakes? Yes, please!

Cake Cafe is my favorite breakfast spot in New Orleans. Steve, the owner started his business by selling single slices of cake on Bourbon Street years ago. I can fondly remember my 19 year old self, working at a gentleman's club waiting for him to walk by so I could grab a slice. I fell in love with his cake back then and was so proud and delighted when he opened this cafe in my neighborhood.

The cakes are absolutely delicious. Especially noteworthy are the champagne cupcakes and the goat cheese/apple king cake during Mardi Gras season.

The regular fare here is just as yummy. I love the healthy grits and the fried tilapia sandwich. The portions are big, the staff is friendly and fun and Steve is always there working hard. 

Surely one of my top New Orleans eateries.

Eeek. I love diners and mediocre food after at the end of a night out, but this place is an exception. It's pretty close to my apartment, and I will go out of my way to go somewhere else. That says something, right? My biggest qualm is that it's really grimy. Griminess is okay at a dive bar, but at a restaurant, not so much.

My boyfriend and I decided to go to brunch on Sunday a few weeks ago. We heard a lot about the new board game cafe, and we were excited to try it out! When we arrived, we were immediately greeted and helped to a table. The game selection is awesome and the best part is the section right out of Saint Louis. The food is good, but doesn't seem to fit the atmosphere completely. I think things that are easier to snack on would be more ideal. The only other thing to mention were the chairs. The chairs are really nice, but they flip easily. We saw at least a half dozen flips while there 

The staff is great there!they made their way around asking us about our experience and making sure we didn't have any questions about our game. I would highly recommend a trip to pieces!
Just WOW! Great People, Great Sandwiches and Great Pickles! Where can I find more stars to give this place!

Love riffs! Always new and exciting items and friendly staff. Way to go guys! I work next door and I no longer have a lunch hour while you are open but when I get a break I normally seek over for a baked treat or a lattee. The honey bee is my favorite latte. Sweet and spicy.

Lolita is a Philadelphia restaurant gem. Everything I've ever tried on the menu has been delicious, but my favorite is the carne asada. The space is small and loud with exposed brick and a lot of character, which is great for conversation. If there is a long wait when you arrive (no reservations), they'll call your cell phone when your table is ready! 

BYOT (Tequila)? Yes please. The margarita mixes are always fresh without being too sweet. Blood orange is totally awesome, and the hibiscus was such a special treat last summer.

I recommend Lolita to everyone I know. Cash only, so come prepared.

We have been to FW a few times. Always been happy. Good service, decent food, good prices, fine live music.
Last night failed on most counts
Good IPA. One catfish sandwich, more bun than fish. Diner described the fish as "eviscerated"
Hamburger was rated as just fine. Two (2) Ruben sandwiches were grilled to death. The bread almost burnt and cardboard like.
Got the bill, but I had a question. I looked around for our server, Jameson, or for that matter ANY server. None were in sight or attendance for 10 minutes. I waited, and waited, and waited, and finally left.

Wow. Wife and I used to come here a lot.  Great location and nice outdoor area on the water 

After arriving and being greeted several staff I proceeded to be ignored for the next 15 minutes until I finally left.  

As I left no one bothered to ask why I was leaving or thought it odd.   Was a real bummer as I had come to rather enjoy it there.  Kinda messes up your chi when you get settled then have to leave.  

Dumbfounded.

Beat sushi I've had in a while! And for decent prices too. Already dreaming when I can go back.

The sushi was fresh, looked good and the service was quick. I was able to try the Special Mexican roll, the Tempura Bagel roll and the Bloomingdale roll. I would get them all again, but my favorite was the tempura bagel roll. It's deep fried, so the salmon and cream cheese fillings comes out warm and super delicious.

Filthy, mediocre food, overpriced!! We almost walked out, we should have walked out!  I'm all about trying the local hole-in-the-wall places but this place was nasty! Where to start...the chairs, sugar packet holder, handrails, floor, all covered in a layer of grime.  I shudder at what the kitchen must look like if these were the common areas that the customer see. Then there was the food. It was mediocre at best and way overpriced. I've made better jambalaya from a box mix at home. Our waiter was nice, but even the lady at the front door who was all smiles while trying to get you in the door to eat, was kind of a b**** when we left. My husband said thanks and goodbye to her as we left and she barely acknowledge him. She looked right at him and kind of grunted a responce. Needless to say we will never be returning, and I highly recommend you don't waste your money. If I could give it zero stars I would.

My review is more about the service I received the other day as opposed to the food.

The food in my opinion is pretty good.

My experience was this:

I ordered delivery as I was stuck at work and completely unable to leave, I work less than a half mile from Shan Chuan.
When my food was delivered I mis-calculated the tip in my head and told the driver to just give me a five and keep the difference.
His immediate reaction was, "What? 50 cents? That's all your tipping me?"
I immediately realized my mistake and corrected my error only to have the driver walk off in a huff.

I didn't really think about it until later but they charge a premium for delivery, so if what I chose was to only give the driver fifty cents he should have been thankful to get it at all. Now I would never do that, but I've been a delivery guy and I didn't always get a tip, but I was always appreciative for every cent I got.

Oh yeah, and a $15 minimum for credit cards is ridiculous, I'm only one person.

I hope that someone from Shan Chuan reads this because I would certainly want to know that my employees are turning customers off to their service.

When we walked in the restaurant and saw many Vietnamese customers we knew this was the real deal.  Service was a little slow but the spare rib Pho was well worth the wait especially on a cold day.  I was unable to eat the whole portion of Pho so the server kindly brought me a to go carton.  The egg rolls were fresh and yummy.   This is definitely a must try place for tasty homemade Vietnamese food.
The pizza was perfectly made and the size was just right for one or two! The spaghetti was about as good as expected. The salad was really good too!
Pleasantly surprised with this new addition.  Delicious bowls (be sure to watch the monitors for pictures of every menu item!). Really fresh and tasty bowls!

Since the last updates, I have tried Jonny Primo's 3 more times and I am still reluctant to rate it. What a struggle. Finally, after I had dinner at Carrrabbas two blocks away last weekend, I decided to end it. Jonny, daring, I like you, but let's just be friend. 

Honestly, there is nothing wrong with Jonny Primo's. It is very popular for groups, families, parties, catering or just hang with your friends. Price are reasonable. Choices on food are variety and not bad taste. It is certainly a safe choice for most of folks. 

My problem of this restaurant is definitely the atmosphere. The layout is way too logical that I feel like I am still in the office. The staffs are way too well trained that it feels like you have been served by an I-Robot. The seats and carpet are way too clean that the only thing I smell is detergent, not mention smell it while you are eating. 

There is nothing wrong with Jonny, and nothing wrong with me! I guess it is just like those awkward moment it simply doesn't work out.

When I come here the staff is always friendly & very helpful fresh coffee. Great hoagies. Well cleaned store. If I need help finding something the staff is always there to help me out or even point me the right direction of what I'm looking for. I never had an issue finding what I'm looking for because they're always stock what I'm looking for at the time.
Decent breakfast, 2 eggs, totast & Hash browns $3.95...How can you beat that, open 24hrs, cash only!

They make great lattes and offer both soy and almond milk. The bagels they offer are really good, I just wish they had a larger variety. If Fa Caldo starting offering vegan cream cheese and vegan baked goods I would never leave.
The margaritas are great! Our bartender, Monica, was excellent! Her customer service were superb. Stop by for a food and drink and see Monica at the bar!

The location is great for people visiting STL or those of us who live on the east side and don't want to drive far to get Pi. We ordered a Lincoln Park with sausage added to 1 half. They messed up and gave us sausage only on 1 side. So they gave us that one and then re-made the correct pizza and comped both of them. Their customer service is great, their beer selection is great and the pizza is unique.

A friend and I ate dinner at the bar on Friday and had a great experience.  The margaritas were really good, quite sour but good.  I was surprised by how many wines by the glass were offered... we tried at least 3 of them... all quite good.  The guacamole is packed with huge chunks of fresh avocado, I would have preferred a bit less lime but would order it again.  I got the taco salad... normally I'd stay away from this type of item since "taco salad" at most places = fatty dressing, big tortilla bowls and loads of cheese, but not here.  The cumin vinaigrette is really spicy and not heavy at all, the grilled shrimp is generously tossed throughout the salad and the greens (piled high) were fresh as can be - by far the best salad I've had in awhile!  I totally wish this place were in my neighborhood.  The bartenders were excellent, friendly, fun and attentive.  The atmosphere is casual, the clientele was a mix of families eating dinner, couples, singles etc. (nice mix) the decor and lighting could be improved but I think it's a work in progress... they wanted to open up ASAP and I'm glad they did!

Amazing cocktails! Food is great and good portion sizes. The highlight of the night was our server. So friendly, yet zen and knew the menu well. Service is everything and The Love did not disappoint! I'll be back next time I'm in Philly!
The food is OK.  Rolls for sandwich good.  The manager (Sue?) just seems unhappy all the time and it reflects to the customers.    Don't need to deal with that when we are trying enjoy a meal.

You could blindly stumble into about any other bar or restaurant in this area and have a better experience. Everything is just "off"

Very high prices for mediocre Italian "mall" food- Think Brio, Macaroni Grill or Carrabba's quality, but you get to pay about 2-3 times more and have it served by sullen, snotty, gum chewing and way-too-cool to get you anything servers and bartenders. 

I've eaten at their NY location and the tragic-trainwreck Geisha in NYC. All bear the unmistakable mark of indifferent and incompetent management. I guess if you can afford an "A" location, you only need to "get" people once. I'm sure there will be plenty of fodder for them in Rittenhouse Sq.     

Three strikes for flat out bad service, non-existent hospitality and mediocre-poor food.

I went here last night on Yelp's recommendation and was less-than-impressed. 

First off, I should mention (at the risk of sounding like an idiot, which I probably was) that my boyfriend and I sat down at the wrong restaurant thinking it was Gnocchi. It wasn't. It was a Kebab House. Gnocchi is small and there's a small sign hanging outside, and the Kebab house was right past the sign so it seemed logical that it was Gnocchi. Plus the Kebab House had outdoor seating and Gnocchi didn't. In retrospect, maybe I would have liked the Kebab House better. 

We had the Caprese appetizer and the mozzarella was very delicious, but my main meal, the Tomato Basil Gnocchi with chicken, was alright at best. The sauce was extremely bland... I even sprinkled some salt in it to see if it would taste any better, and I almost NEVER use salt on anything. The bread they gave us was also bland, and a bit hard which made me think it was old and they just microwaved it so it was warm when it came to the table. Also it wasn't what I thought of as Italian bread, it seemed more like cornbread as it was yellow and grainy. 

My boyfriend said he really liked the food, but I tasted his sweet potato gnocchi and also thought it was boringly bland. 

Maybe if you like cardboard you could eat here, otherwise perhaps try the meat or fish because hopefully that's better than the pasta.

First thing first! Walked in, got a table, didn't even sit down and a cockroach walked across our table! So they offered us a new table and the manager came over and explained that roaches come in with deliveries (eh not acceptable enough of an excuse for a restaurant). We decided to stay because I wanted to try this place anyways. The food was alright, disappointed that they didn't have fresh juices on their menu. Nothing impressive about this place!

Usually don't write reviews, but couldn't resist. This place is fire. Literally one of the best sandwiches I've ever had. I would recommend the pickle&swiss sandwich. It's simple, but so bomb. If your in the area make sure to stop by and try it out.

I liked the environment and it was a nice place and the  Meatloaf,
Mashed potatoes that I ordered was really good and I will go back. It was my first time there and I enjoyed it and I would recommend this place.

Adele's is a great spot in The Gulch. We were visiting from Chicago and we were happy to find some great fresh local dining besides BBQ and fried food. The service was great and they have an awesome outdoor patio for dining. Great vibe!
Good thing this place ain't closer to my house or I'd be broke every payday ! The chargrilled oysters are amazing and some days a dozen just isn't enough ! I save up to go to this place and splurge !

I went here with an unlikely crowd for a business lunch. Me the lone vegan, and everyone else not even vegetarians.

The place is relatively small, but the upstairs is very nice. The server we had was excellent and the food arrived quickly, even for a group of 7.

Everyone really seemed to enjoy the food and I have to say that it was excellent. People in the party had the african stew, pad thai, and a few of us had the vietnamese hoagie. I also had the hot and sour soup. The soup was very good, as good as any vegan hot and sour I've had anywhere and was a nice large portion.

The hoagie was excellent, with just the right mixture of tofu, carrots, cucumber, hot peppers and cilantro. Really one of my favorite sandwiches I've ever had at a restaurant.

Once I go back (which I will the next time I'm in town), it might deserve the 5th star. I just need to go try some more things, but at this point, I think it's likely to be one of the better vegan places around. The hardest part will be whether to get the hoagie again or try something else. It's that good.

I've ran by Public Greens many times on my Monon runs and finally got to stop here a few weeks ago. It was a beautiful Indiana evening when I stopped and got to eat outside, by the Monon, for dinner, which was perfect. I now got to look at all of those runners/walkers exercising as I was dining on some good food. I was initially overwhelmed by the number of options available for the food choices. I decided to go with some of my favorites. I ordered the fried chicken, asparagus and banana pudding. All great choices! I love the 'pick-however-many-sides-you-want' concept. If felt socially accepted by picking 8 of the options, I definitely would have. The chicken was very crispy and juicy, with just the correct amount of spice and salt. It was well-balanced and not over salted or over fried. I got 4-5 pieces of tender white meat chicken. For the asparagus, it was simple but, very delicious. There was a light drizzle of balsamic and a sprinkling of salt to keep it simple and accentuate the flavors of the asparagus. The banana pudding was out of this world! The fresh whipped cream on top really took it to another level. There were heaping chunks of bananas hiding in the delicious banana pudding. I need to come back here often to try out the new options and menu offerings. Updates to come!

The food here was fantastic!! Stopped in based on the Yelp reviews and so glad I did! We started with the flower dumplings. Yum!! For my meal, I got the salmon that was on special and it was amazing!! Perfectly cooked! My cousin got the curry and that was also really awesome! The sauce was fantastic. I took advantage of the free dessert offer through Yelp and it was huge for being free. It was basically a plate of delicious!! I will definitely be going back here again!

The food was good and services was attentive without feeling like they were trying to rush you out. Place was packed but the noise was not so bad that you could not talk.

Staff friendly and helpful.

Was difficult to order over the phone. They kept asking me to spell my address. Very polite. I did not mind the confusion but it was time consuming. First try I never tasted the food yet. 

We switched to Franks for delivery. We go to Carlo's if we want to eat in and Italian Delight by weiss is great!

Like many others, I was excited about a new food option. 
I've tried Freddy's 3x prior to leaving a review. I've been left disappointed and underwhelmed each time. 

Today, I ordered lunch at 2:30pm. There was no line. I got the 3 strip combo and the bacon burger combo wrapped in lettuce.  I was told all the food is fresh. I advised that I prefer the mustard, ketchup and mayo in packs. I also asked could I have my food fresh (it was cold last time). When I got home. I have 1 order of fries, 1 burger, chicken strips,  the lettuce wrap was soggy because it was condiments on it and  I received two drinks which was carbonated water due to the soda needing to be replaced. The food is not hot (I live less than 5 minutes away). I have called the location at +1 (615) 462-5342 numerous of times, no one answers. I have never had a pleasant experience here. My total was $19.00 or so & honestly, it is not worth half of that. 

Now I'm home waiting on UberEats to bring Five Guys due me having a meeting.

Definitely a hidden gem among Gentilly restaurants. The hibachi rice is to die for as is most things on the menu. The sushi is pretty good and definitely has made me a repeat customer. While they do not sell alcohol, they definitely make up for it with the flavor and variety of the food.

Yep, reviewing another Mexican restaurant. Look for my review of Taco Bell next.

ANYway, since the husband and I can always agree on Mexican, and we were in downtown Bellevegas on  Saturday morning, we decided to give Margaritas a shot. This place...well...it looks like a grotto inside. Not the Playboy kind; the muddy, dirty, spelunking-and-miner's-hat kind of grotto. This doesn't faze me. I'm about enchiladas, not decor. 

Husband got a beer. I had three of the 99-cent margaritas (because I had to check the consistency of quality, of course). I liked them a lottttt. Ha. Seriously, from a mix, but not overly sweet, not overly strong...really one of the better margaritas I've had in a while. The salsa was quite good, too- one of my pet peeves with complimentary salsa is that a lot of places (especially in Southern IL) err on the side of tomato paste to make sure no one finds it "too spicy." This had a little more heat to it.

Don't really recall what my husband ate (I was pretty focused on the margaritas, remember), but I got another enchilada platter and this one was delicious. The enchilada sauce was more flavorful and the chicken enchilada had jalepenos in it. Excuse the Chicago homerism, but again I got sour cream and lettuce, but no beans/rice/guac....I'm confused about the condiment/side situation down here. It was a platter, after all, not the lunch special. But that's nothing that can't be remedied by ordering those things as sides; the prices are good.

Our sever was very cute, prompt, and efficient. After my third marg she grinned at me and said, "You want another, mama?" which just made me smile. Overall, I think this is my number one Mexican place (as of now)...and I'm definitely looking forward to having some cheap margaritas late-night at Margaritas After Hours.

I love the atmosphere of this place, and the food's darn good too!  We like to start with the Triple Dip (queso, guacamole, and bean dip) - all are fab and the chips are fresh, hot and crunchy!  I love the Painkiller as well ;-) and my sis likes their bloody Mary's.  You won't go wrong here!

Stopped in tonight around 6 pm.  The night crowd hadn't filled the place up yet so that made me happy.  

Decided on the buffalo burger and a side salad - the burger was superb, the salad was alright.  The house vinaigrette was decent but the salad was just chopped lettuce and carrot shavings. Meh.  My friend had the chicken parm mac and cheese - I enjoyed the bites I had, but it didn't blow me away (in fairness, I'm typically not into mac and cheese when dining out).

The service wasn't poor, but I wouldn't call it attentive either.  I wanted to get a draft Woodchuck after ordering our food, but whenever the server would check in with us she seemed to be trying to get away as fast as possible.  Sort of strange and I ended up giving up on the beer.  Overall experience was good and I'd definitely eat at The Lodge again.

This historic farm house served up decent food although the interior is very outdated. Fresh baked bread was complimentary but not that great. Everything else was surprisingly good. The calamari was not over cooked and had the right amount of seasoning. I usually prefer my marina on the side but it wasn't bad underneath the bed of lightly fried squid rings. Barely needed the sauce. I had the crab & shrimp cake sammy. At first glance, I just knew it was all filler. Well I was so wrong and enjoyed it along with the upgraded truffle fries. My man liked his short rib grilled cheese too. Nice to know we can get some good food in the area without traveling far.

The stench of Italian Market is not something you really want to endure on a hot July day when you have imbibed a little too much the night before.  Outdoor fish storage and rotting produce contribute to the olfactory presence of this Philadelphia outdoor market.  

On the plus side, if you get to know the vendors they will hook you up with the fresher fruit and veg.  Also, you have to insist that you don't want things in large quantities.  Trust me on this.  Unless you plan to eat everything that night, don't do it.  There are some great butchers and the original DiBruno's cheese emporium is on the street as well.  If it's seafood you are after, go to one of the indoor fish markets like Anastasi.  Skip the haddock with the fly droppings.

Great atmosphere and better food! Lou Bird's is a neighborhood gem. Highly recommend the dumplings and steak frites. After dinner Norris treated us to cheesecake on the house! Overall great experience - will definitely be back!

Definitely to here. The chicken bowl was delicious with Rice chicken beans. The staff was friendly and gets your refills and more WARM tortilla chips! If you're in Fishers and not looking for super fancy and/or a quicker really nice meal do make a visit! We'll be back!

This place is super rad! They took over the old Imperial Bar spot and I was surprised to see that the center bar was completely removed--it makes the space so much more open. Although I didn't play any of the arcade games, it seems like they have a large selection and even have a basketball game, air hockey, and skee ball, plus all the normal pinball and arcade type games. 

For the food: i got the fried cheese curds and the Nashville hot chicken sandwich and both were SO good. The cheese curds were crispy and the dipping sauces were bomb.
