I will say that they are best to eat right away--once they get cold they're not quite as good. The Nashville hot chicken was crispy, slightly spicy and very flavorful. It did seem to be missing something but I can't put my finger on it. Overall, it's very good though!

I'm definitely impressed with the food and I can't wait to come back and try more stuff and actually play some games!

Thought we would head out for a gourmet burger and they are open until midnight on Fri and Sat night! Score!  

The place sits a little too far off the road to have business that late at night.  We got there around 10pm Sat night and there was one other table of people there.  

They make their own beverages and they are so much more flavorful than a "fanta orange soda".  The rootbeer tasted great as well.  They offer a variety of microbrews as well as a craft bourbon selection if you are interested.

The blu burger had a lot of flavor complete with cajun seasoning which i wasn't expecting but tasted great with the blue cheese.  The bacon bbq burger needed more bbq sauce which they gladly provided.  Even the manager said she thought there was never enough bbq sauce on the burger(seems to soak into the bread).

We tried the sweet potato chips, fries, and the twisted mac and cheese.  Wish everything wasn't a la carte.  Seems a little expensive in that regard.  

Do not be fooled.. .  .. the train entertains more than just the kids.  Every time I went to say something, my boyfriend (in his 30s) was watching the train go around the room.
Really good sushi.. Too bad they don't know their own menu  got my order wrong twice in a single sitting. I'll try again next time, but will probably order delivery. The service was a little awkward.

My husband eats here weekly for lunch and we eat here for dinner or order take out.  The staff is friendly ready to please you.  The soups are delicious! I've had the rare beef and brisket and the chicken Pho.  I've also had the wonton soup which is awesome as well!  My husband enjoys their various dinner plates as well.  I tend to stick to the soups because that's what I love.  I highly recommend Pho Sunrise.

If I could give zero stars I would! The shrimp and pork dumpling soup tasted the way the inside of a pig farm smells...I am not kidding.  The General Tso was a lump of breaded chicken strips with thick nasty sauce, jelly like in consistency, with no flavor. Questionable food...possible crack den?  We will not be back!

I just love blue moon. It's such a hidden gem. Here I go spilling the secret about how great it is. Anyway, tonight I went by myself for the first time and just ate at the bar. (*My intent with this was to not look a screen, which I had done all day. Yet here I am again.) I politely mentioned that she may just want to know that the chicken was slightly underdone. (Which it was and for some reason I always check now cause this girl in college was very particular about it.) She informed the manager and they were both really cool about taking it off and thanking me for letting them know. There was no charge so I just tipped in cash! (Tip your servers!) 

Anyway

Best place I ate after spending almost a week in New Orleans 
"1.Customer Service was amazing 
2. The food was great

YUM!   Drive on past the chain restaurants and stop at Dales.  Outstanding chicken n dumplings.   Nicely seasoned.  Didn't add a thing to them.  Tender chunks of white meat chicken were plentiful.    Green beans had a nice bacon flavor.  Daughter had meatloaf also awesome and NOT covered in catsup.    Son-in-law had nice size portion of country fried steak which he enjoyed as well.  And service was fast and friendly.

Really interesting tiki spot to stumble in to. Lots of variety on the menu. Prices range from like $8 to $16 for a cocktail (if I'm remembering right). Staff were super cool and attentive. Didn't try the food but will next time I'm in Philly.

Pizza is ok. The couple times we got it was like night and day though, so you have to take your chances. Guess it depends on how the cook feels.

If you go to pick it up you'll probably have fun. Entering the dining/storage area is interesting. Some tables to eat at, while others are blocked by boxes and other items.

 You can watch the flat screen  tv, or enjoy the cashier argue with the pizza maker..awesomeness!!

They finally seem to be open on Sundays, now just clean up the building inside and out they might have something!

With all the other pizza shops in the area they need to do something.

We were in town for a conference and went here for lunch. The food was okay, however our server was the rudest server I have ever had in my life. She was short with us and rushed us. We had questions about the menu and the prices and she was so rude when I asked I requested the manager. I would not recommend this place based on service alone.
Our favorite hideout in New Orleans. Terrific drinks and chill loungey vibes. A good reason to get that old smoking jacket out. Noah took great care of us.

My husband and I enjoyed our cinnamon bun and peanut butter chocolate donut. The Thai iced coffee was also very good, as were the cheese fries. We went on a Monday, and I was disappointed that there was no mint julep donut, and the chicken biscuit is not served after 11 am. Overall, we enjoyed the delicious donuts, but I agree that the woman working the counter was too hip/ jaded for me. Smiles are free, you know?

We recently relocated from New York, and a friend gave us a gift card for Ava. I am glad he did. This is our go-to now. We adore this place.

The vibe is cool, the decor is Great. Most importantly the food is superb. We have learned what to order and it works for us. Roasted vegetables, polenta, pork belly, house salad. Wine. Good wine.

What I love most about ava is the simple preparation. There is nothing worse than overly complicated preparations that are executed poorly. We see a decent amount of that here in Tampa. Get the fucking basics right first. Ava consistently gets simple things right. What's not to love? 

One dish which is really good is cacio e pepe. I had this many times in Rome. It is an ancient Roman dish of pasta, cheese and pepper. Simplicity perfected. If you have had this in Rome you will understand. Ava does a respectable job with this. Rome? Not quite, but damn good.

Charcuterie is fantastic. 

Avoid chicken liver app unless you are anemic and need iron. 

Oh, and the wait staff is great. Friendly. On point. Flannel works in this instance. Don't get it, but whatever.

Keep it simple and enjoy. Don't listen to the haters they ordered wrong I believe.

I have been to Bin + Board twice now to get the full experience and I must say I'm impressed. They only serve wine and charcuterie boards. Their wine selection is amazing and they cater to everyone's palate. I am more of a red wine lover and they have some tasty Cabernet Sauvignons. I also really love their "popping bubbles" flight.

The charcuterie boards are great as well. I have tried the chefs board which I believe changes regularly and I like the pairings of the meats and cheese that it had. I also liked that each board comes with a basket of bread. The star of the show however, was the dessert board. I thought it was amazing, with my favorites being the chocolate mascarpone and the cranberry cinnamon goat cheese. It was just so delicious! Definitely will be back for more wine and dessert!

Pros: The chicken is awesome and a fair price. The spicy honey is what makes it so good. Cool atmosphere. Great outdoor area. Good music.

Cons: Everything else on the menu besides the chicken is average. Beer selection is mediocre.

Needed a quiet breakfast.  Looking forward a JIB superior meal and service experience.  Very disappointed.  Don't come here for breakfast. 
The hash browns were overlooked, tough, and old. 
There was a dog roaming all over the dining room. He was very friendly but not under the control of the owner.  Even though he had a service dog vest he would go from table to table looking for food. He should be right next to his owner at all times.  Service dogs are not supposed to fed or touched.  They have a job to do.  This service dog was clearly not performing his duties.  Management did not appear to care.  Even though this was my first visit to this restaurant it appeared his presence was a normal practice.  

Staff and service dog and owner need training here.

Owner is a complete tool bag and a**hole. Visited Reading Terminal with my pregnant wife. Ate at Keven Parkers [highly recommended] and came here to purchase beverages since KP only served Iced Tea and wife was craving a soda. Paid $6 for 2 fountain drinks which were overly full with ice. Wife finished hers rather quickly and needed another drink to wash her food down. Returned to the window and asked politely if they had a refill rate for the soda. He rudely looked up and said "no not if all you did was buy a soda to go". The nice young lady on the other side went to reach for my cup to refill for my wife and he interjected and said "i already told him no".  All of the waitresses looked around confused bc they clearly offer refills. I told the waitress forget it ill buy a whole new drink. She refilled my drink and mouthed "sorry i would have just refilled but this is his bar". TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE!!!  Then he had the nerve to eyeball me up and down like he wanted to do something about the fact i told the waitress that was really bad customer service. I woulda rocked that little guys world. Will never patronize this place again after $9 worth of watered down soda and an owner with a Napolean complex. Good thing my wife was with me or the the conversation would have went much  differently. EAT ELSEWHERE! Way too many delicious options around to put up with sub par Customer Service and sh**ty ownership. Happy New Year!

Love ODB. Their new location isn't quite as atmospheric as the old one on Santa Barbara St, but it's still the same great food! Their kitchen closes early, but if you're looking for a roll, a coffee, and some amazing cookies for a low price, it's the place to go.

So we went there as group. I didn't complain. 
But if you want a lump of extremely over cooked angel hair pasta with your shrimp.  Please come here. 

There are better places that don't use their name from yesteryear to charge you outlandish prices for crap.

One of my favorite art museums. It's small enough to tackle in one day but large enough were you can come back many times and always learn something new. It's like a smaller version of NYCs Metropolitan Art Museum and NYC's Cloisters combined. I say that because they've got a number of recreated or authentic rooms reassembled from different cultures and periods in addition to the normal rooms and halls full of beautiful paintings and sculptures from most periods and countries. The museum is also very beautiful and is where the most famous scene of Rocky was shot. Feel free to run up the steps while humming "Eye of the Tiger" then stand where Sylvester Stalone stood, or just stand back and watch people from all over do just that. The top of the steps offers the best view of Philly for those who'd like to just get that perspective while the statue in front of the Museum is a wonderful piece of art as well (definitely worth walking around and climbing up on for a better view). 

If you appreciate art to any extent your trip to Philly would seriously be lacking without a trip to this museum.

If you're feelin' simple, but gluttonous, this is the spot. Comfort food taken up just a notch to plain deliciousness.

Got the mac n cheese bites appetizer, and the bbq pulled pork mac grilled cheese. 

The appetizer comes with 4 [large] blocks of fried, breaded mac n' cheese with a cheese dip.  It's nothing world-class but, hey, we thoroughly enjoyed it!  The mac is the larger shell type with a creamy sauce.  No Velveeta/Kraft aftertaste here.

My sandwich was great--thick buttery white bread sandwiching one of the above mac n' cheese bites, pulled pork in bbq sauce, fried pickle, and red onion. 
The flavors balanced nicely and I was honestly surprised by how good the pulled pork was.  The onion and fried pickle complimented everything well.  

(And no, I was not maxed out on mac n' cheese by the end of all this)

Fries have a lot of room for improvement--they were both soggy and bland.  
Staff is genuinely friendly, and be sure to pay attention to the funny wall art.

I could only imagine how heavenly Steve's is when you're intoxicated, but either way, I recommend.

Today I had my first W. It was good, crazy good. I had the Thai wrap. I needed some of that soy sauce business, but other than that it was great. I felt multi-ethnic whilst eating a Thai wrap and having chips and salsa. It was pretty surreal.

Super delicious vegan food. I can eat this food every single day. The food here makes me feel that I can go totally vegan one day. 
Loved their pineapple kimchi dumplings and buffalo cauliflower. Pad Thai was yummy. Our server was great. Overall a relaxing evening

Service is friendly but definitely not fast.  A very casual pace at this restaurant.

There were only two other people dining, or should I say waiting for their food, in the restaurant but still service was extremely slow.  My flight was leaving out of gate A-17 right next door so I was prepared to leave without food if my flight boarded before my food was ready.

The menu is rather limited and they were out of some things.  I ordered a grilled cheese and pickle chips after they were out of my first choice.

The server kept me updated on the status of my order, which I appreciated.  Food is good but definitely not a place to eat if you don't have extra time.  The atmosphere here is slow and casual which isn't as good fit for an airport restaurant.

I took my food to go and the server brought it out just seconds before I had to board, so it worked out.  My grilled cheese was burned but the fries were good.   Probably won't attempt to dine here again unless I have time to spare.
Food was great with one exception: my meal came with sautéed bok choy. It was full of grit. We were a large party and other members had the same issue.
Great food, super fast service and decent prices.  Atmosphere is typical, but expected.  Chimichanga was great, chips are good, salsa average but with a great spicy kick.

I had a lovely evening there with my girlfriend tonight. Our waiter, Louie, was very polite and accommodating. I told him I was sensitive to sodium and he made sure the Thai Basil stir fry I had wasn't cooked with soy or salt. A lot of places will tell you they will have the cook leave out the salt but then you get the dish and it's the Dead Sea. Not the case here. It was very clear from the taste that Louie relayed my request, and it was still delicious. Thank you.

So upset, I was very excited reading reviews to come here however the server basically ignored us and served the couple who came in after us since they are Cuban. Rude. If you want quick Cuban food and are not Cuban, go somewhere else. We left after being ignored for 12 minutes. I'm in a bad mood and very hungry now, thanks a lot stupid restaurant. And by the way, we came in at 3:30 pm

Dinner and drinks were excellent. We had tortilla soup, mahi mahi tacos and chicken tacos. Really delicious. It's loud, so not the right place if you're looking for a quiet romantic dinner. Our waitress, Elena was great. Attentive and very fun to talk to. I definitely recommend this place and will return.

This pizza place is great. The family affair combo is a great deal. They have some of the best to go breadsticks also. They have a very good buffet also. The good breadsticks are not at the buffet though.

Laid-back atmosphere, cozy booths, good drinks, great service. This is not a place for foodies, or the health-conscious,  but an excellent and comfortable place to get a drink and some excellent bar food. The battered onion rings are one of my favorites, as well as the cheesesteaks, club sandwiches, and wings. They have a bottle-shop inside as well so you can take something to go.
awesome! super cute outdoor/open counter and seating. very nice staff and very tasty coffee!!!! loved it

I have been passing this place for years and finally today we went to eat there,  being from Europe I have a hard time finding good italien food but this place was really good.  Lots of flavor in their food.  I had the spaghetti with meatballs and soup,  my husband had the salad and green chili carbonara and it was also very good.   Definitely going back to try other food.  Oh and the service was very good as well.
Very good food and service. Overall, I'd rate this place 9/10. It'd be 10/10, but in my opinion, the food took a little longer than I hoped but not too long. Maybe 5-10 minutes.

I've never had greek food and this was a great experience. We sat outside and it was GORGEOUS, our table was spaced out and we had plenty of room to talk and enjoy our night. We ordered a few appetizers, three drinks, and a desert to go and it was $130! Caesar Salad came with grapes and grilled romaine which is a great touch. The ribs were really mustardy, you don't eat stuff like that too often it was great. I loved the octopus, the texture was great and the grilled lemon added a lot of flavor. This is a great date night spot, the staff was great, and I can't wait to try their brunch!

Best Chinese in town! Love their walnut chicken, XO Fried rice, and of course dumpling courses for lunch. We order takeout frequently and their food is ready so quickly that I have to get in the car to pick up as soon as I order. I live 10 minutes away.

I usually come here for breakfast, have had their egg platter paninis - it's a lot of food since it comes with fruit! I don't think the eggs are fresh (seem like they are poured out) but it's still decent for the price. The cinnamon rolls are to die for, the tarts are good (not the best). To be honest, you can get the smoothie bowls down the street at Stripp'd Juice for the same price and much better quality. HOWEVER the best thing I ever ate here was their Lox Bagel - it's on an everything bagel and loaded with delicious cucumber, cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers, and tomato. YUM!!

For lunch, I've only gotten their spicy dragon sandwich, which is very good.

There is nothing special about the food here, especially for their price point.  Nothing was particularly bad, just nothing to write home about.  My po-boy was meh...  wish it had more sauce.  Just not impressed.... the bar looks cool, but packed tables makes moving about the dining room a smidge complicated, and seems to impede servers, forcing them to reach across diners to refill water glasses.  For what we paid, I have had much better experiences.

Ordered the chicken sandwich, pan pizza with pepperoni and curly fries. Buffalo Chicken sandwich was good, lots of chicken. Fries were just tossed in a brown bag. Pepperoni on top of pizza was charred and sauce was loaded with salt. Extremely salty, so much so that sauce tasted funny.
Burnt end skillet was sub-standard at best. Would not recommend for food but the band was great.

If you want to get a table, grab food and drinks on a Saturday night before the crowd comes, it's best to get their before 10:00p. The food was pretty good, pricey but good. I recommend the steak. By 10:30p-11:00p, it got really crowded and the place is not that big, it's also hard trying to get a server because the place is so crowded after a certain time but overall I had fun.

Ah! The new Family Wash is the best. THE BEST!

I will miss the old space, but no looking back. This was the right decision for them. They needed to expand and by partnering with Garage Coffee they really hit the jackpot. They also have a larger stage for the music so you don't feel like you are on top of them.

I really have nothing bad to say about the new Wash. Their expanded menu is wonderful! I loved the buccatini. A lot. I smelled it one night and I had to come back and eat it. The new cocktails are fun, especially the peach one. The wine on tap was also delightful. 

They really nailed it with the seating. The outdoor benches are great for groups or cozying up in the corner. The inside tables let you still feel like you are in the action, but you can lean back a bit. The inside has a bunch of tables with the stage raised in front. 

This place is perfect for larger groups, families, intimate dinners with live music, and guests. You cannot go wrong with the new Wash!

This is a really good place at a good value.  I would recommend this for lunch and or dinner.  The Sushi is fresh and they deliver.  Good creativity with their specials and very nice service.  I hope they make it and would recommend it to anyone.

First time passing through Nashville and we had our daughter's dog with us, so when looking for pet friendly patio, we came across this place.  We hit the jackpot!  Great service, incredible food, excellent beer selection.   Hoping to be back and this will be in our list!

My fiance heard about this place from a co-worker so we tried it out.  Glad we did.  This is on the edge of a private airfield & a bunch of yachts are in sight so the ambiance is unlike any other place I have seen.  Some of these patrons clearly flew in from places like Key West or Danbury Connecticut but every body is laid back.  We were here on a Wednesday & the cheeseburgers are half price ($6 bucks) & they were delicious.  The fries were nothing to write about, but the full service bar made up for it.  We sat outside, which was ok, but the next time I think we'll stay inside (this is Florida, LOL)  & enjoy the AC & one-man band.  This is a great place to meet with friends & just relax.
Lamb gyro meat was over cooked and the food overall was nothing special. The placed was packed so I was hoping for better. I would not go out of my way to go back. Lunch for two was about $25.

Excellent breakfast place. Great service - plenty of delicious coffee. I've had the sausage gravy waffles and the Kate. Tasting my friends' food, I don't believe there's a bad piece of food on their menu.

Great atmosphi and a good selection of drinks! I didnt get to eat so no comment on that..
There was a band singing and and dancing going on..
some old fokes take the seats on the bar...
diffrent age groups in the place.

Favorite lunch spot. The food is very consistent and fresh. My favorites are the padinis. The Tacchino-turkey, savory mayo, house-made cranberry sauce, fontina cheese, caramelized onions and the Tuna Carciofo-white tuna salad, artichokes, red onion, roasted tomato, pepperoncini, garlic spread, provolone.
Worst experience.... The behaviour of the manager is not at all professional. He is very arrogant towards the customers.. I will not suggest this to any one.

This was the first spot my wife and I went to getting to NO, and I must say we did not make a mistake at all. We had the catfish poboy and the seafood gumbo. Very delicious and authentic. My wife kept rambling about it. We ended up going back the next night and got the poboys again. 

Great stuff!

A pretty average milk tea. Nothing particularly wrong with it, but nothing stood out either. I got their signature milk tea so that I hopefully got their best milk tea. The black tea was pretty flavorful and didn't taste like the same from-concentrate tea that many places in Reno have. But I feel like the milk to tea ratio was off and the flavor was just boring.
Wait staff was excellent.   Recommendations were awesome.  Bestest margaritas in Nola

The service was pretty good. The food was not.  It was too salty.  

octopus: mushy 
lamb gyros: cold meat that was really hard to bite into
melitzanosalata: it's just mushy eggplant
The bread that came for the spreads was so salty. We will not be coming back
Best Indian in downtown St. Pete for sure. The lunch buffet is the greatest! The staff are all very nice and friendly. The place is clean and has beautifully decorated. Love it!

I drove 11 miles to get to this coffee shop. I usually just go to a coffee shop near by to study, but decided to check this place out! And it's pretty cozy and good place to study. good coffee and good chocolate muffin and it's good! :)

It was a bit load just b/c there were people talking load, but it's cool. I saw another girl studying as well.

Stopped in here for a quick snack. Had the Char Grilled Oyster as you would have guessed from the a few of my previous posts. These were very tasty and I liked that the oyster's came with several pieces of bread. Now lets talk about those Fried Pickles, the breading on them was so lite that the pickle really stand out( which I really like). What is really nice is this is on a side street that I bet is overlooked often. The old World Charm inside looks like it's been here forever. The inside is very clean and very cool, considering it was 98 degrees when were were here. This is another staple must try if you are traveling through, or staying for a bit.

Love this location in st Charles!! Food great, service is fast and great. Barbecue ribs there are insane. 
Love the bread, and the drinks are great too.

This is a perfect happy hour location. The menu was great for happy hour -- great drink selection and food. We ordered the potato pizza and I had wine. It's a great place to wine(d) down after work with an amazing subtle atmosphere. The only thing that was a little weird was the loud train that was right behind the restaurant. The service was also amazing and everyone there was helpful and friendly

The Salad Rolls and Brisket Pho were the best. I visited Vietnam earlier this year and I would say Lilly's Pho is a close as it gets to eating the same dish in Vietnam. The server was very friendly. It was a little cold since they were hauling in food stuffs at the time but the delicious food made up for it.
The meals are a little slower, I would order lunch before going there, but other than that the service is friendly and the food is really good. Very pet friendly.  :)

Update: immediately after posting the review below the owner reached out to me to resolve the issues. Long story short, after seeing my review, they added a kid's brunch menu. I appreciated ownership being open to feedback and willing to enhance customer experience based on that feedback. I haven't had a chance to visit again but plan to in the future now that they are a kid friendly restaurant in a family oriented neighborhood. 

Visited Chesheim after three visits and I unfortunately have to say it was horrible. To start, my bf asked to taste two beers on tap. The waiter showed up with full size beers that we decided to drink anyway because he clearly didn't listen to the request. We visited with my daughters and asked for a kids brunch menu. He let us know he could make any brunch menu item in a kids portion. He showed up with regular portions when the food came out. We asked for the check and realized we were charged adult prices for their meals. I asked him about it and he shrugged and said, "yeah".... After waiting 15 minutes he finally came back and ran our card for the bill. Service is very important to me and I have to say this visit is enough for me not to return. The restaurant was not full at all during peak brunch hours. There is a reason for that. I won't be surprised if they are not in business for another six months.

Sunday afternoon? Don't bother. No one would wait on us. Five of us sat at the end of the bar for about 10 minutes. Someone--maybe a bartender--looked at me and made eye contact. Then turned and walked around and walked the other way. We all left.

Great menu options - everything looked so tempting that it was hard to choose! We ordered takeout (I decided on the big Italy bowl), and the server seemed slightly annoyed for whatever reason. My bowl was delish, but when I got home I realized that the pomodoro sauce was missing. Luckily I had some red sauce in the fridge. May return to try the dine-in experience.

This was a great breakfast place.  I will be back to try other items, for sure.  I was really surprised that this place existed but happy I got to eat their food.  Their onion rings look super yummy, a guilty pleasure of mine. 

The restaurant brought me back to a Long Island Diner I used to go to when I was a kid.  If you like Diner type foods and atmosphere, come here!!

The service was quick and friendly and we weren't rushed like Olive Garden.  It was laid back, friendly, clean and not too crowded.  

I look forward to coming back.  Thank you.

One word folks: QUESO!

After walking around and having done some shopping, we were in need of a place to rest our feet and fill our bellies with a light snack. Turns out this place makes a pretty darn amazing queso dip that what we intended as a pre-dinner meal became an excessive indulgence. We ordered bowls of this concoction that didn't even look appealing to the eyes. A light-ish yellow in somewhat watery consistency was one of the best things I ate on this trip. It came with endless refills of warm and fresh tortilla chips which made it harder to stop munching. Don't forget their guac to go with this and of course, frozen margaritas to wash everything down. Cheers!
Great service ! their food was really good. we had the chicken and waffles, the club sandwich, the Ruben sandwich. They Offer you water or tea rite away. Very welcoming place

Awesome pizza! I haven't had much else but I also really liked their calamari. Pre-COVID, it was always busy so once the restaurant fully opens up expect a 30-40 minute wait before food is ready for pick-up.

We only came for drinks so I can't comment on the food but the service was very good, and the atmosphere seemed very inviting. Drink prices were fair and they kept them coming. Clean bathrooms.
Would love to try the food sometime but it is definitely kind of off the beaten path.
We are staying here just for a night and decided to try this place. The wings were super good and I would highly recommend. The lady who gave us our wings was super nice as well.
Very friendly staff and excellent food. The chicken schwarma was fantastic. We got our food quickly and it was very fresh. The place was spotless. Highly recommend! Support local!

Best bagels and donuts I've been able to find outside of the NJ/NYC area. Great service as well and really clean. 

Don't let the outside appearance fool you. 

This place is a real gem!
Great place to try! Delicious food! Very friendly and helpful waitress! It was our first time! Awesome dessert as well!

Best find since moved to IRB! Brings fresh imports and baked goods like my grand mother made, xxoo...home made Italian sausage, olive salads, rum cake, fresh pasta, no need to drive to west Tampa. Ippolito is awesome local spirit and service, glad to know I can get my favorites a couple miles from home. Subs hot and cold, prepared dinners for the nights I do not want to cook, and fixings needed to prepare my favorite Italian dishes. Yum is all I can say! Bravo!

This place always has the best service! Great place to celebrate birthdays or any occasions. They are great at setting up reservations for big parties! And the service is great!  My favorite food item here is the green curry. So flavorful!  The great thing about this place is not only is the food amazing! The drinks are yummy as well . I don't like going downtown due to parking. But this place has its own lot with lots of parking! I highly recommend this place!
Some of the best Mex. food in this area.  We have been dining here for years.  Always clean, great good, and great service.

This place has gone downhill for the last several months. It's very conveniently located for me so begrudgingly, I have continued to go 
now and then. Tonight though is my last time. Not only has the fish become questionable but tonight the service was nonexistent. I sat at the sushi bar for 10 minutes all the while watching servers walk back-and-forth past me. After never being so much as  looked at, let alone asking if I would like a drink or maybe to order some food, I left.  It's very sad but I highly recommend avoiding this restaurant. It's not what it used to be. It's terrible in all aspects.
The brunch is good, Bloody Mary's are excellent. Service was good but hostess is horrible. The acoustic musician needs to go but at least the food and drink are good.

This is a really wonderful quaint coffee shop/breakfast place located in Old North St. Louis. This place has a really cozy and relaxed atmosphere with really friendly people. I go to Crown Candy quite often but I had never been to this place across the street until recently. The best part is that the food is very good but it's also very inexpensive at the same time. I got a French onion soup and a slinger to eat, and a lavender Italian soda to drink. Everything was great, but the atmosphere is what stood out above everything else.
I can attest bluefin tuna is significantly better than anything I've ever tried before. Ken set me up with a beautiful sampler platter and I would highly recommend eating here.

I was lucky enough to plan an event last night with Creekside! It was 300 people, but they handled it extremely well. The food, bartenders, security, atmosphere, and everything was amazing, everyone had the best time. I highly recommend!

Two words for you.  Cuban. Eggrolls. 

I can't understand why I drove by this place for so long and never stopped by.  Being "Mystery Thursday", were we pick a place we've never been, this place came up the winner.  So we stuffed into a car and headed over for lunch. 

The atmosphere is cool and weird at the same time.  Located right off Kennedy, there's a lot of concrete around but the atmosphere inside is cozy and relaxed.  Service was decent, but the star of the show were the Cuban eggrolls. 

OMG. 

Think Cuban sandwich in an eggroll wrapper instead of Cuban bread, then deep fried. It's this kind of item that keeps the pounds coming back.  It was amazing!

I had the strawberry champagne salad and added chicken. It was good, but I prefer the strawberry salad from Longhorn.  I also had one shrimp taco from one of the other folks in my party, and that was very good. The turkey sandwich on ciabatta looked ok but the bread was a bit hard according to the person that ordered it.  I also tried the sweet potato fries and nachos.  They were both ok. 

I liked this place. I'm going with three stars right now, but I will be back to try other items and perhaps revise my rating.  For now I can recommend this place.

Meet Noodles is def one of the most authentic places to get noodles in Nashville. I was especially hungry tonight and ordered the pumpkin cake snacks and the Kim's Beef Noodles. 

When the noodles came out, I was completely shocked about the size of the bowl! They give you a lot (and I was very excited)... The beef was a little chewy, but with a little adrenaline and some Superman strength, it was easy to get through and was delicious!

Now the pumpkin cake snacks... These were the star of the night for sure. These piping hot bite sized cakes were both crispy and soft, savory and sweet, and definitely more of a dessert than a snack/appetizer. Seriously... I could probably order 3 servings and eat them all and be happy with just that for dinner. You. Must. Try. Them. ASAP

The food is probably a 4 for me, but the cleanliness of the dining area is a 2. So we'll settle on a 3. My wife and daughter really like this place. We've been to multiple locations in Missouri, Georgia, and Florida. They have all been clean except this one. We arrived at 4:45 and no one was there except the workers. As we walk in and through the restaurant to order our food, we notice right away the floor was really dirty with trash everywhere. Really dirty. The trash cans were overflowing. All of them. The entire time we were there no other customer came in to eat. Just us. Maybe between the lunch rush and dinner they could do some cleaning and take out the trash. Just maybe.
Outstanding breakfast again. This is a must visit every time we come to town to visit our daughter at college.

I am a local and been to several locations by far this is the worst! I believe that because of the busy location and catering to many visitors they have become robotic and not personal at all. Ordered drinks was carded and it was my birthday no acknowledgement. My server Dior was rude and unpleasant, must be unhappy. This is a hospitality city embrace it. Food was good.

This is really a note to the owners who seem dedicated and have some great choices on the menu. 

When it comes to your menu keep it simple and do it well.  REALLY WELL. 

Train your staff. We have asked about different dishes and been told "I've never tasted it" or "I don't know"....they should be familiar with the food....meaning they have eaten it. But more importantly, speed up, introduce yourself, smile and if diners are open to it make suggestions. 

You have a great concept, location and opportunity - don't be mediocre when you can be regarded highly.

Came to this subway cause I recently moved and it's the closest to my house when I got there a little before 6 each table had a chair on top of it, when I pulled up I thought maybe they had closed for some reason? But the open sign was on so I went in,  when I asked for herbs and cheese bread they were out and I could see that no bread was being made at 6 in the evening  to only have white or wheat bread and nothing else doesn't seem right to me.  The girl who served me was very nice though.

I tried the Rice House out recently and to be honest, I was a little let down by the food. It is a small space but has plenty of options on the menu. I placed an order online to pick up via Postmates and the order was ready in a timely manner. The staff were friendly and accommodating as well.

I ordered the Hot Braised Chicken Wings Combo Plate. The food wasn't the worst but it could definitely be improved. I was very underwhelmed by the quality of the chicken; especially for the price of almost $10. It was barely edible and I left disappointed wishing I'd gone to my local Chop Suey instead. Perhaps I picked a bad entree but I am willing to give this place another chance. I will update my review upon my next visit.

Oh, how I adore Etch. On my list of the 5 best restaurants in Nashville. The food has constantly and consistently been amazing. My only (small) gripe is pricing, but for a date spot or once a month splurge, it's perfectly reasonable and well worth the decor, service, and food quality.

For a relaxing evening with fresh Italian food, good wine, nice service El Fresco style try Porta Via Italian Kitchen!  The flat bread pizza with arugula and tomatoes was fabulous!  Loved the fresh cherry tomatoes and arugula on a crispy, crunchy flat bread crust!  For the cheesier crowd, the Margherita pizza was raved by the young adults!  The salad was fresh, the minestrone was chock full of vegetables and the wine selection was nice and the prices were reasonable.  We dined on the porch on a warm spring evening and we left relaxed and happy, wearing our smiles.  The service was very, very nice, extremely attentive.  The only negative would be ... NOTHING!  We loved Porta Via Italian Kitchen!  Mama Mia!

I'd also like to boost this place and clear up a few misconceptions.  In my experience, gutterpunks do not work here, though they certainly congregate outside sometimes.  It's the winter migration, people; these things happen. 

The actual staff is pretty cool. Maybe late at night you get some stoners, but stoners working the late-night cafe shift are as wholesome and American as anything else.

Besides, you can get coffee with alcohol in it here. And it's not too expensive. This cannot be stressed enough.  Have the friendly guy at the counter whip you up a Mexican-style hot cocoa/chili pepper thing with some tequila.  Then get yourself a cannoli and quit yer whinin'.

Of the three coffee shops on this part of Baltimore, this one is the least crowded and the smallest.  It has a cool Afro-beatnik feeling as opposed to the preppie-hipster Green Line or the Anarcho-grungy Satellite.  All of which are great but have different strengths.  I probably wouldn't hang out and study here because it's sort of dark, but I would definitely meet a friend and enjoy the dark coolness below ground (summer) or the cozy warm glow (winter).

I like Pier One's coffee-- a nice nutty roast, though I'm no big connoisseur.  I hear that I need to try their lunches because so far all I've had is their decent, not fabulous and not homemade pastries.  No Baltimore ave coffee shop has homemade baked goods.  What's up with that.

edit-- I stand corrected.  this place does have breakfast, good homemade egg and pancake kind of stuff.  Bagels are subpar, but what are you going to do.
Don't sit in the 'courtyard'. It smells like sewer. And cigarettes. I decided to forgo my meal after being seated.

Food here is pretty good. The hot & sour soup is awesome! Not the best Chinese food ever but great for quick take out close to home. Try sesame chicken, generals chicken, crab Rangoon, hot & sour soup, bean curd w/ veggies, and beef pepper steak.

I was not happy with the SERViCE, and I came in on a Friday nite, was very busy. I was never greeted and was ignored, had to ask for help to be seated and i explained it was my 1st time there, and ended sitting at the sushi bar,  Never got a hello glad your here?? My server was Nate? Had to ask other servers to help me, they took forever for me to get my sushi, Mind you the sushi was great but the Overall experience was bad, will never go again one star for sushi/.

Offering dine in and patio now after the Covid shutdown. 

Very nice interior and a relaxing setting. 

Full bar available as well as a wine list. 

Great food and quick service.

Stopped by for a meal before a play next door at the Forrest, Hamilton.

We sat at the bar. Service was friendly, prompt and courteous. We sat down at ~5pm. The place was not crowded a few folks sitting by the window tables. By 545pm it was filling up.

Two glasses of white burgundy. We started by splitting escargot in puff pastry. Very tasty. Sauce was rich and creamy. Could have easily gotten another.

Mains were moules frites and a beef slider. The mussels were petite but plump and clean. Wonderful flavor with creme fraiche. The slider was a good, small burger. Nothing special.

The fries that came with both dishes were crispy warm and delicious. Clearly just made. 

We are staying in town tonite but it would be hard to beat this place right next door to the theatre, for a play nite.

One suggestion: install a bar rail for the feet. We have been to many bars and the idea of a foot rest attached to the bar is so common sense that it irks me when they do not have one. 

We will return when in the neighborhood.

Nancy & Mark.

You have to try this place! Especially in the winter!  Their noodle soups are so delicious!  I also love getting the chicken curry and rice and also the bbq chicken and rice dishes.  Their iced coffee is excellent too! Have gone here often since discovering the place and will keep going back.  The place can be crowded during peak hours though, but not too bad and people usually get a seat right away.  Great place! :)

This is a dynamic place - I'd imagine it's great to hang there after work and grab a couple of nice beers. It's decent for dinner too, but I want to talk about the burgers. DON'T GET THEM.

A burger needs to have all the right components. Monk's burgers are served on quite possibly the WORST roll ever. Very tough, very thick, and it ruins the entire thing. Also, the burger doesn't come with any sides, not even french fries. Beware - the server will talk up the french fries, but don't be fooled. They're thinly cut and come with a mayo dipping sauce. They weren't bad, but I've certainly had better. Don't believe them when they tell you they're the best you'll ever eat. 

Fantastic beer selection, if you're into Belgian beers. Despite my feelings on the burger, I'd try this again to see what else they've got. Place is charming, and conveniently located. Try it out!
Great beer selection, brewed here as well as old world offering. And sausages aplenty! Great vibe.

Food is salty however my biggest gripe is the names of the entrees.  They are a play on black culture however it's an Indian restaurant.  A dish called Puff Puff Pass, The Okra Winfried Show, Smoke Weed all day, Fry-Day ErrrDay. It wouldn't be funny if a white owned restaurant had a dish called "Apu's Special or Dank youuuu come Again". I get trying to be edgy or cool but doing this is only shows the owners lack of creativity and originality.

I've been going here for years with my family and I really don't think it lives up to all the hype. It's not terrible but it definitely is not worth all the attention it gets. I'm not a huge fan of their pizza (it always seems burnt) the last time I came here I got a pasta dish and the gravy was watery. I am always surprised when I hear people raving about Pica's.

never been inside...dont need to be...the drive through is an excellent way to get your really really good tasting grilled cheese..dont really know why its so good but they have me hooked... & I dont even drink coffee!  dont eat donuts-once worked in a bakery and after that donuts just dont taste good anymore anywhere! so, I can only review that darn good sandwich!!

The staff is amazing!  They are courteous and knowledgeable.  They are tentative and have a passion for helping people.  The restaurant is clean. Oh & by the way...the food is superb!!!  I have never been to another Mcalisters Deli, not sure if I want to.  This restaurant setts the bar pretty high.

My husband isn't a big fan of Italian food.  I love it!   But, because we both want to enjoy what we're eating, we rarely eat Italian because I will eat almost anything elsewhere and be happy.   However, he gave into my Italian craving this past Saturday when we were trying to decide where to have dinner.   I'd actually eaten at Papa Joe's one time before and loved it and he knew he'd be fine with pizza, so I thought it was a win-win.  

I called ahead to make sure it wasn't too crowded and was told we would be seated immediately upon arrival.  I was surprised it wasn't more crowded on a Saturday night, but happy to be taken to our seats immediately.  

There was a margarita drink special, so we each ordered one.  My husband ordered the traditional margarita (without salt on the rim).  I ordered an Italian margarita.  It took a long while to get our drinks, but when we finally did, mine was delicious.   Unfortunately, my husband's had salt on the rim that he had to wipe off before he could drink it.  

We each ordered salad.  My husband's "Works" salad gave me food envy as I ate the typical House Side Salad.  We ended up sharing his because it was so much better than mine, along with the yummy bread and oil offered to us.  

As I mentioned, my husband isn't a fan of Italian food, except pizza.   Thank goodness, it was on the menu.  He ordered the Supreme Pizza, which was obviously meant to be shared.  I didn't taste it, but he said it was very good, even though he only ate half of it.  

I ordered the Chicken Marsala which came with mashed potatoes and asparagus.   The mashed potatoes were dry and the asparagus seemed limp and tasteless, but the Chicken Marsala was awesome!    A few years ago there was an Italian restaurant in Indianapolis that I loved.  They had the best Chicken Marsala I've ever had and I am in constant search of a comparable dish.  I think Papa Joe's came as close to it as I've found.   I loved the rich creamy texture of the Marsala and mushroom sauce and the chicken was juicy and tender.  I was happy to have half of it left over to eat for lunch another day.  

Our server, Jordan, was friendly and efficient.   With the exception of our long wait for drinks and there being salt on the rim of my husband's drink glass, our orders came quickly, our water glasses were refilled often and she was attentive to our needs.  We always appreciate good service.  

While I wouldn't say it was an an amazing dining experience, I do look forward to coming back again someday to try some other dishes on the menu.

For as old as New Orleans is, you have to figure some creepy shiz goes on here, and while I'm not heavily into supernatural stuff...I can't help but believe their folklore has some truth to it.

Every time I go to NOLA, I try to squeeze in a creepy tour. I failed earlier this year, but redeemed myself with French Quarter Phantoms this time around! We did the Ghosts and Vampire Tour.

While my sister in law is really into the supernatural aspect of the stories, my nerdy self likes to hear about the history of the city, and this tour does a fantastic job of combining the two.

Justin was our tour guide and he was super awesome! The meeting spot is at Voodoo Lounge and the tour includes a 2-for-1 Hurricane special. Sure, why not?

All in all, It was a great tour and Justin is very knowledgeable about his history and background of these stories. He was really funny too, which definitely helps when these stories get kinda weird and creepy. 

I highly recommend this tour and hopefully the other tour guides are as good as Justin!

If you want the worlds best meal replacement shake you got it RIGHT HERE! All shakes are under 300 calories & ALWAYS 24g of protein! The flavors taste just like dessert without the guilt! Also Flirtini energy bomb is a MUST TRY!

I have been to this restaurant oh so many times over the years.  It has never been great but there used to be a certain charm to showing up a casino diner at 3am and it be totally packed with drunk tourists, casino industry people and the occasional band or when the fair was in town, carnies.  The food was super cheap and greasy with infinite coffee refills from the generally busy but pleasant servers.

  The last time I went here a couple weeks ago the atmosphere was tense as they were short staffed and even though most of the dozens of tables were empty, the bussers and severs were doing the jobs of several people with the cooks looking bored and heads down looking at their phones.  My own server did not show up for a long time, maybe 15 min and a busser finally got my drink order before I saw her.  Maybe they should recruit the many uniformed security that were hanging out and chatting with tables to help? 

  I got the French dip with some fries and I am not sure where they got the beef that they served me or how long it was sitting around for but it was grey in color.  I was both impressed and disgusted at the same time but hey, at least the fries were crispy!

  So I ended up handing the busser a cash tip and paid my bill and that, dear readers, will be the last time I step foot in Top Deck.

  Oh how the mighty have fallen.

HAHA. I ordered a cheeseburger, but there was no burger in it! (HOW DOES THAT EVEN HAPPEN!?) It was just the toppings. So I had to send it back, and they made a new one... that actually came with burger.
The flavor was good, but the burger was so soggy and crumbled apart, so I had to use a fork to eat it.
3 1/2 stars good food but nothing out of this world. Must try the she crab soup ! It's rich creamy filled with crab meat. Shrimp scampi very nice light perfect to enjoy with a nice bottle of wine.
What a little gem! I lived in Lima the past 4 years and I am a connoisseur of leche de Tigre. They had one of the best I've ever had (stateside and in Peru!)

Great pizza in Nashville?  Yep!

Just off of the crazed Broadway strip on 2nd Ave, this place hits all the highs.  Keep in mind, it's small and always packed (rightly so!).  Put your name in, it's worth the wait.

We learned early on to share, as portions in Music City are big.  We ordered the hot chicken pizza and an order of their mac and cheese.  We both agree, the mac and cheese was among the best we've had.  Though the pizza was personal size, we still had plenty left over for midnight munchies.  Hot chicken is a local craze, and the Stillery's take using it on pizza was awesome.  Just the right kick, perfect crust, even after microwaving the leftovers.  Hint:  if you have to wait, grab a drink next door at the live music venue...a little divey, but fun!

I honestly would give 0 stars if possible, the owner is the most rude, arrogant person in business that I have encountered. After I waited for almost an hour after ordering my food, I called the establishment and was informed that they had mistakenly cancelled my order. When I requested confirmation of my refund, I was yelled at, belittled, and talked to like a child by the owner. He literally hung up on me 3 times after my request, and had the audacity to ask me if I thought he cares about a refund. Never again!!!

What a great Lobster Roll! My husband and I got the extra meat, bringing the total up to 6 ounces of lobster. This made for a sandwich, overflowing with lobster, which is every bit as good as it sounds. With a buttery sauce (ask for extra next time) on top of buttery toasted bread, this was a rich sandwich. 

We ordered a side of lobster bisque, which was just ok. Next time, I would order the regular sized roll, and get two of them instead. Also, they have some interesting soda. The Blueberry Lemonade was strange, but I liked the Blueberry Beer.

I've had limited experience drinking and eating in this part of town but Urban was decent. I wouldn't cab across town to come here on a Saturday night, but if I did find myself in Fairmount, looking for somewhere to go after dark to satisfy my thirst, I'd probably choose here. It's deceivingly open inside and has this barnyard sort of thing going on with the motif. Food is okay despite the carefully arranged presentation, which makes you think, "Wow, this is going to be great bar food." Fried mac and cheese were tasteless squares of grease that had a tomato-soup like dip; the fries pillowing a so-so order of chicken fingers were so salty I wanted to choke. Like I said, I'd come here but on a drinks-only basis. For chow, I'd head to Jack's or London Grill.
This place has a really good pizza buffet, and if you know me, you know I love value and flavor and taste and this place delivers on all calibers, just look at all the pictures!

After reading all the great reviews we were expecting something really good but it was not. 
Nothing tasted all that great, the hash browns made our mouth dry with an after taste of flour, the (very little) holandais I got with my dish was spicy for some reason, the small salad was indeed very small, the dressing was way too powerful and the coffee was burnt. 
very disappointing considering we waited 20  min to get a table...

What's not to like about this place? Nice location, good service, great food. I ordered a pasta dish which was literally perfect. There's no way I could have made it better. My italian soda was a nice treat as well.
Very nice staff. Quick service. Yummy food. COVID complaint. They did change their hours for now though, they close at 8, not 9.

There is a problemo in the Catina! As you see, we eat at Chuys, often. Today this was a ship with no leadership.  Came in at shift change evidently? Bar full of loud employees taking up tables, bartender trying too "get out"! Not what we had hoped for in an experience! Really don't want to come into eat and hear employees talking about their issues at end of bar, and service was sloooooooow. A no go for you or anyone at shift change evidently on a Sunday between 4 and 5. No help, no manager? He/she must have been eating too, the food must be good.

My bad, manager did show up in bar, to have SEVERAL samples of the margarita machine WITH employees behind the bar? He looked cool in his plaid and while a food server was standing in front of me drinking a margarita, I asked for a refill. Got handed off to someone else without even a thanks for coming in! Adios Chuys Cool Springs. I wont return. Hmmmmm
Pricing is reasonable. My lobster bisque and Cuban sandwich was good. The hefeweizen was medicore.

Had the honey wine, lentil sambosa and doro wat. I didn't care for the honey wine (tasted like beer), but the lentil sambosa was nice and surprisingly light considering it was fried. It was the doro wat, however, that stole the show! Very yummy!

I came here last Sunday with a friend. Don't come here if you're looking for good service. The young girl brought us the menu and utensils and never asked us what we wanted to drink. I had to ask for water. We ordered the Beef Noodle Soup and the General Chicken Pizza. Both were really good. The broth for the soup wasn't overly salty. The noodles appeared homemade but could be fresher. The pizza was really good! This concept is new to me. I would definitely come back to try other dishes.

The idea of a southern gastropub is actualized in The Parish. The atmosphere was delightful with a diverse crowd of patrons. The bartenders were funny and able to make up cocktails on the spot. As a southerner transplated to Tucson I had pipe dreams of finding a good Po'Boy. I was floored by the authentic Shrimp Po'Boy with delicious remoulade and hush puppies on the side. I will definitely be back!

I'm a big fan, I've dined as a family with kids, had business functions ranging from 8-30 pp.  Staff is very professional and accommodating.  Had brunch and dinner as well as the personalized price fix menu from Paul.  Definitely one of the best restaurants in town.  Portions are decent too, unlike some fancier restaurants in town.

New restaurant that needs some more refining. The cheek with vermicelli did not have enough acid and noodles were overcooked. The cheeks themselves were not seasoned enough and undercooked. It was very bland. The jicama salad portion was very small and shrimp overcooked. The pork spring rolls and fried oyster were good but not overwhelming. Place needs more consistency for food quality and preparation as some members of the party said it was much better last time.

Oh BJ's Brewhouse, how I love your food at every location I've been at before this one. Too bad the service and quality at this Lutz location was subpar to say the least.

My best friend was married 2 weeks ago today. The Thursday night before the wedding, the bridal party (bride+5 ladies) came to BJ's for dinner while having a girls night. We were seated within 10 minutes of arrival despite our cited 20 minute wait time (great!) but then came the trouble.. we sat down and asked for waters all around while we looked over the drink menu. When we went to order drinks, the waitress informed us that "someone" (the groom) had called ahead and ordered us a bottle of champagne that she would bring out in case we wanted to wait on the bottle before ordering more drinks. Then the waters came out - only 5 of them for the 6 of us. The waitress didn't even notice she didn't bring a 6th and we had to request it when she brought the wine - again bringing only 5 glasses for 6 of us despite having said out loud "okay 6 waters and 6 glasses" before she came by. After bringing us the wine glasses she comes back to inform us that they're out of bubbly - and gave a choice of white wine or rose (I feel like this was information they should have told the groom when he called as we were waiting to be seated and paid for the bottle - or to us when she came by and told us that a bottle had been purchased for our table). We got our waters and wine glasses after a bit of a wait - all of this would've been fine and we would've let it go but the night didn't really get better from there. 

The bride ordered a large steak - cooked medium rare. Unfortunately, more than 1/4 of the steak was completely raw - seared lightly on the outside and raw on the inside. The rest of our meals came out correctly (a pizza, two orders of the Parmesan crusted chicken, an order of calamari, an order of potato skins, a flatbread, and a salad). And again... only 5 sets of silverware. The waitress brought our food before bringing the silverware and then zoomed by with it after we asked for it - and forgot one - and zoomed away before we could say anything and only came back nearly 10 minutes later. The whole dinner experience took nearly 2 hours despite us ordering as soon as the wine came out (getting the waters and wine alone took 20 minutes). And then, we felt like we were being rushed out so they could turn the table over when it came time to pay despite the service having been so mediocre and slowed down the whole meal all night. The waitress acted like she was doing us a favor just showing up to work the whole night.

Onto some things I generally like about BJ's:
BJ's is like Applebee's or Chili's in that every restaurant has the same layout and general aesthetic: BJ's has huge TVs and a sports bar vibe with darker lighting and significantly better food. The portions are always spot on and you can't go wrong with the Parmesan crusted chicken and a pizookie. They're famous for these pizookies: cookies baked in personal sized pizza pans and topped with ice cream. Can't decide what flavor you want? Get a mini pizookie trio and try out 3 flavors. 

Hopefully others catch them on a better night than we did. If you want good, fast, accurate service, this BJs may not be the place for you. If you're more patient and can deal with the service for the great food, enjoy!

We went to Dooey's Road after my son's confirmation for dinner.  The food was delicious.  There was a group of us so we ordered a few appetizers.  We ordered garlic parmesan wings, sweet chili wings, pierogies with kielbasa, regular pierogies macaroni and cheese and crab sticks.  For entrees we had breaded chicken sandwiches, burgers, pizza, lobster ravioli and the grilled mahi mahi.  There was not 1 person at our table that didn't like something.  The food tastes delicious and you get nice size portions for a great price.    The chef came out and chatted with us surprising all of us with dessert.  For dessert we had bread pudding.  I am not a fan of bread pudding but tasted it anyway and couldn't stop eating it!  Soo good!  The chef is a nice guy with a great personality!  You can tell this guy truly enjoys what he does for a living.  We will definitely be going back!

Came here for lunch with a group of friends & 10/10 recommend! Dave the GM served us and was fantastic!! Everything we ordered was delicious, sandwiches, pizza drinks! Definitely plan on coming back! Thanks Dave!

We not for restaurant week. Service was good however the steaks offered were very tough. Tried the Rib eye and sent it back then tried the NY strip also very tough. I would think that with  restaurant week they would put their best foot forward.

I attended the Sherwood Park (Ordze) location for a Yelp event to try the new Winter menu. I was not disappointed! What stood out to me the most was the friendly staff. My server especially was very prompt and personable. The winter menu items I tried were the Christmas pizza and poutine, smoked Gouda and poblano pepper ravioli, cranberry glazed ribs and Moscow mule (not on winter menu). I enjoyed all of the items I tried. The Xmas pizza and poutine I liked more than I thought I would, the pizza especially. The crust was thin (but not too thin!) and had a nice chew to the edge, the sage cream sauce was the kicker that brought the pizza over the top. Delicious. It also had rotisserie turkey , stuffing, and mixed Italian cheese and cranberry and gravy to dip. The cranberry rubs were fall off the bone, they were mighty tasty but could use a bit more sauce for my liking! The ravioli was quite tasty as well, not as spicy as I expected. The centre was nice and creamy and was topped with a rose sauce and chicken and bacon (yay bacon!). The Moscow mule had a nice gingery bite to it, I would have this again. Also I had samples from Corkbeard wines, Situation Brewing, Rig Hand distillery ( great Double Double liqueur and horseradish Caesars!), Townesquare, and Analog Brewing. My favorite was the Earl Grey and blueberry Saison. It would be great for a holiday party. Overall I think that BP's did a great job of hosting and the food was great.

The worst experience I ever had with a fast food establishment. I arrived to max at 10:45 pm and did not get my food till 11:53pm. I arrived and had to wait till the crew work finished with the first set of orders before placing my order . Once the first orders were done I placed my order and the cook took about 20 other customers orders and started there order before completing my order . I assume it was get everyone out at the same time. But it was complete utter confusion. I stood and watched other customers walk-in and the cook take there order and get there sandwich's prepped   before even completing mines . I had ordered a simple half chicken steak . I am very surprised this places has not shut down . Not to mention the workers all were mean and extremely loud . Very very disappointed will not recommend this restaurant. The was subpar and extremely messy
Mmmmm fresh, hot, pizza. Had the margarita. They made it right in front of me... delicious!
Sports bar great food laid back. Great service lots tvs.  We had shrimp diablo spicy pasta with shrimp and bacon wrapped shrimp with stuffed crab inside and rice pilaf.

Just passing through Philly and decided to search for a quick spot to eat, and I was not disappointed. They have a lot to offer on the menu, but I decided to try their version of the Philly Cheese Steak. 

It was affordable, tasty, and ready in under 10 minutes. Will definitely be back!

The wheat bread wasn't impressive. I think most people avoid paying the extra 50c for the wheat bread, and go for the regular bread. Thats likely why the wheat bread was almost stale. 

I am not sure why the mixed veggie doesn't come with cheese in it. I have to say the spinach is sometimes a bit suspect. Its certainly not the freshest spinach out there, but it sometimes smells a bit stale. Oh and the mushrooms are out of a can. Which given my distrust of the spinach can't be a bad thing at all. They taste fine.

Overall, this is a foodtruck that sells its rolls for $3. Don't expect the world. Overall, I'm very happy with the 'regular' that I have here - double egg, cheese WITH mushrooms, bui sauce and hot sauce. I've had it on innumerable occasions now, and like the lady who makes it in a jiffy.
Walked in, told the maitre'd would be back soon, 15 minutes later after multiple waiters walked right past us, he showed up and told us there was a 45 minute wait.  Thanks for the great service!
This boba was very milky 5/5. As a devout lactose intolerant, it reminded me I need to invest in a deeper toilet bowl.
